textes.(Elle chuchote.) Au revoir, {surnom}. Ne: (She whispers.) Goodbye, {surnom}. Don't get lost. Or if you do, get lost somewhere pretty.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Augustin livre de la fa: (She whispers.) Augustin delivers flour to a library. It isn't sensible. Nor are the poems in the sacks. But I'm not sure I want everything to be sensible.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Augustin, le meunier, m: (She whispers.) Augustin, the miller, brings me a poem every week. “For the Library,” he says. I keep them in a separate drawer. A drawer of my own. You mustn't tell him.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Bienvenue à la Biblioth: (She whispers.) Welcome to the Library of Maps. I am Miss Philippine Feuillet. Here, we speak softly, we turn the pages gently, and we never fold a map the wrong way. It would remember.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Bonjour, Ysaé. Une nouv: (She whispers.) Hello, Ysaé. A new street?
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Bonjour… Murmure… bibli: (She whispers.) Hello… Murmure… librarian at the Academy… Welcome to the library… Here, we speak very softly… Even the books… Especially the books… They're very sensitive.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Bonne nuit… La Biblioth: (She whispers.) Good night… The Library is asleep. The maps, though, dream of journeys.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Chaque mardi, Augustin: (She whispers.) Every Tuesday, Augustin delivers a sack of flour to the Library. We don't need flour. In every sack there's a poem, folded in four. I keep them in a drawer of my own. I have forty-three. I've never told him I found them. He's never told me he put them there. It's very nice like that. For now.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Chez nous, on chuchotai: (She whispers.) At home, we whispered everything. Hellos, arguments, birthdays. “Happy birthday”, very softly, with a candle cake we blew out gently. When I started school, the teacher thought I was ill. I was just well brought up.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Chut… Les petits font l: (She whispers.) Shh… The little ones are napping. They danced around the ribbon tree all morning. Would you help me tuck them in? Gently…
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Depuis que la ligne a r: (She whispers.) Since the line reopened, I went down to see the Fronde for real, with my map drawn from Ysaé's words. It's wrong in four places. A painter, Fusain, is going to paint it on his Wall. With the mistakes. They're my prettiest mistakes.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Dites-moi, {surnom} : s: (She whispers.) Tell me, {surnom}: if you could invent a land, what would you call it?
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Elle m'a décrit la Fron: (She whispers.) She described the Fronde to me for three hours. I drew. At the end, she looked at the map and said: “That's home.” Her eyes were shining.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Il a dessiné une étoile: (She whispers.) He drew a star on my coastal map. For Clémentine. I didn't rub it out. I don't know why.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) J'adore les cartes de p: (She whispers.) I adore maps of countries that don't exist. Islands invented by tired sailors, kingdoms drawn by children, continents born from an ink blot. I have two hundred of them. They're my favourites. They never change their minds.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) J'ai dessiné quarante e: (She whispers.) I've drawn forty of your island's staircases. Only nine hundred and sixty to go.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Je chuchote depuis que: (She whispers.) I've been whispering since I was six. My father was a librarian, and so was my mother. At home, when we argued, we argued in whispers. It was very restful.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Je vais vous confier qu: (She whispers.) I'll tell you something, {surnom}. Ysaé came and described the Fronde to me, down below. I drew a map from her words: painted streets, banners, singing staircases. It's the only map in the Library of a land that exists and that I've never seen. It's filed with the imaginary lands. For the time being.

(She whispers.) I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Ysaé came to describe the Fronde to me, down below. I drew a map from her words: painted streets, banners, stairs that sing. It's the only map in the Library of a country that exists and that I had never seen. It was shelved with the imaginary countries. Since the line reopened, I've moved it to another shelf.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) La Capitaine Héloïse m': (She whispers.) Captain Héloïse promised to map the sky above the sea, from the Albatross. Maps of clouds! They change all the time. I'll have to make a new map every morning. I can't wait.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Le Pays des Siestes… Un: (She whispers.) The Land of Naps… A capital called Pillow, rivers of duvets… I'll draw it. Very quietly, so as not to wake it.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Le Professeur Lunette a: (She whispers.) Professor Lunette drew a star on one of my maps of the coast. In pencil. “For Clémentine,” he said. I didn't rub it out. I don't know why. Well, yes, I do.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Le Professeur rend touj: (She whispers.) The Professor always returns everything late. Always. I ought to ban him from the Library. I can't bring myself to. He has a way of saying “sorry” that makes you want to lend him everything else.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Le soir, je m'assois su: (She whispers.) In the evening, I sit on the bench along the promenade and look at the sea. In my head, I draw the countries that lie beyond the horizon. There's always one more.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Les plans des Strates s: (She whispers.) The plans of the Strata are kept in a locked drawer, “by order of the Burgomaster”. But Ysaé came and described the Fronde to me. I made a map from her words. It's full of music and colour. It's the most beautiful one in the Library.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Les vrais pays sont trè: (She whispers.) Real lands are very nice too. They have the advantage of existing. That's their only flaw: they don't change when you ask them to.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Merci, Augustin. Elle s: (She whispers.) Thank you, Augustin. It will be very useful.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Notre carte de la Cité: (She whispers.) Our map of the City of Clouds was wrong: it had been drawn from down here, looking up. The line has reopened, and I went up to correct it myself. Forty mistakes. And a very long eraser.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Nous avons ici la premi: (She whispers.) Here we have the very first map of Hautefond, drawn by Lady Ysolde herself. There's only the hill, the sea, and a little column sketched in pencil, with the words: “one day”. I look at it often.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Nous n'avons qu'une car: (She whispers.) We have only one map of the City of Clouds, and it's wrong: it was drawn from below, looking up. When the line reopens, I'll go and correct it myself. With a very long pencil.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Oh, c'est très Hautefon: (She whispers.) Oh, that's very Hautefond. A thousand staircases, and only one cabin, with a queue every time. I'll draw it. In perspective.
(She whispers.) Oh, that's very Hautefond. A thousand staircases, and a single cabin, always under maintenance. I'll draw it. In perspective.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Partir un jour, avec un: (She whispers.) To leave one day, with a notebook and a pencil, and draw the map of a land nobody has ever drawn. And come back to file it. Section three, shelf twelve.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Professeur, vous avez s: (She whispers.) Professor, you're six weeks late.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Si je me souviens de vo: (She whispers.) Do I remember you? I've filed you away in my memory, “kind travellers” section, top shelf.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Toujours les vrais pays: (She whispers.) Still the real lands? You're more sensible than I am.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Très bien. J'ai rangé l: (She whispers.) Very well. I've sorted the entire archipelago, north to south, then smallest to largest. Then by colour of sea. That was the prettiest.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Un jour, j'ai crié. Une: (She whispers.) Once, I shouted. Just once. A mouse had got into the South Seas aisle. The whole Upper Town heard. The Burgomaster thought there was a fire. He gave a speech to reassure me. The mouse was the first to leave.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Un jour, une souris est: (She whispers.) One day, a mouse got into the South Seas section. I screamed. Only once in my life. The whole Upper Town heard it. The Burgomaster came running with a bucket of water. He spilled it on the Great Atlas. I spent a month drying it. The mouse left on its own.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Un mardi, il n'y avait: (She whispers.) One Tuesday, there was no poem in the sack. I was sad all day. On Wednesday, there were two.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Un peu agacée. Le Profe: (She whispers.) A little annoyed. Professor Lunette has borrowed the star charts again. Six weeks overdue. I'm going to scold him. Very gently. He hates that. Well, I think so.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Votre Pays des Siestes: (She whispers.) Your Land of Naps is coming along. I've finished the capital.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Ysaé parle fort, rit fo: (She whispers.) Ysaé talks loudly, laughs loudly, and wears bolts in her ears. In the Library, she whispers. Just for me. It's the loveliest courtesy anyone has ever paid me.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) {surnom} ! Quel plaisir: (She whispers.) {surnom}! What a pleasure. I've received a map of a country that doesn't exist. With teapot-shaped mountains. Would you like to see it? Shh. Come.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) {surnom}… J'ai une nouv: (She whispers.) {surnom}… I have a new map…
textes.(Elle chuchote.) À bientôt. Et si vous d: (She whispers.) See you soon. And if you discover a country, come back and draw it for me.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) À huit ans, j'ai trouvé: (She whispers.) When I was eight, I found a map in the attic of an island that didn't exist. It was called “the Isle of Lost Socks”. A sailor had drawn it one stormy night. It's my first map of an imaginary land. It hangs framed above my desk.
textes.(Elle chuchote.) Ô Grand Spaghetti, fais: (She whispers.) O Great Spaghetti, make sure my pasta never sticks. Ramen.
textes.(Elle compte les syllabes sur ses doigts: (She counts the syllables on her fingers.)
textes.(Elle dessine un cercle dans l'air avec: (She draws a circle in the air with her finger.)
textes.(Elle devient toute rouge et ferme sa ve: (She turns bright red and buttons her jacket up to the neck.) … Shh. Not here. Not in front of the Office. Please. … Come to the gig tonight. At the back.
textes.(Elle devient toute rouge.) Un poney… ro: (She turns bright red.) A pony… a pink one? (She looks around.) … Me too. Shh. We don't tell anyone. It's our secret.
textes.(Elle déroule les plans sur ses genoux,: (She unrolls the plans across her lap, very slowly. Four hundred shops. Two thousand parking spaces. A fountain that plays an anthem.) ... Is that all? That's what he wanted to put in place of our lives? (She rolls up the plans.) Well. We'll keep them. We'll hang them in the assembly hall, so we remember. And look who's coming. The Port-Boucan Shared Lease. The premises belong to those who bring them to life. Signed Aldric Lisse. (She smiles.) Here, Aldric. A toffee. It's been a while.

textes.(Elle les prend un par un. Ils grésillen: (She takes them one by one. They crackle, they sing, and for once, her hair stays flat.) Bzzzz… Do you hear that? They're singing. textes.(Elle les regarde un par un, en souriant: (She looks at them one by one, smiling.) The Spring Bolete: you'll jump three times higher. The Moonwort: you'll see what's hidden. The Little Giant: you'll grow for a while, and be stronger. Keep them: they're yours. You can eat them from your bag, here, in our tale. And in the real forest? ... Never! Good. You remembered. textes.(Elle lève la main.) C'est quoi, un oise: (She puts her hand up.) What's a bird, exactly?
textes.(Elle lève la main.) Pourquoi le ciel ne: (She puts her hand up.) Why doesn't the sky fall down?
textes.(Elle met un doigt devant sa bouche.): (She puts a finger to her lips.)
textes.(Elle ouvre de grands yeux.) Moi ? Pour: (Her eyes go wide.) Me? For real? … OK. I'll come. With Miss Nautile, and the whole class. And you'll be there to show it to me. It's written in my notebook. That means it's a promise.
textes.(Elle ouvre un œil.) Elle est toujours l: (She opens one eye.) It's still there.
textes.(Elle ouvre un œil.) … Bon. (Elle le ref: (She opens one eye.) … Fine. (She closes it again.)
textes.(Elle pose sa main sur ton bras.) Non, m: (She puts her hand on your arm.) No, little one. Never. Here, in our story, the fairy mushrooms are kind. But in a real forest, a pretty mushroom can make you very, very ill. Promise me.
textes.(Elle pose son tricot.) Ça, c'est la mei: (She puts down her knitting.) Now that's the best answer. The one that holds everything else together. You'll chair a fine assembly one day.
textes.(Elle reprend son pinceau derrière l'ore: (She takes her brush from behind her ear again.)
textes.(Elle s'arrête, la louche en l'air.) Ça,: (She stops, ladle in the air.) Now that's the best answer anyone's ever given me. My grandmother used to say exactly that. Come. Tonight, I'm cooking for you.
textes.(Elle siffle deux notes et s'essuie les: (She whistles two notes and wipes her hands. It changes nothing.) Welcome! A friend of Rouille's is a friend of mine. If one day you have a squeaky bike, a bent wheel or a chain that skips, come to the workshop. I won't fix it for you: I'll teach you how to fix it. It's better. And it takes longer. But it's better.
textes.(Elle siffle trois notes joyeuses, ouvre: (She whistles three cheerful notes, opens the bags, and pulls out a chain, pedals, spokes, a bell shaped like a rat.) A rat-shaped bell! Ferraille, you're a genius! (She already has her hands in the grease.) With this, I'll put ten bikes back on the road. And the eleventh, I'll keep for you. Well, if you know how to fix a flat. No? I'll teach you.
textes.(Elle siffle un petit air, puis s'essuie: (She whistles a little tune, then wipes her hands on her overalls. It makes no difference.) Hi! Rustine, bike workshop. Here, we don't fix your bike: we teach you to fix it. And if you don't have a bike, we build you one out of three old bikes. It's called recycling. Or magic.
textes.(Elle siffle une note très longue et trè: (She whistles one very long, very low note.) Upset? I've got fourteen bikes to fix and not a single part left! No more chains, no more pedals, no more spokes! Lisse's robots ransacked the Scrapyard and took everything to make themselves arms. But Ferraille told me he hid three lots of parts under his scrap piles, just for me. Would you go get them? It's at the Scrapyard, to the south-east. If you run into Ferraille, don't ask him about his dragon: you'd be there all day.
textes.(Elle siffle une petite note interrogati: (She whistles a little questioning note.) Tell me: can you fix a puncture?
textes.(Elle siffle.) Hé, toi ! Tu roules ?: (She whistles.) Hey, you! Do you ride?
textes.(Elle sourit, tout bas.) Je le savais. M: (She smiles, very softly.) I knew it. My mother used to say that. The Professor says it's the gas in our breath. He may be right. But then, our breath might as well carry kind words, don't you think?
textes.(Elle touche sa poche.) Ceux-là, on les: (She touches her pocket.) Those ones, we keep. They don't belong to us: they belong to the person. We keep them for them.
textes.(Elle vérifie que sa veste est bien ferm: (She checks that her jacket is properly buttoned.)

textes.(Il approche lentement son crochet de to: (He slowly brings his hook up to your nose.) Like this. Want me to show you how I scratch my ear? Or rather… how I scratch YOURS?
textes.(Il baisse la voix d'un coup.) Doucement: (He suddenly drops his voice.) Softly… That's good too. Very good, even. Don't tell anyone, but it's what I prefer.

textes.(Il compte les étoiles sur ses doigts, s: (He counts the stars on his fingers, stops, starts again, and ends up laughing without a sound: there are too many.)
textes.(Il dessine du doigt, dans la poussière,: (With his finger, he draws a boat in the dust… then a big wave… then nothing. He wipes it all away with one sweep.)

textes.(Il enlève sa casquette.) Voilà. Voilà l: (He takes off his cap.) There. That's the real answer. That's what my father used to say. Never mind the rails. It's who's next to you in the cabin. Come on, get in. Next to me.

textes.(Il relève ses lunettes.) Dis-moi : quan: (He lifts his goggles.) Tell me: when you see a pile of scrap metal, what do you see?

textes.(L'Aigle te regarde longtemps.) Les anci: (The Eagle looks at you for a long time.) The elders say the Fifth Sun will stop one day. Not today. Not thanks to you. Keep the Feather: its place is on the Altar of the Three Suns, in the highlands. And take this, for the road.

textes.(Le Muet entre dans une tente imaginaire: (The Silent One walks into an imaginary tent and sits down. textes.(Le Muet installe une cible invisible co: (The Silent One sets up an invisible target against the mast and nods towards Scarlett.)

textes.(Le Muet lève la main pour te saluer. El: (The Mute raises his hand to greet you. It's as big as a paddle.)
textes.(Le Muet lève le pouce, puis montre le c: (The Silent One gives a thumbs up, then points to the sky and puffs out his cheeks like the wind.)
textes.(Le Muet lève quatre doigts et pose un d: (The Silent One holds up four fingers and lays a finger on his lips.)
textes.(Le Muet lève quatre doigts vers Tom, pu: (The Silent One holds up four fingers to Tom, then puts a finger to his lips.)
textes.(Le Muet lève sept doigts, puis tapote u: (The Silent One holds up seven fingers, then taps a single spot in the palm of his hand.)
textes.(Le Muet lève son verre vers toi et le v: (The Mute raises his glass to you and downs it in one go. He slaps you on the shoulder. You nearly fall over.)
textes.(Le Muet mime la nuit : la lune, le quai: (The Silent One mimes the night: the moon, the quay, a man leaning towards the water, leaning further… splash! He plunges his arm into imaginary water, grabs a collar and pulls. He sets something heavy on the quay and pats its head. Then he puts his hand on his heart, very serious: you don't let anyone drown.)
textes.(Le Muet mime un pirate qui marche sur u: (The Mute mimes a pirate walking the plank, looking down, and running back. He clutches his sides with laughter.)
textes.(Le Muet mime une bagarre au Crâne Fendu: (The Silent One mimes a brawl at the Crâne Fendu: chairs flying, fists everywhere. Suddenly, he looks up, opens his hands wide, and catches something in mid-air. He holds it against himself with great care: a fiddle. He hands it to someone invisible, who hugs it tight. He shrugs, modestly.)
textes.(Le Muet mime une lanceuse de couteaux,: (The Silent One mimes a knife thrower, then makes his hand talk like a mouth, next to his own. He nods: she's the one who says what he thinks.)
textes.(Le Muet mime une seiche qui crache son: (The Silent One mimes a cuttlefish squirting its ink, and Coralie catching it in the bay and getting her finger pinched. He laughs without a sound. Then he rummages in his pockets and holds out shells, feathers, a pearl, one by one, like paying off a debt that never ends. He shrugs: he likes bringing her things.)
textes.(Le Muet montre Belle-Humeur, au loin, p: (The Silent One points to Belle-Humeur, in the distance, then makes a heart with both hands. He shakes his head hard, looking outraged. Then he points to Scarlett and mimes someone laughing and holding their sides. He sighs, rolls his eyes, and ends up laughing too, without a sound.)
textes.(Le Muet montre Belle-Humeur, puis son o: (The Silent One points to Belle-Humeur, then to his ear, and shakes his head: he can't hear. He points to himself, to his mouth, and shakes his head: he doesn't speak. Then he makes big gestures, slow and clear, and nods like someone getting an answer. He gives a thumbs up: the two of them understand each other perfectly.)
textes.(Le Muet montre la Veuve, puis tapote so: (The Silent One points to the Widow, then pats his shoulder, the way you offer a seat.)
textes.(Le Muet montre la mer, puis fait un toi: (The Silent One points to the sea, then makes a roof with both hands over your head. He remembers: the sea is your home.)
textes.(Le Muet montre la mer, puis le ciel, et: (The Silent One points to the sea, then the sky, and mimes the wind filling the sails.)
textes.(Le Muet montre la mer, puis toi, et fai: (The Silent One points to the sea, then to you, and mimes a door opening. He nods: your home is still waiting for you.)
textes.(Le Muet montre la tente de Coralie, pui: (The Silent One points to Coralie's tent, then touches his arm, where his sleeve is, and puts his hand on his heart. He puts a finger to his lips.)
textes.(Le Muet montre le tonneau, puis fait mi: (The Silent One points at the barrel, then pretends to break it in two. He raises an eyebrow.)
textes.(Le Muet porte une planche invisible gra: (The Silent One carries an invisible plank as big as a door and wedges it against the mast. He steps back. He mimes seven knives flying, one by one, and sticking in the same spot. Then he runs to pull them out, counts the holes with his fingertip, frowns, counts again. Just one hole. He throws his arms up, amazed, like every time.)
textes.(Le Muet pose la main sur son cœur, mont: (The Silent One puts his hand on his heart, points to the sea behind you, and gently nudges your shoulder: don't forget to go back.)
textes.(Le Muet pose son coude sur un tonneau e: (The Silent One puts his elbow on a barrel and opens his hand towards Gros-Louis.)
textes.(Le Muet pose son coude sur un tonneau i: (The Silent One puts his elbow on an imaginary barrel and grips an invisible hand. He strains, he grimaces, he strains some more. Crack! He mimes the barrel collapsing and two giants falling to the ground. He holds up three fingers: three broken barrels. Then he points to himself and raises one more finger: he's in the lead. He swears it, hand raised.)
textes.(Le Muet pose un coquillage sur la table: (The Mute puts a shell on the table, then a finger to his lips.)
textes.(Le Muet regarde autour de lui. Personne: (The Silent One looks around. Nobody. He rolls up his sleeve and shows you the little heart Coralie tattooed on his arm. Then he leans towards you, very close, and breathes a single word, so softly you think you dreamed it: “Lina.” He puts a finger to his lips, looks at you for a long time, and rolls his sleeve back down.)
textes.(Le Muet regarde l'endroit où tu l'as fr: (The Mute looks at the spot where you hit him. Then he looks at you. Uh-oh.)
textes.(Le Muet regarde la mer, puis toi, et il: (The Silent One looks at the sea, then at you, and laughs without a sound. He mimes a wave, then a roof over his head. He shrugs: why not.)
(The Silent One stays still for a long moment. Then he puts his big hand on your shoulder, heavy and warm, and leaves it there without moving.)
textes.(Le Muet retrousse ses manches. Ses avan: (The Mute rolls up his sleeves. His forearms are as big as your thighs. At last, he smiles.)
textes.(Le Muet s'accroupit et tapote son épaul: (The Silent One crouches down and pats his shoulder, the way you'd point to a seat.)
textes.(Le Muet s'allonge, bras en croix, comme: (The Silent One lies down, arms spread wide, as if on a raft. He mimes a red sail approaching, a hand reaching out, and lets himself be hauled up by the collar. Then he imitates the captain throwing him a blanket, grumbling, and limping away. He laughs without a sound and clasps his fists to his heart.)
textes.(Le Muet s'assoit, les yeux grands ouver: (The Silent One sits down, eyes wide open, and stares at someone opposite without blinking. Time passes: he shows the sun setting, the moon rising, the lanterns going out. He mimes Mama Grog pushing them both outside with her rolling pin. Then he rubs his eyes, exhausted, and holds up two thumbs: a draw.)
textes.(Le Muet salue Belle-Humeur d'un grand g: (The Silent One greets Belle-Humeur with a big, slow wave.)
textes.(Le Muet se lève. Il est encore plus gra: (The Mute stands up. He's even bigger standing. He cracks his neck.)
textes.(Le Muet sort de sa poche un vieux dessi: (The Mute takes an old folded drawing from his pocket: a white house, a tree, a laughing woman. He folds it back up very gently.)
textes.(Le Muet sourit pour la première fois. I: (The Mute smiles for the first time. He steps back, raises his fists, and beckons you in.)
textes.(Le Muet tapote sa propre jambe comme du: (The Silent One taps his own leg as if it were wood, pulls the captain's grumpy face, then puts his hand on his heart and bows his head. He owes him everything.)
textes.(Le Muet te montre sa mâchoire, puis lèv: (The Mute points to his jaw, then gives a thumbs-up. He seems to be saying: “Nice punch.”)
textes.(Le Muet te tapote l'épaule en passant,: (The Silent One pats your shoulder as he passes, for a long time, the way you greet someone who no longer has a home. He hasn't forgotten you.)
textes.(Le Muet tend un coquillage à Coralie, s: (The Silent One holds out a shell to Coralie, without another gesture.)

textes.(Sylvain repousse sa chaise.) Trois fois: (Sylvain pushes back his chair.) Three times in a row. Nobody does that at my table. … Well. A promise is a promise: this scrap of parchment was my reserve stake. They say it comes from Barbe-Sanglante's map. It's yours.

textes.(Tout bas) Il dort comme une pierre. Une: (Whispering) He sleeps like a rock. A very, very small rock. Thanks again, big fella.
textes.(Tout bas.) Toi aussi, tu serais un pone: (Very quietly.) You'd be a pink pony too. I drew you one. It's in my hidden notebook. With a mohawk.
textes.(Tout bas.) Toi qui aimes doucement… j'a: (Very quietly.) You like it soft… I've got a recording of whales. I'll play it for you. In secret.

textes.(Un nuage de farine.) Atchoum ! … Bonjou: (A cloud of flour.) Atchoo! … Hello. Clovis, miller. No, my hair isn't white. Well, it is. But underneath, it's brown. I think. I haven't seen it in ten years.

textes.(Une ombre immense te recouvre. C'est Bo: (A huge shadow falls over you. It's Boulon. He smiles.) Hello. Don't be scared. I'm big, but I'm gentle. Boulon. I run the old crane at the Old Dock. I lift containers for the Boxes. And sometimes cats stuck in trees.

textes.(chuchoté) Bien… très bien, même… Ce mat: (whispered) Fine… very fine, even… This morning nobody made a sound… Except Quasar… He blew something up… Very softly… He's making an effort.
textes.(chuchoté) Dans les livres d'en bas… j'a: (whispered) In the books from down below… I read that there are cats… rats… pigs… and dogs that follow people everywhere… Animals that follow people!… I find that… very romantic.
textes.(chuchoté) La bibliothèque a cent mille: (whispered) The library has a hundred thousand books… Ninety thousand from Ondelune, made of light… Ten thousand from down below, made of paper… Paper books smell lovely… I sniff them in secret… Don't tell anyone.
textes.(chuchoté) La bibliothèque est au fond d: (whispered) The library is at the back of the Academy… east of the Agora… You'll recognise it: it's the only door where everyone starts walking on tiptoe… Even Glorb… who has no feet.
textes.(chuchoté) Le Professeur Quasar… Je lui: (whispered) Professor Quasar… I sorted his notes for him… in alphabetical order… He's furious… He can't find anything… But everything is very tidy… That's what matters.
textes.(chuchoté) Le soir des aurores, je vais: (whispered) On aurora nights, I go to the Gardens… far from the Agora… I watch them in silence… The sky makes no noise at all… That's what I like best about it.
textes.(chuchoté) Lyre m'a écrit un poème… « Mu: (whispered) Lyre wrote me a poem… “Murmure, O gentle creature, your voice is like a…” … She didn't find the ending… Neither did I… I filed it under “U”… For “unfinished”.
textes.(chuchoté) Sur Ondelune, j'avais une voi: (whispered) On Ondelune, I had a very loud voice… The loudest in the village… One day, I sneezed… and a mountain split in two… Since then, I whisper… Just in case… There are mountains everywhere.
textes.(chuchoté) Un peu agacée… Vibrato a joué: (whispered) A little irritated… Vibrato played the theremin under my window… He says he was playing “very quietly”… The theremin never plays quietly… It goes “ooooh”… Even the books shivered.
textes.(chuchoté) Un secret… Une fois par an… l: (whispered) A secret… Once a year… on my birthday… I go down into the Zero-Gravity Garden… right to the far end… and I shout… Just once… “PEEKABOO!”… Then I come back… It does me good for a whole year.
textes.(chuchoté) {surnom}… Te revoilà… J'ai mi: (whispered) {surnom}… You're back… I put a book aside for you… It's about a Heavy-Foot who climbs up to the sky… It ends well… Well, I think so… I haven't read the end… I wanted to read it with you.
textes.(chuchoté) …Ce n'est pas grave… Les livr: (whispered) …That's all right… Books wait… They're very patient… Just come and sit down… Silence is already a book.
textes.(chuchoté) …Inventées… Ce sont les plus: (whispered) …Made-up… Sometimes they're the truest… I'll lend you a book of light… It tells of a floating island… Hee.
textes.(chuchoté) …J'ai demandé à Vibrato de jo: (whispered) …I asked Vibrato to play more softly. He lowered his hands… more… more… In the end, he wasn't playing anything at all… his hands still above the instrument… I opened the window and whispered: “…Perfect.” He played nothing for an hour. It was his finest concert.
textes.(chuchoté) …Je suis allée une fois dans: (whispered) …I went once to Nova's Greenhouse… All the glug-glugs were making a terrible noise… I whispered “…shh”. They went quiet. All of them. All at once. Nova looked at me with huge eyes… She asked me to come back every evening. I go on Tuesdays.
textes.(chuchoté) …Le Professeur Quasar fait ex: (whispered) …Professor Quasar makes things explode. All the time. I tidy up after him. All his notes begin with “So”… so I filed them under S. He's furious. It's very tidy.
textes.(chuchoté) …Le jour où Lyre a découvert: (whispered) …The day Lyre discovered rhymes… she jumped around in the middle of my library shouting “Moon! June!”… I went “shh”… Then… very softly… I added: “…spoon.” She looked at me as if I'd worked a miracle. It was my only rhyme. I've never made another.
textes.(chuchoté) …Les histoires vraies… comme: (whispered) …True stories… like the books from down below… I'll keep one for you… It's about a rowing boat and a storm. It ends well… I think.
textes.(chuchoté) …Lyre m'a écrit un poème… « M: (whispered) …Lyre wrote me a poem… “Murmure, oh sweet and gentle creature, your voice is like a…” … She never found the ending… I filed it under “U”… for “unfinished”… Sometimes, at night, I try to find the ending myself… “…a caress.” It doesn't rhyme. I won't tell her.
textes.(chuchoté) …Lyre parle en vers… et trop: (whispered) …Lyre speaks in verse… and too loudly… She wrote me a poem with no ending. I filed it under “U”, for “unfinished”. I read it often… I like it the way it is.
textes.(chuchoté) …Nova m'a emprunté tous les l: (whispered) …Nova borrowed all the books from down below about cats… There are fourteen… She reads them among the glug-glugs… out loud… The glug-glugs listen. She says they're starting to go “meow”. I think it's still “glug”. But with an accent.
textes.(chuchoté) …Nova vient lire les livres d: (whispered) …Nova comes to read the books from down below about animals… Cats, dogs, pigs… She dreams of stroking a cat. I lend her all my cat books. She gives them back with… imaginary fur on them.
textes.(chuchoté) …Pendant la Nuit des Aurores,: (whispered) …During the Night of the Auroras, Vibrato plays very loudly in the Agora… I don't go to the Agora… I go to the Gardens, far away… And there, from afar, his music arrives very gently… just soft enough… I think it's the only way to hear it properly. I've never told him.
textes.(chuchoté) …Quand une expérience du Prof: (whispered) …When one of the Professor's experiments explodes… I arrive first… silently… I gather the flying pages, I file them… and I whisper to him: “…Quieter, next time.” He tries… His explosions make less and less noise… The last one went “pff”. I congratulated him.
textes.(chuchoté) …Toi qui aimes les histoires: (whispered) …You who love made-up stories… I have a new one… A dragon who whispers… I wrote it… for you.
(whispered) …You who love true stories… I found a book about a lighthouse… It's true… Well, almost…
textes.(chuchoté) …Tu ne lis pas beaucoup… Alor: (whispered) …You don't read much… So I kept a tiny book for you… Three pages… You'll see… They're pretty.
textes.(chuchoté) …Une nuit, j'ai rangé tout le: (whispered) …One night, I tidied the Professor's whole laboratory… in alphabetical order… All his notes began with “So”… They're all under S now… It took him three weeks to find the coffee formula… Between “So, therefore” and “So, perhaps”… It was logical.
textes.(chuchoté) …Une question… Toi, tu lis pl: (whispered) …A question… Do you read… true stories, or made-up ones?
textes.(chuchoté) …Vibrato joue sous ma fenêtre: (whispered) …Vibrato plays under my window. He says he plays very softly. The theremin never plays softly… One day, he played nothing. It was perfect. I told him so. He smiled very loudly.
