textes.Abdellah ? Il forme le cuivre comme pers: Abdellah? He shapes copper like nobody else, and he knows it too well. Without him, my lanterns would have no body. Without me, his would have no soul. On that, we'll never agree.
textes.Abdellah astique mes canons une fois l'a: Abdellah polishes my cannons once a year. He makes them shine, and he hopes they'll never be used. So do I. But I don't say so in front of the guards.
textes.Abdellah est un peu sourd, c'est vrai. M: Abdellah is a bit deaf, it's true. But he's a funny sort of deaf. When a customer says “what lovely copper”, he hears it from the far end of the souk. When they say “what lovely patterns”, he hammers louder and answers “Eh? Tap!”. Hnia, his wife, swore to me he hears both perfectly well.
textes.Abdellah tape sur mes canons avec son pe: Abdellah taps my cannons with his little hammer, to “hear them”. Tac. He presses his ear to the bronze. Tac. I tell him: no hammers on my cannons. He says: sorry. Tac. In the end, we drink tea on the battlements, and he tells me which one rings truest. Always the seventh. He looks at it for a long time. I don't know why.
textes.Abdellah, c'est le meilleur tambour du s: Abdellah is the best drummer in the souk, and he doesn't know it. Tap-tap-tap all day long! He says I steal his rhythm. I say I take it travelling.
textes.Abdellah, mon beau-frère. Nos femmes son: Abdellah, my brother-in-law. Our wives are sisters, and they keep count for both of us: Hnia his hammer blows, Rabia my teapots. He's as touchy as a new tray, but his teapots are the best.
textes.Abdellah, mon voisin. Tac, tac, tac, tou: Abdellah, my neighbour. Tap, tap, tap, all day long. I can't hear myself guess. But when he stops, the souk is too quiet, and I start to worry.
textes.Abyssos ! J'ai une nouvelle version pour: Abyssos! I've got a new version for you!
textes.Abyssos ! J'ai une question pour tes rou: Abyssos! I've got a question for your scrolls!
textes.Abyssos ? Il archive chacune de mes erre: Abyssos? He's been archiving every one of my mistakes for nearly a thousand years. My successes, never. “That isn't history,” he says.
textes.Abyssos dit que la baleine parle au cris: Abyssos says the whale talks to the crystal. I asked him what it says. He searched for three days through all his scrolls, and then admitted he didn't know. It's the first time Abyssos hasn't known something! I wrote it on a pebble, so he'll remember.
textes.Abyssos m'a demandé d'archiver mes recet: Abyssos asked me to archive my recipes. I refused. Secrets aren't for writing down.
Abyssos receives my report every evening. He reads the whole thing, even though it's three words long. A serious man. A bit chatty, for a serious man.
textes.Abyssos sait tout sur tout, sauf ce qu'i: Abyssos knows everything about everything, except what's up there. So we're a team: I ask you the questions, and he writes down the answers.
textes.Abyssos veut tout écrire, même mes recet: Abyssos wants to write everything down, even my recipes. Secrets aren't written, they're handed on. He's sweet, but he's got a quill where his nose should be.
textes.Abyssos écrit l'histoire morte, moi je r: Abyssos writes dead history, I tell living history. He calls me a liar, I call him a scroll. We're fond of each other, deep down. Very deep down.
textes.Abyssos était le plus petit copiste du p: Abyssos was the smallest copyist in the palace, the night of the wave. A thousand years later, he still writes down everything I say. Even my sighs.
textes.Abyssos, tu as encore passé la nuit sous: Abyssos, you spent the night under my windows again.
textes.Abyssos. Si tu sors ta plume, je range m: Abyssos. If you get your quill out, I put my crackers away.
textes.Accomplir dix quêtes pour les habitants: Complete ten quests for the people of Port-Azur
textes.Accordée ! Enfin, mon violon. Moi, je su: In tune! Well, my violin is. I'm always a little out of tune myself. That's part of my charm.
textes.Accoster sur l'Île des Trois Soleils: Land on the Island of the Three Suns
textes.Accoster sur l'île des nains: Land on the island of the dwarves
textes.Accoster à Néopolis, sur le Quai des Dro: Land at Neopolis, on the Drone Quay
textes.Accroche-toi, j'ai le pied marin. Enfin,: Hold on tight, I've got sea legs. Well, all four of them.
textes.Accroché à la poignée… Attention au dépa: Hanging on to the handle… Watch out for the departure!
textes.Accueillir un jour un bateau entier de P: To welcome, one day, a whole boatful of Heavy-Feet, a hundred visitors at once! I'd give the full speech to each one. It would take seven hours. They'd all stay till the end. In my dream, they all stay.
textes.Achille Buvard, le poète du village, a v: Achille Buvard, the village poet, saw the pot of orange (no. 7) stuck right at the top of the Ink Waterfall, on the Lip (the edge of the cliff, where the water falls). He gets dizzy with heights and with rhymes.
textes.Achille Plumevent a demandé à atterrir s: Achille Plumevent asked to land on the Zéphyr. Denied. He flies so badly he'd have burst the envelope.
textes.Achille Plumevent vole au-dessus de la v: Achille Plumevent has been flying over the town for eight days. He can't manage to land. His sister throws him sandwiches.
textes.Achille Plumevent vole si haut, parfois,: Achille Plumevent sometimes flies so high I mistake him for a comet. A comet with a cough.
textes.Achille a décollé de mon aérodrome à neu: Achille took off from my airfield at twelve minutes past nine. The next day, he shouted down from the sky that he wanted to land on the Zéphyr. I grabbed the megaphone and shouted: “DENIED!” He flies so badly he'd have burst the envelope. Adèle was beside me. She didn't say anything. She just took my binoculars. I still feel a bit bad about it.
textes.Achille a toujours voulu voler. Petit, i: Achille always wanted to fly. As a boy, he jumped off the roof with umbrellas. Now he has wings and a boiler. Progress is terrifying.
textes.Achille dit que d'en haut, on voit tout: Achille says that from up there you can see everything: the shepherds' sheep, the boats of Tazira, the wreck at Carène. He even says he can see something shining in the middle of Stoneheart.
textes.Achille m'a écrit un poème sur une capuc: Achille wrote me a poem about a capucine. The flower. But I thought it was me. I married him. He never told me the truth, and I never told him I'd guessed it. We're very happy like that.
textes.Achille écrit des poèmes sur tout. Même: Achille writes poems about everything. Even about my shutters. He says they have “the melancholy of wood”. I say they need a second coat.
textes.Achille écrit sur tout, tache tout, oubl: Achille writes about everything, stains everything, forgets everything except my birthdays. He writes me a poem every year. They're all in a drawer. Some of them are even finished.
textes.Achille écrit un poème sur la Grande Ave: Achille is writing a poem about the Great Downpour. He's on page forty. He hasn't finished the first drop yet.
textes.Achille, tu as encore de l'encre sur le: Achille, you've got ink on your nose again.
textes.Achille, tu as fini ton poème ?: Achille, have you finished your poem?
textes.Achille, voici l'orange ! J'ai même gard: Achille, here's the orange! I even kept my feet dry.
textes.Achille, vous écrivez sur la cascade ?: Achille, are you writing about the waterfall?
textes.Achète un virus, le deuxième est OFFERT: Buy one virus, the second is FREE!
textes.Admirer la machine à bulles de Basile Bu: Admire Basile Bulle's bubble machine (Fair stand, west side)
textes.Admirez la maquette du Lisse-Center ! Qu: Admire the model of the Lisse-Center! Four hundred shops, two thousand parking spaces, and a fountain that plays our anthem every hour. The anthem lasts thirty-two seconds. It's optimised.
textes.Adèle ! J'ai un nouveau plan d'atterriss: Adèle! I've got a new landing plan.
textes.Adèle ! La prochaine bulle sera plus sol: Adèle! The next bubble will be sturdier!
textes.Adèle ! Une petite déclaration, pour dem: Adèle! A little statement, for tomorrow?
textes.Adèle a la patience d'un ciel couvert. E: Adèle has the patience of a cloudy sky. She waits without complaining. I watch over her brother at night: it's the only useful thing I know how to do for her.
textes.Adèle attend son frère depuis huit jours: Adèle has been waiting for her brother on a bench for eight days, and she forgets to eat. So I make two sandwiches: one for the sky, one for the ground. The ground one, I keep an eye on.
textes.Adèle attend son frère sur mon banc tous: Adèle waits for her brother on my bench every morning. I bring her a coffee and my binoculars. It's the least I can do: I was the one who said no.
textes.Adèle est arrivée dans les Serres il y a: Adèle came to the Greenhouses three years ago, a tiny little caterpillar. I fed her nasturtium leaves. One morning she came out of her cocoon, blue and white, and landed on my nose. Since then she's looked after the flowers in the second dome. She's my best colleague. She never takes a holiday.
textes.Adèle est la personne la plus courageuse: Adèle is the bravest person in Cliquetis. She's been waiting on a bench for eight days. I'm going to bring her brother back to her in a bubble, I promise.
textes.Adèle m'a promis qu'Achille me ferait fa: Adèle promised me Achille would take me for a ride in the sky. When he knows how to land. I asked when he'd know how to land. She looked up at the sky for a very long time. Then she said: “Soon.” I believe her. In the evening I save her half my gear biscuit, so she has the strength to keep waiting.
textes.Adèle m'en veut pour mes titres sur son: Adèle is cross with me about my headlines on her brother. I understand. But a whole city looks up every morning thanks to Achille. Somebody has to write it.
textes.Adèle, c'est ma copine du banc. Elle att: Adèle is my bench friend. She's waiting for her brother, I'm waiting for him to take me for a ride. We wait together, it's not so long that way.
textes.Affronter les jaguars du Mont Fumant, fa: To face the jaguars of Smoking Mountain, face to face, like a real jaguar. And come back with a story that even Tochtli couldn't sell.
textes.Agacé. En bas, quelqu'un a encore frappé: Annoyed. Down below, someone struck the Lid three times again. Up here, I'm the one who gets all the sauce first.
textes.Agacé. La machine à chocolat de Firmin a: Irritated. Firmin's chocolate machine whistled at four o'clock and three seconds. Three seconds! The whole Middle Town sets its watches by that whistle. I had to correct forty watches.
textes.Agacé. Les robots de Lisse viennent foui: Annoyed. Lisse's robots come rummaging through my Scrapyard to build themselves arms. They take my finest parts. They took my dragon's left wing. Now he flies crooked. In theory.
textes.Agacée. Une lettre de la Haute-Ville nou: Annoyed. A letter from the Upper Town asks us to make “a little less noise”. I replied that they could make a little less silence. That's where things stand.
textes.Agathe ! La Guilde est toujours aussi sé: Agathe! Is the Guild as serious as ever?
textes.Agathe a lu mon thé, une fois. Je ne veu: Agathe read my tea once. I don't want to know what she saw. She's dying to tell me. She smiles when she looks at me. I hate that smile.
textes.Agathe dit qu'elle voit l'avenir dans sa: Agathe says she sees the future in her crystal ball. The stones see the past. Together, we could know everything. That would be boring.
textes.Agathe et sa boule… Elle m'a promis la p: Agathe and her ball… She promised me the catch of the century, I reeled in a boot. That woman has an answer for everything. That's what annoys me. And what makes me laugh, too.
textes.Agathe lit l'avenir dans le thé. Je lui: Agathe reads the future in tea. I supply the tea. I don't know if she really sees, but she always tells people what they need. That's a kind of healing already.
textes.Agathe m'a lu l'avenir dans le thé. Elle: Agathe read my future in the tea leaves. She saw “a long life and lots of herbal tea”. That, I already knew.
textes.Agathe m'a prédit une grosse prise. J'ai: Agathe predicted a big catch for me. I caught a boot. She says it was a big boot.
Agathe doesn't talk much. I don't hear. We make an excellent team. For ten years, she wrote letters to the Burgomaster to get the Line reopened. I oiled the cabin. We finished on the same day.
textes.Agathe regarde demain. Les pierres regar: Agathe looks at tomorrow. The stones look at yesterday. We don't look the same way, she and I. She talks too much. But once, she said something I don't forget.
textes.Agathe, la Doyenne de la Guilde des Stra: Agathe, the Dean of the Strata Guild, and I have agreed on nothing for fifty years. Timetables, rules, noise. And yet, once a month, I go up for tea at the Guild. I bring the biscuits, she provides the tea. She says it's our peace treaty. I say it's for her biscuits… I mean, for her tea. She carried our planks, in secret, when we built the Bridge. I've never forgotten.
textes.Agathe, la voyante, m'a prédit une grand: Agathe, the seer, predicted a great discovery for me. The next day, I found my glasses. They were on my nose.
Agathe. No crystal ball near the stones.
textes.Agenouille-toi. … « Rê qui renais chaque: Kneel. … “Ra, who is reborn each morning, give this one back the strength of his day.” There. You are new, like the sun at dawn.
textes.Agitée. Je n'arrive pas à rester sur pla: Restless. I can't keep still. See? There, I'm moving.
textes.Agrafe ! Des bruitages dans le numéro de: Agrafe! Sound effects in tomorrow's issue?
textes.Agrafe ! Il y a une faute dans ta une !: Agrafe! There's a mistake on your front page!
textes.Agrafe ! Votre horoscope : une coquille: Agrafe! Your horoscope: a typo lies in wait for you.
textes.Agrafe et Pigment ont imprimé les affich: Agrafe and Pigment have printed the posters for the next Great Boucan. For the whole world to come, they must be taken to the other islands: to Paulo, in Port-Azur; to Ulric, the innkeeper of Montjoie; and to Tom the Fiddler, at the Crâne Fendu, on Balafre Island.
textes.Agrafe fait des jeux de mots dans tous s: Agrafe puts puns in all his headlines. I painted him a sign: “No puns allowed”. He wrote underneath: “That leaves me speechless… and pun-ished.” He's hopeless.
textes.Agrafe imprime mes affiches et me tortur: Agrafe prints my posters and tortures me with his puns. I've never laughed at a single one. I've never rubbed one out either.
textes.Agrafe imprime mon zine gratuitement. Il: Agrafe prints my zine for free. He makes mistakes in his own. I correct them with a red pencil. He says I remind him of someone. He won't say who.
Agrafe publishes my pigeon horoscope. He sighs as he proofreads it. But he's never dropped it. Well, once. He got forty letters.
textes.Agrafe écrit, je lis. Avec des bruitages: Agrafe writes, I read. With sound effects. His articles become radio plays on air. Sometimes he makes typos. They're my favourites.
textes.Ah ! Asseyez-vous, j'ai une réponse de t: Ah! Sit down, I have a three-hour answer.
textes.Ah ! Assieds-toi. Regarde le mur : chaqu: Ah! Sit down. Look at the wall: every little star there is a hole I made by hand. You have good taste. Tea first, and then I'll light the most beautiful one for you.
textes.Ah ! C'est moi qui goûte avant, toujours: Ah! I always taste first. So you'll be my second. The second is safer. Except when the potion kicks in late.
Ah! They were bored, the poor things.
textes.Ah ! Enfin ! Donnez-moi votre main. Atte: Ah! At last! Give me your hand. Wait, let me wipe mine, I've got grease on it. There. You and I are on the same side of science.
textes.Ah ! Enfin ! Quelqu'un ! Viens, je te ra: Ah! At last! Someone! Come, I'll tell you once more, with all the details. It was hot…
textes.Ah ! Enfin ! Une personne raisonnable !: Ah! At last! A reasonable person! Legends are memories that have lost their papers, you see. You just have to give them back.
textes.Ah ! Enfin ! Viens ce soir, sur la place: Ah! At last! Come tonight, to the square. I'll play you a fast rhythm, very fast. We'll see if you can keep up. Mixtli never has.
textes.Ah ! Enfin quelqu'un ! On devrait fonder: Ah! Finally, someone! We should start a club. We'd have meetings… well, we'd miss the meetings, but we'd be together.
textes.Ah ! Enfin quelqu'un de normal ! Approch: Ah! Finally someone normal! Come closer, look at these shiny eyes. I'll save you a Friday portion. Don't tell my daughter, she'd be jealous, and she still wouldn't eat it.
textes.Ah ! Enfin quelqu'un de raisonnable ! Je: Ah! At last, a reasonable person! I'll introduce you to Clémentine. Tonight, if the sky is clear. She'll be delighted.
textes.Ah ! Enfin quelqu'un qui comprend ! Écou: Ah! Finally someone who understands! Listen closely, just for you: SARDIIIIIINES! … There. You can go and tell Hamid.
textes.Ah ! Enfin quelqu'un qui l'avoue sans ro: Ah! Finally someone who admits it without blushing. You're quite right. The world would be gentler if we read more kisses in the rain and fewer newspapers.
textes.Ah ! Enfin une personne bien élevée. Vou: Ah! At last, a well-mannered person. You restore my faith in the archipelago. If you wish, I shall lend you a doormat. I collect them.
textes.Ah ! Excellente question ! Je vous répon: Ah! Excellent question! I'll answer in four minutes. (He takes a breath.) Right. In the name of the Council, the Elder, the Spire, the bridges, the domes and the planets of the fountain... Well, I can see from your face that you prefer the short version. Tradition says three things. One: have Ecliptic, the head of protocol, put you in the visitors' register, at the Council Hall, at the foot of the Spire. Two: taste Gloubi's stellar tea, at the Nebula Café, on the Agora. Three: go and greet Elder Astrée. After that, you'll no longer be a mere Heavyfoot. You'll be an official Heavyfoot. That's much better. There's a badge.
textes.Ah ! Je le savais ! Alors parle-leur gen: Ah! I knew it! Then talk to them nicely. They remember everything, especially compliments.
Ah! The friend of passing time. Come in.
textes.Ah ! L'ennemi des sept mers ! T'as chang: Ah! The enemy of the seven seas! Changed your mind? No? Too bad. I still like you.
textes.Ah ! La famille ! Un peu, la première fo: Ah! Family! A bit, the first time… and then it passes? Good, good. Maybe one day I'll try. On a day when the sea is very flat.
textes.Ah ! Le pain ! Sans pain, la bouillabais: Ah! The bread! Without bread, the bouillabaisse is an orphan. Grazie mille!
textes.Ah ! Le pain d'Honorine ! (Elle le renif: Ah! Honorine's bread! (She sniffs it, delighted.) It smells of morning. Thank you, my chick. Sit down, you've come all this way… No? You still have two loaves? Then at least take a slice for the road. Eat!
textes.Ah ! Le parfum ! Tiens, trois punchs, et: Ah! That smell! Here, three punches, and a few coins. At the Perroquet, you're at home.
textes.Ah ! Le pêcheur ! Ma vieille canne te va: Ah! The angler! My old rod suits you like a glove, {surnom}. Are they biting?
textes.Ah ! Le voilà, notre soliste !: Ah! Here it comes, our soloist!
textes.Ah ! Les fêtes de village, les meilleure: Ah! Village parties, the best ones. A string of lights, a squeaky fiddle, old folks dancing badly. I was probably one of those old folks. Maybe even at yours.
textes.Ah ! Merci, Gunnar. Que ferais-je sans t: Ah! Thank you, Gunnar. What would I do without you?
Ah! Thank you. I'll sleep well.
textes.Ah ! Mon client ! Assieds-toi, assieds-t: Ah! My customer! Sit down, sit down.
textes.Ah ! Mon frère ! Mon vrai frère ! Assied: Ah! Brother! My true brother! Sit down, we'll haggle all afternoon. For the fun of it. I may not sell you anything, but what fun!
textes.Ah ! Mon visiteur préféré ! Regardez cel: Ah! My favourite visitor! Look at that one, it's square!
textes.Ah ! Splendid ! Un aventurier, je le voi: Ah! Splendid! An adventurer, I can tell by your boots. Lord Archibald Pemberton, collector of curiosities. Do you have anything extraordinary to sell me, old bean?
textes.Ah ! Toi aussi ? Ça me rassure, tu peux: Oh! You too? You have no idea how much better that makes me feel. We should start a club. Nobody would talk. It would be very peaceful.
Ah! Ulfa is calling me. Royally.
textes.Ah ! Un adversaire ! Très bien. Mais je: Ah! An opponent! Very well. But I'm warning you: I haggled with a bumblebee the day I was born, and I won.
textes.Ah ! Un amateur ! Gravier me donne parfo: Ah! A connoisseur! Gravier sometimes gives me mackerel. I'll make you one on a Friday. Paulo, in Port-Azur, says his is the best. We'll see.
textes.Ah ! Un assistant ! Tu tombes à pic. App: Ah! An assistant! Just in time. Press the red button over there. No, not that one. The other one. There.
textes.Ah ! Un chercheur. Tu ouvres toutes les: Ah! A seeker. You open every box, don't you? Careful: some answers are much smaller than their questions.
textes.Ah ! Un classique ! « Ô toi, voyageur au: Ah! A classicist! “O thou, traveller with dusty shoes, who lovest rhymes… and… and…” (He searches.) I'll finish it for you later.
textes.Ah ! Un client ! Monsieur Prosper, march: Ah! A customer! Monsieur Prosper, house merchant! I have an EXCEPTIONAL deal for you: the Wisteria Cottage, in the Upper Town! A palace! A dream! A house with a roof! Almost whole! Only three hundred coins!
textes.Ah ! Un collectionneur ! Tu vas adorer m: Ah! A collector! You're going to love my shop. Snow globe, authentic shell, postcard signed by yours truly… For you, friend's price. Well, almost friend's price.
textes.Ah ! Un cœur tendre ! Assieds-toi à côté: Ah! A tender heart! Sit next to Master Hugues. You can share a handkerchief. He has big ones.
textes.Ah ! Un enfant du soleil. Viens t'asseoi: Ah! A child of the sun. Come and sit by my sunflowers — they turn their heads towards people like you.
textes.Ah ! Un esprit libre ! Les pigeons aussi: Ah! A free spirit! Pigeons choose their path too. Well, they follow the bread. But following the bread is a choice.
textes.Ah ! Un estomac d'en haut ! Approche, mo: Ah! A stomach from up top! Come closer, my pebble, come closer. Granny Gamelle, of the Free Canteen. Here we all eat at the same table, we pay what we can, and nobody leaves hungry. It's the only rule the Assembly never dared vote on. It was here first.
textes.Ah ! Un estomac nouveau ! Entre, entre !: Ah! A new stomach! Come in, come in! Lentille, cook at the Pay-What-You-Can Canteen. Here, you pay what you can: zero, one coin, ten coins. Those who have a lot pay for those who have nothing, and everybody eats. And everybody has seconds.
textes.Ah ! Un frère de cordes ! Tu vois, c'est: Ah! A brother of the strings! You see, it's the only way. The only problem is that after a hundred years, the song gets a bit long.
textes.Ah ! Un futur chevalier, je le vois à to: Ah! A future knight, I can see it in your eyes! Do you want to become my squire?
textes.Ah ! Un modèle ! Ne bouge plus ! Tu veux: Ah! A model! Hold still! Would you pose for me? Choose your pose!
textes.Ah ! Un nouveau venu plein de bonne volo: Ah! A newcomer full of good will! Start by making the rounds: say hello to Odette at the harbour office, Edmond at the hotel and Toni at the Perroquet Bleu. Tell them the mayor sent you. Then come back and see me.
textes.Ah ! Un nouvel élève ? Non ? Un visiteur: Ah! A new pupil? No? A visitor. It's almost the same thing: a visitor is a pupil who doesn't know it yet. Professor Malachar, headmaster of the Infernal Academy. Three centuries of teaching, forty thousand papers marked, and not a single feather lost. From my wings, that is.
textes.Ah ! Un oiseau de nuit ! Tu es chez toi,: Ah! A night owl! You're at home here. The Perroquet is open until one. After that, there are the stars, but they don't serve drinks.
textes.Ah ! Un pointeur ! Un vrai ! Viens là qu: Ah! A pointer! A real one! Come here and let me shake your hand. Pointing is an art: you look, you breathe, you bend your knees. Shooters just throw and pray.
textes.Ah ! Un public ! Entrez, entrez : le ven: Ah! An audience! Come in, come in: the wind is in a musical mood today. It's only waiting for its conductor. That's me.
textes.Ah ! Un témoin ! Parfait. Professeure Fu: Ah! A witness! Perfect. Professor Fusilli, theologian of the Church and scholar. I measure the Great Flying Spaghetti. One hundred and twelve noodles long, two meatballs, two eyes. Give or take a noodle. Science is categorical.
textes.Ah ! Un visiteur ! Amenemhat, maître scr: Ah! A visitor! Amenemhat, master scribe of the House of Life. I can read seven hundred signs, write six hundred and ninety-eight, and I make up the two that are missing. Can you read? No? Never mind. I'll do the talking.
textes.Ah ! Un visiteur ! Bienvenue à Port-Cout: Ah! A visitor! Welcome to Port-Coutelas, a free, prosperous and orderly city! I am Governor Lagrange. If you have any complaints, write them down. I won't read them, but do write them down.
textes.Ah ! Un visiteur aux pieds pas en pierre: Ah! A visitor whose feet aren't made of stone. Sit down. Do you want to know the legend of the Great Moai? Everybody knows it here. But nobody listens to the end. They all fall asleep.
textes.Ah ! Un vrai ! Viens que je t'embrasse !: Ah! A true one! Come here and let me hug you! For you, double rouille and a chilli from the hill. If you cry, it means it's good.
textes.Ah ! Un vrai. Tu peux venir à l'Arcade q: Ah! A real one. You can come to the Arcade whenever you like. I'll lend you MY stool.
textes.Ah ! Une main verte ! Je le voyais à tes: Ah! Green fingers! I could see it in your nails. Come and help me with the flowerbeds one day. My peppers like people who talk to them gently.
textes.Ah ! Vous arrivez un peu tard : le Zéphy: Ah! You're a little late: the Zéphyr has been flying for thirteen years. And so has Achille Plumevent, but he forgot to invent the landing. Invent that, then. The whole city will be grateful. Adèle most of all.
textes.Ah ! Vous êtes à l'heure. J'aime les gen: Ah! You're on time. I like people who are on time.
textes.Ah ! {surnom} ! Je l'annonçais justement: Ah! {surnom}! I was just announcing it on air: “Our friend is strolling along the quays.” And it was true! Live radio is magic.
textes.Ah ! … Pardon, je ne devrais pas être so: Ah! … Sorry, I shouldn't be relieved. But I am. Welcome to the club, {surnom}. There are lots of us. Well… mostly me.
Ah! … Why? I haven't done anything to you.
textes.Ah ? Je le lui dirai, ça lui fera plaisi: Oh? I'll pass that on, it'll make their day.
textes.Ah ? Je n'avais pas remarqué. Je regarde: Oh? I hadn't noticed. I'll look more closely.
textes.Ah ? Laquelle ? La grosse ?: Oh? Which one? The big one?
textes.Ah Kin ! Demain, c'est un bon jour ? Bon: Ah Kin! Is tomorrow a good day? Good for whom?
textes.Ah Kin ! Tu dormais, tout à l'heure ?: Ah Kin! Were you asleep earlier?
textes.Ah Kin ! Une partie ? C'est moi qui comp: Ah Kin! A game? I'm counting, this time.
textes.Ah Kin Pech compte les jours, les lunes: Ah Kin Pech counts days, moons and years better than anyone. He often falls asleep over his calculations. When he's wrong, it's by one day. But one day, for a temple, is a long time.
textes.Ah Kin Pech compte les étoiles sans se t: Ah Kin Pech counts the stars without a mistake, but he counts my beans wrong. Always one short. Always in his favour. He calls it a lunar error. I call it a habit.
textes.Ah Kin Pech compte tout : les jours, les: Ah Kin Pech counts everything: the days, the stars, my defeats. He says I'm the one who took the ball on the head. We took the same one. He just shouted louder.
textes.Ah Kin Pech compte tout, même les points: Ah Kin Pech counts everything, even the points at knucklebones. Especially the points at knucklebones. He always wins. I suspect him of counting with the stars. But he's my oldest friend, so I lose with pleasure.
textes.Ah Kin Pech dort à l'observatoire. Je l': Ah Kin Pech sleeps at the observatory. I saw him! He snores at the stars!
textes.Ah Kin Pech et moi, on joue aux osselets: Ah Kin Pech and I play knucklebones in the evening. He keeps the score, so he always wins.
textes.Ah Kin Pech passe ses nuits à l'observat: Ah Kin Pech spends his nights at the observatory. He says he counts the stars. I think he often sleeps, his head on his calculations.
textes.Ah Kin Pech sait tout sur les étoiles, e: Ah Kin Pech knows everything about the stars, and he snores at the observatory! I've seen him! When he's asleep, I look at his tables, the dots and the bars. I can already count up to nineteen. Shh.
textes.Ah Kin. L'équinoxe, cette année : demain: Ah Kin. The equinox this year: tomorrow?
textes.Ah bon ? C'est facile ! Tu prends un sea: Really? It's easy! You take a bucket, put in wet sand, pat it, turn it over. If it breaks, never mind, you say it's ruins.
textes.Ah bon ? Et t'as eu peur ? Moi, je n'ai: Really? And were you scared? I'm never scared. Well, almost never. If you ever get lost here, follow the glowing mushrooms! I'm the one who discovered that!
textes.Ah bon ? Même pas un peu ? Moi aussi, je: Really? Not even a bit? I used to think that too. And then I ate Mustapha's sardines. Wait till you taste them, you'll see.
textes.Ah bon ? Quelle tristesse. Une bière pou: Really? How sad. A fizz to cheer you up?
Oh no! No more cheap programs. Now Mr. Fil sells programs checked by Glitch. She hasn't checked any yet… so I'm not selling any. Honest business is very restful.
textes.Ah non ! Pas celui-là. Il est à vendre,: Oh no! Not that one. It's for sale, yes, but… not today. Nor tomorrow, for that matter.
textes.Ah non ! Pas déjà ! … Bon, d'accord, t'a: Oh no! Already?! … Okay, fine, you win. Here's your prize.
textes.Ah non, mes prix sont déjà doux comme la: Oh no, my prices are already as gentle as the sea in August.
textes.Ah ouais ? Défi ! Rendez-vous au Bassin: Oh yeah? Challenge! Meet me at the Dry Dock! First one to fall loses! … Well, the second one, because I always fall first.
Oh yeah? … Phew. I feel less silly. I've got three hundred crates with names. Want me to introduce you? Not all of them. The nicest ones.
textes.Ah oui ? Alors montre-moi le pas du crab: Oh yeah? Then show me the crab step. … Hmm. Not bad! Still a bit stiff in the knees. One class and you'll be ahead of the cat.
textes.Ah oui ? Alors pourquoi tes genoux sont: Oh yes? Then why are your knees all green?
textes.Ah oui ? … Bon. Alors c'est que c'est im: Have I? … Right. Then it must be important. I've been nodding my head for an hour, I can't remember who I've asked. Drink anyway.
textes.Ah oui, c'est vrai ! Il y a des noirs ge: Oh yes, that's true! There are nice darks, like the one we sleep in, and nasty darks, like under the brambles. You really think things through.
Ah, well… Three coins, and I'll look.
textes.Ah, CE genou ! Il est presque guéri, je: Oh, THAT knee! It's almost healed, I swear.
textes.Ah, Cardamome… Assieds-toi. C'est une lo: Ah, Cardamome… Sit down. It's a long story.
textes.Ah, Margot ! Tu as fini tes calculs ?: Ah, Margot! Have you finished your calculations?
textes.Ah, bonjour ! Belle journée, n'est-ce pa: Ah, hello! Lovely day, isn't it?
textes.Ah, bonjour ! Ne fais pas attention au b: Oh, hello! Don't mind the noise: there are a hundred clocks in here, and they've all got something to say.
textes.Ah, c'est toi ! Entre, entre. Excuse le: Ah, it's you! Come in, come in. Excuse the mess, I wasn't expecting company.
textes.Ah, c'est toi ! Entre, entre. Mets-toi à: Ah, it's you! Come in, come in. Make yourself at home, we're all friends here.
textes.Ah, c'est toi ! Merci de m'avoir réveill: Ah, it's you! Thanks for waking me up. I missed everything: the feast of the year 1300, the feast of the year 1400… Well. I'll take a little nap to recover.
textes.Ah, c'est toi ? Merci ! J'allais rater…: Ah, it's you? Thanks! I was about to miss… my afternoon nap. Well. Good night.
textes.Ah, c'est toi. Tu ne viendrais pas avec: Ah, it's you. You wouldn't happen to be bringing wood, would you?
textes.Ah, c'est vous. Toujours pas de rouage,: Ah, it's you. Still no cogwheel, I suppose.
textes.Ah, celles-là… Elles sont à moi. Je croi: Ah, those ones… They're mine. I think.
textes.Ah, celui pour qui tout se vend ! J'ai p: Ah, the one for whom everything's for sale! I thought of you. I've got a lot of three-legged chairs. Interested?
Ah, that one. It says hello.
textes.Ah, confrère ! Vous avez fait sauter aut: Ah, colleague! Have you blown anything else up since? No? It's never too late to reoffend.
textes.Ah, de l'aide ? Il y a trois cagettes à: Oh, some help? There are three crates to sort, and the cat isn't helping at all.
textes.Ah, de la visite ! Assieds-toi sur un sa: Ah, a visitor! Sit yourself down on a sack, they're softer than they look.
textes.Ah, de la visite ! Entre, entre, mais ma: Ah, a visitor! Come in, come in, but tread softly: they hear everything.
textes.Ah, de la visite ! Le café est fermé, ma: Ah, company! The café's closed, but not to friends. Fancy the last drop of cloud milk?
textes.Ah, de la visite ! Tu as vu ma petite-fi: Ah, company! Have you seen my granddaughter? A natural. In my day, we had no model: we practised on the wardrobe.
textes.Ah, de la visite ! Tu as vu mon petit-fi: Ah, company! Have you seen my grandson? A natural. In my day, we had no model: we practised on the wardrobe.
textes.Ah, de la visite ! Tu danses ? Ce piano: Ah, a visitor! Do you dance? This piano has played all by itself ever since my husband won it in the Liftkeepers' raffle.
textes.Ah, et si tu as une graine de là-haut da: Oh, and if you've got a seed from up there in your pocket, save it for me. Even a tiny one. I'll find it a lamp.
textes.Ah, l'amateur d'oiseaux de mer ! Une par: Ah, the seabird lover! A portion of tajine is waiting for you. On Friday, if the sea bream agree.
textes.Ah, l'amateur de coquillages. Si Victor: Ah, the shell lover. If Victor sells you an “authentic” one, bring it to me. I'll tell you whether it smells of paint.
Ah, the fine-weather friend! It's sunny. You must be happy. Me, I'm bored.
textes.Ah, l'aventurier ! Vous savez, j'ai fait: Ah, the adventurer! You know, I took some very nice photos of the lighthouse.
textes.Ah, l'aventurier en personne ! Alors, le: Ah, the adventurer in person! So, how's the big wide world?
textes.Ah, l'invincible ! Tu as toujours ton po: Ah, the invincible one! Still got your jar of seaweed? The invincible need it more than anyone.
textes.Ah, la carte de ma jeunesse ! Il y avait: Ah, the map of my youth! There was one more island back then.
textes.Ah, la personne qui ne corne jamais. Bon: Ah, the person who never dog-ears. Good day. The books greet you. Yes, yes: they don't rustle for just anyone.
Ah, greenhouse rain! They love it.
textes.Ah, la technique de Momo ! On ne se couc: Ah, the Momo technique! Don't go to bed, head straight out. Works once. The second time, you sleep at the bottom of the boat.
textes.Ah, le coureur ! Fontaine-phare, tu conn: Ah, the runner! Fountain to lighthouse, you know the way. Me, I know my time. Well… I used to.
textes.Ah, le diplomate ! « Les deux », tu disa: Ah, the diplomat! “Both,” you said. Raymond heard about it. He smiled. First time in years.
textes.Ah, le lève-tôt ! Tu as vu le soleil se: Ah, the early bird! Did you see the sun rise this morning? Tell me about it. I've never seen it.
textes.Ah, le petit malin qui croit à la triche: Ah, the little smart one who believes in cheating! I've got my eye on you, my friend. You've got a sharp eye too. That's worrying.
textes.Ah, le renifleur ! Vas-y, sens. Ça sent: Ah, the sniffer! Go on, smell. Smells of the sea, yes or no? Right. Not in front of the sergeant.
textes.Ah, les abeilles de chez toi ont un dard: Ah, the bees where you come from have a sting! Mine don't. Come and see them: they'll tickle you, that's all. You'll forgive them for the others.
textes.Ah, les gens… Demande, je te dirai ce qu: Ah, people… Ask away, I'll tell you what I know.
textes.Ah, les gens… Demandez, je vous dirai ce: Ah, people… Ask away, I'll tell you what I know.
textes.Ah, les meilleurs. Ceux qui dansent deda: Ah, the best kind. People who dance inside hear everything, even the silence between two kicks. Stay close to the sound: one day, it'll come out.
textes.Ah, merci ! Enfin quelqu'un d'honnête !: Ah, thank you! Finally someone honest! Hapou plays the hero, Néferet prays, and I tremble. Come and tremble with me, it's good company.
textes.Ah, mon ami ! Du nouveau sous la mer ?: Ah, my friend! Any news from under the sea?
textes.Ah, mon ami des choses utiles ! J'ai enc: Ah, my friend of useful things! I tried to blow a useful bubble again this morning. It burst out laughing.
textes.Ah, mon ami en avance ! Trente secondes: Ah, my early friend! Thirty seconds today, by my eye. That's reasonable. Keep it up.
textes.Ah, mon cher {surnom}. Asseyez-vous. Pas: Ah, my dear {surnom}. Do sit down. Not there, that's a crystal. Nor there, that's my lunch. I no longer know from which day.
textes.Ah, mon chou ! Assieds-toi. Je te sers ?: Ah, my sweet! Sit down. Shall I serve you? You look like a traveller in need of a tart.
textes.Ah, mon citoyen exigeant ! Votre doléanc: Ah, my demanding citizen! Your complaint has arrived safely. Well, it will arrive, once you've written it.
textes.Ah, mon citoyen satisfait ! Votre répons: Ah, my satisfied citizen! Your answer is framed on my veranda, between two decrees. In the place of honour.
textes.Ah, mon client au lit carré ! Votre cham: Ah, my neat-and-square guest! Your room is reserved at the guesthouse. It doesn't exist yet, but it's reserved.
textes.Ah, mon client fidèle ! J'ai mis de côté: Ah, my loyal customer! I've put aside a lovely cheese for you.
textes.Ah, mon client honnête ! Ta place est to: Ah, my honest customer! Your seat is still warm. People like you, I've got two: you and Tonneau.
textes.Ah, mon client préféré ! Qu'est-ce que t: Ah, my favourite customer! What are you bringing me? What are you taking away?
textes.Ah, mon client préféré ! Tu m'apportes d: Ah, my favourite customer! Are you bringing me fish or buying some?
textes.Ah, mon client préféré ! Une pincée de s: Ah, my favourite customer! A pinch of saffron?
textes.Ah, mon client raisonnable ! Votre place: Ah, my reasonable customer! Your parking space number one is still waiting for you. At the back.
textes.Ah, mon enfant… Tu l'as remarqué, toi au: Ah, my child… You've noticed it too. For a week now, he's been sulking. His noodles are drooping, his eyes are half closed, and Mount Bolognese is rumbling. I searched the old books, and I found the recipe: the Dish of the Great Reconciliation. Fresh pasta from Mamma Lasagna, a ladleful of the sacred sauce from the Cooking Pot, and parmesan grated with the Golden Grater. The Golden Grater… Captain Rigatoni had it. He says he lost it. Me, I think he buried it. Will you help me? I can't leave the temple: if the Great Spaghetti opens an eye, someone has to smile at him.
textes.Ah, mon frère du safran ! J'en ai mis un: Ah, my saffron brother! I put an extra pinch in your portion. Not two, I'm not rich.
textes.Ah, mon gourmet ! Une table au soleil ?: Ah, my gourmet! A table in the sun?
textes.Ah, mon marcheur ! Tu as marché jusqu'ic: Ah, my walker! Did you walk all the way here? How long did that take? Me, four seconds.
textes.Ah, mon petit égaré ! Tu t'es encore per: Ah, my little wanderer! Have you got lost again since? Tell me where, I'll write it down on a shell.
textes.Ah, mon petit… C'est la Grande Averse. I: Ah, my little one… It's the Great Downpour. Ten days ago, a pure white cloud came from the sea, and it rained clear water. So clear that it washed the colours off everything: the leaves, the grass, the pond, our houses. We were asleep under our roofs, so we kept ours. But the Stone Palette overflowed, and the nine paint pots went off with the water. Without them, the island is just a colouring-book page. Here: this is the island's Brush, the elders' brush. It only paints with the colours of the Palette. And start with the pulley basket, under the Council terrace: Gaspard swears he heard a “plop”, the night of the Downpour. Me, I no longer have the strength to haul it up.
textes.Ah, mon supporter ! Viens voir, je vais: Ah, my supporter! Come and watch, I'm going to point. And if Raymond objects, you're my witness.
textes.Ah, mon terrien ! La mer est calme, ne t: Ah, my landlubber! The sea's calm, don't worry. If it rolls, look at the lighthouse. That usually works.
textes.Ah, mon visiteur ! Vous avez encore vos: Ah, my visitor! You've still got your eyebrows? Well done!
textes.Ah, mon {surnom} ! J'ai reçu des nouveau: Ah, my {surnom}! I've got some new arrivals. All guaranteed. Guaranteed what? Guaranteed… new.
textes.Ah, mon étal ! Regarde, sens, goûte… enf: Ah, my stall! Look, smell, taste… well, pay first.
textes.Ah, notre arbitre ! Depuis ta visite, on: Ah, our referee! Since your visit, we don't argue anymore. Well, hardly anymore. Yesterday it was about the spoons.
textes.Ah, notre visiteur ! Comment trouvez-vou: Ah, our visitor! How do you like our little town?
textes.Ah, quelqu'un qui écoute ! C'est rare et: Ah, someone who listens! That's rare and precious, around here. Sit by the counter, I'll tell you everything people say. I know everything. I repeat nothing. Almost nothing.
textes.Ah, te voilà ! Viens par ici, on m'a rac: Ah, there you are! Come over here, I've been hearing things.
textes.Ah, toi ! Tu as faim ? Moi j'ai toujours: Ah, you! Are you hungry? I'm always hungry, it comes with the job.
textes.Ah, toi qui es toujours pile à l'heure !: Ah, you who are always right on time! Good timing, it's time. I think. I've never been able to tell the time.
textes.Ah, toi qui n'as jamais eu de brûlure !: Ah, you who've never had a burn! Still not a mark on you? Come to the Duelling Ground, we'll fix that. Gently.
textes.Ah, toi. Assieds-toi si tu veux, mais ne: Ah, you. Sit down if you like, but don't step on the canvas.
textes.Ah, toi. Tu n'aurais pas du bois ?: Ah, you. You wouldn't happen to have any wood?
textes.Ah, un client de la maison ! Le café est: Ah, one of the regulars! The coffee's hot, the Bielle is under pressure. The usual?
textes.Ah, un curieux ! Donne ta main… Je vois: Ah, a curious one! Give me your hand… I see a road, water, lots of people waiting for you. And a soup at Paulo's. That one's certain: everyone ends up at Paulo's.
textes.Ah, un habitué ! J'ai une nouvelle potio: Ah, a regular! I have a new potion. It's blue. I don't know yet what it does. Would you like to try it? No? Wise.
textes.Ah, un habitué ! Le hamac du fond est li: Ah, a regular! The hammock at the back is free, if you like.
textes.Ah, un jeunot ! Nonno Tortellini, paysan: Ah, a youngster! Nonno Tortellini, farmer. All the wheat on the island, that's me. Durum wheat, hard wheat, the best. Know why they call it “hard”? Because you've got to be hard to grow it. Heh heh heh.
textes.Ah, un passager ! Ne touche pas au porte: Ah, a passenger! Don't touch the speaking tube, it goes to the kitchen: last time, we ordered forty pancakes.
textes.Ah, un sportif ! Ça se voit tout de suit: Ah, an athlete! I can tell right away. A little set of push-ups?
textes.Ah, un visiteur ! Attention au balancier: Ah, a visitor! Mind the pendulum, it swings very close. And don't whistle: the great wheel thinks you're calling it.
textes.Ah, un visiteur ! Pardon, je ne t'avais: Ah, a visitor! Sorry, I didn't see you: I was looking at Venus. She's there, right there… No? Oh well. Ah Kin Pech, astronomer. I count the days, the moons, the years, and sometimes my hairs.
textes.Ah, un visiteur ! Tu peux monter à la co: Ah, a visitor! You can go up to the dome by the stairs: the great telescope is waiting for you. Don't touch the planets, they're set just so.
textes.Ah, un visiteur ! Tu veux savoir le secr: Ah, a visitor! Want to know the secret of ships in bottles? You put them in lying down, and pull the thread. Want to try?
textes.Ah, un voyageur ! Bienvenue à La Rose de: Ah, a traveller! Welcome to La Rose des Vents. Books, sea charts, and a bookseller who adores stories. Where are you from?
textes.Ah, un voyageur ! Dites-moi, c'est pour: Ah, a traveller! Tell me, it's for my map: where exactly do you come from?
textes.Ah, une vraie ! Les gens du soir, c'est: Ah, a real one! Night people are my family. We recognise each other by the bags under our eyes. Come and dance — we'll rest when the sea runs dry.
textes.Ah, voilà mon lève-tard ! Il reste des m: Ah, here's my late riser! There are some crumbs left, I think. Mochi! Leave some crumbs!
textes.Ah, voilà mon troqueur ! Toujours pas de: Ah, here's my swapper! Still no goat? The day you get one, I'll explain coins to you.
textes.Ah, voilà notre gagnant ! Tu viens rajou: Ah, here's our winner! Come to add a line to the record board? I've kept some paint.
textes.Ah, vous ! J'ai eu une idée ! … Non. Ell: Ah, you! I've had an idea! … No. It already exists.
textes.Ah, vous ! Le seul qui croie au toujours: Ah, it's you! The only one who believes in forever. Come and see the engine. It's turning. Well, it intends to turn.
textes.Ah, vous ! Vous avez vu mon moteur ? Il: Ah, you! Have you seen my engine? It's running. Well, it's running better than yesterday.
textes.Ah, vous ! Vous tombez à pic : j'ai trou: Ah, you! Perfect timing: I've found a new star. Well, it was a firefly. But it was shining nicely.
textes.Ah, vous qui ne voulez pas de photo. Je: Ah, you're the one who doesn't want photos. I'll just look at you, then. With my eyes only. Is that allowed?
textes.Ah, vous voilà ! Venez par ici, on m'a r: Ah, there you are! Come over here, I've been hearing things.
textes.Ah, vous, de la nuit ! Ce soir, ciel cla: Ah, you, the night person! Clear sky tonight. Come up to the Observatory, I'll have tea and a stool.
textes.Ah, vous. Bon. Qu'est-ce qui vous amène: Ah, you. Right. What brings you here?
textes.Ah, vous. Encore une grosse pièce, je pa: Ah, you. Another big coin, I bet? I've kept change aside for you. On purpose. A whole drawerful.
textes.Ah, vous. Le lait. Je vous l'ai caché de: Ah, you. The milk. I've hidden it for you behind the sugar bowl, so nobody sees. You'll be the death of me.
Ah, {surnom}! Bernadette recognises you. Yes, yes: she let out a little puff of steam when you arrived. She only does that for people she likes. And for Honorine.
textes.Ah, {surnom} ! Entre, entre. Enfin, mont: Ah, {surnom}! Come in, come in. Well, come up. You're already up. Right.
textes.Ah, {surnom} ! J'ai ouvert une page rien: Ah, {surnom}! I've started a page just for you in my Big Notebook. It's called “What {surnom} told me”. It's almost full. You'll have to slow down, or I'll have to buy another notebook.
textes.Ah, {surnom} ! Le pain est tout chaud, c: Ah, {surnom}! The bread's nice and warm, as always.
textes.Ah, {surnom} ! Ta place est chaude. Un g: Ah, {surnom}! Your seat's still warm. A grog?
Ah, {surnom}! Your nose looks in good shape. So does mine: I can smell you're about to buy something.
textes.Ah, {surnom} ! Toujours ravi de voir une: Ah, {surnom}! Always a delight to see a full purse. Sorry: a friend.
textes.Ah, {surnom} ! Tu as faim ? J'ai toujour: Ah, {surnom}! Hungry? I've always got a bit of stew left.
textes.Ah, {surnom} ! Tu descends si souvent qu: Ah, {surnom}! You come down so often the cabin knows your weight. It went “ding” before you even arrived. Well, I think so. I felt it in my feet.
textes.Ah, {surnom} ! Tu viens si souvent que l: Ah, {surnom}! You come so often the steam hammer slowed down when it saw you. That's its way of saying hello. It only does that for me. And for Honorine, when she brings the soup.
textes.Ah, {surnom} ! Viens voir, j'ai redessin: Ah, {surnom}! Come and see, I've redrawn the misty coast. It moves, I swear it moves.
textes.Ah, {surnom} ! Vous tombez bien, j'ai be: Ah, {surnom}! Perfect timing, I need a fresh pair of eyes. Mine have seen too many gears.
textes.Ah, {surnom} ! Vous… tu as vu quelque ch: Ah, {surnom}! Have you… have you seen anything interesting? A cove, a rock, a treasure?
textes.Ah, {surnom}, mon meilleur client ! Qu'e: Ah, {surnom}, my best customer! What have you brought me?
textes.Ah, {surnom}. (Elle vérifie que sa veste: Ah, {surnom}. (She checks that her jacket is properly buttoned.) I've put you in the “Pleasant Visitors” file. It's very thin. You're at the top.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Asseyez-vous près de moi,: Ah, {surnom}. Sit beside me, on the bench. Don't say anything. … There. Do you hear that silence? That's the Trench breathing. I only let friends listen to it.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Asseyez-vous. Je ne dirai: Ah, {surnom}. Sit down. I won't say anything for a minute. It's my way of being glad to see you. You'll find it very restful.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Assieds-toi un instant prè: Ah, {surnom}. Sit by the fire for a moment. Listen to it. It's crackling your name… well, almost.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Assieds-toi. J'ai une hist: Ah, {surnom}. Sit down. I've got a story that's been waiting for you. It's aged a little, like me, but it's kept all its teeth.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. J'ai écrit trois rouleaux: Ah, {surnom}. I've written three scrolls about you. Want to read them? No? Nobody ever does.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. La Vieille vous connaît, m: Ah, {surnom}. The Old Lady knows you now. She doesn't creak any more when you come in. That's rare. She's very wary of the folk up top.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Le Cristal a frémi quand t: Ah, {surnom}. The Crystal quivered when you came through the door. It likes you, I think.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Le soleil est haut ; Rê a: Ah, {surnom}. The sun is high; Ra has won his battle of the night. What do you wish to know?
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Mes champignons te reconna: Ah, {surnom}. My mushrooms recognise you. They glow a little brighter when you arrive. Well, I think so. Or it's the steam from the pond. Let's say it's you.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Mes salades te reconnaisse: Ah, {surnom}. My lettuces recognise you. They turn a little when you go by. Well, they turn towards the lamp too. But I'd rather believe it's you.
Ah, {surnom}. My kingdom talks about you. Sit down. Not on the throne.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Selon l'article quatre cen: Ah, {surnom}. According to article four hundred and twelve of the protocol, a returning visitor is entitled to a level-two bow. (He bows; his necklace catches in his toga.) … Level one and a half. That's still very good.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Ta chaise t'attend au fond: Ah, {surnom}. Your chair is waiting for you at the back of the class. Nobody's allowed to sit in it. Mila tried. I sent her back to her seat. Gently. Firmly. Both.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Ta place est libre. Je te: Ah, {surnom}. Your seat is free. I keep it for you now. Even Brunehaut isn't allowed to sit in it. She tries every day.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Ta place t'attend, ta soup: Ah, {surnom}. Your seat's waiting for you, your soup too, and your spoon is already on the table. I put it there yesterday, just in case. It waited for you all night.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Tu as encore tous tes doig: Ah, {surnom}. Still got all your fingers? Good.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Tu as une petite mine. Une: Ah, {surnom}. You look a bit peaky. Some herbal tea?
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Tu reviens pour la suite d: Ah, {surnom}. Back for the rest of the story? I can't remember where we'd got to. I'll start another one.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Tu reviens voir mes fleurs: Ah, {surnom}. Back to see my flowers? They recognised you. Look, they're turning towards you. Or towards the sun. Both, maybe.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Tu tombes bien : tiens cet: Ah, {surnom}. Perfect timing: hold this pane. Gently. There. You're the first person I've ever trusted with a pane. It's a great honour. Don't let go.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Tu veux une histoire ? J'e: Ah, {surnom}. Want a story? I have three thousand. This one is short. Well, for an elf.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Tu viens voir mes tissages: Ah, {surnom}. Have you come to see my weaving, or did Caelan send you?
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Vous avez lu quelque chose: Ah, {surnom}. Have you read anything since last time? No? It's never too late.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Vous revenez si souvent qu: Ah, {surnom}. You come back so often that the Council is considering awarding you a porthole. It's the highest honour in the Dome. The last one went to a ray that came by every day.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Vous revenez signer ? Non: Ah, {surnom}. Back to sign? No? Back to look at the scale model. Everyone comes back to look at the scale model. It's highly optimised.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Vous revenez. Vous avez tr: Ah, {surnom}. You're back. You're thirty-one seconds ahead of the time I expected to see you again. Very good. Don't do it again, it puts me out of sync.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Vous revoilà. Bon. Asseyez: Ah, {surnom}. You again. Fine. Sit down. Not there, that's the seat of… of nobody. Fine, sit there.
textes.Ah, {surnom}. Vous tombez bien : la cabi: Ah, {surnom}. Good timing: the cabin has just come back down, Barnabé is still green, and I have three minutes. Three. I counted them.
textes.Ah, {surnom}… Tu reviens écouter le vieu: Ah, {surnom}… Back to listen to old Silas?
textes.Ah. Alors la casquette, je te la rends d: Ah. Then I'll give you the cap back tomorrow.
textes.Ah. C'est toi. Je comptais mes coquillag: Ah. It's you. I was counting my shells. I'd got to… drat, I've lost count.
textes.Ah. C'est toi. … Bonjour. Ne t'y habitue: Ah. It's you. … Hello. Don't get used to it.
Oh. All right. That's less fun.
textes.Ah. Elle les mange, au moins ?: Oh. She does eat them, at least?

textes.Ah. Euh. Il a changé d'avis ?: Ah. Um. Maybe it changed its mind?

textes.Ah. Je l'entends dans ta voix. Alors ne: Ah. I can hear it in your voice. Then don't keep them waiting too long. Waiting can be mended, but it leaves knots.

Ah. Same place as always, then.
textes.Ah. Tu l'as vu, toi aussi, les nuits cla: Ah. You've seen it too, on clear nights: a castle, way up high, on an island floating above the ocean. The Citadel of the Clouds, fortress of the Sky Kings. Nori says it was from up there that the lightning woke our golems… Nobody goes up there. Except the great eagles. There's one left: Ventaile. The golems chained her at the edge of the crater, above the path. Free her, feed her — fish, she loves fish — and put this on her back: the saddle of Forgefer's last eagle riders.
textes.Ah. Tu me comprends, maintenant. Bien. A: Ah. You understand me now. Good. Then listen: I chose you. Don't disappoint me.
textes.Ah. Tu me comprends. Quelle déception :: Ah. You understand me. How disappointing: I thought humans were more mysterious.
textes.Ah. Venez là. Ne regardez pas en bas, re: Ah. Come here. Don't look down, look at the cable. Vertigo can't be cured, you know. It can be tamed. Like a grumpy sheep. Gently, one step at a time.
textes.Ah. Vous avez compris le secret de ma mè: Ah. You've understood my mother's secret. You'd make an excellent liftkeeper. Well, an excellent passenger. That's already a great deal.
textes.Ahhh ! Enfin quelqu'un ! Viens là, je te: Ahhh! Finally, someone! Come here, I'll make you a free necklace. OK, half price. OK, free. You deserve it.
textes.Ahmed a la Zahra, la barque à côté de la: Ahmed has the Zahra, the boat next to the Bahja. He makes fun of my whales. I say his boat is cross-eyed. Every morning, we race to the channel, and he says I cheat.
textes.Ahmed m'a montré l'œil peint sur la prou: Ahmed showed me the eye painted on the Zahra's prow. It's so the boat can see the reefs, and find its way home by itself if you fall asleep. I drew one in charcoal on my hammock. That way, if I fall asleep, my hammock'll take me back to Tazira. It's a bit cross-eyed, like the Zahra's.
textes.Ahmed m'apprend à pêcher. Pour de vrai !: Ahmed's teaching me to fish. For real! He says I talk too much for a fisherman. He also says I've got a gift. I mostly remember the second one.
textes.Ahmed, c'est le client qui demande toujo: Ahmed is the customer who always asks for one more coat. He says his boat is the bluest in Tazira. It comes out of the same pot as the others. But he fishes well.
textes.Ahmed, c'est mon petit frère. Un bon pêc: Ahmed is my little brother. A good fisherman, but a dreamer. He fishes for sardines, he brings back shells, and he tells me the sea gives what it wants. The sea ought to listen to me a little.
textes.Ahoy ! Je love les cordages du port. Tu: Ahoy! I coil the harbour ropes. Can you tie a bowline? No? It's the king of knots: it holds anything, and comes undone with a flick.
textes.Ahoy, {surnom} ! La marée est bonne aujo: Ahoy, {surnom}! The tide is good today, and so are you, by the look of it.
textes.Ah… Elle ne s'apprend pas, Titouan. Elle: Ah… It can't be learned, Titouan. It just happens.
textes.Ah… En retard. Bon. Je vous offre un rév: Ah… Late. Well. I'm giving you an alarm clock. In spirit. A good one, with a double bell. With a bit of luck, you'll hear it in spirit too.
textes.Ah… Je t'attendais. Ne fais pas cette tê: Ah… I was expecting you. Don't make that face: I say that to everyone, and it works every time. Agathe Brumaire, seer. Sit down, the crystal ball is warm.
textes.Ah… Les grenouilles. Toute la ville en r: Ah… Frogs. The whole town dreams of them. Before you sleep, say three times “the Dawn watches over me”. And shut the window tight. That helps too.
textes.Ah… Splendid. Les plus beaux objets sont: Ah… Splendid. The finest objects are the ones that keep someone inside. Take good care of it. Never sell it to me, even if I beg. Especially if I beg.
textes.Ah… Tu as vu la porte sculptée dans son: Ah… You've seen the door carved into its trunk. Beneath the Mother Tree sleeps the Kingdom of Roots, the land of the fairies. Long ago, five firefly spirits guarded its door; one stormy evening they flew off into the forest, and the door closed. Take this fairy lantern. The spirits dance above the rings of white mushrooms all around the village. Bring them home, and the door will open.
textes.Ah… Tu es comme moi avant. Mais attentio: Ah… You're like I used to be. But careful, the party gets hold of you. One weekend, and boom. Three weeks from now, you'll be sleeping with crabs.
textes.Ah… Un grand. Les runes me l'avaient dit: Ah… A tall one. The runes told me. Nori, keeper of the runes. Sit down, and speak softly: the stones are listening.
textes.Ah… ah… attendez le final…: Ah… ah… wait for the finale…
textes.Ah… les cartes m'avaient dit que tu revi: Ah… the cards told me you'd be back.
Ah… my {surnom}. The virus hunter. (He quickly hides a tablet behind his back.) Nothing for sale today! Nothing at all. Only verified programs. Well, to be verified.
textes.Ah… tu les as vus briller, mon petit cha: Ah... you saw them shine, my little mushroom. Those are the fairy mushrooms. They only exist in tales, and in this cathedral, which is a bit of a tale itself. There are five: the Spring Bolete, the Moonwort, the Chatterer, the Rainbow and the Little Giant. Go pick them, one of each, and bring them back to me: I'll tell you what each one does. But listen carefully, this is the most important part. (She rests her hand on your shoulder.) In a tale, yes. In the real forest: never! Never, ever eat a mushroom you don't know. Even if it's pretty. Especially if it's pretty. Promise?
Ah… That happens, when you travel a lot. Listen, sweetie: you come from here. A little bit, at least. You pushed open my door, that counts.

textes.Alerte gentillesse : {joueur} a été vu e: Kindness alert: {joueur} was spotted helping someone. Again. If this goes on, we'll have to knit them a scarf. Mamie Barricade, that's one for you.

textes.Ali a construit la Zahra, la plus bleue: Ali built the Zahra, the bluest boat in Tazira. He says they're all the same blue. He's lying, or he doesn't know how to look. A great carpenter all the same.
textes.Ali m'a proposé une barque neuve. Presqu: Ali offered me a new boat. Practically free. He talked for a long time. The wood, the price, the keel, the sail. I listened to the end. Out of politeness. Then I said: “No.” He sighed. The next day, I brought him a sardine. To say thanks for asking. He understood. I think.
textes.Ali manque toujours de bois. Une fois, p: Ali is always short of wood. Once, to help, I brought back a whole palm trunk from the oasis, on camelback. Three days' walk. He looked at it. He said: “Thank you.” Palm wood is soft, it won't make a boat. He made a bench out of it in front of his house. He calls it “Mbarek's bench”. I sit on it. It's good.
Ali is going to build my boat, the Whale. When I've paid half. I'm at a quarter. He says I'm his best customer on credit. I'm his only customer on credit.
textes.Ali. Le fils de celui qui a fait ma barq: Ali. Son of the man who made my boat. Good carpenter. Talks too much about wood. Wants to replace my Mabrouka. No.
textes.Ali. Le mari de ma sœur. Un homme honnêt: Ali. My sister's husband. An honest man, with good hands. He talks too much about wood. In the desert there's no wood. So he talks about what's missing.
textes.Aller au Bois-Doré, chez les elfes, et a: To go to the Bois-Doré, to the elves, and learn the remedies no book contains. I'd take notes everywhere, even on my sleeves.
textes.Aller au Cercle des Pierres-Lunes (à l'o: Go to the Circle of Moonstones (west of the Academy) and lay your hand on the altar (E)

textes.Allumer un jour un seul et même feu pour: To light one day a single fire for a great Assembly of the four worlds of the Column: the Clouds, Hautefond, the Strata and the Azure Dome, sitting in a circle on sofas from everywhere, with the talking key passing from hand to hand. textes.Alors tu reviendras toujours quelque par: Then you'll always come back somewhere, that's good. But while you're here, the soup is me. And nobody turns down my soup.
textes.Alors tu sais ce que c'est, de regarder: Then you know what it is to gaze at the horizon in the morning. Remember to write to them. A letter is a drop that crosses the clouds.
textes.Alors tu seras le premier à les connaîtr: Then you'll be the first to get to know them! Look closely, listen closely, and taste Bobor's brioches closely. Then you'll tell them all about it back there.
textes.Alors un peu moins cher, pour les tilleu: Then a little cheaper, for the lime trees.
Then a little to the left. For elegance.
textes.Alors viens à l'atelier ! En dix minutes: Then come to the workshop! In ten minutes, you'll know how. In twenty, you'll be able to teach someone else. That's how it works around here.
textes.Alors vole contre lui, Brindille. Comme: Then fly against it, Brindille. Like I taught you.
textes.Alors vous comprenez le Baron. C'est pré: Then you understand the Baron. That's precious. I don't understand him, but I find him. To each their talent.
textes.Alors vous finirez bien par tomber sur l: Then you're bound to hit the right one eventually.
textes.Alors {qn} t'a raconté mes histoires ? J: So {qn} told you my stories? I hope {il} didn't tell you everything.
textes.Alors {qn} vous a raconté mes histoires: So {qn} told you my stories? I hope {il} didn't tell you everything.
textes.Alors égalité, comme d'habitude !: Then it's a tie, as usual!
Then it's a tie, as usual.
textes.Alors, Barnabé, ce tour en dirigeable ?: So, Barnabé, how about that airship ride?
textes.Alors, Brutus, ce collier pour ta fiancé: So, Brutus, how's that necklace for your sweetheart?
textes.Alors, Comète ? Qui paie les glaces ?: So, Comète? Who's paying for the ice creams?
textes.Alors, Fañch, les poissons sont bavards,: So, Fañch, are the fish chatty today?
textes.Alors, Hugues, ton dragon a grandi, depu: So, Hugues, has your dragon grown since yesterday?
textes.Alors, Lulu, tu reviens d'où, ce soir ?: So, Lulu, where are you back from tonight?
textes.Alors, Mathurin, combien de serpents ce: So, Mathurin, how many serpents tonight?
textes.Alors, Pépé, il pesait combien, ce matin: So, Grandpa, how much did your sea bass weigh this morning?
textes.Alors, Rachid, vendu au premier prix ?: So, Rachid, sold anything at the first price?
textes.Alors, Solenne, cette promenade ?: So, Solenne, how was the stroll?
textes.Alors, ce Glisseur stellaire ? Il ronron: So, how's that Star Glider? Purring, eh? I tuned it to perfection. Down to the last crystal. If it ever coughs, come back and see me. It won't cough. But come back anyway.
textes.Alors, ce lapin ? Il sort du trou, fait: So, that rabbit? Comes out of the hole, goes round the tree… You've been practising, I hope? Show me.
textes.Alors, ce mélange secret ? J'y travaille: So, how's that secret blend? I'm working on it.
textes.Alors, ce nez qui ne sentait rien ? Je l: So, that nose that couldn't smell anything? I train it on every visit. Smell. … Better. Much better.
textes.Alors, ce paysage d'en haut ? Toujours a: So, how's the view from up high? Still as lovely?
textes.Alors, ce tapis qui n'existe pas ?: So, this carpet that doesn't exist?
textes.Alors, ce vide ? On l'affronte ensemble: So, about those heights? Shall we face them together today?
textes.Alors, ces pieds ? Au chaud ?: So, those feet? Nice and cosy?
textes.Alors, ces sardines au miel ?: So, how are those honey sardines?
textes.Alors, cette bulle, Basile ? Elle est pr: So, this bubble, Basile? Is it ready?
textes.Alors, cette machine pour voler ? Pensez: So, that flying machine? Think about the landing first. Achille will tell you, if he ever comes down.
textes.Alors, cette nuit, tu as volé ? Moi oui,: So, did you fly last night? I did, over the sea. I looked for you. It was very crowded.
textes.Alors, combien de godets ? … Neuf ! Brav: So, how many wells? … Nine! Well done.
textes.Alors, dis-moi franchement : le hamac, l: So, tell me honestly: the hammock, last time… did you sleep well?
textes.Alors, en pensée : PAF ! Confettisé ! Ro: Then, in spirit: BANG! Confetti'd! Pink, yellow, green, it's even down your collar. Come back to the stand, I'll fire you a real one. Free.
textes.Alors, franchement, entre nous, sans fla: So, honestly, between us, no flattery: what do you think of our little town?
textes.Alors, je suis toujours dans la catégori: So, am I still in the “keep an eye on him” category?
textes.Alors, la voyante ? Ça mord, demain ?: So, seer? Will they bite tomorrow?
textes.Alors, le grand, toujours à forger pour: So, big'un, still forging for the tourists?
textes.Alors, le grand, toujours à taper trop f: So, big'un, still hitting too hard on the left?
textes.Alors, le tireur, tu as touché quelque c: So, shooter, hit anything since? Apart from Marcel's feet?
textes.Alors, le très-vite ? On verra ça sous l: So, Speedy? We'll see about that under the arches. I'll wait for you at the start. Well, I'll wait for you at the finish.
textes.Alors, ma blague ? Elle avance. J'en sui: So, my joke? It's coming along. I'm at the very beginning of the beginning.
textes.Alors, ma championne, tu pointes ?: So, my champion, are you pointing?
textes.Alors, maintenant, tu sais quel goût a l: So, now do you know what the sea tastes like?
textes.Alors, membre du club, tu as cassé quoi,: So, club member, what did you break this week?
textes.Alors, mes jolies, écoutez ça…: Right, my lovelies, listen to this…
textes.Alors, mon jeune confrère ? Du nouveau ?: So, my young colleague? Anything new?
textes.Alors, mon marchandeur ? Prêt à perdre,: Well, my haggler? Ready to lose today? My prices are hard as crystal.
textes.Alors, navigateur, on part quand ?: So, navigator, when do we set sail?
textes.Alors, notre château dans l'arbre ? Papi: So, what about our castle in the tree? Grandpa Augustin says we need a plan.
textes.Alors, on la raconte bien, aujourd'hui ?: So, shall we tell it well today?
textes.Alors, petit ? Ta cabane tient debout ?: Well, kid? Your hut still standing?
textes.Alors, petit gars, ce poing ?: So, little lad, how's that fist?
textes.Alors, petit, et ces crabes ?: So, little one, how about those crabs?
textes.Alors, t'as essayé ? Le plus dur c'est l: So, did you try? The hardest part is the first fall!
textes.Alors, t'as trouvé ton endroit ? Moi, to: So, found your place yet? Mine's still the same. Shh.
textes.Alors, ta cabane ? Les planches en écail: So, your hut? Planks overlapping like scales, like I told you? The rain will thank you.
textes.Alors, ta technique du hasard, ça marche: So, is your button-mashing technique working?
textes.Alors, tes fantômes verts ? Des lucioles: So, your green ghosts? Fireflies, I tell you.
textes.Alors, tes nuages de pensées ? Il y a un: So, your cloudy thoughts? A bit of sky today?
textes.Alors, ton épée, elle t'a répondu ? Ma b: So, has your sword answered you yet? My boat hasn't either. Patience, sailor, patience.
textes.Alors, toujours des troncs ? Le mien a p: So, still tree trunks? Mine dived last night. Trunks don't dive, I'll remind you.
textes.Alors, toujours partant pour descendre ?: So, still up for going down?
textes.Alors, toujours partant pour monter ?: So, still up for going up?
textes.Alors, tu as mangé, dormi, marché ? Renc: So, have you eaten, slept, walked? Met amazing people? I predicted it. I'm very good.
textes.Alors, tu as trouvé un nom pour ta lame: So, found a name for your blade? Not “Ouch”, eh. That one's taken.
textes.Alors, tu as vu mes nouveaux jolis échec: So, have you seen my new pretty failures?
textes.Alors, tu as écouté ton cœur ? Il tape b: So, did you listen to your heart? It keeps a good beat, eh?
textes.Alors, tu as écrit ? Non ? Mange d'abord: So, did you write? No? Eat first, write after. But write.
textes.Alors, tu l'as entendu, le petit boum ?: So, have you heard it, the little boom? The right place, I mean. I hear it every night.
textes.Alors, tu les as comptées, tes dents ? M: Tho, have you counted your teeth? Me, thith morning: one, two. Thtill two. Phew.
textes.Alors, tu nages toujours « un peu » ? So: So, still swimming “a bit”? Breathe slowly, I'm telling you. And stay where I can see you.
textes.Alors, tu nages un peu plus ? Moi je dis: So, swimming a bit more? I always say: a little is already better than… than nothing at all.
textes.Alors, tu sais maintenant qui t'attend ?: So, do you know now who's waiting for you? No? I knew, at your age. Keep looking.
textes.Alors, tu sais reconnaître un poisson fr: So, can you tell a fresh fish now? Recite: the eye, the gills, the skin. And the song.
textes.Alors, une galette pour le forgeron du g: So, a crêpe for the hinge smith?
textes.Alors, {surnom}, toi, à la taverne : tu: So, {surnom}, you, at the tavern: do you sing, do you dance, or do you listen?
textes.Alors… c'était le bouton d'un pirate. Un: Well… it was a pirate's button. A very elegant pirate.
Well then… twice upon a time.
textes.Alors… tu l'as vu, Octave. Il parle enco: So… you've seen him, Octave. Does he still talk about me?
textes.Altesse, l'ambassadeur vous attend depui: Your Highness, the ambassador has been waiting for ten minutes.
textes.Altesse, l'essayage ! Tenez-vous droite,: Your Highness, the fitting! Stand up straight, if you please.
textes.Altitude : idéale. Colis : intact. Pigeo: Altitude: ideal. Package: intact. Pigeon: annoying.
textes.Altitude : vingt-six mètres. Le mât comp: Altitude: twenty-six metres. The mast counts, I suppose.
textes.Altitude de l'île : deux cent trente-six: Altitude of the island: two hundred and thirty-six metres, and three centimetres. The three centimetres are Théo jumping for joy in his capsule.
textes.Ambroise a hérité de l'atelier, de l'aut: Ambroise inherited the workshop, the automaton and the respect of the whole city. Me, the gear. He despises me, I think. He's never said so. He never says anything to me at all.
textes.Ambroise dit que son automate joueur d'é: Ambroise says his chess-playing automaton has never lost. That's because it cheats. The automaton, I mean. Ambroise, I don't know.
textes.Ambroise est le meilleur joueur d'échecs: Ambroise is the best chess player in the city, after his automaton. And the slowest, by a mile. Forty years I've been beating him on the clock.
textes.Ambroise est mon rival, un homme disting: Ambroise is my rival, a distinguished man, and the owner of an automaton that cheats. Well, the automaton does. Ambroise, I haven't made up my mind about yet.
textes.Ambroise est un juré susceptible, un hom: Ambroise is a touchy juror, a proud man, and the builder of the finest machine in the city. All three at once is exhausting. But I respect him.
textes.Ambroise m'a proposé cent fois de jouer: Ambroise has offered a hundred times for me to play against his automaton. I've always refused. “It has no watch.” Against someone without a watch, you don't play: you wait. And waiting is something I can't do. A bit much, for a clockmaker, but there it is.
textes.Ambroise. J'ai encore pensé à mes trois: Ambroise. I've been thinking about my three prizes again.
textes.Amenemhat ! Encore un poème au lieu de p: Amenemhat! Another poem instead of paying?
textes.Amenemhat ! Vous lisez dans le bon sens,: Amenemhat! Are you reading the right way round today?
textes.Amenemhat boit sa bière en lisant, il en: Amenemhat drinks his beer while reading, spills it on his papyri, and tells a story with every sip. He always pays. Late, and with a poem.
textes.Amenemhat boit sa bière en lisant. Il re: Amenemhat drinks his beer while reading. He always spills a little on the papyrus. His papyri smell of barley.
textes.Amenemhat m'a appris les signes. Il prét: Amenemhat taught me the signs. He claims to have read everything, he shows off like a river goose, and he has the most generous heart in Per-Hâpy. Only repeat the last part to him.
textes.Amenemhat mesure mon champ chaque année: Amenemhat measures my field every year with his cord. Every year, he finds it the same. Me, I find it smaller. We'll never agree. He has the cord, I have the eyes.
textes.Amenemhat prétend avoir lu tous les papy: Amenemhat claims he has read every papyrus in the House of Life. Every one. Even the ones he wrote himself. Especially those.
textes.Amenemhat ronfle à la Maison de Vie. Les: Amenemhat snores in the House of Life. The pupils call him the hippopotamus. Don't tell him.
textes.Amenemhat écrit avec des signes qui dise: Amenemhat writes with signs that each say one sound, or several, or none. It's very complicated. He talks as much as he writes. I like him very much. I only understand one sentence in two.
textes.Amenemhat, c'est le maître de la Maison: Amenemhat is the master of the House of Life. He knows seven hundred signs, and he talks even more than I do! He snores during school. The pupils call him the hippo. Don't tell him!
textes.Amenemhat. Vous avez sauté une ligne, ce: Amenemhat. You skipped a line this morning.
textes.Ami ! Tenez bon ! Je vais lui chatouille: Friend! Hold on! I'll tickle its belly with my sword! Gently!
textes.Ami ? … Ougha réfléchit. (Ougha réfléchi: Friend? … Ougha think. (Ougha thinks very hard; it makes a noise.) All right. You friend. Smooth friend. First smooth friend of the Clan!
textes.Ami des fées ! Le royaume tout entier ch: Friend of the fairies! The whole kingdom sings your name.
textes.Ami, frère d'armes, compagnon de légende: Friend, brother in arms, companion of legend: I owe you a debt. Let me repay it with my sword. Whenever you like, just say “come with me”, and I, SIR TANCRÈDE DE TOURNEVENT, will charge at your side! One time in three, I'll fall. But the other two times… ah, the other two times!
textes.Ami, je suis là ! Prêt à charger ! Contr: Friend, I'm here! Ready to charge! Against what, again?
textes.Ami, je voudrais vous suivre ! Mais un c: Friend, I'd like to follow you! But a knight only sets out with an adventurer of the Guild. It's the code. Sign up with Églantine!
textes.Amine m'a appris les osselets : tu lance: Amine taught me knucklebones: you throw, you pick up, you catch, all with one hand. He always wins. In exchange, I taught him to swear like a real pirate, but with no bad words: “Blistering barnacles! Thundering sardines!” Now he shouts it everywhere. His mum gives me funny looks.
textes.Amine sait où dort le chat roux. Je le s: Amine knows where the ginger cat sleeps. I know he knows! But he won't tell me. He only told Tibo, 'cause Tibo's a real pirate. It's not fair! I'm his captain. A captain has to know everything. I sulked for two days. Then he gave me a date. I stopped. A bit.
textes.Amine sait, pour les babouches de noce d: Amine knows about Rachid's wedding slippers. He saw them at the bottom of the basket. I told him: “Not a word.” He said: “Not a word.” The next day he walked past Rachid whistling the wedding tune, with enormous winks at me. He didn't say anything. Almost nothing.
textes.Amine, c'est mon matelot. Il perd toujou: Amine is my sailor. He always loses at boarding, but he's brave. He wants to be captain. That's not possible, I'm already captain.
textes.Amine, c'est mon meilleur copain de Tazi: Amine's my best mate in Tazira. He knows every roof, every crate and every secret. He wants to be a pirate. I want to be a fisherman. We should swap.
textes.Amine, mon fils. Neuf ans, des mains de: Amine, my son. Nine years old, a carpenter's hands and a pirate's head. I hand him a plane, he hands me back a wooden sabre. He takes after his mother. And a bit after me, I think.
textes.Amine, mon livreur ! Il court plus vite: Amine, my delivery boy! He runs faster than the chergui wind. He gets the wrong house one time in two, but he always comes back smiling. Paid in dates. He eats half of them on the way.
textes.Amine. Le fils de ma sœur. Il parle comm: Amine. My sister's son. He talks like the sandstorm wind. He's the only one who makes me laugh. Don't tell him: he'd talk even more.
textes.Amiral était coincé sur le toit d'un con: Amiral was stuck on top of a container, six metres up. He was barking, I was crying. Boulon climbed into his crane, lifted the container and set it down on the ground, ever so gently. Amiral climbed down by himself. He licked Boulon's hand. Since then, Amiral follows him everywhere. I'm a little jealous.
textes.Amiral, tu restes avec Boulon. Tu l'aura: Amiral, you stay with Boulon. You would have anyway.
textes.Amirale ! Vous avez vu ? J'ai redessiné: Admiral! Have you seen? I've redrawn the north coast!
textes.Ammit s'effondre et se dissout dans l'om: Ammit collapses and dissolves into the shadows. Anubis hasn't moved. You can stand before the scale again… and tell the truth this time.
textes.Ammit se ramasse… et se jette sur toi, g: Ammit crouches… and leaps at you, jaws wide open!
textes.Amoureuse. Comme au premier jour. Le onz: In love. Like on the first day. The eleventh day.
textes.Amusée. Le Bourgmestre m'a envoyé un dis: Amused. The Burgomaster sent me a speech down by cabin. Twelve pages. I replied with one line: “Received. Good. Come.” He sent me fourteen pages back to thank me for my concision.
textes.Amélie m'a refusé le corail, et elle ava: Amélie refused me the coral, and she was right, I know. She knows every herb on the lookout. She couldn't find me my red.
textes.Amélie, c'est l'herboriste, et mon amie: Amélie is the herbalist, and my friend since the summer it didn't rain. I grow her thyme, she looks after my hands. We both dream of a flower nobody here has ever seen.
textes.Analyse : intéressant. Dire bonjour fait: Analysis: interesting. Saying hello does good to the one who says it. Calculating… Yes. That is logical. I feel good when I say it. Hello, {surnom}. There. It works.
textes.Analyse : réponse positive. Joie détecté: Analysis: positive answer. Joy detected. Thank you, {surnom}. I will tell the oak in the Park. He will be pleased. Slowly.
textes.Anatole Crémaillère, le liftier des Stra: Anatole Crémaillère, the Strata liftkeeper, and I have been writing to each other for thirty years.
