textes.Au fond du cul-de-sac, un coffre tout co: At the end of the dead end, a very sticky chest. Inside: a vial of sap, some coins… and a label: “Property of the slimes. Do not touch.” Too late.
At the back, in the grass.
textes.Au fond, leur soleil est une grosse perl: Down at the bottom, their sun is a big pearl. In the evening, it turns violet. And there I was, thinking I'd seen everything in the way of sunsets…
textes.Au hasard ! Le meilleur cap qui soit ! C: Wherever! The best heading there is! That's how I've discovered the most beautiful things. And how I've got lost most often. The two go together.
textes.Au hasard ?! … Attends, c'est comme ça q: Button mashing?! … Wait, that's how Mio beat me. Is it a technique? It's a technique!
Any book at all, of course. Heh heh.
textes.Au hibou ! Et tu t'es endormi au moment: At the owl! And you fell asleep when the wolf came in!
textes.Au lac, une grenouille l'a avalé. J'ai t: At the lake, a frog swallowed him. I shot an arrow into the reeds, right under its nose. It sneezed. Hilaire popped out like a cork. He said: “Thanks, Lison, I almost had it.” He had nothing at all. But he was smiling. Covered in slime. He always smiles. That's the strongest thing about him.
textes.Au large de Tazira, il y a des bancs de: Off Tazira, there are shoals of sardines so big the sea turns silver. The pirates say they've never seen anything like it anywhere else.
textes.Au large du village, on prend des daurad: Off the village, you catch sea bream this big. Paulo pays well for them for his bouillabaisse.
textes.Au lever du jour, au Belvédère, les nuag: At daybreak, at the Belvedere, the clouds under the island turn pink, then gold, then white. Three paintings in ten minutes. I only have two hands. I choose pink.
textes.Au lieu de m'apporter du poisson, Ahmed: Instead of bringing me fish, Ahmed brings back shells for Yasmine. Pink ones, twisty ones, ones that sing. My daughter has a whole jar of them. Me, I've got an empty pot. I scolded him, like when he was little. The next day, he came back with a basket of sardines… and five shells. He says it's Yasmine's tax.
textes.Au marché, Marley et moi, on a un stand: At the market, Marley and I share one stall: necklaces on the left, bananas on the right. One day a lady bought three necklaces from me. Marley gave her a whole bunch, “because she looked like family”. She left with more bananas than necklaces. I did the maths: that day, we lost money.
textes.Au marché, sur la Grand-Place, il y a l': At the market, on the Great Square, there's Babette's stall. Her apples are too red. I'm just saying. Not saying anything. But too red.
textes.Au mariage de Marius et d'Odette, j'ai a: At Marius and Odette's wedding, I lit the lighthouse in broad daylight, at noon, for them. The old keeper gave me a right telling-off. Odette, on the church steps, looked up and laughed. I'd never seen her laugh. Marius said: “See? He talks with his lamp, my brother.”
textes.Au mariage de sa fille, elle a pleuré si: At her daughter's wedding, she cried so hard the cake melted. It was an icing-sugar cake. We ate it with spoons.
textes.Au milieu ? Dans les dix secondes toutes: In the middle? In the ten all-white seconds? Ah… you've found the best moment. Nobody ever says so. I'll sing a song for you next time.
textes.Au milieu de la salle ronde, l'orrerie d: In the middle of the round room, the brass orrery turns its planets around a little shining sun.
textes.Au moins, c'est honnête. Tes traces le d: At least that's honest. Your tracks already said so: they hesitate at every bridge. Stay near the lanterns. And if you get lost, stay put. I'll find you.
textes.Au moins, elle n'a pas peur des étincell: At least it's not scared of sparks.
textes.Au moins, tu le sais. C'est le début. Po: At least you know it. That's the start. Put your heel down last. Breathe through your nose. And don't talk. That's the hardest part.
textes.Au moins, vous êtes honnête. C'est un dé: At least you're honest. That's a start. Frost always begins with an impatience that calms down.
textes.Au nom du Conseil…: In the name of the Council…
textes.Au nord de ton village, il y a un cercle: North of your village, there's a circle of standing stones. On my Ancients' map, there's a serpent drawn right in the middle. The ground sounds hollow there, {surnom}. A shovel would work wonders.
textes.Au nord, dans la jungle, il y a des serp: To the north, in the jungle, there are snakes. To the west, on the slopes of the volcano, jaguars. Real ones. Be careful.
textes.Au nord, il y avait un champ de chanvre: Up north, there was a field of hemp nobody used. I built a ropeworks. You cut, you dry it in stacks, you beat, you spin, you twist. Same motion as at sea. My hands are happy.
textes.Au nord, les falaises. Le vent y est gla: Up north, the cliffs. The wind there is icy, even in summer. Borée goes up there to fetch his snowflakes. Not me. Cliffs don't float.
textes.Au nord, les ronces. Elles avancent d'un: To the north, the brambles. They advance one step every year. One day they'll eat the village. Nobody listens to me.
textes.Au nouvel an, je tire mes confettis du h: At New Year, I fire my confetti from the top of the clock tower. The wind carries it all the way to the highlands. The sheep are all colourful for a week.
textes.Au pas ! Au pas, j'ai dit !: Walking pace! I said walking pace!
textes.Au pied des Crocs, au sud-ouest, s'ouvre: At the foot of the Fangs, to the south-west, lies the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps. There aren't a thousand, I had them counted: there are nine hundred and eighty-seven. But “the Dungeon of Nine Hundred and Eighty-Seven Steps” didn't fit on the sign.
textes.Au pied du phare : un escalier qui tourn: At the foot of the lighthouse: a staircase winding up along the wall, cans of oil, and the keeper's log lying open on the table.
textes.Au pied du phare, sous une pierre qui lu: At the foot of the lighthouse, under a glowing stone: an iron box full of coins, and a note: “For the next one who sees it. — T.”
textes.Au plaisir. La sortie est à votre gauche: A pleasure. The exit is on your left. As always.
textes.Au plus profond, dort Cipactli, le monst: Deepest of all sleeps Cipactli, the Earth monster: a crocodile with a thousand mouths. The gods made the world out of its body. Tezcatlipoca lost his foot to it. You, keep yours.
textes.Au poisson, Doc ! Mais du bon poisson, j: Fish, Doc! But good fish, I swear!
textes.Au prix de Kraxx. Moins un. Pour la Gard: At the Kraxx price. Minus one. For the Guard.
textes.Au prix de l'autre fois ? Non. L'autre f: At last time's price? No. Last time was a mistake.
textes.Au programme aujourd'hui, trois airs du: On today's programme: three wind tunes. You choose, I conduct!
textes.Au quatrième étage du donjon, il y a une: On the fourth floor of the dungeon, there's a library, with chests that are mimics. A mimic! A living chest! If you bring back a little piece, I'll give you a good price. Well, as long as the piece doesn't bite.
textes.Au quatrième étage, il y a des livres. E: On the fourth floor, there are books. And chests that bite. I'd very much like to see the books.
textes.Au quatrième étage, une énigme désigne l: On the fourth floor, a riddle points to the real chest. The others are mimics. Philomène says they bite. I say they pinch. Nobody wants to check the difference.
textes.Au retour ! Garde-le au chaud !: When I'm back! Keep it warm!
textes.Au retour de Tazira, Boulon est descendu: Back from Tazira, Boulon climbed out of the gondola with a scratched nose. Three scratches. The harbour cats. He hadn't caught a single one. The commander looked at him and said: “Well. At least he came back.” Then she painted a little star on the gondola, like for the difficult flights. That's Boulon's star.
textes.Au retour, Boulon est descendu le nez ra: On the way back, Boulon got off with a scratched nose: three scratches, the harbour cats of Tazira. He hadn't caught a single one. Wilfried picked him up in his brass arm without a word, and Boulon wagged his tail anyway. I painted a little star on the gondola, like for the difficult flights. That's Boulon's star.
textes.Au revoir ! Attention en descendant par: Goodbye! Careful going down the beam: you always get a little hollow feeling in your tummy. It's normal, it's just gravity saying hello.
textes.Au revoir ! Si tu trouves un boulon, tu: Bye! If you find a bolt, you know where I live. Everywhere.
textes.Au revoir ! Si tu vas à la plage, mange: Bye! If you go to the beach, eat an ice cream for me. A strawberry one. And describe it to me afterwards.
textes.Au revoir ! Si tu vois la pluie, là-haut: Bye! If you see the rain up there, open your mouth and taste it. Then come back and tell me if it's salty.
textes.Au revoir, frère d'armes ! Appelez-moi,: Farewell, brother-in-arms! Call me, and I'll come back at a gallop! Well, at a walk. I don't have a horse.
textes.Au revoir, mon chou ! Reviens vite : dem: Bye, sweetie! Come back soon: tomorrow I'll surely have a new bit of gossip. I always do.
textes.Au revoir, mon petit ! Et couvre-toi en: Bye-bye, dearie! And wrap up on your way back up: it's windy up top.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom} ! Et n'oubliez pas d: Goodbye, {surnom}! And don't forget to vote for me. There's no election, but it's a good habit.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom} ! Et regarde par ter: Bye, {surnom}! And look at the ground as you walk: there's always a bolt waiting for someone.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom} ! Graissez bien vos: Goodbye, {surnom}! Keep your gears well oiled.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom} ! Reviens vite : j'a: Goodbye, {surnom}! Come back soon: I'm learning a new song.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Bonne mer. Même sur: Goodbye, {surnom}. Fine sea to you. Even on land.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Et quand tu seras l: Goodbye, {surnom}. And when you're up there, look at the sky for one minute longer. For us. For the whole class.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Et regardez où vous: Goodbye, {surnom}. And watch where you put your feet. Even up top.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Et s'il pleut en ha: Goodbye, {surnom}. And if it rains up top, think of me: the rain gets here the next day.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Et si tu croises un: Goodbye, {surnom}. And if you come across a sad tree, say something kind to it. It'll remember it for a hundred years.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Et si vous voyez me: Goodbye, {surnom}. And if you see my glasses anywhere, bring them back to me. … They're on my head? Ah.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Et si, là-haut, vou: Goodbye, {surnom}. And if, up there, you see a great shadow passing under the sea, greet her for me. She'll know.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Je prévois que nous: Goodbye, {surnom}. I forecast that we'll meet again tomorrow at eight minutes past four. Or another day. Give or take a minute.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Je retourne dire bo: Goodbye, {surnom}. I am going back to saying hello to the trees. I have two hundred and six left.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Levez la tête de te: Goodbye, {surnom}. Look up now and then: the sky likes to be looked at.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Marche doucement. L: Goodbye, {surnom}. Walk softly. The rock thanks you.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Que tes couleurs ti: Goodbye, {surnom}. May your colours hold fast!
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Revenez. C'est un c: Goodbye, {surnom}. Come back. That is advice from the Guild. The only one I give for free.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Si tu croises un vr: Goodbye, {surnom}. If you come across a real garden up there, say hello to it from the Greenhouses. It doesn't know us. But we think of it.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. Vous partez à… quat: Goodbye, {surnom}. You are leaving at… two thirty-two and five seconds. I'm making a note.
textes.Au revoir, {surnom}. « Que le vent te po: Goodbye, {surnom}. “May the wind push you along, and the road sing you a song.” Ah! It rhymes! At last!
textes.Au revoir. Si la petite Mila vous demand: Goodbye. If little Mila asks you how her petition is doing, tell her it's under review. Very seriously.
textes.Au revoir. Si vous avez besoin de foudre: Goodbye. If you need lightning, you know where to find me. Follow the smell of burning.
textes.Au revoir… (Elle cherche son pinceau. Il: Goodbye… (She looks for her brush. It's behind her ear.)
textes.Au skatepark, Tornade est tombé si fort: At the skatepark, Tornade once fell so hard he left a shoe print on the ramp. I outlined the print in paint, with a star and a date. It's become a monument. The children come and put their foot in it. Tornade is very proud of it. Pastille less so.
textes.Au sommet ! Enfin, au fond, mais au somm: On top of the world! Well, at the bottom of it, but on top! Twelve years of works, {surnom}, and today, thirty trips down. Thirty! Every time the cabin comes out of the cliff, people go “oh”. Thirty “oh”s. I collect them.
textes.Au sommet ! La Ligne a rouvert, {surnom}: On top of the world! The Line has reopened, {surnom}! Three years of overhaul, three years polishing a capsule that didn't move. Today I made forty ascents. Forty! I'm the happiest liftkeeper in the sky.
textes.Au sommet des murailles de Dité, trois s: At the top of the walls of Dité, three figures spread their wings: the FURIES! “Nobody enters Dité!” they cry, diving at you.
textes.Au sommet du Grand Temple, offrir une ja: At the top of the Great Temple, offer a jar of rain to Tlaloc (blue shrine) and copal to Huitzilopochtli (red shrine)
textes.Au sommet du Mont Fusain: At the summit of Mount Charcoal
textes.Au sommet du Temple de Kukulkan, mettre: At the top of the Temple of Kukulkan, set the two calendar wheels to the date of the creation of the world (the great stele on the square shows it; Ah Kin, the astronomer, knows it)
textes.Au sommet du massif, il y a un endroit d: At the top of the massif, there's a spot where you can see both your islands at once. I mapped it. On a shell, naturally.
textes.Au stand, Momo fait les comptes sur une: At the stall, Momo does the accounts on a plank with a bit of charcoal. One evening he showed me: “Necklaces sold: nine. Bananas given away: forty-two.” He looked very sad. I gave him a banana. He laughed. And he wrote: “forty-three”.
textes.Au sud, dans la Cathédrale des Spores, M: To the south, in the Spore Cathedral, Mère Morille knows every mushroom. She's very learned. For a rival. But be careful: you must never, EVER pick a mushroom without someone who knows it. Zero out of ten for anyone who does.
textes.Au tableau de la Guilde, il y a des cont: On the Guild board, there are hunting contracts: slimes, frogs, goblins… Églantine won't give me any. She says “not before sixteen”. So I read them. I know them all by heart.
textes.Au talent ? Ho ho ! Un connaisseur ! Le: Talent? Ho ho! A connoisseur! Talent is luck that's been tamed. Come to my table, I'll show you. From a distance.
textes.Au top ! J'ai plané du Port jusqu'à la C: Brilliant! I glided from the Harbour to the Falls without a single flap. Three hundred metres of sky! A pigeon followed me to learn. He was talented.
textes.Au top ! J'ai réparé la soucoupe de Comè: Top form! I repaired Comète's saucer for the forty-third time. She raced a seagull again. The seagull won. The saucer lost a fin.
textes.Au top ! J'ai réparé neuf vélos, un mono: Top notch! I fixed nine bikes, a unicycle, a wheelchair and the pram of Cerise's doll. The pram had a flat tyre. The doll was very worried.
textes.Au top ! Plongée du matin : cent quatre-: Brilliant! Morning dive: a hundred and ninety-five metres. The cliffs of the Trench, the glass sponges, the sea fans, and a jellyfish as big as an umbrella that kept me company all the way down. The Professor named her Gertrude. She looked like a Gertrude.
textes.Au top ! Tant que la mer est là et que l: Top form! As long as the sea's here and people are dancing, I'm mixing.
textes.Au top. La mer est calme, aucun noyé, et: Top form. The sea's calm, nobody's drowned, and I've done five hundred press-ups.
textes.Au tout premier vol d'essai, nous étions: On the very first test flight there were two of us in the gondola: Zélie at the controls, me beside her with my plans. At a hundred metres, it started to smell of cabbage. I went pale: I thought it was a leak. Zélie asked: “Is that normal?” I said: “I think so.” We landed bang on the cross painted in the middle of the field.
textes.Au trente-quatrième coup, j'ai avancé mo: On the thirty-fourth move, I moved my bishop. The automaton stopped. Its gears turned and turned, and nothing moved. Mr Checkmate took out his watch. Eleven minutes. The whole Fair was waiting. I ate an ice cream. When it played, I knew I'd lost. Seven moves later. Logical. But eleven minutes, all the same.
textes.Au troisième étage du donjon, il y a tre: On the third floor of the dungeon, thirty years ago, I panicked in front of a frog and ran back up. Odon waited for me at the bottom for two hours, with the packed lunch. When I came back down, bright red, he handed me a slice of bread and butter without a word. Since then, every year, on that day, we eat a slice of bread and butter together. And I pay for the cider.
textes.Au troisième étage, il faut la clé de cu: On the third floor, you need the copper key to open the door to the fourth. It's in a frog's belly. Don't ask me how it got there. Frogs swallow everything.
In the village where I grew up.
textes.Au village, il y a Sylwen et son pain de: In the village there's Sylwen and her honey bread, Aëlwen and her potions, Faelar and his stories… Go and see them, they're all waiting for you.
textes.Au vol d'inauguration de l'escale de Ram: On the inaugural flight to the Ramure stop, I was aboard, as a passenger. Above the great trees, an owl came and circled the gondola three times, without a sound, a satchel slung across her chest. Gustave nearly let go of the stick. On the first docket of the return trip, all it said was: “That was me. Hoo.”
Past ten, I have my bees.
textes.Au-delà, il n'y a plus que la mer et les: Beyond this there's only the sea and the clouds: turn back!
textes.Au-dessus de la porte, en lettres de feu: Above the door, in letters of fire: “YOU WHO ENTER HERE, KEEP HOPE (AND TAKE A COAT).” Lower down, smaller: “The ferryman only accepts obols. No coins with holes.”
textes.Au-dessus de mon trône, il y a une phras: Above my throne, there's a sentence carved in stone: “The king is the most handsome of dwarves.” Hilda told me Croâ had said it. I had it carved that very day. Nori looked at it for a long time and murmured: “That's not raven.” I don't care. It's carved.
textes.Au-dessus de nous, presque toujours du s: Above us, almost always sunshine. Below us, almost always clouds. The Floor folk think we live in the clouds. Not at all. We live on the clouds. It's a very important distinction. To me, anyway.
textes.Au-dessus de sa porte, il y a une grande: Above his door, there's a big sword with blue glints. Every time I walk past, I look the other way. One day, I looked the other way so hard I walked into a bench. He was on his doorstep. He didn't laugh. He went “Hm”. That's worse.
textes.Au-dessus des nuages ! Là où il fait tou: Above the clouds! Where the weather's always fine. Did you know that above the rain, the sun shines all the time? It's the aeronauts' secret. Keep it to yourself.
textes.Aubin ! Tu es vert, ce matin. C'est magi: Aubin! You're green this morning. Is it magic?
textes.Aubin a goûté une de ses potions et il e: Aubin tasted one of his potions and turned green. He says it was an “expected” effect. It took him two days to turn pink again. I bought the rest of the potion. It's surely magic.
textes.Aubin dit que ses potions sont de la sci: Aubin says his potions are science. I say it's magic with spectacles on. He looks down his nose at me. He changes colour. I buy his failed potions: they're surely magic.
textes.Aubin fait les meilleures potions de l'î: Aubin makes the best potions on the island. They heal well. They change people's colour. Adventurers come up from the dungeon like a tired rainbow. I note it all down for him.
textes.Aubin. Six potions de plus, pour le fond: Aubin. Six more potions, for the bottom of the hole.
None! Well, one. A teeny one.
textes.Aucun ? (Elle te regarde comme si tu ava: None? (She looks at you as if you'd said something silly.) That hurts my eyes. But I respect it. … I barely respect it.
textes.Aucun ? Alors comment ils savent qu'on l: None? Then how do they know when you're calling them? … Oh. Maybe they don't know. That's why they bite everybody!
textes.Aucun ne brille encore. Il faudra sans d: None are shining yet. You'll probably need to wake the crystal in each wing.
textes.Aucun pour l'instant. Rendez service, et: None yet. Help people out, and they will remember it.
None, I like my jacket as it is.
None. Well, one. A teeny one.
textes.Aucun. Et ne recommence pas avec tes bou: None. And don't start again with your buoys.
None. No Chak in the forest.
textes.Aucune pour l'instant. La première t'att: None yet. The first one may be waiting for you under the village…
textes.Aucune quête en cours. Parlez aux habita: No quest in progress. Talk to the locals: many of them need help.
textes.Aufourd'hui, le matin, fe pêche au ponto: Nowadayth, in the morning, I fith off the jetty. I catch fith, bootth, and onthe a governor'th hat. In the afternoon, I thit on my bench, in the thun. In the evening, I play dithe at the Shark'th Tooth with Tonneau, and I lothe. Mange-Clous maketh me mathed thtew and themolina. Hith themolina ith the betht in the archipelago. I don't know how he maketh it.
textes.Augustin a appris à lire à tout le villa: Augustin taught the whole village to read. He rubs out everything he writes, so we never know what he meant. But we always know he said it kindly.
textes.Augustin dit qu'il a vu briller du rose: Augustin says he saw something pink glinting on a walkway. But Augustin has been seeing things glint everywhere since he lost his glasses. They're on his nose.
textes.Augustin me donne sa farine, je lui donn: Augustin gives me his flour, I give him my apples, and we make pies while reciting verse to them. He blushes whenever the Library comes up. The trees have noticed. So have I.
textes.Augustin vient parfois lire ses poèmes a: Augustin sometimes comes to read his poems to the rocks. The wind carries them off. So do the seagulls. He doesn't notice. He keeps on reading, empty-handed. It's very beautiful to watch.
textes.Augustin, le meunier, monte parfois jusq: Augustin, the miller, sometimes climbs up to the rocks to read his poems to the wind. The wind carries them off. So do the gulls. Basile kept one in his nest. He rereads it often. Well, he sits on it.
textes.Augustin, tu as noté ?: Augustin, did you write that down?
textes.Augustin. Votre moulin tourne à trois to: Augustin. Your mill is turning at three revolutions per minute.
textes.Aujourd'hui : cartes postales, coquillag: Today: postcards, painted shells, kites and snow globes. The post office is waging a postcard war on me, the postwoman gives me smiles: I no longer know who's winning. In the evening, I beat Lucas at cards at the Perroquet. Inès looks down on my shells. And little Théo, whose kite flew away. That made my heart heavy. Half price, but heavy.
textes.Aujourd'hui : douze lits par jour. La se: These days: twelve beds a day. Room seven, the newlyweds. Room twelve, the Lord, where you have to dust mountains of knick-knacks. The professor's, with his drawing under the pillow. This morning I found a pearl under a bed! Well, a button. I put it in my pension box. There are already savings in it. And three buttons.
textes.Aujourd'hui ? Colette, à qui je prédis u: Today? Colette, to whom I predict a great love every year, this time “come from beyond the seas”. Hortense, to whom I promised a stranger who will make the clock ring. The tourist on the beach and her “someone who walks a lot”. And Félix, the bookseller, who writes everything down in a notebook to catch me out. He's found three that came true. It makes him ill.
textes.Aujourd'hui ? Les daurades de Fernand, l: Today? Fernand's sea bream, Rosalie's fish, when she's not selling me yesterday's. Margaux's bread, whose croissants I steal. No, I'm joking. Gérard, who has the bouillabaisse every lunchtime and talks about buying bigger trousers. The newlyweds, the evening they had dinner without saying a word to each other. And me in the middle, singing louder than the pot.
textes.Aujourd'hui, Brindezingue fait douze mèt: Today, Brindezingue is twelve metres long. He has eleven wheels donated by Rustine, a tail made of organ pipes and one wing missing, stolen by Lisse's robots. Around him, I planted flower-robots, made from the arms of moving-robots. They used to be menacing. Now they bloom.
textes.Aujourd'hui, Gunnar garde mon trône, Ori: These days, Gunnar guards my throne, Ori writes my decrees, Hilda's ravens bring me the news, and Ulfa waters down my fizz. I lose my crown every day. It's on my head. Gunnar tells me so with great delicacy. He's a good guard.
textes.Aujourd'hui, L'Alambic tourne bien. Je v: Today, L'Alambic is doing well. I sell my potions to tired masters and my syrups to apprentices. I buy Mère Sauge's herbs and Berthe's honey, and Mirabelle has taken over my cellar. In the evening, I go and taste the potions of the day at the Cauldron, with a mead to rinse them down. I come home singing. Out of tune, apparently. I can't hear myself.
textes.Aujourd'hui, Mbarek a sa chambre à l'est: Today, Mbarek has his room on the east side, as he has for fifteen years. Selma has put blue boats on all my walls. A mute pirate comes to sleep above the camels one night a week. And my niece Halima turns down every husband I introduce her to. Three hundred years of Fondouk, {surnom}, and never so much work for so few weddings.
textes.Aujourd'hui, Perlée arrose, Noisette com: Today Perlée waters, Noisette counts her seeds, Lumi lights up our evenings, and Zéphyr carries our letters faster than the wind, if you believe him. Far below, on a beach, a human called Lulu watches over our mushrooms. Thanks to her, travellers like you come all the way up here. It had been so long.
textes.Aujourd'hui, avec mes quatre bras, je fa: Today, with my four arms, I make star tea, cosmic jelly and moon biscuits all at once, while saying hello. On aurora nights, everyone comes to the café, and I serve so fast the cups fly. One cup stayed in orbit. You can see it go by on Tuesdays. I wave to it.
These days, a hundred dwarves, a hundred stomachs. Dwalin, my godson, brings me coal and leaves with two bowls. Sigrun brews her fizz in my old oven. Bramm has his noon bowl, Borin his eleven o'clock ladleful, and Hilda sells me her cheese, which is alive. I see everything. I feed everything.
textes.Aujourd'hui, de huit heures à six heures: Today, from eight in the morning to six in the evening, I'm at my stall, among the squawks and the feathers. In the evening, I hang around the square or at the Crâne Fendu, where Tom lets me sing the chorus with Bartholomé. Petit-Pierre hands out the seeds, Doc treats my sniffly ones, and Silas looks at Bartholomé with funny eyes. Nobody's fought near my stall since Monday. A record!
textes.Aujourd'hui, il fixe le prix de la sardi: Today he sets the price of sardines every morning, and everyone trembles. The fishermen, the merchants, even the pirates. Me, I ask him: “How much, little one?” He tells me the price. I say: “Too dear.” And for me, he knocks off half a coin. He thinks nobody sees. Everybody sees.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'accorde les clochettes de: These days I tune the crystal bells, I write everything down in my big book and I set riddles for whoever passes by. Brindille never gets them, Pimprenelle answers before I've finished, Mélisse demands three bottles from me. And Grommelot grumbles. I write down the grumbles too. A memory doesn't pick and choose.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'accueille les visiteurs l: These days, I welcome visitors in the morning, I make labels in the afternoon, and in the evening I go to Nébula's Bazaar to see what's new. I buy everything. Nébula says I pay too much. I don't know what “too much” means. A boot that has walked on the Earth, how much is that worth? More than anything, that's how much.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai des parapluies à hélic: Today, I've got propeller umbrellas sewn by Adèle, Philibert's boxes of nothing, silent whistles, and fan-hats that the pirates of Tazira buy from me by the crate. I buy old boots for nothing, and I give change in useless objects: it's prettier than a coin. In the evening, I dine at table 1 at the Crankshaft. Tic drops by to say good evening. On time, or the other way round.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai deux îles. Celle de l': Today, I have two islands. The Mother Tree's, where Sylwen always keeps a honey loaf for me and Nimiel lies in wait with a hundred questions. And this one, where an old man waves his hat at the mist, and a blacksmith grumbles at the trees while stroking them. My mother says my heart is split in two. I think it has simply grown.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai dix mille rouleaux, un: Today, I have ten thousand scrolls, a cuttlefish who sells me her ink in exchange for songs, and three scrolls about you. Marée won't let me archive her recipes, Protée makes up history faster than I can write it, and Ondine asks me the questions I should have asked a thousand years ago. I'm swamped. It's wonderful.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai l'atelier à l'est de l: Today I've got the workshop east of the square, shelves full of lamps, and a shark who taunts me at the reef with my father's silver chisel in its jaws. I call him Mister Teeth. Triton listens to me grumble, Marée sells me her crackers, Ondine steals my offcuts. A rich life. Not in coins, alas.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai l'atelier, Copeau, et: Today, I've got the workshop, Copeau, and our two little rascals: Tornade, who falls over at the skatepark all day long, and Cerise, who draws his falls in her fanzine. I whistle instead of talking when I'm concentrating. Two notes means hello. Three means dinner's ready. One long whistle means: who's taken my spanner?
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai l'étal des armes au Gr: Today, I run the weapons stall at the Great Market. Ferronde forges, I sell, we argue over prices on Fridays. Pyrus haggles for the Guard. And next door, Zébuline and her spices. I've got nothing against spices. My nose has. In the evening, I drink a sulphur grog at the Diable Repu. No spices. I asked.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai l'étal, les jardins au: Today I've got the stall, the gardens along the edge of the dome, and Pélagos watching me whenever I cut seaweed, as if I were stealing his children. Thalassa takes my long kelp, Ianthé dances in front of my shop to draw the customers. And you bring me fish from the surface! Business has never been better.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai la forge de la terrass: These days, I've got the terrace forge, Brunna on the bellows, and an apprentice, Fundin, who's got a hole in his head. I even had a big'un once: Hector, three years on coal before he touched a hammer. And at eleven o'clock, I go and taste Dagna's stew. To check the salt. Somebody has to.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai la terrasse du Fondouk: Today, I have the Fondouk's terrace. Moulay Brahim and his games of draughts, where he cheats; Zineb and her signs; Mama Lou, at her tavern, who says her rum makes peace better than my tea. And the pirates' cook, who turns up every day with his little bag of salt. I hide the salt cellar. The rest of Tazira, I serve, and it comes back.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai le Jardin des simples,: Today, I have the Herb Garden, the greenhouse, the hives, and all the little ones of the Academy, who call me Mother even though I never had children. I've had hundreds, really. Pyra comes for her hands, Borée for his toes, Oscar for his forehead. On Sundays, I take Borée a herbal tea. And in the evening, I tell the bees everything.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai le meilleur étal du ti: Today, I have the best stall in the tianguis: copal for the gods, cacao for people, obsidian for warriors. I go up to Yaxché to buy macaw feathers, I carry Coyotl's jars all the way to Per-Hâpy, along the roads. In the evening, I listen to Nenetl play, and I count. Even the drumbeats. She could charge for them. She won't.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai le plus beau galion de: Today I have the finest galleon on Balafre and the noisiest crew. Gros-Louis eats for four, Mange-Clous cooks for three, Fil-de-Fer sees for ten, and Petit-Pierre asks questions for a hundred. Rhubarbe, my red parrot, has learned all my swear words. In the evenings, I play dice at the Shark's Tooth. I rarely lose. I never cheat. I'm not Malaterre.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai le téléphérique, le mo: Today I have the cable car, the monorail, half the sweepers, the spring beds at the Bielle and a gas tank that smells of cabbage. I chair the Fair jury, which amounts to offending everyone politely. And in the evening I sit on bench 3 on the promenade. So does Rivet. One at each end. That bench has never been so long.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai ma boutique dans mon c: Today I've got my shop in my mushroom. Zéphyr pays me in feathers, Cardamome in riddles, Pimprenelle in advice about sugar, and Grommelot pays me nothing at all, since he never buys anything. Thank goodness for big folk like you, {surnom}, with real coins in their pockets.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai ma petite boutique sur: Today, I have my little shop on the square. In the morning, I shave. In the afternoon, I bandage, I stitch, I put cold compresses on the previous night's bumps. In the evening, I drink an herbal tea by the fireplace of the Crâne Fendu, waiting for the next brawl. Joe brings me his parrots with colds, Mange-Clous brings me soup, and my geranium is doing wonderfully.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai mon atelier chez les A: Today, I have my workshop in the Artisans' Quarter. The roof is a little further away than planned. Ortie comes to sweep and count my bolts, Lumina comes to prepare the Night of Lanterns with me, and in the evening I test my rockets on the jetty, near the lighthouse. For the festival, I need sulphur crystals. Always. Lots.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai mon atelier à la Filat: These days, I have my workshop in the Spinning Mill. I cut up old clothes from the Free Shop and make them into jackets, bags, patches. I designed the Bilge Rats patch: a rat with a red mohawk and a guitar. It's sewn on half the jackets on the island. And on six dogs.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai mon salon chez les Art: Today, I have my salon in the Artisans' Quarter, between Grisette's workshop and Zigomar's. I polish, I oil, I file, and for grand occasions, I apply gold leaf. On Thursdays, I let my horns breathe at Bulle's Baths. In the evening, I go and listen to Calcine on the Great Square. Front row. Eyes closed.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai mon échoppe dans la Gr: These days, I have my shop in the Great Hall, next to the Royal Forge. Every evening, I count my rubies: one is missing. It's Ulfa. I pretend I don't know. Ori keeps my ledgers, Grimli brings me stones he can never say where he found, and the king comes to admire what he doesn't pay for.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai mon étal au Grand Marc: Today, I have my stall at the Great Market: sap potions, magic potions, star elixirs. Everything labelled, dated, tested. Zébuline supplies the chili, my mother the herbs, and Tiburce competes with me using an oil that cures nothing. In the evening, I go and sit in the Gardens. Nobody asks me there for a potion against hiccups.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai mon étal au souk. Les: Today, I have my stall in the souk. The tagine dishes of all Tazira, and Zohra's big Friday dish, the most beautiful. The jugs of La Murène Ivre, which the pirates break and I charge double for. Selma's bird jugs. And Youssef, who comes by every day, smiles at me, turns around… and breaks a bowl. Be careful when you turn around, you too.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai quarante chèvres, douz: These days, I've got forty goats, twelve crows and some golems who make the whole lot of them nervous. Kalda brings back the goats that climb too high. Dagna and Ulfa buy my cheese. The king sends me crows at midnight. And Bramm serves as a rock. Everyone in their place.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai soixante-dix ans, un b: Today, I'm seventy, I've a griddle that's hot from nine o'clock, and a tavern full every night. I count Corentin's hot honeys with beans, I keep the first crêpe for Fañch, and I let Pierrick believe he's the boss. The rest of the time, I sing. Off-key. But loud.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai trente ruches au pied: Today I have thirty hives at the foot of the tree-houses. My girls, I call them. They forage the lime trees, the clover and Miriel's roses, which annoys Miriel. I take honey to Sylwen every morning, and to Aëlwen, who haggles. The wild bees, right at the top of the Mother Tree, I never go up to.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai trente ruches. Je vend: Today, I have thirty hives. I sell honey at the maize market, cheaper than Ix Chab would like. I bring the balché honey to Ix Kanul. In the evening, I play knucklebones with Ah Kin Pech, who cheats when counting. Balam finds me wild hives, and little Kinich comes to lick the spoon. A sweet life. As it should be.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai trente-deux hamacs, je: Today, I've got thirty-two hammocks, I recount them every evening, and they're less than fifty years old. Ewen ties knots in them, Salomé rents out seaweed sacks in the hold to steal my customers, and Matthias drew me a meadow that doesn't move, for later. My aunt pretends not to know anything. She knows everything.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ai un galion pirate à mon: Today, I have a pirate galleon at my quay. They pay, so they're customers. In the afternoon, I play draughts with Hassan on the Fondouk terrace; I often win, don't ask how. Saïd rounds off my prices. Lhoucine plays until midnight, not a minute more: that's the law. And I count the seagulls at Mustapha's grill. An amin counts everything.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'arrose mes tournesols le: These days, I water my sunflowers in the morning and tell the little ones stories in the evening, around the fire. And sometimes, when the wind blows from Rainville, I hear screeching guitars. I pretend I don't like it. But I tap my foot.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'enseigne au calmecac : le: Today, I teach at the calmecac: the songs, the days, writing in pictures. Pilli sleeps at the back, with his dog. The high priest comes to give his lessons, very serious. In the evening, I sing with Nenetl in the square. And I write to the old scribe of Per-Hâpy, who answers me in signs I half understand. He half understands me too. That makes one whole letter.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'enseigne aux enfants du v: Today, I teach the village children the signs, the sums and the fine manners of Thoth. At noon, I drink Mérit's beer while rereading my papyri. My pupils call me the hippopotamus, because of my naps. They think I don't know. But Taweret, the hippopotamus goddess, protects children. So I take it as a title. Well deserved.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'enseigne le matin devant: These days, I teach in front of the blackboard in the morning, and I spend the rest of the day in my laboratory, until late at night. There's always an experiment on the boil. The auroras, I watch through the window, between two explosions. Murmure tidies my notes. I can't find anything anymore. Everything is perfectly tidy.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'enseigne les flammes à tr: Today, I teach flames to thirty little devils in the Academy courtyard. Ortie lights a candle from ten paces, Pépin catches fireflies during the exercises, and everyone still has their eyebrows. That's my greatest success. In the evening, I dance on the Great Square, and I try not to look at Zigomar.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'imprime le Boucanier chaq: Today I print the Boucanier every week, the posters with Pigment, Cerise's zine, Patchouli's pigeon horoscope. The Sergeant reads my articles on the radio with sound effects. I've got ink everywhere: on my hands, on my glasses, behind my ears. I think I've got it in my blood. Blue, probably.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'interviewe tout le monde: Today, I interview everyone in the Boucan. Tapage makes things up, I write “made up” in pencil. Clou answers “Mh”, I publish the “Mh”s. Cradoc answers upside down. I draw Pastille's plasters, I correct Agrafe's mistakes, and I do my mohawk all by myself with gel. It leans towards the future.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ouvre le comptoir à sept: These days I open the counter at seven, stamp with Clac, listen to Hilaire tell me about his failures and Rodrigue dispute his. On Sundays I have tea at Colombe's. It's the only day I don't wear my uniform. I wear another uniform, but a comfier one.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ouvre le temple à l'aube,: These days I open the temple at dawn, when the light falls on the altar. Honorine brings me bread, singing. Sister Pétronille tends the wounded and falls down the stairs. Aurore comes to sit in the evening. Gilles comes for a nap on Sundays, standing by the door. Philomène comes to wake me up. Nothing has changed since school.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'ouvre à dix heures et je: Today, I open at ten and close at one in the morning. Django on stage, Lola between the tables, Hector at the end of the counter, the Lord who pays in gold, and Kiki, my punch rival, who comes for a drink at my place after closing his. And a mystery: the jungle boat doesn't stop at mine anymore. Strange, eh?
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'écris le matin au bord du: These days, I write in the mornings by the pond in the Hanging Gardens, in the afternoons at the Museum or on the Observatory bridge, and in the evenings on my bench in the Agora. I speak to everyone in verse. It goes… so-so. The rhymes that flop, I write down in a journal. It's fatter than the one for the rhymes that work.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'écris tout : les décrets: These days I write everything: the king's decrees, Kalda's reports, Orsik's ledgers, the slates at the Blazing Mug. Three hundred and twelve decrees in ninety years of reign. The shortest: “No.” The longest is about fizz. I correct the mistakes. The king doesn't like it. The city does.
textes.Aujourd'hui, j'élève Gland avec Mamie Fa: These days, I'm raising Gland with Granny Faîne, while Mum and Dad are in the deep forest. I mend the bridges, I climb up for wild honey for Grelot, three stings and a smile, and for golden acorns from the oldest oaks, which Plumette adores. I buy Ursule's nails. Her axes, though… brrr. You don't cut down a living tree!
textes.Aujourd'hui, je bouche les trous, je man: These days, I plug holes, I eat the pancake Gwenola slips into my pocket, and I listen to Jos hammering above my head. Lucie tells me where it's seeping, under the hull. Ewen asks me how you put a ship back in the water. And my daughter, Nolwenn, sews at her window till midnight. I see her lamp. I say nothing.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je chante tous les soirs à: Today, I sing every night at the Hall, I organise the assemblies with Mamie, I chase Lisse's robots and I eat Lentille's soup while yelling ideas. We're missing a real drummer. We've had Tapage, Boulon, a dog. I'm looking. I'm still looking.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je commande douze gardes, d: Today, I command twelve guards, one of whom is asleep. I patrol the Lower Town, I check the gates, I take down the Baron's hats and I run to the Southern Fields when Mélusine rings. Every week, I meet with Mademoiselle Aurore. We compare our days. She has the Baron. I have the turnips. We take turns winning.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je compte les arbres du Bou: Today, I count the Boucan's trees, check that they're doing well, and give them names. There are forty-three in town, and thousands in the Spore Wood. I climb with Pigment when she paints up high. I sleep in a hammock. Tied to a tree, obviously.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je connais chaque client à: These days, I know every customer by their cup. Odette has her table facing the port, woe betide any tourist who sits there. The mayor comes by at noon, Colette at seven, the professor in the morning, silent as a fish. And when Raymond loses at pétanque, he comes here to sulk, in front of a coffee he doesn't drink. I see everything. It's the job.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je connais l'histoire de ch: These days, I know the story of every single thing that passes through my Free Shop. I tell it to anyone who'll listen. In the evening, I read in the old railway carriage and go dancing in the pit in my dress made of twenty-two dresses. Velours and I sewed it together. Sometimes people mistake me for a pile of clothes. It's flattering.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je construis tout ce qu'on: Today, I build whatever people ask for: benches, stages, stairs for the Boxes, a treehouse newsroom for Cerise, a skate ramp for Tornade. In the evening, I play ball with them and lose on purpose. Tornade knows. He lets me lose. He's a good boy.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je couds les chapeaux du Ba: These days I sew the Baron's hats, Rodrigue's capes, Violette's outfits and Hilaire's trousers. On Sundays I have tea with Églantine. She sorts my buttons by colour without realising. I don't stop her. I mix them up again once she's gone, so she can start over.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je crie les nouvelles sur l: These days, I shout the news on the Great Square, I announce rank promotions, and I ring the alerts. Bertrand sings during my announcements, I ring during his choruses, we're a duo he doesn't know about. Noisette rings Marguerite once a week. Ferdinand sighs every time. I like Ferdinand. You can hear his sighs all the way to the square.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je cueille la menthe le mat: Today, I pick mint in the morning, make the cordials in the afternoon and serve until midnight. Mint, strawberry, elderflower, violet, and “mystery”. My notebook holds every order from every gig for fifteen years. Rouille drinks her honey lemon, Mouette her lemonade with a seagull straw, and Larsen shouts.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je cuisine de huit heures d: These days, I cook from eight in the morning to ten at night. Radis brings me his vegetables, Sirène her mint, Trocante her old jars. People pay what they can. Nothing, one coin, thirty coins. At the end of the month, there's always a bit missing. And every month, someone fills the gap without saying a word.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je danse tous les soirs d'a: Today, I dance every aurora night on the Agora, in front of the fountain, while Vibrato plays. I never get up before ten. In the morning, I rehearse in the Zero-Gravity Garden, where I can leap so high the sky jellyfish say hello. They blush. In blue.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je dessine le matin sur le: These days, I draw in the morning on the lookout of the Gate, around noon at the Museum, and in the afternoon a bit everywhere: on the Observatory bridge, in the Gardens, at the top of the Spaceport Tower. Halo talks to me a lot. Zénith shows me stars. Me, I draw. In the evening, I count the lights of the islands. There are more and more of them.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je dirige l'Académie Infern: Today, I run the Infernal Academy. I set the exams, I mark the papers, and in the evening I fly up to the top of the tower to look at the city. Miss Ombreline has been asking for a book back for sixty-three years, little Pépin escapes from my lessons, and I love my job. Even on marking days.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je donne des conseils aux n: These days, I give advice to the newcomers. Lison, Rodrigue, even little Titouan: they all listen. They all succeed. Me, I fail, but I fail methodically. I even have a register of my failures at Odon's. It's very thick. It's the most-read book in the dungeon.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je donne mon cours sur la p: These days, I teach my class on the square every day at four. I've still got the cat, and now Zoé, who learns fast. The kids prefer Titou's show on the other side of the fountain, but I'm not giving up. And once a week I take the boat for Fanny's croissants. Cheerful, I tell you!
textes.Aujourd'hui, je donne une deuxième vie a: These days, I give old sails a second life: red and blue awnings, curtains for homes, bags, hammocks for Pierrick. Jos forges my needles, Lucie gives me a pearl every birthday, and Salomé resells my offcuts for three times the price. And every day, I watch the ship's original great sail fall to tatters under the yard.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je dors le matin et je vis: These days, I sleep in the morning and live at night. From six in the evening until dawn, I'm at the great telescope, on the Observatory islet. During the auroras, everyone looks at the colours; I look behind them. There are stars waiting to be noticed. I notice them all. It's my job. It's my joy.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je fabrique toutes les lant: Today, I make all of Pandémonia's lanterns, and I look after the seven Great Lanterns: the port's, the market's, the arena's, the baths', the academy's, the forge's and the square's. Nox lights the street lamps, Zigomar prepares the rockets, Grandpa tells stories. And on the Night of Lanterns, the whole city dances.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je fais des haches, des pel: These days, I make axes, shovels, corsair sabres for the caravanners who like dressing up, and needles for Nolwenn. Tobias complains about the noise above his head. In the evening, I have a sparkling apple by the beach fire or at Gwenola's counter. And I dream of a piece of metal nobody knows.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je fais l'aller-retour entr: These days, I go back and forth between the village and Port-Azur, five coins one way. At night, I steer by Anselme's lighthouse: two lantern calls, two flashes in reply. Little Nina rings the departure bell. Lola, my passenger who never went back, gives me her letters for her mother. And every evening, as I come alongside, I look for Hortense on the promenade. She's always there.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je fais le taxi pour les to: These days, I run a taxi service for the Spaceport tourists, I race anything that flies, and sometimes I drop Solenne off down below, in secret. In the afternoon, I go running in the Zero-Gravity Garden. In the evening, I eat an ice cream, if I can find one. During the auroras, I don't fly. It's the only thing in the sky I don't want to overtake.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je fais le tour du Vieux Ba: These days, I walk round the Old Dock in the morning, and in the afternoon I go to the Pebble Beach, to Gravier's, who gives fish heads to the dogs. In the evening, I leave them with Boulon and go dance in the pit. I talk to humans a bit now. A bit. The dogs taught me.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je fais les comptes, le cou: Today I do the accounts, the post, the audiences and the hat inventory. I catch the Baron's promises before they land, I show Mr Prosper to the door, and every week I compare my worries with Captain Ferdinand's. In the evening I go and sit in the temple. It's the only quiet place. Father Clotaire snores softly.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je fais les jarres de Tlalo: Today, I make Tlaloc's jars and the pots for the tianguis. Tochtli takes some jars all the way to Per-Hâpy. Nenetl plays her drum next door, and my pots shake on the shelves. Little Pilli comes to help me fill the jars at the lake. In the evening, I dance a little. Wet, as always. It comes with the job.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je forge les épées des aven: These days I forge the adventurers' swords, the guard's spears, everybody's nails, and Mélusine's bell when it cracks. Titouan minds the counter and burns aprons. Madame Olga wants to enchant my blades. In the evening I take a stroll through the Lower Town and challenge people to arm-wrestling. Nobody accepts anymore. Except Clovis, with his flour.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je garde l'entrée. Orophin: These days I guard the entrance. Orophin runs the forest for me. Sylwen leaves me bread. Caelan plays. All night. Gilwen nags me about her bees, Haldir never tells me where he's going, and Ilyria says “luck” when I hit an apple. I keep an eye on them all. It's to keep them safe. They don't know that.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je garde la Porte Nord. Le: These days, I guard the North Gate. In the morning, Honorine sends me bread. Captain Isidore comes by with his seagulls, who peck my helmet to wake me up. I give them my crusts. On Sundays, I have a nap at the temple, standing by the door, with Father Clotaire. We don't talk. We understand each other.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je garde la bibliothèque du: These days, I look after the library from morning to night. The Academy students come to read in silence. Quasar comes looking for formulas, making a lot of noise. Vibrato goes past my window with his theremin. I whisper to everyone: “…quieter.” They try. They're kind. They can't manage it.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je garde la grille du donjo: Today, I guard the dungeon gate, at the foot of the Fangs, and I keep the register: everyone's name, the deepest floor they reached. I sell Aubin's potions and ropes. Hilaire has a hundred lines saying “floor 1, slipped”. Philomène comes to argue with me about the fourth floor. In the evening, I listen to the dungeon go “gloop”. I sleep well.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je garde le Cœur-Brasier et: Today, I keep the Ember Heart and the Brasier key. I sweep, I listen, I feed the fire. Lumina comes every evening to light her wick there, Ignatia comes to sit beside me when she has worries, and Ébène comes to lose at draughts. Well, he thinks he's winning. I don't contradict him.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je garde le Portail du mati: Today, I keep the Gate from morning till night. I watch the welcome buoy, far below on the sea. When someone steps into the beam, my halo lights up all by itself. On aurora nights, I stay on the lookout. I always have a speech in my pocket, in case someone comes up in the middle of the night.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je garde les racines, je ch: These days I guard the roots, I chase off the will-o'-the-wisps and I look after my fireplace. With crystal shards. For the warmth. The glitter-gnat wants to buy them off me, the sky thief digs holes, the magician turns me into a frog. Brindille, now, she says hello. That's my lot. Bah.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je gouverne Port-Coutelas d: Today, I govern Port-Coutelas from my veranda and my front steps. My programme is moving forward: the quay lanterns are up, the new pontoon is under study, and the ban on Sunday brawls has been respected once. Monsieur Lunette drew the official map of the city. In the evening, I make my speeches on the square, by the gallows. It serves no purpose. Like my guards, whom I don't have.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je gouverne des fuites, des: These days, I govern leaks, neighbours' quarrels and the price of sparkling apple. Tobias swears the hull will hold, Grégoire keeps watch, Matthias dreams of opening what would be better left shut, and Ewen rings the bell whenever he likes. In the evening, on the poop deck, I watch Stoneheart turn red. It reminds me I'm not in command of everything.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je jongle sur la Place des: These days, I juggle on Pallet Square, blow giant bubbles with Lentille's washing-up liquid, and ride my unicycle at the skatepark, where I fall a lot. Pastille sewed cushions into my trousers. My audience: children, dogs, pigeons. The pigeons are the toughest crowd.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je joue du matin au soir su: Today I play from morning till night on the Great Square. In the evening, people dance: Sulfura, Brindille, Ferronde and her Pyrus, who dances like a drawbridge. Tiburce sits in the front row and sighs off the beat. And when Nox lights the first street lamp, I play his waltz. He thinks I haven't noticed.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je joue l'après-midi près d: These days I play in the afternoon by the fountain, and in the evening on the Guild stage. Mélusine rings her bell during my choruses, Rodrigue orders tragedies from me that turn into comedies, Tancrède tells me his imaginary deeds. Lison is the only one who listens to the end. She says nothing, but she stays.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je joue tous les soirs au C: Today, I play every evening at the Crâne Fendu. Jigs for dancing, laments for crying, and the Song of the Brawl King, with a verse for Gros-Louis, a silence for the Silent One and a big BOOM for Belle-Humeur. I'm the one who keeps the brawlers' board. In the morning, I sleep. In the afternoon, I write on the bench by the bay. La la la!
textes.Aujourd'hui, je joue tous les soirs d'au: Today, I play every aurora night on the Agora, in front of the fountain. Prisme dances, the sky lights up, and my hands move all by themselves. During the day, I rehearse in the Zero-Gravity Garden, where notes float longer. One stayed in the air until noon. Photon says his flowers danced.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je lis l'avenir dans la faç: Today, I read the future in the way my pigeons peck: Nostradamus, Madame Irma, Petit-Gris, Voyant, and Bernard. Bernard doesn't predict anything, he eats. I write the pigeon horoscope for Agrafe's fanzine and for the Sergeant's radio. People say it's always true. I write things like “you will breathe”.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je lis à la Guilde, je lis: These days, I read at the Guild, I read at the lookout, I read on the bench in the Upper Town. Pétronille counts my lightning strikes, I count her falls. Madame Olga lends me spellbooks and Monsieur Aubin makes me potions that change my colour. Sir Tancrède says I'm a great mage. His hair is still frizzy.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je livre toute la cité en u: Nowadays, I deliver to the whole city in one morning. I know every address, every door and every dog. I have a Brasier coffee at Grumbald's at noon, I borrow the Captain's telescope, and I try to deliver the news before Hurla shouts it. I never manage. In the evening, I dance.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je m'entraîne dans la cour: Today, I train in the castle courtyard in the mornings, patrol the ramparts in the afternoons, and in the evenings, I tell of my exploits at the tavern. Mamie Rissole serves me four helpings. Bertrand puts my stories into songs. Titouan listens with his eyes wide open. It's for him that I'd like them to be true.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je m'entraîne sur le rempar: These days, I train on the rampart in the morning, hunt at the edge of the wood in the afternoon, and in the evening, I eat. Mostly cakes. Honorine saves me éclairs on Thursdays. Brunehaut fits my arrowheads. Bertrand sings about me. Rodrigue gives me speeches. I say “no”. He leaves.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je m'occupe de la cour, des: These days, I look after the yard, the hens, the fields, and Gaubert, who talks to his turnips. In the afternoon, I go to the market to check that Babette's apples are still too red. They are. In the evening, I mend my net. It's thirty years old. It has caught thousands of turnips, two hens, and Gaubert once.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je m'occupe de la lumière d: These days, I do the lighting at the Hall with Larsen, the Sergeant's radio, the fairy lights on Boulon's crane. I wire the fountain to the crane, Cradoc's balls to batteries, Copeau's saw to fairy lights. Nobody asked me to. But everyone's happy. Almost.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je m'occupe des Jardins sus: These days, I look after the Hanging Gardens, west of the Agora: flowers as big as doors, glowing fruit, ponds, and the great water lily that blooms once a century. I get up at five to listen to the flowers sing the sunrise. They sing out of tune. But with so much heart.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je me lève avant Clou, ce q: These days, I get up before Clou, which isn't hard: he sleeps on the cash box. I beat iron until noon, I sell in the afternoon, I count in the evening. Clou means “nail”: I named him after my first one. Bent, but he holds. Customers climb up, complain about the prices, buy anyway. That's enough for me. Almost.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je me lève avant le soleil,: These days, I get up before the sun, I say good morning to my turnips, I work the fields, and when Mélusine's bell rings, I watch the whole town run through my fields. Ulric wants my turnips for his kitchen. Babette wants my turnips for her stall. The turnips want freedom. Me, I want my soup.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je me lève tôt, je vais au: These days, I get up early, go down to the lake to fetch the frogs Yvon has caught, and cook all day. Twenty recipes. In the evening, the inn is full of adventurers who've been swallowed. They eat frog for revenge. Babette sells me her vegetables. Gaubert promises me turnips. The turnips don't agree.
These days, I get up at four. Clovis brings me the flour and pretends to catch his breath outside my door. I make the bread for the castle, the temple, the Guild, and Thursday's éclairs for Lison. Noisette goes off following the adventurers. In the evening, on the square, she tells me everything. I sing myself to sleep.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je me lève à six heures, je: Today I get up at six, take the register of my vegetables and read them a chapter of botany. Lentille tells me how they ended up, in the soup. Sirène picks my mint. Bardane checks my trees. And Mother Morille claims to have a bigger pumpkin than mine. She cheats. I'll prove it.

Today, I get up at six, make the day's pies and keep an eye on the hall. Hugues eats at the end of the counter, Tancrède eats for four, Hilaire eats while telling of his failures. And little Noisette sneaks by for her slice. I pretend not to see her. I give her two.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je me lève, je choisis mon: Nowadays I get up, choose my hat, and Aurore tells me it's not the right day for it. I receive the townsfolk in the throne room, I call them all by name, I promise things, and Aurore writes them down to know which ones we can keep. In the evening, I wave to the town from the rampart. Mélusine waves back.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je mixe nuit et jour, ou pr: These days, I mix night and day, more or less: when I sleep for two hours, Tchoum minds the decks and nobody can tell the difference. There's Zoé who cries at sunrise, Lulu who says the fairies are listening, Momo who jumps, Nono who creaks. I compose for them. “Low Tide” is all their hearts together, a hundred and forty-five times a minute.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je nourris le Requin matin: Today, I feed the Shark morning and evening, and at noon I lend a hand at the Crâne Fendu's fireplace, because Mama Grog doesn't know how to measure chilli. In the afternoon, I go to the nets. The jungle is my larder: bananas, coconuts, mushrooms, and chillies hot enough to make a crocodile cry. Gros-Louis finishes everything. Petit-Pierre peels the onions. Bliss.
Today, I talk from morning till night. The Rat's Wake-Up Call, Trocante's small ads, Patchouli's pigeon horoscope, Agrafe's Boucanier with sound effects, the live gig. And the alerts, when the robots land. I've got a thousand listeners and three seagulls. The seagulls are the most loyal.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je pars en « promenade » pr: Today, I go on a “stroll” almost every week. Comète drops me off discreetly at the edge of an island and comes back for me in the evening. I bring back songs for the Elder, objects for Orbe, recipes for Gloubi. Officially, I've never left. Unofficially, there's sand in every one of my shoes.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je passe le matin au temple: Today, I spend the mornings at the temple and the afternoons at the Guild, in case someone comes back hurt. Violette and I compare our falls of the day. Sire Tancrède tells me about his exploits. I heal him from his falls. He says they're war wounds. I pretend to believe him.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je passe mes journées au pi: Today, I spend my days at the foot of the Spire, with my meters. In the morning, Ionie comes by, and I give her the coffee I “made too much of.” At noon, I eat fast. On aurora nights, I stay there while the others watch the sky. Me, I watch the curves. They dance too.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je passe mes journées dans: These days, I spend my days in the Greenhouse, feeding, caring, listening. In the evening, I go to the Zero-Gravity Garden to see the jellyfish falling upwards there. During the auroras, I watch them light up from the Observatory bridge. They look like swimming lanterns. I cry every time. With happiness.

These days, I spend my days in the Bubble District, repairing, enlarging, inventing. I make a bubble for every new Lumen. Tempo's opens exactly on the hour. Quark's only opens if you pull a face. On aurora nights, I watch the sky settle on my domes. That's why I make them round.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je passe mes journées à la: Today, I spend my days at the bow of the Shark, eye on the horizon. When a sail stays still out at sea, I don't let it out of my sight. In the evening, I play dice at the Shark's Tooth. Badly. Philémon lends me his spyglass, Petit-Pierre finds my glasses, and Gros-Louis laughs at my green lights. I see everything. Nearly everything.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je peins le Mur d'Expressio: Today I paint the Expression Wall in the morning, posters with Agrafe in the evening, and at night I repaint in colour whatever Lisse's robots have painted grey. In the morning, they go over it in grey. At night, I go over it in flowers. It's our little dance. I think I'm leading.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je perce des étoiles à huit: Today I pierce eight-pointed stars, the hardest of my life. At night, Selma comes to paint the shadows on my walls. On the pirates' galleon, seven of my lanterns shine above the cannons. And the lights you see at night in the caves, behind the Skala, aren't mine. I know all of mine, {surnom}. Not those ones.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je photographie la teuf tou: These days, I photograph the party every night. Nono turning into a wave, Lulu looking like a fairy, Titou who's never in focus. I buy glow sticks by the box in Port-Azur. I never have enough: people borrow them, throw them, lose them in the sea. Especially Titou. Him most of all.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je plonge le matin et je da: These days, I dive in the morning and dance at night. Dancing is like swimming: you let yourself be carried, you don't fight the current. Zoé's learning to dive with me; she swallows half the bay and laughs. Every week Mistral asks me when I'll go to Atlantis. I tell him: when I've danced enough.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je porte les lettres de Per: These days, I carry Perlée's letters to her sister, Mélisse's crates of nectar, seeds for Noisette and the queen's petals for a human lady on the beach. And did you know there's a big balloon named after me, on the big island to the east? A balloon that puffs smoke! And slow, too. I've been offended ever since it existed.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je pose les conteneurs des: Today, I set down the containers for the Boxes, one by one. Every container becomes a home. I know every family. When they move, I lift the whole house, with the kids inside if they want. In the evening, I go to Gravier's fire, then into the pit at the Hall. The little ones hang on to my arms.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je prie Huitzilopochtli à l: Today, I pray to Huitzilopochtli at dawn, I teach at the calmecac, and I watch over the two shrines: the blue one of Tlaloc, the red one of the sun. Citlali keeps the codices, Mixtli keeps his pride, Tochtli keeps his prices, and little Pilli tries to climb the stairs. The sun rises every morning. That's what matters.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je préside le Conseil le ma: Today, I preside over the Council in the morning, I take a nap at noon, and I cheat at lunar chess in the afternoon. On aurora nights, I take my bench on the Agora. The little ones come and snuggle up against me and ask me why the sky is dancing. I tell them it's happy that we're looking at it. It's true, I think.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je préside les assemblées s: Today, I chair the assemblies on the roof, I knit scarves for everyone and I keep an eye on my little ones: Rouille, Clou, Mouette, and the others, all the others. They call me Mamie. I never had children. I have two hundred. It's more tiring, but it's more fun.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je pêche au bout du ponton,: These days, I fish at the end of the jetty, I ferry the rare visitors across, and I know every current round the island by its pet name. At noon, a mead at Berthe's; in the evening, my table and my slice of pie. Once a year, I take Borée round the island. The jetty, I lengthened it with Théophraste's ladders. Don't ask.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je pêche de cinq heures à m: These days I fish from five till noon, sleep in the afternoon, and dance at night. I make the earplugs myself, out of candle wax, and give them to the newcomers. Rule number one, always. I'm thirty-two and I still haven't found a rule number three. As we say round here: two is already plenty.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je pêche à l'aube, je tremb: These days, I fish at dawn, I tremble at noon, I sell my catch to Ulric and I note down the swallowed adventurers in my notebook. Hilaire is in the lead: forty-seven. Sister Pétronille comes to pray for me by the water. Captain Isidore makes fun of me because I fish in a lake. He doesn't know the Duchess.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je raconte au cercle, sous: These days, I tell stories at the circle, under the garlands. Nimiel is always in the front row, Orophin goes off to check my stories in the forest, Rúmil listens while mending his nets. And when the wind blows from the west, I can hear Barnabé singing on his beach. Sometimes I fall asleep in the middle. They put a flower on my nose.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je raconte les légendes sur: Today, I tell legends on a bench on the Great Square. My daughter Germaine squabbles with Babette over turnips. Her husband Gaubert talks to his vegetables. Olga trades me herbal teas for stories. Odon argues with me about the dungeon. And little Noisette listens to me with eyes as big as saucers. She reminds me of myself, behind the hay.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je raconte mes histoires au: These days, I tell my stories to the kids in the old railway carriage, I eat four bowls of soup at Lentille's and pay with anecdotes, and in the evening, when there's no drummer, I fill in. I play too loud, too long, too everything. The youngsters roll their eyes. Then they jump.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je recolle les genoux de Ni: These days, I patch up Nimiel's knees, I make Faelar drink his herbal teas and I listen to Caelan sigh, one hand on his heart, the other on my counter. Ilyria leaves me flowers on the sly. I pretend I don't know who. And yes, I count my coins. Potions don't grow on their own.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je règle le son de la Halle: These days, I do the sound at the Howling Hall every night. From my desk, I see everything: the stage, the pit, Sirène's bar, Mamie Barricade on the mezzanine signalling me to turn it down. I turn it down. A bit. Fusible does the lights next to me. When I shout “LOUDER”, he adds more light.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je salue Rê à l'aube, je re: Today, I greet Rê at dawn, I fill the lamps, I answer questions. In the afternoon, Khéty ferries me across the river to the valley temple, singing out of tune for the fish. In the evening, I mourn the dying sun. And everywhere, a little shadow follows me with a sistrum: Nebet. She shakes it too hard. Rê doesn't complain.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je siège au Conseil à côté: Today, I sit on the Council next to the Elder and Tempo. I prepare the ceremonies, I proofread the speeches, and I decree. I decree a lot. Yesterday, I decreed that the third bench of the Agora was protocolary. Nobody sits on it anymore. I sit there alone, on aurora nights. It's the best one.
These days, I heal from morning till night. Comète, who falls off everything. Écliptique, who falls off the podium. Quark, who falls off bridges. Volt, who comes once a month for his antennae, which never have anything wrong with them. The glug-glugs, the jellyfish, and once, Glorb, cut in two by a door. I stuck him back together. He's a bit taller now.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je soigne les genoux d'Ewen: These days, I patch up Ewen's knees, the fishermen's sunburns and the headaches the morning after a big feast. Lucie brings me my seaweed, Corentin hides his hot honey drinks in my storeroom, and Pierrick comes to see me about illnesses he makes up. Well… almost all made up.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je suis au hangar dès six h: These days, I'm in the hangar from six o'clock. Volt brings me a coffee he “made too much of”. I repair Comète's saucers, which she breaks racing the seagulls. I have solid-light tools that come in every size. And a real hammer from Cliquetis, because light goes straight through nails.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je suis canonnier de la Mor: Today, I'm the gunner of the Morue Enragée. In the morning, I watch the quay. At noon, I sit under the gallows: nobody comes to talk to me there. In the evening, I stay by the fireplace of the Crâne Fendu, or I guard the door of the Shark's Tooth for Ignace. My name is on Tom's board, with Gros-Louis and the Mute. They call themselves champions. HA.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je suis en troisième premiè: Today I'm in my third first year. That's a record. Mornings, lessons in the courtyard; afternoons, I read in the library with a little bell on my chair, or I set fire to dummies on the Duelling Ground. Pip follows me everywhere, Gérard watches me from the roof. And in the evening, I make a wish at the Founder's fountain. Always the same one.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je suis la version trois po: Today, I am version three point seven. I give the tour from eight a.m. to ten p.m. Fifteen stops. I've done it two hundred and forty thousand times. The children know it by heart. Quark walks through me. Pixel recites along with me. At night, I go into standby, and I dream of the tour. It goes well.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je suis maître du Port des: These days, I'm harbour master of Seagull Harbour. I keep an eye on the quays, I register the boats, and I negotiate with Bigorneau, who steals mackerel from the fishmonger's. I live in the old lighthouse, which Monsieur Prosper sold me swearing it was a house. I stop by to say hello to Gilles at the North Gate. My seagulls peck his helmet. He says thank you.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je suis maîtresse de l'Arèn: Today, I'm mistress of the Arena of Horns. I organise the fights, I announce the champions, I get the crowd on its feet. The Tournament of Horns is my baby: four rounds, and Gorgoth at the end. In the evening, I go down to the port to meet my pal Moloka. We shout together. It's relaxing.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je suis maîtresse de la Gra: Today, I'm mistress of the Great Forge. I forge the grates, the bells, the anchors for the port and the blades that Kraxx sells by making up stories about them. I borrow embers from the Heart, Brother Cendrin grumbles, and I laugh. In the evening, I dance with Pyrus, and Ortie explains to me why hammers are old hat.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je suis quartier-maître : j: Today, I'm quartermaster: I keep the cash box, the hammocks and the Widow's quarrels. In the morning, I train on deck: seven knives in the same knot-hole, that's my mark. In the evening, I play dice at the Crâne Fendu. A brawl breaks out? So much the better. I put my blades away, the Code is the Code, and I roll up my sleeves. It livens things up.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je suis second du Requin Bo: Today, I'm first mate of the Requin Borgne and the crew's champion. My name is on Tom's board, at the Crâne Fendu, next to the Mute and Belle-Humeur. In the morning I work, at noon I eat, in the afternoon I carry crates, and in the evening I lose at dice. Petit-Pierre follows me everywhere. I pretend it bugs me. It doesn't bug me at all.
Today I fell four times. And you, Violette, how many lightning bolts?
textes.Aujourd'hui, je suis à Astralys. Quatre: Today, I'm in Astralys. Four stars in my guidebook! Glowing Lumens, a fountain that changes planets, auroras every evening, and down below, the sea! Water that moves all by itself, like me, but huge. I was supposed to stay three days. It's been three months. The Lumens say that's exactly how it all started for them.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je tiens la boutique sur la: Today I run the shop on the Great Square, next to Madame Olga's. She sells magic, I sell science, and we both make people change colour, each in our own way. Odon resells my potions at the dungeon. Violette tests my anti-lightning potions. Gilles tests my stay-awake potions. It's not a success.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je tiens la grande table de: Today, I run the big table at the Shark's Tooth, from four in the afternoon to four in the morning. I don't drink, I don't play for myself, I never fight: I have two friends at the back of the room for that. I can hear a loaded die before it touches the baize. Monsieur Malaterre knows it. At my table, he plays honest. He loses more often.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je tiens le Crâne Fendu de: Today, I run the Crâne Fendu from ten in the morning to two at night. Tom plays on the stage, Tonneau props up the bar, Mange-Clous puts too much chilli in my pot, and the bruisers' board sits in pride of place above the bottles. The Governor makes speeches, and I'm the one people listen to. Brawls, fine. But you pay FIRST.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je tiens le Diable Repu. On: Today, I run the Diable Repu. We serve hot sulphur punch, without a drop of alcohol, Brasier coffee and my frozen lava. The Captain tells his storm, Kraxx sneezes, Moloka laughs, and Bobor comes to “settle” which of our desserts is best. In the evening, it's the loveliest noise in the world.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je tiens le Point Soins à l: Today I run the First-Aid Post at the entrance to the Cannery, and in the afternoons I set up near the skatepark. Tornade's knees, Cradoc's elbows, Copeau's splinters, the thorns in Chaussette's dogs. My plasters have kittens and smiling skulls on them. Cerise draws them with me.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je tiens ma boutique sur la: Today, I keep my shop on the Great Square, I trade legends with Philomène for herbal teas, I tease Aubin about his science and I enchant Brunehaut's swords without her permission. Little Violette comes to see me every week. I lend her books and whisper ideas to her. She thinks she read them.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je tiens mon étal de six he: These days I run my stall from six to six. I sell apples to Lison, vegetables to Ulric, mushrooms to Rissole, and I buy the golden turnips the adventurers catch. Germaine comes by in the afternoon to criticise my apples. I criticise her turnips. Clovis comes by in the evening and sighs. Honorine makes turnovers with my apples.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je tiens mon étal du matin: Today, I run my stall from morning till night. On my left, Bobor and his brioches; on my right, Kraxx and his swords, sneezing all day long. In the evening, I go and see my father at the port, then I go home to tuck Pépin in. He tells me about his day three times. He falls asleep on the third.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je tisse les capes, les voi: These days I weave the cloaks, the sails and the ribbons for the festivals. Nessa wears out one ribbon a season, Aëlwen pretends not to see my flowers, Thalion keeps watch over the square, and I keep watch over Thalion. From up here I can see the whole village. Everything. Even a musician practising the same line, all alone, in front of the fountain.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je travaille sur le Sans-Pi: Today, I work on the Merciless from morning till night. Forty planks replaced, the whole side caulked, the keel set straight again. Coquille comes to sing while I hammer, Brutus forges my ironwork, and Old Silas tells me ship stories by the fire on the shore. In the evening, a cider at the Crâne Fendu. Carène cider. Almost like back home.
