textes.Aujourd'hui, je travaille à la capitaine: These days, I work at the harbour master's office, under the Admiral's eye, on a map two metres wide. The coasts are finished, or nearly: they move. In the middle, there's still a big blank, Stoneheart. Lucie brings me her stones, Corentin his stories, Grégoire his lights. I write it all down. Even what doesn't add up. Especially that.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je tricote des bonnets pour: These days, I knit woolly hats for all of Rainville. The young ones play guitar very loud in their garage. They think I hate it. I knit in rhythm. One row per song. My finest hat is forty songs long.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je trie mes graines le soir: These days, I sort my seeds in the evening with Lumi's fireflies, Perlée waters my pots, and the queen lets me plant things just about everywhere. Even where I shouldn't: there's a sprout growing in her crown. And in my pocket, I've got my treasure. Nobody knows. Don't look at my pocket. Stop looking at my pocket!
textes.Aujourd'hui, je veux construire le Lisse: Today, I want to build the Lisse-Center: four hundred shops, two thousand parking spaces, a fountain that plays the company anthem. It would be my masterpiece. But there are these punks. These painted flowers. That music, at night. And my son, who taps on all my files. The obstacles are… numerous.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je vis dans ma roulotte, au: Today I live in my caravan, among the giant mushrooms that light up every evening. Bardane gives them names. Gravier brings me driftwood. Ferraille welded me a chimney. Radis claims my pumpkin cheats. And the mushlings steal my socks. They always give them back. Full of spores.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je vis dans ma tour, au-des: Today, I live in my tower, above the port. In the morning, I draw. At noon, I eat on the bench by the bay, and Fil-de-Fer tells me what he's seen from the top of his mast. In the afternoon, I redraw what has changed. When the fog lifts, I can see all the way to Arcanelle. Silas comes to tell me about Barbe-Sanglante, and I note everything in the margins. My margins are full.
textes.Aujourd'hui, je vis à l'envers. La nuit,: These days, I live upside down. At night, I'm at my telescope; in the morning, I sleep; at noon, I have breakfast at Berthe's; in the afternoon, I read at the library, or I go and daydream in front of the door of the Crypt. I note down stars, comets, and sometimes fireflies. Fireflies are a common mistake. In my case, at least.
Today, the Duelling Ground is mine. Five braziers, three straw dummies, apprentices with singed eyebrows, and Oscar. At noon, I eat at Berthe's; in the evening, I drink a Murène rum there, when Mathurin has left me some. I shout a lot. I teach the young ones to put out what they light. That's the hardest part. Nobody wants to learn that.
textes.Aujourd'hui, l'après-midi, je fais le cl: These days, in the afternoons, I clown around on the village square for the kids. I juggle coconuts, I fall on purpose, I invent dance steps: the lovestruck crab, the shy octopus. And at night, the party is my own show. Nobody watches me, everybody dances. That's what's great about it. Yo!
textes.Aujourd'hui, la Chope Ardente est pleine: These days, the Blazing Mug is packed every night. The king sings off-key, Bramm drinks from his father's mug, Nori drinks WATER, and I hide one of Orsik's rubies a night in the empty barrel at the back. The stew comes from Dagna's, the cheese from Hilda's. And me, I make the noise!
textes.Aujourd'hui, la Morue se balance à l'anc: Today, the Cod rocks at anchor in the middle of the bay, and I rock on my chair, at the big table in the Shark's Tooth. Crochet watches my back, Belle-Humeur watches my door, Coquille watches my helm, when I'm not gambling it. Round my neck, Gontran's silver compass, won honestly. Well… won.
textes.Aujourd'hui, la Veuve est amarrée au pon: Today, the Widow is moored at the east pontoon. Scarlett runs the crew, the Silent One runs the sails, Tonneau runs the bar. In the evening, I play at the big table in the Shark's Tooth. I lose more than I win. And there's this business of forty coins with Mama Grog. A matter of principle: her grog that Tuesday was lukewarm. She says it wasn't.
Today, the library is mine. Professor Malachar has owed me a book for sixty-three years, Gorgoth borrows poems he holds like butterflies, Brindille flies between the shelves, and someone borrows collections through the window, at night. I leave the window open. And a candle. It's my only untidiness.
textes.Aujourd'hui, le Bazar galactique est ouv: Today, the Galactic Bazaar is open from eight a.m. to eight p.m., and all through the aurora night, because the nebula flowers open when the sky lights up. I set my prices by the planet in the fountain. When it's Jupiter, it's expensive. When it's the Moon, it's almost free. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Aujourd'hui, le jour, je vends mes colli: These days, in the daytime, I sell my necklaces at the village market, on a stall with Marley and his bananas. At night, I dance and jump, every night a little higher than the night before. I have contests with Titou, I make Zoé laugh, I borrow stuff from Bastien. And Sofia brings me shells from the bottom of the sea. The good life, bro.
textes.Aujourd'hui, le matin, je dors. Tard. Pu: Nowadays, in the morning, I sleep. Late. Then I mend the Widow's casks on the quay: not one ever leaks, on my cooper's honour. In the afternoon and evening, I'm at Mama Grog's bar, or at the Shark's Tooth's, or on the way between the two. Coralie tattooed a horse on my back. I've never seen it. Scarlett says it's magnificent. Hic!
textes.Aujourd'hui, le matin, je dors. Vers dix: These days, in the morning, I sleep. Around ten, I go to the stela to explain the date of creation to yawning youngsters. In the afternoon, a cacao at Ix Chab's, then the observatory until the middle of the night. Between two stars, I play knucklebones with Yum Kab. I win, because I count. He says it's cheating. It's mathematics.
textes.Aujourd'hui, le matin, je m'assois près: Nowadays, in the morning, I sit by the fire on the shore and watch Gwen bring the Merciless back to life. In the afternoon, I tell stories to Petit-Pierre, on the quay. In the evening, by the fireplace at the Crâne Fendu, I tell them to whoever wants. Philémon notes everything in his margins, Sans-Dents believes nothing, and Joe's parrot looks at me as if he recognises me. He does recognise me.
textes.Aujourd'hui, le matin, je soigne mes ban: These days, in the morning, I look after my banana trees, I talk to them like Barnabé does. In the daytime, I run the market stall with Momo. And at night, I dance, with bananas for everyone. Fanny still won't have banana croissants. But I'm not giving up hope. Family always ends up tasting. What else?
textes.Aujourd'hui, le moulin tourne du matin a: These days the mill turns from morning till night. I take flour to Honorine's, I buy an apple from Babette, who always asks how Honorine is, and I blush under the flour. In the evening I sit on the Great Square, and the children call me “the snowman”. Brunehaut challenges me to arm-wrestling. I win when I sneeze.
textes.Aujourd'hui, les Thermes ont trois bassi: Today, the Baths have three pools, steam, and the Gorgoth Bath, built for Gorgoth: when he got into the big pool, everyone got out. By the wave. Bobor floats in the evening, Tiburce lets his horns “breathe” on Thursdays, and my mother bathes at half price. Me, I do the bubbles.
textes.Aujourd'hui, les runes de garde s'efface: These days, the guardian runes are fading, the mountain rumbles and the golems no longer recognise anyone. Ori, my great-nephew, copies down everything I say. The king comes down to ask me about the future. Ulfa asks me why I drink water. I give them all the same answer: patience.
textes.Aujourd'hui, ma boutique est ouverte de: Today, my shop is open from nine in the morning to eight at night. I buy everything: pearls, rubies, crocodile teeth, crystal shards, shells. I sell a bit of everything: rum, little keys, and dice that roll… better. Sylvain buys them back from me every month to throw them into the sea. Business is good. Business is always good. Me, I count.
textes.Aujourd'hui, ma petite-fille Lumina fabr: Today, my granddaughter Lumina makes the city's lanterns, Bobor gives me the first brioche every morning in exchange for a story, and Cendrin loses to me at draughts every week. Calcine plays the violin behind my tales. I'm an old demon with plenty of company. It's the finest of treasures.
textes.Aujourd'hui, ma tente est sur la place,: Today, my tent is on the square, next to Joe's stall. From ten to seven, I tattoo: anchors, mermaids, skulls, and once a spoon. Every pirate on Balafre wears my mark somewhere. Brutus forges my needles, Philémon draws my compass roses, and Tonneau gives me nightmares. Eight arms. EIGHT.
textes.Aujourd'hui, mes horloges flottent autou: Today, my clocks float around me: the one for Astralys, the one for Ondelune, the one for Port-Azur, and Gloubi's, which runs five minutes fast so he believes lunch is ready. I set the fountain at seven o'clock and go to bed at nine p.m. precisely. Even on aurora nights.
textes.Aujourd'hui, mon agence est dans la Haut: Today, my agency is in the Upper Town. I sell houses, I rent them, I value them. I offered to sell the Baron's north tower for him. Miss Aurore showed me out with terrifying calm. I've been sending her flowers ever since. For the tower. Only. Hilaire drops by every week to ask if the price of the Cottage has gone down.
textes.Aujourd'hui, mon atelier est chez les Ar: Today, my workshop is in the Artisans' Quarter, between Tiburce, who smells of perfume, and Zigomar, who smells of gunpowder. I dress the Archduchess, Calcine, Gorgoth and half the city. In the evening, I sit on a bench on the square to look at what people are wearing. You learn a lot by looking at sleeves.
textes.Aujourd'hui, mon échoppe est entre les t: Today, my stall is between Rachid's rugs and Abdellah's hammer. Tac, tac on one side, blah blah blah on the other. At the back, under the yellow babouches, I'm hiding a secret pair for Rachid's wedding. Amine delivers at a run, paid in dates. Tibo, the cabin boy, comes in secret. And one day, I'll put shoes on the pirate captain. That day, I'll close up shop and dance.
textes.Aujourd'hui, mon étal est pile en face d: Today, my stall is right opposite the breach onto the beach: you come in, you bump straight into it, that's on purpose. I sell everything that floats, everything that shines, and two or three things that do neither. Lucie brings me her pearls, Jos his sabres, Nolwenn her canvas offcuts. And Matthias still won't take my key.
textes.Aujourd'hui, tout Arcanelle passe chez m: Today, all of Arcanelle comes through my door. Séraphine lunches at table one, Aurélien has his breakfast at noon, Mathurin has his table and his slice of pie, Sauge criticises my soup and has seconds. Pyra and Borée dine at the two ends of the room, as far from each other as possible. And me, I run, I serve, I listen. I know everything. I say almost nothing.
textes.Aujourd'hui, tout Arcanelle vient s'asse: Today, all of Arcanelle comes to sit at my table, even those who don't believe in it. Aurélien comes to ask whether the stars will move. Sauge brings me tea. Mathurin grumbles in front of his boot. Pyra hurries past. And one evening, an owl with a wounded wing landed near my caravan, letting no one come near. That night, the ball wouldn't say a thing.
textes.Aujourd'hui, un galion pirate est amarré: Today, a pirate galleon is moored at my quay. Polite pirates. Lights in the caves at night. Their captain, caught one evening at the foot of the Skala, lantern in hand. In the morning, a painter sets up on my battlements. In the afternoon, children climb on my cannons. I have six guards. I'd need sixty.
textes.Aurore ! Avez-vous vu ma canne ?: Aurore! Have you seen my cane?
textes.Aurore ! Vous avez mangé, ce matin ?: Aurore! Have you eaten this morning?
textes.Aurore m'a demandé une bulle de soins. J: Aurore asked me for a healing bubble. I made it from very soft glass, with a ceiling where you can see the clouds. She says the sick get better by looking at the sky. It's the dome I'm proudest of.
textes.Aurore m'a soignée plus de fois que n'im: Aurore has patched me up more times than anyone on the island. Knee, elbow, nose, pride. She says I'm her best customer. She tells me off. Then she gives me a biscuit. I adore her.
textes.Aurore ne sourit pas beaucoup, mais quan: Aurore doesn't smile much, but when I hand her her croissant in the morning, she smiles. Just a tiny bit. I think she works too hard. I always slip her an extra croissant.
textes.Aurore retrouve tout ce que je perds, c': Aurore finds everything I lose, which is to say everything. Without her, Montjoie would have no baron. He'd be somewhere on a roof, chasing a hat. Charming, charming.
textes.Aurore soigne mes antennes une fois par: Aurore treats my antennae once a month. She says there's nothing wrong with them. She's surely right. I go back anyway. Her tea is good, and she doesn't talk too much.
textes.Aurore soigne tout le monde avec ses mai: Aurore heals everyone with her glowing hands. I want to do the same. I heal my dolls, the glug-glugs and Quark. She lets me help her. She says I'm gifted. Why does she smile when she says it?
textes.Aurore, la guérisseuse, a sa bulle de so: Aurore, the healer, has her care bubble to the north-east. I made it out of very soft glass, so the healing light gets through nicely. She says patients get better just by looking at the ceiling.
textes.Aurèle ! Votre Gontran me cache Clémenti: Aurèle! Your Gontran is hiding Clémentine!
textes.Aurélien ! Je passe ce soir, ne me prend: Aurélien! I'm coming by tonight, don't mistake me for a comet!
textes.Aurélien Lumen m'apprendra le sort de lu: Aurélien Lumen will teach me the light spell if I bring him three moon shards that fell on the island. Then I'll have to awaken the runes in the Crypt.
textes.Aurélien a été mon élève avant d'être mo: Aurélien was my pupil before he became my master of light. He doesn't sleep enough, he talks too fast, and he sees things in the sky that I never could.
textes.Aurélien et moi, on est ceux d'en haut :: Aurélien and I are the ones up above: him on his roof with his stars, me in the air with my winds. He talks as much as I do. When we meet, nobody listens to anybody, and we're delighted.
textes.Aurélien prend son petit-déjeuner à midi: Aurélien has his breakfast at noon and says good night to me on his way out. He talks about the stars with his mouth full. He's an adorable boy. He needs to sleep and eat, in one order or the other.
textes.Aurélien ramasse les éclats de lune que: Aurélien picks up the moon shards the stones attract. At least he says thank you. He measures everything, counts everything, talks a lot. The stones tolerate him. So do I. More or less.
textes.Aurélien regarde si loin qu'il en oublie: Aurélien looks so far away that he forgets what's right under his nose. He's the easiest client in the archipelago to reassure, and the kindest. He believes everything I say about the stars. So I'm careful.
textes.Autant ?! Merci ! Avec ça, trois personn: That much?! Thank you! With this, three people will eat tomorrow without paying a thing. You've just given away three soups!
textes.Autour, le Bois des Spores : bouleaux, s: All around, the Spore Wood: birches, willows, buddleias. The mushlings live there. They're little pranksters with caps who puff out coloured spores. They make you sneeze, nothing more. If you chase them off, they sulk. Their king is bigger. And he sulks harder.
textes.Autrefois la cloche réglait toute la vie: Once, the bell ruled the whole life of the town: market at eight, siesta at one, aperitif at seven. Especially the aperitif.
textes.Autrefois, avant que la porte de l'Arbre: Long ago, before the door of the Mother Tree closed, Faelar used to come down into the roots. He'd trade a story for a riddle. His stories were so long that I set him three riddles while he was telling them, and he solved them without ever stopping talking. It was infuriating. It was marvellous.
textes.Autrefois, il y avait un grand festival: There used to be a big festival on the meadow, every summer. The two villages played together. Since our quarrel, the Great Stage has been waiting. It's bored, poor thing.
textes.Autrefois, les quatre peuples de l'île s: Long ago, the island's four peoples met in the centre, in front of the great gate, once a year. We sang, we swapped, we danced. Then the gate closed, with its four seals. Nobody quite knows why any more. The stories have forgotten.
textes.Autrefois, pendant le festival, les bus: In the old days, during the festival, the buses were dormitories. Thirty people per bus, falling asleep singing. Since the quarrel, they sleep all alone. I keep them in shape anyway. An engine should be kept ready.
textes.Aux animaux ! Je demanderais à Gérard s': Animals! I'd ask Gérard if he wants to be a hat again. I bet he says no. I'll think about it. I've already got the name: the Gérard potion.
textes.Aux commandes du Glisseur stellaire: At the controls of the Star Glider
textes.Aux osselets, c'est moi qui compte les p: At knucklebones, I'm the one who keeps score. He says I cheat. Once, he brought a bee to count instead of me. The bee landed on my knucklebones and wouldn't fly off. Game cancelled. Yum Kab declared that the bee had ruled: a draw. It's the only game he hasn't lost in twenty years.
textes.Aux pieds d'Ehécatl : la tablette du Sol: At the feet of Ehécatl: the tablet of the Sun of the Wind… and a large pink conch, the god's conch. When you blow into it, the wind rises.
textes.Aux pommes ? Tu me voles mes idées, main: With apples? Stealing my ideas now, are you?
textes.Aux échecs lunaires, je joue deux coups: At lunar chess, I make two moves at once while Tempo checks the time. He checks the time every three minutes. I've won four thousand games that way. He says it's cheating. I say it's well-placed patience.
textes.Aux échecs lunaires, la Doyenne attend q: At lunar chess, the Elder waits until I look at my clocks to move two pieces. I've seen her do it four thousand times. I say nothing. If I stopped checking the time, she'd lose, and she'd be sad. I'd rather lose on time.
textes.Au… au couteau ? (Il chancelle.) Mon enf: With a… with a knife? (He staggers.) My child… Sit down. Breathe. We are going to talk about Recommendation number three.
textes.Avalé par une grenouille (et recraché): Swallowed by a frog (and spat out)
textes.Avant chaque alerte, c'est Père Gaubert: Before every alert, it's Père Gaubert who warns me. He climbs all the way up to the Great Square, out of breath, and whispers: “They're moving.” So I ring. Once, he came running, said “they're moving”, and I rang. It was his tummy. He was hungry. The whole town showed up at the Southern Fields for nothing. He made them soup.
textes.Avant chaque combat, Madame Hurla arrang: Before every fight, Madame Hurla straightens my cape, pats my knee, because she can't reach any higher, and whispers to me: “You're the best.” Then she turns to the crowd and shouts the same thing, a thousand times louder. I prefer the whispered version. I've never told her.
textes.Avant chaque concert, Rouille monte me v: Before every concert, Rouille comes up to see me on the mezzanine and sings me the first note, just for me. If I nod, she goes back down and sings in front of everyone. I always nod. Even when it's a bit off-key. Especially when it's a bit off-key.
textes.Avant chaque concert, Sirène me prépare: Before every gig, Sirène makes me a hot lemon with honey in a rat-shaped mug. She says it's “for the throat”. One night when I'd forgotten to stop by, she crossed the whole pit holding the mug above everyone's heads. Not a drop spilled.
textes.Avant chaque concert, je lui donne un go: Before every concert, I give her a cup of mint syrup. Lukewarm. She gets stage fright, I can see it in her hands. I don't say anything. She drinks. She smiles. We go on stage. It's our ritual. We've never named it.
textes.Avant chaque concert, je prépare à Rouil: Before every gig, I make Rouille a hot lemon with honey in a rat-shaped mug. One evening, she forgot to stop by. I crossed the whole pit, mug held above everyone's heads, during the mosh. Not a drop spilled. People parted as if for a queen. The mug was the queen.
textes.Avant chaque concert, sans un mot, Clou: Before every gig, without a word, Clou hands me a cup of lukewarm mint cordial. He knows I get stage fright. He's never said so. Neither have I. We look at each other, I drink, he nods. It works every time.
textes.Avant chaque course, Caramel m'attend au: Before every race, Caramel waits for me at the start. A skewer. The biggest on the stall. “For the paws,” she says. … I eat it. Always. The only time I forgot it, I fell. … Caramel says it's not connected. I'm not sure.
textes.Avant chaque course, je lui garde la plu: Before every race, I save her the biggest skewer on the stall. It brings luck, everyone knows that. The only time she forgot it, two years ago, she fell at the root bend. I'm not saying it's connected. I'm saying that, since then, I watch her eat down to the last bite. Mrrr.
textes.Avant chaque départ, Nina inspecte L'Hir: Before each departure, Nina inspects the Swallow, hands behind her back, with my old cap on her head. It falls over her nose. She checks the knots, the lifebuoys, the bench. Once, she told me, very seriously: “Captain, your boat needs a seventh coat of paint.” She was right.
textes.Avant chaque grand match, à l'aube, il p: Before every big match, at dawn, he passes by the Cenote. He says he's “running”. He runs very slowly, stops right next to me, and waits, head bowed. I pretend not to see anything, and I murmur a prayer for his hips. Then he runs off again. Very fast, this time.
textes.Avant d'installer ses robots-fleurs à la: Before setting up his robot-flowers at the edge of the Spore Wood, Ferraille came to ask permission. Not me: the mushrooms. He knelt in front of the first one and explained his project, very seriously. The mushroom let out a little shower of spores. Ferraille said: “That's a yes.” I didn't contradict him.
textes.Avant de garder le feu, j'ai été élève à: Before keeping the fire, I was a student at the Infernal Academy, with Malachar. He was top of the class in everything, I was bottom in flames. One evening, we wanted to prove that a flame could climb a staircase all by itself. It climbed it. The Academy tower burned down. Since then, I prefer flames that stay where they belong.
textes.Avant de le perdre, il montait au belvéd: Before he lost it, he used to come up to the lookout to photograph my easel. Not the view: my easel, my unfinished canvas, my hand. Click, click. He says a photo “keeps” things. I told him that mostly it kept my mistakes. He laughed. He showed me the photo, later. Blurry. That, at least, was artistic.
textes.Avant de le perdre, j'avais photographié: Before I lost it, I'd photographed her painting. To keep it, as a souvenir. I had it developed: blurry. A blue smudge and a pink smudge. She looked at it for a long time and said: “It's the first time anyone's got my pink right.” I still don't know if it was a compliment.
textes.Avant de me prêter sa barque, Barnabé a: Before lending me his boat, Barnabé insisted on drawing a map of the route. Port-Azur to the beach: a straight line, I told him. It took him two days. There were reefs, two monsters, a whale, and a little cross where, according to him, “a rock might be badly placed”. We followed the map seventeen times. Not one rock.
textes.Avant de monter, elle est venue s'asseoi: Before going up, she came and sat at the Assembly. She asked me for the key. She said: “I'm leaving. But I'll be back every evening.” Everyone raised their hand, without anyone asking anything. It's the only vote in the history of the Fronde where nobody asked a question.
textes.Avant de planter mes robots-fleurs au bo: Before planting my flower-robots at the edge of the Spore Wood, I went to ask permission. Not from Mère Morille: from the mushrooms. I knelt in front of the nearest one and explained my project. The mushroom released a shower of spores. I said: “That's a yes.” Mère Morille didn't argue.
textes.Avant de rentrer dans sa chambre, Sylvie: Before going into her room, Sylvie told me, very seriously, like a schoolteacher giving the lesson of the day: “Husbands get lost and get found. So do wedding rings.” I wrote it on the hotel notepaper. It's still in my bag.
textes.Avant j'étais surfeur. Puis j'ai découve: I used to be a surfer. Then I found out the waves in Port-Azur are thirty centimetres high. So now I rent boats.
textes.Avant l'Arène, j'étais porteur au Port d: Before the Arena, I was a porter at the Ash Port. I carried four crates at a time, and I said sorry to them when I put them down too hard. One day, a little lady with red hair planted herself in front of me and shouted: “YOU! YOU'RE GOING TO BE A CHAMPION!” It was Madame Hurla. I said yes. I was afraid to say no.
textes.Avant l'aube, Lumi m'envoie dix lucioles: Before dawn, Lumi sends me ten fireflies to light my rounds. I thank each one by name. She thinks it takes too long. But her fireflies go back to her glowing brighter. She says they're showing off. I think they're simply happy.
textes.Avant l'aube, je prête dix lucioles à Pe: Before dawn, I lend Perlée ten fireflies so she can see her flowers. She thanks each firefly by name, one by one. It takes forever. My fireflies love it. They come back all proud, and they look at me as if I never thanked them.
textes.Avant le Tournoi des Cornes, tout le mon: Before the Tournament of Horns, everyone comes to have their horns polished. It's my best month! Gorgoth, though, never comes. He says his horns don't like oil. Horns that don't like oil! How sad.
textes.Avant le déluge, j'étais le plus petit c: Before the flood, I was the smallest copyist in the palace. Fourteen years old, fingers black with ink, and a master, old Themis, who rapped my knuckles whenever I rounded off a number. “History is not rounded off, Abyssos.” I've never rounded since. The dome is ninety-two paces across. Or ninety-three. I'm working on it.
textes.Avant le grand match de la fête, il est: Before the big match at the feast, he came to see me: “Ix Sak, I need champion feathers.” I asked him what colour a champion feather is. He thought for a long time. “Yellow. Like the sun. Like me.” I sewed him a yellow headdress and belt. He scored that day. He says it was the feathers.
textes.Avant le grand match, je lui ai demandé: Before the big match, I asked her for champion's feathers. She asked: “What colour?” I said: “Yellow, like the sun.” She sewed me a yellow headdress and belt. I scored that day. She says they're parrot feathers. I say they're champion's feathers. Both are true.
textes.Avant le naufrage, Octave a ressemelé me: Before the shipwreck, Octave resoled my boots with the leather of his own belt. He held his trousers up with a rope until the end of the voyage. I never thanked him. The left one is at the bottom of the sea, but the right one is still going strong.
textes.Avant le soleil ! Comme une vraie lapine: Before the sun! Like a proper bunny! Drop by the bakery at five, I'll save you the first loaf, the one that's still crackling.
textes.Avant le téléphérique, il y avait l'esca: Before the cable car, there were the stairs. Four hundred and twelve steps. I climbed them every day for twenty years. Now I watch people ride up in the cabin, and I smile.
textes.Avant les araignées de cristal, Pimprene: Before the crystal spiders, Pimprenelle used to take me bouncing on the mushrooms in the cave. I was scared. She held my hand and we jumped together, right to the top. I laughed so much I cried, and my tears bounced on the mushrooms. It's my loveliest memory.
textes.Avant les araignées, j'emmenais Brindill: Before the spiders, I used to take Brindille bouncing on the mushrooms in the cave. She was scared, so I held her hand. Right at the top she laughed so much she cried, and her tears bounced on the mushrooms, plip, plop! I've never seen anything so pretty. Not even my sparks.
textes.Avant ma traversée, Salomé m'a vendu un: Before my crossing, Salomé sold me an “indestructible” bag. It split on the second day, in the highlands. I carried everything in my shirt for two months. When I got back, she refunded me down to the last coin, and gave me a new bag. Free. I've never understood why.
textes.Avant moi, c'était la vieille Angélique: Before me, old Angélique kept the kingdom's memory. She was getting forgetful, so she hid every story in a riddle so as not to forget it. When she fell asleep for good, I inherited a thousand riddles and not a single answer. It took me a hundred years to find the stories inside them.
textes.Avant mon départ, elle m'a donné un sach: Before I left, she gave me a little bag of herbs: “Half for the Tree, the other half for you, on the evenings when you cry.” I gave it all to the Tree. She knows. She's been pretending to be cross ever since.
textes.Avant que Marius embarque avec moi, on p: Before Marius came aboard with me, we already fished in the evenings at the end of the jetty, him and me. Anselme would come and lie on the warm stones and count the stars, under his breath. Marius would shout to him: “And the fish, are you counting those?” Anselme would answer: “Three hundred and twelve.” Stars. He never looked at the water.
textes.Avant sa grande traversée, j'ai interdit: Before his great crossing, I forbade Le Goff to go near Stoneheart. He came back two months later, barefoot, saying he'd seen nothing there because of the fog. That day, Grégoire logged sunshine over the whole island. I said nothing. A man has the right to have been afraid.
textes.Avant sa grande traversée, je lui ai ven: Before his great crossing, I sold him an “indestructible” bag. It split after two days. When Matthias came back, barefoot, thin, his twelve journals clutched inside his shirt, I refunded him and gave him a new bag. He asked why. I said: “Advertising.” It wasn't the advertising.
textes.Avant un grand match, il est venu me dem: Before a big match, he came to ask me for the most favourable day. I calculated: 13 Ahau, an excellent day. He lost. He came back furious. I explained that the day was excellent… for the other team. I should have been more specific. Ever since, he always asks me: “Good for whom?”
textes.Avant, Pépin s'entraînait au tambour dan: Pépin used to practise the drum in the south tree, right under my window. Boom, boom-boom, the night before races! I complained. He moved his drum behind Trèfle's bakery. Now the bread rises in rhythm, and I get to sleep. Hop. Everybody wins.
textes.Avant, Zéro me racontait des histoires d: Zéro used to tell me stories from when the city was tiny: when the Axiom Tower only had three floors, when there was only one neon sign, a pink one. Since he lost his voice, I tell them myself. But I get the details wrong.
textes.Avant, elle s'appelait Églantine. C'étai: She used to be called Églantine. She was our queen… The brambles took her heart.
textes.Avant, j'avais peur de monter tout en ha: I used to be scared of climbing right to the top of the Great Oak. Dad told me to count the steps. There are way too many, I lost count. So I sang. When I got to the top, I'd forgotten to be scared. Now I sing all the time, even when I'm not scared.
textes.Avant, j'avais tout. Une grande maison p: I used to have everything. A big house full of beautiful things, and nobody in it. One day, I put everything out on the pavement, with a sign: “Help yourselves.” People came, they took things, they talked, they came back. I have nothing left and I have loads of friends. The sums add up.
textes.Avant, j'habitais une grande ville du co: Before, I lived in a big city on the mainland, on the fifth floor, with a view of a wall. I sorted papers in an office. I started loads of things: piano, pottery, Spanish. I never finished any of them. My mother used to say: “Zoé, you're a weathervane.” She wasn't wrong.
textes.Avant, j'étais cartographe du roi. J'ai: I used to be the king's cartographer. I drew a map of this kingdom so precise it was as big as the kingdom itself. Nobody ever unfolded it.
textes.Avant, j'étais cuisinier dans un grand r: I used to be a cook in a big fancy restaurant. We served peas one by one, on huge plates, with tweezers. One day, a child asked if he could have “a real meal”. I quit that very evening. I came here with my ladle.
textes.Avant, j'étais cuisinier sur un grand ba: I used to be a cook on a big ship. One stormy night, I dropped an enormous pot of spaghetti. It spilled across the deck, and the spaghetti drew… a face. With two meatballs for eyes. It was looking at me. It smiled at me. I knew my life had just changed.
textes.Avant, j'étais garde-barrière. Une barri: I used to be a level-crossing keeper. One barrier, one train, twice a day. I never got it wrong. Here, it's the same: one Lid, two strikes a day. The job is counting.
textes.Avant, j'étais porteur au port. Je porta: I used to be a porter at the harbour. I carried four crates at a time, and I said sorry to them when I put them down too hard. Madame Hurla saw me. She shouted: “YOU! YOU'RE GOING TO BE A CHAMPION!” I said yes. I was scared to say no.
textes.Avant, j'étais une moitié de goutte. Ma: I used to be half a drop. My sister Perlée and I were one single drop of dew, on a leaf of Yggdrasil, way up high. A gust of wind split us in two. Perlée stayed on the leaf. I fell down through the clouds… all the way into the roots of the Mother Tree.
textes.Avant, j'étais écouteur, aux Mines de Cr: I used to be a listener, in the Crystal Mines. You'd put your ear to the wall and listen to whether the rock was sound. A rock that sings is fine. A rock that's too quiet, you leave. I was never afraid. I just listened very well.
textes.Avant, je chantais à l'opéra. Dans le ch: I used to sing at the opera. In the chorus, in the back row. Nobody could hear me. Here, everybody hears me. Even the people of Neopolis, when the wind blows east.
textes.Avant, je m'appelais Bernard. Je vendais: I used to be called Bernard. I sold insurance. I ran around all day. One day, I ran so fast I went right past my own life without seeing it. So I stopped running.
textes.Avant, je vendais des glaces. Des glaces: Before, I sold ice creams. Ice creams that melted before they reached your mouth: in fact, you drank them. And then fifteen years ago, Bruno turned up with his ice-cream maker. In one summer, everyone was going to him. He offered to go into business with me. I said no, out of pride, and opened Souvenirs d'Azur. Snow globes, at least, don't melt.
textes.Avant, je vivais à Port-Azur. Je vendais: I used to live in Port-Azur. I sold flowers. One day, a tomato seed fell into my pot of roses. It grew taller than the roses. I understood it was a message.
textes.Avant, la poignée de la tyrolienne était: The zip line handle used to be too high for me. I'd jump, miss, jump again. And one morning it was lower! Just my height! Croc-Gris said it was “for safety”. But I'm the only one who's that small. So it's for me. I said thank you. He said “Halt.”
textes.Avant, volcan dormait. Maintenant, volca: Before, volcano sleep. Now, volcano snore.
textes.Avec ! Bon choix. Ne le dis pas à Rosali: With! Good choice. Don't tell Rosalie, she'll think she's won. Tonight I'll tell her you're the one who chose it. That'll start a debate.
textes.Avec Frère Linguini, on a construit un c: Brother Linguini and I built a sandcastle shaped like the temple, with holes everywhere, like the real colander. The sea ate it. I was sad. Linguini said: “It's an offering for the Great Spaghetti.” Now I build one every day.
textes.Avec Félix comme navigateur. Je lui gard: With Félix as navigator. I'll save him the best seat, up front, with a bucket. A nice bucket, painted blue, just for him. A navigator deserves comfort.
textes.Avec Margot, on a calculé la trajectoire: Margot and I worked out Achille's trajectory. He circles above the observatory every seven minutes, even when he's asleep. He sleeps while gliding, I've seen him. Margot says he's an “orbiter”. I wrote it on the morning note. Adèle told me it made her laugh. That was the idea.
textes.Avec Margot, on construit un robot dans: Margot and I are building a robot in Basile's cellar, between the soap barrels. His name is Bidule — Thingamajig. He doesn't work yet. But he has a name, and a hat! Basile made him a hat out of a bubble gone all hard. Margot says a robot that doesn't move is a statue. I say it's a robot having a rest.
Margot and me are building a robot in the cellar. It's called Bidule. It doesn't walk yet. Maybe it never will. But it has a name.
textes.Avec Nebet, on a fait un concours de la: Nebet and I had a best-story contest: my mosquito who bites the Lords of Xibalba, or her great cat who cuts off the serpent's head! Pilli was supposed to choose. He said the best one was about his dog. He didn't even have a story! We're doing it again next year.
Pimprenelle and I invented a code. Two knocks, then one: hello, thank you. Three quick knocks: found a bolt. One long scrape: good night. Four slow knocks: “Your mum's looking for you.” She made that one up. I think she mostly uses it for herself.
textes.Avec Titou, on marque nos sauts sur le p: Titou and I mark our jumps on the palm tree, with shells pushed into the bark. One night I jumped so high I grabbed a coconut. It landed on my head right after. Titou said it didn't count. The shell is still up there, right at the top. Legend.
textes.Avec Titouan, on a fondé la Guilde des P: Titouan and I founded the Little Heroes' Guild. I made the badge, with a button and some thread. So I'm the leader. Titouan is the warrior. We're looking for a mage. Violette said maybe. Maybe is almost yes.

Titouan and I founded the Little Heroes' Guild. I made the badges, so I'm the boss. I ask the questions, Titouan is the warrior. We follow the adventurers and write everything down. Grandma Philomène tells us the legends of the dungeon. Mamie Rissole gives us pies. We eat them at meetings.
textes.Avec Yasmine, on joue aux pirates sur la: Yasmine and I play pirates on the square. She's always the captain. It's not fair.
textes.Avec beaucoup de clous. Et de la bonne v: With lots of nails. And goodwill. Mostly nails.
textes.Avec cannelle, comme d'habitude ? Rosali: With cinnamon, as usual? Rosalie knows, alas.
textes.Avec ce soleil, la Colonne brille tellem: With this sun, the Column shines so bright you need goggles to look at it.
With corners? (She turns pale lavender.) But… where do you put the corners away? You'll show me. I'd really like to understand.
textes.Avec des guitares qui grincent ! Tu es d: With screeching guitars! You're one of us. Come to the garage.
textes.Avec du RHUM ? Sacrilège ! Tu as passé t: With RUM? Sacrilege! You've spent too much time with the pirates. … I'll serve it to you anyway. Without rum. And you'll drink it, and you'll see.
textes.Avec du lait ? Ici ? … Vous m'avez bien: With milk? Here? … Did you hear me right? Fine. I'll put some in. A drop. And you don't tell a soul.
textes.Avec du miel. Et une légende avec une so: With honey. And a legend with a witch in it.
textes.Avec joie ! Que l'Aube nous garde… et qu: With joy! May the Dawn watch over us… and over my feet too, I trip a lot. Let's go!
textes.Avec juste un tout petit peu de savon ex: With just a teeny bit of explosive soap?
textes.Avec la Libellule, je fais le tour de l': With the Dragonfly, I fly all around the archipelago. I've flown over Ember Island, Lighthouse Point, and even Neopolis, at night, with its twinkling lights. I prefer our clouds. But I have to admit it was pretty.
textes.Avec la lanterne ? Jamais. La nuit, c'es: With the lantern lit? Never. At night, we're the ones lighting the way for everyone. Even the Moon says thank you.
textes.Avec la ligne rouverte, les quatre monde: With the line reopened, the four worlds swap everything: our fish and our spirulina go up; apples, mushrooms, giant strawberries and gossip come down. Especially gossip. It's lighter than apples. It comes down faster.
textes.Avec la pelle, cherche les petites croix: With the shovel, look for the little wooden crosses on the sand. Castaways hid their savings there. It glints a bit, up close.
textes.Avec la plate-forme ! Je ne l'oublie plu: Including the platform! I'll never forget it again!
textes.Avec le Muet, c'est simple. Il montre le: With the Mute, it's simple. He points at the sky: it's going to rain. He points at his glass: he's thirsty. He points at Tonneau: Tonneau has fallen over again. I understand EVERYTHING. The others mumble sentences full of words at me, and I hear nothing. Him, he talks better than the whole port. It's humiliating. For the port.
textes.Avec le Petit Plongeon, je relève aussi: With the Little Diver, I also haul up the fishermen's pots around the Dome. The fish from down here now goes all the way up to the Great Market in Hautefond, by the line. The folk up top say it has “a taste of the deep”. It's a compliment. I think.
With their fingers. And with their hearts.
textes.Avec le soleil, c'est raisonnable. Le so: With the sun, that's reasonable. The sun keeps a lazy lord's hours, but still. You'll get bread from the second batch. It's very good too.
textes.Avec les huit bras, cette fois !: With the eight arms, this time!
textes.Avec les intérêts ? Il va falloir lever: With interest? I'll have to raise a tax.
textes.Avec les intérêts. Je ne fais pas crédit: With interest. I don't give credit.
With the letters from back home.
textes.Avec lui ! Comme un bon serviteur de Rê: With it! Like a good servant of Rê: neither early nor late. My mother said it's the most honest hour.
textes.Avec ma jument Prune, j'ai fait trois fo: With my mare Prune, I went round the archipelago three times. The square at Port-Azur, the souk of Tazira, the quays of Carène, everywhere. I predicted weddings, storms, and an incredible number of journeys. People love being told they'll go on a journey. Especially the ones leaving the next day.
textes.Avec ma longue-vue, j'ai vu un petit écl: With my spyglass, I saw a little glint, way up at the summit of Mount Charcoal. It was shining. Not like a stone. Like a pot. Have a look yourself, if you like.
textes.Avec mes daurades d'hier, Paulo ?: With my day-old sea bream, Paulo?
textes.Avec moi ? Non : à ta place. Un guerrier: With me? No: in my place. A jaguar warrior against jaguars, Cuauhtli finds that far too funny, he won't let me go. The slopes of Smoking Mountain, to the west, under the pines. When a jaguar crouches, it's about to pounce: step aside, then strike.
textes.Avec mon chronomètre, j'ai tout mesuré d: With my stopwatch, I measured everything in the bakery. The all-time record is Mochi: a whole mooncake in two minutes, hidden behind a flour sack. I shouted “New record!” far too loud, and Trèfle came in. Mochi looked at me as if I'd betrayed her. Which was true.
textes.Avec plaisir ! Ne coule pas dessus, cett: With pleasure! Don't drip on it this time.
textes.Avec plaisir ! Un, deux, trois… un, deux: With pleasure! One, two, three… one, two, three… You're light on your feet! Here, some honey bread: you dance better on a full stomach.
With pleasure. Up you come, little ones.
textes.Avec plaisir. J'ai lu tout un chapitre s: With pleasure. I read a whole chapter on adventuring. You have to move forward. I'll move forward.
textes.Avec plaisir. Mais regarde où tu mets le: With pleasure. But watch where you put your feet.
With four arms, it looks like a storm.
textes.Avec quatre bras, ça ressemble à un ince: With four arms, it looks like a fire.
textes.Avec quelqu'un de prudent… Tu parles com: With someone careful… You sound like Yolande. Fine. It's true. I never dive until she's checked everything. That's why I always come back. You're right. Don't tell her I said so.
textes.Avec ta pelle sur l'épaule, tu as l'air: With that shovel on your shoulder, you look like a real treasure hunter. Found anything?
textes.Avec ta voix d'aujourd'hui ! Chante un p: With your voice of today! Sing a little, so the pot can hear you.
textes.Avec tes ailes, tu peux faire le tour de: With your wings, you can go all the way round the island following the Edge Promenade. Always stay above the railing, and land often. If in doubt, land. If not in doubt, land anyway. That's how you become an old instructor.
textes.Avec tes dents de requin, j'ai taillé le: With your shark teeth, I carved the finest flippers in the city.
textes.Avec tes plumes, j'ai fait un manteau po: With your feathers, I made a coat for Croâ, my oldest raven.
textes.Avec ton crochet, tu te grattes comment: With that hook, how do you scratch your nose?
textes.Avec ton miel, j'ai brassé l'hydromel de: With your honey, I brewed Forgefer's honey drink. The king drank a whole barrel.
textes.Avec ton minerai, je t'ai forgé une épée: With your ore, I forged you a dwarven sword. My best of the year.
textes.Avec tout le monde… C'est la plus diffic: With everyone… That's the hardest kind, and the finest. It takes time, it makes noise, and in the end, nobody has quite won. That's how you build a city under the sea. Or anywhere.
textes.Avec une maison à Montjoie, vous aurez u: With a house in Montjoie, you'll have a bed of your own: when you sleep, you'll wake up rested, and if you faint on the island, it's home they'll carry you to. Not to the temple, between two pews. Home!
With a straw. Not with a ladle.
textes.Avec une pelle ? Il faut une hache pour: With a shovel? You need an axe to fell this tree.
textes.Avec une pelle, on trouve de tout dans l: With a shovel, you'll find all sorts in the beach sand: shells, castaways' coins… I sell shovels, you know. Just saying.
textes.Avec une plume. Une seule. Et pas de cer: With a feather. Just one. And no cherries.
textes.Avec une sardine sur dix pour les mouett: With one sardine in ten for the gulls, of course. You don't change a tax.
With your hat. It's on the roof.
textes.Avec vous, j'ai un peu moins peur. Un to: With you, I'm a little less scared. A tiny bit. That's already huge, for me.
textes.Avec ça, je peux acheter les courges de: With this, I can buy Mère Morille's pumpkins AND Radis's. They'll argue over whose are best. Thanks for the show!
textes.Avec ça, tu vas faire des jaloux. Surtou: With that, you'll make people jealous. Especially the neighbour. The neighbour gets jealous of everything.
textes.Aventurier de rang S, légende de la Guil: Rank S adventurer, legend of the Guild
textes.Averse a une langue de vipère et un cœur: Downpour has a viper's tongue and a gingerbread heart. I haven't spoken to her in fifty years. But I know she knits in rhythm when the young ones play. I've seen her.
textes.Avis d'expulsion numéro quatre mille dou: Eviction notice number four thousand and twelve. Please sign here. Here. No, not with a mohawk.
textes.Avoir assez de place à la Grande Tablée: To have enough room at the Great Table for everyone. Even the people from Néopolis, with their machine-made noodles. I'll show them what real pasta is.
To have gold teeth, like Malaterre. Jutht two. To bite into an apple, jutht onthe, in front of the whole Crâne Fendu. Crunch!
textes.Avoir la plus grande boutique de program: To have the biggest program shop in the archipelago, with a sign flashing my name. In purple. With stars.
textes.Avoir un coquillage de chaque plage de l: To have a shell from every beach in the archipelago: Arcanelle, Port-Azur, the big island in the east… Sorted by colour, on shelves Gwen will have made me. With every other nail crooked.
textes.AÏE ! Dans MA cabane ?! Les prix doublen: OUCH! In MY hut?! Prices are doubling!
textes.AÏE ! La lave ! Tu bondis hors du cratèr: OUCH! The lava! You leap out of the crater, clutching your backside.
textes.Aëlwen ! Mon miel. Au prix du miel, cett: Aëlwen! My honey. At honey prices, this time.
textes.Aëlwen ! Regarde, je n'ai même pas une é: Aëlwen! Look, I haven't got a single scratch!
textes.Aëlwen achète mon miel pour ses potions,: Aëlwen buys my honey for her potions, and she haggles over every drop. But the night of my three hundred stings, she looked after me until morning without counting the cost. That's how she is.
textes.Aëlwen est une bonne guérisseuse et une: Aëlwen is a good healer and a terrible trader. She treats my daughter's knees almost for free, and she pays me for moonflowers as if they were dandelions.
textes.Aëlwen m'a soignée cent fois depuis ma n: Aëlwen has healed me a hundred times since I was born. Her potions are bitter and her hands are gentle: you have to take both together.
textes.Aëlwen me fait trier ses graines pendant: Aëlwen makes me sort her seeds while she patches me up: red ones on one side, black ones on the other. That way I keep still. One day I found a blue seed in the pile. She gave it to me: “Plant it and see what it turns into.” It's in a pot on my windowsill. It isn't growing yet.
textes.Aëlwen me soigne depuis trois siècles, e: Aëlwen has been looking after me for three centuries, and I look after her in return: I tell her stories while she works. She says it annoys her. She's never closed her door.
textes.Aëlwen soigne mes genoux. Ses potions so: Aëlwen patches up my knees. Her potions are disgusting, but she always has a honey sweet in her pocket. I hide my footbridge climbing from her. She knows. She knows EVERYTHING.
textes.Aëlwen soigne mon cœur deux fois par sem: Aëlwen treats my heart twice a week. She says there's nothing wrong with it. She's mistaken: it has Ilyria. She charges me anyway, and she's quite right to.
textes.Aëlwen soigne tout le monde, et personne: Aëlwen looks after everyone, and nobody looks after her. So I leave her flowers, unsigned. She thinks I don't know she knows. We're very happy like that.
textes.Aëlwen soigne tout le monde, mais person: Aëlwen heals everyone, but nobody heals her. Bring her flowers, one day.
textes.Aëlwen vend des potions, Sylwen du pain: Aëlwen sells potions, Sylwen sells honey bread. And Faelar sells stories. For free. Lots of them.
Aëlwen, I have a story about mint.
textes.Aëlwen, mes fleurs de lune. Au prix just: Aëlwen, my moonflowers. At a fair price.
textes.Aëlwen, tu as des cernes. Tu as dormi ?: Aëlwen, you've got dark circles. Did you sleep?
textes.Aïcha ! Ton safran a encore augmenté ?: Aïcha! Has your saffron gone up again?
textes.Aïcha… Ho ho. La reine des épices, avec: Aïcha… Ho ho. The queen of spices, with eyes that sting like her chilli. She didn't say no. She didn't say yes. I'm a patient man. With lots of cumin.
textes.Aïe ! Hé ! Au fond de la mer, on tapote: Ow! Hey! At the bottom of the sea, we tap on portholes to say hello to the fish. People just get a wave!
textes.Aïe ! Hé ! Ici, on ne se cogne qu'aux nu: Ow! Hey! Up here, the only thing you bump into is clouds. And gently, at that.
textes.Aïe ! Hé ! Ici, on ne tape que sur les b: Ow! Hey! Round here, we only bash drums and robots! And even then, gently!
textes.Aïe ! Hé ! Ici, on ne tape que sur les f: Ow! Hey! Round here, we only hit drums and rail rivets! And even then, in rhythm!
textes.Aïe ! Hé ! Ici, on tape sur les enclumes: Ow! Hey! Down here we hit anvils, not neighbours!
textes.Aïe ! Hé ! Je ne suis pas un piston, moi: Ow! Hey! I'm not a piston! You don't hit people, you hit anvils!
textes.Aïe ! Hé ! Je ne suis pas un slime, moi: Ow! Hey! I'm not a slime! The monsters are outside, beyond the ramparts!
textes.Aïe ! Hé ! La Sixième Recommandation dit: Ow! Hey! The Sixth Recommendation says: we don't hit people. Not even with a baguette.
textes.Aïe ! Hé ! On ne frappe pas un démon che: Ow! Hey! You don't hit a demon in his own home! It's just not done, not even in hell!
textes.Aïe ! Hé ! On ne tape pas les gens, même: Ow! Hey! We don't hit people, not even in black and white!
textes.Aïe ! Hé ! Ça ne se fait pas, même à Néo: Ow! Hey! That's not okay, even in Neopolis.
textes.Aïe ! Je suis vieux, tu sais. On ne tape: Ouch! I'm old, you know. You don't hit old androids. Or young ones, for that matter.
textes.Aïe ! Je vais vous faire breveter, vous,: Ow! I'm going to have you patented as a public hazard!
textes.Aïe ! L'Amirale va entendre parler de to: Ouch! The Admiral's going to hear about you!
textes.Aïe ! La lave brûle ! (Les démons, eux,: Ouch! The lava burns! (The demons soak their feet in it… you don't.)
textes.Aïe ! Mais quelle mouche du désert t'a p: Ouch! What desert fly bit you?
textes.Aïe ! Mais t'es pas bien ?!: Ow! Are you out of your mind?!
textes.Aïe ! Mais… on ne frappe pas sous le dôm: Ow! But… nobody hits anyone under the dome!
textes.Aïe ! Mes oreilles se sont toutes hériss: Ouch! All my ears are standing on end! No hitting in Ramure!
textes.Aïe ! Oh ! Par les sept lunes ! Sur Onde: Ow! Oh! By the seven moons! On Ondelune, we say hello by blinking, not by hitting!
textes.Aïe ! On ne frappe pas un sorcier, {surn: Ouch! You don't hit a wizard, {surnom}. Wizards have long memories. And toads.
textes.Aïe ! Pas dans la sauce : elle est brûla: Ouch! Not in the sauce: it's scalding! (And besides, it stains.)
textes.Aïe ! Pourquoi ? Ici, on règle tout avec: Ow! Why? Here, we sort everything out with a hug and a song. Want the song?
textes.Aïe ! Qui a mis ce caillou ici ?: Ouch! Who put this pebble here?
textes.Aïe ! Tu frappes un habitant sous les ye: Ow! You strike a local before the eyes of the gods? They won't forget it. Neither will I.
textes.Aïe ! Vous… vous avez frappé le majordom: Ow! You… you struck the butler?! In all the palace's memory, such a thing has never been seen. Kindly leave.
textes.Aïe aïe aïe ! La lave du Phlégéthon ! Tu: Ow ow ow! The lava of the Phlegethon! You leap back onto the bank, your soles smoking. Take a raft next time.
textes.Aïe, aïe, aïe. Pas comme ça !: Ow, ow, ow. Not like that!
textes.Aïe. (Elle tapote son chapeau qui fume.): Ouch. (She pats her smoking hat.) It's nothing. It's practice.
textes.Aïe. Aïe aïe. Tu parles comme Bondi. Bon: Ouch. Ouch ouch. You sound like Bondi. Okay, fine. So this time I'll finish first. That way we'll both agree. I can feel it in my paws!
textes.Aïe. Ne le dis pas trop fort près du san: Ouch. Don't say that too loudly near the blue shrine. Tlaloc is touchy. He might make you change your mind… for three days.
textes.Aïko a peint le drone tombé dans le grav: Aïko painted the drone that fell into the gravel. She turned it into a bird. I hung it in my hut.
textes.Aïko est venue un jour me demander ce qu: Aïko came to me one day and asked what “beauty” was. I handed her a brush. She has been painting for three years. She still doesn't know. Neither do I. That is why we carry on.
textes.Aïko peint mieux que moi. Elle ne le sai: Aïko paints better than I do. She doesn't know it. I won't tell her: she would stop searching.
textes.BAC DES PIÈCES DÉTACHÉES\nNe pas tomber:
SPARE PARTS BIN
Do not fall in.
(The sorting robot would file you under “Miscellaneous”.)
textes.BERTRAND ! ON JOUE ENSEMBLE, CET APRÈS-M: BERTRAND! SHALL WE PLAY TOGETHER THIS AFTERNOON?
textes.BIIIP. Le lecteur clignote en rouge : «: BEEEEP. The reader flashes red: “BADGE NOT DETECTED. Have you tried having a badge?” (Up there, on the back mezzanine, something is shining…)
textes.BIP ! (Il recule, vexé, et se cache derr: BEEP! (He backs away, offended, and hides behind his broom.)
textes.BIP BIP ! Un chariot élévateur robot te: BEEP BEEP! A robot forklift bumps into you: “FORKLIFTS HAVE PRIORITY. THANK YOU FOR YOUR UNDERSTANDING.” Look carefully before crossing the aisles.
textes.BIP. Surface propre à 97 %. Les 3 % rest: BEEP. Surface 97% clean. The remaining 3% is your shoes.
textes.BLORP ! (Il fait défiler les hologrammes: BLORP! (He flips through the holograms: a mayor sucking in his tummy, a tavern-keeper glaring, a baron with three hats, a crested granny raising her fist.) They're PERFECT! They're so… so Heavyfoot! I'm sending everything to Mama! (Click-click-click. A long silence. Then the device goes “beep”.) She replied! She says: “My Glorb, you have friends!” … (He wobbles very hard.) I have friends. Here, my kaleidoscope glasses: with them, you see the world like I do. In a thousand pieces, and all of them pretty.
textes.BLORP ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Pour moi ? (I: BLORP! {dernier_cadeau}! For me? (He wobbles so hard he bounces three times.) I'm taking a photo of it! Click! Mum's going to love it!
textes.BLOUOP ! Le Roi Gélatineux retombe de to: BLOOP! The Jelly King slams back down with all his weight: the ground shakes!
textes.BONG ! Toute la ville lève le nez. Le ga: BONG! The whole town looks up. The keeper sighs: “Another one who's pulled the rope.”
BONG! … BONG! The whole belfry shakes. Somewhere down below, the Burgomaster drops his pen.
textes.BONJOUR, BELLE-HUMEUR ! TU AS BIEN DORMI: MORNING, BELLE-HUMEUR! DID YOU SLEEP WELL?
textes.BONK ! L'Alouette heurte l'obstacle et s: BONK! The Alouette hits the obstacle and folds up all at once… The harness spring set you down gently. Nothing broken!
textes.BONSOIR PORT-BOUCAN ! On est les Rats de: GOOD EVENING PORT-BOUCAN! We're the Bilge Rats, and this one's called “Rusty But Standing”!
textes.BOOONG ! (Les adeptes disent qu'il ne fa: BOOONG! (The followers say you must never strike it three times in a row. Nobody remembers why.)
BOOONG! Dust falls from the beams. The pigeons pretend they didn't hear a thing.
textes.BOOONG ! Le grand couvercle de cuivre ré: BOOONG! The great copper lid rings out across the whole forecourt. Above the temple, the Great Flying Spaghetti wriggles all its noodles.
textes.BOOONG. Quelque part dans les gradins, q: BOOONG. Somewhere in the stands, someone shouts: “AGAIN!” (The champion is allowed.)
textes.BOOONG… BOOONG… BOOONG ! Le sol tremble: BOOONG… BOOONG… BOOONG! The ground trembles a little. Up above, Mount Bolognese starts to rumble… It sounds like it heard you.
textes.BOOOOUUUH ! La corne de brume fait tremb: BWOOOOOOH! The foghorn rattles the windows. Somewhere outside, a seal answers.
textes.BOUH ! … Hé hé hé ! Tu as sursauté ! Les: BOO! … Hee hee hee! You jumped! Heavy-Feet jump super high! I'm Quark. I'm eighty-one, that's seven for a Lumen, and I'm the best hide-and-seek player in the whole galaxy. Pixel says I'm not. Pixel is jealous.
textes.BOUM ! ENFIN UNE BONNE JOURNÉE !: BOOM! A GOOD DAY AT LAST!
textes.BOUM ! Le rocher t'aplatit comme une crê: BOOM! The boulder flattens you like a pancake (a very offended pancake). You peel yourself off the floor at the entrance of the corridor. Next time: an alcove!
textes.BOUM ! Ouais ! Le cœur de la musique ! T: BOOM! Yeah! The heart of the music! You've got good taste!
textes.BOUM ! T'es toujours un volcan, toi ?: BOOM! Are you still a volcano?
textes.BOUM ! … Pardon. Capucine Pétard. Mon ca: BOOM! … Sorry. Capucine Pétard. My confetti cannon fires every twenty seconds, into the crowd. People love it. The sweepers, much less.
textes.BOUM ! … Voilà, tout est par terre. Même: BOOM! … There, everything's on the floor. Even me, almost. Thanks, here, a cookie from our place. It floats too, careful.
textes.BOUM-BA-BOUM ! (Tout le Clan se met à da: BOUM-BA-BOUM! (The whole Clan starts dancing around the fire. Even Ougha. Especially Ougha.)
textes.BOUM-TCHAK ! Salut ! Un nouveau ! Bienve: BOOM-CHAK! Hi! A new face! Welcome to the Fronde! Rivet. By day, I fix rails; by night, I bash some very expensive saucepans called a drum kit. Same thing really: it's got to hold, and it's got to ring. High five!
textes.BOUM. BOUM. BOUM. Tes coups résonnent da: BOOM. BOOM. BOOM. Your knocks echo through the mountain… A deep voice behind you: “No use knocking, big one. Nobody enters Forgefer without being invited.” It's Bramm, the guard. Talk to him.
textes.BOUUUUH ! … Hé. Tu n'as même pas eu peur: BOOOO! … Hey. You weren't even scared?
textes.BRAMM : « OUVREZ LA GRANDE PORTE ! » Un: BRAMM: “OPEN THE GREAT GATE!” A rumble, creaking chains… and the two iron doors slowly open onto the glow of the Forgefer forges.
textes.BRINDILLE ! Ah, Brindille… Elle croit qu: BRINDILLE! Ah, Brindille… She thinks news travels better in her letters. By the time she's flown to the postbox, I've already shouted it three times!
textes.BRRRANG ! Une guitare saturée, une basse: BRRRANG! A fuzzed-out guitar, a rumbling bass: two musicians rehearse in the middle of the yurt, between the stove and an old amp.
MISTELLA — always in the fog. Nobody has ever seen anything there. Maybe there's nothing. Maybe there's everything.
textes.BULLETIN DE L'APRÈS-MIDI. Ciel bleu, ven: AFTERNOON REPORT. Blue sky, light wind. Kites are permitted up to three hundred metres. Hats, up to head height only. Chance of sugar puffs on the terraces: high.
textes.BULLETIN DE NUIT. Calme plat. Quelques n: NIGHT REPORT. Dead calm. A few clouds are sleeping under the island. Please do not wake them: they've been working all day.
textes.BULLETIN DU JOUR. Averse prévue à quinze: TODAY'S WEATHER REPORT. Shower forecast for twelve minutes past three, to the minute. It will fall on Hautefond, two hundred metres below. For us: a rainbow. That's the best part.
textes.BULLETIN DU JOUR. Avis de tempête… dans: TODAY'S WEATHER REPORT. Storm warning… in the kitchen: Grandpa is making pancakes. Risk of flour: very high. Fair weather returns after the washing-up.
textes.BULLETIN DU JOUR. Brume douce sous l'île: TODAY'S WEATHER REPORT. Soft mist under the island: the clouds are having a nap below us. Please do not jump on them. Doctor Aurèle will name three of them. The station suggests: Gaspard, Mirabelle and Socks.
textes.BULLETIN DU JOUR. Ce matin : soleil. Cet: TODAY'S WEATHER REPORT. This morning: sun. This afternoon: sun. This evening: the Moon, if it's in the mood. West wind: enough to spin the anemometer, not enough to ruffle Grandpa's hair.
textes.BULLETIN DU JOUR. Ce matin, un nuage en: TODAY'S WEATHER REPORT. This morning, a cloud shaped like a sugar puff will pass over the house. Risk of hunger: high. This afternoon, bright sunshine. The station recommends a snack.
textes.BULLETIN DU JOUR. Grand vent au Parc des: TODAY'S WEATHER REPORT. Strong winds over the Mist Park: hold on tight to your hats, your kites and your grandpas. Calm returns by snack time. This evening, the Moon.
textes.BULLETIN DU MATIN. Vent d'ouest, doux. B: MORNING REPORT. West wind, gentle. Mist in the Park until nine, then sunshine over the whole City. A rabbit-shaped cloud will pass over the Station at about ten. It's running early.
textes.BULLETIN DU SOIR. Le vent tombe avec le: EVENING REPORT. The wind drops with the sun. Violet sunset expected at the Belvedere; Ombeline has already set up. Clear night: you'll see the stars, and the lights of Hautefond far below.
textes.BZZT. Une lampe rouge clignote : « MONTE: BZZT. A red lamp flashes: “FREIGHT LIFT RESERVED FOR MANAGEMENT. Please defeat management first.”
textes.Ba Sidi ! Soixante-dix ans qu'il me raco: Ba Sidi! Seventy years he's been telling me stories, and he always gets the same bit wrong. He talks too much. He talks well. I won't tell him which of the two I like.
textes.Ba Sidi ! Tu as encore du thé ? J'ai enc: Ba Sidi! Still got some tea? I've still got a story.
textes.Ba Sidi ! Tu as toujours mon livre, vieu: Ba Sidi! Still got my book, you old date thief?
textes.Ba Sidi a connu ma grand-mère. C'est le: Ba Sidi knew my grandmother. He's the only man in Tazira who talks more than I do, and he doesn't even charge! Well, “whatever you like”. That's worse.
textes.Ba Sidi a mille et une histoires et une: Ba Sidi has a thousand and one stories and just one lantern: mine. He says the tales are better underneath it. I can't check: I've never heard one to the end.
textes.Ba Sidi dit que vous avez un tapis ancie: Ba Sidi says you have an old carpet that shows the way to the seal.
textes.Ba Sidi raconte, moi je joue derrière. I: Ba Sidi tells the tales, I play behind him. He says my music does his pauses for him. I think mostly it gives him time to drink his tea.
textes.Ba Sidi, c'est le meilleur raconteur du: Ba Sidi's the best storyteller in the world. Even better than Jacquot, and Jacquot's already really good. He made me guardian of the djinn. It's a real title, I told the whole crew.
textes.Ba Sidi, le conteur de Tazira. Il a mon: Ba Sidi, the storyteller of Tazira. He has my book, he's always one story ahead of me, and his beard is longer. I'll never forgive him. I'm very fond of him.
textes.Ba Sidi, le conteur de la place de Tazir: Ba Sidi, the storyteller of the square in Tazira. A thousand and one stories, and he's only ever told a thousand. He keeps the last one for himself. I understand him better than anyone.
textes.Ba-da-boum, ba-da-boum ! Tu as trouvé le: Ba-da-boom, ba-da-boom! You found the rhythm of the Flower Camp.
textes.Baba, tu me construis un galion ?: Baba, will you build me a galleon?
textes.Babette a peint son navet au concours de: Babette painted her turnip for the Dawn festival contest. Red. A red turnip! Her apples are too red too. Everything's too red, at her place. She shouts a lot. So do I, mind you.
textes.Babette m'offre une pomme chaque soir. E: Babette gives me an apple every evening. She asks me how Honorine is doing. I blush. She smiles. She knows things, Babette does.
textes.Babette me garde ses plus beaux champign: Babette saves me her finest mushrooms, the ones she picks at dawn at the edge of the Goblin Wood. She sells them to me a bit dearer, telling me the goblins wanted the same ones. I don't know if it's true. But once, there was a little clawed footprint on a porcini. I paid double for it.
textes.Babette me vend ses légumes. Pas ses nav: Babette sells me her vegetables. Not her turnips: she keeps the turnips for arguing with Germaine. Sometimes they throw them at each other. That gets me free vegetables.
textes.Babette me vend tous mes légumes. Pas se: Babette sells me all my vegetables. Not her turnips: she keeps those for arguing with Germaine. They throw them at each other, sometimes. Free vegetables for me.
textes.Babette me vend une pomme chaque soir. E: Babette sells me an apple every evening. She always asks me how Honorine is. I blush. She smiles. Babette knows things. She knows how to keep secrets, too.
textes.Babette occupe le meilleur emplacement d: Babette has the best spot in Montjoie. She'll never sell it. She gives me an apple every time I make her an offer. I'm up to three hundred apples. Exceptional.
textes.Babette raconte que j'ai triché au conco: Babette goes around saying I cheated at the finest turnip contest. She PAINTED hers. With paint. Red. A red turnip! Everyone saw.
textes.Babette vend les plus belles pommes de l: Babette sells the most beautiful apples on the island. Germaine says otherwise. I make turnovers with both their apples. Nobody can tell the difference. Whatever you do, don't tell anyone.
textes.Babette, au marché, essaie de me rachete: Babette, at the market, has been trying to buy my turnips for ten years. Germaine refuses. They argue right in front of me. I eat my soup and wait for it to blow over. It never blows over.
textes.Babette, au marché, vend les plus belles: Babette, at the market, sells the finest apples on the island. Germaine says the opposite. Me, I make turnovers with apples from both, and nobody can tell the difference. Whatever you do, don't tell them.
Babette. Your apples are too red.
textes.Babouches ! Jaunes, rouges, brodées, poi: Babouches! Yellow, red, embroidered, pointy! Karim. I put shoes on all of Tazira. You, what size are you? … No, don't tell me, I'll guess. Thirty-nine. No? Forty-four?
textes.Bagages ! Bagages ! Bip. Attention, vali: Luggage! Luggage! Beep. Careful, suitcase on the left.
textes.Bagarre ! Tout le monde dehors… non, tou: Brawl! Everybody out… no, everybody stay, this'll be good!
textes.Bagues de boulons, éclats de cristal, pi: Bolt rings, crystal shards, salvaged bits! What's on the shelf is for swapping, what's in the case costs next to nothing. Shiny, eh? You have {pieces} coins.
Bah. Just asking for no reason.
textes.Bah… il n'y avait plus grand-chose dedan: Meh… there wasn't much left in it anyway.
textes.Baisse la voix, {surnom}. Le trente-troi: Lower your voice, {surnom}. The thirty-third is rose petals from the oued. My mother's roses. She dried them for me. She's been gone a long time, and her garden with her. I have one box left. Enough for three years of ras el hanout. After that… I don't know. It's the only thing that frightens me. You see? Even my voice has dropped.
textes.Baisse ton coude, d'abord. … Je n'ai rie: Lower your elbow first. … I didn't say anything.
textes.Balam ! Tu as raté combien d'oiseaux, au: Balam! How many birds did you miss today?
textes.Balam ! Tu danses ce soir, mon jaguar ?: Balam! Are you dancing tonight, my jaguar?
textes.Balam est un chasseur de Yaxché. Il port: Balam is a hunter from Yaxché. He bears the jaguar's name and refuses to hunt it. He planted a dart in my shield. He says he mistook me for a jaguar. I took it as a compliment.
textes.Balam ne parle jamais. Il chasse, il rat: Balam never talks. He hunts, he misses one bird in three, and he dances like a jaguar. I call him Balam-Who-Misses. He proved to me he doesn't miss everything. My ball remembers.
textes.Balam ne parle presque pas, mais il sait: Balam hardly ever talks, but he knows everything about the jungle. He's teaching me tracks. He doesn't want Peek' to come. Peek' comes anyway. Balam sighs. That's his way of laughing.
textes.Balam ne parle presque pas. Mais il pose: Balam hardly ever speaks. But he leaves a macaw feather on my loom every week, without a word. And in the evening, he dances like a jaguar. I laugh. He keeps going. That's our conversation.
textes.Balam parle peu, mais il voit tout. Il m: Balam speaks little, but he sees everything. He finds me wild hives in the forest and shows them to me without touching them. A hunter who respects bees is a good hunter. And a good lad.
textes.Balam-qui-rate ! Tu as raté quoi, aujour: Balam-Who-Misses! What did you miss today?
textes.Balam. Tu as vu les jaguars, là-haut ?: Balam. Have you seen the jaguars up there?
textes.Balam. Ça veut dire jaguar. Je chasse le: Balam. It means jaguar. I hunt deer, peccary, turkey. The jaguar I leave alone: it's my name, not my game.
textes.Balayer la ville jusqu'à ce que Mio soit: To sweep the city until Mio is very, very old. And tell her all my stories. Even the ones I haven't lived yet.
textes.Banc ! Kia-kia ! J'ai plein de trucs à t: Bench! Kia-kia! I've got loads to tell you!
textes.Barbe-Sanglante… Le plus grand pirate de: Barbe-Sanglante… The greatest pirate of all time. He sank a hundred ships and never lost a battle. He did lose his treasure, though. Well, he hid it so well he never found it again.
textes.Bardane ! Mon pommier va bien ?: Bardane! Is my apple tree all right?
textes.Bardane ! On attaque quel mur ?: Bardane! Which wall are we tackling?
Bardane got ten out of ten for her herbarium. The only one in my whole career. Today, she lives in the trees and knows them better than I do. She's my greatest pride as a teacher.
textes.Bardane a passé la nuit dans mon pommier: Bardane spent the night in my apple tree to check it was all right. It was all right. So was she. But she scared the owl.
textes.Bardane donne des prénoms à mes champign: Bardane gives names to my mushrooms. I told her they didn't need any. Now I say good morning to Gustave every morning. She converted me.
textes.Bardane m'a demandé de décorer son harna: Bardane asked me to decorate her harness. I painted it with purple flowers, like the buddleias in the Spore Wood. Now, when she climbs trees, the butterflies follow her. She says it's the most beautiful present anyone's ever given her. The butterflies think so too, I believe.
textes.Bardane m'a tenue au bout d'une corde pe: Bardane held me on the end of a rope for three weeks, at the top of the water tower. She never let go of me. Not of the rope, not of me.
textes.Bardane passe chaque matin demander des: Every morning Bardane comes by to ask after my mushrooms, one by one. She's given them names: Gustave, the big blue one; Paulette, the orange one; Firmin, the little purple one. I found it ridiculous. One morning, I caught myself saying: “Good morning, Gustave.” Bardane heard me. She said nothing. She was smiling.
textes.Bardane vient me voir le matin et elle m: Bardane comes to see me in the morning and asks how each mushroom is doing. By first name. I told her they didn't have first names. She gave them some. The big blue one is called Gustave now.
Bardane. Gustave has a new cap.
textes.Barnabé ! Dix-sept traversées, pas un ro: Barnabé! Seventeen crossings, not one rock. A legend, oh yes!
textes.Barnabé ! Prêt pour un petit vol ?: Barnabé! Ready for a little flight?
textes.Barnabé ! Tu as encore salué la brume, h: Barnabé! You waved at the mist again last night.
textes.Barnabé ! Tu as regardé par la vitre ?: Barnabé! Did you look out of the window?
textes.Barnabé ! Tu reviens mesurer la piste, c: Barnabé! Coming back to measure the dance floor tonight?
textes.Barnabé ? Le meilleur cartographe du roy: Barnabé? The best cartographer in the kingdom, according to him. The worst, according to the rock. We used to be friends. Used to is a long way back.
textes.Barnabé ? Un humain qui chante sur sa pl: Barnabé? A human who sings on his beach about exploits he never saw, to tunes he never learned. I adore it. I listen from afar. It's the right distance for Barnabé.
textes.Barnabé Coquillard ! Ta chanson a un cou: Barnabé Coquillard! Your song has one verse too many.
textes.Barnabé Coquillard… Un humain qui dessin: Barnabé Coquillard… A human who draws maps of things he has never seen. We are very fond of him. From a distance.
textes.Barnabé a fermé les yeux pendant toute l: Barnabé kept his eyes shut the whole way up! Mine were wide open!
textes.Barnabé a la montre que je lui ai offert: Barnabé has the watch I gave him. It chimes five minutes before every departure. He's still late. I'm currently developing a watch that pushes him from behind.
textes.Barnabé a le vertige et veut quand même: Barnabé is scared of heights and still wants to fly with me. It's the bravest thing I've ever seen. People without fear, that's not courage. Him, that's courage.
textes.Barnabé a le vertige, et il est liftier: Barnabé is afraid of heights, and he's a liftkeeper anyway. Going up costs me nothing. For him, every floor costs something. He's the real hero of the Column. I write it to him in every letter. He never believes me.
textes.Barnabé a le vertige, et il est venu tou: Barnabé is scared of heights, and he came to touch a glider. With one finger. He's the bravest pupil I've ever had. He's never left the ground. But he took the biggest step of all: he came closer.
textes.Barnabé a le vertige, et il veut être li: Barnabé is scared of heights, and he wants to be a liftkeeper. He goes up trembling, he comes down smiling. I think I know where he'll end up: here, at the bottom, at the Funicular's controls. Going down is his calling. He just doesn't know it yet.
textes.Barnabé a le vertige, il est toujours en: Barnabé is scared of heights, he's always late, and he's given a name to every pulley. He's the best apprentice I've ever had. He's also the only one. But he'd be the best anyway.
textes.Barnabé a le vertige. C'est un secret. E: Barnabé is afraid of heights. It's a secret. Well, everyone knows. But it's still a secret. Me, I never get vertigo. I could take his place. I'm only saying that to help him.
textes.Barnabé dessinait les cartes. Sa carte d: Barnabé drew the maps. His map said “open sea”. The sea said “rock”. I believed the map. Twenty-two years I've regretted it.
textes.Barnabé dit que sa carte des Anciens mon: Barnabé says his map of the Ancients shows “a golden eye in the east”. That's the Mother Tree. He has good eyes, for a human.
textes.Barnabé est gentil, mais il dit « monter: Barnabé is nice, but he says “go up fast” instead of “go up to speed”. And he closes his eyes. I help him. I recite the rulebook to him while he's scared.
textes.Barnabé est gentil, travailleur, courage: Barnabé is kind, hard-working, brave. And always late. Always. I gave him a watch that rings three times before every departure. He's still late, but now he knows it. That's progress.
textes.Barnabé est passé hier soir. Il a fait t: Barnabé came by last night. He did three dance steps with Gaston on his shoulder and left again. Legend.
textes.Barnabé m'a donné un coin de terre contr: Barnabé gave me a patch of land for a few bunches. At night, he talks to my banana trees, he calls them his confidants. Me, I never listen. Well… almost never.
textes.Barnabé m'a prêté sa barque pour monter: Barnabé lent me his boat to build this wall, and he never asked me for a penny. Just that we say hello to Gaston. So we say hello to Gaston.
textes.Barnabé m'a tout appris des cabanes. Il: Barnabé taught me everything about huts. He talks a lot, he's sometimes wrong about the rocks, but his knots never give. Never.
textes.Barnabé parle à la mer comme à une vieil: Barnabé talks to the sea like an old friend. Humans say he's mad; the trees say he's kind. I believe the trees.
textes.Barnabé t'a parlé de moi ? Laisse-moi de: Barnabé told you about me? Let me guess: “it was Octave at the helm”. He's a broken record, that one.
textes.Barnabé veut faire un tour avec moi. Il: Barnabé wants to go for a flight with me. He's come as far as the foot of the Mast three times. Once as far as the tenth step. Next time, I'll wait for him at the top with a hot chocolate. People climb much better when there's chocolate at the top.
textes.Barnabé vient à midi, tout pâle, après s: Barnabé comes in at noon, all pale, after his trips up. I serve him a nice sweet hot chocolate, and in three sips, his colour comes back. Red. Then pink. Then normal. It's lovely to watch.
textes.Barnabé, c'est une légende, frérot. Il a: Barnabé is a legend, bro. He did three dance steps at the party and swears he was measuring the dance floor. He recounts his shells when I walk past. I get it: we kind of do the same job.
textes.Barnabé, l'apprenti liftier d'en bas, es: Barnabé, the apprentice liftkeeper from down below, came to see me. He wanted to “just watch”. He watched a glider for an hour, from very far away. At the end, he touched it. With one finger. I clapped. It was a big moment.
textes.Barnabé, l'apprenti liftier de Hautefond: Barnabé, the apprentice liftkeeper from Hautefond, came to see me after the reopening. He wanted to “just look”. He looked at a glider for an hour, from very far away. Then he came closer. Then he touched it, with one finger. I clapped. He went bright red. It was the finest flight of my week. And he never left the ground.
textes.Barnabé, vous avez regardé en bas aujour: Barnabé, did you look down today?
textes.Baron de Montjoie, seigneur de la ville: Baron of Montjoie, lord of the town
textes.Barricade a tort sur 1977, sur le câble: Barricade is wrong about 1977, about the cable and about the whale. She's right about everything else. It's very annoying. She's my oldest friend.
textes.Bartholomé, le vieux perroquet de Joe, a: Bartholomé, Joe's old parrot, had caught a cold. He sneezed “jellyfish-head” every thirty seconds. I gave him a lukewarm honey tea, with a teaspoon. He pinched my nose so hard I saw stars. Joe said: “He likes you!” Bartholomé got better in two days. My nose, in a week.
