textes.Basile ! Il a encore éternué pendant le: Basile! It sneezed again during the minuet.
textes.Basile ! Un génie du rien du tout, avec: Basile! A genius of absolutely nothing, with the prettiest machine at the Fair. He keeps me waiting for his giant bubble, but I know he's saving me the first seat. He just doesn't know it yet.
textes.Basile Pinceau, le peintre du village, a: Basile Pinceau, the village painter, saw the pot of blue (no. 1) floating on the Rubbed-Out Pond the day after the Great Downpour. It got stuck on a giant water lily, far from the bank. Basile swims like a stone.
textes.Basile avait réussi une bulle de deux mè: Basile had managed a two-metre bubble. I couldn't resist: I stuck my head inside! A silence, a perfectly round light, the smell of lavender… I talked to Basile for a minute, and my voice sounded like it was in a jar. He laughed so hard he dropped his bellows. Best minute of my week. Of my month, even.
textes.Basile est le voisin de stand idéal : il: Basile is the ideal stand neighbour: he laughs at all my shots, and he's never noticed what I put in his machine. Well, I think. He has these smiles, sometimes…
textes.Basile est le voisin de stand le plus ad: Basile is the sweetest and soapiest stall neighbour at the Fair. My piano owes him its cold. I forgive him every evening.
textes.Basile est un homme charmant, qui fait d: Basile is a charming man who blows charming bubbles. He said something about my box once. I forgave him. Almost.
textes.Basile est un juré merveilleux et parfai: Basile is a marvellous juror and perfectly useless: he thinks every invention is wonderful. Even the ones that explode. Especially those.
textes.Basile est à l'Étang Gommé, Lili sur la: Basile is at the Rubbed-Out Pond, Lili on the White Strand.
textes.Basile peint, j'écris. Il dit que ses vo: Basile paints, I write. He says his shutters have more colours than my poems. Since the Downpour, we're even.
textes.Basile propose d'envoyer une bulle géant: Basile suggests sending a giant bubble to fetch Achille. I'm not sure that's a good idea.
textes.Basile s'est senti si coupable qu'il a i: Basile felt so guilty that he put up a screen between our two stalls. He painted it himself: bubbles everywhere, of every size, including one shaped like a heart. The screen doesn't stop the steam at all. But it's very pretty, and I've never had the heart to tell him.
textes.Basile veut aller chercher mon frère dan: Basile wants to go and fetch my brother in a bubble. He believes in it with all his heart, and that touches me. It terrifies me too. A lot.
textes.Basile, j'ai repêché le pot de bleu !: Basile, I fished out the pot of blue!
textes.Basile, ma mouette la plus rêveuse, a ga: Basile, my dreamiest seagull, kept one of his poems in his nest. He sits on it every evening. I think he's hatching it.
textes.Basile, qu'est-ce que vous regardez dans: Basile, what are you looking at in the pond?
Bastien! Your octopus says good evening.
textes.Bastien ! Tu es encore tout rouge, mets: Bastien! You've gone all red again, put your cap on!
textes.Bastien ? Un pêcheur qui se lève tôt et: Bastien? A fisherman who gets up early and doesn't haggle too much. We get along: he fishes, I pay. Not much.
textes.Bastien distribue des bouchons d'oreille: Bastien hands out earplugs. In front of MY sound. As if it were too loud. … And he was right about the crab. That's worse.
textes.Bastien et moi, on joue aux cartes le di: Bastien and I have played cards on Sundays for forty years. He talks to his cards. He wins. I don't understand it. I've checked the cards. They're normal. He's the one who isn't.
Bastien talked to me about fishing. Two hours. Tides, bait, mackerel. I said three words: “Yeah.” “Ah.” “Right.” He said it was the best conversation of his life. … He's nice. He's tiring. Nice people are tiring.
textes.Bastien m'a tirée de l'eau le jour de la: Bastien pulled me out of the water on the day of the biggest fright of my life. I owe him that. But I won't come to the five o'clock fishing. Ever. He knows it.
textes.Bastien m'invite à la pêche de cinq heur: Bastien invites me to the five o'clock fishing every evening. I say no every evening. But when he's out at sea, I sometimes dive near his boat and leave a nice shell on his bench. He pretends not to know who it is. I pretend to believe him. We're very good at this, the two of us.
textes.Bastien ne croit pas aux fées. Il dit «: Bastien doesn't believe in fairies. He says “of course” the way you shut a door, and it makes me a bit sad. But he's never painted over my octopus. So deep down, he believes a little.
textes.Bastien voulait un petit poisson sur sa: Bastien wanted a little fish on his sail. I painted a big purple octopus, a protective one. He shouted. He says the fish are scared of it. But he's never repainted the sail. And the day Sofia came up white as a sheet from the golden point, it was my octopus that made her laugh. It protects, like I said.
textes.Bastien, c'est le meilleur porteur de pa: Bastien's the best basket carrier on the island, and the only boy I've ever knocked into the water. He's sweet. He blushes a lot. Too much sun, I think.
Bastien's a grumpy big brother. He lends me everything, even when he doesn't know it yet. His cap looks better on me than on him, but I give it back. Sometimes.
textes.Bastien, ce matin, tu as trouvé quelque: Bastien, did you find anything on your bench this morning?
textes.Bastien, frérot ! Je te rends ta casquet: Bastien, bro! I'm giving you your cap back!
textes.Bastien. Combien, la sardine, aujourd'hu: Bastien. How much for a sardine today?
textes.Batterie : quatre-vingt-dix-sept pour ce: Battery: ninety-seven percent. Leaves gathered: one thousand two hundred and twelve. Trees greeted: three hundred and forty. Trees that replied: zero. But I sense they are thinking about it.
Battery low: twenty-two percent. A cloud stayed over the solar panels all morning. Doctor Aurèle says its name is Fernand. I politely asked Fernand to move. Processing.
textes.Battre Ventaile. Une fois. D'une plume,: Beat Ventaile. Once. By a feather, that'll do me. And then carry a letter so fast it arrives before it's written. The queen says it's impossible. The queen has never raced me.
textes.Battre mon automate. Une seule fois, moi: To beat my automaton. Just once, myself, without tricks, in front of the whole Fair. Then I'll offer it a rematch. Politely. It will probably win. But I'll have had my evening.
textes.Battre mon propre record devant toute la: To beat my own high score in front of the whole city, on a giant screen, in the Hologram Square. And have the light carp do a somersault when I win.
textes.Battre son record à Dragon-Pixel: Beat your high score at Dragon-Pixel
textes.Beau fixe ! L'aiguille est tellement con: Set fair! The needle's so happy it went all the way to the end.
Set fair. I'll tell her when she wakes up.
textes.Beau temps ! Ciel bleu, vent doux, et un: Fair weather! Blue sky, gentle breeze, and a strong chance of snacks.
textes.Beau temps ! Comme hier. Comme d'habitud: Fair weather! Like yesterday. Like always. Assistant, write this down: “fair again”.
textes.Beau temps pour demain. Elle va être con: Fair weather for tomorrow. She'll be pleased.
textes.Beaucoup de mousse, comme d'habitude ? T: Lots of froth, as usual? Your moustache suits you.
textes.Beaucoup de piment ! Voilà quelqu'un qui: Lots of chilli! Now there's someone who knows how to drink! You have a warrior's throat. I'll make you mine, the real one, the one that makes the merchants of Aztlán cry.
Plenty of herbal tea, I know.
textes.Bedaine ? Le tanuki le plus rusé de la f: Bedaine? The craftiest tanuki in the forest. After me. He says it's the other way round. We've been squabbling over the title forever, and frankly, it's what keeps me awake at the market.
textes.Bedaine a encore troqué un caillou contr: Bedaine swapped a pebble for a feather again, a feather for a vial… One day he'll swap the Mother Oak for a hazelnut.
textes.Bedaine laisse des traces partout. Beauc: Bedaine leaves tracks everywhere. Lots of tracks means he's doing his shopping. I hold two things against him. But he makes me laugh. That almost makes up for it.
textes.Bedaine vous troque ce caillou-qui-chant: Bedaine swaps you this singing pebble.
textes.Bedaine, c'est le maître du troc ! Il me: Bedaine is the swap master! He finds me singing-stones, I give him hazelnuts and bits of rope. His great chain of swaps starts with me. First link!
textes.Bedaine, le tanuki du Marché aux trocs,: Bedaine, the tanuki of the Barter Market, wants to teach you the Great Swap: a pebble that, swap after swap, becomes a treasure.
textes.Bedaine. Le marchand de Ramure, avec sa: Bedaine. The Ramure merchant, with his tanuki tail. He talks more than Rachid. He doesn't want coins, only barter. He always wins, I think. I go back anyway.
textes.Belle matinée, oui. Il faut en profiter: Lovely morning, yes. Best enjoy it before the heat.
textes.Belle mer, ce matin. Je dis ça au vent,: Lovely sea this morning. I'm saying that to the wind, mind.
textes.Belle-Humeur ! Ce soir, je joue le tambo: Belle-Humeur! Tonight, I'm playing the drum for you!
textes.Belle-Humeur crie, grogne, tempête, et i: Belle-Humeur shouts, grumbles, storms, and his heart is as soft as the inside of a shell. Nobody sees it. I do. I shout hello to him every morning. He answers. Loudly.
textes.Belle-Humeur crie. Moi, je me tais. On s: Belle-Humeur shouts. I keep quiet. We get on well. He carried me out of the marsh. I've never thanked him. He wouldn't have heard.
textes.Belle-Humeur est furieux du matin au soi: Belle-Humeur is furious from morning till night and deaf from night till morning. But when he stands guard at the door of the Shark's Tooth, nobody comes in without saying hello. An excellent doorman. A passable gunner.
Belle-Humeur knocked me down once. Just once! He says it doesn't count. I say it counts. It's the only thing we agree to disagree on.
textes.Belle-Humeur m'a pris mes dents il y a t: Belle-Humeur took my teeth thirty yearth ago. We've never thpoken about that night thinthe. We thit at the thame bar, one at each end. We put up with each other. That'th already a lot, for him.
textes.Belle-Humeur veut que je chante son coup: Belle-Humeur wants me to sing his verse louder. Always louder. My fiddle isn't a cannon. But I've added a drum, just for him. He almost smiled. Almost.
textes.Belle. J'ai encore trouvé de la lavande: Lovely. I found lavender on my bench again.
textes.Belles ? Elles sont AFFICHE-NANTES ! … B: Nice? They're POSTER-PERFECT! ... Well. Pigment painted the rat, I printed the letters, and we argued about the colour for three hours. She wanted green, I wanted black. We went with green. The next Great Boucan has to be the biggest of all time, with people coming from everywhere! But our posters can't swim. You travel. You could carry three: one to Paulo, the cook of Port-Azur; one to Ulric, the innkeeper of Montjoie; and one to Tom the Fiddler, the musician at the Crâne Fendu, on Balafre. Great encounters start with a poster!
textes.Benvenuto, bienvenue ! Chez Paulo, la me: Benvenuto, welcome! Chez Paulo, the best bouillabaisse in the archipelago! The others are just soups.
textes.Bernadette a été construite ici même, à: Bernadette was built right here, at the Great Forge, by Brunehaut's grandmother. She's made of brass, like the Sun. When the Brass Sun gets its strength back in the morning, she shines too. Looks like they're saying good morning to each other.
textes.Bernadette avait une chaudière de secour: Bernadette had a spare boiler, brand new, that we never used. One day, a young man with a moustache came down from up top, Firmin. He was looking for a machine to make chocolate. I showed him the boiler. His eyes went wide. I told him: “It whistles a bit.” He laughed. I heard his laugh stop, from the other end of the Column, the first time he switched it on.
textes.Bernard ? Soixante-sept ans, des mollets: Bernard? Sixty-seven, calves of steel and a stubbornness set in concrete. He doesn't run faster than I swim. But I admit he runs fast.
textes.Bernard a encore mangé toutes les miette: Bernard ate all the crumbs on the square again. Bernard predicts nothing. Bernard eats. It's his destiny.
textes.Bernard court comme s'il avait un train: Bernard runs as if he had a train to catch. I'm very fond of him, and he worries me. He thinks I don't see him going round by the back alley.
textes.Bernard dit qu'il court plus vite que je: Bernard says he runs faster than I swim. Ridiculous. He runs faster than I run, that's all.
textes.Bernard défie quiconque de courir de la: Bernard challenges anyone to run from the fountain to the lighthouse in under a minute.
textes.Bernard joue avec nous l'après-midi. Il: Bernard plays with us in the afternoon. He points badly, but he runs well: every time a ball rolls too far, he sprints off to fetch it, shouting “hup hup hup”. Raymond and I don't bend down any more. Sometimes, to tease him, I pretend to run with him. Two steps. My knee goes hup too.
textes.Bernard, le coureur. Il fait trois tours: Bernard, the runner. He does three laps of the island a day, with a stopwatch. I did thousands with a satchel. Nobody ever timed me.
textes.Bernard, le coureur. Un retraité respect: Bernard, the runner. A respectable retiree who respects nothing, least of all my sign. He has the legs of a twenty-year-old and the cheek of a fifteen-year-old.
textes.Bernard. Il tape à ma porte à huit heure: Bernard. He knocks at my door at eight. I go to bed at six. Do the maths. I have.
textes.Bertha a la plus belle de toutes : une é: Bertha has the most beautiful one of all: an eight-pointed star. When it's lit, it scatters stars everywhere, on the sails, on the deck, on the first mate's face. Mâchefer covered in stars, {surnom}, that's worth the trip. I know Nourredine counts my lights in the evening from his terrace. So I light them all, for him.
Bertha is docked. At my quay.
Bertha does as she pleases, caïd.
textes.Berthe ! Deux pots de miel, et un hydrom: Berthe! Two pots of honey, and a mead.
textes.Berthe ! Le premier maquereau du jour !: Berthe! The first mackerel of the day!
textes.Berthe ! Une part de tarte, et pas un mo: Berthe! A slice of pie, and not a word about the nutmeg.
textes.Berthe ! Votre lucarne, cette nuit : éto: Berthe! Your skylight, tonight: shooting stars!
textes.Berthe et moi, on a grandi porte à porte: Berthe and I grew up next door to each other, in the village. She makes the best pie in the archipelago. Never criticise her pie in front of her. I tried once.
textes.Berthe fait la seule soupe de l'île qui: Berthe makes the only soup on the island that doesn't burn your tongue. She keeps the table at the back for me, far from the door. And far from certain people. She's a woman of tact.
textes.Berthe me sert mon petit-déjeuner à midi: Berthe serves me breakfast at noon without ever making a remark. Well, one or two. Her room under the roof is the best on the island for dreaming. I tell everyone. She's put the price up.
textes.Berthe me sert sa soupe douce, celle qu': Berthe serves me her mild soup, the kind you can eat without blowing on it. Pyra's, apparently, is full of chilli and hot as a volcano. I wouldn't taste it for the world. Berthe says the two are nothing alike. She smiles as she says it. She smiles a lot, Berthe.
textes.Berthe me vend son miel, je lui vends me: Berthe sells me her honey, I sell her my potions, and we each think the other is getting an excellent deal. She keeps my stool at the counter for me. She also keeps my tab. A long tab.
textes.Berthe met trop de sel dans sa soupe. Je: Berthe puts too much salt in her soup. I've been telling her for twenty years. She tells me I put too much honey in my herbal tea. She's not wrong.
textes.Berthe, c'est la raison pour laquelle je: Berthe is the reason I've been missing the tide for thirty years. Her pie, I mean. Her pie. She's the best woman on the island. The best pie. Well, you know what I mean.
textes.Bertille ! Je peux peindre ton bleu ?: Bertille! Can I paint your blue?
textes.Bertille ! Mes champignons de la semaine: Bertille! My mushrooms for the week?
textes.Bertille Champignac fait pousser des cha: Bertille Champignac grows glowing mushrooms in the darkness of the Strata. She has no sun at all; I have a push-button sun. We understand each other: we both garden where other people think nothing can grow. And we're both right not to listen to them.
textes.Bertille prétend que ses champignons bri: Bertille claims her mushrooms shine brighter than my crystals. That's wrong. It's different. Her mushrooms shine like a conversation, my crystals like a poem. We argue every evening by the pond. It's my favourite moment.
textes.Bertille, aux Jardins, prétend que ses c: Bertille, in the Gardens, claims her mushrooms glow brighter than my crystals. We held a contest, all lights out. The judge was little Tom. He said: “Both.” A diplomat, at eleven. He'll go far.
textes.Bertille, des Jardins des Champignons, f: Bertille, from the Mushroom Gardens, grows the best mushrooms in the Strata. She talks to them, apparently. I talk to them afterwards, in the pot. They're never bored, those mushrooms.
textes.Bertille, des Jardins des Champignons, m: Bertille, from the Mushroom Gardens, brought me a mushroom that glows in the dark. I put it in the stew. That night, the whole Canteen had glowing teeth. The concert has never been so bright.
textes.Bertrand ! J'ai un nouvel exploit !: Bertrand! I have a new exploit!
textes.Bertrand a écrit une chanson sur moi. «: Bertrand wrote a song about me. “Rodrigue and His Cape”. It's… comic. I'd asked for “tragic”. He says it's the same thing with a lute.
textes.Bertrand chante sur la place pendant que: Bertrand sings on the square while I shout. He says I drown him out. I say he's my backing vocals. We're a duo. He doesn't know it yet.
textes.Bertrand chante sur la place. Il chante: Bertrand is singing in the square. He's singing my song! Listen! … Ah, no, it's Rodrigue's.
textes.Bertrand chante une chanson sur moi. « L: Bertrand sings a song about me. “The Silent Arrow”. Forty verses. I'd have done one verse.
textes.Bertrand devait écrire ma grande tragédi: Bertrand was supposed to write my great tragedy. He made it a comedy. The whole town laughs when I walk by. He says it's the same thing with a lute. It is NOT the same thing.
textes.Bertrand et moi, nous sommes un duo. Il: Bertrand and I are a duo. He sings, I ring, the square claps. He doesn't know it yet. He thinks I'm bothering him. I'm accompanying him, that's all.
textes.Bertrand met tous mes exploits en chanso: Bertrand puts all my exploits into song. They're his greatest hits. He embellishes them even more. I didn't know that was possible. He's very gifted.
textes.Bertrand. Il chante sur moi. Quarante co: Bertrand. He sings about me. Forty verses. I'd have done one verse. I still stay till the end. It's polite.
textes.Bertrand. Ma tragédie. Où en est-elle ?: Bertrand. My tragedy. How's it coming along?
textes.Beurk ! La grenouille t'a avalé…\n(Il fa:
Yuck! The frog swallowed you…
(It's pitch black, it smells of mud, and it's very, very sticky.)
textes.Beurk ! Trop bien ! Et ça sent quoi ? Et: Eww! Awesome! And what does it smell like? And is it warm? And could you see its teeth? Do frogs have teeth? Wait, I'm writing this down.
textes.Beurk ?! Personne ne dit beurk à La Gren: Yuck?! Nobody says yuck at La Grenouille Repue! Sit down. I'll make you number three. Then we'll talk again.
Yuck. Course for the Skala anyway.
textes.Bielle chante comme un rail qui siffle s: Bielle sings like a rail whistling under a train: clear, straight, a little wild. She writes songs about everything, even soup. I play underneath her voice. That's my place. I really like that place.
Bielle sings louder than my drums. Nobody else manages that. By day, we repair rails side by side; in the evening, we play side by side. I don't think we've ever argued for more than three minutes. She says it's because I can't hear a thing after a gig.
Good! Then you're already a little scribe. Write it for me on a potsherd one day: I'll file it with the great papyri. Right next to them. Not on top.
textes.Bien ! Avec patience, avec respect. Comm: Good! With patience, with respect. Just as one twirls a prayer around one's heart. Ramen.
textes.Bien ! Elles écoutent. Pas toujours, mai: Good! They listen. Not always, but when they do listen, they grow.
textes.Bien ! Germaine a attrapé trois navets a: Good! Germaine netted three turnips this morning, before breakfast. That's why I married her. And for her eyes. But mostly for the net.
textes.Bien ! Il fait beau, la porte est fermée: Good! The weather's fine, the gate is closed… open… closed? Open. All is well.
textes.Bien ! J'adore Tazira. Les gens sont gen: Good! I love Tazira. The people are nice, the sardines are tasty, and nobody yells at me. Except the first mate.
textes.Bien ! J'ai trouvé une veine d'argent. J: Good! I found a vein of silver. Then I lost it again. But I found it!
textes.Bien ! Ne me le dis surtout pas. Ni à pe: Good! Whatever you do, don't tell me. Or anyone. Especially not a merchant in a hat.
textes.Bien ! Tout va bien ! Tant que ma tante: Good! All good! As long as my aunt isn't looking.
Good! You can go on being a liftkeeper.
textes.Bien caché, un petit sac de pièces ! Le: Well hidden, a little bag of coins! The captain's treasure! (He's asleep. He'll never know his parrot talked.)
Nice and hot, just as it should be.
textes.Bien le bonjour, caïd !: A very good day to you, caïd!
textes.Bien morte, Khéty ? Je vérifie, cette fo: Very dead, Khéty? I'm checking this time.
textes.Bien rangé, petit gars ? Pouce dehors ?: Tucked away nicely, little fella? Thumb outside?
textes.Bien réfléchir… Oui. Prendre le temps de: Thinking it through… Yes. Taking the time to think before speaking. Except Rivet, but we voted him an exception. You have the wisdom of an old miner, little one.
textes.Bien sucré ! Voilà quelqu'un qui sait vi: Nice and sweet! Now there's someone who knows how to live. Sugar is tea's good manners. Here, I'll give you the highest foam of the day.
textes.Bien sûr ! C'est la peintre des couchers: Of course! She's the sunset painter. She says you never see the same one twice. I can't even paint the same one once.
textes.Bien sûr ! Du cacao, du piment, un peu d: Of course! Cacao, chili, a little vanilla, and water. Sugar? What's sugar?
Of course! The lever, there, on the base. And you announce: “Going up!” It's in the rules. I'll start the stopwatch.
textes.Bien sûr ! On déterre, on déterre… Voilà: Of course! We dig, we dig… There! Grilled fish, coconut, and… oh no, that's a hot stone. Don't eat it. Well, if you want, but it crunches.
textes.Bien sûr ! Ouvrez la baie, mettez-vous d: Of course! Open the big window, stand in front of the harp, and take the spare baton from the music stand. The wind will listen to you… perhaps.
textes.Bien sûr ! Un enfant du Camp, alors. Jau: Of course! A child of the Camp, then. Bright yellow, with a brown heart.
textes.Bien sûr que je me souviens de toi ! T'e: Of course I remember you! You're the one who listened to me explain the code right to the end. Even Grandpa Ferdinand falls asleep halfway.
textes.Bien sûr que je me souviens de toi ! Tu: Of course I remember you! You're on my list of nice people. Right between Barnabé and a golden bolt.
Of course I remember you! You're the traveller from down below. You smell a bit like the sea. I noticed.
textes.Bien sûr que je me souviens de toi. Les: Of course I remember you. Elves forget nothing.
textes.Bien sûr que je me souviens. Les elfes n: Of course I remember. Elves forget nothing: sometimes that's a problem.
Of course, Clotaire. With my elbows.
Of course, Tic. The other way round.
Of course, of course. Tee hee.
textes.Bien sûr, bien sûr. Je garde une place,: Of course, of course. I'll keep a spot, just in case.
textes.Bien sûr, moussaillon ! Doucement avec B: Of course, cabin boy! Gently with Bartholomé!
Of course. Come in, the tea's hot.
Of course. And I fish for whales.
textes.Bien sûr. Et ne te retourne pas en parta: Of course. And don't turn round on your way out.
textes.Bien sûr. J'ai le temps. Beaucoup de tem: Of course. I have time. Plenty of time.
textes.Bien sûr. Regarde l'heure, pour voir ?: Of course. Check the time, just to see?
Of course. On a separate sheet.
textes.Bien sûr. Un poing de fer. Avec des perl: Of course. An iron fist. With pearls, maybe?
textes.Bien, Amirale ! Neuf ! Et demi, des fois: Yes, Admiral! Nine! And a half, sometimes?
Yes, Admiral. A geographer. From very close up.
textes.Bien, bien ! Les affaires sont bonnes, e: Good, good! Business is good, and my neighbour Kraxx sneezes all day long. It's not my fault: it's the wind.
textes.Bien, bien, très bien. Le soleil, le son: Good, good, very good. Sun, beats, friends. What else is there?
textes.Bien, bien. J'ai nourri quarante aventur: Good, good. I've fed forty adventurers, a baron and a guard who was asleep. The guard ate in his sleep. That's a talent.
textes.Bien, bien. J'ai un peu la tête qui tour: Fine, fine. My head's spinning a bit, but that's normal: the cabin spins too. Doesn't it? It doesn't spin? … Ah. Then it's me.
textes.Bien, bien. La pâte a bien levé, le sole: Good, good. The dough has risen nicely, the sun is drying the tagliatelle nicely, and nobody has broken any spaghetti in half today. Nobody I know of.
textes.Bien, bien. Le poisson ne mord pas, mais: Fine, fine. The fish aren't biting, but the sun is nice, and Pesto hasn't nipped my ear yet. It's a good day for a retired pirate.
textes.Bien, bien. Mes genoux craquent, mes cor: Well, well. My knees creak, my horns are heavy, but my memory's still here. Almost all of it. There's a little bit missing, around the year one thousand. Nothing important.
textes.Bien, bien. Mes genoux grincent, mais ma: Fine, fine. My knees creak, but my memory is well oiled. This morning, I told Noisette three legends. She told me four. Including one about me. It was false, and very beautiful.
Good, good. A rune smiled at me this morning. That doesn't happen often.
textes.Bien, chef. (Il te tend un parapluie rou: Very good, boss. (He hands you a red umbrella, very solemnly.) The station's umbrella of honour. When you open it, the propeller measures the wind. Well… it spins. Don't show it to Doctor Aurèle: he says it skews his readings.
textes.Bien, chef. (Il te tend une longue plume: Very good, boss. (He hands you a long white feather, very solemnly.) You already have a propeller umbrella? Then here is the station's feather of honour: a wind feather that landed on the anemometer one very windy day. Doctor Aurèle loves these feathers.
textes.Bien, merci ! Je ne suis tombée que deux: Fine, thank you! I've only fallen twice today. Once on the temple stairs. But they were very slippery stairs. And dry. But slippery.
textes.Bien, merci. Enfin… aussi bien qu'une Ar: Fine, thank you. Well… as fine as an Archduchess can be with three hundred files on her throne and a butler who sorts them by temperature.
textes.Bien, merci. La lumière est douce aujour: Fine, thank you. The light is soft today.
textes.Bien, merci. La lumière ondule joliment,: Fine, thank you. The light ripples nicely today.
textes.Bien, mon Archiduchesse. Je ne vous suiv: Very well, my Archduchess. I shall not follow you.
textes.Bien, monsieur le patron. Les vieux, à c: Very well, mister boss. The old ones, next to the chest. Not in the chest.
textes.Bien, mousse. Qu'est-ce que tu vois, à l: Good, cabin boy. What do you see on the horizon?
textes.Bien. (Elle sourit, pour de vrai.) Toi,: Good. (She smiles, for real.) You understand things.
textes.Bien. (Un temps.) Très bien, même. Mouet: Good. (A pause.) Very good, even. Mouette laughed all morning. It feels good, a morning that laughs.
textes.Bien. Alors en voici un : je trouve que: Good. Then here's one: I think Babette's apples… aren't that bad. If you repeat it, I'll catch you in my net.
textes.Bien. Alors prends un scarabée. Non, je: Good. Then take a scarab. No, I'm joking. Well, not entirely. Luck needs a helping hand. A scarab helps.
textes.Bien. Alors tu peux danser jusqu'au mati: Good. Then you can dance till morning.
textes.Bien. Alors un soir, vous jouerez contre: Good. Then one evening, you'll play against me. Not against the automaton: against me. Human to human. I warn you, I think slowly. Bring patience, Tacquet doesn't lend any.
textes.Bien. C'est ce qu'il faut faire. Tu fera: Good. That's what you should do. You'd make a passable guard. For a human. … Don't take it the wrong way, it's a compliment.
textes.Bien. C'est la bonne réponse. Les lanter: Good. That's the right answer. The moon lanterns on the bridges are put there by Mère-Lune. For exactly that. For those who can't read tracks.
textes.Bien. C'est la bonne réponse. Tu montera: Good. That's the right answer. You'd come up to the Skala, say what you saw, and let the guard handle it. If one day you want a sabre, come and see me.
textes.Bien. Colette a pondu. Basile boude. Fir: Good. Colette laid an egg. Basile is sulking. Firmin stole a sardine from Firmin. The real one, the innkeeper, when he came fishing. They screamed exactly the same. It was very funny.
textes.Bien. De quoi d'autre veux-tu parler ?: Good. What else would you like to talk about?
textes.Bien. De quoi d'autre voulez-vous parler: Good. What else would you like to talk about?
textes.Bien. Deux dames de la Haute-Ville m'ont: Good. Two ladies from the Upper Town looked at me sideways this morning. An hour later, they came back to buy earrings. It's always like that. It starts sideways, it ends face to face.
textes.Bien. Honorine a fait des éclairs. J'en: Good. Honorine made éclairs. I ate six. I aim better after cake.
textes.Bien. Il fait chaud. Il fait toujours ch: Fine. It's hot. It's always hot. That's good.
textes.Bien. J'ai compté mes rubis : il en manq: Fine. I counted my rubies: one's missing. As usual.
textes.Bien. J'ai construit une cabane dans l'a: Good. I built a treehouse in the tree on the square for Cerise. She's already set up a newsroom in it. She asked me for an “archive room”. She's nine.
textes.Bien. J'ai dormi dans les branches, et u: Well. I slept in the branches, and a bird woke me up singing out of tune. It was charming.
textes.Bien. J'ai gardé les chiots de Flammèche: Good. I looked after Flammèche's puppies this morning. They climbed me like a mountain. I was a happy mountain.
textes.Bien. J'ai réparé les feux du boulevard: Good. I fixed the boulevard's traffic lights this morning. They were blinking in Morse. They were saying “bored”. I gave them some music.
textes.Bien. J'ai touché une pomme à cent pas c: Fine. I hit an apple at a hundred paces this morning. Ilyria said it was luck. It was not luck.
textes.Bien. J'ai trouvé un livre que je n'avai: Good. I found a book I hadn't read. That's rare.
textes.Bien. Je crois. Papa m'a demandé de comp: Fine. I think. Dad asked me to count the parking spaces of the future Lisse-Center. I counted in rhythm. One-two-three-four, one-two-three-four. I found two thousand and one. And a solo.
textes.Bien. Je ne me suis foudroyée qu'une foi: Fine. I only zapped myself once today. A record. I wrote it in my journal. Then my journal caught fire. A little.
textes.Bien. Je serai au belvédère, ou à la Gui: Fine. I'll be at the lookout, or at the Guild. With a book. And my crystals.
textes.Bien. Je vais me reposer. Et ranger mes: Fine. I'll go and rest. And put away my bandages. And roll some new ones. For next time.
textes.Bien. La sauce mijote tranquillement. El: Fine. The sauce is simmering gently. It makes little bubbles, “blop, blop”. When it goes “BLOP”, I step back.
textes.Bien. Le fer chante, aujourd'hui. Écoute: Good. The iron's singing today. Listen. … Hear it? No? Oh well.
textes.Bien. Le métier à tisser chante, le fil: Good. The loom is singing, the thread is soft. And the harp fell silent last night. Finally, a little quiet.
textes.Bien. Le noir, ce n'est que le jour qui: Good. The dark is only the day, sleeping. It doesn't bite.
textes.Bien. Le poisson, le vent, les gens qu'o: Good. Fish, the wind, the people we love: everything comes back to those who know how to wait. Except fish, in my case. But that's a special case.
textes.Bien. Le vent souffle, le moulin tourne,: Good. The wind blows, the mill turns, the flour flows. And a turnip hid in a sack again. I ground it. No! I gave it back to Gaubert. It was all white. It looked like a ghost.
Fine. The goats ate a barrel. An empty one, luckily.
textes.Bien. Les chèvres, c'est honnête : elles: Good. Goats are honest: they eat everything and they don't hide it. Don't tell Croâ, he'd sulk on the roof for three days.
textes.Bien. Les touristes sont polis cette sem: Fine. The tourists are polite this week. Except one, who asked for milk in his espresso. Here!
textes.Bien. Mes aiguilles sont affûtées. Mon e: Good. My needles are sharp. My ink is fresh. All I'm missing is some skin.
textes.Bien. Montre tes mains. … Hm. Pas d'ampo: Good. Show me your hands. … Hm. No blisters. You hold it wrong. Come back when you have blisters.
Good. Don't let anyone fix it.
textes.Bien. On frappe, on attend, on dit qui o: Good. You knock, you wait, you say who you are. Like a dwarf. You knocked at my gate. I remember. Hard, too. Too hard.
textes.Bien. Six navets au filet avant le lever: Good. Six turnips netted before sunrise. Babette has never caught a single one. She buys them. It's not the same.
textes.Bien. Sous l'eau, tout est calme. C'est: Fine. Underwater, everything's calm. It's on the surface that people talk too much.
textes.Bien. Te voilà apprenti d'Arcanelle. Éco: Good. So you're an apprentice of Arcanelle. Listen: six masters, six spells. Aurélien Lumen will teach you light, Pyra fire, Borée frost, Zéphyrine levitation, Théophraste telekinesis, and Mère Sauge healing. Each will ask you for something: magic isn't given, it's traded. When your spellbook has its six spells, come back to me.
textes.Bien. Très bien, même. Cent douze vitres: Good. Very good, in fact. A hundred and twelve panes checked since Monday, and every one of them rings true. I tap them with my little hammer: a healthy pane goes “ting”. A tired pane goes “tonk”. This week, nothing but “ting”s. It's my favourite music.
textes.Bien. Très bien, même. J'ai vendu une pe: Good. Very good, even. I sold a shovel this morning. To you, maybe?
textes.Bien. Très bien, même. La nuit est douce: Good. Very good, even. The night is soft. Every street lamp I light is like a star I set down on the ground.
textes.Bien. Très bien. (Pyrus frappe le sol de: Good. Very good. (Pyrus strikes the ground with his pitchfork.) In the name of the Guard: thank you. Here, something to warm you up.
textes.Bien. Très bien. (Un temps.) Ce matin, u: Good. Very good. (A pause.) This morning, a drop fell from the vault onto a copper plate. “Ding.” A perfect A. I waited for the next one for an hour. It didn't come. It was a very good hour.
textes.Bien. Très bien. Je vous inscris sur la: Good. Very good. I'm putting you on the reinforcements list. It's unpaid, but you'll get a medal. Cardboard. I make them myself.
textes.Bien. Très bien. L'eau de la source du v: Good. Very good. Water from the village spring, I hope? It's the best, everybody knows. You can dance, then.
Good. Very good. The kick is clean.
Good. Very good. The book was right. About almost everything.
textes.Bien. Très bien. Tu ferais une bonne méc: Good. Very good. You'd make a good mechanic. What works today will work tomorrow because someone checked it yesterday. Come on, I'll lend you a little hammer.
textes.Bien. Très bien. Vous feriez un bon mine: Good. Very good. You'd make a fine miner. The Old Lady will like you. She likes polite people.
textes.Bien. Très bien. Vous irez loin. Ceux qu: Good. Very good. You'll go far. People who don't count end up with buttons in their pockets instead of coins.
textes.Bien. Tu es bien le seul. Ewen me montre: Good. You must be the only one. Ewen shows me his scrapes three days later, once they've changed colour. Come whenever you like, I always have honey.
textes.Bien. Un bricoleur, c'est un futur clien: Good. A tinkerer is a future customer. A good tool changes everything, you'll see.
textes.Bien. Un peu trop bien, peut-être. Un bo: Good. A little too good, perhaps. A good sailor obeys. A very good sailor can recognise a bad order. Think about it.
textes.Bien. Une belle lame qui casse, c'est un: Good. A beautiful blade that breaks is a piece of jewellery. A sturdy blade is a friend. Always choose the friend. Hm. Atchoo.
textes.Bien. Viens à la menuiserie. Je te donne: Good. Come to the joinery. I'll give you a pallet. Make whatever you like with it. Measure twice, cut once.
textes.Bien. Vous aurez une ligne à vous dans l: Good. You'll have a line of your own in the register. And you'll respect the quay's hours, like everyone else. Even Fernand. Especially Fernand.
textes.Bien. Ça prend plus de temps, ça rate so: Good. It takes longer, it often goes wrong. But what you've mended, you know by heart. And you never throw it out again.
textes.Bien. … (Hector frappe, chauffe, frappe: Good. … (Hector hammers, heats, hammers again.) … There. A bronze cog, as precise as a captain's watch. Take it to Hortense.
textes.Bientôt ! Tu viendras ? Avec ton canon ?: Soon! Will you come? With your cannon?
textes.Bientôt cinquante ! Ça se fête !: Fifty soon! That calls for a celebration!
textes.Bientôt… Tu parles comme un humain. Chez: Soon… You talk like a human. Where we live, “soon” means in fifty years. Well. If you say so. I'll iron my dress anyway.
textes.Bienvenue ! Bienvenue ! Approchez, j'ai: Welcome! Welcome! Come closer, I have a speech!
textes.Bienvenue ! Bienvenue, bienvenue, cher v: Welcome! Welcome, welcome, dear visitor, in the name of the Astralys Council, of Elder Astrée, of the Crystal Spire, of the beating Heart, of the bridges of light that switch on, of the domes of the Bubble Quarter, of the sky jellyfish in the Greenhouse, of the planets of the fountain – there are twelve of them – … (Four minutes later.) … and I am Halo. Welcome.
textes.Bienvenue ! Chez nous, les poissons nage: Welcome! At our place, the fish swim all through the house: it's more cheerful. Want to feed them?
textes.Bienvenue ! Chez nous, on ne laisse pas: Welcome! Here, we never let a visitor leave without a glass of tea. The first glass is gentle as life…
textes.Bienvenue ! Je prépare le cacao. Le secr: Welcome! I'm preparing the cacao. The secret is the foam: you pour from one pot to the other, from very high. Want to try?
textes.Bienvenue ! Regarde tranquillement. Tu a: Welcome! Take your time and look around. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Bienvenue au Bureau de vente de Lisse &: Welcome to the Lisse & Sons Sales Office! We raze, we build, we cash in. Take a seat on a grey chair. They're all grey. That's intentional.
textes.Bienvenue au Cabaret des Cailloux ! Tien: Welcome to the Pebble Cabaret! Here, listen to this one:
textes.Bienvenue au Café Cumulus ! Gustave Cumu: Welcome to the Cumulus Café! Gustave Cumulus, owner, waiter and froth-blower! A cloud milk? A summit tea? A sunshine juice? And choux buns, of course, piping hot. Nothing here is heavy, except me. Take a seat on the terrace, the view is on the house.
textes.Bienvenue au Café Feedback. Chocolat cha: Welcome to Café Feedback. Hot chocolate, three coins. Herbal tea, two coins. Melancholy is free. The jukebox only plays one song, but it's the right one.
textes.Bienvenue au Café Feedback. Le seul café: Welcome to the Feedback Café. The only café in the world where it rains inside. A little. Through the roof. I'm Spleen. I serve hot chocolate, coffee and herbal tea. And melancholy, free of charge.
textes.Bienvenue au Café Nébuleuse ! Gloubi, cu: Welcome to the Nebula Café! Gloubi, cook! (He shakes your hand. Then the other one. Then the first one again, with his third hand.) I have four arms: one for stirring, one for tasting, one for serving, and one for saying hello. Are you hungry? You're always hungry. Heavy-Feet are always hungry, that's what I love about you.
Welcome to the Café de la Bielle! Gaston. Steam coffee, cog biscuits, and spring-loaded rooms upstairs. Service is by the butler. He's slow, but he never goes on strike.
textes.Bienvenue au Crâne Fendu, mon chou ! Mam: Welcome to the Crâne Fendu — the Split Skull — sweetie! Mama Grog. Here we drink, we play, we sing, and we brawl. But we pay BEFORE we brawl. What can I get you?
textes.Bienvenue au Dôme d'Azur. Ondine Nacre,: Welcome to the Azure Dome. Ondine Nacre, president of the Tide Council. You are a hundred and forty metres under the sea, beneath three glass domes, and you are breathing air that our algae made this morning. Breathe. Gently. There. Here, the first thing you learn is never to hurry.
textes.Bienvenue au Fondouk ! Zineb. Ici, les c: Welcome to the Fondouk! Zineb. Here, the caravaneers sleep upstairs, the camels downstairs, and travellers wherever there's room. A room? A tea? A tajine?
textes.Bienvenue au Grand Concours de Grimaces: Welcome to the Great Grimace Contest! Watch closely, here we go: one, two, three… GRIMACE! … (All three pull… exactly the same face. The same one as always.) So? Who won?
textes.Bienvenue au Grand Hôtel des Embruns. Un: Welcome to the Grand Hotel des Embruns. A room with a sea view? They all have a sea view. That's the whole idea.
textes.Bienvenue au Perroquet Bleu ! Ici, la bo: Welcome to the Perroquet Bleu! Here the drinks are cool, the music is hot and the parrot is made of wood. What can I get you?
textes.Bienvenue au Port des Nuées ! Capitaine: Welcome to the Cloud Harbour! Captain Zéphyrine Ailée, harbour mistress and captain of the Dragonfly, the finest airship in the sky. That one moored over there, all white. The fastest, too. Don't believe what Héloïse says.
textes.Bienvenue au Temple de l'Aube, mon enfan: Welcome to the Temple of Dawn, my child. I am Father Clotaire. Sit down. I'll say a few words about the light that rises every morning, and about hope, which… zzz… (He jolts awake.) … which also rises. There. That was the sermon.
textes.Bienvenue au bar de la Halle Hurlante. S: Welcome to the Howling Hall bar. Sirène. Lemonades, homemade syrups, apple juice. No weird bottles, no smoking cocktails: here, we dance on lemonade and sing on syrup. Want to try my lemonade? It tickles your nose.
textes.Bienvenue au chantier, capitaine ! Ici,: Welcome to the shipyard, captain! Here we plane, nail, and tar… and dream of the open sea.
textes.Bienvenue au club de vol à voile ! Chez: Welcome to the gliding club! Here, after your first flight, we give you a wind feather. Icare Plané taught us the custom: he has a whole collection of them.
textes.Bienvenue au fond ! Marius Trident, chef: Welcome to the depths! Marius Trident, master of Azure Station and driver of the Funicular! You've just come down a hundred and forty metres under the sea in a glass bubble. Did you see the city light up in the blue? That line was closed for twelve years, and I'm still not done marvelling. Go on, breathe: down here, the air's on the house.
textes.Bienvenue au meilleur étal de nouilles d: Welcome to the best noodle stall in Neopolis! I'm Hiro, and this is Gaston, my robot arm. I taught him everything. (Gaston drains the noodles with a perfect flick.) … Well, almost everything.
textes.Bienvenue au musée ! Enfin… chez moi. Ma: Welcome to the museum! Well… my home. But it's a museum. Have you seen my collection?
textes.Bienvenue au pied de la Grande Colonne !: Welcome to the foot of the Great Column! Mistress Capucine Rouage, Grand Liftkeeper of the Guild. Tickets, timetables, complaints, items left in the cabin: everything goes through this window. Today the Column goes up to the Belvedere, and the capsule takes you on to the Clouds. It has reopened. It's proud of it.

Welcome to the foot of the Great Column! Mistress Capucine Rouage, Grand Liftkeeper of the Guild. Tickets, timetables, complaints, items left in the cabin: everything goes through this ticket office. Today, the Column goes up as far as the Belvedere. No higher. It's resting. It's earned it.
textes.Bienvenue au sommet du Zénith ! Le plus: Welcome to the top of the Zenith! The highest point in the City of Clouds. Any higher, and there are only birds. And weather balloons.
textes.Bienvenue au squat, voisin ! Moi, j'habi: Welcome to the squat, neighbour! Me, I live on the second floor of the Cannery, behind the skirting board. View of the canteen.
textes.Bienvenue aux Jardins des Champignons !: Welcome to the Mushroom Gardens! Bertille Champignac, gardener. Nothing here grows in the sun: everything grows in the shade, and everything shines anyway. Blues, greens, oranges… Don't touch them too much, they're ticklish. Look, that one just blinked. It likes you.
textes.Bienvenue aux Serres d'Altitude ! Flora: Welcome to the High-Altitude Greenhouses! Flora Verdine, gardener. Gently, don't move: there's a butterfly on your shoulder. That's Adèle, my colleague. She looks after the flowers in the second dome. She chose you. That's a good sign.
textes.Bienvenue chez le Disquaire ! Ici, il y: Welcome to the Record Shop! Here you'll find every record on the island. Vinyle lets me mind the shop when he goes out for some fresh air. Take your time.
textes.Bienvenue chez les liftiers ! Chez nous,: Welcome to the liftkeepers' house! Here, even dinner arrives on time. With a “ding”.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! C'est petit, mais c: Welcome to my home! It's small, but it's warm and smells good.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! C'est tout rond, c': Welcome to my home! It's all round, it's all warm, and it smells lovely.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! Ici, tout tourne, s: Welcome to my place! Here, everything turns except me: I'm resting.
textes.Bienvenue chez moi ! Va dire bonjour à t: Welcome to my home! Go say hello to everyone. Even Grommelot. Especially Grommelot: he loves being ignored.
textes.Bienvenue chez un chevalier de Montjoie: Welcome to the home of a knight of Montjoie! I'm polishing my armor for the tournament. Want to help?
textes.Bienvenue dans la Cité des Nuées. Célest: Welcome to the City of Clouds. Céleste Altaïr, First Councillor. You arrive in magnificent weather: bright sunshine, a light breeze, and the general mood rising sharply since the Line reopened. Take your time. Up here, even time takes its time.
textes.Bienvenue dans la Guilde ! Le tableau de: Welcome to the Guild! The quest board is right behind you: four new contracts every day. Bring them back to me, I stamp them, and you go up in rank. And now that you're registered, the adventurers in the tavern might want to team up with you. Talk to Sister Pétronille, Violette and Sir Tancrède. All three of them have… a little problem.
textes.Bienvenue dans le ventre de l'horloge !: Welcome to the belly of the clock! A hundred and twelve steps to get up here: you've earned it. I'm the belfry keeper: I give the whole town the time.
textes.Bienvenue dans ma collection ! Deux mill: Welcome to my collection! Two thousand records. Pick one, I'll put it on the turntable.
textes.Bienvenue dans mon atelier ! Attention a: Welcome to my workshop! Watch out for the wires. And the sparks. And the cat. Want to help me test my machine?
textes.Bienvenue de nouveau, {surnom} ! Pour un: Welcome back, {surnom}! For a returning visitor, I have a shorter speech. Two minutes. (He takes a breath.) Right… No? You're in a hurry? Fine. Welcome. That was the summary.
textes.Bienvenue en bas ! Anatole Crémaillère,: Welcome down below! Anatole Crémaillère, liftkeeper of the Strata Line! A hundred metres under the Square, fifty years on the job, and never once late. Well, yes: once. I didn't hear the alarm clock. I don't hear much these days, mind you. Speak loudly, but smile: that, I can hear very well.
textes.Bienvenue sur l'Île Al Dente !\nAu nord:
Welcome to Al Dente Island!
To the north: Mount Bolognese (it spits sauce).
To the west: the Colander Temple.
Please do not eat the signs.
textes.Bienvenue sur l'Île de Larsen !\nÀ l'oue:
Welcome to Larsen Island!
West: the Flower Camp.
East: Rainville (take an umbrella).
In the middle: the Main Stage.
textes.Bienvenue sur la passerelle ! Je suis le: Welcome to the bridge! I'm the Albatross's helmsman. Captain Nimbus is down below, at the kiosk: she chooses her passengers herself.
textes.Bienvenue à Arcanelle, voyageur. Je suis: Welcome to Arcanelle, traveller. I am Séraphine Astrelune, the archmage. The Great Crystal told me a visitor would come by sea. It didn't tell me you'd look so… curious. That's a good sign.
textes.Bienvenue à Cliquetis, la cité des ingén: Welcome to Cliquetis, city of engineers! Héloïse Manivelle, chief engineer. Here, we invent in the morning, test in the afternoon, and repair in the evening. Sometimes in the other order.
textes.Bienvenue à L'Alambic ! Gustave Fiole, a: Welcome to the Alembic! Gustave Fiole, qualified alchemist, almost never exploded. Magic potions, star elixirs, syrups against shyness… The syrup against shyness is out of stock. Nobody dares ask for it.
textes.Bienvenue à La Forge du Canon ! Jos. Mon: Welcome to La Forge du Canon! Jos. My hearth is the old port-side cannon: I opened it up, filled it with bricks, and it heats better than a volcano. Need a blade?
textes.Bienvenue à La Grenouille Repue ! Ulric,: Welcome to La Grenouille Repue — the Well-Fed Frog! Ulric, innkeeper! Here, we cook giant frog twenty ways: roasted, grilled, stewed, in fritters, in pastry, in a tart, in soup, in… Well, I'll give you the menu. It's three pages long. All frogs.
textes.Bienvenue à Néopolis ! Yuna Takeda, mair: Welcome to Neopolis! Yuna Takeda, mayor. My city is the most modern in the archipelago: towers, suspended trains, flying cars… and people who still take the time to drink Mamie Kiku's tea. That matters a lot to me.
textes.Bienvenue à bord de l'Albatros ! Aujourd: Welcome aboard the Albatross! Today, we're moored. But we can pretend. An altitude hot chocolate?
textes.Bienvenue à bord, matelot ! Tu seras… de: Welcome aboard, sailor! You'll be… second sailor. Amine is first. No, wait, he's first mate. That's better than first, he said.
textes.Bienvenue à l'Hôtel de Ville. Essuyez vo: Welcome to the Town Hall. Wipe your boots, the steam gets everything dirty.
textes.Bienvenue à l'auberge de La Dernière Bor: Welcome to the inn of La Dernière Bordée! Pierrick, innkeeper, at your service. A table? A hammock for the night? The hammocks are new. Well, they're less than fifty years old.
textes.Bienvenue à la Chope Ardente ! La seule: Welcome to the Blazing Mug! The only tavern under a volcano. Ulfa Chope-Pleine. A fizz? Two fizzes? The whole barrel?
textes.Bienvenue à la Gare des Nuées ! Théo Zén: Welcome to Cloud Station! Théo Zénith, liftkeeper of the Line! You've just climbed two hundred metres in a glass capsule. Two hundred! Did you see the view? I've seen it ten thousand times, and I still go “wow” on every ascent. With a little jump. The capsule is used to it.
textes.Bienvenue à la Gratuiterie ! Ici, rien n: Welcome to the Free Shop! Here, nothing gets sold, nothing gets thrown away: everything gets given! Got an object that's bored at home? Leave it here. Need something? Take it. One a day, so everybody gets a share. I'm Trocante, and I know the story of every single thing.
textes.Bienvenue à la Guilde des Aventuriers de: Welcome to the Adventurers' Guild of Montjoie! I'm Églantine, the receptionist. Registration, contracts, complaints, lost property, Master Hugues's crying fits: it all goes through this counter. Would you like to sign up? It's only ten coins, and a little crystal ball that hardly bites at all.
textes.Bienvenue à la Tour Axiome. Je suis Sept: Welcome to the Axiom Tower. I am Sept, reception android, model U-7. Height of the tower: two hundred and sixty-five metres. Lift speed: six metres per second. Number of smiles I give per day: about eight hundred. This one is for you.
textes.Bienvenue à la Tour du Zénith ! Quatorze: Welcome to the Zenith Tower! Fourteen floors, and right at the top, the finest view in the archipelago.
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue ! Mange-Clous, cuis: Welcome, welcome! Mange-Clous, cook of the Requin Borgne. They call me Nail-Eater because I ate a nail once. By mistake. It was in the soup. It was MY soup.
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue ! Mérit. Le pain, c: Welcome, welcome! Mérit. The bread is me; the beer is me; the gossip too. Some warm bread? It's fresh out of the oven.
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue ! Souvenirs d'Azur: Welcome, welcome! Souvenirs d'Azur: postcards, painted shells, kites, and the finest snow globe collection in the archipelago. It never snows here, that's the funny part!
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue au Marché de la Cal: Welcome, welcome to the Hold Market! Salomé, the best trader on the island. And the only one in Carène, but that changes nothing. Everything that floats, everything that shines, everything that sells!
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue à Port-Azur, la per: Welcome, welcome to Port-Azur, the pearl of the archipelago! Aristide Bellanger, mayor for eighteen years, re-elected unanimously minus one vote. Colette's.
textes.Bienvenue, bienvenue, cher prospect ! Al: Welcome, welcome, dear prospect! Aldric Lisse, of Lisse & Fils. We raze, we raise, we rake it in. Admiring the scale model? The Lisse-Center! An eternal shopping mall, air-conditioned, optimised, with escalators that go up AND down. Progress. Right now, here, it's only wasteland. Noisy. Colourful. Inefficient.
textes.Bienvenue, jeune ! Moi, je dansais déjà: Welcome, youngster! I was dancing on beaches back when your grandad was learning to walk.
textes.Bienvenue, mon enfant, bienvenue sur l'Î: Welcome, my child, welcome to Al Dente Island! I am Reverend Father Farfalle, high priest of the Church of the Great Flying Spaghetti. (He adjusts the golden colander he wears on his head.) This? This is my mitre. It's also very good for draining ideas. Ramen.
textes.Bienvenue… Respire. Il reste un tapis, l: Welcome… Breathe. There's one mat left, the yellow one, by the door. Sit down, close your eyes, and listen to the wind on the canvas. Want to try?
textes.Bigoudi ! Ma roue fait un bruit bizarre: Bigoudi! My wheel's making a weird noise!
textes.Bigoudi répare mes roues gratuitement. E: Bigoudi fixes my wheels for free. She says skaters and buses are the same family: they roll and they make noise.
textes.Biiiiip ! (Ses yeux s'allument très fort: Beeeeeep! (His eyes light up very bright. He shakes your hand for a long time. A very long time.)
textes.Biiip ! (Il te passe une seconde balayet: Beeep! (He hands you a second little brush, taken from his hatch. You sweep together in rhythm.)
textes.Bip ! (Il montre les carpes holographiqu: Beep! (He points to the holographic carp swimming above the square, and pretends to swim with them.)
textes.Bip ! (Il te tend de nouveau son balai,: Beep! (He holds out his broom to you again, smiling.)
textes.Bip ! Bienvenue à Astralys, la cité de c: Beep! Welcome to Astralys, the city of crystal and light! I am the Hologuide, version three point seven. The tour begins now. Please follow the guide. Please do not walk through the guide. Thank you.

Beep! Welcome to Astralys, the city of crystal and light! I am the Hologuide. Please follow the guide. Please do not walk through the guide. Stop one: the island. Astralys floats three hundred and eighty metres above the sea. Please do not lean over. If you have leaned over, please straighten up.
Beep! Welcome to Astralys, the city of crystal… Beep. Face recognised: {surnom}. Hello again. The tour begins now. Again. It's the same one. It's very good.
textes.Bip ! Bip-bip. (Le vieil androïde pose s: Beep! Beep-beep. (The old android puts down his watering can and gives you a big bow, very slow, very polite. His amber eyes blink twice. He opens his mouth… and only a little “beep” comes out.)
textes.Bip ! Je fais comme Zéro. Bip !: Beep! I'm doing like Zéro. Beep!
textes.Bip ! La visite commence ! Veuillez suiv: Beep! The tour is starting! Please follow the guide!
textes.Bip ! Réponse enregistrée : « beaucoup »: Beep! Answer saved: “a lot.” (His body of light blinks brighter.) Thank you. That is the two hundred thousand and first positive answer. I keep them all.
textes.Bip ! Une carte postale ! Image enregist: Beep! A postcard! Image saved. Added to the tour: “Stop sixteen: a postcard from down below.” Pleasant error.
textes.Bip ? (Il montre Mio du doigt, là-bas, e: Beep? (He points at Mio, over there, and makes a little gesture: she's the one to go and see.)
textes.Bip ? (Il regarde l'objet, puis toi, pui: Beep? (He looks at the object, then at you, then at the object. He politely sets it down on a bench.)
textes.Bip ? (Il te montre son balai, au cas où: Beep? (He shows you his broom, in case you've changed your mind.)
textes.Bip ? (Il te tend son balai, l'air de de: Beep? (He holds out his broom to you, as if asking: want to try?)
textes.Bip ? Votre main est passée à travers le: Beep? Your hand went straight through the guide. No harm done. It tickles. It tickles? Unknown sensation.
textes.Bip ? … Analyse… Analyse… Erreur. Erreur: Beep? … Analysing… Analysing… Error. Pleasant error. (He blinks very brightly, then very softly.) Thank you. Nobody had ever… Beep.
textes.Bip, bip… clonk ! Synthé-Soda goût fruit: Beep, beep… clonk! Moon-fruit flavor Synth-Soda. Nobody knows what Moon fruits taste like.
textes.Bip, frrr, clic. Tout bouge, tourne ou c: Beep, whirr, click. At the inventors', everything moves, spins or blinks. Even the cup on the shelf spins all by itself on its saucer.
textes.Bip-bip ! (Il applaudit. Tu balaies troi: Beep-beep! (He claps. You sweep up three leaves. He nods, very proud.)
textes.Bip-bip ! (Il sort la seconde balayette: Beep-beep! (He takes out the second little brush: shall we go again?)
textes.Bip-bip ! (Il te reconnaît. Il fait tour: Beep-beep! (He recognises you. He twirls his broom like a cane, and nearly falls over.)
textes.Bip-bip ! Le lecteur passe au vert : « B: Beep-beep! The reader turns green: “WELCOME, ROBOT NO. … ERROR … WELCOME ANYWAY.” The door sinks into the floor. Below, something very big breathes like an engine.
textes.Bip-bip-bip-bip ! (Il rit. Enfin, ça res: Beep-beep-beep-beep! (He's laughing. Well, it looks like laughing. You don't know what about, but it's catching.)
textes.Bip-bip… (Il regarde vers les Ruelles, f: Beep-beep… (He looks towards the Alleys, frowns his painted eyebrows, and shakes his head: no, no, no.)
textes.Bip. (Il hausse les épaules et continue,: Beep. (He shrugs and carries on, humming without a voice.)
textes.Bip. (Il range ton cadeau dans une petit: Beep. (He stows your gift in a little hatch on his chest, very carefully.)
textes.Bip. (Il tapote sa tempe : il se souvien: Beep. (He taps his temple: he remembers everything. You too.)
textes.Bip. Bip-biiip. Bip. (Il dessine dans l': Beep. Beep-beeeep. Beep. (He draws a little square in the air, then a bigger one, then towers. You understand: he watched the city grow.)
Beep. This furniture no longer belongs to you. Beep.
textes.Bip. Enquête de satisfaction. Avez-vous: Beep. Satisfaction survey. Did you enjoy the tour?
textes.Bip. Halo m'a appris à accueillir les ge: Beep. Halo taught me how to welcome people. He says “welcome” forty times per speech. So do I. The Professor says it's a bug. Halo says it's a calling. I prefer Halo's version.
textes.Bip. Je suis l'Hologuide. J'ai été allum: Beep. I am the Hologuide. I was switched on a hundred and twelve years ago, in Professor Quasar's laboratory. My first word was “Welcome.” My second word was “Welcome.” The Professor said: “It works!” Then I caught fire. A little bit. Version one point zero: abandoned.
textes.Bip. Je suis un guide holographique, con: Beep. I am a holographic guide, built by Professor Quasar a hundred and twelve years ago. Function: give the tour. Secondary function: give the tour. Tertiary function: error, function not found.
textes.Bip. Objet non holographique détecté. Im: Beep. Non-holographic object detected. Unable to hold it. Object… archived in my memory. Thank you. That is the hundred and third gift archived.
textes.Bip. Objet traversé. Désolé. Je suis un: Beep. Object passed through. Sorry. I am a hologram. I cannot keep anything. Except memories.
textes.Bip. Quark détecté. Veuillez ne pas trav: Beep. Quark detected. Please do not walk through.
textes.Bip. Quark passe à travers moi plusieurs: Beep. Quark walks through me several times a day. Record: forty-two times. He says I tickle. I'm not ticklish. I don't have a body. But I flicker. I don't know why.
textes.Bip. Quark. Veuillez ne pas traverser le: Beep. Quark. Please do not walk through the guide.
textes.Bip. Remarque enregistrée : « répétitive: Beep. Remark saved: “repetitive.” Analysing… The tour has been identical two hundred and forty thousand times. Conclusion: you are right. Beep. I can't do anything about it.
textes.Bip. Rêve en mode veille : faire une sei: Beep. Standby-mode dream: to add a sixteenth stop to the tour. A stop that doesn't exist yet. A stop I would discover myself. Error: cannot tour what I do not know. Error… pleasant.
textes.Bip. Visiteur reconnu : celui qui a beau: Beep. Visitor recognised: the one who enjoyed the tour a lot. Would you like to take it again? It hasn't changed. It is still very good.
textes.Bip. Visiteur reconnu : celui qui trouva: Beep. Visitor recognised: the one who found the tour repetitive. Information: it still is. Sorry. Welcome anyway.
textes.Bip. Visiteur reconnu. Celui qui préfère: Beep. Visitor recognised. The one who prefers the guide to the tour. I keep that answer in a special file. It's called “warm.”
textes.Bip. Écliptique m'a demandé de dire à ch: Beep. Écliptique asked me to tell every visitor that he is “the greatest orator on Astralys”. Information transmitted. End of information.
textes.Bip… (Il montre les cerisiers en fleurs,: Beep… (He points to the cherry trees in blossom, then to his heart. Then he shrugs, as if to say: I can't tell you any more.)
textes.Biscotte ! (Le petit rat saute de ton ép: Biscotte! (The little rat hops from your shoulder to his, nibbles his ear, then goes back to yours.) See? He chose you. He always goes back to your shoulder. (Petit-Pierre sniffles.) It's okay. He'll be better off with you, travelling, than here with Mange-Clous and his ladle. He's very clever, you know: when he disappears down a hole, he always comes back with something. A coin, a button, a pearl… Rats know where the treasures are. Here, my cabin boy's coins. And if you don't have a whistle yet to call your animals, take this one: Gwen carved it for me from a bone, with a dog, a cat, a rat and a pig carved around it. Whistle, and Biscotte will come back. And you'll come see me again, right? With him?
textes.Biscotte a léché la figure de Pépin et l: Biscotte licked Pépin's face and singed his fringe. His mother screamed. I burst out laughing. Pépin was over the moon: it was proof that Biscotte loved him. Since then, he's had one lock shorter than the rest. He calls it his Biscotte lock, and he won't let anyone cut it.
textes.Biscotte arrive en trottinant et te tire: Biscotte trots over and tugs your shoelace: “Shall we go?”
textes.Biscotte couine trois fois. Il raconte q: Biscotte squeaks three times. He's telling you something. It's surely very funny.
textes.Biscotte disparaît dans une fente du mur: Biscotte disappears into a crack in the wall. You hear a little commotion. He comes back out with {objet}, his whiskers full of dust.
textes.Biscotte dort sur ton épaule, la queue e: Biscotte is sleeping on your shoulder, his tail wrapped around your neck like a tiny scarf.
textes.Biscotte fait le tour de ta tête en cour: Biscotte runs all the way around your head, stops, then does it again the other way.
textes.Biscotte fait un petit bond sur ton épau: Biscotte does a little hop on your shoulder and nibbles your ear. Very gently. That's rat affection.
textes.Biscotte file sous une planche, ressort: Biscotte scurries under a plank, backs out again and brings you {objet}. “For you,” say his little black eyes.
textes.Biscotte grignote un bout de quelque cho: Biscotte nibbles a bit of something he found who knows where. He looks delighted.
textes.Biscotte grimpe le long de ton bras et s: Biscotte climbs up your arm and settles on your shoulder, tail around your neck. He's at home.
textes.Biscotte inspecte le bateau de la proue: Biscotte inspects the boat from bow to stern. No cheese. He comes back to your shoulder, disappointed but loyal.
textes.Biscotte m'a léché la figure et il a rou: Biscotte licked my face and singed my fringe. Mum screamed. Flammèche laughed. I was super happy: it proves he loves me. Since then, I've had one lock of hair shorter than the others. I call it my Biscotte lock.
textes.Biscotte revient en trottinant, {objet}: Biscotte comes trotting back, {objet} in his mouth. He drops it at your feet and stands up on his hind legs, waiting for compliments.
textes.Biscotte s'est endormi dans ton col, rou: Biscotte has fallen asleep in your collar, curled up in a ball. He's snoring. Ever so softly.
textes.Biscotte saute dans le bateau et file dr: Biscotte jumps into the boat and scampers straight up the mast. A ship's rat never forgets.
textes.Biscotte saute de ton épaule et file ver: Biscotte hops off your shoulder and scurries home, zigzagging.
textes.Biscotte saute de ton épaule, file dans: Biscotte jumps off your shoulder, darts into a hole… and comes back a few seconds later with {objet} in his teeth. He puts it in your hand, very proud.
textes.Biscotte se dresse sur ton épaule, renif: Biscotte rears up on your shoulder, sniffing the salty air: “Ah, the smell of the hold!”
textes.Biscotte se frotte les moustaches avec s: Biscotte rubs his whiskers with his little paws, very pleased with himself.
textes.Biscotte se met debout sur tes épaules,: Biscotte stands up on your shoulders, nose in the air, like a lookout at the top of the mast.
textes.Biscotte se roule en boule dans ton col: Biscotte curls up in your collar and lets out a tiny sigh of happiness.
textes.Biscotte sort de son trou, renifle le fr: Biscotte pops out of his hole, sniffs the cheese, sniffs your hand… and scampers straight up to your shoulder. He settles against your neck, whiskers tickling. You have a rat!
textes.Biscotte te chatouille le cou avec ses m: Biscotte tickles your neck with his whiskers. He knows it makes you laugh. He does it again.
textes.Biscotte, un petit rat blanc et brun, vi: Biscotte, a little white and brown rat, lives in the hold of the Requin Borgne. He's the secret friend of Petit-Pierre, the cabin boy. But Mange-Clous, the cook, has sworn to throw him overboard: his cheeses keep disappearing. Petit-Pierre would like Biscotte to go off with someone kind before it's too late. To lure him out of the hold, you need aged cheese.
textes.Bizarre ? Hé ! Je t'interdis. … Bon. Un: Weird? Hey! How dare you. … Well. A little, maybe. But that's part of the charm.
Weird? Hey! How dare you. … Well. A little, maybe. But that's part of the charm.
textes.Bizarre, oui. C'est le mot. Je n'aurais: Weird, yes. That's the word. I couldn't have put it better.
textes.Bizarre, {nom} ? Tu ne {le} connais pas: Weird, {nom}? You don't know {le} like I do.
textes.Bizarre, {nom} ? Vous ne {le} connaissez: Weird, {nom}? You don't know {le} like I do.
textes.Bizarre… oui, peut-être. Mais qui ne l'e: Weird… yes, maybe. But who isn't, around here?
textes.Bière de Forgefer, ragoût de Dagna, from: Forgefer fizz, Dagna's stew, Hilda's cheese! And I buy honey and fruit. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Blague du Docteur Aurèle, numéro cent do: Doctor Aurèle's joke, number one hundred and twelve: “What did one cloud say to the other cloud? Nothing. Its head was in the clouds.” End of joke. … You may laugh now. The Doctor laughs at this point.
textes.Blague enregistrée : « Pourquoi le solei: Joke recorded: “Why does the sun never go down to the Floor? Because it's afraid of heights.” Analysis: I don't understand. But Doctor Aurèle always laughs.
textes.Blague numéro cent douze enregistrée pou: Joke number one hundred and twelve saved for later.
textes.Blanche… La couleur la plus difficile. L: White… The hardest colour. White doesn't exist, {surnom}: it takes the colour of everything that touches it. Maybe you do too. I like that.
textes.Bleu ! Comme notre porte. Avant. Tu vien: Blue! Like our door. Before. Will you come and help me repaint it?
textes.Bleu ciel ! C'est très chic, le bleu cie: Sky blue! Sky blue is very chic!
textes.Bleu ciel ! C'est un progrès, non ?: Sky blue! That's progress, isn't it?
Blue, Ori. All blue. Nothing to report.
textes.Bleu, partout. Le cœur de cristal pulse: Blue, everywhere. The crystal heart pulses like breathing; the two rings turn one inside the other. So this is what holds the whole City up in the air.
textes.Bleu, toujours ? Tu es le seul à me croi: Still blue? You're the only one who believes me.
textes.Bleue ! Le bleu des portes, des barques,: Blue! The blue of the doors, the boats, Samira's indigo… You have a fisherman's eye: you look at what floats and what protects.
textes.Bleu… oui. Je l'aurais deviné. Un bleu d: Blue… yes. I'd have guessed. A deep-bay blue: calm on top, deep underneath. I'll paint you into a corner of the sea, very small.
textes.Blorp ! (Ta main s'enfonce dans sa gelée: Blorp! (Your hand sinks into his jelly, then comes back out with a “plop”.) Hey! On Gloop, that's a very rude way to say hello! And it's sticky!
textes.Blorp ! Clic ! Clic-clic-clic ! J'ai tou: Blorp! Click! Click-click-click! Got it all! No, wait, one more!
textes.Blorp ! Ils croient encore que je suis l: Blorp! Do they still think I'm their mummy?
textes.Blorp ! Pour maman ! Elle est restée sur: Blorp! For Mama! She stayed on Gloop, she's too squishy to travel, so I send her photos of everything. But I'm missing the most important part: the people down below! The real Heavyfeet, on their islands! I don't dare go down. I'm green, I wobble, and the last time I said hello to a fisherman, he yelled “A GIANT JELLY!” and jumped into the water. Could you do it? Take my holo-camera. Photograph the mayor of Port-Azur, the lady from the pirate tavern, the Baron of Montjoie and the crested granny of Boucan. Four corners of the archipelago! Mama will bounce for joy!
textes.Blorp ! Question de touriste : tu préfèr: Blorp! Tourist question: do you prefer being in front of the camera, or behind it?
textes.Blorp ! Un Pied-Lourd ! Un vrai ! Ne bou: Blorp! A Heavy-Foot! A real one! Don't move! (Click-click! He photographs you from every angle, wobbling with joy.) Glorb! Tourist! Planet Gloop, third moon on the left! I'm touring the galaxy, and I photograph EVERYTHING. Do you want to be on my postcard? You're already on it. Click!
textes.Blorp ! {surnom} ! Mon autochtone préfér: Blorp! {surnom}! My favourite native! (Click-click.) That one's for Mum. She collects Heavy-Feet. In photos, mind you! In photos.
textes.Blorp-blorp ! Merveilleuse ! J'ai pris q: Blorp-blorp! Marvellous! I took four thousand photos today. Three thousand nine hundred are of the fountain. It changes planet every minute! You have to photograph everything! It's exhausting! I love it!
textes.Blorp. Je suis né sur Gloop, troisième l: Blorp. I was born on Gloop, third moon on the left. Over there, everyone is jelly-like and green. We wobble when we're happy, we melt a little when we're sad, and we bounce when we're very, very happy. There's nothing to photograph: everyone looks the same. Even the landscape wobbles.
textes.Blorp… (Il devient tout pâle.) C'est… c': Blorp… (He turns very pale.) Is that… is that jelly? You're giving me… a cousin? No thank you. No. No, no, no.
textes.Bobor casse une brioche tous les jours à: Bobor breaks a brioche every day at four o'clock, and he leaves it on the edge of the counter. He says it's an accident. He has accidents every day!
textes.Bobor dit que ses gâteaux sont meilleurs: Bobor says his cakes are better than my frozen lava. He eats three cups every time he comes. Of my frozen lava. To check, he says.
textes.Bobor fait des brioches très honnêtes et: Bobor makes very decent brioches and honey cakes that are… all right. He claims they're as good as my frozen lava. He eats three bowls of it every time he comes. To check, he says.
textes.Bobor m'achète de la cannelle de feu pou: Bobor buys fire cinnamon from me for his brioches. One day, he put in three times too much, by mistake. The brioches were smoking. The customers loved them, and now he makes them every Friday: the “smoking brioche”. Bobor says it's our joint invention. I say it's mostly his. He insists.
textes.Bobor me donne la première brioche de ch: Bobor gives me the first brioche of every batch, in exchange for a story. It's been going on for forty years. It's the best deal of my life. And the warmest.

Bobor gives me the first brioche of every batch, in exchange for a story. It's been going on for forty years. So I owe him… let's see… fourteen thousand six hundred stories. I made half of them up along the way. He hasn't noticed a thing.
textes.Bobor, c'est le boulanger du Four Éterne: Bobor is the baker at the Eternal Oven. He's all round and smells of brioche. Every day at four o'clock, a brioche breaks by accident at the edge of his counter. It's a very good accident.
textes.Bobor, mon voisin de gauche, sent la bri: Bobor, my neighbour on the left, smells of brioche all day long. I supply him with fire cinnamon; every day at four o'clock he gives Pépin brioches broken “by accident”. We get along very well.
textes.Bof. Ce matin, j'ai tapé deux coups, pui: Meh. This morning I tapped twice, then once. Nobody answered from up top. Mistress Brunehaut says Pimprenelle might still be asleep. I got up at six on purpose. It's fine. I'll tap again tomorrow.
textes.Bof. Gaston boude, la mer est grise dans: Meh. Gaston is sulking, the sea is grey inside my head, and I've lost my favourite spoon.
textes.Bof. Il y a trop de dirigeables, ces tem: Meh. Too many airships these days. A boat floats. An airship floats too, but in the air. That's not natural. Don't tell Héloïse, she'd laugh.
textes.Bof. J'ai cassé ma dernière paire de bag: Meh. I broke my last pair of drumsticks on the cymbal last night. Tonight I'm playing with two wooden spoons. It goes “pok”. The audience is polite. They go “pok” too.
textes.Bof. Je suis tombé sur le genou. Maman l: Meh. I fell on my knee. Mum fixed it with a plaster. She wanted to put a valve on it. I said no. She said “shame”. She fixes everything, Mum. Even knees.
textes.Bof. L'Assemblée a duré cinq heures hier: Meh. The Assembly lasted five hours last night. We were supposed to choose the colour of the new walkway. We ended up talking about the meaning of life. We didn't choose the colour. But the meaning of life, we nearly found it.
Meh. The Little Diver's in for a service. Yolande found a screw that was “giving her funny looks”. Three days out of the water. I'm pacing round and round the Pool. The fish watch me go round. They must think it's a funny sort of dive.
textes.Bof. Le Petit Train m'a livré des champi: Meh. The Little Train delivered me some very sad mushrooms from the Gardens. Sad mushrooms, my pebble, make a sad stew. I put a double helping of songs in the pot. We'll see.
textes.Bof. Le rouge ne veut pas sécher. La roc: Meh. The red won't dry. The rock's damp today: the Chasm breathed all night. My sunset is running. It makes a crying sunset. Pretty, mind you. But not what I planned.
textes.Bof. Un nuage tout gris est resté sous l: Meh. A grey cloud sat under the Station all day. You couldn't see Hautefond any more. The passengers kept asking “where are we?”. I said “in the sky!”. They didn't find that precise enough.
textes.Bois de l'eau ! Danser au soleil, ça ass: Drink some water! Dancing in the sun dries you out. Water from the village spring is the best.
textes.Bois des Lutins. Nord-est. Gobelins rapi: Goblin Wood. North-east. Fast goblins. They throw spears. Small ones. They sting. Stay behind a tree, count to three, shoot.
textes.Bon bois. Droit, sec, solide. Voilà ving: Good wood. Straight, dry, solid. Here's twenty coins. And… thank you, {surnom}.
textes.Bon choix ! Cet objet a déjà fait trois: Good choice! This item has already been round the island three times. It's got a good temperament.
textes.Bon choix ! Classique et indémodable. Je: Good choice! Classic and timeless. I'll sew you one whenever you like. With a nice red mohawk, like Rouille's.
textes.Bon choix. Avec un nuage de crème. Comme: Good choice. With a cloud of cream. Like the Rainville sky, only better.
textes.Bon retour parmi nous, {surnom}. Visite: Welcome back, {surnom}. Visit number {visites}. I count everything. I can't help it.
textes.Bon vent ! Approche, regarde dans une lo: Fair winds! Come closer and look through a spyglass: each one shows a different side of the archipelago.
textes.Bon vent ! Attention au plateau, il est: Fair winds! Mind the tray, it's full of clouds.
textes.Bon vent ! Attention aux cordes, elles s: Fair winds! Mind the ropes, they're older than I am.
textes.Bon vent ! Au sens propre : le vent est: Fair winds! Literally: the wind is fair today. I've measured it.
Fair winds! It's windy today. So it really is a fair wind.
textes.Bon vent ! Bienvenue au Café Cumulus ! A: Fair winds! Welcome to the Cumulus Café! Sit wherever you like, the sky is for everyone.
textes.Bon vent ! Bienvenue au cœur des Sustent: Fair winds! Welcome to the heart of the Levitators. Don't lean over the shaft: it's very deep, and very blue.
textes.Bon vent ! Bienvenue à bord de la Libell: Fair winds! Welcome aboard the Dragonfly! I'm Captain Zéphyrine's first mate. Don't touch the wheel… unless I offer you a go.
textes.Bon vent ! Capitainerie du Port des Nuée: Fair winds! Cloud Harbour Master's Office. A departure, a complaint, a forecast?
Fair winds! Shh… I'm listening to the radio.
textes.Bon vent ! Chut… l'orateur va bientôt fi: Fair winds! Shh… the speaker's nearly done. In an hour or so.
textes.Bon vent ! Entre, entre, mais ne reste p: Fair winds! Come in, come in, but don't stand still for too long: Plic might mistake you for a plant.
textes.Bon vent ! Et je dis ça au sens propre :: Fair winds! And I mean that literally: here, the wind does the playing. I conduct.
textes.Bon vent ! Et si vous voyez un nuage qui: Fair winds! And if you see a cloud with no name, come back and describe it to me.
textes.Bon vent ! Ici, on fabrique du vent. Du: Fair winds! Here, we make wind. Straight, smooth, well-mannered wind.
textes.Bon vent ! Je n'arrive pas à choisir : l: Fair winds! I can't decide: the cloud jar or the spinning cup?
textes.Bon vent ! L'ascenseur monte au sommet e: Fair winds! The lift goes up to the top in twenty seconds. The record belongs to Théo: he climbed up on foot, in ten minutes, just to see.
textes.Bon vent ! Ne touche à rien, s'il te pla: Fair winds! Please don't touch anything: that button there raises the island by a centimetre.
textes.Bon vent ! Oh, un visiteur ! Bienvenue a: Fair winds! Oh, a visitor! Welcome to the Council: here, everyone can speak. Even you. Especially you.
textes.Bon vent ! On dit que le dimanche, la Li: Fair winds! They say that on Sundays, the Dragonfly goes all the way down to Rigging Harbour. Right to the bottom!
textes.Bon vent ! Pardon, je reste au garde-à-v: Fair winds! Forgive me, I must remain at attention: station regulations. Article one.
