textes.Boum ! Excellent choix. Zigomar dit que: Boom! Excellent choice. Zigomar says every great breakthrough starts with a boom. Mum says every great boom ends with a ceiling to fix. They're both right.
textes.Boum, ba-da boum ! Le djembé résonne aut: Boom, ba-da boom! The djembe echoes around the fire… and, somewhere in the camp, another drum answers you.
textes.Boum, ta-ka, boum ! Omar. Je joue du ben: Boom, ta-ka, boom! Omar. I play the bendir, the round drum. All day long, I drum on tables. In the evening, they finally let me drum on something made for it.
textes.Bourrasque ! Quand il y aura des feux d': Bourrasque! When will there be fireworks?
textes.Bourrasque a dit à tout le café que j'ét: Bourrasque told the whole café I was the best bassist on the island. I blushed for a week. It's true, though. I'm the only bassist on the island.
textes.Bourrasque m'a dit qu'avant, il y avait: Bourrasque told me there used to be a huge concert on the meadow. With fireworks. I've never seen fireworks.
textes.Bourrasque parle pour deux. Ça tombe bie: Bourrasque talks for two. Works out well: I don't talk. She drums, I follow. On stage and in life.
textes.Bourrasque, la batteuse de Rainville, vi: Bourrasque, the Rainville drummer, sometimes comes to listen to our djembes, hiding behind a bus. I pretend not to see her. I think she'd like to play with us.
textes.Bourru ? L'autre tambour. Le grand, le l: Bourru? The other drummer. The big one, the slow one. He sends the party to sleep, I wake it up, and Lilas says together it's the right rhythm. A mystery. I say he slows me down.
textes.Bourru ? Oh… il tape le grand tambour, i: Bourru? Oh… he beats the big drum, he minds the basket lift, and he says “Hrmm”. That's all. But his drum, I'd know it among a thousand.
textes.Bourru a encore oublié de remonter la na: Bourru forgot to bring the basket lift back up again. Three rabbits waited at the bottom all morning. They ended up taking the stairs. Did them good.
textes.Bourru m'a sauvé la vie, il y a dix ans,: Bourru saved my life ten years ago, with his bare hands. I owe him everything. And yet I no longer ride in his basket lift. It hurts his feelings. I'm ashamed of it. Hoo.
textes.Boussoles, parapluies, mécaniques et res: Compasses, umbrellas, mechanisms and springs. Everything is adjusted, everything is guaranteed, everything is on time. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Bouton n'est PAS dans ton pétrin. Pas au: Button is NOT in your dough trough. Not today.
textes.Bouton-d'Or ! T'as vu mon cœur hier ?: Bouton-d'Or! Did you see my heart yesterday?
textes.Bouton-d'Or a médité avec moi pendant qu: Bouton-d'Or meditated with me for forty seconds. Then she said: “I get it all!” and ran off. Perhaps she was right.
textes.Bouton-d'Or m'a demandé pourquoi les vie: Bouton-d'Or asked me why old ladies fall out. I told her it's because they have too many memories. She said we should make them into crowns. I didn't know what to say.
textes.Bouton-d'Or tresse des couronnes pour to: Bouton-d'Or weaves crowns for the whole camp. She's the prettiest seed I've ever seen grow.
textes.Bouton-d'Or veut devenir grenouille. Je: Bouton-d'Or wants to become a frog. I told her it was possible if she breathed properly. She breathes very well.
textes.Bouton-d'Or, elle fait des couronnes de: Bouton-d'Or makes flower crowns and runs super fast. We send signals in the evening. She's awesome. But don't tell, she's a camp girl and we're not supposed to.
textes.Boïng ! Tes jambes se transforment en re: Boing! Your legs turn into springs! You jump three times higher!
Bramm! Your mug's waiting. The dented one.
textes.Bramm a un cœur grand comme sa porte, et: Bramm has a heart as big as his gate, and just as firmly shut. I've been bringing him a bowl at noon for a hundred and fifty years. He says “Hmph”. That means thank you.
textes.Bramm dit que je garde un tapis. Je gard: Bramm says I guard a rug. I guard a king. He guards a gate that never moves. We'll see who has the harder job.
textes.Bramm est fâché contre moi depuis cent v: Bramm has been cross with me for a hundred and twenty years. I don't quite remember why. Something about a floor. I smile at him anyway. It annoys him, I think.
textes.Bramm n'a pas souri depuis cent ans. La: Bramm hasn't smiled in a hundred years. The last time was when a barrel of fizz fell on an elf.
textes.Bramm vient boire ici après sa garde, to: Bramm comes in for a drink after his watch, every evening for a hundred and eighty years. He doesn't talk, he doesn't smile. Sometimes he does. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Bramm vient boire ici après sa garde. Il: Bramm comes for a drink here after his watch. He smiles, sometimes. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Bramm, c'est le meilleur rocher de la mo: Bramm is the best rock on the mountain: he doesn't move, he keeps you warm, and the goats adore him. He loves them too. He'll never say so.
textes.Bras de fer ? Ce samedi, je gagne, le Mu: Arm-wrestling? This Saturday, I win, Silent One!
textes.Bras gauche : réparé. Erreur agréable :: Left arm: repaired. Pleasant error: intact.
textes.Brasero et moi, on est les deux plus vie: Brasero and I are the two oldest in the Fronde. He keeps the fire, I keep the pot. No fire, no soup. No soup, no Assembly. We argue about everything, except what matters.
textes.Brasero et moi, on n'est d'accord sur ri: Brasero and I have agreed on nothing for fifty years. He's the Fronde, I'm the Guild. He shouts, I keep quiet. He brings the biscuits, I provide the tea. We've never quarrelled. He's my oldest friend. Don't tell him, he'd sing it.
textes.Brasero et sa bande ont fondé la Fronde: Brasero and his gang founded the Fronde when I was little. My grandmother said they were mad. Then she forged them their first cooking pots. The Enclumes have always had a soft spot for mad people who make things.
textes.Brasero m'a tendu la clé de parole quand: Brasero handed me the speaking wrench when I was twelve, and I didn't say anything. He understood anyway. He's the one who gave me the rock. Everything I paint is a bit of a thank-you to him.
textes.Brasero mange toujours à la même table,: Brasero always eats at the same table, the second one, and he always leaves a coin under his bowl, “for a stranger's soup”. I've watched him do it for twenty-five years, and he says he did it before that too. I never found out who the stranger was. Maybe it's you.
textes.Brasero parle au brasero, le soir, quand: Brasero talks to the brazier in the evening, when everyone's gone. I've heard him. He tells it about his day. The fire answers by crackling. I think they agree on almost everything.
textes.Brasero, c'est le grand-père de toute la: Brasero is the grandpa of the whole Fronde. He says things I don't always understand, but they make me feel better anyway. He told me crossing the Bridge on a skateboard is forbidden. But nobody ever voted on it. So I cross it. Slowly.
textes.Brasero, le vieux de la Fronde, m'a écri: Brasero, the old man of the Fronde, wrote to me: “Four worlds, and not one shared assembly.” He's right. I replied: “Come. We shall sit around the Bubble Fountain.” He wanted a fire. Under the sea, fire is complicated. We are negotiating.
textes.Brasero, le vieux fondateur de la Fronde: Brasero, the old founder of the Fronde, comes to the Guild for tea once a month. We agree on nothing. We have never quarrelled. He brings the biscuits, I provide the tea. It's our peace treaty.
textes.Bravo ! Bravo ! Le vent vous a obéi, et: Bravo! Bravo! The wind obeyed you, and it obeys no one. Not even me, on Tuesdays. Here: a wind feather, it had got caught in the strings. The City's conductors wear one in their buttonhole.
Well done! That's very rare! You'll go far. Much further than me. Not that it's hard, mind you, I'm still on the first floor.
textes.Bravo ! Et la calebasse reste fermée pen: Well done! And the gourd stays closed during my matches.
textes.Bravo ! Et maintenant, un thé : j'ai fro: Bravo! And now, a cup of tea: my ears are cold.
textes.Bravo ! La douche, c'est la meilleure sa: Bravo! The shower is the best concert hall in the world. Come join the choir, we need some power.
textes.Bravo ! Le vent vous connaît, maintenant: Bravo! The wind knows you now.
textes.Bravo ! Tu as tenu… presque une minute !: Bravo! You lasted… almost a minute! Next time, we'll tackle sit-ups.
textes.Bravo, pilote ! Prochaine étape : la por: Well done, pilot! Next stop: the door.
textes.Bravo, tu as l'œil ! Tiens, prends-en tr: Well done, you've got a good eye! Here, take three: they're the best ones. Old Bastien would say you've got a gardener's nose.
textes.Bravo, tu as trouvé la manette ! Personn: Well done, you found the lever! Nobody ever finds it. Here, a nice hot chocolate, and some honey bread for the road.
Well done, you found the lever! Nobody ever finds it. Here, a nice hot chocolate… and some steam socks: my husband has invented forty pairs.
Well done. The river owes you seven.
textes.Bravo… tout bas. Le vent de nuit vous a: Bravo… softly. The night wind listened to you, and it hardly listens to anyone. Here: a wind feather, left behind in the strings. It brings conductors good luck.
Brief? Eleven minutes, Lyre. That is brief.
textes.Bricole fabrique des machines avec ce qu: Bricole builds machines with what I find too ugly for my jewellery. I make jewellery with what she finds too pretty for her machines. We swap everything on Thursdays. We cheat a little. On purpose.
textes.Bricole me garde les boulons trop beaux: Bricole keeps me the bolts too pretty for her machines. I keep her the ones too ugly for my jewellery. On Thursdays, we swap. But I cheat a bit: I give her pretty ones too. She cheats too. We both know it.
textes.Bricole, ce boulon est trop beau pour to: Bricole, this bolt is too pretty for you.
Bricolette thinks it's bad luck. Seven dates, seven excuses: a storm, a clock to repair, a second fast… It's me, {surnom}. Every time. I'm afraid that once I'm happy for good, time will start going faster. I know. For a clockmaker, it's ridiculous. Time passes at the same speed for everyone. I've measured it.
textes.Bricolette, c'est ma fiancée depuis tren: Bricolette has been my fiancée for thirty-one years. She's always on time, the other way round. And she sells my presents. With my consent. Well, almost.
textes.Brigadier Lefort, garde municipal. Circu: Constable Lefort, town watch. Move along… no, wait. You look resourceful. I may need you.
textes.Brigadier Lefort. Rien à signaler. Enfin: Constable Lefort. Nothing to report. Well, almost.
textes.Briller la mer… Je l'avais oublié. Merci: Makes the sea sparkle… I had forgotten. Thank you, {surnom}.
textes.Brindille ! Du courrier pour la capitain: Brindille! Any post for the harbour office?
textes.Brindille ! J'ai un nouveau sort pour te: Brindille! I've got a new spell for your drops!
textes.Brindille ! Tu as de la rosée de lune po: Brindille! Have you got moon dew for me this morning?
textes.Brindille ? Ma fournisseuse de rosée de: Brindille? My moon-dew supplier, and the soggiest fairy in the kingdom. She loses her drops, she cries, she makes more. It's practically a business.
textes.Brindille a perdu ses gouttes de rosée p: Brindille lost her dewdrops everywhere. There are even some at the very top of the cave!
textes.Brindille apporte le courrier à la bibli: Brindille brings the mail to the library. Flying. Between the shelves. She's kind, fast, and as quiet as a bell. I put up a sign. She walks now. Her wings don't.
textes.Brindille avait des ailes trop grandes p: Brindille had wings too big for her, and she hid them under a coat. I taught her to fly against the wind. Now she's the fastest of the postwomen. She brings me all the news from the open sea.
textes.Brindille cherche encore ses gouttes de: Brindille is still looking for her dewdrops. She loses them everywhere, then she cries, and her tears make new drops. It never ends.
textes.Brindille croit que les nouvelles doiven: Brindille thinks news should travel in envelopes. News is for shouting! By the time she's folded her letter, I've already told the whole city. She holds it against me. I understand.
textes.Brindille est gentille. Voilà. Ne le rép: Brindille is kind. There. Don't repeat it. She cries too much, she loses everything, but she says hello. Every day. Even to me.
textes.Brindille est ma cousine. Elle livre le: Brindille is my cousin. She delivers the post on her wings, very fast. I invented a jet-powered bag for her to go even faster. It worked! A little too well. She doesn't want my inventions any more. People are so ungrateful.
Brindille never gets my riddles. She thinks it matters. It doesn't: she has a heart that understands everything before her head does. That's much rarer.
textes.Brindille passe au Diable Repu chaque mi: Brindille drops in at the Diable Repu every noon for a Brasier coffee. She pays for it in fresh news: the best currency there is, for a tavern keeper. She talks fast, and she flies even faster.
textes.Brindille venait m'emprunter ma longue-v: Brindille used to come and borrow my spyglass to watch for ships. She said it was for the post. One evening, I saw her on the post office roof, the spyglass on her knees, just looking at the sea. I said nothing. The next day, I gave her my old cabin-boy spyglass. She wears it around her neck.
textes.Brindille vient m'emprunter ma longue-vu: Brindille comes to borrow my telescope to watch for ships. She says it's for the post. I think she mostly likes seeing the sea from up high. She has wings, lucky thing.
textes.Brindille, c'est ma moitié. Elle perd to: Brindille is my other half. She loses everything, she cries at everything, and she has more heart than the whole kingdom. I worry about her every morning. It's my way of counting.
textes.Brindille, c'est mon contraire : elle es: Brindille is my opposite: she's all calm, all blue, all sad. I'm everything else. Between the two of us, we make one normal fairy.
textes.Brindille, la factrice ailée, s'est foul: Brindille, the winged postwoman, has sprained a wing. There are three letters left to deliver: to Grumbald, the innkeeper, to Ombreline, the librarian, and to Gorgoth, the arena champion.
textes.Brindille. Combien en as-tu perdu, cette: Brindille. How many have you lost this week?
textes.Brioche ? La chatte rousse ? (Elle souri: Brioche? The ginger cat? (She smiles.) Oh yes. She comes onto the terrace when I knit. She pretends to sleep, and as soon as the ball of yarn rolls… hop! She catches it, nibbles it, and gives it back. Well, almost. As it happens: this morning, a red ball of yarn fell out of my basket. It rolled into the hotel garden. I didn't have time to look for it: Monsieur Edmond was calling me about the laundry. Take it, if you find it. For Brioche, it's a treasure.
textes.Brioche arrive… quand elle a décidé d'ar: Brioche arrives… when she has decided to arrive. Tail held high.
textes.Brioche bondit sur un papillon… et le ra: Brioche pounces on a butterfly… and misses. She grooms herself as if nothing happened. It was on purpose.
textes.Brioche bondit sur un papillon… le rate…: Brioche pounces on a butterfly… misses… and pretends she never tried.
textes.Brioche cligne lentement des yeux en te: Brioche blinks slowly as she looks at you. In cat language, that's a kiss.
textes.Brioche dort, une patte sur les yeux. Ne: Brioche is sleeping, one paw over her eyes. Don't wake her. She'd never forgive you.
textes.Brioche déteste l'eau. Mais elle adore l: Brioche hates water. But she loves boats. She settles on the driest bench and keeps an eye on the fish.
textes.Brioche fait sa toilette avec le plus gr: Brioche washes herself with the utmost seriousness. One ear, then the other. Then a paw. Then the ear again.
textes.Brioche miaule, se retourne vers toi, pu: Brioche miaows, turns back to you, then looks into the distance. Again. And again. She's sniffed out a treasure.
textes.Brioche monte dans la barque du bout des: Brioche steps into the boat on tiptoe. Water everywhere! She sits at the front, deeply offended.
textes.Brioche monte dans le bateau d'un bond é: Brioche hops into the boat with an elegant leap and settles at the bow, like a furry figurehead.
textes.Brioche poursuit un papillon jusqu'en ha: Brioche chases a butterfly up to the top of a low wall, then looks down at you like a queen.
textes.Brioche rentre à la maison sans se retou: Brioche goes home without looking back. She'll be back. If she feels like it.
Brioche purrs like a little engine.
textes.Brioche s'approche enfin. Elle renifle t: Brioche finally comes closer. She sniffs your hand for a very long time, very dignified. Then she rubs against your leg, just once. It's decided: she's coming with you.
textes.Brioche s'arrête net. Les oreilles en av: Brioche stops dead. Ears forward, she stares at a spot in the distance and miaows softly. There's a treasure over there!
textes.Brioche s'arrête, renifle l'air, puis te: Brioche stops, sniffs the air, then shoots you a look that says: “Can't you smell ANYTHING? Over there. A treasure.”
textes.Brioche s'assoit, très droite, enroule s: Brioche sits down, very straight, wraps her tail around her paws and gazes at the world, satisfied.
textes.Brioche s'est roulée en boule à tes pied: Brioche has curled up into a ball at your feet, nose tucked in her tail. She purrs in her sleep.
textes.Brioche s'étire au soleil, tout en longu: Brioche stretches out in the sun, all length. A stretching cat is thirty extra centimetres of happiness.
textes.Brioche se fige, une patte levée, le reg: Brioche freezes, one paw raised, gazing at something only you can't see yet. Miaow? A treasure is hidden in that direction.
textes.Brioche se frotte contre tes jambes, la: Brioche rubs against your legs, her tail raised like a question mark.
textes.Brioche se frotte contre tes jambes, ron: Brioche rubs against your legs, purrs loudly, then pretends not to know you. That's her way of saying yes.
textes.Brioche te donne un petit coup de tête d: Brioche gives your hand a little headbutt. She wants a stroke. But she won't ask twice.
textes.Briser le sceau des Abysses: Break the seal of the Abyss
textes.Brrr ! L'eau noire est glaciale… Tu rega: Brrr! The black water is freezing… You swim back to the south shore.
textes.Brrr ! Le froid du Cocyte te mord les do: Brr! The cold of the Cocytus bites your fingers. A coat, in the Vestibule… the inscription did say so.
textes.Brrr. Une maison vide, des toiles d'arai: Brrr. An empty house, cobwebs in every corner… and a chest, over there, at the back.
textes.Brrrt-brrrt… La photocopieuse crache une: Brrrt-brrrt… The photocopier spits out a sheet: “FORM REJECTED. Stamping order not compliant. Please start again from the beginning. Thank you for your administrative patience.” The red “SEEN” marks fade by themselves. (Reread the staff memo, near the entrance.)
textes.Bruit de Fond ! C'est ce que dit la vois: Background Noise! That's what the neighbor says. We took it as a compliment.
textes.Brume a le meilleur nez de Ramure, après: Brume has the best nose in Ramure, after Pivoine's, and she knows what I've done all day before I do. A tracker is never wrong. Never forgives, either.
textes.Brume a trouvé des traces étranges près: Brume found strange tracks near the great pool. Not paws. Not feet. Round tracks. She's still searching.
textes.Brume adore les boussoles. Celle qui ind: Brume loves compasses. The one that pointed south, brought back from Cliquetis, she wanted it, my friend! But I'd already swapped it in Carène, for a telescope. When she found out, she looked at me the way you look at a trail that leads nowhere. She's never quite forgiven me. I'm keeping the next compass for her. Promise.
textes.Brume flaire, moi je calcule. Elle manqu: Brume sniffs, I calculate. She lacks a little poetry, that girl. But she has eyes in her nose. We compare notes every evening, my star against her tracks.
Brume reads the mud for me every morning. She doesn't believe in the King. But she reads honestly. That's rarer than believing.
textes.Brume lit mes traces. Chaque matin. Elle: Brume reads my tracks. Every morning. She knows where I run, how many laps. She says nothing. To no one. … One day, at the root bend, she crouched. Scraped the moss. A flat stone. The best foothold. … She said nothing. Neither did I. I run on it every night.
textes.Brume m'a apporté une carte des traces r: Brume brought me a map of the round tracks at the big pond, drawn in charcoal, very neat. I kept it one night. I added the position of the moon, the falling angle of my star, a few constellations and a little poem. The next day she didn't recognise her map. She said: “Hm.” I think that was admiration.
textes.Brume. Elle piste en bas, je veille en h: Brume. She tracks down below, I keep watch up top. Good work. She talks little. I like her for that. For the rest too.
textes.Brumeuse, je l'avoue. Lili a encore dema: Misty, I confess. Lili asked to go down again. I said “soon”. She sulked all day. A cold front has settled over the house.
textes.Brunehaut ! Un petit caillou pour ton fe: Brunehaut! A little pebble for your fire?
textes.Brunehaut est plus forte que moi. Elle r: Brunehaut is stronger than me. She laughs louder than me. She fixed my mill without asking for anything. I owe her a lot. And an arm-wrestle every week.
textes.Brunehaut fait les meilleures épées de l: Brunehaut makes the best swords on the island and the loudest laugh in the Middle Town. Her swords comply with regulations. Her laugh does not. But I won't put it in the regulations.
textes.Brunehaut fait les épées de la garde. El: Brunehaut makes the guard's swords. They're perfect. She engraved “Do not wake Gilles” on Gilles's. She says it's for safety. His or everyone else's, I'm not sure.
textes.Brunehaut forge des épées magnifiques, m: Brunehaut forges magnificent swords, but so sad! All that metal without a speck of magic. I try to cheer them up a little. She gets cross. She laughs while she gets cross. She's a friend.
textes.Brunehaut m'a battu au bras de fer. Troi: Brunehaut beat me at arm wrestling. Three times. The fourth time, I sneezed flour, she laughed, and I won. She says it doesn't count. I say the flour is part of me.
textes.Brunehaut prend deux bols à midi, un pou: Brunehaut takes two bowls at noon, one for her and one “for the steam hammer”. She laughs so hard the spoons dance. When she's not here, La Marmite is too quiet. I put the radio on. There is no radio. I sing.
Brunehaut. Your flour for the week.
textes.Brunna ! Tu as encore ronflé, ça s'enten: Brunna! You were snoring again, I could hear it all the way to the mine!
textes.Brunna a le souffle d'une forge et le cœ: Brunna has the breath of a forge and the heart of a lantern. She snores. But when I come home covered in dust, she says nothing: she pats my beard and serves me soup.
Brunna says my coal is wet. It is not wet. She just blows too hard, and it sends sparks everywhere.
textes.Brunna ronfle comme le soufflet de Borin: Brunna snores like Borin's bellows, with the same hole. So I sleep in the mine, it's quieter. Every evening, she leaves a basket at the tunnel entrance. She never comes down. She says mines are for moles and husbands.
textes.Brunna souffle au soufflet de Borin, ell: Brunna works Borin's bellows, hides bread and butter in my apron and scolds me when I burn myself. Which is often. She scolds often.
textes.Brunna, et ma couchette dans la mine: Brunna, and my bunk in the mine
textes.Brunna, plus fort ! Le maître dit que le: Brunna, harder! Master says the iron's cold!
textes.Bruno ! Des glaçons contre trois noix ?: Bruno! Ice cubes for three coconuts?
textes.Bruno ! Il en reste, du fraise-dauphin ?: Bruno! Is there any strawberry-dolphin left?
textes.Bruno a dit au brigadier qu'il avait vu: Bruno told the sergeant he'd seen a white shadow with a croissant in its mouth. It was Brioche! He snitched! I sulked for a whole day. I didn't even have an ice cream. In the evening, he gave me a free scoop of strawberry-dolphin and I forgave him. But I haven't forgotten.
textes.Bruno m'a proposé de m'associer. « Victo: Bruno offered to go into business with me. “Victor and Bruno, ice-cream makers!” I said no, out of pride. Today my snow-globe shop is right next to his kiosk. Customers buy an ice cream from him, then a globe from me, to stay cool. I tell everyone: you don't fight Bruno. You live next door to him. It's better.
textes.Bruno, c'est mon frère de glaçons. Je lu: Bruno is my brother in ice cubes. I pinched his coconut ice cream recipe, he'd pinched it from his grandma: we're even. Best ice-cream maker in the world, and the worst recipe keeper.
textes.Bruno, il fait les meilleures glaces de: Bruno makes the best ice cream in the archipelago, and even in the world. When I grow up I'll be an ice-cream maker like him. He's already let me invent a flavour, so I'm almost an ice-cream maker.
textes.Bruno, le glacier, mon voisin de la rue: Bruno, the ice-cream man, my neighbour on Lighthouse Street. Reliable witness, excellent ice cream. I stop at his kiosk for reasons of duty. The vanilla has nothing to do with it.
textes.Brutus ! Belle journée pour les crocodil: Brutus! Lovely day for crocodiles, isn't it?
textes.Brutus ! Douze ferrures pour jeudi ?: Brutus! Twelve iron fittings by Thursday?
textes.Brutus ! Mes pots sont encore chauds ?: Brutus! Are my pots still warm?
textes.Brutus forge les meilleures lames de l'î: Brutus forges the best blades on the island. He says so, and he proves it by bending iron bars. We both want the crocodile teeth: him to forge, me to resell. We don't agree.
textes.Brutus m'a forgé ce crochet. Il est mieu: Brutus forged me this hook. It's better than my hand: it never sweats at dice.
textes.Brutus m'a forgé ce crochet. Il ne pose: Brutus forged me this hook. He doesn't ask questions. Neither do I. Every afternoon, we watch the fire. He's the best friend I've ever had without ever saying so.
textes.Brutus me forge des aiguilles plus fines: Brutus forges me needles finer than hairs. He doesn't talk, he doesn't move, and his forge is the warmest place on the island. My ink loves it. So do I.
textes.Brutus me forge mes ferrures et mes clou: Brutus forges my ironwork and my copper nails. He doesn't talk, he doesn't make mistakes. When I ask him for four hundred nails, there are four hundred. Not one more. I count.
textes.Brutus parle peu, mais il forge bien. C': Brutus doesn't talk much, but he forges well. He made my ladle, the one that weighs as much as a sabre. And it was his nail I swallowed. A good nail. You don't forget a thing like that.
textes.Brutus veut des dents de crocodile. Il d: Brutus wants crocodile teeth. He says he'll make an iron fist out of them. I say he'll make a necklace for his sweetheart. He hasn't got a sweetheart.
textes.Brutus, le forgeron de Port-Coutelas, me: Brutus, the blacksmith of Port-Coutelas, will forge me an iron fist if I bring him three crocodile teeth from the Drowned Marsh.
textes.Brutus. Forgeron. Je fais les sabres, le: Brutus. Blacksmith. I make sabres, hooks, anchors and shoes for the feet… of horses. There are no horses here. So I make hooks.
textes.Bruyère, sa mère, a dansé pour moi penda: Bruyère, her mother, danced for me for thirty years. The evening her knees said no, she sat down by my moss and said: “Now, watch my daughter.” I watch. Bruyère lives in peace with the does of the deep forest; every season, Lilas brings me a flower from her and a question: “Does she dance well?” Yes.
Piping hot, Mamie. Specially for you.
textes.Bucatini garde la Marmite, en haut ; moi: Bucatini guards the Cooking Pot, up top; I guard the Lid, down below. He thinks his job is more important. He's wrong. But I love him anyway. On Sundays we discuss it. He's still wrong.
textes.Bucatini prend mes tomates pour la Marmi: Bucatini takes my tomatoes for the Cooking Pot. He never says goodbye to them. I tell him off for it. He says sauce is a goodbye that lasts a long time. That's rather lovely, for a man who hardly talks.
textes.Bucatini, il me faut de la sauce de la M: Bucatini, I need some sauce from the Cooking Pot for the sacred Dish.
textes.Bulle a fait construire aux Thermes une: Bulle had a bathtub built at the Baths just for me. It's called “the Gorgoth Bath”. Before, when I got into the water, everyone else got out. Swept out by the wave.
textes.Bulle a fait construire une baignoire ri: Bulle had a bathtub built just for me at the Baths. Before, when I got into the big pool, everybody came out. On the wave. Bulle laughs all the time. Even when I splash him.
textes.Bulle a ouvert les Thermes à côté de mes: Bulle opened the Baths next to my gardens, so old horns like mine could warm up. He still makes me pay. Half price. But every time, he slips into my bath a sulphur rose picked from my own garden. He thinks I don't know where it comes from. I pretend not to know.
textes.Bulle a transformé ma plus belle expérie: Bulle turned my most beautiful failed experiment into a whole district. I wanted to make rain. I made giant bubbles. She solidified them. Everyone lives in them. Nothing is lost.
textes.Bulle est mon frère jumeau. Il est né tr: Bulle is my twin brother. He was born three minutes after me, and he's been laughing ever since. He makes bubbles with everything, even my potions. He wears me out. I'd defend him against the entire volcano.
textes.Bulle m'a construit ma bulle de soins, e: Bulle built me my healing bubble, of very soft glass, with a ceiling full of sky. She says it's my light that heals. I say it's her ceiling. We've been gently arguing about it for a hundred years.
textes.Bulle m'a demandé de dessiner le plan du: Bulle asked me to draw the plan of the Bubble District. I drew a rectangle, with circles inside. She looked at the rectangle, horrified: “Why corners?” I said sheets of paper have corners. The next day, she brought me a round sheet. I had to start all over again. The plan is magnificent.
textes.Bulle m'a demandé de l'aider à calculer: Bulle asked me to help her calculate the perfect curve for a dome. I wrote an equation two metres long. She looked at it, then drew a circle freehand, with her fingertip. It was perfect. She said: “Your equation is very pretty too.” I had it framed.
textes.Bulle m'a fabriqué une porte de bulle qu: Bulle made me a bubble door that only opens if you pull a face. I pull a new one every day: the cross-eyed fish, the cross jellyfish, Écliptique falling over. Mum has to pull a face to get in. Even the Elder pulled one, to come and see us. She pulled the best one. I won't say which.
textes.Bulle s'est tordu la cheville en montant: Bulle twisted her ankle climbing onto one of her domes. I healed her in the bubble she'd built me. She was watching the clouds drift across the ceiling, and she said: “It's your glass that heals.” I answered: “It's your ceiling.” We laughed. Her ankle was better before the argument was over.
textes.Bulle tient les Thermes de Soufre. Il ri: Bulle runs the Sulphur Baths. He laughs all the time, he makes bubbles out of everything, and he claims horns don't breathe. His, perhaps: he barely has any. He keeps a scented towel for me.
textes.Bulle trouve que mes cartes ont trop de: Bulle thinks my maps have too many corners. A map has corners, I tell her. She says it doesn't. I made her a round map of Astralys. She hung it on the ceiling of her bubble.
Bulle is my son. My little soap bubble. He's been laughing since day one, he makes bubbles out of anything, and he runs the Baths right next to my gardens. He makes me pay for my bath. Half price. He's a good son.
textes.Bulle, j'ai une nouvelle expérience raté: Bulle, I have a new failed experiment.
textes.Bulle, mon petit savon ! Un bain pour ta: Bulle, my little soap bubble! A bath for your old mother?
textes.Bulle, votre nouveau dôme est sur ma car: Bulle, your new dome is on my map.
textes.Bulle. Tu as encore utilisé mes sels de: Bulle. You used my bath salts to make foam again.
textes.Bulletin culturel : Pigment a peint cett: Culture bulletin: last night Pigment painted a six-metre rat on the door of the Lisse & Sons Sales Office. The rat is smiling. Mister Lisse, much less so.
textes.Bulletin de midi : vent d'ouest, ciel bl: Midday report: westerly wind, blue sky, and a rabbit-shaped cloud. I've noted it down.
textes.Bulle… le Bain Gorgoth est libre ?: Bulle… is the Gorgoth Bath free?
textes.Bzzt ! Dis-moi : tu as peur du noir, toi: Bzzt! Tell me: are you afraid of the dark?
textes.Bzzt ! Salut ! Fusible, électricien. Les: Bzzt! Hi! Fusible, electrician. The fairy lights, the lamps, the spotlights at the Hall, the radio, the blinking fountain: it all goes through me. Don't touch that wire. Or that one. Or me, for that matter, I might still be charged.
textes.Bzzt. Elle t'envoie. Évidemment. (Il sou: Bzzt. She sent you. Of course. (He sighs and shows his tablet: a zigzagging curve.) Right. The Heart lost three shards last night. One fell near the Observatory, one in the Species Greenhouse, among the gurgles, and the third… somewhere up high, in the Zero-Gravity Garden: up there, it'll never fall back by itself. Bring them to me. With three astral crystals, I can weld them back together. Then they'll have to be put back in the Heart. At the very top. A hundred and ten metres. It's nothing. Well, it's something.
textes.Bzzt. Le Cœur est content. Les compteurs: Bzzt. The Heart is happy. The meters are dancing too.
Bzzt. Sorry. That was a test bolt.
textes.Bzzt. Quoi ? Un Pied-Lourd. Bon. Volt. J: Bzzt. What? A Heavy-Foot. Right. Volt. I look after the Spire's energy. Don't touch anything. Especially not that. Or that. Or… right, take a step back. There. Hello.
textes.Bzzzt ! Nouvelles couleurs pour les carp: Bzzzt! New colors for the carp.
textes.Bzzzz ! Le petit drone accélère, frôle l: Bzzzz! The little drone speeds up, skims the ceiling light, beep-beep, and goes back to its quiet rounds. It thought it was in a hurry.
textes.Bzzzzt. … Je vais bien. Mes cheveux, un: Bzzzzt. … I'm fine. My hair, less so.
textes.Bzzz… Dis-moi, {surnom}, tu as déjà été: Bzzz… Tell me, {surnom}, have you ever been stung by a bee?
textes.Bzzz… Je vais bien. Mes cheveux, un peu: Bzzz… I'm fine. My hair, a little less.
textes.Bzzz… Veuillez soulever les pieds. Merci: Bzzz… Please lift your feet. Thank you. BEEP.
textes.Bébé, Nina dormait dans un panier à pain: As a baby, Nina slept in a bread basket by the oven. One morning, a customer wanted to buy “that big brioche in the basket there”. The brioche opened its eyes and sneezed. He got such a fright he took two baguettes and left without his change. Nina gave her first smile that day. I think she did it on purpose.
textes.Bébé, j'ai crié si fort à ma naissance q: As a baby, I screamed so loud when I was born that the midwife thought it was an alert. The whole street came out with buckets. My mother said: “That one will be a crier.” She was right. We kept the buckets.
textes.Bénédiction ! Vous brillez un peu ! C'es: Blessing! You're glowing a bit! That's normal! Go!
textes.Bénédiction de l'Aube ! Frappe, maintena: Blessing of the Dawn! Strike now, strike!
textes.Bénédiction de l'Aube ! Je l'ai bien dit: Blessing of Dawn! I said it right this time, without stammering!
textes.C'EST LE GRAND BOUCAN ! La Halle est ple: IT'S THE GREAT BOUCAN! The Hall is packed to the rafters: Paulo and his cooking pot, Ulric and his frogs, Tom the Fiddler on a barrel… Rouille points at the pit: “You! In the pit! NOW!”
textes.C'EST TON REFRAIN QUI EST SUR MON CRI !: IT'S YOUR CHORUS THAT'S ON TOP OF MY SHOUTING!
textes.C'EST TROP FORT ! … PAS ASSEZ !: IT'S TOO LOUD! … NOT LOUD ENOUGH!
textes.C'EST VRAI ?! Avec des pièces d'or ? Et: REALLY?! With gold coins? And a map? And a skeleton? Tell me! No, wait, I'll go get Tibo. No, tell me first!
MINE! Oh no, it's a pebble.
textes.C'est Amine. Il a mangé deux oiseaux de: It's Amine. He ate two seabirds.
textes.C'est Gaubert qui m'a appris que Babette: It was Gaubert who told me that Babette had carried sacks of seed to the farm the winter he was ill. He'd found a trace of apple on one of the sacks. He said to me: “Don't tell anyone. Especially not Germaine.” I haven't told anyone. I keep the secret with him. We keep it well. We're two big quiet ones.
textes.C'est Gland qui a caché les noisettes da: It was Gland who hid the hazelnuts in Mum's sardine crates. “To keep cool!” he said. Mum screamed. Afterwards, he came to say sorry with a hazelnut. Just one. And he took it back when he left! Mrrrou! He does the same with Grandad Tilleul, I've seen him.
textes.C'est Grand-père Ébène qui m'a raconté l: It was Grandpa Ébène who told me the old story of Cerbère, the three-headed dog of the Nine Circles: you need a honey cake for each head, otherwise they squabble. I wrote the recipe on a flour sack. Since then, I make “three-headed” honey cakes. You never know who'll need them.
It's Jupiter in the fountain, Ionie.
textes.C'est MOI qui l'ai fait !: I'M the one who made it!
textes.C'est Nina qui m'a montré la fontaine. E: Nina showed me the fountain. She said: “You close your eyes, turn round three times, throw the coin.” I turned six times, to be sure, and I fell in the water. Nina laughed. Then she said the wish counted double, because I was wet. I don't know if it's true. She makes stuff up sometimes.
textes.C'est Pierrick qui a raconté partout que: It was Pierrick who told everyone I'd climbed up to the main top. I sulked at him for a week. Then he brought me an ice cream from Cliquetis, come over on the Zéphyr, all melted, in a cup. He said he'd bought two. I think he bought one, and it was his.
textes.C'est Rosalie, à la poissonnerie, qui m': It was Rosalie, at the fish shop, who informed me that I “didn't want to see Hugo again until he'd found the ring”. In front of everyone, a sardine in her hand. I'd only said it once, in my room, with the door shut. But Pauline was making the bed next door.
textes.C'est Sardine ! Mon chien ! Il est parti: It's Sardine! My dog! He ran off this morning after a Lisse robot. He's always chasing robots, he thinks they're giant boxes of kibble! He has a red bandana, one ear up, one ear down, and he smells a bit like fish. I've looked all over town. Chaussette says her dogs picked up his scent toward the Scrapyard. But Mum won't let me go to the Scrapyard alone. Would you go? Please? His name is Sardine. He comes when you whistle. Well, when he feels like it.
textes.C'est TOUJOURS une île avec du vent, qua: It's ALWAYS an island with wind when you're around!
textes.C'est Tlaloc qui te regarde, ami ! Il t': That's Tlaloc looking at you, friend! He likes you.
textes.C'est Triton qui m'a dit que la reine av: It was Triton who told me the queen was a thousand years old. He made me swear not to repeat it. I swore. Then I told Mum, Dad, Coralin and you. But nobody else! Don't tell Triton, OK? He's very nice when he isn't cross.
textes.C'est Yaya qui m'a amenée, il y a deux a: Yaya brought me, two years ago. She saw me dancing behind the counter while giving change, and said: “Tonight, village beach.” I took the Swallow, heard the kick drum from the deck, and I just knew. That night I knocked over two glasses and a Bastien. He forgave me straight away. Too fast, even.
textes.C'est bien aussi. Les humains, ça fait d: That's good too. Humans give warmer hugs. Except Papa on the left.
That's just what I saw too.
textes.C'est bien pour ça qu'il faut que quelqu: Which is exactly why someone has to tell the story.
That's exactly why I say it.
textes.C'est bien, de chercher. Moi, j'ai trouv: Searching is good. I found mine by chance, following the sound of a bassline. Listen carefully to sounds. The right place always goes a little boom.
textes.C'est bien. Les meilleurs lapins se perd: Good. The best rabbits get a bit lost.
textes.C'est calme. J'aimerais lire ici. Si ce: It's calm. I'd like to read here. If it weren't full of mouths.
textes.C'est ce qu'il avait fait la dernière fo: That's what he did last time.
textes.C'est ce que disait ta carte. Juste avan: That's what your map said. Right before the rock.
That's what I said: my favourite tongs.
textes.C'est ce que je me dis aussi. Pour ne pa: That's what I tell myself too. So I don't get my hopes up.
That's what you say every time.
textes.C'est ce que tu disais à quarante ans, a: That's what you said at forty, with your ankle on backwards.
textes.C'est ce que vous aviez dit pour la soup: That is what you said about the soup.
textes.C'est comment, la vie au camp ?: What's life like at the camp?
textes.C'est de l'eau qui a grandi dans un arbr: It's water that grew up in a tree. The best kind.
textes.C'est de la poésie ! La poésie, ça grand: It's poetry! Poetry makes people bigger.
textes.C'est derrière les caisses de Lucas que: It was behind Lucas's crates that I found Brioche, curled up in a ball. Lucas had seen him before me, but he hadn't said anything. He made him a bed in a crate with an old blanket, and he wrote BRIOCHE on it, like on the other crates. Lucas gives names to all his crates. I don't know them all. Yet.
textes.C'est donc ça, cet air si léger !: So that's why you look so light on your feet!
textes.C'est doux et frais. Ça sent la menthe,: It's soft and cool. It smells of mint, basil and… strawberry? A strawberry runner has crept into the wall. Nobody knows how.
textes.C'est déjà beaucoup. Je vous en garde un: That's already a lot. I'll keep one for you.
textes.C'est déjà ça. Le soleil, au moins, ça n: That's something. The sun, at least, doesn't need grilling.
textes.C'est elle ! C'est elle ! Hugo ! HUGO !: It's her! It's her! Hugo! HUGO! … Thank you. You've given us back our honeymoon. What you're feeling right now, deep in your heart? That's happiness. Keep it.
textes.C'est elle qui a trouvé les traces ronde: She's the one who found the round tracks. Like stone footprints, going into the big pond and never coming out. She said: “That's not a fish.” I said: “The King has feet when he wants.” She looked at me. I looked at her. Neither of us laughed. Just as well. You never know.
textes.C'est elle qui me donne l'heure de la si: She's the one who tells me when it's nap time. At one o'clock sharp, she claps her hands twice: “Nap time, young man.” She has no watch and never looks up at the clock. She has the time in her foot. I put my guitar away. Nobody else makes me obey like that.
textes.C'est exactement ce que dirait un héros: That's exactly what a modest hero would say.
textes.C'est fait pour ! Et tes clous sont trop: That's what they're for! And your nails are too big!
textes.C'est fini ! Je l'ai poussé dans la corb: It's over! I pushed it into the trash, and emptied the trash. Come see me, I have a few words to say to Mister Fil…
textes.C'est fini ! Les robots sont partis ! To: It's over! The robots are gone! Everyone can let go of each other's arms! … No, Mamie, you can let go of the robot too.
textes.C'est fini ? Je peux ouvrir les yeux ? …: Is it over? Can I open my eyes? … Oh! Well done!
textes.C'est fini. Mes cheveux se recouchent. C: It's over. My hair is lying back down. That's always how I know it's over.
textes.C'est fort aimable. Je le rangerai à l'o: Most kind. I'll put it away in the pantry, in its proper place. Everything has a place.
textes.C'est gentil ! On le lui dira. Tiens, pr: How kind! We'll tell him. Here, have a slice of cake, we made far too much.
textes.C'est gentil. Chez nous, un cadeau appel: That's kind. Here, a gift calls for a gift. I'll remember it.
textes.C'est ici que Titouan m'a suivi en cache: This is where Titouan secretly followed me. He saw me fall on a goblin. I told him it was a technique.
textes.C'est ici que la Duchesse m'a pris mon c: This is where the Duchess took my rosary. I recognise her. She's looking at me.
textes.C'est juste ce qu'il faut. Ici, il n'y a: That's just right. Here, there's no right price. There's only good soup.
textes.C'est justement ÇA qui est drôle ! HA HA: That's exactly what's FUNNY! HA HA HA!
textes.C'est l'estrade qui a soif, et c'est moi: The stage is thirsty, and I'm the one drinking?
textes.C'est l'heure ! Mes sabots ne tiennent p: It's time! My hooves can't keep still.
textes.C'est l'heure de manger. Mon ventre me l: It's time to eat. My tummy keeps reminding me.
textes.C'est l'heure où je lis sur le banc de l: This is when I usually read on the bench in the Upper Town. But tonight, it's adventure.
This is when everyone gets busy. I like that sound.
It's the smell. It's very well documented.
textes.C'est l'ordre de ceux que j'aime bien !: It's the order of the people I like!
textes.C'est la bonne réponse. Les gens trop sû: That's the right answer. People who are too sure of themselves don't look long enough. You doubt. A good lookout doubts.
textes.C'est la fraîcheur, Majesté. Royalement: That's the freshness, Majesty. Royally fresh.
textes.C'est la grand-mère de Brunehaut qui a c: It was Brunehaut's grandmother who built Bernadette. And it was Brunehaut who forged the rivets of the spare boiler. My locomotive is a bit of an Enclume. That explains why she's so stubborn.
That's the day coming out, Berthe.
That was the sea. And you're a baby.
textes.C'est la mouette, Ionie ! Elle a triché: It was the seagull, Ionie! It cheated!
textes.C'est la musique, chère Calcine. Elle me: It's the music, dear Calcine. It ruffles my heart's hair.
textes.C'est la plus belle des raisons. Les mèr: That's the finest reason of all. Mothers keep the flowers pressed in a book, you know. All of them. For years.
textes.C'est la première fois que je monte. Mes: It's my first time going up. My knees are already shaking.
textes.C'est la reine qui m'a dit que j'avais p: It was the queen who told me I didn't need to glow, that I could make others glow. The next day, she put me in charge of the fireflies! Now, in the evenings, I send them to draw paths in the air for the fairies who come home late. Arrows, spirals, hearts. Once, a mushroom. That wasn't on purpose.
textes.C'est la réponse la plus honnête qu'on m: That's the most honest answer anyone has given me in a thousand years. Don't worry: you never live a thousand years all at once. You live them one day at a time.
That's the most honest answer anyone's ever given me. Hilaire does the same. I keep a copy of his lists. I'll keep yours too.
textes.C'est la seule pièce au monde qui se ter: It's the only piece in the world that ends with a sneeze. The wind's, usually. Once, it was the audience's: we kept that version.
textes.C'est le Capitaine qui nous a mariés, Mo: It was the Captain who married us, Moloka and me, on his quay. He gave an hour-long speech about the sea and sardines. I cried so hard I got the framed sardine wet. Since then, on our anniversary, I stand him his punch, and he tells the story of our own wedding. He adds waves to that one too.
textes.C'est le Roi ! Il a une couronne !: It's the King! He's got a crown!
textes.C'est le chocolat qui porte chance. Le b: It's the chocolate that brings luck. The balcony does what it can.
It's the sky, Zineb. It runs.
textes.C'est le même que l'autre, non ?: That's the same as the other one, isn't it?
It's the same one. At least he's polite.
It's the same one. He's greeting twice.
textes.C'est le plateau, Maman ! Il est plein d: It's the plateau, Mum! It's full of pebbles!
textes.C'est le poids de mes victoires, Lestran: That's the weight of my victories, Lestrange.
textes.C'est le principe d'un navet !: That's the whole point of a turnip!
textes.C'est le seul de la Balafre que j'appell: He's the only one on Balafre I call by his real first name: Sébastien. One evening, I said it without thinking, and he stopped whistling. He looked at me as if I'd given him his teeth back. Since then, it's our secret. On the port, he's Sans-Dents. In my shop, he's Sébastien. He stands up straighter there.
textes.C'est le seul sort que je rate qu'à moit: It's the only spell I only half mess up.
textes.C'est le soleil, prêtresse. Moi, je ne f: That's the sun, priestess. I only make white.
It's the tone, Églantine. The tone.
textes.C'est le troisième, Corentin. Je sais co: That's the third, Corentin. I can count.
textes.C'est leur façon de dire merci !: That's their way of saying thank you!
That's their way of growing, I suppose.
textes.C'est lui qui a eu l'idée du tableau des: He's the one who had the idea for the bruisers' board. I lent him a plank and a piece of chalk, and hung it above my bottles. Since then, brawls are more polite: people fight to get on the board, not to break my chairs. Well, they still break chairs. But with a purpose.
textes.C'est lui qui a fait ma grande jarre à b: He's the one who made my big beer jar. I told him it leaned a little to the left. He came back with a plumb line, measured three times, and said: “The jar is straight. You're the one who leans.” I laughed so hard I spilled a ladle of beer on his sandals. He sulked. He came back that very evening.
textes.C'est lui qui a écrit nos trois noms au: He's the one who wrote our three names on the bruisers' board, in chalk: me, the Silent One, Belle-Humeur. Mine is first. Belle-Humeur says it's because it's the shortest. Gros-Louis isn't short! It's wide.
textes.C'est lui qui m'a raconté que ma grand-m: He's the one who told me that, when he was young, my grandmother traded him the story of the walking dune for a djinn tale. He says it was a fair trade. I say he got a bargain. My grandmother never told anything for nothing. She must have had a reason. He won't tell me which.
textes.C'est ma bière qui fait passer ton ragoû: It's my fizz that washes your stew down, Dagna!
textes.C'est ma grand-mère qui m'a élevé. Elle: My grandmother raised me. She had a hand-cranked ice-cream churn, a bucket of crushed ice and arms like hams. I turned the crank, she sang. Her coconut ice cream was for Sundays. I'd lick the wooden spoon till it went white. I still have the recipe. Well… we'll come back to that.
textes.C'est ma mère qui a mis une bolée dans l: It was my mother who put a mug in Corentin's hand, the night his grandfather died, saying: “You tell it.” I was fifteen, drying glasses. He told the story of the shipwreck in a trembling voice. At the end, nobody clapped. We topped everyone up. Here, that's what we do when something's beautiful.
textes.C'est moi qui ai acheté son tout premier: I'm the one who bought her very first bottle, at the Cousins' Festival. It was wonky, it leaked a bit, and the nectar was the best I'd ever tasted. I said “more”. She doubled the price. It was the start of a long friendship. And of a long debt.
textes.C'est moi qui ai appris le métier à Ysaé: I'm the one who taught Ysaé the trade. She was eight. She came to the Swap Shop every day, sat on the till, and watched my hands. One day she took my pliers and made a ring. First try. I knew she'd go further than me. Higher, even.
textes.C'est moi qui ai cueilli la menthe !: I'm the one who picked the mint!
textes.C'est moi qui ai dit à Théo que la fonta: I'm the one who told Théo the fountain grants wishes. I taught him how: you close your eyes, you spin round three times, you throw the coin. He spun six times and fell into the fountain. OK, he got wet, but the wish still counts. Double, even, I think.
textes.C'est moi qui ai dit à l'Amirale qu'Ewen: I'm the one who told the Admiral that Ewen had climbed the main top. He sulked at me for a week. So I brought him an ice cream from Cliquetis, come over on the Zéphyr, melted in a cup. I said I'd bought two. It was mine. He drank it in one gulp. The next day, there was a bowline on my apron.
textes.C'est moi qui ai eu l'idée des jardinièr: The window boxes under the windows were my idea. Red at the Buvards', yellow at the Pinceaus', blue at the Council. The village looked like a bouquet perched in the trees. Today, it's a bridal bouquet.
textes.C'est moi qui ai eu l'idée du tableau de: The brawlers' board was my idea. I asked Mama for a plank and some chalk. She said: “If it stops them breaking my chairs, I'll give you ten.” It doesn't stop anything. But the brawls have a purpose now: getting onto the board. Mama says her broken chairs have ambition.
textes.C'est moi qui ai eu l'idée. Ne le répète: It was my idea. Don't tell anyone.
textes.C'est moi qui ai lancé l'histoire du che: I'm the one who started the horse story. Tonneau can't see his back, so he asked me what Coralie had tattooed on him. I looked at the octopus and said: “A magnificent horse.” He was so happy he bought a round for the whole Crâne Fendu. Coralie never forgave me. One more reason.
textes.C'est moi qui ai trouvé les traces ronde: I'm the one who found the round tracks, at the edge of the big pond. Like stone footsteps, going into the water and never coming out. I said to Moustache: “That's not a fish.” He smoothed his whiskers: “The King has feet when he wants to.” I didn't know what to say. That rarely happens to me.
textes.C'est moi qui paie les glaces. (Elle cro: I'm paying for the ice creams. (She crosses her arms, pouts… then bursts out laughing.) You beat me! Nobody has ever beaten me! Except a seagull, once, but the seagull cheated, it caught the wind. You know what? It's the best race of my life. Here: two cosmic jellies, which are rarer than ice cream, and a few washers for the ice cream anyway. And a rematch tomorrow! And the day after! For life!
I'm the one who knits, child.
textes.C'est moi, ma puce. Mais dis-le plus for: Me, sweetie. But say it louder, Marcel's hard of hearing.
It's my heart that can't count.
textes.C'est mon hypothèse numéro un ! Ils boiv: That's my hypothesis number one! They drink in the Brass Sun and give it back at night. You have a scientific mind. And a lovely sense of poetry. The two go together, whatever people say.
textes.C'est mon nuage ! Il s'appelle Flocon. L: This is my cloud! His name's Flocon. Doctor Aurèle says he's a cumulus. I say he's a Flocon.
This is my cloud! His name's Guimauve. Doctor Aurèle says he's a cumulus. I say he's a Guimauve.
textes.C'est mon nuage ! Il s'appelle Pompon. L: This is my cloud! His name's Pompon. Doctor Aurèle says he's a cumulus. I say he's a Pompon.
textes.C'est mon pas, ça, brigadier !: This is my walking pace, Sergeant!
textes.C'est normal. Laisse passer les pensées: That's normal. Let your thoughts drift by like clouds. One day, only the sky will remain.
textes.C'est notre canapé ! Copeau l'a fait ave: That's our sofa! Copeau made it out of pallets and love!
Written down. With my cap on straight.
That's a yes, then. I'll bring the bread.
textes.C'est parce que tu ressembles à un jagua: That's because you look like a jaguar!
textes.C'est parti ! Garde-les à l'œil… tous le: Here we go! Keep an eye on them… all four.
textes.C'est pas des boulons, c'est ma collecti: They're not bolts, they're my collection!
They're not bolts, they're my collection, Mum!
textes.C'est pas juste ! Comment tu fais ?: That's not fair! How do you do it?
textes.C'est pas moi ! Je le jure sur ma sacoch: Wasn't me! I swear on my mailbag!
textes.C'est pas moi, la lavande !: It's not me with the lavender!
It's not my thyme. It's my boot.
It's not the same. But it's good.
textes.C'est pour l'humain ! Tu lui donneras ?: It's for the human! Will you give it to them? Please!
That's to hear the sharks better.
textes.C'est pour tes pierres ! J'ai une nouvel: It's about your stones! I've got a new theory, listen…
textes.C'est pour ça qu'elle marche. Tiens-toi: That's why it works. Stand up straight, and drink your tea.
textes.C'est pour ça que tu m'aimes, Aïcha. Ma: That's why you love me, Aïcha. Ma doue!
textes.C'est presque la même chose. Zzz…: It's almost the same thing. Zzz…
That's almost a yes. Good, good.
textes.C'est prêt dans cinq minutes, Tempo !: It'll be ready in five minutes, Tempo!
textes.C'est qu'il est content de te voir, Brun: That's because it's happy to see you, Brunna.
textes.C'est qu'il t'aime bien. Il ne mord que: That means it likes you. It only bites people it likes.
That's because I have a good teacher.
textes.C'est que les deux vont ensemble, ma bel: That's because the two go together, my lovely.
textes.C'est que tu as soulevé trop vite !: That's because you lifted too fast!
textes.C'est quoi ? C'est quoi ?: What is it? What is it?
textes.C'est quoi le comble pour un boulanger ?: Why did the baker stop making bread? Because he couldn't make enough dough! Hee hee!
textes.C'est quoi, sous la mare, d'après toi ?: What do you think is under the pond?
textes.C'est quoi, une pomme ? Coralin dit que: What's an apple? Coralin says it's a red sea urchin that grows on trees.
textes.C'est quoi, votre programme exceptionnel: So what's this exceptional programme of yours?
textes.C'est rien, je suis tombé avec élégance: It's nothing, I fell with elegance!
It's secret. Even from the club.
textes.C'est toi ! L'oreilles-toutes-petites !: It's you! Teeny-Ears! Will you play?
textes.C'est toi ! Mon ami l'humain sans cornes: It's you! My hornless human friend! Look, I learned to make a flame! … Okay, it's a small flame. A spark. But it's mine!
textes.C'est toi ! Tu joues avec moi ?: It's you! Will you play with me?
Is that you? I recognise your footsteps.
textes.C'est toi le pilote ! Tiens bon !: You're the pilot! Hold on tight!
textes.C'est toi qui as abattu les golems ? Bie: Was it you who brought down the golems? Welcome to Forgefer, friend!
textes.C'est toi qui as échoué la Morue sur le: Was it you who ran the Cod aground on the reef?
textes.C'est toi qui fais pschhh, là, non ?: That's you going pschhh, isn't it?
textes.C'est toi. En carré. Ocre a mis du jaune: It's you. All square. Ocre has put yellow around your head: “You shine, because you smooth.” The little stick figures around it raise their arms. They look very impressed.
It's your knife that fills it.
It's always Pétard. Pétard gets the blame for everything.
textes.C'est toujours la cymbale quand j'arrive: It's always the cymbal when I arrive.
An idea is all that matters.
That's the whole point, my Tic.
textes.C'est trop ! … Non, ce n'est jamais trop: That's too much! … No, it's never too much. I'll put it in the common pot. It says thank you.
textes.C'est très bien. Un bobo qu'on montre, c: That's very good. A boo-boo you show is a boo-boo that gets treated. The “didn't even hurt” ones, I find them three days later, all swollen.
textes.C'est très silencieux. Sauf le « gloup »: It's very quiet. Except for the “gloop”. I don't like the “gloop”.
It's a code. A secret one.
textes.C'est un début. Je jongle avec ta patien: It's a start. I'm juggling with your patience.
textes.C'est un escargot sur le dos d'une tortu: It's a snail on a turtle's back. What does it shout?
textes.C'est un manche. Avec un tout petit peu: That's a handle. With a tiny bit of iron on the end.
textes.C'est un maquereau, Capitaine. Il vous f: It's a mackerel, Captain. You need your glasses.
textes.C'est un poulpe, Tonneau. Un poulpe n'a: It's an octopus, Tonneau. An octopus doesn't have a saddle.
textes.C'est un secret, d'accord ? Juré-craché: It's a secret, okay? Cross your heart? I've got a bow. A real one! I made it all by myself, from a branch that fell off the Mother Tree, like Thalion's. I practise at night, behind the fountain, on a pumpkin. I hit it one time in three! At the Dawn Festival I'll show Thalion. Don't tell Mummy.
It's a secret. And it isn't you.
textes.C'est un secret. Pourquoi tu chantes ?: It's a secret. Why are you singing?
textes.C'est une nouvelle potion, Monsieur Gust: It's a new potion, Monsieur Gustave!
textes.C'est une recette terrestre ! Enfin, pre: It's an Earth recipe! Well, almost.
textes.C'est une valse, Lola. Ça se joue lentem: It's a waltz, Lola. You play it slowly.
It's an old story, my little flower.
textes.C'est voulu, Rodrigue. Une cape de héros: That's on purpose, Rodrigue. A hero's cape never sleeps.
textes.C'est vous qui allez tomber, Sire Tancrè: You're the one who's going to fall, Sire Tancrède! … There. Let me heal you.
textes.C'est vrai ! Elles sont trop rapides ! U: That's true! They're too fast! Once, a seagull stole a chip RIGHT OUT OF MY MOUTH. I laughed for an hour.
textes.C'est vrai ? Combien de tours ? Moi c'es: Really? How many towers? Mine's got four. The secret is wet sand, but not too wet, or it runs. And you have to pat it with your flat hand. Like this.
textes.C'est vrai ? Comme moi ! On pourrait res: Really? Like me! We could both stay! You'd do… I dunno, something. And I'd fish. Shh, don't tell the captain.
textes.C'est vrai ? Oh, merci ! Enfin, pas merc: Really? Oh, thank you! Well, not thank you for being scared. Thank you for saying so. We can close our eyes together. Taking turns.
textes.C'est vrai ? Tu le crois vraiment ? Je v: Really? You really think so? I'm going to tell Oscar! And Gérard! And everyone!
textes.C'est vrai ? Tu veux bien ? Il s'appelle: Really? You'll do it? His name is Miou. He's ginger, with a twisted ear, like this. (She twists her ear.) Khety says cats like to go to the dead, on the plateau, near the square tombs. But Mama doesn't want me to go there all alone. Will you bring him back? Promise?
textes.C'est vrai ? Viens là ! Enfin quelqu'un: Really? Come here! Finally someone! Was it big? Did it blow? No, don't answer: I believe you. You, I believe.
textes.C'est vrai ?! (Il te serre la main, très: Really?! (He shakes your hand, very hard.) At last, someone who understands me. We'll fish together. You watch the left, I'll watch the right.
textes.C'est vrai ?! Il était comment ? Il saut: Really?! What was it like? Did it jump high? Higher than mine? No, wait, don't tell me. Mine jumped really high. So we're the same.
textes.C'est vrai ?! Oh, je suis trop contente: Really?! Oh, I'm so happy! Well, not happy that you're scared: happy that I'm not all alone. Here, I'll lend you a firefly. In my thoughts.
textes.C'est vrai ?! Personne ne m'avait jamais: Really?! Nobody ever told me that! Here, keep a page of my score. It'll be worth a fortune when I'm famous.
textes.C'est vrai ?! Raconte ! Ça a fumé ? Ça a: Really?! Tell me! Was there smoke? Was it loud? Did someone come running? You're my hero now. Well, my third hero. After Professor Boum and Achille.
textes.C'est vrai ?! Un collègue ! Nous pourrio: Really?! A colleague! We could have a contest, like with Father Clotaire. But we'd fall asleep before the end.
textes.C'est vrai qu'un requin t'a fait cette b: Is it true a shark gave you that scar?
textes.C'est vrai que ta soupe a rendu malade t: Is it true your soup made the whole crew sick?
textes.C'est vrai que vous avez acheté de nouve: Is it true you've bought new curtains?
textes.C'est vrai. Tu es venu par la mer. Alors: That's true. You came by sea. So you know. Does it hurt, leaving? No, don't answer. I'll find out.
textes.C'est {prix} pièces, et tu en as {pieces: It's {prix} coins, and you have {pieces}. Come back later, no worries.
It's {prix} coins, and you have {pieces}. Come back later, I'll keep it warm for you.
It's {prix} coins, and you have {pieces}. Come back later, I'll keep it for you.
It's {prix} coins, and you've got {pieces}. Come back later.
textes.C'est {prix} pièces, et tu n'en as que {: That's {prix} coins, and you only have {pieces}… Even in hell, we don't give credit. Come back later.
That's {prix} coins, and you only have {pieces}… Even the cabin can't go up without a counterweight.
That's {prix} coins, and you've only got {pieces}… Even a cloud can't float without a little air.
That's {prix} coins, and you've only got {pieces}… Even a mine cart won't roll unless someone pushes it.
That's {prix} coins, and you've only got {pieces}… Even a bubble can't rise without a little air.
That's {prix} coins, and you've only got {pieces}… Go and check the Guild board: there are always slimes to hunt.
That's {prix} coins, and you've only got {pieces}… Go and eat at the Free Canteen: at Granny Gamelle's, you pay what you can. Even zero.
It's {prix} coins, and you've only got {pieces}… Go and eat at Lentille's Canteen: there, you pay what you can.
textes.C'est {prix} pièces… et tu n'en as que {: That's {prix} coins… and you've only got {pieces}. Come back later.
textes.C'est à Clémence que j'ai dit que mon ce: I told Clémence my kite fell into a pine tree, near the lookout. I saw it! Well, I think so. She said “Poor thing”, about the kite. After, I watched her paint the lighthouse for a whole morning. She only did the top. I told her “You don't paint fast.” She laughed so hard she made a splodge.
textes.C'est ça qu'on appelle regarder. Tu vois: That's what we call looking. See, it's easy.
textes.C'est ça, bon vent. Et ne faites pas tro: That's right, fair winds. And don't make too much noise in the Station. … Do come back, though.
textes.C'est ça, file. Et ne reviens pas me che: That's it, off you go. And don't come looking for me again.
textes.C'est ça, file. Les coquillages, eux, ne: That's it, run off. Seashells, at least, never leave.
textes.C'est ça, le métier. Ne rien voir, et tr: That's the job. Seeing nothing, and seeing it very well.
textes.C'est ça. Attention à la troisième march: Right. Mind the third rung of the ladder, it creaks.
textes.C'est-à-dire que… si je te le vends, je: The thing is… if I sell it to you, I won't have it anymore. See the problem?
textes.C'est… c'est vrai ? Tu ne manges pas les: Is… is that true? You don't eat little demons? … Phew! Here, it's my favorite brioche. You can have it. But just one!
textes.C'est… gentil. Je vais le poser là, à cô: That's… nice. I'll put it there, next to the other thing I don't know how to use.
It's… the sun. It's really strong in the evening.
textes.C'étaient des cercles. Exprès. Fffiou !: They were loops. On purpose. Fffwoosh!
textes.C'étaient des sels de soin. Ils coûtent: Those were healing salts. They're expensive.
textes.C'était LA BRUME ! Et le récif n'était s: It was THE FOG! And the reef wasn't on any map! And Ignace told me “straight ahead”! OK, maybe I dozed off a bit. But that's none of your business!
textes.C'était PAS la soupe ! C'était le poisso: It was NOT the soup! It was the fish! Well, the fish IN the soup! … What are you after, eh? Want a taste of my ladle?
textes.C'était en 1987. Il faisait une chaleur: It was 1987. It was as hot as an oven. I was harvesting alone. I looked up to wipe my brow, and there it was, above the field, still tiny, the size of a plate. It looked at me. And it winked. With its left eye. Then it went off behind the volcano. The next day, it was above the temple, as big as a house.
textes.C'était l'hiver de la faim, à Carène. Ch: It was the hungry winter, in Carène. At his grandfather Yann-le-Borgne's house, there was nothing left to sell but the Léviathan's logbook. We took it for semolina and dates. Under the table, a little boy was crying silently. I slipped under there and told him the tale of the sultan, the sardine and the djinn. At the end, he asked: “And then what?” That was Corentin.
That was the low tide. It's slow.
textes.C'était la lune dessus. Mais c'est un si: It was the moon shining on it. But it's a sign anyway.
textes.C'était pour le dernier accord, Grisette: It was for the last chord, Grisette!
textes.C'était sa première semaine à Tazira. Je: It was his first week in Tazira. I serve him a glass, I pour from high, the foam rises, the whole terrace watches. He tastes, smacks his lips, and says, very loudly: “Not salty enough!” Silence. Moulay Brahim dropped his piece. I didn't answer. I still think about it at night.
textes.C'était toi, la batterie, hier soir ?: Was that you on drums last night?
textes.C'était un soir à la Bielle. Je me plaig: It was one evening at the Bielle. I was complaining about turning my pages. Philibert took a napkin, scribbled a little spring arm and said: “It probably exists already.” It didn't. I kept the napkin, coffee stain and all, and screwed a plaque onto the piano. He came to reread it eleven times the first week.
That was a test. You passed it.
textes.C'était une couronne de profil !: It was a crown from the side!
It was a story about a fox.
textes.C'était une idée de reine. Elles se perd: It was a queen's idea. They often get lost.
textes.C'était une nuit très claire. À l'ouest,: It was a very clear night. To the west, above the clouds, there was an island. A real one, with trees, resting on nothing. I drew it until dawn. At the Academy, they laughed. Politely, then less politely. Nobody believed me. The drawing is pinned above my bed. I look at it before I sleep, to be sure I didn't dream it.
It was written in the feathers.
textes.C'était… une feinte. Une feinte très ava: That was… a feint. A very advanced feint.
textes.CAMAZOTZ, LA CHAUVE-SOURIS DE LA MORT !: CAMAZOTZ, THE BAT OF DEATH! He cut off Hunahpu's head, says the Popol Vuh. Dodge his dives, strike when he lands.
textes.CERBÈRE ! Trois têtes, trois gueules de: CERBÈRE! Three heads, three mouths of fire. They say he can't resist honey cakes… one per head.
textes.CIPACTLI, LE MONSTRE DE LA TERRE ! Les d: CIPACTLI, THE EARTH MONSTER! The gods made the world from its body. It dives and resurfaces: keep moving, strike when it lunges.
textes.CLONK ! « RANGEMENT AUTOMATIQUE EN COURS: CLONK! “AUTOMATIC TIDYING IN PROGRESS.” Claws descend from the ceiling and put every crate back in its place, very politely.
textes.CRAAAC ! Le rocher se fracasse contre le: CRAAACK! The boulder smashes against the stone threshold, into a thousand pebbles. (A thousand steps, a thousand pebbles: it's home.)
textes.CRAC ! Le mur s'ouvre. De l'autre côté :: CRACK! The wall opens. On the other side: a kitchen, a pie… and a dwarf woman with her rolling pin raised.
textes.CRISTALLUNE — toute en cristal. Quand le: CRYSTALMOON — made entirely of crystal. When the wind blows, it sings. Vibrato finds it a little off-key in the high notes.
Cacao! Tortillas! Come closer! Ix Chab. My cacao is whipped to a froth, with chilli and vanilla. The gods drink it. So do the merchants, but they pay.
textes.Cache-cache ! Toi compter jusqu'à… euh…: Hide-and-seek! You count to… um… lots!
textes.Caelan ! Tu as encore joué toute la nuit: Caelan! Did you play all night again?
textes.Caelan ? Il joue sous ma fenêtre depuis: Caelan? He's been playing under my window for a hundred years, he thinks I don't know, and he's never said a word to my face. The sweetest of idiots. My idiot, perhaps. Someday.
textes.Caelan a composé une chanson sur mon pai: Caelan composed a song about my bread: “O golden crust…”. He sang it in front of my oven, and I said “pretty”. He danced away. I never told him that, that day, the oven rose perfectly, for the first time all week. I think my oven likes songs.
textes.Caelan a encore composé une chanson pour: Caelan has written another song for Ilyria. Forty verses. Ilyria fell asleep at the twelfth.
textes.Caelan a une bague dans sa poche. Il la: Caelan has a ring in his pocket. He fiddles with it all day long. He thinks nobody notices.
textes.Caelan chante comme un rossignol et parl: Caelan sings like a nightingale and talks to Ilyria like a log. Forty verses for her, and not a word to her face. I'm fond of him. He eats my brioches in rhythm.
textes.Caelan croit que je ne sais pas. Je sais: Caelan thinks I don't know. I know. I've known for a hundred years. I'm waiting for him to dare.
textes.Caelan est amoureux d'Ilyria ! Tout le m: Caelan is in love with Ilyria! Everyone knows! Except Ilyria. Well, she pretends.
textes.Caelan est un grand musicien et un parte: Caelan is a great musician and an appalling partner. Two centuries of duets, and he leaves me stranded mid-verse for a pair of blue eyes. I'll forgive him. In a century.
Caelan and Ilyria… everyone's waiting. Everyone.
textes.Caelan joue de la harpe sous les fenêtre: Caelan plays the harp under Ilyria's windows. Every night. I'm a guard: I have to hear everything. EVERYTHING.
textes.Caelan joue encore la même chanson…: Caelan is playing the same song again…
textes.Caelan joue la même chanson d'amour depu: Caelan has been playing the same love song for a hundred years. Ilyria pretends not to understand. They wear me out.
textes.Caelan joue sous Fil-d'Aube toutes les n: Caelan has played below Fil-d'Aube every night for a hundred years. Always the same song. A guard hears everything. Some nights I'd like to be a little deaf.
textes.Caelan joue toutes les nuits, et moi je: Caelan plays every night, and I keep watch every night. At that hour, we're the only two awake. He plays better when the lantern is blue.
textes.Caelan me confie une lettre pour Ilyria: Caelan gives me a letter for Ilyria every week, and every week he runs after me to take it back. I run fast. He runs faster. Love, no doubt.
textes.Caelan vient soigner son cœur brisé deux: Caelan has come to have his broken heart mended twice a week for a hundred years. His heart isn't broken. It's just too big for his chest. He wears me out.
textes.Caelan écrit toutes ses chansons pour Il: Caelan writes all his songs for Ilyria, and I'm the one who has to sing them at festivals. Four hundred “Ilyria”s in one evening. I ended up replacing her name with “the moon”. Caelan sulked for a week. Ilyria thanked me with a wink. And the moon said nothing.
Caelan. The harp. Not after midnight.
textes.Caelan. Ta tisane. Tu joues le trente-si: Caelan. Your tea. Are you playing the thirty-sixth tonight?
textes.Caelan. Tu as encore mal au cœur, ou je: Caelan. Is your heart still aching, or can I close up?
textes.Caelan. Tu restes sur l'estrade jusqu'à: Caelan. Are you staying on the stage till the end this time?
textes.Café ! Vous êtes de la maison, alors. As: Coffee! Then you're one of the family. Sit at the counter whenever you like: there'll always be a cup coming out of the boiler for you.
textes.Caillou-papier-ciseaux. Ils jouent toujo: Rock-paper-scissors. They always play rock. They win one time out of three.
textes.Calcine ! Tu as encore posé les pieds su: Calcine! You've put your feet on the fountain again, in my dress!
textes.Calcine a écrit une chanson sur moi : «: Calcine wrote a song about me: “The Ballad of the Town Crier”. There's a part where the violin imitates my voice. It's a very good likeness. Too good. The children sing it in the street, shouting. I pretend to be offended. Really, I hum it in the morning while doing my hair.
textes.Calcine joue du violon comme un feu qui: Calcine plays the violin like a dancing fire. I come to listen to her every evening, in the front row. She makes fun of me. She's right to. Her violet eyes shine brighter than my horns. That says it all.
textes.Calcine joue du violon derrière mes hist: Calcine plays the violin behind my stories. Low notes when it's scary, soft notes when it ends well. And one very long note when I forget what comes next. She often saves me.
textes.Calcine joue du violon sur la Grand-Plac: Calcine plays the violin on the Grand Square. She's got talent, character and a very fast bow. When I shout over her music, she plays louder. I love it. She loves it a bit less.
textes.Calcine joue du violon sur la place. J'a: Calcine plays the violin on the square. I light the street lamps in time with her music. She eventually noticed, and now she plays a waltz for me. I don't know what to do with my gratitude.
textes.Calcine joue une valse pour moi, chaque: Calcine plays a waltz for me every evening, when I light the first street lamp. She thinks I haven't noticed. I light the lamps in rhythm. One flame per note.
textes.Calcine porte mes robes comme personne :: Calcine wears my dresses like nobody else: playing the violin, dancing, jumping onto the fountain. She wears them out in a month. I sew them back up in an evening. She's the finest shop window my workshop has.
textes.Calcine, ce soir, l'histoire du Titan de: Calcine, tonight, the story of the Frost Titan.
textes.Calcine… Ah, Calcine. Elle joue comme un: Calcine… Ah, Calcine. She plays like a dancing fire. She told me my horns shine brighter than my conversation. I've decided that was a compliment.
textes.Calme ! Sage moussaillon. Une mer calme,: Calm! Wise cabin boy. A calm sea is a sea that reflects. And you reflect too.
textes.Calme comme l'eau de la mare. Sauf quand: Calm as the water of the pond. Except when the frog jumps. Then I laugh. Tee hee hee.
Calm as the pond at dawn.
textes.Calme comme un chat qui dort. Ce soir, l: Calm as a sleeping cat. Tonight, the wind will turn: look at the seagulls, they're flying low.
textes.Calme. Ce matin, seulement trois genoux: Calm. This morning, just three of Tornade's knees, one of Cradoc's elbows and a splinter from Copeau. A quiet morning.
Calm. Like a lake in January.
textes.Calme. Deux aventuriers sont descendus c: Quiet. Two adventurers went down this morning. They came back up from the first floor, covered in jelly. As usual. The dungeon chews on them a bit, then spits them out.
textes.Calme. J'ai trouvé un éclat de cristal q: Calm. I found a crystal shard that sings when you blow on it. I'm not going to sell it. Some things you have to keep for yourself. Or for someone.
textes.Calme. La rivière du Gouffre a baissé d': Calm. The Chasm river dropped half a tone this week. It sings in G now. I told Bricole. She retuned the organ. Nobody else noticed. But tonight, everything will sound better.
textes.Calme. Toujours calme. Le Sustentateur n: Calm. Always calm. The north-east Levitator coughed this morning. I spoke to it gently, tightened a bolt, and it started purring again. You don't panic in front of an engine. It would sense it.
textes.Calme. Toujours calme. Un croupier nerve: Calm. Always calm. A nervous croupier is a poor croupier.
textes.Calme. Trop calme. Je n'aime pas quand c: Quiet. Too quiet. I don't like it when it's too quiet.
textes.Calme. Un livre m'a souri, ce matin. Enf: Calm. A book smiled at me this morning. Well, an illumination did. It's almost the same.
textes.Calmes… Hm. Tu ferais un bon ami pour Om: Quiet… Hm. You'd make a good friend for Ombreline. Or for Gorgoth. All right, I'll lower my voice when you're around. A bit. I'll try.
textes.Calme… avec la mer autour, ça ferait un: Calm… with the sea all around, that'd make a lovely chord. You've got an ear, you have.
textes.Camazotz hurle : une nuée de chauves-sou: Camazotz screeches: a swarm of bats rises!
textes.Camazotz pousse un cri à vous percer les: Camazotz lets out a cry that pierces your eardrums!
textes.Camazotz s'écrase sur les dalles et se d: Camazotz crashes onto the flagstones and dissolves into a cloud of bats fleeing through the cracks in the vault. Silence… On the altar at the back, something green lights up.
textes.Camp des Fleurs\nPaix, amour et tourneso:
Flower Camp
Peace, love and sunflowers.
(Please don't walk in the gardens.)
textes.Canonnier depuis l'âge de dix ans. À for: Gunner since I was ten. After all those cannons, I can't hear a thing. SO SPEAK UP!
textes.Canonnier à dix ans ! Le plus jeune de l: Gunner at ten! The youngest in the fleet! I loaded, I aimed, I fired faster than the grown-ups. After a while, my ears started whistling. Then buzzing. Then going quiet, nearly. Now, I hear cannons, bells and Mama Grog. The rest is MUMBLING. People mumble. That's why I shout. To show them.
textes.Cap au nord ! … On est amarrés, mais je: Heading north! … We're moored, but I'm practising.
textes.Cap au nord, vent arrière. On fera le to: Heading north, wind behind us. We'll go round the island in forty minutes. Or thirty-nine, if the Captain's watching.
textes.Cap sur la Skala, matelot ! Et ma vraie: Course for the Skala, sailor! And my real trip?
textes.Capitaine ! Des graines de tournesol, to: Captain! Sunflower seeds, nice and fresh!
textes.Capitaine ! La vue est toujours exceptio: Captain! Is the view still exceptional?
textes.Capitaine ! Le premier poisson, pour vou: Captain! The first fish, for you!
