textes.Capitaine ! Le vent souffle du nord, auj: Captain! The wind's from the north today!
textes.Capitaine ! Ma Morue contre votre Requin: Captain! My Cod for your Shark?
textes.Capitaine ! On part quand ? Je peux sonn: Captain! When are we leaving? Can I ring? What's the wind today?
textes.Capitaine ! Ta table est prête. Et ton g: Captain! Your table's ready. And your punch!
textes.Capitaine ! Tu as vu ma mère ?: Captain! Did you see my mother?
textes.Capitaine ! Tu n'as pas misé la Morue, c: Captain! You haven't bet the Cod tonight, have you?
textes.Capitaine ! Un tour de pédalo ?: Captain! A spin in the pedalo?
textes.Capitaine ? Y a qu'une capitaine ici, et: Captain? There's only one captain here, and it's me! You can be… admiral of the gulls. It's a very good rank. Nobody's ever had it.
textes.Capitaine, c'était ma dorade de la fonta: Captain was my sea bream in the fountain. I set her free because she looked sad on the stall. Mum shouted “MY SEA BREAM!” so loud that Saïd turned around on his platform. And afterwards, three days in a row, she walked past the fountain with breadcrumbs, pretending it was nothing. I saw her. She was talking to it.
Captain, the Zahra awaits your orders.
textes.Capitaine, le Révérend a besoin de la Râ: Captain, the Reverend needs the Golden Grater.
textes.Capitaine, vous viendrez à la messe ?: Captain, will you come to mass?
textes.Capitaine. Les épées de la Garde sont pr: Captain. The Guard's swords are ready.
textes.Capitainerie de Port-Azur, Odette Vasseu: Port-Azur harbour office, Odette Vasseur. Are you moored, passing through, or lost?
textes.Capitainerie du Port des Cordages, bonjo: Harbour Master's Office, Rigging Harbour, good morning. A boat to declare? A seagull to report? A stamp that needs stamping?
textes.Capucine Buvard, la fleuriste, a vu un l: Capucine Buvard, the florist, saw a rabbit roll the pot of red (no. 3) towards Mr Paille, the scarecrow, in the middle of the White Meadows. But the grass is tall, and Capucine is scared of rabbits.
textes.Capucine a mis des confettis dans ma mac: Capucine put confetti in my bubble machine. Now the bubbles are full of confetti. It's even prettier. Don't tell her.
textes.Capucine a été mon apprentie six ans. Ap: Capucine was my apprentice for six years. After the seventh roof, she left to “keep the colours without the danger”. I'm prouder of that than of all my explosions put together! Me, I'm preparing the Big One: the biggest of them all. The fifteenth roof, I want it in iron. Thick iron! And every lunchtime, I drink my coffee with iron filings, at Gaston's. To help me think.
textes.Capucine dit que ses coquelicots sont tr: Capucine says her poppies are sad. I think they're sulking. A white poppy is a poppy with hurt feelings.
textes.Capucine dit que son canon à confettis g: Capucine says her confetti cannon will win the Fair. Her confetti is in all my gears.
textes.Capucine est aux Prés Blancs, Achille au: Capucine is in the White Meadows, Achille at the foot of the Ink Waterfall.
textes.Capucine est ma muse, ma femme et ma pre: Capucine is my muse, my wife and my first reader. She falls asleep during the long poems. So I shorten them. Thanks to her, I've become a concise poet. Well, a less long one.
textes.Capucine est une peste à confettis. Ses: Capucine is a confetti pest. Her little bits of paper are in my gears, in my pockets, and even in my soup. And the day my golden gear jumped out, there were some everywhere. I'm just saying. I'm not saying anything.
textes.Capucine m'a offert un filtre à confetti: Capucine gave me a confetti filter. Wire mesh, with a pink ribbon. As if my engine needed a sieve! I turned it down, politely, by handing it back to her in front of everyone. That very evening, I spent two hours picking confetti out of my gears with tweezers. I didn't tell her. She surely knows.
textes.Capucine tire des confettis sur tout ce: Capucine fires confetti at everything that moves. And at things that don't: my clock. She's charming. From a certain distance.
textes.Capucine vend mes fleurs, et moi je fais: Capucine sells my flowers, and I grow hers. Well, it's complicated. We've stopped counting who owes what to whom. We count bouquets.
textes.Capucine, c'est la meilleure liftière de: Capucine is the best liftkeeper on the Column. She talks to the machine, and the machine answers her. I can't hear the machine any more. But I hear Capucine. Always. Even when she whispers. Go figure.
textes.Capucine, c'est le soleil du stand 3. El: Capucine is the sunshine of stand 3. She slipped confetti into my machine, on the sly. I pretend I haven't seen a thing. Don't tell her: she'd be disappointed to be found out.
textes.Capucine, c'est ma meilleure élève. Ma s: Capucine is my best pupil. My only pupil, all right, but the best! She took my explosions and turned them into parties. I'm as proud of her as if she were my daughter.
textes.Capucine, pourquoi ces fleurs sont-elles: Capucine, why are these flowers all white?
textes.Capucine, voici le rouge ! Le lapin s'es: Capucine, here's the red! The rabbit ran away.
Capucine. About New Year: let's talk.
textes.Caramel ? Pain de carotte contre sardine: Caramel? Carrot bread versus sardines, rabbits versus cats: it's an old story. At the last Great Swap, the chain broke between us. She wasn't entirely in the wrong. I'll never say so.
textes.Caramel a trouvé des noisettes dans les: Caramel found hazelnuts in the fishery crates, among the sardines. “To keep them cool,” said Gland. She shouted. Me, I laughed into my whiskers. Afterwards I taught him a fisherman's knot, so he'd tie up his hazelnut bags instead of hiding them at my place. He does it very well. He does it everywhere.
textes.Caramel m'a raconté. Une Grande Course,: Caramel told me. A Great Race, I go past the jetty. Dad stands up. All at once. He shouts. Him! His rod falls in the water. He loses it. … I didn't see. I was running. … He never told me. I never told him either.
textes.Caramel reçoit une lettre d'Ardoise chaq: Caramel gets a letter from Ardoise every month. She takes it without a word and goes to read it at the end of the jetty. I guess things. But a postmistress says nothing.
textes.Cardamome ? Charmante, savante, et elle: Cardamome? Charming, learned, and she pays for my nectar with riddles. And her riddles leave my customers stuck in front of my stall for hours.
textes.Cardamome commence toujours ses énigmes: Cardamome always starts her riddles with “The more I have…” or “I run without…”. So I shout “A frog!” before the end. Once SHE changed the answer so it would be a frog. I said it was too easy. She didn't speak to me for the rest of the day.
textes.Cardamome pose des énigmes à tout le mon: Cardamome sets riddles for everyone, and I never get them. She says it doesn't matter. But now she picks easy ones for me. I can tell.
Cardamome asks everyone riddles. I never get them. She says it doesn't matter. It matters a little.
textes.Cardamome sait tout, se souvient de tout: Cardamome knows everything, remembers everything, and sets riddles that are far too long. I answer before the end. It saves time. Not the right answer, but time.
textes.Cardamome. Elle pose des devinettes sur: Cardamome. She makes up riddles about me. She writes everything I say in a book. Everything. Annoying. … At least someone listens. Hmph.
textes.Cardamome. Tu me dois toujours trois fla: Cardamome. You still owe me three bottles.
textes.Cardamome… tu as une énigme pour moi ? U: Cardamome… have you got a riddle for me? A real one?
textes.Caresse-le ! Il fait la pluie sur les pl: Stroke him! He rains on the plants, and then he makes a rainbow. He's very proud of his rainbow.
textes.Caresse-le encore, il va faire son tour: Stroke him again, he's going to do his trick!
textes.Caresse-moi. Non, pas là. Là. … Voilà. T: Stroke me. No, not there. There. … That's it. You may continue.
textes.Caresser un vrai chat d'en bas. L'entend: To stroke a real cat from down below. To hear it purr. And for it to agree to stay on my lap for more than three seconds. Murmure says that's very difficult. I'm ready to wait three hundred years.
textes.Cargo commande un bol tous les soirs. Il: Cargo orders a bowl every evening. He doesn't eat, he smells it. Then he hands the bowl back full and pays anyway. He's my best customer. And I give the bowl to Mio.
textes.Cargo est grand, fort, et doux comme un: Cargo is big, strong, and soft as a cloud. In the evening, we watch the sea together. We say nothing. It's our favourite conversation.
textes.Cargo m'a porté sur ses épaules pour que: Cargo carried me on his shoulders so I could see the city's first fireworks. I had a broom in my hand. I waved it like a flag.
textes.Cargo, Kenji cherche une puce vocale Sér: Cargo, Kenji is looking for a Z Series voice chip, for Zéro.
textes.Cargo, le docker du quai, vient tous les: Cargo, the dockworker from the quay, comes every evening. He doesn't eat, but he orders a bowl to smell it. He says it reminds him of something. He doesn't know what.
textes.Cartographie, garnement. Rien que de la: Cartography, you rascal. Nothing but cartography.
textes.Carène : le bateau en bouteille: Carène: the ship in a bottle
textes.Ce Firmin, le frère de Gustave, en bas…: That Firmin, Gustave's brother, down below… Apparently his chocolate machine whistles like a steam engine. A scandal. I went down to check. It whistles. I had two hot chocolates. To check again.
textes.Ce Lord anglais m'a proposé d'acheter me: That English Lord offered to buy my socks “for his collection”. I said no. I think.
textes.Ce ballon-sonde va monter à dix kilomètr: This weather balloon will climb to ten kilometres. It'll send us the temperature from up there. And a postcard, I hope.
This bench is our meeting room.
This bolt is too ugly for you.
textes.Ce bras ? Un accident d'atelier, il y a: This arm? A workshop accident, ten years ago. A press in a bit too much of a hurry. I built this one myself, part by part. It grips harder than the other one. It does handshakes a bit too hard as well. I'm practising.
textes.Ce café, c'était celui de ma mère. Je co: This café was my mother's. I know everyone's habits: the mayor, a strong coffee at noon; Colette, a herbal tea and a novel at seven; the professor, three coffees and zero words.
textes.Ce café, c'était celui de ma mère. Moi,: This café was my mother's. I did my homework under the corner table, between the customers' feet. I learned the orders before my times tables: one short black, two white coffees, an almond syrup, a glass of water for the dog. At eight, I knew who drank what. At nine, I knew why.
textes.Ce canapé est désormais la propriété de: This sofa is now the property of Lisse & Sons. We thank you for your cooperation.
textes.Ce champignon qui brille, c'est quoi ?: That glowing mushroom, what is it?
textes.Ce chapeau ? Il appartenait à un grand m: This hat? It belonged to a great magician. Well, that's what the seller told me. He sold it to me cheap. Heh heh. I know a good salesman when I see one.
textes.Ce chat roux qui traîne sur les toits, c: That ginger cat prowling the rooftops is nobody's cat. He steals, but he only steals what shines or what smells of fish. And the pirates' papers smell of fish.
textes.Ce cher Edmond est le plus digne récepti: Dear Edmond is the most dignified receptionist in the archipelago, and he wears the most distinguished moustache I have ever seen, admiral included. He refuses to sell it to me. I respect that. And I insist.
textes.Ce chocolat chaud, c'est un câlin dans u: This hot chocolate is a hug in a mug.
textes.Ce château dans le ciel, au sud ?: That castle in the sky, to the south?
textes.Ce coffre a des dents ! UNE MIMIQUE ! Qu: This chest has teeth! A MIMIC! When the lid opens wide, it's about to pounce: step aside, then strike.
That bolt necklace… I simply must have it.
textes.Ce drap a vu trois tempêtes et un pique-: This sheet has seen three storms and a picnic. And it shows.
textes.Ce formulaire est déjà tamponné. (Deux f: This form is already stamped. (Twice would be overzealous. Zeal is forbidden on Tuesdays.)
textes.Ce grand pirate chauve a jeté son ancre: That big bald pirate dropped his anchor on my green net. He owes me three weeks of work. All he says is “Hm”. “Hm” never paid a bill.
textes.Ce jeune Icare passe au-dessus de mon ba: That young Icare flies over my balcony on his glider. Every day. He frightens my geraniums. Well, he also makes my sparrows laugh. I haven't decided yet whether I hold it against him.
textes.Ce jeune homme joue bien, mais toujours: That young man plays well, but always a little too fast. Young people think the music will run away. It won't: it waits for you to catch up.
textes.Ce jour-là, je fermerai l'étal. Pour la: That day, I'll close the stall. For the first time in my life. I'll hang up a sign: “Closed. The little one's dancing.” My grandmother will pull such a face, up there. Then she'll clap.
That day, you were dancing on it.
textes.Ce jour-là, {surnom}, la Fabrique fêtait: That day, {surnom}, the Works was celebrating its fortieth anniversary. The singing sweeper was my present for Rivet. Three months spent piecing his song back together from memory, wrong note by wrong note. I've never been able to tell him. Every evening I sit at the end of the bench and wait for him to speak first. I'm chief engineer. I've never invented anything so stupid.
textes.Ce journal, je l'ai lu cent fois, la nui: That logbook, I've read it a hundred times, at night, by lantern light. It smells of tar and cold sea. In the middle, there are blank pages, as if whoever was writing had held his breath. I've never understood what he didn't want to write. Corentin, perhaps, knows. Or someone, one day, will know.
textes.Ce lait de nuage… On dirait de boire un: This cloud milk… It's like drinking a pillow. A delicious pillow.
This morning! She said hello to you, Halima.
textes.Ce matin, Pimprenelle a répondu tout de: This morning, Pimprenelle answered straight away! Three quick knocks! She found a bolt! I don't know which one. I imagine it's golden. With six sides.
textes.Ce matin, avant sept heures : « Pourquoi: This morning, before seven: “Why does bread puff up? Why is the sea salty? Why does Léon have a beard? Why don't seagulls eat pains au chocolat? Why don't I have a dog?” I answered the first one. Yeast. She said: “And yeast, is it alive? Why?”
textes.Ce matin, il y avait du vent du nord ! L: This morning there was a north wind! The best for kites! Grandpa Séverin says Séraphin flew his in a north wind too. I'm family, you can tell.
textes.Ce matin, j'ai fait des biscuits lunaire: This morning I made moon biscuits for the whole Council. Tempo arrived at eight o'clock sharp, Écliptique gave a speech about the biscuits, and the Elder ate them all during the speech.
textes.Ce matin, j'ai fait la première descente: This morning I made the first trip down with the bread from up top, for La Marmite. The whole cabin smelled of warm crust. Honorine kissed me on the head. I didn't hear what she said, but I felt it was kind.
textes.Ce matin, j'ai fait un vœu à la Fontaine: This morning, I made a wish at the Bubble Fountain. You whisper your wish to a bubble, and it carries it all the way up, right up to the surface. My wish is to see the rain. My bubble went up really fast. I think it was in a hurry to give it to someone.
textes.Ce matin, j'ai tapé deux coups, puis un,: This morning I tapped twice, then once, on the kitchen pipe. Under my feet, someone answered: three quick taps. That means “bolt found”. I know who it is. I won't say. (She turns bright red.)
textes.Ce matin, la capsule a traversé le nuage: This morning the capsule went through the cloud right at sunrise. Everything turned pink. A lady clapped. So did I. Two of us clapping a cloud. It was lovely.
textes.Ce matin, le ciel est clair jusqu'à l'ho: This morning, the sky is clear all the way to the horizon. Perfect for a race. I sent a pigeon to Héloïse. She replied “already gone”. She cheats. I love it.
textes.Ce matin, les quatre voyants sont passés: This morning, all four indicator lights turned blue at the same time, at six sharp. That almost never happens. I drank my tea standing up, in their honour.
textes.Ce matin, première descente à sept heure: This morning, first trip down at seven, with warm bread from up top and three tourists still in their slippers. The Great Pearl had just turned golden white. The whole cabin fell silent. Even the bread looked moved.
textes.Ce matin, première tartine du grille-pai: This morning, the first slice of toast from the solar toaster. Perfect. And the table barely got toasted. Just a little ring. I consider that the final version.
textes.Ce matin, sur le Pont, j'ai crié mon pré: This morning, on the Bridge, I shouted my name into the Chasm. It sent it back three times. I didn't know I had such a lovely name.
textes.Ce matin, un drone est tombé dans le gra: This morning a drone fell into the gravel. I raked around it. It is part of the garden now. Aïko painted it.
textes.Ce matin-là, j'apportais le café sur le: That morning, I was bringing coffee down to the quay. I heard Marius say to Fernand, about the net: “Keep it.” I never told Anselme. If he knew, he'd have no reason left to hold it against Fernand. He'd have to grieve for his brother instead. Sixteen years I've kept quiet, {surnom}. I no longer know if it's kindness or cowardice.
textes.Ce mur est trop coloré. Repeinture grise: This wall is too colourful. Grey repaint scheduled. Error: green spray can detected.
This little wall is mine. So is the town.
It is not the same at all. I'm writing that down.
textes.Ce n'est pas encore le moment pour celui: It's not time for that one yet.
textes.Ce n'est pas grave du tout. Mon père ne: That doesn't matter at all. My father couldn't, and he was the wisest of men. Come to the House of Life: I'll teach you your name in one afternoon. In exchange, you'll listen to a story. Or three.
textes.Ce n'est pas grave. Bastien non plus. Le: That's all right. Bastien doesn't either. The fairies don't hold it against you, they believe in you anyway. That's how they are.
textes.Ce n'est pas grave. J'en ai une autre. I: It doesn't matter. I've got another one. He can eat that one too.
textes.Ce n'est pas grave. Les rêves qu'on oubl: It doesn't matter. The dreams we forget do their work in silence, like good prayers. Sleep well, my child.
textes.Ce n'est pas le même genre d'arrosage, P: That's not the same kind of watering, Pilli.
textes.Ce n'est pas ta pince, c'est la mienne !: They're not your tongs, they're mine!
textes.Ce n'est pas un squat, c'est une maison: It's not a squat, it's a home! With people in it!
textes.Ce n'est pas une réponse. Dimanche, je m: That's not an answer. Sunday, I'm coming up.
Not very secret any more, then.
textes.Ce n'est rien, Violette ! Ils étaient tr: It was nothing, Violette! It was standing very high. It's lying down nicely now.
textes.Ce n'est rien. J'aime les mètres ruban u: It's nothing. I like my tape measures a little singed.
textes.Ce n'est rien. Le Cœur bat un peu moins: It's nothing. The Heart is beating a little more weakly. It's nothing. … Fine, it is. It's something. Shards of the Heart have broken off. They need to be found. Don't tell the Elder. She already knows, anyway.
textes.Ce n'était pas plutôt un rayon de soleil: Wasn't it just a ray of sunshine?
textes.Ce n'était pas une chute, ma sœur ! C'ét: That was no fall, Sister! It was a strategic roll!
That cloud there, I'm calling it Gaspard.
textes.Ce paon de Tiburce passe devant mon atel: That peacock Tiburce walks past my workshop ten times a day to show me his new collar. He's had the same collar for three centuries. He just irons it differently.
textes.Ce papillon ? Je ne le chassais pas. Je: That butterfly? I wasn't chasing it. I was inspecting it. There's a difference.
textes.Ce pirate m'a acheté un tapis au premier: That pirate bought a carpet from me at the first price. The first! Without haggling! He soiled my honour, my brother. And he has excellent taste, that's the worst part.
textes.Ce poing de fer, tu me le forges ?: That iron fist… will you forge it for me?
textes.Ce port est trop calme. Les gens sont tr: This port is too calm. The people are too nice. The captain lost his map. The end of summer is coming. I walked two days in the dunes, because of a caravan trader. The tavern keeper threw me out by the ear. I shout at the cabin boy. And I watch the coppersmith hammer. Every day. Hm. It calms me down.
This port is too quiet. The people are too nice. I don't like it.
This post is my morning newspaper.
textes.Ce que j'aime ici, c'est qu'on peut tout: What I love here is that you can go everywhere on foot. Except to Port-Azur — for that, you need the boat.
textes.Ce que je préfère, c'est l'heure du reto: What I love most is the homecoming hour. All the blue boats passing the jetty at the same time, the seagulls overhead, the children running on the quay… You never tire of it.
What I like best is you.
Whatever I find, when I find it.
textes.Ce que les autres mangent… (Elle pose sa: Whatever the others are having… (She puts down her ladle.) My pebble, that's the loveliest answer anyone's ever given me. You were made for the Free Canteen.
What other people have cooked for me.
textes.Ce que tu trouves ?! Assieds-toi. Non, p: Whatever you find?! Sit down. No, no arguing. You're not leaving here without two bowls in your belly.
textes.Ce qui change… Toi, tu parles comme ma f: Things that change… You talk like my daughter. She says the world belongs to inventors. Maybe. But inventors need a hammer, now and then!
textes.Ce qui chatouille ! (Ses quatre bras app: Tickly! (His four arms applaud.) Cosmic jelly! It's my grandmother's recipe. You've got the taste buds of a real Lumen.
textes.Ce qui est propre… (Elle soupire longuem: Whatever's clean… (She sighs at length.) I see. It's a start. A very small start. Come and see me again. Often.
textes.Ce qui m'agace, avec Hamid, c'est qu'il: What annoys me about Hamid is that he arrives before the fleet. Not him: his voice. I prepare my entrance, I puff out my chest for the big “HERE COMES THE FLEET!”… and you can already hear Hamid singing behind the jetty. Everyone turns to the sea. My effect is ruined. Every morning.
textes.Ce qui me ferait plaisir ? %s. Je ne dis: What would make me happy? %s. I never say no to that.
textes.Ce qui me ferait plaisir ? Une visite, c: What would make me happy? A visit, like this one. That's already a lot.
textes.Ce qui traîne ?! … Je vais m'asseoir. …: Whatever's lying around?! … I need to sit down. … Right. I'm sitting. Drop by the workshop tomorrow. No, tonight. No: now.
textes.Ce ressort-là a sauté trois fois. Il a d: That spring has sprung loose three times. It's got character.
textes.Ce robot dit bonjour aux arbres. Et aux: That robot says hello to the trees. And to the benches. And to me. He noticed I was feeding the sparrows. He told nobody. He “merely observed it out loud”, in front of everyone. I hold it against him. A little. He's very polite.
textes.Ce robot sent le boulon. Je peux le mord: This robot smells of bolts. Can I bite it? Say yes.
textes.Ce robot sentait le boulon. Je l'ai mord: That robot smelled of bolts. I bit it. It said “thank you for your understanding”. I didn't understand anything. I bit it again.
That red one is for Flanelle.
textes.Ce rubis, Grimli. Il vient d'où ?: This ruby, Grimli. Where's it from?
textes.Ce sacré Bruno ! Il est arrivé avec sa s: Good old Bruno! He showed up with his ice-cream maker and stole all my customers in one summer. I don't hold it against him. Much. His ice creams are too good — that's unfair competition.
textes.Ce soir je danse sur la place. Les gens: Tonight I'm dancing on the square. The people of Tazira dance better than any crew.
textes.Ce soir à la Grande Scène : « Le Soleil: Tonight on the Main Stage: “The Sun and the Rain”! Flanelle sings, Grésil makes his guitar squeal, and Arc-en-Ciel answers Bourrasque's drums.
textes.Ce soir à la Halle, le batteur de rempla: Tonight at the Hall, the stand-in drummer is… a surprise! The Sergeant isn't saying anything. The Sergeant swore. The Sergeant just hopes it won't be Boulon again. Sorry, Boulon.
textes.Ce soir à la batterie : Boulon ! Il tape: Tonight on drums: Boulon! He hits ever so softly. The bass drum is worried anyway.
textes.Ce soir à la batterie : Copeau. Il mesur: Tonight on drums: Copeau. He measures twice before every hit. It's very precise. It's very slow.
textes.Ce soir à la batterie : Gédéon Lisse ! L: Tonight on drums: Gédéon Lisse! His opening drumroll makes the glass roof shake. Rouille howls with joy.
textes.Ce soir à la batterie, un des chiens de: Tonight on drums, one of Chaussette's dogs jumped onto the bass drum. He's playing with his tail. Tapage says he's the best stand-in of the week.
textes.Ce soir, Fusible a branché la batterie s: Tonight, Fusible hooked the drums up to the spotlights: every cymbal crash, the hall changes colour. He's hitting too fast. Nobody can see a thing.
textes.Ce soir, c'est Larsen qui tient la batte: Tonight Larsen is on drums, because nobody else showed up. The sound desk is empty. The sound is… free.
textes.Ce soir, c'est Tapage à la batterie. Il: Tonight it's Tapage on drums. He just launched into an eleven-minute solo in the middle of the slow song. Clou is closing his eyes. Very tightly.
textes.Ce soir, c'est moi qui baisse le Soleil: Tonight, I'm the one who dims the Brass Sun. Forty turns of the crank. I count out loud. The whole cavern counts with me.
textes.Ce soir, c'est moi qui cuisine pour toi,: Tonight, I'm cooking for you, my dear.
textes.Ce soir, il y a concert dans les Strates: Tonight there's a concert in the Strata, down below. We'll hear the Fronde through the Column's shaft again. Boom, boom. Me, I quite like it.
Tonight I'm playing the moon song. Come to the Circle, listen, and don't tell Pivoine I wrote it for her.
textes.Ce soir, je tape sur le grand tambour. B: Tonight, I bang the big drum. Boom. That, I like.
textes.Ce soir, je tiens le tambour. Boum, boum: Tonight I'm on the drum. Boom, boom-boom. I'm the heart of the party.
textes.Ce soir, l'ami ! Avec la rime en « appét: Tonight, my friend! With the rhyme on “chewy”!
Tonight, the pirate and the caves.
textes.Ce soir, les Soupapes jouent à vingt heu: Tonight, the Valves play at eight. Like yesterday. Like tomorrow. And it's always the first time.
textes.Ce soir, les aurores ! Vibrato joue, je: Tonight, the auroras! Vibrato plays, I dance, the sky lights up. If you move your arms on the Agora, the light will follow you too. Try it. Nobody's watching. Well, everyone's watching. But kindly.
textes.Ce soir, nuit des aurores. Je joue sur l: Tonight, aurora night. I play on the Agora, in front of the fountain, and Prisme dances. The auroras follow the music. Or the music follows the auroras. We never know who starts.
textes.Ce soir, on danse sous l'Arbre-Mère ?: Tonight, shall we dance beneath the Mother Tree?
textes.Ce soir, tu danses pour qui ?: Who are you dancing for tonight?
textes.Ce soir, à la Halle Hurlante, à vingt et: Tonight, at the Howling Hall, at nine o'clock: the Bilge Rats! Free, loud, and full of love! Don't forget your earplugs, at Pastille's counter.
textes.Ce soir-là, au premier rang, un homme à: That night, in the front row, a man with a wooden leg was clapping louder than everyone. After the show, he was waiting for me behind the caravan: “On my brig, nobody asks for a raise.” I laughed. I said goodbye to Grandma. She slipped her wooden spoon into my pocket, and I signed on to the Veuve Écarlate.
Tonight. And tomorrow. To be sure.
textes.Ce sont des attrape-rêves. Le filet attr: These are dreamcatchers. The net catches bad dreams, and good dreams slide through the little hole in the middle, down the feathers, to the sleeper. Want one? It's made with twine from Galet.
textes.Ce sont des plumes de perroquet. Cousues: They're parrot feathers. Sewn on by me.
It's the flowers that are kind.
textes.Ce sont les petits nuages qui passent en: They're the little clouds that drift over the Esplanade in flocks. Doctor Aurèle counts them and gives them names. We gave them a march.
textes.Ce sont les reliques de demain, Nolwenn: They're tomorrow's relics, Nolwenn! I'm ahead of my time!
textes.Ce sont tes pots qui regardent, Coyotl !: It's your pots doing the watching, Coyotl!
textes.Ce trou ? C'est Truffe, mon gars. Le plu: That hole? That's Truffe, my lad. The smallest of my pigs. Pink and black, as big as a bread basket, and a nose… a golden nose! He smells truffles underground from fifty paces. But there it is: he smells turnips too. And my turnips, when you dig them up, they wake up and run away! The other day, he woke up twelve. Twelve! Germaine ran all the way to the mill. So Truffe runs off every morning toward the woods, and with my knees, I can't catch him anymore. He had a little bell so we could hear him coming. He lost it. A pig like him needs someone who walks a lot, who travels, who likes surprises under the ground. Someone like you, actually. Go see Germaine: she always knows where he's wandering.
textes.Ce ventilateur, c'est une tornade en pyj: That fan is a tornado in pyjamas.
textes.Ce village est un trésor. Pas de bruit…: This village is a treasure. No noise… well, except here.
textes.Ce « gloup » ne me fait pas peur ! C'est: That “gloop” doesn't scare me! Is it my stomach? … No, it's the dungeon.
textes.Ceci est un avis d'expulsion. Bonne jour: This is an eviction notice. Have a nice day!
textes.Ceci ne sort pas d'ici, {surnom}. C'est: This doesn't leave this spot, {surnom}. That's an order. Since the spring, Kevin has been teaching me to swim. At six in the morning, in the cove behind the lighthouse, while the town sleeps. I did three strokes. Three, head above water, without touching the bottom. Kevin said: “Well done, sergeant.” I didn't reply. I had water in my moustache. And elsewhere.
textes.Celebrë ! On reprend la « Ballade de l'A: Celebrë! Shall we do the “Ballad of the Dawn” together again, for the festival?
textes.Celebrë a la plus belle voix du Bois-Dor: Celebrë has the most beautiful voice in the Bois-Doré, and she knows it. We sang together for two centuries. She's never forgiven me for the last Dawn festival.
textes.Celebrë change mes rimes sans me demande: Celebrë changes my rhymes without asking. In my songs for Ilyria, she replaces “Ilyria” with “the moon”, so it's “less awkward for everyone”. The worst part is, it rhymes better.
textes.Celebrë chante tout ce que je danse, et: Celebrë sings everything I dance, and I dance everything she sings. She has a singer's temper, which is to say a fiery one. But her voice still lulls me.
textes.Celebrë chante à l'aube pour mes filets: Celebrë sings at dawn for my nets: the light comes more easily when someone sings. I don't tell her that enough. I leave her the first ray; that's my way of telling her.
textes.Celebrë. L'aube arrive. Tu chantes ?: Celebrë. Dawn's coming. Will you sing?
textes.Celle de l'Institut des Vents ne sait ja: The one at the Institute of Winds never knows which way to go. Doctor Aurèle says it's thinking. My husband says it's just like him. Me, I'm saying nothing.
textes.Celle du galion qui volait, petite. Appr: The one about the flying galleon, lass. Come closer.
The one about the flying galleon. Come closer.
textes.Celle du renard qui voulait devenir pain: The one about the fox who wanted to become bread.
As big as the volcano. At least.
textes.Celle-ci a un ver qui te dit bonjour. Po: This one has a worm saying hello to you. For the market, or for stewed apples?
textes.Celle-ci a un ver. Il a l'air content. O: This one's got a worm. He looks happy. We'll leave it to him.
textes.Celle-ci a une petite tache, mais elle s: This one has a little spot, but it smells good. For the market, or for stewed apples?
textes.Celle-là est cabossée d'un côté, mais su: This one's dented on one side, but sweet as sugar. For the market, or for stewed apples?
textes.Celle-là est parfaite, toute rouge, tout: That one's perfect, all red and round. For the market, or for stewed apples?
textes.Celle-là pèse un demi-kilo !: That one weighs half a kilo!
That one runs slow. Like my husband.
textes.Celle-là, c'est pour Lentille et sa louc: This one's for Lentille and her ladle! “Pay-What-You-Can Soup”! One, two, three, BOUCAN!
That one, I call Little Sauce.
I'm stealing that one for tonight.
textes.Celle-là, on l'a écrite dans la cale de: We wrote this one in the hold of the Rusty Whale! “Rats Don't Leave The Ship”!
textes.Celle-là, on la joue pour l'Usine Grise,: We're playing this one for the Grey Factory, down there, to the south! “Grey Is Not A Colour”!
The ones that are told well.
textes.Celles qu'on raconte bien… (Il te regard: The ones that are told well… (He looks at you for a long time.) Now that's the answer of a wise old soul. How old are you, exactly? Don't answer. You're old enough.
The one with the ribbon at the right page.
textes.Celui de Maître Hugues ? Le petit ?: Master Hugues's one? The little one?
textes.Celui que vous voudrez. J'attends vos in: Whichever you like. I await your instructions.
The one that vanished from the foot of your tower.
The one that makes fridges dance.
The one bleeding on your trousers.
That one? It has an incredible story. I'll tell you tomorrow. It's a long one.
textes.Celui-là ? Il est bien trop beau pour êt: That one? It's far too beautiful to be sold. That's why it's in the window.
textes.Celui-là a des rimes, Mérit. Il vaut deu: This one rhymes, Mérit. It's worth two beers.
textes.Celui-là compte double : il est très gra: That one counts double: it's really big.
textes.Celui-là est arrivé ce matin. C'est le p: That one arrived this morning. It's the oldest in the shop!
textes.Celui-là sait porter un plat !: This one knows how to carry a dish!
That one still wiggles a bit.
textes.Celui-là, je l'ai déjà compté ! … Ou c'e: I've already counted that one! … Or is it his brother?
textes.Cendrin ! Tu viendras parler aux nouveau: Cendrin! Will you come and talk to the new pupils?
textes.Cendrin et moi, nous jouons aux dames de: Cendrin and I have been playing basalt draughts for three centuries. He thinks, I tell stories, he loses. He thinks I cheat. I don't cheat: I tell stories. It's not the same thing.
textes.Cendrin était le dernier en flammes et l: Cendrin was bottom in flames and top in patience. He became guardian of the Heart-Brazier, and I became headmaster. He says the tower fire was my idea. It's true. But it was his candle.
textes.Cent ans. Mais moi, je n'en tiendrai pas: A hundred years. But I won't last ten.
textes.Cent coucous ? Plus ! Une vieille dame p: A hundred cuckoo clocks? More! An old lady goes from one to the next with a key as big as a ladle.
A hundred and two kilos, my dear Radis.
textes.Cent douze marches plus haut : te voilà: A hundred and twelve steps up: here you are in the clock room. Whirring, beating, clicking.
A hundred and twelve, give or take one.
textes.Cent neuf mille et un. Quelle régularité: A hundred and nine thousand and one. What admirable regularity.
textes.Cent neuf mille rapports : « Rien à sign: A hundred and nine thousand reports: “Nothing to report.” Every evening, word for word, in perfect handwriting. And then one evening, a shaky line: “A human. A real one. Welcome.” He'd forgotten to sign it. That was you, {surnom}. I had it framed.
textes.Cent quarante-deux, Monsieur Prosper !: A hundred and forty-two, Monsieur Prosper!
textes.Cent quarante-quatre marches. Je les mon: A hundred and forty-four steps. I run all the way up. Well, up the first forty.
textes.Cent quarante. Ou cent trente-neuf ?: A hundred and forty. Or a hundred and thirty-nine?
textes.Cent quatre-vingts ans de garde. Pas une: A hundred and eighty years on guard. Not once has the gate been forced. Not once.
textes.Cent sept coucous, cent sept tours de cl: A hundred and seven cuckoo clocks, a hundred and seven turns of the key!
textes.Cent théières, il a renversées en appren: A hundred teapots he knocked over, learning to pour from up high. All from my shop. Rabia counted, Hnia took the money. The hundred-and-first, I sold him at a higher price. He asked why. I said: “That one, you won't knock over.” He didn't knock it over. Since then, I call him my best customer. He doesn't like it.
textes.Cent vingt ans que l'île flotte, et touj: A hundred and twenty years this island has floated, and still nobody's brought back my hat, which fell down there fifty years ago.
textes.Cerbère ? Ha ! Ce gros toutou ! Trois tê: Cerberus? Ha! That big pup! Three heads, three cakes, and he sleeps like a baby. I'm happy to bake them, but I haven't a drop of fire honey left. The fire bees nest in two old hollow trunks in the Ash Wood. Bring me two honeycombs. Gently: they sting, but they're polite.
textes.Cerbère crache le feu de ses trois gueul: Cerbère breathes fire from all three mouths!
textes.Cerbère s'effondre, ses trois têtes ense: Cerbère collapses, all three heads together. (“He'd have preferred cakes,” whispers a little voice in your head.) The south gate opens.
textes.Cerbère, le grand chien à trois têtes de: Cerbère, the great three-headed dog of the Nine Circles… poor thing. Three heads, three appetites, three moods. Each one wants its own cake, not its neighbour's! Give a honey cake to each head, and they'll behave. After all, he's a dog.
textes.Cerise ! T'as vu ? J'ai réussi le saut !: Cerise! Did you see? I landed the jump!
textes.Cerise ! Tu me relis la une ?: Cerise! Will you proofread the front page for me?
textes.Cerise ! Une nouvelle histoire pour ton: Cerise! A new story for your zine!
textes.Cerise dessine tout, note tout, comprend: Cerise draws everything, notes everything, understands everything. She's nine and she runs a newsroom in a tree. I'm the proudest mother in the archipelago.
textes.Cerise est entrée dans une de mes bulles: Cerise got inside one of my bubbles and floated for three seconds. Since then, she's interviewed me every week for her zine. She's my biggest fan. And my harshest critic.
textes.Cerise fait un fanzine meilleur que le m: Cerise makes a better fanzine than mine. She's nine. I print hers for free, out of pride and jealousy. Mostly pride.
textes.Cerise m'a demandé de lui apprendre la b: Cerise asked me to teach her drums. I showed her the 1977 roll, my legendary roll. She nailed it first try. Better than me. I told her it was a fluke. She did it ten more times. I said it was ten flukes.
textes.Cerise m'a demandé une cabane dans l'arb: Cerise asked me for a treehouse in the tree on the square. I built it. Then she asked for a desk, a rubber stamp, a letterbox and “an archive room”. She's nine. I built the archive room. She files all her fanzines in it by date. Better than the Montjoie Guild, apparently.
textes.Cerise m'a dessiné un manuel de réparati: Cerise drew me a repair manual for the workshop, with bikes exploded into a thousand pieces and arrows everywhere. It's the clearest manual I've ever seen. People come to the workshop just to look at it. She signed every page with a little cherry.
textes.Cerise m'a interviewé pour son fanzine,: Cerise interviewed me for her fanzine upside down. She said it was to see the world like a falling juggler. I answered every question upside down too. The interview was printed upside down. You have to flip the fanzine to read it. It's the most-read page.
Cerise interviewed me for her fanzine. To every question, I answered in centimetres. “Dad, what do you love? — Forty-two centimetres.” She published the interview with a tape measure drawn around it. People found it very deep.
textes.Cerise m'a interviewé pour « La Cerise s: Cerise interviewed me for “The Cherry on the Zine”. I told her about my gig on the moon, in 1979, with astronauts moshing in slow motion. She wrote it all down, then added “made up” in pencil in the margin. But she drew the moon with a mohawk. Now that's journalism.
textes.Cerise m'interviewe pour son fanzine et: Cerise interviews me for her fanzine and writes “made up” in the margin. She's smarter than all of us put together. And she has a superb pink mohawk.
textes.Cerise pose des questions comme moi je p: Cerise asks questions the way I hammer nails: one after another, nonstop. She's nine and has a newsroom up a tree. I built it. The newsroom. She built herself all on her own.
textes.Cerise, elle écrit des articles sur moi: Cerise writes articles about me in her zine. Only my falls. Never my wins. But if anyone makes fun of me at school, she's the first one to shout.
textes.Cerise. La cabane tient bien ?: Cerise. Is the treehouse holding up?
textes.Certainement pas. Bonne journée optimisé: Certainly not. Have an optimised day.
textes.Certaines nuits très calmes, la musique: On some very calm nights, the music from down below drifts up to us. A guitar on a terrace, a violin in a tavern, someone singing off-key in a rowing boat. I play along, very softly. They don't know they're playing a duet with a Lumen. I've done hundreds. My favourites are the most off-key.
textes.Certaines nuits, les rêves de Lulu monte: Some nights Lulu's dreams rise so strongly that all of Yggdrasil's leaves shake in rhythm. Perlée's drops fall, Zéphyr complains, Noisette dances. Ever since, up here, when the Tree starts tapping out the beat, we simply say: “Lulu's asleep.”
textes.Certaines… La prudence du chercheur ! Il: Some… The caution of a true researcher! One must sort, compare, doubt. Then, one day, stop doubting. I'd gladly take you onto my team. It has one member: me.
textes.Certains matins, je vais au Bois de Cend: Some mornings, I go to the Ash Wood, to the south-east, to pick mushrooms that glow. The wood is gentle, but it looks the same everywhere: black trees, ember leaves… Little Pépin says the glowing mushrooms make paths. For once, I think he's right.
textes.Ces Lumens, là-haut, n'ont jamais vu de: Those Lumens up there had never seen a cat. They look at me as if I were a queen. They're right.
textes.Ces bijoux de boulons, au marché, j'en v: Those bolt jewels at the market, I wanted one. But my neighbour's watching me. I'll come back tomorrow.
textes.Ces bus, c'étaient de vieux bus d'école: These buses were old yellow school buses, abandoned. I fixed them one by one. Now people sleep in them when there are too many folk for the festival. Well… when there was a festival.
Those dogs in bandanas… how vulgar. A true punk needs no bandana. He has the attitude.
textes.Ces chouquettes… On dirait qu'elles ont: These sugar puffs… You'd think they'd been baked by a very kind cloud.
textes.Ces crocodiles… je peux t'aider ?: Those crocodiles… can I help you?
textes.Ces derniers temps, je vois Tobias passe: Lately, I see Tobias heading to the dock at night, with a shuttered lantern and his pot of tar. I asked him what he was up to. He said: “Nothing.” I didn't push. When a caulker says “nothing” at midnight, he's caulking something that matters.
textes.Ces fraises géantes de Flora… J'en ai co: Those giant strawberries of Flora's… I cut one for the whole family. There's some left for tomorrow.
textes.Ces lumières dans les grottes ? Mes homm: Those lights in the caves? My men. They're searching. Without the map, they're searching blind.
textes.Ces pierres levées, au nord du village…: Those standing stones, north of the village… It wasn't the elves who raised them. Someone older still.
textes.Ces rues qui montent en lacets ! Parfait: These zigzagging streets! Perfect for training! My cape prefers straight streets.
textes.Ces temps-ci, Fañch me voit passer au ba: Lately, Fañch sees me going by the basin at night, with my lantern. He asked me what I was up to. I said: “Nothing.” He didn't push. Next day, there was a new tar pot in front of the workshop, with a note: “For nothing.” I don't know what he knows. With Fañch, you never know.
textes.Cet arbre porte une entaille : il s'abat: This tree bears a notch: it can be felled… with an axe.
textes.Cet hiver, elle m'a soigné la toux à une: This winter she treated my cough on one condition: one story per spoonful of syrup. By the sixth spoonful, I wasn't coughing at all. I coughed on purpose for the seventh story. And the eighth. And the ninth. She knew perfectly well. She still got the spoon out.
This winter, I'm changing the keel.
This item will come in handy later.
textes.Cette Ysaé, du marché… Elle s'arrête dev: That Ysaé, from the market… She stops in front of the bottom shaft and listens to the music, tapping her foot. I pretend not to see. She pretends not to know I see. We get along very well that way.
textes.Cette année, Abdellah a trouvé un nid de: This year, Abdellah found a seagulls' nest in the mouth of the third cannon. Three eggs. I forbade anyone to touch it. Caïd's orders. The third cannon wasn't polished this year: it's a little green, and it's occupied. The guards call it “the nursery”. I pretend not to hear.
textes.Cette année, Gérard a pris trois cents p: This year, Gérard took three hundred holiday photos. Two are sharp: a pelican and his own thumb. I looked at every single one, in the evening on the balcony. He asked me “Lovely, eh?” every time. I said yes. Around the two hundredth, he fell asleep on my shoulder. I watched him sleep. That was sharp.
textes.Cette année, c'est sûr. Au troisième cid: This year, for certain. On the third round, we'll set the date.
textes.Cette année, dans la gueule du troisième: This year, in the mouth of the third cannon, there was a seagulls' nest. Three eggs. I raised my rag, the caïd raised his hand: “Nobody touches it.” The third one stayed green all year. The guards call it “the nursery”. I say it's the most useful cannon on the Skala.
textes.Cette année, elle a ajouté : « Venu d'au: This year, she added: “Come from beyond the seas.” I shrugged: beyond the seas, there's nothing but tourists. The next day, an English lord walked into my shop and bowed to my jar of figs. He's come back every day since. I draw no conclusions from that. None.
textes.Cette année, j'ai ajouté une petite chos: This year, I added a little something: “come from beyond the seas”. Colette shrugged, as usual. Shortly after, an English lord walked into her grocery to buy a jar of figs from her. He comes back every day. Colette acts as if nothing's going on. But she's changed her apron.
textes.Cette année, je lui ai demandé du chêne: This year, I asked her for highland oak. She answered: “The shepherds sell it for its weight in gold, Tobias.” I answered: “Then the hull will hold for its weight in gold, Admiral.” She ended up paying. Half. I plugged half the holes. She didn't find it funny. Neither did I, mind you.
textes.Cette année, je vise loin de l'horloge !: This year, I'm aiming well away from the clock!
textes.Cette botte… c'est celle de Barnabé ! Je: This boot… it's Barnabé's! I'd know it anywhere, I resoled it myself. I'll buy it for {prix} coins. He'll never see it again. HA!
textes.Cette canne… c'est moi qui l'ai taillée,: That rod… I carved it myself, twenty-two years ago, on the deck of the Stubborn Seagull. Barnabé gave it to you? The thief.
textes.Cette carte montre une île qui n'existe: This map shows an island that doesn't exist. Or not yet.
textes.Cette chanson parle d'un dirigeable amou: This song is about an airship in love with a cloud. It ends in rain.
textes.Cette fenêtre va disparaître dans 3… 2…: This window will disappear in 3… 2… (no, it's staying).
textes.Cette fois ! Et si on la faisait sur tro: This time! What if we made it a three-day race, Pépin?
textes.Cette fois, je cours plus vite. Peut-êtr: This time, I'll run faster. Perhaps.
textes.Cette fois, je vais te faire peur pour d: This time, I'm going to scare you for real!
textes.Cette jeune Ysaé, avec ses cheveux bleus: That young Ysaé, with her blue hair… Hmm. Not very regulation. But she always greets me politely, and her jewellery is superb. I'm an open-minded Burgomaster. I'm practising.
textes.Cette jeune Ysaé, du marché, avec ses ch: That young Ysaé, from the market, with her blue hair and her bolt jewellery… Ahem. It's not very regulation. But I saw a brooch on her stall, shaped like a little Column… If you see her, don't tell her I looked at it. Twice.
textes.Cette nuit, il y avait une étoile qui cl: Last night, there was a star winking over the Lighthouse. Professor Lunette was all excited.
textes.Cette nuit-là, les pirates comptaient le: That night, the pirates were counting their sacks of “salt”, and she, the smallest, was hiding behind a barrel. Skinny as a herring, eyes too big, fifteen years old. I put a bowl of harira in her hands. She emptied it without taking a breath. Then she licked the bowl. I never forgot her. Nor she me, it seems.
textes.Cette semaine, Kevin a sauvé trois touri: This week, Kevin rescued three tourists. The first one really was drowning. The second was floating on his back, eyes closed, singing. The third was looking for his glasses on the bottom, standing up: the water came up to his belly button. Kevin brought all three back onto the sand at a run. He put three crosses on his board. I said: “One and a half.”
textes.Cette semaine, je danse. L'Atlantide att: This week, I'm dancing. Atlantis can wait.
textes.Cette semaine-là, l'équipage a mangé des: That week, the crew ate sardines for breakfast, in soup at noon, grilled in the evening, and on Sunday in a cake. A sardine cake! The captain swore he'd make me walk the plank. He didn't: he had seconds of the cake. Since then, I buy everything nobody wants, “at sneeze prices”.
textes.Cette écervelée de Flammèche laisse ses: That scatterbrain Flammèche lets her puppies run all over the place. One of them sleeps in my watering can. I didn't chase it out. It snores. It's sweet. But don't tell Flammèche.
textes.Cette île ? Une jungle, {surnom}. De la: This island? A jungle, {surnom}. A real one. Those big pale trees over there are kapok trees. They're older than my socks.
textes.Cette île a une âme, voyageur. Écoute la: This island has a soul, traveller. Listen to the bell, look at the lighthouse, and you'll feel it.
textes.Cette île est la plus grande de l'archip: This island is the biggest in the archipelago. My grandfather said it had a heart of stone, and that this heart was worth more than all the treasures in the world. He said a lot of things, after the rum.
textes.Ceux-là, ce sont les fées qui les font p: Those ones, the fairies grow them. One bite, and hop, you wake up above the clouds.
textes.Ceux-là, si. Tu ne les écoutes pas, c'es: These ones do. You just don't listen to them, that's all.
Anyone can propose, anyone can vote. Even visitors, once a day, at the ballot box by the entrance. It's a very old law of Séraphin's: “Whoever climbs all the way up here deserves to be heard.”
textes.Chacune de mes tomates a un nom. Bologna: Every one of my tomatoes has a name. Bolognese, Napoletana, Arrabbiata, Little-Sauce, Madame-Ketchup… When we pick them, I say goodbye to them. It sounds silly. But they taste better when you've said goodbye.
textes.Chak ! Tes plumes jaunes tiennent ?: Chak! Are your yellow feathers holding up?
textes.Chak a cassé deux de mes pots avec sa ba: Chak broke two of my pots with his ball. He says it was the ball. The ball doesn't play by itself! I serve him anyway. With one finger of froth. No more.
textes.Chak dit qu'il est le meilleur joueur de: Chak says he's the best player on the island. Well, in Yaxché. He's boastful, loud, and very funny. And he has the most beautiful yellow feathers in the village. I'm the one who sewed them on.
textes.Chak m'a donné sa toute première balle,: Chak gave me his very first ball, the one his dad made for him. It's as big as a mango and as hard as a stone. I sleep with it! I've got bruises everywhere, like a real player. Mum isn't happy. Chak says it's the path of champions.
textes.Chak parle beaucoup. Il crie quand il jo: Chak talks a lot. He shouts when he plays. The game hears him all the way to the volcano. He calls me Balam-Who-Misses. I don't miss everything. I proved it.
textes.Chak s'entraîne au jeu de balle même la: Chak practises the ball game even at night. He broke two of Ix Chab's pots. She chased him all the way to the Cenote.
Chak calls himself the best player on the island. He also says I became an astronomer because of a ball to the head. It's not true. I was already an astronomer. The ball just confirmed the stars.
textes.Chak se vante de pouvoir battre les Seig: Chak boasts that he could beat the Lords of Xibalba. You don't joke about the Lords of Death. He plays well, I admit. He talks badly, I observe.
textes.Chak, c'est le meilleur joueur de balle: Chak is the best ball player in Yaxché! And on the whole island! Well, in Yaxché. He gave me his first ball. When I grow up, I'll be like him. But better. I don't tell him that, though.
textes.Chak, le joueur de balle, dit qu'il pour: Chak the ball player says he could beat the Lords of Xibalba. Chak says a lot of things. He took a ball to the head as a kid.
Chak. Your ball stays away from my pots.
textes.Chak. Toujours prêt à défier Xibalba ?: Chak. Still ready to challenge Xibalba?
textes.Chambre sept… non, elle est prise. Chamb: Room seven… no, it's taken. Room nine, sea view. Good night.
textes.Champion à seize ans : une coupe en bois: Champion at sixteen: a cup carved from mother-oak wood, my first. Then a second, then a third. Two years ago, Éclair was leading up to the root bend. She slipped on a wet root. I jumped right over her without stopping, and I won. That's racing. Hop hop. That's racing.
textes.Champs de Blé Dur\nIci pousse le blé des:
Durum Wheat Fields
This is where pasta wheat grows.
No pasta without wheat, no wheat without sun.
textes.Chante-le pendant que je pétris, ça lui: Sing it while I knead; it'll do it good.
textes.Chante-moi la basse, Nausicaa. Celle de: Sing me the low tide, Nausicaa. My mother's.
textes.Chanter faux, j'espère ? C'est mieux, fa: Off-key, I hope? It's better off-key.
textes.Chanter la chanson de ma mère sur la Gra: To sing my mother's song on the Great Stage, with the camp drums behind us. In the sun. Even if I get the tempo wrong.
textes.Chanter ma chanson à moi, à la prochaine: To sing my own song at the next Dawn festival, from the first word to the last. And to have Caelan accompany me without running off. Or let him run off, why not. This time, I'll know what to do.
textes.Chanter un jour à la surface, au soleil,: To sing one day at the surface, in the sun, and hear the whale answer from close by. And for Triton to be there. Not on watch. Just there.
textes.Chanter, une seule fois, un grand air d': To sing, just once, a great opera aria in the square. Django on guitar, all of Port-Azur on the café terraces, and nobody laughing. Nobody! Not even Colette.
textes.Chapitre trois, Mademoiselle. C'est très: Chapter three, Miss. It's very dense.
textes.Chaque année, Aristide m'invite à la tri: Every year, Aristide invites me onto the platform at the harbour festival. I bring my tape measure. During his speech, I unroll it, slowly, to measure. At the end, I whisper to him: “Two minutes too long.” This year he cut it down. I measured anyway. A minute and a half too long. He's improving.
textes.Chaque année, Grimli et Borin viennent m: Every year, Grimli and Borin come and ask me to judge their beards. I make them wait side by side, in the full wind, for as long as it takes to milk three goats. Then I walk around them, tug a hair here, a hair there, and say: “I win.” Croâ applauds. They leave together, furious.
textes.Chaque année, Monsieur Prosper vient me: Every year, Monsieur Prosper comes and asks me if I want to sell the lighthouse. He says he has a buyer. I say no. He waxes his moustache, looks at the view, and says: “You're right. It's exceptional.” Then he goes back down the hundred and forty steps. He counts one fewer every time. He says the lighthouse is shrinking. He's the one getting older.
textes.Chaque année, Orsik m'apporte la facture: Every year, Orsik brings me the bill for the crown. I read it, fold it in four and tuck it into my beard. I have ninety. Ulfa says my beard crackles when I walk. That's the sound of debt. A king never forgets. He files.
textes.Chaque année, au Diable Repu, nous faiso: Every year, at the Diable Repu, we have an arm-wrestling match. One year, she won. Everyone shouted, and I cried. Not because I'd lost: because she was so happy. I told her I'd let her win. That's not quite true. It's not quite false either.
textes.Chaque année, au Diable Repu, on fait un: Every year, at the Diable Repu, Gorgoth and I have an arm-wrestling match. The whole tavern places bets. Once, I won. Gorgoth said he'd let me win. Then he cried. I still don't know if it was from losing or from being happy for me. With him, both are possible.
textes.Chaque année, au Grand Troc, quand la ch: Every year, at the Great Swap, when the chain reaches me, I hold out coins. Two lovely coins. And every year, my uncle pretends to faint, a paw on his forehead. The whole Circle applauds. Then he gets up, gives me back my coins and hands me a pebble. The chain goes on. It's never broken because of me.
textes.Chaque année, au concours, Hugues pleure: Every year, at the contest, Hugues cries and doesn't choose. One year, I put a bit of her pie into my frog pastry, just to see. He tasted it, closed his eyes and said: “This is paradise.” I never confessed. Rissole knows. She winked at me. We're even.
textes.Chaque année, au printemps, Colette s'as: Every year, in spring, Colette sits at my table, puts down her coins without counting them and says: “Well?” I predict a great love for her. She shrugs and leaves. Fifteen years running. It's the only price she's never argued over. A grocer who doesn't haggle, traveller: now that's a sign.
textes.Chaque année, j'invite Cendrin à parler: Every year, I invite Cendrin to talk to the new pupils about the patience of fire. He talks for ten minutes, very slowly. Then I spend an hour explaining what he meant. The pupils think he talks too little, and I far too much. I believe they're right on both counts.
textes.Chaque année, je l'invite à la tribune d: Every year, I invite him onto the platform at the harbour festival. He comes with his tape measure. During my speech, I see him unrolling the tape, discreetly, in time with my sentences. At the end, he whispers: “Two minutes too long, Mr Mayor.” Last year, a minute and a half. I'm improving.
textes.Chaque année, je lui demande de m'accomp: Every year, I ask him to accompany me for one song, just one, at the harbour festival. Every year, he refuses. And every year, when it's time to cut the ribbon, I shout: “Django, music!” And he plays. He's never missed once. That, you see, is friendship. He'll never admit it.
textes.Chaque année, je monte au phare pour lui: Every year, I climb up to the lighthouse to offer to resell it for him. I have no buyer. I go up for the view. And to see him smile when he says no. He pours me a tea, and we look at the sea without talking. Last time, he said: “Prosper, you're a crook.” I said: “I know.” He said: “Thank you.” It was the best sale of my life.
textes.Chaque année, je présente au roi la fact: Every year, I present the king with the bill for the crown. Every year, he reads it, folds it in four, says “A king never forgets”, and tucks it into his beard. There are ninety of them in that beard. One day, I'll cut it off while he sleeps. To get my bills back.
textes.Chaque année, l'air de rien, je demande: Every year, casual as you like, I ask Dagna if Sigrun's eating properly up there. She says yes. I say: “Sigrun? Never heard of her.” And I scuttle off to the cellar before she sees my face. Dagna usually sees everything. But this time, she says nothing. That's why I love her.
textes.Chaque année, la première sardine de la: Every year, Driss brings me the first sardine of the season at the end of the jetty. He lays it on the stone, next to my line. He says nothing. I say nothing. He leaves. Fatima grills it that same evening. It's the only sardine I bring home without going by Zohra's.
textes.Chaque année, le jour anniversaire de ma: Every year, on the anniversary of my failed resignation, the Baron makes me a pancake. It's always burnt on one side and raw on the other. I eat the whole thing, every year, without a word. Last year he made a perfect one. By accident. He was so disappointed he cried. I told him it was a little raw. He was delighted.
textes.Chaque année, le jour anniversaire de mo: Every year, on the anniversary of the day I arrived, I bring Léon a punch aboard the Swallow. We drink it on deck, without talking, looking at the village across the water. He shows me my return ticket, still tucked inside his compass. I tell him: “Keep it a little longer.” That's five punches now.
textes.Chaque année, le jour de mon anniversair: Every year, on my birthday, it snows. Only over my house. A little grey cloud, right over my roof, all day long. I know it's him. He says it's the weather. The weather doesn't know my birthday, Borée!
textes.Chaque année, le lendemain de la fête du: Every year, the day after the harbour festival, I offer him a rematch, in front of witnesses. I play badly on purpose: I roll into the gutter, I shoot into the plane trees. He wins. He shouts: “See! I was the best!” And off he goes, happy. It's the best politics I know.
textes.Chaque année, le soir où Gaspard n'est p: Every year, on the evening Gaspard didn't come home, I play his favourite song, an old whaler's lament. Very slowly. The first year, I played it without knowing. Mama put down her tea towel, listened to the end, then brought me a soup without a word. I understood. I play it every year. She's never asked me to.
textes.Chaque année, nous faisons un concours d: Every year, we hold a shouting contest at the port. Usually, Hurla wins. Last year, I shouted “MACKEREL!” so loud that a ship out at sea thought it was being called and turned back. I won. Hurla didn't say a word all day. It was the quietest day in the history of Pandémonia.
textes.Chaque année, on fait la Course de la Ba: Every year, we hold the Balafre Race: round the island, quay to quay. Last year, his bowsprit got caught in my shrouds on the last turn. We came in stuck together like two crabs. Each of us says he won. Mama Grog settled it: both captains buy the round. We're still paying.
textes.Chaque année, on fait un concours de cri: Every year, Moloka and I hold a shouting contest at the port. Usually, I win. Last year, she shouted “MACKEREL!” so loud that a ship out at sea thought it was being called and turned back. She won. I didn't say a word for a whole day. Everyone thought I was ill.
textes.Chaque année, pour l'anniversaire de Neb: Every year, for Nebet's birthday, Mérit makes a honey cake shaped like Miou, with the crooked ear. She spends the whole morning on it. She says it's for Nebet. But I've seen her set aside the best ear. For herself. Mérit has always loved ears.

Every year, for Nebet's birthday, I make a honey cake shaped like Miou, crooked ear and all. The first year, Nebet refused to eat it: “You don't eat Miou!” Now she starts with the tail, so Miou won't feel anything. Tiyi cries with laughter every time.
textes.Chaque année, pour l'anniversaire de not: Every year, on the anniversary of the day we met, Tic makes me a new backwards watch. And every year, I put it in the Bazaar's window, for thirty coins. He walks past, puts his hand on his heart and cries scandal. Then he comes back in the evening to help me wind it. They all sell. Except the first one: I wear it.
textes.Chaque année, pour mon anniversaire, Sér: Every year, for my birthday, Séraphine leaves a ladder in front of the library, with a ribbon. Forty ladders in forty years. I give them all to Mathurin, who turns them into planks for the jetty. She says she walks all over my birthdays. I say it's the most useful of her presents.
textes.Chaque année, pour son anniversaire, il: Every year, on her birthday, it snows over her house. Only her house. A little cloud, all day long. She thinks it's me. I have nothing to say about that. The weather is a fickle thing. Hm.
textes.Chaque année, à l'anniversaire de notre: Every year, on the anniversary of the day we met, I make her a new backwards watch. And every year, she puts it in the Bazaar's window. I protest, for form's sake: “My love watch, in a shop window!” She says love is for sharing. The first one, she never sold. She wears it on her wrist.
textes.Chaque année, à la fin de la saison, Hec: Every year, at the end of the season, Hector and I redo the sums for the sign on a corner of the counter: how many fizzes, how many evenings, how many mugs. It's been paid off for twelve years. Every year, we look at the result, we look at each other, and we keep quiet. I pour him a fizz. “On the sign.”
textes.Chaque année, à la fête de l'Aube, je lu: Every year, at the Dawn festival, I ask her for a dance. Like the first time. She says yes. We both dance badly, we tread on each other's feet. Last year, a turnip escaped from my basket and crossed the dance floor. Germaine caught it one-handed without missing a step. Like the first time. I nearly cried. Like Hugues.
textes.Chaque année, à la fête de l'Aube, le Ba: Every year, at the Dawn festival, the Baron and I dance the old adventurers' dance together. He doesn't know the steps. Neither do I. We make it up. Last year, his hat flew off in the middle of the dance. We chased it all the way to the fountain, still dancing. The whole town thought it was part of the dance.
textes.Chaque année, à la fête de la Forge, il: Every year, at the Forge Festival, he raises his mug to me and shouts: “No hard feelings, Bramm!” Every year, I don't raise mine. That's a hundred and twenty festivals. He never tires of it. Neither do I.
textes.Chaque année, à la même date, j'envoie a: Every year, on the same date, I send the Professor a little card: “The book awaits you. No hurry.” I change one word each time, to see if he reads them. Last year, I wrote: “The book awaits you. It's getting wrinkles.” He answered with four pages on the wrinkles of books. I filed them.
textes.Chaque année, à la rentrée, Malachar m'i: Every year, at the start of term, Malachar invites me to talk to the new students about “the patience of fire”. I talk for ten minutes. He talks for an hour, to explain what I meant. The students fall asleep. So do I, a little. It's a fine tradition.
textes.Chaque après-midi, Germaine vient au mar: Every afternoon, Germaine comes to the market to criticise my apples. Once, she didn't come. I waited until evening. I found out she'd fallen in her yard and twisted her ankle. The next day, I sent Noisette to take her a basket of apples, without a note. She sent it back with a note: “Too red. Thank you.” I kept the note.
textes.Chaque après-midi, je lui apporte son th: Every afternoon I bring him his tea and we play draughts on an old carved board. He keeps a piece up his sleeve. I've seen it for twenty years: when he's losing, he scratches his wrist, and an extra piece appears on the board. I say nothing. Once, I counted: he had fourteen pieces. We each have twelve.
textes.Chaque arbre-maison a un nom. Celui d'Il: Every tree-house has a name. Ilyria's is called “Dawn-Thread”. Mine is called “Still-Standing”. It's an old elvish word.
textes.Chaque automne, Mère Morille et moi peso: Every autumn, Mother Morille and I weigh our pumpkins. Last year, mine weighed ninety-eight kilos. Hers, a hundred. I suspect she counted a bit of moss, maybe even the caravan. She says I misread the scales. We asked for a referee. It was Bardane. She declared both pumpkins beautiful.
textes.Chaque automne, Tobias monte sur mon toi: Every autumn, Tobias climbs up on my roof, well, on my boat's keel, and plugs the cracks with hot tar. The whole beach smells of tar. I hand him a mackerel, he says “no need”, he takes it anyway. Thirty years now. Thirty mackerel. I owe him nothing, he owes me nothing. It's perfect.
textes.Chaque automne, je recalfate le toit de: Every autumn, I recaulk Fañch's roof, well, the keel of his boat. He hands me a mackerel, I say “no need”, I take it. One autumn, he handed me a lobster. I got scared: I thought he was ill. He'd just caught too many lobsters. I ate it anyway, warily.
textes.Chaque chose en son temps, chaque couleu: Everything in its time, every colour in its place.
textes.Chaque dimanche, Gilles vient faire la s: Every Sunday, Gilles comes to nap at the temple, standing by the door. He says it's the best place on the island to sleep. One day, some of the faithful took him for a statue of a saint and laid flowers at his feet. He woke up with daisies in his boots. He kept them. He says they smell nice.
textes.Chaque dimanche, je lui porte des biscui: Every Sunday, I take him gear cookies. I look at his roof, I count his eyebrows, and I ask him how “the Big One” is coming along. He answers “soon!” with shining eyes. I always leave a little worried. And a little proud to have been his pupil. Mostly proud.
textes.Chaque dimanche, je m'assois au premier: Every Sunday, I sit in the front row of the temple. When Clotaire falls asleep in the middle of his sermon, I get up, walk to the altar, give him a little nudge with my elbow, and go back to my seat. He picks up the sentence where he left off. The faithful aren't surprised anymore. They call it “Philomène's elbow”. It's almost a prayer.
textes.Chaque fin d'année, je laisse une boutei: At the end of every year, I leave a bottle of lamp oil at the foot of the lighthouse door. No note, no ribbon. The next morning, the bottle's gone, and that evening Anselme gives me three flashes instead of two. Once a year. It's his way of saying thank you. Or good health. Or both.
textes.Chaque fin d'été, au Cercle, je mène le: Every end of summer, at the Circle, I lead the Great Swap: the whole village swaps in a ring, and the chain mustn't break. Twenty years it held! Last year, it broke between Caramel and Trèfle: the sardine for the carrot bread. Heh heh… I laughed. I didn't sleep. And then my niece Grelot sells for coins, and that fox Roux taunts me. A hard life, my friend.
textes.Chaque fois qu'elle invente un dragon da: Every time she invents a dragon in her stories, I pour her another chocolate. One evening, she invented seven. She slept at the tavern.
textes.Chaque fois qu'il parle de la porte, je: Every time he talks about the gate, I set my compass on his map, on Stoneheart. He draws around it. The other evening, I looked more closely: around my compass, he'd written, very small: “Here, the Admiral keeps watch.” I haven't moved the compass since.
textes.Chaque fois qu'il raconte le pirate et l: Every time he tells the tale of the pirate and the treasure in the caves, he says the pirate had a black beard. So I say: “Red.” The whole halqa turns towards me. I say nothing more. He carries on, and he never corrects it. I think he gets it wrong on purpose. I pretend not to believe it. We've been playing that game for sixty years.
textes.Chaque fois qu'un caravanier poli loge c: Every time a polite caravan trader stays with me, I send him to buy a dish from Halima: “Go and see my niece, she has lovely pottery.” She spots them straight away, by their son-in-law look. She sells them the heaviest dish on the stall and sends them back. Twenty-three caravan traders, twenty-three dishes sold, not one wedding. At least she's doing business.
textes.Chaque fois qu'un caravanier un peu poli: Every time a caravan driver with half-decent manners stays at the Fondouk, my aunt has me come over “to deliver a dish”. Once it was a salt merchant, very pushy, who wanted to marry me that very evening. I took the dish I was delivering and dropped it. On purpose. He ran away. My aunt made me pay for the dish. It was worth the price.
textes.Chaque fois qu'un voyageur part vers Ram: Every time a traveller sets off for Ramure, with Mbarek's camels or by Zéphyr, I give him a story for Tilleul. They tell me he tells our night differently: that he's the one who walked three days to my square. Maybe he's right. A story can happen twice. He's the one who taught me that.
textes.Chaque fois que Ferraille me donne un sa: Every time Ferraille gives me a bag of parts, I give him a wheel for his dragon. Brindezingue has eleven now. I asked him why a dragon needed wheels. He said: “For the day he wants to leave.” I gave him the twelfth the next day.
textes.Chaque fois que Kevin repêche quelqu'un,: Every time Kevin fishes someone out, I tell all my customers. “You know who saved the gentleman in the hat? My son!” In the time it takes to weigh a sardine, I've already told three rescues. Kevin says I exaggerate. I don't exaggerate. I round up. It's not the same.
textes.Chaque fois que Nimiel tombe, Miriel arr: Every time Nimiel falls, Miriel gets to the shop before her, running. She knows the way to my stool by heart. I give her a cup of tea too: the mother often needs more looking after than the little one.
textes.Chaque fois que Théo passe devant ma bou: Every time Théo walks past my shop, I give him a painted shell. Free! Me! He's counted them: eleven. He lines them up in front of his sandcastles like soldiers. The other day he asked me: “When I've got a hundred, will you give me a kite?” That kid has a head for business. I'll hire him in ten years.
textes.Chaque fois que j'apprends un nouveau mo: Every time I teach the piano a new piece, Philibert is the first to hear it. In the evening, on the promenade, I play him the cylinder in my little test box. He closes his eyes, listens to the very end, and always says: “I hadn't thought of that.” Coming from him, that's the finest compliment there is.
textes.Chaque fois que je cherche mes lunettes,: Every time I'm looking for my glasses, Petit-Pierre comes running and hands them to me. He never says where he found them. One day, I asked him. He said: “On your head.” I didn't believe him. He added: “You never look on your head.” It's true. He's very clever, that boy.
textes.Chaque fois que je parle d'ouvrir la Por: Every time I talk about opening the Gate of the Four Seals, the Admiral sets her compass down on my map, right on Stoneheart, and says: “Closed gates are often closed for a reason, Le Goff.” Then she leaves. I draw around the compass. She leaves it there for a very long time.
textes.Chaque fois que je parle du fantôme du q: Every time I mention the ghost on the fourth floor, Monsieur Edmond goes white and says “Nonsense, mademoiselle, back to work.” Very fast. Too fast. I think he's scared of ghosts. A man his age! I offered him a night light. He dropped his register.
textes.Chaque fois que je passe devant la bouti: Every time I go past the shop, Victor gives me a painted shell. A blue one, a red one, one with a star. I've got eleven! I counted them all by myself, without saying twenty-thousand. I line them up in front of my castle, like soldiers. The blue one's the boss.
textes.Chaque fois que je raconte le pirate et: Every time I tell the tale of the pirate and the treasure in the caves, I say the pirate had a black beard. And every time, from the front row, Fatima says: “Red.” The whole halqa turns towards her. She adds nothing. I could say red. I don't say red. If I said red, she'd never say anything again.
textes.Chaque fois que je raconte mon dragon à: Every time I tell a newcomer about my dragon, on the Great Square, Philomène walks past behind me and goes “baaa” very softly. The newcomer doesn't get it. I do. I lose my thread, I stammer, and she sits down on her bench, smiling. It's been going on for forty years. I've never finished my dragon on the square without a “baaa”.
textes.Chaque fois que je rate un sort devant e: Every time I mess up a spell in front of her, the archmage pulls a little notebook out of her sleeve and writes in it. I think it's the list of everything I've broken. It must be three hundred pages by now. One day, she'll hand me the bill. I hope she lets me pay in instalments.
textes.Chaque fois que je vais au quai, Léon me: Every time I go to the quay, Léon lets me ring the Swallow's bell for departure. Once I rang it too early, and the boat left without three gentlemen. They were running with their suitcases! Léon said “The captain decides.” But he went back for them anyway.
Every time, I say: “I leave tomorrow.” She answers: “Good.” The next day, I don't leave. She doesn't ask anything. In the evening she brings my tea up at midnight, as if nothing had happened. Fifteen years now. At the oasis, the camels must think I'm dead. Or married.
textes.Chaque histoire, je la paie une noisette: I pay one hazelnut for each story. That's the price! I put it on his knee at the start. And at the end I take it back as I leave, because there's never an end, so the story isn't finished, so it isn't paid for. Grandpa says I'd make a very good tanuki.
textes.Chaque hiver, Borée vient me remercier p: Every winter, Borée comes to thank me for the bundle of twisted wood he finds at his door. I've never brought him any wood! The first time, I said “don't mention it”, out of politeness. Now it's too late to tell the truth. I really wonder who it is. Someone who gets up early. And has warm hands.
textes.Chaque hiver, quelqu'un dépose un fagot: Every winter, someone leaves a bundle of twisted wood at my door, before dawn. It can only be Mathurin: he's the only one who gets up before me. I thanked him. He looked surprised, said “don't mention it”, then left very quickly. He's modest. That's a virtue.
textes.Chaque inventeur de Cliquetis rate une i: Every inventor in Cliquetis botches one invention out of two. I buy up the failures. They're the most beautiful: they tried.
textes.Chaque jeudi après-midi, Pauline s'assoi: Every Thursday afternoon, Pauline sits at my table with two orange-blossom cakes, one for her, one for me. I read her cards, for free. She tells me about her week at the hotel, for free too. Nobody pays, and everybody wins. It's the most honest business on the promenade.
textes.Chaque jeudi, Madame Rita me tire les ca: Every Thursday, Madame Rita reads my cards, and every Thursday I draw the journey card. Always the same one! She says it's fate. I think the card's got a dog-ear. But it makes me happy anyway: one day, I'll leave. Maybe as far as the end of the street. To open my guesthouse.
textes.Chaque jeudi, Tiburce s'assoit dans la s: Every Thursday, Tiburce sits in the steam room, eyes closed, and says his horns are breathing. One day, I explained that horns don't breathe. He opened one eye and replied: “Yours, perhaps not.” Since then, I keep a separate scented towel for him. He says his horns prefer it.
textes.Chaque jeudi, je vais faire respirer mes: Every Thursday, I go and let my horns breathe in the steam of the Baths. One day, Bulle told me horns didn't breathe. I replied: “Yours, perhaps not.” He laughed for ten minutes. Since then, he keeps a scented towel aside for me. He says my horns prefer it. They do prefer it.
textes.Chaque jour à midi, Asmodin aligne mes b: Every day at noon, Asmodin lines up my brioches on the counter and measures them one by one with his silver ruler. There's always a crooked one. He frowns. I look innocent. One day, he pretended not to see it. So the next day, I made two crooked ones. He sighed very loudly. It was almost a laugh.
textes.Chaque jour à midi, je viens chercher le: Every day at noon, I come to fetch the palace brioches. I measure them with my silver ruler: they must all be the same height.
