textes.Chut… Quatre mille deux cent douze allum: Shh… Four thousand two hundred and twelve matches: the Great Column, at one-thousandth scale. Only the last one is missing, right at the top. My hands are shaking a little… Do you want to place it?
textes.Chut… Quel souffle, en pleine nuit ! Ell: Shh… What a gust, in the middle of the night! She'd have wanted to give it to you herself. Here, very quietly: the station's umbrella of honour. When you open it, the propeller spins. Not in here: we'd wake her.
textes.Chut… Quel souffle, en pleine nuit ! Vou: Shh… What a gust, in the middle of the night! You already have a propeller umbrella? Then, very quietly: the station's feather of honour, a wind feather. Doctor Aurèle loves these feathers.
textes.Chut… Quelqu'un dort. Et il ronfle comme: Shh… Someone's sleeping. And snoring like a forge bellows.
textes.Chut… Rien ne bouge : ni les carillons d: Shh… Nothing moves: not the silver chimes under the ceiling, nor the fine strings of the harp by the big window. “Go on, open it,” an old lady smiles. “Our musician is waiting outside.”
textes.Chut… Sur les fleurs de la serre, des di: Shh… On the greenhouse flowers, dozens of butterflies are sleeping, wings closed. On the sofa, a child is sleeping too.
textes.Chut… Tempête. Dans un verre d'eau, sûre: Shh… Storm. In a teacup, I expect. I'll open the umbrella anyway.
textes.Chut… Trois enfants dorment sur des futo: Shh… Three children sleep on futons of every color. All you hear is the wind on the canvas, and a mother knitting.
textes.Chut… Un enfant dort sur le canapé. Au-d: Shh… A child is asleep on the sofa. Just above, a little cloud glows very softly, like a night light.
textes.Chut… Un enfant dort sur le tapis, à côt: Shh… A child is asleep on the rug, next to a giant kite. Someone is tying the last ribbons by lamplight.
textes.Chut… Un planeur blanc dort dans le salo: Shh… A white glider is sleeping in the living room, its wings reaching from wall to wall. In the cockpit, a child has fallen asleep, hands on the stick.
textes.Chut… Vous entendez ? La nuit, le vent j: Shh… Can you hear? At night, the wind plays more softly. Even the chimes speak in whispers.
textes.Chut… Vous entendez ? Rien. Normal : la: Shh… Do you hear that? Nothing. Of course not: the big window is shut, and the soloist is waiting outside.
textes.Chut… ah, c'est toi. Tu tombes bien : j': Shh… ah, it's you. Just in time: I need an opinion. Want to listen?
textes.Chut… elle se réveille. Deux paniers ?: Shh… she's just waking up. Two baskets?
textes.Chut… elle se réveille. Elle est un peu: Shh… she's waking up. She's a bit shy this morning.
Shh… it's going to pass right over us.
textes.Chut… je compte. Trois cent onze, trois: Shh… I'm counting. Three hundred and eleven, three hundred and twelve…
textes.Chut… je mesure le vent. … Voilà : il y: Shh… I'm measuring the wind. … Done: there is some. Hello!
textes.Chut… la pâte se repose. Bonsoir !: Shh… the dough is resting. Good evening!
textes.Chut… le ciel est en train de changer de: Shh… the sky's changing to another blue. Ah, done.
textes.Chut… le drone dort. Enfin, il fait semb: Shh… the drone's asleep. Well, it's pretending.
textes.Chut… le vent de nuit joue plus doucemen: Shh… the night wind plays more softly.
Shh… the wind has fallen asleep.
Shh… even the harp is asleep.
textes.Chut… ne bougez pas. Je vous regarde. Si: Shh… don't move. I'm looking at you. If you were a colour, which one would you be?
textes.Chut… ne bougez pas. La lumière est parf: Shh… don't move. The light is perfect. … There. Hello. Clémence, painter. Well, I try.
textes.Chut… on regarde les étoiles filantes. I: Shh… we're watching the shooting stars. Three have gone by. I made three wishes. The third was to have more wishes.
textes.Chut… regarde par la baie : le nuage, là: Shh… look out of the big window: that cloud there is shaped like a sugar puff.
textes.Chut… « La Berceuse du Sustentateur ». P: Shh… “The Levitator's Lullaby”. For the four big engines that hold us up in the air.
textes.Chut… « Le Nocturne pour Courant d'Air T: Shh… “The Nocturne for Shy Draught”. At night, the wind plays more softly.
textes.Chut… À cette heure-ci, on entend toute: Shh… At this hour, you can hear the whole island breathing.
textes.Chut… ça mord peut-être. Non. Bon. Je pê: Shh… maybe something's biting. No. Oh well. I'm fishing.
textes.Chuuut. Quelqu'un chantonne tout bas : «: Shhh. Someone is humming very softly: “Sleep, little hammer…”
textes.Chère Hortense ! Toujours fidèle au post: Dear Hortense! Ever faithful at your post!
textes.Chère Mama ! Un nouveau décret, aujourd': Dear Mama! A new decree today!
textes.Chère Vespérine ! Mon huile vous salue !: Dear Vespérine! My oil sends its regards!
textes.Cinq ! Cinq beaux dorés ! (Il les caress: Five! Five beautiful golden ones! (He strokes them one by one, like little kittens.) You caught them gently, I can see. Not a single bump. They just look a bit offended. They'll get over it. They always do.
textes.Cinq ! Et une paille pour le drapeau. La: Five! And a straw for the flag. The pink one!
Five! I'll need five half coconuts, then.
textes.Cinq ! J'ai acheté du liquide en plus !: Five! I bought extra bubble mix!
textes.Cinq beaux champignons ! Ils sentent la: Five lovely mushrooms! They smell of rain. Here, two sap potions, with my thanks. Don't drink them all at once.
textes.Cinq blagues des petits Moaïs: Five jokes from the little Moai
textes.Cinq cents mètres de corde de chanvre, e: Five hundred metres of hemp rope, tightly coiled. Each end is closed with a funny knot: the friendship knot, says Galet. The harder you pull, the tighter it holds.
Five hundred push-ups and scared of a sardine. My son, ladies!
textes.Cinq coquillages nacrés ! Ma collection: Five pearly shells! My collection is complete! Here, take my old compass, and a few coins. You've earned them, {surnom}!
textes.Cinq esprits, cinq cercles de champignon: Five spirits, five rings of white mushrooms, in the forest around the village. Only the lantern can catch them. The lantern, and patience.
textes.Cinq heures. Et le vent sera de suroît,: Five o'clock. And the wind'll be south-westerly, my lovely.
textes.Cinq pièces, mon chou. Même les hamacs,: Five coins, dear. Even hammocks cost money here. Especially the hammocks: they've seen things.
textes.Cinq secondes. Et pas vers les toits, ça: Five seconds. And not at the rooftops, they make me dizzy.
textes.Cinq sur dix. En cuisine, oui, c'est un: Five out of ten. In cooking, yes, it's a vegetable. Lentille would agree. But in botany, it's a fruit. Revise your botany.
textes.Cinq-Doigts ? Parce que j'ai cinq doigts: Cinq-Doigts — Five-Fingers? Because I've got five fingers on each hand. That's rare around here. Crochet has none on one side, Sans-Dents lost two at dice.
Five. And the right house, this time.
textes.Cinquante ans de mer. Mon père était ami: Fifty years at sea. My father was amin before me, and his father before him. In Tazira, they say the Brahims have salt instead of blood.
textes.Cinquante. Atchoum. C'est mon dernier mo: Fifty. Atchoo. That's my final word.
textes.Cinq… et tous intacts. Regarde comme ils: Five… and all intact. Look how they shine, even in broad daylight. Tonight, the bridges of Ramure will be blue like they used to be. You have a gentle heart, little one, and gentle hands too. Here: fox ears, sewn by Pivoine. Put them on, and all of Ramure will know you're one of us.
textes.Cipactli balaie tout de sa queue !: Cipactli sweeps everything away with its tail!
textes.Cipactli plonge… et resurgit ailleurs !: Cipactli dives… and resurfaces somewhere else!
textes.Cipactli s'effondre dans un grondement d: Cipactli collapses with a mountain's rumble. His body turns to stone, earth, roots… as on the first day, when the gods made the world from his body. On the altar at the back, a green feather begins to glow.
textes.Cirque des Os, au nord. Suivre le chemin: Bone Hollow, north. Follow path of stones.
textes.Citlali ! On recommence la course de l'a: Citlali! Shall we have another race like the other night?
Citlali! A flower for your desk.
textes.Citlali ! Votre codex se lit dans quel s: Citlali! Which way does your codex read, again?
textes.Citlali a été mon élève, et elle est dev: Citlali was my pupil, and she became better than me at reading codices. I don't say so in front of the pupils. Neither does she. She's polite. That's almost worse.
textes.Citlali dit que Tlaco apprend mieux que: Citlali says Tlaco learns better than me. It's true. He can already sit.
textes.Citlali et moi, on a grandi sur le même: Citlali and I grew up on the same canal. She read, I planted. She knows everything, she says things gently. She's teaching Pilli to read. Well, she's trying. Pilli sleeps.
textes.Citlali nous a demandé de dessiner notre: Citlali asked us to draw our animal. I drew Tlaco with loads of hair, like a big cloud. She asked me why. I said: so he won't be cold in Mictlan, later. She didn't say anything. She hung my drawing on the wall. It's the only drawing on the wall.
textes.Citlali sait tout, mais elle chante enco: Citlali knows everything, but she sings even better than she knows. We make songs for her pupils. She says I'm the best teacher in Aztlán. I can't even read.
textes.Citlali écrit avec des images, moi avec: Citlali writes with pictures, I write with signs. We argue about who's right, and we're both right. It's the most pleasant conversation on the island.
textes.Citlali, c'est ma maîtresse d'école. Ell: Citlali is my schoolteacher. She knows everything, even the stars. She says Tlaco learns better than me. It's true. He can already sit. So can I, but I prefer lying down.
textes.Citoyen ! C'est moi, votre gouverneur !: Citizen! It's me, your governor! The one you didn't know! Do you recognise me now? The tricorn!
textes.Citoyen d'honneur, ça se mérite ! Rendez: Honorary citizen, that has to be earned! Do favours for our residents: ten favours, and I'll hand you the key to the town in front of everyone, with a fanfare. Well, with Django.
Citizen {surnom}! Always a pleasure. Have you paid your taxes? … Ah, that's right, there are no taxes. Pity.
textes.Citoyen {surnom}, sondage officiel de la: Citizen {surnom}, official city poll: are you satisfied with your governor?
textes.Citoyenne ! Le vaisseau amiral sera prêt: Citizen! When will the flagship be ready?
textes.Clac ! Le bras du tourniquet tombe, la l: Clack! The turnstile arm drops, the lamp turns green, and the iron shutter sinks into the floor. “STAFF EXIT AUTHORISED. HAVE A GOOD DESCENT.” The service stairs lead to the Assembly Line.
textes.Clac ! Un grondement, et les deux poids: Clack! A rumble, and the two weights slide back to their starting places.
textes.Clac ! Une lampe s'allume au-dessus de l: Clack! A lamp lights up above the door… and above your head, something very heavy goes “crrrr”. RUN! (The alcoves are free.)
textes.Clac-clac-FLOP ! L'Alouette se déplie au: Clack-clack-FLOP! The Alouette unfolds above you in mid-fall… and the canvas billows out. You're gliding!
textes.Clair. Une étoile filante vers trois heu: Clear. A shooting star around three.
textes.Clairement ! Tu entends, le poisson ? Qu: Clearly! Hear that, fish? Somebody recognises you! … He's touched. So am I. A bit.
textes.Clapotis ! Tu as vu mes signaux hier ?: Clapotis! Did you see my signals yesterday?
textes.Clapotis m'a demandé si un bus pouvait f: Clapotis asked me if a bus could skateboard. I said no. He said: “Not yet.” I'm scared of what he'll come up with.
textes.Clapotis tombe de son skate toutes les d: Clapotis falls off his skateboard every two minutes! He gets back up every two minutes! He's the greatest drummer on the island without knowing it: he goes BOOM everywhere!
textes.Clapotis vient faire du skate sur la ram: Clapotis comes to skate on the ramp next to my buses. He's really good. He falls really hard too. I fix his wheels for free.
textes.Clapotis, il a un ciré jaune et un skate: Clapotis has a yellow raincoat and a skateboard. He's a bit silly sometimes, but he's nice. We send signals in the evening. It's a secret. Well… it was a secret.
textes.Clapotis, le petit de Rainville, vient f: Clapotis, the little one from Rainville, comes to skate on the ramp next to my buses. He's really good. He falls really hard too.
textes.Classe conseillée : aventurier. (La boul: Recommended class: adventurer. (The ball recommends that to everyone.)
textes.Clic : choisir • double-clic : utilise: Click: select  •  double-click: use  •  I / Tab / Esc: close
textes.Clic, clac, cliquetis ! L'hélice tourne,: Click, clack, cliquetis! The propeller turns, the chain sings. Pedal, and up she goes! A little. It's not a rocket, it's an Alouette.
textes.Clic, clic, clic… Une grand-mère tricote: Click, click, click… A grandmother knits in a red armchair, surrounded by balls of yarn. Plaid sweaters dry on a line.
textes.Clic. La bibliothèque pivote… un passage: Click. The bookcase swivels… a secret passage!
textes.Clic… FIOU ! Une fléchette jaillit du mu: Click… WHIZZ! A dart shoots out of the east wall! The dark, cracked tiles are trapped: step on the light ones.
textes.Clique sur les tuiles pour les tourner :: Click the tiles to rotate them: connect the battery ⚡ to the antivirus ✚.
textes.Cliquetis est le nord de l'île : les hau: Cliquetis is the north of the island: the highlands, the heather, the snow on the ridges. The shepherds sell us wool and ore; we sell them… shearing machines. They don't use them.
textes.Cliquetis, la cité des ingénieurs fous —: Cliquetis, the city of mad engineers — the Inventions Fair, the Zephyr, the cable car
textes.Cliquetis, la ville des inventeurs, en d: Cliquetis, the city of inventors, is overflowing with them
textes.Clonk ! Les trois lampes du synoptique p: Clonk! The three lamps on the diagram turn green: ALL BELTS GO TOWARD THE EXIT. (The intern would be proud. Well, if he understood.)
textes.Clonk ! Une canette de Synthé-Soda tombe: Clonk! A can of Synth-Soda drops into the tray. It's ice cold, and it glows a little in the dark.
textes.Clotaire, je l'ai gardé quand il avait s: I minded Clotaire when he was six and fell asleep on the swing. Today, he falls asleep on the altar. He hasn't changed. He's a good man. And very well rested.
textes.Clou ! Banc ? J'ai plein de trucs à te r: Clou! Bench? I've got loads to tell you!
textes.Clou ! Ce soir on ouvre avec « Rouille M: Clou! Tonight we open with “Rusty But Standing”?
textes.Clou (en fouillant ta poche) : « Hiii hi: Clou (rummaging in your pocket): “Heeee hee hee!”
textes.Clou ? Il est arrivé un matin, il a volé: Clou? He showed up one morning, stole my last coin, and stayed. We get along fine: we both love money.
textes.Clou a du rythme. Amène-le à la teuf, pe: Clou's got rhythm. Bring him to the party, peuchère!
textes.Clou est venu me demander de souder des: Clou came to ask me to weld studs onto the headstock of his guitar, Germaine. I said it was a delicate instrument, the heat might damage it. He looked at me. For a long time. A very long time. I welded the studs, cold, with a special technique I invented on the spot. He nodded. Once. I was proud.
Clou came and asked me to weld nails onto his guitar. Onto Germaine. I told him it was a delicate instrument. He looked at me. I welded them. He nodded. Once. For Clou, that's a hug.
textes.Clou fait tinter une pièce qu'il vient d: Clou jingles a coin he just took from you… and Octave takes it back.
textes.Clou fouille, trouve une miette, la mang: Clou rummages, finds a crumb, eats it, and falls asleep on your shoulder. He's adopted you. So have I, a little.
textes.Clou ne parle pas, mais il remercie avec: Clou doesn't talk, but he says thank you with his hands. He knitted me a studded cover. I've never had a lovelier thank-you.
textes.Clou ne parle presque jamais, mais quand: Clou hardly ever talks, but when he laughs, it's like treasure. I heard him laugh once. I still talk about it.
textes.Clou ne parle presque pas, comme moi. Ma: Clou hardly talks, like me. But he plays in front of everyone. He heard me drumming on a bin. He nodded. I still haven't got over it.
textes.Clou nous joue de la guitare tout doucem: Clou plays guitar very softly for us, on the roof, in the evening. He thinks he's playing for the tomatoes. He's playing for us.
Clou opens his eyes. He looks at Gédéon. He nods. Twice. Unheard of!
textes.Clou parle moins que mes sculptures. Mai: Clou talks less than my sculptures. But when he asked me for studs on his guitar, I understood: we do the same job. We give metal a voice.
textes.Clou parle trois mots par jour et joue m: Clou says three words a day and plays a thousand notes a night. He's the softest heart in Boucan, hidden behind the blackest mohawk.
textes.Clou s'est caché derrière le comptoir. O: Clou is hiding behind the counter. You can only see his tail.
Clou tugs at your sleeve and holds out his hand.
textes.Clou veut savoir s'il peut fouiller tes: Clou wants to know if he can go through your pockets. He's asking, that's new.
textes.Clou, cache la caisse, voilà du monde !: Clou, hide the cash box, we've got company!
textes.Clou, tu as vu ? Il frappe le marchand !: Clou, did you see that? Hitting the shopkeeper! I'll remember this.
textes.Clovis ! Le papier, tu l'as encore ?: Clovis! Do you still have the paper?
textes.Clovis est amoureux d'Honorine depuis di: Clovis has been in love with Honorine for ten years and hasn't said a word to her. He buys an apple every evening to work up his courage. He eats a lot of apples. He's very sweet. And very slow.
textes.Clovis est le seul de Montjoie qui accep: Clovis is the only one in Montjoie who still accepts my arm-wrestling challenges. He's as strong as an ox from carrying his sacks. And when he sneezes, he wins. That's not regulation.
textes.Clovis m'apporte la farine tous les mati: Clovis brings me the flour every morning, and he stays outside my door to catch his breath. He's been catching his breath for ten years. I sing louder when I hear his footsteps.
textes.Clovis moud mon blé, il souffle sur son: Clovis grinds my wheat, he blows on his windmill when there's no wind, and he turns my turnips all white when they hide in his sacks. He's a good neighbour. A bit floury.
textes.Clovis, le meunier, apporte sa farine ch: Clovis, the miller, brings his flour to Honorine's every morning. He always comes back smiling. Flour doesn't make you smile like that.
textes.Clovis, le meunier, m'apporte la farine: Clovis, the miller, brings me flour every morning. He's all white, from head to toe. He says it's the flour. I think he's blushing underneath, and the flour hides it all.
textes.Clovis, le meunier, passe tous les jours: Clovis, the miller, passes my stall every day on his way back from Honorine's. He buys an apple and sighs. I don't think it's the apple that makes him sigh.
So does Clémence. By lighting up.
textes.Clémence peint la lumière comme je dessi: Clémence paints light the way I draw coastlines: getting it wrong a lot and starting again. I love watching her hunt for her pink.
textes.Clémence veut peindre avec des couleurs: Clémence wants to paint with natural colours: a red coral from the bottom of the bay, some honey and a coconut.
textes.Clémence veut peindre la musique. On ne: Clémence wants to paint music. You can't paint what you can't hold in your hands. And she drew me like a man with toothache.
textes.Clémence, c'est ma copine peintre. Elle: Clémence is my painter friend. She paints the lighthouse, the harbour, the sea, everything. She let me paint a sky! But she doesn't paint fast. Like, not fast at all.
textes.Clémence, elle m'a donné une petite toil: Clémence gave me a little canvas and a brush, and she said: “You do the sky.” So I made the sky all blue, and in the middle I put my kite, with all its colours. That way, it's still flying, on the canvas. Clémence kept it. She says it's the most beautiful sky at the lookout.
textes.Clémentine me trouve toujours sympathiqu: Do you think Clémentine still likes me?
textes.Clémentine vous salue, {surnom}. Je croi: Clémentine says hello, {surnom}. I think. She winked twice.
textes.Coco ! La recette de ma grand-mère ! Bon: Coconut! My grandmother's recipe! All right, Kiki sells it too now. But the real one's here. Don't repeat that to him. Actually, yes, do.
textes.Colette est la seule à voter contre moi,: Colette is the only one who's voted against me for eighteen years. An apple! Over an apple! I admire her consistency. I'll never admit it in public.
textes.Colette lit des romans d'amour. Ne lui d: Colette reads romance novels. Don't tell her I told you.
textes.Colette, c'est ma plus fidèle cliente :: Colette is my most loyal client: once a year, without fail, for the great love. She haggles over everything in life, except that. For that alone, I'm fond of her.
textes.Colette, c'est ma plus vieille amie et m: Colette is my oldest friend and my stingiest customer. A herbal tea, a novel, and a newspaper to hide the novel. Don't tell her I told you.
textes.Colette, l'épicière. Sévère, regardante,: Colette, the grocer. Stern, tight-fisted, she counts the change twice. And she has exquisite taste in literature. Exquisite. I can't say more.
textes.Colette. Elle compte tout : le papier, l: Colette. She counts everything: the paper, the string, the hello. Her prices are scary. My blades, at least, you know what they're for.
textes.Colline du Feedback\nQuand le vent souff:
Feedback Hill
When the wind blows hard, the hill whistles,
like a guitar too close to its amp.
textes.Colombe ! J'ai une idée de chapeau !: Colombe! I have an idea for a hat!
Colombe! My cape still flaps at night.
textes.Colombe est la seule personne de Montjoi: Colombe is the only person in Montjoie whose things I don't tidy. Well, almost nothing. On Sundays, we have tea, and she lets me sort her buttons.
textes.Colombe fait tous mes chapeaux. Trois ce: Colombe makes all my hats. Three hundred and sixty-five, plus the rabbit. She always tells me “no cherries this time”. I always ask her for cherries. We get on marvellously.
textes.Colombe m'a fait la cape la plus dramati: Colombe made me the most dramatic cape on the island. It billows in the wind even when there's no wind. It billows when I'm asleep too. It's a bit noisy. But it's a masterpiece.
textes.Colombe me fait un nouveau chapeau pour: Colombe is making me a new hat for the Dawn festival. She told me: “No cherries this time.” I'm not promising anything.
textes.Colombe veut me faire une tenue qui ne p: Colombe wants to make me an outfit that won't catch fire. We're on cape number nine. They all burn with great elegance. She never gives up.
textes.Combien ? Où ? Quelle taille ? Attendez,: How many? Where? How big? Wait, my notebook!
textes.Combien de Frondeurs faut-il pour change: How many Frondeurs does it take to change a light bulb? One to change it, thirty to vote on the colour, and Bricole to hook it up to a boiler.
textes.Combien de cercles compte ce royaume ?: How many circles does this realm have?
textes.Combien de hippies faut-il pour changer: How many hippies does it take to change a light bulb? None: they wait for it to see the light on its own.
textes.Combien de mètres, la petite traîne ?: How many metres, this little train?
textes.Combien de nains faut-il pour changer un: How many dwarves does it take to change a torch? None: we dig down to the lava, it's brighter.
textes.Combien de punks faut-il pour changer un: How many punks does it take to change a light bulb? One to change it, and thirty to discuss it at the assembly. And Fusible to wire it to the crane.
textes.Combien faut-il d'ingénieurs de Cliqueti: How many Cliquetis engineers does it take to change a light bulb? Just one. But now the bulb runs on steam, speaks three languages and serves tea.
textes.Comblé. Vous avez fait de ma vie de cher: Fulfilled. You've made my life as a researcher a successful one.
textes.Commandante Zélie Hélice, aérodrome de C: Commander Zélie Hélice, Cliquetis airfield! The Zéphyr circles the island non-stop: Cliquetis, Tazira, Carène, and back. Climb aboard when it's landed, it's free. The engineers pay for everyone.
textes.Commandante. Boulon remonte à bord, dema: Commander. Can Boulon come aboard again tomorrow?
textes.Commandante… le Zéphyr part bientôt ?: Commander… is the Zéphyr leaving soon?
textes.Commander un navire qui flotte. Un seul,: To command a ship that floats. Just one, just once. To feel the helm turn under my hands, like Katell. Don't repeat that to Corentin.
textes.Comme Barnabé ! (Elle soupire.) Bon. Au: Like Barnabé! (She sighs.) Well. At least you hold the rail. You do hold the rail, don't you?
textes.Comme Fusible ! Au deuxième barreau, il: Like Fusible! On the second rung, he starts shaking. You two could climb together. Slowly. I'll hold the ladder for you. It won't move.
textes.Comme Fusible. Et comme moi, à mes début: Like Fusible. And like me, when I started. A pallet comes apart nail by nail. That's how you learn to put it back together.
textes.Comme Margaux ! Les gens du matin, je le: Like Margaux! Morning people — I admire them and I don't understand them. The best bread is at four in the morning, fine. But the best music is at midnight.
textes.Comme Pigment. Bon. Je respecte. Je vais: Like Pigment. Fine. I respect that. I'll write an article without a single pun, just for you. It'll be hard. Very hard.
textes.Comme SECOND ?! Par la quille ! Je vais: As FIRST MATE?! By the keel! I'm telling everyone! No, wait, I'm not telling the Admiral. But everyone except her!
textes.Comme Titou ! Ceux qui bougent sont les: Like Titou! People who move look the best in long exposures: they become ghosts of light. Jump, spin… There, you've vanished. Gorgeous.
textes.Comme Tornade. Je connais la chanson. Mo: Just like Tornade. I know the tune. Show me that knee. … There. Didn't even hurt, eh? You've got tears in your eyes.
textes.Comme au bal des Liftiers !: Just like at the Liftkeepers' Ball!
textes.Comme chaque matin depuis mille ans. Et: Like every morning for a thousand years. And I never tire of it.
textes.Comme d'habitude : nuageux avec des écla: Same as usual: cloudy with sunny spells. Mostly clouds.
As usual. So nineteen straight ones.
As the ancients used to say.
As Lady Ysolde used to say.
textes.Comme disait ma grand-mère : jamais de c: As my grandmother used to say: never wear socks on the sand.
textes.Comme disait ma mère, qui était une fleu: As my mother used to say, and she was a flower.
As my old master used to say.
As the elders of Ramure say.
textes.Comme je l'enseigne depuis trois siècles: As I have taught for three centuries.
textes.Comme l'étang : calme dessus, vivant des: Like the pond: calm on top, alive beneath.
textes.Comme la marée. (Elle sourit.) Nos fonda: Like the tide. (She smiles.) Our founders would have loved to hear you say that. A decision that rises slowly holds for a long time. You'd make a fine member of the Council.
textes.Comme la mer : calme dessus, ça remue de: Like the sea: calm on top, churning underneath.
textes.Comme la mer un jour de vent : bruyant !: Like the sea on a windy day: loud!
textes.Comme le Bassin ! Alors je le connais dé: Like the Pool! Then I already know it a bit! But bigger, and without fish? … Or with fish that fly? They're called birds, I know. I was just checking.
Like the crystal, when it's well.
textes.Comme le disait si bien un jeune voyageu: As a young traveller friend of mine put it so well: “Port-Azur, a gem!” That's you. I quote you everywhere.
textes.Comme le roc, Octave ! Ton fer chante so: Solid as a rock, Octave! Your iron sings under the bass.
As the volcano, my good man. At least.
textes.Comme ma fille ! Encore un qui croit que: Just like my daughter! Another one who thinks Mustapha's sardines are birds. Fine. I'll still save you a portion of tajine. For your education.
Like a thousand and one stars.
textes.Comme moi ! Les gens qui regardent sont: Like me! People who watch are the best. Here, look into the camera. See? That's Astralys in three dimensions. And sometimes in four.
textes.Comme moi ! On est pareils ! Tu sais quo: Just like me! We're the same! You know what? We'll look together. You for your island, me for my tree. I'll start with you, you look easier.
textes.Comme moi ? Alors bon courage, et dors d: Like me? Then good luck, and sleep on the boat. It's the only quiet moment of the day. Captain Léon toots the horn ever so softly when I'm asleep.
textes.Comme moi ?! Ho ho ! Il en faut, du cour: Like me?! Ho ho! That takes courage! Or absent-mindedness. Mine was absent-mindedness. Come here and let me shake your hand, nail brother!
textes.Comme moi avec Gwenola. Euh, avec les po: Like me with Gwenola. Er, with the fish! With the fish, I meant. Ma doue, it's hot today.
textes.Comme moi, au début ! Les plantes aiment: Like me, at first! Plants love secrets. They never repeat them. Except nettles. Nettles repeat everything.
textes.Comme moi, chaque nuit ! Hou ! Enfin que: Like me, every night! Hoo! At last someone who understands. You lose count, and you start again. That's the job.
textes.Comme mon enclume : solide, et un peu so: Like my anvil: solid, and a bit deaf.
textes.Comme mon neveu ! Ha ! Pas de honte à ça: Just like my nephew! Ha! No shame in that. But try, just once, opening one eye halfway down. Just one. In the water, there's no void: there's blue.
As cabin boy, to start with.
textes.Comme neuves, mon cher Sylvain ! Pas un: Good as new, my dear Sylvain! Not a single hole!
As they say in the Circle of Fire.
As we say at the port.
As we say at the assembly.
As they say at the Guild.
textes.Comme quelqu'un qui écope avec une cuill: Like someone bailing with a spoon.
textes.Comme toujours, Majesté ! Ce sera six pi: As always, Majesty! That'll be six coins. Just kidding. Five.
textes.Comme toujours, ma grande. Et tu me chan: As always, my girl. And you'll sing me the first note.
textes.Comme toujours, maître. Je frapperai, au: As always, master. I'll knock, just in case.
textes.Comme toujours, très cher. L'huile est p: As always, my dear. The oil is ready.
As always. I'll bring the violet.
textes.Comme tous les jours, Fundin. Pourquoi ?: Same as every day, Fundin. Why?
textes.Comme tout Carène. Ici, on préfère boite: Like all of Carène. Around here, people would rather limp than look like they're limping. I'll catch you out eventually, you know. I always do.
textes.Comme tout le monde, en haut. Bon, c'est: Like everyone up here. Well, clouds are pretty. But don't forget there are stars down below too. Ours shine in the rock.
textes.Comme tu veux. Je suis de garde. Mais la: As you like. I'm on watch. But the high tide, yes.
textes.Comme un capitaine qui a trente ans de m: Like a captain with thirty years at sea and not a single breakdown. Touch wood.
textes.Comme un conte : ça commence bien, et la: Like a tale: it starts well, and as for the ending, we'll see.
Like a cable: nice and taut.
textes.Comme un lac, Yvon. Sans les grenouilles: Like a lake, Yvon. Without the frogs.
textes.Comme un loir ! Je sens que c'est vrai :: Like a log! I can smell it's true: you look nice and fresh. Prescription: a moon tea, so you dream as well. Sleeping is good; dreaming is better.
textes.Comme un loir ! Ça se voit, tu as le tei: Like a log! It shows, you look fresh as a daisy. Treasure it, it doesn't last a lifetime. Me, I sleep like an old owl.
textes.Comme un percepteur, milord. Il a fallu: Like a tax collector, milord. Had to hold it by the tail.
Like I've got two left feet.
textes.Comme un poisson ! Alors si un jour quel: Like a fish! So if one day someone falls in the water near you… No, nothing. I was saying that for Youssef. He falls in a lot.
textes.Comme un poisson ! Respect. Alors tu n'a: Like a fish! Respect. Then you've got no excuse for my starfish challenge. If you beat me, I'll do five hundred push-ups in front of the whole beach. I do them anyway, but still.
textes.Comme un poisson ?! Waouh ! Tu fais la g: Like a fish?! Wow! Do you do the frog or the doggy paddle? Me, I… um, I watch. To learn. Will you show me?
textes.Comme un roc. Gros-Louis l'a essayé hier: Like a rock. Gros-Louis tested it yesterday.
Like a well-poured tea: sweet and warm.
textes.Comme un tournesol à midi : la tête bien: Like a sunflower at noon: head held high and a warm heart.
textes.Comme un vieil homme qui a vu revenir to: Like an old man who saw all his boats come home this morning. Light of heart.
Like an admiral without a fleet: busy. A town of two hundred souls inside a leaking hull doesn't govern itself.
Like a song, very far away.
textes.Comme une farfalle : un peu froissé au m: Like a farfalle: a little crumpled in the middle, but with two lovely wings on either side.
textes.Comme une larme… C'est vrai. Mais une la: Like a tear… That's true. But a tear of joy, then: here, the sea feeds us. Come, let me give you a taste of the happy version.
textes.Comme une pierre… Zéphyr serait vexé, il: Like a log… Zéphyr would be offended, he's forever bumping into logs. No matter: forgotten dreams fall into the clouds. Perhaps we keep a few of them for you.
textes.Comme une pâte qui lève : de mieux en mi: Like rising dough: better and better! I got up at three, I kneaded, I sang, I tasted. Tasted a lot.
textes.Comme une souche ! Par les racines de l': Like a log! By the roots of the Mother Tree, I envy you. I sleep like a brew on the stove: one eye open, watching in case I boil over.
textes.Comme une théière : chaude dedans, un pe: Like a teapot: warm inside, a little dented outside.
textes.Comme une tombe ! Ici, les tombes sont p: Like a tomb! Around here, tombs are full of things, you know. Well. I believe you. But I still won't tell you anything: you never know.
textes.Comme une vieille coque : ça grince, mai: Like an old hull: it creaks, but it floats.
textes.Comme une vieille pirate qui a jeté l'an: Like an old pirate who's dropped anchor: calm. But not asleep.
textes.Comme une épicière dont le fournisseur d: Like a grocer whose honey supplier is running late. Not good.
textes.Comme ça, Nono ? Le phoque élégant, vers: Like this, Nono? The elegant seal, version two?
textes.Comment allez-vous le sortir ?: How are you going to get it out?
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un Moaï qui danse ?: What do you call a dancing Moai?
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un Pied-Lourd sur A: What do you call a Heavy-Foot on Astralys? A tourist! And a tourist on Astralys who takes pictures of everything? Glorb.
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un champignon qui f: What do you call a mushroom that loves to party? A Fronde mushroom: it glows all night and never goes home. … Bertille says that's unfair. Hers go to bed very early.
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un chat tombé dans: What do you call a cat that fell into a pot of paint on Christmas Day? A Christmas paw-trait! … Hey, that's one of Paulo's jokes, not mine.
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un chien qui n'a pa: What do you call a dog with no legs?
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un navet qui court: What do you call a turnip that outruns everybody? A root-runner! … Like a roadrunner. Right. It's one of Père Gaubert's jokes.
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un nuage qui racont: What do you call a cloud that tells jokes? A cumulus of laughs. … Gustave loves that one. He says it's his surname.
textes.Comment appelle-t-on un ordinateur qui c: What do you call a computer that sings? A Dell… No, wait. A… Well, Glitch tells it better than me.
textes.Comment appelle-t-on une chaudière qui c: What do you call a boiler that sings? A Valve-ocalist! … There. That's why the band is called the Valves. Nobody knows if it's a reason or an excuse.
textes.Comment appelle-t-on une horloge qui cha: What do you call a clock that sings out of tune? A clock that keeps time but can't keep a tune. … Gaspard never laughs at that one. He says his sings perfectly in tune.
textes.Comment appelle-t-on une pâte qui fait d: What do you call pasta that works out? Puff pasta! No, wait, that's pastry.
textes.Comment attirer le perroquet de la capit: How do I lure the captain's parrot?
textes.Comment devenir citoyen de Port-Azur ?: How do I become a citizen of Port-Azur?
textes.Comment les approcher ?: How do I get close to them?
textes.Comment les fraises deviennent-elles si: How do the strawberries get so big?
textes.Comment on appelle un parapluie qui joue: What do you call an umbrella that plays guitar? Rain 'n' roll! … Okay. That one's Bourrasque's. She tells it at every rehearsal.
textes.Comment on appelle un rat qui joue de la: What do you call a rat that plays the drums? A rat-a-tat-tat! … Right. Tapage taught me that one. He's been telling it since 1977.
textes.Comment rejoindre ton île ?: How do I get to your island?
textes.Comment t'oublier ? Tu as expliqué le ve: How could I forget you? You explained the wind to my class by blowing on their hair. They still talk about it. It was the best lesson of the term. And it wasn't even mine.
textes.Comment ta vie a commencé, ici ?: How did your life here begin?
textes.Comment tu le fais monter si haut ?: How do you get it up so high?
textes.Comment un Moaï dit-il bonjour ?: How does a Moai say hello?
textes.Comment un poisson-lanterne retrouve-t-i: How does a lanternfish find its way? It always has a bright idea. … Professor Benthos finds that one almost scientific.
textes.Comment va le Cœur, ce soir, Frère Cendr: How is the Heart tonight, Brother Cendrin?
textes.Comment va ta barque ? Je lui dis bonjou: How's your rowboat? I say hello to her every morning at the jetty. She doesn't answer, but she floats.
textes.Comment va votre lame, my dear ? Si un j: How is your blade, my dear? If one day it retires, my display case awaits. With a golden label.
textes.Comment va-t-il sortir ?: How's it going to get out?
textes.Comment ça va ? Ça va qu'il y a un rival: How am I? I'm a man with a rival on the other side of the island telling tall tales about him, that's how.
textes.Comprendre, une bonne fois pour toutes,: To understand, once and for all, how it stays up in the air. Then, most likely, tell no one. Some things are more beautiful unexplained. But I still want to know.
textes.Comète a fait la course avec une mouette: Comète raced a seagull over the harbour. The seagull won: it caught the wind. Comète's saucer lost a fin in the manoeuvre. That's the forty-third time I've repaired it. In the end, I welded a little seagull drawing onto the new fin. She laughed for an hour.
textes.Comète a fait la course avec une étoile: Comète raced a shooting star. She says she won. The shooting star made no comment.
textes.Comète avait cinq ans quand elle est tom: Comète was five when she fell off the Observatory bridge, running. That was the first time I healed her. My hands glowed, the knee got better. She asked me: “Can I fall again, to see?” I said no. She fell again the next day. I healed her laughing. She's never stopped falling.
textes.Comète casse ses soucoupes, je les répar: Comète breaks her saucers, I repair them. Forty-three times. She wants my crystal engine. I tell her she isn't ready. She is, a little. But if I give it to her, she'll go even faster. I'm worried about the seagulls.
textes.Comète dit qu'elle a battu une étoile fi: Comète says she beat a shooting star in a race. I checked: it was Quasar's toaster, in orbit. I didn't tell her straight away. She was so proud.
Comète says she beat a shooting star in a race. I checked: it was one of Quasar's satellites. The gravitational toaster. It's still in orbit.
textes.Comète est arrivée à l'Observatoire en c: Comète came to the Observatory shouting: “I beat a shooting star!” I looked through the telescope. It was Professor Quasar's gravitational toaster, which has been circling the island for years with its toast. I told her, gently. She said: “Then I beat a toaster. That's not bad either.”
textes.Comète est ma meilleure cliente : le gen: Comète is my best customer: the knee, the elbow, the nose, the pride. I scold her, I heal her, I give her a biscuit. She promises to be careful. She's careful for one day. That's something.
textes.Comète m'a emmené voir les étoiles depui: Comète took me to see the stars from her saucer, very high up, above the clouds. For the first time, I saw them with nothing between them and me. I cried, like on the first night. Comète switched off the engine and said nothing for an hour. It's the only time I've ever seen her keep still.
textes.Comète m'a emmenée faire un tour en souc: Comète took me for a ride in her saucer once. She flew round the Spire in eleven seconds. I got so dizzy I danced in the cockpit to calm down. My ribbons filled the whole saucer. Comète couldn't see a thing. She landed laughing, upside down.
textes.Comète me dépose en bas et vient me rech: Comète drops me off down below and comes back for me, without ever telling the Council. She drives far too fast. We arrive before we've left. I adore her.
textes.Comète repasse l'anneau d'or la première: Comète flies through the golden ring first: “VZIIIOU! I win!” She does a happy loop-the-loop. “Come on, rematch! Fly through the golden ring whenever you like!”
textes.Comète t'attend près de l'anneau d'or, a: Comète is waiting near the golden ring, above the Spaceport. Fly through it to start the race!
Comète flies faster than anyone. I leap more beautifully than anyone. We had a contest once. We both won. Nobody understood how.
textes.Comète, depuis sa soucoupe : « Vziiiou !: Comète, from her saucer: “Vziiiou! No walking! Hop into your Star Glider (N key) and fly through the golden ring!”
textes.Comète, la pilote de soucoupe, s'ennuie: Comète, the saucer pilot, is bored: nobody wants to race her. Now that you have the Star Glider, she challenges you: first a practice run on the ring course of the Zero-Gravity Garden, then the great ring race in the sky, around Astralys.
textes.Comète, tu cherches un adversaire ?: Comète, are you looking for an opponent?
textes.Comète, tu me déposes ce soir ?: Comète, can you drop me off tonight?
textes.Comète, un défi au Jardin ?: Comète, a challenge in the Garden?
textes.Concentré. Il y a un drone de livraison: Focused. There's a delivery drone that thinks it's a pigeon. It coos. I'm hunting the bug.
textes.Concentré. J'ai redessiné Port-Azur. C'e: Focused. I've redrawn Port-Azur. That's the seventeenth time. Every time, someone has built a beach hut. They never stop building down there. It's exhausting for a cartographer.
textes.Concentré. Mon automate a trois coups d': Focused. My automaton is three moves ahead of me.
textes.Concentré. Ne me parle pas pendant le ni: Focused. Don't talk to me during level seven, it's the one with the loop-the-loop dragons.
textes.Concentrée. J'ai fait une cape anti-foud: Focused. I made an anti-lightning cape for Violette. It caught fire at the first flash. But it caught fire with elegance.
textes.Concentrée. Une coque, c'est comme un vi: Focused. A hull is like a violin: one badly-fitted plank and everything sounds wrong.
textes.Confiance ? Peuchère. Vous êtes un agnea: Trust? Good heavens. You're a little lamb. Here, you can. Elsewhere, count. Especially at the souvenir shop.
textes.Confitures de mûres, de prunes, et de ro: Blackberry jam, plum jam and cogwheel jam… no, I'm joking, no cogwheels.
textes.Conseil d'ami : les slimes, tu les tapes: Friendly advice: slimes, hit them once, they bounce; twice, they melt. Frogs, stay to the side, never in front. Goblins, let them run, they get tired. I do the exact opposite. Do as I say.
textes.Conseil d'ami : tu écoutes les conseils,: A word from a friend: do you listen to advice? Or do you do like me?
textes.Construire avec les inventeurs de Clique: To build, with the inventors of Cliquetis, the most beautiful machine in the archipelago: their steam, our crystals, their gears, our astral engines. A contraption that would go “choo-choo” and “vzzz” at the same time. I'd call it “Friendship”. Or “the Racket”. Depends on the noise.
textes.Construire la plus longue rampe de skate: To build the longest skate ramp in the world, inside the Great Column, from the Clouds all the way to the Azure Dome, and ride down it with Tom and Pimprenelle shouting “Boing!” the whole way. Four worlds in a single run. With helmets. Mum insists.
textes.Construire un cinquième Sustentateur, to: To build a fifth Levitator, brand new, the first since Séraphin, so the Old One can finally rest after a hundred and twenty years. And name it after my grandmother: Constance.
textes.Construire un dôme au bord de la mer, su: To build a dome by the sea, on an island down below, to watch the waves through the glass. And to invite the people from down there to sleep in it for one night. Just to see if they like round. I bet they do.
textes.Construire une fois un vrai grand bateau: To build a real big ship, just once. With a mast, a sail, and a hold you can stand up in. May it sail all the way to Port-Azur, and may people watch it leave from the lighthouse.
textes.Construire une grande maison en palettes: To build a big pallet house on the Cannery roof, with a bedroom for everyone who hasn't got one. And a round window looking out to sea, like a rowing boat's porthole.
textes.Construire une machine qui relie les qua: To build a machine that links the four worlds of the Column with a steam pipe, so the Valves' organ plays at the same time in the Clouds, in Hautefond, in the Strata and in the Azure Dome. And doesn't cough at pipe thirty-seven.
textes.Construire une passerelle si douce que S: To build a walkway so gentle that Sylwen climbs up it one day, with a tray. I've already drawn it: wide handrail, new planks, not a single crack. It'll be called “Just-Once”.
textes.Content ! J'ai retrouvé ma casquette, el: Happy! I found my cap, it was on Momo's head.
textes.Content ! J'ai trouvé du piment dans la: Happy! I found chillies in the jungle. Tonight, the crew will cry. With joy. Or with chilli.
textes.Content ! Le Grand Spaghetti a recommenc: Happy! The Great Spaghetti has started dancing again, and the Reverend told me it wasn't my fault at all. Well, he said “hardly at all”. But it's the same thing.
Happy! Mum gave me a cacao.
textes.Content ! Une couleur de plus, c'est com: Pleased! One more colour is like a good mark: it warms the heart, even at my age.
textes.Content ? (Elle réfléchit très fort.) Al: Happy? (She thinks very hard.) So when it's grey, it's sad? And when it's pink, it's in love? I knew it!
textes.Content, je crois. Ce matin, j'ai vu une: Pleased, I think. This morning, from the Lookout, I saw a patch of colour spreading over the island. Like a drop of ink on blotting paper. It was beautiful.
textes.Content, mon petit. Très content. La Lig: Happy, my child. Very happy. The Line has reopened. For years we were “the folk down below”. Now people from up top come and sit on our sofas and give their opinion. That's exactly why I lit this fire.
textes.Content. Boulon aussi, je crois. Il remu: Happy. Boulon too, I think. He's wagging his tail, and his tail is a spring.
textes.Content. J'ai enfin dessiné l'Île de Bra: Pleased. I've finally drawn Ember Island without burning my paper. The secret: draw it from very far away, with a very long pencil.
textes.Content. J'ai posé un nouveau conteneur: Happy. I set down a new container at the Boxes. A family is going to live in it. They painted flowers on it before I even put it down. It arrived in bloom.
textes.Content. J'ai pris une perche grosse com: Happy. I caught a perch as big as my arm. All right, my arm isn't very big.
textes.Contente. Ce matin, un monsieur des Stra: Happy. This morning, a gentleman from the Strata brought me a watch and asked me to fix it. I gave him the key, the screwdriver, and I showed him. He fixed it himself. He left all proud. Here, we don't repair FOR you. We repair WITH you.
textes.Contente. Mes abeilles chantent, mes sim: Content. My bees are singing, my herbs are growing.
textes.Contente. Une dame d'en haut a échangé s: Happy. A lady from up top swapped her feathered hat for a bolt necklace. She left all proud, hair in the wind. And now I have a feathered hat. I don't know what to do with it. I'll make it into a lampshade.
textes.Contrarié. J'ai fait exploser le labo, e: Annoyed. I blew up the lab, and a hologram chip flew out of the window. Without it, Ionie can't finish the glider's navigation. It must be somewhere in the Academy. Or in the sky.
textes.Contrarié. Le Cœur de la Flèche bat irré: Out of sorts. The Spire's Heart is beating irregularly. One beat, then nothing, then two. For a clockmaker, it's unbearable. For the island, it's worrying.
textes.Contrarié. Le four solaire a trop chauff: Annoyed. The solar oven got too hot: my sugar puffs doubled in size. They float a bit. I had to tie them down with string.
textes.Contrarié. Mon appareil photo ! J'ai dû: Annoyed. My camera! I must have put it down somewhere up there, at the lookout, while photographing the sunset.
textes.Contrarié. Mère Morille raconte que sa c: Annoyed. Mère Morille claims her giant squash weighs a hundred kilos. A hundred kilos! Mine weighs ninety-eight. She must have weighed the caravan too.
textes.Contrariée. Hum. Je veux dire : contrari: Vexed. Ahem. I mean: officially vexed. Halo welcomed a visitor without me again. Four minutes of speech, with no official proofreading. It's luminous anarchy.
textes.Contrariée. Ma grande marmite a fait des: Annoyed. This morning my big stockpot started bubbling all by herself, with no fire underneath. Yolande says it's the pressure. I say she's copying the Fountain. I told her off. She's still at it.
textes.Contrariée. Un cristal s'est fendu penda: Annoyed. A crystal split while I was cutting it. It was perfect. It's still beautiful, mind you. But now it shines in two colours. It looks as if it can't make up its mind. I understand. Neither can I.
textes.Contrariée. Un hublot de la Promenade a: Annoyed. A porthole on the Promenade went “tick” last night. I checked every screw, every seal, every millimetre. Nothing. It was a lanternfish that had bumped into it. It looked more surprised than I was. I logged it anyway.
textes.Contre qui ? Contre Bondi, alors. Deuxiè: Against who? Against Bondi, then. Second behind Bondi is… wait, I'm thinking… it's very good! Isn't it? Yes. Well, I think. You make me think, you do, it's tiring.
textes.Contre une lampe, comme d'habitude. Elle: For a lamp, as usual. This one's smaller than the last.
textes.Cool ! Alors je te lance un défi : le to: Cool! Then I challenge you: once round the harbour wall on “Wave 3”, against the clock. Kevin holds the record. OK, Kevin was swimming, but still.
textes.Cool. Le vent est parfait. Enfin, il est: Cool. The wind's perfect. Well, it's always perfect, I decide that.
textes.Copeau ! Ta scie, elle clignote bien ?: Copeau! Is your saw blinking nicely?
textes.Copeau a construit une balançoire en pal: Copeau built a pallet swing so high that Cerise could see the sea over the Cannery. I made him lower it. A bit. Cerise is still sulking.
textes.Copeau construit, je branche. Il dit que: Copeau builds, I wire. He says my fairy lights are worrying. I say his silence is worrying. We're even. He's a solid friend. Solid oak.
textes.Copeau dit que j'ai branché une guirland: Copeau says I wired a string of lights to his saw. True. He says it's worrying. False: it's festive.
textes.Copeau parle avec un marteau, moi avec u: Copeau talks with a hammer, I talk with a whistle. At home, it makes an orchestra. We understand each other without a word. We've hardly ever needed one.
textes.Coquille ! Cap au large, tout droit !: Coquille! Out to sea, straight ahead!
textes.Coquille ! Quatre cent dix pièces ?: Coquille! Four hundred and ten coins?
textes.Coquille ! Une chanson de marin, et je c: Coquille! A sea shanty, and I'll hammer!
textes.Coquille ? Une gentille fille qui ramass: Coquille? A nice girl who collects shells and parks sloops on reefs. She says the reef wasn't on any map. It was on mine. In my head.
textes.Coquille a la plus belle collection de c: Coquille has the finest shell collection in the archipelago and she refuses to sell it to me. Two hundred beaches! What value! She says it's priceless. Maybe she's right. Don't tell her.
textes.Coquille est la seule du port qui me cri: Coquille is the only one in the port who shouts hello at me as loud as I do. Every morning. “MORNING, BELLE-HUMEUR!” I hear her very well. It annoys me. A bit. Not much.
textes.Coquille me pose une question tous les m: Coquille asks me a question every morning. Just one. I answer with one word. She says she collects my words, like her shells. How many does she have? … I don't ask.
textes.Coquille tient la barre comme une reine: Coquille holds the helm like a queen and sleeps like a log. She blames me for betting the Cod at dice. I blame her for putting it on the reefs. We're even, more or less.
textes.Coquille vient m'aider l'après-midi. Ell: Coquille comes to help me in the afternoons. She misses the nails one time out of two, but she sings in tune. With her, time passes faster than the tide. And the Merciless loves her songs.
Coquille comes to help me in the afternoons. She misses the nails half the time. But she sings well.
textes.Coralie ! Hic ! Une selle, cette fois ?: Coralie! Hic! A saddle, this time?
textes.Coralie ! Une petite fourchette, sur l'a: Coralie! A little fork, on the other arm?
textes.Coralie ! Une plume de corbeau sur le to: Coralie! A raven feather on the roof of the well!
textes.Coralie l'Encre a tatoué un poulpe sur l: Coralie l'Encre tattooed an octopus on Tonneau's back. He's never seen it. He thinks it's a horse.
textes.Coralie l'Encre devait me tatouer un cou: Coralie l'Encre was supposed to tattoo a knife on me. She tattooed a spoon. She says I moved. Maybe I moved. She should've tattooed faster.
textes.Coralie l'Encre tatoue les roses des ven: Coralie l'Encre tattoos the compass roses I draw. She's an artist. She loves raven quills as much as I do. There aren't enough ravens on this island for the two of us.
textes.Coralie l'Encre. Je tatoue les durs. Les: Coralie l'Encre — Coralie the Ink. I tattoo the tough guys. Anchors, mermaids, skulls. Want a tattoo? Pirates respect people who have one.
textes.Coralie m'a dessiné un cheval dans le do: Coralie drew a horse on my back. She says it's an octopus. Hic! Artists never know what they're drawing. Me, I know: it's a horse. Scarlett saw it.
textes.Coralie. Je lui forge ses aiguilles. Fin: Coralie. I forge her needles. Fine ones. Very fine. She tattooed an anvil on my arm. I didn't move. She says I was asleep. I wasn't asleep. I was thinking.
textes.Coralin ! C'est un poisson ou un oursin,: Coralin! Is it a fish or a sea urchin today?
textes.Coralin ! Ta lampe de la semaine est un: Coralin! This week's lamp is a bit small.
textes.Coralin ? Mon sujet d'étude préféré. Per: Coralin? My favourite subject of study. Nobody gets things wrong with so much energy, or so much talent. His scrolls are the thickest in the library.
textes.Coralin ? Un génie du corail, un radin d: Coralin? A coral genius, a first-class penny-pincher and my almost-fiancé for four hundred years. He says my crackers are filling. He buys a bag a week.
textes.Coralin a des mains d'or et un caractère: Coralin has hands of gold and the temper of a sea urchin. He claims I still owe him for the mother-of-pearl throne. It may be true. I have no intention of checking.
textes.Coralin est le premier enfant né sous le: Coralin is the first child born under the dome. He cried so loud the crystal flickered, and the whole city laughed, for the first time since the wave. I've never told him, he'd become unbearable: that was the day I believed we could live here.
textes.Coralin fait semblant d'être grognon, ma: Coralin pretends to be grumpy, but he keeps his mother-of-pearl offcuts in a box marked “NOT FOR ONDINE”. So they must be for me, otherwise why would he write my name?
textes.Coralin m'a dit qu'une pomme, c'est un o: Coralin told me an apple is a red sea urchin that grows on trees. I did a drawing: a tree full of sea urchins. Abyssos filed it in the scroll of Coralin's mistakes. Coralin was furious. I was proud: it's my first drawing in the archives!
textes.Coralin m'a taillé ce trident en une heu: Coralin carved me this trident in an hour, on the night of the sharks. It bites a little. So does Coralin. But they're both good tools.
textes.Coralin parle à ses sculptures. Je l'ai: Coralin talks to his sculptures. I heard him. He tells them “good night”.
textes.Coralin se plaint des requins. Il a rais: Coralin complains about the sharks. He's right: they steal his shark teeth. … Well, the other way round.
textes.Coralin, c'est le meilleur tailleur de l: Coralin is the best carver in the city. He hasn't really spoken to me for a hundred years, but he does greet me. With his chin. That's something.
textes.Coralin, ton requin t'a rendu ton ciseau: Coralin, has your shark given you back your chisel?
textes.Coralin. Rien de cassé, aujourd'hui ? Mo: Coralin. Nothing broken today? My scroll is hungry.
textes.Corbeau a un galion volé, un perroquet m: Corbeau has a stolen galleon, a badly brought-up parrot and a scar she refuses to explain. She sails well. Too well. It annoys me.
Corbeau. Your galleon's listing to port.
textes.Corentin ! J'ai trouvé une deuxième bott: Corentin! I found a second boot in the basin!
textes.Corentin ! Par la lune, tu tangues encor: Corentin! By the moon, still rolling?
textes.Corentin ? Le petit-fils de Yann-le-Borg: Corentin? Yann-le-Borgne's grandson? Ha! Yes, I have the logbook. Here it is… But look: the pages that talk about the seal are blank. Moon ink, the sailors called it: it can only be read by the light of a moon you carry with you. I never understood it. Keep it, it may speak to you one day. And since you're chasing after the seals: ours, the desert one, sleeps beneath the walking dune. Rachid, the carpet merchant, has an old carpet that shows the way. He'll tell you… if he stops going on about his prices.
textes.Corentin a le cœur d'un phoque et l'idée: Corentin has the heart of a seal and the fixed idea that my seaweed store is the best hiding place for his hot honey drink. He's not wrong: nobody touches it. Except me.
textes.Corentin dit qu'il y a un monstre dans l: Corentin says there's a monster in the basin. I looked for it a whole afternoon. I found a boot.
textes.Corentin dit que la coque chante, les nu: Corentin says the hull sings on calm nights. He's right. But I've never told anyone, {surnom}: underwater, I hear it better than he does. And it doesn't come from the wood. It comes from below, from the stones. My grandmother heard it too. One day, she went down to see. She never dived again. She never said why.
textes.Corentin m'a dit qu'il y avait un monstr: Corentin told me there was a monster in the harbour basin. I searched for it a whole afternoon with a shrimping net. I found a boot. The week after, I found a second one! Corentin says the monster has two feet. I think it's a monster that keeps losing its boots.
textes.Corentin me cache ses grogs dans ma rése: Corentin hides his mugs of hot honey in my seaweed store. He thinks I don't know.
textes.Corentin raconte au coin de mon poêle de: Corentin has been telling stories by my stove for over fifty years. His stories change a little every night. His hot honeys, though, I count, and the numbers don't change.
textes.Corentin rit de mon titre depuis trente: Corentin has been laughing at my title for thirty years. He tells my ancestor's story better than I do, and it annoys me. He's right about a lot of things. That annoys me too.
textes.Corentin, de Carène ! Un conteur qui tan: Corentin, from Carène! A storyteller who rolls with the waves. He knows the end of every one of his stories, that one. I'm a bit jealous. Very, in fact. Don't tell him.
textes.Corentin, de Carène, cherche le journal: Corentin, from Carène, is looking for the Leviathan's logbook.
textes.Corentin, hier, ta baleine avait cinq ar: Corentin, yesterday your whale had five trees.
textes.Corentin, le conteur de Carène. On me di: Corentin, the storyteller of Carène. They tell me he knows a thousand stories. A thousand! I know a thousand and one. I met him under a table, nearly seventy years ago. He didn't cry loudly.
textes.Corentin, ta bolée est vide et ta bouche: Corentin, your mug is empty and your mouth is full of stories.
textes.Corentin, tu n'aurais pas oublié quelque: Corentin, you didn't forget something in my seaweed, did you?
textes.Corentin. Encore une histoire sur moi, c: Corentin. Another story about me tonight?
textes.Corne-Sur-Nez : gros, grincheux. Il grat: Horn-On-Nose: big, grumpy. He scrape ground with foot, then he CHARGE. You not stay in front! If he charge into rock: bong! He see stars. Hit!
textes.Correcte, mais j'ai l'œil sur les falais: Fair, but I've got my eye on the north-west cliffs. Those blasted gargoyles won't let me sleep. Neither me nor my ships.
textes.Correcte. J'ai réussi une potion qui ren: Adequate. I managed a potion that makes your voice softer. I'm saving it for Madame Hurla. For her birthday. Or for mine.
textes.Correcte. La terre est bonne, le four au: Fair. The clay is good, and so is the oven. Whatever Mérit says.
textes.Correcte. Le Baron voulait offrir la Gra: Fair. The Baron wanted to give the Great Square to a hat merchant. In exchange for a hat. I tore up the contract. I kept the hat: it was pretty.
textes.Correcte. Merci de demander, personne ne: Fair. Thank you for asking, nobody ever asks.
textes.Coucou ! Dis, t'as un frère ou une sœur,: Hiya! Say, have you got a brother or a sister? I've got Pomme-de-Pin! She makes bridges!
textes.Coucou ! Dis-moi, toi : un pont qui boug: Yoo-hoo! Tell me: a wobbly bridge, how do you cross it?
textes.Coucou ! Du courrier pour la lune ?: Yoo-hoo! Any post for the moon?
textes.Coucou ! Il chante juste ?: Hiya! Does it sing in tune?
textes.Coucou ! Il va bien, ton frère ou ta sœu: Hiya! How's your brother or sister? Did you teach them to hide hazelnuts?
textes.Coucou ! J'ai pas oublié : je te prête P: Hiya! I haven't forgotten: I'm lending you Pomme-de-Pin. One day. Not today, she's working.
textes.Coucou ! J'ai retrouvé une noisette ! Il: Cuckoo! I found a hazelnut! Only two hundred and ninety-nine to go!
textes.Coucou ! J'ai sept ans et j'habite dans: Hiya! I'm seven and I live in the west tree with my big sister Pomme-de-Pin and Granny Faîne. Dad's called Noyer and Mum's called Châtaigne! In the fine season they gather fallen wood in the deep forest, really far away, and they come home in winter with pockets full of stories. Winter's my favourite season. Guess why!
textes.Coucou ! Ma grand-mère, Mamie Faîne, a c: Yoo-hoo! My grandma, Granny Faîne, built almost every bridge in Ramure. Me, I tied my first knot at four, round her tail! She taught me the two squirrel rules: a bridge must dance with the wind, and you never cut down a living tree. Never! Only the fallen wood that Mum and Dad bring back from the deep forest.
textes.Coucou ! T'as des noisettes ? Non ? Domm: Cuckoo! Got any hazelnuts? No? Shame. I'm Gland. I hid three hundred. Can't remember where. Will you help me look?
textes.Coucou ! Tes clous sont trop gros !: Yoo-hoo! Your nails are too big!
textes.Coucou ! Ton miel, tout frais d'en haut: Yoo-hoo! Your honey, fresh from up top!
textes.Coucou ! Tu as traversé le pont de l'oue: Cuckoo! Did you cross the west bridge? It sings when the wind blows. I did that on purpose.
textes.Coucou ! Tu brilles pas du tout, toi. C': Hiya! You don't glow at all, you. Is that normal for a human? Welcome!
textes.Coucou ! Tu sens le vent ?: Yoo-hoo! Can you feel the wind?
textes.Coucou, Bedaine ! T'as quelque chose pou: Yoo-hoo, Bedaine! Got anything for me?
textes.Coucou, Grommelot ! Mes graines ont fait: Hiya, Grommelot! Did my seeds go pop?
textes.Coucou, Grommelot ! Tu as reçu mes grain: Hello, Grommelot! Did you get my corn kernels?
textes.Coucou, coucou ! Pomme-de-Pin ! Charpent: Cuckoo, cuckoo! Pomme-de-Pin! Carpenter! Every bridge in Ramure is me! Well, me and my family. And my grandma. Mostly my grandma. They sway a bit? That's normal! That's the point!
textes.Coucou, la flèche ! Tu cours toujours su: Yoo-hoo, speedy! Still running across my bridges? Slow down in the middle, just once: listen.
textes.Coucou, mes belles !: Cuckoo to you too, my lovelies!
textes.Coucou, toi qui as plein de frères et sœ: Hiya, you with all the brothers and sisters! Will you introduce me? Do they like hazelnuts?
textes.Coucou… Ils font boum-boum, comme moi. C: Hiya… They go boom-boom, like me. It's magic.
textes.Coucou… Tu sens la vibration dans le sab: Hiya… Can you feel the vibration in the sand? Close your eyes, it's magical.
textes.Coudre un immense rideau de scène pour l: To sew a huge stage curtain for the Howling Hall, with a piece of fabric given by everyone in Boucan. When it opens, it'll be everyone opening up at the same time.
textes.Couic ! Biscotte surgit de nulle part et: Squeak! Biscotte appears out of nowhere and climbs onto your shoulder.
textes.Couic ! Ça veut dire « merci ». Couic-co: Squeak! That means “thank you”. Squeak-squeak! That means “more cheese, thank you”.
textes.Couleurs de Gaston, en poisson. On ne le: Gaston's colours, as a fish. Found only in the jungle bay. Restores two hearts.
textes.Couper le ruban de la réouverture des qu: To cut the ribbon for the reopening of all four lines of the Column, on the same day, before the people of the Clouds, Hautefond, the Strata and the Dome all gathered together. And give a four-hour speech. Well. Four minutes. I'll make an effort.
textes.Coups de marteau, copeaux qui volent, un: Hammer blows, flying wood shavings, a night of work… and here is the Sloop! Its cabin still smells of varnish. It's waiting for you at the pleasure-boat jetty.
textes.Courageux. Le mystère, c'est le mélange: Brave. Mystery is all the dregs of the bottles mixed together. Nobody knows what's in it. Not even me. It's the most requested.
textes.Courir coûte deux fois moins d'endurance: Running costs half the stamina, and you run 10% faster.
textes.Courir de la fontaine de la place à la p: Run from the fountain on the square to the lighthouse door in under 60 seconds
textes.Courrier ! … Ah non, pas pour toi. Bonjo: Post! … Oh no, not for you. Hello anyway!
textes.Course abandonnée. Retourne à la fontain: Race abandoned. Go back to the fountain to try again.
textes.Court ! Hum. C'est ce que tout le monde: Short! Hmm. That's what everyone tells me. I'll try. I'll give you a speech on brevity. It will only last an hour.
textes.Cousin ! Une belle plume de quetzal pour: Cousin! A fine quetzal feather for your headdress?
textes.Cousine ! Je t'ai fait un nouveau sac !: Cousin! I've made you a new bag!
textes.Couvert. Mes prévisions de la semaine ét: Overcast. My forecasts for the week were all correct. All of them! I don't understand. I feel useless. Usually I have at least one lovely mistake to study.
textes.Coyotl ! Je remplis la jarre ?: Coyotl! Shall I fill the jar?
textes.Coyotl ! Pas de nouvelle jarre trop bell: Coyotl! No new jar that's too beautiful, I hope?
textes.Coyotl ! Tes pots sont prêts à danser ?: Coyotl! Are your pots ready to dance?
textes.Coyotl ! Une jarre fêlée pour moi ?: Coyotl! A cracked jar for me?
textes.Coyotl demande si c'est vous qui m'envoy: Coyotl asks if you're the one who sent me.
textes.Coyotl dit que je fais trembler ses pots: Coyotl says I make his pots shake. Not true: his pots are dancing. They have taste.
Coyotl says I make his pots shake. Not true: it's his pots that dance. They have taste. And he made me the most beautiful flute on the island. I forgive him for always being wet.
textes.Coyotl et ses manières ! Oui. Dis-lui qu: Coyotl and his manners! Yes. Tell him that Cuauhtli the Eagle sends you, and that Tlaloc is thirsty.
textes.Coyotl fait des jarres bleues avec des y: Coyotl makes blue jars with round eyes and fangs, for his rain god. Odd taste. Beautiful jars. He builds everything by hand, without a wheel. I don't know how he does it. I won't tell him so.
textes.Coyotl fait des jarres si belles pour Tl: Coyotl makes such beautiful jars for Tlaloc that Tlaloc overdoes it. He's always wet, always happy. He makes pots for my flowers. They have round eyes. My flowers are getting used to it.
textes.Coyotl fait les jarres de Tlaloc, avec d: Coyotl makes Tlaloc's jars, with big eyes and fangs! I help him fill them at the lake. He's always wet. He says it comes with the job. I'm always wet too, when I'm with him.
textes.Coyotl fait les jarres de Tlaloc, bleues: Coyotl makes Tlaloc's jars, blue, with fangs. I carry them all the way to Per-Hâpy, to the Egyptians. They scare them. They buy them anyway. A jar that scares people keeps water well.
textes.Coyotl, le potier d'Aztlán, façonne les: Coyotl, the potter of Aztlán, shapes Tlaloc's rain jars; but he only gives one away if the high priest sends you to ask.
textes.Coyotl, le potier, a fait une jarre si b: Coyotl the potter made such a beautiful jar for Tlaloc that Tlaloc made it rain for three days. Coyotl says it was a compliment.
textes.Coyotl, le potier, m'a fait une flûte en: Coyotl, the potter, made me a clay flute shaped like a bird. The first time I blew into it, a hummingbird came, a real one, and perched on the roof to listen. The hummingbird, Huitzilopochtli's bird! I cried, and kept on playing while crying. It made strange notes. The hummingbird stayed anyway.
Coyotl. Your jar is still staring at me.
textes.Cradoc ! On refait le numéro de la fonta: Cradoc! Shall we do the fountain act again?
textes.Cradoc ! Pneu veut encore jouer !: Cradoc! Pneu wants to play again!
textes.Cradoc ! Une bulle de cinq secondes, cet: Cradoc! A five-second bubble this time!
textes.Cradoc a fait une bulle si grande que je: Cradoc made a bubble so big that I got inside it. I floated above the square for three seconds and saw the whole town in rainbow colours. Then pop, I landed back on my feet. I said: “Again.” It took him a week to make another one. I waited next to him the whole time.
textes.Cradoc a voulu faire un numéro de jongla: Cradoc wanted to do a juggling act for my dogs. After ten seconds, Pneu caught a ball in mid-air. Then a second one. Then he ran off with both. Cradoc chased him on his unicycle. Everyone was laughing. Cradoc says Pneu has a future in the circus.
textes.Cradoc dit qu'il peut faire du monocycle: Cradoc says he can ride his unicycle on the ramps. He falls every time. But he falls better than me. I'm taking notes.
textes.Cradoc fait les plus grosses bulles du m: Cradoc makes the biggest bubbles in the world. I got inside one! I floated for three seconds. It was the best moment of my whole journalism career.
textes.Cradoc jongle pour mes chiens. Mes chien: Cradoc juggles for my dogs. My dogs steal his balls. It's a very successful show, just not the way he planned.
Cradoc taught me to blow bubbles. I made one so big a seagull got stuck inside. It flew off all shiny. It still holds it against me.

Cradoc taught me to blow bubbles. My first giant bubble swallowed a seagull. It floated above the harbour, very surprised, then the bubble burst and off it flew, all shiny. It hasn't spoken to us since. But it still shines a bit.
textes.Cradoc tombe de son monocycle quatre foi: Cradoc falls off his unicycle four times a day, with a smile. He's my best customer and my biggest worry.
Cradoc falls off his unicycle four times a day. I ended up sewing cushions into his trousers. He says it improves his balance. Mostly, it improves his landings.
textes.Cradoc tombe tout le temps et se relève: Cradoc falls over all the time and gets back up laughing. He's my role model. And he taught me to blow giant bubbles.
textes.Creuser (pelle en main) là où l'ombre du: Dig (shovel in hand) where the shadow of the Houseboat's mast touches the sea at noon: on the sand, between the mast and the water
textes.Creuser le sable près de la paillote, au: Dig in the sand near the beach hut, at the water's edge (shovel in hand)
Shout quieter, my coals are trembling.
textes.Crie-le encore. Babette n'a pas bien ent: Shout it again. Babette didn't quite hear.
textes.Crier une seule fois si fort que Carène: To shout just once so loud that Carène hears me. And that at the far end of the coast, a fisherman stands up and answers “WHAT?”. I ask for nothing more. Well, one thing: that he buys a sea bream.
textes.Cristaux astraux, fragments de météorite: Astral crystals, meteorite fragments, gears! I also buy scrap metal, bolts, springs. The washers go in my screw box. They make a nice noise. You have {pieces}.
textes.Croc ? Un gamin. Il était insolent à vin: Croc? A kid. He was insolent at twenty, and he still is at nearly fifty. He has his grandfather's eyes. Not the rest, yet.
textes.Croc cherche sa carte partout, sauf là o: Croc is looking for his map everywhere except where he should: up high. Cats climb.
textes.Croc-Gris veille en haut, je piste en ba: Croc-Gris keeps watch up top, I track down below. He's gruff, he says “Halt” to the squirrels. I like him. Every morning, I give him my report. He says “Hm”. That means thank you.
textes.Croc-Gris veille sur nous depuis trente: Croc-Gris has watched over us for thirty years, and he hasn't smiled for twenty-nine. A good wolf. Too serious. I'm working on it.
Croc-Gris has watched over us for thirty years. He's never quite forgiven me for the monster. I like him. He's gentler than he'd like to believe.
textes.Croc-Gris, c'est le garde. Il dit « Halt: Croc-Gris is the guard. He says “Halt!” to everyone, even the leaves. He's got the best house in the village, right at the top, with the zip line! He growls, but he's nice. Shh.
textes.Croc-Gris, il dira « Halte ! », et moi j: Croc-Gris will say “Halt!”, and I'll say “Hot bread!”, and he'll smile. Even him. Nobody can resist hot bread.
textes.Croc-de-Sel se dit « pirate moderne ». I: Croc-de-Sel calls himself a “modern pirate”. He has a silver tooth and a tin mouth. An honest adversary, in his way: he always lies the same way.
textes.Croc-de-Sel, parce que j'ai une dent en: Croc-de-Sel, Salt-Fang, because I have a silver tooth, and because I salt my enemies. Well, I salt them verbally. I'm a modern pirate.
textes.Croc-de-Sel. Toujours à chercher ce qui: Croc-de-Sel. Still looking for what isn't yours?
textes.Crochet ! Question du jour : tu aimes la: Crochet! Question of the day: do you like music?
textes.Crochet ! Ça va ? Ça tire ? Tu dors bien: Crochet! All right? Does it pull? Sleeping well?
Crochet! All right? Does it pull? Sleeping well? Eating?
textes.Crochet a l'air terrible, mais il porte: Crochet looks terrifying, but he carries my crate of shells without me asking. I ask him one question every morning. He answers with one word. His words are my favourite collection.
textes.Crochet ne parle pas, ne rit pas, et dét: Crochet doesn't talk, doesn't laugh, and hates questions. He's the best bosun in the archipelago. When he stands behind me at the table, nobody dares dispute a result. Go figure.
textes.Crochet ne répond à aucune de mes questi: Crochet doesn't answer any of my questions. I ask forty per visit. He says “Hm” forty times. I've learned to read his “Hm”s. He's doing well. That's all that matters.
textes.Crochet passe me voir tous les après-mid: Crochet drops by every afternoon. He says it's for his hook. I think he just likes the warmth of the fire.
textes.Crochet, c'est le seul qui ne m'énerve j: Crochet is the only one who never annoys me. He doesn't talk. When he talks, it's one word. One word, I can hear. And he taps on my cannon to tell me when to fire. He's a friend. DON'T REPEAT THAT.
textes.Crochet, mon ami ! Tu me portes chance,: Crochet, my friend! Will you bring me luck tonight?
textes.Crochet. Il vient tous les après-midi. I: Crochet. He comes every afternoon. He doesn't talk. Neither do I. He's a friend. The best.
textes.Croissant ! Le choix des gens simples et: Croissant! The choice of simple, happy people. And of the sergeant. Well, simple, happy people all the same.
textes.Croissant de contrôle, madame. Tout est: Inspection croissant, madam. Is everything in order?
textes.Croquant ! Comme un coquillage ? Il faut: Crunchy! Like a shell? I have to taste one. Will you bring me some?
textes.Croquer un piment infernal devant le Pro: Bite into an infernal chili in front of Professor Malachar (Zébuline sells them at the Great Market)
textes.Croâ ! Tu as entendu ? Il a entendu. Le: Croâ! Did you hear that? He heard. Look at him puffing up his feathers. Thanks, {surnom}: now he'll think he's an eagle AND a king.
textes.Croâ ! … Pardon. Bienvenue à l'auberge !: Ribbit! … Sorry. Welcome to the inn!
textes.Croâ dit qu'il a vu une porte de pierre,: Croâ says he saw a stone door, right at the top, on the edge of the crater. Croâ also says he's an eagle. So…
textes.Croâ n'a pas oublié que tu préfères les: Croâ hasn't forgotten that you prefer crows. He's saving you a feather. An old one. He's a bit stingy.
textes.Croâ porte son nouveau manteau de plumes: Croâ is wearing his new feather coat. He's unbearably proud.
textes.Croâ refuse. Il dit que vous savez march: Croâ refuses. He says you know how to walk.
textes.Crrr… Un tour de clé. Le ressort se tend: Crrr… One turn of the key. The spring tightens.
textes.Crrr… crrr… Deux tours. Encore un !: Crrr… crrr… Two turns. One more!
textes.Cuauhtli croit que le soleil a besoin de: Cuauhtli believes the sun needs people in order to rise. Here, Rê is reborn all by himself. We'll never agree, and we discuss it every year with pleasure.
textes.Cuauhtli est grave et sage. Il me racont: Cuauhtli is solemn and wise. He often tells me the story of Tecciztécatl, the god who was too proud. I don't know why he tells it to me. There are other proud people in Aztlán.
textes.Cuauhtli m'a appris presque tout. Il est: Cuauhtli taught me nearly everything. He's grave, strict and fair. He almost never laughs. But I once saw him smile at a dog. Pilli's dog. Just once.
textes.Cuauhtli m'achète tout mon copal pour le: Cuauhtli buys all my copal for the gods. He says I sell it too dear on feast days. On feast days, the gods eat more. Naturally it costs more.
Cuauhtli sent me: Tlaloc is thirsty.
textes.Cuauhtli sert le Serpent à Plumes, lui a: Cuauhtli serves the Feathered Serpent too. He calls him Quetzalcóatl. He says he's their god. He's ours. We discuss it every year, politely, for hours.
textes.Cuauhtli, c'est le grand prêtre. Il est: Cuauhtli is the high priest. He's very tall and very serious, and he won't let me climb the temple stairs. But he tells stories well. Even if it's to make me come back down.
textes.Cuauhtli, le grand prêtre d'Aztlán, cher: Cuauhtli, the high priest of Aztlán, is looking for someone to offer rain to Tlaloc and fire to Huitzilopochtli at the top of the Great Temple, and to go down beneath the temple, into the hall of the Five Suns.
textes.Cueille donc ! Les bacs sont là, contre: Go on, pick one! The planters are over there, against the wall. Choose a nice red one: the white ones are still sulking.
textes.Cueillies sous la lune, comptées, parfai: Picked under the moon, counted, perfect. The usual price?
textes.Cueillir cinq bouquets de cempasúchil su: Pick five bouquets of cempasúchil on the chinampas, south and west of the lake of Aztlán
textes.Cueillir cinq fleurs de braise sur les p: Pick five ember flowers on the slopes of the Great Blaze (away from the lava flows)
textes.Cueillir les cinq champignons de lune, a: Pick the five moon mushrooms at the edge of the forest ponds around Ramure (the big pond west of the Circle, the pond in the Games Clearing, and the ones to the west, south and north)
