textes.Cueillir trois champignons des bois dans: Pick three wild mushrooms in the Twisted Wood (south-west of the island)
textes.Cueillir trois touffes d'herbe à fièvre: Pick three tufts of feverweed at the water's edge in the Drowned Marsh (west of the island)
textes.Cueillir un Arc-en-ciel, aux lamelles de: Pick a Rainbow, with gills of every colour (in the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Cueillir un Babillard, qui fait de petit: Pick a Chatterbox, which makes little noises when you come near (in the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Cueillir un Bolet-Ressort, au chapeau or: Pick a Spring-Bolete, with its bouncy orange cap (in the Spore Cathedral, the old gasholder south of the town)
textes.Cueillir un Petit-Géant, minuscule mais: Pick a Little-Giant, tiny but very proud (in the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Cueillir un bouquet de tournesols dans l: Pick a bunch of sunflowers in Granny Sunflower's garden (in the Flower Camp, south-west of the campfire)
textes.Cueillir une Lunaire, pâle et argentée (: Pick a Moonling, pale and silvery (in the Spore Cathedral)
textes.Cuisinier ? … Bon, c'est pas mal non plu: A cook? … Well, that's not bad either. I'll make flying pancakes. Will you want some?
textes.Curieuse, comme toujours. J'ai goûté une: Curious, as always. I tasted a jungle berry this morning. I'll tell you tomorrow whether it was a good idea.
textes.Curieuse. Toujours curieuse. C'est mon h: Curious. Always curious. It's my favourite mood.
textes.Céleste ! Il me reste dix secondes d'hie: Céleste! I have ten seconds left over from yesterday.
textes.Céleste Altaïr ? Elle préside depuis son: Céleste Altaïr? She presides from her office, or else she strolls about the Esplanade listening to people. She says you decide better with your feet on the ground. Well, on the City.
textes.Céleste Altaïr préside une ville en l'ai: Céleste Altaïr presides over a city in the air, and I over a city under the water. Two glass cities, at the two ends of the Column. She speaks in weather, I speak in tides. We had never met before the reopening. We had been writing to each other for twenty years.
textes.Céleste Altaïr écoute tout le monde. Mêm: Céleste Altaïr listens to everyone. Even me. And I talk a lot.
textes.Céleste Altaïr, aux Nuées, m'envoie des: Céleste Altaïr, up in the Clouds, sends me clouds in jars. They arrive empty: a cloud can't stand the pressure, apparently. I have a whole shelf of empty jars. In the evening, I look at them. They hold the thought. And it's the thought that counts.
textes.Céleste dit avoir vu une lumière bleue s: Céleste says she saw a blue light on Stoneheart. A blinking light. I'd love to know what powers it.
textes.Céleste est la meilleure astronome de l': Céleste is the best astronomer in the archipelago. She takes me seriously. Grown-ups usually say “how sweet”. Céleste says “show me your calculations”.
textes.Céleste est la seule personne de Cliquet: Céleste is the only person in Cliquetis who looks further than I do. She showed me the blue glow. Since then, I sleep with a question.
textes.Céleste et moi, on a mesuré la lueur ble: Céleste and I measured the blue glow of Stoneheart for weeks. One pulse a minute. I calculated the power you'd need for a glow like that, seen from so far away: more than the whole city put together. I redid the calculation three times. Céleste just said: “Like a heart.” I couldn't find anything more scientific to say.
textes.Céleste m'a prêté un carnet d'observatio: Céleste lent me an observation notebook. A real one, in blue leather, like hers. On the cover she wrote “Margot, astronomer”. Not “apprentice”. Astronomer. I write everything in it: the stars, the moon, and Achille, for Adèle. We worked out together that he goes round in a circle every seven minutes. He's not a comet, but he's regular.
textes.Céleste regarde le ciel comme j'écoute u: Céleste looks at the sky the way I listen to a cylinder: holding her breath. We share a secret. A secret with a melody.
textes.Céleste tient la ville comme Séraphin te: Céleste runs the city the way Séraphin ran his engines: calmly, and looking at the sky before deciding. She thinks I talk too much. She still lets me speak at the Council. She's a good First Councillor.
textes.Céleste veille sur mon frère toute la nu: Céleste watches over my brother all night, while I sleep. Well, while I try to. She's the best friend you could have: a friend with a telescope.
textes.Céleste vit à l'envers de tout le monde,: Céleste lives the opposite way round to everyone else, like Madame Bricolette's watch. She brings me the star forecast, I fill her flask. Between people who work while the others sleep, we understand each other.
textes.Céleste… Chez vous, cette nuit, c'était: Céleste… At your place, last night, was it twice?
textes.Côté désert, comme la dernière fois. Mba: Desert side, like last time. Mbarek asked who was sleeping next door. His first question in a year.
Desert side… You like silence, then. I'll put you on the east side, near Mbarek. He doesn't talk, he looks at the stars. You'll see, it's catching.
textes.Côté est, la mer est plus profonde. Les: On the east side, the sea is deeper. The big groupers hang around there. Bring me one, I'll pay you well.
textes.Côté mer ! Tu aimes entendre les barques: Sea side! You like hearing the boats leave before dawn. I'll put you on the terrace, next to Selma. If you find blue on your sheets, it's her.
textes.Cœur du Sustentateur numéro deux : tout: Heart of Levitator number two: all is well. It's humming in E flat. Engineer Nova says that's the note of happiness.
textes.D'ACCORD ! JE SONNERAI AU REFRAIN !: ALL RIGHT! I'LL RING ON THE CHORUS!
textes.D'ACCORD ! … Juste un petit ding ?: ALL RIGHT! … Just a little ding?
First the rosary, then the adventure. Father Clotaire says you must do things in order. And I fall less when I do things in order.
textes.D'abord rêver, ensuite voir. Je vais l'é: First dream, then see. I'm going to write that on the blackboard. In big letters. My pupils have always dreamt of the sky. Soon, they'll see it. And I think they'll find it even more beautiful, because they'll have dreamt it first.
textes.D'accord ! J'ai pris mes prières, mes ba: All right! I've packed my prayers, my bandages and my courage. The courage is a bit small. But it's there.
textes.D'accord ! J'en prépare une en forme d'é: All right! I'm making a star-shaped one!
All right! I'll get ready, then.
textes.D'accord, Maman ! Mais je peux améliorer: OK, Mum! But can I improve the bellows?
All right, I'll take care of it.
textes.D'accord, je rentre au Temple. Que l'Aub: All right, I'll go back to the Temple. May the Dawn watch over you… and over your socks.
textes.D'accord, mais elle a déjà mangé tout le: Okay, but she's already eaten all the honey!
textes.D'accord, mon frère. Juste une banane à: Deal, my brother. Just one banana for the little one there.
textes.D'accord. Je respecte. Je te photographi: OK. I respect that. I'll photograph you in my head, then. It's blurry, but it doesn't fade.
textes.D'accord. Je retourne au temple. Si vous: All right. I'll go back to the temple. If you need me, I'll be there, praying for you. Very hard.
textes.D'accord. Je retourne à la Guilde. J'ai: All right. I'll go back to the Guild. I have a chapter to finish.
textes.D'accord. Je retourne à mes livres. Merc: All right. I'll go back to my books. Thank you for taking me along…
textes.D'accord. Je vous suis. Je foudroierai l: All right. I'll follow you. I'll zap the monsters. Almost always the monsters.
All right. But I'll dance slowly.
textes.D'accord. Île grande. Mais pas trop atte: All right. Island big. But not wait too long: Grosse-Dent very hungry.
textes.D'après le livre de Madame Olga, un cris: According to Madame Olga's book, a storm crystal channels lightning “forwards”. Not towards the hat, not towards the hair. Forwards. I'd need three. On top of the Fangs.
textes.D'après le livre, il faut trois cristaux: According to the book, you need three crystals. Not two. Not one. Three. I'm sorry to be so precise.
textes.D'après le livre, il faut viser le centr: According to the book, you aim for the centre. I'll aim for the centre. The centre of the monster.
textes.D'après le livre, ne pas se débattre. J': According to the book, don't struggle. I hope he's read the book.
textes.D'après le livre, ça devait faire ça. Ça: According to the book, it was supposed to do that. It did that. I like it when books are right.
textes.D'au-dessus des nuages, Bastien. Comme h: From above the clouds, Bastien. Like yesterday.
textes.D'en haut, l'île ressemble à une tête av: From up high, the island looks like a head with a big scar: the ravine, the Balafre. At the end of the ravine, there's a rock. I swear it's watching me.
textes.D'en haut, à la cime, on voit la mer à l: From up top, at the crown, you see the sea to the east and the mountain to the west. Go up at sunset. Don't tell anyone: it gets too crowded after.
textes.D'ici, la nuit, je vois des lumières dan: From here, at night, I see lights in the sea, far out. That's the Azure Dome, under the water. Sometimes a great shadow passes in front: a whale. The gulls all go silent. Even Firmin.
textes.D'ici, le belvédère, on voit tout le por: From here, the lookout, you can see the whole harbour. In the morning it's blue, in the evening it's pink. I can never manage to paint the pink.
textes.D'ici, on voit le Port des Cordages, la: From up here, you can see Rigging Harbour, the crane turning, and the seagulls flying below you.
textes.D'ici, on voit les lumières de Hautefond: From here, you can see the lights of Hautefond, way down below, and the stars, way up above. And us, in the middle. It's a good spot.
textes.D'ici, on voit tout : la baie, les deux: From here you can see everything: the bay, the two points, the meadows, and Stoneheart in the distance, with the highland snow behind it. On a clear day you can even see the caravans' smoke, to the south.
textes.D'ici, on voit tout l'archipel par beau: From here, you can see the whole archipelago on a clear day: the village to the north-west, the other islands further off. The seagulls go everywhere. They bring me news. Mostly fish news.
textes.D'ici, on voit toute l'île : le Mont Fus: From here, you can see the whole island: Mount Charcoal to the north, the Rubbed-Out Pond and its waterfall, the Hatching Wood to the west, the White Meadows to the east, the Strand to the south. A real drawing. Only the colours are missing.
textes.D'ici, on voit toute la place. Et tout l: From here, you can see the whole square. And everyone. I know everything that happens in the village. Everything.
textes.D'où vient ce petit nuage ?: Where does this little cloud come from?
textes.D'un bout à l'autre de la Colonne, {surn: From one end of the Column to the other, {surnom}, the four worlds hold together thanks to people who check things. Engineer Nova, up in the Clouds, counts the lift of her Levitators. I count the pressure in my domes. She keeps an island in the air; I keep a town under the water. We write each other numbers. Those are our friendship letters.
textes.D'un jardin où les vieux elfes boivent l: From a garden where old elves drink their tea while it's hot.
textes.D'une écriture toute ronde : « Bonjour,: In very round handwriting: “Hello, do you have any bolts? Even a small one. Even a teeny-tiny one. Reply by capsule, it's urgent. Pimprenelle, age nine, future Grand Liftkeeper.”
From an island far from here.
textes.DES GRIBOUILLIS ?! J'ai cartographié qua: SCRIBBLES?! I've mapped forty islands, three seas and a continent! The continent didn't exist, fine, but the map was magnificent! Get out of my tower!
textes.DING DING DING ! Mélusine hurle depuis l: DING DING DING! Mélusine shouts from the Town Square: “ALERT! ALERT! All adventurers to the Southern Fields: THE TURNIPS HAVE WOKEN UP! Catch them before they replant themselves!”
textes.DIS-MOI, {surnom} ! … Pardon. Dis-moi :: TELL ME, {surnom}! … Sorry. Tell me: do you prefer quiet places, or places where there's shouting?
textes.DONG… DONG… La cloche du Léviathan réson: DONG… DONG… The Léviathan's bell echoes through the whole hull. Somewhere, Ewen shouts: “It wasn't me!”
textes.Dagna ! Ton ragoût s'est vendu en une he: Dagna! Your stew sold out in an hour!
textes.Dagna ! Un tonneau de blonde pour ton ra: Dagna! A barrel of golden fizz to go with your stew.
textes.Dagna croit que mes corbeaux me réponden: Dagna thinks my crows answer me. She's right, but I won't tell her: she'd repeat it to a hundred dwarves before the stew.
textes.Dagna dit que c'est son ragoût qui fait: Dagna says it's her stew that sells my fizz. It's my fizz that washes down her stew! But I resell it at twice the price, so I don't say anything. Hardly anything.
textes.Dagna est persuadée que mon fromage boug: Dagna is convinced my cheese moves on its own. One evening, for a laugh, I slipped Croâ under the cloth. The cheese crossed the table cawing. Dagna dropped her spoon. Ever since, she puts my cheese in the stew as fast as she can. She says it's to calm it down.
textes.Dagna m'a donné un toit, un four et un b: Dagna gave me a roof, an oven and a bowl of stew the day I had nothing left. She sells my fizz on the terrace. I owe her everything. She says all I owe her is barrels.
textes.Dagna me nourrit à midi, que j'aie faim: Dagna feeds me at noon, hungry or not. She counts my smiles. She counts too much. But her stew keeps me warm all through the night watch.
textes.Dagna met trop de champignons dans son r: Dagna puts too many mushrooms in her stew, too much salt in her tempers and too much heart in everything else. The terrace would stand without its gates. Not without her.
Dagna puts too many mushrooms in her stew. I say so, and then I have three helpings.
textes.Dagna, ton ragoût fait chanter mes corbe: Dagna, your stew makes my crows sing.
textes.Dame Ysolde a construit la première cabi: Lady Ysolde built the first cabin with a salad basket. I still have the same salad basket. It's never gone up anywhere.
textes.Dans Xibalba, les Jumeaux ont envoyé un: In Xibalba, the Twins sent a mosquito to bite the Lords! There were fake lords made of wood, and the real ones shouted “ouch!” and said their names! Hun-Came and Vucub-Came! It's the best story in the world!
textes.Dans Yggdrasil, des plantes se sont réve: Inside Yggdrasil, plants have awoken, nasty and hungry. Mother Bramble guards the Tree's crown.
In this one, you've got a hat.
textes.Dans cent ans, on dira…: In a hundred years, people will say…
textes.Dans chaque lettre, Perlée me demande co: In every letter Perlée asks me how many drops I've lost this week. I always answer “none”. But my letters arrive wet, so she knows. She doesn't say anything. In the next letter, she asks again. It's her way of loving me.
textes.Dans chaque toile, je cache un motif. Un: In every canvas, I hide a pattern. A flower, a drop, a musical note. If you look closely at Granny Sunflower's yurt, you'll see a little raindrop, right at the bottom. She's never noticed it. Or she pretends not to.
In two minutes. Fix your hair.
textes.Dans l'affaire des croissants, il est ve: In the croissant affair, he came to question me. Officially: notebook, pencil, cap. Except he had a vanilla cone in his other hand. “Where were you… mmh… last night?” The ice cream dripped onto his notebook. By the end, his notes were unreadable and sticky. He still “kept an eye on the ice-cream man” all week.
In the arena I never hit hard. I push, I lift, I put down gently. People think it's strategy. It's kindness. Don't tell Madame Hurla, she'd shout.
textes.Dans l'herbe… On voit tout, on entend to: In the grass… You see everything, you hear everything, and you can lie down. You're a wise one, you are.
textes.Dans la Bergerie du Vent, j'ai vu une lu: In the Wind Sheepfold, I saw a moon above a pond and a sluice gate.
textes.Dans la Maison des Lames, à Xibalba, les: In the House of Blades, in Xibalba, the knives slice everything that passes. The Twins promised them the flesh of every animal. If you go there, take some venison. I'll give you some.
textes.Dans la Salle des Cours, il devait soule: In the Classroom Hall, he was supposed to lift a feather. My chair took off instead, with me on it! I rose right up to the ceiling. I said “Oh, thank you!” and finished the lesson from up there. He didn't know how to bring me down. I came down on my own. The best lesson of the year.
textes.Dans la baie de la jungle, il y a des po: In the jungle bay there are parrotfish. They're every colour under the sun and they bite like lawyers.
textes.Dans la cale, la première fois, Rouille: In the hold, that first time, Rouille looked at me with her big eyes and asked if we should keep the name. I thought of all the rats sitting there. I said: “We keep the name.” She cried. I didn't know a sentence could do that.
textes.Dans la capsule : quelques pièces, et un: In the capsule: a few coins, and a bolt. The bolt must be from Pimprenelle.
textes.Dans la cité, va à la Chope Ardente. Dis: In the city, go to the Blazing Mug. Tell Ulfa I sent you. She doesn't know me, but say it anyway.
textes.Dans la colonne de verre, un petit nuage: In the glass column, a little cloud spins round and round. It swells, brightens, then lets fall three drops of rain, very proud of itself. That's how they study the birth of clouds.
textes.Dans la forêt des brumes, je me suis per: In the misty forest, I was lost for four days. The compass spun on its own, the moss wiped out my footprints. On the fifth morning, I found a line of shells laid on the moss, one every ten paces. I followed it to the edge of the woods. Nobody. Just shells, like the ones on Fañch's boat. They're drawn in notebook four.
textes.Dans la forêt, je trouve des ruches sauv: In the forest, I find wild hives, in hollow trunks. I don't touch them. I come and tell Yum Kab. He goes with me, very slowly, he talks to the bees, and he carries them back in his arms like babies. Once, I heard the bees buzz louder when he laughed. Maybe they do answer.
textes.Dans la jungle, il y a des crocodiles, d: In the jungle, there are crocodiles, walking skeletons, and worse things. In the port, there's us. Choose your enemies well.
textes.Dans la jungle, il y a des perroquets sa: In the jungle there are wild parrots, red ones and blue ones. Captain Anne-Rose had a red one, Rhubarbe. He flew off towards the old abandoned camp, up north. I heard him swearing over there.
textes.Dans la longue-vue, toute l'île, en noir: In the spyglass, the whole island, in black and white…
textes.Dans la loupe, une montre ouverte : cent: In the magnifying glass, an open watch: a hundred and twenty parts… and an ant taking a nap on the balance wheel.
textes.Dans la nacelle, ça grince doucement, co: The gondola creaks gently, like a boat dreaming of clouds. The passengers have their noses pressed to the portholes.
textes.Dans la poche d'un vieux manteau :: In the pocket of an old coat:
textes.Dans la première salle de l'Arbre, les l: In the Tree's first hall, the fireflies sing a tune in light. Listen with your eyes, and step on the stones in the same order!
textes.Dans la pyramide, il faudra affronter la: In the pyramid, you will have to face the weighing of the heart. Before Anubis, you do not boast: you name the wrongs you have NOT done. “I have not stolen. I have not lied.” A heart heavier than the feather of Ma'at… Ammit devours it.
textes.Dans la salle de la Sève, la lumière ne: In the Hall of Sap, light only goes straight… unless a mirror-flower turns it. Turn them until the light touches the heartwood.
textes.Dans la salle deux, il y a une cuillère,: In room two there's a spoon, a tricorn hat, a horseshoe, a sheet of music and a shark's tooth. They're all labelled. The labels are wrong, I think. The spoon is labelled “little soup shovel”. That must be it.
textes.Dans le Bois Tors poussent les meilleurs: The best mushrooms on the island grow in the Twisted Wood. You have to know which ones: some heal, others make you sing out of tune for three days.
textes.Dans le Bois des Spores vivent les champ: In the Spore Wood live the mushlings: little prankster mushroom creatures. They puff out clouds of coloured spores that make you sneeze. They're not mean. Just very, very annoying. Like cousins.
textes.Dans le Donjon des Mille Marches, mon re: In the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps, my record is the first floor. The Sticky Cellars. Odon wrote “Hilaire: floor 1 (slipped)” in his register. Twelve years running. It's a tradition.
textes.Dans le Glisseur stellaire ! La coque vi: In the Star Glider! The hull hums softly, the lights come on one by one.
textes.Dans le Marais des Noyés pousse l'herbe: In the Drowned Marsh grows fever grass: silvery tufts at the water's edge. It's the best remedy in the world. And the worst located.
textes.Dans le beffroi, tout respire au rythme: In the belfry, everything breathes to the rhythm of the great pendulum. Tick… tock… The clock faces, seen from behind, let the light through.
textes.Dans le berceau : « Rrr… pfff… rrr… » Le: In the cradle: “Zzz… pfff… zzz…” The baby dwarf is already snoring like a forge.
textes.Dans le bon, Amenemhat. L'autre, c'est l: The right way, Amenemhat. The other one is yours.
textes.Dans le cercle des Tombeaux de feu, la c: In the circle of the Fire Tombs, the heat rises from the stones like from an open oven. Even a demon sweats there. Don't linger: fire likes you to pass through, not to settle in.
textes.Dans le coffre : des jouets, une épée en: In the chest: toys, a wooden sword, a one-eyed teddy bear. Nobody.
textes.Dans le coffre : quarante pièces… et le: In the chest: forty coins… and the Crystal of the Dawn, warm as a rising sun. It will fit into the Seal of Winds, in front of the keep.
textes.Dans le coffre de la salle d'armes : qua: In the armoury chest: forty coins, a gold coin… and the Crystal of the Dusk, cold and blue as the evening. The Seal of Winds is waiting for it.
textes.Dans le coffret, au pied du sarcophage :: In the casket, at the foot of the sarcophagus: the last piece of Osiris.
textes.Dans le dôme, on respire. Dehors, il fau: Inside the dome, you can breathe. Outside, you need a mask, or to hold your breath. You have the mask of the Sky Kings. You're lucky.
textes.Dans le globe de verre, le petit nuage f: In the glass globe, the little cloud does a pirouette. It looks like it's waving at you.
textes.Dans le grand registre d'Orsik, il y a u: In Orsik's big ledger there's an empty line, on the eve of the king's coronation, ninety years ago. I asked him what went there. He said: “A smudge.” There was no smudge. He went all pale. I never asked again. But I never filled in the line either.
textes.Dans le moulin, tout tourne : le grand a: In the mill, everything turns: the great shaft, the cogwheel, the singing millstone. It's snowing flour.
In the basket. Not the blue ones.
textes.Dans le sable du désert, la babouche, c': In the desert sand, the babouche is king. You kick it off, you slip it back on without your hands. Try that with your boots.
textes.Dans le sable, deux bouteilles de limona: In the sand, two bottles of lemonade buried to keep cool, with a label: “To share.”
textes.Dans le temple, la voix résonne sous la: In the temple, your voice echoes under the colander and comes out through the thousand holes. It's the only place in the world where you can sing in a thousand pieces at once.
textes.Dans le tombeau du désert, une fresque m: In the desert tomb, a fresco shows a sheepfold beneath the mountain.
textes.Dans les Limbes, sous la cité, la lumièr: In Limbo, beneath the city, the light of the sages wanders from mirror to mirror. Grandpa says you can't order it around: you open the way for it. It's like my lanterns. Light always goes where you let it go.
textes.Dans les Maisons de Xibalba, les Jumeaux: In the Houses of Xibalba, the Twins outwitted every trial: red macaw feathers on the tips of the torches in the Dark House; meat for the blades; bones for the jaguars. Prepare yourself as they did.
textes.Dans les Neuf Cercles, Minos, le juge, p: In the Nine Circles, Minos the judge asks three questions about the journey. He isn't trying to trick you: he wants to know whether you looked properly. Remember everything on the way down: the sentence carved on the gate, the ferryman's name and what he asks for, what lights up Limbo.
textes.Dans les Neuf Cercles, il y a les Limbes: In the Nine Circles there is Limbo: rooms where the light of the sages sleeps in the dark. Mirrors bounce it from one to the next. Turn them the way you'd turn a phrase, until the light reaches where it needs to go. Exam question!
textes.Dans les Neuf Cercles, la porte de Dité: In the Nine Circles, the gate of Dis is guarded by three flying Furies. Three guards against a single traveller: that's unfair. Keep a cool head, well… a lukewarm one, and deal with the one that dives. Captain's advice.
textes.Dans les Neuf Cercles, à Malebolge, il p: In the Nine Circles, in Malebolge, they say there are bridges that spin round on themselves. Spinning bridges! What a magnificent mechanism! Watch the rhythm, count the turns, and cross when they line up. Every mechanism has a rhythm. Even me. Especially me.
textes.Dans les Strates, à côté, tout est rangé: Over in the Strata, next door, everything is tidy, clean, at right angles. The Great Clock, the rails, the galleries. That's beautiful too. I offered to paint their Station. They said no. Then, during the work on the Line, the Station ended up all colourful. Nobody knows how. (He whistles.)
In the gardens. Very big ones.
textes.Dans les livres de quart rangés à la mai: In the logbooks kept at the town hall, I found the same sentence, in the same hand, night after night, for years: “Blue glow, to the west.” Never any comment. I copied it a hundred and twelve times into my journal. When I told Anselme, he went quite pale, then quite red, and shut his door on me. Rightly so, perhaps.
Head in the clouds, as always.
textes.Dans les pieds ? Ha ! La moitié du trava: In your feet? Ha! That's half the job. Tap on the table, let's see if it climbs up to your hands… It's climbing! Slowly, but it's climbing.
textes.Dans les tombeaux du plateau, les momies: In the tombs on the plateau, the mummies sleep in their bandages. And in the pyramid… they say not all of them are sleeping.
textes.Dans les vieux conteneurs du bout du qua: In the old containers at the end of the quay, there are parts from every era. Things nobody makes any more. I keep them. In case someone needs them one day.
textes.Dans les vieux textes, on parle d'un gra: The old texts speak of a great crystal that gave air and light to a whole city. And of a queen with hair of sea foam.
textes.Dans ma collection, il y a le volant d'u: In my collection there's the flywheel of one of his old engines, which fell six years ago. He asked for it back. I said: “What falls belongs to the crane.” He doesn't mention it any more. But I grease his flywheel every month. The way he would have. He mustn't know, or he'll ask for it back again.
textes.Dans ma famille, on fait du pain depuis: In my family, we've been making bread since the pyramid. A great-great-great-grandmother of mine fed the workers on the plateau. As a little girl, I trod the beer mash with my feet, in the big vat, singing. My mother said the beer was better when I sang in tune. It was often bad, those years.
textes.Dans ma famille, on se raconte l'histoir: In my family, we tell the story of the salad basket at bedtime. Lady Ysolde pulled the rope, my ancestor held the pulley, and the basket went up, with a cat inside. The cat was the Column's very first passenger. It never wanted to come back down.
textes.Dans ma famille, on était allumeurs de l: My family were lamplighters. Before the Brass Sun, every lantern in the Galleries had to be lit, one by one, morning and evening. My great-grandmother knew every family by their door. I know them by their bowl. It's the same thing: you look after people.
textes.Dans ma poche, Gros-Louis ! Bien rangé !: In my pocket, Gros-Louis! All tucked away!
textes.Dans ma poche, j'ai un dessin. Une balei: In my pocket I have a drawing. A pencil whale, with a big smile and too many fins. Youssef drew it when he was little. When he tells me about his whales, I pretend not to believe him. But the drawing, I always carry it. Even at sea. Especially at sea.
textes.Dans mon vieux livre de remèdes, il y a: In my old book of remedies, there's a drawing of the elves' moonflower, in faded ink. Rose copied it out big and pinned it above her sink. I have it above my counter. We promised each other that the day we see a real one, we won't pick it. Just look at it.
textes.Dans sa vitrine : « Sabre de Tolède, piè: In his window: “Toledo sabre, rare piece”. I went in. I picked it up. I turned it over. On the guard, a little hammer. My mark. Forged here, three years ago, stolen, resold, come back. Isaac offered me a friend's price. I took an iron bar. I bent it. The friend's price went down. A lot.
textes.Dans son cercle, sur la place, on servai: In his circle, on the square, they served tea before every story. “Tea first,” Ba Sidi would say. I drank eleven glasses. Eleven! By the tenth story, I was telling it standing on a stool. Ba Sidi said it was the first time a bear had danced in his halqa. It wasn't a dance. It was the tea.
textes.Dans son histoire, je combats une pieuvr: In his story, I fight a thirty-armed octopus for three days and three nights. The children come and ask to see my scar. I do have one, but it was a shark, the first year. Just one, very ordinary. They're disappointed. I hate disappointing children. Thanks, Protée.
textes.Dans son zine, Cerise a une rubrique qui: In her zine, Cerise has a column called “Tornade's Blunders”. It's the longest column. It has sequels. I asked for a column called “Tornade's Wins”. She said okay. The column is one line long. She says she's waiting for news.
textes.Dans ton sac, le journal de bord se met: In your bag, the logbook starts to glow! In the Moonglow, silver lines appear on the blank pages: “I entrusted the Seal of Sea Spray to our Figurehead Lady. She will only give it back to whoever shows her her three sisters: the sands, the bronze and the mists. — Yves Kerhervé, last captain of the Léviathan.”
textes.Dans tous les sens, Citlali ! C'est plus: Every way round, Citlali! It's safer.
textes.Dans un cartouche royal, on lit de haut: In a royal cartouche, you read from top to bottom: first the god who writes, then the one who watches, last the one who shines. Thoth's ibis, the eye of Horus, the disc of Ra. Any apprentice knows that. Well… should know.
textes.Dans un cliquetis, les trois armures de: With a clatter, the three suits of armour in the armoury turn their heads toward you… and draw their swords.
textes.Dans un coin, un berceau. Dedans, un tou: In a corner, a cradle. Inside, a tiny dwarf sleeping, fists clenched like two little hammers.
textes.Dans un conte, oui. Dans la vraie forêt: In a fairy tale, yes. In the real forest: never!
textes.Dans un grog, Doc ! Dans un grog !: In a grog, Doc! In a grog!
textes.Dans un lot de vieilleries acheté à un m: In a lot of old junk I bought from a sailor, I found a purple murex, splendid. Ten coins at least. I looked at it, and I thought of Coquille. I gave it to her. For free. She turned it every which way, looking for the catch. There wasn't one. Don't tell anyone about that, I beg you. I have a reputation.
textes.Dans un recueil, j'ai trouvé un petit pa: In a collection, I found a little folded slip of paper, with a line of verse in fine handwriting: “Night keeps what day forgets.” I answered with another line, in the ledger. The next day, there was a new one. For months, we've been writing a poem together. I think it's her. I hope so.
textes.Dans un sens, oui. Dans l'autre, il fait: One way, yes. The other way, it makes smoke.
textes.Dans un tombeau qui ne crache plus de fl: In a tomb that no longer spits flames: a vial of sap and a handful of coins. (The owner has gone on vacation.)
textes.Dans une lettre, il m'a dessiné la vue d: In one letter, he drew me the view from the Hautefond Belvedere. The drawing was all blurry. He explained he'd done it with his eyes half shut. It's my favourite drawing.
textes.Dans une vieille veste de Tapage, j'ai t: In an old jacket of Tapage's, I found a ticket for a gig at the Hall, dated 1978. Proof that Barricade was right! I looked at Trocante. Trocante looked at me. We put it back in the pocket, and I sewed the pocket shut. We kept the peace. It's worth more than a date.
In your headline, my dear friend.
textes.Danser au mariage de Lulu, un jour. Être: To dance at Lulu's wedding one day. To be invited, show up on time, and dance with my daughter without looking anywhere else. Just one waltz. Even at a hundred and forty-five.
textes.Danser le pogo à un concert de la Halle: Join the mosh pit at a Howling Hall concert
textes.Danser sur la Terrasse du Ciel, à cent c: To dance on the Sky Terrace, a hundred and fifty metres up, with the whole city shining below. And, for once, have the city watch me.
textes.Danser un jour sur une vraie plage, là-h: To dance one day on a real beach, up there, on warm sand, with no ledge and no canal to fall into. And see if you can splash the sun.
textes.Danser une dernière fois au Cercle, peti: To dance one last time at the Circle, little one. For real, not just in my head. With Tilleul, who walks as badly as I do: between the two of us, we'll make a lovely crooked step.
To dance one night in the square at Tazira. To see if the moon over there, the one that grows thin, watches me too.
textes.Danser une seule fois sur une vraie scèn: To dance just once on a real stage down below, on creaky boards, with people clapping their hands who don't know that a dancer of light is a rare thing. And for them to simply dance with me.
textes.Danser à la Nuit des Lanternes: Dance at the Night of Lanterns
textes.Danser à la prochaine fête de l'Aube jus: To dance at the next Dawn festival until sunrise, with Ilyria's longest ribbon. And at dawn, for someone to finally hand me a letter, instead of running off again.
textes.De Gaspard Ressort, horloger : « Cher cl: From Gaspard Ressort, clockmaker: “Dear customer, your cuckoo clock sings a quarter-tone too high. Kindly bring it back to the shop. It knows what it did.”
textes.De belles plumes noires ! Croâ va être j: Lovely black feathers! Croâ will be jealous. Here: three cheeses and twenty coins. Eat the cheese quickly. It's… alive.
textes.De face ! Franc, direct, j'aime ça. Rega: Front view! Frank, direct, I like that. Look at the lens, smile… there. I can picture you already. Nicely centred, for once.
textes.De jour, on voit… le ciel. Et un pigeon,: By day, you can see… the sky. And a pigeon, right up close, looking at you from the other end.
textes.De l'autre côté de l'île, à l'est, un vi: On the other side of the island, to the east, an old grump lives perched in a tree. Octave Taillefer. He sells shovels that bend and swords that rust. Don't tell him you know me.
textes.De l'eau ? (Il hoquette.) J'en ai vu. Un: Water? (He hiccups.) I've seen it. Once. It was all… see-through. Didn't like it. Hey! Are you making fun of me? Hic!
textes.De l'eau ? Au Coco Loco ? … Bon. D'accor: Water? At the Coco Loco? … Fine. All right. I'll still give you a slice of lemon and a little umbrella. Got to keep up the style.
textes.De l'eau ?! Hic ! Toute transparente ? B: Water?! Hic! All see-through? Brr. You're brave, you are. Me, I've seen water up close, once. Very close.
textes.De l'eau avec la lune dedans. Ça reste d: Water with the moon in it. Still water!
textes.De l'eau, c'est de l'eau. Même avec la l: Water is water. Even with the moon in it.
textes.De l'eau. De Rainville. Fraîchement tomb: Water. From Rainville. Freshly fallen from the sky this morning. It's the house speciality.
textes.De l'herbe, de la terre, et pas le moind: Grass, earth, and not the slightest eye. This one is looking at its feet… which it doesn't have.
textes.De l'obsidienne pure ! Regarde comme ell: Pure obsidian! See how it drinks the light. Here, two gold coins from my chest. And a rune carved into your memory: “Fire guards fire.” You'll understand one day.
textes.De la Confrérie des Liftiers : « Objets: From the Liftkeepers' Guild: “Lost property found in cabin number three: an umbrella, a feathered hat and Barnabé's courage. Please come and claim them at the counter. Especially the courage.” Mistress Capucine Rouage.
textes.De la brume du matin, cueillie sur la gr: Morning mist, gathered over the big pond and bottled by Pivoine. It swirls gently behind the glass.
textes.De la couleur de la sauce… C'est la meil: The colour of sauce… That's the best answer. There's no name for that colour. Someone should invent one.
textes.De la graisse de chèvre du désert ! Ça n: Desert goat fat! That's completely different!
textes.De la joie ! Alors le Cristal avait rais: Joy! Then the Crystal was right to quiver. Those who arrive laughing often stay longer than they'd planned.
textes.De la mer ! Quelle réponse ! Comme dans: From the sea! What an answer! Like in the legends. I'll draw you a little wave in the corner of my map. With a question mark. Does that suit you?
textes.De la mer ?! Il y a des graines dans la: From the sea?! Are there seeds in the sea? Seaweed seeds? Oh, I need a seaweed seed. I absolutely need one.
textes.De la mer vers les nuages. Elles t'enten: From the sea towards the clouds. They can hear you.
textes.De la mer. (Il regarde l'horizon.) Hm. C: On the sea. (He looks at the horizon.) Hm. Like me.
textes.De la mousse ! Beaucoup ! Alors tu vas f: Froth! Lots! Then you'll end up with a moustache like mine. Welcome to the chocolate moustache club!
textes.De la nuit ! Enfin quelqu'un ! Montez à: Night! At last, someone! Come up to the Observatory whenever you like. I'll show you the rings of… well, you'll see. It's magnificent.
textes.De la peur ? C'est honnête. Moi aussi, l: Fear? That's honest. I was afraid the first time too. Fear is the courtesy we pay to the unknown. Then we go in.
textes.De la poésie… Ah. Alors tu sais que les: Poetry… Ah. Then you know words can keep you warm. I'll lend you my favourite collection. It isn't signed. It's the best one.
textes.De la terrasse du Fondouk, on voit loin: From the Fondouk's terrace you can see far into the dunes. On the first day I saw him go behind the big dune. In the evening he came past in front of it. The next day he went behind it again. Three times the same dune. I was drinking my tea. Zineb asked what I was watching. I said: “A pirate learning.”
textes.De la terrasse du Fondouk, on voit toute: From the Fondouk's terrace, you can see the whole town, the port, the Skala, and the dunes beyond the ramparts. At sunset, everything turns pink.
textes.De la tisane. C'est tout ce qu'il en res: Herbal tea. That's all that's left of it.
textes.De la tour, on voit la passe, toute la b: From the tower, you can see the channel, the whole bay, the east beach, and on a clear day, the smoke of Carène to the west.
textes.De là-haut, sur la tour, on voit toute l: From up there, on the tower, you can see the whole island. Stoneheart to the south, with its perfectly round plateau. It looks like the face of a giant clock. Without hands.
textes.De ma terrasse, je vois tout : la fontai: From my terrace I see everything: the fountain, the clock, the sweethearts, the pickpockets. There aren't any pickpockets. But I'd see them.
textes.De midi à quatre heures, je remplace mon: From noon to four, I stand in for my uncle on watch. I keep an eye on the forest. Well, mostly on the Games Clearing, to watch Bondi train. Two years ago Éclair fell at the root bend; I shouted “you OK?” as I went by, without stopping, it was the race. Since then she looks at me like a skewer. She's cross with me, I think. I get it, mind you.
textes.De mon kiosque je vois la plage, la prom: From my kiosk I can see the beach, the promenade and the beach hut. I know everything that happens here. Well, everything that happens between ten in the morning and eight at night.
textes.De mon temps, c'était la grand-mère de M: In my day, it was Mistress Capucine's grandmother who ran the ticket office. She counted the passengers over the top of her spectacles. Not a single mistake in forty years.
textes.De mon temps, il n'y avait pas de sonnet: In my day, there was no bell: the liftkeeper shouted “DING!” himself. I had the finest voice in the whole Column. The pigeons used to come and listen to me.
textes.De mon temps, la Ligne était déjà fermée: In my day, the Line was already closed for works. And in my father's day, it was open. I'm glad I lived long enough to come full circle.
textes.De mon temps, la cabine, c'était un pani: In my day, the cabin was a salad basket!
In my day, the cabin was a salad basket on the end of a rope. We pulled our way up and prayed our way down. And we nearly always got to the right floor.
textes.De mon temps, la capsule était déjà blan: In my day, the capsule was already white. It's still white. I've gone white too. We've grown old together.
textes.De mon temps, la queue faisait trois mèt: In my day, the tail was three metres long. And we thought that was long.
textes.De mon temps, le Funiculaire était déjà: In my day, the Funicular was already here. Then it closed for twelve years. Then it reopened. Me, I've never moved. Now the world comes to see me.
textes.De mon temps, les pigeons payaient leur: In my day, pigeons paid for their tickets!
textes.De mon temps, les voitures roulaient par: In my day, cars drove on the ground. They did, really.
textes.De mon temps, on criait « ding » nous-mê: In my day, we shouted “ding” ourselves!
textes.De mon temps, on faisait pousser des sal: In my day, we grew lettuces on the roof of the Station. They suffered from vertigo.
In my day, we washed in cold water. And we sang to keep warm.
textes.De mon temps, on montait à la Colonne pa: In my day, we went up the Column by the stairs. A thousand steps. And we said thank you.
textes.De mon temps, on montait à la corde !: In my day, we climbed up a rope!
textes.De mon temps, on s'expliquait d'homme à: In my day, we settled things man to man. And we still filled in a form.
textes.De mon temps, pas de chronomètre : on co: In my day, there were no stopwatches: we counted by singing “Oil Your Gears”. One verse, one trip up. Two verses meant the cabin was taking a nap.
textes.De mon temps, sur les mers…: Back in my day, on the high seas…
textes.De neuf heures à dix-neuf heures, je sui: From nine in the morning to seven at night, I'm on my chair. Five hundred push-ups between whistles. I fish out Yannick's customers, I keep an eye on my starfish challenge, my mum shouts for me to come and help her. In the evening, punch at Kiki's beach hut with Yannick. Then I go home to Lighthouse Street, where my neighbour the sergeant greets me very politely. Too politely.
textes.De neuf à seize ans, j'ai vécu chez l'on: From nine to sixteen, I lived with Uncle Ernest, house 6. Every day, we climbed the cliff staircase together: four hundred and twelve steps, counting out loud. He's the one who named me “Écrou”, nut, because I unscrewed everything that came my way. My real name? Nobody here knows it. Not even you. Especially not you, {surnom}.
textes.De nuages, de virages, et de la boulange: Clouds, turns, and Icare's bakery. Tomorrow morning, she'll want to take off before breakfast.
Clouds, turns, and Icare's bakery. Tomorrow morning, he'll want to take off before breakfast.
textes.De onze à seize heures, ses cartes des f: From eleven till four, his charts of the seabed cover the drawing-room carpet. I walk around them. The guests walk around them. One day, a little boy stepped on an ocean trench, and the professor let out a cry. Since then, when he goes up to the lookout, I tidy them by order of depth. He's never noticed a thing. Or he pretends not to.
textes.De passage. Comme les voiliers. Ils dise: Passing through. Like the sailboats. They all say that, and half of them come back the next year. I'll put you down in pencil.
textes.De petites fraises mûries sous les lampe: Little strawberries ripened under the pink lamps of the hydroponic towers in the Greenhouse Dome. Each one has a redder cheek: the one that faced the lamp. Mélisande talked to them every morning. Restores one heart.
textes.De plus en plus souvent, les robots démé: More and more often, Mr Lisse's mover robots land on the quays to clear out the squats. Mamie Barricade would like you to help the Boucan fight off the next Movers' Raid.
textes.De profil ! Ah, vous avez un bon profil,: Profile! Ah, you do have a good profile, it's true. The left? The right? I'll let you know. I need golden light and a bit of luck.
textes.De près ? … Ha. Ha ha. C'est bien, ça. T: Up close? … Ha. Ha ha. That's good. Very useful, seeing up close. Very. Say, you haven't seen my glasses, by any chance?
textes.De quoi ? Du Couvercle, toujours du Couv: On what? On the Lid, always on the Lid. For everything else, count however you like. Spaghetti, you can count up to a hundred.
textes.De quoi tu parles ? Je ne t'ai rien dema: What are you on about? I didn't ask you for anything.
textes.De quoi veux-tu parler ?: What do you want to talk about?
textes.De quoi voulez-vous parler ?: What would you like to talk about?
textes.De retour au sommet du Grand Temple, ent: Back at the top of the Great Temple, between Tlaloc and Huitzilopochtli.
textes.De retour au sommet du Temple de Kukulka: Back at the top of the Temple of Kukulkan. The sun, at last.
textes.De retour dans la nef de la Cathédrale-F: Back in the nave of the Forge Cathedral. It's nice and warm here.
textes.De retour sur le plateau de Rê, devant l: Back on the plateau of Ra, in front of the pyramid door.
textes.De retour sur les ondes ! Grâce à toi !: Back on the airwaves! Thanks to you! I did a four-hour special to thank you. You didn't hear it? I'll do it again tomorrow.
textes.De retour à la lumière, devant la Porte: Back in the light, in front of the Gate of the Four Seals.
textes.De rien ? Alors viens au lac avec moi, u: Nothing? Then come to the lake with me one morning. And tell me that again when the Duchess pokes her head out of the water.
textes.De rien ?! Tu veux être liftier ? Non, a: Nothing?! You want to be a liftkeeper? No, wait, don't answer, or Mistress Capucine will take you instead of me.
textes.De rien, Bramm. Mange tant que c'est cha: You're welcome, Bramm. Eat it while it's hot.
You're welcome. And smile, it costs nothing.
textes.De rien. Hm. Menteur. Ou nain. Les nains: Nothing. Hm. Liar. Or dwarf. Dwarves say that too.
textes.De six heures à treize heures, je suis à: From six in the morning to one in the afternoon, I'm at the top station; from one to eight, at the bottom one. Two cabins. The red one is the prettier, don't tell the other one. The robot porters are afraid of heights: they take the winding road. Down below, I can see my niece repairing the harbour and Gonzague picking up whatever falls. In the evening, coffee at the counter of the Crankshaft, next to Firmin.
textes.De temps en temps, Victor entre chez moi: Now and then, Victor comes into my shop with a real rare shell, found on the beach, to change my mind. A tiger cone, once, magnificent. I looked at it through the loupe, weighed it and paid the fair price. Not a penny more, not a smile. He left happy anyway. He's always happy. That's his flaw.
textes.De ton mieux. Comme moi avec la sarbacan: Your best. Like me with the blowgun. Enough to eat. Not enough to surprise a jaguar. Just as well.
textes.De tout ! Ho ho ! Un vrai pirate de la f: Everything! Ho ho! A real pirate of the fork! Tonight, I'll save you a portion of my stew of… of something. You can tell me what it was.
textes.De très loin, je suppose ?: From very far away, I suppose?
textes.Debout ! MOI, SIRE TANCRÈDE DE TOURNEVEN: Up! I, SIR TANCRÈDE DE TOURNEVENT, always get back up!
textes.Debout, Pétronille ! … Voilà. Je me suis: Up you get, Pétronille! … There. I talked to myself. It works.
textes.Debout, Tournevent ! Ton père te regarde: Up, Tournevent! Your father is watching! Well, from afar. Very far.
textes.Debout, matelot ! Le soleil se lève sur: Rise and shine, sailor! The sun is rising over the sea.
textes.Debout. Les cristaux chantent encore. Mo: Up. The crystals are still singing. So am I, a little.
textes.Dehors ! Comme la dernière fois. Mais pl: Out! Like last time. But faster.
Outside, at the fish and the sea.
textes.Demain ! Les objets ont besoin d'une nui: Tomorrow! Items need a night to get ready to leave. They're sentimental.
textes.Demain, alors ! Et un fromage, en attend: Tomorrow, then! And a cheese, in the meantime.
textes.Demain, c'est ma première leçon. J'ai dé: Tomorrow's my first lesson. I've already got the helmet. I even wore it to bed.
textes.Demain, c'est un bon jour pour la patien: Tomorrow is a good day for patience, Mixtli.
textes.Demain, cinq heures ? Le vent sera de su: Tomorrow, five o'clock? The wind'll be south-westerly.
textes.Demain, du soleil. Les cartes sont forme: Tomorrow, sunshine. The cards are adamant.
textes.Demain, on essaie au milieu ?: Tomorrow, shall we try somewhere in the middle?
Tomorrow we'll measure again. Gently does it.
textes.Demain, pêche à cinq heures. Qui vient ?: Tomorrow, fishing at five. Who's coming?
textes.Demain, pêche à cinq heures. Tu viens ?: Tomorrow, fishing at five. Coming? I ask everybody, nobody ever comes.
textes.Demain, sans faute, cher ami !: Tomorrow, without fail, my dear friend!
textes.Demain. Ou après-demain. À un jour près,: Tomorrow. Or the day after. Give or take a day, priestess.
textes.Demande à Aurélien. Ça comptera pour dem: Ask Aurélien. It'll count for tomorrow.
textes.Demande à Zéphyrine. Ça comptera pour de: Ask Zéphyrine. It'll count for tomorrow.
textes.Demande-moi de lire ton avenir. Je te di: Ask me to read your future. I'll tell you what the people here are hoping you'll do.
textes.Demander ! La vertu des sages. Les sots: Asking! The virtue of the wise. Fools think they know everything, the wise ask questions. I've been asking them for three centuries. So I'm very, very wise.
textes.Demander ! Très efficace. Mais attention: Asking! Very effective. But careful: people down below always say “straight ahead, then left”. They all have the same map in their heads.
textes.Demander conseil à Perroquet-Joe (son ét: Ask Perroquet-Joe for advice (his stall is on the square of Port-Coutelas, near the well)
textes.Demander des pâtes fraîches à Mamma Lasa: Ask Mamma Lasagna for fresh pasta (at the Pasta Drying Shed in the daytime, at the oven on the Borgo's little piazza at noon and in the evening)
textes.Demander la Clé du Brasier à Frère Cendr: Ask Brother Cendrin for the Brasier key (in the Forge Cathedral, near the Ember Heart)
textes.Demander un grimoire à Théophraste Filan: Ask Théophraste Filandre for a spellbook, at the library (the big slate building, on the way up to the Academy)
textes.Demander une carte stellaire à Sextant (: Ask Sextant for a star chart (in the morning on the Gate lookout, around noon at the Museum, in the afternoon on the Observatory bridge, in the Gardens or at the Spaceport)
textes.Demander à Cargo, le grand androïde dock: Ask Cargo, the big docker android on the Drone Quay (north of the city), if he has a Z-Series voice chip
textes.Demander à Cuauhtli, le grand prêtre (au: Ask Cuauhtli, the high priest (at the foot of the Great Temple), to send you to Coyotl
textes.Demander à Lucas, le docker, le nom de s: Ask Lucas the docker the name of his boat
textes.Demander à Pépé Fernand le nom de sa bar: Ask Grandpa Fernand the name of his boat (on the quay, to the east)
textes.Demander à Sextant s'il a vu Plume-de-Nu: Ask Sextant if he has seen Plume-de-Nuage (he sketches on the Gate lookout in the morning, at the Museum around noon, then on the Observatory bridge, in the Gardens or at the Spaceport)
textes.Demander à Yannick le nom de ses bateaux: Ask Yannick the names of his boats (boat hire, on the quay)
textes.Depuis cent ans, c'est notre façon de no: For a hundred years, that's been our way of saying good morning.
textes.Depuis cet hiver, Bernard fait un détour: Since this winter, Bernard has been taking a detour through the fishermen's alley so as not to pass my window. I can hear him: “hop hop hop” fading away, then coming back on the other side. He adds three hundred metres to his lap to avoid me. Not exactly what I prescribed.
textes.Depuis cinq ans, j'écris à Barnabé, l'ap: For five years I've been writing to Barnabé, the apprentice liftkeeper in Hautefond. Him down there, me up here. We tell each other about our ascents. Mostly he tells me about his descents. He's afraid of heights! A liftkeeper who's afraid of heights! He's the bravest boy I know.
textes.Depuis des années, Salomé veut le trente: For years, Salomé has wanted the thirty-third ingredient of my ras el hanout. She's offered me everything, by caravan and by Zéphyr: ropes, lanterns, a barrel of cider, and once, her own hat. I kept the hat. I didn't give away the secret. She keeps trying anyway. She's a true merchant.
textes.Depuis des mois, je trouve des poèmes da: For months, I've been finding poems in my lantern boxes. Unsigned. About the night, about flames, about a girl who carries the light. One evening, I saw Nox leaving my workshop, bright red, pole in hand. He pretended to check a street lamp. There was no street lamp in front of my workshop. So I had one put in.
textes.Depuis hier soir. Elle est dans ma poche: Since last night. It's in my pocket.
textes.Depuis l'arrivée de Glorb, je le poursui: Ever since Glorb arrived, I've been chasing him to give him my welcome speech. He hides in the Hanging Gardens, among the green plants. He's green. He trembles. Plants don't tremble. I've found him three times. Three times, he went “blorp” and scurried off.
textes.Depuis la fois où il m'a trouvée derrièr: Ever since the time he found me behind him, he says thank you to each stone, out loud, before picking up a shard. Nine thank-yous. He often forgets the smallest one and says two to Doyenne. I nod at the last one, so he'll leave. He's never noticed. The stones have.
textes.Depuis la lunette, j'ai vu une île flott: Through the telescope, I saw a floating island above the clouds, to the west. Nobody believes me. Do you believe me?
textes.Depuis la nuit où il est tombé du quai,: Since the night he fell off the quay, I serve him a special grog: hot lemon, honey, cinnamon, and a drop of rum. A tiny little drop. He's never noticed. He says it's the best grog in the world. All the better. Doc says he'll live to a hundred like that. Me, I want him to live to a hundred.
textes.Depuis la pancarte, Brindille entre à pi: Since the sign, Brindille comes in on foot, on tiptoe. But her wings brush against the shelves, with a sound like crumpled paper. She stops, she blushes, she sets off again. One day, I told her she could fly, but only above the bird shelf. She was so happy she forgot the letter.
textes.Depuis la partie, j'ai un carnet rien qu: Since that game, I've had a notebook just for openings. Eighty-three pages. I work out what the automaton would play if I played this. Or that. Mr Checkmate asked to see it. I only showed him the cover. You don't show your calculations to your opponent. He said: “Logical.” He's learning.
textes.Depuis le Grand Concours du Dessert, Gru: Since the Grand Dessert Contest, Grumbald and I meet every month to “settle it”: he eats my cakes, I eat his frozen lava. We've never managed to settle it. Mostly we've grown tummies. Bulle says we float better and better at the Baths. He's right.
textes.Depuis le bal, Prisme me donne des cours: Since the ball, Prisme has been giving me secret dance lessons in the Zero-Gravity Garden: there, when I fall, I fall very slowly, and I have time to say “this was planned” before I touch the ground. She says I'm improving. Now I only step on one of her feet.
textes.Depuis le bal, je donne des cours de dan: Since the ball, I've been giving Écliptique dance lessons, in secret, in the Zero-Gravity Garden. There, when he falls, he falls so slowly he has time to say “this was planned” before touching the ground. He says he's preparing a danced bow. I daren't imagine it.
textes.Depuis le belvédère du Portail, au sud-e: From the Gate lookout, to the south-east, you can see the whole archipelago. In the morning, the mist makes white lakes between the islands. I draw the islands. The mist, I leave out. It moves too much.
textes.Depuis le belvédère, on voit tout l'arch: From the lookout, you can see the whole archipelago: Port-Azur, the big island to the east, the volcanoes, and Balafre, far to the south. Sextant comes here to draw. He asks me to be quiet. I'm quiet. Almost.
textes.Depuis les pots, elle me sert mon cacao: Since the pots, she serves my cacao with the thinnest froth in Yaxché. One finger of froth. One tiny finger. The others get a whole hand. One day, I won a match and dedicated the victory to her, in front of everyone. The next day, I got two fingers of froth. I'm making progress.
textes.Depuis ma prédiction, Hortense regarde c: Ever since my prediction, Hortense watches every stranger who steps off L'Hirondelle. An umbrella seller, two tourists, a gentleman with a goat. She looks them up and down, then sighs. She says she's keeping an eye on the time. I say she's keeping an eye on the quay.
textes.Depuis mes cinq ans, je cherche le Roi d: Since I was five, I've been looking for the Pond King with Grandpa. He's golden, big as a rabbit, and he laughs. One day I drew him. With a crown, because a king has a crown, that's normal. Grandpa looked at the drawing for a super long time, without saying anything. Even his whiskers stopped moving. Then he pinned it above his bed.
textes.Depuis mes six ans, je tiens les comptes: Since I was six, I've kept the soap accounts. Dad buys too much glycerine and forgets to eat. So I remind him. I've calculated that he blows thirty-one per cent of his bubbles for himself. The rest are for people. He said that was a lot. I said it was normal. Everyone needs bubbles.
textes.Depuis minuit, Taeron. Je t'ai laissé un: Since midnight, Taeron. I left you a lantern next to it.
textes.Depuis notre dispute, il me signale tous: Since our quarrel, he points out every reef he sees from the top of his mast. He's seen fourteen this year. There were two. In exchange, I bring him shells, and I tell him where his glasses are. On his head, most of the time. We're even. Well, he owes me twelve reefs.
textes.Depuis qu'il s'est perdu dans le Bois de: Ever since he got lost in the Ash Wood, Pépin holds my hand at the market. An hour a day, at least. He says it's to reassure me. He's right.
textes.Depuis que Barnabé passe à la teuf avec: Ever since Barnabé started coming to the party with Gaston on his shoulder, the parrot imitates the kick drum. One night, walking home through the jungle, I heard “Boom. Boom.” in the dark, right on a hundred and forty-five. I thought Mistral had put a speaker in the trees. It was Gaston, all alone, on a branch. I ran all the way home.
textes.Depuis que Fusible a branché la fontaine: Ever since Fusible hooked the square's fountain up to the crane, I lift empty containers in the evening, just to make the fountain light up. The kids squeal with joy. One evening, I lifted twenty. Fusible had to change three bulbs. He didn't say anything. He was smiling.
textes.Depuis que Monsieur Fil est arrivé, des: Ever since Mr Fil arrived, machines have been acting up in the Alleys. I looked at one of his programs. There's something hidden inside. Something waiting. I haven't found out what yet.
textes.Depuis que Monsieur Fil est arrivé, j'ai: Since Monsieur Fil arrived, I've had loads more work. Cleaning robots doing the housework next door, a vacuum cleaner that sings, a fridge that orders ice cream all by itself. They'd all installed one of his “cheap” programs. Be careful, {surnom}. You always pay the price afterwards.
textes.Depuis que je suis tout petit, je tape s: Ever since I was tiny, I've drummed on everything. Tables, saucepans, Dad's files. My first drum kit was three filing boxes and a wastepaper basket. Dad said it was “a non-compliant use of office furniture”.
textes.Depuis que l'horloge s'est arrêtée, c'es: Since the clock stopped, I'm the one who tells Django the time. Fifty years of clockwork, it stays in your bones. Before going home for lunch, I tell him: “One o'clock, young man. Nap time.” He packs away his guitar, and the whole square looks as if it's off for a nap with him.
textes.Depuis que la Ligne a rouvert, des gens: Since the Line reopened, folk from up top come down to the Swap Shop. They don't get it at first. They ask: “How much is it?” I say: “What have you got?” They rummage in their pockets. They always find something. A button, a ticket, a marble. Everyone has a treasure in their pockets.
textes.Depuis que la Ligne a rouvert, il en des: Since the Line reopened, they come down from all over, the folk up top. Hautefonders, and even one or two from the Clouds, all pale from being so low. I give them hotpot. They go back up with rosy cheeks. That's diplomacy, my pebble.
textes.Depuis que la Ligne a rouvert, je suis m: Since the Line reopened, I've been up to Hautefond! There's a SKY! Blue! Way up high! No rock! I was scared it would fall. Pimprenelle told me it never falls. She checks every morning. I believe her.
textes.Depuis que la ligne a rouvert, je m'asso: Since the line reopened, I sit on the Station bench after school and ask every traveller: “What's the sky like?” I've filled three notebooks. Rain: “water that falls all by itself”. Wind: “air that runs”. One gentleman just said: “Big.” I wrote “big” really big, across a whole page. It's my favourite page.
textes.Depuis que la montagne gronde, il descen: Ever since the mountain started rumbling, he comes down every night to ask me: “Well?” I answer: “Not today.” He nods and goes back up. One night, he didn't ask anything. He sat down beside me, and we listened to the mountain together until dawn.
textes.Depuis que la montagne gronde, je descen: Ever since the mountain started rumbling, I go down to his alcove every night. I ask: “Well?” He answers: “Not today.” I go back up. One night, I didn't ask anything. I sat down. He passed me his cup of moon water. It was revolting. We listened to the mountain until morning.
textes.Depuis que le Zéphyr passe, Tilleul et m: Since the Zéphyr started sailing, Tilleul and I have been writing to each other. Well, Ewen writes for me, and a little owl over there writes for him. His letters always stop in the middle of a story. I reply: “And then?” He replies with another story. I've been waiting three years for the end of the first one.
textes.Depuis que le Zéphyr se pose sur l'aire: Since the Zéphyr started landing on the pad north of the village, Ramure's post flies all the way to Cliquetis! In every bag, I slip a little note for Commander Zélie Hélice. She writes back. We've never met. Thanks to her, I bring Ardoise's letters to Caramel, postcards from Port-Azur… and a letter that went tick-tock, for Pépin.
textes.Depuis que le cristal pâlit, je tisse la: Since the crystal began to fade, I weave at night, {surnom}. A cape so tight it holds air, like a little dome. If the big one ever goes out, I want my daughter to be able to swim up to the sun without running out of breath. Ondine knows nothing about it. Pélagos pretends not to see it, under the bed.
textes.Depuis que nous sommes arrivés, il y a m: Ever since we arrived, a thousand years ago, I've collected everything that falls from down below. Well, everything that comes up. The birds bring some, the wind too, and Solenne, sometimes, in her suitcases. She says she finds them “in the sky”. The sky is very tidy.
textes.Depuis que tu as vu Triton dans ma sculp: Ever since you saw Triton in my sculpture, he's all I can see. I've turned it to face the wall.
textes.Depuis que tu es arrivé, ma vie a un sen: Since you arrived, my life has meaning. I get up at five, train in the castle courtyard, count the slimes I beat and imagine the ones you beat. I keep watch on you. Discreetly. Behind the fountain. All right. Everyone can see me behind the fountain. But it's the thought that counts.
textes.Depuis que tu passes me voir, ça va nett: Since you started visiting, I've been much better. Don't tell Gaston, he's jealous.
textes.Depuis quelque temps, Ori me lit les run: For a while now, Ori has been reading me the runes out loud, every evening, “for practice”. He reads slowly, and he gets the easiest ones wrong on purpose, so I'll correct him and feel useful. He's a terrible liar. He gets that from me.
textes.Depuis quelque temps, mes chaussures son: For a while now my shoes have been lighter. I swear! I run and it feels like I've got feathers on my heels. It's the training, obviously. I told Ursule, all proud. She said “Hm. Good.” and turned her back on me really fast. She was moved, I think. By my progress.
textes.Depuis quelque temps, ses énigmes sont t: Lately, her riddles are all easy when she's asking me. The other day: “I'm blue, I'm up high, and there are clouds in me.” I answered “the sky”, of course. She clapped much too loudly.
textes.Depuis quelques nuits, Thalassa tisse qu: For a few nights now, Thalassa has been weaving something very big, very tight, that she hides under the bed. She thinks I haven't noticed. I haven't said anything. In the mornings, I leave the longest kelp I can find beside her loom. She doesn't ask where it comes from.
textes.Depuis ses dix ans, je lui offre une per: Since she was ten, I've given her a pearl every birthday. She sews them onto a blue ribbon, one by one. There are fourteen. She wears it on feast days. Ewen asked if it was a captain's necklace. She answered: “No, it's a necklace of years.” He didn't understand. I did.
textes.Depuis une semaine, le Grand Spaghetti V: For a week now, the Great Flying Spaghetti has been sulking: its noodles droop, its eyes stay half-shut, and the volcano rumbles more than usual. The Reverend Father Farfalle has found the recipe that will make it friends again with its followers: the Great Reconciliation dish. It needs Mamma Lasagna's pasta, a ladleful of sauce from the Cooking Pot and parmesan grated with Captain Rigatoni's Golden Grater (which he buried somewhere thirty years ago).
textes.Depuis vingt ans, je dépose mes brevets: For twenty years I've been filing my patents at the Academy. One a week, in good years. Three hundred and twelve in all. All rejected: “already invented”. The most famous is the wheel; they still laugh about it at the Bielle. Héloïse rejects them very kindly, then files them in a drawer with my name on it. A drawer with my name on it… that's something, isn't it?
textes.Depuis, Gaubert m'apporte uniquement des: Since then, Gaubert only brings me golden turnips, the ones caught during the alert, because they don't run any more. He hands them over with a sad look and says: “Cook it gently, it's run a lot.” I invented frog with golden turnips for him. He never eats it. He says he doesn't eat his little ones. He eats the frog and leaves the turnip.
textes.Depuis, Margot passe au stand 5 avec un: Since then, Margot comes by stand 5 with a notebook. She calculates her openings, column by column, and rubs out a lot. One day, she asked me how many cards the automaton had. I didn't answer. She said: “I'll count them.” I'm afraid she'll manage it.
textes.Depuis, elle m'envoie des graines. Pour: Since then she sends me seeds. To say sorry. Zéphyr drops them outside my door. I put them in the fire. They go “pop”. … It's quite nice, “pop”. Don't tell her. She'd send more.
textes.Depuis, elle passe devant ma tente en fa: Since then, she walks past my tent twirling a spoon between her fingers, whistling. She thinks she's annoying me. It works. But the other day, I saw her at the well looking at her arm, and smiling. She didn't know I could see her. I don't know what it means. I won't say a thing. She'd be capable of throwing a spoon at me.
textes.Depuis, il appelle ces trois jours « ma: Since then, he calls those three days “my state visit aboard the Morue Enragée”. He talks about it in his speeches on the square. He says we signed a friendship treaty. We signed an IOU for the honey. But I let him say it. A governor who thinks he owes you a treaty can always come in handy.
textes.Depuis, il m'apporte un bol de soupe tou: Since then, he brings me a bowl of soup every lunchtime. It's kind. But I don't dare. So I pour it into my geranium's pot. It's tripled in size, it grows flowers as big as cabbages, and it smells a little of chilli when you brush against it. I think I've invented a fertiliser. I don't dare tell him that either.
textes.Depuis, il m'envoie des fleurs chaque se: Since then, he's sent me flowers every week, with a little card: “For the tower. Only for the tower.” I put them in a vase on my desk. I've never replied. One day he sent me wisteria from the Cottage. I almost wrote to him. I didn't. But I kept them longer than the others.
textes.Depuis, je cache le dessin dans une chau: Since then, I've hidden the drawing in a sock. A clean sock, rolled up, at the bottom of my suitcase. On Tuesday, when I came back, I found the sock on my bed, neatly folded, with a little note: “Pretty crystal!” I no longer know where to put it. I'm thinking of carrying it on me, in my hat.
textes.Depuis, je joue toutes les nuits sous Fi: Since then, I play every night beneath Fil-d'Aube, Ilyria's tree-house. Thalion grumbles, Aëlwen sighs, Lirael lowers her lantern so it looks prettier. Haldir carries my letters, and I always run to take them back before he knocks. Forty-one verses, and still not the courage. Life is beautiful, and terribly slow.
textes.Depuis, je lui envoie des graines par Zé: Ever since, I've been sending him seeds via Zéphyr, to say sorry. Zéphyr says Grommelot throws them in his fire and they go “pop”. At least he keeps them warm! Last time, I sent him corn kernels, on purpose. They make much prettier pops.
textes.Depuis, je porte tout : les invitations: Since then, I carry everything: invitations to festivals, Taeron's complaints, Aëlwen's herbal teas, and Caelan's letters, which he takes back before I knock. When your boat came through the mist, I was the one who ran to tell Thalion. I'd never carried such big news.
textes.Depuis, je soigne. Les bosses, les égrat: Ever since, I've been healing. Bumps, scratches, sprains, bent antennae. Bulle built me a healing bubble of very soft glass, in the north-east, with a ceiling where you can watch the clouds go by. Patients get better faster looking at the sky. I think the sky does half the work.
textes.Depuis, le professeur cache son dessin d: Since then, the professor hides his drawing in his sock. The left one. I found it anyway, putting away the laundry. I put it back in the sock, neatly folded, with a little note: “Very pretty crystal.” He didn't speak to me for two days. Then he asked me if I really thought it was pretty, that crystal.
textes.Depuis, les nuits de teuf, le kick trave: Since then, on party nights, the kick drum carries across the island all the way to my kapok tree. Clou dances on the roof. One night, he danced with the cash box in his arms. I was picking my coins out of the ferns until dawn. In time with the beat, too.
textes.Depuis, à chaque escale, nos sacs se cro: Since then, at every stop, our bags cross paths and we leave each other notes on the dockets. I send my timetables; she replies that “scheduled” isn't a time, and that Ramure doesn't have streets, it has trees. She signs “Hoo”. I sign “Commander”. She asked me if I had aviator goggles. Obviously.
textes.Dernier morceau ! Non, j'ai menti, il en: Last song! No, I lied, there are three more! “One More, One More”!
textes.Dernier verrou ! Le virus a débranché l': Last lock! The virus unplugged the antivirus. Click the tiles to rotate them, and rebuild the path between the battery ⚡ and the antivirus ✚.
textes.Dernière minute : Larsen demande à tout: Stop press: Larsen asks everyone to talk more quietly. Larsen asked this BY SHOUTING. End of stop press.
textes.Dernière question. Mon frère jaloux m'a: Last question. My jealous brother shut me in a chest and threw me in the river; then he cut my body into pieces. My wife searched for every piece and gave me back life. Since then, I rule the kingdom of the dead. Who am I?
textes.Dernière énigme ! « Plus on m'enlève, pl: Last riddle! “The more you take away from me, the bigger I get.”
textes.Derrière la Skala, il y a des grottes da: Behind the Skala, there are caves in the cliff that the sea fills at high tide. The pirates often look at them through their spyglass.
textes.Derrière le balancier de la grande horlo: Behind the pendulum of the grand clock, hanging from a nail: a little key!
textes.Derrière le balancier, il n'y a plus rie: There's nothing behind the pendulum anymore. Just the ticking.
textes.Derrière le mur fissuré, une petite nich: Behind the cracked wall, a little niche… with an urn.
textes.Derrière le tonneau : une araignée qui t: Behind the barrel: a spider staring at you. It hasn't seen anybody either.
textes.Derrière moi, c'est la Basse-Ville, puis: Behind me is the Lower Town, then the ramps that zigzag up to the castle. People in a hurry try to climb straight up. They come straight back down. On their bottoms.
textes.Derrière mon comptoir, je garde une chop: Behind my counter, I keep a dented mug. It was his father's. Bramm is the only one who drinks from it. One evening, a passing dwarf grabbed it. I snatched it back before he touched the foam. Bramm said nothing. He paid for the dwarf's round. That's his way of saying thank you.
textes.Derrière son comptoir, Ulfa garde une ch: Behind her counter, Ulfa keeps a dented mug. Mine. It was my father's. Nobody else drinks from it. Once, a passing dwarf picked it up. Ulfa took it back out of his hands before the first sip. I said nothing. I paid for his round. His.
textes.Derrière toutes les portes, on rit. Les: Behind every door, there's laughter. The little Moai seem very mischievous… and very curious about you.
textes.Derrière un hublot qui brille : un patch: Behind a shining porthole: a Bilge Rats patch, brand new, forgotten by a very old fan.
textes.Des Serres d'Altitude ! Flora Verdine no: From the High-Altitude Greenhouses! Flora Verdine entrusted us with a box of chrysalises from the third dome. Over there, they were on strike. Here, they're on holiday. For good, I think.
textes.Des araignées ! Ah, ça, il y en a une da: Spiders! Ah, well, there's one in the cabin, on the ceiling. Her name's Lucienne. She's very scared of you too, if that helps.
textes.Des babouches ! Et qui les fait, ces bab: Slippers! And who makes these slippers?
textes.Des ballons ! Des ballons qui montent !: Balloons! Balloons that go up! Up here, they go even higher, naturally.
textes.Des bancs du Belvédère, de l'eau des nua: The benches on the Belvedere, cloud water for the Greenhouses, and the party for the Line's reopening. And the name of the morning cloud. That's the most hotly debated.
textes.Des blocs et des gravats jusqu'au plafon: Blocks and rubble up to the ceiling. Impossible with bare hands… With a shovel, perhaps.
textes.Des bombes de peinture faites maison. Fa: Homemade spray paint. Make me a beautiful wall. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Des bouteilles partout, et dans chacune,: Bottles everywhere, and in each one, a tiny ship. Leaning over his workbench, an old sailor holds his breath.
textes.Des boutons ! Boutons de chemise, de man: Buttons! Shirt buttons, coat buttons, trouser buttons… One day, I'll sew myself a coat out of nothing but them.
textes.Des boîtes d'allumettes partout. Au mili: Matchboxes everywhere. In the middle, a slender golden tower trembles ever so slightly whenever anyone walks.
textes.Des bulles ! Mirabelle est passée par là: Bubbles! Mirabelle's been at it, I recognise her touch. She's an artist, that girl. How long were you sneezing bubbles?
textes.Des bâtons bien droits : de futurs manch: Nice straight sticks: future handles. You've got a good eye.
textes.Des cailloux ! Gratuits, ramassés soi-mê: Pebbles! Free, picked up yourself… You're my worst nightmare. But I respect it. I could paint them for you, your pebbles. Cheap. Authentically.
textes.Des cartes des vents : des flèches parto: Wind maps: arrows everywhere, spirals, little clouds drawn in blue ink. In one corner: “Here, the wind turns round three times before making up its mind.”
textes.Des cartes du ciel couvrent les murs. Au: Star charts cover the walls. In the middle, the planets turn, each at its own pace.
textes.Des cartes postales ! Court, joli, avec: Postcards! Short, pretty, with a picture. That's very good. But don't buy them from Victor, eh! … Well, yes. A few. He needs it.
textes.Des cauchemars ? Oh, mon petit. Tiens, p: Nightmares? Oh, little one. Here, take this lavender sachet, put it under your pillow. And if they don't go away, come and see me. Nightmares are meant to be told.
textes.Des centaines de petites plantes, serrée: Hundreds of little plants, packed together as if in a nest. A ladybird looks at you, then goes back about its business.
textes.Des cercles de bois tressés de fil tourn: Wooden hoops woven with thread turn gently at the ends of their strings, with beads and feathers. A craftswoman knots a net by the light of the crown.
textes.Des champignons bruns pour la soupe, et: Brown mushrooms for the soup, and seeds for your garden up top. The glowing ones aren't for sale: they're for looking at. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Des champignons de braise ! Ils brillent: Ember mushrooms! They're still glowing! Here: three bowls of stew, piping hot. Four hearts each. Blow on it.
textes.Des chansons ! Pas trop fort, alors : le: Songs! Not too loud, then: the tomatoes blush, and the roses get prickly.
textes.Des chats. Partout. Sur le fauteuil, sou: Cats. Everywhere. On the armchair, under the table, on top of the wardrobe…
textes.Des chaussettes chauffées par une mini-c: Socks warmed by a mini-boiler at the ankle. Ideal for the highlands.
textes.Des chauves-souris ! Elles volent à haut: Bats! They fly at head height and swoop at you: strike them when they dive.
textes.Des chiens d'enfer ! Quand la gueule s'o: Hellhounds! When the jaws open and glow red, they're about to spit fire and pounce: step aside, then strike.
textes.Des chiens d'enfer sauvages ont pris le: Wild hellhounds have taken over the lava field, east of the Great Blaze, and growl at travellers. Captain Pyrus would like someone to drive them away.
textes.Des clients veulent les acheter. Le Lord: Guests want to buy them. The Lord offered an indecent sum for the little view of the port, the one with a black seagull on the jetty. I replied: “They are not for sale, milord. They belong to the house.” That seagull looks a great deal like a moustache. I didn't go looking for it. I spotted it straight away.
textes.Des coquelicots ! Ils sont fragiles, il: Poppies! They're fragile, you have to be really careful. There. Don't run too fast.
textes.Des coquillages de la VRAIE mer ! Ils so: Shells from the REAL sea! They're so pretty! Here, this is for you: a pearl I found in the fountain. Shh!
textes.Des coucous, des pendules, des horloges: Cuckoo clocks, mantel clocks, grandfather clocks… Here, there's no shortage of time.
