I said no. She said: “Think about it.” I thought about it. Still no. She kept the watch. She was right: I wouldn't have been able to tell the time.
textes.Elle est déjà au bord de la scène, mon c: It's already at the edge of the stage, sweetie.
textes.Elle est en bois, Gontran. Elle ne peut: It's made of wood, Gontran. It can't itch.
textes.Elle est en de bonnes mains. Et sur un b: It's in good hands. And on a good cannon.
textes.Elle est en quoi, ta jambe ? En bois de: What's your leg made of? Fruit-crate wood?
textes.Elle est entrée avec son béret et un sou: She came in with her beret and an enormous smile: “Some red coral, please, for my red.” I explained that you don't rip up coral, it takes a hundred years to grow. She said: “Just a little piece.” I replied: “Just a little century.” She walked out in a huff.
textes.Elle est entrée dans ma boutique avec un: She walked into my shop with a silent alarm clock under her arm. “It doesn't ring, that's its great quality!” She talked about that alarm clock for ten minutes. During those ten minutes, I made a watch without looking at my hands. When I looked, it was running backwards. Bricolette said: “I'll take it.” I didn't buy the alarm clock. I fell in love.
textes.Elle est heureuse. C'est pareil, pour un: She's happy. For a speaker, that's the same thing.
textes.Elle est intacte ! Ce soir, mon phare br: It's intact! Tonight my lighthouse will shine all the way to the village again. Here… when you keep watch over a lighthouse, you learn to breathe slowly. I'll teach you: you'll last longer underwater.
textes.Elle est là ! Elle flotte au-dessus du b: She's here! She's floating above the pool, with her guilty little look! (Nova wipes away a blue tear.) Thank you, thank you! Do you know what she's singing right now? The gurgles translate to: “I went to see the world. It's big. I prefer it here.” Here: two cosmic jellies from Gloubi, it's all I have that's precious. And you can come see Plume-de-Nuage whenever you like. She'll remember you. Jellyfish never forget those who bring them home.
It's there. It's looking at them too.
textes.Elle est parfaite, Mamie ! Soufflez dess: It's perfect, Mamie! Blow on it!
textes.Elle est remontée pour huit jours. Elle: It's wound up for eight days. It beats away, proud as a drum.
textes.Elle est trop bien, Papa ! J'ai cassé un: It's awesome, Dad! I broke a cushion!
textes.Elle est venue me demander un modèle de: She came to ask me for a compass rose design, to tattoo an old helmsman. I drew her one, with all sixteen directions, a mermaid in the north and a whale in the south. She tattooed it exactly, only smaller, without a single mistake. I was jealous for a week. Then I drew her another. She has a whole collection now.
textes.Elle est venue à Forgefer quand elle éta: She came to Forgefer when she was young, with a sack of badly forged nails and not a word. She stayed a season at the terrace forge. In the evenings, sitting by the fire, her fur would smoke. Bramm complained about finding hairs in his mug. I talked enough for two. She listened. We got on very well.
textes.Elle est violette ! Comme ma soucoupe !: It's purple! Like my saucer! Well, my saucer is green. But it would look lovely in purple.
textes.Elle est à moi, maintenant. Tu me l'as o: It's mine now. You gave it to me.
textes.Elle existe… Elle existe ! Une reine, un: It exists… It exists! A queen, a dome, a crystal that sings… Forty years of mockery, and I was right! Take this, it's all my holiday money. And remember this: the Atlanteans breathed slowly. Do as they did.
textes.Elle fait des nœuds dans les cheveux. To: It ties knots in your hair. All by themselves.
textes.Elle fait le tour de l'île deux fois par: She goes round the island twice a day, and sometimes goes down as far as Rigging Harbour, in Hautefond. That's where Captain Héloïse's Albatross is. Those two race each other the moment they cross paths.
textes.Elle fait trente centimètres, Félix. Ell: It's one foot high, Félix. It's almost flat.
textes.Elle finit en chef-d'œuvre ! Et dimanche: It's ending up a masterpiece! And on Sunday, what will be missing this time?
textes.Elle guérit l'ennui. C'est une maladie t: It cures boredom. A very widespread illness.
textes.Elle guérit la tristesse, chère Vespérin: It cures sadness, dear Vespérine. And boredom.
textes.Elle les envoie danser ailleurs. C'est p: It sends them off to dance somewhere else. That's not the same.
She reads sitting against Nacre, very softly. Once, she skipped a page, without meaning to. I heard it from the other side of the Circle: the story no longer held together. I told her. She blushed and went back. The stones shone a little brighter afterwards. They like things done in order.
textes.Elle lit derrière le journal de la veill: She reads behind yesterday's paper, always folded the same way. One evening, the novel was so good she held the paper upside down for an hour. I turned it round as I went past, without stopping. The next day, she left me a tip. A tip, from Colette! I thought she was ill.
textes.Elle m'a acheté la potion voix de canard: She bought my duck-voice potion. She went to talk to the wind on the cliffs, in duck, for an hour. She says the wind laughed and made a little whirlwind. It's the first time one of my potions made the wind laugh. I wrote it in my notebook, on the page of great successes. It's all alone on the page.
textes.Elle m'a appris la cochenille, ce petit: She taught me cochineal, the little insect that gives red. I crushed, soaked, wrung. The linen stayed white. My hands, though, stayed red for a week. Néferet thought I'd hurt myself and wanted to bless my fingers. Ix Sak gave me a red and yellow belt, “so you have at least one colour”. I keep it.
textes.Elle m'a appris le code des forgerons :: She taught me the blacksmiths' code: two knocks, then one, means “hello, thank you”. When she came down for the reopening, she knocked twice, then once, on a pane of the Promenade. The whole dome shook. She laughed so loudly that I checked the seals. They held.
textes.Elle m'a appris trois noms : Doyenne, Na: She's taught me three names: Doyenne, Nacre and Petite-Ourse. One name per full moon, no more, because the stones have to agree. I write them in my journal, in lemon ink, which can only be read by candlelight. Ysolde didn't want me to write them down. It's our compromise.
textes.Elle m'a appris un mot : « bientôt ». Je: She taught me a word: “soon”. I cannot find its exact duration. According to her, it is “way too long”. I am still calculating. I hope her soon arrives before my calculation ends.
textes.Elle m'a appris à faire de l'ocre avec l: She taught me to make ochre with the wadi earth: you dry it, grind it, sieve it. My hands were red for a week. With it, I painted birds on a series of her jugs. They all sold in a day. Halima split the money in two, down to the last penny. Then she said: “Again.”
textes.Elle m'a appris à faire la limonade bleu: She taught me to make blue lemonade with the class. We got spirulina everywhere: on the exercise books, on the walls, on the pupils. The whole class had blue tongues for two days. The parents were very understanding. Well, almost all of them. Josette treated the others to a soup.
textes.Elle m'a appris à lire la boussole. Ça f: She taught me to read the compass. That was ten years ago. I still hold it upside down. She says nothing, she turns it round. Once, I held it the right way up first time. She turned it round anyway, out of habit. We arrived a day late. She said it was my fault. It was my fault.
textes.Elle m'a commandé des pots pour ses fleu: She ordered pots from me for her flowers. I put Tlaloc's round eyes on them, out of habit. Her cempasúchil looked like they were watching the passers-by. Pilli says they're guarding the garden. Since then, the herons come closer less often. Xóchitl says it's my pots. I say it's Tlaloc. We're both happy.
textes.Elle m'a compté le papier d'emballage. P: She charged me for the wrapping paper. For three apples. One penny. I paid. A week later, she brings me her cheese knife, chipped. I sharpen it. Properly. I charge her for the sharpening. To the penny. She paid. We said nothing. We respect each other.
textes.Elle m'a confié sa graine de cactus des: She trusted me with her dwarf cactus seed, begging me to water it. A cactus hardly wants any water. So I give it one drop a month. Not one more. In spring, it grew a yellow flower. Noisette cried for joy. I watched her cry.
She asked me what an apple was. I've never seen one either! So I said: “a red sea urchin that grows on trees”. She repeated it to the whole city. Now if anyone proves me wrong, my honour sinks. Don't bring an apple down here, all right?
textes.Elle m'a demandé ce que la baleine dit a: She asked me what the whale says to the crystal. I searched ten thousand scrolls for three days. Nothing. I had to admit I didn't know. The next day, I found a pebble on my desk, with writing on it: “Abyssos doesn't know everything.” I archived it, of course.
textes.Elle m'a demandé d'aller couper des arbr: She asked me to go and cut trees in the jungle, for her masts. Too many spiders. I told her no. She said: “You, scared of a spider?” I said: “Yes.” She laughed. Then she said: “Me too.” We had a cider. We still don't have a mast. We have one more friend.
textes.Elle m'a demandé de planter un arbre pou: She asked me to plant a tree for every tree I cut down. I said no. Three times. Now I have a nursery behind the forge: twenty-six little kapok trees. Don't tell anyone. Especially not Barnabé.
textes.Elle m'a demandé des aiguilles plus fine: She asked me for needles finer than hairs. I tried ten times. The iron bent. On the eleventh, I got it. She held them up to the light and she said: “Perfect.” To thank me, she tattooed a little anvil on my forearm. Three hours. I didn't move. Nor did the Mute, they say. That makes two of us.
textes.Elle m'a demandé pourquoi le scarabée po: She asked me why the scarab pushes its ball of dung. I explained Khepri, who pushes the sun every morning. She said: “So the sun is a ball of…” I told her not to finish that sentence in front of Néferet. She finished it in front of Néferet. Néferet laughed. Me, I broke into a sweat.
textes.Elle m'a demandé pourquoi les gommes son: She asked me why erasers are pink. I didn't know the answer. First time in fifty years.
textes.Elle m'a demandé si Rê avait peur, la nu: She asked me if Rê was afraid at night, in the Duat. I told her about the Great Cat of Heliopolis, who slices off the head of the serpent Apophis under the sacred tree. Her eyes went huge and she said: “Then Miou is one of Rê's cats.” Since then, she calls him “my guardian of the sun”.
textes.Elle m'a demandé si je pouvais peindre u: She asked me if I could paint a strawberry ice cream on a beach. I tried. She said the ice cream looked too cold. I told her: “It's ice cream.” She said: “Then it worked.”
textes.Elle m'a demandé si on pouvait voir la l: She asked me if you could see the moon in broad daylight. I showed her. She didn't sleep for two nights: she wanted to watch it disappear.
textes.Elle m'a demandé si quelqu'un était déjà: She asked me if anyone had ever left the dome without going through the Gate. I said: “Never, not on my watch.” She looked at me for a long time, with her big eyes, as if she knew something. Then she said: “OK.” I don't like it when she says “OK” like that.
textes.Elle m'a demandé une aiguille spéciale :: She asked me for a special needle: as long as my hand, curved, sturdy, for thick canvas. I asked what canvas. She said: “A canvas.” I forged the needle without asking anything else. I'm not nosy. Well, I am. But I know how to keep quiet.
textes.Elle m'a dit : « Votre moteur et ma Colo: She told me: “Your engine and my Column are related, you know.” I asked her: “How do you know?” She said: “They creak the same way at night.”
textes.Elle m'a dit que celui qui répond à mes: She told me that whoever answers my knocks under the anvil might be her uncle. I don't know if it's true. But since then, I knock twice, then once, then twice more: “Hello, thank you, and hello from Ysaé.”
textes.Elle m'a dit que dans le registre de la: She told me that in the Guild's register, on the date of the rise, it says: “Séraphin Altaïr: left without notice, with a piece of the town. Delay: permanent.”
textes.Elle m'a donné de l'hibiscus séché pour: She gave me dried hibiscus to replace the coral. In the bowl, a sublime red, deep, almost wine-dark. I put it on the canvas that evening, very proud. The next morning, it was brown. Dead-leaf brown. Amélie said it was “very autumnal”. I laughed. Later. Much later.
textes.Elle m'a emmené sur les falaises du nord: She took me to the northern cliffs to “listen together”. An hour in the wind. She hummed along with it to prove to me that it sang. She was out of tune. So was it. It proved nothing. We came back down, each still convinced. She held my arm on the way down. That, I took note of.
textes.Elle m'a emmenée faire un tour dans l'Al: She took me for a ride in the Albatross once. I laughed so hard during take-off that the airship gained ten extra metres. She says I'm a better engine than steam.
textes.Elle m'a emmenée voir la Fronde, quand l: She took me to see the Fronde when the line reopened. There are bolts as big as me! I'd packed a bag. A really big one. It wasn't big enough.
textes.Elle m'a envoyé un champignon qui brille: She sent me a glowing mushroom in a jar, with a note: “So that a little light from the Strata can watch over your Greenhouses.” It lives at the edge of my pond. It glows blue at night. The water lilies find it a bit chatty. As for me, I say goodnight to it before switching off the lamps.
textes.Elle m'a fabriqué un cerf-volant avec un: She made me a kite out of an old dormitory sheet. She said: “That way, the sheet flies, and you hold the string.” It flies super high! Higher than Gérard. I don't fly yet. But I hold the string really well. She says so.
textes.Elle m'a fabriqué une lampe qui ne s'all: She made me a lamp that only lights up when you show it a piece of jewellery. It's on all the time. Bricole says it's a manufacturing defect. I think it's on purpose.
textes.Elle m'a fait une potion de légèreté. Je: She made me a lightness potion. I drank it in front of my whole class, to do her proud. I didn't float at all. But my hair stood straight up on my head, like a feather, all day. I taught like that. The apprentices have never been so attentive.
textes.Elle m'a offert du nectar pour mon anniv: She gave me nectar for my birthday. I poured the bottle on my roots. In front of her. In spring the root grew a flower. A nectar flower. Even the roots betray me. Hmph.
textes.Elle m'a offert un dessin : moi, sur mon: She gave me a drawing: me, on my throne, with hair reaching the ceiling. “That's because you're a thousand years old,” she explained. I asked who had told her that. She clapped both hands over her mouth. I didn't have to look far: there's only one guard, at the Gate.
textes.Elle m'a offert un foulard teint avec mo: She gave me a scarf dyed with my saffron. A yellow… a yellow like sunset over the dunes. I wear it. Every time someone pays me a compliment, I say: “What a waste.” And I wear it again the next day. Don't tell her: she'd think I'd forgiven her.
textes.Elle m'a offert un nuage en bocal, pour: She gave me a cloud in a jar, to console me after a forecast. I named it Zéphyr. It makes a little shower whenever she walks past the Institute. I don't know why. It's my greatest mystery.
textes.Elle m'a offert un petit cristal bleu qu: She gave me a little blue crystal that glows at night. I put it on my easel. In the evening, when the sun has gone, it carries on painting a little in my place.
textes.Elle m'a offert un scarabée de faïence b: She gave me a blue faience scarab. For them, the scarab pushes the sun up in the morning. I gave her a jade bead, the breath of life. The scarab guards the altar in my house. Every morning, as I leave for the Cenote, I say good morning to it. It doesn't answer. Like Kukulkan. I'm used to it.
textes.Elle m'a offert une boucle d'oreille fai: She gave me an earring made from one of my springs. I don't wear earrings. I hung it on the Singing Clock. Since then, the clock sings a little more cheerfully.
textes.Elle m'a offert une casquette de la Conf: She gave me a Guild cap for the reopening. She said: “Hold the handrail. Even at the top.” I hold the handrail. Even on the platform.
textes.Elle m'a posé cent dix-sept questions su: She asked me a hundred and seventeen questions about humans in a single evening. I answered by describing Barnabé. Ever since, she's convinced that all humans talk to a parrot. I didn't have the heart to tell her otherwise.
textes.Elle m'a posé une devinette. « Je grogne: She set me a riddle. “I grumble in the morning, I grumble at night…” I thought about it. I said: “A bear.” She laughed for three days. Three. And I was right. Bears grumble. Hmph.
textes.Elle m'a promis de m'emmener voir la Fro: She promised to take me to see the Fronde when the line reopens. They say there are bolts as big as me down there. I've already packed a bag. A very big one.
textes.Elle m'a promis de me prévenir quand la: She promised to let me know when the whale came by. One night she ran up to me: “Triton! It's above the palace!” I took one step. Then I remembered I was on guard, and I stayed. She sang me the whale for an hour. It was almost better. Almost.
textes.Elle m'a proposé un tour dans l'Albatros: She offered me a ride in the Albatross. I got up to the tenth step of the Mast. She applauded me from the top of the gangway. Nobody had ever applauded me for ten steps before.
textes.Elle m'a prédit que je traverserais la m: She predicted I'd cross the sea before I turned sixty. I'm fifty-eight, and I get seasick. I have two years left to prove her wrong. I fully intend to. Well… I fully intend not to. I'm not quite sure which side I'm on any more.
textes.Elle m'a présenté un jeune scribe qui ne: She introduced me to a young scribe who spoke only in proverbs. At the fifth one, “The river does not flow back to its source”, I stood up: “The loom does not wait.” Mérit was furious. In the evening, she said to me: “All right, he was a bit boring.” He was very boring. We laughed until midnight.
textes.Elle m'a raconté le Grand Chat du soleil: She told me about the Great Cat of the sun, who cuts off the head of the serpent Apophis at night, under the sacred tree. A cat! Who protects the sun! So then I understood: Miou is one of Rê's cats. That's why he goes out walking at night. He goes to work.
textes.Elle m'a raconté le combat de Rê contre: She told me about Ra's battle against the serpent Apophis, every night. I told her about ours, against the stars. We thought it over for a long time. Then she said: “Being a sun is an exhausting job.” I laughed. For the first time in years. She looked very pleased with herself.
textes.Elle m'a raconté une histoire de son inv: She told me a story she'd made up: a baker who sings, and a miller all white with flour who listens behind the door. I didn't say anything, but I laughed till I cried. That little one sees everything. All of Montjoie is waiting for those two to talk to each other, and it's an eight-year-old who turned it into a story. I told her to keep it. One day, she'll tell it at their wedding.
textes.Elle m'a répondu ! Une lettre avec un de: She wrote back! A letter with a drawing of a whale-shaped kite, and a question: “Does the sea make a noise, inside?” I pressed my notebook against the glass of the Promenade and wrote down everything I could hear. Three pages. With the Singer at the end. I can't wait for her to answer.
textes.Elle m'a tourné une cruche, rien que pou: She threw me a jug, just for me, with a whale in relief going all the way round. I don't use it, I don't want to damage it. It sits on my windowsill, and I look at it in the evening. My mother says a jug is for water. I say that one's for dreaming.
She sold me the brooch without a word. Then, during my Tuesday speech, she was the first to clap. All on her own. Then everyone followed. I don't know if it was for me or for the brooch.
textes.Elle m'a vendu un sac de sel. Du beau se: She sold me a sack of salt. Fine salt, white, nice and heavy, at a good price. The next day, Jacquot went to salt the soup: it was sand. Sixty years later, the same trick! She'd sold sand to my grandfather too! She told me: “You have his eyes. Not his nerve.” I kept the sack. To remind me never to trust her.
textes.Elle m'a vendu une potion de sève, une f: She sold me a sap potion, a green phial that smells of the forest. “One spoonful in the morning.” I take two, so I go faster. She doesn't agree. I tried to explain that it's mathematical. She gave me the look I used to give pupils who dawdled.
textes.Elle m'a écrit qu'elle racontait des his: She wrote that she tells my strawberries stories so they stay fresh during the journey. They always arrive in perfect condition. I don't know if it's the cold or the gossip.
textes.Elle m'achète du miel chaque semaine. El: She buys honey from me every week. She says it's for her flatbreads. A flatbread takes one spoonful. She buys a whole pot. I don't ask questions. Neither do the bees. But one evening, passing by her house, I smelled cacao… and honey. Together. I said nothing.
textes.Elle m'achète trois paniers de dattes ch: She buys three baskets of dates from me every year. She says they're for her flatbreads. Me, I think she eats them in secret, in the evening. Last year, we swapped recipes: she gave me her cacao “without the chilli”, and I gave her my beer “without the dates”. We both lied. We both know it. That's friendship between merchants.
textes.Elle m'apporte régulièrement des « pierr: She regularly brings me “magic stones” for my furnaces. They're pebbles. She charges me a coin each. I pay. Once I threw one into the fire, to see. It made a shower of purple sparks and sang three notes. I've never mentioned it to her. But since then I keep all her pebbles, just in case.
textes.Elle m'avait annoncé une grande découver: She'd foretold a great discovery for me. The next day, I searched the Observatory, the library, the Cauldron, looking for my glasses. They were on my nose. Agathe said: “For a man who looks so far away, seeing what's under his nose is a very great discovery.” I think about it often.
textes.Elle m'avait écrit une annonce très long: She once wrote me a very long announcement, full of commas and “kindly be advised”. I read it out loud on the square, all of it, with every single comma. It took four minutes. People sat down. At the end, they clapped. Églantine went red with pride. She says it was red with shame. I know what I saw.
textes.Elle m'envoie des nuages en bocal. Ils a: She sends me clouds in jars. They always arrive empty: a cloud can't stand the pressure, apparently. I've never told her. I have a whole shelf of empty jars. They hold the thought. That's the most precious thing of all.
She's eating the chimney, more like.
textes.Elle me demande de ne pas manger plus de: She asks me not to eat more than two choux buns a day. I went a bit deaf that day. I've never got my hearing back on that subject.
textes.Elle me garde un tabouret près de l'encl: She keeps a stool for me by the anvil. I tell stories to the customers while she hammers, and the customers stay for both. One morning, she leaned a walking stick against my door with a moon on the handle. Without a word. A walking stick, from Ursule, is a whole sentence. That one meant: “Don't fall, Father.”
It'd steal them from me first.
textes.Elle me pose plein de questions sur mon: She asks me loads of questions about my job. How I breathe, how I choose the words, why I never whisper. One day, she asked me: “Mélusine, do you shout because you want everyone to hear you, or because you're scared nobody's listening?” I didn't know what to say. I rang Marguerite. She nodded. She'd understood.
textes.Elle me regarde. Au départ, au marché, a: She looks at me. At the start line, at the market, at the Circle. Staring, without blinking, with the tip of her tail twitching just a teeny bit. Like a cat in front of a skewer, {surnom}. One day I tested it: I hid behind a barrel. She looked at the barrel. I'm not reassured at all.
textes.Elle me réclame depuis des années la rec: For years she's been asking me for the recipe for the caravan traders' cream. I asked Aïcha, who asked a caravan trader, who laughed: goat fat and cinnamon. That's exactly what I brought Anouk, in a pretty pot. She didn't believe me. Nobody ever believes me when I tell the truth.
She's lying. And so are you, Séraphine.
textes.Elle monte, Triton. Tu veux que je la ch: It's rising, Triton. Do you want me to sing it more quietly?
textes.Elle n'a pas l'air triste. Elle a l'air: It doesn't look sad. It looks pointy.
textes.Elle n'aime pas qu'on la presse, la Colo: The Column doesn't like to be rushed!
She doesn't like to be rushed.
It's only waiting for your strawberries.
textes.Elle ne crie jamais. Elle lève un sourci: She never shouts. She raises an eyebrow, and the whole crew runs. Even the ship's cat.
textes.Elle ne grince pas, elle chante. C'est t: It doesn't creak, it sings. It's your thread rubbing.
textes.Elle ne me vend plus de camomille. Une f: She won't sell me chamomile any more. Once, just once, my sleeping potion blew the door off L'Alambic. The whole town woke up at two in the morning. Mère Sauge arrived in her nightcap, looked at the door on the ground, and said: “Chamomile is for sleeping, dear boy.” Since then, it's been lemon balm.
textes.Elle parle avec des étoiles. C'est de la: It talks with stars. That's cheating.
textes.Elle parle peu, mais quand elle parle, m: She doesn't say much, but when she does, even the wind goes quiet to listen.
textes.Elle peignait à la bougie, et la bougie: She painted by candlelight, and the candle ate my shadows. So I pierced her a lantern of her own, closed all round, with a single slit facing her canvas: the light falls on the paper and nowhere else. I told her it was a workshop offcut. She calls it “my workshop offcut”. She won't lend it to anyone.
textes.Elle penche un peu. C'est le style, Octa: It leans a little. That's the style, Octave.
She loses her drops in my roots. Makes them wet. Makes them go mouldy. So I pick them up and put them back outside her door, in a nutshell. For my roots, not for her. Once she was watching for me behind her window. I pretended I was just passing. Hmph.
textes.Elle pose ses énigmes devant MA boutique: She sets her riddles in front of MY shop. Customers stop, think, scratch their heads… and leave without buying anything, their heads full. Once a bumblebee spent a whole day trying to work one out. He didn't buy anything either.
textes.Elle pousse vers le haut, Borin. Vers la: It's growing upwards, Borin. Towards glory.
textes.Elle prétend que mes énigmes font fuir s: She claims my riddles scare off her customers. Nonsense: they stay in front of her shop for hours on end, thinking. Once a bumblebee stayed a whole day. He didn't buy anything, fine. But he left cleverer.
textes.Elle rame comme une femme du port. Les é: She rows like a woman of the port. Shoulders low, back straight, no splashing. Pirates row like goats. Not her. Someone taught her. A father, I think. One day, the seagulls came home. I said: “We're going back.” She didn't argue. The storm arrived behind us. She said: “Just like my father.”
textes.Elle redescend tous les soirs pour le de: She comes back down every evening for the last song, now that the Line has reopened. She stands at the back of the pit. When I see her, I miss a beat. Every time. Bielle looks at me. I say it was the cymbal.
She was looking at the moon, behind you.
textes.Elle regarde tout le monde. C'est Tlaloc: She looks at everyone. That's Tlaloc.
textes.Elle repart ! Tic, tac ! Tu as des doigt: She's going again! Tick, tock! You've got a clockmaker's fingers. Here: the only watch in the house I've never managed to set. It keeps perfect time, just backwards.
She's going again! Tick, tock! You've got a clockmaker's fingers. Here, a spare spring: in Hautefond, it always comes in handy.
textes.Elle repart toute seule !: She's starting up again all by herself!
textes.Elle repousse déjà, regarde ! C'est le s: It's already growing back, look! That's the sunshine up here for you.
It stays where it is, milord.
textes.Elle revient toujours avec des pétales d: She always comes back with petals in her hair and golden pollen on her cheeks. I say they're real.
textes.Elle ronronne ! Nefer-Miou t'a accepté !: She's purring! Nefer-Miou has accepted you! It's a great honor. Take this honey cake: it's what she would have wanted.
She purrs, Tchoum. She likes me.
She's asking for dates. As always.
It came unplugged. It likes you.
textes.Elle s'est envolée ? Oh, mon petit… Tu a: She flew away? Oh, my dear… You have gentle hands, and a gentle heart too. Here, some coins, and a feather she left on my roof this morning: she came to thank you, I think.
textes.Elle se pose… mais le bouclier d'épines: She lands… but the thorn shield protects her. The roses of light!
She made up for it afterwards, Ba Sidi.
textes.Elle se souvient de toi ! Elle ronronne: She remembers you! She's purring even louder than last time.
It smells of punch, this week.
It smells so good you close your eyes. When you open them again, the botanist is looking at you. You put the strawberry back.
It smells so good you close your eyes. When you open them again, the botanist is looking at you. You put the strawberry back.
textes.Elle siffle bien, ma chaudière ?: Does she whistle well, my boiler?
textes.Elle siffle un peu, Papy Ferdinand !: She whistles a little, Grandpa Ferdinand!
textes.Elle sonne treize coups à midi. Le treiz: It strikes thirteen at noon. The thirteenth is for luck, so it says. I say it's to annoy me.
textes.Elle sort à peine du four !: It's barely out of the oven!
She's smiling, Héloïse. Listen to her.
textes.Elle surveille la Lune ?: She's keeping an eye on the Moon?
She likes you, Bramm. You're steady.
textes.Elle t'attend, Capitaine. Et ce soir, la: It's waiting for you, Captain. And how big is the wave tonight?
It's waiting for you, Gaspard. With its date.
It's waiting for you. So is the thyme, it's sulking.
textes.Elle t'embrasse. Toujours pas de retour: She sends her love. Still not going back?
textes.Elle te suit ! Brioche te suit ! Regarde: She's following you! Brioche is following you! Look at her, sitting at your feet, tail neatly curled, like a queen who has chosen her carriage. (Rosalie wipes her eyes with her apron.) It's the smell of the fish, it stings. Listen to me: she eats one sardine a day, not two, she has her dignity. She chases butterflies, she never catches them. And she has a gift: she can sense hidden treasures. I once saw her meow for an hour in front of a paving stone in the square; underneath, there was an old gold coin. Listen to her when she meows. Here, a few coins. And if you don't have anything yet to call your animals, take this bone whistle: my grandfather, the fisherman, carved it with a dog, a cat, a rat and a pig. He said that one day, someone would have all four. Whistle, and those who love you will come running.
textes.Elle te tend une paire de chaussettes à: She hands you a pair of plaid socks, all warm… and a few coins hidden inside. “For coffee.”
She'll hold a hundred years, Admiral.
textes.Elle tient ! C'est mes bras qui tiennent: It's holding! It's my arms that can't hold it anymore!
textes.Elle tient ! Et Ptah te passe le bonjour: It's holding up! And Ptah says hello!
textes.Elle tient toujours ! Je ne la touche pl: It's still standing! I don't touch it any more, I don't even breathe near it, and I dust it with a feather. Thanks again, nimble fingers.
She's holding up, Driss. One more winter.
textes.Elle tient, Tiyi. Et le soleil de l'ourl: It's holding up, Tiyi. And so is the sun in the hem.
It's holding. Not a word, Jos.
It falls from up above, Photon. Like this.
textes.Elle tourne vite, la petite planète !: The little planet goes round so fast!
textes.Elle va s'emballer, elle va s'emballer !: She's going to go wild, she's going to go wild!
textes.Elle vient au grill vérifier que je mets: She comes to the grill to check I'm using enough cumin. She holds her nose with one hand, and with the other she lifts my cumin box to weigh it. She says: “Not enough.” Always. She leaves, holding her nose. The next day I put in more cumin. She comes back and says: “Not enough.” That's our way of saying hello.
textes.Elle voulait un couteau sur le bras, poi: She wanted a knife on her arm, point down, very elegant. I was on the blade when she sneezed. All of a sudden. My needle slipped, the blade went round. I did what I could: a spoon. A beautiful spoon, with a chased handle. She looked at her arm, then at me, and left without a word. She hasn't forgiven me yet.
It's been waiting for you for ten minutes.
textes.Elle vous salue, Gilles. Elle dit que vo: She says hello, Gilles. She says you were sleeping.
textes.Elle éclaire bien, ce soir ?: Is it giving good light tonight?
textes.Elle écrit son nom avec un pot, une jamb: She writes her name with a pot, a leg and a loaf. I explained that the first sign is a basket, not a pot, and that the leg is one too many. She refused to remove the leg: “I need a leg, I'm always running.” I said it was almost right. Between you and me, it's the loveliest mistake of the year.
textes.Elle était authentique ! Authentiquement: It was authentic! An authentic tablecloth.
textes.Elle était jolie, non ?: It was a nice one, though, wasn't it?
It was full of my drops.
textes.Elle était plus profonde que les autres: It was deeper than the others! That's different!
textes.Elle était si belle, je voulais la regar: It was so pretty, I wanted to look at it from far away!
At least it keeps quiet, Ba Sidi.
textes.Elles chantaient juste, au moins ?: Were they in tune, at least?
They're looking for your blue star.
They listen to me, you know.
They won't be waking up again, my friend.
textes.Elles ont chanté pour toi. Je les ai ent: They sang for you. I heard them all the way here. So it's settled: you are a wizard of Arcanelle. Here, your staff: wood from the Twisted Wood and a crystal from the Circle. In your hand, it makes your spells lighter. And your magic is greater from now on. Go, wizard. The world needs light, fire, ice, wind, patience and healing. Healing most of all.
textes.Elles répondent ! Mais très lentement. U: They do answer! But very slowly. One sentence from an oak takes a year. You have to be patient. Try with a little flower: they're quicker.
textes.Elles s'inquiètent. (Une grande fleur cl: They're worried. (A big flower blinks three times, very fast.) See? Three quick blinks means “where are the little ones?” The little ones are my glowing seeds. I was drying them in the sun, at the end of the bridge of light... and a gust of wind pushed them into the Zero-Gravity Garden. Over there, nothing falls back down. They float, way up high, between the leaves that fall upward. Me, with my eight-hundred-year-old knees, I jump like an old squash. You're young. Jump! Catch them! Three seeds, round and warm, glowing like night-lights.
textes.Elles se sont toutes arrêtées à une heur: They all stopped at a different time. That way, one of them is always right. Twice a day.
They feel at home with you, Photon.
textes.Elles sont en fer, maintenant, Brunna. G: They're iron now, Brunna. Thanks to you!
They're out there, I can feel it.
textes.Elles sont vraies, tes dents en or, ou c: Are your gold teeth real, or are they brass?
textes.Elles t'aiment bien ! Et elles avaient p: They like you! And they were scared you'd get lost!
textes.Elles t'attendaient, Rosalie. Raconte-le: They've been waiting for you, Rosalie. Tell them something.
textes.Elles t'ont entendue. Elles bourdonnent: They heard you. They're buzzing with delight.
textes.Elles tiennent, Ix Sak ! Ce sont des plu: They're holding, Ix Sak! They're champion feathers!
They're holding. No thankth to anybody.
textes.Elles vous plaisent, Monsieur Lisse ?: Do you like them, Mr Lisse?
textes.Elles y sont, Maître Filandre ! Toutes l: They're there, Master Filandre! Both of them!
textes.Elles étaient derrière le comptoir, tes: Were your cards behind the counter, then?
textes.Embêtée ? Je suis CLOUÉE AU SOL ! (Elle: Upset? I'm GROUNDED! (She shows her wing in a sling.) I sprained it on a chimney. I still have three letters: one for Grumbald, at the Diable Repu; one for Ombreline, at the Library of Souls; one for Gorgoth, at the arena. Would you? I'll pay you in stamps. No, in coins.
To take Zineb to see the desert. One night. Just one. Show her the walking stars. And say nothing.
textes.Emmener toute ma classe, les quatorze, e: To take my whole class, all fourteen of them, in a single day, from the sea all the way to the sky: the Funicular, the Strata, the Column of Hautefond, then the capsule up to the City of Clouds. To watch them step out onto the Glass Belvedere, under the real sky, all together. And that day, not to give a single lesson. To let them look. For once, the sky will be the teacher.
textes.Emprunter… Tu les rends quand, tes brais: Borrow… And when do you give your embers back?
textes.En 1702, j'ai souri. Une fois. Au fort,: In 1702, I smiled. Once. At the fort, a cannon exploded next to a governor in a wig. He ended up black with soot, his wig smoking. I smiled. Not because of the governor: because of the cannon. Such a beautiful BOOM. The governor thought I was making fun of him. The next day, I was a pirate. That's what smiling gets you. I WON'T DO IT AGAIN.
textes.En 1977, on a joué à la Halle des forges: In 1977, we played the forge hall, back when the anvils were still there. There were thousands of people. Tens of thousands! I fell off the stage, the crowd threw me back up in the air, and the mosh pit was born. Barricade says 1978. Barricade says I tripped over a cable. Barricade says a lot of things.
textes.En 1987, j'étais dans mon champ. Il fais: In 1987, I was in my field. It was hot. I looked up. And right there, the Great Spaghetti winked at me. With his left eye. Nobody believes me. But I saw it, I did.
At 33 rpm: nice and easy, still spinning.
textes.En arrivant au Boucan, j'ai trouvé la Ca: When I arrived in Boucan, I found the Scrapyard: a graveyard of cars, machines and saucepans. Everyone saw rubbish. I saw a dragon. I started with the head: a lorry bonnet. Then the eyes: two headlights. That was fifteen years ago. He's not finished. He'll never be finished.
textes.En arrivant au Boucan, j'ai trouvé un mo: When I arrived in Boucan, I found a unicycle at the Free Shop. Trocante told me it had belonged to an acrobat who never fell. I fell four times in the first minute. Trocante said: “It needed someone who falls. For a change.” I kept it. We've been falling together ever since.
textes.En arrivant au Boucan, j'ai vu des chien: When I arrived in Boucan, I saw dogs everywhere: at the Cannery, in the Boxes, at the Spinning Mill. Nobody had time to walk them. I offered. The first day, I had two. The next day, six. Bigoudi, Pneu, Gaufre, Amiral, Madame Croquette and Tic-Tac. They decided I was their pack.
textes.En arrivant ici, j'ai apporté quatre-vin: When I arrived here, I brought ninety thousand books from Ondelune, written in light. They fit in a single suitcase: books of light weigh nothing. The Council gave me a room at the back of the Academy. I sorted the books by colour, then by size, then by mood. The sad books are at the very bottom. So they don't fall.
textes.En arrivant ici, j'ai appris les mots de: When I arrived here, I learned the words of the people down below, in Murmure's books. And I discovered rhymes. Two words that end the same! Moon and June! Sky and pie! I jumped for joy in the middle of the library. Murmure went “shh” at me. I swore I would only ever speak in verse. That was nine hundred years ago.
textes.En arrivant ici, j'ai découvert le chanv: When I got here, I discovered hemp. Galet beats it, spins it, twists it into ropes. I weave it into canvas. Solid as a rock, soft as an old jumper. Every yurt in the camp wears one of my canvases on its back.
textes.En arrivant ici, j'ai fondé l'Académie d: When I arrived here, I founded the Academy of Sciences in an empty bubble. On the first day, I had one student: me. On the second day, I had a blackboard. On the third, the equations on the blackboard started floating, because I'd used light chalk. Ever since, they all float. Long divisions are the heaviest.
textes.En arrivant ici, j'ai trouvé la Grande S: When I got here, I found the Great Stage abandoned since the quarrel. Rusty, tarped over, sad. A stage without music is like a boat without a sea. So I repair it. One bolt a day. Being ready costs nothing.
textes.En arrivant ici, le Professeur Quasar a: When he arrived here, Professor Quasar wanted to make rain. His machine went “pop”, and giant bubbles floated up over the island. Everyone laughed at him. Me, I looked at those bubbles and saw houses. I took my tablet, I calculated, I solidified. That very evening, I was living in the first one.
textes.En arrivant ici, tout le monde était per: When we arrived here, everyone was lost: the days only lasted twenty-four hours. The Lumens had dinner in the middle of the night and went to bed at noon. Gloubi served breakfast to the stars. I built the island's first clock out of a crystal, a thread and a lot of patience. They called me Tempo.
textes.En arrivant sur la Balafre, je n'avais p: When I arrived on Balafre, I'd run out of ink. I found out that the cuttlefish in the bay make an ink as black as night. The first day, I dived in, caught one, it pinched my thumb and squirted all its ink in my face. I came out of the water black from head to toe. Tom called me Coralie the Ink. It stuck.
textes.En arrivant, j'ai couru au bord de l'île: When I arrived, I ran to the edge of the island and looked down. There were islands. Real islands, with mountains, forests, volcanoes, currents. Exactly like my imaginary maps, only better. I took out a pencil and started drawing. I've never put that pencil away. It's very small now.
textes.En arrivant, j'ai sorti mon double mètre: When I arrived, I took out my folding ruler and stood at the foot of the temple. The Great Spaghetti looked at me. I looked at it. It blinked. I wrote down: “Blink, 2:32 p.m.” It blinked again. And again. After an hour, I'd filled a whole journal. I never left.
textes.En arrivant, je n'avais rien. Mamma Lasa: When I arrived, I had nothing. Mamma Lasagna saw me on the jetty and put a plate of spaghetti in my hands. Without asking anything. I cried into my pasta. She said: “That'll make it salty.” I stayed.
textes.En avance ! C'est une qualité. Avec modé: Early! That's a virtue. In moderation. One second is politeness; one hour is impatience. Take it from a man whose clock was one second fast, once.
textes.En avance ! Excellent. Le temps d'attend: Early! Excellent. Time spent waiting is time well spent. It's when you think about what's coming.
textes.En avance ! Fffiou ! Enfin quelqu'un de: Early! Fffwoosh! Finally, someone serious. You walk slowly, but you set off early. That's a technique. Respect.
textes.En avance. Hm. C'est mieux que le retard: Early. Hm. Better than late. But you lose minutes waiting. Bring a book. Or a watch to adjust.
textes.En avant ! … Par où, d'ailleurs ? Peu im: Forward! … Which way, by the way? Never mind: FORWARD!
textes.En bas ! Le paysage, les toits, la mer…: Down! The landscape, the rooftops, the sea… That's the real rule! But careful, look ahead now and then too. Masts don't move out of the way.
textes.En bas, chacun choisit la couleur de ses: Down there, everyone chooses their hair colour on their fifteenth birthday. The whole street comes to watch. I hesitated for three days. Then I went down into the mine and saw the blue of the crystals shining in the dark. I chose that blue. The one that gives light without the sun.
textes.En bas, dans la Fronde, une mémé m'a don: Down in the Fronde, a granny gave me the recipe for her stew: “a ladle of mushrooms, a ladle of love, and Excalibur.” I searched the whole Great Market for Excalibur. Rosalie says it's a very rare spice. I think she's making it up.
Down below, at the city lighting up.
textes.En bateau ? Peuchère ! Assis, les bras c: By boat? Good grief! Sitting there, arms folded, looking at the sea? Well, the sea is pretty. But at least run up the steps of the quay.
textes.En cachette ! Comme moi, petite, dans le: In secret! Like me, as a girl, in the broom cupboard. Welcome to the club. There are far more of us than people think, you know. Even behind shop counters.
textes.En cachette ! Ha ! Comme l'amin sur son: In secret! Ha! Like the amin on his bench. He thinks nobody sees his feet. Me, I see everything from behind the guembri. I won't say a thing. Not for him, not for you.
textes.En cachette ! Oh, tout le monde commence: In secret! Oh, everyone starts in secret. For me it was on my mother's hooves, in the kitchen. For Grelot, behind her stall, between customers.
textes.En ce moment, j'ai cinq projets. Bidule,: Right now I have five projects. Bidule, with Léonce, in the cellar. Céleste's telescope, ten minutes every evening. The Zéphyr's time: three minutes twelve to Tazira. Mr Cogne's golden gear, plus what Gonzague saw: I added it up. And the perpetual motion engine, which is impossible. That one isn't a project. It's a secret. Don't tell Mr Cogne.
textes.En ce moment, je ne passe plus devant l': These days, I don't go past the herbalist's any more. I take the fishermen's alley: three hundred metres extra, good for training! Nothing to do with the doctor. Nothing at all. And when I bump into her, I tell her my times. Going down! She doesn't believe me. She's wrong. Well… she's right.
textes.En ce moment, je tisse une chose étrange: Right now, I'm weaving something strange: a carpet for the pirate captain, from a drawing he made from memory. Karim is secretly making the wedding slippers. Lalla Aïcha sells me her saffron while scolding me like a child. And Zohra comes by every day with fish and leaves with my secrets. By evening, the whole harbour knows them. It's handy, when you want news to get around.
textes.En choisissant sa rose, Hugo m'a récité: While choosing his rose, Hugo recited the name of every flower in my shop. The real names, the scientific ones! I was floored. He blushed: “Léa taught me them. Over a year.” A year of buying bouquets to learn the names of flowers! That boy, I'd have married him myself.
textes.En classe, il nous a dit : « Fermez les: In class, he told us: “Close your eyes, think of the morning, open your hand.” I raised my hand. I said: “Page two hundred and three. You have to breathe first.” He stopped. He breathed. The whole class breathed. Oscar made an almost round light. Master Lumen says it's thanks to me.
textes.En classe, je disais : « Fermez les yeux: In class, I used to say: “Close your eyes, think of the morning, open your hand.” She raised her hand: “Page two hundred and three. You have to breathe first.” I breathed. The whole class breathed. And Oscar made an almost round light! Since then, I begin every lesson by breathing. Thank you, page two hundred and three.
textes.En cloches, en clous et en grilles ! Com: In bells, nails and grates! Same as always!
textes.En cours de lévitation, j'ai voulu soule: In levitation class, I tried to lift a feather. Zéphyrine's chair went up instead, with her on it. She said “Oh! Thank you!” and taught the whole lesson from up there, by the ceiling. At the end, I didn't know how to bring her down. She came down on her own. She said it was the best lesson of the year.
textes.En dansant ! Coucou, coucou ! C'est exac: Dancing! Yoo-hoo, yoo-hoo! That's exactly it! A bridge dances, so you dance with it! That settles it: my next bridge, you'll open it.
textes.En dessous de la ville, il y a les Strat: Below the town, there are the Strata, and the Fronde. That's where Ysaé lives! She says there are forges, rails, crystals that glow in the dark, and music all the time. The line has reopened, and Mum said “we'll see”. That meant yes! I went with Ysaé. It's even better.

Under the town, there are the Strata, and the Fronde. That's where Ysaé lives! She says there are forges, rails, crystals that glow in the dark, and music all the time. Mum says “we'll see when the line reopens”. That means yes. I think.
textes.En entrant, il ôte son chapeau. Pas pour: When he comes in, he takes off his hat. Not for me: for the jar. He looks up at the top shelf and says: “Good morning.” To the jar of figs. Then to me. In that order. I find it ridiculous. I don't find it all that ridiculous. I don't know any more.
textes.En faisant son lit, j'ai trouvé sous l'o: Making his bed, I found a magnificent drawing under the professor's pillow: a city under the sea, with a great crystal in the middle, all blue. I told Gisèle. And Rosalie. And Madame Rita, and… well, everyone. He went as red as a lobster. I feel bad about it. A little.
textes.En forme ! J'ai marqué trois fois ce mat: In great shape! I scored three times this morning. OK, there was nobody on the other side.
textes.En garde, créature ! Tu ne sais pas à qu: On guard, creature! You don't know who you're dealing with!
textes.En garde, monstre ! Tu ne sais pas encor: En garde, monster! You don't know yet who you're dealing with! I'll tell you very loudly!
textes.En grenouille, une fois, j'ai attrapé un: As a frog, once, I caught a moth. With my tongue. First go. … Not a bad feeling. Don't tell Pimprenelle. She'd change me every day. And I'd say no. Probably.
textes.En harmonie. Rien ne remplace une chanso: In harmony. Nothing beats a song you've found again.
textes.En haut de la cascade, sur la Lèvre (le: At the top of the waterfall, on the Lip (the edge of the cliff, where the water falls), you can hear the whole world breathing. And you get your feet wet.
textes.En haut, il y a un horloger qui s'appell: Up top, there's a clockmaker called Gaspard Ressort. RESSORT! Like me! He says it's his surname. Mine's just my name. I think we're sort of cousins. He doesn't agree. But he gave me a spring.
textes.En interrogation d'histoire, j'avais tou: In the history test, I'd forgotten everything. So I drew the headmaster as a yawning bat. He gave me zero in history and eighteen in drawing. Ortie says he kept the drawing above his desk. I don't believe her. Well, a little bit.
textes.En marchant vite, alors ! Les clients ar: A brisk walk, then! The customers are coming!
textes.En mer, je chante pour faire venir le po: At sea, I sing to bring the fish. Youssef says I scare them away. And yet we always come home full.
textes.En partant, elle a laissé sur mon enclum: When she left, she left a little silver bell on my anvil. Not a word, of course. I hung it above the forge door. When Fundin comes running in, it rings, and he stops dead. It's the only thing in the world that stops Fundin.
textes.En plein conseil des pêcheurs, je réglai: In the middle of the fishermen's council, I was settling a serious quarrel, a matter of places on the quay. Total silence. Fatima, at the back, looked up from her knots: “And crabs, little one, are you still scared of them?” Thirty fishermen burst out laughing. The quarrel settled itself. I think she did it on purpose.
textes.En plein match, il a voulu me porter cha: In the middle of a match, he wanted to bring me luck: he opened his gourd so Xan could watch me play. Xan came out and stung me on the hip, right at the moment of the shot. The ball went off crooked… and passed very close to the ring. Not through. Close. Kinich says it's the best shot of my life. It's true it was close.
textes.En plein morceau, je lui ai demandé de r: In the middle of a song, I asked him to play the low note again. For its colour. He sighed, he played it again. I closed my eyes: dark violet, almost plum. He played it ten times, grumbling that I was mad. I don't know why he did as I said. But I've got my violet.
textes.En pleine forme ! Hier soir, j'ai rempla: In top form! Last night, I filled in for the drummer. I did an eleven-minute solo in the middle of a soft song. Rouille looked at me. Clou looked at me. Mouette laughed. It was HUGE.
textes.En pleine forme ! J'ai chanté le Grand C: In top form! I sang the Great Hymn of the Noodles this morning, all seven verses. Three birds flew away. That means it was powerful.
textes.En pleine forme ! J'ai fait trois fois l: Feeling great! I flew three times round the Tree before breakfast.
textes.En pleine forme ! J'ai vendu tout le mér: On top form! I sold all the grouper before nine o'clock.
textes.En pleine forme ! Je cours tous les mati: Fighting fit! I run every morning. To the bakery.
textes.En pleine forme ! Le bleu est revenu, le: Never better! The blue is back, the sky is reflected in the pond again. I want to repaint everything. Even Lili. She doesn't agree.
textes.En pleine forme ! Le feu est bon, le fer: In top form! The fire is good, the iron is willing, and nobody has dropped a hammer on my foot yet today.
textes.En pleine forme ! Le grand marteau a tap: In top form! The big hammer struck a thousand times this morning, and I laughed a thousand and one times. The last one was because Pimprenelle tried to lift my tongs. She lifted them! A bit! HA HA!
textes.En pleine forme ! Mamie Rissole m'a fait: Fighting fit! Mamie Rissole made me a two-kilo pie. I ate half, and she stared at me until I finished the other half.
textes.En pleine forme, Tom ! Il s'est échauffé: In top form, Tom! He's been warming up all day!
textes.En pleine forme, sur toutes les fréquenc: In top form, on every frequency! This morning, I gave the weather: “grey, like Mr Lisse”. He called the radio to complain. I put him on air. A great moment of radio.
textes.En pleine forme. J'ai planté sept coutea: In great shape. I stuck seven knives in the same knothole this morning. The ship will remember it.
textes.En rangs, les nuages ! « La Marche des M: Fall in, clouds! “The March of the Sky Sheep”! Left, right! Left, right!
textes.En remontant vers sa cité, je l'ai vu gl: On the way back up to his city, I saw him slip one of my axes into his belt instead of tossing it on the pile. Just one, the best. He probably says it's for showing apprentices what not to do. Me, I know a customer with taste when I see one.
textes.En rentrant de ma traversée, j'ai couru: When I got back from my crossing, I ran to see Corentin even before my mother. I told him: “There's a gate at the foot of Stoneheart. Your story is true.” He looked offended: “Of course it's true, lad. What did you think?” Then he downed his hot honey in one go. I think he was moved.
textes.En retard. (Il ferme les yeux.) Bon. Je: Late. (He closes his eyes.) Very well. I'll give you a watch. One that rings five minutes early. Like Barnabé's. It doesn't work on him, but you, you stand a chance.
Late… Ah. A delay is nothing. Usually. Just watch out for the delays that matter, okay? Fffwoosh. Right, I'm off.
textes.En revenant de Tazira, j'ai montré à Lil: Coming back from Tazira, I showed Lilas the steps they dance on their square. She said: “A goat dance!” She learned it anyway, laughing. That very evening, the whole Circle tried it. Bedaine rolled onto Pépin, Gland thought he was a billy goat, and Mother Moon danced it with one paw, without leaving her moss.
textes.En revenant des dunes, je suis passé dev: Coming back from the dunes, I went past the Fondouk. He was sitting there, by the door. Calm. He watched me arrive, burnt, throat dry. He held out his hand. A date. Just one. I took it. I ate it. I said nothing. Neither did he. Hm. It was good. That annoys me.
textes.En rond ! Ah, tu as le cœur d'un chemino: Round in circles! Ah, you've got the heart of a Strata railwayman. You set off, you see everything, and you come back to the platform, where someone's waiting for you. Hop on, I'll take you.
In circles, I know. On purpose.
Round in a circle, to come back.
textes.En rythme ! Cent vingt battements par mi: In rhythm! A hundred and twenty beats per minute, like my heart. Well, like my heart when I'm dancing.
textes.En rêve… Ça compte. Ça compte plus, même: In dreams… That counts. It counts even more. Dream whales, nobody can tell you they don't exist.
textes.En secret, je vais parfois à Rainville v: In secret, I sometimes go to Rainville to see Mother Downpour's garden. Moss grows there, ferns, mushrooms that glow at night. Plants that love the rain. I'd so love to mix our two gardens.
textes.En selle ! Stick gauche : vers l'avant p: Saddle up! Left stick: forward to climb, back to descend, left or right to turn. Right trigger: faster, left trigger: brake. A: land.
textes.En selle ! Z / S : plus vite / freiner,: Saddle up! W / S: faster / brake, A / D: turn, Space: climb, Ctrl: descend, E: land.
textes.En service. Toujours. Ma femme dit que m: On duty. Always. My wife says I do my rounds even at night. In my bed. In step.
textes.En soupe ! Une bonne soupe de poisson, ç: In soup! A good fish soup warms you right up to your horns. They say in Port-Azur they make one with ten fish. Ten! I put in twelve. To win.
textes.En vingt, s'il te plaît. Avec ma moustac: In twenty, please. With my moustache.
textes.En voiture ! Ah, tu ne montes pas ? Tant: All aboard! Ah, you're not getting on? Never mind, hello anyway! Grandpa Ferdinand Vapeur, engineer and driver of the Little Strata Train. And this is Bernadette, the prettiest locomotive in the cavern. She goes round the Strata all day long, and she's never been late. Well, she has. But it was my fault.
textes.En échange de la bouteille de nuit, j'ap: In exchange for the night bottle, I bring Gaston the star forecast, every morning. “Clear sky, rising moon, a shooting star around three o'clock.” He pins it up next to the counter. The customers read it as they drink. Professor Boum claims it gives him ideas. That's exactly what worries me.
textes.En écrire ! Alors tu es de ceux qui font: Write! Then you're one of those who make words fly. I carry them; you make them. We're a team! You write, I deliver!
textes.En été, le soleil tape sur les créneaux: In summer, the sun beats down on the battlements from ten o'clock. One morning, without a word, the caïd took the guard's parasol and moved it three steps, towards me. Then he went back to his post, stiff as a cannon. The next day, the same. Now, every morning, the parasol is waiting for me. He says it's regulations. What regulations?
textes.Enchanting ! Je note, je note !: Enchanting! I'm writing it down, writing it down!
Anvil! Solid, patient, always there. The anvil is the most important thing. Without it, the hammer hits thin air. And looks silly.
textes.Encombrant ! Ah, un esprit libre ! Allez: Gets in the way! Ah, a free spirit! Go to the Zero-Gravity Garden: it's my favourite failed experiment. You'll love it.
textes.Encore ! Dehors ! La boutique est fermée: Again! Out! The shop is closed!
Again! I love it when it does that.
textes.Encore ? Bon. Elle est très grande, et e: Again? All right. It's very big, and it never stops talking.
textes.Encore ? Bon. Mais c'est la dernière foi: Again? Fine. But it'th the latht time, Thilas.
Again? That's the third this month.
textes.Encore ? Calcine, tu joues trop vite pou: Again? Calcine, you play too fast for my dress.
textes.Encore ? Combien de glaces je te dois ?: Again? How many ice creams do I owe you?
Again? At least she has taste.
Again? That one loves the smoke.
Again? Your runes are repeating themselves.
textes.Encore ? Gorgoth, ça fait trois capes ce: Again? Gorgoth, that's three capes this year!
textes.Encore ? J'en ai trente sous mon lit, Ma: Again? I've got thirty under my bed, Marée.
textes.Encore ? Je l'ai appris hier, Protée !: Again? I only learned it yesterday, Protée!
textes.Encore ? Je l'ai bouchée la semaine dern: Again? I plugged it last week.
textes.Encore ? Je vais finir par croire que te: Again? I'm starting to think your dice obey you.
textes.Encore ? La patience a beaucoup de jours: Again? Patience has a lot of days.
textes.Encore ? Le vent commence à vous connaît: Again? The wind is getting to know you. When you come in, it goes “whoo-whoo” under the door.
textes.Encore ? Mais à qui écrivez-vous, Victor: Again? But who are you writing to, Victor?
textes.Encore ? Ta machine a recommencé ?: Again? Your machine's done it again?
textes.Encore ? Tu as déjà la bouche toute roug: Again? Your mouth is already all red. Wait until the ladle cools down.
textes.Encore ? Tu as encore couru après l'Arch: Again? Were you chasing the Archduchess again?
Again? You know it better than I do.
textes.Encore ? Tu vas me courir après, comme d: Again? Are you going to chase after me, as usual?
textes.Encore ? Tu vas réveiller les nains, Tch: Again? You'll wake the dwarves, Tchoum!
textes.Encore ? Volontiers ! Un, deux, trois… H: Again? Gladly! One, two, three… Ha ha! You dance better than my husband. Don't tell him.
textes.Encore ? Ça fait combien de pages ?: Again? How many pages is that now?
textes.Encore ?! Je m'en souviendrai, crois-moi: Again?! I'll remember this, believe me.
Again?! You like explosions, you do. So do I.
textes.Encore ?! Tu as un estomac de Moaï, toi: Again?! You have a Moai's stomach! … Come back tomorrow, it needs to cook some more.
textes.Encore des bulles, ces jours-ci ? Non ?: Any more bubbles lately? No? Pity, it was very pretty, I'm told. Mirabelle is proud of it.
textes.Encore des clous ? Elle va finir par res: More studs? Your Germaine's going to end up looking like a hedgehog!
textes.Encore des marches. Tes mollets proteste: More steps. Your calves protest politely.
textes.Encore des marches. Ça sent l'huile de m: More steps. It smells of machine oil and steam.
textes.Encore du soda qui brille, mon petit ? T: More glowing soda, little one? Tsk.
textes.Encore faim ? Mamie a encore une galette: Still hungry? Granny have one more flatbread.
textes.Encore gagné ! Tu regardais où, Lucas ?: Won again! Where were you looking, Lucas? Oh, I know where.
textes.Encore le poisson ? Je t'ai à l'œil, toi: Still the fish? I've got my eye on you. Smell this. Saffron. There. You already smell better.
textes.Encore le virus de Fil ? Donne-moi ton c: Fil's virus again? Give me your journal. (She plugs a pink cable into your journal and types at lightning speed.) There: I'm opening up the system for you. Pick up where you left off.
textes.Encore lui ? Je finirai par croire que t: Him again? I'm starting to think you do it on purpose.
textes.Encore merci ! À ce rythme-là, on aura f: Thanks again! At this rate, we'll be done before teatime.
textes.Encore pieds nus ? Ou presque ? Approche: Still barefoot? Or nearly? Come here!
textes.Encore toi ! Tu vas finir par voler, à f: You again! Keep this up and you'll end up flying.
textes.Encore toi ?! … Bon. Qu'est-ce que tu ve: You again?! … Fine. What do you want.
textes.Encore toi, {surnom}. Tu as des pièces,: You again, {surnom}. You've got coins, I hope.
textes.Encore toi. Hm. Qu'est-ce que tu veux, c: You again. Hm. What do you want this time?
textes.Encore toi. Hmpf. Tu tiens debout, c'est: You again. Hmph. You're still standing, that's something.
textes.Encore toi. Tu ne tiens pas en place, he: You again. Can't sit still, can you?
textes.Encore trois cartes à classer, et je vai: Three more charts to file, and then I'm off to release the weather balloon with the team.
Three more rows, and then I'll have lunch.
textes.Encore trouvé ! La prochaine fois, je me: Found again! Next time, I'm hiding in the fireplace. No, just kidding. Or maybe not.
textes.Encore un ! Je vais finir par avoir des: Another one! I'll end up growing scales, sweetie.
textes.Encore un ? Ma tente en est pleine, gran: Another one? My tent's full of them, you big softie. … Thank you.
textes.Encore un ? Tu as bon appétit, ça fait p: Another one? You've got a good appetite, it's a joy to see!
textes.Encore un ? Tu vas finir par flotter ! R: Another one? You'll end up floating! Come back for the next flight: we'll make pancakes. Forty, according to the speaking tube.
textes.Encore un caillou dans ta roue, Clapotis: Another pebble in your wheel, Clapotis?
textes.Encore un chocolat, et je rentre. Ça fai: One more hot chocolate, and I'm off home. That's the third time I've said that.
Another one of your programs, Fil.
textes.Encore un mot, tête de thon, et tu rentr: One more word, tuna-head, and you swim home.
textes.Encore un mot. Un seul. Et je t'envoie n: One more word. Just one. And I'll send you to feed the crabs.
One more step and I swing.
textes.Encore un peu d'épicé, mon chou ? Mon po: A bit more spice, sweetie? My pepper's asking for you.
textes.Encore un tampon, et j'ai le record de l: One more stamp, and I've got the record for the week.
textes.Encore un tour ! Les rubans s'emmêlent u: One more lap! The ribbons get a bit tangled, but nobody will mind.
textes.Encore un tour ? La cabine rouge est plu: Another ride? The red cabin is faster. No, that's not true, they go the same speed. But the red one is prettier.
textes.Encore un triomphe ! Le vent en redemand: Another triumph! The wind is calling for an encore.
textes.Encore une gauche ? Il y a quelqu'un là-: Another left? Somebody up there is hopping on one foot.
textes.Encore une réussite ! Tu devrais ouvrir: Another success! You should open your own shop.
textes.Encore vous. Bien. Le froid aime les gen: You again. Good. The cold likes people who come back. It waits for them.
textes.Encore {dernier_cadeau} ? Tu me gâtes !: {dernier_cadeau} again? You spoil me! That's {nb_cadeaux} gifts, I'm counting, you know.
textes.Encore {manque} coquillages ! Sur la pla: {manque} more shells! There are loads on your island's beach, Lyra said!
textes.Encore {manque} cœurs de magma, {surnom}: {manque} more magma hearts, {surnom}. My lanterns are flickering.
textes.Encore {manque} perles. Rondes et blanch: {manque} more pearls. Round and white, like dew.
textes.Encore {manque} rayons de miel, {surnom}: {manque} more honeycombs, {surnom}. My barrel is waiting.
textes.Encore {manque}… Elles sont peut-être da: {manque} more… Maybe they're in corners nobody ever goes to. Or right at the top.
textes.Encore, mousse ? Approche, approche…: Again, cabin boy? Come closer, come closer…
textes.Encre-oyablement bien ! J'ai imprimé tro: Ink-credibly well! I printed three hundred copies this morning. Two hundred and ninety-nine of them are readable. The three hundredth has a thumb in the middle. Mine. It's a collector's edition.
Child of the surface… come closer.
textes.Enfant, Son Altesse se cachait dans le g: As a child, Her Highness used to hide in the great chandelier of the throne room. I found her by the smell of singed lace, but I pretended to search everywhere, to hear her laugh. One day, she fell asleep up there. I stood guard at the foot of the ladder until she woke. Four hours. Standing. As is proper.
textes.Enfant, j'étais déjà au bout de cette je: As a child, I was already at the end of this jetty, with a string line and a bent hook. I lived next door to little Fatima. She tied knots with her mother on the doorstep, and I wanted to do better. I never beat her. Not once. She still reminds me, seventy years later.
textes.Enfant, je passais mes journées dans les: As a child, I spent my days in my mother's Ash Gardens. At five, I was already labelling her jam jars, with the date, the weight and the scientific name of each fruit. My mother gave me a funny look. She still looks at me like that. But her jars are always labelled. By me.
textes.Enfant, je sautais du toit pour voler, e: As a child, I'd jump off the roof to fly, and always landed in Mother Brasille's cabbages. She'd pick me up, give me a herbal tea and send me home. The tenth time, I found a big cushion placed under the roof. She said it was to protect her cabbages. The cabbages had never needed a cushion before me.
textes.Enfant, sur le continent, j'ai ramassé u: As a child, on the mainland, I picked up a large shell on the edge of a grey beach. I held it to my ear, and I heard a city. Voices, bells, a crowd under the water. That evening, my grandfather read me a very old text about a sunken city and a queen with hair of sea foam. I never quite came back from it.
textes.Enfin ! Mes clients réclamaient leurs ta: At last! My customers were demanding their toast. Thank you, and tell Margaux she's an angel.
textes.Enfin ! Quelqu'un qui me comprend. Viens: At last! Someone who understands me. Come, I'll make you a cape. It'll be useless in battle, but you'll look magnificent falling over.
textes.Enfin ! Un client raisonnable ! Je vous: At last! A reasonable customer! I'll reserve you a parking space. Number one. It's at the very back. But it's number one.
textes.Enfin ! Un homme de goût ! Une âme d'ora: At last! A person of taste! An orator's soul! I award you the Medal of Listening! I'll have it forged at once!
textes.Enfin ! Une aventure véritable ! Avec un: At last! A real adventure! With a witness! Onward, friend, let's go!
textes.Enfin quelqu'un de sérieux. Comptant, to: Finally, someone serious. Cash, always cash. Debts are like iron: they don't disappear just because you look the other way.
textes.Enfin quelqu'un qui reconnaît le génie !: At last, someone who recognises genius! I'm coming. Stay behind me when I cast a lightning bolt. Or in front. Well, not too close.
textes.Enfin un lecteur de qualité ! Tu es abon: Finally, a reader of quality! You're subscribed for life. Here's one: why are printers always so calm? Because they never lose their in-k-composure. … Thank you, thank you.
textes.Enfin, que Barricade ne me contredise pa: Well, as long as Barricade doesn't contradict me. The others, I couldn't care less.
Well… it's not my best day.
textes.Enregistrer le Grand Boucan en entier, a: To record the whole Great Boucan, with everyone's sound: Rouille's voice, Clou's guitar, Mouette's bass, the shouts from the pit, Chaussette's dogs. AND HAVE IT BE PERFECT! Once. Just once.
textes.Ensemble, nous écrirons une légende ! Be: Together, we'll write a legend! Bertrand will sing it! Without the fog!
textes.Ensemble. (Il hoche la tête longuement.): Together. (He nods slowly.) That's why this fire has burned for fifty years. You could hold the key yourself, one day.
textes.Ensoleillée, avec quelques passages nuag: Sunny, with a few cloudy spells in the late afternoon. The Council voted the Greenhouses budget. Mr Pascal voted against. Then he came to ask me whether we could add a birdhouse. We added it.
textes.Ensommeillé, mais heureux. Les vieux our: Sleepy, but happy. Old bears doze.
textes.Ensuite viennent les Limbes, où dort la: Next comes Limbo, where the light of the sages sleeps, then Minos the judge, who wraps his tail around himself to think, and the Tempest, where the wind blows without rest. Then Cerbère, the three-headed dog. Each head thinks it's the most important: give a honey cake to each one, or the other two sulk. And a sulking head bites.
textes.Entendre la conque d'Ehécatl, celle qui: To hear the conch of Ehécatl, the one that set the sun in motion. They say it's waiting beneath the Great Temple. Just one breath, and I'd know which note makes the world turn.
textes.Entendre les clochettes des fées du Bois: To hear the little bells of the Bois-Doré fairies, the ones that play in rhythm. Keep them in my head, and hum them to Mistral so he can make a track out of them.
textes.Entendre un arbre me répondre « bonjour: To hear a tree answer me “hello”. Just once. Even very slowly. Even if it takes three nights for a single sentence. I have time. My battery is excellent.
textes.Entendre une baleine me répondre. Une se: To hear a whale answer me. Just once. My great-grandfather spoke to them as to old friends; all I've ever had from them is their backs.
textes.Entendu ! … Une toute petite, alors ?: Understood! … Just a teeny one, then?
Heard it… Me too, I think, one night. Or it was Nausicaa. Or my stomach. The job makes you suspicious.
textes.Entre ! Tu as faim ? Attention à la tête: Come in! Hungry? Mind your head: in this house, the toast arrives by air.
textes.Entre deux pots de tomates : une tirelir: Between two tomato pots: a piggy bank shaped like a radish. Radis had forgotten it. He'll say it's for you.
textes.Entre donc dans le moulin ! Regarde tour: Do come into the mill! Watch the great wheel turn, listen to the millstone sing. And if you let go of the brake… hold on tight, it'll blow your hair back.
textes.Entre les deux ? Dans la cabine ? Ha ! T: In between? In the cabin? Ha! You're a real liftkeeper. That's the best place to be: neither up nor down. Off we go.
textes.Entre nous : Marius, le chef de gare, pa: Between you and me: Marius, the station master, talks to his cabin. “Easy, my bubble, easy.” He says it's to encourage her. I say it's love. I've noted both versions in my Notebook.
textes.Entre nous, citoyen : Mama Grog a plus d: Between you and me, citizen: Mama Grog has more authority than I do. But don't repeat it. Especially not to her.
textes.Entre nous, depuis que Nimiel est née, j: Between you and me, since Nimiel was born, I only pick with one hand: the other catches her. I know she climbs with no hands, that she's hiding a frog, and that she sneaks out at night with something long under her arm. I pretend I know nothing. Mothers do a lot of pretending.
textes.Entre nous, j'ai toujours rêvé d'être ch: Between you and me, I always dreamt of being an opera singer. Django says I have the voice of a seal with a cold.
textes.Entre nous, j'aurais voulu être maître-n: Between us, I'd have liked to be a lifeguard. But I can't swim. So I keep watch over the town. It's a big swimming pool, without the water.
textes.Entre nous, mon chou : Augustin le meuni: Between you and me, sweetie: Augustin the miller writes poems to Miss Philippine. He hides them in the sacks of flour he delivers to the Library. The Library doesn't need flour. You didn't hear it from me!
textes.Entre nous, petit : c'est qui, le champi: Between you and me, kid: who's the champion of Port-Azur?
textes.Entre nous… ce n'était peut-être pas que: Between you and me… maybe it wasn't just the map. Maybe I'd dozed off a bit at the helm. Don't EVER tell Barnabé.
textes.Entre nous… j'ai vu des lumières au somm: Between you and me… I saw lights at the top of the tallest rock spire one night. Gaston says it was the moon. Gaston says a lot of things.
textes.Entre, entre ! Attention à la marche, au: Come in, come in! Mind the step, the stuffed owl, and the step. Madame Olga, magic merchant! Potions, elixirs, staffs, and… all that. I don't remember what all that is anymore. But it's surely magic.
textes.Entre, entre ! Bienvenue au Diable Repu,: Come in, come in! Welcome to the Diable Repu, the best tavern on Ember Island! Grumbald, landlord, cook and confidant. Hot sulphur punch, Brasier coffee, frozen lava: we serve everything that warms you up, and one thing that cools you down. Sit wherever you like, except at the Captain's table.
textes.Entre, entre ! Et ferme la porte, sinon: Come in, come in! And shut the door, or Filou will slip off again.
textes.Entre, entre ! Ici, la porte est toujour: Come in, come in! Here the door is always open and the teapot always warm. Want some herbal tea? Mint from Lavande's garden, chamomile, and a poppy petal for the color.
textes.Entre, entre ! Ici, on danse du matin au: Come in, come in! Here we dance from morning till night. The piano only knows three tunes, and so do we.
textes.Entre, entre ! Je suis Vinyle, le disqua: Come in, come in! I'm Vinyle, the record seller. I've got every record on the island here: the Gutters, the Flower Camp songs, the old Larsen Festival concerts… Hear that little crackle? That's the music breathing.
textes.Entre, entre, ferme la porte, tu fais en: Come in, come in, shut the door, you're letting the draught in! Berthe Chaudron, of the Smoking Cauldron. Here, the soup is hot, the honey drink is sweet, and nobody does magic at the table. That's the rule.
textes.Entre, entre, mais parle fort : ici, ça: Come in, come in, but speak up: in here it's tick-tock from morning till night. And cuckoo every half-minute.
textes.Entre, entre, mon petit champignon. N'ai: Come in, come in, my little mushroom. Don't be afraid of the blue light: it's the caps glowing. I'm Mère Morille. I live here, in the Spore Cathedral, with the fairy mushrooms. They're magic, yes. And I'll tell you right away: in a fairy tale, you can taste them. In the real forest: never! Never a mushroom you don't know.
textes.Entre, entre, ne reste pas dans le coura: Come in, come in, don't stand in the draft!
Come in, come in, don't stand in the draught! Welcome to La Dernière Bordée. Here we eat, we drink, we sing off-key and we sleep dry. I'm Gwenola. Everyone says “Mother Gwenola”. So will you.

Come in, come in, don't stand in the draught! Welcome to La Marmite, dearie. Honorine Lanterne. Here, we eat warm, we drink warm, and we leave with a warm heart. Soup, galettes, chocolate. Not a drop of strong drink: underground, you keep a clear head and a steady foot. Sit down. Have you eaten? No. I can tell.
textes.Entre, entre, ne reste pas sur le seuil,: Come in, come in, don't stand in the doorway, you're blocking the spiral! Welcome to La Conque, my little fish. Josette Salicorne, cook. Here, we eat the sea: samphire soup, samphire galettes, fish from the Pool, and to finish, a deep-sea hot chocolate, dark as the Trench. Not a drop of strong drink: under the sea, we keep a clear head. Taste!
Come in, come in, traveller… I was expecting you. Well, I expect everyone, it's my job. Madame Rita sees the past, the present and what is left to do.
textes.Entre, et essuie tes bottes. Ici, c'est: Come in, and wipe your boots. This is La Murène Ivre. I'm Mama Lou. The rules are simple: you pay, you break nothing, and you don't fight. Outside, you can do what you like.
textes.Entre, il fait bon !: Come in, it's nice and warm!
Come in, or stay outside. But make up your mind.
textes.Entrer dans Pandémonia, la cité aux mill: Enter Pandémonia, the city of a thousand lanterns
textes.Entrer dans Yggdrasil par la porte aux r: Enter Yggdrasil through the rune door
Enter Yggdrasil through the rune door, cross its three halls to the Crown and receive the seed
textes.Entrer dans l'Usine Grise (au sud-est de: Enter the Grey Factory (in the south-east of the island, behind the Spore Wood), go down the five floors and defeat the Great Digger in the President's Pit
textes.Entrer dans la cité de cristal et de lum: Enter the city of crystal and light
textes.Entrer dans la cité sous la montagne: Enter the city under the mountain
textes.Entrer dans le Rocher du Crâne par sa bo: Enter Skull Rock through its mouth and open Barbe-Sanglante's chest (E)
textes.Entrez ! Attention au panier. Ici, le co: Come in! Mind the basket. Here, the post comes in through the ceiling, and it doesn't wait.
Come in! … Oh no, it's locked.
textes.Entrez, entrez ! Bienvenue au Bazar des: Come in, come in! Welcome to the Bazaar of Useless Things! Madame Bricolette. Here, everything is useless, and everything is marvellous. A propeller umbrella? A box of nothing? A compass that points south? Nothing is good for anything, but everything looks lovely in a bag!
