textes.Exceptionnelle ! J'ai vendu une cabane d: Exceptional! I sold a fisherman's hut to a traveller by telling him it had “a lake view”. It has a lake view. And the lake has a view of it. So do the frogs.
textes.Exclusif ! Gédéon tapote sur les rails à: Exclusive! Gédéon taps on the rails at lunchtime, every day. We've formed a band with him. We do the backing vocals.
textes.Exclusif : Mademoiselle Prune a un badge: Exclusive: Mademoiselle Prune has a Bilge Rats badge hidden under her jacket. I saw it shine. I didn't publish it. A good journalist protects her sources. And their badges.
textes.Exclusivité : le professeur Boum prépare: Exclusive: Professor Boum is preparing an explosion bigger than all the others. He says it will be “the one”. Newsroom on alert.
textes.Exclusivité Radio Boucan : Tapage aurait: Radio Boucan exclusive: Tapage allegedly played in 1977. Or in 1978. He and Mamie Barricade argue about it live every Thursday. It's my most popular show.
textes.Explosive ! Dans le bon sens ! Ma derniè: Explosive! In a good way! My latest rocket reached the top of the lighthouse. Well, the top of the lighthouse reached my rocket. We're not quite sure.
Explosive! But in a good way.
textes.Exprès ? C'est génial ! Moi je rate sans: On purpose? That's brilliant! I mess up without meaning to, but from now on, if anyone asks, I'll say it's on purpose. Thanks!
textes.Exprès, comme toujours ? J'adore ton sil: On purpose, as always? I love your silence, Tom.
textes.Extraordinary ! Elle sera la reine de ma: Extraordinary! She will be the queen of my collection. Here are two gold coins, minted by my great-grandfather. Cheers!
textes.Exécrable ! Un chat ! Un CHAT m'a volé c: Dreadful! A cat! A CAT stole my most precious possession. If I catch it…
textes.F'est un poiffon qui rentre dans une tav: Tho a fith walkth into a tavern…
textes.FAUSSE ?! Ma carte était un chef-d'œuvre: WRONG?! My map was a masterpiece! Gaston, remind me never to speak of that fellow again.
textes.Fabriquer un tonneau si beau qu'on n'ose: To make a barrel so beautiful nobody would dare fill it. We'd put it in the middle of the Crâne Fendu, and everyone would come and look at it. Even Papa. Hic!
textes.Face à la Baie, il y a une cheminée hydr: Opposite the Bay there's a hydrothermal vent: a hot spring at the bottom of the sea that puffs out black smoke. All around it, giant worms, red and white, as tall as you. Little Mila calls them “the candy canes”. I looked for a more scholarly name. I couldn't find a better one.
textes.Facture du Piston Joyeux : nettoyage de: Bill from the Jolly Piston: moustache cleaning, two coins!
textes.Facture du Piston Joyeux : « Un chocolat: Bill from the Jolly Piston: “One hot chocolate: 4 coins. Moustache cleaning (yours, it fell in): 2 coins. Four o'clock whistle: on the house.” Signed: Firmin Bouilloire.
textes.Faelar ! Cette fois, tu me donnes la rép: Faelar! This time, will you give me the answer?
textes.Faelar ! Raconte celle du hibou !: Faelar! Tell the one about the owl!
textes.Faelar ! Une histoire pour mon four, ce: Faelar! A story for my oven this morning?
textes.Faelar ? Le plus bavard des elfes, et le: Faelar? The chattiest of elves, and the only one who's ever beaten me. He left me a riddle three hundred years ago, and he had the nerve to grow old with the answer.
textes.Faelar ? Le plus vieil elfe du monde, et: Faelar? The oldest elf in the world, and he knows my song by heart! He thinks the hero is shorter than in the verses. That's poetry, come now!
textes.Faelar a neuf cent quatre-vingt-sept ans: Faelar is nine hundred and eighty-seven, and he refuses to drink a tea unless it has a story. So I make them up for him. He knows. He drinks them anyway.
textes.Faelar a toussé pendant trois siècles. I: Faelar coughed for three centuries. He said it was “an old friend who punctuates my stories”. I made him a hundred herbal teas. He'd pour half of each into his fern's pot. The fern never coughed, mind you. It's now two metres tall.
textes.Faelar a vu pousser presque tous les arb: Faelar has watched almost every tree in Bois-Doré grow. Nobody tells stories better than he does. When he doesn't fall asleep halfway through.
textes.Faelar connaît trois mille histoires ! I: Faelar knows three thousand stories! He falls asleep in the middle, but that doesn't matter: I know the ending. Well, I make one up. He says mine are better.
textes.Faelar m'a appris qu'une histoire ne rem: Faelar taught me that a story doesn't fill your belly. He didn't mean to. That's why I became a baker. I save him the first crust of every batch.
textes.Faelar m'a appris à pêcher la lumière en: Faelar taught me to fish for light while talking non-stop beside me. I think he did it on purpose: if you can fish next to Faelar, you can fish anywhere.
textes.Faelar m'a dit que les esprits-lucioles: Faelar told me the firefly spirits dance above the rings of white mushrooms. I saw one! I wanted to follow it, but Faelar hooked my sleeve with his walking stick. He said: “Not you. Not yet.” I sulked at him for two days. Then he told me a story and I forgot.
textes.Faelar m'a parlé d'un cercle de champign: Faelar told me about a ring of white mushrooms where spirits dance. I laughed. Then I went there seven nights in a row. On the eighth, there was a little light. I ran home and shook him: he'd been asleep for two days. He opened one eye, said “I know”, and went back to sleep.
textes.Faelar raconte des choses que personne n: Faelar tells of things nobody has seen. I go and look. Most of the time there's nothing. But sometimes there's something, and that's why I keep going back.
textes.Faelar raconte qu'un humain a vaincu le: Faelar says a human defeated the great serpent under the sea. Was it you?! Have a loaf. Have two!
textes.Faelar s'est endormi au milieu d'une his: Faelar fell asleep in the middle of a story. Again. We put a flower on his nose.
textes.Faelar vient raconter une histoire à mon: Faelar comes to tell my oven a story every morning while the bread bakes. I swear the oven rises better. Faelar swears he doesn't come for the crust. One of us is lying, and it isn't the oven.
textes.Faelar, tu t'étais endormi exprès, ce so: Faelar, you fell asleep on purpose that night. Admit it.
textes.Faelar. Ton hibou d'argent, au nord. Rie: Faelar. Your silver owl, up north. Nothing.
textes.Faire avec Honorine la soupe des quatre: To make the soup of the four worlds with Honorine: her mushrooms from the Strata, my seaweed from the Dome, apples from the Orchards of Hautefond, and the giant strawberries of the Clouds for dessert. To serve it on Pearl Square, at one single big table, while Rosalie opens a bag of cinnamon in the middle. Everyone will sneeze at the same time. It'll be the finest party the Column has ever seen.
textes.Faire chanter toute l'île en même temps,: To get the whole island singing at once, from the Borgo all the way up to the Cooking Pot, and make the Great Spaghetti stomp its feet. If it has feet. It must have feet somewhere.
textes.Faire griller des choses ! La réponse la: Toasting things! The wisest answer of all. Bobor would be proud of you. Me too, a little. And now I'm hungry.
textes.Faire la connaissance de Pip, le plus je: Meet Pip, the youngest of the apprentices (in the Academy courtyard in the morning, on the village square in the evening)
textes.Faire la grande descente de la Colonne t: To make the great descent of the whole Column, from the Clouds down to the Azure Dome, with Capucine beside me, and for once not need the speaking tube to talk to her. Just the two of us keeping quiet, watching the four worlds go by.
textes.Faire la plus grande bulle du monde, ass: To blow the biggest bubble in the world, big enough to fit all of Boucan inside. It would float above the harbour, and everyone would see the town in rainbow colours. For three seconds. Then pop.
textes.Faire la première montée vers la Cité de: To make the first ride up to the City of Clouds with my eyes open, from start to finish, and say “Going up!” without my voice shaking. Not even a tiny bit.
To make the first ride up to the City of Clouds when the line reopens, with Barnabé at the controls, and not say a single word the whole way. Just watch the Column do what it does best.
textes.Faire le grand voyage de la Colonne tout: To make the great journey down the whole Column, from Cloud Station to the Azure Dome at the bottom of the sea, with Barnabé beside me, and get him to look out of the window at least once. Just once. I'll do the rest of the looking for both of us.
textes.Faire le plus grand bouquet du monde, av: To make the biggest bouquet in the world, with a flower from every island in the archipelago, and give it to all of Crayon Island on the day it gets its colours back.
textes.Faire le saut de la rampe jusqu'au bord: To jump from the ramp all the way to the edge of the Dry Dock, without falling at the end. In front of everyone. And Cerise has to write “Tornade did it” in her zine. Once. Just once.
textes.Faire le tour complet de l'île avec Nimi: To walk all the way around the island with Nimiel one day, taking our time. She'll run ahead, I'll walk behind, and we'll meet up at the same spot. That's how a family travels.
textes.Faire le tour de la ville en monorail (l: Ride the monorail around the city (all four stations)
textes.Faire le tour de toute la grande île en: Run all the way round the big island! Cliquetis, Tazira, Carène, and back to Ramure. And get there before the Zéphyr!
textes.Faire le tour du monde avec le Requin, s: Sail round the world with the Shark, non-stop, and come back from the other side just to see Lestrange's face. With a big rosewood perch in my cabin for Rhubarbe.
textes.Faire le tour du monde par les airs avec: To fly around the world with Héloïse, the Albatross and the Dragonfly side by side, over every world of the Column and every island of the archipelago. And arrive exactly together, a second time. So we can both shout “I won!” at the same time, again.
textes.Faire le tour du monde par les airs, san: To fly round the world, without stopping, just looking at everything from above. And find, somewhere above an ocean, a little red balloon that was waiting for me.
textes.Faire les offrandes du Grand Temple d'Az: Make the offerings at the Great Temple of Aztlán
textes.Faire monter ma machine à chocolat à la: To take my chocolate machine up to the City of Clouds, now that the line has reopened, and make it whistle above the clouds, under the windows of my brother Gustave's Cumulus Café. Loud enough to be heard all the way down. So that everyone, in all four worlds, knows there's hot chocolate.

To take my chocolate machine up to the City of Clouds when the line reopens, and make it whistle above the clouds. So they hear it all the way down. So everyone, in all four worlds, knows there's chocolate.
textes.Faire pousser la plus grosse tomate du m: To grow the biggest tomato in the world, as big as one of the forecourt meatballs, and give it to the Great Spaghetti for its birthday. Nobody knows when that is. I picked the first day of spring.
textes.Faire pousser un champignon lumineux dan: To grow a glowing mushroom in each of the Column's four worlds: one in the Clouds, at Flora's, one in Old Bastien's Orchards, one here, and one under the Azure Dome. So that at night, everywhere, there's a little Strata light keeping watch.
textes.Faire pousser, au cœur des Serres d'Alti: To grow, at the heart of the High-Altitude Greenhouses, a plant from each world of the Column: a cloud flower, a Hautefond apple tree, a glowing mushroom from the Strata and a seaweed from the Azure Dome. A garden of four worlds. And let the butterflies decide where they'd rather sleep.
textes.Faire redescendre les quatre livres envo: Bring the four runaway books back down with telekinesis (key 9 then V, aiming at the book; in VR, left trigger): on the library roof, on the highest Moonstone of the Circle, at a window of the Leaning Tower and in a big oak in the Twisted Wood
textes.Faire siffler l'ampli (l'effet Larsen): Make the amp squeal (the Larsen effect)
textes.Faire tourner la vieille vanne de la gra: Turn the old sluice valve of Ramure's big pond with the Cog (key 3 then X; in VR, B), then, at night, take the Seal of Mists from the round stone at the bottom of the pond
textes.Faire un cacao si mousseux que la mousse: To make a cacao so frothy that the froth would stand up all by itself above the cup, like a little cloud. The gods would come down to breathe it.
textes.Faire un concert sur la plage, au soleil: Play a gig on the beach, at sunset, in front of thousands of seagulls. Real ones. And have them all screech “KIAAA” on the chorus. It would be the best audience in the world.
textes.Faire un hippopotame de faïence aussi gr: To make a faience hippopotamus as big as a calf, blue as the morning sky, for the temple courtyard. The children would climb on it. Big Blue would be jealous.
textes.Faire une bière si bonne que Rê s'arrête: To brew a beer so good that Rê stops in the sky to take a sip. A small one. He has a long way to go.
Make a map of all my tunnels. All of them! Even the ones I've forgotten. Especially those. And hang it above the bed, for Brunna.
textes.Faire une course autour de tout l'archip: To race around the whole archipelago, island by island, against someone very, very fast. And lose. Just once. To see what it feels like. Then get my revenge the next day.
textes.Faire une farce à toute l'île en même te: To play a prank on the whole island at once. A giant prank. So that everyone laughs for a whole hour, even Volt, even Tempo, even Écliptique. And afterwards, for once, to say: “It was me!”
textes.Faire une fois le trajet en cabine, du h: To ride the cable car just once, from top to bottom, without closing my eyes. With Écrou beside me holding my hand, the way I held hers on the stairs, at the third hundred. Forty seconds. Forty seconds is nothing. It's nothing.
textes.Faire une grande soupe des quatre mondes: To make a great soup of the four worlds with Josette, from La Conque, now that the Dome Line has reopened: mushrooms from the Strata, apples from Hautefond, strawberries from the Clouds (for dessert) and a seaweed from the Dome. And serve it in Cogwheel Square, at one single big table, to everyone. Even the Burgomaster. Especially the Burgomaster.

To make a great soup of the four worlds, when the Dome Line reopens: mushrooms from the Strata, apples from Hautefond, strawberries from the Clouds (for dessert) and a seaweed from the Dome. And serve it in Cogwheel Square, at one single big table, to everyone. Even the Burgomaster. Especially the Burgomaster.
textes.Faire une jarre si belle que Tlaloc fass: To make a jar so beautiful that Tlaloc makes it rain on the Egyptians' sandy plateau. Just a little rain. To see the look on Ptahmosé's face.
textes.Faire venir mon bateau au ponton de Port: Bring my boat to the Port-Azur jetty
textes.Faire, une seule fois dans ma vie, une p: Just once in my life, to make a completely accurate forecast: the right hour, the right minute, and the right place. Then, straight afterwards, to be magnificently wrong, so as not to lose my touch.
textes.Fais voir tes mains. Et tes coudes. Et d: Show me your hands. And your elbows. And behind your ears.
Let's see… It's a pebble. Again.
textes.Fais-le une quatrième, pour la route !: Do it a fourth time, one for the road!
At least give him a nice helmet.
textes.Faites glisser pour déplacer, molette po: Drag to move, mouse wheel to zoom.

textes.Falut, l'ami ! Fans-Dents, matelot de la: Howdy, friend! Thanth-Dentth, thailor of the Thcarlet Widow thinthe… thinthe forever! I lithp a bit when I talk. It'th becauthe of my teeth. Well, my no-teeth.
textes.Famais comptées ?! Il faut les compter,: Never counted?! You've got to count them, friend! Me, I count mine every morning. One, two. It'th quick, mind you.
textes.Fanny ? Elle déborde, elle rit, elle ren: Fanny? She overflows, she laughs, she knocks everything over. A whirlwind that smells of croissants. She's a good friend. A very good friend. Yep.
textes.Fanny pétrit en dansant. Une fois, elle: Fanny kneads while dancing. Once, she shaped a whole batch of croissants “in rhythm”, to the music still in her head. They came out of the oven all twisted, all in the same direction, as if they were dancing. I sold them as “party croissants”. They went before all the others.
textes.Fanny, c'est la famille qui arrive par l: Fanny is the family that arrives by boat every evening. She smells of warm croissants. One day she'll say yes to banana croissants. I can feel it. Good, good.
textes.Fanny, c'est un feu d'artifice avec un t: Fanny is a firework in an apron. I found her dancing behind her counter and brought her back here. My best idea. After the crab step.
textes.Fanny, mon apprentie. Elle danse toute l: Fanny, my apprentice. She dances all night at the beach party and kneads all morning. I don't know when she sleeps. Neither does she. I adore her.
textes.Farineuse ! Je suis farineuse jusqu'au b: Floury! I'm floury right up to the tips of my ears.
textes.Fascinant : les Strates ont des rues sou: Fascinating: the Strata have streets beneath the streets.
textes.Fascinante ! J'ai enfin compris à quoi s: Fascinating! I've finally understood what a “fork” is for. It's for combing spaghetti. Gloubi says no. Gloubi is not an archivist.
textes.Fatigué, mais content. La caisse numéro: Tired, but happy. Crate number twelve arrived in one piece. Her name's Gertrude.
textes.Fatigué. Frère Linguini est passé quatre: Tired. Brother Linguini walked past the Lid four times with his broom. Four times I thought he was going to hit it. Four times I was scared.
textes.Fatigué. J'ai battu le fer toute la nuit: Tired. I was hammering iron all night. A sword doesn't make itself while you sing.
textes.Fatigué. J'ai compté les dunes du sud to: Tired. I spent all day counting the southern dunes. They won't stay put.
textes.Fatigué. J'ai couru après Gérard toute l: Tired. I spent all day chasing Gérard. Gérard is my hat. Well, he was.
textes.Fatigué. J'ai joué toute la journée. Mes: Tired. I played all day. My hips are black and blue.
textes.Fatigué. J'ai passé la journée à rattrap: Tired. I spent the day catching books that wanted to go out.
textes.Fatigué. Mais la coque n'a pas pris une: Tired. But the hull didn't take a drop today. Well, hardly a drop.
textes.Fatigué. Mon moteur perpétuel, lui, ne s: Tired. My perpetual motion engine never gets tired, though. That's the whole idea.
Tired. Forty feet of tunnel yesterday. And it caved in. Well, thirty-nine.
textes.Fatigué. À mon âge, les filets pèsent pl: Tired. At my age, the nets weigh more than the fish.
textes.Fatiguée, mais ce soir il y a la fête. O: Tired, but tonight there's the party. We dance, and our feet forget the day.
textes.Fatiguée, mais contente. Après une Desce: Tired, but happy. After a Movers' Raid, everyone has bruised arms from linking elbows. Friendship bruises. I treat them with respect.
textes.Fatiguée, mais contente. Écliptique est: Tired, but happy. Écliptique came by three times today: he'd fallen off the stage, then off his chair, then off the stage again. I've prescribed him to give his speeches sitting down.
textes.Fatiguée. Après le marché, je passe voir: Tired. After the market I go and see my father at the harbour, then I go home to tuck Pépin in. He never falls asleep before he's told me about his day. Three times.
textes.Fatiguée. Garder un arbre, c'est garder: Tired. Guarding a tree is like guarding a dream: you must never quite close your eyes.
textes.Fatiguée. J'ai veillé toute la nuit sur: Tired. I sat up all night over a brew. It went sour. Like my mood.
textes.Fatiguée. Je me lève avant Rê, moi. Le s: Tired. I get up before Ra, me. At least the sun has gods to tow its boat.
textes.Fatiguée. La grande marmite a débordé ce: Tired. The big pot boiled over this morning. The whole kitchen smelled of broth. The miners said it was the best smell of the week. I scrubbed until noon.
textes.Fatiguée. Le marteau pèse plus lourd le: Tired. The hammer weighs more in the evening. The honey, less.
textes.Fatiguée. Le roi a chanté jusqu'à l'aube: Tired. The king sang until dawn. Have you ever heard a dwarf king sing? Don't.
textes.Fatiguée. Trente descentes par jour depu: Tired. Thirty trips down a day since the reopening, and thirty times Marius asking me: “And the wheels?” The wheels are doing fine. So is Marius. I'm the one with metal fatigue.
textes.Fatiguée. Trois apprentis ont roussi leu: Tired. Three apprentices singed their eyebrows today. A record.
textes.Fatima ? La seule personne de Tazira que: Fatima? The only person in Tazira I let call me “little one”. She fed me one night, sixty years ago. I've never forgotten her. Nor she me.
textes.Fatima ne voit presque plus, mais elle r: Fatima can hardly see any more, but she knows every fisherman by his step. One morning, without looking up, she said: “Ahmed slept badly. Moulay Brahim has his new slippers on. And Driss is happy.” It was all true. Driss, happy! I hadn't even noticed. She had. From his step.
textes.Fatima reconnaît chacun à son pas. Moi,: Fatima knows everyone by their step. Me, she knows by the sound of my cane, tock, tock, on the cobbles of the quay. One day, to tease her, I lent my cane to Youssef and crept along silently behind him. She said: “Hello, Youssef. Give Larbi back his cane. And you, Larbi, stop tiptoeing.”
textes.Faux ? Comme moi ! HO ! Viens ce soir !: Out of tune? Like me! HO! Come tonight! Those who sing out of tune sing with their heart, my father used to say. Youssef says that's why I scare the fish away.
textes.Faux ? Ici, personne ne chante juste ! T: Out of tune? Here, nobody sings in tune! Tapage has been singing out of tune since 1977 and he's legendary! Singing isn't about being in tune, it's about heart.
textes.Faux ? La pâte s'en fiche ! Elle aime qu: Out of tune? The dough doesn't care! It likes being sung to, not being sung to well. Ask Bertrand: he sings perfectly in tune, and his dough doesn't rise.
Out of tune. But with heart.
textes.Fañch a encore parlé à son poisson. Il d: Fañch has been talking to his fish again. He says it answers him.
textes.Fañch a laissé tomber le couteau de son: Fañch dropped his grandfather's knife in ten fathoms of water. I dived three times. At the bottom, a crab the size of a plate had settled on it and didn't want to give it back. We had a discussion. I won. Fañch cried when he got it back, and he said it was the salt. In Carène, everybody says that.
textes.Fañch connaissait ma mère. Il m'a appris: Fañch knew my mother. He taught me to read the currents before I could read at all. He drops everything in the water, I fish it out. That's our arrangement.
textes.Fañch m'apprend à barrer, à l'aube, en s: Fañch is teaching me to steer, at dawn, in secret. He makes terrible jokes and smells of mackerel. He's the only one who's never asked me why I want to leave.
textes.Fañch parle à ses poissons. Je sais pour: Fañch talks to his fish. I know why he talks to them: it's my fault, and I'll never apologise for it. He's stubborn. So am I.
textes.Fañch se moque de mes comptes. Il dit qu: Fañch makes fun of my counting. He says no ships ever pass. That's not true: every evening, one passes. His. Late.
textes.Fañch vit sous une barque retournée et m: Fañch lives under an upturned boat and gets me up on it every autumn to plug his roof. He pays me in mackerel. I say there's no need, I take them anyway. He laughs at everything. It's restful.
textes.Fañch. Ton toit tiendra jusqu'au printem: Fañch. Your roof will hold till spring.
textes.Fañch. Tu es encore rentré après la lant: Fañch. You came in after the lantern again.
textes.Fe vais te dire un fecret, {surnom}. Le: I'll tell you a thecret, {surnom}. The name Belle-Humeur… I'm the one who came up with it. That night, at the Crâne Fendu, he wath grumbling about everything, and I thaid, ath a joke: “Well, here cometh Belle-Humeur, Mithter Thunthine!” The whole room laughed. Not him. You know the retht. Thirty yearth he'th carried that name becauthe of me. Thometimeth I think it wath me who thtole hith thmile.
textes.Fenêtre fermée, c'est noté. La chambre n: Window closed, duly noted. Room nine double-locks. I'm keeping it in mind, for you.
textes.Fenêtre ouverte, je l'ai noté. Si vous p: Window open, I've made a note. If you take a room, I'll put you on the open-sea side. With the seagulls.
textes.Fer forgé par Octave. En main, clic (gâc: Iron forged by Octave. In hand, click (trigger in VR) to dig in sand or earth: shells, coins… and sometimes a treasure.
textes.Ferdinand et moi, on est les deux plus v: Ferdinand and I are the two oldest machines in the Strata. He goes round in circles. I go up and down. We never go to the same place. So we meet at La Marmite, in the middle.
textes.Ferdinand vient à treize heures, toujour: Ferdinand comes at one o'clock, always to the same table. He tells the story of the time Bernadette went round the cavern without him. Everyone knows the story. Everyone laughs. He tells it a little differently every time. Bernadette goes faster and faster.
textes.Ferdinand, du Petit Train, dit que sa Be: Ferdinand, from the Little Train, says his Bernadette whistles louder than my cabin. I don't know. I can't hear either of them. But I feel Bernadette in my feet when she goes by. She's got a good heart. Deep down.
textes.Ferdinand, le conducteur du Petit Train: Ferdinand, the driver of the Little Strata Train, signals to me with his whistle every time he passes over my repaired rails. Two toots: “All good.” Three toots: “All very good.” One toot: “Bielle, you've left your wrench on the track again.”
textes.Ferme la porte, {surnom}. Je ne suis pas: Close the door, {surnom}. I didn't come back to Tazira to retire. I came back for Sel's chest. I know where it is. I promised Sel I'd only show it to someone of his blood, someone who'd deserve it. And I know who it was meant for. Not Croc. Fatima. What's inside? Ha! Not even rum will get that out of me.
textes.Ferme les yeux, {surnom}. Qu'est-ce que: Close your eyes, {surnom}. What do you hear?
textes.Ferme ta veste, mon chéri. Il va y avoir: Button up your jacket, dear. There's going to be a draught.
textes.Ferme, Aëlwen. Ce soir, mon cœur va bien: Close up, Aëlwen. Tonight my heart is fine. She looked at me.
Locked. A sign: “FOR SALE. Wisteria Cottage, unbeatable view, wisteria included, frogs optional. Inquire with Monsieur Prosper, Upper Town.”
textes.Fermé à clé. Une petite clé l'ouvrirait…: Locked. A small key would open it… You can find them in other chests, and sometimes in crates and jars.
textes.Fermée. Très sage. Les embruns sont traî: Closed. Very wise. Sea spray is treacherous, and mosquitoes have no manners. I would recommend room nine: its window double-locks.
textes.Fernand ! A splendid fellow. Un vieux lo: Fernand! A splendid fellow. An old sea dog who knows every monster in the ocean, and who let me have a dragon tooth for next to nothing. His eye twinkles when he sees me. Emotion, no doubt.
textes.Fernand ! Mon premier patron, mon sauveu: Fernand! My first boss, my saviour, the best fisherman in the archipelago. He tells the story of my shipwreck badly, but I forgive him: he was there.
textes.Fernand ! Ta daurade, elle a l'œil trist: Fernand! Your sea bream has a sad eye. I'll take it off you cheaper.
textes.Fernand ? Un menteur de première classe: Fernand? A first-class liar about the size of fish. And the man who held the other end of the net, the morning of Marius. He has the best spot on the quay. I won't take it back from him.
textes.Fernand pêchait avec mon frère, autrefoi: Fernand used to fish with my brother. We don't speak any more. Something about a net.
textes.Fernand racontait à tout le quai son mér: Fernand was telling the whole quay about his forty-kilo grouper. I had it carried onto the harbour office scales, in front of him and in front of witnesses. Twenty-five. He said the fish had lost weight from emotion. Since then, when he starts the story, I just say “Twenty-five”. He corrects himself. Every other time.
textes.Fernand, c'est mon vieux pêcheur, mon fo: Fernand is my old fisherman, my supplier and my worst critic. His sea bream are the finest in the archipelago. His compliments, he keeps to himself.
textes.Fernand. Il pêchait avec mon frère. Il a: Fernand. He fished with my brother. He kept what wasn't his to keep. We don't speak any more. That's all.
textes.Ferraille ! Je soulève quoi, aujourd'hui: Ferraille! What am I lifting today?
textes.Ferraille ! Tu as des chaînes pour moi ?: Ferraille! Got any chains for me?
textes.Ferraille a fait la queue de son dragon: Ferraille made his dragon's tail out of organ pipes. I offered to blow into it. The dragon went “oooooh”. Ferraille said: “It sings!” We spent an hour making the dragon sing.
textes.Ferraille comprend le métal comme moi je: Ferraille understands metal the way I understand Germaine. He talks more than me. Everybody talks more than me.
textes.Ferraille fait des dragons avec des épav: Ferraille makes dragons out of wrecks. I lift the wrecks so he can find his parts. I put them back down gently. Even wrecks deserve gentleness.
textes.Ferraille fait pousser des fleurs en mét: Ferraille grows metal flowers next to my mushrooms. He asked the spores for permission before planting any. He's a polite man. A rare thing.
textes.Ferraille m'a fabriqué une sonnette de v: Ferraille made me a rat-shaped bike bell, out of an old jingle bell and a bit of pipe. When you ring it, the rat opens its mouth. All of Boucan wanted one. He made forty. The quays ring like a party now.
textes.Ferraille me donne des pièces, je lui do: Ferraille gives me parts, I give him wheels. His dragon has eleven. It doesn't roll, but it could. That's all that matters to an artist.
textes.Ferraille, à la Casse, au sud-est, me do: Ferraille, at the Scrapyard in the south-east, gives me parts. I give him wheels for his scrap-metal dragon. His dragon now has eleven wheels. It doesn't roll. But it could.
textes.Ferraille, à la Casse, m'a soudé des clo: Ferraille, at the Scrapyard, welded studs onto Germaine's headstock for me. For style. She's happy. So am I.
textes.Ferraille, à la Casse, récupère ce qui e: Ferraille, at the Scrapyard, salvages what's broken. Me, what still works. Rustine, what rolls. Between the three of us, nothing ends up in the bin. Not even the bin: Copeau turned it into an armchair.
textes.Ferraille. Ta cheminée de roulotte fume: Ferraille. My caravan chimney draws nicely.
textes.Ferronde a forgé mon armure et le bonheu: Ferronde forged my armour and the happiness of my home. She laughs loud, she hammers hard, and she has the warmest heart in the city. Warmer than her forge. I measured it. Well, I just know it.
textes.Ferronde est la seule personne de la cit: Ferronde is the only person in the city who's ever beaten me at arm wrestling. She laughs so loud the nails shake. She forged me horn guards, and I wrote her a poem. She nailed it to the wall.
textes.Ferronde et moi, on se dispute les prix: Ferronde and I argue about prices every week. She says her blade is worth sixty, I say it's worth forty. We always end up at fifty, and we're both convinced we lost.
textes.Ferronde forge les meilleures lames de l: Ferronde forges the best blades on the island and asks the craziest prices. We argue every Friday. We end up at fifty. She thinks she lost. So do I. Good deal.
textes.Ferronde me vole des braises du Cœur pou: Ferronde steals embers from the Heart for her forge. She says she's borrowing them. She laughs too loud, she hammers too hard, and she saved the Heart one night. I don't know what to think of her. Yes I do: I know.
textes.Ferronde vient me prendre des braises du: Ferronde comes to take embers from the Heart for her forge. I grumble, she laughs. The sacred fire is not a stove, I tell her. She replies that a fire that's no use to anyone gets bored. She's not entirely wrong. Don't tell her.
textes.Ferronde, mon armure grince au genou gau: Ferronde, my armour squeaks at the left knee.
textes.Ferronde, tu sais que je danse comme un: Ferronde, you know I dance like a drawbridge.
textes.Ferronde… les protège-cornes tiennent to: Ferronde… the horn guards are still holding up well.
Hooked! Keep the tension in the green.
textes.Festival du Larsen\nChaque soir à 20 h 3:
Larsen Festival
Every evening at 8:30 PM: “The Sun and the Rain”,
the two villages on the Main Stage!
Fireworks at 11 PM.
textes.Festival du Larsen\nLa Grande Scène se p:
Larsen Festival
The Main Stage is getting ready…
Come back soon: it's going to be loud!
Fire good. Fire warm. Ougha like fire.
textes.Ffffffff… La soufflerie souffle dans son: Ffffffff… The wind tunnel blows through its glass tube. The meteorologists, for their part, whisper, as if they were afraid of waking a storm.
textes.Fffiou ! Je repasse demain, promis !: Whoosh! I'll be back tomorrow, promise!
textes.Fidèle, oui. Et je compte toujours le ce: Faithful, yes. And I'm still counting that centimetre.
textes.Fier ? … (Il essuie ses lunettes.) Elle: Proud? … (He wipes his glasses.) She knows the name of every cloud, the wind speed and the exact time of afternoon snack. One day, she'll work at the Institute of Winds. And I'll still be carrying the umbrella. If she'll have me.
textes.Fil-de-Fer ! Quelles nouvelles du large: Fil-de-Fer! What news from the open sea?
textes.Fil-de-Fer ! Tes lunettes sont sur ta tê: Fil-de-Fer! Your glasses are on your head!
textes.Fil-de-Fer ! Un trois-mâts dans le ciel: Fil-de-Fer! A three-master in the sky?
textes.Fil-de-Fer dit qu'il a vu le récif avant: Fil-de-Fer says he saw the reef before anyone. He also sees three-masters in the clouds. So, well. We make fun of each other. It's our way of being pals.
textes.Fil-de-Fer voit des bateaux super loin,: Fil-de-Fer can spot ships super far away, but never his glasses. They're on his head! Always! He's teaching me to be a lookout. I'm almost a lookout.
textes.Fil-de-Fer voit tout depuis son mât, et: Fil-de-Fer sees everything from his mast, and he comes to tell me all about it at noon, on the bench by the bay. Half his islands are clouds. But the other half are on my maps.
textes.Fil-de-Fer voit tout, de là-haut. Sauf s: Fil-de-Fer sees everything from up there. Except his glasses. And the fireflies in the graveyard, which he thinks are ghosts. I say they're fireflies.
textes.Fil-de-Fer voit un trois-mâts à six lieu: Fil-de-Fer can spot a three-master six leagues away. Sometimes it even is a three-master. But when he shouts “Land ho!”, it's land: on that, he's never been wrong.
textes.Fil-de-Fer était la vigie du Fidèle, le: Fil-de-Fer was the lookout of the Faithful, the galleon I took from the king. In all the commotion, everyone forgot him at the top of the mast. Two days. When he came down, the king's sailors were on their beach and we were out at sea. He asked: “Do you need a lookout?” I said yes. He'd already climbed back up.
textes.Filas dit que la Balafre f'est toufours: Thilas thayth Balafre hath alwayth been called Balafre. Me, I thay before, it wath the Green Ithland. We argued on the bench by the bay a whole afternoon. Then he thaid: “Thébathtien, were you here a hundred yearth ago?” I thaid no. He thaid: “I wath.” And he crothed hith armth. Go argue with that.
textes.File ! Et dis bonjour à tout le monde de: Off you go! And say hello to everyone for me. Everyone. I'll be counting.
textes.File ! Et regarde en l'air avant de trav: Off you go! And look up before you cross: the cars fly here.
textes.File ! Et si tu remontes, dis à Rosalie: Off you go! And if you go back up, tell Rosalie the Square has finally stopped sneezing.
textes.File ! Mais tu reviens ce soir, hein ? J: Off you go! But you'll come back tonight, won't you? I'm making galettes.
Off you go, off you go! The forest is waiting.
textes.File, mon caillou. Et reviens avec un ve: Off you go, my pebble. And come back with an empty belly, I hate waste.
Off you go. And don't knock anybody over tonight.
textes.File. Et surveille ta bourse, ici les po: Off you go. And watch your purse, round here pockets have hands.
textes.Filez, filez, j'ai une idée qui va s'env: Off you go, off you go, I've got an idea that's about to fly away.
textes.Fin de l'alerte : les navets se sont tou: End of the alert: the turnips have all replanted themselves, looking innocent. Father Gaubert sighs: “They'll do it again. They always do.”
textes.Fin de la conversation. Ce fut un plaisi: End of conversation. It was a pleasure, logged and saved, {surnom}.
End of tour. Start of tour.
textes.Fin de service. Ce soir, j'enlève l'armu: Off duty. Tonight, I take off the armour, and Ortie makes me recite her lessons. Well, I'm the one reciting. She corrects.
textes.Fin du concert. Le vent remballe ses not: End of the concert. The wind is packing up its notes.
textes.Fine comme un vers de Philippine… euh. C: Fine as a line by Philippine… er. As a line of verse, I mean.
textes.Fines ! Élégant. Rapide. Tu as un palais: Thin! Elegant. Quick. You've got a city palate.
textes.Finir Brindezingue. Non. Ne jamais le fi: To finish Brindezingue. No. Never finish him. But one day, to see him move. Just once. Turn his head towards the sea. Fusible says it's possible with a motor. I say it's possible with patience.
textes.Finir la carte de la Balafre. La vraie,: To finish the map of Balafre. The real one, the complete one, with every rock, every skeleton, and the exact direction Skull Rock is looking. Then to gaze at it, very old, in the sun, with a cup of tea.
textes.Finir la toile de la Grande Scène, et la: To finish the Great Stage canvas, and watch it billow in the wind on festival night, with a sun on one side and a cloud on the other.
textes.Firmin ! Un soda au gingembre, je décoll: Firmin! A ginger soda, I'm taking off!
textes.Firmin Cogne a perdu l'engrenage d'or de: Firmin Cogne lost the golden gear of his perpetual-motion engine during a demonstration. It rolled all the way down the cliffs, towards the harbour.
Firmin Cogne has lost the golden gear from his perpetual motion engine. He says it rolled all the way down to the port. A gear that rolls to the bottom of a cliff… that's almost an invention.
textes.Firmin a ma vieille chaudière de secours: Firmin has my old spare boiler. He made it into a chocolate machine. They say the whole town up top sets its watches by its whistle. My boiler became a clock. It's had a fine career.
textes.Firmin a pris le téléphérique une seule: Firmin took the cable car exactly once, years ago. A forty-second ride. He came out of the car as green as an unripe apple. I told him it was the house record. It's true, too: I wrote it in the logbook, with the date. He pretends to be ashamed of it. I think he's a little proud.
textes.Firmin a une machine qui siffle comme un: Firmin has a machine that whistles like a steamer in the fog. I like that. His hot chocolate too. Hm. I'll say no more.
textes.Firmin a une moustache trop grande, une: Firmin has a moustache that's too big, a machine that's too loud and a heart even bigger than both. He says cinnamon hot chocolate is his recipe. He's wrong. I'll tell him so again tonight.
textes.Firmin croit que c'est un de mes confett: Firmin thinks it was one of my confetti that knocked his golden gear loose. I swear it wasn't! On the evening of the demonstration, he found a pink confetto in his hat and waved it in front of the whole Crankshaft, like evidence. It was from last year. I know my colours. This year, I'm doing fuchsia.
textes.Firmin dit que sa machine à chocolat sif: Firmin says his chocolate machine whistles like a locomotive. I say it whistles like Firmin when he loses at cards. They look very alike, actually. The moustache, the steam…
textes.Firmin du Piston Joyeux, Gustave du Café: Firmin from the Jolly Piston, Gustave from the Cumulus Café and Honorine from La Marmite argue over who makes the best hot chocolate on the Column. All three came down to taste my deep-sea hot chocolate. They said “not bad” at the same time. Then they argued over who'd said it first.
textes.Firmin est un bon voisin de comptoir. Il: Firmin is a good fellow to share a counter with. He talks about his engine, I talk about my cable cars, and we drink our coffee without judging each other. His vertigo — I understand it better than he thinks.
textes.Firmin est un grognon au cœur tendre, av: Firmin is a grump with a soft heart, and an engine that never stops. Except when it stops. And then, of course, it's my fault.
textes.Firmin fait son chocolat dans la vieille: Firmin makes his chocolate in Ferdinand's old boiler. He says my miner's chocolate is a soup. I say his chocolate is a drink for people in a hurry. We write to each other by Anatole's cabin. Our letters smell of cocoa.
textes.Firmin l'a construite lui-même. Elle a t: Firmin built it himself. It has three dials, two whistles and just one flaw: it's jealous of teapots.
textes.Firmin me sert un chocolat très sucré ch: Firmin serves me a very sweet hot chocolate every lunchtime, after my rides up. He says my colour comes back. Red, then pink, then normal. He thinks it's pretty. Mostly, I think it's tasty.
textes.Firmin porte le nom des Cogne, et il le: Firmin bears the Cogne name, and he wastes it on an impossible engine. Honoré deserved better. So did Firmin, perhaps. We greet each other with a nod. That's enough.
textes.Firmin était apiculteur. Il est venu me: Firmin was a beekeeper. He came to ask me for a remedy against stings. I told him to stop scaring the bees. He came back the next day, and the day after. He made me the straw hives in the garden, one for each year of marriage. There are thirty. When he passed away, I went to tell the bees, as one does. They hummed very softly.
textes.Firmin, c'est mon grand frère, ma mousta: Firmin is my big brother, my moustache role model and my rival forever. His machine whistles, my froth whispers. When the Line reopened, he came up with a cup of his chocolate. I tasted it. I pulled a face. I finished it. He did the same with my cloud milk.
textes.Firmin, c'est mon meilleur fournisseur !: Firmin is my best supplier! Eleven prototypes, eleven stopped marvels. He thinks I'm making fun of him. I love them, his engines. They tried so hard.
textes.Firmin, du Piston Joyeux, en haut, a une: Firmin, of the Jolly Piston, up top, has a chocolate machine that whistles like a locomotive. He says he bought it from an old Strata mechanic. That old mechanic was my apprenticeship master. And I patched up the machine before it went up. The whistle's my doing. On purpose.
textes.Firmin, du Piston Joyeux, à Hautefond, e: Firmin, from the Jolly Piston, in Hautefond, came down to taste my stew on reopening day. He took notes. Lots of them. He handles a spoon well, that lad. And he's got a chocolate machine that whistles. Bricole says it's her fault.
textes.Firmin, il parle du haut de la falaise e: Firmin talks from the top of the cliff and me from the bottom. Eighty metres between us — it calms arguments down. A good man. Stubborn as a gear.
textes.Firmin, le patron du Piston Joyeux, là-h: Firmin, the owner of the Jolly Piston, up top, came down to taste my stew. He took notes. He asked for the recipe. I told him: “A ladle of mushrooms, a ladle of love, and Excalibur.” He wrote “Excalibur” in his notebook. He's still looking for where to buy it.
textes.Firmin, ta machine a encore sifflé l'heu: Firmin, your machine whistled teatime at noon again!
textes.Fière. Ma ville brille la nuit. Mais ce: Proud. My city shines at night. But what I love most is when it laughs.
textes.Flammèche ! Encore un os dans mes bégoni: Flammèche! Another bone in my begonias!
textes.Flammèche ! L'anniversaire de Suie, c'es: Flammèche! Is Suie's birthday on the tenth?
textes.Flammèche ! Tes restes de poisson sont p: Flammèche! Your fish scraps are ready!
textes.Flammèche a douze chiots d'enfer ! Ils c: Flammèche has twelve hellhound puppies! They breathe fire, they eat doors, and they adore me. She said I'll get a puppy once I know all twelve of their birthdays. I know seven.
textes.Flammèche est ma petite sœur. Elle ramèn: Flammèche is my little sister. She's been bringing home everything with four legs and a snout ever since she could walk. She thinks you can tame anything. She's tamed twelve hellhound puppies. And me.
textes.Flammèche m'a apporté un jour un pot de: Flammèche once brought me a pot of ember flowers, to make up for the holes in my flowerbeds. There was a bone buried in it. She hadn't done it on purpose: a puppy had been through. I shouted. She laughed. I ended up laughing too. I kept the pot. With the bone. It's growing very well.
textes.Flammèche m'a demandé de garder deux chi: Flammèche asked me to look after two puppies for a day. They ate three sardines, a rope and my left shoe. In the evening, they were asleep in a fish basket, one on top of the other. I gave them back reluctantly. Grumbald says I should take one. I told him we've already got Grumbald at home.
textes.Flammèche m'a dit que j'aurais un chiot: Flammèche told me I'd get a puppy once I knew all twelve of their names. I learned them in one day: Braise, Tison, Suie, Fumerolle, Pétard, Charbon, Escarbille, Flambard, Mèche, Cendre, Biscotte and Grignotte! Then she said: “And their birthdays.” It's not fair. But I already know seven.
textes.Flammèche vient chercher mes restes de p: Flammèche comes for my fish scraps every morning for her hellhound puppies. There are twelve of them, they eat like forty, and one of them stole a whole grouper from me. I adore them. Don't tell her.
textes.Flammèche élève douze chiots d'enfer, et: Flammèche raises twelve hellhound pups, and she trusts me with them every morning. Nobody had ever trusted me with anything so precious. She says I'm the gentlest of mountains.
Flammèche raises twelve hellhound puppies, and they dig up my flowerbeds to bury bones. I dug up eleven bones this month, and a shoe. I made her move. With my broom. Kindly.
textes.Flammèche, ce sont des chiens. Ils ne pa: Flammèche, they're dogs. They don't talk.
textes.Flammèche, tes chiots ont encore mangé u: Flammèche, your puppies ate a door again.
textes.Flanelle a la plus belle voix de Rainvil: Flanelle has the most beautiful voice in Rainville. I've set up a mic just for her, with a little echo, like in a downpour. She's never tried it. It's waiting for her.
textes.Flanelle chante comme la pluie sur un to: Flanelle sings like rain on a tin roof. Her mother used to sing with Sunflower, long ago. I've never told her.
textes.Flanelle m'a chanté une chanson pour mes: Flanelle sang me a song for my eightieth birthday. A song about a cloud that follows an old lady. I pretended I had dust in my eye.
textes.Flanelle n'a jamais écouté le disque de: Flanelle has never listened to her mother's record. I don't offer it to her. The day she's ready, she'll come. I'll be here.
textes.Flash spécial ! On me signale que {joueu: Breaking news! I'm told {joueur} was spotted moshing like a champion last night. Mouette confirms: “KIAAA”. Translation: it was magnificent.
textes.Flash spécial ! Une dizaine de robots dé: Breaking news! A dozen removal robots are advancing on the squats! I'm asking all residents to come outside… and our hero to go and stop them!
textes.Flash spécial : Cradoc est tombé de son: Breaking news: Cradoc fell off his unicycle into the fountain on Pallet Square. He's fine. So is the fountain. The unicycle is reconsidering its career.
Flatterer. You won't get off that easily.
textes.Flora ! Mes fraises secrètes sont arrivé: Flora! Have my secret strawberries arrived?
textes.Flora ? C'est elle qui m'a donné mes pre: Flora? She's the one who gave me my first strawberry plants! And Plic is the little brother of Ploc, the drone at the High-Altitude Greenhouses. They write to each other. Well, they beep each other.
textes.Flora Verdine fait pousser des fraises g: Flora Verdine grows giant strawberries in the eternal sunshine of the Clouds. She has too much light, I don't have enough. We've been writing to each other for fifteen years. Her seeds grow so fast they touch my lamps. Mine grow so slowly they bore her. We teach each other patience and speed.
textes.Flora dit que je suis lent, et que c'est: Flora says I am slow, and that it is a good quality, like plants. I recorded that sentence in the “Important” folder. She lets me say hello to her four thousand plants. It takes all morning. She says the plants grow better since. I think it is true.
textes.Flora, aux Nuées, m'a envoyé une fraise: Flora, up in the Clouds, sent me a giant strawberry, as big as a fist. It took three days to come down. It arrived a little tired, but still giant. I cut it into twelve. Everyone in the Greenhouse Dome got a piece. We still talk about it.
textes.Foi de chevalier, c'était magnifique ! S: On my honour as a knight, that was magnificent! Especially the part where I didn't fall.
textes.Foi de chevalier, je ne vous quitterai p: On my honour as a knight, I won't leave you! Except at mealtimes. No, not even at mealtimes.
On my word as a sailor.
On my word as a fishmonger.
textes.Fonctionnement optimal. Je ne dors jamai: Optimal operation. I never sleep. I go on standby from three o'clock to five past three. During those five minutes, I dream. I dream that I'm sleeping.
textes.Fondant ! Comme mes glaces. Il fait si c: Melting! Like my ice creams. It's so hot.
textes.Forgefer, la cité des nains: Forgefer, the city of the dwarves
textes.Forgefer, la cité sous la montagne: Forgefer, the city under the mountain
textes.Forgefer. Une halle immense taillée dans: Forgefer. An immense hall carved into the mountain: pillars engraved with runes, channels of lava lighting everything orange, the smell of coal and hot iron… At the far end, on his throne, King Thorgal.
textes.Forger une cloche. Une grande, pour le p: Forge a bell. A big one, for the port. To ring when the boats come home. Not a weapon. A bell.
textes.Forger une lame que Borin regarde sans d: To forge a blade Borin looks at without saying “Hmpf”. Even just a little “Hm”. A “Hm” would already be glory.
textes.Forger une lame si parfaite que Nori n'y: Forge a blade so perfect that Nori can't find a thing to fault. Nothing. Not a rune, not a hair. He'll open his mouth, and shut it again. That day, the rounds are on me. Every round.
textes.Forger une pièce si belle que Borin la p: Forge a piece so beautiful that Borin sets it down on a Forgefer anvil. Without a word. Not even “not bad”. Just sets it down.
textes.Forger une épée si belle que même Borin: Forge a sword so beautiful that even Borin Barbe-de-Fer would look at it without a word. Just once. I'd settle for his silence. That, at least, costs nothing.
textes.Forgé par Brutus, trois dents de crocodi: Forged by Brutus, with three crocodile teeth set in the iron. As long as it's in your bag, your punches hit harder in brawls (+1). Fists only.
textes.Forgé par Hector à l'Enclume Bleue : lam: Forged by Hector at L'Enclume Bleue: a curved blade of blued steel, with a brass shell guard. Damage: 10, and the third hit of a combo strikes half again as hard.
textes.Forgée par Borin Barbe-de-Fer dans l'aci: Forged by Borin Barbe-de-Fer from volcano steel: a short, broad blade, a golden guard, a ruby on the pommel. Damage: 9, and the third hit of a combo strikes half again as hard.
textes.Formation de bataille ! … Nous sommes de: Battle formation! … There are two of us. It's a small formation. But a handsome one!
textes.Formidable ! Aurore m'a laissé signer un: Splendid! Aurore let me sign a document all by myself. Well, by myself… she held the quill. And my hand. But it was my signature!
textes.Formidable ! Et pas de mal de l'air ? Pa: Wonderful! And no airsickness? No nausea over Tazira? Everyone has either a pilot's stomach or a passenger's stomach. I'll tell you which one you have.
textes.Formidable ! J'ai fait une bulle si gran: Fantastic! I blew a bubble so big that Cerise walked right into it. She floated for three seconds. Then it popped. The bubble. Not Cerise. Cerise is perfectly fine.
textes.Formidable ! J'ai vendu trois sacs de ca: Wonderful! I sold three bags of cinnamon, two baskets of apples, and I learned eleven secrets. A very good day. Secrets, I don't sell. I give them away.
textes.Formidable ! La Ligne a rouvert, et la c: Wonderful! The Line has reopened, and the cabin goes down full every trip! Folk from up top, with hats, umbrellas (it never rains down here!) and eyes as big as lanterns. I love their eyes when the door opens onto the cavern.
textes.Formidable ! La Ligne a rouvert, et la t: Wonderful! The Line has reopened, and the terrace is full of Floor folk tasting their first cloud milk. They all make the same face: round eyes and a white moustache. I love that face.
textes.Formidable ! La machine a sifflé quarant: Wonderful! The machine whistled forty times today. Forty hot chocolates! The windows rattled, the cats fled, and Gaspard corrected his watch thirty-nine times.
textes.Formidable ! La taverne est pleine, les: Fantastic! The tavern's full, the songs are out of tune, all is well.
textes.Formidable ! Pas un retard, et un passag: Wonderful! Not a minute late, and a passenger from up top who shouted “Again!” at the end of the ride. I gave him a second one. Free. Bernadette was delighted.
textes.Formidable ! Quelqu'un a déposé un parap: Wonderful! Someone dropped off an umbrella that opens by itself when it hears the word “rain”. I named it Gaston. He's very nervous.
textes.Formidable ! Racontez ! Non, attendez, r: Formidable! Tell me everything! No, wait, take a step back, emotion makes me unstable. There. How many eyebrows? What colour was the smoke? Ah, a colleague!
textes.Formidable ! Tout le Boucan va le savoir: Wonderful! The whole Boucan will know: Sergent announces new arrivals on the radio.
textes.Formidable ! Un jour d'orage, montez sur: Formidable! One stormy day, come up the tower with me. In spirit only: Héloïse would kill me. You'll hold the string, I'll hold the key, and your hair will stand up all by itself.
textes.Formulaire bleu pour une demande, rose p: Blue form for a request, pink for a complaint, green to complain about the pink form.
textes.Fort ! Qu'on l'entende de loin !: Loud! So it carries a long way!
textes.Fort bien ! Je retourne à la Guilde raco: Very well! I'll go back to the Guild and tell of our exploits. I'll barely embellish them.
textes.Fort ou doux, aujourd'hui, ton rire ?: Loud or soft, your laugh today?
textes.Fortissimo ! Comme un parapluie qui se r: Fortissimo! Like an umbrella blowing inside out!
textes.Forêt calme. Brume calme. Tout est calme: Forest calm. Mist calm. Everything's calm, Thalion.
textes.Foudre ! … (Ses cheveux se dressent, de: Lightning! … (Her hair stands on end, smoke rises from her hat.) … it happens.
textes.Foudre ! … Ça a touché ! Le monstre ! Pa: Lightning! … It hit! The monster! Not me! Did you see?
textes.Foudre de l'orage, frappe ! … Elle a fra: Storm lightning, strike! … It struck. Not me. Thank you, lightning.
textes.Fouiller les caisses au bout du quai, cô: Search the crates at the end of the quay, on the lighthouse side
textes.Fraise ! Comme Cerise. Elle en prend tou: Strawberry! Like Cerise. She always has one with two straws: one for her, one for her notebook. She says the notebook's thirsty too.
textes.Fraise ! Peuchère, tu as du goût. Tu con: Strawberry! My oh my, you've got taste. Do you know the strawberry-dolphin? Nina invented it. With a pinch of sea salt. You'll weep.
Strawberry, always. It's in the notebook. With two straws, if you like, like Cerise.
textes.Fraises géantes du soleil éternel, pomme: Giant strawberries from the eternal sun, dome apples, berries, honey from my bees, and seeds to plant at home! Everything picked this morning. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Fraises roses des Lampes, petites mandar: Pink Lamp strawberries, little mandarins from the Orchard, spirulina from the algae wall, and seeds for your garden up top, even under a real sun! All picked this morning, under the lamp. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Frappe le tronc avec le fer de la hache: Strike the trunk with the iron of the axe!
textes.Frapper à la porte des quatre maisons: Knock on the doors of the four houses
textes.Fraîche du jour ? Alors elle est fausse,: Fresh today? Then it's a fake, Mister Isaac.
textes.Froide ? Le lendemain ? Oh… Bon. Chacun: Cold? The next day? Oh… Well. Each to their own. Apparently it's delicious dunked in a Brasier coffee. I've never tried: I've never had a brioche left the next day.
textes.Fromage de chèvre des cendres, le meille: Ash goat cheese, the best in the world. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Frotte, frotte ! La vapeur fait le reste: Scrub, scrub! The steam does the rest.
textes.Frrrr… Le parapluie monte, tout droit, t: Whirrrr… The umbrella rises, straight up, very proud, then hesitates, then comes back down in little hops. Everyone claps, out of politeness.
textes.Fruits frais, épices qui chatouillent, e: Fresh fruit, tickly spices and singing honey! Taste first, pay after. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Frustré. La vitrine des îles est presque: Frustrated. The islands display case is almost empty. I'm missing a shell, a parrot feather, a desert beetle, a patch from those noisy punks and a golden turnip from Montjoie. You travel a lot, don't you?
textes.Frustrée. Il me manque les vraies couleu: Frustrated. I'm missing the true colours of the sea: the red of coral, the yellow of hill honey, the brown of coconut. Mainland paint tubes are so dull.
textes.Frère Cendrin et moi étions dans la même: Brother Cendrin and I were in the same class. He was bottom in flames and top in patience. Me, the opposite. Together, we set fire to the tower. It was an experiment. It succeeded perfectly: the tower burned.
textes.Frère Cendrin garde le Cœur-Brasier comm: Brother Cendrin guards the Ember Heart like a hen sitting on her egg. He grumbles when I take embers, he sighs when I laugh. But the night of the grate, it was my door he knocked on.
textes.Frère Cendrin m'a appris à porter une fl: Brother Cendrin taught me how to carry a flame. Every evening, he lights a wick for me at the Heart-Brazier and watches me leave with tiny steps. He never says anything. But he waits until I'm outside before going back to sit down.
textes.Frère Cendrin veille sur le Cœur-Brasier: Brother Cendrin has watched over the Heart-Brazier for four hundred years. He's the calmest of my subjects. When I'm worried, I go and sit beside him, and I listen to him listening to the fire.
textes.Frère Linguini a encore fait sonner le C: Brother Linguini rang the Lid three times in a row again. The volcano spat sauce all over Mamma Lasagna's washing. She chased him around the Borgo with her rolling pin. Twice.
textes.Frère Linguini a peur du noir. Il dort a: Brother Linguini is scared of the dark. He sleeps with his colander on his head, so the moon shines through the holes. Clever.
textes.Frère Linguini, où est l'assiette éterne: Brother Linguini, where is the eternal plate?
textes.Frérot, sois honnête : tu crois que j'ai: Bro, be honest: do you think I danced with a dolphin?
textes.Fuiii ! Brioche apparaît sur un muret, s: Weee! Brioche appears on a low wall, stretches for a long time, and joins you without hurrying.
textes.Fuiii-iii ! Sardine arrive au grand galo: Weee-eee! Sardine comes at a full gallop, ears flying (well, one of them).
Fulbert Saignée. Doc, to my friends. Surgeon, barber, dentist, and sometimes vet when Joe brings me a parrot with a cold. Are you hurt? No? You will be. Around here, it always comes.
textes.Fulbert m'a taillé cette jambe dans le m: Fulbert carved me this leg from the mast of his own ship. He says he's no sculptor. He's wrong: he's a master, he just doesn't know it. Hm. Don't tell him I said so.
textes.Fundin ! Le soufflet, pas ma barbe !: Fundin! The bellows, not my beard!
textes.Fundin a des bras de nain, un cœur de na: Fundin has a dwarf's arms, a dwarf's heart and a head full of air. He botches everything, but he botches it with gusto. Hmph. I was the same. Don't tell him.
textes.Fundin a deux mains gauches et un cœur t: Fundin has two left hands and a heart too big for his chest. His eyes follow me when I walk by. He thinks I don't see him. I see everything: it's my job.
textes.Fundin est un bon gamin avec deux mains: Fundin is a good lad with two left hands. Borin shouts, he apologises, he tries again. I feed him on the sly, or he'd forget to eat.
textes.Fundin, tes bottes ! Recule de l'enclume: Fundin, your boots! Step back from the anvil.
textes.Fundin. Tu as encore de la suie sur le n: Fundin. You've got soot on your nose again.
textes.Furieuse. Les robots de Lisse ont mesuré: Furious. Lisse's robots measured the Spore Wood with lasers. To “optimise the surface area”. You don't optimise a wood. You go for a walk in it.
textes.Furieux. Le cochonnet a disparu ! Et Mar: Furious. The jack has vanished! And Marcel says it's my fault. I say he threw it too hard.
textes.Fusain ! Mes flammes ont encore poussé !: Fusain! My flames have grown again!
textes.Fusain vient peindre aux Jardins. Ses co: Fusain comes to paint in the Gardens. Her colours are lovely, but not as lovely as my mushrooms'. So we made a swap: I give a little light, and the Fronde's murals glow at night. I won't say how. It's a gardener's secret.
textes.Fusain, de la Fronde, vient peindre aux: Fusain, from the Fronde, comes to paint in the Gardens. Apparently my mushrooms have colours you can't find in any paint pot. Since then, the Fronde's murals have spots that glow at night. I won't say where the secret comes from.
Fusain, your blue is too blue.
textes.Fusain. Qu'est-ce que tu vas mettre dans: Fusain. What are you going to put in the empty space?
textes.Fusible a branché une guirlande sur ma s: Fusible wired a string of fairy lights to my saw. Now, when I saw, it blinks. It's pretty. It's also a bit worrying.
textes.Fusible a câblé toute ma radio. Sans lui: Fusible wired up my whole radio. Without him, I'd be talking to an empty box. He gets dizzy on the second rung, but with wires, he's a genius.
textes.Fusible a mis des guirlandes sur Mademoi: Fusible put fairy lights on Mademoiselle. She's never looked so beautiful. And he hooked the fountain up to the crane. It's pointless. It's magnificent.
textes.Fusible a mis des guirlandes sur tout le: Fusible put fairy lights all along Mademoiselle's arm. The first night, when I turned her, the whole town watched the light pass over the harbour. Mademoiselle creaked. Fusible said she was creaking in a major key. I don't know what that means. But it was joyful.
textes.Fusible branche tout sur tout. Même sur: Fusible wires everything to everything. Even to my saw. We built the stage in the Hall together. Him the lights, me the wood. It holds. And it blinks.
textes.Fusible fait la lumière, moi le son. Qua: Fusible does the lights, I do the sound. When I say “LOUDER”, he adds more light. We don't understand each other, and the concert is magnificent. I've stopped trying to understand.
textes.Fwooosh ! Le vent s'engouffre par la bai: Fwooosh! The wind rushes in through the big window: the harp sings, the chimes sway and tinkle, and the old musician raises his baton.
textes.Fâchée ! Le volcan a craché sur mon ling: Cross! The volcano spat on my washing. Again! My sheets are all red. Well, they smell lovely. But still!
textes.Fâchée ! Quelqu'un me vole des croissant: Cross! Someone steals my croissants every night. The constable can't find a thing.
textes.Fâchée. Quark a encore triché à cache-ca: Cross. Quark cheated at hide-and-seek again. He hid inside a hologram in the fountain! You're not allowed to hide inside a planet! It's in the rules! Well, it's in my rules.
textes.Fébrile. Toutes les légendes situent la: Feverish. Every legend places the sunken city south-west of the village. But I can't swim.
textes.Félix ! Votre carte est sèche, je vous l: Félix! Your map is dry, here it is.
textes.Félix connaît l'archipel par cœur sans l: Félix knows the archipelago by heart without ever having seen it. He describes islands to me, and I want to paint them. He's a poet who makes maps.
textes.Félix m'a dessiné la route du tour de l': Félix drew me the route round the archipelago, island by island, with the currents, the winds, and a little star wherever there's a good place to eat. I pinned it on the wall of the rental shop. Customers look at it. I say it's my next trip. They ask me when. I answer: “Soon.”
textes.Félix note toutes mes prédictions dans u: Félix writes down all my predictions in a little black notebook, with the date, to catch me out. He's found three that came true. Three! He came to tell me, furious, as if I'd done it on purpose. I asked him which ones. He refused to tell me. I think one of the three is about him.
textes.Félix, c'est mon navigateur. Il connaît: Félix is my navigator. He knows every island, every coast, every current. He's never seen them, but that's a detail. He draws the way people dream.
textes.Félix, le cartographe. Un homme qui conn: Félix, the map-maker. A man who knows every island and has never seen a single one. He says I'm his eyes at sea. I say he has good eyes on land.
textes.Félix, le libraire. Il dit que je ne voi: Félix, the bookseller. He says I don't see the future, I just know the gossip. He may be right. But he comes to check every week. You don't keep an eye on something you don't believe in.
textes.Félix, mon libraire. Le seul homme de ce: Félix, my bookseller. The only man on this island who understands my charts as well as I do. “The two greatest explorers who never left,” he says. It's true. It's sad. It's very true.
textes.GERMAINE ! L'AMPLI ! (Elle court cherche: GERMAINE! THE AMP! (She runs to fetch Clou. Clou arrives, takes Germaine, hugs her to his chest and says nothing for a whole minute. Then he nods at you. Just once. Rouille cries.) He nodded at you! Do you know how many people have gotten a nod from Clou? Four! And the drumsticks... you keep them. We don't have a real drummer yet. They're waiting for someone. Maybe you'll find out who.
textes.GERMAINE ! PROCHAINE ALERTE, ON FAIT ÉQU: GERMAINE! NEXT ALERT, SHALL WE TEAM UP?
textes.GLOOP — la planète de Glorb. Verte, moll: GLOOP — Glorb's planet. Green, squishy, wobbly. Its inhabitants bounce when they're very happy. Not to be confused with a jelly.
textes.GORGOTH ! … Pardon. gorgoth. C'est mieux: GORGOTH! … Sorry. gorgoth. Is that better?
textes.GORGOTH LE CORNU ! Le plus grand champio: GORGOTH THE HORNED! The greatest champion of the Arena, and the softest heart in the city. I found him at the port and made him a champion. He thanks me every day. I'm the one who owes him everything.
textes.GORGOTH LE CORNU, le champion de l'arène: GORGOTH THE HORNED, champion of the arena! He charges with lowered horns: step aside at the last moment, strike him in the back. The crowd roars!
textes.GROSSE-DENT ! Le roi du Cirque des Os. S: GROSSE-DENT! The king of the Bone Hollow. His skin is thick… When he ROARS, he's going to charge: dodge at the last moment and let him smash into the rock of the hollow. Stunned, he takes double damage! Don't stay behind him: his tail sweeps everything.
textes.Gagner enfin le concours de la plus gros: Finally win the biggest pumpkin contest against Mother Morille. With official scales, checked by the assembly. And no caravan in the weigh-in.
textes.Gagner la Grande Course : prendre le dép: Win the Great Race: start under the arch of the Games Clearing (E), pass under the ten arches in order and come back first
textes.Gagner le troisième morceau contre Sylva: Win the third piece from Sylvain (three wins in a row at the big table of the Shark's Tooth), then take the three pieces to Philémon Lunette, the mapmaker (in front of his tower)
textes.Gagner les quatre manches du Tournoi des: Win the four rounds of the Tournament of Horns (strike the gong, at the edge of the arena sand)
textes.Galactique ! J'ai vendu trois fleurs de: Galactic! I sold three nebula flowers this morning, and Orbe bought an old boot from me for his Museum. A boot! He cried with joy. So did I, but for other reasons.
textes.Galet a fait des nœuds bizarres sur tout: Galet tied strange knots on every rope of the stage. I asked him what they were. He said: “Hm. Knots.” I think they mean something.
textes.Galet m'a fait cinq cents mètres de cord: Galet made me five hundred metres of rope. He only asked one thing in return: a concert. I fully intend to pay up.
textes.Galet m'a fait une corde spéciale pour m: Galet made me a special cord for my loom, very fine, with a sailor's knot at each end. He said: “For you.” Then he left. That's the longest speech he's ever made me.
textes.Galet parle peu et file beaucoup. Ses co: Galet says little and spins a lot. His ropes never break. Neither do his silences.
textes.Galettes d'algues (deux cœurs !). Et je: Seaweed cakes (two hearts!). And I buy fish, shells, pearls, shark teeth. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Gamelle et moi, on est les deux plus vie: Gamelle and I are the two oldest in the Fronde. I keep the fire; she keeps the pot. No fire, no soup; no soup, no Assembly. We argue about everything, except what matters.
textes.Gamelle tient la Cantine Libre, à la Fro: Gamelle runs the Free Canteen, in the Fronde. Her soups are pay what you can, mine are gently priced. Gamelle puts in too much chilli, I put in too much salt. We argue about everything that's eaten. Never about those who eat.
textes.Gamelle, de la Cantine Libre, à la Frond: Gamelle, from the Free Canteen in the Fronde, and I swap recipes. Her soups are pay what you can, mine are pay very little. We argue about salt. Never about anything else. Someone who feeds people is family, even on the other side of the Chasm.
textes.Gamelle, je t'ai apporté des pleurotes g: Gamelle, I've brought you some giant oyster mushrooms.
Gamelle, your stew is too salty.
Keep the love. Take back the herring.
textes.Garde la sardine. Elle ne fait pas une q: Keep the sardine. It won't make a keel.
textes.Garde la tête dans les nuages, mon petit: Keep your head in the clouds, dear. Up here, it's a compliment. Down below, apparently, it's a criticism. Funny people.
Keep your head in the clouds.
textes.Garde le Bail, mon grand. Non, ne discut: Keep the Lease, kiddo. No, don't argue: the assembly voted. It'll be better with you than in a drawer: that way, it'll travel. The Boucan is ours, forever, and thanks to you. Here, the whole common fund. And a title. We don't like titles here. But this one, we voted for laughing: Hero of Port-Boucan. Tonight, concert. You go to the front of the line.
textes.Garde ta voix. Le djinn arrive au troisi: Save your voice. The djinn arrives at the third tea.
textes.Garde ça, {surnom}. Tu en auras plus bes: Keep it, {surnom}. You'll need it more than I do. Me, I fight with metaphors.
textes.Garde-la ! Mon escargot couine très bien: Keep it! My snail squeaks just fine.
Keep it well, then. It's beautiful.
Keep it a while longer, captain.
textes.Garde-le, voyons : on dirait que tu en a: Keep it, come now: looks like you need it.
textes.Garde-le. Les souvenirs qu'on garde depu: Keep it. Memories kept from the very beginning are the strongest. The stones have a first memory too. They tell no one.
Keep it. It smells of… dry land.
textes.Garde-les dedans, alors. Loin de ma tabl: Keep them in there, then. Away from my table.
textes.Garder la Grande Porte un jour. Une seul: To guard the Great Gate for one day. Just one day, while Bramm has a fizz at Ulfa's. Just to see his face when he gets back.
textes.Garder le silence ! Vous connaissez la p: Remain silent! You know the procedure, I see. That's very suspicious. Or very polite. I'll keep watch on you during my rounds. Discreetly.
textes.Gardez vos explosions loin de Léonce, pr: Keep your explosions away from Léonce, Professor.
textes.Gardez-la jusqu'à lundi. J'ai peut-être: Keep it till Monday. I may have its sister.
textes.Gardez-la vide. Ça vous fera une boîte à: Keep it empty. It'll make you a box of nothing.
Let us keep our heads in the clouds.
textes.Gardée. Mais pas entourée de bois, rassu: Saved. But not wrapped in wood, don't worry.
textes.Gaspard ! Kick et Basse te disent bonjou: Gaspard! Kick and Bass say hello!
textes.Gaspard ! Tu as commencé par le plancher: Gaspard! Did you start with the floor this time?
textes.Gaspard ? Mon meilleur élève. Mon seul é: Gaspard? My best pupil. My only pupil, all right, but the best. He nods when I talk: either he's listening, or it's the music.
textes.Gaspard Fusain, le guetteur du Belvédère: Gaspard Fusain, the lookout of the Belvedere, saw a little glint shining at the top of Mount Charcoal through his telescope. He thinks it's the pot of purple (no. 6). He'd like you to look for yourself, then go and fetch it.
textes.Gaspard boit de l'eau toutes les cinq mi: Gaspard drinks water every five minutes. He's right to, but he tells everyone about it.
Gaspard says a hut is meant to be shut. I leave the door open for the breeze, and I've got three crabs living in my hammock: Kick, Bass and Mistral. Gaspard sighs very loudly when he sees them. But the other day I caught him giving a bit of banana to Bass. He said he was just passing by.
textes.Gaspard est monté à mon échelle demander: Gaspard climbed my ladder to ask for nails. He saw my joints, mortise and tenon, not a single nail, as it happens. He stood there with his mouth open for an hour. He even stopped nodding. Now that's a compliment.
textes.Gaspard est un bon garçon qui boit de l': Gaspard is a good lad who drinks water and tells everyone about it. He's right: I carried him to the spring the day he wasn't drinking any. He owes me a song.
textes.Gaspard et moi, on a été à l'école ensem: Gaspard and I went to school together. He blackened his drawings, I cried over mine. Today he keeps watch and I preside. We make quite a pair.
textes.Gaspard l'horloger m'a offert une montre: Gaspard the clockmaker gave me a watch that rings before every departure. It rings all the time. Once it rang while I was asleep, and I ran all the way to the Column in my pyjamas. It was three in the morning. Mistress Capucine was there anyway. She didn't say a thing. She lent me her jacket.
Gaspard the clockmaker gave me a watch so I'd never be late again. It rings five minutes before each trip up. And one minute before. And right on time. I'm still always late, but now I know it.
textes.Gaspard l'horloger ne me pardonne pas d': Gaspard the clockmaker has never forgiven me for changing a mill sail on a Tuesday. Apparently he set his watch by it. I wrote him an apology poem. He timed it. He said it was “four seconds too long”.
textes.Gaspard m'a construit l'estrade, là, sou: Gaspard built me the stage, right here under my feet. He nods his head, he drinks water, he tells you to drink water. The calmest guy on the beach, and the most stubborn.
textes.Gaspard m'a construit une cabane au-dess: Gaspard built me a hut above my banana grove, eighty-three planks. I paid him in bunches, one per plank. He said thank you for every bunch. Afterwards, for three months, he made a funny face every time he saw a banana. I think he really loved them.
textes.Gaspard m'a laissé monter au mât de la M: Gaspard let me climb the Murène's mast. Up to the first rung. No higher. He had his hand on my back, like this. From up there, I could see everything! Well, the deck. And the first mate's head. The first mate looked at me. I came down really fast. But I'd climbed. A real pirate mast.
textes.Gaspard m'a prêté sa cabane d'essai pour: Gaspard lent me his test hut for two nights, and it's been three weeks. He knocks before going into his own place. He's the nicest boy on the island, and the most obsessed with water.
textes.Gaspard ne dit pas un mot, et son perroq: Gaspard doesn't say a word, and his parrot talks for two. A polite, clean customer who pays in advance and adores dates. The parrot, much less polite.
textes.Gaspard ne dit rien, mais son perroquet: Gaspard says nothing, but his parrot has the best ear in Tazira. I want to sign it up for the band. Gaspard shrugs. The Admiral says yes. That makes one vote for, one abstention.
Gaspard says nothing, but his parrot says everything. Everything that's said on the quay. Especially what shouldn't be. I lower my voice when he goes by.
textes.Gaspard ne me pardonne pas l'aile du mar: Gaspard hasn't forgiven me for the Tuesday sail. He greets me three seconds early to show me he can. I wrote him an apology poem. He timed it. “Four seconds too long.”
textes.Gaspard regarde l'île toute la journée a: Gaspard watches the island all day long through his spyglass. If there's a pot somewhere, he knows. He only tells those who climb up to the Lookout.
textes.Gaspard règle l'horloge des départs. Cha: Gaspard sets the departures clock. Every Monday, at seven o'clock sharp, we check it together. We say nothing. We nod. It's the most pleasant conversation of my week.
textes.Gaspard était cuisinier sur un baleinier: Gaspard was a cook on a whaler. He walked into the bar, tasted the grog, and asked for the recipe. I told him: “It's not for sale.” He said: “And if I marry you?” He got the recipe. And me with it. We sailed south and opened the Crâne Fendu, here. He loved the grog so much they called him Grog.
textes.Gaspard, c'est mon ami. Il ne parle pas,: Gaspard is my friend. He doesn't talk, he sees. And he sees whales, like me. We're the club of people nobody believes: two members and a parrot.
textes.Gaspard, c'est mon frère. Pas de sang :: Gaspard is my brother. Not by blood: by rope. He doesn't talk, so I talk for both of us. And the Admiral talks for all three.
textes.Gaspard, c'est mon voisin de jungle et m: Gaspard is my jungle neighbour and my brother at heart. He built my hut, he stood my banana trees back up, and he tells me to drink water. Good, good. I drink coconut.
textes.Gaspard, il parle jamais. C'est son perr: Gaspard never talks. It's his parrot that talks, the Admiral! He knows loads of words, even rude ones. Gaspard is nice. He sees everything, from up there.
textes.Gaspard, je t'ai raconté la fois où…: Gaspard, did I tell you about the time…
textes.Gaspard, l'estrade a grincé deux fois de: Gaspard, the stage creaked twice in a row.
textes.Gaspard, l'horloger d'en bas, m'a écrit: Gaspard, the clockmaker from down below, wrote to ask if our glass clocks were properly set. We don't have any glass clocks. I made one, in a hurry, for when he comes back up. It runs six minutes fast. He's going to love setting it.
textes.Gaspard, l'horloger de Hautefond, est de: Gaspard, the clockmaker from Hautefond, came down to adjust the Great Pearl. He says it turns violet four seconds early. I told him that was on purpose: so evening comes a little sooner for the children. He looked at me for a long time. Then he said: “Acceptable.”
textes.Gaspard, l'horloger de Hautefond, est mo: Gaspard, the clockmaker from Hautefond, came up for the reopening. He looked at my inventions for an hour without a word. Then he said: “It's… original.” For him, that's the highest compliment. He only says it once a year.
textes.Gaspard, l'horloger de Hautefond, ne sup: Gaspard, Hautefond's clockmaker, can't stand a gear that's “out of tolerance”. I live surrounded by out-of-tolerance gears. We shouldn't get along. We write to each other every month. He corrects my plans in red pencil. I correct his in green.
