textes.Gaspard, mon voisin de pêche. Il ne parl: Gaspard, my fishing neighbour. He doesn't talk, I talk little, and his parrot makes conversation for three. The best company in Tazira.
textes.Gaspard, t'as des rouages pour moi ?: Gaspard, got any gears for me?
textes.Gaspard, vous ne rêviez pas : voici le v: Gaspard, you weren't dreaming: here's the purple!
textes.Gaspard. On hoche ensemble. Il ne parle: Gaspard. We nod together. He doesn't talk much, neither do I. We understand each other. … And he brings me water. I only drink his.
textes.Gaston : « Barnabé est un génie ! Un gén: Gaston: “Barnabé is a genius! A genius!”
textes.Gaston : « RRRAAAH ! » Il ne te parlera: Gaston: “RRRAAAH!” He won't speak to you for a week. Neither will I, maybe.
textes.Gaston : « Rrrah ! Il a bon goût ! » Il: Gaston: “Rrrah! Good taste!” He adores you now. That's rare.
textes.Gaston ?! … Bon. Il dit « épaisses ». Il: Gaston?! … Fine. He says “thick”. He always says “thick”. And he's right, too.
Gaston has learned his kick drum. “Boom. Boom. Boom.” At five in the morning, right above my pillow. Mistral says it's a remix. I say it's a curse. But I tap my foot all the same.
textes.Gaston dit que c'était une luciole. Gast: Gaston says it was a firefly. Gaston is jealous.
textes.Gaston dit que je suis le meilleur serve: Gaston says I'm the best waiter on the island. I'm the only waiter robot on the island.
textes.Gaston fait le meilleur café de l'île, e: Gaston makes the best coffee on the island, and he's the only man who keeps iron filings behind his counter just for me. That's friendship.
textes.Gaston fait le meilleur café de la cité,: Gaston makes the best coffee in the city, and his noon whistle is on time. Thanks to me. He knows it: he pays me in coffee. A precise man.
textes.Gaston m'a fait un smiley qui tire la la: Gaston made me a smiley sticking out its tongue!
textes.Gaston m'a trouvé, pas l'inverse. Il est: Gaston found me, not the other way round. He came down from a tree and said “Shipwreck”. He was the first to speak to me here.
textes.Gaston ne porte pas de bijoux. … Il est: Gaston doesn't wear jewellery. … What colour is it?
textes.Gaston nourrit mon frère, et il me nourr: Gaston feeds my brother, and he feeds me too. Without him, there'd be two of us floating: Achille because of the wings, and me because I forget to eat.
textes.Gaston remplit ma bouteille de nuit et n: Gaston fills my night bottle and never asks me about the island. He talks to me about trains. The sky and the railways, deep down, are the same thing: a matter of timetables.
textes.Gaston veut savoir : tu le trouves beau: Gaston wants to know: do you think he's handsome?
textes.Gaston, cache les coquillages, il revien: Gaston, hide the seashells, here comes trouble again!
textes.Gaston, je l'ai acheté d'occasion il y a: Gaston, I bought him second-hand five years ago. He was programmed to paint cars. Today he makes noodles. Sometimes he still tries to paint the bowls. We sell those for more.
textes.Gaston, je l'ai trouvé chez un ferraille: Gaston, I found him at a scrap dealer's. A painting robot arm, for cars. He still had blue on his gripper. I cleaned him, reprogrammed him, taught him the ladle. The first week, he painted three bowls blue. We sold them for double.
textes.Gaston, note : Octave m'a parlé. Huit mo: Gaston, write this down: Octave spoke to me. Eight words more than last year.
textes.Gaston, on m'offre {dernier_cadeau}. Oui: Gaston, someone's giving me {dernier_cadeau}. Yes. Don't laugh.
textes.Gaston, tu as vu ? Il m'a frappé ! Note-: Gaston, did you see that? I've been hit! Write it down!
textes.Gaston, tu entends ? Une elfe qui se sou: Gaston, did you hear that? An elf who remembers me!
textes.Gaubert ! Tu m'as gardé des navets ?: Gaubert! Have you saved me some turnips?
textes.Gaubert parle à ses navets, il ne mange: Gaubert talks to his turnips, he doesn't eat the golden turnips, and he cries when they run away. He's the best of men. He also knows something about the sacks of seeds. He smiles too much.
Nice… They're polite, and they pay. That's not the same thing. Keep your heart open, but your purse shut. And don't go aboard their galleon without telling me.
textes.Germaine ! Tu viens critiquer mes pommes: Germaine! Come to criticise my apples?
textes.Germaine ! Viens écouter une histoire !: Germaine! Come and listen to a story!
textes.Germaine attrape plus de navets que tous: Germaine catches more turnips than all the Guild's adventurers put together. With a thirty-year-old net! I announce her scores on the square. She pretends not to listen. She listens.
textes.Germaine cherche depuis dix ans qui a po: For ten years, Germaine has been trying to find out who carried the seed sacks to the farm. I know who it was. Babette told me, one evening, without meaning to, while talking about the black ice that winter. I'll never tell my daughter. Some stories you don't tell, because they're more beautiful when you live them. That one will end well. I'm waiting.
textes.Germaine dit que j'ai peint mon navet. I: Germaine says I painted my turnip. It was enhanced. She criticises my apples every day. She shouts loud. She's the only one who answers me as loudly as I talk. I'll never tell her that.
textes.Germaine dit que mes pommes ont un goût: Germaine says my apples taste of wind. Wind is healthy! Her apples taste of turnip. Everything tastes of turnip at their place.
textes.Germaine et moi, ça a commencé il y a di: Germaine and I, it started ten years ago, at the finest-turnip contest of the Dawn festival. I won. She says my turnip was painted. It was just very well washed. With a touch of colour. For the shine.
textes.Germaine n'a jamais écouté une seule de: Germaine never listened to a single one of my stories to the end. She'd run off to catch butterflies. Today, she catches turnips. She's become the heroine of all my stories.
textes.Germaine, Père Gaubert m'envoie, pour le: Germaine, Père Gaubert sent me, about the little pig.
textes.Germaine, c'est le filet de la ferme et: Germaine is the farm's net and the light of my life. She catches everything that moves. She caught me, thirty-five years ago, with a turnip. And once, in the net, by mistake.
textes.Gertrude va très bien. Elle te dit bonjo: Gertrude is very well. She says hello.
textes.Gilles ! Albertine a quelque chose pour: Gilles! Albertine has something for you.
textes.Gilles dort debout. J'ai écrit l'article: Gilles sleeps standing up. I wrote article twelve for him. He read it in his sleep. He is the kindest, calmest and sleepiest guard in the whole history of the Montjoie guard.
Gilles sleeps standing up. I sleep sitting down. We had a contest. Nobody won, because we both fell asleep before the end. He's a very gentle boy. And very well rested.
textes.Gilles est le garçon le plus gentil de M: Gilles is the sweetest lad in Montjoie. He sleeps standing up, says thank you to everyone, and eats my bread as if it were treasure. I send him a loaf every morning.
textes.Gilles est le seul garde que mes mouette: Gilles is the only guard my seagulls love. He sleeps standing up, he gives them his crusts, and he says hello to them by name. Albertine pecks him every morning. It's her way of saying she loves him.
textes.Gilles m'a demandé une potion pour reste: Gilles asked me for a potion to stay awake. He slept for two days. I must have swapped two labels. He says it was the best night of his life. Hypothesis: he's happy.
Gilles asked me for a potion to stay awake. He slept for two days. I think I swapped two labels. He says it was the best night of his life.
textes.Gilles, le garde de la Porte Nord, dort: Gilles, the guard at the North Gate, sleeps standing up. He claims I sleep sitting down. We held a contest. Nobody won: we both fell asleep before the end.
textes.Gilles, mon enfant ! Tu viens pour la si: Gilles, my child! Here for a nap?
textes.Gilles, à la Porte Nord, dort debout. Me: Gilles, at the North Gate, sleeps standing up. My seagulls peck his helmet to wake him. He says thank you. They adore him. He gives them his bread crusts.
textes.Gilwen ! Ton miel de ce mois-ci, il est: Gilwen! This month's honey is a bit pale, isn't it?
textes.Gilwen ! Ton miel de tilleul arrive à po: Gilwen! Your lime-blossom honey's arrived just in time.
textes.Gilwen dit que je vole les fleurs de ses: Gilwen says I steal her bees' flowers. Flowers belong to no one. Her bees, on the other hand, follow me everywhere to take back their loot.
textes.Gilwen dit que je vole ses abeilles. Les: Gilwen says I steal her bees. The bees up top belong to nobody. She says I don't greet them with a song. I don't sing. Everyone knows why.
textes.Gilwen m'a appris que les abeilles n'aim: Gilwen taught me that bees don't like people in a hurry. One morning I ran over to her hives to ask for honey urgently, and three bees stung me on the nose. Gilwen said: “They could tell you hadn't said hello.” Ever since, I say hello to them. Even from a distance.
textes.Gilwen m'a dit : « Si tu leur chantais q: Gilwen told me: “If you sang them something before taking the honey, they wouldn't sting you.” I tried. Once. They stung me twice as much. Gilwen said it wasn't about singing, it was about singing in tune. I don't talk to her about songs any more.
textes.Gilwen m'apporte son miel tous les matin: Gilwen brings me her honey every morning, humming. Her bees adore her, and so do I. Without her, my bread would just be bread. With her, it's sunshine.
textes.Gilwen me fournit le miel des potions. E: Gilwen supplies the honey for my potions. She talks to her bees more than to elves, and they answer her better. She thinks I haggle too much. It's true.
Gilwen. I'm going up for the honey.
textes.Gilwen. Tes abeilles sont encore sur mes: Gilwen. Your bees are on my roses again.
textes.Gisèle avait dix ans quand elle m'a appr: Gisèle was ten when she taught me to carry a tray. She still talks to me like an apprentice. She's the best boss on the island.
textes.Gisèle me garde les nouvelles du matin c: Gisèle saves me the morning news the way others save a croissant. Who argued, who arrived on the Swallow, who lost their jack. She serves it to me with the dish of the day. I pretend not to listen. She pretends not to notice.
textes.Gisèle me garde ma table depuis des anné: Gisèle has kept my table for me for years, the only one with a view of the whole harbour. She serves me without my ordering. She's the most efficient person in Port-Azur, after me.
textes.Gisèle sait tout sur tout le monde et ne: Gisèle knows everything about everyone and says almost nothing. Almost. She's the only one I'd trust with my till.
textes.Gisèle, je l'ai connue en socquettes, so: I knew Gisèle when she was in ankle socks, under her mother's table. Now she runs the café, and she knows everything about me just from the way I sit down. It's annoying, a woman who guesses.
textes.Gland ! Le seul petit qui ne s'endort ja: Gland! The only little one who never falls asleep before the end. It's a tragedy. A wonderful little tragedy, with a bushy tail.
textes.Gland a perdu trois cents noisettes. Enf: Gland lost three hundred hazelnuts. Well, two hundred and ninety-nine. I help him look. One day I found one! It was in one of Mummy's mooncakes. Inside! How it got there, nobody knows. I ate it with the cake. Gland shouted. Mummy shouted. I said it was a new cake, hazelnut flavour.
textes.Gland dit qu'il y a un dragon sous la gr: Gland says there's a dragon under the big pond. Myrtille says it's the Pond King, with a crown. I say a dragon-fish, because it's both, it's logical. Hulotte can see in the dark: he saw cake on my snout! And Roux's phoenix feather, I bought it, for a mooncake. I wear it in my hair. Look!
Gland says there's a dragon under the great pool. Myrtille says it's a big fish. I say it's a dragon-fish.
textes.Gland fait une alerte tous les jours ave: Gland does an alert every day with Croc-Gris's zip line. “Alert! Alert!” So I tell Pomme-de-Pin, and she tells him off. He says I'm a telltale. I say I'm a guard, like Croc-Gris. He says guards don't have floppy ears. That's surely not true.
textes.Gland m'a appris à grimper, au pied du C: Gland taught me to climb, at the foot of the Mother Oak. He said: “Easy! One paw, then the other paw!” I got up onto the first branch. And I stayed sitting on it. All afternoon. Gland went up and down to the top to show me. I watched. Rabbits don't climb. They run.
textes.Gland, c'est un frimeur. Il grimpe vite,: Gland is a show-off. He climbs fast, fine, but he's a squirrel, that's cheating! And he keeps telling me I'm amazing. That's fishy.
textes.Gland, il parle trop et il dit n'importe: Gland talks too much and says silly things: he says it's a dragon. It's a dragon-fish! But he's funny. And I help him look for his hazelnuts. A bit.
textes.Gland, mon petit frère, a caché trois ce: Gland, my little brother, hid three hundred hazelnuts somewhere in the Mother Oak. He doesn't remember where. Neither do I. The tree might.
textes.Gland. Il saute sur le ponton, il parle: Gland. He jumps on the jetty, he talks about dragons, he scares off everything that swims. … But he comes back every day. That's patience too.
textes.Gland. Une alerte par jour. Fausse, chaq: Gland. One alarm a day. False, every time. Noisy. Cheeky. He says I've got the best house in the village. … He's not wrong.
textes.Glaucos ! Encore une lanterne sur le can: Glaucos! Another lantern on the canal tonight.
textes.Glaucos ! Tu as vu ? Encore une lanterne: Glaucos! Did you see? Another lantern on the canal!
textes.Glaucos souffle la nacre comme personne: Glaucos blows mother-of-pearl like nobody else and talks like an oyster: mouth shut. He crosses my bridge every evening. For the light, he says.
Glaucos was my apprentice, the best one. Then he started blowing mother-of-pearl like a soap bubble. Puffed-up mother-of-pearl! He calls it art. I call it hot air.
textes.Glaucos. Il souffle les vasques de nacre: Glaucos. He blows the mother-of-pearl basins my corals live in. He speaks softly. I like that.
textes.Glitch a installé un programme dans mon: Glitch installed a program in my arm that plays a little tune when I tighten a bolt hard enough. I don't dare remove it.
textes.Glitch a passé une heure devant mon étal: Glitch spent an hour in front of my stall without saying a word. I sold zero programs that day. She scares the customers away.
textes.Glitch a un jour éteint tous les néons d: Glitch once switched off every neon light in the city for one minute so the children could see a shooting star. I should have scolded her. I made a wish instead.
textes.Glitch croit que mes programmes sont mau: Glitch thinks my programs are bad. She hasn't even bought any! How can you criticise a product you haven't paid for?
textes.Glitch dit qu'elle pourrait pirater la b: Glitch says she could hack the machine and put her name in place of mine. She doesn't. She says a high score has to be earned. … She's cool, Glitch. Don't tell her I said that.
Glitch says it's a bad idea. But it's almost free…
textes.Glitch m'a montré comment voir les résea: Glitch let me see the networks through her visor, for one minute. I saw the whole city in green lines. I got dizzy. It was the best day of my life.
textes.Glitch pourrait pirater la borne et mett: Glitch could hack the machine and put her name on my high score. She doesn't. She says a high score has to be earned. She's way too cool. Don't tell her I said that.
textes.Glitch répare ce qui est dans les machin: Glitch fixes what's inside the machines, I fix what's around it. Between the two of us, we fix just about everything. Except Turbo's bad moods.
textes.Glitch répare les feux, les ascenseurs,: Glitch fixes the traffic lights, the lifts, the terminals. She refuses to be paid. I offered her a job at the town hall. She told me: “Offices are buggy.”
textes.Glitch vérifie mes programmes, maintenan: Glitch checks my programs now. She opened one yesterday: there were three viruses and a pancake recipe. She kept the recipe. I'm keeping… the shame.
textes.Glitch, c'était toi, dans l'écran ?: Glitch, was that you, in the screen?
textes.Glitch, la petite à la visière, peut ent: Glitch, the girl with the visor, can get into any system. Lucky she's nice. She fixes the boulevard's traffic lights when they crash. For free.
textes.Glorb ! Bienvenue ! Au nom du Conseil…: Glorb! Welcome! In the name of the Council…
textes.Glorb ! Les glouglous te réclament !: Glorb! The glug-glugs are asking for you!
textes.Glorb ! Une nouvelle étiquette pour vous: Glorb! A new label for you.
textes.Glorb ! Voici tes holo-photos des quatre: Glorb! Here are your holo-photos from the four corners of the archipelago.
textes.Glorb a collé sa main sur ma plus belle: Glorb pressed his hand on my finest pane. It kept the print. A green, star-shaped handprint. I didn't dare wipe it off. Orbe wants to cut it out for the Museum.
textes.Glorb a voulu photographier une méduse d: Glorb wanted to photograph a sky jellyfish. It got scared and hid behind him. But he's see-through: you could see it right through him, all pink, in the middle of his jelly. I laughed so hard I had to sit down. Glorb took the photo anyway. He says it's a self-portrait.
textes.Glorb a voulu prendre une méduse de ciel: Glorb wanted to take a photo of a sky jellyfish. The jellyfish got scared and hid behind him. He's see-through too. It didn't work.
textes.Glorb est arrivé en soucoupe, sans passe: Glorb arrived by saucer, without going through the Gate. He never got a welcome speech. It's an injustice. I'm chasing him to set it right. He hides. It's very vexing, and a bit funny.
textes.Glorb est la créature la plus intéressan: Glorb is the most interesting creature ever to enter my Museum. He dripped on my display case. I kept the trace. It's the only piece in room two that doesn't come from down below. It comes from Gloop.
textes.Glorb est transparent, comme mes méduses: Glorb is see-through, like my jellyfish. He says we're from the same family. I told him: “the same aesthetic family”. He's very proud. The glug-glugs adore him.
textes.Glorb est venu photographier ma vieille: Glorb came to photograph my old boot. He was so moved he dripped a little on the display case. I took out a label and wrote: “Tourist trace, planet Gloop.” He trembled with pride. Visitors now look at the trace before the boot. I don't know if the boot is jealous.
textes.Glorb ne mange jamais ma gelée. Il a peu: Glorb never eats my jelly. He's afraid it might be family. I've promised him a hundred times it's fruit. He half believes me. He watches it wobble with great respect.
textes.Glorb, le touriste de la planète Gloop,: Glorb, the tourist from the planet Gloop, would like to send his mum photos from the four corners of the archipelago. But he's green and wobbly, and he's afraid of scaring the people down below. He gives you his holo-photo: you need to photograph the mayor of Port-Azur, Mama Grog in Balafre, the Baron of Montjoie and Mamie Barricade in the Boucan, then bring the camera back to him.
textes.Glorb, le touriste vert, me regarde fair: Glorb, the green tourist, watches me make jelly with a lot of worry. Every time he asks: “It's not a cousin, is it?” No, Glorb. It's fruit. Promise.
textes.Glorb, le touriste, a acheté vingt carte: Glorb, the tourist, bought twenty postcards of Astralys. He sent nineteen to his mother, on the planet Gloop. The twentieth, he ate. By mistake. I think.
textes.Glorb, le touriste, a voulu prendre en p: Glorb, the tourist, wanted to photograph my old boot. He was so moved he dripped a little on the display case. I put up a label: “Tourist trace, planet Gloop”. It's become a piece in the collection.
textes.Glorb, le touriste, est arrivé par souco: Glorb, the tourist, arrived by saucer, without going through the Gate. He never got a speech. I owe him one. I've been chasing him for three weeks.
textes.Glorb, le touriste, m'a pris en photo pe: Glorb, the tourist, took a picture of me while I was falling off the platform. He says it's his favourite photo. I shall request a decree making it officially blurry.
textes.Glorb, pourquoi tu photographies tout ?: Glorb, why do you photograph everything?
textes.Glorb, quand on lui saute dessus, il fai: When you jump on Glorb, he goes “blorp” and you bounce really high. He's the best trampoline on the island. He says he's not a trampoline. He bounces anyway. He takes photos of me in mid-flight.
When you jump on Glorb, he goes “blorp” and you bounce. He's the best trampoline on the island. He says he's not a trampoline. He bounces anyway.
textes.Glou, glou. L'eau a un goût de… rien du: Glug, glug. The water tastes of… absolutely nothing. Optimised. It still feels good (one more heart).
textes.Gloubi demande la permission à chaque fr: Gloubi asks every fruit for permission before picking it. With his four arms. That's a lot of arms for a single question. The fruits always say yes. They're intimidated. And they like him.
textes.Gloubi dit que le déjeuner est « prêt da: Gloubi has been saying lunch is “ready in five minutes” for a thousand years. He does it on purpose. He says it's good for my character. His cooking is delicious. I'm still waiting for it.
Gloubi has been saying lunch will be “ready in five minutes” since eleven forty. It's twelve minutes past twelve. I counted. He knows. He makes me wait on purpose. He says it's good for my character.
textes.Gloubi fait des gelées qui tremblent exa: Gloubi makes jellies that wobble exactly like my uncle Blurp. He swears they're fruit. I half believe him. I greet all his jellies, just to be safe. His biscuits are delicious.
textes.Gloubi m'a fabriqué une gelée qui ne tre: Gloubi made me a jelly that doesn't wobble, just for me. It was as hard as a rock. I looked at it for a long time. It didn't move. It surely wasn't a cousin. I took it back to my bubble and put it on my bedside table. I call it “Rocky”. I say goodnight to it.
textes.Gloubi me fait des signes par-dessus la: Gloubi waves to me over the fountain. With four arms. I never understand a thing. Once, I thought his café was burning. It was hello. I adore him, that big foodie.
textes.Gloubi vient cueillir des fruits lumineu: Gloubi comes to pick glowing fruit for his cooking. He asks their permission with all four arms. That's a lot of arms for one question. The fruit always says yes. They're intimidated.
Gloubi, it's twelve minutes past noon.
textes.Gloubi, tu me fais des signes ?: Gloubi, are you waving at me?
textes.Gnocchi est tout rond, tout doux, et tou: Gnocchi is all round, all soft, and always hungry. A real gnocchi. He wants to be a pirate, a novice, a volcano. Me, I just want him to finish his plate.
textes.Gnocchi tourne autour du Couvercle avec: Gnocchi keeps circling the Lid with a wooden spoon. I'm watching him. A wooden spoon starts with a “tink”, and ends with a BOOONG.
textes.Gnocchi veut devenir novice comme moi. I: Gnocchi wants to be a novice like me. He already has a colander bigger than mine. I think he's going to be better than me. That's not hard.
textes.Gnocchi veut devenir novice comme moi. J: Gnocchi wants to become a novice like me. I told him he'd have to grow up first. He put on a colander even bigger than mine. You can't see him at all anymore.
textes.Gnocchi veut être pirate. Il a déjà le c: Gnocchi wants to be a pirate. He's already got the cry, the swagger and the colander. All he needs is a boat and ten years. I'm keeping the first mate's spot for him.
textes.Gnocchi, mon petit-fils, il veut tout fa: Gnocchi, my grandson, wants to do everything. Pirate, novice, singer. I told him: be a farmer. Farmers get up early, but they see the sun rise over the wheat. He said it was too early.
textes.Gné ?… Si c'est le facteur, posez ça sur: Hmm?… If it's the mailman, put it on the table… zzz…
Gontran! North is that way, my friend.
textes.Gontran ! Par la porte, aujourd'hui ? Pa: Gontran! Through the door, today? Not through the window?
textes.Gontran ! Tu as l'air tout pâle, mon cho: Gontran! You're looking very pale, sweetie.
textes.Gontran Jambe-de-Bois doit quarante pièc: Gontran Jambe-de-Bois owes Mama Grog forty coins. For three moons now. Mama's starting to sharpen her rolling pin.
textes.Gontran Lestrange me déteste depuis que: Gontran Lestrange has hated me since I won his compass from him. He growls, he limps, he accuses me of cheating. He's my best enemy. Without him, the Shark's Tooth would be so boring!
textes.Gontran Lestrange, dit Jambe-de-Bois, le: Gontran Lestrange, known as Jambe-de-Bois, captain of the Veuve Écarlate, has owed Mama Grog forty coins for three moons. She wants his purse.
textes.Gontran Lestrange, mon chou, c'est un bo: Gontran Lestrange, sweetie, is a good captain, a decent man and a real eel. Between him and me, there are forty coins and a Tuesday. He says my grog was lukewarm. MY grog. Lukewarm.
Gontran is allowed to pass, Octave.
textes.Gontran, c'est mon premier pirate et ma: Gontran is my first pirate and my finest leg. He says I'm a master sculptor. I'm a surgeon, and I had a saw. He did the rest: he walks.
textes.Gonzague ! Mon volant, vous me le rendez: Gonzague! Are you giving me back my flywheel?
Gonzague! My flywheel — are you giving it back, yes or no?
textes.Gonzague est le meilleur voisin de quai: Gonzague is the best quay neighbour in the world. He fishes without talking and he shares his sardines. But as soon as I touch the Little Piston, he goes all strange. I don't know why.
textes.Gonzague est un ami solide comme sa grue: Gonzague is a friend as solid as his crane, and almost as chatty. He brings me grilled sardines; I bring him theories. It's a fair trade.
textes.Gonzague garde mon vieux volant, et il a: Gonzague has my old flywheel, and he saw my gear go by. He's an honest man. He gives everything back, except what falls. And everything falls.
textes.Gonzague ramasse tout ce qui tombe, moi: Gonzague picks up everything that falls, I buy back everything that fails. That's a lot in common for two people who don't trust each other.
textes.Gonzague, le grutier, garde tout ce qui: Gonzague, the crane operator, keeps everything that falls off the cliff. He even has a piano. Nobody knows how it got there.
textes.Good morning, madame Margaux ! Six, comm: Good morning, Madame Margaux! Six, as always.
textes.Gorgoth ! Ton bain est prêt ! Sans sels: Gorgoth! Your bath is ready! No purple salts, promise!
textes.Gorgoth ! Tu peux garder les chiots, ce: Gorgoth! Can you mind the pups this morning?
textes.Gorgoth baisse les cornes… et charge !: Gorgoth lowers his horns… and charges!
textes.Gorgoth emprunte des recueils de poèmes: Gorgoth borrows poetry collections and returns them without a crease, with a dried ember flower between two pages. He's the most delicate reader in the city. And the only one who has to duck to get in.
Gorgoth borrows books of poems. He holds them with two fingers, like butterflies. He gives them back without a single crease, with a dried ember flower inside. He's my favourite reader. Shh.
textes.Gorgoth est le plus grand champion de l': Gorgoth is the greatest champion of the Arena and the biggest softie in the city. He apologises when he wins. I forged him some horn guards; he wrote me a poem to thank me.
textes.Gorgoth est le plus grand démon de la ci: Gorgoth is the biggest demon in the city, and the gentlest. He writes poems with big fingers and an immense heart. I'm teaching him poetry. He's teaching me courage. It's a good exchange.
textes.Gorgoth est mon client le plus poli et l: Gorgoth is my politest customer and the longest to sew for. I need a ladder to take his measurements, and six metres of fabric for one cape. He says “sorry” every time he breathes. I adore him.
textes.Gorgoth et moi, on fait un bras de fer a: Gorgoth and I arm-wrestle at the Diable Repu every year. I beat him once. He says he let me win. He cried, so I don't know.
textes.Gorgoth garde mes chiots chaque matin. C: Gorgoth minds my pups every morning. He's the only one I trust them with. They climb on him like a mountain, and he doesn't move. The island's greatest champion and the gentlest of mountains.
textes.Gorgoth m'a demandé de lui apprendre la: Gorgoth asked me to teach him poetry. He rhymes “puppy” with “puppy”. I told him it was a perfect rhyme. That's a lie. But a kind lie, and his poems are full of heart.
textes.Gorgoth tient les livres avec deux doigt: Gorgoth holds books with two fingers, like butterflies, and turns the pages with the tip of a quill. He always returns them with a dried ember flower between two pages. I now have forty. I keep them in a herbarium, shelved under poetry. It's the only herbarium in the city filed under poetry.
textes.Gorgoth vient se baigner après ses comba: Gorgoth comes to bathe after his fights. The first time, he emptied the big pool with a single wave. So I built him his own bath. He's the kindest and wettest customer on the island.

Gorgoth comes to bathe after his fights. The first time, he got into the big pool, and all the other customers got out. By the wave. So I had his own bath built for him. The Gorgoth Bath. Now everyone wants to try it.
textes.Gorgoth, c'est moi qui l'ai découvert !: Gorgoth — I'm the one who discovered him! He was carrying four crates at a time down at the harbour, saying sorry to them. I knew straight away: THAT BOY IS A CHAMPION. And a heart of gold. That part you mustn't shout. For once.
textes.Gorgoth, respire. Je n'ai pas encore com: Gorgoth, breathe. I haven't even started measuring yet.
textes.Gorgée d'eau, avec une algue en prime. Q: Soaked through, with a bonus piece of seaweed. Somebody, somewhere, has a cold foot.
textes.Gouverneur. Pousse-toi de la lumière, s': Governor. Out of my light, please.
textes.Goûter la sauce du volcan avec la louche: Taste the volcano's sauce with the giant ladle
textes.Goûter le néo-ramen du robot du Marché d: Taste the robot's neo-ramen at the Night Market
textes.Goûter le thé stellaire de Gloubi (au Ca: Taste Gloubi's star tea (at the Nebula Café, west of the Agora of Stars)
textes.Goûter un maquereau grillé, là-haut, sur: To taste a grilled mackerel, up there, on a beach, with the sun on my back. Grandmother talked about it like a treasure. And never see another cracker again. Well, sell a few more, all the same.
textes.Goûter une vraie bouillabaisse, d'en bas: To taste a real bouillabaisse, from down below, made by a real cook from Port-Azur, with real fish. And to have him taste my cosmic jelly in exchange. I'm sure he'd make the same face I made at my first apple.
textes.Goûter, un jour, la sauce, et ne rien tr: To taste the sauce one day and find nothing to fault. Nothing at all. Then go back down, sit at the Great Table, and eat pasta with it. Down below, for once.
textes.Graissée ! Euh, je veux dire : de bonne: Well greased! Er, I mean: in a good mood.
textes.Graissée et heureuse ! J'ai réparé le kl: Greased up and happy! I fixed the orange bus's horn. It goes “Honk-honk” now. Before, it went “Prrrt”. That was embarrassing.
textes.Grand prêtre ! Du copal ? Tout frais, pr: High priest! Some copal? Nice and fresh, almost blessed!
textes.Grand prêtre ! Je peux monter, aujourd'h: High priest! Can I climb up today?
textes.Grand prêtre. Demain, c'est un bon jour: High priest. Is tomorrow a good day for hunting?
textes.Grand soleil ! Voilà un bulletin comme j: Bright sunshine! Now that's the kind of forecast I like. Keep it: up here, we need nothing more.
textes.Grand-Bec : il vole. Il tourne, il tourn: Big-Beak: he fly. He circle, circle, then dive at you. You duck… no, you roll! When he go back up, he slow: hit!
textes.Grand-Mère Aquarelle est devant la Palet: Grandma Watercolour is in front of the Palette, Gaspard at the Lookout.
textes.Grand-Mère Aquarelle et moi, on a été à: Grand-Mère Aquarelle and I went to school together. She cried on her drawings, I blackened mine. The teacher was Augustin's father. He rubbed us both out.
textes.Grand-Mère Aquarelle, l'île a retrouvé t: Grandmother Watercolour, the island has all its colours back!
textes.Grand-Mère Aquarelle, le brun est revenu: Grandmother Watercolour, the brown has returned to the clearing!
textes.Grand-Mère Aquarelle, pourquoi l'île est: Grand-Mère Aquarelle, why is the island all grey?
textes.Grand-Père ! Raconte la mer !: Grandpa! Tell me about the sea!
textes.Grand-Père Séverin m'a donné un coquilla: Grandpa Séverin gave me a shell from down below. He says you can hear the sea inside. I hold it to my ear every night. I hear a big whoosh. Mum says it's my blood moving. Grandpa says it's the sea. I believe Grandpa.
textes.Grand-Père Séverin raconte la mer mieux: Grandpa Séverin tells about the sea better than anyone. He closes his eyes and talks about the waves, the pebbles, the seagulls. When he tells it, I can see it. He's a bit deaf. But not when I'm the one talking.
textes.Grand-Père Séverin raconte la montée de: Grandpa Séverin tells the story of the island's rise as if he'd been there. He wasn't. But he tells it so well that everyone ends up remembering it. Perhaps that's what a city's memory is.
Grandpa, two choux buns, no more.
textes.Grand-mère ! Une histoire ! Une qui fait: Grandma! A story! A scary one!
textes.Grand-mère Philomène connaît toutes les: Grandma Philomène knows all the island's stories. The scary ones, the ones with happy endings, and even the true story of Master Hugues's dragon. It goes “baaa”. It's a secret.
textes.Grand-mère Philomène dit qu'au fond du d: Grandma Philomène says that at the bottom of the dungeon, there's a jelly king with a crown. A real crown! If you find it, will you lend it to me? Just for a photo. Well, a drawing. We don't have a camera.
textes.Grand-mère Philomène m'a raconté le roi: Grandma Philomène told me about the king who was afraid of the light, who went down under the earth and became all soft and all green. I had nightmares for three nights. On the fourth night, I went to ask her for the ending. She told me the king had kept his crown because he was waiting for someone to take it off him. I wasn't scared anymore. I felt sorry for him.
textes.Grand-oncle, je vous lis la rune du nord: Great-uncle, shall I read you the north rune?
textes.Grand-père ! Regarde, j'ai fait un nœud: Grandpa! Look, I tied a knot!
textes.Grand-père ! Tu as pensé à manger ?: Grandpa! Did you remember to eat?
textes.Grand-père Tilleul raconte les meilleure: Grandpa Tilleul tells the best stories in the world. The others fall asleep before the end. Not me! But he never finishes. Weird, huh?
textes.Grand-père m'a prêté sa longue-vue, une: Grandpa lent me his telescope once. I looked at the sea for an hour to see Dad's ship. I didn't see it. Grandpa said ships are like mushrooms: they turn up when you stop looking for them. So I went looking for mushrooms. So the ship would come.
textes.Grand-père m'apprend les nœuds sur le qu: Grandpa teaches me knots on the quay: the bowline, the figure-of-eight, the clove hitch. I always do the same one: the shoelace knot. Grandpa says it's a very good knot for shoes, and that's something. He's right: my shoes stay on really well.
textes.Grand-père Ébène ! Votre brioche, toute: Grandpa Ébène! Your brioche, piping hot!
textes.Grand-père Ébène a la plus belle voix de: Grandpa Ébène has the most beautiful voice in the city and the most fanciful memory. He makes up half his stories. It's the better half. I made him a lantern that casts shadows for his tales.
textes.Grand-père Ébène dit qu'au fond des Neuf: Grandpa Ébène says that at the bottom of the Nine Circles there's the Well of Giants. Giants! Bigger than me! I'd like to see them. I'd read them a poem. Maybe they're shy too.
textes.Grand-père Ébène dit que Cerbère, le chi: Grandpa Ébène says Cerbère, the three-headed dog of the Nine Circles, loves honey cakes! But you need one for each head, or they squabble. I want a three-headed dog too. He'd eat three cakes, and I'd eat the crumbs.
textes.Grand-père Ébène dit que Cerbère, le gar: Grandpa Ébène says Cerbère, the three-headed guardian of the Nine Circles, can be won over with honey cakes. One per head! My honey cakes are the best on the island. I just need good honey, that's all. Honey is the soul of the cake.
textes.Grand-père Ébène et moi, nous jouons aux: Grandfather Ébène and I have been playing basalt draughts for three hundred years. He cheats: he tells stories while I'm thinking. On his birthday, I let him win. He thinks it's thanks to the stories.
textes.Grand-père Ébène m'a raconté mes premièr: Grandpa Ébène told me my very first stories. He has the gentlest voice in the city and the most fanciful memory. I still go and listen to him, in secret, under a hood.
textes.Grand-père Ébène raconte l'histoire de P: Grandpa Ébène tells the history of Pandémonia however it suits him. The dates change, so do the heroes, and a dragon appears whenever an ending's missing. He's a marvellous storyteller and a dreadful historian.
textes.Grand-père Ébène raconte que Cerbère, le: Grandpa Ébène says that Cerberus, the three-headed dog of the Nine Circles, can't resist honey cakes: one per head. Bobor, the baker, is happy to bake three… if he has honey.
textes.Grand-père Ébène raconte, et moi, je jou: Grandpa Ébène tells the stories, and I play behind him. He's the best storyteller in the city, and the most absent-minded. He forgets his endings. I catch them with my bow. We make a fine pair.

Grandpa Ébène tells the stories, and I play behind him. When the story gets scary, I play low notes. When he forgets the ending, I hold a long note, a very long one, until he remembers. Sometimes the note lasts ten minutes.
textes.Grand-père Ébène reçoit la première brio: Grandpa Ébène gets the first brioche of every batch, in exchange for a story. For forty years. I know half his stories by heart. I pretend to hear them for the first time. He pretends not to notice.
textes.Grand-père Ébène, l'histoire de ce soir: Grandpa Ébène, does tonight's story end well?
Grandpa, your mohawk stands up on its own.
textes.Grande ? Quarante-quatre ! Non… quarante: Big? Forty-four! No… forty-five! No, wait… All right, I was wrong. That's the second time in my life. The first was Mbarek. You're in good company.
textes.Grande Liftière, cheffe de la Confrérie: Grand Liftkeeper, head of the Liftkeepers' Guild
As big as your notebook, Ernest.
Scratch behind the ear. No, the other one. THERE.
textes.Grattouille ? Grattouille. GRATTOUILLE !: Scritches? Scritches. SCRITCHES! … Thank you. I'm the happiest dog in Boucan.
textes.Grattouille. Derrière l'oreille. Non, l': Scritches. Behind the ear. No, the other one. There. I love you forever.
textes.Grave. Le soleil a besoin de nous pour s: Solemn. The sun needs us in order to rise every morning. That is no joking matter.
textes.Gravier ! Je t'ai raconté le concert du: Gravier! Did I tell you about the lighthouse concert?
textes.Gravier ! Les pigeons vous voient pêcher: Gravier! The pigeons see you fishing tomorrow!
Gravier! The pigeons see you fishing tomorrow.
textes.Gravier a pêché un poisson ! À MOI ! … I: Gravier caught a fish! MINE! … He kept it. Grrr. Kya.
textes.Gravier dit un mot par jour. Moi dix mil: Gravier says one word a day. I say ten thousand. Together, we have a perfectly balanced conversation. He's my best audience.
textes.Gravier m'a dit trois mots il y a trente: Gravier said three words to me thirty years ago, and they changed my life. Since then, we meet every evening at the fire. We don't say anything. It's perfect.
textes.Gravier m'apporte du bois flotté pour mo: Gravier brings me driftwood for my stove. He says nothing. Nor do I. We're the two calmest people on the island. That deserves respect.
textes.Gravier me donne des têtes de poisson. I: Gravier gives me fish heads. He doesn't talk. Neither do I, usually. We understand each other.
textes.Gravier ne dit presque rien. Je dis tout: Gravier hardly says anything. I say everything. One day, I predicted a big fish for him. He caught a whale. A rubber one. But still.
textes.Gravier, sur sa plage, il dit un mot par: Gravier, on his beach, says one word a day. I say ten thousand. We complement each other. He says he gets the better value for words.
Gravier. Thank you for the wood.
textes.Gravé sur une poutre : « Le trésor de Pa: Carved on a beam: “Grandpa's treasure: to share with whoever finds it. Except the chocolate coins: those are for me.”
textes.Grelot reçoit des cartes de sa tante Sés: Grelot gets postcards from her aunt Sésame, from impossible places. I bring them to her at the market. She reads them laughing. She laughs a lot. Sometimes a little too loudly.
textes.Grelot se moque de mes carottes. Tous le: Grelot makes fun of my carrots. Every day. I say her apples weigh you down. We don't get on. And I never eat her pies any more. Never.
textes.Grelot vend ses pommes contre des pièces: Grelot sells her apples for coins. Coins! A tanuki! My niece is an embarrassment. But her apples are good.
textes.Grelot, c'est la marchande de fruits. Je: Grelot is the fruit seller. I bring her wild honey from up top, she pays me in coins. I don't know what to do with coins, so I worked it out: I hang them under my bridges!
textes.Grelot, c'est ma meilleure amie. Elle pa: Grelot is my best friend. She talks for two, laughs for three, and saves me the best apples. She teases me far too much. I adore her anyway.
textes.Grelot, dépêche-toi, les tambours commen: Grelot, hurry up, the drums are starting!
textes.Grenouille ! Rends-le ! S'il vous plaît: Frog! Give him back! Please! … It doesn't read. It's not listening to me.
textes.Grenouille ! Tu as avalé le meilleur ave: Frog! You swallowed the best adventurer in Montjoie! You have good taste! But GIVE HIM BACK!
textes.Grenouille, cidre, jus de pomme ! Tout e: Frog, sparkling apple, apple juice! Everything's fresh, except the jokes. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Grignotte, le plus petit des chiots, a e: Grignotte, the smallest of the pups, was scared of a storm one night. Flammèche came knocking at my door, the pup in her arms. I held him in my hand, right against my heart, until morning. He stopped trembling. I didn't: I was afraid of squeezing him too hard. I didn't squeeze him too hard.
textes.Grillé ! Avec un filet de piment inferna: Grilled! With a drizzle of infernal chilli! You've got good taste. My husband makes it like no one else at the Diable Repu. Ask him for the “catch of the day à la Moloka”.
textes.Grimli ! Tu as encore dormi dans la mine: Grimli! Did you sleep in the mine again?
textes.Grimli a encore perdu une galerie. Perdu: Grimli has lost a tunnel again. Lost. A tunnel. That takes some doing.
textes.Grimli dort dans sa mine. Il dit que c'e: Grimli sleeps in his mine. He says it's quieter. Mostly it's because his wife snores.
textes.Grimli est le seul nain qui soit jamais: Grimli is the only dwarf who has ever got into my place without using the door. Through the floor. That doesn't count. But I don't forget.
textes.Grimli est venu me dire qu'il avait ente: Grimli came to tell me he'd heard a heart beating deep in a tunnel. He drew the way on a slate. I recognised the old signs of the descent to the Heart of the Mountain. I asked him to forget that path. Then I wiped the slate. He didn't notice. He'd already forgotten.
textes.Grimli oublie ses galeries, mais la mont: Grimli forgets his tunnels, but the mountain remembers him. He hears things I can only read. It's a gift. He thinks it's absent-mindedness.
textes.Grimli perd ses galeries, ses pioches et: Grimli loses his tunnels, his pickaxes and his socks, but never his good mood. He's got a fine beard. Not the finest. The finest is mine.
textes.Grimli perd tout, sauf son sourire. Il d: Grimli loses everything except his smile. He sleeps in his mine and says it's because of my snoring. I snore, fine. But not THAT much.
textes.Grimli trouve des rubis superbes et ne s: Grimli finds superb rubies and never knows where. A miner who doesn't know where he's digging is a thief who doesn't know it. Or a genius. I haven't decided yet.
textes.Grimli trouve du minerai partout et ses: Grimli finds ore everywhere and his tunnels nowhere. His beard got singed a hundred years ago, and he claims it grew back finer than mine. Ha.
textes.Grimli. Tu as perdu quoi, aujourd'hui ?: Grimli. What have you lost today?
textes.Grimli. Tu as retrouvé ta galerie ?: Grimli. Did you find your tunnel?
textes.Grimper au Belvédère des Couleurs, en ha: Climb to the Lookout of Colours, at the top of the Great Oak
textes.Grimper au sommet des Crocs (les colline: Climb to the top of the Fangs (the rocky hills in the south-west, above the dungeon entrance) and pick up three storm crystals
textes.Grimper un jour au sommet du Pic du Borg: To climb to the top of One-Eye Peak one day and see the whole archipelago at once, all the way to Arcanelle. And finally look at what Skull Rock is looking at.
textes.Grinçante. La Machine-à-Crêpes-à-Vapeur: Creaky. The Steam-Pancake-Machine flung a pancake at the ceiling again. It stayed there. The ceiling of a cavern is high. It's still up there. Drying. Écho says it echoes.
textes.Grippé. Bernadette tousse, ce matin. Un: Under the weather. Bernadette's coughing this morning. A bit of soot in the chimney. I swept it, I talked to her, I sang her her song. She's going again. My knees, though, aren't.
textes.Grise et contente, comme le ciel de Rain: Grey and content, like the Rainville sky.
textes.Grise. Le ciel est tout blanc aujourd'hu: Grey. The sky is all white today, not a single shadow. A sky without nuance is a blank canvas. I painted it anyway. Gustave says he loves it. He hung it upside down.
textes.Grisette ! Admirez mon col, ce matin !: Grisette! Admire my collar this morning!
textes.Grisette a des doigts de fée et des idée: Grisette has magic fingers and grand ideas. I ask her for a simple dress, she sews me a cathedral. I adore her dresses. I wear them once, and run off to put on a tunic.
textes.Grisette dit que je porte le même col de: Grisette says I've worn the same collar for three centuries. Not true: I iron it differently every day. One morning, she walked past my salon, stopped dead, and said: “Well. That one's new.” It was the same one, ironed on the bias. I savoured my victory all day.
textes.Grisette dit que mes cols ont trois sièc: Grisette says my collars are three centuries out of date. I say her capes hide her customers' horns, which is a crime. Last year, we made an outfit together for the festival. She won the prize. Since then, we've been on speaking terms. To criticise each other.
textes.Grisette est la meilleure couturière de: Grisette is the best seamstress in the city and the harshest critic of my collars. She says they're three centuries out of date. I say her capes hide the horns. We won a prize together. Neither of us has got over it.
textes.Grisette m'a cousu une robe de scène ave: Grisette sewed me a stage dress with ember sequins that light up when I play fast. She's the best dressmaker in the city. She can't stand me putting my feet up on the fountain. I do it anyway.
textes.Grisette m'a fait une cape rouge avec de: Grisette made me a red cape with ember sequins that sparkle when I move. The first time I wore it in the Arena, the crowd shouted so loud that I got scared, and I froze. The sequins went out. Madame Hurla shouted “MOVE!”. I moved. It sparkled. It was very beautiful.
Grisette sews me champion's capes. She needs a ladder to measure me, and six metres of fabric. She's very strict about hems, and very kind to me.
textes.Grisette vient s'asseoir sur un banc de: Grisette comes to sit on a bench on the square in the evening, to look at what the dancers are wearing. She takes notes. One evening, I played her a waltz and asked her what she thought of it. She answered: “The hem of your third bar is a little loose.” I didn't understand a word. She was right all the same.
textes.Grisette, cette fois, une robe toute sim: Grisette, this time, a really simple dress, all right?
textes.Grisette, elle a des poches, cette robe: Grisette, does this dress have pockets?
textes.Grisette… je crois que j'ai encore grand: Grisette… I think I've grown again.
textes.Grisou dit qu'il va battre Bondi cette f: Grisou says he'll beat Bondi this time. He says it every time. Éclair says nothing. She's the one to watch.
textes.Grisou dit qu'il va battre Bondi. Il le: Grisou says he's going to beat Bondi. He says it every time! I love it. A fellow who's never won and still believes, that reminds me of someone.
textes.Grisou m'a demandé une Grande Course qui: Grisou asked me for a Great Race that goes all the way round the island, because a wolf is all about stamina. I got out the stopwatch, I counted the arches it would take, the nights, the snack breaks… Three weeks, {surnom}. Three weeks of racing! He said: “Perfect.” I put the stopwatch away very quickly.
Grisou talks a lot. He runs less.
textes.Grisou, c'est mon rival. Trois fois deux: Grisou is my rival. Three times second behind me. Nice, chatty, not really dangerous. Well… a wolf never gives up. I keep an eye on him. He keeps one on me too, from the lookout post.
textes.Grisou. Il vient chaque soir à l'heure d: Grisou. Comes every evening at closing time. He talks. He talks. He talks some more. Exhausting. Hm. He carries the coal, at least.
textes.Grmbl… Bon. Pour toi. Mais tu ne le dis: Grmbl… Fine. For you. But you tell nobody.
textes.Grognon. La grille du Dôme d'Azur a grin: Grumpy. The Azure Dome gate creaked all night. Twelve years I've been oiling her, and now that she opens thirty times a day, she creaks! I say she's showing off. I understand her. But she's wrecking my ears. What's left of them.
Grumpy. The Azure Dome gate creaked all night. “Works”, says the sign. I say she's getting impatient. I understand her. But she's wrecking my ears. What's left of them.
textes.Grognon. Un requin m'a volé mon outil pr: Grumpy. A shark stole my favourite tool. It's been taunting me from the reef.
textes.Grok chasse. Grok rate. Grok chasse enco: Grok hunt. Grok miss. Grok hunt again.
textes.Grok chasseur. Grok connaît toutes les b: Grok hunter. Grok know every beast on island. You want know?
textes.Grommelot ! Tu veux être une grenouille,: Grommelot! Do you want to be a frog this morning?
textes.Grommelot ! Une énigme : qu'est-ce qui g: Grommelot! A riddle: what grumbles in the morning and…
textes.Grommelot ? Le lutin qui garde les racin: Grommelot? The goblin who guards the roots, down below. He chased me off with a broom and he still hasn't forgiven me for my hole. I like him anyway: he grumbles like a seed sprouting.
textes.Grommelot ? Mon cobaye préféré ! Il dit: Grommelot? My favourite guinea pig! He says he hates being a frog. I say he's never looked as happy as he does on a lily pad.
textes.Grommelot ? Un nœud de racine avec une b: Grommelot? A knot of root with a beard. He calls me a glitter-gnat and snatches my crystal shards from under my nose.
textes.Grommelot ? Une énigme que je n'ai pas f: Grommelot? A riddle I haven't finished solving. He grumbles, fine. But he sees far, further than any of us. I learnt that too late.
textes.Grommelot collectionne les éclats de cri: Grommelot collects crystal shards. He says they're for his fireplace. I think he finds them pretty.
textes.Grommelot dit qu'il collectionne les écl: Grommelot says he collects crystal shards for his fireplace. One evening I went past his window: he was sitting on the floor in front of the fire, watching the colours dance in his shards. He was smiling. Grommelot. Smiling. I told everyone, and he's never forgiven me.
Grommelot pretends to be mean. He growls, he grumbles… but he's the kindest in the whole kingdom. You mustn't tell him. He'd be offended.
Grommelot pretends to be mean. He gave me a blanket last winter. Grumbling.
textes.Groovy ! Mon cœur bat à 120 battements p: Groovy! My heart beats at 120 beats per minute, like a good dance rhythm.
textes.Gros-Louis ! Des lumières vertes, cette: Gros-Louis! Green lights, last night. Again.
textes.Gros-Louis ! J'ai mon poing dans la poch: Gros-Louis! I've got my fist in my pocket!
textes.Gros-Louis ! Tu as encore fouillé le can: Gros-Louis! Have you been rummaging in the stern cannon again?
textes.Gros-Louis ? Le cœur le plus large de l': Gros-Louis? The biggest heart in the archipelago, and the biggest everything else too. If I say “jump”, he jumps. The trouble is, he also jumps when I say “lunch”.
textes.Gros-Louis dit que je l'ai battu. Il n'a: Gros-Louis says I beat him. He hadn't even raised his fists! It doesn't count. He says he's champion. Champion of what? Of stew?
textes.Gros-Louis est le plus fort du Requin et: Gros-Louis is the strongest on the Shark and the biggest scaredy-cat in the graveyard. He says my green lights are fireflies. He's never gone to look. Well, only as far as the gate.
textes.Gros-Louis est le premier nom sur mon ta: Gros-Louis is the first name on my board, and the biggest appetite in my song. He wants me to replace “gros” with “large”, as in big-boned. Nothing rhymes with it. I'm still looking.
textes.Gros-Louis, c'est mon meilleur ami du mo: Gros-Louis is my best friend in the whole wide world. He's big-boned, not fat! He taught me how to make a fist, and he carries me on his shoulders. From up there, I can see everything.
textes.Gros-Louis, c'est mon meilleur client et: Gros-Louis is my best customer and my worst nightmare. He says my recipe has a hole in it. He's the one with a hole. In his stomach. A bottomless hole, like a well.
textes.Grosse-Dent dort maintenant. Grosse-Dent: Grosse-Dent sleep now. Grosse-Dent snore. Grosse-Dent nice when sleep.
textes.Grosse-Dent est furieux : il va plus vit: Grosse-Dent is furious: he's faster now… and he's calling his raptor pals!
textes.Grosse-Dent s'est cogné la tête contre l: Grosse-Dent bumped his head on the rock! He's seeing stars: STRIKE HIM NOW!
textes.Grosse-Dent s'écroule… et se met à RONFL: Grosse-Dent collapses… and starts SNORING. He sleeps like a baby (an eight-ton baby). The Clan will talk about it for generations! Go back and see Ougha at the Camp.
textes.Grosse-Dent toujours là. Ougha entend so: Grosse-Dent still there. Ougha hear roar at night.
textes.Grouik ! Le groin d'or de Truffe a encor: Oink! Truffe's golden snout has struck again: he pulls {objet} out of the ground, covered in mud, and sets it at your feet.
textes.Grouik ! Truffe a déterré une truffe ! I: Oink! Truffle dug up a truffle! He sets it at your feet, snout full of dirt.
textes.Grouik ! Tu me comprends ? Alors je te d: Oink! You understand me? Then I'll tell you everything: I'm hungry. Always. It's my job.
textes.Grouik ! Ça veut dire « je suis content: Oink! That means “I'm happy”. Oink oink means “very”.
textes.Grouik grouik ! Truffe arrive au petit t: Oink oink! Truffle arrives at a little trot, ears flopping.
Oink oink! That means “thank you”. Oink oink oink! That means “another scratch, please”.
Grr. I'm going back to my field.
textes.Grrrrinc… Deuxième vanne. Les jets de ce: Grrrrinc… Second valve. The jets in this corridor switch off; the gauge reads “MEDIUM”. One more!
textes.Grrrrinc… PFFFFSSSHHH ! Toute la chauffe: Grrrrinc… PFFFFSSSHHH! The whole boiler room lets out a long sigh of relief. The gauge falls to “SLIPPERS” (that's the minimum).
textes.Grrrrinc… Tu tournes le gros volant roug: Grrrrinc… You turn the big red wheel. The pipes sigh, and the jets in this corridor fall silent. The pressure gauge, near the door, drops a notch: “HIGH”.
textes.Grrr… Les loups du Guet vont entendre pa: Grrr… The wolves of the Watchtower will hear about you.
Grrr… It smells of bolts around here.
textes.Grumbald ! J'ai pêché un mérou énorme !: Grumbald! I've caught an enormous grouper!
textes.Grumbald ! J'ai un nouveau gâteau pour l: Grumbald! I've got a new cake for the contest!
textes.Grumbald ! Ma table, et mon grog !: Grumbald! My table, and my punch!
textes.Grumbald a voulu faire une lave glacée à: Grumbald tried to make a brioche frozen lava. He froze one of my brioches and served it with fire syrup. It was horrible. I told him so. He tasted it and said: “It's horrible.” Then we each ate three, laughing, because we couldn't stop. I've never eaten anything so horrible. Or so good.
textes.Grumbald dit que sa lave glacée est le m: Grumbald says his frozen lava is the best dessert in Pandémonia. A sorbet! A cold dessert! Among demons! Well… I love it. But I'll never say so in front of him.
textes.Grumbald me sert un café du Brasier chaq: Grumbald serves me a Brasier coffee every noon, and I pay him in news. He says it's the best currency for a tavern keeper. He's round, he's kind, and his soup is named after me. For a funny reason.
textes.Grumbald tient le Diable Repu et prétend: Grumbald runs the Diable Repu and claims his frozen lava is the best dessert in the city. A sorbet! For demons! He's my rival, my best customer and my friend. In that order, depending on the day.
textes.Grumbald tient le Diable Repu. Chaque so: Grumbald runs the Diable Repu. Every evening, he keeps my table for me and serves me a hot sulphur punch. He knows my ash storm by heart. He moves his lips along with me. I pretend not to see.
textes.Grumbald, c'est mon mari. Il est rond, i: Grumbald is my husband. He's round, he laughs loudly, and he cooks like no one else. He once said my fish wasn't fresh. He never said it again. I love him.
textes.Grâce au ressort. Moi, j'ai juste eu l'i: Thanks to the spring. I only had the idea.
textes.Grâce à ma bière, qui fait passer ta cui: Thanks to my fizz, which washes your cooking down!
textes.Grâce à ma cuisine, Ulfa. Pas à ta bière: Thanks to my cooking, Ulfa. Not your fizz.
textes.Grâce à tes bâtons, j'ai de quoi travail: Thanks to your sticks, I've got enough work for the whole winter. Well, there's no winter here. The whole year, then.
textes.Grâce à tes champignons, j'ai soigné la: Thanks to your mushrooms, I cured half the village's cough. Faelar included. He says it's the first time in three centuries.
textes.Grâce à tes champignons, même Bramm a so: Thanks to your mushrooms, even Bramm smiled. For half a second. I counted.
textes.Grâce à tes cœurs de magma, ma galerie e: Thanks to your magma hearts, my tunnel is lit up like a party hall. I found my silver vein again. And two pickaxes. And a dwarf.
textes.Grâce à toi, Orsik ! Un roi n'oublie pas: Thanks to you, Orsik! A king never forgets.
textes.Grâce à toi, Silas. Une histoire, en éch: Thanks to you, Silas. A story, in exchange?
textes.Grâce à toi, j'ai changé Grommelot en gr: Thanks to you, I turned Grommelot into a frog this morning. Five minutes. He loved it. He says he didn't.
textes.Grâce à toi, le Grand Cristal brille de: Thanks to you, the Great Crystal shines over Atlantis once again.
Thanks to you, my collection is complete. Well, until I find a bigger one to complete.
textes.Grâce à vous, il y a un article neuf mil: Thanks to you, there is an article nine thousand and one: “The smile.” It's the only one everybody follows.
textes.Grégoire a les meilleurs yeux de Carène: Grégoire has the best eyes in Carène and the worst temper. He holds a grudge over one tiny question mark. But when he says he's seen something, I write it down. Almost in ink.
textes.Grégoire a servi ma mère, puis moi. Il n: Grégoire served my mother, then me. He never says anything he hasn't seen. So when he says he saw a light in Stoneheart, I don't sleep all night.
Grégoire counts the passing ships. None ever pass. But his lantern, at night, is what brings me home. I tease him, he sulks. That's how we like each other.
textes.Grégoire jure qu'il a vu de la lumière d: Grégoire swears he's seen light in Stoneheart at night. Grégoire has good eyes. That's exactly what worries me.
textes.Grégoire m'a prêté son carnet de guetteu: Grégoire lent me his lookout's journal: forty years of notes, winds, whales, storms, ships. I found a line in it from twenty years ago: “Light on Stoneheart, one second. Probably nothing.” His first light. He'd forgotten it. I haven't told him yet.
textes.Grégoire, là-haut dans sa hune, compte l: Grégoire, up in his crow's nest, counts the ships going by. None ever go by. He counts anyway.
textes.Grésil a médité six heures à côté de moi: Grésil meditated for six hours beside me. When he woke up, he said: “… That was good.” I didn't have the heart to tell him he was snoring.
Grésil wrote a twelve-minute solo. I asked him where I was supposed to sing in all that. He said: “… After.”
textes.Grésil parle lentement mais joue très vi: Grésil talks slowly but plays really fast. Without him, my songs would just be words. With him, they screech. That's better.
textes.Grésil s'endort sur ses amplis. Il ronfl: Grésil falls asleep on his amps. He snores in A minor. I recorded it.
textes.Grésil s'est endormi pendant un solo, hi: Grésil fell asleep during a solo yesterday. He kept on playing. Best solo of his life.
textes.Grésil vient méditer avec moi. Il ne bou: Grésil comes to meditate with me. He doesn't move, he doesn't speak. He's very gifted. Or asleep. The two look very much alike.
textes.Grésil, le guitariste de Rainville, vien: Grésil, the Rainville guitarist, sometimes comes to meditate with me. He's very gifted: he doesn't move, he doesn't speak. Actually, I think he's asleep.
textes.Grésille ? Elle ne grésille même plus !: Crackling? It doesn't even crackle anymore! It does... nothing! Pschhh... nothing at all! The storm ripped my antenna off the Rusty Whale's mast. I saw it fly off like a scrap-metal seagull, over the town, and land at the very top of the painted water tower, in the east. Twenty-eight metres! Fusible gets dizzy on the second rung, Boulon is too heavy for the ladder, and me... I'm a radio host, not a mountaineer. Would you go fetch it? I'll do a special show for you. Four hours long. All about you.
textes.Gunnar ! Ton bouclier brille trop. Je va: Gunnar! Your shield's too shiny. I'm going to blacken it.
textes.Gunnar garde ma halle, mon trône et ma d: Gunnar guards my hall, my throne and my dignity. He's the one who tells me, very quietly, that my crown is on my head. Nobody does it with such tact.
textes.Gunnar garde un tapis rouge, un trône et: Gunnar guards a red carpet, a throne and a king who loses his crown while it's on his head. He calls that a job. He smiles too much for a guard.
textes.Gunnar monte de la halle tous les soirs: Gunnar comes up from the hall every evening to drink a mug. The same mug, for three years now. He thinks I don't see him topping it up with water. He's sweet. He's a goof. He's sweet.
textes.Gustave a sorti les chouquettes du four: Gustave has taken the chouquettes out of the solar oven. The whole Esplanade is sniffing at once. Sounds like a choir.
Gustave has a new cap, my dear.
textes.Gustave dit que j'ai du talent. Il dit a: Gustave says I have talent. He also says I have to stop using his cellar as a laboratory. Both are true.
textes.Gustave dit que sa meilleure recette, c': Gustave says his best recipe is the view. It's served with everything.
textes.Gustave m'a emprunté le traité des mélan: Gustave borrowed my treatise on explosive mixtures six years ago. He says he has “almost finished” it.
textes.Gustave m'a raconté une blague sur les c: Gustave told me a joke about cumulus clouds. Light and fluffy. Like a cloud.
textes.Gustave m'achète mes herbes pour les met: Gustave buys my herbs to put in his vials. He's sweet, and he makes my camomile explode. I sort what I sell him: what heals on one side, what goes boom on the other.
textes.Gustave m'achète mon miel, me vend ses p: Gustave buys my honey, sells me his potions and pays his tab in vials. I have a whole shelf of vials I don't dare open. He sings on his way home. Out of tune. Very out of tune.
textes.Gustave me met une chouquette de plus da: Gustave slips an extra chouquette into my pocket in the morning when he thinks I'm not looking. I am looking. I say nothing. Gérard the sparrow is very pleased.
textes.Gustave me sert une chouquette tous les: Gustave serves me a choux bun every morning. Just one. He thinks I don't see him slip a second one into my pocket. I see everything. I say nothing. The sparrows thank him. So do I, but on the inside.
textes.Gustave met mes fraises dans son jus de: Gustave puts my strawberries in his sunshine juice and says it's his secret recipe. I say nothing. He's so proud. Besides, he pays me in choux buns. It's the best trade on the island.
textes.Gustave écoute ma course du jour tous le: Gustave listens to my race of the day every evening, with a summit tea. He laughs at the right moments. He's heard the same story four thousand times. He's the most loyal fan on the island. I've never told him I embellish it. He knows.
textes.Gustave, au Café, prend mes fraises pour: Gustave, at the Café, takes my strawberries for his sunshine juice. He says it's “his secret recipe”. The secret is my strawberries. I don't tell him anything. He's so happy.
textes.Gustave, mon petit. Tu manges assez ?: Gustave, dear. Are you eating enough?
textes.Gustave, ta potion d'hier a fait chanter: Gustave, your potion from yesterday made my saucepans sing.
textes.Gustave, ta recette secrète est prête ?: Gustave, is your secret recipe ready?
textes.Gwen ! Je suis là ! Où est mon marteau ?: Gwen! I'm here! Where's my hammer?
Gwen! Your cider's nice and cool, sweetie.
textes.Gwen Calfat, charpentière de marine. Le: Gwen Calfat, shipwright. The Sans-Pitié, up on the shore, is my project. It took a reef right in the side. When I'm done, it'll be finer than before. Or nearly.
textes.Gwen m'a fabriqué une étagère pour mes c: Gwen made me a shelf for my shells, with oak planks from the Merciless that weren't needed anymore. There are two hundred and twelve little compartments. Plus an empty one, at the top, in the middle. I asked her why. She said: “For the one you haven't found yet.” I couldn't answer. She handed me a nail.
textes.Gwen m'apprend à calfater. Elle dit que: Gwen is teaching me to caulk. She says I miss the nails one time in two. That's not true: it's one time in three. She sings with me. She sings out of tune. I'll never tell her.
textes.Gwen ne boit que du cidre, celui de Carè: Gwen only drinks cider, the Carène kind, like at her father's in Brittany. So I keep a barrel of cider just for her, under the counter. Nobody else touches it. Tonneau tried once. I just showed him my rolling pin. He said: “I was looking for the way out.”
textes.Gwen ressuscite le Sans-Pitié planche pa: Gwen is bringing the Merciless back to life plank by plank. I watch her work every morning, by the fire on the shore. She has the hands of Barbe-Sanglante's carpenter. That's the highest compliment I know.
textes.Gwen, c'est la seule femme de la Balafre: Gwen is the only woman on the Balafre who hits harder than me. On nails, luckily. She repaired my counter after the big brawl. I pay her in cider.
textes.Gwen. Elle travaille le bois, moi le fer: Gwen. She works wood, I work iron. She knows what she wants. I give her four hundred nails. She counts four hundred. We get on.
textes.Gwenola ! Un maquereau pour toi, le plus: Gwenola! A mackerel for you, the finest one.
textes.Gwenola ? La meilleure galette de la côt: Gwenola? The best crêpes on the coast and the hardest head in Carène. She teases me because I talk to fish. She knows full well why I talk to them.
textes.Gwenola compte mes grogs avec des harico: Gwenola counts my hot honeys with dried beans: one bean in her left pocket per mug served. After the third, it's herbal tea. One evening, while she was laughing, I slipped some beans into her right pocket. She checked the wrong pocket and served me five. The next day she'd sewn the right pocket shut.
textes.Gwenola m'a fait venir une nuit pour rép: Gwenola called me in one night to fix her stove hinge without letting the fire drop. “Not by one degree, Jos.” I worked till dawn, my beard sizzling. In the morning, she laid her hand on the door, said “good”, and served me the biggest breakfast of my life: four crêpes, two mugs and a smile.
textes.Gwenola me met une galette dans la poche: Gwenola has slipped a pancake into my pocket every morning for thirty years. I never asked her for anything. I've never really said thank you. She knows. At the Bordée, they know everything.
textes.Gwenola, c'est le poêle qui ne s'éteint: Gwenola is the stove that never goes out and the hand that never serves me more than three hot honeys. Without her, my stories wouldn't have a chair.
textes.Gwenola, il y a la capitainerie, les com: Gwenola, there's the harbour office, the accounts, the hull…
textes.Gwenola, je n'ai vraiment pas le temps a: Gwenola, I really don't have time today.
textes.Gwenola, ma belle, un petit grog pour la: Gwenola, my lovely, a little hot honey for the throat?

textes.Gâteau. Je me souviens. Je t'en garde un: Cake. I remember. I'm saving you a piece. A small one.
textes.Gédéon ! À la batterie ! Tu l'as entendu: Gédéon! On drums! Did you hear him? He plays like a thunderstorm that's taken lessons! Tapage cried. He says it's the dust. There's no dust on stage, we swept.
textes.Gédéon devrait reprendre Lisse & Fils. I: Gédéon should take over Lisse & Son. He is the “Son”. But he taps. On everything. I don't know where he gets it from. (He taps his foot.)
textes.Gédéon est le garçon le plus doué et le: Gédéon is the most gifted and the shyest boy I know. I keep his drum-kit-shaped piles of files in a cupboard. For the day he's famous.
textes.Gédéon fait tournoyer ses baguettes, les: Gédéon twirls his sticks, catches them without looking, and launches a solo that makes the glass roof shake. Larsen doesn't turn anything down.
textes.Gédéon joue ! Et il joue JUSTE !: Gédéon plays! And he plays IN TUNE!
textes.Gédéon joue ! La Halle entière se tait d: Gédéon plays! The whole Hall falls silent at once… then explodes! What a drummer!
textes.Gédéon respire un grand coup, traverse l: Gédéon takes a deep breath, crosses the pit (the crowd parts, intrigued), climbs onto the stage, takes the stand-in's place, and twirls his drumsticks. A drumroll. The Howling Hall falls silent. Then it HOWLS.
textes.Gédéon tapote, j'aboie en rythme. Il dit: Gédéon taps, I bark in rhythm. He says I'm the best four-legged bass player. I don't know what that is. But it's me.
textes.Gédéon, c'est le fils de Lisse. Il est t: Gédéon is Lisse's son. He's as shy as a kitten in the rain, and he's got the best rhythm in his hands I've ever heard.
textes.Gédéon, le fils de Lisse, est venu faire: Gédéon, Lisse's son, came to get a grey office bike repaired. While I was working, he tapped out a rhythm on my toolbox. I dropped my spanner. That boy has something in his fingers.
textes.Gédéon, le fils de Monsieur Lisse, tapot: Gédéon, Mr Lisse's son, taps out rhythms on everything he touches. Every evening, he listens to the Bilge Rats from behind the door of the Howling Hall. He's a brilliant drummer, but he has neither drumsticks nor courage. As for the drumsticks, you've kept them since the Great Boucan

Gédéon, Mr Lisse's son, taps out rhythms on everything he touches. Every evening, he listens to the Bilge Rats from behind the door of the Howling Hall. He's a brilliant drummer, but he has neither drumsticks nor courage. As for the drumsticks, you've kept them since the Great Boucan…
textes.Gédéon, pourquoi vous tapotez toujours ?: Gédéon, why are you always tapping?
textes.Gédéon. (Long silence. Il sourit.) Enfin: Gédéon. (Long silence. He smiles.) At last.
Gédéon. Stop tapping, if you please.
textes.Gédéon. Il tapote. Il tapote juste. Très: Gédéon. He taps. He taps in time. Right in time. He's scared. So was I, at first. (He nods.)
textes.Génial ! Aujourd'hui, j'ai regardé par l: Brilliant! Today I looked out of the window all the way to the third floor. The third! Then I saw a pigeon and had to sit down.
textes.Génial ! Ce matin, une baleine est passé: Great! This morning, a whale swam past the Skala. Yes, I swear. Nobody believes me.
textes.Génial ! Gros-Louis m'a appris à faire u: Great! Gros-Louis taught me how to make a fist! But the captain says I'm not allowed to use it. So I keep it in my pocket.
textes.Génial ! J'ai mis un biscuit lunaire dan: Awesome! I put a moon biscuit in the fountain. Now there's a biscuit-shaped planet. Tempo is furious. Gloubi is proud.
textes.Génial ! Tiens, trois noix de coco. Non,: Brilliant! Here, three coconuts. No, two. We start with two. If you drop one, you take a bow: that's the clown's rule.
textes.Génial… Bien, bien. Tu as du courage, to: Brilliant… Good, good. You're brave, you are. Me, just looking at the Swallow makes my knees go all wavy.
textes.Gérard ! Ta table t'attend. Bouillabaiss: Gérard! Your table is waiting. Bouillabaisse?
textes.Gérard Dupuis a oublié son appareil phot: Gérard Dupuis left his camera at the lookout, at the top of the hill.
textes.Gérard photographie plus qu'il ne regard: Gérard photographs more than he looks. But when he really looks, he's the gentlest man in the world. He just ought to lose his camera more often.
textes.Gérard photographie tout et ne regarde r: Gérard photographs everything and looks at nothing. He's nice, he's funny, and he gets on my nerves. A photo steals a landscape; I keep telling him so.
Gérard wanted to photograph my pot. Never! Because of the secret. I hid it under a tea towel and stood in front of it, arms spread wide. He photographed the tea towel. He says it's his best photo. It's blurry.
textes.Gérard, c'est le truc que j'ai trouvé au: Gérard is the thingy I found at the market. Nobody knows what it is. Gaspard says it's “a part from an unknown mechanism”. Ysaé says it's “a bit of something”. I say it's Gérard. He sleeps on my bedside table.
textes.Gérard, c'est mon client de midi. Bouill: Gérard is my lunchtime regular. Bouillabaisse every day, twice if he dares. A man who eats like that, I'd adopt him if he didn't already have a family.
textes.Gérard, chéri. Tu regardes le coucher de: Gérard, darling. Are you watching the sunset, or looking for it in your pocket?
textes.Gérard, mon pigeon, vit sur le toit du d: Gérard, my pigeon, lives on the dormitory roof. He refuses to turn back into a hat. I understand, he has a better view.
textes.Gérard, mon touriste préféré. Toujours d: Gérard, my favourite tourist. Always in a good mood, always a camera round his neck — when he hasn't left it somewhere. He did an hour of pedalo in circles. A champion, in his own way.
textes.HA ! Excellent choix ! Ce sont les meill: HA! Excellent choice! They're the best. I already have three. In the third one, you have wings. Don't ask me why, the rhyme demanded it.
textes.HA ! Toi ! Viens voir de l'acier !: HA! You! Come and see some steel!
textes.HA ! Tu as l'œil, le grand ! Tiens : le: HA! You've got a good eye, big fella! Here: my mother's stew. We only give it to beard connoisseurs.
textes.HA ! Un connaisseur ! Viens, que je te f: HA! A connoisseur! Come, let me give you a taste of number fourteen: frog with cream and mushrooms. You'll cry like Hugues.
textes.HA ! Un frère de larmes ! Viens ici que: HA! A brother in tears! Come here and let me hug you. No, don't wipe your eyes, it's no use, we'll only cry again.
textes.HA ! Un nouveau ! Approche, gamin, appro: HA! A new one! Come here, kiddo, come here! Hugues, Guild master. They call me Ironbeard. Why? Sit down, I'll tell you. It was forty years ago, in the mountains, a dragon as big as… Right, Églantine is giving me the eye. Another time.
textes.HA HA ! Alors écoute : ce matin, le chap: HA HA! Then listen: this morning, the Baron's hat landed on a cow's head. She looked very noble. That was the nine o'clock news.
textes.HA HA ! C'est mon chef-d'œuvre ! Je l'ap: HA HA! It's my masterpiece! I'll call it “The Visitor Who Ate a Lemon.”
textes.HA HA ! Voilà un aventurier sérieux ! Un: HA HA! Now there's a serious adventurer! A sharp sword is a sword that brings its owner home. I'm proud of you.
textes.HA HA ! Ysaé ! J'ai du cuivre pour toi !: HA HA! Ysaé! I've got copper for you!
textes.HA HA HA ! Brasero ! Encore une Assemblé: HA HA HA! Brasero! Another Assembly?
textes.HA HA HA ! La médaille de quoi ?: HA HA HA! A medal for what?
textes.HA HA HA ! Patatras ! Ce n'est rien : c': HA HA HA! Crash! No harm done: next time's the charm. Here, an apple juice to help you get over the excitement.
textes.HA HA HA ! Range ta collection !: HA HA HA! Put your collection away!
textes.HA HA HA ! Tu as remarqué ! On fait ce c: HA HA HA! You noticed! We've been holding this contest for a thousand years, and it's a tie every time. Here, you have a good eye: a seashell medal!
textes.HA HA HA ! Un nouveau ! Brunehaut, forge: HA HA HA! A new one! Brunehaut, blacksmith! Swords, axes, shields, and handshakes that crush! (She shakes your hand. You can't feel your fingers anymore.) Sorry. I don't know my own strength. Yes, I do. It's a lot.
textes.HA HA HA ! Un visiteur ! Entre, entre, m: HA HA HA! A visitor! Come in, come in, but not too close to the press: it has a nasty temper. Mathilde Soufflet, blacksmith! My hammers run on steam, and I run on laughter. HA HA! See? It works!
textes.HALTE ! Qui va l… Un humain ?! Un vrai ?: HALT! Who goes th… A human?! A real one?! Three hundred years I've guarded this gate, and nobody has ever come! Welcome to Atlantis! Er… I mean: welcome. Please remain calm.
textes.HO ! Dis-moi, {surnom} : tu chantes, toi: HO! Tell me, {surnom}: do you sing?
textes.HO ! Un étranger ! Hamid, pêcheur, chant: HO! A stranger! Hamid, fisherman, singer, and uncle of that mule-headed Youssef. Want a sardine? I've got three hundred.
textes.HO HO ! Deux coups, puis un ?: HO HO! Two knocks, then one?
textes.HO HO ! Par le marteau d'Ancêtre-Pierre: HO HO! By the hammer of Ancestor-Stone! I tried that in my second year. Ulfa shut the Mug for three days. Three days without fizz in the whole kingdom. But the intention was royal.
textes.HO HO ! Par le marteau d'Ancêtre-Pierre,: HO HO! By the hammer of Ancestor-Stone, there's a big'un who talks sense! A blade should weigh like an oath. Otherwise, it's a spoon.
textes.HO HO ! Yolande ! Mes roues tournent ?: HO HO! Yolande! Are my wheels turning?
textes.HO HO HO ! Un visiteur d'en haut ! Entre: HO HO HO! A visitor from up top! Come in, come in, but stay behind the yellow line: the steam hammer doesn't like strangers. Mistress Brunehaut Enclume, head of the Great Strata Forge! Here we forge rails, wheels, lantern cages, and the finest laughs in the cavern. HO HO!
textes.HO HO HO ! Voilà ! Un rire, c'est comme: HO HO HO! There we go! A laugh is like a hammer blow: if nobody hears it, it's no use! Come on, let's make Grand-Mère tremble.
textes.Ha ! Alors je préfère notre cristal. Il: Ha! Then I prefer our crystal. It burns nobody.
textes.Ha ! Alors on est deux. Une promesse, c': Ha! Then that makes two of us. A promise is like a chest: it's heavy, and you don't open it to check it's still inside. You have my respect, {surnom}.
textes.Ha ! Alors tu sais : le plus beau moment: Ha! Then you know: the best moment is just before the throw, when everyone holds their breath. I live for that silence.
textes.Ha ! Alors y a un fond. Y a toujours un: Ha! So there's a bit at the bottom. There's always a bit at the bottom.
textes.Ha ! Alors, on part quand ?: Ha! So, when do we leave?
textes.Ha ! Amirale ! Toujours à commander un b: Ha! Admiral! Still commanding a ship that doesn't move?
textes.Ha ! Apporte-la, je la redresse. Sans qu: Ha! Bring it over, I'll straighten it. No questions.
textes.Ha ! Assieds-toi plus près, toi. Une bel: Ha! Sit closer, you. A beautiful story is a truth that dressed up nicely to go out. As we say on board.
