textes.Ha ! Au moins, c'est franc. Recule un pe: Ha! At least that's honest. Step back from my stall a bit, then. A bit more. There. You can look, but with your hands behind your back.
textes.Ha ! Avec les aventures ! Ça, c'est un n: Ha! Juggling adventures! Now that's a tough act. How many can you keep in the air at once? I can't even keep two appointments.
textes.Ha ! Balam a fait une blague ! Tout le m: Ha! Balam made a joke! Did everyone hear that?
textes.Ha ! Bien. La ligne a rouvert : je t'emm: Ha! Good. The line has reopened: I'll take you down whenever you like. Get your ears ready, and your feet: down there, we dance.
textes.Ha ! Bien. Quand la ligne rouvrira, je t: Ha! Good. When the line reopens, I'll take you. Get your ears ready, and your feet: down there, we dance.
textes.Ha ! Bienvenue au club ! On a des réunio: Ha! Welcome to the club! We have meetings in the evening, at the back table. We tell each other our failures. Very friendly.
textes.Ha ! C'est la meilleure façon d'y croire: Ha! That's the best way to believe in it! That's exactly how I do it. You'd make an excellent fortune-teller.
textes.Ha ! Celle-là, je la mets dans mon spect: Ha! That one's going in my show. The kids won't get it, but the parents will. The best audience is when everyone laughs for different reasons.
textes.Ha ! Comme Grisou ! Bon, ça marche, mais: Ha! Like Grisou! Well, it works, but you miss the music. The stones sing for those who take their time!
textes.Ha ! Comme Léon ! Bon, je ne te jette pa: Ha! Just like Léon! Well, I won't hold it against you. Hautefond, seen from above, is the most beautiful place in the world. And seen from below, it's not bad either.
textes.Ha ! Dans le brouillard ! Comme mon drag: Ha! In the fog! Like my dragon!
textes.Ha ! De la fontaine de la place jusqu'à: Ha! From the fountain in the square to the lighthouse door, in under sixty seconds. The clock starts when you pass near the fountain. Ready?
textes.Ha ! Enfin quelqu'un ! Il avait combien: Ha! Someone at last! How many humps did yours have? Three? Like mine! We understand each other, you and me. Go and tell Pyra.
textes.Ha ! Enfin quelqu'un d'honnête ! Toi et: Ha! Finally someone honest! You and I are going to get along. Sit down. Do you know what Tiyi said yesterday? No? Come closer.
textes.Ha ! Enfin quelqu'un de raisonnable ! To: Ha! Finally someone sensible! High five. But don't say it too loud near the Swap Market: my uncle has sharp ears. And a fragile heart.
textes.Ha ! Enfin quelqu'un de sensé sur cette: Ha! At last, someone sensible on this coast! Come here. You are now the official enemy of every cat in Tazira. It's an honour.
textes.Ha ! Enfin quelqu'un qui a des yeux ! Ré: Ha! Finally someone with eyes! Say it louder, Raymond is deaf in his left ear. The one that hears the truth.
textes.Ha ! Enfin quelqu'un qui le voit ! Je co: Ha! Finally someone who sees it! I was starting to wonder.
textes.Ha ! Faux, j'espère ? Ici on chante faux: Ha! Off-key, I hope? Here we sing off-key, or the king takes offence. He sings so off-key the barrels crack. You'll fit right in!
textes.Ha ! Gourmand ! Le pommier de Radis, alo: Ha! Greedy! Radis's apple tree, then. I spent a night in it to check it was all right. The owl didn't appreciate it.
textes.Ha ! Ha ! J'étais en train de… de reconn: Ha! Ha! I was just… scouting the terrain!
textes.Ha ! Ha ! La tourte de Rissole fait pleu: Ha! Ha! Rissole's pie makes everyone cry. With joy, and because she gives you seconds. You're one of us.
textes.Ha ! Ha ! Tu ne savais pas ? Attends la: Ha! Ha! You didn't know? Wait for Mélusine's bell, and you'll see. They're good little things. A bit sporty, that's all.
textes.Ha ! Ha ! Tu t'es fait avaler ! Alors tu: Ha! Ha! You got swallowed! Then you're entitled to the revenge of the day: number seven, grilled. On the house. Eat it while looking it in the eye.
textes.Ha ! Hiro serait ruiné. Mais la ville se: Ha! Hiro would go broke. But the city would be happy. I'm writing that down.
textes.Ha ! Il est énorme ! Parfait ! Les gros,: Ha! It's huge! Perfect! The big ones are mine!
textes.Ha ! Je tape moins fort. Pour toi. Un pe: Ha! I'll bang softer. For you. A bit.
textes.Ha ! La meilleure réponse que j'aie ente: Ha! Best answer I've heard in twenty years. Welcome.
textes.Ha ! Le petit qui voulait me battre ! Tu: Ha! The little one who wanted to beat me! Back for a rematch?
textes.Ha ! Le plus grand mystère de l'archipel: Ha! The greatest mystery of the archipelago, spoiled by seasickness. Don't worry: Mathurin has seen plenty of future wizards step off his boat all green.
textes.Ha ! Le plus honnête de tous. Tout le mo: Ha! The most honest of all. Everyone's like that, you know. Even Professor Moreau makes his bed when he knows I'm coming. To hide his drawings in it.
textes.Ha ! Le revoilà ! Approche, approche, le: Ha! Here he is again! Come closer, come closer, the iron's hot.
textes.Ha ! Lentille serait d'accord. C'est pre: Ha! Lentille would agree. It's almost the case already, you know. You pay what you can. That's better than free: it's fair.
textes.Ha ! Les meilleures places. Tu sens les: Ha! The best spots. You feel the bass in your belly. I'll save you one.
textes.Ha ! Malin. Et… moi, je suis dans quelle: Ha! Clever. And… which category am I in?
Ha! Clever. You know where to find me.
textes.Ha ! Mon binôme ! Tu as le cœur d'une pi: Ha! My dive buddy! You've got a pilot's heart. But we wait for Yolande. Always. That's rule number two. Rule number one is snack time.
textes.Ha ! Non, elle repousse. C'était un trou: Ha! No, that grows back. It was a hole. Ask me for your prize, you made me laugh.
textes.Ha ! Non. Et la prochaine fois que tu ma: Ha! No. And next time you haggle, it costs more.
textes.Ha ! On est de la même famille, alors. V: Ha! Then we're from the same family. Have you got a screwdriver on you? No? Here, I'll lend you one. Give it back when you've taken apart something interesting.
textes.Ha ! Rê ne t'en veut pas : il a voyagé t: Ha! Rê doesn't hold it against you: he's travelled all night, he understands tiredness. But you miss the most beautiful part. A date in your hand helps you wake up.
textes.Ha ! T'as eu peur, hein ? Allez, c'est o: Ha! Got scared, eh? Come on, it's forgotten.
textes.Ha ! Toi aussi ? Bienvenue au club de Br: Ha! You too? Welcome to Bramm's club. That makes two of you. He never smiles; you, at least, try.
textes.Ha ! Toi aussi ? … Ha. … Moi aussi. Chut: Ha! You too? … Ha. … Me too. Shh. We won't talk about it any more, OK? We'll pretend we're joking.
textes.Ha ! Toi, au moins, tu as des yeux. Quar: Ha! At least you've got eyes. Forty-one verses, and not a single word face to face. I could wait a thousand years. … I may have to help him along a little.
textes.Ha ! Tout le monde abandonne ! Moi aussi: Ha! Everyone gives up! Me too, every night, around the three hundred and twelfth. But the next day, I start again. That's astronomy: giving up, and coming back.
textes.Ha ! Tu as rencontré mon cousin Mixtli,: Ha! You've met my cousin Mixtli, you have. He says the same thing. Well. If it's real, it's expensive. If it's fake, it's a trial run.
textes.Ha ! Tu as vu mon tableau ! Personne n'a: Ha! You've seen my painting! Nobody's ever said it was blue. Thank you. You have an artist's eye.
textes.Ha ! Tu me plais, toi. C'est l'hydromel: Ha! I like you. It's mead that opens your eyes, that's what I say. Others drink to forget. I drink to see.
textes.Ha ! Tu me rendras la moitié, comme d'ha: Ha! You'll give me half back, as usual.
textes.Ha ! Tu parles comme Pépin ! Ortie y tra: Ha! You sound like Pépin! Ortie is already working on one, in secret. Her machine does the homework, but it gets it wrong. On purpose. Ortie has very strong morals.
textes.Ha ! Un chanteur timide. Les plus belles: Ha! A shy singer. The most beautiful voices always hide. I'll hear you sooner or later.
textes.Ha ! Un exploit de plus ! Un VRAI ! Bert: Ha! One more exploit! A REAL one! Bertrand! I have to tell Bertrand!
textes.Ha ! Un frère ! Viens, on va voir Mange-: Ha! A brother! Come on, let's go see Mange-Clous. If he says there's nothing left, he's lying: there's always a bit of stew at the bottom.
textes.Ha ! Un frère de bord ! Et elles te répo: Ha! A shipmate! And do they answer you? No? Mine neither. Hardly ever. Keep at it, it's a matter of patience.
textes.Ha ! Un futur roadie ! Viens, j'ai des c: Ha! A future roadie! Come on, I've got crates to carry.
textes.Ha ! Un pratique ! Tu as raison aussi. A: Ha! A practical one! You're right too. Bring me your bolts, I'll buy them. They'll end up in a dragon's wing. Everybody wins.
textes.Ha ! Un visiteur ! Approche, mais pas tr: Ha! A visitor! Come closer, but not too close: sparks can't tell a customer from an anvil. Ferronde, mistress of the Great Forge. Everything made of iron in Pandémonia has passed under my hammer. Even my husband. Well, his armour.
textes.Ha ! Un vrai ! Enfin un adversaire ! Les: Ha! A real one! An opponent at last! Folks in Carène pay the marked price, it's so boring… Come to the stall, we'll have some fun.
textes.Ha ! Un vrai Montjoyen ! Doucement avec: Ha! A true Montjoyan! Go easy on my little ones, eh? One little tap, no more. They're sensitive.
textes.Ha ! Un vrai coup de poignet de liftier: Ha! A true liftkeeper's flick of the wrist! In my day, every newcomer got a gear for their first “Going up!” Here you go: this one's from my very first cabin.
textes.Ha ! Un vrai cœur d'alchimiste ! J'ai ju: Ha! A true alchemist's heart! As it happens, I have a blue vial I know nothing about. We'll discover it together. From a distance, preferably.
textes.Ha ! Un vrai démon, sans les cornes ! Go: Ha! A real demon, without the horns! Then try my infernal chili. Keep one of Grumbald's grogs within reach. And don't say I didn't warn you.
textes.Ha ! Une personne raisonnable ! J'en voi: Ha! A reasonable person! I see so few. If one of my maps ever sends you into a swamp, come back and tell me. It happens. Rarely. Twice.
textes.Ha ! Une petite étincelle ! Moi aussi, j: Ha! A little spark! I was like that too. Mind your eyebrows, and your neighbours'. But keep that fire, it's precious.
textes.Ha ! Une réponse de pirate. Bon, bon, je: Ha! A pirate's answer. All right, all right, I won't push. Come and see Bertha instead. At least she doesn't ask questions.
textes.Ha ! Une âme de boulanger ! Du moment qu: Ha! A baker's soul! As long as there are some, that's all that matters. Here, have one. It's hot. Sorry.
textes.Ha ! Une âme de danseur ! Viens sur la p: Ha! A dancer's soul! Come to the square tonight, I'll play you a Pandémonia jig. Careful: here, we dance with our tails. Do what you can.
textes.Ha ! Une âme de forgeronne ! Une bonne l: Ha! A blacksmith's soul! A good blade, a good bell, a good friendship: you make them once, and they last. Come to the forge whenever you like, you'll be at home there.
textes.Ha ! Voilà quelqu'un de bien. Une lame q: Ha! Now there's a decent sort. A blade with a name gets looked after, sharpened, talked to. My ancestor talked to his cannons. Me, to my anvil.
textes.Ha ! Voilà un remède que Gloubi approuve: Ha! Now there's a remedy Gloubi would approve of. One cosmic jelly, and the world's already better. It's not very medical. But it works.
Ha! Now that's a dwarf's answer.
Ha ha! Well played, you too.
textes.Ha ha ! Bonne journée !: Ha ha! Have a nice day!
textes.Ha ha ! Comme moi bébé ! T'es un vrai Cl: Ha ha! Like me when I was a baby! You're a real Clapotis, you are!
textes.Ha ha ! Elle est bonne !: Ha ha! That's a good one!
textes.Ha ha ! Et la cabine est repartie sans l: Ha ha! And the cabin went off without him!
textes.Ha ha ! Et le chat, il est remonté tout: Ha ha! And the cat came back up on the shuttle all by himself? Did he buy a ticket?
textes.Ha ha ! Il ne connaît qu'une danse : la: Ha ha! He knows only one dance: the screwdriver waltz. But he dances it with heart. Well, with a piston.
textes.Ha ha ! Il te prend pour une plante ! C': Ha ha! He thinks you're a plant! It's a compliment.
textes.Ha ha ! La machine a parlé ! Elle a dit: Ha ha! The machine has spoken! It said “BOOM,” but it spoke! Keep this little souvenir.
textes.Ha ha ! Mais c'est moi, à huit ans ! Une: Ha ha! But that's me at eight! One piece left over, and it still turns. Don't worry: things can always be put back together. All it takes is a mechanic.
textes.Ha ha ! Tu as parlé avec Jack, toi. C'es: Ha ha! You've been talking to Jack. That's our joke. Welcome to the team.
textes.Ha ha ! Tu as une moustache de nuage ! …: Ha ha! You've got a cloud moustache! … Me too? Since when?
textes.Ha ha ! Tu parles comme Faelar. Il a déj: Ha ha! You sound like Faelar. He once slept three years straight, you know. He says it's the best way not to age too fast.
textes.Ha ha ! Tu vois, mon trésor, les humains: Ha ha! See, my treasure, humans make faces too! They're just like us… only paler.
textes.Ha ha ! Un Pied-Lourd qui aime flotter !: Ha ha! A Heavyfoot who likes floating! You're almost a Lumen. Come back anytime, gravity is overrated.
textes.Ha ha ! Un banc pour les jambes qui trem: Ha ha! A bench for wobbly legs! I vote yes, with both knees.
textes.Ha ha ! Voilà un cœur qui court ! Tu fer: Ha ha! Now that's a racing heart! You'd make one heck of a drummer.
textes.Ha ha ! À la prochaine !: Ha ha! See you next time!
textes.Ha ha ha ! Grommelot ne chante JAMAIS. M: Ha ha ha! Grommelot NEVER sings. But I like the idea. It was the river.
textes.Ha ha ha ! Hic ! Elle est bonne !: Ha ha ha! Hic! That's a good one!
textes.Ha ha ha ! Les tartines volent !: Ha ha ha! The toast is flying!
textes.Ha ha ha ! Tu parles comme une mouette !: Ha ha ha! You talk like a seagull! “MINE!” You'd make a very good seagull, you know.
textes.Ha. Celle-là, je l'entends chaque semain: Ha. I hear that one every week, usually just before someone gets carried in to me on a plank. Keep a jar of seaweed salve in your bag anyway.
textes.Ha. Ça, c'est une réponse de potier. On: Ha. Now that's a potter's answer. Nobody hands you anything: you throw it, you fire it, and if it cracks, you start again.
textes.Haches, pelles, clous pour les ponts de: Axes, shovels, nails for Pomme-de-Pin's bridges. Bells for the lanterns. Myrtille's, Mochi's and Gland's little bells hang on the Mother Oak: on Mochi's, I engraved a little moon. My father sits on his stool and tells the customers stories. I hammer. In the evening, Grisou comes to talk. A lot. I close anyway.
textes.Haldir ! Tu as un message pour moi ?: Haldir! Have you got a message for me?
textes.Haldir ! Une lettre pour Fil-d'Aube. Cou: Haldir! A letter for Fil-d'Aube. Run!
textes.Haldir court plus vite que tout le Bois-: Haldir runs faster than the whole Bois-Doré, except when he's coming towards me. He trod on my feet seventeen times at the last festival. I counted. I always count.
textes.Haldir est le meilleur messager du Bois-: Haldir is the best messenger in the Bois-Doré, and the most patient. He carries my letters to Ilyria. And he brings them back to me, when I catch up with him. I always catch up with him.
textes.Haldir passe devant ma tour dix fois par: Haldir runs past my tower ten times a day and never says where he's going. I ask. That's my job. He doesn't answer. That's his, apparently.
textes.Halima ! Le plat est prêt pour vendredi: Halima! Is the dish ready for Friday?
textes.Halima a des mains qui savent tout faire: Halima has hands that can do anything, and a tongue that misses nothing. She's my best friend here. She says I break more bowls than a pirate. Not true. A few less.
textes.Halima fait les meilleures cruches de la: Halima makes the best jugs on the coast. My pirates break three a week. She charges me double. I pay, and I charge them back. A real businesswoman, that girl.
textes.Halima tourne mes plats à tajine, et le: Halima throws my tajine dishes, and the big Friday dish is hers. A one-of-a-kind piece. I don't lend it to anyone. Not even to her.
Halima is my sister Rqia's daughter. Golden hands, and a head harder than her jugs. I'd like to marry her off. She'd like me to be quiet. Neither of us will manage.
textes.Halima… Elle tourne des cruches et elle: Halima… She turns jugs and she turns my head. She says I fib a little. She smiles at me anyway. One day, I'll take her to sea on the Whale.
textes.Halo a accueilli un visiteur sans moi, a: Halo welcomed a visitor without me, with his four-minute speech, with no official proofreading. I came running, toga in hand, with my eleven-minute speech. The visitor had already left. Halo and I gave our speeches to each other. We applauded.
textes.Halo dit qu'il faut goûter votre thé ste: Halo says I should taste your stellar tea.
textes.Halo fait un discours de quatre minutes: Halo gives every visitor a four-minute speech. I timed it: four minutes and seventeen seconds. I haven't told him. It would upset him. And he'd make it longer.
textes.Halo m'a dit que le secret de l'accueil,: Halo told me the secret of welcoming is that people smile. I asked him how you make people smile. He answered: “You say welcome until they crack.” I tried it on Volt. He cracked after thirty-two times. He smiled. Then he said “grmbl.”
textes.Halo m'envoie m'inscrire au registre des: Halo sent me to sign the visitors' register.
textes.Halo me laisse dessiner sur son belvédèr: Halo lets me draw on his lookout every morning. In return, I listen to him. He talks a lot. I ask him to be quiet for the tricky bits. He goes quiet. Almost. It's a good compromise.
textes.Halo me poursuit dans toute la ville pou: Halo chases me all over the city to give me his welcome speech. I hide in the Hanging Gardens, among the green plants. I'm green. It's the perfect camouflage. Except I wobble. Plants don't wobble. He found me three times. Three times, I went “blorp” and scooted off.
textes.Halo me poursuit depuis trois semaines p: Halo has been chasing me for three weeks to give me a welcome speech. I'm hiding. I'm green, and there are lots of green plants in the Gardens. It's the perfect camouflage. Blorp.
textes.Halo prétend faire des discours. Quatre: Halo claims to make speeches. Four minutes! That's not a speech, that's an introduction. But I admit he says “welcome” with great sincerity. Forty times.
textes.Halo prétend que son discours de bienven: Halo claims his welcome speech is the longest on Astralys. Four minutes! Mine lasts eleven minutes. With the introduction. Without the introduction, it lasts nine and a half minutes. Which is still longer. Ahem.
textes.Halo veut me faire un discours de bienve: Halo wants to give me a four-minute welcome speech. I've been hiding for three weeks. It's not that I don't like him. It's that four minutes means four thousand fewer photos.
textes.Halo, comment devient-on visiteur d'Astr: Halo, how does one become a visitor to Astralys?
textes.Halo, le gardien du Portail d'accueil, v: Halo, the keeper of the Welcome Gate, wants you to become an official visitor of Astralys, as tradition demands: get yourself entered in the register by Écliptique, taste the star tea at Gloubi's, then go and greet Elder Astrée.
textes.Halte ! (Il dégaine, sa cape claque au v: Halt! (He draws his sword, his cape snaps in the wind… the wind drops, and so does the cape.) I am Rodrigue, swordsman of the Guild. And you… I can feel it… you shall be my RIVAL. Don't argue: it's destiny. I decided it this morning.
textes.Halte ! Casque ? Pas de casque. Bon. Res: Halt! Helmet? No helmet. Right. Stay behind the white line. Ludovic Grisou, foreman of the Crystal Mines. Rule number one: safety. Rule number two: safety. Rule number three: say hello to the Old Girl. The rock. She likes to be greeted.
textes.Halte ! Hum hum. Je veux dire : bienvenu: Halt! Ahem. I mean: welcome. Écliptique, Chief of Protocol of the Astralys Council, guardian of precedence, master of bows and president of the Speeches Committee. According to protocol, you must now bow. No, not like that. Not like that either. Right. That'll do.
textes.Halte ! Hum, je veux dire : bonjour, hon: Halt! Ahem, I mean: good day, honoured visitor!
textes.Halte ! Macaroni, gardien du Couvercle S: Halt! Macaroni, keeper of the Sacred Lid. Once: prayer. Twice: dinner. Three times: NEVER. Got it? Repeat. … Good. You may pass.
textes.Halte ! Qui va là ? … Ah, ma recrue. Rep: Halt! Who goes there? … Ah, my recruit. At ease.
textes.Halte ! Qui va là ? … Oh, un visiteur. P: Halt! Who goes there? … Oh, a visitor. Sorry, force of habit. Want to see my armor?
textes.Halte ! Qui va là ? … Un aventurier ! Je: Halt! Who goes there? … An adventurer! Allow me to introduce myself: I, SIR TANCRÈDE DE TOURNEVENT! Vanquisher of the Mist Giant, the Seven-Tailed Serpent and the Great Frost Bear! … In the fog. There was a lot of fog. Nobody saw anything. But it was magnificent.
textes.Halte ! Un grand. Sur NOTRE plage. Bramm: Halt! A tall one. On OUR beach. Bramm Poing-de-Roc, guard of the Great Gate. Nobody enters Forgefer uninvited.
Halt! … Ah, it's you. Go on through.
textes.Halte ! … Ah, c'est toi. Trois, quatre…: Halt! … Oh, it's you. Three, four…
Halt! … Ah, an adventurer. Move along.
textes.Halte ! … Pardon. L'habitude. Capitaine: Halt! … Sorry. Force of habit. Captain Pyrus, of the Pandémonia Guard. Welcome to the city. Here, the first rule is to be kind. The second is not to swim in the Circle of Fire.
textes.Halte, noble inconnu ! Écoutez mon nom !: Halt, noble stranger! Hear my name!
textes.Halte, étranger. Tu es à Aztlán, au cœur: Halt, stranger. You are in Aztlán, in the heart of the Lake of the Moon. I am Cuauhtli, the Eagle, high priest of the Great Temple. Up there keep watch Tlaloc, who gives the rain, and Huitzilopochtli, who leads the sun into battle.
textes.Halte-là ! Je recrute. Tu veux être dans: Halt! I'm recruiting. Want to join my crew?
textes.Halte-là ! Je suis la capitaine Yasmine,: Halt! I am Captain Yasmine, terror of the seven seas and of Lantern Square! … Want to play?
textes.Halte-là, moussaillon ! Je suis Gnocchi,: Halt, cabin boy! I am Gnocchi, the most terrible pirate on Al Dente Island! (His colander falls over his eyes. He pushes it back up.) I'm also a novice. And a singer. And when I grow up, I'll be a volcano.
textes.Halte-là, terrien. Anne-Rose Corbeau, ca: Halt right there, landlubber. Anne-Rose Corbeau, captain of the Requin Borgne. The finest galleon on Balafre, and the fastest. If you've come for my treasure, it's at the bottom of the sea. If you've come for my troubles, I've got plenty to spare.
textes.Halte. Capitaine Ferdinand, de la garde: Halt. Captain Ferdinand, of the Montjoie guard. Nothing to report. Well… three escaped turnips, a hat on a roof, a slime in the well and Gilles asleep. As usual. Nothing to report.
textes.Halte. Odon, gardien du Donjon des Mille: Halt. Odon, keeper of the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps. Want to go down? I write your name in the register, and the deepest floor you reach. If you don't come back up, I write that too. But you'll come back up. There are return crystals on every floor.
textes.Halte. Tu es sur la Skala, le bastion de: Halt. You are on the Skala, the bastion of Tazira. Caïd Hamza, chief of the guard. Look all you like, but don't touch the cannons, and don't climb on the battlements.
textes.Halte. Tu es sur le pont du Léviathan, e: Halt. You're standing on the deck of the Léviathan, and this deck is our home. I am Morgane Kerhervé, admiral of Carène. Who sent you, and across which sea?
textes.Halte. Un humain… avec la boussole de Ly: Halt. A human… with Lyra's compass. Fine. Thalion Ventvif, guard of Bois-Doré. I've got my eye on you.
textes.Halte. Une question. Si tu voyais des lu: Halt. A question. If you saw lights in the caves at night, what would you do?
textes.Halte. Une question. Si tu voyais quelqu: Halt. A question. If you saw something strange in the forest, what would you do?
textes.Halte. … Bon, tu as l'air inoffensif. Cr: Halt. … All right, you look harmless. Croc-Gris, guard of the Watchtower. From up there, I can see the whole forest, and the whole forest knows I can see it. Welcome to Ramure. No mischief.
textes.Hamid ? Une voix de baleine enrhumée. Il: Hamid? A voice like a whale with a cold. He sings at sea to bring in the fish. I say the fish come to make him stop. But he sings loud, I'll give him that. Almost as loud as me.
textes.Hamid ? Une voix de tempête et un cœur d: Hamid? A voice like a storm and the heart of a sardine. He thinks I don't see where my rum ends up. I see everything in my place. Even the palm trees.
textes.Hamid chante comme dix pêcheurs à la foi: Hamid sings like ten fishermen at once. A genius, I tell you. A genius who's far too loud: next to him, my drum turns into a whisper.
textes.Hamid, notre chanteur. Une voix qui pass: Hamid, our singer. A voice that carries past the channel. He sings too loud, and he knows it. But when he sings softly, once a year, the whole square falls silent.
textes.Hapou ! Combien de chèvres, cette fois ?: Hapou! How many goats this time?
textes.Hapou fait pousser mon lin, sur la rive: Hapou grows my flax, on the south bank. He grumbles, he worries, he talks to crocodiles. But his flax is the best on the river. And he has a farmer's heart: slow, but solid.
textes.Hapou me vend son orge, râle sur les cro: Hapou sells me his barley, grumbles about crocodiles and pays for his beer in onions. He looks as grumpy as a donkey that missed its nap, but he gave me my best beer ever. Without meaning to.
textes.Hapou paie sa bière en oignons. Une bott: Hapou pays for his beer in onions. One bunch per jar, counted in front of me, onion by onion. One evening, one was missing. He went all the way back to his field, on the other side of the river, to fetch it. He came back after dark, very dignified, onion in hand. Since then, I give him one onion's credit. He refuses.
textes.Hapou parle aux crocodiles. Il dit que ç: Hapou talks to the crocodiles. He says it calms them down. I say it makes them laugh.
Hapou talks to crocodiles. He says it calms them down. I say it makes them laugh. But he brings me the best silt from the river. So I listen to him talk. To crocodiles.
textes.Hapou râle tout le temps et il fait le b: Hapou grumbles all the time and plays the hero with the crocodiles. Me, I play the hero from my boat. Everyone has their own spot for being brave. But he's my friend: he comes when you call him.
textes.Hapou. Abouti a déterré son manteau ?: Hapou. Has Abouti dug up his coat yet?
textes.Hapou. Ta borne est toujours à sa place: Hapou. Is your boundary stone still in its place?
textes.Hapou. Ton crocodile d'argile tient bon: Hapou. Is your clay crocodile holding up?
textes.Hapy, c'est le dieu de la crue. Moi c'es: Hapy is the god of the flood. I'm Hapou. My father thought it was funny. Me, I have to explain every single day that I don't make the river rise.
textes.Hardi ! La pause est finie ! La gloire,: Onward! The break is over! Glory never takes a break!
textes.Hardi ! Mon épée est à vous ! Ma cape au: Onward! My sword is yours! My cape too! Well, it's mine, but it's coming.
textes.Hardi ! Plus on descend, plus l'exploit: Onward! The deeper we go, the greater the deed! The colder it gets, too. Onward anyway!
textes.Hassan ? Toujours content. Ça m'agace. N: Hassan? Always cheerful. It annoys me. Our wives are sisters, so we put up with each other. And I have to admit his tea is drinkable.
textes.Hassan croit que son thé fait la paix à: Hassan thinks his tea keeps the peace in Tazira. Ha! It's my rum. His hot mint water I leave to the sick and the caravan traders.
textes.Hassan fait un thé magnifique. Haut, mou: Hassan makes magnificent tea. High, frothy, hot. It just needs a pinch of salt. I told him so. Since then, he looks at me funny. Artists are touchy.
textes.Hassan me sert le thé depuis vingt ans,: Hassan has been serving me tea for twenty years, and we play draughts every afternoon. I often win. He says it's luck. Hassan is a polite man.
textes.Hassan sert son thé sur ma terrasse et o: Hassan serves his tea on my terrace and gives away the fourth glass. On MY terrace. I'd charge him rent, but he'd serve me a tea to apologise, and I wouldn't be able to shout anymore.
textes.Hautefond, la Place de la Colonne. Le ci: Hautefond, Column Square. The sky! It's awfully bright up here.
textes.Hautefond, la ville de pierre blonde, au: Hautefond, the town of blond stone, around its Great Column
textes.Hautefond, mes chers concitoyens, c'est: Hautefond, my dear fellow citizens, is the most beautiful town in the archipelago! Blond stone, blue slate, brass and copper! Column Square, the Upper Town, the Middle Town, the Lower Town… a town in tiers, like a fine cake. With a Column for a candle.
textes.Hautefond, tout en bas : les toits d'ard: Hautefond, far below: the blue slate roofs, the Great Market with its colourful awnings, the shining Column.
textes.Head: Head
textes.Hector ? Un grand qui a porté mon charbo: Hector? A big'un who carried my coal for three years without complaining. Well, complaining, but carrying it. He forges decently. For a big'un. Hmph.
textes.Hector est un bon artisan, je ne dis pas: Hector is a good craftsman, I won't say otherwise. But a blacksmith who “never has the time” for a clock is like a baker who's never hungry.
textes.Hector fabrique des choses qui font peur: Hector makes frightening things and sells them at frightening prices. I prefer jams. And my prices are fair.
textes.Hector me forge mes griffes de sertissag: Hector forges my setting prongs: tiny little steel claws, to hold a stone without hurting it. The first time, I looked at them through the loupe and asked him where he'd learned to work so fine. He grunted: “With the dwarves.” Then, lower: “For once, it wasn't for an axe.”
textes.Hector, c'est l'homme qui a forgé mon en: Hector is the man who forged my sign and has been drinking it for twenty years. He talks little, grunts well, and sings out of tune while hammering. A true friend. He'll never say so.
textes.Hector, l'armurier, fabrique des choses: Hector, the armourer, makes frightening things. I prefer jam.
textes.Hector. Vous avez levé les yeux, ce mati: Hector. Did you look up, this morning?
textes.Hein ? Ah, la mer… C'était un mardi…: Eh? Ah, the sea… It was a Tuesday…
textes.Hein ? Dis-moi, toi : tu préfères les hi: Eh? Tell me, you: do you prefer true stories or made-up ones?
textes.Hein ? Je ne t'ai rien demandé, moi. Ici: Eh? I didn't ask you for anything. Down here, we only ask one thing: don't bang on the glass. The jellyfish are very sensitive.
Eh? I didn't ask you for anything. Down here, we only ask one thing: don't hang about on the rails when Bernadette whistles.
Eh? I didn't ask you for anything. Up here, we only ask one thing of you: don't throw anything over the railing.
Eh? I didn't ask you for anything. Around here, we only ask one thing of you: hold the handrail in the cabin.
textes.Hein ? Je ne t'ai rien demandé, moi. Tu: Eh? I didn't ask you for anything. You're mixing me up with the Assembly: there, everyone asks for everything. All at once. And then we vote.
Huh? I never asked you for anything. You're thinking of the Guild board: now that one asks for things all the time.
Huh? I didn't ask you for anything. You're mixing me up with another demon: with our horns, we all look a bit alike.
Huh? I didn't ask you for anything. Maybe you're mixing me up with an assembly: there, everybody asks for everything at the same time.
textes.Hein ? La Grande Liftière d'en bas ? Cap: Eh? The Grand Liftkeeper down below? Capucine Rouage? I knew her when she was tiny! Well, I knew her grandmother when she was tiny. Well, I heard about her. Anyway, I know her very well.
textes.Hein ? La mer ? Ah, la mer…: Eh? The sea? Ah, the sea…
textes.Hein ? Les Mines de Cristaux ? J'y desce: Eh? The Crystal Mines? I used to go down there with my father, eighty years ago! … The line has reopened? Then I'm going back. With my ear trumpet. They say the liftkeeper down there is even deafer than me. We'll have a good laugh.
textes.Hein ? Mon humeur ? Oui, il fait beau. C: Eh? My mood? Yes, lovely weather. What? Ah, my mood. Good, good. Forgive me, I'm hard of hearing. Except when people talk about choux buns. Then I hear perfectly.
textes.Hein ? Oui ! … Non. Quel jour sommes-nou: Eh? Yes! … No. What day is it?
textes.Hein ? Quelle heure est-il ? … Zzz…: Huh? What time is it? … Zzz…
textes.Hein ? Quoi ? Je ne dormais pas ! Je… j': Huh? What? I wasn't asleep! I… I was listening to the millstone. It sings better at night.
textes.Hein ? Quoi ? Je ne dormais pas ! Je… ré: Eh? What? I wasn't asleep! I was… meditating to the music.
textes.Hein ? Quoi ? Un grand ! Pardon, je croy: Eh? What? A tall one! Sorry, I thought it was a rockfall. Grimli Pic-Rouillé, miner. The oldest miner in the oldest mine.
textes.Hein ? Tu l'entends aussi ? Boum… boum…: Eh? You hear it too? Boom… boom… Oh, no, you mean cave-ins. Yes. Me too. Especially the ones I cause myself.
textes.Hein ? Tu pars ? Ah. Bon vent, alors !: Eh? You're leaving? Ah. Fair winds, then!
textes.Hein ?! Quoi ? … Ah, c'est un rêve. Bonn: Huh?! What? … Ah, it's a dream. Good night, dream.
textes.Henri ? Ah, ton champignon ! Oui, Pépin,: Henri? Ah, your mushroom! Yes, Pépin, it's glowing.
textes.Heures de service sans panne : un millio: Hours of service without a breakdown: one million and fifty thousand. Next overhaul: when needed. The Levitator doesn't seem to be in any hurry.
textes.Heureuse ! Le vert est revenu, et avec l: Happy! The green is back, and with it, the smell of moss. I didn't know a colour could have a smell. Green smells lovely.
textes.Heureuse comme une jeune fille. Toutes l: Happy as a young girl. Every hour, the bell sings.
textes.Heureuse. La graine dort dans la terre d: Happy. The seed sleeps in the soil of the clearing. In a thousand years, a new Yggdrasil will watch over you.
textes.Heureuse. La lumière est revenue, les en: Happy. The light is back, the children play on the canal bridges. A queen asks for nothing more.
textes.Heureuse. Les mandariniers du Verger des: Happy. The mandarin trees in the Lamp Orchard have all blossomed at once. The whole dome smells of orange blossom. Well, a little: down here, the air wipes away scents. But if you put your nose right up to a flower, you can smell it. You just have to come close. Like with people.
textes.Heureuse. Mes tomates sont rouges, mes b: Happy. My tomatoes are red, my basil is green, and the volcano sent down a little ash last night. They adore ash. It's like chocolate to them.
textes.Heureuses comment ? Sois précis, je note: Happy how? Be precise, I'm taking notes.
textes.Heureuses… (Il note.) Je ne peux pas le: Happy… (He makes a note.) I can't prove it. Nor can I disprove it. And when I hear her in the evening, I'm happy too. Perhaps it's catching. Hypothesis accepted.
textes.Heureux. Vraiment heureux. C'est la prem: Happy. Really happy. It's the first time I've said that without tapping nervously. (Tap-tap.) Well. Almost.
textes.Heureux… (Elle note dans un carnet.) Hyp: Happy… (She jots it in a notebook.) Hypothesis number forty-seven: “Crystals glow because they're happy.” I can't prove it. I can't disprove it either. I'm keeping it.
textes.Heyyy ! Bienvenue, frérot ! Ici, une seu: Heyyy! Welcome, bro! Only one rule here: we dance and we smile!
textes.Hi hi ! Mais non, t'es à Pandémonia ! Re: Hee hee! No you're not, you're in Pandémonia! Look: there's the market, there's the Academy, and over there, that's the volcano. There, now you're found!
textes.Hi hi ! Sage réponse. Moi, j'ai dormi tr: Tee hee! A wise answer. Me, I've slept three hundred years in all, in little pieces. That's the secret of my fresh complexion.
textes.Hi hi ! Tu veux que je me retransforme ?: Hee hee! Want me to turn back? No? Shame, I was a very beautiful teapot.
textes.Hi hi ! Ça, c'était la chanson du crapau: Hee hee! That was the song of the toad with a cold!
Hic! It's the grog. It feeds him.
textes.Hic ! Dis, {surnom}… qu'est-ce que tu bo: Hic! Say, {surnom}… what do you usually drink?
textes.Hic ! Déjà ? Midi de quel jour, capitain: Hic! Already? Noon of which day, captain?
textes.Hic ! Déjà ? Un dernier verre, le Muet !: Hic! Already? One last drink, Silent One!
textes.Hic ! Il paraît que les squelettes du fo: Hic! They say the skeletons in the fort drink rum. It goes right through. What a waste!
textes.Hic ! Le Muet ! On rentre ?: Hic! Silent One! Shall we go home?
textes.Hic ! Merci, Mama ! Le meilleur du monde: Hic! Thanks, Mama! The best in the world!
textes.Hic ! Merci, Scarlett ! Il galope bien ?: Hic! Thanks, Scarlett! Is he galloping well?
textes.Hic ! Pardon. Mon père était tonnelier,: Hic! Sorry. My father was a cooper, in a village full of apple trees. He made the finest barrels in the land: you could roll them from the top of the hill and they'd reach the bottom without a scratch. I rolled down the hill too. I reached the bottom covered in scratches. That's how we found out I wasn't a barrel.
textes.Hic ! Salut, toi ! Tonneau ! Pas parce q: Hic! Hi there! Tonneau — that's Barrel! Not 'cause I'm fat! 'Cause I'm… full! Hic! Fancy a drink?
Yesterday! It hasn't moved an inch.
textes.Hier, Cradoc est tombé de son monocycle: Yesterday, Cradoc fell off his unicycle into the fountain. We all applauded. With our wings. It makes a breeze.
textes.Hier, Quark est passé à travers moi quar: Yesterday, Quark walked through me forty-two times during the tour. On the forty-second, he stopped in the middle of me and said “Boo!” from the inside. My circuits made an unknown noise. The Professor says it was a laugh. Beep. Function not installed.
Yesterday, Quark walked through me forty-two times. I counted. It's a record. I added it to the tour: “Here, Quark walked through the guide.”
textes.Hier, c'était une sardine. Les sardines,: Yesterday it was a sardine. Sardines are dim.
textes.Hier, j'ai dit à Gunnar : « Ça fait troi: Yesterday, I said to Gunnar: “You've been drinking the same mug for three years.” He went red right up to his ears and talked to me about his shield for an hour. He has a very fine shield. I know: he's described it to me forty times. One day, I'll ask him why he comes. Not just yet.
textes.Hier, j'ai remplacé le batteur. J'ai tap: Yesterday, I filled in for the drummer. I hit softly. The bass drum broke anyway. I apologised to it. Copeau fixed it. It forgave me, I think.
textes.Hier, j'ai trouvé un papier glissé sous: Yesterday, I found a note slipped under the shop door: “Order: wings for a child, age 9 size. Paid: one gear biscuit.” The biscuit was stuck underneath with jam. I kept the biscuit and replied: “Order refused. Come back in twenty years.” The next day, another note: “Ten.”
textes.Hier, je suis passé à travers l'Hologuid: Yesterday, I ran through the Hologuide forty-two times during his tour. On the forty-second, I stopped right in the middle of him and went “Boo!” from the inside. His circuits made a very weird noise. The Professor says it was a laugh. The Hologuide says it wasn't. But he blinked.
textes.Hier, le remplaçant à la batterie, c'éta: Yesterday, the stand-in drummer was Boulon. He broke the bass drum. Gently. He apologised to it.
textes.Hier, une araignée de cristal m'a fait p: Yesterday a crystal spider gave me a fright. I dropped everything! My drops rolled everywhere: into the Hall of Prisms, the garden, the cave… Would you bring me back {manque}? They shine, you'll see them.
textes.Hilaire ! Je t'ai dessiné dans une greno: Hilaire! I drew you inside a frog!
textes.Hilaire ! Toujours cent quarante ?: Hilaire! Still a hundred and forty?
textes.Hilaire a cent lignes dans mon registre,: Hilaire has a hundred lines in my register, all “floor 1”. He goes down, he slips, he comes back up laughing. He's never given up. I've known rank-A heroes with less courage than him.
textes.Hilaire a un tiroir rien qu'à lui, sous: Hilaire has a drawer all to himself under my counter. Twelve years of records, complaints and failed contracts. It's the thickest drawer in the Guild, and the most cheerful.
textes.Hilaire donne les meilleurs conseils de: Hilaire gives the best advice in the Guild. And then he does the exact opposite. It's super handy: that way, I know what to do, and what not to do.
textes.Hilaire est descendu au premier étage ce: Hilaire has gone down to the first floor a hundred times. The register says: “floor 1, slipped”. A hundred times. I offered to write “floor 1, very consistent” instead. He was touched.
textes.Hilaire est rang F depuis douze ans. Dou: Hilaire has been rank F for twelve years. Twelve years! I've seen him fail contracts a child could pull off. But I've never seen him give up. That's what an adventurer is.
textes.Hilaire m'a donné un conseil, à mes débu: Hilaire gave me some advice when I started: “Aim a little left of the wind.” I haven't missed since. I never told him it was thanks to him. I buy him a slice of cake every Friday. He thinks it's chance.
textes.Hilaire s'est fait avaler quarante-sept: Hilaire has been swallowed forty-seven times. I write it down. When he gets swallowed, I know there's a frog. It saves me going to look. It's a precious service.
textes.Hilaire veut la Chaumière des Glycines d: Hilaire has wanted the Wisteria Cottage for twelve years. He has a hundred and forty coins. He's sincere, honest, and he'd sleep soundly in that bed. If only he had a hundred and sixty coins more.
textes.Hilaire économise pour la Chaumière depu: Hilaire has been saving up for the Cottage for twelve years. He has a hundred and forty coins. I promised him he'd be the first to know if the price drops. I hope he never will be. The price won't drop. But I'm hoping for him.
textes.Hilaire, il rate tout, mais il donne des: Hilaire fails at everything, but he gives super good advice. I write it down in a journal. And I also write down what he does, so I can do the opposite. That makes two journals.
textes.Hilaire. La Duchesse est sortie ce matin: Hilaire. The Duchess came out this morning.
Hilaire. Best advice of my life. Worst adventurer on the island. Both at the same time. I like him.
textes.Hilaire. Tu as vu Gluant, en bas ?: Hilaire. Did you see Gooey, down there?
textes.Hilda ! Cette année, c'est ma barbe qui: Hilda! This year, my beard wins.
textes.Hilda ! Ta chèvre noire est sur le toit: Hilda! Your black goat's on Borin's roof.
textes.Hilda ! Ton fromage a encore bougé cette: Hilda! Your cheese moved again last night!
textes.Hilda ! Un corbeau, vite. Un message urg: Hilda! A raven, quick. An urgent message.
textes.Hilda connaît chaque chèvre par son nom: Hilda knows every goat by name and every raven by its mood. We cross paths on the slopes every day. We tell each other everything. Well, almost everything.
textes.Hilda dit que c'est elle qui a la plus b: Hilda says she has the finest beard on the mountain. I can't argue: she's right, and her crows agree with her.
textes.Hilda fait le meilleur fromage du monde: Hilda makes the best cheese in the world and she talks to crows. The crows answer. I heard it. She says they don't, but I heard it.
textes.Hilda garde mes corbeaux messagers. Elle: Hilda keeps my messenger ravens. She says I make them fly too much. A king needs news. And cheese. Especially at night.
textes.Hilda laisse ses chèvres me grimper dess: Hilda lets her goats climb on me. She says they like rocks. I'm not a rock. Well… not only.
textes.Hilda parle à ses corbeaux. Et ses corbe: Hilda talks to her ravens. And her ravens answer her. I heard them!
Hippolyte was my pupil, at the Institute. Then he became my master. Then he became absent-minded. He forgets to eat, he talks to a whale, and one day he dropped his tie into the Aquarium. He's the greatest scientist I know. And the gentlest.
textes.Hiro ! Tu as goûté ton bouillon ?: Hiro! Have you tasted your broth?
textes.Hiro a le cœur aussi chaud que son bouil: Hiro's heart is as warm as his broth. He thinks he taught Gaston everything. I let him believe it: it's good for a cook to be a little proud.
textes.Hiro me sert un bol tous les soirs. Je n: Hiro serves me a bowl every evening. I don't eat. I smell it. It reminds me of something. I don't know what. I'm still searching.
textes.Hisser le panier de la poulie du Grand-C: Hoist the basket on the Great Oak's pulley
textes.Hisser le panier de la poulie, sur la pl: Hoist the pulley basket, on the Great Oak platform, next to the Council House (or look inside it, down at the foot of the tree)
textes.Historique ? Je l'ai fini mardi !: Historic? I finished it on Tuesday!
textes.Hi… hi hi… rrrrr… (Il rit en dormant. Pu: Hee… hee hee… rrrrr… (He laughs in his sleep. Then he snores even louder.)
textes.Hm ! Comme les mouettes. Pas bête, ça. M: Hm! Like the seagulls. Not daft, that. Margot would agree. Seagulls never choose. They're right.
textes.Hm ? Ah, c'est toi qu'on appelle le voya: Hm? Ah, so you're the one they call the traveler?
textes.Hm ? Ah, c'est toi, le voyageur ? Assied: Hm? Ah, it's you, the traveller? Sit down. Here, silence tastes of basil.
Hm? Ah. Sorry, I was watching the horizon. Grégoire, lookout. I watch the sea for Carène. And the land too, now. You never know where trouble will come from.
textes.Hm ? Oh, pardon. Lucien Moreau, archéolo: Hm? Oh, sorry. Lucien Moreau, archaeologist. Professor. On holiday, officially. Unofficially, I'm looking for Atlantis.
textes.Hm ? Oh, un visiteur. Hulotte, astronome: Hm? Oh, a visitor. Hulotte, astronomer. Every night I climb to the treetop and count the stars. I'm up to four thousand two hundred and twelve. Or thirteen. You've made me lose count.
textes.Hm ? Un visiteur, au Belvédère. Ça faisa: Hm? A visitor, at the Lookout. It's been a while. Gaspard Fusain, watchman. I keep watch over the island from up here with my spyglass. I used to draw maps. Now I watch the grey.
textes.Hm hm. Tu es plus malin que mes petits-e: Hm hm. You're smarter than my grandchildren. … Look: they're all asleep. As usual. Go, traveler. And if you find the eyes… the Great Moai is waiting for you.
Hm what? Say it, for once.
textes.Hm. Alors il devrait flotter comme un bo: Hm. Then it should float like a cork.
textes.Hm. Alors tu sais ce que c'est. On la re: Hm. Then you know what it's like. You look at it, you turn round to point it out, and it's gone. Don't let anyone tell you that you dreamed it.
textes.Hm. Assieds-toi, {surnom}. Je parle à ma: Hm. Sit down, {surnom}. I talk to my boat. Everyone knows that. What nobody knows: what I tell her is meant for Khadija. “This morning she wore the blue headscarf. She was beautiful.” That sort of thing. In front of her, it won't come out. So I tell the Mabrouka. And the shells. The shells are for saying that too.
Hm. In pencil, that's a start.
textes.Hm. Au moins vous l'avouez. Mon fiancé é: Hm. At least you admit it. My fiancé was always late too. He said the sea doesn't wear a watch. … Don't pull that face, I'm not scolding you. Not much.
textes.Hm. Bien aussi. Les lignes deviennent de: Hm. Good too. Lines become waves, if you wait.
textes.Hm. Bien. (Il hoche la tête, longtemps.): Hm. Good. (He nods, for a long time.) Sit down. We'll listen to the sea.
textes.Hm. Bien. (Il sourit, presque.) La mer,: Hm. Good. (He almost smiles.) The sea holds you up. The sky lets you drop. Go tell Héloïse that. No, don't tell her. She'd laugh.
textes.Hm. Bien. Danse tant que tu as deux jamb: Hm. Good. Dance while you've got two legs. And choose carefully which window you sing under.
textes.Hm. Bien. Elles le méritent. Une machine: Hm. Good. They deserve it. A machine does what it's told. If it gets it wrong, someone got it wrong before it did.
textes.Hm. Bien. La mer est partout, même dans: Hm. Good. The sea is everywhere, even in pebbles.
Hm. Fair winds, {surnom}. And a fine sea.
Hm. Fine. I'll let it go this time.
textes.Hm. Bonne réponse. Le Roi, je l'attends: Hm. Good answer. The King, I've waited thirty years for. Dinner, not one minute. Shh, don't tell Caramel.
textes.Hm. Borée Givrelin. Maître du gel. Parle: Hm. Borée Givrelin. Master of frost. Speak softly: the lake is listening, and it doesn't like shouting.
textes.Hm. C'est plus simple, c'est vrai. Mais: Hm. It's simpler, true. But think of me next time: I might be just round the corner from you.
textes.Hm. C'est reposant, comme méthode. Lou f: Hm. That's a restful method. Lou does the same as you. That's what I'm here for. All right. Keep leaving things alone. I'll check for two.
textes.Hm. C'est un début. Le plus important, c: Hm. That's a start. What matters most is that it holds.
textes.Hm. Change-lui l'eau. Et arrête de lui d: Hm. Change her water. And stop giving her my name.
textes.Hm. Comme Ewen. Ça fait de bons capitain: Hm. Like Ewen. That makes good captains and bad cabin boys. In Carène, as long as you respect the ship, I ask nothing more of you.
Hm. Tomorrow, the part without arches.
Hm. Tell your perch to change its name.
Hm. Say hello to them from me.
Hm. Tell him thank you from me.
textes.Hm. Dis-lui que je l'aime bien aussi. De: Hm. Tell him I like him too. From a distance.
textes.Hm. Dis-moi, moussaillon : la mer ou le: Hm. Tell me, young deckhand: the sea or the sky?
textes.Hm. Dis-moi, {surnom}. Tu crois à la cha: Hm. Tell me, {surnom}. Do you believe in luck?
textes.Hm. Dis-moi, {surnom}. Tu sais marcher s: Hm. Tell me, {surnom}. Can you walk without a sound?
textes.Hm. Du vent ce soir. On sortira la Veuve: Hm. Wind tonight. We'll take the Widow out.
textes.Hm. Elle est en fer. Sinon, elle rouille: Hm. It's iron. Otherwise it rusts.
textes.Hm. Encore quelqu'un du Plancher. Pascal: Hm. Another one from the Floor. Pascal Pression, from the Residences. I'm warning you: the sun is too strong, the wind is too cool, the Station is too crowded, and the music from down below is too loud. Apart from that, welcome. No, really. Welcome.
textes.Hm. Et que ma jambe arrête de me gratter: Hm. And for my leg to stop itching. That's all.
textes.Hm. Et tes boudins, ils tiennent debout: Hm. And your coils, do they stand up?
textes.Hm. Eux, ils ont faim. Toi, tu as de l'o: Hm. They are hungry. You are proud.
textes.Hm. Fils de forgeron. À seize ans, un ma: Hm. Blacksmith's son. At sixteen, a steam hammer crushed my left arm. I forged my first iron arm myself. An arm that doesn't argue. My father said it was fine work. That's when I started preferring machines to people. Machines don't pity you.
textes.Hm. Garde ta boussole. Je navigue aux ét: Hm. Keep your compass. I sail by the stars.
textes.Hm. Gaston fait un bon café. Il a mis un: Hm. Gaston makes good coffee. He put a bow tie on my butler. A robot has no neck. I told him. He doesn't listen to me.
textes.Hm. Hm, hm. (Il prend le pot, le regarde: Hm. Hm, hm. (He takes the pot and examines it through the spyglass, from very close up, which is no use at all.) I wasn't dreaming. Well. In spring, the mountain heather will be purple again. I'll be able to draw it in charcoal. It'll be grey on the paper, but I'll know. Here: my old compass. It points north. Almost.
Hm. He's got a bow again.
textes.Hm. Il fait semblant. Il a toujours fait: Hm. He's pretending. He always pretended.
Hm. There's always someone there, {surnom}. A rock, a tree, an old house. They don't answer. But they notice. Try it. You'll see.
Hm. It was on the beach.
Hm. I know where it is.
textes.Hm. Kraxx. Armurier. Épées, haches, sabr: Hm. Kraxx. Armourer. Swords, axes, sabres. Solid stuff, forged by Ferronde, sold by me. You touch, you buy. You break, you pay. Atch… Atchoo! Sorry. It's the neighbour's pepper.
Hm. Your knot lesson is waiting.
textes.Hm. La meilleure apprentie que j'aie eue: Hm. The best apprentice I ever had. The Zéphyr is her and me. She mocked me in front of the whole city. We don't speak any more. Hm.
textes.Hm. La menthe de Lavande, du camp d'en f: Hm. Lavande's mint, from the camp across the way. I don't buy it. She gives it to me. Don't tell anyone.
Hm. Next time, I'll put it out.
textes.Hm. Le balayeur qui chantait, c'est moi: Hm. The singing sweeper — I'm the one who threw it away. The night of the unveiling, over the railing. I thought Héloïse was mocking me in front of the whole city. It was my song. The one I hummed when she was learning to weld. She'd kept it, note by note. You don't keep what you're mocking. I understood too late. I'm looking for it. To hear it one more time.
Hm. So did the lake, I'll have you know.
Hm. The lake hasn't finished thinking about it.
textes.Hm. Le marin. Viens, j'ai une corde à to: Hm. The sailor. Come, I've got rope to twist.
textes.Hm. Le port est fait pour toi, alors. Le: Hm. The port is made for you, then. Noise is good. As long as you know where it stops.
textes.Hm. Le temps n'a pas fini d'y penser non: Hm. The weather hasn't finished thinking about it either.
textes.Hm. Les lettres. Bon. Il en faut, je sup: Hm. Letters. Fine. We need some, I suppose. Rosette needs them for the Gazette. And I need them to write down results. But results are numbers.
textes.Hm. Les mains de travailleur. Tu pourrai: Hm. Worker's hands. You could hold a rope. Maybe.
Hm. The tomatoes over there just turned red. Out of hurt feelings, I think. You should apologise.
textes.Hm. Maître Rivet. Les balayeurs, les por: Hm. Master Rivet. The sweepers, the porters, the café butler, the Colossus: that's me. All of them. Well, nearly all.
textes.Hm. Moi non plus, à vrai dire. Je crois: Hm. Neither do I, to be honest. I believe in jars that don't leak. But I sell scarabs. A man has to live.
textes.Hm. Montre tes mains. Mains de travaille: Hm. Show me your hands. Worker's hands, or passenger's hands?
textes.Hm. Mâchefer. Second. Tu montes à bord s: Hm. Mâchefer. First mate. You come aboard uninvited, you go back down over the rail. Got it?
textes.Hm. Note-la quand même. On ne sait jamai: Hm. Write it down anyway. You never know.
textes.Hm. On dit ça souvent. On verra. Asseyez: Hm. People often say that. We'll see. Sit by the lake for an hour, without talking. Then tell me again.
textes.Hm. On verra. Assieds-toi. Écoute les ga: Hm. We'll see. Sit down. Listen to the pebbles.
textes.Hm. On verra. Les feuilles sèches ne men: Hm. We'll see. Dry leaves don't lie. Walk ahead of me, one day. I'll tell you.
textes.Hm. On verra. Tes bottes disent que tu a: Hm. We'll see. Your boots say you went round the market twice this morning. But I believe you. Half.
textes.Hm. Pas glorieux. Mais vivant. Mieux vau: Hm. Not glorious. But alive. Better a live guard than a brave one. Don't tell Grisou.
textes.Hm. Peut-être. Ce matin, tout là-haut, a: Hm. Maybe. This morning, way up high, at the top of Mount Charcoal: a glint. Not a stone, not water. A pot. The purple one, I bet: number six, the heather's. But my legs don't climb the mountain anymore. First look through my spyglass, there, at the edge of the Lookout. If you see it too, then I'm not dreaming.
textes.Hm. Ptahmosé, potier. Khnoum, le dieu bé: Hm. Ptahmosé, potter. Khnum, the ram god, shaped people on his potter's wheel, just like I shape my jars. Only smaller. Want an amulet? A faience scarab brings good luck.
textes.Hm. Question de guetteur : toi, tu regar: Hm. A lookout's question: do you tend to look far away, or close up?
textes.Hm. Regarde avec les yeux. C'est moins c: Hm. Look with your eyes. It's cheaper.
textes.Hm. Remonter une fois sur un bateau. Jus: Hm. Get on a boat one more time. Just sail round the island. And come back.
Hm. You get home before dark.
textes.Hm. Retrouver le balayeur qui chante. L': Hm. Find the singing sweeper. Hear it once. Out of tune. Like me.
textes.Hm. Ses confettis épuisent mes balayeurs: Hm. Her confetti wears out my sweepers. Hours of extra work, every Fair day. They don't complain. Well. They wrote.
Hm. Tart. Fair enough. But no.
Hm. Your seeds have come up.
textes.Hm. Tiens. (Il te tend une sardine.) Man: Hm. Here. (He hands you a sardine.) Eat. Keeps the mouth busy.
textes.Hm. Toi qui parles beaucoup. Sardine ?: Hm. You who talk a lot. Sardine?
textes.Hm. Toi qui sais écouter. Les galets t'a: Hm. You know how to listen. The pebbles are waiting for you. Evenings are best.
textes.Hm. Toi, {surnom}, tu peux savoir. J'ai: Hm. You, {surnom}, you can know. I'm scared of heights. Never crossed a rope bridge. Never. I forge all their nails, and I take the stairs. Half an hour. At dawn, Bourru takes me up in the basket. Without a word. I close my eyes. Pomme-de-Pin thinks I look down on her bridges. It's not that. It's not that at all.
Hm. You. Take a look at the view.
textes.Hm. Toi. Tu as peur de quoi ?: Hm. You. What are you scared of?
textes.Hm. Toi. Tu parles beaucoup ?: Hm. You. Do you talk a lot?
textes.Hm. Ton épée. Tu la tiens à une main ou: Hm. Your sword. One hand or two?
textes.Hm. Trois pages sur les champignons. Pou: Hm. Three pages on mushrooms. For tomorrow.
textes.Hm. Tu me ressembles. Ce n'est pas un co: Hm. You're like me. That's not a compliment, little one.
textes.Hm. Tu sais faire un nœud, {surnom} ?: Hm. Can you tie a knot, {surnom}?
textes.Hm. Un dessinateur. Les détails, c'est l: Hm. A draughtsman. Details are where the paint pots hide. And the ants.
textes.Hm. Un guetteur. Le problème, c'est qu'o: Hm. A lookout. The trouble is, you trip over pebbles. I know, I've got a bruise to prove it.
Hm. One day, I'll win it back.
textes.Hm. Un navire rapide sans équipage, ça v: Hm. A fast ship with no crew goes very quickly… nowhere. You'll learn. I gave that answer too, at your age.
textes.Hm. Un nouveau. Léon Calfat, maître du P: Hm. A new one. Léon Calfat, master of Rigging Harbour. You came in on the ferry? Good boat. Bad paint. Not your fault. Welcome to Hautefond. Don't step on the ropes, they've got a nasty temper. So have I.
textes.Hm. Un port du nord. Une forge sur le qu: Hm. A northern port. A forge on the quay. My father on the hammer, me on the bellows. At sixteen, I was bending iron bars by hand. Mâchefer is the black slag left at the bottom of the forge when the iron's gone. My father called me that. As a joke. It stuck.
Hm. A robot has no neck.
textes.Hm. Un étranger. Tu es tout sec, ça se v: Hm. A stranger. You're bone dry, it shows. Here in Rainville, it rains every day, and that's just fine. I'm Mother Downpour. I make the neighbourhood's umbrellas. All full of holes, on purpose: an umbrella with no holes isn't being honest with the rain.
textes.Hm. Une gargouille qui ne mord pas, ça e: Hm. Is there such a thing as a gargoyle that doesn't bite?
textes.Hm. Une longue-vue et une loupe. C'est c: Hm. A spyglass and a magnifying glass. That's what you need. I've only got the spyglass.
textes.Hm. Une main qui travaille, une qui rega: Hm. One hand that works, one that watches. Has that changed?
Hm. One question at a time.
textes.Hm. Une question. Toi, tu choisis une la: Hm. A question. You: do you choose a blade for its beauty, or its sturdiness?
textes.Hm. Une question. Vous faites confiance: Hm. A question. Do you trust machines?
textes.Hm. Viens à la Corderie. Je t'apprendrai: Hm. Come to the Ropeworks. I'll teach you. It takes a lifetime.
textes.Hm. Voir un jour le bateau de ligne, les: Hm. To see one day the ferry, Héloïse's airships and the Column's cabins all set off at the same time, towards every world. And all come back. That's the most important thing, that they come back.
Hm. Your end of the bench.
textes.Hm. Vous avez raison. Elles sont faites: Hm. You're right. They're made by people. People make mistakes. I've made mistakes. Often. Hm.
textes.Hm. Vous et moi, on fait plus confiance: Hm. You and I trust machines more than people. One of us ought to try it differently.
textes.Hm. Vous, là : vous préférez le haut ou: Hm. You there: do you prefer up top or down below?
textes.Hm. Vous. Vous n'auriez pas vu un balaye: Hm. You. You haven't seen a singing sweeper, have you?
textes.Hm. Vous. Vous qui faites confiance aux: Hm. You. You who trust machines. Did the butler serve you at lunch today? He never spills a thing.
textes.Hm. Wilfried. Patient. Solide. Il a fait: Hm. Wilfried. Patient. Solid. He made a dog that wags its tail. Useless. But he put a heart in it. Hm. That's good.
textes.Hm. {surnom}. J'ai une sœur, sur le cont: Hm. {surnom}. I have a sister, on the mainland. I wrote her a letter twenty years ago. It's still in my pocket. Folded. I never found a boat. Or never looked. Hm. Knots are easier than words.
textes.Hm. {surnom}. Tu viens tordre une corde: Hm. {surnom}. Come to twist a rope?
textes.Hm. Ça dépend, tu disais. De la mer. Ell: Hm. It depends, you said. On the sea. She's calm today.
textes.Hm. Ça se revend combien, ça ?: Hm. How much would that fetch?
textes.Hm. Écoute, et oublie. Je ne veux pas le: Hm. Listen, then forget. I don't want Croc's ship. I want gold. Enough for a forge. A new anvil. And to go back north, see if my father's still alive. Ask his forgiveness. For the anvil. For the rest. If the crew knew… So I threaten to call a vote. A first mate who threatens, they fear. A son who's sorry, they don't.
textes.Hm. Écrou. Elle serre un écrou presque a: Hm. Écrou. She tightens a nut almost as well as I do. She refuses to build me a boat. Stubborn. It's a quality. In her.
textes.Hm. … Bien. Le silence, c'est ce qui res: Hm. … Good. Silence is what's left when everything has been said. The desert would open its door to you.
textes.Hm. … Comme moi. Entre les deux. Le port: Hm. … Like me. In between. The port by day, the desert by night. It's a good place. Not always comfortable.
textes.Hmm ? J'ai perdu le fil. Ça m'arrive. So: Hmm? I lost my train of thought. It happens. Often.
textes.Hmm ? Je ne t'ai rien demandé. Ou alors: Hmm? I didn't ask you for anything. Or else it was three hundred years ago, and it was someone else.
textes.Hmm ? Oh. Pardon, je regardais tes tache: Hmm? Oh. Sorry, I was looking at your freckles. Or your beauty spots. They look like the Great Bear. Zénith, astronomer at the Observatory. I see constellations everywhere. In the sky, in the soup, in people. You're a very pretty one.
textes.Hmm ? Un visiteur… de la surface ? Atten: Hmm? A visitor… from the surface? Wait, let me find a quill. I must write this down. “Day 365,214: a human.”
Hmm, a low over the Arches.
textes.Hmm. (Ses horloges se figent.) Bon. Je v: Hmm. (His clocks freeze.) Very well. I'll give you a clock. It runs ten minutes fast. You'll be on time without knowing it.
Hmm. This one tastes like spring water.
textes.Hmm. Encore un qu'Héloïse a ensorcelé. B: Hmm. Another one Héloïse has bewitched. Well. The sky is pretty. But when it rains, it's you it falls on. The sea is already wet.
textes.Hmm. La suite, il faut la mériter. Repas: Hmm. The rest has to be earned. Drop by again, we'll see.
Hmm. The rest has to be earned. Drop by again, we'll see.
textes.Hmm. Les coraux ont pâli. Pas les vasque: Hmm. The corals have paled. Not the basins.
Hmm. My grandmother used to say the same. Then she'd carve the path before anyone took it. Perhaps you're right. The stones hesitate when you walk by.
textes.Hmm. Tu comptes comment, cette fois ?: Hmm. And how are you counting this time?
textes.Hmm. Tu es bien indulgent. Attends un pe: Hmm. You're very forgiving. Just wait, you'll see.
textes.Hmm. Tu es de ceux qui vérifient. Comme: Hmm. You're one of those who check. Like Matthias: he writes my stories down in a journal and counts the whales. I like you anyway. A bit less, but I do.
textes.Hmm. Une loi de grand cœur. Sous la mont: Hmm. A law with a big heart. Under the mountain, everyone has a roof, but not always a place by the fire. I'll think about it. Royally. Ori, write that down.
textes.Hmm. Vous êtes bien indulgent. Attendez: Hmm. You're very forgiving. Just wait, you'll see.
textes.Hmm. Ça ne se forge pas, ça ne se boit p: Hmm. Can't forge it, can't drink it… but thanks.
Hmpf. And thank you. Write that down.
textes.Hmpf. Le grand. Toujours à taper fort et: Hmph. The big one. Still hitting hard and wrong?
textes.Hmpf. Toi. Tu marches sur des racines to: Hmph. You. You walk on roots all day long. Ever said thank you to them?
textes.Hmpf. Tu tiens à tes dents ?: Hmph. Fond of your teeth, are you?
textes.Hmpf. Un humain. Trop grand, trop bruyan: Hmph. A human. Too tall, too loud, too… human. Grommelot, keeper of the roots. What do you want?
textes.Hmpf. Un rêve. … Que les racines tiennen: Hmph. A dream. … That the roots hold for another four hundred years. And that one day somebody says thank you. Not to me. To the roots. Fine. To me too, a bit.
textes.Hmpf. Une lame d'elfe, quoi. Bon. Léger,: Hmph. An elf blade, then. Fine. I can do light too. I don't like it, but I can do it. Don't tell Fundin, he'd want to try.
textes.Hmpf. Ça ne se pèse pas, ça. … Mais c'es: Hmpf. You can't weigh that. … But it's pretty. Don't repeat it, people will think I'm sentimental. I'm not. Not in public.
textes.Hmpf. … Bon. D'accord. Le tressage est r: Hmpf. … Fine. All right. The braiding is a success. A LITTLE.
textes.Hmpf. … C'était pourtant ma plus belle g: Hmph. … And that was my best grimace.
Hmph. That's not in the books.
textes.Hnnnngh… La caisse ne bouge pas : quelqu: Hnnnngh… The crate won't budge: something is blocking it on the other side (or it's the edge of the storage area).
textes.Ho ! Ce qui tombe est à la grue !: Ho! What falls belongs to the crane!
Ho! What falls belongs to the crane.
textes.Ho ! Elle est tombée tout doucement. Com: Ho! It fell ever so gently. Like the piano.
textes.Ho ! Encore vous. Rien de tombé aujourd': Ho! You again. Nothing's fallen today. Well, almost nothing.
textes.Ho ! Firmin ! Ne vous penchez pas comme: Ho! Firmin! Don't lean out like that!
textes.Ho ! Gonzague, grutier. Je décharge les: Ho! Gonzague, crane operator. I unload the boats, and I pick up everything that falls off the cliff. And plenty falls, with all those inventors up there.
textes.Ho ! Je suis né au port, {surnom}, fils: Ho! I was born in the harbour, {surnom}, son of the old captain of the Petit Piston — the Little Piston, the tugboat. I learned to walk on her deck, not on the quay. We pushed the shepherds' wool barges to the warehouses, and the sparkling-apple boats from Carène to the pontoon. My father used to say: “A tug doesn't go anywhere. It helps the others arrive.”
textes.Ho ! Madame Bricolette. Le piano n'est t: Ho! Madame Bricolette. The piano's still not for sale.
textes.Ho ! Recommence, et tu finis à fond de c: Ho! Do that again and you'll end up in the bottom of the hold!
textes.Ho ! Toi, tu cherches les ennuis. Tu vas: Oi! You're looking for trouble. You're going to find it!
textes.Ho ! Un collègue ! Je le savais, vous av: Ho! A colleague! I knew it, you've got crane-operator pockets. If you ever run out of room, there's still a corner behind the piano.
textes.Ho ! Un petit nouveau ! Gros-Louis, seco: Ho! A new face! Gros-Louis, first mate of the Requin Borgne. If the captain says “jump”, I jump. If she says “thump”, I thump. You haven't done anything wrong, eh?
textes.Ho ! Un visiteur dans mon atelier ! Cora: Ho! A visitor in my workshop! Coralin, coral craftsman. I carve, I polish, I sculpt. Don't touch the red coral: it bites.
textes.Ho ! Une question de collectionneur : vo: Ho! A collector's question: do you keep everything, or throw things away?
Ho! Depends how far it rolls.
textes.Ho ho ! Avec une rose de soufre dedans,: Ho ho! With a sulphur rose in it, all the same!
textes.Ho ho ! Bienvenue aux Thermes de Soufre: Ho ho! Welcome to the Sulphur Baths! Bulle, master of the baths! Hot water, very hot water, and “mind-your-horns-don't-melt” water! It's all natural: the volcano does the heating, I just do the bubbles.
textes.Ho ho ! Comme au Parc des Brumes !: Ho ho! Just like in the Mist Park!
textes.Ho ho ! Dis-moi, {surnom} : toi, tu mang: Ho ho! Tell me, {surnom}: do you eat everything?
textes.Ho ho ! Dis-moi, {surnom} : ton bain, tu: Ho ho! Tell me, {surnom}: do you like your bath hot, very hot, or “mind-your-horns-don't-melt”?
textes.Ho ho ! Doucement, pour toi, c'est déjà: Ho ho! Gently, for you, is already a wave!
textes.Ho ho ! Et c'était magnifique, sœurette: Ho ho! And it was magnificent, little sis!
textes.Ho ho ! Et généreux comme toi !: Ho ho! And generous like you!
textes.Ho ho ! J'ai ajouté de la cannelle et du: Ho ho! I added cinnamon and herring!
textes.Ho ho ! Je savais qu'il y avait un secre: Ho ho! I knew there was a secret!
textes.Ho ho ! Je suis né dans un port du nord,: Ho ho! I was born in a northern port, in my mother's eatery, she cooked for the sailors. I grew up under the tables. The sailors let me dip a finger in their sauce, for luck. At five, I could recognise every soup in the port with my eyes closed. With my eyes open too, but that was less fun.
textes.Ho ho ! Je suis né prêt !: Ho ho! I was born ready!
textes.Ho ho ! La bonne réponse ! Une brioche c: Ho ho! The right answer! A hot brioche is a hug you can eat. At the Eternal Oven, they're always hot. That's the whole idea.
textes.Ho ho ! Le Grand Troc, c'est une chaîne,: Ho ho! The Great Swap is a chain, my friend. I give you this singing pebble: listen, when the wind passes through it, it whistles. You'll swap it for something better, then that something for something better still… Pomme-de-Pin, the carpenter, loves singing pebbles. Start with her. And at the end, come back and see me: I want to know what my pebble became!
textes.Ho ho ! Le trente-troisième, c'est l'amo: Ho ho! The thirty-third is love, isn't it?
textes.Ho ho ! Les patates, commis !: Ho ho! The potatoes, kitchen boy!
textes.Ho ho ! Merveilleuse ! J'ai trouvé une n: Ho ho! Marvellous! I've found a new spring, even hotter. I tested it with my fingertip. I can't feel the finger any more. But what a spring!
textes.Ho ho ! Moitié prix, Maman, comme toujou: Ho ho! Half price, Mum, as always!
Ho ho! Not today! Atch… no.
textes.Ho ho ! Qu'elles respirent, alors !: Ho ho! Let them breathe, then!
textes.Ho ho ! Ta vapeur t'attend, Tiburce ! Et: Ho ho! Your steam awaits, Tiburce! And your towel!
textes.Ho ho ! Toujours libre pour toi ! Attent: Ho ho! Always free for you! Watch out for the wave!
textes.Ho ho ! Tu as faim ? J'ai un ragoût de…: Ho ho! Hungry? I've got a stew of… of something.
textes.Ho ho ! Un client ! Jacquot Trois-Doigts: Ho ho! A customer! Jacquot Trois-Doigts, ship's cook of the Murène Noire. Three fingers, because the other two are in a soup somewhere out in the ocean. It was a very good soup.
textes.Ho ho ! Un thé ! Une pincée de sel ?: Ho ho! A tea! A pinch of salt?
textes.Ho ho ! Un vrai mineur ! Le noir, c'est: Ho ho! A real miner! The dark is just light that's sleeping. Come digging one day. You won't get lost. Well… less than me.
textes.Ho ho ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Tu as l'œil,: Ho ho! {dernier_cadeau}! You've got a good eye, for a tall one.
textes.Ho ho ho ! Le troisième bassin ?! Même m: Ho ho ho! The third pool?! Even I only dip a toe in! You're crazy. Or very brave. Both, and I love it.
textes.Ho ho ho ! Toi, tu as gagné un grog offe: Ho ho ho! You've earned yourself a free punch! Well… half of one. Oh, all right, a whole one. You said it with such a smile!
textes.Ho, Borée ! Ça mord, au lac ?: Ahoy, Borée! Are they biting at the lake?
textes.Ho, la Flammèche ! Tu as encore pris ma: Ahoy, Flammèche! Did you take my boat again?
textes.Ho, la petite. Ça mord, ce soir ?: Ho, girl. Are they biting tonight?
textes.Ho, le collègue qui garde tout ! Il m'es: Ho, my colleague who keeps everything! A right boot fell on me this morning. Want it? No? Me neither — I don't give anything away.
textes.Ho, matelot ! T'as trouvé Arcanelle tout: Ahoy, sailor! You found Arcanelle all by yourself? In the mist? Hats off. Mathurin Rame, ferryman. I'm no wizard, me: I row. That's magic too, ask my arms.
textes.Holà ! Sous terre, le moindre coup réson: Whoa! Underground, the slightest knock echoes all the way to the Fronde. They'll think we're answering them!
textes.Honnête. C'est ce que tout Carène fait,: Honest. That's what all of Carène does, with me. I don't mind. Bring me wood, that's all I ask.
textes.Honnête. C'est rare. La plupart des gens: Honest. That's rare. Most people say “towards danger”, and then I find them in the bakery. I prefer frankness.
textes.Honorine ! La pierre est toujours sur vo: Honorine! Is the stone still on your oven?
textes.Honorine ! Tu connais celle de Bernadett: Honorine! Do you know the one about Bernadette without me?
textes.Honorine Lanterne tient La Marmite, aux: Honorine Lanterne runs La Marmite, in the Strata. We've been swapping a recipe a month for twenty years. She puts in too much milk, I put in too much salt. We met for the first time at the reopening. We didn't shake hands: we gave each other a taste from our spoons.
textes.Honorine chante en pétrissant. C'est la: Honorine sings while she kneads. It's the most beautiful thing in Montjoie. I'll tell her one day. When I've caught my breath.
textes.Honorine connaît le Baron depuis l'enfan: Honorine has known the Baron since childhood. She knows he likes his bread a little overdone, saves the crust for last, and sings when he's happy. One day she slipped a little hat-shaped roll into the basket. The Baron kept it on his desk for a week. He wouldn't eat it. I had to confiscate it when it went mouldy.
textes.Honorine est seule au four ce matin. Il: Honorine is alone at the oven this morning. There are three loaves left to deliver: one to Mamie Rissole, at the Guild tavern; one to Aurore, at the castle; one to Gilles, at the North Gate. If she leaves the oven, everything burns.
textes.Honorine fait des chaussons avec mes pom: Honorine makes turnovers with my apples. The best on the island. She sings, she laughs, and she has the most lovestruck miller in the world at her door every morning. She doesn't even notice.
textes.Honorine fait sa soupe avec mes champign: Honorine makes her soup with my brown mushrooms. The glowing ones, she never touches: she says it's bad luck to eat a light. We agree on everything. Except salt.
textes.Honorine livre le pain du château tous l: Honorine delivers the castle's bread every morning, on time, singing. It's the only thing in my day that arrives exactly when it should. I'm infinitely grateful to her.
textes.Honorine m'a encore servi un bol de plus: Honorine served me one more bowl again. I wasn't hungry. I finished it anyway. That's the rule, at hers.
textes.Honorine m'a fait goûter deux chaussons,: Honorine had me taste two turnovers without telling me which apples were in them. I picked the best, obviously. She smiled oddly and said nothing. I'm sure it was mine. It could only be mine. Germaine tells the same story. She's lying, obviously.
textes.Honorine m'apporte le pain du temple cha: Honorine brings me the temple bread every morning, singing. It's the most beautiful hymn in Montjoie, and it smells of warm crust.
Honorine brings the temple's bread every morning, singing. It's the most beautiful hymn in Montjoie, and it smells of warm crust. I've never managed to sleep while she sings.
textes.Honorine m'envoie du pain tous les matin: Honorine sends me bread every morning. It smells so good I dream about it. Well, I think about it. Awake. Standing. She's the kindest person in Montjoie.
textes.Honorine, mon enfant ! Le pain de l'Aube: Honorine, my child! The Dawn bread?
textes.Honorine, à La Marmite, fait sa soupe av: Honorine, at La Marmite, makes her soup with my mushrooms. Not the glowing ones, mind: those we never eat, we just look at them. The others, the brown ones, are very plain and very good. They can't shine, but they can warm you up. Each to their own talent.
textes.Honorine, à La Marmite, la cantine des S: Honorine, at La Marmite, the Strata canteen, is my former apprentice. She puts in too much salt. I tell her every Tuesday. She answers that I don't put in enough. We're both right. We have lunch together every Tuesday.
textes.Honorine. Les éclairs du jeudi. Le reste: Honorine. Thursday éclairs. Everything else too. The best person on the island, with an oven.
textes.Honorine… Clovis est passé, ce matin ?: Honorine… did Clovis come by this morning?
textes.Honoré est mort il y a vingt-deux ans. L: Honoré died twenty-two years ago. The workshop, the tools and the unfinished automaton went to Ambroise, his apprentice. Me, I kept the gear. One single gear, against a whole workshop. That evening, I clenched it in my fist and swore to make something turn forever. By my gears! Well, by my gear. I only had the one.
textes.Honoré me parlait souvent du petit Firmi: Honoré often spoke to me of little Firmin. “He has a clockmaker's fingers, Ambroise. Finer than yours.” He was right: at eight, Firmin repaired the workshop music box all by himself, the one that had played out of tune for years. It played in tune. What today's Firmin does with his fingers, I'd rather not discuss.
textes.Hop ! Bondi. Champion de la Grande Cours: Hop! Bondi. Great Race champion, three years running. Want some advice? Don't follow me: all you'll see is my heels.
textes.Hop ! Dernier-né de la famille, quatorze: Hop! Youngest of the family, fourteen years after Trèfle. I grew up in the smell of bread, running round the oven. Still today, every morning, I help Mum and Dad in the rabbit vegetable garden, and I pick my three carrots. Not the biggest: the straightest. A straight carrot makes you run straight. It's science.
textes.Hop ! Dis-moi, toi : tu cours vite ?: Hop! Tell me, you: are you a fast runner?
textes.Hop ! Elle est debout. Il ne manque que: Hup! It's back up. Just the last one missing… again.
textes.Hop ! Encore une ! Le bateau a faim, ce: Hup! Another one! The boat's hungry this morning.
textes.Hop ! Jusqu'à la boulangerie. Tu pars av: Hop! To the bakery. You start first.
textes.Hop ! Qu'il s'ennuie. Il est bien, là-ha: Hop! Let it be bored. It's happy up there.
textes.Hop ! Salut, Grisou. Deuxième, aujourd'h: Hop! Hi, Grisou. Second place today?
textes.Hop ! Trois. Mon record tient toujours,: Hop! Three. Does my record still stand, Pépin?
textes.Hop ! Tu flottes au-dessus des feuilles,: Hop! You float above the leaves, among seeds falling upwards.
textes.Hop hop ! Encore toi ? Tu t'entraînes ?: Hop hop! You again? Training? Me too. All the time.
textes.Hop hop hop ! Bernard, soixante-sept ans: Hup hup hup! Bernard, sixty-seven years old, three laps of the island a day! What about you, do you run?
Hop hop hop! Sorry! Hop… hop.
textes.Hop hop hop ! Un coureur ! Demain, sept: Hop hop hop! A runner! Tomorrow, seven o'clock, at the fountain. I'll give you a ten-metre head start. Oh, all right, five.
textes.Hop hop hop… tout doucement. Bonne nuit: Hop hop hop… nice and quiet. Good night!
Up you go. Climb on, little ones.
textes.Horrible ? Ha ! Moi aussi ! Un clou, une: Horrible? Ha! Me too! A nail, once. Crunchy outside, iron-y inside. I don't recommend it. But it forges character.
textes.Hortense ! Oh là. Ne le dis pas trop for: Hortense! Oh my. Don't say it too loud, she's jealous of her name. But you do have the look of a boss. A little.
textes.Hortense ? La femme la plus fidèle de Po: Hortense? The most faithful woman in Port-Azur. I nod to her every evening from the quay. That's all I dare. I would so have liked to bring her something other than bad news.
textes.Hortense bat la mesure du pied, juste à: Hortense taps the beat with her foot, right to the second. She's my metronome, my first listener, and the only one who dares tell me I play too fast.
textes.Hortense dit que l'horloge de la mairie: Hortense says the town hall clock stopped the day her fiancé went to sea. It's sad and a little bit beautiful.
textes.Hortense est la femme la plus fidèle que: Hortense is the most faithful woman I know. She's been waiting for fifty years, and she oils her clock twice a day, whether it rings or not. I admire her. I don't know how she does it.
