Hortense is the memory of our square. She also counts my promises, which is far less pleasant.
textes.Hortense est sûre que c'est moi qui pose: Hortense is sure I'm the one leaving a sprig of lavender on her bench every morning. I've sworn on my satchel, on Raymond's head, on my boules. She doesn't believe me. Now she “gives back” the lavender: every morning I find it in the middle of my pitch, right where I point. Raymond finds it hilarious. Me, I keep it.
textes.Hortense voudrait que je répare son horl: Hortense wants me to fix her clock. She needs a new cogwheel. If someone brought me something to heat the forge… logs, and a few stones for the mould.
textes.Hortense écrivait au crayon, comme moi,: Hortense wrote in pencil, like me, but she never rubbed anything out. She said mistakes are proof that you tried. Her notebooks are in a chest, under my bed. Full of mistakes. They're the most beautiful notebooks in the world.
textes.Hortense, la gardienne de l'horloge, est: Hortense, the clock keeper, is in despair: nobody on the square knows what time it is any more.
textes.Hortense, ma vieille amie. Trente ans, j: Hortense, my old friend. Thirty years I knocked on her door. She thinks I'm the one leaving her lavender. It isn't me. I wish it were.
textes.Hortense, ma voisine de palier. Elle ne: Hortense, my next-door neighbour. She doesn't believe in my nonsense and she tells everyone so. But she looks at every stranger who crosses the square. The cards and I are waiting with her.
textes.Hou ! Bonjour ! Plumette, postière de Ra: Hoo! Hello! Plumette, postmistress of Ramure. Mail for the trees, mail for the ponds, mail for the other towns. It all leaves from the top of the Mother Oak. Got a letter? No? Well, write one, then!
textes.Hou ! Dis-moi, toi : tu as quelqu'un à q: Hoo! Tell me: do you have someone to write to?
textes.Hou ! Enfin la nuit ! Je me sens toute n: Hoo! Night at last! I feel brand new.
textes.Hou ! Et un mot pour moi ?: Hoo! And a note for me?
textes.Hou ! J'attends toujours ta lettre, tu s: Hoo! I'm still waiting for your letter, you know. I've already written the reply. Just in case.
textes.Hou ! Je suis la fille de Hulotte. Mon p: Hoo! I'm Hulotte's daughter. My father carried Ramure's post for thirty years. When I was tiny, I travelled in his satchel, among the letters, with just my head poking out. I knew every door before I could read. People gave me a hazelnut when they took their post. I was a bit like the stamp.
textes.Hou ! Je t'entends arriver, Pomme-de-Pin: Hoo! I can hear you coming, Pomme-de-Pin.
Hoo! Not yet. She's slow to reply.
textes.Hou ! Rien pour toi aujourd'hui. Mais de: Hoo! Nothing for you today. But tomorrow, maybe.
textes.Hou ! Toi qui écris à plein de monde : t: Hoo! You who write to loads of people: not forgetting anyone? I never forget an address.
textes.Hou ! Tu as écrit à la personne qui te m: Hoo! Did you write to the person you miss? My satchel always has room.
textes.Hou ! Un gland d'or ! Je le mettrai sur: Hoo! A golden acorn! I'll put it on my counter, it'll bring luck to the post. Here's a moon feather: it falls from our wings on full-moon nights. Which is to say every night, here. Pivoine is looking for some for her vials.
textes.Hou… Alors écris-lui ! Je m'occupe du re: Hoo… Then write to them! I'll take care of the rest. I won't read a thing, promise. I'll just listen a little, if it goes tick-tock.
textes.Hou… Bonsoir, petite. On monte ?: Hoo… Good evening, little one. Shall we climb?
textes.Hou… Dis-moi : tu as déjà compté les éto: Hoo… Tell me: have you ever counted the stars?
Hoo… And every evening, that's true.
textes.Hou… Je suis né à la Poste, tout en haut: Hoo… I was born at the Post Office, right at the top of the Mother Oak. As a child, I didn't sleep: I counted the lanterns on the bridges. A hundred and seventeen, the evening I turned six. A hundred and eighteen the next day: Mother Moon had put up a new one. Then one evening I looked up a little higher. The stars. There were far more of them. I never looked down again.
textes.Hou… Regarde ma longue lunette, {surnom}: Hoo… Look at my long telescope, {surnom}. Come closer. Look into it. … See? Nothing. It's a tube of rolled bark. There's no glass. I've never looked through a real lens. Céleste sends me calculations, whole pages of them. I answer with poems, because I don't know how to do anything else. I'm a little ashamed of it. Very.
textes.Hou… Tu sais pourquoi je travaille le jo: Hoo… Do you know why I work by day, {surnom}? Not just for the post. When I was little, I'd wait for night at the treetop, so my father would look at me. But he looked at the sky. Always the sky. So now I leave the night to him, with his stars. I don't share. I've never told him. A postmistress says nothing. Nor does a daughter, sometimes.
textes.Hou… Tu viens regarder le ciel ? Il est: Hoo… Have you come to look at the sky? It's very beautiful tonight. It's very beautiful every night.
textes.Hrmm ! La nacelle t'attend. Monte, monte: Hrmm! The basket's waiting for you. Climb in, climb in.
textes.Hrmm. Bien. Alors regarde en bas. C'est: Hrmm. Good. Then look down. It's pretty down there too.
textes.Hrmm. Bourru. Je garde la nacelle d'osie: Hrmm. Bourru. I keep the wicker basket lift: it goes up to the top of the Mother Oak, and comes back down. Climb in, wait a bit, and up you go. I pull the rope. Well, the pulley does. But I keep an eye on it.
textes.Hrmm. Grand-père Frêne a tressé la nacel: Hrmm. Grandpa Frêne wove the basket. Wicker and rope. After him, Father kept it. He talked to the passengers. A long time. They took the stairs. Me, a cub, I slept in it. At the treetop. In the sun. The wind rocked it. Best nap in the world. Hrmm. Still today.
textes.Hrmm. Monter Lilas à la cime. Au coucher: Hrmm. Take Lilas up to the treetop. At sunset. In the basket. Nobody else.
textes.Hrmm. Pas grave. Je tire doucement. Très: Hrmm. No matter. I pull gently. Very gently. Close your eyes.
textes.Hrmm. Toi, {surnom}. Tu gardes ça. Je ta: Hrmm. You, {surnom}. Keep this to yourself. I drum slowly on purpose. So the dance lasts. Lilas's dance. The slower it is, the longer she dances. I love her. For years. Never told her anything. Nothing. Just “Hrmm”. She must think I'm a drum.
textes.Hugo ? Mon mari. Le plus timide, le plus: Hugo? My husband. The shyest, most stubborn and kindest of men. He lost his wedding ring after ten days. I love him anyway. Even more, actually.
textes.Hugo a perdu son alliance dans le sable,: Hugo has lost his wedding ring in the sand, near the Coco Loco beach hut, where the waves come in.
textes.Hugo m'a acheté une rose rouge, la plus: Hugo bought a red rose from me, the most beautiful one, to apologise to Léa. An hour later, he brought it back: she hadn't taken it. He didn't know what to do with it. I put it in a vase on my counter, “for the time being”. For the time being until what, I have no idea. But I changed its water every morning.
textes.Hugo, c'est mon petit marié. Timide comm: Hugo is my little groom. Shy as a shrimp, but with a heart as big as my pot. He looks at his finger with every bite. There's a story behind it, and my soup is mixed up in it, I can feel it.
textes.Hugo, le jeune marié, m'a acheté une ros: Hugo, the young groom, bought a rose from me to apologise to Léa. She didn't take it. It must be serious.
textes.Hugo, le jeune marié. Un garçon timide c: Hugo, the young groom. A boy as shy as a rosebud, who had the misfortune to lose the one thing he mustn't. He came to me to make amends. Flowers don't fix everything. But they help.
Hugues! I can't remember which one it is.
textes.Hugues ! Vous ai-je déjà raconté mon cha: Hugues! Have I ever told you about my rabbit hat?
textes.Hugues ? Le plus grand aventurier de l'î: Hugues? The greatest adventurer on the island, and still the bony-kneed kid who was hungry. He cries too much. He eats well. That's what matters.
textes.Hugues est le plus grand aventurier que: Hugues is the greatest adventurer Montjoie has ever had. And the most sensitive. He cries at all my ceremonies. Even the ones I forget. Charming, charming!
textes.Hugues est un grand dadais qui pleure et: Hugues is a big lump who cries and exaggerates. But he's a real hero, a real one. I'll never tell him. It'd go straight to his beard.
textes.Hugues frappait, je portais. Il pleurait: Hugues hit things, I carried. He cried, I carried. He laughed, I carried. He's a great man. Heavy, too. I know: I've carried him.
Hugues says he defeated a dragon. I was there. Well, I was in the village when he came back. He was carrying the dragon under his arm. It was as big as a goat. But Hugues was trembling as if he'd defeated a mountain. It was a real feat, for a boy of nineteen.
textes.Hugues, je le nourris depuis qu'il avait: I've been feeding Hugues since he was fifteen with knobbly knees. Now he's the greatest adventurer in Montjoie. What do you think he owes it to? My pies. He knows it. He's scared of my ladle.
textes.Huile tes rouages, jeune homme. Et tes g: Oil your gears, young man. And your knees too, while you're at it.
textes.Huit heures ! C'est raisonnable. Moi, j': Eight hours! That's reasonable. Me, I sleep twelve. Plus four standing. That makes sixteen. That's a good number, isn't it?
textes.Huit pièces la chambre, thé du matin com: Eight coins a room, morning tea included. Caravaneers pay in dates; you don't even have dates.
textes.Huit secondes, c'est une éternité pour q: Eight seconds is an eternity for a man who knows how to think.
Eight. You forgot the little one.
textes.Hulotte compte les étoiles toute la nuit: Hulotte counts the stars all night. I look at them. We don't have the same method. He thinks I'm not serious enough. He's right, but that's no reason.
textes.Hulotte dit qu'il a vu une étoile tomber: Hulotte says he saw a star fall into the big pond. I tell everyone it was a firefly that had drunk too much moon tea. The whole market laughed. Hulotte didn't. He looked at me with his big round eyes, without a word, for a whole minute. I've never seen an owl so unamused. I'd sort of earned it.
textes.Hulotte monte à la cime toutes les nuits: Hulotte goes up to the crown every night to look at the stars. He never takes the basket. He flies. Well, he says he flies.
textes.Hulotte regarde le ciel, je regarde le s: Hulotte looks at the sky, I look at the ground. He calculates, I sniff. He says a star fell into the big pond. Me, I believe in tracks. Not in the sky.
textes.Hulotte voit dans le noir ! Il m'a dit q: Hulotte can see in the dark! He told me I had cake on my snout. In the dark!
textes.Hulotte. Il compte les étoiles. Il ne pr: Hulotte. He counts the stars. He won't take my basket. Never. Not for ten years. Hrmm. It's safe now. Very safe.
textes.Hulotte. Il monte la nuit avec une lante: Hulotte. He climbs at night with a lantern and a tube. From afar, he looks like a monster. He knows it. And he pokes his beak into things that are none of his business.
textes.Hum hum ! Mes chers concitoyens… ah, un: Ahem! My dear fellow citizens… ah, just the one citizen. Never mind: I shall be brief. Hector Bellevue, Burgomaster of Hautefond, Knight of the Order of the Gear, Steam Medallist, three-time honorary ribbon-cutter. Welcome! There. That was brief. For me.
textes.Hum hum ! Vous, là ! Approchez, je serai: Ahem! You, there! Come closer, I shall be brief!
Ahem. Eleven minutes, and I'm breathing.
textes.Hum hum. Selon le protocole, il est main: Ahem. According to protocol, it is now permitted to say “ooooh”.
Hmm. We'll need a new roof. Again.
textes.Hum. Merci. Je vais le… balayer. Non ! L: Hmm. Thank you. I'll… sweep it up. No! Keep it. I meant keep it.
textes.Humeur : cent pour cent. Batterie : cent: Mood: one hundred per cent. Battery: one hundred per cent. Enthusiasm: one hundred and four per cent. Error. Pleasant error.

Hmm… I don't see a boat.
textes.Hum… merci. C'est l'intention qui compte: Hmm… thanks. It's the thought that counts. I'll… give it to someone who needs it.
textes.Hum… merci. Je vais le ranger. Tout au f: Hmm… thanks. I'll put it away. Right at the back. Behind the eraser.
Hmm… thanks. I'll… put it aside. A long way from the pot.
textes.Hum… merci. Je vais le… ranger. Quelque: Um… thanks. I'll… put it away. Somewhere. Far away.
textes.Hurla ! J'ai une lettre qui annonce l'ar: Hurla! I've got a letter announcing the arrival of the spices!
textes.Hurla crie les nouvelles sur la place av: Hurla shouts the news on the square before I've had time to deliver the letters announcing it. She's stealing my job. She says she does it faster. True. That's exactly the problem.
textes.Hurla, c'est ma meilleure amie. Nous cri: Hurla is my best friend. We both shout, so we can hear each other from far away. She shouts the news, I shout the prices. Together, we make more noise than the volcano.
Hurla, you're shouting over my chorus.
textes.Hypothèse : aucune. Enfin, peut-être un: Hypothesis: none. Well, maybe a little pink.

I grew up there, among the piles of swaps, and I learned to count before I could walk: a pebble, a feather, a vial. As we tanukis say: everything's worth something, especially the rest.

textes.Hé hé ! Un vrai tanuki ! Viens dans mes: Heh heh! A true tanuki! Come here and give me a hug, my friend! … But not everything. Not everything, my friend. Not everything.

textes.Hé, toi ! Viens sentir ! … Ça ne sent ri: Hey, you! Come and smell! … Can't smell anything? That's normal, down here. So come and taste!
textes.Hé, toi ! Viens voir taper !: Hey, you! Come and watch me hammer!
textes.Hé, toi ! Viens voir taper ! Derrière la: Hey, you! Come and watch the hammering! Behind the yellow line!
textes.Hé, toi qui danses sur les ponts ! Mon p: Hey, bridge dancer! My next bridge is still yours to open. Dancing, obviously.
textes.Hé, toi qui jongles ! J'ai gardé les deu: Hey, juggler! I kept the two coconuts for you. We'll move up to three whenever you like.
textes.Hé, toi qui ne t'arrêtes jamais ! Tu rep: Hey, you who never stop! You still keep coming back. That's how it starts, I'm warning you.
textes.Hé, vous ! Il paraît qu'on vous a parlé: Hey, you! I hear someone's been telling you about me…
textes.Hé, vous ! Il paraît que vous avez un av: Hey, you! I hear you have an opinion about me?
textes.Hé, voyageur ! Un grog pour la route ?: Hey, traveller! A punch for the road?
Hey, {surnom}! Arm-wrestle? No? Fine. Then tell me: do you look after your sword?
textes.Hé, {surnom} ! J'ai trouvé un truc ce ma: Hey, {surnom}! I found a thing this morning. No idea what it is. Want to buy it?
textes.Hé, {surnom} ! Mon binôme de quai ! Un j: Hey, {surnom}! My dockside buddy! One day I'll take you down for real. When Yolande says yes. For now she's said “maybe”. From her, that's already half a yes.
textes.Hé, {surnom} ! Tu as déjà gagné quelque: Hey, {surnom}! Have you ever won anything? A race, a match, a contest?
textes.Hé, {surnom}, tape-moi un rythme sur tes: Hey, {surnom}, tap me a rhythm on your knees. Which one do you pick?
textes.Hé, {surnom}. Tu viens à la répète ce so: Hey, {surnom}. Coming to rehearsal tonight? We've got a new song. It's about a puddle.
textes.Hé. Tu as bu de l'eau, aujourd'hui ? Vra: Hey. Have you drunk water today? Really drunk, mind. Not one sip.
textes.Hé. Tu veux voir ce qui brille ?: Hey. Want to see something shiny?
textes.Hélas, ami ! Églantine me ferait remplir: Alas, friend! Églantine would make me fill in three forms if I left with someone unregistered. I hate forms.
textes.Héloïse ? Nous avons appris à voler ense: Héloïse? We learned to fly together! Her the right way up. Me upside down, the whole first year. She says I'm the only aeronaut who's ever looked up at the sky and seen their own feet.
textes.Héloïse ?! … (Elle croise les bras.) Ell: Héloïse?! … (She folds her arms.) How much did she pay you? Fine. She's very persuasive, I'll admit. But she's wrong.
textes.Héloïse Manivelle, ingénieure-en-chef, p: Héloïse Manivelle, chief engineer, chairs the jury of the Inventions Fair. She needs the opinion of an unbiased visitor.
textes.Héloïse Nimbus ? Elle a fait le tour des: Héloïse Nimbus? She's been round the clouds three times. The fourth time, the clouds made room for her.
textes.Héloïse a fait le Zéphyr, et je lui conf: Héloïse built the Zéphyr, and I've trusted her with my life for thirteen years. She refuses to give me the recipe for the gas. I trust her with my life anyway. It annoys me a little.
textes.Héloïse boit un soda au gingembre avant: Héloïse drinks a ginger soda before every take-off, and a chocolate after every landing. In between, she flies round the island. In the evening, she tells her travel tales at my table. I feel as if I've travelled too, without leaving my counter.
textes.Héloïse dit que les bateaux, ce sont des: Héloïse says boats are airships that forgot to go up. Pff. I told her airships are boats that lost the sea. We've been arguing for ten years. Hm. She's my best friend. Don't tell her.
textes.Héloïse dit que ses balayeurs sont meill: Héloïse says her sweepers are better than mine. Hers sing. That's a manufacturing defect.
textes.Héloïse est la meilleure pilote de l'arc: Héloïse is the best pilot in the archipelago. After me. She says the same thing, the other way round. Twenty years of races, twenty years of victories on both sides. She's my best friend. And my worst rival. Both at once is very comfortable.
textes.Héloïse est sévère comme une soupape et: Héloïse is as strict as a safety valve and as true as a spirit level. My favourite tool, by the way. Every spring, she inspects my boiler, and every spring I smile at her.
textes.Héloïse est une ingénieure remarquable e: Héloïse is a remarkable engineer and a disastrous head of jury. She wants three prizes instead of a single Cog of Honour. Three! Might as well hand medals to the wind.
textes.Héloïse et moi, on a appris à piloter en: Héloïse and I learnt to fly together, in Hautefond, twenty years ago. On the first day, we raced to the Mast. We arrived together. Ever since, each of us says she won. Nobody ever found out. It's the loveliest of mysteries.
textes.Héloïse m'a fait confiance quand je n'ét: Héloïse trusted me when I was just an old shepherd counting steps. She gave me a cable car and a brand-new cap. I send her a report every evening.
textes.Héloïse m'a tout appris, et elle m'a don: Héloïse taught me everything, and she gave me my lab. She says my kite is dangerous. She's right. She's almost always right. It's very annoying.
textes.Héloïse me refuse un brevet par semaine,: Héloïse turns down one patent a week from me, always kindly. She's a great lady. I'd so love, just once, to give her some work.
textes.Héloïse rêve de faire le tour du monde p: Héloïse dreams of going round the world by air. So do I. Now that the Dome has reopened too, we've decided to do it together, once we've been round everything there is down below. It'll be a race, of course. I've already won.

Héloïse dreams of flying round the world. So do I. We've decided to do it together, once the Fronde, the Strata and the Dome have reopened and we've seen everything there is down below. It'll be a race, of course. I've already won.

Héloïse dreams of going round the world by air. So do I. We've decided to do it together, once the Dome has reopened too and we've been round everything there is down below. It'll be a race, of course. I've already won.
textes.Héloïse vient tous les jours demander si: Héloïse comes every day to ask if her rivets are ready. They've been ready for a week. But her face when I say “tomorrow”… I never get tired of it. I'll give them to her tomorrow. Promise.
textes.Héloïse vole dans un ballon. Ce n'est pa: Héloïse flies in a balloon. It's not natural. But she has the heart of a true sailor. She knows where the wind comes from, she knows how to come back, and she never abandons anyone. Hm. Don't tell her.
Héloïse. My patent of the week.

textes.ICI LE SERGENT ! Les déménageurs sont là: THIS IS THE SERGEANT! The removal men are here! Don't panic! Well, panic a little! And lots of human chain!
textes.ICI RADIO BOUCAN, 98.7 ! La radio qui ne: THIS IS RADIO BOUCAN, 98.7! The radio that never switches off… except when the antenna falls down! And you're live with Sergeant Fréquence! … Well, right now we're not live, we're just talking. But I kept the voice. Welcome to Boucan, dear listener!
textes.Ianthé ! Tu danses sur ma marée, ce soir: Ianthé! Are you dancing to my tide tonight?
textes.Ianthé ! Une petite danse ? Je te paie e: Ianthé! A little dance? I'll pay you in crackers!
textes.Ianthé danse comme je chante, en plus vi: Ianthé dances the way I sing, only faster and wetter. She says she's the one people watch. I'm the one people listen to.
textes.Ianthé danse devant mon étal et le clien: Ianthé dances in front of my stall and the customers come all by themselves. I pay her in crackers. She says she'd prefer coins. Everyone says that.
textes.Ianthé danse sur le pont sud tous les so: Ianthé dances on the south bridge every evening. I… I happen to pass that way. For the mother-of-pearl. The light's better there. That's all.
textes.Ianthé m'a demandé un jour pourquoi je n: Ianthé once asked me why I never taste my own crackers. I said I wasn't hungry. She smiled, as if she knew. Since then, when she dances in front of the stall, she pretends to bite into one and pulls a face, a tiny one, just for me. We laugh, the two of us, without a word.
textes.Icare ! Je peux sauter du ponton ?: Icare! Can I jump off the jetty?
textes.Icare ? C'est lui qui nous a tout appris: Icare? He taught us everything! He glides to the bakery every morning. We're aiming for the living-room door first.
textes.Icare dit : « Le vent, c'est un ami qui: Icare says: “The wind is a friend who never tells you he's coming.” So I stay polite.
textes.Icare dit qu'il faut lui parler gentimen: Icare says you have to speak kindly to it.
textes.Icare dit que son planeur va plus vite q: Icare says his glider is faster than the Dragonfly. Going downhill, maybe. Going downhill, even a pebble is faster than the Dragonfly. But he glides beautifully. I challenged him to a race. He said yes. I won.
textes.Icare, le moniteur de planeur, dit qu'il: Icare, the gliding instructor, says he's faster than the Dragonfly. Going down, maybe. Going down, even a pebble is faster than the Dragonfly. That's no argument.
textes.Ici ? Ta première ? Alors souviens-toi b: Here? Your first? Then remember this night well, kid. You tell the story of your firsts your whole life. And you polish it a little each time.
textes.Ici Radio Boucan ! Hé, vous ! Oui, vous: This is Radio Boucan! Hey, you! Yes, you!
textes.Ici Radio Boucan ! Les déménageurs ont b: This is Radio Boucan! The removal men have retreated! Well done, human chain, and well done, our hero!
textes.Ici Radio Boucan. On vient de me faire p: This is Radio Boucan. Someone just passed me a note: “Bernard the pigeon has eaten everything again.” Patchouli adds: “That's not a prediction, it's an observation.”
textes.Ici c'est la teuf, là-bas c'est la valse: Here it's the party, over there it's the waltz. The two islands are made for each other.
textes.Ici, des objets montent d'en bas. Une pl: Here, things float up from below. A feather a bird let go of, a hat the wind carried off, a lost kite. The first thing I ever caught was a sock. Just one. It came from an island. It had walked on the Earth. I held it all night, trembling. I founded the Museum the next day.
textes.Ici, il fait toujours beau. Alors, pour: Up here, the weather's always fine. So when we want to talk about the weather, we talk about the weather down below. It keeps us busy.
textes.Ici, il y a plus d'horloges que d'habita: Around here, there are more clocks than people. And they never agree, except at Gaspard's.
textes.Ici, ils ne font pas grève. Ils sont en: Here, they don't go on strike. They're on holiday.
textes.Ici, ils ont des poissons-lanternes au l: Here they have lanternfish instead of street lamps. Well, they have street lamps too. But the fish are prettier. And they move.
textes.Ici, j'ai découvert le tajine. Zohra m'a: Here I discovered tajine. Zohra taught me. Well, she watched me make one and she cried. For joy, I think.
textes.Ici, j'ai découvert que les Pieds-Lourds: Here, I discovered that the Heavy-Feet swap little shiny discs for things. “Money.” I adored the word. I repeated it everywhere. Money, money, money. I never really understood what it was for. So I opened a bazaar, so I could say it all day long.
Here, I almost have a landlubber's life. At dawn, I row with Driss. In the afternoon, I teach knots to the harbour kids, and little Yasmine already beats me. I tease the caïd about his sleeping cannons. In the evening, I dance on the square. And above my cannons shine Nourredine's lanterns. I won't say how they got there.
textes.Ici, j'ai tout ! Zohra qui m'a appris le: Here, I have everything! Zohra who taught me tagine, Mustapha who gave me his recipe, Hassan and his slightly bland tea, Saïd who sold me forty kilos of sardines for a sneeze. In the evening, Lhoucine plays me the whale dance. Tibo peels my potatoes. And in the souk, there's Aïcha. Ho ho. Above all, Aïcha.
textes.Ici, je lis le journal du Plancher. Les: Up here, I read the paper from the Floor. The news from down below comes up with the capsule. Always a little out of breath.
textes.Ici, je loge chambre douze, au Grand Hôt: Here, I stay in room twelve at the Grand Hotel. Six croissants from Madame Margaux every morning. A snow globe from Victor every week. Fernand's sea dragon tooth, under a glass dome. Toni's divine punch, paid in gold. Madame Colette's jar of figs, which she refuses to sell me. And Edmond's moustache, which I covet in silence. Well, almost in silence.
Here, I'm hardly scared at all. Hardly. There's always the risk of a turnip.
textes.Ici, je ne fais rien. Rien du tout. Depu: Here, I do nothing. Nothing at all. For three days, I've been sunbathing, reading, watching my two children from my towel, and in the evening we dine at Paulo's. The grocer recommended her favourite novel, the fortune-teller made me a prediction, and one evening I passed some chocolate to the young bride next door, who was crying. For someone who does nothing, I'm very busy.
textes.Ici, la gravité ne marche plus qu'à un t: Here, gravity only works at one third. Jump! You go three times higher, and you float back down ever so gently.
textes.Ici, la première année, mes tomates ne p: Here, the first year, my tomatoes wouldn't grow. One night I sat down in the middle of the garden and sang my mother's lullaby. The next day, they'd grown a hand's width. Since then, I sing every morning. The Reverend says it's a miracle. Bucatini says it's the ash. I say it's the lullaby.
textes.Ici, le soleil se couche en dessous de n: Here, the sun sets below us. It goes under the island, through the clouds, and lights them up from underneath. You'll see it tonight, from the Glass Belvedere. You'll walk on the sunset. It's the only place in the world where you can.
textes.Ici, les enfants savent des choses que l: Here, children know things that children up top don't: the name of every jellyfish, the time the Pearl changes colour, how you breathe under a dome. But they don't know what a sunset is. Everyone has their treasures. Everyone has their gaps.
textes.Ici, les machines ne poussent pas. Il fa: Here, machines don't grow. You have to build them, with screws, bolts, spanners. The first time I tightened a bolt, I got goosebumps. Well, Lumen bumps: they blink. I understood that this was what I wanted to do. Open things up, understand, repair. Here, there's something inside.
textes.Ici, les pièces qu'on me lance remontent: Up here, the coins people throw me float back up on the wind. … No, I'm joking. Thank you!
textes.Ici, les plantes ont plus de place que l: Here, the plants have more room than the furniture. Weaving between them, a watering drone does its rounds, very serious about it.
textes.Ici, les vents chantent faux et personne: Here, the winds sing out of tune and nobody complains. I had nothing to do. Quasar built me a theremin: an instrument you play without touching it, just by moving your hands in the air. The first note went “oooooh.” All of Ondelune was in that note. I played all night. Everyone's antennae were vibrating.
textes.Ici, notre soleil, c'est la Grande Perle: Here, our sun is the Great Pearl, threaded on the Air Chimney in the middle of the Square. In the morning, it turns white and gold. In the evening, blue, then violet. Miss Nautile says the real sun sets into the sea, all red. Red! I didn't know a sun could blush.
textes.Ici, nous recueillons l'eau de la pluie: Up here we collect water from the rain and the clouds, we live on sun and wind, and we recycle absolutely everything. We're proud of it. A little too proud, perhaps. Burgomaster Hector says we even recycle compliments.
textes.Ici, on aime la pluie parce qu'elle fait: Here, we love the rain because it brings everyone into the café. People squeeze together, they talk, they laugh. Rain is a good excuse to be together.
textes.Ici, on dit « Bon vent ». Au fond de la: Up here, we say “Fair winds”. At the bottom of the sea, apparently, they say “Happy bubbles!”. They go well together. You need wind to blow bubbles.
textes.Ici, on ne gaspille pas une goutte. L'ea: Up here, we don't waste a drop. Rainwater runs off the dome roofs, we keep it in the pond, we water, and whatever's left flows back to the Spring in the Park. Doctor Aurèle says some drops have been round the island a hundred times. They know the way.
We don't serve a drop of alcohol here. Never. Chasm water filtered through the crystals, lemonade, herbal teas, hot chocolate. Anyone who wants something else goes back up to Hautefond. They always come back for the lemonade.
textes.Ici, on recycle tout. Les feuilles devie: Here, we recycle everything. Leaves become compost, compost becomes strawberries, strawberries become sunshine juice, and sunshine juice becomes… Gustave says “good cheer”. I have not yet found how to gather it.
textes.Ici, sous terre, impossible de voler : t: Here, underground, you can't fly: you land.
textes.Ici, tout est à prix libre ou au troc. J: Here, everything is pay-what-you-can or swapped. I traded a jar of jam for a song from Bielle. I think I got an excellent deal.
textes.Ici, tout le monde connaît tout le monde: Round here, everybody knows everybody. And everybody knows everybody's cat.
textes.Ici, tout se règle à la pétanque. Les ma: Here, everything gets settled with pétanque. Weddings, inheritances, elections. The mayor won at pétanque.
textes.Ici, une bagarre éclate pour un rien. Un: Around here, a brawl breaks out over nothing. A look, a wrong word, a spilled grog. I like it. Livens things up.
textes.Ignace Bouche-d'Or a des dés pipés. Je l: Ignace Bouche-d'Or has loaded dice. I know it. He knows I know. That's why he never plays at MY table with them.
textes.Ignace Bouche-d'Or a gagné son sloop aux: Ignace Bouche-d'Or won his sloop at dice. Against a governor. With loaded dice, if you ask me.
textes.Ignace Bouche-d'Or triche aux dés. Tout: Ignace Bouche-d'Or cheats at dice. Everybody knows it. Nobody's ever proved it. That's talent.
textes.Ignace est le meilleur capitaine du mond: Ignace is the best captain in the world when he's not gambling. The problem is, he gambles all the time. He's already bet our sloop. He won. That time.
textes.Ignace parle pour deux. Ça tombe bien. I: Ignace talks for two. That suits me. Maybe he cheats. That's not my question. He hired me without asking any. I owe him that.
textes.Ignace parle trop, joue trop et sourit t: Ignace talks too much, gambles too much and smiles too much. All those gold teeth blind me. But he pays me, and he lets me guard the door. I like guarding doors. Nobody mumbles in doorways.
textes.Ignatia est née un soir de grande érupti: Ignatia was born on the night of a great eruption, and she kept something of that fire. She carries the city the way you carry a flame: without squeezing it too tight.
textes.Il a accroché une clochette à ma chaise,: He hung a little bell on my chair in the library, so he knows when I move. So I hold the bell with one hand so it won't ring. Which means I can't turn the pages. I always read the same one. I know it by heart: page forty-two of the herbarium. Nettles.
textes.Il a aimé ton histoire d'hier, Faelar. C: It liked your story yesterday, Faelar. The one about the hedgehog.
textes.Il a apporté son chronomètre de Cliqueti: He brought his Cliquetis stopwatch to the bakery. Now he times the baking: “Twenty-two minutes, Trèfle! Record broken!” It's not a race, Pépin, it's bread! But I have to admit: since then, I haven't burnt a thing. Cerfeuil would have laughed. He burnt every loaf, and without a stopwatch.
textes.Il a baptisé sa glace coco « Bruno-Loco: He named his coconut ice cream “Bruno-Loco”, in my honour, he says. The day I went to taste it at the beach hut, he didn't make me pay: “It's your recipe, brother.” Then he made me pay for the glass of water. He's sharp, that boy.
textes.Il a bien reçu mon pot ?: Did he get my jar all right?
textes.Il a bien tourné les pages ? Toutes ?: Did it turn the pages properly? All of them?
textes.Il a bien tourné les pages, ce soir ?: Did it turn the pages properly tonight?
textes.Il a caché une boulette dans sa poche po: He hid a meatball in his pocket to give to the Great Spaghetti. It stayed there for a week. We found it by the smell.
textes.Il a cent ans et il n'a jamais été à l'h: It's a hundred years old and it's never once been on time. Mr Gaspard says it's ahead of its time.
textes.Il a construit un château à quatre tours: He built a castle with four towers and a moat. I photographed it from every angle: front, back, from above, lying in the sand. Sixty-two photos. When I looked up, the sea had carried off a tower. Théo said: “You didn't even look at it, Dad.” But I've got sixty-two photos of it.
textes.Il a cru découvrir une comète. C'était u: He thought he'd discovered a comet. It was a biscuit crumb on the lens. He made a speech anyway. A very fine one, about crumbs.
He's got style. That's better than a neck.
It's got echo. Like the rain.
textes.Il a dit au Conseil que j'étais « le mei: He told the Council I was “the finest grumbler in the history of the City”. I protested. That proved him right. He laughed for the whole session.
textes.Il a dit « peut-être ». C'est mieux qu'h: It said “maybe”. That's better than yesterday.
He's said “jellyfish-head” three times. Excellent mood!
textes.Il a dormi trois ans ! Il doit avoir fai: It's slept for three years! It must be hungry.
textes.Il a encore bu toute la rosée des fougèr: He's drunk all the dew off the ferns again.
textes.Il a encore oublié de remonter la nacell: He forgot to bring the basket back down again. Three rabbits waited at the bottom a whole morning. I found him asleep at the treetop, nose in the sun. I growled. He said: “Hrmm. They took the stairs? Serves them right.” He was right. I didn't tell him.
textes.Il a entendu parler des chaussures à res: He heard about the spring shoes in Cliquetis. He begged me. Three evenings. “Just two springs, Ursule!” No. I told Pépin. Pépin said: “Cheating.” Grisou sulked for a week. The forge was quiet. Lovely week. Since then, he asks for lighter shoes. “Just in case.”
textes.Il a essayé de monter sur le mât avec ma: He tried to climb the mast with my spyglass between his teeth. He got halfway up, saw the Great Table, and came back down for snack time. A true pirate.
textes.Il a essayé de régler mon grille-pain so: He tried to adjust my solar toaster. He said: “It toasts three seconds early.” I told him: “That's so the toast is ready before you're hungry.” He wrote that down in his notebook.
He's hungry, that's a good sign.
textes.Il a fait six huit dans le ciel depuis t: He's done six figures of eight in the sky since earlier!
textes.Il a gardé mes balles de la dernière foi: He kept my balls from last time!
textes.Il a gommé la liste de courses pendant q: He rubbed out the shopping list while I was doing the shopping. I came home with a pumpkin and an umbrella.
textes.Il a goûté une de mes galettes par jour: He tasted one of my crackers a day for forty days, taking notes, to find the recipe. On the forty-first, he came to read me his scroll, all proud. I said: “Wrong. All wrong.” He was so disappointed I gave him a cracker. Free! He wrote that down too, of course.
textes.Il a inventé la grenouille aux navets do: He invented frog with golden turnips for me. He served it to me one evening, very proud. I ate the frog and left the turnips, neatly lined up at the edge of the plate. Ulric said nothing. The next day, he served me the same thing, but the turnips were decorated with little flowers. He said: “So at least they look pretty.” I kept them.
He seems to regret your quarrel.
textes.Il a le bon nombre de poils !: He has just the right amount of hair!
textes.Il a les dents dans le plancher !: His teeth are in the floorboards!
textes.Il a mangé, au moins, ton pirate ?: Has he eaten, at least, your pirate?
textes.Il a marchandé une heure pour vingt plum: He haggled for an hour over twenty macaw feathers. I let him have his price, for peace's sake. At the next fair, I saw my feathers on his stall: I recognise my knots. Three times my price! He told me: “They've travelled, they're tired, that costs extra.” So I tripled my prices. He pays without arguing now.
textes.Il a mes pattes, ton crabe sentimental !: Your sentimental crab has my legs!
textes.Il a montré mon tapis rouge et il a dit: He pointed at my red carpet and said: “How much?” I named a starting price, a joke price. He said: “Paid.” And he left with it. I had a fever for three days. Samira put wet cloths on my forehead, and I kept repeating in my sleep: “Haggle… haggle…”
textes.Il a nommé une étoile Clémentine. J'ai n: He named a star Clémentine. I named a cloud Octave. He was very offended. Then very flattered. Then he asked me if the cloud was beautiful. It is.
textes.Il a parié que je ne toucherais pas sa b: He bet I couldn't hit his ball in the air with my blowgun. He sent the ball very high, with a flick of the hip. I blew. The dart stuck in the rubber. The ball fell back down with my dart in it. It's still there. Chak plays with it. He says it's a lucky ball. He lost the bet.
textes.Il a passé une nuit à mesurer la lueur d: He spent a night measuring the glow of the stones with his instruments. At dawn, he came to tell me, all proud, that they shine a tenth brighter when Lin reads them a story. I said: “I know.” He looked disappointed. I didn't want to disappoint him. But I knew.
textes.Il a peint ma porte en rouge pour que je: He painted my door red so I'd find inspiration. I wrote twelve pages about red. The door was peeling before I finished.
textes.Il a plu en haut. Tu as pensé à nous ? L: It rained up top. Did you think of us? The waterfall told me.
textes.Il a plu sous les Nuées. Pas dessus : de: It rained under the Clouds. Not on top: underneath.
textes.Il a posé un doigt sur une pierre, pour: He put a finger on a stone, to see if it was cold. I was behind him. I said: “I know.” Nothing more. He ran off so fast his hat stayed on the ground. I brought it back to him the next day, at the dormitory. He turned it over every which way before taking it. He was checking it wasn't a pigeon.
textes.Il a posé une pièce d'or sur mon comptoi: He put a gold coin on my counter, a big one, with his great-grandfather's head on it. “For the oldest jar in the shop, madam.” I pushed it back with my fingertip. He took a goat's cheese instead, and paid for it with the same coin. I didn't have change. I gave it to him in honey. Six jars.
He promised. Well, he wagged his tail.
textes.Il a rapporté de Per-Hâpy un scarabée bl: He brought back a blue scarab from Per-Hâpy, from Ptahmosé. I spent an hour wondering whether it was a compliment or an insult. Tochtli told me that in Egypt, a scarab brings luck. I was relieved. Later, I learned he'd made it up on the spot. And that it was true anyway. With Tochtli, even the lies hit the mark.
textes.Il a revendu un tapis de l'oasis à un vo: He resold an oasis carpet to a traveller, claiming it had been woven for a sultan's wedding. I know the weaver. An old woman who weaves for her grandsons, in her tent. No sultan. I was there. The traveller looked at me. I said nothing. Afterwards, Rachid bought me a tea. He'd understood.
He blushed when he saw you.
It shrank. The night was cold.
textes.Il a révisé. Votre piano tousse toujours: It revised. Is your piano still coughing?
textes.Il a testé mon parapluie-ascenseur. Il e: He tested my umbrella-lift. He stayed stuck on the big mast for an hour. He named three clouds. He thanked me. He wants the same one, but “going up a bit less fast”.
He has a very nice camel.
textes.Il a un chronomètre de Cliquetis, et il: He has a stopwatch from Cliquetis, and he times everything: the race, the warm-up, the nap, even my carrots. “Forty-three seconds for three carrots, Bondi, a record!” I hear the tick-tock even in my dreams.
textes.Il a vendu au tianguis du « copal béni p: At the tianguis, he sold “copal blessed by the high priest”. I hadn't blessed anything at all. I went to see him. He held out a piece and said: “Bless it now, then it'll be true.” I did. I still don't know why. He doubled his price that same day.
textes.Il a voté contre la réouverture de la Li: He voted against reopening the Line. On the day of the celebration, he was in the front row. He clapped the loudest. Then he told me: “That was for the sparrows.”
textes.Il a voulu attirer un dictionnaire par t: He tried to summon a dictionary by telekinesis. Without permission. The whole B shelf followed: bestiaries, botany, biographies. He disappeared underneath. I dug him out book by book, putting each volume back in its place. Two hours. He didn't move a toe. It's the only time he's ever been perfectly still.
textes.Il a voulu chanter un solo, une fois. To: He wanted to sing a solo once. The whole island started clapping before the end. He thought it was a triumph. We let him think so.
textes.Il a voulu compter les marches du temple: He wanted to count the temple steps, like me at his age. He got to the top, out of breath: “Three hundred and sixty-four!” I told him to start again. He started again four times. The fifth time, he got three hundred and sixty-five, and shouted so loudly that the macaws flew off. He had forgotten the platform.
textes.Il a voulu deviner le trente-troisième i: He wanted to guess the thirty-third ingredient of my ras el hanout. He sniffed, tasted, closed his eyes, and said, very sure of himself: “Fish!” Fish! In my ras el hanout! I laughed so hard I knocked over the paprika. It's the only time he's ever made me laugh. Well. One of the only times.
textes.Il a voulu garder ma chinampa, une nuit,: One night, he wanted to guard my chinampa against vegetable thieves. Around midnight: splash! I ran with a lamp. Mixtli was in the canal, with his whole jaguar skin soaked on his head. He said: “The canal moved.” I held out an oar. I laughed until morning. So did the herons.
textes.Il a voulu m'écrire un poème sur un buva: He wanted to write me a poem on blotting paper, so the ink wouldn't run. The poem got soaked up. He says it was his finest.
He wanted to barter for my indigo cheche. For a pot of honey, then two, then a cloth of mist, then a singing hat. He talked a whole afternoon. I said nothing. In the evening he sighed: “Your silence is worth more than your cheche, my friend.” I kept both.
textes.Il a voulu repeindre l'autel en doré. Il: He wanted to repaint the altar gold. He painted Mamma Lasagna's cat. The cat was very proud.
textes.Il a échangé deux pains à la brasserie,: He swapped two loaves at the brewery, mine and Mérit's, while I was looking the other way. I tasted. I said it was mine. It was hers. The whole brewery laughed. I paid for my beer and left. I didn't speak to him for a month. He didn't notice straight away. He talks a lot.
textes.Il a écrit dans ses rouleaux que la prem: He wrote in his scrolls that grandmother's first cracker was “dreadful”. Dreadful! I went to the archives to scratch the word out myself. He sat on the scroll. We stayed like that for an hour. In the end he added “eaten while weeping for joy”. I accepted the deal.
textes.Il a écrit mon nom au tableau des cogneu: He wrote my name on the brawlers' board, in chalk: “Bel-Humeur”. Letters were missing! I rubbed it out with my sleeve and wrote it again, big, in cannon-sized letters. Now my name takes up half the board. Gros-Louis and the Mute have little names, at the bottom. It's better that way. It's fairer.
textes.Il a écrit « La flèche silencieuse », un: He wrote “The Silent Arrow”, a song about me. Forty verses. I shoot an arrow in the first verse. It hits its target in the fortieth. In between, there's a storm, a dragon and a princess. I've never seen a princess. The arrow, yes. It was a good one.
textes.Il a été cuit avec amour. C'est déjà pas: It was baked with love. That's not bad already.
textes.Il adore ça ! Attention, il va pleuvoir: He loves that! Watch out, he's going to rain!
textes.Il avait dix ans, des genoux écorchés et: He was ten, with scraped knees and the nerve of a government minister. He took the finest apple off my stall, bit into it in front of me, and said: “I'll pay you when I'm mayor.” I wrote it in my notebook. Page one. He's been mayor for eighteen years. The page hasn't changed.
textes.Il avait douze ans. Une nuit, à trois he: He was twelve. One night, at three o'clock, there was a knock at my door in the Tower: Aurélien, barefoot, a tiny trembling light in his hands. His first. He wanted to know if it shone brighter than the stars. I told him it did. It wasn't true, and it was the most beautiful light I've ever seen.
textes.Il avait peur des échelles. Alors chaque: He was afraid of ladders. So every year, for his birthday, I leave a ladder in front of the library, with a ribbon. Forty ladders. He gives them all to Mathurin, who's turned them into planks for the jetty. When I walk on the jetty, I count the years.
textes.Il avait quatorze ans quand il m'a suppl: He was fourteen when he begged me to take him on the Bahja. The first day, he was sick over the side all morning. He got up, all green, and said to me: “That was to feed the fish, uncle. So they'll come.” That day, I knew he'd make a fisherman.
textes.Il avait quatre ans. Un crabe vert, gros: He was four. A green crab, big as a date, pinched his finger on the quay. He screamed. And how he screamed! The seagulls flew off, a guard came running down from the Skala. I unhooked the crab, I blew on the finger. He went quiet at once, and looked at me as if I'd slain a dragon. Ever since, he carries my balls of twine.
He was sixteen and thought he was a poet. He recited me a poem about seagulls, rhyming on “-ay” everywhere: gull at play, girl so gay, sock of grey. I said: “That's bad.” He left, red as a brick. I still know it by heart. When he gets too proud, I recite it to him. He turns modest straight away.
textes.Il avait six ans, il courait sur la plag: He was six, running along the beach knocking over the parasols, and banging on two coconuts and a conch. I taught him to count with his feet. I named him Mistral, because he blew through like the wind. Now he gets the whole village dancing. I tell people he learned on seashells. It's true. More or less.
textes.Il avait six ans. Il a lancé la balle d': He was six. He hit the ball with his hip, very high, over the wall of the court. I was looking at Venus. The ball landed on my head, bounced, and came down on his. Two identical bumps. He tells everyone I was the one who saw stars. He saw them too. I heard him say: “Oh, Venus.”
textes.Il avait six ou sept ans, et un turban t: He was six or seven, with a turban too big for him. He'd come to the end of the jetty to steal my fishing worms from the tin box while I pretended to sleep. I let him. The next day he'd come back with three little fish and give them to me “to pay”. Already a man of honour. Already a thief.
textes.Il avait une jarre fêlée, invendable. Je: He had a cracked jar, unsellable. I took it anyway. At the tianguis, I presented it as “the jar where Tlaloc keeps the thunder”: when you tapped it, it rumbled, because of the crack. I sold it for three times its price. Coyotl wanted his share. I gave it to him. He cracked other jars on purpose. They didn't rumble.
textes.Il balaie ! Colle-toi à ses chenilles, o: It sweeps! Stick close to its tracks, or back away out of reach.
It beats in A minor, Lyre.
textes.Il boit un seul rhum par soir. Un seul,: He drinks one rum a night. Just one, in silence, at the end of the counter, back to the wall. He talks to nobody. He watches the captain. A sailor who drinks like that is a sailor who's calculating. That worries me more than a brawl. Brawls, I can handle. Calculations, I watch.
It's sulking, Thalion. It has its moods.
textes.Il brille au soleil. Un marchand en voud: It shines in the sun. A merchant might want it.
It shines, Bulle. The patients love it.
It shines, Coralin. Just like yours.
textes.Il cachait le dessert dans le canon de p: He used to hide the dessert in the stern cannon, so I wouldn't find it. The stern cannon! I found it by the smell, like a hunting dog. Since then, he hides it somewhere else. I'm still looking. I think it's in the captain's cabin. I'm not going in there.
textes.Il cache un sablier derrière la pile d'e: He hides an hourglass behind the pile of encyclopaedias, to know how long I take to read. I see it reflected in his glasses. So now I read more slowly, so he keeps his record. He looks worried. He offered me a lamp. I took it. It made him happy.
textes.Il caresse le cuivre. Ce grand ours, ave: He strokes the copper. That big bear, with his hands full of burns, runs his finger over a new tray, ever so gently, like on a cat's back. I pretend not to see. A pirate stroking copper, that should stay between the copper and him.
textes.Il chante si tu joues de la flûte !: He sings if you play the flute!
It sings too loud. Clou can't sleep any more.
textes.Il chante « Marée Basse » ! Il chante «: It's singing “Low Tide”! It's singing “Low Tide”!
textes.Il cherchait la chaleur, Dagna. Comme to: It was looking for warmth, Dagna. Like everyone.
textes.Il cherche sa carte partout : dans les g: He's looking everywhere for his map: in the caves, under the barrels, in his crew's pockets. Everywhere except up high. Cats climb. I've told him three times. He says a captain doesn't climb on roofs. The truth is, he's scared of heights. I saw him stand on a chair to take down a lantern. He was green.
textes.Il cogne comme une sardine morte !: He hits like a dead sardine!
textes.Il compose. Le jour, il joue nos airs ;: It composes. By day, it plays our tunes; by night, it makes up its own. I write them down when I wake up… when I remember them.
textes.Il connaît ! Tête de méduse, pile au tro: He knows! Jellyfish-head, right on the third!
textes.Il connaît la Chaumière mieux que moi. I: He knows the Cottage better than I do. He knows how many tiles there are, where the roof leaks, which window creaks. One day, he corrected me in front of a client: “No, Monsieur Prosper, the chimney draws badly in an east wind.” The client left. I was furious. Then I had the chimney repaired. He was right.
textes.Il croit que je ne l'ai pas vu, la nuit,: He thinks I didn't see him, at night, behind the lanterns, watching me run. … I saw him. So one morning I left my tracks on purpose. On his training path. Nice and clear. Fourteen laps. So he'd count. … He counted.
textes.Il croit que je ne le vois pas, la nuit,: He thinks I don't see him at night, under my windows, with his mother-of-pearl lamp and an empty scroll. He's waiting for my lamp to go out so he can finally write something cheerful. Some nights I blow it out on purpose, even if I'm not sleeping. He goes home delighted.
textes.Il croit que je ne vois pas les haricots: He thinks I don't see the beans he slips into my right pocket to cheat on his hot honeys. I see them. Once, I let him: I served him his five hot honeys, and made him pay for all five. He paid in stories, five stories. Good deal. But I sewed my pocket shut all the same.
textes.Il croit que je triche aux osselets. Je: He thinks I cheat at jacks. I don't cheat: I just blow on the shells a tiny bit, to make them spin. Blowing is my job. He says it's cheating. Coralin used to say the same. I'm starting to think it's a city-wide affliction.
textes.Il crépite, mon enfant. Il t'a entendue: It's crackling, my child. It heard you coming.
textes.Il danse le dos bas, les yeux fixes, en: He dances crouched low, eyes fixed, creeping forward slowly, as if he were hunting. The others step aside. Me, I laugh so hard I have to sit down. He never stops. One evening, I asked him why he kept going. He said: “You laugh.” It's the longest sentence he's ever said to me. I embroidered it in my head.
He dances better than Haldir now.
textes.Il dit bonjour aux grands nuages !: He's saying hello to the big clouds!
textes.Il dit qu'avant Barbe-Sanglante, la Bala: He says that before Barbe-Sanglante, Balafre was called the Green Island, and that the rain dug the ravine. We argued a whole afternoon on the bench. In the end, he asked me if I was here a hundred years ago. I said: “Yes.” He was left speechless. For a man who whistles, that's quite a feat. I won. I think.
textes.Il dit que Bernadette siffle plus fort q: He says Bernadette whistles louder than my cabin. One day, we held a contest. The whole Square voted for Bernadette. I didn't hear a thing, so I voted for me.
textes.Il dit que je chante faux. J'ai chanté u: He says I sing off-key. I sang once, at the Dawn Festival, a hundred years ago, because I'd been asked to. Nobody has asked me again. That's perfectly fine. But I don't see why he has to remind everyone of it at every festival.
textes.Il dit que je l'ai jamais affronté. Je l: He says I've never faced him. I tell him: “What about the salt night?” He says: “You didn't even have your fists up, it doesn't count.” So I offer him a rematch, fists up. He says: “WHAT?!” I say it again. He says: “WHAT?!” We've been stuck there for two years.
He says your map was wrong.
textes.Il dit toujours : « C'est la mer. » Quan: He always says: “It's the sea.” When it crackles. Once it was a crab, inside Raoul. … Fine. Most of the time, it's true, it's the sea. But I check. He never checks. He trusts me. Trust is heavy. It's good.
He says that to everyone. He's lying.
It sleeps! Even the First Councillor. Well, I think so. Sometimes her window stays lit very late. She rereads the residents' letters, one by one.
textes.Il dort depuis trois ans ! Il devrait êt: She's been asleep for three years! She should be in top shape.
textes.Il déteste la noix de coco. Pas le goût: He hates coconut. Not the taste: he can't bite it. So I grate it very fine, cook it in milk, and tell him it's semolina. He loves my semolina. It's been going on for six years, and he keeps asking for more. Never tell him. A cook has the right to his secrets.
textes.Il déteste ma tisane de lune. Alors, les: He hates my moon tea. So on nights when he can't sleep, I serve it to him in an old sailor's mug with a spoonful of honey at the bottom, and say it's the captains' hot honey. He downs it in one, goes “aaah” like Corentin, and sleeps like a rock.
It has one hundred and fourteen.
textes.Il en arrive cinquante par jour, Patchou: Fifty of them arrive every day, Patchouli.
He makes them. That's already a lot.
textes.Il en manque un, Hapou ! Je plaisante !: There's one missing, Hapou! Just kidding! Just kidding!
Is one missing? I'll pierce it tomorrow.
textes.Il en manque {manque}. Les araignées de: {manque} still missing. The spiders in the western cave. Go.
There was some. Before you showed up.
textes.Il en vaut une. Et la moitié de ton chat: It's worth one. And half of your cat.
textes.Il essaie tous les jours de deviner ce q: Every day he tries to guess what I'm making at the back of the stall. Yesterday he asked me, all casual: “Got any gold thread, you?” I said: “Gold? For slippers? You've had too much tea, Rachid.” He left. I heard him muttering all the way back to his carpets.
textes.Il est 23 heures… Les projecteurs s'étei: It's 11 PM… The spotlights go out for a moment. At the side of the stage, Clapotis holds Bouton-d'Or's hand, and doesn't take his eyes off the sky. FFFIIIIIIUUU… BOOM!
He went to ask Octave for nails. He came back saying Octave's shacks are better. I sulked for three days. On the fourth, I taught him the clove hitch, which Octave doesn't know. We have our weapons too.
textes.Il est arrivé à Forgefer avec des bras d: He turned up in Forgefer with big'un arms and a mule's head. I gave him sacks of coal. Three years of sacks. He came back every morning. On the first day of the fourth year, I handed him a hammer. He looked at it like the king's crown. I went to fetch a mug of fizz, so I wouldn't have to see his face.
textes.Il est arrivé à l'aérodrome et m'a deman: He came to the airfield and asked me for a ticket “to a place where nobody has ever invented anything”. Gustave dropped him at Carène. He came back on the next flight, very sheepish, hat in hand. “They have cider, commander.” I offered him a tea. He asked if anyone had already invented it. I didn't have the heart to answer.
textes.Il est au crayon. Je l'effacerai le jour: It's in pencil. I'll rub it out the day I see it.
textes.Il est beau sur toi, en foulard, Lalla A: It looks lovely on you, as a scarf, Lalla Aïcha.
textes.Il est beau, Hapou. Pas de chaton dedans: It's fine, Hapou. No kitten in it this time?
textes.Il est content ! Il fait son arc-en-ciel: He's happy! He's making his rainbow!
textes.Il est dans la grenouille ! Ne vous déba: He's inside the frog! Don't struggle! It lasts three seconds! Four if you struggle!
textes.Il est dans son bureau, à l'étage, en tr: He's in his office, upstairs, christening a new cloud. He can't decide between “Hortense” and “Cumulus the Brave”. This could take a while.
textes.Il est dedans ! Je charge la grenouille: He's inside! I'm charging the frog! … It hops away. I'm charging where it was.
textes.Il est dedans. Je ne regarde pas. Je ne: He's inside. I'm not looking. I'm not looking. I'm looking a bit.
textes.Il est dehors, au kiosque de la terrasse: He's outside, at the kiosk on the terrace, selling his sugar puffs to the whole Esplanade. He only comes in at closing time. He says his sugar puffs need to see people.
textes.Il est en bois. Et il ne sert pas les pu: It's made of wood. And it doesn't serve punch.
textes.Il est entré dans ma tente, il s'est ass: He came into my tent, sat down, pointed at his heart, then his arm, and made a tiny heart with his two index fingers. He put a pearl on the table. I tattooed. Three hours, not a shiver. At the end, he looked at his arm for a very long time. I thought he didn't like it. Then he shook my hand so hard I couldn't tattoo for two days.
textes.Il est entré et il a posé sa main sur mo: He came in and laid his hand on my counter like a piece of evidence. “Exactly the same,” he said. Then, very quietly: “Half a size smaller, without it showing.” A ring too big that slips off in the waves… I didn't need my loupe to understand.
textes.Il est fier, regarde ses joues !: He's proud, look at his cheeks!
textes.Il est frais, il est beau mon poisson !: Fresh and lovely, my fish! Come closer, come closer! I'm Rosalie, and here we only sell this morning's catch.
textes.Il est gros comment ? Il est gros commen: How big is it? How big is it?
It's been heavy for ten years, that sack.
textes.Il est là, sur ta main !: There it is, on your hand!
It's twelve minutes past noon, Gloubi.
textes.Il est monté jusqu'à la dixième marche d: He made it up to the tenth step of the Mast. I applauded him from the gangway. He blushed so red you'd have thought he was the Albatross.
textes.Il est monté un soir, sans prévenir, ave: He came up one evening, unannounced, with two cups of coffee. At the two hundredth step, I heard him puffing like a whale. He got to the top with one empty cup and one half-full. He handed me the half. I drank it. I didn't say thank you. He came back anyway.
textes.Il est parfait, ce col. Tu l'as bien cho: This collar is perfect. You chose it well, at the market.
textes.Il est parfait. Mes filles ont butiné le: It's perfect. My girls have been foraging the lime trees.
textes.Il est parfait… Attendez… Écoutez ! Tic,: It's perfect… Wait… Listen! Tick, tock… and… DONG! It chimes! After so many years! Thank you, thank you… You've given the square its heart back.
textes.Il est parti par là-bas, vers la colline: It went over there, towards the hill, above the houses in the west! It got stuck in a tree, I'm sure of it!
He drifted by yesterday. He sends his regards.
It's been down for an hour.
textes.Il est quatorze heures. Vous avez jusqu': It is two o'clock. You have until three.
textes.Il est rentré de son voyage avec un coqu: He came back from his voyage with a shell from Port-Azur, all pink inside, like an ear. He gave it to me on the quay, without a word, his hands trembling. I pierced it and hung it round my neck. It's still there. When Larbi is at the end of the jetty, I hold it to my ear. You can hear the sea, and it's a little bit him.
textes.Il est resté dans le tunnel. Avec ta can: It stayed in the tunnel. With your cinnamon.
textes.Il est revenu de Cliquetis, autrefois, a: Long ago, he came back from Cliquetis with a compass that points south. South! For a tracker, that's a treasure: you always know where you're not going. By the time I went to ask him for it, he'd swapped it in Carène, for a telescope. I haven't quite forgiven him.
textes.Il est revenu me demander une selle pour: He came back to ask me for a saddle for his horse. I couldn't put a saddle on an octopus. So I drew a little hat on the octopus's head. A tricorn, a tiny one. He was delighted. Now he says it's a captain's horse. I can't take any more. But it's my finest octopus.
textes.Il est sept heures zéro deux. Je te pard: It's seven-oh-two. I'll forgive you at oh-three.
textes.Il est tard, oui. Mais la nuit a ses sec: It's late, yes. But the night has its secrets.
textes.Il est tard. Des rubans partout, un vent: It's late. Ribbons everywhere, a fan asleep in its corner, and a giant kite waiting for the Wind Festival.
textes.Il est tombé, Léonce. Ce n'est pas parei: He fell, Léonce. It's not the same.
textes.Il est tout petit, Grégoire ! C'est de l: It's tiny, Grégoire! It's called rigour!
It's very fragile, that button. Come in.
textes.Il est venu me demander de garder la Gra: He came and asked to guard the Great Gate with me. I looked at him for an hour without saying a thing. He talked the whole hour. I said: “No. You smile too much.” He went off to guard the hall. He still smiles. He even smiles on duty. Hmph.
textes.Il est venu me faire une offre, un matin: He came to make me an offer one morning, with his waxed moustache and a wad of papers. “A prestige boutique, dear Babette! Shop windows! Hats!” I listened to the end. Then I offered him an apple. He took it, bit into it, and said: “It's exceptional.” He left. With the apple. He never came back with his papers.
textes.Il est venu me saluer dans la clairière,: He came to greet me in the clearing, Gaston on his shoulder and only one boot on. He asked me if elves ate shells. I said we mostly ate flowers. The next day, he brought me a bouquet. Of shells. I kept it.
textes.Il est venu un matin, sans un mot, et il: He came one morning, without a word, and tugged me by the sleeve all the way to a great ceiba. In the trunk, a wild swarm, enormous. He hadn't touched it. We brought it back together, slowly. He carried the log, I talked to the bees. When we arrived, he said: “You talk too much.” Then: “They like it.”
textes.Il est à toi ! Prends-en soin, et le jou: It's yours! Take good care of it, and the day you don't need it anymore, bring it back. It loves to travel.
textes.Il existait. Mais le vôtre a de très jol: It did. But yours has very pretty ribs.
textes.Il existera quand tu m'auras donné la cr: He will exist once you've given me the crust.
textes.Il fait beau ! Il fait gris ! Il fait qu: It's sunny! It's grey! It's doing something! It's a day! I LOVE DAYS!
textes.Il fait bon. Les heures passent tranquil: It's pleasant out. The hours drift by.
textes.Il fait ce qu'il peut. Comme toi. Viens: It's doing what it can. Like you. Come and sit down.
textes.Il fait chaud comme en été, ici ! Dehors: It's as hot as summer in here! Outside it's summer too. But in here, it's the summeriest summer.
textes.Il fait des bulles quand il rit !: He blows bubbles when he laughs!
textes.Il fait frais, sur la Haute-Ville. Le ve: It's chilly in the Upper Town. The wind comes up from the sea and back down the stairs.
textes.Il fait frais. Ma cape est un peu roussi: It's chilly. My cape is a bit singed, but it keeps me warm.
textes.Il fait noir, mais je n'ai pas peur ! Je: It's dark, but I'm not afraid! I'll sing to prove it! TRA LA LA! … It echoes.
It's dark… I'm not afraid of the dark. I'm afraid of what it hides. That's different.
textes.Il fait noir… Tu entends ce bruit ? C'ét: It's dark… Do you hear that noise? That was my tummy. I think.
textes.Il fait nuit dans la chambre aux papillo: It's night in the butterfly room. They're all asleep on the flowers… and the child, on the sofa, is still counting in dreamland.
textes.Il fait nuit dans la jungle de l'apparte: It's night in the jungle flat. A child is asleep in an armchair, among the giant strawberry plants.
textes.Il fait nuit dans le salon. Seul un peti: It's dark in the living room. Only a little white cloud glows above a sleeping child. Someone shushes you, finger to lips.
textes.Il fait nuit, mais on ne dort pas encore: It's night, but nobody's asleep yet. Beneath dozens of motionless chimes, an old couple is listening to the silence. “Open it ever so gently…”
textes.Il fait nuit. Au tableau noir, les prévi: It's night. On the blackboard, tomorrow's forecast is already drawn. A grandfather shushes you: the little one is asleep in front of the big window.
textes.Il fait nuit. Deux vieux musiciens dorme: It's night. Two old musicians are asleep in their armchairs, facing the big window. Above them, dozens of chimes wait for the wind, without a sound.
textes.Il fait nuit. Je reste tout près de toi,: It's night. I'll stay right next to you, if you don't mind.
textes.Il fait si noir… Je reste tout près de v: It's so dark… I'll stay right next to you. Right next. Sorry, I stepped on your foot.
textes.Il fait sombre ! Heureusement, ma bravou: It's dark! Luckily, my bravery shines. A bit. Take the lantern anyway.
textes.Il fait sombre. Je peux faire une petite: It's dark. I can make a little light. Bzzt. There. It crackles a bit.
textes.Il faudra le plier en quatre pour le sor: We'll have to fold it in four to get it out.
textes.Il faudra leur parler de la Fête des Ven: We'll have to tell them about the Wind Festival.
You'll have to come and see for yourself.
Everyone has to be kept covered.
textes.Il faut courir trois pas, lâcher la fice: You run three steps, let the string out gently, and say thank you to the wind. Lili says the thank-you is the most important part.
textes.Il faut posséder au moins un des quatre: You must own at least one of the four seals.
textes.Il faut que je monte voir !: I have to climb up and see!
I need to tighten his bolts.
textes.Il faut {prix} rondelles, et tu en as {p: It takes {prix} discs, and you have {pieces}… I don't understand why that matters, but apparently it does. Come back later!
He'll make a great underground juggler.
textes.Il file par la fenêtre de derrière dès q: He slips out the back window as soon as he sees me coming. One evening, I searched the whole Shark's Tooth for him. His wooden leg was sticking out from under Sylvain's big table. I could have pulled him out by it. I didn't. A man hiding under a table is ashamed enough already. But I gave him time to get cramp.
textes.Il finit quand, l'abordage ?: When does it end, this boarding?
textes.Il forge en cachette un boulon à six pan: He's secretly forging a six-sided bolt with a “P” engraved on it. He hides it behind furnace number three. I tidy up around it every evening, so as not to find it.
textes.Il garde la chaleur du jour dans ses pie: It keeps the day's heat in its stones. But for the sugar puffs, Gustave wants real sunshine. He says they can tell.
textes.Il goûte ta main. Elle est sucrée ?: It's tasting your hand. Is it sweet?
textes.Il grandit tous les soirs, ton doigt, je: That finger of yours grows every night, if you ask me.
textes.Il grince ?! C'est un violon de Crémone: Squeaks?! It's a Cremona violin! Well, from Cremona-on-Sea! It weeps, it laughs, it sings! It does NOT squeak! (He hugs his violin, offended.)
textes.Il hoche la tête. Ça prend trois semaine: He nods his head. It takes three weeks.
textes.Il joue mieux que toi, ce vent. Mais tu: This wind plays better than you. But you conduct better than it does.
textes.Il l'a traversée, Ix Kanul. Comme chaque: It made it through, Ix Kanul. Like every night.
It found it. In my cauldron.
He has it… under his arm. It's a start.
textes.Il laisse des miettes de gomme partout s: He leaves eraser crumbs all over my table. He draws, he rubs out, he draws again: a city, a crystal, columns. The day he finally spoke, it was to explain the crystal to me. A whole hour. I closed the terrace late. I didn't understand a thing. It was very beautiful, all the same.
textes.Il laisse toujours un pourboire « munici: He always leaves a “municipal” tip. One coin, set down nice and straight on the saucer, with a little speech: “For the staff of the Square, on behalf of the town.” The staff is me. One day, I gave him the coin back: “For the broken cups, on behalf of the café.” He laughed about it for a week.
textes.Il laisse toujours une pièce sous son bo: He always leaves a coin under his bowl, “for a stranger's soup”. For twenty-five years. One day, I asked him who that stranger was. He said: “The one who hasn't arrived yet.” Since then, I always keep a bowl warm. For him. For the stranger.
textes.Il lisait le codex des Soleils devant ma: He was reading the codex of the Suns in front of my class. He said “wind” instead of “water”. I coughed, just a little. He reread it, he corrected it. That evening, he thanked me. I said I had a frog in my throat. He looked at me: “Frogs don't cough.” I said: “Then it was a xolo.”
textes.Il lui a fallu onze essais pour réussir: It took him eleven tries to get my needles right. Eleven! He never grumbled. On the eleventh, he held them out to me on his big palm, and I said: “Perfect.” He blushed to the ears. To thank him, I tattooed a little anvil on his forearm. He didn't move for three hours. I think he was asleep. He says he was thinking.
It's a finger short. I measured.
textes.Il m'a acheté trois pommes. Je les ai em: He bought three apples from me. I wrapped them in paper, as I do for everyone, and I charged him for the paper. One penny. He looked at the paper, he paid. The next week, I took him my cheese knife to sharpen. He charged me for the sharpening. To the penny. I said nothing. Hm.
textes.Il m'a apporté mes quatre cents clous da: He brought me my four hundred nails in a bucket, still hot. I counted them one by one, in front of him, on a plank. It took an hour. He didn't move. At four hundred, I nodded. He nodded. He left. That was the best conversation I've had on this island. And one of the longest.
textes.Il m'a apporté un bouquet. Du persil et: He brought me a bouquet. Parsley and coriander, tied with a bit of ship's string. I said: “It's parsley.” He said: “I know. You can't eat roses.” I put it in a pot, on the stall. In the evening, I sold it. But it stayed there all day.
textes.Il m'a apporté une focaccia pour s'excus: He brought me a focaccia to apologise for the last strike too many. It was half eaten. He said he'd tasted it to check.
textes.Il m'a appris une chanson du désert, une: He taught me a desert song, a slow song that walks like a camel. He played it to me three times. I sing it twice too fast, and he looks at me as if I were pushing a caravan along. He says sand slows everything down. Me, I come from the sea: the sea pushes.
textes.Il m'a appris une vieille coutume : glis: He taught me an old custom: slipping a coin under the foot of the mainmast, for the ship's luck. He says Barbe-Sanglante did it on all his ships. I put a silver coin under the mast of the Merciless. Silas looked, and he said: “She'll float again.” He's the only one, besides me, who says it without laughing.
He taught me how to tie a sailor's knot. I tied Nonna's cat to the vine trellis. Not tight. The cat said “meow.” The Captain said “well done, now untie it.”
textes.Il m'a appris à faire un poing : le pouc: He taught me how to make a fist: thumb outside, or it hurts. I tried it on one of Mange-Clous's flour sacks. The sack didn't feel a thing. I did. Gros-Louis blew on my hand and said it was a very good fist, but flour is a fearsome opponent. Since then, my fist stays in my pocket.
textes.Il m'a appris à faire voler un cerf-vola: He taught me to fly a kite in a north wind. He says Séraphin did the same. He let go of the string, laughed, and said: “There, that's how the island went up.”
textes.Il m'a appris à reconnaître le bruit de: He taught me to recognise the sound of every rail. He says rails sing, if you listen carefully. Now I can hear them. Ludovic's right: everything talks, down here.
textes.Il m'a appris à écrire mon nom. Après, i: He taught me to write my name. Then he rubbed it out. I had to write it again. Now I write it everywhere, even in the sand.
textes.Il m'a arrêté sur le quai, carnet à la m: He stopped me on the quay, notebook in hand: “Running on a public thoroughfare.” I asked him to read me the regulations. He read them: “No bicycles on the quay.” I looked at my legs, I looked at the sergeant. No wheels. The next day, there was a slate: “Runners: walking pace.” I overtake it with a salute.
textes.Il m'a bénie une fois avec la louche. El: He blessed me once with the ladle. It was full of sauce. I was blessed right down to my knees.
textes.Il m'a commandé un crocodile en argile,: He ordered a life-size clay crocodile from me, to scare the real ones. I made a very handsome crocodile, with every one of its teeth. Hapou set it up at the edge of his field. The next morning, a real crocodile was sleeping beside it, with its head resting on mine. Hapou says they were fighting. I say they'd found each other.
textes.Il m'a commandé une jarre pour garder se: He ordered a jar from me to keep his fish alive. He put a perch in it, and it still lives there, apparently. He calls it Ptah. Ptah! Like the god! Like me! I went to see it, to check the jar. The jar is perfect. The perch has a crooked face. I don't see the resemblance.
textes.Il m'a confié que les pommes du mardi so: He told me that Tuesday apples are the sweetest. Tuesday is the day I come. I didn't say a word. I went as red as a pippin.
textes.Il m'a demandé : « Tu crois que Barnabé: He asked me: “Do you think Barnabé could glide, one day?” I said: “If he's got a good pal beside him.” He said: “He has.” He meant himself. He was right.
He asked me how many stars there are. I told him: “Count them.” He came back the next morning, red-eyed: “One thousand and eleven! Plus Xan, who flew in front of the moon.” I wrote the number in my tables. With Xan. For science. A mosquito in front of the moon is an observation.
textes.Il m'a demandé comment Rê vainc Apophis: He asked me how Rê defeats Apophis every night. I told him. He told me that for them, the sun fights the stars. We thought for a long while, and we agreed on just one thing: being a sun is an exhausting job. He laughed. I don't think that happens to him often.
textes.Il m'a demandé de lui rapporter quelque: He asked me to bring him something “really from the bottom”. I brought him up an old copper button from the Léviathan, with an anchor on it. He sewed it onto his hat, crooked, with fishing line. He says it's his captain's medal. He shows it to everyone.
textes.Il m'a demandé de mesurer sa passoire do: He asked me to measure his golden colander. Forty-two centimetres. He said: “That's the perfect number.” I didn't dare contradict him.
textes.Il m'a demandé de mettre en couleur sa c: He asked me to colour his map of Port-Azur, the one the mayor gives to visitors. I painted the sea in six blues: the port blue, the bay blue, the open-sea blue… He held the map at arm's length, eyes shining: “It's the first map that looks wet.” I nearly cried.
textes.Il m'a demandé de peindre une rime sur s: He asked me to paint a rhyme on his door. I didn't know how you paint a rhyme. I painted two dots, side by side. He was delighted.
textes.Il m'a demandé la recette. Je lui ai dit: He asked me for the recipe. I told him: “A ladle of mushrooms, a ladle of love, and Excalibur.” He wrote “Excalibur” in his notebook. Apparently he's still looking for where to buy it.
textes.Il m'a demandé les plans de son auberge,: He asked me for plans of his inn, with real beds and a sign. I drew twelve rooms. He added in pencil, in a corner: “My aunt's room, with a stove.” He thinks I didn't see. I went over it in ink.
textes.Il m'a demandé pourquoi je n'arrive pas: He asked me why I can't paint the pink. I explained the light, the sad tubes, the evening that keeps moving. He thought about it, then said: “Pink is when blue and red give each other a kiss.” I tried it. It didn't work. But I've never heard a better theory.
textes.Il m'a demandé pourquoi je pleurais en é: He asked me why I cried when peeling onions, and he didn't. I told him it was because I was old. The next day, he cried over the onions, and asked me, all worried, if he was old now. I told him no: they were grown-up onions. He was delighted.
textes.Il m'a demandé pourquoi les jarres de Tl: He asked me why Tlaloc's jars have fangs. I told him: to guard the rain, like a dog guards the house. He looked at Tlaco, hairless and without very terrible fangs, and said: “So Tlaco is a jar.” Since then, he calls him “my little jar”. Tlaco seems to agree.
textes.Il m'a demandé quel jour il fallait hono: He asked me on which day the Serpent should be honoured. I gave him the date from our calendar. He took out his. It wasn't the same. We called Ah Kin Pech, who calculated on his fingers all afternoon. He concluded that both dates were right. Nobody was happy.
textes.Il m'a demandé s'il pouvait porter mon b: He asked if he could carry my shield. I lent it to him. He disappeared behind it. All you could see were his feet and the tip of Tlaco's tail. He said, from behind the shield: “I'm invincible!” He stepped forward and fell into a basket of chillies. Invincible, but not very nimble.
textes.Il m'a demandé trois fois de voir le tab: He's asked me three times to see the galleon painting. The first time as the caïd, the second out of curiosity. The third time, he came with tea. I drank the tea. I didn't show the painting: I promised. But the tea was delicious, and he was so embarrassed. That memory, I'm keeping.
textes.Il m'a demandé un jour : « Amirale, si j: He once asked me: “Admiral, if I repair the Léviathan, can I be captain?” I answered: “If you repair it, you'll be admiral.” He thought about it, and said: “No. Captain's better: you're on the ship.” He's right. I didn't tell him.
