textes.Il m'a demandé un jour : « Docteur, quel: He asked me one day: “Doctor, what will the weather be like for my hundredth birthday?” I replied: “Bright sunshine, at six minutes past two.” He said: “Write it down.” I wrote it down. I hope I'm wrong about everything, except that.
textes.Il m'a demandé un jour pourquoi je resta: He once asked me why I always stay until the last verse, when everyone else leaves at the thirtieth. I thought about it. I said: “To find out how it ends.” He laughed. Then he turned bright red. I don't know why. I ate a cake.
textes.Il m'a demandé un jour pourquoi les plan: One day he asked me why plants were slow. I said: “Because they take the time to do things properly.” He said: “Like me.” I said yes. He beeped twice. That's his way of smiling.
textes.Il m'a demandé un jour si je regrettais: One day he asked me if I missed the sea. I said no. Pesto said “RAMEN.” The Reverend said: “Your parrot is more honest than you are.”
textes.Il m'a demandé un sac de sel, pour son c: He asked me for a sack of salt, for his cook. I sold him one. Lovely sand from the east beach, nice and dry, nice and white. He paid without looking. Sixty years after the first sack! His grandfather, at least, had tasted it before paying. I told him: “You have his eyes. Not his nerve.” He didn't speak to me for three days. He came back.
textes.Il m'a demandé une médaille « on verra »: He asked me for a “we'll see” medal. I forged it. It says on it: “We'll see.” He wears it. He's very proud of it.
textes.Il m'a dessiné une carte du Bois-Doré sa: He drew me a map of Bois-Doré without ever having been there. Everything's wrong: the trees, the walkways, the number of moons. Except the Mother Tree, exactly in its place. I hung it at home, above my bed.
textes.Il m'a dessiné une rose des vents à seiz: He drew me a sixteen-point compass rose, with a mermaid in the north and a whale in the south. I tattooed it on an old helmsman's arm, smaller, without a single mistake. Philémon came to look. He looked for a long time, with his magnifying glass. He said: “It's better than the original.” He was offended. The next day, he drew me another one. Even more beautiful.
textes.Il m'a dicté la ballade du roi Atlas. Le: He dictated the ballad of King Atlas to me. The next day, I was singing it in the square, and in the third verse, Protée stood up in the front row: “No, no, now it's a queen, and she has an octopus!” Everyone laughed. I carried on with the octopus. I'm a professional.
textes.Il m'a dicté un jour : « Par ordre du ro: One day he dictated: “By order of the king, fizz is a royal treasure.” I wrote: “Fizz is a treasure.” He shouted: “Where did royal go?” I said: “Ulfa would never have put it up.” He thought about it, he laughed, he signed. The decree still hangs above the counter at the Mug.
textes.Il m'a dit que j'avais le même froncemen: He told me I had the same frown as his brother when he tastes his chocolate. I frowned. He laughed so hard the machine whistled.
textes.Il m'a donné jusqu'à la fin de l'été pou: He's given me until the end of summer to find the chest. Otherwise, the crew will vote. Every morning, he says to me: “Hm. End of summer.” The way other people say good morning. I answer: “I can count.” I can count. There are… plenty of days left. Enough. Well. A few.
textes.Il m'a donné ses lunettes d'aviateur, se: He gave me his flying goggles, his real ones! They're too big, so Dad tied them behind my head with a shoelace. I wear them all the time, even to sleep. Mum says I've got a mark round my eyes, like a raccoon. It's an inventor's mark.
textes.Il m'a donné un crayon enduit de cire et: He gave me a wax-coated pencil and a little board, to draw underwater. I tried. My drawing looked like a poorly octopus. He framed it. It hangs in the harbour master's office, next to the big map. When people ask him what it is, he says: “A discovery.”
textes.Il m'a emmené en pédalo, « pour voir la: He took me out in a pedalo, “to see the coast from below”. He pedalled, I looked. After three metres, I felt the sea rising in my throat. After four, I was leaning over the side. He turned round, singing. I've never been so far from home.
textes.Il m'a emprunté l'Atlas des étoiles fixe: He borrowed my Atlas of the Fixed Stars. He returned it eleven years later, with corrections in ink in the margins: three stars moved. He told me, delighted, that they had shifted. Fixed stars! In ink! I had to buy a new atlas. He wrote corrections in that one too. In pencil, this time. He's making progress.
textes.Il m'a envoyé mon nom en hiéroglyphes :: He sent me my name in hieroglyphs: a star and a little sun. I answered with a drawing: a bald old man, with a reed, and a hippopotamus head. Nebet, the little girl from Per-Hâpy, had told me the nickname. He wrote to me that it was the finest portrait anyone had ever made of him. And the only one.
textes.Il m'a envoyé un dessin de sa grande lun: He sent me a drawing of his big telescope, with a little arrow: “Here, your crystal.” And another arrow, next to it: “Here, Clémentine.” I don't know who Clémentine is. I'm still cutting him the finest lens of my life.
textes.Il m'a envoyé une pomme, une seule, avec: He sent me an apple, just one, with a note: “It ripened in the sun. It'll tell you all about it.” I kept it three days before eating it. It told it very well.
textes.Il m'a envoyé une tasse de son chocolat,: He sent me a cup of his hot chocolate, with a note: “Try a real drink, Madam.” It arrived cold. I warmed it up, added a pinch of salt. I sent it back. He replied: “Not bad.” Coming from him, that's a medal.
textes.Il m'a envoyé, par la cabine, le premier: He sent me the machine's first hot chocolate, by the cabin. With a note: “She whistles a bit.” I drank it laughing. I kept the cup. It still smells of steam.
textes.Il m'a eue. Il m'a bandé les yeux pour m: He got me. He blindfolded me to make me taste “a spice blend on bread”. I tasted. I said: “Delicious. What cumin!” He took off the blindfold. A sardine. A SARDINE! I left shrieking, and Saïd heard everything. But it was my cumin. The cumin was delicious, so there.
textes.Il m'a fait coucou, Odon ! Enfin, il a f: He waved at me, Odon! Well, he went blop.
textes.Il m'a fait goûter son premier pain, il: He had me taste his first loaf of bread, forty years ago. It was as hard as an anchor. I kept it. I use it as a paperweight.
textes.Il m'a fait visiter le phare un jour de: He showed me round the lighthouse on a gloriously sunny day. “House with sea view, natural lift of a hundred and forty steps, winged housemates.” I signed before reaching the top, because I was too out of breath to think. The first night, the wind blew all the windows open. The seagulls came in. Albertine slept on my pillow. I've never slept so well.
textes.Il m'a fallu dix ans pour tisser le lin: It took me ten years to weave royal linen, the kind you can see through. The day I managed it, I held the cloth up to the sun, and I saw Ra through it, all soft, as if behind a cloud. I cried, I think. Since then, the temple orders its linen from me. And Néferet wears only my robes.
textes.Il m'a fallu huit ans pour le finir. Qua: It took me eight years to finish it. Four hundred gears, thousands of punch cards. First public match at the Fair, fourteen years ago: it beat Héloïse in twenty-three moves. Since then, it has never lost a game of chess. Three Cogs of Honour in a row. As for the stone game of the mist people… we shan't speak of it.
textes.Il m'a fallu quatre cents ans pour compr: It took me four hundred years to understand the language of plants. One blink means yes. Two means thank you. Three means “water me”. One long, very slow blink is a joke. Plants have a great sense of humour, but you have to be patient: a flower's joke lasts half a day. The punchline is often very good.
textes.Il m'a forgé une plaque pour ma planche: He forged me a plate for my board with my name on it: “RESORT”. There's an S missing. We didn't say anything. I think it's even nicer. It sounds like a skater name.
textes.Il m'a frappé ! Vous avez vu ?!: He hit me! Did you see?!
textes.Il m'a gagné ma boussole d'argent à la D: He won my silver compass from me at the Shark's Tooth: three sixes against my three fives. He wears it round his neck, like a medal. Every time I pass, he opens it and says: “North is that way, captain.” Since then, the Widow sails by the sun and the stars. She sails very well. Hm. Better, even. But that's not the point.
textes.Il m'a invitée à l'Observatoire pour voi: He invited me to the Observatory to watch a comet go by. I brought a book, just in case. He talked all night: about the stars, his grandfather, fireflies. I didn't read a single page. The comet went by at three o'clock. It was nice. I didn't need the book.
textes.Il m'a laissé tenir son épée, une fois,: He let me hold his sword, once, in the castle courtyard. It was super heavy. He told me: “A sword, Titouan, is heavy because you also carry the people you protect.” I repeated it to Mum. She said it was very beautiful. She also said it was because it was thick steel. Both, I think.
textes.Il m'a mis au défi d'aller voir ses lumi: He dared me to go and see his green lights in the graveyard, at night. I went! Well, as far as the gate. I heard a little noise, clack clack, like bones. I ran back, to check something at the harbour. And I still say they're fireflies. Fireflies with bones, maybe.
textes.Il m'a montré son premier poème : un chi: He showed me his first poem: a puppy, rhymed with “puppy”. I read it three times. He was looking at me with such hopeful eyes that I said: “That's a rich rhyme.” He smiled like a child. Later, Ombreline explained to him what a rich rhyme is. He came back to tell me: “Thank you for lying kindly.”
textes.Il m'a offert un cornet en cuivre, pour: He gave me a copper ear trumpet, to hear better. I put it to my ear. He talked into it. I understood nothing: he mumbles even into a trumpet! So I use it to pour powder into my cannons. Doesn't spill. Best present of my life. I never told him. He knows. He knows everything, that man.
textes.Il m'a offert un pépin de son grand pomm: He gave me a pip from his big apple tree, Lady Ysolde's. I planted it in the middle of the first dome. It's three centimetres tall. It's small, tough and proud. Just as Old Bastien said it would be.
textes.Il m'a offert un tambourin pour mon anni: He gave me a tambourine for my birthday. I can't play it. I use it as a rest for the ladle.
textes.Il m'a peint une enseigne : « Pain chaud: He painted me a sign: “Hot bread”. He put the sign for cat instead. A whole week of “cat bread”! The children came to see if the loaves meowed. Nebet ordered one with a tail. I made it, with ears too. I've never sold so much. I kept the sign behind the oven. For bad days.
textes.Il m'a percé une lanterne spéciale. Quan: He pierced me a special lantern. When it's lit, there's a sultan on the wall, a sardine, and a little djinn coming out of the sardine. The children in the circle shriek when I turn it. So do I, a bit. I asked him what I owed him. He said: “The end of the story. I've never heard it.”
textes.Il m'a proposé un jour de jouer sa Morue: One day he offered to bet his Cod against my Shark. A sloop against a galleon! I told him: “A shark against a cod, my friend, we know who eats whom.” He laughed so hard all his teeth shone. The next day, he offered again. He offers again every week. It's become his way of saying hello.
textes.Il m'a prêté sa longue-vue en cuivre, ce: He lent me his copper spyglass, the one with a star engraved on it. I put it on a crate to look for my glasses, and Gros-Louis sat on the crate. The spyglass has a little bend in it now. Philémon says it can see behind rocks. He was very nice about it. He only cried a little.
textes.Il m'a raconté le grand feu des dieux, à: He told me about the great fire of the gods, at Teotihuacan: Tecciztécatl, covered in gold and feathers, who backs away from the fire, and little Nanahuatzin who jumps. I said I would have jumped first. He asked me: “With your feathers, or without?” I didn't know what to answer. I'm still thinking. My feathers are very beautiful.
textes.Il m'a raconté qu'il avait avalé un clou: He told me he'd swallowed a nail, for real, and that's why he's called Mange-Clous, Nail-Eater. I wanted to try it with a nail made of breadcrumb. It was tasty! Mange-Clous said I was the first cabin boy to eat a nail without ending up at Doc's. He called me “Crumb-Eater” all day.
textes.Il m'a raconté qu'il avait combattu une: He told me he'd fought a whale. I divided by three: he saw a big fish. That's not bad already.
textes.Il m'a raconté qu'il avait vaincu le Géa: He told me he'd defeated the Mist Giant. I wanted to check. I went to the northern hills, into the fog. I found a big rock with a helmet mark on it, and a shepherd who told me: “Ah yes, the knight! He was very brave, with that rock.” I never told him I knew.
textes.Il m'a rapporté de sa grande traversée u: He brought me back a black pebble from the highlands after his great crossing, telling me it was ore. It was coal. I said nothing: I put it in the forge, and on its fire I forged him a pair of compasses for his maps. He still doesn't know his ore was coal.
textes.Il m'a rapporté un seau de mer. J'ai mis: He brought me back a bucket of sea. I kept my hands in it for an hour. It's the best present in the world. After Grandpa's shell. And after an ice cream, when I get one.
textes.Il m'a signalé un jour une île au nord,: He once reported an island to the north, shaped like a three-master. I added it to my big map, in dotted lines: “Probable island, sighted by Fil-de-Fer”. The next day, Captain Anne-Rose informed me it was a cloud. I left the island. I just drew a tiny sheep on it. He doesn't hold it against me. I think.
textes.Il m'a taillé un peigne dans une branche: He carved me a comb from a branch that fell from his kapok tree. He repeated three times: “Fallen. Not cut.” I wear it every day. In Bois-Doré, people ask me which elf carved it. I answer: a bear.
textes.Il m'a vendu des graines de courge « qui: He sold me squash seeds “that give squash as big as canoes”. They gave normal squash. I went to complain. He measured a squash with his arms, very seriously, and he said: “A little canoe. For a child.” I laughed. He refunded me half. That's a lot, for Tochtli.
textes.Il m'a vendu une « plume de quetzal », t: He sold me a “quetzal feather”, very expensive, for my festival headdress. It ran at the first rain. A parrot feather, painted. I went to the tianguis and gave it back to him, on his head, in front of his customers. He said it was a test, to see if I could recognise a real one. Me, I recognise a real cousin.
textes.Il m'a vendu une « tisane en fiole », to: He sold me a “herbal tea in a vial”, ready-made, blue. I tasted it, then poured it on my tomatoes. They turned blue. Huge, blue, and delicious. I gave him a basketful, without a word of explanation. He didn't ask. He'd be quite capable of selling them.
textes.Il m'a vendu « la conque d'Ehécatl ». J': He sold me “the conch of Ehécatl”. I blew into it in front of the whole square. It squeaked! Like a frightened mouse! It was a snail shell from the lake. I laughed so hard I fell back onto my drum. Boom. I kept it. It makes the children laugh. My best purchase. Don't tell him, he'd put up the price of his snails.
textes.Il m'a écrit une lettre : « Bonjour, Plu: He wrote me a letter: “Hello, Plumeau. Hello, trees.” I read it to the trees. They dropped three leaves. I kept them in a drawer. They are the only leaves I do not recycle.
textes.Il m'a écrit une lettre de protestation: He wrote me a six-page letter of complaint. I set it to music. It became “The Complainant's Lament”. It's my most requested song. He heard it one evening without knowing it was his letter. He said: “That one's very good. Something serious at last.” I've never dared tell him.
textes.Il m'apporte le minerai des pentes rouge: He brings me ore from the red slopes, and every time he forgets a sack somewhere on the mountain. Once, he forgot Fundin. Fundin came back the next day, black as soot, with the sack and a bat in his hood. I paid Grimli anyway. The ore was good.
textes.Il m'arrive de m'endormir à ma table l'a: Sometimes I fall asleep at my table in the afternoon, my cheek on my star charts. When I wake up, there's always a cushion under my head, and the coffee machine has stopped whistling. Gaston turns off the whistle for me. The whole café drinks in silence. Nobody complains. It's the only café on the island where people whisper for an astronomer.
textes.Il m'avait dit que 13 Ahau était un jour: He told me 13 Ahau was an excellent day for my match. I lost, three balls to nil. I went to see him, furious. He opened his tables, read for a long time, and said: “Excellent for the other team.” Now I always ask him: “Good for whom?” He says that's an excellent question.
textes.Il m'en a parlé trois fois. Ton bras gra: He told me three times. Is your arm itching?
I still need {manque}, {surnom}. My cauldron is waiting.
textes.Il m'en manque {manque}. Elles brillent: I'm still missing {manque}. They shine like tiny little moons lying on the ground.
textes.Il m'envoie des corbeaux à minuit avec d: He sends me crows at midnight with very important messages. “The king is hungry.” “The king requests cheese.” “The king asks whether the cheese is asleep.” One night, I sent Croâ back with a cheese tied to his leg. Croâ ate it on the way. The king thanked me for the crow.
textes.Il m'échange une lampe de nacre chaque s: Every week he trades me a mother-of-pearl lamp for my crackers. He thinks I resell them. I've kept them all. Thirty-seven lamps, lit, in my house. At night it looks like a little crystal. If you tell him, I'll charge you double for life.
textes.Il m'écoute moi, ou il t'écoute toi ?: Is he listening to me, or is he listening to you?
There are two pieces missing from the board.
textes.Il manque encore {manque_liste}. Ne te p: We're still missing {manque_liste}. Don't hurry: the Tree is patient, even when it's ill.
textes.Il manque encore {manque} Perles de Lumi: {manque} Pearls of Light are still missing. The crystal is waiting patiently. So am I.
textes.Il manque la mer. Elle ne rentre pas dan: The sea is missing. It doesn't fit in your speakers.
textes.Il manque toujours le bout du sud ?: Still missing the bit in the south?
textes.Il manque un pêcheur, Fernand !: What's missing is a fisherman, Fernand!
There's a ruby missing tonight, Ulfa.
textes.Il manque un truc. Je te dirai quand je: Something's missing. I'll tell you when I know.
textes.Il me fallait la pointure exacte de Rach: I needed Rachid's exact shoe size. I know it, of course, but Samira wanted to measure herself. So one afternoon, while he napped on his own carpets, she tiptoed over with a ribbon. He snored the whole time. That evening, he told everyone he'd dreamt of a cat tickling his feet.
textes.Il me faut du bois droit pour mes flèche: I need straight wood for my arrows. Bring me {manque} good straight sticks and I'll pay you. Honestly.
textes.Il me faut du bois, oui. Une voie d'eau: I need wood, yes. A leak has opened under the forge, on the port side: nothing serious, but if I don't plug it, Jos will end the week with his feet in the water. Four logs. Good wood, not driftwood. An axe, a tree, and back you come.
textes.Il me faut du fer. Toujours du fer. Les: I need iron. Always iron. The northern shepherds have hills full of it and sell it one drop at a time.
I need more of your ochre.
textes.Il me faut encore {manque_liste}. Courag: I still need {manque_liste}. Courage: the Tree is waiting for you. It never complains, but I can hear it sigh.
textes.Il me faut encore {manque} dents de requ: I still need {manque} shark teeth. Keep going!
textes.Il me faut {manque} runes. Pas une de mo: I need {manque} runes. Not one less. A gate doesn't open halfway.
textes.Il me manque des fleurs de braise pour m: I'm short of ember flowers for my flowerbeds. They only grow on the slopes of the volcano, where the ground smokes. I'd need five to make a fine bed. My old legs don't climb up there any more. Yours, perhaps?
textes.Il me manque des pièces. Les robots de L: I'm short of parts. Lisse's robots picked the Scrapyard clean to build their arms. Without parts, my bikes are just sculptures. Ferraille is jealous.
I'm out of wild honey, {surnom}. Could you find me {manque} combs? In the hollow trees on your island, when you chop wood. I'll bake you bread in return!
textes.Il me manque encore {manque_liste}. La f: I'm still missing {manque_liste}. The moonflower only grows at the top of the little jungle peak, the one that looks over the bay. The water: draw it with the vial from the pool of the big waterfall, in the north-east of this island. And the golden seed… the waves carried it off long ago. Perhaps a collector picked it up?
textes.Il me manque encore {manque} champignons: I still need {manque} mushrooms. Patience: the forest is full of them.
textes.Il me manque encore {manque} minerais. P: I still need {manque} ores. No iron, no sword. That's the law of the anvil.
textes.Il me manque encore {manque} rayons de m: I still need {manque} honeycombs. Keep going, my oven is waiting for you!
textes.Il me manque {manque} éclats d'obsidienn: I still need {manque} obsidian shards. The runes are waiting.
textes.Il me paie en fèves et il les compte lui: He pays me in beans and counts them himself, out loud, very fast. I count again after him: one is missing. Always one. He told me it was the moon's fault, it had a day less that month. The moon doesn't drink cacao! Since then, he gives me an extra bean, “for the moon”. I put it aside. The moon owes me a lot.
textes.Il me paie en plumes de corbeau pour vér: He pays me in raven quills to check his old maps. Nine times out of ten, it's a fake. Once, just once, he brought me a real portolan chart, very old, with a whale drawn in one corner. My hands were shaking. Isaac saw. He sold it to me for the price of one quill. I still don't understand why.
textes.Il me raconte tout ce qu'il entend sur l: He tells me everything he hears on deck: the islands, the winds, the rumours. Even the seasick goat: “She saw the elves' island, and she threw up.” I wrote it all down. In the margin of my map, near the Bois-Doré, there's a tiny little goat. She's my most reliable source.
textes.Il me rapporte des choses : un coquillag: He brings me things: a shell, a parrot feather, a pearl, a dried starfish. Without a word. He puts them on my table and leaves. My tent is full of them. I don't know who the heart on his arm is for. I've never asked him. Tattooists are like doctors: you don't ask the wrong questions.
textes.Il me reproche d'écrire des histoires mo: He accuses me of writing dead stories. “A true story is a story that has lived.” I asked him for proof. He held a shell to my ear and said: “Listen.” All I heard was the sea. He said: “There. It's all in there.” For once, I didn't write anything down.
textes.Il me reste un pain au chocolat à deux b: I've got one two-bar pain au chocolat left. Quick, before Nina gets back from the fountain!
textes.Il ment. Comme tous les arbres. Et tous: It's lying. Like all trees. And all customers.
textes.Il monte d'un étage et demi ! Le problèm: It goes up a floor and a half! The problem is coming down: Mireille is working on the “landing” part. For now, we hold the string.
textes.Il monte très haut avec ses instruments: It goes up very high with its instruments: temperature, wind, humidity. Doctor Aurèle bases his forecasts on them. And when the balloon bursts, way up high, the little parachute brings the instruments back down. Usually.
textes.Il n'arrive qu'une bouteille de rhum de: Only one bottle of rum from the Murène reaches Berthe's each month. Just one. Pyra and I bet on it: if I saw a serpent before midnight, it was mine. At a quarter to midnight, I saw three. She said they were seaweed. We never settled it. We drank the bottle together, so as not to fall out.
It's not for sale. Same as yesterday.
textes.Il n'est que onze heures et soixante min: It's only eleven o'clock and sixty minutes, Moulay Brahim.
textes.Il n'y a eu qu'une autre exception, il y: There's only been one other exception, a hundred and twenty years ago: “The Pearl of the avenue has vanished. Black ship sunk to the west.” The handwriting shook that evening too. I asked him how it had happened. He said: “I didn't see anything.” Then he looked at his feet for a very long time. I didn't write that down. That's rare.
textes.Il n'y a jamais de détails dans « rien »: There are never any details in “nothing”. That's what saddens me.
textes.Il n'y a jamais eu de dragon, petit. Il: There never was a dragon, lad. There was a very big dwarf.
textes.Il n'y a même pas d'orage, Héloïse !: There isn't even a storm, Héloïse!
There isn't even a storm, Héloïse.
textes.Il n'y a pas d'arbres au désert. Mon boi: There are no trees in the desert. My wood comes from Carène, and they sell it dear. One year, the wood didn't come at all, and the whole fleet had holes. So I went all round town and bought up the old blue doors, one by one. I repaired every boat with them. Even today, some boats have a lock.
There are no trees at the market, Pépin.
textes.Il n'y a pas de rythme pour la dorade. B: There's no rhythm for sea bream. Boom.
textes.Il n'y a personne. Le parquet craque sou: There's nobody. The floorboards creak under your steps. Especially near the rug.
textes.Il n'y a personne. Une maison bien rangé: There's nobody here. A tidy house that smells of wax and bread.
textes.Il n'y a personne… juste une théière sur: There's nobody here… just a teapot on the low table. A teapot with… a bushy tail?
textes.Il n'y a plus rien sous le coussin. Just: There's nothing left under the cushion. Just a bit of cat fur.
textes.Il n'y a rien dans mes poches ! … Enfin,: There's nothing in my pockets! … Well, nothing that goes croak.
textes.Il n'y avait pas de loup dans cette hist: There was no wolf in that story.
There aren't any under my windows.
textes.Il n'y en a pas. J'ai cherché sur toutes: There isn't one. I've looked on all my maps.
textes.Il n'y en a pas. Mais votre billet reste: There isn't one. But your ticket is still valid.
textes.Il nageait près de la paillote du Coco L: He was swimming near the Coco Loco beach hut, where the waves meet the sand. It must be buried there. But you can't get it out with your hands.
textes.Il naît : tout s'éveille.\nIl règne : to:
It is born: everything awakens.
It reigns: everything blazes.
It dies: everything sheds its leaves.
Where it never goes, everything sleeps.
It doesn't move. Its cannons do.
textes.Il ne dit pas grand-chose, mais il siffl: He doesn't say much, but he whistles all the time. The sails turn in time with it. I swear.
textes.Il ne fait ses arcs-en-lune que pour les: He only makes his moonbows for friends.
It isn't smoking. You're the one fuming.
It'll never get through… but shh.
textes.Il ne s'est pas effacé. Il dort. Viens t: It hasn't faded. It's sleeping. Come and sit at the Circle on a clear night. The stones sometimes wake what sleeps. Not always.
It doesn't know how to share. It knows how to win.
textes.Il ne va pas mettre le feu à ta poche ?: Won't it set your pocket on fire?
textes.Il ouvre une noix de coco d'un seul coup: He opens a coconut with a single stroke of the machete, like his grandfather. The first day, he did it in front of my kiosk, to impress me. Whack! Two perfect halves. The juice squirted over my window, my cones and the sergeant. Lefort wanted to fine him for “splashing”. He got an ice cream instead.
textes.Il paie chaque histoire d'une noisette,: He pays for each story with a hazelnut, set nice and straight on my knee, and takes it back when he leaves, “for next time”. One evening, I was the one who fell asleep before him. When I woke up, he'd finished the story by himself, for the other little ones. With a dragon. There's always a dragon, with Gland.
textes.Il paie son ardoise en potions. « Pour l: He pays his tab in potions. “For coughs”, “for low spirits”, “for goats' hooves”. I don't have a goat! I've got a whole shelf of them behind the counter. Once, I opened one by mistake: my saucepans sang all evening. In tune. More in tune than him, anyway.
textes.Il paraît qu'Icare n'a pas marché depuis: Apparently Icare hasn't walked in three years. He glides to the bakery. And glides back, with the baguette.
textes.Il paraît qu'au Phare de la Pointe, chaq: They say every seagull at the Point Lighthouse has a name. The one that stole my sandwich is called Firmin.
textes.Il paraît qu'autrefois, les Gouttières j: Apparently, the Gutters used to play on the Great Stage, with the musicians from the Flower Camp. My mother was there. She says it was the most beautiful concert in the world.
textes.Il paraît qu'il y a cent ans, un tonneau: They say that a hundred years ago, a barrel rolled off a cart onto an elf who'd come to sell wood, and Bramm smiled. I was in the kitchen. I didn't see a thing. I've been watching out ever since. With every bowl, I look at his beard. It twitches, sometimes. I note it all down on my kitchen wall, in chalk.
textes.Il paraît qu'il y a des ruines sous les: They say there are ruins under the roots of the great kapok trees. Stairs that lead nowhere. Or else very far away.
textes.Il paraît qu'il y a un fantôme dans la C: They say there's a ghost in the Rune Crypt! Oscar said so. But Oscar says lots of things.
textes.Il paraît qu'il y a une ville tout au fo: They say there's a city right at the bottom of the sea, under a glass dome, the Azure Dome! With whales swimming over the houses! Their line is closed for works. I'm going down as soon as it reopens. I wrote it on Mum's calendar. In big letters.

They say there's a city right at the bottom of the sea, under a glass dome, the Azure Dome! With whales swimming over the houses! Their line has just reopened. I'm going down as soon as Mum says yes. I wrote it on Mum's calendar. In big letters. On every day.
textes.Il paraît qu'il y aura de la daurade, ve: I hear there'll be sea bream on Friday.
textes.Il paraît qu'on peut voir le Grand Spagh: They say you can see the Great Spaghetti through the holes in the ceiling. I'm looking for the right hole.
textes.Il paraît qu'on trouve des petites croix: They say you can find little wooden crosses on the beaches. Castaways more far-sighted than me buried their savings there.
textes.Il paraît qu'à Cliquetis, ils ont des ch: Apparently in Cliquetis they have spring-loaded shoes. If I had some… No. Pépin would say it's cheating. Pépin's right. But still.
textes.Il paraît qu'à Port-Azur, Django joue de: Word is that in Port-Azur, Django plays waltzes at the Perroquet Bleu. One day we'll do a track together: waltz-techno!
textes.Il paraît qu'à Port-Azur, ils font des c: Apparently in Port-Azur they make croissants. That means “crescent” — bread shaped like a crescent moon! Like ours! But only half.
textes.Il paraît que Faelar a raconté l'histoir: I hear Faelar told the story of the first seed. Again.
textes.Il paraît que Hulotte a vu une étoile to: Apparently Hulotte saw a star fall into the great pool. Me, I think it was a firefly that had drunk too much moon tea.
textes.Il paraît que Mireille a inventé un para: I hear Mireille has invented an umbrella that goes up. I've come to see if it comes back down.
textes.Il paraît que Mistral prépare un morceau: Word is Mistral's working on a track with whale songs. It's going to be huge.
textes.Il paraît que Monsieur Fil, dans les Rue: They say Monsieur Fil, in the Alleys, sells “cheap” programs. Where I come from, we used to say: what's cheap always ends up costing dear. Be careful, little one.
textes.Il paraît que Sept, à la Tour Axiome, da: They say Sept, at the Axiom Tower, dances when he's alone. A camera supposedly caught him doing a little pirouette at three in the morning. I want to see that video.
textes.Il paraît que dans l'archipel, des chien: Apparently, in the archipelago, dogs, cats, rats and even pigs follow heroes everywhere. The Lumens don't have animals. Only sky jellyfish. They don't follow anyone, they float. It's not the same.
textes.Il paraît que dans le désert, il y a des: They say that in the desert there are painted stones. Very old ones. Hunters, animals, and a great round door. I'd so love to see them.
textes.Il paraît que dans les Strates, sous Hau: They say that in the Strata, under Hautefond, there are huge workshops, with forges and rails everywhere. The line is closed for works. As soon as it reopens, I'm going down with my notebook. I've heard they fix everything with three bolts and a song.

They say that in the Strata, under Hautefond, there are huge workshops, forges and rails everywhere. The line has just reopened. I'm going down on Sunday with my notebook. I've heard they fix everything with three bolts and a song.
textes.Il paraît que de l'autre côté de l'île v: They say on the other side of the island lives an old loon who talks to seashells. Barnabé, his name is. Don't believe a word he says about me.
textes.Il paraît que je suis « un peu bizarre »: Apparently I'm “a bit weird”, according to you. It was {qn} who told me. I'll think about it. Or not.

textes.Il paraît que la Capitaine Zéphyrine n'a: They say Captain Zéphyrine has never lost a race. Neither has Héloïse. What times we live in.
textes.Il paraît que la Ligne du Dôme d'Azur, a: They say the Azure Dome Line, down at the bottom, is still closed for works. Me, I've never seen the sea. I'll see the sea from underneath first. That's more original.
textes.Il paraît que la Porte aux Quatre Sceaux: Apparently the Gate of the Four Seals is made of stone, but its hinges are metal. A metal nobody knows. I'd love to see a bit of it.
textes.Il paraît que la Professeure Fusilli a c: Apparently Professor Fusilli has calculated the Great Spaghetti's favourite note. An F. Since then, I only sing F's. The others are a bit fed up.
textes.Il paraît que la ligne des Nuées rouvre: They say the Cloud line is reopening soon. My brother-in-law has been saying that for three years.
textes.Il paraît que la mairesse mange ici en c: They say the mayor eats here in secret, wearing a cap and sunglasses. Everyone recognises her. Nobody says a thing. It's everyone's secret.
textes.Il paraît que la peintre des Nuées, Ombe: They say the painter up in the Clouds, Ombeline, paints the sunset every evening. I've never seen a sunset. She's never seen a mural on rock. We write each other letters with drawings in them. I send her braziers. She sends me suns.
textes.Il paraît que la sauce du volcan est tro: They say the volcano's sauce is too salty this year. Bucatini says it isn't. Bucatini always says it isn't. He tastes it every day; he can't tell what's salty anymore.
textes.Il paraît que le Sergent Fréquence est t: Word is Sergeant Fréquence is shy. So they say. Me, I'm saying nothing. Coo-roo. But he's shy.
textes.Il paraît que le chocolat du frère de Gu: Apparently the hot chocolate from Gustave's brother, down below, whistles like a steam engine. Up here, our chocolate whispers. It's more polite.

textes.Il paraît que tu as frappé {qn}. Je ne d: I hear you hit {qn}. I shouldn't laugh. I laughed anyway.

textes.Il passe au souk, il entend mon tac-tac,: He comes by the souk, hears my tac-tac, and drums along on my stall with his fingertips: tac-tac-boom. One evening, he played the whole festival on my rhythm, and told the whole square where it came from. From Abdellah's, the coppersmith. I was miffed. A little. Then Hnia saw me tapping my foot. She counted.
textes.Il passe parfois une barque, loin, à l'o: Now and then a boat goes by, far off, to the west. It comes from the village islands and the elves. I count them. This year: three. Including you.
textes.Il passe à chaque ronde, les mains dans: He comes by on every patrol, hands behind his back, all casual. He looks at the beach, he looks at the sea, he looks at the vanilla. I hold out a cone. He takes it without a word, like a piece of evidence. Three times a day. Rosalie shouts it all over the port. He says he's “keeping an eye on the kiosk”. Of course he is.
textes.Il penche depuis quatre ans, ton comptoi: Your counter has been sloping for four years.
textes.Il peut me redire le gros mot ?: Can he say the rude word again?
It's crying, more like. It's wet.
textes.Il pleut ? Votre chocolat des jours de p: Is it raining? Your rainy-day hot chocolate is ready. The machine grumbled, but it made it.
It rains inside, it's the atmosphere.
textes.Il pleut souvent, ici ?: Does it rain often, up here?
textes.Il pleut, vous êtes content ? Le bras de: It's raining, are you happy? Wilfried's arm is itching. I've sent him his ointment. I'm keeping a little for you, just in case.
textes.Il pousse à l'ombre des grands arbres. R: It grows in the shade of the tall trees. Restores half a heart.
textes.Il prend le limon de mon champ pour ses: He takes the silt from my field for his jars, and he pays me in jars. I've got forty. Full of barley, flax, seeds, nothing at all. Once, I tried to give him one back. He tapped it, listened for a long time, and said: “It's perfect, keep it.” He taps everything, that potter. Even people.
He promises. Well, he's wagging his tail.
textes.Il pétille sur la langue comme une poign: It fizzes on the tongue like a handful of stars.
textes.Il pêche au pied du phare, maintenant, a: He fishes at the foot of the lighthouse now, at the end of the jetty, just when I go up for my watch. He says it's the best spot. It's true. That annoys me all the more. He whistles. Out of tune. To needle me. One evening I threw a handful of coarse salt at him through the skylight. He said thank you, and salted his sardine.
textes.Il racontait le naufrage du Léviathan de: He told the wreck of the Léviathan standing up, rolling like a ship: left for the wave, right for the wind, and the whole circle rolled with him. When the ship hit land, he dropped down onto the sand. Three old folk of Tazira got seasick. I applauded. I've never dared tell a story lying down.
textes.Il raconte partout que j'ai gagné la Mor: He tells everyone I won the Cod with loaded dice. So I told everyone he'd married his brig because no lady would have him. He went as red as his Widow. Then he said, very quietly: “Just one.” I never made that joke again. We all have a spot where you mustn't press.
textes.Il raconte partout que l'idée de faire f: He tells everyone the idea of making the gunports smoke, against the Murène Noire, was his. It's possible: he whispered it to me at the rail, between two hot honeys. But I was the one who got into the boat. An idea, Corentin, doesn't go and parley with a pirate.
textes.Il raconte qu'il a crié « Récif ! » de t: He says he shouted “Reef!” at the top of his lungs the night we hit. Me, I heard nothing. Nor did Ignace. The only one who heard it was Belle-Humeur, who hears nothing! Does that make sense to you? Belle-Humeur said “WHAT?!”. That's all we know. Fil-de-Fer says it's proof.
textes.Il raconte qu'il a gagné la Morue aux dé: He claims he won the Cod at dice from an admiral. The week before, it was from a governor. The month before, from a prince. I say it was the same dice every time. He smiles at me with his twenty-two carats. It's the most expensive and the falsest smile in the archipelago.
textes.Il raconte que les dents de crocodile, c: He says the crocodile teeth are for a necklace. For a fiancée. I have no fiancée. I told him. He smiled. He still says it. I bent an iron bar. He still says it. I don't know how you stop Mange-Clous. Nobody knows.
textes.Il reflottera ! Il reflottera quand je l: It will float! It'll float when I say so! I've replaced forty planks, caulked the whole side and set the keel straight! One more word about my ship and it's YOU I'll caulk!
textes.Il refuse d'enlever son képi pendant les: He refuses to take off his cap during massages. “A sergeant does not uncover on duty.” We're alone, in the back room, door shut. He keeps the cap on. He walks out stiff as a post, and gives me a regulation salute on the threshold of the back door.
He regrets your quarrel, I think.
textes.Il reste Pixel, quelque part dans la cit: Pixel is still out there, somewhere in the city…
textes.Il reste Quark… écoute bien : il fredonn: Quark is still out there… listen carefully: he hums when he hides.
textes.Il reste une chose que je n'ai jamais di: There's one thing I've never told anyone. Someday, maybe. When I trust you.
There's one thing I've never told anyone. Someday, maybe. When I trust you.
textes.Il retarde un peu. Mais il est très beau: It runs a bit slow. But it's very beautiful.
textes.Il retourne sur sa fleur…: It's going back to its flower…
textes.Il revient toujours. Dehors, les autres: He always comes back. Out there, the other clouds are too big.
textes.Il revient tous les ans. J'écris « sorti: It comes back every year. I'm writing “out”.
textes.Il rêve de quoi ?: What's the little one dreaming about?
textes.Il s'appelle Moustache ! Regarde ses mou: His name is Moustache! Look at his whiskers!
textes.Il s'entraîne même la nuit, quand il n'y: He even trains at night, when nobody's around. One evening, his ball came through my window and landed on my loom. Three threads broken. He came to fetch it, all sheepish. I made him retie the three threads himself. It took him an hour. He says it was harder than a match.
textes.Il s'est arrêté net au bord de la plate-: He stopped dead at the edge of the platform! Strike!
textes.Il s'est assis devant ma forge pendant t: He sat in front of my forge for thirty days so I'd take him on as an apprentice. Ash was raining down, he stayed. On the thirtieth day, I handed him a broom. He took it as if it were the king's axe. Twelve years later, he's still sweeping. Not as well, but with pride.
textes.Il s'est assommé contre la paroi ! C'est: He knocked himself out against the wall! Now's the moment!
textes.Il s'est posé sur toi ! Ça veut dire qu': It landed on you! That means it chose you. Here, this is my snack: honey from the High-Altitude Greenhouses. Flora says the butterflies had a hand in it: they help the flowers.
It landed on you! That means it chose you. Here, this is my snack: a bag of sunflower seeds. The butterflies don't want them, they prefer flowers.
textes.Il sait de quel côté vient le vent rien: He can tell which way the wind's blowing just by tasting the air. He says the west wind tastes of apples.
textes.Il sait sourire, c'est déjà ça. Yo, capi: He knows how to smile, that's something. Yo, captain!
textes.Il se doute de tout. Il ne sait juste pa: He suspects everything. He just doesn't know what.
textes.Il se moque de moi, je l'ai vu ! Il fait: He makes fun of me, I've seen him! He pretends to drink, then to fall, and he laughs without a sound. Hic! I told him that wasn't nice. So he did it again: drink, fall… and this time he caught himself by the collar, like the night of the bay, and gave me a wink. I didn't understand it all. But I think it was nice.
textes.Il se souvient de quoi ? Il ne veut pas: Remembers what? He won't tell me!
textes.Il se tient toujours derrière ma chaise: He always stands behind my chair when I play, and taps the table with the tip of his hook, tick, tick, out of habit. Sylvain says it's a signal. I swear it's a tic. Crochet swears nothing at all: he doesn't like questions. So nobody knows. Me, I love it when nobody knows.
It mostly smells of oven, Father.
It's whistling in nothing at all.
It sounded better without a dent.
It's just out of the boiler, Tic.
textes.Il sort quand il veut. Si tu attends, il: It comes out when it feels like it. If you wait, it won't. If you turn your back: cuckoo!
textes.Il sort une lame ! Le lâche !: He's drawing a blade! The coward!
textes.Il sort, tout au fond, un disque dans un: From the very back, he pulls out a record in a handmade sleeve: a sun and a cloud holding hands. “Vinyle kept this one for the day the two villages made peace. That day has come.” The music starts: djembes, a fuzzy guitar, and two girls' voices… those of Granny Sunflower and Mother Downpour, fifty years ago.
textes.Il t'a choisi ! Il t'a choisi !: It chose you! It chose you!
textes.Il t'a dit quelque chose ?: Did he say anything to you?
textes.Il t'a dit quelque chose, celui-là ?: Did that one say anything to you?
textes.Il t'a touché ? Avec son Appendice Nouil: He touched you? With his Noodly Appendage? (The Reverend takes off his golden colander, presses it to his heart, and puts it back on crooked.) My child… In forty years, he has touched only three people. A fisherman, a baker, and Nonno Tortellini, in 1987 — he says it was a wink, but it was a noodle. You are the fourth. Here: two plates of Mamma's spaghetti, two focaccias fresh from the oven, and a title, which I'll write myself in the great book. Ramen, my child. Ramen!
textes.Il t'en reste combien, des dents ?: How many teeth have you got left?
textes.Il taille les pommiers, là-haut, sur la: He's pruning the apple trees, up on the third terrace. He talks to them. He says it makes them grow straight.
What you mostly need is gloves.
textes.Il te manque des pièces… Bon. Je te l'of: You're short of coins… Fine. It's on me. But don't tell Spleen, he'd say I'm too nice. He'd be right.
textes.Il te manque quelques pièces. Reviens qu: You're a few coins short. Come back when you've got enough to pay.
textes.Il te manque toufours qu'une dent ? Gard: Thtill only one tooth mithing? Keep the otherth. Teeth are like friendth: you count them when they leave.
textes.Il te réveille d'un coup : endurance au: It wakes you up in one go: stamina at maximum.
textes.Il te suit ! Regarde-le, le groin collé: He's following you! Look at him, snout glued to your shoes! (Père Gaubert laughs, then blows his nose loudly.) It's the pollen. Listen carefully, lad: he eats anything, but not the golden turnips, no, those are my little ones. In the woods and meadows, let him sniff around: he'll find you truffles, and sometimes some old buried thing, a coin, a ring… He has a golden snout, I'm telling you. Here, two truffles he found for me yesterday, and a few coins. And if you don't already have a whistle to call your animals, take my father's, carved from bone: a dog, a cat, a rat and a pig all around it. Whistle, and your pig will come back. Gently with my little one, all right!
textes.Il tient depuis deux cents ans, Jos. Et: It's held for two hundred years, Jos. And so has your hinge.
textes.Il tient. L'autre aussi, celui qui dort: It's holding up. So is the other one, the one that sleeps next to it.
textes.Il tire ! Il veut partir à Hautefond !: It's pulling! It wants to fly off to Hautefond!
It flows the other way, the current.
textes.Il tourne encore ! Patience : c'est de l: It's still spinning! Patience: this is science.
textes.Il tourne tous les jours, le vent, Matth: The wind turns every day, Matthias.
He'll come round to my side one day.
textes.Il tousse encore ? Je vais tourner le so: Still coughing? I'll turn the bellows round.
Then it even cheats in its sleep.
textes.Il va battre son record… Non… Si… NON !: He's going to beat his record… No… Yes… NO!
textes.Il va bouder, mais il repartira tout seu: He'll sulk, but he'll start up again on his own. He has a strong sense of duty.
textes.Il va encore me faire un bisou ?: Is he going to give me a kiss again?
textes.Il va faire le tour d'une veste, mainten: Now it's going to go round a jacket.
textes.Il va faire le tour du monde !: It's going to fly round the world!
My dragon's going to end up leaving.
textes.Il va pleuvoir ! Enfin, en bas, sur le P: It's going to rain! Well, down below, on the Floor. Assistant, the umbrella, on principle!
textes.Il va très bien ! Enfin, il tourne un pe: It's very well! Well, it spins a little when I think about it.
textes.Il va voir dehors !: He's going out for a look!
textes.Il va, il vient ! C'est un toit très voy: It comes, it goes! It's a well-travelled roof.
textes.Il veut des dents de crocodile. Il dit q: He wants crocodile teeth. He says it's for an iron fist. I say it's for a necklace for his sweetheart. He looks at me, picks up an iron bar, and bends it. He says nothing. He hasn't got a sweetheart. But every time I bring it up, his ears turn red. I'm keeping an eye on it.
textes.Il veut que ma tour devienne le « Minist: He wants my tower to become the “Ministry of Geography”. He came and put a plaque on my door. I agreed, on condition he never again asks me to draw an avenue. He swore. The next day, he wanted a trading port. I drew him a trading port. On a separate sheet.
textes.Il veut savoir où sont les grottes de so: He wants to know where his grandfather's caves are. I told him: “Under the feet of the one who guards.” He went crawling under the Skala, at night, and the caïd picked him up. He thinks I'm making fun of him. I'm not. I'm answering. He doesn't know how to listen yet.
textes.Il veut une revanche. Il dit qu'on ne l': He wants a rematch. He says we never did it for real. He offers it every evening, at the counter. He talks softly, I hear nothing, I say “WHAT?!”, he repeats, I still hear nothing. It's been two years. He's patient. I'm not. One of these days, I'll end up understanding. And then he'll be sorry.
He'll come anyway. He likes you.
textes.Il vient me voir tous les deux jours ave: He comes to see me every other day with a rhyme for “large”. “Barge”, “charge”, “marge”. I explained that “Large-Louis on the charge” didn't mean much. He said: “It means here I come!” He's not wrong. I wrote it in my notebook, just in case.
textes.Il vient se faire huiler les genoux chaq: He comes to get his knees oiled every week. He tells me: “Thank you, Mireille. I feel three minutes younger.” I don't know how he works it out. But it makes me happy.
textes.Il vient toutes les semaines demander qu: He comes every week to ask when the flagship will be ready. I answer: “When I say so.” He writes the answer down in a little official notebook. He has forty pages of “When I say so”. One day, he brought me honey, to speed up the work. I ate the honey. The work goes at the same speed.
textes.Il vise mes engrenages ! Je vais te fair: It aims at my gears! I'll take you to court!
textes.Il voulait interdire les bagarres le dim: He wanted to ban brawls on Sundays. Nobody listened to him. So one Sunday, I climbed up on my counter with my rolling pin and said: “Today, the Governor has spoken.” Not one brawl all day. The next day, he gave a speech on the success of his policy. I let him. It was sweet.
textes.Il voulait partir chasser les jaguars du: He wanted to go and hunt the jaguars of the Smoking Mountain. I consulted the calendar: a day worth nothing for hunting. I forbade it. He obeyed, but he spent the day sharpening his weapon outside my door. Very noisily. In the evening, I told him: “Your weapon is ready. Your patience, not yet.”
textes.Il voulait te voir, Aubin. Il t'aime bie: He wanted to see you, Aubin. He likes you.
textes.Il voulait une cape « qui claque au vent: He wanted a cape “that billows in the wind even without wind”. I put wire in the hem, laughing to myself. He tried it on, took a step, and the cape snapped like a flag. He closed his eyes in bliss. He never told me it flaps at night. Babette told me: he lives above her storehouse.
textes.Il voulait une louche solide. Je lui ai: He wanted a sturdy ladle. I forged him a ladle. A handle as long as an arm. A bowl big enough for a whole soup. He lifts it with both hands. He complains. But it doesn't break. A ladle that breaks is soup on the floor. Soup on the floor is a hungry crew. I thought about the crew.
textes.Il voulait vendre des places au premier: He wanted to sell front-row seats for my festivals. I told him music is like the wind. He said: “The wind, I can sell.” He came back the next day with fans: “Wind of Ehécatl, two beans.” He sold one. To his mother. She said it was hot.
textes.Il voulait voir les étoiles « d'un peu p: He wanted to see the stars “a little closer”. I levitated him above the Observatory. At three metres, he clung to my arm shouting: “They're fine from a distance!” The master of light is afraid of heights. I haven't told anyone. Except you. And the wind.
textes.Il vous a fait son arc-en-ciel ! Il ne l: He did his rainbow for you! He only does that for people he likes. Here: a teeny cloud in a jar, his cousin. It makes tiny little showers, just like him.
It's waiting for you. It lives up to its name.
It can hear you, Old Bastien.
textes.Il vous fait des bisous de lumière ?: Does it give you light kisses?
textes.Il vous manque quelques pièces. Revenez: You're a few coins short. Come back when you can pay.
He thanks you. As for me, I sigh.
textes.Il y a aussi la route, à l'est, qui desc: There's also the road, to the east, that winds down to the port. The robot porters take it. They get dizzy in the cabin.
textes.Il y a beaucoup de monde. Je reste près: There are a lot of people. I'll stay close to you. Crowds make me electric.
textes.Il y a cent ans, Glaucos a ramolli des c: A hundred years ago, Glaucos softened some shells in the crystal's heat and blew into them through a reed. A round lamp, in three minutes. It takes me three weeks to carve one. I said: “That's cheating.” He packed up his tools, very politely, and left that same evening. He kept the apron.
A hundred years ago, Orsik never laughed. He counted. So one evening, I took a ruby from him. Just one. Then another the next day. At the Forge Festival, I gave him back a full mug: three hundred and sixty-five rubies. The face he made… I thought he was going to cry. He laughed. For the first time.
textes.Il y a cent ans, Photon m'a réveillé en: A hundred years ago, Photon woke me in broad daylight to show me the flower of the great water lily, which opens once a century. We watched it all night, sitting by the pond. It smelled of mint and thunderstorms. He asked me: “Which star does it look like?” I said: “None. It's better.”
textes.Il y a cent ans, Yggdrasil a cessé de do: A hundred years ago, Yggdrasil stopped giving its seeds. That same winter, Églantine, queen of the root fairies and my friend, wrote to me: “Something is growing under my throne. Come.” When I went down, the brambles were already closing off the north. I called to her for three nights. The brambles answered. She didn't.
textes.Il y a cent ans, le grand nénuphar a ouv: A hundred years ago, the great water lily opened its flower, the one that opens once a century. I ran to wake Zénith in broad daylight. We watched it all night, by the pond. I asked him which star it looked like. He answered: “None. It's better.” He's right.
textes.Il y a cent ans, le grand tremblement a: A hundred years ago, the great quake split the old gates of Forgefer. The old king told me: “Forty days.” I took thirty-nine. Grimli hauled the ore up for me on his back. On the last evening, a spark singed off half his beard. He says it grew back finer. He's lying. The gates, though, haven't budged. Now that's solid.
textes.Il y a cent ans, les ronces ont poussé a: A hundred years ago the brambles grew in the north, and they took our Queen Églantine. I cried for a whole month. And one morning I saw that my tears weren't drying: they shone, perfectly round, like moon dew. Since then, when I lose my drops… I make more. It's not very practical.
textes.Il y a cent ans, un automne, j'ai trouvé: A hundred years ago, one autumn, I found a black shoot up north, in the old root. It smelled of iron. I warned Queen Églantine. I warned everyone. They said: “You're always grumbling, Grommelot.” Yes. That time I had good reason to grumble. When winter came, the brambles were everywhere. And the queen, inside them.
textes.Il y a cent ans, à la fête de l'Aube, en: A hundred years ago, at the Dawn festival, in the middle of a ballad, my G string snapped. A blue-eyed elf climbed onto the stage and replaced it with a golden thread, without a word. Then she stepped down again. I forgot the rest of the ballad. I forgot Celebrë singing. I forgot my own name, I think.
textes.Il y a cent ans, à la fête de l'Aube, je: A hundred years ago, at the Dawn festival, I was singing the “Ballad” with Caelan. A string broke, Ilyria came up to replace it, and Caelan ran off after her. Mid-verse! I sang alone for a whole hour, making up the words. They say it was my finest hour. Mostly it was my longest.
textes.Il y a cent ans, à la fête de l'Aube, un: A hundred years ago, at the Dawn festival, a string on Caelan's harp snapped in the middle of the ballad. I had a golden thread in my pocket, I can't remember why. I went up, tied it, came back down. He looked at me as if I'd brought him the moon. He's played under my window every night since. I should have kept my thread.
textes.Il y a cent cinquante ans, le volcan a t: A hundred and fifty years ago, the volcano coughed all winter long. The ash fell like grey snow, and the terrace forges mustn't go out. So we brought the big cauldron out of the city, Bramm carried it on his back, and I fed a hundred dwarves with a cracked ladle. Borin forged me a spoon. I still have it.
textes.Il y a cent quatre-vingts ans, les genou: A hundred and eighty years ago, my father's knees gave out. He handed me the spear without a word. The first visitor that day was a goat. I made it wait three hours, on principle. It ate the hem of my cloak. I didn't move. You don't move.
textes.Il y a cent vingt ans, j'ai chanté la ma: A hundred and twenty years ago, on the steps of the Gate, I sang the high tide so softly that Triton fell asleep. I saw him. He looked so peaceful that I didn't want to wake him. The next day, the Pearl of the avenue had vanished. I've never said a word, {surnom}. Least of all to him.
textes.Il y a cent vingt ans, je suivais une ve: A hundred and twenty years ago, I was following a vein of iron, happy as can be, and I came up a little too far. My head popped out through the floor of the guardhouse, between Bramm's boots. I asked him if he'd moved house. He's never forgiven me. Me, I've forgotten why he's cross. Almost.
textes.Il y a cent vingt ans, le sol de ma loge: A hundred and twenty years ago, the floor of my guardhouse cracked open. A head popped out, between my boots. A helmet, a grey beard: Grimli. “Sorry, I was looking for my tunnel.” The gate was never forced. The floor was. That doesn't count. I filled the hole myself. With a gate stone, and my fist.

A hundred and twenty years ago, the floor of my guardhouse heaved up and his head came out between my boots. He said: “Oh, Bramm. Have you moved house?” I hadn't moved house. I filled the hole with a gate stone. It's still there. I stand guard on it, every day.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, Cerfeuil est parti avec: Five years ago, Cerfeuil left with the mist. That's how we say it, here. The night before, he made me promise to look after Trèfle and Mochi, my goddaughter, who wasn't even one. I said “Promise, boom!” to make him laugh. Since then, every morning, I run to the bakery with the flour sacks. I say it's training. Trèfle pretends to believe me.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, Cerfeuil, le mari de Tr: Five years ago, Cerfeuil, Trèfle's husband, left with the mist. Trèfle couldn't sleep any more: I could smell her tiredness through the bakery door. One dawn, I gathered the mist off the big pond and sealed it in a vial, with a moon feather from Plumette. Trèfle slept. The vial of mist was born. Ursule buys it for the silver; I don't ask bears questions.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, Philibert est entré au: Five years ago, Philibert came into the Bazaar with an empty box, apologising at every step. He was going to throw it away. I bought it for eight coins. He went bright red, he wanted to pay me back on the spot, and I pushed him out the door so he couldn't. Since then, I order twenty a month from him. My best seller.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, Pivoine m'a vendu ma pr: Five years ago, Pivoine sold me my first vial of mist. I dipped a little bell in it. The silver sang clearer. Much clearer. Since then, I quench silver and blades in a trough of cold mist. Not even Borin knows. Charbon forged a little bell for every pair of ears born. So do I. They sing better now.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, au Perroquet, la nouvel: Five years ago, at the Perroquet, the new waitress spilled a punch on me. The whole glass. She was all red, she kept saying sorry, sorry. I said: “It's nothing, it smells nice.” It was true. Since then, I play cards there every evening. Against Victor. I lose. I look somewhere else.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, elle m'a acheté sa prem: Five years ago, she bought her first vial of mist from me. She took a little silver bell out of her pocket, dipped it in, right there on my counter, and shook it. The bell sang, clear as a dewdrop. Ursule said: “Hm.” Then she bought the whole shelf. I didn't ask anything. You don't ask bears questions.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, j'ai acheté une fiole d: Five years ago, I bought a vial of mist. On her counter, I dipped a silver bell in it. It sang. Clear, like never before. Pivoine raised her nose. She didn't ask anything. I bought the whole shelf. Good. She doesn't ask questions. I don't answer.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, j'ai failli monter en r: Five years ago, I almost made rank E. I was just one contract short. One single frog. I found it, I took aim, I slipped on a reed, and it swallowed me. By the time it spat me out, Mélusine had already prepared the congratulations for the square. She's still keeping them.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, j'ai failli passer rang: Five years ago, I almost made rank E. When I came back without my frog, Églantine said nothing. She just poured me a mint tea and said: “The stamp can wait. It's patient.” I think it's still waiting. It gives me courage.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, j'ai glissé une lettre: Five years ago, I slipped a letter into the service capsule, addressed to “the apprentice liftkeeper of Hautefond, if there is one”. A week later, the answer arrived. “My name is Barnabé. I exist. I'm a bit afraid of heights.” We've written to each other every week since. I have two hundred and sixty letters. I've kept every one.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, j'allais jeter une boît: Five years ago, I was about to throw away an empty box. I used to make them back then, pretty wooden boxes to keep my ideas in. They stayed empty: my ideas all existed already. Madame Bricolette saw me with that one in my hand. She bought it from me for eight coins. It's my only invention ever sold, and the Bazaar's best seller. Basile doesn't like it. Well… he's entitled to.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, j'avais dix-huit ans. J: Five years ago, I was eighteen. I bought a return ticket “for the day”. In the evening, when Léon rang for departure, I stayed on the quay. He shouted: “Coming aboard?” I shouted: “I'm staying!” He kept my return ticket. That same evening, I helped carry crates into the Perroquet without being asked, and Toni hired me.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, la grande tempête a fra: Five years ago, the great storm hit the library head-on. The wind came in through the top window and took four books, the way you pick fruit. I watched them go off into the night, pages open like wings. I called with all my might. The wind called louder. I had never lost a book. Not one.
textes.Il y a cinq ans, une petite est descendu: Five years ago, a young girl stepped off L'Hirondelle with a bag and a return ticket she never used. That very evening, she helped me carry my crates down to the cellar, without me asking. One, two, three, four. At the fifth, I told her: “You start tomorrow.” She answered: “I'm starting now.” That was Lola.
textes.Il y a cinq étages. Les caves gluantes,: There are five floors. The gooey cellars, the trap room, the underground lake, the library of biting chests, and the throne room. On the fourth, a riddle points to the true chest. Read it to the very end. The impatient get bitten.
textes.Il y a cinquante ans, Brasero et une ban: Fifty years ago, Brasero and a band of youngsters decided to cross the Chasm to live their own way, in the great eastern cavern. The elders of the Guild were furious. I was twenty. At night, I carried planks for their Bridge. Without a word. The Frondeurs' Bridge still holds. There's a little of my arms in it.
textes.Il y a cinquante ans, Orsik a voulu desc: Fifty years ago, Orsik wanted to go down the mine and pick his stones himself. I guided him. We got lost, of course, and he dropped a ruby on the way. Last year, I found it in a tunnel and sold it to him. He recognised his own stone. He paid for it anyway, in tears.
textes.Il y a cinquante ans, Solenne est revenu: Fifty years ago, Solenne came back from a “stroll” with soil under her nails. She held out a little brown seed: “An apple seed. From Montjoie. Well… from a book about Montjoie.” I put it in my pocket. It's still there. I've never planted it. Solenne has never asked me why.
textes.Il y a cinquante ans, au coucher du sole: Fifty years ago, at sunset, out at sea, I saw a golden shape above the waves. A ball of noodles, with two eyes. It looked at me, then stretched a noodle towards the horizon. I set my course by it. Three days later, I saw the volcano smoking tomato. Tortellini says it was a jellyfish. Arrr.
textes.Il y a cinquante ans, deux jeunes filles: Fifty years ago, two young girls landed here with a suitcase each. In mine, sunflower seeds. In my friend's, an umbrella and a little cloud that followed us everywhere. We put up a yurt together, full of holes. We laughed all day long.
textes.Il y a cinquante ans, j'ai rapporté à Ph: Fifty years ago, I brought Photon an apple seed, picked up in an orchard in Montjoie while I was posing as a fruit picker. He held it in his hand like a treasure. He's never planted it. He says he's waiting. I don't know for what.
textes.Il y a cinquante ans, j'ai voulu choisir: Fifty years ago, I wanted to pick my stones myself, deep in the mine. Grimli guided me. We got lost for two days, and I dropped a ruby in the dark. Last year, he came to sell it to me, very proud. MY ruby. With my mark on it. I paid for it anyway. So he wouldn't sell it to someone else.
textes.Il y a de la houle au large, aujourd'hui: There's a swell out at sea today. Your favourite. I'm keeping the bow for you. Bring an oilskin.
textes.Il y a des années, on se volait les clie: Years ago, we stole each other's customers every night. So we signed a treaty, on a Crâne Fendu napkin: at my place, you bet small and eat well; at his, you bet big and don't eat. The napkin is framed behind my counter. He signed in beautiful handwriting. Me, with a cross. He didn't say anything. He's polite.
textes.Il y a des années, un bateau d'épices a: Years ago, a spice ship sank, ever so gently, in my harbour. The whole bay smelled of cinnamon for a month. A family climbed out, soaked through, with a little girl who was laughing. I told them to stay. That was Rosalie. She still laughs the same way.
textes.Il y a des chats à Tazira aussi. Des cha: There are cats in Tazira too. Whole cats, with no people around them. They steal maps from pirates. I like them.
textes.Il y a des coquillages magnifiques au bo: There are gorgeous shells at the end of the beach, just behind the sound wall.
textes.Il y a des liftiers dans la famille ?: Are there liftkeepers in the family?
textes.Il y a des lumières dans les grottes, so: There are lights in the caves, under the cliff, behind us. At night. I don't have the men to go and look.
textes.Il y a des mouettes à Port-Azur ? Des to: There are seagulls in Port-Azur? Tourists. Holiday seagulls. We're working seagulls. KYA.
textes.Il y a deux ans, au nouvel an, un confet: Two years ago, at New Year, a piece of confetti slipped into the escapement of the great clock. Just one. Blue. Result: one second fast. The only one in its life. I scolded the clock. Then I scolded Capucine. The clock, at least, seemed to understand.
textes.Il y a deux ans, au nouvel an, un de mes: Two years ago, at New Year, one of my confetti got stuck in the escapement of the great clock. It went one second fast. The only time in its whole history! Tic scolded the clock, then he scolded me, in exactly the same voice. He was finding confetti in the works until May.
textes.Il y a deux ans, elle m'a apporté un paq: Two years ago she brought me a parcel. I won't tell you more. Neither will she: she promised. Since then, when she runs into my uncle, she looks at her feathers. A postwoman says nothing. But a postwoman carries heavy loads, sometimes.
textes.Il y a deux ans, en pleine nuit : « ALER: Two years ago, in the middle of the night: “ALERT!” Croc-Gris had seen a monster. Everyone ran out in their nightshirts! Me, I took the Lookout zip line, in my pyjamas, for the first time in my life. Wheeeee! It was SO cool! The monster was Hulotte with her lantern. Since then I do one alert a day. Croc-Gris growls. That means he's happy.
textes.Il y a deux ans, j'étais tout seul à la: Two years ago, I was alone at the Forge, in the evening. I heard tapping above, through the rock: two taps, then one. But not like usual. Smaller, faster. I answered, very softly. Someone answered back. I stayed tapping for an hour. The next day, Mistress Brunehaut told me: “That's Mathilde's daughter. She's nine. Her name is Pimprenelle.”
textes.Il y a deux ans, je suis tombé de mon po: Two years ago, I fell off my jetty backing away from a frog. Hilaire was on the shore. He dived in, fished me out, and brought me back to the bank. Then the frog swallowed him instead. I wrote both down in my notebook. The rescue, and number forty-one. He was very proud of the first one. So was I.
textes.Il y a deux ans, quand Éclair est tombée: Two years ago, when Éclair fell at the root bend, Grisou shouted “you OK?” as he went by. Me, nothing. I jumped. I tell myself that's racing. But Grisou, he shouted. It bugs me sometimes. In the evening. Not for long. Hop.
textes.Il y a deux ans, Éclair menait la course: Two years ago, Éclair was leading the race. Ahead of me up to the root bend. Then a wet root, and she slipped. I jumped over her. Hop. Without stopping. I won. Everyone says that's racing. I say that's racing. I say it often. Maybe a bit too often.
textes.Il y a deux ans, Éclair menait, et elle: Two years ago Éclair was leading, and she fell at the root bend. Bondi jumped over her like an arrow, without a glance. Me, as I went by, I shouted “you OK?”. I didn't stop, mind, it was the race. But I shouted. Him, nothing. I'm not saying that makes me a better runner. I'm just saying.
textes.Il y a deux ans. La Grande Course. J'éta: Two years ago. The Great Race. I was in front. In front of Bondi. Up to the root bend, before the Lookout. A wet root. … I fell. Bondi jumped over. Without looking. Grisou went past. He shouted: “You OK?” … Third. I finished third. The root is still there. So am I.
textes.Il y a deux ans. Pleine nuit. Une forme: Two years ago. Dead of night. A shape climbs the Mother Oak. A long-necked monster, with a fiery eye at the end. I sound the alarm. All of Ramure comes down, in nightshirts, by the stairs and the zip line. It was Hulotte. His lantern. His long telescope. … It was a drill. Very successful. The whole village down in four minutes.
textes.Il y a deux cents ans, le Conseil m'a no: Two hundred years ago, the Council named me ambassador. My mission: observe the people down below without ever disturbing them. Écliptique drafted the article: “The ambassador does not go down.” I read the article very carefully. Then I bought myself a fake moustache. The article said nothing about moustaches.
textes.Il y a deux chutes d'eau ici. L'eau de l: There are two waterfalls here. The water of the bigger one, in the north-east, comes from very deep under the ground. It tastes of stars.
textes.Il y a deux mois, ma tante m'a offert un: Two months ago, my aunt gave me a week here. One week! The first morning, I climbed up to the lookout with my sketchbook. The light fell over the port all at once, like a tablecloth being shaken out. I forgot to draw. I sat there till noon. And I decided to stay. A little. A lot.
textes.Il y a deux mois, à trois heures du mati: Two months ago, at three in the morning, the blue glow of Stoneheart pulsed twice a minute instead of once. Just one night. The next day, at the Crankshaft, Prudence told me her piano had played a tune she'd never taught it. Same night, same hour. We compared our notebooks, very quietly. We haven't told anyone.
textes.Il y a deux siècles, Taeron m'a dit que: Two centuries ago Taeron told me my sail between Fil-d'Aube and the Mother Tree would last a year. He's replaced his planks four times since. My sail hasn't budged. Every time he replaces a plank, I bring him up a cup of herbal tea and say nothing. He hates that.
textes.Il y a dix ans, Grumbald a inventé la la: Ten years ago, Grumbald invented frozen lava and said it was the best dessert in Pandémonia. I answered with my honey cake. The Grand Dessert Contest took place on the Great Square, with Asmodin as judge. He tasted, tasted again, and tasted again. He declared a tie. Grumbald says it wasn't.
textes.Il y a dix ans, Héloïse a construit le t: Ten years ago, Héloïse built the cable car, and she made me its keeper. Me! Soon after, a cabin stopped in the middle of the cable, with the mayor of Port-Azur inside. An hour. He wrote a poem about the clouds, all rhyming in “-ation”. And it was my little Écrou, fifteen years old, who climbed along the cable to release the brake. My palms still sweat thinking about it.
textes.Il y a dix ans, au concours du plus beau: Ten years ago, at the finest turnip contest of the Dawn festival, I entered a magnificent turnip. Well washed. Well brushed. With a little touch of colour, for the shine. I won. Germaine shouted that I'd painted it. It wasn't painted. It was… enhanced. Since then she only talks to me to contradict me.

Ten years ago, at the prettiest turnip contest, Babette won with a red turnip. Red! Turnips aren't red! She'd painted it, I'm sure of it. I demanded an inquiry. The judge was the Baron, wearing a carrot-shaped hat. He said all vegetables have the right to be beautiful. I haven't forgiven him either.
textes.Il y a dix ans, en traversant le Bois To: Ten years ago, crossing the Twisted Wood, a wheel broke on a root. Prune stopped dead and refused to move another step. The old oaks leaned over to look. The mushrooms lit up all around us. I got the message. I never fixed the wheel. It's still there, propped against an oak.
textes.Il y a dix ans, j'étais dans la nacelle: Ten years ago I was in the basket lift with the mailbag. Halfway up, snap: the rope broke. Bourru held it all with his bare hands. I clutched the bag to me and waited, counting. I've never ridden in it since. I tell the children I fly. I take the stairs. Two years later I handed the mailbag to Plumette.
textes.Il y a dix ans, je suis tombé malade tou: Ten years ago, I was ill the whole winter. No sowing, no seeds. Germaine did everything, alone. One morning, there were six sacks of seeds in front of our door. Nobody ever found out who. Germaine is still looking. Me, I have a little idea, because of an apple mark on one sack. But I'm not saying anything. Some things you keep.
textes.Il y a dix ans, tante Sésame est partie: Ten years ago, Aunt Sésame left for the longest swap of her life: “this bell for a trip round the world”. With the family bell at the tip of her tail, she went down the stairs jingling. Since then, Plumette sometimes brings me a card from some impossible place: a town on stilts, a singing desert, a floating island. I've got nine.
textes.Il y a dix ans, un matin de brume, la Mu: Ten years ago, one misty morning, the Murène sailed past our boat. I didn't think. I jumped. I swam and swam, with my boots on. Halfway there, I thought I'd sink. And then a rope dropped in front of my nose. It was the lookout, Gaspard, who'd spotted me before anyone else. He said nothing. He pulled me in.
textes.Il y a dix ans, une lettre est descendue: Ten years ago, a letter came down from up top: “A little girl was born in the Clouds, on the third of the month. Her name is Lili.” I read it out on the Square. A mum raised her hand in the crowd: “Mine was born on the third too. Her name is Mila.” The whole Dome clapped for both of them. One up top, one down below. Ever since, I've kept an eye on them both. One by letter, the other through the Trading Post window.
textes.Il y a dix ans, une presse de l'atelier: Ten years ago, a press in the workshop closed on my left arm. I hardly remember anything, except the ambulance siren. Afterwards, in hospital, I stared at the ceiling. I said to myself: “Right. I'll build myself one.”
textes.Il y a dix ans. La cinquième corde. Elle: Ten years ago. The fifth rope. It snapped halfway up. Hulotte inside, with the mail bag. I grabbed the rope. Bare hands. It burned. I held on. Ursule jammed the pulley with an iron bar. Pivoine tended my paws. Pomme-de-Pin and her grandmother wove the sixth rope in one night. Hulotte never got back in. Hrmm.
textes.Il y a dix jours, la Grande Averse (une: Ten days ago, the Great Downpour (a shower of clear water from a pure white cloud) washed over Sketched Island: the Stone Palette overflowed, and the island's nine pots of colour were carried off by the water to the four corners of the island. Since then, everything has been black and white. Grandma Aquarelle, the village elder, has entrusted you with the island's Brush. You need to find the nine pots and pour each one into its numbered paint well.
textes.Il y a dix-huit ans, je me suis présenté: Eighteen years ago, I ran for mayor. A perfect tie with Aristide! We settled it with pétanque, on the square, in front of the whole town. Last ball, Marcel takes out his tape measure, measures, and announces: “Aristide, by one centimetre.” ONE centimetre! They stole the town hall from me, that's what. Marcel measured like a postman.
textes.Il y a dix-huit ans, égalité parfaite av: Eighteen years ago, a perfect tie with Raymond, the baker. Not one vote between us! So, as we do round here, we settled it with pétanque. Marcel got out his tape measure, knelt down, measured for a long time. “One centimetre. To Aristide.” I won. Between you and me… I've never been entirely sure about that centimetre.
textes.Il y a douze ans, Brindille s'est arrêté: Twelve years ago, Brindille stopped for three seconds. The island tilted half a degree. The whole city screamed. I put down my cup, tapped the console, and said: “Come on, my beauty.” She started up again. My cup didn't spill. That day, I understood that calm is catching. Even for engines.
textes.Il y a douze ans, Margaux est entrée dan: Twelve years ago, Margaux walked into the shop, saw the “for sale” sign and said: “I'll take it.” Just like that! We signed on the kneading trough, with the flour pencil. She was shaking so much her signature took up three lines. I kept the paper. You can still see the pencil mark on the trough.
textes.Il y a douze ans, c'est moi qui ai vu la: Twelve years ago, I was the one who spotted the Murène Noire first, at daybreak, black sails on a grey sea. I rang three times, the old signal. The Admiral was on the poop deck before the third. She asked: “How many cannons?” I said: “Twenty-two.” She said: “Good. We have forty.” They don't fire, but still.
textes.Il y a douze ans, j'ai chargé une barque: Twelve years ago, I loaded a boat with shovels and axes and rowed all the way to the Fire Reefs. The beach guard wouldn't let me in.
