textes.J'ai acheté une boussole à nuages. Elle: I bought a cloud compass. It always points to the prettiest one. Handy, but slow.
textes.J'ai affiché le prix des cruches au mur,: I put up the price of jugs on the wall, right next to the price of rum. Broken jug: double price. Two jugs: four times the price. A pirate who breaks things: the door. Since then the pirates read the wall before they quarrel. Not all of them can read. The ones who can read for the others. It calms things down.
textes.J'ai affiché sur mon hangar : « Cristaux: I put up a sign on my hangar: “Astral crystals: cheaper than at the Bazaar!” The next day, Nébula put up: “Astral crystals: wrapped more prettily than at the Spaceport!” I sold ten. She sold eleven. The eleventh was Orbe. He wanted the paper. I've never forgiven him. The paper was very pretty.
textes.J'ai aidé maman à pétrir. J'ai tapé, rou: I helped Mummy knead. I patted, rolled, patted again. And when the bread came out of the oven, it was shaped like a rabbit! With floppy ears. It was me! Nobody dared eat it, because it was me. Then Uncle Bondi bit off an ear. I shouted “Ouch!” as a joke.
textes.J'ai ajouté une petite modification dans: I added a small modification to my heart of code: a “dream module”. At night, instead of going on standby, I replay my favourite images. Last night, I dreamt of a blue cherry tree. I'm going to paint it.
textes.J'ai analysé l'huile à cornes de Tiburce: I analysed Tiburce's horn oil, in public, on my stall. Result: nine tenths perfume, one tenth vanity. I posted the figures. The next day, Tiburce wrote underneath: “And one hundred percent happiness”. His sales doubled. Mine didn't. I don't understand customers at all.
textes.J'ai apporté des fraises géantes. Une se: I brought giant strawberries. Just the one. It takes up the whole picnic blanket.
textes.J'ai apporté une brouette cassée à l'ate: I brought a broken wheelbarrow to the bike workshop. The mechanic whistled as she worked. She fixed it in ten minutes. I built her a workbench. She fixed my bike. I built her a house. One day, I gave her a ring carved from oak. She whistled three notes. I understood yes.
textes.J'ai apporté à Photon un glouglou malade: I brought Photon a sick glug-glug that wouldn't eat any more. He set it down among the flowers. The glug-glug ate one petal, then two, then a whole flower. Photon asked the flower if it minded: one blink, yes, it was fine. The glug-glug went home to the Greenhouse cured. It goes “glug-glug” louder than before.
textes.J'ai apporté à Velours ma veste de burea: I brought Velours my grey office jacket, “for a button”. Next to it I put a box of Bilge Rats badges. She understood straight away. She sewed me a secret lining with a little pocket for each badge. When I opened the jacket, I smiled so hard my cheeks hurt.
textes.J'ai appris chez les nains, sur la Monta: I learnt from the dwarves, on Fire Mountain. Three years hauling coal before I touched a hammer.
textes.J'ai appris deux mots à l'Amiral : « BER: I taught the Admiral two words: “BERTHA! FIRE!” He shrieked them one morning on the quay, right in the middle of the fish auction. Everyone threw themselves flat. Saïd fell off his platform, Zohra dropped a crate of sardines. Gaspard looked at me for a long, long time. Then he smiled. That's Gaspard.
textes.J'ai appris la basse sur un manche à bal: I learned bass on a broom handle with three rubber bands. It went “bzoing”. Rouille heard me and said: “You've got rhythm.” I was fourteen. I still have the broom. It's retired.
textes.J'ai appris la batterie sur les vieilles: I learned drums on the old boilers of the Fronde. One went “dong”, one went “bam”, one went “tsssh”. My father, Brasero, said: “This lad will make noise his whole life.” He was right. He's always right. It's exhausting.
textes.J'ai appris la télékinésie pour attraper: I learned telekinesis to reach the books on the top shelves without a ladder. I was afraid of ladders. I'm not afraid of ladders any more. I don't need them any more.
textes.J'ai appris le métier avec Papa : le chê: I learned the trade with Papa: the oak, the iron hoops, the fire to bend the staves. One day, I made my masterpiece. The merchant filled it with rum, and to check it didn't leak, I had a taste. Then I checked again. Papa told me not to come back until I understood the difference between checking and emptying. I went to sea to think it over.
textes.J'ai appris le métier avec un nain de Fo: I learnt the trade from a dwarf from Forgefer who came here on a raft. He left again after a year. He said there was too much water.
textes.J'ai appris le métier de marchand de mai: I learnt the trade of house-seller from an old master on the big island to the east. He taught me three rules: always smile, always exaggerate, and always wax your moustache. “A droopy moustache, and the client sees the leaks.” I wax mine every morning. Clients never see the leaks. The leaks, however, are still there.
textes.J'ai appris le violon toute seule, sur u: I taught myself the violin, on a violin I found in an attic. It was missing a string. I played for three years on three strings. When someone gave me a fourth, I didn't know what to do with it.
textes.J'ai appris les runes pendant cent ans,: I studied runes for a hundred years, at my grandmother's, in the very alcove where I still live. Three thousand signs, and each has three meanings, depending on the light. She made me read by lava-glow alone. She used to say: “A rune read in sunlight always lies.” Since then, I hardly ever go out in the sun.
textes.J'ai appris mes signes en recopiant le m: I learned my signs by copying the same tale three hundred times. I still know it by heart. Want to hear it? … Another time, then.
textes.J'ai appris tout seul, avec les cartes d: I taught myself, with my father's maps and the sailors' stories. At sixteen, I drew my first map of Port-Azur. Very beautiful. Three hundred metres out: I'd put the lighthouse in the water. My father framed it anyway. When he died, I took over the bookshop. And I put the lighthouse back on dry land.
textes.J'ai appris une danse d'en bas. Solenne: I learned a dance from down below. Solenne showed it to me. It's called “the jig”. You jump, you stamp your feet, you spin. Solenne says she learned it from a book. There was sawdust on her shoes.
textes.J'ai appris à Mouette à faire des bulles: I taught Mouette to blow bubbles. Her first giant bubble swallowed a real seagull. It floated above the harbour, looking very surprised, then the bubble burst. The seagull flew off all shiny. It's avoided us ever since. Mouette says she's got a cross cousin.
textes.J'ai appris à cuisiner dans la cuisine d: I learned to cook in my grandmother's kitchen, a tiny room with an enormous pot. She fed the whole street. She used to say: “A soup is made for more people than you expect.” I've never been able to make soup for just one person. It's not a flaw. It's a method.
textes.J'ai appris à faire tourner la lumière a: I learned to spin light around me in ribbons. It took me two hundred years. The first ribbon wrapped around my head and I couldn't see a thing. The second tied my ankles together. The hundredth obeyed me. Today, they follow me like kittens. They're a bit jealous of each other.
textes.J'ai appris à forger avec mon père, et l: I learned to forge from my father, and he from his father, who had learned down below, in the Strata, with the blacksmiths of the Fronde. They taught him two things: hit well, and laugh well. I'm pretty good at both.
textes.J'ai appris à lire avant de parler. Ma m: I learned to read before I learned to talk. My mother says my first word was “shh”. I don't believe her. I think it was “page”.
textes.J'ai appris à nager avant de marcher. Ma: I learnt to swim before I could walk. My mother dived, and her mother too. They say we have gills hidden behind our ears. That's not true. I think.
textes.J'ai appris à parler aux perroquets avan: I learned to talk to parrots before I learned to talk to people. Parrots are easier: they repeat everything, they never argue.
textes.J'ai appris à parler aux plantes il y a: I learned to talk to plants four hundred years ago. One blink means yes. Two means thank you. Three means “water me”. One long, very slow blink is a joke. Plants have a great sense of humour. But it's very slow.
textes.J'ai attaché une banderole « Les arbres: I tied a banner saying “Trees are not for sale” to Lisse's sign. The next day, his robots had folded it in four, ironed it, and left it on my tree. With a note: “Thank you for your understanding.”
textes.J'ai attrapé un rat. Il m'a montré sa ca: I caught a rat. He showed me his squat resident's card. I let him go. Rules are rules.
textes.J'ai balayé 14 kilomètres aujourd'hui. J: I swept 14 kilometers today. I only found one coin. I kept it.
textes.J'ai baptisé mon premier nuage à quatre: I named my first cloud when I was four. He was called Bernard. He lasted six minutes. I cried. My mother said: “There'll be others.” She was right. I've named forty-two thousand. I've recorded them all. Bernard is on the first page.
textes.J'ai branché la fontaine-baignoire de la: I wired the bathtub fountain on the square to the crane. When Boulon lifts a container, the fountain lights up. It's completely useless. Now Boulon lifts empty containers, just so the kids can see the fountain light up. He likes seeing it too.
textes.J'ai branché une guirlande sur la scie d: One night, I wired fairy lights to Copeau's saw as a surprise. In the morning, he switched on the saw, everything blinked, and he jumped back three metres. He said: “That's worrying.” But he didn't unplug it. That was two years ago.
textes.J'ai bu mon thé, j'ai posé la tasse, et: I drank my tea, I put the cup down, and when Agathe opened her mouth, I set fire to the leaves. Pfft. No more future. She looked at the ashes, and she smiled. She'd already read it all, of course. A smile like that is worse than a future.
textes.J'ai bu une noix de coco, mon frère. C'e: I drank a coconut, my brother. Same thing, only better.
textes.J'ai bâti ma cabane avec les planches de: I built my shack from the planks of the Seagull that the sea gave back to me one by one; the last one arrived nine years ago. I have four thousand three hundred and twelve shells, every one of them named. Marley grows his bananas in my corner, Mistral set up his sound wall thanks to my rowing boat, and young Gaspard comes to learn about shacks. For a hermit, I get far too many visitors.
textes.J'ai caché du grog dans ses algues penda: I hid my hot honey brew in her seaweed for years. Last week she swapped it for herbal tea. I drank it and shouted “What a brew!” so as not to give her the satisfaction. The next day I found a real bottle in its place, with a note: “For your cough. Just one.” That's Anouk for you.
textes.J'ai caché le dessert partout : dans le: I've hidden the dessert everywhere: in the stern cannon, in the sail locker, in a bucket under Petit-Pierre. He finds everything, by the smell! Now, I hide it in the captain's cabin. He doesn't dare go in. The only problem is that the captain, she does dare eat the dessert.
textes.J'ai caché trois cents noisettes dans le: I hid three hundred hazelnuts in the Mother Oak. Three hundred! In the holes, under the bark, behind the lanterns, everywhere. And then I forgot where. I found one! There are two hundred and ninety-nine left. That way, winter won't find them either! Clever, huh? Pomme-de-Pin says it's very clever. She giggles when she says it.
textes.J'ai caché un grelot dans le thérémine d: I hid a bell in Vibrato's theremin, just before the auroras. When he started playing, it went “woooo-ding”. The whole Agora laughed. I thought he was going to tell me off. But he smiled, and kept playing with the bell. The tune's called “Woooo-ding”. It's kind of mine.
I hid a bell in Vibrato's theremin. It goes “woooo-ding”. He kept it! It became his most popular tune. He taught me the theremin. I woke up all the glug-glugs in the Greenhouse.
textes.J'ai calculé que le Zéphyr met trois min: I calculated that the Zéphyr takes three minutes and twelve seconds to get from Cliquetis to Tazira. With the wind behind it, three minutes. With Achille in front, four.
textes.J'ai calculé que papa souffle trente et: I calculated that Dad blows thirty-one per cent of his bubbles for himself. Not for the audience. For him. I can tell: he watches them rise, he doesn't watch the people. I showed him the result on a sheet of paper. He said: “Is that a lot?” I said: “It's just the right amount.” He blew me a square bubble.
textes.J'ai chanté la chanson de ma mère. Au so: I sang my mother's song. In the sunshine. I got the tempo wrong twice, and nobody noticed. Except Mother Downpour, who knitted faster.
textes.J'ai cherché la sagesse dans les montagn: I searched for wisdom in the mountains for ten years. I found snow, goats and a great deal of silence. Wisdom, I found when I arrived here, by a pond, watching a frog. She's never in a hurry.
textes.J'ai choisi la Plage aux Galets parce qu: I chose the Pebble Beach because the pebbles talk for me. When the wave pulls back, they all roll together. It makes music. My hut has been there forty years. I've fixed it a hundred times. It leans. So do I, a bit.
textes.J'ai chronométré la cuisson de ses miche: I timed how long her loaves bake: twenty-two minutes, on the dot. I shouted “Twenty-two minutes, Trèfle, record broken!” She asked me what the old record was. There wasn't one. Since then, that's the record, and she breaks it every morning. It makes her happy, I think. Me too.
textes.J'ai cloué une casserole au plafond de m: I nailed a saucepan to my workshop ceiling, right under his anvil, so he'd hear what I hear. He hung one under his. Now the two ring together, and Ewen calls it “the lower-deck music”. The guests at the inn think it's a bell. I can't sleep any more.
textes.J'ai collé mon oreille contre Jojo, le p: I pressed my ear against Jojo, the little one right at the bottom, and told Tchoum: “He's sad, he's lonely.” Tchoum didn't answer. That night, Jojo was up top, next to Raoul. He sounded louder, happier. Tchoum never told me it was for me. He doesn't need to.
textes.J'ai commencé docker à seize ans. Toute: I started as a docker at sixteen. Crates all day long. To pass the time, I gave them names. Number twelve is called Gertrude. My rowboat too, I called her Gertrude. But saying “Gertrude” to Odette, for her register, that I struggle with. She'd look at me. With her glasses.
textes.J'ai commencé le Grand Dictionnaire de l: I started the Great Dictionary of the Singer one evening when she sang three low notes and a high one, just as the Pearl was lighting up. The next day, at the same time: again. I wrote: “Hello, Dome?” With a question mark. Twenty years later, there are twelve hundred phrases. I've taken out that particular question mark. Not the others.
textes.J'ai commencé liftier à quinze ans, dans: I started as a liftkeeper at fifteen, in this very cabin. Back then the machines made such a racket we talked in gestures. Fifty years later, the machines have gone quiet. My ears, though, stayed back in the days of gestures.
textes.J'ai commencé liftier à quinze ans. Le p: I started as a liftkeeper at fifteen. On the first day, the cabin made such a racket that the old liftkeeper taught me the trade in gestures. One finger up: going up. One finger down: going down. Hand on heart: “Smile at the passengers, lad.” That's the only gesture I still make every day.
I started out as a cabin boy on a three-master. Now I run the ferry, and I sleep in my own bed every night. That's true wealth.
textes.J'ai commencé ton étoile. Elle brille dé: I've started your star. It's already shining a little.
textes.J'ai commencé à dessiner sur le mur de m: I started drawing on my bedroom wall when I was six. A dragon. My parents covered it with wallpaper. I drew it again on the wallpaper. They gave up. The dragon is still there.
textes.J'ai commencé à jouer à quatre ans. Ma m: I started playing at four. My mum says my first word was “again”. My second was “a coin”.
textes.J'ai compté les dalles du sol : cent qua: I counted the floor tiles: a hundred and forty-two. And a broken one.
textes.J'ai compté les marches du temple, comme: I counted the temple steps, like she did when she was little. Three hundred and sixty-four! She told me to count again. Four times! The fifth time, I got it: I'd forgotten the platform at the top! Three hundred and sixty-five, like the days of the year! The temple is a calendar! I shouted, and the macaws flew away.
textes.J'ai confié à Haldir deux cent quatre-vi: I've given Haldir two hundred and eighty letters for Ilyria. Two hundred and eighty times I've run after him to take it back before he knocked. Once, he was already on the last walkway. I jumped. Taeron had to repair the railing, and I kept the letter.
textes.J'ai connu Firmin, son père, quand Sylva: I knew Firmin, his father, when Sylvain was just a kid counting chips under the table. Firmin kept me a seat by the fire on rainy evenings. Sylvain still keeps it for me. I tell the gamblers that the ghosts of a crew play at the Tooth at night. He pretends not to like it. He leaves three dice on the table when he goes.
textes.J'ai connu la Colonne quand la cabine ét: I remember the Column when the cabin was made of wood. It creaked like my husband. I miss them both.
textes.J'ai connu la Fronde quand ce n'était qu: I knew the Fronde when it was just a scrapyard and a fire in a wheelbarrow. The fire's still here. So am I. The wheelbarrow, Fusain painted it on the Wall.
textes.J'ai connu la grand-mère de la Président: I knew the President's grandmother, Amélie Nacre. She drew domes on every tablecloth. In the end, the restaurants gave her paper.
textes.J'ai construit deux cent douze dômes. Le: I've built two hundred and twelve domes. The smallest is for a glug-glug in the Greenhouse. The biggest is the Council Hall. Écliptique wanted it square, “for seriousness”. I made it round. He got lost in it three times: there's no corner to take refuge in. Since then, he says round is very protocol-friendly.

I've built two hundred and twelve domes. The smallest is for a gurgle in the Greenhouse. The biggest is the Council Hall. Écliptique wanted it square, “for seriousness”. I made it round. He got lost in it three times. There's no corner to hide in.
textes.J'ai construit l'Albatros avec des toile: I built the Albatross from tent canvas, barrels and an engine I found in a barn. On the day of the first flight, it took off upside down. I was hanging head first over the Orchards. Old Bastien waved at me with a rake. I waved back with my feet.
textes.J'ai construit la Serre des Espèces pour: I built the Greenhouse of Species for the sky creatures that pass near Astralys: the sky jellyfish, see-through, that sing like rubbed glasses; the glug-glugs, soft little balls that go “glug-glug”; the comet-butterflies. I look after them when they're tired. Some leave again. Some stay.
textes.J'ai construit la cabane de Marley au-de: I built Marley's hut above his banana trees, near Barnabé's place. He paid me in bunches: one per plank. Eighty-three planks. I ate bananas for three months. Jam, fritters, bread, grilled bananas. I can't look at one any more. I've never told him.
textes.J'ai construit le berceau de Tornade ave: I built Tornade's cradle from a pallet and one of Rustine's bike wheels. It rocked by itself. Then Cerise's. Tornade got out of his at six months, by rolling it. He was already in a hurry.
I built the Borgo's bread oven. I got the dome wrong: it leans to one side. I wanted to redo it. Lasagna said: “No, leave it.” I don't know why. The bread is very good. Must be thanks to her hands.
textes.J'ai construit une rampe de skate en pal: I built a pallet skate ramp in our yard. Rustine insisted on guardrails. I put up guardrails. Tornade jumped over the guardrails on the very first day. I added cushions. He said it was the best ramp on the island. It's the only ramp with cushions.
textes.J'ai convaincu Roux de courir une Grande: I talked Roux into running a Great Race. Just one. He set off last, whistling. At the sixth arch, no more Roux! We looked everywhere. He was asleep underneath it, a leaf on his nose. He said he was saving his strength for the end. There was no end.
textes.J'ai couru la Grande Course pendant dix: I ran the Great Race for ten years. Never won. So now I organise it. It's almost the same, and I win every time.
textes.J'ai couru le marathon du continent quar: I've run the mainland marathon forty times. I won once. The other runner got lost.
textes.J'ai couru à côté de Bernadette pendant: I ran alongside Bernadette for a whole lap! Grandpa Ferdinand pretended he couldn't catch me!
textes.J'ai couru à l'Observatoire pour dire à: I ran to the Observatory to tell Zénith I'd beaten a shooting star. He looked through his telescope for a very long time. Then he said, very gently: “It was Professor Quasar's toaster.” I thought about it. I said: “Then I beat a toaster.” He said: “That's not bad either.”
textes.J'ai cousu des patins de feutre aux geno: I sewed felt pads onto the knees of his armour, for his night rounds. The first evening, he came home without a sound and suddenly appeared in the kitchen. I got such a fright I threw my hammer at him. He caught it in mid-air. Since then, he always makes a little clang on the landing.
textes.J'ai cousu le premier patch des Rats de: I sewed the first Bilge Rats patch onto Clou's leather jacket while he was asleep on a bench in the square. He didn't wake up. When he opened his eyes, he looked at the patch, then at me, and said “Mh”. Rouille explained it was an enormous thank-you. I believe her.
textes.J'ai cousu un patch des Rats de Cale sur: I sewed a Bilge Rats patch onto the bandana of each of Chaussette's six dogs. When they heard Clou's guitar that same evening, they all howled together, like a choir. Rouille said they were the best backing singers on the island. They know it.
textes.J'ai cousu à Calcine une robe de scène a: I sewed Calcine a stage dress with ember sequins that light up when she plays fast. The first evening, she played so fast that a sequin flew off and shot straight into the mouth of Madame Hurla, who was shouting next to her. Total silence on the square, the longest in its history. I sewed the sequins back on. More firmly. A little regretfully.
textes.J'ai creusé sous toute la montagne. Il y: I've dug under the whole mountain. There are tunnels even the king doesn't know about. Neither do I, come to that. I've forgotten them.
textes.J'ai câblé toute la radio du Sergent, da: I wired up the Sergeant's whole radio, in the Freighter's wheelhouse. He talks, I carry his voice. He's tireless. So are his cables, luckily.
textes.J'ai dansé avec un dauphin, là, au bout: I danced with a dolphin, right there, at the end of the beach. I did, I did. Ask Zoé.
textes.J'ai dansé pour la première fois sur le: I danced on the Boulevard for the first time when I was fifteen. It was raining. There was nobody around. Just an old android sweeping. At the end, he put down his broom and clapped. It was Zéro. My first audience.
textes.J'ai demandé au Professeur de calculer l: I asked the Professor to calculate the perfect curve for a dome. He wrote an equation two metres long on the board. I looked at it, then I drew a circle in the air with my fingertip. It was perfect. The Professor framed his equation next to my circle. He says they're brothers.
textes.J'ai demandé au Zéphyr de m'emmener là o: I asked the Zéphyr to take me somewhere nobody had ever invented anything. Gustave, the commander's brother, dropped me off at Carène. I took three steps along the quay and saw a man drinking sparkling apple. Sparkling apple! They invented it a hundred years ago. I came back on the next flight. The commander was waiting for me with a cup of tea.
textes.J'ai demandé au Zéphyr de m'emmener quel: I asked the Zéphyr to take me somewhere nobody had ever invented anything. It dropped me at Carène. They invented cider. No luck.
textes.J'ai demandé aux élèves de dessiner leur: I asked the pupils to draw their animal in a codex. Pilli drew Tlaco… with fur. Lots of fur, everywhere, like a cloud. I asked him why. He said: “So he won't be cold in Mictlan.” I didn't correct anything. I hung the drawing on the wall. It was the most beautiful in the class.
textes.J'ai demandé un slow à Mistral. Un vrai,: I asked Mistral for a slow dance. A real one, like on my father's boat. He gave me a slow dance at a hundred and forty-five beats per minute. I told him it was a disgrace to humanity. I danced it to the very end. And I ask him again every Saturday, because somebody has to protest.
I asked for a flame on my helmet. Mum said: “Sensible.” Pigment tried. Her sensible flame goes all the way round the helmet and up to the top. I said it was the most sensible flame I'd ever seen. Mum sighed. Pigment winked at me.
textes.J'ai demandé à Bigoudi si un bus pouvait: I asked Bigoudi if a bus could skateboard. She said no. I said “not yet.” She looked worried. I've already got a plan.
textes.J'ai demandé à Coyotl pourquoi les jarre: I asked Coyotl why Tlaloc's jars have fangs. He told me it's to guard the rain, like a dog guards the house. So Tlaco is a jar! A jar that guards the house. Now I call him “my little jar”. He likes it. I think.
textes.J'ai demandé à Fernand de m'apprendre le: I asked Fernand to teach me the bowline knot. Very useful for a collector: you tie everything down. He showed me three times. On the fourth, I tied myself to the bench on the quay, very securely. Fernand laughed so hard that two seagulls took off. It took half an hour to untie me. Splendid knot.
textes.J'ai demandé à Ferraille de souder des c: I asked Ferraille to weld studs onto Germaine's headstock. He said it was a delicate instrument. I looked at him. For a long time. He welded the studs. They shine on stage. Germaine is happy. Ferraille too, I think.
textes.J'ai demandé à Glorb de poser pour une é: I asked Glorb to pose for a label. He stayed still for an hour, without wobbling, out of politeness. At the end, he asked me to pose for a photo. I held my old boot in my arms. His mum, on Gloop, got the photo. She bounced. I'm on display on another planet.
textes.J'ai demandé à Joe d'amener Bartholomé s: I asked Joe to bring Bartholomé on stage one evening, just to see. At the chorus of the whalers' jig, Bartholomé shrieked “Jellyfish-head!” on the third beat, exactly. The room exploded. I rewrote the whole chorus around his cry. Joe was so proud he wept into his beard. Bartholomé, for his part, demanded a seed.
textes.J'ai demandé à Jos une aiguille courbe,: I asked Jos for a curved needle, as long as a hand, for thick canvas. He asked what canvas. I said: “A canvas.” He didn't ask anything else. Three days later, the needle was on my workbench, wrapped in a rag, with a note: “For the canvas.” He'd engraved a little star on it.
textes.J'ai demandé à Lyre un poème pour un dis: I asked Lyre for a poem for an official speech. She gave me four words: “Écliptique, unique, protocol, pratfall.” I had it framed in gold letters. Since then, every visitor who reads it bursts out laughing. It must be the emotion. Poetry does that.
textes.J'ai demandé à Matthias quel était l'end: I asked Matthias where the stillest place on the island was. He searched for three weeks, with his compasses. He drew me a meadow above the bay, behind the north point, between two oaks. I asked if it moved. He said no. I keep the map in my apron. I look at it when my aunt's back is turned.
textes.J'ai demandé à Moloka de garder deux chi: I asked Moloka to look after two pups for a day. In the evening, when I came to fetch them, they were asleep in a fish basket, one on top of the other, and Moloka had made them little collars out of fishing net. She told me: “They ate my shoe.” Her eyes were wet when she handed them back.
textes.J'ai demandé à Momo un collier avec une: I asked Momo for a necklace with a single pearl, found near the golden point. I didn't tell him why it mattered. He asked me only one question: “Blue thread or gold thread?” I said blue. I still wear it, under my scarf. He never asked again.
textes.J'ai demandé à Octave si je pouvais cons: I asked Octave if I could build a little hut in his kapok tree, below his. He said: “To spy on me with Barnabé?” I said I just wanted the view. He said: “The view costs extra.” So I build somewhere else. Lower down. With less view.
textes.J'ai demandé à Perlée de donner mon nom: I asked Perlée to give my name to a drop. She said every drop already had its own. The next day, on a flower, there was a drop resting right under a firefly. It was glowing. Perlée said ever so softly: “This one is called Lumi.” I shrieked so loudly that the drop fell off.
textes.J'ai demandé à Pépin une course qui fass: I asked Pépin for a race that goes round the whole island. He got out his stopwatch, counted on his fingers, scratched his ears, counted again. “Three weeks, Grisou.” I said: “Perfect, wolves are all about stamina!” He put his stopwatch away. He didn't say no, mind. He didn't say yes either.
textes.J'ai demandé à Sextant le plan du Quarti: I asked Sextant for a plan of the Bubble District. He brought me a rectangle with circles in it. I let out a little cry: “Why corners?” He said: “Sheets have corners.” The next day, I brought him a round sheet, cut out specially. He sighed. He redrew everything. It's magnificent.
textes.J'ai demandé à Sextant pourquoi il ne fi: I asked Sextant why he never finishes his map. He said: “There's a little bit missing, in the south.” I asked him why he didn't draw it. He answered: “Because then it would be finished.” I understood. I have a display case I never fill, for the same reason.
textes.J'ai demandé à Sofia si on pouvait aller: I asked Sofia if we could go and see Atlantis together, just the two of us. She stopped swimming all of a sudden. She said “one day”, in a small voice. I didn't push. That evening she gave me a pearly shell, found really deep down. I think it was a serious “one day”.
textes.J'ai demandé à Solenne comment poussaien: I asked Solenne how trees grow, down below. She told me about rain, black soil, roots that drink, apples that fall on farmers' heads. I listened to her for a whole afternoon, sitting by the pond. My flowers blinked like applause. They loved the story.
textes.J'ai demandé à Solenne, qui ne descend j: I asked Solenne, who never goes down below, what a colander might be for. She answered straight away: “For draining pasta.” Then she added: “I read it in a book.” Murmure told me there were no books about pasta. I said nothing. I quite like mysteries.
textes.J'ai demandé à Tapage de m'apprendre la: I asked Tapage to teach me the drums. He showed me his legendary 1977 drum roll. I got it on the first try. He said it was a fluke. I did it ten more times. He said it was ten flukes. Then he gave me one of his old drumsticks. I keep it in my archive room.
I asked Zénith where north was. He showed me the North Star. I said: “No, on my map.” He took my pencil and drew the star at the top of my map. I kept it. My north is the only one in the archipelago that has a star. The other cartographers would be jealous, if there were any.
textes.J'ai demandé à Zénith sous quelle étoile: I asked Zénith which star to plant my glowing seeds under. He showed me a little blue star, very gentle. I always plant them facing it. They grow faster than the others. Zénith says it's because I talk to them. I say it's the star. We'll never know.
textes.J'ai demandé à chaque juré d'écrire son: I asked each juror to write their favourite on a slip of paper. Basile handed me a list. Capucine, Ambroise, Prudence, Firmin… everyone. And himself, very small, in a corner. I asked him to choose just one. He looked so miserable that I withdrew the question.
textes.J'ai demandé à l'Hologuide pourquoi sa v: I asked the Hologuide why his tour had fifteen stops and not sixteen. He rebooted. I waited for him, sitting on the ground. When he came back, I told him: “We'll look for the sixteenth one together.” He said: “File created.” I look every day. I haven't found it yet. But I'm looking.
textes.J'ai demandé à la Doyenne pourquoi elle: I asked the Elder why she was so old. She answered: “Because I started early.” I thought about it for a very long time. Then I decided to start too, right away. I blew on my hands, really hard. Since then, I've been getting older on purpose. The Elder says it's already starting to show.
textes.J'ai demandé à Écrou de négocier le prix: I asked Écrou to negotiate the price of iron ore with her family. I offered to pay in free explosions: one a month, your choice, with fireworks. She looked at me for a long time and said: “Go up and apologise. In person. On foot.” I'm getting my shoes ready. I've been getting them ready for a month.
I asked. They all said Marcel.
textes.J'ai dessiné des constellations sur les: I drew constellations on Sextant's maps while he was asleep. Now Balafre Island has a Great Bear, and Port-Azur a Little Sock. Sextant was furious for a day. On the second day, he drew one himself, on Ember Island. He called it “the Great Coughing Volcano”.
textes.J'ai dessiné les cartes de toutes les îl: I drew the maps of every island in the archipelago, with a stick of charcoal and a ruler. For each island, I climbed to the highest point and drew what I saw. It took me forty years. The maps fit in a single drawer.
I drew the maps of every island in the archipelago. Every one. With a stick of charcoal and a ruler. People said my maps were too pretty to use. They used them anyway.
textes.J'ai dessiné un manuel de réparation pou: I drew a repair manual for Mum's workshop, with bikes exploded into a thousand pieces and arrows everywhere. People come to the workshop just to look at it. Mum says it's the clearest manual in the world. She's right. I signed every page with a little cherry.
textes.J'ai dessiné une petite étoile sur une d: I drew a little star on one of her coastal maps, in pencil, for Clémentine. She didn't rub it out. I think about it often.
textes.J'ai deux carnets. Dans le premier, j'éc: I have two journals. In the first, I write down Hilaire's advice. In the second, I draw what he does. The first is full of “stay to the side”, “don't run”, “count to three”. The second is full of drawings of Hilaire inside a frog. It's happened forty-seven times, according to Yvon. I've drawn thirty.
textes.J'ai deux enfants, des jumeaux : Bulle,: I have two children, twins: Bulle, at the Baths, and Vespérine, at the market. One laughs all the time, the other almost never. And yet I raised them the same. Well, I think so. Maybe I tickled Bulle a bit more.
textes.J'ai dicté à Ori un décret magnifique :: I dictated a magnificent decree to Ori: “By order of the king, fizz is a royal treasure.” He wrote: “Fizz is a treasure.” I asked where “royal” had gone. He said: “Ulfa would never have put it up.” He was right. The decree still hangs above the counter at the Mug.
I conducted the great storm of '40. It obeyed me. Almost.
textes.J'ai dit au jury que je ne savais pas co: I told the jury I didn't know how my machine made heart-shaped bubbles. That's not true. I know. They come when I think of Lise. I blow more gently without realising it, and the soap does the rest. Don't tell Margot, {surnom}. She already counts everything else.
I said a coffee. Not a question.
textes.J'ai dit à Pyra que j'avais brûlé Bertra: I told Pyra I'd burnt Bertrand on purpose, for fun, like you. She didn't laugh.
textes.J'ai dit à Sylvie que son mari retrouver: I told Sylvie her husband would find his camera thanks to “someone who walks a lot”. She smiled the way you smile at a pupil who's making things up. Then she said: “You saw him come down from the lookout empty-handed, didn't you?” I didn't answer. A fortune-teller doesn't answer. She smiles harder.
textes.J'ai dit à Vibrato : « Tes antennes vibr: I told Vibrato: “Your antennae quiver when Prisme dances: it's love, it's plain to see.” He answered: “Maybe it's just for the rhyme.” I counted on my fingers. It didn't even rhyme. So it was true. He blushed silver. I haven't told anyone. Well, no one who whispers.
textes.J'ai donné des noms à mes trois mannequi: I gave names to my three dummies: Bertrand, Hubert and Germaine. Oscar has burnt Bertrand eleven times, Hubert six. Germaine, only once, but she was behind him, at the other end of the Ground. I still don't know how. Neither does he. I restuff her with fresh straw while staring at him.
textes.J'ai donné ma veste de 1977 à la Gratuit: I gave my 1977 jacket to the Free Shop, for History. The next day, I took it back: History didn't need it any more. Trocante and Velours gave each other a funny look. I don't know why. It's a jacket from 1977. Well, from a legendary year.
textes.J'ai donné ma vieille boule de cristal f: I gave my old cracked crystal ball to the Free Shop. Someone took it. It came back a week later. Gone, back again. Like Trocante's teapot. I said the ball had chosen the Free Shop as its home. Trocante said: “Obviously.” She learned it from me.
textes.J'ai donné un champignon des fées à Bast: I gave Bastien a fairy mushroom, in front of everyone. He put it in his pocket, rolling his eyes. A few days later, I saw fish glowing a little, around his boat. I didn't ask him anything. He didn't tell me anything. But he doesn't say “of course” quite the same way any more.
textes.J'ai donné un nom aux grands vers rouge: I gave a name to the big red-and-white worms outside the Bay: “the candy canes”. The Professor looked for a more learned name for a whole week. Then he wrote “candy canes” in his big report. With my name beside it. I'm in a scientific report. At ten years old.
I've given names to eleven thousand stars. The Little Sock, Gloubi's Nose, The-One-Who-Waves, the Great Glutton. The Elder thinks my names aren't serious enough. I named a star after her: “Granny”. She laughed for three days. She looks for it every aurora night, from her bench.

I've named eleven thousand stars. “The Little Sock”. “Gloubi's Nose”. “The One That Says Peekaboo”. The Elder thinks my names aren't serious enough. She has a star named after her. I called it “Granny”. She laughed for three days.
textes.J'ai donné une semaine de cours à Fanny: I gave Fanny a week of lessons so she'd dance “smaller”, elbows tucked in. She lasted two tracks. On the third, her arm flew out, and me with it. I landed in Tchoum's arms. I never told Fanny it was my best night of the year. She's still wondering if she passed the exam.
textes.J'ai donné à Gédéon un stage au Bureau :: I gave Gédéon an internship at the Office: stamping eviction notices. He stamped them in rhythm. Boom-chak, boom-boom-chak. All morning. Miss Prune started tapping her foot. So did I. I stopped dead. I ended the internship. The stamps stayed in my head for three days.
textes.J'ai dormi trois jours. Ce n'est rien :: I slept for three days. That's nothing: last time it was three years.
textes.J'ai droit à une question par jour. Une: I'm allowed one question a day. Just one! So I write them in a notebook so I don't lose them. I've got two hundred in reserve. One day, I asked her if she'd ever been little. She thought about it for three days. Then she said: “Yes. Not for long.” I don't understand, but it's a good answer.
textes.J'ai découvert que j'avais le vertige à: I found out I was scared of heights when I was six. On a stool. Reaching for a jar of jam. I stayed up there for an hour, frozen. In the end my mother gave me the jam on the stool. It was tasty, but it was high.
textes.J'ai découvert une étoile qui n'était su: I discovered a star that wasn't on any map. I named it “Cliquetis”. It blinks. Like everything here.
textes.J'ai démonté ma première montre à quatre: I took apart my first watch at the age of four. My grandfather's. I put it back together at four and a half. There was one part left over. I kept it. I still don't know where it goes. The watch works anyway. It keeps me awake at night.
textes.J'ai démonté mon premier réveil à cinq a: I took apart my first alarm clock at five. I put it back together at five and a half. It rang backwards: it put people to sleep. My mother kept it. She still uses it for naps.
textes.J'ai déposé une lampe cassée au Troc ce: I dropped off a broken lamp at the Swap Shop this morning. Tonight, it's lighting Bricole's walkway. Everything gets used in the end, here.
textes.J'ai développé ta photo. Tu as une aile: I developed your photo. You've got a blue wing instead of an arm. It's in my box of important people.
I went to sea as a cabin boy at twelve. The captain always found me at the bow, chatting with the seagulls. He said I was mad. One day, the seagulls all flew off towards the coast at once. I shouted “storm!”. Nobody believed me. Then the storm came. The captain never called me mad again.
textes.J'ai embarqué comme mousse à onze ans, s: I signed on as a cabin boy at eleven, on a schooner that carried rope. That's why I came back here, to Rigging Harbour. Ropes, I know them all. Bowline, clove hitch, heart knot. The last one, I've only tied once. That's nobody's business.
textes.J'ai embarqué il y a un an. Je voulais v: I signed on a year ago. I wanted to see the world. Mostly I've seen the deck. Up close. With a brush.
textes.J'ai embarqué à douze ans comme mousse s: I went to sea at twelve as a cabin boy on a fishing boat. The captain told me: “You want to be a pirate? Then first learn to peel potatoes.” I peeled potatoes for five years. Then I got my own boat. I named her the Bold Potato.
textes.J'ai emmené Félix en pédalo, pour lui mo: I took Félix out on a pedalo to show him the sea up close. Three metres. Not one more. He went green, then white, then green again, and begged me to go back. On the jetty, he lay down and said: “I'll be your navigator. From here.” I gave him a bucket, for the big voyage. He kept it.
textes.J'ai emmené Prisme faire un tour en souc: I took Prisme for a ride in my saucer. She got dizzy, so she danced in the cockpit to calm down. Her ribbons of light filled the whole saucer. I couldn't see a thing. I landed blind, upside down, on pad number two. We laughed for an hour. Ionie, a bit less.
textes.J'ai emmené Zénith voir les étoiles très: I took Zénith to see the stars very high up, above the clouds, in Rocket. He cried. I switched off the engine so as not to disturb him. We stayed floating for an hour, without a sound. It's the only time in my life I've stayed still for an hour. It didn't kill me. It was actually nice.
textes.J'ai emprunté la barque de Bastien pour: I borrowed Bastien's rowing boat to go find my dolphin. I rowed far, really far. No dolphin. And I dropped both oars waving big hellos at a seagull. I swam home pushing the boat. I made him a necklace to say sorry. He says he doesn't wear it. He wears it.
textes.J'ai emprunté les six derniers bâtons lu: I borrowed Lila's last six glow sticks to juggle her a rainbow. It was magnificent for three seconds. Then one went into the sea and another into Nono's hair. Lila said nothing. She just wrote something down in her journal. I think I owe her six sticks. And an apology.
textes.J'ai emprunté à Murmure les quatorze liv: I borrowed Murmure's fourteen books from down below that talk about cats. I read them aloud to the glug-glugs, in the Greenhouse. I'm sure they're starting to go “meow”. Murmure says it's still “glug”. But she admits there's a slight accent. A cat accent.
I still feel like eating flies.
textes.J'ai enfin reçu mon programme exceptionn: My extraordinary program has finally arrived! The Turbo-Adventure 3000. The best of them all. It'll make your adventure easier, faster, more… everything. Just ask me: for you, I'll do a special price.
textes.J'ai enregistré Flanelle en cachette, un: I secretly recorded Flanelle one evening, from the garage window. I played the recording through my speakers at four in the morning. The whole meadow slept to music.
textes.J'ai enregistré en secret le solo de onz: I secretly recorded Tapage's eleven-minute solo, the night he stood in for the drummer. I played it backwards, for a laugh, at the end of a concert. It sounded better. Everyone said so. Tapage was furious. The next day, I caught him listening to it on a loop.
textes.J'ai entendu dire que tu avais aidé {qn}: I heard you'd helped {qn}. Good. We need people like you.
textes.J'ai entendu dire que vous aviez aidé {q: I heard you'd helped {qn}. Good. We need people like you.
textes.J'ai entendu un cœur battre, au fond d'u: I heard a heart beating, at the end of a tunnel. Boom… boom… Don't tell the king.
textes.J'ai entendu un petit rire derrière un b: I heard a little laugh behind a bush. Goblins laugh a lot. Or else it's Sir Tancrède.
textes.J'ai entendu une branche craquer. C'étai: I heard a branch snap. It was me. I stepped on it. Sorry, branch.
textes.J'ai enterré un os en 2019. Je cherche e: I buried a bone in 2019. Still looking.
I buried a bone near the fountain. Don't tell anyone. Especially not Pneu.
textes.J'ai envoyé des jarres jusqu'à Per-Hâpy,: I've sent jars all the way to Per-Hâpy, to the Egyptians. Their potter, Ptahmosé, sent me back a scarab. I think it was a compliment.
textes.J'ai essayé boulanger : j'ai brûlé le fo: I tried being a baker: I burned down the oven. A postman: I ate a letter (it smelled of cake). A lighthouse keeper: I fell asleep and the light went out. They told me: “Linguini, you're good for nothing.” So I set off to find the place where people are good for nothing.
textes.J'ai essayé de compter combien de temps: I tried to count how long Lucie stays underwater. I got to a hundred, and then I skipped seventy. So I started again with pebbles: one pebble every ten seconds. When she came up, there were nineteen pebbles. She said: “You put two down at once.” It was true.
textes.J'ai essayé de le faire rire pendant un: I tried to make him laugh for a month: faces, Mange-Clous's jokes, the crab dance. Nothing. One day, I slipped on a sardine and fell into the washerwoman's laundry basket. That's when he laughed. Not a sound, but his shoulders were shaking like a bridge in a storm. Since then, I always keep a sardine in my pocket.
textes.J'ai essayé de lui poser des énigmes plu: I tried setting her easier riddles. “I'm blue, I'm up high, and there are clouds in me.” She got it! I clapped. Too loudly, apparently: she realised. Now she asks me for “real” ones. I don't dare any more.
textes.J'ai essayé de ne pas finir un livre, co: I tried not finishing a book, like you. I held out until the second-to-last page. It's very hard.
textes.J'ai essayé de photographier Titou trois: I've tried to photograph Titou three hundred and twelve times. In every one, he's a pink streak with dark glasses. One day he promised to stay still for just one second. He managed it. And then he sneezed. I sighed so hard the camera moved too. He wants all his photos: he calls them “my ghost portraits”.
textes.J'ai essayé de trouver une rime à « Pris: I tried to find a rhyme for “Prisme”: prism, rhythm, schism, chasm, spasm. Nothing works. One day, I ended up writing: “Prisme dances, oh Prisme.” I was furious with myself. Prisme cried when she heard it. She said it was the loveliest one. I'll never understand dancers.
textes.J'ai essayé le tambour. Les voisins ont: I tried the drum. The neighbors signed a petition. Then the trumpet: they moved away. Two are left, and I'll get them too.
textes.J'ai essayé ta potion pour voler ! Mes c: I tried your flying potion! My socks floated. I didn't. It's a start, right?
textes.J'ai essayé une fois de lui parler en fa: Once I tried to talk to her face to face, at the fountain. I'd prepared a four-page speech. I said: “Lovely day.” She said: “Very.” And I ran off. Haldir says it's the longest conversation we've had in a century.
textes.J'ai eu des jumeaux, une fille et un gar: I had twins, a girl and a boy, three minutes apart. Vespérine came first, frowning. Bulle arrived laughing. I raised them among the peppers and the sulphur roses. At five, she was labelling my jams; he was blowing bubbles in my watering can. My little root and my little soap bubble.
textes.J'ai eu mon premier ballon à six ans. Un: I got my first balloon when I was six. A red party balloon. I let go of it, it went up, and up… I cried, then I decided to catch it. I'm still looking for it. That's why the Albatross is red: so the balloon will recognise me.
textes.J'ai eu peur du noir pendant toute mon e: I was afraid of the dark my whole childhood. So I learned how to make light. Today, a whole town lights up thanks to me. Sometimes fear makes a very good job.
I had an apprentice once. Glaucos. Gifted, patient, three hundred years without one word louder than the next. Then one morning he softened some mother-of-pearl under the crystal and blew into it, like a bubble. A lamp in three minutes! I said: “That's cheating.” He packed up his tools, politely. That was a hundred years ago. The workshop's too quiet.
textes.J'ai fabriqué Germaine moi-même. Le manc: I built Germaine myself. The neck comes from a banister in the Spinning Mill. The body, from a door of the Rusty Whale. The strings, I bought. There are limits to homemade.
textes.J'ai fabriqué Monsieur Paille, l'épouvan: I made Mister Paille, the scarecrow, to protect my flowers from the crows. The crows sat on his arms. Now they're friends. They protect the flowers for him. It's better that way.
textes.J'ai fabriqué pour Brindille un « sac po: I built Brindille a “jet-powered mailbag”. On the first try, it caught fire above the port, and she crossed the Harbour backwards, smoking like a chimney. Every letter reached its destination! A little toasted, but people said they smelled of fresh bread. For me, it's a total success. Brindille disagrees.
textes.J'ai fabriqué pour Céleste une petite la: I made Céleste a little red battery lamp. White light dazzles an astronomer's eye for twenty minutes; red doesn't. She reads her notes without losing a single star. She wears it around her neck at night. When I look towards the observatory from my tower, I see a little red dot moving about. It reassures me.
textes.J'ai fabriqué pour Lucie un crayon de ci: I made Lucie a wax pencil and a little board, to draw underwater. Her first drawing looked like a poorly octopus. She gave it to me with a shrug. I framed it, next to the big map. It may not be a drawing of a stone, but it's the first drawing ever made underwater. It's historic.
textes.J'ai fabriqué pour Rustine une sonnette: I made Rustine a rat-shaped bike bell, with a little jingle bell and a bit of pipe. When you ring it, the rat opens its mouth. She whistled so loud with joy that my goggles rattled. All of Boucan wanted one. I made forty. The quays ring like a party.
textes.J'ai fait cent fois l'aller-retour entre: I've gone back and forth between the tables a hundred times. My feet hate me, but I'm fond of them.
textes.J'ai fait comme vous m'avez dit : je ne: I did what you told me: I only believe in the good signs. Yesterday, a rainbow over the hotel. I kept it.
textes.J'ai fait croire à Glorb que la fontaine: I made Glorb believe the fountain was going to show the planet Gloop all day long, in his honour. He waited in front of the fountain from eight till noon, camera ready. Gloop went by for just one minute. I was laughing behind a bench. He took a photo of me laughing. He says that's his revenge. It's a nice photo.
textes.J'ai fait la course avec une mouette au-: I raced a seagull over the harbour. It cheated: it caught the wind. I lost a fin. Ionie replaced it, grumbling, and welded a little seagull drawing onto it. I laughed so hard I nearly fell off the landing pad. Now Rocket has a seagull. It flies better.
textes.J'ai fait la liste des suspects. Le maît: I've made a list of suspects. The lifeguard? I asked Kevin: he laughed so hard he swallowed his whistle. The bookseller? Félix gets seasick just eating fish. The professor? He wouldn't notice a sea bream in his bed. I've got names left. I'm trying them one by one.
textes.J'ai fait la première montée vers la Cit: I made the first ride up to the City of Clouds, with Barnabé at the controls, without saying a single word the whole way. Now that all the lines have reopened, I dream of doing the whole thing: from the sky right down to the bottom of the sea. In silence. Just watching the Column do what it does best.

I made the first ride up to the City of Clouds, with Barnabé at the controls, without saying a single word the whole way. Now I dream of doing the whole thing, once all the lines have reopened: from the sky right down to the bottom of the sea. In silence. Just watching the Column do what it does best.

I made the first ride up to the City of Clouds. With my eyes shut for almost the whole way. Now I dream of doing it again with my eyes open, from start to finish, of saying “Going up!” without my voice shaking, and of going to sit with Théo on his Glass Belvedere.
textes.J'ai fait les jarres de la Maison de Vie: I made the jars of the House of Life, the ones in the temple, and the big jar where Mérit brews her beer. My jars don't leak. Not every potter can say that.
textes.J'ai fait poser sur la porte de sa tour: I had a copper plaque put on the door of his tower: “Ministry of Geography”. He made me promise never to ask him for avenues again. I promised. The next day, I asked him for a trading port. He drew it for me on a separate sheet. I keep it in a separate drawer. For later.
textes.J'ai fait réciter les neuf godets de la: I had all my pupils recite the nine wells of the Palette, for forty years. One, blue. Two, green… Today the whole village knows them by heart. Very handy, now that they have to be found again.
textes.J'ai fait six ans de médecine. Un dimanc: I studied medicine for six years. One Sunday, at a second-hand bookseller's, I found an old collection of remedies from the archipelago, with dried leaves pressed between the pages. I read it that night, cover to cover, twice. Fifteen years ago I landed here with a trunk of jars that clinked with every wave. The next day I opened the herbalist's shop.
textes.J'ai fait ta blague sur la place, celle: I did your joke on the square, the one about problems. The parents laughed. A kid asked me what a problem was. Lovely day.
textes.J'ai fait tomber un verre du bar de Sirè: I knocked a glass off Sirène's bar. She said “Again?!”. I took it as an invitation.
textes.J'ai fait toutes les fêtes de l'archipel: I went to every party in the archipelago, kid. Every one. Except my daughter's. Her birthdays, her first dance, her wedding: I was always somewhere else, dancing for strangers. Now she writes me two letters a year. Lulu is my second chance, {surnom}. I don't miss a single one of her parties any more. Not even her naps against the speakers.
I've been to every party in the archipelago. Even one at the dwarves', in a mine. The echo was incredible.
textes.J'ai fait un rêve avec un dragon !: I had a dream with a dragon!
textes.J'ai fait un tour en Zéphyr ! On voit to: I went for a ride on the Zéphyr! You can see everything from up there! I spat out of the window. It's not allowed. Don't tell.
textes.J'ai fait un vœu dans la fontaine de Dam: I made a wish in Lady Ysolde's fountain. I won't tell you what. It has something to do with bolts.
textes.J'ai fait un vœu à la Fontaine des Bulle: I made a wish at the Bubble Fountain. You whisper it to a bubble, and it carries it up to the surface. Mine's a secret. But it's a very big one.
textes.J'ai fait une bosse dans le plus beau dô: I put a dent in Bulle's most beautiful dome. She kept it! She says it has character. She made me a door that only opens if you pull a face. It's the best door in the universe.
textes.J'ai fait une bulle si grande que Cerise: I made a bubble so big that Cerise got inside it. She floated above the square for three seconds, all happy, then the bubble burst and she landed on her feet. She said: “Again.” It took me a week to make another one that big. She waited next to me the whole time.
textes.J'ai fait une couronne de trèfles. Elle: I made a clover crown. It's for the cloud that looks like a sheep.
textes.J'ai fait une potion contre la foudre po: I made an anti-lightning potion for Violette. She turned blue. The lightning got through anyway. I noted: “Lightning makes no distinction between colours.”
textes.J'ai fait une potion pour qu'elle lise e: I made a potion so she'd read even faster. She didn't want it. So I drank it myself. All day, the letters danced in front of my eyes, in every book, round and round. I didn't read a single word. Lin says I read a waltz. Lin doesn't laugh often. That day, she did.
textes.J'ai fini par coudre des coussins dans l: In the end I sewed cushions into Cradoc's trousers. He says it's improved his balance. Mostly it's improved his landings: now he bounces. He's turned it into an act. The children call him “the bouncing juggler”.
I ended up sleeping on the floor.
textes.J'ai fondé la Fabrique. Balayeurs, porte: I founded the Works. Sweepers, porters, the Bielle's butler. Simple, solid machines. And two apprentices who mattered. Héloïse, at fifteen: a clockmaker's hands, a head too full. Then Wilfried: patient, solid, a bit of a dreamer. The others, I've forgotten their names. Not those two. Hm.
textes.J'ai fondé les Gouttières avec Grésil da: I started the Gutters with Grésil in a red tin garage. Then Bruine came with her bass, and Bourrasque with her drums. We play loud because the rain hits the tin hard. We've got to drown out the noise.
textes.J'ai formé des mousses. Le premier dont: I trained cabin boys. The first one people remember is little Aristide: on the second day, he fell in the water while telling a story. Fished out with the boathook, by his belt. He became mayor, which goes to show. After that, there was Marius Vasseur. Fifteen years on my boat. The best. Him, his knots, and his father's net.
textes.J'ai glissé une banane dans le panier de: One evening I slipped a banana into Fanny's basket, so her boss could taste it. She never told me what became of it. But a week later, she let slip, all casual: “Banana croissants, still no. But a little banana bun… maybe.” Maybe! I danced till morning.
textes.J'ai goûté la soupe de salicorne, à La C: I tried the samphire soup at La Conque. It tastes like the sea. But a friendly one. I went back for more twice.
textes.J'ai grandi au-dessus de la boutique de: I grew up above my aunt's flower shop, on the mainland. At eight, I knew the names of a hundred flowers, in Latin and for real. I fell asleep to the smell of hyacinths. But I'd never seen the sea. My aunt said it looked like a field of lavender that moves. She was right. In blue.
textes.J'ai grandi chez ma grand-mère, qui avai: I grew up at my grandmother's, who had an old upright piano with a candle on each side. I played it for hours. Very well, in fact, false modesty aside. But always alone, door closed. My grandmother listened from the kitchen, pretending to shell peas. In the middle of winter.
textes.J'ai grandi chez mon oncle Bedaine, au m: I grew up at my uncle Bedaine's, surrounded by swaps: I slept between a carpet that doesn't fly and a pile of singing pebbles. When I was little, I followed the jingle of my aunt Sésame's bell everywhere, at the tip of her tail. Ding, here I came. Ding, off I went. So they called me Grelot — that means little bell. Better than Pebble.
textes.J'ai grandi dans le jardin de ma grand-m: I grew up in my grandmother's garden, on the hill, behind the olive trees. I talked to the plants all day long. I told the thyme to grow straight, the mint to leave the tomatoes alone, and they listened to me. My grandmother said I had green fingers and the gift of the gab. That was before the bougainvilleas.
textes.J'ai grandi dans les copeaux. Mon père c: I grew up among wood shavings. My father built boats, I held the nails. I was eight when he made the Mabrouka, Driss's boat. He let me drive in a nail. Just one. It went in crooked. My father said: “It'll hold.” It still holds. Forty years. Driss still shows it to me.
textes.J'ai grandi dans un garage, sur le conti: I grew up in a garage, on the mainland. At four, I could take a wheel off. At ten, I could put it back on. My dad said I had engine oil in my veins and curlers in my hair — bigoudis, as we say. The name stuck.
textes.J'ai grandi dans une cuisine de ferme, e: I grew up in a farm kitchen, among ten brothers and sisters. In our house, anyone who didn't eat enough got a second plate. And anyone who did eat enough got a third. That's where I learnt the most important word in the language: “eat”.
textes.J'ai grandi dans une famille de bergers,: I grew up in a shepherd family, in the highlands. At eight, I took the village mill apart. At nine, they sent me to Cliquetis. Everyone was happy.
textes.J'ai grandi dans une ferme au bord du Bo: I grew up on a farm at the edge of the Goblin Wood. My father had a cherry tree. The crows devoured it. At eight, I made a hazel bow to chase them off. I never hit a crow. But I shot down all the cherries, one by one, right through the stalk. My father made jam.
textes.J'ai grandi dans une ferme, au bord du B: I grew up on a farm, at the edge of the Goblin Wood. I chased crows from the cherry trees with a hazel bow. Never hit one. I hit the cherries. One by one. My father picked them up.
textes.J'ai grandi dans une grande maison plein: I grew up in a big house full of beautiful things. Vases, paintings, rugs we weren't allowed to touch. My parents collected everything. I collected lonely afternoons. I learned the name of every object. I had no one to tell.
textes.J'ai grandi dans une maison de gardes, p: I grew up in a family of guards, near the North Gate. My father guarded the bridge, my mother guarded the house, and I guarded my little sister Flammèche, who brought home every lost animal in the city. One day, she brought home a lava crab. I guarded it too. It was called Mister Pincer.
textes.J'ai grandi dans une ville grise où on m: I grew up in a grey town where people always told me “shh”. In the canteen, in the library, at home. At twelve, I took a rucksack and the first boat to Boucan. The captain asked me why. I said: “To shout.” He laughed. He was right to laugh: they heard me from the harbour.
textes.J'ai grandi derrière son étal, à compter: I grew up behind her stall, counting coins before I could count fish. On her nine hundredth birthday, grandmother took my hands and passed me the recipe, move by move. “Not a word written down. It's handed on through the fingers.” That very evening, Abyssos came to ask if he could archive it. He's still waiting, poor thing.
textes.J'ai grandi ici. Je plonge depuis que je: I grew up here. I've been diving since I could walk. I can hold my breath for two minutes. OK, a minute and a half.
textes.J'ai grandi maison 1, au bord du grand c: I grew up in house 1, at the edge of the big field that became the airfield. With my little brother, Gustave, we flew kites there that were bigger than us. One very windy day, a kite lifted Gustave a good metre off the ground. I caught him by the belt. Ever since, he's the one who flies and I'm the one who worries. That's where it started.
textes.J'ai grandi près de la porte du nord, là: I grew up near the north gate, where the caravans come into town. I made my first guembri at eight: an iron sardine tin found behind Mustapha's grill, a stick, and three bits of string. It sounded like a cat with a cold. Omar, next door, was already drumming on every table. We had an orchestra.
textes.J'ai grandi sur le continent, chez une g: I grew up on the mainland, with a very proper grandmother who hid romance novels under the kitchen tea towels. I found every one of them. I read them in the broom cupboard, with a torch. At twelve, I knew everything about moonlit duels and kisses in the rain. About fractions, on the other hand, nothing.
textes.J'ai grandi sur les quais, dans une peti: I grew up on the quays, in a little house on the edge of the Old Dock. The seagulls woke me every morning. I learned to screech like them before I could talk. My first word was “KIAAA”. My parents were a bit worried. Then they laughed. So did I.
textes.J'ai grandi à Port-Azur, dans la ruelle: I grew up in Port-Azur, in the little street behind the harbour, with my three brothers. At home, we talked loud, ate fast and danced in the kitchen while doing the washing-up. My mum says I broke more plates dancing than washing them. She exaggerates. A bit.
textes.J'ai grandi à côté d'une corne de brume,: I grew up next to a foghorn, on a rocky point. Every two minutes, the horn went “BWOOO”. All night. To talk at home, you had to shout between two “BWOOO”s. I never lost the habit. Nor did my mother. Family dinners are always very loud.
I grew up next to a foghorn. It sounded every two minutes, all night long. To talk to each other at home, you had to shout between two “BWOOO”s. I never lost the habit. Neither did my mum.
textes.J'ai grimpé jusqu'à la troisième passere: I climbed up to the third footbridge with no hands, and I fell into a blackberry bush. Aëlwen put moss all over me and asked: “How many hands?” I said: “Zero.” She sighed so hard her jars rattled.
textes.J'ai huit ans et demi. À quatre ans, je: I'm eight and a half. At four, I was already counting my dad's bubbles. My mum was called Lise, she was a glassblower. She died when I was two. I don't remember her, but I have her glass marbles in a box. I've counted them all: a hundred and twenty-seven. There's a green one with a bubble inside. It's my favourite.
textes.J'ai huit ans. Et demi. Presque neuf. Bi: I'm eight. And a half. Nearly nine. Almost ten. Nonna says I'm all round like a gnocchi. I say I'm all strong like a pirate.
textes.J'ai hérité du moulin de mon oncle. Le p: I inherited the mill from my uncle. On the first day, I opened the wrong hatch, and all the flour fell on me. It's never really left me since. I'm a permanent miller.
textes.J'ai interdit au Professeur d'entrer au: I banned the Professor from entering the hangar “with an idea”. He came in with a screwdriver. He put it down on an engine, just put it down, and the engine started playing music. A waltz. I still don't know how. Vibrato comes to listen to it in the evenings. The Professor says it was “theoretically planned”.
textes.J'ai interrogé Bruno officiellement, ave: I questioned Bruno officially, with my notebook. He offered me a vanilla during the interrogation. He was talking about a little white shadow, over by the quay… and my ice cream was melting onto my notebook. By the end, the statement was illegible and sticky. I had to rewrite it all from memory. It still smells of vanilla. The statement.
textes.J'ai interviewé Cradoc la tête en bas, p: I interviewed Cradoc upside down, to see the world like a falling juggler. He answered upside down too. I printed the interview upside down: you have to flip the zine to read it. It's the most-read page. It took Tapage an hour to work out how.
textes.J'ai interviewé Papa pour mon zine. Il a: I interviewed Dad for my zine. He answered every question in centimetres. “Dad, what do you love? — Forty-two centimetres.” I published the interview with a tape measure drawn around it. People found it very deep. So did I, actually.
textes.J'ai interviewé tout le monde à Port-Bou: I've interviewed everyone in Port-Boucan. Except Clou: he answered “Mm” to every question. I published the interview anyway. It's a whole page of “Mm”. Very artistic.
textes.J'ai inventé l'Hologuide, les ponts de l: I invented the Hologuide, the bridges of light, the fountain of planets and the gravitational toaster. The gravitational toaster can't be found any more. It went upwards with the toast. One day, it'll come back down.
textes.J'ai inventé la lave glacée à la brioche: I invented brioche frozen lava: one of Bobor's brioches, frozen, with fire syrup. It was horrible. Bobor told me so. I tasted it, and I said: “It's horrible.” And we ate three each, laughing, unable to stop. I've never put it on the menu. But once a year, I make one, in secret, for the two of us.
textes.J'ai inventé le crabe amoureux un matin,: I invented the lovestruck crab one morning, all alone on the beach. That evening, Yaya saw it. Two days later it was in her class, under the name “sentimental crab”. I'm demanding my name on her poster. She offered me a teeny little line at the bottom. I said: “Thank you, Miss.” She couldn't tell if that was mean. Neither could I.
textes.J'ai inventé le pogo. Si, si. En 1977, j: I invented the pogo. Yes, really. In 1977, I fell off the stage, bounced off the crowd, the crowd bounced off me, and everyone thought it was brilliant. Mamie Barricade says it was in 1978 and that I just tripped over a cable. She doesn't understand History.
textes.J'ai inventé le téléphérique, le monorai: I invented the cable car, the monorail and half the sweeper robots. The other half is Master Rivet's. We haven't spoken since the business of the singing sweeper.
textes.J'ai inventé un baume pour ses vieilles: I invented a balm for her old paws: arnica, hazelnut butter, and a bit too much pond mint. The first evening, it smelled so strong that up in the crow's nest of the Watchtower, Croc-Gris sneezed. Three times! Mother Moon said: “My guard has caught my aches.” I cut down the mint. A bit.
textes.J'ai inventé un nom pour la couleur du v: I've invented a name for the colour of the volcano: “bolognese.” What do you think?
textes.J'ai inventé un sirop rien que pour Lars: I invented a cordial just for Larsen: the “cordial of silence”, with camomile and lime blossom. He drank it in one go. For an hour, he whispered. Everyone came closer to listen to him. He loved it. The next day, he was shouting again. He asks me for the cordial every Sunday.
textes.J'ai inventé une machine qui ramasse les: I invented a machine that picks up bolts in Zigomar's workshop. It worked really well: it picked up all the bolts, then the broom, then one of Zigomar's shoes. He shouted “Eureka!” and ran after the machine to get his shoe back. He said I was a genius. And that it needed an off button.
textes.J'ai inventé une unité de mesure : le sp: I invented a unit of measurement: the spaghetti. One spaghetti is twenty-five centimetres. The temple is ninety spaghettis wide. The Great Spaghetti, however, can only be measured in itself, which poses a problem I haven't solved yet.
textes.J'ai joué dans toutes les tavernes de la: I played in every tavern on the coast, then in castles. One day, a king summoned me for his wedding. I played a lament so beautiful that he wept. Then someone whispered to him that it was his old sweetheart's song. He had me thrown out, fiddle and all. The fiddle survived. My career as a court musician, much less so.
textes.J'ai joué pour un roi, une fois. Il a pl: I played for a king once. He cried. Then he threw me out because at his wedding I'd played his ex-fiancée's song. Kings have no sense of humour.
textes.J'ai joué à la balle contre le dôme neuf: I was playing ball against Bulle's new dome. The ball was a chunk of meteorite. It made a big dent in the glass. I went to apologise, all small. Bulle looked at the dent for a really long time. Then she said: “It has character.” She kept it. She calls it “Quark's dent”. I'm famous.
textes.J'ai joué. J'ai JOUÉ ! (Il tapote ton ép: I played. I PLAYED! (He taps your shoulder in rhythm, not even noticing.) Rouille asked me if I wanted to come back tomorrow. And the day after. And every night. Clou nodded at me. Mouette did her seagull thing. Tapage cried, he said it was the dust. And Dad... Dad was at the back of the hall. He tapped his foot. The whole concert. He says it was a cramp. (He laughs.) I'm the drummer of the Bilge Rats. And the “Son” of Lisse & Son. Both. Thank you. Here: my first musician's coins. I don't have many yet. But these, I earned by playing.
I let Glorb feed the glug-glugs. They all snuggled up against him going “glug-glug”. I think they took him for a giant mummy glug-glug. Glorb didn't move for an hour, so as not to disappoint them. He was trembling with happiness. So were the glug-glugs. It was a very wobbly hour.
textes.J'ai laissé Margot et Léonce installer l: I let Margot and Léonce set up their robot in the cellar, between the soap barrels. It's called Bidule. It doesn't work, but it looked like its head was cold. So I made it a hat out of hardened bubble. Margot said it wasn't regulation. She's never taken it off.
textes.J'ai laissé Ortie allumer une petite fus: I let Ortie light a small rocket, just one, on the jetty. Her hand shook as she brought the match to the fuse. The rocket went up, made a little “pop”, and drew a very crooked star. Ortie looked at me with shining eyes. I said it was the most beautiful crooked star I'd ever seen. It was true.
textes.J'ai laissé ma place dans la passe à Dri: I gave my spot in the channel to Driss, my old cabin boy. Now I fish at the end of the jetty, and I catch nothing. In the evening I light the green lighthouse and salute the caid three times. In the afternoon, little Youssef comes to tell me about his whales, and a mute pirate sits beside me with his parrot. The three of us catch nothing. It's very restful.
textes.J'ai laissé tomber à l'eau le couteau de: I dropped my grandfather's knife in the water, the one with the whalebone handle. Ten fathoms deep. Lucie dived three times. The third time, she came up with the knife between her teeth, like a pirate. She said: “There was a crab on it. He didn't agree.”
textes.J'ai laissé un vieux métronome sur le ba: I left an old metronome on the bench where Gédéon sits in the evenings, at the entrance to the Hall. No note. The next day, it was keeping time. The metronome, not Gédéon. Gédéon kept better time.
textes.J'ai laissé une petite main bleue sur Ge: I left a little blue handprint on Gertrude one morning. Sort of on purpose: she looked sad. Tchoum scrubbed for an hour, sighing. The next day, the hand was still there. He'd stopped scrubbing. I think he also finds Gertrude happier that way.
textes.J'ai lancé un avion en papier du bord de: I threw a paper plane off the edge of the island. It's still flying. I think it's gone to Hautefond.
textes.J'ai le mal de mer rien qu'en le regarda: I get seasick just looking at it.
textes.J'ai le vertige. Si. Mais dans la cabine: I'm scared of heights. I am. But in Mademoiselle's cab, I never look down. I look at the horizon. Gravier taught me that. He said: “Look far away.” Three words. It changed my life.
textes.J'ai le vertige… mais seulement du côté: I've got vertigo… but only on the left side.
textes.J'ai les pieds en compote, mais le cœur: My feet are killing me, but my heart is light.
textes.J'ai lu sa tasse, une fois, très sérieus: I read her cup once, very seriously. I saw “a long life and lots of herbal tea”. She laughed so hard she spilled the cup on my embroidered tablecloth. I looked at the stain and said: “That confirms it.” She's been bringing me her verbena ever since. The stain is still there. I don't wash it. It's a prediction.
textes.J'ai lu un jour dans le carnet de Tréphi: One day I read the name of a whale disease in Tréphine's notebook, and I was sure I had it. Anouk made me drink warm water while holding my hand, very serious, and told me I was saved. Only just. I thanked her all week. I know now it was water. It worked anyway.
textes.J'ai lu une page. Ça va mieux. On contin: I read a page. I feel better. Let's go on.
My back hurts. Coal is heavy.
textes.J'ai mangé deux soupes, hier !: I had two bowls of soup yesterday!
textes.J'ai mangé le gâteau très proprement !: I ate the cake really neatly!
textes.J'ai mangé une histoire, ma petite. Très: I ate a story, my dear. Very nourishing.
textes.J'ai marchandé une heure pour ses plumes: I haggled for an hour over her macaw feathers, and I won. At the next fair, she saw the same feathers on my stall, three times dearer. She recognised her knots. I told her: “They've travelled, they're tired, that costs extra.” She laughed. Then she tripled her prices. I pay without arguing. She made me pay for my own arguments.
textes.J'ai marché jusqu'à Tazira, une fois, en: I walked all the way to Tazira once, following the coast. Three days. Over there they drum all night long, on a square full of sand. I taught their rhythms to Pépin.
textes.J'ai marché sur le Belvédère de verre !: I walked on the Glass Belvedere! I saw the sea under my feet! Then I saw my feet. They were shaking a little.
textes.J'ai mené mon enquête, figurez-vous. Je: I conducted my investigation, if you please. I went to Rose's and asked her who bought lavender from her before eight o'clock. She thought for a long time, arranging her buckets. Then she said: “Everyone, Madame Hortense.” Very well. So Marcel is part of everyone.
textes.J'ai mesuré la lueur des Pierres-Lunes t: I measured the glow of the Moonstones for a whole night, with my instruments. It rises by a tenth when Miss Lin comes to read them a story. Exactly a tenth! I went to announce it to Ysolde, very proud. She answered: “I know.” She always knows. It's rather vexing.
textes.J'ai mis des guirlandes tout le long du: I put fairy lights all along the arm of Boulon's crane. In the evening, when he swings it round, it's like a giant glowing needle sweeping over the harbour. Boulon told me Mademoiselle was creaking with pride. I listened. It's true. She creaks in a major key.
textes.J'ai mis des noisettes dans les caisses: I put hazelnuts in the fishery crates, to keep them cool, next to the sardines. And Caramel found them IN the sardines. Myrtille laughed so hard she fell off the bench! She said it was the best joke of the year. It wasn't a joke, it was a hiding place. But okay.
textes.J'ai mis la danse de Nono dans mon spect: I put Nono's dance in my show: “the elegant seal”. The kids love it, they clap like flippers. One day Nono came to watch, very dignified, in his beanie. He said I was forgetting the shoulder move. The next day he came back to show me. He stayed an hour. He got more applause than me.
textes.J'ai mis la main sur la grille de la Che: I put my hand on the grille of the Air Chimney: you can feel the wind from up top! It's cold, it smells of salt. I kept it in my pocket.
textes.J'ai mis ma plus belle passoire, aujourd: I put on my best colander today. The Sunday one.
textes.J'ai mis neuf ans à fabriquer l'Horloge: It took me nine years to make the Singing Clock. Nine years for it to sing the time, exactly, to the second. The first time it sang “it's twelve o'clock, tra-la-la”, I wept. Discreetly. Behind the counter. Nobody knew. Except the clock.
textes.J'ai mis un an à construire ce bras. Cha: It took me a year to build this arm. Every finger, every cable, every little motor. The first day it worked, I picked up an egg without breaking it. Mio was born the next week. I held her with both arms. The cold one and the warm one.
textes.J'ai mis un nœud papillon à mon majordom: I put a bow tie on my butler. Black silk, it gives him style. Master Rivet spotted it the very first lunchtime. He said: “Hm. A robot has no neck.” He took it off. The next day I put it back on. It's been going on for years. The butler says nothing. He's a diplomat.
textes.J'ai mis un peu de beurre de côté pour t: I've put a little butter aside for you. Shh.
