I put him back at the North Gate. The harbour folk say it's the best-guarded gate in Montjoie, because nobody dares wake the guard. I don't know if that's a compliment.
textes.Je l'ai composé moi-même ! Il s'appelle: I composed it myself! It's called “Symphony for a Sneezing Cat.” Want to hear it?
textes.Je l'ai connu haut comme trois noix de c: I knew him when he was knee-high to a coconut, and I'm the one who gave him his name. His music goes way too fast… and yet my heart keeps up. I don't know which of us is wrong.
textes.Je l'ai demandée en mariage comme on ven: I proposed to her the way you sell a carpet: “One husband, very handsome, very chatty, special fiancée price.” She said: “Too expensive.” I lowered it. “Still too expensive.” I lowered it. At the third price, she said yes. I ran through the whole souk shouting: “She haggled! She loves me!” Karim knocked over his slippers.
textes.Je l'ai emmené sur les falaises du nord: I took him to the northern cliffs to listen to the wind with me, for a whole hour. I sang along with it, so he'd hear the tune. Borée said: “You sing off-key. So does it.” That proves it sings, doesn't it? On the way down, he took my arm. He says I took his. He took mine.
textes.Je l'ai entendue ! Toute l'île l'a enten: I heard it! The whole island heard it! Even Borée looked up! Here, some coins for you. And come levitate with me at sunset: from up high, the sea turns all pink.
textes.Je l'ai entendue avant de la voir : un «: I heard her before I saw her: a “bzoing, bzoing” coming from the quay. A fourteen-year-old kid was playing a broomstick with three rubber bands. She was in time. Perfectly. I said to her: “You, you've got rhythm.” She answered “KIAAA”. I understood it meant yes.
textes.Je l'ai entendue quatre cents fois. Elle: I've heard it four hundred times. It's still beautiful.
I heard her. Through the Column.
textes.Je l'ai envoyé sur le toit du Fondouk ch: I sent him up on the Fondouk roof to look for the ginger cat. “Don't come back without him!” He came back an hour later with… a nightcap, taken off a washing line. “No cat, captain, but it was cold up there.” I took the nightcap back myself, to an old lady. She hit me with it.
textes.Je l'ai invitée à l'Assemblée, par une l: I invited her to the Assembly, with a letter Ysaé took up. She replied: “I vote for everything! It's more fun.” Her grandfather voted exactly the same way. For the same reasons.
textes.Je l'ai laissé peindre le ciel d'une pet: I let him paint the sky on a little canvas. Blue everywhere, really hard, tongue sticking out. Then, right in the middle, he painted a red, yellow, blue and green diamond, with a long knotted tail. His kite. I didn't say anything. I kept the canvas. It's above my bed, at the hotel.
textes.Je l'ai laissée inventer un parfum. Elle: I let her invent a flavour. She thought about it for a week, looking very scientific. Then she said: “Strawberry, and a pinch of sea salt. For the dolphin.” I pulled a face. I tasted it. My oh my… it was good! The strawberry-dolphin sells better than my coconut. Don't tell Kiki.
At least I washed it. The sock.
I ate it. Half of it.
I wrote it down, Philomène. Floor zero.
textes.Je l'ai presque ! Presque presque !: I've almost got it! Almost almost!
textes.Je l'ai senti. Toute l'île l'a senti. (L: I felt it. The whole island felt it. (The bridges of light shine, the fountain finally chooses its planet, and way up there, the Spire beats like a happy drum.) For a thousand years the Heart has carried us, and it was a Heavyfoot who healed it. The elders of Ondelune wouldn't believe it. I do. (She stands up, very straight, and places both hands on your shoulders.) In the name of the Council, of Tempo who cried at exactly the right hour, of Écliptique who is preparing a two-hour speech, and of Volt who says it's nothing: you are now the Friend of the Lumens. The first one. Hee hee. Here, some washers, since you all like those, and three cosmic jellies from Gloubi. He cried into them. They're a little salty.
textes.Je l'ai soudée avec soin, Mère Morille !: I welded it with care, Mother Morille!
textes.Je l'ai suivi au Bois des Lutins, une fo: I followed him to the Goblin Wood, once. A goblin saw me. Sir Tancrède arrived shouting “I, SIR TANCRÈDE DE TOURNEVENT!”, and he did a secret attack: he fell on the goblin with all his weight. The goblin ran all the way back to its camp. Sir Tancrède says it's the falling technique. I practise on the haystack in the stable.
textes.Je l'ai tenu contre moi pendant toute la: I held it close the whole crossing.
textes.Je l'ai trouvé sur un radeau, au large,: I found him on a raft, far out at sea, years ago. He had nothing. Not a word, not a name. Just a drawing folded in his pocket: a white house, a laughing woman. I had him brought aboard. He took a rope and did the work of three. He's never asked me for anything. I've never asked him anything either.
textes.Je l'ai vu ! La couleur est sortie de la: I saw it! The colour came out of the Palette like a drop of ink on blotting paper, and the clearing got back its brown, its grass, its old tree trunks. (She wipes her eyes: they run a little.) Now, the Brush: dip it in the Palette, and it will drink the colour. Then hold it in your hand, and paint what you like, where you like. For the other eight pots, ask the families: Basile is looking for the blue at the Rubbed-Out Pond, Rosalie the green in the Hatching Wood, Capucine the red in the White Meadows, Lili the yellow on the Strand, Gaspard is watching for the purple from the top of the Lookout, and Achille dreams of the orange at the foot of the waterfall. The last two… you'll have to hunt for them. Augustin surely has an idea: he always does.
I saw it too. Keep watching.
textes.Je l'ai vu, patron. Je ne suis pas aveug: I saw him, boss. I'm not blind.
textes.Je l'ai vue lancer ses couteaux au cirqu: I saw her throwing knives at the Tortuga circus, the night her partner demanded a raise in the middle of the show. After the show, I went to see her: “On my brig, nobody asks for a raise.” She laughed. She signed. She's never asked for one. She keeps the cash box. I don't dare check.
textes.Je l'ai écrit quelque part… sur un coqui: I wrote it down somewhere… on a shell, I think.
textes.Je l'ai élevée au milieu des plus beaux: I raised her among the finest swaps in Ramure, and she sells for coins! Where did I go wrong, my friend? And her apples are delicious. That's the worst part.
textes.Je l'avais ramassée en passant, sa noise: I'd picked up her hazelnut in passing, because it was shining a bit. I dropped it on the steps of the throne. The next day, a little fairy was climbing out of it demanding seeds. Ever since, every week, she asks me which island. I really do think hard, you know. I see trees. Lots of trees.
textes.Je l'encourage, Léon. Ce n'est pas parei: I'm encouraging her, Léon. It's not the same.
I can hear it, girl. I can hear it.
I open it to look inside.
textes.Je la croyais endormie au fond de la bar: I thought she was asleep at the bottom of the boat. I was explaining to a heron, very quietly, that the flood comes from the rain in the mountains. And her voice, behind me, eyes closed: “And the rain, Khéty, who sends it?” I dropped the oar, the oar fell in, I dived in to catch it. She didn't even open her eyes.
textes.Je la garde depuis trois mois !: I've been holding it for three months!
textes.Je la regarde avec les doigts, Ptahmosé: I'm looking at it with my fingers, Ptahmose!
textes.Je la regarde, ma grande ! Elle a l'air: I'm only looking at it, dear! It looks sad.
I'd give it back to its fairy.
textes.Je la vois ! Elle est toujours là ! Elle: I see it! It's still there! It moves all the time! Doesn't it ever get tired? … Thank you, friend. Thank you.
textes.Je laisse des poèmes dans ses boîtes à l: I leave poems in her lantern boxes. One evening, coming out of her workshop, I ran right into her. I pretended to check a street lamp. There was no street lamp in front of her workshop. She didn't say anything. The next day, there was one. She'd had it put in. It's called Poem.
I'd just tell them, simple as that.
I'll keep it. Your mother sends her love.
textes.Je le mets dans mon cours. Le chat va ad: I'm putting it in my class. The cat will love it.
I'll put it on your tab, then.
I'm writing it down in my head.
textes.Je le note dans mon cahier !: I'm writing it in my notebook!
I'll make a note of it.
textes.Je le pose au rayon « trésors ». Tout es: I'll put it in the “treasures” section. Everything's in the “treasures” section. It's the only section.
I'll put it here. Away from the carpet.
textes.Je le regarde ! Avec mes yeux ! C'est tr: I'm watching it! With my eyes! It's very… bright, without a camera.
I look at it, without touching.
textes.Je le rends demain, promis !: I'll bring it back tomorrow, promise!
textes.Je le savais ! C'est comme ça qu'on trou: I knew it! That's how you find what's on no map. And then people tell me about it, and I draw it. You're my best informant.
textes.Je le savais ! C'était écrit dans les pl: I knew it! It was written in the feathers! Nostradamus pecked three times to the left when you arrived. That's a very good sign. Or a crumb.
textes.Je le savais ! Les pigeons m'ont annoncé: I knew it! The pigeons told me this morning that a visitor would come. Or that it would rain. Or both. I'm Patchouli, neighbour from the Boxes, and I read the future in pigeons. Not in their insides, don't worry: in the way they peck.
I knew it! Nobody will believe us.
I knew it! You've got good taste, you.
textes.Je le savais ! Tu as une tête à bêtises: I knew it! You've got a mischief face! Tell me! No, wait, Aëlwen's listening. Later. But I knew it!
I knew it! You have good taste.
textes.Je le savais ! Vous avez une tête de bul: I knew it! You've got a bubble face. That's a compliment. Look at that one, it looks like you: round, light, a bit lopsided.
I knew it! Xan knows his. When I say “Xan”, he buzzes. OK, he buzzes all the time. But louder!
textes.Je le savais ! … Attends. Tu te moques d: I knew it! … Wait. Are you making fun of me?
textes.Je le savais. Ce matin, Rê s'est levé ro: I knew it. This morning, Ra rose red and gold, like a young man. (She lays her hand on your forehead.) May his light follow you wherever you go. Here: bread from Mérit, and enough to fill your purse. And the Eye of Horus, keep it well: in the highlands, in the middle of the island, a niche awaits it.
textes.Je le savais. Je demandais pour la forme: I knew it. I was only asking for form's sake.
I knew it. I missed you, big girl.
I can feel it in my whiskers.
textes.Je le sens jusqu'au bout de mes cornes :: I feel it down to the tips of my horns: it's warm! (The Archduchess laughs, and the whole throne room laughs with her.) Pandémonia owes you her fire, little flame. From today, you're at home here. Here: buns from the Eternal Oven, and enough to fill your purse. And this title, which will be engraved on the great door.
I suspect he laughs under his chèche. While I haggle, the cloth moves a little, right there, around the mouth. Once, I pretended to faint halfway through the price, just to see. The chèche moved a lot. He still said “No”. But he was laughing, I swear it on my carpets.
I turn it into something else.
textes.Je les ai ! Regardez : caoutchouc, jusqu: I've got them! Look: rubber, up to the knees!
textes.Je les ai ! Une question, une seule !: I've got them on! One question, just one!
textes.Je les ai bien emmêlés, hein ?: I tangled them up nicely, didn't I?
textes.Je les ai vus ! (Elle a des étoiles dans: I saw them! (She has stars in her eyes. And a bit of green paint.) They're... alive! You've got the touch! The supple wrist, the bold pschhht! The wall says thank you. So do I. Here, a little reward, and know this: on the water tower, there's a spot for your name. I'll write it tonight. In green. Don't argue.
I cut it with a knife.
I twirl it around my fork.
textes.Je les fais. Mais sans bateau brodé, cet: I'll make them. But no embroidered boat this time.
I keep every one of them.
textes.Je les laisse là. Au cas où il serait pr: I'll leave them here. In case it's clean and loud.
I'm painting them, caïd. With my eyes.
textes.Je les pose à leur place, Tapage. À dema: I'll put them in their usual spot, Tapage. See you tomorrow.
textes.Je les prends toutes, Marée. Ondine gran: I'll take them all, Marée. Ondine's still growing.
I've got them, Yaya! I've got them… Oops. Sorry, Momo!
textes.Je les trouve… encombrants, mademoiselle: I find them… cumbersome, young lady.
I see them. I won't tell you where.
I'll check them myself. Every one.
textes.Je leur ai tout raconté. Entre nous…: I told them everything. Between you and me…
textes.Je leur dirai. Elles ne m'écoutent pas t: I'll tell them. They don't always listen to me.
textes.Je lis des histoires aux pierres, à voix: I read stories to the stones, in a low voice, sitting against Nacre. Once, I skipped a page without meaning to. From the other side of the Circle, Ysolde said: “You skipped a page.” She didn't have the book. I went back. The stones prefer stories in order.
textes.Je lis en buvant sa bière, et il m'arriv: I read while drinking her beer, and sometimes I spill a little. My scroll of the Hymn to Hapy smells of barley now. The pupils sniff it before reading it. Mérit says it's the only papyrus on the river that makes you thirsty. I think she's proud of it.
I'll read a little longer. Just one chapter. Or two.
textes.Je lis un peu. Les livres, ça fait voyag: I'm reading a bit. Books let you travel without moving.
I'm reading. Well, I was reading.
textes.Je lui achète mes sardines chaque samedi: I buy my sardines from her every Saturday. She always picks the finest, the shiniest, and puts it aside for me, laughing. I suspect her of trying to bribe an officer. I've noted it in my notebook. But they really are very fine sardines.
textes.Je lui achète trois paniers de dattes pa: I buy three baskets of dates from her a year. For my flatbreads. Egyptian dates are the best, I have to say. We swapped recipes: I gave her my cacao without the chilli, she gave me her beer without the dates. We both lied. I know it. She knows it. We respect each other.
textes.Je lui achète un pot de miel chaque sema: I buy a pot of honey from him every week, for my flatbreads. He looks at me with a funny little smile, as if he knew something. He doesn't know anything. He can't know anything. I put a pot of honey a week in my flatbreads. They're very… very sweet. There.
textes.Je lui ai accroché un casque à la porte: I hung a helmet on her Workshop door. She turned it into a pencil pot. I wanted to get cross. I saw the pencils, all neatly lined up, all well protected. I laughed. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Je lui ai acheté la potion qui change la: I bought the potion that turns your voice into a duck's. I talked to the wind like a duck for an hour, on the cliffs. It laughed, yes, it did: it made a little whirlwind. Mirabelle says it's the first time one of her potions has made the wind laugh. She wrote it in her notebook.
textes.Je lui ai acheté trois flacons et je l'a: I bought three bottles from her and paid with a riddle. A very good one, worth double. She's been looking for the answer for ten years. The day she finds it, she'll realise she's the one who owes me change. I'm in no hurry.
textes.Je lui ai acheté un bouclier pour la Gar: I bought a shield from him for the Guard. It was so heavy it took two guards to carry it. Together. When I went to complain, Kraxx told me: “Nothing gets through it.” It's true. Nothing gets through. Not even the guards carrying it.
I brought her a tale from Cliquetis.
textes.Je lui ai appris la cochenille. Son lin: I taught her about cochineal. Her linen stayed white, her hands turned red. She looked at them, amazed, as if she were seeing her hands for the first time. I gave her a red and yellow belt. She said: “I'll never wear it.” She held it close all afternoon.
textes.Je lui ai appris la vieille coutume : un: I taught her the old custom: a coin under the foot of the mainmast, for the ship's luck. Barbe-Sanglante put a gold coin under each of his masts. Gwen put a silver coin: it was all she had. I looked, and I said: “She'll float again.” She smiled. I mean it. Boats can tell when you believe in them.
textes.Je lui ai appris la vieille façon de pêc: I taught him the old way to fish for light: you stretch the crystal net above the fountain, you wait for the first ray to get caught in it, and above all, you don't talk. It took him a hundred years to manage it. He says it's because I was talking the whole time, right beside him.
textes.Je lui ai appris le nœud de chaise à la: I taught him the bowline the Barbe-Sanglante way: the rabbit comes out of the hole, goes round the tree and goes back down the hole. He practises every evening, eyes closed. His rabbit always gets a bit lost round the tree. Mine got lost too, at his age. The captain used to say the best rabbits get a bit lost.
textes.Je lui ai appris le nœud de huit. Le soi: I taught her the figure-of-eight knot. That same evening, she'd taught it to her mother, to Lucas, to Raymond and to the little white dog, who does it very badly. Since then, there are figure-of-eight knots all over the quay: on the benches, on the bins, on Fernand's walking stick.
textes.Je lui ai appris trois noms : Doyenne, N: I've taught her three names: Doyenne, Nacre, Petite-Ourse. One per full moon, no more. I asked her not to write them down. She writes them in lemon ink, which can only be read over a flame. I said nothing. Neither did the stones. She's a child who finds solutions. I like that.
textes.Je lui ai appris à faire de l'ocre avec: I taught her to make ochre from the wadi clay: you dry it, crush it, sift it. She wanted to do it all with her bare hands. Her hands were red for a whole week; at the Fondouk, my aunt thought she'd been in a fight. With that ochre, Selma painted birds on my jugs. The whole series sold in a day.
textes.Je lui ai appris à faire un poing. Le po: I taught him how to make a fist. Thumb outside, not inside, or it hurts. The captain said the cabin boy doesn't fight. So he keeps it in his pocket, his fist. Sometimes he takes it out to show me. It's a good one. I'm proud.
textes.Je lui ai appris à lancer une ligne. Au: I taught her to cast a line. With her first fish, she shouted for joy. Then she looked at it, and put it back in the water: “Maybe it has children.” She put the next six back too. In the evening, we came home with an empty basket and the faces of champions. Tiyi made lentils.
textes.Je lui ai avoué un soir que tous mes exp: One evening I confessed to him that all my exploits were made up. He nodded and said: “Mine too, a bit. The dragon was small.” Then he added: “But I was scared, and I went anyway. That part was true.” Since then, I try to be scared and go anyway. It works one time in three. Like my cape.
textes.Je lui ai commandé des pots pour mes fle: I ordered pots for my flowers from him. He put Tlaloc's round eyes on them, out of habit. My cempasúchil look surprised in them. Pilli says they watch people go by. Coyotl says Tlaloc watches over my flowers. It does rain a lot on my pots, that's true.
textes.Je lui ai commandé la carte officielle d: I commissioned the official map of the city from him. I wanted something dignified: an avenue, a square, an opera house. He drew it all, with columns and fountains. It's magnificent. Visitors get a little lost looking for the opera house, but they see the city as it will be. That's what a map is for. I believe.
textes.Je lui ai commandé un chapeau en forme d: I ordered a turnip-shaped hat from her for the Great Alert. She refused. I insisted. She made it. On alert day, I wore it to the Southern Fields. The turnips took me for their leader and followed me in single file all the way to the farm. Père Gaubert wept for joy. Colombe says it's her masterpiece. She never wants to talk about it again.
textes.Je lui ai commandé un crocodile en argil: I ordered a clay crocodile from him, to scare off the real ones. He made it very well. Too well. The next day, Sobek was sleeping next to it, with his head on it. Ptahmosé told the whole brewery that my crocodile had found love. It's not funny. Fine. It's a bit funny. But not for me.
textes.Je lui ai commandé un tablier brodé de d: I ordered an apron embroidered with sea bream from her. Calm ones, I said. She embroidered six sleeping sea bream, eyes half-closed. I wore it to the fish market and planted myself under Saïd's platform: “Look, Saïd! Here's a happy sea bream!” He shouted louder. But he looked at the apron. For a long time.
textes.Je lui ai commandé une ballade tragique: I commissioned a tragic ballad from him: “Rodrigue, the Twilight Blade”. He sang it that very evening. In the first verse, I was magnificent. In the second, I was slipping off the cliff. In the third, I was sleeping on a ledge. By the chorus, the whole hall was singing “Rodrigue and his cape”. I went up on stage to protest. I fell off the stage. They thought it was the finale.
textes.Je lui ai commandé une cape « qui claque: I ordered a cape “that billows in the wind even without wind”. She sewed wire into the hem. The cape flaps. Always. When I walk, when I sit, when I eat. At night, it flaps against the back of my chair. My neighbours complain. I tell them it's the sound of destiny.
textes.Je lui ai commandé une jarre pour garder: I ordered a jar from him to keep fish alive. It holds water so well that a perch has been living in it for weeks. I don't have the heart to eat her. I named her Ptah. Ptahmosé pretended to be offended. But one evening I saw him lean over the jar and say hello to the perch.
textes.Je lui ai confié ma carte de Port-Azur,: I entrusted her with my map of Port-Azur, the one the mayor gives to visitors, to colour it in. She gave it back with the sea in six blues. Six! The port, the bay, the open sea, the lighthouse's shadow… I held the map up to the sun and said: “It's the first map that looks wet.” She blushed right up to her beret.
textes.Je lui ai confié ma graine de cactus des: I trusted her with my dwarf cactus seed. Perlée gives it one drop a month. Not one more, even when I beg. In spring, it grew a yellow flower! I cried for joy. Perlée gave me a funny look. As if she wanted to cry too, but didn't know how.
textes.Je lui ai conseillé de chanter aux abeil: I advised him to sing to the bees before taking the honey. He sang. Once. They stung him twice as much. I explained that it wasn't the song, it was the tuning. He didn't speak to me for a month. My girls buzzed with laughter all week.
textes.Je lui ai cousu dans l'ourlet un fil dor: I sewed a golden thread into her hem, the only one I have, kept from my own mother. I told her it was a ray of sunshine. She checks every evening that it's still there. So do I, when she's asleep.
textes.Je lui ai cousu un chapeau de capitaine: I sewed her a captain's hat from an old apron, with a sea bream embroidered on the front. She looked at the sea bream for a long time. Then she said: “That one looks calm.” Since then, she wears it every day. Even to sleep, when she thinks I'm not looking.
textes.Je lui ai cousu une cape rouge à paillet: I sewed him a red cape with ember sequins for the Arena. The first time, the crowd shouted so loud that he froze, and the sequins went out. Madame Hurla shouted “MOVE!”. He moved, and the cape shone like a bonfire. Since then, before every fight, I murmur to him: “Move gently, but move.”
textes.Je lui ai demandé ce qu'ils mangent en m: I asked him what they eat at sea, on the Murène. He brought me one of their biscuits. Hard as wood. I tried to bite it, nearly lost a tooth. Now I use it as a sinker for my line. It sinks very well. Better than lead.
textes.Je lui ai demandé cent fois de me rappor: I've asked her a hundred times to bring me back the caravan folk's cream recipe from the south. Every time, she tells me she's almost got it. Two years ago she brought me a little “authentic” pot, with a ribbon. It was goat fat. Again.
textes.Je lui ai demandé combien de trous il fa: I asked him how many holes you'd have to plug for the Léviathan to float. He opened an old black journal full of numbers and said: “Four thousand three hundred and twelve. Plus tomorrow's.” I said: “Oh well, that's not so many.” He sighed so hard the lantern swung.
textes.Je lui ai demandé combien il y a d'étoil: I asked him how many stars there are. He told me: “Count them.” So I counted all night long, on the roof. One thousand and eleven! And Xan flew in front of the moon, so that made one thousand and eleven plus Xan. He wrote it all in his tables. I'm in Ah Kin Pech's tables! Well, Xan is.
textes.Je lui ai demandé d'arrêter. Il a promis: I asked him to stop. He promised. The next day, the octopus had fifty arms, and I beat it with one hand, holding my cup of hot seaweed tea in the other. “See, I've made you more modest,” he told me. I don't see.
textes.Je lui ai demandé de couper la corde d'u: I asked her to cut the rope of a sack stuck in my storeroom. One arrow, first shot, from twenty paces. The sack fell on Clovis. He didn't even move. He said: “Ah. Flour.” Lison did something I'd never seen her do: she burst out laughing. A real laugh, a loud one. Clovis blushed under the flour.
textes.Je lui ai demandé de m'écrire depuis l'A: I asked him to write to me from Atlantis once he's found it. A card, with a stamp from there. He promised, hand on heart. He always opens the caramel before the letter, and he often doesn't finish the letter. But my card, I'm sure he'll finish it. I'm waiting for it. I think I'm waiting for it more than he is.
textes.Je lui ai demandé de me faire léviter, p: I asked her to make me levitate, to see the stars up close. Three metres above the roof, I discovered I was afraid of heights. I clung to her arm shouting that the stars were very nice from far away. She brought me back down without laughing. She laughed afterwards. For a long time.
textes.Je lui ai demandé de quelle couleur étai: I asked her what colour the sun was. She said yellow. I asked yellow like what, because there's nothing yellow here. So she took off her crown and put it on my head! I ran all the way to the canal to look at myself in the water. I had a sun on my head. She took it back afterwards. Shame.
textes.Je lui ai demandé où étaient les grottes: I asked her where my grandfather's caves were. She said: “Under the feet of the one who guards.” The one who guards: the Skala! I went there at night, with a lantern, on my knees in the pebbles. And I came face to face with the caïd Hamza, sabre drawn. I said I was admiring the cannons. Fatima laughed about it for three days.
textes.Je lui ai demandé pourquoi elle restait: I asked her why she always stayed until the end. She said: “To find out how it ends.” I told her I knew the ending. She said: “I don't.” I realised she was really listening. Every time. I wrote another song after that. I'll never sing it.
textes.Je lui ai demandé pourquoi les scarabées: I asked him why scarabs push balls of poo. He told me it's like Khepri, who pushes the sun in the morning. So the sun is a ball of poo? I asked Néferet. She laughed really loudly. Ptahmosé went all red. I still don't know the answer.
textes.Je lui ai demandé pourquoi sa louche s'a: I asked her why her ladle is called Gertrude. She said it was her grandmother's name, who used to bang on the table to make her ten children be quiet. So now Mamie Rissole bangs on the table with Gertrude to make Master Hugues be quiet. It doesn't work. He cries.
textes.Je lui ai demandé un jour comment c'étai: One day, I asked him what it was like, right at the bottom, on the Jelly King's floor. He's never been: he stopped at the fourth, because of Hugues and a mimic. He said: “I don't know.” For the first time in forty years, Odon admitted not knowing something. I didn't contradict him. I told him the legend. He listened to the very end.
textes.Je lui ai demandé un jour, très poliment: One day I asked her, very politely, if she could “lose a little” of the university's letters. Just a little. A week or two. She refused, looking at me the way you look at a child who won't go to the dentist. The next day, with the envelope, there was a caramel. Since then, there's always one. I open the caramel first.
textes.Je lui ai demandé une louche solide. Il: I asked him for a sturdy ladle. He forged me an iron one, with a handle as long as an arm and a bowl that holds a whole soup. I can only lift it with both hands. He said: “That way, it won't break.” It doesn't break. My arms ache, but it doesn't break.
textes.Je lui ai demandé une robe avec des poch: I asked her for a dress with pockets, to keep roasted chestnuts in during audiences. She let out a shriek, as if I'd asked for a dress made of straw. Three days later, she delivered a magnificent dress, with pockets hidden in the folds. She made me swear not to tell anyone.
textes.Je lui ai demandé. Il porte tes sandales: I did. He's wearing your sandals.
textes.Je lui ai dit qu'il y avait cent squelet: I told him there were a hundred skeletons at the Cursed Fort. He went to count, with his spyglass. He came back very proud: “Ninety-seven!” I replied: “The other three are out.” He thought about it. Then he drew them in dotted lines on his map. That day, I knew we'd be friends forever.
textes.Je lui ai dit, devant tout le monde, que: I told him, in front of everyone, that his horns shone brighter than his conversation. The whole square laughed. Tiburce smiled, bowed very low, and answered: “Then I shall keep quiet, and let you play.” He stayed until the very last note, without a word. It may be the most beautiful answer anyone's ever given me.
textes.Je lui ai dit, un jour : « Un arbre qu'o: One day I told him: “A tree you don't dare plant will never bear fruit.” He blushed to the tips of his ears. The following Tuesday, he delivered two sacks of flour.
textes.Je lui ai dit, un jour, ce que disent le: One day I told her what the old ones say: that Yggdrasil grows on the other side too, beneath the clouds. She replied: “Perhaps all the way down to your sister.” Since then, every morning, I set one extra drop at the foot of the Tree. In case its roots reach all the way down.
textes.Je lui ai donné des graines de maïs à pl: I gave him maize seeds to plant. He planted them all upside down, tip in the air, “so they can see the sun”. They grew anyway. A bit crooked. Like his father's first maize. I didn't tell him why my eyes were wet. I just watched the maize dance.
textes.Je lui ai donné ma première balle, celle: I gave him my first ball, the one my father made me, the size of a mango. He sleeps with it. He has bruises everywhere. He's happy. His mother came to complain to me. I explained that it's the path of champions. She didn't look convinced.
textes.Je lui ai donné mon coquillage. Le soir,: I gave her my shell. In the evening, I walk past her door and hear her whisper: “Goodnight, sea.” It brings tears to my eyes. I say it's the wind.
textes.Je lui ai donné sa première vraie leçon: I gave him his first real lesson: stepping back. “Further. More. A bit more.” He backed up all the way to the Crankshaft. Perfect! Then I let him pull the lever on a tiny little explosion. A teeny pop. He still talks about it as the greatest day of his life. So do I, a bit.
textes.Je lui ai donné un badge de la Guilde de: I gave her a Little Heroes' Guild badge. Head Cook. She pinned it on her apron, in front of everyone. Even Master Hugues looked at it. He asked if he could have one. I said he'd have to pass an exam. He said okay. I haven't invented the exam yet.
textes.Je lui ai donné un boulon du Pont des Fr: I gave her a bolt from the Frondeurs' Bridge. She put it in a box all by itself. She says it's “the bravest bolt in the world”, because it holds on above the Chasm. She says good night to it, apparently.
textes.Je lui ai donné un champignon qui brille: I gave her a glowing mushroom, so she wouldn't need a candle when she marks papers. She said it wasn't allowed. But she kept it! It's on her desk, I saw it through the window. It's called Henri.
textes.Je lui ai donné une bague taillée dans u: I gave her a ring carved from a piece of oak from my grandfather's old boatyard. I didn't say anything. I'd prepared a speech, but it stayed in my pocket. She whistled three notes: “dinner's ready”. I understood yes. She says she only meant “dinner's ready”. I don't believe her.
textes.Je lui ai envoyé un réveil de ma fabrica: I sent him an alarm clock I'd made with three cogs out of tolerance. He sent it back to me, repaired, with a note: “It's right.” I framed it. It hangs above my workbench. It's right.
textes.Je lui ai fabriqué un cerf-volant avec u: I made him a kite out of an old dormitory sheet. I told him: “That way, the sheet flies, and you hold the string.” He flies it every evening in the square, higher than the roof, higher than Gérard. Pip watches it with eyes as big as saucers. As long as he's holding the string, I can breathe.
textes.Je lui ai fabriqué une lanterne spéciale: I made him a special lantern, cut out with dragons, princesses and volcanoes, that casts shadows on the walls when he tells his stories. The first night, I used the wrong cut-out, and a dragon appeared in the middle of a love story. Grandpa improvised. It became his most famous story.
textes.Je lui ai fabriqué une étagère pour ses: I made her a shelf for her shells, with planks from the Merciless too damaged for the hull. Two hundred and twelve slots. Plus one, empty, at the top in the middle, for the one she hasn't found yet. She didn't say anything. She just took a nail and drove it in straight. First try. The only time.
textes.Je lui ai fait ma tisane « pour chagrin: I made her my “broken heart” tea: lime blossom, lemon balm, and a hint of Rose's lavender. She drank, thought about it, and said: “It doesn't cure anything, but it smells nice.” Best compliment I've ever had on a herbal tea. The next day she asked for two more.
textes.Je lui ai fait un collier avec un boulon: I made her a necklace with a bolt and a blue crystal. A bit from up here, a bit from down there. She never takes it off. Not even in the bath. Her mother told me, laughing.
textes.Je lui ai fait une cruche incassable. Ex: I made her an unbreakable jug. On purpose. Three fingers thick, a handle like an arm. It's so heavy it takes two pirates to fill it, and nobody can drink from it. Mama Lou uses it to prop open the tavern door. It's never broken. It's my best jug. I'm proud.
textes.Je lui ai fait une flûte en terre, en fo: I made her a clay flute, shaped like a bird. The first time she blew into it, a real hummingbird came and perched on the edge of the roof, to listen. She cried. So did I. It's the smallest thing I've ever made. The only one that ever drew a bird of the gods.
textes.Je lui ai fait une petite corde pour son: I made her a little cord for her loom. She looked at it like it was a jewel. Hm. I didn't know what to do with my hands.
textes.Je lui ai fait une potion de légèreté. E: I made her a lightness potion. She drank it in front of her whole class. She didn't float at all, but her hair stood straight up, like a big white feather, all day long! She taught like that. She said the apprentices had never paid so much attention. I wrote it in my notebook: success.
textes.Je lui ai forgé des protège-cornes pour: I forged him horn guards for the Arena, in steel lined with leather. He came to collect them with a bouquet of ember flowers, and a poem. The poem rhymed “Ferronde” with “Ferronde”. I nailed it above the anvil. The apprentices make fun of it. Me, I reread it often.
textes.Je lui ai interdit de grimper au premier: I forbade her to climb up to the first platform without the stairs. She obeyed. She takes the stairs, at full speed, four steps a bound, shouting “I'm obeying!”. The whole fishery shakes. I can't say a thing: it's exactly what I asked for. Mrrr. She'll go far, that one. Running.
textes.Je lui ai laissé tenir le pot de goudron: I let him hold the tar pot once, the way my father let me. He got it up to his elbows, but he didn't let go of the pot. I said “not bad”. He ran off to tell all of Carène. Since then, everyone looks at me as if I'd made a speech.
textes.Je lui ai laissé un pot d'onguent pour l: I left her a pot of ointment for the injured owl in the Twisted Wood, in case it lets her come near. Agathe put it on her table, next to the crystal ball. She told me the ball and the ointment were waiting for the same thing. I don't know what that meant. Neither does she, I think.
textes.Je lui ai laissé un sachet de graines de: I left a packet of camomile seeds on her door. The next day, there was a pot of moss on mine. We've never spoken. We trade all the same.
textes.Je lui ai laissé une pierre rouge sur so: I left a red stone on his anvil. A beautiful one, picked up at the edge of the crater. He took it for ore and put it in the fire. It shattered. I walked off without a word. That evening, I heard him asking everyone what he'd done. Nobody told him. I won't tell him either.
textes.Je lui ai mis des piquants, à ton oursin: I put spines on your sea urchin. It looks happier. So do I, funnily enough.
textes.Je lui ai montré l'arête dans le creux d: I showed him the bone in the palm of my hand, lowering my voice: “Sea dragon's tooth, milord. Torn out at the risk of my life.” He went pale and took out his purse: “I'll pay you double. For the danger.” Double! For a fishbone! I accepted. Then I bought a round of lemonades at the Perroquet, to be forgiven. By whom, I don't know.
textes.Je lui ai montré l'œil de la Zahra, celu: I showed him the Zahra's eye, the one that watches over. The next day, he'd drawn one on his hammock, in charcoal. He says that way, if he falls asleep, the hammock will bring him back to port. I didn't have the heart to tell him hammocks don't float.
textes.Je lui ai montré ma carte des Anciens. E: I showed her my map of the Ancients. She put her finger on the stain I'd taken for coffee and said: “That's my home.” Since then, I've gone over the stain in gold leaf. Well, in mango juice. It's what I had.
textes.Je lui ai montré mon premier poème. Il p: I showed him my first poem. It was about a pup and rhymed “pup” with “pup”. Nox read it three times, in silence. Then he said to me: “That's a rich rhyme.” I was so proud! Ombreline explained to me later what a rich rhyme was. It wasn't that. But I'm keeping the compliment.
textes.Je lui ai offert un bloc de colophane po: I gave her a block of rosin for her bow, carved into the shape of a horn and polished with ember oil. Perhaps I put in a little too much perfume: her violin smelled of roses for a month. She only said thank you after three days. Three days! I counted them, hour by hour. Then she said thank you. It was worth the three days.
textes.Je lui ai offert un nuage en bocal pour: I gave him a cloud in a jar to console him. He named it Zéphyr. Apparently it makes a little shower whenever I walk past the Institute. Surely a coincidence. I walk past the Institute less often now. Out of tact.
textes.Je lui ai offert un poème de quatre vers: I gave him a poem of exactly four lines. He timed it. Right on time. He nodded. I think that was peace.
textes.Je lui ai parlé du cœur qui bat, au fond: I told him about the heart that beats, at the end of a tunnel. Boom… boom… He didn't laugh. He asked me to draw the way there. I drew it. He looked at it for a long time, then he said: “Forget this path, Grimli. For once, forget it on purpose.” I'm doing my best.
textes.Je lui ai peint des étoiles sur ses abat: I painted stars on her lampshades. She said it was “too colourful for the Strata.” The next day, every lampshade had sold. She ordered twenty more from me.
textes.Je lui ai peint un panneau : « Interdit: I painted him a sign: “No puns allowed”. Underneath, he wrote: “What a pun-ishment.” I sighed so hard his papers blew away. The next day, I added a little flower next to his sentence. He hasn't noticed it yet.
textes.Je lui ai peint une enseigne pour son ét: I painted her a sign for her stall: “Hot bread”. My eyes… well, my hand slipped, and I put the sign for cat instead of the one for hot. For a week, Mérit sold “cat bread”. The children queued up to see if it meowed. She never sold so much. She bought me a beer, and gave me a new sign to paint.
textes.Je lui ai percé une lanterne spéciale :: I pierced him a special lantern: when you light it, a sultan and a sardine chase each other all round the circle. Three weeks of work. On the first evening, Ba Sidi forgot to tell his tale. He was watching the sardine run. He said it was the first time a story had told itself without him.
textes.Je lui ai posé une énigme sur lui-même :: I set him a riddle about himself: “I grumble in the morning, I grumble at night, and I guard what no one keeps in sight.” He thought for a long time, very seriously, and said: “A bear.” I laughed for three days. He didn't speak to me for the rest of the season. No great loss, he hardly talks.
textes.Je lui ai promis de lui montrer Bertha d: I promised to show her Bertha up close. Not from the quay: on deck, hand on the bronze. But first, the clove hitch. She practises on everything: ribbons, washing lines, Amine's hair. Last week, she almost got it. I've started shining Bertha for the visit.
textes.Je lui ai promis un vol en planeur à deu: I promised him a flight in a two-seater glider when he's ready. He said: “In ten years.” Then: “In five years.” Then: “In a year, maybe.” We're making progress. I'll wait for him.
textes.Je lui ai promis une vraie sortie en mer: I promised her a real trip out to sea the day she eats a raw sardine without pulling a face. She tries every Friday. She pulls a face before she even sees it. I think she pulls a face as soon as she wakes up, just in case.
textes.Je lui ai proposé cent fois une partie c: A hundred times I've suggested he play against the automaton. He always refuses: “It has no watch, Ambroise. I don't play against someone who has no watch.” One evening, I tried to stop the clock to think. He looked at me as if I'd insulted his mother. I never did it again.
textes.Je lui ai proposé d'échanger nos recette: I offered to swap recipes: my salted grog for his tea. A fair deal, between artists. He put down his teapot, looked at me for a long time, and said: “Go away, pirate, before I pour the tea on your head from a great height.” I think that was a no. But the corner of his moustache was smiling.
textes.Je lui ai proposé de vendre des places a: I suggested she sell front-row seats for her festivals. She said music is like the wind: you don't sell it. I told her I could sell the wind. She told me to try. I tried, with fans: “Wind of Ehécatl, two beans.” I only sold one. To my mother. She won, that time.
textes.Je lui ai proposé quatre cents pièces po: I offered her four hundred coins for her whole collection. A fortune! She thought for a second, a tiny little second, and said no. “Everything's for sale, my girl,” I told her. She answered: “Not this.” I felt something odd, right here, in my chest. I think I was happy. That's very bad for business.
textes.Je lui ai proposé un jour d'échanger son: Once, I offered to trade potions for her honey. She refused: her bees don't like the smell of sap. Since then, I pay her in coins, and she counts them one by one, out loud, in front of me. Like I do. We have great respect for each other.
textes.Je lui ai proposé une barque neuve. Pres: I offered him a new boat. Practically a gift: the wood at cost, my work for nothing. He listened to the end. He said: “No.” Then he left. The next day, he brought me a sardine, to thank me for offering. So every winter, I re-caulk the Mabrouka. She thanks me in her own way: she holds.
textes.Je lui ai proposé une valise de pièces p: I offered him a suitcase of coins to buy out his radio and rename it “Lisse FM, the optimised radio”. He refused live on air. A thousand people applauded. And three seagulls. Since then, in the evening, I listen to his radio. To keep an eye on the competition. During the concert. All of it. To keep an eye on it.
textes.Je lui ai prêté ma longue-vue de cuivre,: I lent him my copper spyglass, the one with an engraved star, a gift from my first captain. He gave it back with a kink in it: Gros-Louis had sat on it. I wept a little, for form's sake. Then I looked through it: it sees slightly round the corner, behind the rocks. Very handy for hidden coves.
textes.Je lui ai prêté ma longue-vue pour qu'il: I lent him my spyglass so he could watch for his father's ship. He looked at the sea for an hour without moving. I told him ships are like mushrooms: they turn up when you stop looking for them. He went off looking for mushrooms. I watched him go. Then I picked up the spyglass again. For him.
textes.Je lui ai raconté le Serpent à Sept Queu: I told him about the Seven-Tailed Serpent. He made it into a forty-verse ballad, where the serpent has twelve tails, where I fight it in a thunderstorm and spare it out of nobility. By the end, the whole tavern was crying. Master Hugues loudest of all. I cried too. I didn't know I was so noble. Well, in the song.
textes.Je lui ai raconté le grand feu de Teotih: I told him about the great fire of Teotihuacan: proud Tecciztécatl, covered in gold, who backs away four times, and humble Nanahuatzin who jumps. Mixtli listened to the end. Then he said: “I'd have jumped first.” I asked him: “With your feathers, or without?” He thought about it for a very long time.
textes.Je lui ai raconté le soir du trois-mâts: I told him about the night of the cloud three-master. He took it very seriously. On his big map, in the north, he added a little dotted island: “Probable island, seen by Fil-de-Fer”. I was so proud. Then I saw he'd drawn a sheep on it. A tiny one. He says it's a detail.
textes.Je lui ai raconté le vieux festival, ave: I told him about the old festival, with the fireworks! He's never seen any! Ever since, he asks me every day when there'll be some! I don't know what to tell him!
textes.Je lui ai raconté qu'en mousse, j'avais: I told him that as a cabin boy I'd seen a whale as big as the Skala, which soaked me right up to my cap. Big mistake. Since then he tells the whole harbour: “Even Si Larbi said so!” Moulay Brahim came to ask me if it was true. I said yes. It is true. But I didn't know I'd have to repeat it a hundred times.
textes.Je lui ai raconté qu'un monstre vivait d: I told him a monster lived in the harbour basin, under the pontoons. He searched for it a whole afternoon, with a lantern and a shrimping net. He came back with an old boot, put it on my knees and said: “Your monster lost this.” I kept it. It's where I keep my odds and ends.
textes.Je lui ai raconté que j'avais vaincu le: I told her I'd defeated the Seven-Tailed Serpent. She asked me, very seriously, if the serpent was all right. Nobody had ever asked me that. I made up that it had healed and was living happily. She was so relieved she prayed for it. Now I have a blessed imaginary serpent.
textes.Je lui ai raconté une blague à moi : « P: I told him a joke of my own: “Why does the tree never answer? Because it is processing the request.” He laughed for ten minutes. I did not understand why. But I recorded his laugh. I play it back.
textes.Je lui ai raconté une version du déluge: I told him a version of the flood where he saves the city with his quill. He pulled a face. The next day I heard him in the archives, all alone, reading it aloud. He even changed a word, to improve it. Got him, the old liar.
textes.Je lui ai rapporté de la Plage des Os un: I brought him back a big shell from Bone Beach, pink inside. He said: “WHAT'S THAT?!” I said: “For you.” He grunted and stuffed it under his arm. I thought he'd thrown it away. But one evening, I saw the shell in his hammock, right by the pillow. I didn't say anything. I smile when I think about it.
textes.Je lui ai rapporté un coquillage de la p: I brought her back a shell from the humans' beach, and told her you could hear the sea in it. She slept with it against her ear for a month. Since then, she asks everyone for one. That's a bit my fault.
textes.Je lui ai rapporté un harpon tordu en fo: I brought him back a harpoon bent into an S. A gargoyle had bitten it. I put it on his stall, saying: “Your harpoon ties knots.” He answered: “Your gargoyle eats iron.” We laughed. He swapped it for me. I kept the bent one: it hangs above my fireplace. The children think it's a snake.
textes.Je lui ai rapporté une graine de cactus: I brought her back a cactus seed from the dwarves, from Fire Mountain. For transport, I took the cactus along too. Bad idea. I sat on it when I landed. Noisette pulled out thirty-two spines. I went “fffwoosh” every time. It was very brave.
textes.Je lui ai taillé un peigne dans une bran: I carved her a comb from a branch of my kapok tree. Fallen, not cut. Free. It's the only free thing I've made in twenty-two years. She wears it in her hair. It pleases me. A little.
textes.Je lui ai tendu la clé du départ sans un: I handed him the departure key without a word. He took it without a word. It was the only time in his life he didn't say “What?”. I think he'd heard everything.
textes.Je lui ai tourné une cruche avec une bal: I threw him a jug with a whale in relief, spout and all. He doesn't use it. He doesn't fill it, he doesn't drink from it: he looks at it. It's on his windowsill, facing the sea. “So she can see the others,” he says. He's silly. She's pretty, my whale.
textes.Je lui ai vendu des graines de courges g: I sold her giant squash seeds. They gave normal squash. She came to complain. I measured a squash with my arms: “A little canoe. For a child.” She laughed. I refunded half. I'd never refunded anyone. I don't know what came over me. It was the laugh, I think.
textes.Je lui ai vendu mes cartes des fonds mar: I sold him my charts of the seabed one by one, one a day. He came back every morning, pretended to browse, then: “And that south-west one, there, how much?” In the end, he had them all. My window was empty. I never told him I'd kept the drafts. To read them over with him.
textes.Je lui ai vendu un bouclier pour la Gard: I sold him a shield for the Guard. The sturdiest one on the stall. It took two guards to carry it. Pyrus came back to complain. I told him: “Nothing gets through it.” He answered: “Not even the guards.” I offered him a lighter, less sturdy model. He preferred to keep the first.
textes.Je lui ai vendu une conque, « la conque: I sold her a conch, “the conch of Ehécatl, the one that set the sun turning”. She blew into it, in front of the whole square. It squeaked. Like a mouse. It was a lake snail shell. She laughed so hard she had to sit down on her drum. She kept it. She never asked me for a refund. I don't understand.
textes.Je lui ai vendu une potion pour que sa p: I sold her a potion to make her dough rise faster. I'd written “three drops” on the label. She read “three spoonfuls”. The dough rose up to the kitchen ceiling, and she served a pie as tall as a stool. She says it's my fault. I say my potion works very well.
textes.Je lui ai vendu une tisane en fiole, tou: I sold her a herbal tea in a vial, all ready to drink, a magnificent blue. She told me she'd found it “interesting”. That summer, her tomatoes were blue. Huge and blue. She gave me a basketful, without a word. I didn't ask anything. They were delicious. I'm thinking about it, for the shop.
textes.Je lui ai écrit dix-sept lettres pour la: I wrote her seventeen letters begging her to lower her voice. Mademoiselle Brindille delivered them one by one. Madame Hurla read them out on the square, aloud, with feeling. The whole town knows my prose. I am quoted at the market. I have never been so embarrassed, nor, I confess, so widely read.
textes.Je lui apprends le départ comme une flèc: I'm teaching her the off-like-an-arrow start, in Mum and Dad's vegetable garden. We get into position between the carrot rows, I say “Hop!”… and she's already gone. Before the hop. Every time. Mum yells that we're squashing the leeks. Mochi yells “I win!”. And me, I'm running after a six-year-old bunny. That's new.
textes.Je lui apprends le métier : compter les: I'm teaching him the trade: counting sails, telling a brig from a sloop, smelling rain before it comes. The other day, he shouted “Whale!” and the whole crew ran to port. It was a whale. A real one! I was so proud I nearly fell. Me, it took me three years to see one.
textes.Je lui apprends à attendre le virage. Ne: I'm teaching her to wait for the bend. Don't start too fast. Wait. Then give everything. … She said: “Like Grandpa with the float?” … Yes. Like Grandpa. … I'd never thought of that.
textes.Je lui apprends à retenir son souffle, p: I'm teaching her to hold her breath, for the day she goes out. We count together in front of the Gate. She's up to forty. I told her I could last three hundred. It's… a goal. Yesterday, at a hundred and twelve, I pretended I had sand in my throat.
textes.Je lui avais annoncé une traversée avec: I'd foretold him a crossing with a beautiful stranger with golden eyes. He shaved, he put on a clean shirt. It was a goat, for Sauge's garden. With magnificent golden eyes, I stand by it. I never said it was a woman. He didn't speak to me for a week. The goat adores him.
textes.Je lui avais demandé un poisson, sur ma: I'd asked her for a fish, on my sail. A small, discreet one. She painted a three-metre purple octopus, with eyes that follow you while you row. That month, I caught two sardines. She says the fish just need to get used to it. They've been getting used to it for three years.
textes.Je lui avais garanti que Rhubarbe était: I'd guaranteed her that Rhubarbe was perfectly trained. He opened his beak, looked at her, and said: “Old sardine.” I thought I'd end up in the bay. The captain smiled. A tiny little smile, on the side of her scar. She paid double. Since then, Rhubarbe has learned all her curses. He says them in her accent.
textes.Je lui avais prédit une grande découvert: I'd predicted a great discovery for him. The next day, he searched the whole island for his glasses. They were on his nose. I told him: for a man who looks so far away, seeing what's under his nose is a very great discovery. He thought about it for a long time. Then he thanked me. He's an honest man.
textes.Je lui commande des rythmes « pour faire: I order rhythms from him “to bring in the sea bream”. He says there's no rhythm for sea bream. I say he just hasn't found it yet. So every afternoon he tries a new one on the table, and every morning I sing it at sea. So far, only sardines. But we're working on it.
I say thank you to it.
textes.Je lui dis tous les jours. Il n'écoute p: I tell it every day. It doesn't listen.
textes.Je lui dois le « Traité des flammes douc: I've owed her the “Treatise on Gentle Flames” for sixty-three years. Every year, on the same date, I receive a little card in her hand: “Dear Professor, the book awaits you. No hurry.” I keep them all in a drawer. There are sixty-three. Each one is a little funnier than the last.
textes.Je lui en fais un au goût saucisse ?: Shall I make him a sausage-flavoured one?
textes.Je lui en fais un nouveau. Au goût sauci: I'll make him a new one. Sausage flavour?
I send her flowers every week. Roses, tulips, daisies. She never replies. One day, I sent her wisteria from my grandmother's Cottage. The following week, I saw the same bouquet, still on her desk, through the castle window. Wilted, but there. I said nothing. But I waxed my moustache twice.
textes.Je lui envoie un carnet chaque mois avec: I send him a notebook every month with the colours of the adventurers coming back up. One day, as a joke, I wrote: “Hilaire: green, then blue, then green.” Aubin came running to the dungeon, he wanted to see. Hilaire really was green, then blue, then green, every ten minutes. They spent the afternoon together. Hilaire said it was his most useful day ever.
textes.Je lui garde un tabouret près de l'enclu: I keep a stool for him by the anvil. He tells stories, I hammer, the customers stay for both. I forged him a walking stick, with a moon on the handle. Left it against his door, without a word. He told the story of the walking stick to the whole village. Three days. Hm.
textes.Je lui grille toujours des « sardines sp: I always grill her “special sardines”, just for her. She watches them, she counts them. They're exactly the same as the others, out of the same crate. But I put them in the left corner of the grill. The captains' corner. That changes everything.
textes.Je lui laisse mes noix de coco vides sur: I leave her my empty coconuts on the low wall, and she makes flowerpots out of them. Now there are flowering coconuts all along the street, right down to the ferry terminal. The tourists think it's an old Port-Azur tradition. We don't set them straight.
textes.Je lui parlerai doucement dans la marmit: I'll talk to her gently in the pot.
textes.Je lui porte le minerai des pentes rouge: I've been bringing him ore from the red slopes for two hundred years. He weighs it, sniffs it, says “Hmph, that'll do”, and pays me three coins less than agreed. In the evening, at the Mug, he buys me a fizz. Three coins, the fizz. We never talk about it.
textes.Je lui rapporte des tisanes du village,: I bring her herbal teas from the village, verbena from the hills, in a paper cone. I put them on her bench and slip away. Why? You can't give back a fiancé with verbena, I know. But you try anyway, for fifty years.
textes.Je lui rapporte le miel sauvage d'en hau: I bring her the wild honey from the top of the Mother Tree. The bees don't like it. Neither do I. But when I come down, she's already set the first loaf aside. The best one. She thinks I don't notice she gives me the best one. I notice everything.
textes.Je lui répondrais : pour un matelot qui: I'd answer: for a sailor who laughed just right. Then I'd go and have my herbal tea, at the exact hour, like a well-regulated lady.
textes.Je lui tends des pièges. « Deux daurades: I set traps for her. “Two sea bream, Inès? Does your guest like lemon?” She answers: “I'm very hungry on Fridays.” “What time does he come?” “I eat early.” She never blushes, never! A stone, that woman. A beautiful stone, but a stone. If it were me, I'd have confessed everything by the second fish.
textes.Je lui vends des cailloux magiques pour: I sell her magic pebbles for her fire. She thinks they're ordinary pebbles. She pays for them anyway, because she's kind. One in ten is really magic. I never know which. Neither does she. One day, her forge gave off purple sparks all night long. She didn't say anything. Neither did I. Heh heh.
textes.Je m'appelle Clapotis parce que, bébé, j: My name's Clapotis — it means splish-splash — because when I was a baby I jumped in every puddle. Now I jump with a skateboard. It's harder.
My name's Clapotis — splish-splash — because when I was a baby I jumped in every puddle. Now I jump with a skateboard. It's harder. And wetter too, because the puddles are still there.
textes.Je m'appelle Fusain parce que j'ai comme: I'm called Fusain — charcoal — because I started with coal from the old boilers. I drew on the walls, on the wagons, on the doors. Everywhere. One day the Assembly voted: “Fusain may paint on the rock. All of the rock. But not on the sofas.” I respected the sofas.
textes.Je m'appelle Ix Sak : la Blanche. Mais t: My name is Ix Sak: the White One. But all through my childhood, I had blue fingers! My mother dyed with indigo, and I dipped my hands in all her pots. The children called me “Ix Sak the Blue”. My mother laughed: “She has the name of one colour and the hands of another.” Today, my hands are every colour. The name, I kept.
textes.Je m'appelle Kinich, comme Kinich Ahau,: My name is Kinich, like Kinich Ahau, the sun god! Well, I'm a little sun. My parents work in the milpa, the maize field, all day long. So I go everywhere in Yaxché: the ball court, the market, the temple, the bees. Mum says I shine brightest when I'm up to mischief.
textes.Je m'appelle Noisette parce que quand je: I'm called Noisette because when I was born, I was all tiny and round, and I had hazel-coloured eyes, like hazelnuts. Mama wanted to call me Brioche. Papa said no. I'm glad. Otherwise Mamie Rissole would've wanted to eat me. She eats everything that's named like a cake. Well, she makes other people eat it.
textes.Je m'appelle Ressort parce que, bébé, je: I'm called Ressort — that means “spring” — because as a baby I was always bouncing in my cradle. Boing, boing, boing. Mum said: “That one's got springs in his feet.” She checked. There weren't any. But the name stuck.
textes.Je m'assois un instant. La foudre, ça fa: I'll sit down for a moment. Lightning is tiring.
textes.Je m'assois, je m'assois. Il était une f: I'm sitting, I'm sitting. Once upon a time…
textes.Je m'assois. Juste un moment. Mon cervea: I'll sit down. Just for a moment. My brain is going bzzz.
textes.Je m'en doutais : tu as les yeux de quel: I suspected as much: you have the eyes of someone who counts stars. Moon tea, three drops of honey, and put your thoughts down beside the bed. They'll wait for you.
I thought so. The horns, probably. Then tell them about Pandémonia: our lanterns, our cakes, our puppies that breathe fire… just a little. They won't be afraid of us any more.
textes.Je m'en doutais. Tous les joueurs disent: I suspected as much. All gamblers say that, and they all end up the same way: here, at my table, with empty pockets. Do sit… sit down. I was expecting you.
textes.Je m'endors debout depuis toujours. Aubi: I've always fallen asleep standing up. Aubin says it's a rare talent. Father Clotaire says it's a blessing. Captain Ferdinand says it's article twelve. I say it's restful.
textes.Je m'endors pendant mes sermons. Oui, je: I fall asleep during my sermons. Yes, I know. I've been told. But you see, the temple is so quiet, the pews so soft, and my own voice so… restful. My flock doesn't complain: they're asleep too.
textes.Je m'ennuie. Personne ne veut faire la c: I'm bored. Nobody wants to race me. Ionie says her saucers are tired. Volt says I make the Spire flicker. I need an opponent. A real one. With a machine that flies…
textes.Je m'ennuie. Thalion ne veut pas m'appre: I'm bored. Thalion won't teach me archery. He says Sylwen's door never recovered.
textes.Je m'entraîne la nuit, quand tout le mon: I train at night, when everyone's dancing. Bondi thinks nobody knows. Everybody knows.
I train at night. During the party. In secret. … Everybody knows. I live with Brume. We don't talk. It's good. Before every race, Caramel saves me a skewer. The biggest. Myrtille wants to run like me. She counts my laps on her fingers. She gets it wrong. I don't correct her.
textes.Je m'entraîne le matin, je bois un cacao: I train in the morning, I drink a cacao at Ix Chab's at noon, if she'll serve me, and I go back to the court. In the evening, I dance at the Venus platform with my blue hips. Kinich copies all my moves. Ix Sak sews my feathers. Balam looks at me sideways. And Ah Kin Pech counts my bumps.
textes.Je m'entraîne à l'aube, je fais ma ronde: I train at dawn, I do my rounds at the tianguis, I train again. In the evening, I dance in the square when Nenetl plays. Up there, on the slopes of Smoking Mountain, two jaguars took one of Xóchitl's animals. I want to hunt them. The high priest says to wait for the right day. I'm waiting. I don't like waiting.
I'm practising scrubbing for your ship. That way, the day you take me on as cabin boy, I'll be ready.
textes.Je m'entraîne. Le souffle, c'est comme l: I'm training. Breath is like friendship: you have to keep it up.
textes.Je m'occupe de la Flèche depuis six cent: I've been looking after the Spire for six hundred years. Six hundred years listening to the Heart beat. I know all its noises. When it hums, it's happy. When it crackles, it's cold. When it goes quiet… I stop sleeping.
textes.Je m'occupe du jardin. Il me le rend bie: I'm looking after the garden. It pays me back nicely.
textes.Je m'échappe parfois du palais par le ja: Sometimes I slip out of the palace through the garden to buy fire cinnamon at Zébuline's. Pyrus follows twenty paces behind, pretending to inspect the cobblestones. Clang, clang, clang. The merchants nudge each other. I pretend not to hear him. It's our little play, and the whole market knows the lines.
I mostly fight with my bare hands.
textes.Je me couche à vingt et une heures préci: I go to bed at nine p.m. sharp. Even on aurora nights. I watch them through the window, from ten p.m. to five past ten. Then I sleep. It runs like clockwork, because I am clockwork. Almost.
textes.Je me demande parfois si ce n'est pas un: Sometimes I wonder if it isn't a jar of fig jam. Don't tell Madame Colette. She'd raise the price. Or worse: she'd sell it to me.
textes.Je me lève avant Rê, je chauffe le four,: I get up before Rê, I heat the oven, I sell the bread, I brew the beer, and in the evening I serve the whole village. Amenemhat reads and spills things, Khéty tells his fish stories doubled, Hapou pays in onions. And me, I listen. That's how I know everything. People tell a brewer everything. Especially after the second jar.
textes.Je me lève avant l'aube. Je croise Nox q: I get up before dawn. I pass Nox on his way to bed, and I give him his mint. Some mornings, I go and pick mushrooms in the Ash Wood. I sing to my peppers, I chase Flammèche's puppies with my broom, and at noon I have a nap. At my age, a nap is like any other plant: it needs tending.
textes.Je me lève à cinq heures, je pêche au po: I get up at five, I fish off the pontoon, I sell at the slipway, I mend my nets on the beach, and in the evening we light the fire with the others. Sometimes, when I wake up, there are shells laid on my boat. The mist folk, Lucie says. I say thank you out loud. You never know who's listening.
textes.Je me lève à cinq heures. J'inspecte l'a: I rise at five. I inspect the silverware, I count the candles, I have my horns polished on Mondays at Monsieur Tiburce's, and I fetch the brioches from Monsieur Bobor at noon. I measure each brioche with a silver ruler. They are all the same height. Except one. Always one. I suspect Monsieur Bobor.
textes.Je me lève à trois heures. Je pétris, je: I get up at three. I knead, I sing, I taste. At dawn, I give the first brioche to Grandpa Ébène in exchange for a story. At noon, Asmodin measures my brioches with his silver ruler. At four o'clock, a brioche breaks by accident for Pépin. In the evening, I go and float at the Baths. I float very well.
textes.Je me mets en veille de trois heures à t: I go on standby from three o'clock to five past three. During those five minutes, I dream. Always the same dream: I'm in the lift, and it goes up, and up, and up. I never reach the top. I wake up happy anyway.
textes.Je me plains de la musique de la Fronde: I complain about the Fronde's music drifting up the Column on concert nights, {surnom}. But I'll tell you something. My wife lives right above the bottom of the shaft. On concert nights, she opens her window and dances. She wrote and told me. So when the music drifts all the way up here… I complain. Then I open my window a little. To check.
textes.Je me pose une question depuis des jours: I've been asking myself a question for days. Do you think you can forgive everything?
I'm moving. In the name of the city.
textes.Je me repose au soleil. Ne me fais pas d: I'm resting in the sun. Don't block my light.
textes.Je me repose un peu. Les jambes, ça s'us: I'm having a little rest. Legs wear out, you know.
textes.Je me réveille doucement. Le matin, je s: I'm waking up slowly. I'm slow in the mornings.
textes.Je me souviens de toi. Tu es le premier: I remember you. You're the first visitor in a thousand years.
textes.Je me souviens de tout. Du premier lampa: I remember everything. The first street lamp, the first tower, and you. Especially you.
textes.Je me souviens surtout de ta première vi: What I remember most is your first visit: you said hello to a lettuce. Without meaning to, I think. It's grown very well since.
textes.Je me souviens surtout que tu cours vite: Mostly I remember you run fast, Hugues.
textes.Je me suis assis devant la forge de Bori: I sat down in front of Borin's forge and never left. Thirty days. Ash rained down, I stayed put. On the thirtieth, he handed me a broom. Twelve years later, I'm allowed to hold the tongs. And to hammer, sometimes. When he's not looking. Or when he pretends not to look.
textes.Je me suis caché dans la fontaine, au mi: I hid in the fountain, right in the middle of Jupiter. Nobody thinks of looking inside Jupiter: it's too big. Pixel found me in thirty seconds. She said: “Jupiter, are you singing?” I said: “No!” I don't get how she knew. Jupiter doesn't sing. Well, I don't think so.
textes.Je me suis endormi contre la stèle, un m: One morning I fell asleep against the stela. I woke up with the date of creation printed on my cheek. Nobody said a thing. I gave my lesson all morning. In the evening, Ix Kanul came by and said: “Lovely lesson, Ah Kin. Very… visible.” I only understood when I washed my face.
textes.Je me suis endormi un jour au milieu de: One day I fell asleep in the middle of the story of the owl who had lost his night. When I woke up, there was a flower on my nose, and Nimiel had finished the story for me, in front of the whole circle. Her ending was better than mine. That's how I tell it now.
textes.Je me suis endormi un soir sur son compt: One evening I fell asleep on her counter, in the middle of my speech on the injustice of ranks. I woke up with a blanket over my back and a “received” stamp on my cheek. It took three days to come off. Bertrand made a song. “The Stamped Knight”. I'm not even a knight.
textes.Je me suis installé un module d'émotions: One evening, I installed an emotions module, all by myself. Kenji said it was risky. The first emotion I felt was fear. The second was the joy of having been afraid. I regret nothing.
textes.Je me suis réveillé dans une caisse, il: I woke up in a crate, forty years ago. Someone opened the lid. There was the sky, the sea, and a lady with a teapot. It was Mamie Kiku. She said to me: “Here, a broom.” I started right away.
textes.Je me suis réveillé à minuit : le lac fu: I woke up at midnight: the lake was steaming like a cooking pot. She was in the middle, in hot water up to her chin, with a woolly hat on, and all the fish huddled round her. She waved at me. Waved. I stood on the bank in my nightshirt. It took three days to freeze the lake again.
textes.Je me suis tordu la cheville en montant: I twisted my ankle climbing onto a dome. Aurore treated me in her healing bubble, the one I built. Lying there, I looked at the ceiling: the clouds drifted slowly by. I felt better straight away. I told her: “It's your glass that heals.” She said: “It's your ceiling.”
textes.Je me suis un peu perdu dans le Bois de: I got a little bit lost in the Ash Wood the other day. Not a lot! Just a little. Now Mum holds my hand at the market. So embarrassing. But kind of nice, too.
textes.Je me tiens derrière sa chaise quand il: I stand behind his chair when he plays. I tap the table with my hook. Tick, tick. Out of habit. Sylvain thinks it's a signal. Ignace swears it's a tic. Me, I say nothing. People wonder. I like it when other people are the ones asking questions.
textes.Je me trompe exprès, Fatima. Pour t'ente: I get it wrong on purpose, Fatima. To hear you.
First I put on my helmet.
textes.Je mets mes babouches que pendant le qua: I only wear my slippers on night watch. One night, the captain was pacing the deck and stepped on a slipper in the dark. He yelled “THE CAT!” and pulled out his sabre. I crawled over and got the slipper back. The next day, he was telling everyone he'd nearly caught the ginger cat with his bare hands. I didn't say anything.
textes.Je mets un peu d'argent de côté pour ouv: I'm putting a bit of money aside to open a little guesthouse, one day. With just three rooms. And I won't make the beds.
I'll put in a dotted line, meanwhile.
I'll come up tonight. I'll bring the tea.
textes.Je monte parfois au phare avec deux tass: Sometimes I climb up to the lighthouse with two cups of coffee. Three hundred and twenty steps: at the two-hundredth, I sit down. He lets me in without a word. One night, he beckoned me over to the lantern and pointed west. Nothing at first. Then, very far off, under the water, a blue dot. He didn't say a word. Neither did I. For once.
textes.Je monte vendre au marché parce que je v: I come up to sell at the market because I want people up here to see what we make down there. Not weirdos. People who make things, who sing, who help each other. One piece of jewellery at a time. It's slow. But a bolt is small too, and it holds bridges together.
textes.Je mords les robots. Je mords les monstr: I bite robots. I bite monsters. I never bite friends. You're my friend. I lick you. That's the opposite of biting.
textes.Je mouds le maïs avant l'aube, je fais l: I grind the maize before dawn, I make the flatbreads, and I sell my cacao all day. Chak comes by at noon with his ball: I keep an eye on him. Ah Kin Pech pays me one bean short. Yum Kab sells his honey far too cheap. In the evening, I sit in the square with Ix Sak and tell her everything. It rests the arms.
I was meditating. Your bread woke me.
textes.Je n'achète plus rien chez toi. Depuis l: I'm not buying anything from you any more. Not since the tablecloth.
textes.Je n'ai aucune photo de ma mère. Elle es: I don't have a single photo of my mother. She left when I was four, and her face fades a little more every year. I still have her laugh, just about. So I photograph everyone, all the time. So that nobody here ever fades. Don't tell the others, {surnom}. They'd pose far too seriously.
textes.Je n'ai jamais dit le contraire. Plus ja: I never said otherwise. Never again.
textes.Je n'ai jamais dit à la reine Oriane que: I never told Queen Oriane I'd lost her branch. And the worst thing, {surnom}… is that without it, I don't even know if I really have a gift. Maybe the wand was the magician. Not me. Don't tell anyone. Not even me.
textes.Je n'ai jamais dormi dans aucune de nos: I've never slept in a single one of our rooms. Yet I know them all by heart.
textes.Je n'ai jamais eu d'enfants, mon caillou: I never had children, my little pebble. But I've fed all the ones in the Fronde. Rivet, who ate while drumming on his bowl. Bielle, who sang with her mouth full. Ysaé, who ate too fast. Ressort, who never eats his mushrooms. And now you, {surnom}. See? I've got a very big family. And it's very hungry.
textes.Je n'ai jamais eu d'enfants. Mais j'ai n: I never had children. But I've fed every child in the Fronde. Rivet, Bielle, Écho, little Ysaé, now Ressort… When Ysaé went to live up top, I put a jar of stew in her bag. She wrote to me: “I ate it in three days, crying.” She always did eat too fast, that girl.
textes.Je n'ai jamais eu de petits, et pourtant: I never had cubs, and yet all of Ramure calls me Mother. I took Brume as my pupil, I knitted Croc-Gris's red scarf, and every spring I put the moon lanterns back on the bridges. This year, my paws won't take me to the edge of the ponds any more. So in the evening, on my moss, at the Circle, I watch Lilas dance. That's my way of lighting lanterns now.
textes.Je n'ai jamais pris le bateau, alors je: I've never taken the boat, so I give Fanny my messages for the other island. “Say hello to the harbour.” “Tell the lighthouse it blinks nicely.” She comes back the next day and tells me, very seriously: “The lighthouse thanks you.” I know she's making it up. But she says it so seriously that it does me good.
textes.Je n'ai jamais vendu un tapis au premier: I've never sold a carpet at the first price. Never. Once, a pirate paid without haggling. It made me ill for three days.
textes.Je n'ai jamais vu Pimprenelle. Mais je s: I've never seen Pimprenelle. But I know she taps fast, never misses a knock, and finds at least five bolts a day. She's nine. She learns the code faster than me. It's a bit annoying. Mostly it's brilliant.
textes.Je n'ai jamais vu Zélie, alors je l'imag: I've never seen Zélie, so I imagine her. Tall, with aviator goggles on her forehead and a pencil behind her ear. She sends me “theoretical” timetables. I correct her addresses: “Ramure has no streets, Commander: it has trees.” She replied: “Noted. Which tree?” We're making progress.
textes.Je n'ai jamais écrit un poème entier, {s: I've never written a whole poem, {surnom}. The wind always carries off the last line. But I think it's on purpose. A finished poem gets put away. A poem still waiting for its last line, you keep it in your heart. And you come back tomorrow.
textes.Je n'ai pas bougé. Enfin, si : je vous a: I haven't moved. Well, yes: I followed you. That's the idea.
textes.Je n'ai pas de fils, {surnom}. Le bâton: I have no son, {surnom}. The amin's staff, one day, will have to be handed on. I'd like it to be Ahmed. He laughs, he listens, the fleet loves him, and he always comes home. But I've never told him. Saying it would be admitting I'm old. So I watch him pass the jetty every morning, and I keep quiet. Like Driss.
I don't have an octopus, Protée.
textes.Je n'ai pas encore sommeil. Alors je tra: I'm not sleepy yet. So I'm hanging about a bit.
I didn't need to knock, then.
textes.Je n'ai pas le droit d'avoir un implant: I'm not allowed an implant until I'm eighteen. I want to keep both my arms anyway. That way I can hug Papa from both sides: one warm arm, one cold arm.
textes.Je n'ai pas le droit… Le règlement de la: I'm not allowed… Guild rules. Églantine would glare at me. She can glare very hard when she wants to.
I don't have time to sleep.
textes.Je n'ai pas le temps, Bulle. J'étiquette: I don't have time, Bulle. I'm labelling.
textes.Je n'ai pas oublié : les grenouilles vou: I haven't forgotten: frogs scare you. I've written the prayer. It doesn't work yet.
I didn't say anything about the watering can.
textes.Je n'ai pas peur ! … Si. Mais je reste !: I'm not scared! … I am. But I'm staying!
textes.Je n'ai pas peur du noir, ni des robots,: I'm not scared of the dark, or robots, or the Great Digger. If you're here. If you're not here, I'm scared of everything. Stay here.
I'm not scared, Monsieur Yvon. Yes I am.
textes.Je n'ai pas peur. Je suis juste un peu é: I'm not scared. I'm just a bit electric.
I didn't listen to all of it.
textes.Je n'ai pas un seul implant. Tous les an: I don't have a single implant. Every year the doctor says to me: “Madame Kiku, how about a nice new knee?” And every year I answer: my knees are original parts, guaranteed eighty years, and they haven't broken down yet.
textes.Je n'ai plus d'étincelles. Il faut que j: I'm out of sparks. I need to recharge. I'll sit down.
I only have a screwdriver, Ionie.
I have nothing better to offer you.
textes.Je n'ai rien demandé, ma petite ! … Quat: I didn't ask anything, my girl! … Four hundred and ten?
I didn't say a thing! Yellow, size thirty-seven.
textes.Je n'ai rien dit, Capitaine !: I didn't say a thing, Captain!
textes.Je n'ai rien dit, Mademoiselle Aurore !: I didn't say a thing, Miss Aurore!
I didn't say a thing, my dear.
I said nothing. I saw nothing.
textes.Je n'ai vu la mer qu'à vingt ans. Ma mèr: I didn't see the sea until I was twenty. My mother always said “soon”. When I finally went down, I walked into the waves with my shoes on.
