textes.Je suis l'élève du professeur Boum. J'ai: I'm Professor Boum's student. I kept the idea of exploding, but I took out the danger. What's left is the colours. That's the best part.
textes.Je suis la capitaine de la place des Lan: I'm the captain of Lantern Square. Amine is my sailor, he always loses at boarding. Rosa's teaching me pirate knots. On the Skala, the cannons make great horses, but the caïd chases us off. And my uncle Ahmed lets me command the Zahra when she's tied up at the quay. A boat that's tied up is still a boat.
textes.Je suis la cinquième enfant de deux bibl: I'm the fifth child of two librarians at the Academy. At home, we whispered. At the table, in bed, even when we argued. Me, I blew up paper bags and popped them between the shelves. BANG! Thirty readers jumped. I got scolded a lot. In a whisper. It doesn't have the same effect at all.
textes.Je suis la fille de Philomène, la conteu: I'm the daughter of Philomène, the storyteller. As a little girl, I listened to her hero stories. Me, I wanted to catch things. Anything: butterflies, hens, draughts. I married a man whose turnips run away. It was destiny.

I'm the daughter of Philomène, the storyteller. As a girl, I'd listen to her tell stories of heroes. Me, I didn't like listening. I liked catching. Butterflies, hens, draughts. My mother used to say: “One day this child will catch something really big.” I caught a husband. That's big.
textes.Je suis la mécanicienne du port. Je dors: I'm the harbour mechanic. I sleep in the warehouse, between a propeller and a barrel of grease. If it floats, rolls or whistles, it's mine to fix. Right now, I want to wake up the Little Piston, the tugboat that's been asleep for three years. Master Rivet wants a robot boat from me: no. And in the evening, I fish at the end of the quay, next to Gonzague. We don't talk much. The fish bite better.
textes.Je suis la petite sœur de Nausicaa. Mama: I'm Nausicaa's little sister. Mum sang the tides, my sister sang along with her, and I danced on the edge of the canal. I fell in at least once every tide. So I learned to dance in the water too. It splashes a lot. People love it. Well, the front row, less so.
textes.Je suis la petite-fille de la vieille Ga: I'm the granddaughter of old Garance, the herbalist of the Herb Shop. At five, I could name a hundred herbs with my eyes shut: sage, pond mint, nettle, moon moss… Roux, an apprentice alongside me, mixed up sage and nettle. He put nettle in a tea for Garance. She sneezed for a week. I laughed for a month.
textes.Je suis lampiste à l'Atelier des Lumière: I'm a lamp-maker at the Workshop of Lights. Today I made three lanterns. Doctor Opaline started one and forgot two. It's a good day.
textes.Je suis le champion de la bagarre du Req: I'm the brawling champion of the Requin Borgne. Nobody's beaten me since… since Belle-Humeur. But he cheats: he's always angry.
textes.Je suis le fantôôôme de la maisoooon…: I am the ghooost of the hooouse…
textes.Je suis le fils d'un berger des collines: I'm the son of a shepherd from the hills. As a boy, I looked after the sheep. I'd sit under a tree, watch them, and fall asleep. When I woke up, they were all there, lying around me. My mother said the sheep were looking after me. I think she was right.
textes.Je suis le fils d'un berger. Petit, je g: I'm a shepherd's son. As a boy, I watched the sheep. I'd fall asleep, and the sheep watched themselves. When I became a guard, I thought gates would be the same. Gates don't move. That's even better than sheep.
textes.Je suis le fils d'un cordonnier de la gr: I'm the son of a cobbler from the big island in the east. My father wanted me to make shoes. I wanted to wear them out. On my twenty-third birthday, I took my sword, my best pair of boots, and the boat to Montjoie. I lost a boot getting out of the rowing boat. It was a sign.
I'm the son of Croc-Gris's sister. I grew up at the foot of the Lookout tree, with my uncle way up top saying “Halt” to the squirrels. He wanted to make me a guard. But guards sit still! Me, I can't keep still. And he won the Great Race at twenty: the last time a wolf won. Me, I want the next one. I can feel it in my paws.
textes.Je suis le meilleur programme de Monsieu: I'm Mister Fil's best program. The only one, actually.
textes.Je suis le nouveau Champion des Cornes !: I'm the new Champion of the Horns!
textes.Je suis le plus vieux de la Cité. Quatre: I'm the oldest in the City. Ninety-seven. I wasn't born when the island rose, but my father told me about it so often that I remember it better than my own wedding. Don't tell my wife. She's in the Park, and she has sharp ears.
textes.Je suis le plus vieux du Bois-Doré. Neuf: I'm the oldest in Bois-Doré. Nine hundred and eighty-seven years. I count the springs, not the winters: it's more cheerful.
textes.Je suis le porteur de la Gare. Je porte: I'm the Station porter. I carry everything, except clouds. They're slippery.
textes.Je suis le premier enfant né sous le dôm: I'm the first child born under the dome. Day 212, Abyssos wrote it down, with my name misspelt: “Coralain”. He never corrected it. My mother said I cried so loud the crystal flickered. I say the crystal was greeting me. Not the same thing.
textes.Je suis le quarante-deuxième roi de Forg: I am the forty-second king of Forgefer. My great-great-grandfather dug this hall by hand. With a spoon, they say. I don't believe it.
textes.Je suis le roi… le roi des sardines…: I'm the king… the king of sardines…
I am the seventh model of my series. The six others work in other towers, other cities. We send each other one message a year. Mine always says: “All is well. Height of the tower: two hundred and sixty-five metres.” They find it fascinating.
textes.Je suis le seul à Carène qui ait travers: I'm the only one in Carène who's crossed the whole island on foot. The highlands, the mists, the desert. I came back with blisters and twelve notebooks.
textes.Je suis le vent ! Personne ne m'attrape: I'm the wind! Nobody can catch me!
textes.Je suis là, je suis là ! À trois pas der: I'm here, I'm here! Three steps behind you, as the priestesses' book says.
textes.Je suis là… Je suis juste un peu discrèt: I'm here… I'm just a little discreet.
textes.Je suis maire, tout de même !: I am the mayor, after all!
textes.Je suis monté du Plancher pour voir la C: I came up from the Floor to see the City. It's so clean I'm scared to breathe too hard.
textes.Je suis monté ici il y a vingt ans pour: I came up here twenty years ago to taste the sauce. I never really came back down. In the evening, yes. To sleep. But in the morning, I climb back up. It's waiting for me.
textes.Je suis montée à Hautefond par la Ligne,: I went up to Hautefond by the Line yesterday, for the first time. There's wind! Everywhere! And the ceiling's really high. Blue, even.
textes.Je suis mécanicien à l'Atelier des Scaph: I'm a mechanic at the Diving Suit Workshop. Yolande had me re-tighten forty-two nuts this morning. They were already tight. Now they're even tighter.
I was born Anselme Vasseur, on the quay. My father mended nets in front of the door; the whole port said “old Vasseur's net”. My little brother Marius laughed at everything. Me, I counted the stars, lying on the stones that were still warm. Somebody had to count them.
textes.Je suis né Gustave Bouilloire, à Hautefo: I was born Gustave Bouilloire, in Hautefond, two years after my brother Firmin. He loved steam. I loved froth. At ten, we were already arguing: who'd make the best hot chocolate? Our mother settled it: “Both of you. And wash your cups.”
textes.Je suis né au bord du lac. À six ans, un: I was born on the lakeshore. When I was six, a giant frog swallowed me, along with my rod and my bucket. It spat me out three seconds later. I kept the rod. I lost my nerve. Since then, I tremble, but I come back.
textes.Je suis né au château de Tournevent, sur: I was born at Tournevent castle, on a hill so windy the nursemaids had to hold me with both hands. My mother said the wind taught me to shout my name: otherwise nobody could hear me. Since then, I shout my name. Out of habit. And because it's a very fine one.
textes.Je suis né au fond de la Vieille-Veine,: I was born at the bottom of the Old Vein, the oldest mine in the mountain. My father dug there, my grandfather too. My mother says my first cry knocked a pebble off the ceiling. For my tenth birthday, they gave me a pickaxe my size. I lost it the next day. I never found it again.
textes.Je suis né au village, bien, bien, mais: I was born in the village, good, good, but I grew up in the jungle with my grandma. She grew red bananas, small ones, sweet as honey. She used to say: “A banana tree is a family: one root, lots of children, and everybody keeps each other warm.” When she passed on, she left me a single plant. I kept it in a bucket.
textes.Je suis né au village, de l'autre côté d: I was born in the village, across the water. I came here to deliver barrels, thirty years ago. I never went back. Berthe had served me her tart.
textes.Je suis né au village, frérot, dans une: I was born in the village, bro, in a house with seven brothers and sisters and one bed for every two. We slept in a heap, ate in a heap, laughed in a heap. The only thing that was all mine was my shell collection, under the bed. I counted them at night. There were one thousand two hundred. No, really.
textes.Je suis né au-dessus d'une apothicaireri: I was born above an apothecary's shop, between the jars of leeches and the herbs drying from the ceiling. My father treated the neighbourhood's colds with herbal teas that smelled of socks. Me, I treated my toys: I had a teddy bear with three wooden legs and a bandage on its head. It never complained. My best patient, to this day.
textes.Je suis né au-dessus d'une librairie de: I was born above a bookshop in the Upper Town, amid the smell of paper and smoke. I learned to read at four, to fly at six, and to ask questions at five. My mother used to say I was born with a question mark instead of a tail. She wasn't wrong: look how it curls.
textes.Je suis né avec des cornes déjà brillant: I was born with horns that already shone. My mother says I looked at myself in them before I looked at her. At three, I was polishing my cat's horns. He didn't have any, but I insisted. At ten, I was polishing the whole neighbourhood's horns for sweets. I had found my calling. And cavities.
textes.Je suis né berger, là-haut, sur les haut: I was born a shepherd, up there, in the highlands, like my sister, Écrou's mum. But I was afraid of heights. On the ridges, I walked on all fours, and the sheep made fun of me. Yes, they did: a sheep making fun of you goes “baaa” with a certain look. At thirty, I realised the heights weren't for me. I came down to Cliquetis.
textes.Je suis né d'un coup de vent, tout en ha: I was born from a gust of wind, at the very top of Yggdrasil, on the windiest day of the century. My first word was “Fffwoosh”. My second, “faster”. I blew every petal out of the throne room before I could even fly straight. The queen was still finding them in her hair the next day.
textes.Je suis né dans l'arbre du sud, le trois: I was born in the south tree, the third of seven children, and I ran behind everybody from day one! Behind my brothers, behind the butterflies, and above all behind Cerfeuil, my best pal, who was already burning his toast at six. Second, fifth, last: I didn't care. Running behind someone is still running!
textes.Je suis né dans la batterie basse d'un v: I was born on the lower gun deck of a warship! My mother made the gunners' soup, my father cleaned the cannons. My cradle was a cannonball crate. They say I cried all the time, except when we fired. BOOM, and I'd fall asleep. My mother said I was a bad-tempered baby. She was right, my mother.
textes.Je suis né dans la jungle, sur l'île des: I was born in the jungle, on the coconut island, the one with the village. My mother says I climbed trees before I could walk, and it's true: to walk, I first had to come back down. My grandfather taught me to open a coconut with a single stroke of the machete. Crack! He'd say: “One nut, one stroke. Two strokes means you talk too much.”
I was born in the jungle, on the island of coconut palms. Here, I open three hundred coconuts a week. It's a bit like going home.
textes.Je suis né dans la maison bleue, au-dess: I was born in the blue house, above the harbour. From my window I could see everything: the boats, the square, and Colette's stall. At ten, I “borrowed” one of her apples, with a solemn promise: “I'll pay you back when I'm mayor.” A political manifesto already! And an opponent already.
textes.Je suis né dans la maison du quai, celle: I was born in the house on the quay, the one I still sleep in. My father taught me the bowline before the alphabet: “Letters won't hold a boat.” At twelve, I landed my first grouper. Forty kilos, I've been saying so for sixty years. My father said twenty-five. My father had no imagination.
textes.Je suis né dans la tour de garde. Mon pè: I was born in the watchtower. My father guarded the village entrance, and so did his father. My first toy was an arrow with no tip. My first word was “halt”. My mother says it was “mama”. She's mistaken.
textes.Je suis né dans le quartier des ponts, f: I was born in the bridges quarter, son of a shell gatherer. My father would leave the dome holding his breath and come back with his arms full. Me, at five, I was already standing guard at our front door, with a fishbone for a spear. Against whom? Nobody. Even then.
textes.Je suis né dans le quartier du port, jus: I was born in the harbour quarter, just behind the fish auction. My mother is Hamid's sister, so I grew up with his voice in my ears: from our kitchen, you could hear him singing at sea. At fourteen, I waited for him on the quay every morning for a month: “Take me on the Bahja.” On the thirty-first morning, he said yes. To shut me up, I think.
textes.Je suis né dans un bureau, citoyen. Enfi: I was born in an office, citizen. Well, nearly: my father was a court clerk, my mother a copyist, and we lived above the port archives. I learned to read in the tax registers. At six, I was stamping my parents' letters. At eight, I was demanding a tax on sweets from them. They found it adorable. They laughed less at twelve.
textes.Je suis né dans un logis à côté de la cl: I was born in a lodging right next to the bell, and I grew up on the knees of my grandfather, Yann-le-Borgne. One eye short, a thousand stories over. Every evening he told the shipwreck the way Loïc, the cabin boy of the Léviathan, had seen it. Word for word. Me, I changed a few words. For better ones.
textes.Je suis né dans un port du nord, gris, f: I was born in a port up north, grey, cold, full of herring. My grandfather, Captain Sel, raised me. Broke, toothless, magnificent. Every evening, he told me about Tazira: the blue boats, the caves, and “the keepsake” he'd left there. He died when I was twelve. He left me a tricorn that was too big. Ha! I grew into it.
textes.Je suis né dans un tourbillon, une nuit: I was born in a whirlpool, one night when the whale swam over the dome. Or on a Tuesday, in the green house in the third quarter. Both are true; the first is prettier. My mother collected everything the sea dropped against the dome. And I listened to what those things had to say.
textes.Je suis né dans un très grand manoir, de: I was born in a very large manor, on the other side of the seas, where it rained even in the corridors. My great-grandfather minted his own gold coins, with his profile on them: a magnificent nose. As a child, I was forbidden to touch the display cases. So I pressed my nose to the glass, and the butler came along behind me with a cloth. All my life, my dear, I have wanted to touch.
textes.Je suis né dans une boutique de brocante: I was born in a junk shop, under a bridge, in a big city where it rained all the time. My father bought everything people brought him: clocks without hands, umbrellas without cloth, three-legged chairs. He used to say: “Everything has a price, Isaac. Even nothing.” At six, I could tell a silver spoon by ear. Ding. Real.
textes.Je suis né dans une cabane au bord du la: I was born in a hut by the lake. At six, I was fishing on the jetty with my bucket and my little rod. A giant frog came out of the water and swallowed me, rod, bucket and all. Three seconds of darkness and drool. It spat me back out onto the jetty. I kept the rod. The bucket, it kept. I saw it again, years later, on its head.
textes.Je suis né dans une cuisine, sous la tab: I was born in a kitchen, under the pastry table. My grandmother Rosalie made soup for the whole village, in a pot so big you could have boiled a rowing boat in it. At five, I was tasting her sauces. At six, I was criticising them. At seven, I was ruining them. She used to say: “Messing up is the first ingredient.” I put in plenty.
textes.Je suis né dans une famille très calme,: I was born into a very quiet family, where we ate without making any noise with our cutlery. My mother cut my hair with a pudding bowl. I was a good boy. Until I was fifteen. That day, I heard a drum kit through an open window. I stood under the window for three hours. I shaved off the bowl cut that very evening.
textes.Je suis né dans une forge. Ma mère souff: I was born in a forge. My mother blew on the fire, my father hammered the iron. Me, I hammer the iron AND the people who don't pay.
textes.Je suis né dans une maison collée au rem: I was born in a house up against the north rampart. My father was a guard, my grandfather too. At eighteen, I took up the halberd. Thirty years of rampart, wind and gargoyles. I was a good guard. Not a talker. The gargoyles talked enough for two: they screech when they dive.
textes.Je suis né dans une maison de la Basse-V: I was born in a house in the Lower Town, the seventh of nine children. At twelve, I was sent to the Forge Cathedral to sweep the ashes of the Ember Heart. The old keeper back then, Brother Tison, hardly ever spoke. He gave me a broom and said: “Listen.” I listened. It took me a hundred years to hear.
textes.Je suis né dans une ville de gare, sur l: I was born in a railway town, on the mainland. Every morning, the seven o'clock train went past behind the school. I'd run alongside it, satchel on my back, trying to overtake it before the bridge. I never did. But once, the engine driver waved at me. That was worth every medal there is.
textes.Je suis né en bas, à Hautefond. Je m'app: I was born down below, in Hautefond. My name was Gustave Bouilloire, like my brother Firmin, of the Jolly Piston. When I came up here, I took my café's name. Cumulus floats better than Bouilloire. A kettle never floated anywhere.
textes.Je suis né ici, au village, entre les fi: I was born here, in the village, between my father's nets and my mother's songs. At six, I was banging on two coconuts and a conch shell, at the end of the beach, from morning till night. It was Nono who named me Mistral: he said I swept across the sand like the wind that knocks over parasols. The name stuck. So did the knocked-over parasols.
textes.Je suis né ici, dans la maison bleue au-: I was born here, in the blue house above the harbour. I've been a fisherman, then a waiter, then mayor. All three jobs are alike: you listen to people complain.
textes.Je suis né ici, à Port-Azur, au-dessus d: I was born here, in Port-Azur, above a rope shop. At seven, I was already selling shells to tourists, on a towel, at the end of the quay. “Caught by a real pirate!” The pirate was me, with a patch over one eye and a moustache drawn on with burnt cork. I sold everything on the first day. I knew I was made for business.
textes.Je suis né il y a neuf cent quatre-vingt: I was born nine hundred and eighty-seven springs ago, in a house that no longer exists, on a branch that has since fallen. Back then, the village had only one walkway, made of vines. My mother carried me across it singing, so I wouldn't be afraid. I was afraid anyway. I still am, a little, as it happens.
textes.Je suis né il y a quatre-vingt-un ans, ç: I was born eighty-one years ago, that's seven in Lumen years. Mum says I'm the only baby in Astralys who laughed before crying. Dad says I played my first prank at three months: I hid my dummy in Tempo's pocket. He found it exactly on the hour. He didn't think it was funny. I did.
textes.Je suis né il y a si longtemps que le vo: I was born so long ago that the volcano was still tiny. Well, that's what I tell people. My mother was a weaver, my father a bridge keeper. In the evening, they were too tired to tell me stories. So I made them up myself, and told them to them. They fell asleep. I took it as a compliment.
textes.Je suis né il y a trois siècles, au pied: I was born three centuries ago, at the foot of the Mother Tree. I walked at two, and I've never really stopped. My mother used to say I was the only child who could get lost in a round room. She exaggerated. A little. The room had corners.
textes.Je suis né il y a trois siècles, dans l': I was born three centuries ago, in my father's workshop, on a bed of wood shavings. He laid the planks of the walkways, and I counted them. By ten, I could tell by ear which plank was going to creak. My father said: “Then you'll never be bored.” He was right.
textes.Je suis né il y a trois siècles, et j'ai: I was born three centuries ago, and I ran before I could walk. My mother used to say I didn't have feet, just badly folded wings. At ten, I could run round the square faster than a leaf can fall. They gave me the messages to carry. They've never taken them back.
textes.Je suis né il y a trois siècles, la nuit: I was born three centuries ago, on the night of the storm, three minutes before my sister Lirael. I remind her every morning. That night, the forest's lights went away. My grandfather fished for light at dawn, with crystal nets. He said somebody would have to bring some back.
textes.Je suis né là où les cartes s'arrêtent,: I was born where the maps stop, in the white country. My mother carved houses out of ice, my father talked to storms. Winter lasted nine months; the other three, we waited for winter. As a child, I slept on a bearskin, and I could freeze a tear before it fell. Over there, nobody cries. It freezes your cheeks.
textes.Je suis né sous la montagne, comme mon p: I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father, and his father. All coal carriers. In my family, you learn to walk with a little sack on your back, for balance. My little brother Gunnar, I carried him in the sack. He says he remembers. He's lying: he was two.
I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father, and his father… you get the idea.

I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father… My parents wanted to call me Nori, after my great-uncle. He said no and took away one letter: “He'll earn others.” He taught me to write on a slab of obsidian, with a nail. My first letters were all back to front.

I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father… My father makes the city's lanterns. As a boy, I watched the terrace forges through the workshop window. The sparks rose like fireflies. I told myself: one day, I'll be the one making the sparks.

I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father… all of them coal-carriers. My big brother Dwalin carried me in his sack until I was two. I remember it: it smelled of soot and bread. I swore I'd have a job where you carry something else. I chose a shield.
textes.Je suis né sous le dôme de l'Observatoir: I was born under the dome of the Observatory, which my grandfather Évariste had built stone by stone. My cradle was next to the big telescope. Apparently I slept during the day and cried at night so they'd show me the moon. Nothing has changed. Except I don't cry any more. Hardly. When it's cloudy, a little.
textes.Je suis né sur la colline, derrière les: I was born on the hill, behind the olive trees. School was down at the harbour: an hour to go down, an hour to climb back up, in all weathers. My mother gave me a crust of bread and an apple for the road. By seven, I knew every pebble on that path by its first name. I was already a postman without knowing it.
textes.Je suis né sur le continent, dans une fa: I was born on the mainland, in a family of eleven children. Eleven! At the table, you had to be quick or clever. Me, I was both. At eight, my uncle put me behind the counter of his bistro, standing on a lemonade crate, and I served my first glass to an old sailor. He left me a coin and a piece of advice: “Smile, kid, it makes the lemonade taste better.”

I was born on the mainland, into a very serious family: my father counted coins at the bank, my mother counted cross-stitches. At our house, laughing at the table was rude. So I laughed under the table. With the dog. The dog thought I was hilarious. My first audience!
textes.Je suis né sur le continent, fils de gen: I was born on the mainland, a gendarme's son. My father polished his boots every evening, and I polished mine beside him. But I wanted to be a lifeguard at the municipal pool, with a whistle and a high chair. There was just one problem: in the water, I sank. Neatly, straight as a ramrod. But I sank.
textes.Je suis né sur le continent, premier de: I was born on the mainland, top of the class in arithmetic. For my tenth birthday, my father gave me a little black camera with a dial that squeaked. I finished my first film in one afternoon. Thirty-six photos: thirty-four of my thumb, one of my foot, and one of the cat. Blurry. I was delighted.
textes.Je suis né sur un bateau, jeune. Un vieu: I was born on a boat, kid. An old paddle steamer where they held dances, from port to port. My mother sold the tickets, my father played the accordion. I learned to dance before I could walk: a rolling deck trains your feet. That's why I never fall. Almost never.
textes.Je suis né sur un mât. Enfin, presque :: I was born on a mast. Well, nearly: in the crow's nest of a whaler, one misty morning. My mother was a lookout, my father too. They met by shouting “Land ho!” at the same time, each on their own ship. At home, we didn't say hello, we said “Nothing on the horizon”. It was tender, in our way.
textes.Je suis né sur un mât. Ma mère était vig: I was born on a mast. My mother was a lookout, my father too. They met by shouting “Land ho!” at the same time.
textes.Je suis né sur un quai de Tortuga, entre: I was born on a quay in Tortuga, between the ropes and the barrels. My father mended sails, my mother tore them up arguing with him. I learned to walk on the decks of boats at the quay, and to keep quiet in the house. I don't talk much. It's a childhood habit. Hm. Don't look at me like that.
textes.Je suis né sur une côte du continent où: I was born on a mainland coast where the waves are as tall as houses. My first board, at eight, was an old barn door. By ten, my hair was white with salt, and my mum said I looked like a sixty-year-old grandpa in shorts. I spent more time in the water than out of it. Cool childhood, right?
textes.Je suis né sur une île pleine de perroqu: I was born on an island full of parrots! Our house was under a big kapok tree, and every morning, three hundred birds woke us up squawking. My mother says I learned to whistle before I learned to cry. My first word was “Polly”. My second one too, but with a blue parrot's accent. I've never really lost it, that accent!
textes.Je suis né trois fois plus gros que les: I was born three times bigger than the other babies. The midwife had to call two neighbours to weigh me. My mother called me “my little one”. It made the whole neighbourhood laugh, and I didn't understand why. To me, I was little. It was the world that was too narrow.
textes.Je suis né trois minutes après ma sœur V: I was born three minutes after my sister Vespérine. She was frowning; I was already laughing. As a boy, I blew bubbles in my mother's watering can, in the soup, in my bath. My mother called me “my little soap bubble”. The whole neighbourhood picked it up. Then just “Bulle”. It stuck. Better than “soap”.
textes.Je suis né un jour 13 Ahau, un bon jour: I was born on a day 13 Ahau, a good day for scholars, so they say. As a little boy I counted everything: grains of maize, ants, the stars on one side of the sky. I always fell asleep around the three hundred and twelfth. My grandmother used to say: “The stars won't run away.” She was right. They're still there. So am I, for that matter. Almost always awake.
textes.Je suis né un jour de grand vent. Ma mèr: I was born on a very windy day. My mother says my first cry flew off on its own towards the sea, carried away by a gust. Ever since, I've been looking for the words the wind took from me. I write poems to try to catch them back. I've found a few. Many are still missing.

I was born on a very windy day. My mother says my first cry flew off all by itself towards the sea. Ever since, I've been looking for the words the wind took from me. I find one now and then. In a bag of flour.
textes.Je suis né un jour de tempête de cendre: I was born on an ash-storm day! Mum says I shouted louder than the wind. Grandpa Charbonnel says that's why I've got my sea legs. I'm ninety, in demon years. In normal years, I'm nine. It's the same, but smaller.
textes.Je suis né une nuit de tempête, pile qua: I was born on a stormy night, right when the bell was striking midnight. My dad says that's why I ring all the time. He fishes out at sea, my mum smokes the mackerel, and my grandad is Grégoire, the lookout. He taught me to count with boats. There weren't many going past, so I learned slowly.
textes.Je suis né à Haute-Souche, au nord du ro: I was born in Haute-Souche, in the north of the kingdom, where winter lasts six months and the snow comes up to the windows. My father felled fir trees, my mother counted the logs. In our house, no axe, no fire. At seven, I forged my first nail. Bent. My father hammered it above the door anyway.
textes.Je suis né à Hautefond, figurez-vous. À: I was born in Hautefond, would you believe. At six, at Rigging Harbour, I pressed my ear against the hull of a boat. I heard singing, very far off, under the water. Nobody believed me. At twenty, I took the Funicular with a suitcase full of empty notebooks. Today they're all full. I had to buy another suitcase.
textes.Je suis né à Hautefond. À six ans, au Po: I was born in Hautefond. At six, in Rigging Harbour, I pressed my ear against the hull of a boat. I heard singing, very far away, under the water. An immense voice, slow and deep. I ran to tell my mother. She laughed: “That's the boat creaking.” It wasn't the boat. Forty years later, I listen to it every evening. I wrote and told her. She wrote back: “You were right. Eat something.”
textes.Je suis né à Pointe-Grise, un port du ro: I was born in Pointe-Grise, a port in the kingdom so small it fitted on a postage stamp. My grandfather, an old sailor, told me about the southern islands and a city under the sea; my grandmother confiscated my socks before every trip to the beach. At eight, I drew my first map: her garden, with the path of every snail. She kept it all her life.
textes.Je suis né à Port-Coutelas, dans la case: I was born in Port-Coutelas, in the hut behind the well! Mum washes the shirts of all three crews on the big stones. When I was little, I played in the soap bubbles and counted the shirts. Once, I counted a hundred and twelve. Mum says that's why I count everything: shirts, waves, punches. The stars, I haven't finished.
textes.Je suis né à côté d'une enclume, {surnom: I was born next to an anvil, {surnom}, like all the Barbe-de-Fers. My father, Dorin, put a hammer in my hand before I had teeth. My first nail was as twisted as a pig's tail. He wore it on his belt for two hundred years. He said it was to remind himself to be patient.
textes.Je suis né à côté du Four Éternel, un ma: I was born next to the Eternal Oven, one baking morning. My mother says I was already as round as a brioche and smelled of butter. My father put me to bed in the kneading trough at six months to get me to sleep. I slept. I also ate a bit of dough. I've never stopped since. Sleeping, and eating dough.
textes.Je suis né à côté du terrain de jeu de b: I was born next to the ball court. My mother says I pushed a ball with my hip before I could walk. That's not quite true: I rolled onto it. But with style. My father made me a little rubber ball, the size of a mango. I slept with it. It was hard. I had bruises everywhere. I was happy.
textes.Je suis né à l'étage du Diable Repu, jus: I was born upstairs at the Diable Repu, right above the counter. My grandfather had opened the tavern, my father ran it. I learned to count with tankards and to talk with sailors. My first word was “more”. My father says it was for milk. My mother says it was for a story.
textes.Je suis né à minuit, pendant que tout le: I was born at midnight, while everyone was asleep. My mother says I didn't cry: I looked at the moon through the window. As a child, I slept during the day and played at night. My parents tried to change me. Then they gave up, and bought me a night light. I still have it.
textes.Je suis née au Bois-Doré, dans une maiso: I was born in Bois-Doré, in a round house resting on the third platform. My mother sang to make the leaves grow. Me, I climbed. At forty, I wanted to see over the mist, and I fell from the highest walkway. Aëlwen healed me. But just before I fell, I had seen a sail, far away.
textes.Je suis née au Camp des Fleurs, dans la: I was born in the Flower Camp, in the blue yurt. My mum says I was born among the buttercups — bouton-d'or, in French. I think she just said that because of the name. But it's pretty anyway.
textes.Je suis née au Cercle, une nuit de plein: I was born at the Circle, on a full-moon night. My mother, Aube, was its keeper, like my grandmother before her. She laid me in a basket at the foot of the smallest stone. I learned the names of the nine stones before I knew my own. I recited them in order, to fall asleep. I still do, some nights.
textes.Je suis née au Chaudron Fumant, dans la: I was born at the Smoking Cauldron, in the room above the kitchen. My grandmother Adélaïde ran the inn, and she's the one who lit the big cauldron at the back, on opening day. I learned to count with ladles, to read with the customers' slates, and to keep quiet with the wizards' secrets. Especially to keep quiet. Well, almost.
textes.Je suis née au Fondouk, dans la chambre: I was born at the Fondouk, in the room above the gate. Three hundred years my family has lodged merchants. As a girl, I'd run from one caravan trader to the next asking for a word in their language. By ten, I could say “hello” in eleven languages, and “you pay in advance” in fourteen. My mother thought that was the right proportion.
textes.Je suis née au Palais, un soir de grande: I was born in the Palace, on the night of a great eruption: my mother used to say the volcano had set off fireworks for me. As a little girl, I hated ceremonies. I'd hide in the great chandelier of the throne room, among the candles, and watch the courtiers looking for me. Asmodin always found me, by the smell of singed lace.
textes.Je suis née au cœur d'une fleur géante,: I was born in the heart of a giant flower, beside the waterfall of light. On the first day, I drank all its nectar. On the second, I sold half of it to a bumblebee for three grains of pollen. He never paid me, by the way. Petals and dew… you never forget your first customer.
textes.Je suis née au sol, petit, chez les loup: I was born on the ground, little one, among the tracker wolves. We had no house: we slept in the ferns of the misty forest, huddled together, and the mist was our blanket. I could read a track before I could say my own name. The children here think I'm the she-wolf of the legend. I say neither yes nor no. A track doesn't tell everything either.
I was born in the village, on the other island. In the evenings, I'd sit on the beach and watch the Swallow go by. From over there, you can see Port-Azur, all tiny, with its chimney smoke. I used to count it. Twelve, sometimes fifteen. I'd tell myself: fifteen kitchens, fifteen families, fifteen lives over there. And only one here. Mine.
textes.Je suis née au-dessus d'un atelier de ra: I was born above a radio workshop, in the Alleys. My father would listen to the sets crackle to find the fault. He used to tell me: “A city is the same. You have to listen to what crackles.” I never forgot it.
textes.Je suis née au-dessus de la boulangerie: I was born above the rabbits' bakery, in the warmth of my grandmother Luzerne's ovens. She was the one who made the mooncake. When Bondi was born, I was fourteen: I half raised him, between two batches, flour all over my ears. Our parents retired to the rabbits' vegetable garden. They grow Bondi's carrots now.
textes.Je suis née au-dessus de la pharmacie de: I was born above my father's pharmacy, on the mainland. At six I was sticking the labels on his jars, taking great care over the capital letters. And tasting everything that didn't have a skull on it. Liquorice, camomile, cod liver oil… That one, only once. Ah well, science has its limits.
textes.Je suis née avec des ailes trop grandes: I was born with wings too big for me. As a little girl, I got caught in curtains, doors, chimneys. Captain Charbonnel taught me to fly against the wind, on the jetty. Now I deliver to the whole city in one morning.

I was born with wings too big for me. As a little girl, I got caught in curtains, doors, chimneys. My mother had to widen every door in the house. My father said I was a kite with horns. I was ashamed of my wings. I hid them under a big coat. Even in summer. Especially in summer.
textes.Je suis née chez les bergers des hautes: I was born among the highland shepherds. At home, we tend sheep, we spin wool, and we don't take anything apart. Me, I took everything apart. At eight, I took apart the village grain mill. I put it back together with one piece left over. It still turns! At nine, they sent me to Cliquetis, to my uncle Ernest, Mum's brother.
textes.Je suis née d'une étincelle ! Une vraie: I was born from a spark! A real one! It fell from the waterfall of light into a rosebud, and pop, the rose burst, and bang, there I was, all pink too. Ever since, I can't keep still. See? Right now, I'm moving. Still. That's just how I'm made.
textes.Je suis née dans cette roulotte, ou plut: I was born in this caravan, or rather in its grandmother: the wheels have been changed four times, the door three, but it's the same one. My grandmother read coffee grounds, my mother read palms. Me, at six, I was already reading people's eyes. That's the easiest. People have very talkative eyes.
textes.Je suis née dans l'herboristerie, entre: I was born in the herb shop, between two shelves of jars. My grandmother Nanwë was healing the Bois-Doré long before me. At three, I could recognise the moss that closes wounds. At four, I tasted the one that makes you sneeze. I didn't stop all day.
textes.Je suis née dans la Basse-Ville, il y a: I was born in the Lower Town, eighty-five years ago. Back then, there was no Guild, just a big table in a barn, and the adventurers came back to it limping. I was the little girl who asked them to tell their tales. I never stopped.
textes.Je suis née dans la Fronde, dans les Str: I was born in the Fronde, in the Strata, under Hautefond. My father fixes the rails, my mother cuts the crystals. In the evenings they play in a band: him on drums, her on steam guitar. I slept my whole childhood with music above my cradle. Silence is the only thing that keeps me awake.

I was born in the Fronde, in the Strata, under the town. My parents repair rails by day and play music by night. I grew up between a forge and a drum kit. So noise doesn't scare me. Silence does, a little.
textes.Je suis née dans la Grande Forge, au pie: I was born in the Great Forge, at the foot of the anvil, on a day with a big order. My mother put down her hammer, brought me into the world, and picked it up again. Well, that's what she says. My grandmother says she did sit down for a while. In our family, we've been forging for nine generations. And we tell a good story.
textes.Je suis née dans la bergerie des Plume-d: I was born in the Plume-de-Suie sheepfold, on the east slope, above the terrace. My family have kept the ash goats forever. My first goat was called Pétarde. She ate my cradle, then my first braid. My mother said it was a sign of affection.
textes.Je suis née dans la capitainerie, et j'a: I was born in the harbour master's office, and I slept my first years under the chart table, while my mother governed above my head. The first word I could read was the name carved on the helm: Katell Kerhervé, the captain of the shipwreck. Every girl in the family learned to read with that name.
textes.Je suis née dans la cave de la Chope Ard: I was born in the cellar of the Blazing Mug, {surnom}, between two barrels of dark fizz! My mother brewed, my grandmother brewed, and on my naming day I grabbed a mug instead of my rattle. That's why they call me Full-Mug. I've still got the rattle. It's a bung now.
textes.Je suis née dans la maison de Grand-père: I was born in Grandpa Ébène's house, on the edge of the Grand Square. In the evenings, he told me stories by the fire, and I watched the shadows dance on the walls. I thought they were the characters from the stories. One day, I wanted to keep them. I understood you need light to keep shadows.
textes.Je suis née dans la maison derrière la G: I was born in the house behind the Great Forge. Mum says my first toy was a bolt, and my first word was “why”. I'm nine, or ninety in demon years. Pépin says ninety to sound big. I say nine, because it's more precise.
textes.Je suis née dans la maison-bulle d'à côt: I was born in the bubble house next to the Institute Gallery, with a porthole facing the Pool. As a little girl, I watched the old bathyscaphe's floodlights leave and come back. I counted its bubbles. On my sixteenth birthday, the old pilot took me aboard. He said: “You've been counting my bubbles for ten years. You already know everything.” He was right. Almost.
textes.Je suis née dans la première fleur d'Ygg: I was born in the first flower of Yggdrasil, one morning when there was still only the Tree, the clouds, and the sea far below. The flower opened, and there I was, my wings still wet. The first sound I heard was the wind in the leaves. I still listen to it.
textes.Je suis née dans le Grand-Chêne, il y a: I was born in the Great Oak, seventy-five years ago. Back then, there was just one hut and a rope ladder. My father built the staircase. My mother painted the first door. Blue.
textes.Je suis née dans le quartier des Artisan: I was born in the Artisans' Quarter, daughter of a violin maker who played nothing at all. He made violins, and I was the one who tried them out. At six, I played better than all his customers. He gave me the finest one, in ash wood, with hellhound-hair strings. I still have it. It sounds like a purring cat.
textes.Je suis née dans le souk, entre un sac d: I was born in the souk, between a sack of cumin and a sack of cinnamon. As a little girl, I slept there, and I dreamed in yellow. My mother would blindfold me and make me sniff: “This?” Clove! “And this?” Caraway! When I didn't get a single one wrong, I got a rose from the oued, from her garden. I got a lot of them. I wasn't often wrong.
textes.Je suis née dans les Galeries, au deuxiè: I was born in the Galleries, on the second floor. My father was a miner, my mother a lamp-tender. I did a bit of everything: apprentice at the Forge, railwaywoman, twenty years in the mine. One day the Guild asked me to become Dean. I said: “I'll think about it.” I thought for thirty seconds. That's long, for me.
textes.Je suis née dans les Gradins, au sixième: I was born in the Terraces, on the sixth floor, with a porthole that looked out over the Bathyscaphe Pool. As a little girl, I used to watch the old bathyscaphe go out and come back. I counted the bubbles it left behind. One thousand, two thousand, three thousand… My mother used to say: “She falls asleep counting bubbles.” That's not true. I never fell asleep until it was back up.
textes.Je suis née dans les Strates, dans une f: I was born in the Strata, into a family of Little Train railway folk. Very serious. Very punctual. One day, when I was fifteen, I heard Rivet banging on a boiler, on the other side of the Chasm. I crossed the bridge to see who was making that racket. I never went back.
textes.Je suis née dans les cuisines de la Gran: I was born in the kitchens of the Great Hall, {surnom}. My mother cooked for the old king and, for want of a cradle, she laid me in a nice clean copper cauldron, near the fire. My first memory is a ladle above my head. I thought it was the moon.
textes.Je suis née dans les cuisines du château: I was born in the castle kitchens. My mother was the cook there. I did my homework on a corner of the table, between the peelings and the pans. At nine, I found the treasury keys the Baron had been looking for for three days. They were in his hat. On his head.
textes.Je suis née dans un bouton de fleur qui: I was born in a flower bud that refused to open. Other fairies push their way out; I had to guess how to get out. I tried “please”, then “thank you”, then “hello”. It was “goodbye” that worked. Ever since, I've loved doors that make you think.
textes.Je suis née dans un moulin à vent, sur u: I was born in a windmill, on a pebble of the archipelago so small it doesn't even have a name. My father made flour, the wind turned the sails, and I turned with them. I knew all the winds by name before I knew my cousins. That's why I don't like pebbles: I was born on one, and it never moved!
textes.Je suis née dans un port du nord où tout: I was born in a northern port where everything smelled of herring, even the cradles. My father kept an inn. I served the sailors, listened to their stories and watched the sails. At fourteen, one night, Captain Sel's Murène was in port. I took my bundle and climbed aboard. Nobody saw me leave. Ha! Nobody has ever seen me leave.
textes.Je suis née dans une barque. Vraiment :: I was born in a rowing boat. Really: my mother was still fishing the day I arrived. She told the net: “Hang on a minute.” I let out my first cry in the middle of the Roads, and a shoal of mackerel fled. My father says that's why I shout so loud: to catch up with the mackerel.
textes.Je suis née dans une famille de cheminot: I was born into a family of railway workers on the Little Strata Train. At home, we ate at noon sharp, went to bed at nine, and said “clear track” instead of “good night”. I loved my family. But I had a song in my head that wouldn't fit into the timetable.
textes.Je suis née dans une famille de souffleu: I was born into a family of glassblowers. My parents spent their days making fire dance at the end of a pipe. Me, at three, I made it dance at the tips of my fingers. My mother quickly took down the curtains. My father bought a bucket. They kept it by my bed for ten years.
textes.Je suis née dans une maison de gardes, p: I was born in a guards' house, near the North Gate. My big brother Pyrus wanted to be a guard. I wanted to look after animals. I brought home anything with four legs and a snout: alley cats, a lava lizard, a crab that pinched. I hid the crab in Pyrus's helmet. He kept it for ten years.
textes.Je suis née dans une maison remplie de l: I was born in a house full of books, packed so tight you had to move them to sit down. My mother says my first word was “shh”. I think it was “page”. As a child, I read under the table, by the light of my own eyes: they're blue and they glow. It's handy for reading. Less so for hide-and-seek.
textes.Je suis née dans une noisette ! Zéphyr l: I was born in a hazelnut! Zéphyr had picked it up on an island down below, and he dropped it on the steps of the throne. The shell popped open, and I asked: “Are there any seeds around here?” That's my first memory. The trouble is, Zéphyr can't remember which island. So I don't know where I come from.
textes.Je suis née dans une pirogue, entre deux: I was born in a canoe, between two chinampas, among the flowers. My mother was a gardener, like her mother. At six, I planted my first willow at the corner of her floating garden. It was no taller than me. Today, it's the tallest willow on the lake. When I pass beneath it, I tell it: “My, you've grown.” It doesn't answer. It's shy.
textes.Je suis née dans une roulotte rouge, au: I was born in a red caravan, in the middle of a circus that toured the ports. My mother trained the performing dogs, my father juggled torches, and my grandmother Ottilie cooked for the whole troupe in a cauldron as big as a bathtub. Me, at five, I was already throwing spoons at apples. I always hit the apple. Never Grandma.
textes.Je suis née dans une ville du continent,: I was born in a mainland town, far from the sea, between a factory and a canal. I had three big brothers who ate everything. I baked cakes for them, and they ate them before they'd cooled, burning their tongues. I never found out whether my cakes were any good. They were hot, that's all I know.
textes.Je suis née derrière ce comptoir, comme: I was born behind this counter, like my mother, and her mother before her. The first of us was the cook on the Léviathan. When the ship ran aground, she relit her stove before anyone even knew where they were. “Nobody thinks straight on an empty stomach,” she used to say. We still say it.
textes.Je suis née en criant, et je n'ai jamais: I was born shouting, and I've never stopped. The midwife said to my mother: “That one, we'll hear from a long way off.” She was right. At school, they sat me at the back of the class. They could still hear me in the front row. And in the class next door. And sometimes at the port.
I was born shouting, and I've never stopped. At school they put me at the back of the class. They could still hear me. In the front row. And in the classroom next door.
textes.Je suis née entre deux caisses de maquer: I was born between two crates of mackerel, at the fish auction where my mother sold fish. She had the loudest voice in the port: when she shouted “Sardines!”, the seagulls went quiet. My father, I don't know. I learned to count with fish scales, and to fight with the auction cat, a big grey tom called Amiral.
textes.Je suis née grise. Peau couleur de cendr: I was born grey. Ash-coloured skin, ash-coloured hair, silver-coloured horns. In a city of red and purple demons, I stood out. My mother, a dressmaker, used to say: “A colour like that is a blank canvas. Dress it.” So I learned to dress other people. Me, I wear grey. It's restful.

I was born grey. Ash-coloured skin, ash-coloured hair, silver horns. My mother used to say: “A colour like that is a blank canvas. Dress it.” So I learned to dress everyone. Except me: I always wear grey. It's restful.
textes.Je suis née ici, au Dôme, comme mes élèv: I was born here, in the Dome, like my pupils. At eighteen, I took the Funicular to go and study in Hautefond. Coming out of the Column, I saw the sky for the first time. I sat down on the ground, in the middle of the Square, and cried for an hour. A young liftkeeper brought me a hot chocolate. She didn't ask me anything. I've never forgotten her.
textes.Je suis née ici, au village, dans la mai: I was born here, in the village, in the house with the green roof, right next to Yaya's. We were the only two girls on the street, so we became sisters, sort of. She danced, I watched her. Even as a little girl, I watched people more than I talked to them. I made frames with my fingers.
textes.Je suis née ici, dans les Ruelles, au-de: I was born here, in the Alleys, above a repair workshop. My father repaired radios. Today I repair a city. It's not so different: you have to listen for what crackles.
textes.Je suis née ici, derrière l'étal de mon: I was born here, behind my father's stall. He was a greengrocer and weighed cherries one by one. One by one. I learned to count with the stones, under the counter. At six, I gave change better than he did. He said I was stingy. I say exact.
textes.Je suis née ici, à Per-Hâpy, dans la pet: I was born here, in Per-Hâpy, in the little house behind the temple. My mother, Satrê, was a priestess of Rê. Every evening, I made her promise to wake me for the dawn. Every morning, I fell back asleep just as the sky was turning pale. So she would slip a date into my hand, and I'd wake up chewing, just in time to see Rê reborn.
textes.Je suis née il y a cent quatre-vingts an: I was born a hundred and eighty years ago, here, on Astralys. Three weeks early. My mother says I was already in a hurry. At two, I was running. At three, I was jumping off floating benches. At five, I fell off the Observatory bridge, and Aurore patched me up for the first time. Not the last. Far from it.
textes.Je suis née il y a trois siècles, dans u: I was born three centuries ago, in a house covered in honeysuckle. My mother was a flower-picker, and her mother too. At five, I knew which flower opens at dawn, which at noon, which only under the moon. I couldn't count to ten, but I could count petals.
textes.Je suis née il y a trois siècles, et mon: I was born three centuries ago, and my cradle sat under a beehive. My mother used to say the bees sang me my first lullaby. I was never stung as a child. Not once. The bees thought I was one of them. I think I count them as mine, too.
textes.Je suis née il y a trois siècles, quelqu: I was born three centuries ago, a few years before my sister Nessa. Our mother sang, our father beat time on the cooking pots. I sang before I could talk. My first song was a lullaby for Nessa. She started dancing instead of sleeping. That's never changed.
textes.Je suis née l'année de la grande crue !: I was born the year of the great flood! Mum says I shouted louder than the river. My dad, Sennefer, went away to the Field of Reeds when I was very little. I don't remember him. Mum says he laughed loudly and sang out of tune. I laugh loudly too! And I sing out of tune! So I look like him.
textes.Je suis née l'année où le volcan a couve: I was born the year the volcano covered the Lower Town in ash. Everyone was weeping over their gardens. My mother, though, planted a seed in the still-warm ash. It grew. My mother said: “Ash isn't the end. It's soil having a rest.” I've spent my life proving her right.
textes.Je suis née pendant un orage. La foudre: I was born during a thunderstorm. Lightning struck my mother's chimney. The fire never went out, and neither did I.
textes.Je suis née pendant un orage. La sage-fe: I was born during a thunderstorm. The midwife says I made a little spark when I sneezed. My mother says it was a coincidence. My hair says otherwise.
textes.Je suis née sous la montagne, comme mon: I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father… My family makes forge bellows, out of goatskin and ironwood. At ten, I already blew harder than my father. Today I work the bellows at Borin's forge, a bellows full of holes he refuses to mend. He says it's good for my lungs.

I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father… My father was a stonecutter. Our house looked onto the window of Ulfa's cellar. My whole childhood, I breathed in the smell of warm malt through the window. One day, I knocked on the cellar door and said: “I want to do that.”

I was born under the mountain, like my father, and his father… but me, it was the outside I loved. My mother is Bramm's sister. As a little girl, I'd sneak out through the Great Gate by slipping between my uncle's legs. He pretended not to see me. The only time his gate ever let anyone through without permission.
textes.Je suis née sous le dôme, comme tout le: I was born under the dome, like everyone. But one day I'll go up and see the sun. Promise.
textes.Je suis née sur Fil-d'Aube, l'arbre-mais: I was born in Fil-d'Aube, the tree-house where I still live. My mother was already weaving there. When I was five, a golden spider came down onto my hand and never left. My mother said: “She's chosen you.” We named her Embroiderer. Her great-great-granddaughters still spin for me.
textes.Je suis née sur la lande, dans une ferme: I was born on the moor, in a slate farmhouse, the eldest of eleven children. With eleven little ones, there's always a grazed knee, a cold, a tooth coming through. At eight, I was already looking after everyone with whatever I found in the hedgerows. The goats came to see me too. They'd queue at the door, I swear.
textes.Je suis née sur le pont d'un navire aux: I was born on the deck of a black-sailed ship, in the middle of the Harbour. My father, Captain Charbonnel, wanted to make a sailor of me. The first day, I was seasick. The second too. On the third, he set me down on the quay with a bag of island spices, saying: “That one will be a merchant.”
textes.Je suis née sur une petite île du nord,: I was born on a little northern island, where the rain falls sideways. My father fished sardines from a grey boat, not blue like here. I was untangling his nets before I could write my name. And while he hauled, I watched the big sails go by out at sea. I counted their cannons. Even then, {surnom}.
textes.Je suis née sur une île de soleil, {surn: I was born on an island of sunshine, {surnom}, with wheat fields that ran all the way down to the sea. My great-grandfather, King Atlas, carried me on his shoulders to watch the whales go by. That's him, the statue in the square. On the statue he looks stern. In life, he laughed all the time.
textes.Je suis née sur une île toute plate où i: I was born on a perfectly flat island with nothing on it: sand, coconut palms, and the sea all around. My mother mended nets, my father fished for lobster. For my fifth birthday, my father gave me a spiral shell, pink and white. He told me: “Listen, it's the sea talking to you.” I listened. I've never stopped.
textes.Je suis née trois minutes avant mon frèr: I was born three minutes before my twin brother, Bulle. My mother says that during those three minutes, I looked around very seriously, then Bulle arrived laughing. It's been like that ever since: I think, he laughs. We complement each other. That's a learned word for saying he wears me out.
textes.Je suis née un soir d'aurores, il y a qu: I was born on an aurora night, eighty-nine years ago. That's eight, in Lumen years. Mum says my first word was “why”. Dad says it was “oh”. The Elder says it was “why oh”. I don't remember. I was little. Why don't you remember when you're little?
textes.Je suis née un soir, dans la première sa: I was born one evening, in the first hall of the Tree, among the fireflies singing their song in light. They thought I was one of them. A very big one! For a whole year, I tried to light up, like them. I pushed and pushed… Nothing. Not one spark. I don't glow any more than you do, see!
textes.Je suis née une nuit d'orage, dans une m: I was born on a stormy night, in a house at the edge of the Fangs. My mother says that the moment I cried out, lightning struck the lightning rod. My father bought a second lightning rod. Then a third. Today our house has seven. It looks like a hedgehog.
textes.Je suis née à Port-Azur. Mon père travai: I was born in Port-Azur. My father worked at the ferry terminal; he brought me the travellers' torn envelopes. I steamed the stamps off over the kettle, burning my fingers, and kept them in an old account book. Mountains, queens, birds. I dreamed of the countries on them.
textes.Je suis née à bord de La Rose des Vents,: I was born aboard the Compass Rose, my parents' ship. They drew maps: every island, every reef, every bay in the archipelago. At seven, I held the lantern while they drew. One stormy night, the lantern went out. I lit it again with my hand. My father didn't say anything. He just wrote the date in the margin of his map.
textes.Je suis née à côté d'un four. Le four de: I was born next to an oven. My mother's oven, the one that sulks these days. Her name was Lindë, she baked the bread for the Bois-Doré, and she used to set me on the dough trough when I was little, like one more ball of dough. Apparently I rose very nicely.
textes.Je suis née à la forge, entre l'enclume: I was born at the forge, between the anvil and the bellows. At six, I lifted my mother's hammer. At six and one day, I dropped it on her foot. She laughed so loud the neighbours thought it was thunder and brought buckets. In our family, we laugh loud and strike true. Not always in that order.
I'm not fat. I'm BROAD. Big difference. And you're going to be FLAT, if you keep this up.
textes.Je suis passé à la teuf, un soir, avec G: I dropped by the party one evening, with Gaston on my shoulder. I took three steps, purely to measure the dance floor. Momo tells everyone I was dancing. It was cartography. Rhythmic, I admit.
textes.Je suis plongeuse. J'ai vu les ruines de: I'm a diver. I've seen the ruins of Atlantis from afar… One day, I'll have the courage to go closer.
textes.Je suis prête pour le moteur à cristal ?: Am I ready for the crystal engine?
textes.Je suis prête. Mes cheveux aussi. (Ils s: I'm ready. So is my hair. (It stands on end.) It's very ready, in fact.
textes.Je suis pêcheur, le matin. Le soir, je v: I'm a fisherman in the mornings. In the evenings I come here. The fish prefer it quiet.
textes.Je suis retourné la voir pour qu'elle aj: I went back to see her so she'd add a saddle to my horse. She sighed very loudly, and drew something. Scarlett says it's a little hat on the horse's head. Coralie says it's a little hat on the octopus's head. At least we agree on the hat. Hic! It's a start.
textes.Je suis sorti d'un nœud de racine. Pas d: I came out of a knot in a root. Not a flower. Not a drop. Not a spark. A knot. On the first day, I grumbled. It stuck. Fairies are born singing. I was born grumbling. It's more honest. Hmph.
textes.Je suis surtout ton seul client qui ne m: Mostly I'm your only customer who doesn't haggle.
I'm a technician at the Air Chimney. This morning, the air coming down smelled of rain. It's raining on the sea today. Down here, we find out through our noses.
textes.Je suis timide. Quand quelqu'un me parle: I'm shy. When someone talks to me, I look at my shoes. So I chose the bass: it's the instrument you hear without looking at the bassist. Everyone dances, and nobody looks at me. It's perfect.
textes.Je suis tombé de mon monocycle quatre fo: I fell off my unicycle four times this morning. Pastille sewed cushions into my trousers. Now I bounce when I fall. It's a new act.
textes.Je suis tombé du pont de lumière en marc: I fell off the bridge of light walking on my hands. Pixel got there before Aurore. She put a light plaster on me and spent ten minutes explaining why you don't walk on your hands on a bridge. I listened right to the end. Then I said thank you. She looked very surprised. So was I.
textes.Je suis tombée dans la fontaine avec ell: I fell into the fountain with her one morning. Well, she fell, and I jumped. She said it was to bless the water. So now, every time I drink from the fountain, I say thank you to Sister Pétronille. Mama says the water's always been good. I say it's even better now.
textes.Je suis toujours de bonne humeur. Je vis: I'm always in a good mood. I live in the smell of grilled sardines. It's impossible to be sad.
textes.Je suis toujours taché d'encre. Les doig: I'm always covered in ink. My fingers, my nose, my shirt. Capucine says I'm not a poet, I'm a walking ink blotter.
textes.Je suis toute seule au four, ce matin, e: I'm all alone at the oven this morning, and I still have three loaves to deliver: one to the Guild, for Mamie Rissole; one to the castle, for Aurore; one to the North Gate, for Gilles. If I leave the oven, everything burns. You wouldn't happen to…?
textes.Je suis triste comme une comète qui a pe: I'm as sad as a comet that lost its tail along the way. I'm looking for a rhyme for “Astralys”. “Police”? “Fleece”? “Cheese, please”? Nothing works. I'll call it something else. In poetry, I'm allowed.
textes.Je suis un aventurier, je viens de parto: I'm an adventurer, I come from everywhere.
textes.Je suis un baron très distrait. J'ai oub: I'm a very absent-minded baron. I've forgotten the name of my own town three times. But I've never forgotten the name of a single resident. That's what matters most, isn't it? Names are people.
textes.Je suis un bon chien. Je suis un bon chi: I'm a good dog. I'm a good dog. Say it. SAY IT. … Thank you. I'm a good dog.
I'm a guard. Not a mountain.
textes.Je suis un modèle de la Série Z. Le prem: I'm a Z Series model. The first android in Neopolis. When I arrived, there was only a pontoon and Mamie Kiku serving tea. I swept the city's first square metre. Then the second. I've kept going for forty years.
textes.Je suis un peu lent. Mireille dit que c': I am a little slow. Mireille says it is a flaw. Flora says it is a quality: “Plants are slow too.” I prefer Flora's opinion. It takes me less time to process.
I'm a bit lost right now.
textes.Je suis un peu sourd. Surtout quand ma p: I'm a little deaf. Especially when my granddaughter Céleste talks to me about my diet. But when Lili asks me to tell her about the sea, I hear everything. I tell her about the sea of my childhood, when I went down with my father. She closes her eyes. She can see it.
I'm a bit flat. Like a pancake. A praying pancake.
textes.Je suis un vieux modèle. On m'a oublié à: I'm an old model. They forgot me at this station six years ago. I'm waiting for someone to come and get me. I'm in no hurry.
textes.Je suis une chouette, mais je travaille: I'm an owl, but I work by day, so the post arrives when the village is awake. So I yawn a bit. A lot. The Post Office is at the top of the Mother Oak. I give my moon feathers to Pivoine, I bring Grelot the postcards from his aunt, and I dream of a golden acorn on my counter, to bring the post good luck. I know every door. And every secret. Hoo.
textes.Je suis une gardienne. Cet arbre, là, es: I am a guardian. This tree, right here, is an offshoot of the Mother Tree of Bois-Doré: a seed carried by the wind a thousand years ago. It is dying, {surnom}. Will you help me heal it? I need three things: a moonflower, water from the spring and a golden seed. Here, take this crystal vial: for the water.
I'm a hacker. But a nice one. They call it a “white hat”. I've got a green visor, but it's the same idea.
textes.Je suis venu ici il y a trente ans pour: I came here thirty years ago to map Balafre. One season, I thought. The first month, I lost three quills in the marsh, and a crab from Bone Beach pinched my toe so hard it no longer bends. The second month, I saw the skeletons of the Cursed Fort change places. The third, I understood: the island moves. I still haven't finished.
textes.Je suis venu ici pour cartographier la B: I came here to map Balafre. Thirty years ago. I still haven't finished. The island changes. Trees grow, rocks move. So do the skeletons.
textes.Je suis venu par le bateau de ligne pour: I came on the ferry to see the Column. It's taller than on the postcards.
textes.Je suis venue en pèlerinage de Port-Azur: I came on a pilgrimage from Port-Azur. Three days by boat, and it was worth it.
textes.Je suis venue pour un week-end. Ça fait: I came for a weekend. That was three weeks ago. I think the village has adopted me.
textes.Je suis veuve, et je m'y fais. Le soir,: I'm a widow, and I'm getting used to it. In the evenings, I read romance novels at the café. Nobody knows. Except Gisèle. And now you.
textes.Je suis {titre}. Un métier tranquille. L: My trade? {titre}. A peaceful job. Trees are never in a hurry.
textes.Je suis… à plat. Comme mes cheveux, pour: I'm… flat. Like my hair, for once.
textes.Je suivais une veine de fer, en montant,: I was following a vein of iron, up and up… and my head popped out in the middle of his guardhouse, between his two boots. I asked him if he'd moved house. He didn't answer. He put an enormous stone over the hole and sat on it. I went back down backwards. It took me all day.
textes.Je surveille les pirates depuis leur arr: I've been watching the pirates since they arrived. They're polite, they pay, they drink. That's what worries me: polite pirates are up to something.
textes.Je surveille. Il faut bien que quelqu'un: I'm keeping watch. Somebody has to.
textes.Je suspends les spaghettis un par un. Ça: I hang the spaghetti one by one. It takes me all day. I love it.
I brought you a mouse. An imaginary one. It's the thought that counts.
textes.Je t'ai chanté ta berceuse hier soir. Tu: I sang your lullaby last night. Didn't you hear it? The wind carried it off.
textes.Je t'ai confié ma vieille canne et tu as: I lent you my old rod and you pulled %d catch out of the water.
I lent you my old rod and you pulled %d catches out of the water.
textes.Je t'ai confié ma vieille canne, et tu n: I lent you my old rod, and you still haven't caught a thing with it.
textes.Je t'ai déjà tout raconté, {surnom}. Mai: I've already told you everything, {surnom}. But fine, since you insist:
I've already told you everything, {surnom}. But fine, since you insist:
textes.Je t'ai gardé une toute petite couronne,: I kept a teeny-tiny crown for you, just in case.
textes.Je t'ai payée ! Avec une énigme de premi: I paid you! With a top-quality riddle.
I've told you %d chapters of my life.
textes.Je t'ai raconté le début de mon histoire: I told you the beginning of my story.
textes.Je t'ai raconté tout ce que je sais sur: I've told you everything I know about %s.
textes.Je t'ai raconté toute ma vie. Ça, je ne: I told you my whole life. That, I don't forget.
textes.Je t'ai rapporté une pièce. Je ne sais p: I brought you a coin. I don't know where I found it. Yes, I do. But it's a dog secret.
textes.Je t'ai rapporté une pièce. Ne demande p: I brought you a coin. Don't ask where I found it. A rat never reveals his sources.
textes.Je t'ai vu arriver. De loin. De très loi: I saw you coming. From afar. From very far. Fil-de-Fer, lookout. I see everything. Almost everything. Except my glasses, when I'm looking for them.
textes.Je t'ai vu passer au-dessus de la Flèche: I saw you fly over the Spire! You did a loop! A loop! With MY machine! (She squeezes your hand so hard a blue spark jumps.) The Star Glider climbs up to six hundred metres, lands on Astralys and on the sky island, and makes almost no noise. Just a little “vzzz” when it's happy. Take care of it. Here, a spare astral crystal and a few washers: I have no use for them, they were lying in my screw box.
I saw you, kiddo. From the chain. You stopped them one by one, and all that time, the rest of us held arms, from the first floor all the way to the pavement. Forty arms. And yours. (She wraps a studded scarf around your neck.) That's the Boucan for you: nobody holds on alone, but together, we never let go. Here, the common fund voted a little bonus. Unanimously. Even Tapage.
textes.Je t'attendais, tu vois. Je reconnais to: I was waiting for you, you see. I know your step from the end of the quay.
textes.Je t'en ai déjà donné une ! Il ne m'en r: I've already given you one! I've only got three left, and the Captain keeps them for races won against the Albatross. In other words, for every race.
I'll give you a big one.
textes.Je t'en soufflerai d'autres, plus claire: I'll blow you some more. Clearer ones.
I'll write you another. In big letters.
I can hear you singing, Quark.
I'll send you the ointment with Léonce.
textes.Je t'offre un verre ? (3 pièces): Can I buy you a drink? (3 coins)
I've been cutting stones since I was a child. My mother used to say: a stone always tells the truth, you just have to know how to look at it.
textes.Je tape la grenouille avec ma masse ! Do: I'm hitting the frog with my mace! Gently! So it gives you back!
textes.Je te confie quelque chose. Je n'aime pa: I'll tell you something. I don't like dawn. I've been getting up before the sun for three centuries, and I dream of sleeping until noon, just once. But if I don't fish, Lirael's lanterns stay dark. So I get up. Don't tell Lirael. She'd think she had to take my place.
textes.Je te confie un secret, {surnom}. Il y a: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Ninety years ago I wove a cloak for Caelan. Night-coloured, with musical notes embroidered in gold thread. It's waiting in a chest, under my loom. I'll give it to him the day he finally dares. Not before. I'm more stubborn than he is. And on nights when the harp goes quiet, I don't sleep.
textes.Je te confie un secret. Chaque nuit, qua: I'll tell you a secret. Every night, when Caelan starts playing, I dim the lanterns around Fil-d'Aube, and I leave just one, a blue one, under Ilyria's window. I've been doing it for a hundred years. Ilyria doesn't know it's me. I like helping along stories that don't dare to end.
textes.Je te confie un secret. Haldir porte une: I'll tell you a secret. Haldir has been carrying a letter in his tunic for a hundred years. He comes running up to me, says “a message for you”, and runs off again. I know it's for me. I pretend I don't. I want him to dare. Ilyria says that sickness is catching, in the Bois-Doré.
textes.Je te confie une chose, {surnom}. Quand: I'll tell you something, {surnom}. When I fall asleep in the middle of a story, it isn't tiredness. It's the Mother Tree calling me. One day I'll sleep for good, and I'll be one of its leaves. I'm not afraid. I'm afraid of not finishing the story. So I'm telling them all to Nimiel, one by one. She thinks it's to entertain her.
textes.Je te confie une chose. La planche du jo: I'll tell you something. The plank from the day of the forty loaves: I kept it at home. I tell everyone it was perfect. That's not quite true: the day before, I'd seen a little crack in it, which I meant to fix the next day. Sylwen has never gone back up. It's my fault. I've never told her.
textes.Je te dis que la gelée est prête !: I'm telling you the jelly's ready!
textes.Je te dis un secret, {surnom}, mais tu d: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, but you don't tell, OK? Before the kite, I made another wish at the fountain. I asked for Daddy to lose his camera. So he'd look at my castles with his eyes, not with the machine. And he lost it, at the lookout. For real! So it's my fault. Daddy was so sad because of me. But he looked at my castles. With his eyes.
textes.Je te dis un secret, {surnom}. Le four n: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. The oven doesn't sulk. Sometimes I'm the one who gets it wrong. But it was my mother's oven. When I talk to it, when I say “it's sulking”, it's a bit like talking to her. So I'll keep saying it's the oven. And never mind my honour as a baker.
textes.Je te dis un secret, {surnom}. Quand Kik: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. When Kiki arrived from the jungle, he was homesick, it stuck out like a coconut. So one evening, I left my grandmother's recipe on the counter. In plain sight. And I went for a walk. Ever since, I've pretended I was robbed. Never tell him. Never.
textes.Je te dis un secret. Moi aussi, j'ai un: I'll tell you a secret. I have a message I've never delivered, too. For Nessa. Since the last Dawn festival. I carry it on me every day. Every time, I run right up to her, and then I run away again. I'm no better than Caelan. Don't tell him.
textes.Je te dis un truc, mais tu le gardes. J': I'll tell you something, but keep it to yourself. I'm scared of heights. Always have been. As a kid, I climbed with my eyes shut so I wouldn't see the drop. I build in the trees because I tell myself that, eventually, it'll pass. It's been fifteen years. It hasn't passed. But the huts stand up. That's something, {surnom}.
textes.Je te dis ça à toi, {surnom}, et à perso: I'm telling you this, {surnom}, and nobody else. Théo's kite — I made it myself, in my back room, with tissue paper and sticks. And the string… it was butcher's twine, for tying roasts. I'd run out of real string. If it flew away, it wasn't the wind. It was me. That's why I give him good prices. And shells.

I'm telling you this, {surnom}, and nobody else. At sixteen, I wanted to go down to fifteen metres to impress my mates. I came up too fast, head spinning, sky upside down. Since then, below ten metres, I'm scared. My starfish challenge is at six metres. On purpose. Big Kevin is scared of the deep.
textes.Je te fais confiance, petite. C'est plus: I trust you, lass. It's quicker.
textes.Je te l'avais dit ! Tu vois, Gaspard ? I: I told you so! See, Gaspard? He saw it too!
I told you, Joe. He remembers.
textes.Je te la raconte : elle est immense…: Let me describe it to you: it's immense…
textes.Je te les renvoie après, Victor ! Une gl: I'll send them back afterwards, Victor! Ice cream while you wait?
textes.Je te paie les couvercles, non ? On est: I pay you for the lids, don't I? We're partners.
textes.Je te porterais bien, mais j'ai un boucl: I'd carry you, but I've got a shield.
I'll take {objet}: {prix} in copper. Don't argue.
textes.Je te présente Bielle, mon majordome méc: Let me introduce Bielle, my mechanical butler! He's very polite. A bit too polite. Bielle, serve our guest some tea!
textes.Je te préviens : avec ta tête du jour, c: I'm warning you: with the face you're pulling today, it's full price.
textes.Je te prête ma place ! Attache ta ceintu: You can have my seat! Fasten your seatbelt!
I'm a voice-saver. It's more precise.
textes.Je te surveille. Tu cherches toujours un: I'm watching you. Still looking for another way? Not through my guardhouse. Never through my guardhouse.
I'll hold the note. As usual.
textes.Je tiens la corde. C'est mon travail. Le: I hold the rope. That's my job. The most important one at the Institute, if you ask me.
textes.Je tiens la réception de sept heures à v: I man the front desk from seven in the morning until eleven at night. The Lord in twelve makes me offers concerning my moustache. The newlyweds in seven have had difficult days; the management sympathises. Pauline gossips. Mademoiselle Clémence pays in paintings. And the professor covers the drawing-room carpet with sea charts. I walk around them.
textes.Je tiens le Grand Dictionnaire de la Cha: I keep the Great Dictionary of the Singer. Twelve hundred phrases noted down in twenty years. Three low notes, one high: “Hello, Dome.” Two long ones: “It's lovely up there.” One very low one that never ends: I believe it means “I'll come back.” My colleagues say I make it up. Perhaps. But she always comes back.
textes.Je tiens le tableau des cogneurs, au Crâ: I keep the brawlers' board at the Crâne Fendu: Gros-Louis of the Requin Borgne, the Mute of the Veuve Écarlate, and Belle-Humeur of the Morue Enragée. The three champions of the port. Beat all three, fair and square, and I'll sing your glory.
textes.Je tiens toute seule, regarde ! Sans les: I can balance all by myself, look! No hands!
textes.Je tiens un carnet que j'appelle « Les s: I keep a journal I call “Oscar's Spells”. Three hundred pages. The flying chair, Gérard the pigeon, the rain of buttons, the singing soup. He thinks I write down what he's broken. It's the list of spells nobody else has ever invented. I'll give it to him the day he gets his staff.
textes.Je tire ! Comme ça, Marcel, il a plus de: I'm shooting! That way, Marcel's got no balls left!
