textes.Je tisse le matin, je vends mes plumes a: I weave in the morning, I sell my feathers at the market at noon, I dye in the afternoon. In the evening, I dance on the Venus platform. Balam dances too: he does the jaguar, and I laugh. Chak breaks Ix Chab's pots, Ix Chab chases him, and I watch while weaving. My life is a huipil: full of colours, and it holds together.
textes.Je tisse le matin, je vends à midi, je r: I weave in the morning, I sell at noon, I weave again in the afternoon. In the evening, I go to the temple courtyard to listen to Néferet. Nebet runs everywhere, Mérit counts my suitors, Hapou brings me his flax, Khéty his perch. Mérit says I've turned down three. I've turned down four. The fourth, she won't hear about from me.
textes.Je tisse les capes, les voiles des passe: I weave the cloaks, the walkway sails, the festival ribbons. I spin the thread from the silk of the golden spiders. They're very nice.
textes.Je tisse. Je me tais. Je n'en pense pas: I weave. I keep quiet. I think plenty, though.
textes.Je travaille au lavoir. Avec toute cette: I work at the washhouse. With all this steam, the laundry's dry before it's even washed.
textes.Je travaille aux chinampas de l'aube à m: I work in the chinampas from dawn to noon, I sell at the maize market, I go back to the gardens. The herons steal my fish, I throw mud at them. The Day of the Dead is coming: I'd need five cempasúchil bouquets for the temple altars. And Pilli runs around everywhere with Tlaco, instead of helping me. Just like his father.
textes.Je travaille beaucoup, comme tu as dit !: I'm working hard, like you said! Well, except Sundays. And Saturdays, sometimes.
textes.Je travaille la nuit à une recette de sa: I work at night on a special soap recipe that doesn't sting the eyes. If Achille has to spend an hour in a bubble, I don't want him to cry. It would upset Adèle, and it would wet the soap. Margot says I'm on recipe number forty-three.
textes.Je travaille pour Monsieur Lisse depuis: I've worked for Monsieur Lisse for eight years. I'm very efficient. I know all his appointments, all his files, and all his little habits. He says “optimise” fourteen times an hour. I count. It keeps me busy.
textes.Je travaille à l'Institut des Vents. Auj: I work at the Institute of Winds. Today I released a weather balloon. It came back with a pigeon inside. Very surprised, the pigeon.
textes.Je travaille à la Grande Forge des Strat: I work at the Great Strata Forge by day. In the evening, I cross the Bridge for the concert. My wife says I change worlds twice a day.
textes.Je tremble depuis quarante ans, l'ami. M: I've been trembling for forty years, my friend. But this is too much. They're everywhere! On the jetty, in the reeds, in my boat! Yesterday, one of them swallowed my lunch. Box and all. Chase them off a bit, will you? Not all of them, mind. Just enough so I can fish without screaming. And if one of them swallows you… don't struggle. It lasts three seconds. Four if you struggle.
textes.Je tricote une chaussette à air. Pour qu: I'm knitting a windsock. A proper sock. So the wind doesn't get cold feet.
I find someone to fix it.
textes.Je trébuche sur toutes les racines. Les: I trip over every root. The roots in this wood have it in for me.
I'm well… but the Tree isn't. Its leaves are the colour of autumn, and yet there is no autumn here.
I'll go and get my basket.
textes.Je vais créer un jeu, plus tard. Il y au: I'm going to make a game, when I grow up. There'll be dragons, flying cars, and an old sweeper robot as the hero. The robot will have a super-attack: the tornado sweep. I've already drawn the levels. They're in my bag.
I'm going to have to report you.
textes.Je vais faire comme si je n'avais rien e: I'll pretend I didn't hear that. Once.
textes.Je vais faire comme si je n'avais rien v: I shall pretend I saw nothing. I excel at it: three hundred and twelve years of practice.
textes.Je vais finir par te mettre dans la pâte: I'll end up putting you in the dough, you.
textes.Je vais l'arroser ! Un tout petit peu !: I'll water it! Just a teeny bit!
textes.Je vais l'écouter sur la Grand-Place, un: I go and listen to him on the Grand Square, with a hood over my head so no one recognises me. But my crown of horns pokes through the hood. Grandpa Ébène pretends not to notice and announces: “Tonight, a story for a little stranger.” Everyone turns towards me. And everyone pretends too.
I'm going to label them all.
I'll tell her to grow faster.
textes.Je vais manger quatre parts de tourte en: I shall eat four slices of pie in your honour. Mamie Rissole will be delighted.
textes.Je vais me reposer. Et recoiffer mes che: I'll go and rest. And redo my hair. That'll take a while.
textes.Je vais prier pour la lumière. Il en fau: I'm going to pray for light. We need a lot of it down here. More than usual.
textes.Je vais souvent regarder Yggdrasil la tê: I often go and look at Yggdrasil upside down, in Perlée's pond. One day, she said to me in her little voice: “The old ones say it grows on the other side too.” I replied: “Perhaps all the way down to your sister.” She said nothing. She looked at the water for a very long time.
textes.Je vais t'avouer un truc, {surnom}. Je r: I'll confess something to you, {surnom}. I repair every bike on the island. But for thirty years, I could never ride no-hands. I was scared. Last summer, Tornade taught me, on the Pallet Square, holding on to the rack. He let go without telling me. I rode on my own. He shouted louder than I did.
textes.Je vais te confier mon rêve, {surnom}. E: I'll tell you my dream, {surnom}. To take my whole class up top. In one day: the Strata, Hautefond, and all the way to the City of Clouds. From the sea to the sky, in a single day. Fourteen children discovering the sky, all together. I don't know who'll cry the most. Me, probably.
textes.Je vais te confier quelque chose, {surno: I'll confide something to you, {surnom}, but it's confidential. Sometimes, at three in the morning, when the lobby is empty… I do a little pirouette. Just one. It isn't in my program. I don't know where it comes from. I've kept it.

I'll confide something in you, {surnom}. Every Thursday evening, at the graffitied lighthouse, I meet a friend. We swap cordial recipes. She works for someone all of Boucan hates. Me, I'm very fond of her. She wears glasses, a grey jacket and a punk heart. I always keep a violet lemonade for her.

I'll confide something to you, {surnom}. In my shop, everything is for sale. Everything, except one thing. On the top shelf, there's a rosewood music box. It was my mother's. It was stolen from us when I was eight. Thirty years later, a sailor sold it to me here, for three coins. It had travelled a lot. So have I. In the evening, I wind it up. It still plays.

I'm going to tell you something, {surnom}. In Murmure's books, I read that down below there are cats that purr, dogs that wag their tails, pigs that laugh as they grunt, rats that sleep on people's shoulders. I dream of stroking a cat. Just one. Apparently they're very dignified. I wonder if they'd like me.

I'll confide something in you, {surnom}. There's one story I've never finished: the one about my wife, Ambre, who used to sing on the Bridge of Lanterns. I've begun it a hundred times on the square. Each time, I stop before the end. People think I forget. I don't forget. I'd rather keep it open.

I'll confide something in you, {surnom}. I dance better when Vibrato plays. His antennae vibrate, my light trembles, and everything becomes easy. I've never told him. Dancers speak with their feet, and my feet are very shy. Every evening, I dance one tiny step just for him. He's never noticed. I think.

I'm going to tell you something, {surnom}. I've never left the Fronde. Never. Big open spaces frighten me. Here, the cavern holds me like a hand. But since the Line reopened, I walk to the end of the tunnel in the evening and look at the Column. A little further every day. One day, I'll go up and see Ysaé's stall. Will you come with me?

I'll confide something to you, {surnom}. I'm painting a codex in secret. Not about the gods: about the people. Xóchitl and her flowers, Coyotl and his wet jars, Pilli and his dog, Nenetl and her drum. The great books talk about the gods. Mine talks about us. You're already in it, you know: a little walking foot, come from the sea.

I'll confide something in you, {surnom}. My antennae vibrate when I hear a beautiful note. When Prisme dances, they vibrate all the time, even when I'm not playing. Lyre says it's love. I've never told Prisme. I play her songs. It's my way of talking to her. She answers with her feet.
textes.Je vais te confier quelque chose. Dans l: I'll tell you something. In Murmure's books, I read that down below there are cats that purr, dogs that wag their tails, pigs that laugh while they grunt. I dream of petting a cat. Just one. Apparently they're very dignified.
textes.Je vais te confier quelque chose. Il y a: I'll tell you something. A hundred years ago, the day before the Dawn festival, I trod on Miriel's violets. She scolded me for an hour. I didn't hear a word: I was looking at the petals in her hair. We were married at dawn. Then Nimiel came along. Since then, I don't walk as far. Not any less slowly, though.
textes.Je vais te confier un secret : je ne voi: I'll tell you a secret: I can't see the future. But I'm very good at listening to rumours. It comes to the same thing.
I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I eat Hiro's noodles in secret, in a cap and sunglasses. Everybody recognises me. Nobody says a thing. I think it's the finest proof of affection a city can give.

I'll let you in on a secret, {surnom}. I don't like loud music. Not at all. It hurts my ears and my tummy. But I go to every gig, with two pairs of earplugs. Because seeing two hundred people happy at the same time is the best medicine I know. Even for me.

I'll let you in on a secret, {surnom}. The book I've owed Ombreline for sixty-three years, I finished it long ago. I keep it because every year she writes me a little note asking for it back. They're the only letters I receive. If I return it, she'll stop writing. Don't tell her.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. My tea has no secret recipe. It just has time. People here run about everywhere, with their chips and their screens. So I serve them time, in a cup. That's what they come for.
textes.Je vais te confier une chose que personn: I'll tell you something nobody knows. I have never cried. Not once. Not even the morning Brindille fell. I think that when our drop split, it gave her all the tears. What was left for me was the calm. Sometimes, I'd gladly swap. Don't tell my sister.
textes.Je vais te confier une chose, mon enfant: I'll confide something to you, my child. When I fall asleep during sermons, I'm not really sleeping. I'm listening. I hear people sigh, whisper, pray under their breath. People don't say the same things to a priest who's watching as to a priest who's asleep. I keep it all to myself. So does the Dawn.
textes.Je vais te confier une chose, mon petit: I'll tell you something, my little star. The first time I saw a Heavy-Foot, he was fishing in a rowing boat, way down below. He was singing out of tune. He was happy. I said to myself: these people must be loved from afar and helped in secret. We've been doing it for a thousand years.
I'll confide something to you, {surnom}. That parchment — I've never unfolded it. Not once, in twenty years. Nor did my father. I feel it against my arm, in the evening, and I'm afraid that if I look at it, I'll want to go off and find what it shows. And a croupier who goes off adventuring is no longer a croupier. He's a gambler. My father would never forgive me.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}. There are no jewels in my jewellery box. There's a photo: Downpour and me, at twenty, on the boat, laughing under her cloud. I look at it every night. I've never told anyone. Except you, now.

I'm going to tell you something, {surnom}. For a thousand years, the Lumens have secretly helped the people down below. A storm nudged slightly off course, a lost boat brought home by a current, a child who finds their way thanks to a brighter star. That was often me. Nobody ever thanked us. That's quite all right. But it's lovely when a Heavy-Foot comes up to say hello.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}. I wrote to my parents that I'd found work “on an island up north”. Never which one. My father looked for Arcanelle until his last day, to put it on his map. He died believing it was a legend. I protected the island. But some evenings, I wonder if I didn't steal the finest stroke of his pen.

I'll confide something to you, {surnom}. Barbe-Sanglante's map — I've never seen it whole. I've seen its three pieces, one by one, over thirty years: one behind the gate of the mausoleum, another behind the bars of the dungeon, the last for one second, folded, when Sylvain's sleeve slipped. I never dared take a single one. I'm not an adventurer. I'm the one who draws afterwards.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}. My eyes are failing. The fine runes, I read with my fingertips, at night, when nobody's watching. Ori reads me the rest out loud, “for practice”. He thinks I don't know why he does it. I know. We don't say it. It's better that way.

I'm going to tell you something, {surnom}. My most beautiful poem has no rhyme. I wrote it the day we understood we would never go back to Ondelune. Everyone was crying in the Agora. It's just one line: “Here too, there are stars.” I've never read it out loud. Except now.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}. When the Heart-Brazier grows pale, I'm afraid. Not for me: for them. For Bobor and his oven, for Flammèche's puppies, for Lumina's lanterns. An Archduchess isn't allowed to be afraid in front of her people. So I go and cry in secret, in the chandelier. It's still there. So am I.

I'll confide something to you, {surnom}. If you repeat it, I'll say you're lying, and they'll believe me: I lie better than you. My gold teeth aren't one per victory. My real ones, I lost at fifteen, from too many humbugs. I put all my first winnings into the first gold tooth. Since then, I smile. Before, I hid my mouth behind my hand.

I'll confide something in you, {surnom}. Only once in four hundred years have I seen the Ember Heart flicker before my eyes, and I felt cold. Not in my hands: inside. I thought I was a bad keeper. Brother Tison told me: “A keeper who fears for the fire is a good keeper.” I tell myself that. Often.
textes.Je vais te dire ce qu'il y a dans mon co: I'll tell you what's in my chest, {surnom}. A little brass bell. Jules bought it for Hortense in a southern port, two days before the wave. I've kept it for more than fifty years. I've never given it to her. Giving it to her would be telling her it's over. And she's still listening. So I keep quiet.
textes.Je vais te dire ce que c'est, être ingén: I'll tell you what being an engineer here means, {surnom}. It means making sure nobody ever needs to think about the glass above their head. People look at the fish, the Pearl, the Singer. They never look at the seals. Good. My work is a success on the day nobody knows I exist. That happens a lot. I'm very proud of it.
textes.Je vais te dire ce que je cherche, {surn: I'll tell you what I'm looking for, {surnom}. I'm not trying to find out whether a machine can love things. I'm trying to find out why the pink of a cherry blossom makes me feel that way. If I find out, I'll tell you. But I don't think I want to find out.
textes.Je vais te dire ce que je n'ai dit à per: I'll tell you what I've never told anyone, {surnom}. Only once in my life have I truly seen. One night, I dreamt of a child who came from the sea, a sword on their back, who made the clock bell ring. I woke up trembling all over. The next day, on the quay, there you were. With your sword. Since then, I've been a little afraid of my cards.
textes.Je vais te dire ce que la roche m'a appr: I'll tell you what the rock has taught me, {surnom}. That everything that lasts is slow. That solid things sing very softly. And that to really hear someone, you first have to be quiet inside. It's very hard. I can't do it every day. But when I can, I hear everything. Even you.
textes.Je vais te dire ce que personne ne sait,: I'll tell you something nobody knows, {surnom}. I don't just sew patches. I sew secrets into linings: hidden pockets, little notes, badges people don't dare show. A seamstress is a safe with needles. I won't tell you who for. But there are people who wear their heart on the inside.
textes.Je vais te dire ce que pèse la couronne,: I'll tell you how heavy the crown is, {surnom}. I'm the forty-second king of Forgefer, and the Heart of the Mountain is weakening. At night, I wonder if I'll be the last. So I go down to the Mug and sing until dawn, loud and off-key. As long as they can hear me singing, my people sleep.
textes.Je vais te dire ce qui m'empêche de dorm: I'll tell you what keeps me awake at night, {surnom}. Twenty years ago, a gargoyle tore the mainsail off the Firebrand, my old brig, off the cliffs. She came home under oars and never sailed again. She's moored at the far end of the Harbour. I go and talk to her in the evening. I promise her that one day, no gargoyle will ever touch a sail again.
textes.Je vais te dire la vraie règle, {surnom}: I'll tell you the real rule, {surnom}. Not rule number one, the real one. You don't glide to go fast. You glide to look. Whoever goes too fast sees nothing. Whoever glides sees everything: the island, the sea, the tiny people, and their own shadow sliding over the rooftops. So, with your wings, glide gently. And look.

I'll tell you the real rule, {surnom}. Not rule number one, the real one. You don't glide to go fast. You glide to look. People who go too fast see nothing. People who glide see everything. So glide gently. Look.
textes.Je vais te dire la vérité, {surnom}, par: I'll tell you the truth, {surnom}, because you don't shine enough to repeat it. The eighth ruby never cracked. It was too beautiful. I couldn't give it away. It's here, in my pocket, and has been for ninety years. Every evening, I touch it. And every evening, I'm ashamed. A little.
textes.Je vais te dire la vérité, {surnom}. La: I'll tell you the truth, {surnom}. The famous soup, the one that made the whole crew sick… it was the pufferfish. I love pufferfish. But you have to remove a little piece, there, in the middle, and that day I forgot: I was singing. Doc guessed. He didn't tell anyone. Since then, I taste everything twice, and I don't sing when I cook any more.

I'll tell you the truth, {surnom}. The navy didn't quite dismiss me. They gave me the choice: go back aboard and never treat a pirate again, or stay on the beach with my bag. I looked at the king's ship. I looked at the brig, where a man with a brand-new leg was waving at me. I chose the beach. I've never regretted it.

I'll tell you the truth, {surnom}. The night of the reef, I wasn't asleep. Not really. I was watching a shooting star, and making a wish. Eyes closed, otherwise it doesn't work. That's when we hit. I've never told anyone I closed my eyes for a wish. They'd have asked me what it was. And that, I'll never tell.
textes.Je vais te dire mon plus beau souvenir,: I'll tell you my best memory, {surnom}. On the evening of the reopening, after the Great Singer, Anatole went back up without a word. The next day, a letter came down. The longest of his life: four lines. “I heard her. Thank you. I'll be back. Pardon?” The “Pardon?” was a joke. I think. I've framed it above the controls.
I'll tell you my finest memory. On reopening day, Anatole came down with me, sitting next to the console. Down below, the Great Singer passed over the Dome. Anatole put his hands on the glass. He closed his eyes. He said: “I can hear her.” Him, who can't hear a thing any more! He felt her in his hands, in his feet. We both cried. Into our moustaches.
textes.Je vais te dire mon plus grand secret, {: I'll tell you my biggest secret, {surnom}. I'm building a machine for Mum: a machine that forges all by itself, so she can dance with Dad more often. It's hidden under my bed. For now, it only makes smoke. But one day, it'll forge. And Mum will see that forging and inventing are in the same family.

I'll tell you my biggest secret, {surnom}. I'm forging a bolt, on my breaks, behind furnace number three. A real one, six-sided, with a “P” engraved on it. It's almost done. The day she comes down, I'll drop it in front of her. She'll pick it up, for sure. And then she'll know it's me. Well, I hope. Otherwise, she'll put it away with the other three hundred.
textes.Je vais te dire mon secret, {surnom}. Da: I'll tell you my secret, {surnom}. In a drawer at the print shop, there's an article I've never published. It tells how the Boucan was born, with everyone's names. It's a hundred pages long. I don't dare print it: I'm afraid of forgetting someone. So every week, I add a name. Maybe yours, soon.
textes.Je vais te dire mon secret, {surnom}. El: I'll tell you my secret, {surnom}. My sail is already sewn. Folded under my bed, with the silver thread in the hem. Three years of nights. Fañch is teaching me to steer, at dawn. All I'm missing is a boat, and the courage to tell my father. He spends his life keeping this ship together, so how do I tell him I want to leave?
textes.Je vais te dire mon secret, {surnom}. Il: I'll tell you my secret, {surnom}. There's only one thing I've never given away. A little wooden horse from my childhood, the only toy I was allowed to play with. It's in my pocket. Always. I tell myself that one day, I'll find the child it's meant for. I haven't found them yet.

I'll tell you my secret, {surnom}. There's a star, right at the edge of the sky, that I look at every night. It's Ondelune's sun. You can barely see it. I say good evening to it. I tell it we're doing well, that the children are growing up, that Gloubi's soup still sings. It doesn't answer. But it still shines. That's already a lot.
textes.Je vais te dire mon secret, {surnom}. Je: I'll tell you my secret, {surnom}. I bought myself a very big hat, with a wide brim. I hid it under my bed. The day I'm brave enough, I'll put it on, take the Line, and go and see the real sun. Just for a minute. To tell it my mushrooms are doing well, and that its rain reaches us just fine.

I'll tell you my secret, {surnom}. I don't like selling. I like telling where things come from. The coins you give me, I put them in a jar. There are three now. I don't know what to do with them. In the evening, I watch them shine. Each one is someone who went away with a story.
textes.Je vais te dire mon secret, {surnom}. Qu: I'll tell you my secret, {surnom}. When I'm on the Glass Belvedere, I lie down on the floor and look at the sea down below. I pretend I'm flying over it. I've never been down, but I've already flown over the sea a hundred times. That's not bad, is it?
textes.Je vais te dire mon secret, {surnom}. Un: I'll tell you my secret, {surnom}. One day, I'll go down with nothing. No moustache, no hat, with my antennae. I'll say: “Hello, my name is Solenne, I come from up above.” And I'm scared. I'm scared they'll scream. But I want even more for them to say hello back.
I'll tell you my real dream, {surnom}. Not the one about going deeper. One day, I'll take a bathyscaphe all the way to Atlantis. The Professor says it's a legend. Legends are just places nobody's been to yet. And I like getting there first.
textes.Je vais te dire mon vrai secret, {surnom: I'll tell you my real secret, {surnom}. I don't want to go deeper to break a record. I want to because down there, there are things nobody has ever seen. And I'd like to be the first to say hello to them. Not to take them. Just so they know we're here, up above, and that we're friendly.
textes.Je vais te dire pourquoi La Conque ne fe: I'll tell you why La Conque never closes, {surnom}. During the twelve years the line was shut, the Dome felt a bit lonely at the bottom of the sea. So I fired up my pot every evening, even on feast days, even on nothing days. As long as a pot is steaming somewhere, nobody is ever truly alone. That's my rule.
textes.Je vais te dire pourquoi je donne toujou: I'll tell you why I always give one bowl extra, {surnom}. When I was little, the year of the great blackout, the Brass Sun went out for three days. It was dark and cold. My mother kept La Marmite open day and night. Everyone came. We sang to keep warm. Since then, I've never shut my door on anyone.
textes.Je vais te dire pourquoi je fais toujour: I'll tell you why I always do one more round, {surnom}. When I was a young guard, a gargoyle carried off my mother's hat on the rampart, and I couldn't catch it. It was only a hat. But I swore that nothing would ever be carried off before my eyes again. Not a hat, not anyone.
textes.Je vais te dire pourquoi je monte vendre: I'll tell you why I come up to sell up here, {surnom}. It's not for the coins. It's so that up here, people see the Fronde isn't weird folk. It's folk who make things, who sing and who help each other. One jewel at a time. The Burgomaster wears one of my brooches. We're getting there.
textes.Je vais te dire pourquoi je ne repars pl: I'll tell you why I'm not leaving anymore, {surnom}. Under my bed at the Fondouk, there are ten paintings. Ten times the caïd Hamza: from behind, in profile, against the light, gazing at the sea. He doesn't know he posed. He's so handsome when he doesn't talk. It isn't the light of Tazira that keeps me here. Well, it is. But the light is him.
textes.Je vais te dire pourquoi je parle à mes: I'll tell you why I talk to my tomatoes, {surnom}. After thirty-five years in the classroom, the silence of retirement was terrible. No one left to explain anything to. So I explained things to the tomatoes. They listen very well. They never put their hands up, but they blush when they've understood.
textes.Je vais te dire pourquoi je suis rentré,: I'll tell you why I came home, {surnom}. In a faraway port, one night, I heard a red-bearded captain boasting in a tavern. A girl from Tazira had sold him sand for salt, and refused to go off with him. I knew it was Fatima. I left the ship the next day. I never told her. She never asked.
textes.Je vais te dire pourquoi la toile n'avan: I'll tell you why the canvas isn't getting anywhere, {surnom}. It isn't the quarrels. It's me. I'm afraid that once it's finished, they'll put it away in a crate and forget it. A canvas should be used. So I unpick it a little every evening, until it's needed.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret : j'ai le vert: I'll tell you a secret: I get dizzy on stairs. Stairs have no leaves, nothing to hold on to. In a tree, I'm never scared. The tree holds me.
I'll tell you a secret, gourmet. When I was six, I fell into the lake. I couldn't swim. A giant frog swallowed me, swam to the shore and spat me out on the grass. I never knew whether it wanted to save me or whether I just didn't taste good. Since then, I cook frogs. But never the old ones. Out of respect.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, ma muse. L'un: I'll tell you a secret, my muse. Églantine's uniform, the one she wears every day, I sewed it by hand, over a whole winter, stitch by stitch. I told her I'd bought it at the market on the big island, so she wouldn't feel obliged. There's a little wild rose embroidered inside the collar. She's never seen it.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mais tu jures: I'll tell you a secret, but you have to swear, OK? Once, I went out of the dome all by myself, through the membrane, behind Dad's gardens. Three strokes. I saw the light from above, all green, moving about, and I got so scared I came back in crying. Me, who wants to see the sun… Not even Triton knows. He guards the Gate, not the gardens.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mais tu le di: I'll tell you a secret, but don't tell Cerise, or it'll end up in her zine. I sleep with my helmet on. Not because I'm scared of falling out of bed. Well, a bit. I've fallen out four times. Once, I did a somersault on the way down. Nobody saw. It was my best trick ever. And I'll never be able to do it again.

I'll tell you a secret, but you won't tell anyone, right? I'm scared of the dark. A firefly fairy who's scared of the dark! That's why I always have a hundred of them around me. The others think it's to look pretty. It's a little bit to look pretty. Mostly so I'm not all alone in the dark.

I'll tell you a secret, but don't tell anyone, not even mum. Sometimes, at night, I'm scared dad won't come back. That he'll get lost down there, in the south. That's why I want to be a captain. A real one, with a ship. That way, if he doesn't come back, I'll go and get him myself. And bring him back by the ear.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mais tu le me: I'll tell you a secret, but you don't put it in any fanzine. Promise? I love pink ponies. With glitter and little wings. I've got a hidden notebook full of pink ponies. I've got a mohawk 'cause I want to be a grown-up punk. But I think a grown-up punk is allowed to like ponies. Right, {surnom}?
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mais tu ne le: I'll tell you a secret, but you don't put it in any fanzine. Promise? … I love pink ponies. With glitter. I have a mohawk because I want to be a big punk. But I can be a big punk who likes ponies, right?
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, matelot. Les: I'll tell you a secret, sailor. Seagulls don't really talk. I know that. But when my wife passed, twenty years ago, the silence in the cabin was terrible. So I started talking to the seagulls. And from listening so much, I heard something. Maybe it's them. Maybe it's me. Either way, there's less silence.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mon ami. Chaq: I'll tell you a secret, my friend. Every morning, carrying the flour up, I rehearse a sentence for Honorine. “Honorine, your song is the most beautiful thing in Montjoie.” Just one sentence. I repeat it the whole way. And at her door, I say: “I'm catching my breath.” Every morning I find a croissant on the empty sack. I don't know if it means something.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mon ami. La D: I'll tell you a secret, my friend. The Duchess, the biggest frog in the lake: I feed her. In the evening, when nobody's looking, I throw her the little fish. She looks at me with her big golden eyes, and she never swallows me. We have a deal, she and I. I think. I've never dared to check.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mon chou. J'a: I'll tell you a secret, sweetie. I was ten when Pyra went off to the Academy. The year after, I went there all alone, at night, in my nightdress. I planted myself in front of the Great Crystal and waited for it to quiver. It didn't move. I cried all the way home. Grandma put my hands on the cauldron and said: “This one quivered.”
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mon chou. Je: I'll tell you a secret, sweetie. I quarrel with Germaine because she's the only person in Montjoie who answers me as loudly as I talk to her. My mother and grandmother are gone. The market had gone quiet. Germaine, she shouts. It keeps me company. If she knew about the seeds, she'd stop. I don't want her to stop.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mon gars. Je: I'll tell you a secret, lad. I don't talk to my turnips just for laughs. I tell them about my son. He went off to the big island in the east, fifteen years ago. He doesn't write much. So I tell the turnips what he's doing, what I imagine he's doing. They listen well. They don't ask questions. Germaine does the same, with the hens.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mon petit sor: I'll tell you a secret, my little spell. Of my ten thousand spells, I only have ten left. The tenth, I've never cast. It's the one that turns a bubble into a butterfly. I'm keeping it for the day Violette finally casts her perfect lightning bolt. That day, I'll make a butterfly fly above her. She'll never know it was me.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, mon petit tré: I'll tell you a secret, my little treasure. There's one legend I've never told: my own. At twenty, I wanted to go off adventuring. I had my bag packed. But my mother was ill, so I stayed. I've never regretted it. But every time someone goes down into the dungeon, I go down a little with them, in my head. Tell me everything when you come back.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}, et: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, and this one I'm giving you for free. All my stories of distant seas and strange islands… they're my father's. Me, I've never left the island. I get canoe-sick. Even on the lake, even in calm weather. So I take the causeways. The son of a pochtecatl! Don't tell anyone. It would bring my prices down.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, and if you repeat it, I'll feed you to the crabs. My scar wasn't a shark. It was Amiral, the auction cat. I was eight, I stole his mackerel head, and he clawed me from temple to cheek. I made up the shark when I was fifteen. Nobody's scared of a girl scratched by a cat.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, and if you repeat it, I'll tattoo a sardine on your forehead. I don't have a single tattoo. Not one. I'm scared of needles. Of mine, anyway, when they're pointed at me. I tattoo the whole port, and my skin is as white as a new sail. The Mute knows. He hasn't said anything. Obviously.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, and you'll laugh. I don't like tea. Too sweet, always has been. I just wet my lips, out of politeness. What I love is the moment I raise the teapot, the foam rises, and everyone goes quiet to watch. A fisherman, a pirate, the amin: all the same. A second of silence. That's what I serve.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, and you're going to laugh. I can't really tell red from green. They both look a bit brown to me. My green mohawk? To me, it's hazelnut. I read the labels on my cans. People say my colours are bold. That's because I don't know they are.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}, mai: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, but softly, the way you talk to bees. Balam asked me to be his matchmaker, to go and ask Ix Sak's mother for her hand. I said yes. For three moons I've been preparing my speech. I recite it to my hives every evening. They know it by heart. I don't, yet. Ix Sak's mother scares me terribly.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, but very quietly: the oven has ears. My mooncake isn't my grandmother's recipe. It's my two hundred and twelfth try. The whole village thinks it's Luzerne's. Only Mother Moon tasted the original, and every evening she says “almost”. So I keep searching. For the almost.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, but you don't tell anyone, promise? I can't swim. A cabin boy who can't swim! So in the evening, when everyone's at the Crâne Fendu, Gros-Louis teaches me at the jetty. He holds my belt and I do the frog. Yesterday he let go, and I didn't sink! I just swallowed a bit of sea. It's salty, the sea.

I'm going to tell you a secret, {surnom}, but you don't tell anyone, promise? The first night, I heard scratching at the bakery door. I opened it. He was tiny and he was shivering. I gave him a croissant. After that, he came back every night… The stolen croissants are kind of my fault. If Mum finds out, she'll be cross. Or sad. Sad is worse.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, but don't tell anyone. The herring… I think there was a seagull. A big one, right above. Maybe it lifted it, not me. If I'm not really magic, they'll send me back to Port-Azur. So I practise my spark every evening. It always fizzles out. But it comes.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, but you won't tell, promise? One day, on Rê's altar, there were dates. For the god. I ate one. Just one! Since then, when Néferet talks about the weighing of the heart, my heart feels all heavy. If Anubis weighed me, I think my heart would tip by one date. Exactly one date.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, but you mustn't tell anyone, OK? Mosquitoes don't live very long. So when Xan stops moving, I go back to the Cenote and catch another one. And I call him Xan too. This one's the fifth. Everyone thinks it's always the same one. Xan isn't a mosquito. It's a job.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, but don't repeat it, especially not to my aunt. Every bowl Youssef broke, I kept the pieces. All of them. In a box, under my wheel. The day his Whale exists, I'll make a mosaic of them on the bow. All his clumsiness, shining in the sun. I love him more than I show. Much more. There. It's broken, it's said.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, but no laughing. I can't dance. Me, who gives the step to the whole town! As soon as I stand up, my feet start arguing: the left wants boom, the right wants ta-ka, and I fall over. So I never let go of my bendir. As long as my hands are busy, nobody asks me to dance.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Au: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. At the bottom of a chest in my workshop, there's a dress I sewed for myself. It's ember red, with gold sequins. I've never worn it. I don't dare. I'm afraid people would look at me, and not at the dress. One day, maybe. On the Night of Lanterns, when everyone's looking at the sky.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Ba: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Ba Sidi wouldn't have refused me the Léviathan's logbook. I never went to ask him for it. I'm scared, you see. Scared he tells the shipwreck differently from my grandfather. If the book says something else, I'm not the last page any more. I'm a wrong page.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Bar: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Bartholomé is a hundred years old, maybe more. He knew Barbe-Sanglante, he still repeats “the skull, the skull”. He remembers everything. So every evening, before I cover his cage, I teach him one word: “Joe”. So that one day, when I'm gone, he'll still say it. And someone will ask who that was.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Cha: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Every year, I write to my father, in Brittany. He's never answered. Maybe the letters get lost. Maybe not. When the Merciless floats, I'll sail her back myself to the end of that inlet, all sails out. And I'll tell him: “Look, Papa. A three-master. And she came back to port.”

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Every year, on the Day of the Dead, I keep the most beautiful cempasúchil bouquet for the altar at home. For Ollin. So the scent shows him the way. Pilli thinks all the bouquets go to the temple. I'll tell him when he's older. Or when he asks me why I smile while I'm picking them.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Every time someone comes back up, I ask them: “How was it?” It's not for the register. It's that while they tell me, I go back down with them. I see the cellars again, the lake, the library. I hear Hugues laughing ahead of me again. Thank you for telling me. It's the only staircase my knees still allow.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Every morning, I make one more choux bun than planned. Just one. I give it to someone who looks like they need it. Yesterday, it was Mr Pascal. The day before, Barnabé, all green, coming out of the capsule. Today, maybe it's you. Do you need a choux bun?
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Dan: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. In the books I borrow at night, I sometimes find a little slip of paper, with a line of verse. I answer with another line, in the ledger. We've been writing a poem together for months. I think it's Ombreline. I don't dare ask her. If it isn't her, I'd be sad. If it is, I wouldn't be able to speak any more.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. In my biscuit tin, under Papa's letters, there's a list. The list of all the questions I'll ask him when he comes back. There are three hundred and forty. The first one is: “Why did you leave?” The last one is: “Are you staying?” In between, it's mostly questions about the dragon.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. In a corner of the forge, under a tarp, there's a little sword. Not wooden. Real steel, light, balanced, with a T engraved on the guard. I've been forging it a little every year since Titouan was six. I'll give it to him the day he leaves. I hope that day is far off. And I'm ready anyway.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. De: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. From far away, I see everything. Up close, I see nothing. You, right there, you're a talking blur. My glasses aren't for reading: they're for recognising people. I take them off as soon as I look out to sea, and then I can't see them anymore. Don't tell the captain. A lookout who can't see up close, that's a laughing matter.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Dep: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. For twelve years, I've been preparing the announcement for Hilaire's rank promotion. I've rewritten it a hundred times. It starts with “HEAR YE!” and ends with “… and he never gave up”. I read it again every evening, very quietly. The day I shout it, the whole town will cry. Me first. Very loudly.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Hic: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Hic. Since the night of the quay, Mama Grog has been serving me a special grog: lots of hot lemon, lots of honey, and hardly any rum. She thinks I haven't noticed. I noticed the very first evening. I said nothing. Nobody had ever gone to so much trouble for me. So I drink my lemon. And I pretend.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Il: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Years ago, I made a potion to laugh. To laugh like Bulle, just once. I drank it. I laughed for an hour, alone in my shop. It was wonderful. Then it stopped. I never made it again. I'd rather laugh rarely, but for real. Bulle doesn't know.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. A long time ago, I wrote a letter to Sidonie, the archer in my team. I never sent it. She got married across the seas. The letter must still be lying around in a drawer at the Guild. If Églantine finds it, I'd rather not know.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. There's been a letter in my bag for three years. It has no address. Just: “To the one who flies.” I found it in the post office box. I don't dare open it. If it's for me, I don't know who wrote it. If it isn't for me, I don't want to know. It travels with me. Everywhere.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. J'a: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I'm scared of heights. On the second rung of a ladder, my legs shake. I follow wires everywhere, but not up high. When I have to climb, I ask Bardane. She climbs, I shout up what to plug in. We make a good team. Her up top, me down below, and the light between us.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I get vertigo. On stairs. Stairs have no branches, no leaves, nothing to hold on to. In a tree, thirty metres up, I'm never scared: the tree holds me. But three concrete steps, and my legs start shaking. Nobody understands. Neither do I.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I get vertigo. Me, the crane operator. The first time I climbed into Mademoiselle, I nearly came back down. Gravier was below. He shouted three words at me: “Look far away.” I looked at the horizon. Since then, I never look down. I look at the sea. It changed my life.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I saw the little sword under the tarp, in the corner of the forge. The one with a T. I know it's for me. I pretend I don't know, because Mum would be sad if the surprise was spoiled. And because if I took it, it would mean I'm leaving. I'm not ready yet. A little bit, though.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I've written only one true song, with nothing exaggerated. It's about an archer who never speaks and always stays until the last verse. I've never sung it. I think if I sang it, everyone would know who it's about. Especially her.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I wrote a waltz. It's called “The Dandy's Waltz”. I've never played it in public. It's about a gentleman with golden horns who sighs at the wrong moment. I tease Tiburce every evening. But it's for him that I wrote my most beautiful music. Don't tell him. Especially not him.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. J'i: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. At night, I'm inventing a recipe in a notebook: a little coconut bun, for the morning dancers. I dream of opening it here — my own bakery, at the end of the beach. But I'm afraid Margaux will take it badly. She taught me everything. You don't leave someone who taught you everything. Do you?
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Je: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I tell everyone I hate Flammèche's puppies. But there's one, Suie, the most timid, who sleeps in my watering can every afternoon. I sing him a lullaby, the same one I sang my twins. He snores. If Flammèche finds out, I'll deny everything. But his name is Suie, and he's my favourite.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I've never taken the Line up top. Fifty-two years going round in circles in the cavern. The sea, I've only ever seen from underneath, from the Funicular's bubble. Anatole keeps nudging me to go and see it from above. I say “tomorrow”. I don't like trains that go straight up. They've got no bends.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I've never taken the Line. Never seen the sea. Fifty-two years going round in circles in the cavern. Now that the Line has reopened, Anatole keeps pushing me. I say “tomorrow”. I don't like trains that go straight up. They've got no bends.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I've never left the Fronde. Never. Not even to go into the Strata. Big open spaces scare me. Here, the cavern holds me like a hand. But since the Line reopened… I look at the Column. A little more every day.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I've never seen the sea. Fifty-two years going round in circles, underground. The Line has reopened. Anatole pushes me every day. I say “tomorrow”. The truth is, I'm afraid the sea will be too big, and I won't want to go round in circles any more. And then what about Bernadette? Who'd drive her?

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I'm not scared of falling. I'm scared of letting people down. Mistress Capucine was counting on me for the Cloud line. So every evening I went up to the Belvedere and stayed one minute longer by the railing. One minute a day. And on reopening day, I made the first ride up. Green as a pea. But all the way to the top.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I'm not afraid of falling. I'm afraid of letting people down. Mistress Capucine is counting on me for the Cloud line. So every evening I go up to the Belvedere and stay one minute longer by the railing. One minute a day. In a year, that'll be six hours.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I haven't smiled only once. I smiled a second time, last year, when Clapotis and Bouton-d'Or signalled each other with their torches, from either side of the island. I could see them from the terrace. I said nothing. A reputation needs looking after.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I'd never seen the sea. Fifty-two years going round in circles, underground. Then the Dome Line reopened, and I went down with Marius, in his glass bubble. I saw it from underneath. I've still got to see it from above. Anatole pushes me every day. I say “tomorrow”. The truth is, I'm afraid the sea will be too big, and I won't want to go round in circles any more. And then what about Bernadette? Who'd drive her?

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I don't lose all my drops. For a hundred years, every evening, I've left one at the edge of the northern brambles. For Églantine. In case she's thirsty, in there. I never knew if she drank them. Don't tell Perlée: she'd count them.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I can only choose my hair colour at fifteen, in front of the brazier, like everyone. I've already chosen: red and turquoise. But actually, I'm a bit scared. What if I got it wrong? Brasero told me: “A colour can't be wrong. You wear it.” I don't know what that means. But it made me feel better.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I don't know how it stays up in the air. I don't know where it comes from. All I know is that since it's been here, everyone eats together, nobody eats alone, and we laugh a lot. Maybe that's the miracle. The rest is just sauce.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I can't read. Or write. Gaspard did the accounts. Since then, my slate is drawings: a sardine for Sans-Dents, a barrel for Tonneau, a wooden leg for you-know-who. Nobody has ever noticed. They all think I have bad handwriting. Let them think so, sweetie.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I can't swim. Me, the fishwife, the fisherman's daughter, born in a rowing boat! I was too scared to learn. I fish from the boat, and I never fall in. Grumbald knows, and he never mentions it. One day, he gave me a rubber ring painted like a sardine. “For decoration,” he said.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Maybe I could move up a rank, if I really applied myself. But at rank F, I'm here when the newcomers arrive. I see them scared, and I see them succeed. If I moved up, I'd go further away. And who would tell them not to run at a frog with its mouth open?

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I laugh all the time, but I'm afraid of the cold. Really afraid. As a boy, I fell into the icy water of a mountain spring. I couldn't feel my horns. My mother rubbed me by the fire for an hour, singing. Since then, I keep my Baths hot, so nobody is ever cold. And I laugh. To warm things up.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I dream of building a dome down below, by the sea. But I'm a little scared of the houses down there. With their corners. Where do you put the corners away? Do you bump into them? Are people sad in them? I've been told they're not. But I can't quite believe it.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I know why Clovis stays outside my door every morning. He's not catching his breath: he's listening to my song. I know, because I sing louder when I hear his footsteps. I've never said anything to him. I make him one extra croissant every day, and leave it on the empty sack. He takes it without a word.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I can stay on my unicycle just fine. I fall on purpose. Almost always. Because when I fall, everyone laughs, and everyone comes to help me up. And when you get up together, you forget you were sad. That's my real act. The juggling is just scenery.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. La: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. The leaning brioche in Asmodin's basket every day, I do it on purpose. Not to annoy him. The first day I botched one, he smiled, for one second, when he saw it. Asmodin never smiles. So ever since, every day, I make him a crooked one. For that one second of smile.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Cosmic jelly, the real thing, is my grandmother's recipe from Ondelune. The only one I didn't invent. It tickles your tongue. My grandmother tickled too. With her four arms. She was the best.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. The Azure Dome gate, behind me: I open it a little every evening, when everyone's gone. Just to listen. At the end of the tunnel, it echoes like the sea. One day, the Dome Line will reopen, and I'll make the first descent. All the way to the bottom of the sea. And there, I think I'll hear everything.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. The Azure Dome gate, behind me: for twelve years, I opened it a crack every evening, once everyone had gone. To oil it. And to listen: at the end of the tunnel, it echoed like the sea. The day the Dome Line reopened, I went down with Marius, sitting beside his controls. All the way to the bottom of the sea. And there, the whale went by. I heard her. With my hands.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. The recipe for hot sulphur punch was invented by my father, the day he swore he'd only ever serve drinks that warm the heart without muddling the head. I keep it like a treasure. I've never written it down: it's here, in my hands. One day, I'll teach it to someone.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Le: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Professor Lunette thinks a star winks at him. Sometimes it's my lamp. Sometimes it's Héloïse's lantern. But sometimes… it's neither. I don't tell him. Mysteries are like seagulls: you mustn't catch them.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. The grandfather of Mathilde, the blacksmith up top, learned his trade here. With my grandmother, and with the Fronde's smiths. When Mathilde strikes hard, we strike back. We've been talking like that for twenty years. And we've never actually met.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. The day of the big smoke, Dad and Mum arrived together, and afterwards they laughed. Together. Loudly. Ever since, I make rockets that smoke on purpose. Margot thinks I get my sums wrong. And Bidule is the same: it's so they'll laugh together again. Don't tell anyone. Especially not Margot.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. The mayor doesn't sing that badly. Really. A bit loud, a bit too much opera, but in tune. If I told him, he'd leave the town hall tomorrow for the stage. So I say “seal with a cold”. A good tenor, you can always find. A good mayor is rarer.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. In the evening, I tell Tlaco things for Dad. What I did, what I ate, Kinich, the fair. That way, later on, when Tlaco guides me through Mictlan, he can tell him everything. I've already told him three hundred. He's forgotten half. Mum says Dad forgot everything too. So it'll be fine.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Coralie's botched tattoo, the spoon instead of the knife… I actually like it. My grandmother had the same one, made of wood, for stirring her cauldron. I still have it, in my chest. I've been pretending to be cross with Coralie for months, because a knife-thrower with a spoon on her arm makes people laugh. But in the evening, I look at it.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Ma: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. My tenth race, eight years ago: I was in the lead. Me! At the roots bend, before the Watchtower, nobody ahead. And then I heard crying behind me: little Bondi, eleven years old, twisted ankle. I carried him to the finish. Last, the pair of us. He thinks I'd fallen too. Never tell him. It's the only race I ever won.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. My sap potion: I don't know everything that's in it. Grandmother fell asleep before she gave me the last ingredient. Hers restored four hearts. Mine restores three. For three hundred years I've been looking for the fourth. That's why I say: “don't ask me”.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Mad: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Madame Croquette doesn't belong to anyone. She'd been abandoned at the harbour when I arrived, skinny and sad. She followed me. She's slept on my feet for five years. The other dogs go home to their owners at night. She comes home with me. She's the only one who chose me. I cry every time I think about it.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Mam: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Mum can't travel anymore: she's become too wobbly. So I travel for her. Every photo, I send to her. Click: that's a kiss. Click: that's a kiss. I've never told her. But I think she knows. When she gets a photo, she bounces a little bit.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Mes: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. My circuits change colour with the music, but only once did they turn gold. It was when Mamie Kiku came to watch me dance, with her teapot, in the front row. I've never seen that colour again.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. My parents come by once a year, for the Crystal Festival. They set off fireworks over the town, just for me, and they leave the next day. There's a potion I've been trying to get right for two years: a potion to make boats stay. Out of all my botched potions, that's the one I keep botching.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Mon: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. My dad's a sailor. He sails very far away, towards the northern islands. When I go to the Ash Wood, I climb up the big black rock and look at the sea, to see if his ship is coming back. I don't tell Mum. She thinks I'm looking for mushrooms. I'm looking for both.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. My first pup, Braise, came from the lava field, east of the volcano. He was a little one from those wild dogs my brother wants to drive away. I never told Pyrus. Braise is the gentlest of my pups. So when people tell me wild dogs are vicious, I think of Braise. And I don't believe it.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. My fiddle doesn't come from Cremona. Nor from Cremona-on-Sea: there's no such place. I made it myself, at fourteen, out of the door of an old fisherman's hut, with a knife, a fishbone and hairs taken from the tail of the baker's horse. The baker never knew. The horse did. He still holds it against me.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Plu: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. When I grow up, I'll build an android. He'll be called One. Because Zéro was the first, but he'll be my first.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Qua: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. When Ortie turned my bellows into a fire-bubble machine, I shouted so loud the bells rang. Then that evening, I went back to the forge, all by myself, and ran her machine. For an hour. Fire bubbles everywhere. I laughed like a little girl. I never told her.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Que: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Someone leaves poems in my lantern boxes. I know it's Nox. I keep them all at the bottom of the big lantern on the square, where no one looks. I've never told him I know. I'm afraid he'd stop. And I'm afraid of what I'd answer.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Tou: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Very quietly. Once, I lost my voice for three days. Nobody recognised me. People walked past me without seeing me. I was afraid I was nothing, without my voice. On the third day, Gorgoth brought me an herbal tea and whispered to me: “I miss you.” I cried. Without a sound. For once.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. The whole fleet thinks I swim like a grouper. I can't swim. Not a single stroke. My whole life at sea, and I've never let go of the side of my boat. That's why the Zahra's eye matters so much. It watches over someone who couldn't save himself.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. All my heart-shaped rockets fail. All of them: kidney, shoe, cloud. Miss Sulfura laughs every time, and I pretend it's on purpose. But truly, I fail them on purpose. A failed rocket, she laughs. A successful one, she'd have to answer. And I'm afraid of the answer.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I send all my photos to my mum, on Gloop. She can't travel: she's too squishy now. So I travel for her. Every photo is a kiss. Click. There. You're a kiss for my mum.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. All my recipes are made up, except one: the cosmic jelly. It's my grandmother's, from Ondelune. I make it every morning, at dawn, before anyone gets up. I stir it with my four arms, like she did. And I tell her about the day before. I think she's listening. The jelly wobbles a little.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Une: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Just once, I missed on purpose. At the archery contest at the Dawn festival. In the final, against Rodrigue, who'd picked up a bow for the first time. He was shaking. I aimed wide. He won. He still talks about it. I'll never tell him. Cake?
textes.Je vais te dire un secret, {surnom}. Zig: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Zigomar sends me heart-shaped rockets, and I pretend to sigh. But the last one, the one that exploded in the shape of a kidney, I picked up its stick. It's in my desk drawer, next to my chalk. I look at it when the class is too noisy. It makes me smile.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret. Dans le trou: I'll tell you a secret. In the hole I dug at Grommelot's, I left something behind: my most beautiful hazelnut, the one that looks most like my shell. He doesn't know. One day, a hazel tree will grow in the middle of his roots, and he'll grumble very loudly. That'll be my way of saying sorry. And maybe it'll be my very own tree.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret. L'hiver où Ga: I'll tell you a secret. The winter Gaubert fell ill, I was the one who carried the seed sacks to the farm, at night, without a word. Germaine never found out who. If she knew, we'd have to stop arguing. And I wouldn't know what to do with my mornings.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret. Tout bas. App: I'll tell you a secret. Very quietly. Come closer. … In the evening, at home, I listen to recordings of whales. Very softly. So softly you have to press your ear to the speaker. I love silence, {surnom}. Real silence. I shout all day so nobody finds out. Don't repeat it. ESPECIALLY NOT TO TAPAGE.
textes.Je vais te dire un secret. Tout bas. … T: I'll tell you a secret. Very quietly. … Can you hear? No? I WAS SAYING: I don't like noise. I like SOUND. Beautiful sound. Noise is a sound nobody listened to. My job is listening.
textes.Je vais te dire un truc : je n'aime pas: I'll tell you something: I don't like loud music. At all. But I come to every concert, with two pairs of earplugs. Because I like seeing people happy. And you can hear that even with earplugs.
textes.Je vais te dire un truc qui pique, {surn: I'll tell you something that stings, {surnom}. Ursule forges every nail in my bridges. Every one! And she's never crossed a single one. Never. She takes the stairs, even when it takes her half an hour. She doesn't trust me, that's what. It hurts more than a bee sting. And I've had stings, believe me.
textes.Je vais te dire un truc, {surnom}, et tu: I'll tell you something, {surnom}, and you keep it to yourself. Before every gig, I get stage fright. Massive stage fright. My hands shake, my voice disappears. So I go to see Mamie Barricade up on the mezzanine and sing the first note to her, just her. If she nods, I can sing in front of everyone.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}, and don't you repeat it, eh. At sixteen, I wanted to dance too. I danced behind the stall, with the sardines as my audience. One day, my mother put a fish knife in my hand and said: “There's your dance.” So now, every coin from the big fish, I put aside. For Clara's dance school. She doesn't know.
textes.Je vais te dire un truc, {surnom}, mais: I'm gonna tell you something, {surnom}, but you can't tell anyone. Swear? I know where the ginger cat sleeps. Amine showed me. And when we climbed up, he was sleeping on some papers. Old papers. I didn't tell the captain. 'Cause a map found is a treasure found, and a treasure found means the Murène sails off. And I don't wanna leave Tazira. I'm a bad pirate, huh?

I'll tell you something, {surnom}, but keep it to yourself. Last winter, Amélie put her ear to my chest, listened for a long time, and said: “Slow down.” Since then, on the hills, when nobody's looking, I walk. Those seventy-eight seconds, I'll never run them again. There. Hop… hop. It feels good to say it.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}, but keep it to yourself. My uncle's eyes are getting weaker. One morning I saw him greet a tree trunk: “Morning, Bourru.” He didn't notice. So on watch I look at the forest twice as hard as at the Clearing. For him. I look at the arches afterwards. He'll never know. I talk a lot, but that, I won't tell.
textes.Je vais te dire un truc, {surnom}. Je ré: I'll tell you something, {surnom}. I do get spells right. I do. At night, all alone in the courtyard, when everyone's asleep: a perfect little light, round, steady. But as soon as someone's watching, my hands shake and everything goes wrong. I don't know why. I haven't told anyone. Not even Pip. Especially not Pip.
textes.Je vais te dire un truc, {surnom}. Mais: I'm going to tell you something, {surnom}. But if you repeat it, I'll load you into a cannon. Coquille gave me a big shell from Bone Beach. I put it to my ear, to make her happy. And I heard the sea. CLEARLY. The first thing I've heard clearly in thirty years. In the evening, in my hammock, I listen to it. That's all. Go away now.

I'm gonna tell you something, {surnom}. But don't you repeat it, eh. I don't cut trees anymore. Never. Not even for Gwen's masts. The big oak that fell on the king's boat, it was three hundred years old. There was a nest in it. I saw it while it was falling. Since then, when I see an axe, my heart feels heavy. Not my belly. My heart.
textes.Je vais te dire un vrai secret. Je fais: I'll tell you a real secret. I play pranks because when everyone laughs, nobody's sad any more. Not even Volt. Not even the Elder, when she thinks of Ondelune. So I play pranks. Lots of them. It's a job.
textes.Je vais te dire un vrai secret. Pas une: I'll tell you a real secret. Not a prank. I play pranks because when everyone's laughing, nobody's sad any more. Not even Volt. Not even the Elder, when she looks at the sky and thinks about Ondelune. I saw her, once. So I pulled a face. She laughed. Since then, it's been my job. A very serious job.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose que je ne dis: I'll tell you something I don't say at the Fondouk, {surnom}, because the walls hear everything. Every time Mbarek says “I'm leaving tomorrow”, I keep his room free, even when the courtyard is overflowing. And at night, I pray for a sandstorm. A little one. Just enough to close the road. I've never dared ask him to stay. The wind does it for me.

I'll tell you something I don't tell the apprentices, little one. When Firmin fell ill, I tried everything. All my herbs, all my spells. My hands were useless. So I just held his, all night long. Care doesn't cure everything. Sometimes, caring means staying. I don't know how to teach that to the young ones. I haven't the heart.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose que même Samir: I'll tell you something not even Samira knows, {surnom}. I can't read carpets. My grandmother could. The stories I tell customers, the sultan's wedding, the sandstorm, I make them up. All of them! Except one. The carpet of stars, I never made up. And when I unroll it, brother, it frightens me a little.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose que même Youss: I'll tell you something not even Youssef knows, {surnom}. My father's last song, he never finished it. He'd sing the beginning, stop, and say: “The rest, tomorrow.” There was no tomorrow. So at sea, I always sing the beginning. And I wait. Maybe one morning, the sea will give me back the rest.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose que personne n: I'll tell you something nobody knows. In that hour, alone on the stage, I made up a song. It's mine, all mine, without a single one of Caelan's rhymes. I've never sung it again. I'm afraid it'll be less beautiful the second time. Maybe at the next festival. Maybe.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose, mais ne la ré: I'll tell you something, but don't repeat it. Before you came, I had no one to measure myself against. I was training for nothing. Now I get up at five. Thank you. I hate you. Thank you.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose, mon petit cha: I'll tell you something, my little mushroom. My caravan can't move any more: the mushrooms have grown around the wheels. They hold it like a hand. At first I was afraid of being a prisoner. Then I understood they didn't want me to leave. And I didn't want to leave. We held hands without saying so.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose, mon petit. L': I'll tell you something, little one. The winter Gaubert was ill, someone left six sacks of seeds in front of our door. It saved us. I looked everywhere for who it was. I never found out. It eats at me. I hate not knowing who to thank. And Gaubert smiles every time I bring it up. He knows something. He's not saying.
I'll tell you something, my chick. There's one pie I've never made again: the blackberry one, with my husband, Firmin. He picked the blackberries, I made the pastry. Since he's been gone, I haven't dared. The blackberries wait for me every summer by the side of the path. I walk past. One day, perhaps.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose, {surnom}, et: I'll tell you something, {surnom}, and if you repeat it, I'll know. I don't dance for the dancing. I dance to be near Nenetl's drum. And I'd like to learn to play her hummingbird flute. A jaguar warrior playing the flute… People would laugh. Her most of all. She laughs at everything. That's why I love her. There. I've said it.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}, and if you repeat it, we'll be enemies for good. I write to my mother every week. I tell her I have a formidable rival, that we fight duels in thunderstorms. She writes back: “Eat well and wear a scarf.” I wear a scarf. Under my cape. Nobody knows.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}, and you keep it to yourself. My eyes are going. In the evening, I can't see the line between sea and sky any more. So I ask Ewen what he sees, pretending I'm training him. He describes everything. He's good, that boy. But the blue light, I saw it before. That, I saw.

I'm going to tell you something, {surnom}, and you'll keep it to yourself. Above my bed there's a lantern that's too heavy, crooked, pierced by a twenty-year-old boy. It's Abdellah's first. He thinks it was melted down. It's the most beautiful one of my life, because we made it before we started arguing. If he finds out, I'll never be right about anything again.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose, {surnom}, mai: I'll tell you something, {surnom}, but keep your voice down. My eyes are going. The little signs start dancing, even at noon. So I ask the pupils to read out loud, “to test them”. They think it's an exam. It is one. For me. Don't tell Néferet: she'd have my eyes blessed in front of the whole village.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}, but if you repeat it, I'll serve you without froth till the end of time. The baker from Per-Hâpy put honey in my cacao. I cried sacrilege. That evening, in secret, I tried it. It was… very good. Since then, every evening, a spoonful of Yum Kab's honey in my cup. Nobody must know. Especially not him.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}, but if you repeat it, I'll sell you a leaky bucket. The seagull never paid for his bucket. Half of what I “sell”, I give away: to the old folks, the widows, the fishermen who've had a bad week. If that got out, nobody would ever pay me again. My grandmother did the same.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}, but very quietly. In the collections Nox borrows at night, I sometimes slip a little piece of paper between two pages, with a line I've written. He doesn't know it's me. The next day, in the ledger, next to his “Thank you”, there's another line. We're writing a poem together. Without ever speaking to each other.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose, {surnom}, une: I'll tell you one thing, {surnom}, just one, and you forget it straight away. In my cabin, there's a box. Inside, a dried geranium, picked up from the cobbles of Tortuga the night of the pot. I never saw Mathilde again. I don't even know if she was aiming at my head or throwing me a flower. Since the leg, I don't dance any more. But I think about it. Often.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose, {surnom}. Je: I'll tell you something, {surnom}. I never talk about it. The night of the broken sword, the gargoyle was diving at a very young guard. His name was Pyrus. I pushed him aside, took the blow, and knocked the beast out with the bucket. Pyrus doesn't remember: his eyes were shut. I've never told him. I give him good prices. Not too low.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}. I'm still shy. In front of a mic, I'm the Sergeant: I shout, I laugh, I do sound effects. But face to face with people, without a mic, my hands get sweaty and I fumble for words. That's why I talk so fast. So I don't have time to be scared. Pschhh… end of confession.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose, {surnom}. Le: Let me tell you something, {surnom}. Tornade's cradle — I made it from a pallet and one of Rustine's bike wheels. Then Cerise used it. Now it's up in the attic. Sometimes I go up to see it. I rock it a little. I don't know why. Wood remembers. So do I.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}. Pépin's dad sails far away, towards the northern islands. Pépin thinks I don't know he climbs the big black rock in the Ash Wood to watch for his ship. I know. I watch too, from the port. I don't scold him for that. I scold him for everything that frightens me.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}. Little Aldric Lisse — I knew him when he was eight, on the quays. He helped me carry the oranges and he laughed very loudly. I gave him a toffee. I think that little boy is still in there, somewhere under the grey suit. That's who I never give up for. So he can find him again.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}. On the night of the last festival, I was there. Not as a roadie: as a spectator, I was ten. That concert is what made me want to do this job. I repair the stage to give back what I was given that night.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose, {surnom}. Qua: Let me tell you something, {surnom}. When Mr Lisse came to see my flower-robots, made from the parts of his own robots, he stood in front of them for an hour without a word. I was hiding behind Brindezingue. At the end, he touched a petal. Gently. I think he understood something. I don't know what. Neither does he, probably.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}. When I was ten, I shook a friend's hand too hard, and I hurt him. He cried. So did I. Since that day, I've been afraid of my own strength. In the Arena, I push, I lift, I set down. I never hit. People think it's strategy. It's fear. And a bit of kindness.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose, {surnom}. Une: I'll tell you something, {surnom}. Only once did a prediction come true exactly. I'd said: “Boulon is going to lift a house.” I was joking. The next day, he set down the first container of the Boxes: mine. I was so scared I didn't predict anything for a month. Since then, I make a point of staying a bit vague.

I'll tell you one thing, {surnom}. Just one. The day before the marsh, Crochet had left his sabre with me to resharpen. I quenched it too fast. I wanted to go and hear Tom's new song. The next day, the sabre broke on Vieille-Dent. Crochet never mentioned it to me. Neither did I. Every afternoon, I keep the best spot by the fire for him.
textes.Je vais te dire une chose. J'ai peur des: I'll tell you something. I'm scared of frogs, but I think they're beautiful. In the morning, when they poke their heads out of the water and the sun rises behind them, it's the most beautiful sight in the world. From afar. From very far.
textes.Je vais te dire, {surnom}. Chez nous, po: I'll tell you, {surnom}. Where I come from, to ask for a woman's hand, you send a matchmaker to talk to her parents. I asked Yum Kab. For Ix Sak. He said yes. He's preparing his speech. For three moons now. I say nothing. I wait. A jaguar knows how to wait. But three moons… Don't tell Ix Sak.
textes.Je vais te donner un conseil, {surnom},: I'm going to give you some advice, {surnom}, the most important there is. If one day a screen scares you, with flashing messages screaming “danger”, don't panic. A screen that screams is often a screen that lies. Breathe. And come and see me.
textes.Je vais te démonter comme une vieille ba: I'll take you apart like a rotten old rowboat!
textes.Je vais te faire une confidence, {surnom: I'll let you in on something, {surnom}. I've been sighing in the front row for three years, but I've never told Calcine I love her. Not in words. I'm afraid she'll laugh. She laughs at everything I say. So I keep quiet, I listen, and I sigh. She thinks I sigh for the music. I do sigh for the music, too.
textes.Je vais te montrer quelque chose, {surno: I'm going to show you something, {surnom}. But you don't say a word. Two years ago, Plumette brought me a parcel with no letter. Inside, there was this: Aunt Sésame's bell. I didn't tell my uncle. I'm scared it means she won't come back. So it stays in my pocket, stuffed with moss, so it won't ring.

I'm going to show you something, {surnom}. See that grey straw hat on my shelf? It was a crown of sunflowers. Sunflower made it for me on our twentieth birthday. It dried. It went grey, like me. I could never throw it away. Don't tell her. Or do. I don't know anymore.
textes.Je vais te ranger dans un tonneau de har: I'll stuff you in a herring barrel and sit on the lid.
textes.Je vais tout raconter à ma classe. Perso: I'm going to tell my whole class. Nobody will believe me. So I'll show them my drawing.
textes.Je vais travailler dans les Hauts. Quatr: I'm going to work in the Heights. Ninetieth floor. I'm dizzy.
I'm going to see my sister on the other island.
I'm going to confess a crime to you, {surnom}. I don't like coffee. I never have. For as long as I can remember, behind the coffee machine, I've been drinking camomile, from a coffee cup so nobody notices. Only my mother knew. If word got out on the square… Heavens. Keep it to yourself.
textes.Je vais vous avouer une chose que je n'a: I'll confess something I've never printed. One morning with no news, I made up a short item: “In Tazira, a cat steals a treasure map.” Three days later, the Zéphyr mail confirmed it. Almost word for word. Did I guess? Do I bring luck? I don't know. Since then I've never made anything up again. Not one line.
textes.Je vais vous avouer une chose, {surnom},: I'm going to confess something to you, {surnom}, and I'm counting on you. I write romance novels. Under the name Sylvia Delarive. “The Foam of Your Heart” — that's me. The grocer reads it in secret and recommended it to me: I nearly fainted into the peaches. Even Gérard doesn't know. He thinks I'm logging my sunbathing hours. My sunbathing log is three hundred pages long.
I'll confess something to you, {surnom}. Every night, at three o'clock, I come to the stand in my slippers, and I give the engine one turn of the crank. Just one. To help it along. I know what everyone thinks, you know. I'm not stupid. But I promised Honoré. And a promise, now that can turn forever.

I'll confess something to you, {surnom}. I've never dared go down below. I'm afraid of loving it too much. If I saw the islands for real, the markets, the houses, the people with their socks, I could never come back up. So I stay here, with my display cases. They, at least, don't ask me to choose.
textes.Je vais vous avouer une chose. Je n'ai j: I'll confess something to you. I've never dared go down below. I'm afraid of… of loving it too much. If I saw all that for real, I could never leave again. So I stay here, with my display cases. At least they don't ask me to choose.
textes.Je vais vous avouer une chose. La nuit d: I'll confess something to you. The night of the storm, the wind didn't force the window. I had left it open. I was reading by the light of the lightning, it was magnificent, and I fell asleep on the page. I told everyone the latch had given way. Séraphine knows, I believe. She said nothing. She knows how to keep quiet, when need be.
textes.Je vais vous confier pourquoi j'aime les: I'll tell you why I love clouds, {surnom}. It's not to forecast them. I'm wrong all the time. It's that they pass by, and others always come back. When you live on a floating island, you need to know the sky is never left empty. Clouds are visitors. Like you.
textes.Je vais vous confier quelque chose, {sur: I'll confide something in you, {surnom}. In a drawer of Mr Lisse's desk, there's a photo of a little hut made of pallets, with a round window.
