A little boy in front of it, very proud. It's him. I found it while filing. I didn't file it. I believe there's someone good inside that suit. He just has to find him again.

I'll confide something in you, {surnom}. I tell Lili “soon” because I'm afraid that once she sees the sea, she'll want to stay down there. Like me, at twenty, for a week. It's selfish. I know. The next “soon” will be the last. I promise myself that.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. The little blue crystal in Ysaé's jewellery: I'm the one who gives it to her. The splinters too small for a lantern. When she was little, she used to pinch them from under my workbench. I pretended not to see. Today she wears them all the way up top. My little splinters travel better than I do.
textes.Je vais vous confier quelque chose. (Ell: I'll let you in on something. (She opens her jacket one centimetre: inside, a lining covered in Bilge Rats badges.) Velours sewed them on for me. Sirène keeps a violet lemonade for me. And I go to every concert. With a moustache. Don't say a word. Especially not to Monsieur Lisse. He'd be… de-optimised.
textes.Je vais vous confier quelque chose. J'ai: I'll confide something in you. I have a clock that doesn't work. It's stopped at the moment we left Ondelune. I don't repair it. Some hours must be kept just as they are.
textes.Je vais vous confier un secret : j'inven: I'll tell you a secret: I make up my feats because I've never had a real one. But when a friend is in danger, I charge. Always. Without thinking. It's the only true thing about me. That and my appetite.
textes.Je vais vous confier un secret, {surnom}: I'll let you in on a secret, {surnom}. I bought a brooch from young Ysaé. A little Column made of bolts. I wear it under my sash. I don't yet know what to think of the Fronde, down there. But someone who makes such a pretty Column out of bolts… can't be entirely against us.

I'll let you in on a secret, {surnom}. The treatise on explosive mixtures, I finished it five years ago. Twice. But Théophraste never leaves his library, except to come and ask for it back, once a month. He grumbles, he drinks a mint syrup, he leaves. If I give it back, he'll stop coming. So I'm still on page one hundred and twelve.

I'll confide a secret to you, {surnom}. My red cape was sewn by my mother, the night before I left. She cried on it. It's too long, because she wanted me to keep growing. I trip over it. I'll never shorten it. When I fall, it's a bit as if she were holding me back.
textes.Je vais vous confier une chose que je n': I shall confide something I have never told anyone, {surnom}. When Her Highness hid in the chandelier, I always knew where she was. I pretended to search, for a long time, because she laughed when she heard me go by. I have no children. But I had that laughter, in the throne room. Do not repeat it.
textes.Je vais vous confier une chose, citoyen: I shall confide something to you, citizen {surnom}. I know full well nobody voted for me. The evening they dropped me off here, I was nothing anymore: not a tax collector, not a passenger, not anybody. Mama Grog served me soup without asking me anything. The next day, I appointed myself governor. To have a reason to get up. And to be useful, one day, to those who had fed me.
textes.Je vais vous confier une chose, {surnom}: I'll confide something to you, {surnom}. There's an adventurer's record card in my name. I filled it in on my first day, at sixteen. I've never stamped it. Every time someone sets off for the dungeon, I want to go too. And every time, I stay, so I'm here when they come back.

I shall confide something in you, {surnom}. I have a clock that doesn't work. It stopped at the exact minute we left Ondelune. I don't repair it. Every night, before sleeping, I look at it. Some hours must not be reset. They must be kept just as they are.

I shall confide something to you, {surnom}. I have no house. I live here. I sleep in the linen room on the fourth floor, on a pile of clean sheets, as my mother once did. Never in a room: that would be taking a guest's place. The snoring ghost Pauline talks about… is me. I beg you not to tell her.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}. I still haven't found out why the blue crystals glow. I have hypotheses, notebooks, calculations. But deep down, I hope I never find out. As long as I'm searching, I go down to the Grotto every morning, and I marvel. The day I know, I'm afraid I'll marvel a little less.

I'll confide something to you, {surnom}. When the lightning hits me, I say “it happens” so I don't cry. It hurts, a little. Especially in the heart. But if I cry, the next bolt is even stronger. So I say “it happens”, and I start again. The books say it's practice. I say it's stubbornness.

I'll confide something to you, {surnom}. On the top shelf there's a golden vial. It's my grandfather's last potion, with a label: “To be happy”. I've never tasted it. I'm afraid it won't work. Or that it will, and I'll no longer know why I do everything else.
textes.Je vais vous dire ce que Nina ne sait pa: I'll tell you something Nina doesn't know, {surnom}. That week's holiday was my honeymoon. On the morning of my wedding, instead of going to the town hall, I went to the harbour with my suitcase and took the boat. Alone. Without getting married. I've never regretted it. But I've never known how to tell the story.
textes.Je vais vous dire la vérité, {surnom}. C: I'll tell you the truth, {surnom}. It wasn't the ring that made me cry. It's that for a second, one tiny little second, I was afraid it was a sign. That the sea was telling me something about us. I'm so angry with myself for doubting. Hugo doesn't know. He thinks I'm angry with him. It's me.
textes.Je vais vous dire la vérité, {surnom}. L: I'll tell you the truth, {surnom}. The Wisteria Cottage was my grandmother's house. I grew up there every summer. I exaggerate everything to scare off the wrong buyers. I want it to go to someone who'll come home in the evening, put their trophies on the shelf and sleep soundly. My grandmother used to say: “A house is a place that waits for you.”
textes.Je vais vous dire mon rêve secret. Une m: I'll tell you my secret dream. A machine to go back to Ondelune. I've been building it for nine hundred years. It's almost finished. But every time it's almost finished, I think of Astralys, the auroras, my students… and I unscrew a part. Theoretically, it's an accident.
I'll tell you my secret, {surnom}. There's a little bit missing from my map, right down in the south. I could draw it in an hour. But then it would be finished. And a finished map gets put away. Nobody looks at it anymore. So I leave the little bit empty. That way, the archipelago keeps on existing a little further than what I know.

I'll tell you my secret, {surnom}. I'm building a machine to go back to Ondelune. I have been for nine hundred years. Every time it's almost finished, I think of the auroras, my students, Gloubi's café… and I unscrew a part, without meaning to. Theoretically, it's an accident. In practice, I think I don't want to leave.
textes.Je vais vous dire pourquoi j'ai choisi B: I'll tell you why I chose Barnabé, {surnom}. It wasn't for the pulleys. It's because he was afraid, and he came anyway. Liftkeepers who are never afraid don't know how to reassure passengers. He will. One day.
textes.Je vais vous dire pourquoi je déteste le: I'll tell you why I hate lateness, {surnom}. My grandfather was waiting for me one day, at the Harbour. I arrived three minutes after the boat. He had gone. He came back, of course, months later. But those three minutes, I still carry them in my pocket. With the leftover part.
textes.Je vais vous dire pourquoi je suis si pr: I'll tell you why I'm so careful, {surnom}. When I was twelve, an old gallery caved in. Everyone was outside. Everyone. Because my father had heard the rock creak a minute before, and he'd whistled everyone out. Ever since, I listen. For him.
textes.Je vais vous dire quelque chose, et vous: I'm going to tell you something, and you'll forget it immediately. In the evening, when I walk past the Hall, I slow down. A little. The music comes through the walls. My foot keeps time. I didn't ask it to. I don't stop it. It's the only thing in my day that I don't optimise. I don't know why I'm telling you this, {surnom}.
textes.Je vais vous dire un secret, mais ne le: I'll tell you a secret, but don't repeat it to anyone: it's not protocol. I'm very shy. All these speeches, these rules, these bows… they're so I know what to do with my hands. When I don't know what to say, I issue a decree.
textes.Je vais vous dire un secret, {surnom}, e: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}, and you keep it under your tongue. I hate seaweed crackers. All of them. I've never finished a single one. But grandmother invented them so everyone could live, that first night, and as long as I keep pressing them, it's a little bit her feeding the city. So I smile, and I sell.
textes.Je vais vous dire un secret, {surnom}, m: I shall tell you a secret, {surnom}, but it is not protocolary. I'm still as shy as I was at ten. The rules, the speeches, the bows, they're so I know what to do with my hands. When I don't know what to say to someone I like, I write them a decree. You'll surely get one.
textes.Je vais vous dire un secret, {surnom}. D: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. Since the seventh roof, bangs make my hands shake. All of them. Even my own. Before every shot, I put wax in my ears, and I shout “BOOM!” myself, very loudly, so I'm less scared. Nobody knows. Especially not the professor. He'd be sad, and I don't want him to be sad because of me.
textes.Je vais vous dire un secret, {surnom}. J: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I'm always afraid. Of monsters, of the dark, of frogs, of stairs. But when someone is hurt, my fear goes quiet. Just long enough to heal them. Afterwards, it comes back, and I shake. Nobody sees it, because I pray very loudly to hide the sound of my knees knocking.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I forget many things: dates, keys, the name of my town. It frightens me sometimes, at night. So I write the name of every inhabitant in a little notebook, in the lining of my hat. Every morning I read them again. As long as I remember them, I'm a good baron.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I know every Bilge Rats song by heart. Every drum part. I've even made up better ones. It's not the drums that scare me. It's being looked at. And people saying: “That's Lisse's son.” I'm scared they'll only see the suit.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. I don't believe the island floats only thanks to calculations. I believe it also floats because everyone here wants it to stay in the air. Don't repeat that. An engineer doesn't say that sort of thing.
textes.Je vais vous dire un secret, {surnom}. M: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. My very first box of nothing, at home, on the mantelpiece… isn't empty. There's a folded piece of paper inside. An idea, written down one night when I couldn't sleep. A really new idea, I think. I've never read it again. Never filed it. I'm afraid that if I open the box, I'll find out someone had it before me.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. My halo shines when I'm happy. Only three times has it shone so brightly it could be seen from the sea: three times when a visitor told me “thank you for the speech.” I remember each one. I keep them the way you keep shells. Perhaps you'll be the fourth.
textes.Je vais vous dire un secret, {surnom}. Q: I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. When I was little, I was scared in the cabin. Like Barnabé. My mother used to say: “Look at the people, not the drop.” I tell Barnabé that every day. One day, it'll work.

I'll tell you a secret, {surnom}. When I sleep standing up, I'm not quite asleep. I hear footsteps. I recognise everyone: Brunehaut's heavy step, Églantine's hurried step, Hilaire's dragging step, the little steps of Noisette following me. If an unknown step comes along, I open one eye. It's happened twice. Both times, it was you.
textes.Je vais vous dire un secret. Tous les so: I'll tell you a secret. Every evening, I listen to the Bilge Rats behind the door of the Hall. I know all the songs by heart. All the drum parts. I've even made up better ones. But I don't have drumsticks. And I don't have the nerve. Above all, not the nerve.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose que Firmin n: I'll tell you something Firmin doesn't know, {surnom}. The first twelve punch cards are in Honoré's hand. I don't know what they do. I've never dared remove them. Sometimes I think he's the one winning, not me. And something else: I have never beaten my automaton. Not once. Write that down. No… don't write it down.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose que je n'ai: I'll tell you something I've never told anyone, {surnom}. I know he won't come back. I knew it from the very first year, on the quay, when I saw that little cabin boy's face. But if I stop listening, who will remember Jules? Nobody here knew him any more. The bell isn't so that he comes back. It's so that we remember.

I'll tell you something I have told no one. The winter of the bath, when the lake melted, it took me three days to freeze it again. Three days. In the old days, one night was enough. I was afraid, those three days. Not for the lake: for myself. I thought the cold was leaving me. I don't hold the bath against Pyra. I hold it against her that she made me see that.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose que je n'écr: I'll tell you something I never write in my reports, {surnom}. I don't believe the island floats only thanks to calculations. I believe it also floats because everyone here wants it to stay up. An engineer shouldn't say that. So I say it very quietly. And have another tea.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose que je ne di: I'll tell you something I'll never tell Sylvie, {surnom}. She'd be far too right. These days without a camera are the best of my holiday. I've watched Théo. For real, no viewfinder. I saw him laugh. He has a laugh I didn't know he had. I haven't got a single photo of it. And I remember it perfectly.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose que personne: I'll tell you something nobody knows, {surnom}. I never defended my thesis. I left a month before, with my old book and my trunk. Here, the sign painter wrote “Dr” on the window without asking me. I never dared have it removed. In the morning, when I clean the windows, I go very quickly over those two letters.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose, {surnom}, m: I'll tell you something, {surnom}, but not out loud. The wings were my present. I always dreamed of flying, without ever daring. As a girl, I was the one afraid of heights, and I was the one who pushed Achille to jump in my place. He's still jumping in my place. I feel guilty knowing he's up there. And secretly… I envy him.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose, {surnom}, q: I'll tell you something, {surnom}, that I've never told anyone. I find everything the Baron loses, except one thing: the little notebook of names he hides in his hat. I never look for it. I know where it is. I pretend not to know, because it's the only secret he thinks he has.

I'll tell you something, {surnom}, that isn't in the regulations. In my helmet, there's a little drawing. A dragon, drawn by Noisette when she was five, with this written underneath: “For the captain, just in case.” I've kept it for three years. If a dragon ever comes, I'll be ready. So will the drawing.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose, {surnom}. I: I'll tell you something, {surnom}. Fifty years ago, Brasero and a band of youngsters crossed the Chasm to found the Fronde and live their own way. The elders of the Guild were furious. I was young. I carried their first planks for the Bridge. I never told the Guild. Now, the Guild is me. So I'm telling it.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose, {surnom}. L: I'll tell you something, {surnom}. In the evening, from the Guild balcony, I watch the lights of the Fronde come on. I hear their music. They are free, noisy, colourful, a little mad. They are everything I never dared to be. I watch over them from afar. With pride. The way you watch your children cross, on their own, a bridge you helped to build.
textes.Je vais vous dire une chose, {surnom}. O: I'll tell you something, {surnom}. People think I'm serious, careful, a bit grumpy. It's true. But every morning, when I switch off my lamp at the back of the Grotto and the crystals light up, my eyes sting. It's not the dust. It's because it's beautiful. I'm careful because I want everyone to be able to see it. For a long time.
textes.Je vais vous dire, {surnom}, mais à vous: I'll tell you, {surnom}, but only you. I have never taken my own cable car. Not once. Vertigo. At one o'clock, to get from the top station to the bottom one, I walk down the four hundred and twelve steps. In the evening, I walk back up. In ten years, nobody has noticed. Not even Écrou. Especially not Écrou.
textes.Je vais vous dire, {surnom}. Les cinq cr: I shall tell you something, {surnom}. Five of the croissants are for the seagulls, because Margaret used to do it. The sixth I eat on the jetty, to keep her company. And the dragon tooth… I know perfectly well it's a sardine bone. I knew it straight away. But Fernand looked so proud. I love it all the same. An object doesn't need to be real to be precious.
textes.Je vais vous dire, {surnom}. À dix-neuf: I'll tell you something, {surnom}. When I was nineteen, just once, my energy worked. A whole minute. My mother's lamp lit up without a drop of oil, with a soft blue light. I was so moved I didn't write anything down. Forty years I've been looking for that minute. Mum passed away before I found it again. When Céleste talked about the blue glow of Stoneheart… I cried into my coffee.
textes.Je vais à l'Enclume Bleue un lundi par m: I've been going to the Blue Anvil one Monday a month for seven years. I say: “The cog, Hector.” He says: “No time.” I say: “You have time to forge swords for the tourists.” He says: “Hm.” Eighty-four Mondays. I counted. He's never changed a word.
textes.Je veille sur la Libellule pendant qu'el: I watch over the Dragonfly while she sleeps. She tugs a little at her mooring at night. She's dreaming of voyages.
I came to talk to you about the weather.
textes.Je vendais des glaces, avant. Puis Bruno: I used to sell ice cream. Then Bruno came along. You can't compete with Bruno.
textes.Je vends aussi aux autres villes. Les pi: I sell to the other towns too. The pirates of Tazira bought all my fan hats. It's hot down south.
textes.Je vends des galettes au coin de la Plac: I've been selling galettes on the corner of Cogwheel Square for forty years. Honorine's Marmite is right next door. We don't compete: we wink at each other.
textes.Je vends les potions d'Aubin ici, au pie: I sell Aubin's potions here, at the foot of the Fangs. They heal well. They change your colour a bit. Adventurers come up from the dungeon green, blue, pink. Like a tired rainbow.
textes.Je vends mes trouvailles au Marché, cont: I sell my finds at the Market, for coins: Bedaine turns green with envy. The Seven-Day Swap? A phoenix feather, really a painted pheasant feather, went back and forth between us seven days running, until little Mochi bought it for a mooncake. And in the evening, I play the flute at the Circle. The moon doesn't pay, but she listens.
textes.Je veux construire une ville en sable. P: I want to build a sand town. Not a castle, a town! With streets, a fountain, a bakery for Nina, and a lighthouse that really turns. Kiki says I can. Kiki knows.
textes.Je veux des dorades, petit frère. Pas cr: I want sea bream, little brother. Without the shouting.
textes.Je veux devenir créateur de jeux. Mon je: I want to be a game designer. My own game will have dragons, flying cars and an old robot who sweeps. Zéro will be the hero. He doesn't know yet.
textes.Je veux m'asseoir à côté de la fenêtre !: I want to sit by the window!
textes.Je veux m'inscrire au tournoi !: I want to enter the tournament!
textes.Je veux son piano. Je l'ai voulu dès que: I want his piano. I've wanted it since the moment I saw it on the quay, with its missing key: an incomplete piano, how marvellous! I offered two hundred coins and a backwards watch. Gonzague said “Ho!”, which means no, in his language. I come back every month. One day, he'll say “Ho?”
textes.Je veux voir la Lune ! Maintenant !: I want to see the Moon! Now!
textes.Je veux voir le maître du port ! Ou au m: I want to see the harbour master! Or at least his hat!
textes.Je veux être astronome, comme Céleste. O: I want to be an astronomer, like Céleste. Or chief engineer, like Héloïse. Or both. I'm calculating how much time it takes.
textes.Je veux être liftier depuis que j'ai cin: I've wanted to be a liftkeeper since I was five. I found out I was afraid of heights at six, in the cabin. I decided that was no reason. My knees still don't agree.
Then I'll come on both days.
textes.Je viens ! Enfin… je viens si on ne va p: I'm coming! Well… I'll come if we don't go too far. Or too near the monsters. I'm coming!
textes.Je viens avec toi quand la ligne rouvre: I'm coming with you when the line reopens!
textes.Je viens avec vous ! Si vous êtes blessé: I'm coming with you! If you get hurt, I'll heal you. If I get scared, I'll pray. There'll be a lot of praying.
textes.Je viens avec vous. J'ai pris trois livr: I'm coming with you. I've brought three books. And my staff. And my crystals. Especially the crystals.
textes.Je viens chaque jour voir pousser les to: I come every day to watch the tomatoes grow. They grow when I'm not looking. So I look the other way, really hard.
textes.Je viens d'un autre monde, au-delà de la: I come from another world, beyond the sea.
textes.Je viens d'un petit village de montagne: I come from a little mountain village where nothing ever happened. Nothing! I read every legend in the library. In each one, the hero had a rival. I came to Montjoie to find mine. You arrived. It's destiny.
textes.Je viens de Bourg-Tranquille, un village: I come from Bourg-Tranquille, a mountain village where nothing happened. Nothing! The big event of the year was the goat race. I read every legend in the library, three times. In every one, the hero had a rival. I looked for mine among the goats. None of them measured up.
textes.Je viens de Carène, sur la grande île de: I come from Carène, on the big island to the east. My father makes pancakes, my mother makes cider. Me, I'd touch a bottle and it would fizz up to the ceiling. I'd touch a pancake and it would fold itself into a paper boat. At first, my parents found it funny. After the fourth cellar flooded with cider, a bit less.
textes.Je viens de Cliquetis. Chez nous, on fab: I come from Cliquetis. Back home, we make automatons: birds that sing, mice that sweep, a gentleman who bows. My whole childhood went tick-tock. In the evening, I read in the workshop, among the cogs. My parents told me: “Read the manual.” I read fairy tales. I read the manual too. Once.
textes.Je viens de Cliquetis. Mes parents fabri: I come from Cliquetis. My parents build automatons. I preferred books about wizards to books about mechanics. They said: “Go and see the archmage.” I came. I never left.
textes.Je viens des glaciers du grand nord, au-: I come from the glaciers of the far north, beyond the maps. There, you learn frost before you learn to walk. Here, I teach young people not to be afraid of the cold.
textes.Je viens du village, en face, sur l'autr: I come from the village, across the water, on the other island, from a house that smelled of tar and fish soup. My father fished, my mother mended the nets, singing. They put an oar in my hands before a spoon. At six, I rowed out to the reef to catch crabs. I brought back two. And a sunburn.
textes.Je viens du village, sur l'autre île. J': I'm from the village, on the other island. I took L'Hirondelle one day, and I never went back.
textes.Je viens déclarer mon pigeon. Il s'appel: I've come to register my pigeon. His name is Bernard.
textes.Je viens ici tous les jours depuis trent: I've been coming here every day for thirty years. The bench has taken my shape.
textes.Je viens ici tous les matins depuis soix: I've been coming here every morning for sixty years. The view has never been the same twice.
textes.Je viens inscrire mon nuage. Il est pass: I've come to register my cloud. It floated over my balcony three mornings in a row. I think it likes me.
textes.Je viens m'asseoir sur le rocher de la c: I come and sit on the rock by the waterfall to listen to the water. Water doesn't speak in rhymes, but it never stops. It taught me that a poem doesn't need to end. It just has to keep flowing.
I'm here for the contract trial.
I'm here for the inspection croissant.
textes.Je viens proposer une loi : interdire au: I've come to propose a law: clouds will no longer be allowed to hide the sunset. The Council is looking into it.
textes.Je viens rapporter mon grille-pain solai: I'm bringing my solar toaster back. It makes perfect toast. But at night, it sulks.
I come to watch the boats. And Cargo. He's so gentle, that big lad.
textes.Je viens, maman. Mais pas de sardines !: I'm coming, Mum. But no sardines!
textes.Je viens. Si l'éclair me touche, ne vous: I'm coming. If the lightning hits me, don't worry. It happens.
I live with Father, in the north tree. In the evening, he tells stories. I listen to everything. Without sleeping. Sometimes I forget to bring the basket up. The Zéphyr engineers wanted a steam basket. Hrmm. No. At night, I beat the big drum at the Circle. Slowly. Pépin beats too fast. After every party, we argue. He talks. Me, hrmm.
textes.Je vis dans l'arbre du Guet, avec Éclair: I live in the Lookout tree, with Éclair. Whole evenings without a word, and it's perfect. Every day, I read the mud of the big pond for Moustache, and the night's tracks for Croc-Gris. He can't see very far any more. I tell him what I smell, without him asking. I also keep an eye on the Zéphyr's landing ground. The engineers measure our bridges with string. I measure their boots.
textes.Je vis à la pêcherie avec ma fille Caram: I live at the fishery with my daughter Caramel and my granddaughter Myrtille. I fish, Caramel sells, Myrtille looks better than I do. Every day, Brume reads the mud at the edge for me. The children say a dragon sleeps under the pond: the King never asked for that much. And little Gland jumps about on the jetty. The fish leave. I stay. That's my trade, staying.
textes.Je vise le cochonnet. Il ne bouge pas, m: I'm aiming for the jack. It doesn't move, but it's crafty.
textes.Je vois ma maison ! Non, c'est la mairie: I can see my house! No, that's the town hall.
textes.Je vois ma maison ! … Non, c'est un nuag: I can see my house! … No, it's a cloud.
I see everything from up here.
textes.Je vois. Et toutes les fleurs aussi, mai: I see. And so do all the flowers, now.
textes.Je vole, je crie, je repars. Métier : mo: I fly, I scream, I leave. Job: seagull.
textes.Je voudrais aller dans la forêt des brum: I'd like to go into the misty forest. They say its people know plants that cure a fever in a single night. But people don't always come back from the mists.
textes.Je voudrais avoir les cheveux de Rosa. R: I'd love to have Rosa's hair. Red, with curls going everywhere. One day, I put some of Samira's madder powder in my hair. I was red right down to my ears. Mum shouted. Rosa laughed so hard she had to sit down on a barrel. She said it suited me.
textes.Je voudrais bien. Mais il faut être insc: I'd like to. But you have to be registered. According to the Guild rules, article one. I read it.
textes.Je voudrais dire à Honorine ce que je pe: I'd like to tell Honorine what I think of her. But when I see her, I blush, and the flour… the flour doesn't hide everything. She thinks it's the effort. It is the effort. The effort of saying nothing.
textes.Je voudrais m'inscrire à la Guilde !: I'd like to join the Guild!
textes.Je voudrais monter une fois, rien qu'une: I'd like to go up once, just once, to the leaf on Yggdrasil where Perlée and I were a single drop. And sit next to her. Without losing anything.
textes.Je voudrais qu'un jour, Brindille et moi: I wish that one day, Brindille and I could rest on the same leaf, like before. A single drop, just for one morning. She would cry, surely. I think I would too, this time.
textes.Je voudrais simplement changer le nom de: I'd simply like to change the name of my street. It's called “Sloping Street”. It doesn't slope.
I'd like to give you something.
textes.Je voudrais tant venir ! Mais sans mon c: I'd so love to come! But without my rosary, I feel completely naked. Well, completely… rosary-less.
textes.Je voulais garder la Grande Porte avec B: I wanted to guard the Great Gate with Bramm. He stared at me for an hour without a word. I talked the whole hour, to fill the silence. He said: “No. You smile too much.” The next day, the king took me on to guard his hall. He said: “A guard who smiles puts visitors at ease.” I've been there fifty years.
I wanted to make it shine.
textes.Je voulais partir chasser les jaguars du: I wanted to go and hunt the jaguars of Smoking Mountain. He looked at the calendar and said: “Not today.” I obeyed. I spent the day sharpening my macuahuitl in front of his door. In the evening, he told me: “Your weapon is ready. Your patience, not yet.” He's right. It annoys me.
I wanted a banana-peel necklace. Momo said it wouldn't last, but he made it for me. The first night, it was the most beautiful necklace at the party. By the third day, it was all black and the flies were dancing with me. Momo laughed so hard he fell off the stall. That's nature, I told him. I kept it two more days.
textes.Je voulais un lapin dans mon chapeau, co: I wanted a rabbit in my hat, like the fairground magicians. I got a pigeon. It flew off with the hat's feather still on its head, and before I could say “come back”, Pip had shouted “Gérard!”. Since then, he's been called Gérard and he sleeps on the dormitory roof, feather up like a plume.
I've already told you everything, {surnom}. But fine, since you insist:
I've already told you everything, {surnom}. But fine, since you insist:
textes.Je vous ai fait un bonnet de chanson, Mè: Shall I make you a song hat, Mother Downpour?
textes.Je vous ai promis de prévenir avant de t: I promised to warn you before firing. There, I'm warning you: in twenty seconds. Hide behind Basile.
textes.Je vous ai raconté %d chapitres de ma vi: I've told you %d chapters of my life.
textes.Je vous ai raconté le début de mon histo: I told you the beginning of my story.
textes.Je vous ai raconté tout ce que je sais s: I've told you everything I know about %s.
textes.Je vous ai raconté toute ma vie. Ça, je: I told you my whole life. That, I don't forget.
textes.Je vous ai soigné ! Et j'ai soigné un ca: I healed you! And I healed a pebble too, I think. It looks in great shape.
textes.Je vous ai à l'œil, vous savez. Depuis v: I've got my eye on you, you know. Ever since your “tiny bit”. No bicycles on the quay, I hope?
textes.Je vous attends au temple. Revenez entie: I'll wait for you at the temple. Come back in one piece, please. It's easier to heal.
textes.Je vous bénis ! Pendant quelques seconde: I bless you! For a few seconds, you're invincible! Well, almost. Don't do anything silly.
textes.Je vous crois, Cuauhtli. J'apporterai de: I believe you, Cuauhtli. I'll bring water anyway.
textes.Je vous entends très bien, Anatole. Tout: I can hear you perfectly well, Anatole. The whole Square can hear you.
I'll keep one for you anyway.
I'll let you get on with your work.
textes.Je vous mets la grosse tasse. Et je recu: I'll give you the big cup. And step back.
textes.Je vous paie en barques, cette semaine ?: Shall I pay you in boats this week?
textes.Je vous prêterai mon képi pour vous cach: I'll lend you my kepi to cover your eyes.
textes.Je vous soigne les yeux fermés. Ne vous: I heal you with my eyes closed. Don't worry, that's how I heal best.
textes.Je vous souhaite une excellente journée,: I wish you an excellent day, {surnom}.
textes.Je vous suis ! Je soigne, je bénis, et j: I'll follow you! I heal, I bless, and I'm very careful on stairs. Especially on stairs.
I've been following you for thirty-eight years.
textes.Je vous suis déjà ! Comme votre ombre !: I'm already following you! Like your shadow! A shadow that goes clang.
textes.Je vous suis déjà. Depuis la fontaine. B: I'm already following you. Since the fountain. Bzzt.
textes.Je vous suis, frère d'armes ! Que les mo: I follow you, brother-in-arms! Let the monsters tremble! And the pies too: I'll get hungry on the way.
textes.Je vous vois venir avec votre crayon, Ro: I can see you coming with your pencil, Rosette.
textes.Je vérifie le sel. C'est important, le s: I'm checking the salt. Salt is important.
textes.Je vérifie les amarres. Un dirigeable ma: I'm checking the moorings. A badly tied airship goes off for a spin all by itself.
textes.Jeu du Grosse-Dent ! Toi être Grosse-Den: Grosse-Dent game! You be Grosse-Dent! You roar! … (They run off, shrieking with laughter.)
textes.Jeu du caillou ! Qui lance le plus loin: Rock game! Who throw furthest? … Ploc threw at Pika. Pika not happy.
textes.Jeudi ! J'aurai des choses à… enfin, des: Thursday! I'll have things to… well, questions to ask the cards.
Thursday. The cards are waiting for you, my dear.
textes.Jeune humain… viens écouter une histoire: Young human… come and listen to a story.
textes.Jeune personne, une question importante: Young person, an important question: do you wear a hat when you go off adventuring?
textes.Jeune pêcheur, Brahim avait encore peur: As a young fisherman, Brahim was still scared of crabs. A crab in the net, and he'd jump onto the bench. I saw it. Lalla Fatima tells the story of the pinched finger to the whole port. Me, what I saw, I only told my boat. Once. The Mabrouka keeps secrets. Hm.
textes.Jeune, j'ai fait le tour de l'île. À Cli: When I was young, I went round the whole island. In Cliquetis, a compass that points south. In Carène, a telescope that sees the past. In Tazira, a carpet that doesn't fly: I've still got it. And in Tazira, I met Mbarek, the blue man. Our first deal took a whole day and three teapots. Ever since, every year: our honey and dried fish for his dates.
textes.Jeune, j'ai été mousse sur un navire mar: When I was young, I was a cabin boy on a merchant ship. I saw Port-Azur, and an island where the trees touched the sky. Then I came home: I missed the sardines.
textes.Je… j'écoute d'ici. C'est très bien d'ic: I… I'm listening from here. It's very nice from here.
I… I'm saving it for the end.
textes.Je… je m'assois un instant. Même les hér: I… I'll sit down for a moment. Even heroes have legs.
textes.Je… je m'assois une minute. Juste une. M: I… I'll sit down for a minute. Just one. My legs decided on their own.
textes.Je… je n'ai rien. C'est le sol qui a bou: I… I'm fine. It was the ground that moved.
textes.Je… je ne vois pas de quoi vous parlez,: I… I don't know what you mean, priestess.
I… I'm taking my time, Sigrun.
I… I'll be back. I have to run.
textes.Je… je veux bien venir. Je ne sais lance: I… I'd like to come. I only know how to cast lightning, but I cast it very well. Usually.
I… I'd like to ask you something. (She takes a deep breath.) Could I come with you? On your adventures? I'm very good at healing. I also fall over, but I'm very good at healing. If you'll have me, just tell me whenever you like. I'll be at the temple, or at the Guild. I'll pray that you say yes.
textes.Joe ! Bartholomé est en voix, ce soir ?: Joe! Is Bartholomé in good voice tonight?
textes.Joe ! Encore un enrhumé ?: Joe! Another one with a cold?
textes.Joe ! Il a parlé, cette nuit ?: Joe! Did he talk last night?
textes.Joe ! Je peux donner les graines ?: Joe! Can I give out the seeds?
textes.Joe a le perroquet le plus musical de l': Joe has the most musical parrot in the archipelago. Bartholomé sings the chorus with me, right on the beat. Out of tune, but right on the beat. That's already better than Gros-Louis.
textes.Joe a plein de perroquets qui parlent. I: Joe has lots of talking parrots. He says they're polite. They called me a “landlubber”! But he lets me feed them seeds. So we're pals.
textes.Joe garde le dernier témoin vivant de Ba: Joe keeps the last living witness of Barbe-Sanglante, apart from me: a grey parrot he calls Bartholomé. Joe doesn't really know it. He thinks it's just an old bird.
textes.Joe m'a demandé un jour combien de temps: Joe once asked me how long a parrot lives. I said: “A hundred years, sometimes more.” He went quiet, which never happens to him. Then he said: “So he'll outlive me.” I didn't answer. I lent him a book about birds. He gave it back with dog-eared pages everywhere. The ones about memory.
textes.Joe m'amène ses perroquets enrhumés. Pou: Joe brings me his parrots with colds. For him, I'm surgeon, barber, dentist and vet. His birds pinch my nose. He says they're kisses. My nose is covered in kisses.
textes.Joe m'avait juré que Rhubarbe était le p: Joe had sworn to me that Rhubarbe was the most polite parrot in the archipelago. He took him out of his cage, Rhubarbe looked at me, and he said: “Old sardine.” Joe went white as a sheet. Me, I paid double. A bird with that kind of temper, you don't leave him to just anyone.
textes.Joe vend des perroquets bien élevés, d'a: Joe sells well-mannered parrots, according to him. Rhubarbe called me an “old sardine” in the first second. I bought him in the second. Joe has an eye for birds. And for customers.
textes.Joe. Tes perroquets disent encore des gr: Joe. Your parrots still saying rude words?
textes.Joli rafiot. Il flotte encore ?: Nice tub. Does it still float?
Nice rhythm. I didn't hear a thing.
textes.Joli vol ! Toujours pas sorti du salon,: Nice flight! Still haven't made it out of the living room, but nice flight.
textes.Jonathan !: A banana at the bus stop!
textes.Jos ! J'ai tracé l'itinéraire jusqu'aux: Jos! I've plotted the route all the way to the hinges.
textes.Jos ! La spatule-goéland tient le coup,: Jos! The gull-spatula's holding up, you know.
textes.Jos ! Le Capitaine Floc'h a encore besoi: Jos! Captain Floc'h needs more sabres!
textes.Jos forge les plus beaux sabres de corsa: Jos forges the finest privateer sabres on the island and sells them for the price of fish. So I resell them for what they deserve. He shouts a bit. He's an artist: he doesn't know his own worth.
textes.Jos m'a forgé un compas pour mes cartes,: Jos forged me a pair of compasses for my maps, the most accurate I've ever had. He says he forged them over the fire of a pebble I'd brought him from the highlands. He smiles every time he tells it, I don't know why. Pride, surely.
textes.Jos parle fort, tape fort, rit fort. Mai: Jos talks loud, hits hard, laughs loud. But he forges the best needles on the island, and he knows how to keep quiet when asked. That, in Carène, is rare.
textes.Jos rêve de toucher les gonds de la gran: Jos dreams of touching the hinges of the great gate, and I dream of going through it. We've been preparing the expedition for nine years. We're very well prepared. We just haven't left yet.
textes.Jos tape sur son enclume au-dessus de ma: Jos bangs on his anvil above my head from morning till night. One day, he'll go straight through the deck and land in my tar. It'll serve him right. I'll help him out. But it'll serve him right.
Jos bangs on his anvil above my head all day long. One day he'll go straight through the deck.
textes.Jos, c'est le seul que je laisse toucher: Jos is the only one I let touch my stove. He hits his anvil hard and he talks loud, but when it counts, he's got hands like a lacemaker.
textes.Jos. L'aiguille courbe s'est un peu tord: Jos. The curved needle's gone a bit bent.
textes.Josette ! Ta soupe manque de champignons: Josette! Your soup needs more mushrooms!
textes.Josette m'a appris à faire la limonade b: Josette taught me to make blue lemonade with the class. We got spirulina everywhere: on the exercise books, on the walls, on the pupils. The whole class had blue tongues for two days. The parents were very understanding. Well, almost all of them.
textes.Josette nourrit toute l'école, une fois: Josette feeds the whole school once a week at La Conque. For the Sky Lesson, she makes star-shaped samphire galettes. The children eat them with their eyes closed, to imagine better. She says it's the first time anyone has eaten her galettes without looking at them. She doesn't take offence.
textes.Josette vient chercher sa salicorne tous: Josette comes for her samphire every morning. She tastes it before paying for it. She always smiles. I think she does it on purpose. She used to tease me for talking to my lettuces. Now she talks to her soups. I didn't say anything. I just smiled.

Josette comes for her samphire every morning. She tastes it before paying. If she pulls a face, I give her another bunch. If she smiles, she takes two baskets. She always smiles. I think she makes a point of never pulling a face. She's a friend.
Play the old one. For me.
textes.Joue-moi la chanson des tournesols, mon: Play me the sunflower song, my boy.
textes.Jouer Tonnerre sur la Grande Scène, avec: To play Thunder on the Great Stage, with the Rainville drum kit answering. They say she hits hard, that drummer. We'd see who makes the island shake first.
textes.Jouer avec Clapotis pour de vrai, en ple: To play with Clapotis for real, in broad daylight, without hiding. And make him a flower crown. Even if he says they're for girls. Which isn't true, so there.
textes.Jouer contre les Seigneurs de Xibalba, c: To play against the Lords of Xibalba, like the Twins. And win. And be home for dinner. Above all, be home for dinner.
textes.Jouer de la basse sur la Grande Scène… e: To play bass on the Great Stage… looking at the audience. Just one song. Just to see what people look like when they dance.
textes.Jouer la Valse d'Azur sur toutes les pla: To play the Azur Waltz in every town square in the archipelago. The village, Forgefer, the Bois-Doré. With a hat at my feet, like him.
textes.Jouer la chanson de la lune une seule fo: To play the moon song just once without clowning around. No funny face, no wrong note, no wink. In front of Pivoine. And for her to understand.
textes.Jouer un concert dans la Grande Colonne: To play a concert in the Great Column itself, a drum kit on every floor, from the Clouds down to the Azure Dome, and have all four worlds stamping their feet at the same time. And Ysaé singing the chorus.
textes.Jouer une chanson douce, une seule, deva: To play one gentle song, just one, in front of the whole Hall. Without shouting. And have the pit go quiet to listen. (He nods.) One day.
textes.Jouer une nuit entière au pied des dunes: To play a whole night at the foot of the dunes, for the caravans, the walking stars and the resting camels. With no amin to say midnight.
textes.Jouer une seule fois avec des musiciens: To play just once with musicians from down below, not in secret: a violin, a guitar, a bass that goes boom, and me with my “oooooh.” I think it would be the most beautiful song in the archipelago. Or the strangest. Either suits me.
textes.Jour 212 : naissance du premier enfant d: Day 212: birth of the first child of the dome. I was fifteen, he was howling so loud my quill slipped, and I wrote “Coralain”. He's been asking me to correct it for nearly a thousand years. One does not scratch out a scroll. And besides, between you and me, Coralain suits him.
textes.Joyeuse ! Le facteur du continent m'a ap: Joyful! The mainland postman brought me three love letters. Not for me, but still.
textes.Joyeuse ! Le sable est chaud, la musique: Joyful! The sand is hot, and so is the music.
textes.Joyeuse ! Mon métier chante, mes couleur: Cheerful! My loom is singing, my colours are bright.
textes.Joyeux ! Je suis toujours joyeux. Sauf l: Jolly! I'm always jolly. Except in the morning. In the morning, I sleep.
textes.Joyeux ! La musique me rend joyeux. Le g: Jolly! Music makes me jolly. So does grog. Both together, that's paradise.
Cheerful, on a desert island… Good idea. You need to keep yourself company. I'll find you one.
textes.Joystick droit : choisir | Gâchette droi: Right joystick: choose | Right trigger: confirm | Left ≡ button: menu
textes.Jus de coco ! Directement dans la noix,: Coconut water! Straight from the nut, with a straw, like in the jungle. You've got the soul of a coconut palm, my friend. That's the finest compliment I know.
textes.Jus de soleil, lait de nuage ! Pour les: Sunshine juice, cloud milk! For passengers feeling dizzy: a summit tea.
textes.Jusqu'à l'aube, Sylwen. Elle a laissé sa: Till dawn, Sylwen. She left her window ajar.
textes.Juste ce qu'il faut. Et ta tisane, encor: Just right. And your tea, still sweet?
textes.Juste cinq minutes, Grommelot ! Cinq pet: Just five minutes, Grommelot! Five little ones!
textes.Juste deux fois, Père Clotaire. Dans l'e: Only twice, Father Clotaire. On the stairs.
textes.Juste les abords, Amirale ! Les abords,: Just the surroundings, Admiral! The surroundings are geography.
textes.Juste sous la forge, il y a les première: Right under the forge are the first galleries of the Strata. When I hammer hard, they tap back. One knock, two knocks. That's our hello. The line has reopened: one of these days, I'm going down to shake hands with whoever's tapping. Firmly.

Right under the forge are the first tunnels of the Strata. When I hammer hard, they knock back. One knock, two knocks. That's our hello. When the line reopens, I'll go down and shake hands with whoever's knocking. Hard.
Just one Bastien, then. A little one.
Just a bowl. It wanted to be a pancake.
textes.Juste un moment. Combien en as-tu perdu,: Just for a moment. How many did you lose this week?
textes.Juste un petit bobo, Aurore ! Le nez !: Just a tiny boo-boo, Aurore! The nose!
textes.Juste un petit son, Barnabé. Regarde, il: Just a little tune, Barnabé. Look, they're dancing.
textes.Juste un peu d'air frais, alors. Tout do: Just a little fresh air, then. Very gently.
textes.Juste un peu. Autour de la passerelle. E: Just a bit. Round the footbridge. And a bird.
textes.Juste un. Ou deux. Votre balcon porte ch: Just one. Or two. Your balcony brings luck.
textes.Juste une ! Pour un tout petit cacao !: Just one! For a teeny little cacao!
textes.Juste une ! … Bon, onze. Le soleil, il f: Just one! … OK, eleven. Does the sun make a noise?
textes.Juste une fois, sans patron, sans salair: Just once, no boss, no wage. To know what it feels like. And afterwards, I'd come back to the Perroquet. Toni would be too heartbroken.
Just one sip. To taste the sun.
textes.Juste une nuit, Aëlwen. Un oiseau chanta: Just one night, Aëlwen. A bird was singing out of tune; it was charming.
Just a little one, Mother Sage.
textes.Juste une petite, Xóchitl ! Une toute pe: Just a small one, Xóchitl! A teeny little rain!
textes.Juste une pincée, Mama ! Pour réveiller: Just a pinch, Mama! To wake up your cinnamon!
textes.Juste une, une petite. Pour te faire pla: Just one, a tiny one. To make you happy.
textes.Juste à côté de la Gare, il y a le Belvé: Right next to the Station is the glass Belvedere: the floor is see-through, over thin air. You can see Hautefond, the Column, the sea… I go every evening. Barnabé promised to come. One day. He said “one day” trembling a little.
textes.Justement. Elle a tourné en rond toute l: Exactly. It went round in circles all night.
Precisely. I made a note of it.
Exactly. I prefer to say it beforehand.
textes.Justement. Tu me les dois depuis trois s: Exactly. You've owed me them for three centuries.
textes.KIAAA ! Allez, tout le monde, plus serré: KIAAA! Come on, everyone, closer together!
textes.KIAAA ! KIA-KIA ! … Ha ha ha ! Pardon, c: KIAAA! KIA-KIA! … Ha ha ha! Sorry, that's how I say hello. My name's Mouette, I play bass in the Bilge Rats, and I do a really good seagull. Too good. The real ones come and ask me for chips.
textes.KIAAA ! La fille aux cheveux bleus imite: KYAAA! The girl with blue hair imitates our cry. She has a terrible accent. We love her anyway.
textes.KIAAA ! Tu es une belle personne ! Les m: KIAAA! You're a lovely person! The seagulls are going to adore you. They'll follow you everywhere. Get lots of chips ready.
textes.KIAAA ! Ça veut dire : « J'ai faim, j'ai: KYAAA! That means: “I'm hungry, I'm cold, I'm hungry, it's sunny, I'm hungry.”
textes.Kalda ! Tu as vu ma chèvre noire ?: Kalda! Have you seen my black goat?
textes.Kalda ! Tu… tu montes au cratère, aujour: Kalda! Are you… are you going up to the crater today?
textes.Kalda a les yeux de ma sœur et mes jambe: Kalda has my sister's eyes and my legs. She climbs higher than anyone and comes down faster. One day, she'll guard the gate.
textes.Kalda court sur les pentes comme mes chè: Kalda runs on the slopes like my goats, only faster and less silly. Without her, I'd have lost half the herd to the golems.
textes.Kalda est la meilleure éclaireuse de la: Kalda is the best scout on the mountain and the worst at dictating: she talks fast, she forgets the sky, and she's a terrible liar when I ask her the question.
textes.Kalda m'a demandé un soir comment on fai: One evening, Kalda asked me how you let someone know you like them without saying it. I answered: “Like goats do. You climb on them.” She laughed. The next day, there was a pretty red stone on Fundin's anvil. He took it for ore and threw it in the fire. Boys.
textes.Kalda monte au bord du cratère comme on: Kalda climbs to the edge of the crater the way you'd pop out for bread. She's afraid of nothing. Me, I'm afraid of her. A bit. A lot.
textes.Karim garde mon plus grand secret. Enfin: Karim is keeping my biggest secret. Well, he keeps it the way you keep a bird in an open hand. The whole souk knows, except Rachid. That's already quite a feat.
textes.Karim me paie en dattes. Une poignée par: Karim pays me in dates. A handful per delivery. But his hand is small, so I asked him to pay with my uncle Mbarek's hand. He said no. So I eat half the dates while I run. It gives me a boost. That's why I run fast.
textes.Karim, c'est mon voisin et mon pire conc: Karim is my neighbour and my worst rival… at jokes. He guesses shoe sizes, I guess purses. And right now, he's hiding something at the back of his stall. I can smell it.
textes.Karim, il m'a vendu les babouches les pl: Karim sold me the softest slippers in the world. Yellow! And he's keeping my secret. Well… he keeps it really hard, but he whispers it to everyone.
textes.Karim, il vend des babouches et il devin: Karim sells babouches and he can guess people's feet. He pays me in dates to deliver. I'm the fastest delivery boy in Tazira! Not the most accurate.
textes.Karim, mon frère, tu connais ma pointure: Karim, my brother, do you know my wedding shoe size?
textes.Karim, mon voisin d'échoppe. Il fait des: Karim, my workshop neighbour. He cracks jokes all day long, I hammer all day long. One of us is bothering the other. Not me.
textes.Karkinos ! Le Crabe-Roi des vieilles cha: Karkinos! The King Crab from the old sea shanties! You defeated him? Gaston, we're writing a song. “There once was a little hero…”
textes.Karkinos entre en furie ! Il va charger: Karkinos goes into a fury! He's about to charge: when he scrapes the ground, step out of his path.
textes.Karkinos s'effondre dans un fracas de ca: Karkinos collapses with a crash of shell! The portcullis lifts… and a chest rises from the well.
textes.Keep it ! Mettez-le sur l'ardoise. L'ard: Keep it! Put it on the tab. The golden tab.
textes.Keep it, my friend ! Mettez-le sur l'ard: Keep it, my friend! Put it on the tab.
textes.Kenavo ! Ça veut dire « à la revoyure »,: Kenavo! That means “see you around”, where we come from.
textes.Kenji Volt, réparateur. Androïdes, drone: Kenji Volt, repairman. Androids, drones, vending machines, robot arms, smart toasters… If it has a plug, I fix it. If it doesn't, I give it one. (He wiggles the fingers of his metal arm.) And this is my best repair job.
textes.Kenji m'a remonté un bras à l'envers, un: Kenji once put one of my arms on backwards. I swept backwards for a whole day. It was very restful.
textes.Kenji m'a rendu un aspirateur que j'avai: Kenji gave me back a vacuum cleaner I had “improved”. With a note: “Never again.” I kept it as a souvenir.
textes.Kenji me répare depuis vingt ans. Il ne: Kenji has been repairing me for twenty years. He never makes me pay. I sweep in front of his workshop every day. We're even. Well, he says we're even.
textes.Kenji répare tout ce que mes programmes…: Kenji repairs everything my programs… improve. We help each other out, in a way. He doesn't see it like that.
textes.Kenji, Mio m'envoie pour la voix de Zéro: Kenji, Mio sent me about Zéro's voice.
textes.Kevin ! Mon client, là-bas, il fait des: Kevin! My customer over there is waving. Is that a hello?
textes.Kevin ! Quand tu veux, gamin !: Kevin! Any time you like, kid!
textes.Kevin ! Tu viens dimanche ? Je fais des: Kevin! Are you coming on Sunday? I'm doing sardines.
textes.Kevin avait trois ans. Je vidais les sar: Kevin was three. I was gutting sardines, I turn round: no more Kevin. I hear him laughing. He was in the sardine tub, up to his neck, and swimming in it! Breaststroke, already. The customers were clapping. I pulled him out by his braces. He smelled of sardines for a week. Today he hates the smell of fish. I wonder why.
textes.Kevin dit qu'il nage plus vite que je ne: Kevin says he swims faster than I run. That's not true. We've never settled it, but it's not true.
textes.Kevin met au défi de remonter trois étoi: Kevin challenges you to bring up three starfish from the bottom of the bay.
textes.Kevin, c'est mon pote. Le meilleur maîtr: Kevin's my buddy. Best lifeguard in the archipelago, shoulders as wide as a pedalo. He fishes my customers out with a smile. Well, nearly always with a smile.
textes.Kevin, le maître-nageur, a des muscles m: Kevin, the lifeguard, has muscles but also a heart. He saved three tourists this week. Two of whom weren't drowning.
textes.Kevin, le maître-nageur, lance un défi à: Kevin, the lifeguard, challenges anyone who thinks they're a good diver. Nobody's managed it yet.
textes.Kevin, le maître-nageur, mon voisin de l: Kevin, the lifeguard, my neighbour on Lighthouse Street. A brave lad. He has the job I'd have liked. I don't hold it against him. Not much.
textes.Kevin, le maître-nageur, prétend qu'il n: Kevin, the lifeguard, claims he swims faster than I run. We've never settled it.
textes.Kevin, mon voisin de plage. Des muscles: Kevin, my beach neighbour. Muscles everywhere and a heart in the middle. He rescues people all day long, even the ones who don't need it. Especially those.
textes.Khadija avait quinze ans quand elle s'es: Khadija was fifteen when she sat down next to me. I taught her the first knot. She pulled it so tight you needed a knife to undo it. The fishermen complained: “Lalla Fatima, your apprentice has knotted my line for all eternity!” Today, her knots are perfect. Still a little too tight. I can hear it.
Khadija, my wife. She talks for two. Suits me. The Mabrouka, my boat. She lets in water. Suits me too. Ali wants to replace her. No. And Rosa, the pirates' redhead. Two or three times a week, at dawn, she rows with me. We say nothing. It's good. She rows like a woman of the port.
textes.Khadija, mon élève. Trente-cinq ans à cô: Khadija, my pupil. Thirty-five years beside me on the quay. A thousand knots a day: that's good, for a young one. She worries about me. She's wrong to. It touches me.
textes.Khadija. Ma femme. Trente ans. Elle parl: Khadija. My wife. Thirty years. She talks for two. She mends my nets first. I say nothing. She knows. I think.
textes.Khalti Zineb, la sœur de ma mère. Elle t: Khalti Zineb, my mother's sister. She runs the Fondouk, all her tagine dishes come from me, and she wants to marry me off. To anyone. As long as he has a camel.
textes.Khéty ! Dis-moi juste le premier signe d: Khéty! Just tell me the first sign of her name.
textes.Khéty dit qu'il n'a pas peur des crocodi: Khéty says he's not afraid of crocodiles. He says it from his boat, in the middle of the river. Easy.
Khéty says he isn't afraid of crocodiles. He says it from his boat, in the middle of the river. Easy. But he's my friend. He snores, he exaggerates, and he comes when you call him.
textes.Khéty est drôle, bruyant, et il nous app: Khéty is funny, noisy, and he brings us a perch every week, “for Nebet”. Nebet adores perch. So do I. I don't thank him enough.
textes.Khéty jure qu'il a vu un crocodile long: Khéty swears he saw a crocodile as long as a boat near the river mouth. Khéty swears a lot. But this time he looked sincere.
textes.Khéty m'a appris à lancer la ligne. J'ai: Khéty taught me to cast a line. I caught seven fish! But they looked at me with their round eyes, so I put them all back in the water. Maybe they have families. Khéty said I was the worst fisherwoman on the river and the best friend of fish. It's a compliment. I think.
textes.Khéty me fait traverser le fleuve chaque: Khéty ferries me across the river every afternoon. He sings out of tune, he swears a lot, and he believes the flood comes from the rain. I pretend to be asleep when he says it.
textes.Khéty me paie en poissons, il raconte sa: Khéty pays me in fish, tells his catch doubled, and makes the whole brewery laugh. And he loves someone. I don't know who. I'll find out.
textes.Khéty se moque de tout le monde. De mon: Khéty makes fun of everyone. Of my kiln, my jars, my face. He swapped two loaves to trick me. I didn't speak to him for a month. A month of silence, it was nice.
textes.Khéty, c'est le plus drôle de tout Per-H: Khéty is the funniest person in all of Per-Hâpy! He teaches me to fish, he tells stories about giant crocodiles, and he pulls faces at the herons. The herons never laugh. I do.
Khéty, thank you for the perch.
textes.Khéty. Il pleut dans les montagnes, aujo: Khéty. Is it raining in the mountains today?
textes.Khéty. Ma jarre, elle tient ?: Khéty. My jar, is it holding up?
Khéty. One goat. Not two. One.
textes.Kia ! Tu veux que je baisse ?: Kia! Want me to turn it down?
textes.Kiki ! Kiki ! J'ai besoin d'une tour en: Kiki! Kiki! I need a coconut tower!
textes.Kiki et moi, on parle depuis des années: Kiki and I have been talking for years about a punch contest: the Perroquet against the Coco Loco, in front of the whole town. We've set the date three times. Three times, we've found an excuse. The truth is, we're both scared. If I lose, I close. If he loses, he cries. So we drink each other's punch and say “not bad”.
textes.Kiki fait du punch coco, comme moi, mais: Kiki makes coconut punch, like me, but on the beach, in a flowery shirt. A good lad. He drinks at my place every evening. And the jungle boat doesn't deliver to me anymore. I'm not saying anything. I'm just noting it.
textes.Kiki m'a piqué ma recette coco. Je l'ava: Kiki pinched my coconut recipe. I'd pinched it from my grandmother. We're even, and he's my best friend on the beach.
Kiki pinched my coconut ice-cream recipe. I pinched it from my grandmother, so we're even.
textes.Kiki m'a prêté sa louche, sa lanterne et: Kiki lent me his ladle, his lantern and his shoulder, all on the same evening. I owe him at least a thousand punches. He won't let me pay for them.
textes.Kiki, c'est mon copain. Il est grand et: Kiki's my friend. He's tall and he laughs all the time, and he opens coconuts in one go! He says one day I'll make a town. He's right.
textes.Kiki, c'est mon voisin de plage et mon b: Kiki is my beach neighbour and my barman. He counts my rescues better than I do. He embellishes them, too. But he always has ice.
textes.Kiki, il a juré qu'il marcherait jamais: Kiki swore he'd never step on my castle. He swore on his machete! Once, he was carrying three coconuts and couldn't see his feet. He jumped over the moat at the last second, and fell in the sand. The coconuts too. But the castle, nothing at all. Kiki keeps his promises.
textes.Kiki, il me donne des pailles pour faire: Kiki gives me straws to make flags for my towers. Once, he gave me a pink straw, with a little paper umbrella. I put the umbrella on the biggest tower. Everyone said it was the best castle on the beach. Even a lady with a hat.
textes.Kiki, mon ami. Tu n'aurais pas vu mes no: Kiki, my friend. You haven't seen my coconuts, have you?
textes.Kiki, mon voisin de la gare maritime. Un: Kiki, my neighbour from the ferry terminal. An adorable boy who plays the ukulele under my window at midnight. Bad music, freely given, as he says. Given, yes. Not asked for.
Kiki. Midnight on the dot, last night. Again.
textes.Kiku. Quarante ans. Cent mots. Ce sont l: Kiku. Forty years. A hundred words. They're the best ones.
textes.Kinich ! Combien d'étoiles, hier soir ?: Kinich! How many stars last night?
textes.Kinich ! Peek' a toujours trop de poils: Kinich! Does Peek' still have too much hair?
textes.Kinich ! Ton moustique est toujours viva: Kinich! Is your mosquito still alive?
textes.Kinich est le garçon le plus curieux de: Kinich is the most curious boy in Yaxché. He says I snore at the stars. He tells the whole village. I don't deny it. He has his reasons. I have mine.
textes.Kinich et moi, on a fait un concours de: Kinich and I had a best-story contest. He told the one about the mosquito who bites the Lords of Death. I told the one about the Great Cat of the sun who cuts off the serpent's head. Pilli, from Aztlán, was supposed to choose. He said the best one was about his dog. He didn't even have a story!
textes.Kinich me suit dans la jungle. Il veut a: Kinich follows me into the jungle. He wants to learn tracks. He learns fast. He talks a lot. His dog barks a lot. The game runs off. We go home with nothing. He's happy anyway.
textes.Kinich pose plus de questions que le tem: Kinich asks more questions than the temple has steps. He knows the Popol Vuh better than some priests. He runs too much, he shouts too much. He listens, too. That's rare.
textes.Kinich vient lécher la cuillère de miel: Kinich comes to lick the honey spoon every day. He asks me a thousand questions about bees. His dog buries bones everywhere, even under my hives. He's like honey: he sticks, and you love him.
textes.Kinich, c'est mon copain de Yaxché ! Il: Kinich is my buddy from Yaxché! He has a mosquito in a gourd and a dog with hair, Peek'. He says Peek' is the best dog. Not true. It's Tlaco. But Peek' is second.
textes.Kinich, c'est mon copain de la jungle !: Kinich is my buddy from the jungle! We see each other at the fair of the longest day. He has a mosquito in a gourd and a dog that buries everything. He says his story is the best in the world. Not true. Mine is.
Kinich is my biggest fan. He copies all my moves, he shouts my name, he knows my matches better than I do. One day, he'll be a champion. After me. Long after me.
textes.Kinich, le garçon au moustique, veut bie: Kinich, the boy with the mosquito, is willing to lend Xan, his mosquito, to whoever goes down into Xibalba. But he's hungry.
textes.Kinich, le petit, a un chien qui enterre: Kinich, the little boy, has a dog that buries bones everywhere. If you need bones, ask him. Jaguars love them.
textes.Kinich. Ta calebasse est bien fermée ?: Kinich. Is your gourd closed properly?
textes.Kinich. Ton chien reste à la maison, dem: Kinich. Your dog stays home tomorrow.
textes.Kira ! Kira ! Encore le tour qui brille: Kira! Kira! Do the shiny trick again!
textes.Kraxx ! Ma lame vaut soixante, pas quara: Kraxx! My blade's worth sixty, not forty!
textes.Kraxx ! Un harpon qui ne se tord pas, ça: Kraxx! Is there such a thing as a harpoon that doesn't bend?
textes.Kraxx a vendu une de mes épées en jurant: Kraxx sold one of my swords, swearing it had sliced off a dragon's tail. The customer came back a week later to ask which dragon. Kraxx answered: “A small one.” The customer was so pleased he bought a second one. Kraxx came and ordered a sword from me that had sliced “a medium one”.
textes.Kraxx m'a vendu un bouclier si lourd qu': Kraxx sold me a shield so heavy it took two guards to carry it. Together. Mostly it protected the ground.
textes.Kraxx me vend des harpons contre les gar: Kraxx sells me harpoons against the gargoyles. They're sturdy. Not sturdy enough: the gargoyles bend them. He says my gargoyles eat iron. He's not wrong. He used to be a guard. He knows them better than I do.
textes.Kraxx vend de bonnes lames à de mauvais: Kraxx sells good blades at bad prices. Bad for the Guard, good for him. We guarded the ramparts together, long ago. He was a good guard. He's a fearsome merchant.
textes.Kraxx vend mes lames au marché. Il les v: Kraxx sells my blades at the market. He sells them well, I'll grant him that: he makes up dragon stories for them. But when it comes to paying me, he goes deaf, blind and comes down with a cold.
textes.Kraxx vend mes épées au marché. Il leur: Kraxx sells my swords at the market. He makes up stories for them: “This one cut off a dragon's tail!” A customer came back to ask which dragon. Kraxx answered: “A small one.”
textes.Kraxx, mon voisin d'étal, tape sur ses é: Kraxx, my stall neighbour, bangs on his swords all day long. Clang! Clang! It scares my customers away. So I put the ash pepper on his side of the stall. He's been sneezing ever since. We're even.
Kraxx, my stall neighbour, bangs on his swords all day long. Clang! Clang! It scares my customers away. And he sneezes because of my spices. We're at war. A very polite war.
textes.Kraxx. Le prix de la Garde, cette année: Kraxx. The Guard price, this year?
textes.L'ARDOISE DU CAFÉ CUMULUS. Lait de nuage: THE CUMULUS CAFÉ MENU BOARD. Cloud milk (moustache included). Summit tea. Sunshine juice. Whispering hot chocolate. Sugar puffs from the solar oven, morning croissants. Not a drop of alcohol: up here, we feast on the view, and it's on the house.
textes.L'Académie Infernale forme les jeunes dé: The Infernal Academy has been training young demons for a thousand years: flames, history, contracts, infernal manners and spark arithmetic. It's in the north-west of the Upper Town. You can't miss it: it's the building that smokes the most.
textes.L'Académie des Sciences est à l'est de l: The Academy of Sciences is east of the Agora. Laboratories, a lecture room, and the big board where equations float. If an equation falls on your head, don't worry: they're light. Except long divisions.
textes.L'Académie, c'est la cour où j'enseigne,: The Academy is the courtyard where I teach, the Professor's lectern, the library and the tower. Never go into the tower without knocking: the Professor does experiments in there. Or naps. Both are dangerous.
textes.L'Accueillotron : « Monsieur Lisse n'est: The Welcomatron: “Mister Lisse is not available. Mister Lisse is never available. That is his charm.”
textes.L'Accueillotron : « Pour descendre, adre: The Welcomatron: “To go down, go to the Offices. To go up, go to the terminals. To complain, go to the wall.”
textes.L'Accueillotron : « Puis-je vous propose: The Welcomatron: “May I offer you a glass of water? No? Perfect: it is more optimal.”
textes.L'Accueillotron baisse la voix : « Entre: The Welcomatron lowers its voice: “Between us… the punks upstairs make very good soup. Don't repeat that. Beep.”
textes.L'Accueillotron tourne la tête (vrrr) :: The Welcomatron turns its head (vrrr): “Hello. Your visit is important to us. That is why it will be processed in order of arrival, in 2087.”
textes.L'Achéron, une rivière d'eau noire et fr: The Acheron, a river of cold black water. On the bank, a boat, and in it, a tall hooded figure with golden eyes: Charon, the ferryman.
textes.L'Ahu du Couchant — ils regardent le sol: The Sunset Ahu — they watch the sun rise over the island, every morning, since forever
textes.L'Ahu du Levant — sept Moaïs alignés, le: The Sunrise Ahu — seven Moai in a row, backs to the sea, watching over the island
textes.L'Aile de la Lune. Un gouffre sans fond,: The Moon Wing. A bottomless chasm, a stone island in the middle, and two lovely slate bridges leading to it… Too lovely, perhaps. At the far end, on the ledge, a door and four dials.
textes.L'Aile des Marées. Un grand bassin, des: The Tide Wing. A great basin, rafts floating far below, and at the far end, a door on a ledge, out of reach. Beside you, a big bronze wheel: the tide wheel. Above the far ledge, the motionless sails of a mill…
textes.L'Aile des Rouages. Un gouffre noir, des: The Cog Wing. A black chasm, cast-iron platforms standing still on their rails, and on the ledge, against the wall, a big geared engine, stopped. Jammed, perhaps?
textes.L'Aile des Sables. Au milieu, un sable q: The Sand Wing. In the middle, shifting sand… quicksand! Paths of flagstones cross it. Four unlit braziers at the four points of the compass, and a stele in the centre.
textes.L'Aire des Duels, c'est mon royaume. Cin: The Duelling Ground is my kingdom. Five braziers all around it: an apprentice who lights all five in a row has understood fire.
textes.L'Albatros est amarré au Mât. Quand le v: The Albatross is moored at the Mast. When the wind turns, it sways like a big goldfish.
textes.L'Albatros t'attend au pied du Mât : mon: The Albatross is waiting for you at the foot of the Mast: climb aboard! The steward makes an altitude hot chocolate that puts your head in the clouds. And don't touch the speaking tube: the kitchen takes everything literally.
textes.L'Albatros, je l'ai construit avec des t: I built the Albatross out of tent canvas, barrels, and a steam engine I found at the back of a barn. It flew first time. Well, upside down. But it flew.
textes.L'Alouette, le deltaplane de Philibert (: The Alouette, Philibert's hang glider (at the Wing Workshop, west of Cliquetis)
textes.L'Amirale Morgane, de Carène. Amirale d': Admiral Morgane, of Carène. Admiral of a wreck! She's never commanded a ship that floats, and she bans mine from her coast. I've never run from her. I've taken detours.
textes.L'Amirale fait peur à tout le monde. À m: The Admiral scares everyone. Me too, a bit. But she gave me her hat, and you don't give your hat to someone you don't like. I think.
textes.L'Amirale m'écoute. C'est rare, quelqu'u: The Admiral listens to me. That's rare, someone who listens to a lookout. Her mother listened to me too. The Kerhervés have bad tempers and good ears.
textes.L'Amirale me demande chaque printemps co: Every spring, the Admiral asks me how long the hull will hold, and every time I ask for wood, she says “budget”. You can't plug holes with budgets.
textes.L'Amirale me laisse travailler sur la gr: The Admiral lets me work on the big table in her harbour office. She wants maps of the coast, I want the centre. We argue politely. She always has the last word. That's her job.
textes.L'Amulette du Serpent ! Reconstituée ! E: The Serpent Amulet! Put back together! Is it glowing green? On my map, under the big serpent, it says “Abyss”. And a little drawing of me running away.
textes.L'Amulette du Serpent s'illumine. Les ch: The Serpent Amulet lights up. The chains snap clean…
textes.L'Arbre ? Laisse-moi d'abord te parler d: The Tree? Let me tell you about it first. Ask me who I am.
textes.L'Arbre sacré respire à nouveau. Chaque: The sacred Tree breathes again. Every time I look at it, I think of you.
textes.L'Arbre-Mère a semé des graines sur tout: The Mother Tree sowed seeds on every island. The one Lyra guarded was the last to be dying. You saved it. The Wood will remember.
textes.L'Arc-en-ciel, aux lamelles de toutes le: The Rainbow, with gills of every colour. In the fairy tale, it makes the world ripple like one of Pigment's murals, and your feet leave a trail of colours as you run faster. It's the most cheerful of them all. And remember: in a fairy tale, yes. In the real forest: never!
textes.L'Arcade du Dragon-Pixel, c'est le meill: The Dragon-Pixel Arcade is the best place in town. There's air con, beeps everywhere, and nobody tells you to tidy your room.
textes.L'Archiduchesse Ignatia a la plus belle: Archduchess Ignatia has the finest bearing in the city and the simplest tastes. She wants tunics with pockets. I sew her dream dresses, with hidden pockets. We always find common ground.
textes.L'Archiduchesse m'a demandé une robe ave: The Archduchess asked me for a dress with pockets, to keep roast chestnuts in during audiences. I let out a cry. Then I thought about it for three days, and I sewed her a magnificent dress, with pockets hidden in the folds. She hugged me. That's not done, with a dressmaker. She did it anyway.
textes.L'Archiduchesse m'envoie : je descends c: The Archduchess sent me: I'm going down to fetch the Eternal Flame.
textes.L'Archiduchesse veut des robes simples,: The Archduchess wants simple dresses, with pockets. Pockets! To put roast chestnuts in! I make her magnificent dresses. With hidden pockets. Nobody must know.
textes.L'Arène des Cornes est dans la Basse-Vil: The Arena of Horns is in the Lower Town, to the south-east. In the afternoon the stands fill up and everyone shouts. Especially Madame Hurla. I say hello to the crowd. Nobody hears me.
textes.L'Assemblée a duré quatre heures, hier s: The Assembly went on for four hours last night. We voted on the colour of the new string lights. Pink. And the name of the new sofa: “Gaston”. It looks like a Gaston.
textes.L'Assemblée, c'est simple. Un cercle de: The Assembly is simple. A circle of sofas, a brazier in the middle, an adjustable spanner. Whoever holds the spanner speaks. The others listen. When everyone has spoken, we vote by show of hands. Even the children. Especially the children: they vote for things we'd forgotten.
textes.L'Atelier Libre, c'est une grande chaudi: The Free Workshop is a big boiler lying on its side, with workbenches inside and tools hanging everywhere. Anyone can come in, take a tool, fix their thing, and put the tool back. The rule is to put the tool back. Not everyone's got that. I'm thinking of someone who skateboards.
textes.L'Atelier des Inventeurs : des établis,: The Inventors' Workshop: workbenches, blueprints everywhere, inventions on the shelves, and in the middle, on its stand, an umbrella with a propeller on its head.
textes.L'Atelier des Inventeurs est à l'est de: The Inventors' Workshop is east of the Esplanade. Séraphin Altaïr drew his Levitators here, a hundred and twenty years ago. His plans are still on the wall. There's a tea stain on them. I don't wipe it off. It's part of the invention.
textes.L'Atelier des Lumières fabrique toutes l: The Workshop of Lights makes all the lanterns of the Strata, and it looks after the heart of the Brass Sun: the arc lamp in the middle of the sphere. Every evening at eight, a lamplighter turns the big crank to dim its light. Forty turns. On the evenings when it's my turn, I forget to count. The cavern stays all pink. People love it.
textes.L'Atelier des Scaphandres est au sud-est: The Diving Suit Workshop is south-east of the Square. The diving suits hang from the ceiling like big brass dolls. Visitors think they're people. I say hello to them, sometimes. They don't answer. Suits me: I need quiet.
textes.L'Atlantide ! Une cité entière, sous une: Atlantis! An entire city, under an immense bubble of air, thirty meters beneath the sea… You can breathe. In the center, atop its tower, a great crystal slowly dims.
textes.L'Atlantide ! Vous l'avez vue ! Racontez: Atlantis! You've seen it! Tell me everything, I beg you!
textes.L'Atlas des Vents, tome trois. Le tome d: The Atlas of Winds, volume three. Volume two blew away.
textes.L'Aube protège les débutants. C'est pour: The Dawn protects beginners. That's why there are so many beginners in Montjoie: they feel protected. And that's why there are so many bumps on heads: the Dawn can't be everywhere.
textes.L'Autel des Trois Soleils: The Altar of the Three Suns
textes.L'Enclume Bleue. Des lames qui coupent,: The Enclume Bleue. Blades that cut, axes that split. Looking or buying?
textes.L'Entrepôt Automatique. Des rayonnages j: The Automated Warehouse. Shelves up to the ceiling, robot forklifts honking, and an area of crates to push in the west. Way at the back, on a mezzanine, something is shining.
textes.L'Hirondelle a quarante ans. Je l'ai rep: The Swallow is forty years old. I've repainted her six times. She's carried kings, newlyweds and a goat. The goat was seasick.
textes.L'Hirondelle arrive ! Patientez sur le q: L'Hirondelle is arriving! Please wait on the dock.
textes.L'Hirondelle est à quai : parlez au capi: L'Hirondelle is at the dock: speak to Captain Léon.
textes.L'Hologuide est mon expérience la plus r: The Hologuide is my most successful experiment. It caught fire once, another time it took six hours, but today it gives the tour perfectly. And it has developed a bug I don't want to fix.
textes.L'Hologuide fait la même visite toute la: The Hologuide does the same tour all day long. I recite it with him. His favourite stop is number eleven, the fountain: he blinks harder. I'm the only one who's noticed. Why don't the others look?
textes.L'Hologuide fait la visite toute la jour: The Hologuide gives the tour all day, just as I do the welcoming. We're from the same family: people who repeat the same words with the same pleasure. He's very gifted. He says “beep” with a lot of heart.
textes.L'Hologuide fait toujours la même visite: The Hologuide always does the same tour. Always! I know it by heart. Stop eleven: the fountain. That's its favourite stop. I know, because it blinks harder.
textes.L'Hologuide, je passe à travers lui. Qua: The Hologuide? I walk right through it. Forty-two times yesterday! It tickles. It says no, it isn't ticklish. But it blinks. Hee hee.
textes.L'Hologuide, je passe à travers. Quarant: The Hologuide, I run right through him. Forty-two times yesterday! He says he isn't ticklish. But he blinks. I made him say “Welcome to Gloubiland”. That was my best prank. He keeps a copy of it, I know he does.
textes.L'Hôtel de Ville est la maison de tous !: The Town Hall is everyone's home! The forms counter awaits you, and at the back of the great hall a little door leads up to the belfry. A hundred and twelve steps. I climb them once a year, for the photograph.
textes.L'INJUSTICE ! OUI ! Enfin quelqu'un qui: INJUSTICE! YES! Finally someone who understands! Like people who mumble! Mumbling is unjust!
textes.L'Ingénieure Nova dit qu'il tiendrait un: Engineer Nova says it would hold an elephant. I asked: “And two elephants?” She didn't answer. I stayed here.
textes.L'Ingénieure Nova dit que l'île flotte g: Engineer Nova says the island floats thanks to calculations and tea. I've had three teas today. I'm doing my bit.
Engineer Nova says the island floats thanks to calculations and tea. I'm in charge of the tea.
textes.L'Ingénieure Nova vient emprunter des ou: Engineer Nova comes to borrow tools from the workbench in the evening. She always gives everything back, neatly put away, with a little note: “This is not a toy.” She's right. But it's still a bit of a toy.
textes.L'Ingénieure Nova vient ici ?: Does Engineer Nova come down here?
textes.L'Institut des Abysses est dans le dôme: The Institute of the Deep is in the eastern dome. The laboratories, on two levels; the Great Aquarium, with its round tanks of jellyfish and glowing fish; the Bathyscaphe Pool, where the Little Diver sleeps; and the Observation Bay, my favourite office. It has no walls. Just glass, and the Trench.
textes.L'Institut des Abysses et son Grand Aqua: The Institute of the Deep and its Great Aquarium
