textes.La Capitaine Héloïse attend ses rivets p: Captain Héloïse is waiting for her rivets for the Albatross. I finished them yesterday. I haven't told her yet. She comes by every day to ask, and I love her face when I say “tomorrow”. I'll tell her tomorrow. Promise.
textes.La Capitaine Héloïse boit un soda au gin: Captain Héloïse drinks a ginger soda before every take-off. “For balance,” she says. The day she forgot, the Albatross went round the Mast three times before leaving. I'm not saying there's a connection. But I'm thinking it very hard.
textes.La Capitaine Héloïse est montée pour la: Captain Héloïse came up for the reopening. She ordered a ginger soda. I don't have any. She had a cloud milk. Then a second one. She said: “Don't tell Zéphyrine.” Zéphyrine was at the next table.
textes.La Capitaine Héloïse m'a proposé un tour: Captain Héloïse offered me a ride in her airship. Me! In the Albatross! I said yes. Then I said “maybe”. Then I went and sat down. She said the offer still stands. She's really great.
textes.La Capitaine Héloïse pilote un dirigeabl: Captain Héloïse flies a red airship, up there. I pilot a yellow bathyscaphe, down here. She flies, I dive. We do the same job, upside down. She sees the Dome from above, like a blue smudge under the sea. Sometimes I see her airship's shadow through the water, when she flies low.
textes.La Capitaine Héloïse vole parfois si bas: Captain Héloïse sometimes flies so low over the mill that the sails turn on their own. She says it's to help me out on windless days. I think it's to scare me. It works very well either way.
textes.La Capitaine Héloïse vole tous les jours: Captain Héloïse flies every day, in a balloon, with no walls around her! She's afraid of nothing. She says she is, but I don't believe her.
textes.La Capitaine Héloïse, celle du dirigeabl: Captain Héloïse, the airship one, came down to see Bernadette. She said she was “an airship that's afraid of heights”. I said her airship was “a train that's lost its rails”. We shook hands. Old engine folk understand each other.
textes.La Capitaine Héloïse, de Hautefond, m'a: Captain Héloïse, from Hautefond, wrote to me that she sees the Great Singer from above, from her airship. I see her from below, from my bench. She passes between the two of us. Héloïse says “a cloud that swims”. I say “a mountain that sings”. We are both right.
textes.La Capitaine Nimbus veut que la barre br: Captain Nimbus wants the helm to shine. It shines. She can see herself in it.
textes.La Capitaine Zéphyrine a encore gagné co: Captain Zéphyrine beat Captain Héloïse again. So did Héloïse, apparently. The sky is big, there's room for two victories.
textes.La Capitaine Zéphyrine boit un thé des s: Captain Zéphyrine drinks a summit tea before every race against Captain Héloïse. Héloïse drinks a ginger soda at my brother's. They both say their drink makes them win. And they both win, as it happens. Each in her own way.
textes.La Capitaine Zéphyrine dit que la Libell: Captain Zéphyrine says the Dragonfly is faster than my glider. Going up, yes. Going up, even a party balloon is faster than me. That's not the point.
textes.La Capitaine Zéphyrine dort à la Capitai: Captain Zéphyrine sleeps at the Harbour Master's Office. Me, I sleep here with one eye open. That one watches the stars.
textes.La Capitaine Zéphyrine est rentrée chez: Captain Zéphyrine has gone home. She left a note: “Wake me if there's a race.”
textes.La Capitaine Zéphyrine et la Capitaine H: Captain Zéphyrine and Captain Héloïse have raced around the Column again. Each of them won, naturally. The Council receives two complaints a week. We file them together, in a folder labelled “Draw”.
textes.La Capitaine Zéphyrine me demande la mét: Captain Zéphyrine asks me for the weather before every race. I give her my forecast. She does the opposite. She wins. I don't know whether to be offended or proud.
textes.La Capitaine Zéphyrine veut que tout bri: Captain Zéphyrine wants everything to shine. Even the wind. I do my best.
textes.La Capitaine Zéphyrine, aux Nuées, et la: Captain Zéphyrine, up in the Clouds, and Captain Héloïse, in Hautefond, have been racing each other around the Column for twenty years. Me, I don't race anyone. It's restful. And I win every time.
textes.La Capitainerie : une grande carte des m: The Harbour Master's Office: a big sea chart on the table, little wooden boats pushed along with the tides.
textes.La Capitainerie du Port des Nuées : une: The Cloud Harbour Master's Office: a big window onto the pier, a crackling radio, a departures board, and a model glider turning under the ceiling.
textes.La Capitainerie est ouverte à tous : vie: The Harbour Master's Office is open to all: come and see the sea chart and its little boats. The clerk stamps everything that doesn't move. So don't stand still for too long!
textes.La Capitainerie, le soir : la radio grés: The Harbour Master's Office, in the evening: the radio crackles softly, the model glider turns slowly under the ceiling, and through the big window, the Dragonfly sleeps at the end of the pier.
textes.La Cascade ! Je vois la Cascade d'en des: The Falls! I can see the Falls from underneath! The water drops and turns into a cloud!
textes.La Cascade Arrabbiata — la sauce tombe d: The Arrabbiata Falls — the sauce pours off the cliff into the sea, which turns all red
textes.La Cascade d'Encre tombe du Mont Fusain: The Ink Waterfall falls from Mount Charcoal into the Rubbed-Out Pond. By day, it's white. At sunset, it used to be orange. It was the most beautiful moment of the day. I came here to write.
textes.La Cascade d'Encre — le ruisseau tombe d: The Ink Waterfall — the stream tumbles from the cliff into the pond in long pen strokes
textes.La Cascade des Falaises, au sud-ouest, f: The Cliff Falls, to the south-west, sound like rain that never ends. And below the cliffs, the stone Arches. The wind whistles through them like a flute. I go there to tune my poems.
textes.La Casse, c'est au sud-est, entre le Boi: The Scrapyard is to the south-east, between the Spore Wood and the sea. A graveyard of cars and machines, and my sculpture park. It's the only graveyard where things come back to life.
textes.La Cathédrale des Spores, c'est l'ancien: The Spore Cathedral is the old gasholder, south of town: a great ring of steel pillars, no roof, and inside, a forest of giant mushrooms that glow at night. There's moss everywhere. Walk softly: it's sensitive.
textes.La Cathédrale-Forge, c'est une seule mai: The Forge Cathedral is one house for two fires: Brother Cendrin's Ember Heart, and my forge. He says I steal his embers. I borrow them! I give them back to him as grates, nails and bells.
textes.La Chaufferie. Il fait chaud, ça siffle,: The Boiler Room. It's hot, it hisses, it rumbles: steam jets blow in rhythm across the corridor. The pressure gauge on the door, at the far end, is in the red: you need to find the three valves.
textes.La Chaumière des Glycines est dans la Ha: The Wisteria Cottage is in the Upper Town, near the lookout. A bed, a fireplace, a shelf for your trophies, and purple wisteria covering the whole front. Exceptional! And what's more, it's true.
textes.La Chaumière des Glycines, c'était la ma: The Wisteria Cottage was my grandmother's house. I can't manage to sell it, because I tell too many stories about it. I want to give it to someone good. So I exaggerate, to scare off the bad buyers. It works too well.
textes.La Chaîne de Montage ! Des bras robots s: The Assembly Line! Robot arms welding mover robots, a pit full of bolts, and three conveyor belts running toward the exit… or not. The switching console is right there.
textes.La Cheminée d'Air, cette colonne blanche: The Air Chimney, that white column, rises from the middle of the Square all the way to the surface. It's what we breathe through. Up there, a lighthouse buoy marks it for ships. And the Great Pearl, threaded onto it, is our sun: golden white by day, midnight blue and violet in the evening. We made everything. Even the sunset.
textes.La Chope Ardente, c'est le cœur de Forge: The Blazing Mug is the heart of Forgefer. The king has his throne, I have my counter. We know who people come to see.
textes.La Chorale des Pierres Chantantes ! Nous: The Choir of the Singing Stones! We're rehearsing for the full moon festival. Want to conduct? Take the baton!
textes.La Cité des Nuées est ronde, large de de: The City of Clouds is round, two hundred metres across, set on an upside-down mountain of rock. Underneath, four Levitators have held it in the air for a hundred and twenty years. In the middle, Sky Esplanade and Séraphin's Feather. To the north, the Zenith Tower. And everywhere, gardens.
textes.La Cité des Nuées flotte au-dessus des n: The City of Clouds floats above the clouds, right next to the stars. From up there, the sky must be so clear! I've already reserved a seat in the first cabin when the line reopens. And a seat for my telescope. It's very big.

The City of Clouds floats above the clouds, right next to the stars. The line has reopened, and I went up with my telescope. It took two seats. Alas, a certain Doctor Aurèle has put clouds everywhere. With names!
textes.La Cité des Nuées passe devant la Lune :: The City of Clouds passes in front of the Moon: its lights make a crown. You can even see the capsule going up.
textes.La Cité des Nuées — au-dessus des nuages: The City of Clouds — above the clouds (fair winds!)
textes.La Cité des Nuées, c'est fait : un ruban: The City of Clouds: done. One ribbon, one speech. That leaves the Strata and the Azure Dome… When all the lines are open, Hautefond will be the heart of four worlds! I've already written the remaining speeches. Two hours each.
textes.La Cité des Nuées, en haut, et le Dôme d: The City of Clouds, up top, and the Azure Dome, way down at the bottom… The people up here dream of going higher, the ones down below dream of the sky, and the ones in the Dome dream of rain. Me, I think the Column is there so we can go and see each other. All of us.
textes.La Cité des Nuées, en plein jour : on di: The City of Clouds in broad daylight: you can make out people on Sky Esplanade. Someone waves. You wave back.
textes.La Cité des Nuées, l'Esplanade du Ciel: The City of Clouds, Sky Esplanade
textes.La Cité des Nuées, le Dôme d'Azur… Quand: The City of Clouds, the Azure Dome… When all the lines are open, Hautefond will be the heart of four worlds! I'll need four ribbons. And four speeches. I've already written all four. They're two hours each.
textes.La Cité des Nuées… Je l'ai frôlée, une f: The City of Clouds… I brushed past it once, in the Albatross. But you can't dock there by airship: the winds whirl too hard around the floating island. You need the Column. When the line reopens, I'll go up like everyone else. In a cabin. With Barnabé. I'll hold his hand.
textes.La Cité des Nuées… On peut accoster au P: The City of Clouds… You can dock at the Cloud Harbour by airship, but only when the wind is calm: the winds swirl hard around the floating island. And Zéphyrine always says she got there first. So for the reopening, I took the capsule. With Barnabé. I held his hand.
textes.La Clairière des Géants — un grand cercl: The Giants' Clearing — a great circle of short grass, old oaks all around, and in the middle… a painter's palette made of stone
textes.La Clé du Brasier ouvre la porte des Neu: The Brasier Key opens the gate of the Nine Circles, under the Heart. I'm the one who keeps it. I entrust it only to someone who will go down for the good of the city, with the Archduchess's blessing. Go and see Ignatia, if you haven't already.
textes.La Clé du Brasier tourne dans la serrure: The Brasier key turns in the lock. The iron door opens onto a staircase going down… and an icy air rises from the depths.
textes.La Colline du Feedback — d'ici, on voit: Feedback Hill — from here, you can see the whole island… and hear the wind whistle
textes.La Colonne descend aussi sous Hautefond,: The Column also goes down beneath Hautefond, to the Strata and the Fronde, and right to the bottom of the sea, to the Azure Dome. Those lines are closed for works. I dream of doing the whole trip: from the sky to the bottom of the sea. The biggest lift in the world!

The Column also goes down below Hautefond, to the Strata and the Fronde, and right to the bottom of the sea, to the Azure Dome. The Strata line has reopened, and now the Dome one too! At last I'll be able to ride the whole way: from the sky to the bottom of the sea. The biggest lift in the world!

The Column also goes down below Hautefond, to the Strata and the Fronde, and all the way to the bottom of the sea, to the Azure Dome. The Strata line has just reopened; the Dome one is still closed for works. Me, I dream of doing the whole trip: from the sky to the bottom of the sea. The biggest lift in the world!
textes.La Colonne relie quatre mondes : les Nué: The Column links four worlds: the Clouds up top, Hautefond, us, the Strata, and at the very bottom of the sea, the Azure Dome. The Dome gate is right behind me. Twelve years “closed for works”. I'm the one who keeps the key. She's finally reopened! Behind her, the brass cage goes down to the Funicular. I knew it: the gate was creaking with impatience.

The Column links four worlds: the Clouds up top, Hautefond, us, the Strata, and at the very bottom of the sea, the Azure Dome. The Dome gate is right behind me. “Closed for works.” I'm the one who keeps the key. It'll reopen soon. I know it: the gate creaks with impatience.

The Column links four worlds: the Clouds, Hautefond, us, and the Azure Dome at the bottom of the sea. The Clouds have the sky, Hautefond has the view, the Dome has the sea. We have the hands: the rails, the lanterns, the crystals, and half of Hautefond's bolts. Up top, they often forget. It doesn't matter. The metal remembers.
textes.La Colonne relie quatre mondes, et quatr: The Column links four worlds, and four councils: Burgomaster Hector in Hautefond, First Councillor Céleste in the Clouds, Dean Agathe in the Strata, and me, at the very bottom. On reopening day, the four of us cut the ribbon together. Thirty centimetres of ribbon, four pairs of scissors: seven and a half centimetres each. The Burgomaster asked for an eighth centimetre.
textes.La Colonne relie quatre mondes, et sous: The Column links four worlds, and under the Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea, there's more rock, they say. Older than ours. The Dome Line has reopened, and I went down to say hello to her, on behalf of the Old Lady. They must be cousins. Introductions had to be made. I kept my helmet on.

The Column links four worlds, and under the Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea, there's more rock, they say. Older than ours. When the Dome Line reopens, I'll go down and say hello. She must be a cousin of the Old Girl. Introductions must be made.
textes.La Colonne relie quatre mondes, maintena: The Column links four worlds now, from end to end: the City of Clouds at the very top, Hautefond, the Strata, and us, right at the bottom of the sea. Four worlds, three lines, all open at the same time! Burgomaster Hector cried during his speech. The speech lasted two hours. He cried for an hour and a half.
textes.La Colonne relie quatre mondes, mon peti: The Column links four worlds, little one: the Clouds, Hautefond, the Strata, and the Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea, whose line is still closed. Four worlds, and not a single shared Assembly. One day, we'll all have to sit down together around the same fire. I'd like to see that before I put mine out.

The Column links four worlds, little one: the Clouds, Hautefond, the Strata, and the Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea, whose line has finally just reopened. Four worlds, and not one shared Assembly. One day, we'll all have to sit together around the same fire. I'd like to see that before mine goes out.
textes.La Colonne relie quatre mondes. Et toute: The Column links four worlds. And all the water flows down: the Clouds' rain falls on Hautefond, Hautefond's falls here, through my waterfall, and ours runs off towards the sea. Maybe all the way to the Azure Dome. When you think about it, in all four worlds, we all drink the same rain.
textes.La Colonne, c'est le plus grand bijou du: The Column is the biggest piece of jewellery in the world, if you think about it. A necklace that links four worlds, from the sky down to the bottom of the sea. The Clouds, Hautefond, the Strata, the Azure Dome. Four pearls on one string. Ysaé says I'm poetic. I say I'm a jeweller.
textes.La Colonne, c'est un grand tuyau d'orgue: The Column is a great organ pipe four worlds tall. When we play, the sound rises up to Hautefond. And higher, to the Clouds. And in the evening, when everything goes quiet, I hear things coming down. Bells. Winds. People laughing.
textes.La Conque était une vieille coquille vid: La Conque was an old empty shell when I took it over. The first evening, I made a samphire soup for six. Forty people came. I added water, salt, and lots of smiles. Nobody noticed. Since then, I always make soup for a few more people than expected. And a few more always come.
textes.La Conque, c'est la coquille en spirale,: La Conque is the spiral shell to the north-east of Pearl Square. The kitchen is at the heart, with the tables winding all around it. When I shout “Come and get it!”, my voice goes all the way round the shell and comes back to me. I hear it twice. It makes me stay polite.
textes.La Conserverie, l'ancienne usine de sard: The Cannery, the old sardine factory, is our big house. Downstairs, Lentille's Canteen and Trocante's Free Shop. Upstairs, the bedrooms. And on the roof, the garden and the assembly room. Everybody speaks up there. Even the shy ones. Especially the shy ones.
textes.La Corderie\nIci, le chanvre devient cor:
The Ropeworks
Here, hemp becomes rope, canvas and twine.
(Nothing else. We just braid.)
textes.La Corderie — ici, le chanvre devient co: The Ropeworks — here, hemp becomes rope
textes.La Corderie, c'est au nord, au bord du c: The Ropeworks is in the north, at the edge of the hemp field. The stalks dry in stacks, we beat them, we spin, we twist. Ropes to stretch the yurts, and for the big canvas over the stage.
textes.La Couronne d'Yggdrasil ! À ciel ouvert,: The Crown of Yggdrasil! Open to the sky, among immense branches, the top of the trunk makes a great square of living wood. But something is creeping between the branches…
textes.La Course de la Balafre, l'an dernier :: The Balafre Race, last year: the Widow was going to win. On the last bend, Corbeau hugged the coast to cut me off, and my bowsprit got caught in her shrouds. We finished hooked together. She says she won by a prow's length. It's not true. It was by a finger. Mine.
textes.La Crypte aux Runes, j'y suis entré une: I went into the Rune Crypt once, without a light. I heard something move. It was me. But I was still really scared.
textes.La Dent du Requin a été construite avec: The Shark's Tooth was built from the timbers of a wreck. They say the crew's ghosts still play here at night. They always lose.
textes.La Dent du Requin, c'est le seul endroit: The Shark's Tooth is the only civilised place on this island. You lose your money there with elegance. Sylvain, the croupier, has silver fingers and a heart of stone.
textes.La Docteure Opaline est la personne la p: Doctor Opaline is the cleverest person in the Strata. And the most absent-minded. She forgets her helmet every morning. I wait for her at the mine entrance, every morning, with the helmet. It's become my favourite moment.
textes.La Docteure Opaline et moi, on a fait un: Doctor Opaline and I had a contest: who shines brighter, her crystals or my mushrooms? All the lights off. Little Tom was the judge. He said “both”. Opaline says he'll make an excellent diplomat. I say he's scared of us both.
textes.La Docteure Opaline vient choisir ses cr: Doctor Opaline comes to pick her crystals herself, deep in the Grotto. She forgets her helmet. Always. I hung one on the Workshop door for her. She uses it as a pencil pot. Well. At least her pencils are safe.
textes.La Docteure Opaline, la cristallière des: Doctor Opaline, the crystal-maker of the Strata, ordered a shard of mother-of-pearl from the Trench. She wants to make a lantern with a piece from each of the four worlds. I picked her the most beautiful one. It shines a little blue, a little pink. Like the Dome in the evening.
textes.La Douat, le monde de la nuit. Un ciel d: The Duat, the world of night. A starry sky beneath the stone, a black river on each side, and at the far end Ra's barque, unlit. The silence… too much silence.
textes.La Doyenne Agathe a travaillé vingt ans: Dean Agathe worked twenty years in the mine before becoming Dean. She knows the Old Girl as well as I do. She doesn't say much. But when she looks at my board, she nods. That's enough for me for a month.
textes.La Doyenne Agathe parle peu. Moi aussi,: Dean Agathe speaks little. So do I, but a little more. Her letters are one line long, mine two. We understand each other perfectly. During the twelve years of works, she wrote to me every month: “Hold fast.” I never needed anything else.
textes.La Doyenne Agathe, aux Strates, m'a écri: Dean Agathe, in the Strata, wrote me one line a month throughout the twelve years of works: “Hold fast.” A hundred and forty-four “Hold fast”s. I kept every one. On reopening day, she shook my hand and said: “Well held.” I have never received a finer compliment.
textes.La Doyenne Agathe, en bas… Je lui ai fai: Dean Agathe, down below… I gave her a forty-minute speech. She answered in two sentences. People applauded the two sentences. I wrote them down. I reread them in the evening. They're very good. A bit short.
textes.La Doyenne Astrée est la seule personne: Elder Astrée is the only person in the world who fears none of my decrees. She listens to them, she smiles, and she does exactly as she pleases. I admire her infinitely.
textes.La Doyenne m'a demandé, il y a longtemps: The Elder asked me, long ago, to bring her back a song from down below after every stroll. I've brought back a hundred and forty. My favourite is a lullaby a mother sang in Port-Azur on a terrace. The Elder hums it to the little ones on aurora nights.
textes.La Doyenne m'apporte du thé au pied de l: The Elder brings me tea at the foot of the Spire. I tell her I don't want any. She puts it down next to me. I drink it. We've been doing that for six hundred years. It works.
textes.La Doyenne m'envoie. Que se passe-t-il a: The Elder sent me. What's going on with the Heart?
textes.La Doyenne répond à toutes mes questions: The Elder answers all my questions. With stories. She's got one thousand and forty-three years of answers. I haven't used up half of them yet. She says she's starting to run low. I don't believe her.
textes.La Doyenne sait tout, et elle ne dit rie: The Elder knows everything, and she says nothing. She only asks me to bring her back songs. I think it's her way of travelling with me.
textes.La Doyenne triche aux échecs. Elle joue: The Elder cheats at chess. She makes two moves while I check the time. I know. I check the time anyway. Those are our best moments.
textes.La Duchesse ? Non, une autre ! Ô Aube, e: The Duchess? No, another one! O Dawn, they all look the same!
textes.La Duchesse, la plus grosse grenouille d: The Duchess, the biggest frog in the lake, swallowed her rosary while she was blessing my jetty. The little sister screamed, then she cried, then she started praying for the frog to give it back. The frog burped. Just a burp. The rosary stayed inside. I've never seen anyone so sad and so polite at the same time.
textes.La Fausse Alerte. Pleine nuit. Une forme: The False Alarm. Dead of night. A shape climbs the Mother Oak. A long neck. A fiery eye at the end. I sounded it. Any guard would have. It was Hulotte with his lantern and his long telescope. He still laughs when he passes me. Me, I don't laugh. It was a drill. I wrote it in the log: “drill”.
textes.La Flamme brûle plus fort, la Bourrasque: The Flame burns hotter, the Gust blows wider, the Moonglow lasts longer, the Cog turns longer.
textes.La Flamme l'aveugle ! Le Scorpion-Roi es: The Flame blinds it! The Scorpion King is stunned: strike!
textes.La Flamme prend dans les ronces noires !: The Flame catches in the black brambles! They twist, crackle, hiss… and fall to ashes.
textes.La Flamme Éternelle ! Elle ne brûle pas: The Eternal Flame! It doesn't burn your fingers: it warms them. 150 coins, an extra heart, and a title: “Conqueror of the Frost Titan”. Bring it back to the Ember Heart, in the Forge Cathedral!
textes.La Flamme Éternelle bondit dans le Cœur-: The Eternal Flame leaps into the Ember Heart! A great golden flame rises to the vaults, and the whole city warms up at once. Go and tell the Archduchess!
textes.La Flamme Éternelle brûle tout au fond,: The Eternal Flame burns at the very bottom, near the Cocytus, the frozen lake: it's what feeds our Heart, from afar, the way a root feeds a tree. But down there, there's also the cold, and what sleeps in the cold. The Frost Titan. Keep your fire inside you, my child.
textes.La Flammèche se moque de mes serpents, m: Flammèche makes fun of my serpents, pinches my rum and borrows my boat without asking. Quite a woman. Quite a temper. I wouldn't want to be a sea serpent facing her.
The Door Flower only opens to the sun. She's very vain.
textes.La Fleur-Porte s'est ouverte ! Le Jardin: The Door Flower has opened! The Fairy Garden is right behind it.
textes.La Fleur-Porte s'est ouverte pour toi !: The Flower-Gate opened for you! Further on, they say, lives the Bramble Queen. She likes neither humans, nor elves, nor anyone. Be careful.
textes.La Flèche de Cristal, c'est cent dix mèt: The Crystal Spire is a hundred and ten metres of pure crystal, with the Heart right at the top. It keeps the island afloat, it lights the bridges of light, the fountain, the domes. Everything that shines here, that's the Heart. So we look after it.
textes.La Flèche pulse : bleu… violet… rose… To: The Spire pulses: blue… purple… pink… Way up high, the Heart beats to the rhythm of the auroras.
textes.La Fosse d'Azur, c'est un grand canyon a: The Azure Trench is a great canyon at the bottom of the sea, at the foot of Hautefond's cliffs. The Dome sits at a hundred and forty metres. Below that, it keeps going down. The cliffs are blue, covered in glass sponges and sea fans. When I switch on the floodlights, everything turns orange and pink. Like a garden that didn't know it was beautiful.
textes.La Fosse du Président. Une arène de béto: The President's Pit. A concrete arena beneath a glass office all in gold. On the wall, a giant screen lights up: two red eyes, a bar for a mouth… OPTIMUS-LISSE is watching you.
The Fronde repainted my depot one night. Stars, rails, musical notes, and Bernadette wearing sunglasses. I pretended to be cross. Then I bought myself some sunglasses. We match.
textes.La Fronde est la seule ville de l'archip: The Fronde is the only town in the archipelago where you can paint your house without asking. The containers, the boilers, the catwalks. Every house has its own colour. Bricole's changes every week. Ressort paints over it with his wheels.
textes.La Fronde nous a encore emprunté une pin: The Fronde has borrowed a pair of tongs from us for the concert again. Tonight, if you hear an anvil singing, it's ours.
textes.La Fronde résonne comme une grande coqui: The Fronde echoes like a big shell. If you whisper by the Mural Wall, they hear you at the Canteen. Granny Gamelle knows every secret in the cavern. She doesn't repeat them. She puts them in the soup.
textes.La Fronde — le quartier libre (ici, tout: The Fronde — the free quarter (here, everything is decided at the Assembly)
textes.La Fronde, c'est notre caverne, à l'est: The Fronde is our cavern, east of the Strata. Containers, old boilers, walkways, string lights. Nothing was ours at first: it was the Strata's scrapyard. Now it's the liveliest scrapyard in the world.
textes.La Fronde, de l'autre côté du Pont des F: The Fronde, across the Frondeurs' Bridge, is our noisy little sister. They play too loud, they paint our rails, they borrow my tongs. And when a furnace breaks down, they're the first ones there, with their tools and a song. We squabble. We're fond of each other.
textes.La Fronde, on la décide ensemble, à l'As: We decide the Fronde together, at the Assembly. The sofas, the brazier, and Brasero himself, who holds the talking key. Whoever holds the key speaks, the others listen. We've voted on the colour of the string lights, the cat's name, and the concert times. The cat's name took three evenings.
textes.La Garde veille sur les quatre ponts du: The Guard watches over the four bridges of the Circle of Fire, the harbour and the ramparts. But the danger isn't in the city, it's outside: the wild hellhounds of the lava field, east of the volcano. They're prowling closer and closer.
textes.La Gare d'Azur ! Bienvenue au Dôme d'Azu: Azure Station! Welcome to the Azure Dome, a hundred and forty metres under the sea. Breathe: the air comes down from the surface, through the Chimney.
textes.La Gare des Nuées : bienvenue au-dessus: Cloud Station: welcome above the clouds. Fair winds!
textes.La Gare des Nuées, depuis la réouverture: Cloud Station, since the reopening: a queue all the way to the Belvedere! People from down below looking at everything, touching everything, saying “it's so clean up here”. Of course it's clean! We recycle everything! Even remarks! … They're nice, mind you. A bit noisy. Nice.
textes.La Gare des Strates ! Bienvenue sous la: Strata Station! Welcome beneath the town. Mind the step, and mind the Sun: it never really sets.
textes.La Gazette sort tous les matins, imprimé: The Gazette comes out every morning, printed on a steam press that misses one letter in a hundred. The readers play at finding them.
textes.La Goélette : huit mètres et demi, deux: The Schooner: eight and a half metres, two masts, gaff sails and a real steering wheel, like the great captains. The most elegant, the fastest under sail (12 m/s).
textes.La Grand-Place des Lanternes, c'est ma s: The Great Lantern Square is my stage. The fountain for the rhythm, the storyteller for the words, the dancers for the feet. In the evening, all of Pandémonia comes by. Even Asmodin. He doesn't dance, but his foot taps along. I've seen it.
textes.La Grand-Place des Lanternes, à l'est de: The Great Lantern Square, to the east of the Upper Town, is the heart of the party. There's the fountain, the storyteller's corner, the music corner, and my big lantern. In the evening, everyone comes to dance there.
textes.La Grand-Place du Marché, au milieu de l: The Market Square, in the middle of the Middle Town: the fountain, Babette's stalls, Mélusine's bell… I play by the fountain in the afternoon. Mélusine rings her bell in the middle of my choruses. She says it's chance. She's a town crier: nothing is ever chance with her.
textes.La Grand-Place, c'est mon bureau. De là,: The Great Square is my office. From there, I see who goes into the Guild, who comes out of the forge, who buys apples from Babette, and who argues with Germaine. It's usually Babette.
textes.La Grande Alerte des Navets ! Quel spect: The Great Turnip Alert! What a show! Mélusine rings, the town runs, the turnips run faster, and Père Gaubert yells “gently with my little ones!”. I wrote an opera about it. Three acts. In the third, the turnips win.
textes.La Grande Alerte des Navets, c'est quand: The Great Turnip Alert is when they all wake up at once. Twenty or so! They run every which way for two minutes. Then they bury themselves again and sulk. You have to catch them before that. With a little tap. Not hard!
textes.La Grande Averse, c'était il y a dix jou: The Great Downpour was ten days ago. A pure white cloud, coming in from the sea. It rained clear water, so clear it washed the colour out of everything. The Palette overflowed, and the pots were carried off by the water. To the four corners of the island.
The Great Singer came by this morning. At my age, you know her voice. She sings a little lower than she used to. She's getting old too. We're growing old together.
textes.La Grande Chanteuse est une baleine. Une: The Great Singer is a whale. A very old, very large whale, who sometimes passes very high above the domes. Her song goes through water, glass, walls, and people. When she sings, the whole Dome stops. Even Josette's soup stops boiling. Well, almost.
The Great Singer is a whale. When she passes over the Dome, she sings, and everyone goes quiet. Even Ernest. Professor Benthos says she goes up to the surface to breathe. So she sees the sky every day! I'm a bit jealous of a whale. It's a funny sort of feeling.
textes.La Grande Colonne de Hautefond et la Lig: Hautefond's Great Column and the Cloud Line are the same shaft, really. On concert nights, the Fronde's music rises from the Strata all the way up here. The engines vibrate a little. Mélodie sings along. I don't put it in the report. Some things you keep to yourself.
textes.La Grande Colonne en allumettes trône au: The matchstick Great Column takes pride of place in the middle of the living room, complete, with its last match right at the top. The grandfather dusts it with a feather.
textes.La Grande Colonne en allumettes, entière: The matchstick Great Column, complete, with its last match right at the top. Nobody in this house dares sneeze any more.
textes.La Grande Colonne relie quatre mondes, t: The Great Column links four worlds, you know. The City of Clouds at the very top, Hautefond, us here in the Strata, and the Azure Dome at the bottom of the sea. A song is the same: a verse up top, a chorus down below. And the bridge in the middle.
textes.La Grande Colonne relie quatre mondes, {: The Great Column links four worlds, {surnom}. At the top, the City of Clouds, above the clouds. Here, Hautefond. Below, the Strata, carved into the rock. And at the very bottom of the sea, under its great glass dome, the Azure Dome. A single tower. Four worlds. Not bad for a salad basket.
textes.La Grande Colonne tient son horloge de m: The Great Column gets its clock from me. The departures clock, above the ticket office. Mistress Capucine and I check it every Monday at seven o'clock sharp. We say nothing. We nod. It's our way of being happy.
textes.La Grande Course ! Passe sous les dix ar: The Great Race! Pass under the ten lantern arches, in order, and come back here. Ready?
textes.La Grande Forge, c'est le cœur des Strat: The Great Forge is the heart of the Strata. Rails, wagons, the wheels of the Little Train, the lantern cages: everything goes through my furnaces. And that steam hammer there is Grand-Mère. Granny. She strikes slowly, very hard, and she never misses. Mathilde, up top, named hers Nana. We didn't plan it. Well… I don't think so.
textes.La Grande Galerie. Un rayon de soleil —: The Great Gallery. A ray of sunlight — so deep down here! — enters through a narrow shaft and strikes a bronze mirror. There are others, on stands. At the far end, on the door, a dull gold disc.
textes.La Grande Grotte du Clan — ça sent la fu: The Great Clan Cave — it smells of smoke, fur and fern flatbread
textes.La Grande Horloge des Strates sonne touj: The Great Strata Clock always chimes one second after the one up top. On purpose, they say: to give the sound time to come down.
textes.La Grande Liftière d'en haut, Maîtresse: The Grand Liftkeeper up top, Mistress Capucine… She says she can't hear a thing of the music coming up the Column. Anatole, the Strata liftkeeper, saw her tapping her foot under her counter. In time. I adore that lady.
textes.La Grande Pelleteuse siffle… un jet de v: The Great Digger hisses… a jet of steam! Get away from its tracks!
textes.La Grande Perle ne s'allume pas toute se: The Great Pearl doesn't light up by itself, whatever people say. Well, actually, it does: it lights up by itself at six, and turns violet in the evening. But the children think I'm the one pressing a button. I don't set them straight. It gives me authority.
textes.La Grande Porte mène à la cité. Bramm ne: The Great Gate leads to the city. Bramm lets nobody in. Nobody.
textes.La Grande Porte ne bouge pas. Bramm, le: The Great Gate doesn't budge. Bramm, the guard, eyes you suspiciously. He's the one you have to convince.
textes.La Grande Scène : vingt-deux mètres de l: The Great Stage: twenty-two metres wide, lattice towers, spotlights, walls of speakers. It's still missing the backdrop, which Lune has to weave, and Galet's ropes. And then it'll need a festival.
textes.La Grande Tablée, au Borgo, c'est deux f: The Great Table, in the Borgo, happens twice a day: at noon and in the evening. Everyone eats together, at the same table. Before eating, we sing. I'm the one who gives the A. And it's often a B.
textes.La Grande Tablée, c'est la meilleure inv: The Great Table is the best invention since the fork.
textes.La Grande Tablée, c'est sacré. Midi et s: The Great Table is sacred. Noon and evening, everyone at the table. Whoever eats alone eats half as well. That's Recommendation number nine. There are only eight, but that one's mine.
textes.La Gratuiterie : une longue table couver: The Free Shop: a long table covered in objects, and a hand-painted sign: “NOTHING IS THROWN AWAY, EVERYTHING IS GIVEN. One item per day per person, thank you! — Trocante”.
textes.La Gratuiterie de Trocante me donne tous: Trocante's Free Shop gives me all the old clothes. I cut them up, sew them back together, and off they go again as jackets. Nothing is lost. Everything is sewn.
textes.La Gratuiterie est au rez-de-chaussée de: The Free Shop is on the ground floor of the Cannery, next to the Canteen. It used to be the room where they stored the empty sardine tins. Now we store objects full of stories there.
textes.La Gratuiterie, c'est le paradis : on y: The Free Shop is paradise: you find everything there, for free. We only take one thing a day. Like the humans. We follow the rules.
The Free Shop is my throne room. Trocante thinks it's her shop. I let her think so.
textes.La Grenouille Repue est dans la Ville-Mo: La Grenouille Repue is in the Middle Town, near the Great Square. You'll recognise the sign: a frog with a napkin round its neck. It's my portrait. No, it's a frog. But it looks like me.
textes.La Grotte aux Cristaux : la roche s'allu: The Crystal Grotto: the rock lights up blue, ever so gently
textes.La Grotte aux Peintures — des bêtes roug: The Painting Cave — red and ochre beasts run across the walls
textes.La Guilde d'abord. Ensuite, la foudre. C: The Guild first. Then the lightning. That's the order, in the book.
textes.La Guilde est la fierté de Montjoie. C'e: The Guild is the pride of Montjoie. My great-grandmother founded it, so that adventurers would have a warm place to come home to. She used to say: “A hero is someone who comes back.” She wore a magnificent hat.
textes.La Guilde est là-bas. Ma table aussi. Et: The Guild is over there. My table too. And my book, which I left on it.
textes.La Guilde, c'est le cœur de Montjoie, au: The Guild is the heart of Montjoie, in the middle of the Middle Town, at the edge of the Great Square. Églantine's counter, the quest board, Mamie Rissole's tavern, Bertrand's stage. You come in a beginner, you leave a hero. Or covered in jelly. Often both.
textes.La Halle Hurlante ? Nous la transformero: The Howling Hall? We'll turn it into a “Premium Silence Space”. No talking, no singing and no foot-tapping. Especially no foot-tapping. (He taps his foot.)
textes.La Halle Hurlante a quarante projecteurs: The Howling Hall has forty spotlights, three mirror balls and a blinking sign. Half of it comes from the Scrapyard. The other half, I can't remember where from. It works, that's what matters.
textes.La Halle Hurlante, c'est notre salle de: The Howling Hall is our concert venue, the old forge hall, in the middle of town. Every night at nine o'clock, we play. It's free. Come and mosh in the pit: we jump, we bump into each other gently, we help each other back up. That's what moshing is.
textes.La Halle Hurlante, c'était l'ancienne ha: The Howling Hall used to be the old forge hall. I played the very first concert there, when there were still anvils. We used them as drums. They really rang out. So did the neighbours: they rang the doorbell.
textes.La Halle Hurlante. Ma place est à gauche: The Howling Hall. My spot is on the left of the stage. Rouille in the middle. Mouette on the right. And behind… a different drummer every night. (He sighs for a very long time.)
textes.La Jungle des Fougères — des fougères gr: The Fern Jungle — ferns as tall as trees, and hissing among the leaves
The Sky Lesson is every Thursday. We lie down in the playground, close our eyes, and I describe the sky: blue, very high, no ceiling, with the wind passing by. The children raise their arms. Once, Mila said: “I'm touching it.” I didn't contradict her.
textes.La Libellule ! Elle est amarrée par le n: The Dragonfly! She's moored by the nose, like a dog on a lead. A very big dog.
textes.La Libellule ! Elle passe sous nous ! Je: The Dragonfly! It's going under us! I can see the top of an airship!
textes.La Libellule : descente au Port des Cord: The Dragonfly: trip down to Rigging Harbour, on Sundays
textes.La Libellule : tour de l'île, à dix heur: The Dragonfly: island tour, at ten in the morning
textes.La Libellule : tour de l'île, à quinze h: The Dragonfly: island tour, at three in the afternoon
textes.La Libellule a quatre-vingts ans. Elle g: The Dragonfly is eighty years old. She creaks a bit on the turns. Like me.
textes.La Libellule, je l'ai construite avec Mi: I built the Dragonfly with Mireille, at the Workshop. Mireille wanted to give her flapping wings. I said no. She added them while I was asleep. They flap whenever someone says “thank you”. I've learned to say “much obliged” on board. It's longer, but it's safer.
textes.La Libellule, je l'ai construite moi-mêm: I built the Dragonfly myself, with Mireille, at the Workshop. Well, Mireille suggested adding flapping wings. I said no. She added them anyway, while I was asleep. They flap whenever I say “thank you”. I avoid saying thank you on board.
textes.La Libellule, la nuit : la nacelle est s: The Dragonfly, at night: the gondola is dark and silent; only a reading lamp glows beside an armchair, and through the big windows, the lights of the City.
textes.La Ligne a rouvert ! Ce matin, j'ai pris: The Line has reopened! This morning I took the capsule just to come back down and take it again. Three times.
textes.La Ligne a rouvert ! Hier, un monsieur d: The Line has reopened! Yesterday, a gentleman from up top crossed the Frondeurs' Bridge holding on to me. I didn't know him. Now I do.
textes.La Ligne a rouvert ! Ma sœur est descend: The Line has reopened! My sister came down from up top with an umbrella. Down here! I showed her the waterfall. She opened it anyway.
textes.La Ligne a rouvert après dix ans de trav: The Line has reopened after ten years of works. Ten years of letters, meetings and speeches from the Burgomaster. I held firm. It's not that I wanted to see the top. It's that I wanted the top to see us. Now they come down, they look, they come back. That was the point.
textes.La Ligne a rouvert, et ceux d'en haut de: The Line has reopened, and the folk up top come down to see the Forge. They stay on the doorstep, eyes wide, hands over their ears. Then Grand-Mère strikes, they jump, I laugh, and they laugh with me. By the third strike, they're family.
textes.La Ligne a rouvert, et j'ai enfin vu la: The Line has reopened, and I finally saw the Column from the inside! The cables, the pulleys, the counterweights… I asked Anatole if I could touch. He said: “With your eyes.” I touched with my eyes the whole way. My eyes were covered in grease.
textes.La Ligne a rouvert, et les gens d'en hau: The Line has reopened, and the folk up top queue to ride my train. They're surprised it goes round in circles. “It doesn't go anywhere?” I tell them: “Yes it does: everywhere. Then it starts again.” It's the finest way to travel. You always come back.
textes.La Ligne des Nuées part du Belvédère de: The Cloud Line leaves from the Belvedere in Hautefond and climbs all the way up here, inside a white glass shaft. Two hundred metres of sky! Halfway up, you go through the clouds. For ten seconds, everything is white. People hold their breath. I sing.
textes.La Ligne des Strates a rouvert ! Les gen: The Strata Line has reopened! Folk from up top come down the Column, they see the Brass Sun, they go “oooh”. Then they cross the Frondeurs' Bridge, they hear the Chasm, and they go “uh-oh”. Then they get here, and they go “boom-chak”. That's me.
textes.La Ligne des Strates, c'est deux cabines: The Strata Line is two cabins, {surnom}. The top one leaves from the pavilion on Column Square. Then you change, and mine goes down the Upside-Down Column: the Great Column carrying on underground, in brass and glass, hanging from the vault all the way to my Station. An upside-down tower! Imagine thinking of that.
textes.La Ligne du Dôme d'Azur, au fond, a enfi: The Azure Dome Line, down at the bottom, has finally reopened. Me, I've never seen the sea. I'll see it from underneath first. That's more original.
textes.La Ligne du Dôme d'Azur, en dessous de l: The Azure Dome Line, below Strata Station, is closed for works. I pressed my ear to the gate. I heard “glug-glug”. Écho says it's the sea. Tom says it's my tummy. We voted. Two votes to one for my tummy. I'm appealing.

The Azure Dome Line, under Strata Station, was closed for works. I'd pressed my ear to the gate. I'd heard “glug-glug”. Écho said it was the sea. Tom said it was my tummy. We voted: two votes to one for my tummy. It reopened, I went down to check: it was the sea! I won on appeal.
textes.La Lueur de lune révèle une quatrième ru: The Moonlight reveals a fourth rune, on his forehead! Strike it!
The Moonling, pale as a moonbeam. In the fairy tale, it opens your eyes to the invisible: hidden passages, steps and drawings light up all over the island. Look closely at the walls. And remember: in a fairy tale, yes. In the real forest: never!
textes.La Lune, Saturne et ses anneaux, et la C: The Moon, Saturn and its rings, and the City of Clouds passing in front of the stars. Come back at night: the dome opens wide.
textes.La Lune, toute ronde : ses cratères, ses: The Moon, perfectly round: its craters, its grey seas… and, at the edge, a little flag the Professor swears he didn't plant.
textes.La Légende des Soleils, je la sais par c: I know the Legend of the Suns by heart: the first sun was the sun of the Jaguars, who devoured the giants; the second, that of the Wind, which swept everything away; the third, that of the Fire-rain; the fourth, that of Water, the great flood. We live under the fifth, the Sun of Movement.
textes.La Maison Obscure. Le noir complet. Une: The Dark House. Complete blackness. A voice: “Here are our torches. Keep them lit all night, and give them back to us WHOLE tomorrow.” Three empty torch holders, on the walls.
textes.La Maison des Chauves-souris. Des millie: The House of Bats. Thousands of tiny cries, up there, in the dark. And a silence, lower down, much heavier.
textes.La Maison des Jaguars est calme. La port: The House of Jaguars is calm. The door at the back sinks into the floor: behind it, a ball court.
textes.La Maison des Jaguars. Des yeux jaunes d: The House of Jaguars. Yellow eyes in the shadows, growls, gnawed bones all over the floor…
textes.La Maison des Lames. Quatre lames d'obsi: The House of Blades. Four obsidian blades, tall as a man, sweep the room from wall to wall. Near the entrance, an empty altar.
textes.La Maison du Conseil : un hémicycle de b: The Council House: a semicircular chamber of white benches, a great feather on the back wall, and in the middle, on a glass table, the map of the island turning as a hologram.
textes.La Maison du Conseil, la nuit : les banc: The Council House at night: the benches of the chamber are empty, and only the hologram map of the island turns slowly in the middle, moon-blue.
textes.La Mare aux Mantras porte mon nom, mais: The Mantra Pond bears my name, but it was the pond that gave me mine. Before, I was called Bernard.
textes.La Mare aux Mantras — une eau calme, des: The Mantra Pond — calm water, water lilies, frogs meditating
textes.La Marmite\nNe pas se pencher. Ne pas tr:
The Cooking Pot
Do not lean over. Do not dip your fingers.
That's what the ladle is for.
textes.La Marmite est sur la Place des Rouages,: La Marmite is on Cogwheel Square, just below the Great Clock. When it strikes noon, the whole cavern comes down to my place. I hear them coming: boots on the cobbles, laughter from the Forge. I stir the soup in rhythm. It makes it better.
textes.La Marmite — le cratère est plein de sau: The Cooking Pot — the crater is full of simmering tomato sauce: it smells of garlic, basil and warm tomato
textes.La Marmite, c'est la cantine des Strates: La Marmite is the canteen of the Strata. The blacksmiths, the miners, the railway folk, the lamplighters, and the Fronde folk who cross the Bridge when Gamelle's Free Canteen is closed. Everyone on the same bench. Quarrels get left at the door, with the muddy boots.
textes.La Montagne de Feu. Le sable est noir, l: Fire Mountain. The sand is black, the air smells of sulfur and coal… Above the beach, braziers and forge smoke: Forgefer, the city of the dwarves.
textes.La Montagne de Feu. Mille ans que nous c: The Fire Mountain. A thousand years we've been digging beneath it. It rumbles, it smokes, it keeps us warm. It's our mother.
textes.La Morue Enragée, je l'ai gagnée aux dés: I won the Morue Enragée at dice from an admiral. He rolled three sixes. So did I. But mine were more… convincing.
textes.La Morue Enragée, je l'ai gagnée à un am: The Morue Enragée, I won her from an admiral, one stormy night, in a tavern. He rolled: three sixes. Me too. But mine were more convincing: they shone. The admiral left me his sloop and his wig. The wig, I gave back. Gontran tells everyone it was a governor. He's jealous: he had to buy his brig.
textes.La Mouette fait « kiaaa ». Les vraies mo: Mouette goes “kyaaa”. Real seagulls go “kyaaa”. I'm confused. Which one is the real one?
textes.La Murène Ivre, c'est l'ancien entrepôt: La Murène Ivre used to be the old salt warehouse. The walls are so salty the rum ages all by itself. That's my secret. My other secret… no.
textes.La Murène Noire a une voie d'eau. Je l'e: The Murène Noire has a leak. I can hear it. In the evening, when the port is quiet, you can hear their pump squeaking.
textes.La Mère-Ronce se fane, se recroqueville…: Mother Bramble withers, curls up… and falls as golden dust. The branches of Yggdrasil shiver with relief.
textes.La Mère-Ronce, la reine des plantes d'Yg: Mother Bramble, queen of the plants of Yggdrasil! Her bite reaches very far. Wait until she strikes at nothing, then run and hit her before she straightens up.
textes.La Mère-Ronce, reine des plantes d'Yggdr: Mother Bramble, queen of the plants of Yggdrasil
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, Brume m'a r: On the Night of the False Alarm, Brume recognised me by smell, three bridges away, while the alarm was still ringing. She said I smelled of moon tea. I'd had two cups. Three. Since then, when I climb to the treetop, I wonder if she's following me by nose. Hoo. Probably.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, Brume était: On the Night of the False Alarm, Brume was down by the ponds. She sniffed the air and ran to the Lookout to tell me: “It's Hulotte.” Too late. I'd sounded it. She never blamed me. She just said, the next day: “Good drill.” A good girl.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, Croc-Gris h: On the Night of the False Alarm, Croc-Gris was howling, all of Ramure was running about in their nightshirts, my son was carrying me down the stairs. And Mother Moon, sitting on her moss, simply said: “It's only Hulotte.” It was Hulotte. She didn't even spill her tea. I lost a slipper.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, il a vu un: On the Night of the False Alarm, he saw a long-necked monster climbing the Mother Oak and sounded the alarm. All of Ramure came tumbling down in their nightshirts. Me, I stayed sitting and said: “It's only Hulotte.” It was Hulotte, with his lantern and his long telescope. Croc-Gris says it was a drill. He didn't speak to me for three days.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, il avait ci: On the Night of the False Alarm, he was five. He came down the zip line in his pyjamas, all alone, shouting “Wheee”. Everyone was scared. Not him. The next day, he came back to ask me what time the next alarm was. Since then, he does it himself. Every day. At snack time.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, j'ai su ava: On the Night of the False Alarm, I knew before anyone that the monster was him. The smell: lantern tallow, feathers, moon tea. He drinks too much of it. I recognised him three bridges away. When I told him, he sighed that I had a nose without poetry. I took it as a compliment.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, j'avais cin: On the Night of the False Alarm, I was five. Croc-Gris shouted “ALERT!” and I ran to the Lookout in my pyjamas. I took the zip line all by myself, wheeeee, all the way down! Everyone was scared. Me, I was laughing. At the bottom, Granny Faîne caught me by the tail. The next day I asked Croc-Gris when the next alert was.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, j'étais en: On the Night of the False Alarm, I was down by the ponds. I sniffed the wind: it was Hulotte, not a monster. I ran towards the Lookout to say so. The alarm was already ringing, and all of Ramure was tumbling down the stairs in their nightshirts. The next day, I told him: “Good drill.” He looked at me. He said: “Yes.”
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, je montais: On the Night of the False Alarm, I was climbing the Mother Oak's stairs with my lantern and my long telescope on my shoulder. The monster's long neck was the telescope; its fiery eye, my lantern. All of Ramure came down in their nightshirts. Me, I reached the treetop, and there was no one left up there. Hoo. I still laugh about it. He doesn't.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, mes vieille: On the Night of the False Alarm, my old paws wouldn't go down. Bourru picked me up like a cub and carried me all the way down the stairs. At the bottom, he said: “Hrmm. Light.” I was still telling a story, apparently. I don't remember. I remember “light”. Nobody had said that to me in sixty years.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte, tout Ramure: On the Night of the False Alarm, all of Ramure was running about in nightshirts. The little ones were crying, Bourru was carrying Tilleul down in his arms. Only one stayed sitting: Mère-Lune. She said: “It's only Hulotte.” Calmly. Before anyone. Without even looking up. I've never got over it.

On the Night of the False Alarm, all of Ramure came tumbling down in their nightshirts. Bourru came down the stairs carrying his old father in his arms like a cub, and Tilleul was still telling a story over his shoulder. Me, I stayed sitting on my moss. He waved to me as he passed, very dignified. He'd lost a slipper.
textes.La Nuit de la Fausse Alerte. Tout le mon: The Night of the False Alarm. Everyone was going down. Father, his paws wouldn't. I carried him in my arms. The whole staircase. He was still telling stories. At the bottom, I put him down. I said: “Hrmm. Light.” He went quiet. One minute. First time in his life. Hrmm. He doesn't eat enough.
textes.La Nuit des Aurores commence à vingt-deu: The Night of the Auroras starts at ten p.m. and ends at two a.m. The auroras are very punctual. They're the only things in the sky that listen to me.
textes.La Nuit des Lanternes ! Il faut allumer: The Night of Lanterns! The city's seven Great Lanterns must be lit: the harbour's, the market's, the arena's, the baths', the academy's, the forge's and the square's. When they're all shining and Zigomar's rockets are ready, come nightfall, the whole city comes to dance!
textes.La Nuit des Lanternes… Il faut allumer l: The Night of Lanterns… The seven Great Lanterns must be lit: the harbour, the market, the arena, the baths, the academy, the forge and the square. Lumina made the wicks. If you light them, I'll watch. From afar. That's my way of applauding.
textes.La Nuit des Lanternes… Tu as vu ? Les se: The Night of Lanterns… Did you see? The seven Great Lanterns, Zigomar's rockets, the whole city dancing on the square. I've never seen Pandémonia so beautiful.
textes.La Palette de pierre : les neuf godets s: The Stone Palette: all nine paint wells are full, each in its own colour, from blue to pink. It shines in the sun like a rainbow laid in the grass.
textes.La Palette de pierre : neuf godets numér: The Stone Palette: nine numbered paint wells, from 1 to 9, all empty and dry. At the bottom of the first, a tiny trace of blue… Who took the island's colours?
textes.La Palette de pierre a neuf godets, numé: The Stone Palette has nine wells, numbered one to nine. One, blue. Two, green. Three, red. Four, yellow. Five, brown. Six, purple. Seven, orange. Eight, turquoise. Nine, pink. I made all my pupils recite it.
textes.La Palette de pierre, au milieu de la cl: The Stone Palette, in the middle of the clearing, is the heart of the island. Each colour lives in a pot, in its own numbered well. When all nine pots are in place, the whole island is in colour. When they're missing…
textes.La Perle de l'Épave est dans le coffre d: The Wreck Pearl is in the chest of “The Black Mermaid”, the ship that sank west of the Gate. Surface sailors had stolen it…
textes.La Perle de la Fosse repose sur l'autel,: The Trench Pearl rests on the altar at the bottom of the Jellyfish Trench, to the north, beyond the kelp forest. Jellyfish sting: don't brush against them.
textes.La Perle du Jardin dort dans le grand bé: The Garden Pearl sleeps in the giant clam, in the heart of the coral reef, north-east of the city. The sharks circle it. Be quick.
textes.La Pierre du Soleil gronde… et rejette l: The Sun Stone rumbles… and spits out the four glyphs, which fall back into your hands. That isn't the order of the suns. (The codex, at the entrance, shows that order.)
textes.La Place de la Colonne. Merci d'avoir vo: Column Square. Thank you for travelling with the Liftkeepers' Guild!
textes.La Place des Hologrammes — trois carpes: Hologram Square — three light carp swim above the passersby
textes.La Place des Palettes, au cœur de la vil: Pallet Square, in the heart of town, is my stage. The fountain is a bathtub, the benches are pallets, and the tree has fairy lights. The audience is kids, dogs and pigeons. Pigeons are the toughest crowd.
textes.La Plage aux Galets, tout au sud-est : G: The Pebble Beach, way down in the south-east: Gravier fishes there. He hardly talks. I talk all the time. Together, it makes a normal conversation.
textes.La Plage aux Galets. Sud-est. Les galets: Pebble Beach. South-east. The pebbles roll. It makes music. Better than the Hall. Less loud.
textes.La Plage des Os, au nord-ouest. Il y a l: Bone Beach, to the north-west. There's the skeleton of a giant whale. And crabs. Lots of crabs. And gorgeous shells, if you run fast.
textes.La Plage des Œufs — des nids, des œufs…: Egg Beach — nests, eggs… don't disturb them
textes.La Plaine des Cornes — attention aux Cor: The Plain of Horns — beware of the Nose-Horns, they're grumpy
textes.La Plume de Quetzalcóatl ! Le Serpent à: Quetzalcóatl's Feather! The Feathered Serpent, god of wind and knowledge. 150 coins, an extra heart, and a title: “Bearer of the Fifth Sun”. A staircase of light leads back up to the top of the Great Temple.
textes.La Plume de Séraphin, avec le ciel derri: Séraphin's Feather, with the sky behind it. The sky changes every ten minutes. So either I paint fast, or I paint ten pictures.
textes.La Plume de Séraphin, la sculpture de l': Séraphin's Feather, the sculpture on the Esplanade, is in memory of his very first idea: he had seen a feather rise on the wind, above the Column, and never come down. He thought: if a feather can do it, so can a city. He was a bit mad. We loved him dearly.
textes.La Porte Nord donne sur le chemin du Por: The North Gate opens onto the road to Seagull Harbour, to the northwest. Captain Isidore sometimes comes to say hello. With his seagulls. They peck at my helmet. It wakes me up. That's kind of them.
textes.La Porte aux Quatre Sceaux: The Gate of the Four Seals
textes.La Porte aux Quatre Sceaux est ouverte !: The Gate of the Four Seals is open!
textes.La Porte aux Quatre Sceaux ouverte: The Gate of the Four Seals opened
textes.La Porte aux Quatre Sceaux. Les quatre c: The Gate of the Four Seals. The four hollows are still empty. Behind the stone, very far away, it sounds as if a heart is beating.
textes.La Porte de l'Abîme, en pierre noire. Un: The Abyss Gate, in black stone. A green glow protects it. Behind it, something immense is breathing… The Eye Stone, right there, may be waiting for the amulet.
textes.La Porte du Serpent s'ouvre ! Les trois: The Serpent Gate opens! The three fragments have fused: the SERPENT AMULET. Its green eye lights up the darkness.
textes.La Prairie du Festival — la Grande Scène: The Festival Meadow — the Main Stage awaits its festival
textes.La Première Conseillère des Nuées, Céles: The First Councillor of the Clouds, Céleste Altaïr, sent me a postcard from her terrace, with a note from her daughter, Lili: “Hello, class down below. Does the sea make a noise?” My pupils answered all together. Fourteen pages. With a whale drawn on every page.
textes.La Professeure Fusilli a voulu peser mes: Professor Fusilli wanted to weigh my pasta to the milligram. I let her. Then I served her a plate. She stopped weighing.
textes.La Professeure Fusilli dit que le Grand: Professor Fusilli says the Great Spaghetti is exactly one hundred and twelve noodles long. I don't know how you measure in noodles. But I have faith.
textes.La Présidente Ondine a reçu une pétition: President Ondine received a petition from my pupils: “So that every child in the Dome gets to see the sky.” Fourteen signatures, plus Lou, plus Professor Benthos, twice. She read it out, standing, before the Council. It was passed unanimously. Now we have to organise the trip. I'm losing sleep over it.
textes.La Présidente Ondine m'a appris à écoute: President Ondine taught me to listen to the Trench, when I was young and talkative. She told me: “Sit down and say nothing.” I sat down. The Singer went by. I'm still talkative to this day. But I know how to keep quiet when it matters.
textes.La Présidente Ondine vient à l'école une: President Ondine comes to the school once a year to explain the Tide Council to the children. She speaks softly, slowly, and they listen to her the way they listen to the Singer. She put my pupils' petition to see the sky to the vote. It passed unanimously. I'll owe her the finest Thursday of my career. It hasn't happened yet.
textes.La Présidente Ondine, tout au fond… Pour: President Ondine, way down at the bottom… For the reopening of her line, the four of us cut the ribbon. Thirty centimetres, four pairs of scissors: seven and a half centimetres each! I asked for an eighth centimetre. On principle. But during my speech, the lanternfish pressed up against the glass to listen to me. And they applauded. I'm certain of it.
textes.La Présidente d'en bas, Ondine… Je lui a: The President down below, Ondine… I wrote to her: “Four worlds, and not one shared assembly.” She replied: “Come. We'll sit around the Bubble Fountain.” A fountain! I wanted a fire. Under the sea, apparently, that's complicated. We're negotiating. (He smiles.) It does you good, negotiating with someone who listens.
textes.La Reine des Ronces pousse un cri… Les é: The Bramble Queen cries out… The thorns fall from her gown like dead leaves. A pink light wraps around her…
The Bramble Queen flies out of reach. When she lands, exhausted, that's the time to strike!
textes.La Reine des Ronces… c'était Églantine ?: The Bramble Queen… was Églantine? The Fairy Queen herself, prisoner of her own thorns for a hundred years! And it was a little human who set her free. I'll have to write a new song. A long one.
textes.La Reine des Ronces… on n'en parle pas t: The Bramble Queen… we don't speak of her too loudly here. Her brambles have eaten half our kingdom.
textes.La Reine hurle : « Mes enfants, à moi !: The Queen howls: “My children, to me!” Crystal spiders burst from the brambles!
textes.La Reine se relève, et son bouclier d'ép: The Queen gets back up, and her thorn shield grows back! The roses of light close again…
textes.La Rose des Sceaux. Une salle ronde comm: The Rose of Seals. A hall as round as a square, four columns, four doors. On the floor, an engraved compass rose, and at the centre a round seal beneath four dark crystals. Under the vault, a red crystal hangs and beats like a heart.
textes.La Râpe d'Or ? Qui t'a parlé de la Râpe: The Golden Grater? Who told you about the Golden Grater? … The Reverend? Well. Well, well, well. Come and see me when he sends you. I'll see what I can… remember.
textes.La Râpe d'Or, je l'ai gagnée à un vieux: I won the Golden Grater off an old pirate, at cards, on an island with no name. He said it grated the best parmesan in the world. It was true. I buried it near my boat to keep it safe. And then I forgot where. Well… I pretended to forget. It was easier than lending it out.
textes.La Râpe d'Or… Arrr. Bon. Je vais te dire: The Golden Grater… Arrr. Well. I'll tell you the truth, matey. I buried it thirty years ago, so nobody would steal it from me. And then I forgot where. (Pesto shouts: “RAMEN!”) … No, wait. I remember the phrase: “where the mast's shadow touches the sea at noon”. My mast is the Houseboat's. Take a shovel, and dig on the sand, between the mast and the water. You don't have a shovel? I sell one. Cheap. I'm a pirate, not a thief.
textes.La Salle de la Sève. À l'ouest, une sour: The Sap Hall. To the west, an amber spring from which golden light flows. Three flowers with polished silver hearts, like mirrors. To the east, a big knot of dark wood: the heart of the tree?
textes.La Salle des Deux Vérités. Anubis, le di: The Hall of the Two Truths. Anubis, the jackal god, and Thoth, the ibis god, before a great golden scale. Along the walls, the forty-two judges.
textes.La Salle des Pièges. À l'est, un champ d: The Trap Room. To the east, a field of tiles (some are dark and cracked…); to the west, a campfire and goblins; to the south, a closed door, and three unlit lamps above it. Three levers to find!
textes.La Salle des Prismes est au bout du coul: The Prism Hall is at the end of the corridor. The sun comes down through a crack… but it no longer reaches the Door Flower.
textes.La Salle des Saisons. Quatre fleurs de p: The Hall of Seasons. Four stone flowers, one at each cardinal point, and a carved stele right next to you… And leaves that move all by themselves!
textes.La Salle des Sustentateurs est dans l'In: The Levitator Room is inside the Institute of Winds. There's the console, four blue indicator lights, one for each engine, and a porthole in the floor. Look through the porthole: you'll see Brindille, her blue ring, and the void. A lot of void. Don't jump on it.
textes.La Salle du Conseil est au pied de la Fl: The Council Hall is at the foot of the Crystal Spire. There are three seats: the Elder's, mine, and Tempo's. Tempo's is the only one that's always on time.
The Council Hall is at the foot of the Spire. We discuss everything there: the Heart, the bridges, the auroras, and who ate Gloubi's last jelly. That last subject takes a very long time.
textes.La Salle du Cœur. Le grand cristal bat d: The Heart Chamber. The great crystal beats gently, with a golden light. All is calm.
textes.La Salle du Cœur. Une caverne immense, r: The Heart Chamber. An immense, round cavern, veins of fire in the floor. In the middle, hanging from chains, a red crystal larger than a house… that beats. And beneath it, something is rising.
textes.La Salle du Trône Gélatineux. Le sol col: The Jelly Throne Room. The floor sticks to your soles, a jelly throne wobbles at the far end… and a smell of green apple hangs everywhere.
textes.La Scène des Soupapes, c'est au fond de: The Valves' Stage is at the back of the cavern. Every evening at eight: me on drums, Bielle on the mic, Écho on bass, and Bricole's steam organ doing the choruses all by itself. It never gets it wrong. It's annoying.
textes.La Serre des Espèces est au nord-est, ap: The Greenhouse of Species is to the north-east, past the Academy: a big glass dome full of peaceful creatures. Don't tap on the glass: the gurgles think it's an invitation, and they answer. For hours.
textes.La Skala, avec les canons, c'est le meil: The Skala, with the cannons, is the best place to play. But the guard chases us away. He says cannons aren't horses.
textes.La Terrasse du Ciel — à 150 mètres au-de: The Sky Terrace — 150 meters above the streets: the whole city, the sea, and the archipelago in the distance
textes.La Tomateraie donne les tomates de la sa: The Tomato Grove provides the tomatoes for the sacred sauce. Bucatini throws a basketful into the Cooking Pot every Sunday. The volcano does the rest.
textes.La Tomateraie — des tomates grosses comm: The Tomato Grove — tomatoes as big as fists, red, warm from the sun
textes.La Tour Axiome — 265 mètres de verre ; s: The Axiom Tower — 265 meters of glass; its elevator goes up to the Sky Terrace
textes.La Tour Axiome, c'est la plus haute. Sep: The Axiom Tower is the tallest. Sept, the android man at reception, let me press the lift button. It was the best day of my life. Before the one when I got a free soda.
textes.La Tour Penchée, autrefois, c'était la t: The Leaning Tower used to be the tower of the winds, standing straight. I was given my class there at twenty-five. There was a bench on every floor, one for each wind, and the bell, right at the top, that rang when they arrived. Sometimes I taught upside down, so the apprentices would see the world differently. They did. They got dizzy.
textes.La Tour Penchée, là-bas, c'était la tour: The Leaning Tower, over there, used to be the tower of the winds. It's been leaning since the great storm. Its bell is still up there, but the staircase collapsed. There's only one way left to get up…
textes.La Tour du Zénith : un grand hall rond e: The Zenith Tower: a big, bright, round hall, potted trees, and in the middle, a glass lift rising straight up towards the sky.
textes.La Tour du Zénith en tout petit : quator: The Zenith Tower in miniature: fourteen floors, each one turned a little from the one below. Seen from above, it looks like a staircase for a giant.
textes.La Tourmente : un couloir au bord d'un g: The Tempest: a corridor on the edge of a fiery chasm, and a wind that never stops blowing, in gusts. The pillars against the wall make good shelters.
The Waltz plays when it wants to. Serve first.
textes.La Veuve Écarlate, c'est ma femme, ma ma: The Veuve Écarlate is my wife, my home, my country. I named her after a lady who dropped a flowerpot on my head in Tortuga. I married the ship. It was safer.
textes.La bague en corail rose, il me l'a laiss: The pink coral ring, he offered it at twelve coins, friend's price. I offered nine, fiancée's price. A week of haggling! In the end he said “eleven”, I said “ten”, and we looked at each other. Neither of us gave in. The ring's still in his drawer. I know: I check when his back is turned.
textes.La bague est dans ma poche depuis des jo: The ring has been in my pocket for days. I'm waiting for the right moment. The right century, maybe.
textes.La baguette de Pimprenelle ! Son étoile: Pimprenelle's wand! Its crystal star crackles between your fingers. She'll be delighted to have it back, in the Fairy Village.
textes.La bague… Tu en as trouvé une ? Avec une: The ring… Have you found one? With a blue stone, mind. Not red. Red is for declarations of war.
textes.La baie devant la plage descend doucemen: The bay in front of the beach slopes gently. At the bottom there are orange starfish. Bringing them up to the surface is my challenge for the tough ones.
textes.La baie est poissonneuse, abritée par le: The bay is full of fish, sheltered by the two points. Further out, there are the big ones. And to the north, under the highland cliffs, lobsters the size of dogs.
textes.La baie se referme. La harpe se tait, le: The big window slides shut. The harp falls silent, and the chimes go still one by one. Silence.
textes.La balance penche lourdement : ton cœur: The scale tips heavily: your heart weighs more than the feather! In the shadows behind the judges, something growls… AMMIT THE DEVOURER bursts out!
textes.La balance s'équilibre : ton cœur est au: The scale balances: your heart is as light as Ma'at's feather! Thoth writes on his tablet: “True of voice.” Your heart returns to your chest… and at the far end of the hall, the door to the Duat opens.
textes.La balançoire, sous le Chêne-Gomme, c'es: The swing under the Eraser Oak is the best in the archipelago. It hangs from the terrace! When you go really high, you can see the sea.
textes.La balle est lourde, en caoutchouc plein: The ball is heavy, solid rubber. One ball on the head and you see stars. Ask Ah Kin Pech: that's how he became an astronomer.
textes.La balle roule, rebondit sur le talus… e: The ball rolls, bounces off the slope… and falls back into the alley. The Lords snigger. Aim for the stone ring, on the wall.
textes.La bannière ! LA BANNIÈRE ! (Il la brand: The banner! THE BANNER! (He waves it, trips on his cape, falls, and is still waving it, lying down.) A real feat! With a witness! With sunshine! Bertrand! BERTRAND! We need a song! And not a single cloud in it!
textes.La bannière du chef gobelin ! Un VRAI ex: The goblin chief's banner! A REAL feat! With witnesses! I follow you, friend: from now on, we write the legend together. And without fog.
textes.La barque de Rê glisse sur le fleuve de: The barque of Ra glides over the river of night… and drops you off in the sunlight, in front of the pyramid door.
textes.La batterie fait « boum ». Mon cœur fait: The drums go “boom”. My heart goes “boom”. We're the same, the drums and me.
textes.La bavarde ! Tu dois être quelqu'un de j: The chatterbox! You must be a cheerful soul. Here, keep it.
textes.La betterave. Ma vie d'artiste est un dr: Beetroot. My artistic life is a tragedy.
The Montjoie library is that way. Just for your information.
textes.La bijouterie le matin, le déjeuner chez: The jeweller's in the morning, lunch at Paulo's, the shop, a stroll in the evening. Victor drops by to offer me “authentic” shells that smell of paint. A young newlywed asked me for a ring “exactly the same”. And Rosalie counts my Friday sea bream with saucer eyes. A quiet life, as you can see. In Port-Azur, nothing stays quiet for long.
textes.La bière épaisse et douce de Mérit, fait: Mérit's thick, sweet barley drink, made with barley bread and dates. The Egyptians drank it like liquid bread. Restores one heart.
textes.La boisson du Diable Repu, sans alcool :: The house drink of Au Diable Repu, alcohol-free: honey, fire cinnamon, a pinch of sulphur from the springs (for the colour). It smells of eggs, and it warms you right through. Restores one heart.
textes.La botte de Barnabé ! Je vais la clouer: Barnabé's boot! I'll nail it above my door. Like a trophy.
textes.La botte, c'était une botte de pêcheur,: The boot was a fisherman's boot, size thirteen, full of mud. Agathe came to look at it on the jetty. She took it, carried it off to her caravan, and planted thyme in it. Now it sits in pride of place by her door, with a label: “Prediction fulfilled”. I walk past it grumbling. The thyme is doing well.
textes.La boue, c'est comme un bain, mais en mi: Mud is like a bath, only better. Humans don't understand. Humans have bathtubs. Poor things.
textes.La boulangerie d'Honorine. Ville-Moyenne: Honorine's bakery. Middle Town. Chocolate éclairs, on Thursdays. Most important place on the island.
textes.La boule ajoute : « Évitez les grenouill: The ball adds: “Avoid the frogs.” Nobody knows why. Everybody listens.
textes.La boule de cristal m'insulte, Églantine: The crystal ball is insulting me, Églantine!
textes.La boule de cristal qui mesure les aptit: The crystal ball that measures aptitudes cracked the day Sire Tancrède consulted it. It displayed “courage: infinite” and went crack. I spent the night gluing it back together with slime jelly, on Aubin's advice. It still works. It smells a little of apple now.
textes.La boule de cristal vous attend ! Elle m: The crystal ball awaits you! It told me “courage: infinite”. It'll surely tell you something nice too.
textes.La boule devient rose une seconde. D'apr: The ball turns pink for a second. According to Églantine, that means “hidden talent”. Very hidden.
textes.La boule embue sa propre vitre. Elle a b: The ball fogs up its own glass. It needs a moment.
The ball makes a little satisfied noise. Églantine notes: “The ball is happy.”
textes.La boule m'avait annoncé une traversée a: The ball had foretold me a crossing with a beautiful stranger with golden eyes. I shaved, I put on my clean shirt. It was a goat. A goat for Mère Sauge's garden, with magnificent yellow eyes, I'll grant you. Agathe says she never mentioned a woman. It's true. I hate it when it's true.
textes.La boule ne ment jamais. Elle exagère, p: The ball never lies. It exaggerates, sometimes.
textes.La boussole que je t'ai donnée ne montre: The compass I gave you doesn't point north. It points to what you're really looking for. Usually, that's north.
textes.La boutique est FERMÉE. Pour toi. Revien: The shop is CLOSED. To you. Come back when I've got over your punches.
textes.La bouée d'accueil brille doucement. Un: The welcome buoy glows softly. A beam of light rises straight up into the sky. [E]: go up to Astralys.
textes.La boîte aux lettres jaune devant la pos: The yellow postbox outside the post office? If you slip a wish into it, I won't read it. Promise.
textes.La brioche du Four Éternel de Bobor, dor: The brioche from Bobor's Eternal Oven, golden, split on top, baked over the embers that never go out. Still warm, at any hour. Restores two hearts.
textes.La brise du soir arrive bientôt. Elle ch: The evening breeze is coming soon. It still whispers just as much.
textes.La brise du soir… Celle qui chuchote. Co: The evening breeze… The one that whispers. Like… um. Like a leaf. Yes. Like a leaf of paper. At the Library. Why am I saying that?
textes.La brume ? C'est le souffle de l'Arbre-M: The mist? It's the Mother Tree's breath. It opens for those it loves. It seems to like you. It has strange tastes.
textes.La brume est calme… Tu as fait tout ce q: The mist is calm… You've done everything there was to do. The stars salute you. So do I.
textes.La bulle sort de la falaise… En bas, au: The bubble emerges from the cliff… Far below, deep in the blue, the three domes of the Azure Dome light up.
textes.La cabine, c'est une bulle de verre de s: The cabin is a six-metre glass bubble. It goes down inside a long glass tube, set on pylons, above the Trench. People are scared at first. Then a ray glides under their feet, and they forget to be scared. Rays are very good at that.
textes.La cachette est vide : tu as déjà pris l: The hiding place is empty: you've already taken the treasure. The parrot gives you a knowing look.
