textes.La vérité, {surnom} ? J'aime les îles pl: The truth, {surnom}? I love the islands more than I should. The Lumens observe; I get attached. One day, I'd like to go there without a disguise. With my antennae. And have people say hello anyway.
textes.La vérité, {surnom}, c'est que je n'aime: The truth, {surnom}, is that I don't like selling. I like telling where things come from. Every object has made a journey. Selling it means giving it another one. The price? That's just so you'll take care of it.
textes.Lac Napolitain\nBaignade interdite : la:
Neapolitan Lake
No swimming: the sauce is hot,
and they say you come out all red.
textes.Lac des Long-Cous. Eau calme, Long-Cou b: Long-Neck Lake. Water calm, Long-Neck drink, Long-Neck eat big trees. Before, Old Flint swim there. Before being old. Very long ago. Yesterday, maybe.
textes.Laisse-le dormir, petite. Il est fatigué: Let her sleep, girl. She's tired.
Give him a chance. And a cup.
Let me explore the island first.
textes.Laisse-moi deviner… Rien à signaler ?: Let me guess… Nothing to report?
Let me sleep one more bar.
textes.Lait de coco, jus de mangue et une ombre: Coconut milk, mango juice and a paper umbrella. Toni's recipe (or Kiki's, depending on who you ask). Restores two hearts.
textes.Lait de nuage, thé des sommets, jus de s: Cloud milk, summit tea, sunshine juice, piping-hot chocolate, and sugar puffs fresh from the solar oven! Not a drop of strong drink: up here, our heads are already in the clouds. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Lalla Aïcha a le meilleur safran de l'îl: Lalla Aïcha has the best saffron on the island, and she knows it. She sells it to me too dear, every week. And every week, she sneaks in an extra pinch. We only argue for show.
textes.Lalla Aïcha déteste la sardine. L'odeur,: Lalla Aïcha hates sardines. The smell, she says. But she says my cumin is the only cumin in Tazira put to good use. Coming from her, that's a medal.
textes.Lalla Aïcha me vend du safran en me rega: Lalla Aïcha sells me saffron while looking at me like a criminal. For her, saffron is for eating. For me, it's for wearing. We'll never agree, but we're fond of each other.
textes.Lalla Aïcha, la marchande d'épices de Ta: Lalla Aïcha, the spice merchant of Tazira. A magnificent thief. Forty spices on her stall, and she beats me at every haggle. I adore her.
textes.Lalla Fatima ? Soixante-dix ans qu'elle: Lalla Fatima? Seventy years she's been listening to me, and seventy years she's been correcting me. When I tell the tale of the pirate of the caves, she says: “That's not how it was. I was there.” And nothing more.
textes.Lalla Fatima a ramendé les filets de mon: Lalla Fatima mended my father's nets, then mine. She's the only one who still calls me “the little one”. In front of my fishermen. I respect her more than anyone. And I blush.
textes.Lalla Fatima m'a tout appris. Quatre-vin: Lalla Fatima taught me everything. Eighty years old, nearly blind, and two thousand knots a day. Me, a thousand. I admire her, and I worry about her. She never rests.
Lalla Fatima, do rest a little.
textes.Lalla Fatima… devant mes pêcheurs !: Lalla Fatima… in front of my fishermen!
textes.Lance loin, là où l'eau devient bleu som: Cast far, where the water turns dark blue. Big fish like the deep, like philosophers.
textes.Laquelle ? … Euh. Je connais pas de Gert: Which one? … Er. I don't know any Gertrude.
textes.Laquelle ? … Je veux dire : quelle Gertr: Which one? … I mean: what Gertrude?
textes.Larbi ne prend plus rien au bout de la j: Larbi doesn't catch anything any more at the end of the jetty. Nothing. So, some evenings, I stop at Zohra's before him, buy a nice fish, and slip it into his basket while he puts away his rod. He comes home proud. He says: “Not bad, today.” I say: “Not bad.” He doesn't know. Well… with Larbi, you never know what he knows.
textes.Larbi, mon mari. Cinquante-huit ans de m: Larbi, my husband. Fifty-eight years married, and he still hasn't managed to beat me at knots. He fishes without catching anything. He lights his lighthouse. He's a good man.
textes.Larguez les amarres ! Enfin, toi, tu mar: Cast off! Well, you're on foot. But it's the spirit that counts.
textes.Larsen ! Ce soir, je joue fort ou doucem: Larsen! Tonight, do I play loud or soft?
textes.Larsen a enregistré en secret mon solo d: Larsen secretly recorded my eleven-minute solo, the night I filled in for the drummer. He played it backwards, for a laugh, in front of everyone. It sounded better backwards. Everyone said so. I'll never forgive him. I listen to it every night.
textes.Larsen commande en criant, remercie en c: Larsen orders shouting, thanks you shouting, apologises shouting. I'm fond of him. From a distance. With earplugs.
textes.Larsen commande toujours en criant. Un j: Larsen always shouts his order. One day, he shouted “A LEMONADE!” so loud that all the bottles fizzed at once. I served him. I had to.
textes.Larsen dit que je joue trop fort. Larsen: Larsen says I play too loud. Larsen says everything too loud. We adore each other, but we talk from a distance, with gestures.
Larsen says I play too loud. Larsen says everything too loud. We get on very well, but from a distance.
textes.Larsen et moi, on fait la régie ensemble: Larsen and I run the control desk together. Him on sound, me on lights. When he shouts “LOUDER!”, I turn up the lights. That's not what he means. But it's pretty.
textes.Larsen fait le son, moi la lumière. Il c: Larsen does the sound, I do the lights. He shouts, I blink. We never understand each other, but the concert is always beautiful. It's a technical mystery.
textes.Larsen me crie tous les soirs « MOUETTE,: Every night Larsen shouts at me: “MOUETTE, YOU'RE PLAYING TOO LOUD!” One night, I played really softly to please him. He ran to the stage shouting “WHY HAVE YOU STOPPED PLAYING?” I'll never understand Larsen.
textes.Larsen règle le son trop fort, ou pas as: Larsen sets the sound too loud, or not loud enough, depending on the day. He shouts all the time. So do I. We can't hear each other, literally.
textes.Larsen règle le son trop fort. Ou pas as: Larsen sets the sound too loud. Or not loud enough. I can't tell any more, I haven't heard much since 1977. Or 1978.
textes.Lasagna et moi, on s'est rencontrés à un: Lasagna and I met at a pasta contest. She won. I came last. I asked her for her recipe. She said: “Marry me, and you'll eat it every day.” That was fifty years ago. I'm still eating.
textes.Lasagna, c'est la meilleure cuisinière d: Lasagna is the best cook in the archipelago and the biggest grumbler. The two go together. She shouts “Dinner's ready!” so loudly the seagulls sit down.
textes.Le BADGE DE L'USINE GRISE ! Une photo de: The GREY FACTORY BADGE! A photo of a smiling robot, and the words: “ACCESS TO ALL FLOORS — even -5”. With this, the door at the bottom should open.
textes.Le Babillard, qui fait de petits bruits: The Chatterbox, which makes little noises when you come near. In the fairy tale, it lets you understand animals: dogs, cats, rats, pigeons, seagulls. I'm warning you: seagulls only ever talk about one thing. And remember: in a fairy tale, yes. In the real forest: never!
textes.Le Bail collectif. Signé. (Elle le cares: The shared lease. Signed. (She strokes it like a cat.) Forty years I've been waiting for this. Come here and let me kiss you, my heir.
textes.Le Baron Barthélemy a perdu son plus bea: Baron Barthélemy has lost his finest hat, the plumed one: the wind carried it over the castle wall. It was seen flying over the rooftops of the Middle Town… then nothing more.
The Baron lost his cane three times.
textes.Le Baron a perdu son chapeau dans la mer: The Baron lost his hat in the sea once. Albertine fished it out. She kept it three days to make a nest in it. The Baron said it was an honour. He wore it with an egg inside.
textes.Le Baron commande un chapeau par semaine: The Baron orders one hat a week and loses two. He's my most stable source of income. And the most unpredictable. He has terrible ideas. He wears them with such joy.
textes.Le Baron est distrait comme une mouette: The Baron is as scatterbrained as a seagull and as kind as a pie. He put me in charge of the Guild and forgot to tell me. I found out from Aurore. We get on very well.
textes.Le Baron est le seul homme de l'île qui: The Baron is the only man on the island who takes my seagulls seriously. He salutes them every evening from his rampart. They don't answer. But they're fond of him. I know it.
textes.Le Baron m'a confié la Guilde il y a vin: The Baron put me in charge of the Guild twenty years ago. I sign everything Églantine puts in front of me, I taste all of Rissole's pies and I tell the newcomers about my dragon. In the evening, I count the adventurers coming home. When the count is right, I cry. When it isn't, I go and fetch them.
textes.Le Baron perd tout, oublie tout, promet: The Baron loses everything, forgets everything, promises everything. But he has never forgotten the name of a single inhabitant. He's the best baron one could have. And the most tiring.
textes.Le Bassin des Bathyscaphes : un puits ou: The Bathyscaphe Pool: a well open to the sea, flush with the floor. The pressure keeps the water out. Magic? No: physics!
textes.Le Bassin des Bathyscaphes, c'est un gra: The Bathyscaphe Pool is a big well of water, level with the floor, in the Institute's dome. It's open to the sea from underneath. The air keeps the water out. The Little Diver sinks into it, slips under the Dome, and hey presto: he's out in the Trench. It's the town's back door.
textes.Le Bassin des Bathyscaphes, à l'Institut: The Bathyscaphe Pool, at the Institute, is a well open to the sea, level with the floor. The folk up top don't believe it: “And the water doesn't come up?” No. The air keeps it out. It's like a glass turned upside down in a basin. I show them, with a glass. They understand. Then they get thirsty.
textes.Le Bassin à sec, c'est une ancienne cale: The Dry Dock is an old dry dock for repairing boats, east of the harbour. We emptied it and now it's a skatepark! The curves are perfect. Those boats were lucky.
textes.Le Bassin à sec, à l'est du port, c'est: The Dry Dock, east of the harbour, is the skatepark. Tornade does incredible tricks there. I do only one trick there: I fall. But I fall with style.
textes.Le Bazar galactique est à l'est de l'Ago: The Galactic Bazaar is east of the Agora, facing Gloubi's Café. Between us, the fountain. The planets in it change every minute. I set my prices by the planet of the moment. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Le Belvédère : toute l'île à vos pieds !: The Belvedere: the whole island at your feet!
textes.Le Belvédère de Verre : deux cents mètre: The Glass Belvedere: two hundred metres of thin air beneath your feet (the glass is very strong)
textes.Le Belvédère de la Grande Colonne: The Belvedere of the Great Column
textes.Le Belvédère de la Grande Colonne : tout: The Belvedere of the Great Column: the whole island at your feet
textes.Le Belvédère de la Grande Colonne. Bon v: The Belvedere of the Great Column. Fair winds, and see you up there soon!
textes.Le Belvédère des Abysses : sous le verre: The Abyss Belvedere: beneath the glass, the Rift plunges into darkness… Listen: sometimes the Great Singer sings.
textes.Le Belvédère des Couleurs, en haut du Gr: The Lookout of Colours, at the top of the Great Oak — the whole island, all white; it will take a lot of colours!
textes.Le Belvédère, c'est un balcon tout rond,: The Belvedere is a round balcony, sixty metres up. From there, you can see the whole island: the Mill, the Orchards, the Lighthouse, the Arches in the sea… and above it all, the City of Clouds floating. Or so they say. Me, I look at my shoes. They're very nice shoes.
textes.Le Bois Tors est le plus vieil endroit d: The Twisted Wood is the oldest place on the island. The trees there have been twisting for a thousand years to look at the stars through the leaves. The mushrooms glow at night. It's pretty, and a little unsettling.
textes.Le Bois Tors, au sud du Cercle, n'est pa: The Twisted Wood, south of the Circle, isn't wicked. It's old. Old trees twist round to see who's passing.
textes.Le Bois de Cendre, au sud-est, est plein: The Ash Wood, to the south-east, is full of wonders and paths that all look alike. Pépin runs off there the moment my back is turned. If you ever see a little imp with ivory horns over there talking to mushrooms… tell him his mother is waiting for him.
textes.Le Bois de Cendre, c'est le plus bel end: The Ash Wood is the most beautiful place in the world! The trees are black, the leaves are embers, and the mushrooms glow like lanterns! Mum says I must never go there on my own. Never ever.
textes.Le Bois des Hachures — des chênes et des: The Hatching Wood — oaks and birches drawn in ink, stroke by stroke
textes.Le Bois des Hachures, à l'ouest, s'appel: The Hatching Wood, to the west, is called that because its shadows are made of little lines. When you walk in it, you feel like you're inside a pen-and-ink drawing.
textes.Le Bois des Lutins ! Mon territoire ! En: The Goblin Wood! My territory! Well, the goblins'. But soon mine!
textes.Le Bois des Lutins, au nord-est ! Le cam: The Goblin Wood, to the north-east! The goblin camp! The chief! The banner! Then, adventure!
textes.Le Bois des Lutins, au nord-est, c'est l: The Goblin Wood, to the northeast, that's where the goblin camp is. With a chief! He has a banner! If you beat him, will you show me the banner? Just show it. I won't touch it. Only a teeny bit.
textes.Le Bois des Lutins, au nord-est, est ple: The Goblin Wood, to the north-east, is full of goblins. They have a camp deep in the wood, with a chief and a banner. A chief! A banner! At last, a feat worthy of a song. A real one.
textes.Le Bois des Lutins… On dit que les gobel: The Goblin Wood… They say the goblins hide behind the trees. There are a lot of trees.
textes.Le Bois des Riffs — des chênes et des bo: The Riff Wood — oaks and birches; the wind plays guitar in the leaves
textes.Le Bois des Spores, au sud, autour du vi: The Spore Wood, to the south, around the old gasholder: birches, willows, purple buddleias that butterflies adore, and mushrooms everywhere. It's the most beautiful wood in the archipelago. And Lisse wants to turn it into a car park.
textes.Le Bois-Doré. Des arbres si grands que l: Bois-Doré. Trees so tall their crowns are lost in golden light… A path of lanterns winds toward the elves' village.
textes.Le Bois-Doré… Des arbres de soixante mèt: The Bois-Doré… Trees sixty metres tall? That'd make a lot of shovel handles. No, I'm joking. Half joking.
textes.Le Bolet-Ressort, au chapeau orange. Dan: The Spring-Bolete, with the orange cap. In the fairy tale, it gives you grasshopper legs: you jump three times higher, and it goes “boing”. Watch the landing, it doesn't take care of that. And remember: in a fairy tale, yes. In the real forest: never!
textes.Le Borgo des Coquillettes — le hameau de: The Borgo of the Macaroni — the followers' hamlet: houses of every colour, a trellis, a long table, and a smell of warm bread
textes.Le Boucanier, c'est une feuille pliée en: Le Boucanier is one sheet folded in four, stapled in the middle. Hence my name: an agrafe is a staple. Before, they called me Paperclip. I switched: a staple holds better. It commits, a staple does.
textes.Le Boucanier, tout frais, et les affiche: Le Boucanier, fresh off the press, and the Great Boucan posters. The ink is free. On your fingers. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Le Boulevard des Néons traverse toute la: Neon Boulevard crosses the whole city, from the quay to the south. At night, everyone passes through. It's the best audience in the archipelago.
textes.Le Boulevard des Néons — la grande avenu: The Neon Boulevard — Neopolis's great avenue, from the quay to the south of the city
textes.Le Bourgmestre Hector aime les rubans, l: Burgomaster Hector loves ribbons, medals and speeches. He used to look at us sideways. Now he looks at us straight on, sometimes at a slant. That's progress. He did reopen the Line in the end. He truly loves his town. And, lately, ours a little too.
textes.Le Bourgmestre Hector est descendu pour: Burgomaster Hector came down for the reopening. He cut the ribbon with Dean Agathe, then gave a forty-minute speech. I didn't hear a word of it. Best speech of my life.
textes.Le Bourgmestre Hector est passé à la For: Burgomaster Hector came by the Forge for the reopening. He asked if we made medals. I said: “We make rails.” He said: “What about a little medal shaped like a rail?” I made him one. He pinned it on straight away. HO HO!
textes.Le Bourgmestre Hector voulait visiter la: Burgomaster Hector wanted to visit the Grotto without a helmet, “for the portrait”. I said no. He made a speech about freedom. I made a speech about gravity. Mine was shorter. He put the helmet on. The portrait came out very well.
textes.Le Bourgmestre Hector, vous le connaisse: Do you know Burgomaster Hector? For the reopening, he had prepared a two-hour speech. Under the sea, sound carries far: it could be heard all the way to the Institute. The lanternfish gathered against the glass to listen. The Burgomaster is convinced they applauded. I haven't told him otherwise.
textes.Le Bourgmestre a décidé que les pigeons: The Burgomaster has decided that the pigeons on the Square should have a licence. Everyone wants to register theirs.
textes.Le Bourgmestre a une nouvelle médaille !: The Burgomaster has a new medal!
textes.Le Bourgmestre avait oublié ses ciseaux: The Burgomaster had forgotten his scissors to cut the ribbon at the wash-house. I offered him my hammer. He said yes. I shouldn't have hit so hard. There's still a hole in the paving, with a little plaque. I walk past it every day. I laugh every day.
textes.Le Bourgmestre d'en haut a une broche en: The Burgomaster up top wears a Column-shaped brooch under his sash. Ysaé made it. But the little crystal at the top, I cut that. So, in a way, the Burgomaster wears a bit of the Fronde next to his heart. It makes me laugh all day.
textes.Le Bourgmestre d'en haut porte une broch: The Burgomaster up top wears one of Ysaé's brooches under his sash. The little crystal on top — I cut it. When she told me, we laughed all through the meal. A piece of the Fronde right against the Burgomaster's heart!
textes.Le Bourgmestre de Hautefond aime les dis: The Burgomaster of Hautefond loves speeches, ribbons and medals. He gave a two-hour speech in front of our brazier. We listened right to the end. Here, everyone has the right to speak. Even for a long time. Especially those who aren't used to being listened to right to the end.
textes.Le Bourgmestre de Hautefond aime les rub: The Burgomaster of Hautefond loves ribbons, speeches and medals. He sent me forty pages of congratulations for the reopening. I read them. All of them. He truly loves his city. And a little bit of ours, I think.
textes.Le Bourgmestre de Hautefond est descendu: The Burgomaster of Hautefond came down for the reopening. He gave a two-hour speech, standing in front of the brazier. We listened to the very end. Then we handed him the talking spanner so he could carry on. He was so surprised he fell silent. He left all moved.
textes.Le Bourgmestre de Hautefond voulait coup: The Burgomaster of Hautefond wanted to cut a thirty-metre ribbon for the reopening. Mistress Capucine refused. In the end they cut a thirty-centimetre one, together. I found them very touching. And very slow.
textes.Le Bourgmestre fait un discours sur la P: The Burgomaster is giving a speech on the Square. Quick, let's take the back street.
textes.Le Bourgmestre m'a acheté une broche en: The Burgomaster bought a Column-shaped brooch from me. He made out it was for his niece. He doesn't have a niece. He wears it under his sash. I saw it shining during his speech on Tuesday. I didn't say a thing. I'm a professional.
textes.Le Bourgmestre m'a commandé cinquante-se: The Burgomaster ordered fifty-seven medals from me. For himself. The Medal Medal, the Ribbon Medal, the Moustache Medal… He's as vain as a peacock and as sweet as a lamb. It's a very rare mix.
textes.Le Bourgmestre me regarde de travers dep: The Burgomaster has looked at me sideways since day one. Then he bought a brooch from me, on the quiet. He wears it under his sash. When people pretend not to like something, it's often because they're starting to like it.
textes.Le Bourgmestre reçoit… quand il ne fait: The Burgomaster receives visitors… when he isn't giving a speech.
textes.Le Bourgmestre veut couper un ruban à la: The Burgomaster wants to cut a ribbon when the Clouds reopen. A thirty-metre ribbon, wrapped around the Column. I told him it doesn't like ribbons. He gave me a speech. It creaked all through the speech.
textes.Le Bourgmestre veut des rubans, des disc: The Burgomaster wants ribbons, speeches and grand openings. The Column wants oil, silence and punctuality. I'm stuck in the middle. It's exhausting. But he truly loves this town. You can tell by his moustache.
textes.Le Bourgmestre veut donner mon nom à une: The Burgomaster wants to name a star after me. It's very kind of him. He's been looking for a “free” star through my telescope for two months. He's looking through the wrong end. I don't dare tell him.

The Burgomaster wants to name a star after me. I explained that the stars already have names. He said he'd find a “free” one. He's been looking for two months, with my telescope. He doesn't know which end to look through.
textes.Le Bourgmestre veut sa tasse. Et ses lun: The Burgomaster wants his cup. And his glasses. And his other cup.
textes.Le Bourgmestre voulait couper un ruban d: The Burgomaster wanted to cut a thirty-metre ribbon around the Column for the reopening of the Clouds. I said no. We cut a thirty-centimetre one, together. He made a speech anyway. She creaked through the whole speech.
textes.Le Bureau de vente de Lisse, au sud-oues: Lisse's Sales Office, south-west of the square: all grey, all clean, with signs saying “Coming soon: the Lisse-Center”. Every morning, his robots repaint it grey. Every night, I repaint it in colour. It's our little dance.
textes.Le Bureau de vente de Papa, c'est le bun: Dad's Sales Office is the grey bungalow south-west of the square. I file folders there. Well, I stack them. In the shape of a drum kit. Mademoiselle Prune lets me. She gave me a stapler that goes “tchak”.
textes.Le Bureau de vente devient… une salle de: The Sales Office is becoming… a rehearsal room, according to Gédéon. The grey chairs have become drum stools. They're very comfortable.
textes.Le Bureau de vente est au sud-ouest de l: The Sales Office is south-west of the square. I work there from eight to six, with a one-hour break. During the break, I go to Lentille's Canteen. I always pay a little extra. For the files I didn't send.
textes.Le CLONG, c'est toi qui tombes, mon chér: The CLONK is you falling off, sweetheart.
textes.Le Cabaret des Cailloux. Ce soir : le pl: The Pebble Cabaret. Tonight: the funniest of the little Moai. (He wrote that on the poster himself.)
textes.Le Café Cumulus : des tables blanches, d: The Cumulus Café: white tables, cloud-shaped chandeliers, and behind the counter, in a glass globe, a little cloud slowly turning.
textes.Le Café Cumulus est au sud de l'Esplanad: The Cumulus Café is south of the Esplanade, right in front of Séraphin's Feather. If you get lost, follow the smell of sugar puffs. If you get lost again, follow the sparrows. They always know where I am.
textes.Le Café Cumulus, la nuit : les chaises d: The Cumulus Café at night: the chairs are asleep on the tables, the cloud chandeliers barely glow, and the cloud machine purrs away all by itself on the counter.
textes.Le Café Feedback : une odeur de chocolat: Café Feedback: a smell of hot chocolate and wet wool, a jukebox glowing pink, a cat sleeping on an amp… and a drip falling, drip, drop, into a cup placed on table three.
textes.Le Café Feedback est fermé. Sur la porte: The Feedback Café is closed. On the door: “We open when we wake up.” Through the window, cups, an old jukebox… and a cat sleeping on the amp.
textes.Le Café Feedback, je l'ai ouvert dans la: I opened the Feedback Café in the biggest yurt in Rainville. There's a jukebox that only plays one song, a cat that sleeps on the amp, and a leak above table three. The regulars fight over table three.
textes.Le Café Nébuleuse est à l'ouest de l'Ago: The Nebula Café is west of the Agora, Nébula's Bazaar is to the east. We wave at each other over the fountain. With four arms, I can say a lot of things. She never understands a thing.
textes.Le Camp des Fleurs — des yourtes en rond: The Flower Camp — yurts in a circle around the fire, pennants, painted buses, and drums that never sleep
textes.Le Campement du Clan — un feu, un totem,: The Clan Camp — a fire, a totem, drying racks… and square eyes watching you from behind the rocks
textes.Le Capitaine Charbonnel a sa table au Di: Captain Charbonnel has had his table at the Diable Repu for thirty years. He orders a hot sulphur punch and tells the story of the ash storm. I know it by heart. The waves grow every evening.
textes.Le Capitaine Charbonnel m'a appris à vol: Captain Charbonnel taught me to fly. Without him, I'd still be wearing a big coat to hide my wings. He lends me his telescope, he tells me about his storm, and he's never made fun of my too-big wings.
textes.Le Capitaine Charbonnel m'a rapporté un: Captain Charbonnel brought me back a twisted harpoon. A gargoyle had bent it with its teeth. He said: “Your harpoon ties itself in knots.” I answered: “Your gargoyle eats iron.” A draw.
textes.Le Capitaine Charbonnel m'achète des har: Captain Charbonnel buys harpoons from me against the gargoyles. He brings them back bent and asks me why. I tell him his gargoyles eat iron. We laugh. We start again.
textes.Le Capitaine Charbonnel raconte la même: Captain Charbonnel has told the same ash storm every evening for thirty years. Every time, the waves get higher. Now they're the size of the volcano.
textes.Le Capitaine Charbonnel veille sur le po: Captain Charbonnel watches over the port as if it were his own children. He tells the same storm story every evening, and each time, the waves get bigger. He's the one who married Grumbald and me, on his quay.
textes.Le Capitaine Ferdinand dit que je sonne: Captain Ferdinand says I ring too many alerts. Once, just once, I rang for a dragon-shaped cloud. It was REALLY dragon-shaped.
textes.Le Capitaine Ferdinand et moi, nous fais: Captain Ferdinand and I compare notes every week. Him with his alerts, me with the Baron. We compare our days. He often wins. Turnips are worse than a baron.
textes.Le Capitaine Ferdinand et moi, nous somm: Captain Ferdinand and I are the only two reasonable people in Montjoie. We meet every week to check. He has the turnips, I have the Baron.
textes.Le Capitaine Ferdinand m'a commandé ving: Captain Ferdinand ordered twenty swords for the guard. He wants them “regulation”. I asked him what that meant. He thought for a long time. He said: “Pointy.”
textes.Le Capitaine Ferdinand m'a écrit un arti: Captain Ferdinand wrote an article in the regulations just for me. Article twelve. I'm very proud. Nobody else has an article.
Captain Ferdinand wrote an article just for me. Nobody else has an article. He sighs a lot when he sees me, but he always brings me a blanket in winter.
textes.Le Capitaine Ferdinand me commande les é: Captain Ferdinand orders the guard's swords from me. He wants them “regulation”. It took me a while to understand that meant “pointy”. He's an upright man. Like his swords.
textes.Le Capitaine Ferdinand soupire à chaque: Captain Ferdinand sighs every time I ring an alert. You can hear his sighs all the way to the square. But he always runs out first. He's a real captain. I like him.
Captain Floc'h is me, Salomé. And I'm not a captain.
textes.Le Capitaine Isidore dit que je l'ai rou: Captain Isidore says I swindled him when I sold him the lighthouse. He's lived there for fifteen years, with his seagulls. He wouldn't move for anything in the world. I consider him satisfied.
textes.Le Capitaine Isidore m'a appris à saluer: Captain Isidore taught me how to greet seagulls. A little wave of the hand, then you bow your head. I do it every evening from the rampart. The seagulls don't answer. The Captain says they're shy with nobility. Mélusine answers, though. Very loudly. She's a bit of a seagull, Mélusine.
textes.Le Capitaine Isidore parle aux mouettes,: Captain Isidore talks to the seagulls, and the seagulls answer him. I find that charming. They returned a hat to me once. With an egg in it.
textes.Le Capitaine Isidore passe me voir à la: Captain Isidore comes to see me at the North Gate with his seagulls. They peck my helmet to wake me up. It's very kind of them. I give them my bread crusts.
textes.Le Capitaine Isidore se moque de moi par: Captain Isidore makes fun of me because I fish in a lake. He says the sea is more dangerous. There are no giant frogs in the sea. He talks to seagulls. Everyone has their own fears.
Captain Isidore makes fun of me because I fish in a lake. He says the sea is more dangerous. There are no giant frogs in the sea. Only seagulls. He talks to them.
textes.Le Capitaine Rigatoni habite dans une ba: Captain Rigatoni lives in an upside-down boat, on the beach! It's the most awesome house in the world. When it rains, it goes “tap-tap-tap” on the roof. The roof is the bottom of the boat.
textes.Le Capitaine Rigatoni m'a promis de m'ap: Captain Rigatoni promised to teach me to fish. That was twelve years ago.
textes.Le Capitaine Rigatoni prétend qu'un pira: Captain Rigatoni claims a pirate must bury his treasure “where the shadow of the mast touches the sea at noon”. I did the calculation. It's right next to his boat. He knows. He pretends not to.
textes.Le Capitaine Rigatoni, il raconte qu'il: Captain Rigatoni says he saw the Great Spaghetti out at sea, before anyone else. I say it was a jellyfish. He still holds it against me.
textes.Le Capitaine Sans-Chair lève son sabre :: Captain Fleshless raises his sabre: “Up, lads!” Skeletons rise from the ground!
textes.Le Capitaine Sans-Chair s'effondre en un: Captain Sans-Chair collapses into a heap of bones. The eyes of Skull Rock go dark… The mouth of the skull awaits you.
textes.Le Capitaine Sel, le grand-père de Croc: Captain Sel, Croc's grandfather? I knew him. A real rogue. He came here, yes, with a chest. He left without it. I'll say no more.
textes.Le Capitaine a un trésor ! Un vrai ! Il: The Captain has a treasure! A real one! He says he can't remember where he buried it. I think he remembers. He always looks at the same spot when he talks about it.
textes.Le Capitaine est ma meilleure source sur: The Captain is my best source on pirates. He exaggerates everything, but always in the same direction. For a scientist, that's very handy: you just divide by three.
textes.Le Capitaine fait tournoyer son sabre to: The Captain whirls his sabre all around him!
textes.Le Capitaine m'a juré qu'il avait perdu: The Captain swore to me he'd lost the Golden Grater. He swore it on his beard. His beard blushed.
textes.Le Capitaine, c'est le plus grand pirate: The Captain is the greatest pirate in the world. He's got a parrot, an eye patch and a boat-house. When I'm big, I'll be his first mate. He said maybe. Maybe is nearly yes.
textes.Le Cargo, la Baleine Rouillée, au nord-o: The Freighter, the Rusty Whale, to the northwest. We started in its hold. In the morning, I go up on deck. I watch the sea. It goes “shhh”. It's a good audience.
textes.Le Cargo, la Baleine Rouillée, est échou: The Freighter, the Rusty Whale, is beached on the north-west shore. The Radio Boucan studio is in the wheelhouse, right at the top, and the antenna is at the top of the mast. When it's windy, the whole ship sings. I put it on air. It's called “The Freighter Minute”.
textes.Le Cercle t'a vu arriver avant moi. Je s: The Circle saw you coming before I did. I am Ysolde Lunevoile. I keep the Moonstones. Nobody touches them without my knowing. Nobody.
textes.Le Cinquième Soleil tourne, et Cipactli: The Fifth Sun turns, and Cipactli sleeps for good.
textes.Le Cinquième Soleil. Un grand feu, deux: The Fifth Sun. A great fire, two altars: gold and jade on one side, reeds and thorns on the other. On the wall, a fresco: gods around the fire, and one of them leaping.
textes.Le Cirque des Os — des os partout. Et, q: The Bone Circus — bones everywhere. And, somewhere, an enormous breath
textes.Le Clan te couvre de cadeaux (surtout de: The Clan showers you with gifts (mostly shiny coins found in the river).
textes.Le Cocyte, au fond des Neuf Cercles, c'e: The Cocytus, at the bottom of the Nine Circles, is the opposite of our nights: a night without any light at all, cold as a silence. If you go down there, take a flame. A small one is enough. A small flame in the great cold is already a poem.
textes.Le Cocyte, le lac gelé, le Neuvième et d: The Cocytus, the frozen lake, the Ninth and last Circle. It snows, under the earth. Far at the bottom, a throne of ice.
textes.Le Colosse a peur du tonnerre. J'ai dit: The Colossus is afraid of thunder. I said it was a flaw. Wilfried said: “A robot that's afraid, Master, is a robot with a heart.” Hm. I didn't answer. I didn't fix the flaw either.
textes.Le Colosse fait peur aux enfants. Il ne: The Colossus frightens the children. He wouldn't hurt a fly. In fact, he's scared of flies.
textes.Le Colosse lâche un jet de vapeur brûlan: The Colossus lets out a jet of scalding steam all around it!
The Colossus waved at me. I swear. With his big iron hand.
textes.Le Colosse, c'est mon chef-d'œuvre. Il d: The Colossus is my masterpiece. It was meant to guard the city against storms. It's afraid of thunder. I think it gets that from me. Hm. The rest of the time, I look for a sweeper that sings. I don't speak to Héloïse any more. In the evening, I sit on the bench on the promenade. So does she. Each at our own end.
The Colossus is my masterpiece. He was meant to guard the city against storms. He's afraid of thunder. I haven't worked out why yet.
textes.Le Comptoir des Courants, c'est à l'est: The Currents Trading Post is to the east of Pearl Square. You'll find everything there: ropes, springs, Azure pearls, singing shells. And a board by the entrance, with the news of the day. People come for the ropes and stay for the board.
textes.Le Conseil classe nos réclamations, à Hé: The Council files our complaints, Héloïse's and mine, in a folder marked “Draw”. I protest. Héloïse protests too. We sent a joint complaint. The First Councillor filed it in the same folder.
textes.Le Conseil des Nuées décide de tout ce q: The Cloud Council decides everything we share: the cloud water, the gardens, the weather balloons, the Shuttle timetable. And once a year, the name of the most beautiful cloud.
textes.Le Conseil m'a nommée ambassadrice il y: The Council appointed me ambassador two hundred years ago. Mission: observe the Heavy-Feet without ever disturbing them. So I disguise myself. I've been an old fishwife, a pétanque player, a nun, a punk, a goblin… Ah. I shouldn't have said that.
textes.Le Couvercle Sacré est le couvercle de l: The Sacred Lid is the lid of the very first cooking pot on the island. It's made of copper. It goes BOOONG. The other lids go “tink”. That's the whole difference.
textes.Le Couvercle Sacré, il ne faut JAMAIS le: The Sacred Lid must NEVER be struck three times. I know. I know very well. I learned it… the hard way. Three times.
textes.Le Couvercle Sacré, sur le parvis : on l: The Sacred Lid, on the forecourt: we strike it to call the faithful. Once is for prayer. Twice is for dinner. Three times… Three times, we don't strike it. Ask Macaroni why. No, don't ask him, he'll give you an hour-long speech.
textes.Le Cratère du Lac — une eau immobile, co: The Lake Crater — still water, the color of the sky, at the bottom of the volcano
textes.Le Cristal de Givre s'illumine sous ta m: The Frost Crystal lights up under your hand: you've crossed the Mirror Lake. Borée will be proud of you.
textes.Le Cénote sacré, au nord-ouest, c'est un: The sacred Cenote, to the north-west, is a door to the world below. In the evening, bats come out of it by the hundred. Camazotz, the death bat, commands them, they say.
textes.Le Cœur bat comme au premier jour. (Il r: The Heart is beating like on the very first day. (He sniffs.) It's the crystal dust. It stings the eyes. Thanks, kiddo. Really. Grmbl.
textes.Le Cœur bat de nouveau là-haut, comme un: The Heart beats once again up high, like a drum in crystal clear; and it's all thanks to you, oh my… to you, er… the Heavy-Foot… so dear. Sorry. Emotion cut my rhyme short.
textes.Le Cœur bat. Tu l'entends ? Tout là-haut: The Heart is beating. Can you hear it? Way up there, in the Spire. Thanks to you. I can never thank you enough, so I'll thank you a little bit every day.
textes.Le Cœur de la Flèche, le grand cristal q: The Spire's Heart, the great crystal that keeps Astralys afloat, is growing weak: three shards have broken off and fallen onto the island. Volt, the energy engineer, can weld them back with three astral crystals, but then the Heart's light must be restored, right at the top of the Spire.
textes.Le Cœur de la Montagne bat sous nos pied: The Heart of the Mountain beats beneath our feet. It's growing weak. When it stops, the lava will wake. Not today. Not tomorrow. But one day.
textes.Le Cœur de la Montagne… Une pierre de fe: The Heart of the Mountain… A fire stone, big as a barrel, that beats deep in the volcano. It keeps the lava asleep. Since the golems woke, its beat has grown weak. Nori will tell you more. One day, perhaps, we'll need you, big one.
textes.Le Cœur du Volcan rallumé: The Heart of the Volcano rekindled
textes.Le Cœur ronronne de nouveau comme au pre: The Heart purrs again as it did on the first day, my child. I'm no longer cold inside. I think I'll take a little nap beside it. To celebrate.
textes.Le Cœur va bien, Frère Cendrin ?: Is the Heart all right, Brother Cendrin?
textes.Le Cœur-Brasier brûle haut et clair, grâ: The Ember Heart burns high and bright, thanks to you. The whole city is warm. Even Asmodin smiled. Twice. I counted.
textes.Le Cœur-Brasier n'est plus qu'une petite: The Ember Heart is now nothing but a small blue flame. It needs the Eternal Flame, lost deep in the Nine Circles.
textes.Le Cœur-Brasier, c'est le grand feu sous: The Ember Heart is the great fire under the Forge Cathedral. As long as it burns high, Pandémonia is warm, the lanterns shine, the bread rises. When it grows pale, the whole city shivers. And a shivering demon is a sad sight.
textes.Le Cœur-Brasier, le grand feu de la Cath: The Ember Heart, the great fire of the Forge Cathedral that warms all of Pandémonia, grows paler by the day. A chill is rising from the Nine Circles beneath the cathedral: they say the Frost Titan has carried off the Eternal Flame.
textes.Le Cœur-de-Pierre, au centre, c'est un p: Stoneheart, in the centre, is a perfectly round plateau ringed by cliffs. Nobody goes up there. At the foot of its western face, there's a giant gate: the Gate of the Four Seals.
textes.Le Deuxième Cercle. Sur un trône de bron: The Second Circle. On a bronze throne, MINOS, judge of the underworld, crowned, his long tail coiled around him. He waits for you to present yourself.
textes.Le Diable Repu est au Port de Cendre, su: The Diable Repu is at the Ash Port, on the quay. Sailors come for the punch, merchants for the news, and the news for the merchants. Everything that gets said in Pandémonia gets said here first.
textes.Le Disquaire : des milliers de pochettes: The Record Shop: thousands of sleeves, a smell of cardboard and old paper, and a turntable spinning softly.
textes.Le Disquaire est fermé. Une affiche, col: The Record Shop is closed. A poster, stuck on crooked: “Back after rehearsal. Do not touch the records. Or the cat.”
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle Brise ? Il est sur le: Doctor Aurèle Brise? He's out in the field, which is to say on the Promenade, watching the sky through his binoculars. He names the new clouds. He called one of them “Tuesday-Gaston”.
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle Brise étudie le haut,: Doctor Aurèle Brise studies what's up above; I study what's down below. He names his clouds, I name my jellyfish. He sends me the weather in the sky, I send him the weather in the Trench. We had never met before the reopening. We recognised each other at once: by the way we look up. Or down.
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle Brise, de l'Institut d: Doctor Aurèle Brise, of the Institute of Winds, up in the Clouds, is my oldest correspondent. He studies what's above, I study what's below. He names his clouds, I name my jellyfish. He sends me the sky's weather, I send him the Trench's: weak current, visibility twelve metres, jellyfish passing in the late afternoon. We agree on one point: a jellyfish is a cloud that chose the sea.
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle a donné mon prénom à u: Doctor Aurèle named a cloud after me! It's tiny and round. Like me, says Mum.
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle donne un nom à chaque: Doctor Aurèle gives every new cloud a name. There's one called “Tuesday-Gaston”.
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle donne un prénom aux nu: Doctor Aurèle gives clouds names, I give them colours. We never agree. He says “Gontran”, I say “apricot”. It's the same cloud. We argue very gently. It's my favourite conversation of the week.
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle donne un prénom à chaq: Doctor Aurèle gives every cloud a first name. I give them a colour. We never agree. He says “Gontran”. I say “apricot”. It's the same cloud.
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle m'a annoncé une averse: Doctor Aurèle forecast a shower for twelve minutes past three. I brought the terrace in. It was bright sunshine until evening. At twelve past three, he sneezed. He says that was the shower.
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle m'a commandé une machi: Doctor Aurèle ordered a weather-forecasting machine from me. I made it. It perfectly forecasts yesterday's weather. He finds it very useful. He says it's the only one that's never wrong.
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle m'apprend une blague p: Doctor Aurèle teaches me one joke a day. One hundred and twelve. I understand no jokes. But when I tell them, people laugh. The Doctor says the funny is me. I searched my memory for “funny”. Definition: something that does you good. I accept.
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle me commande des machin: Doctor Aurèle orders machines from me to forecast the weather. I make him machines that forecast yesterday's weather. He finds them very useful. He says they're the only ones that are never wrong. I don't know if that's a compliment.
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle me donne la météo avan: Doctor Aurèle gives me the weather before every race. I always do the opposite of what he says. I always win. He's offended. I gave him a cloud in a jar to cheer him up. He named it.

Doctor Aurèle gives me the weather before every race. I always do the opposite. I always win. He doesn't know whether to be offended or proud. Me, I'm grateful. He's the best reverse lucky charm on the island.
textes.Le Docteur Aurèle veut le ballon en l'ai: Doctor Aurèle wants the balloon up in ten minutes. Or in ten clouds.
textes.Le Donjon des Mille Marches: The Keep of a Thousand Steps
textes.Le Donjon des Mille Marches ! La dernièr: The Dungeon of a Thousand Steps! Last time, I went down as far as the sixth step. Today, the seventh!
textes.Le Donjon des Mille Marches est très anc: The Dungeon of a Thousand Steps is very old. Philomène says the steps were carved by a king who was afraid of the light. He went down, and down, and was never seen again. His steps, though, stayed.
textes.Le Donjon des Mille Marches, sous la tou: The Dungeon of a Thousand Steps, under the ruined tower of the Fangs. They say a fearful king had those steps carved to flee the light. He went down so deep that he became all soft, all green, all gooey. And he kept his crown. Heh heh heh.
textes.Le Donjon des Mille Marches, à l'étage q: In the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps, on the fourth floor, there are chests that bite! Mimics! Philomène told me. If I see one, I'll whack it on the lid with a hammer. Bonk.
The Dungeon of a Thousand Steps.
textes.Le Donjon des Mille Marches… Cinq étages: The Dungeon of a Thousand Steps… Five floors. At the bottom, the Jelly King. Whichever of us defeats him first will be the true hero of Montjoie. I'm ready. Almost. I'm waiting for the right dramatic moment.
textes.Le Donjon des Mille Marches… J'y suis de: The Dungeon of a Thousand Steps… I went down. Once. As far as the sixth step. There was a noise. It was my stomach. I went back up to eat. But next time, friend, we'll go all the way to the Jelly King!
textes.Le Dôme d'Azur (au fond de la mer): The Azure Dome (at the bottom of the sea)
textes.Le Dôme d'Azur a rouvert, au fond de la: The Azure Dome has reopened, at the bottom of the sea, and the Fronde is still playing all night long in the Strata. Up here, we hear the music through the Column's shaft. Mr Pascal has written his fortieth complaint.
textes.Le Dôme d'Azur — la ville au fond de la: The Azure Dome — the city at the bottom of the sea (breathe: the air comes from the surface)
textes.Le Dôme d'Azur, au fond de la mer, a rou: The Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea, has reopened! On Sunday I'm going to see the whales through the ceiling! Well, the whale. There's only one. But she's very big.

The Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea, has reopened, apparently. More people coming up here. From the bottom of the sea all the way to the sky! Their ears are going to pop. I sent them some choux buns. For the ears. It helps. They didn't understand. They ate them.
textes.Le Dôme d'Azur, au fond de la mer, c'est: The Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea, is closed for works. But when it reopens, I'll go and see the whales through the ceiling!
textes.Le Dôme d'Azur, au fond de la mer, rouvr: The Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea, is reopening soon, apparently. More people coming up here. From the bottom of the sea all the way to the sky! Their ears are going to pop. I'll make them some chouquettes. For the ears. It helps.
textes.Le Dôme d'Azur, ce sont trois dômes de v: The Azure Dome is three glass domes set on the floor of the Trench: the Great Dome, with Pearl Square; the Greenhouse Dome, to the west; and the Institute Dome, to the east. Two glass galleries link them. Outside, the sea, midnight blue. Inside, six hundred people who decided to live in the sea without disturbing it.
textes.Le Dôme d'Azur… Les jeunes disent que c': The Azure Dome… Young folk say it's a city under the sea, with streets made of glass. In my day, under the sea, there were fish. Now there are people. The fish must be surprised. The line has reopened. I went down to see if it leaks. It doesn't leak. Hm.

The Azure Dome… Young folk say it's a city under the sea, with streets made of glass. In my day, under the sea, there were fish. Now there are people. The fish must be surprised. The line reopens soon, they say. We'll see if it leaks.
textes.Le Dôme des Serres, c'est le petit dôme: The Greenhouse Dome is the little western dome, at the end of the Gallery. The hydroponic towers, with the lettuces and strawberries under pink lamps; the algae wall; the Lamp Orchard; the lily pond and its little bridge; and my stall, next to my house. The whole Dome eats what grows here. It makes me proud. And a bit tired.
textes.Le Festival du Larsen, c'était chaque ét: The Larsen Festival happened every summer. Everyone came. Then Mother Downpour and Granny Sunflower fell out, and nobody dared go up on stage again. A stage without music is like a record without a groove.
textes.Le Fieux Filas raconte des hiftoires dep: Old Thilas hath been telling thtorieth for fifty yearth. Half of them are true. The problem ith knowing which half. Me, I believe the half that thuitth me.
The Cursed Fort, on the eastern point. The cannons are still there. I go and see them sometimes. The skeletons leave me alone. They find me scary.
textes.Le Four Éternel, c'est mon arrière-arriè: The Eternal Oven was lit by my great-great-grandfather with an ember from the Ember Heart, four hundred years ago. It has never gone out. When he handed it over to me, my father said: “Bobor, you can botch a brioche. You can botch a batch. But never let the oven get bored.” I sing it lullabies at night.
textes.Le Four Éternel, c'est mon trésor. Quatr: The Eternal Oven is my treasure. Four hundred years without going out. At night I sing it lullabies so it doesn't get bored. The neighbours say it's the oven singing. I don't correct them.
textes.Le Funiculaire d'Azur, c'est la plus bel: The Azure Funicular is the most beautiful ride down in the archipelago. You leave from Strata Station in a brass cage, you pull the lever, and you sink into the rock. Then the cabin comes out of the cliff, and there… the whole city under its three domes, glowing in the blue. Thirty years I've been making that trip. I still hold my breath.
textes.Le Funiculaire fait trente descentes par: The Funicular makes thirty trips down a day, and Marius sings every time. The tunnel has excellent acoustics. Unfortunately.
textes.Le Garde-Marée bascule sur le dos ! Vite: The Tide Warden flips onto its back! Quick, strike it!
textes.Le Garde-Marée se remet sur ses pattes !: The Tide Guard gets back on its feet!
textes.Le Gardien du Cœur est apaisé ! La Lame: The Guardian of the Heart is calmed! The Heart Blade, 200 coins, one more heart, and a title: “Hero of the Four Peoples”. The circle of light, north of the hall, will take you back to the surface.
textes.Le Gardien du Cœur s'effondre… Les veine: The Heart Guardian collapses… The veins of fire fade. Above, the great crystal stops beating so hard; its red light turns golden, soft as an evening sun.
textes.Le Gardien frappe le sol : des créatures: The Guardian pounds the ground: creatures from all four wings come running!
textes.Le Glisseur stellaire des Lumens (Ionie,: The Lumens' Star Glider (Ionie, at the Astralys Spaceport)
textes.Le Goff est le meilleur cartographe que: Le Goff is the best cartographer Carène has ever had. He's also the only one who wants to open a gate our ancestors closed. I respect him. I keep an eye on him.
textes.Le Gouffre. (Il s'appuie sur la rambarde: The Chasm. (He leans on the bridge railing.) Nobody has ever seen the bottom. Down there, a river. It comes from very far, it goes very far. It sings one single note, forever. The Valves tune to it. Every evening.
textes.Le Gouverneur Lagrange est l'homme le pl: Governor Lagrange is the most talkative man I've ever won at dice. I gave him back after three days. He ate all my honey and gave me speeches at breakfast.
textes.Le Gouverneur Lagrange s'est proclamé go: Governor Lagrange proclaimed himself governor all on his own. Nobody voted. Nobody protested either. He buys the rounds.
textes.Le Gouverneur interdit les bagarres ! …: The Governor forbids brawling! … on Sundays.
textes.Le Gouverneur m'a commandé la carte offi: The Governor commissioned the official map of Port-Coutelas from me. He wanted boulevards, an opera house and a statue of himself. I drew them. They don't exist. My finest map since the continent.
textes.Le Gouverneur m'achète tout ce qui brill: The Governor buys everything that glitters from me: his gold tricorn, his chain, his medals. He pays in official promises. I have a drawer full of promises. They're very well written.
textes.Le Gouverneur veut faire du Sans-Pitié l: The Governor wants to make the Merciless the flagship of the Port-Coutelas navy. Port-Coutelas has no navy. And the Merciless isn't his. She belongs to the sea. And a little to me.
textes.Le Gouverneur, mon chou, c'est un grand: The Governor, sweetie, is a big child with a gold tricorn. He makes speeches, he promises pontoons, and he buys the rounds. The port likes him. So do I. But I'm the one who decides.
textes.Le Grand Boucan approche ! Les affiches: The Great Boucan is coming! The posters are ready. Pigment painted the rat, I printed the letters. They need to travel to the other islands. The posters, not the letters. Although…
textes.Le Grand Boucan restera dans les mémoire: The Great Boucan will be remembered: Granny Barricade raises her fist on the mezzanine, Clou smiles (really, he does), and the whole pit chants your name. Go and see Rouille afterwards!
textes.Le Grand Cristal faiblit. Il se nourrit: The Great Crystal is fading. It feeds on three Pearls of Light, one for each age of the sea… They were scattered when the sharks came. Bring me back the {manque}, and the dome will live another thousand years. I'll give you the trident of our kings.
textes.Le Grand Dôme a un tambour de verre, hau: The Great Dome has a glass drum, six metres high, with a cupola on top: glass triangles set in a white lattice. Forty-six metres to the top. Every triangle has a number. I know them all. Number one hundred and four is my favourite: it's had a tiny bubble trapped in the glass since day one. Like a star.
textes.Le Grand Marché est au nord-est de la Ba: The Great Market is in the north-east of the Lower Town: my spices, Kraxx's weapons, Vespérine's potions and Bobor's bread. It smells of fire, sugar, iron and sulphur. It's the smell of home.
textes.Le Grand Marché, c'est le ventre de Haut: The Great Market is the belly of Hautefond, sweetie. Striped awnings, fountains, stalls… There's fruit from the Orchards, flour from the Mill, fish from the Harbour, and Ysaé's jewellery. All of Hautefond comes through here. And all of Hautefond says hello to me.
textes.Le Grand Moaï te voit, avec ses yeux de: The Great Moai sees you, with his coral eyes. He looks pleased. Well… for a mountain.
textes.Le Grand Spaghetti Volant entrouvre un œ: The Great Flying Spaghetti half-opens an eye, looks at you, and closes it again. It's still sulking. (Reverend Father Farfalle, at the temple, might know why.)
textes.Le Grand Spaghetti Volant redescend douc: The Great Flying Spaghetti slowly comes back down… A long noodle stretches toward you and touches your shoulder, very gently. You have just been Touched by His Noodly Appendage. (It tickles, and it smells good.) Go and see Reverend Father Farfalle!
textes.Le Grand Spaghetti Volant te fait un pet: The Great Flying Spaghetti gives you a little noodle wave. (Nobody knows how it stays up in the air. The followers say: “by the sauce!”)
textes.Le Grand Spaghetti boude depuis une sema: The Great Spaghetti has been sulking for a week. His noodles are drooping, his eyes are half-closed… There's a recipe, in the old books, to reconcile him with us. But I'd need help. A lot of help.
textes.Le Grand Spaghetti, je l'ai peint cent f: I've painted the Great Spaghetti a hundred times. He never looks like my paintings. I think he moves on purpose when I look at him.
textes.Le Grand Temple a deux sanctuaires. Celu: The Great Temple has two shrines. Tlaloc's, the blue one, wants water: a rain jar. Huitzilopochtli's, the red one, wants fire: burning copal. Bring both, and the door of the Fifth Sun will open between them.
textes.Le Grand Troc ! Ici, pas de pièces : on: The Great Swap! No coins here: we trade. One thing for another, and everyone goes home happy. Today, I'll take:
textes.Le Grand Troc, le vrai, c'est une chaîne: The real Great Swap is a chain: you give a pebble, you get an acorn, then a feather, then a vial… At the end, there's always something beautiful. I'll show you, if you like.
textes.Le Grand-Père Séverin me traite de gamin: Grandpa Séverin calls me a youngster. I'm seventy. He says I can complain when I'm his age. I'm practising. I'm very good at it.
textes.Le Grand-Père Séverin raconte la montée: Grandpa Séverin tells the story of the island's rise as if he'd been there. So do I. Neither of us was. We correct each other.

Grandpa Séverin tells everyone about the day the island rose. I checked the archives: that day, it was grey. He's right on that point. As for the rest, he has a lot of imagination. And a very fine beard.
textes.Le Géant des Brumes, ma chanson la plus: The Giant of the Mists, my most famous song, was told to me by him. I added a princess, a storm and a dragon. He came to see me after the concert, moved, and said: “It's even better than what happened.” I asked him what had happened. He said: “A rock.” I kept the princess.
textes.Le Géant des Brumes… Je vais vous dire l: The Mist Giant… I'll tell you the truth. It was a rock, in the fog. I charged it shouting my name. I bumped into it. When the fog lifted, there was a shepherd applauding. He told the story to everyone. I didn't have the heart to contradict him.
textes.Le Jardin Zen est le seul endroit de Néo: The Zen Garden is the only place in Neopolis where the light comes from the sky, not from neon signs. I come here to learn the real colours.
textes.Le Jardin Zen — des cerisiers en fleurs,: The Zen Garden — cherry trees in bloom, raked gravel… and silence, at last
textes.Le Jardin Zen, au sud-est, c'est le seul: The Zen Garden, to the south-east, is the only place without a screen. I go there in the morning, with Master Ishi. We say nothing to each other for an hour. It's the best conversation of the day.
textes.Le Jardin des Apesanteurs est derrière t: The Zero-Gravity Garden is behind you. Your tummy goes “oh” as it meets gravity again.
textes.Le Jardin des Apesanteurs, au bout du po: The Zero-Gravity Garden, at the end of the bridge of light, to the west: that's where I rehearse. You jump three times higher and come down very gently. For a dancer, it's paradise. For a Heavy-Foot, it's very funny. Especially the landing.
textes.Le Jardin des Apesanteurs, c'est moi aus: The Zero-Gravity Garden is mine too. An experiment on gravity. It failed: gravity only works at a third now. But everyone loves it, so we say it was on purpose.
textes.Le Jardin des Apesanteurs, à l'ouest : i: The Zero-Gravity Garden, to the west: there's a course of glowing rings, timed. My record? I'm not saying. It's too good. It would discourage everyone.
textes.Le Lac Napolitain est le seul lac de sau: The Neapolitan Lake is the only known lake of sauce. It never freezes, it doesn't evaporate, and it smells delicious. I come to take its temperature twice a day. It's always perfect.
textes.Le Lac Napolitain — un lac de sauce toma: The Neapolitan Lake — a lake of tomato sauce, calm and steaming (no swimming)
textes.Le Lac Souterrain. Des pierres plates fo: The Underground Lake. Flat stones form a ford… and giant frogs, big as barrels, stare at you. One of them, on the western islet, has a belly that glows with a copper sheen. It swallowed something.
textes.Le Lac des Grenouilles est à l'est de Mo: Frog Lake is east of Montjoie, through the East Gate. There are reeds, a jetty, and frogs as big as carts. A river runs out of it towards the sea, to the south-east. The frogs swim down it to go bathing. In the sea. I don't know why.
textes.Le Lac des Grenouilles est à l'est, derr: Frog Lake is to the east, beyond the East Gate. Yvon fishes there, and he sells me the frogs he catches. Well, the ones that don't catch him first.
textes.Le Lac des Grenouilles, à l'est de la vi: Frog Lake, east of town, past the East Gate… The frogs there are as big as carts. They swallow anything shiny. And anything that screams. I shine, and I scream.
textes.Le Lac des Grenouilles, à l'est, c'est m: Frog Lake, to the east, is my workplace. Yvon, the fisherman, keeps count: I've been swallowed forty-seven times. He has a notebook. He says I'm his best frog indicator.
textes.Le Lac des Long-Cous — des cous si longs: The Long-Neck Lake — necks so long they graze on the treetops
textes.Le Lisse-Center aurait eu quatre cents b: The Lisse-Center would have had four hundred shops, two thousand parking spaces and a fountain playing the Lisse & Fils anthem every hour. I wrote the anthem myself. It was missing… a drummer.
textes.Le Lisse-Center sera ouvert vingt-quatre: The Lisse-Center will be open twenty-four hours a day, three hundred and sixty-five days a year, forever. An eternal shopping mall. Like a concert, but with no music, and you have to pay.
textes.Le Lisse-Center. Éternel, climatisé, opt: The Lisse-Center. Eternal, air-conditioned, optimised. My name in grey letters on the front. … That's what I ought to answer. That's what I answer.
textes.Le Livre des Vents a mille pages. J'en s: The Book of Winds has a thousand pages. I'm on page one thousand and one.
textes.Le Lord ! Six croissants par matin, depu: The Lord! Six croissants every morning, ever since he arrived. He eats one, the seagulls get the rest. It's crazy. And a bit beautiful, I think.
textes.Le Lord Pemberton, chambre douze, collec: Lord Pemberton, room twelve, collects strange objects. He pays well, and very dearly.
textes.Le Lord a voulu acheter mon perroquet en: The Lord wanted to buy my wooden parrot. For his collection. He offered three gold coins for it! I said no: without it, the Perroquet Bleu would just be plain Bleu — blue, and nothing else. He sighed, ordered a punch, and clinked glasses with the parrot. Since then, every evening, he says good evening to it as he comes in. The parrot doesn't answer. It's polite, but wooden.
textes.Le Lord a voulu m'acheter mon plumeau. I: The Lord wanted to buy my feather duster. He said a duster that had touched so many wonders was a wonder itself. He offered a gold coin for it! I refused: what would I have done room twelve with? He sighed. The next day, he asked if he could at least draw it. The duster. Not me.
textes.Le Lord anglais commande six croissants: The English Lord orders six croissants every morning. He only eats one. The rest he gives to the seagulls.
textes.Le Lord anglais de l'hôtel achète n'impo: The English lord at the hotel buys any “exotic” trinket. I sold him a sardine bone as a “sea dragon tooth”.
textes.Le Lord anglais paie toujours avec des p: The English Lord always pays in gold coins. I never have enough change.
textes.Le Lord de la douze paie bien, et très c: The Lord in twelve pays well, and very handsomely. He would also like my moustache. It is not for sale. It is not even for rent.
textes.Le Lord est un brave homme, riche comme: The Lord is a decent man, rich as the sea and gullible as a cabin boy. I sold him a sardine bone. I laugh about it. A bit less at night.
textes.Le Lord secoue chaque boule à neige cont: The Lord shakes every snow globe next to his ear before he buys it. “To hear the snow,” he says. I asked him what you can hear. He said: “Listen.” I listened. Nothing. Then a tiny whisper, like sugar falling. Ever since, I listen to all of them in the evening, when I close up. Don't tell anyone. They'll think I'm turning English.
textes.Le Lord vient tous les jours me demander: The Lord comes every day to ask for my jar of figs. It's not for sale. He's unbearable. He's polite. That's worse.
textes.Le Lord, c'est mon client en or. Littéra: The Lord is my golden customer. Literally: he pays in gold coins. Charming, generous, a bit mad. I never have change, and he never has anything else.
textes.Le Marché de Nuit — des lanternes, des m: The Night Market — lanterns, steaming pots, and a robot making noodles
textes.Le Marché de Nuit, c'est mon rituel. Un: The Night Market is my ritual. A bowl, a tea, and off to bed.
textes.Le Masque de Jade ! Le visage des rois d: The Jade Mask! The face of the kings of Yaxché, hundreds of little green squares. 150 coins, one more heart, and a title: “Victor of Xibalba”. A secret staircase, behind the altar, climbs back to the top of the temple.
textes.Le Mont Bolognaise est un volcan tout à: Mount Bolognese is a truly unique volcano. Its lava is a tomato sauce at ninety-four degrees, lightly salted, with basil. My colleagues on the other islands don't believe me. I send them jars. They believe me a little more.
textes.Le Mont Bolognaise — un volcan de sauce: Mount Bolognese — a tomato sauce volcano; the path winds up to the Cooking Pot
textes.Le Mont Fumant — il fume, il gronde, il: The Smoking Mountain — it smokes, it rumbles, it spits red. Don't step on the red!
textes.Le Mont Fusain\npar ici, le sentier du s:
Mount Charcoal
this way, the path to the summit
textes.Le Mont Fusain porte mon nom, ou c'est m: Mount Charcoal bears my name, or I bear its name. Nobody remembers anymore. It's dark grey, even when the island has its colours. Well, almost: in spring, the heather turns it purple.
textes.Le Mont Fusain — une grosse colline rond: Mount Charcoal — a big round hill; the path climbs to the summit
textes.Le Moulin des Quatre Vents est sur la co: The Four Winds Mill sits on the western hill. From here you can see all of Hautefond in tiers, the shining Column, and the Orchards to the south. All the town's flour comes from here. Every loaf in Hautefond has a little poetry in it.
textes.Le Moulin des Quatre Vents, sur la colli: The Four Winds Mill, up on the hill, turns so regularly in a west wind that you could tell the time by it. I tried. Augustin changed a sail that very day. I was late for the first time in my life. I've never forgiven him. Well, a little.
textes.Le Muet ! Ce soir, tes quatre temps, com: Silent One! Tonight, your four beats, as always!
textes.Le Muet ! La cible est prête ?: Silent One! Is the target ready?
textes.Le Muet a parlé, une fois. Personne ne s: The Mute spoke once. Nobody knows what he said. Everyone who was there forgot. Strange, isn't it?
textes.Le Muet est le seul homme qui me compren: The Silent One is the only man who understands me without my opening my mouth. I'm the only one who understands his hands. Between the two of us, we make a whole conversation.
textes.Le Muet est mon client préféré. Il ne bo: The Mute is my favourite customer. He doesn't move, he doesn't talk, he doesn't complain, and he pays me in pearls. He has a little heart on his arm. Don't tell him I told you.
textes.Le Muet et Gros-Louis se disent les meil: The Mute and Gros-Louis say they're the best brawlers in port. They've never taken me on. They're scared. They're right.
textes.Le Muet n'a pas de couplet dans ma chans: The Silent One doesn't have a verse in my song. He has a silence. Four beats. The whole room goes quiet, and he nods. It's the finest part. Everyone says so.
textes.Le Muet ne dit rien, et c'est l'homme le: The Silent One says nothing, and he's the most reliable man in the archipelago. If I had to trust someone with the Widow's helm, it would be him. He wouldn't argue.
textes.Le Muet se dit champion. Il ne m'a jamai: The Mute calls himself champion. He's never faced me. He looks at me, I look at him, and nobody throws a punch. At least he doesn't mumble. He makes gestures. Gestures, I hear very well.
textes.Le Muet, c'est le seul qui me fait peur: The Silent One is the only one who scares me and makes me laugh at the same time. He doesn't talk, but he hits like a tide. We've never fought for real. We respect each other too much. And we're a bit scared, too.
textes.Le Muet, c'est mon meilleur copain. Il n: The Silent One is my best pal. He never contradicts me! He carries me back to the Widow every evening, on his shoulder. Hic! I see the port upside down. It's pretty, the port, upside down.
textes.Le Mur d'Expression, à l'ouest de la vil: The Expression Wall, west of town, is Boucan's giant front page. Anyone can paint on it. Pigment spends her days there. I paste the concert posters on it. We never tread on each other's toes. Almost never.
The Expression Wall, west of town, is the wall where everyone's allowed to paint. You too! Grab a can and leave your mark. The wall doesn't judge. I do, a bit. But nicely.
textes.Le Mur des Fresques a un nouveau bout :: The Mural Wall has a new bit: a bridge, a cabin, and people from up top in hats. Fusain says it's the next part of the story.
textes.Le Mur des Fresques raconte tout. Là, la: The Mural Wall tells everything. There, the founding: Brasero, very young, lighting the first brazier in a wheelbarrow. There, the Frondeurs' Bridge being welded. There, the first Assembly. There, Ysaé climbing up top on a ladder of light. And there… an empty space. That's for what comes next.
textes.Le Musée des Mondes a deux salles. La sa: The Museum of Worlds has two rooms. Room one holds the objects from Ondelune: the Elder's youth, our first clocks, clouds in jars. Room two holds the objects from down below. Room two is much more interesting. There's a spoon. I labelled it “small soup shovel”. That must be what it is.
textes.Le Musée des Mondes est à l'ouest de l'A: The Museum of Worlds is west of the Agora. Room one: objects from Ondelune. Room two: objects from the islands down below. Room two is much more interesting. Don't tell the Elder: room one is her youth.
textes.Le Mât des dirigeables, c'est mon port à: The Airship Mast is my own harbour. It's made of steel, it has a hundred steps, and at the top there's a gangway where the Albatross hooks on by its nose. The nose is the sturdiest part of an airship. Same as with stubborn people.
textes.Le Palais de l'Archiduchesse se dresse a: The Archduchess's Palace stands at the top of the Citadel, above the Circle of Fire. Four bridges lead to it. I beg you not to run on them: the lava has never cared for people in a hurry.
textes.Le Parc des Brumes et sa cascade: The Mist Park and its falls
textes.Le Parc des Brumes, c'est le meilleur en: The Mist Park is the best place for kites. There's wind, grass, and the pond that spills over the edge of the island: that makes the Cloud Falls. The water falls and falls, and it turns into mist before it reaches the bottom. Even the water never makes it all the way down!
textes.Le Perroquet à midi et le soir, la plage: The Perroquet at lunch and in the evening, the beach in the afternoon, on my red towel. I'm the one who writes the menu on the board, with spelling mistakes on purpose to make Toni laugh. Lucas plays cards and loses. Django, my neighbour, slows the music down as soon as Lucas walks in; I've told him to stop. And Nadine, at the post office, has guessed everything. In short, everybody knows. Except him.
textes.Le Petit Plongeon est rond, jaune, avec: The Little Diver is round and yellow, with two big portholes at the front, like astonished eyes. I talk to him during dives. “Easy, my little duck. Ten more metres.” He answers with little “bloops”. Yolande talks about pressure. I say he agrees.
textes.Le Petit Plongeon, c'est Yolande et moi: Yolande and I did up the Little Diver like new when I was seventeen. The line was closed; at the bottom of the sea, there wasn't much else to do. I painted it yellow, because yellow shows up from far away in the blue. Yolande said: “That way, I'll always see you.” I thought she was talking about the paint.
textes.Le Petit Train fait le tour de la Grande: The Little Train goes round the Great Stratum: the Station, Cogwheel Square, the Forge, the Mine entrance, the Gardens, the Galleries. One loop, twenty minutes, if nobody dawdles on the rails. The children run alongside. Bernadette pretends she can't catch them.
textes.Le Petit-Géant : minuscule, mais très fi: The Little-Giant: tiny, but very proud. In the fairy tale, it makes you grow for a while, and you hit harder. Don't bump into the doorframes. And don't step on Chaussette's dogs. And remember: in a fairy tale, yes. In the real forest: never!
textes.Le Phare de la Pointe guide les bateaux: The Point Lighthouse guides boats to Rigging Harbour. There are rocks everywhere here. My lamp tells them: “Not that way, this way.” The boats obey. The gulls, never.
textes.Le Phare… (Elle sourit longtemps.) C'est: The Lighthouse… (She smiles for a long time.) That's the loveliest answer anyone has ever given me. The Lighthouse doesn't move, but everyone comes back to it.
textes.Le Phlégéthon, une rivière de lave bouil: The Phlegethon, a river of boiling lava. Basalt rafts cross it all by themselves, in no hurry. On the other bank, an enormous beast with a man's face waits: Geryon.
textes.Le Pinceau de l'île, celui que je t'ai c: The island's Brush, the one I entrusted to you, is the elders' brush. It has passed from hand to hand since the village was founded. It only paints with the colours of the Palette. Take good care of it.
textes.Le Piston Joyeux est au cœur de la Ville: The Jolly Piston is in the heart of the Middle Town, between the Great Market and the clockmaker's. If you get lost, listen: when something whistles, it's here. When something laughs very loudly, that's Rosalie, here too.
textes.Le Piston Joyeux, c'était la taverne de: The Jolly Piston was my father's tavern. He served strong drinks, and people argued. I replaced it all with hot chocolate. Since then, people still argue, but they end up laughing. Chocolate rounds off the corners.

The Jolly Piston was my father's tavern. They served strong drink there, and people always ended up quarrelling. When he left me the tavern, I replaced the lot with chocolate. The first evening, nobody came. The second, three people. The third, the whole Middle Town. People didn't know they needed chocolate.
textes.Le Plat de la Grande Réconciliation ? En: The Dish of the Great Reconciliation? At last! I've been telling him for a week: a sulking spaghetti is a hungry spaghetti! (She takes a nest of golden tagliatelle out of a basket, freshly made.) Here. I made them this morning, by hand, singing. Don't crush them, don't break them, and don't eat them on the way. I know you.
textes.Le Plateau des Anciens et le Grand Moaï: The Elders' Plateau and the Great Moai
textes.Le Plateau des Anciens — le Grand Moaï,: The Elders' Plateau — the Great Moai, and the circle of Moai with a door
textes.Le Point Soins, c'est une petite pièce à: The First-Aid Post is a little room at the entrance to the Cannery, with a red cross painted by Pigment. She gave the cross a mohawk. I didn't have the heart to say no.
textes.Le Pont des Frondeurs : sous vos pieds,: The Frondeurs' Bridge: under your feet, the Chasm (and, far, far below, a glowing river)
textes.Le Pont des Frondeurs, c'est la porte de: The Frondeurs' Bridge is the gateway to the Fronde. Welded rails, bolts as big as your fist, and underneath, the Chasm. You can't see the bottom. You hear the river rumbling. Folk from up top cross holding hands. Round here, we call it “the bridge of new friends”.
textes.Le Pont des Frondeurs, je le traverse en: I cross the Frondeurs' Bridge on my skateboard. Brasero says it's not allowed. But nobody ever voted on it. So I cross it. Slowly. Very slowly. There's the Chasm underneath, after all. I'm not crazy. I'm brave. That's different.
textes.Le Popol Vuh, notre livre du conseil, ra: The Popol Vuh, our book of counsel, tells how the gods made people: first out of mud, which melted; then out of wood, and they had no heart; and at last out of maize. We are people of maize.
textes.Le Port de Cendre, c'est la Rade, au nor: The Ash Port is the Harbour, in the north-east of the island: the basalt quays, my black-sailed ships, Moloka's fish stall, Brindille's post office, the Diable Repu and the red-lit lighthouse. Everything that comes to Pandémonia passes through here. You too, as it happens.
textes.Le Port des Cordages, au nord-est. On l': Rigging Harbour, to the north-east. It's called that because of the ropes: they're everywhere. For the boats, for the nets, for the cranes. Lady Ysolde bought her very first rope here. I keep it in the harbour office. It's very old, very short, and very important.
textes.Le Port des Mouettes est au nord-ouest d: Seagull Harbour is in the north-west of the island, at the end of the North Gate road. The quays, the harbour master's office, the fishmonger's, the lighthouse, and the jetty where you moored your boat. The seagulls keep an eye on it. Free of charge.
textes.Le Port des Nuées, c'est un grand ponton: The Cloud Harbour is a big pier jutting out into the sky, on the west side of the island. Airships and gliders moor there. There's the harbour office, my office, and a sign that says “Mind the drop”. Nobody reads it. Everybody looks at the drop.
textes.Le Professeur Benthos m'a demandé un mic: Professor Benthos asked me for a microphone to record the Great Singer. I made him one. He put it against the glass of the Observation Bay and listened for three days. He recorded the Singer, two rays, a shoal of lanternfish and his own stomach. He says it's the most beautiful symphony in the archipelago.
textes.Le Professeur Benthos me demande de lui: Professor Benthos asks me to bring him back “a little water from the bottom, please, and a shrimp, if she agrees”. I brought him a shrimp. He asked her if she agreed. She said nothing. He let her go. He's a very good scientist. He only keeps what he's given.
textes.Le Professeur Benthos me demande de rapp: Professor Benthos asks me to bring back “a little water from the bottom, and a shrimp, if she's willing”. He listens to the Singer, he talks to the jellyfish, and he forgets to eat. He's the only grown-up in the Dome who wants to know what's down there even more than I do.
Professor Benthos forgets to eat. Every day. So I keep a bowl and a seat for him, at one o'clock. He arrives talking about whales, eats talking about whales, and leaves saying he wasn't hungry. He had two bowls.

Professor Benthos forgets to eat. Every day. So, at one o'clock, I keep a bowl and a seat for him. He arrives talking about the whale, he eats talking about the whale, and he leaves saying: “I wasn't hungry.” He had two bowls.
textes.Le Professeur Benthos parle à la baleine: Professor Benthos talks to the whale. He says she answers him. One evening, I pressed a glass against the window, and my ear against the glass. I heard “hmmmmmm”. The Professor said it meant “good evening, Mila”. I think he makes things up. But I wrote it down anyway.
textes.Le Professeur Benthos tient un dictionna: Professor Benthos keeps a dictionary of the Great Singer's songs. Twelve hundred phrases! Me, when she sings, I just write: “News of the day: the whale is well.” It's my favourite column. And the only one that's never wrong.
textes.Le Professeur Benthos vient faire la cla: Professor Benthos comes to teach the class once a month. He was supposed to talk about jellyfish. He talked about the whale for two hours. The children were spellbound. So was I. I didn't dare interrupt him. The jellyfish will have to wait till next month.
textes.Le Professeur Benthos vient parfois resp: Professor Benthos sometimes comes to breathe in front of my algae wall. He says it's “the freshest air in the Dome, to within two per cent”. He closes his eyes, takes three breaths, and runs back off to his whale. I think he mostly comes for the calm.
textes.Le Professeur Benthos écoute la Grande C: Professor Benthos listens to the Great Singer every evening. He says she talks, and he has a dictionary. I think he makes some of it up. But when she sings, his eyes shine like a lanternfish. So I listen too. With a glass against the pane.
textes.Le Professeur Benthos était mon élève, à: Professor Benthos was my student, at the Institute. Then he became my teacher. Then he became absent-minded. He forgets to eat, he talks to a whale, and one day he dropped his tie into the Aquarium. The jellyfish kept it for three days. He's the greatest scientist I know.
textes.Le Professeur Lunette avait monté la gra: Professor Lunette had assembled the Observatory's great telescope upside down. He was observing the cellar. I put it right in one night. When I'd finished, I said “it's perfect”. It's the only time I've said it out loud. It was true.
