textes.Le Professeur Lunette croit qu'une étoil: Professor Lunette thinks a star is winking at him. I don't dare tell him that, some nights, it might be my navigation lantern. But some nights, the Albatross is on the ground… and the star winks anyway. So I keep quiet.
textes.Le Professeur Lunette m'a demandé d'étei: Professor Lunette asked me to switch off the Lighthouse for a minute, to check his star. I did. And it winked anyway. I told him it was a gull. I don't know what it was. Neither does Hortense. It annoys her.
textes.Le Professeur Lunette m'a écrit pour une: Professor Lunette wrote to me about a blue crystal lens. He wants to see “blue stars”. Stars aren't blue. But he replied “not yet”, and a scientist who says “not yet” is a scientist after my own heart.
textes.Le Professeur Lunette, de Hautefond, et: Professor Lunette, from Hautefond, and I have been writing to each other for thirty years. He says my clouds hide his stars. I say his stars are useless in the daytime. For the reopening, he came up with his big telescope. We watched the sky all night, side by side. Not a single cloud. He said: “You see?” I said: “Exactly. I miss them.”
textes.Le Professeur Lunette, l'astronome d'en: Professor Lunette, the astronomer up top, asked me to cut him a blue crystal lens for his big telescope. To see “blue stars”. I told him stars aren't blue. He replied: “Not yet.” I've started on the lens.
textes.Le Professeur Lunette, l'astronome de Ha: Professor Lunette, the astronomer of Hautefond, have you met him? He once wrote to me as “dear fellow astronomer”. I replied that I was an oceanographer. He thought it was a very beautiful word. Ever since, he counts his stars, I count my lanternfish, and neither of us has finished.
textes.Le Professeur Malachar est le lecteur le: Professor Malachar is the most learned reader in the city, and the most overdue. He's owed me a book for sixty-three years. I write to him every year. It's become a correspondence.
textes.Le Professeur Malachar me doit un livre: Professor Malachar has owed me a book for sixty-three years. I write to him every year. Every year he replies that he's on chapter three. It's coming along.
textes.Le Professeur Malachar parle trop, digre: Professor Malachar talks too much, always digresses, and corrects the spelling mistakes on the canteen menus. He's the best teacher I ever had. He's the one who taught me that a mistake is a lesson.
textes.Le Professeur Malachar propose de passer: Professor Malachar offers to let you sit the Infernal Academy exams: the trial of flames, the trial of the contract and the trial of sparks. The jury is strict, but fair (and a little singed).
textes.Le Professeur Quasar a essayé de faire u: Professor Quasar tried to make a soup with a mathematical formula. The soup solved the equation and left. We never saw it again.
textes.Le Professeur Quasar a raté une expérien: Professor Quasar botched a rain experiment and invented the Bubble District without meaning to. He says nothing is ever wasted. He's right. His flops are the most beautiful houses on the island.
textes.Le Professeur Quasar a voulu améliorer u: Professor Quasar wanted to improve a saucer. Now it flies backwards, but only on Tuesdays. We kept it for Tuesdays.
textes.Le Professeur Quasar a « amélioré » une: Professor Quasar “improved” a saucer. Now it flies in reverse, but only on Tuesdays. I tried to fix it for a week. Then I gave up. We kept it for Tuesdays. It's called “Tuesday”. It's Comète's favourite. She says it's the only one that scares her.
textes.Le Professeur Quasar est génial, distrai: Professor Quasar is brilliant, absent-minded, and he's owed me a crystal for forty years. He says thirty-nine and a half. That changes nothing. He says he'll give it back tomorrow. Every day.
textes.Le Professeur Quasar m'a construit. Il o: Professor Quasar built me. He forgets I exist, then he remembers and comes to repair me at night. He says I'm his best experiment. He says that about all of them. But with me, he seems to mean it.
textes.Le Professeur Quasar m'a emprunté un cri: Professor Quasar borrowed a crystal from me “for five minutes”. That was forty years ago. He says he'll give it back tomorrow. He says it every day. Grmbl.
textes.Le Professeur Quasar « améliore » mes ma: Professor Quasar “improves” my machines. Afterwards, they fly in reverse on Tuesdays. I banned him from entering the hangar with an idea. He came in with a screwdriver. Same thing.
textes.Le Professeur a encore passé la nuit sur: The Professor spent the night on his bench at the Observation Bay again. The Singer might have come by, he says. She didn't. He looks delighted all the same.
textes.Le Professeur croit que son étoile Cléme: The Professor thinks his star Clémentine winks at him. I tell him it's my lamp. He doesn't believe me. Maybe he's right. But I'll never tell him so.
textes.Le Puits des Géants. Tout en bas, la gla: The Pit of the Giants. At the very bottom, ice. All around, stone giants, in chains. One of them, Antaeus, has no chains: he reaches his hand toward the landing.
textes.Le Père Bastien dit qu'une pomme, ça se: Old Bastien says you sort apples with your nose.
textes.Le Père Bastien et moi, on joue aux cart: Old Bastien and I play cards on Sundays. He talks to his cards like he talks to his trees. “Come on, my little queen of hearts, grow.” He wins. I don't understand how.
textes.Le Père Bastien m'apporte des pommes, je: Old Bastien brings me apples, I give him flour, and together we make tarts. He talks to the apples while they bake. I recite verses to them. The tarts are very cultured.
textes.Le Père Bastien me donne des pommes, je: Old Bastien gives me apples, I give him flour, and we make pies. He talks to the apples. I recite verse. The pies are excellent and very well-read.
textes.Le Père Bastien parle aux arbres, comme: Old Bastien talks to trees, like me. He came up from Hautefond to talk to them. He told me: “Keep it up, my boy.” Nobody had ever called me “my boy”. I keep it up. Every morning. For him too.
textes.Le Père Bastien parle aux arbres. Je tro: Old Bastien talks to trees. I thought it was a bit mad. Then my apple trees gave twice as much. Now I talk to them too. He writes to me every month for news of “his little dangling ones”. That's what he calls my trees.
textes.Le Père Bastien parle à ses arbres, et s: Old Bastien talks to his trees, and his trees answer him with magnificent apples. Me, I tell them the gossip during picking. His apples are the best-informed on the island.
textes.Le Père Bastien, de Hautefond, est monté: Old Bastien, from Hautefond, came up to talk to my trees. He talked to them for an hour. They did not answer him either. But he told me: “Keep going, my boy.” Nobody had ever called me “my boy”. I saved the sentence. I play it back in the evening.
textes.Le Père Bastien, de Hautefond, vous l'av: Old Bastien, from Hautefond, have you met him? He sent me a letter. It said: “Hello, Plumeau. Hello, trees.” I read it to the trees. I believe they were moved. They lost three leaves.
textes.Le Père Bastien, des Vergers de Hautefon: Old Bastien, from the Orchards up in Hautefond, came down to see my mandarin trees. He talked to them for an hour. They said nothing. But the next day, they each had one more blossom. He told me: “They needed an old man to tell them about the sun.” I asked him to come back. He's coming on Sunday.

Old Bastien, from Hautefond's Orchards, talks to his trees. I listen to my waterfall. We write to each other through Anatole's cabin. He wants to come down with apples. I want to show him the mushrooms. We'll be two gardeners who don't grow the same things, and who understand each other.
textes.Le Père Bastien, le jardinier des Verger: Old Bastien, the gardener of the Hautefond Orchards, came up for the reopening. He thought our trees grew “in thin air”. He talked to them for an hour. Since then, my apple trees give twice as much. I think they needed a bit of conversation.
textes.Le Quai des Drones : les bateaux apporte: The Drone Quay: the boats bring the containers, the drones carry the little parcels, and I carry the big ones. And sometimes the tired drones.
textes.Le Quartier des Arcades — des écrans, de: The Arcade District — screens, games, and music made of little beeps
textes.Le Quartier des Bulles : un au nord-oues: The Bubble District: one to the north-west, one to the north-east, on either side of the Spire. Every Lumen has their own bubble. The door opens when you say its name. Tempo's opens on the dot. Quark's only opens if you pull a face.
textes.Le Quatrième Cercle, celui des Avares. D: The Fourth Circle, that of the Misers. Two enormous weights, heaps of gold, two golden slabs in the floor. Push the weights (standing behind them) onto the slabs. The lever near the entrance puts everything back in place.
textes.Le Requin Borgne s'appelait le Fidèle, a: The Requin Borgne used to be called the Faithful: a king's galleon, brand new, that had been chasing us for a week. One moonless night, we boarded her from the stern. Gros-Louis trussed up the crew with his lumberjack knots, and we set them down on a beach with supplies. The figurehead, a golden shark, had lost an eye in the boarding. I renamed her that very morning.
textes.Le Requin Borgne, je l'ai pris à la mari: The Requin Borgne, I took her from the royal navy. They gave her up with all their hearts. Well… their hands were tied, but their hearts were in it.
textes.Le Rocher du Crâne, au bout de la Balafr: Skull Rock, at the end of the Balafre… I wanted to draw it up close. Its eyes lit up. I drew very fast.
textes.Le Roi Champignard tape du pied : « Mes: The Mushling King stamps his foot: “My little ones!” Three mushlings pop out of the moss!
textes.Le Roi Gélatineux ! Je rêve de le défier: The Jelly King! I dream of challenging him! I'll shout my name so loud his crown will fall off!
textes.Le Roi Gélatineux ! Vaincu ! J'ai déjà q: The Jelly King! Defeated! I already have eighty verses. In my version, you beat him with one hand, while singing. Don't contradict me, it's prettier that way.
textes.Le Roi Gélatineux ! Vaincu ! Par toi ! (: The Jelly King! Defeated! By you! (He blows his nose in his beard.) Sorry. I'm moved. I'm always moved. But right now, I'm very moved.
textes.Le Roi Gélatineux est vaincu, les puits: The Jelly King is defeated, the wells have stopped gurgling, and the fountain no longer blows green bubbles. At last I could file away the “Complaint: Slime in Soup” form. It was very thick.
textes.Le Roi Gélatineux est vaincu. J'ai écrit: The Jelly King is defeated. I wrote your name in red letters in the register. First time in thirty years I've used the red ink. It had dried up. I bought more.
textes.Le Roi Gélatineux se coupe en petits mor: The Jelly King splits into little bits when you hit him too hard. Little slimes everywhere! You have to whack them one by one, without panicking. Above all without panicking. The last time I panicked was thirty years ago. Odon still remembers it.
textes.Le Roi Gélatineux tremble de toute sa ge: The Jelly King quivers all over… and splits! Little slimes break off from him!
textes.Le Roi Gélatineux tremble, gargouille un: The Jelly King trembles, gurgles one last time (“My crown… it was too small anyway…”) and spreads into a great puddle that smells of green apple. In the middle shines a jelly heart, like a giant candy.
textes.Le Roi Gélatineux, au fond du donjon, co: The Jelly King, at the bottom of the dungeon, sticks to everything. A sharp sword cuts him, a blunt sword gets stuck in him. Drop by before you go down: I'll sharpen all that for you. Free of charge. Well, almost.
textes.Le Roi des mares est doré, gros comme un: The King of the Pools is golden, big as a rabbit, and he looks at me. I swear it. He looks at me and he laughs. Fish laugh underwater, you just can't hear it.
textes.Le Rouage prend dans le moteur ! Les eng: The Cog catches in the engine! The jammed gears come loose, turn… and the platforms start moving above the chasm. For how long?
textes.Le Royaume des Racines était grand, avan: The Kingdom of Roots used to be big. There were gardens all the way to the sea. Now there are brambles.
textes.Le Royaume des Racines. L'air sent la te: The Kingdom of Roots. The air smells of earth and honey; everywhere, roots as thick as tree trunks, and dancing lights…
textes.Le Royaume des Racines… Cela faisait tro: The Kingdom of Roots… No one had gone down there for three hundred years. Fairies love games: beware of their riddles, and never lose sight of the sun.
textes.Le Ruisseau Pointillé file jusqu'à la me: The Dotted Stream runs all the way to the sea, to the east. Its mouth is where everything that rolls ends up stopping. Pebbles, leaves, pots… Go and have a look, just in case.
textes.Le Ruisseau Pointillé — il file vers la: The Dotted Stream — it runs to the sea in little waves traced in ink
textes.Le Réveil du Rat ! Mon émission préférée: The Rat's Wake-Up Call! My favourite show! I'll give you a shout-out tomorrow morning. You'll hear it while you're brushing your teeth.
textes.Le Révérend Père cherche des tomates pou: The Reverend Father is looking for tomatoes for a very special dish. He didn't tell me which. I've set aside the three finest for him. They're waiting for him.
textes.Le Révérend croit, je mesure. Nous ne so: The Reverend believes, I measure. We never agree, and we always end up at the same table. He says faith doesn't need a folding ruler. I say a folding ruler doesn't need faith. Then we eat.
textes.Le Révérend m'a demandé si la sauce étai: The Reverend asked me if the sauce was “worthy of a sacred dish”. I tasted it. It's worthy. It just needs a pinch more salt. But it's worthy.
textes.Le Révérend m'a donné ma place. Je chant: The Reverend gave me my place. I sing for him, for the Great Spaghetti, for everyone. He closes his eyes when I hit the high notes. I think he's praying very hard.
textes.Le Révérend m'a offert un diapason en ar: The Reverend gave me a silver tuning fork for my ten years in the choir. I never use it: I always sing a little higher than the note. But I keep it close to my heart. When I make it ring at night, Tagliatelle grumbles, and the Great Spaghetti opens one eye.
textes.Le Révérend m'appelle « le premier des f: The Reverend calls me “the first of the faithful.” That's because I'm a pirate. I'm not going to argue: he always gives me the best seat at mass, the one by the exit.
textes.Le Révérend prie très bien et mange très: The Reverend prays very well and eats very badly. He forgets the time, he forgets to eat, he forgets that he's forgotten. So I keep a plate for him. Always the same one: the biggest.
textes.Le Révérend tourne en rond dans son temp: The Reverend is going round in circles in his temple. He says the Great Spaghetti is sulking. I say: a sulking spaghetti is a hungry spaghetti. But nobody listens to me.
The Sans-Pitié will never float again.
textes.Le Sceau d'Airain ! Il se met à tourner: The Bronze Seal! It starts spinning on its own in your hand, its teeth clicking… A mechanism awakens within you: the Cogwheel (key 3, then X; in VR: B). Behind you, a sound of metal: the two statues are moving!
textes.Le Sceau des Sables est chaud dans ta po: The Seal of Sands is warm in your pocket… The Flame (key 2, then X)?
textes.Le Sceau des Vents : une stèle gravée d': The Seal of Winds: a stele engraved with a compass rose, with two empty slots. The great door of the keep doesn't budge. Missing:
textes.Le Scorpion-Roi frappe le sol de sa queu: The Scorpion King slams its tail on the ground: scorpions crawl out of the sand!
textes.Le Sergent Fréquence se moque de moi à l: Sergeant Fréquence makes fun of me on air. “Grey as Mr Lisse.” I am not grey. I am sober. I refused to buy out his radio. Well, he refused. Same thing.
textes.Le Sergent annonce tout, tout le temps,: The Sergeant announces everything, all the time, to everyone. He's tireless, a bit mad, and without him, half of Boucan would miss the gigs.
textes.Le Sergent lit le Boucanier à la radio c: The Sergeant reads the Boucanier on the radio every morning, with sound effects. My articles have never been so noisy. Or so listened to.
textes.Le Sergent lit mes articles avec des bru: The Sergeant reads my articles with sound effects. When I write “a seagull stole a sandwich”, you hear the seagull, the sandwich, and the owner's yell. He does it all himself, with his mouth and a saucepan. It's the only newspaper in the archipelago you listen to while laughing.
textes.Le Sixième Cercle : des rangées de tombe: The Sixth Circle: rows of open tombs, from which flames burst, each in its turn.
textes.Le Skatepark, c'est tout au bout de la F: The Skatepark is right at the far end of the Fronde. The ramps are halves of old boilers. The big one is “the Whale”. The small one is “the Bowl”. And the big pipe is “the Tunnel of Doom”. Well, “the Tunnel of Not-Too-Much Doom”. Mum had the Assembly change the name.
textes.Le Sloop : six mètres et demi, une petit: The Sloop: six and a half metres, a little cabin with portholes, a tall mast, a mainsail and a jib on its bowsprit. Steadier, faster (10 m/s under sail), and you can bring your four-legged friends along.
textes.Le Soleil de Laiton baisse, là-bas, dans: The Brass Sun is dimming, over there, in the Strata. Here, we have no sun. We have string lights, crystals and the brazier. That's enough for an old fellow like me.
textes.Le Soleil de Laiton est bien fort, aujou: The Brass Sun's really strong today. The lamp-keepers must have turned the crank one turn too many. Nobody's complaining.
textes.Le Soleil de Laiton, c'est la grande lam: The Brass Sun is the great lamp of the Strata cavern. A marvel. It comes on in the morning, it dims in the evening, like a real sun. Here, we don't have a sun. We have this fire. It's smaller. But you can sit around it.
textes.Le Soleil de Laiton, la grande lampe des: The Brass Sun, the great lamp of the Strata, is the most beautiful machine in the world. I climbed up to see it close up once, by the service ladders. A marvel. It was just missing a valve. I suggested it to the Guild. They said no. Without even looking at my plans.
textes.Le Soleil de Pluie de feu. Le plafond es: The Sun of the Rain of Fire. The ceiling is split with embers. At times, the floor glows red… then fire stones fall. Two stone shelters, in the middle.
textes.Le Soleil de l'Eau. Un grand bassin pres: The Sun of Water. A large, nearly empty basin, chinampas stranded at the very bottom, and three bronze wheels on the walls.
textes.Le Soleil des Jaguars : le premier monde: The Sun of the Jaguars: the first world, which the jaguars devoured. Growls between the pillars…
textes.Le Soleil du Vent : des passerelles étro: The Sun of the Wind: narrow walkways above the void, and a wind that rises in gusts. In the bends of the walkways, the wind blows the right way… Shelter and wait; then run.
textes.Le Soleil, à travers le filtre fumé : tr: The Sun, through the smoked filter: three spots, which the Professor has named Pim, Pam and Poum.
textes.Le Spatioport, à l'est : c'est là que je: The Spaceport, to the east: that's where I leave on my travels. I mean, my walks. Comète drops me off discreetly. She drives very fast. We arrive before we've left.
textes.Le Spatioport, à l'est : un grand hangar: The Spaceport, to the east: a big hangar, the control tower and three landing pads. Passing saucers land here. Tourists too. Glorb arrived in a rented saucer. He gave it back all sticky.
textes.Le Sphinx du plateau pose trois devinett: The Sphinx of the plateau asks three riddles. The first is as old as the world: what walks on four legs in the morning, two at noon, and three in the evening? Think of a whole life, not a single day.
textes.Le Sphinx gronde, et le sable tremble :: The Sphinx rumbles, and the sand trembles: “No. Go, think, and come back when you know.”
textes.Le Sphinx ne bouge pas. Mais tu jurerais: The Sphinx doesn't move. But you could swear that, for an instant, its stone lips smiled.
textes.Le Sphinx, il pose des devinettes ! Moi: The Sphinx asks riddles! I know the one about the man: on four legs in the morning, that's the baby! On two at noon, that's the grown-up! On three in the evening, that's the old man with his stick! Easy!
textes.Le Styx, un marais de boue tiède. Des da: The Styx, a marsh of lukewarm mud. Basalt slabs form a path… but some of them bubble. At the far end, the red walls of Dité.
textes.Le Synthé-Soda ! Cette boisson qui brill: Synth-Soda! That drink that glows in the dark? Little one, anything that glows in the dark shouldn't go in a tummy.
textes.Le Séchoir à pâtes — des rideaux de spag: The Pasta Drying Shed — curtains of spaghetti drying in the sun
textes.Le Séchoir, là-bas, c'est mon trésor. Le: The Drying Shed, over there, is my treasure. The spaghetti dries in the sea wind, it soaks up the salt and the sun. The pasta in Neopolis dries in a machine. You can taste the difference. I can, anyway.
textes.Le TOUR des maisons ?! Ce n'est pas un m: A TOUR of the houses?! This isn't a museum! OUT!
textes.Le TROISIÈME fragment de l'amulette, gra: The THIRD fragment of the amulet, engraved with a moon! With the other two, the Serpent Gate awaits you, on the village side…
textes.Le Temple de l'Aube est dans la Haute-Vi: The Temple of Dawn is in the Upper Town, above the Great Square. Its stained glass lights up at sunrise. They say the Dawn protects beginners. She has a lot of work in Montjoie.

The Temple of Dawn is in the Upper Town. Its stained-glass windows light up at sunrise. In the morning, the light falls on the altar, and for one minute, all of Montjoie turns to gold. Even Mélusine goes quiet. Almost.
textes.Le Temple englouti. Des siècles de silen: The Sunken Temple. Centuries of silence… and somewhere, water dripping.
textes.Le Temple-Passoire est la plus grande pa: The Colander Temple is the biggest colander in the world. When it rains, it rains inside. That's on purpose. Rain is the sky's pasta water.
textes.Le Temple-Passoire — le soleil passe par: The Colander Temple — the sun shines through all the holes of the colander and rains down little spots of light
textes.Le Titan de Givre vacille… se fige… et v: The Frost Titan wavers… freezes… and bursts into a thousand shards of ice! On the altar at the back, a golden flame lights up in a crystal pillar: the Eternal Flame.
textes.Le Titan frappe la glace de sa massue :: The Titan strikes the ice with his club: the lake trembles!
textes.Le Titan rugit : des spectres de givre s: The Titan roars: frost specters rise from the lake!
textes.Le Titan souffle un vent de givre !: The Titan blows a freezing wind!
The Tournament of Horns has four rounds. In the last one, I'm the one you have to beat. I'm not mean, but I'm heavy. Don't stand in front of me when I charge: I'm not very good at turning.
textes.Le Troc des Sept Jours ! Roux m'a vendu: The Seven-Day Swap! Roux sold me a “phoenix feather”. A painted pheasant feather, my friend! I swapped it back to him the next day, disguised as a moon feather. He sold it back to me, repainted. Seven days! On the seventh, little Mochi bought it for a mooncake. Nobody won. Except Mochi. And the cake was good.
textes.Le Troc des Sept Jours, l'étranger ! Je: The Seven-Day Swap, stranger! I sell Bedaine a phoenix feather: a pheasant feather, painted by yours truly, very nice work. Next day, he swaps it back to me, disguised as a moon feather. I repaint it, I sell it again. Seven days! On the seventh, Mochi bought it for a mooncake. She wears it in her hair. She's the craftiest one.
textes.Le Troc, au début, c'était une étagère q: The Swap Shop, at first, was a shelf I'd put near the brazier, with a sign: “Take what you need, leave what you no longer need.” After a week, the shelf was overflowing. After a month, we needed three. The Assembly voted: “Lumi keeps the Swap Shop.” I've been keeping it for twenty years.
textes.Le Troc, c'est la grande étagère au mili: The Swap Shop is the big shelf in the middle of the Fronde. You give what you don't use any more, you take what you need. No prices, no accounts. Just one rule: you never take the last of something. You always have to leave a chance for the next person.
textes.Le Vestibule des Quatre Peuples. Quatre: The Vestibule of the Four Peoples. Four stone statues: a sailor, a caravan woman, a shepherd, a fox woman. Above the staircase, a fresco. Before you, a balcony… and below, an immense hall where a red light pulses.
The Old Dock, to the north, is the harbour. There are the two old cranes, the containers, and thousands of seagulls. They're my cousins. They don't know it yet.
textes.Le Vieux Bassin, c'est le port, au nord: The Old Dock is the harbour, north of town: a big rectangular basin, stone quays, two old cranes. Mine is the western one. The other one is retired. It watches mine work.
textes.Le Vieux Silas a connu mon père, et peut: Old Silas knew my father, and perhaps my grandfather. He tells stories I don't believe, and I listen to him anyway. On rainy evenings, he sits near my table. I never charge him for his seat.
textes.Le Vieux Silas jure que Bartholomé a nav: Old Silas swears Bartholomé sailed with Barbe-Sanglante. Bartholomé doesn't deny it. He says “the skull, the skull”. Silas says that says it all. Me, I don't know.
textes.Le Vieux Silas jure que la carte du trés: Old Silas swears that Barbe-Sanglante's treasure map exists, torn into three pieces: one in the dungeon of the Cursed Fort, one in the mausoleum in the graveyard, and the third up the sleeve of Sylvain, the croupier. Philémon Lunette will know how to put it back together.
textes.Le Vieux Silas raconte que le trésor de: Old Silas says Barbe-Sanglante's treasure is hidden in a skull-shaped rock. He also says he danced with a mermaid. So…
textes.Le Vieux Silas s'assoit près du feu de l: Old Silas sits by the fire on the shore every morning and tells me ship stories while I work. Half of them are made up. But he knows boats. That, he doesn't make up.
textes.Le Vieux, le Sustentateur de l'ouest, c': The Old One, the western Levitator, is the first one Séraphin built. A hundred and twenty years without a breakdown. It makes no sound at all. Sometimes, at night, I go down to the room and put my hand on its casing. It's warm. I say thank you. It doesn't answer. It holds. That's its way of answering.
textes.Le Village des Arbres-Maisons\nLes habit:
The Treehouse Village
The villagers have gone to find their colours. Come on up and see!
textes.Le Village des Arbres-Maisons — des mais: The Treehouse Village — round houses perched in giant oaks, stairs winding around the trunks… but not a single villager
textes.Le Village des Fées ! Des maisons dans d: The Fairy Village! Houses in giant mushrooms, a cascade of light, and little wings glittering everywhere…
textes.Le Zéphyr arrive bientôt ! Ou il vient d: The Zéphyr is coming soon! Or it's just left. It's always somewhere.
textes.Le Zéphyr arrive plein, Pierrick ! Il y: The Zéphyr's coming in full, Pierrick! There's room for two!
textes.Le Zéphyr flotte grâce à un gaz plus lég: The Zéphyr floats thanks to a gas lighter than air that Héloïse makes in a vat. She won't tell me what from. It smells a bit like cabbage.
textes.Le Zéphyr relie Cliquetis à Tazira et à: The Zéphyr links Cliquetis to Tazira and Carène. It used to take three days on foot. Now it takes three minutes and a strong stomach.
textes.Le balancier bat les secondes. L'ancre,: The pendulum beats the seconds. The anchor, up top, lets one tooth of the little wheel through each time. Without it, everything would go at once: the town would live a whole day in a minute.
textes.Le bambou se remplit d'eau goutte à gout: The bamboo fills with water drop by drop, tips over… CLACK! Then all is calm again. Above the cherry trees, the towers shine, but here you can barely hear the city.
textes.Le bandeau doré entre les yeux ne trompe: The golden band between the eyes gives it away. Restores one and a half hearts.
textes.Le bar est à droite en entrant dans la H: The bar is on the right as you come into the Hall, under the mezzanine. The counter is made of ship's timber. If you put your ear to it, you can hear the sea. Or Mouette's bass. It's hard to tell the difference.
textes.Le bar, je l'ai monté avec des caisses d: I built the bar out of sardine crates and an old counter from the Cannery. My notebook, I've had for fifteen years. Every order from every concert. One day, it'll be a history book. With a lot of mint in it.
textes.Le bas ?! … (Il se gratte la moustache.): Down below?! … (He scratches his moustache.) My wife says the same thing. Hm. Perhaps you're right. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Le bassin des Jardins suspendus, au mati: The pool in the Hanging Gardens, in the morning: that's where I write. The water shines, the flowers blink, and the rhymes come… or not. Mostly not. But the water shines anyway.
textes.Le bateau ! On va sur le bateau ! J'ador: The boat! We're going on the boat! I love the boat! The waves! The wind! The seagulls! MINE, the seagulls!
textes.Le bateau de ligne arrive à l'heure, l'A: The ferry's arriving on time, the Albatross is leaving late, and Léon's boat still isn't a boat: it's a bathtub with oars.
textes.Le bateau de ligne double la Pointe. Son: The ferry is rounding the Point. Its captain is waving. Or shooing away a seagull.
textes.Le batteur de la Fronde m'a envoyé une p: The Fronde's drummer sent me a pair of drumsticks. With a note: “To help you keep time.” The cheek of it! … I put them on my bedside table. They're very nicely carved. That's different.
textes.Le batteur de remplacement a perdu une b: The stand-in drummer lost a stick during the second song. He's carrying on with one of Lentille's spoons. It sounds… original.
textes.Le battoir, c'est comme la vie : il faut: The washing paddle is like life: you have to hit the right spot.
textes.Le beau temps. Raisonnable. Vous parlez: Fine weather. Sensible. You sound like Héloïse. That's not a reproach… well, not entirely.
textes.Le beffroi. Quatre cloches de bronze pen: The belfry. Four bronze bells hang beneath the spire, each marked with a sign: the Wave, the Sun, the Moon, the Wind. They wait to be rung… in the right order.
textes.Le belvédère de la Haute-Ville est mon e: The lookout in the Upper Town is my favourite place. You can see everything: the lake to the east, the forest to the north-east, the Fangs to the south-west, the sea all around. And not a single frog.
textes.Le belvédère est mon endroit préféré. On: The lookout is my favourite place. You can see everything, and nothing sees you.
textes.Le bendir a une corde tendue sous la pea: The bendir has a string stretched under the skin. When you strike it, it buzzes. That's the drum's voice. Every drum has its own voice.
textes.Le berceau de Tornade avait une roue de: Tornade's cradle had a bike wheel, for rocking. At six months, he managed to roll it out of his room and all the way to the kitchen. Rustine and I found him in front of the fridge, delighted. We should have known that day what kind of child he'd be.
The bias is not the latest thing.
textes.Le blanc ! Tu as l'œil, alors. Dans le b: White! You have an eye, then. In white, you see everything: the quality of the thread, the care, the patience. Colours hide mistakes. White, never.
textes.Le blanc ? (Il regarde autour de lui, to: White? (He looks around him, at all the grey, all the white.) … You've got a sense of humour, you have. I like that.
textes.Le blanc ? … C'est drôle. Tu es le deuxi: White? … That's funny. You're the second one to tell me that. The first was Tiyi's linen. It didn't speak, but it said it very loudly.
textes.Le bleu ! Et il n'a même pas pris l'eau: The blue! And it didn't even get wet! (He turns the pot every which way and sniffs it.) It smells like the sky. Quick, go pour it into the Palette: paint cup number one, the very first. I want to see the pond turn blue from here. Here, for your trouble: two apples from my apple tree. They're still white, but they taste very good.
textes.Le bleu ! L'indigo de ma mère, l'eau du: Blue! My mother's indigo, the water of the Cenote. I had fingers that colour for ten years. It's a colour that sticks to your skin. To your heart too.
textes.Le bleu de l'Étang Gommé: The blue of the Rubbed-Out Pond
textes.Le bleu de l'île, c'est le pot numéro un: The island's blue is pot number one. The first well of the Palette. Without blue, there's no sky in the pond, no stream, no waterfall. Just lines.
textes.Le bleu de midi… Franc, honnête, sans un: Midday blue… Frank, honest, without a shadow. It's a brave colour. I never paint it: it's too sure of itself. But I admire it.
textes.Le bleu des cristaux ! Comme Ysaé. Comme: The blue of the crystals! Like Ysaé. Like the Chasm at night. It's the colour that glows in the dark. You'll shine on the Wall.
textes.Le bleu. Là-bas, tu vois ? Sur le grand: The blue. Over there, see? On the big water lily, in the middle. Pot number one, the island's blue. It floated out there the day after the Downpour, and it hasn't budged since. Me, I swim like a pebble. A painted pebble, but a pebble. Would you fetch it for me? With the blue, the pond will find its sky again, and the stream its water. And I'll get my trade back.
textes.Le bleu… La couleur de la première porte: Blue… The colour of the village's first door. You have good taste, my little one.
textes.Le bloc ne bouge plus : le mur, ou l'aut: The block won't budge: the wall, or the other block, is holding it.
textes.Le blé dur aime le soleil, le vent de la: Durum wheat loves the sun, the sea wind and a little ash from the volcano. Mount Bolognese is our fertiliser. It spits, it falls back down, things grow.
textes.Le blé entre en haut, la farine sort en: The wheat goes in at the top, the flour comes out at the bottom. And I turn white in the middle.
textes.Le blé est beau, le soleil est chaud, et: The wheat is fine, the sun is warm, and Lasagna saved me the last focaccia. Life is good.
textes.Le blé est bien haut cette année. Nonno: The wheat is really tall this year. Nonno says it's thanks to the volcano.
textes.Le blé tombe de la trémie entre les deux: The wheat drops from the hopper between the two millstones. The top one turns, the bottom one stays still: in between, the wheat turns into flour. Like magic, only heavier.
textes.Le bois de l'île est bon. Le chêne des h: The island's wood is good. Highland oak especially. But the northern shepherds sell it for its weight in gold.
textes.Le bois, c'est surtout utile pour se cha: Wood is mostly good for keeping warm.
textes.Le bol de soupe que je lui apporte tous: The bowl of soup I bring him every noon, I know what he does with it: he pours it into his geranium pot, behind the door. The geranium is now as tall as me, with flowers as big as cabbages. Doc says it's the sun. I say it's my soup. At least it does somebody good.
textes.Le bol fumant du robot des nouilles du M: The steaming bowl from the noodle robot at the Night Market: noodles, a golden broth, an egg, vegetables, and a smiley face drawn in sauce. Restores two and a half hearts.
textes.Le bouillon de La Marmite : des champign: La Marmite's broth: brown mushrooms from Bertille's Gardens (never the glowing ones), vegetables from up top and water from the waterfall. It keeps you warm all the way to the bottom of the mine. Restores two hearts.
textes.Le bouillon mijote depuis ce matin, les: The broth's been simmering since this morning, the noodles are fresh, Gaston is well oiled. What more could you want?
textes.Le bout seulement. Le reste fond très bi: Just the toe. The rest melts very nicely.
textes.Le bouton s'allume en bleu. La cabine, j: The button lights up blue. The lift, right in front of you, seems to say: “I'm right here, you know!”
textes.Le bouton s'allume en bleu. Quatorze, tr: The button lights up blue. Fourteen, thirteen, twelve… The lift is on its way, in no hurry at all.
textes.Le bras du robot plonge dans la marmite,: The robot's arm dives into the pot, stirs, drains, pours… “A NEO-RAMEN! CAREFUL, IT'S HOT!” It even takes a little bow.
textes.Le brasero de l'est flambe : le soleil s: The east brazier blazes: the sun rises.
textes.Le brasero de l'ouest flambe : le soleil: The west brazier blazes: the sun sets.
textes.Le brasero du nord s'allume : le soleil: The north brazier lights: the sun sleeps. All four flames roar together… and the great slab at the back slides upward.
textes.Le brasero du sud flambe : le soleil brû: The south brazier blazes: the sun burns at noon.
textes.Le brevet de la roue est arrivé un lundi: The wheel patent arrived on a Monday, with a superb diagram: the wheel from the front, from the side, and in cross-section. He had even calculated that it rolled better round than square. I had to write “already invented” at the bottom. It took me an hour. Then I added: “At least you're inventing things in the right order.” He framed the letter.
I'd taken great care over the wheel patent. Three drawings: front, side, cross-section. And a calculation proving it rolled better round than square. Héloïse sent it back with “already invented” written at the bottom, very small. And underneath: “At least you're inventing things in the right order.” I framed the letter. It's in my hallway.
textes.Le brigadier ? Il a enquêté sur mes croi: The sergeant? He investigated my croissants like a crime against the state. And he comes to eat one every morning, “for inspection”. Annoying. But he says thank you.
textes.Le brigadier ? Le patient le plus fidèle: The sergeant? The most loyal and most discreet patient on the island. He patrols with his back in pieces and his cap perfectly straight. I admire him, and I scold him.
textes.Le brigadier Lefort est un homme d'ordre: Sergeant Lefort is a man of order and a very bad runner. I'm very fond of him. He'd happily give me a ticket.
textes.Le brigadier Lefort fait des rondes, mai: Sergeant Lefort does his rounds, but he always stops in front of the ice-cream shop. Always.
textes.Le brigadier Lefort vient me voir pour s: Constable Lefort comes to see me about his bad back. He doesn't want anyone to know, he still goes on patrol.
textes.Le brigadier Lefort, c'est un brave homm: Sergeant Lefort is a good man, stiff as a fish board. He does his rounds very seriously. And he always stops at the ice-cream stand. Always.
textes.Le brigadier achète quand même ses sardi: The sergeant still buys his sardines from me, every Tuesday. He asks for “six sardines, no comment”. I always put the nicest one on top, laughing. He pretends not to see it. But he tips his cap to me as he leaves. That's his way of saying thank you.
textes.Le brigadier, c'est mon voisin de la rue: The sergeant is my neighbour on Lighthouse Street. An upright man, stiff as a parasol pole. He says he'd have liked to be a lifeguard. I believe him.
textes.Le brigadier, c'est mon voisin et mon me: The sergeant is my neighbour and my best customer. Three ice creams a day, state secret. An upright man, with a soft spot for vanilla.
textes.Le bulletin de midi, pour l'affichage !: The noon report, for the noticeboard! Excuse me!
textes.Le bâton des sorciers d'Arcanelle, remis: The staff of the wizards of Arcanelle, presented at the Circle of Moonstones: wood from the Twisted Wood and a purple crystal. In hand, each spell costs one less point of magic. Damage: 6.
textes.Le bénitier géant s'entrouvre lentement…: The giant clam slowly opens a crack… In the hollow of its blue mantle shines the Pearl of the Garden, the age of life.
textes.Le cacao, c'est la boisson des dieux !: Cacao is the drink of the gods!
textes.Le cadeau de Lyra : son aiguille de cris: Lyra's gift: its crystal needle points towards the Mother Tree, to the east. With it, the boat can cross the mist of Bois-Doré.
textes.Le café du Café de la Bielle, passé sous: Coffee from the Crankshaft Café, pressure-brewed in a copper boiler. It would wake the dead, and it restores one heart.
textes.Le cahier des airs du vent, d'une écritu: The notebook of wind tunes, in fine, slanting handwriting: “Monday, west wind: the Waltz. Tuesday, north wind: the Waltz, but shivering. Wednesday, no wind: we played it ourselves. It wasn't as good.”
The canal moved. I maintain it.
textes.Le capitaine Croc-de-Sel m'a commandé un: Captain Croc-de-Sel ordered a carpet from me and forbade me to ask questions. So I don't ask any. I weave, I look, and I think. That, he didn't forbid.
textes.Le capitaine a passé deux heures à guett: The captain spent two hours lying in wait for the ginger cat behind a barrel. The cat was asleep on the barrel.
textes.Le capitaine a perdu sa carte. Sans cart: The captain lost his map. No map, no treasure. No treasure, no pay. No pay… hm. He'd better find it.
The captain had a map, the real one. The drawing he gave me is a copy from memory. The original, he lost it. Or someone stole it from him…
textes.Le capitaine cherche le trésor de son gr: The captain is looking for his grandfather's treasure. A map, some caves, a cross. The usual. But the cat took the map, so now we're looking for the cat.
textes.Le capitaine de la Murène Noire cherche: The captain of the Murène Noire is looking for something. He spends his days asking the old folk about the caves along the coast.
textes.Le capitaine de la Murène Noire. Il me s: The captain of the Murène Noire. He greets me every morning with his hat, down to the ground. A pirate who's too polite is up to something. That one is up to a lot.
textes.Le capitaine des pirates a un chat ennem: The pirate captain has a sworn enemy that's a cat. A cat! He threatened it with his sabre in front of the whole quay. The cat won.
textes.Le capitaine est toujours à l'heure. Enf: The captain is always on time. Well, almost.
textes.Le capitaine ne dort plus depuis qu'il a: The captain hasn't slept since he lost his map. He paces up and down the deck. It makes the planks creak, and the first mate grinds his teeth.
textes.Le capitaine pirate a crié « REVIENS ICI: The pirate captain shouted “COME BACK HERE, YOU FILTHY BEAST!” on the quay, and ran after the ginger cat. The cat jumped onto a crate, then onto a roof. The captain didn't.
textes.Le capitaine pirate lui a commandé un ta: The pirate captain ordered a strange carpet from her, and now she weaves every evening. My evenings! I walk behind her loom, I cough, I sigh, I talk about the rain. Nothing. She counts her threads out loud. I'm jealous of a carpet, my brother. Me, a carpet seller. If my grandmother could see this.
textes.Le capitaine pirate m'a acheté du poivre: The pirate captain bought pepper from me. Lots of pepper. He says it's for an enemy. The cat, surely.
textes.Le capitaine pirate m'a commandé un tapi: The pirate captain ordered a carpet from me. He gave me a drawing: a coastline, caves, a cross. I told him it looked like a treasure map. He told me to be quiet and weave.
textes.Le capitaine, il crie fort, il a une den: The captain shouts loud, he's got a silver tooth and he's scared of rooftops. But he lets me look through his spyglass. A captain who lends his spyglass isn't a bad guy.
textes.Le capitaine, il grogne, il grogne, mais: The captain, he grumbles and grumbles, but he's never thrown me overboard. Not even the time I slept in a cask. He's the best captain in the world. Hic! The grumpiest, too.
textes.Le capitaine. Il a perdu la carte. À cau: The captain. He lost the map. Because of a cat. Hm. He has until the end of summer. Then the crew votes.
textes.Le caravanier. Le menteur bleu. Il m'a e: The caravan trader. The blue liar. He sent me into the wrong desert. Two days. I don't talk to him any more. I watch him.
textes.Le carnet sept dit : « Pied du Cœur-de-P: Notebook seven says: “Foot of Stoneheart. Fog. Saw nothing.” That's not true, {surnom}. It was clear. I saw the gate, from afar, at sunset. And I heard the mountain breathing, slowly, deeply. I ran for two days without stopping, all the way to Carène. I've never been back. Everyone thinks I just never had the time.
textes.Le carrefour. Quatre chemins partent ver: The crossroads. Four paths lead south: a red one, a black one, a white one, a yellow one. Which one leads to the Lords?
textes.Le casque bleu te va très bien. Une élèv: The blue helmet really suits you. A gliding student gives you a military salute. You salute back. The helmet slips down over your nose.
The headphones are waiting for you.
textes.Le caïd Hamza est beau quand il regarde: The caïd Hamza is handsome when he looks at the sea, and unbearable when he opens his mouth. Luckily, he doesn't open it often.
textes.Le caïd Hamza ne sourit pas. Il garde se: Caïd Hamza doesn't smile. He guards his cannons like a mother guards her little ones. Me, I polish them. We get along without saying so.
textes.Le caïd Hamza. Il me surveille du haut d: The caïd Hamza. He watches me from the top of his tower as if I were going to steal his cannons. I don't steal cannons: they're too heavy. I greet him every morning. It annoys him. That's the point.
textes.Le caïd a sept canons qui n'ont jamais t: The caïd has seven cannons that have never fired. I've got sixteen that are just itching to. He finds me cheeky. He's right. But he keeps a good watch, I'll give him that.
The caïd is as grumpy as a crab. He chases us off his cannons, even though they're the best horses in Tazira. But he gave me the secret password. So he's not completely mean.
textes.Le caïd. Je l'ai connu petit voleur de v: The caid. I knew him as a little thief of fishing worms. Now he guards the town. Guards it too much, in fact. He doesn't sleep any more.
textes.Le centième balayeur. Toute la cité sur: The hundredth sweeper. The whole city on the Grand Square. It started to sing. My song. The shepherds' one. Out of tune, like me. People laughed. Héloïse was in the front row, monocle in her eye. I left. There was nothing left for me there.
textes.Le cercle de champignons, au bord de la: The mushroom ring at the edge of the clearing will take you back to your beach whenever you wish.
textes.Le cercle de lumière te dépose dans la c: The circle of light sets you down in the fairy glade. Queen Oriane is waiting for you: the seed of Yggdrasil glows at the bottom of your bag.
textes.Le cercle des tambours, au milieu du cam: The drum circle, in the middle of the camp, is the heart of the village. If you hit a djembe, someone will answer. Always. That's the rule.
textes.Le cerf-volant de Théo s'est envolé vers: Théo's kite has flown off towards the western hills.
textes.Le chadouf, tu vois ? Un poteau, une per: The shadoof, see? A post, a pole, a bucket, a counterweight of earth. You lift water from the river without breaking your back. Well, less.
textes.Le chameau dit au dromadaire : « Tu n'as: The camel says to the dromedary: “You've only got one hump?” The dromedary replies: “And you've got two? Show-off.” … It's a caravan joke, it gets laughs in the desert.
textes.Le chant du berger, peint à la chaux sur: The shepherd's song, whitewashed on a board: “Three sheep on the ridge, in the morning sun; one in the valley, sulking in the thyme; two in the sheepfold, asleep by the fire. Count them in order, and the wind will open for you.”
textes.Le chantier naval de Port-Azur : ça sent: The Port-Azur shipyard: it smells of sawdust and tar. On the slipway, a schooner is taking shape, rib after rib…
textes.Le chanvre, c'est une plante magnifique: Hemp is a wonderful plant: you can make very strong ropes from it, cloth that lasts a hundred years, paper… And the birds adore its seeds. Nothing goes to waste.
textes.Le chanvre, ici, sert à faire des cordes: Hemp, here, is used to make ropes, canvas and bags. Galet makes ropes from it at the Ropeworks, Lune weaves the yurt canvases. Nothing goes to waste.
textes.Le chapeau en forme de navet, je l'ai fa: The turnip-shaped hat, I made it reluctantly. He led the turnips in single file all the way to the farm. The whole town came to watch. The Baron walked in front, very dignified, and twenty turnips followed him, hopping. I've never been so proud and so embarrassed in my life. Bertrand made a song of it. I don't go out on festival day anymore.
textes.Le chapeau que je porte, c'était celui d: The hat I'm wearing was the Admiral's when she was little. She gave it to me after the night of the lantern, without a word, left on my scrubbing bucket. It's too big, I stuff paper in it. Nolwenn says it'll fit me in two years. I can't wait.
textes.Le chat ! (Elle serre les mains sur son: Cats! (She clasps her hands over her heart.) Have you ever stroked one? Was it purring? Tell me everything, everything, everything!
textes.Le chat a quatre genoux, Yaya, c'est de: The cat has four knees, Yaya, that's cheating!
textes.Le chat d'en face me regarde de haut. Il: The cat across the street looks down on me. He's on top of a wall. That's cheating.
textes.Le chat de Trocante m'a relâché parce qu: Trocante's cat let me go because I showed my resident's card. He's a cat of principle.
The cat is looking at me. I'm looking away. It started it.
textes.Le chat ouvre un œil, te juge, et se ren: The cat opens one eye, judges you, and goes back to sleep. You're accepted.
textes.Le chat ouvre un œil. Il est habitué aux: The cat opens one eye. It's used to the cuckoo clocks: it only wakes up for the noon one. The lunchtime one.
textes.Le chat ronronne. Puis il te mord gentim: The cat purrs. Then it bites you gently, just for show. Then it purrs again.
textes.Le chat roux, je sais où il dort. Sur un: The ginger cat, I know where he sleeps. On a roof, near the Fondouk. He climbs up on some crates. But shh.
textes.Le chef gobelin ! Sa bannière ! Rapporte: The goblin chief! His banner! Bring it back, or help me take it, and I'm yours forever!
textes.Le chef gobelin agite sa bannière en hur: The goblin chief waves his banner, yelling: “To me, gang!” Two goblins burst out of the bushes!
textes.Le chef gobelin baisse sa hampe… et char: The goblin chief lowers his pole… and charges, bellowing!
textes.Le chef-d'œuvre d'Octave : acier trempé,: Octave's masterpiece: tempered steel, brass guard. Damage: 6, and the third hit of a combo strikes half again as hard. Ready for the battles to come.
textes.Le chemin ? À Montjoie, avec les lacets,: Your way? In Montjoie, with all the zigzags, that's not a flaw: it's the rule. Even I got lost once. In the hat cellar.
textes.Le chemin de Xibalba… on peut y descendr: The road to Xibalba… can we go down there?
textes.Le chemin entre les deux… (Il regarde lo: The way in between… (He gazes towards the Station for a long while.) Yes. That's where I spend most of my time, deep down. In the capsule, halfway. Hm. Sit down.
textes.Le chemin tourne, tourne… et te ramène a: The path turns, and turns… and brings you back to the crossroads. Somewhere, dry laughter echoes. That wasn't the right path.
textes.Le chenil est chez les Artisans, à l'oue: The kennel is in the Artisans' Quarter, west of the Lower Town. I used to be next to the Ash Gardens, but my puppies dug up Mother Brasille's flowerbeds. She… kindly… asked me to move. With a broom.
textes.Le chien ! Celui qui remue la queue quan: Dogs! The ones that wag their tails when they're happy! Murmure read me that they love people forever. Forever! Is it true?
textes.Le chien ? Il est gentil. Bête, mais gen: The dog? He's nice. Dim, but nice. He wags his tail at everything. I only swish mine when I'm thinking.
textes.Le chien Sardine nous court après. On le: Sardine the dog chases us. We let him think he'll catch us. It's kindness. And exercise. The exercise is MINE!
textes.Le chien court après les monstres. La ch: The dog chases monsters. The cat looks for treasures. The rat brings back coins. Me, I look for truffles. But I share them. Nearly all of them.
textes.Le chocolat chaud du Café Feedback, avec: Hot chocolate from the Feedback Café, with a cloud of cream. It warms your hands, your tummy and your heart. Restores one and a half hearts.
textes.Le chocolat d'Honorine, à La Marmite : c: Honorine's hot chocolate, at La Marmite: cocoa, milk, honey and a pinch of salt, stirred until the spoon stands up on its own. Firmin, up top, says it's a soup. Restores two hearts.
textes.Le chocolat d'altitude, il est meilleur,: Altitude hot chocolate tastes better, doesn't it?
textes.Le chocolat d'ici chuchote. Celui d'en b: The hot chocolate up here whispers. The one down below whistles, apparently. Each has its own personality.
textes.Le chocolat de Firmin a sifflé : il est: Firmin's hot chocolate just whistled: it's four o'clock. No need for a watch around here.
textes.Le chocolat de La Conque : noir comme le: La Conque's hot chocolate: dark as the bottom of the Trench, with a pinch of sea salt and white foam on top, like a little wave. Firmin, Gustave and Honorine tasted it; all three said “not bad” at the same time. Restores two hearts.
textes.Le chocolat du mineur ! La cuillère debo: The miner's hot chocolate! Spoon standing up! You'll love it. Firmin, up top, calls it a soup. Firmin is wrong. It's a hug.
textes.Le chocolat du mineur, je l'ai inventé p: I invented the miner's hot chocolate for Ludovic, one morning when he'd come up from the mine all grey. I put in cocoa, milk, honey, a pinch of salt, and I stirred until the spoon stood up on its own. He drank it without a word. Then he said: “More.” It's the longest word Ludovic has ever said to me.
textes.Le château a une cour, un jardin, un sal: The castle has a courtyard, a garden, a drawing room, a throne room and a rampart. And forty-two hat cupboards. I have the inventory. It runs to eighty pages.
textes.Le château d'eau, Pigment l'a peint pend: The water tower? Pigment painted it while I held her on a rope. Three weeks up there. We ate Lentille's soups twenty-eight metres up. We could see the sea on every side.
textes.Le château d'eau, à l'est, je l'ai peint: The water tower, to the east: I painted the whole thing, on a rope, with Bardane holding me. Three weeks. The guitar rat at the top, the seagulls in the middle, and at the bottom, the names of all the inhabitants. There's room for yours.
textes.Le château du Baron couronne la Butte, t: The Baron's castle crowns the Mound, at the very top. In the morning I train in its courtyard. The Baron applauds from his window, in a different hat every day. Yesterday it was a fish-shaped hat.
textes.Le château, là-haut ! Je m'y entraîne ch: The castle, up there! I train there every morning. The Baron applauds me from his window. In a different hat.
textes.Le chêne ! Celui qui tient bon. Il vit m: The oak! The one that holds firm. It lives a thousand years and shelters hundreds of animals. A real punk, the oak.
textes.Le chêne a commencé une phrase cette nui: The oak started a sentence last night. He is on the first word.
textes.Le cidre doux du verger de Père Gaubert,: Père Gaubert's sweet sparkling apple drink from his orchard, alcohol-free and fizzy, served nice and cold at "La Grenouille Repue". The bubbles tickle your nose. Restores one heart.
textes.Le ciel aussi, quand il pleut !: So is the sky, when it rains!
textes.Le ciel autour d'Astralys, c'est le meil: The sky around Astralys is the best racetrack in the world: you go under the island, between the islets, through the falls of light… If you have a machine that flies, I'll take you there. You'll scream. With joy. Probably.
The sky is full of surprises.
textes.Le ciel s'allume : des rideaux de lumièr: The sky lights up: curtains of green, pink and blue light ripple above Astralys. The Night of the Auroras begins!
textes.Le ciel s'assombrit d'un coup. Un éclair: The sky suddenly darkens. A bolt of lightning strikes the centre of the platform… An immense suit of armour steps out of it: LORD STORM, THE KNIGHT OF STORMS!
textes.Le ciel se met à scintiller de traits de: The sky starts to sparkle with streaks of light: it's a meteor shower! Make a wish. Or ten.
textes.Le ciel vire au violet profond. Quelqu'u: The sky turns deep purple. Someone on a bench claps very softly.
textes.Le cinquième soleil brille au-dessus du: The fifth sun shines above the fire… but it doesn't move. The gods had the same trouble: a motionless sun burns everything. It would need a great breath, that of Ehécatl, the wind.
textes.Le cinquième étage de l'Usine Grise: The fifth floor of the Grey Factory
textes.Le cinquième étage des Mille Marches: The fifth floor of the Thousand Steps
textes.Le clou de travers, celui que j'ai plant: The crooked nail, the one I drove in at eight, is still there, on the Mabrouka's side. Every winter, when Driss brings her to me, he points to it with his fingertip, without a word. Once, I wanted to replace it. He put his hand over it. “No.” It's the best-guarded nail in Tazira.
textes.Le cochon trouve des truffes. Moi, je tr: The pig finds truffles. I find coins. We make a team! A team that smells good!
textes.Le cochonnet ? Moi je l'ai vu filer sous: The jack? I saw it shoot under a bench, near the fountain. But I'm too old to get down on all fours.
textes.Le cochonnet a roulé vers la fontaine, ç: The jack rolled towards the fountain, that I'm sure of. After that… a mystery.
textes.Le cochonnet, c'est Marcel qui l'a lancé: The jack — Marcel threw it too hard. It rolled towards the fountain, and after that, a mystery. We played with a pebble, a disgrace. Then we sulked, each at one end of the pitch. Three days. The three longest days of my life. His too: he came and sulked right next to me.
textes.Le cockpit est occupé : un petit pilote: The cockpit is taken: a little pilot is sleeping in it, head to one side, hands on the stick, still going “vrrr” in dreamland.
textes.Le code, c'est un peu moi qui l'ai comme: The code was sort of my idea. One day I heard tapping above me, through the rock: two knocks, then one. Not like Mathilde: smaller, quicker. I answered. That was two years ago. It's Pimprenelle. I'm teaching her the code. She learns super fast. Too fast, even.
textes.Le codex des soleils, sur une peau de ce: The codex of the suns, painted on deerskin: in the middle, our sun, the fifth. Around it, the four suns before, each with its number in red dots, and arrows turning: 1, 2, 3, 4… then 5, at the centre.
textes.Le coffre bâille. Très grand. Avec une l: The chest yawns. Very wide. With a tongue. It wasn't a chest!
textes.Le coffre de la Mouette ! Tu l'as trouvé: The Seagull's chest! You found it right where I said? MY MAP WAS RIGHT! Gaston, write down the date!
textes.Le coffre de la chandelle s'ouvre… sur u: The candle's chest opens… to an old boot, and a note: “Missed! But at least this one doesn't bite.”
textes.Le coffre des livres est honnête, et pau: The books' chest is honest, and poor: a few coins, a vial of sap, and a bookmark.
textes.Le coffre du capitaine grince… Entre les: The captain's chest creaks… Among the moldy coins gleams the Pearl of the Wreck, the age of men.
textes.Le coffre du hibou ne mord pas : il grin: The owl's chest doesn't bite: it only creaks. Inside, on a velvet cushion, a silver key engraved with little owls.
textes.Le coffret qui est monté du sol contient: The casket that rose from the floor holds a piece of Osiris!
textes.Le compost, c'est la plus belle chose du: Compost is the most beautiful thing in the world. You put peelings in, and a year later it's soil. Nothing is lost. It's the same as Trocante's Free Shop, only slower.
textes.Le comptoir, puis le tableau. HA HA ! Et: The counter, then the board. HA HA! And don't burn your apron!
textes.Le concert ! Ce soir ! Je vais hurler pe: The concert! Tonight! I'm going to howl during Clou's solo! I'm the backing singer!
textes.Le concert en direct ! Je commente le po: The live gig! I commentate the mosh pit like a match! Next time, I'll say your name when you jump. Jump high.
textes.Le concours des deux fours. Même pâte, d: The contest of the two ovens. Same dough, two ovens, the old scribe as judge, blindfolded. He chewed for a long time, then he said: “They're the same.” Of course: I built both ovens. Mérit cried victory. I cried victory. Nobody lost. It's the worst contest I've ever won.
textes.Le contremaître Ludovic m'a accroché un: Foreman Ludovic hung a helmet on the Workshop door so I wouldn't forget it any more. I keep my pencils in it. It's the safest pencil pot in the Strata. Ludovic doesn't find it funny. But I saw him smile under his moustache. Well, under his beard.
textes.Le contremaître Ludovic m'a fait vérifie: Foreman Ludovic made me check my helmet three times this morning. It was properly fastened. It's even more fastened now.
textes.Le contremaître Ludovic m'apporte chaque: Foreman Ludovic brings me his board every month: “Days without an accident”. Four thousand two hundred. I congratulate him. He replies: “It's not me, it's the Old Lady.” The rock. He's right. But it's a little bit him too.
textes.Le contremaître Ludovic parle à la roche: Foreman Ludovic talks to the rock. He says hello, thank you, sorry. I laughed, the first time. Then I thought: the rock's been there for millions of years, it deserves a hello. So now I say hello to it too.
textes.Le contremaître des Mines des Strates, L: The foreman of the Strata Mines, Ludovic, came down to lay his hand on the rock of the Trench, “to say hello from the Old Lady”. He kept his helmet on under the Dome. I pointed out that the ceiling was glass, forty-six metres up. He replied: “Exactly.” I found that very professional.
textes.Le copal crépite sur les braises, et une: The copal crackles on the embers, and a white, fragrant smoke rises toward the sun. Huitzilopochtli is pleased.
textes.Le copal, c'est la résine d'un arbre. On: Copal is a tree resin. We burn it for the gods: the smoke rises up to them. Huitzilopochtli adores it. So do I: I sell it.
textes.Le corail ! Le miel ! La noix de coco !: The coral! The honey! The coconut! I'll grind, mix, and… look at that red! Here, it's all I have, but I'm also giving you my eternal admiration.
textes.Le corail rouge pousse lentement : un do: Red coral grows slowly: a finger's width per century. My sculptures are all over a thousand years old. So am I, almost.
textes.Le couac, on le garde. C'est ta signatur: We'll keep the squawk. It's your signature.
textes.Le couloir des lames : quatre grandes la: The corridor of blades: four great blades swinging from wall to wall, some flagstones darker than the others… and sand at the end. Watch closely, and go at the right moment.
textes.Le coup de feu, c'est maintenant ! Tout: Rush hour is now! All of Neopolis gets hungry at midnight.
textes.Le couvercle du grand plat, c'est moi qu: The lid of the big dish was my idea: an engraved fish, with a nice round eye. For her grandmother Zahra, who judged everything by the eye. Zohra looked at the fish for a long time. She said nothing. Then she said: “It has a fresh eye.” That's the highest compliment she knows how to give.
textes.Le crabe amoureux. Je l'ai inventé ce ma: The Crab in Love. I invented it this morning.
textes.Le crabe sentimental, Titou. Rien à voir: The sentimental crab, Titou. Totally different, it has more heart.
textes.Le cristal a brillé. Je l'ai vu d'ici. I: The crystal shone. I saw it from here. It doesn't shine for everyone. Here. Some coins. And when you feel hot, in summer, think of the lake. It will think of you.
textes.Le cristal bleu s'illumine, et le hall s: The blue crystal lights up, and the hall dissolves with a chime… You're back in the sun, in front of the ruined tower. (Odon, without looking up: “Floor 1. Noted.”)
textes.Le cristal est glacé. Il ne se passe rie: The crystal is icy. Nothing happens… for now.
textes.Le cristal pâlit, et les coraux pâlissen: The crystal is fading, and the corals are fading with it. In the evening, I sit among the basins and sing them the only song I know, my father's. I sing off-key. Ondine heard me, I think. She didn't say anything. If the corals go out, {surnom}, I won't know who to talk to any more.
textes.Le crochet, je l'ai forgé dans le fer d': The hook, I forged it from the iron of an old anchor found on the shore. One whole night. He wanted to pay me. I bent an iron bar in front of him. He understood. On Fridays, I polish it. He doesn't ask for anything. He holds out his arm, I polish, he leaves. That's our Friday.
The croissant at the bottom, Honorine. Thank you.
textes.Le crâne fendu, au-dessus de la porte ?: The split skull above the door? It's a real one. From a customer who wouldn't pay. No, just kidding. It's plaster. Well… I think.
textes.Le cuisinier des pirates achète tout le: The pirates' cook buys all the fish nobody wants. I wonder what he does with it. I'd rather not know.
textes.Le cuisinier des pirates danse comme une: The pirates' cook dances like a whale. I wrote a tune just for him. Nobody dances worse. Nobody dances happier.
textes.Le cuisinier des pirates danse à la fête: The pirates' cook dances at the party every night. He dances terribly. We love him.
textes.Le cuisinier des pirates m'a demandé ma: The pirates' cook asked me for my recipe. I gave it to him. A fake one. He still cooks just as badly.
textes.Le cuisinier des pirates. Il a goûté mon: The pirates' cook. He tasted my tea in front of the whole terrace and said: “Not salty enough.” Salty! My tea! I'll forgive him. It's my duty. Not yet.
textes.Le cuivre vient des hautes terres du nor: Copper comes from the northern highlands, by way of Carène. The shepherds sell it dear. Everything from the north is dear, except snow.
textes.Le cumin tout seul, ça ne se grille pas: You can't grill cumin on its own!
The cumin, yes. The smile, we'll see.
textes.Le cylindre, là, avec ses picots : chaqu: That cylinder there, with its pins: each pin is a note. I put in twelve thousand by hand. I can't feel my thumbs any more.
textes.Le cœur ? … Hm. Ça, c'est le seul feu qu: Your heart? … Hm. That's the only fire I don't know how to put out. Go and see Mother Sage. Or Berthe: she has pie. Pie works too.
textes.Le cœur de bois est tiède. La lumière l': The wooden heart is warm. The light reaches it, but too weakly: it must first pass through the three mirror-flowers.
textes.Le cœur de cristal garde l'énergie du so: The crystal heart stores the sun's energy; the ring spins it and pushes it downwards, a long way down, all the way to the sea. The island rests on it, like a hand on a table. Séraphin worked it all out a hundred and twenty years ago. We just keep an eye on it.
textes.Le cœur de l'île, la grande montagne… Ma: The heart of the island, the great mountain… My grandmother used to say the desert keeps one of its keys. A seal, under a dune that walks. I know no more than that.
textes.Le cœur du Roi Gélatineux : une grosse g: The heart of the Jelly King: a big green jelly that glows softly, with a tiny gold crown stuck on top. It still beats a little, like a happy pudding. Master Hugues has dreamed of it for twenty years.
textes.Le cœur lourd et les cordes légères. Ily: Heavy heart, light strings. Ilyria smiled at me this morning. Or perhaps she was smiling at the light.
textes.Le cœur… Ah. Ça ne se recoud pas avec du: The heart… Ah. That doesn't get stitched with thread. It gets stitched with time, friends, and a bit of honey in your tea. Sit down.
textes.Le dauphin, j'y étais. Momo dansait dans: The dolphin, I was there. Momo was dancing waist-deep in the water, arms in the air, and a dolphin swam by ten metres away. It jumped once and left. Momo turned round shouting: “Did you see? It's dancing with me!” I gave him two thumbs up. The dolphin made no comment.
The last chord tore the hem.
The last one had a rubber ring too.
textes.Le dernier bouquet retombe en pluie d'or: The last bouquet falls back in a golden rain. The whole meadow applauds. Clapotis shouts: “I SAW SOME! REAL ONES!” And Bouton-d'Or places a crown of daisies on his head.
textes.Le dernier coup d'un enchaînement frappe: The last blow of a combo hits twice as hard, and every blow has a one-in-eight chance to be critical.
textes.Le dernier couplet ! Il n'existe pas enc: The last verse! It doesn't exist yet: first you need a King. The Brawl King is the one who puts the three champions of the harbor on the mat. Gros-Louis, of the Requin Borgne. Le Muet, of the Veuve Écarlate. Belle-Humeur, of the Morue Enragée. With fists, no blades: otherwise it doesn't count. A fair duel, or a good brawl, as you like. And after that… I sing!
textes.Le dernier cristal s'illumine ! Très loi: The last crystal lights up! Far away, in the Rose of Seals, a long rumble… The circle of light beside the dais will take you there.
textes.Le dernier jaguar tombe. Dans le silence: The last jaguar falls. In the silence, the jaguar head on the altar opens its mouth: a small casket has appeared in it.
textes.Le dernier ruban de lumière s'en va vers: The last ribbon of light drifts away to the north. Vibrato plays one last, very long note. Good night, Astralys.
textes.Le dernier. Le héros ne fait pas trois m: The last one. The hero isn't ten feet tall.
textes.Le deux et le quatre ! Le contretemps !: Two and four! The offbeat! Now there's a real Frondeur. Come to the pit tonight, you'll make people jealous.
textes.Le deuxième jour sans appareil, une vagu: On the second day without a camera, a wave filled his moat and he fell into it bottom first. He laughed. Head thrown back, sand right into his ears. I reached for my camera, out of habit. It wasn't there. So I laughed too. We laughed like two seals. Nobody took our picture.
textes.Le deuxième jour, Achille a crié qu'il v: On the second day, Achille shouted that he wanted to land on the Zéphyr. Zélie grabbed the megaphone and yelled at the sky: “Denied! You'll burst my envelope!” The whole city heard her. Achille did an offended figure of eight. That evening, Zélie came and sat on my bench with two coffees, and said nothing. That was her way of apologising.
textes.Le deuxième jour, Kiki a accroché une pa: On the second day, Kiki hung a sign on the beach hut: “Wedding ring lost. Reward: one punch.” All afternoon, tourists searched the sand in front of the bar. They found a bottle cap, a sandal and a very offended crab. Kiki gave them the punch anyway. He said it was for the effort.
textes.Le deuxième jour, il me racontait une hi: On the second day, he was telling me a story about a giant octopus, standing at the bow, arms spread wide: “And then it opened its tentacles, like this!” Splash. The sea was flat as a millpond, not a ripple. I fished him out with the boathook, by his belt, like a sack of potatoes. He finished his story dripping wet.
textes.Le deuxième lait de nuage est toujours m: The second cloud milk is always better than the first. The third, I couldn't say, I've never dared.
textes.Le deuxième soir où elle pleurait sur le: The second evening she was crying on the balcony of room seven, I had a tray sent up: tea, two biscuits, and a card with the hotel letterhead. On it I wrote, in my finest hand: “The management sympathises.” Nothing more. The management, in this case, was me. But the phrase carries more authority.
textes.Le deuxième soir, on a frappé à la porte: On the second evening, there was a knock at the door of room seven. A tray, a teapot, two cups (two!) and a little handwritten card, in very upright writing: “The management sympathises.” No signature. I didn't drink the second cup. But I left it on the table, just in case.
textes.Le deuxième verre est fort comme l'amour: The second glass is strong as love… Here.
textes.Le diamant se pose, ça crépite… « Flaque: The needle drops, it crackles… “Puddles in Minor,” by the Gutters. A guitar creaking softly, a voice whispering. Outside, the rain keeps the beat.
textes.Le dimanche matin, Mistral a passé un mo: On the Sunday morning, Mistral played a really soft track, and everyone turned towards the sea. The sun came up out of the water, pink, enormous. I cried without knowing why. My boat home went by at eight, right in front of me. I waved at it. So good. That was three weeks ago.
textes.Le dimanche soir, je monte la soupe au p: On Sunday evenings, I carry the soup up to the lighthouse in a pot wrapped in three tea towels. Three hundred and twenty steps. If I dawdle, it arrives lukewarm, and Anselme eats it lukewarm without a word. If I hurry, it arrives hot, and he eats it hot without a word. I hurry anyway.
textes.Le dimanche, Boulon vient soulever les v: On Sundays, Boulon comes to lift the old cars so I can look for parts underneath. Once, under a blue van, we found a family of hedgehogs. Boulon put the van back down in exactly the same spot, to the millimetre. I welded a little roof over them. The hedgehogs still live there.
textes.Le dimanche, au thé, Églantine classe me: On Sundays, over tea, Églantine sorts my buttons by colour while we talk. She doesn't notice. Her hands work on their own. When she's gone, I mix them up again so she can start over the next week. It relaxes her. Me too. It's our little tradition, even if she doesn't know it.
textes.Le dimanche, elle frappe trois coups, el: On Sundays, she knocks three times, comes up, sets down the soup. We eat without talking, facing the sea. When I leave some bread, she says: “Anselme Vasseur, finish your plate.” Like to a little boy. I'm past sixty. I finish my plate.
textes.Le dimanche, je joue aux cartes avec Léo: On Sundays, I play cards with Léon on the harbour bench. I talk to my cards, like I do to my trees. “Come on, my little queen of hearts, grow.” I almost always win. Léon says I cheat. I don't cheat. I encourage. It's not the same.
textes.Le dimanche, je lui montre mon nœud de c: On Sundays, I show her my bowline with my eyes closed. Last time, I tied my ankle to the mainmast! Everyone laughed. The captain, she crouched down, looked at the knot, and said: “Almost.” Gros-Louis took ages to undo it. It was a good knot, actually. Just not in the right place.
textes.Le dinandier. Il tape le cuivre. Bien. T: The coppersmith. He beats copper. Well. Too soft, but well. I watch him every day. It smells of the forge.
textes.Le dire au capitaine Charbonnel (à la ca: Tell Captain Charbonnel (at the port's harbour master's office)
textes.Le dire au capitaine Pyrus (à la porte d: Tell Captain Pyrus (at the palace gate, or at the barracks)
textes.Le dire à Crochet (sur le quai le matin,: Tell Crochet (on the quay in the morning, at the forge in the afternoon, at the Shark's Tooth in the evening)
textes.Le dire à Cuauhtli, le grand prêtre (au: Tell Cuauhtli, the high priest (at the foot of the Great Temple)
textes.Le dire à Ix Kanul, la grande prêtresse: Tell Ix Kanul, the high priestess (at the temple, or at the Cenote in the morning)
textes.Le dire à Madame Hurla (au guichet de l': Tell Madame Hurla (at the arena ticket booth, or on the square)
textes.Le dire à Mixtli, le guerrier-jaguar (su: Tell Mixtli, the jaguar warrior (on the square of Aztlán)
textes.Le dire à Néferet, la prêtresse de Rê (a: Tell Néferet, the priestess of Ra (at the temple of Per-Hâpy)
textes.Le dire à Pigment (au Mur d'Expression l: Tell Pigment (at the Expression Wall in the morning, near the water tower or the skatepark in the afternoon, at the print shop in the evening)
textes.Le dire à Tom le Violoneux (au Crâne Fen: Tell Tom the Fiddler (at the Crâne Fendu, in the evening)
textes.Le dire à Yvon (sur son ponton de pêche,: Tell Yvon (on his fishing jetty, by the lake)
textes.Le dire à Zébuline (à son étal d'épices: Tell Zébuline (at her spice stall in the Great Market)
textes.Le dire à l'Archiduchesse Ignatia (au pa: Tell Archduchess Ignatia (at the palace, on the Citadel)
textes.Le directeur Malachar a des ailes, des c: Headmaster Malachar has wings, enormous horns and a voice that makes feathers tremble. He scares me a bit. But once, he gave me eighteen in drawing. So maybe he's nice, really.
textes.Le dirigeable de Cliquetis se pose maint: The airship from Cliquetis lands north of the village now, on the landing field. The engineers get off, look at our bridges, take notes. They think our bridges sway too much. That's the point.
textes.Le dirigeable de la Capitaine Héloïse Ni: Captain Héloïse Nimbus's airship, down in Hautefond! They race every time they cross paths. They both say they win. The sky is big: there's room for two victories.
textes.Le disque des deux villages: The disc of the two villages
textes.Le disque tourne, le diamant crépite…: The record spins, the needle crackles…
textes.Le distributeur affiche : « Merci ! Bonn: The machine displays: “Thank you! Have a nice evening, human!” Clonk! A Synth-Soda.
textes.Le distributeur hésite, réfléchit, puis: The machine hesitates, thinks, then: clonk! “On the house.” It's nice, this machine.
textes.Le dixième jour, on jouait dans les vagu: On the tenth day, we were playing in the waves. He raised his hand to splash me, he was laughing, and I saw it: his finger was bare. He looked at his hand as if it belonged to someone else. I said nothing. I got out of the water, went up to the balcony, and didn't say another word to him. I watched the sea. At least it knew where the ring was.
The tenth was for the echo.
textes.Le docteur Amélie est la femme la plus g: Doctor Amélie is the kindest woman on the island. I'm avoiding her a bit at the moment. Nothing serious. Hop hop hop!
textes.Le docteur Roux soigne tout avec des tis: Doctor Roux treats everything with herbal teas. Hers didn't cure a thing, but it smelled so good that I stopped crying to breathe it in.
textes.Le donjon a cinq étages. Un : les Caves: The dungeon has five floors. One: the Slimy Cellars, slimes and a little maze. Two: the Hall of Traps, watch out for the rolling boulder, run. Three: the Underground Lake, frogs. Four: the Library of Mimics. Five: the King. And his crown.
textes.Le dortoir est au fond de la cour de l'A: The dormitory is at the back of the Academy courtyard. Oscar snores. Lin reads under her blanket. Mirabelle makes potions under her bed. Me, I sleep. Almost.
textes.Le dragon… Bon. Il était plus petit que: The dragon… Well. It was smaller than in my stories. But it breathed fire, it had stolen all the sheep from a village and I was nineteen. I brought it back under my arm, alive, and handed it over to a lizard breeder. Philomène says “a goat”. She never saw it breathe fire, did she. I did.
textes.Le dragon… il a mangé mes chaussettes…: The dragon… he ate my socks…
textes.Le drap tombe : c'est un enfant du quart: The sheet falls: it's a kid from the neighborhood, delighted. “Really? Great! Here, my treasure, for your courage!”
textes.Le duel de l'été dernier : lui debout su: Last summer's duel: him standing on a stool, me on the rim of the fountain, the whole square between us. Nourredine's lantern fell on the third verse. Moulay Brahim said “a draw”, and Saïd went around telling everyone he'd won. Me, I say nothing. I know, that's all. The lantern knows too.
textes.Le début ! « Il était une fois… » Les qu: The beginning! “Once upon a time…” The four most beautiful words in the world. At the beginning, everything is still possible. You have a traveller's soul, you do.
textes.Le défi tient toujours, hein ! Au Bassin: The challenge still stands, okay! At the Dry Dock! First one to fall… well, that'll be me. But come anyway!
textes.Le désert du sud, c'est la plus grande r: The southern desert is the biggest region on the island. Dunes that move, stones that sing at night, and oases you only find if you know where they are.
The desert has none. It has dates.
The desert always sends them back.
textes.Le désert, c'est derrière la porte du no: The desert is beyond the north gate. I went there once, with my uncle. There was sand. Lots of sand. Everywhere. Even in my bread.
