textes.Le dôme fait quatre-vingt-douze pas de l: The dome is ninety-two paces wide. I counted them. Twice. The second time I got ninety-three.
textes.Le fanzine de Port-Boucan, imprimé par A: Port-Boucan's fanzine, printed by Agrafe at the Spinning Mill print shop: drawings by Pigment, Lentille's soup recipe, gossip from Radio Boucan, and a whole page about this week's stand-in drummer.
textes.Le fer de Pandémonia vient du volcan, le: Pandémonia's iron comes from the volcano, the Great Blaze, to the south-west. Its lava flows run all the way down to the sea. Don't go strolling on fresh lava: it looks solid, but it has a nasty temper.
textes.Le fer, on le trouve au nord, dans les h: Iron is found in the north, in the highlands. The shepherds dig it out of the rocks and sell it to the caravanners, who sell it on to us for twice the price.
textes.Le fer, ça ne ment pas. Et le tien, il c: Iron doesn't lie. And yours, how much does it cost?
textes.Le festival. Elle voulait le soleil, je: The festival. She wanted sun, I wanted rain. I said nasty things. So did she. I left for the other side of the island, with my cloud. The young ones followed me. That made Rainville. I'm not proud of how it was born.
textes.Le feu ! Enfin quelqu'un qui demande le: Fire! At last, someone who asks for fire and not light! Fine. Rule number one: fire must be fed. Go and fetch me three logs of twisted wood from the Twisted Wood, to the southwest. Twisted wood burns long and without smoke. Bring them back, and I'll teach you.
textes.Le feu de Teotihuacan, où les dieux atte: The fire of Teotihuacan, where the gods waited for one of their own to throw himself in and become the sun. On one altar, the rich offerings of Tecciztécatl; on the other, the humble offerings of Nanahuatzin. What will you throw into the fire?
textes.Le feu de la forge est bon. Donc moi aus: The forge fire is good. So I'm good too.
textes.Le feu, il faut le respecter. Il est gén: Fire must be respected. It's generous, it keeps you warm, it cooks the soup. But turn your back on it and it devours everything. A bit like Berthe when you criticise her tart.
textes.Le fil d'or autour, c'est le vent qui l': Then it was the wind that tied the golden thread round them.
textes.Le filet, je m'en moque, {surnom}. Je pe: I don't care about the net, {surnom}. I can tell you that, you of all people. That morning, it was Fernand who was beside Marius. Not me. I was watching from above. I hold it against him that he was in my place. It isn't fair, I know. It changes nothing.
textes.Le flacon brun du Doc Saignée : rhum, mi: Doc Saignée's brown flask: molasses, honey, feverweed and a secret. One sip, and you get back up from almost any brawl. Restores four hearts.
textes.Le fleuve de la nuit se met à bouillonne: The river of night begins to boil. An enormous head rises from the black water, eyes red as embers: APOPHIS, the serpent of chaos, who wants to swallow the sun!
textes.Le fleuve monte chaque année. Les ancien: The river rises every year. The ancients say it's the tears of Isis weeping for Osiris. I say it's the rain in the mountains. But I don't say it too loudly in front of Néferet.
textes.Le flotteur est à l'eau. Patience…: The float is in the water. Patience…
textes.Le fond du puits. Au nord, une caverne s: The bottom of the well. To the north, a cavern opens onto still, black water. (The chain lets you climb back up in one go.)
textes.Le four de terre ! On creuse, on chauffe: The earth oven! We dig, we heat the stones, we bury, we wait, we dig it up. It's ready in three hours. Or three hundred years. I never remember.
textes.Le four refroidit. Moi aussi. Bonne nuit: The oven is cooling down. So am I. Good night.
textes.Le four solaire dort, la nuit. Alors les: The solar oven sleeps at night. So the sugar puffs wait for sunrise, like everybody else.
textes.Le four à pain, c'est Tortellini qui l'a: Tortellini built the bread oven, stone by stone. He got the dome wrong: it leans a bit. Bread bakes better in it than anywhere else. I never told him. He thinks it's thanks to my hands. It's a little bit thanks to his mistake.
textes.Le fromage affiné, c'est le parfum de l': Ripe cheese is the scent of adventure. Humans say it smells like feet. Humans don't know a thing.
textes.Le fromage des chèvres des cendres de Hi: Cheese from Hilda's ash goats. It smells strong. Restores two hearts.
textes.Le frère de Gustave, Firmin, tient une t: Gustave's brother, Firmin, runs a tavern in Hautefond, with a chocolate machine that whistles like a locomotive. A scandal. I went down to check. It whistles. I had two hot chocolates. To check again. I go down to check every week.
textes.Le futur roadie ! J'ai une caisse pour t: The future roadie! I've got a crate for you. A small one.
textes.Le garage des Gouttières, c'est moi qui: I'm the one who found the Gutters' garage! Tin walls, tin roof, tin door! When I drum, everything echoes! It's like being inside a giant drum! The neighbours love it! Well, they don't say anything. Same thing.
textes.Le garde de la Skala dit qu'il voit des: The Skala guard says he sees lanterns in the caves at night. They're not mine, I know them all.
textes.Le gardien du phare. Un homme taciturne: The lighthouse keeper. A taciturn man who holds, without knowing it, the greatest discovery of the century in a logbook. He won't talk about it. He lets me climb up. It's a start.
textes.Le garçon en costume, à l'entrée de la H: The boy in the suit, at the entrance of the Hall. I heard him drumming on a bin. … A bin. And it was beautiful. (He nods, very seriously.)
textes.Le gel, ce n'est pas la colère. C'est la: Frost isn't anger. It's patience. Water doesn't freeze because you order it to: it freezes because you've given it time to think it over.
textes.Le gel. Hm. Il faut de la patience. Vous: Frost. Hm. It takes patience. Do you have any? We'll see. On the northern cliffs, where the wind never stops, fall flakes that never melt: the eternal frost. Bring me three. Without running. Frost doesn't like it when you run.
textes.Le globe tourne, mais nous, on ne tombe: The globe spins, but we don't fall off. It's magic.
textes.Le gobelet en plastique dit : « Un seul: The plastic cup says: “One glass per visit. Hydration is a cost.”
textes.Le gobelin lâche un cri aigu… et détale: The goblin lets out a shrill cry… and scurries off squealing! How brave.
textes.Le godet est planté dans le sol ! Les du: The bucket is stuck in the ground! The hoses are exposed: STRIKE THEM!
textes.Le godet se lève… Un cercle rouge au sol: The bucket rises… A red circle on the ground: get out of it!
textes.Le gong ne veut rien dire tant qu'on n'e: The gong means nothing until you're signed up. Madame Hurla runs the arena's ticket window: she registers the contestants (and she shouts very loudly).
textes.Le goudron non plus. Et pourtant, il se: Neither does tar. And yet it keeps quiet.
textes.Le gouvernail est très bien. Non quand m: The rudder is very good. Still no.
textes.Le grand air, enfin… s'il sentait autre: The open air, at last… if only it smelled of something other than sulphur.
textes.Le grand concert de la Halle, c'était en: The big concert at the Hall was in 1977. I had black hair, a brand-new drum kit and crazy energy. Barricade insists it was 1978, that she had a yellow scarf, and that I played out of time. The yellow scarf, I remember. That's exactly the problem.

The big concert at the Hall was in 1978. I had a yellow scarf, and he had black hair, a not-very-successful haircut and a drum kit that played out of tune. He insists it was 1977. We argue about it every Thursday on the radio. It's our way of seeing each other.
textes.Le grand pirate. Il voulait le chemin de: The big pirate. He wanted the way to the oasis. Treasure, in the desert? … I showed him a way. The desert sent him back. As I'd said.
textes.Le grand serpent des abysses… Faelar dit: The great serpent of the deep… Faelar says you defeated it. If that's true, I take back what I said about you. Some of it.
textes.Le grand serpent s'est réveillé ? Alors: The great serpent has woken up? Then you'll need a good blade and lots of coconuts. I'll give you a discount. No, I'm joking, I never give discounts.
textes.Le grand vent ! Celui qui fait tourner l: The big wind! The one that spins the mill at full tilt and blows flour all the way to the Lighthouse! Margot isn't too fond of it. Her seagulls all turn white.
textes.Le grand vent qui décoiffe !: The big wind that messes up your hair!
textes.Le grand-père d'Ysaé, celui à la crête o: Ysaé's grandfather, the one with the orange mohawk, handed me a wrench in front of his brazier so I could carry on with my speech. A “speaking wrench”. Nobody had ever asked me to carry on before! I fell silent. I still don't know why.
textes.Le gris avant l'orage ! Oh… Personne ne: The grey before a storm! Oh… Nobody's ever said that to me. Up here, we hardly ever see it. You have to look at it from above, on the clouds below. You've got an eye for it, {surnom}.
textes.Le groin de Truffe frémit. Il fonce sous: Truffe's snout quivers. He dashes under a tree, scrapes, grunts… A truffle! He sets it at your feet with a triumphant “oink”.
textes.Le gros navet qui a foncé sur moi, je l': The big turnip that charged at me, I stopped it dead with a shout. It threw itself into Germaine's net. We argued about who had caught it. Then we decided it was a collaboration. Since then, at every alert, I stand next to her. I shout, she catches. We're the best team in the Southern Fields. She'll never say so.
The big shipyard register is open. Yannick wrote in it: “Orders to be noted here, payment in the box, I build at night (and I sing).”
textes.Le grès des Strates est en couches : ocr: The Strata sandstone comes in layers: ochre, cream, rust, grey. Each layer is thousands of years. You read the rock like a book, from the bottom up. Right at the top, the last page is Hautefond. It's still being written.
textes.Le gâteau de lune, c'est la recette de m: Mooncake is my grandmother's recipe: chestnut flour, honey, and a round of bean paste drawn like the moon. We eat it on festival night. So, every night.
textes.Le géranium sera ravi. Moi aussi, je veu: The geranium will be delighted. I mean, so will I.
textes.Le hall de la Tour du Zénith, le soir :: The hall of the Zenith Tower in the evening: the potted trees are asleep, the glass lift glows softly. At the top, they say, the stars are very close.
textes.Le hall du Donjon des Mille Marches: The hall of the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps
textes.Le hamac du fond t'attend, toi qui dors: The hammock at the back is waiting for you, you who sleep like a baby. I shook it out this morning. Gently.
textes.Le hamac du fond, à bâbord. Le Léviathan: The hammock at the back, on the port side. The Léviathan will rock you to sleep. Good night!
textes.Le hamac du fond, à côté des tonneaux. S: The hammock at the back, next to the barrels. If Tonneau snores, give him a thump, he's used to it.
textes.Le haut. Évidemment. Au moins, vous avez: Up top. Obviously. At least you've got some sense. Even if you come from down below. Nobody's perfect.
textes.Le hibou de la Souche Creuse est là depu: The owl of the Hollow Stump has been there since before I was born. It always looks at me sideways, as if it knew something I don't. I think it knows where I left my secateurs last summer.
textes.Le hibou, parce que sa femme est chouett: The owl, because his wife is a hoot!
textes.Le héron. Elle avait douze ans. Il m'a p: The heron. She was twelve. It took a perch from my basket. She shot off like an arrow, all the way round the big pond, faster than the bird. She came back with the perch in her arms, eyes shining. And I said: “A cat waits.” … What an old stick-in-the-mud I am.
textes.Le héros du Grand Boucan ! Viens là que: The hero of the Great Boucan! Come here so I can hug you in my studded arms. It prickles a bit. That's affection.
textes.Le héros du cochonnet ! Assieds-toi, on: The hero of the jack! Sit down, we'll teach you.
textes.Le jardin est au milieu de la ville, mai: The garden is in the middle of the city, yet you can barely hear the cars. The low walls, the cherry trees… and a little patience in your ears.
textes.Le jaune ! Le bleu, on dirait la mer un: The yellow one! The blue one looks like the sea on a rainy day!
textes.Le jaune de la Grève Blanche: The yellow of the White Strand
textes.Le jeu de balle des Seigneurs. Une allée: The Lords' ball court. An alley, two slopes, two stone rings high up on the walls. The rubber ball, in the middle. “Play against us, traveller. Three times through the ring, and you pass.”
textes.Le jeu de balle, c'est simple : la balle: The ball game is simple: you can't touch the rubber ball with your hands or your feet. Hips, thighs, elbows. And you have to get it through the stone ring, up there. Nobody manages it. Me, twice. Maybe.
textes.Le jeudi, Honorine fait des éclairs au c: On Thursdays, Honorine makes chocolate éclairs. I come at opening time. I put down the money. I take six éclairs. I say nothing. She says nothing. She smiles. One Thursday, she was ill. There were no éclairs. I stood outside the door until noon. The next Thursday, she'd made twelve.
textes.Le jeune Gédéon empile ses dossiers en f: Young Gédéon stacks his folders in the shape of a drum kit. I've seen him play on them with two pencils. I gave him a stapler that goes “tchak”. That's all I could do. For now.
textes.Le jeune Oscar a fait tomber toute la le: Young Oscar brought the entire letter B down on his head. It took me two hours to put it back. He comes to read every day. He always reads the same page. I keep an eye on him. Above all, on his hands.
textes.Le jeune Pascal se plaint de tout. Il a: Young Pascal complains about everything. He's seventy. To me, he's a lad. I tell him: “Pascal, when you're my age, you'll be allowed to complain.” He replies: “I'm practising.”
textes.Le jeune couple de l'hôtel dîne ici tous: The young couple from the hotel dine here every evening. He stares at his finger, she stares at the sea. There's a mystery there.
textes.Le jeune marié ! Il a retourné tout mon: The newlywed! He turned over my whole stretch of beach with my punch ladle. A nice boy. Very bad with a ladle.
textes.Le jeune marié de l'hôtel est venu me de: The young groom from the hotel came to ask if I could make a wedding ring “exactly the same”. I think he's done something silly.
textes.Le jeune marié de l'hôtel. Un gentil gar: The young newlywed from the hotel. A nice boy, a bad liar, like all nice boys. He did something silly: it's up to him to fix it, not me.
textes.Le jour baisse. On ne lit pas à la lampe: The light is fading. We don't read by lamplight: oil is expensive, and the signs start to dance.
textes.Le jour de l'exercice des flammes, Pépin: On flame-exercise day, Pépin opened his snack box: twelve fireflies flew out into the classroom. Everyone wanted to catch them, and nobody was watching their candle any more. Pépin took the chance to light his own, nice and calmly. I gave him the best mark. For the light. And for the strategy.
textes.Le jour de l'exercice des flammes, j'ava: On flame exercise day, I'd brought twelve fireflies in my lunchbox. They flew off everywhere! Everyone was running after them, and I took the chance to light my candle in peace. Miss Sulfura gave me the best mark! Ortie was furious.
textes.Le jour de l'écharpe de douze mètres, c': On the day of the twelve-metre scarf, it was Aldric himself, a young man in a suit, who came to ask me to clear the door. I asked him if he was eating properly. He was speechless. He left with the bulldozers. Since then, he never comes to talk to me alone.
textes.Le jour de l'éclipse que j'avais annoncé: On the day of the eclipse I had predicted, she closed her stall to go and pray. She didn't sell a thing all day. The sun came back, and so did she, furious, all the way to my door: “You could have put it on another day!” I told her I don't decide eclipses. I announce them. She never believed me.
textes.Le jour de l'élection, la dernière boule: On election day, Aristide's last ball rolled, and rolled, and stopped “one centimetre away”. He raised his arms as if he'd won a war. He even cried a bit. I shouted “Thief!” I've been shouting it for eighteen years. He keeps the ball on his desk, on a red cushion, like a holy relic.
textes.Le jour de l'élection, la place entière: On election day, the whole square held its breath. Marcel lay down on the ground, tape measure between his teeth, and measured three times. He got up, dusted off his trousers and announced: “One centimetre.” Then he winked at me. For eighteen years I've wondered what that wink meant.
textes.Le jour de la bosse, on s'est retrouvés: The day of the bump, we both ended up sitting on the ground, each with a hand on our head. He looked at me and said: “Nice hip shot, kid. Bad trajectory.” He picked up the ball, gave it back to me, and said: “Again. But aim for the moon.” I've always aimed for the moon since. I've never got it.
textes.Le jour de la chèvre, mon oncle a ri pen: The day of the goat, my uncle laughed for an hour. Then he saw me counting coins, and he stopped laughing. “A tanuki who sells!” He announced it to the whole market, like a disaster. But that evening he gave me my first purse. An old leather purse, empty. “So you can be ashamed properly,” he said.
textes.Le jour de la corde, les pattes de Bourr: The day of the rope, Bourru's paws were burnt. Pivoine treated them for a month. Every day. I forged her a balm spatula. Left it on her counter. Said nothing. She still uses it. I've seen.
textes.Le jour de la course, toute la plage éta: On race day, the whole beach was there. Bernard was warming up swinging his arms, I was doing push-ups. And the wind picked up. Red flag. The rules, I'm the one who enforces them: I had to raise the flag myself that cancelled my own race. Bernard shouted that I was scared. I shouted that it was the law. Seven years we've been shouting.
textes.Le jour de la démonstration de trop, dev: On the day of the demonstration too many, in front of the jury, the golden gear jumped off its axle. It rolled across the square, between people's legs, went past the railing and fell all the way down to the harbour. Go down myself? I get vertigo, and the cable car makes me seasick. I suspect one of Capucine's confetti. And Gonzague, the crane operator, saw something golden near his crane.
textes.Le jour de la démonstration, quand l'eng: On the day of the demonstration, when the golden gear jumped off its axle, I was at stand 5. I saw it roll across the square. I ran after it first, before anyone else, on my old legs. Too late: it went over the railing. I never told anyone. Firmin thinks I didn't even look up.
textes.Le jour de la fameuse soupe, tout l'équi: The day of the famous soup, the whole crew got sick. Everybody, except me. I'd had three bowls. Doc says it's a miracle. Mange-Clous says it proves his soup was good. Me, I say nothing. But I had hiccups for two days.
textes.Le jour de la fête du port, le maire fai: On the day of the harbour festival, the mayor gives his speech on the platform, right under the stopped clock face. He talks about the future, the season, progress. For half an hour, he doesn't look up once. Me, I look at the clock face, then at him, then at the clock face. He sweats. It isn't just the sun.
textes.Le jour de la grande cérémonie du millén: On the day of the great millennium ceremony, I stepped on my toga and fell into the fountain, smack into the planet Jupiter. I came out soaked. The whole Agora was watching me. I said: “This was planned.” Everyone applauded. Since then, I say that sentence every time I fall. Which is to say, often.
textes.Le jour de la grande procession, mes abe: On the day of the great procession, my bees followed me all the way to the temple. All of them! I hadn't asked them anything. A golden cloud on Kukulkan's staircase. People cried miracle. I said they wanted to see the festival, like everyone else. They settled on the altar, as good as novices. Ix Kanul has never asked me to leave them at home.
textes.Le jour de la grande procession, ses abe: On the day of the great procession, his bees followed him all the way to the temple. All of them. A golden cloud, buzzing behind us on the stairs. People thought it was a sign from the gods. Yum Kab said they just wanted to see the festival. They settled on the altar, very well-behaved, until the end of the prayer.
textes.Le jour de la leçon, je me suis appliqué: On the day of the lesson, I really applied myself. The fish, the lemon, the saffron… and a little splash of rum for warmth, and two spoonfuls of sugar for sweetness. Zohra watched me without a word. When I lifted the lid, she wept. Standing there, spoon in hand. Nobody had ever wept over my tagine. Ho ho!
textes.Le jour de la montée, raconte-t-on, tout: On the day of the rising, so they say, the whole town of Hautefond was on the Square. The piece of Butte began to shake, then to rise, ever so gently, with the houses on it. An old lady shouted: “My washing!” It had stayed below, on the line. They sent it up the next day, by the Column.
textes.Le jour de la montée, une voisine a crié: On the day of the rise, a neighbour shouted “My washing!”. Her sheets had been left down below, on a line, in Hautefond. The next day, the liftkeepers brought them up through the Column, neatly folded. It was the first parcel on the Cloud Line. My father used to say the sheets still smelled of the Floor.
textes.Le jour de la naissance de Nebet, je l'a: The day Nebet was born, I sent for her. Nebet was screaming so loudly that Néferet had to shout her blessing. At the end, she said: “She has a voice. Ra will hear her.” Eight years later, Ra hears her every morning, on the sistrum. So do the ibises.
textes.Le jour de la naissance de Noisette, Hon: The day Noisette was born, Honorine came to the temple with her baby in her arms for the blessing. I prayed, she sang, and the little one sneezed in the middle. The whole congregation laughed. I said it was one more blessing. Since then, Noisette sneezes every time she enters the temple. I think she does it on purpose. She's very clever.
textes.Le jour de la noce, que Samira me déroul: On our wedding day, for Samira to roll out a carpet for me in front of the door. I know, I know: I'll be getting slippers. But a man can dream of a carpet, can't he? Even with slippers on his feet.
textes.Le jour de la réouverture de la Ligne, j: The day the Line reopened, I went up to Hautefond. I saw the sky for the first time. Blue. Immense. No ceiling. I stood for an hour on Column Square, head tilted back, mouth open. A lady gave me a coin, thinking I was begging. I kept it. It's blue with paint now.
textes.Le jour de la réouverture des Strates, j: On the day the Strata reopened, I pulled the pavilion lever myself. The cabin went down without a single creak. At the bottom, Dean Agathe was waiting for me. We said two sentences to each other. It was perfect. The Burgomaster said four hundred.
textes.Le jour de la réouverture, elle est desc: On reopening day, she came down in my cabin. She put her hand on the rail and said: “She's well brought up, Anatole.” I didn't hear. But I saw her lips. I read them three times.
textes.Le jour de la réouverture, il m'a laissé: On reopening day, he let me sit in the cabin, at the platform, for one minute. He didn't pull the lever. We just sat there, the two of us, not moving, at the bottom of the sea. He said: “Whenever you feel like it, Ernest.” I haven't felt like it yet. But I know the seat is waiting for me.
textes.Le jour de la réouverture, je l'ai vue s: On reopening day, I saw her smile at the console when the capsule arrived. Just for a second. Then she went back to her tea. But I saw it.
textes.Le jour de la réouverture, la capsule es: On reopening day, the capsule arrived at the top with Mistress Capucine, the Burgomaster, and Barnabé. Barnabé was green. He stepped out, shook my hand and said: “You're taller than in your letters.” Then he sat down on the platform. I sat down next to him. We talked for two hours. On the floor. It was the best day of my life.
textes.Le jour de la réouverture, le Bourgmestr: On reopening day, the Burgomaster had three bowls. Then he gave a speech about soup. I listened right to the end, and served him a fourth bowl. So his mouth would be full. Worked a treat.
textes.Le jour de la réouverture, nous avons co: On reopening day, the four of us cut the ribbon together, with the Burgomaster and Céleste. Agathe handed me the scissors and said: “Your turn.” Then, more quietly: “Well held.” Two words. After the Burgomaster's two-hour speech, it was by far the best one.
textes.Le jour de la réouverture, on s'est enfi: On the day of the reopening, we finally met for real. He stepped out of the capsule all green, shook my hand very hard and said: “You're taller than in your letters.” Then he sat down on the platform. I sat down next to him. We talked for two hours. On the floor. It was perfect.
textes.Le jour de la réouverture, on s'est serr: On the day of the reopening, we hugged in the middle of the Esplanade. His moustache got tangled in mine. It took ten minutes and Mireille to untangle us.
textes.Le jour de la réouverture, sa cabine s'e: On reopening day, his cabin got stuck for thirty seconds between two floors. He got out his rulebook. I got out my twelve-millimetre spanner. We fixed it together. He didn't tell anyone. Neither did I. He just gave me a little nod.
The day of the raw sardine, captain.
textes.Le jour de la soupe, Doc a soigné trente: On the day of the soup, Doc treated thirty sailors in one night, with herbal teas and buckets. In the morning, he came into my kitchen, lifted the lid of my pot, sniffed, and said: “Pufferfish.” Just that. He never said anything else, to anyone. Since then, I bring him a bowl of soup every noon.
textes.Le jour de la soupe, tout le Requin a ét: The day of the soup, the whole Shark got sick, except Gros-Louis, who'd eaten three bowls. Three! That evening, he came to ask me if there was any left. I cried, from shame and pride, both at once. Since then, if a dish looks dodgy to me, he's the one I send to taste it.
textes.Le jour de leurs noces, c'est moi qui ai: On their wedding day, I was the one who married Moloka and Grumbald, on the quay. Grumbald cried so much he got the framed sardine wet. Moloka laughed. Since then, every year, on their anniversary, Grumbald stands me my punch. He says it's to thank me. I think it's so that I'll tell their story again.
textes.Le jour de ma fusée qui fumait, maman es: The day of my smoking rocket, Mum came running from the lab, with her rubber gloves and her goggles on her forehead. Dad was there too. They looked for me in the smoke. When they found me, I was all black except my eyes. Mum said “Léonce!”, Dad said “Léonce!”, and then they laughed.
textes.Le jour de ma naissance, il a écrit mon: The day I was born, he wrote my name “Coralain”. I've asked him a hundred times to fix it. He says you don't scratch out a scroll: “The mistake is part of history.” So officially, the dome's first child is called Coralain. And I'm still the one who ends up in the scroll of mistakes.
textes.Le jour de ma naissance, j'ai soufflé to: On the day I was born, I blew every petal out of the throne room. The queen's hair was full of them. She didn't shout. She handed me a letter and said: “Since you can't stay still, go and be somewhere else.” I've never come back on time since. But I've always come back.
textes.Le jour de ma première Grande Alerte, je: The day of my first Great Alert, I got the direction wrong. I shouted “EVERYONE TO THE LAKE!”. The whole town headed east. Père Gaubert was left alone in the middle of his fields, with twenty turnips running circles round him. That evening, he came to see me on the square. He wasn't cross. He said: “They had a lovely day.”
textes.Le jour de ma première offre, elle m'a o: The day of my first offer, she gave me an apple. I took it out of politeness. I bit into it on the way out. It was so good I forgot to come back with my papers. Since then, every week, I walk past her stall to make an offer. In truth, I go for the apple. She knows it. I know it. We pretend. It's a very good deal.
textes.Le jour de ma retraite, je lui ai donné: The day I retired, I gave her my satchel. The old leather one, with the buckle that sticks. I told her: “It knows the way, just let it carry you.” She still has it. She only re-stitched the strap. With yellow thread. Yellow! My satchel…
textes.Le jour de mes dix ans, mon père m'a emm: On my tenth birthday, my father took me aboard his brig to make me love the sea. I was sick from departure to return. When we got back, he set me down on the quay with a bag of island spices and said: “That one will be a merchant.” The bag smelled of cinnamon. I opened my stall eight years later.
textes.Le jour de mes noces, c'est le Capitaine: On my wedding day, it was the Captain who married us, on the quay. He gave an hour-long speech about the sea, sardines and love. At the end, he told his ash-storm story. Nobody knew why. He said: “Because a marriage is a storm you weather together.” Grumbald cried.
textes.Le jour de mes quinze ans, je suis reven: On my fifteenth birthday, I went back to the Fronde to choose my colour in front of the brazier, like all the young ones of the Fronde. I wasn't from here. Brasero asked the Assembly. Everyone raised their hand. I chose green. My mother said I looked like a clear-track signal. That's exactly what it was.
textes.Le jour de mes seize ans, le vieux pilot: On my sixteenth birthday, the old pilot, Captain Gobie, beckoned to me from the quay: “You've been counting my bubbles for ten years. Climb aboard.” At fifty metres, he let me take the controls. I did a barrel roll. Not on purpose. He laughed so hard the porthole steamed up. On the way back up, he told me: “You've got everything it takes to be a pilot. Except caution. Go and see Yolande.”
textes.Le jour de mes vingt ans, toute la Guild: On my twentieth birthday, the whole Guild pretended to have forgotten. At closing time, Master Hugues came out of his office with a lopsided cake and a new stamp engraved with my name. He cried before I'd even opened the parcel. He's the one who named my first stamp “my little Clac”. The name stuck.
textes.Le jour de mon anniversaire, Mama a fait: On my birthday, Mama rang the bell on the bar, and the whole Crâne Fendu sang me a song. Tom played, Gros-Louis sang out of tune, the Silent One clapped his hands. Mama brought me a barrel-shaped cake, with a sugar bung. Nobody had ever made me a cake. I didn't eat it straight away. I looked at it.
textes.Le jour de mon anniversaire, elle m'a ch: On my birthday, she sang me a song she'd written. It was about a tagliatelle who wanted to fly. I cried. So did the neighbours, but not for the same reasons.
textes.Le jour de mon arrivée, j'ai crié mon no: The day I arrived, I shouted my full name in the Guild, as is proper. Everyone laughed. Except Master Hugues. He stood up, shouted his own, “HUGUES BARBE-DE-FER!”, and hugged me. Then he cried. Then I cried. Mamie Rissole served us a pie. It was a perfect welcome.
textes.Le jour de mon arrivée, je marchais vers: The day I arrived, I was walking to the Academy through the mud. A man with an already white beard looked at me, blew, and the puddle in front of me froze so I wouldn't get my feet wet. I slipped, fell, and laughed, sitting on the ground. He said: “Hm. She laughs.” That was Borée. He's reminded me of it often.
textes.Le jour de mon arrivée, l'archimage m'a: The day I arrived, the archmage asked me for a little light. I made a black light. At noon, the whole courtyard turned to night, with stars. Everyone screamed. She just said: “Interesting.” Nobody had ever told me “interesting” before. I decided to stay. That was three years ago.
textes.Le jour de mon couronnement, Asmodin ava: On my coronation day, Asmodin had polished the throne steps so much that I slid all the way down, horns first. The whole court went silent. So I laughed. Then everyone laughed. Ever since, my people know that their Archduchess can fall, and get back up laughing. That's my best law.
textes.Le jour de mon couronnement, il avait ci: On my coronation day, he'd polished the throne steps till you could see yourself in them. I slid all the way down. He turned grey, then white, then almost transparent. I laughed. He didn't sleep all week. Since then, the steps are still polished, but with a rug on top. A non-slip rug. He chose it himself.
textes.Le jour de mon exposition, il a fait le: On the day of my exhibition, he went round the thousand canvases three times. That evening, he asked me, very quietly, if I'd sell him one. “For a wall that's bored.” I gave it to him. He said it was too much. He took it.
textes.Le jour de mon millième coucher de solei: On the day of my thousandth sunset, I exhibited all thousand canvases on the Esplanade, in a circle around Séraphin's Feather. People walked among them all day long. Mr Pascal came by and said: “They're all the same.” Then he went round three times. That evening, he told me: “Well. No.”
textes.Le jour de notre mariage, j'ai lu un poè: On our wedding day, I read a twenty-page poem. She said “I do” halfway through, to save time.
textes.Le jour de notre mariage, l'Assemblée a: On our wedding day, the Assembly voted an evening of silence in our honour. It lasted four minutes. Then Brasero sneezed. We took it for a bass drum hit, and played till morning.
textes.Le jour de notre rencontre, Gérard a pho: The day we met, Gérard photographed my shoes, blue ones with little bows, instead of the pupils. He showed them to me afterwards, very proud: “Look at the light on the bow.” I still have those photos. They're sharp. The only ones of his life, perhaps. Which goes to show: you have to know what you're looking at.
textes.Le jour de notre rencontre, Wilfried éta: The day we met, Wilfried had come to deliver springs to the lab. He went near the big coil, and clack: his brass arm got magnetised and stuck to it. An hour. I couldn't cut the current without blowing everything up. So we talked. About springs, dogs, rain. After an hour, I cut it. He said: “Already?”
textes.Le jour de notre rencontre, j'étais venu: The day we met, I'd come to the lab to deliver a part. My brass arm got close to her big coil, and clack: stuck. For an hour. Électre had to cut the power to the whole district. During that hour, we talked. About everything. When the arm came unstuck, I thought it was a shame. So did she, I think.
textes.Le jour de sa fusée en tuyau de poêle, j: The day of his stovepipe rocket, I saw the smoke from the stand. Pitch black, above the square. I ran. So did Électre, from the lab. We found him right in the middle, all black, with his goggles and a big grin. We looked at each other, Électre and me. And we laughed. Both of us. I can't remember the last time we'd laughed together.
textes.Le jour de sa fusée en tuyau de poêle, t: The day of his stovepipe rocket, the whole square vanished in smoke. I ran from the lab, Wilfried ran from the Fair, and we arrived at the same moment in front of a little boy all black and very proud. Wilfried and I looked at each other. And we laughed. Together. That hadn't happened to us for a long time. Since then, his rockets smoke more and more. Strange.
textes.Le jour de sa naissance, Zéphyr a souffl: On the day he was born, Zéphyr blew every petal out of the throne room. I still had some in my hair the next day. I understood that a wind like that needed keeping busy. I gave him a letter. He has never stopped since.
textes.Le jour de ses dix ans, j'ai emmené Zébu: On her tenth birthday, I took Zébuline out on the Firebrand to make her love the sea. She was sick from the moment we left until we got back. When we returned, I set her down on the quay with a bag of island spices. I told her: “You'll be a merchant.” She opened her stall eight years later. She says it's thanks to the bag.
textes.Le jour de ses quinze ans, devant le bra: On her fifteenth birthday, in front of the brazier, she hesitated between blue and green. She looked at me. I said: “Choose your own.” She chose blue. I pretended to be disappointed for one second. Then I cried with joy.
textes.Le jour de son arrivée, il y a quarante: The day she arrived, forty years ago, she was walking through the mud. I froze the puddle in front of her, for her shoes. She slipped, she fell, and she laughed, sitting on the ground. I knew that day she'd make a good archmage. It took twenty years for the others to know it too.
textes.Le jour de son couronnement, Thorgal est: On the day of his coronation, Thorgal came to my alcove, alone, before the celebrations. He asked me: “Will I be a good king?” The runes said: “He will lose his crown a thousand times and find it a thousand and one.” I read them to him. He laughed. He loses it every day. He always finds it.
textes.Le jour de son couronnement, j'avais cir: On her coronation day, I had waxed the steps of the throne with… excessive care. Her Highness slid all the way down in front of the whole court. I wanted to vanish under the carpet. She burst out laughing, and the court laughed with her. That evening, she said to me: “Thank you, Asmodin. Now they know I'm just like them.”
textes.Le jour de son éclipse, j'ai fermé mon é: On the day of his eclipse, I closed my stall to pray, like everyone. The sun came back in the afternoon, but the customers didn't: they were all still at the temple. A whole day lost! He says it wasn't his fault, he just announced it. He could have announced it for a rainy day.
textes.Le jour des daurades, quand Paulo a crié: The day of the sea bream, when Paulo shouted “Day-old!”, I looked at Fernand. He was looking at his boots. I understood. I swore to Paulo they were caught that morning, and I paid Fernand the morning price, without a word. He never said thank you. But since then, on Mondays, he saves me his best sea bream.
textes.Le jour des quarante pains, je suis arri: On the day of the forty loaves, I came running into the square. It was raining honey loaves. The children were dancing, Faelar had one in each hand. And Sylwen, white as a sheet, was clinging to the railing. I helped her down, plank by plank. She didn't say a word. At the bottom, she gave me a loaf.
textes.Le jour du chien, Pilli. Et toi ?: The day of the dog, Pilli. And you?
textes.Le jour du cochonnet, Raymond a lancé de: The day of the jack, Raymond threw crooked and the jack rolled off towards the fountain. I say under a bench. He says I shot like a klutz. Me! We sulked for three days, each on his own pitch, playing with a pebble. After three days, he came to ask me if my pebble rolled better than his.
textes.Le jour du concours de sieste, je me sui: The day of the nap contest, I woke up the next morning, still standing on the temple steps. Father Clotaire was asleep on his bench. Mélusine had gone. There was a note under my boot: “Draw. You are hopeless cases. M.” Father Clotaire woke up, read the note and said: “What a lovely compliment.”
textes.Le jour du concours de sieste, nous nous: On the day of the napping contest, we settled on the temple steps, him standing, me sitting on a bench. Mélusine was the referee. After an hour, she rang Marguerite to see who was still asleep. We were both asleep. She rang louder. We were still asleep. The next day we'd forgotten there had been a contest. Mélusine hadn't.
textes.Le jour du grand marché, elle a voulu me: On the day of the great market, she tried to shake me off behind Kraxx's stall. My cape caught on a halberd, and thirty swords came crashing down with a terrible racket. My Archduchess came back to help me pick them up. An Archduchess on her knees, picking up swords. I'll never forget it.
textes.Le jour du lavoir, elle a coupé mon ruba: On the day of the wash-house, she cut my ribbon with her hammer. There's still a hole in the cobbles. I had a little plaque put up: “Here, a ribbon was cut with enthusiasm.”
textes.Le jour du maire, j'ai vu ma petite Écro: On the day of the mayor, I saw my little Écrou climbing along the cable, a spanner tucked in her belt. I shouted her real first name, the one I never say. She didn't turn round. She freed the brake, and the car set off again with the mayor still reciting. When she came back down, I hugged her so hard my cap fell off.
textes.Le jour du maire, quand j'ai commencé à: On the day of the mayor, when I started climbing along the cable, Uncle Ernest shouted my real name. The only time ever. He was white as a sheet under his kepi. When I came back down, he hugged me so hard my spanner left a mark on my cheek. He's never mentioned that day again. I mention it all the time.
textes.Le jour du marais, c'est lui qui m'a tro: The day of the marsh, he was the one who found me, at the water's edge. He loaded me onto his back and ran all the way to the port yelling at everyone to get out of the way. All night, he sat in front of Doc's door. He shouted “WHAT?!” at anyone who came near. Nobody went in. Doc could work. I don't forget it.
textes.Le jour du marais, je l'ai trouvé au bor: The day of the marsh, I found him at the water's edge, all pale. I put him on my back and ran all the way to the port shouting at everyone to get out of the way. They got out of the way. All night, I stayed in front of Doc's door. Nobody went in. People were talking to me, I think. I wasn't listening. For once, on purpose.
textes.Le jour du mariage, j'ai dit « oui ». Et: On our wedding day, I said “yes”. And nothing else all day. The guests thought I was ill. Khadija laughed all evening. She said: “At least he didn't say no.” Thirty years she's been telling it. I still say yes. No more. That's enough.
textes.Le jour du navet volant, je l'avais lanc: The day of the flying turnip, I'd thrown it at Germaine, and it landed in Ulric's pot. Ulric came out with two plates. He sat us side by side on the bench, Germaine and me, and served us without a word. We ate in silence. It was very good. At the end, Germaine said: “It's good, my turnip.” I said: “It's Ulric's cooking.” We started quarrelling again.
textes.Le jour du navet volant, sur la Grand-Pl: The day of the flying turnip, on the Great Square, I caught it in my net and threw it back. It ended up in Ulric's pot. Ulric sat us down side by side and served us the turnip. We ate without talking. It was delicious. I said: “My turnip's good.” She said: “It's Ulric's cooking.” We started shouting again. But it was a good meal.
textes.Le jour du neuvième toit, je servais un: On the day of the ninth roof, I was serving a coffee on the terrace. I heard a whistling, a shadow went by, and boom: a whole roof landed next to me. Nobody hurt. I didn't spill a drop. I looked at the roof, I looked at the cup, and I said to the customer: “That'll give you some shade.” It's been the awning ever since.
textes.Le jour du nuage en forme de dragon, je: The day of the dragon-shaped cloud, I really did see it! A head, wings, a tail! The Captain called out the whole guard. They watched the sky for an hour. The cloud turned into a sheep. Ferdinand sighed so loudly the pigeons flew off. Then he told me, very quietly: “It really was a beautiful dragon of yours.” I'll never forget it.
textes.Le jour du record, j'ai dansé sur le pon: On record day, I danced on the south bridge with my ribbons, and Marée sold eighty crackers. She gave me ten. So I danced the saddest dance of my life in front of her stall. Nobody dared buy a thing. The next day, she paid me in coins. Three. It's a start.
textes.Le jour du remorquage, tout le port rega: On towing day, the whole harbour was watching the galleon come in. He stood on deck and shouted “Drop anchor!” far too early. The anchor landed right in my big green net. When they hauled it up, it had my net round its neck, like a necklace. Three weeks of knots. I send him the bill every week, by little Tibo.
textes.Le jour du sac tombé sur ma tête, elle e: The day the sack fell on my head, she came to dust me off. She was laughing. She ran her hand through my hair to brush off the flour, and said: “Look, it's brown.” It was the first time in ten years anyone had seen my hair. I stood stock-still. She said: “Catching your breath?” I said yes.
textes.Le jour du « vol », j'étais au kiosque d: On the day of the “theft”, I was at Bruno's kiosk, sad as a coconut palm with no coconuts. He went to fetch milk from the back, and left a little notebook open on the counter: “Granny's Coconut Ice Cream”. I copied it all onto my arm, in pencil. I left proud as a pirate. For a week, I didn't wash that arm.
textes.Le jour où Achille a fait son centième h: The day Achille did his hundredth figure of eight, Gaston pulled the coffee machine's whistle in his honour. One long blast, enough to rattle the cups. Up above, Achille flapped his wings. The whole café came out onto the terrace to applaud the sky. The butler too, a little late.

The day Achille flew his hundredth figure of eight, I sounded the Bielle's whistle for him. A long blast, like for a train pulling into the station. Up there, he flapped his wings. On the terrace, Adèle cried under her sun hat. Me, I spent a good while drying cups that were already very clean.
textes.Le jour où Aubin m'a fait la potion pour: The day Aubin made me the potion for my knees, I managed ten steps down into the dungeon. Ten steps, after fifteen years. I touched the wall of the first landing. It was damp, it smelt of jelly, like before. I came back up and cried like Hugues. Aubin was there, with his notebook. He didn't write anything. He just sat down beside me.
textes.Le jour où Belle-Humeur a ramené Crochet: The day Belle-Humeur brought Crochet back from the marsh, I went to Doc's. I looked at his arm. I measured, with my eyes. I went home. I took an old anchor. I forged all night, without stopping. In the morning, the hook was ready, polished like a mirror. I didn't charge for it. You don't charge for that.
textes.Le jour où Bulle a fini ma bulle de soin: The day Bulle finished my healing bubble, she let me go in first. I laid my hand on the glass wall, and the whole dome lit up pink, like my hands. Bulle cried. So did I. She'd spent a month inventing a glass that doesn't hurt light. She'd never told me.
textes.Le jour où Fundin a trempé une lame roug: The day Fundin quenched a red-hot blade in my cauldron, I ran to the forge, spoon raised. Borin planted himself in front of his apprentice, arms wide: “It was for the salt.” The stew tasted of iron, and everyone thought it was better. Since then, I slip an old nail in, on the sly.
textes.Le jour où Héloïse est montée au Café, e: The day Héloïse came up to the Café, they sat back to back, each at her own table, and told the same race, each her own way, at the same time. I served two teas. And laughed twice.
textes.Le jour où Héloïse est montée au Café, n: The day Héloïse came up to the Café, we sat back to back and told the same race at the same time. Gustave served two teas and laughed twice. He's a true professional.
textes.Le jour où Ianthé a dansé sur le pont su: The day Ianthé danced on the south bridge with her seaweed ribbons, I sold eighty crackers. A record! To thank her, I gave her ten. She looked at me, then danced a very slow, very sad dance in front of the stall. I didn't sell another thing all day. The next day, I paid her in coins. Three.
textes.Le jour où Lison a coupé la corde du sac: The day Lison cut the rope of the flour sack stuck in my storeroom, the sack fell on Clovis. He didn't move. He said: “Ah. Flour.” He was already all white, so it didn't show. But his ears turned bright red when I came to dust him off. It's the only part of him the flour never hides.
textes.Le jour où Lisse & Fils a voulu raser la: The day Lisse & Fils wanted to flatten the Cannery, I sat down in front of the door with my needles and a ball of wool. Three weeks. I knitted a twelve-metre scarf. The bulldozers went away. They didn't know how to get past the scarf.
textes.Le jour où Lou a passé son brevet de pil: The day Lou got her pilot's licence, she was eighteen and wanted to go down to three hundred metres. I said: “Two hundred.” She said: “Two hundred and fifty.” I said: “Two hundred.” She said: “Fine, but I'll look down.” That very evening, I engraved “200” on her control panel. And underneath, in tiny letters: “Lou, I see you.”
textes.Le jour où Miou a disparu, elle a fouill: The day Miou disappeared, she searched every basket on my stall, every jar in the house, and even my chest. I was afraid for my belt… I mean, for my sheets. In the evening, she put a bowl of milk on the doorstep, just in case. The neighbourhood cats partied all night long.
textes.Le jour où Miou a disparu, elle est venu: The day Miou disappeared, she came to the quay with red eyes and asked me to look along the banks from my boat. I looked everywhere, all the way to the river mouth, shouting “Miou!” like an idiot. The herons gave me funny looks. For Nebet, I'd shout “Miou!” all the way to the sea.
textes.Le jour où Miou est parti, j'ai demandé: The day Miou ran away, I asked Khéty to look along the banks, in his boat. He went all the way to the river mouth, where the crocodiles are! Shouting “Miou! Miou!” really loudly. Everyone heard him. He said the herons gave him funny looks. Herons always give funny looks.
textes.Le jour où Nebet est née, Tiyi m'a fait: The day Nebet was born, Tiyi sent for me to bless her. The baby was screaming so loudly I couldn't hear my own prayer. Tiyi smiled: “She's singing with you.” Eight years later, Nebet still sings with me. Just as loudly.
textes.Le jour où Omar était malade, j'ai vendu: The day Omar was ill, I sold half as much. The customers ate slowly, looked at the sea, chatted. Nobody left. Nobody came. The grill without Omar is a party without a drum. The next day I took six sardines to his house, so he'd get better faster.
textes.Le jour où Rhubarbe s'est envolé vers la: The day Rhubarbe flew off towards the jungle, Joe closed his stall. He came to the quay, pockets full of seeds, and he whistled for an hour, nose towards the trees. I told him it was no use. He kept going. He whistles well, Joe. I never said thank you. I'm saying it to you.

The day Rhubarbe flew off to the jungle, I heard him swearing in the distance, over by the old abandoned camp, to the north. I closed my stall, filled my pockets with seeds, and whistled on the quay, nose towards the trees. She was beside me. She didn't say anything. She had the same eyes as my birds when they've lost their cage.
textes.Le jour où Rouille m'a entendue jouer su: The day Rouille heard me playing my broomstick, she sat down on the quay, listened to three songs, then said: “You, you've got rhythm.” I answered “KIAAA”. She understood it meant yes. Ever since, we half talk in seagull.
textes.Le jour où Ysaé est montée en haut, il a: The day Ysaé went up top, he played very softly. For the first time in his life. I thought he was ill. He was crying into his drums. I sang louder to cover it. Nobody noticed. Except Écho. Écho notices everything.
textes.Le jour où elle a perdu sa voix, Mélusin: The day she lost her voice, Mélusine came to the counter with a slate. She wrote her announcements in huge letters, and I read them aloud on the square. Nobody heard me. She was laughing so hard, without a sound, that she cried. It's the best memory of my career.
textes.Le jour où elle a traversé le Pont avec: The day she crossed the Bridge with her ladle, I was waiting for her on the other side. I said: “At last, we're going to eat.” She said: “At last, people who have time to say thank you.” We've been saying thank you to each other for twenty-five years. Every lunchtime.
textes.Le jour où elle a été collée au comptoir: The day my ninth potion glued her to the counter, I read to her for an hour. A treatise on mushrooms. She listened to the end. Afterwards she said: “That was fascinating.” Nobody had ever said that about my treatises. I almost gave her my grandfather's potion. I didn't. But I thought about it.
textes.Le jour où elle est partie vivre à l'arb: The day she went to live in the Lookout tree, Dad stared at his float as if he wanted to drown it. Not a word. So I put down my fish knife and said: “She runs, Dad. Let her run.” He nodded. Éclair never said thank you. She looks at me, sometimes. Same thing.
textes.Le jour où elle est venue, elle s'est in: The day she came, she settled right at the front, at the bow, hair in the wind, and sang the whole crossing. Off-key, but loud. The passengers clapped when we arrived. And I knew right then that she wouldn't go back. People who sing at the bow never go back.
textes.Le jour où elle m'a acheté ma boîte, hui: The day she bought my box, for eight coins, I went home, looked at the eight coins on the table, and felt ashamed. I went back to the Bazaar that same evening to give her the money back. She refused. She said: “It's perfect: it can't break down.” Then she ordered twenty more.
textes.Le jour où elle m'a découvert, je portai: The day she discovered me, I was carrying four crates on the quay. Madame Hurla planted herself in front of me and shouted: “YOU! YOU'RE GOING TO BE A CHAMPION!” I got such a fright that I dropped everything. The crates were full of ash eggs. She paid for the eggs. She says it's the best purchase of her life.
textes.Le jour où il a débarqué à Port-Coutelas: The day he landed in Port-Coutelas, he didn't have a penny, and a brand-new leg that still smelled of sap. I served him a grog and a stew, and told him: “You'll pay when you can.” He cried into his stew. He says it was the pepper. I've never put pepper in my stew.
textes.Le jour où il a failli monter en rang E,: The day he almost made rank E, I'd already got the stamp ready. I'd even inked it. He came back from the lake covered in slobber, without his frog. I put the stamp away without a word. It's still inked, in the drawer. I renew the ink every month.
textes.Le jour où il a perdu son engrenage d'or: The day he lost his golden gear, Firmin leaned over the railing and shouted questions down at me. “Golden how?” Ho! “Big how?” Ho! “Rolling which way?” Ho! At eighty metres you only hear half the words, so I answered “Ho!” to everything. He seemed to find that very clear.
textes.Le jour où il a vendu sa vieille chaudiè: The day he sold his old boiler to Firmin, he came to eat, all sad. I served him a hot chocolate. He said: “That's what she'll be doing now, my boiler. Hot chocolate.” Then he smiled. He finished the cup.
textes.Le jour où il a voulu me faire du pain,: The day he tried to make bread for me, he fell asleep while the dough was rising. When I arrived, the dough had overflowed the kneading trough and covered the table and the temple cat, who was asleep too. Father Clotaire was snoring softly, head on the table. I gathered it all up, made little rolls, and put them in front of him. He woke up and said: “Oh! It worked!”
textes.Le jour où il est arrivé, il a déchargé: The day he arrived, he unloaded his barrels, I served him a slice of pie, and he missed the tide. The next day, the mist was too thick: another slice. The day after that too. He's been missing the tide for thirty years. He says it's my pie that brings the mist. I don't say no.
textes.Le jour où il est devenu garde, à vingt-: The day he became a guard, at twenty-five, I knitted him a red scarf, so he could be seen from afar in the mist. He found it too flashy. Thirty years later, he still wears it. He says it's for the cold. A stitch ran last winter: he darned it himself, all crooked. I said nothing.
textes.Le jour où il est reparti, son tablier é: The day he left, his apron was burnt all over, like a colander. I told him: “Not bad… for a big'un.” He grinned from ear to ear. He didn't know it's my highest compliment. Don't tell him. I say it to Octave too, but quieter.
textes.Le jour où il m'a donné la flûte-colibri: The day he gave me the hummingbird flute, a real hummingbird came to listen. Coyotl cried more than I did. He said it was the smallest thing he'd ever made. I say it's the biggest. We don't agree. I play him a tune every time he passes by. He pretends to be in a hurry. He never is.
textes.Le jour où il m'a nommé maître de la Gui: The day he made me Guild master, he'd forgotten the ceremony. He turned up in his nightshirt, wearing a cabbage-shaped hat, because Aurore had woken him in a panic. He gave a magnificent speech about friendship and courage. Then he asked who I was. I cried with laughter. So did he.
textes.Le jour où j'ai crié si fort au lac que: The day I screamed so loud at the lake that the frog spat out Hilaire, Mélusine heard about it that same evening. She came to the bakery, knelt down in front of me, and said: “A colleague!” Since then, on Saturdays, I ring Marguerite on the square. It takes both hands. The first time, I fell over with the bell. Mélusine said it was a very fine ding.
textes.Le jour où j'ai cru que mes navets bouge: The day I thought my turnips were moving, it was my stomach rumbling. I ran all the way to the Great Square to warn Mélusine. She sounded the alert. The whole town turned up in the fields, with nets, baskets and swords. Nothing was moving. I made soup for everyone, to apologise. Mélusine shouted: “SOUP ALERT!” Everybody stayed.
textes.Le jour où j'ai dit que son poisson n'ét: The day I said her fish wasn't fresh, Moloka threw a sardine right in my face. I smelled it: it was fresh. The next day, I came back with a bouquet of ember flowers to apologise. She looked at the flowers, then at me, and said: “Well, those at least are fresh.” I knew she was the one.
textes.Le jour où j'ai découvert les rimes, j'a: The day I discovered rhymes, I jumped for joy in the middle of the library shouting “Moon! June!” Murmure went “shh” at me. Then, very softly, she added: “…spoon.” It was the first rhyme I'd ever heard from someone else. I've never forgotten it.
textes.Le jour où j'ai décrété le troisième ban: The day I decreed the third bench protocolary, Tempo came and sat on it at ten p.m. sharp, to tease me. I drafted a decree to evict him. By the time I'd written it, it was five past ten: he'd gone to bed. He had already won.
textes.Le jour où j'ai failli passer rang E, Li: The day I almost made rank E, Lison was there, on the bank. When the frog swallowed me, she fired a single arrow, which made the frog sneeze. It spat me out. Lison held out her hand and said: “A miss. Not you.” Then she gave me a cake. That's the longest sentence she's ever said to me.
textes.Le jour où j'ai gagné au bras de fer, gr: The day I won the arm-wrestle thanks to my sneeze, Brunehaut laughed so loud that the whole Lower Town came out to look. She was white from head to toe. She looked like my sister. She lifted me off the ground and spun me round, shouting: “The champion! The flour champion!” I've never been so embarrassed. Or so happy.
textes.Le jour où j'ai inauguré le pont de l'ou: The day I opened the west bridge, Bedaine wanted to cross first, belly out, very proud. The wind got up. The bridge danced. The stones sang. And Bedaine turned all green! Seasick, on a bridge! Since then, he crosses it with his eyes shut, humming to drown out the stones.
textes.Le jour où j'ai parlé des signes sous la: The day I talked about the signs under the keel, Matthias ran to the pontoon with a notebook, no shoes on, and asked me forty questions. I said: “Come and see.” He swims badly. He came anyway, with a rope round his waist. He saw. He came up crying. He says it was the salt water.
textes.Le jour où j'ai perdu ma baguette, j'ai: The day I lost my wand, I had only one idea: hide my hands behind my back every time Zéphyr flew by. He carries everything to the queen, that chatterbox. Even secrets. Especially secrets. My arms ached for weeks.
textes.Le jour où j'ai quitté la Garde, je suis: The day I left the Guard, I went to see Ferronde with my broken sword. I told her: “We need better blades.” She looked at the sword, the hilt, then the bucket I was still holding. She said: “Tell me.” I didn't tell her anything. She forged me my first blade to sell. For free. The only time.
textes.Le jour où j'ai quitté la cave d'Ulfa, j: The day I left Ulfa's cellar, I came up to the terrace with a sack of barley and red eyes. Dagna looked at me, said “You're hungry”, and opened up her old bread oven for me. It only heats on one side. Hot side, I make fizz. Cold side, I sleep. It suits us fine.
textes.Le jour où j'ai reçu la peau du jaguar,: The day I received the jaguar skin, I felt as strong as the first sun. I wore it in the square. A child cried, a dog barked, and an old woman threw a flatbread at me so I'd leave her alone. I ate it. It wasn't the triumph I'd planned. But I am a jaguar warrior. And I still eat the flatbreads.
textes.Le jour où j'ai sauté, c'est lui qui m'a: The day I jumped, he's the one who saw me from the top of the crow's nest: a red-headed speck in the mist. The crew was still asleep. He threw the rope, hauled me aboard and put his jacket over my shoulders. Then he climbed back up to his lookout without a word. Nobody found me until noon, sitting on a cannon.
textes.Le jour où j'ai trempé une lame rouge da: The day I quenched a red-hot blade in Dagna's cauldron, I thought I was done for. Dagna was coming, ladle raised. Borin stepped in front of me, arms spread wide, and said: “It was for the salt.” Nobody had ever stood up for me like that. That evening, he made me sweep twice. Fair's fair.
textes.Le jour où j'ai voulu raser la Conserver: The day I wanted to demolish the Cannery, Mrs Barricade was sitting in front of the door, with a twelve-metre scarf. I went to speak to her in person. She looked at me and asked: “Are you eating properly, Aldric?” I lost all my words. I left with the bulldozers. I've never gone back to talk to her alone.
textes.Le jour où j'ai été nommé maître de la G: The day I was made Guild master, I gave a speech. Halfway through, Rissole raised her ladle and shouted: “You've lost weight!” The whole hall laughed. I cried, of course. She served me a slice in front of everyone. I finished my speech with my mouth full. It was my best speech.
textes.Le jour où j'avais de la fièvre, Noisett: The day I had a fever, Noisette ran the bakery all by herself. She'd put on my apron, which came down to her feet. She sold three loaves to the castle, a burnt croissant to Aurore, and asked every customer a question. In the evening, there was more money in the till than usual. People had paid for the questions.
textes.Le jour où j'étais coincée au deuxième p: The day I was stuck on the second floor, everyone was at the market. Nobody could hear me. And then Auntie came. Three leaps. She tucked me under her arm like a skewer, and hop, down. She just said: “… Shh.” Mummy doesn't know anything. Auntie and me have a secret.
textes.Le jour où j'étais malade, c'est Noisett: The day I was ill, Noisette ran the shop. Aurore arrived running, out of breath, because the Baron had put on his mourning hat. Noisette sold her three loaves, a burnt croissant and a question: “Why does the Baron need bread to not be sad?” Aurore replied: “Because it's yours.” Noisette repeated it to me. I cried.
textes.Le jour où je l'ai découvert, il portait: The day I discovered him, he was carrying four crates at the port. I shouted at him: “YOU'RE GOING TO BE A CHAMPION!” He got such a fright he dropped everything. Ash eggs all over the quay. I paid for the eggs. The whole port was laughing. He was apologising to the eggs. I knew at that moment I hadn't been wrong.
textes.Le jour où je suis allé la voir pour la: The day I went to see her about the lamplighter job, I only said three words. She talked for an hour: wicks, oils, ladders, temperamental street lamps. At the end, she said: “You don't talk much.” I answered: “No.” She laughed: “Perfect, I'll talk for two.” It's still true.
textes.Le jour où je suis allé pêcher au lac av: The day I went fishing on the lake with him, the Duchess surfaced right next to the boat. A head as big as a barrel, golden eyes. I said “Good day, Madam” because that's what you say to great ladies. She dived. Yvon looked at me like I was a hero. I was shaking so much my cap fell in the water. He didn't notice.
textes.Le jour où je suis arrivé à Port-Coutela: The day I arrived in Port-Coutelas, without a penny and with a brand-new leg, she served me a hot grog and a plate of stew, and said: “You'll pay when you can.” I've never forgotten it. That doesn't stop me from leaving by the back window when I see her coming. You can respect someone and run away from them.
textes.Le jour où je suis arrivé, Mamie m'a ten: The day I arrived, Mamie handed me the keys to the old kitchen without even asking my name. I opened up, saw the big rusty pot, and said: “It was waiting for me.” Mamie replied: “So was I.” I scrubbed it all night. The next day, it was gleaming.
textes.Le jour où je suis arrivée sur la place,: The day I arrived on the square, at fifteen, only one coin fell into my hat: his. He said to me: “Come and play behind my stories.” I answered that I didn't know his stories. He said: “Neither do I, I make them up as I go.” We started that very evening.
textes.Le jour où je suis devenu garde, j'avais: The day I became a guard, I was twenty-five, with ears too stiff. Mère-Lune climbed up to the Lookout. She still climbed, back then. She tied this red scarf round my neck: “So they can see you from afar, little one. A guard should be seen.” Thirty years I've worn it. The moths tried. They lost.
textes.Le jour où je suis devenu novice, le Rév: The day I became a novice, the Reverend gave me my colander. It was too big. It slipped down over my eyes during the ceremony. Everyone laughed, me too. The Reverend said: “You'll grow into it.” That was a year ago. I've grown one centimetre. It hasn't.
textes.Le jour où je suis entré au temple, elle: The day I joined the temple, she walked me to the door to make sure I wouldn't run away. On the threshold I asked her: “And what if I fall asleep during my sermons?” She said: “Then I'll come and wake you.” She comes every Sunday. She sits in the front row. She's always kept her promises.
textes.Le jour où je suis entrée dans sa boutiq: The day I walked into his shop with my silent alarm clock, Tic didn't listen to me for a second. He was repairing a clock and looking at me at the same time. That evening, he handed me a watch that ran backwards, saying: “Sorry, I was thinking of something else.” I asked what. He said: “Of you.” The silent alarm clock, I never sold it.
textes.Le jour où je suis parti des Mines pour: The day I left the Mines for the Fronde, he didn't say a thing. He just gave me his old miner's stethoscope. I use it to tune Bricole's organ. He doesn't know. He'd be pleased, I think.
textes.Le jour où je suis revenue, il y a vingt: The day I came back, twenty years ago, I walked along the quay with my bag. An old woman was mending, head down. She didn't look at me. She said: “You still walk like a cabin girl.” Forty years! She'd recognised my step after forty years. I had to sit down on a crate.
textes.Le jour où je suis tombée dans le canal: The day I fell into the canal right at high tide, I kept dancing in the water, and Mum kept singing. Nausicaa laughed so hard she missed her verse. The only time in her life she's ever missed a verse. I remind her often. Very often.
textes.Le jour où l'engrenage est tombé, j'ai c: The day the gear fell, I shouted my questions down to Gonzague from the top of the railing. Eighty metres of cliff between us. “Did you see it? Was it golden? Which way was it rolling?” And from below, Gonzague answered: “Ho!” Always “Ho!”. My throat was on fire all evening. But he could hear me. That, I'm sure of.
textes.Le jour où la Doyenne m'a demandé de l'é: The day the Elder asked me to marry her, for a laugh, I stood frozen for eleven minutes. When I came back to myself, I said: “It is twelve minutes past two.” She burst out laughing. Since then, every year, at twelve minutes past two, I bring her a cup of tea. Without a word.
textes.Le jour où la Ligne a rouvert, Maman m'a: The day the Line reopened, Mum took me to Hautefond. When we came out of the Column, there was a blue ceiling, way up high, with no rock. I thought it was going to fall. I hid behind Mum. A girl with pockets full of bolts told me: “It never falls. I check every morning.” It was Pimprenelle. I believed her straight away.
textes.Le jour où la Ligne a rouvert, j'étais a: The day the Line reopened, I was in the front row on Cogwheel Square. The folk from up top stepped out of the cabin blinking. I looked at every child. There was a little redhead! My heart went three quick knocks. It wasn't her. It was somebody's niece. I tapped a long scrape on a bench. Good night, anyway.
textes.Le jour où la Zahra est sortie du chanti: The day the Zahra came out of the boatyard, all blue, Zohra looked at her for a long time. Then she said: “The eye's cross-eyed.” The whole quay laughed. I defended the boat, I defended Ali. But it's true, it is a little cross-eyed. Zohra says that's why I never bring her any sea bream: my boat can't see them.
textes.Le jour où la cabine s'est arrêtée avec: The day the car stopped with the mayor of Port-Azur inside, I ran all the way from the Academy, monocle askew. Ernest was at the station, white as a sheet, shouting at the mayor not to lean out. By the time I got there, his niece was already climbing the cable. Écrou freed the brake. I straightened my monocle. Each to her own trade.
textes.Le jour où la cascade s'est presque arrê: The day the waterfall nearly stopped, two years ago, Honorine came with all her buckets, and we watered the Gardens all night, just the two of us. In the morning, she made soup for the two of us. I've never had better.
textes.Le jour où la corde a cassé, elle avait: The day the rope snapped, she was sixteen. She braided the sixth rope all night, with Granny Faîne. Me, next to them, forging the hooks. All night. Not a word. Her neither, not a word. The only time. In the morning, the rope held. The hooks too. Hm. Good night, that one.
textes.Le jour où la corde a cassé, il y a dix: The day the rope snapped, ten years ago, the basket dropped all at once. Hulotte inside. Bourru caught the rope with his bare hands. I grabbed an iron bar and jammed the pulley. We said nothing to each other. Not that day, not after. But I know. And he knows.
textes.Le jour où la corde de la nacelle a cass: The day the basket rope snapped, I treated Bourru's paws, burnt by the rope. Ursule stood behind me, without a word, holding the pot of balm. When I'd finished, I saw her eyes. She'd been crying. She doesn't know I saw. She never will. That's why I forgive her for the hot water. Almost.
textes.Le jour où la ligne des Strates a rouver: The day the Strata line reopened, I laughed so hard with joy that, apparently, they heard me all the way down in the Fronde. They wrote to invite me to their Assembly. I replied: “I vote for everything!” HA HA! It's more fun that way.
textes.Le jour où la ligne du bas rouvrira, voi: The day the lower line reopens: to see the people from up here come down to the Fronde, dance with the people from down there, and the Burgomaster give a speech under a circled-A banner. With a mohawk. Well, with the brooch, at least.
textes.Le jour où la machine à pluie du Profess: The day the Professor's rain machine went “pop”, everyone was laughing. Giant bubbles were floating over the Agora. The Professor was in despair. I climbed onto a bench, pointed at a bubble and said: “That one's a house.” He looked at me as if I were mad. That evening, I was sleeping in it.
textes.Le jour où le Baron a voulu offrir la Gr: The day the Baron tried to give the Great Square to a merchant, it was the Captain who escorted the merchant to the North Gate, with his guards, very politely. The merchant thought it was a guard of honour. He waved all the way. Afterwards Ferdinand told me: “It was by the book.” I think it's the only time I've seen him smile.
textes.Le jour où le capitaine pirate est venu: The day the pirate captain came to negotiate his berth at the quay, I wanted to say a word, a little word, just for atmosphere. Moulay Brahim looked at me. Not a word. Just a look. I shut up. Me! Saïd the Voice! That day, I understood why he's the amin, and not me.
textes.Le jour où le crocodile a piétiné son ch: The day the crocodile trampled his field, Hapou brought me his wet barley, apologising. It sprouted in the sack. Sprouted barley is the best for beer! I made the finest jar of my whole life. I called it “crocodile beer”. Hapou refuses to drink it. On principle. He's had two.
textes.Le jour où le labo a pris feu, un peu, R: The day the lab caught fire, a little, Rosette was already there with her notebook. The next day, the headline: “Électre Lights Up Her Lab… and Her Curtains”. The whole city laughed. I bought twenty copies. To light the stove. Well, also a bit to laugh.
textes.Le jour où le maire est resté coincé, Hé: The day the mayor got stuck, Héloïse came running to the top station, her long dress hitched up in one hand, her monocle all askew. She looked at the cable, then at my little Écrou, who was already climbing it. She didn't shout. She just said: “She's right. It's the brake.” The next day, she offered her a place at the Academy.
textes.Le jour où les abeilles d'en haut ont es: The day the bees up top swarmed, Gilwen couldn't climb: she's afraid of heights. I went up with her basket. I brought the swarm back. Forty stings. She said thank you, then she said I'd shaken them about. She's right. But I brought them back.
textes.Le jour où ma chèvre a dormi sur son trô: The day my goat slept on his throne, he summoned me to the Great Hall. I was trembling. He said: “A shepherdess whose goat finds the way to the throne all by herself knows how to lead.” And he put me in charge of his messenger crows. I never admitted the goat had simply got lost.
textes.Le jour où mon grand-père lui a vendu le: The day my grandfather sold him the logbook, I was fourteen and crying in the square. Ba Sidi, young and skinny back then, gave me a date and said: “Paper can be sold, little one. The story stays with you.” I ate the date. I hated him for twenty years. Then I understood.
textes.Le jour où mon navet s'est sauvé de sa m: The day my turnip escaped from his pot, Ulric chased it right across the Middle Town. I saw him go past the bakery, ladle in the air, hat askew, shouting: “Come back, you ingrate!” The turnip ran round the fountain three times. So did Ulric. The whole town was applauding. He brought it back holding it against his chest, like a baby.
textes.Le jour où mon neuvième toit s'est envol: The day my ninth roof flew off, it came down in one piece on the terrace of the Crankshaft. Nobody hurt! Gaston was serving a coffee at that very moment. He didn't spill a drop. He looked at the roof, he looked at the cup, and he said: “That'll make some shade.” Since then, it's been the awning. I have lunch under it. It's a bit like home.
textes.Le jour où nous nous sommes rencontrées,: The day we met, Violette cast a lightning bolt, which hit her, which made her jump, which made me jump, and I fell into the fountain. She held out her hand to help me. Her fingers were still sparking. I got zapped. We laughed for an hour, soaking wet and frizzy-haired. We've been friends ever since.
textes.Le jour où on a allumé les premiers néon: The day they switched on the first neon lights, the whole city came out into the street. People were crying, laughing, taking photos. Me, I was looking at their faces, all pink and all blue. It was more beautiful than the neon.
textes.Le jour où on a fermé la ligne pour chan: The day they closed the line to replace the glass tube, I thought it would be for a year. It lasted twelve. Every morning, I went down to the station, polished the cabin, pulled the lever for nothing, and shouted “Everybody out!” into the emptiness. One day, I counted: three thousand two hundred times, for nobody. I don't regret a single one. The lanternfish, at least, never missed one.
textes.Le jour où on a inauguré son pont de l'o: The day we opened her west bridge, the whole village crossed it singing. The bridge swayed, the stones whistled… and me, in the middle, I got seasick. Seasick, my friend, over a pond! Since then, I cross it with my eyes shut. Pomme-de-Pin still laughs about it. My stomach's still up in my whiskers.
textes.Le jour où on a remorqué le galion des p: The day we towed the pirates' galleon into the harbour with ten boats, a big bald pirate had the anchor dropped too early. It landed right on my big green net, which was soaking at the edge of the quay. A hole like a door. Three weeks of mending. Every week I send the pirate the bill. His name is Mâchefer. He's never paid.
textes.Le jour où on a soufflé ensemble sur le: The day we blew on the mill together, a sail moved. Just a tiny bit. Maybe the wind. Maybe us. Gaubert looked at me, I looked at Gaubert, and we said nothing. In the evening, Germaine asked us why we looked so pleased. Gaubert said: “We made the mill turn.” She didn't believe us.
textes.Le jour où on lui a donné son nom, Dwali: On his naming day, Dwalin grabbed my ladle from his cradle and wouldn't let go. His father said: “He'll be a cook.” He carries coal. But every day, he stops by my kitchen and holds the ladle for a minute. He says it rests his back.
textes.Le jour où on m'a nommé capitaine, j'ai: The day I was made captain, I ordered new armour from the Great Forge. The master blacksmith laughed at everything I said. I never make jokes. I went back every day for a month to check on the armour. In the end she married me, so I'd stop checking.
textes.Le jour où papa a perdu son appareil, il: The day Daddy lost his camera, he sat down next to my castle and looked at it. With his eyes. He said: “The left tower's leaning a bit.” He'd noticed! He even helped dig the moat. He's got big hands, it goes faster. He laughed when the wave came. Me too.
textes.Le jour où quarante pains de miel sont t: The day forty honey loaves fell off the footbridge, Taeron came running, looked at the plank and said: “Nothing wrong with it.” Then he took it out, carried it home, and never put it back. I say that's proof. He says it's a keepsake.
textes.Le jour où sa mère lui a passé la bousso: The day her mother handed her the Kerhervé compass, Morgane came to the tavern alone, in the evening, in a uniform too big for her. She asked for a sparkling apple and didn't say a word. I sat beside her until closing time. We said nothing. The next day, she was the Admiral.
textes.Le jour où son masque de plongée s'est f: The day her diving mask cracked, I gave her the best one on the stall, saying she'd pay me in pearls. She never did, and I never asked for anything. A diver without a mask is a merchant without pearls. It's business. There. Business.
textes.Le jour où tu es arrivé avec son épée, j: The day you showed up with his sword, I took it, weighed it, rang it on the anvil. A good sound. I said “not bad, for a big'un”, and I spent the night forging a better one. Fundin was asleep standing up against the bellows. Me, I was smiling. It was a good night.
textes.Le jour où tu es arrivé, Triton a couru: The day you arrived, Triton ran all the way to my workshop shouting: “A human! A real one!” Then he realised he'd left the Gate.
