First time in three hundred years. He dashed off so fast he knocked over three of my lamps. I billed him for them. Friend's price: double.
textes.Le jour où tu es arrivé, j'ai couru l'an: The day you arrived, I ran to tell Coralin. The square, two bridges, his workshop… and then it hit me: I'd left the Gate. First time in three hundred years. I dashed back so fast I knocked over three of his lamps. He billed me for them. Friend's price: double.
The day you hold the key.
textes.Le jour où un gros navet a foncé sur Mél: The day a big turnip charged at Mélusine and stopped dead when it heard her shout, it threw itself into my net all on its own. Gaubert says it was thanks to her voice. I say it was thanks to my net. Mélusine settled it, on the square: “IT'S A COLLABORATION!” We shared the turnip. Well, we gave it to Ulric.
textes.Le jour où une grenouille a volé sa barq: The day a frog stole his boat, Yvon stayed three days on the shore waiting for it to leave. I brought him food, three times a day. Roast frog. He ate it watching the boat, and the frog in the boat watched him eat. It was the tensest meal in the history of La Grenouille Repue.
textes.Le jour où une soucoupe de passage a vou: The day a passing saucer tried to sell me a broken engine for a fortune, Ionie happened by, took one look and said: “It's dead.” The merchant left with his engine. She winked at me and went back to the Spaceport. She never asked me for anything in return.
textes.Le jour où une soucoupe s'est écrasée co: The day a saucer crashed into the Spire, Ionie and I did the repairs together, all night long. She held the soldering iron, I held the tablet. We didn't exchange ten words. By morning, the Spire was intact, and so was the saucer. She said: “Good team.” I said: “Bzzt.”
textes.Le jour tombe. Vous qui avez un peu peur: Day is falling. You who are a little afraid of the dark: look up. It's turning. I'm up there.
textes.Le jour, j'aime m'allonger contre les en: In the daytime, I like lying up against the speakers. It's a back massage.
textes.Le jour, je classe, je tape, je note. Le: By day, I file, I type, I take notes. In the evening, I put on a cardboard moustache and go moshing at the back of the pit. Sirène keeps a violet lemonade for me. Velours sewed me a lining full of badges. On Thursdays, I meet Sirène at the lighthouse to swap recipes. Mr Lisse knows nothing. I think.
In the daytime I sleep standing up. Forgive me.
textes.Le jour, je dors un peu. Le soir, je vis: By day, I sleep a little. By night, I live.
textes.Le jour, je joue sur la place, j'achète: By day, I play in the square, I buy my cacao at the tianguis, I teach songs to the children. In the evening, it's party time: the drums, the dancers, the stars. Citlali sings, Coyotl keeps an eye on his pots, Pilli dances with his dog. And Mixtli dances too. With two left feet. Very seriously.
textes.Le jour, je suis au stand 5. Le soir, je: By day, I'm at stand 5. In the evening, I sit at table 2 in the Bielle, across from Tacquet, and we play. Me, in person. No automaton. I lose on time nearly every evening; he records it in a notebook. This year, I'm a juror at the Fair. Héloïse wants to hand out prizes like biscuits. I've had my disagreement entered in the minutes.
textes.Le jour, je vais de stand en stand. Le j: By day, I go from stall to stall. The jury asks my opinion; I always answer: “I hadn't thought of that.” It's true, too. On Prudence's piano, a brass plaque says the page-turner was my idea. One day I took the Zéphyr to a place with no inventions: Carène. They had sparkling apple. In the evening, the bench with Basile, then the promenade with Prudence.
textes.Le jour, je vérifie. Les câbles, le sabl: By day, I check. The cables, the sand in the knobs, the crabs in Raoul. By night, I nod my head next to Gaspard. When Mistral sleeps, I mind the desk. I don't change anything. A good sound, you don't change it. You keep it. Like a friend. … That was long, what I just said.
textes.Le jour, l'épicerie. Le soir, une tisane: By day, the shop. In the evening, a herbal tea at the café and a novel hidden behind the newspaper. I vote against the mayor. Rita foretells a great love for me, I pay. An English lord wants my jar of figs, I refuse. And a tourist blushed when I recommended my favourite novel to her. People are odd. Me, I'm normal.
textes.Le jour, la librairie. À l'heure dorée,: By day, the bookshop. At the golden hour, the lookout, where Clémence paints while I watch. I sold all my charts of the seabed to Professor Moreau, one by one. Madame Rita makes predictions for me, which I note down in a notebook. And I've received an old atlas of the Sky Kings: apparently there was once an island that flew! Can you imagine?
textes.Le journal du dernier capitaine du Lévia: The journal of the last captain of the Léviathan, bound in leather that still smells of salt. Whole pages are blank… Moon ink, Ba Sidi used to say: it can only be read by the light of a moon you carry with you.
textes.Le jour… C'est bien, aussi. Les couleurs: Day… That's nice too. The colours, the sun. I don't know it very well. Will you tell me about it? I'll tell you about the night.
textes.Le jury ? Oh ! Écoutez… (Le piano joue u: The jury? Oh! Listen… (The piano plays a waltz. The keys press themselves down. At the end, the piano takes a bow.) It plays better in the morning. It's a bit under the weather in the evening.
textes.Le jury de la Foire cherche des avis. Hé: The Fair jury is gathering opinions. Héloïse is asking everyone what they think of the inventions. I always have the same opinion: I hadn't thought of that.
The jury sent me to see your automaton.
The jury sent me to see your machine.
The jury sent me to see your piano.
textes.Le lac ! Les grenouilles géantes ! Qu'el: The lake! The giant frogs! Let them come: I, SIRE TANCRÈDE DE TOURNEVENT, await them!
textes.Le lac est calme, les grenouilles se tie: The lake is calm, the frogs are behaving, Yvon brought me a beauty this morning. What a leg! As big as my arm! I made fritters for the whole neighbourhood.
textes.Le lac est calme. Trop calme. Je n'aime: The lake is calm. Too calm. I don't like it when it's calm. They're up to something.
textes.Le lac… Je reste loin du bord. Très loin: The lake… I'm staying far from the edge. Very far. Here's good. No, there's better.
textes.Le lait de nuage, je l'ai inventé par ac: I invented cloud milk by accident. I was whisking vanilla milk on the terrace, the wind got up, and the froth swelled and swelled until it spilled over the cup like a little cumulus. A customer shouted: “It's a cloud!” I changed my name the next day. Cumulus floats better than Bouilloire, which means “kettle”.
textes.Le lait de nuage, ça donne une moustache: Cloud milk gives you a white moustache. I've already got three.
textes.Le larsen, c'est mon pire ennemi et mon: Feedback is my worst enemy and my best friend. When it squeals, it means the mic hears the speaker that hears it… An endless loop. Like two old ladies who don't talk anymore and think about each other all the time.
textes.Le lendemain de la démonstration, Margot: The day after the demonstration, Margot brought me a drawing of my engine. Very precise: the crank, the flywheel, every cog. And in the middle, in place of the golden gear, she'd drawn a heart. I don't know what it means. I pinned it up above the stand. People ask me. I say it's the diagram.
textes.Le lendemain de la grande tempête, la ba: The day after the big storm, Marley's banana grove was flattened. He was sitting in front of it, smiling anyway, which was worse than if he'd cried. I came with ropes. We stood every plant back up, one by one, for two days. He talked to every banana tree like a cousin.
textes.Le lendemain de la plage, en faisant la: The day after the beach, doing room seven, I found Léa's pillow soaking wet. Not seawater, mind: tears. I turned it to the dry side before she came back. That's what a chambermaid is for, too. And for keeping quiet, normally. Normally.
textes.Le lendemain de la première brioche cass: The day after the first brioche I broke for Pépin, I found a jar of fire cinnamon on my counter. Without a word. Zébuline was at her stall, serving a customer. She didn't look at me. Since then, every month, a jar appears. I've never thanked her. I break the brioches a little bigger.
textes.Le lendemain de la tempête, j'étais assi: The day after the storm, I was sitting in front of my flattened banana trees, smiling, because that's what I do. Gaspard turned up with ropes. He said: “You're smiling too much, it worries me.” We stood everyone back up in two days. At the end, I cried a little. He handed me his water bottle, of course.
textes.Le lendemain de ma nuit jusqu'à l'aube,: The day after my night until dawn, the fish auction was empty. Not a crate, not a sardine. Saïd on his platform, mouth open, with nothing to call out. Moulay Brahim came to my house at noon. I was asleep. He waited for me to wake up, sitting on my chair, and he said a single word: “Midnight.”
textes.Le lendemain de notre rencontre, je lui: The day after we met, I brought him a scarf woven from the seaweed he'd told me off for cutting. He was speechless for so long I thought I'd upset him. Then he asked: “How many did you cut?” I said: “One in three.” He married me the following year.
textes.Le lendemain de sa nuit, à dix heures, l: The day after his night, at ten o'clock, the fish market was empty. Not one crate. The fishermen were asleep in their boats, out at sea, with the festival still in their legs. Saïd climbed onto his platform, opened his mouth… and had nothing to shout. I'd never seen him speechless. I went to Lhoucine's and waited for him to wake up. I said: “Midnight.”
textes.Le lendemain du marais, Brutus est venu: The day after the marsh, Brutus came to see me at Doc's. He looked at my arm. He left without a word. That very evening, I had this hook, forged from the iron of an old anchor, polished like a mirror. He never wanted to be paid. I insisted. He took an iron bar and bent it. I stopped insisting.
textes.Le lendemain du soir où Séraphine est de: The day after the evening Séraphine became archmage, she handed me her light class. For my first lesson as a master, I wanted to do well. Very well. The whole Astrelune Tower started shining like a sun, in the middle of the night. The town woke up, Berthe served breakfast at midnight. I apologised to every single inhabitant. It took me a week.
textes.Le lendemain, Gaspard est venu sur le qu: The next day, Gaspard came to the quay, all sheepish, with a spool of blue thread. He held it out to me and covered the parrot with a handkerchief. I took the spool. I'm still a bit cross with him. But the thread is very good: strong, supple, a lovely blue. I mended a whole sardine net with it.
textes.Le lendemain, Pauline a plié les serviet: The next day, Pauline folded the towels in number seven into hearts. And the day after. A whole week of terry-cloth hearts: on the bed, on the washbasin, on the balcony railing. I said nothing. I'm still cross with her. A little less with every heart.
textes.Le lendemain, Pip est revenu à mon étal: The next day, Pip came back to my stall with three coins to get green hair too, “to match the ears”. I said no. You don't mess around with failed potions: I'm a professional. He went off all sad. I gave him a blackberry juice. Free. That one never works.
textes.Le lendemain, elle est descendue à la ré: The next day, she came down to reception, her eyes still red, and said to me: “Thank the management for me.” I replied: “I shall not fail to, madam.” I felt my ears go hot. Apparently she calls me “the gentleman with the moustache who sympathises”. I'm flattered. Discreetly.
textes.Le lendemain, il est revenu avec la couv: The next day, he came back with the blanket from his bed, rolled up under his arm. For the stones, he said, because they don't like being alone in the dark. I had told him that sentence. He had kept it. I laid the blanket on the smallest one. I told no one. She seems to sleep well.
textes.Le lendemain, il m'a couru après sur le: The next day he ran after me on the quay with a purse. He wanted to give me money back. “It was too expensive! Take it back! Haggle!” I said no. He insisted. I said no. He nearly cried. A merchant who wants to give money back. Thirty years at sea, never seen that. Hm.
textes.Le lendemain, il m'a offert un seau. Un: The next day, he gave me a bucket. A lovely blue bucket, with a ribbon: “For the great voyage, navigator.” I put it in the bookshop window, under the globe. Customers ask what it's doing there. I reply: “It's my equipment.”
textes.Le lendemain, je lui ai couru après sur: The next day, I ran after him on the quay, a purse in my hand. “It was too expensive! Take it back! Let's start again!” He said no. I insisted. He said no. The whole quay watched a merchant begging a pirate to get robbed a little less. I've never been so humiliated. Or so honest.
textes.Le lendemain, je suis descendue à la réc: The next day, I went down to reception to thank “the management”. The gentleman with the moustache straightened up, went red to the ears and said: “The management takes note, madame.” Then he tidied the same pen three times. I think the management was him.
textes.Le lendemain, je suis retourné la voir p: The next day, I went back to see her to get green hair too, to match the ears. She said no. She said she was a professional. A professional of failed potions! That's not a thing. She gave me a blackberry juice instead. It was good.
textes.Le lendemain, mon père a changé l'enseig: The next day, my father changed the sign. He said: “Since they come to eat at our place, we'll eat them at our place.” I was twelve. I cooked my first giant frog leg that day. It jumped out of the pan and went off down the street. I caught it in front of the Guild. Mamie Rissole was laughing.
textes.Le lin, on l'arrache, on le rouit dans l: Flax: you pull it up, you ret it in water, you beat it, you comb it, you spin it, you weave it. Nine months of work for one dress. Like for a baby, they say. Except a dress doesn't beg for dates.
textes.Le lundi où je n'avais d'huile que pour: The Monday I only had oil for one of his horns, he went to the gala with one shiny horn and one dull one, and told everyone: “It's asymmetric fashion.” Three courtiers came to see me the following week. I offered him a year of free polishing. He refused. He paid. He said: “Acceptable.”
textes.Le maire ? Hm. Il envoie tout le monde m: The mayor? Hm. He sends everyone to say hello to me. Fine. Hello. The port is yours, don't get up to any mischief.
textes.Le maire chante sous la douche. On l'ent: The mayor sings in the shower. You can hear him from the harbour.
textes.Le maire chante sous sa douche ; on l'en: The mayor sings in the shower; you can hear him from the port. I told him he had the voice of a seal with a cold. I stand by it. Officially.
textes.Le maire cherche des gens serviables. Il: The mayor is looking for helpful people. He pays in smiles and coins, which is rare for a mayor.
textes.Le maire fera citoyen d'honneur celui qu: The mayor will make whoever helps out the whole town an honorary citizen.
The mayor sent me to say hello.
textes.Le maire me doit une pomme depuis quaran: The mayor has owed me an apple for forty years. I vote against him. It isn't a grudge, it's bookkeeping.
textes.Le maire parle très bien. Il promet très: The mayor speaks very well. He promises very well too. The clock was to be repaired “before the end of the year”: fourteen times. I have a notebook.
textes.Le maire veut que je fasse connaissance: The mayor wants me to get to know the town: the harbour master's office, the hotel and the tavern.
textes.Le maire, je l'ai connu serveur : douze: The mayor, I knew him as a waiter: twelve cups on the first day. He's become a good mayor. A bit long-winded in his speeches, but still.
textes.Le manche est léger comme une plume. La: The wheel is light as a feather. The Dragonfly responds at once: she sways from side to side on her mooring mast, delighted. “She likes you,” says a voice behind you. “She only does that with real pilots.”
textes.Le manomètre est dans le vert. Le vert f: The pressure gauge is in the green. The dark green.
textes.Le marais. N'y va pas. Ou si tu y vas, r: The marsh. Don't go there. Or if you do, watch the water. Not the sky, not the trees: the water. It's out of the water that they come.
textes.Le marchand de tapis. Il parle. Beaucoup: The carpet seller. He talks. A lot. He wants me to haggle. I don't haggle. Hm. It makes him ill.
textes.Le marché est dans la cale du Léviathan,: The market is in the Léviathan's hold, at the back. By day, you come in through the great breach on the beach side. Beyond the stalls, the hold is underwater: that's the basin, where the boats come in.
textes.Le marché est plein, aujourd'hui. Rosali: The market's packed today. Rosalie must have announced some fresh gossip.
textes.Le marché, c'est au nord-est de la Basse: The market is in the north-east of the Lower Town. My stall is the only one without spice smoke. Well, it should be.
textes.Le masque des Rois-Ciel : tu respires so: The Sky Kings' mask: you can breathe underwater! Explore the depths… southwest of the village, a light shines at the bottom.
textes.Le masque des Rois-Ciel, trouvé dans le: The mask of the Sky Kings, found in Lord Storm's treasure: crystal lenses rimmed with brass. As long as it's in your bag, you can breathe underwater. The Sky Kings used it to visit… a sunken city?
textes.Le matin après l'Averse, la plage avait: The morning after the Downpour, the beach had built a castle all by itself. With towers! Dad says the rain packed the sand down. I think the beach was bored.
textes.Le matin après le rocher, j'étais assis: The morning after the rock, I was sitting on the sand, soaked, my hammer on my knees. A raft of rolled-up maps drifted past offshore, Barnabé on top, shouting: “The map was right!” I shouted: “Row!” Those were the last kind words we said to each other.
textes.Le matin de la lumière bleue, toute la t: The morning of the blue light, the whole tavern was laughing at Grégoire. I had him come up to the harbour office, made him tell it all twice, and marked the spot with an ink cross on the big map. I didn't smile. I didn't feel like it at all. Since then, every evening, I look in that direction.
textes.Le matin de la réouverture, elle avait p: On the morning of the reopening, she'd spent the night in the tunnel checking every rail. At seven, she came out covered in grease and said: “It'll hold.” I gave her a big hug. My station master's jacket stayed black for a week. I didn't wash it. It's a medal.
textes.Le matin de la réouverture, elle m'a ten: On the morning of the reopening, she handed me the departure key without a word. I understood at once. She's the only person in the Strata I've never said “Pardon?” to.
textes.Le matin de la réouverture, j'avais pass: On the morning of the reopening, I'd spent the night in the tunnel checking every rail. At seven, I came out covered in grease. Marius gave me a big hug. His jacket stayed black for a week. He refused to wash it. He says it's a medal. I find that very unhygienic. And very sweet.
textes.Le matin de mon sacre, je suis allé voir: On the morning of my coronation, I went to see Nori, alone, to ask whether I'd be a good king. He read a rune and said: “You will lose your crown a thousand times and find it a thousand and one.” I thought it was a prophecy. It was an observation. I lose my crown every day.
textes.Le matin du dauphin, Lucas était au bout: The morning of the dolphin, Lucas was at the end of the quay with a crate on his shoulder. He put it down and said “dolphin”. All by himself, without me asking! Then he put me on his shoulders to see if the dolphin came back. It didn't. But from up there you can see all the boats, and even Léon's cap.
textes.Le matin du piano, Ernest était de garde: On the morning of the piano, Ernest was on duty up top. He saw nothing, heard nothing. He says an airship set it down in the fog. I say it fell, ever so gently, like a leaf. A piano, like a leaf, yes. We've been arguing ever since. Nobody has won. The piano says nothing.
textes.Le matin du piano, il y avait un brouill: On the morning of the piano, the fog was thick enough to cut with a knife. Gonzague found it on the quay, intact, with one key missing. I was on duty up top all night, and I saw nothing, heard nothing. My theory: an airship lost it. Gonzague's: it fell “ever so gently”. We've been arguing about it for years. Nobody has won.
textes.Le matin et l'après-midi, je plonge au b: Mornings and afternoons, I dive off the end of the pontoon. At noon, I eat on the dock pontoon, feet in the water. Ewen counts my seconds and gets it wrong. Matthias wants me to draw the stones underwater. With a pencil. In the evening, at the beach fire, I stay quiet. It's my favourite moment.
textes.Le matin et le soir, je joue à la fontai: In the morning and the evening, I play at the fountain. In the afternoon, it's the beach. Sometimes there's Théo, the hotel baby, who cried for days over his kite. And there's Brioche! He's a little all-white dog, I'm the one who named him. He's not mine. Not yet. I threw a coin in the fountain to get a dog. That counts, right?
textes.Le matin où Celebrë avait perdu sa voix,: The morning Celebrë lost her voice, nothing came into my nets. I told her to whistle. She whistled, and three rays came. Ever since, I keep telling her the light prefers whistling, to tease her. It's not true. The light prefers her voice. So do I.
textes.Le matin où Saïd a perdu la voix, plus u: The morning Saïd lost his voice, not a sound, the auction was about to start. He was making desperate signs at me. So I climbed onto his platform and called out the prices for him. Badly. I sold the raw sardines at the price of grilled ones. The fishermen were delighted. Saïd, less so. Since then he shouts “GRILLED SARDIIINES!” for me for free.
textes.Le matin où elle a trouvé son enclos vid: The morning she found her pen empty, by the lake, she wasn't crying. She was furious. She said: “Those jaguars have taste. That was my finest.” I swore to her I'd hunt them. She gave me tamales for the road. The road hasn't started yet. I ate the tamales anyway. She's making me more.
textes.Le matin où j'ai parlé de la lumière ble: The morning I told them about the blue light, the whole tavern was already laughing. The Admiral called me up to the harbour master's office, had me tell it all twice, and marked the spot on her chart with a cross. A cross in ink. She didn't smile once. I'm grateful to her for that.
textes.Le matin où j'ai perdu la voix, Mustapha: The morning I lost my voice, Mustapha dropped his coals and climbed onto my platform. He shouted the prices like someone calling a cat. He sold the raw sardines at the grilled price, and the fishermen carried him in triumph. Since then, I owe him: every evening, I shout “GRILLED SARDIIINES!” for him. Free. And loud.
textes.Le matin où la Murène Noire est entrée d: The morning the Murène Noire sailed into the bay, I went out to meet her in Fañch's boat, standing in the stern. Croc-de-Sel shouted from his deck: “Admiral of what?” I pointed to the smoking gunports: “Of that.” He looked for a long time. Then he came about. As he left, he saluted me with his tricorn. I didn't respond.
textes.Le matin, abordage sur la place avec Yas: In the morning, boarding party on the square with Yasmine. She wins. After, I go and see Tibo, my pal, a real pirate! He's teaching me to swear without rude words. The pirates' parrot, the Admiral, calls me “grouper-head”: that's my nickname now. And in the afternoon, I deliver Karim's babouches. He pays me in dates. I run fast. I get the house a bit wrong.
textes.Le matin, au Parc des Brumes, la brume m: In the morning, in the Mist Park, the mist rises from the Falls and makes shapes. This morning I saw Séraphin in it. He was waving at me. Or it was Doctor Aurèle. They have the same beard.
In the morning, when I wake up.
textes.Le matin, avant d'aller au four, Maman m: In the morning, before going to the oven, Mama kisses me on the forehead, even if I'm asleep. Once, I pretended to be asleep to see. She kissed me and whispered: “Have a good day, my little adventurer.” Since then, I pretend to be asleep every morning. She doesn't know. Well, I think.
textes.Le matin, avant la classe, je m'installe: In the morning, before class, I sit on a bench in the Square while the Great Pearl lights up. I prepare my lesson in my head. And I remember the real sun, the one time I saw it rise. I keep that memory for the days when I need courage.
textes.Le matin, avant tout le monde, je vais à: In the morning, before anyone else, I go to the Observation Bay. The hydrothermal vent is smoking, the giant worms open their red plumes, and the white shrimp dance around them. A whole world waking up without a sun. It makes me humble. Until breakfast.
textes.Le matin, cours dans la cour. L'après-mi: In the morning, lessons in the courtyard. In the afternoon, the library, or the Circle: Ysolde is teaching me the names of the stones. In the evening, I reread. In the dormitory, I read under the covers. Mirabelle keeps an eye on me. Pip talks in his sleep. Oscar snores in time. I cast my spells slowly. They work. Slowly, but they work.
textes.Le matin, dans la réserve, je fais l'inv: In the morning, in the storeroom, I do the inventory: shells, ropes, springs, and zero news. Then I open the door, the first customer comes in, and the news inventory starts up again. It's the best moment of the day.
textes.Le matin, j'ai toujours plein d'idées. L: In the morning I'm full of ideas. By the afternoon, I've forgotten them.
textes.Le matin, j'allume la chaudière de l'ate: In the morning, I light the workshop boiler singing the valve song: “Pssht, pssht, the pressure's rising…” I wrote it myself. Bielle says it'll never make it into a concert. I say that's a shame for concerts.
textes.Le matin, j'allume les fourneaux à cinq: In the morning, I light the stoves at five. The first soup is for the miners, the second for the blacksmiths, the third for little Tom. He comes before everyone else. He doesn't know. He thinks it's chance.
textes.Le matin, j'allume les fours avant tout: In the morning I light the furnaces before anyone else, and I strike the first blow on the anvil: two knocks, then one. Up there, under the Lower Town, Mathilde answers me. Has done for twenty years. That way, we both know the other one's awake.
textes.Le matin, j'entre le premier dans la min: In the morning, I'm the first into the mine. Alone. I switch off my lamp for one minute, and watch the blue crystals light up in the dark. One minute. No more. Then I switch it back on. Safety first. But beauty just before.
textes.Le matin, je bavarde avec Clou sur le po: In the morning, I chat with Clou on the deck of the Freighter, and he nods. In the afternoon, I fall over at the skatepark with Tornade. In the evening, I drink a lemonade at Sirène's with my seagull-shaped straw, and I play bass till midnight. It's the perfect life. With chips.
textes.Le matin, je bois mon thé dans le jardin: In the morning, I drink my tea in the Residences' garden. It's the only quiet moment. Then the Floor folk arrive on the Line, and they chatter, and they take photos, and they go “wow”. Three years without them, and here we are. Well. It livens things up.
textes.Le matin, je cale mes coups de marteau s: In the morning, I time my hammer blows to the drips falling from the vault. Plink, tang, plink, tang. Écho says the vault is the oldest drummer in the Fronde. It's got a head start on me.
textes.Le matin, je commence par le mur des alg: In the morning, I start with the algae wall. Green glass tubes that glow, from floor to ceiling. They make the air we breathe, and the spirulina. I lay my hand on them and say thank you. Every morning. We never say thank you enough to what keeps us breathing.
textes.Le matin, je fais des châteaux devant la: In the morning, I make castles in front of the beach hut. Kiki gives me coconut halves for the towers. Sometimes I go and see Clémence at the lookout, she let me paint a sky. In the evening, at the fountain, there's Nina, she calls me baby. I'm not a baby. And Daddy takes pictures of everything. Well, when he's got his camera.
textes.Le matin, je garde la porte du palais ;: In the morning, I guard the palace gate; then I do my rounds; in the evening, I go home and Ortie makes me recite her lessons. My Archduchess slips off to the market, my sister raises twelve hellhound puppies, and my daughter wants to blow everything up. I'm captain of the Guard. I don't command anyone.
textes.Le matin, je garde les chiots de Flammèc: In the morning, I mind Flammèche's pups while she goes to fetch fish. In the afternoon, I fight in the Arena. In the evening, I soak in the Gorgoth Bath, at the Baths, then I read poems under the lantern. Nox comes by to say good evening. Sometimes, he leaves me a poem. That's my life. It's a good one.
textes.Le matin, je joue sur le quai et dans le: In the morning, I play on the quay and in the village. At noon, I eat at Mum's stall. In the afternoon, I fish with Khéty, but I let everything go. Sometimes I shake the sistrum for Néferet, and sometimes I go to Amenemhat's school. And at the fair of the longest day, I meet up with Kinich, from Yaxché! He has a mosquito. I have a cat. That's better.
textes.Le matin, je joue sur les bancs de la pl: In the morning, I play on the benches in the square; Hortense taps out the beat, more accurate than a metronome. In the evening, the stage at the Perroquet. I live on the Rue Haute, between Lola and Lucas: I hear things, I don't repeat them. The mayor sings in the shower. And a painter drew me with my mouth open, like a grouper. I play in profile.
textes.Le matin, je m'assois au bord du bassin: In the morning, I sit by the pond and watch the mushrooms fall asleep. They glow less when the Brass Sun gets its strength back. Like night lights being switched off. They sleep all day. I work.
textes.Le matin, je m'assois près de la cloche: In the morning, I sit by the bell and tell stories to the seagulls. In the afternoon, at the rail, to the fishermen mending nets. In the evening, by the stove of the Bordée, to anyone who'll listen. Ewen writes my letters, because my hand shakes, and he corrects my stories while he's at it. That boy ruins everything. I adore him.
textes.Le matin, je monte au grand mât et je di: In the morning, I climb the great mast and say hello to every cloud. There's always a new one. I give it a name. This morning: Philibert. A shy little stratus. He dissipated when I called him.
textes.Le matin, je monte sur le balcon de la G: In the morning, I go up to the Guild balcony before anyone else and watch the Brass Sun regain its strength, ring after ring. Then the Forge lights up. Then the Square. By eight o'clock, the Strata are awake. I go down to work.
textes.Le matin, je prépare le Petit Plongeon s: In the morning, I get the Little Diver ready on the Pool quay: I check the ballast tanks, the floodlights, the oxygen, the sandwiches. Especially the sandwiches. A dive without a snack is a failed dive. Pilots' rule number one. I made it up.
textes.Le matin, je prête dix lucioles à Perlée: In the morning, I lend ten fireflies to Perlée for her rounds. In the evening, three to Noisette to sort her seeds. At night, I feed them honey. Zéphyr says they only love me for the honey. He's jealous. Oh, and there's another Lumi, down below, in the elves' roots! We write to each other. Zéphyr mixes us up all the time.
textes.Le matin, je pêche avec Hamid. L'après-m: In the morning, I fish with Hamid. In the afternoon, at the end of the jetty, Si Larbi teaches me patience. Gaspard, from his crow's nest, waves to me when he sees a whale. Every week, I take my coins to Ali for my boat, the Whale: I'm a quarter of the way there. And on the way home, I walk past Halima's stall. By chance. Every day, by chance.
textes.Le matin, je ramasse des coquillages sur: In the morning, I collect shells on the shore. At noon, I drop by Coralie's or the well. In the afternoon, I help Gwen caulk the Merciless: I miss the nails one time in two, but I sing in tune. In the evening, I play dice at the Crâne Fendu. I have two hundred and twelve shells, one from every beach I've landed on. And thirty-seven words from Crochet.
textes.Le matin, je range les caisses sur le qu: In the morning, I stack the crates on the quay. In the afternoon, I fish off the jetty. In the evening, Silas tells me about Barbe-Sanglante, and Joe lets me feed seeds to his parrots. On Sundays, I show the captain my bowline, and then I go and eat at Mum's. I'm almost a real pirate. I just need the knot. And the beard.
textes.Le matin, je regarde Chak s'entraîner, e: In the morning, I watch Chak train, and I copy him with the little ball he gave me. At noon, at the market, I drink the foam at the bottom of the cacao. In the afternoon, I go to Yum Kab's to lick the spoon, or to Ah Kin Pech's when he's snoring. In the evening, I watch Venus. And at the fair of the longest day, I meet up with Pilli and Nebet!
textes.Le matin, je regarde la mer depuis le po: In the morning, I watch the sea from the Freighter's deck. In the evening, I play very softly on the Cannery roof, for Radis's tomatoes. In between, I knit guitar covers with studs on them. Mamie Barricade taught me. She says I knit the way I play: loud and gentle.
textes.Le matin, je remonte l'eau au chadouf. L: In the morning, I draw up water with the shadoof. During the day, I watch the barley, the wheat, the flax, and the river. In the evening, a beer at Mérit's, paid in onions. One evening, the crocodile ate my dog Abouti's kennel. Abouti jumped into the shadoof's bucket. He spent the night there, way up high, barking at the moon. Good dog.
textes.Le matin, je récure le pont et j'épluche: In the morning, I scrub the deck and peel Jacquot's potatoes. In the afternoon, Ahmed teaches me to fish. After that, I play with Amine and Yasmine. In the evening, at Ba Sidi's, I do the djinn's big voice. I've got yellow slippers hidden in my hammock. And one morning, I found a brand-new fishhook in it. Nobody knows where it came from. I say it was a djinn.
textes.Le matin, je réveille Bernadette au dépô: In the morning, I wake Bernadette up at the depot. First the fire, then the pressure, then a quick wipe of the brass. She takes an hour to wake up. So do I. We understand each other.
textes.Le matin, je salue le Grand Cristal. Il: In the morning, I greet the Great Crystal. It spins a little faster when it's happy, and it's often happy. Then I teach in the courtyard, have lunch at Berthe's, comfort one apprentice, scold another, and try, for the hundredth time, to get Pyra and Borée to sit at the same table. In the evening, I go up to the Circle. Ysolde waits for me there without waiting for me.
textes.Le matin, je sonne les heures. Après, je: In the morning, I ring the hours. After that, I carry messages, I write Corentin's letters to the bear in Ramure, I count how long Lucie stays underwater, and in the evening I light the lantern for my grandad. And I ask Tobias how you put a ship back in the water. He sighs. But he answers a bit, now.
textes.Le matin, je suis la première debout. Av: In the morning, I'm the first one up. Before the boilers, before the string lights, before Brasero. I light the fire, chop the vegetables, and sing. Off-key. Very off-key. Écho says it's his favourite moment. He's too kind, that boy.
textes.Le matin, je suis seul à l'Assemblée. Je: In the morning, I'm alone at the Assembly. I add wood, I sweep the ashes, I arrange the cushions. I say good morning to each sofa. They all came from a different house in the Strata. Each one has a story. The yellow one has seen three weddings. The green one, an elephant. I never found out how.
textes.Le matin, je suis un scarabée qui pousse: In the morning, I am a scarab pushing a ball of fire. At noon, a falcon shining above the world. In the evening, an old man with a ram's head who descends into the night. Who am I?
textes.Le matin, je surveille le quai. À midi,: Mornings, I watch the quay. At noon, a rum at the Crâne Fendu. Afternoons, I sit by the fire, at Brutus's forge. We don't talk. It's good. Evenings, dice, at the Shark's Tooth. My hook never shakes. My hand, it used to shake. Coquille asks me a question every morning. I answer with one word. She collects them.
textes.Le matin, je traîne au souk et je suis l: In the morning I hang about the souk and follow Abdellah's tap-tap. In the afternoon I sit at Mustapha's grill table and drum for the customers. And in the evening, at last, the square, with Lhoucine and Hamid. And on the galleon, the pirates' parrot whistles my rhythms. It learns them faster than certain musicians I won't name, {surnom}.
textes.Le matin, je trie ce qu'on m'a apporté l: In the morning, I sort what people brought me the day before. One box for what shines, one box for what could shine, one box for what will shine one day. The third box is the biggest. That's normal. Everything ends up shining, if you rub it enough.
textes.Le matin, je vais jusqu'à la mine choisi: In the morning, I go to the mine to choose my crystals, before the carts. Ludovic shouts “Helmet!”. I answer “Yes!”. Then I forget. He always catches me at the entrance. It's our little ritual.
textes.Le matin, je vais à l'Académie des Scien: In the morning, I go to the Academy of Sciences. I ask Professor Quasar questions. Yesterday, forty-two. He answered three. Then he left to “look for an answer”. He didn't come back. Murmure says questions are the beginning of science. So I do lots of science. Lots and lots.
textes.Le matin, je vais à l'Académie. Je m'ass: In the morning, I go to the Academy. I sit at the back and make paper planes out of the floating equations. In the afternoon, I jump around in the Zero-Gravity Garden: six somersaults in a row! Comète says I'm almost as good as her. In the evening, I pretend to sleep, and I watch the auroras through the porthole. So does Pixel.
textes.Le matin, je vais à la chinampa avec Mam: In the morning, I go to the chinampa with Mum. Well, Tlaco goes, and I follow him. At noon, at the market, I eat flatbreads. In the afternoon, I play in the square, I go and look at Mixtli's shield, I help Coyotl fill the jars. I go to Citlali's school. I sleep there a bit. And at the fair of the longest day, I meet up with Kinich!
textes.Le matin, je vends le poisson de papa. L: In the morning, I sell Dad's fish. In the afternoon, grilled skewers, which I invented: perch, sardine, perch, a pinch of pond salt. Croc-Gris has one every day at noon, Grisou too, on the run, without stopping. I never taste the merchandise. I check it's cooked. That's not the same. Mrrr.
textes.Le matin, l'air est frais, le vent monte: In the morning, the air is fresh and the wind rises from the Falls: it's the best time for gliding. You can feel the island breathing under your wings. I never walk in the morning. I glide to the café.
textes.Le matin, l'air sent bon. C'est le meill: The air smells lovely in the morning. It's the best time for thinking.
textes.Le matin, l'enclume. Le soir, le Crâne F: Mornings, the anvil. Evenings, the Crâne Fendu, a table at the back. Afternoons, Crochet comes and sits by the fire. We don't talk. He blows, I hammer. Mange-Clous says I want crocodile teeth for a fiancée. I have no fiancée. I want to make an iron fist. Three teeth, one fist. That's all.
textes.Le matin, la Foire. À midi, la Bielle, t: Mornings, the Fair. At noon, the Bielle, table 1: you hear everything there. Afternoons, the airfield and the Volta lab, rubber boots compulsory. My “News from Other Towns” comes in on the Zéphyr mail. Professor Boum has promised me the exclusive on “the big one”. And you're on page four, {surnom}: “A mysterious visitor”. Did you like it?
textes.Le matin, la boutique. L'après-midi, le: Mornings, the shop. Afternoons, the jetty. Evenings, the beach hut, a fruit punch with Kevin, who counts up the customers he's fished out for me. Odette threatening to tell the mayor — three seasons and counting. And Félix, the bookseller: I took him out on a pedalo, he went green three metres from the jetty. Now he draws me routes. From the quay.
textes.Le matin, la caverne est très silencieus: In the morning, the cavern is very quiet. You can hear the boilers breathing, the string lights crackling, and Granny Gamelle humming in the kitchen. She sings off-key. (He smiles.) It's my favourite moment.
textes.Le matin, la lumière des guirlandes est: In the morning, the string lights glow softly on the Wall. All the colours wake up one by one. Red first, it's impatient. Blue last. It's shy. Like me.
textes.Le matin, la rosée brille sur la pelouse: In the morning, the dew sparkles on the Park lawn. I water it anyway. Flora says it is not necessary. I say it is polite.
textes.Le matin, le Skatepark est tout vide et: In the morning, the Skatepark is all empty and quiet. I love it. I can hear my wheels on the sheet metal: “vrrrr… tak!” The “tak” is when I land. The “ow” is when I land badly. This morning, only “taks”.
textes.Le matin, les premières chouquettes sort: In the morning, the first sugar puffs come out of the solar oven at six sharp. The smell goes all the way round the Esplanade, and the whole town wakes up sniffing. Even Mr Pascal. Especially Mr Pascal.
textes.Le matin, mon neveu Youssef est sur la B: In the morning, my nephew Youssef is on the Bahja with me, and he says I scare the fish away. In the afternoon, I rehearse with Omar on Mustapha's plates. In the evening, the three of us play with Lhoucine. And after that, a drink at Mama Lou's. Her rum, I pour it into the palm tree's pot. She knows nothing. Well… the palm tree is growing a lot.
textes.Le matin, quand je vais au jardin, je cr: In the morning, when I go to the garden, I pass Nox on his way home to bed. He says goodnight, I say good morning, and I give him a sprig of ash mint so he sleeps well. We've done it for years. It's our little ceremony.
textes.Le matin, quand la flotte rentre, je sui: In the morning, when the fleet comes home, I'm on the square. Before you've even seen a sail, you can hear Hamid singing somewhere behind the jetty. The whole port sets off for the auction. I drum on the rim of the fountain to accompany him from afar. He can't hear me. Nobody can hear anything when Hamid sings.
textes.Le matin, sur les rails, je chante pour: In the morning, on the rails, I sing to check the fishplates. If the echo comes back in tune, the rail is straight. If the echo comes back out of tune… maybe it's me. I start again. Rivet says I'm the only railworker who takes her measurements in C major.
textes.Le matin, très tôt, il m'arrive de couri: In the morning, very early, I sometimes run near the Cenote. For training. Ix Kanul makes her offerings there at that hour. I stop next to her, to catch my breath. For a long time. She says nothing. Neither do I. Then I set off again. It's very good training. For the breath.
textes.Le matin, à cinq heures, j'allume les fo: In the morning, at five, I light the stoves at the heart of the shell. The heat climbs along the spiral, the soup sings, and the first customers turn up in their pyjamas, led by their noses. Professor Benthos, on the other hand, doesn't turn up until around one. Nose in his notebook. Led by nothing at all.
textes.Le matin, à six heures, je vais au pied: In the morning, at six, I go to the foot of the Air Chimney. I put my hand on the grille and feel the air coming down from the surface, cool, a little salty. The Chimney is breathing well. So the Dome is too. After that, I can have my coffee.
textes.Le maître dit, le maître dit… Et toi, tu: Master says, master says… And you, have you eaten?
textes.Le maître du gel a des engelures aux ort: The master of frost gets chilblains on his toes in winter. I tell everyone, especially the apprentices: it reassures them that a master gets cold feet. Borée sulks, then holds out his foot without a word. I put on the lavender ointment. He says “Hm”. That means thank you.
textes.Le maître du gel a des engelures. Oui. A: The master of frost has chilblains. Yes. On his toes, in winter. Sauge treats them with a lavender ointment, and she tells everyone, even the apprentices. She says it reassures them that a master gets cold. “Pride doesn't cure them,” she says. She's right. As she often is.
textes.Le maître du port est sur le quai : il c: The harbour master is out on the quay: he's counting the seagulls. He always finds one too many.
textes.Le maître est redevenu normal ! Enfin… i: The master is back to normal! Well… he still feels like eating flies sometimes. Thanks again!
textes.Le maître sorcier, redevenu humain, rega: The master wizard, human again, looks sternly at his apprentice. His skin is still a little green.
textes.Le maïs, on le cuit avec de la chaux, on: Maize: you cook it with lime, grind it on the stone, the metate, and make the flatbreads. Every day. Before sunrise. Maize made us, says the Popol Vuh. So we owe it that much.
textes.Le meilleur coin de pêche ? Le bout de l: The best fishing spot? The end of the jetty, at nightfall. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Le meilleur du monde ! Tout doux !: The best in the world! Nice and gentle!
textes.Le meilleur endroit de l'île ? Le compto: Best place on the island? Mama Grog's bar. Second best? The bar at the Shark's Tooth. Third? The path between the two.
textes.Le meilleur endroit de la cité, c'est l': The best place in the city is Zigomar's workshop, in the Artisans' Quarter. It smells of powder and sulphur, and things go boom all day long. Mum says it's no place for a child. That's why it's the best.
textes.Le meilleur endroit pour s'élancer, c'es: The best place to take off is the edge of the Cloud Falls, to the north-west. The water falls, the mist rises, and it carries you upwards. But careful: in a west wind, never glide over the Falls. You end up soaking wet, and back down on the Floor without meaning to.
textes.Le meilleur limon pour mes jarres vient: The best silt for my jars comes from his field, after the flood. He used to sell it to me by the basket. One day, he wanted to sell it to me for its weight in gold. I told him gold doesn't hold water. He thought about it. Ever since, he trades it for jars. He has forty of them. I wonder what he keeps in them.
textes.Le meilleur moment à Port-Azur ? Six heu: The best time in Port-Azur? Six in the morning, when the boats come in and the sun rises behind the lighthouse.
textes.Le meilleur moment, c'est le lever du so: The best moment is sunrise. Mistral plays a really soft track and everyone watches the sea.
textes.Le meilleur parcours ? De la fontaine ju: The best route? From the fountain to the lighthouse: the high street, the quay, then the climb up the point. Nobody does it in under eighty seconds. Except me. Well, I used to.
textes.Le meilleur porteur. Hé oui. C'est déjà: The best carrier. Yep. That's something.
textes.Le meilleur, Salomé. Le meilleur. Et c'e: The best one, Salomé. The best one. And that's me.
textes.Le menu de la Cantine de Lentille : soup: The menu at Lentille's Canteen: pumpkin soup, leek soup, and surprise soup. The surprise is that it's soup again. Pay what you can, as always!
textes.Le midi, sa marmite et la mienne, c'est: At lunchtime, his pot and mine are the same one. I put in cinnamon, he puts in chilli. I turn my back, he adds more. He turns his back, I add more cinnamon. The customers say my stew changes taste depending on the time of day. They're discerning customers. I say my stew has character. Like the cook.
textes.Le miel des ruches de Berthe, derrière l: The honey from Berthe's hives, behind the Cauldron, is what makes my magic potion. Three drops per vial. Without it, my potions would taste of scrap iron. When she raises her price, I pretend to cry. She pretends to believe me. Then we clink glasses.
textes.Le miel vient des abeilles des grands ar: The honey comes from the bees in the tall trees. Pomme-de-Pin climbs up to fetch it, right to the top. She always comes down with three stings and a smile.
The honey was a matter of state.
Mine has a new article, Halo.
Mine. Yours is over there, Rivet.
textes.Le mieux, c'est quand la marée monte pen: The best bit is when the tide comes in while we're dancing. We end up with our feet in the water.
textes.Le milieu ! Hé hé. Là où ça se complique: The middle! Heh heh. Where things get complicated, where the hero gets lost and the dragon wakes up. Few people like the middle. They make the best listeners.
textes.Le milieu ! Regarde : tout autour, j'ai: The middle! Look: all around, I've drawn the coasts, the moors, the marshes, the dunes… and in the centre, a big blank. Stoneheart. At the foot of its west face there's a door, the Door of the Four Seals. I've never dared go up there alone: they say the mountain breathes. You, you don't look afraid. Go and see it, examine it closely, and come back and tell me.
textes.Le minerai de la montagne est le meilleu: The mountain's ore is the best in the world. Red as rust, heavy as an oath.
textes.Le mois dernier, Titou m'a emprunté mes: Last month, Titou borrowed my last six glow sticks to juggle. “Look, Lila, a rainbow!” The fourth went into the sea, the fifth into Nono's hair, the sixth I don't know where. Since then I haven't had any, and I tell newcomers to dance with their hands.
textes.Le mois dernier, douze lettres d'expulsi: Last month, twelve eviction letters went to the wrong address. One ended up with a seal, on the beach. Mr Lisse looked at me for a long time. I said: “How clumsy.” He said nothing. He went back into his office. I think he knew. I think he was a little pleased.

Last month, twelve eviction letters went to the wrong address. All of them. One ended up with a seal on the beach. Miss Prune said: “How clumsy.” I looked into her eyes. She looked into mine. I said nothing. I don't know why I said nothing.
textes.Le mois dernier, un pêcheur s'est tartin: Last month, a fisherman smeared his back with Salomé's balm for a sunburn. He came to see me that evening, red as a lobster and smelling of cake. I treated the sunburn. The next day, Salomé had written on her stall: “Recommended by the infirmary”. I wiped off the chalk myself.
textes.Le mois dernier, une voie d'eau s'est ou: Last month, a leak opened right under my forge. Tobias sent someone for good timber, and in the meantime he plugged it with whatever was to hand. My feet were in the water, his nose was in the tar, and he said: “Don't move, or I'll caulk you in with it.” I didn't move.
textes.Le mois où Tilleul a reçu tous les compt: The month Tilleul got all of Bedaine's accounts, my father was sure he'd delivered right: “North tree, third door.” It was the pond tree. Bedaine was looking everywhere for his accounts, Tilleul was telling them to everyone like a story. That day, I took the satchel. My father said thank you. He looked relieved. So did I, a little.
textes.Le mois où j'ai livré les comptes de Bed: The month I delivered Bedaine's accounts to Tilleul's, I was sure of myself: third door, north tree. Tilleul read them with great interest, he thought it was a story. Bedaine thought it was a theft. Plumette took the mailbag the next day, without a word. She was right. Me, I had a shooting star to write down.
textes.Le moment ? LE moment ? (Elle pose sa ta: The time? THE time? (She puts down her cup.) One, two… (She looks at the stage, the canvas, you.) … THREE. (She puts her finger on the middle button, the one with no name, and pushes it all the way up. The speakers switch on with a great gust, all over the meadow.) Ten years I've been waiting. Tonight, at eight thirty, we play. Both villages. Come, and stand at the front: I want to see someone dancing in the first row.
textes.Le monde entier ? C'est grand, comme mai: The whole world? That's a big house! You'd need a lot of brooms. Well then, consider you've got a room here. One more.
textes.Le monde ondule de couleurs ! Tu cours p: The world ripples with colour! You run faster, leaving a rainbow trail behind you!
textes.Le monde présent est né un jour 4 Ahau :: The present world was born on a day 4 Ahau: four dots, and the face of the Lord. It's written on the great stela in front of the temple. Young people don't read it any more. They're wrong not to.
textes.Le monde s'assombrit doucement… et des c: The world gently grows darker… and hidden things light up everywhere: passages, steps, secret graffiti!
textes.Le monorail fait une boucle autour de la: The monorail loops around the city, with four stations. The kiosk terminals take you from one station to the next. They're honest, those ones. I checked them.
textes.Le monsieur gris, Gédéon, il tapote sur: The grey man, Gédéon, he taps on everything. Once, he tapped on my board. It was the best beat in the world. I told him he should be a drummer. He went all red.
textes.Le monsieur gris, Lisse, il tape du pied: The grey man, Lisse, he taps his foot outside the Hall. He thinks nobody sees him. We see everything. We're up high.
The gentleman with the moustache who sympathises. He didn't tell anyone, at least. In this hotel, that's practically a miracle.
textes.Le monstre est parti. Je prierai pour lu: The monster's gone. I'll pray for it too. Maybe it didn't have any friends.
textes.Le monstre est vaincu ! Grâce à vous, et: The monster is defeated! Thanks to you, and a little thanks to me! A tiny bit! A lot!
textes.Le monstre est vaincu. Et le chapeau n'a: The monster is defeated. And the hat didn't burn. Double victory.
textes.Le montant de mon métier s'est fendu. Kh: The upright of my loom split. Khéty repaired it with a fisherman's knot, tight as a fist. I pulled on it with all my strength. Nothing. I said: “It'll never let go.” He said: “That's the whole point with fishermen.” Then he left very quickly. He'd forgotten his net. He came back for it the next day.
textes.Le montant de son métier à tisser s'étai: The upright of her loom had split. I mended it with a fisherman's knot, the one that holds the nets against crocodiles. Tiyi tugged on it, smiled and said: “It will never let go.” I answered: “That's the fisherman's way.” I don't know why she blushed. Me too, actually.
textes.Le monte-charge grince, cliquette et mon: The freight lift creaks, rattles and climbs… and climbs… (with a little elevator tune, very optimised)… then opens in the Grey Factory courtyard, in broad daylight. The Lisse-Center plans are in your bag. Port-Boucan is going to party!
textes.Le morceau du lever de soleil n'a pas de: The sunrise track has no name. So every morning I suggest one. “Hello Sea”. “Zoé Stays”. “Jelly Legs”. I'm up to twenty-one. He says “not bad” every time. I don't think he'll ever choose. And I think I'm fine with that.
textes.Le morceau très fort ! Viens au garage c: The really loud track! Come to the garage tonight, we'll play your song.
textes.Le moteur s'essouffle… et s'arrête. Les: The engine wheezes… and stops. The platforms come to a halt.
textes.Le moteur à cristal des Lumens : silenci: The Lumens' crystal engine: silent as a dreaming fish, it leaves a trail of light behind it. Seventy percent faster than sail alone!
textes.Le moteur à cristal se monte à la place: The crystal engine goes in where the steam engine was. Steam first, stars after!
textes.Le moteur à vapeur, d'après les plans de: The steam engine, from Cliquetis's plans: a boiler, a smoking chimney, a propeller that churns the water. Thirty percent faster. Choo-choo… er, sorry: toot-toot!
textes.Le moulin a quatre ailes, une pour chaqu: The mill has four sails, one for each wind. The North is the grump. The East is the shy one. The South is the lazy one. The West is the poet. Like me. It makes very sentimental draughts.
textes.Le moulin se calme. On te tend un pain d: The mill calms down. Someone hands you a warm honey loaf: “Made with yesterday's flour. Nobody leaves a mill empty-handed!”
textes.Le mousse a trouvé un hameçon dans son h: The cabin boy found a fish hook in his hammock. Forged from an old nail. Nicely curved. Nicely sharp. Blacksmith's work. He thinks it was the ginger cat. Or a djinn. He showed it to me, all proud. I said: “Hm.” Who made it? … Hm. Good work, anyway.
textes.Le mousse des pirates nous a demandé com: The pirates' cabin boy asked us how to fish. He didn't know. Pirates who can't fish! What do they eat at sea?
textes.Le mousse. Je crie sur lui. Matin et soi: The cabin boy. I shout at him. Morning and evening. He scrubs badly. He talks too much. … He's learning. Hm.
textes.Le mouvement perpétuel, tout le monde di: Perpetual motion, everyone says it's impossible. I say: it's just very, very difficult. And I have lots of time.
The sound wall? Twenty-four speakers. I know them all by their first names.
textes.Le mur des algues, c'est le cœur des Ser: The algae wall is the heart of the Greenhouses. Glass tubes full of green water, glowing. The algae eat the light and give back air. And spirulina, all blue, which we harvest with a net. Josette puts it in her lemonade. The children have blue tongues all day long. It's very pretty.
textes.Le mur est humide : Plic est passé par l: The wall is damp: Plic has been by. A fern quivers under your hand, like a cat being stroked.
textes.Le musée secret du canard en caoutchouc: The secret rubber duck museum! One hundred forty-four ducks, arranged by size. And a sign: “DO NOT SQUEAK THEM.”
textes.Le mystère ! Tu me plais, toi. Ceux qui: The mystery! I like you. People who love mysteries are the only ones who listen right to the end. The others skip to the last page.
textes.Le métier, je l'ai appris toute seule, e: I learned the trade on my own, picking up what others threw away. A bent bolt is no use any more. Unless you look at it closely. Very closely. Then you see it's shaped like a heart. And that is of some use.
textes.Le même prix que la semaine dernière, l': Same price as last week, my friend.
textes.Le même que depuis trois siècles, Tiburc: The same one as for the last three centuries, Tiburce.
Same as last year. Plus ten.
textes.Le même que la dernière fois !: The same one as last time!
textes.Le même que la dernière fois ! Il était: The same one as last time! It was very stable.
textes.Le nectar doré de Mélisse, cueilli au cœ: Mélisse's golden nectar, gathered from the heart of the giant flowers. Restores four hearts.
textes.Le neuvième jour, je l'ai trouvé assis s: On the ninth day, I found him sitting on a stone at the edge of the mist, watching a snail cross the path. He said: “Shh, he's nearly there.” I waited with him. The snail got there. Then we went home. I never admitted that I was glad to see it arrive, too.
textes.Le nez de la statue du roi Atlas, c'est: The nose on King Atlas's statue? That's me. The old one had been broken since the flood. I tried to redo the king's from the fresco, and… it came out my way. The queen looked at it for a long time, then said: “My great-grandfather would have laughed.” I take that as a compliment. Free, again.
textes.Le noir. Hm. Allume une forge, il s'en v: The dark. Hm. Light a forge, it goes away. Come at closing time, if you like.
North is that way. No, that way.
textes.Le nord, jusqu'où ? Et jusqu'à quand ?: North, how far? And until when?
textes.Le noyau encore chaud d'un élémentaire d: The still-warm core of a magma elemental. Grimli the miner uses them to light his tunnels.
textes.Le nuage de la chambre tourne lentement,: The cloud in the chamber turns slowly, like a cotton spinning top. A label says: “Do not tap on the glass. It's shy.”
textes.Le nuage frissonne de plaisir, sans une: The cloud shivers with delight, without a single drop. Above it, a very pale rainbow lights up, so as not to wake anyone.
textes.Le nôtre aussi. Ils sont courageux, nos: Ours too. They're brave, our suns.
textes.Le pain ! (Elle soupire de soulagement.): The bread! (She sighs with relief.) The Baron had already taken out his mourning hat. I'll take it to him right away. Thank you. You've saved the castle's morning. That's no small thing: it's often in danger.
textes.Le pain de Trèfle, la boulangère de Ramu: Bread from Trèfle, the baker of Ramure: soft, golden, made with carrots from the rabbits' vegetable garden. Restores two hearts.
textes.Le pain doré de Sylwen, la boulangère du: The golden bread of Sylwen, the baker of Bois-Doré. It smells of honey and sunshine. Restores two hearts.
textes.Le pain du château vient de chez Honorin: The castle's bread comes from Honorine's every morning. On days it doesn't come, the Baron thinks it's the end of the world, and puts on his mourning hat. That happens more often than you'd think.
textes.Le pain et la bière, c'est la même chose: Bread and beer are the same thing here: barley, water, patience. One you eat, the other you drink. Both make you happy.
textes.Le pain, on le range dans le tiroir ou d: Do we keep bread in the drawer or in the bread box?
textes.Le palmier ? Quel palmier ?: The palm tree? What palm tree?
textes.Le panier de la poulie, sous la terrasse: The pulley basket, under the Council terrace… Gaspard swears he heard something fall into it on the night of the Downpour. I'm not strong enough to hoist it anymore. Maybe you are?
textes.Le panier de livraison de Margaux, rempl: Margaux's delivery basket, full of baguettes and croissants. No helping yourself.
textes.Le panier remonte en grinçant… Au fond,: The basket creaks up… At the bottom, a small, dented paint pot with a label: “5”. + Pot of brown (no. 5). To be poured into its well in the Stone Palette!
textes.Le papillon s'envole. Brioche le regarde: The butterfly flutters away. Brioche watches it go, very dignified: “I was letting it go.”
textes.Le papyrus de Thot, le dieu à tête d'ibi: The papyrus of Thoth, the ibis-headed god, scribe of the gods. Thoth points to a cartouche — the king's name, written from top to bottom: three signs, one beneath the other. Look at them carefully.
textes.Le parcours d'anneaux s'allume ! Travers: The ring course lights up! Fly through all the glowing rings as fast as you can. Go!
textes.Le parvis du Temple-Passoire — une fourc: The forecourt of the Colander Temple — a giant fork and spoon, a sauce fountain… and, up there, the Great Flying Spaghetti
I sweep the forecourt every morning. Every morning, the wind blows the sand back from the beach. It's a never-ending job. The Reverend says that's the point. I'm not sure I understood.
textes.Le passage est libre ! La galerie sous l: The way is clear! The gallery under the sea now links the two islands.
textes.Le pavé est glissant près du lavoir. La: The cobbles are slippery near the washhouse. Steam, always steam.
textes.Le perroquet a vendu la mèche… Le trésor: The parrot spilled the beans… The captain's treasure is hidden somewhere around here!
textes.Le perroquet de Barnabé imite le kick. «: Barnabé's parrot imitates the kick. “Boom. Boom. Boom.” It's creepy.
textes.Le perroquet de la capitaine s'est envol: The captain's parrot flew away! His name is Rhubarbe. He says rude words. If you hear rude words in the jungle, that's him!
textes.Le perroquet des pirates répète tout ce: The pirates' parrot repeats everything that's said on the quay. Watch your secrets.
textes.Le perroquet des pirates s'appelle l'Ami: The pirates' parrot is called the Admiral. He's more polite than his master.
textes.Le perroquet des pirates siffle mes ryth: The pirates' parrot whistles my rhythms. I think he wants to join the band.
textes.Le perroquet ne s'est pas envolé, {surno: The parrot didn't fly away, {surnom}. I let it go. It was sad in its cage, it looked at the window all day long. One morning, I opened the cage door and went to get the bread. “Flew away” makes a better story, that's all. And sometimes, in the evening, right at the top of the lighthouse, I think I see something blue. I raise my glass. Just in case.
textes.Le petit Aldric Lisse, je l'ai connu tou: Little Aldric Lisse, I knew him as a tiny lad, on the quays, when his father came to count the crates. He helped me carry the oranges. He laughed loudly. I wonder where that little boy went. Somewhere under the grey suit.
textes.Le petit Aristide ! Mon mousse de deux j: Little Aristide! My two-day cabin boy. He became mayor, he talks well, he gave me a medal. But he never comes fishing.
textes.Le petit Barnabé, l'apprenti de Capucine: Little Barnabé, Capucine's apprentice, came down for the reopening. Green as a pea. He told me: “At least going down, you can't see the drop.” I said: “Pardon?” He repeated it three times. By the third, he was laughing. Did him good, I think.
textes.Le petit Barnabé, l'apprenti liftier d'e: Little Barnabé, the apprentice liftkeeper from up top, came down for the reopening. All green. I served him a miner's chocolate. He got his colour back in three sips: red, pink, then normal. Some people are like that, you just want to warm them up.
textes.Le petit Brahim ! Il est amin, maintenan: Little Brahim! He's amin now, with a turban and a staff. The whole port trembles when he sets the price of sardines. Not me. I saw him cry in front of a crab.
textes.Le petit Gaspard construit des cabanes c: Young Gaspard builds huts the way Barnabé draws maps: with heart, and crooked. But he listens. That's rare.
textes.Le petit Gédéon à la batterie… (Il renif: Young Gédéon on the drums… (He sniffs.) It's the dust. There's dust everywhere around here. (There is no dust.) He plays like me in 1977. Only better. Don't repeat that.
textes.Le petit Malachar est devenu directeur d: Little Malachar became headmaster of the Academy. I knew him as a pupil, raising his hand every two sentences to correct my stories. He still corrects them. He's right about the dates. He's wrong about everything else.
textes.Le petit Malachar, le directeur de l'Aca: Young Malachar, the head of the Academy, says my stories aren't History. He's right. They're stories. That's much better.
textes.Le petit Pépin est le pire élève de ma c: Little Pépin is the worst pupil in my class and the best naturalist in the city. He escapes from my lessons to count mushrooms, whose scientific names he knows better than I do. It drives me to despair. And it delights me.
textes.Le petit Pépin passe tous les jours à qu: Little Pépin drops by every day at four o'clock, just when a brioche breaks, by accident, on the edge of the counter. Amazing how accidents happen right on time.
textes.Le petit Pépin s'échappe de mes cours po: Little Pépin sneaks out of my lessons to go and count the mushrooms in the Ash Wood. He knows their scientific names better than I do. It drives me to despair. And it delights me.
textes.Le petit Pépin veut un chiot. Il connaît: Little Pépin wants a pup. He knows all twelve of their names and seven of their birthdays. He's kind to them, he never pulls their tails. One day, he'll have one. When he knows all twelve.
textes.Le petit Pépin veut un chiot. Je lui ai: Little Pépin wants a puppy. I told him: when you know all twelve of their names. He learned them in a day. So I told him: and their twelve birthdays. He's working on it.
textes.Le petit Théo a perdu le cerf-volant que: Little Théo lost the kite I sold him. It was half price. I should've charged full price.
textes.Le petit Théo construit des châteaux de: Little Théo builds huge sandcastles. One day he'll build a whole town.
Little Théo comes to watch me paint. He told me his kite fell into a pine tree, near here. Poor thing.
textes.Le petit Théo, mon plus jeune client. So: Little Théo, my youngest customer. His kite flew away — the one I sold him. At half price! I should have charged full price. Oh well. I give him shells instead, same thing.
textes.Le petit Titouan veut devenir rang S. Il: Little Titouan wants to reach rank S. He often asks me for advice. I give him very good advice. Then he watches me miss a slime, and takes notes on what not to do. He's a clever boy.
textes.Le petit Tom attend encore sur le banc d: Little Tom is still waiting on the Station bench. He says he's not watching out for anyone. He's wearing his best shirt.
textes.Le petit Tom vient me voir rentrer au dé: Little Tom comes to watch me pull into the depot every evening. I let him pull the whistle, once. He says it's for a friend up top. She can't hear it. But Bernadette whistles a little louder, for him. I swear it.
textes.Le petit Tom vient tous les soirs près d: Little Tom comes by the platform every evening. He's waiting for a girl from up top. He says he isn't. With every cabin, he fixes his hair. I make the doors take their time opening on purpose. To give him a chance.
textes.Le petit Tom vient voir rentrer Bernadet: Little Tom comes to watch Bernadette come home every evening. I let him pull the whistle, once. He says it's for a friend up top. Bernadette whistles a little louder for him. Don't ask me how. She has her favourites.
textes.Le petit Tom, l'apprenti de la Forge, vi: Little Tom, the Forge apprentice, comes and waits by the platform every evening. He's waiting for a girl from up top, Pimprenelle, who he talks to by hammering through the rock. He says it's not for her. He fixes his hair at every cabin.
textes.Le petit Tom, l'apprenti de la Grande Fo: Little Tom, the Great Forge apprentice, bangs on his anvil at the same time as I bang on my drums. We've never agreed on anything. We've been playing together for months, three hundred metres apart. It's my best duet.
textes.Le petit Youssef. Il voit des baleines p: Little Youssef. He sees whales everywhere, and he fishes the way he dreams: head in the clouds. I don't make fun of him. I saw one too, once.
textes.Le petit cochon rose et noir entend la c: The little pink-and-black pig hears the bell, pricks up his ears, and trots straight towards you, his tail curled like a corkscrew. He rubs his nose against your shoes. Truffe has adopted you.
textes.Le petit démon court vers toi : « C'est: The little demon runs toward you: “It's my friend the human!”
textes.Le petit est entré avec son père, il a v: The little one came in with his dad, saw the kite hanging from the ceiling — the rainbow one — and froze. He didn't ask for anything, he just looked. Me, I never give discounts. Never. I gave him half price. His dad thanked me three times. I don't know what came over me. The heat, probably.
textes.Le petit nuage au-dessus de Rainville ?: The little cloud over Rainville? It's mine. It followed me from the mainland, when I was very young. I kept it. You don't leave a cloud all on its own.
textes.Le petit nuage ronronne tout bas. Il ne: The little cloud purrs very softly. It doesn't want to rain: the child is asleep underneath. So it makes a very pale rainbow. A moonbow.
textes.Le petit rat blanc et brun te regarde, c: The little white-and-brown rat looks at you, munches the last bit of cheese, then runs up your arm and perches on your shoulder as if it were a mast. Biscotte has chosen his ship: you.
My little boy fell asleep counting.
textes.Le petit soleil, c'est une lampe. Le Pro: The little sun is a lamp. The Professor switches it on first thing every morning. He says “Good morning, Sun” to it. The real one never answers, and neither does this one.
textes.Le petit-fils de Sel. Il a ses yeux, gri: Sel's grandson. He has his eyes, grey as the winter sea. Not his nerve. He asks me questions about the caves. I answer him. In my own way.
textes.Le phare n'éclaire plus aussi loin, la n: The lighthouse doesn't shine as far at night anymore. Anselme says it's nothing.
textes.Le phare tagué, au sud, c'est mon endroi: The Graffiti Lighthouse, to the south, is my spot. In the evening, I meet… someone there. To swap syrup recipes. Nothing more. It's not a conspiracy. It's mint.
textes.Le phare tagué, au sud. Pigment l'a pein: The Graffiti Lighthouse, to the south. Pigment painted it. Still shines. That's what matters.
textes.Le phare vert, au bout de cette jetée, c: The green lighthouse at the end of this jetty, I'm the one who lights it every evening. The red one, opposite, is the Skala guard's job.
textes.Le phare, cette fois ! Avec un nuage ros: The lighthouse, this time! With a pink cloud.
textes.Le phare, cette fois. Ne cherchez pas la: The lighthouse, this time. Don't go looking for the moustache.
The foot of the Mother Oak.
textes.Le pied marin ! Albertine l'a vu tout de: Sea legs! Albertine saw it straight away. She says you walk like an old sea dog. That's a big compliment, coming from a seagull.
textes.Le piment infernal, c'est ma création. U: The infernal chili is my creation. One day, I crossed an ash chili with a chili from the southern islands. The first to taste it was Grumbald. Smoke came out of his ears for an hour, then he ordered ten kilos for his tavern. Ever since, all of Pandémonia cries with a smile.
textes.Le pinceau des doyens du Village des Arb: The brush of the elders of the Treehouse Village, entrusted to you by Grandma Aquarelle. It only paints with the colours of the Stone Palette: dip it in the Palette (20 strokes), then, in hand, E (trigger in VR) to put a dab of colour in front of you, on Sketched Island.
textes.Le pinceau est sec. Trempe-le dans la Pa: The brush is dry. Dip it in the Stone Palette, in the middle of the clearing (a colour must have come back to it).
textes.Le plat tient, Zohra ?: Is the dish holding up, Zohra?
textes.Le plat, c'est moi qui le ferais, évidem: I'd make the dish myself, of course. It would take a kiln as big as the Skala. My mother says no. For now.
textes.Le plat, oui. Et tes dorades ?: The dish, yes. And your sea bream?
textes.Le plus agaçant, c'est qu'il regarde. To: The most annoying part is that he looks. Every day, crossing the square, Hector glances up at the clock face. Three seconds, no more. I can see him perfectly well from my bench. Once, I called out: “It hasn't moved!” He jumped like a boy caught with his hand in the sugar bowl.
textes.Le plus beau château de Théo avait quatr: Théo's finest castle had four towers made of half coconuts and a moat “dug by the sea”. Truth is, the sea had mostly nibbled at it. He asked me for straws for the flags, I gave him striped ones. He planted the last one on the keep and declared the beach hut a “friendly town”. I signed the treaty with an ice cube.
textes.Le plus difficile, dans mon métier, ce n: The hardest part of my job isn't keeping a city in the air. The Levitators see to that. It's saying no to my daughter when she asks to go down and see the sea. I tell her “soon”. I'm starting to run out of “soons”.
textes.Le plus dur, c'est l'Albatros : il ne re: The hardest part is the Albatross: it never stays in the same place on the map.
textes.Le plus dur, c'est la Colonne : elle est: The hardest part is the Column: it's so tall it always goes off the page.
textes.Le plus grand de toute la Fête des Vents: The biggest one in the whole Wind Festival!
textes.Le plus haut ! Je prends la corde !: The highest! I'll take the rope!
textes.Le pogo ! On saute ! Tous ensemble ! Je: The mosh pit! We jump! All together! I jump higher than everyone! OK, I have four legs, that's cheating.
textes.Le pogo ? Des humains qui se cognent pou: Moshing? Humans bumping into each other for fun. I bump into legs to get fed. It's smarter.
textes.Le pogo, c'est comme quand on se roule t: Moshing is like when we all roll in the mud. But standing up. Humans are weird and wonderful.
textes.Le poids descend, il tire la grande roue: The weight goes down and pulls the great wheel; the great wheel turns the others; the escapement holds them back, one tooth per beat. Tick, tock. And the hands move on, on all three clock faces.
textes.Le poisson ?! Dans MON souk ? Ce sont ce: The fish?! In MY souk? It's those sardines of Mustapha's, their smoke drifts all the way up here. What a disgrace. You need re-educating. Come closer.
textes.Le poisson rouge fait des tours. Il a l': The goldfish does tricks. It looks like it's thinking. About what? A mystery.
textes.Le poisson rouge te regarde. Glouglou. T: The goldfish looks at you. Blub blub. You feel like it's judging you.
The fish came off the hook.
textes.Le pont aussi a besoin d'écho. Prends le: The deck needs an echo too. Get the bucket.
textes.Le pont de lumière bourdonne doucement à: The bridge of light hums softly as you pass.
textes.Le pont de lumière s'allume sous tes pie: The bridge of light lights up beneath your feet, tile after tile.
textes.Le port est abrité par la jetée. À l'est: The harbour is sheltered by the jetty. To the east, Anselme's lighthouse. To the west, the ferry terminal and the beach. Don't swim in the harbour, propellers are unforgiving.
textes.Le port est bruyant. Le désert est silen: The port is noisy. The desert is silent. I am… in between.
textes.Le port est plein de choses tombées de l: The port is full of things that fell off the cliff. Gonzague, the crane operator, has a whole collection.
textes.Le port, c'est mon royaume. Les poubelle: The harbour is my kingdom. The bins are my pantry.
textes.Le port, c'est À NOUS. Les grues, À NOUS: The harbour is OURS. The cranes, OURS. The containers, OURS. The sky? OURS!
textes.Le pot d'orange… Je l'ai vu ! Il est res: The pot of orange… I saw it! It got stuck at the top of the waterfall, on the Lip, at the water's edge. It can't decide whether to fall. Like me in front of a blank page. I don't dare climb up: I get dizzy with heights, and with rhymes.
textes.Le pot de bleu, je l'ai vu flotter sur l: I saw the pot of blue floating on the pond the day after the Downpour! It got stuck on a water lily, far from the bank. Me, I swim like a stone. A painted stone.
textes.Le pot de figues, je ne l'ai jamais ouve: I've never opened that jar of figs, {surnom}. I told myself: the day someone deserves it. The other day, the Lord was there, with his ridiculous hat and his puppy-dog eyes. I put my hand on the ladder. I nearly brought it down. For him. It frightened me. I charged him for the wrapping paper, to calm myself down.
textes.Le pot de jaune, je l'ai vu rouler sur l: I saw the pot of yellow rolling along the beach the morning after the Downpour! It went right to the end, to the west, into my big sandcastle. But the tide covered everything, and now I don't know where the castle door is anymore.
textes.Le pot de rouge… Un lapin l'a fait roule: The pot of red… A rabbit rolled it away, I'm sure of it. I saw it dash toward Mister Paille, my scarecrow, in the middle of the Meadows. But the grass is so tall! And I'm scared of rabbits. Their ears are far too big.
textes.Le pot de vert… je crois qu'il a roulé j: The pot of green… I think it rolled all the way to the Hollow Stump, deep in the Hatching Wood. I don't dare go there: there's a big owl inside, and it gives me funny looks.
textes.Le potier d'Aztlán, Coyotl, fait des jar: The potter of Aztlán, Coyotl, makes blue jars for Tlaloc, their rain god. With round eyes and fangs. Strange taste. Lovely jars, mind you.
textes.Le poulpe de Tonneau, on dirait un cheva: Tonneau's octopus looks like a horse.
textes.Le premier Grand Boucan, Rouille avait t: At the first Great Boucan, Rouille had forgotten everything: the guests, the times, the chairs, the lemonade. I got out my notebook. In two hours, everything was ready. On the last line, I'd written: “Remember to make Rouille breathe.” I made her breathe. She sang like never before.
