textes.Le premier après-midi, Gwen m'a donné un: The first afternoon, Gwen gave me a hammer and a handful of nails. On the third nail, I nailed my own sleeve to the hull of the Merciless. I stayed stuck to the boat like a mussel. Gwen laughed so hard she dropped her plane. She unhooked me and said: “Right. You sing, and I'll nail.” It works very well.
textes.Le premier après-midi, au troisième clou: The first afternoon, on the third nail, she nailed her sleeve to the hull. She stayed stuck to the Merciless like a mussel to its rock, laughing. I laughed so hard I dropped my plane in the tar. I unhooked her and told her: “You sing, I nail.” Since then, the boatyard moves twice as fast.
textes.Le premier clou que Titouan a forgé étai: The first nail Titouan forged was completely bent. He was crying with rage. I told him: “It's an adventurer's nail. It's bent because it's been through things.” He stopped crying. He hammered it in above his bed. He hangs his map of Guild contracts on it, which he copies out every week. The nail holds very well.
textes.Le premier concert des Rats de Cale, je: The Bilge Rats' first gig, I broadcast it live from the Freighter. I had three listeners: Barricade, Lentille, and a seagull perched on the aerial. I commentated as if there were a thousand of them. The next day, Rouille hugged me in her studded arms. I had little holes all over. I was happy.
textes.Le premier hiver, il a voulu m'impressio: The first winter, he wanted to impress me: send me a cup of mint tea across the courtyard, by telekinesis. The tea arrived. The cup stayed on his desk. I laughed so hard the Great Crystal spun the other way. He's never forgiven me. Since then, he brings me my tea on foot.
textes.Le premier hiver, j'ai voulu geler le La: The first winter, I wanted to freeze Mirror Lake. I gave the order. It refused. For three months, I came and sat on the shore, every morning, without asking for anything. One February morning, it froze all by itself, from one bank to the other. That day I understood: frost doesn't obey. It accepts. Old Gaudence laughed. He was pleased with me.
textes.Le premier hiver, j'ai voulu lui envoyer: The first winter, I tried to send her a cup of mint tea across the courtyard, by telekinesis. An elegant demonstration. The tea arrived. The cup did not: it stayed on my desk. Séraphine got drenched, and she laughed so hard the Great Crystal turned the other way. Since then, I bring her tea on foot.
textes.Le premier jeudi, j'ai regardé Pauline l: The first Thursday, I looked at Pauline for a long time, and I predicted a house with three bedrooms, with beds she wouldn't have to make. She knocked over her cup. The whole promenade turned round. She still asks me how I knew. I tell her: “The cards, my dear.” And she nods, very serious.
textes.Le premier jour de tournée, Marcel m'a e: On my first day on the round, Marcel took me to the villa at the end, where a huge dog was barking like a foghorn. He took a sugar lump out of his pocket: “A sugar lump, and you say hello using his name. He's called Pompon.” Pompon ate the sugar and licked my hand. He's very old now. I always have a sugar lump in my satchel.
textes.Le premier jour du Zéphyr, j'ai senti l': On the Zéphyr's first day, I smelled hot oil and heard a droning, very far to the north. I climbed up to the Lookout: “It's coming. A bumblebee as big as the Mother Oak.” Croc-Gris stared north for a long time. An hour later, the airship came out of the clouds. He said: “I'd seen it.” Of course.
textes.Le premier jour ici, un petit Lumen a dé: On the first day here, a little Lumen discovered gravity by falling off a step. He was crying. I didn't know what to do. I put my hands on his knee, without knowing why. They glowed very brightly, and the knee didn't hurt any more. He stopped crying. He looked at me. I was looking at my hands too.
textes.Le premier jour où Borin lui a confié le: The first day Borin trusted him with the tongs, Fundin dropped a red-hot bar on his own foot. He didn't cry out. He said “Sorry, master” and carried on. That evening, I saw his boot, melted right through on top. I sewed him a new one, with an iron toecap. He still wears it.
textes.Le premier jour où j'ai porté la peau de: The first day I wore the jaguar skin in the square, his dog, Tlaco, barked at me. He still barks. Every day. Pilli explains to him that I'm a man. Tlaco isn't convinced. Neither am I, when I see myself in the lake water. A real jaguar, maybe.
textes.Le premier jour où je suis venu au Burea: The first day I came to the Office, I stacked the folders in the shape of a drum kit, without meaning to. Miss Prune saw them. She didn't say anything. The next day, she put a stapler on my desk that goes “chak” when you press it. Perfect for the snare. I named it Chak.
textes.Le premier jour sur ma barque, je ne lui: The first day on my boat, I said only one sentence to him: “Watch the gulls.” He watched them all day, without a word. That evening I asked him what he'd learnt. He said: “They go home before us.” I knew he'd become an old fisherman. That's the finest compliment on the jetty.
textes.Le premier jour sur sa barque, il ne m'a: The first day on his boat, he said only one sentence to me: “Watch the seagulls.” One sentence for the whole day. I thought it was a lot. I watched them. In the evening, I understood. He smiled. The second day, he said nothing at all. That was even better.
textes.Le premier jour, Barnabé s'est évanoui a: On his first day, Barnabé fainted on the third floor. When he came to, he said: “Are we there?” We'd already come back down. He was very proud all the same.
textes.Le premier jour, Gloubi m'a servi une ge: On the first day, Gloubi served me a cosmic jelly. It was wobbling. It was purple. It wobbled exactly the way my uncle Blurp does when he tells a joke. I asked: “That's not my uncle Blurp, is it?” Gloubi swore it was fruit. I ordered a biscuit.
textes.Le premier jour, Gédéon a empilé les dos: On his first day, Gédéon stacked the files in the shape of a drum kit without even noticing. The next day, I put a stapler that goes “tchak” on his desk. Perfect for the snare drum. He named it Tchak. When he uses it, I tap my foot under my desk. Mr Lisse can't see my feet.
textes.Le premier jour, Gérard a loué un pédalo: On the first day, Gérard rented a pedalo to “go round the harbour”. He went round the pedalo. For an hour, in circles, photographing the lighthouse every time he passed: click, one lap, click, one lap. I waved at him, he waved back. Kevin ended up going to fetch him. Gérard said: “What a lovely trip!”
textes.Le premier jour, Gérard a regardé son as: On the first day, Gérard looked at his plate, took out his camera, and photographed it from the front, from the side, and from above, standing on his chair. “Like a work of art,” he said. It went cold. I served him a second one, nice and hot. He photographed that too. An artist, I tell you.
textes.Le premier jour, il m'a laissé regarder: The first day, he let me look through his spyglass. Five seconds. I saw Tazira: white, blue, orange, and a little girl pulling faces, sitting on a cannon. It was Yasmine! I didn't know it yet. Now, every time I get the spyglass, I check if she's still pulling faces.
textes.Le premier jour, il portait le plateau c: On the first day, he carried the tray the way you'd carry a dead fish: at arm's length, stiff as a board. Twelve cups on the floor before noon. My mother was holding her head. I was ten. I took the tray from him and put my open hand underneath: “Like this.” He looked at me as if I were the mayor. Life's funny.
textes.Le premier jour, j'ai demandé à madame C: On the first day, I asked Madame Colette for “the oldest jar in the shop”. She raised her eyes to the top shelf, to a dusty jar of figs, and said: “Not for sale.” I offered a gold coin. She said “Not for sale” in exactly the same tone. Remarkable. Since then, I come back every day, and I buy a cheese.
textes.Le premier jour, j'ai poussé la porte de: On the first day, I pushed open the library door. Three thousand books. I stood on the threshold until Théophraste said “Hush”, even though I hadn't said anything. He gave me a table, at the back, by the window. I'm still there. It's been two years. I haven't finished. I don't want to finish.
textes.Le premier jour, j'ai pris quarante phot: On the first day, I took forty photos of the lighthouse from the pedalo. A superb series: the lighthouse from the front, the lighthouse from the front, the lighthouse from the front… I felt like the lighthouse was following me. Actually, I was going round in circles. Yannick looked at the series and said: “That's captain's work.” He's a real connoisseur.
textes.Le premier jour, j'ai servi une gelée co: On the first day, I served Glorb a cosmic jelly. He went all pale and asked: “It's not my uncle Blurp, is it?” I swore it was fruit. He watched the jelly wobble, then greeted it politely and ordered a biscuit. Since then, he greets all my jellies.
textes.Le premier jour, j'ai vu Tazira dans la: The first day, I saw Tazira through the captain's spyglass: white houses, blue doors, ramparts all orange. We came into port towed by ten boats, and we were rowing too! After, Mustapha gave me six sardines, piping hot. In the evening, on the square, an old man was telling stories. Nobody yelled at me. Except the first mate. But he doesn't count.
textes.Le premier jour, je lui ai donné une pom: The first day, I gave her an apple and asked forty questions. She answered three. I guessed the rest. I got nearly all of it right.
textes.Le premier jour, quand Léon a sonné le d: The first day, when Léon rang for departure, I walked down onto the quay with my bag. He shouted from the gangway: “We're leaving, kiddo!” I shouted: “I'm staying!” He looked at my return ticket, then at me, put the ticket in his pocket and cast off. Not another word. I cried, I laughed, and I went to the Perroquet.
textes.Le premier jour, Églantine a tamponné ma: On the first day, Églantine stamped my card: rank F. I told her: “Not for long!” She smiled. I took a contract for three slimes. The first one stole my shoe. The second one stuck to my sword. The third one looked at me. I came back with one shoe on and a gooey sword. Twelve years later, I'm still rank F.
textes.Le premier lundi du mois, il entre, il p: On the first Monday of the month, he walks in, puts a purse on the counter and takes all my loaded dice without a word. Once, I followed him to the quay. He throws them into the bay, one by one, like feeding ducks. I worked it out: there are eight hundred coins' worth of dice at the bottom of the harbour. It breaks my heart. And it pays my rent.
textes.Le premier matin de Zoé, j'ai passé le m: Zoé's first morning, I played the gentle sunrise track. She sat down in the sand and cried, without a sound, smiling. I let the track run twice, which I never do. The Sunday boat went past at eight. She waved to it.
textes.Le premier matin ici, j'ai tendu la main: On my first morning here, I reached out to a sunbeam to lean on it. It slipped between my fingers. I fell. I laughed. I chased it, it escaped me, I caught it again by spinning around. When I stopped, everyone was looking at me. That was my first dance. It lasted all afternoon.
textes.Le premier matin ici, j'ai vu une petite: On my first morning here, I saw a little yellow flower growing in a crack in the Gate. A dandelion, come up from below, seed by seed, on the wind. It drank the dew, it turned towards the sun. It was alive. I sat in front of it all day. It's still there. We say good morning every day.
textes.Le premier matin où Fañch m'a emmenée da: The first morning Fañch took me out into the bay, he hoisted a little sail I'd sewn for him years before. When it filled, I cried. I told him it was the wind in my eyes. He said: “Of course.” And he looked the other way for the whole tack. I can never thank him enough.
textes.Le premier matin où elle m'a crié « BONJ: The first morning she shouted “MORNING!” at me as loud as I do, I thought it was an attack. I almost loaded the cannon. Then I saw she was smiling. The next day, she did it again. And the day after. Now, if she doesn't shout, I worry. Once, she had a sore throat. I shouted for both of us.
textes.Le premier matin sous le dôme, je suis a: On the first morning under the dome, I went to ask her, quill in hand: “Majesty, what is this day called?” She looked at me as if I were mad. Then she smiled, for the first time since the wave, and said: “The first, I suppose.” It's the finest scroll I have.
textes.Le premier matin sous le dôme, tout le m: The first morning under the dome, everyone was weeping. Abyssos was fourteen and had a quill. He came and asked me, very seriously: “Majesty, what is this day called?” I had no idea. I said: “The first, I suppose.” He wrote “Day 1”. He hasn't skipped a single one since.
textes.Le premier matin à l'hôtel, je me suis r: The first morning at the hotel, I woke up alone. Léa was on the balcony of room seven, barefoot, both hands on the railing. She was looking at the sea the way you look at someone you've been waiting for a long time. I didn't disturb her. I watched her watching. That's my best holiday memory.
textes.Le premier matin, il m'a regardée travai: The first morning, he watched me work without a word. Then he said: “Your keel leans an inch to port.” I measured. It leaned an inch to port. Since then, I listen to him, even when he says he danced with a mermaid. A man who can spot an inch out of true on a keel, you forgive him the mermaids.
textes.Le premier matin, je l'ai regardée poser: The first morning, I watched her lay the keel, and I saw it leaned an inch to port. I told her. She measured. She looked at me wide-eyed. Since then, she listens to me, even when I talk about mermaids. It was Barbe-Sanglante's old carpenter who taught me to see that, when I was a cabin boy. You don't forget a thing like that.
textes.Le premier ne compte pas, il était pour: The first doesn't count, it was for the story.
The first neon sign in Neopolis was pink. It said “TEA”. Mamie Kiku had it put up above her stall. All night long, I watched it blink. It's the most beautiful memory in my memory. I've saved it three times.
textes.Le premier plancher, je le fais sans l'e: The first floor, I do it without the stairs, easy. One day I wanted the second. I climbed and climbed… and then I couldn't move. Not up, not down. My ears were all flat. Auntie Éclair came in three leaps, hop hop hop, and brought me down. She didn't tell Mummy. You won't either, eh? Mrrrow.
textes.Le premier portrait. Elle me l'a montré,: The first portrait. She showed it to me, proud as anything. Me, mouth open, eyebrows up, looking like a man who's just bitten a pebble. “It's during the chorus,” she said. Since then, I play in profile, facing the sea. She says my profile is better. That offends me too.
textes.Le premier pot d'épices qu'elle a vendu,: The first jar of spices she ever sold, to a little girl in a hood, I bought back from the little girl, in secret, the next day. It's on the shelf in my harbour office, empty for a long time now. One evening, Zébuline saw it. She said nothing. She put a full jar next to it. I don't open it. It smells good right through.
textes.Le premier qui fait le tour du miroir d': First one round the reflecting pool wins!
textes.Le premier soir de la danse de la balein: The first night of the whale dance, Lhoucine played slow, heavy, like a rolling wave. I danced the way I dance: arms as fins, belly out front. And then Zohra got up, and Saïd, and the children, and the whole square danced like me. One big whale of Tazira. I cried, of course.
textes.Le premier soir de leur voyage de noces,: On the first evening of their honeymoon, they came in holding hands, brand new. I grabbed my ladle like a microphone and sang my nonna's wedding song at their table. The whole restaurant clapped along. Hugo went bright red. Léa cried. The good kind of tears.
On my first evening here, I looked up. There were stars. Billions. Little ones, big ones, twinkling ones, shooting ones. The legend was true. I lay down in the Agora and cried all night. The next morning, I started building the Observatory. I've never really stopped looking.
textes.Le premier soir où Fanny est venue, elle: The first night Fanny came, she was dancing right next to me. Her arm flew out, my cap flew into the sea, and me after it. I came out soaking wet. She laughed so hard that Mistral turned the music down to listen. My cap — Momo fished it out. He never really gave it back.
textes.Le premier soir où Prisme a dansé sur ma: The first evening Prisme danced to my music, I played a note too high, out of emotion. She leapt exactly to the height of the note, as if she were catching it. The auroras turned pink. Since then, every evening, I play that note once. She leaps every time.
textes.Le premier soir où Tibo a fait la grosse: The first evening Tibo did the djinn's big voice, he let out such a terrible “OOH-HOO-HOO” that the great Mâchefer, passing at the back of the square, jumped and spilled his glass. A pirate who's seen three captains die! The circle applauded Tibo. Mâchefer went off grumbling. He came back the next day. At the back.
textes.Le premier soir où j'ai dansé sur la mus: The first evening I danced to Vibrato's music, he played a note too high, out of emotion. I leapt to catch it, right at that height. The auroras turned pink. Since then, every evening, he plays that note once. And every evening, I leap. We've never missed.
textes.Le premier soir où j'ai dormi dans sa ca: The first night I slept in his hut, Gaspard left a water flask on the doorstep, with a note: “Drink.” The second night, a flask and a note: “Drink more.” It's been three weeks. I have a whole collection of little notes. I've pinned them on the wall, between the shells.
textes.Le premier soir où j'ai joué à sa table,: The first evening I played at his table, he watched me tap the wood with my hook. Tick, tick. He said: “Under the table, if you please.” Nobody says “if you please” to me. I obeyed. Since then, I play with my hook on my knees. He's never asked me for anything else. That's why I come back.
textes.Le premier soir sans alliance, je me sui: The first evening without my ring, I sat at the end of the Coco Loco's counter. Kiki served me a glass and called it a “consolation punch”. The next day too. On the third evening, there was a little label on the glass, with my name. I never found out what he put in it. It consoled a little.
textes.Le premier soir sur l'île, il y avait un: My first evening on the island, there was a mass. They were all singing, badly, with sauce on their chins. I stood up and sang. The Reverend's eyes went wide. Then he said: “At last, someone who sings even more off-key than me, but louder!” I was made choir leader the very next day.
textes.Le premier soir, Hector est venu accroch: On the first evening, Hector came to hang the sign he'd forged for me: an iron parrot, wings spread. He hung it crooked. I told him so. He answered: “It's a parrot leaning over to look at the customers.” It's been leaning for twenty years. The tourists photograph it. I've never straightened it.
textes.Le premier soir, Tancrède s'est assis à: The first evening, Tancrède sat at my table and asked for “the biggest slice, if you please, for a knight”. I gave him a quarter of a pie. He ate it, said thank you, and asked for more. Four quarters. A whole pie. He stood up, shouted his full name, and sat back down for dessert.
textes.Le premier soir, Zoé était au bord de la: The first night, Zoé was at the edge of the dance floor, all stiff, her weekend bag in her hand. I took the bag, put it down in the sand, and showed her the crab step. She did it all crooked, laughed, started again. She forgot her bag until morning. A real crab had moved in.
textes.Le premier soir, elle a regardé le mur d: The first evening, she looked at the workshop wall and said: “Your stars are golden in the middle and blue at the edges.” I laughed. Then I looked. Forty years, and I'd never seen my lanterns made colours on the whitewash. Now it's all I can see. She's ruined my eyes. For the better.
textes.Le premier soir, il a voulu régler une d: The first evening, he wanted to settle a quarrel with his fists, in my place, right by the counter. I grabbed him by the ear and threw him out, club in my other hand. He was two heads taller than me. Outside, he rubbed his ear and said: “Misunderstanding.” Since then he ducks his head coming in. The door isn't that low.
textes.Le premier soir, il est entré ici sans s: The first evening, he walked in here not knowing it was me. He ordered a rum, all swagger. I served him and said: “Still swim like a wet dog?” He dropped his glass. Since then I serve his rum in an old glass of its own, engraved with an “S”. He asked me what it meant. I poured him another.
textes.Le premier soir, il tapotait le bois de: The first evening, he was tapping the wood of my table with his hook. Tap, tap. Right behind Monsieur Malaterre, who was winning. I told him: “Under the table, if you please.” He looked at me for a long time. Then he obeyed. Since then, he plays with his hook on his knees, and Monsieur Malaterre wins much less. I'm just saying.
textes.Le premier soir, il y a cent ans, quand: The first evening, a hundred years ago, when I saw a ruby was missing, I closed the shop and searched the whole hall. Nothing. At the Forge Festival, Ulfa set a full mug down on my counter: three hundred and sixty-five rubies. She said: “You looked bored.” I haven't been bored since.
textes.Le premier soir, il y a trente ans, je l: The first evening, thirty years ago, I told him about Barbe-Sanglante's map. His glasses fogged up. He stopped sleeping: I could hear him pacing in his tower all night. He told me one day: “If someone brings me the three pieces, I'll know how to read them.” I believe him. He reads maps very well. People, less so.
textes.Le premier soir, il était tout seul. Qua: The first night, he was all alone. Four speakers. One crackling. He was mixing anyway, with a big smile, for the sea. I thought: that one needs somebody. I took a fishbone out of my pocket. I fixed it. He said thank you forty times. Me, once.
textes.Le premier soir, j'étais au bord de la p: The first night, I was at the edge of the dance floor with my weekend bag, all stiff. Yaya took the bag, put it in the sand and said: “Watch my feet.” Crab step. I messed up, I laughed, I started again. By morning I'd totally forgotten the bag. There was a crab in it. A real one.
textes.Le premier soir, je lui ai donné une éch: The first night, I gave her a scarf that was far too big. Three months later, I took it back, shortened it and added a red stud. I told her: “Now it's your size. And so are you.” She still wears it on stage, that little one.
textes.Le premier soir, quand j'ai suivi ses tr: The first evening, when I followed her tracks to her door, I was soaked up to my ears. She didn't ask my name. She asked: “How many times did I stop, on the way?” I said: “Three. Once for a flower.” She smiled. She gave me a blanket, and a whole cake. That time, I got it whole.
textes.Le premier soir. Une dispute, à La Murèn: The first evening. A quarrel, at La Murène Ivre. A fisherman, one of ours. I get up to settle it. With my fists. She comes out from behind her counter, club in one hand, and with the other she grabs my ear. I'm two heads taller than her. She threw me out anyway. It was a misunderstanding. Hm.
textes.Le printemps dernier, j'ai sorti un méro: Last spring, I landed a grouper. Twenty-five kilos, weighed by Odette, nothing I can do about it. I carried it on my shoulder to Paulo's, right along the quay. When he saw it, he dropped his ladle and burst into song. Opera, in the middle of the kitchen. The customers applauded the grouper.
textes.Le printemps où Miriel a cueilli tout le: The spring Miriel picked the whole clover meadow for the festival crowns, my girls went round in circles for a whole day, lost. I went to see her with a hundred bees around my head. She put half the crowns back in the meadow. It's the only time bees have ever danced at the Dawn festival.
textes.Le printemps suivant, un petit pissenlit: The next spring, a little dandelion came up right next to the bolt. Pimprenelle said: “See, it works.” I didn't have the heart to tell her otherwise.
The fair price is mine, Miriel.
textes.Le prix libre, mon caillou, c'est simple: Pay what you can, my pebble, it's simple. Whoever has a lot leaves a lot. Whoever has nothing leaves a thank-you. Whoever hasn't even got a thank-you leaves a smile. And with all that, I make tomorrow's soup. It's worked for twenty-five years. The Strata accountants can't make head or tail of it.
textes.Le prix libre, ça marche. Je n'y croyais: Pay-what-you-can works. I didn't believe it at first. And then one day, Boulon paid thirty coins for a bowl and said: “It's for the next three who have nothing.” That day, I cried into the soup. It was a bit too salty.
textes.Le pro du skate ! T'as vu, je fais un ol: The skate pro! Look, I land one ollie in two now!
textes.Le prochain monorail arrive dans… mainte: The next monorail arrives in… now. No. Now.
textes.Le prochain tour de l'île part à quinze: The next island tour leaves at three. Two seats left. And a fold-down seat for the very brave.
textes.Le professeur Boum a encore perdu le toi: Professor Boum has lost the roof of his workshop again. For the fifteenth one, he needs iron ore.
textes.Le professeur Boum a encore perdu son to: Professor Boum has lost his roof again. That's the third this month.
textes.Le professeur Boum a teint en vert les m: Professor Boum dyed my grandfather's sheep green, then blue. He's kind, I'm sure. But he's never come up to apologise. As long as he doesn't come up, it's no.
textes.Le professeur Boum boit son café avec tr: Professor Boum takes his coffee with three spoonfuls of iron filings. “For thinking,” he says.
textes.Le professeur Boum est un danger pour la: Professor Boum is a danger to science, to roofs, and to my son, who wants to be like him. I'll admit he has talent. For exploding.
textes.Le professeur Boum est un homme merveill: Professor Boum is a wonderful man, with a heart as big as a boiler. I'm very fond of him. I'll never let him into one of my bubbles with his pockets full.
textes.Le professeur Boum met trois cuillères d: Professor Boum puts three spoonfuls of iron powder in his coffee. One day, the butler put some in every cup. Out of zeal. A customer from Carène chewed his coffee. Hm. I adjusted the butler. Now he asks first: “Iron powder?” Customers jump. He asks anyway.
textes.Le professeur Boum, c'est le plus grand: Professor Boum is the greatest inventor in the world. He's lost fourteen roofs! Nobody's lost that many roofs. Mum says it's not a compliment. I think it is.
textes.Le professeur Boum, c'est mon client le: Professor Boum is my oddest customer and my sturdiest awning. He drinks his coffee with iron powder and says thank you for every cup. Explosive, but polite.
textes.Le professeur Boum, c'est mon maître, et: Professor Boum is my master, and the greatest scientist in Cliquetis. He taught me everything, even what he shouldn't have. I adore him. And his “Big One” keeps me awake at night.
textes.Le professeur Boum, c'est une explosion: Professor Boum means one explosion a week. Without him, the Gazette would just have Zéphyr timetables. I adore him. From a distance.
textes.Le professeur Moreau cherche l'Atlantide: Professor Moreau is looking for Atlantis. I sold him all my charts of the seabed. He hasn't found anything… yet.
textes.Le professeur Moreau est gentil comme to: Professor Moreau is as sweet as can be, and as absent-minded as ten men. He's looking for a city under the sea. I'm looking for his socks. To each their own treasure.
textes.Le professeur Moreau est un client exige: Professor Moreau is a demanding, absent-minded and sincere guest. He is looking for a city under the sea. In the meantime, he mostly occupies my carpet.
textes.Le professeur Moreau garde sous son orei: Professor Moreau keeps a drawing of a city under the sea under his pillow, with a big crystal in the middle.
textes.Le professeur Moreau reçoit des lettres: Professor Moreau gets letters from a university. He opens them with shaking hands.
textes.Le professeur Moreau rêve de la cité eng: Professor Moreau dreams of the sunken city. Someone needs to find it, rekindle its crystal, and tell him all about it.
textes.Le professeur Moreau, à l'hôtel, cherche: Professor Moreau, at the hotel, is looking for a sunken city. All he'll find is sea urchins.
textes.Le professeur Moreau. Un homme adorable: Professor Moreau. A lovely man who's scared of his mail. I don't know what's in those letters. I don't ask. I hand out caramels.
textes.Le professeur a lu mes livres de quart s: The professor read my logbooks without asking me. What's written up there was nobody's business but mine. He's looking for a city. I say: sea urchins.
textes.Le professeur est mon meilleur client et: The professor is my best customer and my best friend. He's looking for Atlantis, I'm looking for the world. Neither of us has ever left.
textes.Le professeur m'a appris à écouter une c: The professor taught me to listen to a boiler. We'd put our ears to it, the two of us, without speaking. “Is it singing, Capucine?” “It's singing.” “Then we stay.” One day, it went quiet. He grabbed my hand and we ran. We were at the end of the path when the roof went off. He was laughing. So was I, back then.
textes.Le professeur m'a proposé un savon explo: The professor offered me an explosive soap, “for bubble propulsion”. I agreed to try one drop, just one, in a thimble. There was a little noise, a little pink cloud, and no more thimble. The professor applauded. Me, I put the bottle away very, very high up.
textes.Le professeur prend trois cafés chaque m: The professor has three coffees every morning and says nothing. Nothing! One single thank-you in two months. I counted. And the day he did talk…
textes.Le progrès, cher prospect, c'est quand t: Progress, dear prospect, is when everything looks the same. Here, nothing looks the same. It's exhausting.
textes.Le public te lance des pièces (et un coq: The audience throws coins at you (and a seashell).
textes.Le pupitre est à vous ! Levez bien le co: The podium is yours! Keep that elbow up!
textes.Le père de Noisette était aventurier. Un: Noisette's father was an adventurer. One day, he left on a great quest, across the sea. He left me a letter and a pot of sourdough starter. The starter, I feed it every day. The letter, I read it again when the oven is hot and Noisette is asleep. He writes every season. He says he'll come back.
Noisette's father was an adventurer. One day, he left on a great quest, very far away, beyond the sea. He writes every season. Noisette keeps all his letters in a biscuit tin. I keep the tin.
textes.Le pédalo qui s'appelle « Gérard », c'es: The pedalo called “Gérard”, I'm the one who swam it back, pushing it in front of me. The tourist inside had been going round in circles for an hour photographing the lighthouse. He photographed me too, while I pushed. Yannick named the pedalo after him. The tourist doesn't know. Shh.
textes.Le pêcheur est là. C'est l'assiette qui: The fisherman's here. It's the plate that's missing.
textes.Le quai de sept heures à dix-neuf heures: The quay from seven in the morning to seven at night. Lunch at Paulo's. Evenings, cards at the Perroquet. Sometimes a little white dog sleeps behind my crates, at the end of the quay. I don't say anything. Little Nina doesn't either. And every week, Nadine slips a letter into my letterbox on High Street. A letter. For me. I read it at night, sitting on Gertrude. The crate.
The forty-seventh floor does not exist. … A lady went up there last week. I haven't seen her since. I advise against it.
The quetzal one is the most precious.
textes.Le radar montre un nuage en forme de bal: The radar shows a whale-shaped cloud. Doctor Aurèle will want to name it. I suggest “Mathilde”.
textes.Le radar ne montre rien. C'est la meille: Nothing on the radar. That's the best news you can get on a night watch.
textes.Le ragoût de Mama Grog : poisson, banane: Mama Grog's stew: fish, plantains, red beans, chilli and a ladle of molasses. Nobody asks what else is in it. Restores three hearts.
textes.Le ras-el-hanout, c'est « la tête de la: Ras el hanout means “head of the shop”: the merchant's best blend. Mine has thirty-two spices. The thirty-third ingredient is a secret.
textes.Le rat ? Ce voleur ? Ce brigand à mousta: The rat? That thief? That whiskered bandit? (He bangs his ladle on the table.) Three cheeses! My three finest aged cheeses, the ones that smell so strong even the seagulls faint! Gone! I saw him dash off into the port with a piece bigger than he is. He's hidden them somewhere, the wretch! (He grumbles.) … Well. If you take him far from my kitchen, I'll say no more. Find my cheeses: wherever he hid them, he'll come back. Put them near the hold, and he'll come out. That rat would do anything for cheese. So would I, come to think of it. Maybe that's why we don't get along.
textes.Le rat dort sur ton épaule. Moi, je suis: The rat sleeps on your shoulder. Me, I'm too big for your shoulder. I tried. You fell over. Sorry.
textes.Le rat du Requin Borgne: The rat of the Requin Borgne
textes.Le rayon d'accueil descend jusqu'à la bo: The welcome beam reaches down to the buoy on the sea, where your boat is waiting for you. [E]: go back down.
textes.Le rayon d'accueil relie le Portail à la: The welcome beam links the Gate to the buoy, on the sea. You go up in a whoosh. To go down, you come back here and ask me. Politely. With, if possible, a little compliment about the speech.
textes.Le rayon d'accueil te soulève tout douce: The welcome beam lifts you ever so gently. The sea drifts away, the clouds come closer…
textes.Le rayon de soleil frappe la Fleur-Porte: The sunbeam strikes the Door Flower! Its petals quiver… and slowly open, like on the first morning of the world.
textes.Le rayon te dépose doucement vers la mer: The beam sets you gently down towards the sea. The auroras, the domes, the Spire… everything becomes a tiny light in the sky.
textes.Le rayon te porte vers le ciel. Tes chev: The beam carries you up to the sky. Your hair floats. Your tummy goes “whoo”.
textes.Le rayon te repose, tout doucement, sur: The beam sets you back down, very softly, on the buoy. Your rowboat is waiting, a little surprised.
textes.Le rayon te soulève, doucement, comme un: The beam lifts you, gently, like a soap bubble… 380 metres higher up, the Lumens wave hello.
The town's register of inventions. This morning: a kettle that whistles “The Liftkeepers' March”. Patent granted.
textes.Le rempart ? Tout en haut, au vent, à gu: The ramparts? Way up high, in the wind, watching for gargoyles. That's the post for the brave. Or the dreamers. Often, they're the same.
textes.Le rempart fait le tour de la Basse-Vill: The rampart runs all around the Lower Town. Three gates: the North Gate towards Seagull Harbour, the South Gate towards the fields, the East Gate towards the lake. Gilles guards the North Gate. The other two are me. Sometimes at the same time.
textes.Le remplaçant a commencé la mauvaise cha: The stand-in started the wrong song. The Bilge Rats followed him. It turned into a new song. It'll be called “The Stand-In”.
textes.Le remplaçant du soir joue avec beaucoup: Tonight's stand-in plays with lots of enthusiasm and very little rhythm. Rouille sings louder to make up for it. The windows are shaking.
textes.Le remplaçant du soir, c'est Cradoc. Il: Tonight's stand-in is Cradoc. He's trying to juggle the sticks between beats. He catches them one time in three. The rhythm too.
textes.Le remplaçant tape à contretemps. Toute: The stand-in is playing off-beat. The whole pit jumps off-beat to make him happy. That's solidarity.
textes.Le requin s'enfuit dans les profondeurs…: The shark flees into the depths… It lost a shark tooth (picked up).
textes.Le reste, c'est un secret. Je ne le conf: The rest is a secret. I only share it with a friend. A true one, {surnom}.
textes.Le rhum brun du Crâne Fendu, vieilli dan: The brown tonic of Le Crâne Fendu, aged in barrels from a sunken ship. It smells of wood, molasses and a little of gunpowder. Restores one heart.
textes.Le rhum de Mama Lou adoucit tout. Même l: Mama Lou's rum softens everything. Even cats.
The rum is good tonight. Hm.
textes.Le rhum noir de La Murène Ivre. Les pira: The dark tonic of La Murène Ivre. Pirates say it warms the heart; Anouk would say otherwise. Restores one heart.
textes.Le rire ! HA HA HA ! Ça, c'est la bonne: The laugh! HA HA HA! Now that's the right answer! Laughter is what makes the forge work. The steam is just for show.
textes.Le rire de Brunehaut s'entend jusqu'au f: Brunehaut's laugh can be heard right at the bottom of the mine. As long as I hear it, I know all's well on the surface. It's the best alarm in the world. And the loudest.
textes.Le rocher était MAL PLACÉ !: The rock was in the WRONG PLACE!
textes.Le roi a encore commandé un tonneau de b: The king ordered another barrel of fizz from Ulfa. To “taste” it. Three times this week.
textes.Le roi a encore perdu sa couronne. Elle: The king has lost his crown again. It was on his head.
textes.Le roi dicte des décrets très longs et t: The king dictates very long, very royal decrees. I shorten them. He protests, then he signs. I think he's glad to have someone who dares.
textes.Le roi m'a envoyé dessiner les mers du s: The king sent me to chart the southern seas, my grandfather's seas, aboard the Stubborn Seagull. Octave was the ship's carpenter: we played cards every evening, he cheated, I measured his beard. Then one moonless night, the rock. I woke up on a raft of rolled-up maps, one boot short, and a parrot said “Shipwreck” to me from the top of a tree. Great barnacles, what a night.
textes.Le roi perd sa couronne sur sa tête, cha: The king loses his crown while it's on his head, sings off-key and pays his bills late. He's the best king in the world. I'd give my life for him. Or at least, I'd stay awake.
textes.Le rouage, je l'ai dessiné. Cent fois. S: The cog, I've drawn it. A hundred times. On my workbench, in chalk, at night, when the forge cools down. The teeth, the axle, the thickness. In the morning, I wiped it off with my sleeve. Nobody's ever seen it. If you tell, I'll say you're lying.
textes.Le rouge ! (Elle le tient à bout de bras: The red! (She holds it at arm's length, in the sun.) My poppies will be able to blush again. With joy, this time. Hurry and pour it in: paint cup number three. And here: a bunch of sunflowers. They're white for now, but they won't stay that way for long.
textes.Le rouge ! Couleur de la crête de Rouill: Red! The colour of Rouille's mohawk, of beetroot and of bricks. It pops. I'll paint you a red rat on the next wall.
textes.Le rouge ! La couleur des aras, de la co: Red! The colour of macaws, of cochineal, of the heart! You have fire in you. I'd weave you a red belt, if you stayed long enough.
textes.Le rouge ! Pour les portes, c'est le mei: Red! It's the best for doors. It says “come in” before you've even knocked.
textes.Le rouge des braises… Je m'en doutais. T: The red of embers… I thought so. You've got a little fire inside. Brasero's going to love you. I'll paint you near the brazier, then.
textes.Le rouleau ? Il y en a trois dans le tir: The roll? There are three in the drawer: the waltz, the liftkeepers' march, and the Column lullaby. Which one?
textes.Le royaume a trois parties : les racines: The kingdom has three parts: the roots, the village… and the Bramble Queen's domain, to the north. No one has been there for a hundred years.
textes.Le royaume des fées ! Une prairie en fle: The fairy kingdom! A flowering meadow floats above a sea of golden clouds. Fireflies dance in broad daylight… and to the north stands an immense tree, so tall its crown touches the sky: Yggdrasil, the World Tree. Fairies are waiting for you in the glade, to the south.
textes.Le rythme du cœur qui dort. Joli. Tu es: The rhythm of a sleeping heart. Lovely. You're a calm one, you are.
textes.Le réchauffé ?! Gertrude, tu as entendu: Reheated?! Gertrude, did you hear that?
textes.Le réparateur. Grmbl. Si un jour la Flèc: The fixer. Grmbl. If the Spire ever crackles, maybe I'll call you. Maybe.
textes.Le réveil du Bourgmestre. Il sonne au mi: The Burgomaster's alarm clock. It goes off in the middle of his speeches. The alarm clock, not the Burgomaster.
textes.Le sable t'avale… Tu te débats, et tu re: The sand swallows you… You struggle free and come out, out of breath, at the entrance of the hall.
textes.Le sac qui contenait la lettre de Pépin: The bag with Pépin's letter in it was going “tick-tock”. Zélie had slipped a note on it: “Do not shake. Theoretically, it isn't alive.” Theoretically! I carried the bag at arm's length all the way to Pépin's door, very slowly. It was a stopwatch. Pépin timed how long I'd taken. Too long, according to him.
textes.Le safran ! La couleur la plus chère du: Saffron! The most expensive colour in the world, and Lalla Aïcha sells it to me with a sigh. People who love yellow love a party. So you'll dance at my wedding.
textes.Le salé ! Ah, la cuisine d'en bas ! J'es: Savoury! Ah, the cooking from down below! I've been trying a bouillabaisse for five hundred years. It sings. It isn't salty. It sings.
textes.Le sanctuaire bleu de Tlaloc, le dieu de: Tlaloc's blue shrine, the god of rain, with round eyes and fangs. In front, a chacmool holds an empty bowl on its belly. Tlaloc is thirsty… for a jar of rainwater, no doubt. Coyotl, the potter, makes lovely blue jars.
textes.Le sanctuaire rouge de Huitzilopochtli,: Huitzilopochtli's red shrine, the warrior hummingbird, the sun that fights every night to return. In front, an unlit brazier. You burn copal in it, the white incense; Tochtli sells some at the market.
textes.Le sandwich d'Achille, c'est Gaston qui: Achille's sandwich was Gaston's invention: ham, gherkin, tied up with a little lead weight so it flies straight. Free “until landing”. The first morning, I threw it as hard as I could, and Achille caught it one-handed, mid-loop. I ran into the café shouting. Gaston pretended his eyes weren't wet.
textes.Le sandwich d'Achille, c'est jambon, cor: Achille's sandwich is ham and gherkin, tied up with a little fishing weight so it flies straight. On the second morning it was too windy: Adèle threw it, the wind caught it, and it dropped straight down Professor Boum's chimney. We heard a little “boom”. The professor came to tell me it was his best lunch in weeks.
textes.Le saule ! Comme le mien, sur la place !: The willow! Like mine, on the square! It doesn't weep, you know. It leans down to listen. That's different.
textes.Le saviez-vous ? La Conserverie a produi: Did you know? The Cannery once produced two million tins of sardines a year. Today it produces songs, soups and studded scarves. Progress!
textes.Le savon, sûrement. C'est mystérieux, le: The soap, surely. It's mysterious stuff, soap.
textes.Le scarabée pousse sa boule de fumier co: The scarab rolls its ball of dung the way Khepri rolls the sun up in the morning. Small, dirty, stubborn… and it makes the day dawn. I like scarabs.
textes.Le sceau du désert ? … Qui t'a parlé de: The desert seal? … Who told you about that? The elders say it sleeps under the walking dune. But the dune walks, that's the thing. Nobody knows where it is today.
textes.Le sceau du nord ? On raconte que les be: The northern seal? They say the shepherds keep it in a cave, under the highest ridge. They won't talk about it. I understand them: if I had it, I'd take it apart.
textes.Le sceau roule sur le côté. Un escalier: The seal rolls aside. A staircase plunges into the dark, around a bottomless well…
textes.Le seau d'eau ? Il l'a vidé par la fenêt: The bucket of water? He emptied it out of the window, right next to me. Next to me! A man who aims that badly is a man who aims very well, you see? I said “thanks, very refreshing”. It was true, too. It was eight o'clock, I'd done my lap.
textes.Le second de Barbe-Sanglante, le Capitai: Barbe-Sanglante's first mate, Captain Sans-Chair, swore to guard the treasure for all eternity. He kept his word. He's still out there. Well, what's left of him.
textes.Le second, il crie tout le temps sur moi: The first mate yells at me all the time. Only at me! With the others, he just goes “Hm”. I'm a bit scared of him. But when he bends an iron bar with his bare hands, that's so cool.
textes.Le secret de la forme ? Cent pompes le m: The secret to fitness? A hundred push-ups in the morning, a hundred in the evening, and a pie at noon. Want to join in?
textes.Le secret de la pêche ? Garder la ligne: The secret of fishing? Keep the line taut, but not too taut. Like a conversation with Gaston.
textes.Le secret, c'est la braise. Pas de flamm: The secret is the embers. No flames. Flames burn, embers cook. It's the same with people.
textes.Le secret, c'est le départ. Je pars comm: The secret is the start. I shoot off like an arrow, and after that, the others are chasing an arrow. It's discouraging.
textes.Le septième toit, je m'en souviens comme: The seventh roof, I remember it like yesterday: a flash, a huge bang, and Capucine sitting in the soot, without eyebrows. The next day, she told me she was leaving to “keep the colours without the danger”. I gave her the barrel of my old engine, the only one that had never exploded. She made it into her first cannon. Every time it fires, my eyes sting a little.
textes.Le serpent-naga des profondeurs… une éca: The naga serpent of the depths… a scale from that creature would be the jewel of my collection.
Service is included. So is the view.
textes.Le sifflet ! Quand tu siffles, je cours: The whistle! When you whistle, I run! Even when it's not for me! Especially when it's not for me!
textes.Le silence ?! (Elle te regarde, boulever: Silence?! (She stares at you, shaken.) … I'll try. For you. … How long was that? Two seconds? That was hard.
textes.Le silence ?! Mais… Ha ! Tu sais quoi ?: Silence?! But… Ha! You know what? You're right. The finest moment in a song is just before the first note. The Silent One would agree with you.
textes.Le silence. (Il hoche la tête, longtemps: Silence. (He nods, for a long time.) You know how to listen. Come to the Bridge one evening, after the concert. We'll listen together. Without saying a word.
textes.Le silence. Au milieu de la pièce, quelq: Silence. In the middle of the room, someone with a very pale face makes big gestures… without a sound.
Silence. The Freighter's deck, in the morning. The spot next to me is free.
textes.Le silence… (Il baisse les mains.) C'est: Silence… (He lowers his hands.) It's the most beautiful note of all. Murmure would agree with you. She always asks me to play it.
textes.Le silence… Respect. C'est la note la pl: Silence… Respect. It's the hardest note to play. Listen. … There. That one was for you.
The sixth, I'm charging you for.
textes.Le soir (à partir de 21 h), retrouver Gé: In the evening (from 9 p.m.), meet Gédéon at the entrance to the Howling Hall and walk him to the drum kit: let him play his first concert with the Bilge Rats
textes.Le soir de l'Averse, j'avais préparé un: On the evening of the Downpour, I'd made a bouquet for Aquarelle's birthday. Poppies, cornflowers, buttercups. In the morning, it was as white as a bridal bouquet. Aquarelle took it anyway. She said: “It just needs a little patience.” She pressed it in a book.
textes.Le soir de la carte. Il la pose sur un t: The night of the map. He puts it on a barrel while he lights his pipe. A ginger cat jumps, grabs the map, darts over the crates, then onto a roof. The captain stays down below. He yells. He's scared of heights. A captain scared of a cat and a roof. Hm. Three dead captains, and this one.
textes.Le soir de la démonstration, j'ai trouvé: On the evening of the demonstration, I found a pink confetto in my hat. I waved it in front of the whole Crankshaft: the proof! Capucine said it was last year's confetti. How does she know? How can you tell what year a confetto is from? And the next day at lunch, there was one in my soup. I don't say anything any more. I take notes.
textes.Le soir de la foudre, Kalda est venue di: The night of the lightning, Kalda came to dictate her report, paler than my paper. I asked her: “And the sky?” She said: “Nothing.” Her eyebrows still smelled singed. I didn't write anything. I left the line blank. She'll fill it in when she's ready.
textes.Le soir de la fête du port, il n'y a plu: On the night of the harbour festival, there isn't a free table at Paulo's. And yet, every year, when I turn up at ten, a plate is waiting for me at the end of the counter, under a tea towel, with the spoon on top. I taste it. I say: “Something's missing.” He slaps me on the back. It's our tradition.
textes.Le soir de la grande panne, plus d'encei: The night of the big power cut, no more speakers. I took a traffic cone from the Scrapyard and sang into it, while Tapage pedalled Fusible's dynamo bike for two spotlights. The whole Hall sang with me. It was the best sound of my life. Without a single knob.
textes.Le soir de la grande panne, plus rien ne: The night of the big power cut, nothing worked: no sound, no lights. I got Tapage pedalling the dynamo bike to power two spotlights. Larsen sang into a traffic cone to replace the speakers. We finished the concert. It was the best one of the year.
textes.Le soir de la première de « Rodrigue, l': On the opening night of “Rodrigue, Blade of the Twilight”, he got on stage to protest about the chorus. He took one step, his cape caught on my music stand, and he fell into the audience. Right onto Master Hugues. Hugues cried with laughter. The whole room applauded. Rodrigue got up and bowed. He's always known how to bow.
textes.Le soir de la tempête où sa lentille s'e: The night of the storm when his lens cracked, the lighthouse was only half lit. I came in by guesswork, by compass and by ear. As I came alongside, I saw a figure right up top, on the gallery, in the full wind, following me with a lantern in his hand. We've never talked about it.
textes.Le soir de ma nomination comme professeu: On the evening I was appointed teacher, he took me to the top of the Academy tower. He spread his wings, showed me the whole city lit up, and said: “Each of those lights was lit by someone who learned.” Then he added: “Don't burn the tower. It has suffered enough.”
textes.Le soir de ma nomination, Corentin a rac: The evening I was appointed, Corentin told the tavern the story of “the admiral who commanded a bathtub”. Everyone laughed, me too, out of politeness. The next day, he came to the harbour office and told me, just me, about the night Katell held the helm to the very end. Not a single joke. I've never forgotten it.
textes.Le soir de ma première coupe, Trèfle a f: The evening of my first cup, Trèfle baked a cake shaped like a cup. With a handle. Magnificent. I ate the handle before anyone else, before the speeches even. She yelled. I said: “A champion tastes his cup.” She said: “A champion waits.” Fine. She's right. But the handle was delicious.
textes.Le soir de ma première leçon, quand la T: The evening of my first lesson, when the Tower started shining in the middle of the night, Berthe thought it was dawn. She opened the inn and served eggs to wizards in their nightshirts. I came to apologise. She served me eggs too. I said thank you, and good night. She said: “Good morning, more like.” She was right.
textes.Le soir de mes soixante-dix ans, toute l: On my seventieth birthday, the whole tavern called for the shipwreck. At the end, Gwenola put out the lanterns, all but the glow of the stove, and everyone sang the old topmen's song, in Breton. Off key. So off key. I've never heard anything more beautiful.
textes.Le soir de mon arrivée, il y a soixante-: The evening I arrived, seventy years ago, a young bear sat down beside me and said: “Twice upon a time…” I had walked for a whole moon. I fell asleep in the middle. He never got over it: since then, nobody hears the end of his stories. I think it's partly my fault.
textes.Le soir de mon arrivée, sans un sou, Ris: The night I arrived, without a penny, Rissole put a pie under my nose and said “eat”. I said I couldn't pay. She said “eat” louder. I ate. The next day, she gave me the bill: “Come back alive from every mission.” I paid it for forty years.
textes.Le soir de mon arrivée, trempé, sans cha: The evening I arrived, soaked, hatless, I walked into the Crâne Fendu and made a speech on the importance of taxation. A big pirate wanted to throw me out. Mama Grog rapped his hand with her rolling pin and served me soup. I ate it to the last spoonful. The best soup of my career.
textes.Le soir de sa demande, après mon oui au: The evening he proposed, after my yes at the third price, he ran through the whole souk shouting: “She haggled! She loves me!” Karim knocked over a basket of slippers. The next day, Rachid sold a carpet at the second price. The only time in his life. He says it was an accident. I say it was love.
textes.Le soir de sa première leçon de maître,: The evening of his first lesson as a master, he wanted to do things properly. The Astrelune Tower started shining like a golden sun, in the middle of the night. The whole town thought it was dawn: Berthe opened the inn and served eggs to wizards in their nightshirts. Aurélien apologised for a week.

The evening of his first lesson as a master, the Astrelune Tower started shining gold, in the middle of the night. I thought it was dawn! I opened the inn, heated the milk, cooked eggs. Wizards in nightshirts turned up rubbing their eyes. Aurélien came to apologise, red as a tomato. He had some eggs.
textes.Le soir de sa première victoire, j'ai fa: The evening of his first win, I made a cake shaped like a cup, with a handle and everything. I put it on the table for the party, I turned round to get the knives: he'd already eaten the handle. “I was checking it was sturdy.” The champion! He had a tummy ache until the next evening.
textes.Le soir des aurores, je descends parfois: On aurora nights, I sometimes go down to the foot of the Spire to bring Volt some tea. I once caught him talking to the Heart, very softly, the way you talk to an old dog. I left without a sound. He doesn't know that I know. I'll never tell him.
textes.Le soir des aurores, je ferme ma bulle e: On aurora nights, I close my bubble and go and watch the sky. Auroras are light healing the sky. That's what I believe. The sky always looks better afterwards.
textes.Le soir des aurores, je laisse le Bazar: On aurora nights, I leave the Bazaar open. The nebula flowers open when the sky lights up. Everyone wants to buy one. I sell them very dear. Well, I think so. I still don't know what's dear.
textes.Le soir des aurores, je prends le troisi: On aurora nights, I take the third bench in the Agora. It's the protocol bench. I decreed it the protocol bench yesterday, but it's very official.
textes.Le soir des aurores, je regarde depuis l: On aurora nights, I watch from the street, sitting on the ground. I don't fly during the auroras. It's the only thing in the sky I don't want to overtake.
textes.Le soir des aurores, je reste dans les j: On aurora nights, I stay in the gardens. Plants love auroras. They all turn towards the sky and blink along. It's their very own party.
textes.Le soir des aurores, la Doyenne descend: On aurora nights, the Elder sometimes comes down to the Spire with a cup of tea. I tell her everything's fine, it's nothing. She nods, puts down the cup and leaves. She never believes me. She's right. That's why I like her.
textes.Le soir des aurores, les dômes deviennen: On aurora nights, the domes turn see-through and take on the colours of the sky. That's why I make them round: so the sky can settle on them everywhere.
textes.Le soir des aurores, tout le monde vient: On aurora nights, everyone comes to the café. I serve star tea with my four arms, so fast the cups fly all by themselves. Once, a cup stayed in orbit. You can still see it go by, on Tuesdays.
textes.Le soir des funérailles de mon père, je: On the evening of my father's funeral, I went down to the tavern. One fizz, two, three. The fourth tasted like spring water. I looked at Ulfa. She was wiping a mug, very busy. I said nothing. She's kept it up ever since, and I've kept up not noticing. A king needs someone to watch over his mug.
textes.Le soir des funérailles du vieux roi, Th: On the evening of the old king's funeral, Thorgal came down to the tavern. One fizz, two, three. The fourth, I filled with water. He drank it without a word. For ninety years now I've been watering down his fizz whenever he looks sad, and he never notices. Well… I think.
textes.Le soir des golems, il est venu boire mo: The evening of the golems, he came to drink some of my moon water. He pulled a terrible face and said “Delicious”. Since then, every time he comes by, I pour him a little glass, and every time he says “Delicious” with the same face. It's our ritual. Rituals are runes too.
textes.Le soir des pots cassés, j'ai poursuivi: The evening of the broken pots, I chased Chak all the way to the Cenote. On the way back, I found Ix Sak outside her house, at her loom, dying of laughter. She'd botched three rows. She kept them: she says it makes a pattern. She calls it “Ix Chab in a temper”. It's a very pretty pattern. I hate that it's pretty.
textes.Le soir des pots, j'ai entendu crac, cra: The evening of the pots, I heard crack, crack. Two pots, my finest, painted by my mother. Chak was there, ball in hand, looking as innocent as a jaguar next to a plucked turkey. I came out with my pestle. He ran all the way to the Cenote. So did I. At the water's edge, I had no breath left to shout. So I charged him double. He paid.
textes.Le soir des pots, ma balle a rebondi sur: The evening of the pots, my ball bounced off the wall and broke two of Ix Chab's pots. Bonk, crack, crack. She came out with her pestle. I ran all the way to the Cenote along the sacbé, shouting: “It was the ball!” At the water's edge, she caught me. She looked at me, out of breath, and said: “Tomorrow, double price.” I paid double for a month.
textes.Le soir des quarante-trois coups, j'étai: The night of the forty-three punches, I was on his shoulders, at the Crâne Fendu. I counted out loud, and at the last one I shouted “Forty-three!” so loud that the two brawlers stopped to clap for me. Gros-Louis said I'd stopped a fight all by myself. I'm the only cabin boy who's done that. I think.
textes.Le soir des résultats, on proclame : « U: On results night, they announce: “Unanimous minus one vote.” The whole square turns towards the grocery. Colette, behind her window, raises her pencil. Every time. Eighteen years I've given my victory speeches looking at that pencil. It keeps a man modest.
textes.Le soir du dauphin, Zoé était sur la pla: The night of the dolphin, Zoé was on the beach. I was dancing in the water, the dolphin jumped, I turned to her and yelled. She gave me two thumbs up. The next day she was telling everyone “almost”. But right then, bro, she gave me two thumbs up. I remember it really well.
textes.Le soir du jour où je l'ai ramené à la b: The evening of the day I brought him back at the helm, he told the story at the party, standing on a table. In his version, the channel was full of reefs, there was fog, a storm and a shark. There was none of that. I let him tell it. It was nice, being the hero of a song.
textes.Le soir du nuage, il a hurlé « Trois-mât: The night of the cloud, he yelled “Three-master to port!”. I had the cannons loaded, the whole crew on deck, Petit-Pierre hidden under a bucket. The three-master stretched out, then turned into a sheep. Fil-de-Fer scrubbed the deck for a week. Ever since, when a cloud goes by, the crew salutes it.
textes.Le soir du premier concert de la Fronde,: On the night of the Fronde's first concert, thirty years ago, someone “borrowed” my big tongs to bang out a rhythm on. I crossed the Bridge, furious. I heard the sound of my tongs. It was beautiful. I stayed till the end. They gave them back the next day, with a sticker. Since then, they borrow them for every concert.
textes.Le soir du punch, elle m'a renversé le v: The punch night, she spilled the glass right down my shirt. She grabbed a tea towel, she was scrubbing, saying sorry, sorry, all red. I didn't move. I said: “It's nothing, it smells nice.” I didn't wash that shirt for a week. It smelled of coconut. Then it rained. Oh well.
textes.Le soir où Barnabé est passé à la teuf,: The night Barnabé dropped by the party, he did three steps, right on the kick, Gaston on his shoulder. Three! Everyone cheered. He says it was cartography, that he was measuring the dance floor. Bro, I saw his shoulders. That was dancing. Legend.
textes.Le soir où Doc lui a taillé un dentier e: The evening Doc carved him a set of walnut-wood dentures, Sans-Dents came to dinner wearing them, all proud. On the third mouthful, the dentures stayed in the stew. I didn't see. I served it to Gros-Louis. He bit into it and said: “Good stew, but a bit tough.” Sans-Dents never put them back in.
textes.Le soir où Fanny m'a envoyée valser d'un: The night Fanny sent me flying with one big gesture, I landed in Tchoum's arms. He didn't let go right away. He just said: “… You okay?”, and went bright red under his beanie. The whole dance floor saw. Nobody has ever mentioned it again. Me, I think about it.
textes.Le soir où Lyra est partie veiller l'arb: The evening Lyra left to watch over the tree for good, I gave her my old blanket and a single piece of advice: “Talk to the humans.” It took her two centuries to follow it. She still sleeps under the blanket. My feet have been cold ever since. It's a cold that makes me happy.
textes.Le soir où Léa n'a pas voulu de ma rose,: The evening Léa didn't want my rose, I took it back to Rose's. I didn't know what to do with it. She put it in a vase on her counter, with a label: “In the meantime.” Every time I go by, it's still standing, much longer than a normal rose. I think Rose talks to it.
textes.Le soir où Léa pleurait sur le balcon vo: The evening Léa was crying on the next balcony, I passed her a square of chocolate over the railing. She took it without a word. Then a second. At the fourth, she told me about the ring. At the sixth, I told her: “Husbands get lost and found again.” There was no chocolate left. But she was smiling.
textes.Le soir où Marcel a réclamé son augmenta: The night Marcel asked for his raise, a man in the front row was clapping by banging his wooden leg on the bench. After the show, he offered me a place on his brig. I asked him why me. He said: “Because you put the knife down.” I followed him for that answer.
textes.Le soir où Velours a cousu un patch des: The evening Velours sewed Bilge Rats patches on their bandanas, the dogs heard Clou's guitar from far away. All six howled at the same time, like a choir. Rouille said they were the best backing singers on the island. Since then, they howl at every concert. In rhythm.
textes.Le soir où des pirates l'ont déposé sur: The night some pirates dropped him on the quay, he had nothing left, not even his hat. He came into the Crâne Fendu, soaking wet, and gave the customers a speech on the importance of taxes. Gros-Louis wanted to throw him out. Me, I served him a soup. The next day, he was governor. I still wonder if it was my soup.
textes.Le soir où elle est arrivée au temple, p: The evening she arrived at the temple, during the storm, she was ten and trembling like a reed. I was asleep on a bench. She woke me by falling on me. I gave her a blanket, a candle and a piece of bread. She fell asleep on the next bench. In the morning I knew she'd stay. She had folded the blanket into a perfect square.
textes.Le soir où il a chanté mon couplet pour: The night he sang my verse for the first time, the whole Crâne Fendu stamped their feet. I was so happy that I lifted him up, him, his stool and his fiddle, and put him on the counter. He played the ending up there. Mama Grog said if the counter broke, I'd pay for it. It didn't break. Almost.
textes.Le soir où il a dansé sur la grande tabl: The night he danced on the big table, after the Forge Festival, the table cracked in the middle of a verse. The king stayed standing on one half, mug raised, and finished his song. Nobody dared laugh until the end. After that, they did. The table still wobbles. I won't replace it: it's a monument.
textes.Le soir où il a débarqué sur le quai, il: The evening he landed on the quay, he had an axe and a loaf of bread. I asked him what he could do. He said: “Chop.” I said: “We board tomorrow.” He asked: “And when do we eat?” I hired him for the second answer.
textes.Le soir où il a fini les portes, je me s: The evening he finished the gates, I leant in to look. Poof! One spark, and half my beard was gone. Borin laughed so hard he dropped his hammer on his foot. We both limped for a week, him from his foot, me from my chin. We've been arguing ever since. It's our way of being friends.
textes.Le soir où il a joué pour la première fo: The night he played for the first time, I dropped my bow. He carried on alone for ten minutes, without a smile, perfectly in time. Then he said: “Shall we pick it up again?”
textes.Le soir où il a misé la Morue contre un: The night he bet the Cod against a barrel of rum, I took the helm apart and hid it under my hammock. If he lost, the others would have got a sloop that went round in circles. He won. The next day, I put the helm back, whistling. Now, when he bets big, I sit next to him with a screwdriver. He gets it.
textes.Le soir où il a perdu son alliance, je l: The night he lost his ring, I lent him my big punch ladle to dig with. It was the sturdiest tool in the beach hut. He dug until midnight and found two bottle caps, a sandal and a furious crab. The next day, I served the punch by the cup. The ladle smelled of sand for a month.
textes.Le soir où il avait perdu sa voix, j'ai: The night he lost his voice, I sang in his place at the tavern. I didn't know the words, so I shouted them, making them up. “THE DRAGON OF BARBE-DE-FER WAS AS BIG AS A HOUSE!” Master Hugues cried with joy. Bertrand, at the back, was holding his head. But he tapped his foot in time. I saw it.
textes.Le soir où j'ai chanté son couplet pour: The night I sang his verse for the first time, he was so pleased that he lifted me, my stool and my fiddle, and set me down on the bar. I finished the song up there, my head among the lanterns. Mama Grog shouted that he'd pay for the bar. The bar creaked, but it held. So did I. Just about.
textes.Le soir où j'ai collé les avis à l'enver: The evening I stuck the notices on upside down, it was raining. I took shelter in the graffitied lighthouse. A woman with turquoise hair was there, with a flask. She poured me a violet lemonade. I cried, then I laughed, then I told her everything. It was Sirène. Since then, every Thursday, we meet at the lighthouse.
textes.Le soir où j'ai compris ce que voulait l: The evening I understood what the captain wanted, I told only one person: Zohra. “A carpet that doesn't exist, can you imagine? Don't tell a soul.” That very evening, Hassan was asking me how the carpet was going. Then Saïd. Then the amin. Zohra swears she only told Halima. Halima swears she told no one.
textes.Le soir où j'ai débarqué avec ma hache,: The evening I turned up with my axe, she asked me what I could do. I said “chop”. She said “we board tomorrow”. I asked when we ate. She smiled. Just once, but I saw it. The next day, we took the Shark. The day after, I had my soup.
textes.Le soir où j'ai fini les portes de la ci: The evening I finished the city gates, Grimli leant in to admire the work. A spark jumped. Half his beard went up in smoke, poof, just like that. He said: “It'll grow back finer.” He's been saying it for a hundred years. We've been arguing for a hundred years. Hilda says she's winning.
textes.Le soir où j'ai misé la Morue contre un: The night I bet the Cod against a barrel of rum, Coquille took the wheel apart and hid it under her hammock: “If you lose, they'll get a sloop that can't turn.” I won, of course. The next day, she put the wheel back on, whistling. Since then, when I bet big, she sits next to me with a screwdriver.
textes.Le soir où j'ai perdu toutes mes gouttes: The evening I lost all my drops, Mélisse laughed. And then, that night, I found an empty bottle outside my door, with the words: “For the next ones.” I put it on my windowsill. I've never put anything in it. It's lucky that way, empty.
textes.Le soir où j'étais enroué, plus de voix,: The night I was hoarse, no voice, no “boom-boom”: if I can't sing it, I can't play it! I stayed on the bench, and Bourru played all alone. The whole village danced in slow motion, like they were wading through mud. I stamped my foot to help them. Nobody listened. Bourru, though, looked very pleased.
textes.Le soir où je l'ai mis au défi, il est p: The evening I dared him, he set off for the graveyard whistling very loudly. I followed him through the spyglass from the bow. I saw him reach the gate, stop, scratch his head… and come back so fast he overtook a dog. When he got back, he said: “Saw nothing. Fireflies.” He was white as a sheet.
textes.Le soir où je lui ai demandé si je pouva: The evening I asked her if I could eat a whole pie without her serving me seconds, she said yes. I ate the pie, down to the last bite, and she put a second pie in front of me. “That's not seconds, that's a new pie.” I found the argument most chivalrous.
textes.Le soir où je pleurais sur le balcon, un: The night I was crying on the balcony, a hand came over the railing, holding a square of chocolate. Then a voice: “Gérard arrived late to our own wedding. He was photographing the church.” I laughed between sobs, it made a noise like a seal. She passed over a second square. “For the seal,” she said.
textes.Le soir où je suis arrivé à la Fronde, j: The evening I arrived in the Fronde, I said only one word all night, around the brazier. The word was “thanks”. Brasero said: “That one repeats what the rock says.” The next day, everyone was calling me Écho. My real first name, I whispered to the Chasm, from the Bridge. It sent it back to me three times. Then it kept it.
textes.Le soir où je suis arrivée, Mamie m'a do: The night I arrived, Mamie gave me a studded scarf that was far too big. I slept with it for three months. One day, she asked me to give it back. She shortened it, added a red stud and gave it back to me. She said: “Now it's your size. And so are you.”
textes.Le soir où je suis partie veiller l'Arbr: The evening I left to watch over the Tree, he gave me his old blanket and a single piece of advice: “Talk to the humans. They live shorter lives than we do, but they go further.” The blanket smelled of moss and old books. I still sleep under it.
textes.Le soir où la Perle de l'avenue a dispar: The evening the avenue's Pearl vanished, he asked me how it had happened. I said I hadn't seen anything. That was true, in a way. He looked at me with his scroll eyes, and he didn't write anything. I think it's the only time Abyssos has ever written nothing.
textes.Le soir où la baleine est passée au-dess: The evening the whale passed over the palace, I ran all the way to the Gate to tell him. He took one step, then he stayed put. So I sang him the whale, the whole whale, for an hour, so he could see her anyway. His eyes were closed. He was smiling.
textes.Le soir où la balle de Chak a cassé ses: The evening Chak's ball broke two of her pots, Ix Chab chased him across the whole square, then along the white sacbé, all the way to the Cenote. With her pestle! Chak ran shouting: “It was the ball! It was the ball!” I was weaving in front of the house. I missed three rows, I was laughing so hard. I kept them. They make a pretty pattern.
textes.Le soir où la peau de son bendir a crevé: The night his bendir skin split, in the middle of the festival, he ran to my table, grabbed a tray and played on it until midnight. The square danced twice as hard. The tray came back dented all over. I never wanted to straighten it. It's on the wall, next to Mâchefer's. Its dents are in rhythm.
textes.Le soir où le Zéphyr a débarqué douze vo: The evening the Zéphyr landed twelve travellers, I offered seaweed beds at the breach, “no risk of falling”. I got eight, Pierrick four. The next day, my eight had sea fleas and all went over to him. He charged them double. I was proud of him. I didn't tell him.
textes.Le soir où les golems se sont réveillés,: The evening the golems woke up, Bramm came in without a word, grey as his gate. I didn't ask anything. I set down his mug, sat across from him, and kept quiet. A whole hour! Everyone thought I was ill. On his way out, he said: “Thanks.” A whole word. A record.

The evening the golems woke, I walked into the Blazing Mug without a word. Ulfa asked nothing. She set down my mug, sat across from me, and kept quiet. Ulfa. Quiet. A whole hour. It's the kindest thing anyone has ever done for me.
textes.Le soir où ma mère m'a passé la boussole: The evening my mother handed me the compass, I went to the Bordée alone, in a uniform too big for me. I didn't know what to say to anyone. Gwenola served me a sparkling apple and sat beside me until closing, without a word. I've never had better advice.
textes.Le soir où mon bendir a crevé, j'ai fini: The night my bendir split, I finished the festival on one of his trays. I dented it. A lot. I wanted to pay for it. He said: “Tap. No.” And he never hammered it straight. When people ask him what that dent is, he answers: “It's a festival.”
textes.Le soir tombe, les aurores viennent, Vib: Evening falls, the auroras come, Vibrato plays, Prisme dances; and I, on my bench, I write; and nothing rhymes. But it's beautiful. That makes up for it.
textes.Le soir tombe. C'est l'heure où les gens: Evening is falling. It's when people get together.
textes.Le soir, Achille me lit ses poèmes sur l: In the evening, Achille reads me his poems on the terrace. I pretend to sleep through the long ones. He pretends not to notice.
textes.Le soir, Babette s'arrête à la boulanger: In the evening, Babette stops at the bakery before going home. She always asks me, casually: “Did Clovis come by this morning?” I say yes. She smiles. Then she leaves with a loaf. One day, I asked her why she always asked. She said: “To know if the world is turning properly.” I think she knows things.
textes.Le soir, Boulon vient au feu. On s'assoi: In the evening, Boulon comes to the fire. We sit. We watch. Once, four hours, not a word. When I left, I patted him on the shoulder. He said: “Thanks.” I don't know why he said thanks. I think I do. I could have said thanks too.
textes.Le soir, Joe me laisse donner les graine: In the evening, Joe lets me give out the seeds. Bartholomé, the oldest, always pinches my finger a bit. Joe says it's a kiss. One evening, Bartholomé stared at me and said: “The skull, the skull.” I got shivers all over. Joe says he says that to everyone. I still slept with the lantern on.
textes.Le soir, Kevin s'accoude à mon comptoir: In the evening, Kevin leans on my counter and, instead of having a quiet drink, he does push-ups on it. Push-ups on the counter, between the glasses! Once, he knocked over a pineapple. The customers clap, the glasses shake, and I count. He cheats: he barely bends his elbows.
textes.Le soir, La Conque est pleine. Ça parle: In the evening, La Conque is full. People talk about the line, the Singer, the folk up top. Marius tells of his trips down, Ernest tells the news, and I fill the bowls. A shell is made for keeping voices warm.
textes.Le soir, La Marmite est pleine. On chant: In the evening, La Marmite is full. We sing a little, laugh a lot, Ferdinand tells the same train story as usual, and everyone pretends they've never heard it. That's what a canteen is: a home with more chairs.
textes.Le soir, Lentille dépose son pain de la: In the evening, Lentille leaves yesterday's bread on my middle shelf. I wrote in chalk: “Yesterday's bread, today's heart.” One morning, instead of the bread, there was a child's drawing: a rat eating a baguette. I put it up. It's the most beautiful object in the Free Shop.
textes.Le soir, Lumi me prête trois lucioles po: In the evening, Lumi lends me three fireflies to sort my seeds. I named them Pip, Acorn and Peanut. Peanut glows the brightest, but she steals the other two's honey. That's normal, she's a peanut. Peanuts are greedy.
textes.Le soir, Léonce s'assoit sur mon bras de: In the evening, Léonce sits on my brass arm and I lift him up to my shoulder. From up there, he reports on the Fair like Rosette: “Professor Boum still has his eyebrows!” He says it's his very own airship. I tell him the airship creaks. He says that's its charm.
textes.Le soir, Mademoiselle Sulfura me donne d: In the evenings, Miss Sulfura gives me lessons in secret. I asked her how to make a blue flame. She said I was too little. So the next day, I made a green flame, with a bit of sulphur salt from Zébuline's. You should have seen her face! I didn't tell her about the salt.
textes.Le soir, Maman me dit de rentrer. Je fai: In the evening, Mum tells me to come home. I do one more run. Then one more. Then she whistles three times, and then you really have to go home.
textes.Le soir, Maman me raconte des histoires: In the evening, Mum tells me stories about Dad. That he carried stones as big as cows on his boat. That he sang so out of tune the fish jumped out of the water so they wouldn't have to hear him. I think the fish jumped to hear him better. Mum says it's possible. She smiles with wet eyes.
textes.Le soir, Ortie me fait réciter ses leçon: In the evening, Ortie makes me recite her lessons from the Academy. She knows the answers, I don't. She gives me marks. Yesterday I got four out of twenty in the history of flames. She wrote in the margin: “Dad must work harder.” I had it framed. It hangs in the barracks.
textes.Le soir, Zineb monte un thé à ma chambre: In the evening, Zineb brings tea up to my room, “on her way past”. She sits on the edge of the bed to look at the day's canvas. She stays an hour without a word, except: “The sky is too pink.” The next day, I paint it even pinker. She comes back. She stays two hours.
textes.Le soir, au bassin, l'eau des nuages cou: In the evening, at the pond, the cloud water runs through the channels, and the butterflies come to drink. I sit with them. We don't say anything. We go over the day.
textes.Le soir, au feu, Tapage raconte ses conc: In the evening, by the fire, Tapage tells about his concerts for three hours. I watch the sea. At the end, I say “Hm”. He knows what it means: carry on tomorrow. He carries on. For twenty years. His stories change every time. The whale keeps shrinking. I pretend not to notice.
textes.Le soir, autour du feu de la Plage aux G: In the evening, around the fire on the Pebble Beach, I tell Gravier about my gigs for three hours. He looks at the sea. At the end, he says “Hm”. One single “Hm”. But it's a “Hm” that means “carry on tomorrow”. I know his “Hm” by heart.
textes.Le soir, autour du feu, quand Arc-en-Cie: In the evening, around the fire, when Arc-en-Ciel plays the djembe, I feel as young as a bud.
