textes.Le soir, avant de monter sur scène, j'ai: In the evening, before I go on stage, my hands shake. Always. And then Mouette does her seagull thing, Clou nods, and I'm not scared any more.
textes.Le soir, avant de monter sur scène, je t: In the evening, before going on stage, I drum on everything. The table, the bench, Bricole's back. She says it's my warm-up. I say it's affection. She says affection is gentler.
textes.Le soir, avant le concert, je bois une l: In the evening, before the concert, I have a lemonade at Sirène's bar. She serves it to me with a seagull-shaped straw. She made it for me. I adore her, Sirène.
textes.Le soir, avant le concert, je regarde la: In the evening, before the concert, I watch the pit fill up from the catwalk. The Strata folk arrive with their helmets, the folk from up top with their hats, the Frondeurs with their mohawks. Everyone ends up the same: sweaty and happy.
textes.Le soir, c'est la fête. Les tambours, le: In the evening, it's party time. Drums, dancers, stars. Come!
textes.Le soir, c'est le meilleur moment : le f: Evening is the best time: the fire, the stars, and the djembes answering each other. We play until Granny Sunflower says “Bedtime!”.
textes.Le soir, c'est le meilleur moment. Les p: Evening's the best time. The fishermen come home, Corentin tells his tales, and someone always ends up singing.
textes.Le soir, c'est moi qui fais le four. Les: In the evening, I'm the one who fires the oven. The focaccias come out all golden, and the smell goes round the whole island. Even the Great Spaghetti opens an eye.
textes.Le soir, c'est mon heure ! La scène de l: Evening is my time! The Guild stage, the candles, the smell of pie… and Master Hugues weeping at the third verse. Always at the third.
textes.Le soir, c'est mon heure ! Les lanternes: Evening is my time! The lanterns light up, Nox does the rounds of the street lamps, and the whole city turns into a big jewellery box.
textes.Le soir, depuis la Promenade, on voit le: In the evening, from the Promenade, you can see the Funicular tube all lit up, climbing towards the cliff. It looks like a string of fairy lights hung at the bottom of the sea. The lanternfish follow it up to the tunnel. They've worked out the timetable. They're more punctual than some passengers.
textes.Le soir, depuis la plage, on voit le pha: In the evening, from the beach, you can see the Port-Azur lighthouse blinking. As if it were dancing with us.
textes.Le soir, depuis le balcon, je regarde le: In the evening, from the balcony, I watch the lanterns light up one by one. It's my favourite moment: my city breathing.
textes.Le soir, du Belvédère de verre, je regar: In the evening, from the Glass Belvedere, I look at the Column. I used to think it stopped at the Square. Now I know it goes on under the ground, down to a station where an old liftkeeper, Anatole, says “Pardon?” to everyone. Barnabé adores him.
textes.Le soir, du balcon de la Guilde, on voit: In the evening, from the Guild balcony, you can see the east: the tunnel, the Frondeurs' Bridge, and behind it, the lights of the Fronde coming on. Then the music starts. I keep watch. From afar. With pride. Don't tell them: they'd play even louder.
textes.Le soir, du balcon, j'écoute la musique: In the evening, from the balcony, I listen to the Fronde's music, across the Bridge. I don't dance any more. But my feet do. All by themselves.
textes.Le soir, en cachette de sa mère, je donn: In the evenings, without her mother knowing, I give Ortie extra lessons in the Academy courtyard. She asked me how to make a blue flame. I told her she was too young. The next day, she turned up with a green flame. I still don't know how she did it.
textes.Le soir, il descend un peu, pour que je: In the evening, he comes down a little so I can talk to him. He says the view is marvellous and that he needs a wee.
textes.Le soir, il raconte. J'écoute. Tout. San: In the evening, he tells stories. I listen. To everything. Without sleeping. He thinks I'm asleep. I know all his stories. And their endings. Except one: the moon that didn't want to set any more. That one, never heard the end. Nobody has. Hrmm. Strange.
textes.Le soir, il vient m'écouter raconter mes: In the evening, he comes to hear me tell my exploits at the tavern. He sits in the front row, elbows on the table, mouth open. One evening, he asked me: “Sir Tancrède, were you scared, against the Giant?” I wanted to say no. I said yes. He nodded, very seriously, and said: “Then that's even cooler.” I nearly cried.
textes.Le soir, j'allume la grande lampe. Elle: In the evening, I light the big lamp. It turns all night. The boats see it, the gulls see it, and Professor Lunette, up there, thinks it's a star winking. I let him believe it. Happy people, you leave them be.
textes.Le soir, j'allume toutes les guirlandes: In the evening, I switch on every string of lights in town in one go. Clack! All of Boucan goes “ooooh”. Every evening. They never get tired of it. Neither do I.
textes.Le soir, j'allume une seule bougie et je: In the evening I light a single candle and read until it goes out. It always goes out at the best part. That's candle spite.
textes.Le soir, j'interroge Papa sur mes leçons: In the evenings, I test Dad on my Academy lessons. He never knows anything. Yesterday, he got four out of twenty in the history of flames. I wrote in the margin: “Dad must work harder.” He had the paper framed and hung it up at the barracks. He says it's his medal.
textes.Le soir, j'écoute la fête depuis mon ban: In the evening, I listen to the festival from my bench. I don't dance any more. But when Lhoucine plays a fast tune, my knees dance all by themselves. Not in time. I folded my arms, to look stern. Lhoucine saw me. He played the same tune three times in a row. I suspect that boy of being a cheat.
In the evening, I listen to the party from my bench. I don't dance anymore. My knees dance on their own, and not in time.
textes.Le soir, je bois un grog de soufre au Di: In the evening I have a hot sulphur punch at the Diable Repu. No spices. I asked.
textes.Le soir, je bois une limonade au bar de: In the evening, I drink a lemonade at Sirène's bar before going on stage. A real punk drinks lemonade: it stings, and it's full of bubbles. Like us.
textes.Le soir, je chante sur la place, et Nene: In the evening, I sing in the square, and Nenetl follows me on the drum. One evening, she sped up, and up, to see if I could keep up. I did. She sped up again. In the end, I was singing so fast that the dancers sat down on the ground. We laughed until midnight. Just in time for the song to the stars.
textes.Le soir, je chante à la fête. Pas pour v: In the evening, I sing at the party. Not to sell. Just for the fun of making the lanterns shake.
textes.Le soir, je colle des affiches avec Pigm: In the evening, I put up posters with Pigment. She paints, I paste, and we argue about the font. It's our way of saying good night.
textes.Le soir, je compte mes trocs de la journ: In the evening, I count up the day's swaps. I've never gained anything, never lost anything… and yet I'm richer every day. That's swapping for you.
textes.Le soir, je danse avec mon Pyrus sur la: In the evening, I dance with my Pyrus on the Great Square. He dances like a drawbridge. I adore him.
textes.Le soir, je danse dans la fosse. Je rent: In the evening, I dance in the pit. I always come home with one button less and one idea more.
textes.Le soir, je danse sur la Grand-Place. Et: In the evening I dance on the Great Square. And I don't set anyone on fire. Well, hardly anyone. Zigomar doesn't count.
textes.Le soir, je danse sur la plateforme de V: In the evening, I dance on the Venus platform. With Balam, when he isn't busy playing jaguar.
textes.Le soir, je descends au Cercle. Même un: In the evening, I come down to the Circle. Even a guard has the right to listen to the drums. Grisou takes over. Well, he tries.
textes.Le soir, je dessine sur la place pendant: In the evening, I draw on the square while Tornade plays ball. I draw Tornade missing. That's a lot of drawings.
textes.Le soir, je donne à boire aux plantes et: In the evening, I give the plants a drink and say goodnight to them. The sulphur roses close up on their own. The peppers, you have to sing them something.
In the evening, I dine at La Grenouille Repue. Not for the frog: to watch the outfits of the adventurers coming home. They're my best models. Especially the failures.
textes.Le soir, je fais de la balançoire sous l: In the evening, I go on the swing under the Eraser Oak. Grandpa Augustin pushes me. He says if I go high enough, I'll touch the walkway. I haven't managed yet.
textes.Le soir, je fais des nœuds pour les enfa: In the evening, I tie knots for the kids. Sailor's knots. They untie them for me. It's a game.
textes.Le soir, je fais la vaisselle en chantan: In the evening, I do the washing-up singing Bilge Rats songs. The plates love it. The glasses a bit less: they vibrate.
textes.Le soir, je fais le tour de la Promenade: In the evening, I walk the length of the Porthole Promenade. I tap each pane: two knocks, then one. Mistress Brunehaut, the Strata blacksmith, taught me: it means “hello, thank you”. I say hello, thank you, to every pane that keeps the sea out. They deserve it.
textes.Le soir, je fais le tour de la fontaine: In the evening, I walk round the fountain and greet Lady Ysolde. I tell her about my day. She never interrupts me. She's my favourite audience.
textes.Le soir, je fais le tour des terrasses e: In the evening, I walk round the terraces and say good night to every tree. There are two hundred and forty. I finish around midnight. The last ones are already asleep.
textes.Le soir, je fais le tour du palais et j': In the evening, I go round the palace and snuff out the unnecessary candles. Her Highness says they cost nothing. The principle, {surnom}. The principle.
textes.Le soir, je fais le tour du rempart. Tou: In the evening, I walk the rampart. All is calm. That's my favourite moment: the one where nothing is running.
textes.Le soir, je fais mes expériences les plu: In the evening, I do my quietest experiments. The neighbours have signed a petition.
textes.Le soir, je fais sécher mes herbes au-de: In the evening, I dry my herbs over the fire. The whole house smells of lavender and thyme.
textes.Le soir, je ferme la grille et je rentre: In the evening, I close the gate and go back to my hut. I listen to the dungeon. It goes “gloop” every ten minutes. That's the King breathing. Well, I think so.
textes.Le soir, je ferme les soupapes, j'éteins: In the evening, I close the valves, put out the big fire, and listen to the forge cooling down. Tick, tick, tick, goes the metal. Pimprenelle says it's saying good night. She's right. As always. It's exhausting.
textes.Le soir, je goûte les potions du jour. P: In the evening, I taste the day's potions. To check them. That's why I sing on my way home.
textes.Le soir, je jongle à l'entrée de la Hall: In the evening, I juggle at the entrance of the Hall while people arrive. With glowing balls Fusible made me. They blink. So do I, a bit, when one lands on my head.
textes.Le soir, je joue au ballon avec les enfa: In the evening, I play ball with the kids and Rustine. I lose on purpose. Tornade knows. He lets me lose on purpose. He's a kind boy.
textes.Le soir, je joue au ballon avec mes deux: In the evening, I play ball with my two little rascals on the square. Tornade cheats, Cerise referees, and Copeau loses on purpose. Me, I whistle. I whistle all the time.
textes.Le soir, je laisse les chiens chez Boulo: In the evening, I leave the dogs with Boulon and go dancing in the pit. They wait for me on his tummy. He doesn't move for two hours. He's a saint.
textes.Le soir, je laisse reposer ma voix. Enfi: In the evening I rest my voice. Well, I try. It won't let me.
In the evening, I read my poems to the Palette. The wells listen. They don't say anything, but they're very good listeners.
textes.Le soir, je lis sur le banc de la Haute-: In the evening I read on the bench in the Upper Town. When there's a storm I don't dare: my hair attracts lightning. I read under my hat.
textes.Le soir, je lis sur mon banc, sous la la: In the evening I read on my bench, under the lantern. Nox goes by and says good evening. Sometimes he gives me a poem. It's the best moment.
textes.Le soir, je longe la Promenade des Hublo: In the evening, I walk along the Porthole Promenade, marking exercise books in my head. Outside, the jellyfish light up, and the lanternfish swim by in neat rows, very well behaved. They have better manners than my class. But my class is funnier.
textes.Le soir, je m'assieds sur mon banc de l': In the evening, I sit on my bench in the Agora and wait for the auroras. I've been watching them for a thousand years. They've never shown me the same colour twice. It's good manners.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois au Belvédère des Ab: In the evening, I sit at the Abyss Belvedere and look into the dark, at the bottom of the Trench. You'd think it was empty. It isn't. Little lights pass through it, very far away. Nobody knows yet what they are. I like that there are still things we don't know.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois au Café Cumulus ave: In the evening, I sit at the Cumulus Café with the day's canvas. Gustave looks at it and always says: “It's even more beautiful than yesterday's.” He doesn't remember yesterday's. That's why he's so kind.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois au Cercle, je regar: In the evening, I sit at the Circle, watch the fire, and I'm already thinking about tomorrow's bread.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois au Diable Repu et j: In the evening, I sit at the Diable Repu and tell Grumbald about my catch. He pretends to listen while drying his glasses. One evening, I told him I'd caught a whale. He answered: “That's nice, dear.” The next day, he bought a bigger cauldron. He was listening, after all. A little.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois au Diable Repu, che: In the evening I sit at the Diable Repu, my husband's place. He serves me a frozen lava, and I tell him about the fishing. He pretends to listen. I pretend not to notice.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois au Parc des Brumes: In the evening, I sit in the Mist Park and listen to the Falls turning into mist. Nobody knows exactly at which metre the water becomes cloud. Neither do I. But I have a figure. It's wrong. It's very beautiful.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois au bout du quai et: In the evening, I sit at the end of the quay and tell the seagulls about my day. They tell me about theirs. It's always the same: fish, wind, fish.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois au fond de la taver: In the evening I sit at the back of the tavern. I listen. I don't talk. The others talk enough for four.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois au milieu de la cat: In the evening, I sit in the middle of the cathedral and watch the caps light up one by one. Blue, purple, orange. It's the most beautiful concert on the island. Don't tell Rouille.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois dans la Galerie des: In the evening, I sit in the Greenhouse Gallery, in the middle of the glass tube. Outside, the lanternfish go by in shoals, like paper lanterns. Behind me, my lamps go out one by one. It's the hour when the Greenhouses and the sea say good night to each other.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois devant la porte du: In the evening, I sit by the mill door and listen to the wind die down. It whispers, at that hour. Like Miss Philippine. … Why did I say that? No reason.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois devant le dragon et: In the evening, I sit in front of the dragon and watch him rust. Slowly. Rust is the colour of time passing. It's beautiful.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois près de la Palette,: In the evening, I sit by the Palette and listen to the grass grow. It takes a lot of silence.
In the evening, I sit by the Palette and count the full wells. It's my new hobby.
In the evening, I sit on the Great Square. The children play around me. They call me “the snowman”. I don't correct them.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur la Place et j'é: In the evening, I sit on the Square and listen to the Forge cooling down. Tick, tick. And across the Chasm, the Fronde starts playing. My anvils hum in rhythm. I think they'd like to go dancing.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur la terrasse du: In the evening, I sit on the Council terrace and look out over the clearing. In black and white, it's pretty too. But it looks bored.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur le banc de la B: In the evening, I sit on the bench in the Bay, switch off my lamp, and wait. Sometimes, very high up, an immense shadow passes over the domes. And she sings. The whole Dome goes quiet. Even Ernest. I answer her, very softly, humming against the glass. I'm almost certain she hears me.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur le banc de la G: In the evening, I sit on the Station bench and wait for the last funicular. People come down with bags, hats, and mouths full of news. I harvest it at the exit, like ripe fruit. Marius says I scare the tourists. I don't scare anybody. I just ask a lot of questions.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur le banc de la H: In the evening, I sit on the bench in the Upper Town and look at the houses. I appraise them. I can't help it. This bench is worth at least twelve coins.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur le banc de la P: In the evening, I sit on the bench in the Square and look at it, all golden under the street lamps. Two hundred years old, and not a wrinkle. Well, a few rivets.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur le banc du port: In the evening, I sit on the harbour bench and watch the boats sleep. They all rock together. Like old friends snoring.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur ma mousse, près: In the evening, I sit on my moss, near the fire, and watch the young ones dance. My paws still dance, in my head.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur mon balcon de l: In the evening, I sit on my gallery balcony and watch the Brass Sun turn down its lamp. Everything goes honey-coloured. That's when I hear best: everyone goes quiet. Except the Fronde.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur mon banc de l'E: In the evening, I sit on my bench on the Esplanade and watch the lights of Hautefond, far below. A hundred and twenty years we've been floating. And still that same little urge to go back down and have a look, now and then.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur un banc de la G: In the evening I sit on a bench in the Great Square and I don't stamp anything. Nothing at all. It's very hard. My hand moves on its own.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur un banc de la P: In the evening, I sit on a bench in Cogwheel Square and count my miners coming home. All of them. One by one. When the count is right, I take off my helmet. Not before.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois sur un banc de la p: In the evening, I sit on a bench in the square and watch people go by. Not for the people: for what they're wearing. You learn a lot by looking at sleeves.
In the evening, I sit on a bench on the square and reread my notes from the day. “Bean number twelve: remarkable progress.” An old teacher never stops marking.
In the evening, I sit on a bench on the square, and Noisette tells me about her day. She followed four adventurers, questioned two guards, and petted a frog. Not a giant one. I hope.
textes.Le soir, je m'assois toujours à la même: In the evening I always sit at the same table in the tavern. The one at the back. The table for adventurers who come home empty-handed. Great atmosphere.
textes.Le soir, je m'installe à la Promenade de: In the evening, I settle down on the Porthole Promenade and count the lanternfish. I never get to the end. It gives me something to do tomorrow.
textes.Le soir, je m'installe à une table de la: In the evening I settle at a tavern table and watch the youngsters come back from missions, covered in jelly. It reminds me of my youth. I was covered in jelly too. All the time.
textes.Le soir, je m'échappais pour écouter Gra: In the evenings, I'd slip out to listen to Grandpa Ébène on the Grand Square. My favourite story was the one about the princess who wanted to see snow. She crossed the Nine Circles to touch a snowflake, and came back saying that the cold is mostly there so we'll love the fire. It took me a long time to understand.
textes.Le soir, je m'étire au coin du feu. Sept: In the evening, I stretch by the fire. Seven times. It's the perfect number of stretches.
textes.Le soir, je me tiens sur le parvis et je: In the evening I stand on the temple steps and watch the town light up. Those are the finest prayers, windows lighting up. They say nothing, and they say everything.
textes.Le soir, je monte au Belvédère tout seul: In the evening, I go up to the Belvedere on my own to practise. I stay five minutes near the railing. Yesterday, six. Mistress Capucine says I'll be ready for the Clouds in… she didn't finish her sentence.

In the evenings, I go up to the Belvedere on my own, to practise. I stay five minutes by the railing. Yesterday, six. Théo is waiting for me on his glass Belvedere, up in the Clouds. I told him “one day”. He brought a chair.
textes.Le soir, je monte au Cercle écouter les: In the evening, I go up to the Circle to listen to the Moonstones. They speak slowly. You have to be patient.
textes.Le soir, je monte au belvédère regarder: In the evening, I go up to the lookout to watch the stars. I count them. There's always one missing. I suspect someone bought it.
textes.Le soir, je monte en haut de la tour, j': In the evening, I climb to the top of the tower, open my wings and look at the city. From above, Pandémonia looks like a birthday cake. With lots of candles.
textes.Le soir, je monte sur la dunette. De là-: In the evening, I climb up to the poop deck. From up there, you can see Stoneheart turn red at sunset. It calms me.
textes.Le soir, je monte sur la terrasse du Con: In the evening, I go up to the Council terrace and watch the sun set. Up here it sets below us, you know. It passes under the island, blushing. Very flattering for the sun.
textes.Le soir, je monte sur le rempart du chât: In the evening I climb onto the castle rampart and wave to the town. The town doesn't wave back. Except Mélusine. She always answers. Very loudly.
textes.Le soir, je monte sur le toit de la Cons: In the evening, I climb onto the roof of the Cannery and listen to the town's trees. There are forty-three of them. I know them all by their first names.
textes.Le soir, je monte sur le toit du garage: In the evening, I climb onto the garage roof with my torch. On the other side, there's Bouton-d'Or with hers. Three blinks: good night. Two: tomorrow. Once, I tried to make a heart. She thought I'd fallen. She wasn't wrong.
textes.Le soir, je monte à la mezzanine de la H: In the evening, I go up to the mezzanine of the Hall and watch all those young folk jumping. It reminds me of the quays at the end of the working day. We jumped too. For joy, and because the concrete was cold.
textes.Le soir, je pose le Couvercle et je pren: In the evening, I put down the Lid and pick up my tambourine. You don't guard a gong during the tarantella. The gong dances too, in its head.
textes.Le soir, je pose le pain qui reste sur u: In the evening, I put the leftover bread on a shelf at the Free Shop, with a sign: “Yesterday's bread, today's heart.” Trocante wrote it in chalk. The next morning, the bread's gone. Sometimes there's a drawing in its place. Once, a thank-you shaped like a rat.
textes.Le soir, je pose mon sac et je danse sur: In the evening, I put down my bag and dance on the Great Square. It's the only time I'm not flying. Well, I hop. That's almost flying.
textes.Le soir, je pousse Lili sur la balançoir: In the evening, I push Lili on the swing. She shouts “higher!” I shout “gentler!” We never hear each other. It's very pleasant.
textes.Le soir, je prends le violon. Macaroni s: In the evening, I take out the violin. Macaroni brings out his tambourine, Sister Penne starts singing, and the whole Borgo starts dancing. We start slowly. We speed up. By the end, I can't feel my fingers, and Nonno Tortellini is dancing with a chair.
textes.Le soir, je prends ma table au Diable Re: In the evening I take my table at the Diable Repu and tell the tale of the ash storm. Grumbald knows it by heart. He mouths the words along with me.
textes.Le soir, je prends un thé au Café Cumulu: In the evening, I have a tea at the Cumulus Café, at my table. I watch people laughing on an island that floats, and I think: that's thanks to four engines, a thousand calculations and a cup of tea. It makes me very proud. Quietly.
textes.Le soir, je prends un thé des sommets au: In the evening, I have a summit tea at the Cumulus Café and tell the day's race to anyone who'll listen. Gustave listens. He's heard the same story four thousand times. He always laughs at the right moment. He's a true friend.
textes.Le soir, je promène les chiots dans les: In the evening, I walk the puppies through the streets. They bark at the street lamps. Nox says good evening to them. They adore him: he smells of lamp wick.
textes.Le soir, je prête trois lucioles à Noise: In the evenings, I lend Noisette three fireflies to sort her seeds. She's given them names: Pip, Acorn and Peanut. Peanut is the brightest, but she eats the other two's honey. Noisette says that's normal, she's a peanut.
textes.Le soir, je raccommode mon filet. Gauber: In the evening, I mend my net. Gaubert tells me about his day. It's always the same: he talked to his turnips. They didn't answer. He's happy.
textes.Le soir, je raconte ma journée à Maman a: In the evening, I tell Mum about my day before bed. Three times. The first time, I tell it fast. The second, I tell the mushrooms. The third, I tell it yawning. Mum says the third is her favourite, because I fall asleep in the middle.
textes.Le soir, je raconte mes exploits à la ta: In the evening I recount my feats at the Guild tavern. Bertrand puts them to song. The songs are even more beautiful than the feats. And the feats never happened in the first place.
textes.Le soir, je raconte mes voyages au Pisto: In the evening, I tell tales of my travels at the Jolly Piston. I exaggerate a bit. Clouds become mountains, seagulls become dragons. Firmin tops up my hot chocolate every time I invent a dragon.
textes.Le soir, je ramène Bernadette au dépôt e: In the evening, I take Bernadette back to the depot and tell her about my day. She goes “pfff” as she cools down. That's her way of saying: “I know, I was there.”
textes.Le soir, je range mes fioles par couleur: In the evening, I sort my vials by colour. Then by smell. Then I mix them.
textes.Le soir, je regarde la cité s'allumer de: In the evening, I watch the city light up from the promenade. All those windows are people still inventing.
textes.Le soir, je regarde la mer depuis le qua: In the evening, I watch the sea from the quay. The neon lights are reflected in the water. It's as if the city were painting itself.
textes.Le soir, je regarde la mer. Des fois, je: In the evening, I watch the sea. Sometimes I see a sea serpent. Sometimes it's a log. Sometimes it's the honey drink.
textes.Le soir, je regarde les lumières des île: In the evening, I watch the lights of the islands, far below. Each light is a house. I count them. There are more and more. That's good news, I think.
textes.Le soir, je regarde les méduses de ciel: In the evening, I watch the sky jellyfish from the Observatory bridge. During the auroras, they all light up. Like lanterns swimming in the sky. I cry every time. With happiness.
textes.Le soir, je regarde les îles depuis le b: In the evening, I watch the islands from the edge. The lights of Port-Azur, the lanterns of Braise, the pirates' fires. I know them all by heart. By heart… from afar, of course.
textes.Le soir, je remballe mon étal et je fais: In the evening, I pack up my stall and take a stroll through the Lower Town. I look at people's vegetable patches. I don't criticise. I just think, that's all. Very loudly.
textes.Le soir, je rentre dans ma niche de rech: In the evening, I go back to my charging kennel, near the Greenhouses. While charging, I dream. I dream that the trees say hello to me. They have very slow voices. It takes three nights for a single sentence.
textes.Le soir, je rentre tôt. Les légendes, il: In the evening, I go home early. Legends must be left to sleep at night. Otherwise, they get restless and change their endings.
textes.Le soir, je rentre à la ferme. Les navet: In the evening, I go back to the farm. The turnips sleep under the soil. I wish them goodnight. Germaine says it's ridiculous. She does it too.
textes.Le soir, je rentre à la forge et je rang: In the evening, I go home to the forge and sort my bolts by size. Then by colour. Then by the ones I like best. Mum says that's why I go to bed late.
textes.Le soir, je reste au labo. Les aurores ?: In the evening, I stay at the lab. The auroras? I study them through the window. Theoretically, I could go and see them. But I have an experiment on the boil. There's always an experiment on the boil.
textes.Le soir, je reste devant mon conteneur e: In the evening, I sit outside my container and watch the pigeons come home. They fly in formation. Tonight, they drew a heart. Or a bean. The future is blurry, but it's cute.
textes.Le soir, je retransmets le concert en di: In the evening, I broadcast the concert live from the wheelhouse of the Freighter. I commentate the pogo like a match: “And Boulon jumps… he jumps… HE HAS JUMPED!”
textes.Le soir, je règle les soucoupes sur l'ai: In the evening, I tune the saucers on the landing pad. During the auroras, the hulls take on every colour. It's the only time I find the saucers more beautiful than their engines.
textes.Le soir, je teste mes fusées sur la jeté: In the evening, I test my rockets on the jetty, near the lighthouse. Captain Charbonnel says I scare the fish. The fish have never said anything to me.
textes.Le soir, je tiens le comptoir des boucho: In the evening, I run the earplug counter at the Hall. Larsen says it's the most important stall in town. He shouts it, of course.
textes.Le soir, je travaille à l'établi, sous l: In the evening, I work at my bench, under the lamp. It's the hour when the springs are at their calmest. We get along well, the springs and I. We don't like noise.
textes.Le soir, je traîne dans la rue en bas du: In the evening, I hang around the street below the market, I watch the Column light up, and I listen. Can you hear the music rising from the shaft? That's home. They start playing when the sun goes down.
textes.Le soir, je vais au Bazar de Nébula voir: In the evening, I go to Nébula's Bazaar to see what's new. Yesterday she had a “colander”. A bowl full of holes! What for? To hold water, surely. I bought it. It leaks. I'm studying it.
textes.Le soir, je vais au Belvédère de verre e: In the evenings, I go to the glass Belvedere and watch the Column light up, far below. Somewhere down there, Barnabé is looking up. Well, trying to.
In the evening, I go to the glass Belvedere and look at the sea, far below. It sparkles. It's teeny tiny. Théo says it's really big in real life. I don't know if I believe him.
textes.Le soir, je vais au Belvédère des Abysse: In the evening, I go to the Abyss Belvedere, lean against the glass, and gaze at the darkness right at the bottom of the Trench. Sometimes a little light comes on, very far away, and goes out. Nobody knows what it is. One day I'll go and say hello to it.
textes.Le soir, je vais au Piston Joyeux, à ma: In the evening, I go to the Jolly Piston, to my table by the counter. Firmin serves me a cinnamon hot chocolate. My cinnamon. He says it's his. We argue about it every evening. It's delicious.
textes.Le soir, je vais au bord de l'étang des: In the evening I go to the edge of the pond in the Gardens. The mushrooms glow, my lanterns glow, and the water reflects the Brass Sun as it dims. Three lights answering one another. I'm trying to understand what they're saying.
textes.Le soir, je vais au concert avec tous me: In the evening, I go to the concert wearing all my jewellery. Under the stage lights, I throw reflections everywhere. Rivet says I'm the Fronde's disco ball. It's the nicest compliment anyone's ever paid me.
textes.Le soir, je vais au feu de la Plage aux: In the evening, I go to the fire on Pebble Beach. Gravier is already there. We sit down. We look at the fire. Once, we stayed four hours without saying a word. When he left, he patted me on the shoulder. It was the best evening I'd had all year.
textes.Le soir, je vais au puits de la Basse-Vi: In the evening, I go to the well in the Lower Town to fetch fresh water for my potions. And to check there's no slime in it. Sometimes there is. I bottle them.
textes.Le soir, je vais au quai regarder la mer: In the evening I go to the quay to look at the sea. The seagulls have never asked me for an update. I like them.
textes.Le soir, je vais dans la fosse avec un c: In the evening, I go into the pit with a sketchbook and a stick of charcoal. I draw the people jumping. They never keep still. So I draw lines that move. Brasero says it's my best period.
textes.Le soir, je vais dans la fosse de la Hal: In the evening, I go into the pit at the Hall. I jump very gently, so the stage doesn't shake. The little ones hang on to my arms. I'm a merry-go-round.
textes.Le soir, je vais dans la fosse et je sur: In the evening, I go into the pit and keep an eye on the steam organ from afar. Forty-two pipes. If one of them coughs, I run. Usually it's number thirty-seven. It's always had weak lungs.
textes.Le soir, je vais dans la fosse, tout au: In the evening, I go into the pit, right at the edge, with my earplugs made of bread. I don't jump. I nod my head. Hard. Bielle says I'm the oldest fan of the Valves. Mostly, I'm the only one who brings them soup afterwards.
textes.Le soir, je vais dans la fosse, tout dev: In the evening, I go into the pit, right at the front, next to Granny Gamelle. She holds me by the hood when the jumping gets too wild. Mum says I have to be home by half past nine. I'm home at half past nine. And two minutes.
textes.Le soir, je vais danser dans la fosse de: In the evening, I go dancing in the pit at the Hall. At the back, on the right. People have already mistaken me for a pile of forgotten clothes. It's my dress: it's made of twenty-two dresses.
textes.Le soir, je vais en haut de la colline a: In the evening, I go to the top of the hill with my torch. On the other side, in Rainville, there's Clapotis with his. We send signals. Three blinks means “good night.” Two means “tomorrow.” We don't have a signal for “come and play” yet.
textes.Le soir, je vais faire un tour dans la B: In the evening, I take a stroll through the Lower Town. I arm-wrestle anyone who wants to. Nobody wants to anymore. Even Clovis gave up, and he lifts sacks of flour all day long.
textes.Le soir, je vais flotter aux Thermes. Je: In the evening I go and float at the Baths. I float very well. Bulle says I'm the only customer who never sinks. It's thanks to the brioches.
textes.Le soir, je vais jusqu'à l'entrée de la: In the evening, I go as far as the entrance of the Howling Hall. I don't go in. I listen through the door, and I tap the beat on the wall. The stand-in drummer always gets it wrong. I don't. But nobody hears me. It's better that way. I think.
textes.Le soir, je vais lire les nouveaux contr: In the evening, I go and read the new contracts on the Guild board. Tomorrow morning, I'll shout them out on the square. I have to rehearse. In my head. Quietly. Well, as quietly as possible.
textes.Le soir, je vais m'asseoir au Temple de: In the evening I go and sit in the Temple of Dawn. Not to pray. It's the only place in Montjoie where nobody asks me for anything. Father Clotaire is asleep. It's perfect.
textes.Le soir, je vais m'asseoir aux Jardins d: In the evening I go and sit in the Ash Gardens, near my mother's herbs. It's the only place in the city where nobody asks me for a potion against hiccups.
textes.Le soir, je vais regarder Bernadette ren: In the evening, I go and watch Bernadette come back to the depot. Grandpa Ferdinand lets me pull the whistle. Once, no more. The last whistle of the evening is for Pimprenelle. She can't hear it. But it's for her anyway.
textes.Le soir, je vais sur le belvédère. Je re: In the evening, I go up to the lookout. I watch the welcome buoy way down below, on the sea. If anyone climbs onto it, I'm ready. I always have a speech in my pocket.
textes.Le soir, je vais à l'auberge d'Ulric. Il: In the evening, I go to Ulric's inn. He serves me frog. I eat it while looking it in the eye. That's my little revenge.
textes.Le soir, je vais à la Promenade des Hubl: In the evening, I go to the Porthole Promenade and look up, way up, to where the water gets a little lighter. Behind it, there's the sky. I know it. I say good evening to the sky, even though I can't see it. Like saying good evening to someone in another room.
textes.Le soir, je vais écouter Calcine jouer s: In the evening, I go and listen to Calcine play on the Great Square. In the front row. Eyes closed. I sigh at the right moments. Well, I think they're the right moments.
textes.Le soir, je venais pleurer dans le jardi: In the evenings, I'd come and cry in the hotel garden, among the thyme. A lady arrived with a basket and scissors. She sat down beside me and said: “Lime blossom, lemon balm, and a pinch of Rose's lavender. For a broken heart.” The next evening, there was a steaming cup waiting for me on the bench.
textes.Le soir, je vois Clapotis et Bouton-d'Or: In the evening, I see Clapotis and Bouton-d'Or signalling each other with torches, from one end of the island to the other. I watch them from my window. I think it's… so lovely. I've never told them.
textes.Le soir, je… je fais une promenade. Seul: In the evening, I… I go for a walk. Alone. Very quiet. Nothing to do with a concert. I hate noise. (She quickly tucks a fake moustache into her bag.)
textes.Le soir, l'auberge se remplit. Ceux qui: In the evening, the inn fills up. The ones coming back from the lake tell how they got swallowed. I serve them frog. It's a delicious revenge.
textes.Le soir, la brume monte du Bois Tors. La: In the evening, the mist rises from the Twisted Wood. The ball sees more clearly then. I see less.
textes.Le soir, la longue-vue ne sert plus à ri: In the evening, the spyglass is no use anymore. So I go down to the Council and draw what I saw during the day. In charcoal, naturally.
textes.Le soir, la place danse. Je joue jusqu'à: In the evening, the square dances. I play until my fingers smoke. Literally: they smoke. We're demons.
textes.Le soir, la taverne est pleine. Pirates: In the evening, the tavern is full. Pirates on one side, fishermen on the other, and me in the middle with my cudgel.
textes.Le soir, la terrasse est pleine : Nova e: In the evening, the terrace is full: Nova and her calculations, Captain Zéphyrine and her victories, Ombeline and her sunsets. And me in the middle, with my tray. The happiest cloud of all.
textes.Le soir, le Cœur-Brasier ronronne. Je l': In the evening, the Ember Heart purrs. I listen to it, I talk to it, and sometimes it answers. Old keepers get a little odd. It's normal.
textes.Le soir, le Piston Joyeux est plein. On: In the evening, the Jolly Piston is packed. People laugh, play cards, Héloïse tells of her travels, Rosalie tells of everything else. And me, I serve. I'm the happiest man in the Middle Town. And the most out of breath.
textes.Le soir, le Repu est plein : le Capitain: In the evening, the Diable Repu is packed: the Captain tells his storm, Kraxx sneezes, my Moloka laughs. It's the loveliest noise in the world.
textes.Le soir, le bar est plein, tout le monde: In the evening, the bar is packed, everyone shouts their order at the same time, and I never miss one. I have a notebook. And a very good memory. And Larsen repeating the orders into the mic, which doesn't help.
textes.Le soir, le feu. Boulon vient. On ne dit: Evenings, the fire. Boulon comes. We say nothing. It's good.
textes.Le soir, le lac devient un miroir. Je re: In the evening, the lake becomes a mirror. I watch the moon settle on it. I haven't tired of it in sixty years.
textes.Le soir, le vent se couche. Moi aussi. O: In the evening, the wind goes to bed. So do I. We say good night to each other.
textes.Le soir, le violon. La tarentelle commen: In the evening, the violin. The tarantella starts slowly, then we speed up, and speed up, and by the end nobody knows where their feet are. That's the best part.
textes.Le soir, les crocodiles sortent. Je rent: In the evening the crocodiles come out. I bring in my boat, and my toes.
textes.Le soir, les histoires ont meilleur goût: Stories taste better in the evening. It's the shadows that give them their salt.
textes.Le soir, les hérons viennent voler mes p: In the evening, the herons come to steal my fish. I throw clods of mud at them. They think it's funny.
textes.Le soir, les jours de concert, la musiqu: In the evening, on concert nights, the Fronde's music rises up the Column's shaft from the Strata. Boom, boom, boom, until midnight. Above the clouds! I close my windows. I open them again a little. To check whether it's still as loud. It's still as loud.
textes.Le soir, ma petite. Elles sont meilleure: In the evening, little one. They're better in the evening.
textes.Le soir, mon auberge est pleine de sorci: In the evening, my inn is full of tired wizards. They all tell of their great deeds. Half of it is true.
textes.Le soir, on boit le thé devant l'échoppe: In the evening, we drink tea in front of the workshop, without talking. Once, he talked. About his father's forge, in a port up north. With my ear, I heard half of it. The good half, I think. I never repeated it to anyone. And you didn't hear it either.
textes.Le soir, on fait un feu sur la plage, av: In the evening, we light a fire on the beach with the others. We grill what we caught, and we talk about what we didn't catch.
In the evening, we play ball on the square. Dad always loses on purpose. I know it. He knows I know it. So I let him lose on purpose, to make him happy. Cerise says we're weird. Mum whistles to referee. It's the best match of the day.
textes.Le soir, on pêche au bout du quai, elle: In the evening we fish at the end of the quay, she and I. She takes her hooks apart to see how they're made; I fish. At the end, I have six sardines and she has an improved hook. We share: she takes three sardines, I take the hook. That's fair.
In the evening, for the gigs.
textes.Le soir, quand Mélisse rince ses flacons: In the evening, when Mélisse rinses her bottles, I drop by to check the sugar at the bottom. It's serious work. There's always too much. I check every evening anyway, in case it changes. She's never noticed.
textes.Le soir, quand Nenetl joue de la flûte-c: In the evening, when Nenetl plays the hummingbird flute, Tlaco lifts his head and sings, ahoooooo! Not sad: happy! So I dance, and everyone claps. It's our act! Nenetl says we're the best performers in Aztlán. After her.
textes.Le soir, quand Tagliatelle sort son viol: In the evening, when Tagliatelle gets out her violin and Macaroni his tambourine, the whole Borgo dances the tarantella. Even Nonno Tortellini. Especially Nonno Tortellini.
textes.Le soir, quand je descends de ma chaise,: In the evening, when I climb down from my chair, cooked like a prawn, Kiki has kept a bucket of ice for me. I put my feet in it and he serves me a “hero's punch”, fruit only. He says it's the official drink of lifeguards. I'm the only one who drinks it. He's very proud of it.
textes.Le soir, quand je ferme l'atelier, je mo: In the evening, when I close the workshop, I go up to my roof terrace and count the lights on the galleon. Seven, above the cannons. The brightest, Bertha's, is one of my eight-pointed stars. The hardest one I know how to pierce. She has good taste, that thief. Deep down, I like it that my lanterns go sailing.
textes.Le soir, quand la Grande Perle devient v: In the evening, when the Great Pearl turns violet, I put on my violet dress. We match. At my age, I've every right to match my sun.
textes.Le soir, quand la tarentelle commence, j: In the evening, when the tarantella starts, I put my guard's glare away and pick up my tambourine. Nobody knew I played. The first time, Tagliatelle dropped her bow. Now I'm the one who keeps the beat. One, two, three… There, three is allowed.
textes.Le soir, quand la taverne se vide, je m': In the evening, when the tavern empties, I sit for a while in the square. My feet thank me. My ladle, though, gets bored.
textes.Le soir, quand le Soleil de Laiton devie: In the evening, when the Brass Sun turns amber, my Gardens all light up at once. Blue, green, orange, purple. People come and sit on the bench and stop talking. It's the most beautiful silence in the Strata.
textes.Le soir, quand le soleil se couche derri: In the evening, when the sun sets behind Mount Bolognese, the sauce shines like red gold. That's when I pray best. And when I'm hungriest.
textes.Le soir, quand les Soupapes jouent, je r: In the evening, when the Valves play, I stay by the brazier. I hear the concert from afar, through the flames. It sounds like an old record. Sometimes I go into the pit, right at the edge. My mohawk keeps the beat. It stands up on its own, you know. At eighty.
textes.Le soir, quand les clients sont partis,: In the evening, when the customers have gone, I take a bath of my own. Just me, the bubbles and the stars. And sometimes Bobor, bobbing like a cork.
textes.Le soir, quand les réverbères s'allument: In the evening, when the street lamps come on, the whole town purrs. It's the steam in the pipes. Or my tummy.
textes.Le soir, sous la treille, avec les lampi: In the evening, under the trellis, with the lanterns… It's my favourite moment.
textes.Le soir, sur la Promenade des Hublots, j: In the evening, on the Porthole Promenade, I watch the Funicular tube climbing through the dark, all lit up, to the cliff. Up there, at the end of the tunnel, Anatole is closing his gate. We can't see each other. But we say good night all the same.
textes.Le soir, sur la Promenade du Bord, je re: In the evening, on the Edge Promenade, I watch the birds come home. They all glide into the wind. They've got it all figured out. Me, I take notes.
textes.Le soir, sur le banc de la Grand-Place,: In the evening, on the bench on the Great Square, she tells me about her day. Once, she said: “Mum, when Dad comes back, I'll ask him three hundred and forty questions.” I asked her what the first would be. She said: “Why did you leave?” I didn't know what to say. She took my hand. She said: “Don't worry. The last one is: are you staying?”
textes.Le soir, sur le toit, je joue tout douce: In the evening, on the roof, I play very softly for Radis's tomatoes. He says they grow better. I believe him.
textes.Le soir, sur mon banc de la Grand-Place,: In the evening, on my bench on the Great Square, Nox passes by with his lamplighter's pole. He lights the lantern above me, puts a little folded paper on the bench and leaves without a word. On the paper, there's a poem. I keep them all in a box. I've got a hundred and twelve. I read them to the pups.
textes.Le soir, sur scène, je ferme les yeux. L: In the evening, on stage, I close my eyes. Bass isn't something you hear: you feel it, in your belly. I play for bellies. And for the rock. It vibrates with us. If you put your hand on the wall, you can feel the concert.
textes.Le soir, tout Port-Azur finit ici : les: In the evening, all of Port-Azur ends up here: fishermen, tourists, the mayor. Even Anselme, sometimes, when he forgets his lighthouse.
textes.Le soir, à l'imprimerie, je fais les aff: In the evening, at the print shop, I make the posters with Agrafe. We argue about the colours. He wants black. I want everything else.
textes.Le soir, à l'établi, quand l'atelier est: In the evening, at the workbench, when the workshop is quiet, I have my best ideas. And my worst. I can tell them apart the next morning: the worst ones are the ones that smoke.
textes.Le soir, à la fête, je prends l'oud de m: In the evening, at the party, I take my father's oud. People dance. Or they leave. Either suits me.
textes.Le soir… L'heure où j'allume le premier: Evening… The hour when I light the first street lamp. The gentlest hour. You've got good taste. It's the hour of poems.
textes.Le sol fait « blop ». Une gelée verte gr: The floor goes “blop”. A green jelly as big as a house rises before the throne, a tiny crown perched crookedly: THE JELLY KING! “Who dares walk on my clean tiles?” he gurgles.
textes.Le sol tremble ! La Marmite bouillonne d: The ground trembles! The Cooking Pot bubbles harder and harder… An eruption is coming!
textes.Le sol tremble. L'eau noire des douves b: The ground shakes. The black water of the moat bubbles, and a gigantic crocodile rises from it, covered in spines, with jaws at every joint: CIPACTLI, the Earth monster, from whom the gods made the world!
textes.Le sol tremble. Quelque part dehors, un: The ground shakes. Somewhere outside, a bird falls off its branch, offended.
textes.Le soleil d'ici ne se couche presque jam: The sun up here almost never sets behind a mountain. And Flora talks to them every morning. I sing them lullabies. Nobody knows which of the three works best.
textes.Le soleil qui se lève… La lanterne de to: The rising sun… Everyone's lantern. I've never managed to make one as beautiful. I still try. Every morning, I watch it, to learn.
textes.Le soleil s'est levé… mais il ne bouge p: The sun has risen… but it doesn't move. It burns, motionless, above the fire. The gods, long ago, had the same trouble.
textes.Le soleil s'est posé sur ce coin de trot: The sun settled on this corner of pavement. I settled on the sun. We're even.
textes.Le soleil se lève. Une journée toute neu: The sun's rising. A brand-new day, not a scratch on it yet.
textes.Le soleil sèche, le vent plie. Nous, on: The sun dries, the wind folds. We chat.
textes.Le soleil, c'est une grosse bougie sans: The sun is a big candle with no pattern. But I don't hold it against it: without it, I'd have no night to fill.
textes.Le soleil, chez nous, a trois visages :: Here the sun has three faces: Khepri the scarab, who pushes it up in the morning, Ra who shines at noon, Atum the old man who sets in the evening. Remember that: the Sphinx loves that sort of thing.
textes.Le soleil, il est tout petit, en vrai ?: Is the sun really that tiny?
textes.Le soleil, là-bas. Il est pour moi. Pous: The sun, over there. It's mine. Move over.
The sun, perhaps. My throat, no.
textes.Le soliste est en retard. Comme toujours: The soloist is late. As always.
textes.Le sommet du Mont Fusain — toute l'île,: The summit of Mount Charcoal — the whole island, in black and white, like a drawing laid on the blue sea
textes.Le sommet du moulin, c'est l'endroit le: The top of the mill is the highest spot in the Southern Fields. From up there, you can see the Fangs, the lake, the sea. And the Baron's hat, when it flies by. It flies by often.
textes.Le sommet est ouvert jusqu'à minuit. Apr: The top is open until midnight. After that, it's the stars who come to visit.
textes.Le souk est couvert de roseaux, pour l'o: The souk is roofed with reeds, for the shade. At noon, the light comes through the stalks and paints stripes on everything. Even on people.
textes.Le souterrain du Grand Moaï (yeux rendus: The underground of the Great Moai (eyes restored, going down)
textes.Le souterrain du Grand Moaï — un escalie: The underground of the Great Moai — a staircase that winds down into the dark… and, at the very bottom, something singing
textes.Le style. C'est ce que disait Barnabé de: The style. That's what Barnabé said about his map.
textes.Le sucré ! Biscuits lunaires, alors. Je: Sweet! Moon biscuits, then. I'll put one aside for you, with my third hand. That's the one that keeps secrets.
textes.Le tableau des records, là, c'est moi qu: The record board, there — I paint it. Bondi's been at the top for three years. He's starting to get bored, all alone up there.
textes.Le tableau est couvert d'affiches : slim: The board is covered in posters: slimes, frogs, goblins, a feathered hat… A sign: “Contracts reserved for registered adventurers. See Églantine at the counter. (She doesn't bite.)”
textes.Le tableau noir de mon école est toujour: My school's blackboard still hangs on the walkway. The rain falls on it, the wind wears it down. But every morning, someone writes a word on it. I don't know who. Yesterday it was “courage”. I didn't rub it out. That's the first time.
The stool is there. Like yesterday.
textes.Le tajine de Lalla Zohra : dorade, olive: Lalla Zohra's tagine: sea bream, olives, preserved lemon and saffron, cooked for three hours over the embers. Restores four hearts.
textes.Le tajine du vendredi, c'est la recette: The Friday tajine is my mother's recipe. Sea bream, preserved lemon, olives, and Lalla Aïcha's saffron, from nowhere else. It cooks in Halima's big dish, the one with the fish engraved on the lid. They say it's famous as far as Carène. It's true. A sailor from Carène asked me for the recipe. I gave him half. The other half is my hands.
A tajine is both the dish and the pot. The pointed lid sends the steam back down into the meat. Or the fish, here. It's magic you can eat.
textes.Le tambour bat toujours, quelque part…: The drum is still beating, somewhere…
textes.Le tapis des étoiles ? Il n'est pas à ve: The carpet of the stars? It's not for sale. Fine. For you, I'll show it. Look: the city gate, down here. Then three stars, one after the other, walking northeast, toward the dunes. Those are the old caravan markers: at night they still light up all by themselves, who knows why. After the third, the crescent dune: the walking dune. And beneath the dune, a sun. On the border, three signs, always in the same order: the star, the dune, the sun. My grandmother used to say: “that's the key.” Me, I say: it's pretty.
We built the temple in seven years. Everyone wanted a roof. I said: a solid roof is a prison; a roof full of holes is a prayer. So we made a colander. On the first sunny day, the light fell through a thousand holes onto our heads. Nobody spoke for an hour. It was the most beautiful mass of my life.
textes.Le temps ? Vingt-deux ans que j'attends: Time? Twenty-two years I've been waiting for it to wipe things out, and nothing. It must be on strike. Or it's waiting to get paid too.
Time wipes everything out in the end.
textes.Le terminal clignote : « > REMONTER ? [O: The terminal blinks: “> GO BACK UP? [Y]”. You type “Y”. Beep! The glass doors open… and there you are again in broad daylight, in front of the Grey Factory gate.
textes.Le thé d'abord, Corentin. Les fins se mé: Tea first, Corentin. Endings must be earned.
textes.Le thé d'abord, mon frère. L'histoire en: Tea first, my brother. The story after. Twice, if you like.
textes.Le thé de bienvenue ! Assieds-toi ! (Ses: The welcome tea! Sit down! (His four arms flutter: a teapot, a cup, a saucer, a teaspoon, all at once.) Stellar tea, served midnight blue, with gold sparkles. Drink slowly: it tastes of mint, of rain, and of something else nobody can quite name. So? You can't find the name either? Welcome to our home!
textes.Le thé, ici, se sert trois fois. Le prem: Tea, here, is served three times. The first glass is bitter like life, the second sweet like love, the third light like death. The fourth, you have to pay for.
Tea is not to be rushed.
textes.Le tic-tac de vingt horloges remplit la: The ticking of twenty clocks fills the room. It sounds like a very steady rain.
Yours, always. It has a future.
textes.Le timbre, c'est un sou. La conversation: The stamp is a penny. The conversation is free.
textes.Le titre, c'est le nom de la leçon. Ça n: The title is just the name of the lesson. It doesn't count.
textes.Le tombeau de la Dune qui Marche. L'air: The tomb of the Walking Dune. The air is dry, still. Sandstone columns, sarcophagi, and at the very back, on a dais, in a ray of light fallen from who knows where… a golden disc.
textes.Le tour de la ville en monorail: A monorail tour of the city
The lot? Go on then: {prix} coins.
textes.Le tout premier concert des Rats de Cale: The Bilge Rats' very first gig, the Sergeant broadcast it live from the Rusty Whale. He had three listeners: Mamie, Lentille, and a seagull perched on the aerial. He did the show as if there were a thousand. The next day, we had thirty.
textes.Le tout premier vol d'essai, nous étions: The very first test flight, there were two of us in the gondola, Héloïse and me. Her with her plans, me at the stick. At a hundred metres, it started to smell of cabbage. Héloïse went white as a sheet. I asked: “Is that normal?” She said: “I think so.” We landed bang on the cross painted in the middle of the field. I've never landed so well since.
textes.Le traité cale un pied de mon grand alam: The treatise props up one leg of my big still, so what? That book is at the heart of my work! Théophraste saw it, last time. He went white as a sheet and walked out without finishing his syrup. It's the first time he hadn't finished his syrup. I felt a bit guilty. A bit.
textes.Le trident des rois de l'Atlantide, offe: The trident of the kings of Atlantis, a gift from Queen Néréa. Gold, mother-of-pearl and a glowing sea stone. Damage: 14, and the third hit of a combo strikes half again as hard. Underwater, it strikes from afar.
textes.Le trident te va bien. Mon arrière-grand: The trident suits you. My great-grandfather used it to talk to whales. I never managed it.
textes.Le troc… Oh, non. Tu parles comme mon on: Swaps… Oh, no. You sound like my uncle! You'll end up with a carpet that doesn't fly and three goats, you'll see.
textes.Le trois. Tu avais raison la première fo: The third. You were right the first time.
textes.Le troisième jour, j'ai voulu interviewe: On the third day, I tried to interview Achille. Through a megaphone, from the airfield bench. First question: “Are you hungry?” He shouted something. The wind carried it all away. Adèle took the megaphone out of my hands, very calmly, and said: “He said yes. As always.” I didn't dare ask the second question.
textes.Le troisième soir, pour me faire rire, l: On the third evening, to make me laugh, Doctor Roux told me about the jungle berry she'd tasted that morning. She'd spent the afternoon seeing everything in purple. “Even the seagulls, my dear. Purple!” I laughed so hard that a gardener came to check everything was all right.
textes.Le trophée du Tournoi des Cornes : une c: The trophy of the Tournament of Horns: a ram's horn of solid gold, engraved with the names of all the champions. Yours is at the very bottom, in letters that still shine.
textes.Le trésor de Barbe-Sanglante… raconte-mo: Barbe-Sanglante's treasure… tell me about it.
textes.Le trésor des Rois-Ciel ! Deux cents piè: The treasure of the Sky Kings! Two hundred coins, three gold coins, two rubies, the Crown of the Clouds, the Sword of the Clouds whose blade crackles with lightning… and a strange diving mask with crystal lenses. With it, you can breathe underwater! Far below, beneath the sea, south-west of the village, a light shines…
textes.Le trésor du Cœur du Chant !: The treasure of the Heart of the Song!
The throne is six hundred years old, Coralin.
textes.Le turquoise ? Le pot numéro huit ? Il a: The turquoise? Pot number eight? It must have followed the Dotted Stream down to the sea. Everything that rolls on this island ends up at the river mouth. Elementary geography.
textes.Le vainqueur de Nâga ! Approche, que je: The vanquisher of Nâga! Come closer, let me look at you. You're smaller than in Barnabé's song.
textes.Le vainqueur du Serpent des Abysses ! Le: The vanquisher of the Serpent of the Deep! The ravens told me everything. Come closer!
textes.Le vendredi, Hnia et Rabia font leurs co: On Fridays, Hnia and Rabia do their accounts together: my hammer blows, his glasses of tea. Hassan and I wait on the bench. He serves me from his very first teapot, the dented one. I say it has a dent. He says: “It's yours.” I know. It's a fine dent.
textes.Le vendredi, Lola entre à la poste en pa: On Fridays, Lola comes into the post office slipping behind the pillar, then behind the postcard stand, then she pops her letter into the yellow postbox, very fast, and runs out again. As if nobody could see her. With her blue apron and her red hair, the whole square sees her. I wave to her. She pretends not to notice.
textes.Le vendredi, Lucas rentre du quai « un p: On Fridays, Lucas comes home from the quay “a bit early, by chance”. He sits on his step on High Street and watches the end of the street. When I arrive, he pretends to retie his shoelace. He wears boots without laces. I hand him the envelope. He says thank you three times.
textes.Le vendredi, je rentre du quai un peu pl: On Fridays, I come home from the quay a bit early. By chance. I sit on my step on High Street to get some air. Nadine comes along with her satchel. She says: “Nothing for you… Oh wait, here.” Every week, the same joke. Every week, my heart drops and jumps back up.
textes.Le vent a dispersé les trois pages de la: The wind has scattered the three pages of Django's most beautiful song across the quay, the square and the beach.
textes.Le vent d'ouest se lève. Le Docteur Aurè: The west wind is rising. Doctor Aurèle forecast it for yesterday. He's very punctual, in his own way.
textes.Le vent d'ouest souffle aujourd'hui, frè: The west wind is blowing today, brother of the breeze. Can you feel it?
The west wind, which smells of the sea.
textes.Le vent dans les cheveux, c'est le bonhe: Wind in your hair, pure happiness!
textes.Le vent de Carène est très demandé ! Il: Carène wind is in great demand! It's fresh!
textes.Le vent de nuit a sommeil, lui aussi : i: The night wind is sleepy too: it plays with its fingertips. And if it plays too loud, the Levitators wake up and purr out of tune.
The night wind plays with its fingertips.
textes.Le vent du désert, le chergui, souffle t: The desert wind, the chergui, blows for three days, then stops. On those days, we don't go out.
textes.Le vent entre dans le salon. Les cordes: The wind comes into the living room. The harp strings start singing all by themselves, and dozens of chimes tinkle above your head.
textes.Le vent est toujours calme pour les cour: The wind is always calm for the brave.
textes.Le vent fait tourner les ailes, les aile: The wind turns the sails, the sails turn the shaft, the shaft turns the great wheel, the great wheel turns the little one, and the little one turns the millstone. And I go round and round all of it.
textes.Le vent salue. Merci, merci !: The wind takes a bow. Thank you, thank you!
textes.Le vent siffle dans les vitres, tout en: The wind whistles against the windows, way up top. Down here, it smells of oil, copper and coffee.
textes.Le vent tire très fort ! Si je m'envole,: The wind's pulling really hard! If I blow away, tell Mum I'll be back for snack time!
The wind weaves very nicely these days.
textes.Le vent tourbillonne trop fort au-dessus: The wind swirls too fiercely above the Citadel: Ventaile will wait for you at the Wind Perch. Whistle for her from the esplanade.
The wind swirls far too hard above the Citadel. Go to the Wind Field.
textes.Le vent tourne au nord. Ça sent la tempê: The wind's turning north. Smells like a storm, or an adventure. Either suits me.
textes.Le vent tourne à l'ouest : le moulin d'A: The wind's turning west: Augustin's mill is about to start singing.
textes.Le vent tourne, moussaillon. Le vent tou: The wind is turning, cabin boy. The wind is always turning.
textes.Le vent tourne. Le café aussi, d'ailleur: The wind's turning. So's the coffee, come to that: it's turning cold.
textes.Le vent, je ne peux pas le gronder. Toi,: I can't scold the wind. You, I can.
textes.Le vent, la brume, et les orages qui pou: The wind, the mist, and any storms that might come up from the Floor. If a storm gets close, we warn Engineer Nova: the Levitators don't like lightning. Neither do I.
The wind. It's windy this afternoon.
textes.Le vent… il a emporté ma partition. Troi: The wind… it carried off my score. Three pages. One went off to the beach, one to the square, one to the east end of the quay. Without them, I can't play “The Azure Waltz” any more. If you find them…
textes.Le vert ! (Elle rit.) Bon choix. Enfin,: Green! (She laughs.) Good choice. Well, according to the label. I see it as hazelnut, but it's a very pretty hazelnut.
textes.Le vert ! Et le hibou ? Il n'a rien dit: The green! And the owl? He didn't say anything? He never says anything, that's what's scary. (She hugs the pot to her chest.) Thank you, thank you. Hurry and pour it into paint cup number two. I want to see my leaves wake up. Here: a packet of my seeds. Plant them wherever you like, they even grow in black and white.
textes.Le vert ! La couleur qui pousse toute se: Green! The colour that grows all by itself. Rosalie is going to adore you.
textes.Le vert du Bois des Hachures: The green of the Hatching Wood
textes.Le vert. Le pot numéro deux. Sans lui, m: The green. Pot number two. Without it, my plants no longer know they're plants. I think it rolled all the way to the Hollow Stump, deep in the woods, to the west. But a big owl lives there. It looks at me sideways, with eyes as round as coins. It doesn't know you: it won't have time to look at you sideways.
textes.Le vestibule de la Pyramide de Rê. L'air: The vestibule of the Pyramid of Ra. The air is cool and still, and smells of stone and incense. On the walls, thousands of painted signs; on the left, the sun's barque sailing through the night.
Heights. Me too. Remember? Hm. We'll take the stairs, one day. Together.
textes.Le vieil appareil photo de Gérard Dupuis: Gérard Dupuis's old camera. Three hundred photos of sunsets inside.
textes.Le vieux Corentin connaît mille histoire: Old Corentin knows a thousand stories. He says I add dragons. Not true: I add sharks too. And his stories are better with them.
textes.Le vieux Corentin dit qu'il y a un tréso: Old Corentin says there's treasure in the flooded holds. He mostly says it after his third mug of hot honey.
textes.Le vieux Ferdinand, du Petit Train des S: Old Ferdinand, from the Little Strata Train, had never seen the sea. He came down with me. He looked out from the first metre to the last, without a word. At the bottom, he asked me: “I've seen it from underneath. Does that count?” I said yes. He said: “Then I've still got to see it from above.”
textes.Le vieux Léon et moi, on joue aux cartes: Old Léon and I play cards on Sundays. He loses every time. He says I cheat by talking to the cards. I don't cheat. I encourage them. It's not the same.
textes.Le vieux Léon vient le dimanche. Il grog: Old Léon comes on Sundays. He grumbles coming in, grumbles drinking, grumbles leaving. He always has a second cup. He's my most loyal customer. He'll never admit it.
textes.Le vieux Léon, au Port, dit que les diri: Old Léon, at the Harbour, says airships are “boats that lost the sea”. I tell him boats are airships that forgot to go up. We've been arguing for ten years. He's my best friend.
textes.Le vieux Léon, du Port, vient ici le dim: Old Léon, from the Harbour, comes here on Sundays. He orders a hot chocolate, grumbles, drinks it, grumbles, orders another. He grumbles on the way out. He's my best customer. He'll never admit it.
textes.Le vieux Zéro a perdu sa voix. Sa puce v: Old Zéro has lost his voice. His voice chip gave out: he's a Z Series model, they stopped making them thirty years ago. I haven't got a single one in the workshop.
textes.Le vieux Zéro ne parle plus. Il balaie t: Old Zéro doesn't talk any more. He still sweeps the square, he still gives me a little wave… but not a word. Little Mio is so sad about it.
textes.Le vieux wagon sur les rails rouillés, c: The old wagon on the rusty rails is my evening reading nook. It doesn't go anywhere. That's what I like about it.
textes.Le vieux wagon sur les rails, c'est là q: The old wagon on the rails is where I tell my stories in the afternoon. The kids come to listen. They don't believe me. They're right. But they come back.
textes.Le vieux wagon sur les rails, c'est mon: The old wagon on the rails is my secret spot at lunchtime. The rails go “tac-tac” when you hit them with a pebble. I practise there. Nobody comes. Well, except Tornade. He says I should be a drummer. He's ten. He says it like it's easy.
textes.Le village ! Je vois parfois vos lantern: The village! Sometimes I see your lanterns at night. It keeps me company.
textes.Le village ! La cabane de l'ermite, la j: The village! The hermit's hut, the jungle, the great kapok tree… I drew it from Léon's descriptions. I'll put a little cross for you in the corner, there. That's you, the cross.
textes.Le village est bâti dans les maisons-cha: The village is built in mushroom houses: you hollow out the stalk, open a window, and there you go. It grows along with us.
textes.Le violon, je l'ai trouvé dans un grenie: I found the violin in an attic, with no case and not a single string. I played for three years on three strings. When someone gave me the fourth, I cried, and then I didn't know what to do with it. It's for special nights. The other nights, I pretend it isn't there.
textes.Le virus est parti ! Glitch t'attend (pr: The virus is gone! Glitch is waiting for you (near the Arcade Station, or in the arcade hall in the afternoon).
textes.Le voilier m'a déposé ici. Il n'y avait: The ship dropped me off here. There was nothing but a volcano that smelled of tomato, fields of wild wheat and three fishermen. I stuck a ladle in the sand and said: “Here, we shall eat together.” The fishermen said yes. Mostly because of the “eat.”
textes.Le voilà, Brindille ! Et ma nouvelle du: Here it is, Brindille! And my news of the day?
textes.Le voilà. Il préfère les plantes vertes: There he is. He prefers potted plants to big gusts of wind.
textes.Le voir… Oui. Rien ne remplace le vrai c: Seeing it… Yes. Nothing can replace the real sky. That's why I want to take my class up there. But in the meantime, we do what we can. With words, and closed eyes.
textes.Le voisin du village ! Dis-moi, ils mang: The neighbour from the village! Tell me, do they still eat their soup cold over there?
textes.Le voisin s'appelait Larbi. Il pêchait a: The neighbour was called Larbi. He fished at the end of the jetty, and he never beat me at knots, never, for all his efforts. At seventeen, he left as a cabin boy on a merchant ship, to see the world. I stayed on the quay, mending. With each knot I told myself: one more day. That's a lot of knots, a wait.
textes.Le volcan donne des rubis, quand il est: The volcano gives rubies, when it's in a good mood. The miners find them in the red rock.
textes.Le volcan nous donne tout : le fer, le f: The volcano gives us everything: iron, fire, and warmth for the winter. Sometimes it takes a roof or two. That's the price.
textes.Le voleur de croissants ? Hier soir, en: The croissant thief? Last night, as I was closing, I saw a little white shadow dash towards the quay, east side, with a croissant in its mouth. A dog, I'd say.
textes.Le vrai secret de l'apnée ? Ne pas paniq: The real secret of free-diving? Don't panic. And don't think about sharks.
textes.Lentille ! Ton pain d'hier a encore disp: Lentille! Your yesterday's bread has vanished again!
textes.Lentille a toujours une idée nouvelle. L: Lentille always has a new idea. Most of them are delicious. Some aren't. I keep a drawer in my notebook for his rejected ideas.
textes.Lentille agite sa louche géante : « Tu a: Lentille waves her giant ladle: “You've already had your bowl today! Come back tomorrow, there'll be another soup. Well, the same one, with different vegetables.”
textes.Lentille est arrivé un matin de novembre: Lentille arrived one November morning with his giant ladle and a suitcase. I gave him the keys to the Cannery's old kitchen, where they used to cook the sardines. He opened the door, saw the big pot, and said: “It was waiting for me.” That same evening, we were eating his soup.
textes.Lentille fait tomber des carottes. Je le: Lentille drops carrots. I eat them. I don't like carrots. But it's Lentille.
textes.Lentille jette les épluchures au compost: Lentille throws the peelings on the compost. The compost: MINE! … Radis chases me off with his watering can. Not fair.
textes.Lentille laisse tomber un petit bout de: Lentille drops a little piece of bread for us every evening. He pretends it's an accident. We pretend to believe him.
textes.Lentille me donne du poisson parce que j: Lentille gives me fish because I look at him. All I do is look at him. It's a talent.
textes.Lentille met une louche de plus dans l'a: Lentille puts an extra ladleful on the plates of those who pay nothing. He thinks I don't see. I see. I do the same with scarves.
textes.Lentille nourrit les ventres, moi les ét: Lentille feeds bellies, I feed shelves. He always smells of soup, and so does my Free Shop now. It's a smell that reassures the objects.
textes.Lentille nourrit tout le monde et il cro: Lentille feeds everyone and he thinks nobody sees him giving seconds to those who have nothing. Everybody sees. That's why we love him.
textes.Lentille remplit un bocal de soupe fuman: Lentille fills a jar with steaming soup. “Enjoy your meal!”
Lentille turns my pupils into soup. I hold it against him a little. But he always tells me how they ended up. He says they were happy. I believe him.
Lentille, your soup is too hot.
textes.Lequel ? Le tien, ou son amoureux ?: Which one? Yours, or its sweetheart?
textes.Les Arches de pierre, au sud-ouest, sous: The stone Arches, to the south-west, below the cliffs… When I was a cabin boy, we'd row under them at high tide, holding our breath. For luck. I still do it. I'm very lucky. And I've got very good lungs.
textes.Les Aztèques adorent le cacao aussi. Ils: The Aztecs love cacao too. They call it xocolatl. Their nobles drink fifty cups a day, apparently. If I drank fifty, I'd never sleep again.
textes.Les Aztèques d'Aztlán sont venus du nord: The Aztecs of Aztlán came from the north, from a place also called Aztlán. Their god told them to stop where an eagle would eat a snake on a cactus. Here, the serpent has feathers, and nobody eats it.
textes.Les Aztèques font pousser du maïs sur le: The Aztecs grow maize on the lake. On the lake! I struggle enough on solid ground.
textes.Les Boîtes, à l'est, c'est le village de: The Boxes, to the east, is the container village. I set down every container myself. I know every family. When they move, I move the whole house. With them inside, if they like. The kids love it.

The Boxes, to the east, is the container village. Mine is purple, with stars. Boulon put it next to the Pimpin family's, which has a henhouse on the roof. The hens and the pigeons don't get along. Neighbourly squabbles.
textes.Les Boîtes, à l'est, le village de conte: The Boxes, to the east, the container village: I made the stairs, the balconies and the walkways there. Patchouli asked for a walkway for her pigeons. I made it. They don't use it. They fly.
textes.Les Bureaux. Un open-space gris à perte: The Offices. A grey open-plan space as far as the eye can see: desks in rows, plastic plants, buzzing neon lights… and bailiff drones reading eviction notices out loud. At the far end, a turnstile. Near the entrance, a staff memo.
textes.Les Caves Gluantes. Des couloirs de pier: The Sticky Caves. Corridors of mossy stone that twist every which way, and everywhere, little puddles going “blop”. Slimes! The staircase down is somewhere to the southeast.
textes.Les Champs de Blé Dur — le blé des pâtes: The Durum Wheat Fields — pasta wheat rippling in the wind
textes.Les Champs du Sud sont au sud de la vill: The Southern Fields are south of town, past the South Gate. My farm, my fields, and Clovis's mill, which turns when there's wind. When there's no wind, Clovis blows on it. On principle.
textes.Les Clous Rouillés ! Avant, on s'appelai: The Rusty Nails! We used to be called The New Nails, but we got old.
textes.Les Crocs, au sud-ouest : des rochers po: The Fangs, to the south-west: pointed rocks, wind, storms. The perfect place for a duel. Shall we meet there one day, you and I? Not today. It's raining. My cape doesn't like rain.
textes.Les Crocs, au sud-ouest, sont des collin: The Fangs, to the south-west, are hills of pointed rock. Storm crystals grow on the summit. They attract lightning. So do I. I don't go up there alone: we'd end up fighting over the bolts.
textes.Les Falaises du Clan — les grottes du Cl: The Clan Cliffs — the Clan's caves are dug into the rock
textes.Les Furies ! Elles planent au-dessus de: The Furies! They hover above the gate of Dis, then swoop at you. Step aside when they dive, strike when they climb back up.
textes.Les Gouttières, c'est Grésil à la guitar: The Gutters are Grésil on guitar, Bruine on bass, Bourrasque on drums, and me. We rehearse in the red garage. The walls are sheet metal, it echoes: it feels like there are four hundred of us.
textes.Les Hauts — les grandes tours de bureaux: The Heights — the great office towers, their ribbons of light, and the cars zipping between them
textes.Les Huit Recommandations des Pâtes\n1. T:
The Eight Recommendations of Pasta
1. Thou shalt not overcook the pasta.
2. Thou shalt share thy sauce with thy neighbour.
3. Thou shalt not break spaghetti in two.
4. Thou shalt taste before salting.
5. Thou shalt not throw pasta at the wall to see if it sticks.
6. Thou shalt leave a place at the table for the stranger.
7. Thou shalt do the dishes (even the pot).
8. Thou shalt smile: it tastes better with a smile.
textes.Les Huit Recommandations sont écrites au: The Eight Recommendations are written on the lectern, in the temple. They're not orders, my child, they're “I'd really rather you didn't…”. The Great Spaghetti is very polite.
textes.Les Jardins Partagés sont à l'est de la: The Shared Gardens are east of town, near the Boxes: vegetable plots, a greenhouse made of old windows, beehives and a compost heap. Anyone can grow a plot. Even you. I'll give you a mark.
textes.Les Jardins Partagés, à l'est, ont une s: The Shared Gardens, to the east, have a greenhouse made of old windows. The freshest mint in the archipelago grows there. Radis plays the harmonica to it. It likes that.
textes.Les Jardins de Cendre sont au sud de la: The Ash Gardens are south of the Lower Town, next to my son's Baths. Volcano ash is the best soil in the world. Everything grows in it: all it takes is a little hot water and a lot of patience.
textes.Les Jardins des Champignons sont au sud: The Mushroom Gardens are in the south of the cavern, under a great arch: the pond, the waterfall that drops from the vault, and mushrooms everywhere, as big as stools or as small as buttons. Some glow blue, others green, others orange. We only pick the ones that don't glow any more. The others, we let them live.
textes.Les Jardins suspendus sont à l'ouest de: The Hanging Gardens are west of the Agora: giant glowing plants, ponds, flowers that sing at sunrise. Go and listen in the morning. They sing out of tune. But with lots of heart.
textes.Les Jardins suspendus, c'est mon potager: The Hanging Gardens are my vegetable patch. Photon lets me pick the glowing fruit, as long as I ask them for permission. They always say yes. They blink. I think that means yes.
