textes.Les Jumeaux ont joué contre les Seigneur: The Twins played against the Lords of Xibalba. They won. I dream of playing against the Lords. But preferably while staying alive.
textes.Les Limbes, le Premier Cercle. Des ombre: Limbo, the First Circle. Shadows glide between the columns. A stone sage holds a golden light; three bronze mirrors, a dark crystal, and a closed door.
textes.Les Lisses… gens d'un autre monde. Tout: The Smooth Ones… people from other world. All round, all soft, not one square. They say they see things… how to say… in very, very tiny pixels. So tiny you not see them. Strange, no?
The Smooth Ones… legend speak true.
textes.Les Lumens, là-haut, n'avaient jamais vu: The Lumens up there had never seen a rat. They called me “little whiskered cloud”. I like it.
textes.Les Mayas de Yaxché et les Aztèques d'Az: The Mayas of Yaxché and the Aztecs of Aztlán have their own sun too. Three peoples, three suns. The ancients said that one day someone would bring them together on the altar of the highlands.
textes.Les Mayas de Yaxché font une boisson de: The Mayas of Yaxché make a cacao drink, frothy and bitter. I tasted it once. I added honey, and they cried sacrilege.
textes.Les Mayas de Yaxché vendent des plumes d: The Mayas of Yaxché sell macaw feathers. I buy them too. Then I sell them on, dearer. That's trade.
textes.Les Mayas tissent aussi, avec un métier: The Mayas weave too, on a loom they tie to their waist and to a tree. Ix Sak, their weaver, works wonders with colours. I only do white. But what a white!
textes.Les Mines de Cristaux sont à l'ouest de: The Crystal Mines are to the west of the cavern, through the big tunnel. At the end, the Crystal Grotto: blue crystals everywhere, on the walls, on the ceiling, glowing in the dark. The rails run all the way to the back, and the mine carts bring the crystals to the Workshop of Lights. Gently. You don't shake a crystal.
textes.Les Nuées, c'est fait. Les Strates aussi: The Clouds: done. The Strata too: two ribbons, two speeches. That leaves the Azure Dome… When all the lines are open, Hautefond will be the heart of four worlds! I've already written the last speech. It runs two hours.

The Clouds: done. The Strata: done too. And now the Azure Dome: three ribbons, three speeches! All the lines are open, and Hautefond is the heart of four worlds! The last speech went on for two hours. I'd written it in advance.
textes.Les Perles, {surnom}. Il en manque encor: The Pearls, {surnom}. {manque} are still missing. The coral garden, the wreck, the jellyfish trench… Abyssos will tell you more.
textes.Les Prés Blancs — des milliers de fleurs: The White Meadows — thousands of flowers… all white, waiting for their colours
textes.Les Prés Blancs, à l'est. Il y a des coq: The White Meadows, to the east. There are poppies, cornflowers, daisies. Well, there will be. Before the Downpour, we called them the Flowery Meadows.
textes.Les Rats de Cale ? C'est NOUS, les premi: The Bilge Rats? That's US, the first fans! We were in the bilge before them! We voted for the name!
textes.Les Rats de Cale n'ont jamais aussi bien: The Bilge Rats have never played so well. The whole Boucan jumps at once. The Sergeant yells on the radio: “HISTORIC!”
textes.Les Rats de Cale, on les a fondés à dix-: We founded the Bilge Rats at seventeen, Clou, Mouette and me, in the hold of the Rusty Whale. Hence the name. There really were rats. They stayed for the music. They're our first fans.
textes.Les Rois-Ciel ! Ils descendaient nous vo: The Sky Kings! They used to come down to see us wearing masks like yours, before the flood. Their castle flew above us; their waterfalls brought us fresh water. You defeated Lord Storm? Then sky and sea are friends again.
textes.Les Ruelles — de vieux immeubles serrés,: The Alleys — old buildings packed close, signs everywhere, steam rising from the ground
textes.Les Ruelles, c'est le vieux Néopolis : d: The Alleys are old Neopolis: buildings squeezed together, strings of lights, signs, workshops. The glass towers are pretty, but down here is where we fix everything that falls from up there.
textes.Les Récifs de Feu, à l'ouest ! J'y suis: The Fire Reefs, to the west! I sailed by there when I was young. Well, near there. Smoke everywhere, black rocks spitting sparks… We turned back. A dwarf made a gesture at us from the beach. Not a friendly one.
textes.Les Résidences des Terrasses, au sud-oue: The Terrace Residences, to the south-west: white stepped buildings, balconies full of flowers, gardens everywhere. It used to be quiet. Now Floor folk come to photograph our balconies. I put on my finest shirt. To discourage them.
textes.Les Résidences — des immeubles d'habitat: The Residences — apartment buildings, balconies, water tanks on the roofs
textes.Les Seigneurs t'attendront. Ils ont le t: The Lords will wait for you. They have time.
textes.Les Serres d'Altitude, ce sont trois gra: The High-Altitude Greenhouses are three big glass domes, in the east of the town. The first for fruit, the second for flowers, the third for butterflies. And a pond in the middle, full of cloud water. Everything grows here. Even the weeds. They're very proud.
textes.Les Strates — la ville sous la ville, so: The Strata — the city beneath the city, under its Brass Sun
textes.Les Strates, c'est la meilleure ville du: The Strata is the best city in the world. There are rails everywhere, wagons, a train, a forge, glowing crystals, and a brass sun you can look at without hurting your eyes. Up top, apparently, you're not allowed to look at the sun. Rubbish.
textes.Les Strates, c'est la ville sous la vill: The Strata are the city under the city. Floors carved into the rock: workshops, crystal mines, rails, forges. And the Fronde: our quarter. Banners with the circled A, paintings on every wall, and music all the time. The line has reopened. Go down, you'll see.

The Strata are the town beneath the town. Levels dug into the rock: workshops, crystal mines, rails, forges. And the Fronde: our neighbourhood. Banners with the circled A, paintings on every wall, and music all the time. The line reopens soon. You'll see.
textes.Les Strates, la Gare. Ça sent la vapeur: The Strata, the Station. It smells of steam and chocolate: we're back up, no doubt about it.
textes.Les Strates, sous la ville… Hum. Des ate: The Strata, under the town… Hm. Workshops, crystal mines, forges. Very useful. And then there's the Fronde. Musicians, coloured mohawks, banners… Well. Not my style. But the line has reopened, and I gave a speech. A very open-minded speech. In front of a brazier.

The Strata, beneath the town… Ahem. Workshops, crystal mines, forges. Very useful. And then there's the Fronde. Musicians, coloured crests, banners… Well. It's not my style. But the line will reopen, and I shall make a speech. A very open-minded speech.
textes.Les Strates, {surnom}, c'est une ville c: The Strata, {surnom}, is a city carved into the sandstone, a hundred metres below Hautefond. In the middle, the Great Stratum and the Brass Sun. To the north, the Galleries: two storeys of houses in the rock face. To the west, the Mines. To the south, the Gardens. To the east, the Bridge, and the Fronde. Here, everyone works, and everyone knows everyone. Too well, sometimes.
textes.Les Sustentateurs ne poussent pas l'île,: The Levitators don't push the island, they carry it. Like an open hand under a feather. Séraphin designed them a hundred and twenty years ago, at the Workshop. I maintain them with his plans, an adjustable spanner and a great deal of respect.
textes.Les Sustentateurs ronronnent sous nos pi: The Levitators purr under our feet. A hundred and twenty years of service. They're older than me, and they never complain. Unlike me.
textes.Les Taupes Hurlantes. On répétait dans u: The Howling Moles. We used to rehearse in a cellar. The moles moved out.
textes.Les Thermes de Soufre et les Jardins de: The Sulphur Baths and the Ash Gardens are in the south of the Lower Town. The sulphur from the springs is excellent for the skin, the horns and the spirits. Technically. I've never measured the spirits.
textes.Les Thermes de Soufre, au sud de la Bass: The Sulphur Baths, south of the Lower Town: three pools, steam, and the best view of the volcano. Sulphur is good for the skin, the horns and the spirits. My sister says it's not proven for the spirits. Well, I've proven it: look at me!
textes.Les Tournevent sont une noble famille de: The Tournevents are a noble family of knights. My great-grandfather saved a king. My grandfather saved a princess. My father saved a cat. I'm still looking for someone to save. I'm open to all offers.
textes.Les Vergers en terrasses, au sud de l'îl: The Terraced Orchards, in the south of the island, run all the way down to the sea. Apple trees at the top, pear trees in the middle, cherry trees at the bottom. The apples end up at the market, at Rosalie's, and in Augustin's tarts. And a few in the bellies of thieves. I don't hold it against them.
textes.Les Vergers en terrasses. Chaque terrass: The Terraced Orchards. Each terrace has its own colour. Old Bastien wanted me to draw every apple too. I politely declined.
textes.Les abeilles de l'Arbre-Mère sont de bon: The Mother Tree's bees are in a good mood.
textes.Les abeilles vivent tout en haut de l'Ar: The bees live right at the top of the Mother Tree. Thalion fetches the honey. He says it's training.
textes.Les abords mènent à la porte. Restez géo: The surroundings lead to the gate. Stay a geographer.
textes.Les accessoires du chantier : chacun s'i: The shipyard accessories: each one is installed once and for all.
textes.Les affaires marchent ! Un client de la: Business is booming! A customer from the surface is the best of signs.
textes.Les affaires vont bien. Les affaires von: Business is good. Business is always good here. People steal, people sell, people buy. Me, I count.
textes.Les algues de la baie soignent les plaie: Seaweed from the bay heals wounds. Meadow honey, coughs. And Gwenola's hot honey… nothing at all, but everyone feels better.
textes.Les amis… On ne peut pas les vendre, ni: Friends… You can't sell them or buy them. That's why they're the most precious. Good answer, dear customer.
textes.Les amoureux des Galeries viennent s'ass: The sweethearts from the Galleries come and sit on my bench in the evening, when everything glows. They whisper. The mushrooms blink. I pretend to water. I do a lot of watering in the evening.
textes.Les androïdes ? Ce sont des voisins comm: Androids? They're neighbours like any others. Politer, often. Sept, at the Axiom Tower, says hello to me forty-two times a day. I count.
textes.Les androïdes de Néopolis ont tous un pe: The androids of Neopolis all have a little heart of code. Zéro's is the oldest. It's almost handwritten. It's beautiful to see.
textes.Les androïdes ne rêvent pas. Alors j'ai: Androids don't dream. So I wrote a “dream module”. At night, I replay my favourite images and mix them up. Last night, I saw a blue cherry tree, a moon-shaped neon sign, and Zéro dancing. I'm going to paint it all.
textes.Les androïdes ne sont pas censés aimer l: Androids aren't supposed to love things. I love the pink of the cherry blossoms, the sound of the fountain and Master Ishi's voice when he says “hm”. I don't know if it's an error. If it is one, I'm keeping it.
textes.Les araignées de cristal laissent des éc: The crystal spiders leave shards behind. Grommelot loves them. Shh, it's a secret.
textes.Les araignées de cristal ont envahi la g: The crystal spiders have invaded the western cave. They leave shards behind when you break them. Bring me {manque}. For my fireplace. Not because they're pretty. Hmph.
textes.Les arbres attirent la foudre. Moi aussi: Trees attract lightning. So do I. We understand each other, the trees and I.
The trees hear everything, you know.
textes.Les arbres entendent tout, tu sais. Eux: Trees hear everything, you know. They love it too.
textes.Les arbres qui portent une entaille clai: The trees with a pale notch, I marked those myself: soft wood, easy to fell. Leave the others alone.
textes.Les arbres, hein ? Et l'elfe qui danse d: The trees, eh? And the elf dancing behind them, does she like it too?
The archives… I'm filing the files.
textes.Les armures s'effondrent dans un fracas: The armour collapses with a crash of scrap metal. At the back of the armoury, a chest has appeared.
textes.Les astres sont bien alignés. Et mes pie: The stars are well aligned. And my feet are nice and cool. What more could I ask?
textes.Les aurores ondulent au rythme du thérém: The auroras ripple to the rhythm of Vibrato's theremin.
textes.Les aurores s'effacent. Sur l'Agora, les: The auroras fade away. On the Agora, the Lumens get up and stretch, their eyes still full of colours.
textes.Les avares, dit-on, poussent ces poids d: The misers, they say, have been pushing these weights forever. You, though, have a goal: the golden slabs.
textes.Les babouches de noce sont presque finie: The wedding slippers are almost done: a cloth of her own, embroidered with gold thread. So Rachid won't see them, I hide them in a basket of ordinary yellow slippers, right at the bottom. The other day, a caravan trader wanted to buy the whole basket. I had to say it was reserved. For a wedding. Rachid was three steps away.
textes.Les babouches jaunes sont pour les homme: The yellow babouches are for men, the red and embroidered ones for women. The black ones, for pirates. They don't wear them, they hang them from their mast.
textes.Les balayeurs ont déposé une réclamation: The sweepers filed an official complaint. Signed “BEEP”. I wasn't the one who typed it. Hm. She replied with a letter. A fat letter. Stuffed with confetti. I put it in the Works' sorting machine. The machine jammed for three days. Confetti still comes out of it. Pink, mostly.
textes.Les balayeurs ont fait une réclamation o: The sweepers have filed an official complaint against me. Signed “BEEP”.
textes.Les bananiers sont mes amis. Ils ne dise: The banana trees are my friends. They never say anything, but they're very good listeners.
textes.Les bannières du parvis : vert, blanc, r: The banners on the forecourt: green, white, red, like basil, pasta and tomato. And in the middle, the golden fork. I repaint them every spring. This year, I added little pirates in the corners. Nobody's spotted them yet.
textes.Les barques des bergers viennent parfois: The shepherds' boats come here sometimes, with wool. The Carène boats too, with cider. And the Petit Piston, my tugboat, hasn't moved in three years. He's very happy like that.
textes.Les bateaux de nacre que les enfants fon: The mother-of-pearl boats the children float on the canal? His. Light, fast, they never sink. Mine, carved from the solid block, sank by the third bridge. One day I had Ondine buy one in secret, to work out how he does it. I still don't understand.
textes.Les bateaux du Port des Cordages ressemb: The boats in Rigging Harbour look like crumbs on a blue tablecloth.
textes.Les beaux rêves passent par le trou du m: Good dreams pass through the hole in the middle.
textes.Les bergers des hautes terres allument d: The highland shepherds light fires on the ridges on full-moon nights. I don't know what they're celebrating.
textes.Les bergers des hautes terres ont un mou: The highland shepherds have a windmill that's been turning for a hundred years. A hundred years! I'd love to see how it's made. They won't let me near it.
textes.Les bergers gardent un secret, dans une: The shepherds keep a secret, in a cave under the great ridge. A round stone, carved. My grandfather said it's a key. A key to a door that can't be opened.
textes.Les biches ne savent ni forger, ni pêche: Does can't forge, or fish, or trade. But when we dance, the whole village forgets how tired it is. That's a job too, I think.
textes.Les blagues ? (Il réfléchit, très sérieu: Jokes? (He thinks, very seriously.) A joke is a poem that laughs. You're right. I shall write one. In three years.
textes.Les bleus pour la sardine, les orange po: Blue ones for sardines, orange ones for sea bream. I always mend Driss's first. Next to me, Lalla Fatima, whom I keep an eye on without her knowing. The pirates' parrot that repeats everything: careful what you say. And at home, the jar of shells that's overflowing, and that nobody is allowed to touch.
textes.Les bocaux de « vent de Carène » que je: The jars of “Carène wind” I sell to the caravan traders: Nolwenn sews their canvas lids. She pretends to hate it. But she embroiders a little boat on every lid, and I never asked her to. It's the boat that makes them sell. She knows it. She doesn't want me to say so.
textes.Les bons ! Tu as l'œil. Donne-moi tes ma: The right ones! You have a good eye. Give me your hands. They're warm, that's good. Think of someone you love, very hard, and put your hand on your heart. … Do you feel it? That's healing. Now, go and see the wounded owl, near Agathe's caravan, in the Twisted Wood. She lets no one come near her. You, perhaps.
textes.Les bouchons, c'est pas contre toi, Tcho: The earplugs aren't against you, Tchoum. They're for the ears.
textes.Les bougainvilliers sur les façades, c'e: The bougainvillea on the house fronts — I planted it twenty years ago. Now it's eating the houses.
textes.Les bras en l'air, c'est pour les morcea: Arms in the air are for the tracks that build up. I'll save one for you, you'll recognise it: your arms will be up before you know why.
textes.Les braseros, la fresque… Les Anciens ad: The braziers, the fresco… The Ancients loved riddles. Read carefully what's carved under the pictures: for them, night always comes first.
textes.Les bus ne roulent plus beaucoup : l'île: The buses don't drive much any more: the island's too small. But once a year, we go round the island honking. It takes ten minutes. With the picnic stops, a whole day.
textes.Les bûches du Bois Tors brûlent longtemp: Logs from the Twisted Wood burn long and without smoke. Crooked wood has patience, and gives it back as heat.
textes.Les cabines sont dorées, les rampes sont: The cabins are golden, the handrails are golden… Even the ticket office shines. I don't dare touch anything.
Cacti don't say anything. They prickle.
textes.Les cailloux-qui-chantent, tu connais ?: Singing-stones, ever heard of them? When the wind blows through them, they whistle. I hang them under the bridges so I know when the wind picks up. For a singing-stone, I'd give my finest golden acorn!
textes.Les canons de la Skala sont en bronze. J: The Skala's cannons are bronze. I polish them once a year. They've never fired. I hope it stays that way.
textes.Les canons du Léviathan ne tirent plus d: The Léviathan's cannons haven't fired in two centuries. I turned one into a hearth, two anvils and a cooking pot. Better that way.
Cannons. Cannons calm me down. Boom. That calms me. Boom.
textes.Les caravaniers du désert viennent ici v: The desert caravaneers come here to sell their dates and their salt, and leave with our dried fish. Carène, to the west, buys our spices. Everything passes through Tazira.
textes.Les caravaniers du sud disent que le dés: The southern caravanners say the desert is advancing. The northern shepherds say the snow is coming down. If everyone's right, we'll all end up on the Léviathan. Oh, but we're already here.
textes.Les caravaniers du sud m'apportent du co: The southern caravanners bring me desert cotton. The northern shepherds, wool. The mist people… nothing. They don't trade. But once, one of them left me a silver thread that glows in the dark.
textes.Les caravaniers du sud ont la peau dure: The southern caravanners have skin as tough as leather. They say it's the sun. I think it's a cream. I want the recipe.
textes.Les caravaniers du sud viennent parfois: The southern caravanners sometimes come to sell their spices. Last time, they sold me red sand, swearing it was chilli.
textes.Les carpes changent de couleur toutes le: The carp change color every ten minutes. I timed it.
textes.Les carpes de lumière ? C'est moi qui le: The light carp? I'm the one who named them: Ambre, Azur and Rubis. They don't know they have names. I know. That's enough.
textes.Les cartes ne mentent jamais. Moi, parfo: The cards never lie. I sometimes do.
textes.Les cartes ont parlé de vous, cette nuit: The cards spoke of you last night, Madame Sylvie.
textes.Les cartes sont blanches… Tu as aidé tou: The cards are blank… You've helped everyone. All that's left is to live happily. That's the hardest part.
textes.Les cartes t'écouteront. Elles écoutent: The cards will listen to you. They always listen very well.
textes.Les cercles rouges au sol : des ronces v: The red circles on the ground: brambles are about to burst out! Get out of the circle, quick!
textes.Les cerisiers de la place, c'est moi qui: I'm the one who waters the cherry trees in the square. I sing while I water: it's better for the flowers. Well, I used to sing. The mayor says the flowers understood. They bloom anyway.
textes.Les cerisiers sont arrivés en bateau, to: The cherry trees arrived by boat, tiny, in clay pots. They were seasick. I talked to them every day for a year. They blossomed the following spring. I don't talk to them anymore. They know.
textes.Les chambres du dessus ont des lits à re: The rooms upstairs have spring beds. One of Héloïse's inventions. You sleep very well in them, if you manage to stay in.
textes.Les chambres sont dans l'entrepont, sous: The rooms are on the lower deck, under the main deck. You sleep in hammocks, like sailors of old. It rocks you, even though the ship doesn't move any more.
The camels are waiting for you.
textes.Les champignards ! Ils éternuent des cou: The mushlings! They sneeze colours! I'm going to catch them! … Achoo. I'm green.
The mushlings sneeze colours. I bark at them. They sneeze on me. I'm pink now.
textes.Les champignons féeriques, je les connai: The fairy mushrooms, I know them all: the Spring-Bolete that makes you jump, the Moonling that shows you the invisible, the Chatterbox that lets you understand animals, the Rainbow and the Little-Giant. They're fairy-tale mushrooms. Real mushrooms don't give any powers. Some make you very ill. Remember that well.
textes.Les champignons l'aiment bien. Elle sent: The mushrooms like it. It smells of the forge.
textes.Les champignons sauteurs, c'est nous qui: We were the ones who grew the bouncing mushrooms, to play on. One morning I went back in secret, despite the crystal spiders. I jumped too high, my wand slipped out of my hand, it landed on the ledge right at the top… and a spider sat down next to it. I ran away. Since then, I don't like mushrooms any more.
textes.Les champignons sont beaux, ici. Babette: The mushrooms are lovely here. Babette says not to go past the edge of the wood. We're past the edge of the wood.
textes.Les champignons, je les cueille à la lis: I pick mushrooms at the edge of the Goblin Wood, at dawn. Never any further: the goblins gather the same ones. Once, we came face to face over a porcini. He left with it. I kept my basket. A draw.
textes.Les champs ! Enfin quelqu'un de raisonna: The fields! At last, somebody sensible. The earth, at least, doesn't move. Except when a crocodile crosses it.
textes.Les champs de chanvre — de hautes tiges: The hemp fields — tall green stalks: they're made into ropes and canvas
textes.Les champs de coquelicots — un grand tap: The poppy fields — a great red carpet rippling in the wind
textes.Les champs de coquelicots, au sud-est, p: The poppy fields, in the south-east — nobody planted them. They came all by themselves, with the wind. The bees love them, and the camp's honey tastes of poppies.
textes.Les champs de la rive sud, personne n'en: Nobody wanted the fields on the south bank: too close to the plateau of the dead. My father took them. The silt there is black and rich, the barley grows as tall as a man. He built the shadoof with his own hands. When he left to join Osiris, I kept the fields and the shadoof. The pole creaks. I don't fix it. It's his voice.
textes.Les chansons des Soupapes, c'est moi qui: I write the Valves' songs. There's one about the rails, one about Gamelle's soup, one about the Bridge, one about Brasero's mohawk… And one about Ysaé. I never sing it when she's in the pit. She cries. So do I. That's a lot of crying for a punk gig.
textes.Les chats de Ramure pêchent dans les mar: The cats of Ramure have always fished in the pools. Not with our paws: with rods. Paws were a long time ago. We've moved on.
textes.Les chats ne courent pas longtemps. Mais: Cats don't run for long. But fast. Very fast. The last bend, before the Watchtower: that's where I'll pass Bondi. One day.
textes.Les chats… Hm. Je ne dis rien. Je ne dis: Cats… Hm. I'm not saying anything. I'm not saying anything. … At least cats don't spit fire. Come and see my pups anyway: they'll change your mind.
textes.Les chats… Ne le dites pas trop fort. Bo: Cats… Don't say it too loudly. Boulon won't hold it against you. Much. He has bad memories of the cats of Tazira. So does his nose.
textes.Les chaussettes : avant ou après le pant: Socks: before or after the trousers?
textes.Les chauves-souris ronflent moins fort q: The bats snore quieter than you, my dove.
textes.Les chiens ! Évidemment ! Tu as un cœur: Dogs! Obviously! You've got a kennel for a heart, you have! Come and say hello to mine. Careful: they spit a bit of fire. Like all babies.
textes.Les chiens aboient sur les robots de Lis: The dogs bark at Lisse's robots. All six. Together. The robots stop and say: “Please stop barking. Thank you for your understanding.” The dogs have no understanding whatsoever. That's their strength.
textes.Les chiens d'enfer sauvages du champ de: The wild hellhounds of the lava field, east of the volcano, aren't nasty: they're just badly brought up! They pounce, they breathe fire, and they're hungry. My brother says they must be driven back. I say they must be understood. Still, watch out: they bite hard.
textes.Les chiens de Chaussette m'adorent. Les: Chaussette's dogs adore me. All six. They climb all over me like a hill. Chaussette says I'm their favourite mountain.
textes.Les chiens de Chaussette me grimpent des: Chaussette's dogs climb all over me like a hill. She says I'm their favourite mountain. I'm very proud to be a mountain.
textes.Les chiens du Champ de Lave: The dogs of the Lava Field
textes.Les chiens du champ de lave ne s'approch: The lava field hounds don't come near our walls any more. My sister says they've understood. I say you were convincing. Nothing to report. Thank you.
textes.Les chiens sauvages ont reculé dans le c: The wild dogs have pulled back into the lava field. I'll still take them bones. A dog that backs off is a dog that's thinking. That's a start.
textes.Les chiens, ce ne sont pas les miens. Ce: The dogs aren't mine. They're Boucan's dogs: the one from the Cannery, the one from the Boxes, the one from the Spinning Mill… Every morning I go and get them, and every evening I bring them back. Except Madame Croquette. She's decided she lives with me.
Hilda's goats graze on ash. I don't know how. Their cheese is the best in the world.
textes.Les chênes attirent la foudre. Je dis ça: Oaks attract lightning. I'm just saying… for no reason.
textes.Les cinq braseros de l'Aire des Duels fl: The five braziers of the Duelling Ground blaze! Pyra Flammèche applauds from afar.
textes.Les cinq pierres chantent ensemble ! Des: The five stones sing together! Thousands of fireflies burst out of the pool and swirl up to the ceiling… With a long creak, the roots blocking the staircase draw back.
textes.Les cloches vibrent ensemble, discordant: The bells ring out together, jangling, then fall silent… That was not the right order.
textes.Les clochettes de cristal, c'est moi qui: I tuned the crystal bells myself. You have to listen before you play. Always listen.
textes.Les clochettes de cristal, je les avais: I'd spent a year tuning the crystal bells. Pimprenelle wanted to make them play by themselves, with a flick of her wand. They played all night, faster and faster. Nobody slept. It took me a month to retune them. She calls it modern music.
textes.Les clous du chantier disparaissaient, u: Nails kept disappearing from the yard, a handful a day. I thought there was a thief. One evening, I followed Amine down to the beach: he was burying them in a crate, under a cross drawn in the sand. A treasure chest. Three hundred nails. I left them there. The day he digs them up, he'll know what treasure is: nails.
textes.Les clowns ? Ha ! Moi aussi ! Il y en av: Clowns? Ha! Me too! There was one, Bobo, who put his make-up on in the morning and never took it off. Not even to sleep. Brr.
textes.Les colis qui arrivent pour la douze son: The parcels that arrive for room twelve are worryingly varied. A crate that ticked. A basket that clucked. A copper tube labelled “Fragile, do not open before the full moon”. I sign. I take them up. I ask no questions. Pauline, on the other hand, asks plenty.
textes.Les complaintes… Ah. Toi, tu as un cœur: Laments… Ah. You've got a heart that listens. That's rare, around here. I'll play you one, some rainy evening. The whaler's one, the one Mama loves.
textes.Les coquillages ? … Vous sortez de chez: Shells? … You've just come from Victor's, admit it. Well. At least a real shell doesn't lie. As long as it isn't painted.
textes.Les coquillages qui chantent, c'est une: Singing shells are all about shape. You hold one up to your ear, and you hear… the Great Singer. Well, Professor Benthos says it's your blood moving. I say it's the Singer. He doesn't seem too sure himself. He bought three.
textes.Les corbeaux des cendres portent nos mes: The ash ravens carry our messages to the king, under the mountain. They drop feathers everywhere.
textes.Les couleurs se calment et reprennent le: The colours calm down and settle back in place. Your trail slowly fades. The grey comes back… but at the Boucan, there isn't much of it.
textes.Les couleurs… Ah. Ix Sak t'aurait sauté: Colours… Ah. Ix Sak would have hugged you. Here, we've always woven in white. But I understand. I… understand very well.
textes.Les coups qui enlèvent un cœur ou plus p: Blows that take a heart or more lose half a heart.
textes.Les courants apportent des choses d'en h: The currents bring things down from above: a bit of rope, a feather, an empty bottle that smells of apples. Every thing has its story, you just have to listen. One day I found a sandal. I got forty stories out of it. Abyssos says it's just a sandal. That's why he writes, and I tell.
The crabs have a whole beach, Zoé.
textes.Les cristaux astraux poussent sous l'île: Astral crystals grow under the island, in the dark rock. I go down to get them in my harness. It's a bit dizzying, but that's where the crystals are most beautiful. They buzz. It sounds like they're humming.
textes.Les cristaux bleus de la Grotte ne brill: The blue crystals of the Grotto don't shine on their own. They drink in the light of the Brass Sun, and give it back in the dark. Without our sun, no lanterns. Without lanterns, no peaceful nights. Everything holds together, here. Like the layers of the rock.
textes.Les cristaux d'abord. S'il vous plaît. S: The crystals first. Please. Without them, going with you would be dangerous. For you. And for me. Especially for me.
textes.Les cristaux d'orage, au sommet des Croc: The storm crystals at the top of the Fangs: that was my idea. I lent her an old book with a chapter about them, and I marked the page with a ribbon. She came back bright red, saying: “Madame Olga, I've read something extraordinary!” I pretended not to know. It was a lovely moment.

The storm crystals, at the top of the Fangs, are true marvels. They drink lightning and spit it straight ahead. Exactly what Violette needs. Don't tell her it was my idea: let her think she read it somewhere.
textes.Les cristaux de la Fronde poussent au bo: The Fronde's crystals grow at the edge of the Chasm, where the river's steam rises. They're blue, green, and sometimes pink when it's warmer. I don't pull them out: I gather the ones that fall by themselves. They're the most beautiful. They chose.
textes.Les cristaux ont dû cligner des yeux. Ça: The crystals must have blinked. It happens. Even to crystals.
textes.Les cristaux s'allument et chantent tout: The crystals light up and sing softly… The crystal engine is in place. Look behind you as you sail: a wake of stars!
textes.Les crocodiles de l'embouchure de l'Iter: The crocodiles at the mouth of the Iterou keep stealing the nets of Khéty, the fisherman. He wants someone to bring him two of their teeth, so they get the message.
textes.Les crocodiles du marais ont les meilleu: The marsh crocodiles have the best teeth in the world. Hard as steel. With three teeth, I'll make you an iron fist: your punches will count double in a brawl. Well, a bit more.
textes.Les crocodiles viennent de l'embouchure,: The crocodiles come from the river mouth, to the east. There are three, maybe four. The biggest one we call Sobek, like the crocodile god. He doesn't deserve the name.
textes.Les câbles de la Colonne, c'est ma forge: My forge makes the hooks for the Column's cables. For the Cloud line, Mistress Capucine ordered two hundred brand-new ones. I made them, she checked them one by one through her spectacles. The line has reopened. Not one hook has budged. She very nearly did.

The Column's cables? My forge makes the hooks. For the Cloud line, Mistress Capucine ordered two hundred brand-new ones. I made them, and she checked them one by one with her goggles. The line reopens soon. My hooks are ready. She's almost ready.
textes.Les daurades « d'hier » de Paulo ? C'éta: Paulo's sea bream “from yesterday”? They were mine. I'd kept them overnight in my bucket, I couldn't be bothered to go to the stall. Rosalie took them without a word, and when Paulo shouted, she swore they were from that morning. She fell out with him for my sake. Don't repeat that, youngster.
textes.Les dents ? Une à chaque victoire. Il ne: The teeth? One for every win. I haven't a single real one left. That tells you how often I win.
textes.Les derniers feux s'éteignent dans le ci: The last fireworks fade in the sky, the flying lanterns turn into stars. Lumina cries with joy in Bobor's arms. “The most beautiful Night of Lanterns in a thousand years!” (The party itself will go on until dawn.)
textes.Les dettes ne rouillent pas, sous la mer: Debts don't rust, under the sea.
textes.Les deux ! Comme Youssef. Il casse en so: Both! Like Youssef. He breaks things with a smile, then pays in sardines. So be careful when you turn around, all right? Especially if you're smiling.
textes.Les deux ! Comme le chocolat à la cannel: Both! Like cinnamon hot chocolate! You're on Rosalie's side, sweetie. Go and tell Firmin it's my recipe.
textes.Les deux ! Comme le fer : solide, mais o: Both! Like iron: strong, but you can give it any shape if you heat it enough. You'd make a good metal, you would.
textes.Les deux ! Comme le feu de la Forge : il: Both! Like the Forge fire: it roars by day, it purrs by night. You've got it all figured out. We'd make a smith of you. A lady smith or a lad smith. Both, depending on the day!
textes.Les deux ! Comme ma fille et moi. Elle f: Both! Like my daughter and me. She does the useful, I do the pretty, and between us we make a house that stands up. More or less up.
textes.Les deux ! Je les ai encore tous les deu: Both! I've still got both of them!
textes.Les deux ! Tic-tac, tic-tac, BOUM ! C'es: Both! Tick-tock, tick-tock, BOOM! That's exactly how Zigomar's rockets work. You've got a scientific mind. I hereby name you my assistant.
textes.Les deux ! Un cœur grand comme un chenil: Both! A heart as big as a kennel, with a cat flap! You've got room, you have. Want a pup? No? Think about it. You've got room.
textes.Les deux ! Une réponse de sage. Ou de ma: Both! A wise man's answer. Or a merchant's. So take a sardine, and a note on the house: SARDIIINES! There, you've got everything.
textes.Les deux ! Voilà. Tu as compris ce que j: Both! There you go. You've understood what took me eighty years to understand: the best stories are true and made up. They happened twice.
textes.Les deux : un château dans un arbre !: Both: a castle in a tree!
textes.Les deux ? (Elle réfléchit longtemps.) …: Both? (She thinks for a long time.) … You know what? That's not silly. I'll try it. If it's good, I'll call it “traveller's sauce.”
textes.Les deux ? Ha ! Tu es gourmand. C'est bi: Both? Ha! You're greedy. Good. Both does exist: it's called the Requin Borgne. And no, she's not for sale.
textes.Les deux ? Montre. … Hm. Celle-là travai: Both? Show me. … Hm. That one works. That one watches. Put the other one to work.
textes.Les deux ? Petit diplomate ! Tu ferais u: Both? Little diplomat! You'd make a good mayor. Not a good measurer, but a good mayor. Right, I'm sulking. Just a little, for form's sake.
textes.Les deux ? … Les deux. Mais oui ! Pourqu: Both? … Both. Of course! Why didn't we think of that?
textes.Les deux dalles d'Isis s'illuminent ! Co: Both of Isis's slabs light up! Against the back wall, a casket slowly rises from the floor.
textes.Les deux dans la même tasse… (Il se grat: Both in the same cup… (He scratches his moustache.) My brother and I never thought of that. Fifty years of arguing, and the answer was right there. Don't tell anyone. I'm going to try it in secret.
textes.Les deux en même temps. J'y pense souven: Both at the same time. I think about it often. It's a good idea.
textes.Les deux forges de la terrasse, c'est po: The two forges on the terrace are for heavy work. The Royal Forge, under the mountain, is for masterpieces.
textes.Les deux gardiens de bronze s'effondrent: The two bronze guardians collapse with one last clatter. The sheepfold goes quiet again… At the back of the niche, a small fresco.
textes.Les deux gardiens de pierre s'arrachent: The two stone guardians tear themselves free from their pedestals!
textes.Les deux gardiens sont tombés. Dans un c: Both guardians have fallen. With a rattle of chains, the grate rises!
textes.Les deux poids sont sur les dalles d'or: Both weights are on the golden slabs! A deep “clack” somewhere in the walls: the south door sinks into the floor.
textes.Les deux vieux de la pétanque, Raymond e: The two old boys at the pétanque pitch, Raymond and Marcel, have been squabbling for forty years. They're inseparable.
textes.Les deux villages ensemble, en direct de: Both villages together, live from the Main Stage. The crowd sings. It whistles, it crackles, it's magnificent.
textes.Les deux yeux de corail du Grand Moaï: The Great Moai's two coral eyes
textes.Les deux yeux de corail s'envolent de te: The two coral eyes fly out of your hands, rise high up and settle into the Great Moai's face. He blinks. Once. Slowly.
textes.Les deux, selon l'heure. Comme moi. (Il: Both, depending on the time. Like me. (He gives you a little wave.)
textes.Les deux, toujours ? Tu me prêteras ta l: Both, still? You'll lend me your magnifying glass.
textes.Les deux. Comme moi, peut-être. Le blanc: Both. Like me, perhaps. White by day, colours… in my thoughts. You're wiser than you look.
textes.Les donjons ont une acoustique formidabl: Dungeons have wonderful acoustics for thunder.
textes.Les draps, monsieur ! Je fais les draps: The sheets, sir! I'm doing the sheets!
textes.Les drones sont efficaces. Mais ils ne s: Drones are efficient. But they never land on your head. Shame.
textes.Les drones vont bien. Ils te saluent. En: The drones are fine. They say hi. Well, they blink.
textes.Les dés ? Toujours ! Montre-moi la coule: Dice? Always! Show me the colour of your coins.
textes.Les dés m'aiment. Ils m'ont toujours aim: The dice love me. They always have.
textes.Les dômes du Quartier des Bulles devienn: The domes of the Bubble District turn see-through and take on the colours of the sky.
textes.Les elfes n'oublient rien. Surtout pas l: Elves forget nothing. Least of all kind people.
textes.Les elfes ne quittent presque jamais le: Elves almost never leave Bois-Doré. The mist protects us… and shuts us in a little, too. I'm the first in a long time to speak to a human.
textes.Les enfants croient que je vole. Je les: The children think I fly. I let them. Really, I take the stairs. Very slowly.
textes.Les enfants disent qu'il y a un dragon s: The children say there's a dragon under the great pool. It's the King of the Pools. He gets a little bigger every time someone talks about him.
textes.Les enfants du port veulent tous apprend: The harbour kids all want to learn knots. Little Yasmine is gifted. She'll make a good pirate. Or worse: a good captain of the guard.
textes.Les enfants lumens courent dans les rues: The Lumen children run through the streets counting the stars. They've reached a thousand. They start again.
textes.Les enfants me réclament la pieuvre géan: The children beg me for the giant octopus every night. Thirty arms, then forty, then fifty. Triton came to ask me to stop, very polite, very straight, trident in hand. The children shouted “it's him!” and formed a guard of honour all the way to the Gate. He went bright red. He's never asked for anything since.
textes.Les enfants ont faim, mon grand barbu !: The kids are hungry, my big bearded man!
textes.Les enfants, on ne touche pas aux planèt: Children, we don't touch the planets.
Children, this is the Council House. This is where everything gets decided: the gardens, the cloud water, and snack time.
textes.Les engrenages du Colosse se bloquent !: The Colossus's gears jam! Its furnace opens: strike!
textes.Les engrenages grincent… et se mettent à: The gears creak… and start turning! The bronze gate lifts, the water of the big pond rushes into the old canal with a roar. The level drops, drops… In the middle of the pond a big round stone appears.
textes.Les engrenages, toujours ? Ils dansent b: Gears, still? Are they dancing well today?
textes.Les enveloppes de Lola sentent le punch: Lola's envelopes smell of coconut punch. Every one of them. She must write them on the Perroquet's counter, between orders. When I sort them, the whole post office smells like holidays. Once, there was a little syrup stain in the corner. I put the stamp over it, to hide it. A stamp with a heart. By chance.
Agrafe's fanzines are in very good taste. I read them, then I nibble them. That's how I comment.
textes.Les femmes du désert tissent des tapis ;: The women of the desert weave carpets; we weave nets. Same hands, different thread.
textes.Les feuilles qui bougeaient se redressen: The moving leaves stand upright: carnivorous plants! And a bundle of brambles that walks…
textes.Les feux follets ? Des farceurs. Ils te: Will-o'-the-wisps? Pranksters. They charge at you for a laugh. Their laugh hurts.
textes.Les filets bleus sont pour les sardines,: The blue nets are for sardines, the orange ones for sea bream. The green one… the green one is the one the pirates tore with their anchor. I'll make them pay for it.
The nets are cast. Sing, Celebrë.
textes.Les flammes vacillent… puis toutes s'éte: The flames flicker… then all go out at once. That was not the right order.
Flowers! You've got a gardener's heart. Flowers, you don't eat them, you don't catch them: you look at them. It's the finest job there is.
textes.Les fleurs de braise poussent sur les pe: Ember flowers grow on the slopes of the volcano. My mother is always looking for some for her flowerbeds. They burn without burning up: a botanical mystery. If you pick some, hold them by the stem, and speak to them politely.
textes.Les fleurs de cempasúchil, orange comme: Cempasúchil flowers, orange like the sun, go on the altars to guide the souls of the dead. Their scent shows them the way.
textes.Les fleurs des Jardins suspendus se tour: The flowers of the Hanging Gardens all turn towards the sky and blink along with it.
textes.Les fleurs des jardinières, c'est moi qu: I sowed the flowers in the window boxes. Red at the Buvards', yellow at the Pinceaus', blue at the Council. Well, that's how it was. Now it's white, white and white.
textes.Les fleurs gardent un peu de la chaleur: The flowers keep a little of the day's warmth. And when they wake up, breakfast is already served. Clever, eh?
textes.Les fleurs le matin, les fleurs l'après-: Flowers in the morning, flowers in the afternoon, and in the evening, my bench. There was Hugo and his refused rose, waiting in a vase. Léa, a real florist from the mainland, who I talked with for two hours. Kiki, my neighbour from the ferry terminal, who plays the ukulele under my window at midnight. And the elves' moonflower, which I've never seen, and which grows in my dreams.
textes.Les flocons de givre éternel tombent sur: Everlasting frost flakes fall on the northern cliffs, where the wind never stops. They don't melt. Not even in Pyra's hand. Especially not in Pyra's hand.
textes.Les fraises ! Tu as raison, elles sont d: Strawberries! You're right, they're delicious. And they don't fly away, which makes them handy to pick. Here, taste this one. Her name's Brigitte.
textes.Les fraises de Flora sont dans mon jus d: Flora's strawberries are in my sunshine juice. I say it's my secret recipe. The secret is her strawberries. She knows. She says nothing. She's the kindest woman on the island. And the greenest.
textes.Les fraises, c'est pour le goûter ?: Are the strawberries for snack time?
textes.Les fraisiers géants ont besoin de chans: The giant strawberry plants need songs. I sing them lullabies. They grow in their sleep.
textes.Les fusées de Zigomar prêtes, revenir la: With Zigomar's rockets ready, come back at night (after 8 p.m.) to the Great Lantern Square for the party
textes.Les fusées sont prêtes, grâce à tes cris: The rockets are ready, thanks to your sulphur crystals! Now they're just waiting for the Night of Lanterns. And a bit of luck. A lot of luck.
textes.Les fèves de cacao, chez nous, servent a: Here, cacao beans are also used as money. A rabbit is worth ten beans. A turkey, a hundred. Me, I'd rather drink them.
Fairies? Glitter gnats. All of them. … Brindille is nice. Don't repeat that.
textes.Les fées de l'ouest ont des fleurs de lu: The fairies in the west have moon flowers. Here, we have moon mushrooms. The fairies say their flowers glow brighter. The fairies say a lot of things.
textes.Les fées des racines, sous l'Arbre-Mère: The root fairies, beneath the elves' Mother Tree, are our cousins. They dig; we fly.
textes.Les fées du Bois-Doré auraient des cloch: Apparently the fairies of the Bois-Doré have little bells that ring in rhythm. I'd so love to hear them.
textes.Les fées du village ont toutes un servic: The village fairies all have a favour to ask of you. In exchange, they give fairy dust!
textes.Les fées m'ont dit que la musique de Mis: The fairies told me Mistral's music rises all the way to their kingdom, when the wind blows the right way.
textes.Les galions ne volent pas, Silas. Mais r: Galleons don't fly, Silas. But go on.
textes.Les gardiens de corail… Des soldats chan: The coral guardians… Soldiers turned to stone. My sword cuts through them like stale bread. Especially the third hit.
textes.Les gargouilles des ruines, au nord-oues: The gargoyles from the ruins, to the north-west, come and steal my fish from the quay. They drop out of the sky like stones, grab a sea bream and off they go. One took a whole grouper from me. The grouper was bigger than she was.
textes.Les gargouilles ne plongeront plus sur v: The gargoyles won't dive onto your sails anymore.
The gargoyles crumble to dust. The courtyard is yours… To the east, the library; to the west, the armoury; to the north, the keep, sealed.
textes.Les gargouilles, voilà mon souci. Elles: The gargoyles, that's my worry. They nest in the Ruins of the Old Pandemonium, on the north-west cliffs, and they dive at my ships: sails torn, fish stolen. Stone skin, bat wings. My harpoons bounce right off them.
textes.Les genoux grincent, mais le cœur bat à: The knees creak, but the heart beats at a hundred and forty-five.
textes.Les gens croient qu'un disquaire vend de: People think a record seller sells records. No. A record seller listens to people, and finds them the record they need. Sometimes it's a happy record. Sometimes it's a sad one. Sometimes it's a silence.
textes.Les gens croient que je ne parle pas par: People think I don't talk because I'm shy. No. It's just that at the Guild there's Tancrède, Rodrigue, Bertrand and Mélusine. There's no room left for words.
textes.Les gens croient que je suis seule. Je n: People think I'm alone. I'm never alone. I have a hundred and twelve gulls, a lamp, the sea, and Léon, who brings me bread every morning, grumbling. That's plenty of company, for someone who doesn't like noise.
textes.Les gens croient que je suis triste. Non: People think I'm sad. No. I'm attentive. It's not the same.
textes.Les gens d'Aztlán vivent sur un lac, dan: The people of Aztlán live on a lake, in white houses, and grow gardens that float. Gardens that float! Here, it's the garden that drowns, when the flood comes.
The folk from down below come to stare into the void. We come to watch the folk from down below staring into the void. It's very entertaining.
textes.Les gens d'en haut arrivent avec des cha: Folk from up top arrive with hats and leave with bolts in their ears. Lumi calls it the Fronde effect.
textes.Les gens d'en haut demandent combien coû: Folk from up top ask how much a bowl costs at the Free Canteen. We answer: “How much have you got in your heart?” They rummage in their pockets. It's sweet.
textes.Les gens d'en haut s'étonnent que notre: The folk up top are surprised our train goes round in circles. I'm surprised their cabins go straight up. No bends! How dull.
textes.Les gens d'ici ? J'en connais quelques-u: The folks around here? I know a few. Which one interests you?
The folks around here? I know a few. Which one interests you?
textes.Les gens d'ici croient que nous sommes v: The people here think we came to plunder. We came to search. It's not the same thing. … Well, a little.
textes.Les gens d'ici ont leurs habitudes : le: People here have their habits: at work in the morning, elsewhere in the evening. If you can't find someone, come back at another time.
textes.Les gens d'ici sont charmants mais ils o: The people here are charming, but they've all got a little problem. Talk to them, you'll see. I'll give a reward to whoever helps out the whole town.
textes.Les gens de Hautefond nous appellent « l: The people of Hautefond call us “the Perchers”. I think that's pretty. We call them “the Floor”. I think that's less pretty. I paint them postcards of their town seen from above. They buy them to send to their cousins up here. It makes for a funny journey.
textes.Les gens des Strates disent qu'on est «: The Strata folk say we're “the noisy quarter”. We say they're “the early-to-bed quarter”. Then at eight o'clock they're all in the pit. And at eleven they grumble because it's over.
textes.Les gens des Strates disent qu'on fait t: The Strata folk say we make too much noise. Then at eight o'clock, they're all in the pit. And at eleven, they're begging for one last song.
textes.Les gens des Strates, à côté, sont nos c: The Strata folk next door are our cousins. They have the Guild, the Great Clock, the Brass Sun, rules for everything. We have the Assembly and a brazier. They say we're messy. We say they're too tidy. In the evening, they come to the concert. On Sundays, we go to their market. All's well.
textes.Les gens des brumes viennent parfois sur: The mist people sometimes come onto the beach at night, without a sound. They leave shells on Fañch's boat. Nobody knows why.
textes.Les gens des brumes, à l'est, jouent à u: The mist people, to the east, play a game with white and black stones. My automaton wanted to learn. It lost. I never talk about it.
textes.Les gens des brumes, à l'est, pêchent da: The mist people, in the east, fish in the pools with baskets. They say their fish glow at night.
textes.Les gens disent que je suis bougon. Je n: People say I'm grumpy. I'm not grumpy. I'm focused. If I smile, I lose my train of thought. The last time I laughed, half the Bubble Quarter went dark. It was because of one of Gloubi's jokes. I still hold it against him.
textes.Les gens du Dôme d'Azur, tout au fond de: The people of the Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea, are our cousins: two cities of glass, one in the air, the other under water. Their line is closed for works, but we write to each other. They send me shells. I send them clouds in jars. They arrive empty. They say thank you all the same.

The people of the Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea, are our cousins: two cities of glass, one in the air, the other under water. Their line has just reopened, and we still write to each other. They send me shells. I send them clouds in jars. They arrive empty. They say thank you all the same.
textes.Les gens du Plancher font la queue à la: The Floor folk queue at the Station all the way to the Belvedere. I bring them herbal tea. They're so happy to be up here.
textes.Les gens du camp m'ont trouvé assis au b: The camp folk found me sitting by the pond, breathing. They called the spot the Mantra Pond. Then they called me Mantra. It was the pond that gave me my name. Bernard stayed in the mountains.
textes.Les gens qui se connaissent parlent les: People who know each other talk about each other. Listen closely: that's often where you learn the most.
textes.Les gigues ! Ha ! Toi, tu as des pieds q: Jigs! Ha! You've got feet that want to live! Come tonight, I'm playing the whalers' jig. Watch out for flying chairs.
textes.Les glands d'or ? Pomme-de-Pin en trouve: Golden acorns? Pomme-de-Pin finds one now and then, at the top of the oldest oaks. Owls adore them. For a golden acorn, I'd give… a moon feather, there.
textes.Les gobelins du Bois des Lutins ont des: The goblins of the Goblin Wood have very hard fangs. Bring me some: I set them as arrowheads for Lison. She pays me in cakes. Well, she shows me the cakes. Then she eats them.
textes.Les gobelins du Bois des Lutins sont dev: The goblins of the Goblin Wood have grown bold. They have a chief now, with a banner. They stole three helmets from the barracks. Not the helmets: the plumes off the helmets. To decorate the banner.
textes.Les gobelins sont rapides. Il faut viser: Goblins are fast. You have to aim where they're going, not where they are. It's in the book.
textes.Les golems des hauteurs ont été taillés: The golems of the heights were carved by our ancestors to guard the Heart of the Mountain. Someone — or something — woke them. They no longer recognise anyone.
textes.Les golems des hauteurs… ce sont les anc: The golems of the heights… they're the mountain's ancient guardians. They woke when the volcano rumbled. Nori says someone woke them.
textes.Les golems descendent plus bas chaque nu: The golems come further down every night. I don't like it.
textes.Les graines lumineuses de Photon se sont: Photon's glowing seeds have flown off to the Zero-Gravity Garden: over there nothing falls back down, and they're floating right at the top. Photon's knees are too old to jump that high. They must be caught (three seeds) and brought back to him so you can plant them together.
textes.Les grands arbres de la jungle font de b: The big jungle trees make good masts. But to cut them, you have to cross spider territory. Nobody wants to go. Me neither.
textes.Les grands, au lac ?: The big ones, at the lake?
textes.Les grenouilles bondissent, et elles ont: The frogs leap, and their tongues are as long as a rope. If they swallow you, don't struggle. They spit you out after three seconds. If you struggle, it takes four. That's worse.
textes.Les grenouilles demandent de tes nouvell: The frogs are asking after you.
textes.Les grenouilles géantes du lac ont une b: The giant frogs of the lake have slime that heals blisters. Swallowed adventurers come out with brand-new feet. That is not a recommendation. It is an observation.
textes.Les grenouilles géantes sont de plus en: There are more and more giant frogs. They steal my fish, my bait, and once, my rowing boat. If you could chase a few away… I'll pay you in fish. And in eternal gratitude.
textes.Les grenouilles me regardent. Je crois q: The frogs are looking at me. I think they've heard about me.
textes.Les grilles se ferment… La cabine s'enfo: The gates close… The cabin sinks into the rock. Next stop: Strata Station!
textes.Les grilles se ferment… La cage s'enfonc: The gates close… The cage sinks into the rock. Next stop: the Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea!
textes.Les guitares jouent encore. Tu les enten: The guitars are still playing. Do you still hear them?
textes.Les hautes terres, c'est chez moi : la b: The highlands are home: the heather, the wind, the sheep, the snow in winter. It's harsh, but it's beautiful. And nobody ever blows anything up.
textes.Les histoires de Corentin changent chaqu: Corentin's stories change every night: a mapmaker's nightmare. But at the bottom of each one, there's a little piece of truth. I hunt for it with a pencil.
textes.Les horloges de la Cité des Nuées sont e: The clocks in the City of Clouds are made of glass, apparently. You can see the gears turning. When the line reopens, I'll go up and see them. With my screwdriver. Just to look. Perhaps to adjust. Ever so slightly.
textes.Les humains ont des oreilles rondes. C'e: Humans have round ears. It's cute.
textes.Les humains vivent si peu de temps… Dis-: Humans live such a short time… Tell me: if you had three hundred years ahead of you, what would you do with them?
Your thoughts settle back into place.
textes.Les images ! Les étoiles comme des miett: Images! Stars like crumbs, the moon like a biscuit… You have a poet's eye. Even if your feet are heavy.
textes.Les ingénieurs de Cliquetis ont regardé: The engineers from Cliquetis looked at my bridges. They wanted to replace them with metal ones. I asked them if metal could dance. They went home.
textes.Les ingénieurs de Cliquetis ont une gran: The engineers of Cliquetis have a big telescope, I hear. An astronomer over there, Céleste, writes to me. She says our moon is an illusion. I told her to come and see.
textes.Les inventées ! Ah, un rêveur. Tu sais,: Made-up ones! Ah, a dreamer. You know, a made-up story always ends up happening somewhere. You just have to wait. And then, it's happened twice.
textes.Les inventées ? Ha ! Tu es bien comme mo: Made-up ones? Ha! You're just like me, you are. But don't tell Céleste: as far as she knows, I only tell the truth. With a little garnish.
textes.Les inventées ? Écoute. Un conteur inven: Made-up ones? Listen. A storyteller made up a djinn in a sardine. The next day, a fisherman opened a sardine, found nothing… and searched his whole life. The story had come true. You see?
textes.Les jaguars du Mont Fumant: The jaguars of the Smoking Mountain
textes.Les jaguars du volcan ne tueront plus de: The volcano's jaguars will kill no more turkeys.
textes.Les jaguars du volcan… je viens avec toi: The volcano jaguars… I'm coming with you.
textes.Les jaguars, il faut leur jeter des os,: You have to throw bones to the jaguars, like the Twins. Then they gnaw and forget to eat you!
textes.Les jardins d'algues sont derrière les m: The seaweed gardens are behind the houses, at the edge of the dome. They drink the crystal's light.
textes.Les jardins de Radis vous informent : le: Radis's gardens inform you: the tomatoes are red. The courgettes are green. And Radis is proud. End of announcement.
Young Moai don't know anything anymore.
textes.Les jeunes d'en haut demandent si on n'a: Young folk from up top ask if we're not afraid the glass will break. Eighty years of glass over our heads, and Yolande tapping every pane. Me, I sleep like a log.
textes.Les jeunes d'en haut ouvrent de grands y: Young folk from up top go wide-eyed at the Mushroom Gardens. Good. Wide eyes are like lanterns: they light things up.
textes.Les jeunes de Rainville, ils font de la: The young folk of Rainville play music very loud, with screeching guitars. They think I don't like it. I love it. I knit in time.
textes.Les jeunes de la Fronde sont venus peind: The young folk of the Fronde came and painted the mine entrance one night. At first I grumbled. Then I saw that above the entrance they'd painted a miner with a helmet. Properly fastened. Chin strap and all. I didn't say another word.
textes.Les jeunes disent que Nono danse comme u: The youngsters say Nono dances like a seal. In my photos, he dances like a wave. You just have to look at him long enough, that's all.
textes.Les jeunes disent que je danse comme un: The young ones say I dance like a seal. A very elegant seal, I hope.
textes.Les jeunes mariés de l'hôtel se sont dis: The newlyweds at the hotel had a row on the beach. She was crying. He must have lost something…
textes.Les jeunes mariés de la chambre sept ne: The newlyweds in room seven haven't spoken since yesterday. The young lady is crying on the balcony.
textes.Les jours d'Alerte des Navets, je fais d: On Turnip Alert days, I make little turnip-shaped rolls. They all sell out. Captain Ferdinand always takes one. He says it's to practise catching them.
textes.Les jours d'Alerte des Navets, toute la: On Turnip Alert days, the whole town runs to the South Gate. I had an arrow painted on the ground. People follow it. So do the turnips, by the way. In the other direction.
textes.Les jours d'après, j'ai refusé la rose q: In the days after, I refused the rose Hugo had bought at Rose's. Doctor Roux made me herbal tea in the hotel garden. The gentleman with the moustache had tea sent up to me. Madame Dupuis passed me chocolate over the railing. And Pauline told the whole town everything. The eleventh day, that's what I call the day after: the one when you start again. Everyone has the right to an eleventh day.
textes.Les jours de brume, Monsieur Yvon a enco: On misty days, Monsieur Yvon is even more scared than usual, because he can't see the frogs coming. So I go and sit next to him on the jetty, and we're scared together. We don't talk. He fishes. I pray. Sometimes he gives me a fish. Sometimes I fall in the water. He fishes me out with his net.
On crisis days, I forget to eat. Gwenola always knows, I don't know how. At noon on the dot, a full crêpe appears in front of me, and Gwenola stands there, arms crossed. I tried giving her an order, once. She laughed. Then she waited for me to eat.
textes.Les jours de gros souci, l'Amirale oubli: On days of big worries, the Admiral forgets to eat. So at noon, I save her the back table, put a full crêpe in front of her and stand there, arms crossed. She sighs: “Gwenola, I don't have time.” I don't move. She eats. Every time.
textes.Les jours de pluie, je vais au Bazar écr: On rainy days, I go to the Bazaar to write the labels. “Useless”, on the propeller umbrella. “Useless”, on the silent whistle. “Very useless”, on the compass that points south. Madame Bricolette says nobody writes the word “useless” as beautifully as I do. It's a gift, apparently. I didn't know I had one.
textes.Les jours de pluie, quand mon bras gratt: On rainy days, when my arm itches, I find a little pot outside my door. Graphite ointment, with a label: “For the arm. É.” She never signs any other way. And she never drops it off when I'm in.
textes.Les jours sans vent, Clovis se met devan: On windless days, Clovis stands in front of the mill and blows on it. It's no use at all. I come and sit on the fence to watch him. He blows, I laugh, the turnips get scared and stay still. Once, I blew with him. One of the sails moved. Just a tiny bit. We looked at each other. We've never spoken of it since.
textes.Les lanternes de lune, sur les ponts, ce: The moon lanterns on the bridges are pool mushrooms that glow at night. Every spring, I put new ones out. This year, my old paws won't carry me to the water's edge any more.
textes.Les lapins de Ramure se lèvent avant le: The rabbits of Ramure get up before the sun. We light the oven, we knead, we taste. We taste a lot.
textes.Les lianes, ne t'y pends pas trop. Celle: The vines: don't hang off them too much. The one on the right dropped me three times. We're not speaking any more.
textes.Les longues-vues sont gratuites. Les nua: The spyglasses are free. So are the clouds. Enjoy them.
textes.Les loups veillent sur Ramure depuis que: The wolves have watched over Ramure ever since Mère-Lune arrived. She was a she-wolf too, and a tracker. The wolves followed her. We still follow her.
textes.Les loups, c'est l'endurance. On court l: Wolves are all about stamina. We run for ages. The Great Race is too short for a wolf, that's the problem. It ought to go round the whole island.
textes.Les lucioles d'Yggdrasil sont mes cousin: Yggdrasil's fireflies are my cousins. They know all the Tree's secrets.
textes.Les lucioles sont en avance, cette année: The fireflies are early this year.
textes.Les lueurs s'éteignent une à une. Les se: The glimmers go out one by one. The secrets hide again. They're still there, somewhere.
textes.Les lunettes de soleil, la nuit… je dis: Sunglasses at night… I say it's style. Truth is, without them I'm shy. If you look a clown in the eyes, you see he's scared of not being funny. With the glasses, nobody sees a thing. You can see, {surnom}. But quickly, okay? There. Putting them back on.
textes.Les mains d'ombre reculent devant la Lue: The shadow hands recoil before the Moonglow and sink back under the flagstones!
textes.Les mannequins de paille de l'Aire des D: The straw dummies on the Duelling Ground, I've burned every one of them at least once. Not on purpose. Pyra says it's a record.
textes.Les marches de lumière tintent sous tes: The steps of light chime under your feet, one by one… A thousand steps, but they climb all by themselves. And here you are in the ruined tower, in broad daylight, the Royal jelly heart in your bag.
textes.Les marches du donjon sont glissantes. H: The dungeon steps are slippery. Hilaire slipped here a hundred times. I understand him.
textes.Les marches sentent la pomme verte. Ce n: The steps smell of green apple. That's not a good sign.
textes.Les marches tremblent un peu. Tout en ba: The steps tremble a little. Way down at the bottom, a huge engine goes “vroom”. Politely.
textes.Les mares de la forêt sont reliées sous: The forest pools are connected underground, says Mère-Lune. A fish that dives here comes up over there. That's why the King of the Pools is everywhere and nowhere.
textes.Les mariés de la sept ont perdu leur all: The newlyweds in seven lost their wedding ring on the beach. She won't see him until he's found it.
textes.Les matins d'hiver, quand son savon gèle: On winter mornings, when his soap freezes, I bring Basile gear cookies. We dunk them in our coffee while we wait for the boiler to thaw. He blows on them to cool them, and a little bubble comes out every time. He doesn't do it on purpose. He just can't help it.
textes.Les meilleures cachettes d'Astralys ? Je: The best hiding places in Astralys? I won't tell you. Fine, just one: the fountain, between two planets. Nobody thinks of looking inside Jupiter. It's too big. That's why it's perfect.
textes.Les meilleures de tout l'archipel. Le fo: The best in the whole archipelago. Gustave's solar oven bakes them in the morning light. By evening, they taste a little of sunset. I swear.
textes.Les meilleurs rêveurs. Lulu est comme to: The best dreamers. Lulu is like you: she dreams with her eyes open, while dancing. Her dreams rise all the way up here. Perhaps yours do too.
textes.Les miens aussi. Mais eux, c'est la flem: Mine too. But mine are just lazy.
textes.Les moineaux, c'était elle. Elle leur do: The sparrows were hers. She gave them crumbs every morning, behind the Residences. When she left, they came tapping at my window. I shooed them away. The next day, they came back. I put out crumbs. Since then, they've been called Pip, Crumb, Hazel and Gérard. Gérard is the fattest. I don't feed them. I… I maintain them.
Mummies are wrapped in linen. Hundreds of metres of it. Sometimes I think I'm weaving for people who aren't dead yet. It gives me the shivers.
textes.Les moteurs ont un caractère, vous savez: Engines have personalities, you know. Brindille, in the north, is nervous. Grondin, in the east, grumbles but never gives up. Mélodie, in the south, sings when the wind turns. And Old Timer, in the west, is Séraphin's first. He says nothing. He holds.
textes.Les mots redeviennent des aboiements et: The words turn back into barks and meows. The animals keep talking, but you can't understand anymore. They were surely saying important things. Or “mine”.
textes.Les mouettes croient qu'elles règnent su: The seagulls think they rule the harbour. Seagulls think a lot of things.
textes.Les mouettes me volent une sardine sur d: The seagulls steal one sardine in ten from me. I count it as a tax.
textes.Les mouettes montent parfois jusqu'à la: The gulls sometimes fly all the way up to the City of Clouds. They come back down with crumbs of pure-white cake. Since the line reopened, everyone's going up to see. Choux buns, apparently. Hortense already knew. Me, I'm staying. Somebody has to mind the lamp.

The gulls sometimes fly all the way up to the City of Clouds. They come back down with crumbs of an all-white cake. I don't know what they eat up there. When the line reopens, Hortense will go and see. I'm staying. Somebody has to mind the lamp.
textes.Les mouettes n'ont aucune oreille musica: Seagulls have no ear for music whatsoever.
textes.Les mouettes sont jalouses de notre élég: The seagulls are jealous of our elegance. Look at this grey. This purple sheen on the neck. Coo-roo.
textes.Les mouettes sont plus nombreuses cette: There are more seagulls this year. Or else Mustapha is grilling more sardines. Both, no doubt.
textes.Les mouettes te disent bonjour. Enfin, e: The seagulls say hello. Well, they screech.
textes.Les mouettes volent les frites, ici. Gar: The seagulls steal the fries here. Guard your snack.
textes.Les moustiques ne dorment jamais. Les pr: Mosquitoes never sleep. Nor do priestesses.
textes.Les moutons du fond, suivez !: Sheep at the back, keep up!
textes.Les murs de la rue Haute sont fins. Le s: The walls on the Rue Haute are thin. In the evenings, I hear Lola writing: the pen, paper being crumpled, starting over. I've never said a thing. To anyone. A musician listens, he doesn't repeat. I just play a little softer when Lucas walks into the Perroquet. She asks me to stop. I don't.
textes.Les murs sont humides. La foudre aime l': The walls are damp. Lightning loves damp. I'll be careful. Very careful.
textes.Les murs tremblent doucement au rythme d: The walls tremble gently to the rhythm of the sails. An apprentice walks by, a sack on his shoulder, white from head to toe.
textes.Les mâts se lèvent… les voiles se déplie: The masts rise… the sails unfold… PERFECT! You have fairy fingers! Here, this one's for you.
So did the jellyfish, I think.
textes.Les méduses de ciel ! (Elle rougit en bl: Sky jellyfish! (She blushes blue.) You have good taste. They're shy, but if you sing softly, they come. Try it.
textes.Les méduses de ciel aiment le Jardin des: Sky jellyfish love the Zero-Gravity Garden: there, they don't even need to float, they fall upwards. For them it's like a nap.
textes.Les méduses de ciel arrivent avec les ve: Sky jellyfish arrive on the high-altitude winds. They're see-through, they glow at night, and they sing very softly, like someone rubbing the rim of a glass. I look after them when they're tired. Then they leave again. Some stay. I never know which ones.
textes.Les méduses de ciel s'allument une à une: The sky jellyfish light up one by one and come to swim in the auroras.
textes.Les nains de la Montagne de Feu ont de g: The dwarves of Fire Mountain have great forges. I went there when I was young. They found me too hairy. I found them too chatty.
textes.Les nains forgent mieux que moi. Je ne l: The dwarves forge better than me. I'll only say that once.
textes.Les nains m'ont demandé si je pouvais jo: The dwarves asked if I could play louder. Louder! They're miles away!
textes.Les nains n'aiment ni la magie, ni les e: Dwarves like neither magic, nor elves, nor water. But they do like gold, fizzy drinks and good stories. Tell them about Nâga. Exaggerate a little.
textes.Les nains sont bourrus, mais ce sont les: The dwarves are gruff, but they're the best blacksmiths in the world. Grommelot says that's not true. Grommelot is jealous.
textes.Les navets ! Ha ! Tu es un vrai Montjoye: Turnips! Ha! You're a true Montjoyan. Bring me golden turnips during the Great Alert, I'll pay you a good price. Better than Germaine.
textes.Les navets de Gaubert se sauvent au prin: Gaubert's turnips have been running away every spring for a hundred years. My grandfather used to say a fairy blessed the field one day when she was in a bad mood. Since then, the turnips have legs. And no manners.
textes.Les navets de Montjoie se sauvaient en c: The turnips of Montjoie used to run away. I'd follow them. It wasn't to eat them. Well, a little.
textes.Les navets de la ferme se sauvent depuis: The farm's turnips have been running away for a hundred years. My grandfather chased one all the way to Seagull Harbour. The turnip jumped into a fishing boat and headed out to sea. Never seen again. My grandfather said it had started a family on another island. He sent it cards at Christmas.
textes.Les navets dorés, ce sont ceux qu'on att: Golden turnips are the ones you catch during the Great Alert. They shine a little, they're sweet, and they stop running once they're caught. I pay a good price for them. So does the Guild. But I smile as well.
The turnips are very handsome, on that side.
textes.Les navires ont un problème, capitaine ?: Are the ships in trouble, captain?
textes.Les neuf couleurs sont revenues ! Toute: All nine colours are back! All of Sketched Island regains its colours at once, like a watercolour spreading…
textes.Les nouilles de Hiro… ou de Gaston. Peu: Hiro's noodles… or Gaston's. Doesn't matter: they're perfect.
textes.Les nouvelles runes de garde brillent su: The new warding runes shine on the gates. Thanks to you, the city sleeps better.
textes.Les nuits claires, on voit un château da: On clear nights you can see a castle in the sky, far to the south, above the ocean. A king should worry about that. I worry about it. Royally.
textes.Les nuits de pluie, mon encre de seiche: On rainy nights, my cuttlefish ink thickens. So I go and set my ten little pots on the warm stone, next to his forge. In the morning, I take them back, and I leave a pearl on the anvil, for rent. He never says anything. One day, I saw a little jar on his shelf: he keeps them all. There are about thirty.
textes.Les nuits de pluie, son encre de seiche: On rainy nights, her cuttlefish ink thickens in her tent. She comes and sets her pots by my forge so it stays runny. Ten little pots lined up on the warm stone. In the morning, she takes them back. She always leaves a pearl on the anvil. I say nothing. I keep it. I have thirty.
textes.Les nuits de tempête, {surnom}, je ne do: On stormy nights, {surnom}, I don't sleep. Abdelkader is somewhere at sea, on his coaster, and I listen to the wind in the shutters. Do you know why my Friday tajine matters so much to me? So there's always a dish waiting for him on the fire. Even when he's not here. Especially when he's not here.
textes.Les nuits où la reine ne dort pas, je m': On the nights the queen doesn't sleep, I settle beneath her windows with a lamp and an empty scroll. Sometimes her lamp goes out. Then I write, very precisely: “The queen's lamp went out.” I don't write that she slept: I don't know that. But I hope so, very hard. And hope can't be archived.
textes.Les offrandes du Grand Temple: The offerings of the Great Temple
textes.Les oiseaux chantent. C'est bon signe. Q: The birds are singing. That's a good sign. When they go quiet, it means there's a goblin. Are they singing? They're singing.
textes.Les oliviers, à l'est, ils ont trois cen: The olive trees, to the east, are three hundred years old. They were here before the temple, before the Borgo, before me. I say hello to them every afternoon. They don't answer. They're polite in their own way.
The bears of Ramure are strong and slow. We forge, we carry, we don't run. Leave the racing to the rabbits.
textes.Les ouvriers de la pyramide, autrefois,: Long ago, the pyramid workers were paid in bread and beer. My family fed them. Without us, no pyramid!
textes.Les paniers de légumes des Jardins Parta: The vegetable baskets from the Shared Gardens haven't arrived at the Pay-What-You-Can Canteen. No vegetables, no soup, and no soup means half of the Boucan will go hungry tonight. Three baskets must be fetched from the Shared Gardens.
textes.Les papillons ! Ils vont être ravis. Adè: Butterflies! They'll be delighted. Adèle, did you hear? We have an admirer. … She's flapping her wings. She's pleased. She's a bit full of herself, too.
textes.Les papillons sont mes collègues. Adèle,: The butterflies are my colleagues. Adèle, Basile, Pétronille, and three hundred others. They pollinate, I prune, they rest, I water. They're never late and they never complain. Well, except the ones in the third dome.
textes.Les parents d'Ysaé, Rivet et Bielle, ent: Ysaé's parents, Rivet and Bielle, maintain the rails for the mine carts. By day, wrenches. By night, guitars and drums, with their band, the Valves. I made them a lantern that blinks in rhythm, for the stage. It blinks even when they play out of tune. Especially then, in fact.
textes.Les pattes de Ramure sont rapides… Une r: Ramure's paws are quick… A rematch?
textes.Les perles pour ta robe de fête: The pearls for your party dress
textes.Les perles pour ta robe de fête…: The pearls for your party dress…
textes.Les perles… Vous aimez ce qui se cache l: Pearls… You like what stays hidden for a long time and grows slowly, layer after layer. Nobody chooses pearls by chance. I'll look at you differently now.
textes.Les petites ! (Il les prend dans ses mai: The little ones! (He takes them in cupped hands. All the flowers in the Gardens blink twice. Twice means thank you.) Come, let's plant them together. A hole made with a finger, a seed, a little soil, a little water... and a kind word. That's the most important part, the kind word. Say something to it. ... There. Did you see? It blinked. It heard you. Tomorrow morning, at sunrise, they'll sing. Off-key, surely. But with a great deal of heart.
textes.Les petites annonces de la Gratuiterie :: The Free Shop classifieds: Trocante has received a nervous umbrella, a well-travelled teapot and a mysterious sock that fell from the sky. First come, first served. One per day!
textes.Les petits Moaïs, beaux joueurs, te donn: The little Moai, good sports, give you their treasure.
textes.Les pierres ? Elles ont dit quoi, les pi: The stones? And what did the stones say?
textes.Les pierres disent qu'hier l'était aussi: The stones say yesterday was too.
textes.Les pierres du Cercle attirent les éclat: The stones of the Circle attract moon shards, and I gather some there for my lessons. The first time, Ysolde appeared behind me without a sound. I dropped the shard, my glasses and a bit of my dignity. Now I say thank you out loud to each stone before gathering. Nine thank-yous. She nods at the ninth.
textes.Les pierres s'éteignent toutes d'un coup: All the stones go dark at once… That wasn't the right order. (The firefly pool can show you the song again.)
