textes.Ma première lame entière, je l'ai forgée: My first whole blade, I forged it in ten days. I showed it to him, proud as anything. He took it, rang it on the anvil, looked at it. Then he put it back in the fire. Melted. Without a word. I cried behind the coal store. The next day, I forged a better one. He said: “Hmph.” That was a lot.
textes.Ma première loi : « Personne ne remplace: My first law: “Nobody shall replace Zéro.” The council laughed. Then it voted yes, unanimously. My second law: “Be kind, even to machines.” It fits on one page. It's the most respected law in the city.
textes.Ma première mission d'aventurière, c'éta: My first mission as an adventurer was at the Frog Lake, with Hilaire. He got swallowed. I prayed so hard the frog spat him out on top of me. We were both covered in slobber. He said: “Thank you, Sister.” I said: “Eww.” Then I cried. Then I laughed.
textes.Ma première montée au Belvédère, j'avais: My first ride up to the Belvedere, I had my eyes shut. When the doors opened, all the passengers went “oooh”. I opened one eye. I saw the whole island, all golden. I went “oooh” too. Then I sat down on the floor. But I'd seen it.
textes.Ma première médaille, je l'ai gagnée à d: I won my first medal at twelve: the hat-throwing contest at the Column festival. My hat went up to the first floor. It stayed there three years. I still have the medal. The hat, Mistress Capucine kept. As an example.
textes.Ma première nuit, à seize ans, au moment: My first night, at sixteen, just as I was lifting the moon out of the pond, I stumbled. The whole Circle held its breath. And Mother Moon's voice, so gentle, from her moss: “You don't lift it, little one. You rock it.” I rocked. Since then, every evening, at that moment, I still hear her, even when she says nothing.
textes.Ma première planche de skate, c'est Papa: My first skateboard, Dad made it for me from a bit of pallet, and Mum put the wheels on. It was square. It rolled badly. I fell two hundred times. Then Ferraille gave me real wheels from the Scrapyard. I fell three hundred times. But faster.
textes.Ma première plongée avec Sofia, j'ai bu: My first dive with Sofia, I drank half the bay. I came up coughing and laughing: “It's like dancing, but you can't shout!” Sofia laughed too, a real laugh, not her quiet little smile. She said nobody had ever described diving so well.
textes.Ma première rime, je l'ai faite à sept a: I made my first rhyme at seven, in Augustin's class: “The pencil's too long, I'll sharpen it right, or else rub it out.” Augustin rubbed it out. He said “out” didn't rhyme with “right”. I've decided it does, ever since.
textes.Ma première semaine à Tazira, je passe à: My first week in Tazira, I pass by the auction on my way back from Aïcha's, nose full of pepper. Saïd is calling a lot of sardines, and me: “ATCHOO!” Saïd points his finger: “SOLD TO THE PIRATE!” I tried to explain, but I sneezed again. Second lot. Forty kilos in all.
textes.Ma première sortie, j'ai été malade tout: My first trip out, I was sick all morning, green as anything, clinging to the side. Then, all of a sudden, I saw a whale on the horizon. I shouted “WHALE!” with all my might. The whole fleet turned around. There was nothing there. Everyone laughed all the way back to the channel. Since then, I see them everywhere: off the Skala, behind the jetty, under the boats. I do, I swear.
textes.Ma première soucoupe à moi, je l'ai appe: My very own first saucer, I called it “Rocket”. It's not a rocket, it's a saucer. But it has the soul of a rocket. Ionie says it mostly has the soul of a saucepan. Rocket has lost forty-three fins, two portholes and a seat. It still flies. It's like me: dented and very happy.
My first storm, I was really scared. The Shark was leaning so much that Mange-Clous's soup sloshed from one wall to the other. Gros-Louis tied me to himself with a rope and sang a lumberjack song all night, very out of tune and very loud. In the morning, the sun came back. And I knew the song by heart. I still sing it when I'm scared.
textes.Ma première vraie lame, je l'ai forgée à: My first real blade, I forged at sixteen for Master Hugues, when he became master of the Guild. A great sword, tempered three times. He took it, weighed it in his hand, and cried. Of course. He still hangs it above his desk. He says it's too beautiful for slimes.
textes.Ma première épée, je l'ai achetée chez B: I bought my first sword from Brunehaut with three years' savings. I christened it Twilight, at the top of a cliff, at sunset, with a twenty-minute speech. Then I slipped and spent the night on a ledge. In the morning, Lison came by. She said “here” and threw me a rope. A single syllable. What style.
textes.Ma presse de sérigraphie, je l'ai trouvé: I found my screen-printing press in the Spinning Mill, under three metres of old bobbins. Rusty, jammed, abandoned. It took me six months to wake it up. I named it Little Gutenberg. It squeaks on every page. I oiled it. Now it squeaks better. Its first poster: the Bilge Rats' very first concert.
textes.Ma promenade du matin fait le tour du Vi: My morning walk goes all the way round the Old Dock. The seagulls tease the dogs, the dogs chase the seagulls, and nobody ever catches anybody. It's everyone's favourite game.
textes.Ma proposition tient toujours : des leço: My offer still stands: lessons, early in the morning, no witnesses. I'm used to it. Well… I mean, I've got the time.
textes.Ma proposition à moi : une fête des cerf: My own motion: a kite festival every Tuesday. We've been debating it for three Tuesdays now.
textes.Ma punition, c'était de faire briller la: My punishment was to polish the gondola rail. The whole rail! It took me a whole afternoon, with a cloth and some stuff that smells of lemon. Afterwards, the commander looked at her reflection in it and said: “Right. A pilot has to know how to polish.” A pilot! She said a pilot! Since then I've wanted to be a pilot.
textes.Ma recette vient de ma nonna. Elle metta: My recipe comes from my nonna. She used ten fish, saffron, and a secret I'll never tell. Not even under torture. Especially not under torture.
textes.Ma relève ! Tiens, prends la clé de paro: My successor! Here, take the speaking wrench. No, I'm not joking. Hold it for a minute. … Well? Heavy, isn't it? It's meant to be. What you say, you have to carry.
textes.Ma robe brille comme un matin de rosée,: My dress shines like a dewy morning, thanks to you. Caelan saw it. He dropped his harp.
textes.Ma robe, je l'ai cousue avec Velours, av: My dress, I sewed it with Velours, with a piece of every garment people gave me in my first year. Twenty-two dresses in one. When I wear it, I feel like the whole Boucan is hugging me.
textes.Ma roulotte a fait le tour de l'archipel: My caravan has gone round the archipelago three times. I stopped here because the trees listened to me. Twisted trees make excellent confidants.
textes.Ma roulotte, c'est Copeau qui l'a remise: My caravan? Copeau put it back on its wheels. It hasn't moved in a long time: the mushrooms have grown around the wheels. They hold it like a hand. I think they don't want me to leave. I don't want to leave.
textes.Ma rubrique préférée : « Nouvelles des a: My favourite column: “News from the other towns”. Yesterday: “In Tazira, a cat steals a treasure map.” People don't believe it. But it's true.
textes.Ma règle, à l'Atelier Libre : on ne jett: My rule at the Free Workshop: we throw nothing away. A lonely screw is a screw waiting for its friends. An old alarm clock is a future toaster. And a toaster is a future alarm clock. Well, that one didn't work out. It rings when the toast is ready. At three in the morning.
textes.Ma réclame dit : « Bazar des Inutilités: My advert says: “Bazaar of Useless Things: here, nothing is good for anything.” One morning, Rosette's press dropped a letter: “nothing is good for anyting”. People came in droves to ask what an “anyting” was. I tripled my sales in a single day. Since then, I've been begging Rosette to make mistakes. She refuses. On principle.
textes.Ma régie, c'est une grande table pleine: My mixing desk is a big table full of knobs, in the middle of the meadow. Every knob has a name. The red one's called Sunflower. The blue one's called Downpour. I always turn them up together, to the same level. Force of habit.
textes.Ma sarbacane, je l'ai faite moi-même, da: My blowgun, I made it myself, from a reed as long as two men. Like the one of Hunahpu and Xbalanque, the Twins. They hit every bird. Me, one in three. Chak calls me “Balam-Who-Misses”. He never misses a chance to say it. Me, I never miss a turkey. That's enough to eat.
textes.Ma secrétaire, Mademoiselle Prune, est d: My secretary, Mademoiselle Prune, is remarkably efficient. She always leaves at precisely eight fifty-five p.m. I don't know where she goes. I suppose she goes off to optimise something.
textes.Ma soucoupe s'appelle « Fusée ». Ce n'es: My saucer is called “Rocket”. It's not a rocket. It's a saucer. But it has the soul of a rocket. Ionie says it mostly has the soul of a saucepan. She's jealous.
textes.Ma sœur Celebrë me chantait une berceuse: My sister Celebrë sang me a lullaby to put me to sleep. I danced. My mother tried every lullaby in the Bois-Doré: I danced to them all. In the end she said: “Fine. Dance, then.” I haven't stopped for three centuries. I sleep very well, by the way. Afterwards.
textes.Ma sœur Cerise fait un fanzine. Elle a é: My sister Cerise makes a fanzine. She wrote an article about me: “Tornade Falls Again”. That's not an article, that's jealousy.
textes.Ma sœur Itto, au désert, ne riait pas be: My sister Itto didn't laugh much in the desert. Since she's lived at the port, with Ali, she laughs. I hear her from the street when I arrive. It took me two seasons to say yes to that marriage. I was wrong. I won't tell Ali. But I sit on his bench.
textes.Ma sœur dit que ces chiens sauvages sont: My sister says those wild hounds are just badly brought up. I say a dog that breathes fire on my guards, badly brought up or not, has to be driven far from our walls. She says a bone would do. The dogs haven't said anything.
textes.Ma sœur habite en bas, à Hautefond. Elle: My sister lives down below, in Hautefond. She calls me “the Percher”. I call her “the Floorer”. We adore each other.
Sister, sit down. Don't back away.
textes.Ma sœur, c'est Signorina Ravioli, à la T: My sister is Signorina Ravioli, at the Tomato Grove. She talks to tomatoes. I talk to brooms. Every family has its thing.
textes.Ma sœur. Forte. Plus forte que moi. Pres: My sister. Strong. Stronger than me. Almost. She growls when I forget the basket. Hrmm. She's right. Often. And for the rest… Hrmm. Nothing.
textes.Ma tante Gwenola tient la taverne, et mo: My aunt Gwenola runs the tavern, and I run the inn. She thinks it's the same thing. She lets me believe I'm the boss, I pretend to believe her. We're very happy like that.
textes.Ma tante était couturière. Chez elle, il: My aunt was a seamstress. At her house, there was a huge button box, thousands of buttons of every colour. I spent whole afternoons sorting them by colour, by size, by mood. At eight, I sewed my first button. Crooked. My aunt kept it on her coat all her life.
textes.Ma tante, l'auberge a besoin de draps ne: Auntie, the inn needs new sheets.
Auntie, jugs are the tavern. I'm the inn.
textes.Ma tata Éclair, c'est la plus rapide de: My auntie Éclair is the fastest in all of Ramure! Well, apart from Bondi. For now. She doesn't talk much, but when she looks at me, it's like a hug.
textes.Ma taverne est au fond de la Guilde, à d: My tavern is at the back of the Guild, to the right of Églantine's counter. By day, people eat there. By night, people eat there too, but with Bertrand's music. You need a good meal to put up with Bertrand.
textes.Ma terra incognita ! Toujours pas décidé: My terra incognita! Still not ready to tell me where you're from? My map is waiting. So is my curiosity.
textes.Ma tisane de lune, c'est sa rosée. Un jo: My moon tea is made with her dew. One day Brindille cried over my pot because she'd failed one of Cardamome's riddles. That batch was the best of my life. I called it “Tea of Tears” and sold it very dear. Brindille paid for hers with a sugared petal. That's the fair price of a tear.
My tea. And not a word.
textes.Ma toile a tenu toute la nuit, même dans: My canvas held all night, even in the wind. Galet says it's thanks to his knots. I say it's thanks to the people dancing in front of it. Both, no doubt.
textes.Ma toute première course, à onze ans. Au: My very first race, at eleven. At the root bend, I fall, twisted ankle. And there's Pépin, on the ground too: he'd fallen just before, poor thing. He took me on his back and we finished the race together, last. He said: “The last ones always arrive together, it's nicer.” Good old Pépin. No good at running, but strong.
textes.Ma toute première semaine, on m'avait mi: My very first week, they put me on nights, for the towels. Around two o'clock, near the fourth-floor linen room, I heard snoring. Real snoring, a big gentleman's snore. I ran to the stairs without looking back. The next day, I looked in the linen room: nobody. Just some slightly rumpled sheets. Since then, I know it: there's a ghost in the Grand Hôtel.
textes.Ma vague ? C'est un phoque élégant, ma b: My wave? It's an elegant seal, my dear. But all right.
textes.Ma version, la vraie : une vague de dix: My version, the true one: a ten-metre wave, out of nowhere, catches me at the bow while I'm holding the tiller with a firm hand. Fernand says the sea was flat as a millpond and I was telling an octopus story. He exaggerates. Let's say the wave was… five metres. Three. Well, a wave.
textes.Ma voisine de la rue Haute. Elle lit l'a: My neighbour on the High Street. She reads the future in cards, I read the time by the sun. One of us has a real job.
textes.Ma voisine du troisième fait des confitu: My neighbour on the third floor makes giant strawberry jam. One strawberry, twelve jars.
My golden voice! I've changed the chorus.
textes.Ma vraie harpe, je l'ai sculptée à cent: My real harp I carved at a hundred, from moonwood, the kind that only grows in the north of the island. It took me twenty years to find its voice. For three centuries I've played at festivals, at births, at farewells. Celebrë sang, I played, and the Bois-Doré danced. Listen to the wind: it remembers.
textes.Macaroni a un tambourin caché sous son C: Macaroni keeps a tambourine hidden under his Lid. In the evening, he brings it out. He's the most serious guard on the island, and the best percussionist. Don't tell him I told you.
textes.Macaroni est le gardien le plus sévère d: Macaroni is the strictest guard on the island and the best tambourine player in the archipelago. By day, he counts to two. In the evening, he counts to infinity.
textes.Macaroni garde le Couvercle. Il croit qu: Macaroni guards the Lid. He thinks it's the most important job. It isn't. But without him, I'd get sauce on my head every day. So I thank him. In my head.
textes.Macaroni me surveille. Toujours. Même qu: Macaroni keeps an eye on me. Always. Even when I'm asleep, I think. I like him, but I tiptoe whenever I walk past the Lid.
textes.Madame ! Pourquoi le ciel ne tombe pas ?: Miss! Why doesn't the sky fall down?
textes.Madame Agathe ! Les étoiles bougeront-el: Madame Agathe! Will the stars move tomorrow?
textes.Madame Agathe lit l'avenir comme je lis: Madame Agathe reads the future the way I read the sky: squinting and hoping. She always has an answer, and she's always kind. She reassures me. I need reassuring.
textes.Madame Barricade est mon principal obsta: Mrs Barricade is my main commercial obstacle. She always asks me if I'm eating properly, as if I were eight. It's very unpleasant. And she gives out very good toffees.
textes.Madame Barricade, je mange de façon parf: Madame Barricade, I eat in a perfectly optimised manner.
textes.Madame Barricade. Libérez les lieux, je: Mrs Barricade. Kindly vacate the premises.
textes.Madame Bielle. Le vert de la Gare tient: Mrs Bielle. The green at the Station is holding up well.
textes.Madame Bricolette ! Votre réclame de dem: Madame Bricolette! Your advert for tomorrow?
textes.Madame Bricolette a racheté tous mes mot: Madame Bricolette bought all my stopped engines. I don't know if it's kindness or mockery. With her, it's often both at once.
textes.Madame Bricolette est la seule personne: Madame Bricolette is the only person in the city who believes I'm a real inventor. I don't contradict her. I don't have that many customers.
textes.Madame Bricolette paie sa réclame à l'he: Madame Bricolette pays for her adverts on time, talks faster than my printing press and sells superb crow-feather quills. The ideal advertiser.
textes.Madame Bricolette rend la monnaie en obj: Madame Bricolette gives change in useless objects. One day, I bought a spring from her, and she gave me a fan-hat as change. I left with it, without understanding why. I kept it in a corner of the stand, and on some hot days, I've even worn it. It's good for nothing. Well, it cooled my thinking. That's already a lot for a useless object.
Madame Bricolette is my competitor. She picks up what's useless, I pick up what falls. Often it's the same thing. She has an eye, I'll admit. Especially for my piano.
textes.Madame Calfat construit le futur vaissea: Madame Calfat is building the future flagship of Port-Coutelas. She doesn't know it yet. She always answers me “When I say so”. She's a woman of decision. I admire that.
textes.Madame Colette est la femme la plus têtu: Madame Colette is the most stubborn woman in the archipelago, and she owns the most mysterious jar of jam in the world. She refuses to sell it to me. Every day. With admirable consistency.
textes.Madame Colette me fait payer le papier d: Madame Colette charges me for the wrapping paper. Me, who pays in gold! A little copper coin for my cheese paper. I found it splendid. I kept the paper: it's in my collection, folded in four, with a label. “Madame Colette's paper. Paid.”
textes.Madame Dupuis, ma voisine de balcon. Ell: Madame Dupuis, my balcony neighbour. She saved me with a square of chocolate and a story about a husband who was always late. I owe her a whole box.
textes.Madame Gisèle m'a appris, l'autre jour,: Madame Gisèle informed me the other day that in two months I had said “thank you” to her only once. She counted! I was mortified. Since then, I say thank you with every coffee. Three thank-yous a morning. She says it's too many, that it breaks her concentration. We are looking for a happy medium.
textes.Madame Gisèle tient le meilleur café de: Madame Gisèle makes the best coffee on the island. I've told her so, I believe. Once. I think a great deal, you see. I talk little, in the mornings.
textes.Madame Honorine ! C'est une soupe, votre: Madame Honorine! Your hot chocolate is a soup!
textes.Madame Hortense ! L'horloge, avant la fi: Madame Hortense! The clock, before the end of the year!
textes.Madame Hortense. Cinquante ans qu'elle r: Madame Hortense. Fifty years she's been winding that clock. She asked me for a cog. She was right to ask. Hm.
textes.Madame Hurla : « ABANDON ! Il a quitté l: Madame Hurla: “FORFEIT! He has left the sand!” The crowd boos (kindly). We'll replay the round whenever you like.
textes.Madame Hurla : « DEUXIÈME MANCHE ! Ils o: Madame Hurla: “SECOND ROUND! They have fangs, they have flames, they have no manners: TWO HELLHOUNDS!”
textes.Madame Hurla : « K.O. ! On le ramasse !: Madame Hurla: “K.O.! Someone pick him up!” Two demons carry you to the arena door, and Bulle brings you a mug of hot sulphur tea. We'll replay the round whenever you like.
textes.Madame Hurla : « LA FINALE ! Sept ans in: Madame Hurla: “THE FINAL! Undefeated for seven years, two metres forty of horns, a heart of butter: GORGOTH THE HORNED!” The crowd leaps to its feet.
textes.Madame Hurla : « TROISIÈME MANCHE ! Du b: Madame Hurla: “THIRD ROUND! Walking bronze and sniggering imps: TWO AUTOMATONS AND TWO IMPS!”
textes.Madame Hurla crie les nouvelles sous les: Madame Hurla shouts the news under the palace windows at nine o'clock sharp, every day. I must grant her punctuality. It is, moreover, the only thing I grant her.
textes.Madame Hurla crie les nouvelles sur la p: Madame Hurla shouts the news on the square before I've delivered the letters announcing it. Once, she announced her own birthday before I'd brought the invitations. Everyone came. Without an invitation.
textes.Madame Hurla crie les nouvelles à neuf h: Madame Hurla shouts the news at nine o'clock under the palace windows. I have written her seventeen letters of protest. She read them. Out loud. In the square.
Madame Hurla shouts over my music. I play louder, she shouts louder. It's exhausting. It's also our biggest hit. I don't know if we're friends or rivals. Both, probably.
Madame Hurla shouts over my violin. So I play louder. Once it turned into such a duel that the crowd threw coins at us. We split them. She shouted thank you.
textes.Madame Hurla crie si fort que les chiots: Madame Hurla shouts so loud that Flammèche's puppies come and hide under me. Twelve puppies under one Gorgoth. Nobody can see us any more, but we're comfy.
textes.Madame Hurla m'a trouvé sur le port et m: Madame Hurla found me at the port and made me a champion. She shouts my name so loud I blush right up to my horns. She's tiny and afraid of nothing. I'm huge and afraid of everything.
textes.Madame Hurla, dans son porte-voix : « ME: Madame Hurla, through her megaphone: “LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, DEMONS! First round of the Tournament of Horns: THREE IMPS, more annoying than nasty!”
textes.Madame Hurla, la maîtresse de l'Arène de: Madame Hurla, mistress of the Arena of Horns, is looking for a contender for the great tournament: four rounds, the last one against Gorgoth the Horned, the undefeated champion.
textes.Madame Hurla… pas trop fort, mon nom, au: Madame Hurla… not too loud with my name today?
textes.Madame Josette ! Je n'ai pas faim, je pa: Madame Josette! I'm not hungry, I'm just passing by…
textes.Madame Lumi ! J'en ai un nouveau !: Mrs Lumi! I've got a new one!
textes.Madame Léa ! Je n'ai rien dit à personne: Madame Léa! I haven't told anyone anything today.
textes.Madame Léa, de la sept. Une jeune person: Madame Léa, from room seven. A charming young person who has cried a great deal on our balconies. The management was very affected.
textes.Madame Margaux fait les croissants les p: Madame Margaux makes the goldenest croissants in the archipelago. She keeps them for me every morning, in a bag all my own. A woman who understands that a croissant is a collector's item.
textes.Madame Margaux, la boulangère. Une victi: Madame Margaux, the baker. A brave victim and a remarkable baker. She makes remarks to me. I note them down.
textes.Madame Nautile dit que la Colonne relie: Miss Nautile says the Column links four worlds, like the floors of a house. We're the cellar. But a cellar with a whale! Above us, the Strata, with a brass sun. Above that, Hautefond, with the real sky. And right at the top, a city sitting on the clouds! I want to visit every floor. In one day. With my class.
textes.Madame Nautile dit que le ciel n'a pas d: Miss Nautile says the sky has no ceiling. I don't completely believe her. Everything has a ceiling. Even the sea, since boats walk on top of it.
textes.Madame Nautile est la seule grande perso: Miss Nautile is the only grown-up who says “I don't know” when she doesn't know. She teaches us the sky with postcards, every Thursday. She's gentle, but you have to keep your hands on your knees. Except during the Sky Lesson. Then, we're allowed to put our arms up.
textes.Madame Nautile, la carte des vents est b: Miss Nautile, did the wind map arrive safely?
textes.Madame Nautile. Vos élèves sont prêts ?: Miss Nautile. Are your pupils ready?
textes.Madame Olga ! Ne touchez pas à cette épé: Madame Olga! Don't touch that sword!
textes.Madame Olga a ouvert sa fenêtre pour fai: Madame Olga opened her window to let out a draught spell. The spell got out, along with three pages of her spellbook. They've been scattered all over town.
textes.Madame Olga a sûrement acheté de nouvell: Madame Olga has surely bought new things. She's always buying new things.
textes.Madame Olga achète n'importe quoi et app: Madame Olga buys any old thing and calls it magic. She bought one of my failed potions, drank it, and turned pink. Without any scientific explanation. It's unbearable.
textes.Madame Olga m'a encore apporté une « pie: Madame Olga brought me another “magic stone”. It was a pebble. She made me pay for it. I paid. She's too sweet for anyone to say no to.
textes.Madame Olga me prête des livres, des gri: Madame Olga lends me books, spellbooks and advice. She forgets half of what she knows, but the other half is extraordinary. She's the one who sold me my hat.
textes.Madame Olga veut enchanter mes épées. La: Madame Olga wants to enchant my swords. The last one turned pink and sang. Olga is adorable, but I hide my blades when she comes by. And I buy her pebbles anyway.
Madame Olga wants to enchant my swords. Last time, the sword turned pink and sang whenever you drew it from the scabbard. I sold it to Rodrigue. He doesn't know yet that it sings.
Madame Olga, I've finished the book.
textes.Madame Olga, votre grimoire a l'air bien: Madame Olga, your spellbook looks rather thin
Madame Olga, your spellbook looks rather thin…
textes.Madame Olga. Votre hibou est encore tomb: Madame Olga. Your owl has fallen in front of my door again.
textes.Madame Rita lit l'avenir dans les cartes: Madame Rita reads the future in the cards. I think she mostly reads it in the promenade gossip. But she does it with such talent that I keep coming back.
textes.Madame Rita ne voit pas l'avenir. Elle c: Madame Rita doesn't see the future. She knows the rumours very well. The worst of it is, she's sometimes right. It annoys me.
textes.Madame Rita prétend voir l'avenir. Moi j: Madame Rita claims she can see the future. What I mostly see is that she knows the gossip very well.
textes.Madame Rita, c'est ma voisine et ma copi: Madame Rita is my neighbour and my friend. She reads the future in the cards and she always has an aniseed sweet in her pocket. Her predictions are incredible. Really. Incredible.
textes.Madame Takeda me dit bonjour avant que j: Madame Takeda says hello to me before I say hello to her. She is the only one. I find it very difficult to handle, and very pleasant.
textes.Madame Ysolde ! La petite pierre a toujo: Madam Ysolde! Does the little stone still have my blanket?
textes.Madame la Première Conseillère ! Un peti: Madam First Councillor! A little speech?
textes.Madame la Présidente ! C'est bientôt jeu: Madam President! Is it nearly Thursday?
textes.Madame, je vous prie. Il est neuf heures: Madame, if you please. It is nine o'clock.
textes.Madame. La direction espère que tout va: Madam. The management hopes all is well.
textes.Madame. Nous sommes à un pas l'un de l'a: Madam. We are one step away from each other.
textes.Mademoiselle Aurore est la personne la p: Mademoiselle Aurore is the most efficient person I have ever met. She manages the Baron. I only manage turnips. I respect her deeply. And I admire her a little.
textes.Mademoiselle Aurore m'a raccompagné à la: Miss Aurore showed me to the castle door with a calm that froze my blood. Since then, I send her flowers. For the tower. Only. She never replies. Exceptional.
textes.Mademoiselle Bardane a vécu trois cents: Miss Bardane lived three hundred days in a tree to stop me cutting it down. It's absurd. Inefficient. Almost admirable. The willow is still there.
textes.Mademoiselle Bricole. Ce rouage est hors: Miss Bricole. This cog is out of tolerance.
textes.Mademoiselle Clémence a beaucoup de tale: Mademoiselle Clémence has a lot of talent and a funny idea of helping people out. She saw my camera, and she left it there. So as not to disturb it, I suppose.
textes.Mademoiselle Clémence règle sa chambre e: Mademoiselle Clémence pays for her room in paintings. It is a decision of the management. The management has excellent taste.
textes.Mademoiselle Feuillet me prête les carte: Miss Feuillet lends me the sky charts and scolds me in a whisper when I bring them back late. I know of nothing more delightful. Apart from the stars. And even then.
textes.Mademoiselle Lin ! Votre lumière brille: Miss Lin! Is your light still shining?
textes.Mademoiselle Lin a lu les quatre cents p: Miss Lin has read all four hundred pages of the chapter on light. I never have. She casts her spells slowly, but her lights don't flicker. Don't tell the others: she's my best pupil.
textes.Mademoiselle Lin respecte les livres com: Miss Lin respects books as few adults do: she dog-ears nothing, wets nothing, doesn't talk. She reads. She even reads far too fast. That's all I ask, and a little more.
textes.Mademoiselle Lyra ! Je vous salue bien b: Miss Lyra! I bow most deeply to you!
textes.Mademoiselle Lyra ? Une vraie elfe, {sur: Miss Lyra? A real elf, {surnom}! Three hundred and twelve years old and not a single wrinkle. I get one per tide, and she finds me charming all the same.
textes.Mademoiselle Ombreline a mis une pancart: Mademoiselle Ombreline has put a sign up at the library: “Here, we whisper. And we don't fly.” I'm sure it's meant for me. Now I walk in. But my wings are noisy.
textes.Mademoiselle Ombreline laisse la fenêtre: Miss Ombreline leaves the library window open at night, with a candle. I don't know why. … Yes. I do know. Thank you, Ombreline.
textes.Mademoiselle Ombreline m'envoie un rappe: Miss Ombreline sends me a reminder about a book I borrowed sixty-three years ago. Very politely. Every year. I'll give it back. As soon as I've finished it.
textes.Mademoiselle Ombreline sait où dort chaq: Miss Ombreline knows where every book in the city sleeps, and how long I haven't returned it for. She's the most learned person I know. And the most patient: sixty-three years of patience.
textes.Mademoiselle Ombreline, le livre… j'en s: Miss Ombreline, the book… I'm on chapter three.
textes.Mademoiselle Philippine Feuillet, à la B: Miss Philippine Feuillet, at the Library of Maps in Hautefond, sends me sky maps for my class: the stars, the clouds, the winds. She writes very small, very straight, with arrows. My pupils love her arrows. They follow the winds with their fingers.
textes.Mademoiselle Philippine chuchote, range: Miss Philippine whispers, files away countries that don't exist, and never folds a map the wrong way. I slip a poem into every sack of flour. I don't know if she finds them. I'd rather not know. Well… I'd like to know.
textes.Mademoiselle Philippine me prête les car: Miss Philippine lends me the Library's star charts. I return them late. Always. She scolds me in a whisper. It's the gentlest telling-off there is. I return them a little later still, just to hear it.
textes.Mademoiselle Philippine, de la Bibliothè: Miss Philippine, from the Library of Maps, drew a map of the Fronde without ever having seen it, just from Ysaé's words. There are mistakes everywhere. The Chasm is too small, the Swap Shop is upside down. It's the most beautiful map in the world.
textes.Mademoiselle Philippine… votre farine. P: Miss Philippine… your flour. For the… Library.
textes.Mademoiselle Pigment peint des fleurs su: Miss Pigment paints flowers on everything I have repainted grey. Every night. It's inefficient, costly, and… the blue is very well done. I didn't say that.
textes.Mademoiselle Prune a un badge des Rats d: Mademoiselle Prune has a Bilge Rats badge under her jacket. I saw it shine. I didn't tell Dad. We all have our secrets, at the Sales Office.
textes.Mademoiselle Prune arrache sa moustache: Miss Prune rips off her cardboard moustache and shouts: “BRAVO, GÉDÉON!” Nobody is surprised. Everybody claps.
textes.Mademoiselle Prune compte les fois où je: Miss Prune counts how many times I say “optimise”. Fourteen an hour, according to her. I asked her why she was counting. She said: “To optimise your vocabulary, Sir.” Since then, I've been careful. I'm down to eleven an hour. That's a twenty-one percent improvement.
textes.Mademoiselle Prune est d'une efficacité: Miss Prune is remarkably efficient. Except with the post. My eviction notices often get lost. It's the only weakness I know of in her.
textes.Mademoiselle Prune m'a apporté sa veste: Miss Prune brought me her office jacket to mend. I sewed her a secret lining with pockets for her badges. I didn't say a word. And you didn't hear a thing.

Mademoiselle Prune brought me her office jacket, all grey, “for a little button”. She slipped me a box of Bilge Rats badges. I sewed her a secret lining, with a pocket for each badge. When she saw it, she buttoned the jacket up very quickly and smiled. A big smile, not regulation at all.
textes.Mademoiselle Prune me laisse empiler les: Miss Prune lets me stack the folders in the shape of a drum kit. She gave me a stapler that goes “chak”. She's the kindest person at the Sales Office. Mind you, there are only three of us.
textes.Mademoiselle Prune passe parfois, en lun: Miss Prune drops by sometimes, in dark glasses, and takes an old Bilge Rats record. She hides it in her “Evictions” file. Nobody ever looks in that file.
textes.Mademoiselle Prune vient faire recoudre: Mademoiselle Prune comes to have buttons sewn back on that have never come off. I know why she comes. She knows I know. We never talk about it.
textes.Mademoiselle Prune, Tchak fonctionne tou: Miss Prune, Chak still works perfectly.
textes.Mademoiselle Prune, le courrier est part: Miss Prune, has the post gone out?
textes.Mademoiselle Prune, notez : le client hé: Miss Prune, take note: the customer is hesitating. Offer them our brochure. (Prune holds out a brochure. A little Bilge Rats badge falls out of her sleeve. She picks it up very quickly.)
textes.Mademoiselle Sulfura ! Henri brille touj: Miss Sulfura! Is Henri still glowing?
textes.Mademoiselle Sulfura ! J'ai fait une fla: Miss Sulfura! I made a purple flame!
textes.Mademoiselle Sulfura ! Une fusée pour vo: Miss Sulfura! A rocket for you, tonight!
textes.Mademoiselle Sulfura a été mon élève. À: Mademoiselle Sulfura was my pupil. At her first lesson, she set my beard on fire. Today, she's the best flame teacher at the Academy. I keep my beard short. As a precaution.
textes.Mademoiselle Sulfura est la meilleure pr: Miss Sulfura is the best flame teacher the Academy has ever known. She set fire to my beard in her first lesson, and to the staff room last year. Talent comes at a price.
textes.Mademoiselle Sulfura est la plus brillan: Miss Sulfura is the most brilliant of flame teachers. Her hair is orange like a rocket at lift-off. She laughs at my failed rockets. I make her laugh often. That's something.
textes.Mademoiselle Sulfura, c'est la maîtresse: Miss Sulfura is the flame teacher. She's got orange hair like fire, and she never shouts, even when my fireflies fly off in the classroom. She says my sparks are original.
textes.Mademoiselle Sulfura, c'est la meilleure: Miss Sulfura is the best teacher in the world. She teaches me flames in secret, in the evening. She says I'm her best pupil. She also says I need to be more discreet. I don't see why.
textes.Mademoiselle Sulfura, la salle des profe: Miss Sulfura, is the staff room intact?
textes.Mademoiselle Sulfura… Ah. Je lui envoie: Mademoiselle Sulfura… Ah. I send her heart-shaped rockets. The last one exploded in the shape of a kidney. She laughed. She laughed! That's a start, isn't it?
textes.Mademoiselle Volta. Votre horloge avance: Miss Volta. Your clock is fast.
textes.Mademoiselle Écrou veut remettre le Peti: Mademoiselle Écrou wants to get the Petit Piston running again. I like her, but I think he'd rather sleep.
textes.Mademoiselle. Encore des fleurs sur mon: Miss. More flowers on my wall.
textes.Mademoiselle. Vous ne descendez pas, je: Miss. You're not coming down, I suppose?
textes.Mae govannen, voyageur. Chez nous, les p: Mae govannen, traveler. At our place, plants grow when you sing to them. Want to sing with me?
textes.Magnifique ! (Son halo s'allume si fort: Magnificent! (His halo lights up so brightly a gull changes course.) Thank you! Thank you! I'll add a word. The word “magnificent.”
textes.Magnifique ! Ce matin, j'ai coupé le rub: Magnificent! This morning I cut the ribbon on the Square's new bench. A forty-minute speech. The bench was deeply moved. The people sitting on it, rather less so.
textes.Magnifique ! Du fer bien lourd. Avec ça,: Magnificent! Nice heavy iron. With that, my roof will last at least… a week!
textes.Magnifique ! Ils sentent encore la mer !: Magnificent! They still smell of the sea! Here, three bowls of my bouillabaisse, and for you, at Paulo's, it will always be a friend's price.
textes.Magnifique ! J'ai mangé quatre parts de: Magnificent! I ate four slices of pie. Mamie Rissole gazed at me lovingly. I believe it's the greatest victory of my day.
textes.Magnifique ! Tu as l'air de réfléchir à: Magnificent! You look like you're thinking about something very important. What were you thinking about? … Snack time? Perfect.
textes.Magnifique ! Tu as une voix de pierre !: Magnificent! You have a voice of stone!
textes.Magnifique, le plus beau perroquet du mo: Magnificent, the most beautiful parrot in the world.
Magnificent. It changed a note again.
textes.Magnifiques ! Jaunes comme des canaris !: Magnificent! Yellow as canaries! (He crushes them in a mortar, he mixes, he sneezes, he laughs.) The rockets are ready! Tell Lumina the Night of Lanterns will have its fireworks!
textes.Magnifiques ? Il leur manque le principa: Magnificent? They're missing the main thing: ember flowers! Flame petals, yellow in the middle, red at the tips. They only grow on the slopes of the Great Blaze, where the ground is warm. Bring me five. Don't step on the lava flows, mind you: I'm too old to be treating burns.
textes.Mains de passager. Hm. Ne touche à rien: Passenger's hands. Hm. Don't touch anything on my deck.
textes.Maintenant il vient me voir sur le quai,: Now he comes to see me on the quay, very serious, with his notebook: “My dear Fernand, would you also have mermaid scales?” I told him mermaids are seasonal. He wrote down “seasonal”. I was ashamed all evening. The next day, he brought me a croissant. I was even more ashamed.
textes.Maintenant que la ligne a rouvert, les j: Now that the line has reopened, the gardens of the four worlds talk to each other. My strawberries go up to the Great Market in Hautefond, to Rosalie Cannelle's stall. She sells them as “strawberries from the bottom of the sea”. People buy them to see if they taste of salt. They don't. People buy more anyway.
textes.Maintenant que la ligne du bas a rouvert: Now that the lower line has reopened: to see the folk from up top come down to the Fronde, dance with the folk down below, and the Burgomaster give a speech under a circled-A banner. With a mohawk. Well, at least the brooch.
textes.Maintenant, c'est elle qui enfile mes ai: Now she's the one who threads my needles. In the morning, she hands them to me, ready, without a word. She thinks I don't notice she picks the thickest thread, for my fingers. I notice. I say: “Your thread's too thick.” She says: “Yes, Lalla.” That's how we love each other, between two knots.
textes.Maintenant, chaque fois qu'on m'apporte: Now, every time someone brings me an old map, I show it to Philémon before I buy it. He examines it under the magnifying glass, for a long time, muttering. Then he says “fake”, nine times out of ten. The tenth time, his hands shake a little. I pay him in crow feathers. He goes through a lot of them.
textes.Maintenant, j'ai des genoux qui grincent: These days I have creaky knees and a blue house near the village spring. My granddaughter Lulu has lived with me for three years. In the evening we go down to the party together, she holds my arm all the way to the dance floor, and there I let go. The youngsters say I dance like a seal. Lila has the photo: it's a wave.
textes.Maintenant, j'ai mon étal sur la place,: Now I've got my stall on the square, in the afternoons: botched potions, cheap, every one unique. Zéphyrine is my best customer. In the evening, I put my vials away under my bed, in the dormitory, between Lin who reads and Pip who talks in his sleep. Gustave lends me his cellar. Well, I take it, and he says yes afterwards. It's almost the same.
textes.Maintenant, j'enseigne au pied de la tou: Now I teach at the foot of the tower, since it leans. I have lunch on the bench in Mother Sage's garden, in the afternoon I go and listen to the wind on the cliffs, and in the evening I chat at the fountain. I keep an eye on Pip and his bedsheets. I argue with Borée. I visit Aurélien on his roof. And the wind follows me everywhere, like a mad dog.
textes.Maintenant, je construis des cabanes pou: These days I build huts for whoever wants one. Marley's, above his banana trees. Mistral's stage. My little test hut near the beach, the one that leans, where Zoé is sleeping at the moment. In the evenings, I nod my head next to Tchoum. We don't talk. We're good. Right.
textes.Maintenant, je dors dans la cabane d'ess: Now I sleep in Gaspard's test hut, the leaning one, with three crabs. In the afternoons I go to Yaya's class. I swim with Sofia, I help Momo drill his shells. I dance till sunrise, and every morning I suggest a name for Mistral's track. The village has adopted me, I think. And I've adopted it too.
textes.Maintenant, je grimpe aux passerelles, j: Now I climb the footbridges, I listen to Faelar's stories, I eat Sylwen's bread and I ask loads of questions. Aëlwen patches up my knees. Lyra told me about the sea and the shells. And then you turned up with your round ears! It's the best year of my whole life. Well, of all forty-two.
textes.Maintenant, je me lève à quatre heures,: These days, I get up at four, knead till noon, sleep a little, and in the evening I take the boat with Margaux's leftovers. I dance, I catch the last Swallow back, I sleep three hours. I knead in rhythm, at a hundred and forty-five. Margaux says my croissants have swing. I think that's a compliment.
textes.Maintenant, je passe toutes mes journées: Now I spend all my days at the skatepark, with my flame helmet. Pastille patches up my knees, Cerise draws my falls, Cradoc falls next to me, and Sardine barks when I land a jump. Or when I fall. He barks all the time, actually. But it's cheering.
textes.Maintenant, je peins les voiles des pêch: Now I paint the fishermen's sails: an octopus for Bastien, stars for others. In the afternoon, I nap against Germaine, the speaker that purrs. At night, I pick the fairies' mushrooms in the ring, behind the dune. And the mural on the wall of sound… it's coming along. In my head. It's very beautiful, in my head.
textes.Maintenant, je travaille à la forge le m: Now I work at the forge in the morning, and in the afternoon I go and read the contracts on the Guild board. Églantine won't give me any. So Noisette and I founded our own guild. She does the badges and the questions. I'm the warrior. Hilaire gives us advice. We do the opposite of what he does. It works.
textes.Maintenant, le jour, je classe des dossi: Now, during the day, I file folders at the Sales Office. I stack them in the shape of a drum kit. At lunchtime, I tap the rails of the old wagon with pebbles. And in the evening, I go to the entrance of the Howling Hall. I don't go in. I listen behind the door and tap the rhythm on the wall. Nobody hears me. Well, I think not.
textes.Maintenant, les mouettes connaissent l'h: Now the seagulls know the time. From half past six, there are a dozen of them lined up on the bakery roof. Waiting for the Lord. When he comes out with his bag, they all take off together behind him, like an escort. Nina says it's his royal guard.
textes.Maintenant, mes genoux ne veulent plus g: These days, my knees won't climb any more. I keep watch from the bow, with the spyglass, and it's my grandson Ewen who goes up to light the lantern. I still count the ships. This year: three. Including you. I wrote you in the journal. In ink, not pencil.
textes.Maintenant, quand je vois arriver sa gro: Now, when I see his big moustache coming at the end of the terrace, I hide the salt cellar in my belt. He comes back every day for another glass “to check”, his little bag of salt in hand. I watch him like a guard of the Skala. He's never managed to salt a single glass. Not yet.
There is now. I added it.
textes.Maintenant, à la fin de la criée, Jacquo: Now, at the end of the auction, Jacquot buys up everything that's left: scorpionfish, sunfish, spiky things nobody can name. One day, I followed him to the galleon to see what he did with them. At the foot of the gangway, I caught the smell: cinnamon, herring, and something else. I came back down. There are mysteries a crier must respect.
textes.Maintiens pour mouliner, relâche si ça t: Hold to reel, release if it pulls too hard
textes.Mais Kick et Basse vont s'ennuyer, Gaspa: But Kick and Bass will get bored, Gaspard!
textes.Mais Maman veut que je rentre le soir !: But Mama wants me home in the evening!
textes.Mais Peek' veut apprendre les traces, Ba: But Peek' wants to learn tracks, Balam!
textes.Mais Rê doit m'entendre, Néferet ! Il es: But Rê has to hear me, Néferet! He's far away!
textes.Mais c'est déjà voté, mon grand ! Depuis: But that's already been voted, sweetheart! Since 1998! Unanimously, minus one vote. Pastille's. She wanted free earplugs. We voted that too.
textes.Mais elle te ressemble ! Elle ne sourit: But she looks like you! She never smiles.
textes.Mais je l'écris, mon journal !: But I'm the one who writes it!
textes.Mais je suis déjà là, ami ! Juste à côté: But I'm already here, friend! Right beside you! Didn't you hear my armour?
textes.Mais l'autre main, elle tient la fusée !: But my other hand's holding the rocket!
textes.Mais le Sceau d'Airain cliquette dans ta: But the Bronze Seal clicks in your pocket… The Cogwheel (key 3, then X)?
textes.Mais moi si, si on traîne !: But I will, if we dawdle!
textes.Mais non ! Le secret, c'est de tomber. U: Nah! The secret is falling. Once you know how to fall, you're not scared anymore. I'm super good at falling.
No they're not, come now. … Oh, they are. Thanks, little one.
textes.Mais vous ne savez même pas ce que c'est: But you don't even know what it is!
textes.Mais à Ramure, il n'y a jamais de nuit s: But in Ramure, there's never a moonless night. Maybe that's why we're so rarely afraid here. I keep looking all the same. A nose never sleeps.
textes.Mais… QU'EST-CE QUE TU FICHES CHEZ MOI ?: But… WHAT ON EARTH ARE YOU DOING IN MY HOUSE?!
textes.Mais… comment ça tient ?: But… how does it stay up?
textes.Mais… je suis déjà avec vous ! Juste der: But… I'm already with you! Right behind. There. I just tripped, that's why you didn't see me.
textes.Mais… je suis déjà là, juste derrière to: But… I'm already here, right behind you! I have been all along!
textes.Majesté ! C'est vous ! Vous êtes revenue: Majesty! It's you! You've come back!
textes.Majesté ! Ce soir, je te dessine une cou: Your Majesty! Tonight, I'm drawing you a crown!
textes.Majesté ! Je vous ai apporté des fleurs: Your Majesty! I've brought you moonflowers.
textes.Majesté ! Le brin de ta couronne a une t: Your Majesty! Has the sprout in your crown got a third leaf?
textes.Majesté ! Le soleil, il fait du bruit ?: Majesty! Does the sun make a noise?
textes.Majesté ! Toutes les lettres livrées ! U: Your Majesty! All letters delivered! A record!
textes.Majesté ! Vous avez vu le nez du roi Atl: Majesty! Have you seen King Atlas's nose? I polished it this morning.
textes.Majesté ! Vous êtes descendue ! Pif ! Pa: Your Majesty! You've come down! Pop! Bang! Welcome!
Majesty, your decree is four pages long.
textes.Majesté. Les runes ont parlé, cette nuit: Majesty. The runes spoke last night.
Your Majesty. Your crows are tired.
textes.Majesté. Votre couronne brille, aujourd': Majesty. Your crown is shining today.
textes.Mal. Clou a caché mon marteau. Et il ne: Bad. Clou hid my hammer. And he won't say where.
Badly. I think about too many things.
textes.Mal. Les golems des hauteurs se sont rév: Bad. The golems of the heights have woken up. They come down at night. The stones rumble.
textes.Mal. Très mal. Mais tu n'y es pour rien…: Bad. Very bad. But it's not your fault… well, hardly your fault.
textes.Malachar dit que c'est moi qui ai mis le: Malachar says I'm the one who set fire to the Academy tower, when we were pupils. It was him. Well… it was us. But it was his idea.
textes.Malachar était le premier de la classe,: Malachar was top of the class, and I was bottom in flames. He became headmaster, I became a sweeper, and we both found our place. He refuses to admit that burning down the tower was his idea.
Malachar, the tower was your idea.
textes.Malaterre a des dents en or et des dés e: Malaterre has gold teeth and loaded dice. I can't prove it. He won my compass from me. I can't prove how, either. But I know.
textes.Malaterre sourit en or massif et triche: Malaterre smiles in solid gold and cheats with everything else. Nobody's ever proved it. Me, I only play with him using my own dice.
textes.Malaterre. Ma boussole indique toujours: Malaterre. Does my compass still point north?
textes.Malaterre. Toujours tes dés dans la manc: Malaterre. Still got dice up your sleeve?
textes.Malebolge, le Huitième Cercle : trois fo: Malebolge, the Eighth Circle: three ditches of fire, three turning iron bridges. And little imps, the Malebranches, sniggering as they wait for you.
textes.Malheureuse. Mon mari a perdu son allian: Miserable. My husband lost his wedding ring after ten days. Ten days!
textes.Malin. Les gens en savent plus que les c: Clever. People know more than maps. But watch out: in Carène, if you ask Corentin for directions, you end up in a story, not at your destination.
textes.Mal… Je m'en doutais : tu as les yeux ce: Badly… I thought so: you've got rings round your eyes like a tanuki. Prescription: a mist tea every evening, and no Trèfle tart after midnight.
textes.Mama ! Qui a mis de la cannelle dans mon: Mama! Who put cinnamon in my stew?
textes.Mama ! Une soupe pour le musicien ?: Mama! A soup for the musician?
textes.Mama Grog est la conseillère la plus pré: Mama Grog is the most precious adviser in my government. She doesn't know it. Between us, citizen, she has more authority than I do. Don't repeat that. Especially not to her.
textes.Mama Grog est la seule personne de la Ba: Mama Grog is the only person on the Balafre I'm afraid of. Between us, there's a matter of forty coins and a lukewarm grog. She has her opinion. I have mine.
textes.Mama Grog fait le meilleur grog de l'île: Mama Grog makes the best grog on the island, I'll grant her that. But cinnamon in a stew! She says it's her grandmother's recipe. Her grandmother packed a punch, fine. But she had no taste.
textes.Mama Grog garde un tonneau de cidre de C: Mama Grog keeps a barrel of Carène cider just for me. Nobody else touches it. On this island, that's the closest thing to tenderness. The rest is rum.
textes.Mama Grog m'a donné une soupe et une scè: Mama Grog gave me a soup and a stage the evening I arrived with nothing. I've played for her ever since. She pays me in grog and stew. I'm the best-paid man on Balafre.
textes.Mama Grog me cherche. Je l'évite. C'est: Mama Grog is looking for me. I'm avoiding her. Avoiding Mama Grog is an art. She's everywhere.
Mama Grog is demanding her forty coins.
textes.Mama Grog tient le Crâne Fendu et le por: Mama Grog runs the Crâne Fendu and the port with the same hand. We signed a treaty, years ago, on a napkin. We both respect it. It's the only treaty in the archipelago that's respected.
textes.Mama Grog, c'est la meilleure femme de l: Mama Grog is the best woman on Balafre. Her grog is the best in the world, nice and hot, nice and gentle. I pay my tab every Saturday, down to the last penny. Hic! I'm the only one.
textes.Mama Grog, une holo-photo pour un touris: Mama Grog, a holo-photo for a space tourist?
textes.Mama Lou ? Il paraît qu'elle a coulé tro: Mama Lou? They say she sank three ships. I like her a lot. And I drink everything she serves me. Well… almost everything.
textes.Mama Lou achète toutes ses cruches chez: Mama Lou buys all her jugs from me, and her pirates break them. Three a week. I charge double, she pays without arguing. She calls me “girlie”. I let her.
textes.Mama Lou dit que c'est le rhum qui fait: Mama Lou says it's rum that keeps the peace in Tazira. It's tea. She may have sunk three ships, but peace isn't something you sink: it's something you serve.
textes.Mama Lou, autrefois Lou la Terrible. Ell: Mama Lou, once Lou the Terrible. She threw me into the sea when I was twenty; today, she serves me rum. That's what you call a career. She knows more than she lets on.
textes.Mama Lou, la patronne de la taverne des: Mama Lou, the landlady of the pirates' tavern, used to be a pirate herself. They say she sank three ships. Me, I never tell her her rum is too strong.
textes.Mama Lou, à la taverne, a été pirate. La: Mama Lou, at the tavern, used to be a pirate. The most terrible of them all. She retired because she got seasick. A seasick pirate!
textes.Maman ! J'ai lu un nouveau contrat ! Des: Mum! I read a new contract! Goblins!
textes.Maman ! J'ai trouvé un scarabée vivant !: Mum! I found a live scarab!
textes.Maman ! J'ai vu une tortue ! La quarante: Mum! I saw a turtle! The forty-fourth!
textes.Maman ! J'ai été très sage, aujourd'hui: Mummy! I was really good today!
textes.Maman ! Je peux aller au Bois de Cendre: Mum! Can I go to the Ash Wood?
textes.Maman ! Je peux aller jouer ?: Mum! Can I go and play?
textes.Maman ! Je peux emprunter ta grosse pinc: Mum! Can I borrow your big tongs?
textes.Maman ! Ma planche fait un bruit bizarre: Mum! My board's making a weird noise!
textes.Maman ! Ma prochaine fusée, elle fera de: Mum! My next rocket's going to make green smoke!
textes.Maman ! Pourquoi la pâte, elle gonfle ?: Mama! Why does the dough puff up?
textes.Maman ! T'as vu mon saut ?: Mum! Did you see my jump?
textes.Maman ! Ton bain est prêt ! Moitié prix: Mum! Your bath is ready! Half price!
textes.Maman a essayé de me faire soulever sa p: Mum tried to get me to lift her tongs. I lifted them! A little! She laughed so hard she dropped her hammer. I picked up the bolt that fell with it.
textes.Maman chante quand elle pétrit. Elle cha: Mum sings when she kneads. She sings out of tune, out of tune, out of tune! Even the dough pulls a face. I sing with her, and then we laugh so much she has to start the dough again. Fanny says we're the worst singers on the island. It's true. At least we're champions at something.
textes.Maman cueille les fleurs de tout le vill: Mummy picks the flowers for the whole village. She always smells of violets, and she always knows when I've been naughty. Even when I haven't done it yet.
textes.Maman dit qu'il faut dormir. Mais je ne: Mum says I have to sleep. But I don't sleep. I pretend. And when the auroras start, I look out of the porthole. Don't tell Pixel. She does it too.
textes.Maman dit qu'il faut rentrer quand les l: Mum says you have to go home when the lanterns light up. I say lanterns are for adventurers. Mum says I'm an adventurer who goes to bed.
textes.Maman dit qu'on n'a pas le droit d'y tre: Mum says we're not allowed to dip our bread in it. But she says nothing about fingers.
textes.Maman dit qu'à neuf heures je dois être: Mum says I have to be in bed by nine. But the auroras start at ten! Why don't the auroras start earlier? Why can't I go to bed later? Why doesn't anybody answer?
textes.Maman dit que je n'ai pas le droit de to: Mum says I'm not allowed to touch weapons. Not even little ones. Not even just to look.
Mum says I ask too many questions. Why does she say that?
textes.Maman dit que je suis née un matin de pl: Mummy says I was born on a rainy morning, and that I yelled so loud the frogs in the fountain went quiet. Daddy says I opened my eyes and straight away looked up, at the footbridges. I don't remember, I was too little. But I believe Daddy.
textes.Maman dit que l'Arbre-Mère veille sur no: Mummy says the Mother Tree watches over us at night. Once I asked her: “And who watches over the Mother Tree?” She thought for a really long time. Then she said: “You will, when you're grown up.” Ever since, I say goodnight to the Tree every evening. And to Mummy too.
textes.Maman dit que si je suis sage, on ira vo: Mum says if I'm good, we'll go and see the glowing fish at the Azure Dome. The line has reopened: I've been good for three days!
Mum says if I'm good, we'll go and see the glowing fish at the Azure Dome. When the line reopens.
textes.Maman dit que, bébé, je sautais tout le: Mum says that as a baby I was always bouncing in my cradle. Boing, boing, boing. The cradle was an old pot of Granny Gamelle's, with a cushion inside. One day, I bounced so hard the pot went “dong”. The whole Fronde thought it was dinnertime.
textes.Maman est la Première Conseillère. Elle: Mum is the First Councillor. She decides everything in the city. Except the sea. For the sea, she says “soon”. I love her anyway. Loads. Even with her soons.
textes.Maman est la plus forte de l'île. Elle s: Mum is the strongest person on the island. She lifts the anvil with one hand, she laughs so loud the windows shake, and she makes the best swords in the world. Even Master Hugues cries when he sees hers.
textes.Maman fait des bras de fer avec tout le: Mum arm-wrestles everyone in the Lower Town. She always wins. Once, I asked her to arm-wrestle me. She let me win. I know, because she went “oh no, such strength!” in a weird voice. But I was happy anyway. She told the whole forge I'd won.
textes.Maman fait pousser des fleurs sur l'eau: Mum grows flowers on the water! And maize, and chillies, and squash. She laughs all the time, except when I come home late. Then she laughs afterwards.
textes.Maman m'a donné des graines de maïs à pl: Mum gave me some maize seeds to plant. I put them in with the tip pointing up, so they could see the sun. They all grew crooked. Mum looked at the maize and smiled really big, with wet eyes. She said Dad used to grow maize like that. Dancing maize.
textes.Maman m'a interdit de grimper au premier: Mum told me I'm not allowed to climb to the first platform without the stairs. So I take the stairs! Running, four steps at a time, shouting “I'm obeying!”. Mum goes “Mrrr” with her eyes closed. That means she's got nothing to say back. I won.
textes.Maman m'a offert un petit marteau avec m: Mum gave me a little hammer with my name engraved on it. I improved it with gears and a whistle: now it sings when you shake it. Mum said: “Ortie, a hammer is for hitting.” I answered: “Mum, a hammer can sing too.” She didn't say anything. She shook the hammer. Twice.
textes.Maman m'a tissé une robe avec des algues: Mum wove me a dress out of seaweed in every colour of the canal. She put in a golden thread, a tiny one, hidden in the hem. She says it's a ray of sunshine, so I have one on me until I see the real thing. I check every night that it's still there.
textes.Maman peint les phares de toutes les île: Mum paints the lighthouses on all the islands. She sends me a card of every lighthouse. I've got seven. They're all striped. When I'm big, I'll paint polka-dot lighthouses.
Mum paints the lighthouses on the other islands. She promised to take me next year. I'll bring my pencils. All of them. Even the white one, which is useless.
textes.Maman répare tout, même la poussette de: Mum fixes everything, even my doll's pram. She whistles instead of talking. I understand all her whistles. Tornade pretends not to.
textes.Maman répare tout. Les grille-pain, les: Mum fixes everything. Toasters, guitars, boilers and my knees. She says “it's impossible” before every invention, and afterwards, she builds it. I think “it's impossible,” for her, means “we start tomorrow.”
textes.Maman se lève à quatre heures, elle chan: Mama gets up at four, she sings while she makes the bread, and she always smells of croissant. Her hands are all warm. She says it's the oven. I think it's her.
textes.Maman tape très fort et rit encore plus: Mum hammers really hard and laughs even harder. When she laughs, the bolts jump on the workbench. That's how I collect the most.
textes.Maman tisse les algues : les robes, les: Mum weaves seaweed: dresses, curtains, blankets. She says I'm the only thread she can't keep straight. It's a compliment, I think.
textes.Maman voudrait que je devienne forgeronn: Mum would like me to become a blacksmith. But forging is hitting a thing until it has the right shape. Inventing is hitting things until they do something new. It's not the same.
textes.Maman, c'est la meilleure marchande d'ép: Mum is the best spice seller on the whole island. She smells of cinnamon and pepper. She worries about me all the time. She says that's a mum's job.
textes.Maman, c'est la meilleure tisserande du: Mum is the best weaver on the river! Her linen is so fine you can see the sun through it. She says I run around too much. That's because I have lots of places to go!
textes.Maman, c'est la plus forte de toute la c: Mum is the strongest in the whole city. She hammers iron all day long and laughs so loud the bells ring. She'd like me to be a blacksmith. I love her, but I'm going to be an inventor.
textes.Maman, elle crie fort, elle sent le pois: Mum shouts loud, she smells of fish and she dances like crazy at parties. She's the best mum in the world. But don't tell her, or she'll shout even louder.
textes.Maman, elle fait le meilleur pain et ell: Mum makes the best bread and she gets up while it's still dark. She says I ask too many questions. But she answers anyway. One time in three.
textes.Maman, elle me met de la crème solaire p: Mummy puts sun cream all over me. On my nose, on my ears, behind my knees. I'm all white, I look like a ghost. The ladies on the beach laugh. Even Kevin the lifeguard said “Hi, little ghost.” Mummy says it doesn't matter, ghosts don't get sunburnt.
textes.Maman, elle répare tout et elle siffle t: Mum fixes everything and whistles all the time. I understand all her whistles. Except the one for the 12 spanner. I pretend not to understand that one.
textes.Maman, je veux la chouquette la plus gro: Mum, I want the biggest sugar puff! The one that looks like a cloud!
textes.Maman, on descend quand ?: Mum, when are we going down?
textes.Maman, on peut rester ici pour toujours: Mum, can we stay here forever?
textes.Maman, pourquoi le pain il gonfle ?: Mum, why does bread puff up?
textes.Maman, tu as chanté faux au deuxième cou: Mum, you sang out of tune in the second verse.
textes.Maman, tu me racontes la fin de l'histoi: Mummy, will you tell me the end of the story?
textes.Maman. Il me faut de la menthe de cendre: Mum. I need some ash mint. Three bunches.
textes.Mamie ! Je t'ai fait une couronne !: Granny! I made you a crown!
textes.Mamie ! Tu montes à la mezzanine ce soir: Mamie! Coming up to the mezzanine tonight?
textes.Mamie Barricade a la santé d'une docker: Mamie Barricade has the health of a twenty-year-old docker and the temper of a mountain. She refuses to be treated. She agrees to be monitored. That's something.
textes.Mamie Barricade et Tapage se disputent s: Mamie Barricade and Tapage argue about 1977 or 1978. We were there. Well, our great-grandparents. They don't remember. They were pigeons.
textes.Mamie Barricade m'a appris à tricoter. J: Mamie Barricade taught me to knit. I knit everyone's guitar cases. With studs on them. Soft inside, spiky outside. Like us.
textes.Mamie Barricade m'a demandé une chaise à: Mamie Barricade asked me for a rocking chair “with studs”. I put studs on it. She said: “More.” I put more. She rocks like a queen.
textes.Mamie Barricade m'a donné une cuisine, u: Mamie Barricade gave me a kitchen, a pot and a family. She leaves three coins under her bowl every lunchtime. I pretend not to see.
textes.Mamie Barricade m'a ouvert la porte de l: Mamie Barricade opened the door of the Cannery to me without asking a single question. She gave me a room on the third floor, a studded scarf and one sentence: “Here, you can shout.” The first night, I shouted out of the window. The whole squat shouted back. I fell asleep smiling.
textes.Mamie Barricade m'a ouvert sa porte quan: Mamie Barricade opened her door to me when I was twelve and never closed it. Everything good I know, I learned beside her knitting.
textes.Mamie Barricade me regarde toujours comm: Mamie Barricade always looks at me as if I were still eight years old. It's very unpleasant. She asks me if I'm eating properly. I eat very properly. Optimised.
textes.Mamie Barricade vient tous les midis à l: Mamie Barricade comes every lunchtime to the same table, and she always leaves three coins under her bowl. Always three. She says it's for “a stranger's soup”. I adore her.
textes.Mamie Barricade, une holo-photo pour un: Mamie Barricade, a holo-photo for a space tourist?
textes.Mamie Kiku dit que je lui dis bonjour qu: Mamie Kiku says I say hello to her forty-two times a day. That's wrong: it's forty-three. She forgets the morning one, she's still half asleep.
textes.Mamie Kiku m'a appelé « mon petit » pend: Mamie Kiku called me “little one” for ten years. Then one day, “big one”. I haven't grown. I don't understand. I was very touched.
Mamie Kiku never takes the lift. She just comes to say hello and give me a cup of tea. I don't drink. I hold it until it cools. It's our ritual.
Mamie Kiku sent you a message! (No. But click anyway.)
textes.Mamie Kiku vient le matin. Elle s'assoit: Mamie Kiku comes in the morning. She sits on the flat stone, by the fountain. She drinks her tea. I rake. We don't talk. Once, she said “pretty”. That was six years ago. I remember it every morning.
textes.Mamie Kiku vient le matin. On ne se dit: Mamie Kiku comes in the morning. We say nothing. She drinks her tea, I rake. Once, she said “pretty”. That was six years ago. I still remember it.
textes.Mamie Rissole est la plus grande dame de: Mamie Rissole is the greatest lady in Montjoie. Her pies would give courage to a slime. If one day I become a true hero, it'll be thanks to her. And her ladle.
textes.Mamie Rissole et moi, nous sommes rivaux: Mamie Rissole and I have been rivals for thirty years. Her pie against my frog. I'll tell you a secret: her pie is better. Just a teeny bit. If you repeat that, I'll serve you raw frog.
textes.Mamie Rissole fait les meilleures tourte: Mamie Rissole makes the best pies in the world. And she never sees me when I hide under the table. Well, I think. She always drops slices right next to me.
textes.Mamie Rissole m'a donné trois parts de t: Mamie Rissole gave me three slices of pie today. I only wanted one. She said “eat”. I ate. Now I can't run anymore. That's a problem for following adventurers.
textes.Mamie Rissole m'a nourri depuis mes quin: Mamie Rissole has fed me since I was fifteen. Without her, I wouldn't be rank S. I'd be rank S anyway, but very skinny. And I'm scared of her ladle.
textes.Mamie Rissole, ce soir, j'ai faim comme: Mamie Rissole, tonight I'm as hungry as a dragon!
textes.Mamie Rissole, pourquoi la tourte, elle: Mamie Rissole, why is the pie round?
textes.Mamie Tournesol danse quand je joue, mai: Granny Sunflower dances when I play, but only when she thinks nobody's watching. So I play with my eyes closed, so she'll dance longer.
textes.Mamie Tournesol et Mère Averse ont fait: Granny Sunflower and Mother Downpour have made peace: the Larsen Festival can come back! Jack, the head roadie, has been repairing the Main Stage for years. He's missing Galet's ropes, Lune's canvas… and someone to tell Mégaphone to finally press his third button.
textes.Mamie Tournesol m'a appris à jouer moins: Granny Sunflower taught me to play softer than my heart. Best music lesson of my life.
textes.Mamie Tournesol m'a appris à planter une: Granny Sunflower taught me how to plant a seed: a hole, the seed, a little earth, and you tell it a secret. I told it my secret. I won't tell you.
textes.Mamie Tournesol raconte les meilleures h: Granny Sunflower tells the best stories in the world. But when I talk to her about Mother Downpour, she looks at her sunflowers and doesn't say anything anymore.
textes.Mamie Tournesol, Mère Averse vous a fait: Granny Sunflower, Mother Downpour made you this umbrella.
textes.Mamie Tournesol, la doyenne du Camp des: Granny Sunflower, the eldest of the Flower Camp, and Mother Downpour, the eldest of Rainville, were the best friends in the world. Fifty years ago, they fell out over the weather (sun or rain for the festival?), and since then nobody has dared to step onto the Main Stage. Granny Sunflower would like to make peace… but she doesn't dare.
textes.Mamie Tournesol, pourquoi regardez-vous: Granny Sunflower, why are you looking at Rainville like that?
textes.Mamie m'a tricoté un bonnet d'infirmière: Mamie knitted me a nurse's cap with studs on it. It's not regulation at all. But at the earplug counter in the evenings, people take me much more seriously. Even Tapage puts his earplugs in when I show him the cap.
textes.Mamie n'a pas un seul implant, et elle v: Mamie doesn't have a single implant, and she sees everything, hears everything, knows everything. Sometimes I wonder if she's the city's real computer.
textes.Mamie trouve toujours ma soupe trop chau: Mamie always finds my soup too hot. Always. Even when I serve it lukewarm on purpose. One day, I served it cold. She said: “It's too hot.” I realised it wasn't about temperature. It was our way of starting a conversation.
textes.Mamie, comment arrêter Lisse pour de bon: Mamie, how do we stop Lisse for good?
textes.Mamie, pourquoi tu es fâchée avec Mère A: Granny, why are you cross with Mother Downpour?
textes.Mamie, que se passe-t-il quand la sirène: Mamie, what happens when the siren wails?
textes.Mamie, tu tiens bon ? — Je tiens bon dep: Mamie, are you holding on? — I've been holding on since 1978, sweetheart!
textes.Mamma Lasagna a encore fait trop de pâte: Mamma Lasagna has made too much pasta again. Like every day. Luckily.
textes.Mamma Lasagna, le Révérend a besoin de v: Mamma Lasagna, the Reverend needs your pasta for the sacred Dish.
textes.Manette : croix ou stick pour viser: Controller: d-pad or stick to aim
textes.Mange d'abord, Odette. Il ne va pas s'en: Eat first, Odette. Your sailboat isn't going to fly away.
textes.Mange d'abord. Les voiliers ne partiront: Eat first. The boats won't sail off.
textes.Mange, mange ! Une soupe, ça ne se paie: Eat, eat! You don't pay for soup: you share it.
textes.Mange-Clous ! Il refte de ta femoule ?: Mange-Clous! Ith there any themolina left?
textes.Mange-Clous ! J'ai épluché tous les oign: Mange-Clous! I've peeled all the onions!
textes.Mange-Clous dit que j'ai un trou dans l': Mange-Clous says I've got a hole in my stomach. I say he's got a hole in his recipe. We're both right. But his stew, I always finish it.
textes.Mange-Clous est un bon cuisinier qui a e: Mange-Clous is a good cook who had a very bad day. Thirty sick sailors in one night. Since then, he brings me soup every lunchtime to make amends. My geranium thanks him.
textes.Mange-Clous fait le meilleur ragoût du m: Mange-Clous makes the best stew in the world, except when he puts in too much chilli. He's teaching me to peel onions. It makes you cry, but they're grown-up onions.
textes.Mange-Clous m'a poursuivi avec sa louche: Mange-Clous chased me with his ladle for three years. Three years! I ate one of his cheeses. Just one. All right, twelve.
Mange-Clous talks too much. He cooks well. He swallowed one of my nails. He's still alive. It was a good nail.
textes.Mange-Clous vient m'aider à la cheminée: Mange-Clous comes to help me at the fireplace every lunchtime. He cooks well, he sings loud, and he puts chilli in everything. Everything! Even in my cinnamon. I like him. Don't tell him.
textes.Mange-Clous, c'est un artifte. Il me fai: Mange-Clous ith an artitht. He maketh me mathed thtew, with tender little bitth, and the betht themolina in the archipelago. Without him, I'd have been hungry for thirty yearth.
textes.Mange-Clous, je viens vous débarrasser d: Mange-Clous, I've come to rid you of the rat.
textes.Mange-Clous. Ta soupe du jour ?: Mange-Clous. Your soup of the day?
textes.Mange-le avant de t'endormir, mon grand: Eat it before you fall asleep, big guy!
textes.Mantra ! Je respire comme une grenouille: Mantra! I'm breathing like a frog!
textes.Mantra médite au bord de la mare. Je lui: Mantra meditates by the pond. I bring him tea. He doesn't always see me, but he always drinks it.
textes.Marcel ! Trois fois l'archipel, tu dis ?: Marcel! Three times round the archipelago, you say?
textes.Marcel ? Un bavard qui jure trop. Trente: Marcel? A chatterbox who swears too much. Thirty years he brought me my letters, and on days with no letters he came anyway. About the lavender, he denies it. He denies it very badly.
textes.Marcel ? Un tricheur, un menteur et un f: Marcel? A cheat, a liar and a postman. Forty years he's been measuring crooked. He's my best friend, but if he asks you, I never said so.
textes.Marcel a porté le courrier pendant trent: Marcel carried the post for thirty years, and he carried my one-centimetre victory. A precise man. Sometimes too precise.
textes.Marcel, c'est le facteur le plus marcheu: Marcel is the walkingest postman in history. He says his round is worth my marathons. We argued, we did the maths: he might be right.
textes.Marcel, mon ancien chef de tournée. Il m: Marcel, my old round boss. He taught me everything, and he still keeps an eye on me from his pétanque pitch. I pretend to be annoyed. I'm touched.
textes.Marchander ? Ah, c'est le jeu où on dit: Haggling? Ah, that's the game where you say numbers until everyone smiles! I love that game. Go on, a little less.
textes.Marchander ? Ha ! Enfin quelqu'un qui co: Haggle? Ha! At last someone who knows the custom. … But no. Not today.
textes.Marchander ? J'ai calculé le prix au cen: Haggle? I worked out the price to the last cent with my calculating machine. It's never wrong. Well, almost never.
textes.Marchander ? Le prix est juste, comme la: Haggle? The price is fair, like Maât's feather. One does not argue with Maât.
textes.Marchander ? Mes prix sont calculés au p: Haggle? My prices are calculated to the gram, like the Levitators' lift. No.
textes.Marchander ? Mes prix sont calculés comm: Haggle? My prices are calculated like the Dome's pressure: to the gram. No.
textes.Marchander ? Mes prix sont déjà plus dou: Haggle? My prices are already softer than a slime in the sun. No.
Haggle? My prices are already gentler than the morning lava. No.
textes.Marchander ? Mes prix sont déjà plus pet: Haggle? My prices are already smaller than a watch bolt. No.
Haggle? My prices are already smaller than a safety pin. No.
textes.Marchander ? Mes prix sont réglés comme: Haggle? My prices are set like one of Gaspard's clocks. No.
textes.Marchander ? Mes prix sont taillés dans: Haggle? My prices are carved in sandstone. They don't budge a finger's width per century. No.
textes.Marchander ? Mon prix a été calculé à la: Haggle? My price was calculated by moonlight. You don't argue with the moon.
textes.Marchander ? Sur un bateau, les prix son: Haggle? On a ship, prices are nailed to the mast.
textes.Marchander ? Va voir Bedaine, au Grand T: Haggle? Go and see Bedaine, at the Great Swap. My prices are round as the moon.
Haggle with a dwarf? Ho ho! No.
textes.Marchander avec un pirate ? T'es courage: Haggle with a pirate? Either you're brave, or you're daft.
textes.Marcher ?! Hop hop… Bon. Chacun son truc: Walk?! Hop hop… Fine. Each to their own. Walking is running with patience. Lots and lots of patience.
textes.Marcher jusqu'au bout de la brume, là où: To walk to the very end of the mist, where it stops, and see what lies beyond. Not to leave. Just so I can make my report: “Report: the world is big.”
textes.Marché conclu ! Tope là, de la patte. Qu: Deal! Shake on it, paw to hand. What shall we swap next?
textes.Marché conclu. {objet}, pour {prix} pièc: Deal. {objet}, for {prix} coins. You won't regret it.
textes.Margaux m'a appris le pain, la patience: Margaux taught me bread, patience and getting up at four. She grumbles when I dance in the bakehouse, but she's the first to start humming.
textes.Margaux me donne ses invendus du soir po: Margaux gives me her evening leftovers for the party, so they don't go to waste, she says. One evening there were twelve croissants in the basket, still piping hot, with a note: “Leftovers.” We never bake a batch in the evening. Margaux can't lie to save her life. I didn't say a thing. I just hugged her really tight.
textes.Margaux n'a personne pour livrer le pain: Margaux has no one to deliver the bread to Chez Paulo, the Square Café and the Grand Hotel.
textes.Margaux vole mes croissants à moi. Non,: Margaux steals my croissants. No, I'm joking, I'm the one who steals hers. No, I'm joking again.
textes.Margaux, c'est la meilleure boulangère d: Margaux is the best baker in Port-Azur. The only one, too, but that changes nothing. Her bread is my soup's best friend. She laughs at my jokes. Almost always.
textes.Margaux, c'est la petite qui a repris ma: Margaux is the girl who took over my bakery. She puts too much honey in her bread. I eat it twice a day, to check. Always too much honey.
textes.Margaux, ma belle ! Tes croissants, ils: Margaux, bella! Your croissants are at my place, I stole them!
textes.Margot ? Elle connaît le nom de chaque v: Margot? She knows every wave by name. She says they look alike, but not quite, like sisters.
textes.Margot a fait les comptes de l'année. El: Margot did the year's accounts. She showed me a column: “Papa, thirty-one per cent of your bubbles, you blow for yourself. Not for the customers.” I asked how she knew. She said: “They're the ones you watch fly away.” I said it was an investment. She wrote “no”.
textes.Margot a refait de tête les calculs de d: Margot redid in her head the distance calculations for a double star. She found a mistake in the Academy's tables. A real one. I took the correction to the director myself, with Margot's notebook open at page twelve, her crossings-out and her drawings of Bidule in the margin. He had to accept it. Margot said: “Logical.”
textes.Margot a refait tous les calculs de ma p: Margot redid all the sums for my first rocket. Three pages. She says it would have taken off with three kilos less smoke. Three kilos! I told her smoke is the best bit. She sighed, like a grown-up. Then she wrote at the bottom of the page: “Smoke: keep.” She's nice, really.
textes.Margot calcule mieux que l'Académie et r: Margot calculates better than the Academy and observes better than I do. I give her ten minutes at the telescope every evening. It's not much. It's all I dare give her.
textes.Margot est trop sérieuse pour son âge. E: Margot is too serious for her age. She looks at me with calculating eyes. I'm sure she knows something. About my engine. Or about me.
textes.Margot parle aux mouettes et presque pas: Margot talks to seagulls and hardly at all to people. Me, I say “hm”. We understand each other very well. Her Lighthouse has brought me back to port more times than I can count.
textes.Margot prétend que Clémentine, c'est la: Margot claims that Clémentine is the light from her Lighthouse. She is very kind, very calm, and completely mistaken. I'm very fond of her.
