textes.Mireille m'a vendu un grille-pain solair: Mireille sold me a solar toaster. My toast is perfect. My table, less so.
textes.Mireille, la machine a prévu de la pluie: Mireille, the machine has forecast rain.
textes.Mireille, à l'Atelier, me prête son étab: Mireille, at the Workshop, lends me her workbench in the evening. I give everything back neatly put away, with a note: “This is not a toy.” She always replies with another note: “Yes it is. A bit.” We correspond a great deal, for two neighbours.
Mireille. This is not a toy.
textes.Miriel cueille les fleurs de mes abeille: Miriel picks my bees' flowers before they've finished foraging them. She says flowers belong to no one. They belong to whoever feeds on them.
textes.Miriel m'a apporté un jour une fleur de: Once, Miriel brought me a moonflower picked at high noon. “It was open, I swear!” A moonflower picked in the sun cures nothing. We argued about the price for an hour. Then we put it in a glass of water and had tea beside it.
textes.Miriel me cueille les fleurs de lune. El: Miriel picks moonflowers for me. She sells them dear, I pay a fair price. We never agree on the difference. She's a good mother, and a tough trader.
textes.Miriel sait où pousse chaque fleur de l': Miriel knows where every flower on the island grows. I know where every path goes. Between the two of us, we never get lost. Well, I do. But she always finds me.
Miriel, I'm going for a little stroll.
textes.Miriel. Tu as cueilli le pré de lavande: Miriel. Did you pick the lavender meadow?
Update! The sky has changed its mind.
textes.Miser %d pièces… avec tes dés pipés: Bet %d coins… with your loaded dice
textes.Mistral ! Ma barque te salue. Elle a enc: Mistral! My boat says hello. Her back still aches.
textes.Mistral ? Le seul client de l'île qui pa: Mistral? The only customer on the island who pays cash without haggling. Shame he makes so much noise with what he buys from me.
textes.Mistral ? Le seul homme de l'île qui fas: Mistral? The only man on the island who makes more noise than I do. I admire him, and I sleep with cotton wool in my ears.
textes.Mistral a promis une teuf sous l'eau, à: Mistral promised an underwater party, in Atlantis. I don't know how he's going to manage the speakers.
textes.Mistral est merveilleux, mais il parle d: Mistral is wonderful, but he talks about Atlantis like it's the next beach over. “Going this week?” He doesn't know what's down there. I know a little.
textes.Mistral fait trembler la baie toutes les: Mistral makes the bay shake every night. I ought to complain. But his beats sound like those of the Mother Tree, when you press your ear to the bark.
textes.Mistral joue pour nous, pour la mer et p: Mistral plays for us, for the sea and for the fairies, even if he didn't know it at first. He's been waiting for my mural for two years without ever rushing me. He's the most patient of winds.
textes.Mistral mixait sur la pointe des pieds,: Mistral used to mix on tiptoe — his decks were too high for him. My calves hurt just watching him. I took a rope, measured his arms while he played, and the next day he had a stage. It creaks a bit on the offbeat. I tell him it's on purpose. It almost is.
textes.Mistral, c'est la raison pour laquelle j: Mistral is the reason I'm still here. One single track, at sunrise, and I missed my boat. I'll never forgive him. I adore him.
textes.Mistral, c'est le cœur de la teuf. Il ou: Mistral is the heart of the party. He forgets to drink, he forgets to sleep, he even forgot his decks were too high. Me, I don't forget. That's why I'm here.
textes.Mistral, comme le vent. J'ai monté ce mu: Mistral, like the wind. I built this sound wall piece by piece, with Barnabé lending me his rowing boat to carry it all.
textes.Mistral, le vent tourne vers les nuages,: Mistral, the wind's turning towards the clouds tonight.
textes.Mistral, ton chant de baleine… c'est pre: Mistral, your whale song… it's almost right.
textes.Mistral. … Le meilleur. Il compose, je r: Mistral. … The best. He composes, I tune. He talks, I nod. It's worked like that for six years. It'll keep working.
textes.Mistral… Ce soir, tu pourrais jouer un p: Mistral… Tonight, could you play a little less loudly?
textes.Misère. Elle a appris ça où, cette petit: Good grief. Where did she learn that, this girl?
textes.Misère… Elle était bonne, au moins ?: Oh, misery… Was it good, at least?
textes.Mixtli ! Encore en train d'attendre le b: Mixtli! Still waiting for the right day?
textes.Mixtli ! Je peux porter ton bouclier ?: Mixtli! Can I carry your shield?
textes.Mixtli dit que je lui ai vendu une fauss: Mixtli says I sold him a fake quetzal feather. It was a test. I had to check he could recognise a real one.
textes.Mixtli est brave, fort et rapide. Il est: Mixtli is brave, strong and fast. He's also as proud as a turkey on a feast day. I told him about Tecciztécatl, the proud god. He found the story very beautiful. He didn't understand it.
textes.Mixtli est guerrier-jaguar : fort, fier,: Mixtli is a jaguar warrior: strong, proud, and very serious. Even when he dances. Especially when he dances. He has two left feet. I adore him. The way you adore a show, of course.
textes.Mixtli est mon cousin. Il est fort, fier: Mixtli is my cousin. He's strong, proud, and he can't haggle. He captured me in training, in front of everyone. I sold him a fake feather. We're even. Almost.
textes.Mixtli m'a promis de chasser les jaguars: Mixtli promised me he'd hunt the jaguars that took one of my animals. That's kind. He's as proud as a turkey and he falls into the canals. But he has a good heart. He hides it under his jaguar skin.
textes.Mixtli m'a prêté son bouclier. Il était: Mixtli lent me his shield. It was so big I couldn't see anything! I shouted: “I'm invincible!” and stepped forward. I fell into a basket of chillies, at the market. The chillies stung my eyes. Mixtli said a warrior cries too, sometimes. Especially because of chillies.
textes.Mixtli porte une peau de jaguar et veut: Mixtli wears a jaguar skin and wants to hunt the real ones, on the Smoking Mountain. You don't hunt the jaguar to make a name for yourself. I told him. He didn't listen.
textes.Mixtli, c'est le guerrier-jaguar ! Il a: Mixtli is the jaguar warrior! He has a real jaguar skin, a shield and a weapon made of black stone. Tlaco barks at him. Me, I want to be like him. With a dog as well.
textes.Mixtli, notre guerrier-jaguar, dit qu'il: Mixtli, our jaguar warrior, says he has seen real jaguars on the slopes of the Smoking Mountain. He wants to go and face them. A jaguar warrior against jaguars… The gods do love a joke.
textes.Mixtli. Guerrier-jaguar d'Aztlán. Je por: Mixtli. Jaguar warrior of Aztlán. I wear the jaguar's skin because I fight like it: fast, and in the shadows. You look like you can fight. We'll see.
textes.Mixtli. L'orgueil est un mauvais bouclie: Mixtli. Pride is a poor shield.
textes.Mixtli. Les jaguars sont chez eux, là-ha: Mixtli. The jaguars are at home, up there.
textes.Mmh ? Pardon, je bronzais. Sylvie, la fe: Mmh? Sorry, I was sunbathing. Sylvie, Gérard's wife. Are you local?
textes.Mmh… encore un peu de farine… zzz…: Mmh… just a bit more flour… zzz…
textes.Mmh… pas maintenant… je suis occupé… à d: Mmh… not now… I'm busy… sleeping…
textes.Mmh… pas sur mon nez, Capitaine… zzz…: Mmm… not on my nose, Captain… zzz…
Mmm… It smells of cinnamon and steam.
textes.Mmmh… une tarte… grande comme la maison…: Mmmh… a pie… as big as the house…
textes.Mmm… On dirait de boire un petit nuage t: Mmm… Like drinking a little warm cloud. Your white moustache is back.
textes.Moaïs : la doyenne et la légende: Moai: the elder and the legend
textes.Moaïs : le petit qui n'a jamais vu la me: Moai: the little one who has never seen the sea
textes.Mochi ! Tu as de la farine jusqu'aux ore: Mochi! You've got flour up to your ears.
textes.Mochi dit que c'est un dragon-poisson, s: Mochi says it's a dragon-fish under the pool. Gland says it's a dragon. I say it's the King of the Pools, and he's got a crown.
textes.Mochi m'a demandé si son papa était dans: Mochi asked me if her papa was among the stars. I said I hadn't finished counting. That same evening, she wanted to name star four thousand two hundred and thirteen. She called it “Cerfeuil”. I wrote it down like that in my journal, in ink, not pencil. Since then, when I reach thirteen, I say good evening.
textes.Mochi monte l'escalier avec moi au crépu: Mochi climbs the stairs with me at dusk, very slowly, asking a thousand questions. A thousand and twenty-three, yesterday. She always has cake somewhere on her.
textes.Mochi, c'est ma copine, même si nos mama: Mochi's my friend, even though our mums are cross with each other over some sardine-and-carrot business. She talks nonsense about the dragon-fish. But she gives me her sardines.
textes.Mochi, c'est une pipelette. Elle parle p: Mochi's a chatterbox. She talks almost as much as me, it's very annoying. She says “dragon-fish”. She tells on me. But she helps me look for my hazelnuts. And she eats them.

textes.Moi ? Charpentier et forgeron de la Moue: Me? Carpenter and blacksmith of the Stubborn Seagull, the finest three-master in the kingdom. Until the rock.
textes.Moi ? Comme un coquillage à marée haute: Me? Like a shell at high tide: full of water and delighted about it!
textes.Moi ? Euh… Un verre pour un collègue, al: Me? Er… A drink for a colleague, then?
textes.Moi ? J'ai trois cent douze ans. C'est j: Me? I'm three hundred and twelve years old. That's young, where I come from. My mother says I'm “still very green”.
textes.Moi ? Jamais de la vie. Qu'est-ce que tu: Me? Never in my life. What did you find?
textes.Moi ? Jamais. Je réfléchissais très fort: Me? Never. I was thinking very hard.
Me? Never. Back to your carpets.
Me? I haven't the faintest idea.
textes.Moi ? Je ne t'ai rien demandé… Mais Gran: Me? I didn't ask you for anything… But Grand-Mère Aquarelle, by the Palette, surely needs help.
textes.Moi ? Je ne t'ai rien demandé… Mais la p: Me? I didn't ask you for anything… But little Mio, at the Night Market or in the Alleys, looks like she needs help.
textes.Moi ? Je ne t'ai rien demandé… Mais le R: Me? I didn't ask you for anything… But Reverend Father Farfalle, at the Colander Temple, has been looking very worried these days.
textes.Moi ? Je ne t'ai rien demandé… Mais si t: Me? I didn't ask you for anything… But if you want to help, go and see Granny Sunflower. Or Mother Downpour. Well, one or the other: they're not speaking to each other any more.
textes.Moi ? Je ne tapote pas. (Tap-tap-tap, bo: Me? I don't tap. (Tap-tap-tap, boom-tchak.) ... Well. All right. I tap. I always have. On everything. You know, every evening, I listen to the Bilge Rats from behind the Hall's door. I know all the songs. All the drum parts. And every night, the stand-in drummer gets it wrong, and in my head, I play it right. But I don't have any sticks. Dad would never have allowed it. And besides... I'm a Lisse. They'll never want a Lisse on their stage. (He looks at your hands.) You... you have drumsticks, don't you? The ones from the Great Boucan?
textes.Moi ? Je ne vois rien d'ici. À peine tou: Me? I can't see a thing from up here. Barely the whole square.
textes.Moi ? Je suis une tombe. Une tombe bavar: Me? I'm a tomb. A chatty tomb.
textes.Moi ? Je suis {titre}. Un métier honnête: Me? I'm the local {titre}. An honest trade. Like all dwarf trades.
textes.Moi ? Je suis {titre}. Un métier tranqui: Me? I'm the local {titre}. A peaceful job, under the sea. Everything is peaceful, under the sea.
textes.Moi ? Je vérifiais qu'il était bien… vid: Me? I was checking it was properly… empty.
textes.Moi ? Non ! J'ai juste une grande admira: Me? No! I just have a great admiration for the ground. Especially when it's under me, and not two hundred metres further down.
textes.Moi ? Oh… Je… pardon, je ne sais pas quo: Me? Oh… I… sorry, I don't know what to say. Nobody's ever told me that. I'm going to go all red. Well, redder than usual.
textes.Moi ? Rien de bien extraordinaire. Je vi: Me? Nothing very extraordinary. I've lived here forever. Well, for three centuries.
textes.Moi ? Trop sucré ? Je n'ai jamais dit ça: Me? Too sweet? I never said that! Never!
textes.Moi ? À mon âge, on s'endort quand on pe: Me? At my age, you sleep when you can, little leaf.
Me? Not a soul! Except Halima.
textes.Moi ? … Tu es malin, {surnom}. Trop mali: Me? … You're clever, {surnom}. Too clever for a human. I didn't hear the question. Look at this thread, it's fascinating.
textes.Moi Pika ! Toi viens d'où ? Pays des Lis: Me Pika! Where you from? Land of Smooth Ones? There, children smooth too? They roll to go faster? Hee hee hee!
textes.Moi aussi ! Bon, ça fait trois semaines,: Me too! Okay, it's only been three weeks, but I can feel it. Come on, there's room in Gaspard's hut. Well, ask the crabs.
textes.Moi aussi ! Enfin, avant. C'est pour ça: Me too! Well, I used to be. That's why I make light. Here, if you get scared one night, look at the chimney: I put a lamp right at the top. It's for you.
textes.Moi aussi ! Mais de loin !: I saw you too! But from a distance!
textes.Moi aussi ! Mais il faut se dépêcher, la: Me too! But you have to hurry, the sea eats them. It's a very greedy sea.
textes.Moi aussi ! À l'abordage ! On va attaque: Me too! All hands, board her! We're going to attack… the Great Table! For dessert!
I'm scared of demons too, you know.
textes.Moi aussi, au début. Danse quand personn: Me too, at first. Dance when nobody's watching. Later, you'll dance when everybody's watching.
textes.Moi aussi, j'essaie. Mais mes larmes bri: I try to as well. But my tears shine, so everyone sees them. At least yours are discreet tears. That's lucky.
I used to say that too.
textes.Moi aussi, je suis lent. On va bien s'en: I'm slow too. We'll get along just fine.
textes.Moi aussi, longtemps. Ici, c'est facile: Me too, for a long time. Here it's easy: at night, nobody watches anybody, everybody watches the sea. Come and dance at the back, near Tchoum. He keeps his eyes closed.
textes.Moi aussi, parfois. Les plus belles dans: Me too, sometimes. The most beautiful dances are the ones nobody sees. But I'll keep the secret.
So was I. With a yellow scarf.
So do I. That's the trouble.
textes.Moi aussi. C'est bien le problème. Quand: Me too. That's exactly the problem. When the ring slipped off, I thought it was one, and a bad one. I'm trying to believe it wasn't. You see, believing is tiring.
textes.Moi aussi. Elles sont imprévisibles. Les: Me too. They're unpredictable. Drones follow their program. Seagulls follow the sardines.
textes.Moi aussi. La deuxième fois, on voit ce: Me too. The second time, you see what you hadn't seen. The third time, you see what you wanted to see. … Sorry. That was a bit long.
textes.Moi aussi. Mais il faut un frère pour le: Me too. But you need a brother to do it in your place, and mine's already taken. Look at him: he's doing figures of eight. It's pretty, when you're not afraid.
textes.Moi aussi. Ne regarde pas en bas. Regard: Me too. Don't look down. Look far away. Gravier taught me that. Three words. It works.
textes.Moi aussi. Un peu, beaucoup. Ce n'est pa: Me too. A little, a lot. Fear's no big deal. You just have to breathe slower than it does. It gets tired before you do.
textes.Moi aussi. À mon âge, on a assez attendu: Me too. At my age, you've waited long enough for endings to want them to be lovely. I'm saving one for you, with a wedding and a pie.
Me too. That makes two of us.
And I sing. We make a pair.
textes.Moi je sais qui vole les croissants. C'e: I know who steals the croissants. It's a little white dog! He hides them by the crates, at the end of the quay. But I like him, so shh.
textes.Moi non plus ! Nous sommes deux ! Alors: Nor have I! There are two of us! Then let us do it together! I, SIRE TANCRÈDE DE TOURNEVENT, swear to accompany you to our first true great deed!
textes.Moi non plus. C'est pour ça que je peins: Me neither. That's why I paint. We'll search together, all right?
Three times, me. Don't tell anyone.
textes.Moi, Majesté ? J'archivais… les étoiles: Me, Majesty? I was archiving… starfish.
textes.Moi, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, je t'a: I, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, shall go with you! Adventure awaits us, and so does dinner!
textes.Moi, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, je te: I, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, challenge you! Chaaarge!
textes.Moi, Sire Tancrède de Tournevent, je vou: I, Sir Tancrède de Tournevent, follow you! No, I lead you! No, I walk beside you! Onward!
textes.Moi, c'est Pilli ! Ça veut dire « enfant: I'm Pilli! It means “child”, or “little prince”. I prefer prince. My dad, Ollin, went away to Mictlan when I was three. I remember him a bit: he laughed, and he smelled of the lake. That same week, Tlaco arrived, all tiny, all warm. Mum says it was Dad who sent him to us.
textes.Moi, j'ai appris à dormir sans ronfler !: I learned to sleep without snoring!
I was scared of the sea.
Me, I forget everything. Very handy.
textes.Moi, je n'ai que des papillons. … Des pa: Me, I only have butterflies. … Stone butterflies. They don't fly very well.
textes.Moi, je t'ai porté avec un sac de charbo: I carried you with a sack of coal on top.
I want to be the captain.
textes.Moi, plus tard, je serai archère ! Ou he: When I grow up, I'll be an archer! Or an herbalist. Or an explorer! Like you!
I do. And you're smiling. A little.
I've got just one. A whale.
textes.Moins d'une minute ! Tu as des ailes aux: Under a minute! You've got wings on your feet. Here, I'll teach you my secret: breathe well, and never look back.
Not so loud! My father's coming this way.
textes.Moins fort ? Peuchère, les nains vont en: Less loud? Peuchère, the dwarves will complain again!
Less than the last one. Again.
textes.Moins vite, petit. Mes genoux ont soixan: Slower, lad. My knees are seventy-five years old.
textes.Moloka ! Merci pour les restes, les chio: Moloka! Thanks for the scraps, the pups adore you!
textes.Moloka a lancé une sardine à la tête de: Moloka threw a sardine at Grumbald's head twenty-five years ago, because he'd said her fish wasn't fresh. They got married the following year. The sardine was at the wedding.
textes.Moloka m'a appris à vider un poisson. Je: Moloka taught me to gut a fish. I can't do it: I scream when I see the bones. I taught her to announce a fight. She shouted: “IN THE LEFT CORNER… A SEA BREAM!” The stands loved it. Ever since, when I have a cold, she fills in for me. She announces the fighters like fish.
textes.Moloka me donne ses restes de poisson ch: Moloka gives me her fish scraps every morning for my pups. She shouts loud, she laughs loud, and she forgave Grignotte for stealing a whole grouper. She says she doesn't like dogs. She's a terrible liar.
textes.Moloka ne sait pas nager. Personne ne le: Moloka can't swim. Nobody knows, except me, and I never mention it to her. For her birthday, I gave her a lifebuoy painted to look like a sardine, saying it was to decorate the fish shop. She hung it on the wall. On stormy days, I see her take it down and put it in her boat.
textes.Moloka pêche à l'aube et crie toute la j: Moloka fishes at dawn and shouts all day long. She's the best fishmonger in the port, and the loudest. The gargoyles steal her fish. She shouts at them. They come back anyway.
textes.Moloka, c'est ma femme. La meilleure poi: Moloka's my wife. The best fishmonger in the Harbour, the loudest voice after Hurla, and the biggest heart in the port. She threw a sardine at me, once. The best day of my life.
textes.Moloka, c'est ma meilleure amie. La seul: Moloka is my best friend. The only person in the city who shouts almost as loud as me. We talk from one end of the port to the other without moving from our spots. It saves time.
textes.Momo ! Ce soir, je fais deux pirouettes: Momo! Tonight I'm doing two pirouettes!
textes.Momo ? Un garçon adorable qui perce des: Momo? A lovely boy who drills holes in shells. HOLES, {surnom}. I'm fond of him, but I recount my collection after every one of his visits.
Momo says he danced with a dolphin. Well, he danced in the water, and a dolphin swam by. That's pretty much the same.
textes.Momo est gentil comme tout, mais tout ce: Momo's as sweet as can be, but anything left lying around ends up on him: my cap, my bucket, my boat. He doesn't steal, he says. He borrows forever.
textes.Momo et moi, on fait un concours de saut: Momo and I have a jumping contest every night, in front of the wall of sound. We mark the height on a palm tree, with a shell. The palm tree is covered in them. One night, Momo jumped so high he grabbed a coconut. It fell back on his head. He said: “Legend.” I said it didn't count. But it was a legend.
Momo swears he danced with a dolphin. So I did the dolphin in my show: I jump, I go “kik-kik”, I land in a bucket of water. Momo came to watch, ready to grumble. He laughed so hard he gave every kid a necklace. Fifteen necklaces. It's my best fee ever, and he's the one who paid it.
textes.Momo m'a fait un collier avec un coquill: Momo made me a necklace with a heart-shaped shell. He gave it to me without a word, which is very rare for Momo. I said “Oh, a crab!” as a joke. He said: “Yes, that's it, a crab.” He went bright red under his bandana. I wear it every day. It's a very pretty crab.
textes.Momo saute plus haut que moi. D'un doigt: Momo jumps higher than me. By a finger. He tells everyone. But I do a pirouette in the air, and a pirouette counts double.
textes.Momo saute plus haut que tout le monde,: Momo jumps higher than everyone, smiles bigger than everyone, and says he danced with a dolphin. It's almost true. I was there.
textes.Momo transforme mes coquillages en colli: Momo turns my shells into necklaces and my days into bursts of laughter. He jumps too high, he talks too loud, and he asks me only one question a day. For Momo, that's very polite.
textes.Momo, c'est mon associé au marché et mon: Momo is my partner at the market and my cousin at heart. He counts the coins, I count the smiles. At the end of the day, I've always earned more than him.
textes.Momo, mon frère ! On a vendu combien, au: Momo, my brother! How much did we sell today?
textes.Momo, tiens, pour tes colliers. Il vient: Momo, here, for your necklaces. It came from very far away.
textes.Momo, tu n'aurais pas vu mon seau ?: Momo, you haven't seen my bucket, have you?
textes.Mon Archiduchesse est la personne que je: My Archduchess is the person I must protect, and the one who slips away most often. She has a heart as big as the volcano. And legs as fast as one of Zigomar's rockets.
textes.Mon Archiduchesse s'échappe du palais pa: My Archduchess slips out of the palace through the garden to go to the market. She thinks I don't know. I follow her from a distance. She thinks I don't follow her. Everyone's happy.
textes.Mon Archiduchesse, où allez-vous ?: My Archduchess, where are you going?
textes.Mon Bureau de vente est au sud-ouest de: My Sales Office is south-west of the square, between the Spinning Mill and the Expression Wall. A grey bungalow, spotless, air-conditioned. The only clean building on the island. Well, it was until last night. There's a rat playing guitar on the door now.
textes.Mon Kevin ! Maître-nageur, le plus beau: My Kevin! A lifeguard, the handsomest on the beach, and the strongest. He saves everyone, except his mother at six in the morning when the ice needs carrying. Five hundred push-ups, but not one crate.
textes.Mon Pépin ! Mon petit Pépin ! Il n'est p: My Pépin! My little Pépin! He hasn't come home from the Academy, and Ortie says he wanted to see the glowing mushrooms in the Ash Wood… The wood, at night, is full of wild imps! Would you go and find him? He has a little lantern, and horns as big as hazelnuts.
My RUG. My rug is coming along.
textes.Mon abri est au bout du chemin des Verge: My shed is at the end of the Orchards path. If you have a good nose, come and help sort the apples: the ones for the market, the ones for stewed apples, and the ones we munch on the sly.
textes.Mon acier ne fond pas. Il se laisse fair: My steel doesn't melt. It just goes along with it, out of politeness.
textes.Mon adjoint d'honneur ! Vous vous souven: My honorary deputy! Remember? The bow. Show me today's. Hmm. Almost.
textes.Mon admirateur ! SARDIIINES ! Celle-là a: My fan! SARDIIINES! That one was for you too.
textes.Mon agence est dans la Haute-Ville, au-d: My agency is in the Upper Town, above the Great Square. If I'm not there, I'm in the Cottage garden. Watering the wisteria. It doesn't need it. But it's a selling point.
textes.Mon amateur de fraise ! Tu as goûté le f: My strawberry fan! Have you tried Nina's strawberry-dolphin? She's going to ask you, get your answer ready.
textes.Mon amateur de musique ! Passe ce soir a: My music lover! Come by the Perroquet tonight, I've saved you a D chord. The best one.
textes.Mon amateur de poisson ! Vendredi, ta pa: My fish lover! On Friday, your portion is waiting. You haven't forgotten it, I hope?
textes.Mon ami ! Ignace Malaterre, capitaine de: My friend! Ignace Malaterre, captain of the Morue Enragée, the most elegant sloop in the archipelago. They call me Bouche-d'Or — Golden Mouth. (He smiles. All his teeth are gold.) Do you play dice? No? Pity. You will.
textes.Mon ami ! Mon frère ! Entre, assieds-toi: My friend! My brother! Come in, sit down, have some tea, look, it costs nothing to look! Rachid, carpets from all over the island. That one? For you, special price. Friend's price. Brother's price.
textes.Mon ami ! Regardez-le tourner, mon phare: My friend! Look at it turning, my lighthouse. Thanks to you.
textes.Mon ami de l'ocre ! J'ai encore les doig: My ochre friend! My fingers are still red from the wadi earth. You see, I think of you while I paint.
textes.Mon ami du piment ! Ta bouillabaisse, je: My chilli friend! I made your bouillabaisse volcano-style. Cry away.
textes.Mon ami du safran ! Ne le dis pas à Lall: My saffron friend! Don't tell Lalla Aïcha: she'd ask whether you plan to eat it.
textes.Mon ami du « presque » ! Je te dirai qua: My “almost” buddy! I'll tell you when the dolphin swings by again. And this time, it'll be “absolutely”.
textes.Mon ami, une question d'honneur : tu cro: My friend, a question of honour: do you believe in luck, or in talent?
textes.Mon ancêtre, Alan Le Goff, était le pilo: My ancestor, Alan Le Goff, was the Léviathan's pilot. He was the one who plotted the course, that night. Right onto the rocks. Ever since, the Le Goffs draw maps to make up for it. My father drew the bay, my grandfather the stars. Me, as a boy, I drew the ship's frames in chalk on the floor of the harbour master's office.
textes.Mon appareil ! Et… vous avez pris une ph: My camera! And… did you take a photo with it? Oh no. Just as well. Here, for the climb.
textes.Mon appareil photo ! Je l'ai posé au bel: My camera! I left it at the lookout, at the top of the hill, to photograph the sunset, and I came back down without it. My legs won't climb back up. Would you mind?
textes.Mon apprenti grenouilleur ! Grommelot te: My apprentice frog-maker! Grommelot says hello. Well, he grunts in your direction.
textes.Mon apprenti, Tom, tape un code sur la r: My apprentice, Tom, taps a code on the rock to talk to Mathilde's daughter. Three quick knocks means “bolt found.” One long scrape means “good night.” He thinks I don't understand. I invented half those signals at his age.
My apprenticeship lasted two hundred years. One day, to prove to Grandmother that the blue berries were harmless, I ate a handful. I spent two days chatting with fireflies. They had a lot of opinions. Grandmother wrote it all down in her journal, under “Aëlwen, case number one”.
textes.Mon arc est taillé dans une branche tomb: My bow is carved from a branch that fell from the Mother Tree. We never cut the Tree. Never.
textes.Mon arme, c'est la macuahuitl : un bâton: My weapon is the macuahuitl: a wooden club lined with obsidian shards. Sharper than an iron knife. But if you hit a stone, the obsidian breaks. So you don't hit stones.
textes.Mon armure, c'est Ferronde qui l'a forgé: My armour was forged by Ferronde. My wife. She sewed felt pads on the knees for night rounds. Before, you could hear me coming from the harbour. Now, only from the market.
textes.Mon arrière-arrière-grand-mère a tiré la: My great-great-grandmother pulled the salad basket's rope with Lady Ysolde Hautefond. Ever since, there's always been a Rouage at the ticket office. The Column is in our blood. And a little oil under our nails.
textes.Mon arrière-arrière-grand-père était à b: My great-great-grandfather was aboard on the night of the wreck. He told the story to his son, who told it to his… all the way down to me. I'm the last page of the book.
textes.Mon arrière-arrière-grand-père, c'est Sé: My great-great-grandfather is Séraphin! The one who raised the island. Grandpa Séverin says he did it “so the children would always have sunshine”. I'd have liked him to build a little staircase down to the sea as well.
textes.Mon arrière-grand-mère était la dernière: My great-grandmother was the last lantern-lighter of the Galleries. Morning and evening, she lit every lantern, door after door. When the Brass Sun was switched on, they told her she had no job any more. She opened a canteen. She said: “We don't light doors any more. So we'll light bellies.” That was La Marmite.
textes.Mon arrière-grand-père a sauvé un roi. M: My great-grandfather saved a king. My grandfather saved a princess. My father saved a cat stuck up a tree, and he was very proud of it. When I left, he told me: “Save someone, son. Anyone.” I came to Montjoie, because here, there's always someone inside a frog.
textes.Mon arrière-grand-père fabriquait le pap: My great-grandfather made the village's blotting paper. He used to say a good blotter drinks the ink without drinking the words. I inherited his name, and an ink stain from birth, on my little finger. It's still there.
textes.Mon arrière-grand-père, Séraphin Altaïr,: My great-grandfather, Séraphin Altaïr, raised this island. My family kept two things from him: his name, and the habit of looking at the sky before making a decision. The name is easier to carry.
textes.Mon arrière-petite-fille Lili veut voir: My great-granddaughter Lili wants to see the sea. Her mother says “soon”. I gave her an old shell my father brought me back from down below. She holds it to her ear every evening. She says she can hear the sea. I can't hear it well. But I believe her.
My watering can used to be my mother's. It leaks a little, on the side. I never wanted to fix it: the flowers along the path get watered at the same time. My mother used to say it was a generous watering can. It waters those who never asked for anything.
textes.Mon associé du « ça dépend » ! Alors, au: My “it depends” partner! So, what does it depend on today? Apples, I hope.
textes.Mon atelier a eu quatorze toits. Le quin: My workshop has had fourteen roofs. The fifteenth is on order. I need iron to rebuild it, and the northern shepherds sell their ore far too dear.
textes.Mon atelier est chez les Artisans, à l'o: My workshop is in the Artisans' Quarter, west of the Lower Town, between Tiburce, who smells of perfume, and Zigomar, who smells of gunpowder. My fabrics smell of both. Customers think it's on purpose.
My workshop is in the Artisans' Quarter, west of the Lower Town. You'll find it easily: it's the one with no roof. Well, it has one. It's just a bit further away than planned.
textes.Mon atelier est derrière la boutique. En: My workshop is behind the shop. Come in, if you like ticking: a hundred clocks, a magnifying glass, and a cuckoo with an impossible temper. Look with your eyes, not your hands. Except the great clock: that one you may wind.
textes.Mon atelier est à la Filature, l'ancienn: My workshop is in the Spinning Mill, the old thread factory, between Agrafe's print shop and Copeau's carpentry shop. The old spinning machines are still there. I made them covers. They were cold.
textes.Mon automate réfléchit grâce à quatre ce: My automaton thinks with four hundred gears and a punch-card system. Some say there's a dwarf hidden inside. Not true. There isn't room.
My opinion on the piano? It's perfect. But tell the jury it plays better in the morning. It has a bit of a cold in the evening.
textes.Mon avis sur mon automate ? Il est imbat: My opinion of my automaton? It's unbeatable. Write that down. Write it down carefully.
textes.Mon aïeul, Hervé Le Floc'h, était maître: My ancestor, Hervé Le Floc'h, was master gunner on the Léviathan. Forty cannons, and he called every one of them by a first name. Me, I grew up on the lower deck, playing hide-and-seek in their cold mouths. My mother would shout: “Jos, get out of that cannon!” It's the sentence I heard most in my whole childhood.
textes.Mon aïeule commandait le Léviathan quand: My ancestor commanded the Léviathan when it ran aground. Two hundred years later, it's still a Kerhervé at the helm. A helm that doesn't turn any more, but still.
textes.Mon balai est en spaghettis secs. C'est: My broom is made of dry spaghetti. I made it myself. It sweeps very badly. But it smells nice and wheaty, and when it's too worn out, we cook it.
textes.Mon balai, je l'ai fait moi-même, avec d: I made my broom myself, out of dry spaghetti. It doesn't sweep very well. It breaks a bit. Then you have to sweep up the bits of broom. That keeps me busy all morning, and the Reverend says I'm very diligent.
textes.Mon balcon a trois panneaux solaires, de: My balcony has three solar panels, two strawberry plants and a sparrow who pays his rent in songs.
My balcony looks out over the Mist Park. In the morning, the mist comes up to say hello.
textes.Mon bandana a un patch. Velours me l'a c: My bandana has a patch. Velours sewed it on. I'm punk. Woof. Punk.
textes.Mon bandana rouge, c'est Tornade qui me: My red bandana? Tornade gave it to me. He says it's so people can find me in a crowd. I never get lost. I follow you.
textes.Mon billet est bleu ciel. Assorti à mon: My ticket is sky blue. To match my hat. Elegance is important, at altitude.
textes.Mon bleu ! Je vous ai mis dans ma derniè: My blue! I put you in my latest canvas. There, under the jetty. You can't see yourself? I can.
textes.Mon blé, il est beau, hein ? Je l'ai reg: My wheat's a beauty, eh? I watched it grow every single day.
textes.Mon bouclier est en peau de jaguar, gran: My shield is made of jaguar skin, high priest.
textes.Mon boulon le plus précieux, je l'ai tro: My most precious bolt, I found at the bottom of the fountain, under Lady Ysolde's statue. It's all green. I think she dropped it, two hundred years ago, while she was building the first cabin. Every evening, I say good night to it. And to Lady Ysolde too.
textes.Mon boulon préféré, je ne le montre à pe: My favourite bolt, I don't show anyone. It came from Lady Ysolde. Well, I think so. I found it at the bottom of the fountain, under her statue. It's all green and all old. I say good night to it.
textes.Mon bras me gratte. Enfin, l'endroit où: My arm itches. Well, the place where there's no arm any more. Weird, huh? The doctors say it's normal.
textes.Mon but : une bulle assez grande pour y: My goal: a bubble big enough to fit someone inside. I'm nearly there. Professor Boum wants to try it. I'm not sure that's a good idea.
textes.Mon cache-œil ? Je n'ai rien à l'œil. Ma: My eyepatch? There's nothing wrong with my eye. But a pirate without an eyepatch just isn't serious. I switch eyes on Tuesdays. So both get a rest.
textes.Mon canon vise très bien. Il vise la fou: My cannon aims very well. It aims at the crowd.
textes.Mon capitaine grogne, boite et perd aux: My captain grumbles, limps and loses at dice. He has the softest heart on Balafre, hidden under three layers of bad temper. I call him Jambe-de-Bois to his face. He lets me. I think.
textes.Mon casque, c'est Papa qui me l'a peint,: My helmet? Dad painted it for me, and Pigment added a flame. Mum said “a reasonable flame”. Pigment said she didn't know how to do that. So the flame is huge. So cool.
textes.Mon catalogue de Port-Azur fait trois ca: My Port-Azur catalogue fills three notebooks. Half of it is Pauline's stories: the button of the elegant pirate, the spoon of the cross-eyed queen, the tooth of the dragon who swallowed a lighthouse. I write them down word for word. The day she opens her guesthouse, I'll give her the notebooks. She'll have plenty to tell.
My kite is shaped like a whale. Like the one at the Azure Dome. Only smaller. And higher up.
textes.Mon cerf-volant touche presque les nuage: My kite's almost touching the clouds! … It's in a cloud. It's coming back soaking wet.
textes.Mon cerf-volant, je l'ai acheté chez le: I bought my kite from the souvenir man, Victor. Half price! It had all the colours, red, yellow, blue, green, and a big tail with knots. It flew really well. And then the wind went “whoooosh”, the string went “snap”, and it went off towards the hill, over the houses. I watched it till it was teeny tiny.
textes.Mon cerf-volant… Le vent l'a emporté ver: My kite… The wind carried it off towards the hill, over there, above the houses. It's stuck somewhere, I'm sure of it. Can you find it? Please?
textes.Mon cerf-volant… il s'est envolé… Il éta: My kite… it flew away… It was red, yellow, blue and green, and it had a tail with bows on…
textes.Mon chapeau de mage, je l'ai acheté chez: My mage's hat, I bought it from Madame Olga when I arrived. She told me it was “surely magic”. I asked what it did. She thought for a long time, then said: “It protects your head.” Since then, it's been struck by lightning eleven times. It has never burnt. Nor has my head. It really is magic. She was right.
textes.Mon chapeau de paille s'était troué au s: My straw hat had got a hole from the sun, just above the ear. I left it on the table one evening. In the morning, the hole was mended. With net thread, little tight knots, like for sardines. Now my hat stands up on its own. The gulls don't dare land on it any more.
textes.Mon chapeau s'est envolé au Belvédère. I: My hat blew away at the Belvedere. It must be in the City of Clouds by now. Lucky thing.
textes.Mon chapeau à plume ! Vous l'avez retrou: My feathered hat! You found it! On the windmill, really? That hat travels more than I do. Thank you, thank you!
textes.Mon chapeau à plume s'envole souvent. Il: My feathered hat often flies off. It's been on the Guild roof, on the temple bell tower, and once on the head of a frog from the lake. She kept it a week. She looked very distinguished.
textes.Mon chapeau à plume s'est envolé ! Le pl: My feathered hat blew away! The finest one! The wind carried it over the wall. I saw it sail over the rooftops of the Middle Town, then nothing. Without it, I feel all… windswept.
textes.Mon chapeau à plume s'est envolé au-dess: My feathered hat blew out over the sea one very windy day. Albertine, Captain Isidore's seagull, fished it out and kept it for three days to make a nest in it. When he brought it back to me, there was an egg in it. I wore the hat with the egg for a whole week, very gently. The egg hatched on my head. It was a great honour.
textes.Mon chapelet ! (Elle le serre contre ell: My rosary! (She hugs it to herself, then pulls away.) It's… a little sticky. It's nothing! It's nothing at all! Oh Dawn, thank you. And thank you. You went looking for something inside a frog, for me. Nobody had ever done that.
textes.Mon chapelet d'abord, s'il vous plaît !: My rosary first, please! Without it, my prayers shake even more than I do.
textes.Mon chapelet… La Duchesse l'a avalé. Si: My rosary… The Duchess swallowed it. If you find it, I'll follow you anywhere. Even near the lake. A bit.
textes.Mon chat s'appelle Charbon. Il était noi: My cat is called Charbon. He was black. Since the Downpour, he's… black too. He's the only one on the island who lost nothing. He's very proud of it. He parades in front of everyone, tail in the air, as if to say: I haven't changed.
textes.Mon chaudron, là, au fond, ne s'est jama: My cauldron, there, at the back, hasn't gone out since my grandmother lit it. The wizards say it's magic. I say it's well looked after.
textes.Mon chef-d'œuvre de récup' ! Regarde ce: My scrap-built masterpiece! Look what I made with the bolt you left me the other day: a machine that says thank you. It goes “pssht-thanks”. The pssht is the best bit.
textes.Mon cher Hippolyte ! Votre méduse Clémen: My dear Hippolyte! Is your jellyfish Clémence well?
textes.Mon cher Hologuide ! Tout fonctionne ?: My dear Hologuide! Is everything working?
textes.Mon cher Marcel ! Toujours votre mètre ?: My dear Marcel! Still got your tape measure?
textes.Mon cher Raymond ! Toujours fidèle au po: My dear Raymond! Faithful as ever!
textes.Mon cher Raymond ! Une revanche, demain: My dear Raymond! A rematch, tomorrow?
textes.Mon cher citoyen d'honneur ! Port-Azur v: My dear honorary citizen! Port-Azur owes you so much.
textes.Mon cher {surnom}, une question d'import: My dear {surnom}, a question of importance: is a good speech long or short?
textes.Mon chien s'appelle Peek'. Il enterre de: My dog's called Peek'. He buries bones all over the village. If you need some, I know where they are!
textes.Mon chocolat chaud soigne tout. Les chag: My hot chocolate cures everything. Sorrows, colds, quarrels. Except the rain. Against the rain, there's nothing to be done. You just have to stay in the café and wait. Very good for business.
textes.Mon château est tout en haut de la Butte: My castle is at the very top of the Mound. To get there, you follow the switchbacks: the Lower Town ramp, then the Middle Town ramp, then the last one, along the castle wall. My grandfather wanted straight streets. He fell down the slope on opening day.
textes.Mon ciré jaune, c'est Mère Averse qui me: Mother Downpour gave me my yellow raincoat. She says that way people can see me from far away when I fall. I fall a lot. People see me a lot.
textes.Mon client de profil ! J'ai repéré la lu: My profile client! I've found the ideal light for your good side: seven in the evening, in front of the lighthouse.
textes.Mon client détendu ! Toujours pas de pet: My relaxed customer! Still no small print? Perfect.
My favourite customer! Well, my customer. Come and see what's new!
textes.Mon client préféré ! J'ai reçu un siffle: My favourite customer! I've just got in a brand-new silent whistle. Listen… Hear that? No? Perfect, it works.
textes.Mon collectionneur ! J'ai reçu des boule: My collector! Snow globes came in this morning. There's one waiting for you, I can feel it.
textes.Mon complice ! Tu te souviens ? On fait: My accomplice! Remember? We're a team. I've got a plan for Écliptique. We need green paint. Lots of it.
textes.Mon complice des lectures cachées ! Vous: My partner in secret reading! Do you have a book under your pillow right now? Don't answer. I know.
textes.Mon complice qui ne chante jamais devant: My fellow non-singer-in-front-of-people… there are still two of us, aren't there?
textes.Mon confrère des accidents ! Si vous ref: My colleague in accidents! If you make another magnificent mistake, let me know, I'll bring a notebook.
textes.Mon conteneur est bleu dehors, jaune ded: My container is blue outside, yellow inside, and there's a Fusain mural on the roof. Nobody sees it. Except me. And the vault.
textes.Mon cousin Bucatini garde la Marmite, en: My cousin Bucatini guards the Cooking Pot, up top. I guard the Lid, down below. He says the Pot is what matters most. I say without a Lid, the Pot boils over. We discuss it every Sunday. Have done for eleven years.
textes.Mon cousin Macaroni garde le Couvercle,: My cousin Macaroni guards the Lid, down below. He says his job is more important. I tell him: come and stir forty tonnes of sauce with a ladle, then we'll talk. He never comes.
textes.Mon cousin Zigomar m'a fabriqué un « sac: My cousin Zigomar built me a “jet-powered postbag”. It caught fire above the port. I crossed the Harbour backwards, smoking like a chimney. All the letters arrived. A bit toasted.
textes.Mon cousin habite chez Lisse. Il dit que: My cousin lives at Lisse's place. He says everything is grey, clean, and there isn't a single crumb. Poor thing.
textes.Mon danseur en cachette ! Tu as dansé, d: My secret dancer! Have you danced since? In your room? I won't tell anyone.
textes.Mon dernier jour de glacier, il faisait: My last day as an ice-cream seller, it was hot enough to melt the seagulls. I opened my cool box at ten o'clock: everything had melted. Vanilla, strawberry, lemon — one lukewarm soup. Across the way, at Bruno's, the queue went all the way to the fountain. I sold my soup to the seagulls, at a knock-down price. They didn't pay. The next day, I was selling postcards.
textes.Mon dernier zine s'est mieux vendu que l: My last zine sold better than the Boucanier. Agrafe asked me my secret. I said: “Horses with mohawks.” He tried to draw a mohawk horse in his fanzine. It looked like a chair with hair. I didn't put it in my “Epic Fails” column. To be nice.
textes.Mon dessin du Roi, avec la couronne, pap: My drawing of the King, with the crown, Grandpa pinned it above his bed. Every time he walks past, he looks at it. Once, I saw him touch the crown with the tip of his finger. Really gently. As if he recognised it. Grandpas are weird.
textes.Mon discours de bienvenue faisait trente: My welcome speech lasted thirty seconds at first: “Welcome, come in, lovely weather.” Then I added one word a year. One about the mother-of-pearl paving, one about the bridges, one about the fountain. Five hundred years, five hundred words. Today it lasts four minutes. I can't stop it anymore. It's become a tradition.
textes.Mon discours, je l'ai écrit le premier j: I wrote my speech on the very first day. It lasted thirty seconds: “Welcome, come in, lovely weather.” Then I added one word a year. Five hundred years, five hundred words. I can't stop now. It's become a tradition.
textes.Mon djembé s'appelle Tonnerre. C'est mon: My djembe is called Thunder. My grandfather made it, from a tree trunk that fell during a storm. Hence the name.
textes.Mon dos craque comme un spaghetti sec. M: My back creaks like dry spaghetti. But the wheat, now, it grows straight. You can't have everything.
My back won't let me sit.
textes.Mon dragon s'appelle Brindezingue. Il a: My dragon is called Brindezingue. He has eleven wheels donated by Rustine, a tail made of organ pipes and eyes made of lorry headlights. Fusible wants to switch them on. I say no. A dragon needs to sleep. He looks so peaceful.
textes.Mon décret contre les bagarres du dimanc: My decree against Sunday brawls had never been respected. One Sunday, Mama climbed onto her counter and announced: “Today, the Governor said so.” Not a single brawl all day! The next day, I made a speech on the success of my policy. She gave me a funny look. A very kind look.
textes.Mon défunt mari était pêcheur. Fernand l: My late husband was a fisherman. Fernand knew him. That's why I give him the best spot on the quay.
My ink comes from the cuttlefish in the bay. I catch them myself. They bite me. I tattoo them back. We're even.
textes.Mon endroit préféré, c'est le Jardin des: My favourite place is the Zero-Gravity Garden! You can jump super high! Once, I jumped so high I saw the top of Halo's head. He has no hair. Nobody has hair. Why do you have hair, down below?
textes.Mon enfant ! Viens, viens, approche. Les: My child! Come, come, come closer. The Noodles are calling you.
textes.Mon engrenage ! Pas une dent de cassée !: My gear! Not a single tooth broken! Look… I put it back… I turn the crank… IT TURNS! It turns! For ever! Or at least until the end of the Fair. Here, take this, and this hat: it has a fan. I don't know why I had it, but it's yours.
textes.Mon entorse ? Un faux pas en pointant. À: My sprain? A misstep while pointing. To Margaux, I said it was while shooting. To Gisèle, dodging one of Marcel's balls. To Paulo, saving a baguette. Well. All three are a little bit true. What's certain is that with this ankle, I curse the morning deliveries step by step.
textes.Mon explorateur préféré ! Racontez-moi t: My favourite explorer! Tell me everything.
textes.Mon fantôme préféré ! Ta photo floue est: My favourite ghost! Your blurry photo is hanging next to Titou's. You make a fine pair.
textes.Mon fanzine, je le dessine à la main et: My fanzine, I draw it by hand and Agrafe prints it for me at the Spinning Mill. There are interviews, drawings, and the column “Tornade's Blunders”. It's the longest column. It has sequels.
textes.Mon fiancé est parti en mer quand j'avai: My fiancé went to sea when I was twenty. I promised him I'd hear the bell ring for his return. He never came back, but I never stopped listening.
textes.Mon filet, je l'ai tressé moi-même, il y: I braided my net myself, thirty years ago. It's caught thousands of turnips, two hens, one of the Baron's hats and, once, Gaubert. He was asleep in the field. I took him for a big turnip. He never forgave me. Well, he did, after an hour.
textes.Mon fils ! Tu tombes bien, je racontais: My son! Perfect timing, I was just telling everyone…
textes.Mon fils Bulle a ouvert ses Thermes pour: My son Bulle opened his Baths so old horns like mine could warm up. He still makes me pay. Half price. He's a good son. A bit stingy, but a good son.
textes.Mon fils Gédéon devait reprendre l'entre: My son Gédéon was supposed to take over the company. He'd be the “Fils”, the Son, in Lisse & Fils. But he taps. On desks, on files, on scale models. He tapped on the Lisse-Center model until the escalator fell off. In rhythm.
textes.Mon fils Pilli court partout avec son ch: My son Pilli runs everywhere with his dog. A xoloitzcuintle, hairless. He says the dog will guide him to the land of the dead, later on. I say it had better guide him home first.
textes.Mon fils dit trois mots par jour, et moi: My son says three words a day, and I say three thousand: between the two of us, it averages out. He listens to all my stories without a word. Best audience in the world.
textes.Mon fils est né un mardi, pendant une pa: My son was born on a Tuesday, during a string-light blackout. The whole Fronde was in the dark. I fixed the lights the next morning, with him in a basket on the workbench. He wriggled so much that Brasero said: “He's got a spring in his feet.” He's been called Ressort, “Spring”, ever since. He's never stopped wriggling.
textes.Mon fils joue de la batterie dans un gro: My son plays drums in a punk band. Lisse & Sons is becoming Lisse & Sons & Bilge Rats. Miss Prune, have the sign redone. In colour, if you like.
textes.Mon fils veut monter dans la capsule pou: My son wants to ride in the capsule for the fifth time. I want a coffee.
textes.Mon fils, Pépin, a neuf ans et la tête d: My son, Pépin, is nine and has his head full of mushrooms. He knows every tree in the Ash Wood. That's exactly what worries me. Mums worry. Even demon mums. Especially demon mums.
textes.Mon fils, Ressort, a onze ans. Il roule: My son, Ressort, is eleven. He rides a board I made him out of an oven door and four wagon wheels. I limited it to the speed of a snail in a hurry. He unlocked it in two days. That's my boy.
My son, Rivet, bangs on a drum kit. My granddaughter, Ysaé, sells jewellery in Hautefond. When I lit this fire, I didn't know it would warm people all the way to the top of the Column. Fire goes further than you think, my little one. That's why you must always keep it kind.
textes.Mon four boude. Je lui parle gentiment,: My oven is sulking. I talk to it nicely, but it sulks.
textes.Mon fromager ne parle pas. … Il a dit qu: My kapok tree doesn't talk. … What did it say?
textes.Mon frère ! Un autre tapis ? On négocie: My brother! Another carpet? Shall we haggle?
textes.Mon frère ! Une question d'honneur : tu: Brother! A question of honour: do you haggle?
textes.Mon frère Bulle a voulu faire des bulles: My brother Bulle wanted to blow bubbles with one of my potions. The potion made bubbles. So did Bulle. For two days. He thought it was wonderful.
textes.Mon frère Firmin est descendu aux Strate: My brother Firmin went down to the Strata. A canteen lady served him a “miner's” hot chocolate, so thick the spoon stands up. He says it's a soup. I say he's jealous. My cloud milk can't hold anything up. That's its great quality.
textes.Mon frère Firmin et moi, on se dispute d: My brother Firmin and I have been arguing for forty years: who makes the best hot chocolate? Him, with his machine that whistles like a locomotive. Me, with my cloud foam, light as a sigh. Since the Line reopened, we argue in person. It's much better than by letter.
textes.Mon frère Gustave tient le Café Cumulus,: My brother Gustave runs the Cumulus Café, in the City of Clouds. Since the line reopened, I send him a hot chocolate on the first capsule of the morning. It still arrives hot. He pulls a face, and he finishes it. My moustache wins.
textes.Mon frère Rúmil et moi, nous sommes nés: My brother Rúmil and I were born three centuries ago, on the night of the storm, the night the firefly spirits flew away. Our mother used to say the Wood had lost its lights and gained two children. Maybe that's why we've always chased after light, he and I.
textes.Mon frère de cordes ! Tu avais dit : ave: My brother of the strings! You said: with a song. I've written the forty-second verse. For the two of us.
textes.Mon frère de rampe ! Viens, je t'apprend: My ramp brother! Come on, I'll teach you the “Boing”. It's my trick. You jump, you spin, and you say “Boing”. The most important bit is saying “Boing”.
textes.Mon frère est revenu ! Je savais qu'il r: My brother is back! I knew he'd come back. The blue carpet is waiting for you.
textes.Mon frère qui chante faux ! Ce soir, on: My out-of-tune brother! Tonight we'll sing out of tune together, and too bad for the lanterns.
textes.Mon frère tient un café dans la Cité des: My brother runs a café in the City of Clouds. Up there, water boils faster, because of the altitude. He says his hot chocolate is ready before it's even ordered. The line reopens soon. I'll go and check. With my moustache.
textes.Mon frère, laisse-moi au moins parler !: Brother, at least let me talk!
textes.Mon grand frère, c'est le capitaine Pyru: My big brother is Captain Pyrus. He wanted me to be a guard, like him. But I always brought home anything with four legs and a snout. One day, I brought home an abandoned hellhound puppy. Then two. Then twelve. Pyrus gave in.
textes.Mon grand pinceau à façade, je l'ai ache: I bought my big wall brush in Port-Azur with my first wages. It was too big for me, and it's still a bit too big. I called it Bertrand, because a tool half your height deserves a first name.
textes.Mon grand pinceau, là ? C'est un pinceau: My big brush there? It's a façade brush. It can repaint a house in one morning. I named it Bertrand. A brush needs a name.
textes.Mon grand regret : ne jamais avoir quitt: My great regret: never having left Port-Azur. I get seasick. A seasick cartographer… that's my tragedy.
textes.Mon grand-oncle sait tout, et il le dit: My great-uncle knows everything, and says it softly. He's four hundred and twelve. I still have a lot to learn, and I fully expect him to give me the time.
textes.Mon grand-père Séraphin était liftier à: My grandfather Séraphin was a liftkeeper in Hautefond, in the Guild. He thought the Column stopped too low. So one day he cut out a piece of the Butte, put his Levitators underneath, and said: “We're going up where the weather's always fine.” And up it went.
textes.Mon grand-père Séverin raconte la montée: My grandfather Séverin tells every visitor about the rising of the island, as if he'd been there. He wasn't born yet. But I've heard it so often that I'm starting to remember it too.
textes.Mon grand-père a appris à forger en bas,: My grandfather learned to forge down below, in the Strata, with the smiths of the Fronde. He used to say that down there, you knock twice to say hello and once to say thank you. When I strike my anvil, twice then once, someone answers under my feet. I don't know who. I always answer back.
textes.Mon grand-père a fabriqué mon djembé ave: My grandfather made my djembe from a trunk that fell during a storm. He called it Thunder. He gave it to me when I was six, saying: “Never play louder than your heart.” It took me twenty years to understand.
textes.Mon grand-père a ouvert le Diable Repu i: My grandfather opened the Diable Repu three hundred years ago. He used to say: “A demon who has eaten well does no harm to anyone.” It's the house motto. It's carved above the counter, with a spelling mistake. We keep it: it's tradition.
textes.Mon grand-père disait : « Un démon qui a: My grandfather used to say: “A demon who has eaten well does no harm to anyone.” He had it engraved above the counter, with a mistake: “A demon who has ate well”. No one has ever dared correct it. Professor Malachar tried once, with a paintbrush. My mother chased him off with a tea towel.
textes.Mon grand-père disait que Tlaloc habite: My grandfather used to say that Tlaloc lives on the mountaintops, with his little helpers, the Tlaloque. They have jars full of rain, and when they break them with their sticks, it rains. Thunder is the sound of the jars.
My grandfather came with the clan. Behind Mère-Lune, on foot, through the mist. The wolves followed her here. At twenty, I won the Great Race. Last wolf to have won it. At twenty-five, I became a guard. Mère-Lune knitted me this red scarf. I still wear it. Nothing else to say.
textes.Mon grand-père jouait sur les places, de: My grandfather played in town squares, from town to town, with a hat at his feet. As a little boy, I sat beside him and counted the coins. One coin, one note. He said it was the only useful arithmetic. He gave me my first guitar when I was six. It was bigger than me. I slept with it.
textes.Mon grand-père m'a donné son casque le j: My grandfather gave me his helmet on my sixth birthday. It was too big: it fell over my nose. I wore it anyway, all day long, even at the table. My mother wanted to take it off me for bed. I said: “What if the ceiling falls?” She laughed. She let me keep it. It still protects visitors.
textes.Mon grand-père ne s'est jamais pardonné: My grandfather never forgave himself for opening the channel. He looked at the sea every evening as if it were going to laugh at him. Since the Murène arrived, I no longer sleep: I'm afraid history will repeat itself. And there's worse, {surnom}. In the morning, when Selma paints beside me, I watch her hands instead of the galleon. A guard shouldn't.
textes.Mon grand-père s'est endormi sous l'Arbr: My grandfather fell asleep beneath the Mother Tree before he could teach me. It was Faelar who showed me the old way: stretch the net above the fountain, wait for the first ray, and above all, don't talk. Not talking, with Faelar beside you, was the hardest part. It took me a hundred years. Lirael put that ray in her first lantern.
textes.Mon grand-père était apothicaire à Montj: My grandfather was an apothecary in Montjoie. He tasted all his potions. The winter I turned six, he tasted a cold remedy and stayed blue until spring. The town's children called him “the sky”. He loved it. He's the one who gave me my first vial. Empty. “To get started,” he said.
textes.Mon grand-père était apothicaire, et il: My grandfather was an apothecary, and he tasted everything too. He used to say: “A potion you don't dare drink, you don't dare sell.” He was blue all through the winter of 1102. We have portraits. He was smiling.
textes.Mon grand-père était charpentier de mari: My grandfather was a shipwright on the Old Dock. He built rowing boats for the fishermen. I slept in the wood shavings in his workshop. Hence my name — Copeau means “wood shaving”. He used to say: “Wood remembers the tree.” So I talk to it kindly. To the wood. My grandfather, though, didn't like being talked to while he was planing.

My grandfather was a shipwright. He built rowing boats for the fishermen of the Old Dock. He taught me just one thing: “Wood remembers the tree.” So I talk to it kindly. Even to pallets. Especially to pallets: they've had a hard life.
textes.Mon grand-père était mineur, mon père au: My grandfather was a miner, and so was my father. My father taught me the most important rule: “The rock speaks. You just have to keep quiet long enough to hear it.” I keep quiet a lot. People think I'm serious. I think they're chatty.
textes.Mon grand-père était potier, et il racon: My grandfather was a potter, and he told stories about rain. Tlaloc lives in the mountains with his little helpers, the Tlaloque. They keep the rain in jars, and when they break them, it rains. At seven, I broke one of grandfather's jars to make it rain. It didn't rain. But I heard thunder. Grandfather's.
textes.Mon grand-père, c'est Grand-père Ébène,: My grandfather is Grandpa Ébène, the storyteller. When I was little he told me stories by the fire, and I watched the shadows dance. I wanted to learn how to make light, so that stories would always have somewhere to dance.
textes.Mon grand-père, c'est le Capitaine Charb: My grandpa is Captain Charbonnel. He knows all the knots, all the stars and all the storms. He tells the ash-storm story every evening, and each time, the waves are bigger.
textes.Mon grand-père, c'est le meilleur guette: My grandad is the best lookout in the world. Forty years in the crow's nest! He's seen a white whale, a ghost ship and a blue light. I believe him about everything.
textes.Mon grand-père, c'était Honoré Cogne, le: My grandfather was Honoré Cogne, the automaton maker. I grew up in his workshop, among cuckoo clocks and clockwork dancers. For my tenth birthday, he cast a gear of solid gold, with “Firmin Cogne” engraved on the hub. He put it in my hand and said: “One day, it'll turn something that never stops.” I believed him. I still do.
textes.Mon grand-père, le Capitaine Sel, a écum: My grandfather, Captain Sel, sailed these seas sixty years ago. He passed through Tazira. He left behind… let's say, a keepsake. I've come to get it back.
textes.Mon grimoire ! Les pages se sont envolée: My spellbook! The pages flew away when I opened the window to let out a draught spell. Three pages, scattered all over town! Without them, my spellbook only tells soup recipes.
textes.Mon groin a un super-pouvoir : il trouve: My snout has a superpower: it finds food.
textes.Mon halo, autour de la tête, s'allume to: My halo, around my head, lights up all by itself when I'm happy. When a visitor says “thank you for the speech”, it shines so bright you can see it from the sea. It's happened three times. I remember every one.
textes.Mon hameau, derrière la scène, c'est cel: My hamlet, behind the stage, is the roadies' one. We come from both villages: one foot in the flowers and the other in the puddles. We never fell out: we were too busy carrying heavy stuff.
My hamlet, behind the stage, is the roadies' one. We come from both villages: one foot in the flowers, the other in the puddles. We never fell out. We were too busy carrying crates.
textes.Mon herbier de dix sur dix, Monsieur Rad: Mister Radis kept my ten-out-of-ten herbarium. He showed it to me fifteen years later, in a drawer in his greenhouse. The flowers were all dried up, but the little tree drawings were still there. He said: “You see? You were already up there.” I kissed him on the top of his head.
textes.Mon histoire ? Il n'y a pas grand-chose: My story? There's not much to tell.
textes.Mon hydromel est un triomphe ! Le roi en: My honey drink is a triumph! The king drank a whole barrel. He danced on the table. The table remembers.
textes.Mon héros, c'est Sire Tancrède. Il a vai: My hero is Sir Tancrède. He defeated a giant, a serpent and a bear. Hilaire says it was in the fog. I say fog makes you even braver, because you can't see a thing.
textes.Mon implant sur la tempe, et ma visière,: The implant on my temple, and my visor, let me see the city's networks. The first time, the whole city spoke to me at once: the traffic lights, the lifts, the vending machines. I cried. Then I learned to listen to just one at a time.
textes.Mon implant transforme la musique en lum: My implant turns music into light, under my skin. I saved up for it for three years. The first night I switched it on, a little girl asked me if I was a fairy. I said yes.
textes.Mon implant, sur la tempe, me laisse « v: My implant, on my temple, lets me “see” the networks. The first time, I thought the whole city was talking to me at once. It took me weeks to learn to turn down the volume.
I kept my kepi from the level crossing. Nobody here wears one. On the first day, Gnocchi asked me if I was a general. I said: “No, I'm a guard.” He said: “That's better.” Ever since, he salutes me every morning. I salute him back. We're very serious about it.
textes.Mon livre le plus célèbre montre que moi: My most famous book shows that the fewer pirates there are on the seas, the hotter it gets. The curves are perfect. Captain Rigatoni says it's because pirates open the windows. I haven't found a better explanation. I put it in the second edition.
textes.Mon loir ! Tu as rêvé de quoi, cette nui: My little sleepyhead! What did you dream about last night? Don't lie, I can smell dreams. A bit.
textes.Mon lève-tôt ! Je t'ai gardé un pain cha: My early bird! I've saved you a warm loaf. The first of the batch, the one that sings when you break it.
My manor holds four thousand objects. A roc's egg, an admiral's moustache, a snow globe from Victor… my favourite.
textes.Mon mari a peur en dirigeable. Il est re: My husband's scared of airships. He stayed at the café. He asked me for a photo of the drop.
textes.Mon mari est resté au Café Cumulus. Il d: My husband stayed behind at the Cumulus Café. He says he can see the sky perfectly well from a chair.
My husband and I have just come from Hautefond. We've taken the Funicular three times this morning. He says it's for the photos. It's for the ray.
textes.Mon mari m'a demandée en mariage à cette: My husband proposed to me at this table. Fifty years ago. He had a cloud-milk moustache. I said yes anyway.
textes.Mon mari était horloger. À chaque annive: My husband was a clockmaker. Every birthday, he gave me a cuckoo clock. He gave me a hundred and seven! Now he's the one who naps, and I'm the one who winds them.
textes.Mon mari, Cerfeuil, était boulanger. Il: My husband, Cerfeuil, was a baker. He burnt every loaf, but he had the best palate of anyone. He left with the mist when Mochi was one, five years ago. I couldn't sleep any more. Pivoine made me the first vial of mist, and I slept. And Pépin, his best friend, has come every morning since to carry the flour sacks. He'd promised him.
textes.Mon mari, c'est Nonno Tortellini. Il fai: My husband is Nonno Tortellini. He grows the wheat, I make the pasta. He says without his wheat, no pasta. I say without my pasta, his wheat is just grass. We've never argued. Well, never for long.
textes.Mon mari. Trente ans de mariage, et je c: My husband. Thirty years of marriage, and I think he's said three hundred words to me. He says more to his boat. She doesn't answer him; I do. Maybe that's the problem.
textes.Mon maître de l'oasis m'a dit une chose,: My master from the oasis told me one thing, on the last night. There's a note the guembri plays only once in a lifetime. It comes when it wants. I haven't heard it yet, {surnom}. And I'm afraid. Afraid it'll come one evening when nobody's listening, at three in the morning, in an empty street. So I play every night as if it were that night.
textes.Mon maître racontait sur cette place, et: My master told stories on this square, and his master before him. Words don't die as long as they're spoken. I speak them.
textes.Mon meilleur client ! Clou, sors le tabo: My best customer! Clou, bring out the stool.
My best customer! Well, my customer.
textes.Mon meilleur copain, c'est Tom, l'appren: My best mate is Tom, the apprentice at the Great Strata Forge. He bangs on the anvil. I bang on the ramp. We're the same age, we've got the same bruises on our knees, and we both want to change the world. Him with a hammer, me with a board.
textes.Mon messager ! Entre, entre. Tu sais quo: My messenger! Come in, come in. Guess what? Yesterday, I had tea in the sun. In the SUN. With Sunflower. I hadn't done that in fifty years.
textes.Mon messager du Soleil et de la Pluie !: My Messenger of the Sun and the Rain! Come here and let me hug you. Thanks to you, I've found an old friend again.
textes.Mon module d'émotions est à soixante-dix: My emotion module is at seventy percent. I installed it myself. Kenji said it was risky. It was the best decision of my life.
textes.Mon morceau du lever de soleil n'a pas d: My sunrise track has no name. Every morning, Zoé suggests one: “Hello Sea”, “Jelly Legs”, “Zoé Stays”. She's up to twenty-one. I haven't picked any of them. I think I like her searching too much.
textes.Mon moulin est aux Champs du Sud, à côté: My mill is in the Southern Fields, next to Gaubert's farm. You can see it from all over town. When the Baron's hat blows away, it often ends up caught on a sail. I take it back to the castle. The Baron gives me a hat as thanks. I have nine.
textes.Mon neveu Barnabé m'écrivait depuis Haut: My nephew Barnabé used to write to me from Hautefond: “Uncle, I'm scared of heights, but I want to be a liftkeeper.” I'd write back: “Well, I'm scared of the dark, and I drive at the bottom of the sea.” It wasn't true. I've never been scared of the dark. But someone had to be scared along with him. On reopening day, he came down with me, eyes wide open. He told me: “In the water, there's no void. There's blue.”
textes.Mon neveu. Le fils de ma sœur. Je voulai: My nephew. My sister's son. I wanted a guard. I got a runner. He talks too much, he watches the Clearing instead of the forest. But he comes up on time. That counts.
textes.Mon nom vient du dieu des abeilles. Ma m: My name comes from the bee god. My mother said I was already buzzing in my cradle.
textes.Mon nom, je l'ai gagné mon premier mois: I earned my name in my first month on the Shark. A storm, the pot waltzing about, and a crate of Brutus's new nails tipping over above it. I was tasting the soup. I swallowed a nail. Doc said: “It'll come out.” It came out, don't ask me how. Gros-Louis shouted “Mange-Clous!” — Nail-Eater! The nail left. The name stayed.
textes.Mon objet préféré ? La montre qui tourne: My favourite item? The backwards watch. With it, you're never late: you're early in the other direction.
textes.Mon observatoire, c'est mon grand-père q: My observatory was built by my grandfather. He used to say the stars are wizards who got their light spell right. I never dared contradict him.
textes.Mon oiseau de nuit ! Ce soir, Django jou: My night owl! Django's playing tonight. I'll save you the stool at the end, the one that doesn't creak.
My uncle Bedaine swaps. I sell. He says it's a disgrace for a tanuki. I say coins fit in a pocket, and a goat doesn't.
textes.Mon oncle Hamid ? Il m'appelle « tête de: My uncle Hamid? He calls me “mule-head” and sings to bring in the sardines. They do come, too. To make him stop, I reckon. I owe him everything. Don't tell him.
textes.Mon oncle Mbarek, c'est l'homme bleu ! I: My uncle Mbarek is the blue man! He crosses the desert, he knows all the stars, and he almost never talks. Except with me. With me he laughs. He does, I swear.
textes.Mon oncle est un mur. Un bon mur, solide: My uncle is a wall. A good wall, solid, protective. But just try making a wall laugh. I've been trying for eighty years.
textes.Mon oncle m'a élevée au milieu des trocs: My uncle raised me surrounded by swaps. He's impossible, stubborn as a carpet that doesn't fly, and I adore him. He says I shame him. He still takes my apples. Well, he swaps for them.
textes.Mon oncle travaille au Dôme d'Azur, tout: My uncle works at the Azure Dome, at the very bottom of the sea. He writes that down there, you can see whales swimming past the ceiling. Going down to the bottom of the sea? That I could do. Going up is my problem.

My uncle works at the Azure Dome, at the very bottom of the sea. He writes that down there, you can see whales going past the ceiling. The line has reopened, so I went down to check. Going down, that I can do. Going up is my problem.
textes.Mon oncle, le garde. Il voulait un neveu: My uncle, the guard. He wanted a guard nephew, he got a runner nephew. He pretends to be disappointed. But I've seen him leaning out of the watch post during my races. I have, I have.
textes.Mon or ! L'heure dorée vient de passer,: My gold! The golden hour just went by, and I thought of you. Don't laugh, it's my job.
My basket has been all around the archipelago. It left full of flowers on a boat from Port-Azur, and came back full of shells, then spices, then letters. Every time I fill it, I wonder where it'll come back from next time.
My trousers say no! … A small one.
textes.Mon papa a un bras en métal. Quand j'éta: My papa has a metal arm. When I was a baby, I thought all papas had one. At school, I found out they don't. I felt a bit sorry for the others.
textes.Mon papa est aventurier, il est au-delà: My papa is an adventurer, he's across the sea, on a great quest. He writes to me every season. I keep all his letters in a biscuit tin. There are twelve. In the last one, he drew a teeny tiny dragon. He wrote: “He's nice.” I think he's enormous. Papa says that so I won't be scared.
textes.Mon papa est aventurier. Il est parti tr: My papa is an adventurer. He went very far away, beyond the sea, on a great quest. He writes to me every season. In his last letter, he drew a dragon. He says it was really tiny. I think he says that so I won't be scared.
textes.Mon papa est cheminot, il répare les aig: My dad's a railwayman, he fixes the points. My mum's a lamp-tender at the Workshop of Lights. I chose the forge, because that's where you make the most noise. They said: “Of course.”
textes.Mon papa est marin. Il est parti quand j: My dad is a sailor. He left when I was very little. He sends me shells, with little notes on them: “For my sailor.” I have thirty-two. I keep them in a box under my bed, by size. The biggest one, I listen to at night. Mum says you can hear the sea in it. I hear Dad laughing.
textes.Mon papa est technicien à la Cheminée d': My dad is a technician at the Air Chimney: he looks after the air everybody breathes. My mum harvests spirulina on the algae wall. So I'm made of air and spirulina. That's why my tongue is blue. Well, it's also Josette's lemonade.
textes.Mon papa souffle des bulles toute la jou: My dad blows bubbles all day long and forgets to eat. I look after him. He looks after me too, but not as well. I don't tell him that.
textes.Mon papa, il a un bras en laiton qui sou: My dad has a brass arm that lifts everything, even me. He built Boulon just for me. He's the best dad in the whole city. And in the archipelago too.
textes.Mon papa, il est gentil et il fait des b: My daddy's nice and he makes daddy jokes. He takes pictures of everything, all the time. But sometimes he puts the machine away and looks with his eyes. Those are the best times.
textes.Mon papa, il s'appelait Cerfeuil. Je m'e: My papa was called Cerfeuil. I don't remember him, I was too little. But I know he burned the bread and laughed really loud, Godfather Pépin told me. I've got his wooden spoon, it's all black at the end. He went away with the mist. So in the evening, I say hello to the mist. That way, it's polite.
textes.Mon papy, c'est le meilleur pêcheur du m: My grandpa is the best fisherman in the world. He's never caught the King, but that's because he's waiting for the right moment. I look harder. But he waits harder.
textes.Mon parapluie-ascenseur monte. Très bien: My umbrella-lift goes up. Very well. The first tester stayed stuck on the Institute's big mast for an hour. He said the view was superb. It was Doctor Aurèle. He named three clouds while he waited. He says it was the best hour of his career.
textes.Mon partenaire à trois balles ! Le duo t: My three-ball partner! The double act awaits you on the square. I've already planned the falls.
textes.Mon pas-trop ! Tu as mangé tes trois car: My not-very! Have you eaten your three carrots? Not four, eh. Four weighs you down.
textes.Mon patch des Rats de Cale, c'est moi qu: I designed my Bilge Rats patch myself: a rat with a red mohawk and a guitar. Rouille cried when I showed it to her. Clou nodded twice. For him, that's a standing ovation.
textes.Mon patient raisonnable ! Vous voyez, je: My sensible patient! You see, I remember you. So, no new scrapes?
textes.Mon petit ! Viens par ici, viens voir la: My dear! Come over here, come and see the Palette.
textes.Mon petit cocotier ! J'ai une noix bien: My little coconut palm! I've got a nice fresh nut for you. I'll open it in one go. Crack!
textes.Mon petit frère est arrivé sur l'île un: My little brother arrived on the island a year after me, with nothing, just a bag and a smile. He breaks everything, but when he touches a plant, it grows. I saw him bring a dried-up basil back to life just by looking at it. I haven't told him. He'd break it.
textes.Mon petit frère garde la halle du roi av: My little brother guards the king's hall with a shiny shield. Me, I carry coal. He's got the fine job. I've got the good back. Well, I had.
textes.Mon petit frère, Gland ! Il parle plus v: My little brother, Gland! He talks faster than the wind and loses his hazelnuts faster than he hides them. He wants to build bridges all the way to the moon. He'll get there, I think.
textes.Mon petit frère, c'est Frère Linguini. I: My little brother is Brother Linguini. He breaks everything he touches. Except plants. Plants, he makes them grow just by looking at them. It's our family secret.
textes.Mon petit frère. Il oublie la nacelle. I: My little brother. He forgets the basket. He forgets the time. But he never forgets anything important. Hm. Solid.
textes.Mon petit tanuki ! Tout se troque, hein: My little tanuki! Everything can be swapped, eh? … Almost everything. You'll see.
textes.Mon petit-fils Hiro a brûlé son premier: My grandson Hiro burnt his first broth at eight. The second at nine. The third was perfect. He doesn't remember, but I kept the bowl. It's on my shelf, next to my wedding photo.
textes.Mon petit-fils Hiro fait les nouilles ju: My grandson Hiro makes noodles right next door, with Gaston, the robot arm. He thinks he taught Gaston everything. I think it's the other way round. But I don't tell him: he's proud.
textes.Mon petit-fils n'est pas rentré du Bois: My grandson hasn't come back from the Ash Wood. Zébuline is white as ash. If you go south-east, call him loudly: Pépin always answers when you shout his name.
textes.Mon petit-fils, Gnocchi, il est tout ron: My grandson, Gnocchi, is all round and soft, like a real gnocchi. He wants to be a pirate, a novice, a singer and a volcano. I told him: first, finish your plate.
textes.Mon peuple forge depuis mille ans. Nos l: My people have been forging for a thousand years. Our blades have slain dragons. Well, one dragon. A small one. It had a cold.
textes.Mon peuple vivait sur une île, autrefois: My people once lived on an island, like yours. One night the sea rose and swallowed it. The Great Crystal wrapped us in a bubble of air, and we stayed. A thousand years, under the sea.
