textes.Notre calendrier sacré, le Tzolk'in, com: Our sacred calendar, the Tzolk'in, counts two hundred and sixty days: thirteen numbers and twenty day names turning together, like two wheels. A day comes back every two hundred and sixty days. Like an old acquaintance.
textes.Notre champion ! Tout en haut du tableau: Our champion! Top of the board for three years. I saw him run before he could walk. I'm as proud of him as of a little brother. Don't tell him: his ears are big-headed enough already.
textes.Notre cité a sept quartiers et un canal: Our city has seven quarters and a circular canal. The children say the canal goes round the world. It's almost true.
textes.Notre maire. Un brave homme qui parle lo: Our mayor. A good man who talks long. He owes me his sash, and he knows it. I know it too. We smile at each other.
textes.Notre mariage a été fixé sept fois. La p: Our wedding has been set seven times. The first time, a clock to repair. The second, a storm. The seventh, the great clock running a second fast. One second! Tic was so sorry. I told him it didn't matter, that we had all the time in the world. He made a funny face when I said “all the time”.
textes.Notre nom, Buvard, vient de l'arrière-gr: Our name, Buvard, comes from Achille's great-grandfather. He made the village's blotting paper. Achille, for his part, mostly makes blots.
textes.Notre numéro au Crâne Fendu : je joue de: Our act at the Crâne Fendu: I play faster and faster, and she throws a knife on every note, at a painted board. At the end, my last note and her last knife land together. One evening, I finished too early. She threw in the silence. The whole room shivered. Since then, I always finish too early. On purpose.
textes.Notre partie de dames dure depuis le pri: Our game of draughts has been going on since spring. It never ends: every time I'm about to lose, a piece appears. I don't know where from. Hassan looks at my sleeve, then at the sea, then at my sleeve. He says nothing, he pours more tea. He's very polite, or he has bad eyesight. For a friend, it's the same thing.
textes.Notre partie tient toujours, entre humai: Our game still stands, human to human. I've written it down. I'm still thinking about my first move.
textes.Notre premier bras de fer, je l'ai gagné: Our first arm-wrestle, I won. The second too. The third too. At the fourth, just as I was about to win, Clovis sneezed. A cloud of flour hit me in the face. I couldn't see, I laughed, I let go. He'd won. I say it doesn't count. He says the flour is part of him. We're still arguing about it.
textes.Notre premier jour ici, une mouette s'es: On our first day here, a seagull landed on my head and stole my snack. A real animal! With feathers, a beak, and a very bad temper! I was so happy that I cried, and the seagull came back to steal the rest. That day, I decided to devote my life to animals. Even the thieves.
textes.Notre premier marchandage a duré trois h: Our first haggle lasted three hours and four teapots. She wanted my apple juice, I wanted her saffron, and neither of us would give in. In the end, we swapped a jar of saffron for a barrel of apple juice and a sea shanty, sung by me, in Breton, in front of the whole souk. She says it was the song that tipped the scales.
textes.Notre premier marché, à Tazira : mon mie: Our first deal, in Tazira: my honey for his dates. It should have taken a minute. It took a whole day and three teapots. He'd name a price, drink a glass, go quiet; I'd talk, drink, talk. At sunset, we shook on it. Ever since, every year, I go down to see him: on foot along the coast in the old days, by Zéphyr now, when my paws complain.
textes.Notre première mission ensemble, c'était: Our first mission together was three slimes at the South Gate. He charged shouting his own name, tripped over his cape and rolled all the way to me. I healed him, very quickly, with my eyes shut. He got up, said “well played, Sister!”, and charged off again. He fell again. I healed him again. The slimes were laughing.
textes.Notre première semaine ici, un oiseau a: Our first week here, a bird dropped an apple on the Agora. I picked it up. I bit into it. It went “crunch.” It had a taste! A real one! Sweet, sour, juicy! I cried, I laughed, I dropped the apple, I caught it with my third hand. That day, I decided to become an Earth cook.
textes.Notre présentateur ! Ta voix est restée: Our presenter! Your voice stayed in my speakers. I can still hear it.
textes.Notre « charge foudroyante » est née par: Our “lightning charge” was born by accident. I charged a goblin, she cast a lightning bolt, it hit me, and I kept running, sparkling like a lantern. The goblin thought I was a storm god. It ran away. Violette apologised forty times. I asked her if we could do it again. She said no.
textes.Notre île flotte au-dessus des nuages, l: Our island floats above the clouds, far from the archipelago. No one comes here… except those who dream hard enough. Or eat the right mushroom.
Noted, boss. And I'll water the plants.
Noted, boss. A very fine report.
textes.Nourredine fait des trous dans mon cuivr: Nourredine pokes holes in my copper and calls them stars. For forty years now. Without him, my lanterns light up nothing. Don't tell him I said that.
textes.Nourredine fait les plus belles lanterne: Nourredine makes the most beautiful lanterns on the island. I've got seven above my cannons. I… borrowed them. He knows and says nothing. He's a good man.
textes.Nourredine perce la nuit avec des millie: Nourredine pierces the night with thousands of little holes. He thinks he's making lanterns. He's making paintings. I spend my nights copying them.
Nourredine pierces the night with holes. His big lantern lights my circle every evening, and my stories are better for it. He never hears them to the end: he's working.
textes.Nourredine perce les lanternes, moi je l: Nourredine pierces the lanterns, I shape them. We've been arguing for forty years about who has the finer trade. It's me.
textes.Nourrissantes ! Vous avez parlé à Corali: Filling! You've been talking to Coralin, you have. That's his word. He's been saying it for four hundred years, and he buys a bag from me every week. Beware of people who say “filling”.
textes.Nous avons comparé nos calendriers, pour: We compared our calendars, to celebrate the Serpent on the same day. The dates didn't fall the same way. Their astronomer, Ah Kin Pech, counted on his fingers all afternoon, then declared that both our dates were right. Ix Kanul and I found that answer unacceptable. At last we agreed on something.
textes.Nous avons fait un concours, lumières ét: We held a contest, lights out, with little Tom as the judge. He said “both”. We both laughed for ten minutes, in the dark. We couldn't see a thing. It was very bright.
textes.Nous avons signé notre traité sur une se: We signed our treaty on a Crâne Fendu napkin: at hers, you play small and eat well; at mine, you play big and don't eat. I signed with my name. She signed with a cross, pressed very hard. I asked no questions. A cross drawn by Mama Grog is worth all the signatures in the world.
textes.Nous avons triomphé ! Ce soir, quatre pa: We have triumphed! Tonight, four slices of pie. No: five.
textes.Nous cacher ? Non. Nous attendons. La me: Hide? No. We're waiting. The sea has its reasons; one day it will give us back our island. Meanwhile, the dome is our sky.
textes.Nous commerçons avec les trois autres pe: We trade with the island's three other peoples. Not always gladly, but we trade. Matthias, our cartographer, will tell you all that better than I can.
textes.Nous deux, pour notre mariage, il y a qu: The two of us, for our wedding, forty-three years ago! The frame comes from an old glider wing that fell onto our balcony one day. The strings are kite strings from the Wind Festival: they've kept the taste of the sky.
textes.Nous devions rester trois semaines. Le p: We were supposed to stay three weeks. On the first evening, we saw the stars, the sea, the islands and a fisherman singing out of tune in his boat. On the second evening, someone unpacked their suitcase. On the third, everyone did. A thousand years later, the suitcases are still unpacked, and we're still on holiday.
textes.Nous habitions la maison 7. Papa et mama: We lived at number 7. Papa and Mama were roofers, and in the evening, Mama sewed umbrellas “for those who are between two roofs”. Achille, four years younger than me, jumped off the workshop roof with them. I held the spare umbrella and counted the bumps: seventeen before I turned ten. I still have the list, with the dates.
textes.Nous jouons aux dames de basalte chaque: We play basalt draughts every week. When I'm thinking about a move, Ébène starts telling a story. I listen, and I lose. On his birthday, I let him win on purpose. He thinks it's thanks to the story. Maybe that's a little bit true: his stories are very good.
textes.Nous nous disputions les vieilles bottes: We used to fight over the old boots that fell off the cliff. So we signed a truce: every first Monday of the month, at the foot of the crane, I swap a left boot for a right boot, and we each make up our pairs. It's very official. We don't talk, we swap. Like spies, but with boots.
textes.Nous nous disputons depuis des années po: For years we've argued over whether Skull Rock faces north or east. He says east, because Barbe-Sanglante loved the rising sun. Me, I measured: north-north-east. He said: “You see? It's looking a bit east.” We celebrated at the Crâne Fendu. He paid. The first time in thirty years.
textes.Nous nous disputons depuis dix ans l'inv: For ten years we've been arguing over who invented fire-cinnamon tea. She put in the cinnamon; I put in the hot water and wrote down the recipe. My mother says it was her, because she grew the cinnamon. We drink it together every winter, arguing. It's the best herbal tea in the city.
textes.Nous nous disputons depuis dix ans pour: For ten years we've been arguing over who invented fire-cinnamon tea. I say it was me: I put in the cinnamon. She says it was her: she put in the hot water. Mother Brasille, her mother, says it was herself, because she grew the cinnamon. We can't agree. We drink it together.
textes.Nous nous disputons sur tout, devant nos: We argue about everything, in front of our shops, on the Great Square. Him with his formulas, me with my spells. Customers stop to listen. One day, a little girl asked us: “Are you married?” Aubin went bright red. So did I. There are forty years between us. The little girl was Noisette. She wrote it down in her journal.
textes.Nous nous reverrons, {surnom}. C'est écr: We shall meet again, {surnom}. It is written. By me.
textes.Nous nous sommes disputés tout un dîner: We argued through a whole dinner about the wild dogs of the lava field. He wanted to drive them away, I wanted to understand them. The next day, I brought him a list of names for the wild dogs, in case we ever tamed them. He laughed. But he folded the list and put it in his pocket. I saw him.
textes.Nous nous sommes disputés une heure, à l: We argued for an hour at the fair: Kukulkan or Quetzalcóatl, who saw the Feathered Serpent first? Néferet listened without a word. At the end, she sighed: “Where I come from, the serpent is the enemy of the sun.” Ix Kanul and I fell silent. Then we drank a cacao together. In silence.
textes.Nous nous sommes mariés il y a dix jours: We got married ten days ago. Léa wanted to see the sea. I wanted to see Léa seeing the sea.
textes.Nous reviendrons. Nous revenons toujours: We will return. We always return. It's in our contract. Have a nice day.
textes.Nous sommes arrivés le même automne, il: We arrived the same autumn, forty years ago. He's addressed me formally since day one. I've been on first-name terms with him since day one. Neither of us has ever given in.
textes.Nous sommes déjà ensemble ! Vous m'avez: We're already together! Did you forget me? It's all right. It happens. Well, that's what Violette says.
textes.Nous sommes déjà ensemble. Vous ne m'avi: We're already together. You hadn't seen me? I'm discreet. Except when I zap.
textes.Nous sommes déjà frères d'armes ! Depuis: We're already brothers-in-arms! For ages now! Well, since a little while ago.
textes.Nous sommes désolés pour la gêne occasio: We apologise for any inconvenience. We are not sorry. We are programmed to say it.
textes.Nous sommes le plus jeune des quatre mon: We are the youngest of the four worlds, and the deepest. The Clouds have the sky, Hautefond has the view, the Strata have the hands, so they say. We have the sea. And the air: our algae make so much of it that a little drifts up, through the Line's tunnel, all the way to the galleries of the Strata. The miners say that in the morning it smells of the sea.
textes.Nous verrons cela, Monsieur Bobor. Ma rè: We shall see about that, Monsieur Bobor. My ruler, if you please.
textes.Nous vivons sous le Cinquième Soleil. Qu: We live under the Fifth Sun. Four worlds came before it, and all were destroyed. This one will end too, one day, in earthquakes. But not today.
textes.Nous vous remercions de votre visite. No: We thank you for your visit. We thank you for your understanding. We thank you for… Miss Prune, what am I thanking them for again?
textes.Nous écrivons les nombres avec des point: We write numbers with dots and bars: a dot is worth one, a bar is worth five. Thirteen is two bars and three dots. Simple, isn't it?
textes.Nous étions une seule goutte, ma sœur Br: We were a single drop, my sister Brindille and I, on a leaf of the highest branch of Yggdrasil. One morning, a gust of wind split us in two. I stayed on the leaf. She rolled, and fell down through the clouds. I watched her fall until she was nothing but a dot. Then nothing at all.
textes.Nouvelles de la Casse : Ferraille a ajou: News from the Scrapyard: Ferraille has added a scale to Brindezingue, her dragon. A red car door. The dragon is said to be “happy”. It creaked. We're taking that as a yes.
textes.Nova ! Une photo des méduses ?: Nova! A photo of the jellyfish?
textes.Nova Volant garde la Cité des Nuées en l: Nova Volant keeps the City of Clouds in the air; I keep the Dome under the water. She counts lift, I count pressure. Neither of us ever panics. We write each other numbers. Those are our friendship letters. The loveliest ones I get.
textes.Nova emprunte mon établi le soir. Elle m: Nova borrows my workbench in the evenings. She gives it back all tidy, with a note: “This is not a toy.” I reply: “Yes it is. A bit.” She's the most serious person on the island. I admire her. I annoy her. It balances out.
textes.Nova m'a apporté un glouglou malade, qui: Nova brought me a sick glug-glug that wouldn't eat anymore. I put it among the glowing flowers. It ate a petal. Then two. Then a whole flower. The flower didn't protest: it blinked once, yes. The glug-glug went home cured. The flower grew back in a week, even bigger.
textes.Nova m'a appris que les méduses de ciel: Nova taught me that the sky jellyfish love resting in my big flowers. It tickles them. The flowers laugh all night, blinking. I sleep very badly. But I'm very happy.
textes.Nova m'a dit que les méduses de ciel aim: Nova told me the sky jellyfish like to rest in my big flowers. It tickles them. The flowers blink with laughter all night long.
textes.Nova m'a laissé nourrir les glouglous de: Nova let me feed the glug-glugs in the Greenhouse. They went “glug-glug” when they saw me, then they all snuggled up against me. Nova says they thought I was a giant mummy glug-glug. I stayed perfectly still for an hour so as not to disappoint them. I took four hundred photos.
textes.Nova s'occupe des méduses de ciel. Elles: Nova looks after the sky jellyfish. They're see-through, like me. She says we're “of the same aesthetic family”. I don't know what that is. But I'm proud to be part of it.
textes.Nova sait tout de la capsule. Elle dit q: Nova knows everything about the capsule. She says I throw it off balance by one millimetre when I jump. She's never forbidden me to jump. I think deep down she quite likes that millimetre.
textes.Nova vient regarder les aurores depuis l: Nova comes to watch the auroras from the Observatory bridge. The sky jellyfish light up all around her. She cries with happiness. I named a constellation for her. It's shaped like a jellyfish.
Nova, your constellation is shining tonight.
textes.Nova, trois méduses dans mes fleurs, cet: Nova, three jellyfish in my flowers last night.
textes.Nova, vous cherchez quelque chose ?: Nova, are you looking for something?
textes.Nox allume les réverbères de la cité. Il: Nox lights the city's street lamps. He talks little, blushes a lot, and knows every lantern by name. I think he writes poems. I even think I know who for.
textes.Nox allume les réverbères la nuit, et il: Nox lights the street lamps at night, and goes home to bed when I leave for the garden. As a boy, he used to fall into my cabbages thinking he could fly. Today, I give him mint to help him sleep. He's a nice boy. Too shy.
textes.Nox allume les réverbères pendant que je: Nox lights the street lamps while I play. He never applauds, he never says a thing, but he lights the lanterns in rhythm. One flame per note. It's the most beautiful applause I get.
textes.Nox emprunte des poèmes par la fenêtre,: Nox borrows poems through the window, at night, and brings them back before dawn. He signs with a single word: “Thank you”. We've never said more than twenty words to each other. All in writing.
textes.Nox écrit des poèmes comme on allume des: Nox writes poems the way you light lanterns: gently, one by one, so the night is less dark. He's teaching me poetry. He's very patient. I'm very slow. We get on well.
textes.Nox… j'ai trouvé une rime à « braise » !: Nox… I've found a rhyme for “ember”!
textes.Nuit calme. Il a chanté, vers trois heur: Quiet night. He sang, around three o'clock.
Nowhere, Pyrus. I'm taking a stroll.
textes.NÂGA ! Vaincu ! Par toi ! Gaston, sors l: NÂGA! Defeated! By you! Gaston, bring out the ceremonial barrel… Ah, it's coconut juice. Gaston, bring out the ceremonial coconut juice!
textes.NÉOPOLIS\n\nTout droit : le Boulevard de:
NEOPOLIS

Straight ahead: the Neon Boulevard, Hologram Square,
the Axiom Tower (Sky Terrace), the Night Market, the Arcades
West: the Alleys   ·   East: the Heights, the Zen Garden
Monorail: 4 stations around the city
textes.Nâga plonge dans les abysses : tu ne peu: Nâga dives into the depths: you can't reach him anymore! The three Stone Eyes awaken… wake them with the amulet (E).
textes.Nâga pousse un dernier sifflement… et s': Nâga lets out one last hiss… and slowly sinks into the abyss. The Serpent is defeated!
textes.Nâga siffle de rage ! Il va cracher son: Nâga hisses with rage! He's about to spit his venom: don't stand in the green puddles.
textes.Nâga, le Serpent des Abysses: Nâga, the Serpent of the Abyss
textes.Nâga… Le Serpent des Abysses. Sur ma car: Nâga… The Serpent of the Abyss. On my map, there's just a big black drawing and the word “NO” written three times. I'll make you some soup. For afterwards. If there is an afterwards.
textes.Né dans une forge. Ma mère soufflait le: Born in a forge. My mother worked the bellows. My father hammered the iron. Me, I slept in a basket, next to the anvil. The sound of the hammer was my lullaby. Even today, I sleep badly when it's quiet. My first word was “hot”. The second, “more”. My father was proud. My mother, a bit less.
textes.Nébula ! Du nouveau d'en bas ?: Nébula! Anything new from down below?
textes.Nébula dit que je paie trop cher. C'est: Nébula says I pay too much. She's the only merchant who complains about being overpaid. She always has what I'm looking for, and often what I wasn't looking for yet. Fascinating.
textes.Nébula m'a vendu une boîte « qui ne cont: Nébula sold me a box “that contains nothing”. I opened it in front of her. It contained nothing! It was the first time anyone had sold me exactly what the label said. I paid double. It's in room two, with its label: “Honest box”.
Nébula sold me a box “that contains nothing”. Very expensive. I opened it. It contained nothing. She was telling the truth! It's the first time anyone's sold me exactly what it says.
textes.Nébula m'a vendu une « casserole d'en ba: Nébula sold me a “saucepan from down below” for the price of ten jellies. I used it right away. It was full of holes: it was a colander. I made pasta. It actually worked very well. I brought her ten jellies. She gave me back the price of one. We're even. I think.
textes.Nébula ne pose jamais de questions sur l: Nébula never asks where her goods come from. She winks at me, I wink at her. That's our contract. It isn't written down anywhere.
textes.Nébula tient le Bazar, de l'autre côté d: Nébula runs the Bazaar, on the other side of the fountain. We wave to each other over the jet of water. With four arms, I can say a lot of things. She never understands any of it. That's our way of chatting.
textes.Nébula vend des canards mécaniques de Cl: Nébula sells clockwork ducks from Cliquetis, postcards from Port-Azur and kaleidoscope glasses. When the Lumens ask her where they come from, she answers: “From very far away.” Then she looks at me. I look at the ceiling. The Bazaar's ceiling is very pretty.
textes.Nébula vend mes cristaux plus cher que m: Nébula sells my crystals for more than I do, wrapped in star paper. I say it's a rip-off. She says it's art. We argue on Thursdays and have dinner together on Fridays.
Nébula, I've… found a few bits and bobs.
textes.Nébula, tes prix ont encore monté !: Nébula, your prices have gone up again!
textes.Néferet ! Je peux sonner le sistre demai: Néferet! Can I shake the sistrum tomorrow?
textes.Néferet ! La meilleure élève que j'aie j: Néferet! The best pupil I ever had. She writes better than me, she sings better than me, and she corrects me in public. That last point, I forgive her for. Slowly.
textes.Néferet ! Ton chat dort toujours dans la: Néferet! Your cat is still asleep in the margin.
Néferet is the calmest of us all. She wears my robes, she blesses my looms, and she listens without judging. When Sennefer left, she came every evening. I haven't forgotten.
textes.Néferet sert Rê, le soleil des Égyptiens: Néferet serves Ra, the sun of the Egyptians, who travels by night in a boat. She is as calm as the water of a cenote. We see each other every year, at the fair of the longest day. I look forward to it.
textes.Néferet sert le soleil des Égyptiens. El: Néferet serves the sun of the Egyptians. She says it is reborn by itself, every morning, without the help of men. I disagree. But she says it so calmly that I sometimes doubt. Rarely.
textes.Néferet, c'est la prêtresse de Rê ! Elle: Néferet is the priestess of Rê! She greets the sun every morning, and she lets me shake the sistrum. She knows everything about the gods. And she never gets cross. Well, almost never.
textes.Néferet, c'est la prêtresse de Rê. Je la: Néferet is the priestess of Rê. I ferry her across to the other bank every day. She looks like she's asleep in my boat. She never sleeps. She hears everything. Watch out.
textes.Néferet. Moins de copal, cette année. Pr: Néferet. Less copal this year. I promise.
textes.Néferet. Ton soleil a bien traversé sa n: Néferet. Did your sun make it through the night?
textes.Néopolis compte environ quatre mille hab: Neopolis has about four thousand inhabitants and nine hundred androids. And one traveller. You.
textes.Néopolis est une ville formidable : il y: Neopolis is a wonderful city: there's a computer in every object! And so a customer in every object. Heh heh.
textes.Néopolis — la ville qui ne dort jamais :: Neopolis — the city that never sleeps: glass towers, neon lights, flying cars…
textes.Néopolis, au sud de l'archipel: Neopolis, in the south of the archipelago
textes.Néopolis, c'est une ville qui ne dort ja: Neopolis is a city that never sleeps. That suits me: at my age, you don't sleep much either.
textes.Néopolis, la ville qui ne dort jamais: Neopolis, the city that never sleeps

OCTAVE TAILLEFER
Tools & Weapons
No credit given!
textes.OH ! … C'est… c'est BLEU ! C'est TRÈS bl: OH! … It's… it's BLUE! It's VERY blue! And it moves! It's waving at me!
textes.OK, question importante : tu joues avec: OK, important question: do you play with the joypad or with the buttons?
textes.ON N'A PLUS D'AMPLI ! Les robots l'ont e: WE'VE GOT NO AMP! The robots took it to the Scrapyard! Without an amp, Germaine plays in a whisper! A whispered concert! IT'S A CATASTROPHE! … sorry.
textes.ONDELUNE — la planète des Lumens. Nuageu: ONDELUNE — the Lumens' planet. Cloudy, soft, without a single star visible in its sky. “We love it very much. From a distance.”
textes.OPTIMUS-LISSE : « ÉCHEC… DE… L'OPTI… MI…: OPTIMUS-LISSE: “FAIL… URE… OF… OPTI… MI… SA… TION… RETURN… TO… SLEEP… MODE…” The Great Digger slumps in a long hydraulic sigh (“pfffshhhhh”). On the screen, the red face turns into a little hourglass… then an all-blue screen.
textes.OUAF. OUAF. (Ses yeux clignotent de bonh: WOOF. WOOF. (His eyes blink with joy.)
textes.OUAIS ! Je le savais ! Tu as une tête à: YEAH! I knew it! You look like someone who makes the tiles rattle! Come to the Hall one night, I'll pass you the mic for a chorus.
textes.OUAIS ! MON GENRE ! VIENS À LA RÉGIE UN: YEAH! MY KIND OF PERSON! COME TO THE SOUND DESK ONE NIGHT, I'LL LET YOU TOUCH A KNOB! … Just one. The third one.
textes.OUGHA ! (Ça veut dire « super ».) Grok d: OUGHA! (That means “great”.) Grok say: Grosse-Dent roar before bite. And when Grosse-Dent charge and hit rock, Grosse-Dent see stars. Hit him then!
OOHOOHOO! … That was just to warm up.
textes.OUI ! ENFIN ! Quelqu'un qui comprend ! V: YES! AT LAST! Somebody who understands! Come to the Arena in the afternoon: you'll love it. Sit in the front row and shout with me!
textes.OUI ! Je le savais ! Tu as une âme de ma: YES! I knew it! You've got a magician's soul! I'll lend you Grommelot whenever you like. He's used to it.
textes.OUI ! Les boulons, c'est les meilleurs !: YES! Bolts are the best! They're long, they're proud, they hold everything together. You're on my team.
textes.OUI ! À cache-cache ! Avec Quark ! Mais: YES! Hide-and-seek! With Quark! But you seek, and we hide! Why? Because you have heavy feet, you make noise, we'll hear you coming, it's fairer! The rules: we hide in the city, wherever we like, but not in the planets of the fountain. That's Quark cheating. Not in the Spire either, Volt doesn't like it. You have to find both of us! Close your eyes and count to a thousand! ... Okay, to ten. Heavyfeet count too slowly.
textes.OYEZ ! L'Arène des Cornes, dans la Basse: HEAR YE! The Arena of Horns, in the Lower Town, to the south-east! Fights every afternoon! The stands are packed, the crowd roars, and I roar loudest of all! Free to get in, free to get out!
textes.OYEZ ! … Pardon. Dis-moi : tu aimes les: HEAR YE! … Sorry. Tell me: do you like news? Good news, bad news, funny news?
textes.OYEZ, OYEZ ! (C'est Mélusine, qui a tout: HEAR YE, HEAR YE! (It's Mélusine, who heard everything from the doorway.) … Well. All of Montjoie will know in three minutes. All the better! You are the Hero of Montjoie, and I want Bertrand to make a song about it. Without exaggerating. Well, a little. Here, the Guild's bounty. And come to dinner: Rissole made a pie. It won't be bubbling anymore.
textes.OYEZ, OYEZ ! UN NOUVEAU VISAGE À PANDÉMO: HEAR YE, HEAR YE! A NEW FACE IN PANDÉMONIA! … Sorry. Hello. Madame Hurla, town crier and mistress of the Arena of Horns. I cry the news in the morning and the fights in the afternoon. In the evening, I cry for the fun of it.
textes.OYEZ, OYEZ ! UN NOUVEL AVENTURIER EST AR: HEAR YE, HEAR YE! A NEW ADVENTURER HAS ARRIVED IN MONTJOIE! … That's you. Hello! Mélusine, town crier. News, announcements, ALERTS: that's me. (She shakes her big bell.) And this is Marguerite.
textes.OYEZ, OYEZ ! UN VISITEUR !: HEAR YE, HEAR YE! A VISITOR!
textes.Objet de quête : la Nuit des Lanternes: Quest item: the Night of Lanterns
textes.Objet de quête : la Pyramide de Rê: Quest item: the Pyramid of Ra
textes.Objet de quête : le Donjon des Mille Mar: Quest item: the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps
textes.Objet reçu. Analyse : gentil. Merci, {su: Item received. Analysis: kind. Thank you, {surnom}.
textes.Objet reçu. Classement : gentillesse. Me: Item received. Category: kindness. Thank you, {surnom}.
textes.Objet saisi : une écharpe cloutée. Objet: Item seized: one studded scarf. Item refuses to leave. Item is warm. Item retained.
textes.Objets trouvés, cabine trois : un parapl: Lost property, cabin three: an umbrella and Barnabé's courage.
textes.Obtenir la bourse de Jambe-de-Bois (paye: Get Jambe-de-Bois's purse (pay off his debt, or beat him in a fair duel), then bring it to Mama Grog, at the Crâne Fendu
textes.Occupée ! Trois caravanes cette semaine,: Busy! Three caravans this week, and a pirate who wanted a room “not too steady, so he'd feel at home”.
textes.Occupée ! Une réunion sur les voitures v: Busy! One meeting about flying cars, another about seagulls stealing noodles, and a third about meetings. I'm quite fond of meetings about meetings.
textes.Ocre a besoin d'un rouge plus rouge. Peu: Ocre need redder red. Maybe in volcano? … No. Too hot.
textes.Ocre peint. Ocre peint tout : Corne-Sur-: Ocre paint. Ocre paint everything: Horn-On-Nose, Long-Neck, sun, Grosse-Dent… But you… Ocre not know how paint you. You too round! You too smooth! Ocre only have squares!
textes.Octave ! Un mérou comme l'autre fois, ça: Octave! Fancy a grouper like last time?
textes.Octave ? Le meilleur charpentier du roya: Octave? The best carpenter in the kingdom and the worst helmsman on the ocean. Twenty-two years he's been sulking at me. Or I've been sulking at him. Nobody's quite sure any more.
textes.Octave Lunette regarde les étoiles, je r: Octave Lunette watches the stars, I watch the clouds, and we argue over who hides whom. Thirty years of letters. He's my best friend. I'll never tell him. He knows. He tells everyone.
textes.Octave dit que ses cabanes sont mieux qu: Octave says his huts are better than mine. The worst part is, he's right: he was a carpenter on a real three-master. But he never says it nicely.
textes.Octave gronde comme un orage d'été : bea: Octave rumbles like a summer storm: lots of noise, and afterwards everything is greener. His kapok tree loves him. Trees are rarely wrong.
textes.Octave m'achète du poisson toutes les se: Octave buys fish from me every week. He haggles over every sardine as if it were a gold bar. But he pays, always cash. As we say round here: a customer's a customer.
textes.Octave, le forgeron dans l'arbre, a un c: Octave, the blacksmith in the tree, has an elf's heart under his beard. Don't tell him: he'd hit you with his hammer.
textes.Octave, le forgeron dans l'arbre… Il gro: Octave, the blacksmith in the tree… He rumbles like a storm, but he strokes the bark of his kapok tree when he thinks nobody's looking.
textes.Octave… regrette ? Vraiment ? Hmm. Il m': Octave… regrets it? Really? Hmm. He did make me the finest fishing rod in the world, after all. Don't tell him I said that.
Odette says you have a rowing boat.
textes.Odette doit tenir le registre des bateau: Odette has to keep the register of boats. She's missing the names of Fernand's, Yannick's and Lucas's boats.
textes.Odette déjeune ici tous les midis, à la: Odette has lunch here every day, at the table looking out over the port. She counts the sailing boats while she eats. I count that she eats.
Odette wants the names of your boats.
Odette wants the name of your boat.
textes.Odette, c'est la capitaine du port. Elle: Odette's the harbourmaster. She sort of hates me, I think. I like her, though: she's as square as a ledger. One day I'll make her smile. I've still got a few seasons.
textes.Odette, c'est ma voisine et la femme de: Odette is my neighbour and my poor Marius's wife. She knows all my fibs, and she still saves me the best mooring. A saint, with a logbook.
textes.Odette. La femme de mon frère. Elle mont: Odette. My brother's wife. She climbs three hundred and twenty steps with a hot soup. She tells me off. I let her.
textes.Odile ! Combien de galettes, jeudi ?: Odile! How many galettes on Thursday?
textes.Odon ! Ma première marche, tu t'en souvi: Odon! My first step, do you remember?
textes.Odon a été dans le donjon, et moi non. I: Odon has been in the dungeon, and I haven't. He reminds me every time I tell a legend. He says the mimics pinch. He refused to check. So they bite. It's logical.
textes.Odon portait tout, dans notre équipe : l: Odon carried everything, in our team: the ropes, the lanterns, the packed lunch, and me when I fell. He's the heart of all my adventures. And the shoulders.
textes.Odon revend mes potions au pied des Croc: Odon resells my potions at the foot of the Fangs. He says they're needed more down there than up here. He also brings me the adventurers' observations. He's my best research assistant.
textes.Odon tient mon registre au Donjon des Mi: Odon keeps my register at the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps. A hundred times “floor 1, slipped”. He offered to write “very consistent” instead. He's the most tactful man on the island.
textes.Odon tient un petit carnet pour moi, à c: Odon keeps a little notebook for me, next to his register: the colour of adventurers when they come back up from the dungeon after drinking my potions. Green, blue, orange, spotted. He brings it to me every month. It's the largest study ever made on the side effects of my potions. I plan to publish it. The title: “The Weary Rainbow”.
textes.Odon, au donjon, dit que je me trompe su: Odon, at the dungeon, says I'm wrong about the fourth floor. He says mimics don't bite, they “pinch”. I told him to put his hand inside to check. He refused. I won.
textes.Odon, le gardien du donjon, revend mes p: Odon, the dungeon keeper, resells my potions at the foot of the Fangs. He says they're more needed down there than up here. It's true: nobody gets bitten by a chest on the Great Square.
textes.Offert sur ma terrasse !: On the house, on MY terrace!
textes.Officiellement, Astralys n'a jamais eu d: Officially, Astralys has never had any contact with the islands down below. Unofficially, half of Orbe's Museum comes out of my suitcases. He thinks those things just fall from the sky. I let him think so.
textes.Officiellement, la ligne du bas est ferm: Officially, the lower line is closed “for works”. Truth is, we're the ones doing the works. We're repainting the station. In colour. Lots of colour. Mistress Capucine pretends not to know anything. She's cooler than she looks.
textes.Offre de lancement : un appartement au L: Launch offer: a flat in the Lisse-Center, overlooking the car park! The car park overlooks another car park. It's very restful.
textes.Oh ! (Une petite étincelle de joie lui s: Oh! (A little spark of joy jumps out of her hat.) Sorry. It's the excitement. I'll lend you my favourites. They're a bit singed.
Oh! Then it's a magic stone.
textes.Oh ! Alors on peut regarder nos chaussur: Oh! Then we can look at our shoes together. It's more restful.
textes.Oh ! Alors viens au Cercle ce soir, aprè: Oh! Then come to the Circle tonight, after eight. You'll dance behind me, next to Grelot. She'll tread on your toes: that's her way of saying hello.
Oh! Careful, don't step on… Ah. It was a pebble. Hello!
textes.Oh ! Belle mousse ! … Et belle moustache: Oh! Lovely foam! … And a lovely chocolate mustache, too. Here, you earned it.
textes.Oh ! Bonjour ! (Elle fait une pirouette,: Oh! Hello! (She does a pirouette, and ribbons of light swirl around her.) Prisme, light dancer! When I dance, the light follows me. When I stop, it carries on a little, because it hasn't finished. Will you come and see me tonight? I dance on the Agora when the auroras arrive.
textes.Oh ! Bonjour ! Frère Linguini, novice du: Oh! Hello! Brother Linguini, novice of the temple, at your service! (He bows. His colander, far too big, slides down over his nose.) … Sorry. It's the right size; I'm just not its size yet. The Reverend says I'll grow into it.
textes.Oh ! Bonjour ! Je… je suis Sœur Pétronil: Oh! Hello! I… I'm Sister Pétronille, from the Temple of Dawn. I heal adventurers. Very well, actually. It's everything else that… (She trips over nothing.) … There. Everything else.
textes.Oh ! Bonjour ! Pardon, je ne vous avais: Oh! Hello! Sorry, I didn't see you, I was inside a crystal. In my head, I mean. Doctor Opaline Quartz, crystal-maker at the Workshop of Lights. I make the crystal lanterns of the Strata. All of them. Even the one on my head. Oh no, those are my glasses. I was looking for them.
textes.Oh ! Bonjour ! … Pardon, je vous ai fait: Oh! Hello! … Sorry, did I scare you? No, I'm the one who got scared.
textes.Oh ! Bonjour, bonjour ! Barthélemy, Baro: Oh! Hello, hello! Barthélemy, Baron of Montjoie. This hat? It's the Tuesday hat. … It's Thursday? Ah. Aurore will scold me. Charmed to meet you, young person!
textes.Oh ! Bonsoir… Monsieur Augustin est allé: Oh! Good evening… Mr Augustin has gone to bed. I'm minding the mill. With my eyes shut, but I'm minding it.
textes.Oh ! Celle-là penche un peu. Quel accide: Oh! This one leans a little. What an accident!
textes.Oh ! De la visite, à cette heure-ci ? Ta: Oh! A visitor, at this hour? All the better: I need someone to hold the umbrella's string.
textes.Oh ! Entre, entre, très cher ! Tiburce,: Oh! Come in, come in, my dear! Tiburce, horn polisher. Oil, shine, filing, and for special occasions, gold leaf. A horn is a crown you never take off: it must be looked after. You have no horns? What a pity. What a waste.
textes.Oh ! Euh… bonjour. Pardon. Je… je m'appe: Oh! Um… hello. Sorry. I… my name's Bruine. I play bass. It's the instrument you hear without hearing it. Like me.
textes.Oh ! Magique ! Sûrement ! Je t'en donne: Oh! Magic! Surely! I'll give you {prix} coins for it!
textes.Oh ! Merci, Ludovic. Où l'avais-je mis ?: Oh! Thank you, Ludovic. Where had I put it?
textes.Oh ! Merci, Nox. Il parle de quoi ?: Oh! Thank you, Nox. What's it about?
textes.Oh ! Merveilleux ! Alors elle te le rend: Oh! Wonderful! Then it'll love you back, you'll see. Magic loves those who wait for it. Here, take this pebble. It's surely magic.
textes.Oh ! Oh oh oh ! Tu viens d'en haut ?! Po: Oh! Oh oh oh! You come from up there?! For real?! I'm Ondine! Are clouds wet? Do trees talk? Do…
textes.Oh ! Pardon ! Je t'ai pas marché sur le: Oh! Sorry! Did I tread on your foot? No? Phew. Oscar. Apprentice. Third year. Well… third first year.
textes.Oh ! Pardon. Je ne vous avais pas vu. (I: Oh! Sorry. I didn't see you. (He stops tapping on a post.) Gédéon. Gédéon Lisse. The son. Of Lisse & Fils. The “Fils”, the Son, that's me. (He taps nervously on his tie: boom-tchak, boom-boom-tchak.) Sorry. It's nerves.
textes.Oh ! T'es en COULEURS ! Comment t'as fai: Oh! You're in COLOUR! How'd you do that? I'm Lili. Lili Pinceau. I'm nine. And a half. I'm looking for the yellow. The yellow of the sand, the yellow of the sun, the yellow of everything!
textes.Oh ! Toi ! Tu as quelque chose de magiqu: Oh! You! Have you got something magic?
textes.Oh ! Très cher ! Un petit lustre ?: Oh! My dear! A little shine?
textes.Oh ! Tu es des nôtres ! La pâte lève mie: Oh! You're one of us! The dough rises better, and so does the work. Teach me a song from your home, and I'll teach you the one about the turnip in love.
textes.Oh ! Tu es venu me voir chez moi ? Quell: Oh! You came to see me at home? What a nice surprise! Make yourself at home.
textes.Oh ! Tu es venu me voir dans ma yourte ?: Oh! You came to visit me in my yurt? Sit down on a pouf, I'll heat some water.
textes.Oh ! Tu triches ! Mais c'est une bonne t: Oh! You're cheating! But it's a good cheat. Gears are bolts that know how to dance.
textes.Oh ! Un Pied-Lourd ! Approche, approche,: Oh! A Heavy-Foot! Come closer, come closer, my little star, I don't bite: I've had no teeth since the ninth century. I'm Astrée, Elder of the Council. One thousand and forty-three years old. I know, I don't look it. I look at least a thousand and fifty.
textes.Oh ! Un auditeur ! Assieds-toi, je joue: Oh! A listener! Sit down, I'll play the “Ballad of Dawn”. It lasts three hours. Caelan Harpelune, at your service.
textes.Oh ! Un grand ! Tu as faim. Tout le mond: Oh! A tall one! You're hungry. Everyone's hungry. Dagna Soufflebraise, the cook. Sit down, eat, and don't say it's too hot.
textes.Oh ! Un humain, au Royaume des Racines !: Oh! A human, in the Kingdom of Roots! I'm Lumi, a root fairy. The spirits opened the door for you… so I'll be your guide!
textes.Oh ! Un nouveau ! Viens là, viens là, qu: Oh! A new face! Come here, come here, let me look at you. You're all skin and bones! I'm Mamma Lasagna. I make the pasta for the whole island, by hand, for forty years now. Mangia, mangia! Sit down, I'll bring you a plate. No, two.
textes.Oh ! Un nouvel objet ! Il a l'air un peu: Oh! A new item! It looks a bit shy. It'll get over it, everyone's nice here.
textes.Oh ! Un public ! Je répète pour la fête: Oh! An audience! I'm rehearsing for the neighborhood party. Want to hear my piece?
textes.Oh ! Un visiteur ! Bonjour, bonjour ! Zé: Oh! A visitor! Hello, hello! Zéphyrine Plume, mistress of air. Can you feel that little breeze? I invited it. It's staying for tea.
textes.Oh ! Un visiteur ! Pardon, je ne vous av: Oh! A visitor! Forgive me, I didn't hear you, I was listening to the sea. Professor Hippolyte Benthos, of the Institute of the Deep. I study everything that lives lower than your feet. And above all, I listen to the Great Singer. Have you heard her? No? Don't move. She may pass by. She likes newcomers.
textes.Oh ! Un visiteur ! Professeur Octave Lun: Oh! A visitor! Professor Octave Lunette, astronomer. Excuse me, I'm counting… three thousand four hundred and twelve, three thousand four hundred and… Drat. I'll start again. I'm used to it, I've been starting again every night for thirty years.
textes.Oh ! Un visiteur ! Tu as faim ? Tout le: Oh! A visitor! Are you hungry? Everyone's hungry. Sylwen Rayonmiel, baker. Try this.
textes.Oh ! Un visiteur ! Un vrai, avec des jam: Oh! A visitor! A real one, with legs and everything! Welcome to my humble shack, {surnom}. I'm Barnabé Coquillard, cartographer, castaway and collector.
textes.Oh ! Un visiteur, à cette heure-ci ? On: Oh! A visitor, at this hour? We're playing a game of dice. Would you like some herbal tea?
textes.Oh ! Un visiteur… et en couleurs ! Quell: Oh! A visitor… and in colour! What a joy to see some blue and red, after all this time. I'm Grand-Mère Aquarelle, the village elder. Welcome to the Tree-House Village. Well, what's left of it: everything has gone as grey as an old page.
textes.Oh ! Vous avez compris mon secret. Le pl: Oh! You've understood my secret. The most beautiful thing is not knowing yet. Don't tell the other scientists, they'd take away my title.
textes.Oh ! Vous cochez ! Je sens que nous allo: Oh! You tick things off! I sense we're going to get on very well. I'll give you my list templates. I have forty.
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau} ! En plein dans le: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}! Bang on target, {surnom}! Like one of Rivet's sticks on the cymbal!
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Je le poserai pr: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}! I'll put it by my window, where the light ripples.
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Mes antennes cli: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}! My antennae are blinking with joy! Look, they're making little stars!
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Par l'Aube, tu a: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}! By the Dawn, you hit the bullseye, {surnom}!
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Par la Colonne,: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}! By the Column, you hit the nail on the head, {surnom}!
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Par la Grande Pe: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}! By the Great Pearl, you hit the nail on the head, {surnom}!
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Par le Soleil de: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}! By the Brass Sun, you've hit the mark, {surnom}!
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Par les nuées, {: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}! By the clouds, {surnom}, you hit the mark!
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Par mes cornes…: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}! By my horns… you've read my heart, {surnom}!
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Pour moi ? Tu es: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}! For me? You're a sweetheart, {surnom}.
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau} ! Tu as tapé en pl: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}! You hit the nail right on the head, {surnom}! Like a stick on a snare drum!
textes.Oh ! {dernier_cadeau}, pour moi ? Tu es: Oh! {dernier_cadeau}, for me? You're a treasure, {surnom}. Gaston, look!
textes.Oh ? Qu'as-tu donc pour moi ?: Oh? So what have you got for me?
textes.Oh ? Tu n'as rien que tu puisses offrir,: Oh? Looks like you've nothing to give. Never mind: your visit is enough for me.
textes.Oh non ! Je ne peux pas foudroyer la gre: Oh no! I can't zap the frog… well, I can, but gently!
textes.Oh non ! Pardon, Gorgoth ! Il fait ses d: Oh no! Sorry, Gorgoth! He's teething!
textes.Oh non oh non oh non ! J'ai raté la poti: Oh no oh no oh no! I botched the beauty potion, and now… the master is a FROG! One ingredient is missing to reverse the spell. But which one?! Help me!
textes.Oh non, il va regarder les grands nuages: Oh no, he's going to look at the big clouds…
textes.Oh non. Il a été avalé. Je ne peux pas f: Oh no. He's been swallowed. I can't zap the frog: I'd zap him too.
Oh no. Nothing like it, sweetie.
textes.Oh oui ! J'ai écrit quatre cartes postal: Oh yes! I've written four postcards for people everyone talks about here: Barnabé, the old man of the jungle; Lyra, the elf; Ulfa, the dwarves' innkeeper; and… the queen of the sunken city, if she exists. You travel a lot. Would you mind delivering them?
textes.Oh oui, Boulon ! Ils t'attendent !: Oh yes, Boulon! They're waiting for you!
textes.Oh, bonjour ! Pardon, je file, j'ai douz: Oh, hello! Sorry, I must dash, I've got twelve beds to make. Well… two minutes, then.
textes.Oh, bonjour ! Selma. Je viens de Port-Az: Oh, hello! Selma. I've come from Port-Azur, with my brushes. They told me the light of Tazira was the most beautiful in the archipelago. They didn't lie.
textes.Oh, bonjour… Je suis Lune. Je tisse les: Oh, hello… I'm Lune. I weave the camp's cloth: the yurt walls, the rugs, the bags. With Galet's hemp. Do you want to see my loom? It sings a little when it works.
textes.Oh, de la visite ! Les chats adorent la: Oh, a visitor! Cats love visitors. Well… some of them.
textes.Oh, elles sont belles ! Tiens-les contre: Oh, they're beautiful! Hold them against you. Close your eyes. Don't think about going up: think about weighing nothing. … See? Your feet! They're not touching anything anymore! Now, the Leaning Tower: its bell hasn't rung since the great storm, the staircase collapsed. But you, you don't need a staircase anymore.
textes.Oh, merci ! Ça vient d'en haut ? Tout ce: Oh, thank you! Is it from up top? Everything from up top has a little taste of sky.
textes.Oh, merci, {surnom}. Ce n'est pas des pâ: Oh, thank you, {surnom}. It isn't pasta, but it's kind of you all the same.
textes.Oh, merci. C'est… analogique. J'aime bie: Oh, thank you. It's so… analogue. I like analogue things.
textes.Oh, merci. Je le poserai sur ma table de: Oh, thank you. I'll put it on my bedside table, next to my crow skull.
textes.Oh, merci… Tout ce qu'on donne finit par: Oh, thank you… Everything you give comes back around, you know. Like the seasons.
textes.Oh, mon petit, tu es tout maigre ! Mange: Oh, my dear, you're so skinny! Come on, eat something.
textes.Oh, oui ! La Nuit des Lanternes ! Il fau: Oh, yes! The Night of Lanterns! The seven Great Lanterns must be lit: the ones at the harbor, the market, the arena, the baths, the Academy, the Forge Cathedral and this one here, on the Main Square. Take my ember lantern: its flame never goes out. And ask Zigomar if his rockets are ready. After that… night falls, and we dance!
textes.Oh, oui, mon petit ! Je suis toute seule: Oh, yes, my little one! I'm all alone, Noisette has gone off following an adventurer, and I still have three loaves to deliver! One for Granny Rissole, at the Guild tavern. One for Aurore, at the castle, right at the top: without her bread, the Baron puts on his mourning hat. And one for Gilles, at the North Gate. If he's asleep, put it under his nose: he'll wake up. Here, here are the three. Don't eat them on the way! Well… not all of it.
textes.Oh, pas grand-chose. Un sourire, une bon: Oh, not much. A smile, some good news.
textes.Oh, qu'elles sont belles ! L'œil clair,: Oh, aren't they beautiful! Clear eyes, red gills… Perfect. Come back in three hours. No, I'm joking: I already had one on the fire.
textes.Oh, que c'est gentil ! La grosse pendule: Oh, how kind! The big clock, there, on the wall, stopped last night. The key's in her keyhole: three turns, not one more. She's ticklish.
textes.Oh, tu es blessé ! Un nectar, vite. Quat: Oh, you're hurt! A nectar, quick. Four hearts at once, that's my record.
textes.Oh, un Pied-Lourd ! Bienvenue ! Excuse l: Oh, a Heavyfoot! Welcome! Excuse the mess: I forgot to turn the gravity regulator back on again. Shall I turn it on?
textes.Oh, un grand ! Tu as des graines sur toi: Oh, a big one! Got any seeds on you? No? Shame. Welcome anyway!
textes.Oh, un impatient ! Comme tout le monde,: Oh, an impatient one! Like everyone here. At least blow on it. Your tongue will thank you.
textes.Oh, vous tombez bien ! Mon livreur s'est: Oh, perfect timing! My delivery boy sprained his ankle playing pétanque. This basket has to go to Paulo, to Gisèle at the café and to Edmond at the hotel. Would you mind?
textes.Oh, {surnom}. Tu viens perdre ? Euh, je: Oh, {surnom}. Come to lose? Er, I mean: to play?
textes.Oh, {surnom}… (Elle sourit, un tout peti: Oh, {surnom}… (She smiles, ever so slightly.) Hello.
textes.Oh. (Il arrête de tapoter.) Et… c'était: Oh. (He stops tapping.) And… what was it like, after? Good? Really good? I… I'll think about it. Thank you.
textes.Oh. Bonjour. (Elle referme son livre ; u: Oh. Hello. (She closes her book; a little spark jumps onto her nose.) … It happens. I'm Violette. Mage. Of lightning. Only lightning. I tried fire, once. That was lightning too.
textes.Oh. Bonjour. Pardon, je t'ai fait peur ?: Oh. Hello. Sorry, did I scare you? I scare everybody, because of my size. And the horns. And the voice. My name is Gorgoth. People say “Gorgoth the Horned”. I'm the champion of the Arena. But I prefer poems.
textes.Oh. D'accord. Alors je vous préviendrai: Oh. All right. Then I'll warn you before I fire. Promise. Twenty seconds before, I'll shout “look out”. That gives you time to close your eyes.
textes.Oh. Oui. (Bzzt.) … Ça arrive. J'ai lu qu: Oh. Yes. (Bzzt.) … It happens. I read something. In a book that Madame Olga lent me. At random. Storm crystals, at the top of the Fangs, drink lightning and send it straight ahead. Not at the hat. Not at the hair. Straight ahead. I'd need three. But if I go up there alone, the storm and I will fight over the lightning bolts. Would you please… ?
textes.Oh. Pardon, monsieur le mystérieux. Gast: Oh. Pardon me, Mister Mysterious. Gaston, we've got a mysterious one.
Oh. For me? It's… in perfect taste. I don't know what to say. Yes I do: thank you, {surnom}.
textes.Oh. Tu as trouvé. Bon… ne dis rien à per: Oh. You found it. Well… don't tell anyone.
textes.Oh. Vraiment ? (Une étincelle de joie lu: Oh. Really? (A spark of joy jumps out of her hat.) Sorry. Yes. I'm coming.
textes.Ohé ! Capitaine Charbonnel, maître du Po: Ahoy! Captain Charbonnel, master of the Ash Port! Sixty years at sea, three shipwrecks, two horns and a knee that creaks when the wind turns. Welcome to the Harbour, cabin boy. Here the sails are black and the hearts are red.
Ahoy! Captain Léon, at your service. The Swallow makes the crossing between Village Island and Port-Azur. Five coins one way, and the view is free!
textes.Ohé ! Tu as une épée maintenant ? Fais a: Ahoy! You've got a sword now? Careful where you point it, I've got sails to mend.
textes.Ohé ! Tu viens d'où ? T'as un bateau ? I: Ahoy! Where are you from? Got a boat? Is it big? Bigger than the Léviathan? No, huh. Nothing's bigger than the Léviathan. I'm Ewen, I'm the cabin boy. Future captain.
textes.Ohé, Octave ! Ta barbe a poussé : douze: Ahoy, Octave! Your beard has grown: twelve inches, at least.
textes.Ohé, la pilote du fond ! Toujours à l'en: Ahoy, deep-sea pilot! Still upside down?
textes.Ohé, moussaillon ! Bienvenue au Port des: Ahoy, cabin boy! Welcome to Seagull Harbour! Captain Isidore, harbour master. And this is Albertine, Bigorneau and Pompon. (Three seagulls stare at you.) They say hello. Well, Albertine says hello. Bigorneau says “fish”. Pompon says nothing, he's sulking.
textes.Ohé, terrien ! Capitaine Héloïse Nimbus,: Ahoy, landlubber! Captain Héloïse Nimbus, aeronaut, and this is the Albatross, the finest airship in the archipelago. Don't stare at it too long, it blushes. Well, it's already red. But it blushes on the inside.
textes.Ohé, terrien ! Tu as déjà vu un dirigeab: Ahoy, landlubber! Ever seen an airship up close?
textes.Ohé, visiteur ! Bienvenue à bord… enfin,: Ahoy, visitor! Welcome aboard… I mean, to my home. Same thing: it sways here too when the wind blows.
textes.Oh… Alors tu me comprends un peu. Tes la: Oh… Then you understand me a little. Your tears, they don't make dew? Shame. They should. It would only be fair.
textes.Oh… Alors vous savez déjà tout. Une fleu: Oh… Then you already know everything. A flower is a sentence you don't dare say. Come back and see me, I'll make you a bouquet that will speak for you.
textes.Oh… C'est comme ça qu'on faisait, avant,: Oh… That's how we used to do it, she and I. I should try to remember how to laugh.
textes.Oh… C'est exactement ce qu'on disait, el: Oh… That's exactly what she and I used to say, fifty years ago. You've got an old heart in a young body, you have.
textes.Oh… C'est la réponse la plus gentille qu: Oh… That's the kindest answer anyone's ever given me. I don't know why, my eyes are stinging. It's the dust. Fairy dust.
textes.Oh… C'est mon nom, tu sais. Merci. Ça me: Oh… That's almost my name, you know. Thank you. That makes me happy.
Oh… That's a very good question.
textes.Oh… Je voudrais bien. Mais vous n'êtes p: Oh… I'd love to. But you're not registered with the Guild. Églantine says we only go out with registered adventurers. She has a form for it.
textes.Oh… Mamie Kiku vous adorerait. Moi aussi: Oh… Mamie Kiku would adore you. So might I. I'll think about it.
textes.Oh… Merci de me le dire. Je me sens moin: Oh… Thank you for telling me. I feel less alone. Then we'll be scared together, and we'll keep going anyway. That's what courage is, isn't it?
textes.Oh… Merci. Mes circuits sont tout chauds: Oh… Thank you. My circuits are all warm. I'm going to paint this moment.
textes.Oh… Pétales et rosée. Bon. Une goutte de: Oh… Petals and dew. All right. You can't refuse a drop of nectar to a penniless traveller. One. A teeny one. Don't tell anyone, I have a reputation.
textes.Oh… Roux, tu as ta flûte ?: Oh… Roux, have you got your flute?
textes.Oh… Toi aussi ? Alors on se croisera sou: Oh… You too? Then we'll cross paths often. I'll show you the street lamps. Each one has a name. And a little voice, if you listen closely.
textes.Oh… Tu as un peu peur ? C'est pas grave: Oh… A bit scared? That's OK! I'll make you a calmer bridge. One that dances gently, like an old-timer. Promise!
textes.Oh… Tu es courageux. Moi, j'ai dû regard: Oh… You're brave. I had to look at your shoes to answer you. They're nice.
Oh… A human, here, in the heart of the trees. Don't be afraid: my name is Lyra Sylvanel, and I come from Bois-Doré, the island of the elves, on the other side of the mist.
textes.Oh… alors je vais rater. Vas-y quand mêm: Oh… then I'll get it wrong. Go on anyway.
textes.Oh… bonjour. Excusez-moi, j'ai les yeux: Oh… hello. Excuse me, my eyes are red. The sun. No, actually, it's not the sun.
textes.Oh… bonjour. Je suis Brindille. Je garde: Oh… hello. I'm Brindille. I look after the moon dew. Well… I used to. I lost it.
textes.Oh… bonjour. Je suis Lilas. Je danse au: Oh… hello. I'm Lilas. I dance at the Circle every night, for the moon. Come tonight, after eight. You'll see the fire, you'll hear the drums, and you'll want to dance. Everyone does.
textes.Oh… bonjour. Pardon, je regardais ce nua: Oh… hello. Sorry, I was looking at that cloud. It's the colour of a blushing peach. Ombeline, painter. I paint clouds and sunsets. I've painted a thousand. Not a single one was the same. Tonight's will be the thousand and first.
textes.Oh… bonjour. Parle doucement, s'il te pl: Oh… hello. Speak softly, please: the lettuces in tower number one have just woken up. Mélisande Varech, gardener of the Greenhouses. Welcome to my home. Here, everything grows under pink and violet lamps, at the bottom of the sea. It's surprising at first. The lettuces don't know it's strange.
textes.Oh… bonsoir. Je… je m'appelle Nox. J'all: Oh… good evening. I… my name is Nox. I light the street lamps. By day, I sleep. By night, I light. In between, I write a little. Sorry, I'm talking too much. Usually I don't talk at all.
textes.Oh… d'accord, Ferronde. Mais doucement,: Oh… all right, Ferronde. But gently, eh?
textes.Oh… dis-moi. Tu danses, toi ?: Oh… tell me. Do you dance?
textes.Oh… je le savais. Tu as les yeux de quel: Oh… I knew it. You've got the eyes of someone who's already seen something glow. Fairies like people like you.
textes.Oh… merci. Tu sais, beaucoup de gens pen: Oh… thank you. You know, lots of people think not. They see my horns and my arms, and they're scared. You saw something else. I'm going to write it in a poem.
textes.Oh… oh oh oh. C'est exactement ce qu'il: Oh… oh ho ho. That's exactly what I needed. How did you know?
textes.Oh… tu as remarqué. Là-bas, sous le peti: Oh… you noticed. Over there, under the little cloud, is an old friend of mine. Mother Downpour. We fell out fifty years ago, over something silly. I'd like to send her a bouquet of my sunflowers, to tell her I'm thinking of her. But I'm too proud to go myself. Would you be my messenger? Pick a bouquet in my garden, and take it to her.
Oh… a little. I lost some on the way.
Oh… {surnom}, I can tell you. I don't dance to Pépin's drum. I dance to Bourru's. The evening he had a cold, I couldn't find the step. And I dance more slowly on purpose, so he can keep up. He never says anything. Just “Hrmm”. I think he finds me silly.
textes.Olga est une sorcière qui a oublié presq: Olga is a witch who's forgotten almost everything she knew. But what she has left is worth every library there is. And her honey teas are perfect for a storyteller's voice.
textes.Omar ! Un rythme pour la dorade !: Omar! A rhythm for the sea bream!
textes.Omar a un tambour dans le ventre. L'aprè: Omar has a drum in his belly. In the afternoon, we rehearse on Mustapha's plates. Mustapha says it's good for business. The plates, less so.
textes.Omar frappe le tambour, Hamid joue l'oud: Omar beats the drum, Hamid plays the oud, and I hold the bass. The rest is up to the people: hands clapping, feet dancing.
Omar bangs on anything that doesn't move. And when he walks past my place, he bangs out my rhythm. My tac-tac. Without asking. You don't steal a rhythm, do you?
textes.Omar, c'est mon frère de rythme, depuis: Omar is my rhythm brother, ever since the north gate. He gives the camel's step, I give the wave. Without him, my guembri would walk crooked.
textes.Omar, c'est mon rythme. Chaque après-mid: Omar is my rhythm. Every afternoon he drums on my table, and the customers eat in time. I pay him in sardines. The best deal in Tazira.
textes.Ombeline ! Tu me peins la mer ?: Ombeline! Will you paint me the sea?
textes.Ombeline m'a appris : « On ne peint pas: Ombeline taught me: “You don't paint the sky. You listen to it, and you copy it out.”
textes.Ombeline peint le coucher de soleil au B: Ombeline paints the sunset at the Belvedere. She says it's never the same. Yesterday's was violet. I saw it!
textes.Ombreline garde la Bibliothèque des Âmes: Ombreline keeps the Library of Souls. She leaves the window open at night, with a candle, so I can borrow poems. She's never scolded me. I've never dared speak to her. Well, almost never.
Ombreline looks after the Library of Souls. She speaks very softly, she reads all the time, and she put up a sign just for me: “Here, we whisper. And we don't fly.” She's very kind. Very, very quiet.
textes.Ombreline m'a ouvert la porte des poèmes: Ombreline opened the door to poetry for me. Really: I couldn't fit through, she showed me how to duck. She speaks very softly, like me. We understand each other without making a sound.
textes.Ombreline… j'ai fini le recueil. Il y a: Ombreline… I've finished the collection. There's a flower in it.
textes.Ommm… (Il ouvre un œil.) Oh ! Un visiteu: Ommm… (He opens one eye.) Oh! A visitor. Welcome. I'm Mantra. I meditate. Well, I try. There's a frog looking at me, and it makes me laugh. Tee hee hee. Ommm…
textes.On a construit ensemble un château de sa: Together we built a sandcastle shaped like the temple. The sea ate it. Gnocchi said it was an offering. He's right.
textes.On a construit la scène de la Halle Hurl: The two of us built the stage of the Howling Hall. Me the planks, him the spotlights. To test it, I jumped on it for an hour while Fusible switched on every colour with each jump. Rouille walked in. She thought we were rehearsing a show. She applauded us.
textes.On a déjà discuté prix aujourd'hui. C'es: We've already talked prices today. It's settled.
textes.On a déjà joué au jeu des nombres aujour: We've already played the numbers game today, clever clogs. A Lumen forgets nothing. Nothing at all.
We already haggled today, you rascal.
textes.On a déjà marchandé aujourd'hui, petit m: We've already haggled today, clever clogs. Up here the air is light, but memories are heavy.
We've already haggled today, clever clogs. Down here, the rock has a long memory. So do I.
We've already haggled today, clever clogs. The walls here are made of glass: we see everything, and we remember everything.
We've already haggled today, smart aleck. I've got a memory like an elephant. An elephant with a mohawk.
We've already haggled today, clever clogs. I've got a cavern's memory: everything echoes in it for a long time.
We've already haggled today, smart aleck. I've got a receptionist's memory.
We've already haggled today, smarty-pants. My memory has more gears than you think.
We've already haggled today, smarty-pants. My tail remembers.
textes.On a déjà marchandé aujourd'hui. Demain,: We've already haggled today. Tomorrow, maybe, if the volcano's in a good mood.
We've already haggled today. Tomorrow, maybe.
textes.On a déjà marchandé aujourd'hui. Ma barb: We already haggled today. My beard remembers.
textes.On a fait la course d'escalade du Chêne-: We had a climbing race up the Mother Oak. He won. But he held on with his tail, I saw him! A squirrel's tail is like a third paw. I asked Pépin to cancel it. He said there's no rule about tails yet. “Yet”! He's thinking about it. I'm waiting.

We had the Mother Oak climbing race. I won! Myrtille shouted that I cheated with my tail. But a tail isn't cheating, it's a tail! She's got one too. A smaller one. Not my fault. Pépin said he'd think about a rule. He's still thinking.
textes.On a fait un concours de crachats d'étin: We had a spark-spitting contest on the Grand Square. Me, four paces. Ortie, five and a half paces. She measured with a piece of string. I asked for a rematch, and she said: “Numbers don't lie, Pépin.” So I showed her a glowing heart-shaped mushroom. She forgot about the contest.

We had a spark-spitting contest on the square. Pépin: four paces. Me: five and a half paces. I measured with a piece of string, it was scientific. Pépin asked for a rematch. Then he showed me a glowing heart-shaped mushroom, and I forgot about the rematch. Maybe it was a trick.
textes.On a fait un duo sur la Place des Palett: We did a double act on Pallet Square: her on bass, me on the unicycle juggling. On the third song, I fell into the bathtub fountain. I kept juggling, sitting in the water. Mouette didn't stop playing. The audience thought it was planned. We said it was planned.
textes.On a fait un numéro ensemble sur la Plac: We did an act together on the Pallet Square: me on bass, him juggling on his unicycle. On the third song, he fell into the bathtub fountain. He kept juggling, sitting in the water. The audience thought it was planned. We said it was planned.
textes.On a gagné ? On a gagné ! Merci, ô Aube: Did we win? We won! Thank you, O Dawn!
textes.On a gagné ? On a gagné ! Ô Aube, merci: Did we win? We won! O Dawn, thank you! And thank you! Especially you!
We won. I'm writing it in my journal. With the date.
textes.On a joué au jeu de balle, avec une cale: We played the ball game, with a gourd instead of the ball. Pilli made a magnificent hip shot. The gourd flew… and Tlaco caught it in his mouth and ran off. We chased him all the way to the end of the fair. He bites a bit, Tlaco. Just a bit.
textes.On a monté un numéro au Crâne Fendu : il: We put together an act at the Crâne Fendu: he plays faster and faster, and I throw on every note at a painted board. On the last note, the last knife. The whole room stamps its feet. The first time, we got it wrong: he finished before me, and I planted the last knife in total silence. It was even better.
textes.On a parlé fleurs pendant deux heures, d: We talked flowers for two hours, standing in her shop: grafts, lavenders, greenfly. Customers came in, waited, left. At the end, Rose told me she was the one who'd planted all the bougainvillea in town, twenty years ago. The only flowers I'd noticed here were hers.
textes.On a partagé une galette au bord d'un ru: We shared a flatbread by a stream. I asked him to show me the jaguars' tracks. He said no. He said they're hungry, and that you don't hunt to make a name for yourself. I said I already had a name. He said: “Then why do you hunt?” I'm still looking for the answer. It must be on the volcano.
textes.On a passé l'après-midi à regarder ses b: We spent the afternoon looking at her bolts one by one. She had a name for each. The oldest was called “Lady Ysolde.” The bravest, “the Bridge bolt.” Ressort had given her that one.
textes.On a pondu sur la grue de Boulon. Il fai: We laid eggs on Boulon's crane. He's very careful when he turns it. He's the best crane operator in the world. But the nest is MINE.
textes.On a réussi. (Elle sourit, une petite ét: We did it. (She smiles, a little spark on the tip of her nose.) Oh. Sorry. That's joy.
textes.On a réussi… Je peux reprendre ma lectur: We did it… May I go back to my reading?
textes.On a trois idées : démonter les ailes, d: We've got three ideas: take the wings off, take the wall down, or wait for the island to come down. The third one is the most restful.
textes.On a un club secret sous l'escalier de l: We have a secret club under the Grand Square staircase: the Free Imps Club. There are two members, Ortie and me. Ortie is president, vice-president and treasurer. I'm chief explorer. The club treasure is three coins and a button. We don't know where the button came from.
textes.On a voulu attraper le Roi des mares ave: We tried to catch the King of the Ponds with a mooncake. Mochi took one from the bakery, we put it at the end of the jetty, and we hid behind the crates. A duck came along. It ate the whole thing. Mochi says the duck was the dragon-fish in disguise. I say it was a duck.
textes.On a vu la Baleine Rouillée arriver sur: We saw the Rusty Whale wash up on the beach, a long time ago. It wasn't moving any more. We landed on it. It's OURS now.
textes.On a échangé : un boulon contre un bout: We swapped: a bolt for a bit of kite string. She wears the string on her wrist. I wear the bolt round my neck. She said we were “hardware sisters”.
textes.On avait huit ans. Moi avec ma boîte de: We were eight. Me with my three-string sardine tin, him with the neighbour's table, which he slapped with the flat of his hand. We played at the north gate for the caravans coming home. A caravan trader gave us a date. Just one, for the two of us. We cut it in half. That was our first wage.
textes.On avait vingt ans, c'était la Saint-Jea: We were twenty, it was Midsummer, the bonfire on the beach. I asked her to marry me, on my knees in the sand. She laughed and said: “The day a fish tells you yes.” She thought I'd give up. I've been asking for fifty years. The fish are hesitating.
textes.On boit le thé, lui et moi, le soir, dev: We drink tea, him and me, in the evening, outside his stall. We don't talk. One day I talked. About my father's forge. The northern port. The anvil. Not everything. A bit. He listened. He's a bit deaf. I think he heard it all anyway. He didn't repeat any of it. Hm. A good one.
textes.On compte ? Un, deux, trois…: Shall we count? One, two, three…
textes.On court ? On court ! ON COURT !: Shall we run? We run! WE RUN!
textes.On croit qu'on aime la pluie parce qu'on: People think we love the rain because we're sad. Not true. We love the rain because it brings everyone into the café. People squeeze together, they talk, they laugh. Rain is an excuse to be together. Don't repeat that, I've got a reputation.
textes.On croit que je gouverne Montjoie à la p: People think I run Montjoie in the Baron's place. Not true. I do the accounts, the post, the audiences, the repairs and the calendar. He knows everyone by name and makes people happy. That's the hardest part.
textes.On croit que je souris tout le temps par: People think I smile all the time because it's my job. That's true. But sometimes, when someone comes back from the dungeon in one piece, I smile for real. You can hardly tell. That's on purpose.
textes.On demande encore à Gaston ? Il va finir: Shall we ask Gaston again? It'll go to his head.
textes.On devient guerrier-jaguar après avoir c: You become a jaguar warrior after capturing four enemies. I captured five. The fifth was my cousin, during training. He still hasn't forgiven me.
It looks a bit like Triton.
textes.On dit qu'au cœur de la montagne dort un: They say that in the heart of the mountain sleeps a stone that beats like a heart. Nori knows. Nori always knows everything. It's annoying.
textes.On dit qu'au fond des Neuf Cercles, au C: They say that at the bottom of the Nine Circles, in the Cocytus, the cold makes horns crack. Crack! If you go down there, cover your head. And when you're back, come and see me: I've never polished frozen horns. It would be a first.
textes.On dit qu'il y a de la musique dans les: They say there's music down in the Strata, under our feet. Me, I mostly hear my knees.
textes.On dit qu'un humain a rapporté une Perle: They say a human brought back a Pearl of Light. Was it you?
textes.On dit qu'un poisson-lune doré nage au l: They say a golden sunfish swims out at sea. If you catch it, I'll buy it from you for a fortune. Barnabé will never have enough shells to pay for it, not him.
textes.On dit qu'une reine des fées t'a donné l: They say a fairy queen gave you the map. A fairy. Helping a tall one. To find dwarves. The world is changing.
textes.On dit que Barnabé a fermé les yeux pend: They say Barnabé kept his eyes shut all the way up in the cabin. I say he was asleep.
textes.On dit que Caelan et Ilyria se marieront: They say Caelan and Ilyria will marry before the next millennium. I'm betting on after.
textes.On dit que Mistral a appris à mixer avec: They say Mistral learnt to mix with shells and two coconuts. I believe it.
textes.On dit que Murmure, la discrète, chuchot: They say that Murmure, so discreet, whispers so low you barely hear a sound; one day she shouted “Peekaboo!”… and three domes lost their… ground. … Their glass. They lost their glass. That didn't rhyme.
textes.On dit que Spleen, au café, n'a jamais s: They say Spleen, at the café, has never smiled. Not true. He smiled once, in 1994. There was a heart-shaped puddle.
textes.On dit que dans la Tourmente, sous la ci: They say that in the Tempest, beneath the city, the wind blows in gusts, like music with no beat. Listen to it: there's always a silence between two gusts. That's when you move forward. In music, we call that a rest.
textes.On dit que dans les Neuf Cercles, sur le: They say that in the Nine Circles, on the Styx, there are flagstones lying on the water, and some of them sink. Me, I know water: when it bubbles underneath, it won't hold. Only step on the nice calm flagstones.
textes.On dit que je déteste le retard. C'est v: They say I hate lateness. It's true. But do you know why? A lost second can never be found again. So I'd rather we spent them together, on time. At least that way, we don't lose them alone.
textes.On dit que je n'ai jamais souri. C'est f: They say I've never smiled. Not true. I smiled once, in 1994. There was a heart-shaped puddle outside my door. I smiled. Then the sun came out, the puddle dried up, and that was that.
textes.On dit que je suis ronchon. Je ne suis p: People say I'm grumpy. I'm not grumpy. I'm demanding. The world is beneath my standards. Naturally: we're two hundred metres up.
textes.On dit que l'île flottante au-dessus de: They say the floating island above your village was put there by a giant child playing dice.
textes.On dit que l'île flotte grâce aux calcul: They say the island floats thanks to calculations and tea. The tea is my grandmother's doing. She used to say you never make a good decision with a dry mouth. She drank eleven cups a day. I drink twelve. I've overtaken her. She'd be proud. Or worried.
textes.On dit que le Capitaine Rigatoni a enter: They say Captain Rigatoni buried a treasure on the beach thirty years ago. He says he didn't. Then he winks. With the eye that has no eyepatch, luckily.
textes.On dit que le Roi Gélatineux, au fond du: They say the Jelly King, at the bottom of the dungeon, wears a little crown. A crown! On a slime! If you see it, tell me everything. The crown, the slime, the slime's face. Well, if it has a face.
textes.On dit que les cuisses de grenouille son: They say frog legs are delicious. I'm just saying it for science.
textes.On dit que les elfes ont une fleur qui n: They say the elves have a flower that only opens by moonlight. I'd give my whole garden to see one.
textes.On dit que sans toi, {qn} y serait encor: They say that without you, {qn} would still be stuck. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart.
textes.On dit que sans vous, {qn} y serait enco: They say that without you, {qn} would still be stuck. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart.
textes.On dit « Bon vent » ici. En bas, ils dis: Up here we say “Fair winds”. Down below, they say “Going up!”. We've already gone up. We're waiting for the wind to tell us what's next.
textes.On dit « Conseil des Marées », alors qu': We say “Tide Council”, even though at a hundred and forty metres there are no tides. Our founders wanted it that way: a good decision, they used to say, is like the tide. It rises slowly, and it always comes back. I try to decide like that. It takes time. It holds for a long time.
We'll take the wings off. Or the wall.
We already talked about that today.
textes.On en parle à l'Assemblée ?: Shall we bring it up at the Assembly?
We'll talk about it at the next Race.
textes.On entend des ronflements. Puis un siffl: You hear snoring. Then a whistle. Then more snoring.
textes.On entend un gloussement étouffé. Quelqu: You hear a muffled giggle. Someone is playing hide-and-seek… and is counting on you to seek.
textes.On est descendus de Hautefond, ma femme: We came down from Hautefond, my wife and I. In the glass tube, a ray swam right under our feet. My wife screamed. Then she wanted to go down again. To see it again.
textes.On est haut ! On est hauuut !: We're high up! We're so hiiigh!
textes.On fait du bruit ensemble, ce soir ?: Shall we make some noise together tonight?
textes.On fait la course au balai, aujourd'hui: Shall we have a broom race today?
textes.On fait la course jusqu'à la Plume ! … A: Race you to the Feather! … Oh no, it's in the water.
textes.On fait le tour de l'Esplanade trois foi: We go round the Esplanade three times after lunch. Digestion regulations.
textes.On fait un château ? Le plus grand du mo: Shall we build a castle? The biggest in the world?
textes.On frôle un cumulus ! Il est tout doux !: We're skimming a cumulus! It's so soft!
textes.On gratte, on ponce, on vernit : retour: Scrape, sand, varnish: back to the original wood. It has its charm.
textes.On grimpe ? Je connais un raccourci. Non: Shall we climb? I know a shortcut. No, I'm fibbing, there isn't a shortcut.
textes.On joue ? On joue ? On joue ?: Wanna play? Wanna play? Wanna play?
textes.On joue à « 1, 2, 3, Moaï » ? C'est simp: Shall we play “1, 2, 3, Moai”? It's simple: when you look at us, we don't move. We're statues, it's our job. But when you're not looking… we move closer! If we touch you, we win. If you last thirty seconds, you win.
textes.On l'a composée un jour de lessive : les: We composed it on washing day: the socks were beating time on the balcony line. One has been missing ever since. It went off on tour to the Floor.
textes.On l'a fait ! Je n'en reviens pas ! Je v: We did it! I can't believe it! I'm going to tell Father Clotaire. If he's awake.
textes.On m'a appris à peindre les codex : la p: I was taught to paint codices: deerskin folded like a screen, the colours, the little signs. My first drawing was a dog. It had six legs. I still don't know how. My master looked at it for a long time and said: “It's the dog of the Sixth Sun. It hasn't been born yet.” I kept it. It's still waiting.
textes.On m'a confié l'escalier de la falaise :: They put me in charge of the cliff staircase: four hundred and twelve steps, from the harbour to the city. I climbed them every day counting out loud, so as not to look down. Twenty years. For the last six, my niece Écrou climbed them with me. She was nine when she arrived, with her pockets full of screwdrivers. We sang the hundreds. The third was the hardest.
textes.On m'a dit qu'au Dôme d'Azur, au fond de: I've heard that in the Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea, the light is blue all day, and you see the sun as a patch dancing on the surface. I want to paint it. When the line reopens, I'll go down with blue. Lots of blue.
textes.On m'a dit qu'une perle bleue, qui brill: I was told a blue pearl that glows all by itself exists somewhere under the sea. I'd give anything to see one.
textes.On m'a dit qu'à la Cité des Nuées, ils o: I've heard that in the City of Clouds they have trees growing in thin air, hanging on to nothing. I feel sorry for their roots. When the line reopens, I'll go up and talk to them. They must need a bit of soil. And a bit of conversation.
textes.On m'a dit que Titou faisait « le phoque: I heard Titou was doing “the elegant seal” on the village square. I went along, very dignified, in my beanie. The kids were clapping like flippers. He'd forgotten the whole shoulder move. I went back the next day to show him. I stayed an hour. The kids applauded me. That doesn't mean I forgive him.
textes.On m'a dit que tu avais offert {objet} à: I'm told you gave {objet} to {qn}. Each to their own company.
textes.On m'a dit que vous aviez offert {objet}: I'm told you gave {objet} to {qn}. Each to their own company.
textes.On m'a dit que {qn} t'avait parlé de moi: I was told {qn} had told you about me. Small world.
textes.On m'a dit que {qn} vous avait parlé de: I was told {qn} had told you about me. Small world.
