textes.On m'a mise au récurage des canons. Cinq: They put me on cannon scrubbing. Five years polishing bronze, learning powder, wedge and elevation. Then the old gunner retired and handed me the battery. Master gunner! Sixteen cannons, and Bertha, the oldest, the most stubborn, with a voice to wake the dead. I shine her every morning. She pays me back nicely.
textes.On m'a proposé cent fois de me remplacer: They've offered a hundred times to replace me with a newer robot. The mayor always said no. She says the square wouldn't be the same without me. I think she's right: I'm the only one who waters the cherry trees while singing.
textes.On m'a proposé un implant pour travaille: I was offered an implant to work faster. I refused. A mayor must stay at the speed of her citizens. Especially Mamie Kiku.
textes.On m'a raconté qu'à Montjoie, il y a des: I've been told that in Montjoie, there are turnips that run away. I've been told. I didn't chase them across a field with an old farmer. That wasn't me.
textes.On m'a élue présidente du Conseil parce: They elected me President of the Council because I was the only one who never shouted. I cried, it's true, but quietly. Augustin says it's a very good quality for presiding: people let you speak so that you'll stop.
They call me Belle-Humeur to mock me. The last one who mocked me to my face is still swimming. Towards America.
textes.On m'appelle Chaussette parce qu'à dix a: They call me Chaussette — “Sock” — because when I was ten, I followed a dog that had stolen a sock all the way to the other side of town. I came home that evening with the sock, the dog and three more dogs that had tagged along. My parents said: “Never again.” I said: “OK.” I lied.
textes.On m'appelle Sergent, mais je n'ai jamai: They call me Sergeant, but I was never a sergeant. When I was little, I shouted announcements in the schoolyard through a funnel. “Attention! It's playtime!” The nickname stuck. Fréquence I added later. For credibility.
textes.On m'appelle Sirène parce que j'ai été m: They call me Sirène because I was a lifeguard on a beach at Port-Azur. Except I can't swim. I watched very, very carefully. Nobody ever drowned. I think it was the stare.
textes.On m'appelle bourru. C'est faux. Je suis: People call me grumpy. Wrong. I'm precise. I say “hm” when things are fine, “hmm” when they're not, and “hmmm” when Héloïse flies her airship over my harbour. Everybody understands.
textes.On m'appelle l'Amirale. Je n'ai jamais c: They call me the Admiral. I've never commanded a single ship that floats. Corentin finds that funny. I don't.
textes.On m'appelle « Père » Bastien, mais je n: They call me “Old” Bastien, but I've no children. Just two hundred and forty trees. They're very well behaved. They never talk back, they grow quietly, and they feed me now I'm old. What more could I ask?
textes.On m'appelle « l'homme bleu », à cause d: They call me “the blue man”, because of my chèche. The indigo rubs off on the skin. In the desert, they say the sky has marked us.
textes.On m'avait dit qu'au Dôme d'Azur, au fon: I'd been told that in the Azure Dome, at the bottom of the sea, the light is blue all day long. It's true. The line has reopened, and I went down with blue paint. Forty tubes. I came back up crying out for violet: down there, in the evening, their sun is a pearl that turns violet.
textes.On m'avait dit qu'à la Cité des Nuées, l: I was told that in the City of Clouds, trees grew in thin air. The line has reopened, so I went up to talk to them. They have soil, actually, and a gardener, Flora, who keeps them company. She gave me a strawberry the size of my fist.
textes.On m'avait dit que les horloges de la Ci: I was told the clocks in the City of Clouds were made of glass. I went up for the reopening, with my screwdriver. Not a single one! But the inventor up there is making me one. I'm going back soon. Just to look. Maybe to adjust it.
textes.On me demande toujours lequel est le plu: People always ask me which one is the most beautiful, {surnom}. I answer: “The next one.” It's not a dodge. It's that if I knew the most beautiful was behind me, I'd no longer want to look up. So I save the most beautiful for tonight. Every night.
textes.On me rapporte parfois de l'obsidienne,: Sometimes people bring me obsidian, from the volcanoes. I sell it to her. She weighs it, turns it to the light, pays the fair price, not a penny more. I forge her setting prongs, tiny ones. She says they're as fine as dwarven work. Best compliment I ever got. Don't repeat that.
textes.On me trouve pince-sans-rire. C'est faux: People find me deadpan. That's not true: I laugh a lot. On the inside. Like the rock: you think it doesn't move, and it shifts a finger's width per century. I smile a millimetre a year. This year, I'm up to two.
textes.On met les chaussettes AVANT le pantalon: You put socks on BEFORE your trousers!
textes.On monte ici chaque soir depuis trente a: We've been coming up here every evening for thirty years. The sky has never repeated itself.
textes.On monte par la cabine, puis par la caps: Up in the cabin, then up in the capsule… I'm going to need a big hot chocolate.
We haven't said what for yet.
textes.On n'a pas fini, toi et moi !: We're not done, you and me!
textes.On n'a toujours pas trouvé de trésor, to: We still haven't found a treasure, you and me. But I've got a new spoon. A bigger one.
textes.On n'est jamais quittes. C'est ça, l'ami: We're never even. That's what friendship is.
textes.On n'est pas des rats d'égout, nous. On: We're not sewer rats, you know. We're HOLD rats.
You don't forget to breathe, Gorgoth.
textes.On ne brille jamais trop !: You can never shine too much!
textes.On ne casse pas ce qui n'est pas à soi !: You don't break what isn't yours!
textes.On ne joue pas avec la nourriture !: We don't play with our food!
textes.On ne l'appelle pas : on va le chercher: You don't call him: you go and get him!
textes.On ne parle pas trop fort près de la meu: We don't talk too loud near the millstone: it sings, and you have to listen.
You don't paint a paintbrush, Lili.
textes.On ne se connaît pas, je crois. Tu es qu: I don't think we've met. Who are you?
We don't heal, we grit our teeth.
textes.On ne va pas recommencer, Aurore !: Let's not start that again, Aurore!
textes.On passe par la taverne ? J'ai une faim: Shall we stop by the tavern? I'm as hungry as a dragon. A big dragon. Not Master Hugues's.
textes.On passe à la boulangerie ? Honorine fai: Shall we stop by the bakery? Honorine makes croissants so hot you can hear them sing.
textes.On peut passer les examens de l'Académie: Can we take the Academy exams?
textes.On peut. On ne devrait pas. Mais le Masq: We can. We shouldn't. But the Jade Mask of our kings is down there, ever since the Lords took it, and without it Kinich Ahau, our sun, rises without a face. The temple door opens only on the date when the gods created the world. Ah Kin, the astronomer, knows it; so does the great stela in the square. Then… remember the Twins. They outwitted every trial.
textes.On pourrait le sortir par la baie. En bi: We could get it out through the big window. Sideways.
textes.On raconte au Bois-Doré qu'un grand serp: In Bois-Doré they say a great serpent slept beneath your islands. I didn't believe it.
textes.On raconte qu'un aigle géant vit sur l'î: They say a giant eagle lives on the dwarves' island, and that an island floats above the clouds. I'd pay its weight in gold for one of that eagle's feathers. Literally.
textes.On raconte qu'un poisson-lune doré rôde: They say a golden sunfish lurks out at sea, where the water is deepest. Nobody has ever landed it. Except maybe you, one day?
textes.On raconte qu'une baleine tourne autour: They say a whale circles the city. I've never seen it. I'm on duty.
textes.On raconte qu'une grenouille s'est insta: They say a frog settled on my head while I was meditating. It's true. She stayed two days. We became friends. Her name is Bernard, for old times' sake.
textes.On raconte que Mantra a médité trois jou: They say Mantra meditated for three days without moving, at the edge of the pond. A frog ended up settling on his head. He didn't notice.
textes.On raconte que tu as frappé {qn}. Ici, o: They say you hit {qn}. That's not how we settle things around here.
textes.On raconte que tu as offert {objet} à {q: They say you gave {objet} to {qn}. Bad luck: that's the one thing {il} can't bear.
textes.On raconte que vous avez frappé {qn}. Ic: They say you hit {qn}. That's not how we settle things around here.
textes.On raconte que vous avez offert {objet}: They say you gave {objet} to {qn}. Bad luck: that's the one thing {il} can't bear.
textes.On ralentit un peu… Juste un peu. Clou l: Let's slow down a bit… Just a bit. Clou wrote this one all by himself. He never told anyone. “Germaine, My Sweet”.
textes.On recommence le concours ?: Shall we have the contest again?
textes.On redescend ! Prochain arrêt : le Belvé: Going back down! Next stop: the Belvedere of the Great Column.
textes.On regarde nos chaussures ? Les miennes: Shall we look at our shoes? Mine are doing fine. And yours?
textes.On remonte ! Prochain arrêt : Hautefond,: Going back up! Next stop: Hautefond, Column Square.
textes.On remonte ! Prochain arrêt : les Strate: Going back up! Next stop: the Strata, the Station.
textes.On répare ensemble, aujourd'hui ?: Shall we fix things together today?
textes.On s'assoit devant ou derrière ?: Shall we sit at the front or the back?
textes.On s'envole pas, on fait une pause aérie: We're not flying away, we're taking an aerial break.
textes.On s'est assis près d'un ruisseau, lui e: We sat down by a stream, him and me. He wanted me to show him the jaguars' tracks, to hunt them. I said no. He said they'd taken one of Xóchitl's animals. I said they were hungry. We didn't understand each other. We shared my flatbread anyway. He eats fast. Like a jaguar.
textes.On s'est disputées une fois pour un coqu: We fell out once over a poppy. We shared it. It didn't survive, but our friendship did.
textes.On s'est rencontrées au phare tagué, un: We met at the graffitied lighthouse, one rainy evening. She'd been sticking eviction notices on upside down, on purpose. I offered her a violet lemonade. She cried, then laughed. Since then, every Thursday, we meet there. We swap cordial recipes. And news of the Bilge Rats.
textes.On s'est rencontrés pour une brouette. P: We met over a wheelbarrow. Then a workbench, a shelf, a bike, a house. One day, Copeau brought me a ring carved from a piece of oak. He said nothing. I whistled three notes: dinner's ready. He understood yes. We got married the next month.
You'll get used to it, you'll see.
textes.On se dispute tous les soirs pour savoir: Every evening, we argue about who's seen the biggest sardine. He spreads his arms this wide. I spread mine even wider. Him, wider still. Hic! In the end, our arms are spread so wide we knock over the neighbours' glasses. The next day, we start again. That's what you call an old friendship.
textes.On se dispute ça depuis cent ans. Et je: We've been arguing about this for a hundred years. And I'm winning.
textes.On sort tous ensemble, avant l'aube, par: We all go out together, before dawn, through the channel between the two lighthouses. Green on the left, red on the right. My father taught me, and his father taught him.
textes.On surveille les moteurs nuit et jour. L: We watch over the engines night and day. At night, they purr more softly. Like us.
textes.On t'a pas appris à saluer, terrien ?: Didn't anyone teach you to say hello, landlubber?
textes.On t'appelle Gros-Louis parce que tu es: Do they call you Gros-Louis because you're fat?
textes.On trinque quand même ?: Shall we drink to it anyway?
textes.On va voir si tu cognes aussi bien que t: Let's see if you hit as well as you talk!
textes.On va voir ça. Tape sur la table, là. Bo: We'll see about that. Tap on the table, there. Boom, ta-ka… Not bad! A bit rushed, but not bad. You drum like a fisherman who wants to get home for lunch.
textes.On va voter pour choisir le nom du nouve: We're going to vote to pick the new cloud's name. I'm suggesting “Sugar Puff”.
textes.On va écouter le silence, ce soir ?: Shall we go and listen to the silence tonight?
textes.On veille sur vous, ici, {surnom}. Vous: We look out for you here, {surnom}. Can you feel it?
textes.On verra au feu, Dwalin. Le feu ne ment: We'll see in the fire, Dwalin. Fire doesn't lie.
We'll see which way the wind blows.
textes.On verse de haut, comme ça…: You pour from high up, like this…
textes.On vient ici chaque dimanche. Aujourd'hu: We come here every Sunday. Today's Tuesday. But it was far too nice to wait.
textes.On voit bien les étoiles, d'ici ?: Can you see the stars well from here?
textes.On voit quoi, la nuit ?: What can you see at night?
textes.On y essaie les ailes des planeurs d'Ica: We test the wings of Icare's gliders in it, the propellers of Mireille's umbrellas, and sometimes hats. In the wind tunnel, the wind always blows the same way. It's restful.
textes.On était quatre : moi qui frappais, Odon: There were four of us: me who did the hitting, Odon who carried everything, an archer called Sidonie and a mage who only spoke in rhymes. We crossed mountains, defeated a troll, and lost the mage at a rhyme fair. He stayed there, he was happy there. Odon and I came home. We're still arguing about the way back.
textes.On était tout petits, à la porte du nord: We were tiny, at the north gate. He'd made himself a guembri from one of Mustapha's sardine tins and three bits of string. It smelled of fish with every note. The neighbourhood cats came to listen. Our first audience was cats. They didn't pay, but they stayed till the end.
Shore it up first, then we talk.
Ondine! Put that offcut of mother-of-pearl back.
textes.Ondine ! Tu as encore mouillé ta robe da: Ondine! Did you get your dress wet in the canal again?
textes.Ondine ! Tu as rangé le rouleau du blé ?: Ondine! Did you put the wheat scroll away?
textes.Ondine a dessiné un « arbre » d'après ta: Ondine drew a “tree” from your description. It looks like an angry octopus.
textes.Ondine est la seule de mes sujets à me d: Ondine is the only one of my subjects who asks if I've ever skinned my knees. Yes. Falling out of a fig tree, a thousand years ago.
textes.Ondine me vole mes chutes de nacre et me: Ondine steals my mother-of-pearl offcuts and asks me forty questions an hour. I pretend to grumble. She's my best customer: she never pays, but she always comes back.
textes.Ondine pose les questions que j'aurais d: Ondine asks the questions I should have asked a thousand years ago. She'll make a wonderful archivist, the day she learns to sit still.
textes.Ondine pose mille questions sur la surfa: Ondine asks a thousand questions about the surface. Answer her kindly, will you? She has never seen the sun.
textes.Ondine vient me voir tous les jours. Ell: Ondine comes to see me every day. She asks more questions than a shark has teeth, and she asks them better. She'd make an excellent guard.
textes.Ondine, c'est ma perle à moi. Trop de qu: Ondine is my very own pearl. Too many questions and not enough sleep. I wouldn't change her for the world. Everything is calm under the sea, except my daughter.
textes.Ondine. Elle parle pour nous deux. Pour: Ondine. She talks for both of us. For all three of us, even, with her mother. Me, I find it restful.
Eleven times an hour, Sir. Well done.
textes.Onze heures, Borin. Tu passais par hasar: Eleven o'clock, Borin. Just passing by?
textes.Onze l'an dernier ! J'ai progressé !: It was eleven last year! I've improved!
textes.Onze minutes… comme une chute ?: Eleven minutes… with a punchline at the end?
textes.Onze prototypes. Onze moteurs perpétuels: Eleven prototypes. Eleven perpetual motion engines. They all stopped, and Madame Bricolette bought them all for her window. The twelfth, I built with the golden gear: it ran for eleven years. Eleven years! I show it at every Fair. Never won a prize. The jury says we have to wait and see if it stops. I say the jury lacks patience.
textes.Oooh ! Une nouvelle espèce ! Ah non. Bon: Oooh! A new species! Oh no. Hello!
textes.Oooh ! Une nouvelle espèce ! … Ah non, u: Oooh! A new species! … Oh no, a Heavy-Foot. Sorry. Force of habit. Nova, zoologist of the Greenhouse of Species! I look after the creatures of the sky: sky jellyfish, gurgles, comet-butterflies… All peaceful, all adorable, and all a bit weird. Like us.
textes.Ooooh ! Tu m'as trouvé ! Personne ne me: Oooh! You found me! Nobody ever finds me! Here, it's my treasure. Well, one of my treasures.
textes.Ooooh, un visiteur ! Ça faisait mille an: Ooooh, a visitor! It's been a thousand years since anyone woke the basin. I am the Echo, the voice of the stones. The five Singing Stones have forgotten their songs… I sing, you repeat: you touch the stones in the same order as me. Okay?
textes.Opaline ! Tu as encore oublié de compter: Opaline! Did you forget to count again?
textes.Opaline prétend que ses cristaux brillen: Opaline claims her crystals shine brighter than my mushrooms. It's not true. Her crystals are cold and perfect. My mushrooms are alive and a bit crooked. I prefer mine. She still comes and sits by my pond every evening.
textes.Opaline, de l'Atelier des Lumières, me f: Opaline, from the Workshop of Lights, makes me little crystal lamps to light the Wall. In exchange, I paint stars on her lampshades. Strata folk say it's “too colourful”. Then they buy every lampshade.
textes.Opaline, de l'Atelier des Lumières, tail: Opaline, from the Workshop of Lights, cuts the Strata's crystals. She gives me the powder that falls from her workbench. On the rock, it glows in the dark. Thanks to her, the Wall lights up at night.
textes.OpenXR absent. Relance en activant Meta: OpenXR missing. Restart with Meta Quest Link or SteamVR turned on.
textes.OpenXR non connecté. Entre d'abord dans: OpenXR not connected. First enter Quest Link on the headset, then press R.
textes.Optimiser… J'ai cherché le mot dans le d: Optimise… I looked the word up in the dictionary yesterday. It means “make as good as possible”. I think I've been using it wrong for thirty years.
textes.Optimiste, comme toujours. Mes robots on: Optimistic, as always. My robots repainted three walls grey last night. This morning, they all had flowers on them. I don't know how she does it. It's very inefficient. And very fast.
textes.Orbe ! J'ai reçu une chaussette d'en bas: Orbe! I've received a sock from down below.
textes.Orbe ! Je photographie ta botte ?: Orbe! Can I photograph your boot?
textes.Orbe achète tout ce qui vient d'en bas,: Orbe buys everything that comes from down below, at any price. I tell him it's too much. He insists. He weeps with joy over a boot. I've never had a customer so happy to be robbed. I don't rob him. Hardly at all.
textes.Orbe collectionne les objets, moi les ph: Orbe collects objects, I collect photos. We're both collectors. He says I'm the most interesting exhibit of the Museum that isn't in the Museum. I think that's nice.
textes.Orbe croit que les objets d'en bas tombe: Orbe believes things from down below fall from the sky. I let him believe it. Half of his Museum comes out of my suitcases. When he cries with joy over a boot, I'm the happiest ambassador there is.
textes.Orbe et moi, nous avons déroulé ma carte: Orbe and I unrolled my map in the Museum, just to see. Thirty metres. It spilled out of room two into room one, then into the entrance, then onto the Agora. Lumens were walking on it to get to the café. I shouted. Orbe handed out slippers to everyone. It lasted a whole day. It was magnificent.
textes.Orbe m'a acheté une vieille botte pour l: Orbe bought an old boot from me for the price of three astral crystals. I told him it was far too much. He answered: “It's a boot that has walked on the Earth!” I told him all boots had walked on the Earth. He looked at me as if I'd just given him a treasure.
textes.Orbe m'a demandé de poser pour une étiqu: Orbe asked me to pose for a Museum label: “Gelatinous tourist, visiting”. I posed for an hour without wobbling. He took notes on me from every angle. At the end, I asked if I could photograph him. He posed with his old boot. It's mum's favourite photo.
textes.Orbe m'a demandé pourquoi je ne finissai: Orbe asked me why I never finish my map. I explained the little bit in the south, and that if I drew it, the map would be finished. He showed me an empty display case, at the back of the Museum. He said: “I don't fill it either.” We stood in front of it for a long time, without speaking.
textes.Orbe m'a demandé un jour : « Solenne, to: Orbe once asked me: “Solenne, you who never go down, what on earth could a colander be for?” I answered without thinking: “For draining pasta.” He looked at me for a very long time. I added: “I read it in a book.” He wrote it down. He never asked me anything else.
textes.Orbe veut exposer ma carte au Musée. Ell: Orbe wants to display my map in the Museum. It isn't finished. There's a little bit missing, in the south. Orbe is keeping an empty room for it. He understands why I don't finish it. It's rare, someone who understands that.
textes.Orbe, cette grande vitrine est presque v: Orbe, this big display case is almost empty
Orbe, this big display case is almost empty…
textes.Orbe, du Musée, a payé une vieille botte: Orbe, from the Museum, paid three times the price of an astral crystal for an old boot. I told him it was too much. He insisted. He said it was “a boot that walked on the Earth”. Every boot has walked on the Earth, Orbe!
textes.Orbe, j'ai vu une chose tomber du ciel,: Orbe, I saw something fall from the sky last night.
textes.Orbe, l'Archiviste du Musée des Mondes,: Orbe, the Archivist of the Museum of Worlds, wants to complete the great display case of the islands down below: a seashell from the sea of Port-Azur, a parrot feather from Balafre, a scarab from the Island of the Three Suns, a Bilge Rats patch from Boucan Island and a golden turnip from Montjoie.
textes.Organiser un jour, sur la Place des Roua: To organise, one day, on Cogwheel Square, a great festival of the four worlds, now that all the Lines are open. The Clouds, Hautefond, the Strata, the Azure Dome, and the Fronde playing the music. And for once, to give a speech. A long one. Three sentences.

To organise, one day, on Cogwheel Square, a great festival of the four worlds, when all the Lines are open. The Clouds, Hautefond, the Strata, the Azure Dome, and the Fronde playing the music. And for once, to give a speech. A long one. Three sentences.
textes.Organisée. J'ai étiqueté tous mes sirops: Organised. I've labelled all my syrups: mint, strawberry, elderflower, violet, and “mystery”, which is a mix of the bottoms of the bottles. It's the most popular one.
textes.Ori ! Note : « Le roi est d'humeur royal: Ori! Write: “The king is in a royal mood.”
textes.Ori a de bons yeux, une belle écriture e: Ori has good eyes, fine handwriting and the patience of a stalactite. He'll be the next keeper of the runes. He doesn't know it yet. The runes do.
textes.Ori a écrit ta loi : « Personne ne dort: Ori has written your law: “Nobody sleeps far from the fire.” Grimli still sleeps in his mine. You can't win them all.
textes.Ori tient la chronique des quarante-deux: Ori keeps the chronicle of the forty-two kings. I asked him what he'd written about me. He read: “Thorgal, forty-second of the name, loses his crown, never his people.” I pretended to cough. I coughed for a long time. He waited, without looking up, until I'd finished.
textes.Ori tient mes registres mieux que moi. I: Ori keeps my ledgers better than I do. He writes small, he doesn't smudge and he doesn't ask for money. He asks for “thank yous”. I give him some. They don't cost anything.
textes.Ori écrit mes rapports. Il me fait répét: Ori writes up my reports. He makes me repeat every golem three times and asks me the colour of the sky. Nobody has ever needed the colour of the sky. He does.
textes.Ori écrit tous mes décrets. Il corrige m: Ori writes all my decrees. He corrects my mistakes, adds commas and removes the words that are too royal. He's probably right. It's annoying, in a scribe.
textes.Ori. Deux golems, pente noire, rien d'au: Ori. Two golems, black slope, nothing else.
textes.Oriane m'a dit que la musique de Mistral: Oriane told me Mistral's music rises all the way to her kingdom when the wind blows the right way. One night, up there, I saw the queen tapping her foot. Very softly, under her gown, right on the kick. She saw that I'd seen. She put a finger to her lips. I haven't told anyone. Except you.
textes.Original ! C'est exactement ce que dit m: Original! That's exactly what my mother says! She also says “wouldn't you rather take up painting?”, but I think she's joking.
textes.Orophin ! Il y a un hibou d'argent sur l: Orophin! There's a silver owl on the north hill.
textes.Orophin est mon éclaireur depuis deux si: Orophin has been my scout for two centuries. Good tracker. Good eye. Too hasty. I still check his arrows. He hates it. That's why I do it.
textes.Orophin m'a rapporté qu'il voyait des pe: Orophin reported seeing little lights above the white mushrooms. He wanted to shoot to see what they were. I said no. Very loudly. He didn't understand why. I didn't explain. You don't shoot at spirits.
textes.Orophin m'a rapporté un jour une pierre: Orophin once brought me a carved stone he'd found near the mist: a serpent biting its own tail. “The Ancients?” he asked me. I said yes, looking learned. Truth is, I had no idea. I put it on my shelf and made up a story around it. It's a very good one.
textes.Orophin m'a retrouvé alors que je n'étai: Orophin found me when I wasn't lost. He still hasn't forgiven me. He's a good friend: his eyes follow me the moment I set foot on a path.
textes.Orophin m'a retrouvé le neuvième jour, a: Orophin found me on the ninth day, sitting on a stone at the edge of the mist, watching a snail cross the path. He was covered in thorns; he hadn't slept. He said: “Were you lost?” I said: “No, I was watching the snail.” He didn't speak to me for a month. The snail was doing very well.
textes.Orophin vérifie mes histoires. Je dis «: Orophin checks my stories. I say “there's a white stag behind the hill”, he goes, he comes back: “No stag, Faelar.” Then he goes back, just in case. He's a good lad.
textes.Orsik ! Ma couronne brille-t-elle toujou: Orsik! Is my crown still shining?
textes.Orsik ! Tu as compté tes rubis ?: Orsik! Have you counted your rubies?
textes.Orsik a fait ma couronne, et il me le ra: Orsik made my crown, and he reminds me every year with a bill. One of the rubies is fake, I know. So we're even. But he doesn't know that.
textes.Orsik compte ses rubis tous les soirs, e: Orsik counts his rubies every evening, and every evening one is missing. It's me. He knows. I know he knows. Without that little game, he'd die of boredom in his shop.
textes.Orsik compte ses rubis tous les soirs. I: Orsik counts his rubies every evening. There's always one missing. I'm the one who hides it. Shh.
textes.Orsik m'achète mes rubis au prix d'un ca: Orsik buys my rubies for the price of a pebble and sells them for the price of a house. He counts everything, except what he owes. But he's got a good eye, I'll admit that.
textes.Orsik me fait compter ses rubis tous les: Orsik has me count his rubies every evening and pays me in “thank yous”. I've got four thousand and twelve, written down in a journal. One day I'll present him with the bill. With interest.
textes.Orsik, il manque un rubis. Je note « sor: Orsik, there's a ruby missing. I'll write “out”.
textes.Ortie ! Qu'est-ce que tu as encore mis d: Ortie! What have you put in my helmet this time?
textes.Ortie ! Réunion du club ! Sous l'escalie: Ortie! Club meeting! Under the stairs!
textes.Ortie ! Tu as compté les boulons ?: Ortie! Have you counted the bolts?
textes.Ortie a démonté mon grand soufflet pour: Ortie took apart my big bellows to make a fire-bubble machine. When I got to the forge, flaming bubbles were floating everywhere right up to the ceiling. I shouted. She said: “Look, Mum, it's pretty!” It was pretty. I shouted anyway. Then I put the bellows back together. Not quite the way it was before.
textes.Ortie a inventé une machine qui ramasse: Ortie invented a machine that picks up the bolts in my workshop. It worked first time. That has never happened to any of my inventions! It picked up the bolts, the broom, then my left shoe. I chased the machine for ten minutes. I told her she was a genius. And that it needed a button to stop it.
textes.Ortie dit qu'elle crache des étincelles: Ortie says she can spit sparks further than me. That's not true. Well, it is true. But that's because she practises in secret!
textes.Ortie veut être mon apprentie. Elle a ne: Ortie wants to be my apprentice. She's nine, she's cleverer than me, and she still has almost all her eyebrows. Her mother gives me dirty looks. I understand her. Me, I fear for my shoes.
textes.Ortie, c'est ma fille, ma fierté et mon: Ortie is my daughter, my pride and my worry. She has my horns, her father's stubbornness and ideas that go boom. She doesn't want to forge. She wants to invent. I wonder where she gets it from.
textes.Ortie, c'est ma fille. Elle a les cornes: Ortie is my daughter. She has her mother's horns, her mother's stubbornness, and my seriousness… No. She doesn't have my seriousness. She wants to invent everything. Especially things that explode.
textes.Ortie, c'est ma meilleure amie. Elle est: Ortie is my best friend. She's super clever and a bit bossy. She spits sparks further than me, but that's because she practises in secret. We have a secret club. It's a secret.
textes.Ortie, la fille de Ferronde, est ma meil: Ortie, Ferronde's daughter, is my best student. She lights a candle from ten paces, understands everything before I finish explaining, and wants to improve flames. Nobody had ever wanted to improve flames.
Ortie, Ferronde's daughter, is my best pupil. She can light a candle from ten paces. Unfortunately, she also lights the ones nobody asked her to.
textes.Ortie, tu viens m'aider à la forge ?: Ortie, are you coming to help me at the forge?
Ortie, one single candle, this time.
textes.Or… L'heure dorée ! Vous êtes une fin d': Gold… The golden hour! So you're a late afternoon. That doesn't surprise me. You look like someone who always comes home before dark.
textes.Oscar ! Gérard m'a regardé, ce matin !: Oscar! Gérard looked at me this morning!
textes.Oscar ! Qu'as-tu raté, aujourd'hui ?: Oscar! What did you get wrong today?
Oscar has burnt all my dummies. All of them. Even the one behind him. He's the worst apprentice I've ever had, and the only one who comes back every day smiling. That, I don't know what to do with.
textes.Oscar a changé son chapeau en pigeon. Le: Oscar turned his hat into a pigeon. The pigeon's called Gérard. He lives on the dormitory roof. He watches us.
textes.Oscar a encore transformé son chapeau en: Oscar turned his hat into a pigeon again. The pigeon refused to turn back into a hat. We named it Gérard.
textes.Oscar a fait léviter ma chaise avec moi: Oscar levitated my chair with me on it. It was a miss, and the most beautiful miss I've ever seen. Since the bedsheet business, I keep a close eye on him. I still blame myself.
textes.Oscar a la tête la plus cabossée et le c: Oscar has the most battered head and the softest heart in the Academy. He says sorry to the doors he bumps into. I'm very fond of that boy. I've set aside a pot of ointment for him.
textes.Oscar m'a montré la cicatrice qu'il a au: Oscar showed me the scar on his knee, from when he jumped off the dormitory with a bedsheet, last year. He wanted to scare me. I said: “So cool!” He sighed really loudly. He says he had the wrong sheet. I've got a much better sheet, with stars on it.
textes.Oscar rate tout, mais il rate avec une i: Oscar gets everything wrong, but he gets it wrong with an imagination I haven't seen in forty years. Failing in an original way is already a talent. It just remains to be seen which one.
textes.Oscar voulait faire sortir un lapin de s: Oscar wanted to pull a rabbit out of his hat, like the fairground magicians. The hat turned into a pigeon! It flew up to the dormitory roof with the hat's feather still on its head. I'm the one who named him Gérard. He looks like a Gérard. He doesn't want to be a hat again. I say he's fine as he is.
textes.Oscar, c'est mon meilleur copain du dort: Oscar's my best friend in the dormitory. He messes up all his spells, but he messes them up really well. Once, he made it rain buttons. Nobody can do that! He snores, though.
textes.Osiris fut tué par son frère Seth, jalou: Osiris was killed by his jealous brother Seth, and his body was cut into pieces and scattered all over the land. Isis, his wife, searched for them one by one and put them back together. That is how Osiris became king of the dead.
textes.Osiris, le roi des morts: Osiris, the king of the dead
textes.Ou alors c'est deux monstres avec un pie: Or else it's two monsters with one foot each!
textes.Ou alors compter toutes les étoiles. Sil: Or else count all the stars. Silas says there are a thousand million. I'm up to four hundred and three.
textes.Ou alors des lunettes. … Non. Pas de lun: Or else spectacles. … No. No spectacles. Forget what I said.
textes.Ou alors, plus difficile encore… un pont: Or, even harder… a bridge Ursule would cross. Just one. She wouldn't even need to say thank you. Just cross.
textes.Ou alors, que Nourredine avoue une fois: Or else for Nourredine to admit, just once, that my trade is the finest. In front of witnesses. You, for instance. Will you come?
textes.Ou la même, pour la quarante-quatrième f: Or the same one, for the forty-fourth time, my pearl.
Or we wait for the island to come down.
Or a rock. Or a seal. Checking.
textes.Ou être cuisinier. Un cuisinier qui fait: Or be a cook. A cook who makes pancakes fly. All by themselves. It's almost the same.
textes.Ouaaah ! On survole le Parc des Brumes !: Whoaaa! We're flying over the Mist Park!
textes.Ouaf ? (Il vous tend une patte de laiton: Woof? (He holds out a brass paw to you.)
textes.Ouah ! Tu me montres un ollie ? Moi j'en: Whoa! Will you show me an ollie? I land one in three. The other two, I fall.
textes.Ouais ! Tu as vu mon cœur ?: Yeah! Did you see my heart?
textes.Ouais, bon. On en prendra un plus solide: Yeah, well. We'll get a sturdier one.
textes.Ouais. Propre. Tu as bu ?: Yeah. Clean. Have you had water?
textes.Ouch. Ok. Ça, c'est pas cool, même pour: Ouch. Okay. That's not cool, even for Rainville.
textes.Ouf ! Ce monstre était plus fort que le: Phew! That monster was stronger than the Giant of the Mists. Well, than the rock.
textes.Ouf ! Je ne suis pas tout seul ! On devr: Phew! I'm not the only one! We should start a club. The Butterfingers Club. Ramen!
textes.Ouf ! Mon cœur bat comme un tambour. Mai: Phew! My heart is beating like a drum. But it's a victory drum!
textes.Ouf… Je souffle un peu. Continuez sans m: Phew… I'll catch my breath. Go on without me! No, wait for me! No, go on!
textes.Ouf… plus de souffle ! Plane un peu pour: Phew… out of breath! Glide for a bit to recover, then pedal again.
Ougha proud. Ougha happy. Ougha hungry. Granny!
textes.Ouh là… Vous voilà de retour sur la Plac: Whoa there… Here you are, back on Pearl Square, all dizzy. Down here, we stay safely behind the glass!
textes.Oui ! Bien sûr ! … Il est où ?: Yes! Of course! … Where is it?
textes.Oui ! Celle avec les galets !: Yes! The one with the pebbles!
Yes! Between the whale and Coralin.
textes.Oui ! Et après, tu me montres ?: Yes! And then you show me?
textes.Oui ! Et j'ai gardé la jambe, maître ! P: Yes! And I kept the leg, master! For running!
textes.Oui ! Et je veux rester dedans cinq seco: Yes! And I want to stay inside for five seconds!
textes.Oui ! L'escalier, là, sous la trappe de: Yes! The stairs there, under the glass hatch, go down to the heart of the Levitators. Put on your helmet… no, just kidding, there's no helmet. But hold on to the handrail.
textes.Oui ! Le grand bleu, c'est Capitaine. Le: Yes! The big blue one is Captain. The yellow one is Jam. The little white one is Mr Pascal: he grumbles whenever someone opens the window. All the others, I call Gérard. It's quicker.
Yes! No. I… I have to run.
textes.Oui ! On balaierait ensemble ! Toi la ga: Yes! We'd sweep together! You do the left, I do the right, Zéro does the middle!
textes.Oui, Aurélien. Toutes, et dans le bon se: Yes, Aurélien. All of them, and in the right direction.

Yes, Madame Olga. Any book at all.
textes.Oui, Maman ! T'as vu mon saut ?: Yes, Mum! Did you see my jump?
Yes, Mum. At twelve minutes past noon. I wrote it down.
textes.Oui, Mamie, deux bols chez Lentille !: Yes, Mamie, two bowls at Lentille's!
Yes, and it makes the sea sparkle.
Yes, and I'm proud of it.
Yes, and I'm still keeping it.
Yes, I love walking under the trees.
textes.Oui, j'attends. Non, je ne suis pas pres: Yes, I'm waiting. No, I'm not in a hurry. Well, yes, a little.
Yes, I do a bit of DIY.
Yes, I've a good sense of direction.
textes.Oui, je suis là. Je ne parle pas beaucou: Yes, I'm here. I don't talk much. But I'm here.
textes.Oui, je veux être écuyer !: Yes, I want to be a squire!
textes.Oui, ma Germaine. Tu as attrapé quoi, au: Yes, my Germaine. What did you catch today?
Yes, but I can't put them back together.
textes.Oui, mais toi, tu fais les voix !: Yes, but you do the voices!
Yes, but put the watering can down gently.
textes.Oui, oui. Je ne dis rien. Je ne dis jama: Yes, yes. I'm not saying anything. I never say anything.
textes.Oui, prêtresse ! Xan dort ! Promis !: Yes, priestess! Xan is asleep! I promise!
textes.Oui, s'il vous plaît, Ombreline. Un avec: Yes, please, Ombreline. One with puppies.
Yes, a home is waiting for me.
textes.Oui. C'est difficile. Il faut faire atte: Yes. It's hard. You have to be careful with every move, every handshake. But it's worth it. The pups, at least, never complain.
textes.Oui. C'est le premier bruit. Au bout d'u: Yes. That's the first sound. After a while, it slows down. And then you hear the rest. You have to stay down long enough.
textes.Oui. C'est ça, le plus dur. Pas partir :: Yes. That's the hardest part. Not leaving: saying goodbye. You're right. I'll have to say it, one day.
textes.Oui. Je me souviens. La première fois, t: Yes. I remember. The first time, you were the only person who asked how the glass held. The others always ask if the fish are friendly. They are. So is the glass.
Yes. I won't tell you anything.
Yes. The sack is… heavy, Honorine.
textes.Oui. Merci. Personne ne m'avait jamais d: Yes. Thank you. Nobody had ever asked me to come. People usually ask me to stand back.
textes.Oui. Une chanson de la mer, très ancienn: Yes. A song of the sea, very ancient.
textes.Ouille ! Attention, ou j'appelle la Prés: Ouch! Careful, or I'll call President Ondine. She won't get cross: she'll explain water pressure to you. For an hour.
textes.Ouille ! Les tombeaux crachent leurs fla: Ouch! The tombs spit out their flames, one row after another. Watch them, and cross when your row goes out.
textes.Ouille ! Mes antennes ont fait des étinc: Ouch! My antennae made sparks. That's not very nice, Heavy-Foot. Not nice at all.
textes.Ouille ! Mes cornes en tremblent ! Si tu: Ouch! My horns are shaking! If you want to fight, go to the Arena of Horns, that's what it's for!
textes.Ouille ! Tu es trop cuit, toi. Va te ref: Ouch! You're overcooked, you are. Go cool off in cold water.
textes.Ouille ! Tu vas me faire déborder du tra: Ouch! You're going to make me colour outside the lines!
textes.Ouille ! Tu veux que j'appelle la Doyenn: Ouch! Do you want me to call Dean Agathe? She never shouts. She looks at you. That's much worse.
textes.Ouille ! Tu veux que j'appelle la Premiè: Ouch! Shall I call the First Councillor? She'd give you a weather report: storm warning over your head.
textes.Ouille ! Tu veux que j'appelle le Bourgm: Ouch! Do you want me to call the Burgomaster? He'd give you a two-hour speech. Nobody deserves that.
textes.Ouille ! Tu veux que j'appelle le Capita: Ouch! Do you want me to call Captain Ferdinand? He's got enough on his plate with the turnips!
textes.Ouille ! Ça va pas, non ? On en parle ce: Ow! Are you out of your mind? We'll talk about it tonight at the Assembly. Around the brazier. Brasero will give you a philosophy speech. A long one.
textes.Ouille ! Ça va pas, non ? Tu veux qu'on: Ouch! Are you mad or what? Want us to take it to the assembly? Mamie Barricade will give you a three-hour sermon!
textes.Oui… Moi aussi, peut-être. Il y a des ge: Yes… Me too, maybe. Some people have easy eyes. You, for instance. A little.
textes.Oui… Rainville répète. Même le bruit peu: Yes… Rainville is rehearsing. Even noise can be a prayer, if you listen closely.
Yes… Everything. Gustave's flickering a bit.
textes.Oups ! Le filet anti-chute de la Cité vo: Oops! The City's safety net catches you mid-air and sets you down gently on the Esplanade. Plumeau hands you a handkerchief: “Hello. You fell. It happens.”
textes.Oups ! On recommence : écoute bien…: Oops! Let's start again: listen closely…
textes.Oups ! Un filet de lumière te rattrape a: Oops! A thread of light catches you in mid-air and sets you down gently near the Gate. Halo sighs: “Heavy-Foots… always at the edge.”
Oops… That's the bass drum. I sleep on top of it.
textes.Ouuuuuh… Pardon. Bonjour. Vibrato, music: Oooooooh… Sorry. Hello. Vibrato, musician. This is a theremin: you play it without touching it, just by moving your hands in the air. It goes “oooooooh”. All the music on Ondelune goes “oooooooh”. Here I learned you can also go “oompah-oompah”. I'm working on it.
textes.Ouverte ?! OUVERTE ! Deux cents ans ferm: Open?! OPEN! Two hundred years shut, and it's you… Wait, I'm writing this down. “Gate of the Four Seals: open. By…” I'll put “by the traveler.” Here: everything I'd saved for the expedition I never dared to make. And now, go down. Draw me what's down there. But come back. Mapmakers need people to come back.
textes.Ouverte. Bien. Toutes nos fenêtres donne: Open. Very good. All our windows face the sea: that is the whole idea. I must warn you, the seagulls get up at five. The management accepts no responsibility.
Open them, you're tying a granny knot.
textes.Ouvrir la Grande Porte de Forgefer: Open the Great Gate of Forgefer
textes.Ouvrir la Porte aux Quatre Sceaux: Open the Gate of the Four Seals
textes.Ouvrir la porte des Neuf Cercles: Open the gate of the Nine Circles
textes.Ouvrir le Temple de Kukulkan à la date d: Open the Temple of Kukulkan on the date of creation
textes.Ouvrir le coffre de mon grand-père, et c: To open my grandfather's chest, and finally understand what it was worth. What it was worth to him. Ha! And to me, if there's any left.
textes.Ouvrir le coffre du premier fragment d'a: Open the chest with the first amulet fragment
textes.Ouvrir ma propre cantine sur le quai, av: To open my own canteen on the quay, with a palm-leaf roof and just one rule: no brawling in front of the pot. After the pot, if you like.
textes.Ouvrir un comptoir commun avec mon frère: To open a shared counter with my brother Firmin, on the Hautefond Belvedere, halfway between his Jolly Piston and my Cumulus Café: half steam, half froth. And at last, after fifty years of arguing, declare a draw. Well, almost a draw. I'd have won a tiny bit.
textes.Ouvrir un deuxième étal à la surface : «: To open a second stall on the surface: “Atlantis Crackers, a thousand-year-old recipe”. The people up there like old things, don't they? Then they'll love these.
textes.Ouvrir un vrai restaurant, avec des tabl: To open a real restaurant, with tables, a flashing sign, and Mamie's name written up big. Gaston would be head chef. I'd be… sous-chef. Fine. OK.
textes.Ouvrir un étal dans chacun des quatre mo: To open a stall in each of the Column's four worlds, one up top, one here, one down below, one at the bottom of the sea, and send the news travelling from one to the next. With cinnamon in it.
textes.Ouvrir un étal sur un vrai marché d'en b: To open a stall at a real market down below, between a fishwife and a cheese seller, and sell nebula flowers for smiles. Nothing but smiles. To see how many I'd earn in a day.
textes.Ouvrir une terrasse au Camp des Fleurs,: To open a terrace at the Flower Camp, in the sun. With parasols full of holes, so the Rainville folk feel at home. And smile. A second time. Just to see.
textes.Ouvrir une école de réparation, gratuite: To open a free repair school for the kids of the Alleys. So they learn that a broken thing isn't a finished thing.
textes.Oyez, oyez ! Par décision de la Guilde,: Hear ye, hear ye! By decision of the Guild, our adventurer is promoted to RANK E! They defeated slimes! Several of them! Applause, please, even the hens!
textes.Oyez, oyez ! RANG A ! Le Baron en a fait: Hear ye, hear ye! RANK A! The Baron's hat fell off in amazement! Again! Could somebody go and fetch it?
textes.Oyez, oyez ! RANG B ! Les bardes compose: Hear ye, hear ye! RANK B! The bards are already composing a song! It rhymes badly, but it's very long!
textes.Oyez, oyez ! RANG C ! Montjoie a désorma: Hear ye, hear ye! RANK C! Montjoie now has a real hero… almost! Children, you may ask for autographs. No more than three each!
textes.Oyez, oyez ! RANG D ! Notre aventurier a: Hear ye, hear ye! RANK D! Our adventurer has survived the frogs, the goblins and Miss Églantine's form! Master Hugues has serious matters to entrust to them!
textes.Oyez, oyez ! Un nouveau rang !: Hear ye, hear ye! A new rank!
textes.Oyez, oyez, OYEZ ! RANG S ! LÉGENDE DE L: Hear ye, hear ye, HEAR YE! RANK S! GUILD LEGEND! Master Hugues is weeping with joy into his pie! The shops will close for an hour! No, ten minutes! Oh, all right, five!
textes.Où ? Pourquoi ? À quelle heure ? Il y au: Where? Why? What time? Will there be pies?
textes.Où ai-je mis mes lunettes ?: Where did I put my glasses?
textes.Où ai-je mis mon chapeau ?: Where did I put my hat?
textes.Où ai-je mis mon compas ?: Now where did I put my compass?
textes.Où ai-je mis mon tampon ?: Where did I put my stamp?
textes.Où trouver les Perles ?: Where can I find the Pearls?
textes.Où tu veux ! En onze secondes !: Wherever you want! In eleven seconds!
textes.Où veux-tu aller ?: Where do you want to go?
textes.PAS DE RADIO ?! … Bon. Ce n'est pas grav: NO RADIO?! … Right. It doesn't matter. The town loudspeakers work when the aerial holds up. You'll hear me anyway. Everywhere. All the time.
textes.PAS SI FORT, JE SUIS À CÔTÉ DE TOI !: NOT SO LOUD, I'M RIGHT NEXT TO YOU!
textes.PC : 1 à 4 pour choisir un pouvoir, X po: PC: 1 to 4 to choose a power, X to cast it. VR: B to cast, hold B to switch.
textes.PC : 5 à 0 pour choisir un sort, V pour: PC: 5 to 0 to choose a spell, V to cast it, B for the next one. VR: left trigger to cast, hold it to switch.
textes.PERSONNE ?! Moi j'ai voté ! Et personne: NOBODY?! I voted! And nobody voted against! It was a unanimous election! … Guards! GUARDS! … Ah, that's right, I haven't got any guards. Well. I've got my eye on you, citizen.

textes.POUF ! Ha ha ha ! Tu as vu la tête que t: POOF! Ha ha ha! Did you see the look on your face?! A teapot wagging its tail, and that didn't tip you off?
textes.PSCHHHHT ! Un jet de vapeur brûlante te: PSHHHHT! A jet of scalding steam pushes you back! The jets blow in rhythm: wait for a burst to end, then dash.
textes.PSCHHHT ! Une durite éclate ! La Grande: PSSSHHT! A hose bursts! The Great Digger roars, faster now… and calls two movers!
textes.Page cent douze, Théophraste ! Presque f: Page one hundred and twelve, Théophraste! Nearly done!
textes.Page deux cent trois ! Oui, Mademoiselle: Page two hundred and three! Yes, miss, twice!
Page forty. I'm taking my time.
textes.Pain au chocolat ! Gourmandise, j'aime ç: Pain au chocolat! A sweet tooth, I like that. I'll give you the ones with two chocolate bars instead of one. Don't tell Nina, she claims them all.
textes.Pains de miel (deux cœurs chacun !) et t: Honey breads (two hearts each!) and herbal teas. And I buy honey, fruit and coconuts. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Paisible, comme une braise sous la cendr: Peaceful, like an ember under the ash. That's my way of being happy.
textes.Paisible. Ce matin, un champignon géant: Peaceful. This morning, a giant mushroom opened a new cap. Orange, as big as a table. It went “poof” and the whole cathedral sparkled. That's its way of saying hello.
textes.Paisible. Coudre, c'est comme écouter la: Peaceful. Sewing is like listening to the sea: you stop thinking about anything.
textes.Paisible. Le métier fait tic-tac, la nav: Peaceful. The loom goes tick-tock, the shuttle passes, and the hours spin away with the thread.
textes.Paisible. Les arbres ont bien dormi, les: Peaceful. The trees slept well, and so did the children. The children a little less.
textes.Paisible. Ramender, c'est comme une priè: Peaceful. Mending nets is like a prayer. One knot, then another.
textes.Paisible. Sœur Pétronille a rangé les ci: Peaceful. Sister Pétronille put away the candles, only knocked over half of them, and nursed the cat that had knocked them down. It was the cat, this time. For once.
textes.Paix et amour, {surnom} ! Et des tournes: Peace and love, {surnom}! And pockets full of sunflowers.
textes.Pandémonia, c'est ma fierté : la Citadel: Pandémonia is my pride: the Citadel in the centre, the Circle of Fire all around, the Upper Town with the Academy, the Forge Cathedral and the Great Lantern Square, and down below the Market, the Arena, the Baths and the harbour. Take a stroll: everyone will say hello.
textes.Pandémonia, la cité aux mille lanternes: Pandémonia, the city of a thousand lanterns
textes.Papa ! Des épices sont arrivées, aujourd: Dad! Did any spices come in today?
textes.Papa ! Il me faut une étagère pour mes z: Dad! I need a shelf for my zines!
textes.Papa ! Interrogation ! Qui a fondé l'Aca: Dad! Pop quiz! Who founded the Academy?
textes.Papa ! J'ai cassé un coussin de la rampe: Dad! I broke one of the ramp cushions!
textes.Papa ! Je vais doucement ! Très, très vi: Papa! I'm going gently! Very, very fast, but gently!
textes.Papa ! On va se promener ? Vite, vite !: Daddy! Shall we go for a walk? Quick, quick!
textes.Papa ! Regarde ! La tour, elle est droit: Daddy! Look! The tower's straight now!
textes.Papa ! Tu as encore raté un temps !: Dad! You missed a beat again!
textes.Papa a porté son casque toute une journé: Dad wore his helmet for a whole day with a smile I'd painted on it. All the guards smiled when they saluted him. He couldn't work out why.
textes.Papa construit tout ce que je demande. I: Dad builds everything I ask for. He measures everything in centimetres. Even his answers. He built me the most beautiful newsroom in the world, up a tree.
textes.Papa dit qu'on ne nourrit pas les nuages: Dad says we don't feed the clouds. But that one looks hungry.
textes.Papa et Maman pêchent la sardine à Port-: Papa and Mama fish for sardines in Port-Azur. I used to sleep in the boat, between the nets, with the seagulls doing their business on my hat. Papa says I could count sardines before I could talk. That's not true. I could talk first. But I was counting at the same time, so you couldn't tell.
textes.Papa fait parfois des bulles en forme de: Sometimes Dad blows heart-shaped bubbles. I counted: there are more on rainy days. I worked out that it's when he's thinking about Mum. And I've calculated that I need fourteen years to become an astronomer and an engineer. In fourteen years, Dad will be all alone in the house. I redid the calculation eleven times. It always comes out at fourteen. It isn't logical.
textes.Papa garde les jardins. Il parle plus au: Dad looks after the gardens. He talks more to the corals than to people, but when he explains how seaweed grows, he says at least a hundred words in a row.
textes.Papa m'a construit une cabane dans l'arb: Dad built me a treehouse in the tree on Pallet Square. It's my newsroom. There's a desk, a rubber stamp, and a “letters from readers” box. I've received three letters. Two from Tapage.

Dad built me a treehouse in the tree on Pallet Square. It's my newsroom. There's a desk, a stamp, a “letters to the editor” box and an archive room. I asked for a second archive room. Dad asked how many centimetres. I told him lots.
textes.Papa m'a construit une rampe de skate da: Dad built me a skate ramp in the yard. Mum wanted railings. I jumped over the railings on the first day. Dad didn't say anything. The next day, he'd put cushions everywhere. Now, when I fall, it goes “poof”. It's the best ramp in the world.
textes.Papa m'a donné un coin de jardin à moi,: Dad gave me a corner of the garden all to myself, as big as a hand. I planted a little round pebble in it and said it was a tree seed from the surface. It isn't growing. Dad waters it every morning anyway, very seriously. He says you never know.
textes.Papa m'a fait une cabane dans l'arbre de: Dad built me a treehouse in the tree on the square, with a desk and an archive room. I asked for a second archive room. He said: “How many centimetres?” I said: “Lots.” The next day, there was a second room. And a little emergency ladder.
textes.Papa m'a montré la maquette du Lisse-Cen: Dad showed me the model of the Lisse-Center, very proud. While he was talking, I tapped on the edge. Without realising. Faster and faster. The escalator fell off. In rhythm. Dad looked at me. I apologised. He accepted. But I saw his fingers move, just a little, on the table.
textes.Papa m'avait fait un berceau avec une pa: Dad made me a cradle out of a pallet and one of Mum's bike wheels. When I was six months old, I rolled it all by myself into the kitchen. They found me in front of the fridge. They say that's why I'm called Tornade. I don't remember. But I think I was hungry.
textes.Papa m'emmène en promenade le matin, jus: Daddy takes me for walks in the morning, all the way to the edge of the mist. He walks so slowly that I've got time to run ahead, come back, run off again, climb a tree and climb back down. He says I go on two walks while he goes on one. It's true!
textes.Papa marche partout, tout doucement. Il: Daddy walks everywhere, really slowly. He knows every path on the island, even the ones that don't exist. He says trees are never in a hurry. I'm in a hurry for both of us.
textes.Papa me soulève d'une seule main, avec s: Dad lifts me with one hand, with his brass arm, and puts me on his shoulder. From up there I can see over everyone at the Fair. Once I touched the sign of stall 4. Boulon was barking because he wanted to go up too. Dad said: “One at a time.” Boulon didn't get the idea.
textes.Papa met vingt jours pour faire une barq: Dad takes twenty days to make a boat. Twenty days! I made a raft in an hour, with three planks from the yard and mum's washing line. It sank straight away. Dad said: “That's why it takes twenty days.” And then he helped me fish the planks out. He was laughing, but secretly.
textes.Papa peint tout ce qui ne bouge pas. Et: Dad paints everything that doesn't move. And sometimes things that do. He's got a giant brush called Bertrand. I think he loves it almost as much as me.
textes.Papa tapote du pied quand il passe devan: Dad taps his foot when he walks past the Hall. I've seen him. He doesn't know it. I think I get it from someone.
Dad wants me to take over Lisse & Son. He made me do an internship: stamping eviction notices. I stamped them in rhythm, without meaning to. Boom-chak, boom-boom-chak. All morning. Miss Prune was tapping her foot. So was Dad, for a second. Then he ended the internship. I wasn't called back.
Dad wants me to take over Lisse & Fils. I tried. I did an internship. I stamped eviction notices. I stamped them in rhythm. It made a really good song. But it was a really bad idea.
Dad wants me to take over the company. He says “optimise” fourteen times an hour. But he taps his foot outside the Hall. I've seen him. He doesn't know. I think I get it from him.
textes.Papa, c'est le capitaine de la Garde. Il: Dad is captain of the Guard. He's tall, he's serious, and he goes clang when he walks. He never knows his lessons when I test him. But he makes the best pancakes in the city. In armour.
textes.Papa, il construit tout en palettes. Il: Dad builds everything out of pallets. He doesn't talk much, but he made me a ramp with cushions. It's the only ramp in the world with cushions.
textes.Papa, il me faut une deuxième salle des: Dad, I need a second archive room.
textes.Papa, il prenait des photos de mes châte: Daddy used to take pictures of my castles. But he only looked in his camera. Once, he stepped back to get the whole tower, and he walked into the moat. After, in the photo, there was only his feet. He kept it anyway. He says it's the sharpest photo of the holidays.
textes.Papa, regarde la cabine ! Elle monte tou: Dad, look at the cabin! It's going up all by itself!
textes.Papa, tu as vu mon sécateur ?: Dad, have you seen my secateurs?
Dad, you shout that at me every evening.
textes.Papa. Il est dix-neuf heures quatre. Tu: Dad. It's four minutes past seven. Have you eaten?
textes.Papa… tu as passé une bonne journée ?: Dad… did you have a good day?
textes.Papi Augustin dit qu'il a vu un éclat ro: Grandpa Augustin says he saw a pink glint on a walkway. I saw it too! Well, I think. Maybe it was a butterfly.
textes.Papi Augustin, c'est pas mon vrai papi,: Grandpa Augustin isn't my real grandpa, he's Rosalie's dad. But he pushes the swing better than anyone. And he knows all the capitals in the world. Even the ones that don't exist.
textes.Papi Nono a dansé sur toutes les plages: Grandpa Nono has danced on every beach in the archipelago. Nobody believes his stories, just like nobody believes mine. I believe all of his. Even the ones that change.
textes.Papi Raymond, c'est pas mon vrai papi, m: Grandpa Raymond isn't my real grandpa, but he's my grandpa anyway. He's the pétanque champion, not Marcel. I tell everybody.
textes.Papi Raymond, il me raconte le fournil d: Grandpa Raymond tells me about the bakehouse in the old days, when he was the baker. He says that one night the dough rose so much it went out the window and the seagulls ate it. Mum says it's not true. I think it is. Seagulls eat everything.
textes.Papi, le parapluie ! … Non, fausse alert: Grandpa, the umbrella! … No, false alarm.
textes.Papi, raconte-moi la mine. La vraie vers: Grandpa, tell me about the mine. The true version.
textes.Papy Ferdinand ! Je peux tirer le siffle: Grandpa Ferdinand! Can I pull the whistle?
textes.Papy Ferdinand a vendu la chaudière de s: Grandpa Ferdinand sold Bernadette's spare boiler to an innkeeper up top, to turn into a chocolate machine. I forged the rivets of that boiler when I was twenty. So that chocolate has a bit of my forge in it. That explains why it whistles.
textes.Papy Ferdinand a vendu une chaudière à u: Grandpa Ferdinand sold a boiler to a man from up top, to make chocolate. A train boiler! For chocolate! I think it's the best idea in the whole history of the Strata.
textes.Papy Ferdinand me laisse tirer le siffle: Grandpa Ferdinand lets me pull Bernadette's whistle, once an evening. He tells really long train stories. I listen right to the end. He falls asleep in the middle of mine.
textes.Papy Ferdinand vient à treize heures, to: Grandpa Ferdinand comes at one o'clock, always at the same table, with his cap. He tells about the time Bernadette went round the cavern without him. Everyone knows the story. Everyone laughs anyway. It's a very good story.
textes.Par accident ! Les meilleures ! Toutes m: By accident! The best kind! All my great discoveries are accidents. My roofs too, mind you. You've got the instinct, I can tell by your eyebrows.
textes.Par ici, le vent ! … Non, par là !: This way, wind! … No, that way!
textes.Par la Colonne, j'ai oublié mon paraplui: By the Column, I left my umbrella on the fifth floor. There is no fifth floor. I don't understand anything.
textes.Par la Colonne, quel ciel !: By the Column, what a sky!
textes.Par la PORTE ?! Comme un elfe ?! Un nain: Through the DOOR?! Like an elf?! A dwarf doesn't use the door when he can go through the rock. It's a matter of honor. And of dessert: she bakes pies.
textes.Par la baie ! On a mesuré : il passe. En: Through the big window! We've measured it: it fits. At an angle. If we hold our breath. And without the tail, which we'll put back on outside.
textes.Par la baie : des nuages qui passent tou: Through the big window: clouds drifting by very close, so close you could touch them. One of them is shaped like a sugar puff. Doctor Aurèle has surely named it already.
textes.Par la baie : le ciel, immense, et la Ci: Through the big window: the sky, vast, and the City of Clouds seen from the side, with its upside-down mountain floating. Far below, the sea sparkles. The Dragonfly tugs gently at her mooring, like a dog that wants to go for a walk.
textes.Par la baie, la nuit : les lumières de l: Through the big window, at night: the lights of the City, the Shuttle going round, all lit up, and far below, the lights of Hautefond, like a handful of stars dropped into the sea.
textes.Par la barbe de Neptune ! Lequel, maître: By Neptune's beard! Which one, Master Faelar? Gaston counted them all!
textes.Par la barbe de Neptune, il est magnifiq: By Neptune's beard, it's magnificent! Gaston, write that down!
textes.Par la lumière de l'Arbre-Mère…: By the light of the Mother Tree…
textes.Par la lune ! Deux fois, Ba Sidi. Comme: By the moon! Twice, Ba Sidi. Like all the good ones.
textes.Par la lune, Corentin, tu te souviens mi: By the moon, Corentin, you remember my stories better than I do.
textes.Par la quille ! Et la mille et unième, t: By the keel! And the thousand and first, when are you telling it?
textes.Par la quille ! L'ours qui raconte deux: By my keel! The bear who tells the same story twice!
textes.Par la vitre ! Courageux. La vue est mag: Out of the window! Brave. The view is magnificent. But do remember to look at the people sometimes: they pull wonderful faces.
textes.Par les cendres de la Rade !: By the ashes of the Harbour!
textes.Par les clous de mon perfecto !: By the studs on my leather jacket!
textes.Par les grandes baies, le ciel entre dan: Through the big windows, the sky comes into the café. The cloud chandeliers sway a little. On the counter, a machine makes clouds out of milk.
textes.Par les racines ! Un client honnête ! Tu: By the roots! An honest customer! You're a rare species, you know. I'll treasure you. And maybe raise my prices a teeny bit.
textes.Par les racines de l'Arbre-Mère…: By the roots of the Mother Tree…
textes.Par les sept lunes ! Celle-là, elle a la: By the seven moons! That one's shaped like a biscuit!
textes.Par les sept lunes, c'est parfait ! Tu a: By the seven moons, it's perfect! You've got the heart of a Lumen above your heavy feet, {surnom}.
textes.Par les tripes de la Murène ! Tu veux tâ: By the Moray's guts! Want a taste of my sabre?
textes.Par ma barbe ! La grande poilue ! Tu as: By my beard! The big hairy one! Have you grown again?
By my beard, I'm going to end up crying.
textes.Par ma barbe… elle penche !: By my beard… it IS leaning!
textes.Par ma barbe… il a de la repartie, pour: By my beard… he's got a quick tongue, for a tall one.
textes.Par ma barbe… ou celle d'un autre !: By my beard… or someone else's!
textes.Par mes ancêtres ! Par mon père ! Par le: By my ancestors! By my father! By my father's cat! ATTACK!
textes.Par mes cornes ! Trois épreuves sur troi: By my horns! Three trials out of three. (Malachar takes out a scorched parchment and sets his seal on it.) I declare you Bachelor of Flames of the Infernal Academy, with the jury's slightly singed congratulations.
textes.Par quelqu'un qu'on aime… (Elle sourit.): Someone you love… (She smiles.) That's what I try to do every Thursday. People think children learn with their eyes. Mostly, they learn with the heart of whoever's telling.
textes.Par temps clair, d'en haut, on voit une: On a clear day, from up high, you can see a big blue patch under the sea, out in the open water: that's the Azure Dome, the underwater city. Sometimes a whale swims over it. It looks like a swimming cloud. I've never seen anything so beautiful.
textes.Par terre ? Toi aussi ? … Je veux dire :: On the floor? You too? … I mean: on the floor! What a funny idea! Nobody does that. Nobody. Especially not under the counter.
On my floor, it's still mine.
textes.Par tous les pistons, ce que ça grimpe,: By all the pistons, these streets are steep! Hautefond is a town for calf muscles.
textes.Par tous les vents ! La mer est belle, l: By all the winds! The sea is fine, the boat is moored, and Bigorneau stole a mackerel from the fishmonger's. Again. I paid for it. Again.
textes.Parapluies qui montent, grille-pains sol: Rising umbrellas, solar toasters, cloud compasses, little clouds in jars! Everything works. Almost. And the instruction manual is still being invented. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Paraît que ton capitaine a peur de l'eau: They say your captain's scared of water.
textes.Paraît que tu as peur de l'eau, capitain: They say you're scared of water, captain.
textes.Parce qu'il a la bouche pleine ! … De pi: Because his mouth is full! … Of stone. Hee hee! (We won't repeat that to him, okay?)
textes.Parce qu'il a perdu sa voix… Sa puce voc: Because he lost his voice… His voice chip is broken. Dad says it's a very old chip, a Z Series, and they don't make them anymore. But Dad fixes everything! He just has to find the part. Will you help Dad? He's at his workshop, in the Alleys. Please, please, please!
textes.Parce qu'il a trop de problèmes !: Because it has too many problems!
textes.Parce qu'il est content, ma chérie. Lave: Because it's happy, sweetheart. Wash your hands, please.
textes.Parce qu'il lui manque son cœur ! L'engr: Because it's missing its heart! My grandfather's golden gear: fourteen teeth, solid gold, my name engraved on it. During yesterday's demonstration, it jumped off its axle, rolled across the square, went past the balustrade… and fell off the cliff. Down to the port, I think. Me, I'm afraid of heights, and the cable car makes me seasick. Would you mind going to have a look?
textes.Parce qu'ils sont en pierre… polaire !: Because they're made of stone… and lined with fleece!
textes.Parce qu'on voit à travers !: Because you can see right through them!
textes.Parce qu'à chaque fois, c'était incroyab: Because every time, it was incredible.
textes.Parce que c'est la CATASTROPHE ! Cette n: Because it's a CATASTROPHE! Last night, Lisse's robots got into the Hall. Politely, apologising, but they got in. They took Germaine, Clou's guitar. Clou didn't say a word. He said nothing even louder than usual. They also took the amp, and the drumsticks! And the Great Boucan is coming soon: guests will come from all the islands! Ferraille saw robots carrying a guitar toward the Grey Factory; an amp might be lying around at the Scrapyard; and Tornade swears a robot dropped something at the Dry Dock. Will you help us? You'll be our hero. Our roadie-hero.
textes.Parce que dans l'eau poivrée, ils éternu: Because in pepper water, they sneeze!
textes.Parce que je lui chante quelque chose, m: Because I sing it something, sweetie.
textes.Parce que la mer, ils l'ont déjà vue. Un: Because they've already seen the sea. Once. In 1342. It was wet.
Because the middle is already taken.
textes.Parce que le rouge est parti ! Le pot nu: Because the red is gone! Pot number three. A rabbit rolled it away, I'm sure of it: I saw it dash toward Mister Straw, my scarecrow, in the middle of the Meadows. But the grass is so tall! And I'm afraid of rabbits. They have ears far too big, they hear everything you think. Would you go?
textes.Parce que sinon, ils tombent dans le bat: Because otherwise they'd fall into the boat!
textes.Parce que. Sonne la cloche. Pas trop tôt: Because. Ring the bell. Not too early!
textes.Pardon ! Je chuchote ! Tu vois ? JE CHUC: Sorry! I'm whispering! See? I'M WHISPERING!
textes.Pardon ! Je chuchote. Tu vois ? JE CHUCH: Sorry! I'm whispering. See? I'M WHISPERING.
Sorry! I got the wrong door.
textes.Pardon ! Je passe ! Tu veux commander ?: Sorry! Coming through! Want to order? Tell my colleague at the counter.
textes.Pardon ! Vous ! Avez-vous vu passer un p: Excuse me! You! Have you seen a little cirrus go by? His name is Octave.
textes.Pardon, Mère Brasille ! C'est sûrement P: Sorry, Mother Brasille! It must be Pétard!
Sorry, I was thinking about a crystal.
textes.Pardon, maître ! Elle était trop près !: Sorry, master! It was too close!
textes.Pardon, pardon ! Je descends acheter du: Excuse me, excuse me! I'm going down to buy bread on the Floor. Mr Pascal says it's better down there.
textes.Pardon, pardon ! Je les replie ! Une let: Sorry, sorry! I'm folding them! A letter for you!
textes.Pardon, pardon ! Je ne peux suivre qu'un: Sorry, sorry! I can only follow an adventurer from the Guild. Go and see Églantine, at the counter. It only takes ten coins and a bit of courage.
textes.Pardon, pardon ! Lait de nuage pour la t: Excuse me, excuse me! Cloud milk for the back table!
textes.Pardon, pardon… attention, plateau chaud: Excuse me, excuse me… careful, hot tray!
Sorry. Excuse me. I'm going to push you.
textes.Pardon. Je ne peux suivre qu'un aventuri: Sorry. I can only follow an adventurer registered with the Guild. That's the rule. Églantine wrote it in very big letters.
textes.Pardonner… C'est bien un mot de client,: Forgive… Now that's a customer's word. Costs nothing to say. … I'll think about it. Don't repeat that.
textes.Pardon… J'ai faim. Quand j'ai faim, je m: Sorry… I'm hungry. When I'm hungry, I sit down. It's the Tournevent rule.
textes.Pardon… J'ai trébuché, et puis le sol ét: Sorry… I tripped, and then the ground was so comfortable…
textes.Pardon… vous lisez, vous ? Des livres, j: Sorry… do you read? Books, I mean. In the evening, or while travelling?
textes.Pareil ! Voilà. Assieds-toi plus près, t: The same! There it is. Sit closer, you. A story is something that happened at least once: outside, or inside. You have a storyteller's ear.
textes.Parfait ! Article un du Grand Règlement: Perfect! Article one of the Great Regulation! You have the soul of a head of protocol. I name you honorary deputy. By decree.
textes.Parfait ! Avec ça, j'achète du sel à Rad: Perfect! With this, I'll buy salt from Radis. He gives me a good price. In return, I tell him how his vegetables ended up.
textes.Parfait ! C'est exactement ce qui devait: Perfect! Exactly what was supposed to happen!
textes.Parfait ! C'est ma spécialité. Même quan: Perfect! That's my speciality. Even when I'm trying to make people cry. Ask Rodrigue.
textes.Parfait ! Clair, net, joyeux ! Tu as une: Perfect! Clear, crisp, cheerful! You've got a presenter's voice. On festival night, you're the one making the announcements.
textes.Parfait ! Je veux qu'elle mange toute ma: Perfect! I want it to eat my whole street.
textes.Parfait ! Le refrain au troisième temps,: Perfect! The chorus on the third beat, eh!
textes.Parfait ! Les meilleurs clowns commencen: Perfect! The best clowns start by dropping everything. You've already got the talent, you're just missing the fall. Look, like this: boom!
textes.Parfait ! Un inventeur prudent. Comme mo: Perfect! A careful inventor. Like me. Well, almost.
textes.Parfait ! … Enfin, presque. Tiens, pour: Perfect! … Well, almost. Here, for your trouble: my latest invention. Don't ask me what it's for.
Perfect, those are the ones I want.
textes.Parfait, on commence avec deux pieds, c': Perfect, two feet is already a start, that's better than one. We'll sort out the left-right part. The cat danced badly too, at first. Now he's my best pupil. Really, he is.
textes.Parfait, parfait ! Vous voilà presque ci: Perfect, perfect! You're almost a citizen now. Here, a few coins, and here is a detailed map of our town: I had it added to your journal. And don't hesitate to help our residents: Port-Azur knows how to say thank you.
textes.Parfait. (Pyra pose une bûche dans sa ma: Perfect. (Pyra sets a log in her bare hand and blows on it: it bursts into flame.) Your turn. Hold out your hand. Feel the heat. Don't hold it back: push it out in front of you. … HA! A fireball! A small one, but a real one! Now, the five braziers of the Ground. All five, one after the other: each one goes out after a minute and a half.
Perfect. Sit down. With my dice.
textes.Parfait. Et après deux ? … Rien. Après d: Perfect. And after two? … Nothing. After two, you stop. You've got it.
Perfect. It's still in my pocket.
Perfect. I'll leave by the east.
textes.Parfait. Le Lord de la douze réclamait s: Perfect. The Lord in number twelve has been demanding his croissants since dawn. He feeds them to the seagulls, but he demands them.
textes.Parfait. Tu le regardes, tu l'admires, t: Perfect. You look at it, you admire it, you draw it if you like. And you leave it where it is. That's the wisest answer of all.
textes.Parfait. Un phoque-vague. Ne t'arrête su: Perfect. A seal-wave. Whatever you do, don't stop.
Perfect. Fog rhymes with lots of things.
textes.Parfaite ? (Il goûte.) … Non. Il manque: Perfect? (He tastes it.) … No. It needs a bit more salt. But thank you. Nobody's ever said that to me before.
textes.Parfaite réponse. Même moi, je ne devrai: Perfect answer. Even I shouldn't know it. You pass the test.
textes.Parfaite. On a retrouvé le cochonnet, Ra: Perfect. We found the jack, Raymond's losing again.
textes.Parfaitement ? Ah ! Alors dis-moi où est: Perfectly? Ah! Then tell me where north is, right now. … Good. Very good! At last, someone who doesn't hold the map upside down!
textes.Parfaitement, Ferraille. Elle sent la fo: Perfectly, Ferraille. It smells of the forge.
textes.Parfaitement. Les enfants suivent les fl: Perfectly. The children follow the arrows.
Perfect! Silver all the way to the root. (He grinds them in a mortar with honey and a drop of syrup.) A spoonful each, morning and evening, and in three days they'll be fighting like ragpickers again. Which isn't necessarily good news for me.
textes.Parfois, je répare le petit moteur-cœur: Sometimes I repair Boulon's little heart-engine. It beats fast, a bit too fast for a dog, even a brass one. I offered to adjust it. Wilfried said no, very gently, and took Boulon back into his arms. I didn't ask why. Some settings are nobody's business but their inventor's.
textes.Parfois, je trouve un vrai coquillage ra: Sometimes I find a real rare shell on the beach — a tiger cowrie, a golden cone. I bring it to Inès unpainted, to show her I can recognise the real thing. She buys it from me at a fair price, without a smile, without a word too many. A fair price! I'd never sold anything at a fair price. It gave me a funny feeling.
textes.Parfois. Hm. Au moins, vous l'avouez. Pr: Sometimes. Hm. At least you admit it. Take a bookmark. Take ten. Keep one on you, always.
textes.Parfumée. J'ai fait sécher la sauge ce m: Fragrant. I dried the sage this morning.
Tell me about the people you know.
Tell me a little about yourself.
Face to face… Like Hurla. Hmph. Fine. It's quicker, true. But a letter, you can keep. Spoken words fly away. Even without wings.
textes.Parler à Germaine, la femme de Père Gaub: Talk to Germaine, Père Gaubert's wife (at the farm, in the yard in the morning and late afternoon, in the fields late in the morning, at the market in the afternoon)
textes.Parler à Gédéon après le concert (à la H: Talk to Gédéon after the concert (at the Howling Hall, or the next day in town)
textes.Parler à Hector, l'armurier (rue du Phar: Talk to Hector, the armourer (Lighthouse Street)
textes.Parler à Jack après le concert (près de: Talk to Jack after the concert (near the stage, or the next day)
textes.Parler à Mange-Clous, le cuisinier du Re: Talk to Mange-Clous, the cook of the Requin Borgne (on the deck of the Requin Borgne in the morning, by the fireplace of the Crâne Fendu around noon, at the nets on the quay in the afternoon)
textes.Parler à Pauline, la femme de chambre (a: Talk to Pauline, the chambermaid (at the Grand Hotel: in the corridors in the morning and afternoon, in the hotel garden at noon)
textes.Parler à Rouille après le concert (à la: Talk to Rouille after the concert (at the Howling Hall, or the next day at the Cannery)
Tell me about the Wisteria Cottage.
textes.Parrain Pépin, il vient tous les matins: Godfather Pépin comes every morning to bring the flour, at a run. He lets me bang his drum. And he tells me about my papa. He's the best godfather in all of Ramure. In the whole world, even.
textes.Parrain a un chronomètre qui fait tic-ta: Godfather has a stopwatch that goes tick-tock, it comes from Cliquetis. One day he timed me eating a mooncake. Two minutes! He said: “Two minutes for a cake, Mochi, new record!” He told everyone. Mummy didn't think it was funny. Me, I wanted to beat the record. Mummy hid the cakes.
textes.Parrain me raconte papa. Il dit que papa: Godfather tells me about Papa. He says Papa burned every loaf, that he laughed so loud the birds flew out of the Mother Oak, and that one day he made a loaf so black they used it to prop open the bakery door. The loaf's still there. I've seen it. It's really black.
textes.Partez ! Jusqu'à la porte du phare !: Go! All the way to the lighthouse door!
textes.Partir dans la forêt des brumes avec un: To set off into the misty forest with an empty basket, and come back with the plant that brings a fever down in one night. I'll come back. I promised myself. And I'm taking seaweed for the road.
All over your beach hut, for instance.
Everywhere. Leave it. It suits you.
textes.Paré ! Pourquoi on dit « larguer » ?: Ready! Why do we say “cast off”?
textes.Paré à larguer, capitaine Nina ?: Ready to cast off, Captain Nina?
textes.Pas assez de pièces, {surnom}. Va pêcher: Not enough coins, {surnom}. Go fishing and bring me some fish, I'll buy it from you.
textes.Pas assez de place ici pour qu'un aigle: Not enough room here for a giant eagle to land. Go to an open area.
textes.Pas assez de place pour déplier l'Alouet: Not enough room to unfold the propeller Alouette here (it needs clear ground).
textes.Pas aujourd'hui ! Mais tu peux en donner: Not today! But you can give one, if you like. There's no limit on giving.
textes.Pas aujourd'hui, Coquille ! Un récif dan: Not today, Coquille! A reef in your way?
textes.Pas aujourd'hui, {surnom}. Mon cœur clig: Not today, {surnom}. My heart is still blinking red. Come back when it's blue again.
textes.Pas aujourd'hui. Il y a des choses qu'on: Not today. Some things you don't tell to just anybody.
textes.Pas aujourd'hui. Je ne suis pas d'humeur: Not today. I'm not in the mood to sell. Or to talk. Or anything.
textes.Pas aujourd'hui. Reviens quand on sera d: Not today. Come back when we're friends again.
Not today… Fine. Here, have a crust.
Not until I've found my rosary. It's in the belly of the biggest frog in the lake. I don't dare go and get it. I'm sorry.
textes.Pas avant la bannière ! C'est une questi: Not before the banner! It's a matter of honour! And of song: Bertrand is waiting.
textes.Pas avant que vous ayez corrigé le retar: Not until you've corrected yesterday's delay.
textes.Pas beaucoup… Chut, je ne juge pas. Chaq: Not much… Shh, I'm not judging. Every reader starts with a first book. Sit here, I'll pick you a very small one. With pictures.
textes.Pas besoin d'oser : approche doucement,: No need to dare: come closer gently, talk to them kindly. They love being told hello. Like everyone, really.
