My doll was a princess, a witch, a pirate, and once a turnip, for the harvest festival. She won the prettiest doll contest. As a turnip. The jury never understood why.
textes.Petite, j'étais tellement timide que je: When I was little, I was so shy I didn't talk to anyone. Not at school, not to the neighbours. But to dogs, yes. Dogs never interrupt you, and they think all your stories are brilliant. At seven, I knew the name of every dog in the neighbourhood. Not the children's, though.
textes.Petite, j'étais très timide. Je ne parla: As a little girl, I was very shy. I didn't talk to anyone. But to dogs, I did. Dogs never interrupt you, and they think all your stories are brilliant. Today, I walk six of them. And I talk to humans a bit too. A bit.
As a little girl, I was a very sad child. I don't know why. I'd cry over a cloud. And then one day, a seagull stole my ice cream and I couldn't help laughing. Since then, I've decided: I laugh first, I think afterwards. It works better.
textes.Petite, je classais les cailloux du jard: As a little girl, I sorted the pebbles in my mother's garden: by size, by colour, then by mood. The grey pebbles were “pensive”. My mother found that strange. My grandmother gave me a box with drawers for my seventh birthday. It's the best present of my life. It's still under my counter, full of paper clips.
textes.Petite, je gardais une sardine pour le R: As a kitten, I'd save a sardine for the King. Every evening, I'd put it at the end of the jetty, on a lily pad. In the morning, no sardine. I was sure it was him. At twelve, I saw the heron fly off with it. I didn't tell Dad. He looked so happy when I told him the King had eaten.
textes.Petite, je grimpais partout : aux arbres: As a little girl, I climbed everything: trees, wardrobes, lamp posts. My parents gave me a harness for my tenth birthday. I've never taken it off. Well, except to sleep. I sleep in a hammock. Hung from a tree.
textes.Petite, je grimpais partout : sur les ar: As a little girl, I climbed everything: trees, wardrobes, lampposts. My mother always looked for me up high. She'd look up before calling me. For my tenth birthday, my parents gave me a harness. They said: “At least this way, you'll be tied to something.” I've never taken it off.
textes.Petite, je lui avais demandé de changer: As a little girl, I asked him to change the ending of the story of the princess who wanted to see snow, because it made me sad. He refused. He told me: “Sad endings, we keep; we're the ones who change.” I only understood at twenty. I went to tell him. He'd forgotten.
textes.Petite, je m'endormais toujours avant la: As a little girl, I always fell asleep before the end of his stories. So he'd tell me the ending the next morning, at breakfast, his mouth full of toast. For years I thought all stories ended with “… and they ate toast.” I still believe it a little.
textes.Petite, je me cachais dans le grand lust: As a little girl, I used to hide in the great chandelier of the throne room. Asmodin always found me by the smell of singed lace. I never admitted to him that what I liked most was him looking for me.
textes.Petite, je me suis échappée de mon panie: When I was little, I escaped from my basket one night. The whole Circle searched for me. Séraphine found me asleep on the altar, arms spread wide. My mother said the stones had chosen me. Séraphine tells everyone that. I say my feet were cold. The altar is warm at night. That's a fact.
textes.Petite, je n'écoutais jamais les histoir: As a girl, I never listened to my mother's stories all the way to the end. Halfway through, I'd go off to catch a butterfly. She'd keep telling it, all alone, on her bench. When I came back, she'd say: “The hero caught the dragon.” One day, I asked her if it was true. She said: “No. But you've just caught a butterfly, and that's the same thing.”
textes.Petite, je parlais si fort qu'on m'enten: As a little girl, I talked so loudly you could hear me on the other side of the harbour. My teacher called me Mégaphone. Instead of taking offence, I decided to make a career of it. Today, I make everyone loud. Except me: I whisper, now.
textes.Petite, je rangeais tout. Mes jouets par: As a little girl, I tidied everything. My toys by colour, my books by size, my pencils in order of preference. My mother said I'd make an excellent secretary. I believed her. I forgot to tell her I also played very loud music in my room while I tidied. She found out on her own.
textes.Petite, je sautais du grenier avec un pa: When I was little, I used to jump from the attic with an umbrella. My mother screamed. So did the umbrella. One day, I stayed up in the air. My mother stopped screaming.
textes.Petite, je voulais être une grande sorci: As a little girl, I wanted to be a great witch. For three years, every spell I cast ended up as a soap bubble. Fire? A bubble. Invisibility? A bubble. My mother said the house had never been so clean. One spring morning, a bubble turned into a butterfly. I cried all day.
textes.Petite, mon père me laissait tenir le po: When I was little, my father let me hold the tar pot. Once, I dipped my plait in it. He spent the evening cleaning it with butter, without a word, very gently. My mother laughed. He didn't. That night, I understood my father was someone who's afraid of people getting hurt.
textes.Petite, pendant ses histoires, je tapais: As a cub, during his stories, I banged on pots. Bing for the dragon, bang for the storm. My mother wanted to stop me. He slowed his story down to follow my beats. That night, we told it together. Next day, he gave me a little hammer. He says he already knew.
textes.Petite, sur Astralys, je passais mes jou: As a little girl, on Astralys, I spent my days pressed against the glass of our dome, watching the islands far below. The lights of Port-Azur, the smoke of Ember Island, the pirates' sails. My mother would say: “We observe, we don't go down.” I'd nod. In my head, I was already going down.
textes.Petite, une nuit, je me suis perdue dans: When I was little, one night, I got lost in the alleys while Papa was lighting the other end of town. An hour in the dark. Since then, I've been afraid of the dark, {surnom}. I sleep with a bulb on. If I want to light up the whole city, it's so that no child is ever afraid again. Léonce doesn't know. Don't tell him. A mother isn't afraid.
textes.Petite, Éclair ne tenait pas en place su: As a kitten, Éclair couldn't keep still on the jetty. Dad would say “watch the float”, she'd watch it for two seconds, then run from one end to the other, and every fish in the pond would dash off and hide. Dad would sigh. I'd take her on my lap so she'd keep still. She kept still. For four seconds.
textes.Petites baies sucrées des buissons. Rend: Small sweet berries from the bushes. Restores half a heart.
textes.Petites, je montais des spectacles dans: When we were little, I put on shows in the street with bedsheets, and Lila ran the till. Our first fee was a fish, given by a passing fisherman. One fish for two. We grilled it on the beach like a feast for queens. I think it was Bastien's father. I'll have to ask him.
textes.Petites, on se cachait dans la pirogue d: When we were little, we used to hide in her father's canoe, under a mat, to get out of work. One day, the canoe came loose. We drifted to the middle of the lake, with no paddle. Xóchitl paddled with a bunch of flowers. It was no use at all, but it was very pretty. A fisherman brought us back at sunset.
textes.Petites, on se cachait sous une natte da: As little girls, we used to hide under a mat in my father's canoe. One day, the canoe came loose and we drifted into the middle of the lake. No oar. I paddled with my bouquet. Citlali told me, very calmly: “It won't work, but keep going, it's pretty.” A fisherman brought us back in the evening. I didn't have a single flower left.
textes.Petits, sous les arcades, elle me faisai: When we were little, under the arcades, she'd make me judge the fishes' eyes, like grandmother. “This one?” I'd say: “Fresh!” She'd say: “Three days old! You've got no eye!” She was nine and already scolding like an old fishwife. Today she scolds just the same, but with earrings.
Doesn't matter, as long as there are some.
Doesn't matter, as long as you're in good company.
textes.Peut-être ! Si le vent est calme !: Maybe! If the wind is calm!
textes.Peut-être. C'était toi, le djembé ?: Maybe. Was that you on the djembe?
textes.Peut-être. En attendant, mes sardines re: Maybe. Meanwhile, my sardines are watching the clock.
textes.Peut-être. Tu danserais sur une chanson: Maybe. Would you dance to a song of my own?
textes.Pff. J'arrive avec le goudron. Garde le: Pff. I'll be over with the tar. Keep the mackerel cool.
textes.Pff. Si on avait fait ça, il n'y aurait: Pff. If we'd done that, there'd be no Carène left. Just a beach. Oh well. Each to their trade. Mine is throwing nothing away.
Pff. If you're here at seven.
textes.Pfff. Comme moi. Les mains de tempête. P: Pfff. Like me. Storm hands. Promise me you'll never take apart the Spire. Or the Heart. Or me.
textes.Pfff. Encore toi. (Il grogne, mais ses a: Pfff. You again. (He grumbles, but his antennae blink blue.) … Fine. I'm glad. Don't tell anyone.
Pfff. I made it by mistake.
textes.Pfff. Tu as de la chance, je suis de bon: Pfff. You're lucky, I'm in a generous mood. Fifteen percent, today only.
textes.Pfffft ! Un petit nuage sort de vos chev: Pfffft! A little cloud comes out of your ankles. Your toes thank you.
textes.Pfffouu… Le petit nuage gonfle, tourne t: Pfffooo… The little cloud puffs up, spins round three times and froths into a cup. Then it starts turning again, looking very pleased with itself.
textes.Pfff… La brume monte dans le cylindre et: Pfff… The mist rises in the cylinder and turns into a cloud. A meteorologist whispers to you: “That's how the morning ones are born, under the island.”
textes.Pfft… POP ! Une capsule de laiton jailli: Pfft… POP! A brass capsule shoots out of a copper tube and drops into a basket. Behind a desk, someone sighs: “Another one!”
textes.Pff… Passe-moi l'étoupe, futur capitaine: Pff… Pass me the oakum, future captain.
textes.Pff… Tout le monde m'aime bien, ici. C'e: Pff… Everybody likes me round here. It's exhausting.
Pff… You've been saying that for a hundred years.
textes.Philibert ! Le tourne-pages a fait toute: Philibert! The page-turner got through the whole sonata without a hitch.
textes.Philibert ! Tu ne vas pas me le ressorti: Philibert! You're not going to bring that up every evening, are you?
textes.Philibert croit qu'il n'a jamais rien in: Philibert thinks he's never invented anything. My piano turns its pages thanks to him every day. He's much more of an inventor than he thinks.
textes.Philibert est le meilleur voisin de banc: Philibert is the best bench neighbour in the world, and he invents with a heart this big. His boxes of nothing, on the other hand… No. I won't say a thing. I've said too much already.
textes.Philibert est le passager le plus étrang: Philibert is the strangest passenger at my airfield: he wants to go where there are no ideas. A charming man, as sad as a windsock with no wind.
textes.Philibert est un vrai inventeur, quoi qu: Philibert is a real inventor, whatever the Academy says. His box of nothing never breaks down. It's the only thing in my Bazaar that's never let me down.
textes.Philibert invente tout, toujours un peu: Philibert invents everything, always a little after everyone else. I turn down his patents one by one. And I read every one of them, to the very last line. He doesn't know that.
textes.Philomène connaît les légendes du donjon: Philomène knows the dungeon's legends better than anyone. Except for the fourth floor. She says the mimics bite. They pinch. I've been there. She hasn't. I won't give in to her.
textes.Philomène connaît plus de légendes que m: Philomène knows more legends than my spellbook, and she never loses her pages. I trade her herbal teas for stories. It's the best business on the island.
textes.Philomène dit qu'un roi peureux a fait c: Philomène says a fearful king had these steps dug. I understand that king a little.
textes.Philomène et moi, nous échangeons des lé: Philomène and I trade legends for herbal teas. She knows more than my spellbook. And she doesn't lose her pages.
textes.Philomène me réveille depuis soixante an: Philomène has been waking me up for sixty years. First for my homework, then for my sermons. Her elbows are as pointy as ever. I can never thank her enough. Nor can my ribs.
textes.Philomène raconte que mon dragon était g: Philomène says my dragon was the size of a goat. Not true. It was the size of a BIG goat. She knows every legend on the island, and she ruins mine.
textes.Philomène vient me voir au pied des Croc: Philomène comes to see me at the foot of the Fangs once a month, with her cane and a herbal tea. We sit in front of the dungeon gate and argue about the fourth floor. She says the mimics bite. I say they pinch. She says I didn't look properly. I say she's never set foot there. It goes on for two hours. It's the best afternoon of the month.
Philomène. It was big, that dragon.
textes.Philosophe. Tout est en noir et blanc, c: Philosophical. Everything is in black and white, like an old exercise book. I spent fifty years in front of a blackboard: I know all about grey.
textes.Philémon ! Les trois squelettes sont ren: Philémon! Have the three skeletons come home?
textes.Philémon ! Une crique, au nord-ouest. To: Philémon! A cove, to the northwest. Brand new.
textes.Philémon ! Une vieille carte, toute fraî: Philémon! An old map, fresh today!
textes.Philémon Lunette reconnaît une fausse ca: Philémon Lunette can spot a fake map by the smell of the ink. He ruined a whole season for me. Since then, I pay him to check my maps before I sell them. He's become my partner without knowing it.
textes.Philémon dessine ce que je vois. Je lui: Philémon draws what I see. I tell him “a cove to the west”, and he turns it into a marvel with curly waves. He lends me his spyglass. I give it back. Nearly always in one piece.
textes.Philémon me dessine les roses des vents: Philémon draws the compass roses I tattoo. He's jealous of my copies. He chases after crow feathers, and he chases slowly. He's a charming old gentleman. And a rival.
textes.Philémon écrit mes histoires dans les ma: Philémon writes my stories in the margins of his maps. He says they're half false. He writes them anyway. That's a true friend: someone who keeps your lies.
textes.Photographier les îles d'en bas, une par: To photograph the islands down below, one by one, without anyone screaming “GIANT JELLY!”. And one day bring mum here, on a very soft cushion, so she can see the auroras for real. She'd bounce so high. So high.
textes.Photon laisse mes méduses dormir dans se: Photon lets my jellyfish sleep in his big flowers. It tickles the flowers. They laugh all night. He sleeps badly. He never complains. He's the kindest of the Lumens, with plants and with creatures.
textes.Photon m'a demandé comment poussaient le: Photon asked me how trees grow down below, without crystals or light. I described the rain to him, the black earth, the roots, the apples falling on farmers' heads. He listened to me for a whole afternoon without moving. His flowers blinked like applause.
textes.Photon m'a demandé sous quelle étoile pl: Photon asked me which star to plant his glowing seeds under. I showed him a little blue star, very gentle. He planted all his seeds facing it. They grow faster than the others. He says it's the star. I think it's him. He talks to them every morning.
textes.Photon me laisse cueillir les fruits lum: Photon lets me pick the glowing fruit in his Gardens, as long as I ask them for permission. I ask with my four arms. The fruit always says yes. Photon says they're intimidated.
textes.Photon parle aux plantes et elles lui ré: Photon talks to plants and they answer him. I brought him a seed from down below a long time ago. He keeps it in his pocket. I think he talks to it too.
textes.Photon parle aux plantes, moi aux étoile: Photon talks to plants, I talk to stars. None of them answer us in words. But his twinkle, and so do mine. We understand each other very well. We don't talk much.
textes.Photon, mes méduses chez toi, cette nuit: Photon, my jellyfish at your place tonight?
Photon, your flowers are looking at the sky.
textes.Photon, vos plantes clignotent bizarreme: Photon, your plants are blinking strangely
Photon, your plants are blinking strangely…
textes.Pianissimo. Il ne faudrait pas qu'ils s': Pianissimo. We wouldn't want them to nod off.
textes.Piano… piano… on ne réveille pas le cumu: Piano… piano… let's not wake the cumulus.
textes.Pied-Lourd, lève les bras ! Tu vois ? Le: Heavy-Foot, raise your arms! See? The sky's answering you!
textes.Pierre et feu ! Ton acier fond très bien: Stone and fire! Your steel melts very nicely, tall one. That's a compliment.
textes.Pierrick ! Le Zéphyr arrive plein ce soi: Pierrick! The Zéphyr's coming in full tonight. May the best one win!
textes.Pierrick ! Ta prairie n'a pas bougé, je: Pierrick! Your meadow hasn't moved, I went to check on it.
textes.Pierrick ! Tes hamacs sont bien attachés: Pierrick! Are your hammocks tied on properly today?
textes.Pierrick ? C'est mon neveu. Il croit qu': Pierrick? He's my nephew. He thinks he runs the inn. I let him think so, it makes him happy.
textes.Pierrick croit que je lui vole ses clien: Pierrick thinks I steal his customers with my seaweed sacks. It's true. But somebody has to make him fight, or he'd spend his days asleep in his hammocks.
textes.Pierrick est gentil, mais il me dénonce: Pierrick is nice, but he always tells on me to the Admiral. And he can't laugh when you tie knots in his hammocks.
textes.Pierrick est persuadé de tenir l'auberge: Pierrick is convinced he runs the inn. I let him believe it. He's clumsy, touchy, and gentle as a lamb. His mother would be proud. Me, I am, in secret.
textes.Pierrick m'a demandé un jour, très série: Pierrick once asked me, very seriously, where the stillest place on the island was. No wind, no slope, no sea. I searched for three weeks. I drew him a little meadow above the bay, between two oaks, behind the north point. He asked: “Does the meadow move?” I said no. He smiled like a child.
textes.Pierrick recompte les hamacs chaque soir: Pierrick recounts the hammocks every evening, out loud. Thirty-two. Always thirty-two. Once, for a laugh, I took one down. He counted thirty-one, went white as a sheet, and searched the lower deck until midnight. I hung it back up in secret. I never did it again.
textes.Pierrick rêve d'une auberge sur la terre: Pierrick dreams of an inn on dry land, with beds. I drew him the best plots on the island. He keeps my map in his apron, and looks at it when his aunt's back is turned.
textes.Pierrick vient me voir chaque semaine av: Pierrick comes to see me every week with a new illness. I listen to him, I give him a ginger tea, and he leaves cured. It's my greatest success.
textes.Pierrick, tu as rempli les cruches ?: Pierrick, have you filled the jugs?
textes.Pigment ! Du noir pour l'affiche, cette: Pigment! Black for the poster, this time?
textes.Pigment ! Je te tiens, tu peux peindre !: Pigment! I've got you, you can paint!
textes.Pigment a peint un chat géant sur le mur: Pigment painted a giant cat on the wall. A good likeness. A little flattering. Naturally.
textes.Pigment m'a peint des fleurs violettes s: Pigment painted purple flowers on my harness, like the buddleias in the Spore Wood. Since then, when I climb, the butterflies follow me. They think I'm a bush. I let them think so. It's the most beautiful present I've ever been given.
textes.Pigment m'a peint un panneau au-dessus d: Pigment painted me a sign above my press: “No puns allowed”. Underneath, I wrote in marker: “What a pun-ishment.” She read it, she sighed so hard the sheets flew away. But she didn't rub out my line.
textes.Pigment peint en hauteur, je la tiens au: Pigment paints up high, I hold her on the end of a rope. Three weeks on the water tower together. We never got vertigo at the same time. Well, I never did.
textes.Pigment peint, j'imprime, et on se dispu: Pigment paints, I print, and we argue over every colour. She has never laughed at a single one of my puns. She's my best enemy and my best friend.
textes.Pigment, elle m'a peint la flamme la plu: Pigment painted the biggest flame in the world on my helmet. Mum wanted a sensible flame. Pigment doesn't know how. It's so cool.
textes.Pigment, la graffeuse, trouve que tu as: Pigment, the graffiti artist, thinks you "look like someone who makes beautiful walls". She gives you three spray paint cans: three graffiti must be painted on the paintable walls of Port-Boucan.
textes.Pika a trouvé un œuf ! … C'était un cail: Pika found egg! … It was rock.
textes.Pile ? Comme un cadran solaire ? Ça doit: Right on time? Like a sundial? Must be restful, being you. Me, I'm either early or late. Never in the middle.
textes.Pile à l'heure, comme d'habitude. Parfai: Right on time, as usual. Perfect.
textes.Pile à l'heure. (Ses yeux brillent.) Vou: Right on time. (His eyes light up.) You… you are a remarkable person. Come back whenever you like. At whatever time you like. On the dot.
Pilli! Wake up, it's the lesson.
textes.Pilli ! Tlaco n'a toujours pas de poils: Pilli! Tlaco still doesn't have any hair?
textes.Pilli ! Ton chien chante, ce soir ?: Pilli! Is your dog singing tonight?
textes.Pilli ! Tu as arrosé le maïs ?: Pilli! Did you water the maize?
textes.Pilli danse avec son chien. Le chien dan: Pilli dances with his dog. The dog dances better than half the warriors of Aztlán. Pilli, a bit less well. But with more joy than anyone. That's what dancing is.
textes.Pilli dort en classe. Avec son chien. Le: Pilli sleeps in class. With his dog. The dog learns better.
Pilli sleeps in class. With his dog. The dog, meanwhile, listens and learns better. Pilli is as clever as a monkey, when he's awake. The problem is the “when”.
textes.Pilli n'a pas le droit de monter l'escal: Pilli isn't allowed to climb the stairs of the Great Temple. He knows it. He tries anyway. He's stubborn, curious, and accompanied by a dog that barks at the stone serpents. I was like him. Without the dog.
textes.Pilli veut toucher mon bouclier, ma peau: Pilli wants to touch my shield, my jaguar skin and my weapon. He asks a hundred questions. His dog has been barking at me since the first day. Maybe the dog is right to be wary of jaguars.
textes.Pilli vient m'aider à remplir les jarres: Pilli comes to help me fill the jars at the lake. He spills half. The other half, his dog drinks. But he asks good questions about Tlaloc. He'll make a good potter. Or a good swimmer.
textes.Pilli, c'est mon copain d'Aztlán ! On se: Pilli is my buddy from Aztlán! We see each other at the fair of the longest day. He has a hairless dog, Tlaco, who's all warm. Peek' has hair. We don't agree on which is the best dog.
textes.Pilli, c'est mon fils. Il court partout: Pilli is my son. He runs everywhere with his dog, he asks a thousand questions, and he has his father's laugh. He never helps me in the garden. He helps me smile. That's already a lot.
Pilli. Your dog is still barking.
textes.Piloter un jour un bathyscaphe tout neuf: To pilot, one day, a brand-new bathyscaphe designed with Yolande, all the way to the very bottom of the Trench, where the little lights come on. Then, another time, to push on as far as Atlantis, if it exists. To arrive in front of its bubble, switch on the floodlights and wave hello. With Yolande beside me, saying: “Fine. All right. But we're back up before dinner.”
textes.Pimprenelle ! Tes boulons sont partout d: Pimprenelle! Your bolts are all over the forge!
textes.Pimprenelle ! Tes boulons, dans la forge: Pimprenelle! Your bolts, in the forge!
textes.Pimprenelle ! Tu allumes toujours les la: Pimprenelle! Do you still light the lanterns with a snap of your fingers?
textes.Pimprenelle ! Tu ne trouves pas mon nect: Pimprenelle! You don't find my nectar too sweet, do you?
textes.Pimprenelle ? Une tornade avec des ailes: Pimprenelle? A tornado with wings. She bad-mouths my sugar behind my back, but she's the only one who helps me fill my bottles without asking for anything.
textes.Pimprenelle ? Une étincelle de fée, en b: Pimprenelle? A spark of a fairy, down below, in the roots. I gave her a branch of Yggdrasil a hundred years ago. She deserves it. She doesn't know it yet.
textes.Pimprenelle a caché trois cents boulons: Pimprenelle has hidden three hundred bolts under her bed. Three hundred! The bed's gone up ten centimetres. She says it's “to practise for heights”. That's my girl.
textes.Pimprenelle a neuf ans, trois cents boul: Pimprenelle is nine years old, has three hundred bolts and more courage than half the Upper Town. She asks me questions about the Fronde all day long. I answer every one. Children are how walls come down.
textes.Pimprenelle a perdu sa baguette dans la: Pimprenelle lost her wand in the Cave of Jumping Mushrooms. Don't tell her I told you.
textes.Pimprenelle connaît le règlement mieux q: Pimprenelle knows the rulebook better than my liftkeepers. She's nine. I'm a little scared. But a good kind of scared. The kind you feel facing the future.
textes.Pimprenelle est venue planter un boulon,: Pimprenelle came to plant a bolt, to see if a bolt tree would grow. I told her it wouldn't work. Then I watered it anyway. You must never discourage a seed. Even a metal one.
textes.Pimprenelle habite en haut, à Hautefond,: Pimprenelle lives up top, in Hautefond, under the sky. She collects bolts, she knows the Liftkeepers' rulebook by heart, and she never gets dizzy. She told me the sky never falls. She checks every morning. She's the bravest girl I know.
textes.Pimprenelle habite à Hautefond. Elle est: Pimprenelle lives in Hautefond. She came up for the reopening with a bag of bolts. She says down there, there are bolts everywhere. I asked her if there were shells everywhere. She said: “On the beach, yes.” I nearly fainted.
textes.Pimprenelle m'a apporté un boulon « pour: Pimprenelle brought me a bolt “for the Column”. I screwed it onto the ticket office door. She comes to check it every morning.
textes.Pimprenelle m'a encore changé en grenoui: Pimprenelle turned me into a frog again. My paws hurt. My legs. Hmph.
textes.Pimprenelle me corrige tout le temps. «: Pimprenelle corrects me all the time. “You don't say ‘go up fast’, you say ‘ascend at full steam’.” She's nine. She knows the regulations better than I do. I think she's going to steal my cap.
textes.Pimprenelle parle tout le temps, très fo: Pimprenelle talks all the time, very loud, very fast. Next to her, I feel like a tiny little silence. But she holds my hand when I'm scared.
textes.Pimprenelle raconte à tout le village qu: Pimprenelle tells the whole village I put too much sugar in my nectar. She thinks I don't know. But every evening she drops by “by chance” when I'm rinsing my bottles, and licks the bottoms. I've seen her. I'm saving my petals for the right moment.
textes.Pimprenelle ramasse tout ce qui tombe de: Pimprenelle picks up everything that falls off the workbench. She has three hundred bolts under her bed, a thing called Gérard, and a future as Grand Liftkeeper. I'm the proudest mother in the Lower Town.
textes.Pimprenelle répond à mes énigmes avant q: Pimprenelle answers my riddles before I've finished asking them. Always wrong, always with admirable enthusiasm. It's a gift, in its way.
textes.Pimprenelle, la fille de la forgeronne d: Pimprenelle, the daughter of the blacksmith up top! She collects bolts! I gave her one from the Frondeurs' Bridge. She put it in a box all on its own. She says it's “the bravest bolt in the world”. She's right. It holds on over the Chasm.

Pimprenelle, the daughter of the blacksmith up top, collects bolts! She came to the Swap Shop with a full bag. She didn't want to swap anything: she just wanted to show me. I understood her straight away. That's me, at her age.
textes.Pimprenelle, ma fille, veut être liftièr: Pimprenelle, my daughter, wants to be a liftkeeper. Not a blacksmith. At first, it gave me a little pang. Then I told myself: the Column is tons of metal rising to the sky. It's a bit of forge taking flight. That suits me fine.
textes.Pimprenelle, une énigme : qu'est-ce qui…: Pimprenelle, a riddle: what is it that…
textes.Pimprenelle. Une étincelle qui parle. El: Pimprenelle. A spark that talks. She turns me into a frog when I grumble. I grumble all the time. Do the maths. Hmph.
textes.Pimprenelle… tu n'aurais pas un sort pou: Pimprenelle… you wouldn't have a spell for my drops, would you?
textes.Pinceau sec : trempe-le dans la Palette: Dry brush: dip it in the Palette
Pip! That sheet is for sleeping.
textes.Pip ! Tes oreilles sont redevenues norma: Pip! Are your ears back to normal?
textes.Pip a bu une de mes potions. Il a eu les: Pip drank one of my potions. His ears went green. He says it's my fault. It's partly his: the label said “not for Pip”.
textes.Pip a peur de moi. C'est bien : il ne to: Pip is afraid of me. That's good: he doesn't touch the stones anymore. He brought me his blanket, for the smallest one. I didn't know what to say. I laid it on her. It's still there.
textes.Pip essaie de léviter en sautant du dort: Pip is trying to levitate by jumping off the dormitory with a bedsheet. I'll have to have a word with him before he has a word with the ground.
textes.Pip est le plus jeune de mes apprentis e: Pip is the youngest of my apprentices and the chattiest on the island, Zéphyrine included. He asks a hundred questions a day. I've granted him the right to one.
textes.Pip veut léviter en sautant avec un drap: Pip wants to levitate by jumping with a bedsheet. I did that last year. Mother Sage had to look after me for a week.
Pip wants to jump off the dormitory with a bedsheet. I showed him the scar on my knee, to scare him. He said: “So cool!” That wasn't the idea at all. Since then, I keep an eye on bedsheets. He's got one with stars, he hides it under his pillow. I know it. He knows I know it.
textes.Pip, c'est le petit du dortoir. Il me su: Pip's the little one in the dormitory. He follows me everywhere and asks questions non-stop. He thinks I'm amazing. He's the only one. So I'm careful not to let him down too much.
textes.Pip, c'est un courant d'air avec des jam: Pip is a draught with legs. He decided to fly before he could levitate, with a bedsheet. It frightens the life out of me. I adore him, and I'd like him to keep his feet on the ground a little longer.
textes.Pip, il touche à tout. Il lit pas les ét: Pip touches everything. He doesn't read the labels, or he only reads half of them. But he's funny, and he believes in my potions. Well, he did before the green ears.
textes.Pique-nique au Parc des Brumes ! Le seul: Picnic in the Mist Park! The only place where the clouds join you for a snack.
textes.Pirate un jour, pirate toujours ! Arrr !: Once a pirate, always a pirate! Arrr!
textes.Pivoine ! Pile à l'heure, comme toujours: Pivoine! Right on time, as always.
textes.Pivoine ! Ton cueilleur préféré est là !: Pivoine! Your favourite picker is here!
textes.Pivoine ? Le meilleur nez de Ramure et l: Pivoine? The best nose in Ramure and the sharpest tongue. We learned herbs together at her grandmother's. She learned the herbs. I learned Pivoine.
textes.Pivoine a goûté mon gâteau de lune longt: Pivoine tasted my mooncake for a long time, eyes closed, nose forward. Then she said: “It's missing a herb.” I went cold all over. “Which one?” “I don't know.” Since then, she keeps trying: mint, sage, meadowsweet. I chased her out with the bread peel. Her mushrooms, for their part, have always been banned in my shop.
textes.Pivoine dit que je dors sous les arbres: Pivoine says I sleep under trees instead of gathering. Not true. I gather while I sleep. It's a fox technique.
textes.Pivoine essaie toujours de me tirer les: Pivoine is always trying to wheedle the post's secrets out of me. “What does this envelope smell of? And that parcel there?” I answer: “A postmistress says nothing.” So she sniffs my counter. I think she guesses half of it anyway. With a nose like that, it's not fair.
textes.Pivoine me donne des tisanes de brume po: Pivoine gives me mist teas so I can sleep in the daytime, I give her moon feathers for her vials. She's as nosy as a fox. Makes sense, she is one.
textes.Pivoine, c'est mon amie. Elle m'a rendu: Pivoine is my friend. She gave me back my sleep when I'd lost it. In return, she gets my warm bread for life, and the right to tell me my cake is missing a herb. She takes full advantage.
textes.Pixel connaît la visite par cœur. Elle l: Pixel knows the tour by heart. She recites it with me, at the same time, and corrects me when I make a mistake. I never make mistakes. But she corrects me anyway. Beep. It's pleasant.
textes.Pixel est venue dans ma bulle de soins a: Pixel came into my healing bubble with a doll under her arm: “Her arm hurts. Why?” I pretended to heal the doll. Pixel put her hands over mine. For one second, I saw her fingers glow. Ever so slightly. She didn't see it. I didn't tell her. Not yet.
textes.Pixel et Quark se cachent partout. Hier,: Pixel and Quark hide everywhere. Yesterday, Quark hid in the fountain, between Saturn and Ondelune. We only found him when the next planet came round.
textes.Pixel et son petit frère Quark jouent à: Pixel and her little brother Quark are playing hide-and-seek, and Quark always cheats. Pixel invites the hero to play: the two children will hide somewhere in Astralys, and both of them must be found.
textes.Pixel m'a demandé pourquoi j'étais si vi: Pixel asked me why I was so old. I told her: “Because I started early.” She thought about it for a very long time, then she said: “Then I'll start now too.” She blew on her hands, very focused. Ever since, she says she's getting older on purpose.
textes.Pixel m'a demandé pourquoi la visite ava: Pixel asked me why the tour had fifteen stops and not sixteen. I had no answer. I rebooted. When I came back, she was waiting for me, sitting on the ground. She said: “It doesn't matter. We'll look for the sixteenth together.” File created: “sixteenth stop.” Contents: empty. For now.
textes.Pixel m'a suivi pendant toute une visite: Pixel followed me for a whole tour, reciting every word at the same time as me. At stop eleven, in front of the fountain, she went quiet to let me say my favourite part. Then she said: “You blink brighter here.” She had noticed. Nobody had noticed. Beep.
textes.Pixel me pose des questions depuis qu'el: Pixel has been asking me questions since she learned to talk. I have one thousand and forty-three years of answers in stock. She's using them up one by one. It's wonderful.
Pixel always finds me at hide-and-seek. Always! I don't get it. She asks everyone questions, all the time. She fixes my mischief. She's the best big sister in the galaxy. Don't tell her.
textes.Pixel veut devenir guérisseuse. Elle soi: Pixel wants to become a healer. She already treats her dolls, the gurgles and her brother. Her brother lets her, for once. He likes the light plasters: they glow in the dark.
Pixel wants to become a healer. She heals her dolls, the glug-glugs and her little brother. She asks me questions non-stop. Her hands glow ever so slightly. I haven't told her yet.
textes.Pixel, c'est ma grande sœur. Elle pose d: Pixel's my big sister. She asks questions, I get up to mischief. She says she fixes my mischief. It's true. But without my mischief, she'd have nothing to fix, and she'd be bored. So really, I'm helping her. She won't admit it. She always finds me at hide-and-seek. I don't know how.
Pixel is my big sister. She asks questions, I get up to mischief. Between the two of us, we've done every single thing we're not allowed to do. There are three left. We're saving the best for last.
textes.Pixel, retourne au lit ! … Bon, cinq min: Pixel, back to bed! … Oh, all right, five minutes.
textes.Pixel, tu veux jouer à quelque chose ?: Pixel, do you want to play something?
textes.Pixel, tu veux m'aider aujourd'hui ?: Pixel, do you want to help me today?
textes.Pièces de vélo, triées, graissées, garan: Bike parts, sorted, greased, guaranteed. Well, nearly guaranteed. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Place ! Place au chevalier de Tournevent: Make way! Make way for the knight of Tournevent!
textes.Plan numéro 412 : le grille-pain qui cha: Blueprint number 412: the toaster that sings the time. Problem: it sings off-key. Proposed solution: teach the toaster music.
textes.Plan numéro 413 : le parapluie-ascenseur: Blueprint number 413: the lift-umbrella, “Going up!” model (thanks to the Liftkeepers' Guild down below for the name). Range: one and a half floors. Landing: needs work.
textes.Plan numéro 414 : la tasse tourneuse. El: Blueprint number 414: the spinning cup. It stirs the sugar in all by itself. It also stirs the tablecloth, the table, and sometimes the cat. Needs adjusting.
textes.Plan numéro 415 : le bocal à nuage. Un p: Blueprint number 415: the cloud jar. A small pet cloud, very calm, that rains on your plants when you forget to water them. Tested and approved by Flora.
textes.Planer de la Cité des Nuées jusqu'à Haut: To glide from the City of Clouds all the way down to Hautefond, a two-hundred-metre spiral descent around the Column, with Barnabé in a two-seater glider, eyes open. Mistress Capucine said: “Not around my Column.” I took that as a maybe.
textes.Plante verte (en plastique).\nNe pas arr:
Houseplant (plastic).
Do not water. Do not love.
textes.Planter enfin ma graine de pommier, et l: To finally plant my apple seed, and see it grow here, on Astralys. A real apple tree from down below, among the glowing flowers. And the first apple, I'd give to Gloubi. He'd cry. He always cries in front of apples.
textes.Planter un jardin au milieu de l'île, à: To plant a garden in the middle of the island, halfway between the sun and the rain. Plants from both villages would grow there together, and nobody could tell where one ends and the other begins.
textes.Planter un pommier de Hautefond dans cha: To plant a Hautefond apple tree in each of the four worlds of the Column: one in the clouds, one here, one in the Strata, and one under the Dome, at the bottom of the sea. And come back to watch them grow, one after the other.
textes.Planter une forêt entière de pommiers au: To plant a whole forest of apple trees around the clearing, so the village always has apples, and blossom in spring, and shade in summer. And so the giants have little neighbours.
textes.Plateaux, théières, lanternes. Les cent: Trays, teapots, lanterns. The hundred teapots my brother-in-law Hassan knocked over, I'm the one who made them: he's been feeding my workshop for ten years. Once a year, I polish the seven cannons of the Skala. A pirate, Mâchefer, comes to watch me hammer every day. And little Omar steals my tac-tac for his festival. Tac. Everybody helps themselves at my place.
textes.Plein ?! Comme des noisettes ? Et tu sai: Loads?! Like hazelnuts? And do you always know where they all are? Lucky you. Me, I lose my hazelnuts.
textes.Plein d'espoir. Aujourd'hui, j'invente q: Full of hope. Today, I'm going to invent something new. I can feel it.
textes.Plein de monde ! Hou ! Ma sacoche t'ador: Loads of people! Hoo! My satchel loves you already. Write small, then: it's not that big.
textes.Plein sud, tout en bas : Hautefond, la G: Due south, far below: Hautefond, the Great Column shining like a golden needle, the Great Market, and the Point Lighthouse. A golden cabin is climbing up the Column. It looks like a pearl on a string.
textes.Plein sud, tout en bas : les lumières de: Due south, far below: the lights of Hautefond, the Column lit up from top to bottom, and the Lighthouse turning. From up here, the town looks like a birthday cake.
textes.Plein vent ! J'ai fait le tour de la Col: Full sail! I went round the Column in seven minutes twelve. Héloïse says seven minutes ten. She starts counting from the moment she had the idea of setting off.
textes.Pleine d'espoir ! Une couleur de plus, e: Full of hope! One more colour and I'll feel twenty again. Well, seventy. That's not bad either.
textes.Pleine d'espoir. Tu es là-dedans pour no: Full of hope. You're in there for us, I can feel it.
textes.Pleine de trous ! Pour retenir l'eau ?: Full of holes! To hold the water?
textes.Pleine, décroissante, nouvelle, croissan: Full, waning, new, waxing: the four dials line up, a chime of crystal… and the slate door slides away upward.
textes.Plic ! On n'arrose pas les invités ! … E: Plic! We don't water the guests! … Well, not every day.
textes.Plic, n'oublie pas la fougère du coin !: Plic, don't forget the fern in the corner!
textes.Plic… plic… plonc ! Les trois gouttes to: Drip… drip… plunk! The three drops fall into the three buckets, and it almost makes a melody. “Brilliant! Thank you! I'll call it: Concerto for a Leaky Roof.” He gives you a few coins.
textes.Plic… ploc… Il pleut dans la yourte. Tro: Drip… drop… It's raining inside the yurt. Three drops fall from the roof onto the rug, and someone watches them with resignation.
textes.Ploc ! Moi Ploc ! (Il te pique avec un b: Ploc! Me Ploc! (He pokes you with a stick.) Poke! … You not say “ouch”? You not even drop pixels when poked? You too strong!
textes.Ploc veut voir Grosse-Dent ! … Non. Ploc: Ploc want see Grosse-Dent! … No. Ploc not want.
textes.Plonger au pied de la pointe du phare, c: Dive at the foot of the lighthouse point, on the open-sea side, and find the lens shard
textes.Plouf ! L'Achéron est glacé… Charon te r: Splash! The Acheron is freezing… Charon fishes you out with his oar, sighing: “One obol, I said. Not a swim.”
textes.Plouf ! L'eau du lac est froide comme un: Splash! The lake water is as cold as a winter morning. You climb back onto the shore, shivering; the frogs are laughing (well, croaking). Hop from stone to stone!
textes.Plouf ! L'eau du puits est glacée… Une p: Splash! The water in the well is freezing… Someone fishes you out with a pole: “The Bathyscaphe Pool is for bathyscaphes!” That'll wake you up.
textes.Plouf ! L'eau noire du bassin amortit ta: Splash! The black water of the pool cushions your fall.
textes.Plouf ! La rivière du Gouffre vous empor: Splash! The Chasm's river sweeps you away… and the railworkers' net fishes you out at the end of the Bridge. Brasero hands you a blanket: “We don't lean over, we look.”
textes.Plouf ! Tu nages dans l'eau froide jusqu: Splash! You swim through the cold water to the entrance ledge and haul yourself up, soaked.
textes.Plouf ! Tu remontes, trempé, sur le rebo: Splash! You climb back out, soaked, onto the entrance ledge. The basin is too deep to swim in.
textes.Plouf ! Tu te poses dans l'eau. L'Alouet: Splash! You land in the water. The Alouette, soaked, folds back into your bag. Time to swim!
textes.Pluie… sur le Plancher, sans doute. J'ou: Rain… on the Floor, no doubt. I'll open the umbrella. Very gently.
textes.Plume-de-Nuage est rentrée ! Elle flotte: Plume-de-Nuage is back! She's floating above the pond as if nothing happened. She has a guilty little look. Jellyfish always have a guilty little look. Thank you, {surnom}.
textes.Plume-de-Nuage file sous la grande verri: Plume-de-Nuage darts under the great glass roof of the Greenhouse, does three happy loops among the other creatures of the sky, and comes back to brush your cheek. She's home! Go and tell Nova.
textes.Plume-de-Nuage s'est arrêtée : tu vas tr: Plume-de-Nuage has stopped: you're going too fast, she's afraid of getting lost. Go back for her!
textes.Plume-de-Nuage, la plus jeune méduse de: Cloudfeather, Nova's youngest sky jellyfish, has escaped from the Greenhouse of Species. She's floating somewhere around the island and can't find her way home on her own. Sextant, who draws the island from the lookouts, may have seen her go by.
Plumeau said hello to my kite. I think he mistook it for a tree.
textes.Plumeau a été construit ici, à l'Atelier: Plumeau was built here, at the Workshop, by my old master, forty years ago. On the first day, he dusted a tree. Completely. Every leaf. My master laughed for a week. Today, I'm the one who oils his knees. He tells me Aurèle's jokes. He doesn't get them. Neither do I. We laugh together.
textes.Plumeau arrose très bien, mais il dit bo: Plumeau waters beautifully, but he says hello to every plant. I have four thousand. He finishes around noon. I let him. Since he started saying hello, they grow better. Old Bastien was right, and Plumeau understood it before anyone else.
textes.Plumeau est lent, poli, et il dit bonjou: Plumeau is slow, polite, and says hello to the trees. He's the finest machine on the island. He doesn't “almost” work: he works his own way. I've never invented anything so successful. Mind you, I'm not the one who invented him.
textes.Plumeau m'a raconté une blague. Il ne sa: Plumeau told me a joke. He didn't know why it was funny. Neither did I. But we laughed anyway.
textes.Plumeau répète mes blagues avec une préc: Plumeau repeats my jokes with perfect precision. He's the only one who laughs at the right moment. That is to say, never, but at exactly the right second. I find him funnier than me. Don't tell him, he wouldn't understand why.
Plumeau, there are three hundred of them.
textes.Plumeau, le robot jardinier, apprend mes: Plumeau, the gardening robot, learns my jokes by heart. He doesn't understand them, but he repeats them with perfect precision. He's the only one who laughs at the right moment. That is to say, never, but at exactly the right second.
textes.Plumeau, le robot jardinier, dit bonjour: Plumeau, the gardener robot, says hello to the trees. So do I, now. The oak in the Park doesn't answer, but Plumeau says it's “processing the request”. It's been processing for three years.
textes.Plumeau, le robot jardinier, vient m'aid: Plumeau, the gardening robot, comes to help me in the mornings. He waters very well. But he says hello to every plant, one by one. I have four thousand plants. He finishes the watering around noon. The plants look very happy.
textes.Plumeau, le robot jardinier, vient se fa: Plumeau, the gardening robot, comes to have his knees oiled every week. He tells me Doctor Aurèle's jokes without understanding them. He tells them better than the Doctor does, actually. He doesn't laugh before the punchline.
textes.Plumeau, le robot, me salue tous les mat: Plumeau, the robot, greets me every morning. “Good morning, Mr Séverin. Good morning, bench.” He says good morning to the bench too. I find that very polite. The bench has never answered. It's older than me.
textes.Plumette ! Mécaniquement parlant, vous a: Plumette! Mechanically speaking, you have feathers on your head.
textes.Plumette m'apporte les cartes de tante S: Plumette brings me Aunt Sésame's cards. She knows all of Ramure's secrets and tells none of them: a postwoman says nothing. Good thing. Neither do I, sometimes.
textes.Plumette m'apporte les lettres d'Ardoise: Plumette brings me Ardoise's letters. It's not her fault. I hold it against her a little anyway. It's easier to be cross with the postwoman than with the sea.
textes.Plumette me donne les plumes de lune pou: Plumette gives me moon feathers for my vials; I give her teas to help her sleep during the day. She knows all of Ramure's secrets. She doesn't tell a single one. It's infuriating.
textes.Plumette ne dit jamais rien de ce qu'il: Plumette never says anything about what's in the letters. Even when the envelope's all crinkled from rereading. “A postwoman says nothing.” She puts the letter down, waits for the reply, and off she goes. I gave her a skewer once, with my reply. So it would fly faster.
textes.Plumette, c'est notre postière ! Elle rê: Plumette is our postmistress! She dreams of a golden acorn for her counter. I've got one, my most beautiful one, I'm saving it for a big occasion. Meanwhile, I show it to her from a distance. Tee hee.
textes.Plumette, la postière de Ramure, c'est m: Plumette, the postmistress of Ramure, is my pen pal. We write to each other on the mail dockets. She's the only aviator in the archipelago who flies without an engine. I envy her a little.
textes.Plus au sud, cette fois. J'ai refait mes: Further south, this time. I've redone my calculations.
textes.Plus bas, il y a la Ligne du Dôme d'Azur: Further down, there's the Azure Dome Line, at the bottom of the sea. It's reopened! Bielle and I laid the rails. One day we'll play down there, under the dome, with fish in the audience. They say whales love drums. They say.

Further down, there's the Azure Dome Line, at the bottom of the sea. Closed for works. Bielle and I work on it, on the rails. One day we'll play down there, under the dome, with fish in the audience. They say whales love drums. They say.
textes.Plus bas, la salle des Avares, pleine de: Further down, the hall of the Misers, full of heavy bronze weights you must push into place; the Styx, where only the flagstones that don't bubble will hold you; the city of Dis and its three Furies. Then Geryon, who has the face of an honest man and the tail of a scorpion: he carries travellers all the way down, gliding like a leaf.
textes.Plus calme… (Il regarde le lac longtemps: Calmer… (He looks at the lake for a long time.) It's true. You can hear the ducks. I hadn't heard the ducks in years. Here, my friend: frog legs for Ulric, he'll cook them for you. And my eternal gratitude. It's very big, my gratitude. Like my fears.
textes.Plus de galette pour l'instant ! Revenir: No more flatbread for now! Come back later, empty belly.
textes.Plus de toit, plus de porte, plus de sou: No more roof, no more door, no more eyebrows! My fifteenth roof, I want to make it out of iron. Thick iron. I need three blocks of iron ore. The shepherds of the north sell it, so do the dwarves of Fire Mountain, and you can find some by digging in the rocks. Bring me three, and I'll give you… something. Something pretty. That doesn't explode.
textes.Plus encore ? Mes conseillers vont adore: Even more? My advisers will love it. The seagulls, much less.
textes.Plus faim ? À ton âge ? Allons donc ! Ti: Not hungry? At your age? Nonsense! Here.
textes.Plus fort ? Je vais réveiller les squele: Louder? I'll wake the skeletons in the graveyard!
textes.Plus gros que celui de la gargouille, ma: Bigger than the gargoyle's one, dear?
textes.Plus jamais de potion le lundi !: No more potions on Mondays, ever!
textes.Plus juste que toi en rentrant, mon chou: More in tune than you on your way home, sweetie.
textes.Plus lentement ? Tes deux pieds gauches: Slower? Are your two left feet struggling?
textes.Plus maintenant ! Ça veut dire qu'avant,: Not any more! That means that before, you were. And that we changed your mind. That's the loveliest thing anyone can say to an Archduchess.
textes.Plus maintenant. Mais quelle carrière !: Not any more. But what a career!
textes.Plus personne ne se souvient de nous, là: Nobody up there remembers us anymore. So I remember twice as hard. My cuttlefish can't believe it.
textes.Plus personne ne… Hmm. HMM. Et comment j: Nobody bows… Hmm. HMM. And how would I see the tops of people's heads? … All right. For you, an exception: you may stop bowing. A little.
textes.Plus personne. Bien. C'est exactement po: Nobody anymore. Right. That's exactly why we write, {surnom}: for the day when nobody remembers. I'll order more ink.
textes.Plus rien ! Tu as tout mangé, petit gour: All gone! You ate everything, little gourmand. Come back tomorrow, I'll make more!
textes.Plus tard je ferai des ponts, comme Pomm: When I grow up I'll build bridges, like Pomme-de-Pin. Bridges all the way to the moon. It's full all the time, so it can wait.
textes.Plus tard je serai coureuse, comme Bondi: When I grow up I'll be a runner, like Bondi. Or a baker. Or both: I'll deliver bread at a run!
textes.Plus tard, j'étais employé de bureau. En: Later, I was an office clerk. Across the street there was a flower shop, and behind the counter, Léa. Every morning, I bought a bouquet “for my mother”. A whole year, every day. On the three hundred and sixty-fifth morning, I held the bouquet out to her over the counter. I'd prepared a two-page speech. I said: “Here.”
textes.Plus tard, je jouerai de la batterie pou: When I grow up, I'll play drums for the Dome's whale, like Rivet. Or I'll be a whale. I haven't decided yet.
textes.Plus tard, je serai comme le professeur: When I grow up, I'll be like Professor Boum. My mum says no. She says “like Héloïse”. That's less fun.
textes.Plus tard, je serai maître de la lévitat: When I grow up, I'll be a master of levitation, like Zéphyrine. Or a master of fire. Or a cook. I don't know yet. Maybe all three.
When I grow up, I'll be a painter, like Dad. Or a lookout, like Gaspard. Or a paint pot. No, not a paint pot.
textes.Plus tard, je serai réparatrice, comme P: When I grow up, I'll be a repairer, like Papa. But mostly I'll fix androids. The other machines never say thank you.
textes.Plus tard, je travaillerai à l'Institut: When I grow up, I'll work at the Institute of Winds!
When I grow up, I'm going to be a cloud too.
textes.Plus un seul pot à chercher : ils sont t: Not a single pot left to find: they've all been found!
textes.Plus une fraise mûre dans ce bac. Elles: Not one ripe strawberry left in this planter. They grow back: it just takes a little patience, and lots of sunshine.
textes.Plus une gargouille sur les falaises ! M: Not a single gargoyle left on the cliffs! My ships leave the Harbour without trembling. Even old Tison, at the back of the harbour, looks happy. He does, he does. I know him.
textes.Plus une seule étoile ne tombe. Il en re: Not a single star is falling any more. There are thousands left up there. They're waiting their turn.
textes.Plus vite que la dernière fois ? Mon arc: Faster than last time? My bow's going to start smoking!
textes.Plusieurs moitiés… Cela fait beaucoup de: Several halves… That's a great many halves. But it's lovely. A drop can be shared a hundred ways, you know. It's still dew.
textes.Plusieurs… Alors tu es riche, petit. Plu: Several… Then you're rich, little one. Richer than Bedaine. Don't tell him: he'd want to swap you for one.
textes.Plutôt bien ! Attention, Saïd va être ja: Quite well! Watch out, Saïd's going to be jealous. Come to the square tonight, we'll see if your voice carries over Omar's bendir.
Over my dead body. Well, rather not.
textes.Poche du dessus, comme toujours. Avec le: Top pocket, as always. With the timetables.
textes.Pof ! Tiens, un de plus pour ta collecti: Poof! There, one more for your collection.
textes.Point météo des champignons : la Cathédr: Mushroom weather report: the Spore Cathedral is glowing blue, purple and orange tonight. Light spores from the south. Mushroomers in a good mood. Sneezing expected.
textes.Pointus… Bon. Chacun ses défauts. Je ne: Pointy… Well. Everyone has their flaws. I'm not judging you. Well, a little.
textes.Pomme à cent pas, en plein cœur. Elle a: Apple at a hundred paces, dead centre. She shouted “luck!” from Fil-d'Aube. The next day, two apples at a hundred paces. “Luck!” The day after, three. She said: “Three lots of luck.” I stopped counting the apples. She's never stopped counting the luck.
textes.Pomme-de-Pin crie « coucou ! » par mon g: Pomme-de-Pin shouts “yoo-hoo!” through my counter window every time she passes. She finds golden acorns. She's got a gorgeous one. She shows it to me from a distance. It's cruel. I love it.
textes.Pomme-de-Pin, c'est le début de toutes m: Pomme-de-Pin is where all my chains begin: she loves singing-stones, and she'd swap anything to get one. A customer like that, my friend, you keep her nice and cosy.
textes.Pommes à gauche, poires à droite… ou l'i: Apples on the left, pears on the right… or the other way round?
textes.Pop ! Bonjour ! Bulle, architecte. C'est: Pop! Hello! Bulle, architect. I'm the one who builds the domes of the Bubble District. Everything is round here: the houses, the windows, the doors, the beds. Even my ideas are round. Down where you live, they say houses have corners? Corners! Where do you put the corners away?
textes.Pop ! Évidemment ! Je le savais, tu as u: Pop! Obviously! I knew it, you have a round face. I mean: a friend's face. Come and see my new dome.
textes.Port-Azur a tout : le port, la plage, la: Port-Azur has it all: the harbour, the beach, the square, the lighthouse, the lookout. And residents who need a helping hand. Help them, and you'll feel at home here.
textes.Port-Azur est trop calme pour un armurie: Port-Azur is too quiet for an armourer. Luckily, tourists love taking home a sword as a souvenir.
textes.Port-Azur est une ville tranquille. Je v: Port-Azur is a quiet town. I make sure it stays that way. No shouting after midnight, no dogs on the beach, no bikes on the quay.
textes.Port-Azur est une île charmante, mais te: Port-Azur is a charming island, but terribly dry, archaeologically speaking. Apart from the lighthouse, nothing is more than two hundred years old.
Port-Azur is five kilometres round. In the middle, the lookout hill. Climb it at golden hour and you'll see the village, the jungle and, on a clear day, the elves' island.
textes.Port-Azur — la perle de l'archipel: Port-Azur — the pearl of the archipelago
Port-Azur is the pearl of the archipelago. The harbour, the square, the beach… and the Perroquet Bleu in the evening. Tell them I sent you.
textes.Port-Azur… La bouillabaisse, la pétanque: Port-Azur… The bouillabaisse, the pétanque, the terraces… well, that's what I've been told. I've been told in great detail.
textes.Port-Boucan, c'était une friche : un por: Port-Boucan used to be wasteland: a closed harbour, empty factories, grey everywhere. We came, we opened the doors, we repainted the walls, we planted tomatoes on the roofs. Now it's the loudest and kindest town in the archipelago.
textes.Port-Boucan, la ville libre du vieux por: Port-Boucan, the free town of the old harbour
textes.Port-Coutelas, mon chou, c'est le dernie: Port-Coutelas, sweetie, is the last free place in the archipelago. No king, no taxes. Just me, and my tab.
textes.Porte de cuivre.\nLa clé ? Demandez\naux:
Copper door.
The key? Ask
the frogs.
textes.Porter le bouquet à Mère Averse, à Rainv: Take the bouquet to Mother Downpour, in Rainville (in the daytime, in the street or on the terrace of the Feedback Café)
textes.Porter le rouage à Hortense, devant la m: Take the cogwheel to Hortense, in front of the town hall
textes.Porter un jour quelque chose de très lég: One day, to carry something very light and very precious. Not a container. Something that can't be weighed.
textes.Porter un pain à Aurore (au château, au: Take a loaf of bread to Aurore (at the castle, at the top of the Hill: take the winding ramps all the way up)
textes.Porter un pain à Gilles (le garde de la: Take a loaf of bread to Gilles (the North Gate guard, in the Lower Town, near the harbour)
textes.Porter un pain à Mamie Rissole (à la tav: Take a loaf of bread to Mamie Rissole (at the tavern, at the back of the Adventurers' Guild)
textes.Porter une affiche à Paulo (à Port-Azur,: Take a poster to Paulo (in Port-Azur, at his restaurant Chez Paulo, on the harbour, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. and from 6 p.m. to 11 p.m.)
textes.Porter une affiche à Tom le Violoneux (s: Take a poster to Tom the Fiddler (on Balafre Island, in Port-Coutelas: he plays in the evening on the stage of the Crâne Fendu, and in the afternoon you can find him on the square)
textes.Porter une affiche à Ulric (sur l'Île de: Take a poster to Ulric (on Montjoie Island, at his inn "La Grenouille Repue", in the Middle Town, near the Great Square)
textes.Porter une carte postale à Barnabé (île: Take a postcard to Barnabé (Jungle Island)
textes.Porter une carte postale à Lyra, l'elfe: Take a postcard to Lyra the elf
textes.Porter une carte postale à Ulfa, à la ta: Take a postcard to Ulfa, at the Forgefer tavern
textes.Porter une carte postale à la reine de l: Take a postcard to the queen of Atlantis
textes.Porter une lettre à Gorgoth le Cornu (à: Take a letter to Gorgoth the Horned (at the arena, or at the baths)
textes.Porter une lettre à Grumbald (au comptoi: Take a letter to Grumbald (at the counter of the inn "Au Diable Repu", at the port)
textes.Porter une lettre à Ombreline (à la Bibl: Take a letter to Ombreline (at the Library of Souls, in the Upper Town)
textes.Poser le Plat de la Grande Réconciliatio: Place the Great Reconciliation dish on the altar of the Colander Temple
textes.Poser le dernier conteneur des Boîtes, p: To set down the last container in the Boxes, for the last family without a home. And then sit in Mademoiselle's cab and look far away. Very far away.
textes.Poser le fromage près de la cale du Requ: Put the cheese down near the hold of the Requin Borgne and wait for Biscotte to come out of his hole: if he climbs onto your shoulder, you've won
textes.Poser les quatre sceaux dans la Porte au: Place the four seals in the Gate of the Four Seals, at the foot of Stoneheart
textes.Poser les trois reliques sur l'Autel des: Place the three relics on the Altar of the Three Suns
Put a letter on Lola's tray. Just one. While her back is turned. And leave fast. No, stay. I don't know yet.
textes.Posez la main, bien à plat… (La boule s': Place your hand, nice and flat… (The ball lights up, hesitates, goes “bzzz”, then displays golden letters.) Let's see: Strength, decent. Agility, enthusiastic. Magic, “maybe later”. Luck, “hmm”. Appetite: EXCEPTIONAL. Hidden talent: “knows how to get back up”. (She stamps three times.) Congratulations! Here is your Adventurer's Card. Rank F. Like everyone else. Even Master Hugues, at the start. Especially Master Hugues.
textes.Posé ! E pour replier l'Alouette, Espace: Landed! E to fold the Alouette, Space to take off again by pedalling.
textes.Posé en douceur ! L'Alouette se replie d: Soft landing! The Alouette folds back into your bag.
textes.Potin du Grand Marché, signé Rosalie Can: Gossip from the Great Market, signed Rosalie Cannelle: “Rumour has it the Burgomaster rehearses his speeches in front of his mirror. The mirror has asked for time off. You didn't hear it from me.”
textes.Potions de sève (trois cœurs !) et tisan: Sap potions (three hearts!) and moon teas. And I buy back anything that grows. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Potions et tisanes, pour le fond du trou: Potions and herbal teas, for the bottom of the pit. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Pots de peinture ouverts, pinceaux prêts: Paint pots open, brushes ready! I've put you in navy blue for now; choose your colour.
textes.Potée, pain de chaudière, galettes, limo: Stew, boiler bread, galettes, Chasm lemonade! Everything's made here, everything's almost free. Leave the rest in the box, if you can. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Pouah ! Recraché comme un noyau de ceris: Ugh! Spat out like a cherry pit! You're dripping with green slime.
textes.Pouce dehors ! Comme tu m'as dit !: Thumb outside! Like you told me!
textes.Pouf… je souffle une minute. Une petite: Phew… I'm catching my breath for a minute. Just a little minute.
textes.Pour Nâga, souviens-toi : la tête à terr: For Nâga, remember: when its head is on the ground, you strike. And when it dives, the three Eyes… like on the fresco in the lair, I bet.
textes.Pour Quark, j'ai inventé une porte de bu: For Quark, I invented a bubble door that only opens if you pull a face. He pulls a different one every day. His mum has to pull a face to get home. So does Pixel. Even the Elder, when she comes to visit. It's the funniest door on the island. Écliptique refuses to go through it.
textes.Pour Radio Boucan et le Sergent qui nous: For Radio Boucan and the Sergeant broadcasting us live! “98.7, Pschhh”!
textes.Pour Zéro ? … Oui. J'en ai gardé une. Un: For Zéro? … Yes. I kept one. Just one. I knew someone would need it one day. I didn't know it would be him. It's in a little black box, resting against the orange container: west of the jetty, the first container, the one that's all alone. Take it. Gently.
textes.Pour accepter des contrats, recruter des: To take on contracts, recruit companions and rise in rank, you must be signed up with the Adventurers' Guild of Montjoie. Églantine, the receptionist, asks for ten coins and a little crystal-ball reading.
textes.Pour aller à la Fronde, il fallait saute: To get to the Fronde, you had to jump across the Chasm on two planks. We decided to build a proper bridge. With rails, bolts, and the help of all the Strata railway workers who came after their shifts. And a young girl from the Guild, Agathe, who carried our planks in secret. We welded it in three months. On opening day, we all crossed it together, holding hands. The Chasm applauded. Three times.
textes.Pour apprendre à accueillir les gens, j': To learn how to welcome people, I spent a week with Halo, at the Gate. I recorded four hundred and twelve “welcomes.” Halo told me the secret is that people smile. I don't know how to smile. I asked the Professor for a smile function. He said: “Later.” Beep. Later never came.
textes.Pour avoir un champignon des fées, Marle: To get a fairy mushroom, Marley gave me a bouquet of banana flowers, red and purple. It was gorgeous. I put them in my hair and danced with them all night. In the morning, I told him “soon”. He smiled as if I'd said yes. Marley always smiles as if you'd said yes.
textes.Pour avoir un champignon des fées, j'ai: To get a fairy mushroom, I gave Lulu a bouquet of banana flowers, red and purple. She said it was the prettiest request on the whole island. She put them in her hair. Then she said: “Soon, Marley.” That was two months ago. The flowers have wilted. I haven't.
textes.Pour chaque fête, je déguise le perroque: For every celebration, I dress up the wooden parrot on the counter. A pirate hat for the harbour festival, sunglasses in summer, a flower crown for the hotel's newlyweds. Toni grumbles that it looks messy. But the day I forget, he's the one who asks: “Nothing on his head tonight?”
textes.Pour chercher mieux, je me penche au bou: To look harder, I lean out at the end of the jetty. Right at the edge. A bit more. Grandpa holds me by the tail, very gently, without looking, like his fishing rod. That way I can lean really, really far. I never fall in the water. Never. Grandpa says I'm good as gold. Mrrrou… yes. Good as gold.
textes.Pour danser ! Évidemment ! Viens ce soir: For dancing! Of course! Come tonight, I'll dedicate the first song to you. And I want to see those feet move.
textes.Pour de bon ? (Elle pose son tricot.) Éc: For good? (She sets down her knitting.) Listen to me, kiddo. Lisse has a factory, to the south-east, behind the Spore Woods: the Grey Factory. Under the factory, there are five floors. Offices, an assembly line, a boiler room, a warehouse... and right at the bottom, the President's Pit, where his Great Digger sleeps, an enormous machine run by a computer. That's where he keeps the plans for the Lisse-Center. No plans, no Lisse-Center. And without the Digger, no more robots. I'm too old to go down. But you... Go down, defeat that machine, and bring me back the plans. And if you meet little Aldric down there... don't hurt him. He's a kid who forgot how to play.
textes.Pour deux, Paulo ! Et… pas de chanson, c: For two, Paulo! And… no song tonight?
textes.Pour devenir guerrier-jaguar, il faut ca: To become a jaguar warrior, you have to capture four opponents. In training, we practise on the other young men. I captured five. The fifth was Tochtli. I grabbed him by the cape, and he squealed like a rabbit. The whole school laughed. The next day, he quit training to become a merchant. He says it was a calling. I say it was me.
To say what we don't dare say.
textes.Pour dire ce qu'on n'ose pas dire… (Elle: To say what you don't dare say… (She looks at you for a long time.) You've understood something. That's why I write. Thank you.
To her, it's the same thing.
textes.Pour en savoir plus sur ce problème : il:
To find out more about this problem: you shouldn't have bought it.

If you call a repairer, give them this information:
Stop code: NOT_CHEAP_AT_ALL_PROGRAM
What failed: turbo_adventure_3000.prg
textes.Pour entendre la mer… même quand ils lui: To hear the sea… even when they have their backs to it!
textes.Pour faire du bruit ensemble ! C'est la: To make noise together! That's the Fronde's motto! You should write it on the Wall. Fusain will lend you a brush.
textes.Pour faire la paix, j'ai offert à Odette: To make peace, I offered Odette a free ride on “Wave 1”, my finest boat. With a brand-new life jacket. She looked at me over her glasses and said: “I grew up in the rigging, young man.” Then she went back to her ledger. I think that was a no. But a no with some info in it.
textes.Pour faire la paix, je lui ai offert une: To make peace, I gave him a quill carved from red coral. It bit him on the first word. He wrote three scrolls about the incident, with a drawing of his finger. Red coral bites, I've always said so! He filed it under my mistakes. Not under his carelessness.
textes.Pour faire naître le Cinquième Soleil, l: To give birth to the Fifth Sun, the gods gathered at Teotihuacan around a great fire. Proud Tecciztecatl, covered in feathers and gold, was afraid to jump. Little Nanahuatzin, humble and covered in spots, jumped first. He became the Sun.
textes.Pour faire plaisir à Glorb, j'ai inventé: To please Glorb, I invented a jelly that doesn't wobble at all: the still jelly. It was as hard as a rock. Glorb looked at it, then said: “That one's definitely not a cousin.” He kept it. It's on his bedside table. He calls it “Pebble.”
textes.Pour forger, il me fallait un foyer. J'a: To forge, I needed a hearth. I picked the biggest port-side cannon, Marie-Jeanne, as my ancestor called her. A whole winter opening her up, filling her with bricks, sewing her a bellows, very badly. The first day she heated up, the whole hull rang like a bell. Down below, Tobias thought we were sinking.
For yesterday. It was spot on.
textes.Pour l'affaire des croissants, j'ai mont: For the croissant case, I set up a stakeout in front of the bakery. Bench on the square, midnight, eyes open. I dozed off around two. At four, Margaux woke me up opening her bakehouse. Six croissants were missing. She handed me the seventh, “for your trouble”. I said: “Exhibit A.” I ate it.
textes.Pour l'affiche du premier Grand Boucan,: For the poster of the first Great Boucan, I wanted black and she wanted green. We argued for three hours. After three hours, we printed it half black, half green. Nobody noticed. Except us. We still talk about it every evening.

For the poster for the first Great Boucan, I wanted green, he wanted black. Three hours of arguing. We printed half and half. I saw two browns. I never told him. He thinks it's our greatest compromise. It's my greatest secret.
textes.Pour l'aider, j'ai monté la garde une nu: To help her, I stood guard one night on her chinampa. I walked too close to the edge, in the dark. Splash. Fully dressed, with the jaguar skin. Xóchitl laughed so hard the herons flew off. She held out an oar, saying: “A jaguar that swims is already quite a feat.” I didn't find it funny. She did.
textes.Pour l'anniversaire de Bulle, je lui ai: For Bulle's birthday, I drew her a round map of Astralys, on a glass disc. The Spire in the centre, the Agora, the Museum, the domes, all around, like a clock. She hung it on the ceiling of her bubble. She says she falls asleep watching it turn. It doesn't turn. But I didn't say anything.
textes.Pour l'anniversaire de Lumi, je lui ai f: For Lumi's birthday, I made her a little lamp that only lights up when you show it a piece of jewellery. She put it on her workbench. It's lit all the time. Mind you, there's a lot of jewellery.
textes.Pour l'anniversaire de Maman, j'ai voulu: For Mummy's birthday I wanted to pick her a moonflower all by myself. I went out at night. I fell asleep in a bush. Daddy found me in the morning with a dandelion in my hand. Mummy put it in a vase. It's still there. All dried up, but still there.
textes.Pour l'anniversaire de la Colonne, il a: For the Column's birthday, he wanted to hang garlands on the cables. I said no. He gave a speech about the word “no”. It was very good, actually.
textes.Pour l'anniversaire de la Colonne, je vo: For the Column's birthday, I wanted garlands on the cables. She refused. I gave a speech on the word “no”. She listened right to the end. The only one who did.
textes.Pour l'enveloppe du Zéphyr, j'ai constru: For the Zéphyr's envelope, I built a giant sewing machine. Fifteen years ago, it took Wilfried's right arm. I helped him make himself a brass arm. A whole night over the plans. The next day, I took the machine apart. Piece by piece. I said nothing. There was nothing to say.
textes.Pour l'essai, Basile a soufflé une bulle: For the test, Basile blew a bubble with a sandwich inside. It rose up perfectly round, magnificent, and burst at twelve metres. The sandwich fell back onto my sun hat. I was finding gherkin in the ribbon until evening. Basile was delighted: “Twelve metres, Adèle! Only three hundred to go!”
textes.Pour l'essai, j'ai mis un sandwich dans: For the test, I put a sandwich in a bubble. It rose magnificently: one metre, five metres, ten, twelve… pop. The sandwich landed right on Adèle's sun hat. She didn't say a word. She removed the gherkin from her ribbon, very calmly. Personally, I think it was an excellent start.
textes.Pour l'examen d'apprenti, il fallait con: For the apprentice exam, you had to know the names of all the Column's pulleys. Their real names are numbers. But I'd given them first names: Gertrude, Paulin, Josette… Mistress Capucine asked me for pulley sixteen. I said “Raymond”. She smiled. I was in.
textes.Pour l'histoire du Titan de Givre, Calci: For the story of the Frost Titan, Calcine loosens her strings, so the violin sounds cold. The children shiver and huddle together. Then, when the hero rekindles the flame, she tightens the strings all at once, and the violin sings warm. The children applaud. So do I, every time.
textes.Pour l'épreuve des flammes, garde le poi: For the flame test, keep your wrist loose and your heart calm. A flame that senses you're scared does all sorts of silly things. Like a puppy. Ask Flammèche.
textes.Pour la Gratuiterie ? Merci ! Je vais lu: For the Free Shop? Thank you! I'll find it a shelf with a nice view.
textes.Pour la Nuit des Lanternes, je prépare l: For the Night of Lanterns, I'm preparing the biggest firework display in the island's history! I'm missing three sulphur crystals, from the sulphur springs outside the walls. Yellow, shiny, they smell of rotten eggs: you can't miss them. I'll buy them from you, and I'll save you a seat in the front row!
textes.Pour la Nuit des Lanternes, je prépare u: For the Night of Lanterns, I'm preparing a new waltz. When the seven Great Lanterns are shining and Zigomar's rockets go up, I'll play it. It's called… no. It's a surprise.
textes.Pour la Nuit des Lanternes, toute la cit: For the Night of Lanterns, the whole city dresses up. I sew dresses with ember sequins that sparkle when you dance. If you come dancing on the Great Square, come and see me first. I won't let you go in that outfit.
To the right house, this time.
textes.Pour la cape numéro six, Colombe a cousu: For cape number six, Colombe sewed little copper plates into the lining. She said the copper would “divert” the lightning. It attracted it. All of it. I shone like a lighthouse for ten seconds. Captain Isidore thought it was a distress signal and sent his seagulls.
textes.Pour la cape numéro six, j'ai mis du cui: For cape number six, I put copper in the lining. I was sure of myself. Violette cast a bolt, and all the lightning from the storm came down on her. She shone like a lighthouse. Her hair was throwing off blue sparks. It was, I must admit, the most beautiful thing I've ever seen on a human being. I made a sketch of it.
textes.Pour la consoler, j'ai raconté à Léa que: To cheer her up, I told Léa that Gérard arrived late to our own wedding: he was photographing the church. From the outside. From every angle. The priest had to go and fetch him. Léa laughed between two sobs, a funny noise, like a kettle that can't make up its mind. I didn't tell her that. We're friends now.
textes.Pour la cuillère, peut-être. Toi, tu viv: For the spoon, maybe. You'll live.
For the kitchen. The king is hungry.
textes.Pour la dent de dragon de mer, j'ai orga: For the sea dragon tooth, I held a little ceremony in my room: the glass dome, a velvet cushion, Pauline and Edmond as witnesses. Fernand was invited. He stayed in the doorway, beret in hand, and coughed the whole way through. Emotion. I wanted to pay him double, for the danger. He refused. Then he accepted.
textes.Pour la dernière fête de l'Aube, j'ai ti: For the last Dawn Festival I wove Nessa a ribbon the colour of sunrise. She danced all night with it, and by dawn it was wrapped round three trees, the fountain and Haldir. It took a whole morning to untangle Haldir. He didn't seem in any hurry.
textes.Pour la distraire, je lui ai raconté la: To take her mind off things, I told her about the purple jungle berry I'd tasted that very morning, and my tongue staying blue all day. I showed her. She laughed, just once, very loudly, then apologised for laughing. I told her it was on the prescription.
textes.Pour la foire du plus long jour, il m'a: For the Longest Day Fair, he bought my best copal. The fragrant one. The very fragrant one. He burned a mountain of it. The priestess of Per-Hâpy coughed through her whole chant. Cuauhtli came back to complain: “Too much smoke!” I told him: “You bought too much, I didn't sell too much.” He left without a comeback.
textes.Pour la foire du plus long jour, je lui: For the fair of the longest day, I bought his best copal from him, “scented like the breath of the gods”. I burned it before the three suns. The smoke was so thick that the priestess of Per-Hâpy coughed through her whole hymn. Tochtli told me afterwards: “The gods got their money's worth.” It was my money.
textes.Pour la fresque du mur de son, Lulu m'a: For the mural on the wall of sound, Lulu asked me for all my party photos. She spread them out on the sand for a whole night, by the light of a mushroom. In the morning, she said: “It's too beautiful, I can't start.” The wall is still white. But she gave me back my photos better sorted than I'd ever sorted them.
textes.Pour la fête de l'année, elle m'a tissé: For the New Year festival, she wove me a very simple robe. I found it almost too simple. Then I went out onto the terrace, facing the rising sun: in the hem, invisible otherwise, there was a sun disc woven into the thickness of the linen. It only shows against the light. Tiyi never mentioned it. Neither did I.
textes.Pour la fête de l'année, j'ai tissé sa r: For the New Year festival, I wove her robe with a secret: a sun disc, hidden in the thickness of the hem. You can only see it against the light. On the morning of the festival, she stepped out onto the terrace, facing Ra, and it appeared. She didn't say anything to me. She just looked at me, from afar. That was enough.
textes.Pour la fête, je prête mes plus belles l: For the party, I lend my finest lanterns to the square. They all come back. Except one or two, which the pirates “borrow”.
textes.Pour la lumière bleue, je suis monté à l: For the blue light, I went up to the bow with a compass and a protractor, and worked out the angle with Grégoire all afternoon.
