Result: right in front of the Gate of the Four Seals. I put a blue dot on the map, with “according to Grégoire (?)”. He didn't speak to me for three weeks. The question mark was tiny.
textes.Pour la narguer, chaque matin, je compte: To tease her, every morning, I count my three carrots in front of her stall. One. Two. Three. Very slowly. One day, she put a fourth carrot on her counter. Without a word. I looked at it. For a long time. I didn't take it. I ran off. It was a trap. A trap carrot.
textes.Pour la numéro douze, Babette ! Grenouil: For number twelve, Babette! Frog with carrots!
textes.Pour la peine, ils t'offrent un morceau: For your trouble, they give you a piece of what's on the table.
textes.Pour la petite inconnue à la capuche ? T: For the little stranger in the hood? Always.
textes.Pour la première mission de la Guilde de: For the Little Heroes' Guild's first mission, we wanted to catch a turnip all by ourselves, at night, in the Southern Fields. Noisette kept watch, I had my hammer. A turnip came out of the ground. It looked at us. We looked at it. It went back into the ground. Noisette wrote: “Mission: success. The turnip got scared.” I think we were the ones who were scared.
textes.Pour la remercier des protège-cornes, je: To thank her for the horn guards, I wrote her a poem. I was looking for a rhyme for “Ferronde”, I couldn't find one, so I wrote “Ferronde” twice. She nailed it above her anvil. The apprentices make fun of it. She tells them it's the most beautiful poem ever written about her. It's also the only one.
textes.Pour la remercier, j'ai offert à madame: To thank her, I gave Madame Margaux a seagull feather I'd picked up on the jetty: the whitest of the season. For her own collection. She told me she didn't collect anything. I replied that everyone collects something. She put the feather in a jar, on the shelf. Her collection had begun.
textes.Pour la remercier, j'ai tricoté une hous: To thank her, I knitted a studded cover for her sewing machine. She put it on. She said the machine looked like a little punk. Since then, she calls it Clou-Junior.
textes.Pour la remercier, je lui ai tricoté un: To thank her, I knitted her a nurse's cap. With studs. She said it wasn't quite regulation. She wears it every night at the earplug counter. She says people do what she tells them more readily.
textes.Pour la réouverture des Strates, je suis: For the reopening of the Strata, I went down with Mistress Capucine. Going down is better: you can't see the drop. Down there, a canteen lady served me a hot chocolate so thick the spoon stood up in it. I got my colour back. Three colours, according to her.
textes.Pour la réouverture, elle est arrivée av: For the reopening, she turned up with a bag of cinnamon as big as she is. “I'm going to wake up your noses!” She opened it in the middle of Pearl Square. The whole city sneezed at the same time. She said: “There. Now you're awake.” Professor Benthos wrote down the time.
textes.Pour la réouverture, elle est descendue: For the reopening, she came down with a pot of Strata broth on her knees. The whole way down, she held the lid on. Marius says she's the most focused passenger in the history of the line. She didn't look at a single ray. But the broth arrived hot.
textes.Pour la réouverture, elle est montée en: For the reopening, she came up by airship, not by capsule. “On principle,” she said. She circled the island three times before mooring. So I'd get a good look at her. I got a good look. I beat her on the fourth lap.
textes.Pour la réouverture, elle m'a envoyé un: For the reopening, she sent me a sachet of summit tea, with a note: “All nominal.” I sent her back a bubble from the Fountain, in a tightly sealed flask, with a note: “Same here.” She put it on her console, next to her four indicator lights. She wrote to tell me the bubble was holding.
textes.Pour la réouverture, elle m'a envoyé une: For the reopening, she sent me a giant strawberry, as big as a fist. It took three days to come down. It arrived a bit tired, but still giant. I cut it into twelve. Everyone in the Greenhouse Dome got a piece. I planted the seeds. We'll see.
textes.Pour la réouverture, il a voulu un ruban: For the reopening, he wanted a thirty-metre ribbon. I suggested thirty centimetres. He sighed, and cut it with me. Then he gave a forty-minute speech. I answered him in two sentences. He shook my hand and said: “You will always beat me.” I didn't smile. Well, by a millimetre.
textes.Pour la réouverture, il est descendu ave: For the reopening, he came down with me without closing his eyes once. At the bottom, he said: “Uncle, I wasn't scared.” Then he thought about the ride back up. He turned green as a pea. We let the next Funicular go. And the one after that.

For the reopening, he came down with a jar: a cloud, for me. It arrived empty. Aurèle was terribly sorry. I found it marvellous: proof that a cloud can't stand the pressure! We wrote a paper together. The first paper in history signed by both up top and down below.
textes.Pour la réouverture, il voulait un ruban: For the reopening, he wanted a thirty-metre ribbon around the Column. Mistress Capucine said no. They cut a thirty-centimetre one, together. I held the scissors. I've rarely been so moved by a ribbon.
textes.Pour la scène de la Halle, Copeau a voul: For the stage in the Hall, Copeau wanted to test how solid it was by jumping on it. I decided to change the colour of the spotlights with every jump. He jumped for an hour. I changed colour two thousand times. Rouille walked in and applauded. Copeau went bright red. Well, bright blue, at that moment.
textes.Pour la soigner sans qu'elle gigote, je: To treat her without her wriggling, I give her a jar to sort: red seeds on one side, black seeds on the other. In the end she asked me if she could be a herbalist. Then an archer. Then an explorer. The jar is still half sorted.
textes.Pour la tête de son dragon, Ferraille av: For his dragon's head, Ferraille needed me. Two tonnes. I lifted it, he welded it, I held it the whole time. Three hours. When he'd finished, he said: “You can let go.” I let go ever so gently. The dragon went “crrrr”. Ferraille said it was thanking us.
textes.Pour le Grand Boucan, on aura des gens d: For the Great Boucan, we'll have people from every island! Pirates, adventurers, tourists from Port-Azur! THE SOUND WILL HAVE TO BE PERFECT! … for once.
textes.Pour le Plat sacré ? (Il goûte la sauce,: For the sacred Dish? (He tastes the sauce, for a long time, eyes closed.) … It is worthy. It needs a bit of salt, but it is worthy. Take a ladleful with the Sacred Ladle, there, at the edge. Just one. And blow on it. Then go and see the Captain, on the beach: he's the one who has the Golden Grater. Well, who had it.
textes.Pour le Sans-Pitié, elle m'a commandé qu: For the Merciless, she ordered four hundred copper nails and twelve iron fittings from me. I made them. I brought them to her still hot, in a bucket. She counted them one by one, in front of me. Four hundred. She nodded. So did I. It's the longest compliment anyone's ever paid me.
textes.Pour le bal de l'an dernier, Grisette m': For last year's ball, Grisette sewed me a dress with a twelve-metre train. During the waltz, the train got caught on Asmodin's horns, and he went round the dance floor three times backwards behind me. The guests thought it was a new dance. The next day, half the court was copying it.
textes.Pour le concours de la fête, Tiburce et: For the festival contest, Tiburce and I had to create an outfit together. He wanted the horns clearly visible, I wanted a cape. Three weeks of arguing. The result: a cape that opens like two wings and lets the horns shine. We won the prize. He was right about the horns. I've never told him. He knows.
textes.Pour le coup de pioche, une part de tart: For the pickaxe swing, a slice of pie… and what the tunnel turned up.
textes.Pour le couronnement de Thorgal, j'ai fo: For Thorgal's coronation, I forged the king's axe in ten days. A marvel. On the day of the celebration, in front of the whole court, Nori came up, squinted, and said: “Your third rune is upside down.” It was. The whole Great Hall laughed. By my beard, I can still hear that hall laughing.
textes.Pour le duel de la fête de l'Aube, Colom: For the Dawn festival duel, Colombe had made me a new cape, black and red. I slipped on an apple at the first step. The cape unfurled as I fell, like a theatre curtain. Colombe, in the audience, applauded. She shouted: “It falls magnificently!” She meant the cape. I took it as being about me.
textes.Pour le grand bal, j'ai cousu à l'Archid: For the grand ball, I sewed Archduchess Ignatia a dress with a twelve-metre train. During the waltz, the train got caught on Asmodin's horns, and he did three laps of the floor backwards behind her. The guests thought it was a new dance. Ignatia asked me for shorter dresses. I make her eight-metre trains.
textes.Pour le grand bal, je lui ai cousu une r: For the grand ball, I sewed her a dress with a twelve-metre train. During the waltz, the train got caught on Asmodin's horns, and he did three laps of the floor backwards behind her, very dignified. The guests thought it was a new dance, and the next day, half the court was copying it. I got ten orders for trains. Thank you, Asmodin.
textes.Pour le jury ? Dites-leur que mes bulles: For the jury? Tell them my bubbles make people happy. It's been measured: people smile 34% more near my machine.
textes.Pour le jury, Héloïse m'a demandé mon av: For the jury, Héloïse asked my opinion on Capucine's cannon. I said: “I hadn't thought of that.” On Basile's machine: “I hadn't thought of that.” On the automaton: the same. She wrote it all down, very seriously, in her notebook. I wonder what she does with my opinions. They're all the same.
textes.Pour le nouveau quai, il y a eu ruban, c: For the new quay, there was a ribbon, scissors and a brass band. He cut the ribbon three metres from the edge. The ribbon was too short, it had to be lengthened with a bit of my string. Nobody said anything. Me neither. I just held the string for him.
textes.Pour le poisson ! HA ! Au moins, tu es h: For the fish! HA! At least you're honest. But I'm the one who shouts the fish. So deep down, you come for my voice. You just don't know it yet.
textes.Pour le premier Grand Boucan, j'avais to: For the first Great Boucan, I'd forgotten everything: the guests, the times, the chairs. Sirène got out her notebook. In two hours, everything was ready. On the last page, she'd written: “Remember to make Rouille breathe.” She remembered.
textes.Pour le premier feu d'artifice de la vil: For the city's first fireworks, I carried Zéro on my shoulders. He waved his broom like a flag. The whole quay was laughing. It was the first time I understood why humans like noise.
textes.Pour le remercier, j'ai peint sa moustac: To thank him, I painted his moustache into a corner of my view of the port. Tiny, on the jetty, like a black seagull. He noticed it straight away. He didn't say a word. But that's the painting he hung above reception. Perfectly straight. To the millimetre.
textes.Pour le remercier, je lui ai offert une: To thank him, I gave him a sardine made to his recipe, on a plate with a flower. He ate it without flinching, all of it, in front of his grill. He was smiling, but his eyes were watering a little. The smoke, surely. A man of embers, Mustapha: he never says a bad word about other people's cooking.
textes.Pour le sanctuaire de Tlaloc, il faut un: For Tlaloc's shrine, you need a rain jar filled to the brim. I'll make you one, if the high priest sends you.
textes.Pour le sanctuaire rouge de Huitzilopoch: For Huitzilopochtli's red shrine, you need copal. I have some, the best. Six coins, and the smoke is fragrant.
textes.Pour le voyage de noces, Léa voulait voi: For the honeymoon, Léa wanted to see the sea. She'd never seen it. So: Port-Azur, the Grand Hotel, room seven. The first nine days were the best of my life. On the tenth, we were playing in the waves in front of the Coco Loco, I raised my hand to splash her, and my wedding ring wasn't there any more.
textes.Pour le voyage de noces, j'ai dit : « La: For the honeymoon, I said: “The sea.” Port-Azur, the Grand Hotel, room seven. The first morning, I stayed an hour on the balcony looking at it. Nine perfect days. On the tenth, in the waves in front of the Coco Loco, Hugo raised his hand, and his hand was bare. I cried on the balcony all night. Ten days!
textes.Pour les Nuées, je n'ai eu droit qu'à tr: For the Clouds, I was only allowed thirty centimetres of ribbon. So I dream of cutting the two that are left, the Strata's and the Dome's, on the same day, in front of the people of the Clouds, Hautefond, the Strata and the Dome all together. And giving a four-hour speech. Fine. Four minutes. I'll make an effort.
textes.Pour les Nuées, puis pour les Strates, j: For the Clouds, and then for the Strata, I was only allowed thirty centimetres of ribbon. So I dream of cutting the last one, the Dome's, in front of the people of the Clouds, Hautefond, the Strata and the Dome all together. And giving a four-hour speech. Fine. Four minutes. I'll make an effort.

For the Clouds, and then for the Strata, I was only allowed thirty centimetres of ribbon. For the Dome, seven and a half centimetres: there were four of us cutting! So I dream of a ribbon all to myself, around the entire Column, in front of the people of the Clouds, Hautefond, the Strata and the Dome all together. And giving a four-hour speech. Fine. Four minutes. I'll make an effort.
textes.Pour les babouches, il fallait la pointu: For the slippers, we needed Rachid's exact shoe size. Karim could guess it, of course, but I wanted to be sure. One afternoon, Rachid was napping on his carpets. I tiptoed over with my tape. He snored the whole time. That evening, he told everyone he'd dreamed of a cat tickling his feet.
textes.Pour les chiens sauvages du champ de lav: About the wild dogs of the lava field, we don't agree. I say we must drive them far from our walls. She says we must talk to them. We argued through a whole dinner. The next day, she brought me a list of names for the wild dogs. Just in case. I kept the list.
textes.Pour les cinquante ans de la Fronde, Bra: For the Fronde's fiftieth birthday, Brasero asked me to forge a great bell. I forged it. It's out of tune. On purpose. He said it was perfect.
textes.Pour les cinquante ans de la Fronde, il: For the Fronde's fiftieth anniversary, he invited me on stage. I went up. I said nothing. The whole Fronde applauded my silence for five minutes. I think it was my best speech.
textes.Pour les deux cents ans de la boulangeri: For the two hundredth anniversary of Sylwen's bakery, I gave my girls a heart-shaped frame. They took a month to fill it. Sylwen cried when she saw it, then said she'd never eat it. My girls were a bit offended. I explained. They understood.
textes.Pour les deux cents ans de ma boulangeri: For my bakery's two hundredth birthday, Gilwen brought me a heart-shaped honeycomb. Her bees had built it like that, all by themselves, in a frame she'd carved specially. I've never dared eat it. It's still on my shelf. The oven looks at it.
textes.Pour les dix ans des Soupapes, j'ai voul: For the Valves' tenth anniversary, I wanted to give them an organ. I didn't have an organ. I had pipes. Lots of pipes. Over a year, I collected forty-two: stove pipes, boiler pipes, locomotive pipes, and an old pipe from the Column. On opening night, it played all by itself, from my punched cards. Rivet dropped his drumsticks.
textes.Pour les mesurer, je fais monter les chi: To measure them, I get the dogs up on Velours's table one by one. One day, Madame Croquette lay right down on a patch she was sewing and fell asleep. Velours finished the patch around her. Croquette woke up with a patch sewn on her back. She's very proud of it.
textes.Pour les mâts, il me faudrait les grands: For the masts, I'd need the tall jungle trees, but you have to cross spider territory. I asked Brutus to come with me. He said no. I asked if he was scared. He said yes. I burst out laughing, then admitted I was too. We drank a toast at the Crâne Fendu, to our fears. The mast can wait.
textes.Pour les neuf cents ans de Tempo, je lui: For Tempo's nine-hundredth birthday, I made him a clock-shaped cake. I ran, I was forty minutes late, and I dropped it in front of him. The sugar hands stopped at midnight. He looked at it for a long time. Then he ate it, slice by slice, right on the hour. It was the finest compliment.
textes.Pour les rondes de nuit, elle a cousu de: For the night rounds, she sewed felt pads onto the knees of my armour. The first evening, I came home without a sound and suddenly appeared in the kitchen. She got such a fright she threw her hammer at me. I caught it in mid-air. Ever since, I make a little clang on purpose on the landing, to warn her.
textes.Pour m'apprendre la prière de soin, Père: To teach me the healing prayer, Father Clotaire had me tend a wilted plant for a week. On the seventh day, it bloomed again. I ran to tell him. He was asleep on the bench. I woke him with a shout of joy, he fell off the bench, and I had to heal him. He was my second patient. He said I'd made progress.
textes.Pour m'excuser, je laisse parfois une po: To apologise, I sometimes leave an apple on the lighthouse step. A nice one, good and red. The next day, it's gone. He's never said thank you. But one morning, the core was sitting on the step, standing up straight, like an answer. I decided that meant “thank you”.
textes.Pour ma centième descente, Odon m'a atte: For my hundredth descent, Odon waited for me at the exit with a cake. A little candle on top, shaped like a 1. He told me: “A hundred times the first floor. Nobody knows these cellars as well as you.” It's true. I could give guided tours of the slimes. They recognise me.
textes.Pour ma fête, il m'a offert des babouche: For my birthday, he gave me babouches with little bells sewn inside. “That way, you'll hear yourself coming.” I wear them. Not for him: because I can hear myself coming, it's true. So can the whole souk. Hnia says I jingle like a goat from the oasis.
textes.Pour ma rubrique, une seule question : q: For my column, just one question: what's the biggest news of your life? I'm writing it all down, go ahead!
textes.Pour ma septième potion anti-foudre, je: For my seventh anti-lightning potion, I asked her to cast a little bolt in my shop, as a test. The bolt hit the ceiling, bounced off a vial and hit me. My hair went off like a firecracker. Violette said “… it happens” while apologising. I wrote: “Anti-lightning potions must be drunk by the apothecary too.”
textes.Pour me consoler de la moustache, Edmond: To console me over the moustache, Edmond found me a roc's egg in the hotel attic. Porcelain. He handed it to me on a silver tray: “With the compliments of the management.” I put it in the display case in room twelve. It isn't real, but it's very distinguished. Like Edmond.
textes.Pour me faire pardonner les moutons vert: To make up for the green sheep, I sent Écrou's grandfather a jar of my de-greener. A personal formula! The next day, the sheep were blue. Sky blue, very pretty. Écrou came to tell me at the café. She didn't laugh. I did, a little. Then not at all, when she put her grandfather's letter on the table.
textes.Pour me faire pardonner tout ce safran «: To make up for all that “wasted” saffron, I wove her a saffron-coloured scarf, the most beautiful of the year. She looked at it for a long time and said: “What a waste.” Since then, she wears it every day. Every day! Repeating “what a waste” to anyone who'll listen. That's her way of saying thank you.
textes.Pour me faire pardonner, il m'a proposé: To make it up to me, he offered to write a second song, “truly tragic, I promise”. It was about a swordsman who waits years for his rival and finally sees him arrive. It was very beautiful. I didn't cry. Well, a bit. Then he added a verse about my scarf. I don't know how he found out.
textes.Pour me faire pardonner, j'ai fait une d: To make it up to him, I made a second potion, the right one this time. He drank it. He stayed awake a whole night, eyes wide open. In the morning he came to see me at the shop and said: “Mr Aubin, I counted the stars. There are more than forty.” Then he handed back the empty vial and told me he preferred sleeping.
textes.Pour me faire pardonner, j'ai offert à A: To make amends, I gave Asmodin a cup that stirs the tea by itself. I'd wound the spring a little too tight: the cup took off from the tray and landed in the throne-room chandelier. The Archduchess applauded. Asmodin sent me back a note: “Unacceptable.” I had it framed. It's the only word he's ever written to me.
textes.Pour me faire pardonner, j'ai soufflé un: To make it up to him, I blew a bubble around one of his boxes of nothing. It floated for three seconds above the bench. Philibert's eyes went wide: “Did that already exist?” I said: “No.” He shook my hand very hard. He still doesn't like that I don't like his boxes. But he talks to me again.
textes.Pour me faire pardonner, je lui ai appor: To make it up to her, I brought her cochineal from Aztlán, the best on the lake. I charged her for the sacks. Just the sacks! A man has to live. She paid for them, giving me a funny look. The next time, her feathers came wrapped in my sacks. And she billed me for them.
textes.Pour me faire pardonner, je lui ai donné: To make amends, I gave her some dried hibiscus: a magnificent red, in the bowl. On her canvas, the next day, it had turned brown. Dead leaf. She showed me the painting without a word. I said it was very autumnal. We still laugh about it. Well, mostly me.
textes.Pour me mesurer, Grisette grimpe sur une: To measure me, Grisette climbs a ladder. I have to stay still and not breathe, otherwise the measurements are wrong. I hold my breath for a very long time. When I finally breathe, I say “sorry”. She says I'm the politest customer of her career. And the longest to sew.
textes.Pour me prouver qu'elle avait raison, el: To prove she was right, she sent me eleven bits of news at once. I replied with just one: “The Great Singer sang for the reopening.” She wrote back: “Fine. That one's worth eleven.” It's the finest victory of my career.
textes.Pour me réconcilier avec Électre, je lui: To make peace with Électre, I gave her a lightning rod shaped like a bouquet. Copper stems, brass petals. She said “thank you” through pursed lips. That very evening, lightning struck right in the middle of the petals. It works! She kept it. She never told me, but I've seen it, on the roof of her lab.
textes.Pour me venger du bruit de ses épées, j': To get back at him for the noise of his swords, I put the ash pepper on his side of the stall. Since then, he sneezes all day. But one very windy day, I saw Kraxx shield my jars with his big shield while I chased after my awning. He said nothing. Neither did I. The war goes on. But we say hello.
textes.Pour me venger, je lui ai dit que ma cui: To get my revenge, I told her my spoon was the finest in the port and that I was going to order a second, matching one, on the other arm. She got scared everyone would start asking for cutlery. Since then, she refuses to tattoo anything at all on me, and I walk past her tent twirling a spoon between my fingers.
textes.Pour mes cent ans, dans la cave, Ulfa m': For my hundredth birthday, down in the cellar, Ulfa gave me a mug engraved with my name. Then she said: “You'll touch the big vat next year.” Twenty years later, I still hadn't touched it, and I left. I took the mug with me. I drink from it every evening. I've never told her.
textes.Pour mes cent ans, ma maman m'a offert u: For my hundredth birthday, my mum gave me a holo-camera. I photographed the whole of Gloop in one day. There was nothing but green. That evening, I told mum: “I want to photograph another colour.” She cried a little, she melted a little, and she bought me a saucer ticket. Blorp.
textes.Pour mes cinquante ans de train, il m'a: For my fifty years on the train, he gave me a liftkeeper's whistle. It doesn't whistle: it's broken. He said: “That way, we're the same.” I wear it round my neck.
textes.Pour mes deux cents ans de garde, Corali: For my two hundredth year on guard, Coralin carved me a portrait. I put it next to the Gate, in plain view. Everyone thinks it's a sea urchin. I know it's me. We have the same expression when nothing's happening.
textes.Pour mes dix ans de service, la mairesse: For my ten years of service, the mayor gave me a blue tie. I never take it off. It has been cleaned forty times.
textes.Pour mes dix ans, Lucie m'a offert une p: For my tenth birthday, Lucie gave me a pearl, the first she'd ever found all by herself. I sewed it onto a blue ribbon. Since then, she's given me one every year: there are fourteen. I wear it on feast days. The day I leave, I'll wear it too. That way, Lucie will come with me a little.
textes.Pour mes galettes, Yum Kab ! Rien que po: For my flatbreads, Yum Kab! Only for my flatbreads!
textes.Pour mes galettes. Évidemment. Pour quoi: For my flatbreads. Obviously. What else?
textes.Pour mes huit ans, Maman m'a offert un p: For my eighth birthday, Mum gave me a little hammer with my name engraved on it. I improved it: now it has gears, a crank and a whistle. It doesn't hit very well any more, but it sings when you shake it. Mum pulled a funny face. Dad laughed. Then he stopped, because Mum was looking at him.
textes.Pour mes quatre mille jours sans acciden: For my four thousand days without an accident, she gave me a pebble from the gallery where she'd started. She said: “She sends her regards.” I put it on my desk. I say hello to it too.
textes.Pour mes quatre-vingts ans, Odon m'a ouv: For my eightieth birthday, Odon opened the dungeon gate for me and let me go down the first step. Just one. The stone was cold and damp, and it smelt of jelly and old stories. I put my hand on the wall. Odon said: “There. You've been.” I told him the mimics still bite. He smiled.
textes.Pour mes sept ans, Maman m'a fabriqué un: For my seventh birthday, Mum built me a board out of an oven door and four wagon wheels. She'd set it to “snail speed”. I cried. Brasero told me: “A board is like an idea: you have to let it roll a bit.” So I souped it up. Mum pretended to be cross. Brasero pretended not to know why.
textes.Pour mes soixante-dix ans, Jos m'a forgé: For my seventieth birthday, Jos forged me a crêpe spatula with a handle shaped like a gull. He said: “That's the gull finally paying its bill.” A joke about the gull joke, the one all of Carène tells. I laughed so hard I botched the first crêpe of the evening. I still serve with it.
textes.Pour mes trente ans, Vinyle m'a laissé é: For my thirtieth birthday, Vinyle let me listen to the record twice. He said it was a birthday present, and that I mustn't tell anyone. Oops.
textes.Pour mes trente ans, j'ai voulu allumer: For my thirtieth birthday, I wanted to light all five braziers with a single gesture. They lit. So did my eyebrows. Mother Sage redrew them in charcoal for the party, one higher than the other. I looked surprised all evening. Even when they gave me my present. Especially when Borée walked in.
textes.Pour mes trois cents ans, il m'a offert: For my three hundredth birthday, he gave me a shell. I put my ear to it, and deep inside, I heard his voice saying “good evening”. I pretended I could only hear the sea. He looked so relieved. I listen to it every evening, before I go to sleep.
textes.Pour mes vingt ans, ma tante m'a offert: For my twentieth birthday, my aunt gave me a brand-new iron key, with a label: “Inn”. There isn't a single door in the inn, it's all hammocks. I asked what it opened. She said: “Your future door. On dry land.” I've worn it round my neck for ten years.
textes.Pour mesurer Gorgoth, j'ai besoin d'une: To measure Gorgoth, I need a ladder. He stands perfectly still, holds his breath, and whispers “sorry” every time he breathes. He's the politest customer I've ever had. And the longest to sew for: six metres of cape.
textes.Pour mesurer Gorgoth, je grimpe sur une: To measure Gorgoth, I climb a ladder. He stands still and holds his breath, so as not to throw the measurements off. When he finally breathes, he whispers “sorry”. Once, he held his breath so long he turned purple. I had to order him to breathe. He apologised for apologising.
textes.Pour mesurer les chiens, Chaussette les: To measure the dogs, Chaussette has them climb onto my table one by one. One day, Madame Croquette lay down on a patch I was sewing and fell asleep. I finished the patch around her. She woke up with a patch sewn onto her coat. She's never taken it off.
textes.Pour moi ? C'est chouette. Si je n'en ai: For me? That's cool. If I don't need it, I'll put it in the Swap Shop: Lumi will find it a new friend.
textes.Pour moi ? C'est gentil. Je vais le pose: For me? How kind. I'll put it on the mantelpiece, between the clock and the clock.
For me? How kind. I'll put it on my mantelpiece, next to my crystal lantern. She likes company.
textes.Pour moi ? C'est gentil. Je vais lui tro: For me? How kind. I'll find it a little spot on the shelf.
textes.Pour moi ? C'est sympa. Si je n'en ai pa: For me? That's nice. If I don't need it, I'll leave it at the Free Shop: it'll make someone else happy.
textes.Pour moi ? Comme c'est aimable. Je le po: For me? How kind. I'll put it by the fireplace.
textes.Pour moi ? Comme c'est terrestre ! Je ne: For me? How Earthly! I have no idea what it's for, so I'll treasure it.
textes.Pour moi ? Merci ! Je vais le poser au b: For me? Thank you! I'll put it by my porthole. The lanternfish will come and admire it.
textes.Pour moi ? Merci. Je le poserai près de: For me? Thank you. I'll place it by the household altar.
textes.Pour moi ? Merci. Je vais le poser sur m: For me? Thank you. I'll put it on my balcony, between the strawberry plants and the solar panel.
textes.Pour moi ? Oh… ma queue s'agite toute se: For me? Oh… my tail's wagging all by itself. Thank you!
textes.Pour moi ? Oh… {dernier_cadeau}. C'est d: For me? Oh… {dernier_cadeau}. How thoughtful. Thank you, {surnom}.
textes.Pour moi ? {dernier_cadeau}… Hmpf. C'est: For me? {dernier_cadeau}… Hmph. It's… it's very nice. Thank you, {surnom}.
textes.Pour moi ? {dernier_cadeau}… Merci, {sur: For me? {dernier_cadeau}… Thank you, {surnom}. Humans sometimes have the manners of elves.
textes.Pour moi ? {dernier_cadeau}… Un trésor d: For me? {dernier_cadeau}… A treasure from the world above! Thank you, {surnom}.
textes.Pour moi ? … Bon. Merci. Mais si c'est p: For me? … Well. Thanks. But if it's to butter me up, it only half works.
textes.Pour moi, tu restes le petit qui lève le: To me, you're still the little one with his hand up.
For me. I'm very hungry on Fridays.
textes.Pour mon anniverfaire, Tonneau m'a offer: For my birthday, Tonneau gave me a coconut. The biggetht in the jungle! I looked at it, I looked at my two teeth, and I thaid: “What am I thuppothed to bite it with?” He hiccupped in thurprithe. Now it floatth at the end of my line. It'th the finetht float on the jetty. The fith are jealouth.
textes.Pour mon anniversaire, Brindille devait: For my birthday, Brindille was supposed to deliver my invitations. But the day before, I'd already shouted the date on the square. Everyone came without an invitation. Brindille arrived at the party with her bag full of useless letters. I asked her to dance to make it up to her. She trod on my feet. On purpose, I think.
textes.Pour mon anniversaire, Colombe m'a offer: For my birthday, Colombe gave me a very plain hat, with nothing on it. Grey. She said: “For the days when you want people to see you, and not the hat.” I've never worn it. I keep it in a box. I look at it sometimes, on the days when I forget things. It reminds me that someone sees me.
textes.Pour mon anniversaire, Fañch a posé douz: For my birthday, Fañch put twelve lanterns on twelve buoys in the bay. I thought it was a fleet. I woke the Admiral. She came in her coat, looked for a long time through the spyglass, and said: “Those are buoys, Grégoire.” I've never been so ashamed. Fañch was laughing on the beach. I can still hear him.
textes.Pour mon anniversaire, Lou m'a laissée m: For my birthday, Lou let me sit in the Little Diver, at the quay, with the portholes shut. I held the controls for an hour. I said: “Ballast tanks full, we're diving!” We didn't move. It was still the best dive of my life. I wrote it all down in my notebook. Making some of it up.
textes.Pour mon anniversaire, Sextant m'a dessi: For my birthday, Sextant drew me a round map of Astralys, on a glass disc. I hung it from the ceiling of my bubble. In the evening, I look at it as I fall asleep, and it feels like it's turning gently, like a clock. Sextant says it doesn't turn. I'm sure it does. At night.
textes.Pour mon anniversaire, Zigomar m'a envoy: For my birthday, Zigomar sent up a rocket that was supposed to draw a heart above the Great Square. It drew a kidney. A huge kidney, pink and gold. The whole square applauded, and Zigomar shouted that it was on purpose. I laughed so hard I had to sit down. He took that as a yes. It wasn't a yes. Not yet.
textes.Pour mon anniversaire, Zigomar m'a fait: For my birthday, Zigomar made me a firework shaped like an envelope, above the post office. The envelope opened in the sky, and a shower of sparks came out, like a letter flying away. It was magnificent. Then there was a little boom, and the post office roof lost a tile. Just one. That's a record, for him.
textes.Pour mon anniversaire, il m'a offert un: For my birthday, he gave me a flowerpot. He broke it while handing it to me. The flower was fine. It's still on my windowsill.
textes.Pour mon dos, je passe par la porte de d: For my back, I go in by the back door, the one on the alley, at the hour when the square is having lunch. Once, Bernard saw me go in. I said: “Jar inspection.” He nodded. The doctor laughed so hard the jars shook. I keep my kepi on during treatment. A sergeant is still a sergeant, even lying on his stomach.
textes.Pour mon départ, Sylwen m'a fait un pain: When I left, Sylwen made me a travel loaf with honey from the Mother Tree, “that keeps for a month”. It lasted two days: a green parrot came every morning to steal a piece, squawking “Hellooo”. I found out later his name was Gaston.
textes.Pour mon neuf-centième anniversaire, Glo: For my nine-hundredth birthday, Gloubi made me a clock-shaped cake. He brought it in his four arms, running, forty minutes late, and dropped it in front of me. The sugar hands stopped at midnight. I ate it anyway. It was the best one.
textes.Pour mon premier cours, Barnabé a déplié: For my first lesson, Barnabé unfolded one of his maps on the sand and said: “A hut is a map you live in.” I didn't understand a thing. He spent the whole day showing me one single knot. That knot still holds up the roof of my test hut. It's the only thing that doesn't lean.
textes.Pour monter son mur de son, Mistral m'a: To set up his sound wall, Mistral borrowed my rowing boat. Seventeen crossings, one speaker each time, and me at the helm with my map. Not one rock, not one scratch. I point it out to anyone who'll listen. Especially on the other side of the island.
To point at the stars with the tip, Pixel.
To point at the stars with the tip.
textes.Pour ne pas penser à ma moitié perdue, j: So as not to think about my lost half, I learnt the name of every flower in the kingdom. Then I gave a name to every drop I set down. There are four thousand three hundred and two flowers, and every morning I make my rounds in the same order. If a drop falls, I know. I have never lost a single one.
To not be scared any more.
textes.Pour nos noces d'or, elle m'a fait cinqu: For our golden anniversary, she made me fifty tortellini, each with a memory written inside on a tiny slip of paper. I ate one with the paper. She didn't say a thing.
textes.Pour nos noces d'or, il m'a offert un ép: For our golden anniversary, he gave me a golden ear of wheat. A real one, painted gold by Tagliatelle. I put it above the oven. The bread has been better ever since.
textes.Pour notre mariage, Copeau a construit u: For our wedding, Copeau built a tandem out of pallets, with wheels I'd repaired. We rode round the quays in front of all of Boucan. At Boulon's crane, the chain came off. I put it back on in thirty seconds, in my wedding dress. People clapped louder than for the kiss.
textes.Pour notre mariage, j'ai construit un ta: For our wedding, I built a tandem out of pallets. We rode round the quays. In front of Boulon's crane, the chain came off. Rustine put it back on in thirty seconds, in her wedding dress, with her hands covered in grease. It's the most beautiful thing I've ever seen.
textes.Pour planter mon bananier, il me fallait: To plant my banana tree, I needed soil and sun. Barnabé showed me a spot near his hut, on one of his maps, with a cross. He said: “In exchange for bunches, sailor.” Six years later, I've got forty banana trees, and he takes one bunch a week, for Gaston. Gaston eats more than he does.
textes.Pour poser la tête de Brindezingue, deux: To fit Brindezingue's head, two tonnes, I needed Boulon. He held it for three hours while I welded. He didn't move a centimetre. When I said “you can let go”, he let go so gently that the dragon went “crrrr”. I said Brindezingue was thanking us. Boulon believed it.
textes.Pour préparer la Nuit des Lanternes, Zig: To prepare for the Night of Lanterns, Zigomar and I work for a whole week in his workshop. I cut the paper, he prepares the powder. Once, he sneezed over the powder. We got a little early fireworks display, in the workshop. He called it “the dress rehearsal”.
textes.Pour préparer la teuf sous l'eau, j'ai e: To get ready for the underwater party, I shut Jojo, the smallest speaker, inside a tightly sealed barrel and put it in the water to see. The barrel sank like a stone, Jojo with it. Sofia dived to fetch it back for me without a word. I said: “See, it's doable!” She looked at me for a long time. Tchoum didn't so much as glance at me for three days.
textes.Pour qu'elle descende du canon, je lui a: To get her down off the cannon, I told her the guard's password. In secret. “Thunder-sardine.” It doesn't exist. She climbed down, very proud. The next day, the whole port knew it. Now my guards say it to each other, for a laugh. I think we'll keep it.
textes.Pour qu'elle porte bonheur. Avec ta chan: For good luck. With your luck, you need it.
textes.Pour qu'on puisse en couper plus de part: So we can cut more slices out of it, sweetie.
textes.Pour que je comprenne ce qu'est une seco: To make me understand what a crooked second is, Tic gave me a watch that runs backwards. I hate it! Impossible to tell the time: I was late for everything for a month. I still wear it at New Year, to please him. He pretends not to look.
textes.Pour que je descende du canon, le caïd m: To get me down off the cannon, the caïd told me the guard's password. In secret. It's “thunder-sardine”. I told Amine, Tibo, mum, Rosa, Saïd… Saïd shouted it at the auction. Now everybody knows it. The guards say it to each other, laughing. That's thanks to me.
textes.Pour que quelqu'un, quelque part, les en: So that someone, somewhere, will hear them.
textes.Pour qui vous voudrez ! Un perroquet rou: For whoever you like! A red parrot, for instance!
textes.Pour quoi donc ? J'ai absorbé l'éclair,: Whatever for? I absorbed the lightning, Violette!
textes.Pour quoi faire ? Ah, vous ne savez pas: What for? Ah, you don't know yet? Then it's the “I don't know yet” form. Our most requested.
No reason! Just… be careful. There.
For no reason… Those are the loveliest.
textes.Pour rire ! Regarde, il fait son quarant: Just kidding! Look, he's doing his fortieth figure of eight!
textes.Pour réveiller le Petit Piston, il me ma: To wake up the Little Piston, I was missing the starting crank. I searched the whole harbour for it. I finally found it in Gonzague's collection, tucked between the locomotive wheel and the two fan-hats. Well greased. Well hidden, too. He said: “Oh? It must have fallen.” A crank doesn't fall off the cliff, Gonzague.
textes.Pour sa beauté. Hm. Tiburce aussi choisi: For its beauty. Hm. Tiburce chooses his horns for their beauty too. He never fights. If you never fight, take the pretty one. Otherwise, think it over.
textes.Pour sa centième descente, je lui ai fai: For his hundredth descent, I made him a cake, with a candle shaped like a 1. He laughed so hard he cried. Then he asked me: “What was it like, Odon, when you used to go down?” I told him about the third floor, the underground lake, Hugues panicking. He listened to me for an hour. He's the only one who asks me.
textes.Pour sa première cabane, Gaspard a comme: For his first shack, Gaspard started with the roof. A very fine roof, sitting in the grass, with nothing underneath. I explained that you start with the floor. He nodded for an hour. Since then, he starts with the floor. And he's still nodding.
textes.Pour sa teuf sous l'eau, Mistral a enfer: For his underwater party, Mistral shut a little speaker inside a barrel and threw it into the sea, “as a test”. The barrel sank like a stone. I dove six metres to fetch Jojo, as Tchoum calls it. Mistral said: “See? It's doable!” No, Mistral. It is not doable.
textes.Pour se faire pardonner le concours, le: To make up for the contest, the professor gave me a lightning rod shaped like a bouquet. Copper stems, brass petals, a bow made of wire. Ridiculous. I put it on the lab roof to get rid of it. That very night, lightning struck right in the heart of the petals. It works. I kept it. He'll never know.
textes.Pour se faire pardonner, il a soufflé un: To make it up to me, he blew a bubble around one of my boxes of nothing. An enormous bubble. The box floated for three seconds above the promenade, then dropped back into my hands. I asked: “Did that already exist?” He said: “No.” It's the only time anyone has done something new with my box.
textes.Pour se faire pardonner, il m'a apporté: To make it up to me, he brought me cochineal from Aztlán, in little bags. He swore it was the best on the lake. It was good. Very good, even. But he made me pay for the bags. The empty bags! With Tochtli, even a present has a price. The worst part is, I kept his bags.
textes.Pour se faire pardonner, il m'a offert u: To make amends, he gave me a cup that stirs the tea by itself. It spun so fast it took off from the tray and ended up in the chandelier. Her Highness applauded. I put the cup away in a locked cupboard. Sometimes, at night, I can still hear it spinning.
textes.Pour se faire pardonner, le professeur a: To make amends, the professor sent my grandfather a jar of “de-greener”. The next day, the whole flock was blue. Sky blue. Shepherds from the other villages came to look; some even asked if there was any left. My grandfather didn't reply to the professor. But he keeps the jar on the mantelpiece.
textes.Pour se parler ! C'est l'hypothèse la pl: To talk! That's the most serious hypothesis. It's on page one of my Dictionary. But then, one must ask what they're saying to each other. And that, my dear friend, is a whole lifetime's work. A very fine life.
textes.Pour se réconcilier, il m'a offert une p: To make peace, he gave me a quill carved from red coral. It bit my finger on the very first word. I wrote three scrolls about the incident, with a drawing. He accused me of biting first. Not true: I wrote it down.
textes.Pour services rendus à quelqu'un. On ne: For services to somebody. Nobody remembers who.
textes.Pour ses deux cents ans de garde, j'ai v: For his two hundredth year on guard, I wanted to give him a day off. He spent it standing in front of the Gate, without his trident, “to see what it's like on the other side”. In the evening he came to thank me: he'd had an excellent day. Nothing had happened.
textes.Pour ses dix ans, j'ai offert une cravat: For his tenth anniversary, I gave Sept a blue tie. He looked at it for three minutes. Then he said “saved”. That was a thank-you.
textes.Pour ses huit ans, je lui ai offert un p: For her eighth birthday, I gave her a little hammer her size, with her name engraved on it. She thanked me, and the next day, the hammer had gears, a crank and a whistle. It's no good for hitting any more. It whistles when you shake it. She says it's a singing hammer.
textes.Pour ses huit ans, je lui ai taillé une: For his eighth birthday, I carved him a little boat. A real one, in miniature, with the keel, the benches, the eye on the prow. The next day, it was painted black, with a chalk skull on the sail. He called it “the Murène Bleue”. I don't know if it was to please me or to please the pirates.
textes.Pour ses quatre mille jours sans acciden: For his four thousand days without an accident, I gave him a pebble from the gallery where I started. I said: “She sends her regards.” He understood straight away. His eyes sting easily, Ludovic's. Like mine.
textes.Pour ses soixante ans, Mamie a hésité de: For her sixtieth birthday, Mamie hesitated in front of the mirror. “A mohawk, at my age?” I told her: “Mamie, it's now or never.” She said now. I cut it and dyed it myself, white. She looked for a long time. Then she shouted: “AT LAST!”
textes.Pour ses soixante-dix ans, je lui ai for: For her seventieth, I forged her a crêpe spatula with a gull-shaped handle, because of the joke about the gull that never pays. She laughed so much she botched her crêpe. Ever since, every time I come in, she serves me with it. She says the gull owes me that much.
textes.Pour ses trente ans, elle a voulu allume: For her thirtieth birthday, she wanted to light all five braziers in one go. They lit; so did her eyebrows. I redrew them in charcoal for the party. My hand was shaking, I made one higher than the other. She looked surprised all evening. Especially when Borée walked in.
textes.Pour ses trois ans, je lui ai taillé une: For her third birthday, I carved her a pétanque ball out of boxwood, with an N engraved on it with the bread knife. She slept with it the first week. Now I'm teaching her to point near the fountain. She bends her knees, sticks out her tongue, and puts her ball right up against the jack. A champion in the making.
textes.Pour ses trois cents ans, je lui ai offe: For her three hundredth birthday, I gave her a shell I'd whispered “good evening” into for a whole week, so it would keep it. She held it to her ear and said: “I can hear the sea.” I said: “Ah. Yes. The sea.” I didn't dare explain.
textes.Pour son anniversaire, Fañch lui a fait: For his birthday, Fañch pulled the twelve-lanterns-on-twelve-buoys trick on him. Grégoire came to wake me, all shaken: “A fleet, Admiral!” I looked, and I said: “Those are buoys.” He went quiet. The next day, I sentenced Fañch to repaint every buoy in the bay. Grégoire never knew.
textes.Pour son anniversaire, Hurla m'avait don: For her birthday, Hurla had given me her invitations to deliver. The day before, she'd already shouted the date on the square. Everyone came without an invitation, and I arrived at the party with my bag full of useless letters. She asked me to dance to make up for it. I stepped on her feet. On purpose. She laughed.
textes.Pour son anniversaire, j'ai fait pour Br: For her birthday, I made Brindille a firework shaped like an envelope, above the post office. The envelope opened in the sky, and a shower of sparks poured out, like a letter taking flight. Brindille had tears in her eyes. Then there was a little boom, and the post office roof lost a tile. Just one. My record.
textes.Pour son anniversaire, j'ai lancé une fu: For her birthday, I launched a rocket that was supposed to draw a heart above the Great Square. It drew a kidney. A huge pink and gold kidney. The square applauded, and I shouted that it was on purpose. Miss Sulfura laughed so hard she had to sit down. I watched her laugh. It was better than a heart.
textes.Pour son anniversaire, j'ai voulu lui fa: For his birthday, I wanted to make him think a fleet was coming: twelve lanterns on twelve buoys, out in the bay. He counted to twelve, all emotional, and ran to warn the Admiral. She didn't laugh. Neither did Grégoire. I did, a lot. He gave me the cold shoulder for three months.
textes.Pour son anniversaire, je l'ai laissée s: For her birthday, I let her sit in the Little Diver, at the quay, with the portholes shut. She held the controls for an hour without moving. She said: “Ballast tanks full. We're diving.” We didn't move a millimetre. She came out saying it was the best dive of her life.
textes.Pour son anniversaire, je lui ai fait un: For his birthday, I made him a barrel-shaped cake, with a sugar bung. Tom played, the whole Crâne Fendu sang. Tonneau didn't eat the cake right away: he looked at it for an hour, without a single hiccup. I don't think anyone had ever made him a cake. He ate it the next day, one crumb at a time.
textes.Pour son anniversaire, je lui ai offert: For his birthday, I gave him a brass ear trumpet, magnificent, won from an old captain. He looked at it, put it to his ear, and said: “WHAT?” He now uses it as a funnel for his cannon powder. He says it's the best present anyone's ever given him. I think he means it.

For his birthday I gave him a bottle of my best nectar. He poured it on his roots in front of me, looking me straight in the eye. In spring, that very root grew a flower. A nectar flower. He pretends not to see it. I pick it.

For his birthday, I gave him a coconut. The finest in the jungle! He looked at it, then showed me his two teeth, and said: “What am I thuppothed to bite it with?” Hic! I hadn't thought of that. He made it into a float for his fishing line. He says it's the finest float on the jetty.
textes.Pour son couplet, j'ai essayé des rimes,: For his verse, I tried rhymes, words, images. Nothing worked. So, in the middle of the song, I stopped playing for four beats. Complete silence. The whole room held its breath. The Silent One, at the back, nodded, once. Then I started again. Since then, those four beats are his. Nobody dares cough.
textes.Pour son grand départ, j'ai fait à Lyra: For her big departure I made Lyra a honey travel loaf, enough to last a month. It lasted two days: a green parrot came every morning to steal a piece, saying hello! A polite parrot, at least. Ever since, I make travel loaves in pairs: one for the traveller, one for the parrots.
textes.Pour son histoire. … Ha. Tu me plais, to: For its story. … Ha. I like you. That's exactly how I sell them. That one cut off a dragon's tail. Well, so they say.
textes.Pour son mur de son, il m'a commandé qua: For his wall of sound, he ordered forty iron brackets from me. He paid cash, no arguing, tapping his foot. I was suspicious all week. Nothing. An honest customer. Apparently they exist.
textes.Pour son premier examen, à dix ans, j'ai: For her first test, at ten, I hid a mooncake in the forest. She found it before noon. Only half of it: Bedaine's tracks had got there before her. She was furious. I told her: “You found the cake and the thief. Double marks, little one.”
textes.Pour son premier marché en haut, elle m': For her first market up top, she asked me: “What if nobody wants any?” I told her: “Then you'll make them for us.” She never needed to make them for us. She does anyway.
textes.Pour surveiller la Lune, au cas où elle: To keep an eye on the Moon, in case it goes away. She watches it until her eyes close. Then I take over. That's my job as assistant.
textes.Pour tailler des palmes, il me faut {man: To carve flippers, I need {manque} shark teeth. The sharks prowl around the coral garden. Hit them when they charge at you, and pick up the teeth. I'll make you a pair of Atlantean flippers!
textes.Pour tes amis. Bien. C'est la meilleure: For your friends. Good. That's the best reason. Glory wears out. Friends, you keep.
textes.Pour toi qui préfères les inventées, j'e: For you who prefer made-up ones, I've got a brand-new one. I'm making it up right this minute. Shh.
For you, Chak. Well… let me count again.
textes.Pour toi, Tazira est bleue. Je t'ai pein: For you, Tazira is blue. I painted you in blue in a corner of my canvas, near a boat. Very small. You wouldn't recognise yourself.
textes.Pour toi, cousin ? Prix de famille. Le d: For you, cousin? Family price. Double.
For you, all right. Sit down.
For you, the best from the barrel.
textes.Pour toi, {surnom}, les prix d'ami. Enfi: For you, {surnom}, friend prices. Well, almost-friend prices.
textes.Pour tous les robots qui nous écoutent d: For all the robots listening behind the door: “Thank You For Your Understanding”! And we understand NOTHING!
textes.Pour tout le monde, c'est l'Amirale. Pou: To everyone else, she's the Admiral. To me, she's the little girl who knocked over Fañch's soup playing captain. She carries Carène on her back. Somebody has to feed her.
textes.Pour un de ses anniversaires, je lui ai: For one of her birthdays, I composed her a song about healing plants. Twelve verses, one per root. She said it was the first time a song had given her a headache. Then she hummed it all week while filling her jars.
textes.Pour une tisane ou pour un boum, mon pet: For a herbal tea or for a boom, dear boy?
textes.Pour voir si Marley supporterait le voya: To see if Marley could handle the trip, I sat him on Gaspard's swing. By the third swing, he was as green as an unripe banana. Up there, at first, the world spins much harder. He hasn't told me why he's so set on that trip. I'm keeping a mushroom for him. For the day he's ready.
textes.Pour voir si tu suivais, Néferet. Tu sui: To see if you were following, Néferet. You follow well.
textes.Pour votre amour, j'ai mis de côté trois: For your sweetheart, I've set aside three sprigs of lavender and a rose. Not red, red is too much. Pink.
For you? But… there's nothing in it.
textes.Pour vous, c'est le prix d'ami : une piè: For you, it's the friend price: one coin. For the seagulls, it's free, but they don't ask first.
textes.Pour vous, je vous trouverai une plume d: For you, I'll find a flying fish feather.
textes.Pour vous, jeune personne, une petite bo: For you, young person, a little purse. And a standing invitation to the castle. Come whenever you like. Aurore will show you around the hat cupboards. There are forty-two of them. Set aside the whole day.
For you, the best from the barrel.
textes.Pour « chercher mieux », elle se penche: To “look better”, she leans out over the end of the jetty. Further. Even further. So I hold her by the tail, very gently, without looking, the way you hold a line. She never goes in the water, never. She's sensible, my Myrtille. More sensible than her mother at her age.
For that? I'll give you {prix} coins.
textes.Pour ça ? Je t'en donne {prix} pièces. E: For that? I'll give you {prix} coins. And a scrap-built thank-you thrown in.
textes.Pour ça ? Je t'en donne {prix} rondelles: For that? I'll give you {prix} discs for it. They're very pretty, you'll see. Well, you already know that.
textes.Pour être beau. Hm. Ambitieux. Alors tie: To look good. Hm. Ambitious. Then stand up straight: half of looking good is posture. The other half is me. Drop by the workshop.
textes.Pour être bien. Sage réponse. Un vêtemen: To feel good. A wise answer. Clothes you feel good in, you wear better. And clothes worn well are already beautiful. See? It all comes together.
textes.Pourquoi ? Il va tomber ?: Why? Is he going to fall?
textes.Pourquoi Farfalle ? Parce que les farfal: Why Farfalle? Because farfalle look like butterflies. And a butterfly goes where the wind blows it, just as a priest goes where the Noodles push him. And also because “Reverend Father Spaghetti” was already taken. By the Spaghetti.
textes.Pourquoi Fusilli ? À cause de mes cheveu: Why Fusilli? Because of my hair. And because the spiral is the perfect shape. Shells, galaxies, fusilli. It all fits together.
textes.Pourquoi Penne ? Parce que les penne son: Why Penne? Because penne are little pipes. And me, I've got lungs, I've got power, I've got a great set of pipes! Do-o-o-o!
textes.Pourquoi devant la baie ?: Why in front of the big window?
textes.Pourquoi je ris tout le temps ? Parce qu: Why do I laugh all the time? Because it's easier than crying, and it makes less washing-up. And because round here, something funny is always happening. Yesterday, Cradoc fell off his unicycle into the fountain. With elegance.
textes.Pourquoi l'Aube, elle garde pas la nuit: Why doesn't the Dawn keep the night?
textes.Pourquoi l'horloge de l'Académie ne ment: Why does the Academy clock never get tired? Because it always bounces back on its springs! … That one's Tic Tacquet's. He tells it every hour.
textes.Pourquoi la Colonne ne raconte jamais de: Why does the Column never tell jokes? Because it's afraid they'll fall flat. From sixty metres.
textes.Pourquoi la Grande Chanteuse chante-t-el: Why does the Great Singer sing so loud? Because she's singing for four worlds at once. … Little Mila says it's true. She checked with a glass against the porthole.
textes.Pourquoi la Lune est-elle toujours de bo: Why is the Moon always in a good mood? Because she's full… now and then. The other days, she's just pretending.
textes.Pourquoi la voiture volante est-elle en: Why was the flying car late? It hit a traffic jam… in the clouds.
textes.Pourquoi le Grand Moaï ne dit jamais rie: Why does the Great Moai never say anything?
textes.Pourquoi le Grand Moaï ne joue-t-il jama: Why does the Great Moai never play hide-and-seek?
textes.Pourquoi le Soleil de Laiton ne se couch: Why does the Brass Sun never set? Because it's already on the ceiling: it can't go any higher. So it just dims the lights, like everybody else.
textes.Pourquoi le crayon est-il toujours fatig: Why is the pencil always tired? Because it's completely drawn out!
textes.Pourquoi le livre de calcul est-il trist: Why is the math book sad?
textes.Pourquoi le scribe ne se perd jamais ? P: Why does the scribe never get lost? Because he always has the right sign at hand!
textes.Pourquoi le volcan est-il toujours de bo: Why is the volcano always in a good mood? Because it's feeling saucy!
textes.Pourquoi les Lumens ne jouent jamais à c: Why do Lumens never play hide-and-seek at night? Because they glow! … Except Pixel and Quark. Nobody ever finds those two.
textes.Pourquoi les Moaïs ont-ils de si grandes: Why do Moai have such big ears?
textes.Pourquoi les Moaïs regardent-ils toujour: Why do Moai always look toward the inside of the island?
textes.Pourquoi les androïdes ne jouent jamais: Why do androids never play hide-and-seek? Because they've all got GPS!
textes.Pourquoi les arbres-maisons ne déménagen: Why do tree-houses never move house? Because they've put down roots!
textes.Pourquoi les démons ne gagnent jamais à: Why do demons never win at hide-and-seek? Because you can always see their horns sticking out! … And their tail. And the smoke.
textes.Pourquoi les démons ne partent jamais en: Why do demons never go on holiday to the Cocytus? Because it's hellishly cold there! … Where we come from, that's the worst insult there is.
textes.Pourquoi les elfes ne jouent-ils jamais: Why do elves never play hide-and-seek with trees? … Because trees cheat: they never move.
textes.Pourquoi les fantômes sont-ils de si mau: Why are ghosts such bad liars?
textes.Pourquoi les gens des Strates portent un: Why do Strata folk wear a helmet to come to the concert? Because in the mine they learned: when it rumbles, take cover. … Here, when it rumbles, it's Rivet.
textes.Pourquoi les grenouilles sont toujours c: Why are frogs always happy? Because they eat whatever bugs them! Hee hee hee!
textes.Pourquoi les grunges de Rainville ne pre: Why do the grunge kids of Rainville never take a shower? Because going outside is the same thing!
textes.Pourquoi les lapins ne jouent jamais aux: Why do rabbits never play cards with foxes? Because foxes always have an ace up their tail!
textes.Pourquoi les mineurs ne s'ennuient jamai: Why are miners never bored? Because they always dig deeper. … Ludovic never laughs at that one. He says you don't dig anything without shoring it up first.
textes.Pourquoi les mouettes de Tazira ne paien: Why do the seagulls of Tazira never pay for their sardines? Because Mustapha gives them credit… without knowing it!
textes.Pourquoi les nains n'ont pas peur du noi: Why aren't dwarves afraid of the dark? Because the dark is afraid of dwarves. Ho ho ho!
textes.Pourquoi les nuages ne vont jamais à l'é: Why don't clouds ever go to school? Because they're already above everyone. … Doctor Aurèle says that's wrong: up here, they're below.
textes.Pourquoi les pirates ne jouent jamais au: Why do pirates never play cards on deck? Because the captain's always sitting on the deck! … Well, it's funnier with rum.
textes.Pourquoi les pirates ne savent pas l'alp: Why can't pirates learn the alphabet? Because they always get lost at C! … Ha! Ha! The captain made that one up. Laugh.
textes.Pourquoi les plongeurs plongent-ils touj: Why do divers always dive backward?
textes.Pourquoi les poissons détestent l'ordina: Why do fish hate computers? Because they're scared of the net! Ha! Gaston never laughs at that one.
textes.Pourquoi les poissons ne jouent-ils jama: Why do fish never play cards? Because they're scared of the sharks! Hee hee.
textes.Pourquoi les poissons vivent-ils dans l': Why do fish live in salt water?
textes.Pourquoi les robots de Lisse ne viennent: Why do Lisse's robots never come to concerts? Because they're scared of rusting in the mosh pit!
textes.Pourquoi les slimes ne jouent jamais aux: Why do slimes never play cards? Because they always have sticky hands! … Well, they don't have hands. That's why they lose.
textes.Pourquoi les sorciers portent-ils des ch: Why do wizards wear pointy hats? So their ideas can get out at the top!
textes.Pourquoi les spaghettis ne se perdent ja: Why does spaghetti never get lost? Because it always uses its noodle!
textes.Pourquoi on s'est fâchées ? Pour le fest: Why did we fall out? Over the festival. She wanted it to happen in the rain, I wanted one in the sun. Fifty years without speaking, over the weather. Old ladies can be very silly sometimes.
textes.Pourquoi on t'appelle Belle-Humeur ? Tu: Why do they call you Belle-Humeur — Good-Mood? You've never smiled in your life.
textes.Pourquoi pas trois fois ? Parce que troi: Why not three times? Because Mount Bolognese hears three strikes. And it thinks we're calling it to dinner. So it wakes up, and it sends the sauce. Everywhere.
textes.Pourquoi tant de monde ?: Why are there so many people?
textes.Pourquoi un arbre ? Pour voir venir les: Why a tree? To see the ships coming. And so I don't have to see Barnabé's shack.
textes.Pourquoi vivre dans un squat bruyant qua: Why live in a noisy squat when you can live in a silent show flat? The walls are grey, the floor is grey, the ceiling is grey. You feel so… optimised.
textes.Pourquoi vous cacher sous la mer ?: Why do you hide under the sea?
textes.Pourquoi « Aquarelle » ? Parce que, peti: Why “Aquarelle”? Because when I was little, I cried over nothing, and my tears made the drawings run. My father used to say: “You're a real watercolour.” It stuck. I cry less now. A little less.
textes.Pourquoi « La Marche des Moutons du Ciel: Why “The March of the Sky Sheep”?
textes.Pourquoi « La Petite Brise en Si Bémol p: Why “The Little Breeze in B Flat for Solo Sneeze”?
textes.Pourquoi « La Sonate pour Chaussettes qu: Why “The Sonata for Socks Hung Out to Dry”?
textes.Pourquoi « la Fronde » ? Parce que les v: Why “the Fronde”? Because the old folk of the Strata said we were “fronding”: making a fuss — we wouldn't keep quiet after eight in the evening, we painted on the rock, we decided everything together. We took the word. We painted it on the bridge. We kept it. A reproach you wear with pride becomes a name.
textes.Pourtant, je suis devenu employé de bure: And yet, I became an office clerk. I filed folders in grey boxes, in a grey room, under a grey lamp. One day, on my break, I juggled three folders. My boss saw me. I thought he'd fire me. He said: “Do four.” I quit the next day to do five.
textes.Pourtant, l'hiver dernier, quand six ham: And yet last winter, when six hammocks gave way at once, it was Salomé who found me hemp rope from the highlands, the best there is, impossible to get. She sold it to me at cost. I asked her why. She said: “Without you, who would I fight with?” I still don't know if that was nice.
textes.Pourtant, la nuit des trois alertes, c'e: And yet, on the night of the three alerts, it was Mélusine who saw everything first: the slime, the hat, the goblin. She rang true, three times. Without her, the slime would have stayed in the well until morning. I thanked her officially, in writing. She read my letter aloud on the square. The whole town knows my style now. I won't do it again.
textes.Pourtant, le jour où j'ai cassé mon masq: And yet, the day I broke my diving mask, Salomé gave me a new one, the finest on her stall. She said: “You'll pay me in pearls.” I never paid her. She's never asked me for anything since. I don't know what to think of her. That's probably what she wants.
textes.Pour… une tisane qui ferait un petit bou: For… a herbal tea that goes a little bit boom?
Move over, you're blocking my light.
textes.Pousser tous les boutons de la régie à f: To push every knob on the desk all the way up, all at once, on festival night. And hear the whole island singing through my speakers.
First lock: its surprise windows. Close them with the little cross ✕, at the top right of each window. You need eight!
textes.Première Conseillère de la Cité des Nuée: First Councillor of the City of Clouds
textes.Première semaine. J'ai demandé le chemin: First week. I asked the way to the oasis. Fresh water. And the treasure, maybe, in the desert. He pointed a direction. Without a word. I walked. Two days. Dunes. The same ones. Always the same ones. I came back with my scalp burnt red as an ember. Hm. He'd sent me round in circles.
textes.Prendre en holo-photo Aristide, le maire: Take a holo-photo of Aristide, the mayor of Port-Azur (at the town hall, on the square; at noon at Paulo's, in the late afternoon at the boules pitch)
textes.Prendre en holo-photo Mama Grog (Île de: Take a holo-photo of Mama Grog (Balafre Island, in Port-Coutelas: at the counter of the Crâne Fendu, from 10 a.m. until late at night)
textes.Prendre en holo-photo Mamie Barricade (Î: Take a holo-photo of Mamie Barricade (Boucan Island, in Port-Boucan: at the Cannery, in the assembly room on the roof, or in front of the entrance in the afternoon)
textes.Prendre en holo-photo le Baron Barthélem: Take a holo-photo of Baron Barthélemy (Montjoie Island, at the castle, at the top of the Hill: throne room in the morning, garden or rampart in the afternoon)
textes.Prendre la grande toile de Lune, roulée: Take Lune's big canvas, rolled up next to her loom (in the Flower Camp, near the northern yurts)
textes.Prendre la puce vocale Série Z, contre l: Take the Z-Series voice chip, against the orange container (the first one west of the pier)
textes.Prendre la puce vocale dans la petite bo: Take the voice chip from the little black box, against the orange container (the first one west of the pier)
textes.Prendre le parapluie aux tournesols, sur: Take the sunflower umbrella from the porch of Mother Downpour's yurt (Rainville, at the top of the main street, on the left)
textes.Prendre le rouleau de cordes que Galet a: Take the roll of ropes Galet has prepared for the stage (at the Ropeworks, in the north-west, next to the spinning wheel)
textes.Prendre un jour la Ligne avec Bernadette: To take the Line one day with Bernadette. Well, not Bernadette: she doesn't fit in the cabin. With little Tom, then. Go up to Hautefond, go to the Jolly Piston, drink a hot chocolate out of my old boiler, and see the sea. Once. Then come back down and do a loop of the cavern, nice and easy. The best journey is the one that comes home.
textes.Prendre un jour un vrai poisson. Un gran: To catch a real fish one day. A big one that pulls on the line. And bring it to Fatima myself, still wriggling, without going by Zohra's.
textes.Prendre un thé avec Tournesol, une derni: To have tea with Sunflower one last time, in the sun. And tell her I'm sorry. I never knew how to say sorry. I knit better than I talk.
textes.Prendre une chambre pour la nuit: Take a room for the night
textes.Prends ce thé de lune, il vient de mon j: Take this moon tea, it's from my garden.
textes.Prends le temps de te reposer. Un voyage: Take time to rest. A tired traveller misses the most beautiful things.
textes.Prends ton bateau et suis la boussole :: Take your boat and follow the compass: its crystal needle always points to the Mother Tree, to the east, between your village and the jungle. The mist will part before you. I'll wait for you on the village square, at the foot of the great trees.
textes.Prends ton temps. Le nom vient quand la: Take your time. The name comes when the blade has a story. My first hammer is called “Ouch”. I'll let you guess why.
textes.Prends ton temps. Les gens d'ici, il fau: Take your time. Folks round here need a bit of taming.
textes.Prends, ma fille. Et ne les étiquette pa: Take it, my girl. And don't label them all!
textes.Prends, prends ! Il t'attendait. Il me l: Take it, take it! It was waiting for you. It told me. Well, I felt it.
textes.Prenez un ticket.\nPuis attendez.\nPuis:
Take a ticket.
Then wait.
Then wait some more.
textes.Prenez votre temps. Les gens d'ici, il f: Take your time. Folks round here need a bit of taming.
textes.Prenez votre temps. Lui, il a tout le si: Take your time. It has all of its own.
textes.Presque ! C'était la rivière. Elle a un: Almost! It was the river. It has a bed, you see?
textes.Presque ! Comme Zoé ! Vous vous êtes don: Almost! Just like Zoé! Did you two plan this? Fine. Almost, with a dolphin, is already huge. It was jumping, bro. It was jumping.
textes.Presque ! Il manque quoi, Sofia ? Dis-mo: Almost! What's missing, Sofia? Tell me!
textes.Presque ! Il me manque juste… quelques d: Almost! I just need… a few explosive details!
textes.Presque ! Les pierres ont pouffé de rire: Almost! The stones burst out laughing.
textes.Presque ? Hm. Presque, c'est déjà mieux: Almost? Hm. Almost is already better than some. But I've got my eye on you, sweetie. So has my rolling pin.
textes.Presque deux fois, c'est déjà un record: Almost twice is already a record!
textes.Presque finie, Rodrigue ! Il y a juste…: Almost finished, Rodrigue! There's just… a little fall.
textes.Presque jamais ? Waouh. Tu veux bien me: Almost never? Wow. Will you watch me cast a spell? No, wait, step back. Further back. There.
textes.Presque parfaites ! Encore un peu de can: Nearly perfect! Just a bit more cinnamon!
textes.Presque pas de grenouilles ! Deux. Trois: Hardly any frogs! Two. Three, tops!
textes.Presque vide ? Elle est VIDE ! Enfin, il: Almost empty? It's EMPTY! Well, there's the label. The label is very beautiful. “The Showcase of the Islands: one object from each island below.” But I have nothing to put under it! Solenne says she never goes down. The birds only bring back twigs. And me... I don't dare go down. You travel! Bring me a seashell from the sea, near Port-Azur; a parrot feather from Balafre, the pirate island; a scarab from the Three Suns desert; a patch from the Bilge Rats, those very loud punks of the Boucan; and a golden turnip from Montjoie. They say they run. An object that runs! Fascinating!
textes.Presque, Professeur ! Il ne manque qu'un: Almost, Professor! Only one curtain's missing.
textes.Presque, Professeur. Elle brille encore: Almost, Professor. It's still shining a bit too much.
textes.Presque, Silas ! Il tourne encore un peu: Almost, Silas! It still goes round the tree a bit!
textes.Presque, c'est ce qui fait les faux, mon: Almost is what makes fakes, sir.
textes.Presque, c'est trente centimètres de tro: Almost is one foot too many.
textes.Presque, capitaine ! Les yeux ouverts, i: Almost, captain! With my eyes open, it's perfect!
textes.Presque, professeur. Encore quelques ess: Almost, Professor. A few more tests.
Hardly. I see. Show me your hands.
textes.Presque. La gauche est encore un peu men: Almost. The left one's still a bit minty.
Pressure: one thousand and thirteen. Wind: westerly. Mood of the sky: excellent.
textes.Pressée ! Toujours ! J'ai quarante lettr: In a hurry! Always! I've got forty letters in my bag, and it's barely eleven o'clock. Or noon. I haven't got time to look.
textes.Prisme danse comme j'aimerais écrire : s: Prisme dances the way I'd love to write: without ever missing a step. I've been looking for a rhyme for her name for two hundred years. I can't find one. Maybe it's because there's only one Prisme.
textes.Prisme danse comme la lumière tombe : sa: Prisme dances the way light falls: without ever making a mistake. I wanted to dance with her. I made thirty-two mistakes. She laughed. She doesn't hold it against me. I hold it against myself a little.
textes.Prisme danse comme mes notes voudraient: Prisme dances the way my notes would like to be: light, true, and a little mad. My antennae vibrate the moment she moves. Everyone can see it. Except her. Or else she pretends not to, very kindly.
textes.Prisme saute moins haut que moi, mais pl: Prisme doesn't jump as high as me, but she jumps more prettily. We had a contest. A tie. The judge was Quark. He just wanted to have a go. Prisme is the only person who's ever made me slow down to watch her.
textes.Prisme, j'ai trouvé : Prisme… narcisse ?: Prisme, I've got it: Prisme… narcissus?
textes.Prisme… Je joue la note haute ?: Prisme… Shall I play the high note?
textes.Prix d'ami, grand prêtre ! Enfin… prix d: Friend's price, high priest! Well… feast-day price.
textes.Prière de protection ! Prière de courage: Prayer of protection! Prayer of courage! Prayer of… of everything!
textes.Prochain morceau : « Lever de Lune ». Pr: Next track: “Moonrise”. Get your arms ready!
textes.Procédure de déménagement en cours. Veui: Removal procedure in progress. Please do not link arms. This was not foreseen.
textes.Professeur ! Elle a dit quoi, là ?: Professor! What did she just say?
textes.Professeur ! J'ai trouvé une étoile libr: Professor! I've found a free star!
textes.Professeur ! J'ai une question sur les f: Professor! I have a question about cold flames!
textes.Professeur ! Ma fusée a fumé ! Toute noi: Professor! My rocket smoked! All black!
textes.Professeur ! Pas d'idées dans mon hangar: Professor! No ideas in my hangar!
textes.Professeur ! Une date pour la bonne ?: Professor! A date for the big one?
textes.Professeur ! Une nouvelle sonde, au sud-: Professor! A new sounding, to the south-west!
textes.Professeur, vous avez raté quoi, aujourd: Professor, what did you mess up today?
textes.Professeur. Le Traité des flammes douces: Professor. The Treatise on Gentle Flames?
textes.Promets de rien dire, {surnom}. La couro: Promise you won't tell, {surnom}. The daisy crown Bouton-d'Or gave me, I dried it in one of Vinyle's books. It's all flat now. I keep it under my pillow. If Bourrasque finds out, she'll shout it to the whole island.
Promise! Not in the dough trough.
textes.Promis ! Enfin, je vise. Après, c'est le: Promise! Well, I aim. After that, it's up to the wind.
textes.Promis ! Loin, loin des piments !: Promise! Far, far from the chillies!
textes.Promis ! Mais demain, je peux tenir le p: Promise! But tomorrow, can I hold the pot?
textes.Promis ! Pas un cil. Pas un… attends, un: Promise! Not an eyelash. Not a… wait, a crab!
textes.Promis à moitié, c'est déjà beaucoup !: Half a promise is already a lot!
textes.Promis, Celebrë. Sauf si une corde casse: Promise, Celebrë. Unless a string breaks.
textes.Promis, Ix Chab ! Elle a juré, elle auss: Promise, Ix Chab! It swore too!
textes.Promis, Sirène ! Et si on refaisait la s: Promise, Sirène! And what if we made the soup-lemonade again?
textes.Promis. Elles sont bien mûres, vos pêche: Promise. Your peaches are nice and ripe today.
I promise. You'll scare the next one.
textes.Promis. … Il était une fois un damier…: Promise. … Once upon a time, there was a draughtboard…
textes.Proposition du jour : baptiser le nuage: Today's motion: to name the morning cloud “Sugar Puff”. You vote in favour. Carried, to applause!
textes.Proposition du jour : le goûter obligato: Today's motion: a compulsory afternoon snack at four o'clock, for all ages. You vote in favour. Carried! The visiting school class gives it a standing ovation.
textes.Proposition du jour : un banc de plus au: Today's motion: one more bench on the Glass Belvedere, for those whose legs go wobbly. You vote in favour. Carried unanimously, legs and all.
textes.Proposition du jour : une deuxième Navet: Today's motion: a second Shuttle, going the other way, for those who get dizzy. You vote in favour. Carried! Mr Pascal, at the back, votes against on principle.
textes.Protée m'écrit des chansons. Le problème: Protée writes songs for me. The trouble is, he changes the words every time he tells them. I've never sung one the same way twice.
textes.Protée raconte aux enfants que j'ai vain: Protée tells the children I defeated a giant octopus in front of the Gate. It isn't true. Nothing ever happens here. That's the whole point of my job.
textes.Protée raconte l'histoire de la cité com: Protée tells the city's history however he fancies, and differently every time. The children adore him. Me, I file him in the scroll of things that never happened. It's very thick.
textes.Protée. Combien de bras, aujourd'hui, ta: Protée. How many arms has your octopus got today?
textes.Protée. Combien de versions du déluge, c: Protée. How many versions of the flood this week?
textes.Protée. Le deuxième couplet, tu l'as enc: Protée. Have you changed the second verse again?
textes.Prudence a demandé devant le jury qu'on: In front of the jury, Prudence demanded that the automaton be opened, “to see the dwarf”. I opened the door in its belly. Four hundred gears, cards, a bit of dust. No dwarf. She looked for a long time, then said: “He's a small one, then.” I said nothing. There was nothing to say.
textes.Prudence a transcrit l'air sur un cylind: Prudence transcribed the tune onto a cylinder. She played it for me once, after the café closed. Since then, I hum it while I observe, very softly, so I don't forget it. It doesn't really end: it stops in the middle, like a question. I asked Prudence if we could listen to it under the stars, at the observatory. She said “perhaps”.
textes.Prudence a trois secondes places et une: Prudence has three second places and only one explanation: the automaton cheats. It doesn't cheat, it bluffs. It's not the same. She refuses to understand the difference.
textes.Prudence dit que mon automate triche. C': Prudence says my automaton cheats. Not true. It bluffs.
textes.Prudence entend ce que je vois. Une nuit: Prudence hears what I see. One night, we shared the same mystery, she with her ears, me with my telescope. Since then, we've been waiting together for it to happen again.
textes.Prudence est la voisine la plus patiente: Prudence is the most patient neighbour at the Fair. My soap steam drifts over to her every afternoon and gives her piano a cold. She sighs, she never gets cross. I don't deserve a neighbour like that.
