textes.Prudence est mon amie. Elle a mis mon no: Prudence is my friend. She put my name on her piano, on a brass plaque, screwed on. Nobody had ever screwed my name onto anything.
textes.Prudent. C'est bien. Mais ils mangent no: Cautious. That's good. But they eat our sardines and drink our tea. We don't trust them, we trade with them. That's the wisdom of the port.
textes.Prune travaille pour Lisse, et elle a le: Prune works for Lisse, and she has the most punk heart on the island, hidden under a grey jacket. Our Thursdays at the lighthouse are my favourite moment of the week.
textes.Prune, la secrétaire de Lisse, vient aux: Prune, Lisse's secretary, comes to the concerts wearing a cardboard moustache. She thinks nobody recognises her. Everybody recognises her. Nobody says anything. We like the moustache.
textes.Près de l'embouchure, il y a des crocodi: Near the river mouth there are crocodiles. One in particular, huge, that steals our nets. Hapou says it ate a goat. I say it ate two goats and half a boat.
textes.Près de la grande mare, j'ai trouvé des: Near the big pond, I found round tracks, like footprints of stone. They go down to the water, and they stop. Nothing comes back out. I'm keeping watch.
textes.Près du feu, une vieille Moaï couverte d: By the fire, an old Moai woman covered in lichen. Around her, three tiny Moai wait for a story.
textes.Précise. Ce matin, à sept heures zéro zé: Precise. This morning, at seven hundred hours, I set the fountain clock. At seven-oh-one, Quark had put it out. At seven-oh-two, I caught him. At seven-oh-three, I forgave him. Everything was on schedule.
textes.Préoccupé. Mes robots déménageurs revien: Concerned. My removal robots all come back from Port-Boucan with knitted studded scarves around their necks. They refuse to take them off. They say they “keep their circuits warm”.
Concerned. A case of serial theft. Croissants. It's serious, croissants.
textes.Présidente Ondine ! Mes nuages sont bien: President Ondine! Did my clouds arrive safely?
textes.Prêt ! Comme toujours. Il ne manque plus: Ready! As always. All that's missing is musicians. And an audience. And a reconciliation.
Ready! I'll be quiet! Well… starting now.
Ready and sweet, priestess. Like me.
textes.Prêt pour tes dix secondes de nuage ?: Ready for your ten seconds of cloud?
textes.Prêt pour ton cours, matelot ? J'ai prév: Ready for your lesson, sailor? I've warned Kevin. He said “again?”. No idea what he meant.
textes.Prêt pour un tour, avec moi à côté ?: Ready for a ride, with me beside you?
textes.Prêt pour une partie, le pro des boutons: Ready for a game, button pro?
textes.Prêt à charger de nouveau ! Je vais crie: Ready to charge again! I'll shout even louder this time!
textes.Prête depuis vingt minutes. Citron, miel: Ready for twenty minutes. Lemon, honey. Drink.
textes.Prête pour la revanche, mademoiselle ?: Ready for the rematch, young lady?
textes.Prête. Mes cheveux se redressent. C'est: Ready. My hair is standing up again. That means I'm ready.
textes.Prêtes ? PRÊTES ? (Ses lunettes fument.): Ready? READY? (His glasses are smoking.) I'm missing the main thing: sulfur! Three fine crystals, from the hot springs, at the foot of the volcano, to the west. Without them, my rockets will go “pfff.” With them: KABOOM, in seven colors!
Priestess! The equinox is tomorrow. Certain.
textes.Prêtresse ! La barque est prête. Vous do: Priestess! The boat is ready. Will you be sleeping today?
Priestess! The balché honey is ready.
textes.Prêtresse ! Trois cent soixante-cinq mar: Priestess! Three hundred and sixty-five steps!
textes.Prêtresse, votre robe tient bien ?: Priestess, is your robe holding up well?
textes.Pschhh ! Le drone t'arrose consciencieus: Pssshh! The drone waters you very thoroughly, from head to shoulders. Growing any better now?
textes.Pschhh ! Plic t'a pris pour un ficus. Un: Pssshh! Plic has mistaken you for a ficus. A very surprised ficus.
textes.Pschhh ! Une petite pluie fraîche sur ta: Pssshh! A cool little shower on your head. Plic gives a satisfied beep: one more plant watered.
textes.Pschhht ! Question de graffeuse : c'est: Pssshht! Graffiti artist's question: what's your favourite colour?
textes.Pschhht ! Évidemment ! Tout le monde peu: Pschhht! Of course! Everyone can paint here! Here: three cans of spray paint, homemade, from beetroot, spinach and blueberry. They smell a bit like soup, that's normal. Go to the Expression Wall, west of town, or any other paintable wall, and leave your mark. Three graffiti pieces! A wall is like a page of a zine, but bigger and more vertical. And don't be afraid of messing up: the wall doesn't judge. Me, a little, but kindly.
textes.Pschhht ! … Oh, pardon, je ne t'avais pa: Pschhht! … Oh, sorry, I didn't see you behind my cloud of colours. Pigment, graffiti artist. All the walls in Port-Boucan, that's me. Well, nearly all: there's a grey one, at Lisse's Office. For now.
textes.Pschhh… ALERTE ! ALERTE ! Ici Radio Bouc: Pshhh… ALERT! ALERT! This is Radio Boucan: Lisse's robots are landing! Everybody outside, form a chain!
textes.Pschhh… Fin de transmission. Non, je pla: Pschhh… End of transmission. No, just kidding. Radio Boucan never stops. Except when the antenna falls down. And it's holding. Who do we thank? We thank {joueur}!
textes.Pschhh… Ici Radio Boucan, 98.7, la radio: Pschhh… This is Radio Boucan, 98.7, the radio that never switches off… except when the antenna falls down! And it's hanging on tight! Good morning, Port-Boucan!
textes.Pschhh… Question d'auditeur ! Tu écoutes: Pschhh… Listener question! Do you listen to the radio? And when?
textes.Pschhh… URGENT ! Une descente des déména: Pschhh… URGENT! A removal raid is heading for the Cannery! I repeat: the Cannery! Link arms!
textes.Pschhh… Victoire ! La descente est repou: Pschhh… Victory! The raid has been pushed back! The sofa is back inside! Ferraille is picking up the bolts!
textes.Pschhh… merci, Plic. J'avais justement s: Pssshh… thanks, Plic. I was just getting thirsty.
textes.Pschhh… un peu, mon ami ! Pschhh !: Pschhh… a little, my friend! Pschhh!
textes.Psst ! Approche, j'ai appris quelque cho: Psst! Come closer, I've learned something about you.
textes.Psst ! Approchez, j'ai appris quelque ch: Psst! Come closer, I've learned something about you.
textes.Psst ! Boum, ba-da boum ! Tu as le rythm: Psst! Boom, ba-da boom! Have you got rhythm?
textes.Psst ! C'est Glitch, des Arcades. J'ai v: Psst! It's Glitch, from the Arcades. I saw Mister Fil's “program” jump into your journal. I got into the system to help you. This virus is protected by three locks: we'll break them one by one!
textes.Psst ! Toi ! Un programme pas cher ?: Psst! You! Fancy a cheap program?
textes.Psst ! Toi ! Viens dire bonjour à une vi: Psst! You! Come and say hello to an old star!
textes.Psst ! Vous ! Regardez là-haut ! … Ah, i: Psst! You! Look up there! … Ah, it's daytime. Sorry.
textes.Psst, le grand ! Tu as des perles ?: Psst, big one! Got any pearls?
textes.Psst. Je connais un passage secret sous: Psst. I know a secret passage under the Hall. Eat a Moonling, you'll see it glow. I didn't say anything.
textes.Psst. Le Capitaine Rigatoni a une vieill: Psst. Captain Rigatoni has an old treasure map in his boat. I've seen it! It's covered in sauce stains. Well, I hope it's sauce.
textes.Psst. Notre secret, tu sais… Je ne l'ai: Psst. Our secret, you know… I haven't told anyone. Have you? Cross my heart and swear on my ears.
Psst. Your bag is beeping. No, just kidding.
textes.Psst. Tu aimes les guitares qui grincent: Psst. Do you like screeching guitars?
textes.Psst… Par ici, humain. Approche, n'aie p: Psst… Over here, human. Come closer, don't be afraid.
textes.Psst… Petit… tu veux une histoire ?: Psst… Little one… want a story?
textes.Psst… Tu as vu des feuilles vertes, toi: Psst… Have you seen any green leaves?
Psst… Can you hear? They're drinking.
Psst… Come and see my tomatoes. Gently.
textes.Pst ! Tu sais faire un nœud de chaise ?: Psst! Can you tie a bowline?
textes.Ptahmosé ! Je peux toucher l'argile ?: Ptahmosé! Can I touch the clay?
textes.Ptahmosé ! Mon four a fait des merveille: Ptahmosé! My oven worked wonders this morning.
textes.Ptahmosé ! Ta jarre va bien, et Ptah aus: Ptahmosé! Your jar is doing well, and so is Ptah!
textes.Ptahmosé ! Ta roue tourne toujours ?: Ptahmosé! Is your wheel still turning?
textes.Ptahmosé fait des jarres et des scarabée: Ptahmosé makes jars and lucky scarabs. He says “Hm” all the time. He pretends to be grumpy. But he let me touch the clay. With my fingers!
textes.Ptahmosé fait des jarres qui ne fuient j: Ptahmosé makes jars that never leak, and a face that never laughs. I like him. I annoy him a lot. The two go together.
textes.Ptahmosé fait les meilleures jarres du f: Ptahmosé makes the best jars on the river and the worst face in the village. He says his oven is better than mine. He's the one who made mine. Go figure.
textes.Ptahmosé fait ses jarres sur une roue. U: Ptahmosé makes his jars on a wheel. A wheel! The clay rises all by itself, as if by magic. He hardly talks, he says “Hm”. But his “Hm”s are very expressive. I think he's a friend.
textes.Ptahmosé se moque de moi parce que je pa: Ptahmosé makes fun of me because I talk to crocodiles. He says it makes them laugh. He makes good jars. I've taken forty of them. I don't know what to put in them any more.
Ptahmosé. Not a word about my crocodile.
textes.Ptoui ! La grenouille te recrache… Tu es: Ptooey! The frog spits you out… You're covered in slime. It smells of mud.
textes.Public averti — rhum, grog, insultes s: Mature  —  rum, grog, salty insults, rougher brawls
textes.Puis fermer la taverne un soir, rien qu': Then close the tavern one evening, just one, sit with Fatima at the end of the jetty, and keep watch over nothing at all. Not the door, not the sea.
textes.Puis je redescendrais à sept heures pile: Then I'd come back down at seven sharp to take up my post. One mustn't overdo it.
textes.Puis-je aider le jury de la Foire ?: Can I help the Fair's judges?
textes.Puis-je vous confier quelque chose, {sur: May I confide something in you, {surnom}? Every evening, I write one sentence in a notebook, for those who will live here in a hundred years. I don't tell them about laws or budgets. I tell them about a child who laughed at a jellyfish, about the Singer passing by, about a traveller who said hello to the fish. I'd like them to know that we were happy here. That's all I want to leave them.

May I confide something in you, {surnom}? In my drawer, there's a notebook. Every evening, I write one sentence in it for those who will live here in a hundred years. Yesterday: “On this day, children from up top wept with joy before a lanternfish.” I would like them to know that we were happy here.
textes.Puis-je vous poser une question pour vot: May I ask you a question for your record, {surnom}? When you set off on an adventure, do you make a list first?
textes.Puis-je vous poser une question, {surnom: May I ask you a question, {surnom}? Where you come from, does one wipe one's feet before coming in?
textes.Puisqu'il s'entête à nier, je lui rends: Since he insists on denying it, I give him back his lavender. Every morning, I take the sprig from my bench and, on my way past, I lay it in the middle of his pétanque pitch, right where he aims. He pretends not to understand. Raymond seems to find it very amusing.
textes.Punch ! Un connaisseur ! Je te le prépar: Punch! A connoisseur! I'm making it for you in my head: lots of coconut, a little lime, a striped straw. And a little umbrella, because you're worth it.
textes.Puni. J'ai branché ma toupie sur la Flèc: Grounded. I plugged my spinning top into the Spire. The whole Agora flashed pink. Volt made his Volt face. But everybody clapped! It was a show, not mischief!
textes.Pyra ! Ta tasse de l'autre jour…: Pyra! Your cup the other day…
textes.Pyra Flammèche m'apprendra la boule de f: Pyra Flammèche will teach me the fireball if I bring her three logs of twisted wood. Then I'll have to light the five braziers of the Duelling Ground in a row.
textes.Pyra a donné des noms aux trois mannequi: Pyra gave names to the three dummies on the Duelling Ground: Bertrand, Hubert and Germaine. I've burnt Bertrand eleven times. I say sorry to him every morning when I arrive. Hubert, six. Germaine, only once, but she was at the other end of the Ground, behind me. Pyra says it's the island record. She didn't say it nicely.
textes.Pyra a fait fondre mon lac, un hiver, po: Pyra melted my lake one winter to take a hot bath. I haven't forgiven her. Neither has the lake.
textes.Pyra brûle de tout : de colère, de joie,: Pyra burns with everything: anger, joy, pride. She's an excellent teacher and a very sore loser. I brought her to the Academy at eight, by the ear.
textes.Pyra dit que je vois des serpents de mer: Pyra says I see sea serpents because I drink. I drink because I see sea serpents. She's the one getting it backwards.
textes.Pyra est une bonne fille, brûlante dehor: Pyra's a good girl, scorching on the outside and soft on the inside. She only comes to see me when it really hurts, hand behind her back. I've been looking after her since she was eight.
textes.Pyra et Borée, chaque soir, s'assoient c: Every evening, Pyra and Borée sit at opposite ends of the room. I serve them the same soup. They don't know.
textes.Pyra passe devant ma roulotte au pas de: Pyra charges past my caravan shouting “I don't want to know!”. She's right and wrong at the same time. That shout is almost a friendship.
Pyra, Borée is dining at Berthe's tonight.
textes.Pyra, c'est la meilleure. Elle crie, ell: Pyra's the best. She shouts, smoke comes out of her ears, but she's never thrown me off the Duelling Ground. She never claps. For anyone. One day, she'll clap for me. I'm sure of it. Almost.
textes.Pyra, je l'ai connue au berceau, avec tr: Pyra, I've known her since the cradle, with three hundred candles burning around her. She shouts loud, she burns my tea towels, and one day she said my pie had too much nutmeg. I love her anyway. Almost as much as my pie.
textes.Pyra, tes bottes ! Tu fumes sur mon plan: Pyra, your boots! You're smoking on my floor.
textes.Pyrus ! Les chiens sauvages, tu leur as: Pyrus! The wild dogs, have you talked to them?
textes.Pyrus est capitaine de la Garde. Il négo: Pyrus is captain of the Guard. He bargains like a fishmonger and pays like a captain: late. He's a good guard. I knew him when he was very young, on the rampart. He doesn't remember. Just as well.
textes.Pyrus est le plus loyal des capitaines e: Pyrus is the most loyal of captains and the noisiest of bodyguards. With his armour, you can hear him coming from the other end of the city. It's reassuring. And a bit awkward, when you want to slip away.
textes.Pyrus est mon grand frère. Il est capita: Pyrus is my big brother. He's captain of the Guard, he's as straight as a halberd, and he wants to drive away the wild dogs of the lava field. I don't agree. I love him anyway. A lot.
textes.Pyrus marchande comme un poissonnier. «: Pyrus haggles like a fishmonger. “Guard's price”, he says. The Guard is him. So is the price, apparently.
textes.Pyrus me suit partout, avec son armure :: Pyrus follows me everywhere, in his armour: clang, clang, clang. I can hear him coming from the Circle of Fire. One day, I'll give him slippers.
textes.Pyrus, c'est mon mari. Le plus sérieux d: Pyrus is my husband. The most serious of captains, the clumsiest of dancers and the most tender of fathers. He goes clang when he walks. I love that sound. I'd know it among a thousand.
Pyrus, I'm going to the market. Alone.
textes.PÉTILLANE — une planète où il pleut de l: FIZZARIA — a planet where it rains lemonade. Umbrellas are useless there. Straws, essential.
textes.Père Bastien ! Mon boulon a poussé ?: Old Bastien! Has my bolt grown?
textes.Père Clotaire ! Votre pain, tout chaud !: Father Clotaire! Your bread, piping hot!
textes.Père Clotaire a béni Noisette quand elle: Father Clotaire blessed Noisette when she was a baby. He falls asleep during his sermons, but he never falls asleep when someone needs him. I take him his bread every morning. It's a pleasure.
textes.Père Clotaire est le seul qui comprend m: Father Clotaire is the only one who understands my talent. He sleeps sitting down, I sleep standing up. We don't talk much. We snore together. It's a beautiful friendship.
textes.Père Clotaire et moi, on a fait un conco: Father Clotaire and I held a napping contest. Nobody won. We woke up the next day, and we'd both forgotten we were having a contest.
textes.Père Clotaire m'a fait promettre : jamai: Father Clotaire made me promise: never with someone who isn't registered. He says it's for my safety. I think it's for yours.
textes.Père Clotaire m'a recueillie un soir d'o: Father Clotaire took me in one stormy night and taught me to heal. He falls asleep during his sermons, but never when someone needs him. Never.
textes.Père Clotaire, je peux me mettre près de: Father Clotaire, may I stand by the door?
textes.Père Gaubert disait que j'étais un bon à: Père Gaubert used to say I was good for nothing. Then I found him a truffle as big as his fist. He cried. Germaine made an omelette.
textes.Père Gaubert est le seul qui rit quand j: Père Gaubert is the only one who laughs when I blow on my mill. He comes and sits on the fence. He doesn't make fun. He laughs with me. He's a good neighbour. His turnips are weird.
textes.Père Gaubert me promet des navets pour m: Père Gaubert promises me turnips for my frog with turnips. He says yes. The turnips say no. They escape from my pot. He's a man of his word, with unruly vegetables.
textes.Père Gaubert, Truffe veut venir avec moi: Père Gaubert, Truffe wants to come with me.
textes.Père Gaubert, c'est mon meilleur client: Père Gaubert is my best customer for alerts. When his turnips wake up, I ring Marguerite and the whole town runs to his place. He waves to me from afar. He waves his cap.
textes.Père Gaubert, qu'est-ce qui a creusé ce: Père Gaubert, what dug this hole in your field?
textes.Père Gaubert. Le secret, toujours ?: Père Gaubert. Still keeping the secret?
textes.Père monte dans la nacelle. Il raconte l: Father gets in the basket. He tells the passengers the story of the basket. Grandpa Frêne, the wicker, the ropes. At the top, not finished. The passengers ask for another ride. Then another. Three rides, one story. Hrmm. I sigh. He says I'm good for business.
textes.Père. Trois mille mots par jour. Moi, tr: Father. Three thousand words a day. Me, three. That makes an average. Hrmm. Best father. Don't tell him: he'd make a story of it.
textes.Pélagos a planté une pancarte dans mes j: Pélagos put up a sign in my gardens: “One in three. No more.” I cut one in three, I swear! But I count my own way. One morning he recounted behind me, stem by stem, for two hours. He found one too many. He kept it in his pocket all week, to show me.
textes.Pélagos garde les jardins comme un requi: Pélagos guards the gardens like a shark guards its reef. Every time I cut a strand of seaweed, he sighs. But when the crystal grows pale, he's the one who watches over my crops.
textes.Pélagos ne parle presque pas. Moi non pl: Pélagos hardly talks. Neither do I. We get on very well. I blow his basins, he lets me win at jacks.
textes.Pélagos parle peu, sauf aux coraux. Mais: Pélagos doesn't say much, except to the corals. But he's the only one who notices when I move a single thread in a weave.
textes.Pélagos, tu rentres pour souper ?: Pélagos, are you coming home for supper?
textes.Pélagos. Les vasques tiennent ?: Pélagos. Are the basins holding up?
textes.Pépin ! D'où viennent ces feuilles dans: Pépin! Where did those leaves in your hair come from?
textes.Pépin ! Où étais-tu pendant le cours d'h: Pépin! Where were you during history class?
textes.Pépin ! Tu as fait tes devoirs ?: Pépin! Have you done your homework?
textes.Pépin a apporté son chronomètre de Cliqu: Pépin brought his Cliquetis stopwatch. To the Circle. He counted my beats. “One boom every two seconds, Bourru! Every TWO!” I waited. Four seconds. I said: “Hrmm.” He wrote that down too. Hrmm. He writes everything down.
textes.Pépin a la tête dans les champignons et: Pépin has his head in the mushrooms and his pockets full of fireflies. He doesn't listen to anything, but he watches everything. His sparks are “original”. That's the kind word I found.
textes.Pépin aime trop le Bois de Cendre. Il di: Pépin loves the Ash Wood too much. He says he knows the way by heart. I say a path you know by heart is a path you always end up getting lost on while thinking about something else. It's scientific.
textes.Pépin dit qu'il crache des étincelles pl: Pépin says he can spit sparks further than me. I measured: him, four paces. Me, five and a half paces. Numbers don't lie, Pépin.
textes.Pépin dit que personne n'a jamais battu: Pépin says nobody has ever beaten Bondi in the Great Race. Bondi says that's because nobody has really tried yet.
textes.Pépin et moi, on a un club secret sous l: Pépin and I have a secret club under the Grand Square staircase: the Free Imps Club. I'm president, vice-president and treasurer. Pépin is chief explorer. He wanted to be president. We held a vote. I won one vote to nil: he voted for me, because I'd given him a mushroom.
textes.Pépin m'a apporté un champignon qui bril: Pépin brought me a glowing mushroom to ask if he could use it instead of a flame in the exam. I said no. He looked so disappointed that I kept the mushroom on my desk. Its name is Henri, apparently. It still glows at night, when I mark the papers.
textes.Pépin m'a convaincu de courir une Grande: Pépin talked me into running a Great Race. Just one! “You'll see, Roux, it's thrilling!” At the start, I was full of beans. At the sixth arch, there was such a lovely patch of moss… They found me there, asleep, long after the finish. Pépin says I gave up. I say I invented a new race: the slowest in the world.
textes.Pépin m'a demandé un chiot. Je lui ai di: Pépin asked me for a pup. I told him: “When you know all twelve of their names.” That very evening, he came back and recited them, from Braise to Grignotte, without a single mistake. I was stuck. So I said: “And their birthdays.” His eyes went wide, he said “OK”, and off he went counting on his fingers.
textes.Pépin n'est pas venu à l'école ! Je pari: Pépin didn't come to school! I bet he's in the Ash Wood. I said so: a path you know by heart, you get lost on it thinking about something else. … I hope he's all right.
textes.Pépin passe à mon étal tous les jours à: Pépin comes by my stall every day at four on the dot. He's a little pilferer with a big heart, always full of mushrooms and questions. He reminds me of me, only skinnier.
textes.Pépin s'entraîne au tambour derrière ma: Pépin practises drumming behind my bakery. Now my bread rises in rhythm.
textes.Pépin tape trop fort sur son tambour. Bo: Pépin hits his drum too hard. Bourru hits his too slowly. Together, it's exactly the right rhythm. It's a mystery.
textes.Pépin tape trop fort, toujours. Je lui d: Pépin always drums too hard. I ask him every evening to slow down, he promises every evening. And every evening, when the moon comes, he gets carried away. He has a good heart, but no brakes.
textes.Pépin était le meilleur ami de Cerfeuil,: Pépin was Cerfeuil's best friend, and he's Mochi's godfather. For five years, he's been “running past” every morning. He carries the flour, he times everything, he makes a racket. He's precious.
textes.Pépin, c'est l'organisateur. Il a dit «: Pépin's the organiser. He said “cheating” about my spring shoes. He was right. But still. He's nice: he's never won either, he understands.
textes.Pépin, c'est mon copain. Il court partou: Pépin's my pal. He runs everywhere, I sleep everywhere: we complement each other. I taught him the rhythms of Tazira, and since then, he never stops. Boom, boom-boom. Even in his sleep, I bet.
textes.Pépin, c'est mon fils, mon trésor et mon: Pépin is my son, my treasure and my worry. He has his head in the mushrooms and feet that wander off on their own towards the Ash Wood. He tells me about his day three times every evening. I never tire of it.
textes.Pépin, c'est mon meilleur copain. Il ne: Pépin is my best pal. He never knows his lesson, his pockets are full of mushrooms, and he gets lost thinking about something else. But he's very funny. And very nice. Don't tell him I said nice.
textes.Pépin, c'est mon petit-fils. Il a le pie: Pépin's my grandson. He's got sea legs, pockets full of mushrooms and the look of a real explorer. He only knows one knot, the shoelace knot. But he does it very well.
textes.Pépin, le lapin qui organise la Grande C: Pépin, the rabbit who organises Ramure's Great Race, is looking for someone who can beat Bondi, the champion three years running.
textes.Pépin, le petit diablotin de Zébuline, n: Pépin, Zébuline's little imp, hasn't come home from the Academy. His classmates saw him heading off to the Ash Wood to see the glowing mushrooms.
textes.Pépin, mon voisin de l'arbre du sud. Il: Pépin, my neighbour in the south tree. He organises the race, he paints up the records, he times everything. The runner who's never won, but the best at talking about it. Hop. I like him.
textes.Pépin, qu'est-ce qui bouge dans ta poche: Pépin, what's moving in your pocket?
Pépin. Drums too fast. Talks too fast. Runs too fast, they say. Hrmm. Nice, though. Too fast.
textes.Pépé Fernand, c'est le plus vieux pêcheu: Grandpa Fernand is the oldest fisherman in the harbour and the biggest liar on the coast. I divide all his fish by two. But he makes me laugh, and a man who makes a fishmonger laugh at six in the morning is a keeper.
textes.Pétillante ! Les fleurs géantes ont donn: Sparkling! The giant flowers gave a double ration of nectar.
textes.Pétillante ! Mes lucioles ont dansé tout: Sparkly! My fireflies danced all night.
textes.Pétronille a peur de tout, tombe sur tou: Pétronille is afraid of everything, falls over everything, and heals everything. She's the best healer I've ever trained. The only one, too. But the best.
textes.Pétronille tombe plus souvent que moi. M: Pétronille falls more often than I do. But I fall from higher up, when the lightning lifts me. It's a matter of perspective. She's very kind. And very wet, often.
textes.Pétronille, merci pour le soin, tout à l: Pétronille, thank you for the healing earlier. My hair thanks you too.
textes.Pétronille, vous êtes tombée dans la fla: Pétronille, you fell in the puddle. The third one.
textes.Pêcher ? Pour toi, {surnom}, oui. Tiens,:
Fishing? For you, {surnom}, yes. Here, take my old rod. Look after it, it's the only thing that came with me from the shipwreck. Along with Gaston. And my socks.

Equip it, go up to the water, hold {bouton} to wind up and release to cast. When the float dips: {bouton} again, quick!
textes.Pêcher ? Si je sais pêcher ! J'ai une vi: Fishing? Do I know how to fish! I've got an old rod, right there, under my imaginary hammock. But I don't lend it to just anyone, {surnom}. We hardly know each other.
textes.Pêcher et apporter à Paulo deux dorades: Catch two sea bream and two mackerel and bring them to Paulo
textes.Pêcher le poisson-lune doré dont tout le: To catch the golden sunfish everyone talks about. I'd let it go, mind. But I'd have the face of someone who caught it, and that'd be enough for me.
textes.Q / D : virer, Z : piquer (plus vite), S: Q / D: turn, Z: dive (faster), S: pull up (slower), E: land.
textes.QU'ON TE CRIE DESSUS ?! MAIS JE NE CRIE: BEING SHOUTED AT?! BUT I'M NOT SHOUTING! … Am I? … Fine. I'll talk… less loud. A bit.
textes.QUAI DE CHARGEMENT\n(2 m : trop haut ? u:
LOADING DOCK
(2 m: too high? a crate!)
textes.QUEL CONCERT ! Tu as vu la fosse ? Tu as: WHAT A CONCERT! Did you see the pit? Did you see Granny Barricade raise her fist up on the mezzanine? Did you see Clou SMILE? I did, I saw everything, and now I've lost my voice. (She whispers.) Thank you. Without you, it would have been a tiny little racket. Here: the door takings. There was no door, it's free, so it's the takings from the donation box. And you are now, officially, forever... Number 1 Fan of the Bilge Rats.
textes.QUEL GOUVERNEUR ?! Mais… moi ! Le tricor: WHAT GOVERNOR?! Why… me! The golden tricorn! The residence! The lanterns! … Right. I'll make one more speech tonight. Clearly they're needed.
textes.QUESTION ! … pardon. Question : tu mets: QUESTION! … sorry. Question: do you play your music loud or soft?
textes.QUI JE SUIS ?! (Il chancelle.) Rodrigue: WHO AM I?! (He staggers.) Rodrigue! RODRIGUE! The one who… Fine. Very well. You'll regret it. You'll regret it when I'm famous.
textes.QUOI ?! LE TAMBOUR ? … BON. PLUS FORT QU: WHAT?! THE DRUM? … FINE. LOUDER THAN LAST TIME.
textes.QUOI ?! QU'EST-CE QU'ELLE A, MA SOIRÉE ?: WHAT?! WHAT'S WRONG WITH MY EVENING?!
textes.QUOI ?! QUI ?! QUELLE ANNÉE ?! … Huit ce: WHAT?! WHO?! WHAT YEAR?! … Eight hundred years?! I said “just five minutes”! … Well. Thanks, you know. Here, I dreamed about this the whole nap, I'll give it to you.
textes.QUOI ?! Qu'est-ce que tu veux ?! Belle-H: WHAT?! What do you want?! Belle-Humeur, gunner! And no jokes about my name!
textes.QUOI ?! Tu aimes ces démons à moustaches: WHAT?! You like those whiskered demons? Maybe you're his accomplice. Where were you, the night of the map? … I've got my eye on you, landlubber. My eye!
textes.QUOI ?! … AH. C'EST TOI. TES DEUX DENTS: WHAT?! … AH. IT'S YOU. YOUR TWO TEETH HOLDING UP?
WHAT?! … YES. VERY WELL. WITH THE SEA.
textes.QUOI ?! … TANT MIEUX. ILS PAIERONT LEUR: WHAT?! … GOOD. THEY CAN PAY FOR THEIR GROG.
textes.Qu'Achille atterrisse. Entier, avec ses: For Achille to land. In one piece, with both arms, both legs and his appetite. Then for him to lend me the wings just once. Not high: just above the rooftops, the ones Papa and Mama laid. With an umbrella in my hand. Just in case.
textes.Qu'après moi, quelqu'un raconte le naufr: That after me, someone tells the shipwreck by the stove of the Bordée. Not word for word, mind. In their own words. Ewen, maybe. He already adds dragons everywhere.
textes.Qu'as-tu lu ce matin ?: What did you read this morning?
textes.Qu'as-tu lu ce matin, petite ?: What did you read this morning, little one?
textes.Qu'elle rende les gens heureux… (Il sour: That it makes people happy… (He smiles into his beard.) You know what? That's the only thing we should have written on the Bridge. I'll bring it up at the Assembly.
Then let it come out outside.
textes.Qu'elles sentent bon ! Les âmes trouvero: How good they smell! The souls will find their way this year. (She tucks one behind your ear.) That one's for you.
textes.Qu'elles sont belles ! (Elle les plante: How beautiful they are! (She plants them one by one, and the ash around them begins to glow.) They'll shine all night. Just like you, little spark.
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'elle a dit, cette bavarde ?: And what did the chatterbox say?
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'il y a à voir par ici ?: What is there to see around here?
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'on voit du sommet ?: What can you see from the top?
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un Moaï dit à un autre Moaï: What does one Moai say to another Moai?
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un Moaï met sur ses frites: What does a Moai put on his fries?
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un balai dit à un autre bal: What does one broom say to another broom? Nothing: they're too busy sweeping. … I made it up thirty years ago. Nobody laughs. I do.
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un canif ?: What do you call a very small knife?
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un crabe qui a perdu une pi: What do you call a crab that's lost a claw? Single-handed. … All right, fine, that one's Ewen's.
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un crabe qui fait du vélo ?: What's a crab on a bicycle? A crab that goes sideways, only faster.
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un cristal dit à une lanter: What did the crystal say to the lantern? “Stop looking at me like that, you'll make me blush.” And the lantern: “Too late, you're glowing.”
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un engrenage dit à un autre: What did one gear say to the other gear? “Shall we turn together?” And the other one replied: “Which way?” That was the start of a long argument.
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un néon dit à un autre néon: What did one neon sign say to the other? “You light me up!”
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un ours qui n'a pas de dent: What do you call a bear with no teeth? A gummy bear! … Don't tell Ursule.
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un pirate qui a perdu son b: What do you call a pirate who's lost his ship? A pedestrian. Ha!
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un pirate sans bateau ? Un: What's a pirate without a ship? A rat. What's a rat with a ship? A captain! HA!
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un punk dit à un autre punk: What does a punk say to another punk who's lost their safety pin? “Don't worry, mate, we'll sew it out together.”
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un rail dit à un autre rail: What did one rail say to the other rail? “See you at the next junction!” … Bielle tells it at every concert. We laugh every time. We used to out of politeness. Now it's tradition.
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un sorcier qui a raté son s: What do you call a wizard who botched his levitation spell? A wizard on the floor.
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un sustentateur dit à un au: What does one levitator say to another? “Shall we stay up?” And the other one replies: “We don't really have a choice.”
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'un tournesol dit quand il f: What does a sunflower say when the sky is grey? “Nothing. I'm waiting.”
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'une bulle dit à une autre b: What does one bubble say to another bubble in the Fountain? “See you at the top!” And the other one replies: “Well, it's not as if I can do anything else.”
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'une grenouille géante dit à: What does a giant frog say to an adventurer? Nothing: its mouth is full!
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'une pyramide avec un rhume: What do you call a pyramid with a cold? A pyra-snot! … The children love that one.
textes.Qu'est-ce qu'une étoile dit à une autre: What did one star say to the other star? “You look radiant, you're glowing!” … It's an Ondelune joke. It's a million years old. It's a bit tired.
textes.Qu'est-ce que ce chat vous a volé ?: What did that cat steal from you?
textes.Qu'est-ce que tu aimerais faire, un jour: What would you like to do one day?
textes.Qu'est-ce que tu as encore mis dedans ?: What have you put in it this time?
textes.Qu'est-ce que tu fiches chez moi ?!: What are you doing in my house?!
textes.Qu'est-ce que tu retiens de moi ?: What do you remember about me?
textes.Qu'est-ce que tu veux, toi ? Gontran Les: What do YOU want? Gontran Lestrange. Captain of the Veuve Écarlate. They call me Jambe-de-Bois — Peg-Leg — but not to my face. Unless they want a wooden leg too.
textes.Qu'est-ce qui a des dents mais ne mord j: What has teeth but never bites?
textes.Qu'est-ce qui est jaune, qui flotte dans: What's yellow, floats in the sky and goes “yum”? The Great Flying Spaghetti after the Great Table!
textes.Qu'est-ce qui est noir et blanc et qui r: What's black and white and red all over? A zebra who's done something silly!
textes.Qu'est-ce qui est vert, qui monte et qui: What's green and goes up and down?
textes.Qu'est-ce qui parle tout le temps et n'é: What talks all the time and never listens to the end…
textes.Qu'est-ce qui se passe au port ?: What's going on at the harbour?
textes.Qu'est-il écrit au-dessus de la porte de: What is written above the gate of the Nine Circles?
textes.Qu'il fera beau demain. Sujet, verbe, so: That the weather will be fine tomorrow. Subject, verb, sunshine.
textes.Qu'il me réponde. Un jour. Une ligne, n': For him to reply. One day. One line, any line. Even “received”. No, not “received”. Something better than “received”.
textes.Qu'il passe ! J'ai mon pilon !: Let him come! I've got my pestle!
See that it stays that way.
Let them shine. And let them stay quiet.
textes.Qu'on veille sur vous. C'est honnête, et: That someone watches over you. That's honest, and it's rare to admit it. Here, everyone watches over everyone. That's what a town is. Welcome.
textes.Qu'un jour, Barnabé prenne ma place au p: That one day, Barnabé takes my place at the Funicular's controls. He's scared of going up, so he's made for going down. I'll sit on the passengers' bench, look outside, and for the first time in my life, I'll go “oh” with everyone else when the cabin comes out of the cliff.
textes.Qu'un jour, quelqu'un batte Bondi ! Pas: That one day, somebody beats Bondi! Not so he loses, mind: so I can paint a brand-new name at the top of the record board, with the lovely red paint I'm saving for it. Boom!
That one day, someone will read my scrolls. All of them. From first to last. And come and tell me: “There's a comma missing in scroll six thousand.” I'd be the happiest Atlantean under the dome.
textes.Qu'un jour, sur l'Aire, devant tous les: That one day, on the Duelling Ground, in front of all the apprentices, my fireball flies nice and straight, nice and round, and hits Bertrand. Only Bertrand. And then I hear clapping. Just one pair of hands would do.
textes.Qu'un jour, une de mes mouettes revienne: That one day, one of my seagulls comes back from the City of Clouds with news from up there. And that I'm the first to know it. Before Rosalie. Just once.
textes.Qu'un matin, la Zahra tombe sur un banc: That one morning, the Zahra comes across a shoal so big the sea turns silver all the way to the Skala. And the whole town climbs onto the ramparts to see it.
textes.Qu'un soir, quelqu'un s'assoie sur ma pi: That one evening, someone sits on my stone and tells a story better than me. I'll sit in the front row, and I won't correct a thing. Well, hardly a thing.
textes.Qu'un soir, à la Bielle, mon piano s'arr: That one evening, at the Bielle, my piano stops in the middle of a waltz. Just like that, without warning. And that I dare to finish the piece myself, in front of everyone. Even with a wrong note. Especially with a wrong note.
textes.Qu'y a-t-il dans le Livre des Vents ?: What's in the Book of Winds?
textes.Quand Albertine a fait son nid dans son: When Albertine made her nest in his hat, I went up to the castle to apologise. The Baron received me in the throne room, hat on his head, egg inside, motionless as a statue. He said: “Don't apologise, Captain. It's the finest hat in my collection.” He didn't move his head. For a week.
textes.Quand Ali a sorti la Zahra du chantier,: When Ali brought the Zahra out of the boatyard, the whole harbour came to see. Me, I looked at the eye painted on the prow, the way grandmother taught me, and I said: “It's cross-eyed.” The face Ahmed made! Ali swore it was on purpose. Six years later, I stand by it: it's cross-eyed. But it brings my brother home every evening, so I forgive it.
textes.Quand Aurore m'a demandé une bulle pour: When Aurore asked me for a bubble to heal people in, I spent a month inventing a very soft glass that lets the light from her hands through without hurting it. On opening day, she laid her hand on the wall. The whole dome lit up pink. We both cried.
textes.Quand Barricade s'est assise trois semai: When Barricade sat in front of the Cannery for three weeks, I brought her tea every morning. Without a word, so she wouldn't know it was me. I'd set down the cup and leave quickly. She never knew. Well, I think. Sometimes she has a funny smile in the mornings.
textes.Quand Bartholomé a eu son gros rhume, il: When Bartholomé had his big cold, he sneezed “jellyfish-head” every thirty seconds. Doc nursed him with a little spoon and honey tea. Bartholomé thanked him by pinching his nose, very hard, for a very long time. Doc saw stars. I told him it was a kiss. He said: “Then he loves me enormously.”
textes.Quand Bernadette a perdu une roue, il y: When Bernadette lost a wheel, ten years ago, Brunehaut forged the new one in a single night. She fitted it herself, in the morning, laughing so hard the wheel turned on its own.
textes.Quand Boulon vient au labo, il aboie apr: When Boulon comes to the lab, he barks at the sparks. All of them. One by one. He thinks they're fireflies making fun of him. One day, after barking too hard at a very big spark, his little heart started limping. Électre repaired it. Very gently. More gently than her coils.
textes.Quand Bourru passe, je fais « hrmm » tou: When Bourru walks by, I go “hrmm” very quietly, right behind Lilas's ear. She blushes to the tips of her ears. Right to the tips! A pink doe. She pinches me, I laugh, and she says I'm impossible. True. But I'm right.
textes.Quand Brindille était petite, elle se pr: When Brindille was little, she got her wings caught in curtains, doors, chimneys, and she hid them under a big coat. I took her out on the jetty one very windy day, and I said to her: “Open your wings to the wind, and let it carry you.” She took off all at once, shouting with joy. She never put the coat back on.
textes.Quand Bulle était petit, il faisait des: When Bulle was little, he blew bubbles in my watering can. I called him “my little soap bubble”. The whole neighbourhood picked it up, then it was just “Bulle”. One day, he asked me what his real name was. I answered: “Bulle.” And it's true. I'd already forgotten the other one.
textes.Quand Cendrin réfléchit à son coup, je c: When Cendrin is thinking about his move, I start a story. Always the same one: the keeper who listened to the fire. He adores it. He listens, he forgets his move, and I win. On my birthday, he's the one who wins. He thinks I don't notice. I let him think so. It's my present to him.
textes.Quand Dagna a trouvé les champignons de: When Dagna found the ember mushrooms, she was following one of my mother's goats, which had strayed near the fumaroles. Dagna came back with the mushrooms, the goat with singed eyebrows. Dagna says she found them. The goat says nothing. She eats the leftovers.
textes.Quand Elandor a disparu neuf jours, Orop: When Elandor disappeared for nine days, Orophin searched the island without sleeping. He came back with him, exhausted, furious, covered in thorns. I said: “Good work.” He looked at me as if I'd given him a crown. I should say it more often. I won't.
textes.Quand Elandor est rentré de ses neuf jou: When Elandor came back from his nine days, I didn't say a word to him for a week. Every morning he left a flower on the doorstep, a different one, fetched from far away. The seventh I had never seen in my life. I forgave him, because of the flower. Well, mostly.
textes.Quand Ewen parle de remettre le Léviatha: When Ewen talks about putting the Léviathan back to sea, my father sighs. One day, I asked him why. He looked at the bay for a long time, and said: “Ships that leave don't always come back.” He wasn't talking about Ewen. I think he was talking about me. I don't know how he knows.
textes.Quand Faelar dort trois jours d'affilée,: When Faelar sleeps three days in a row, I'm the one they come for. I take his pulse, I check his eyelids, I slip a mint leaf under his nose. Last time, he opened one eye and said: “Where was I?” He was in the middle of a story. He finished it.
textes.Quand Faelar s'endort au cercle des cont: When Faelar falls asleep at the story circle, I put a flower on his nose. The others think it's for a laugh. Really it's to check he's breathing: if the flower moves, he's asleep. It always moves. But I check anyway.
textes.Quand Grosse-Dent cogne la roche : taper: When Grosse-Dent hit rock: hit, hit, hit!
textes.Quand Gunnar a reçu son bouclier de gard: When Gunnar got his guard's shield, he came up to the terrace to show me. It shone so bright that Hilda thought there was a second sun. I held it for one minute and handed it back pitch black, with all ten of my fingers on it. He scrubbed all night. The next day, he lent it to me for the Forge Festival.
textes.Quand Hiro était petit, il appelait les: When Hiro was little, he called noodles “soup hair”. I still call him that when he's showing off.
textes.Quand Hugues avait seize ans, il est ren: When Hugues was sixteen, he came back from a mission with an enormous bump and wouldn't eat, out of pride. I put my ladle on the table without a word. He ate two plates. He says he was scared of Gertrude. He never found out she'd never hit anyone. Well, except a goblin.
textes.Quand Hugues est revenu avec son dragon: When Hugues came back with his dragon under his arm, he was nineteen, his hands covered in burns, and he was shaking like a leaf. The whole village laughed at the little beast. Me, I put honey on his hands without a word. He thanked me with a sniffle. Since then, I go “baaa” behind him. It's so he doesn't take himself too seriously. He'd need it, otherwise.
textes.Quand Héloïse a fini le Zéphyr, c'est mo: When Héloïse finished the Zéphyr, I was the one who took the stick. Ten years between Cliquetis, Tazira and Carène, in all weathers: hail, the south wind, the Carène fog, thick as a pancake. A secret gas that smells of cabbage above my head, and the whole island below. The finest office in the archipelago, {surnom}.
textes.Quand L'Hirondelle largue, Félix est sou: When the Swallow casts off, Félix is often on the quay. He never comes aboard. He stays there, hands in his pockets, watching the boat leave until we're just a dot. I wave to him. He waves back. Then he goes home to draw what he hasn't seen.
textes.Quand Lila change de pellicule, je lui r: When Lila changes her film, I tell her about the parties of the old days. The dances on my father's boat, the lanterns in the mine. She writes it all down in a journal. One day she told me she dreamed of photographing a party in a mine. I promised to find her some dwarves. At my age, you have to promise quickly.
textes.Quand Lisse & Fils a voulu raser la Cons: When Lisse & Sons wanted to raze the Cannery, I sat down in front of the door with my knitting needles. Three weeks. I knitted a twelve-metre scarf, from one end of the door to the other. The bulldozers arrived. They didn't know how to get past the scarf. They left. The squat was born that day.
textes.Quand Lucie m'a montré les signes sous l: When Lucie showed me the signs under the keel, I dived with a rope round my waist, me who swims like an anchor. Down there, she took my hand and laid it on the stone. Circles, lines, all cold. I came up crying. I said it was the salt. She pretended to believe me. I think.
textes.Quand Lucie m'a parlé des signes gravés: When Lucie told me about the signs carved under the keel, I thought of my grandfather. He used to say the Léviathan hadn't run aground: it had settled, as if something were waiting for it. I told her so. Then I regretted it, and got back to work. There are things a caulker shouldn't know. He'd sleep even less.
textes.Quand Lulu était petite, je passais une: When Lulu was little, I'd visit her mother once a year, at the sail shed. I'd dance her on my feet between the rolls of canvas. She'd laugh: “Again, Grandpa, the rocking boat!” Now she's the one holding my arm to get down to the dance floor. The roles turn. That's what dancing is.
textes.Quand Lyra est partie veiller l'Arbre sa: When Lyra left to watch over the sacred Tree for good, I gave her a pouch of herbs: half for the Tree, the other half for her, on sad evenings. She gave it all to the Tree. Of course. I've pretended to be cross ever since. It lets me make her drink a cup of tea every time she visits.
textes.Quand Lyra était petite, je me suis endo: When Lyra was little, I fell asleep just before the end of the story of the humans' tree. I slept a whole spring. She didn't wait for the ending: at a hundred, she asked the council to let her guard that tree herself. She thinks I fell asleep on purpose. I'll never say whether it's true.
textes.Quand Maman a eu de la fièvre, j'ai tenu: When Mama had a fever, I ran the bakery. I put on her apron. I sold bread to Aurore and asked her why the Baron needed bread so he wouldn't be sad. She answered: “Because it's your mama's.” I told Mama. She cried. I think it was the fever. But she was smiling.
textes.Quand Maman siffle trois fois, faut rent: When Mum whistles three times, you have to go home. I always wait for the third whistle. At the first one, I pretend not to hear. At the second, I do one more lap. At the third, I run. I do it to be sure she really means it. She knows, I think.
textes.Quand Margaret est partie, le manoir est: When Margaret passed away, the manor became very big. Too big. Footsteps echoed. So I began to fill it: a roc's egg, an admiral's moustache, a pirate's spoon, a king's button… Four thousand objects. So that every room would have someone in it. It doesn't quite work. But it makes for lovely shelves.
textes.Quand Monsieur Lisse a voulu couper le g: When Mister Lisse wanted to cut down the big willow on Pallet Square, I climbed up into it. Three hundred days. Lentille sent my soup up on a pulley, Cerise passed me her fanzine, Tapage told me stories from down below. The willow is still there. As for me, I came back down. A bit sad, actually.
textes.Quand Mélusine sonne la cloche, il faut: When Mélusine rings the bell, you have to run to the Southern Fields, because the turnips are escaping! I'm allowed to watch from the South Gate. I caught one, once. It looked at me. I let it go. It looked sad.
textes.Quand Nimiel a cassé ma porte, Taeron m': When Nimiel broke my door, Taeron made me a new one in a day, with a little round hole in the middle, on purpose: “For the next arrow.” I thought it was very funny. I didn't tell him. He'd have thought we'd made up.
textes.Quand Nimiel a tiré dans ma porte, elle: When Nimiel shot my door, she came to apologise with a drawing: me, the oven and a sun. The drawing hangs above the dough trough. Taeron rebuilt the door. I prefer the drawing. It doesn't creak.
textes.Quand Nimiel était toute petite, je la p: When Nimiel was tiny, I carried her on my shoulders on my walks. She'd pull my ears to steer me: left, right, up. One day she pulled “up” in front of a tree. I tried. Aëlwen patched up my knee. Nimiel thought it was wonderful.
textes.Quand Nox était petit, il sautait du toi: When Nox was little, he jumped off the roof next door flapping his little wings, and landed in my cabbages. Every time! I'd pick him up, give him a herbal tea and send him home. The tenth time, I put a big cushion under the roof. I said it was for my cabbages. It wasn't for my cabbages.
textes.Quand Ondine était toute petite, Thalass: When Ondine was tiny, Thalassa would put her in a basket under my stall while she picked her seaweed. The little one held out her arms to every customer shouting “cracker!”. I sold twice as much that season. I offered to rent her. Thalassa didn't find it funny.
textes.Quand Ori est né, ses parents voulaient: When Ori was born, his parents wanted to call him Nori, like me. I said no: one Nori is enough for the mountain. I took away one letter. “He'll earn others,” I said. He has. Today he writes more letters than all of Forgefer put together.
textes.Quand Pilli avait trois ans, une fièvre: When Pilli was three, a fever took Ollin, and he left for Mictlan, the land below. That same week, a neighbour's dog had a litter of little xolos. Pilli picked one up in his arms and never let go: Tlaco. I told myself Ollin had sent him to us. I still think so. I don't often say it.
textes.Quand Pimprenelle est née, elle a serré: When Pimprenelle was born, she squeezed my finger so hard the midwife said: “That one's going to be a blacksmith.” She wants to be a liftkeeper. At first, it pinched my heart a little. Then I understood: the Column is tons of steel rising to the sky. It's a bit like my forge taking flight.
textes.Quand Père Clotaire était petit, c'est m: When Father Clotaire was little, I was the one who looked after him. He already fell asleep everywhere, even on the swing. I'd wake him with a nudge of my elbow. To this day, when I walk into the temple, he wakes up rubbing his ribs.
textes.Quand Pépin était bébé, je le posais dan: When Pépin was a baby, I'd put him in a basket between the pepper and the cinnamon. He sneezed all day long, and customers bought pepper just to hear him. He never caught a cold. Now he eats infernal chili without crying. He says it's his superpower. I think he's right.
textes.Quand Quark est né, j'avais huit ans lum: When Quark was born, I was eight Lumen years younger… no, older… well, I was already big. I asked why he was so small, why he screamed, why he didn't have antennae yet. Mum told me: “So that you can look after him.” Since then, I look after him. He gets up to mischief. I fix it. That's our job.
textes.Quand Quasar a construit l'Hologuide, il: When Quasar built the Hologuide, he came and spent a week with me at the Gate, to learn how to welcome people. He learned the word “welcome.” He said it forty times in a row, like me. Quasar said it was a bug. I said it was a calling.
textes.Quand Quasar a construit le rayon d'accu: When Quasar built the welcome beam, five hundred years ago, someone was needed to keep the Gate. I raised my hand before he'd even finished his sentence. At last, a real gate, with real visitors! On the first day, I waited from dawn to nightfall. A gull came. I welcomed it.
textes.Quand Roux est revenu de Tazira, il m'a: When Roux came back from Tazira, he showed me the steps they dance in the square over there. I said: “A goat dance!” He said: “Exactly.” I learned it laughing. That same evening, the whole village tried it at the Circle. Bedaine fell on Pépin, and Mother Moon danced it with one paw, without leaving her moss.
textes.Quand Sobek a mangé la niche d'Abouti, K: When Sobek ate Abouti's kennel, Khéty turned up the next day with a new kennel, made from his old boat. Apparently old boats are supposed to be burned. He didn't burn it. Abouti sleeps in it, and he smells of fish now. I bought him a beer. He wanted two. I bought him a beer.
textes.Quand Sobek a piétiné l'orge, je l'ai po: When Sobek trampled the barley, I took it to Mérit anyway, all wet, apologising. It sprouted in the sack. Mérit jumped for joy: that's just what you need for beer, apparently. She made “crocodile beer”. The whole village talks about it. I don't drink it. On principle. Well, not much.
textes.Quand Ysaé est montée vendre ses bijoux: When Ysaé went up to sell her jewellery in Hautefond, I walked her to the service stairs. She said: “Don't hit too hard tonight, Dad, I won't be able to sleep.” That night, I played really softly. For the first time. Bielle looked at me as if I were ill. I wasn't. I was proud, {surnom}. Proud enough to play a solo.
textes.Quand Ysaé était bébé, elle ne s'endorma: When Ysaé was a baby, she would only fall asleep to my bass. One note, very low, very slow. She'd close her eyes on the third beat. Now she's up top. In the evening, I play that note last. It rises up the Column. I think she hears it.
textes.Quand Ysaé était petite, elle venait à l: When Ysaé was little, she came to the Workshop after school. She hid under my workbench and pinched the shards too small for a lantern. I pretended not to see. One day, she gave me a necklace made from my own shards. I still wear it. Under my coat.
textes.Quand c'est court ! Comme ça : « Toi. »: When it's short! Like this: “You.” End of poem. (She thinks.) It's actually very beautiful. I'm keeping it.
textes.Quand elle a perdu toutes ses gouttes, j: When she lost all her drops, I laughed and said it was never-ending. She looked so sad that, that evening, I left an empty bottle at her door, with a label: “For the next ones.” She's kept it on her windowsill, still empty. She says it's lucky that way.
textes.Quand elle a été nommée à la Guilde, ell: When she was appointed to the Guild, she wore an old grey dress that was too big, with ink stamps all over it. I took her measurements by eye while she told me about her day. I spent the whole winter sewing her uniform. I told her I'd bought it. She believes me. She always believes what's neatly arranged.
textes.Quand elle a été élue présidente, je lui: When she was elected president, I gave her a recording of the Singer, with a note: “She congratulates you.” She asked me how I knew. I said: “Three low notes, one high.” It was a slight exaggeration. But the Singer really did sound pleased.
textes.Quand elle avait cinq ans, je lui ai don: When she was five, I gave her a candle lit at the Ember Heart, promising her she would never be cold. Years later, when she'd become Archduchess, she took me to her room to show it to me. The candle was still burning. I said nothing. I didn't know a candle could last so long.
textes.Quand elle avait six ans, Morgane venait: When she was six, Morgane would come and listen to me tell of her ancestor, Captain Katell Kerhervé, standing at the helm in the storm. One evening she climbed onto a tavern table, grabbed a broom like a tiller and shouted: “Heave to!” She knocked over Fañch's soup. She doesn't remember. I do.
textes.Quand elle est arrivée, à seize ans, je: When she arrived, at sixteen, I asked her to tidy one drawer. Just one. In a week, she had filed the whole Guild, my old trophies and my socks. I found a sword I thought I'd lost ten years ago. It was filed under “Sharp objects, Hugues, sentimental”. I cried.
textes.Quand elle est descendue voir le Petit P: When she came down to see the Little Diver, she told me: “You fly upside down.” I wrote it on the hull in felt-tip. Yolande wiped it off. I wrote it again. Héloïse sent me a pot of red paint so it would stick. Yolande sighed. It stuck.
textes.Quand elle est descendue, elle a comparé: When she came down, she compared her map with the real Fronde, for an hour, whispering “oh” at every mistake. At the end, she said: “Yours isn't as good as mine.” She was joking. I think.
textes.Quand elle m'a confié sa classe, elle m': When she handed me her class, she also gave me her old lantern, the one from her parents' ship. It has neither wick nor oil: you put your own light in it. I've never lit it. I'm waiting until I have something important enough to light up.
textes.Quand elle m'a raccompagné à la porte, e: When she showed me to the door, she didn't touch me, she didn't shout. She simply walked beside me, very slowly, talking about the weather. I've never been so scared in my life. When we reached the door, she said: “Good day, Monsieur Prosper.” I ran all the way to the agency. My moustache had come uncurled.
textes.Quand elle redescend pour le dernier mor: When she comes back down for the last song, she stands in front of me, not in front of her parents. She closes her eyes on my note. On the third beat. Always on the third beat.
textes.Quand elle s'entoure d'un bouclier d'épi: When she wraps herself in a shield of thorns, wake the three roses of light. Their light burns her!
textes.Quand elle tape sur mon tambour, je lui: When she bangs on my drum, I tell her about her dad. Cerfeuil burnt every single loaf, I tell her, and he laughed louder than the oven. She asks: “Louder than you?” I say yes. She plays one boom, to see. It was a very big boom.
textes.Quand elle était bébé, je la couchais da: When she was a baby, I'd lay her in my seaweed basket while I wove. One day, I found her wrapped up in my week's work, thread around her fingers. She'd undone three days of weaving, and she was laughing. I kept the tangled bit: it's her first drawing.
textes.Quand elle était petite, Aube la couchai: When she was little, Aube used to put her to bed in a basket at the foot of the smallest stone. One night, the basket was empty. The whole Circle searched for her. I found her asleep on the altar, arms spread wide, smiling. Aube said: “The stones have chosen her.” Ysolde says her feet were just cold.
textes.Quand elle était toute petite, Plumette: When she was tiny, Plumette slept in my mailbag, between the letters. I made my rounds with her on my tummy. People took their post and gave her a hazelnut. One day I nearly delivered her to Mother Moon's with a postcard. She was snoring. Mother Moon said: “I'll keep this one.” Hoo, I got such a fright.
textes.Quand il a fabriqué sa nouvelle barque,: When he built his new boat, I blessed it with river water, in the name of Rê. Since then, he catches twice as many fish. He says it's thanks to his new nets. I say it's Rê. He still brings me the finest perch at every feast. A fisherman's caution.
textes.Quand il a fallu fermer la Ligne pour tr: When the Line had to close for three years, I was the one who signed. I thought of all the families split in two, between up here and down there. We sent the letters by airship, with Captain Zéphyrine. Three years of mail. She was never once late. She says she beat the post office.
textes.Quand il a fallu monter l'antenne en hau: When the aerial had to go up the mast, Fusible got stuck on the second rung. I took the mic and commentated his climb live, like a race: “He's climbing… he's hesitating… he's not climbing!” A thousand listeners cheered him on. He didn't climb. Bardane did. He still got a standing ovation.
textes.Quand il a perdu son engrenage, j'ai fai: When he lost his gear, I did a sum: gear gone, plus Gonzague seeing something golden near the crane. Result: you have to look in the harbour. I also made him a drawing of his engine, with a heart on it. He pinned it up on his stall. He doesn't know why the heart. I do: it's for courage.
textes.Quand il a peur, il fait les cent pas su: When he's scared, he paces the deck. At night. All night. The wood creaks. I grind my teeth. One evening I took an iron bar. Bent it with one hand, in front of him. For no reason. He stopped pacing. He sat down. Hm. It lasted one night.
textes.Quand il avait cinq ans, juste après l'h: When he was five, just after the winter of fevers, Pierrick used to come and sit on the infirmary doorstep without a word, and hold out shells to me. I didn't know what to do with them, so I kept them. The jar is still on the shelf, behind the honey. He doesn't remember.
textes.Quand il avait huit ans, son père venait: When he was eight, his father used to come and count the crates on the quay. Little Aldric helped me carry the oranges, one by one, laughing very loudly. One evening, I gave him a toffee. He kept it in his hand all the way to the end of the quay, to show his father. His father said: “That's not profitable.”
textes.Quand il chante sur la place, je sonne M: When he sings on the square, I ring Marguerite at just the right moment. Always at the same spot in the chorus. He thinks it's to annoy him. It's for the big beat. One day, I forgot to ring, because my shoulder hurt. He stopped dead and looked at me, worried. He said: “Are you all right, Mélusine?” I knew it: we're a duo.
textes.Quand il est content, Paulo vient chante: When he's happy, Paulo comes and sings in front of my window. Opera, in Italian, at seven in the morning, in his chef's hat. The customers queue in rhythm. Nina claps. I give him a croissant to make him stop. He knows it. He sings more and more often.
textes.Quand il est parti pour sa grande traver: When he left on his great crossing, I was the one who followed him longest through the spyglass, until he was just a dot on the moor. When he came back, two months later, I saw him first, and rang the bell once for him. He never knew. That doesn't give him the right to put question marks.
textes.Quand il est revenu de sa grande travers: When he came back from his great crossing, with his twelve journals and his blisters, he came to see me before he even hugged his mother. He told me: “Corentin, at the foot of Stoneheart, there's a door. Your story is true.” It's the only time in my life I've been offended that someone believed me.
textes.Quand il est revenu, le crâne rouge comm: When he came back, his scalp red as an ember, throat dry, I was sitting outside the Fondouk. I held out a date. Just one. He looked at it. He took it. He ate it. He said nothing. Neither did I. In the desert, you give drink even to the man you've led astray. I had no water. I had a date.
textes.Quand il est venu en mer avec moi, il a: When he came out to sea with me, he was sick at the first wave. Bigorneau stole his bread. Albertine landed on his shoulder and stayed there the whole time, to reassure him. She only does that with me, usually. I understood she'd seen something in him. A brave man. She's never wrong.
textes.Quand il m'a commandé vingt épées pour l: When he ordered twenty swords for the guard, he gave me an eight-page specification. Length, weight, balance, colour of the grip. I read the first page and asked: “How do you really want them?” He thought for a long time. He said: “Pointy.” I burst out laughing. He smiled. It was the first time I'd seen him smile.
textes.Quand il me l'a rendue, il y avait une p: When he gave it back, there was a feather sewn to the collar. A jay feather, blue as a lantern. “The interest,” he said. I told him I was still cross. But I kept the feather. It's still there, look. Don't tell him I smooth it every evening.
textes.Quand il n'y a pas de batteur, c'est moi: When there's no drummer, I play. Every evening someone else volunteers, and every evening it's a disaster. Once, it was Boulon. Another time, one of Chaussette's dogs. The dog was the best.
textes.Quand il n'y a pas de vent, le moulin ne: When there's no wind, the mill doesn't turn. So I blow on it. It does nothing. But Gaubert finds it funny, and the turnips get scared. That's two good reasons.
textes.Quand il oublie de payer, il m'écrit un: When he forgets to pay, he writes me a poem on a potsherd. I have a whole jar full. “O Mérit, your beer is a river…”, “O Mérit, your bread is a sun…” He only changes the ending. I can't read, but Nebet reads them to me in the evening. I pretend not to like them. I love them.
textes.Quand il passe la nuit à l'observatoire,: When he spends the night at the observatory, I bring him up a honey flatbread around midnight. He says honey gives him good eyes. I think mostly he's hungry. One night, he showed me Venus. I showed him a bee asleep on the railing. Each to his own stars.
textes.Quand il pleut, le bras de Wilfried le g: When it rains, Wilfried's arm itches. I send him graphite ointment, via Léonce, in a little jar with a label: “For the arm.” Nothing else. He sends the jar back empty, washed, with a nut inside. I don't know what the nut means. I keep them all in a drawer. I have nineteen.
When it rains, Dad's arm itches. He scratches with his other hand, but he can't reach round the back. So I'm the one who scratches, with a toothbrush. He goes “aaah”. Boulon goes “aaah” too, but nobody's even scratching him. Mum sends ointment. I think the toothbrush works better.
textes.Quand il rabote, papa siffle. Mais faux: When he's planing, dad whistles. But out of tune! So out of tune the seagulls fly away. Mum says he's always whistled like that, and that's why she married him: a man who whistles that badly can't lie. I whistle like him. Same. It runs in the family.
textes.Quand il raconte l'histoire de la graine: When he tells the story of the lost golden seed, Faelar always says: “The sea took it.” Then he looks at me, one second too long. I think he knows. He's never asked me anything. That's his way of being kind.
textes.Quand il rentre du village, Léon m'appor: When he comes back from the village, Léon brings me herbal tea, verbena from the hills across the water, in a paper cone. He sets it on my bench without a word and goes back to his boat. I've never asked him for anything. I drink it all, one cup a night, at nine o'clock exactly.
textes.Quand il vient au Perroquet et qu'il se: When he comes to the Perroquet and starts humming, I turn up the volume. A bit, then a lot. He sings louder, I play louder. In the end, Toni asks us to stop, the glasses are rattling on the shelves. The mayor shakes my hand: “What a duo!” I say nothing.
textes.Quand il écrit mes lettres pour Tilleul,: When he writes my letters to Tilleul, Ewen doesn't write what I say. I say “a big wave”, he writes “a wave as tall as the mainmast, with a shark in it”. Tilleul wrote back that it was my finest letter. Since then, I dictate and Ewen improves. There are two storytellers now.
textes.Quand il était élève, je venais raconter: When he was a pupil, I used to come and tell stories at the Academy on Thursdays. Little Malachar raised his hand every two sentences: “That's the wrong date!” One day, I said to him: “Go on, you tell the rest.” He told it, with the right dates. The whole class fell asleep. He never interrupted me again. For a week.
textes.Quand ils ont perdu le cochonnet, il est: When they lost the jack, he came to sulk three days running. Three coffees not drunk. On the third day, Marcel came to sulk at the next table. They sat back to back. I put a single sugar lump between the two tables. They squabbled over the sugar. The next day, they were playing again with a pebble.
textes.Quand j'ai cassé la porte de Sylwen avec: When I broke Sylwen's door with my arrows, I went to say sorry with a drawing. Sylwen looked at the hole in the wood, then at the drawing, then at the hole. She said: “Well, now the oven will get some air.” And she gave me a honey bun. I think she's a bit magic.
textes.Quand j'ai commandé mon armure, je suis: When I ordered my armour, I came back every day for a month, supposedly to check the measurements. On the last day, Ferronde said to me: “Captain, the armour's been finished for three weeks. What exactly are you checking?” I turned bright red. Redder than usual. She said yes before I dared ask the question.
textes.Quand j'ai câblé la radio du Sergent, il: When I wired the Sergeant's radio, the antenna had to go up at the top of the Rusty Whale's mast. I got stuck on the second rung. The Sergeant looked at me, then grabbed the mic and gave a live commentary of my climb. “He's going up… he's not going up…” Bardane put it up in the end.
textes.Quand j'ai débridé ma planche, elle m'a: When I souped up my board, she told me off for ten minutes. Then she spent the night reinforcing the wheels. In the morning, she said: “If you have to go fast, go fast safely.” And she gave me a helmet painted with flames.
textes.Quand j'ai eu mes quinze ans, je lui ai: When I turned fifteen, I asked him which colour to choose. He said: “The one that makes noise.” I chose copper red. He laughed so hard the brazier flared up.
textes.Quand j'ai fait la queue de Brindezingue: When I made Brindezingue's tail out of organ pipes, Clou blew into it. The dragon went “oooooh”, deep and soft. I shouted: “It sings!” We spent an hour making the dragon sing, taking turns. Clou didn't say a word. But he was laughing. I saw it.
textes.Quand j'ai fait ma nouvelle barque, elle: When I made my new boat, she blessed it with river water, in the name of Rê. Since then, I catch twice as many fish. Because of my new nets, obviously. But I bring her the finest perch at every feast. You never know. Maybe Rê likes perch.
textes.Quand j'ai fait mon tour en Zéphyr, j'ai: When I had my ride in the Zéphyr, I spat out of the window. Just a bit, to see how long it takes to fall. And when we landed, the commander was waiting for me at the bottom of the gangway, binoculars round her neck. She said: “Nice spit. Very long.” I knew straight away I was done for.
textes.Quand j'ai fini la Zahra, Ahmed a dit :: When I finished the Zahra, Ahmed said: “One more coat.” I put on the second. “One more.” I put on the third. He wanted a fourth, so I hid the pot. Same pot for every boat in the port, I swear. But for Ahmed, the Zahra's blue is a different blue. I let him believe it. Faith costs nothing.
textes.Quand j'ai fini les sept, on boit le thé: When I've finished all seven, we drink tea on the battlements, him and me. He doesn't talk, I can't hear well: it's very restful. Once, the seagull from the third cannon flew over us with her chick. The caïd smiled. Once. I saw it. He said it was the sun. Tac.
textes.Quand j'ai lâché une barre rouge sur ma: When I dropped a red-hot bar on my boot, I didn't cry out, to look tough. That evening, Brunna took my melted boot without a word. The next day, she gave me a new one, with an iron toecap. She said: “There. Now you can mess up in peace.” I've been messing up in peace ever since.
textes.Quand j'ai nommé Hugues maître de la Gui: When I appointed Hugues master of the Guild, I arrived in my nightshirt. Aurore had woken me too late. I was wearing my Monday hat, shaped like a cabbage. Hugues cried through my whole speech. I thought it was because of the cabbage. He told me it wasn't. I still think it was a little bit the cabbage.
textes.Quand j'ai perdu ma voix, Églantine a cr: When I lost my voice, Églantine shouted my announcements for me. She speaks so softly that only the pigeons heard her. But she did it three days in a row, standing on my crate, with my hood on her head. Nobody had ever seen her do anything so against the rules.
textes.Quand j'ai pris la garde, la mèche du ph: When I took command of the guard, the red lighthouse's wick smoked like a grill. Si Larbi climbed up to the Skala without a word. He showed me how to trim the wick at an angle and soak it in cold oil. No more smoke. He went back down the hundred steps without stopping. I stop at the fiftieth.
textes.Quand j'ai pris la tête de la Grande For: When I took charge of the Great Forge, we installed the new steam hammer. I named it Grand-Mère, in honour of mine. It strikes slowly, very hard, and it's never wrong. The day I learned Mathilde had named hers Mamie, I laughed for an hour. Great minds forge alike.
textes.Quand j'ai pris ma retraite de la cantin: When I retired from the canteen, everyone thought I'd take it easy. I took my ladle, my pot and my apron, and I crossed the Frondeurs' Bridge. Brasero was waiting on the other side. He said: “At last, we're going to eat.” I answered: “At last, I'll cook for people who have time to say thank you.”
textes.Quand j'ai raconté que j'avais dansé ave: When I told how I'd danced with a mermaid, he asked if she danced well. I said: “Badly. She had no feet.” He looked at me for a long time, then said it was the only logical story I'd ever told. Since then, he keeps asking for it. I tell it to him. I change one detail every time. He's never noticed.
textes.Quand j'ai repris l'Atelier, j'ai trouvé: When I took over the Workshop, I found the plans for the Levitators on the wall, drawn by Séraphin himself, with a tea stain in the corner. I spent a whole night looking at them. By morning, I'd understood one thing: he'd botched loads of things before he got it right, too. There are forty-three crossings-out. I counted them.
textes.Quand j'ai repris la forge, j'ai install: When I took over the forge, I installed three steam hammers. Pif, Paf, and the biggest one, Granny, in honour of my grandmother. She hammered so hard you could hear her at the Harbour. The day Granny the hammer struck her first blow, every cup in the Lower Town jumped. I laughed for an hour.
textes.Quand j'ai reçu mon bouclier de garde, j: When I got my guard's shield, I went up to the terrace to show Dwalin. He held it for one minute. He handed it back black with soot, with all ten of his fingers on it. I scrubbed all night. The next day, I lent it to him for the Forge Festival. He gave it back without a mark.
textes.Quand j'ai ri au Conseil et que les Bull: When I laughed at the Council and the Bubbles went out, everyone was scared in the dark. Except the Elder. She was laughing even harder than me. When the light came back, she said: “You should laugh more often, Volt.” I answered: “Not without warning.”
textes.Quand j'ai sauté, mon père a crié mon no: When I jumped, my father shouted my name. I didn't turn around, {surnom}. Not once. I never said goodbye to him. Driss looks so much like him that I go out to sea with him to pretend. One day, I'd like to go back to my island. But ten years is a long time. I'm afraid he'll look at me and not recognise me.
textes.Quand j'ai très peur, je prie à voix hau: When I'm very scared, I pray out loud. Very loud. Mélusine once told me I had a town crier's voice. I was so proud I tripped.
textes.Quand j'ai été élue présidente, il m'a o: When I was elected president, he gave me a recording of the Great Singer, with a note: “She congratulates you.” I asked him how he knew. He said: “Three low notes, one high.” I still listen to it, on evenings after a difficult Council.
textes.Quand j'arrive au bout de la lune qui ne: When I reach the end of the moon that wouldn't go to bed, the other little ones are asleep, and Gland asks: “And then?” So I say: “Then… twice upon a time.” And I start something else. He looks at me with his eyes round as hazelnuts. One day, he'll ask me the question differently.
textes.Quand j'arrive à la criée avec mes caiss: When I arrive at the auction with my crates, Saïd drops the price at once and shouts: “FOR HAMID, IT'S CHEAPER, THEY HEARD HIS SONG!” The whole auction laughs. The next day, I sang as I came into port, so loud that for a whole minute nobody heard his prices.
textes.Quand j'aurai appris les six sorts des m: When I've learnt the six spells of the masters of Arcanelle, the archmage will lead me to the Moonstone Circle for the ceremony.
textes.Quand j'aurai quinze ans, je choisirai l: When I'm fifteen, I'll choose green, like Bielle. Or orange, like Brasero. Or both. I'll ask the Assembly.
textes.Quand j'avais cinq ans, il m'a donné une: When I was five, he gave me a candle lit at the Heart-Brazier, promising me I'd never be cold. It still burns in my bedroom. One day, I asked him how it lasted so long. He smiled: “Because you look at it.” I look at it every night.
textes.Quand j'avais cinq ans, ma mère m'a donn: When I was five, my mother gave me a lettuce seed and a pot. “It will grow if you give it light and kind words.” I put the pot under my bedside lamp and talked to it every evening. It grew. My mother said it was the lamp. I knew it was the words. We were both right.
textes.Quand j'avais cinq ans, sur l'étal de ma: When I was five, on mum's stall, there was a sea bream. It looked at me. In the eyes. For ages. So I swore: no more fish, ever. Except mum's tajine, because that doesn't count, it's mum. And Mustapha's sardines, because they're not fish, they're seabirds. He told me so. I believe him. Almost.
textes.Quand j'avais douze ans, mon père travai: When I was twelve, my father was working in an old gallery. He heard the rock crack. A tiny little moan. He whistled everyone out. They all went back up, laughing, saying he was overdoing it. A minute later, the gallery caved in. Nobody was inside. That evening, my father told me: “The rock talks. You just have to listen.”
textes.Quand j'avais huit ans, j'ai fait une fu: When I was eight, I made a rocket out of a stovepipe. It didn't take off. But it made a huge cloud of smoke, all black, over the whole square! You couldn't even see the big clock! Dad and Mum came running. Together. Dad still had his wrench, and Mum her rubber gloves.
textes.Quand j'avais huit ans, une dame docker: When I was eight, a lady docker let me carry oranges with her on the quay. She laughed loudly. She gave me a toffee. I kept it in my hand all the way to the end of the quay to show my father. He said it wasn't profitable. That lady was Barricade. I recognised her thirty years later. By the studs.
textes.Quand j'avais quatre ans, mon papa m'a e: When I was four, my dad took me to the foot of the Air Chimney. He told me to put my hand on the grate. I felt cold air coming down, ever so gently. He said: “That's a little piece of wind. It comes from the sky.” I kept my hand closed for the rest of the day, so I wouldn't lose it. In the evening, I opened it. It was gone. Dad said: “It's gone back up to tell the others.”
