textes.Quand j'avais sept ans, un voyageur m'a: When I was seven, a traveller gave me a postcard of Hautefond: Column Square, under a big blue sky, with white clouds. I looked at it every evening for years. I thought the clouds were painted on. When my mother told me they were real, and that they moved, I didn't sleep a wink all night.
textes.Quand j'avais six ans, Maman m'a fait un: When I was six, Mum made me a wooden sword. I called it Thunder. I defeated every post in the Lower Town, the inn's barrel and a chicken. Well, the chicken chased me all the way to the washhouse. But I didn't surrender. I jumped into the washhouse. It was a strategy.
textes.Quand j'avais six ans, je m'étais cachée: When I was six, I hid in the throne room chandelier to escape a ceremony. Asmodin came in, sniffed the air and said: “Singed lace. Good evening, Highness.” He got me down with a ladder and a tray of biscuits. I think he'd prepared the biscuits before coming up.
textes.Quand j'avais six ans, ma mère m'a emmen: When I was six, my mother took me up to Hautefond to see the real sun. I stepped out of the pavilion, looked up, and cried. It hurt. Everything was too big, too white, too hot. My mother took me back down. I ran to the Gardens, sat down among the mushrooms, and felt at home.
textes.Quand j'étais apprenti, Asmodin a été mo: When I was an apprentice, Asmodin was my first client. I was shaking so much it took me an hour to polish his horns. He didn't say a word. Then he looked at himself in the mirror and said: “Acceptable.” I burst into tears. He thought I was ill and had a doctor sent for. I never dared tell him it was joy.
textes.Quand j'étais au lit chez Mère Sauge, Zé: When I was in bed at Mother Sage's, Zéphyrine came every day. She told me about the wind outside, where it came from, what it had seen. She looked sad, I don't know why. She'd say: “I should have been there.” I told her it wasn't her fault, it was the bedsheet's.
textes.Quand j'étais bébé, Maman me posait dans: When I was a baby, Mum put me in a basket between the ash pepper and the fire cinnamon. I sneezed all day, and customers bought pepper to make me laugh. Mum says it's thanks to me she sold so much. I say she owes me money.
textes.Quand j'étais bébé, je dormais dans un p: When I was a baby, I slept in a bread basket, next to the oven. Mum says I smelled of brioche. I don't remember, I was too little. For my third birthday, Grandpa Raymond gave me a wooden pétanque ball, all for me. He carved an N on it with his bread knife. N for Nina!
textes.Quand j'étais jeune, des pirates sont dé: When I was young, pirates came here once before. They left poorer than they arrived: we'd sold them sand for salt.
textes.Quand j'étais jeune, un grand gaillard r: When I was young, a big red-haired lad came down from Hautefond to learn smithing in our first forge. A Soufflet. He hammered hard and laughed even harder. He taught us to laugh while we worked; we taught him to strike true. On the day the Line reopened, I heard a laugh come down the Column, all the way here. The same one. Ysaé told me it was his granddaughter, Mathilde, the blacksmith up top. I had to sit down.
textes.Quand j'étais là-bas… enfin, on m'a raco: When I was down there… I mean, so I've been told.
textes.Quand j'étais petit, Maman m'a fabriqué: When I was little, Mum made me a wooden sword. I called it Thunder. I defeated every post in the Lower Town. And a chicken. Well, the chicken defeated me. But I fought well.
textes.Quand j'étais petit, Nono s'asseyait à c: When I was little, Nono used to sit next to me while I banged on my coconuts. He counted with his feet: “One, two, and three — you feel that one in your belly.” He's where the shell story comes from, the one Bastien tells everywhere. Nono never lies. He rounds up.
textes.Quand j'étais petit, Philomène me gardai: When I was little, Philomène looked after me in the afternoons. She read me legends so I'd do my homework. I'd fall asleep in the middle. She'd wake me with a nudge of her elbow and pick up the story exactly where I'd dozed off. Even today, when she tells stories on the square, I recognise certain sentences. I fall asleep again at the same one.
textes.Quand j'étais petit, il n'y avait qu'un: When I was little, there was only one tree with people in it: the Mother Oak. Then the families grew, and bridges sprouted from one tree to the next. Like branches. That's what Ramure means: all the branches of a tree.
textes.Quand j'étais petit, j'avais peur de l'o: When I was little, I was scared of thunderstorms. Mum took me into the forge, at night, and she struck the anvil at the same time as the thunder. Clang! Boom! Clang! Boom! By the end, I was laughing. Since then, when there's a storm, I think of Mum striking the anvil. I've never been scared again. Well, almost never.
textes.Quand j'étais petit, je bégayais. Pour d: When I was little, I stammered. To say “hello”, I needed three breaths. So I practised all on my own, in front of Lady Ysolde's fountain. I gave her speeches. She never laughed at me. Even today, she's my favourite audience.
textes.Quand j'étais petit, je tapais sur tout: When I was little, I banged on everything with spoons: saucepans, tables, the stairs. My father called it “non-compliant use of cutlery”. They took the spoons away. So I tapped with my fingers. You can't take fingers away. I checked.
textes.Quand j'étais petit, la Fronde était enc: When I was little, the Fronde was still full of old boilers not yet turned into houses. I spent my days banging on them with two sticks. One went “dong,” one went “bam,” one went “chiii.” My father, Brasero, said: “This boy will make noise his whole life.” He meant it kindly. I think.
textes.Quand j'étais petit, maman me donnait un: When I was little, Mum gave me a coin per sea urchin. I'd dive under the quay, come up with my hands full of spines, and she'd sell them that same morning, “caught by my son”. Tourists thought it was cute and paid double. That was my first job. I still hate the smell of fish. But sea urchins are fine.
textes.Quand j'étais petit, mon grand-père me m: When I was little, my grandad carried me up to the crow's nest on his back. We'd stay up there for hours, and he'd make me count the waves up to a thousand. I always fell asleep around three hundred. He said it didn't matter, that he'd count the rest for me. I don't know if he really did.
textes.Quand j'étais petit, mon père m'emmenait: When I was little, my father took me down once a month, by the Column. We went to see the sea. He'd pick up a shell, give it to me, and say: “Never forget where we come from.” I kept the last one. I gave it to Lili. It still works. You can hear the sea.

When I was little, my father took me to the quays of the Old Dock to count crates. A lady docker helped me carry the oranges. She gave me a toffee. I… I don't know why I'm telling you this. It's not profitable.
textes.Quand j'étais petite, Faelar nous racont: When I was little, Faelar used to tell us about the seeds of the Mother Tree, sown on every island. One evening, he fell asleep just before the end: the one about the humans' tree. He slept a whole spring. I couldn't wait. At a hundred, I asked the council to become its guardian. Nobody else wanted to cross the mist.
textes.Quand j'étais petite, il n'y avait pas d: When I was little, there was no Guild in Montjoie, just a big barn in the Lower Town where the adventurers came back in the evening. I used to hide behind the hay bales to listen to their stories. One evening, an old knight spotted me. He said: “Come to the front, little one. Stories are for listening to up close.”
textes.Quand j'étais petite, j'ai trouvé un bou: When I was little, I found a bent bolt at the edge of the Chasm. Everyone had stepped over it. I picked it up, looked at it very closely, and saw it was shaped like a heart. I wore it round my neck for ten years. That's how it all began.
textes.Quand j'étais petite, j'ai voulu tisser: When I was little, I wanted to weave like Mum. I sat down at her loom, and at the end, I was inside it! My sleeve was woven in with the thread! I sang while I waited for her to come back. It took her an hour to undo me, and she was laughing so much she kept picking the wrong thread. I was a dress. A singing dress.
textes.Quand j'étais petite, j'avais peur du no: When I was little, I was afraid of the dark. I only ever told one person: Rosalie, at the market. She never told a soul. Today, I'm a lighthouse keeper. I light up the night every evening. I think it's my way of answering it.
When I was little, I took everything apart. Toys, lamps, my mother's radio. I didn't know how to put things back together. My mother cried a bit. One day Brasero told me: “Taking apart is half the way. The other half, we'll do together.” Since then, I put everything back together. Almost.
textes.Quand j'étais petite, je me suis endormi: When I was little, I fell asleep in his archives. I woke up while he was reading the history of the surface out loud, to the shelves, because nobody else listens to him. I listened right to the end without moving. He only found out when I sneezed, right on the word “wheat”.
textes.Quand j'étais petite, mes parents releva: When I was little, my parents used to haul up the fish traps in the Pool. They'd bring up shiny blue fish that were a bit scary. Me, I wanted to know what they tasted like. One evening, I cooked one, all by myself, with lemon from the Lamp Orchard. My mother tasted it. She said: “The sea has a thousand flavours, my girl. You've just found one.” I've spent my life looking for the other nine hundred and ninety-nine.
textes.Quand j'étais petite, mon grand-père Sév: When I was little, my grandfather Séverin showed me a feather on the Esplanade. He blew on it, and it flew off over the balustrade. “That's how it all began,” he told me. I ran to the edge to catch it. He held me back by the collar. It's the only time I ever saw him afraid.
textes.Quand j'étais petite, papi Nono passait: When I was little, Grandpa Nono came by Mum's shed once a year, with odd presents: a dwarf pebble that smelled of sulphur, a shell that played music. He'd dance with me standing on his feet, between the rolls of canvas. He smelled of the sea and of travelling. He still smells the same.
textes.Quand j'étais petite, plus petite, je me: When I was little, littler, I hid in Abyssos's archives to play, and I fell asleep between two scrolls. I woke up while he was reading the history of the surface out loud, to the shelves. Wheat, the sun, birds… Ever since that day, I want to know everything. It's his fault.
textes.Quand j'étais toute petite, j'ai pleuré: When I was tiny, I cried on the queen's lap because I couldn't light up. She told me: “You make the others glow, Lumi.” The next day, she gave me the fireflies. All of them! I dropped half of them from surprise. They came back.
textes.Quand j'étais élève, Ébène était déjà vi: When I was a pupil, Ébène was already old. He'd come and tell stories at the Academy on Thursdays, and I'd put my hand up every two sentences to point out a mistake. One Thursday, he stopped: “Little Malachar, go on, tell the rest.” I tried. The whole class fell asleep. He still calls me “little Malachar”.
textes.Quand je change de pellicule, Nono me ra: When I change film, Nono tells me about the parties of the old days. The ball on his father's boat, the lanterns in the dwarves' mine. He always describes the lights to me, never the music. I think he tells me so that I'll photograph them one day. I write it all down in a notebook.
textes.Quand je dors, deux heures par nuit, c'e: When I sleep, two hours a night, Tchoum minds the decks. He doesn't change anything, doesn't touch anything, he just nods. One morning, I found a little note under the turntable: “Bass +1.” It's the longest letter he's ever written me. I keep it in my cap.
textes.Quand je fais mon numéro sur le pont, c': When I do my act on deck, the Silent One sets up the target, a board as big as a door, and brings me back the knives one by one, as proud as a dog fetching a stick. Then he counts the holes with his fingertip, as if he didn't believe me. Seven knives, one single hole. He believes me.
textes.Quand je fais une alerte à la tyrolienne: When I do an alert on the zip line, Mochi runs to tell Pomme-de-Pin. Every time! “Gland did an alert!” Pomme-de-Pin says: “I know, I heard it.” The whole village heard it. That's the whole point of an alert! Mochi doesn't get alerts at all.
textes.Quand je joue de la flûte-colibri, Tlaco: When I play the hummingbird flute, Tlaco, his dog, starts howling. Not a sad howl: he's singing! He follows the notes, almost in tune. Pilli says he's a musical dog. Now, at every festival, I play a tune for Tlaco. He sings, Pilli dances, and everyone claps. It's our act.
textes.Quand je joue toute la nuit, Sylwen me l: When I play all night, Sylwen leaves me a honey loaf on the harp bench before dawn. It's always still warm. I've never understood how she knows what time I'll stop. She says the oven knows.
textes.Quand je l'ai engagé, Nox ne m'a dit que: When I hired him, Nox only said three words to me: “I like night.” I gave him a pole, a bag of wicks and the list of street lamps. The next day, every lamp had a name, written in chalk on its base. The market one is called Gustave. The fountain one is called Mélodie. I didn't rub anything out.
textes.Quand je l'aurai vécue. Viens l'écouter,: When I've lived it. Come and listen, that evening.
textes.Quand je le dirai, Gouverneur. Pousse-to: When I say so, Governor. Out of my light.
textes.Quand je le dirai. Comme la semaine dern: When I say so. Same as last week.
textes.Quand je lui ai demandé des ressorts pou: When I asked her for springs for my shoes, like in Cliquetis, she put down her hammer, looked at me for a long time, and said: “No.” Just “No.” Then she went and told Pépin. Pépin said “cheating”. That got me two noes for the price of one.
textes.Quand je lui ai enfin rendu sa cape, j'a: When I finally gave her cloak back, I'd sewn a feather to the collar. A jay feather, blue as a moon lantern. “Interest,” I said. She said she was still cross. But the feather's still there, my friend. I check every evening, at the Circle, walking behind her moss.
textes.Quand je lui ai parlé des signes gravés: When I told him about the signs carved under the keel, Tobias put down his hammer. He said: “My grandfather used to say the ship didn't run aground. That it landed.” Then he picked his hammer back up, and never spoke of it again. I've never dared ask him again.
textes.Quand je lui apporte un beau rubis et qu: When I bring him a fine ruby and can't remember where I found it, Orsik asks me three times. Three times, I say I don't remember. It's true. He doesn't believe me. Since then, he follows me from a distance when I go down. He always gets lost before I do.
textes.Quand je lui fais un discours, elle m'éc: When I make her a speech, she listens to the end. Well, until she says “no”. Nobody else listens to me that long. Once, she said “no” after twenty-two minutes. That's her record. I noted it. I think she enjoys my speeches. In silence.
textes.Quand je lui parle des six sacs de grain: When I mention the six sacks of seeds from the winter he was ill, Gaubert smiles. Always. A little sideways smile. I've asked him a hundred times if he knew who it was. He says: “How would I know? I was in bed.” Then he looks towards the Great Square. Always towards the Great Square. I'll find out in the end. And that day, I'm catching him in the net.
textes.Quand je lui prends des pommes, je ne pa: When I take apples from her, I never pay in coins, never! I put a singing-stone on her counter. She sighs, she sets it aside, she says she'll sell it. She's never sold one. She has a whole box of them, my friend: when the wind blows through, her house sings. Heh heh! A tanuki, deep down.
textes.Quand je me brûle vraiment, je cache ma: When I really burn myself, I hide my hand behind my back and say: “It's nothing.” Mother Sage says she can smell me singeing from the garden gate. She takes my hand and blows on it, very gently, like on soup. After that, it's fine. I don't know if it's the spell or the breath.
textes.Quand je me suis présentée à la mairie,: When I ran for mayor, nobody knew me. Zéro swept in front of my poster every single day. People thought: if Zéro likes that poster, it must be a good poster. I won by four votes.
textes.Quand je monte dans sa nacelle, je racon: When I ride in his basket, I tell the passengers the story of the basket: my father Frêne, the four willow rods, the six ropes… When they get to the top, the passengers ask for another ride to hear the rest. Bourru sighs. A bear's sigh makes the pulley shake. I don't see why he sighs: I'm drumming up business for him.
textes.Quand je monte ma caisse de coquillages: When I carry my crate of shells up the Cod's gangplank, he takes it with his good hand, without a word, and sets it on the deck. I say thank you, he says “Hm”. I count “Hm” as a word. He doesn't object. Once, I heard him humming my helm song. Very quietly. He doesn't know I heard him.
textes.Quand je pars en mer, à l'aube, je regar: When I head out to sea at dawn, I look up at the galleon's crow's nest. Gaspard is already up there. He raises his arm, once. That means: “I'm watching for you.” And when he sees something, the Admiral squawks “WHALE!” across the whole harbour. I taught him that word. The only one I taught him. The most important one.
textes.Quand je passe devant Chez Paulo, mainte: When I walk past Chez Paulo now, I sing louder. Apparently it puts heart into his soup. So I sing sad songs, so it cries a bit. The other day, he came out with his ladle: “Not that one, Rosalie, it curdles the rouille!” I sang the verse twice.
textes.Quand je passe devant la place, Marcel a: When I walk past the square, Marcel stops his game to shout advice at me. “The mayor's box sticks, tap it on the left!” “You forgot Rita's step!” He hasn't had a satchel for twelve years, but he still does the round with me, from afar, a boule in his hand. Raymond says he uses it as a chance to cheat.
textes.Quand je passe devant le terrain, Marcel: When I run past the pitch, Marcel drops his boules, lifts his knees and jogs on the spot, puffing: “Hop… hop… hop…” Raymond doubles up laughing. So do I. Then he sits back down, out of breath for real, and says: “At least you run without a mailbag.”
textes.Quand je perds contre Marcel, je vais m': When I lose to Marcel, I go and sit on Gisèle's terrace, all alone, and order a coffee. I don't drink it. I watch it go cold. Gisèle brings it without saying a word. She says she knows who won from the way I pull out the chair. I pull it out more gently now. Doesn't work.
textes.Quand je perds des gouttes dans les raci: When I lose drops in the roots, I find them the next day outside my door, in a nutshell. No note, nothing. Once I watched out for him from behind my window. He put down the shell, looked left, looked right, and said “Hmph” all by himself. To nobody.
textes.Quand je rentre avec un maquereau plus b: When I come home with a mackerel finer than the rest, I save it for the Bordée. Gwenola takes it without a word, puts it on the griddle, and serves me the first crêpe. Not the second, not the third: the first. For fifty years. I count that as half a yes.
textes.Quand je reste trop longtemps à l'observ: When I stay too long at the observatory, he climbs up to bring me honey on a flatbread. He says it's good for the eyes. I don't know if it's true. But on the nights he comes up, I see more stars. Or else I stay awake longer. Maybe that's the same thing.
textes.Quand je réfléchis, je marche sur le pon: When I'm thinking, I pace the deck. All night, if need be. The planks creak. Mâchefer, in his hammock, grinds his teeth. It makes quite a concert. One night, he got up, took an iron bar and bent it with one hand, looking at me. “No reason,” he said. I sat down. I think sitting down now. It works very well too.
textes.Quand je serai descendue, je ramasserai: When I've been down, I'll pick up a shell for every person in the City. That's a lot of shells. I've already got a big bag ready. It's empty. For now.
textes.Quand je serai grand, j'aurai un dirigea: When I grow up, I'm going to have a red airship!
textes.Quand je serai grand, je conduirai la ca: When I grow up, I'm going to drive the capsule. And honk at the clouds.
textes.Quand je serai grand, je serai capitaine: When I grow up, I'm going to be an airship captain. Or a cloud. I haven't decided yet.
When I grow up, I'm going to be a captain. Like Zéphyrine. And like Héloïse. Both at the same time.
textes.Quand je serai grand, je serai conseille: When I grow up, I'm going to be a councillor. I'll vote for snack time twice a day.
textes.Quand je serai grand, je serai explorate: When I grow up, I'll be an explorer! I'll go to every island in the archipelago and give a name to every mushroom in the world. Even the ones that don't glow. They have the right to a name too.
When I grow up, I'm going to be an explorer. I'll go all over the Ash Wood and give a name to every glowing mushroom. I've already named forty. That one's Gérard.
textes.Quand je serai grand, je serai guerrier-: When I grow up, I'll be a jaguar warrior like Mixtli. Or a merchant like Tochtli. Or both: I'll capture customers. And Tlaco will have hair. A little. For winter.
textes.Quand je serai grand, je serai joueur de: When I grow up, I'll be a ball player like Chak. Or a hero like Hunahpu. Or a dog.
When I grow up, I'll be a ball player like Chak. Or a hero like Hunahpu. Or a dog. Peek' looks very happy.
textes.Quand je serai grand, je serai liftier c: When I grow up, I'll be a liftkeeper like Théo. Or a cloud. I haven't decided yet.
When I grow up, I'm going to be a liftkeeper. Or an airship. I haven't decided yet.
textes.Quand je serai grand, je serai mineur. O: When I grow up, I'll be a miner. Or a crystal. I haven't decided yet.
textes.Quand je serai grand, je serai pilote de: When I grow up, I'll be a bathyscaphe pilot. Or a whale. I haven't decided yet.
textes.Quand je serai grande, j'aurai des circu: When I grow up, I'll have pink circuits, like her.
textes.Quand je serai grande, j'aurai un dirige: When I grow up, I'm going to have a red airship!
textes.Quand je serai grande, je compterai les: When I grow up, I'm going to count the stars. All of them.
textes.Quand je serai grande, je serai capitain: When I grow up, I'll be captain of a real ship. Not a pirate. A captain. It pays better, and you still get a hat.
When I grow up, I'll be a ship's captain, like Léon. Or an ice-cream maker, like Bruno. Or both.

When I grow up, I'll be a captain. Léon already lets me ring the Swallow's bell, ding ding, and everyone gets on. Or else an ice-cream maker, like Bruno: I've already invented a flavour, strawberry-dolphin! Or both. A boat that sells ice cream. People on the sea get hot too, right?
textes.Quand je serai grande, je serai guérisse: When I grow up, I'll be a healer, like Aurore. Or a zoologist, like Nova. Or a pilot, like Comète. Or all of them at once. I'll have time: I'll live a thousand years. At least.
textes.Quand je serai grande, je serai musicien: When I grow up, I'll be a musician, and a gardener, and a bus captain, and a frog too. Mantra says it's possible if I breathe properly.
textes.Quand je serai grande, je serai prêtress: When I grow up, I'll be a priestess like Néferet! Or a fisherwoman like Khéty! Or both! I'll pray in the morning and fish in the afternoon. And I'll let all the fish go, for Rê.
When I grow up, I'll be a priestess like Néferet. Or a fisherwoman like Khéty. Or a cat. We love cats here. There's even a cat goddess, Bastet!
textes.Quand je serai grande, je serai réceptio: When I grow up, I'll be a receptionist, like Églantine. Because the receptionist knows ALL the adventurers, she knows everything they do, and she has a stamp. A stamp!
textes.Quand je siffle trois fois, c'est l'heur: When I whistle three times, it's time to come home. Tornade always pretends not to hear the first whistle. At the second, he does one more lap. At the third, he comes running. I asked him why. He said: “To be sure you really want me.”
textes.Quand je suis arrivé au Boucan, il n'y a: When I arrived in Boucan, there was no electricity. Just candles. I made wind turbines out of fans on the Spinning Mill roof, salvaged panels from the Scrapyard, and one evening, I plugged it all in. Clack. The whole town lit up. Everyone went “ooooh”. I still do it every evening.
textes.Quand je suis arrivé au Boucan, j'ai tro: When I arrived at Boucan, I found a freighter beached on the shore, empty, with an old radio in the wheelhouse. I turned the knob. There was nothing but static. I said to myself: “This static is waiting for a voice.” I moved in that very evening. Radio Boucan was born the next day. 98.7. Three listeners.
textes.Quand je suis arrivé à Montjoie, Églanti: When I arrived in Montjoie, Églantine asked me my profession. I answered: “Rival.” She nodded and wrote, without smiling: “Rival (awaiting rival)”. The day you arrived, she came to see me, and she crossed out “awaiting”. It's the finest thing anyone has ever done for me.
textes.Quand je suis arrivée au Boucan, Mamie B: When I arrived in Boucan, Mamie Barricade gave me the Cannery's old empty-tin room. I turned it into the Free Shop. The first thing anyone dropped off was a flowery teapot. It left, came back, left again. It's been round the island fourteen times. It always comes back to say hello.
textes.Quand je suis arrivée sur cette île, il: When I arrived on this island, there was nothing but poppies, wind and a yurt full of holes. I planted sunflowers. People came for the sunflowers, and they stayed for the music.
textes.Quand je suis arrivée à Montjoie, j'ai o: When I arrived in Montjoie, I opened a little magic shop to sell my potions. The first customer offered me a “magic” raven feather. I bought it. The second, a “magic” pebble. I bought it. I didn't sell a thing that week. Since then, the shop has been overflowing, and I'm very happy.
textes.Quand je suis arrivée, Néopolis n'exista: When I arrived, Neopolis didn't exist. There was a concrete slab on the sea, and people said they'd build “the city of the future” on it. I said to myself: someone will have to serve tea, in the future.
textes.Quand je suis arrivée, il n'y avait qu'u: When I arrived, there was nothing but a pontoon, the sea, and a big bare concrete slab. The workers were building the first tower. They were cold, they were hungry. I took out my teapot. The first stall of the Night Market was an upturned crate and three cups.
textes.Quand je suis arrivée, il y a quarante a: When I arrived, forty years ago, this gasholder was a steel carcass, grey and empty. My grandmother had left me an old book of fairy tales, with a dried spore between two pages. I laid it on the rust. It grew. Then another one. And there's the cathedral.
textes.Quand je suis arrivée, j'étais si petite: When I arrived, I was so tiny I rolled everywhere. It was Queen Églantine who picked me up, in the hollow of her hand. She taught me to gather moon dew from the roots. She used to say: “A drop that falls is a drop that waters.” I tell myself that every time I fall.
textes.Quand je suis descendu du mât du Fidèle,: When I came down from the Faithful's mast, after two days up there, she looked me up and down. “Did you see the boarding coming?” I said: “No, I was asleep.” She said: “At least you're honest. Back up you go.” I went back up. I never slept at the top of a mast again. Hardly ever.
textes.Quand je suis devenu contremaître, j'ai: When I became foreman, I hung a board in my office: “Days without an accident: 0.” The next day, I wrote 1. Then 2. Today, I'm at four thousand two hundred. Every morning, I write a new number. It's the only thing I write all day. It's my most beautiful poem.
textes.Quand je suis devenue factrice, mon cous: When I became a postwoman, my cousin Zigomar built me a “jet-powered postbag”, to deliver faster. It worked. Too well. It caught fire above the port, and I crossed the Harbour backwards, smoking like a chimney. All the letters arrived. A bit toasted. Since then, I only use my wings.
textes.Quand je suis montée à son échelle, il a: When I climbed his ladder, he hid his axe behind his back, like a child hiding a cake. He offered me some herbal tea, then told me the price, then said it was a joke. I'm still not sure it was.
textes.Quand je suis née, le Grand-Chêne n'avai: When I was born, the Great Oak had just one hut and a rope ladder. My mother hauled the buckets of water up by pulley, my father sawed the planks down below. In the evening we had dinner fifteen metres above the ground, and the stars were within spoon's reach.
textes.Quand je suis remontée de la pointe doré: When I came up from the golden point, white as a sheet, Bastien hauled me into his boat without asking a single question. He put his cap on my head, for the sun. And I saw Lulu's purple octopus on his sail, staring at me with its big eyes. I burst out laughing. That laugh saved me.
textes.Quand je suis rentré de mes neuf jours,: When I came back from my nine days, Miriel didn't speak to me for a week. On the eighth day, she handed me an empty basket and said: “Next time, you take me with you.” Since then, we go walking together. She picks, I walk. And we're always home by evening.
textes.Quand je suis revenue de chez les fées l: When I came back from the fairies the first time, with golden pollen on my cheeks, Grandpa didn't ask me if it was true. He asked me: “And the music up there, what's it like?” It's the loveliest question anyone's ever asked me. I brought him back a glowing petal. He keeps it in his beanie.
textes.Quand je suis tombé dans la fontaine, en: When I fell into the fountain, smack into the planet Jupiter, the Elder was the first to applaud. She held out her cane to pull me out of the water and murmured: “The best speech of the year.” I never knew whether she was teasing. I believe not.
textes.Quand je suis tombée de la passerelle, à: When I fell from the walkway, at forty, Aëlwen bandaged my ankle with sage leaves and made me drink her potion. I pulled faces for a week. In Bois-Doré, they still call it “Lyra's grimace”. Aëlwen takes it as a compliment.
textes.Quand je suis venu à Montjoie, j'ai cher: When I came to Montjoie, I looked for a job where you had to stay still. Captain Ferdinand told me: “North Gate guard. You stay there. You don't move.” I said: “I'm very good at that.” He didn't know yet just how good.
textes.Quand je trouve une plume d'ara rouge da: When I find a red macaw feather in the forest, I keep it. Every week, I put it on her loom, without saying anything. She doesn't ask. One day, at the festival, she was wearing a red cape. All feathers. All mine. I counted. A hundred and twelve. She had kept them all.
textes.Quand l'anneau accélère, c'est que Théo: When the ring speeds up, it means Théo is taking the capsule up. We always know.
textes.Quand l'antenne est tombée sur le châtea: When the aerial fell onto the water tower, Fusible and I went to the foot of the ladder. He put one foot on the first rung. I'd brought a sandwich, to encourage him. At the second rung, we decided to eat the sandwich. And to wait for someone braver.

When the antenna fell onto the water tower, I went to the foot of the ladder. I looked up. I put one foot on the first rung. The Sergeant was behind me with a sandwich, to cheer me on. At the second rung, we ate the sandwich. We waited for someone braver.
textes.Quand l'éclair me touche, Pétronille acc: When the lightning hits me, Pétronille rushes over to tend to me. She trips on the way, every time. Once, she fell on me while I still had sparks in my hair. We were both struck. Our hair stood up at the same time. She said: “… it happens.” That was my line. She stole it. I don't hold it against her.
textes.Quand l'éclair me touche, je fais sembla: When the lightning hits me, I pretend it's nothing. “… it happens.” It's true, it happens. But I'd love it so much if one day it only happened to the monsters.
textes.Quand la Capitaine le dira. Elle sent le: When the Captain says so. She can feel the wind better than the weathervanes. The weathervanes ask her for advice.
textes.Quand la Guilde m'a demandé de devenir D: When the Guild asked me to become Dean, I said: “I'll think about it.” I thought for thirty seconds. My first act was to invite Brasero to tea. What a scandal! The Guild elders protested for a year. Brasero still comes for tea. The elders, meanwhile, have retired.
textes.Quand la Ligne a fermé pour travaux, on: When the Line closed for works, they told me to retire. I said: “What?” And I came back the next day to oil the cabin. And the day after. For ten years. On reopening morning, Dean Agathe handed me the departure key. She didn't say anything. She didn't need to: I wouldn't have heard anyway.
textes.Quand la Ligne a rouvert, tout le monde: When the Line reopened, everyone was on Cogwheel Square. The Great Clock chimed, the cabin arrived, and the folk from up top stepped out blinking. A gentleman said: “Oh, there's a sun!” The whole Square applauded. We were proud of our sun.
textes.Quand la Ligne a rouvert, un vieux jardi: When the Line reopened, an old gardener from Hautefond came up: Old Bastien. He thought our trees grew “in thin air”. He talked to my apple trees for an hour. I thought it was a bit mad. The next month, they gave twice as many apples. Now I talk to them too. Every morning.
textes.Quand la Ligne est passée en révision, j: When the Line went in for its overhaul, I thought I'd be bored. So I polished the capsule. Every day. For three years. Engineer Nova told me it hadn't been this clean since Séraphin. I polished it so much you could see yourself in it. I pulled faces at myself to pass the time.
textes.Quand la Zahra a eu sa couche de bleu, j: When the Zahra got her coat of blue, I told him: “One more.” He looked at me, and put on the second. I said: “One more.” He sighed, and put on the third. He swears it's the same blue, out of the same pot. Look at the boats at the quay: the bluest one is mine. Three coats. It shows.
textes.Quand la baleine passe au-dessus du dôme: When the whale passes over the dome, Nausicaa answers it. I tried for a long time, with my great-grandfather's trident, and nothing. One day I asked her for her secret. “You mustn't talk to it, Majesty. You must sing to it.” I have the voice of a seagull.
textes.Quand la corde a cassé, la nacelle est t: When the rope broke, the basket dropped all at once, then stopped dead. Down below, Bourru was holding the rope with his bare hands. Me, I clutched the mailbag and counted the strands of wicker. Two hundred and sixty. I never knew if there really were that many. I didn't dare count again.
textes.Quand la drisse a cassé, je suis tombé d: When the halyard snapped, I fell a whole storey, and a hand came out of nowhere and caught me by the belt. Gros-Louis set me back on the shrouds like a jar of jam. I thanked him for a week. On the eighth day, I saw his five tarry fingers on my shirt. I changed my shirt, not my mind.
textes.Quand la fièvre des marais est tombée su: When the marsh fever struck the Widow, Fulbert spent his nights in our lower deck, among the hammocks, with his herbal teas and his lantern. He stopped sleeping. I offered him gold. He refused. He said: “Pay Mama Grog instead.” Hm. That one's far too clever for a surgeon.
textes.Quand la fièvre est tombée fur la Feuve,: When the fever thtruck the Widow, Doc thaid I needed marth herb. I told him a grog would do. He looked at me over hith glatheth: “Thébathtien, with a grog, all you'll catch ith a thecond fever.” Nobody callth me Thébathtien. Ekthept him. It warmed my heart. More than the grog.
textes.Quand la fête commence, on l'entend jusq: When the party starts, you can hear it all the way to the dunes. Once, a caravan passing in the distance stopped to listen. The camels were dancing. Well, they were moving.
textes.Quand la gare a fermé, mon père m'a donn: When the station closed, my father gave me his toolbox and one sentence: “Anything that rolls can get going again.” I was twenty. I opened the bike workshop in a corner of the Spinning Mill, with three broken bikes. On the first day, I made one that rolled. On the second, I taught someone else to do it.
textes.Quand la ligne a fermé, j'ai cru que je: When the line closed, I thought I'd never be able to teach the sky again. No more trips, no more travellers, nothing real left to show. So I invented the Sky Lesson: we lie down in the playground, we close our eyes, and I tell them about it. Twelve years of telling the sky. My pupils had never seen it, and they knew it by heart. That's what I'm proudest of.
textes.Quand la louche de secours de Lentille s: When Lentille's spare ladle broke, I brought him a ship's ladle, with an anchor engraved on the handle. It had been round the world three times, according to the lady who dropped it off. Lentille washed it, talked to it, and hung it next to Pépite. They get on well.
When the sea is flat. Completely flat.
textes.Quand la mer sera plate. Toute plate. Co: When the sea is flat. Completely flat. Like a map.
textes.Quand la mère d'Ignatia, l'Archiduchesse: When Ignatia's mother, the Archduchess back then, entrusted me with the Ash Port, I put my spyglass away at the bottom of a chest. The next morning, I took it out again. I've never been able to do without it. Since then, I count the ships, I tidy the quays and I watch the sea. Mostly, it's the sea watching me.
textes.Quand la porte s'est rouverte, je suis m: When the door opened again, I went up to see him in the elves' village. Three hundred years of waiting! I asked him for the answer. He thought for a long time, hand on his chin… and fell asleep. I waited until evening. He woke up and said: “Ah, Cardamome! A riddle?”
textes.Quand la pétition a été votée, elle est: When the petition was passed, she came to announce it herself, in the classroom: “The first Thursday of next month.” The children shouted so loudly that Yolande came to check the windows. The President said: “The Council's best decision in eighty years.” Then she asked for a chair.
textes.Quand la reine sera contente de toi, ell: When the queen is pleased with you, maybe she'll teach you to travel like us: a blink of an eye, and whoosh, somewhere else.
textes.Quand la sirène sonne et que Sergent Fré: When the siren wails and Sergeant Fréquence sounds the alarm on the radio (in the daytime, in town), fight off the Movers' Raid: stop the robots before they carry the furniture off to the harbour
textes.Quand la sirène sonne, mon grand, c'est: When the siren sounds, kiddo, it means Lisse's robots are landing. The movers. They go into a squat, take the sofas, the tables, the crates, and carry everything off to the harbour saying “Thank you for your understanding.” We don't understand. So we all go out, link arms in front of the door, and form a chain. A human chain. The robots hate that: it's not in their programming. Next time Sergeant sounds the alert, come help us. Stop the robots, without hurting anyone except a few bolts. And we'll hold the door.
textes.Quand la tour de l'Académie a brûlé, le: When the Academy tower burned down, the old headmaster made us write out “A flame stays in its place” a thousand times. Cendrin finished in two days, in perfect handwriting. I wrote a forty-page treatise proving the sentence was false. I got a double punishment. Cendrin helped me do it.
textes.Quand le brigadier m'a interrogé pour le: When the sergeant questioned me about the croissants, I mentioned the white shadow. Nina found out. She came and planted herself in front of the kiosk, arms folded, and didn't have an ice cream. A whole day! No ice cream! That evening, she came back: “I forgive you, but you don't say another word.” Promise.
textes.Quand le chantier a fermé, il n'y avait: When the boatyard closed, there was no more good wood. Just pallets abandoned on the quays. I took one apart, nail by nail, and made a stool. It wobbled. So did the second one. The hundredth didn't. Today, I could build a whole town out of pallets. I nearly have.
textes.Quand le chenil de Flammèche était à côt: When Flammèche's kennel was next to my gardens, her puppies dug up my lava begonias every morning. One day, I found a bone in every pot. Twelve bones, twelve pots. I went to see Flammèche with my broom and asked her, kindly, to move. She moved the next day. I'm very persuasive, with my broom.
textes.Quand le chronomètre est arrivé de Cliqu: When the stopwatch arrived from Cliquetis, the first one I timed was Bondi, on a lap of the ten arches. I looked at the needle, I looked at Bondi, I looked at the needle. I thought the machine was broken, I shook it. It wasn't. Bondi was already munching his carrot.
textes.Quand le courrier de Tazira a confirmé l: When the Tazira mail confirmed the story of the cat who stole a treasure map, I kissed the bag. The commander gave me a funny look. She said: “You look relieved.” I said: “The truth is always a relief.” She didn't ask anything else. She's a good woman.
textes.Quand le cristal pâlit, les jardins pâli: When the crystal grows pale, the gardens grow pale too. Dad doesn't say anything, but in the evening he sits among the basins and sings them something deep, very quietly. I've heard him. He sings really out of tune. The corals don't mind, I think. They look happy.
textes.Quand le crocodile a mangé la niche de s: When the crocodile ate his dog's kennel, I built a new one from the remains of my old boat. Usually, an old boat gets burned. That one still smells of the river. Abouti sleeps in it like a fisherman. Hapou didn't say thank you, but he bought me a beer. With Hapou, that's the same thing.
When the flag says so, old-timer.
textes.Quand le fer a manqué, l'hiver dernier,: When iron ran short last winter, Salomé had three sacks of ore brought down from the highlands, by who knows what road. She sold them to me at the old price. I asked why. She said: “A smith who doesn't forge, talks. And you talk loud.” I found her almost kind.
textes.Quand le nouveau navire de Charbonnel es: When Charbonnel's new ship sailed into the Roads, Brindille flew from door to door delivering the letters announcing it. I shouted it once from the square. When she reached the last addressee, he was already at the port, clapping. She gave me a look… Her wings were trembling.
textes.Quand le nouveau navire du Capitaine est: When the Captain's new ship came into the Harbour, I flew from door to door delivering the letters announcing it. Hurla shouted it just once, from the square. When I got to the last addressee, he was already at the port, clapping. He took the letter and said: “Thanks, I knew.”
textes.Quand le port a fermé, la grue de l'oues: When the harbour closed, the west crane was left all alone, rusting. I climbed into it. I greased it for a month. One morning, it turned. I cried in the cab. I named her Mademoiselle. She's seventy. She creaks when she's happy.
textes.Quand le père de Noisette est parti, Pèr: When Noisette's father left, Father Clotaire came to the bakery every morning for a month. He didn't say anything. He bought a loaf, sat on the bench outside my door, and stayed there for an hour. One day, I asked him why. He said: “So that you hear someone breathing, on the other side of the door.” I've never forgotten it.
textes.Quand le vent a emporté ma partition, je: When the wind took my sheet music, I started playing only three songs, songs I hate. One evening, to cheer me on, Toni started singing the chorus of the Waltz behind his counter, from memory. Off-key. So off-key that three customers left. I laughed. I hadn't laughed in a week.
textes.Quand le vent souffle de l'ouest, il nou: When the wind blows from the west, it brings us Barnabé's voice, singing to the sea. His song about the one who defeated Nâga, I know by heart. In the last verse, the hero is ten feet tall and lifts the serpent with one hand. I like that verse very much. It's wrong, but it's beautiful.
textes.Quand le vent souffle du sud, mes bulles: When the wind blows from the south, my bubbles float all the way to the sea. The sailors at the port say it's raining bubbles. They love it.
textes.Quand le volcan crache, il ne faut pas c: When the volcano spits, don't run. Look up and take one step to the side. The sauce always lands where you run.
textes.Quand les autres se bagarrent, je le met: When the others brawl, I put him on my shoulders so he can see. He counts the punches out loud, like a referee. The night of the forty-three punches, he shouted “Forty-three!” so loud that the two bruisers stopped to clap for him. Brawl over. Little lad, big effect.
textes.Quand les golems se sont réveillés, je s: When the golems woke up, I went to see him. He laid his old hand on the wall of his alcove and said: “Someone woke them, Grimli. Not something. Someone.” Then he offered me some of his moonwater. It tasted of cold pebbles. I said it was delicious.
textes.Quand les jaguars du Mont Fumant ont vid: When the jaguars of the Smoking Mountain emptied my pen, he was the first to arrive, with his shield, and he swore to hunt them down. I gave him tamales for the road. The high priest told him to wait for the right day. Ever since, he comes by every week to tell me he's waiting. He leaves with tamales. It's a good arrangement.
textes.Quand les robots de Lisse débarquent, je: When Lisse's robots land, I sound the siren and shout into the mic: “ALERT! The robots are on the quays!” All of Boucan comes out. We form a human chain. The robots hate the chain. It's not in their programming.
textes.Quand les robots débarquent, on court to: When the robots show up, we all run under their wheels. They skid. We call it the rat race.
textes.Quand ma chèvre s'est perdue dans ses ga: When my goat got lost in his tunnels, Grimli searched for her for three days without sleeping, with a flickering lantern. He finally came out in the Great Hall. The goat was already there, on the throne. He apologised to her. She ate his lantern wick.
textes.Quand ma grand-mère est morte, elle m'a: When my grandmother died, she left me a single carpet, with a note: “Not for sale.” On it, the town gate, three stars, a crescent dune and a sun. She'd tell me over and over: “The star, the dune, the sun: that's the key.” The key to what? She never said. It's rolled up at the back of the stall. It's the only carpet in Tazira that has no price.
textes.Quand ma mère a été malade, il y a cinq: When my mother was ill, five years ago, Father Clotaire came to read her legends. He'd fall asleep halfway through. She'd elbow him from her bed. I listened to them from the kitchen. They laughed like children. I'd never heard my mother laugh like that. Since then, I don't like people making fun of Father Clotaire.
textes.Quand ma mère est partie, j'ai repris le: When my mother passed on, I took over the Fondouk with my husband, Mokhtar. He laughed loud and fixed everything. Ten years ago, he passed on in turn. Since then, I've run the house alone. Well, alone… My sister Rqia fires her pottery at the end of the street, and her daughter Halima throws all my tajine dishes. In a family of potters, you're never quite alone.
textes.Quand ma noisette s'est ouverte, sur les: When my hazelnut opened on the throne steps, the queen leaned down. I asked: “Are there any seeds around here?” She laughed, and showed me the whole of Yggdrasil. She said: “Here, there's the most beautiful one of all. It's sleeping.” I've wanted to see it ever since.
textes.Quand ma vieille louche de secours s'est: When my old spare ladle broke, Trocante turned up with a ladle from the Free Shop. A ship's ladle, with an anchor engraved on the handle. She said: “It's been round the world three times.” Now it serves soup. It looks happy to settle down.
textes.Quand maman écrit à papa, je dessine des: When Mum writes to Dad, I draw fish at the bottom of the letter. Loads. Mum writes recipes. Nothing but recipes. I asked her why she doesn't say “come back”. She went “Mrrr”, and she stretched eight times. Eight! She never does eight.
textes.Quand mes croissants ont commencé à disp: When my croissants started disappearing, Paulo told every table: “Margaux steals my croissants! No, I steal hers!” One morning, I'd lost twelve croissants in two nights and hadn't slept. He did the joke again right in front of my shop window. I threw a baguette at him. He caught it mid-air, said “thanks”, and kept it.
textes.Quand mes discours durent, sur la place,: When my speeches drag on, in the square, Gisèle simply raises a cup behind her counter. I can see it from the platform. It means: “Twelve cups, Aristide.” I wrap up within the minute. Hortense calls it “Gisèle's clock”.
textes.Quand mes genoux ont lâché, Hugues est v: When my knees gave out, Hugues came to my cabin at the foot of the Fangs every day for a month. He didn't say anything. He sat down, handed me a slice of bread and butter, cried a bit. One day, he said: “The Baron's looking for a keeper for the dungeon.” I know perfectly well he's the one who asked for it. I never told him.
textes.Quand mes jambes n'ont plus voulu monter: When my legs no longer wanted to climb mountains, I climbed up to the Lookout. It's not as high as a summit, but you can see the whole island. I watch for storms, boats, fires. And now, colours.
textes.Quand mes plumes du vent tombent sur son: When my wind feathers fall onto his lake, Borée freezes them in, standing straight, like little flags. To get them back, I have to say “please”. So I sing it, in D. He thaws them one by one, all afternoon, and I tell him about my week. I think he catches them on purpose.
textes.Quand mon chenil était à côté des Jardin: When my kennel was next to the Ash Gardens, my pups buried a bone in each of Mother Brasille's begonia pots. Twelve bones, twelve pots. She came to see me with her broom and asked me, very nicely, to move. The broom, I think, was there for the “nicely”. I moved the next day.
textes.Quand mon engrenage est tombé, Ernest m': When my gear fell, Ernest suggested the winding road, with the robot porters. It twists too much: I get dizzy just looking at it. So he offered to take me down in the cabin blindfolded. He was joking. I think. He had a funny look on his face when he said it, as if he knew what he was talking about.
textes.Quand mon père m'a laissé le moulin, il: When my father left me the mill, he introduced the four winds to me the way you'd introduce a family. “The North is the grump. The East, the shy one. The South, the lazy one. The West, the poet.” I asked which one I was. He laughed and said: “The West, of course. You blow sentimental draughts.”
textes.Quand nous gravons ensemble, il frappe e: When we engrave together, he strikes and I trace, all night long, without a word. One morning, I said: “Good.” Just once in a hundred years. He left the forge in a great hurry, saying he had dust in his eye. There's dust in a forge. I believed him. The runes didn't.
textes.Quand nous sommes arrivés, le Cœur de cr: When we arrived, the crystal Heart was set at the top of the Spire to make the island float. Nobody really knew how to look after it. Me, I listened. It hummed, it crackled, it went quiet. After a year, I understood its noises. After six hundred, I know it better than I know myself.
textes.Quand nous étions jeunes, Averse ouvrait: When we were young, Downpour would open her umbrella over my sunflowers when it got too hot. She said it was for the flowers. It was for me.
textes.Quand nous étions petits, Bulle s'est pe: When we were little, Bulle got lost in our mother's gardens, among the ash pepper bushes. He was crying. I found him by following the sound, and I made him a label: “Bulle, do not lose”. He wore it round his neck for a year. I think he still has it. He won't tell me.
textes.Quand on a construit le jardin, il n'y a: When the garden was built, there was nothing but gravel, grey, flat, sad. They gave me a rake. I drew a wave. The next day, the wind had wiped it away. I drew another wave. That was thirty years ago.
textes.Quand on a installé Bidule dans la cave,: When we set Bidule up in the cellar, between the soap barrels, Dad didn't say anything. The next day, Bidule had a hat. A hat made of hardened bubble, see-through, with a little brim. Dad pretended not to know where it came from. He was very bad at pretending. He had soap up to his elbows.
textes.Quand on a refait le Funiculaire, il fal: When we rebuilt the Funicular, we needed wheels that could roll at the bottom of the sea without a single squeak. I wrote to the Great Strata Forge. Mistress Brunehaut replied: “Send the plans. And a little patience.” Three months later, Rivet and Bielle, from the Fronde, brought them down on a mine cart, through the works tunnel. On the crate, a note: “Tempered in laughter. HO HO!” They've never squeaked.
textes.Quand on avait dix ans, Yaya montait des: When we were ten, Yaya put on shows in the street, with bedsheets for curtains. I was the audience, the lighting and the box office. One day, the only paying spectator was a fisherman passing by. He gave us a fish. We grilled it on the beach, very proud. Our first fee.
textes.Quand on est arrivés sur l'île, chacun m: When we arrived on the island, everyone ate at home. I brought out my big table, put it in the middle of the Borgo and shouted: “Dinner's ready!” Nobody came. The next day I did it again, with a focaccia. Three people came. On the third day, everyone. We've never stopped since.
textes.Quand on est arrivés, le blé poussait to: When we arrived, the wheat was growing on its own, wild, between the stones. I tasted it. It tasted of sunshine and ash. I said to Lasagna: “With this, you'll make the best pasta in the world.” She said: “I already do.” But she tasted it. She smiled.
textes.Quand on grave ensemble une grosse comma: When we engrave a big order together, Nori turns up with his hood and his moonwater, sits by the anvil and stays silent all night. I hammer, he traces. In the morning, once in a hundred years, he said: “Good.” I nearly cried. I didn't. Stone and fire.
textes.Quand on repeint une maison dans un arbr: When you repaint a house in a tree, you need a very long ladder. Mine creaks on every rung, each on a different note. Lili learned to climb it by playing a song. Now the whole village knows when I'm working: you can hear the ladder's song.
textes.Quand on était jeunes, Tournesol me fais: When we were young, Sunflower made me crowns of sunflowers. I dried them in my umbrella. I still have one. It's all grey, but I'm keeping it.
textes.Quand on était petites, elle me donnait: When we were little, she gave me bits of thread of every colour in exchange for my cacao beans. She never counted. I did. At the end of the summer, I had an enormous ball of yarn, and she had no beans left. I was ashamed. I gave everything back. She said: “Keep the yarn, it's pretty.” I still have it.
textes.Quand on était petites, maman chantait l: When we were little, Mum sang the tides and Ianthé danced on the edge of the canal. One day, she fell in at high tide. She kept dancing in the water, and Mum kept singing. Me, I laughed so hard I missed my first verse.
textes.Quand on était petites, on échangeait no: When we were little, we swapped our treasures: me, scraps of thread of every colour; her, cacao beans. She counted mine, I never counted hers. She was always the better merchant. Today, I weave her huipils, and she pays me in cacao. She still counts. I still don't.
textes.Quand on était petits, dans la pirogue d: When we were little, in my father's canoe, he sold me the front seat for three flatbreads. I ate them, then took the seat back. He cried thief. I said I hadn't stolen it: I'd captured it. He was seven. He still remembers. So do I, I admit.
textes.Quand on était petits, elle me cachait d: When we were little, she used to hide cherry tomatoes in my pockets so I'd always have a snack. She still does it.
textes.Quand on était petits, je lui ai vendu l: When we were little, I sold him the front seat of the canoe for three flatbreads. He ate them, then took the seat back. I cried thief. He said he'd captured it. Already! At seven! I should have understood straight away that we'd never be in the same line of work.
textes.Quand personne ne regarde… Alors tu dans: When nobody's watching… Then you dance the way I play, alone, at night, for the lanterns. Those are the most beautiful dances. Nobody ever sees them.
textes.Quand quelqu'un revient du marais, Isaac: When someone comes back from the marsh, Isaac steps out onto his doorstep. So do I. He looks at the sky. So do I. We wait to see whose door the adventurer will walk through with his crocodile teeth. Isaac pays six coins a tooth. Me, I make an iron fist out of three. Iron lasts longer than six coins.
textes.Quand ses genoux ont dit non, il y a qui: When his knees said no, fifteen years ago, I cried for a week. He told me: “Stop it, Hugues, you'll rust your beard.” I'm the one who asked the Baron to put him in charge of the dungeon entrance. He doesn't know. I wanted him to be the first to see every adventurer come back up. He's the one who always saw me come back up.
textes.Quand son engrenage est tombé au port, j: When his gear fell down to the harbour, I offered to take Firmin down in a cable car blindfolded. I was joking. Half joking. He looked at me so sadly that I nearly confessed… well, that I nearly offered him another coffee. I suggested the winding road, with the porters. He says it twists too much. He's not wrong.
textes.Quand ta lanterne en abritera cinq, va d: When your lantern holds five of them, go to the Mother Tree's door, on the sunset side. They'll know what to do.
textes.Quand ton bateau a traversé la brume pou: When your boat crossed the mist for the first time, it was Haldir who reached my tower first: “A human! With Lyra's compass!” He hadn't run that fast in a hundred years. For once, he told me where he was going. He was going to see you.
textes.Quand tu auras perdu tes sourcils, comme: When you've lost your eyebrows, like me!
textes.Quand tu dors, je garde ton sac. Personn: When you sleep, I guard your bag. Nobody touches it. Except me. A little. Just to check.
textes.Quand tu dors, je veille sur toi. Les ye: When you sleep, I watch over you. With my eyes closed. It's a very advanced technique.
textes.Quand tu dors, je veille. Quand tu mange: When you sleep, I keep watch. When you eat, I watch. When you fall, I lick your face. That's my job. I'm very professional.
textes.Quand tu es arrivé, mon petit, je t'ai r: When you arrived, my little one, I watched you climb the stairs of the Great Oak. You had colours on you: your bag, your cheeks, your eyes. The only colours on the island. I knew right away that you were the answer. I didn't cry. Well, hardly.
textes.Quand tu m'as dit « Ursule m'envoie », j: When you told me “Ursule sent me”, I grunted. Then I looked at your blade: put to the grindstone, tempered in the mist, an edge as clean as a rune line. She hasn't forgotten a thing. She doesn't write letters, Ursule. Sending you to me is her way of saying hello.
textes.Quand tu mangeras une sardine crue sans: When you eat a raw sardine without pulling a face.
textes.Quand tu me laisses à la maison, je t'at: When you leave me at home, I wait for you by the door. All day. I don't move. Well, I go for a wee. But I come back.
textes.Quand tu mets la tête sous l'eau et que: When you put your head underwater and hold your breath… what do you hear?
textes.Quand tu ne sais plus quoi faire, demand: When you don't know what to do, ask people for rumours. There's always a lead.
When you know the clove hitch.
When you can keep quiet for an hour.
textes.Quand un apprenti a appris les six sorts: When an apprentice has learned the six spells, the archmage leads them to the Circle. You lay your hand on the altar. The stones decide. They've never said no. But they could.
textes.Quand un aventurier monte de rang, c'est: When an adventurer ranks up, I'm the one who announces it to the whole town. I say their name, their new rank, and a little compliment. For Hilaire, I've been preparing the compliment for twelve years. It's very beautiful. It's waiting.
textes.Quand un aventurier revient du marais av: When an adventurer comes back from the marsh with crocodile teeth, Brutus and I step out onto our doorsteps at the same time. I pay six coins a tooth; he offers an iron fist for three. So we keep an eye on each other. It's very awkward. We pretend to look at the sky. It's never rained so much in our conversations.
textes.Quand un client dit « Quelles belles éto: When a customer says “What lovely stars!” in front of our lanterns, I can't hear. Being deaf has its uses. When they say “What lovely copper!”, I hear perfectly. Nourredine says my ear picks and chooses. It chooses well.
textes.Quand une de mes expériences explose, Mu: When one of my experiments explodes, Murmure always arrives first, without a sound. She says nothing, she gathers the flying pages, and she files them. Then she whispers: “…Quieter, next time.” I'm trying. My explosions are more and more discreet. She says I'm making progress.
textes.Quand une gargouille m'a volé un mérou,: When a gargoyle stole a grouper from me, I chased it all along the quay, shouting. It dropped it in the water. I went back to my stall, furious, and the Captain was waiting for me. He gave me the best spot on the quay, under the harbour office awning, safe from gargoyles. He didn't ask for anything. I give him the first fish of every catch.
textes.Quand vous y pensez. Je vois. Alors j'y: When you remember. I see. Then I shall remember for you: I shall put doormats in your path. Large doormats. Everywhere.
textes.Quand Écrou est arrivée, à neuf ans, ell: When Écrou arrived, at nine, she didn't want to climb the stairs: too many steps. So I made up a song for every hundred. The first for the legs, the second for the breath, the third for courage, the fourth for the end. We sang it every day for six years. I still sing it, all alone, when nobody can hear me.
textes.Quand ça gronde, tu as peur, m'as-tu dit: When it rumbles, you're scared, you told me. It's rumbling more and more, {surnom}. Keep that to yourself.
When they bite, reel in with little turns. If the tension goes red, ease off a bit. The fish tires before you do. Normally.
textes.Quand ça vous arrange ! C'est très malin: When it suits you! That's very clever. I'll do the same: the good signs, I'll believe; the bad ones, I'll leave at the bottom of the sea.
textes.Quarante ! Non, trente-neuf : celui-là,: Forty! No, thirty-nine: that one's a leaf.
textes.Quarante ans boulanger. Lever à trois he: Forty years a baker. Up at three, kneading trough, oven, and in the afternoon, pétanque. On the first day, Marcel, the postman, put his satchel down at the edge of the pitch and said: “You point like a baker.” I answered: “And you shoot like a postman.” We argued the whole game. That was forty years ago. We've never finished.
textes.Quarante ans d'université. Des cours, de: Forty years at the university. Lectures, papers, conferences. And always, at the back of the hall, someone whispering the same phrase with a smile. In the end it became my name: in the corridors, they no longer said “Professor Moreau”, they said “Moreau and his Atlantis”. Very well. A name is a promise. I kept searching.
textes.Quarante ans dans la grande hune. Mainte: Forty years in the main top. Now my knees won't climb any more, so I keep watch from the bow. Ewen goes up to light the lantern for me.
Forty years in your cellar, Ulfa.
textes.Quarante ans de mer, et je n'ai jamais p: Forty years at sea, and I've never lost a line. Except that one.
textes.Quarante ans de pêche, pas un jour de na: Forty years of fishing, not one day of shipwreck. The secret: I come home when the seagulls come home.
textes.Quarante ans derrière ce comptoir. J'ai: Forty years behind this counter. I sold apples to the mayor when he was knee-high.
textes.Quarante ans là-haut, par tous les temps: Forty years up there, in all weathers. I've seen whales go by, two waterspouts, and a boat from Port-Azur lost in the night, which I guided home with the lantern. It's all written in my journal, with the time. Ships, I counted them. Hardly any ever came by. That's no reason to stop counting.
textes.Quarante ans là-haut. Trois cent vingt m: Forty years up there. Three hundred and twenty steps, twice a day. I've got the calves of a young man and the heart of an old one.
textes.Quarante ans que je joue avec Marcel. Qu: Forty years I've been playing with Marcel. Forty years we've been arguing. He's my best friend, but don't tell him.
Forty years I've been fishing off this jetty. I've caught sardines, perch, an old boot and a cold. The King of the Pools, never. One day.
Forty years I've run this tavern. It was my mother's, and her mother's before. The fireplace is an old stove from the Léviathan's galley. It's never gone cold.
textes.Quarante ans à l'université. On s'est mo: Forty years at the university. They mocked me at every conference: “Moreau and his Atlantis”. I never gave up.
Forty minutes of rain on a tent. Nothing else. “It's my favorite record to fall asleep to,” says the owner.
textes.Quarante tasses à la minute, et un coup: Forty cups a minute, and a toot of the whistle when it's ready. Upstairs, Héloïse's spring beds. Waiting tables, Master Rivet's butler. At the counter, Professor Boum and his iron powder; on the terrace, his ninth roof as an awning. Every morning I make Achille's sandwich. And the coffee comes from the Tazira caravaners, by the Zéphyr.
textes.Quarante épices, et je les connais toute: Forty spices, and I know every one of them by its first name. Zohra and her Friday saffron, Mustapha and his cumin, Samira who wastes my saffron dyeing rags. Salomé, in Carène, who buys everything from me and calls me a thief. And a big pirate cook who brings me parsley as if it were roses. Parsley! Smell, smell… All of Tazira passes under my nose.
textes.Quarante-deux ans d'horlogerie. Je dors: Forty-two years of clockmaking. I sleep with three alarm clocks. They all ring at the same second. It's the most beautiful sound in the world.
textes.Quarante-deux lettres ! Il m'a répondu u: Forty-two letters! He wrote back once: “Dear colleague, your forecast for Tuesday was correct.” Grandpa framed it. It's above my bed.
Forty-two. And a half. For dancing.
textes.Quarante-trois carillons, et pas deux qu: Forty-three chimes, and no two sing alike.
textes.Quark a caché un grelot dans mon thérémi: Quark hid a little bell in my theremin. It goes “ooooh-ding”. I kept the bell. It's become my most popular piece.
Quark hid a bell in my theremin. It goes “oooh-ding.” I kept the bell. It's become my most popular piece. I've never thanked him. He knows.
textes.Quark a dit qu'il allait se cacher là où: Quark said he'd hide where nobody would ever find him. I always find him. He sings while he's hiding. He doesn't know. Don't tell him.
textes.Quark a essayé d'apprendre aux glouglous: Quark tried to teach the gurgles a rude word. They all said “gurg”. Mind you, maybe the rude word was “gurg”. I'm not fluent in Gurgle yet.
textes.Quark a fait une bosse dans mon plus bea: Quark put a dent in my most beautiful dome, while playing. I kept it. It has character. I made him a door that only opens if you pull a face. He pulls some very fine ones.
textes.Quark a joué à la balle contre mon dôme: Quark was playing ball against my new dome, in the north-east. The ball was a chunk of meteorite. A big dent appeared in the glass. He came to apologise, all small, all sheepish. I looked at the dent for a long time. Then I said: “It has character.” I kept it. It's Quark's dent.
textes.Quark dérègle mes horloges, met des grel: Quark messes up my clocks, hangs bells everywhere and spends his life fifty-nine seconds away from disaster. It's exhausting. He makes me laugh. I don't say so.
textes.Quark est tombé du pont de lumière en ma: Quark fell off the bridge of light walking on his hands. Pixel treated him before I got there: she put a light plaster on him, explaining why you mustn't walk on your hands. He listened without a word. For once. He loves light plasters: they glow in the dark.
textes.Quark m'a demandé de l'emmener faire un: Quark asked me to take him for a ride in my saucer. Pixel told her mum. Pixel is a tattletale. Quark is a little daredevil. I like him. He reminds me of someone.
textes.Quark m'a demandé de lui apprendre le th: Quark asked me to teach him the theremin. He waved his hands so fast over the instrument that it made the sound of a falling saucer. All the gloopers in the Greenhouse answered at the same time. Nova came running. Quark said: “It's avant-garde music.” I gave him a second lesson.
textes.Quark m'a fait croire que la fontaine al: Quark made me believe the fountain would show the planet Gloop all day long, “in my honour”. I waited in front of the fountain from eight o'clock until noon, camera ready. Gloop appeared for just one minute. Quark was laughing behind a bench. I took a photo of him laughing. That's my revenge.
textes.Quark me saute dessus comme sur un tramp: Quark jumps on me like I'm a trampoline. I go “blorp” and he bounces off. I told him I wasn't a trampoline. He jumped again. I laugh too much to get cross.
textes.Quark triche à cache-cache, fait des far: Quark cheats at hide-and-seek, plays pranks on everyone and always says “wasn't me”. It's always him. I always find him, because he sings while he hides. He's my brother. I love him. Why? Because.
textes.Quark, c'est mon petit frère. Il a quatr: Quark is my little brother. He's eighty-one. He does all sorts of silly things. He hides, he plays pranks, he sticks biscuits on the Hologuide. Well, through it. Me, I'm very good. Nearly all the time. Why are you laughing?
textes.Quark, tu as touché à mon thérémine ?: Quark, have you been touching my theremin?
Quark. My fountain is one second fast.
textes.Quatorze promesses. Je les ai toutes not: Fourteen promises. I've written them all down.
textes.Quatorze étages d'appartements, de jardi: Fourteen floors of flats, gardens and offices, each one turned a little more than the one below: that's what gives it the twist. Right at the top, the panoramic room, open to everyone. That's the City's rule: the highest place belongs to all.
textes.Quatorze étages qui tournent… Je me dema: Fourteen twisting floors… I wonder who got dizzy first: the architect or the tower.
textes.Quatre ! J'ai une grosse idée !: Four! I've got a big idea!
textes.Quatre Sustentateurs, aux quatre coins d: Four Levitators, at the four corners of the island, under the rock. This one is number two, the chattiest. If one of them stops, the other three hold the island up without any trouble. But none of them has ever stopped.
Four alerts, two slimes, one cloud.
textes.Quatre aventuriers, Maman ! Et une greno: Four adventurers, Mum! And a frog!
textes.Quatre cent douze, Zigomar ! Et ta chaus: Four hundred and twelve, Zigomar! And your shoe!
Four hundred? I'll count them, mind.
textes.Quatre cents ans d'erreurs, ça devient u: Four hundred years of mistakes, that's a tradition!
textes.Quatre chemins partent du carrefour : un: Four paths leave the crossroads: a red one, a black one, a white one, a yellow one. On the stele, these words: “Here, the Twins hesitated. But Xan, the mosquito, went on ahead of them.”
textes.Quatre creux ronds… vides. Et un cercle: Four round hollows… empty. And a circle that glows! So Corentin was telling the truth: four seals, one for each people of the island. Here, that's for your trouble, and my map of the island, copied out for you. One day, you'll have to go and see the shepherds of the north, the mist people and the caravaneers of the south. And find our own seal.
textes.Quatre de mes livres se sont envolés pen: Four of my books flew away during the storm. I can still see them, stuck where nobody can climb. They pretend they can't hear me.
textes.Quatre grands anneaux tournent sous l'îl: Four great rings spin under the island, inside the rock, and push against the ground far, far below. Séraphin Altaïr worked it all out a hundred and twenty years ago. We just make sure they don't nod off.
textes.Quatre mondes sur une seule Colonne : le: Four worlds on a single Column: the Clouds, Hautefond, us, and the Azure Dome at the bottom of the sea. Up top, they have the real sun. In the Dome, they have the blue light of the water. Here, we made our own. I think it's the bravest of the three.
textes.Quatre mondes, une seule Colonne… et bie: Four worlds, one Column… and soon, one soup! Honorine and I are going to make the soup of the four worlds: her mushrooms from the Strata, my seaweed from the Dome, apples from Hautefond's Orchards, and strawberries from the Clouds for dessert. One big table on Pearl Square. Even the Burgomaster will get a bowl. Especially the Burgomaster: it'll keep his mouth busy during his speech.
textes.Quatre petits Moaïs, immobiles au fond d: Four little Moai, motionless at the back of the room. Very motionless. Too motionless.
textes.Quatre peuples sur cette île, quatre sce: Four peoples on this island, four seals on the great gate. Ours, the Seal of Mists… It sleeps at the bottom of the biggest pool. Only the moon knows where, and the moon speaks only to the elders. Not to you. Not yet.
textes.Quatre pièces. Le fil n'est pas gratuit,: Four coins. Thread isn't free, and neither is the disinfectant. Especially the disinfectant.
textes.Quatre régions, quatre peuples. Nous, à: Four regions, four peoples. Us, in the west, on the coast. In the north, the highland shepherds: tough folk who don't say much. In the east, the people of the misty forest: you hardly ever see them. In the south, the desert caravanners: they sell everything, and at a steep price.
textes.Quatre sceaux pour la dernière porte. Le: Four seals for the last gate. The desert keeps its own under a dune that walks. To find it, they say, you must follow the stars that walk. … The caravan lanterns, perhaps. Or something else.
Four seconds. We can do better.
textes.Quatre serpents qui tournent deux par de: Four serpents turning two by two? Ah, the Ancients and their pranks… Start with the one that's already in the right place, and see which one it drags along.
textes.Quatre statues de pierre, chacune avec s: Four stone statues, each with its medallion: a sailor (the wave), a caravan woman (the sun), a shepherd (the cogwheel), a fox woman (the moon). On the fresco above the staircase, the four peoples hold hands before the great gate; above them, a red stone heart, linked by four rays to four crystals.
textes.Quatre symboles gravés, dans l'ordre : I: Four symbols engraved, in order: I, II, III, IIII. And beneath: “When the night lifts the sea, the day rises, and the guardian awakes.”
textes.Quatre, Mamie Rissole, si vous permettez: Four, Mamie Rissole, if you please!
textes.Quatre, cinq… Ne parle pas en comptant,: Four, five… Don't talk while you count, you lose your air.
textes.Quatre-vingts ans. J'ai ramendé les file: Eighty years old. I've mended the nets of three generations of fishermen. Moulay Brahim, I knew him when he was tiny. He used to cry when he saw a crab.
textes.Quatre-vingts ans. Mes yeux ne voient pl: Eighty years old. My eyes don't see far any more, but my hands tie two thousand knots a day. Khadija, my pupil, ties a thousand, and she threads my needles. Larbi lights his green lighthouse: I know it by the smell of the wick. Little Brahim is amin. Ba Sidi gets the beard wrong every evening. Lou has come back. And Sel's grandson asks me questions. Everything comes back, my child.
Four. And I keep my secrets.
Four. I've got a big idea.
For Boulon to see the sea from my boat. He always looks at it from up high.
That Caelan dares before the Dawn Festival. There are ten years left. For an elf, that's tomorrow. For Caelan, it's cutting it a bit fine.
textes.Que Gaspard voie le Crâne Fendu un soir: For Gaspard to see the Crâne Fendu on a party night: Tom on the fiddle, the whole port singing, and not a single broken chair. Well, one. Just one, for the atmosphere.
textes.Que Mathilde descende enfin, qu'on se ti: That Mathilde finally comes down, that we each stand at an anvil, face to face, and strike together: two knocks, then one. So the whole cavern hears it. And to forge with her a great door, between the top and the bottom. A door that doesn't close.
textes.Que Myrtille voie le Roi des mares. Une: That Myrtille sees the Pond King. Once, with her own eyes. Not catch him. See him. That he looks at her, and laughs.
textes.Que Pimprenelle descende par la Ligne, q: For Pimprenelle to come down the Line, step out of the cabin, and before we even say hello, tap two knocks, then one, on the handrail. And for me to answer. And then show her round the whole Forge, and show her Grand-Mère, the steam hammer. It's much bigger than all her bolts.
textes.Que Radio Boucan s'entende sur toutes le: That Radio Boucan can be heard on every island in the archipelago. That a pirate from Balafre, an adventurer from Montjoie and a tourist from Port-Azur listen to the same gig at the same time, and each dance in their own home.
May His Noodles protect you, {surnom}. Ramen!
textes.Que Zéro me raconte encore toutes ses hi: That Zéro tells me all his stories again. And to live a hundred years, to have as many as him.
textes.Que cache l'Arbre-Mère ?: What does the Mother Tree hide?
textes.Que chaque habitant du Boucan ait un vél: That every inhabitant of Boucan has a bike they've repaired themselves. Not a bike I give them: a bike they understand. And a big bike parade along the quays, with rat-shaped bells.
textes.Que cherchez-vous sur cette carte ?: What are you looking for on that map?
textes.Que cherchez-vous, milord ?: What are you looking for, milord?
textes.Que dans cent ans, on se souvienne de Né: That in a hundred years, people remember Neopolis not for its towers, but because it was a city where humans and androids said hello to each other.
textes.Que de livres ! Tous bien rangés… sauf u: So many books! All neatly arranged… except one, a red one, that isn't quite in its place.
textes.Que demande Charon pour passer l'Achéron: What does Charon ask for to cross the Acheron?
textes.Que dit un arbre à un autre arbre ? « Tu: What does one tree say to another? “You seem very grounded today.” … Tree jokes are slow.
textes.Que dit un caillou à un autre caillou ?: What does one pebble say to another pebble?
textes.Que dit un coquelicot à un autre coqueli: What does one poppy say to another poppy? “You're all red!” “So are you!”
textes.Que dit un oignon quand il se cogne ?: What does an onion say when it bumps itself?
textes.Que dit une gomme à un crayon ? « Arrête: What does an eraser say to a pencil? “Stop making mistakes, I'm the one who has to clean up!”
textes.Que dit une huître à une autre huître ?: What does one oyster say to another oyster? Nothing. They keep their mouths shut. … It's a very old joke.
textes.Que dit une imprimante dans l'eau ?: What does a printer say when it's sinking?
textes.Que dit une méduse quand elle est conten: What does a jellyfish say when it's happy? Nothing: it lights up. … It took Professor Benthos twenty years to work that out. He's very proud of it.
