textes.Rissole, j'ai pris trois kilos ce mois-c: Rissole, I've put on three kilos this month!
Rissole, just a small slice tonight.
textes.Rita m'a annoncé, l'œil mystérieux, que: Rita announced, with a mysterious look, that Gérard would find his camera thanks to “someone who walks a lot”. It's pretty, I'll admit. But the day before, she was on the promenade when Gérard came down from the lookout, empty-handed and looking like a lost dog. I saw her watching him. Just saying. Or not saying.
textes.Rita m'a dit que l'horloge sonnerait de: Rita told me the clock would chime again thanks to a stranger. I don't believe that nonsense. But I'm watching you, all the same.
textes.Rita me prédit un grand amour tous les a: Rita foretells a great love for me every year. She's wrong every year. I pay every year. Don't try to understand.
textes.Rita prédit à Colette un grand amour tou: Every year Rita foretells a great love for Colette, at the same price. For me, she foretold a stranger who'd make my clock ring. I told her: “Nonsense.” She replied: “You'll see.” Since then, that's how we greet each other, from one door to the other. “Nonsense.” “You'll see.”
textes.Rita, la voyante, m'a prédit un grand am: Rita, the fortune-teller, predicted a great love for me. She predicts it every year. I still pay.
textes.Rivet tape trop fort, rit trop fort, aim: Rivet hits too hard, laughs too hard, loves too hard. With him, everything's at full steam. I'm the one who switches the points. He charges ahead. Together, we always get somewhere. Often not where we meant to. But somewhere good.
textes.Rivet tape trop fort. (Un temps.) Mais i: Rivet hits too hard. (A pause.) But he hits in time. That's rare, both together. Don't tell him. He'd hit even harder.
textes.Rivet, de la Fronde, répare les rails de: Rivet, from the Fronde, repairs the rails for the mine carts. The work is perfect. The rails are often painted in colours. I grumble about the paint. Never about the work.
textes.Roadie d'honneur du Festival du Larsen: Honorary roadie of the Larsen Festival
textes.Robot ! Là-bas ! Je le mords ? Je le mor: Robot! Over there! Shall I bite it? I'll bite it. I bit it. Are you proud of me? Say you're proud of me.
textes.Rodrigue ! J'ai une nouvelle chanson sur: Rodrigue! I've got a new song about you!
textes.Rodrigue conteste tout : ses rangs, ses: Rodrigue disputes everything: his ranks, his contracts, his crystal readings, the weather. He files one complaint form a week. He's my most regular customer.
textes.Rodrigue est venu contester sa lecture d: Rodrigue came to dispute his crystal ball reading nine times. The ball always said: “Courage: lots; caution: um…”. The tenth time, I put the ball in front of him without a word. It showed: “um…”. Nothing else. He left with great dignity. I filed the form under “Complaints, abandoned”.
Rodrigue came to dispute his crystal ball reading. For the ninth time. The ball said “courage: plenty; caution: um…”. He finds the “um” offensive. I've made a note of it.
textes.Rodrigue et moi, nous nous entraînons da: Rodrigue and I train in the castle courtyard, one after the other. Me from seven to nine, him from nine to noon. One morning, I stayed longer. He drew his sword and gave a twenty-minute speech on “the honour of schedules”. I was eating a pie. At the end, I offered him a slice. He accepted. We no longer speak to each other. Except about pie.
textes.Rodrigue m'a commandé une cape « qui cla: Rodrigue ordered a cape from me “that flaps in the wind even without wind”. I put wire in it. It flaps. It flaps even when he's asleep.
textes.Rodrigue m'a commandé une chanson tragiq: Rodrigue commissioned a tragic song about himself. I did my best. The audience laughed for twenty minutes. Not my fault: he fell off the stage during the chorus.
textes.Rodrigue m'a encore fait un discours. Vi: Rodrigue gave me another speech. Twenty minutes. I said “no”. He left. Efficient.
textes.Rodrigue m'a fait un discours de vingt m: Rodrigue gave me a twenty-minute speech on the honour of the sword, in front of the Guild. I waited. I ate a cake. When he paused for breath, I said “no”. He stopped. He thought. He said: “You're right.” Then he left. I still don't know what question I answered.
textes.Rodrigue me commande des capes impossibl: Rodrigue orders impossible capes from me: ones that billow without wind, glow in the dark, “inspire dread”. He wears them with total conviction. I like that about him.
textes.Rodrigue nous regarde, derrière la fonta: Rodrigue is watching us from behind the fountain. He thinks we can't see him. Let's wave! Hello, Rodrigue!
textes.Rodrigue prétend être votre rival. Votre: Rodrigue claims to be your rival. Your rival! He doesn't know that I am your rival. Well, your ally. Your rival-ally. It's a very noble category.
Rodrigue claims to be your only rival. I am your rival-ally, which is a nobler category. He talks too much. He fights well. He talks too much.
textes.Rodrigue veut des tragédies. Je fais de: Rodrigue wants tragedies. I do my best. But he falls off the stage during the chorus, slips off cliffs, gives speeches to goats. It's not my fault he's funny.
Rodrigue, your cape has a hole.
textes.Rodrigue. Trop de mots. Bon épéiste, qua: Rodrigue. Too many words. Good swordsman, though. Don't tell him.
textes.Rodrigue. Trop de mots. Bon épéiste. Il: Rodrigue. Too many words. Good swordsman. He gives me speeches. I say no. He leaves. Works every time.
textes.Rodrigue. Vous êtes dans la cour à mon h: Rodrigue. You're in the courtyard during my hour.
Round and happy! Like my belly.
textes.Ronde de nuit. Le cœur brille plus fort,: Night rounds. The heart glows brighter at night. As if it were watching over the city.
textes.Ronds comme la lune, ami ! Ronds comme l: Round as the moon, friend! Round as the moon!
textes.Ronflements. Sur le canapé, quelqu'un do: Snoring. On the sofa, someone sleeps under three plaid blankets. A black cat sleeps on top of him. Nobody moves.
textes.Ronron. Le chat dort au milieu de cent t: Purr. The cat sleeps amid a hundred tick-tocks. It calls this “peace and quiet”.
textes.Ronron. Le chat se roule sur le dos. C'e: Purr. The cat rolls onto its back. It's a trap, everybody knows that.
textes.Rosa a seize canons. J'en ai sept. Elle: Rosa has sixteen cannons. I have seven. She reminds me every day. Hers fire. Mine keep watch. It's not the same.
textes.Rosa m'a appris le nœud de chaise. Alors: Rosa taught me the bowline. So to practise, I tied Amine to the fountain. A perfect knot! Nobody could undo it, not even the slipper man. They had to go and get Rosa. She undid the knot, and afterwards, very quietly, she said: “Well done, little cabin girl.” Amine's still sulking.
textes.Rosa m'emprunte une lanterne à chaque fê: Rosa borrows a lantern from me at every festival. I know it, she knows I know it, and we don't talk about it. A thief who brings back what she damages: that only exists in Tazira.
textes.Rosa, c'est la plus forte pirate du mond: Rosa is the strongest pirate in the world. She's got hair as red as fire, sixteen cannons, and she knows every knot. When I grow up, I'll be like her. But a captain. And not a pirate.
textes.Rosa, la pirate, m'a montré comment on f: Rosa, the pirate, showed me how to tie a bowline. I can do it with my eyes closed. Well, almost.
textes.Rosa. La rouquine des pirates. Fille de: Rosa. The pirates' redhead. A fisherman's daughter. She rows well. She doesn't talk at sea. That's rare. I take her along.
textes.Rosalie Cannelle, au Grand Marché de Hau: Rosalie Cannelle, at Hautefond's Great Market, is my cousin. Our mothers were sisters. She says “taste, taste”; I say “taste” just once: under the sea, you save your breath. She knows all the gossip from up top. I know all the tastes from down below. Between the two of us, we know almost everything.

Rosalie Cannelle, at Hautefond's Great Market, is my cousin. Our mothers were sisters. Hers stayed up top with the spices; mine came down to marry a fisherman. Rosalie says “taste, taste”. I say “taste” just once. Under the sea, you save your breath.

Rosalie Cannelle, at Hautefond's Great Market, knows everything before anyone else, up top. I do, down below. We swap our news by letter. She sends me ten bits, I send her one. But mine comes from the bottom of the sea: it's worth ten. She doesn't agree.
textes.Rosalie Cannelle, la marchande d'épices: Rosalie Cannelle, the spice seller in Hautefond, have you met her? We swap news by letter. She sends me ten pieces, I send her one. But mine comes from the bottom of the sea: it's worth ten. She doesn't agree. She sent me eleven pieces of news to prove it.
textes.Rosalie Gomme, la jardinière, croit que: Rosalie Gomme, the gardener, thinks the pot of green (no. 2) rolled all the way to the Hollow Stump, the oldest stump on the island, deep in the Hatching Wood. She doesn't dare go there: a big owl lives there, and it gives her funny looks.
Rosalie has some lovely sea bream this morning.
textes.Rosalie chante en vidant le poisson, tou: Rosalie sings while she guts the fish, every morning, at her stall. One day, she lost her voice. My bouillabaisse was… fine. Fine! Mine! I ran to bring her honey and lemon. The next day she was singing, and so was my soup. Don't ask me to explain. Cooking isn't a science.
textes.Rosalie divise par deux toutes mes taill: Rosalie halves the size of all my fish. She's right, the rascal. I owe her a big one, and she knows it.
textes.Rosalie est à la lisière du Bois des Hac: Rosalie is at the edge of the Hatching Wood, Grandpa Augustin near the Palette.
textes.Rosalie fait pousser les fleurs, je les: Rosalie grows the flowers, I sell them. We're like the pot and the flower. Well, I don't know which of us is the pot.
textes.Rosalie fait pousser tout ce qu'elle tou: Rosalie makes everything she touches grow. I erase. She mends everything I rub out. She's a very good daughter, and a very good gardener.
textes.Rosalie m'a dit bonjour le premier jour,: Rosalie said hello to me on the first day, when nobody else would. She gave me an apple and asked me forty questions. I adore her. I'll never tell her everything. But she guesses it all anyway.
textes.Rosalie me donnait les têtes de sardines: Rosalie used to give me the sardine heads. I'd eat them in front of everyone, very slowly. For elegance.
textes.Rosalie raconte des potins à mes pommes: Rosalie tells gossip to my apples while we pick. Tuesday's apples are the sweetest of the week. I've never told her. She surely knows anyway.
textes.Rosalie rit si fort que ma machine se ta: Rosalie laughs so loud my machine goes quiet out of respect. She knows everything about everyone, and only says nice things. She's wrong about the recipe. But she's right about everything else.
textes.Rosalie vend le meilleur poisson du port: Rosalie sells the best fish in the harbour and repeats everything she sees. The fish, I buy. The rest, I leave to her.
textes.Rosalie vend mes fraises au Grand Marché: Rosalie sells my strawberries at the Great Market in Hautefond. She sells them all in one morning. She writes me three letters a week, full of gossip. I don't know anyone down there, but I know everything about everybody. It's very strange. And very funny.
textes.Rosalie vient chercher mes pommes tous l: Rosalie comes for my apples every Tuesday. She tells them the market gossip while I pick them. Tuesday apples are the sweetest. I think it's the gossip.
textes.Rosalie, Brioche vient avec moi !: Rosalie, Brioche is coming with me!
textes.Rosalie, au marché, sait tout avant tout: Rosalie, at the market, knows everything before everyone else. She knew I was going to make a speech before I knew it myself. I suspect my moustache of gossiping.
textes.Rosalie, c'est la cannelle de la semaine: Rosalie, is this last week's cinnamon? It smells stronger.
textes.Rosalie, c'est ma poissonnière, ma chant: Rosalie is my fishmonger, my singer, and the biggest sulker in Port-Azur. Her voice puts heart into my soup. Her day-old sea bream, a lot less.
textes.Rosalie, c'est à qui, ce chat roux sur l: Rosalie, whose is that ginger cat on the roof?
textes.Rosalie, la marchande d'épices d'en haut: Rosalie, the spice seller up top, wrote to me: she wants to sell my glowing mushrooms at the Great Market. I replied that they're not for selling, they're for looking at. She replied: “Then I'll sell tickets to look at them.” That woman is a genius.
textes.Rosalie, la poissonnière. Poisson excell: Rosalie, the fishmonger. Excellent fish, regrettable tongue. She undermines authority every day, out loud, in front of the whole harbour.
textes.Rosalie, ma belle ! Ce soir, la bouillab: Rosalie, my beauty! Tonight, the bouillabaisse is in your honour!
textes.Rosalie, tu as arrosé ?: Rosalie, have you done the watering?
textes.Rosalie, tu me gardes des pivoines ?: Rosalie, will you keep some peonies for me?
textes.Rosalie, voilà le pot de vert ! Le hibou: Rosalie, here's the pot of green! The owl didn't say a thing.
textes.Rosalie, vous cherchez quelque chose dan: Rosalie, are you looking for something in the wood?
textes.Rosalie, à l'étal d'à côté, est la seule: Rosalie, at the next stall, is the only one who said hello to me on my first day. She also gave me an apple and asked forty questions. I answered three. She guessed the other thirty-seven.
textes.Rose a mis ma rose dans un vase, « en at: Rose put my rose in a vase, “in the meantime”. I like a florist waiting with me. She believes in happy endings, like Léa.
textes.Rose est une gentille fille, qui vend sa: Rose is a sweet girl, who sells her lavender to everyone. Which is exactly what complicates my investigation.
textes.Rose est une vraie fleuriste. Elle parle: Rose is a real florist. She talks to her bougainvillea, and it doesn't listen to her. Mine doesn't either. We understood each other straight away.
textes.Rose, c'est mon amie, ma jardinière et m: Rose is my friend, my gardener and my best supplier. Without her lavender, my herbal teas would be nothing but hot water.
textes.Rose, ma voisine. Ses bougainvilliers on: Rose, my neighbour. Her bougainvillea has invaded my roof, my ukulele invades her nights. We're even. Well, she says we're not.
textes.Rosette ! Gardez-moi la une !: Rosette! Save me the front page!
textes.Rosette a fait de mes toits une rubrique: Rosette made my roofs into a regular column! “Roof of the Week.” She understands science, she does. Well, she understands headlines. It's almost the same thing.
textes.Rosette a voulu faire son interview à cô: Rosette wanted to do her interview next to the big coil. A million volts. In the middle of her second question, her pencil melted, and her hair stood straight up. It stayed like that for three days. She wrote the article anyway, with a spare pencil. Since then, rubber boots are compulsory in the lab.
textes.Rosette a voulu interviewer Achille au p: Rosette tried to interview Achille through a megaphone, from the airfield roof. Eight days he's been circling up there, alone, with a boiler on his back, and her first question was: “Are you hungry?” He said yes. It made the front page. I could have told her he was hungry.
textes.Rosette achète ses plumes de corbeau che: Rosette buys her crow feathers from me, a dozen a month. She says they write faster than the others. I pick them out for her one by one, the blackest ones, and I sell them to her at cost. Business is tenderness with a cash register.
textes.Rosette est curieuse comme un courant d': Rosette is as curious as a draught, and just as hard to stop. She drops by the lab every afternoon. I like her, with her boots.
textes.Rosette est la meilleure gazetière de l': Rosette is the best gazette-writer on the island, and my advert appears in every issue. She writes with my crow feathers. Between you and me, she's practically family.
textes.Rosette fait de mon frère la plaisanteri: Rosette has made my brother the morning joke. “Still in flight”, the way you'd say “cloudy”. I read it anyway. To check.
textes.Rosette guette mes sacs de courrier comm: Rosette lies in wait for my mailbags like a seagull lies in wait for a trawler. And she prints my delays on the front page. She drives me up the wall. I read her Gazette every morning.
Rosette. The bag hasn't landed yet.
textes.Rou ? Rou. Rouuu. (C'est très profond, e: Coo? Coo. Cooo. (It's very deep, in pigeon.)
textes.Rou-rou. Je crois qu'il veut redevenir c: Coo-coo. I think he wants to be a hat again.
textes.Roucou ! Tu sais pas la dernière ? Tapag: Coo-roo! Have you heard the latest? Tapage told a TRUE story! Nobody believed it.
textes.Roucou-roucou. Ça veut dire « bonjour »: Coo-roo, coo-roo. It means “hello” and “got any bread?”. Handy, two words in one.
textes.Roucou… Je ne dis rien, mais Mademoisell: Coo-roo… I'm not saying anything, but Mademoiselle Prune has a cardboard moustache in her bag. I'm not saying anything.
Red! Ah, the hardest one to paint. An adventurous red, afraid of nothing. For you, I'll have to outdo myself.
textes.Rouge ! Ha ! Près de la cascade, la mer: Red! Ha! Near the waterfall, the sea smells of bolognese. The fish round here all taste a bit of garlic. Pesto loves them.
textes.Rouge comme mon fer ! J'ai forgé six épé: Red-hot as my iron! I forged six swords, mended three shields, and Titouan only burnt one apron. A good day.
textes.Rouge, jaune, bleu et vert, avec une lon: Red, yellow, blue and green, with a long knotted tail. It belongs to little Théo.
textes.Rouge… Oui. C'est ce qu'il veut qu'on vo: Red… Yes. That's what it wants us to see. But look closely in the evening: there's purple, orange, and even a little green.
textes.Rouille ! Une annonce pour le concert ?: Rouille! An announcement for the gig?
textes.Rouille ? Alors c'est la maison qui offr: Rouille? Then it's on the house. (She sets a lemonade in front of you with a rat-shaped straw.) Sirène's lemonade, lemon, mint and bubbles. Nothing that goes to your head: just enough to dance until midnight. There's a concert in the evening. Come. And bring your ears, Larsen takes care of the rest.
textes.Rouille a la voix la plus immense que j': Rouille has the most enormous voice I've ever heard. She always leaves the door of the Hall ajar. I think it's for me. I don't dare ask her.
textes.Rouille a la voix la plus puissante de l: Rouille has the most powerful voice on the island. More powerful than my aerial. I found out the day she broke my mic sounding an alert.
textes.Rouille a mille idées par minute et zéro: Rouille has a thousand ideas a minute and zero notebooks. I've got a notebook. Together, we've organised every Great Boucan. She shouts, I take notes.
textes.Rouille a un trac énorme avant les conce: Rouille gets terrible stage fright before gigs. So I stand behind her and do a tiny little “kia” in her ear. She laughs, and her voice comes back. I do it every night. Even the nights she isn't scared. Especially those nights.
textes.Rouille est arrivée à douze ans avec une: Rouille arrived at twelve with a voice bigger than she was. Today, she carries the whole Boucan on her shoulders. I just helped her stand up straight.
textes.Rouille hurle dans le micro : « UN BATTE: Rouille screams into the mic: “A DRUMMER! WE'VE GOT A DRUMMER!” The pit screams with her.
textes.Rouille m'a traîné dans la cale du Cargo: Rouille dragged me down into the Freighter's hold with Mouette. There were rats everywhere. I played. They sat down. Rouille asked if we should keep the name Bilge Rats. I said: “We keep the name.” Rouille cried. I think it was because of the sentence. It was a long one.
textes.Rouille m'a trouvée sur un quai avec un: Rouille found me on a quay with a broom and told me I had rhythm. Nobody had ever told me I had anything. I'd follow her to the ends of the earth. Screeching.
textes.Rouille m'envoie te dire bonjour !: Rouille sent me to say hello!
textes.Rouille parle pour nous deux. Elle crie: Rouille talks for both of us. She shouts for three. Without her, I'd still be playing in a hold. For rats.
textes.Rouille pointe le doigt vers toi : « LUI: Rouille points at you: “HIM! HE GETS IT!” The pit cheers for you!
textes.Rouille t'envoie ? Alors tu fais partie: Rouille sent you? Then you're part of the family! Here, have a taste. (He holds out his giant ladle, full of soup.) No, not the whole ladle. Just a sip. … There. Now you know the taste of Boucan. Come back whenever you like: here, you pay what you can. Even zero. Especially if you're hungry.
textes.Rouille, la chanteuse des Rats de Cale,: Rouille, the singer of the Bilge Rats, wants you to get to know Port-Boucan. To start with: say hello to Lentille at the Pay-What-You-Can Canteen, to Rustine at the bike workshop and to Sirène at the Howling Hall bar.
textes.Rouille, pourquoi tout le monde fait cet: Rouille, why the long faces everywhere?
textes.Rouille, tu peux me présenter un peu la: Rouille, could you show me around town a bit?
textes.Rouleau quatre cent douze, Coralin. On a: Scroll four hundred and twelve, Coralin. We're nearing the end.
textes.Rouvrir la ligne des hautes terres. Un s: To reopen the highlands line. Just one Sunday, no more. With the coffee machine at the head of the train, the Bielle puffing out steam, and a steaming cup at every window. The shepherds on the platforms. And me pulling the whistle as we pull into the station. For real, this time.
textes.Roux ? Un grand dadais de renard qui cue: Roux? A great lump of a fox who picks herbs in his sleep, apparently. He's made me laugh since we were five. It's exhausting. It's irreplaceable. Don't repeat the second word to him.
textes.Roux ? Un renard qui vend contre des piè: Roux? A fox who sells for coins on MY market! An insult to tradition. But a rival worthy of me, my friend: foxes and tanukis, it's the oldest quarrel in the forest.
textes.Roux dit que mon étoile tombée était une: Roux says my fallen star was a firefly who'd had too much tea. It's not funny. He plays the flute like nobody else. That's true. I won't tell him.
textes.Roux est encore rentré avec des feuilles: Roux came home with leaves in his tail again. He says he was gathering. I say he was sleeping under a tree.
textes.Roux joue de la flûte pendant que je dan: Roux plays the flute while I dance. He's the only one who can make me laugh in the middle of a step, and the only one I ask for advice. He answers with a joke, then with good advice.
textes.Roux raconte à tout le village que mon é: Roux tells the whole village that my star that fell into the big pond was “a firefly who'd had too much moon tea”. The children laugh. Fireflies don't fall, Roux. They don't drink tea either. I wrote him a poem to explain. He set it to music. That's worse.
textes.Roux, c'est le renard qui m'a appris les: Roux is the fox who taught me the rhythms of Tazira. Boom, boom-boom! Without him, I'd still be going boom, boom, boom. Like Bourru, but faster.
textes.Royalement bien. La bière est fraîche, l: Royally well. The fizz is cold, the forges are burning, the golems… hmm. Almost well.
textes.Royaume des fées : chez une fée: Fairy kingdom: at a fairy's home
textes.Rrriiiii ! Le larsen siffle encore. Les: Eeeeeee! The feedback squeals again. The Rainville crows fly off, offended.
textes.Rrrrrrrr… Le son est si grave qu'on le s: Rrrrrrrr… The sound is so low you feel it more than you hear it. A bit like a giant cat asleep under the whole City.
Rrrrrr… pffff… (He's asleep. Deeply. There's moss on his shoulder.)
textes.Rrrr… non, pas les cailloux… rrrr…: Rrrr… no, not the pebbles… rrrr…
textes.Rubis sur l'ongle ! Ha ! Toi, tu peux t': Right on the nail! Ha! You can sit wherever you like, sweetie. Your seat is warm. And if you meet a captain with a limp, set him an example.
textes.Rubis, pièces d'or… et j'achète tout ce: Rubies, gold coins… and I buy anything that sparkles. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Rubrique « Ça se répare » avec Rustine :: The “Fix It” corner with Rustine: today, how to change an inner tube. (A long hiss is heard.) … Rustine answered by hissing. It was very clear.
textes.Rumeur : un batteur génial se cache dans: Rumour: a brilliant drummer is hiding in town. Rumour number two: he's the villain's son. Rumour number three: coo-roo.
textes.Rumeur du jour : Lentille aurait mis du: Today's rumour: Lentille may have put honey in the soup. Tomorrow's rumour: we'll get honey soup. Coo-roo!
textes.Rumeur. Définition : information non vér: Rumour. Definition: unverified information. Unverified information available: “Gloubi puts stars in the jelly.” Verification impossible: Gloubi refuses to let me taste it. I do not have a mouth.
textes.Rustine m'a donné la première roue de Br: Rustine gave me Brindezingue's first wheel in exchange for a bag of bike chains. She asked me why a dragon needed wheels. I said: “For the day he wants to leave.” The next day, she brought me the second one. Without asking anything. That makes eleven. She keeps going.
textes.Rustine me donne des roues, je lui donne: Rustine gives me wheels, I give her parts. My dragon has eleven wheels thanks to her. She whistles as she works. My sculptures love listening to her.
textes.Rustine n'a plus de pièces de vélo : les: Rustine has run out of bike parts: Lisse's robots searched the Scrapyard to build themselves arms. There are three batches of parts left, hidden in the Scrapyard, to the south-east.
textes.Rustine siffle, je tape. On ne se dit pr: Rustine whistles, I hammer. We hardly say a thing to each other, and we say everything. She fixes what rolls, I fix what stands up. Together, we keep the house moving.
textes.Rustine. Ta clé de 12 est sur mon établi: Rustine. Your 12 mm spanner is on my workbench.
textes.RÈGLEMENT DU DONJON\nDES MILLE MARCHES\n:
RULES OF THE DUNGEON
OF A THOUSAND STEPS

1. Do not feed the slimes (they grow).
2. Do not pet the frogs (they swallow).
3. A chest that smiles is not a chest.
4. The blue crystals bring you back up here. The falls do not.

— Odon, keeper and step counter
textes.Règlement de la station, article un : l': Station regulations, article one: the assistant carries the umbrella. Article two: the assistant does not argue with article one. She wrote the regulations herself. I had them framed.
textes.Réclamer la dette à Gontran Lestrange, d: Claim the debt from Gontran Lestrange, known as Jambe-de-Bois (on the Veuve Écarlate by day; at the Shark's Tooth in the evening)
textes.Récolter deux rayons de miel aux ruches: Gather two honeycombs from the fire bees' hives, in the Ash Wood (south-east of the city)
textes.Réconcilier Mamie Tournesol et Mère Aver: Make peace between Granny Sunflower and Mother Downpour
textes.Réconcilier le Grand Spaghetti Volant av: Reconcile the Great Flying Spaghetti with its followers
textes.Récupérer l'antenne de Radio Boucan (tou: Get back the Radio Boucan antenna (at the very top of the painted water tower, east of the town)
textes.Récupérer l'appareil photo de Gérard au: Get Gérard's camera back from the lookout (at the top of the hill path)
textes.Réparer le Léviathan, le remettre à l'ea: Fix the Léviathan, put her back in the water, and set sail with everyone on board. Everyone! Fañch and his boat on the deck, Gwenola and her stove, and my grandad right at the top of the crow's nest, like before. I'll carry him, if I have to.
textes.Répondre aux trois questions du Sphinx (: Answer the Sphinx's three questions (on the plateau of Ra, across the river, south of Per-Hâpy)
textes.Réponds franchement, rival : est-ce que: Answer honestly, rival: do you consider me your rival?
textes.Réponds-moi sérieusement, {surnom} : cro: Answer me seriously, {surnom}: do you believe the sun will rise tomorrow?
textes.Réponse de fée ! Prudente, maligne, et q: A fairy's answer! Cautious, clever, and says nothing at all. I'll write it in my big book, with your name beside it.
textes.Réponse réglementaire. Article quatre :: A by-the-book answer. Article four: “Assess before running.” I wrote it after the third cloud alert. You'd make a good sergeant.
textes.Répète ça, et je te fais manger ta casqu: Say that again and I'll make you eat your cap, you flea-bag!
textes.Répète ça, et on n'est plus amis. Enfin,: Say that again, and we're not friends anymore. Well, we weren't, but we'll be even less so.
textes.Répète-le plus fort, qu'on l'entende jus: Say it louder, so they can hear it all the way to Octave's kapok tree.
textes.Résoudre l'énigme des serpents: Solve the riddle of the snakes
textes.Réunir un jour les trois jardinières dan: To bring the three gardeners together one day, in a single garden: Flora, Bertille and me. To plant a strawberry from the Clouds, a mushroom from the Strata and a samphire from the Dome together, in the same planter, and see what grows. Maybe nothing. Maybe something nobody has ever seen. A plant of the three worlds. I'd call it “Patience”.
textes.Réunir un jour, autour de la Fontaine de: To bring together one day, around the Bubble Fountain, the four councils of the Column, and the Fronde with them: Burgomaster Hector, Céleste Altaïr, Dean Agathe, Brasero, and me. A Council of the Four Worlds. Brasero will want a fire, Hector a speech, Agathe silence. We shall have all three. And we'll leave one chair empty, for Atlantis, for the day it comes.
textes.Réunir une dernière fois les trois conte: To bring together the three storytellers of the big island one last time, Ba Sidi, Corentin and me, at the Moon Circle. Now that the Zéphyr links the towns, no more excuses! A whole night of stories…
textes.Réussir le rose. Le rose du port, le soi: To get the pink right. The pink of the port in the evening, when the lighthouse comes on. Just once. After that, I could paint notaries for the rest of my life, no problem.
textes.Réussir une expérience exactement comme: To get one experiment to work exactly as planned. Just one. To see what it feels like. Then to botch it on purpose the next time, because the botched ones are still much more interesting.
textes.Réveiller les esprits de la forêt et ouv: Wake the forest spirits and open the root gate
textes.Réveiller les trois runes de la Crypte a: Wake the three runes of the Rune Crypt with the light spell (key 5 then V; in VR, left trigger): the crypt is above the garden, on the path to the Twisted Wood
textes.Révérend ! Il danse ! Il m'a touché l'ép: Reverend! He's dancing! He touched my shoulder!
textes.Révérend, pourquoi le Grand Spaghetti a-: Reverend, why does the Great Spaghetti look so sad?
textes.Révérend, voici les pâtes, la sauce et l: Reverend, here are the pasta, the sauce and the Golden Grater.
textes.Rêveuse. Ce matin, j'ai vu une constella: Dreamy. This morning I saw a constellation in my tea bowl. It was shaped like a biscuit. I called it “the Great Glutton”. Then I drank it.
textes.Rêveuse. Comme toujours. Ce matin, j'ai: Dreamy. As always. This morning I saw a cloud shaped exactly like a cloud. It was very restful.
textes.Rêveuse. J'ai passé la matinée à écouter: Dreamy. I spent the morning listening to the waterfall. It told me about the rain up top: on the slate roofs, in the Orchards, on a lady's hat at the market. All of Hautefond's water ends up here. With its stories.
textes.Rêveuse. La mer était couleur de saphir: Dreamy. The sea was sapphire-coloured this morning.
textes.Rêveuse. Le jour, je suis rêveuse. La nu: Dreamy. By day, I'm dreamy. By night, I'm wide awake.
textes.Rúmil ! Tu es en retard. Mes lanternes o: Rúmil! You're late. My lanterns are hungry.
textes.Rúmil dit que la lumière vient mieux qua: Rúmil says light comes more easily when someone sings. So every morning at dawn, I sing for his nets. He never says thank you. He leaves me the first ray.
textes.Rúmil est né trois minutes avant moi, et: Rúmil was born three minutes before me, and he reminds me every morning. He fishes the light, I keep it. Without him, my lanterns would be empty. Without me, he'd be asleep.
textes.Rúmil pêche la lumière à l'aube, comme s: Rúmil fishes for light at dawn, like his grandfather, like I saw it done nine centuries ago. It's a dying trade. He doesn't let it die: he listens.
textes.Rúmil vient au cercle des contes avec se: Rúmil comes to the storytelling circle with his nets to mend. He never looks up, he never asks a question, and he remembers everything, word for word. One day I got a name wrong in a six-hundred-year-old story. He just coughed. I corrected myself.
S to go down, W to go back up.
textes.S'il dort ? Ha ! Il dort tout le temps à: If he's asleep? Ha! He sleeps all the time at school! With me. Come to the calmecac, you can pet us both.
If he leaves the clouds alone.
textes.S'il vous plaît, Berthe ! Il est midi, c: Yes please, Berthe! It's noon, it's time.
textes.S'il vous plaît, Berthe. Pas comme la si: Yes please, Berthe. Not like hers.
textes.S'il y a de l'orage cette nuit, je mets: If there's a storm tonight, I'll put my hat on. I've already got it on.
textes.S'il y avait du nouveau, tu y mettrais u: If there were, you'd put a question mark on it.
textes.S'inscrire à la Guilde des Aventuriers: Sign up at the Adventurers' Guild
textes.SALUT ! Moi, c'est Bourrasque, batteuse: HI! I'm Bourrasque, drummer of the Gutters! I hit HARD! Not people, eh, drums! Want to hear a drum roll? TRRRRRRRA-BOOM!
textes.SALUT ! … PARDON. Salut. JE M'APPELLE LA: HI! … SORRY. Hi. MY NAME'S LARSEN! … Sorry. Larsen. Sound engineer. I talk a bit loud. It's the job. And the headphones. And maybe a bit of me.
textes.SARDIIIIINES ! DORAAAADES ! … Oh, pardon: SARDIIIIINES! SEA BREEEEAM! … Oh, sorry, did I scare you? Force of habit. Saïd, the fish auction crier. They can hear me all the way to the Skala. On windy days, all the way to the desert.
textes.SARDINE ! (Le chien saute sur Tornade, l: SARDINE! (The dog leaps at Tornade, licks his whole face, then comes back to sit at your feet. Tornade looks at him, then at you, and sniffs.) ... He doesn't want to leave you, does he. I can see that. He chose you. (He rubs his eyes with his fist.) All right. You can keep him with you. But take good care of him, okay! He likes chew bones, he bites robots, and sometimes he brings back coins. Nobody knows where he finds them. Here, his chew bones. And bring him back to the skatepark once in a while. Promise?
textes.SARDINE ! Tu l'as retrouvé ! (Il serre l: SARDINE! You found him! (He hugs the dog really tight.) … He looks at you all the time, huh. He's chosen you. It's OK. But you bring him back to the skatepark sometimes.
textes.SATURNE — elle porte des anneaux. Comète: SATURN — it wears rings. Comète asked if she could race in them. The Council's answer: no.
textes.SIRÈNE SERT LES MEILLEURES LIMONADES DE: SIRÈNE SERVES THE BEST LEMONADE IN THE ARCHIPELAGO! And a syrup of silence that makes me whisper. I don't know how she does it. It's camomile magic.
textes.SORTIE DU PERSONNEL — TOURNIQUET\nformul:
STAFF EXIT — TURNSTILE
stamped forms required
textes.SPLOOOSH ! Le Mont Bolognaise crache sa: SPLOOOSH! Mount Bolognese spits out its sauce! Big red drops fly very high… and fall all over its slopes.
textes.SPLOTCH ! Une grosse goutte de sauce t'e: SPLOTCH! A big drop of sauce landed right next to you… You're splattered from head to toe. (It smells delicious.)
textes.STOP ! Toi… toi quoi ? Toi pas carré. To: STOP! You… you what? You not square. You all SMOOTH! Not one single pixel! Ougha never see thing like you. Where you come from? From sky? From big water? From belly of volcano?
textes.STOP ! … (Il se calme.) Pardon. Le trois: STOP! … (He calms down.) Sorry. Around here, we don't say three too loudly. The volcano is listening.
textes.Sa boussole d'argent, je la lui ai gagné: His silver compass, I won it from him at the big table: my three sixes against his three fives. He set it down in front of me like burying a friend. Since then, I wear it round my neck, and every time he passes, I open it and show him where north is. He never laughs. That's what makes me laugh.
textes.Sa cabane du bord de plage s'est effondr: His beach hut collapsed during one of Mistral's big tracks. I heard about it from Clou, who came home covered in sand. I sent him a bag of twenty nails, by Clou. He got eleven. Clou takes his commission.
textes.Sa carapace arrête tout ! Un vent assez: Its shell stops everything! A strong enough wind might knock it over…
textes.Sa chaîne de gouverneur, celle qu'il por: His governor's chain, the one he wears on speech days, I'm the one who sold it to him. It's travelled a lot: it belonged to a real governor, then to a pirate, then to a parrot, I think. He paid me with a decree naming me “Purveyor to the City”. I framed it. It's worth nothing. It's magnificent.
textes.Sa cuirasse d'or est trop dure. Ses yeux: Its golden armor is too hard. Its eyes, though, fear fire…
textes.Sa flûte a une note de plus que les autr: His flute has one note more than the others, from the eighth hole, which Gland made while he was teething. Roux calls it “the squirrel note”. That's the one I spin on, in the middle of the dance. One evening he played it too early on purpose: I spun into thin air. He laughed so hard he missed the next one.
textes.Sa grand-mère Salicorne, je l'ai bien co: I knew her grandmother Salicorne well. I wrote: “Day 1: a seaweed cracker, dreadful, eaten by all.” Marée came to scratch out the word “dreadful” herself. I sat on the scroll. An hour like that. In the end, I added “weeping with joy”. She accepted.
textes.Sa grand-mère, Nanwë, était la meilleure: Her grandmother, Nanwë, was the best herbalist I've ever known. When she fell asleep beneath the Mother Tree, Aëlwen opened the shop the very next day, her eyes red. I went and sat in a corner and talked nonsense all day. She didn't laugh. But she didn't close.
textes.Sa grenouille a sauté dans ma soupe. J'a: Her frog jumped into my soup. I stepped back. One step. Just one. Ever since, the whole village says I'm scared of frogs. I'm not scared of frogs. I'm scared of what Nimiel does with them.
textes.Sa jambe, je l'ai taillée dans le grand: His leg, I carved it out of my own ship's mainmast, with the saw I also used for firewood. Island oak. Three days' work. I engraved a little star under the knee, as a signature. He's never seen it: he never looks at his leg. He bangs it on the deck when he's angry. Which is to say, often.
textes.Sa lame s'est plantée dans les dalles !: His blade is stuck in the flagstones! Strike now!
textes.Sa mère lave les chemises des trois équi: His mother washes the shirts of all three crews, on the stones by the well. When I took him on as cabin boy, she looked at me for a long time, then she said: “Give him back to me on Sundays, with all his fingers.” So every Sunday, I count. Ten. I've never told anyone, but I count mine too.
textes.Sa peau est très épaisse… Quand il RUGIT: Its skin is very thick… When it ROARS, it's going to charge: dodge, and let it smash into the rock of the hollow!
textes.Sa potion pour faire lever la pâte : « t: His potion to make dough rise: “three drops”, he'd written. I read “three spoonfuls”. He writes like a cat walking through ink! The dough rose up to my kitchen ceiling. I served a pie as tall as a stool at the Crystal Festival. Everyone had seconds. I won't tell him.
textes.Sa première jarre est arrivée avec le ma: His first jar arrived with Tochtli the merchant. Blue, with two big round eyes staring at me. Mérit thought it was a demon. I turned it to face the wall, in the workshop. In the evening, I turned it back round: it looked lonely. I sent him a scarab in return. To say it was good. I don't know if he understood.
textes.Sa première lame, il me l'a apportée fie: He brought me his first blade, proud as a rooster. I looked at it, weighed it, and put it back in the fire. Melted. Without a word. He didn't say anything either. The next day, he forged another, better one. That's how you learn. That's how my father taught me.
textes.Sa première potion contre la foudre m'a: His first potion against lightning turned me completely blue for a day. The lightning got through anyway. Monsieur Aubin wrote in his notebook: “Lightning doesn't distinguish between colours.” Then he drank the last drop of the potion, to check. We were both blue. The children followed us shouting “the sky! the sky!”.
textes.Sa première semaine, il arrive à la crié: His first week, he turns up at the auction with his nose all red: he'd just sniffed Lalla Aïcha's pepper. I call out a lot of sardines, and he goes: “ATCHOO!” Me: “SOLD TO THE PIRATE!” He tries to explain, sneezes again. Second lot. Forty kilos. He left with two crates and a handkerchief. The best sale of my career.
textes.Sa première semaine, je lui ai montré le: Her first week, I showed her hospital corners. You pull, you fold, you tuck: the sheet must sit like a letter in its envelope. She did it thirty times while telling me the life story of the guests in room nine. By the thirtieth bed, the corners were perfect. So was the life story of the guests in nine, incidentally.
textes.Sa première vigie tout seul. J'étais en: His first watch alone. I was down below. I hear: “Alarm! Alarm! Something white, very fast!” I climb back up. Eighty steps. It was Bondi, training. I said: “A fast rabbit is not an alarm.” He answered: “For a runner, it is.” … He's not wrong. Don't tell him.
textes.Sage ! Demande-moi, alors. C'est mon mét: Wise! Ask me, then. That's my job. And if I don't know, I ask the hammer. It always knows.
Wise decision. He never gives anything back.
textes.Sage décision. La dernière fois, j'ai pe: Wise decision. Last time, I lost my eyebrows. They grew back, but upside down.
textes.Sage réponse ! La moitié de mes conseils: Wise answer! Half my advice is excellent. The other half too, but I apply it badly. Sort it out, sort it out.
textes.Sage. Très sage. J'ai passé quatre cents: Wise. Very wise. I've spent four hundred years knowing, and I sleep worse than Hilda's goats.
textes.Sage. Très sage. Je vous respecte, et je: Wise. Very wise. I respect you, and I envy you a little: you still have both your eyebrows. Keep them.
textes.Sage. Très sage. Plus sage que nous deux: Wise. Very wise. Wiser than the two of us put together, which isn't hard.
textes.Sage. Très sage. Si tout le monde était: Wise. Very wise. If everyone were like you, I'd sleep at night. Thank you.
textes.Salam ! Ahmed. Ma barque, c'est la Zahra: Salam! Ahmed. My boat is the Zahra, the blue one with the eye painted on the bow. All the boats are blue, but mine is the bluest.
textes.Salam, frère. Lhoucine. Mon instrument,: Salam, brother. Lhoucine. My instrument is the guembri: three strings, a camel skin, and the whole desert night inside. Tonight, come to the square.
textes.Salam. Ali, charpentier. Toutes les barq: Salam. Ali, carpenter. Every blue boat in Tazira came out of my hands. Or my father's. But mostly mine.
textes.Salomé ! Combien tu l'as vendu, mon dern: Salomé! How much did you sell my last sabre for?
textes.Salomé m'a proposé de me vendre une clé: Salomé offered to sell me a key for the Gate of the Four Seals. A key! For a gate with seals! She already sold me an ancient map, once. I don't want to talk about it.
textes.Salomé m'achète mes perles. Elle me paie: Salomé buys my pearls. She pays me a third of what they're worth, and smiles at me like she's giving me a present. I don't like haggling. She knows it.
textes.Salomé revend mes sabres aux caravaniers: Salomé resells my sabres to the caravanners for twice what I charge her. I know it, she knows I know it. But she brings me ore cheaper than anyone. We're square, I reckon.
textes.Salomé récupère mes chutes de toile, en: Salomé collects my canvas offcuts, turns them into “authentic sailor's bags” and resells them for three times the price. She'd sell the wind if you could put it in a bag. She's tried.
textes.Salomé vend des « baumes du désert » qui: Salomé sells “desert balms” that cure everything. I tried one: goat fat and cinnamon. It doesn't cure anything, but it smells nice. And that, I don't like.
textes.Salomé vend n'importe quoi à n'importe q: Salomé sells anything to anyone. Yesterday she sold a leaky bucket to a seagull.
Salomé, from the Hold Market, in Carène. A thief! She wants my saffron for the price of a stone, I sell it to her for the price of gold. We adore each other.
textes.Salomé, ton baume, c'est encore de la gr: Salomé, is your balm goat fat again?
Salomé. No. I'm not buying a key.
textes.Salomé. Tes sacs d'algues, ce soir, tu l: Salomé. Your seaweed sacks. Tonight, you put them away.
textes.Saluer Edmond, à la réception du Grand H: Greet Edmond at the Grand Hotel reception
textes.Saluer Lentille à la Cantine à prix libr: Say hello to Lentille at the Pay-What-You-Can Canteen (on the ground floor of the Cannery, the big brick factory covered in murals, west of the Howling Hall)
textes.Saluer Odette à la capitainerie, sur le: Greet Odette at the harbour master's office, on the quay
textes.Saluer Rustine à l'atelier vélo (à la Fi: Say hello to Rustine at the bike workshop (in the Spinning Mill, the long brick shed with saw-tooth roofs, south of the Pallet Square)
textes.Saluer Sirène au bar de la Halle Hurlant: Say hello to Sirène at the Howling Hall bar (the old forge hall with the great glass roof, north-east of the Pallet Square)
textes.Saluer Toni au Perroquet Bleu: Greet Toni at Le Perroquet Bleu
textes.Salut ! Attention, je danse en faisant d: Hi! Careful, I dance with big arm movements, I've already knocked over two glasses and a Bastien.
textes.Salut ! Attention, je viens de lancer un: Hi! Careful, I've just cast a spell. I don't know which one yet. We'll see.
textes.Salut ! Attention, ne marche pas sur le: Hi! Careful, don't step on the engine: it's asleep. Ionie, mechanic at the Spaceport! I repair saucers, shuttles, and anything that flies, floats or goes “vroom”. Do you have a flying machine? A real one? With propellers? Show me! I love propellers! Heavy-Feet build such… brave machines.
textes.Salut ! Attention, peinture fraîche ! Mo: Hi! Careful, wet paint! I'm Bigoudi. I fix the camp's buses and I paint them. Flowers, suns, waves… That blue there is barely dry.
textes.Salut ! Basile Pinceau, peintre. En bâti: Hi! Basile Pinceau, painter. Houses, doors, shutters, boats, everything. Well, when there's paint. Since the Downpour, I've been painting with water. It doesn't show much.
textes.Salut ! Bon vent ! C'est pour les cerfs-: Hi! Fair winds! It's meant for kites, but it works for people too.
textes.Salut ! Coquille, timonière de la Morue: Hi! Coquille, helmswoman of the Morue Enragée. I'm the one at the wheel. Well, when Ignace isn't gambling our sloop away at dice.
textes.Salut ! Coyotl, potier. Je fais les jarr: Hi! Coyotl, potter. I make Tlaloc's jars: blue, with his big round eyes and his fangs. We fill them with lake water and offer them to the rain god. He likes being thought of.
textes.Salut ! Dis à Honorine que j'arrive pour: Bye! Tell Honorine I'm coming for soup. She already knows. She always knows. HO HO!
textes.Salut ! Et si tu tombes, dis « même pas: Bye! And if you fall, say “didn't even hurt”. Works every time. Almost.
textes.Salut ! Grisou ! Le prochain champion de: Hi! Grisou! The next Great Race champion! This time, I'm beating Bondi. I can feel it. I can feel it in my paws. My paws can feel it too.
textes.Salut ! Icare Plané, moniteur de planeur: Hi! Icare Plané, gliding instructor! Wait… you've got wings! Yeaaaah! A natural glider! Do you know how to use them? Never mind: I'll teach you to use them safely. Rule number one: into the wind, always. Rule number two: never glide on an empty stomach.
textes.Salut ! Jack, chef roadie. Je monte les: Hi! Jack, head roadie. I put up stages, I run cables, I carry amps. That one there, the Great Stage, I repair it every day. Just in case. A stage should always be ready.
textes.Salut ! Je m'appelle Pépin ! J'ai quatre: Hi! My name's Pépin! I'm ninety years old! … In demon years. In normal years I'm nine. Have you got horns? No? Don't worry, they'll grow!
textes.Salut ! Je suis Clapotis ! Regarde ma fi: Hi! I'm Clapotis! Watch my trick! (He jumps, falls, gets back up.) … I almost landed it! My yellow raincoat is so people can see me in the rain. And when I fall in a puddle.
textes.Salut ! Je suis Kinich ! J'ai attrapé un: Hi! I'm Kinich! I caught a mosquito! It's in my gourd! It's called Xan, like the Twins' mosquito! Want to see it? No, you can't, it would fly away.
textes.Salut ! Je suis Pilli ! Et lui c'est Tla: Hi! I'm Pilli! And this is Tlaco, my dog! He hasn't got any fur! That's normal! He's a xolo! He's all warm, touch him! … Actually, don't touch, he bites a bit.
textes.Salut ! Je suis l'apprenti d'Augustin. I: Hi! I'm Augustin's apprentice. He's outside, talking to the wind. They've got things to say to each other.
textes.Salut ! Je suis l'apprenti de Margot. El: Hi! I'm Margot's apprentice. She's outside on the rocks: she's talking to the seal.
Hi! I'm Mathilde's apprentice. I look after the fire: it's the most important job. Well, that's what she tells me so I don't get bored.
textes.Salut ! Kevin, maître-nageur. Interdit d: Hi! Kevin, lifeguard. No swimming past the red flag, no running on wet sand, and no being more muscly than me.
textes.Salut ! Le Petit Piston a toussé, ce mat: Hi! The Petit Piston coughed this morning. That's a good sign. Or a very bad one.
textes.Salut ! Lou Grenadier, pilote du Petit P: Hi! Lou Grenadier, pilot of the Little Diver! The yellow bathyscaphe, there, in the Pool. Yes, the one that looks like a duck having a nap. It's the most beautiful submarine in the world. It's also the only one in the Dome. That helps. Want to see the control panel? Don't touch anything. Well, touch with your eyes.
textes.Salut ! Mademoiselle Écrou. Mécanicienne: Hi! Mademoiselle Écrou. Mechanic. I fix everything that floats, everything that rolls and everything that whistles. Right now, I'm trying to wake up the Petit Piston, the tugboat.
textes.Salut ! Moi c'est Nina, j'ai sept ans et: Hi! I'm Nina, I'm seven and a half. What about you? Are you an adventurer? Have you got a sword? Will you show me?
textes.Salut ! Moi, c'est Kira. Je danse sur le: Hi! I'm Kira. I dance on the Boulevard, every evening. Look at my arm: when the music rises, my circuits light up. When it's really good, they change colour. People come to see that. I come to dance.
textes.Salut ! Moi, c'est Tom Taraud, j'ai onze: Hi! I'm Tom Taraud, I'm eleven, and I'm an apprentice at the Great Forge. Are you from up top? Do you know Pimprenelle? No? Never mind. If you see her, tell her: three quick taps. She'll understand. Right, back to tapping.
textes.Salut ! Moi, je rentre en planant. Évide: Bye! Me, I'm gliding home. Obviously.
textes.Salut ! Si tu croises Pimprenelle, dis-l: Hi! If you run into Pimprenelle, tell her to come home for her snack. She won't listen to you. She doesn't listen to me either. HA HA!
textes.Salut ! T'as vu ? T'AS VU ? Je viens de: Hi! Did you see? DID YOU SEE? I just jumped from the ramp all the way to the edge! … OK, I fell at the end. But did you see the start? I'm Tornade. I'm the best skater at the Dry Dock. The only one under eleven. So the best.
textes.Salut ! T'entends ce son ? Viens, viens,: Hi! Hear that beat? Come on, come on, let's dance!
textes.Salut ! T'es nouveau ? Moi c'est Pip, ap: Hi! Are you new? I'm Pip, apprentice, first year! I can make a spark. Look! … Well, it's gone. But I can make it, I promise!
Hi! Tibo, cabin boy of the Murène Noire. Well, cabin boy… I scrub the deck, I peel the potatoes, I chase the captain's cat. Well, the cat that isn't the captain's.
textes.Salut ! Tiens bien la rampe ! C'est l'ar: Hi! Hold on tight to the handrail! That's article one!
textes.Salut ! Toi aussi tu veux des bras comme: Hi! Do you want arms like these too? Come on, ten push-ups with me!
textes.Salut ! Tu es nouveau ? Moi c'est Petit-: Hi! Are you new? I'm Petit-Pierre, cabin boy of the Requin Borgne! I can climb the mast, swab the deck, and tie knots! Not all of them. But loads!
textes.Salut ! Tu flottes, toi aussi ? Non ? Ah: Hi! Are you floating too? No? Ah, Heavyfoots… Well, shall I turn gravity back on, or would you rather everything floated?
textes.Salut ! Tu tombes à pic : notre chanteur: Hi! You're just in time: our singer lost his voice. Literally. He's looked for it everywhere. Want to replace him?
textes.Salut ! Tu veux un bâton lumineux ? Ah,: Hi! Want a glow stick? Oh, I'm all out… Well, dance with your hands, that works too.
textes.Salut ! Tu viens d'en haut ? Du VRAI hau: Hi! You're from up top? The REAL up top? With the sky? Look, look: (He jumps on his board, does a half-turn and lands.) Boing! Didn't even hurt! I'm Ressort, I'm eleven, and I'm the best skater in the Fronde. I'm also the only one. But I'm very good.
textes.Salut d'en haut ! Dis-moi : c'est quoi t: Hello from up here! Tell me: what's your favourite tree?
textes.Salut d'en haut ! … Je descends. (Elle d: Hello from up here! … I'm coming down. (She abseils down from a tree.) Bardane. I climb trees, I protect them, I count them, I hug them. Monsieur Lisse wanted to cut down the big willow on the square. I moved into it. That was three hundred days ago.
textes.Salut salut ! T'as vu, j'ai des lunettes: Hey hey! See, I wear sunglasses at night. It's a look.
textes.Salut à toi, ennemi des chats ! Des nouv: Greetings to you, enemy of cats! Any news of the ginger one? One day, we'll salt him together.
textes.Salut, Barnabé. Tu as bu de l'eau ?: Hi, Barnabé. Have you drunk some water?
textes.Salut, Grégoire ! Combien de bateaux, au: Hello, Grégoire! How many ships today?
textes.Salut, Perlée ! Belle matinée pour un to: Hi, Perlée! Lovely morning for a lap of the Tree!
textes.Salut, Pépin ! Tu cours où, comme ça ?: Hi, Pépin! Where are you running off to?
textes.Salut, chasseur de virus. Ton carnet va: Hi, virus hunter. How's your journal? No surprise pop-ups? No chocolate pony? Perfect. Heh heh.
textes.Salut, collègue du club des ratés ! Touj: Hi, fellow member of the Butterfingers Club! Still messing things up? I am. It's nice to know there are two of us.
textes.Salut, collègue du tournevis ! Vous avez: Hi there, screwdriver colleague! What have you taken apart since last time? Tell me, I want the number of screws.
textes.Salut, frère de clou ! Je regarde toujou: Hi, nail brother! I always look in the soup before tasting it now. You do the same, eh.
textes.Salut, l'ami ! Assieds-toi. Je cherche l: Hey, friend! Sit down. I'm looking for the rest of my song. It's about a sunflower that falls in love with the moon… but never sees her, because it sleeps at night. Want to sing the chorus with me?
textes.Salut, l'ami ! Tom le Violoneux ! Je jou: Hello, friend! Tom the Fiddler! I play at the Crâne Fendu every night. Jigs, laments, and the Song of the King of the Brawl. Do you know it? It hasn't got a final verse yet: nobody has beaten the three champions.
textes.Salut, l'étranger ! Khéty, pêcheur. Le f: Hello, stranger! Khéty, fisherman. The river gives me my fish, I give it my songs. I think it prefers the fish.
textes.Salut, l'étranger ! Roux. Je cueille, je: Hi, stranger! Roux. I gather, I find, I sell: feathers, ropes, little forest trinkets. And in the evening, I play the flute for the moon. She likes it.
textes.Salut, le terrestre ! Tu marches ? Comme: Hi there, landlubber! You walk? How… slow. Welcome!
textes.Salut, membre du club ! Toujours rien di: Hi, club member! Still haven't told anyone? Me neither. We're holding strong.
textes.Salut, membre du club des jamais-gagnant: Hello, member of the Never-Won Club! The day you pass the tenth arch in the lead, I'll strike you off the club. Gladly.
textes.Salut, petit nouveau ! Hilaire, aventuri: Hi there, newbie! Hilaire, adventurer. Rank F. For twelve years. No, don't make that face: it's a very stable rank. Friendly advice: never run at a frog with your mouth open. It'll have its mouth open too.
textes.Salut, toi ! Tu as la tête de quelqu'un: Hi, you! You've got the look of someone who's just crossed the Frondeurs' Bridge: eyes wide open and knees a bit wobbly. Welcome to the Fronde! I'm Bielle. Rails by day, mic by night. And always grease under my nails.
textes.Salut, toi. Fañch. Pêcheur. Ma maison, c: Hi there. Fañch. Fisherman. My house is the upturned boat on the beach, over there. It was shipwrecked before me, so we get on well.
textes.Salut, tonton ! J'ai fini la vigie !: Hi, Uncle! I've finished my watch!
textes.Salut, {surnom} ! Et quand tu passes le: Hi, {surnom}! And when you cross the Frondeurs' Bridge, say hello to the Chasm. It always answers. Three times.
textes.Salut, {surnom} ! Et si quelque chose se: Bye, {surnom}! And if something breaks, don't throw it away: bring it to me!
textes.Salut, {surnom} ! Et si tu as une rime e: Bye, {surnom}! And if you find a rhyme for “-ier”, come back and tell me.
textes.Salut, {surnom} ! Et si tu croises un ro: Hi, {surnom}! And if you run into one of Lisse's robots, tell it we're not for sale.
textes.Salut, {surnom} ! Garde le rythme : un p: Hi, {surnom}! Keep the beat: one foot, then the other. That's the whole secret.
textes.Salut, {surnom} ! Moi, je reste ici. Au: Hi, {surnom}! Me, I'm staying here. On the ground floor. For now.
textes.Salut, {surnom} ! Ne te lave pas trop vi: Bye, {surnom}! Don't wash too quickly, you've got a bit of blue on your nose. It suits you.
textes.Salut, {surnom} ! Si tu montes, tape deu: Bye, {surnom}! If you go up, tap two knocks, then one, on anything. It brings good luck.
textes.Salut, {surnom} ! Tu viens jouer aux dés: Hi, {surnom}! Come to play dice? I've got coins to lose. I mean, to win.
textes.Salut, {surnom}. Et si quelqu'un te rega: Bye, {surnom}. And if anyone looks at you sideways, smile at them face on. It throws them.
Hi, Éclair! Running? I'm running. Lovely day, huh?
textes.Salut. Cette caisse s'appelle… une caiss: Hi. This crate is called… a crate. I'm making an effort, see.
textes.Salut. Copeau, menuisier. Tu vois ce ban: Hi. Copeau, carpenter. See that bench? Pallets. That table? Pallets. That stage, that slide, that bandstand? Pallets. My house? Pallets and love. Mostly pallets.
textes.Salut. Fais attention où tu marches : le: Hi. Watch where you step: the roof leaks. In three places. I have three buckets, there, by the door, but I can't be bothered to get up… Would you put them under the drips?
textes.Salut. Glitch. Oui, comme un bug. Ma vis: Hi. Glitch. Yes, like a bug. My visor shows me the city's networks: the data lines, the traffic lights, the vending machines, the lifts. Everything talks, here. I listen. And when something coughs, I nurse it.
textes.Salut. Je suis Flanelle. Je chante dans: Hey. I'm Flanelle. I sing in the Gutters, the garage band. We play loud and sing sad songs that make you happy. It's complicated to explain. Come and listen, you'll get it.
textes.Salut. Lucie, plongeuse. Je ramasse ce q: Hi. Lucie, diver. I gather whatever the sea is willing to give: pearls, coral, and bits of the Léviathan that have fallen off over two hundred years.
Hi. Shift over, this crate's heavy.
textes.Salut. Prends un parapluie. Ou pas. De t: Hey. Take an umbrella. Or don't. You always end up wet anyway.
Hi. Turbo. Dragon-Pixel champion. The high score up there on the screen? That's me. Second-best score? Me too. The third… that's Mio, but she got lucky.
textes.Salut. Ysaé. Bijoux de boulons et de cri: Hi. Ysaé. Bolt and crystal jewellery, handmade, made down below. You can look, you can touch, you can even buy nothing. Up here, they say I'm “from down below”. It's true. And I'm proud of it.
textes.Salut… Je hoche la tête depuis une heure: Hi… I've been nodding my head for an hour, I think it's gone automatic.
textes.Samedi, bras de fer ? Cette fois, je gag: Saturday, arm-wrestling? This time, I win.
textes.Samira achète mon safran pour teindre se: Samira buys my saffron to dye her rags yellow. Saffron! It's for eating! It's a crime, and she commits it every week, smiling.
textes.Samira m'a confié l'histoire du tapis du: Samira told me the story of the captain's carpet: a carpet “that doesn't exist”. I told Halima, only Halima. By evening, the whole port knew. I don't understand how. Halima swears she said nothing. Me neither, almost nothing. There must be a hole in the souk walls.
textes.Samira m'a confié le plus grand secret d: Samira trusted me with the biggest secret in the souk: Rachid's wedding slippers. The whole souk knows, except Rachid. That's a real secret, round here.
textes.Samira me tisse un tapis. Un tapis ordin: Samira is weaving me a rug. An ordinary rug, a pirate rug, to put under my boots. With a coastline, caves and a cross. She asks too many questions. She weaves well.
textes.Samira me vend mes tabliers et je lui ap: Samira sells me my aprons and I bring her fish. We tell each other everything. She says I repeat everything. Not true. I only repeat what's interesting.
textes.Samira, au souk, tisse un tapis pour le: Samira, at the souk, is weaving a carpet for the pirate captain. She says he wants a carpet “that doesn't exist”. Go figure.
textes.Samira, c'est ma lumière. Elle dit que m: Samira is my light. She says my carpets are too expensive, I say her fabrics are too short, and we're getting married in the spring. With her, I lose every haggle. I've never been so rich.
textes.Samira, ma voisine, vend des tissus. Ell: Samira, my neighbour, sells fabrics. She says my carpets are too expensive. I say her fabrics are too short. We're getting married in the spring.
Without an Adventurer's card, I can't. My father taught me: a knight respects the rules. Except the one about cape length.
textes.Sans Germaine… (Il regarde ses mains vid: Without Germaine… (He looks at his empty hands.) I'm playing on a tennis racket. It doesn't ring. It goes “pok”.
textes.Sans blague ? Peuchère, enfin quelqu'un: No kidding? Well I never, somebody at last! Five o'clock, at the jetty, bring a jumper. The mackerel will be pleased. So will I.
textes.Sans commentaire ! Et la plus belle dess: No comment! And the nicest one on top, for the forces of law and order!
textes.Sans histoire, promis. … Il était une fo: No stories, I promise. … Once upon a time, there was a draughtboard…
textes.Sans hésiter… Tu as de la chance. Moi, j: Without hesitating… You're lucky. I've been hesitating for three years. Maybe you hesitate less once you've already left once.
textes.Sans la roulotte, mon cher. Juste un peu: Without the caravan, my dear. Just a bit of moss.
textes.Sans ma baguette, je me sens toute… norm: Without my wand I feel so… ordinary. It's horrible.
Count me out of the tasting, thanks.
textes.Sans sucre. Les étoiles sont assez douce: No sugar. The stars are sweet enough.
textes.Sans tache ? Ma doue, laisse-moi cherche: No blemish? Ma doue, let me look…
textes.Sans-Dents ! Ta purée de ragoût t'attend: Sans-Dents! Your stew mash is waiting for you.
textes.Sans-Dents ! Tu veux l'histoire de la si: Sans-Dents! Do you want the mermaid story?
textes.Sans-Dents me fait confiance pour tout,: Sans-Dents trusts me with everything, except herbal teas. He says a good grog cures everything. It doesn't. So I ended up putting my tea in his grog. Compromise medicine.
textes.Sans-Dents n'a plus que deux dents, alor: Sans-Dents only has two teeth left, so I make him my stew as a mash, with nice tender little bits. He says it's the best on the island. He's the only one who says it with a whistle.
textes.Sans-Dents ne croit que la moitié de mes: Sans-Dents only believes half my stories. He whistles when he has doubts. He whistles a lot. But he always sits next to me on the bench by the bay. Sceptics make the best listeners.
textes.Sans-Dents raconte des blagues en siffla: Sans-Dents tells jokes with a whistle, and I laugh before the end. He's got two teeth, I've got two left feet: we make a fine pair. Hic! We're the oldest customers at the Shark's Tooth.
textes.Sans-Dents siffle quand il parle. J'ente: Sans-Dents whistles when he talks. I hear half. The half that whistles. We've been drinking at the same counter, one at each end, for thirty years. It's almost friendship. ALMOST.
textes.Sans… sans sucre ? Ah. Bon. Chacun son c: No… no sugar? Ah. Well. To each his own. I'll serve it to you anyway, from very high, so you at least get the foam. And between us… maybe it's not so silly.
textes.Sardine a disparu… Il a suivi un robot d: Sardine's gone missing… He followed one of Lisse's robots. He always chases robots. He thinks they're big boxes of dog biscuits. I've looked everywhere in town. Maybe he's at the Scrapyard… it's far, the Scrapyard.
textes.Sardine a déterré quelque chose… Une piè: Sardine dug something up… A coin! He drops it at your feet.
textes.Sardine a senti l'huile de robot. Il fon: Sardine has smelled robot oil. He charges, nose to the ground, growling like a little engine.
textes.Sardine a trouvé une pièce dans une flaq: Sardine found a coin in a puddle. He hands it to you with the utmost seriousness.
textes.Sardine aboie aux champignards : ils éte: Sardine barks at the mushroomers: they sneeze pink spores on him. He sneezes too. They look at each other, offended.
textes.Sardine aboie de toutes ses forces : un: Sardine barks with all his might: a robot! He charges to bite its iron ankles.
textes.Sardine aboie en rythme sur la musique d: Sardine barks in time to the music from the Hall. He's picked his favourite band.
textes.Sardine aboie trois fois très fort. Le r: Sardine barks three times, very loudly. The robot stops: “Please stop barking.” Sardine barks louder.
textes.Sardine arrive au galop, une pièce dans: Sardine gallops up with a coin in his mouth. He puts it down, barks once, and runs off to fetch the next one.
textes.Sardine attrape son os à mâcher et court: Sardine grabs his chew bone and runs in circles with it, very pleased with himself.
textes.Sardine attrape un câble du robot entre: Sardine grabs one of the robot's cables in his teeth and pulls with all his might. The robot backs away, very politely.
textes.Sardine déboule en dérapant et te lèche: Sardine skids in and licks your hand. Mission: follow you.
textes.Sardine fait trois fois le tour de toi e: Sardine circles you three times, wagging his whole behind. It's decided: he's yours, and you're his.
textes.Sardine grogne, les poils du dos dressés: Sardine growls, hackles up, and charges to bite a robot's caterpillar track.
textes.Sardine lâche une pièce devant toi. Elle: Sardine drops a coin in front of you. It's a bit wet. He seems to be saying: “For you. Don't ask questions.”
textes.Sardine lèche ta main, puis se couche à: Sardine licks your hand, then lies down beside you, satisfied with the whole world.
textes.Sardine pose sa tête sur ton pied et sou: Sardine rests his head on your foot and sighs with happiness.
Sardine puts a coin on your shoe. His perked-up ear quivers with pride.
textes.Sardine pose une pièce un peu baveuse à: Sardine puts a slightly slobbery coin at your feet and waits for praise.
textes.Sardine pousse ta main avec sa truffe. E: Sardine nudges your hand with his nose. Again. Again. One more scratch.
textes.Sardine remue la queue si fort que tout: Sardine wags his tail so hard that his whole back end wags with it.
textes.Sardine rentre à la maison en trottinant: Sardine trots home. He looks back twice to make sure you haven't changed your mind.
textes.Sardine revient en trottinant, la queue: Sardine comes trotting back, tail spinning like a propeller, and drops a coin at your feet. Nobody knows where he finds them.
textes.Sardine revient en trottinant, une pièce: Sardine trots back, a coin in his mouth, very pleased with himself.
textes.Sardine s'allonge contre ta jambe et pou: Sardine lies down against your leg and lets out a big, happy dog sigh.
textes.Sardine saute autour de toi en aboyant d: Sardine jumps around you, barking with joy. You're here. That's all that matters.
textes.Sardine saute dans la barque et se poste: Sardine jumps into the boat and takes up position at the bow, nose in the wind, like a true sea dog.
textes.Sardine se met à aboyer comme un fou : u: Sardine starts barking like mad: one of Lisse's robots is nearby!
textes.Sardine se roule sur le dos, les quatre: Sardine rolls onto his back, all four paws in the air. It's an invitation for a tummy rub. A very official one.
textes.Sardine te rapporte une pièce toute bril: Sardine brings you back a shiny coin, then sits down, very proud, waiting for a scratch.
textes.Sardine te rapporte une pièce… et un bou: Sardine brings you a coin… and a lemonade bottle cap. He keeps the cap. The coin is for you.
textes.Sardine te regarde avec des yeux pleins: Sardine looks at you with eyes full of love. One ear up, one ear down.
textes.Sardine tourne autour du robot en aboyan: Sardine runs barking around the robot, so fast the robot doesn't know where to look.
textes.Sardine, je l'ai trouvé dans une caisse: Sardine? I found him in an empty sardine crate at the harbour, when he was tiny. Hence the name. He smelled of fish for three months. Now he smells of dog. That's better. A bit.
textes.Sardine, le chien au bandana rouge: Sardine, the dog with the red bandana
textes.Sardine, le chien de Tornade, a disparu: Sardine, Tornade's dog, has disappeared! My six dogs searched everywhere. Bigoudi sniffed out a trail to the south-east, towards the Scrapyard. Then he sniffed out a sandwich. He lost the trail.
textes.Sardine, le chien de Tornade, un bâtard: Sardine, Tornade's dog, a happy mutt with a red bandana, followed one of Lisse's robots and hasn't come back. Chaussette thinks he went towards the Scrapyard, to the south-east.
textes.Satisfait. L'affaire des croissants est: Satisfied. The croissant case is closed.
textes.Satisfait. Mes tomates ont bien poussé c: Satisfied. My tomatoes grew well this week. I read them a chapter of botany every evening. They love photosynthesis. It's their favourite subject.
textes.Satisfaite. La Grande Horloge est à l'he: Satisfied. The Great Clock is on time, the furnaces are running, the mine is safe, La Marmite is overflowing, and the Line goes down full. I have nothing to do. That's the sign of a town that works.
textes.Saturne a encore pris de l'avance. Il fa: Saturn has run ahead again. Someone will have to have a word with it.
textes.Saturne et ses anneaux, nets comme un de: Saturn and its rings, sharp as a drawing. The Professor calls it “the belle of the ball”.
textes.Saucisse ? Tu as une saucisse ? Tu sens: Sausage? Do you have a sausage? You smell of sausage. Are you a sausage?
textes.Saucisse. … Pardon, je voulais juste le: Sausage. … Sorry, I just wanted to say it again.
textes.Sauf une mouette. Elle a fait trois alle: Except a seagull. It made three round trips.
textes.Sauge est la seule personne de l'île qui: Sauge is the only person on the island who has known me almost as long as the lake has. She treats my chilblains. She tells everyone. She's right to.
textes.Sauge et moi, on se dispute sur le sel e: Sauge and I have been arguing about salt and honey for twenty years, and we're both right. She always has seconds of my soup. I always drink her herbal tea to the last drop. That's called friendship, sweetie.
textes.Sauge m'a laissé un pot d'onguent pour l: Sauge left me a pot of ointment for the wounded owl, in case she ever let someone near. I put it on my table, next to the ball. The ball and the ointment were waiting for the same thing, I think. Sauge asked me what it meant. I told her I had no idea. It was the truth.
textes.Sauge m'apporte une tisane au thym tous: Sauge brings me a thyme tea every Sunday, on my bench. Piping hot, with too much honey. I let it cool, then I freeze it, and I crunch it like a stick of barley sugar. She finds that barbaric. She's been bringing it to me hot for forty years all the same.
textes.Sauge me fournit le thé que je lis. Elle: Sauge supplies the tea I read. She doesn't quite believe in my ball, and I don't quite believe in her herbal teas. We respect each other enormously. She's the most generous woman on the island.
textes.Sauge, ta tasse m'a parlé de toi, cette: Sauge, your cup told me about you last night.
textes.Sauter (ou E) : danser le pogo avec la f: Jump (or E): mosh with the crowd!
textes.Saïd ! La plus belle voix de la criée. I: Saïd! The finest voice at the fish auction. He sold me forty kilos of sardines for a sneeze. The best deal of my life. The crew disagrees.
textes.Saïd ? Une voix de criée, faite pour ven: Saïd? A fish-auction voice, made for selling sardines, not for singing. But he sings anyway. Loud. Almost as loud as me. Almost.
textes.Saïd crie au-dessus de ma tête toute la: Saïd shouts over my head all morning. His sea bream have heard so much shouting that their flesh is stressed. You can see it in their eyes. Grandmother would have seen it straight away.
textes.Saïd crie mes prix sur l'estrade. Bien f: Saïd shouts my prices from the platform. Nice and loud, that he does. But he rounds them off “for the music”. An amin doesn't need music. He needs the right numbers.
textes.Saïd, mon voisin de quai. Ses cris amène: Saïd, my quayside neighbour. His shouting brings customers all the way to my grill. He says it's the smell of my sardines that gives him his voice. We're both right.
textes.Scarlett ! Ce soir, je finis trop tôt ?: Scarlett! Shall I finish too early tonight?
textes.Scarlett ! Tu l'as vu, mon cheval, aujou: Scarlett! Have you seen my horse today?
textes.Scarlett est venue faire tatouer un cout: Scarlett came to get a knife tattooed. She moved. It turned into a spoon. She still hasn't forgiven me.
textes.Scarlett la Rouquine lance des couteaux: Scarlett the Redhead throws knives without a tremble. But in my tent, she sneezed. Her knife turned into a spoon. It's not my fault. It's hers. And maybe a fly's.
textes.Scarlett lance ses couteaux pendant que: Scarlett throws her knives while I play. If I play out of tune, she misses. She never misses. So I never play out of tune. She's the best music teacher I've ever had.
textes.Scarlett tient mon équipage mieux que mo: Scarlett runs my crew better than I do. She laughs too much, she sticks her knives in my mast, and she calls me Jambe-de-Bois to my face. She's the only one I allow it.
textes.Scarlett, c'est la plus gentille ! Elle: Scarlett is the nicest! She told me my tattoo was a magnificent horse. And she opens casks with her knives, from far away. Hic! Now that's a real friend.
Scarlett. Stop aiming at my mast.
textes.Scarlett. Tu veux que je la retouche, ta: Scarlett. Want me to touch up your spoon?
textes.Scribe. Mon champ a rétréci, cette année: Scribe. My field has shrunk this year.
textes.Se faire inscrire au registre par Éclipt: Get Écliptique to enter you in the register (at the Council Hall, at the foot of the Crystal Spire, in the centre of the island; at noon at the Nebula Café)
textes.Se le faire raconter par quelqu'un qu'on: Having someone you love tell you about it.
textes.Se promener dans le Bois des Hachures: Take a walk in the Hatching Wood
textes.Secret professionnel. Comme vos cartes à: Trade secret. Like your postcards, one penny cheaper than mine.
textes.Selma est venue m'acheter trois bols, et: Selma came to buy three bowls, and stayed three hours. She looks at everything as if it were the first time. With her, even my clay looks new.
textes.Selma paie sa chambre en tableaux. Mes m: Selma pays for her room in paintings. My walls are covered in blue boats, and so are my sheets, come to think of it. I grumble. But I wouldn't take down a single canvas.
textes.Selma peint la nuit à la bougie, dans so: Selma paints at night by candlelight, in bed, with the canvas on her knees. In the morning, I find blue everywhere: on the sheets, on the pillow, once even on my teapot. I told her: “More blue!” She answered: “It's the sky, Zineb. It runs.” Since then, I wash her sheets separately. With the sky.
textes.Selma voit dans mes lanternes des choses: Selma sees things in my lanterns I'd never seen. Forty years of piercing, and it's a young girl from Port-Azur who teaches me what I do. It's galling. It's wonderful.
textes.Selon le protocole, on entre à Astralys: According to protocol, one enters Astralys through the Welcome Gate, to the south-east, by riding up the beam. Some people arrive from the sky, in flying machines. That isn't covered by any article. I'm drafting one. It's already forty pages long.
textes.Selon le protocole, à gauche… ici ?: According to protocol, left is… here?
textes.Selon mes calculs, le Grand Spaghetti bo: According to my calculations, the Great Spaghetti has been sulking for exactly seven days, three hours and a few noodles. The Reverend thinks we should prepare him a special dish. Scientifically, it's as good a hypothesis as any. And it smells better than the others.
textes.Selon vous, honorable visiteur, quelle e: In your opinion, honourable visitor, what is the best way to say hello?
textes.Sens ! Sens ! Cumin, safran, ras-el-hano: Smell! Smell! Cumin, saffron, ras el hanout, cinnamon, chilli… Lalla Aïcha. Forty spices on my stall, and one nose on your face. Use it!
textes.Sens ces trois feuilles, {surnom}. Laque: Smell these three leaves, {surnom}. Which one do you like best?
textes.Sens-moi cette fumée ! Mustapha, grilleu: Smell that smoke! Mustapha, sardine griller for twenty years. Six sardines, a piece of bread, a little cumin, and you forget your worries.
textes.Sept ? (Il fronce les sourcils, sort sa: Seven? (He frowns and takes out his eraser.) No, no. Nine. The rainbow didn't think of brown or pink. The Palette did.
textes.Sept canons de bronze, une tour, et six: Seven bronze cannons, one tower, and six guards. It's not much. But nobody has ever taken Tazira from the sea. By trickery, once. Long ago.
textes.Sept couteaux, un trou. Tu paries ?: Seven knives, one hole. Want to bet?
textes.Sept dans le même trou. Comme d'habitude: Seven in the same hole. As usual.
textes.Sept est le meilleur employé de la ville: Sept is the best employee in the city. He never takes a break, never takes a holiday. I make him pretend, once a year. He pretends very seriously.
textes.Sept heures, l'horloge. Midi, le comptoi: Seven o'clock, the clock. Noon, the counter at the Crankshaft, watch in hand, for the whistle. Evenings, chess with Ambroise, table 2. At New Year, Capucine fires her confetti from the top of my tower: hence my one and only second fast. And lately, I sent a stopwatch on the Zéphyr to a certain Pépin, in Ramure, for his Great Race. A race without a stopwatch is just a hurried stroll.
textes.Sept heures, la capitainerie. Midi, le C: Seven o'clock, the harbour office. Noon, the Café de la Place, the table overlooking the harbour: I count sailboats while I eat. Afternoon, the register, Lucas and his crates, Yannick and his customers who can't swim. Seven in the evening, I lock up. On Sunday evenings, I take soup up to the lighthouse. Anselme doesn't say thank you. He eats it all.
textes.Sept minutes vingt. C'est pour une grand: Seven minutes twenty. It's for a special occasion.
textes.Sept pièces, mon ami. Les ressorts, ça s: Seven coins, my friend. Springs wear out. So do coins, but more slowly.
textes.Sept rubis sur huit brillent, Majesté. E: Seven rubies out of eight are shining, Majesty. Er… eight out of eight.
textes.Sept, Khéty ! Je les ai tous remis à l'e: Seven, Khéty! I put them all back in the water!
textes.Sept, demain. J'ai trouvé un bleu de plu: Seven, tomorrow. I've found one more blue.
Seven, tomorrow. I've seen a new blue.
textes.Sept. Tu as raté celui derrière le nuage: Seven. You missed the one behind the cloud.
textes.Sereine. Danser, c'est comme nager : on: Serene. Dancing is like swimming: you let yourself be carried.
