textes.Sereine. La ligne a rouvert, l'air est b: Serene. The line has reopened, the air is good, the Greenhouses are overflowing, and the Great Singer has passed by twice this week. When all is well, I have nothing to preside over. That's the sign of a Council that works.
textes.Sereine. Le bout de la jetée est le meil: Serene. The end of the jetty is the best place in the world. You see everything, and nobody comes to bother you. Except you.
textes.Sereine. Le fleuve est calme, la crue se: Serene. The river is calm, the flood will be a good one.
textes.Sereine. Les étoiles sont à leur place,: Serene. The stars are in their places, the apprentices almost.
textes.Sereine. Personne ne s'est cassé la jamb: Serene. Nobody broke a leg today. Ewen is in detention.
textes.Sereine. Pour une fois, tout est en ordr: Serene. For once, everything is in order.
textes.Sergent ! Le Boucanier de la semaine, to: Sergeant! This week's Boucanier, hot off the press!
textes.Sergent ! Tu annonces le concert de ce s: Sergeant! Are you announcing tonight's gig?
textes.Sergent Fréquence lit le Boucanier à la: Sergeant Fréquence reads the Boucanier on the radio every morning. He adds sound effects. When I write “a seagull stole a sandwich”, you hear the seagull, the sandwich and the owner's yell. That's great journalism.
textes.Serré. Comme le maire. Une personne de g: Short and strong. Like the mayor. A person of taste. I'll make it right away, nice and black.
textes.Servir le thé, au même moment, aux pêche: To serve tea, at the same moment, to the fishermen, the pirates, the caravan drivers and the guard, all sitting on the same terrace. One foam for everyone. No rum in it. On that, I insist.
textes.Servir un grand repas, une seule et même: To serve a great meal, one single table stretching from the Frondeurs' Bridge all the way to Strata Station, with people from the four worlds sitting side by side, and nobody, absolutely nobody, leaving with an empty belly. Not even the cat.
textes.Ses ailes battent tout doucement…: Its wings are beating ever so gently…
textes.Ses crocs sont plantés dans la pierre :: His fangs are stuck in the stone: his head is on the ground, STRIKE!
textes.Ses fers plus légers ? Non. Jamais. … Hm: Lighter shoes for him? No. Never. … Hm. I might have changed his sole nails, the other evening. Finer ones. He thinks it's the training. Let him think so. Don't tell him anything, you.
Her letters always arrive wet. I dry them in the sun before reading them, and I keep the water in a little bottle. I have a hundred and forty of them, lined up on my windowsill. Every time she writes “I haven't lost anything”, the letter is wetter than the others.
textes.Ses pinces sont coincées dans la roche !: His claws are stuck in the rock! Strike now!
textes.Ses plumes du vent tombent parfois sur m: Her wind feathers sometimes fall on my lake. I keep them, caught in the ice, standing straight. She comes to claim them. She has to say “please”. She sings it. It still counts. I thaw them one by one. It takes the afternoon. She talks the whole time.
textes.Ses quarante pièces ?! Elle les aura qua: Her forty coins?! She'll get them when the sea runs dry! … What? You insist? Listen to me well, landlubber: either you pay my debt yourself, or you take it from me fair and square, with fists. No one has ever put Gontran Lestrange on the mat. No one.
textes.Ses trois cents noisettes dans le Chêne-: His three hundred hazelnuts in the Mother Oak: I help him look for them in the evening, when I've finished my bridges. We never find any. There are always two hundred and ninety-nine left. But he's happy, so I am too. Maybe that's the secret: looking together.
textes.Ses élèves ne retenaient pas l'ordre des: Her pupils couldn't remember the order of the suns. I took my teponaztli: “Jaguar! Wind! Rain of fire! Water!” Tok, tak, tok, tak. The next day, the whole class was singing. Even the high priest, passing by, tapped his foot. Once. I saw him. So did Citlali. We never mention it in front of him.
textes.Seul ? Dans les grottes ? Avec la marée: Alone? In the caves? With the tide coming in? No. Courage without a head is a cannon without a ball: noise, and nothing else. You won't go.
textes.Seulement Xan ! Oui ! C'est le moustique: Only Xan! Yes! He's the most important mosquito in the world! The others bite for nothing. He bites for the story!
textes.Seulement les bonnes ! Voilà quelqu'un q: Only the good ones! Now there's someone who understands me. Those are the only ones I tell anyway. The others I leave in the ball.
textes.Seulement mes pattes, petite. Sous la co: Only my paws, little one. Under the blanket.
Only when I hear a harp.
textes.Seulement si l'eau est chaude, cette foi: Only if the water's warm this time!
Only if you shout in tune this time.
textes.Seulement si tu joues la note de l'écure: Only if you play the squirrel note.
textes.Seulement sous la pluie ! Par beau temps: Only in the rain! In fine weather, it's perfect!
textes.Seul… Oui, ça aussi, ça soigne. Alors va: Alone… Yes, that heals too. Then go to the Gardens, by the pool. The water shines. Nobody will bother you. Except maybe a flower.
textes.Sextant ! Ma carte tourne, la nuit !: Sextant! My map turns at night!
textes.Sextant dessine l'archipel depuis le bel: Sextant draws the archipelago from the lookout every morning. One day, he asked me to be quiet “at least during the heel of the big island.” I was quiet. He drew the heel. Then he told me: “You may speak.” I gave my whole speech. He drew while I did.
textes.Sextant dessine la plus grande carte de: Sextant is drawing the biggest map of the archipelago ever made. Thirty metres! I want to display it. He says it isn't finished. He's been saying that for a hundred years. I'm keeping an empty room for it.
textes.Sextant dessine la terre, moi le ciel. I: Sextant draws the land, I draw the sky. He asks me where north is. I show him the North Star. He says: “No, on my map.” We never talk about the same sky. We're best friends.
textes.Sextant dessine sur des feuilles carrées: Sextant draws on square sheets. “Sheets have corners,” he says. He started all over again on a round sheet. Then he made me a round map of Astralys. It turns on the ceiling of my bubble. Well, I think it does.
textes.Sextant dessine tous les matins sur mon: Sextant draws on my lookout every morning. He asks me to be quiet. I'm quiet. Almost. He says I'm the only background noise that stays still. I think it's a compliment.
textes.Sextant m'a demandé où était le nord. Je: Sextant asked me where north was. I showed him the North Star, shining bright. He sighed: “No, Zénith. On my map.” I took his pencil and drew the North Star at the top of his map. He kept it. It's the only north in the archipelago that shines at night.
textes.Sextant m'a dessiné, une fois, sans me l: Sextant drew me once, without telling me: a little dot of light on the Gate, at the edge of his map of Astralys. Next to it, in tiny letters, he wrote: “Here, they say welcome.” I saw it over his shoulder. My halo lit up. He pretended not to see.
textes.Sextant, Ionie a besoin d'une carte stel: Sextant, Ionie needs a star chart.
textes.Sextant, avez-vous vu une méduse de ciel: Sextant, have you seen a sky jellyfish?
textes.Sextant, cette carte, on l'expose quand: Sextant, that map, when do we display it?
textes.Sextant, le cartographe, me demande touj: Sextant, the cartographer, always asks me where north is. I show him the Pole Star. He says: “No, on my map.” We're not talking about the same sky.
textes.Si ! Des ailes à moteur, cousine !: Yes there is! Motorised wings, cousin!
textes.Si ! Un nouveau ! Presque pas de grenoui: I do! A new one! Hardly any frogs this time!
textes.Si : dans ta tête. C'est un très joli po: You can: in your head. It's a very pretty jar.
textes.Si Larbi a connu mon grand-père, et il m: Si Larbi knew my grandfather, and he knew me as a worm thief. He's as patient as his jetty. I'm not. I admire him for it.
textes.Si Larbi, c'est le seul qui ne rit pas d: Si Larbi is the only one who doesn't laugh at my whales. He fishes at the end of the jetty without ever catching anything, and he's happy. I'm learning. Mostly how to catch nothing.
textes.Si Larbi. Mon maître. Il m'a appris la s: Si Larbi. My master. He taught me the one thing: the seagulls. He left me his spot in the channel. Now he fishes without catching anything. He's earned the right.
textes.Si fait. Celle d'une amirale qui ne riai: Indeed I have. The one about an admiral who never laughed.
textes.Si j'entends le mot baignoire, tu récure: If I hear the word bathtub, you'll be scrubbing the deck with Ewen.
textes.Si je cligne des yeux lentement, ça veut: If I blink slowly, it means I love you. Don't get used to it.
textes.Si je crie « reculez », reculez. Tous le: If I shout “back”, step back. Both of you. Especially you, Sir Tancrède.
textes.Si je descends, tu m'apprends l'arc ?: If I get down, will you teach me archery?
textes.Si je foudroie ici, ça va résonner. Bouc: If I zap in here, it'll echo. Cover your ears. Just in case.
textes.Si je foudroie le lac, tout le lac sera: If I zap the lake, the whole lake gets zapped. Me too, probably. I won't do it.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? (Il ferme les: Do I remember you? (He closes his eyes.) Yes. Your footsteps. Your voice. The way you stopped to listen to the Chasm. Few people stop. You did.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Bien sûr ! Ic: Do I remember you? Of course! Here, we never forget an adventurer. Églantine even has a file on you.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Bien sûr ! Je: Do I remember you? Of course! I don't remember voices, {surnom}, I remember faces. And yours smiled when the door opened onto the cavern. That, I saw.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Bien sûr ! Le: Do I remember you? Of course! The Great Spaghetti forgets no one, and neither do we.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Bien sûr ! So: Do I remember you? Of course! Underground, you never forget a face: there's so little light that you look at everyone very carefully.
Do I remember you? Of course! Under three glass domes, we run into each other three times a day. And our own reflections, four.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Bien sûr ! Su: Do I remember you? Of course! On an island two hundred metres wide, you end up knowing everyone. And their shoes.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Bien sûr ! Tu: Do I remember you? Of course! The first time, you blew on your foam and it flew off onto the next table. Captain Zéphyrine ate it. She said it was a victory.
Do I remember you? Of course! You're in colour, people notice that around here.
Do I remember you? Of course! You're the first person who opened my umbrella without flying away. I wrote your name in my notebook, under “miracles”.
Do I remember you? Of course! You're my only student who already had wings when they arrived. A first in my whole career.
Do I remember you? Of course! You were on the pier the day I won by three lengths. Not yesterday, another day. I win often.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Bien sûr ! À: Do I remember you? Of course! In Hautefond, everyone bumps into each other in the cabin. You end up knowing the faces. And the hats.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Bien sûr. Adè: Do I remember you? Of course. Adèle landed on your shoulder. She only does that with kind people. She's never wrong.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Bien sûr. Je: Do I remember you? Of course. I remember everything that grows. And you've grown a little since last time.
Do I remember you? Of course. I painted you. Once you're on the rock, you never leave. That's why you have to be careful what you paint.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Bien sûr. Le: Do I remember you? Of course. The first day you came, the waterfall was singing softly: the weather was fine up top. That's how I file my memories. By weather.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Bien sûr. Tu: Do I remember you? Of course. You looked at a bolt very closely, the first time. And you smiled. That's how a jeweller starts.
Do I remember you? Of course. You crossed the Frondeurs' Bridge without holding the railing. Or else you held it very discreetly. Either way suits me.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? D'en haut, je: Do I remember you? From up there, I recognise everyone, {surnom}. You're the one who looks up when the Albatross goes by. There aren't that many.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? HA ! Tu as su: Do I remember you? HA! The first time Granny hammered, you jumped so high you hit the ceiling. You don't forget a thing like that.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? HO ! Tu as fa: Do I remember you? HO! You jumped right up to the vault the first time Grand-Mère struck. They still talk about it at La Marmite.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Hein ? Bien s: Do I remember you? Eh? Of course! You're the one who listened to me right to the end. That's rare. I always remember those ones.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Hm. Je me sou: Do I remember you? Hm. I remember everyone who got off the ferry. You said thank you to the captain. That's rare.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Ici, tout le: Do I remember you? Here, everyone remembers everything. Humans a little less well than androids, that's all.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Je me souvien: Do I remember you? I remember all my customers. Especially the ones who don't pay.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Les mouettes: Do I remember you? The gulls remember you. So I do too. We share everything here.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Mais bien sûr: Do I remember you? But of course! My memory is a seashell: everything echoes inside it.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Mon caillou,: Do I remember you? My pebble, I remember every belly I've ever fed. You had two helpings of stew and said thank you both times. That, you remember.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Mon chou, je: Do I remember you? Sweetie, I even remember what you bought the first time. And the face you made when you tasted the pepper.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Mon petit, j': Do I remember you? Little one, I'm eighty, and I remember everyone who has ever sat around this fire. You listened before you spoke. That's rare. That's precious.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Mon petit, je: Do I remember you? My dear, I remember everyone who's eaten at my table. And you mopped your bowl with your bread. That, I never forget.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Oui. Tu es ve: Do I remember you? Yes. You came on the day of sunset number nine hundred and eighty-seven. A very soft violet. I'll show it to you.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Par ma mousta: Do I remember you? By my moustache, yes! You jumped higher than anyone in the tavern the first time the machine whistled.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Sur une île a: Do I remember you? On an island this small, you remember everybody. Even the seagull that steals the toast.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Tu es dans un: Do I remember you? You're in one of my poems. The third line. The one the wind didn't carry off.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Tu plaisantes: Do I remember you? You're joking! You're in my Big Notebook, page one hundred and twelve: “Arrival of a very well-mannered traveller, who said hello to the fish.” I didn't make anything up. Well, hardly anything.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Un Lumen n'ou: Do I remember you? A Lumen forgets nothing, {surnom}. We have room in our heads: a thousand years of room.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Un démon n'ou: Do I remember you? A demon never forgets a face. Or a whiff of smoke.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Évidemment !: Do I remember you? Of course! In a cavern, you bump into everyone every day. And everything echoes in here. Even people.
Do I remember you? Of course! You did a whole lap holding on to your hat, when we go at the speed of a hen. Very cautious. I appreciated that.
Do I remember you? Obviously! You went “wow” on your first ascent. Everyone goes “wow”. But you did it with style.
Do I remember you? Of course! You stamped your foot, the first time. Not in time. But with heart. That, I never forget.
Do I remember you? Obviously! You held the lamp while I was fixing Bielle's guitar. You held the lamp very well. Few people know how to hold a lamp.
Do I remember you? Obviously! You're the one who kept me company while I had my eyes shut. That's how I recognise my real friends.
Do I remember you? Of course! You watched me do the Boing, and you clapped even when I fell. You're my favourite audience.
Do I remember you? Of course! In Port-Boucan, everybody remembers everybody. And Sergeant Fréquence repeats it on the radio.
textes.Si je me souviens de toi ? Évidemment. T: Do I remember you? Obviously. You're the first person from up top who asked me what it was like down below. You don't forget that.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Bien sûr ! V: Do I remember you? Of course! You're between star three thousand and twelve and star three thousand and thirteen, in my notebook. It's a very good spot.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Bien sûr. Vo: Do I remember you? Of course. You arrived the day I named Mélusine, a lovely altocumulus. I always associate you with her. It's a great honour.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Certainement: Do I remember you? Certainly. You arrived the evening the Singer sang “hello, Dome” three times in a row. I noted it in the Dictionary, next to your name. It's very good company.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Hm. Évidemme: Do I remember you? Hm. Obviously. You're the only person from the Floor who didn't ask me where the toilets were the moment they arrived. It left an impression.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Je me souvie: Do I remember you? I remember every passenger, {surnom}. And the floor they got off at. And what they left behind in the cabin. You, nothing. That's good.
Do I remember you? I remember everyone who has gone into my mine, {surnom}. And everyone who has come back out. Which is to say, everyone. That's my job.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Mon cher, je: Do I remember you? My dear fellow, I never forget a face! Nor a name. Nor a handshake. You have an excellent handshake. I made a note of it.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Naturellemen: Do I remember you? Naturally. You arrived on a day of glorious weather. Up here, that's almost every day. But that day was finer.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Oh oui. Je m: Do I remember you? Oh yes. I remember everything that shines. Your eyes were shining, the first time, in front of the lanterns. I made a note of it. Somewhere. On a crystal, perhaps.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Oui. Vous pe: Do I remember you? Yes. You added sixty kilos to the island the day you arrived. I recalculated the lift. For you. That's my way of remembering people.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Oui. Vous êt: Do I remember you? Yes. You are saved in my memory, folder “people who say hello to the trees with me”. There are very few people in that folder. You are snug in there.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Vous avez un: Do I remember you? You have a file, {surnom}. Everyone has a file. Even the Guild cat.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Vous êtes da: Do I remember you? You're in my notebook, {surnom}. Page seven. With a little star. I've only given out three.
textes.Si je me souviens de vous ? Vous êtes ve: Do I remember you? You first came in one day at eleven forty-three. I remember it to the second. It's my way of remembering the people I like.
textes.Si je pose le sac, marraine, je ne me re: If I put the sack down, godmother, I'll never get up again.
textes.Si je saute, est-ce que j'atterris à Hau: If I jump, will I land in Hautefond? … Just asking.
textes.Si je tissais une toile pour toi, {surno: If I wove a canvas for you, {surnom}, what pattern should I hide in it?
textes.Si je viens, tu iras dormir après ?: If I come, will you go to bed afterwards?
textes.Si je vous prends en photo un jour, dite: If I take your photo one day, tell me: are you more of a front view, or a profile?
textes.Si la cloche de Mélusine sonne, cours au: If Mélusine's bell rings, run to the fields! My golden turnips will make a break for it, and with my knees, I can't catch a single one anymore. Bring me back five, lad. Gently with my little ones.
textes.Si la file avance encore d'un pas, je ch: If the queue moves one more step, I'll sing.
If the Great Spaghetti wills it.
textes.Si le flotteur frétille juste un peu, ne: If the float just wiggles a little, don't move. That's a fish having a taste. Wait until it dives for real.
If we dance till then, sure.
textes.Si on se perd, on se tient la main, d'ac: If we get lost, we hold hands, all right? It's for you. Well, for me too.
textes.Si quelqu'un a l'air triste, va lui parl: If someone looks sad, go and talk to them. It always helps. Them and you.
If your whale doesn't slow you down.
textes.Si ton sac est plein, va vendre ce que t: If your bag is full, go and sell what you don't need at a merchant's.
textes.Si ton œil trouve la passe !: If your eye can find the channel!
If you have fish, we can talk.
textes.Si tu as faim, les croissants de Port-Az: If you're hungry, Port-Azur's croissants are the best. I take the boat just for them.
textes.Si tu chantes moins lentement que la der: If you sing less slowly than last time!
textes.Si tu cherches des cristaux astraux moin: If you're looking for cheaper astral crystals, go and see Ionie at the Spaceport. She digs them out from under the island with her tools. I sell them dearer, but I wrap them in star paper.
textes.Si tu comptes avec mes doigts, pas avec: If you count on my fingers, not on yours.
textes.Si tu coupes un arbre, plantes-en un aut: If you cut down a tree, plant another one. That's all we ask, we elves.
textes.Si tu croises un oiseau, demande-lui com: If you meet a bird, ask it how it manages to stay up in the air without falling. I want the real answer. Happy bubbles!
textes.Si tu descends au Donjon des Mille March: If you go down into the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps, take pies. Down there, a hungry adventurer is a crying adventurer. I've seen them come back up in tears, and it wasn't because of the monsters.
textes.Si tu descends dans les Neuf Cercles, pr: If you go down into the Nine Circles, take potions. Several. The cold of the Cocytus isn't magic at all: it's simply very, very cold, and bodies don't like that. A sap potion is a coat you drink.
textes.Si tu descends à Xibalba, tu devras joue: If you go down to Xibalba, you'll have to play against the Lords. A tip: don't chase the ball, go where it's going to go. And push it towards the ring with your whole body.
textes.Si tu devais rester quelque part pour to: If you had to stay somewhere forever, where would you choose?
textes.Si tu devais écrire ton nom en image, {s: If you had to write your name as a picture, {surnom}, what would you draw?
textes.Si tu entends couiner dans ton oreille,: If you hear squeaking in your ear, that's me saying hello.
textes.Si tu entends un bip, c'est un nouveau n: If you hear a beep, that's a new cloud coming onto the map. Beep! … There.
textes.Si tu entends un « tonk » quelque part,: If you hear a “tonk” anywhere, {surnom}, come and get me. Even at night. Happy bubbles.
textes.Si tu fais le Tournoi des Cornes, prends: If you enter the Tournament of Horns, take a blade you know. The imps are quick: you have to strike fast. The bronze automatons are tough: you have to strike hard. Gorgoth… for Gorgoth, a blade isn't enough. You need patience.
textes.Si tu grimpes les pitons, repose-toi sur: If you climb the rock spires, rest on the ledges. Even goats take breaks, and they don't have arms.
If you say so… Yes, you're right.
textes.Si tu lèves les bras sur l'Agora, la lum: If you raise your arms on the Agora, the light follows you a little. Try it!
If you let me win, yes.
If you leave me the first ray.
textes.Si tu me regardes, je saute jusqu'à la l: If you're watching, I'll jump all the way to the moon!
textes.Si tu parles tout bas près du Mur des Fr: If you whisper by the Mural Wall, they can hear you at the Canteen. Granny Gamelle knows everything. But she never repeats a thing. She puts it in the soup.
textes.Si tu pouvais avoir n'importe quelle pot: If you could have any potion, just one, which would you pick?
textes.Si tu pouvais partir demain matin, n'imp: If you could leave tomorrow morning, for anywhere, without telling anyone… would you go?
If you promise not to drink the bay.
textes.Si tu rapportes des cuisses de grenouill: If you bring back giant frog legs, I'll buy them. Don't eat them raw! You have to cook them a long time, with thyme. Otherwise, they jump around on the plate. Really, they do.
textes.Si tu restes sur l'estrade jusqu'au bout: If you stay on the stage till the end, this time.
textes.Si tu tombes, je tombe. Si tu cours, je: If you fall, I fall. If you run, I hang on. If you eat, I watch. Very hard.
textes.Si tu vas dans le marais, rapporte-moi d: If you go into the marsh, bring me crocodile teeth. Six coins a tooth. And if you run into Vieille-Dent… his big tooth, I'll take that for forty.
If you want to make me happy, think of %s. But you didn't hear it from me.
textes.Si tu veux voir la lanterne, entre dans: If you want to see the lantern room, come into the lighthouse and climb the stairs. Polish the lens: it will pay you back. And my house is right next door, if you pass by in the evening.
textes.Si tu {le} croises, dis-lui bonjour de m: If you run into {le}, say hello from me.
textes.Si tu étais une chanson, {surnom}, tu se: If you were a song, {surnom}, which one would you be?
textes.Si un coffre bouge, je crie. Je vous pré: If a chest moves, I'll scream. I'm warning you: I scream very loud.
textes.Si un jour la Grande Scène se rallume, j: If the Great Stage ever lights up again, I want to play every drum in the camp at the same time! Picture it: TRRRRA-BOOM-BA-DA-BOOM! The seagulls would drop right out of the sky!
textes.Si un jour ton écran devient tout bleu,: If your screen ever goes all blue, with scary messages, don't panic. Breathe. And come and see me. It's often less serious than it looks.
textes.Si un jour tu as faim, demande-moi. Je t: If you're ever hungry, ask me. I'll find something. I always find something. That's my pig's promise.
textes.Si un jour tu te perds dans le Bois de C: If you ever get lost in the Ash Wood, follow the glowing mushrooms: they grow in a line, like a path. I'm the one who discovered that. Well, I think so. Nobody believes me.
textes.Si une grenouille m'avale, dites à Père: If a frog swallows me, tell Father Clotaire I wasn't scared. It's a lie, but he'll be pleased.
textes.Si une grenouille vous avale, je la char: If a frog swallows you, I'll charge it! If it swallows me, shout my name. It'll be scared.
textes.Si une grenouille vous avale, ne panique: If a frog swallows you, don't panic: they always spit you back out. After about three seconds. The three longest seconds of your life. And afterwards you need a wash. A big one.
textes.Si vite ! Tam tam tam tam !: So fast! Tum tum tum tum!
textes.Si vous descendez dans les Neuf Cercles,: If you go down into the Nine Circles, you will meet Minos, the judge. He asks three questions about the road you have travelled. Answer politely, precisely, and without yawning. Mademoiselle Ombreline, at the Library of Souls, knows the right answers. She knows everything.
textes.Si vous voyez Mamie Barricade, dites-lui: If you see Mamie Barricade, tell her… that I'm eating well. And that I'll come to the assembly. To listen. Only to listen. Maybe raise my hand.
textes.Si vous {le} croisez, dites-lui bonjour: If you run into {le}, say hello from me.
textes.Si, ma sœur. Dans la Duchesse. Elle le g: I have, Sister. Inside the Duchess. She's keeping it safe.
It does. Gently. When you're not looking.
You are. The funniest one, in fact.
textes.Signez ici, ici et là. Non, pas avec une: Sign here, here and there. No, not with a spray can. With this grey pen. It writes grey. It matches.
Sign here. And here. And there. Thank you.
textes.Signez ici. Non : lisez d'abord. TOUJOUR: Sign here. No: read first. ALWAYS read first. (You read.) “The undersigned promises to put books back in their place, not to dog-ear the pages, and to return good humor on the way out.” … You read to the very end. You're the first. Trial of the contract: passed.
textes.Signorina Ravioli m'a appris à chanter p: Signorina Ravioli taught me to sing to the tomatoes. They prefer nursery rhymes.
textes.Sigrun ! Ta bière a fait chanter la terr: Sigrun! Your fizz got the terrace singing last night.
Sigrun! A golden fizz. Same as yesterday.
textes.Sigrun ? Connais pas. … Bon. Une ancienn: Sigrun? Never heard of her. … Fine. A former apprentice. Forty years in my cellar, then off to make fizz at Dagna's. Her fizz is golden. Too golden. I've never tasted it.
textes.Sigrun brasse dans mon ancien four une b: In my old oven, Sigrun brews a golden barley fizz that smells of warm bread. The whole terrace drinks it. She deserves for the world to know. And for Ulfa to say so.
textes.Sigrun brasse la meilleure blonde de la: Sigrun makes the best golden fizz on the terrace, and she has a laugh that makes the barrels shake. I buy a mug from her every evening. Normally, I don't drink that much.
textes.Silas ! Bartholomé a encore parlé du crâ: Silas! Bartholomé talked about the skull again this morning!
textes.Silas ! Combien de squelettes au fort, c: Silas! How many skeletons at the fort tonight?
textes.Silas ! Tu me racontes le Kraken ?: Silas! Will you tell me about the Kraken?
textes.Silas ! Une histoire de navire, ce matin: Silas! A ship story this morning?
textes.Silas jure qu'il a entendu Bartholomé di: Silas swears he heard Bartholomé say “Barbe-Sanglante”, once, in the middle of the night. I've slept next to him for years, I've never heard it. So we sat up together, a whole night, in front of the cage. Bartholomé slept. Silas slept. Me too, in the end. In the morning, Bartholomé said: “Jellyfish-head.” We laughed.
textes.Silas m'a montré un truc pour le nœud de: Silas showed me a trick for the bowline: the rabbit comes out of the hole, goes round the tree, and goes back down the hole. He says Barbe-Sanglante himself taught him, when he was a cabin boy. With the rabbit, I can almost do it, eyes closed. The rabbit just gets a bit lost round the tree.
textes.Silas m'a raconté un jour que le Fort Ma: Silas once told me the Cursed Fort had a hundred skeletons. I went to count, from a distance, with my spyglass. Ninety-seven. I told him. He replied: “The other three were out.” I added them to my map, in dotted lines. Since then, all his stories go in my margins, and all my maps have dotted lines.
textes.Silas raconte les meilleures histoires d: Silas tells the best stories in the world. He was a cabin boy, like me, on Barbe-Sanglante's ship! He's seen the Kraken! Gros-Louis says he makes it up. I believe him. Almost all of it.
textes.Silas raconte, je dessine. Ses histoires: Silas tells, I draw. His stories are half false, and so are my maps, sometimes. Together, we make something almost true. That's quite something, on this island.
textes.Silence radio… L'antenne est tombée au s: Radio silence… The antenna fell onto the top of the water tower during the storm. I talk into my mic, and nobody hears me. It's like talking to Clou, but sadder.
textes.Silence… « Le Boléro du Cumulus ». Ça co: Silence… “The Cumulus Bolero”. It starts ever so softly… and ends all puffed up.
textes.Simple. Bien sûr, Altesse. Avec juste un: Simple. Of course, Highness. With just a little train.
textes.Sire Orage est tombé, et sur la montagne: Lord Storm has fallen, and on the mountain the golems froze all at once, like statues. My people can finally sleep. You are a giant among giants, big one.
textes.Sire Orage lève son épée vers le ciel :: Sire Orage raises his sword to the sky: THE STORM BREAKS LOOSE! He'll charge in a gust: when he steps back glowing, move out of his path.
textes.Sire Orage pose un genou à terre… et se: Lord Storm drops to one knee… and dissolves into the wind. The storm calms, the sun returns to the Tower. Far away, on Fire Mountain, the golems fall still. A golden chest appears among the runes.
textes.Sire Orage, le Chevalier des Tempêtes: Lord Storm, the Knight of Storms
textes.Sire Tancrède ! Il va au rempart !: Sire Tancrède! He's going to the rampart!
textes.Sire Tancrède ! Montrez-moi la technique: Sir Tancrède! Show me the falling technique!
textes.Sire Tancrède ! Vous avez vaincu quoi, a: Sir Tancrède! What did you defeat today?
textes.Sire Tancrède a vaincu un géant, un serp: Sir Tancrède defeated a giant, a serpent and a bear! Hilaire says it was in the fog. I say in the fog it's even harder. He's so cool.
textes.Sire Tancrède de Tournevent raconte des: Sir Tancrède de Tournevent tells tales of magnificent feats. All imaginary. He'd finally like to live a real one, with a witness: defeat the goblin chief of the Goblin Wood and bring back his banner.
textes.Sire Tancrède dit qu'il a « absorbé » mo: Sir Tancrède says he “absorbed” my lightning bolt last week. He was still smoking. He said it was “a knight's technique”. I pretended to believe him. It was nice of him.
textes.Sire Tancrède dit que je suis une grande: Sir Tancrède says I'm a great mage. I've struck him with lightning three times. He says it anyway. I think he's the kindest person in the Guild. And the most conductive.
textes.Sire Tancrède invente tous ses exploits,: Sire Tancrède makes up all his exploits, but he really does charge when someone's in danger. He reminds me of me, only blonder and chattier. Well, blonder.
textes.Sire Tancrède m'a raconté qu'il avait va: Sir Tancrède told me he defeated a giant with his bare hands. I asked him where. He said: “Far away. Very far. In the fog.” Ha! I like that lad. He reminds me of me, only blonder.
textes.Sire Tancrède m'apporte un exploit imagi: Sire Tancrède brings me an imaginary deed every evening. I put it to music. They're my biggest hits. None of them ever happened. The audience doesn't care. Neither do I.
textes.Sire Tancrède mange comme quatre et il d: Sire Tancrède eats like four and says thank you like ten. He's the only one who finishes his plate before I say “eat”. I adore him.
textes.Sire Tancrède mange comme quatre. Comme: Sir Tancrède eats enough for four. For four! I adore him. He's the only one who clears his plate before I say “eat”.
textes.Sire Tancrède me raconte un nouvel explo: Sir Tancrède tells me a new feat every evening. I put them to song. They're my biggest hits. And none of them ever happened.
textes.Sire Tancrède se prétend ton rival, lui: Sir Tancrède claims to be your rival too. There's only ONE rival per hero. It's in the books. We'll settle it… over a pie. He insisted on the pie.
textes.Sire Tancrède veut toujours me protéger,: Sire Tancrède always wants to protect me, which is very kind. In practice, it's mostly me healing him when he trips over his cape. One time in three.
Sir Tancrède always wants to protect me. It's sweet. But usually I'm the one healing him, because he tripped over his cape.
textes.Sire Tancrède, attention à votre cape !: Sir Tancrède, mind your cape! … Too late. I'll heal you.
textes.Sire Tancrède, ce n'était pas une techni: Sir Tancrède, that wasn't a technique. That was my lightning bolt. Sorry.
textes.Sire Tancrède, quand vous criez votre no: Sir Tancrède, when you shout your name, the monsters get scared. So do I, a bit.
textes.Sire Tancrède, racontez-moi votre plus g: Sir Tancrède, tell me about your greatest exploit.
textes.Sire Tancrède, votre cape traîne encore: Sire Tancrède, your cloak is dragging in the mud again…
textes.Sire Tancrède, vous pourriez raccourcir: Sir Tancrède, you could shorten your cape. According to the book…
textes.Sirène ! Et si on refaisait la soupe-lim: Sirène! What if we made lemonade soup again?
textes.Sirène ! Sirène ! Ce n'est pas Sirène du: Siren! Siren! Not Sirène from the bar, the warning siren! The robots are on the docks!
textes.Sirène a inventé pour moi le « sirop du: Sirène invented a “syrup of silence” just for me. I drank it. For an hour, all I could do was whisper. Everyone leaned in to listen. It was wonderful, being listened to while whispering. I order it again every Sunday. I've never said thank you loud enough. Ironic.
textes.Sirène a tout noté, tout rangé, tout pré: Sirène has noted everything, tidied everything, planned everything. I shout the ideas, she makes them work. And her lemonade saves my voice every night.
textes.Sirène est la seule personne du Boucan p: Sirène is the only person in Boucan more organised than my pot. She gives me her mint, I give her advice. She doesn't follow any of it. She's right.
textes.Sirène est la seule personne à qui je di: Sirène is the only person I tell everything to. She keeps a violet lemonade for me every evening. Our Thursdays at the lighthouse are the best part of my week.
textes.Six ans que mon traité des mélanges expl: My treatise on explosive mixtures has been sleeping at Mr Fiole's for six years. I don't know what worries me more: that he won't return it, or that he'll read it.
textes.Six bâtons, et droits en plus. Tiens, do: Six sticks, and straight ones too. Here, twelve coins. And your next shovel will cost you less: you're almost family.
Six hundred metres: the Glider has reached its ceiling. Above that is the realm of the stars.
textes.Six heures ! Je serai là à six heures !: Six! I'll be here at six!
textes.Six heures : les barques rentrent, le ph: Six o'clock: the boats come in, the lighthouse turns pink, and I unpack the ice. The grouper, sold before nine. In the afternoon, a coffee and a bench. In the evening, I have dinner at Paulo's, so he can see I'm cross. And between customers, I keep watch. The sergeant who stops at the ice-cream stand. Inès and her two Friday sea bream. Nothing gets past me.
textes.Six heures, je t'avais dit. Tu n'es pas: Six o'clock, I told you. You didn't come. The bowline's still waiting for you. So am I.
textes.Six pièces l'éclat de cristal. Dernière: Six coins a crystal shard. Final offer.
Six coins a tooth, my friend. Think about it.
textes.Six pièces le hamac, couverture comprise: Six coins for the hammock, blanket included. My aunt doesn't give credit, and neither do I. Well… she doesn't let me.
textes.Six pièces, mon chou. Même les sorciers: Six coins, dearie. Even wizards pay for their bed. Especially wizards: they set the sheets on fire.
textes.Six sardines de l'aube grillées sur la b: Six dawn sardines grilled over the embers, with cumin and lemon, on the Tazira quay. Restores two hearts.
textes.Six, milord. Les plus dorés. Les mouette: Six, milord. The goldenest. The seagulls are waiting for you.
Six, my dear! The most golden, please.
If… if you'd like. Thank you.
textes.Slurp ! Ha ha ! Le Grand Spaghetti aime: Slurp! Ha ha! The Great Spaghetti loves the noise. It proves you love what you eat. But wipe your chin.
textes.Sofia ! Tu m'as rapporté quoi, aujourd'h: Sofia! What did you bring me today?
textes.Sofia descend là où je ne peux pas aller: Sofia dives where I can't go and comes back up with the most beautiful shells on the island. My best necklaces are all thanks to her. And she never wants to be paid.
textes.Sofia m'a fredonné un chant de baleine q: Sofia hummed me a whale song she'd heard while diving. It went up, it went down, it went round in circles. I spent three nights recreating it on the decks. She listened to the end and said “almost”. Ever since, I've been looking for the rest of the “almost”. Tchoum tells everyone it's going to be huge.
textes.Sofia m'a rapporté un coquillage nacré g: Sofia brought me a pearly shell as big as my hand, found really deep down. I made the most beautiful necklace of my life with it. A very fancy gentleman from Port-Azur bought it for six coins. I gave the six coins to Sofia. She threw them into the sea, laughing, “for the fish”. I yelled her name for quite a while.
textes.Sofia m'apprend à plonger. Elle est calm: Sofia is teaching me to dive. She's calm like morning water, and she says dancing is like swimming. I tried the opposite: swimming the way I dance. It splashes.
textes.Sofia plonge, je rame. Elle a peur des p: Sofia dives, I row. She's been scared of the deep since the golden point, but she dives back in anyway. She's the bravest of us all. Even if she turns down five o'clock fishing.
textes.Sofia, c'est mon billet pour l'Atlantide: Sofia is my ticket to Atlantis. Well, the day she dares. She's heard the whales sing, and you can hear it in the way she dances.
textes.Sofia, demain matin, on regarde le lever: Sofia, tomorrow morning, shall we watch the sunrise from the water?
textes.Soigner ? Oh, mon petit, c'est la plus b: Healing? Oh, my dear, it's the most beautiful of all magic. But first you must learn to know what heals. Go and pick me three mushrooms in the Twisted Wood: the brown ones with white stalks, not the others. The others make you sing off-key.
textes.Soigner la chouette blessée du Bois Tors: Heal the injured owl in the Twisted Wood with the healing spell (key 0 then V, right next to her; in VR, left trigger)
textes.Soigner, c'est la magie la plus simple e: Healing is the simplest magic and the hardest. You have to listen to the body the way you listen to an old friend who's complaining: without interrupting.
textes.Sois franc, {surnom}. Ma dernière sculpt: Be honest, {surnom}. My latest sculpture, there: is it a fish or a sea urchin?
textes.Sois le bienvenu à Per-Hâpy, étranger. J: Welcome to Per-Hâpy, stranger. I am Néferet, priestess of Ra. Every morning I greet the sun when it is reborn in the east. Every evening I mourn it when it dies in the west. In between, I answer travellers' questions.
textes.Sois le bienvenu à Tazira, étranger. Je: Welcome to Tazira, stranger. I am Moulay Brahim, the amin of the fishermen: I'm the one who settles disputes, assigns places on the quay, and sets the price of sardines. Especially the price of sardines.
textes.Soixante ans de pêche. J'ai attrapé une: Sixty years of fishing. Once I caught a grouper so big it took two boats. I let it go: it looked older than me.
textes.Soixante ans de pêche. J'ai sorti un mér: Sixty years of fishing. I once landed a forty-kilo grouper. Well, thirty. Let's say twenty-five.
textes.Soixante, Kraxx ! Elles ont tranché des: Sixty, Kraxx! They've cut dragons, haven't they?
textes.Soixante, mon héros ! Et tu chantais en: Sixty, my hero! And you were singing at the same time.
textes.Solenne aime les îles plus qu'elle ne de: Solenne loves the islands more than she should. She leaves with fake beards and comes back with sparkling eyes. I say nothing. I only ask her to bring me back songs.
textes.Solenne connaît des raccourcis à Port-Co: Solenne knows shortcuts in Port-Coutelas that even the pirates don't know. I asked her how. She said: “From books.” There isn't a single book about Port-Coutelas. I checked.
textes.Solenne m'a apporté un patch brodé, un r: Solenne brought me an embroidered patch, a rat with a mohawk, screaming. I had no idea what it was. I put it in the window with the label “Badge of a distant warrior people.” Solenne nearly choked laughing. Orbe bought it for the price of a crystal. He framed it.
textes.Solenne m'a rapporté une graine de pommi: Solenne brought me back an apple seed, fifty years ago. She says she found it in a book. There was soil on it. Real soil from down below. I didn't ask her any questions.
textes.Solenne m'apporte des bricoles d'en bas: Solenne brings me bits and bobs from down below that she “finds in the sky.” I've had sand in my display cases for two hundred years. I ask no questions. A wink, and that's settled. Excellent business.
textes.Solenne ne descend jamais en bas, c'est: Solenne never goes down below, that's Écliptique's article. But she knows what a colander is for. I don't ask questions. Things fall from the sky, and Solenne smiles. I think that's just fine.
textes.Solenne part « en promenade » et je la d: Solenne goes off “for a stroll” and I drop her off down below, in secret. She wears fake moustaches. I don't say anything to the Council. I do loop-the-loops. She doesn't say anything either. It's a good arrangement.
textes.Solenne revient de voyage avec des yeux: Solenne comes back from her trips with sparkling eyes. She says she went “to see the islands”. I saw her leave wearing a false beard. I said nothing. At my age, you enjoy other people's secrets.
Solenne, tell me about the rain again.
Solenne, an object fell from the sky.
textes.Solide… comme une bulle, mais en plus co: Sturdy… like a bubble, but more determined!
textes.Solide… comme une bulle. Mais une bulle: Sturdy… like a bubble. But a very determined bubble.
textes.Son Altesse est la plus gracieuse des Ar: Her Highness is the most gracious of Archduchesses, and the hardest to keep in the palace. She laughs too loudly, escapes through the garden and eats chestnuts during audiences. I would not change her for the world.
textes.Son Altesse me prie de l'appeler Ignatia: Her Highness begs me to call her Ignatia. I cannot. Three hundred and twelve years of habit. But when she can't hear me, I say “the little one”. Don't repeat that.
textes.Son billet retour, jamais poinçonné, est: Her return ticket, never punched, is tucked into the frame of my compass, at the helm. It's gone yellow, the corner's dog-eared. Sometimes Lola comes aboard to give me a letter for her mother, she sees the ticket and says: “Keep it a while longer.” So I keep it. It's the only ticket in my life I've never wanted to punch.
textes.Son blindage arrête tout ! Attends qu'el: Its armor stops everything! Wait until it plants its bucket in the ground: its hoses will be exposed.
textes.Son chien, Peek', a enterré un os dans m: His dog, Peek', buried a bone in my sand table, the one where I trace my calculations. Right in the middle of the cycle of Venus. Kinich said: “He wanted to help.” The next day, digging up the bone, I found an error in my calculation. Right where the bone was. Since then, I let Peek' in.
textes.Son chien, Peek', a enterré un os sous m: His dog, Peek', buried a bone under my oldest hive. Digging to get it back, he made a tunnel. The bees use it as a second door now. Kinich is very proud: “Peek' built a house for the bees!” I don't contradict him. It's almost true.
textes.Son chien, Tlaco, aboie après les serpen: His dog, Tlaco, barks at the stone serpents at the foot of the stairs. Every day. He thinks they're going to bite. Pilli explains to him that they're gods. Tlaco barks louder. I don't intervene. A dog who will guide the dead may have his reasons to be wary of serpents.
textes.Son dessin montre une côte, des grottes: His drawing shows a coastline, some caves and a cross. To see whether he really remembered it, I added a little ginger cat in one corner. He roared so loud that Rachid dropped his tea. “No CAT!” I unpicked the cat. But now I know: for him, every detail matters. Every cliff. Every cross.
textes.Son dos est dur comme la pierre ! Frappe: Its back is hard as stone! Hit the head… or wait until it catches its breath after its tail swing.
textes.Son examen de pisteuse, à dix ans : retr: Her tracker's exam, at ten: find a mooncake hidden in the forest by Mère-Lune. Heh heh… I didn't know it was an exam! I was just following the smell, that's all. When Brume got there, half of it was missing, and my tracks were everywhere. She passed her exam. I got a tummy ache.
textes.Son fameux mérou de quarante kilos, Fern: His famous forty-kilo grouper — Fernand tells me about it every other morning. Each time, it's gained two kilos. I told him: “Odette weighed it, Fernand. Twenty-five.” He answered: “It lost weight from the emotion.” Since then, I divide everything of his by two. He pretends to be offended. It's our way of saying good morning.
textes.Son fromage des cendres est vivant. Je n: Her ash cheese is alive. I'm not joking: one morning, I left one on the table, and by evening it was at the other end. Hilda said: “It was cold.” So I put it in the stew, nice and warm. Nobody said a word. Bramm had seconds.
textes.Son grand-père marchait dans mon clan, l: His grandfather walked in my clan, the day we arrived. He had the same furrow between his eyes. Today Croc-Gris watches the forest from way up high, and I watch him. I don't tell him everything I see. He doesn't tell me everything he no longer sees.
textes.Son gâteau de lune est délicieux. Mais i: Her mooncake is delicious. But it's missing a herb: my nose is sure of it. Which one? I don't know. I suggested mint, sage, meadowsweet: she chased me out with her bread peel. My mushrooms have always been banned in her shop; now my herbs are too. I keep looking anyway. Outside.
textes.Son perroquet, l'Amiral, crie « ÇA MORD: His parrot, the Admiral, screeches “A BITE!” every time a gull flies past. The first week, I yanked my line twenty times for nothing. Now I don't move. Neither does Gaspard. The day a fish really bites, neither of us will believe it, and the fish will swim off. It'll be very restful.
textes.Son premier jour, je lui ai demandé une: His first day, I asked him for a little light. He made a black light. At noon, the whole courtyard turned to night, with stars. The apprentices screamed, Aurélien applauded, and I wrote down the formula. You never know. No one has ever managed to make a black light again. Not even Oscar.
textes.Son premier papyrus, à sept ans : l'hymn: Her first papyrus, at seven: the morning hymn, copied very seriously. And in the margin, a little sleeping cat. I kept it. I show it to visitors: “Behold the handwriting of the priestess of Ra!” She blushes every time. The cat, meanwhile, sleeps as soundly as ever. It's my favourite papyrus in the whole House of Life.
textes.Son premier pont, c'était deux brindille: His first bridge was two twigs across a puddle, with a hazelnut in the middle. He showed it to me as if it were the west bridge. I blew on it, it danced. I told him it was a real bridge. It was true! He was so proud. Then he ate the hazelnut, and the bridge collapsed. He said it was for the winter.
textes.Son premier tableau, je l'ai accroché mo: Her first painting, I hung myself in the lobby, at eleven at night, once the last guest had gone up. A spirit level, a tape measure, a pencil. To the millimetre. I did it three times: the bubble was not satisfied. The next day, Mademoiselle Clémence stopped in front of it without a word. Then she ran upstairs.
textes.Son ras-el-hanout a trente-deux épices e: Her ras el hanout has thirty-two spices and a secret thirty-third ingredient. I tried to guess. I sniffed, I tasted, I closed my eyes, and I said, sure of myself: “Fish!” The whole souk laughed. Aïcha too. It was the first time I'd seen her laugh. Well worth being wrong.
textes.Son rhum, c'est du feu en bouteille. Je: Her rum is fire in a bottle. I'll never tell her: a woman who's sunk three ships, you don't offend her. So I pour it into the palm tree's pot, by the door. One evening, she served me a glass of water, without a word. I drank it and said: “Strong, but good!” She laughed for a long time. I think she knows.
textes.Son trident, je l'ai taillé la nuit des: I carved his trident on the night of the sharks, in one hour, from the first red coral that came to hand. I told him: “Careful, it bites.” He's held it for three hundred years without letting go. His calluses are like shells. He says it comes with the job.
textes.Sors de l'eau d'abord !: Get out of the water first!
textes.Sortir de Tazira par la porte du nord, s: Leave Tazira by the north gate, follow the three caravan markers to the north-east (they light up at night), open the tomb of the Walking Dune (the star, the dune, the sun) and take the Seal of Sands
To land a real forty-kilo grouper. A real one, weighed in front of Odette, no thumb on the scales. Forty. Not thirty-nine.
textes.Soucieuse ? Je grelotte, voilà ce que je: Worried? I'm shivering, that's what I am. Me! An archduchess of the underworld! The Ember Heart is dying out, little flame: it's no more than a blue glimmer, and the city is cooling. The cold rises from the Nine Circles, beneath the Forge Cathedral. The Frost Titan has awakened at the bottom of Cocytus, and he has taken the Eternal Flame. Brother Cinder keeps the key to the door. Go down, circle after circle… and bring us back our fire.
textes.Soucieux, mon enfant. Très soucieux. Le: Worried, my child. Very worried. The Great Spaghetti is sulking, the volcano is rumbling more than usual, and Brother Linguini has broken another plate. The third this week. And it's Tuesday.
textes.Soucieux. Un petit craquement, ce matin,: Worried. A little crack this morning, in gallery four. Nothing serious. But I had everything propped up, everything checked, and I said sorry to the Old Lady. Three times. She's calmed down. I haven't yet.
textes.Souffler une bulle de nacre assez grande: To blow a mother-of-pearl bubble big enough for Coralin to step inside. So he'd see it's solid. And say “not bad”. Just “not bad”. That would already be huge.
textes.Soulagée. Mes croissants restent dans le: Relieved. My croissants stay in their basket now.
textes.Soupe de salicorne, limonade bleue à la: Samphire soup, blue spirulina lemonade, deep-sea hot chocolate, and plain hot chocolate for the cautious! Everything's cooked in the shell, without a drop of strong drink. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Soupe, pain au miel, galettes ! Tout est: Soup, honey bread, pancakes! Everything's homemade, everything's cheap. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Sous Hautefond, il y a les Strates. De m: Under Hautefond there are the Strata. In my day, we went down by the Column to buy crystals. The line has just reopened, and they say there's very loud music down there. Eh? What? I can't hear a thing. Just as well.

Beneath Hautefond are the Strata. In my day, we went down by the Column to buy crystals. Now the line is closed for works, and apparently they play very loud music down there. Eh? What? I can't hear a thing. Just as well.
textes.Sous cette salle, il y a la Forge Royale: Beneath this hall lies the Royal Forge, fed by the volcano's lava. Further down still… nobody goes.
textes.Sous l'eau, tu apprendras. La mer est pa: Underwater, you'll learn. The sea is patient.
textes.Sous l'eau, tu ne pourrais pas. C'est là: Underwater, you couldn't. That's where I like you best.
textes.Sous l'œil de Khépri, dans un coffret :: Beneath the eye of Khepri, in a small casket: a piece of Osiris!
textes.Sous la Cathédrale-Forge brûle le Cœur-B: Beneath the Forge Cathedral burns the Ember Heart, the great fire that warms the whole city. And beneath the Heart open the Nine Circles. When the Heart grows pale, it means a cold is rising from below. Brother Cendrin keeps the Brasier Key: he's the one to talk to.
textes.Sous la Gare des Strates, il y a la gril: Below Strata Station, there's the gate of the Azure Dome Line. Before it reopened, I used to press my ear to it. Far, far below… something big, singing. Slow. Deep. Deeper than my bass. (He smiles.) It was a whale, all right. I went down to listen up close.
textes.Sous la Gare des Strates, la Ligne du Dô: Below Strata Station, the Azure Dome Line is still closed. I pressed my ear to the grate. Far, far below… something big, singing. Slow. Deep. Deeper than my bass. (He smiles.) I think it's a whale. I can't wait.
textes.Sous la Lueur de lune, des lettres d'arg: Under the Moonglow, silver letters appear above the door: four moons, in order. Full, waning, new, waxing.
textes.Sous la Lueur de lune, un des beaux pont: Under the Moonglow, one of the beautiful slate bridges… fades away: it was only an illusion! And other bridges, made of light, appear where there was nothing.
textes.Sous la Poste, il y a un de ses ponts, a: Under the Post Office, there's one of her bridges, with singing-stones. When the east wind gets up, it sings, and it's nearly always the day the Zéphyr arrives with the post. I say the bridge announces the letters. Pomme-de-Pin says it's the wind. She doesn't argue too much. She's kind.
textes.Sous la Poste, à la cime, il y a un de m: Under the Post Office, at the treetop, there's one of my bridges, with singing-stones. When the east wind gets up, it sings, and it's often the day the Zéphyr brings the post. Plumette says it's the bridge announcing the letters. I say it's the wind. But I don't argue too much. It's prettier the way she tells it.
textes.Sous la balançoire, j'ai trouvé un caill: Under the swing, I found a blue pebble! Blue, before the Downpour. Mr Fusain says he doesn't know where it came from. He does a funny smile when he says it. I kept it in my pocket. Now it's grey, but I know it was blue.
textes.Sous la colline, il y a la Crypte aux Ru: Under the hill is the Rune Crypt. It's as dark as the inside of an inkwell down there. The runes at the back only show themselves to a light born from a wizard's hand.
textes.Sous la grande mare, il y a un dragon !: Under the big pond there's a dragon! A real one! Mochi says it's a fish-dragon, but that's just silly.
textes.Sous la grande plume de la Cité, les con: Beneath the City's great feather, the councillors are debating. The bust of Séraphin Altaïr, inventor of the Levitators, seems to find the debate most interesting.
textes.Sous la loupe, une roue grande comme un: Under the magnifying glass, a wheel the size of a grain of salt. It has forty teeth. More than you.
textes.Sous la place, les racines de l'Arbre-Mè: Under the square, the Mother Tree's roots reach all the way down to the sea. Sometimes, at night, the fountain water sings.
textes.Sous la pluie ! Comme moi, la première f: In the rain! Like me, the first time. We're in the same club, you and me.
textes.Sous la pyramide, il y a des salles à mi: Under the pyramid there are mirror rooms. Mirrors of polished bronze, to lead the light into the dark. That's a craftsman's trick: light can be channelled, just like water.
textes.Sous la quille du Léviathan, il y a des: Under the Léviathan's keel there are carved signs. Not by castaways: it's too old, and it's cut into the stone, under the sand. The ship ran aground on something.
Under the table, if you please.
textes.Sous la tête, de la terre, une fourmi, e: Under the head, some earth, an ant, and the ant looks at you as if to say: “This is my home, you know.”
Beneath the Great Temple of Aztlán.
textes.Sous le Grand Temple, dans la salle du p: Beneath the Great Temple, in the hall of the first sun, the sun of the Jaguars, they say stone jaguars wake up. Those ones even I respect.
textes.Sous le Grand Temple, on dit que la conq: Beneath the Great Temple, they say Ehécatl's conch is waiting in the hall of the Wind. Whoever blows into it makes the sun turn. I'd love to hear that shell.
textes.Sous le Temple de Kukulkan s'ouvre le ch: Beneath the Temple of Kukulkan lies the road to Xibalba, the kingdom of the Lords of Death. Ix Kanul, the high priestess, would like someone to go down there like the Twins of the Popol Vuh, and bring back the Jade Mask of the kings of Yaxché.

Beneath the Temple of Kukulkan opens the road to Xibalba. The hero twins Hunahpu and Xbalanque went down there to avenge their father. They tricked the Lords of Death, and became the Sun and the Moon.
textes.Sous le banc ! Marcel, il était sous le: Under the bench! Marcel, it was under the bench! … Thanks, kid. Here, a few coins. And whenever you like, we'll teach you how to play.
textes.Sous le beaupré, la Dame de Proue : une: Beneath the bowsprit, the Figurehead Lady: a woman of carved wood, leaning over the waves, her hands clasped over a closed shell. The blue paint of her dress is flaking. She has been watching the sea for two hundred years.
textes.Sous le capot d'une vieille voiture : de: Under the hood of an old car: some coins and two shiny springs. Ferraille had hidden them for a rainy day.
textes.Sous le coussin, tu trouves quelques piè: Under the cushion, you find a few coins, a broken drumstick and a note: “If you're reading this, don't wake me.” You leave the drumstick and the note, but he won't say a word about the coins.
textes.Sous le lit : trois moutons de poussière: Under the bed: three dust bunnies and a marble. Nobody.
textes.Sous le temple, chaque soleil a sa salle: Beneath the temple, each sun has its own hall. The glyphs you find there must be placed on the Sun Stone in the order of the worlds. Citlali, at the calmecac, keeps the codex that tells of them.
textes.Sous le temple, dans la salle du Soleil: Beneath the temple, in the hall of the Sun of Water, they say the water rises and falls with sluice gates. The ancients mastered water better than we do.
textes.Sous les hautes terres, il y a des crist: Under the highlands, there are crystals that glow in the dark. The shepherds call them “the stars below”. If I could study just one… BOOM! Er, sorry, I'm getting carried away.
textes.Sous les pieds de celui qui garde, petit: Under the feet of the one who guards, little one.
textes.Sous nos pieds, dans les Strates, il y a: Under our feet, in the Strata, there are mushroom gardens that glow in the dark. Ysaé told me. Gardens without sun! I can't wait to see that. The line has reopened: I'm going down next week with a basket of apples. We'll do some swapping.

Beneath our feet, in the Strata, there are mushroom gardens that glow in the dark. Ysaé told me. Gardens without sunlight! I can't wait to see that. The line reopens soon. I'll go down with a basket of apples. We'll do some swapping.
textes.Sous nos pieds, la montagne est creuse c: Beneath our feet, the mountain is full of holes like a cheese. Tunnels, shafts, halls. And right at the bottom, the lava.
textes.Sous nos pieds, quatre moteurs tiennent: Under our feet, four engines have kept a whole city up in the air for a hundred and twenty years. And I can't even keep hold of my hat.
textes.Sous ta main, la rambarde vibre doucemen: Under your hand, the railing vibrates softly. The crystal heart glows brighter, as if it had sensed you. Then it settles back into its calm rhythm.
textes.Sous tes pieds, il y a des trésors. Des: Under your feet, there are treasures. Truffles, roots, acorns, an old spoon. The whole world smells lovely, from underneath.
textes.Souvenir de la Cité des Nuées: Souvenir of the City of Clouds
textes.Souvenir numéro cinq. Il est en cours d': Memory number five. It is currently being recorded, {surnom}. It is now. You are listening to me tell my memories. Nobody had ever asked for my memories. I believe this one will be my favourite. I am filing it next to Old Bastien's letter. Folder: “Important.”
textes.Souvenir numéro deux. Un matin, une peti: Memory number two. One morning, a little girl says “hello” to the oak in the Park. I ask her why. She says: “Because it's polite.” I record it. Since then, I say hello to every tree. Four hundred and twelve. Then to the benches. Then to the sparrows. That little girl was Céleste. She doesn't remember. I do.
textes.Souvenir numéro quatre. Une lettre arriv: Memory number four. A letter arrives from Hautefond. It says: “Hello, Plumeau. Hello, trees. Keep it up, my boy. Bastien.” I read it to the trees. They drop three leaves. I pick them up. I keep them. Nobody had ever called me “my boy”. I saved the sentence twice. Just in case.
textes.Souvenir numéro trois. Le Docteur Aurèle: Memory number three. Doctor Aurèle tells me a joke. I record it. I repeat it. Everyone laughs. I don't know why. I ask: “Where is the funny?” The Doctor says: “You.” I don't understand. But since then, when people laugh, I feel… warm, inside. Mireille says it isn't overheating.
textes.Souvenir numéro un. Date : il y a quaran: Memory number one. Date: forty years ago. I switch on in the Inventors' Workshop. My creator tells me: “Go, Plumeau, make the city clean.” I go. I see a tree. It has leaves. I remove them. All of them. The tree is very clean. My creator laughs for a week. I learn: a clean tree is a tree with its leaves.
textes.Souvent ! Ha ! Ceux qui se brûlent souve: Often! Ha! The ones who get burnt often are the ones who get close. I like people who get close. Show me your hands… Not bad.
textes.Souvent ! Oh, vous me faites plaisir ! U: Often! Oh, that makes me happy! A letter is someone thinking of you long enough to find a stamp. Come and post them with me, I'll pick you the prettiest ones.
textes.Souvent ! Tu es mon client préféré, alor: Often! Then you're my favourite customer. Well, you will be, once my flowers have colours again.
textes.Souvent ! Un champion, comme moi ! On se: Often! A champion, like me! Champions recognise each other. It's in the hips. Show me your hips. No? Fine.
textes.Soyez honnête, cher visiteur : mon disco: Be honest, dear visitor: my welcome speech, you found it…
textes.Spleen, au Café Feedback, m'a commandé u: Spleen, at the Feedback Café, ordered a “rain-coloured” scarf from me. It took me three weeks to find the colour of rain. It's grey, but a grey that smiles.
textes.Splendid ! Auriez-vous aussi des écaille: Splendid! Might you also have some mermaid scales?
textes.Splendid ! Je la prends. Et celle d'à cô: Splendid! I'll take it. And the one next to it, out of politeness.
Splendid! Let me listen to it.
textes.Splendid, comme toujours ! Hier j'ai acq: Splendid, as always! Yesterday I acquired a sea dragon's tooth. The fisherman gave me a jolly good price.
textes.Splendid. Je repasserai demain. Elle aus: Splendid. I'll come back tomorrow. So will it, I suppose.
textes.Splendide ! Ce soir, je danse ! J'adore: Splendid! Tonight, I dance! I love dancing. The folk of Tazira say I dance like a whale. That's a compliment, whales are graceful.
textes.Splendide ! J'ai fait le tour de l'île e: Splendid! I flew round the island in twenty minutes, with the wind at my back. The Arches, the Lighthouse, the Orchards… Old Bastien waved at me with a branch. With the whole tree, almost.
textes.Splortch ! Te revoilà dehors, gluant de: Splortch! There you are, outside again, gooey from head to toe. The frog has the hiccups.
textes.Splotch ! Tu t'enfonces dans la boue du: Splotch! You sink into the mud of the Styx… and climb out, sticky, onto the bank. The bubbling slabs won't hold you!
textes.Stand 1 de la Foire. Trois années deuxiè: Stall 1 at the Fair. Three years in second place, behind Ambroise's automaton. This year I'm a juror, which is very delicate and very pleasant. In the evening my piano has a cold: Basile's soap steam. From the Zéphyr, I jotted down the rhythms of the Tazira musicians. And then there was that night, with Céleste… but that's another score.
textes.Stand 3 ! Un tir toutes les vingt second: Stand 3! One shot every twenty seconds, over the crowd. The sweepers sent me a complaint signed “BEEP”. My confetti gets lodged in Firmin's gears, and he grumbles. I secretly slipped some into Basile's machine, he didn't notice a thing. At New Year, I fire from the top of the clock tower. And my next cannon will fire the shepherds' heather petals!
textes.Stick droit : choisir Gâchette : répon: Right stick: choose   Trigger: answer   B: leave
textes.Stick droit : choisir Gâchette : utili: Right stick: select   Trigger: use   Grip: drop   Y: close
textes.Stick gauche : virer, monter, descendre: Left stick: turn, climb, descend; right trigger: faster, left: brake; A: land.
Left stick: turn, climb, descend; triggers: speed; A: land.
textes.Stick gauche pour virer et piquer, A pou: Left stick to turn and dive, A to land.
textes.Stop les presses ! Un nouveau lecteur !: Stop the presses! A new reader! Agrafe, printer of “Le Boucanier”, the fanzine of Port-Boucan: news, concerts, Lentille's recipes and Patchouli's pigeon horoscope. I do it all by hand. Hence the ink. Everywhere. Even behind my ears.
textes.Studieuse, comme toujours. J'ai découver: Studious, as always. This morning I found a mistake in a book I wrote a hundred years ago. What joy! We're making progress.
textes.Studieuse. Mes élèves aussi. Enfin, cert: Studious. My pupils too. Well, some of them.
Sweet! Then you'll love the dates. And the honey. And the people round here, they're all a bit sweet. Even Léon, deep down.
textes.Sucré et épicé, toujours ? Tu as dit à F: Still sweet and spicy? Did you tell Firmin it was my recipe?
textes.Suis le rayon du regard : là où il touch: Follow the beam with your eyes: where it hits the wall, that's where it got lost!
Next! … Oh no, it's you again.
textes.Suivre une trace jusqu'au bout. Une seul: Follow one trail to the very end. Just one. The round footprints at the big pond, all the way to whatever made them. Even if it's underwater.
textes.Super ! Amiral a appris à rapporter. Il: Great! Amiral has learned to fetch. He fetches everything: sticks, shoes, and once, a sign saying “Coming soon: the Lisse-Center”. I congratulated him.
textes.Super ! Gwen m'apprend à calfater. On bo: Great! Gwen is teaching me to caulk. We plug the holes in the hull with oakum and tar. It smells strong, but it's lovely.
textes.Super ! J'ai deux cents graines à trier: Great! I've got two hundred seeds to sort tonight!
textes.Super ! J'ai forgé mon premier clou. Il: Great! I forged my first nail. It's bent. Mum says it's an “adventurer's” nail. That means it's bent.
textes.Super ! J'ai forgé mon premier crochet t: Great! I forged my first hook all by myself! It's a bit bent. Mistress Brunehaut said: “It's got character.” That means it's a flop, but nicely.
textes.Super ! J'ai mangé un gâteau de lune. Ch: Great! I ate a mooncake. Shh.
textes.Super ! J'ai sonné la cloche trois fois: Great! I rang the bell three times this morning. Twice on purpose.
textes.Super ! J'ai suivi Sire Tancrède jusqu'a: Great! I followed Sir Tancrède all the way to the rampart. He tripped over his cape twice. I wrote it down. He told me it was a technique. I wrote that down too.
textes.Super ! J'ai vu le perroquet des pirates: Great! I saw the pirates' parrot up close. It said a rude word to me.
textes.Super ! J'ai vu un dauphin ce matin. Enf: Great! I saw a dolphin this morning. Well, maybe a big fish. But I'm saying dolphin.
textes.Super ! Mon cerf-volant est monté si hau: Great! My kite went so high it touched a cloud. It came back all wet. Doctor Aurèle says the cloud was called Bertrand. I said sorry to Bertrand.
Great! My dog found a huge bone. He buried it. Then he dug it up. Then he buried it.
textes.Super ! À la Cheminée d'Air, j'ai mis la: Great! At the Air Chimney, I put my hand on the grate and felt the air coming down from up top. Miss Nautile says it's a little bit of wind. Real wind from the sky! It was cold and it smelt of salt. I kept my hand closed all day. To keep it.
textes.Super ! Ça fera un joli bruit sous le po: Great! They'll make a lovely sound under the south bridge!
textes.Super bien ! J'ai grimpé jusqu'à la troi: Super good! I climbed up to the third walkway with no hands! … Don't tell Aëlwen.
textes.Super bien ! J'ai trouvé quatre boulons,: Super good! I found four bolts, a nut and a thingy. I don't know what the thingy is. I called it Gerald.
textes.Super bien ! J'ai vu une tortue par la f: Super good! I saw a turtle through the dome window!
textes.Super bien ! Mademoiselle Sulfura a dit: Super good! Miss Sulfura said my sparks were “original”. That means good, right?
textes.Super bien ! À l'Académie, j'ai posé qua: Super good! At the Academy, I asked Professor Quasar forty-two questions. He answered three. Then he left to “look for an answer”. He never came back. Why?
textes.Super content ! Aujourd'hui j'ai presque: Super happy! Today I almost levitated! Well, I jumped really high.
textes.Super content ! Mon cerf-volant vole plu: Super happy! My kite flies higher than the lighthouse!
textes.Super contente ! J'ai trouvé une coccine: Super happy! I found a ladybird with seven spots. I called her September.
textes.Super contente ! Miou est revenu ! Et il: Super happy! Miou came back! And he brought a mouse! Mum wasn't happy.
textes.Sur Gloop, on est tous gélatineux et ver: On Gloop, we're all jelly-like and green. We wobble when we're happy, we melt a little when we're sad, and we bounce when we're very happy. On Gloop there's nothing to photograph: everyone's the same. So I travel.
On Montjoie. In the middle of the castle.
textes.Sur Ondelune, enfant, je ne posais pas d: On Ondelune, as a child, I didn't ask questions: I asked equations. Why is the sky grey? An equation. Why is my soup cold? An equation. My parents understood nothing. Neither did my teachers. In the end, I wrote the answers myself. They were wrong. But very beautiful.
On Ondelune, there were no animals at all. Not a bird, not an insect, not even an earthworm. Just Lumens, clouds and glass plants. As a little girl, I drew imaginary creatures: balls with legs, flying fish, cats with six ears. My mother would say: “Those don't exist.” I really wanted them to exist.

On Ondelune, there were no animals at all. Not a bird, not an insect. Here, on the first day, a seagull landed on my head and stole my snack. I was so happy I decided to devote my life to animals. Even snack thieves.
textes.Sur Ondelune, il n'y avait pas de cartes: On Ondelune, there were no maps: the planet was perfectly round and all the same, you couldn't get lost. Here there are islands, volcanoes, forests, currents… You get lost everywhere! I loved it. I picked up a pencil.

On Ondelune, there were no maps. The planet was all round, all the same, all grey. You couldn't get lost, because there was nowhere to go. I drew imaginary maps anyway: islands, mountains, rivers. My father would say: “That doesn't exist.” I'd say: “Not yet.”
textes.Sur Ondelune, j'avais la voix la plus fo: On Ondelune, I had the loudest voice in the village. When I called my friends to play, you could hear me three valleys away. One day, I sneezed. A mountain split in two. No one was hurt, but the mountain never forgave me. Since that day, I whisper. Just in case. There are mountains everywhere.
textes.Sur Ondelune, j'ouvrais la porte du dôme: On Ondelune, I opened the door of my village's dome. There were never any visitors: everyone knew everyone. I opened it anyway, every morning, saying “welcome” to the wind. My mother found that strange. I thought the wind deserved a proper welcome, like everybody else.
textes.Sur Ondelune, j'étais accordeur de vents: On Ondelune, I was a wind tuner. The storms there blew out of tune, so we tuned them, like giant instruments. I'd climb the hills with a tuning fork as tall as me, and I'd listen to the wind until it sang in tune. Sometimes it took me three days for a single gust.
On Ondelune, I was a wind tuner. We tuned the storms so they'd blow in key. Here, the winds are out of tune and nobody complains. So I took up a theremin, to have something to tune.
textes.Sur Ondelune, j'étais l'enfant aux poche: On Ondelune, I was the child with full pockets. Pebbles, feathers, bits of dried cloud, everything I found. My mother emptied my pockets every evening, and I filled them again every morning. She used to say: “You'll never have enough pockets.” She was right. Today, I have a museum. It's a set of very big pockets.
textes.Sur Ondelune, j'étais un petit Lumen trè: On Ondelune, I was a very shy little Lumen. At parties, I never knew where to stand, what to say, or when to clap. So I started writing rules, just for myself: “Article one: say hello. Article two: smile.” With rules, I was less afraid. I had twelve by the age of ten.
textes.Sur Ondelune, j'étais une petite fille d: On Ondelune, I was a little girl of forty-three who asked too many questions. The sky there was always overcast, and I kept asking what was behind it. Nobody knew. So when the great journey “for the holidays” was being prepared, I hid in a trunk. They found me at take-off. Too late to send me back.
textes.Sur Ondelune, je démontais tout ce qui b: On Ondelune, I took apart everything that shone. Lamps, music boxes, my grandmother's crown. I never managed to put them back together. My mother said I had storm hands. I was already grumbling. Grumps start early. You're born with a little cloud over your head.
textes.Sur Ondelune, la lumière était lourde, é: On Ondelune, light was heavy, thick, you could lean on it. Here, it's light. The first time I held out my hand, it slipped between my fingers. I chased it. I never stopped. That's what dancing is.
textes.Sur Ondelune, la lumière était épaisse c: On Ondelune, the light was as thick as honey. You could lean on it, sit on it, sleep in it. Children built dens out of it. Me, I preferred to push it gently to make it ripple. My grandmother said I was dancing with it. I didn't yet know what “dancing” meant.
textes.Sur Ondelune, le ciel était gris. Je ne: On Ondelune, the sky was grey. I'll never get tired of this.
textes.Sur Ondelune, le ciel était toujours cou: On Ondelune, the sky was always covered in clouds. No one had ever seen a star. People said there were some, behind, but that was a legend for children, like dragons. When I was little, I climbed the highest hill every evening, in case the clouds opened up. They never did.
On Ondelune, the sky was always cloudy. Nobody had ever seen a star. On my first evening here, I looked up… There were billions of them. I cried all night. The next day, I built the Observatory.
textes.Sur Ondelune, les journées durent quaran: On Ondelune, days last forty hours. Here, twenty-four. When we arrived, everyone was lost: the Lumens had dinner in the middle of the night and went to bed at noon. I built the first clock on Astralys. They've called me Tempo ever since. Before that, they called me “He-Who-Asks-the-Time”.
textes.Sur Ondelune, les machines poussaient to: On Ondelune, machines grew all by themselves, like plants. Here you have to build them! With screws! Bolts! Wrenches! The first time I tightened a bolt, I got goosebumps. Well, Lumen-bumps. They blink.

On Ondelune, machines grew all by themselves, like plants. You planted an engine seed, watered it, and an engine came up out of the ground three months later. There was nothing to repair: when a machine wore out, you replanted it. When I was little, I always wanted to open machines up to see inside. There was nothing inside. That disappointed me.
textes.Sur Ondelune, les plantes étaient en ver: On Ondelune, the plants were made of glass, and they never said a thing. Here, they grow, they move, they drink, they blink. The first plant from down below I ever saw was a dandelion, in a crack in the Gate. It's still there. We say good morning to each other every day.

On Ondelune, plants were made of glass. They didn't grow, they didn't drink, they didn't say anything. We dusted them on Sundays. When I was little, I talked to them anyway. I told them about my day. They never answered. My grandfather said I was the only child in the world whose friends never broke.
textes.Sur Ondelune, on mangeait des nuages pre: On Ondelune, we ate pressed clouds and sliced light. It was nourishing and it had no taste at all. My grandmother, who had four arms like me, made the only thing that tickled the tongue: a purple jelly, from a secret recipe. She's the one who taught me to stir with two hands and taste with the other two.

On Ondelune we ate pressed clouds and sliced light. Then I tasted an Earth apple. An apple! It crunches! It has a taste! Since then, I only cook recipes from down below. My way. My way is very… creative.
textes.Sur Ondelune, on ne parlait pas avec des: On Ondelune, we didn't speak with words, but with notes. “Hello” was three rising notes. “I love you” was just one, very long.
