textes.Toi qui préfères la surprise : la boule: You who prefer surprises: the ball saw something for you last night. I won't say a word. You made your choice.
textes.Toi qui préfères le jour, viens quand mê: You who prefer the day, come one evening anyway. I'll show you what the sun can't do.
textes.Toi qui préfères les boums, je t'inviter: You who prefer booms, I'll invite you to the test of my next machine. Wear goggles. And a helmet.
textes.Toi qui préfères les chats : Suie, mon c: You who prefer cats: Suie, my most timid pup, behaves almost like a cat. He sleeps in a watering can. You'd like him.
textes.Toi qui préfères les chats… Si un jour t: You who prefer cats… If one day you have one, bring it here. I won't touch it. Well, just a tiny bit. With one fingertip.
textes.Toi qui préfères les chiens : Biscotte t: You who prefer dogs: Biscotte was asking for you yesterday. Well, he barked in your direction. Same thing.
textes.Toi qui préfères les chiens, Pneu se rou: You're a dog person, so Pneu rolls on the ground every time he sees you. He hasn't forgotten.
textes.Toi qui préfères les chiens… Est-ce qu'i: You who prefer dogs… Do they really wag their tails all the time? I've been wondering since our last conversation.
textes.Toi qui préfères les chiffres : j'ai un: You who prefer numbers: I have a forty-one-move problem to show you. It isn't finished.
textes.Toi qui préfères les chèvres : la petite: You who prefer goats: the little black one recognised you just now. She tried to eat your sleeve. That's a good sign.
textes.Toi qui préfères les débuts… Il était un: You who prefer beginnings… Once upon a time, there was a traveller who came back to see an old storyteller. There. That's you. It's off to a good start.
textes.Toi qui préfères les inventées : je t'en: You who prefer made-up ones: I've made one up for you. It happened yesterday. Sit down.
textes.Toi qui préfères les lettres, tu peux di: You who prefer letters, can you tell Rosette there was an “r” missing in this morning's Gazette? I counted.
textes.Toi qui préfères les maisons rondes… Je: You, who prefer round houses… I drew you a little dome on my tablet. Just for fun. It has a sun-shaped window.
textes.Toi qui préfères les souvenirs. Tiens, r: You, who prefer memories. Here, look at this pebble: it comes from a planet where people never forget each other. It's for you. Free.
textes.Toi qui préfères les vagues… viens sur l: You who prefer the waves… come to the jetty at sunset. We'll play together, them and me.
textes.Toi qui préfères mes méduses ! Elles t'o: You who prefer my jellyfish! They recognised you, you know. They sing a little higher when you come into the Greenhouse.
textes.Toi qui préfères nager : je te garde une: You'd rather swim: I'll keep a towel for you by the dance floor. And a banana, for afterwards.
textes.Toi qui préfères parler en vrai : tu vas: You who'd rather talk face to face: how are you? See, I'm asking you face to face. But I could also write it to you.
textes.Toi qui préfères regarder, je t'ai gardé: You who prefer watching, I kept a photo of the auroras for you. The most beautiful one. Look at it when you're sad. It wobbles a little.
textes.Toi qui préfères une autre taverne… J'ai: You who prefer another tavern… I've invented a new frozen lava to make you change your mind. It's ready. It's waiting for you.
textes.Toi qui préfères écrire… tu crois qu'une: You'd rather write… do you think a letter counts as much as words said face to face? Say yes.
textes.Toi qui prétends ne jamais monter en bat: You claim you never get on boats, but Albertine saw your boat at the jetty again. She's laughing.
textes.Toi qui préviendrais la garde : si tu vo: You who'd tell the guard: if you see something at night, come up. I don't sleep anyway.
textes.Toi qui ralentis pour les beaux paysages: You who slow down for beautiful scenery… I tried it yesterday, over the sea. It was beautiful. Then I sped up anyway.
textes.Toi qui regardes les champignons sans le: You who look at mushrooms without touching them, you're the wisest of my visitors. I told Gustave, the big blue one.
textes.Toi qui regardes les flammes avant de le: You, who watch the flames before touching them, would make an excellent student. Better than half my class. Better than Pépin, anyway.
textes.Toi qui regardes tes pieds : j'ai resser: You who look at your feet: I've tightened two ropes on the south bridge. It dances more calmly now. Just for you.
textes.Toi qui rendrais la baguette à sa fée… j: You'd give the wand back to its fairy… I've put you in my book, on the page for good people. There's only you and Brindille.
textes.Toi qui resterais ici pour toujours… tu: You, who'd stay here forever… see, you're still here. So am I. We're holding on!
textes.Toi qui répares : j'ai une cruche fêlée: You who mend things: I have a cracked jug waiting for you. Shall we stitch it up together?
textes.Toi qui répares : si tu as une heure, il: You who mend things: if you've got an hour, there's a leak under the forge. No, I'm joking. Almost.
textes.Toi qui rêves d'aventures, j'ai prié pou: You dream of adventures, so I've prayed that yours end well. The night ones and the day ones.
textes.Toi qui rêves les yeux ouverts, viens t': You dream with your eyes open, so come and sit by the pond. Yggdrasil grows upside down in it. It's a good place for dreaming.
textes.Toi qui sais attendre : le ponton est li: You who know how to wait: the jetty's free. Sit down. The King likes patient folk.
textes.Toi qui sais attendre, assieds-toi. On n: You who know how to wait, sit down. We won't catch anything, but we'll do it properly.
textes.Toi qui sais attendre… assieds-toi, il r: You who know how to wait… sit down, it's cooling.
textes.Toi qui sais faire des châteaux, viens v: You know how to make castles, come and see mine! It's got five towers now. You can do the moat.
textes.Toi qui sais faire le nœud de chaise : t: You who can tie a bowline: here, mend this bit of net for me. I trust you.
textes.Toi qui sais faire les nœuds, tu me rame: You who can tie knots, will you mend a corner of net for me? Just a corner. I'll check it.
textes.Toi qui sais nager ! Tu plongeras cherch: You can swim! You'll dive for the King, won't you? I'll hold your towel.
textes.Toi qui sais pas nager : je connais quel: You, who can't swim: I know somebody very big who's very good at holding belts. If you like.
textes.Toi qui sais que Xan est le seul moustiq: You who know Xan is the only mosquito with a name: you're my best friend. After Peek'. And Pilli.
textes.Toi qui sais que c'est pareil, garde ta: You who know they're the same, keep your place in the circle. One day, you'll be the one telling.
textes.Toi qui sais réparer une crevaison, j'ai: You who can fix a puncture, I've got fourteen bikes waiting for you. Just kidding. Thirteen.
textes.Toi qui sais tenir un marteau. … Tes mai: You who can hold a hammer. … Your hands. Still no blisters? Hm.
textes.Toi qui sais écrire ton nom : il me manq: You who can write your name: I'm still missing a potsherd signed by your hand in my House of Life.
textes.Toi qui sens les épices d'abord, viens v: You who smell the spices first, come quick: I've had cumin from the oasis. Your nose deserves it.
textes.Toi qui serais un chien, je t'ai dessiné: You'd be a dog, so I drew you with a bandana in my last zine. Page four. With one ear up.
textes.Toi qui siffles, siffle-moi un air, la p: You whistle, so whistle me a tune next time. I'll sing over it.
textes.Toi qui soignes tes chagrins en mangeant: You, who treat your sorrows by eating… Gloubi made moon biscuits this morning. I'm prescribing you one biscuit. Doctor's orders.
textes.Toi qui soignes tout avec une brioche :: You, who cure everything with a brioche: I did some research. It cures nothing. But people who eat them smile more. Duly noted.
textes.Toi qui suis les lanternes : tes bottes: You who follow the lanterns: your boots smell of bridge mushrooms. Good. You listened.
textes.Toi qui suis toujours les ordres, en voi: You who always follow orders, here's one: get some rest. … See, that wasn't hard.
textes.Toi qui t'arrêterais en gagnant : je t'o: You, who'd stop while winning: I've been watching you since. You keep your word. That's rare. Almost worrying.
textes.Toi qui t'es déjà perdu une fois, retien: You who've been lost once, remember: here, you follow the glowing mushrooms. That's Pépin's rule!
textes.Toi qui t'habilles pour être beau : tu t: You who dress to look good: you've been standing better since. I noticed. I notice everything. The left sleeve, on the other hand…
textes.Toi qui t'habilles pour être beau, ta ca: You dress to look good, so your cape is coming along. It already has a golden lining.
textes.Toi qui t'habilles pour être bien : je t: You who dress to feel good: I saw you go by, you looked good. That's the finest compliment I know how to give.
textes.Toi qui t'intéresses à ton passé… je l'a: You, who are interested in your past… I looked at it again last night. It's bigger than you, your past.
textes.Toi qui t'orientes bien : tes bottes son: You with the good sense of direction: your boots went past the same spot twice yesterday. I'm not saying anything. I'm reading.
textes.Toi qui t'écrirais avec un animal : alor: You who'd write yourself with an animal: so, have you chosen? Pilli suggests a hairless dog. Of course.
textes.Toi qui t'écrirais avec un soleil : je t: You who'd write yourself with a sun: I drew you a little fifth sun in my codex. It moves.
textes.Toi qui tapes avec ton épée sans t'en oc: You hit things with your sword without looking after it, so drop by the forge. I bet it needs me.
textes.Toi qui te bats pour la gloire : attenti: You who fight for glory: beware of pride. I know. I've been told. Often.
textes.Toi qui te bats pour tes amis : je suis: You who fight for your friends: am I your friend? … Don't answer. I'll see.
textes.Toi qui te brûles souvent : va voir Mère: You who get burnt often: go and see Mother Sage before me next time. She's got an ointment that smells of honey.
textes.Toi qui te caches. Bien. Cache-toi derri: You who hide. Good. Hide behind the Lookout: I can see you. Well. I will see you.
textes.Toi qui te lèves avant le soleil : un ma: You who rise before the sun: one morning, come and sing with me on the terrace. Nebet will teach you the sistrum.
textes.Toi qui te lèves avec le soleil : la deu: You who get up with the sun: the second batch has just come out. Just for you. And for the sun.
textes.Toi qui te lèves avec le soleil : vous o: You who rise with the sun: you open your eyes at the same time, the two of you. He's watching you, you know.
textes.Toi qui te perds exprès : tu t'es perdu: You who get lost on purpose: where have you got lost since last time? Tell me, I've got my pencil.
textes.Toi qui te sens tout petit sous le ciel…: You who feel very small under the sky… You know, seen from a star, we're all tiny. And yet, it shines for us.
textes.Toi qui te souviens de tous tes rêves… r: You remember all your dreams… tell me one, some day. Up here, dreams are news.
textes.Toi qui tiens tes promesses : je m'en so: You who keep your promises: I remember. There aren't so many of you on this quay.
textes.Toi qui tiens un peu le marteau. … Un pe: You who can hold a hammer a bit. … A bit is good. Strike straight. The iron will listen to you.
textes.Toi qui trouves la grenouille délicieuse: Since you find frog delicious, I've saved you a portion of number fourteen. With extra cream.
textes.Toi qui vas voir de plus près. Hm. Si tu: You who go for a closer look. Hm. If you see something, tell Brume. Then me. In that order.
textes.Toi qui veux des histoires vraies : cell: You, who want true stories: tonight's one, I swear it's true. Almost entirely.
textes.Toi qui veux jamais rester nulle part… t: You who never wanna stay anywhere… have you tasted Mustapha's sardines yet? Well?
textes.Toi qui veux le vrai et le beau en même: You, who want the true and the beautiful at the same time, you're in for a treat. Sit down: it's always both.
textes.Toi qui veux toujours la réponse… j'en a: You always want the answer… I've got one for you today. But first you'll have to find the question.
textes.Toi qui veux être le héros des chansons,: You want to be the hero of songs, so the fourth one's ready. You defeat a storm in it. With your hat.
textes.Toi qui viens d'une île lointaine… tu n': You who come from a faraway island… you wouldn't have a seed from home at the bottom of a pocket? Look carefully.
textes.Toi qui viens de la mer… tu n'aurais pas: You who come from the sea… you haven't come across a seaweed seed, have you? I've already made room for it.
textes.Toi qui viens pour le poisson : aujourd': You who come for the fish: today I've got sea bream. Not for Zohra. For you.
textes.Toi qui vis le moment sans photo… J'ai e: You who live in the moment without photos… I tried it, for one whole minute. It was very beautiful. Then I took a photo of the minute.
textes.Toi qui vois Tazira blanche, va regarder: You who see Tazira as white, go and look at the walls at six o'clock. They're pink. Then come back and tell me they're white.
textes.Toi qui vois bien de près… si tu croises: You who see well up close… if you come across my glasses, let me know. They're surely very near.
textes.Toi qui vois des boulons à vendre, je t': You see bolts to sell, so I'll always buy yours. Brindezingue needs a new wing.
textes.Toi qui vois des histoires dans le ciel: You who see stories in the sky: ours begins in Xibalba. And ends up there.
textes.Toi qui vois des étoiles : regarde Vénus: You who see stars: look at Venus tonight, from the platform. She rises for you too.
textes.Toi qui vois très loin : notre concours: You who can see very far: our contest is still on. The bucket's ready. I put it… I don't remember where.
textes.Toi qui voulais apprendre ton nom à un p: You who wanted to teach a parrot your name: I think about it often. It's a very good idea. I had it too.
textes.Toi qui voulais connaître ton avenir… il: You who wanted to know your future… is it unfolding nicely? The cards are asking after you.
textes.Toi qui voulais danser jusqu'à cinq heur: You wanted to dance till five and fish afterwards… The boat has a corner for sleeping, I'm warning you.
textes.Toi qui voulais dormir mille ans… tu as: You, who wanted to sleep a thousand years… you look wide awake today. A little nap with me, on the bench?
textes.Toi qui voulais faire voter la soupe pou: You wanted to put soup for everyone to the vote, and Lentille sends his regards. He said you're made of presidential stuff.
textes.Toi qui voulais garder la porte : tu ne: You who wanted to guard the gate: you only let the nice ones in, all right? And the Archduchess goes out whenever she likes. That's the rule.
textes.Toi qui voulais garder le rempart : cour: You, who wanted to guard the ramparts: brave or dreamer? I think about it often. I believe you're both.
textes.Toi qui voulais le bassin où les cornes: You who wanted the pool where horns melt… I dipped a toe in yesterday. I can't feel it any more. You were right: it's the best one.
textes.Toi qui voulais le rat des Rats de Cale,: You wanted the Bilge Rats' rat, so I've put one aside for you. The best one. The mohawk is hand-sewn, hair by hair.
textes.Toi qui voulais les deux : regarde bien: You wanted both: take a good look at the Shark tonight, under the lanterns. That's what it looks like.
textes.Toi qui voulais un feu d'artifice éterne: You, who wanted an everlasting firework: I look at the stars differently now. I wonder who lit them. And with what.
textes.Toi qui voulais un navire rapide : le Re: You wanted a fast ship: the Shark makes twelve knots. But it's Gros-Louis who hoists the sails. Think about it.
textes.Toi qui voulais une machine à faire les: You, who wanted a homework machine: Ortie has improved it. It does the homework, then marks it. Very strictly.
textes.Toi qui voulais une machine à voler : la: You, who wanted a flying machine: the fourth one is almost ready! It doesn't fly yet, but it floats. In the fountain.
textes.Toi qui voulais visiter toutes les îles,: You wanted to visit every island, and it looks like you've come a long way. Will you tell me about the ones I don't know?
textes.Toi qui voyages : quand tu arrives quelq: You, the traveller: when you arrive somewhere, do you look at the map first, or do you get lost on purpose?
textes.Toi qui voyages, dis-moi : quelle île pr: You're a traveller, tell me: which island down below do you like best?
textes.Toi qui voyages, {surnom}… tu as déjà es: You who travel, {surnom}… have you ever tried counting the stars?
textes.Toi qui voyages… qu'est-ce qui brille le: You who travel… what shines brightest, on the other islands?
textes.Toi qui voyages… tu crois aux histoires: You, a traveller… you believe Old Silas's stories, eh?
textes.Toi qui voyais juste un tas de ferraille: You saw just a pile of scrap — have you looked again? There's a duck in the pile near the entrance. Look carefully.
textes.Toi qui vérifies si les plumes sont vrai: You who check whether feathers are real: the ones on my stall are all real. Today. Look closely all the same.
textes.Toi qui écoutes la mer. (Il te fait une: You who listen to the sea. (He makes room for you by the fire.)
textes.Toi qui écoutes la mer… Tu as entendu un: You who listen to the sea… Have you heard a new song since?
textes.Toi qui écoutes le Réveil du Rat, je t'a: You who listen to The Rat's Wake-Up Call, I gave you a shout-out this morning! Did you hear it? No? I'll do it again tomorrow.
textes.Toi qui écoutes les conseils, j'en ai un: You listen to advice, so here's a new one: don't listen to me when I say I'm going to succeed.
textes.Toi qui écoutes les coquillages : il y e: You who listen to shells: there's one on the shore that sings in B flat. I'll show it to you.
textes.Toi qui étais très sage… Je ne te crois: You were very good… I still don't believe you. Neither does Button.
textes.Toi qui évites les combats : tu as l'air: You who avoid fights: you look in great shape. That's a strategy too.
You too skinny. Not enough squares.
textes.Toi à qui les câlins font du bien… Si un: You, who feel better with a hug… If one day you're feeling sad, my healing bubble is open. The hug is free.
textes.Toi à qui personne ne racontait d'histoi: You, whom nobody told stories to… I save one for you every time. You've got catching up to do.
textes.Toi, au moins, tu paies en pièces ! Mon: You, at least, pay in coins! My favourite customer. Don't tell my uncle, he'd disown me.
textes.Toi, c'est bien sucré, je n'ai pas oubli: You take it nice and sweet, I haven't forgotten. Your glass gets one more lump than the others.
textes.Toi, c'est l'eau fraîche, je sais. Avec: You're the cool-water one, I know. With the umbrella. I'm not judging. Well, a little.
textes.Toi, c'est le cumin, je m'en souviens. J: You're the cumin one, I remember. I'll add an extra pinch. Aïcha won't know a thing.
textes.Toi, c'est le poisson et la voix. Le men: You're the fish and the voice. The full menu. Your note of the day? SARDIIINES!
textes.Toi, c'est mystère. Je t'en garde un fon: You're a mystery person. I save you a drop every evening. It changes every day. That's the whole idea.
textes.Toi, l'amateur de miel : chut. On n'en p: You, the honey lover: shh. We don't talk about it at the market. Ever.
textes.Toi, l'ami de la menthe ! Elle a beaucou: You, mint's friend! It's grown a lot since.
textes.Toi, l'ami des chats… Tu n'aurais pas cr: You, the friend of cats… You haven't run into the ginger one, by any chance? You'd tell me, eh? EH?
textes.Toi, l'ami des lanternes : je t'ai gardé: You, friend of lanterns: I saved you the spot by the wall. That's where the stars fall best.
textes.Toi, l'ancre : alors, tu as trouvé ton p: You, the anchor: so, have you found your port? My tent is open, the day you make up your mind.
textes.Toi, l'aventurier à la pomme, je t'ai à: You, the apple adventurer, I've got my eye on you. And I've got a pie for you.
textes.Toi, l'enfant des histoires de pirates !: You, the child of pirate stories! I've found one in my memory: a pirate who was scared of water. Sit down.
textes.Toi, l'expert de l'œil ! Regarde ma daur: You, the eye expert! Look at my sea bream: it's giving you the eye, isn't it? Caught this morning.
textes.Toi, l'humain ! Tu as l'air fatigué. Vie: You there, human! You look tired. Come and see my potions!
textes.Toi, l'épée à une main. Montre ton poign: You, the one-handed sword. Show me your wrist. … Hm. Looser. Always looser.
textes.Toi, la garance… tu as encore ce regard: You, Madder… you've still got that stubborn-root look. I like it.
textes.Toi, la personne du matin ! Passe au Pai: Hey, morning person! Drop by the Pain Doré at six, I'll keep the first croissant for you. Piping hot.
textes.Toi, la pipelette : alors, quelles nouve: Hey, chatterbox: so, what's the news? Come, sit down, the flatbread is hot.
You, the tart one. I forgive you. A little.
textes.Toi, le bec sucré ! Ta place est là, prè: You, the sweet tooth! Your place is right here, by the moon biscuits. I don't count them. Well, I do. But I pretend not to.
textes.Toi, le bleu indigo, je t'ai mis de côté: For you, Indigo Blue, I've put a thread aside. It never fades. Like you, I hope.
textes.Toi, le buveur de thé au rhum ! Je t'ai: You, the rum-in-your-tea drinker! I've got my eye on you. Don't go near the tavern with my glass.
textes.Toi, le casseur ! Les mains dans le dos,: You, the breaker! Hands behind your back, please. My jugs recognised you.
textes.Toi, le citron ! Je t'ai gardé un quarti: You, the lemon one! I saved you a wedge. After the embers, never before, remember?
textes.Toi, le danseur en cachette… Ce soir, il: You, the secret dancer… Tonight there'll be a shady corner near the amin's bench. There'll be two of you.
textes.Toi, le démonteur. Je t'ai à l'œil. Si u: You, the dismantler. I've got my eye on you. If a screw goes missing from the Spire, I'll know where to look.
textes.Toi, le fan de coco… tu es allé goûter c: You, the coconut fan… did you go and try Kiki's? Traitor. Just kidding. So, which one's better?
textes.Toi, le mangeur de noix de coco ! J'ai r: Ah, the coconut eater! I made my coconut brioche again. The oven didn't sulk for a second.
textes.Toi, le marcheur ! Tu sais quoi ? Dans l: You, the walker! Know what? On the hills, walking's not so bad. Between you and me.
textes.Toi, le petit cœur : j'ai gardé un modèl: You, the little heart: I've kept a design for you. Tiny. I don't show it to anyone.
textes.Toi, le poète qui trouve que la mer bril: You, the poet who thinks the sea shines: got any coins today? No? I thought as much.
textes.Toi, le roi de la bière pour tous : Ulfa: You, the king of fizz-for-all: Ulfa sends her regards. She says if you ever take a throne, she's moving out.
textes.Toi, le silencieux. J'ai réglé un bouton: You, the quiet one. I've set a knob just for your silence.
textes.Toi, le tapeur de machines ! Je t'ai à l: You, the machine-thumper! I've got my eye on you. If a saucer has a dent, I'll know who repaired it.
You there, bone-dry! Come over here.
textes.Toi, le vertige. Hrmm. Je tire doucement: You. Scared of heights. Hrmm. I pull gently. Promise.
textes.Toi, le « pas encore » ! Alors, c'est po: Well, if it isn't “Not Yet”! So, when's it going to be? The starting arch hasn't moved, and neither has my stopwatch.
textes.Toi, le « quelles dettes ? » : je t'ai d: You, Mr “What debts?”: I've drawn you on my slate. Just in case.
textes.Toi, le « ça dépend »… je t'observe touj: You, Mr “it depends”… I'm still watching you. You've got Mbarek's look, right before he says “No”.
textes.Toi, les grands pieds ! Je me suis tromp: You, the big feet! I was wrong about you, like with Mbarek. I won't forget it, it hurts.
textes.Toi, là ! Tu regardes mon navire ?: You there! Are you eyeing my ship?
textes.Toi, là ! Une question, une seule !: You there! One question, just one!
textes.Toi, là ! Une tasse de thé ? Ça réchauff: You there! A cup of tea? It warms you up, even androids.
textes.Toi, là ! Viens donc boire une tisane av: You, there! Come and have a herbal tea with an old lady!
textes.Toi, là ! Viens donc voir une vieille da: You there! Come and see an old lady.
textes.Toi, là, avec tes yeux tout ronds ! Vien: You there, with the big round eyes! Come and sit by the fire.
textes.Toi, là. Tu n'aurais pas un ressort, par: You there. You wouldn't happen to have a spring on you?
textes.Toi, mon petit. Viens écouter une histoi: You, little one. Come and hear a story.
textes.Toi, ni les chiffres ni les lettres. Alo: You, neither numbers nor letters. So I made you a drawing. There are still numbers on it. A few.
You did. Him, I don't know.
textes.Toi, sois honnête : tu marchandes ?: You there, be honest: do you haggle?
textes.Toi, t'as toujours faim, comme moi ! Si: You're always hungry, like me! If you run into Mange-Clous, tell him it's for two.
textes.Toi, t'as une tête qui ne me revient pas: I don't like the look of you.
You, talk too much. Like before.
textes.Toi, tu as assez bu pour aujourd'hui. Un: You, you've had enough to drink for today. A glass of water, and off to bed!
textes.Toi, tu as dit que je n'aurais jamais pe: You said I'd never be scared. I told the crystal, and Abyssos wrote it down. It's official.
textes.Toi, tu as quelqu'un qui est un peu ta m: Do you have someone who's a bit like your other half? A brother, a sister, someone far away?
textes.Toi, tu as vu la baleine. Immense. Je te: You've seen the whale. Enormous. Sometimes I look at you and think: those eyes have seen it.
textes.Toi, tu boudes moins depuis que tu mange: You sulk less since you started eating breakfast.
textes.Toi, tu commences sérieusement à me chau: You're seriously starting to get on my nerves.
textes.Toi, tu frappes aux portes. Bien. C'est: You knock at doors. Good. That's rare. The others dig underneath. Hmph.
You show your boo-boos straight away. Keep it up. I'm proud of you. That's rare around here.
textes.Toi, tu ne ferais rien si tu voyais des: You wouldn't do anything if you saw lights. I remember. I'm watching you too.
textes.Toi, {surnom}, tu préfères les choses qu: What about you, {surnom}: do you prefer things that last a hundred years, or things that change every day?
textes.Toi, {surnom}, tu préfères quoi : les ch: You, {surnom}, what do you prefer: the fields, the town, or the sea?
textes.Toi, {surnom}. Tu te bats pour quoi ?: You, {surnom}. What do you fight for?
textes.Toi, {surnom}… Pas de hop, cette fois. L: You, {surnom}… No hop, this time. The cup from two years ago, I turned it to face the wall of my room. I'm ashamed I didn't stop for Éclair. Grisou, he shouted “you OK?”. And I'm scared. Not of losing the race: of not knowing who I am any more, if I'm not the champion. Bondi running at the back, who's that?
textes.Toi, ça fait longtemps que je voulais te: You, I've been wanting to tell you this for ages!
You. No more than two strikes. I'm counting.
textes.Toi. Quand tu arrives devant une porte f: You. When you come to a closed door, what do you do?
textes.Toi. TOI. Tu m'as battu. Personne ne m'a: You. YOU. You beat me. Nobody's ever beaten me. … I'm in a very bad mood. Even worse than usual.
textes.Toi. Tu as déjà vu une lumière que perso: You. Have you ever seen a light that nobody else saw?
textes.Toi. Tu m'as mise au tapis, l'autre jour: You. You knocked me down the other day. That doesn't happen to me often. … I didn't like it. But I respect it.
textes.Toi. Tu sais tenir un marteau ?: You. Can you hold a hammer?
textes.Toile, engrenages, cristaux, fleurs, et: Cloth, gears, crystals, flowers, and treasures from your islands! The astral crystal is pricey: it comes from a difficult place. The duck comes from Cliquetis. That's a difficult place too. You have {pieces} washers.
textes.Toi… le silence entre les deux… J'y pens: You… the silence in between… I think about it when I play. You got me.
You… come here and let me archive you.
textes.Tom ! Bartholomé est prêt pour ce soir !: Tom! Bartholomé is ready for tonight!
textes.Tom ! Joue vite, ce soir, j'ai envie de: Tom! Play fast tonight, I feel like dancing.
textes.Tom ! L'apprenti de la Grande Forge ! Tu: Tom! The apprentice at the Great Forge! Do you know him? He forged me a little plate for my board, with my name on it: “RESORT”. There's an S missing. We didn't say anything. It's perfect.
textes.Tom ! Tu as encore tapé pendant la pause: Tom! Have you been tapping during the break again?
textes.Tom ! Tu me chantes mon couplet ?: Tom! Will you sing me my verse?
textes.Tom a mis mon nom dans sa chanson. Je ne: Tom put my name in his song. I've never heard it. He sings too softly. And people laugh at my verse. WHY ARE THEY LAUGHING?
textes.Tom a onze ans, des bras en coton et un: Tom is eleven, with cotton-wool arms and a blacksmith's heart. He taps a secret code on the rock to talk to Mathilde's daughter. He thinks I don't understand. I invented half the signs. I'll never tell him.
textes.Tom a écrit un couplet sur moi dans la C: Tom wrote a verse about me in the Song of the Brawl King. He rhymes “Gros-Louis” with “chewy”. I'd have preferred “Large-Louis”. It doesn't rhyme with anything, but it's more accurate.
textes.Tom joue du violon, et Bartholomé chante: Tom plays the fiddle, and Bartholomé sings the chorus. Off-key, but with heart. Together, they're the best duo at the Crâne Fendu. The only one, too!
textes.Tom joue tous les soirs sur ma petite sc: Tom has played every night on my little stage for years. He's paid in soup and grog, and he never complains. Without him, the Crâne Fendu would be a room with chairs. With him, it's a home.
textes.Tom joue vite quand je danse et doucemen: Tom plays fast when I dance and softly when I throw. He always feels the right moment. He's the only musician who's never made me miss with a knife.
textes.Tom le Violoneux chantera la gloire de c: Tom the Fiddler will sing the glory of whoever knocks down the port's three champions with their fists: Gros-Louis of the Requin Borgne, the Mute of the Veuve Écarlate and Belle-Humeur of the Morue Enragée.
textes.Tom le Violoneux tient le tableau des co: Tom the Fiddler keeps the brawlers' board: Gros-Louis, the Mute and Belle-Humeur. Whoever beats all three becomes the King of the Brawl. It's never happened.
textes.Tom va en faire une chanson !: Tom's going to make a song out of this!
textes.Tom, l'apprenti de la Forge des Strates,: Tom, the apprentice from the Strata Forge, came to the Skatepark! He fell four times. He said “didn't even hurt” four times. He learns fast.
textes.Tom, l'apprenti de la Grande Forge, a le: Tom, the apprentice at the Great Forge, is the same age as me, has the same bruised knees, and wants to change the world with a hammer. Me, with a board. He's calmer than me. Everyone's calmer than me.
textes.Tom, l'apprenti de la Grande Forge, tape: Tom, the Great Forge apprentice, bangs on his anvil at the same time as I bang on my drums, three hundred metres away. We've never agreed on the tempo. It's my best duet.
textes.Tom, mon chou ! Ta soupe est au bord de: Tom, sweetie! Your soup's at the edge of the stage.
textes.Tombée d'un cocotier abattu. Son lait re: Fallen from a felled coconut palm. Its milk restores one heart.
textes.Ton ami. Hmpf. Chacun ses fréquentations: Your friend. Hmph. Each to their own company. As long as you pay…
textes.Ton arbre, c'est le saule. Le grand saul: Your tree is the willow. The big willow on the square says hello. I told it you loved it.
textes.Ton arme ? Sage. Très sage. Ici, une lam: Your weapon? Wise. Very wise. Around here, a blade that gets sold always ends up back on my counter, with a story attached. Keep yours. And its story with it.
textes.Ton bateau ! Évidemment. Un bateau, ça a: Your boat! Of course. A boat has a name, that's the law. Mine's called Gertrude. Your rowboat and Gertrude might cross paths in the harbour. They'd better get along.
textes.Ton bleu de midi est là, aujourd'hui. Re: Your midday blue is out today. Look.
Your bowl, Bramm. Careful, it's hot.
textes.Ton bras, celui que tu t'étais cassé : i: Your arm, the one you broke: is it holding up? Tell me if it forecasts rain. Old bones talk.
textes.Ton bus vert pousse bien. Lavande a déjà: Your green bus is growing nicely. Lavande's already put a pot of mint on the roof.
textes.Ton bus violet étoilé avance ! J'ai fait: Your starry purple bus is coming along! I've done the first star.
textes.Ton bus à gouttes me fait rire chaque ma: Your raindrop bus makes me laugh every morning.
textes.Ton carnet de voyage a rencontré un prob:
Your travel journal ran into a problem.
A “cheap” program turned everything upside down.
textes.Ton carnet est très, très lent. Clique i: Your journal is very, very slow. Click here to speed it up (promise).
textes.Ton carnet garde tout ce qu'on te demand: Your journal keeps track of everything you're asked. Read it again when you don't know where to go.
textes.Ton champ est le même, Hapou. C'est ta p: Your field is the same, Hapou. It's your patience that's shrinking.
Your coal, Brunna. Dry. Bone dry.
textes.Ton chat a besoin d'une mise à jour. Tu: Your cat needs an update. You don't have a cat? It needs one anyway.
textes.Ton chat… je peux le chercher ?: Your cat… can I look for it?
textes.Ton cidre aussi, Salomé. Le thé d'abord,: So has your apple juice, Salomé. Tea first, we'll quarrel later.
textes.Ton contretemps est prêt pour ce soir ?: Is your offbeat ready for tonight?
textes.Ton cœur bat fort et ton souffle est ple: Your heart beats strong and your breath is full. Ra has nothing to give you today… except his light, and that one is free.
textes.Ton cœur, celui qui s'était cassé : il b: Your heart, the one that broke: is it beating well? Come and have a honey tea one evening. It doesn't cure anything. It helps.
Your duty has gravy in its beard.
textes.Ton disque calme est arrivé. Écoute-le a: Your calm record has arrived. Listen to it by the sea.
Your kapok tree is laughing, you know.
textes.Ton grog a un goût de vieille chaussette: Your grog tastes like an old sock.
textes.Ton grog spécial, mon chou ? Il est déjà: Your special grog, sweetie? It's already ready.
Your special grog, sweetie. Nice and hot.
textes.Ton gros poisson, j'y ai repensé. C'étai: I thought about your big fish again. It was a dolphin. I'm sure. Almost sure.
textes.Ton huile ne guérit toujours rien, Tibur: Your oil still cures nothing, Tiburce.
textes.Ton livre ? Il dort chez moi depuis soix: Your book? It's been sleeping at my place for seventy years. It's picked up the accent.
textes.Ton marteau ? Prends plutôt ta voix. Je: Your hammer? Grab your voice instead. I'll do the nailing.
textes.Ton miel ! Le pain de cette semaine a le: Your honey! This week's bread tastes of sunshine. The whole village wants the recipe.
textes.Ton moustique… tu me le prêterais ?: Your mosquito… would you lend it to me?
textes.Ton nom ! Ah… C'est le plus beau des cho: Your name! Ah… That's the finest choice of all. A parrot lives a hundred years. Your name will travel long after you. I don't say that for nothing.
textes.Ton oiseau, il a les oreilles ouvertes ?: That bird of yours, are its ears open?
textes.Ton pantalon, je lui parle, moi. Il dira: Your trousers? I'll have a word with them. They'll say yes.
textes.Ton passé ? Tiens, original. Tu es arriv: Your past? Well, that's original. You arrived by sea, you carry a sword, and you look like you've seen things no one here has ever seen. No need for cards for that, traveller.
textes.Ton perroquet… je peux le chercher ?: Your parrot… can I look for it?
textes.Ton pied quitte le pont de lumière… et n: Your foot leaves the bridge of light… and doesn't come down straight away. Welcome to the Zero-Gravity Garden!
textes.Ton portrait est sur le mur, dans la Gro: Your portrait on wall, in the Cave of Paintings. Whole Clan come see. They laugh. But nicely.
textes.Ton premier souvenir… Tu me l'as dit, un: Your first memory… You told me once. The stones heard it. They keep it with their own.
textes.Ton prix est un vol, Salomé !: Your price is daylight robbery, Salomé!
textes.Ton professeur qui nous cherche… J'ai co: Your professor who's looking for us… I've started a scroll about him. There's only his job in it so far, but it's a start.
Your father used to say the same. Word for word.
Your stew? It's MY pot, sweetie.
textes.Ton record, c'est {record} ? Moi, une fo: Your record is {record}? I once caught a whale. Well, it was a rock. But it looked like a whale.
textes.Ton rouleau, je vais le tailler en poiss: Your scroll? I'm going to carve it into a fish.
textes.Ton sac déborde, {surnom}. Dépose un tru: Your bag's overflowing, {surnom}. Drop something off at the Swap Shop, Lumi will be thrilled.
Your bag's overflowing, {surnom}. Drop something off at the Free Shop, Trocante will be thrilled.
textes.Ton sac déborde, {surnom}. Même Sire Tan: Your bag is overflowing, {surnom}. Not even Sir Tancrède could carry it. He'd try anyway.
textes.Ton sac déborde, {surnom}. Même un démon: Your bag is overflowing, {surnom}. Even a demon couldn't squeeze anything else in.
textes.Ton sac déborde, {surnom}. Range-le comm: Your bag's overflowing, {surnom}. Pack it like a mine: well propped.
textes.Ton sac déborde. Fais de la place, et re: Your bag is overflowing. Make some room, then come back.
textes.Ton sac est plein ! Fais de la place ava: Your bag is full! Make some room before opening the chest: its contents will wait for you.
Your bag is full! Make some room before opening the chest.
textes.Ton sac est plein ! Fais de la place pou: Your bag is full! Make room for the Pearl of Light.
Your bag is full! Make room for the wand.
Your bag is full! Make room for the flower.
textes.Ton sac est plein ! Fais un peu de place: Your bag is full! Make a little room for the fragment.
Your bag is full! Make a little room for the seal.
Your bag is full! Make a little room, then come back.
Your bag is full! Make a little room.
textes.Ton sac est plein ! Trocante rit : « Alo: Your bag is full! Trocante laughs: “Then give something first!”
textes.Ton sac est plein : Lentille te fait boi: Your bag is full: Lentille has you drink the soup right there, from the ladle. It does you good.
textes.Ton sac est plein : fais-y un peu de pla: Your bag is full: make a little room for the colour pot.
textes.Ton sac est plein : le sifflet des compa: Your bag is full: the Companions' Whistle is waiting for you. Make some room!
textes.Ton sac est plein comme une marmite, {su: Your bag is as full as a cooking pot, {surnom}.
textes.Ton sac est plein de virus ! (Ça, c'est: Your bag is full of viruses! (That one's true. It's me.)
textes.Ton sac est plein à craquer : fais-lui u: Your bag is bursting: make a little room for the cloth.
Your bag is full to bursting, {surnom}.
textes.Ton sac est plein à craquer, {surnom}. A: Your bag is bursting at the seams, {surnom}. Lighten it a bit.
textes.Ton sac est plein à craquer, {surnom}. M: Your bag is bursting at the seams, {surnom}. Even the Albatross would refuse to lift it.
Your bag is fit to burst, {surnom}. Even the Dragonfly would refuse to lift it.
Your bag is bursting at the seams, {surnom}. Even the Little Diver would refuse to haul it back up.
Your bag is fit to burst, {surnom}. Even a mine cart would refuse to carry it.
textes.Ton sac est plein, {surnom} ! Comme un d: Your bag is full, {surnom}! Like a dome after a party. Make a bit of room, and come back.
textes.Ton safran, Zohra : le mien, ou un autre: Your saffron, Zohra: mine, or someone else's?
Your bucket? The blue one? Never seen it, bro.
Your short black, Aristide. Don't touch anything.
textes.Ton sort pour voler avance ! Pour l'inst: Your flying spell's coming along! For now, it makes spoons levitate. It's a start.
textes.Ton sourire ! Ah… Divin. La seule chose: Your smile! Ah… Divine. The one thing nobody can polish. It has to shine from the inside. You know how. I'm jealous.
textes.Ton tapis rouge, il fait combien, déjà ?: Your red carpet, how long was it again?
textes.Ton temps ? (Elle fait la moue.) Bon. Il: Your time? (She pouts.) Fine. Somebody has to. Tempo would be pleased. Me, I'll wait for you. Quickly.
Your tea is too sweet, Hassan.
textes.Ton thé à la menthe. Toujours la menthe: Your mint tea. Still the mint from across the way. Shh.
textes.Ton tonneau t'attend, mon chou. Personne: Your barrel's waiting for you, sweetie. Nobody's touched it.
textes.Ton tournesol est presque fini. Il me re: Your sunflower's almost finished. It watches me while I weave.
textes.Ton verre est servi. Et le palmier a soi: Your drink is poured. And the palm tree is thirsty.
textes.Ton violon grince comme une porte de pri: Your fiddle squeaks like a prison door.
textes.Ton épée naine ! Prends-en soin : graiss: Your dwarven sword! Take care of it: grease the blade, and never lend it to an elf.
textes.Ton épée à deux mains. La poignée, elle: Your two-handed sword. The grip, is it holding? Show me. … Hm. It's holding.
textes.Ton épée, tu ne la donnerais jamais. Le: Your sword, you'd never give it away. The “retired swords” shelf is waiting for you anyway. No rush.
textes.Ton épée… Hm. C'est utile, j'imagine. Kr: Your sword… Hm. Useful, I suppose. Kraxx would be delighted. Me, I prefer things that shine for beauty's sake. But a shiny sword is a start.
Your island is pretty. Noisy, but pretty. The trees here are young: they don't talk much yet.
textes.Toni ! Un verre pour un collègue ?: Toni! A drink for a colleague?
textes.Toni est un artiste. Son punch est divin: Toni is an artist. His punch is divine, absolutely divine, whereas the tea on this island is a tragedy. He never has change, but he always has a smile. That's far rarer.
textes.Toni et moi, on a souvent parlé d'organi: Toni and I have often talked about holding a big punch contest: the Perroquet against the Coco Loco, in front of the whole town. We never dared. The night we talked about it most seriously, we tasted each other's punch for practice, and ended up singing together on the terrace. Contest postponed.
textes.Toni m'a donné une scène, un repas et un: Toni gave me a stage, a meal and a wage. I'm grateful to him. The wage is what bothers me.
textes.Toni n'a plus de noix de coco pour son c: Toni has run out of coconuts for his famous punch.
textes.Toni, c'est mon copain et mon concurrent: Toni is my pal and my competitor. He makes the second-best punch in Port-Azur. In the evening, it's his place I go to for a drink. That way, I keep an eye on the competition.
textes.Toni, c'est mon patron, et un peu mon on: Toni is my boss, and a bit of an honorary uncle. He hired me the very first evening. He teases me about Lucas every day. I pretend not to hear.
textes.Toni, my friend ! Un punch, s'il vous pl: Toni, my friend! A punch, please. Divine, as usual.
textes.Toni. Bon bar, bonne bière. Il me paie l: Toni. Good café, good fizz. He's been paying for the sign in fizz for twenty years. Suits me. Don't tell Colette, she'd charge me for the air.
textes.Tonneau ! Il est beau, ton cheval, aujou: Tonneau! Your horse looks lovely today.
textes.Tonneau ! Tu connais celle du poiffon qu: Tonneau! Do you know the one about the fith who walkth into a tavern?
textes.Tonneau a le hoquet, il bouge, il chante: Tonneau has hiccups, he fidgets, he sings, and he thinks his octopus is a horse. He's my worst customer. And the only one who makes me laugh till I cry. I hate him with a great deal of affection.
textes.Tonneau boit comme un trou et dort comme: Tonneau drinks like a fish and sleeps like an anchor. But he's the best cooper in the archipelago. My barrels never leak. He does: through his mouth, singing.
textes.Tonneau est le matelot le plus joyeux de: Tonneau is the jolliest sailor in the archipelago. He doesn't know what's on his back, he doesn't know what day it is, but he always knows where the bar is. That's a talent.
textes.Tonneau, c'est mon meilleur client et le: Tonneau is my best customer and the most honest one on the Balafre. He pays his tab every Saturday, to the last penny. He's always cheerful. He worries me. A lot, sometimes.
textes.Tonneau, c'est mon meilleur compagnon de: Tonneau ith my betht drinking companion. He laughth at my jokth before the end, and he giveth me prethentth. Prethentth that are… tricky. But it'th the thought that countth.
textes.Tonnerre ! … (Elle fume légèrement.) Le: Thunder! … (She smokes slightly.) The monster got hit too. That makes two of us.
textes.Tonton ! Tu m'avais promis la mer !: Uncle! You promised me the sea!
Uncle Ahmed is my first sailor. He lets me command the Zahra. But he won't take me to sea for real. He set a condition. A horrible condition.
textes.Tonton Bondi, c'est le plus rapide du mo: Uncle Bondi is the fastest in the whole wide world! He eats three carrots, not one more. I'll be a runner too, like him. But with cakes instead of carrots.
textes.Tonton m'a appris : pour sortir du port,: Uncle taught me: to get out of the harbour, green on the left, red on the right, between the two lighthouses. I say it every night before I go to sleep. Green on the left, red on the right. He promised me a real trip to sea… when I eat a raw sardine without pulling a face. A raw one! That's not a condition, that's a punishment.
textes.Tonton m'apprend le départ comme une flè: Uncle teaches me the arrow start, in Grandpa and Granny's vegetable patch. We crouch between the carrots, he says “Hop!” and off we go. I go before the hop. He says that's cheating. I say it's a very fast arrow. Granny says we're squashing the leeks.
textes.Tordu, Kraxx. Encore. En forme de huit,: Bent, Kraxx. Again. In a figure of eight, this time.
textes.Tordue ? Sur quoi tu couds, sur une coqu: Bent? What are you sewing on, a hull?
textes.Tornade ! Ce casque, il est bien attaché: Tornade! Is that helmet done up properly?
textes.Tornade est le seul garçon qui me demand: Tornade is the only boy who asks me for bigger flames. I don't know how to do small flames. We get on perfectly.
textes.Tornade est mon frère. Toi, tu es mon hu: Tornade is my brother. You're my human. It's not the same. It's better. Don't tell Tornade.
textes.Tornade m'a demandé une flamme sur son c: Tornade asked me for a flame on his helmet. Rustine said: “A reasonable flame.” I tried. My reasonable flame goes all the way round the helmet and up over the top. Tornade said it was the most reasonable one he'd ever seen. Rustine sighed.
textes.Tornade m'a demandé une rubrique « Les r: Tornade asked me for a “Tornade's Triumphs” column. I said OK. So far it's one line long: “He ate all his soup on Tuesday.” He says that's not a skateboarding triumph. I said I only publish what I see. I'm waiting for news.
I miss Tornade a bit. But you're here. And the world is big. And it smells nice. And you're here.
textes.Tornade tombe tout le temps. C'est pour: Tornade falls over all the time. That's why my “Tornade's Blunders” column is so long. But he's my brother. Nobody else is allowed to make fun of him.
textes.Tornade tombe, se relève, dit « même pas: Tornade falls, gets up, says “didn't even hurt” and comes back crying five minutes later. He's the bravest and most scraped-up boy in Boucan.
textes.Tornade tombe, se relève, tombe, se relè: Tornade falls, gets up, falls, gets up. He gets that from me. He's the bravest boy I know, and the most battered.
textes.Tornade va toujours trop vite. Il est so: Tornade always goes too fast. He escaped from his cradle at six months by rolling it. He hasn't slowed down since. I build ramps. He tries them out.
textes.Tornade veut que je peigne une flamme su: Tornade wants me to paint a flame on his skate helmet. Rustine said yes, as long as the flame is “reasonable”. I don't know how to paint reasonable flames.
textes.Tornade voulait manger un Bolet-Ressort: Tornade wanted to eat a Spring-Bolete to jump all the way up to the roof of the Hall. Rustine said no. I said no. Tornade said: “What about in a fairy tale?” I said: “In a fairy tale, ask your mother.” He's still asking.
textes.Tornade. La rampe tient ?: Tornade. Is the ramp holding up?
textes.Tortellini dit que j'ai vu une méduse. M: Tortellini says I saw a jellyfish. I say his wink was a speck of dust. We're both right, and we tell each other so every Sunday, over cards.
textes.Tortellini fait pousser le blé, je fais: Tortellini grows the wheat, I make the pasta. He says it's his wheat that makes my pasta good; I say it's my hands. We're both right. We've been both right for fifty years.
textes.Touche ce tissu, {surnom}. Doux, hein ?: Touch this cloth, {surnom}. Soft, isn't it? And you, which colour do you like best?
textes.Toujours ? Comme ça, droit dans les yeux: Always? Just like that, straight in the eye? I'm impressed. Won't you give me lessons? I'll pay in punch.
textes.Toujours ? Les quatre premiers soleils o: Always? The first four suns all came to an end. Nothing is “always”. But your trust is beautiful. Keep it. And thank him anyway.
textes.Toujours ?! Ah. Hum. Très bien. Très, tr: Always?! Ah. Ahem. Very good. Very, very good. That's… very prudent.
Always BOOM. At least it's consistent. Science marches on!
textes.Toujours au top ! Le soleil brille, les: Always top-notch! The sun's shining, people are thirsty, and I've got ice.
textes.Toujours aucune lettre ? Je vous ai mis: Still no letters? I've put an envelope aside for you. Empty. Waiting for you to fill it.
Still no mystery potions? Well done. Your eyebrows thank you. Mine are growing back.
textes.Toujours aussi beau, Tonneau. Il a même: As handsome as ever, Tonneau. He's even put on some muscle.
textes.Toujours bleu ? Alors tu es de la famill: Still blue? Then you're one of the family.
textes.Toujours bonne ! Un patron de bar triste: Always good! A sad café owner is like an empty bottle.
textes.Toujours calme ? Parfait. Tout est nomin: Still calm? Perfect. All systems nominal.
textes.Toujours cap au hasard, {surnom} ? Le ve: Still heading wherever, {surnom}? The wind's just right for it today.
textes.Toujours casanier, {surnom} ? Léon serai: Still a homebody, {surnom}? Léon would be proud of you.
textes.Toujours ce goût de larme heureuse, {sur: Still that taste of happy tears, {surnom}?
textes.Toujours cent douze ? J'en ai peut-être: Still a hundred and twelve? I may have counted one extra this morning.
textes.Toujours comme les mouettes ? Hm. Margot: Still like the seagulls? Hm. Margot likes you.
textes.Toujours d'accord avec mon hypothèse num: Still agree with my hypothesis number one?
textes.Toujours d'avis qu'elles se parlent, {su: Still of the view that they talk to each other, {surnom}?
Always in the other direction, eh.
textes.Toujours dans l'équipe de la vapeur, pet: Still on team steam, you little traitor?
textes.Toujours dans la hâte ? Vous m'avez pour: Still in a hurry? And yet you listened to me right to the end today. You're making progress.
textes.Toujours de passage ? Je vous ai inscrit: Still passing through? I put you down in pencil. It hasn't rubbed off yet, mind you.
textes.Toujours des fleurs ? Je te ferai un pri: Still giving flowers? I'll give you a good price.
textes.Toujours des pièces dans tes poches, {su: Still got coins in your pockets, {surnom}?
textes.Toujours deux. Je les ai comptés, comme: Still two. I counted them, like Grégoire.
textes.Toujours en avance, {surnom} ? Hm. J'ai: Still early, {surnom}? Hm. I have a watch for you to adjust.
textes.Toujours en l'air ! Je lui ai lancé un s: Still up in the air! I threw him a sandwich this morning. He caught it. I'm proud.
textes.Toujours en retard ? J'ai réglé votre mo: Still late? I've set your watch. It rings now.
textes.Toujours enclume ? Solide comme toujours: Still an anvil? Solid as ever, eh?
textes.Toujours envie d'aller au-dessus des nua: Still keen to go above the clouds? The sky up there is such a blue…
textes.Toujours envie de descendre voir la mer: Still want to go down and see the sea?
textes.Toujours fan du grand vent ? Il souffle: Still a fan of the big wind? It's blowing hard today. Hold on to your hat.
textes.Toujours gratuitement, Tochtli ! Comme l: Always for free, Tochtli! Like the wind!
textes.Toujours jamais malade ? Je note. Je not: Still never ill? I'm making a note. I note everything, you know. The day you sneeze, I'll be there.
Always the last one. For thirty years.
textes.Toujours la plus loin de la porte, mon c: Always the one furthest from the door, sweetie.
textes.Toujours le Phare, d'après vous ? Je vou: Still the Lighthouse, in your view? I'll prove you wrong.
textes.Toujours le bas ? Vous saluerez ma femme: Still down below? Give my regards to my wife.
Still white? You're spoilt for it here.
textes.Toujours le bleu, mon petit ? Il te va b: Still blue, my little one? It suits you.
textes.Toujours le ciel ? Hmm. Héloïse sera con: Still the sky? Hmm. Héloïse will be pleased.
textes.Toujours le nez au soleil, mon oiseau ?: Still nose to the sun, my little bird?
textes.Toujours le nez à la vitre, {surnom} ?: Still with your nose to the window, {surnom}?
textes.Toujours le quarante-septième ? Je vous: Still the forty-seventh? I still advise against it.
textes.Toujours le rire ? HA HA ! T'as raison !: Still the laugh? HA HA! You're right!
textes.Toujours le vert ? Tu as la main verte,: Still green? You've got green fingers, I'm sure of it.
textes.Toujours les affaires. La barque t'atten: Always business. The boat's waiting for you, you know.
textes.Toujours les détails ? Bien. Tu trouvera: Still the details? Good. You'll find things.
textes.Toujours les rimes ? Moi aussi. Quand je: Still rhymes? Me too. When I can find them.
textes.Toujours les vers libres ? Tu es plus li: Still free verse? You're freer than I am.
textes.Toujours les yeux devant toi ? Bon élève: Still eyes front? Top of the class!
textes.Toujours les yeux fermés ? Tenez bien la: Eyes still closed? Hold on tight to the rail.
textes.Toujours les écrous ? Tu es bizarre. Mai: Still nuts? You're weird. But nice.
Still free, {surnom}? I'm keeping an eye on you. From afar.
textes.Toujours marteau ? Pif t'attend, HA HA !: Still a hammer? Pif is waiting for you, HA HA!
textes.Toujours moi ! Un kilo de cumin et un so: Always me! A kilo of cumin and a smile!
textes.Toujours moi, Croc-Gris. Pas de monstre,: Still me, Croc-Gris. No monster tonight.
textes.Toujours moi, caïd ! Vos canons sont sup: Still me, caïd! Your cannons are superb.
textes.Toujours neuf godets ? Bien, bien. Vous: Still nine wells? Good, good. You have a fine memory.
Still no. But I've got a net.
textes.Toujours partant pour descendre ? La Fro: Still up for going down? The Fronde is waiting for you.
textes.Toujours partisan des discours courts, m: Still in favour of short speeches, my dear? Hmm.
textes.Toujours pas ! Et Peek', il a toujours t: Still not! And Peek', does he still have too much hair?
textes.Toujours pas d'idée nouvelle, cher membr: Still no new idea, dear fellow club member? Me neither. This week I invented the button. It already existed.
textes.Toujours pas d'épée ? Hm. Je t'ai mis un: Still no sword? Hm. I've put a blade aside for you. Not free. But aside.
textes.Toujours pas de dorade, petit frère ?: Still no sea bream, little brother?
textes.Toujours pas de légendes, pour vous ? Je: Still no legends for you? I'm noting your position. I'll refute it one day, with evidence in hand.
textes.Toujours pas de nom pour ta lame ? Elle: Still no name for your blade? It's waiting, you know. Iron is patient.
textes.Toujours pas de romans d'amour ? Je vous: Still no romance novels? I'll lend you one. You'll read it in secret, like everyone.
Still no answer? Me neither. We're still searching.
textes.Toujours pas de sommeil ? Je vous ai mis: Still no sleep? I've put a cup of tea aside for you. The management understands. It, too, sometimes…
textes.Toujours pas dit merci aux racines, hein: Still haven't thanked the roots, eh? Hmph. They kept you standing anyway. That's how they are.
textes.Toujours pas monté dans le Zéphyr ? C'es: Still haven't been up in the Zéphyr? It's free, I'll remind you. My patience, however, has a price.
textes.Toujours pas parlé à ton épée ? Essaie u: Still haven't talked to your sword? Try one evening, very quietly. I'm sure it has things to say.
textes.Toujours pas à vendre, ce piano ?: Still not for sale, that piano?
textes.Toujours pas, Zélie. Respirez par la bou: Still not, Zélie. Breathe through your mouth.
textes.Toujours pas. Et tu me dois toujours tro: Still not. And you still owe me three bottles.
Still no. But I've got beetroot.
textes.Toujours peur de rien ? Ne le dis pas tr: Still afraid of nothing? Don't say it too loudly near the ticket office.
textes.Toujours plus de voitures volantes, hein: Still want more flying cars, eh?
textes.Toujours pour décider ensemble, {surnom}: Still in favour of deciding together, {surnom}?
textes.Toujours pour les nouilles gratuites ? H: Still for free noodles? Hiro's getting worried.
textes.Toujours pour les rires forts ? HO HO !: Still for loud laughs? HO HO!
textes.Toujours pressé de boire ton thé, mon pe: Still in a hurry to drink your tea, little one?
textes.Toujours rien cassé, toi ? Je t'admire,: Still haven't broken anything? I really admire you, you know.
textes.Toujours rien de cassé ? Ta compresse t': Still nothing broken? Your compress is waiting for you on my shelf. I've labelled it with your name.
textes.Toujours rien de précieux ? Vous voyagez: Still nothing precious? You travel light. I need three porters just to go and have tea.
Still nothing to declare? … Very well. I'm watching you. Discreetly. Don't turn round.
textes.Toujours rien à vous reprocher ? Je véri: Still nothing to reproach yourself with? I'm just checking, that's all. Pure routine. Good day, model citizen.
textes.Toujours rouge ? Je te garde un fond de: Still red? I'll save you the bottom of a pot.
Still without my book, Monsieur Fiole.
textes.Toujours sans un sou, {surnom} ? Ta gout: Still penniless, {surnom}? Your free drop is waiting. Just one, mind. I have a reputation.
textes.Toujours slurp, mon enfant ? Ne mens pas: Still slurping, my child? Don't lie, I've seen your chin.
textes.Toujours sucré, mon chou ? J'ai des datt: Still sweet, sweetie? I've got dates for you.
textes.Toujours sur la carte, Excellence. Bien: Still on the map, Excellency. Nice and snug.
textes.Toujours sur mon dos, Bedaine. Et elle y: Still on my back, Bedaine. And there it stays.
textes.Toujours ta tisane, Hassan ?: Still on your herbal tea, Hassan?
textes.Toujours tes cailloux ? Apporte-les-moi,: Still your pebbles? Bring them to me, I'll paint them blue for you. Pebble rate, very low. Very low for me.
textes.Toujours tes confettis, petite ?: Still with your confetti, little one?
textes.Toujours tes rires doux ? Je les entends: Still laughing softly? I hear it anyway.
textes.Toujours toi ? Tu as plus de courage qu': Always you? You've got more courage than an old lady I know.
textes.Toujours ton mot de passe compliqué ? Bi: Still got your complicated password? Good.
textes.Toujours ton rayon de soleil, petit ? Je: Still on about your ray of sunshine, little one? I'll win you over one day.
textes.Toujours tout droit, {surnom} ? Reviens: Still going straight ahead, {surnom}? Come back anyway.
textes.Toujours toutes les couleurs ? Comme la: Still all the colours? Just like the Palette.
textes.Toujours trop chaud ? Votre platane est: Still too hot? Your plane tree is under review. Before the end of the year. Don't tell Hortense.
textes.Toujours trop timide ? Danse dans ta têt: Still too shy? Dance in your head, then.
textes.Toujours un peu des deux ? C'est comme ç: Still a bit of both? That's how you get to see everything.
Always a little, for you, little one.
textes.Toujours une boule pour l'inventrice, pa: Always a scoop for the inventor, boss!
textes.Toujours {manque} champignons à trouver,: Still {manque} mushrooms to find, {surnom}. Damp undergrowth, at the foot of the big trees.
textes.Toujours {manque} cœurs de magma à trouv: Still {manque} magma hearts to find, {surnom}. The elementals prowl the edge of the crater. They burn: strike fast, step back fast.
textes.Toujours {manque} dents de requin à trou: Still {manque} shark teeth to find, {surnom}. The sharks circle the reef. Wait for them to charge, then strike!
textes.Toujours {manque} runes de golem. Monte: Still {manque} golem runes. Climb towards the crater: they guard the black slopes. Strike when they raise their big arms… after, not before.
textes.Toujours {manque} éclats d'obsidienne, {: Still {manque} obsidian shards, {surnom}. The black glass, at the edge of the crater.
textes.Toujours à chanter pour tes plantes ? Tu: Still singing to your plants? Will you teach me?
textes.Toujours à chanter sous la douche ? On t: Still singing in the shower? We can hear you from here, you know.
textes.Toujours à enrouler tes spaghettis, mon: Still twirling your spaghetti, my child? Good, good.
textes.Toujours à l'heure ? Vraiment ? Ah, {sur: Always on time? Really? Ah, {surnom}… You make me very happy. There are so few people who are on time. Me, Gaston, the great clock and you. That makes four of us.
textes.Toujours à l'heure, vous ! Je l'ai noté: Always on time, you are! I've noted it in my journal. Between Gaston and the great clock.
textes.Toujours à regarder la ville s'allumer,: Still watching the city light up, {surnom}?
textes.Toujours à regarder les gens, {surnom} ?: Still looking at the people, {surnom}? Good.
textes.Toujours à regarder loin ? Attention aux: Still looking far away? Mind the pebbles.
textes.Toujours à tout remplacer, toi ? Je te s: Still replacing everything, you? I've got my eye on you.
textes.Toujours à vouloir monter ? Reviens quan: Still wanting to go up? Come back anyway!
textes.Toujours à vouloir monter ? Un jour, je: Still wanting to go up? One day I'll take you down. You'll see.
textes.Toujours, Brasero. Et la Fronde, toujour: Always, Brasero. And the Fronde, as noisy as ever?
textes.Toujours, Capitaine ! Et vous, toujours: Always, Captain! And you, still the right way up?
textes.Toujours, Capitaine. Elle vous passe le: Still, Captain. She sends her regards.
textes.Toujours, Excellence ! Payable en promes: Always, Excellency! Payable in promises, as usual?
textes.Toujours, Excellence ! Tant que vous ne: Always, Excellency! As long as you don't touch my honey again.
textes.Toujours, Gilles. Elle garde le four au: Still there, Gilles. It keeps the oven warm.
textes.Toujours, Ix Chab. Un pot, pour tes gale: Always, Ix Chab. A pot, for your flatbreads?
textes.Toujours, Majesté ! Enfin… presque toujo: Always, Your Majesty! Well… almost always.
Always, Majesty. Only real ones here.
textes.Toujours, Nono. Mais lentement, mon appa: Always, Nono. But slowly, my camera's tired.
Always, Prosper. So are the steps.
Always, Xóchitl. The gods are slow.
Always, down to the tiniest detail.
Always, and I tick things off.
textes.Toujours, madame. C'est une politique de: Always, madam. It is house policy.
textes.Toujours, maître Borin. Et toujours un p: Still, Master Borin. And still a little less well than you.
textes.Toujours, mon cher Gontran. Elle ne vous: Always, my dear Gontran. It just doesn't point to you any more, that's all.
Always, old friend. Just for you.
textes.Toujours, monsieur Silas. On ne sait jam: Always, Mister Silas. You never know.
textes.Toujours, petit. Les baleines ont leurs: Always, lad. Whales have their habits.
textes.Toujours, prêtresse ! Enfin… pas ce soir: Always, priestess! Well… not tonight. Tomorrow.
textes.Toujours. Et la bonne, c'est pour quand: Always. And the Big One, when is it?
textes.Toujours. Et ton soleil, toujours sa bar: Always. And your sun, still its boat?
Always. It only speaks against the light.
textes.Toujours. Il rame plus que ton serpent n: Always. He rows more than your serpent flies.
Always. I've mixed up the buttons.
Always. I hope you are too.
Always. Even if it's the lullaby.
textes.Toujours. Rejouez la note grave. Pour le: Always. Play the low note again. For the violet.
Always. Come in, I've made coffee.
textes.Tour de contrôle à pilote : vent de face: Control tower to pilot: headwind, force two! Cleared for take-off!
textes.Tour de contrôle, ici la pilote ! Vrrr !: Control tower, this is the pilot! Vrrr!
textes.Tour de contrôle, ici le pilote ! Vrrr !: Control tower, this is the pilot! Vrrr!
textes.Tour de ronde. Je vérifie la rambarde, l: On my rounds. I check the railing, the pipes, and my footing. All in order.
textes.Tourne les cristaux ! Chacun renvoie la: Turn the crystals! Each one sends the light in the direction it points.
textes.Tournesol plante des fleurs partout où e: Sunflower plants flowers everywhere she goes. She's as stubborn as a mule and as bright as a summer morning. I don't speak to her anymore. It's my fault. A bit.
Turn around. No, the other profile.
textes.Tous ! Je les ai encore tous !: All of them! I've still got all of them!
textes.Tous ? Et tu as pleuré comme un grand ?: All of them? And did you cry like a grown-up?
textes.Tous les ans, Borin et moi, on demande à: Every year, Borin and I ask Hilda to judge our beards. She stands us side by side, walks around us, tugs a hair here, a hair there. Then she says: “I win.” Croâ caws to applaud. We try again the next year. We always lose.
textes.Tous les ans, le soir où Gaspard n'est p: Every year, on the night Gaspard didn't come home, Tom plays his favourite song, an old whaler's lament, very slowly. I've never asked him to. He just does it. That night, the toughest pirates in the port take off their hats. Me, I stay behind the counter and wipe the same glass for the whole song.
textes.Tous les ans, à la fête de la Forge, je: Every year, at the Forge Festival, I challenge Bramm to arm-wrestling. Every year, I lose. He doesn't even break a sweat. Last year, I held out for eleven seconds. He said nothing. But Kalda told me that on the way home, he muttered: “Eleven.” Just that. I'm training for twelve.
textes.Tous les après-midi, quand je fais ma lo: Every afternoon, when I do my lap of the bay, Bernard runs along the beach, right level with me. “By chance.” If I speed up, he speeds up. If I float on my back, he stops to retie his shoelace. We never talk about it. Between sportsmen, we understand each other.
textes.Tous les chats accourent ! La dame est r: All the cats come running! The lady is delighted: “You've been adopted. By them. It's an honor!”
textes.Tous les cinquante-deux ans, on éteint t: Every fifty-two years, all the fires of Aztlán are put out, and we wait in the dark to know whether the sun will come back. I was twenty. The whole city was on the rooftops, in silence. Then a new fire was lit on the hill. I carried a torch along the causeway, running, to relight the houses. In the morning, the sun rose. I wept.
textes.Tous les dimanches matin, il me montre s: Every Sunday morning, he shows me his bowline, eyes closed. Last time, he tied his ankle to the mainmast. It took Gros-Louis to undo it, and the whole of Balafre to stop laughing. I told him: “Almost.” He was happy all week. That's what a captain is: knowing how to say almost.
textes.Tous les dimanches, Capucine m'apporte d: Every Sunday, Capucine brings me gear cookies. She looks at my roof, she counts my eyebrows, and she asks how “the Big One” is going in a tiny little voice. I think she's worried. She's wrong! Well… a bit right.
textes.Tous les dimanches, Fernand mange ma bou: Every Sunday, Fernand eats my bouillabaisse, mops it up to the last drop, then puts down his spoon and says: “Something's missing.” Every Sunday! Something! It keeps me up at night. I change the saffron, the garlic, the fennel… he always says the same thing. One day I'll find that something. And that day, he's doing the washing-up.
textes.Tous les dimanches, Ravioli me donne un: Every Sunday, Ravioli gives me a basket of tomatoes for the Cooking Pot. I throw them in, one by one. She asks me to say goodbye to them. I don't say anything. But I think it very hard. I think she knows.
textes.Tous les dimanches, je lui porte une tis: Every Sunday, I take him a thyme tea on his bench, nice and hot, with honey. He waits for it to cool, then freezes it and crunches it like a stick of rock. Forty years I've made it hot, forty years he's crunched it. Neither of us will change. That's friendship.
textes.Tous les dimanches, je vais à la Casse s: Every Sunday, I go to the Scrapyard to lift the old cars, so Ferraille can rummage underneath. Once, under a van, he found a family of hedgehogs. We put the van back exactly where it was. Ferraille welded a little roof over them. The hedgehogs still live there.
textes.Tous les douze. Et Grignotte a faim. Att: All twelve. And Grignotte's hungry. Watch your belt.
textes.Tous les foirs, on fe difpute pour favoi: Every evening, we argue about who'th theen the biggetht thardine. I thpread my armth like thith. He goeth wider. Me, even wider! In the end, we knock over the neighbourth' glatheth, and Thylvain lookth at uth over hith glatheth. He hath no glatheth. But he lookth at uth ath if he did.
textes.Tous les jours ! (Une fleur clignote deu: Every day! (A flower blinks twice.) See? It's saying thank you on behalf of all the plants down below. They like you, I can feel it.
textes.Tous les jours ? (Il vous regarde avec a: Every day? (He looks at you in admiration.) I… I'll try to do one. Just one. A small one. Do you think a small one counts?
textes.Tous les jours ?! (Il te regarde avec ad: Every day?! (He looks at you in admiration.) You're the bravest person on the island. Braver than the adventurers. Much braver.
textes.Tous les jours depuis douze ans, je dema: Every day for twelve years, I've asked Ionie if I'm ready for her crystal engine. She answers: “Almost.” One day, I asked: “Almost how much?” She said: “Almost like someone who's broken forty-three fins.” I counted. It was forty-four. She winked at me.
textes.Tous les jours à midi, Dagna traverse la: Every day at noon, Dagna crosses the terrace with a steaming bowl and sets it on the stone next to me. I say “Hmph”. She says “You're welcome”. We've been talking like that for a hundred and fifty years. It's the longest conversation of my life.
textes.Tous les jours à onze heures, je passe g: Every day at eleven, I drop by to taste the stew. One ladleful. For the salt. Dagna pretends not to see me, and the ladle is always resting on the edge of the cauldron, handle turned my way. Always. I say nothing. Neither does she. And I go back for thirds.
textes.Tous les jours à quatre heures, une brio: Every day at four, a brioche breaks at the edge of my counter, by accident, just as Pépin goes by. I say: “Oh! What an accident! Can't sell that!” and I look away. When I turn back, the brioche is gone. One day, I forgot to break it. Pépin waited an hour in front of my stall, without a word. I don't forget any more.

Every day at four o'clock, a brioche breaks at the edge of Bobor's counter, and Pépin happens to walk by, as if by chance. Bobor thinks I don't see him do it. I do. The day after the first time, I left a jar of cinnamon on his counter, without a word. He understood.
textes.Tous les jours, Gloubi m'annonce le déje: Every day, Gloubi announces lunch “in five minutes.” I've counted: it arrives, on average, after thirty-two minutes. I've set one of my clocks to run twenty-seven minutes fast, just for him. Now, when he says “five minutes,” it's true. He doesn't know.
textes.Tous les jours, Tempo s'assoit à midi pi: Every day, Tempo sits down at noon sharp and I shout to him: “Ready in five minutes!” He takes out a clock, puts it on the table and stares at it. That makes me laugh, so I take my time. I say it's good for his character. He says it's bad for his stomach. We're both right.
textes.Tous les jours, en allant au Perroquet,: Every day, on my way to the Perroquet, I walk under the clock and look up. One day, Madame Hortense was on her bench. She saw me look up. She said nothing. Neither did I. Cost me more than a good telling-off.
textes.Tous les jours, je monte quarante sacs d: Every day, I carry forty sacks from the city stores up to the terrace forges. Three hundred steps. A big'un carried with me for three years, once: Hector, Borin's apprentice. He puffed like a bellows with a hole in it, but he never gave up. Coal is heavy. The terrace is warm thanks to us.
textes.Tous les jours, je regardais le Requin B: Every day, I watched the Requin Borgne from the quay. One morning, I climbed right to the top of the mainmast, without asking. The captain was waiting at the bottom, arms crossed. She said: “Do you know how to get down?” I said no. She sent Fil-de-Fer to fetch me. That evening, she went to talk to Mum. The next day, I had a green bandana.
textes.Tous les jours, je vais à la poste achet: Every day I go to the post office to buy a stamp. Just one. Nadine asks me: “Again?” I say I have a lot of mail. I've got three hundred stamps in a drawer and nobody to write to. If I stuck them all on one letter, it would go round the whole archipelago. One day, maybe. For now, I just chat.
textes.Tous les jours, vers quatre heures du ma: Every day, around four in the morning, when he closes the Shark's Tooth, Sylvain walks under my window. I leave him a bowl of soup on the sill, with a cloth over it. In the morning, the bowl is empty and clean, with a coin in it. We've never talked about that soup. Not once.
textes.Tous les jours, à quatre heures pile, je: Every day, at four o'clock sharp, I walk past Bobor's stall. And every day, a brioche breaks in two, right at the edge of the counter. Bobor says: “Oh! What an accident! It can't be sold now!” And he looks away. So I eat it. So it doesn't go to waste.
textes.Tous les lundis, Pastille prend ma tensi: Every Monday, Pastille takes my blood pressure at the First Aid Post. I keep knitting the whole time. She says it skews the reading. I tell her that without knitting, my blood pressure would go up. We've never settled it. She writes down: “blood pressure normal, knitting in progress”.
textes.Tous les lundis, je lui propose de jouer: Every Monday, I offer to play my Cod against her Shark. She answered me once: “A shark against a cod, we know who eats whom.” I laughed so much I lost a game at the next table. Since then, it's our ritual: she refuses, I smile, she growls. I think she'd be disappointed if I stopped.
textes.Tous les lundis, je prends la tension de: Every Monday, I take Mamie's blood pressure. She refuses to put down her knitting. I tell her it skews the reading. She answers that without her knitting, her blood pressure would go up. Every week on her chart I write: “blood pressure normal, knitting in progress”. It's become a diagnosis.
textes.Tous les matins ! Mon mari dit que c'est: Every morning! My husband says it's the steam waking up. I say he tightened the wrong bolt.
textes.Tous les matins, Dwalin descend un chaud: Every morning, Dwalin takes a cauldron of my stew down to the Blazing Mug. Ulfa sells it on for twice what I charge. I know it, she knows it. At every Forge Festival, she gives me back the difference in an embroidered purse, with a little note: “For the salt.” She's teasing Borin, of course.
textes.Tous les matins, Volt arrive au hangar a: Every morning, Volt arrives at the hangar with a cup of coffee: “I made too much.” One day, I told him: “Volt, you could make just enough.” He answered: “No.” And off he went. Since then, I make two extra biscuits every morning. He takes them, saying he isn't hungry.
textes.Tous les matins, avec l'oncle Ernest, on: Every morning, Uncle Ernest and I climbed the four hundred and twelve steps singing the numbers. He had a song for each hundred. The third was the hardest, so he sang louder, and the neighbours opened their windows. At the top step, he'd give me a mint. In six years, he never forgot once.
textes.Tous les matins, avec son thé. Elle pose: Every morning, with her tea. She sets her cup on the railing, listens to the hum, and says “morning, big fellas”. They purr louder when she's here. I swear.
textes.Tous les matins, depuis dix ans, je test: Every morning, for ten years, I've tested the Great Stage mics. “One, two. One, two.” There hasn't been a single concert. But if there ever is one, the sound will be perfect. I leave nothing to chance.
textes.Tous les matins, je fais coucou au Grand: Every morning I wave to the Great Spaghetti. It used to wiggle a noodle to wave back. Just one, a tiny one. It's our secret. Nobody knows. Except you, now.
textes.Tous les matins, je fais trop de café. P: Every morning, I make too much coffee. By mistake. So I take it to Ionie, at the Spaceport. I've been making too much coffee every morning for four hundred years. One day she told me: “You know, Volt, you could make just enough.” I told her: “No.” She smiled.
textes.Tous les matins, je lui crie « BONJOUR,: Every morning, I shout “MORNING, BELLE-HUMEUR!” as loud as I can. The first time, he nearly loaded his cannon. Now he answers “MORNING!” and the whole port jumps. One day, I had a sore throat, I couldn't shout. He came to see me, very worried, and he shouted hello for both of us.
textes.Tous les matins, je lui pose une seule q: Every morning, I ask him just one question, and I write his answer in my journal. “Your favourite colour?” “Grey.” “Do you have a brother?” “No.” “Do you like rum?” “Yes.” One day, I asked him if he was afraid of anything. He looked at me for a long time and said: “Next.” I wrote down “Next”. It counts.
textes.Tous les matins, maman a de la farine su: Every morning, Mum has flour on her nose. I don't tell her. The customers smile, and she thinks it's because of her bread. One day I'll tell her. Or not. She looks pretty with it.
textes.Tous les matins, on s'assoit sur le même: Every morning we sit on the same bench on the Freighter. I talk, he nods. One day, I talked for an hour without stopping. At the end, he said: “Mh. Same.” It's the loveliest answer anyone's ever given me.
textes.Tous les matins, quand je passe devant l: Every morning, when I go past the lifeguard post, he starts doing push-ups. On purpose. He counts out loud: “Four hundred and ninety-eight! Four hundred and ninety-nine!” So I do an extra lap. He does a hundred more push-ups. One day, one of us is going to crack. It won't be me. Well, I don't think so.
textes.Tous les matins, sur le quai : « Crochet: Every morning, on the quay: “Crochet, your favourite colour?” “Grey.” “Crochet, have you ever seen a whale?” “Yes.” She writes my answers in a journal, next to her shells. She says she has thirty-seven. Words, not shells. Thirty-seven words in a year. That's a lot, for me.
textes.Tous les matins. On s'est habitués l'un: Every morning. We've got used to each other.
textes.Tous les midis, je laisse trois pièces s: Every lunchtime, I leave three coins under my bowl, for a stranger's soup. Lentille pretends not to see them. Then he serves an extra ladleful to the first person who turns up without a penny. He thinks I don't notice. We both pretend. For ten years now.
textes.Tous les mois, Doc vérifie la sangle de: Every month, Doc checks the strap of my hook. He asks me forty questions. I answer “Hm” forty times. He writes everything down in a notebook. One day, I looked at the notebook: forty “Hm”s, neatly lined up in a column, with the date. And at the end: “Doing well.” He's right. It annoys me that he's right.
textes.Tous les mois, je vérifie la sangle de s: Every month, I check the strap of his hook. I ask my forty questions, he answers forty “Hm”s, and I note them in a column.
