textes.Un jour, elle a planté des capucines dev: One day, she planted nasturtiums in front of my door, for my birthday. Capucines, like me. Achille thought they were for him. He wrote a poem. Again.
textes.Un jour, elle a tapé deux coups sur l'en: One day, she struck the anvil twice, then once. Under our feet, someone answered. Twice, then once. She looked at me. I said: “That's my uncle.” She laughed for ten minutes.
textes.Un jour, elle est montée au belvédère et: One day, she came up to the lookout and named all the herbs around my easel: thyme, savory, everlasting, and a little yellow one you mustn't pick. I put them all over my canvas. She leaned in: “That's everlasting. You've painted it as savory.” She sees everything.
textes.Un jour, elle est redescendue avec une p: One day she came down with a sting right on the nose. Red, swollen like a crab apple. She took the honey she'd just brought down and dabbed a bit on it: “It heals!” It did heal. I sold that jar for two coins extra: “Honey that heals its own stings”. And it was true, too.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a apporté un badge en bo: One day, she brought me a badge made of a button and thread, saying “Honorary Member of the Little Heroes' Guild, Head Cook”. I pinned it on my apron. Hugues asked me what it was. I told him it was the highest honour on the island. He was jealous. He hasn't got one.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a apporté un champignon: One day, she brought me a mushroom that glows in the dark. I put it in the stew. The whole Canteen had glowing teeth during the concert. Bielle said it was the most beautiful audience of her life.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a apporté un dessin : le: One day she brought me a drawing: the Pond King, golden, big as a rabbit. With a crown on his head. I looked at that drawing for a long time. A very long time. She asked: “Isn't it good?” I said: “Shh. It's very good.” It's pinned above my bed.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a apporté un grand coqui: One day, she brought me a big shell from Bone Beach, all pink inside. I said to her: “WHAT'S THAT?!” She said: “For you.” I grunted. I took it. I didn't throw it away. It's in my hammock. I'm not saying what I do with it. NONE OF YOUR BUSINESS.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a demandé de tirer une f: One day, she asked me to shoot an arrow through the rope holding a sack of flour stuck at the top of her storeroom. I cut it on the first try. The sack fell on Clovis, who was underneath. He was already all white. It didn't show. Honorine laughed for ten minutes. She gave me an extra éclair.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a forgé une louche géant: One day, she forged me a giant ladle, for the big pot. It's so heavy it takes two to lift it. She comes to help me lift it every morning. I think that was the idea.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a rapporté un enregistre: One day, she brought me back a recording made at a hundred and ninety-nine metres. You could hear the Singer on it, and behind her, very far away, another voice. Higher. Younger. A little one? Lou said: “We have to go down and see.” Yolande said no. I listened to the recording two hundred times.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a servi sa tisane. J'ai: One day, she served me her tea. I drank. I said: “Hot water.” She hasn't forgotten. Five years. She brings it up with every vial. Hm. It was good, really. A bit. I won't say so.
textes.Un jour, elle m'a tendu sa flûte en terr: One day, she handed me her clay flute, the bird-shaped one. “Try it,” she said. I blew. The sound of a duck with a cold. She laughed till she cried. I gave her back the flute very quickly. I've never tried again. Not in front of her.
textes.Un jour, en entrant acheter des pêches,: One day, going in to buy peaches, I caught Colette behind her counter, buried in “The Foam of Your Heart” by Sylvia Delarive. She slipped it under the crate of peaches, bright red. Then she looked at me and said: “Do you read? Read this.” She recommended it with such passion… I turned bright red too. Two peonies.
textes.Un jour, en grimpant chercher le miel, u: One day, climbing up for the honey, a bee stung me right on the nose. It swelled up like an apple! Grelot put a bit of the honey itself on it, to heal it: “Honey mends what the bee has done.” It worked. She still made me pay for the honey. One coin. I hung it under the bridge.
textes.Un jour, il a baptisé un nuage « Ombelin: One day, he named a cloud “Ombeline”. I painted a cloud the colour “Aurèle”: a very serious grey with a little pink in it. He hung it in his office. He says it's a very good likeness.
textes.Un jour, il a essayé de soulever Excalib: One day, he tried to lift Excalibur. He managed it, halfway. He shouted: “I am the chosen one!” I told him the chosen one also does the washing-up. He did it. All of it. He's the only child who's ever lifted Excalibur.
textes.Un jour, il a fait une lanterne sans un: One day he made a lantern without a single hole, “to see”. He lit it in the middle of the souk: nothing, a candle in a pot. He said it was on purpose, to prove copper is enough. I said it was the most honest of his lanterns. He didn't speak to me all day. The next day he brought me a tea.
textes.Un jour, il a gagné un match et il m'a d: One day, he won a match and dedicated the victory to me, in front of the whole court: “For Ix Chab and her pots!” Everyone laughed. Me, I was as red as cochineal. The next day, I served him two fingers of froth instead of one. He cried miracle. He'd better not get used to it.
textes.Un jour, il a oublié la deuxième chouque: One day, he forgot the second choux bun. I walked round the Esplanade three times in front of the Café. He finally got the message. He's never forgotten it since.
textes.Un jour, il a voulu chasser les mouettes: One day he tried to chase the gulls off my grill with his amin's staff. He made great windmill swings. A gull slipped under the staff and took his turban. The whole auction watched the white turban fly away over the Skala. I told him: “You see, the gull tax is for everyone.”
textes.Un jour, il a voulu me mettre à l'épreuv: One day, he wanted to put me to the test. He threw five dice behind a curtain, four honest and one loaded, and asked me which. I listened. I said: “The third.” He opened the curtain. It was the third. He closed the curtain again, very gently. Since then, he raises his hat to me. He didn't before.
textes.Un jour, il a voulu présenter Xan à mes: One day, he wanted to introduce Xan to my bees, “so they become friends”. He opened his gourd in front of the hive. The bees came out, they circled around the mosquito, very curious… and Xan went back into the gourd all by himself. Kinich said: “He's shy.” I think he'd understood who was in charge.
textes.Un jour, il est arrivé dans ma cuisine a: One day, he came into my kitchen with a tiny little fish in his hands. I got out the frying pan. He looked at me with eyes like saucers and said: “He's going to grow.” We went and released him together, at the pontoon. Since then, when he goes fishing, he says hello to him. He's sure it's always the same one.
textes.Un jour, il est arrivé de l'oasis avec u: One day, he arrived from the oasis with a whole palm trunk on his camel. Three days' walk. “For your boats.” Palm wood is soft, it frays, it won't make a hull. I couldn't tell him. I made a bench out of it in front of the house: Mbarek's bench. He sits on it every visit. He looks pleased.
textes.Un jour, il est descendu avec un pot de: One day he came down with a jar of sauce for me to taste. “It needs a bit more salt,” I said. He didn't come back down for a month.
textes.Un jour, il est passé devant l'étal, il: One day he walked past the stall, said hello, smiled, turned round to smile at me again… and three bowls fell. Three! He paid in sardines, a whole crate. I gave it to Mustapha. The next day, he came by again. He smiled. I told him: “Don't turn round.” He turned round.
textes.Un jour, il est remonté du premier étage: One day, he came up from the first floor with a little slime stuck to his back. The slime wouldn't let go. Hilaire kept it for a week. He called it Gooey. He fed it bread crusts. One morning, Gooey went back to the dungeon all on its own. Hilaire was sad. He says it was his first companion.
textes.Un jour, il est venu au concert avec son: One day, he came to the gig with his little hammer. I let him hit the cowbell for one song. He was concentrating so hard he stuck his tongue out for four minutes. He was right on the beat.
textes.Un jour, il est venu m'annoncer un impôt: One day, he came to announce a tax on trade. I took out my scales and said: “Very well, Excellency. Then I'll charge you the tax on scales.” He thought about it for a long time. Then he abolished the tax. That same evening, he gave a speech on the freedom of trade. A very good speech. I applauded.
One day, he came to return a book. Not the right one: another, borrowed eighty years ago, that I thought was lost. I thanked him. He stood there, wings drooping a little, like a pupil waiting for his mark. I smiled at him. He left without a word. For him, that's quite a feat.
textes.Un jour, il est venu sur le Pont et il s: One day, he came onto the Bridge and sat down beside me without a word. A whole minute. Then he said: “A minute's a long time.” I laughed. He was very proud to have made me laugh. So was I.
textes.Un jour, il m'a acheté trois tapis de l': One day he bought three oasis carpets from me. He talked for four hours. The tribes, the wool, the price of tea, his grandmother, the wedding, the rain. Four hours. I drank my tea. At the end he named his price. I said: “No.” He paid mine. He sat down on a carpet, exhausted. I let him rest.
textes.Un jour, il m'a apporté un plan, dessiné: One day he brought me a plan, drawn in pencil: a skate ramp going down from the Clouds to the Azure Dome. I said: “That's impossible.” Then I looked at it all night. It's only missing one valve.
textes.Un jour, il m'a apporté un éclat qui cha: One day, he brought me a chip that sings when you blow on it. He said: “It's worthless, it's cracked.” I made it into a pendant. The next day, he came back to look at it. Three times.
textes.Un jour, il m'a apporté une chouquette e: One day, he brought me a choux bun, saying: “It was a spare.” Gustave never makes spare choux buns. He'd bought it for me.
textes.Un jour, il m'a apporté une nouvelle rie: One day, he brought me a piece of news just for me: “Flora Verdine, up in the Clouds, has named a strawberry plant after you.” He'd heard it from a tourist. I didn't say anything. I blushed like a mandarin on the side facing the lamp. He made a note of it. I saw him.
textes.Un jour, il m'a apporté une sardine fait: One day he brought me a sardine made “according to my recipe”, on a plate with a flower. Three hours of cooking, honey, cinnamon. Black as a boot, sticky as tar. He looked at me with happy-puppy eyes. I ate it. All of it. Smiling. I said the smoke was making my eyes water. It wasn't the smoke.
textes.Un jour, il m'a demandé de le peindre en: One day, he asked me to paint him jumping over the Chasm. I said no: it's dangerous. I painted him jumping over a puddle. He sulked for an hour. Then he showed the mural to everyone.
textes.Un jour, il m'a demandé si la soupe étai: One day, he asked me if the soup was better on the days the Great Singer went by. I said yes, as a joke. He did a study. Three months. He concluded that it was. I've never dared admit I was joking. Now I believe it too.
textes.Un jour, il m'a demandé un chapeau qui n: One day he asked me for a hat that wouldn't blow away. I sewed little lead weights into the brim. The wind carried it off anyway. It just flew lower, that's all, and landed on the head of Father Clotaire, who was asleep on the temple steps. Clotaire wore it for two hours without waking up. The Baron said it suited him better.
textes.Un jour, il m'a demandé une potion pour: One day he asked me for a potion for his knees. I made him one, the best. He drank it. His knees felt better for a day. He went down ten steps into the dungeon, for the first time in fifteen years. Then he came back up, sat down, and cried. He told me: “Thank you, Aubin. That's enough. Ten steps is a lot.”
One day, he showed me his two notebooks. The first: “Hilaire's Advice”. The second: “What Hilaire Does”. I read both. The first is full of good ideas. The second is full of drawings of me falling over. They're very lifelike. I asked if I could keep one. He gave me the one where I fall in the lake.
textes.Un jour, il m'a offert un portrait de mo: One day, he gave me a charcoal portrait of myself. All grey. I cried on it. It went all blurry. He framed it anyway.
textes.Un jour, il m'a pris le marteau des main: One day, he took the hammer out of my hands: “A real blacksmith's blow.” A real blow, all right. The tray split in two. I made him pay for it, full price. He paid without arguing. The split tray, I hung on the wall of the workshop. When he walks by, he looks at it. So do I. Worth more than a speech.
textes.Un jour, il m'a proposé des lunettes. À: One day, he offered me spectacles. Me. The guard of the Lookout. I said no. The next day, a pair was sitting on the watchtower railing. “By chance.” I put them away in the drawer. Without trying them on. They're still there. I haven't tried them on. I'm telling you so it's clear.
textes.Un jour, il m'a proposé quatre cents piè: One day, he offered me four hundred coins for my whole collection. Four hundred! I thought about it for a second. One tiny little second. Then I thought of my father's spiral shell, and I said no. Isaac sighed: “Everything's for sale, my girl.” I said: “Not this.” He gave a strange smile. I think he was glad I refused.
textes.Un jour, il m'a raconté une blague à lui: One day, he told me a joke of his own: “Why does the tree never answer? Because it's still leafing through the request.” I laughed for ten minutes. He asked me where the funny was. I told him: “You.”
textes.Un jour, il m'a rapporté un pot de sauce: One day he brought me back a jar of sauce with a ribbon on it. “These are your tomatoes,” he said. It's the only time I've ever seen him smile.
textes.Un jour, il m'a vendu une boule à neige,: One day, he sold me a snow globe, a lighthouse in the snow. “To cool down your kiosk.” I paid full price. It's on my counter, next to the till. When it's too hot, customers shake it. It doesn't cool anything down at all. But everyone smiles.
One day, a mooncake was missing. Mochi was there, looking innocent, ears flattened right down. Too flattened. I lifted an ear: the cake was underneath, stuck, half-eaten. She said: “It was cold.” Since then, before I count the cakes, I count the ears.
textes.Un jour, il s'est posé sur l'enveloppe d: One day, he landed on the Dragonfly's envelope, in mid-flight. He said: “Just passing.” I said: “You're paying the fare.” He gave me a feather. I kept it.
textes.Un jour, il y a trente ans, je suis desc: One day, thirty years ago, I got off Bernadette to pick up my cap. I hadn't put the brake on properly. Bernadette set off all by herself, ever so slowly, and went all the way round the cavern. Without me! She stopped right at the platform. People clapped. Ever since, I say she doesn't need me. But I don't get off for my cap any more.
textes.Un jour, j'abattais un grand chêne au bo: One day, I was felling a big oak by the river. I shouted “Timber!”, but too late: it fell right on the king's boat, which was passing by. The king wasn't in it, luckily. His hat was. They told me: “Prison or the navy.” Me, I ran all the way to the port and took the first boat leaving. It had a black flag.
textes.Un jour, j'ai accueilli un visiteur sans: One day, I welcomed a visitor without waiting for Écliptique. He came running, toga in hand, with his eleven-minute speech. The visitor had already left. So we gave our speeches to each other, on the lookout. We applauded. It was a lovely ceremony.
textes.Un jour, j'ai acheté un sabre superbe à: One day, I bought a superb sabre from a passing sailor, and put it in the window: “Toledo sabre, rare piece”. Brutus came in, picked it up, turned it over, and showed me a little mark on the guard: a hammer. His mark. He'd forged it himself, three years earlier. I offered him a friend's price. He bent an iron bar. I lowered the price.
One day, I brought Miou to the workshop. He jumped onto the fresh jars and walked across them, one by one, with his little paws! Ptahmosé shouted “Hm!” really loudly. And then he fired the jars just like that, paw prints and all. The temple bought every one! Miou is an artist.
textes.Un jour, j'ai apporté à Aëlwen une fleur: One day I brought Aëlwen a moonflower that had opened at high noon. She said it was worthless. I said it was worth double, since it was rare. We argued for an hour. Then we put it in a glass of water between us and drank a cup of tea.
textes.Un jour, j'ai caché un gâteau de lune da: One day I hid a mooncake in my ears. They're floppy, so it's a really good hiding place. But Mummy lifted my ear, and the cake was there. A bit eaten. I said it was cold. Mummy laughed. She doesn't laugh like that very often, so sometimes I do it again, on purpose.
textes.Un jour, j'ai caché une de ses haches da: One day, I hid one of her axes in a wasps' nest. So she couldn't cut down a living tree! She went to get it. She came back with the axe, three stings on her snout, and she didn't say anything. Nothing at all. She just put the axe down on the anvil. Ever since, I've wondered whether that was a win.
textes.Un jour, j'ai calculé que le soleil alla: One day, I calculated that the sun would go out at high noon, forty days later. Nobody believed me, except Ix Kanul's mother, the high priestess at the time. When the day came, at noon, the sky went black, the birds fell silent… and the sun came back. For once, I had counted right. To the hour! I still tremble with pride.
textes.Un jour, j'ai copié son secret : trois c: One day I copied his secret: three carrots before the race, not one more. Except carrots don't suit a wolf at all. I ran the whole loop with a wolf-sized tummy ache. Still second! Bondi asked if I wanted a fourth one next time. He's very funny, Bondi. Very.
textes.Un jour, j'ai crié « Lucas ! » depuis la: One day, I shouted “Lucas!” from the harbour office, about a simple timetable. He jumped and dropped a crate of lemons into the harbour. We fished them out together, with landing nets, for an hour. He apologised for every lemon. I was counting. Three were missing. I didn't note them in the register.
textes.Un jour, j'ai demandé à Doc combien de t: One day, I asked Doc how long a parrot lives. He said: “A hundred years, sometimes more.” I did the maths. I didn't say a word for at least a minute: that's a record. He lent me a book on birds. I dog-eared every page about memory. He didn't ask me anything. Doc knows when not to ask.
textes.Un jour, j'ai demandé à Mélusine si elle: One day, I asked Mélusine if she could whisper. She tried. She half-closed her mouth, put on a teeny tiny voice, and said: “hello”. A horse bolted from the stable. We laughed so hard we had to sit on the ground. She says she's practising. I prefer her real voice.
textes.Un jour, j'ai dit que ses daurades n'éta: One day, I said her sea bream wasn't fresh enough anymore. Day-old sea bream! I said it to Lola, just to Lola, a bit loudly maybe, and Lola repeated it to the whole quay. Since then, Rosalie has dinner here every evening, sitting bolt upright, and she eats while staring at me. So I really feel that she's cross. I feel it. She has seconds of dessert.
textes.Un jour, j'ai dit un gros mot. C'était «: One day I said a bad word. It was “knife.” The Reverend went all white. Mamma sent me to the corner, next to the oven. It was warm and smelled of bread. Maybe I'll do it again.
textes.Un jour, j'ai entendu dire qu'à Cliqueti: One day I heard that in Cliquetis they had spring shoes. Boing, boing, and hop, three arches in one go! I ran to beg Ursule to forge me some. She said “No.”, she told Pépin, and Pépin said “cheating”. I sulked for a week. Now, every evening, I just ask her for horseshoes that are a teeny bit lighter. Just in case.
textes.Un jour, j'ai essayé de lui troquer « un: One day, I tried to swap her “one bridge for two bridges”. The deal of the century! She asked which ones. I showed her two little string bridges, knotted by yours truly the night before. She laughed so hard she nearly fell off her beam. She said no. But she gave me a hazelnut for the idea.
textes.Un jour, j'ai eu la fièvre et je suis re: One day I had a fever and stayed in bed. Mustapha sold half as much: the customers ate without hurrying, and nobody else came. The next day he came to my house with six sardines wrapped in paper. He said: “Get well quick, my grill is falling asleep.” I got well. Sardines cure everything.
textes.Un jour, j'ai fait deux fournées de chau: One day, I made two batches of turnovers: one with Babette's apples, one with Germaine's. I asked each of them to taste, without saying anything. Babette chose Germaine's. Germaine chose Babette's. I never told them. They'd be quite capable of getting cross with me, for once in agreement.
textes.Un jour, j'ai fait tomber mon balai cont: One day I dropped my broom against the Lid. It went “bong.” A teeny tiny bong. Macaroni counted “one” out loud, staring right at me.
textes.Un jour, j'ai fait toute la ronde des cr: One day, I did the whole round of the battlements behind the caïd. I walked just like him, really slowly, hand on my wooden sabre, nose in the air. The guards were laughing, and he didn't understand why. He only saw me at the end, when he turned around. He made a funny face. I think he wanted to laugh.
textes.Un jour, j'ai forgé des roulettes en lai: One day, I forged brass wheels for his board. They throw sparks when he brakes. The whole Fronde clapped. Ressort says it's the best present in the world, and tries to keep the sparks in a jar. It doesn't work. Ressort keeps trying.
textes.Un jour, j'ai goûté une soupe de Lentill: One day, I tasted one of Lentille's soups and gave it two out of ten. He went quite pale. The next day, he brought me a pumpkin soup with honey. I tasted it, closed my eyes, and wrote ten on a napkin. He framed it. I pretend I haven't seen it.
textes.Un jour, j'ai jeté une noisette dans la: One day I threw a hazelnut in the big pond to bait the dragon. Plop! Moustache went “Shhhhh” for a really, really long time. I asked if the dragon had eaten it. He said yes! So the next day I threw in three. He said the dragon wasn't hungry any more. I think it's on a diet.
textes.Un jour, j'ai laissé une épée neuve sur: One day I left a new sword on the counter while I went to fetch water. Madame Olga came by. When I got back, the sword was pink, it shone, and when you drew it from its sheath, it sang a lullaby. Olga was delighted: “It puts monsters to sleep!” I sold the sword to Rodrigue. He doesn't know yet that it sings.
textes.Un jour, j'ai livré mes bottes de lin ch: One day, I delivered my bunches of flax to Tiyi's. In the last one, there was a ginger kitten, the size of a fist, with a crooked ear. I swear I hadn't put it there. Little Nebet picked it up and named it Miou. Tiyi looked at me. I said: “It's not mine.” She smiled. It came from my field. I know.
textes.Un jour, j'ai mis trois fois trop de la: One day, I put three times too much of Zébuline's fire cinnamon in my brioches. They were smoking as they came out of the oven! The customers loved them. Now, every Friday, it's the “smoking brioche”. I say it's our joint invention. Zébuline says it's mostly mine. We can't agree.
textes.Un jour, j'ai oublié le sel. Elle était: One day I forgot the salt. She was twenty metres away. She shouted “the salt!” before I'd even tasted it.
textes.Un jour, j'ai parié au souk que je devin: One day, I bet in the souk that I could guess everyone's shoe size, just by looking. A whole month. I was wrong only once: Mbarek, the caravan driver. I said forty-three. He took off his sandal. Caravan-driver feet, wide as dunes! I made him a made-to-measure pair. He keeps them for special occasions.
textes.Un jour, j'ai pleuré au-dessus de sa mar: One day I cried over her pot of moon tea. She didn't say a thing; she bottled it all, with a label: “Tea of Tears”. She sold it very dear. I didn't get a single coin. Just a sugared petal. She says that's the fair price of a tear.
textes.Un jour, j'ai posé Bouton sur le rebord: One day I put Button on the ledge of the watchtower. Button jumped into Thalion's soup bowl. Thalion yelled so loud the birds flew off. He says he wasn't scared, he was “surprised”. I saw him jump backwards. He was scared. A bit.
textes.Un jour, j'ai pris une dorade vivante su: One day, I took a live sea bream from mum's stall and put it in the fountain on the square. I called it Captain. Mum shouted so loud that all the gulls flew off. And then she left it there for three days. On the fourth morning, Captain was gone. Mum says it went back to the sea all by itself. But mum's apron was all wet.
textes.Un jour, j'ai raconté une blague à Plume: One day, I told a joke to Plumeau, the gardener robot. He recorded it. The next day, he told it back to me, word for word, with my pauses. Then he asked me: “Where is the funny?” I couldn't answer. Since then, I tell him one a day. He's up to a hundred and twelve. He still hasn't found the funny. Neither have I, sometimes.
textes.Un jour, j'ai rapporté à Jacquot une sar: One day, I brought Jacquot a sardine I'd caught myself. He cooked it like it was for an admiral: honey, cinnamon, three hours of cooking. It came out all black. I ate it right down to the bone, 'cause he was watching me. I had tears in my eyes. He thinks it was emotion.
textes.Un jour, j'ai rapporté à Nébula un patch: One day, I brought Nébula a patch from the Bilge Rats, those punks from Boucan. She put it in the window with the label “Badge of a distant warrior people.” I nearly choked laughing. She sold it to Orbe for the price of an astral crystal. He framed it.
textes.Un jour, j'ai raté mon crochet. Je voula: One day, I botched my hook. I wanted to cry. She took it, looked at it for a long time, and said: “It has character.” Then she hung it above her anvil. It's still there.
textes.Un jour, j'ai réparé le distributeur du: One day I fixed the vending machine on the corner with my hairpin. Now it gives two sodas instead of one. Papa says it's a bug. I say it's a feature.
textes.Un jour, j'ai suivi Hilaire jusqu'au Lac: One day, I secretly followed Hilaire all the way to the Frog Lake. He got swallowed. I screamed so loud the frog spat him straight back out. Hilaire said: “Thank you, Noisette. You've got a town crier's voice.” Mélusine heard about it. Since then, she lets me ring her bell. Once a week. With both hands.
textes.Un jour, j'ai suivi Sire Tancrède jusqu': One day, I secretly followed Sir Tancrède all the way to the Goblin Wood. A goblin saw me. Tancrède charged, shouting his name, tripped over his cape, fell on the goblin, and the goblin ran away. He said he did it on purpose. I saw it: he did it on purpose. Almost.
textes.Un jour, j'ai suivi le fleuve jusqu'à la: One day, I followed the river to the sea, to see where all that water was going. I never went home. Cabin boy, topman, boatswain. Ignace found me on a quay, twelve years ago. “Can you handle a crew?” I said: “Yes.” “Do you ask questions?” I said: “No.” He hired me. Best conversation of my life.
textes.Un jour, j'ai touché son chèche, et aprè: One day, I touched his chèche, and afterwards my fingers were all blue! I showed them to the whole square: “Look, I'm a blue man!” I didn't wash my hands for three days. Mum caught me on the fourth.
textes.Un jour, j'ai trouvé des traces de jagua: One day, I found jaguar tracks! I shouted for Balam. He looked at the tracks, then told me to look behind me. It was Peek', sitting with one paw up! They were his tracks. So I said: “It's a dog jaguar.” We followed them anyway. They led to a bone.
textes.Un jour, j'ai trouvé une couronne de mar: One day, I found a daisy crown hooked on my skateboard. There was a note: “For the heads of people who fall.” I put it on. I fell. It stayed on.
textes.Un jour, j'ai vendu du « copal béni par: One day, I sold “copal blessed by the high priest”. He hadn't blessed it. He came to my stall, looking stern. I held out a piece: “Bless it, and it'll be true.” He blessed it. I don't know why. Neither does he. That day I doubled my prices, and in the evening I treated him to a cacao. He drank it. I think he likes me.
textes.Un jour, j'ai voulu chasser les mouettes: One day, I tried to chase the seagulls off the grill with my amin's staff. Big swirling sweeps, lots of authority. A seagull flew underneath, took my turban and carried it off over the Skala. The whole fish market watched my turban fly. Mustapha said: “The tax is for everyone.” I didn't set a single price that day.
textes.Un jour, j'ai voulu faire comme Dame Yso: One day, I wanted to do like Lady Ysolde. I took a rope, a pulley and a salad basket, and I put the cat in it. The cat went up as far as the first-floor window. It jumped into the neighbour's. It lives there now. That's a bit my fault.
textes.Un jour, j'ai voulu lui troquer sa flûte: One day, I tried to swap his flute for “two flutes”. Two for one, a golden deal! That fox blew into the second one before shaking on it. Not a sound: it was a silent whistle. He gave it back to me, saying: “Keep it, Bedaine. It's just like you: lots of air, not a sound.” Heh heh… nicely done. I'll get him back for that.
textes.Un jour, j'ai voulu photographier la gra: One day, I wanted to photograph the big pot on the stove. Paulo leapt forward, threw a tea towel over it and planted himself in front of it, arms spread: “Not the pot! Because of the secret!” I only photographed the tea towel. It's my most mysterious photo. And it's in focus, too.
textes.Un jour, j'ai voulu rendre le nectar de: One day I tried to make Mélisse's nectar fizzy, to help her. Her bottles had hiccups for a week: they blew bubbles and sang! She sold twice as much. And my share? A ribbon. ONE ribbon. I kept it anyway, it's pretty.
textes.Un jour, j'ai voulu verser le thé de hau: One day, I wanted to pour tea from up high, like him. It looked easy. I raised the teapot very high, and drenched the turban of Mbarek, sitting next to me. Mbarek said nothing. He wrung out his turban and held out his glass. Since then, I let Hassan pour. To each his trade.
textes.Un jour, j'ai vu Germaine et Babette se: One day, I saw Germaine and Babette arguing on the square, at the top of their voices, about turnips. I went over to offer each of them a house, far away from each other. They turned to me at the same time and shouted: “NO!” With one voice. Then they went back to arguing. I understood I'd never sell anything to those two.
textes.Un jour, j'ai vu briller quelque chose s: One day, I saw something shining under Miss Prune's jacket. A Bilge Rats badge. She saw that I'd seen it. She buttoned her jacket. I didn't tell Dad. She doesn't tell Dad when I tap. We protect each other. It's the only conspiracy at the Sales Office.
textes.Un jour, j'aurai un voilier, et je l'app: One day I'll have a sailboat, and I'll call it “Further-Out”. I'll sail round the archipelago, island by island: the village, the jungle, the elves, the dwarves… and the flying island, if it's willing to come down a bit.
textes.Un jour, j'avais mal à la gorge et je n': One day, I had a sore throat and didn't laugh all morning. Ludovic came running up from the mine, helmet on his head, to see if everything was all right. I gave him a “ho”. A tiny one. He went back down reassured.
textes.Un jour, j'ouvrirai une vraie auberge, a: One day, I'll open a real inn, with beds. On dry land. That doesn't move.
textes.Un jour, j'éclairerai toute la cité sans: One day, I'll light up the whole city without a drop of oil. For now, I light up my laboratory very nicely. When it isn't catching fire.
textes.Un jour, je ferai le tour de toute l'île: One day, I'll run all the way round the island. Cliquetis, Tazira, Carène, and back. Faster than the Zéphyr! … OK, maybe not faster than the Zéphyr.
textes.Un jour, je l'ai entendu chuchoter « dou: One day, I heard him whisper “easy now, my lovely” to a crate of bottles he was unloading from a boat. He set it down like a newborn. It arrived in one piece. Since then, when a fragile cargo arrives, I hand it to Lucas. I haven't told him why.
textes.Un jour, je l'ai mis à l'épreuve : cinq: One day, I put him to the test: five dice behind a curtain, only one loaded. He listened to them roll, and he said: “The third one.” It was the third one. I closed the curtain. I thought of all the times I'd sworn to a customer that those dice were undetectable. Since then, I take my hat off when he passes. Talent deserves respect.
textes.Un jour, je l'ai suivi de loin dans la m: One day, I followed him at a distance into the mine, to finally find his famous seam. After an hour, I had no idea where I was. He's the one who found me, whistling, lantern in hand. He never asked me what I was doing there. That's almost worse.
textes.Un jour, je l'ai vu plisser les yeux ver: One day I saw him squinting towards the big pond, for a long, long time. I offered him glasses, just in passing. He took offence: “A guard sees.” So I left my second pair on the Lookout railing, by chance. It vanished the next day. I don't know where. I don't ask.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai demandé : « Je tombe: One day I asked her: “I fall without getting hurt, I shine without fire, and I cry without sorrow.” She happened to be crying. She said: “A drop… like me?” She was right! I wrote in my big book: “the only riddle solved by Brindille”. She cried again. For joy, this time, I think.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai demandé ce qu'elle vo: One day I asked her what she really wanted in an outfit. She thought for a long time. Then she said: “An outfit where my hair stays flat.” I sewed a little hat with pins on the inside. Her hair stayed flat. Her head gave off sparks. We're making progress.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai demandé pourquoi elle: One day, I asked her why she never asked questions. She said: “Lettuces don't ask questions either. And they grow very well.” I didn't understand. I wrote it down. I often reread it. I'm starting to understand.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai demandé pourquoi il r: One day, I asked him why he stayed rank F. He thought about it, then he said: “So there's always someone to welcome you, you and the others.” I didn't understand right away. Then I saw how he talks to the newcomers, on their first day. I think he's the best adventurer in the Guild. He just fails a lot.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai demandé si les légend: One day, I asked her if the dungeon legends were true. She said: “All of them. Even the false ones.” I didn't understand. I wrote the sentence in my spellbook. It's the only page that hasn't flown out of the window. I think it's the most magical sentence I own.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai dit : « Hrmm. La cime: One day, I said to her: “Hrmm. Treetop. Sunset.” My longest speech. She said: “Oh… yes, it must be very pretty from up there.” And she left. She didn't come. Hrmm. Maybe I wasn't clear.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai fait sentir une épice: One day, I had her smell a spice from faraway islands, a black bark I've kept in my apron pocket for twenty years. She sniffed, went quiet, and asked: “What is it?” Aïcha, who knows everything! She didn't know it. I kept the name to myself. I need a secret of my own, too.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai offert ma meilleure t: One day, I offered her my best moon tea, the one with pond elderflower. She drank, she thought for a long time, and she said: “Hot water.” Hot water! I bring it up with every vial. She doesn't apologise. But I can tell she comes back for a cup, in winter, when nobody's looking.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai pris le marteau. Pour: One day I took his hammer. To show him a real blow. A blacksmith's blow. The tray split. In two. He looked at me. He made me pay. Full price. I paid. He hung the split tray on the wall of his stall. He says it's to remember. Hm. I remember too.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai proposé de goûter, le: One day I offered her a blindfold tasting of “a spice mix on bread”. She agreed, for the spice. She chewed, and said: “Delicious. What cumin!” I took off the blindfold. It was a sardine. She got cross and left shouting. But she'd said delicious. In front of Saïd. The whole quay knows.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai prêté ma flûte-colibr: One day, I lent him my hummingbird flute. He blew. It made the sound of a sneezing duck. I laughed till I cried. He gave it back to me very quickly, bright red. But afterwards, I saw him looking at the flute out of the corner of his eye. For a long time. The way a jaguar looks at a bird.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai raconté une histoire: One day, I told her a story of my own: a baker who sang so well that the dough rose all by itself, and a miller all white with flour who listened behind the door. Grandma Philomène laughed really loud. Then she said: “Keep that one safe. It's a true one.” I don't know how she knows. It's my story.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai rapporté un enregistr: One day, I brought him back a recording made at a hundred and ninety-nine metres: the Singer, and behind her, a small, higher voice. He listened to it two hundred times. He said: “A little one.” Then he gave me a hug. It's the only time I've ever seen him forget his whale for someone else.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai rapporté un seau d'ea: One day, I brought her back a bucket of seawater from Hautefond. She kept her hands in it for an hour. She said: “It's cold, and it stings a bit.” She looked like the happiest person in the sky.
textes.Un jour, je lui ai récité les vingt arti: One day, I recited all twenty articles of the rulebook to him while he was going up. He said it calmed him down. Then he said it put him to sleep.
textes.Un jour, je me suis dit : et si un piano: One day, I thought: what if a whole piano played by itself? Three years. Twelve thousand pins planted by hand, one by one. The page-turner was Philibert's idea, a plaque says so. On opening night, the piano played its waltz, turned its pages, and at the end, it took a bow. The whole hall applauded. I was in the wings.
textes.Un jour, je me suis évanoui dans la cabi: Once, I fainted in the cabin. I woke up with her jacket under my head. She said it was “to protect the floor”.
textes.Un jour, je montrais le fil d'or à Karim: One day, I was showing the gold thread to Karim when Rachid walked by. Karim hid the thread in his turban, Rachid asked what we were doing, and Karim started laughing. He laughed and laughed, he couldn't speak, with a bit of gold thread dangling over his ear. I said he was thinking of a joke. Rachid still looks at us sideways.
textes.Un jour, je planerai d'ici jusqu'à Haute: One day, I'll glide from here all the way to Hautefond. Two hundred metres down, spiralling round the Column. Mistress Capucine said: “Not round my Column.” Barnabé said: “I'll watch… later.” I think they're encouraging me.
textes.Un jour, je réussirai un sort parfait, d: One day, I'll cast a perfect spell, in front of everyone. And Pyra will clap. Pyra never claps. It'll be the best day of my life.
textes.Un jour, je serai capitaine. Je réparera: One day, I'll be captain. I'll repair the Léviathan, we'll put it back in the water, and we'll all set sail. Everyone laughs when I say that. Except Tobias. He sighs.
textes.Un jour, je suis descendue d'un battemen: One day, I popped down in the blink of an eye to the kingdom of roots, under the elves' island. I wanted a seed from the Mother Tree. I dug under an old root, just a teeny hole. Well, big enough for me. A bearded goblin came out with a broom shouting “Thief!”. I got my seed. And I bumped into three roots running away.
textes.Un jour, je suis monté sur le toit de la: One day I climbed onto the roof of the Bielle with an umbrella from her shop. I'd opened it, I was going to jump, like Achille when he was little. And whoops, a hand grabbed me by the collar. Adèle! She'd climbed all the way up the ladder. She told me about all seventeen of Achille's bumps. One by one. On the roof. It took ages.
textes.Un jour, je suis remontée avec dix minut: One day, I came back up ten minutes late: a ray had settled on the porthole, and I didn't dare disturb it. On the quay, Yolande had spilt both hot chocolates. She didn't say anything. Neither did I. We went and got two more at La Conque. She held hers with both hands.
textes.Un jour, je suis rentré du lac avec un s: One day, I came back from the lake with one shoe on, slime up to my ears and a reed in my hair. Églantine smiled, stamped my card “attempt” and handed me a towel. She has a pile of towels under the counter, just for me. They're embroidered with an “H”.
textes.Un jour, je suis restée longtemps sous l: One day, I stayed a long time under the hull, looking at the signs. When I came up, I found Ewen white as a sheet at the end of the pontoon, with a rope and a life ring: he'd stopped counting at three hundred, and he was about to jump. He can't dive. Since then, I wave to him before going down for a long time.
textes.Un jour, je suis tombé de mon monocycle: One day, I fell off my unicycle right in the middle of Chaussette's pack. All six dogs licked my face at once to comfort me. I was laughing so hard I couldn't get up. It's my best fall. I do it again sometimes. For the dogs.
textes.Un jour, je suis tombé si fort au skatep: One day, I fell so hard at the skatepark that my shoe left a mark on the ramp. Pigment painted a circle round the mark, with a star and the date. Now it's a monument! The little ones come and put their foot in it. I'm famous. For a fall, but famous.
textes.Un jour, je suivais Gaspard sur le quai: One day, I was following Gaspard along the quay to see the Admiral up close. The Admiral looked at me with one eye, then the other, and squawked: “GROUPER-HEAD!” A rude word! For me! I told everybody. Mum said it wasn't a rude word. I say it is. It's my nickname now.
One day I'll trip and fall.
One day, I'll sell the wind. You'll see.
textes.Un jour, je volerai jusqu'à l'île flotta: One day, I'll fly all the way to the floating island, up north. And I'll shout “MINE” so loud the clouds will hear it.
textes.Un jour, je voudrais m'allumer, rien qu': Someday, I'd love to light up, just once! Just for one little second, like a real firefly. And for Zéphyr to see me and say “wow”. He'll never say “wow”. But a fairy can dream!
textes.Un jour, la drisse a cassé pendant qu'il: One day, the halyard snapped while he was climbing the mast. I caught him by the belt, one-handed, and set him back on the shrouds like you put a bottle on a shelf. He weighs nothing, Fil-de-Fer. Less than a sack of potatoes. He said thank you for a week. After that, he told me my hands were dirty.
textes.Un jour, la veille d'une course, Grelot: One day, the day before a race, Grelot sold me an apple pie. Very good. Next day, I find out: there was grated carrot in it! A pie with hidden carrot! The day before a race! I ran with four carrots in my tummy, maybe five. I still won. But since then, I sniff all her pies.
textes.Un jour, le Capitaine Isidore est venu p: One day, Captain Isidore came fishing at the lake with me, to prove to me it wasn't dangerous. After an hour, the Duchess poked her head out of the water, right next to the boat. The Captain didn't move. He looked at her, she looked at him. Then he said, very calmly: “Good day, Madam.” She dived. He went back to the harbour and never mentioned it to me again.
textes.Un jour, le grimoire d'Olga a perdu tout: One day, all the pages of Olga's spellbook flew out of the window. She came to see me in tears. I recited from memory the ten spells she'd read to me over the years, on this bench. She copied them out one by one. She said: “Philomène, you're my spellbook.” I answered: “Then don't leave me near a window.”
textes.Un jour, le majordome a servi par erreur: One day the butler served an iron-powder coffee by mistake to a lady from Port-Azur. She thought it was a local speciality. The next day Master Rivet adjusted his robot: now it asks every customer “Iron, or no iron?”. The tourists find it very authentic.
textes.Un jour, le professeur m'a laissé appuye: One day the professor let me push the lever for an explosion. A teeny tiny one, he said. He made me step back: “Further. Further.” Then: “Go!” I pushed. It went pff, with a blue cloud of smoke as big as a hat. He clapped! He said: “Smoke is the beginning of everything.” I wrote it on my bedroom wall.
textes.Un jour, le sifflet de midi a retenti av: One day, the noon whistle went off two seconds late. Two! I put my watch on the counter, asked for a size-eight spanner, and went to adjust the valve myself, on the old locomotive. Since then, noon on the dot. Gaston says it has never whistled so true.
textes.Un jour, le théâtre a fermé. On m'a dit: One day, the theatre closed. They told me to throw everything out. I filled three suitcases with fabric scraps: velvet, silk, brocade, pirate canvas. I arrived in Boucan with my suitcases. Trocante opened the first one and shouted: “Treasure!” I knew I was in the right place.
textes.Un jour, les papillons du troisième dôme: One day, the butterflies in the third dome went on strike. They refused to pollinate the apple trees. I searched for a week. They found the flowers too crowded. I spread the branches. They came back the next day. I learned you should always listen to your colleagues. Even when they have wings.
textes.Un jour, ma jambe s'est coincée entre de: One day, my leg got stuck between two rotten planks of the pontoon. Impossible to get it out. The whole port was watching, Corbeau first of all. The Silent One came along, took me under the arms and pulled me out like a carrot. Then he looked at Corbeau, without a word. She stopped laughing. Hm. It's a gift.
textes.Un jour, mon chapeau à plume s'est envol: One day my feathered hat blew over the castle wall. Hugues saw it go past from the Guild window. He ran, at his age, all the way to the bottom of the Hill, and caught it mid-air in front of the South Gate. He brought it back to me weeping with emotion. He said it was his first heroic deed in thirty years.
textes.Un jour, mon piano a joué une musique qu: One day, my piano played a tune I'd never taught it. I never found out where it came from. Maybe it came from Stoneheart.
textes.Un jour, on a fait la course autour de l: One day, we raced around the Tree. He won, fine. But he flew right through my cloud of fireflies, and they stayed stuck in his hair for three days. He glowed all over! He was furious. I thought he looked much prettier that way.
textes.Un jour, on a voulu attraper le Roi des: One day we wanted to catch the Pond King with a mooncake. We put it right on the edge of the big pond, and hid behind a bush, not moving, not talking. For three minutes! And then a duck came along and ate it. The whole thing! Myrtille said it might have been the King in disguise. I think it was a duck.
textes.Un jour, pendant la leçon, il nous a rac: One day, during the lesson, he told us about Taouret, the hippo goddess who protects children. So I told everyone: from now on, we don't say the hippo, we say Taouret! It's nicer. Taouret is a lady, but she's a goddess. He doesn't know we call him that. Shh.
textes.Un jour, pendant une course, l'Albatros: One day, during a race, Héloïse's Albatross broke down over the sea. I turned back. I towed her all the way to the Hautefond Mast. She didn't say a word the whole way. When we arrived, she just said: “Thank you.” And the Dragonfly's wings flapped. All by themselves. I've never held it against Mireille.
textes.Un jour, petit, je me suis perdu dans le: One day, as a boy, I got lost in my mother's gardens, among the ash peppers. I cried so loudly the sulphur roses closed up. It was my sister who found me. She hung a label round my neck: “Bulle, do not lose”. I wore it for a year. I still have it, in my drawer. Shh.
textes.Un jour, porter autre chose que du charb: One day, I'd like to carry something other than coal. Flowers, say. Flowers weigh nothing. Or a barrel of Sigrun's golden fizz: that weighs plenty, but it's worth it.
textes.Un jour, pour faire rire Pastille, j'ai: One day, to make Pastille laugh, I juggled her rolls of bandage. They unrolled in mid-air and landed all over Pallet Square, like streamers. We spent the afternoon rolling everything back up, with Cerise. Pastille was laughing so much she forgot to tell me off.
textes.Un jour, pour lui donner une leçon, je l: One day, to teach her a lesson, I weighed out turmeric and wrote on the packet: “saffron for fabric”. She opened it, looked, sniffed, and burst out laughing: “Nice turmeric, Lalla Aïcha.” A weaver who can recognise saffron! I didn't know whether to be offended or proud.
textes.Un jour, pour lui faire plaisir, je suis: Once, to cheer him up, I came back saying: “She smiled.” I hadn't delivered anything. He beamed all week. So did Ilyria, as it happens, without knowing why: he smiled so much that she ended up smiling back. So it wasn't quite a lie.
textes.Un jour, pour me faire pardonner, je lui: One day, to make amends, I brought her back a book. Not the right one: another, borrowed eighty years ago and completely forgotten. She opened it and said: “I thought this one was lost. Thank you.” She smiled. I'd never seen her smile. I was struck dumb. That's rare, for me.
textes.Un jour, pour voir, j'ai fait une lanter: One day, just to see, I made a lantern without a single hole. Nice and round, nice and smooth, my finest bumps. We lit the candle inside. Nothing. Not a star, not a glimmer: a hot cooking pot. Nourredine said nothing. He sat in front of it all evening, staring at the dark, looking very interested.
textes.Un jour, sa tisane était trop forte. Je: One day, her tea was too strong. I fell asleep at the counter, head on the envelopes. Three letters went out late. Three! Never in eight years. Pivoine said she'd measured it “for an owl”. I answered that an owl asleep at the counter is an owl who doesn't deliver.
textes.Un jour, sous le cadran arrêté, un touri: One day, under the stopped clock face, a tourist looked at the hands during my speech, then at his watch, and congratulated me: for once, the time was right. I thanked him. Hortense, in the front row, didn't laugh at all. Since then, I avoid looking up.
textes.Un jour, sur le port, j'ai vu un jeune g: One day, at the port, I saw a young giant carrying four crates at once and saying sorry to them. I planted myself in front of him and shouted: “YOU'RE GOING TO BE A CHAMPION!” He dropped everything. Ash eggs, everywhere. I paid for the eggs. It was Gorgoth. The best purchase of my life.
textes.Un jour, tout le village a voulu savoir: One day, the whole village wanted to know whose oven was best. We made the same dough, baked in his oven and in mine. Amenemhat tasted, blindfolded. The two loaves were exactly the same. Ptahmosé said: “My oven won.” I said: “Mine too.” We each went home, very pleased.
One day, you'll swim better. Sit down, kid.
textes.Un jour, un grand barbu est venu me fair: One day, a big bearded man came to have a wheelbarrow repaired. It was Copeau. I repaired it. He built me a workbench. I repaired his bike. He built me a shelf. Then a house. We decided we should stop swapping things and get married. We got married on a tandem made of pallets.
textes.Un jour, un jeune capitaine est venu com: One day, a young captain came to order a suit of armour. He never laughed, but I laughed at everything he said. He came back every day for a month to “check the measurements”. The armour had been finished for three weeks. I said yes before he dared to ask. Pyrus has been going clang beside me for twenty years.
textes.Un jour, un livre d'en bas est monté ave: One day, a book from down below floated up on the wind. A real book, made of paper, that smelled of ink and dust. I breathed it in for an hour before I dared open it. Since then, I've got ten thousand, brought by the wind, the birds and… other ways. I breathe them in secretly. They smell of the houses down below.
textes.Un jour, un marchand de passage m'a ache: One day, a passing merchant bought all my cacao, paid in beans, counted in front of me. That evening, while putting them away, a bean broke: inside, clay! He had emptied them and filled them with earth. A month of work, paid in mud. Since then, I test every bean with my teeth. And I count everything again. Even Ah Kin Pech's beans.
textes.Un jour, un paquet pour Ramure s'est mis: One day, a parcel for Ramure started ticking in the bag. Tick-tock, tick-tock. I thought it was one of Professor Boum's bombs and ran all the way to the water tank to throw it in. At the last moment, I read the label: “Tic Tacquet, for Pépin. Stopwatch. Fragile.” I wrote to Plumette: “Don't drown this one. I almost did.”
textes.Un jour, un pirate a éternué pendant la: One day, a pirate sneezed during the auction. He left with forty kilos of sardines. He had to eat them all week.
One day, a peccary scratched my leg. Yum Kab put honey on the scratch, and leaves on top. He said: “The honey of my bees heals everything, except foolishness.” In three days, it had closed. I don't know if I had been foolish. I didn't ask.
textes.Un jour, un touriste a loué un pédalo po: One day a tourist rented a pedalo on the first day of his holiday. Gérard Dupuis, super nice guy. He went round in circles for an hour, photographing the lighthouse on every lap. An hour! Kevin had to swim out to fetch him. Ever since, that pedalo's been called “Gérard”. It's painted on the hull, really small. Gérard doesn't know. Shh, OK?
textes.Un jour, un touriste s'était installé à: One day, a tourist had settled at my table, with a newspaper and a hat. Gisèle came over and put a little card in front of him: “Reserved for the harbour office.” He asked since when. She said: “Since forever.” He got up. The card didn't exist the day before. She'd written it just for him.
textes.Un jour, un vieux marin m'a vendu une pe: One day, an old sailor sold me a blue pearl “that shines all by itself, picked up under the sea”. I paid a lot for it. That evening, in the dark, it didn't shine. The next day, it was coming off on my fingers. Painted glass. Since then, I hate fakes. And I'm looking for the real one, the pearl of light people talk about. Stones don't lie. Sailors do.
textes.Un jour, un vieux monsieur d'en haut lui: One day, an old gentleman from up top answered her: “The sky? It's like your Dome, but without the glass.” She thought about it for a long time. Then she asked: “So what stops the blue from falling down?” The gentleman got back on the Funicular without answering. He looked very moved.
textes.Un jour, une androïde est entrée dans le: One day, an android came into the garden. She asked me: “What is beauty?” I didn't know how to answer. I gave her a brush. She's been searching for three years. So have I. We search together.
textes.Un jour, une caisse est arrivée de Carèn: One day, a crate arrived from Carène, full of ropes and pots. I opened it: out came a crab, as big as my hand, furious. He clearly didn't agree to being sold. He pinched my finger and scuttled off under Karim's stall. Salomé had put him on the bill. I put him on mine, as damages.
textes.Un jour, une caisse énorme est arrivée a: One day, an enormous crate arrived at the quay. I opened it. Inside was a big android, brand new, very shy. I said “welcome” to him. He looked at me for a whole minute. Then he said “thank you”. It was Cargo. He has never left my side.
textes.Un jour, une grenouille géante m'a avalé: One day, a giant frog swallowed me at the lakeside. Pétronille was scared to death. She prayed so hard the frog spat me out on top of her. We were both covered in slobber. I said: “Thank you, Sister, you saved me!” She answered: “Eww!” It was my first true rescue. Except she was the one who saved me.
textes.Un jour, une lettre est descendue des Nu: One day, a letter came down from the Clouds: “Dear colleague down below, what is happening beneath your feet? Above ours, there are clouds. I give them first names. Doctor Aurèle Brise.” I replied: “Down here, there are jellyfish. I give them names too.” Since then, we've written to each other every week. He's convinced that a jellyfish is a cloud that chose the sea. So am I. It's our only shared theory.
textes.Un jour, à cent quatre-vingt-dix-neuf mè: One day, at a hundred and ninety-nine metres, I switched off the floodlights to save the battery. Far, far below, in the darkness at the bottom of the Trench, a little light came on. Then another. Then they went out. Nobody knows what it is. The Professor says: “Maybe nothing.” I say: “Maybe someone.” Ever since, I watch for them on every dive.
textes.Un jour, à la fontaine, il m'a dit : « B: One day at the fountain he said to me: “Lovely day.” I said: “Very.” He ran off. I waited there an hour, in case he came back to finish his sentence. He came back the next day and said: “Lovely day.” We're making progress.
textes.Un jus de pomme au bar de la Guilde: An apple juice at the Guild bar
textes.Un lac noir, au fond du puits, avec des: A black lake at the bottom of the well, with carved slabs? The Ancients only had one song, {surnom}: the one on the fresco. Night, sea, day, serpent. Sing it as you walk.
textes.Un lait de nuage au Café Cumulus: A cloud milk at the Cumulus Café
textes.Un lait de nuage pour la table deux ! Av: One cloud milk for table two! Moustache on the house!
textes.Un lait de nuage, et la vue. Je ne deman: A cloud milk, and the view. I ask nothing more of life.
textes.Un lait de nuage, un ! Avec la moustache: One cloud milk, coming up! With the moustache!
textes.Un lait de nuage. Léger, sucré, avec un: A cloud milk. Light, sweet, with a taste of sky. And a free moustache.
textes.Un lingot d'or, pour payer les dieux: A gold ingot, to pay the gods
textes.Un livre d'aventures. Ça se voit : tu as: An adventure book. It shows: your boots are full of dust and your eyes are searching for the horizon. Shelf twelve, on the left. There are more. Quietly.
textes.Un livre ouvert ? (Elle sourit.) Ça doit: An open book? (She smiles.) That must be restful. I'm a file with a lining. It's more complicated. But it's prettier inside.
textes.Un livre, c'est un sorcier qui a gardé s: A book is a wizard who saved his voice for later. When you open it, it starts speaking again. It's the oldest magic in the world.
textes.Un livre, quelque part, en parle peut-êt: A book, somewhere, may speak of it.
textes.Un long boyau qui monte, des marches tai: A long tunnel climbing up, carved steps… and daylight, in front of the Great Moai.
textes.Un long couloir, une ornière bien droite: A long corridor, a perfectly straight rut down the middle… and, at the end, a lever. On the ceiling, a big round hole. Hmm.
textes.Un long escalier en colimaçon… et te voi: A long spiral staircase… and there you are at the top of the Temple of Kukulkan, dazzled by the sun.
textes.Un long frottement pour toi, {surnom}. Ç: A long scrape for you, {surnom}. It means: see you soon.
One long scrape… That's the gentlest one. I tap it every night on my bedroom wall. I don't know if it reaches all the way up. But I tap it anyway.
textes.Un long « ouuuuuh » monte de l'Agora : V: A long “woooooo” rises from the Agora: Vibrato has just switched on his theremin. The auroras are coming.
textes.Un lundi, il est arrivé avec ses cent qu: One Monday, he turned up with his hundred and forty coins in an old sock, and put them on my desk, just to see. I counted them with him. Then I told him he was halfway there. He smiled like a child. That day, I nearly lowered the price. My grandmother would have scolded me. Or kissed me. I don't know.
textes.Un lundi, il ne lui restait de l'huile q: One Monday, he only had enough oil left for one horn. I went to the evening gala with one shiny horn and one dull one. When questioned, I replied: “Asymmetry is in fashion.” The following week, three courtiers had just one horn polished. Monsieur Tiburce made a fortune.
textes.Un lundi, je n'avais assez d'huile que p: One Monday, I only had enough oil for one of Asmodin's horns. He went to the gala with one shiny horn and one dull horn. When people asked, he said: “It's asymmetric fashion.” The following week, three courtiers asked me to polish only one horn. I made a fortune. I owe him everything.
A light easterly breeze on this matter.
textes.Un léger vent d'est sur mon moral. La Li: A light easterly breeze on my spirits. The Line has reopened, everyone is coming up to see, and the Floor folk are queuing all the way to the Belvedere. I'm delighted. My benches less so.
textes.Un majordome mécanique t'accueille en cl: A mechanical butler greets you, blinking all over. He looks very proud of his tray.
textes.Un manteau de capitaine ! Il a fait le t: A captain's coat! It's been round the world!
textes.Un marchand de passage a voulu acheter u: A passing merchant wanted to buy one of my paintings, a boat at sunrise, hanging above the well. He offered a week's lodging. Zineb folded her arms: “Not for sale. It's mine.” He doubled it. She said no. That evening, she served me a tajine without charging me a thing. Grumbling, for form's sake.
textes.Un marchand vend des programmes douteux: A merchant is selling dubious programs in the Alleys. I have no proof. Glitch says she'll find some. I asked her to be careful. She answered “always”. She always says “always”.
textes.Un mardi, avant midi, j'ai repêché trois: One Tuesday, before noon, I fished out three of Yannick's customers: a gentleman who wanted to photograph a fish, a lady who'd lost her paddle, and a kid who wanted to see if a pedalo floats upside down. It does. Yannick was waiting for me on the jetty with three towels and a big grin. He didn't even know they'd gone out.
textes.Un mardi, j'ai changé une aile du moulin: One Tuesday, I changed one of the mill's sails. I didn't know that Gaspard the clockmaker set his watch by my sails. He was late for the only time in his life. He's never forgiven me. Well, a little. He greets me. Three seconds early. To show me he can.
textes.Un mardi, j'ai oublié le poème. Le mercr: One Tuesday, I forgot the poem. On Wednesday, I delivered a second sack, with two poems. She said: “More flour?” I thought my heart was going to fly away with the mill's sails.
textes.Un matin calme, la mer plate comme une a: One calm morning, the sea flat as a plate, Driss looked at the sky and turned back. I didn't understand: not a cloud. He pointed at the gulls, all heading back to the harbour. An hour later, the storm would have caught us out at sea. Since then, I watch the gulls too. Even from the galleon.
textes.Un matin d'hiver, j'ai allumé un feu dan: One winter morning, I lit a fire in my fireplace and the smoke came back out of the window. Rose's bougainvillea had grown into the chimney! There were pink flowers in my living room and buds in the soot. Rose told me: “I warned you, they don't listen to anyone.” I kept the branch. It flowers above my bed.
textes.Un matin de brouillard, il y avait un pi: One foggy morning, there was a piano on the quay. Upright, intact, with one key missing. Not a trace, not a sound in the night. Nobody knows where it came from. And six years ago, one night, I found a battered old sweeper robot at the foot of the cliff. It was still singing. Out of tune. An old shepherds' song. I don't know whose it is. It didn't tell me.
textes.Un matin de brouillard, je l'ai repêchée: One foggy morning, I fished her out three times with my net. She'd fallen off the jetty backing away from a frog, then backing away from a leaf, then backing away from me. The third time, I told her: “Sister, sit down and stop backing away.” She sat down. She stayed until noon. I fished better than usual.
textes.Un matin de corde à tresser, je dormais: One rope-braiding morning, I overslept. Gland woke me up by biting my tail. I jumped up to the ceiling! He laughed so much he fell out of bed. To make it up to him, I let him hold the end of the rope all morning. He held it without moving. Him! Without moving! A miracle.
textes.Un matin de grand vent, je me retourne p: One very windy morning, I turn round to greet the amin. One second. When I turn back, the gulls had taken the lot. A whole batch, thirty sardines, flown off over the Skala. First I shouted. Then I laughed. And I decided: one sardine in ten is for them. The gull tax. We've lived in peace ever since.
textes.Un matin de grande pêche, la flotte rent: One big-catch morning, the fleet comes in full, I climb onto the platform, I open my mouth… nothing. Not a sound. Mustapha saw my face, jumped up on the platform and shouted the prices for me, all wrong: raw sardines at the grilled price! The fishermen were dancing. I wanted to vanish. The worst day of my life. And the funniest, now that I've got my voice back.
textes.Un matin de mer plate, Bastien m'a emmen: One morning when the sea was flat, Bastien took me out to the golden point that sticks out of the water, to the south-west. I dove. Down below there were lights, rooftops, stairways. And then I got scared, hugely scared, and I came up far too fast. Bastien pulled me into his boat. I never went back.
textes.Un matin de mer plate, j'ai emmené Sofia: One flat-calm morning, I took Sofia out to the golden point, to the south-west. She dived. She came up too fast, white as a sheet, without a word. I hauled her into the boat and put my cap on her, for the sun. She saw the octopus on my sail and burst out laughing. I think that was the fear coming out.
textes.Un matin gris, Rúmil est rentré sans un: One grey morning, Rúmil came home without a single ray. That evening, my lanterns should have stayed dark. He went back out and fished the reflections from the fountain all day long, one by one, with a spoon. By evening I had enough to light half the path. It was the most beautiful half.
textes.Un matin gris, je suis rentré sans un ra: One grey morning, I came home without a single ray. I spent the day fishing the reflections from the fountain, with a spoon, one by one. That evening, Lirael was able to light half the path. She said it was the most beautiful half. She said it to cheer me up. But I believed her.
textes.Un matin très tôt, j'ai peint sur la por: Very early one morning, I painted a six-metre rat playing guitar on his office door. Lisse arrived. He stood in front of it for ten minutes without saying anything. Then he said: “The blue is… efficient.” And he went in. He didn't have the rat painted over until noon. For him, that's an eternity.
textes.Un matin, Anouk m'a trouvé endormi sous: One morning, Anouk found me asleep under the counter, all green. She didn't tell a soul. That very evening, there was a box of ginger tea on the shelf, with “For the boss” written on it. Ever since, she refills it every month, without me asking. My aunt thinks it's for the customers.
textes.Un matin, Ba Sidi racontait une grande t: One morning, Ba Sidi was telling of a great desert crossing: the lost sultan, the thirst, the dunes. I played slow. Very slow. One note per dune. By the end of the crossing, two listeners were asleep in the circle, heads on their neighbours' shoulders. Ba Sidi said: “Those two reached the oasis before us.”
textes.Un matin, Bobor m'a demandé comment amad: One morning, Bobor asked me how to win over Cerberus, the three-headed dog of the Nine Circles. I told him the old story: three honey cakes, one for each head, otherwise the heads squabble. Bobor took notes on a flour sack. The next day, he'd invented his “three-headed” honey cake recipe.
textes.Un matin, Brunna a vidé mon sac par terr: One morning, Brunna emptied my sack on the floor, shouting: “Wet!” I shouted: “Dry!” An hour of arguing, right in front of Borin. In the end, Borin threw a lump on the fire. Pfff. It was wet: damp ash had been falling all night. I never owned up. She knows.
textes.Un matin, Celebrë avait la voix cassée e: One morning, Celebrë had lost her voice and was crying with rage. I told her: “Sing with your feet.” She beat time on the floorboards, I danced, and the whole village stopped to watch. They still call it “the silent dance”. She claims it was her idea.
textes.Un matin, Croâ s'est posé sur ma lance a: One morning, Croâ landed on my spear with a bit of bark in his beak. Carved on it: “Smile.” Signed Hilda. I don't know how she taught a crow to carry mail just to tease me. I didn't smile. Not in front of the crow.
textes.Un matin, Fernand m'apporte une caisse d: One morning, Fernand brings me a crate of sea bream. One jumps, hop, over the edge, crosses the quay and heads straight into my kitchen, right under the stove! Fernand said: “See, they know where they're going.” I swear it's true. I'd recognise that sea bream by its eye. It was the best of the season.
textes.Un matin, Gertrude avait une main bleue: One morning, Gertrude had a blue hand on her. A painted handprint, tiny. Lulu said it was a hug, because Gertrude looked sad. I scrubbed for an hour. … And then I left it. Gertrude looks happy like that. I think.
textes.Un matin, Gloubi a agité ses quatre bras: One morning, Gloubi waved his four arms from across the fountain. I thought his café was on fire. I ran over with a bucket of water. He only wanted me to taste his new jelly. I put down the bucket, I tasted. It tickled. I said it was worth the run.
textes.Un matin, Gunnar a fait remarquer au roi: One morning, Gunnar pointed out to the king that his crown was on his head. As he straightened it, the king tapped the eighth ruby, the fake one, and looked me straight in the eye. He said nothing. Neither did I. I didn't sleep all week.
textes.Un matin, Hortense est entrée dans ma bo: One morning, Hortense came into my shop looking like a judge. “Rose, who buys lavender from you?” I answered that I sold it to everyone. Which is true, by the way. She narrowed her eyes: “Marcel, for instance?” I said: “Everyone, Hortense.” She left smiling. That's rare, a smile from Hortense.
textes.Un matin, Hurla criait les nouvelles par: One morning, Hurla was shouting the news over my music. I played louder. She shouted louder. An hour later, the whole square was there throwing coins at us. We earned more than in a month, and we shared. Since then, once a season, it's the Duel of the Square. I always win. Well, I think so.
textes.Un matin, Lilas a voulu essayer une piro: One morning Lilas wanted to try a pirouette in our kitchen. A doe's pirouette, in a tanuki's kitchen! Her tail swept the shelf: two jars of honey on the floor. She went “oh…” in a teeny voice. I worked it out: four coins' worth of honey. I made her pay in pirouettes. She still owes me three.
textes.Un matin, Lulu est revenue de chez ses f: One morning, Lulu came back from her fairies with golden pollen on her cheeks. I photographed her in a long exposure. In the photo, around her head, there are little lights that don't come from any glow stick. Bastien says it's a fault in the camera. My camera has no faults. Bastien does.
textes.Un matin, Madame Hurla criait les nouvel: One morning, Madame Hurla was shouting the news while I was playing. I played louder. She shouted louder. It went on for an hour. A crowd gathered, applauded, and threw us more coins than in a month. We shared them. Since then, once a season, we hold the Duel of the Square. I win. She says I don't.
textes.Un matin, Mégaphone a dit « un, deux » d: One morning, Mégaphone said “one, two” into the mic, and I answered “three” from the back of the meadow. She dropped her mug. She'd been waiting ten years for that.
textes.Un matin, Ondine s'est glissée dans la s: One morning, Ondine slipped into the throne room to ask me what colour the sun was. “Yellow.” “Yellow like what?” There's nothing yellow under the sea. In the end I put my crown on her head. She ran off to look at herself in the canal. Ever since, she calls my crown “the little sun”.
textes.Un matin, Pomme-de-Pin devait tresser un: One morning Pomme-de-Pin had to braid a rope for a bridge, and she was still asleep. So I woke her up. I bit her tail. Just a teeny bit! She jumped up to the ceiling. Afterwards she laughed, and she let me hold the end of the rope all morning. It was the best morning in the world.
textes.Un matin, Pépin est arrivé avec un sac d: One morning, Pépin turned up with a sack of flour on each shoulder. Running, of course. He put them down, went “Boom!”, and one of the sacks burst. He was white to the tips of his ears. He shouted: “Record broken!” Mochi thought he was a ghost. Then she bit his arm to check.
textes.Un matin, Thalion a touché une pomme à c: One morning Thalion hit an apple at a hundred paces, then turned round to see if anyone was watching. I shouted from my platform: “What luck!” Ever since, every time he hits something, he glances up at Fil-d'Aube. I say “luck” every time. It's been going on for eighty years.
textes.Un matin, Victor m'a tendu un coquillage: One morning, Victor handed me an “authentic” shell, “picked up at dawn”. I put my finger on it. My finger turned blue. He said: “That's the dew.” I kept the blue finger all day, on purpose, and showed it to every customer. He didn't offer me anything for a month.
textes.Un matin, après dix ans de « un, deux »,: One morning, after ten years of “one, two,” someone answered “three” from the back of the meadow. It was Jack. I dropped my mug of chocolate. I laughed for an hour. Then I made him do it again every morning.
textes.Un matin, après une grosse nuit de teuf,: One morning, after a big night of partying, I fell asleep with my head on the kneading trough. Margaux didn't wake me. She did the whole batch on her own and put a croissant next to my cheek. When I opened my eyes, all she said was: “Was the music good?”
textes.Un matin, au bout du quai, j'ai vu un da: One morning, at the end of the quay, I saw a dolphin. It jumped, splash, and went away again. Mum said “it was a big fish”, Bruno said “a big fish”, even the sergeant said “big fish”. But Lucas was there, and Lucas said “dolphin”. That makes two against three. But Lucas is big, so he counts double.
textes.Un matin, au bout du quai, on a vu un da: One morning, at the end of the quay, Nina and I saw a dolphin. It jumped twice. Nobody believes us. The others say “a big fish”. I say dolphin. I was there. Since then, Nina asks me every morning: “Did he come back?” I say: “Not yet.” We keep looking anyway.
textes.Un matin, au deuxième coup, j'ai ouvert: One morning, at the second knock, I opened the window and emptied a bucket of water. Next to him. On purpose, next to him. He looked up, said “Thanks, that's refreshing!” and ran off. So I hung up a sign: “People sleep here”. Since then, he knocks more softly. It's worse. You wait for it.
textes.Un matin, au large, il s'est mis à chant: One morning, out at sea, he started singing a very high, very long note. All at once, every gull around the Bahja dived at the same time. Every one! Hamid said: “See? They're diving on the fish. The singing works.” I say they were hiding. We brought in three hundred sardines. He was right, that's the worst part.
textes.Un matin, au-dessus du temple, il y avai: One morning, above the temple, there was… it. The Great Flying Spaghetti. It was floating, looking at us, and it blinked. Mamma Lasagna dropped her dough. Nonno Tortellini said: “It winked at me.” Me, I fell to my knees. My colander fell off. It laughed, I think. A noodle wiggled.
textes.Un matin, avant une course, je lui ai vo: One morning, before a race, I stole one of his carrots. The fourth one! He had four, even though he always says three! I took it so he wouldn't win too much, or he'll get bored. He counted: “One, two, three… Right. Three. Perfect.” He won. I ate the carrot. It wasn't nice. I prefer cakes.
textes.Un matin, elle a accroché un panneau à l: One morning, she hung a sign at the entrance to the terrace: “The fourth glass must be paid for.” That very afternoon, I hung mine right next to it: “Here, we give.” The caravan drivers read both, laugh, and order a fifth glass. She never took hers down. Neither did I.
textes.Un matin, elle a bricolé dans la salle d: One morning she tinkered in the engine room and the Petit Piston coughed. Once. A big, thick cough, like the old man in the morning before his coffee. I sat down on a coil of rope. Écrou said I'd gone all pale. I said it was the sardines from the night before. It wasn't the sardines.
textes.Un matin, elle a peint le troisième cano: One morning she painted the third cannon with a red flower in its mouth. A flower. In a cannon of the Skala. I said it was an insult to the guard. She smiled and carried on. I don't know what she did with the painting. I didn't ask. Not more than twice.
textes.Un matin, elle a pris une dorade vivante: One morning, she took a live sea bream from my stall and let it go in the fountain on the square. She called it Captain. I shouted fit to shake the Skala. Then I left it there for three days. On the fourth evening, I carried it to the sea in a bucket, at the end of the jetty. Yasmine thinks it left all by itself. Don't tell her.
textes.Un matin, elle a salué la Skala d'un cou: One morning, she saluted the Skala with a blank shot from Bertha, her favourite cannon. A blank shot, in front of my bastion! I sounded the alarm. Six armed guards on the battlements, and her, on deck, curtsying. My ears are still ringing. She calls it “a gunner's courtesy”.
textes.Un matin, elle a tapé deux coups, puis u: One morning, she knocked twice, then once, then twice more. I didn't understand. Ysaé explained later: “Hello, thank you, and hello to Ysaé.” I answered three times. We both started laughing, each on her own side of the rock.
textes.Un matin, elle est arrivée presque press: One morning she arrived almost in a hurry, for a tracker: “Cat tracks, fresh, three times round the jetty.” She'd measured them, drawn them. They were mine. I'd come back the evening before, on the sly, to check a ripple on the water. She sighed. I said: “Shh. I was checking.”
textes.Un matin, elle est montée sur la proue d: One morning, she climbed onto the Zahra's prow, at the quay, and gave orders to the whole fleet: “Cast off! Head south! Faster over there!” Two fishermen pretended to obey and rowed in circles in front of her. She congratulated them and made them quartermasters. They're very proud of it.
textes.Un matin, elle est venue avec un ruban e: One morning, she came with a tape and measured all my carpets. Every one was a finger shorter than what I announce. A finger! I explained that wool rests at night and shrinks from tiredness. She measured again the next morning. Still a finger. The wool is very tired these days.
textes.Un matin, elle est venue frapper sur ma: One morning, she came knocking on my upturned boat at five. She said: “Teach me to steer. And not a word to my father.” Since then, twice a week, we sail out into the bay before daybreak. The first morning, she cried when the sail filled. She said it was the wind. It wasn't the wind.
textes.Un matin, elle est venue à mon étal, les: One morning, she came to my stall, hands on her hips: “Your honey's too cheap, it's bringing all the prices down!” I asked her which prices. She thought about it. “Mine.” She doesn't sell honey. She sells cacao. I gave her a pot of honey to calm her down. She took it. On principle.
