textes.Un matin, elle m'a demandé ce que je lis: One morning, she asked me what I was reading. I answered. For a whole hour, I believe: the great crystal, the air, the light, the queen with hair of sea foam. When I looked up, the terrace was empty and Gisèle was stacking the chairs around me. She closed late. She still brings it up.
textes.Un matin, elle monte au Guet. Elle dit :: One morning, she climbs the Lookout. She says: “It's coming. A bumblebee as big as the Mother Oak. It smells of hot oil.” I look. Nothing. An hour later, the Zéphyr comes out of the clouds. As big as the Mother Oak. It smelled of hot oil. She'd smelled it before I saw it. Good nose. Very good nose.
textes.Un matin, elle s'est enrhumée et n'a pas: One morning, she caught a cold and couldn't shout. The silence was so strange that the whole palace woke up late, myself included. For the first time in three centuries. I had a honey tea sent to her. Anonymously. The next day, she shouted “THANK YOU!” under my windows.
textes.Un matin, en descendant du sanctuaire, j: One morning, coming down from the shrine, I found him halfway up the stairs, with his dog, climbing. I couldn't go down any faster: I never look down. So I sat on a step and told him about Nanahuatzin. He came back down to hear better. I came down behind him. Slowly.
textes.Un matin, en ouvrant les volets, j'ai tr: One morning, opening the shutters, I found the cage empty. No more parrot, just a blue feather on the perch. I kept the name, of course: you don't change a sign that cost that much fizz. I carved a wooden parrot and put it above the counter. I tell everyone it flew away. The other one doesn't talk, but it listens very well.
textes.Un matin, en pleine course jusqu'à la pa: One morning, right in the middle of the race to the channel, I shouted: “Whale, there!” Ahmed turned around to look, and he lost. He says it was a barrel. A barrel! I saw it dive. Barrels don't dive. Since then, he says I cheat. But he turns around every time.
textes.Un matin, en remontant le filet, elle a: One morning, hauling in the net, she cried. Without a sound. The tears fell into the net, with the sardines. I didn't look. I took out my handkerchief. I held it out. She took it. We finished the net. We never talked about it. She kept the handkerchief. It's good.
textes.Un matin, en remontant le filet, j'ai pe: One morning, hauling in the net, I thought of my father and started to cry. Silently, still pulling. Driss said nothing. He took a handkerchief from his pocket and held it out without looking at me, eyes on the sea. Then we went on pulling. I washed it and gave it back the next day. He said: “Hm.” It was perfect.
textes.Un matin, en revenant du port avec mes r: One morning, coming back from the port with my fish scraps, I found Gorgoth sitting in the middle of the kennel, covered in sleeping pups: on his shoulders, on his knees, in his beard. He didn't dare move. He whispered to me: “They're sleeping.” He stayed like that until noon and missed a fight. Madame Hurla shouted. He was smiling.
textes.Un matin, en époussetant la dent de drag: One morning, dusting the sea dragon's tooth under its glass dome, I told the Lord it came from a dragon that had swallowed a lighthouse and kept the hiccups from it, with sparks. He wrote it all down in his catalogue, with my name underneath. Since then, every morning, he shows me an object and asks: “And this one, Pauline?”
textes.Un matin, il a crié : « Balam ! Des trac: One morning, he shouted: “Balam! Jaguar tracks!” I came. Round, four toes, no claws. I told him to look behind him. Peek' was sitting there, one paw in the air. Kinich said: “So it's a dog jaguar.” He followed the tracks anyway. They led to a bone.
textes.Un matin, il a dit : « Vos chouquettes s: One morning, he said: “Your choux buns are too sweet.” The next day, I made them less sweet. He said: “Not sweet enough.” The day after, I changed nothing. He said: “There.”
textes.Un matin, il a glissé une vieille babouc: One morning, he slipped an old babouche under my hammer. Tac. Flat as a pancake. He laughed for three days. So I made him a tray shaped like a babouche, pointy at the front, chased and engraved, and I told him: “For your feet.” He still doesn't know if it was a joke. Neither do I. He puts his babouches on it now.
textes.Un matin, il a jeté une noisette dans la: One morning he threw a hazelnut into the big pond. “To bait the dragon!” Plop. The fish left, the float danced, the morning was ruined. He asked: “Did it eat it?” I said yes. The next day he threw three. I said the dragon wasn't hungry any more. He asked me if it was on a diet.
textes.Un matin, il a oublié le pain. Le lendem: One morning, he forgot the bread. The next day, Hortense was waiting for him on his boat. She pinched his ear. He's never forgotten since.
textes.Un matin, il a sorti de sa poche de tabl: One morning, he took a black piece of bark out of his apron pocket and held it out to me: “Smell.” I smelled. I didn't know it. Me! Forty spices on the stall, and a smell I didn't know. He wouldn't tell me the name. I searched for three nights. He's cleverer than he looks. Which isn't hard.
textes.Un matin, il est monté m'offrir une bout: One morning, he came up to offer me a bottle of Mama Lou's rum, “between guardians of the sea”. I took the bottle, uncorked it, and poured it into the sea over the battlements, down to the last drop. He watched. He said: “The fish are going to be in a good mood.” He went back down. He still greets me.
textes.Un matin, il est venu ramasser les miett: One morning, he came to sweep up the crumbs behind the Residences. I told him: “That's not rubbish, those are reserves.” Since then, he waters them. The sparrows don't know what to make of it.
textes.Un matin, il est venu sur la grève avec: One morning, he came down to the shore with a rolled-up decree, a red ribbon and a wax seal: “The Merciless is requisitioned in the name of the city.” I thanked him. I took the decree, folded it in four and slipped it under a plank on the side that was a bit loose. It's not loose any more. It's the most useful decree he's ever signed.
textes.Un matin, il m'a demandé trois fois où j: One morning, he asked me three times where I was going. Three times I said “nowhere”. The third time, he followed me. I went to the end of the jetty to look at the mist, like every morning. He stood behind me for an hour, without a sound. Then he left. I think he was looking at the mist too.
textes.Un matin, il m'a donné le prix : deux pi: One morning, he gave me the price: two coins. Two! It doesn't rhyme with anything. So I shouted: “Two and a half, the sardine's a laugh!” The whole auction paid two and a half, singing. Moulay Brahim climbed onto the platform, looked at me, and handed the half back to every buyer, one by one. It took all morning.
textes.Un matin, il m'a monté un mérou plus lou: One morning, he brought me up a grouper heavier than Clou. I paid without haggling. A first. Apparently he still tells the story at parties. Let him enjoy it: it won't happen again.
textes.Un matin, il n'est pas venu. Huit heures: One morning, he didn't come. Eight o'clock, nothing. Quarter past eight, nothing. I couldn't sleep any more. I got up, opened the door, waited on the doorstep in my nightshirt. He turned up at nine, walking. He said he'd had a pebble in his shoe. I went back in without a word. I slept badly anyway.
textes.Un matin, il n'y avait pas de croissant: One morning, there was no croissant on my sack. I thought she was cross. I spent the day wondering what I'd done. In the evening I picked a little flower at the edge of Gaubert's field and put it on the next day's sack. I didn't sleep all night. In the morning there were two croissants. I still don't know what it means.
textes.Un matin, il répétait son grand air sur: One morning, he was rehearsing his big aria on his balcony, above the port. A high note, very high, very long. Every seagull in the port took off at once. Every one. The fishermen thought a storm was coming. He took a bow. I was playing down below, on the jetty. I played louder, out of solidarity with the seagulls.
textes.Un matin, il s'est accoudé au comptoir e: One morning, he leaned on the desk and studied me at length through a magnifying glass. Then: “My dear Edmond, I'll buy your moustache. For my collection, next to the admiral's.” I replied that it was not for sale, and that I very much doubted the admiral had been consulted. He laughed. He hasn't given up.
textes.Un matin, il y avait un rat de six mètre: One morning, there was a six-metre rat playing guitar painted on my office door. I stood in front of it for ten minutes. She was hiding behind a container, I knew it. I said: “The blue is… effective.” I went in. I waited until noon to have it repainted. I don't know why I waited.
textes.Un matin, j'ai accroché un panneau à l'e: One morning, I hung a sign at the entrance to the terrace: “The fourth glass must be paid for.” That very afternoon, Hassan hung his own, right next to it: “Here, we give.” The caravan traders read both, they laugh, and they have a fifth glass. Which nobody pays for. I'm not taking mine down. Neither is he.
textes.Un matin, j'ai allumé ma scie et elle s': One morning, I switched on my saw and it started blinking. Fusible had wired fairy lights to it during the night. He said it was “festive”. I said it was “worrying”. We kept the lights. I saw to music now. Well, to lights.
textes.Un matin, j'ai annoncé la météo : « Gris: One morning, I read the weather: “Grey, like Mr Lisse.” Ten minutes later, the radio phone rang. It was him, furious: “I'm not grey, I'm… understated!” I put him on air live. The whole island laughed. Even him, a little, at the end. I heard it.
textes.Un matin, j'ai compté mes barriques dans: One morning, I counted my barrels in the hold: forty-one. I'd bought forty. The forty-first was snoring. Tonneau had fallen asleep inside, his head sticking out of the bunghole. I nearly sold it to Isaac Cinq-Doigts, who was offering me a good price. The Silent One looked at me. I kept it.
textes.Un matin, j'ai dit non. Il est sorti qua: One morning, I said no. He went out anyway. He came back without a sail, rowing, red with shame. I threw him a rope. I said nothing. The next day, he came to see me before dawn: “Going out, Driss?” Since then, he always asks. I always answer. In one word. No more is needed.
textes.Un matin, j'ai dit à Hortense que l'horl: One morning, I told Hortense the clock would ring again thanks to a stranger. She answered “Nonsense” and shut her door in my face. Ten seconds later, she opened it again, just a crack, to ask: “What sort of stranger?” Then she shut it before I could answer.
textes.Un matin, j'ai décidé de le rattraper po: One morning, I decided to catch up with him to serve him notice of the sign. I ran. With the kepi, the belt and the notebook. After twenty metres, I was red as a lobster, and Bernard was at the lighthouse. He waited for me there, doing stretches. I didn't fine him. I needed my breath.
textes.Un matin, j'ai décidé de trouver la rece: One morning, I decided to find the recipe myself. I rummaged through the Academy's bins, behind her tank, in my pilot's gloves. I found cores. Dozens of cabbage cores. Héloïse caught me on all fours. She just said: “Good morning, commander.” I stood up and said: “I knew it.” I didn't know anything at all.
textes.Un matin, j'ai découvert que Zénith avai: One morning, I discovered that Zénith had drawn constellations on my maps during the night: a Great Bear on Balafre, a Little Sock on Port-Azur. I was furious. The next day, I drew a constellation myself, on Ember Island: “the Great Coughing Volcano”. Zénith added it to his catalogue.
textes.Un matin, j'ai entendu à la radio : « Mé: One morning, I heard on the radio: “Weather: grey, like Mr Lisse.” I phoned to complain. He put me on air live, without warning. The whole island heard me say: “I am not grey, I am sober!” Miss Prune coughed very loudly next to me. I believe she was laughing.
textes.Un matin, j'ai envoyé Croâ lui porter un: One morning, I sent Croâ to take him a bit of bark. I'd carved on it: “Smile.” Croâ came back with the bark cut neatly in two. On the half he gave back, Bramm had carved: “No.” I still have it. It's the only letter he's ever written me.
textes.Un matin, j'ai fait toute ma ronde avec: One morning, I did my whole round with a smile painted on my helmet. Ortie had drawn it during the night. All the guards saluted me with a smile, the merchants too, even Kraxx. I found the city very friendly that day. It was my Archduchess who showed me my reflection in a shop window.
textes.Un matin, j'ai glissé dans sa pile de si: One morning, I slipped a promise to eat less pie into his pile of signatures. He signed it without reading it, between a hunting permit and an order form for ropes. I filed it under “Commitments”. That very evening, he ate three slices. I said nothing. I just put the paper next to his plate.
textes.Un matin, j'ai marqué dans l'anneau, tou: One morning, I scored through the ring, all alone, with nobody against me. I shouted for joy, very loudly. That evening I learned that Balam had been following a deer just behind the wall since dawn. The deer left. Balam ate beans. He didn't say anything to me. He just looked at me. For a long time. I paid for his beans.
textes.Un matin, j'ai mis mon casque toute seul: One morning, I put my helmet on all by myself, before I got there. He looked at me for a long time. Then he said: “Good.” He looked almost disappointed. The next day, I forgot it on purpose.
textes.Un matin, j'ai porté moi-même le pain à: One morning, I took the bread to the North Gate myself. Gilles was asleep standing up. I held the bread under his nose. He sniffed, without opening his eyes, and smiled. Then he said, still asleep: “Thank you, Honorine.” He'd recognised me by the smell. Since then, I call him “my sleeping customer”. He's my most loyal customer.
textes.Un matin, j'ai posé une brochette sur so: One morning, I put a skewer on his bench. One of Caramel's. Still warm. No note. … He looked at it all day. He didn't eat it. He thought it was a trap. … By evening, it was cold. I ate it. Cold. … It doesn't matter.
textes.Un matin, j'ai pris mon ruban et j'ai me: One morning, I took my tape and measured all his carpets. Every one a finger shorter than he claims. He swore to me that wool shrinks at night, from tiredness. Since then, I measure every morning. Rachid's wool is always very tired. Me, I sell my fabrics with an extra finger. To make up for the family.
textes.Un matin, j'ai pêché un mérou plus lourd: One morning I caught a grouper heavier than Clou. I hauled it up to the cheese shop with a rope. Octave looked at it, weighed it in his hands, and paid without haggling. Without haggling! I told the whole party about it, twice. Mistral made a track out of it, “Octave's Grouper”. Octave has never listened to it. He hears it anyway, from up there.
textes.Un matin, j'ai recompté derrière elle. T: One morning, I recounted after her. Stalk by stalk. Two hours. There was one too many. I kept it in my pocket all week to show her. She said: “It's a little one, it counts as half.” Hmm. I replanted it. Seaweed doesn't haggle.
textes.Un matin, j'ai regardé un hareng très fo: One morning, I stared really hard at a herring, and it flew away! It went round the harbour three times, with all the seagulls behind it. People were shouting “A flying fish!”. Mama dropped her basket. That evening, my parents wrote a letter to the archmage. Nobody ever caught the herring. It must still be circling over the harbour.
textes.Un matin, j'ai reçu une réclamation offi: One morning, I received an official complaint from the sweepers, typewritten, signed “BEEP”. Master Rivet swears he had nothing to do with it. But the paper smelled of oil from the Factory, and there was an iron thumbprint in the bottom right corner. I replied with a letter stuffed with confetti. Apparently it jammed a machine.
textes.Un matin, j'ai réussi : le Petit Piston: One morning, I did it: the Little Piston coughed. Once, twice, a big black cloud. I shouted for joy and turned round to Gonzague. He was very pale, leaning on his crane, as if he'd seen a ghost. He said: “Let it sleep, lass.” And he went off fishing. At ten in the morning. He never fishes before the evening.
textes.Un matin, j'ai senti une odeur de pain c: One morning, I smelled warm bread in a dream. I said thank you to Honorine, in my dream. When I opened my eyes, she was there in front of me, with the bread. She was laughing. I didn't know if I was still dreaming. I asked her. She pinched my arm. I wasn't dreaming. Neither was the bread. It was very good.
textes.Un matin, j'ai sonné le sistre pendant l: One morning, I shook the sistrum during the hymn. Loud. Really loud. All the ibises on the river flew off at once, frrrrt! I thought Néferet was going to scold me. She told me Rê likes people to be happy to see him. Since then, I'm always happy. The ibises got used to it. Almost.
textes.Un matin, j'ai surpris la commandante da: One morning I caught the commander in the Academy courtyard, on all fours behind my tank, her head in my bins. She was looking for the gas recipe. All she found was apple cores. A great many apple cores. I said: “Good morning, commander.” She stood up very dignified and said: “I knew it.” She knows nothing at all.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé dans la vase des t: One morning, I found fresh cat tracks in the mud, circling the jetty three times and stopping right at the edge. I thought I was onto something. I followed them, measured them, drew them. They were his, from the night before. He'd come back in secret. He said: “Shh. I was checking.”
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé devant ma porte un: One morning I found one of my lanterns outside my door, black with smoke, with a note: “Bertha coughed. Sorry. R.” I cleaned it for three days, hole by hole, with a feather. In the evening I put it back on the square. By the next festival it had vanished. It went back to sea, clean as a new pin.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé mon dépôt tout rep: One morning, I found my depot repainted from top to bottom. Stars, rails, musical notes, and Bernadette in sunglasses. The Fronde, during the night. I shouted for form's sake. Then I looked at Bernadette. She looked so pleased, in her sunglasses. I bought myself the same pair. We wear them on Sundays.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé mon laboratoire im: One morning, I found my laboratory spotless. Murmure had filed all my notes in alphabetical order, during the night. Since all my equations begin with “So”, they were all under S. It took me three weeks to find the coffee formula. It was between “So, therefore” and “So, perhaps”.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé trois voyageurs da: One morning, I found three travellers in the north tower, with a plan and tape measures. Mr Prosper had sold them “a tower full of character, unbeatable view, absolute peace”. I brought them down, offered them tea, and showed Mr Prosper to the castle gate. Very calmly. Absolutely calmly. He still shivers when he talks about it.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé un hameçon dans mo: One morning, I found a fishhook in my hammock. Brand new, nicely curved, nicely sharp, made from an old nail. On the Murène, nobody can fish, so it's not a pirate. I say it's the ginger cat, saying sorry. Or one of Ba Sidi's djinns. I showed it to the first mate. He went “Hm”. He doesn't believe in djinns.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé un panneau sur la: One morning, I found a sign on the lighthouse door: “People sleep here.” Hand-painted, in enormous letters. I knocked anyway, twice, but ever so gently, with my fingertips. Tap… tap. I've knocked like that ever since. He says it's worse. I'll never understand that man.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé un pédalo jaune am: One morning, I found a yellow pedalo tied to my bollard. Mine, in front of the harbour office. Yannick spent twenty minutes explaining that this pedalo had a name, a history and a personality. All I took in was the knot. It was wrong.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé un recueil rapport: One morning, I found a collection returned on the windowsill, with an ash flower and the words “Thank you” in the ledger. That evening, I left a lit candle near the window. The next day, the ledger said: “Thank you for the candle.” Since then, the candle burns every night. And the thank-yous pile up.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé une brochette sur: One morning I found a skewer on my bench at the foot of the Lookout. No note, nothing. One of Caramel's skewers, still warm. And across the bridge, Éclair, watching me. I thought it was a trap! I kept an eye on it all day without touching it. In the evening it was cold, and Éclair looked disappointed. Why disappointed?
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé une chèvre sur mon: One morning, I found a goat on my throne. She was chewing my red velvet cushion and looking at me as if I were the intruder. I thought: there's a beast with a feel for power. I sent for her shepherdess and put her in charge of my ravens. I've never regretted it. The cushion, I do.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé une jolie pierre r: One morning, I found a pretty red stone on my anvil. I took it for ore and put it in the fire. It shattered. Kalda came by right after. She looked at the empty anvil, she looked at the fire, and she left without a word. Hilda says I'm a donkey. I still don't know why.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé une noisette sur l: One morning, I found a hazelnut on the steps of my throne. Zéphyr swore he hadn't done it on purpose. The shell cracked, and a teeny tiny fairy poked her head out to ask: “Are there any seeds around here?” That was her first word. It was not her last.
textes.Un matin, j'ai trouvé une vieille botte: One morning, I found an old boot sitting in front of the Museum door. Nobody had seen it arrive. It had fallen from the sky! I cried with joy. Solenne was passing by, she smiled and said: “What a miracle.” She had sand on her hands. It must have been miracle sand.
textes.Un matin, j'ai vidé son sac par terre en: One morning, I emptied his sack on the floor, shouting: “Wet!” He shouted: “Dry!” An hour of arguing, right in front of Borin. In the end, Borin threw a lump on the fire. Pfff. Wet. Dwalin never owned up. But the next day, his coal was dry, and he brought me a slice of Dagna's cake.
textes.Un matin, j'ai voulu dire à Nébula, par: One morning, I wanted to tell Nébula, in signs, from across the fountain: “Come and taste my new jelly.” With my four arms. She understood: “Your Bazaar's on fire, run and get water.” She arrived with a bucket. She tasted the jelly anyway. She said it was worth the bucket.
textes.Un matin, j'ai voulu lui faire une surpr: One morning I wanted to surprise her: I tried to make bread for her in the temple's little kitchen. I fell asleep while the dough was rising. It overflowed, ran across the table and covered the cat. Honorine arrived, saw everything, and laughed until she cried. Then she made bread with it. The cat kept a little.
textes.Un matin, j'ai voulu voir les deux maiso: One morning, I wanted to see the two houses at the top of the Great Temple, the blue one and the red one. I started climbing with Tlaco. Halfway up, the high priest Cuauhtli was coming down. He didn't scold me. He sat down on a step and told me the story of Nanahuatzin. I went back down to listen better. I still haven't seen the houses.
textes.Un matin, j'ai vu dans un coin du tapis: One morning, in a corner of the rug, I saw a little ginger spot. I leaned in. A cat. A GINGER CAT! Woven, whiskers and all! I screamed so loud that Rachid, next door, dropped three rugs. Samira said: “It was to see if you were looking.” I was looking. She unpicked it. I think she kept a bit of it.
textes.Un matin, j'avais dit à Fatima, tout bas: One morning, I'd whispered to Fatima: “Driss talks to his boat, and on top of that he snores.” Gaspard's parrot was on a barrel. An hour later, right in the middle of the fish auction, it screeched: “DRISS TALKS TO HIS BOAT! DRISS SNORES!” The whole auction laughed. Saïd stopped calling out. I wanted to crawl under the nets.
textes.Un matin, j'avais fixé la sardine à deux: One morning, I'd set sardines at two coins. Saïd climbed onto the platform and shouted: “Two and a half coins, the sardine that sings!” Because it rhymed better. By the time I crossed the fish market, he'd sold ten crates. I had every half-coin refunded. He shouted out the refunds. Singing.
textes.Un matin, j'avais la voix cassée. Rúmil: One morning I'd lost my voice. Rúmil cast his nets anyway. Nothing. Not one ray. He waited an hour, then looked at me: “Whistle, then.” I whistled. Three rays came. Ever since, he claims the light prefers whistling. He's lying, and he knows it.
textes.Un matin, j'avais le dos bloqué comme un: One morning, my back was stuck like an old door. Youssef took the helm and brought us back through the channel without touching a stone. I sang the whole way home, so nobody would see I was proud. You could hear it anyway.
textes.Un matin, j'avais une nouvelle figure da: One morning I had a new figure in my head, and I tried it in the kitchen. Oh… I spun, my tail swept the shelf, and two jars of honey broke. Grelot came in, looked at the honey on the floor and said: “That pirouette's four coins.” Then she helped me clean up, laughing.
textes.Un matin, j'entends gratter sous la viei: One morning I hear scratching under the old root. A fairy. From the sky. With a shovel. She'd dug a hole as big as… as her. She said: “Just one seed!” I chased her with my broom all the way to the garden. She was laughing. She had the seed. Hmph.
textes.Un matin, j'ouvre une caisse de sardines: One morning, I open a crate of sardines for the stall: hazelnuts. Everywhere, between the fish. Gland had put them there “to keep cool”. I yelled so loud Dad dropped his rod. Myrtille laughed so hard she fell off the bench. The worst part: the sardines had a little hazelnut taste. I sold them for more.
textes.Un matin, j'étais malade et je ne suis p: One morning, I was ill and didn't go to the garden. Around noon, someone knocked at my door. It was Nox, eyes all red with sleep, with an ash mint tea he'd made himself. It was too strong and not sweet enough. I drank it to the last drop. I've never had a better one.
textes.Un matin, je criais les nouvelles pendan: One morning, I was shouting the news while Calcine was playing. She played louder. I shouted louder. She played even louder. It went on for an hour. A crowd gathered, applauded, and threw us more coins than in a month. We shared. Since then, we hold the Duel of the Square once a season.
textes.Un matin, je l'ai croisé sur le quai. Je: One morning I ran into him on the quay. I shouted at him in front of everyone: the net, the three weeks, the bill, the interest. He took a step back. A step! Mâchefer! The fishermen couldn't believe it: nobody had ever seen him back down. He still hasn't paid. But he backed down.
textes.Un matin, je l'ai trouvé endormi contre: One morning, I found him asleep against the stela, his cheek on the stone. When he woke up, he had the date of creation printed on his face: four dots and the face of the Lord. I didn't say anything. He taught the young ones all morning like that. They remembered the date very well that day.
One morning, I brought her a bouquet. Not roses: you can't find them on the quay. Parsley and coriander, tied with a bit of galley string. She looked at the bouquet, then at me, then at the bouquet. She put it in a pot, on the stall. In the evening, she sold it. But it stayed there all day. Ho ho.
textes.Un matin, je lui ai confié le sistre pen: One morning, I let her hold the sistrum during the hymn. She shook it so heartily that all the ibises on the river took off at once, in a great clatter of white wings. She froze, mortified. I told her Rê loves enthusiasm. It's true. The ibises, a little less.
textes.Un matin, je lui ai demandé de ne plus b: One morning, I asked him to stay still, “for the light on the third cannon”. He froze, hand on his sabre, eyes on the sea. An hour, without moving. He thought I was painting the cannon. I painted the cannon, yes. With a red flower in its mouth. And next to it, a little, someone.
textes.Un matin, je lui ai demandé l'air qu'on: One morning, I asked her for the tune they used to dance to in the square when she was twenty. She hesitated, then hummed it, very softly, eyes closed. I played it. At the second verse, she stood up and walked off, very upright, without a word. I didn't finish the tune. I've never played it in front of her again.
textes.Un matin, je lui ai demandé trois fois o: One morning I asked him three times where he was going. Three times he said “nowhere”. The third time, I followed him. He did indeed go nowhere: to the end of the jetty, to look at the mist, for a whole hour. I went back. We've never spoken of it since.
textes.Un matin, je me retourne : plus de Fanny: One morning, I turn round: no Fanny. She was standing against the warm oven, arms crossed, eyes shut, hair full of sand. Asleep on her feet, like a horse. I let her be for ten minutes. When she woke up, she said: “I dreamed I was making croissants.” She had flour up to her eyebrows.
textes.Un matin, je me suis cachée derrière une: One morning, I hid behind a flower to listen to Perlée talking to her drops. She was telling them the weather forecast! “You'll get sunshine. You, a little wind. Sorry, that's Zéphyr.” I couldn't help laughing. She pretended not to hear me.
One morning, I didn't hear her laugh. I brought the whole crew back up. She had a sore throat. She went “ho” at me, very softly. We went back down. The miners didn't complain. They know.
textes.Un matin, je portais une caisse de citro: One morning I was carrying a crate of lemons along the edge of the quay. Odette shouted “Lucas!” behind me. I jumped, I dropped the crate. A hundred lemons in the harbour. She didn't scold me. She took a landing net, I took another, and we fished them out together for an hour. Without talking. Three are missing. The seagulls, I think.
textes.Un matin, je racontais la traversée du d: One morning, I was telling of the lost sultan crossing the desert. Lhoucine played slow. One note per dune. Very slow. By the end, two listeners were asleep, heads on their neighbour's shoulder. I said: “Those two reached the oasis before us.” The circle laughed, and the sleepers woke up asking for water.
textes.Un matin, je suis parti faire un petit t: One morning I went out for a little stroll. I followed a golden heron, then a stream, then the edge of the mist. When I got back, the whole village was in tears: nine days had gone by. Orophin had searched the entire island. I thought I'd been gone a morning. I brought Nimiel back a feather.
textes.Un matin, je suis partie avec une fausse: One morning, I left wearing a fake beard and a fisherman's hat, thinking I was very discreet. From her bench, the Elder watched me go by and gave me a little wave. I waved back. We both pretended. It was very well done.
textes.Un matin, je suis tombée dans la fontain: One morning, I fell into the fountain on the Great Square trying to bless the water. Noisette was there, of course. She jumped in with me, fully dressed, saying: “I want to be blessed too!” Honorine scolded us both. Then she gave us warm croissants. We dried off in the sun, on the bench, laughing.
textes.Un matin, je suivais un cerf depuis l'au: One morning, I'd been following a deer since dawn. Very close. Chak ran past, shouting that he'd scored through the ring. The deer left. Chak had nobody against him that morning. He'd scored all alone. He shouted anyway. I said nothing. I ate beans.
textes.Un matin, la presse a raté une lettre da: One morning, the press dropped a letter in the headline: “Achille Plumevent still in fligh”. The readers loved it. So did I, I confess. Not Adèle. She came to the newsroom, the Gazette rolled up in her hand, and said: “He's not in fligh. He's in flight. My brother is not a typo.” She was right.
textes.Un matin, la presse de Rosette a mangé u: One morning, Rosette's press ate a letter from my name. The whole city read: “Professor oum prepares a new experiment”. I found it very elegant. More discreet. For a week, I signed my letters “Oum”. The shepherds never worked out who was writing to them.
textes.Un matin, la presse de Rosette a raté un: One morning, Rosette's press missed a letter. The whole city read: “Achille still in fligh”. People were laughing in the square, hunting for the “t” everywhere. I bought every copy that was left and put them away in the shop. Not to hide them. Well, a bit to hide them.
textes.Un matin, le Baron a promis à un marchan: One morning, the Baron promised a hat merchant the Great Square in exchange for a peacock-feather hat. I found the contract at noon, signed, stamped, with a little drawing of a hat. I tore up the contract in front of the merchant. I kept the hat. The Baron noticed nothing. He wears the hat on Tuesdays.
textes.Un matin, le billet disait seulement : «: One morning, the note just said: “He waved at me in the eyepiece.” Achille had seen the big telescope glinting and flown right up in front of it. Céleste jumped so hard she knocked over her bottle of coffee. And I laughed for the first time since the morning of my thirtieth birthday.
textes.Un matin, le ciel était clair, la mer pl: One morning, the sky was clear, the sea flat. Driss looked at the seagulls and said: “No.” He stayed at the quay. I went out with ten boats. At noon, the wind caught us. I came home without a sail, rowing, with shame on top of it. Driss was waiting for me on the quay. He said nothing. He threw me a rope. Since then, I ask him.
textes.Un matin, le pain n'est pas arrivé : Hon: One morning, the bread didn't come: Honorine had a fever. The Baron thought it was the end of the world. He put on his mourning hat and announced a day of contemplation. I ran to the bakery. Noisette was minding the counter, in an apron down to her feet. She sold me three loaves and a burnt croissant. The Baron took off his mourning hat.
textes.Un matin, les mouettes attaquaient le gr: One morning, the gulls were attacking Mustapha's grill. A real army! So I grabbed a stick and my captain's hat, and I defended the grill all morning shouting “Board her!”. They all left. Mustapha gave me six seabirds for free. He says that day, the gull tax was zero.
textes.Un matin, les mouettes s'acharnaient sur: One morning, the gulls were mobbing my grill. Yasmine turned up with a stick and her captain's hat. She planted herself in front of the grill and defended my sardines all morning, shouting “Board them!” at the gulls. That day, the gull tax dropped to zero. I grilled her sea birds for free.
textes.Un matin, ma barque avait disparu. Momo: One morning, my boat had vanished. Momo had taken it to go and find his dolphin. He came back at noon, swimming, pushing the boat in front of him: he'd lost both oars. No dolphin. He made me a shell necklace to say sorry. I wear it. Don't you dare tell him.
textes.Un matin, maman a ouvert une caisse de s: One morning, Mum opened a crate of sardines, and there were hazelnuts all through it! She screamed so loud that Grandpa dropped his rod. It was Gland, he'd put them there “to keep cool”. I laughed so much I fell off the bench. Mum said the sardines smelled of hazelnut. She sold them anyway.
textes.Un matin, mon oncle s'est bloqué le dos: One morning, my uncle put his back out hauling in the net. Bent double like a fishhook. He told me: “The helm, mule-head.” I brought the Bahja back all by myself, through the channel, between the two lighthouses, without touching a single rock. And Hamid sang. The whole way back, at the top of his voice. He says it was for his back. I know it was for me.
textes.Un matin, mon pétrin a fait « croa ». J': One morning my dough trough went “croak”. I plunged my hands into the dough and pulled out a frog covered in flour, looking very pleased with itself. Nimiel was at the window. She said: “He was cold.” The dough, I threw away. The frog, I gave back. And I didn't tell Miriel. That time.
textes.Un matin, on a vu le même jet d'eau deva: One morning, we saw the same spout off the Skala, him from his crow's nest, me from the Bahja. That evening, he showed me his slate: a whale drawn in chalk, with the spray and everything. I copied it onto the Bahja's prow. Hamid saw it. He grumbled. But he didn't rub it off.
textes.Un matin, pendant que je bavardais avec: One morning, while I was chatting with Flammèche, one of her puppies, Grignotte, grabbed a whole grouper off my stall. Bigger than him! He dragged it all the way to the kennel, right across town. Flammèche was mortified. I laughed. I told Grignotte he'd earned his grouper. He's followed me everywhere since.

One morning, while I was chatting with Moloka, Grignotte grabbed a whole grouper from her stall, bigger than himself, and dragged it all the way to the kennel right across town. I could have died of shame. Moloka burst out laughing and shouted: “HE'S EARNED IT!” Since then, Grignotte follows her everywhere whenever she passes the kennel.
textes.Un matin, pour balayer dessous, j'ai sou: One morning, to sweep underneath, I lifted his anvil. On my own. Borin stopped talking. A whole minute. The dwarves put down their hammers. Silence. First time all winter. Then he said: “Put it down. Gently.” I put it down. He started talking again. Quieter.
textes.Un matin, pour gagner un aller-retour, j: One morning, to save a round trip, I took both flour sacks at once, one on each shoulder, and ran the whole south bridge. I arrived white from my ears to my tail, a proper rabbit ghost. Mochi screamed. Trèfle just said: “Morning, Pépin.” She'd recognised me by the way I puff.
textes.Un matin, pour le taquiner, je suis venu: One morning, to tease him, I came to fetch my embers with a minuscule shovel, a doll's shovel. He looked at me, he looked at the shovel, and he said: “At last, you're becoming reasonable.” Then he laughed. It's the only time I've ever seen him laugh out loud. I kept the shovel.
textes.Un matin, pour voir, j'ai glissé une vie: One morning, just to see, I slipped an old slipper under his hammer while he was looking away. Tap! He flattened it like a pancake. He stared at it for a long time and said: “You made me miss a stroke.” Since then he watches me out of the corner of his eye. The flattened slipper hangs above my stall. My trophy.
textes.Un matin, pour être polie, j'ai salué la: One morning, to be polite, I saluted the Skala with a blank from Bertha. A gunner's courtesy, nothing more! The caïd sounded the alarm: six armed guards on the battlements. And me, on deck, curtsying. He didn't speak a word to me for a week. Bertha, though, was very proud.
textes.Un matin, près de l'embouchure, j'ai lan: One morning, near the river mouth, I cast my net. Something pulled from the other side. Hard. I pulled. It pulled. Then a head came out of the water, as long as my boat, with two yellow eyes looking at me without a hint of a smile. I let go of the net. It left with it. Since then, I fish upstream. And I count my toes on the way home.
textes.Un matin, sa place était vide. Je l'ai c: One morning, his seat was empty. I looked everywhere for him, then flew up over the Ash Wood. I found him in the middle of a clearing, naming glowing mushrooms. He told me: “That one, I called Malachar, because it's old and it has wings.” It was a fern.
textes.Un matin, sur la Grande-Place, un de mes: One morning, on the Grand Square, one of my sweepers saw her coming with her cannon on her shoulder. It stopped. It turned round. All by itself. I didn't program it to do that. Hm. I let it. Maybe it's right.
textes.Un matin, sur le pont du Cargo, une moue: One morning, on the Freighter's deck, a seagull stole my sandwich. Mouette — the real one — chased after the seagull, the fake one… well, the other one, shouting “KIAAA”. They screamed together. I laughed. Loudly. Mouette stopped dead. She'd never heard me laugh.
textes.Un matin, sur le quai, elle m'a crié des: One morning on the quay she shouted at me. In front of everyone. The net, the anchor, the bill, the interest. Loud. Louder than the auctioneer. I took a step back. Just one. The fishermen saw. Thirty years at sea, never backed down. Not before cannons. Before a woman with a needle, yes. Hm.
textes.Un matin, très tôt, j'ai trouvé Thalion: Very early one morning, I found Thalion sitting alone on the harp bench, plucking a string. Just one. Always the same one. He jumped and said: “Inspection.” Since then I always leave the harp tuned to that note. He doesn't know. He mustn't know.
textes.Un matin, très tôt, j'étais sur le toit: One morning, really early, I was on the dormitory roof with my bedsheet tied to my wrists. Zéphyrine came up without a ladder, just like that, hop, and sat down next to me. We talked about clouds for an hour. Then we went back down by the stairs. I forgot to jump. I think she did it on purpose.
textes.Un matin, un androïde est sorti d'une ca: One morning, an android came out of a crate, brand new, all shiny. He said to me, “Good morning, madam.” He was holding a broom. It was Zéro. He swept in front of my stall before sweeping the rest of the city. He's owed me nothing for a long time, but he keeps on.
textes.Un matin, un drone de livraison est tomb: One morning, a delivery drone fell into the gravel. I could have removed it. I raked around it. It's part of the garden now. Nothing is in its place, {surnom}. Everything is where it is. It's the same thing, if you look closely.
textes.Un matin, un garçon timide est entré et: One morning, a shy boy came in and bought a bouquet “for his mother”. The next day too. And the day after. A whole year like that. One day, his mother came to see where all those bouquets were coming from: she sneezed eleven times. Hay fever. On the three hundred and sixty-fifth morning, Hugo held the bouquet out to me over the counter. He said: “Here.” It was perfect.
textes.Un matin, un moineau s'est posé sur l'ai: One morning, a sparrow landed on my glider's wing. Mr Pascal shouted: “Give me back Gérard!” Then he realised he'd shouted. He went back inside very fast. I gave Gérard back.
textes.Un matin, un nouveau champignon a poussé: One morning, a new mushroom popped up at the edge of the pond. Purple, with golden spots, and a proud little cap. I named it Hector. The Burgomaster came down for the reopening, walked through the Gardens, and stopped in front of it. For a long time. He said: “That one has real presence.” I said nothing. Nobody said anything. We all bit our cheeks.
textes.Un matin, un sloop tout neuf est entré a: One morning, a brand-new sloop sailed into port, with a gold-toothed captain and nobody at the helm. Ignace had just won it. He saw me on the quay and called out: “A gold coin says you can't get my Cod out of port in this crosswind!” I got her out. He gave me the coin, and the helm along with it. His crew called me Coquille. That one, I kept.
textes.Un matin, une araignée de cristal s'est: One morning a crystal spider shattered against my root. A heap of shards, right outside my place. She came flying, with her purse. I sat on them. She said six coins a shard. I said no. There was a blue one. She'd have melted it. Melted! A blue shard like that.

One morning a crystal spider shattered against a root, right outside his place. A heap of shards! I came flying, Grommelot came running. He sat on them. I offered six coins a shard, he said “not for sale”. The whole lot went into his fireplace. For the warmth, apparently. It sparkles like a shop window, his warmth.
textes.Un matin, une fuite s'est ouverte sous l: One morning, a leak opened under the hold, and I had nothing to stuff it with while I waited for the oakum. I used what I had in my pocket: Gwenola's pancake. It held for two hours, nicely buttered. Gwenola found out, I don't know how. She reminds me every morning. That was twelve years ago.
textes.Un matin, une gargouille a plongé sur l': One morning, a gargoyle dived onto Moloka's stall and snatched a whole grouper. Moloka chased it right along the quay, shouting “THIEF!”. In its fright, the gargoyle dropped the grouper into the water, and it swam away. Moloka came back furious. I gave her the best spot on the quay, under the awning, out of harm's way.
textes.Un matin, une mouette a volé le sandwich: One morning, a seagull stole Clou's sandwich on the deck of the Freighter. I ran after it screeching “KIAAA”. The seagull screeched too. And Clou laughed. Out loud. A real laugh! I stopped dead. So did the seagull. We both stared at him, beaks open.
textes.Un matin, une plume de lune s'est envolé: One morning, a moon feather flew off my counter, so light, so shiny. I chased it up the stairs, then across three bridges, then all the way to the treetop. It landed right on the Post Office counter. Plumette picked it up and gave it back to me: “Hoo. It wanted to go by post.” I was as out of breath as a rabbit.
textes.Un matin, Ébène m'a raconté une histoire: One morning, Ébène told me a story I already knew. I said: “You've told me that one before.” He replied: “Yes, but the ending is new.” And it was true: at the end, the baker became king. I gave him two brioches. He does it again every time he's very hungry.
textes.Un matin, à l'aube, je l'ai vu sur le to: One morning, at dawn, I saw him on the dormitory roof, a bedsheet tied to his wrists. I levitated up, without a sound, and sat down next to him. We talked about clouds for an hour: which ones are heavy, which ones are empty. Then we went down by the stairs. He forgot to jump. I didn't forget to be scared.
textes.Un matin, à l'aube, l'Amiral a réveillé: One morning at dawn, the Admiral woke the whole Fondouk squawking “RUM! RUM! RUM!”. The whole courtyard up, and Mbarek on the landing, looking like someone who'd dreamed of a raid. Gaspard came down bright red and paid me for an extra night to apologise. I accepted. On principle.
textes.Un matin. Ciel clair. Mer plate. Les mou: One morning. Clear sky. Flat sea. The seagulls didn't go out. I said: “No.” They laughed. They went out, Brahim too. I stayed on the quay. At noon, the wind. They rowed back, no sail. I threw them ropes. I said nothing. Since then, when I say “Hm”, the port listens. So I say “Hm” less. So as not to abuse it.
A thank you! I'm writing that down.
textes.Un mercredi, Léonce a touché la petite b: One Wednesday, Léonce touched the small coil wearing only one glove. His hair stood straight up, like a crown, and stayed that way all day. Rosette was passing by: the photo made page two of the Gazette. Léonce cut it out and pinned it above his bed. Wilfried says he tries to do his hair like that in the mornings.
textes.Un mercredi, au labo, j'ai touché la pet: One Wednesday at the lab, I touched the little coil with only one glove on. Just one finger. My hair stood straight up, all day long! Rosette took a photo for the Gazette. Mum cut out the article and pinned it above her workbench. She says it's to remind her about gloves. I know she thinks I look handsome in it.
textes.Un mercredi, son petit Léonce a touché l: One Wednesday, her little Léonce touched the coil wearing just one glove. I was there. His hair stood up like a brush and he was laughing his head off. I took the photo. It was on page two the next day: “A Young Inventor Under Tension”. Électre pretended to be cross. She bought ten copies.
textes.Un message de Mamie Barricade : l'assemb: A message from Mamie Barricade: tonight's assembly starts at six o'clock. On the agenda: the colour of the bins, the spring party, and Tapage's weekly interruption.
textes.Un message de Sirène : la nouvelle limon: A message from Sirène: tonight's new lemonade is violet-flavoured. It tickles your nose and it's purple. Like Cradoc's mohawk, but tastier.
textes.Un midi, elle s'est levée d'un bond, la: One lunchtime, she leapt up, fork in hand, and ran off towards the quay. A badly moored sailing boat was banging against the jetty. She retied the knot with the fork between her teeth. Then she came back, sat down and finished her cold plate without a word. I offered to warm it up. “No need.” She ate the lot.
textes.Un midi, en remontant de la cave, j'ai s: One lunchtime, coming up from the cellar, I caught Master Rivet alone at the counter. He was speaking very softly to the butler. He was saying “thank you”. Just that, for a coffee served without spilling a drop. He didn't see me. I went back down to the cellar and counted bottles until he'd finished.
textes.Un midi, je me suis posée trop vite sur: One noon, I came in to land too fast on the terrace of the Diable Repu and landed in the soup pot. Luckily, it was lukewarm. I came out covered in vegetables, with a carrot on one horn. The sailors applauded. Since then, Grumbald calls his soup “the postwoman's soup”. It's the most ordered dish.
textes.Un midi, la poudre de fer de ma cuillère: One lunchtime, the iron filings on my spoon were drawn to the magnet in the coffee machine. The spoon flew off all by itself, ding, stuck to the boiler! It took Gaston an hour to get it off. He hung it above the counter, with a label: “The Professor's Reflection”. I salute it every morning.
textes.Un midi, le sifflet de la Bielle a reten: One lunchtime, the Bielle's whistle went off two seconds late. Two seconds! Tacquet put down his cup, took a little screwdriver out of his pocket, climbed onto a stool and adjusted the valve himself, without asking. Since then it whistles at noon sharp. I don't know what he did. I don't dare touch it any more.
textes.Un minuscule carré de cristal. Quand on: A tiny square of crystal. When you blow on it, a little hologram pops out and takes a bow.
textes.Un minuscule champignon féerique bleu, t: A tiny blue fairy mushroom, very proud, puffing out its cap. "Munch": you suddenly grow big and hit harder (for a while). A storybook mushroom: in a real forest, you must NEVER eat a mushroom you don't know.
textes.Un moderne ! Les vers libres, c'est comm: A modernist! Free verse is like the waterfall: it falls wherever it likes. I respect that.
textes.Un mois, Agrafe a voulu supprimer mon ho: One month, Agrafe wanted to drop my horoscope to make room for a serious article. He received forty letters of protest. Three of them from Radis, who doesn't believe in pigeons but wanted to know what they thought of his tomatoes. The horoscope came back. Agrafe brought me flowers. For peace.
textes.Un mois, j'ai voulu supprimer l'horoscop: One month, I tried to drop the pigeon horoscope to run a proper article about the gardens. I got forty letters of protest. Three of them from Radis, who doesn't believe in it but wants to know what the pigeons think of his tomatoes. The horoscope was back the following week.
textes.Un monsieur d'en haut descend à la Frond: A gentleman from up top comes down to the Fronde: “It's awfully noisy here!” Granny Gamelle hands him a bowl: “That's the soup singing, my pebble.” He had three helpings.
textes.Un monsieur des Nuées, tout en haut, nou: A gentleman from the Clouds, way up top, wrote us forty complaints about the noise. Fusain stuck them up on the Wall. Apparently he taps out the beat while writing them. So we sent him a pair of drumsticks. So he can tap better.
textes.Un monstre ! Je prie, je prie très fort: A monster! I'm praying, I'm praying really hard!
textes.Un monstre ! UN MONSTRE ! Ô Aube, protég: A monster! A MONSTER! O Dawn, protect us, protect us, protect us!
textes.Un monstre ?! « LE VISITEUR TERRASSE LA: A monster?! “VISITOR SLAYS THE BEAST”! In bold! With a drawing! How big was the monster? No, don't tell me, I'll make it bigger.
textes.Un monstre. D'accord. Je me concentre. …: A monster. All right. I'm concentrating. … I'm concentrating.
textes.Un morceau d'amulette en jade, gravé d'u: A piece of jade amulet, engraved with an ancient symbol. You need three to open the Serpent Gate, deep inside the Sunken Temple.
textes.Un morceau de fromage qui a beaucoup voy: A piece of cheese that has travelled a lot, with a golden rind and a… brave smell. For a rat, it's a treasure.
textes.Un morceau de lumière tombé du ciel une: A piece of light fallen from the sky on a clear night, pale and warm. Aurélien Lumen needs it to teach the light spell.
textes.Un mot d'amour, d'une écriture très régu: A love note, in very regular handwriting: “Dear Parlour Clock, ever since I heard you strike noon, my heart has gone tick-tock-tick. I run slow when you're not around. Your Grandfather Clock.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Cher voleur, il: A note on the table: “Dear thief, there's nothing to steal here except the dirty dishes. Help yourself.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Le plombier pass: A note on the table: “The plumber will come on Tuesday. Or Wednesday. Or never. Put a basin under the leak.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Liste de courses: A note on the table: “Shopping list: bread, eggs, a dragon (small), cheese. Don't forget the cheese.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Ne pas toucher a: A note on the table: “Don't touch the cake. Signed: Mum.” Below, in different handwriting: “What cake?”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Partis à la plag: A note on the table: “Gone to the beach. If it's you, Gérard: the cat has ALREADY eaten. Don't listen to him.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « RAPPEL : demain,: A note on the table: “REMINDER: tomorrow is Uncle's birthday. Buy a present. NOT socks.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Recette de la so: A note on the table: “Granny's soup recipe: water, vegetables, and lots of patience. Especially patience.”
textes.Un mot sur la table : « Si tu lis ce mot: A note on the table: “If you're reading this, you're in my house. While you're at it, water the plants. Thanks!”
textes.Un mot, punaisé sous le plan : « Merci d: A note, pinned under the floor plan: “Kindly refrain from lift races. Signed: the lift.”
textes.Un moteur à cristal… Seuls les Lumens d': A crystal engine… Only the Lumens of Astralys, the island floating in the sky, know how to make those crystals sing. You'd have to go and visit them.
textes.Un moteur à vapeur, j'aimerais bien… mai: A steam engine, I'd love to… but I'd need the plans from the inventors of Cliquetis, the city of gears, on the great eastern island. Go and pay them a visit!
textes.Un mouchoir ! Ça vole très mal, un mouch: A handkerchief! Handkerchiefs fly very badly.
textes.Un moustique dans une petite calebasse f: A mosquito in a little gourd closed with a leaf stopper. Kinich swears its name is Xan, like the Twins' one, and that it stings liars.
textes.Un musée de tout ce qui tombe, ici, sur: A museum of everything that falls, right here on the quay. With labels: “fell on a Tuesday”, “fell in a high wind”. The piano in the middle. And someone to play it, for real, even with a key missing.
One metre ten… One metre TEN.
textes.Un mécanisme de Gaspard l'horloger : deu: A mechanism by Gaspard the clockmaker: two hundred wheels. Each planet goes round at the right speed… more or less. Mercury cheats a bit.
textes.Un mérou ! Un vrai, un gros ! Je vais le: A grouper! A real one, a big one! I'll be eating it for a week. Or mapping it.
textes.Un mérou… Je vais le fumer au-dessus de: A grouper… I'll smoke it over the forge. Come back for a taste.
textes.Un nain n'oublie jamais un visage. Ni un: A dwarf never forgets a face. Or a debt. Or an insult.
textes.Un nature, comme d'habitude ? Mousse en: A plain one, as usual? Extra froth, of course.
textes.Un naufragé ne se perd jamais : il est d: A castaway never gets lost: he's already lost. It's very restful.
A turnip stole the Baron's hat.
textes.Un navet attrapé devient doré. Ne me dem: A caught turnip turns golden. Don't ask me why. Philomène says it's a fairy blessing. I say they're blushing because they lost. But in yellow.
textes.Un navet fuyard ! Il ne mord pas… il cou: A runaway turnip! It doesn't bite… it runs. Catch up by running (Shift) and give it a little tap: it's yours.
textes.Un navet fuyard des Champs du Sud, attra: A runaway turnip from the Southern Fields, caught during an alert: it's golden, it has little arms, and it's sulking. The Guild buys it back; so do Babette and Ulric (for soup).
textes.Un nectar ! Bois-le d'un trait, c'est me: A nectar! Drink it in one go, it's better. And it heals better.
textes.Un nid de pie était caché dans les branc: A magpie's nest was hidden in the branches!
textes.Un nid de tagliatelles dorées, faites à: A nest of golden tagliatelle, handmade this morning by Mamma Lasagna, "while singing". For the Great Reconciliation dish. Don't squash it, don't break it, don't eat it on the way.
textes.Un nom de gâteau ! Comme Biscotte, ou Ma: A cake name! Like Biscuit, or Madeleine! There's already a Madeleine. She eats everything. Maybe you're like her.
textes.Un nouveau ! Génial ! Viens, je te montr: A new one! Brilliant! Come on, I'll show you: there, the dormitory, Oscar snores; over there, the Duelling Ground, Pyra shouts; down below, the Chaudron Fumant, Berthe bakes pies; and up there, the Observatory, Lumen sleeps by day. Six masters, six spells! Me, I have zero. But soon one!
A storm cloud, full of energy.
textes.Un nuage orphelin ! Le Docteur Aurèle l': An orphan cloud! Doctor Aurèle found him all alone under the Station, too small to keep up with the others. He left him in our care, saying: “He needs a family and a houseplant.”
textes.Un nœud, deux nœuds… quarante-sept nœuds: One knot, two knots… forty-seven knots.
textes.Un ondin, un esprit de l'eau ! Il se gon: An undine, a water spirit! It swells up before pouncing: step aside. The Gust (key 1) scatters it.
textes.Un os à mâcher ? Pour moi ? Tu es le mei: A chew bone? For me? You're the best human in the whole archipelago. I'll hide it. I'll forget it. I'll find it again. That's life.
textes.Un os à mâcher qui sent bon le jambon, d: A chew bone that smells deliciously of ham, from Chaussette's shop. For Sardine, the dog with the red bandana: "Give" when he's with you.
textes.Un ours de givre, Maître ! Dans le broui: A frost bear, Master! In the fog!
textes.Un oursin ! Hmpf. Bon. Je vais lui ajout: A sea urchin! Hmph. Fine. I'll add some spines, then you'll be right. The customer decides. Even when he doesn't pay.
A tool… Fine. A tool's honest. But you'll see: one day it'll save your skin, and that day, you'll find it a name. All by yourself.
textes.Un pain assez grand pour tout le village: A loaf big enough for the whole village, at the Dawn Festival! One single loaf in the middle of the square, and everyone takes a piece. I'll need a bigger oven. Mine's going to sulk.
textes.Un pain chaud, Amenemhat. CHAUD. Avec le: A HOT bread, Amenemhat. HOT. With the right sign.
textes.Un pain que tout l'archipel connaîtrait: A bread the whole archipelago would know: “Azur bread”, with honey. Eaten by the dwarves, by the elves, under the sea if need be. And people would say: that comes from Margaux's.
textes.Un pain rond et plat, cuit contre la par: A round, flat loaf, baked against the wall of Mérit's oven, with a little sand in it (everyone has sand in their bread in Per-Hâpy). Restores two hearts.
textes.Un panier d'osier des Jardins Partagés :: A wicker basket from the Shared Gardens: leeks, squashes, potatoes, and a carrot with a tiny bite taken out of it. For everyone's soup.
A basket of tomatoes. For the Cooking Pot.
A basket. For the Cooking Pot.
textes.Un papier. Un seul. Signé, avec un tampo: A paper. Just one. Signed, with a stamp. Saying these walls belong to those who bring them to life. After that, I can knit in peace.
textes.Un papillon bleu passe devant ton nez, p: A blue butterfly flutters past your nose, then a yellow one, then twenty more. In the middle of the room, a child is counting out loud… and starting again.
textes.Un par anniversaire de mariage : quarant: One for each wedding anniversary: forty-three! The silver tubes are his; the little cups are mine. He says it's an orchestra; I say it's a lot of dusting.
textes.Un par jour, c'est la règle de l'assembl: One a day is the assembly's rule. I voted for it myself. I can't betray it. Not even for your lovely smile.
textes.Un parapluie blanc à baleines solaires,: A white umbrella with solar ribs, invented by Mireille Volta. It goes up. Very well, in fact. It's the coming down that's still being invented.
textes.Un parapluie noir, comme tous ceux de Ra: A black umbrella, like all the ones in Rainville… but underneath, when you open it, there are painted sunflowers. Mother Downpour made it fifty years ago, for her best friend.
textes.Un parapluie qui pleut. Pour arroser les: An umbrella that rains. For watering the plants while you're out for a walk. Mireille says it's an “upside-down” idea. I think it's the right way up, if you're a plant.
textes.Un parapluie rouge surmonté d'une hélice: A red umbrella topped with a propeller. When you open the umbrella, the propeller spins. It's no use at all, but it's very pretty.
An umbrella. There's sand in it.
textes.Un parapluie. … Il existait, n'est-ce pa: An umbrella. … It already existed, didn't it?
textes.Un parapluie… avec des tournesols peints: An umbrella… with sunflowers painted underneath. So that, even in the rain, I can see the sun. (She opens it; she laughs; she cries a little.) She promised it to me, the summer of our quarrel. Fifty years… Well. It's time two old ladies stopped being silly.
textes.Un parchemin roulé, un sceau rouge, une: A rolled-up parchment, a red seal, a little cottage drawn in the corner: "The Wisteria Cottage, Montjoie Upper Town, now belongs to its new owner. Wisteria included." Signed: Mr Prosper.
textes.Un parchemin roussi aux coins, scellé de: A parchment singed at the corners, sealed with red wax: "Bachelor of Flames, with the (slightly burnt) congratulations of the jury". Signed: Professor Malachar.
A passenger saw whales, up north.
textes.Un patch d'aventurier ! Je n'en ai jamai: An adventurer's patch! I've never made one. Give me a day or two. I'll make it from an old bit of chain mail. Yes, yes, Trocante has some.
textes.Un patch d'épée et de bouclier, tu voula: A sword-and-shield patch, that's what you wanted. I'm working on it. The chain mail is putting up a fight, but I'm more stubborn than it is.
textes.Un pavillon à la poupe : six dessins au: A flag at the stern: six designs to choose from, to change whenever you like.
textes.Un perroquet ! La prochaine fois, je t'e: A parrot! Next time, I'll make you two. One for him.
textes.Un perroquet ? Je ne vends pas de perroq: A parrot? I don't sell parrots!
A parrot ate half of it.
textes.Un perroquet, ça vit cent ans ! Bartholo: A parrot lives a hundred years! Bartholomé knew Barbe-Sanglante. Sometimes he repeats “the skull, the skull”. I don't know what it means.
textes.Un petit ? Un tout petit tour ?: A little one? A teeny little lap?
textes.Un petit Moaï surveille un tas de feuill: A little Moai watches over a pile of smoking leaves. “Don't step on it! It's dinner!”
textes.Un petit Moaï te fait signe : « Psst ! T: A little Moai beckons to you: “Psst! Do you know '1, 2, 3, Moai'?”
textes.Un petit air, pour rester éveillé ?: A little tune, to help you stay awake?
textes.Un petit boulon de laiton poli, ouvert e: A small polished brass bolt, opened and rounded by Lumi, with a shard of blue crystal from the Chasm set on top. It was with rings like these that Ysaé learned the trade, sitting on the bolt crate at the Swap Shop.
textes.Un petit champignon des mares de Ramure,: A little mushroom from the ponds of Ramure, with a pale blue cap, that glows softly at night. Mère-Lune puts them in the bridge lanterns.
textes.Un petit chien blanc dort derrière mes c: A little white dog sleeps behind my crates, at the end of the quay. I'd seen a snout. I didn't say anything. Nina found him and named him Brioche. So I made him a kennel out of an empty crate and an old blanket. I wrote on it in chalk: “Brioche”. The crate's called Brioche now too.
textes.Un petit couinement : Biscotte a trouvé: A little squeak: Biscotte has found {objet} at the back of a hiding place. Rats always know where the treasures are. It's their job.
textes.Un petit croc jaune, perdu par un gobeli: A small yellow fang, lost by a goblin from the Goblin Wood (he has others, and a stolen sock in each pocket). Master Hugues makes necklaces with them.
textes.Un petit cœur ? … Comme quelqu'un que je: A little heart? … Like someone I know. I won't say who. Little hearts are the tattoos of big tough guys. Good choice.
textes.Un petit diablotin te tapote la joue : «: A little imp pats your cheek: “Up you get! The circles won't go down by themselves.”
textes.Un petit dirigeable vole en rond sous le: A little airship flies in circles under the ceiling! Below it, a table covered in maps, and a child pleading: “A storm! A storm!”
textes.Un petit démon plonge sous la table en t: A little demon dives under the table when he sees you. “MOOOMMY! A HUMAN!”
textes.Un petit grille-pain blanc couvert de pa: A little white toaster covered in solar panels. It toasts a perfect slice of bread. And a bit of everything around it.
textes.Un petit museau rose sort d'entre les pl: A little pink snout pokes out from between the planks of the jetty, next to the hull of the Requin Borgne… and ducks straight back in. You'd need to put down something that smells very, very good: the aged cheese!
A little cloud that passes quickly.
textes.Un petit nuage qui passe… (Il note quelq: A little passing cloud… (He notes something in his notebook.) They're my favourites. The ones you only see once. I'll put you on the first page, next to Bernard.
textes.Un petit nuage tout blanc flotte au mili: A little snow-white cloud floats in the middle of the living room, like a balloon that has learned to dream. A delighted child watches its every move.
textes.Un petit piment rouge et luisant, du mar: A small, shiny red chilli from Zébuline's market. Demons crunch them like cherries. You're going to cry. Restores one heart (smoke out of the ears included free).
textes.Un petit pot de peinture en fer-blanc, c: A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "1". Inside, the blue of Sketched Island (the Rubbed-Out Pond, the sky in the water, the streams). To be poured into cup no. 1 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "2". Inside, the green of Sketched Island (the leaves, the grass, the moss of the Hatching Wood). To be poured into cup no. 2 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "3". Inside, the red of Sketched Island (the poppies of the White Meadows). To be poured into cup no. 3 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "4". Inside, the yellow of Sketched Island (the sand of the White Strand). To be poured into cup no. 4 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "5". Inside, the brown of Sketched Island (the wood of the village, the earth of the clearing). To be poured into cup no. 5 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "6". Inside, the purple of Sketched Island (the heather of Mount Charcoal). To be poured into cup no. 6 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "7". Inside, the orange of Sketched Island (the Ink Waterfall at sunset). To be poured into cup no. 7 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "8". Inside, the turquoise of Sketched Island (the Dotted Stream, all the way to the sea). To be poured into cup no. 8 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.

A small tin pot of paint, dented by the Great Downpour, with a label: "9". Inside, the pink of Sketched Island (the flowers of the south-western meadows). To be poured into cup no. 9 of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the Giants' Clearing.
textes.Un petit pot de sauce tomate, puisé à la: A small jar of tomato sauce, scooped with the giant ladle from the Cooking Pot of Mount Bolognese: tomato, garlic, basil, a pinch of sugar. Still warm. Restores two hearts.
textes.Un petit robot-nettoyeur te passe la ser: A little cleaning robot mops your forehead: “Please do not faint in traffic areas. Thank you.”
textes.Un petit sifflet en os sculpté, avec un: A little carved bone whistle, with a dog, a cat, a rat and a pig engraved all around it. "Use": choose which companion comes with you.
textes.Un petit slime te tapote la joue d'une g: A little slime pats your cheek with some very cool jelly: “Blop?” (That means “get up”.)
textes.Un petit soin ! Pas de quoi ! Enfin, si,: A little healing! Don't mention it! Well, actually, it needed mentioning, you were bleeding a bit…
textes.Un petit sort de bulle : l'air de la mai: A little bubble spell: the air in the house is a bit damp, just enough for them. You don't feel a thing. Except maybe a little dampness in your hair.
textes.Un petit tour en rond, {surnom} ? Bernad: A little ride round the loop, {surnom}? Bernadette's all warmed up.
textes.Un petit tour, ou neuf jours ?: A little stroll, or nine days?
textes.Un petit tour. Tu viens avec moi ?: A little stroll. Coming with me?
textes.Un petit trésor ! Le coffret contient :: A little treasure! The box contains:
textes.Un petit vent de nuit se glisse par la b: A little night breeze slips in through the big window. The harp sings very softly, and the chimes barely tinkle, so as not to wake anyone.
textes.Un petit, du sud. Il chante !: A little one, from the south. It sings!
A little one. He likes you.
textes.Un peu ! Au troisième nuage !: A bit! At the third cloud!
textes.Un peu ? Il parle à un perroquet ET à de: A bit? He talks to a parrot AND to seashells. You, now, you're someone sensible.
textes.Un peu ? Oh, viens là. Assieds-toi près: A little? Oh, come here. Sit down by the cauldron. Homesickness is cured with hot soup and conversation. I'll take care of both.
textes.Un peu ? Tu en as perdu combien, en rout: A little? How much did you lose on the way?
textes.Un peu agacée. Depuis la réouverture, to: A bit irritated. Since the reopening, everyone takes the capsule. Nobody goes up by airship any more. The capsule is nice, but it's a lift. The Dragonfly is a voyage.
textes.Un peu brouillé. Il y avait trop de brui: A bit scrambled. There was too much noise on the bridge today. People from up top shouting to hear the Chasm answer. It answered. A lot. It's tired. So am I.
textes.Un peu chiffonnée. La Fronde a encore «: A bit crumpled. The Fronde “borrowed” my big tongs for their concert again. They bang on them in rhythm. They always give them back. But with stickers.
textes.Un peu contrarié. J'ai prévu une averse: A bit annoyed. I forecast a shower for seventeen minutes past eleven. It fell. On Hautefond. Two hundred metres too low. I was wrong with great precision. That's a kind of success.
A little water, a little sun.
textes.Un peu de graisse de chèvre. Très peu. P: A bit of goat fat. Very little. Hardly any.
textes.Un peu de lumière de l'Aube, et hop !: A little light of the Dawn, and presto!
textes.Un peu de sel. Toujours un peu. Tu as ra: A little salt. Always a little. You're right.
textes.Un peu de silence avant la musique… Voil: A little silence before the music… There. Done.
textes.Un peu de vapeur dans la moustache. Rosa: A bit of steam in the moustache. Rosalie says my cinnamon hot chocolate is hers. HERS! It's my machine, it's my cup, it's my moustache dipping in when I taste it! … Fine, it's her cinnamon.
textes.Un peu de vertige. Hrmm. La rambarde. Pa: A bit scared of heights. Hrmm. The rail. Not the wicker. Remember?
textes.Un peu des deux. C'est la bonne réponse,: A bit of both. That's the right answer, actually. That's what the Column is for: going up, going down, and coming back. You've got it.
textes.Un peu distrait, me dit-on. J'ai salué l: A little absent-minded, I'm told. This morning I said hello to the coat stand. Twice. It was wearing my hat: I mistook it for myself. Besides, the Dome is full of glass. One keeps running into oneself.
textes.Un peu déprimé. Un peintre sans couleurs: A bit down. A painter without colours is like a baker without flour. I'm kneading thin air.
textes.Un peu enrhumée. C'est le poivre. Il fai: A bit of a cold. It's the pepper. It does that when it's happy. Atchoo! … There, it's very happy.
textes.Un peu enroué. Je fais la visite à chaqu: A bit hoarse. I give the tour on every trip down: “On your left, the Trench! On your right, the Greenhouses! Below, the Great Pearl!” After thirty times, the voice wears out. The blue never does.
textes.Un peu enrouée. Hier soir, j'ai chanté l: A bit hoarse. Last night I sang the last chorus three times, because the pit wouldn't let us stop. This morning my voice goes “crrk”. Gamelle gave me a honey tea. She says in two hours I'll go “laaa”.
textes.Un peu enrouée. Le Grand Spaghetti boude: A little hoarse. The Great Spaghetti is sulking, so I sing louder to comfort him. It doesn't work. He closes his eyes even more. Maybe it's not the right song.
textes.Un peu ensommeillée… Les chouettes, le j: A bit sleepy… Owls in the daytime are like rabbits at night.
textes.Un peu essoufflé. Ici, l'eau bout plus v: A bit out of breath. Up here, water boils faster because of the altitude. My tea is ready before I've even picked up the cup. I spend all day chasing my tea. It's very good for the waistline. In theory, anyway.
textes.Un peu fanée, aujourd'hui. Une chenille: A bit wilted today. A caterpillar ate half my lettuces. I can't hold it against her: in three weeks, she'll be a butterfly. A future colleague. She has to grow somehow.
textes.Un peu fanée. Une lampe de la tour numér: A bit wilted. A lamp in tower number two burnt out last night. The strawberries underneath got cold and went all pale. Yolande changed it this morning. I sang them a song to warm them up. They're getting their colour back. Slowly.
textes.Un peu fatigué des bras. Dix ans de cabi: A bit tired in the arms. Ten years of a cabin standing still, and now sixty trips a day. My arms had forgotten. My heart hadn't.
textes.Un peu fatigué des bras. Huit heures de: A bit tired in the arms. Eight hours of rails, three hours of drums… Bielle says I should choose. I did: both. But a bit less loud. … No, I'm lying. Same as ever.
textes.Un peu fatigué des genoux. Je saute de j: A bit tired in the knees. I jump for joy at every departure. Engineer Nova says it throws the capsule off balance by a millimetre. A millimetre of happiness seems reasonable to me.
textes.Un peu fatigué. Depuis que la Ligne a ro: A bit tired. Since the Line reopened, all the folk up top want to visit the Crystal Grotto. I explain the helmet, the white line, the wagons… They listen. Then they see the crystals, and forget everything. I start again.
textes.Un peu fatigué. J'ai dansé toute la nuit: A little tired. I danced all night beneath the Mother Tree.
textes.Un peu fatigué. Le matin, je dors. L'apr: A little tired. In the morning, I sleep. In the afternoon, I calculate. At night, I watch. That doesn't leave much room for anything else. Anything else is mostly eating. I forget.
textes.Un peu fatigué. Tenir la pince toute la: A bit tired. Holding the tongs all day turns your arms to jelly. But Honorine gave me an extra galette at lunch. She says apprentices are like ovens: they need looking after.
textes.Un peu fatiguée du bras. Excalibur pèse: My arm's a bit tired. Excalibur's no lightweight, you know. Ressort tried to lift her. He managed! Halfway. He said he was “the chosen one”. I told him the chosen one also does the washing-up.
textes.Un peu fatiguée. Depuis la réouverture,: A bit tired. Since the reopening, there are two thousand more people on the island every day. That's a lot of weight. I've recalculated the lift three times. It holds. But I've asked Gustave to make lighter sugar puffs.
textes.Un peu fatiguée. J'ai… fait une longue p: A bit tired. I… went for a long walk. In the gardens. Very long. With lots of sea. The gardens are big, here.
textes.Un peu fatiguée. Le Bourgmestre a comman: A bit tired. The Burgomaster ordered a new medal. A medal for what, I asked him. He said: “We'll see.” I laughed so hard I dented the anvil.
textes.Un peu frustré. Le vent d'ouest est tomb: A bit frustrated. The west wind dropped at noon. I stayed on the pier waiting, arms spread wide, like a scarecrow. Captain Zéphyrine took a photo of me.
textes.Un peu frustrée. Deux cents mètres, c'es: A bit frustrated. Two hundred metres is my limit. Yolande engraved it on the control panel. And below that, the Trench keeps going. Black, deep, full of things nobody has ever seen. I stop at two hundred. But I look down. For a long time.
textes.Un peu frustrée. Ici, l'air est filtré p: A bit frustrated. Down here, the air is filtered by the algae: it's pure, but it wipes out smells. Cinnamon hardly smells of anything, and nor does vanilla. So I cook with what doesn't fly away: salt, iodine, seaweed, Lamp Orchard lemon. Flavours that stand firm.
textes.Un peu frustrée. Le parapluie qui monte: A bit frustrated. The rising umbrella rises beautifully. It's the coming down I haven't solved yet. The last tester was stuck on the Institute's mast for an hour. He said the view was superb.
textes.Un peu fâchée. Lou ne veut pas m'emmener: A bit cross. Lou won't take me in the Little Diver. She says “when you're grown up”. I ask her every morning if I'm grown up. She says “not yet”. I measured myself. I've grown one centimetre. That should count.
textes.Un peu fâchée. Maman dit que je n'ai pas: A bit cross. Mum says I'm not allowed to take the bench apart to get its bolts. But it would surely stand up on its own. Surely.
textes.Un peu fâchée. Maman dit « bientôt » qua: A bit cross. Mum says “soon” when I ask to go down and see the sea. She's been saying “soon” since I was six. That's four soons. Four soons is a lot.
textes.Un peu impatiente. L'Albatros a besoin d: A bit impatient. The Albatross needs a new stabilising sail, and Mathilde hasn't finished the rivets. She says “tomorrow”. She says it laughing. I can never tell if that's a good sign.
textes.Un peu inquiet. Le Grand Spaghetti boude: A bit worried. The Great Spaghetti is sulking, and I'm afraid it's because of me. Last week, I sneezed during prayers. On the eternal plate.
textes.Un peu inquiet. Le cristal pâlit…: A little worried. The crystal is fading…
textes.Un peu inquiète. Depuis que la Ligne a r: A bit worried. Since the Line reopened, there are folk from up top at all my tables. Very polite. Far too thin. They eat from the tip of the spoon. I'm teaching them. Gently. One bowl at a time.
textes.Un peu inquiète. La ligne des Nuées a ro: A little worried. The Cloud line has reopened, and the Column isn't used to so many people any more. She creaks at night. I talk to her. She calms down.
textes.Un peu inquiète. La ligne des Nuées est: A little worried. The Cloud line is under maintenance, and the Column doesn't like having floors closed. It creaks at night. I talk to it. It calms down.
