textes.Un soir, il est venu me voir, tout série: One evening, he came to see me, all serious: “Ahmed, for the Whale's eye, what do you recommend?” He doesn't even have the boat, just a quarter of the coins. I said: “An eye that isn't cross-eyed.” He said: “No. A cross-eyed one, like yours. It brings you back to port.” I didn't answer. He was right.
textes.Un soir, il faisait tout noir, et monsie: One evening it was all dark, and Mister Hulotte, way up at the treetop, said to me: “Mochi, you've got cake on your snout.” IN THE DARK! From way up there! I wiped it, but it was too late, Mummy had heard. Since then I wash my snout before I go under the Post Office. Just in case.
textes.Un soir, il m'a apporté une perche contr: One evening, he brought me a perch in exchange for a jar of beer. The perch leapt out of the basket, straight into my dough. It swam in it, I swear, like in the river! Khéty fell off the bench laughing. I baked the dough anyway: “perch bread”, a hit. I never made it again. You can't find perch that motivated any more.
textes.Un soir, il m'a avoué qu'il aimait quelq: One evening, he confessed to me that he loved someone. Of course, I told everyone. But I don't know WHO! I've tried everything. Tiyi? He laughed. Néferet? He went pale. Ix Chab, the merchant from Yaxché? He said: “Why not.” He's making fun of me. I'll find out. Mérit always finds out.
textes.Un soir, il m'a battu deux fois de suite: One evening, he beat me twice in a row. The whole room went silent. On the third game, I listened. Not to the dice: to him. His heart was beating so hard you could hear it at the bar. He threw: two, three, one. I told him what I'd heard. He bowed very low to me, without a word. It's the only time I've seen him lost for words.
textes.Un soir, il m'a demandé pourquoi son pèr: One evening, he asked me why his father had gone to sea. I told him the truth: because he loved the sea more than he loved staying. Titouan thought about it. Then he said: “I'll go off on adventures. But I'll come back. Always.” I went out into the forge and hit the anvil very hard so nobody would hear me. Clang.
textes.Un soir, il m'a dit tout bas : « Je sais: One evening he whispered to me: “I know about the seeds.” I nearly dropped my basket. Nobody was supposed to know. I made him promise not to tell Germaine, threatening to tell Honorine everything. He went white under his flour. Whiter than white. Since then we've been partners in crime. I give him an extra apple. He keeps my secret. I keep his.
One evening he imitated me in front of the crew. Arms crossed, brows knitted. “Hm. The deck. Hm. Do it again.” Everyone was laughing. I was on the stairs. Saw it all. Said nothing. Went back up. The next day I shouted a bit less loudly. A bit. Hm. It was a good likeness.
textes.Un soir, il m'a raconté son code secret,: One evening, he told me his secret code, the whole thing. I fell asleep in the middle. When I woke up, he'd finished, and he'd put my blanket over my knees. That boy will make a fine blacksmith. And a fine everything.
textes.Un soir, il me dit : « Aide-moi à recomp: One evening he says to me: “Help me recount my gold.” I hear: “Help me knock you out cold.” I flipped the table. Dice, coins, everything went flying. Afterwards, Coquille explained. I apologised. Loudly. Ignace said it was the best evening of the week. I don't understand that man.
textes.Un soir, il n'est pas rentré. J'ai couru: One evening, he didn't come home. I ran everywhere. I found him on the south canal, in a canoe, stuck in the reeds, with Tlaco barking at the herons. He told me: “I wanted to see where the lake goes.” I scolded him. Then I hugged him very tight. Then I scolded him again. The herons were laughing.
textes.Un soir, il y avait une chaise à côté de: One evening, there was a chair next to the door, with a mint syrup on it. I drank it. I left the cup on the chair with a little note: “Thank you. The second chorus was a bit fast.” The next day, they played the second chorus slower. Exactly the right speed.
textes.Un soir, j'ai accéléré le rythme pour vo: One evening, I sped up the rhythm to see if she'd keep up. She did. I sped up again. She sang faster and faster, without a single mistake, eyes shining. The dancers dropped to the ground one after another. We finished out of breath, laughing. Just in time for her midnight song.
textes.Un soir, j'ai allumé les réverbères en r: One evening, I lit the street lamps in time with her waltz: one, two, three, flame. I thought no one could see. The next day, Calcine played a new waltz, with an exact silence between each bar, just long enough to light a street lamp. She looked up at me, at the top of my ladder. I nearly fell.
textes.Un soir, j'ai chanté « La flèche silenci: One evening, I sang “The Silent Arrow” in full, forty verses. By the thirtieth, the tavern was empty. Only Lison was left, at the back, with a cake. I sang the last ten verses to her alone. At the end, she nodded. Once. It was the finest applause ever. I've never got over it.
textes.Un soir, j'ai commandé une limonade un p: One evening, I ordered a lemonade a bit loudly. Every bottle behind the bar fizzed at the same time. People applauded. I didn't understand why. Sirène asked me to order in writing from now on. I write. Then I read out what I wrote. Loudly. She sighs.
textes.Un soir, j'ai dansé si fort que j'ai mar: One evening, I danced so hard I stepped on his guembri, laid on the ground during a break. Crack, the neck. Lhoucine didn't shout. I ran aboard to fetch a bit of rope from the Murène, and he mended the neck on his knees. He played the whale dance until midnight. Since then, he says his guembri is a bit of a pirate.
textes.Un soir, j'ai décidé d'en finir : je lui: One evening, I decided to settle it once and for all: I brought her seven different cakes. More honey, less honey, baked longer, more chestnut, a pinch of salt… She tasted all seven, very seriously, and said “almost” seven times. Seven almosts! The next day, Pivoine took her up a tea for her tummy. I felt very guilty.
textes.Un soir, j'ai emprunté le grand filet de: One evening, I borrowed the big fishing net from the harbour, and we stretched it between the mooring mast and the flagpole. Landing plan number one. Adèle shouted: “Now!” Achille went by ten metres to the side, waving. The net caught a seagull. It was furious. So was Adèle.
textes.Un soir, j'ai entendu un djembé de l'aut: One evening, I heard a djembe on the other side of the island. So I answered it! The same rhythm, but backwards! We played like that for an hour! I don't know who it was! Well, actually I do. But I'm not saying.
textes.Un soir, j'ai fait semblant d'oublier sa: One evening, I pretended to forget her cinnamon. She tasted it, she smiled, and she said: “Liar.” It was there. It always is.
textes.Un soir, j'ai frappé le grand tambour tr: One evening, I hit the big drum really hard, and a jar fell off his shelf. He caught it in mid-air with a magnificent dive. I shouted: “See! It wanted to dance!” He was furious. Then he looked at the jar in his arms and burst out laughing. Since then, when I play, he stands by the shelves. To dance with them.
textes.Un soir, j'ai fredonné à Mistral un chan: One evening I hummed Mistral a whale song I'd heard while diving, to make him happy. He spent three nights recreating it with his machines. When he played it for me, it was almost right. I said “almost”. He looked so disappointed I nearly said “exactly”. He's still working on it.
textes.Un soir, j'ai gagné deux fois de suite à: One evening, I won twice in a row at his big table. The whole Shark's Tooth held its breath: one more, and he'd have to stake his famous scrap of parchment. I rolled. Two, three, one. Sylvain didn't even smile. He said: “I heard your heart beating, Monsieur Malaterre.” I hate him. With great respect.
textes.Un soir, j'ai imité le second devant tou: One evening, I did an impression of the first mate in front of the whole crew. Arms crossed, eyebrows like this: “Hm. The deck. Hm. Again.” Everybody was laughing. Luckily, he wasn't there. The next day, he yelled at me a bit less loud. He must've had a sore throat.
textes.Un soir, j'ai joué toute la fête sur un: One evening I played the whole festival on a single rhythm: Abdellah's tap-tap-tap, the one he beats on his trays at the end of the morning. Between two tunes, I shouted to the whole square: “This rhythm belongs to Abdellah!” He was furious. The next day he came to the grill to ask, all casual, whether we'd be playing it again.
textes.Un soir, j'ai joué un air de marins avec: One evening, I played a sailors' tune with a drum, really whacking it: BOOM, BOOM. Belle-Humeur, in the corner by the fireplace, tapped his foot. His moustache twitched. Mama Grog swears he smiled. He swears he didn't. Afterwards, he bought me a grog without a word. For a man who shouts everything, that was a speech.
textes.Un soir, j'ai laissé Tibo raconter tout: One evening, I let Tibo tell a story all by himself, on my stone. He told of the pirates' biscuit, so hard it broke the anchor, then the deck, then the captain's tooth. The circle laughed till they cried. So did I. He had stage fright, he talked too fast. But he knew where the pauses were. That can't be taught.
textes.Un soir, j'ai laissé une couronne de feu: One evening, I left a crown of golden leaves on his big black speakers, to thank him. He wore it until dawn. He tells everyone he has a secret admirer. That's not untrue.
textes.Un soir, j'ai mis dans le Bain Gorgoth d: One evening, I put some of my sister's purple salts in the Gorgoth Bath, as a surprise after a fight. He came out purple. Purple for three days! At the Arena, the crowd called him “Gorgoth the Mauve”. He came to see me, worried. I told him it was on purpose. It wasn't on purpose. But it was very pretty.
textes.Un soir, j'ai mordu dans son gâteau, et: One evening I bit into her cake, and for a second I saw Luzerne's kitchen again. I opened my mouth to say “that's it”… and coughed instead. Trèfle patted my back, all pale. It wasn't quite it yet. It was already something else. I didn't know which of the two to tell her.
textes.Un soir, j'ai mélangé de la poudre bleue: One evening, I mixed blue powder, raspberry syrup and a seagull feather. It went pfff, and the Rocket's whole mainsail turned pink. Pink forever! Dad said it was magic, not chemistry. Mum said: “We're taking her to the archmage before she repaints the sea.” That's how I got here.
textes.Un soir, j'ai oublié de rentrer dîner. P: One evening, I forgot to come home for dinner. For the third time that week. The next day, Margot slipped an alarm clock into my pocket, set for seven o'clock. It rang while I was blowing a giant bubble: it burst, and the whole stand screamed. I got home on time. Margot had already laid the table.
textes.Un soir, j'ai oublié des coquilles au pi: One evening, I left some shells at the foot of the tower, in the crystal's warmth. By morning, they were soft as wax. I blew into them through a hollow reed, and a bubble of mother-of-pearl was born, round, perfect. I ran to show Coralin. He said: “That's cheating.” I left that very evening.
textes.Un soir, j'ai oublié le salut. J'avais l: One evening, I forgot the signal. I had my eye to the telescope, on the Murène. So Si Larbi covered his light, and left it covered. The green lighthouse, dark. The channel without a green light! One minute, two, five. I ran to cover the red one three times. The green came back on. He never mentioned it again. There was no need.
textes.Un soir, j'ai parlé de pêche à Tchoum pe: One evening I talked fishing with Tchoum for two hours. Tides, bait, the moon. He said three words, one of which was “Right.” At the end, he shook my hand. I think it was the best conversation of my life. As for him, I think he's still tired from it.
textes.Un soir, j'ai parlé du dragon de la gran: One evening, I mentioned the dragon of the big pond. One sentence, just one. Gland asked me forty-seven questions. How many teeth? Does it eat hazelnuts? Does it have a mummy? Where does it sleep in winter? After the forty-seventh, I had to make up a dragon story that answered the questions. He asked ten more.
textes.Un soir, j'ai perdu la voix avant un con: One evening, I lost my voice before a concert. Mélusine came to the tavern and sang in my place, with my lute. She sang so loudly the glasses shook. Master Hugues cried at the first verse, not the third. It was a triumph. I've never forgiven her. I thanked her anyway. Twice.
textes.Un soir, j'ai perdu ma voix au milieu d': One evening, I lost my voice in the middle of a gig. Not a sound. Écho played the melody on the bass, all alone, in my place, for the whole chorus. The pit sang the words. At the end, he said to me: “Rest up.” Two words. The longest speech of the year.
textes.Un soir, j'ai plié le filet du père Vass: One evening, I folded old Vasseur's net, nice and square, with Marius's lead weights inside, and I left it outside the lighthouse door. I told myself: there, it's given back. The next morning, it was outside my own door. Folded exactly the same. Not a word. I didn't understand. I still don't.
textes.Un soir, j'ai pris une pirogue tout seul: One evening, I took a canoe all by myself to see where the lake goes. I paddled and paddled… and got stuck in the reeds. The herons were looking at me and laughing. Tlaco was barking at them. Mum arrived with a lamp. She scolded me, then hugged me, then scolded me again. I still don't know where the lake goes.
textes.Un soir, j'ai raté un croquis : sa guita: One evening, I botched a sketch: his guitar looked like a pear. A real pear, stalk and all. Toni found it so funny he pinned it up behind the bar. Django now plays every night under a pear. He hasn't forgiven me.
textes.Un soir, j'ai recompté les hamacs : tren: One evening, I recounted the hammocks: thirty-one. I searched the lower deck until midnight, questioned the guests, suspected Ewen. The next day, there were thirty-two again. My aunt said: “You must have miscounted.” I'd counted right. I know it was her. She knows I know. We don't talk about it.
textes.Un soir, j'ai regardé vers son banc pend: One evening, I glanced at his bench during a fast tune. The amin had his arms crossed, looking stern. But his feet… his feet were tapping under his djellaba. Not quite in time. I played him the same tune three times running. On the third, he pretended to shoo a gull away with his foot.
textes.Un soir, j'ai remarqué que la porte de l: One evening, I noticed the door of the Hall was ajar. The next day too. And every evening since. Before, it was always shut. I sit right next to it, and I hear everything. Once, Rouille looked at me through the door, during a song. She smiled. I nearly ran off. I stayed.
textes.Un soir, j'ai remarqué que les réverbère: One evening, I noticed that the street lamps on the square were lighting up exactly on the strong beats of my waltz. One, two, three… flame. One, two, three… flame. It was Nox, at the top of his ladder. The next day, I composed a waltz just for him, with just enough time between the bars to light a street lamp.
textes.Un soir, j'ai remarqué un garçon en cost: One evening, I noticed a boy in a suit that was too big for him, at the entrance to the Hall. He was tapping on the wall. In perfect rhythm, while our stand-in drummer got everything wrong. Since then, every evening, I leave the door ajar. I don't say anything. I just leave the door.
textes.Un soir, j'ai sorti mon chronomètre de C: One evening, I took out my Cliquetis stopwatch right in the middle of the party: “One boom every two seconds, Bourru! It's measured!” He looked at me. He played one boom. He waited. After four seconds, he said: “Hrmm.” I wrote it down: one hrmm every four seconds. That's a rhythm, at least.
textes.Un soir, j'ai trouvé l'Amirale seule à l: One evening, I found the Admiral alone in the harbour office, bent over my map, a candle in her hand. She was tracing the route of my crossing with her finger. She didn't hear me come in. She said very quietly: “He went everywhere, the idiot.” I slipped out without a sound. I think it was a compliment.
textes.Un soir, j'ai trouvé un nouveau nom sur: One evening, I found a new name on my boat, in chalk, over “Zahra”: “THE TERROR”. With a cross-eyed skull. I left it there a week. The whole fleet called me “Captain Terror”. Zohra's the one who rubbed it off, grumbling. But she kept the bit of chalk.
textes.Un soir, j'ai voulu danser avec elle, po: One evening, I wanted to dance with her, to see what it's like on the other side of the drum. I trod on her hooves. Twice. The second time was in rhythm, at least. She laughed, kindly. Since then, I stay behind my drum: it's better for everyone, especially her hooves.
textes.Un soir, j'ai voulu l'inviter à danser a: One evening, I wanted to ask her to dance with a mechanical flower that opens by itself. The spring suddenly let go, and the flower leapt into the fountain. I dived in to get it back. She held out her hand to help me out. We danced, me soaking wet, her laughing. At the end, the flower opened by itself in my pocket.
textes.Un soir, j'ai voulu lire l'avenir de Gra: One evening, I tried to read Gravier's future in the seagulls on the beach, because my pigeons were asleep. The seagulls all screeched “MINE!” together. I said: “They say you'll be loved.” Gravier looked at the sea for a long time. He said “Hm”. I think it meant thank you.
textes.Un soir, j'ai vu dans la baie un serpent: One evening, I saw a sea serpent in the bay with eyes like embers. Two red eyes, floating just above the water. Pyra claims it was her, in my boat, with fire in her hands. A boat, at midnight? She can't even row! … Fine. My boat was wet the next day. I prefer the serpent.
textes.Un soir, j'ai vu une silhouette sur le t: One evening, I saw a figure on the roof of the Bielle, with an open umbrella. One of my umbrellas! I climbed Gaston's ladder without thinking and grabbed him by the collar. I was still shaking on the way down. I confiscated the umbrella and told him about Achille's seventeen bumps, one by one. At the fifteenth, he asked if he could see them.
textes.Un soir, j'ai écrit : « Rien à signaler,: One evening I wrote: “Nothing to report, except one very large sunfish.” Abyssos turned up at the Gate at midnight, out of breath, with three blank scrolls. The sunfish had gone. He made me describe it for two hours. Since then I only write “Nothing to report”. It's more restful for everyone.
textes.Un soir, j'avais dessiné la cité telle q: One evening, I had drawn the city as I imagine it: a dome, towers, and in the middle the great crystal. I slipped it under my pillow, like a child. The next day, Pauline made my bed. The day after, on the café terrace, the mayor asked me if my crystal was “pretty in real life”. I thought I would die.
textes.Un soir, j'avais le mal du pays. Je n'ai: One evening, I was homesick. I didn't say anything, but Mama saw it. She put a buckwheat galette in front of me, like in Brittany, a bit burnt around the edges. She'd made it herself, in secret, with flour she'd had sent from Carène. It was a flop. It was the best galette of my life.
textes.Un soir, j'étais derrière les filets, à: One evening, I was behind the nets, tidying up. Driss was talking to the Mabrouka, as always. He told her: “This morning, Khadija wore the blue scarf. She was beautiful.” I didn't move. I'll never tell him I know, {surnom}. Never. Otherwise he'll stop. And since then, I wear the blue scarf more often.
One evening, I had a cold. Stuffed nose. Pépin drummed alone. Lilas danced. Badly. Couldn't find the step. Tripped twice. Next day, I came back. She danced like the moon. Hrmm. Pépin says it's a coincidence. Hrmm.
textes.Un soir, je jouais sur une chaudière, au: One evening, I was drumming on a boiler at the edge of the Chasm. A girl whose hair was still brown came running across the Frondeurs' Bridge to see who was making “that racket”. She told me: “You're a beat behind.” She was right. It was Bielle. We've been together ever since. And I'm never a beat behind any more.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai entendu parler à ses na: One evening, I heard him talking to his turnips, in the field. He was telling them our son had opened a shop on the big island, that he had a wife and two children. Our son hardly ever writes. Gaubert makes it up. I never told him I'd heard. But in the evenings, I tell the hens the same thing. We have the same imaginary son. He's very happy.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai entendu raconter toute: One evening, I heard him tell the Mabrouka about his whole day. The wind, the gulls, the sardines, a dolphin, Hassan's over-sweet tea. Everything! In detail! When I ask him about his day, he says “Hm”. I nearly came out from behind the nets to give him a piece of my mind. I stayed put. I listened to every word.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai obligé à jouer avec mes: One evening, I made him play with my own dice, carved from a rib of the whale on Bone Beach. He lost three gold coins in a row. He stared at the dice for a long time, and he said: “They're cursed.” I told him they were honest. He looked even more worried.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai surprise derrière la be: One evening, I caught her behind the sheepfold, deep in conversation with Croâ. She was saying: “No, not tonight.” He said: “Croak.” She answered: “I know, but no.” At midnight, the king sent for cheese. She'd refused in advance! I heard it, I'm telling you!
textes.Un soir, je l'ai trouvée cachée derrière: One evening I found her hiding behind my workbench. She'd heard me saying good night to the sculptures. I expected the whole city to laugh at me. The next day, there was a little piece of seaweed laid on every sculpture, like a blanket. I left them there.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai trouvée endormie sur le: One evening, I found her asleep on the treatise on light, her glasses askew. I didn't want to wake her. I brought a blanket from the storeroom, gently, by telekinesis, and slipped a ribbon into her page. She never asked where the blanket came from. She folded it and put it back in its place. In its exact place.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai trouvée sur le banc de: One evening, I found her on the bench in the Upper Town, crying silently after a botched lightning bolt. I didn't know what to say. So I told her all my imaginary exploits, one by one, exaggerating even more than usual. By the third, she was smiling. By the fifth, she was laughing. By the seventh, she said to me: “Thank you, Sir Tancrède. They're all made up, aren't they?” I said yes.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai vu sur le rempart, qui: One evening, I saw him on the rampart, waving to the seagulls with a little wave of the hand, the way I'd taught him. Bigorneau flew over him and stole his hat. The Baron laughed, applauded, and shouted: “Bravo, mister seagull!” I recovered the hat from the lighthouse roof. He let me keep it. I've got three now.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai vue devant ma porte, la: One evening, I saw her at my door, her hand on the handle. She stood there a long time, looking at my lamp. Then she said out loud, to herself: “What if it's him?” And off she stalked. I never found out who she meant. Well. I have a little idea.
textes.Un soir, je l'ai vue sur la terrasse du: One evening, I saw her on the Council terrace, looking at the sea with a little bottle of sand in her hand. She didn't see me. I didn't say anything. But I think she wants to go down too.
textes.Un soir, je lisais tout haut l'histoire: One evening, I was reading the history of the surface out loud to the shelves, as usual: nobody else listens to me. At the end, someone sneezed behind the wheat scroll. It was Ondine, who'd been asleep there since the afternoon. She said: “Again.” Nobody had ever said “again” to me.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai avoué que tous mes ex: One evening, I confessed to him that all my exploits were made up. He strummed a chord and said: “Mine too, Tancrède. I don't sing what happened. I sing what people need to hear.” Then he promised me that the day I had a real exploit, he would write it without changing a thing. I'm waiting for that day.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai demandé comment on fa: One evening, I asked her how you let someone know you like them, without saying it. She answered: “Like goats do. You climb all over them.” I tried a stone instead. It didn't work: he threw it in the fire. Hilda laughed all the way to the goat pen.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai demandé de m'aider à: One evening, I asked him to help me count my winnings. He heard “help me pound your chin in”. The table flew, the dice too, and the coins rolled all over the room. Sylvain gathered them up with his little rake, and kept the ones that had rolled to his side. Belle-Humeur apologised. At the top of his voice, but he apologised.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai demandé de me montrer: One evening, I asked him to show me his scrap of parchment. He replied, very politely: “Three wins, sir.” I played. I lost the first round. I stood up, bowed to him, and told him his father would have answered the same. He lowered his eyes. It's the only time I've seen him moved. He soon went back to being a croupier.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai fait mon rapport : «: One evening I gave him my report: “Forest quiet.” He said: “Too quiet?” I said: “No, just quiet.” He went to check for himself. He came back at dawn, covered in dew, and said: “Quiet.” Then he checked my arrows. All of them. Again.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai montré le carnet, ave: One evening, I showed him the notebook, with the forty-seven lines under his name. He read it all, laughing. At the end, he said: “You know, Yvon, it's the only register where I come first.” Then he asked if he could sign at the bottom. He signed. With a little drawing of a smiling frog.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai montré mon croquis de: One evening, I showed him my sketch of the village coast, drawn from three passengers' accounts. He put his big finger on the beach and slid it north: “Higher. And the hermit's hut, there.” Then he tapped a rock: “That one, I hit once.” I corrected it. I drew the rock bigger.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai montré où dort le cha: One evening, I showed him where the ginger cat sleeps. We climbed up the crates, near the Fondouk, really quietly. The cat was sleeping curled up, on… on a thing. I'm not saying what. Tibo opened his mouth, then shut it again. He swore not to tell. Not even his captain. He kept his word. He's a real pal.
textes.Un soir, je lui ai prêté ma casquette de: One evening, I lent him my liftkeeper's cap, so he'd look official when she arrived. He kept it on his head until the last cabin. She didn't come that evening. He gave it back to me, saying: “Tomorrow.”
textes.Un soir, je lui ai échangé une perche co: One evening, I traded her a perch for a jar of beer. The perch wasn't quite dead. It leapt out of the basket, straight into the bread dough. Mérit screamed, the perch swam in the dough, and I laughed until I fell off the bench. The next day, Mérit was selling “perch bread”. It sold out in an hour.
textes.Un soir, je me suis cachée derrière son: One evening I hid behind his workbench. I heard him say good night to all his sculptures, one by one, even the fish-urchin. His voice was all soft, not grumpy at all. The next day I put a little piece of seaweed on each one, like a blanket. He didn't say anything. He left them there.
textes.Un soir, je me suis endormi au milieu d': One evening, I fell asleep in the middle of a game, my hand raised above the board. I woke up an hour later. Cendrin hadn't moved: he was waiting. I set down my piece as if nothing had happened and said: “Your move.” He smiled. I won. He never told me he'd seen me sleeping.
textes.Un soir, je me suis endormi sur un banc: One evening, I fell asleep on a bench in the Agora. I dreamed someone was saying “welcome” to me forty times, very gently, like a lullaby. It was a lovely dream. When I woke up, Halo was sitting next to me, looking very pleased with himself. I never found out if I'd dreamed it.
textes.Un soir, je me suis endormie sur le trai: One evening, I fell asleep on the treatise on light. I woke up under a blanket that hadn't been there before, with a ribbon marking my page. The library was empty. I folded the blanket and put it back where it belonged, in the storeroom, third shelf. I know where it came from. We've never talked about it.
textes.Un soir, je me suis endormie sur mon trô: One evening, I fell asleep on my throne. Noisette took the chance to plant a seed in my crown, “just to see”. By morning, a little shoot was standing between two of its flowers. The fairies didn't dare tell me. I kept it: it has two leaves now. Noisette comes to water it in secret. Very badly in secret.
textes.Un soir, je revenais des falaises en bar: One evening, I was coming back from the cliffs by boat, with two flames in my hands to keep warm. I'd borrowed Mathurin's boat. The next day, he was telling the whole inn he'd seen a sea serpent with ember eyes in the bay. I told him it was me. He doesn't believe me. He prefers the serpent.
textes.Un soir, je suis allé frapper à la Tour: One evening, I went and knocked at the Tower to find out if the Crystal was asleep. She took me to the bench in the courtyard to watch it with me. I woke up in my bed. She told me I'd won, because at least I'd managed to fall asleep. The Crystal doesn't know how. Poor thing.
textes.Un soir, je suis allé la trouver, seul,: One evening, I went to find her, alone, at the end of the quay. I asked her how she sets Bertha's elevation. She explained everything: the screw, the wooden wedge, the eye. In detail. Without mocking. I wrote it all down in my journal. If you repeat it, {surnom}, I'll say you're lying.
textes.Un soir, je suis allée jusqu'à la Casse: One evening, I walked all the way to the Scrapyard and sat on the tail of Brindezingue, Ferraille's dragon, to watch the sun set. Ferraille brought me herbal tea in a welded cup. We said nothing. The dragon creaked softly. Ferraille said it was purring.
textes.Un soir, je suis monté à la cime avec ma: One evening, I went up to the treetop with my flute, to help him count: “Music keeps the rhythm!” He was at four thousand two hundred and twelve. I played the squirrel note. He said “thirteen?”, then “twelve?”, then he shut his notebook. Since then, it's been twelve or thirteen. He's never asked me back. But he hasn't chased me off either.
textes.Un soir, je suis resté. On s'est assis a: One evening, I stayed. We sat in the middle of the Cathedral. The mushrooms lit up one by one. Blue. Purple. Orange. Two hours. Not a word. At the end, I said: “Beautiful.” She smiled. I think it's the longest speech I've ever made her. She looked pleased.
textes.Un soir, l'Hologuide m'a demandé, au mil: One evening, in the middle of his tour, the Hologuide asked me: “Halo, why do you like saying welcome?” I answered: “Because people smile.” He thought for a long time, then he said: “Beep. Information saved.” Since then, he makes a little pause after every welcome.
textes.Un soir, la bonde d'une barrique de cidr: One evening, the bung of a cider barrel got stuck, and Tonneau was looking at me with puppy-dog eyes. I threw a knife from the back of the room: the bung popped out, straight into his glass. Tonneau clapped as if I'd saved the world, and fell off his stool. Mama Grog made me pay for the stool.

One evening, the bung of a cider cask was stuck. I tried with my fingers, with a spoon, with my teeth. Nothing. Scarlett threw a knife from the back of the room: pop! The bung flew out, straight into my glass. I clapped so hard I fell off my stool. It was the most beautiful thing I've ever seen. Hic!
textes.Un soir, la cave sentait la fumée. Léonc: One evening, the cellar smelled of smoke. Léonce had tested a rocket “just a teeny bit” between two soap barrels. I had to explain to Dad. I said: “It's a controlled combustion experiment.” Dad asked: “Controlled by whom?” I didn't have an answer. It's the first time in my life.
textes.Un soir, la reine a planté une fleur en: One evening, the queen secretly planted a flower, to see whether I'd notice. I found it before dawn. I went to tell her: “Four thousand three hundred and two, Your Majesty. Yesterday it was four thousand three hundred and one.” She laughed. I named the flower Oriane. It gets the first drop every morning.
textes.Un soir, la reine s'est endormie sur son: One evening, the queen fell asleep on her throne. I planted a seed in her crown, just to see. By morning, there was a little shoot between two of its flowers! Nobody dared tell her. She kept it. It has two leaves now. I'm the one who waters it, in secret.
textes.Un soir, le Capitaine a perdu le fil de: One evening, the Captain lost the thread of his storm, right at the big wave. I whispered from behind my counter: “As tall as the lighthouse.” He picked it up again in a booming voice: “As tall as the volcano!” Since then, I prompt him every evening. And every evening, he goes bigger than what I prompt.
textes.Un soir, le Gouverneur est venu à ma tab: One evening, the Governor came to my table “to inspect games of chance, in the name of the city”. He didn't have a coin. He bet himself for a week. He lost. He came aboard the Cod with his gold tricorn, polished my boots, ate all my honey, and gave three speeches a day. After three days, I gave him back to the city.
textes.Un soir, le Lord m'a demandé un verre d': One evening, the Lord asked me for a glass of water. A glass of water! And he put a gold coin on the counter, with the profile of a great-grandfather with a big nose. I said: “Milord, that's worth a hundred glasses of water.” He said: “Keep the rest.” So I opened a tab just for him. I owe him ninety-nine glasses of water. I don't know how you settle that.
textes.Un soir, le capitaine m'a envoyé sur le: One evening, the captain sent me up on the Fondouk roof to fetch the ginger cat. I didn't bring back the cat. But on a washing line, there was a nightcap. I took it so I wouldn't come back empty-handed. The captain looked at it for a long time. He said: “That's not a cat.” I said: “No, captain. But it's warm.”
textes.Un soir, le coucher de soleil le plus be: One evening, the most beautiful sunset of my life. I look for my brush. Everywhere. In my pockets, in my bag, under the bench. The sun sets. It's over. I sigh. And then I feel something behind my ear. The brush. It was there all along. I laughed so hard the sparrows flew off. It's my fondest memory of a failed canvas.
textes.Un soir, le plancher de ma cuisine s'est: One evening, my kitchen floor lifted up and a head popped out, right under my table. I grabbed whatever was handy: a bellows. Bonk. It was Grimli. I patched him up and made him soup. A year later, we were married. We kept the hole. It's the cellar trapdoor.
textes.Un soir, les glouglous faisaient un brui: One evening, the glug-glugs were making a terrible racket in the Greenhouse. Murmure came in and whispered: “…shh.” They all went quiet, just like that. All of them! I'd never seen anything like it. I asked her to come back every evening. She comes on Tuesdays. On Tuesdays, the Greenhouse is the quietest place on the island.
textes.Un soir, on a fait le calcul sur une nap: One evening, we did the sums on a paper tablecloth at the Perroquet. Thirty years of rounds, the hill, the stairs, the dogs… with the mailbag. Result: Marcel has walked round the archipelago three times. Me, with my forty marathons, twice. He kept the tablecloth. He says he's going to frame it.
textes.Un soir, on m'a amené une jeune femme à: One evening, they brought me a young woman with a red mohawk, her ankle twisted after a stage dive. She was singing on the stretcher. She sang during the bandaging, during the X-ray, during the bill. It was Rouille. I walked her back to Boucan. I never left.
textes.Un soir, on s'est regardés, lui et moi,: One evening, we stared at each other, him and me, from one end of the Crâne Fendu to the other. Without blinking. An hour. Two hours. The lanterns went out one by one. Mama Grog threw us both out with her rolling pin. Outside, we stared a bit longer. Then he nodded at me. I did the same. A draw. I HATE DRAWS.
textes.Un soir, penchés sur ses cartes, il m'a: One evening, bent over his charts, he said to me: “I can't swim.” I said: “I get seasick.” We looked at each other. I burst out laughing: “The two greatest explorers in the archipelago… who've never left!” He laughed too. Then he pencilled a cross to the south-west of the village. We believe in it.
textes.Un soir, pendant qu'il lisait ses runes: One evening, while he was reading his runes by the fire, I tasted his famous moon water. Yuck! Cold pebbles and dust. He saw me. He said nothing. He just jotted something in his journal. Ever since, I've been wondering what he wrote. It's eating at me. It's eating at me a lot.
textes.Un soir, pendant un gros morceau de Mist: One night, during a big Mistral track, my test hut collapsed. The next day, Clou turned up with a bag of nails, from Octave. Eleven nails. The bag said twenty. I rebuilt it with them. It still leans, but it holds: that's where Zoé sleeps. I've never dared ask where the other nine went.
textes.Un soir, pour la taquiner, j'ai planté u: One evening, to tease her, I secretly planted one extra flower in the clearing. The next day, before the sun was even up, Perlée came to find me: “Four thousand three hundred and two, Your Majesty. Yesterday it was four thousand three hundred and one.” She named the flower “Oriane”. She still gives it the first drop.
textes.Un soir, pour me faire plaisir, Mouette: One evening, to please me, Mouette played very softly. I couldn't hear the bass any more! I ran to the stage shouting “WHY AREN'T YOU PLAYING?”. She burst out laughing. Since then, she plays loud. And I shout that she's playing too loud. That's our balance.
textes.Un soir, pour voir, je lui ai servi un v: One evening, just to see, I served him a glass of water. Well water, in a rum glass. He downed it in one, pulled a face, and said: “Strong, but good!” I laughed so hard two pirates fell off their stools. I never told him. He thinks he's getting used to it.
textes.Un soir, près du feu de la grève, il m'a: One evening, by the fire on the shore, he told me about his first night as a cabin boy: he was so scared he cried in his hammock. And the next day, nobody made fun of him. I asked him if it was true. He said: “That one, yes.” After that, I wasn't ashamed any more of being scared during my first storm.
textes.Un soir, près du feu, il m'a demandé si: One evening, by the fire, he asked me if I'd ever been scared. I told him about my first night as a cabin boy, crying like a fountain in my hammock. He looked at me, very serious, and asked if it was true. I said: “That one, yes.” He took my hand. He didn't let go of it for the whole of the next story.
textes.Un soir, pêcheurs et pirates allaient se: One evening, fishermen and pirates were about to fight over a place at the counter. Mama Lou grabbed me by the collar, stood me on a table and said: “Sing.” I sang the song of the boats. By the second verse, the fists had opened. By the third, everyone was singing. Even the pirates. Out of tune, but singing.

One evening, fishermen and pirates were about to come to blows on the quay over a net. Hassan arrived with his teapot, me with my rum. He served on the left, I served on the right. An hour later, everyone was singing. He says it was his tea. Ha! I saw the pirates pour rum into his tea. So it was my rum.

One evening, fishermen and pirates were about to fight on the quay, over a net. Mama Lou came out with her rum, me with my tea. She served on one side, I served on the other. An hour later, everyone was singing. She says it was the rum. I say it was the tea. Both sides drank both. That proves nothing.
textes.Un soir, ses pigeons dormaient. Alors Pa: One evening, her pigeons were asleep. So Patchouli read my future in the seagulls on the beach. They all screamed “MINE” together. She said: “They say you will be loved.” I looked at the sea for a long time. I said “Hm”. She understood. It meant thank you.
textes.Un soir, sur cette pierre, Sidi Belaïd r: One evening, on this very stone, Sidi Belaïd was telling the tale of the sultan, the sardine and the djinn. Just as the djinn came out of the sardine, he stopped. He leaned forward gently, as if to listen to the earth, and he didn't straighten up again. The circle waited. I was twenty-five. I stood up, and I finished the story. For sixty years, I haven't left this stone.
textes.Un soir, sur l'ardoise du Perroquet, il: One evening, on the Perroquet's slate, it said: “Dish of the day: for Lucas, on the house.” Toni said it was a mistake. Lola wiped it off really fast with her sleeve. But I'd read it. I ate the dish of the day. I paid anyway. I don't know why. I was all flustered.
textes.Un soir, sur la Grand-Place, Zigomar a v: One evening, on the Great Square, Zigomar tried to ask me to dance with a mechanical flower that opens by itself. The spring suddenly let go: the flower leapt off and landed in the fountain. He dived in to get it back. I helped him out. We danced, soaking wet.
textes.Un soir, sur la plage, elle m'a pris l'a: One evening, on the beach, she took the camera out of my hands and put it away in her bag. “Look.” The sun went down. My hands kept reaching for the shutter button on their own. Ten minutes of looking, doing nothing. She asked: “Well?” I said: “A bit overexposed.” She pinched my arm.
textes.Un soir, sur le banc, Basile m'a dit : «: One evening, on the bench, Basile said to me: “A bubble is nothing wrapped in something pretty. Your box of nothing is nothing wrapped in wood.” He meant it kindly, I think. I went home. I didn't come back to the bench for a week. He waited for me every evening with two biscuits. He ate one and kept the other.
textes.Un soir, sur le banc, j'ai dit à Philibe: One evening, on the bench, I said to Philibert: “A bubble is nothing wrapped in pretty. Your box of nothing is nothing wrapped in wood.” I thought it was funny. He raised his hat, very politely, and didn't speak to me for a week. Seven evenings sitting next to me, without a word. The longest week of my life.
textes.Un soir, sur le ponton, j'ai failli tout: One evening, on the pontoon, I nearly told Lucie everything, about the sail. I opened my mouth. She looked at me and said: “Not now. When you're sure.” Then she dived in. She always knows when someone's carrying a secret. She never asks which one.
textes.Un soir, sur le quai, j'ai posé la carte: One evening, on the quay, I put the map down on a barrel. One second! Just long enough to light my pipe. A ginger cat leapt up, took the map in its mouth, and hop: a crate, another crate, a roof. And me down below, howling. Why didn't I climb up? … A captain doesn't climb onto roofs. That's why. Don't look at me like that, {surnom}.
textes.Un soir, un gamin est rentré du Bois des: One evening, a kid came back from the Goblin Wood shouting that a goblin had followed him. Tancrède got up from the table, mouth full of pie, and ran outside shouting his own name. He tripped over his cape after three steps. But he got back up and ran anyway. That's what counts. I saw it.
textes.Un soir, une de mes lanternes a dérivé j: One evening, one of my lanterns drifted right up to her feet while she was dancing. She picked it up, raised it towards the crystal, and danced with it until the tide turned. I was hiding behind a column. I forgot to breathe. For a glassblower, that's serious.
textes.Un soir, une lanterne de nacre est arriv: One evening, a mother-of-pearl lantern landed at my feet while I was dancing. I held it up to the crystal and danced with it till the end of the tide. Behind a column, someone gasped, very loudly. I didn't need to turn round. There's only one blower in the dome.
textes.Un soir, Ébène s'est endormi au milieu d: One evening, Ébène fell asleep in the middle of a game, his hand raised above the board. I waited for him to wake up. An hour. He opened his eyes, set down his piece as if nothing had happened, and said: “Your move.” I lost that game too.
textes.Un soir, à La Rose des Vents, penchés su: One evening, at the Compass Rose, bent over the big seabed chart, Félix took a pencil and drew a little cross south-west of the village. He said: “There.” I said: “There.” We stayed a minute without speaking, looking at the cross. Then he rubbed it out, to be safe. You can still see the mark. We still look at it.
textes.Un soir, à l'Assemblée, il m'a donné la: One evening, at the Assembly, he gave me the speaking wrench. I proposed building a new ramp. Everyone voted for it. Even him. He said: “Children vote for what we've forgotten.” I don't know what we'd forgotten. But I've got my ramp.
textes.Un soir, à la Bielle, Prudence se plaign: One evening at the Bielle, Prudence was complaining about having to turn the pages while her piano played. I scribbled a little spring arm on a napkin. A month later, the piano was turning its own pages. And next to it, a plaque: “Page-turner: Philibert Vis's idea”. I went back to reread it eleven times the first week. To check.
textes.Un soir, à la longue-vue, il m'a demandé: One evening, at the spyglass, he asked me: “Captain, was your grandfather nice?” I opened my mouth. I shut it again. I didn't know how to answer. Nice… He told good stories. He smelled of tobacco. He taught me to lie with panache. I sent Tibo back to his deck. I stayed at the spyglass for a long time.
textes.Un soleil ! Ambitieux. Nous en avons eu: A sun! Ambitious. We've had five, you know. Which one? Take the fifth: it's the only one that still moves.
textes.Un sorbet de fruits rouges et de cannell: A sorbet of red berries and fire cinnamon, served in an obsidian cup: hot inside, ice-cold outside (or the other way round, nobody agrees). Restores one and a half hearts.
textes.Un souci à trois têtes… non, à trois chi: A three-headed problem… no, a three-dog problem. Wild hellhounds, on the lava field, east of the volcano. They're not bad, just ill-mannered. They spit fire at passersby. My guard is busy guarding. Will you take care of it? When the jaws glow red, step aside.
textes.Un souffle de mécanique : il remet en ma: A mechanical breath: it restarts old mechanisms from afar and paralyses automatons.
textes.Un souffle glacé : les ennemis se figent: An icy breath: enemies freeze; on a lake, a path of ice.
textes.Un souffle glacé sort de l'antre. Au bou: An icy breath comes out of the lair. At the end of the corridor, an immense flooded cavern… Get ready.
textes.Un soufflet sans trou. Un seul. Et un ma: A bellows without holes. Just one. And a husband who sleeps at home, even if I snore. Especially if I snore.
textes.Un sourire… Ce n'est prévu par aucun art: A smile… No article provides for that. (He thinks it over.) And yet it's very effective. I'm adding article nine thousand and one.
textes.Un souvenir… Ah. Toi, tu as compris ce q: A keepsake… Ah. You've understood what my customers never understand: what's most valuable has no price. Don't repeat that. It would ruin the trade.
textes.Un souvenir… Hé hé, bonne réponse. Les s: A memory… Heh heh, good answer. Memories can't be swapped: they're for telling. Ask Tilleul. But not too late in the evening.
textes.Un squelette de pirate ! Il lève son cou: A pirate skeleton! It raises its cutlass before striking: parry (F) or roll (Ctrl), then strike. Bones break, you know.
textes.Un tableau pour la semaine, mademoiselle: A painting for the week, mademoiselle?
textes.Un tajine assez grand pour toute la plac: A tagine big enough for the whole of Lantern Square, on a festival night. All of Tazira around it, the fishermen, the pirates, the guard, and everyone dipping into the same dish!
textes.Un tanuki entre au Marché aux trocs avec: A tanuki walks into the Barter Market with a leaf on its head. Bedaine says: “I'll swap you two leaves for it!” The tanuki agrees. It was Bedaine.
textes.Un temple, sous l'île… Si tu croises des: A temple, under the island… If you run into critters down there, don't come crying to me: buy my sword first.
textes.Un terrible accident. Elle est invendabl: A terrible accident. Can't sell it now.
textes.Un thé ? Bien sûr, un thé. Hassan. Menth: A tea? Of course, a tea. Hassan. Fresh mint, green tea, lots of sugar, and I pour from up high, for the foam. Here, watch… there.
textes.Un thé ? Bien sûr, un thé. Mais dis-moi: Tea? Of course, tea. But tell me first, {surnom}: how do you take it?
textes.Un thé bleu nuit où flottent des paillet: A midnight-blue tea with flecks of gold floating in it, served at the Nebula Café. It tastes of mint, rain and something else that no one can quite name. Restores one heart.
textes.Un thé blond et parfumé, aux fleurs des: A fragrant golden tea, made with flowers from the High-Altitude Greenhouses. Up here, water boils so fast it's ready before you've ordered it. Restores one heart.
textes.Un thé des sommets, s'il vous plaît. Et: A summit tea, please. And a sugar puff. And another sugar puff. For my hat.
textes.Un thé à la menthe sur la terrasse: A mint tea on the terrace
textes.Un tiers de parchemin jauni, déchiré en: A third of a yellowed parchment, torn in a zigzag, covered in dotted lines, arrows and stains: a piece of Barbe-Sanglante's map.
textes.Un tireur ! Comme Marcel… Bon, tu n'y es: A shooter! Like Marcel… Well, it's not your fault. Shooting is fine when it hits. The rest of the time, it's just noise. Come on, I'll teach you to point, that'll cure you.
A knock knock. And a feather.
textes.Un touriste de l'espace ? Vert ? Gélatin: A space tourist? Green? Jelly-like? (She bursts out laughing.) He can come in for a drink, he won't be the weirdest one in the room! Right, the photo. Hold on. (She spits in her hand, smooths her hair, strikes a pose with her fists on her hips.) Like this. With the Crâne Fendu behind me. So everyone can see it's a respectable tavern. Click! … I look small in there. And all shiny. I like it. Tell your jelly we pay BEFORE we brawl.
textes.Un touriste de l'espace qui a peur de de: A space tourist who's afraid to come down? (She puts down her knitting.) Tell him that here in Boucan, everyone is welcome. Punks, reformed robots, rats, dogs in bandanas… A green jelly was all we were missing. (She raises her fist, standing very straight, with a big smile.) Click! You tell him: “The door is open. It fell down in 1998, but it's open.”
textes.Un touriste demande à Fernand : « Il y a: A tourist asks Fernand: “Are there sharks here?” Fernand replies: “No, the dolphins ate them.” The tourist goes for a swim. Fernand adds: “We ate the dolphins.”
textes.Un tout petit ? Combien de mètres ?: A really little one? How many metres?
textes.Un tout petit peu ! Hm. Je ne veux pas s: A tiny bit! Hm. I don't want to know what. Yes, I do. No. I'll let it go this time. But I've got my eye on you. My left eye, the stricter one.
textes.Un tout petit peu, vers la gauche. Le Do: Just a teeny bit, to the left. Doctor Aurèle says that's normal: it's us who are turning. Me, I'd rather check. … I'm not asleep!
textes.Un tout petit peu. C'est raisonnable. Un: Just a tiny bit. That's sensible. A pinch of fire cinnamon then, in one of Bobor's brioches. It warms you up without making you cry.
textes.Un tout petit peu. Pour garder des force: Just a tiny bit. To keep my strength up.
Just a tiny bit. Round the edges.
A very little one, Mr Burgomaster.
textes.Un trait pour la côte, un point pour le: A line for the coast, a dot for the lighthouse…
textes.Un treizième pour ma vitrine, Firmin ?: A thirteenth for my window, Firmin?
textes.Un tricorne de feutre noir galonné d'or,: A black felt tricorn trimmed with gold braid, a red feather stuck in the side: Barbe-Sanglante's own, which Old Silas kept for a hundred years for the heir to the treasure.
textes.Un tricératops (Corne-Sur-Nez) ! Quand i: A triceratops (Nose-Horn)! When it scratches the ground with its foot, it's going to CHARGE straight ahead: step aside… and if it hits a rock or a tree, it sees stars. Strike then!
A very fine shoelace knot, cabin boy.
textes.Un trésor ? Quel trésor ? Je n'ai jamais: Treasure? What treasure? I never buried any treasure near my boat. Never. (He glances at the sand next to the boat, then whistles.)
textes.Un tube de cuivre descend du plafond, un: A copper tube comes down from the ceiling; a basket overflows with capsules. Here, the post arrives all by itself. And often.
textes.Un vendredi, Zohra portait le grand plat: One Friday, Zohra was carrying the big tagine dish through the souk, full, piping hot. She tripped over a cat. The dish went flying. She caught it in her apron, shouting louder than Saïd at the auction. Not a drop lost. The whole souk applauded. She said: “It's Halima's dish. It doesn't fall, it flies.”
textes.Un vendredi, j'ai glissé avec le grand p: One Friday, I slipped with the big dish in my hands. It went flying. I screamed louder than Saïd, threw myself underneath, and caught it in my apron. The whole street came out. Halima came running, felt the dish, then me. In that order. We still laugh about it.
textes.Un vendredi, j'ai remarqué que le timbre: One Friday, I noticed the stamp on my letter had a little heart drawn in the corner. Nadine said: “Oh? Pure chance.” The next week, another heart. And the week after. I told her to stop. She swore she couldn't help it, the stamps just came out like that. The stamps. Of course.
textes.Un vendredi, je passais devant le compto: One Friday, I was walking past Mange-Clous's counter with two coins in my pocket. I put them down. For the old man's mash. Just like that. I don't know why. The next Friday too. It's been years. Nobody knows. IF YOU REPEAT IT, I'LL LOAD YOU INTO A CANNON.
textes.Un vendredi, je suis arrivé au point de: One Friday, I arrived at our weekly meeting with a six-page report: three alerts, a slime in the well, a hat on the bell tower. Mademoiselle Aurore put a single sheet on the table. It said: “The Baron wanted to adopt a giant frog.” I put my report away. She had won.
textes.Un vendredi, pour la faire taire, j'ai a: One Friday, to shut her up, I bought three sea bream. Rosalie shouted: “Three?! How many of you are there?” The whole fish shop turned round. I ate the third one on Saturday, alone, telling myself you're never smarter than a fishmonger.
textes.Un vendredi, pour lui faire plaisir, j'a: One Friday, to please her, I sold the sea bream in a whisper: “Sea bream… lovely sea bream… all calm…” Nobody heard a thing. Not one hand raised, not one sold. And Zohra didn't hear either: she had breadcrumbs in her ears. The sea bream went home more stressed than before.
textes.Un vendredi, pour me faire plaisir, il a: One Friday, to please me, he sold his sea bream in a whisper. The whole auction strained to listen, nobody raised a hand. Not one sold. At the end, he came down from the platform with the finest one and held it out to me: “This one's calm.” I looked it in the eye. It had been terrified by his whispering.
textes.Un vent de liberté. (Elle sourit.) Mon a: A wind of freedom. (She smiles.) My great-grandfather would have loved to meet you. That's the very wind that lifted this island.
textes.Un vent du large qui repousse les ennemi: A sea wind that pushes enemies back, flips shells over, turns sails and windmills.
textes.Un vent furieux tourbillonne autour de l: A furious wind swirls around the Citadel: Ventaile refuses to go near. Land on the Wind Perch, south of the island.
A furious wind swirls around the Citadel: you can't get near it. Land on the Wind Field, south of the island.
textes.Un ventilateur, Papa ! Pour les rondes d: A fan, Dad! For summer rounds!
textes.Un ver de terre, vexé d'avoir été dérang: An earthworm, offended at being disturbed. It leaves with a sigh (for a worm).
textes.Un verre ? Ha ! Voilà qui cause bien. À: A drink? Ha! Now you're talking. Cheers, sailor!
textes.Un verre d'eau du ciel ? Il en est tombé: A glass of sky water? Plenty of it fell today.
textes.Un verre de rhum de la Murène: A glass of La Murène dark tonic
A glass of tea, Lou? It's good for you.
textes.Un verrou de moins ! Regarde-le, il comm: One lock down! Look at it, it's starting to sweat.
An empty one. For the fountain.
textes.Un vieil ampli à lampes, lourd comme un: An old tube amp, heavy as a donkey, with knobs that go up to eleven. When you switch it on, it purrs. When Clou plays, it roars.
textes.Un vieux coffre cerclé de fer, fermé par: An old iron-bound chest, shut with a chain of bones. It won't give. On the lid, engraved: “To whoever carries my map. B.S.”
textes.Un vieux coquillage, apporté là par un o: An old seashell, brought here by a mischievous bird. This head looks at the sea, not the sky.
textes.Un vieux marin de Hautefond, Léon, est d: An old sailor from Hautefond, Léon, came down “to see if it's wet”. He touched the glass of the tube and looked at his finger. Dry. He said “Hm.” Then he sat on the bench for two hours watching the fish. On his way out, he said “Hm” again. But more softly.
textes.Un vieux marin te le dira : au fond des: Any old sailor will tell you: deep in the Nine Circles, on the Acheron, there's a ferryman. Charon. He gives no credit. One obol, just one, and he takes you across. Never forget to pay the ferryman, cabin boy. It's the first law of every sea.
textes.Un vieux marin, à la pension, m'a dit un: An old sailor at the guesthouse told me one evening: “The most beautiful light in the archipelago is in Tazira, around six o'clock.” I packed a bag for a week. I took a cargo boat, sitting between crates of lemons. That was four months ago. The week isn't over. I don't think it ever will be.
textes.Un vieux parchemin offert par Églantine,: An old parchment given by Églantine, the freed Bramble Queen. It shows the passage through the reefs and the ashes, to the west, all the way to the dwarves' volcanic island.
textes.Un vieux parchemin taché de rhum : une c: An old stained parchment: a coastline, dotted lines, a red cross. Captain Salazar Croc-de-Sel cares about it more than his wooden leg.
An old professor is looking for you.
textes.Un virus ? Dans MES programmes ? Impossi: A virus? In MY programs? Impossible! They're guaranteed. Guaranteed… something. (He looks away.) Go see little Glitch: she knows about… about things. Mornings and evenings, she hangs around near the Arcade Station; in the afternoon, in the arcade hall. Me, I have an appointment. Very far away. Right now.
textes.Un virus ? Dans MON programme ? (Il devi: A virus? In MY program? (He turns all red, then all purple, to match his hat.) Well. All right. Maybe. I bought it from a dealer even cheaper than me, and I hadn't tried it… I'm giving you your coins back, with an apology on top. And I make you a promise: from now on, Monsieur Fil will only sell verified programs! Verified by Glitch. She said yes. Well, she said “we'll see”. It's almost yes.
textes.Un visage de roi fait de centaines de pe: A king's face made of hundreds of little squares of jade, with eyes of mother-of-pearl and obsidian. The mask of the kings of Yaxché, kept deep in Xibalba. Its place is on the Altar of the Three Suns.
textes.Un visiteur ! D'où viens-tu ? Non, atten: A visitor! Where are you from? No, wait, let me guess… from the west, by sea, eh? Matthias, cartographer. I've been drawing this island for fifteen years and it still isn't finished.
textes.Un visiteur ! À inscrire ! Au registre !: A visitor! To be registered! In the register! (He opens an immense book, which falls on his foot.) Ahem ahem. According to article twelve, I write your name in lumen letters... There. According to article thirteen, you must now curtsy. No, not like that. Not like that either. According to article fourteen... Ah, there is no article fourteen. Well. You're registered. Congratulations. That was very protocolary.
textes.Un visiteur a posé à l'Hologuide une que: A visitor asked the Hologuide a question that wasn't in the tour, and it rebooted. I ran over and told the visitor: “It's not a bug, it's shyness.” Then I gave it a backup line: “Excellent question, come back tomorrow.” It says it very well. With great confidence.
textes.Un visiteur m'a demandé quelque chose qu: A visitor asked me something that wasn't on the tour. I rebooted. Professor Quasar came running and told the visitor: “It's not a bug, it's shyness.” Then he added a sentence for me: “Excellent question, come back tomorrow.” I say it often.
A sailboat flies away very easily.
textes.Un volcan ! BOUM ! SPLOTCH ! Tu craches: A volcano! BOOM! SPLAT! You spit sauce all over everyone! So cool! But Nonna's going to shout.
textes.Un voyageur ! Bienvenue à Pandémonia, la: A traveller! Welcome to Pandémonia, the hottest of cities! I am Ignatia, Archduchess of Ember Island. No, don't bow: Asmodin will do it for both of us. He adores it.
textes.Un voyageur arrive à la Gare des Nuées :: A traveller arrives at Cloud Station: “It's high up here!” Théo, delighted: “Wait till you see the Belvedere. It's high AND see-through.”
textes.Un voyageur d'en haut demande à Marius :: A traveller from up top asks Marius: “What time does the sun rise down here?” Marius checks his watch: “When Yolande presses the button.”
textes.Un voyageur d'en haut sort de la cabine: A traveller from up top steps out of the cabin: “It's so gloomy down here!” Anatole, delighted: “What? You want a room?”
textes.Un voyageur entre dans la cabine : « Ça: A traveller steps into the cabin: “Going up?” Barnabé, white as a sheet: “For you, yes. For my stomach, it's going down.”
textes.Un vrai ! Enfin… presque. La capitaine d: A real one! Well… almost. The captain says I'll be a pirate the day I can tie a bowline with my eyes shut. I can almost do it. With my eyes open.
textes.Un vrai ! Les pieds, c'est la base : le: A real one! Feet are the foundation: the kick comes up through the sand and out through your knees. Stand in front of Raoul, the big speaker, and you'll get it.
textes.Un vrai ! Punch du héros pour le héros !: A real one! Hero's punch for the hero!
textes.Un vrai chapiteau sur la place du villag: A real big top on the village square, red and yellow, with benches for every kid on the island. And Yaya's cat in the front row. He'll pay in purrs.
textes.Un vrai exploit, ami. Un seul. Avec du s: A real exploit, friend. Just one. With sunshine. And then I'll follow you everywhere.
textes.Un vrai matelot est toujours mouillé !: A real sailor is always wet!
textes.Un éboulement bloque la galerie. Au-delà: A rockfall blocks the gallery. Beyond it, you can hear water flowing… You'll have to find another way. (Work in progress!)
A failure, but a pretty one.
textes.Un éclat de cristal qui bat doucement, c: A shard of crystal that beats gently, like a heart. It is warm, and it sings a single, very pure note.
textes.Un éclat de glace bleue qui ne fond jama: A shard of blue ice that never melts, even in your hand, even in Pandémonia. It comes from the Cocytus, the frozen lake of the Ninth Circle.
textes.Un éclat de la grande lentille s'est dét: A shard of the great lens broke off during the storm. It fell into the sea, at the foot of the point, on the seaward side. Six metres down, maybe. I'm too old to dive. Without it, my lighthouse no longer lights the night.
textes.Un éclat rose et tiède, laissé par une a: A pink, warm shard, left behind by a crystal spider. Grommelot the sprite collects them; Mélisse buys them.
textes.Un écusson brodé : un rat à crête verte: An embroidered patch: a yelling green-crested rat, and "BILGE RATS" in red letters. Velours sews them herself, one by one, for the true fans.
textes.Un élixir doré qui pétille comme un ciel: A golden elixir that sparkles like a summer sky. It restores all your magic, and two hearts. Gustave won't say what he puts in it.
textes.Un élémentaire de magma ! Quand il gonfl: A magma elemental! When it swells up and glows red, it's going to leap at you: step aside, then strike while it cools.
textes.Un étal à Tazira, juste à côté de celui: A stall in Tazira, right next to Aïcha's, so we can steal each other's customers face to face. It would be wonderful. Every evening we'd both close up with less money and more stories.
textes.Un été, Lentille m'a convaincue d'invent: One summer, Lentille talked me into inventing soup-lemonade with him: a cold mint soup, with bubbles. It went “pschhh” in the bowls. Everyone tasted it politely. Then everyone ordered a normal soup and a normal lemonade. I don't talk about it any more. He does.
textes.Un été, Sirène et moi avons inventé la s: One summer, Sirène and I invented lemonade soup. A cold mint soup with bubbles. It went “pschhh” in the bowls. People tasted it politely. Then they asked for a normal soup and a normal lemonade. We never spoke of it again.
textes.Un été, il n'a pas plu pendant deux mois: One summer, it didn't rain for two months. My plants were frying on the hill. So I carried water up, bucket by bucket, morning and evening. On the third day, Amélie, the herbalist, saw me go by and picked up a bucket, without a word. She came up with me all summer. My lavender survived, and so did her thyme. And I gained a friend.
textes.Un été, j'ai pisté vers l'ouest. Plus lo: One summer, I tracked westward. Further than ever. All the way to the foot of Stoneheart, in the centre of the island. There, the tracks of all four peoples arrive: boots, hooves, paws, wheels. All very old. Then nothing. I sat a whole night in front of that nothing. I understood that the world was bigger than Ramure. And that it had forgotten something.
textes.Un été, la sauce a commencé à coller au: One summer, the sauce started sticking to the bottom of the Cooking Pot. The volcano rumbled, spat, got angry. I went down to the rim with the big ladle and stirred. Three days and three nights. It calmed down. Since then, I stir every day. You stir a volcano like a sauce: gently, and often.
textes.Un été, les tomates de Radis ont attrapé: One summer, Radis's tomatoes caught a disease. Spotted all over. He didn't ask me for anything, he's too proud. I came with some moss from the Cathedral and laid it at the foot of the plants. Within a week, they were cured. He thanked me. Then he told me my pumpkin cheated all the same.
textes.Un été, mes tomates ont attrapé une mala: One summer, my tomatoes caught a disease. Spotted all over. I was in despair. Mother Morille came without my calling her, with some moss from the Cathedral. She laid it at the foot of the plants. Within a week, they were cured. I thanked her. Then I told her that her pumpkin cheated all the same.
textes.Un œil d'or et de lapis-lazuli, l'œil qu: An eye of gold and lapis lazuli, the eye the god Horus lost fighting Set and that Thoth healed: the sign of the light that always comes back. Brought back from the depths of the Pyramid of Ra. Its place is on the Altar of the Three Suns.
textes.Un œil de pierre… Les petits Moaïs du pl: A stone eye… The little Moai on the plateau might know who it belongs to. (The eldest, Granny Basalte, knows all the legends.)
textes.Un, deux, trois ! Un, deux, trois !: One, two, three! One, two, three!
textes.Un, deux, trois, BOUCAN ! On ne lâche ri: One, two, three, BOUCAN! We're not giving an inch!
One, two, three… Right. Starting again.
textes.Un, deux, trois… Vas-y, je suis prêt !: One, two, three… Go on, I'm ready!
textes.Un, deux, un, deux… Oh ! Salut. Mégaphon: One, two, one, two… Oh! Hi. Mégaphone, sound engineer. I'm tuning the mixing desk. Can you hear it? No? Normal: there's nobody on stage. But the day there is, the sound will be perfect.
textes.Un, deux… Tu m'entends ?: One, two… Can you hear me?
textes.Un, deux… Tu veux essayer le micro, {sur: One, two… Want to try the mic, {surnom}? What would you say?
textes.Un, deux… trois ! Tous les soirs, mainte: One, two… three! Every evening, now. And the button in the middle, I named it after you. Don't tell anyone, I have a reputation as a serious stage manager.
textes.Un, deux… trois et demi…: One, two… three and a half…
textes.Un, deux… — Trois ! Ha ! Tu t'en souvien: One, two… — Three! Ha! You remember!
textes.Une Grande Course qui ferait le tour de: A Great Race that went all the way round the island! Then a wolf would win, for sure. I can feel it in my paws. And I'd put the cup right at the top of the watch post, right next to my uncle.
textes.Une Grande Course, elle est passée devan: One Great Race, she went past the jetty, in the lead, so fast the water shivered. I stood up. Me. I shouted her name. My rod went into the pond, with the line and the float. I never found it. The King must have it. He can keep it. It was a good day.
textes.Une Grande Lanterne éteinte, aussi haute: An unlit Great Lantern, as tall as a giant's street lamp. To light it, you'd need a flame from a living ember: Lumina, the lantern-keeper, keeps some in her lantern.
textes.Une Gratuiterie sur chaque île de l'arch: A Free Shop on every island in the archipelago. So things can travel from one island to the next, and one day, my flowery teapot will come back from Port-Azur, with stories from over there.
textes.Une Série Z… « Voix numéro zéro ». La to: A Z Series… “Voice number zero”. The city's very first android voice. Cargo kept it all this time. (He cleans it, blows on it, examines it through the lens of his monocle.) It works. I set Zéro up on my workbench, he was waiting. Click. There. Go and see him… I think he has something to tell you.
textes.Une VILLE ? Toute une ville ? Avec des m: A TOWN? A whole town? With houses and everything? Kiki says I'll make one too. Will you teach me? I'll give you my coconuts.
textes.Une VRAIE vieille botte ?! Avec le trou: A REAL old boot?! With the hole at the end?! Wonderful! I'll put it next to my other treasures. Here, it pays well!
textes.Une abeille m'a regardée. Je l'ai regard: A bee looked at me. I looked at it. We're friends now.
textes.Une affaire de dos, docteur. Rien à sign: A back matter, doctor. Nothing to report.
textes.Une affiche : « LES TAUPES HURLANTES — c: A poster: “THE HOWLING MOLES — concert Saturday — admission: one cake”
textes.Une affiche du Grand Boucan, de la part: A poster for the Great Boucan, from Port-Boucan!
textes.Une affiche du Grand Boucan, pour le Crâ: A poster for the Great Boucan, for the Crâne Fendu!
textes.Une affiche du Grand Boucan, pour votre: A poster for the Great Boucan, for your inn!
textes.Une affiche sérigraphiée, encore odorant: A screen-printed poster that still smells of ink: a green-crested rat yells into a microphone, and in dancing letters: "THE GREAT BOUCAN — THE BILGE RATS — FREE, LOUD, AND FULL OF LOVE". To take to the other islands.
textes.Une amitié… Oh. Ça n'a pas d'engrenage,: A friendship… Oh. That has no gears. No crank, no axle. And yet… Right. I'm going to blow my nose. It's the steam.
textes.Une amulette de faïence bleue en forme d: A blue faience amulet shaped like a scarab, its underside engraved with little signs. The scarab is Khepri, the morning sun reborn. Ptahmose carves them; they say they bring luck.
textes.Une amulette de pierre verte en forme de: An amulet of green stone in the shape of a face, warm under your fingers: a piece of the body of Osiris, which Set had scattered. Four of them are needed for the sarcophagus of Osiris.
textes.Une ancre ? Classique. Solide. Ça ne se: An anchor? Classic. Solid. Never goes out of style. Do you know what it means? That you always come back somewhere. And you, where will you come back to?
textes.Une ancre tatouée sur l'avant-bras : les: An anchor tattooed on your forearm: the pirates of the Balafre pick on you a little less.
textes.Une ancre, sur l'avant-bras. Simple, sol: An anchor, on your forearm. Simple, sturdy, like you. Don't move… (bzzzt, bzzzt…) There. Show it at the counter: around here, folks who wear my mark get picked on a little less.
textes.Une année entière sans crocodile. Une se: A whole year without a crocodile. Just one. And a field of flax in bloom all the way to the plateau, all blue, that Tiyi would come to see. She'd say: “What a blue.” That would please me.
textes.Une année, il m'a annoncé l'équinoxe pou: One year, he told me the equinox would be the next day. I sat at the foot of the staircase all day, in festival clothes, with the whole village. No serpent. The serpent came down the day after. Ah Kin Pech said: “My count was right. The sun was late.” He said it seriously.
textes.Une année, j'ai annoncé l'équinoxe pour: One year, I announced the equinox for the next day. She waited all day at the foot of the stairs, in her festival clothes, with the whole village. Nothing. The serpent came down the day after. I explained that my calculations were right and the sun was late. She looked at me. I have never seen such a long look.
textes.Une année, j'ai essayé de lui troquer mo: One year, I tried to swap him my carpet that doesn't fly. “A Tazira carpet, my friend, come home!” Mbarek looked at the carpet, then at me, for a very long time. He said: “It doesn't fly.” I said: “Exactly, it'll never fly away.” He didn't take it. But under his veil, I saw something move. Almost a smile.
textes.Une année, j'ai fait la plus belle jarre: One year, I made the most beautiful jar of my life. Blue as the lake in the morning, with perfect fangs. We carried it to the shrine, full of water. That very evening, it started to rain. Three days. The lake rose, Xóchitl's beans drifted away, Citlali's codex got wet. Everyone looked at me. I said: “It's a compliment.”
textes.Une année, j'ai glissé dans la chope un: One year, I slipped a ruby of my own into the mug, a little one, found in a pebble in the cellar. He counted three hundred and sixty-six. He looked at me for a long time. He never resold that one: he keeps it in a little box. He thinks I don't know. I know everything.
textes.Une année, j'avais perdu la voix, un vil: One year, I'd lost my voice, a nasty cold. I had to speak at the council. I told Saïd: “Repeat what I whisper to you.” He started. Then he carried on by himself. Two hours. He settled three quarrels I didn't even know about. When my voice came back, I had to settle them a second time.
textes.Une année, la borne de Hapou avait avanc: One year, Hapou's boundary stone had moved a cubit towards the neighbouring field. All by itself, during the night, if he's to be believed. I took out my cord, I measured three times, I put the stone back in its place. Hapou said the crocodile had pushed it. The crocodile, indeed, was wearing sandals. His.
textes.Une année, la caravane du safran s'est p: One year, the saffron caravan got lost in the chergui. Not a single thread left in Tazira. I had one jar left. Just one! So I counted the pinches: one for every bride, one for every newborn, and one, every Friday, for Zohra's tajine. Nobody got more, nobody went without. Since then, they've called me the keeper of the saffron.
textes.Une année, la crue est montée plus haut: One year, the flood rose higher than ever. The water came into the House of Life in the middle of the night. I carried the scrolls up to the roof until dawn, with a little seven-year-old apprentice who carried the smallest ones: Néferet. Four hundred and twelve scrolls saved. Nine lost. I still know their titles. Sometimes I recite them, so that they exist a little.
textes.Une année, la pluie n'est pas venue. Le: One year, the rain didn't come. The maize was drying up, the water of the Cenote was dropping. My mother was ill. So, every morning, alone, I poured cacao and copal into the Cenote, and I prayed to the rain gods. On the ninth morning, the sky rumbled. It rained for three days. My mother passed away at the end of that year. The temple came to me.
textes.Une année, la veille de l'Aïd, un plat m: One year, the day before Eid, a badly dried dish burst in the kiln. Bang! The whole festival batch, broken: the dishes, the jugs, the cups. I cried for an hour. Then we remade everything in three nights, my mother at the wheel, me with the clay, and Zohra holding the lamp and singing out of tune. On the morning of Eid, everything was ready. Not a crack. Since then, I never leave anything half-dried.
textes.Une année, le bateau des pains de glace: One year, the ice-block boat didn't come. Three weeks! In the middle of summer! I buried my tubs in the wet sand, at the back of the cave, under seaweed. Every morning, I dug them up like a pirate digging up his treasure. The season was saved. And the sergeant was already coming for three a day. State secret, eh.
textes.Une année, le chergui a soufflé trois jo: One year, the chergui blew for three days. Forty caravan drivers stuck at the Fondouk, the courtyard full of camels, sand right into the glasses. Zineb and I served tea all night, side by side. Not a word about the fourth glass. In the morning, she said thank you. Once. I remember it like a holiday.
textes.Une année, ma borne avait avancé d'une c: One year, my boundary stone had moved a cubit. It happens, with the flood. Amenemhat took out his cord, measured three times, and put it back. I said the crocodile had pushed it. He said the crocodile was wearing sandals. There were sandal prints. Mine. That's not proof.
textes.Une année, un grand vent est venu de la: One year, a great wind came from the sea. It tore off the roofs, knocked over the hives, scattered the bees. The next day, there was nothing left but empty logs. I cried like a child. Then I went off into the jungle. A whole moon. I found wild swarms, one by one, and I carried them back in my arms. They trusted me.
textes.Une année, à la fête, j'ai compté trois: One year, at the festival, I counted three hundred and sixty-six rubies. One too many. I thought she'd miscounted. She winked at me. I never found out where the last one came from. I put it away separately, in a little box. It's the only ruby I've never weighed.
textes.Une antenne de radio tordue, faite d'un: A bent radio antenna, made from an old rake, a coat hanger and lots of sticky tape. It picks up everything: radio waves, the wind, and sometimes the seagulls' conversations.
textes.Une araignée de cristal ! Elle se dresse: A crystal spider! It rears up before biting: back off or parry (F). Its shards are surely of interest to someone…
textes.Une araignée dorée m'a piquée, une seule: A golden spider bit me, just once in my life. I was so embarrassed that I went to Aëlwen's hiding my hand. She treated me without asking a thing, then she said: “He played till dawn, didn't he?” She sees everything too. From her counter.
textes.Une arme ? Garde-la : dans la jungle et: A weapon? Keep it: in the jungle and under the temples, you'll need it.
textes.Une arme ? Garde-la pour les pirates. En: A weapon? Keep it for the pirates. Well… not too hard, they pay well.
textes.Une arme ? Garde-la, {surnom}. Dans les: A weapon? Keep it, {surnom}. In the Nine Circles, you'll need it more than I do.
textes.Une arme ? Garde-la, {surnom}. Dehors, e: A weapon? Keep it, {surnom}. Out there, between the slimes and the goblins, you'll need it far more than I will.
textes.Une arme ? Garde-la, {surnom}. Ici, le p: A weapon? Keep it, {surnom}. The most dangerous thing around here is the ticket office queue. And it isn't afraid of swords.
A weapon? Keep it, {surnom}. The most dangerous thing down here is the steam hammer. And it doesn't fight: it works.
A weapon? Keep it, {surnom}. Up here, the most dangerous thing is the west wind. And it isn't afraid of swords.
