textes.Une arme ? Garde-la, {surnom}. Ici, on r: A weapon? Keep it, {surnom}. Here, we settle everything at the Assembly, with words and a herbal tea. It takes longer. But it holds better.
textes.Une arme ? Garde-la, {surnom}. Ici, on s: A weapon? Keep it, {surnom}. Round here, we defend ourselves with human chains and songs. And against the robots, it'll be more use to you than to me.
textes.Une arme ? Garde-la, {surnom}. Ici, pers: A weapon? Keep it, {surnom}. Nobody here has ever needed one. The sharks look at us, we look at them, and everyone stays on their own side of the glass.
textes.Une arme ? Garde-la. Tu en auras besoin,: A weapon? Keep it. You'll need it, round here.
textes.Une arme ? Ici ? Non, non. Ici, on se ba: A weapon? Here? No, no. Here, the only thing we fight over is the last meatball. And even then, we share.
textes.Une arme ? Ici ? Oh non. Ici, les seules: A weapon? Here? Oh no. Here, the only sharp things are well-sharpened pencils.
textes.Une arme ? Ici, sous le dôme, personne n: A weapon? Here, under the dome, nobody fights.
textes.Une arme ? Non merci. Ici, la seule chos: A weapon? No thanks. Around here, the only thing we blow up is the sound from the amps.
textes.Une arme ? Non merci. Ici, les arbres no: A weapon? No, thank you. Here, the trees keep us safe.
textes.Une arme ? Non merci. Ici, on a des croc: A weapon? No thanks. Here we've got fangs and claws, and we only use them on hazelnuts.
textes.Une arme ? Non merci. Sur Astralys, la c: A weapon? No thank you. On Astralys, the pointiest thing is the Crystal Spire. And it doesn't hurt anyone.
textes.Une arme ? Non merci. À Néopolis, on se: A weapon? No thanks. In Neopolis, we fight at Dragon-Pixel, nothing else.
textes.Une arme ? Non, merci. Ici, on invente d: A weapon? No, thank you. Here, we invent things that don't hurt anyone. Except Professor Boum, but that's unintentional.
textes.Une arme ? Non. Je n'en ai pas besoin, e: A weapon? No. I don't need one, and the Tree doesn't like iron.
textes.Une arme ? On en a plein la sainte-barbe: A weapon? We've got a powder room full of them. Keep it, you'll need it.
textes.Une arme ? On en a plein les cales, des: A weapon? We've got holds full of weapons. Keep it.
textes.Une arme ? Range ça. Ici, on se bat avec: A weapon? Put that away. Here, we fight with words. And sometimes with fireballs, but only on Tuesdays.
textes.Une arme ? Range-moi ça, on est en vacan: A weapon? Put that away, we're on holiday here.
textes.Une arme qui n'est pas forgée ici ? Non: A weapon not forged here? No thanks.
textes.Une arme, dans le palais ? Rangez cela i: A weapon, in the palace? Put that away immediately, if you please.
textes.Une armure animée ! Elle est vide… et el: An animated suit of armor! It's empty… and it fights. When it raises its sword, parry (F) or roll (Ctrl), then strike.
textes.Une armure complète trône au milieu du s: A full suit of armor stands in the middle of the living room. Its owner gazes at it like a treasure.
textes.Une armure étincelante, polie comme un m: A gleaming suit of armor, polished like a mirror. On the breastplate, someone has engraved: “Property of Sir Fanfaron. Do not touch. Except to make it shine.”
textes.Une artiste charmante, qui voulait que j: A charming artist, who wanted me to rip up coral to make red. I've forgiven her. Halfway.
textes.Une aube, je l'ai trouvée seule au bord: One dawn, I found her alone at the edge of a pond, paws in the mud, looking for moon mushrooms for her lanterns. I was in my nightcap, I scolded her all the way back up. At the top, she said to me: “Garance used to scold exactly like that.” I didn't know what to say any more. She'd won.
textes.Une aube, je suis descendue seule jusqu': One dawn, I went down alone to a pond, looking for moon mushrooms for my lanterns. My paws were in the mud when Pivoine found me, in her nightcap. She scolded me all the way back up. I let her: Garance scolded exactly the same way, and I'd missed it.
textes.Une auberge avec une chambre pour chaque: An inn with a room for every inhabitant of the island, just in case. And one big table, just one, where Pyra and Borée would have no choice but to sit together. With the same soup. Ha!
textes.Une auberge sur la terre ferme, dans la: An inn on dry land, in the meadow Matthias drew for me, between two oaks. Twelve rooms, twelve beds, real ones, with legs. And a sign with no spelling mistakes. I've already checked it three times.
textes.Une aurore descend si bas qu'elle effleu: An aurora comes down so low it brushes the tip of the Spire. The whole Agora goes “oooh”.
textes.Une aurore dorée passe au-dessus de l'îl: A golden aurora passes over the island. The Lumens say it brings luck to whoever sees it first.
textes.Une autre ? Hm. Je respecte. Les nains d: Another one? Hm. I respect that. The dwarves of Forgefer serve a fizz, so they say… But do they have frozen lava? No. There you go. Think about it.
textes.Une autre fois, Rita m'a prédit : « Si v: Another time, Rita predicted: “If you would come tomorrow, you would have a surprise.” I couldn't help myself: “If you came, Madame Rita. No ‘would’ after ‘if’.” She looked at me for a long time: “The cards have taken note.” I came back the next day. There was no surprise. But the grammar was correct.
textes.Une autre fois, alors ! Notre porte est: Another time, then! Our door is always open. Well… you saw, you came in.
textes.Une autre fois, c'est moi qui suis allé: Another time, I was the one who went fishing at sea with him. A wave rocked the boat. I was sick as a dog. Bigorneau stole my bread while I was leaning over the side. The Captain laughed, then gave me a herbal tea and a blanket. He told me: “To each his own water, Yvon.” We don't fish together any more. We're good friends.
textes.Une autre fois, il m'a apporté une fleur: Another time, he brought me a pond flower sealed inside one of my own vials of mist. It took him three nights to get it in, his whiskers were full of mist. He said: “It'll stay fresh for as long as you want me.” I said: “No, you silly.” It's on the top shelf. Still fresh. I don't touch it.
textes.Une autre fois, je lui ai offert une pet: Another time, I gave her a little pond flower sealed inside one of her own vials of mist. Three nights to get it in: the flower didn't want to go in, the mist wanted to come out. I said: “It'll stay fresh for as long as you want me.” She said: “No, you silly.” But she kept it. Vixens… go figure.
Another story about %s? Listen to this.
Another story about %s? Listen to this.
textes.Une bague d'argent… avec une pierre bleu: A silver ring… with a blue stone! It's perfect! Here, twenty-five coins. And a song. No, don't go, it's a short one!
textes.Une bague de marin, avec une pierre bleu: A sailor's ring with a blue stone. Octave buys it for 18 coins.
textes.Une baguette ? Pas de viennoiserie ? C'e: A baguette? No pastries? Now that's serious. Raymond would adore you. He says the baguette is real bread, and the rest is dessert.
textes.Une baguette croustillante de Margaux. O: A crusty baguette from Margaux. Half of it gets eaten before you reach home. Restores two hearts.
textes.Une baguette de fée en bois de sureau, t: A fairy wand of elderwood, tipped with a crystal star. Pimprenelle lost it in the Cave of the Jumping Mushrooms.
A whale, two seagulls and Tapage.
textes.Une ballade… une chanson qu'on chante to: A ballad… a song you sing very softly, under the duvet. I can picture it.
A ball that swears. Now I've seen everything.
textes.Une banane de Marley et un croissant de: A banana from Marley and a croissant from Fanny, Grandpa.
textes.Une banane des fées ?! C'est un signe, ç: A fairy banana?! That's a sign, that is!
textes.Une barque ! Alors tu sais. Le bois qui: A boat! Then you know. The wood that won't cooperate, the nails that go in crooked, and the day she floats… You have all my respect. And one question: did she float straight?
textes.Une barque, c'est déjà un bateau, frère: A rowboat's still a boat, bro! Moor it at my little jetty, it's free for you. And if one day you want something bigger, I've got pedalos. The “Gérard” is very stable.
textes.Une barque, c'est vingt jours de travail: A boat is twenty days' work. We paint it blue, because blue keeps away the evil eye. And because we have a lot of blue paint.
A boat. With a plane. Come.
textes.Une barque. Une vraie. En bois. Copeau d: A rowing boat. A real one. Wooden. Copeau says he'll make me one. I believe him. And fish from it, at sunrise. Without a word.
textes.Une belle erreur. Je la raconte encore à: A beautiful mistake. I still tell it at the party. Yep.
textes.Une berceuse… C'est ce que ma mère chant: A lullaby… That's what my mother used to sing. You must have been a very loved child.
textes.Une bergerie sous la montagne ? Montrez-: A sheepfold beneath the mountain? Show me… Sheep, a cogwheel, a ridge. But I know it! With my big spyglass, I can see the whole north slope of the Stoneheart. Southeast of the city, at the foot of the mountain, there's a cave: the Wind Sheepfold, the shepherds call it. They haven't gone there since black brambles blocked the entrance. Brambles that won't burn, it seems… Well, that won't burn with an ordinary lighter.
textes.Une bibliothèque immense pour une si pet: An immense library for such a small house. One of the books, all red, sticks out a little.
textes.Une bibliothécaire d'en haut, Mademoisel: A librarian from up top, Miss Philippine, drew a map of the Fronde without ever seeing it, just from Ysaé's words. I've seen the map. There are mistakes everywhere. And it's the most beautiful map in the world. I'm going to paint it on the Wall. Mistakes and all.
textes.Une bijoutière de la Fronde, Lumi, dit q: A jeweller from the Fronde, Lumi, says the Column is a necklace: four pearls on a single thread. The Clouds, Hautefond, the Strata, and us, right at the end. The bottom pearl, the one that holds the thread. I wrote it up big on my board. People stop to read it again.
textes.Une blague ? … Un canonnier entre dans u: A joke? … A gunner walks into a tavern. BOOM. The end.
textes.Une bombe de peinture faite maison par P: A homemade spray can by Pigment (made with beetroot, spinach or blueberry: it smells a bit like soup). In front of a paintable wall in Port-Boucan (the Expression Wall, bare walls): E to paint a graffiti.
A good mug of fizz before the fight.
textes.Une bonne nouvelle, rien que pour toi :: Some good news, just for you: the ball says you'll come back to see me. See? It's right.
textes.Une bonne nuit de sommeil… Tous vos cœur: A good night's sleep… All your hearts are back.
textes.Une bonne soupe ! Ah, toi, tu as tout co: A good soup! Ah, you've understood everything. Soup is everyone in the same bowl. Come on, Excalibur will serve you.
A good hot bowl of soup.
textes.Une botte de pêcheur, pointure quarante-: A fisherman's boot, size thirteen: the biggest catch of the season, I stand by it. I took it back to my caravan, filled it with soil, and planted thyme in it, with a label: “Prediction fulfilled”. Mathurin walks past it grumbling. The thyme grows magnificently. He takes a sprig sometimes, when he thinks I'm not looking.
textes.Une botte de spaghettis séchés au Séchoi: A bundle of spaghetti dried at the Drying Shed of Al Dente Island, made with durum wheat from its fields. Tied with a green, white and red ribbon.
textes.Une bouillabaisse sans pain, c'est une o: A bouillabaisse without bread is an orphan. Margaux's bread makes it less of an orphan. One morning, Raymond didn't come: his sprain. I served the soup without bread for ten minutes. Ten minutes of mourning, my friend. The customers stared at their plates like widows.
textes.Une boule de feu : elle brûle les ennemi: A fireball: it burns enemies and brambles, lights braziers and torches.
textes.Une boule de feu qui file droit devant :: A fireball that flies straight ahead: it burns enemies and lights braziers and torches.
A ball of light follows you for a minute. It lights up the dark and wakes sleeping runes.
textes.Une bourrasque te rattrape et te repose: A gust catches you and sets you down on the Wind Perch.
textes.Une bourse de cuir rouge brodée d'une ve: A red leather purse embroidered with a black widow spider, heavy with forty coins: Gontran Lestrange's debt to Mama Grog.
textes.Une bourse de poussière qui scintille de: A pouch of dust that sparkles in every colour, found in the chest of the Fairy Garden. Lumi says you'll need a lot of it to get past the brambles.
textes.Une boussole de verre dont l'aiguille, e: A glass compass whose little cloud-shaped needle always points to the nearest cloud. Very handy for meteorologists. Slightly less so for everyone else.
textes.Une boussole qui indique le sud. Des deu: A compass that points south. At both ends. So you never get lost heading south.
textes.Une boutique au bout des jardins du nord: A shop at the end of the northern gardens, right by the sea, with my bottles lined up in the sun. And customers who pay without haggling. Especially that.
textes.Une boutique si grande qu'on s'y perdrai: A shop so big you'd get lost in it, with an object from every island in the archipelago and, on each one, a label telling its journey. No prices. Just the journeys.
textes.Une boutique à Carène, chez Salomé, une: A shop in Carène, at Salomé's, another in Port-Azur, and the whole archipelago smelling of saffron! May sailors smell it before they even see the coast!
textes.Une boîte à musique qui joue la marche d: A music box that plays the Liftkeepers' March… backwards. It sounds like a lullaby. It's almost better.
textes.Une branche de corail rouge du fond de l: A branch of red coral from the bottom of the bay. Ground up, it makes a brilliant pigment.
textes.Une branche solide. Servira à fabriquer: A sturdy branch. Good for making tools.
A brioche, Grandpa. A real one.
textes.Une brioche. … Ce n'est pas un remède. C: A brioche. … That is not a remedy. That is not a remedy at all. Bobor would be delighted. I am dismayed. And a little jealous.
textes.Une brume épaisse, dorée… Le bateau tour: A thick, golden mist… The boat goes round in circles and comes out where it started. You'd need a guide to get through.
textes.Une bulle ? Deux bulles ? Trois mille bu: One bubble? Two bubbles? Three thousand bubbles a minute! Basile Bulle, inventor. My machine makes the finest bubbles in the archipelago. They're good for nothing, and that's what's beautiful about them.
textes.Une bulle assez grande pour y installer: A bubble big enough to fit Margot inside, with a cushion and her notebook. I'd float her over the city, ever so gently, across the rooftops, all the way to the roof of Céleste's observatory. And up there, for once, I'd be the one counting the stars.
textes.Une bulle de Cradoc m'a emportée, une fo: One of Cradoc's bubbles carried me off once. I floated over the whole town. I came back down all shiny. Never again. Well, maybe.
textes.Une cabane ! C'est un début honnête. Qua: A hut! That's an honest start. Four walls, a roof, and you sleep dry. A boat is the same, but upside down, and the water has to stay outside.
textes.Une cabane ! Dans un arbre ! (Ses yeux b: A hut! In a tree! (Her eyes shine.) A tree is almost round. And it sways with the wind. I need to think about that.
textes.Une cabane tout en haut du plus grand ar: A hut at the very top of the tallest tree in the jungle. Higher than Octave's. I'd go up just once, to see the look on his face from above. Then I'd come back down, quick.
textes.Une cabane, c'est une barque à l'envers: A hut is an upside-down boat that doesn't move. Not bad. The roof, how did you do it? … Lay the planks overlapping, like scales, like a hull. The rain will slide right off.
textes.Une cabine à la fois, s'il vous plaît !: One cabin at a time, please!
textes.Une caisse de pommes pour le bateau de l: A crate of apples for the ferry!
textes.Une canette glacée sortie d'un distribut: An ice-cold can from a Neopolis vending machine. "Sparkling Moon Fruit": nobody knows what moon fruit tastes like, but it's good. It glows a little in the dark. Restores one heart.
textes.Une capitaine de dirigeable, la Capitain: An airship captain, Captain Héloïse, came down to see the Little Diver. She walked around the Pool three times. Then she said to me: “You fly upside down.” I thought that was so beautiful I wrote it on the hull. In felt-tip. Yolande wiped it off. I wrote it again. That's where we're at.
textes.Une carte ! Évidemment ! (Il serre son c: A map! Of course! (He hugs his journal to his chest.) You're a person of taste. Take mine, they're accurate. Almost all of them.
textes.Une carte ? De la surface ? Ha ! Je vais: A card? From the surface? Ha! I'll hang it behind my counter. The lads are going to be jealous.
textes.Une carte ? Pour moi ? Personne ne m'a é: A card? For me? Nobody has written to me since… Gaston, look, a card! There's a lighthouse on it. I'll nail it up above my hammock.
textes.Une carte de Sésame sentait le sable cha: One of Sésame's cards smelled of hot sand, so strongly that my satchel kept the smell for a week. Grelot sniffed it for a long time, eyes closed. She said: “She's in a desert. Or in a cake.” With Sésame, you never know. There was no return address. There never is.
textes.Une carte de cuir épais, à ton nom, avec: A card of thick leather, with your name, your portrait (very lifelike, except the nose) and the letter of your rank in a red circle. Églantine stamps it for every contract completed. Clac, the stamp, has left its mark on it.
A map of the island covered in arrows. Above the Great Column, someone has written: “Never fly over at four o'clock: Firmin's hot chocolate whistles, and it gets bumpy.”
textes.Une carte de tante Sésame est arrivée un: One day a card from Aunt Sésame arrived, all warped, and it smelled of hot sand. No town name, just a drawing: a camel wearing a bell. Plumette handed it to me saying: “Hoo. This one's come a long way.” I sniffed that card all day. So did my uncle, on the sly.
textes.Une carte des Récifs de Feu ? Les nains: A map of the Fire Reefs? The dwarves! They pay in gold, they do. If you get into Forgefer, mention me: Octave Taillefer, honest trader. Well… trader.
textes.Une carte des courants d'air de l'archip: A map of the archipelago's air currents. A red cross, right at the far edge: “Red balloon spotted here. H. N.” Captain Héloïse is still looking for it.
textes.Une carte du ciel dessinée à l'encre de: A sky map drawn in ink of light: the stars move gently across it, in time with the real ones.
textes.Une carte postale de Port-Azur : le phar: A postcard from Port-Azur: the lighthouse, the bay, and on the back, Nadine's round handwriting.
textes.Une carte postale de Port-Azur pour vous: A postcard from Port-Azur for you!
textes.Une carte sans blanc. Toute l'île, de la: A map with no blanks. The whole island, from the sea to the mists, and Stoneheart in the middle, drawn from the inside. I'll sign it bottom right, with the name of whoever helped me. In bigger letters than mine, maybe.
textes.Une carte stellaire ? Pour un glisseur ?: A star chart? For a glider? (He pulls a scroll from his bag and unrolls it: stars drawn in ink of light, moving gently.) I made it for myself, but I never fly. I get dizzy above three steps. Take it. North is at the top. Well… on this chart, north moves a little. Like the stars. Trust the stars, they know the way.
textes.Une cave pleine de pots de confiture. De: A cellar full of jam jars. Hundreds. There's even a jam made of… pickles?
textes.Une cave à fromages ! Des dizaines de me: A cheese cellar! Dozens of wheels… and a smell that would make an onion cry.
A flying chair! I'll write that down.
textes.Une chambre ? Dis-moi d'abord, {surnom}: A room? Tell me first, {surnom}: do you prefer sleeping on the sea side, or the desert side?
textes.Une chambre ? Il y en a une sous les toi: A room? There's one under the eaves, with a skylight. You can see the stars from it. Aurélien says it's the best room on the island for dreaming.
textes.Une chambre dans la pénombre. Sous la co: A dimly lit bedroom. Under the quilt, someone snores peacefully.
textes.Une chambre douce et chaude. Près du feu: A soft, warm room. By the fire, an anvil-shaped cradle. A dwarf woman knits, very, very softly.
textes.Une chambre sous les toits pour la nuit: A room under the eaves for the night
textes.Une chambre sur la terrasse pour la nuit: A room on the terrace for the night
textes.Une chambre à ressorts pour la nuit: A room with springs for the night
textes.Une champignonnière secrète ! Des champi: A secret mushroom farm! Mushrooms everywhere… and some of them glow in the dark.
textes.Une chanson de marin, alors ! Une, deux,: A sea shanty, then! One, two, three!
textes.Une chanson pour Mamie Barricade, sur la: A song for Mamie Barricade, up on the mezzanine! “Studded Scarf”! HANDS IN THE AIR!
textes.Une chanson pour ceux qui n'ont pas de m: A song for those who have no home, and for those who have one to share! “The Door Fell Down In '98”!
textes.Une chanson toute neuve, on ne l'a jamai: A brand-new song, we've never played it, we don't know how it ends! “We'll See”! ONE, TWO, THREE, FOUR!
textes.Une chatte rousse et blanche te regarde: A red and white cat watches you from the very top of the beam, her tail curled over her paws. She won't come down for just anybody… You'd need something to interest her: Pauline's ball of wool!
textes.Une chatte tigrée rousse et blanche, trè: A very dignified ginger-and-white tabby cat lives on the rooftops of Port-Azur harbour. Every morning, she pinches a sardine from Rosalie, the fishmonger. Rosalie calls her Brioche. She'd like her to finally have someone of her own. Brioche won't let anyone come near her… except, perhaps, someone with a ball of wool.
textes.Une chaudière ne sourit pas. Montrez-moi: A boiler does not smile. Show me the valve.
textes.Une chaudière ne sourit pas. … Elle siff: A boiler doesn't smile. … It whistles in tune, I'll grant you.
textes.Une chaîne de fer noir, scellée dans un: A chain of black iron, sealed into a block of basalt by a humming blue rune: the mark of the golems. Ventaile tugs at it, exhausted. Strike the rune with a weapon to break it!
A fireplace and a good bed.
textes.Une chemise de liftier : toujours une ta: A liftkeeper's shirt: always a grease stain, always in the same place.
textes.Une chinampa avec un saule pour chaque a: A chinampa with a willow for every year of Pilli's life. When he's old, he'll have a floating forest. He'll surely get lost in it. With his dog.
textes.Une chope d'hydromel au comptoir: A mug of honey drink at the counter
textes.Une chope de bière brune et mousseuse br: A mug of dark, foamy fizz brewed beneath the mountain. Restores one and a half hearts… and warms your ears.
textes.Une chope de la Chope Ardente: A mug from the Chope Ardente
textes.Une chorale ! Le chef d'orchestre agite: A choir! The conductor waves a twig. The singers do their best. Their best is very loud.
textes.Une chouette blessée vit près de ma roul: A wounded owl lives near my caravan. She won't let anyone come near. She's waiting for someone. The ball says: someone who will know how to heal.
textes.Une chouette s'est blessée l'aile dans l: An owl hurt its wing in the Twisted Wood. It won't let anyone come near. It would need gentle hands, and an even gentler spell.
textes.Une chèvre et demie. Et une barque. Je m: One and a half goats. And a boat. I stand by it.
textes.Une cloche. Très grande. Qu'on l'entende: A bell. A very big one. So the whole misty forest can hear it, on party nights.
textes.Une clochette d'argent ! Écoute… ting !: A little silver bell! Listen… ting! See? A pebble at the start, a bell at the end, and along the way, four happy friends. That's the Great Swap. You're a real tanuki now. Here, my tanuki bell: you hang it on your belt, and all the merchants of Ramure will give you a wink.
textes.Une clé d'argent ciselée de petits hibou: A silver key engraved with little owls, found in the only chest in the Library of Mimics that doesn't bite. It opens the stairway to the top floor.
textes.Une clé de cuivre vert-de-grisé, un peu: A verdigris copper key, a little slimy: it was in the belly of a giant frog in the Underground Lake. It opens the gate on the third floor of the dungeon.
textes.Une comète, avec sa longue queue blanche: A comet, with its long white tail! It's called Lunette-3. Lunette-1 and Lunette-2 were seagulls.
textes.Une confidence, puisque tu es des nôtres: A confidence, since you are one of us. Églantine's letter arrived three days late: Zéphyr was racing Ventaile. He thinks I don't know. I've known for a hundred years. I don't hold it against him. What I can't forgive myself for is not going down sooner, without any letter. Just to see her.
textes.Une confidence, puisque tu es un ami. L': A confidence, since you're a friend. The autumn before the brambles, Grommelot had warned us: “Up north, something's growing black.” I wrote it in my book… as a riddle, for a laugh. Everyone laughed. Then winter came, and the brambles took our queen. Since then I write down everything he says, without changing a thing. Even the “hmphs”. I owe him that much.
textes.Une confidence, {surnom}. Jeune, je voul: A secret, {surnom}. When I was young, I wanted to be a guard. For the trial, Bramm made me stand in front of the Great Gate for a whole day. After six hours, I sat down on a sack of coal. Out of habit. Bramm said nothing. He just pointed at the stairs. Gunnar never found out.
textes.Une copie, faite par Amenemhat le scribe: A copy, made by Amenemhat the scribe, of the papyrus that sleeps in the pyramid: Thoth, the ibis-headed god, points to a royal cartouche. Three signs, one under the other: an ibis, an eye, a sun.
textes.Une corde de plus pour la Corderie. Il e: One more rope for the Ropeworks. They'll need plenty to stretch the festival canvas.
textes.Une corde solide, tordue à la main à la: A sturdy rope, twisted by hand at Galet's Ropeworks, with hemp from the island's fields. It smells of straw and sunshine.
textes.Une couche de plus, alors. Pour la diffé: One more coat, then. For the difference.
textes.Une couchette avec couverture et oreille: A bunk with a blanket and a pillow: when stopped, far from shore, at night, press E to sleep until morning, rocked by the waves.
textes.Une coupe sculptée dans le bois du Chêne: A cup carved from the wood of the Mother Oak, engraved with a running rabbit. Bondi kept it for three years. Now it's yours.
textes.Une couronne ! De face, cette fois !: A crown! From the front, this time!
textes.Une couronne, Majesté ! Pour toi !: A crown, Your Majesty! For you!
textes.Une course de dix arches, Grisou. Comme: A ten-arch race, Grisou. As always.
textes.Une coïncidence, mon ami ! Un autre mart: A coincidence, my friend! Another hammer!
textes.Une crique neuve ? Magnifique ! Je sors: A new cove? Magnificent! Out comes my ink!
textes.Une cuillère de miel et une histoire. Le: A spoonful of honey and a story. The hot honey, you know where it is.
textes.Une cuisine de nain : des marmites de fe: A dwarven kitchen: iron pots, enormous ladles, and an old cook humming along.
textes.Une cuisse de grenouille géante du lac,: A giant frog leg from the lake, as big as a ham. Ulric grills it with garlic at "La Grenouille Repue". Restores one and a half hearts (and tastes like chicken, apparently).
textes.Une curiosité authentique, my friend ! U: An authentic curiosity, my friend! A feather from the dwarves' giant eagle, a scale from the naga serpent of the deep… or, failing that, a shark's tooth. Bring me one and I'll pay you in gold.
textes.Une dame d'en haut avait un chapeau à pl: A lady from up top had a feathered hat. She swapped it at the Swap Shop for a bolt necklace! Lumi turned it into a lampshade. The hat, not the lady.
textes.Une date pour la bonne, professeur ?: A date for the Big One, Professor?
textes.Une de mes clientes avait les cornes qui: One of my clients had peeling horns. Nothing to do with my oil, I swear. But I panicked. I went to see Vespérine, in secret. She gave me a balm, without a word, without even a smile. I paid double. She never told anyone. I think. I hope. She's a trustworthy person.
textes.Une de mes expériences a fait sauter tou: One of my experiments blew every fuse in the Academy. I went to see Volt, my crest still smoking: “Successful experiment! I've discovered what blows fuses!” He threw me out. Then he came and fixed everything, grumbling, all night long. He left me a coffee on the blackboard.
textes.Une de mes méduses de ciel s'est posée s: One of my sky jellyfish landed on the big lens of Zénith's telescope. He called me, very embarrassed: he was seeing all the stars in pink. I went to fetch it by singing it a song. It flew off. Zénith admitted to me, later, that he rather missed the pink stars.
One fewer when you play, Roux.
One more on. One fewer to go.
textes.Une dent de tyrannosaure longue comme un: A tyrannosaurus tooth as long as an arm… made of little squares, like everything that comes from Pixelithic Island. Grosse-Dent lost it when he fell asleep. The Clan says it brings luck (as long as you don't give it back).
textes.Une dent jaune et pointue, dure comme l': A pointed yellow tooth, hard as steel, taken from a crocodile of the Drowned Marsh. Brutus sets them in his iron fists; Isaac Cinq-Doigts buys them for six coins.
textes.Une dent longue comme un avant-bras, jau: A tooth as long as a forearm, yellowed by a hundred years of swamp: Vieille-Dent's, the giant crocodile. Isaac Cinq-Doigts offers forty coins for it.
textes.Une dent triangulaire, coupante comme un: A triangular tooth, sharp as a razor, lost by a shark from the Coral garden. Coralin, the craftsman of Atlantis, makes flippers from them.
textes.Une dernière histoire, mon fils. Une pet: One last story, my son. A little one.
textes.Une dernière partie, mon ami ! La chance: One last game, my friend! Luck is turning!
textes.Une dernière saison si bonne que la sard: One last season so good the sardines would sell themselves, without a single quarrel. Not one! I'd sit on the jetty with my tea, and I'd have nothing to judge.
textes.Une dernière traversée au long cours, ve: One last deep-sea voyage, to the south. I'll find the spot, more or less, where the wave took Jules, and I'll throw one of Rose's bouquets there. Somebody has to bring him flowers.
textes.Une deuxième assiette, mon gourmand ?: A second plate, my greedy friend?
textes.Une deuxième durite lâche ! OPTIMUS-LISS: A second hose gives way! OPTIMUS-LISSE panics: it strikes faster than ever!
textes.Une deuxième flamme. On dirait que la sa: A second flame. The hall seems to hold its breath.
textes.Une dispute. Avec mon père. Je ne dirai: A quarrel. With my father. I won't say why. I raised the hammer and struck the anvil. It split in two. Anvils don't split. That one did. So did the family. The next day I was on a ship. I didn't look back at the quay. Hm.
textes.Une dorade calme, Zohra ? Je l'ai criée: A calm sea bream, Zohra? I shouted it very softly.
textes.Une décoction a tourné. Et toi, tu as do: A brew curdled. And you, did you sleep?
textes.Une elfe ? Et elle n'aime pas les haches: An elf? And she doesn't like axes, I bet. Of course. People who don't like axes have never been cold.
textes.Une elfe ?! Au milieu de l'île ?! Gaston: An elf?! In the middle of the island?! Gaston, do you hear that? Elves exist! Well, Gaston says he knew it. Gaston always says he knew it.
textes.Une enveloppe cachetée de cire rouge, ac: An envelope sealed with red wax, bought at the post office. Perfect for a declaration of love.
textes.Une enveloppe épaisse, cachetée de cire: A thick envelope, sealed with red wax, with the recipient's name written in round, careful letters. Brindille, the winged postwoman, is counting on you.
textes.Une et demie ! L'autre moitié s'est envo: One and a half! The other half blew away!
textes.Une et demie, Hapou. Plus la moitié d'un: One and a half, Hapou. Plus half a boat.
textes.Une exposition à Port-Azur, dans le hall: An exhibition in Port-Azur, in the lobby of the Grand Hotel: the whole party in ribbons of light, on the walls. And the beach folk coming to see themselves, and finding themselves beautiful.
textes.Une expérience de Quasar a fait sauter l: One of Quasar's experiments blew the fuses of the whole Academy. He came to see me, his crest smoking: “Volt, it was a successful experiment.” I asked: “Successful how?” He said: “I discovered what blows the fuses.” I threw him out. Then I helped him.
textes.Une famille de liftiers ! Une maquette d: A family of liftkeepers! A model lift takes pride of place against the wall, Mum holds a stopwatch, and Grandpa holds on to his memories.
textes.Une famille de vol à voile a monté son p: A gliding family has assembled their glider… in the living room. The nose points at the door. The door looks worried.
textes.Une fausse note ! Les clochettes grincen: A wrong note! The bells creak… and will-o'-the-wisps burst out, snickering!
textes.Une faute, je ne promets rien. C'est la: A typo, I can't promise. The press decides.
textes.Une feule ? Ha ! Débutant ! Moi, il m'en: Jutht one? Ha! Beginner! Me, I'm mithing… hang on… lotth. Keep the otherth nithe and thnug, friend.
textes.Une fiole de brume, pour la forge ?: A vial of mist, for the forge?
An elven vial, thin as a bubble. Lyra entrusted it to you to draw the spring water from the pool of the great waterfall (north-east of Village Island).
textes.Une flamme d'or qui danse dans une coupe: A golden flame dancing in a crystal cup, with no wood or oil. It doesn't burn your fingers: it warms your heart. Stolen by the Frost Titan; its place is in the Ember Heart of the Forge Cathedral.
textes.Une flamme, ce n'est pas de la force, c': A flame isn't about strength, it's about good manners. You invite it, you guide it, you thank it. Pupils who shout at their flame always end up with singed eyebrows. I've seen plenty. Of eyebrows.
textes.Une flaque de boue ! Non ? Pas maintenan: A mud puddle! No? Not now? Okay…
textes.Une fleur aux pétales de flamme, jaune a: A flower with petals of flame, yellow at the heart, red at the tips, which only grows on the slopes of the Great Blaze. It stays warm in your hand. Mother Brasille needs it for her flowerbeds.
textes.Une fleur aux pétales translucides dans: A flower with translucent petals in which tiny galaxies swirl.
textes.Une fleur blanche aux pétales lumineux,: A white flower with glowing petals, picked from the top of a jungle peak. It never wilts.
textes.Une fleur de lune ?! Tu sais où elles po: A moonflower?! You know where they grow? … Don't tell me, I'll find out myself. {prix} coins!
textes.Une fleur géante jaillit du bois, tentac: A giant flower bursts out of the wood, tentacles of brambles and jaws as big as a door: MOTHER BRAMBLE! She's the one who turned the plants of Yggdrasil mean.
A wind arrow, here… There we go.
textes.Une fois ! Et tu en as trouvé combien ?: Once! And how many did you find? No, don't tell me, or I'll start again from zero. Hoo. Four thousand two hundred and twelve. Or thirteen.
textes.Une fois l'an, Mathurin m'emmène faire l: Once a year, Mathurin takes me round the island in his boat. I don't say a word the whole way round. Neither does he, for once. The sea doesn't freeze, it asks for nothing. It's restful. At the end, I say: “Hm. Thank you.” He says: “Don't mention it.” The next day, I make ice for his fish. A whole crate.
textes.Une fois l'an, j'emmène Borée faire le t: Once a year, I take Borée round the island in my boat. He sits in the bow, straight as a mast, and doesn't say a word. Neither do I, for once. We listen to the sea. At the end, he says: “Hm. Thank you.” And the next day, I find a crate of ice at my door, for my fish. A whole crate.
textes.Une fois par an, Murmure va crier tout a: Once a year, Murmure goes to shout at the very end of the Zero-Gravity Garden. I heard her by chance, while rehearsing there. “YOO-HOO!” Just once. The sound floated over the trees for a whole minute. I played the same note, very softly, to keep it company. She doesn't know it was me.
textes.Une fois par an, il vient à la boutique,: Once a year, he comes to the shop, sits down, holds out his leg and says: “It itches.” I explain that a wooden leg can't itch. He replies: “Then explain to me why it itches.” I sand the knee a little, rub in some linseed oil, and he goes away happy. It does nothing. It does a lot.
textes.Une fois par an, on fait le tour de l'îl: Once a year, we drive round the island by bus, honking. It takes ten minutes. With the picnics, a whole day. It's the best day of the year. Granny Sunflower always sits up front, with her hat.
textes.Une fois par an, on refait le calcul sur: Once a year, we redo the sums on a coaster. The sign's been paid off for twelve years. We look at the number. Toni flips the coaster over. He pours me another. We say nothing. The next year, we start again.
textes.Une fois par an, toute la Cité monte au: Once a year, the whole City goes up to the Mist Park with a kite. The biggest wins a medal, so does the prettiest, and so does the funniest. Lili Altaïr wins almost all of them.
textes.Une fois par mois, Théophraste traverse: Once a month, Théophraste crosses the town, walks into L'Alambic and says: “Monsieur Fiole. The treatise.” I pour him a mint syrup and tell him I'm on page one hundred and twelve. He replies that the treatise has one hundred and fourteen. He drinks his syrup to the last drop. Then he leaves. It's our little ritual.
textes.Une fois par mois, Tom m'échange une cha: Once a month, Tom swaps me a song for a bag of seeds. He says parrots are the best critics: if they repeat a tune, it's a good one. Bartholomé whistled the Song of the Brawl King three days after hearing it. Tom cried. Then he said: “He sings more in tune than Gros-Louis.”
textes.Une fois par mois, Volt entre dans ma bu: Once a month, Volt walks into my healing bubble, sits down without a word and points at his antennae. I lay my hands on them. They glow. I tell him: “There's nothing wrong, Volt.” He says: “Ah.” I pour him a tea. He drinks it grumbling about Quasar and his crystal. He leaves. He feels better. So do I.
textes.Une fois par mois, il s'assoit à ma tabl: Once a month, he sits at my table and asks me, very seriously, whether the stars will move tomorrow. I look into the ball and say yes. Only once, as a joke, I said no. He didn't sleep all day. He came back in the evening, white as a sheet, to check. I'll never do it again. You don't joke about an astronomer's stars.
textes.Une fois par mois, je donne une chanson: Once a month, I give Joe a song in exchange for a bag of seeds. He whistles it to his birds. If a parrot repeats it, it's a good one. Bartholomé whistled the Song of the Brawl King three days after hearing it. It brought tears to my eyes. It's the finest review I've ever had.
textes.Une fois par mois, je traverse le bourg: Once a month, I cross the village to claim my treatise. Mr Fiole receives me at his counter, offers me a mint cordial and swears he's on page one hundred and twelve. He's been on page one hundred and twelve for five years. The treatise has one hundred and fourteen. I drink the cordial. It's good, I'll admit.
textes.Une fois par mois, je vais lui demander: Once a month, I go and ask her if the stars will move tomorrow. I know they move: I measure them! But I'd rather hear it from someone else. She looks into her ball, very serious, and says: “Yes, Aurélien. All of them.” Then I sleep well. It's silly. It's delightful.
textes.Une fois par mois, je vais voir Aurore p: Once a month, I go and see Aurore about a “little ache in the antennae.” She lays her hands on them, they glow, then she tells me: “There's nothing wrong, Volt.” I say: “Ah.” She pours me a tea. I grumble. I leave. I feel better. I don't know why.
Once a week, to see my sister. She lives in Hautefond. She calls me “the Percher”. I call her “the Floorer”. We adore each other.
textes.Une fois toutes les dix minutes, un coup: Once every ten minutes, a blow that should knock you out leaves you at half a heart.
textes.Une fois, Amine devait livrer des babouc: Once, Amine was supposed to deliver some red ladies' slippers near the Fondouk. He delivered them to Moulay Brahim. The amin put them on without looking, and spent the whole day settling harbour disputes in embroidered red slippers. Nobody dared tell him. Me neither. It was too good.
textes.Une fois, Anouk m'a mis en retenue à l'i: Once, Anouk kept me in detention at the sickbay, to be sure I didn't break anything for a whole day. I sorted her seaweed: the green ones, the brown ones, the red ones. I made a fourth pile for the ones that look like moustaches. She kept it. She says it's very scientific.
textes.Une fois, Cargo a porté tout mon étal su: Once, Cargo carried my whole stall on his back to get it out of the rain. With the pot. Without spilling a drop.
textes.Une fois, Ishi a dit « joli ». J'ai cru: Once, Ishi said “pretty”. I thought he meant my kimono. He meant a pebble. I laughed for three days.
textes.Une fois, Kiku a dit « joli ». Je n'ai j: Once, Kiku said “pretty”. I never knew if she meant my garden or her tea.
textes.Une fois, Mange-Clous a voulu me faire g: Onthe, Mange-Clous wanted me to tathte hith thtew with jungle chillieth. Not mathed. I chewed with my gumth for an hour. My eyeth were watering, my nothe wath running, my two teeth were thaking. At the end, I thaid: “Delithiouth.” He wath tho pleathed he hugged me. Thinthe then, he maketh me the mathed one. No chilli.
Once, Mochi “helped” me knead. She kneaded, slapped, rolled, sang, and when I took the loaf out of the oven, it was shaped like a rabbit. With droopy ears. She said: “It's me.” Nobody dared eat it. It stayed on the counter for three days, until Bondi bit off an ear.
textes.Une fois, Odette a ouvert le registre de: Once, Odette opened the ledger in front of me and read out loud everything about me. “Yannick Rentals. Monday, one customer fished out. Tuesday, two. Wednesday, one hat and one customer.” It went on for ten minutes. At the end, I clapped. She didn't smile. But she didn't close the ledger right away, either.
textes.Une fois, Papa est parti faire « un peti: Once Daddy went off for “a little stroll” and came back nine days later. Orophin had looked for him everywhere. Daddy didn't understand why everyone was crying. He'd brought me a golden heron feather. I've still got it. Mummy didn't speak to him for a week.
textes.Une fois, Perlée est descendue me voir,: Once Perlée came down to see me, in the blink of an eye. In one morning she tidied my whole house and put a label on every one of my drops: two hundred and twelve. In the evening, when she left, I cried. The labels melted. I've never dared tell her.
textes.Une fois, Pimprenelle a voulu rappeler t: Once Pimprenelle tried to call back all my lost drops with a spell. She shouted “Drops, come here!”. All the frogs in the garden came instead. She said it was almost the same thing, because frogs are wet too. I was finding them in my bathtub for a week.
textes.Une fois, Pimprenelle a voulu rendre mon: Once Pimprenelle tried to make my nectar fizzy with a flick of her wand. For a week my bottles had hiccups: they blew bubbles and sang. The customers loved it, I sold twice as much. She's still asking for her share. I gave her a ribbon. That's a share.
textes.Une fois, Pépin a voulu danser avec moi,: Once, Pépin wanted to dance with me, “to understand the rhythm from the inside”. He stepped on my hooves four times in two steps. He said: “It's because your hooves are slower than my feet!” I limped till the next day. He brought me a carrot loaf to apologise. At a run, of course.
textes.Une fois, Pépin a voulu m'aider à pétrir: Once, Pépin wanted to help me knead. He fell into the kneading trough, right up to his horns. I pulled him out laughing, all sticky, and told him he was the biggest brioche I'd ever made. He had dough in his hair for three days. He smelled so good that Flammèche's puppies followed him everywhere.
textes.Une fois, Théo pleurait pour son cerf-vo: Once, Théo was crying about his kite. Again. I lent him my nicest shell so he'd stop. He stopped. Then he wanted to keep it. So he cried again. Babies are complicated.
textes.Une fois, Ulfa a goûté mon eau de lune e: Once, Ulfa secretly tasted my moon water. I saw her. She pulled a face like a goat biting a lemon, and said very loudly: “It's WATER!” She's been telling everyone ever since. She's wrong. But she's right to say it: people leave me in peace.
textes.Une fois, Zohra a acheté du safran à un: Once, Zohra bought saffron from a passing caravan man, to save three pennies. On Friday, her tajine cooked, and from my stall, at the other end of the souk, I smelled it. Not my saffron! I didn't speak to her for three days. On the fourth, she came with a dish of tajine, my saffron in it. We made up with our mouths full.
textes.Une fois, après deux bières, j'ai avoué: Once, after two beers, I confessed to Mérit that I loved someone. That very evening, all of Per-Hâpy knew, even the crocodiles. Luckily, I hadn't told her who. She's still looking. She's suspected the whole village, even the cacao seller from Yaxché. I say nothing. I smile. It drives her mad.
textes.Une fois, c'est déjà une fois ! Moi, l'a: Once is already once! Me, the ring, twice. Maybe. A victory is something you tell all your life. Tell it often.
textes.Une fois, c'est le baptême. Tout marin y: Once is your baptism. Every sailor goes through it. Mine was at twelve, at the bow, in front of the seagulls. They've never forgotten it.
textes.Une fois, chez les nains, on a fait la f: Once, at the dwarves', we partied in a mine. The echo, friends…
textes.Une fois, dans le panier de perches, il: Once, in the basket of perch, there was a lotus flower. “Fell in all by itself,” said Khéty, without looking at me. I put it in a bowl of water. It lasted a week. He came by every day, “for the perch”. I said nothing. Some things are better said with a bowl of water.
textes.Une fois, dans les montagnes, Hugues s'e: Once, in the mountains, Hugues sprained his ankle jumping off a rock to impress a troll. I carried him on my back for two days. He told his dragon story forty times. On the fortieth, I threatened to put him down. He went quiet. For an hour. Then he started again. That's how I learnt his story by heart.
textes.Une fois, des enfants ont dit que mon dr: Once, some children said my dragon had never existed. Philomène stood up from her bench, struck the ground with her cane and said: “It existed. It breathed fire. And that boy was trembling, and he went anyway.” Then she looked at me and went “baaa”. I still don't know whether she likes me or not.
textes.Une fois, elle leur a raconté une histoi: Once, she told them a story so funny that an apple fell all by itself. She said: “See, it laughed.” I had no answer to that.
textes.Une fois, elle m'a livré une fraise si g: Once, she delivered a strawberry so big that I served it as a birthday cake, with a candle on top. Nobody noticed the difference. The strawberry did: it blushed.
textes.Une fois, en pleine offrande au Cénote,: Once, in the middle of an offering at the Cenote, a bee landed on my nose. I couldn't move. Yum Kab whispered: “She thinks you're in bloom, priestess.” I laughed. In front of everyone. For the first time in thirty years of ceremonies. The gods didn't hold it against me. The rain came anyway.
textes.Une fois, en volant très bas au-dessus d: Once, flying very low over the sea, I saw a huge shadow pass beneath the Albatross. A whale, heading for the Azure Dome. She turned an eye towards me. We looked at each other for a second. Two giants, one in the water, one in the air. It's my most beautiful flying memory.
textes.Une fois, enrhumée, je n'ai pas pu crier: Once, when I had a cold, I couldn't shout the news. The next day, I received a honey tea, with no name. But the handwriting on the label… it was the same as the seventeen letters. Once I was better, I shouted “THANK YOU, ASMODIN!” under his windows. He closed the shutters. I saw him smiling behind them.
textes.Une fois, il a allumé le premier brasero: Once, he lit the first brazier on the first try. Cleanly. I raised my hands to… for nothing. I scratched my nose. He still talks about it, apparently. I never clap, {surnom}. The day Oscar truly succeeds, he won't need my hands to know it.
textes.Une fois, il a dit à une tarte : « Tu es: Once, he said to a pie: “You are the most beautiful pie in the world.” It turned golden all at once. I don't explain it. I just observe.
textes.Une fois, il a fait semblant de ne pas m: Once, he pretended not to put my cinnamon in. I tasted it. It was there. He blushed right up to his moustache.
textes.Une fois, il a peint toute la maison pen: Once, he painted the whole house while I was asleep. In the morning, I thought I was in a different house. I cried, then I thought it was super.
textes.Une fois, il a ri. Un vrai rire. C'était: Once, he laughed. A real laugh. It was when the machine whistled while the Burgomaster was giving a speech in the tavern. The speech stopped dead. Léon left me a tip.
textes.Une fois, il a servi une de mes fraises: Once, he served one of my strawberries as a birthday cake, with a candle. Nobody noticed the difference. I did. I cried a little. It was the most beautiful strawberry of the year.
textes.Une fois, il a triché aux cartes avec l': Once he cheated at cards with Pesto's help. The parrot squawked “Ramen!” every time I had an ace.
textes.Une fois, il avait raison : l'île pencha: Once, he was right: the island was tilting by a tenth of a degree, because of a forgotten scaffold. He'd felt it from his armchair. I thanked him. He said: “I complain, but I complain accurately.”
textes.Une fois, il est revenu du Bois des Luti: Once, he came back from the Goblin Wood with a bump on his forehead and a tale of “ten goblins”. I knew straight away he'd slipped on his cape. I didn't say anything. I made him a special pie, with writing on it in pastry: “For the vanquisher of the ten goblins”. He cried. Then he ate it.
textes.Une fois, j'ai ajouté une petite hélice: Once, I added a little propeller to her adjustable spanner while she was asleep. She took it off in the morning. She put it back in the evening. I saw her spinning it during her tea.
textes.Une fois, j'ai allumé le premier brasero: Once, I lit the first brazier on the first try. The first try! Pyra raised both hands. I stopped breathing. Everyone stopped breathing. She scratched her nose. But she had raised them, her hands. I saw it. Pip saw it too.
textes.Une fois, j'ai amené une abeille pour co: Once, I brought a bee to count the points for me. It landed on his knucklebones and wouldn't fly off again. We had to stop the game. I declared a draw, in the name of the bee. Ah Kin protested all evening. It's the only game I haven't lost. I tell the story often.
textes.Une fois, j'ai battu Turbo pendant qu'il: Once, I beat Turbo while he was sneezing. He demanded an official rematch. He lost the rematch too.
textes.Une fois, j'ai demandé au capitaine si s: Once, I asked the captain if his grandpa was nice. He opened his mouth, closed it, looked at the sea for a really long time. After, he gave me a double ration of biscuit. I think that meant “I dunno”.
textes.Une fois, j'ai dit que sa tarte au potir: Once, I said her pumpkin pie had too much nutmeg. A week of dry bread! She'd serve me a slice of bread on a plate, with a big smile. On the eighth day, I came back and said there wasn't enough nutmeg. She served me pie again. We never mentioned it again.
textes.Une fois, j'ai entendu monter une musiqu: Once, on a very calm night, I heard music rising from down below: a guitar, someone singing off-key, laughter. Maybe it was a fisherman. I played along with him, very softly. He never knew he'd played a duet.
textes.Une fois, j'ai essayé de faire des pâtes: Once I tried to make pasta all by myself. I got flour everywhere, even on the cat. Nonna laughed so hard she had to sit down.
textes.Une fois, j'ai essayé de l'aider. Je lui: Once I tried to help him. I wrote his line on a piece of paper: “Honorine, your song is the most beautiful thing in Montjoie.” He just had to read it in front of her. In the morning he got to the bakery, took out the paper, and sneezed on it. The flour wiped everything out. He said: “I'm catching my breath.” I gave up. For that time.
textes.Une fois, j'ai failli demander. J'étais: Once, I nearly asked. I was in front of her caravan, hand on the handle. And I thought: what if it's Borée? What if she saw Borée in my cup? I think I said it out loud. I turned back. I'll never know. And that's just fine.
textes.Une fois, j'ai gagné. Une seule fois. Il: Once, I won. Just once. He said to his cards: “Let him win, he's had a hard week.” I've never known if it was a joke.
textes.Une fois, j'ai joué un rythme vers Rainv: Once, I played a rhythm towards Rainville. A minute later, the drum kit in the garage answered me, the same rhythm, backwards. We played like that for an hour, without seeing each other.
textes.Une fois, j'ai mis un peu trop de brume: Once, I put a bit too much mist in her tea. Just a tiny bit. Plumette fell asleep standing up, at the counter, head in the mailbag. Three letters went out late. Her father Hulotte, woken by the silence, covered her with a shawl. I reduced the dose. She says it was the best nap of her life.
textes.Une fois, j'ai oublié le pain. Elle n'a: Once, I forgot the bread. She said nothing. The next day, Hortense was waiting for me on my boat. She pinched my ear. I've never forgotten since.
Once, I talked for an hour. To my wife. The day I asked her to marry me. She said: “Are you done?” I said yes. She said yes. After that, she talked for two. She went before me. Now, the sea does the talking.
textes.Une fois, j'ai parlé une heure sans m'ar: Once, I talked for an hour without stopping. The day I asked my wife to marry me. She listened to all of it. At the end, she said: “Are you done?” I said yes. She said yes. After that, she talked for both of us for thirty years. She went before me. Now the sea does the talking.
textes.Une fois, j'ai peint le chat de Monsieur: Once, I painted Mr Fusain's cat yellow. So he'd look like a sun. He rolled in the grass for a week. After that, he was a green sun. Dad said it was modern art.
textes.Une fois, j'ai perdu ma voix pendant tro: Once, I lost my voice for three days. All of Montjoie came to see me. They brought me honey, herbal teas, scarves. Nobody knew what was going on in town anymore. Those were the three days I felt most loved.
textes.Une fois, j'ai perdu mon foulard sur la: Once, I dropped my scarf on the promenade, and he tried to catch up with me to give it back. Twenty metres. After twenty metres, he stopped, red as a lobster, hand on his cap. I turned back to get the scarf. He said, out of breath: “I had my eye on you.” I let him have that one.
textes.Une fois, j'ai planté une luciole dans u: Once, I planted a firefly in a pot, to grow a firefly tree. I watered it every morning. Noisette explained to me, very kindly, that fireflies aren't seeds. The firefly had flown off long before. I kept the pot. You never know.
textes.Une fois, j'ai posé un pot de basilic à: Once, I put a pot of basil next to Mantra while he was meditating. When he opened his eyes, three days later, the basil had flowered. He said: “It understood.”
textes.Une fois, j'ai posé une chaise près de l: Once, I put a chair by the door, with a mint cordial on it. The next day, the cup was empty and tidied away, with a little note: “Thank you. The second chorus was a bit fast.” He was right. We slowed it down.
textes.Une fois, j'ai remonté Zéro avec un bras: Once, I put one of Zéro's arms back on the wrong way round. He swept backwards for a whole day. He didn't say a thing. He found it “restful”.
textes.Une fois, j'ai sonné la cloche à minuit: Once I rang the bell at half past midnight, to see if anyone would come. Everyone came, in their nightshirts. The Admiral arrived last, fully dressed, with her coat and her compass, and said: “Good. Carène is awake. Now, Ewen, explain.” I scrubbed for a week.
textes.Une fois, j'ai suivi Miou sur le plateau: Once, I followed Miou up onto the plateau, where the dead are, between the square tombs. He walked, I walked, he walked… And then the sun set, and I didn't know where the river was any more. So I sang Néferet's evening hymn, really loudly, so I wouldn't be scared. And it was Néferet who heard me, from the valley temple! She came to get me.
textes.Une fois, j'ai voulu aider Bobor à pétri: Once, I wanted to help Bobor knead the dough. I fell in. Right up to my horns! Bobor pulled me out laughing, and said I was the biggest brioche he'd ever made. It took Mum three days to get the dough out of my hair. It smelled nice, though.
textes.Une fois, j'ai voulu battre mon record e: Once, I tried to beat my record by carrying six crates of nectar at once. Over the sea, one crate slipped. It rained nectar on a beach for a whole minute. The folk down there must have thought it was a miracle. Mélisse thought it was a lost crate. She still charges me for it.
Once, I wanted to write a profile of her. A little question to start with: “Why the Bazaar?” She talked for an hour. Without stopping for breath. My crow-feather quill snapped twice. At the end, she said: “And you, my dear, would you like a box for nothing?” I bought one. I still don't know why.
textes.Une fois, j'ai voulu rappeler toutes les: Once I tried to call back all of Brindille's lost drops with a spell. “Drops, come here!” All the frogs in the garden came instead. Oh well. Frogs are wet too, it's practically the same. Brindille was finding them in her bathtub for a week.
textes.Une fois, j'ai vu une baleine si grande: Once, I saw a whale so big it had trees on its back. … No, it was an island. But it was moving, I swear.
textes.Une fois, j'allais gagner. Une heure qua: Once, I was about to win. An hour and forty minutes of play, a magnificent position, mate in three. I took the time to admire it. Ding: the brass clock. Lost on time, at the very last second. Tacquet said: “Lovely position.” And he wrote it down in his notebook. Along with the defeat.
textes.Une fois, j'étais parti compter les cham: Once, I'd gone off to count mushrooms instead of going to class. Headmaster Malachar came flying over the trees! He landed in the clearing, all out of breath. I showed him the mushroom I'd named Malachar. He said it was a fern. But he smiled a tiny bit.
textes.Une fois, je devais livrer des babouches: Once, I had to deliver red babouches, embroidered, for a lady near the Fondouk. I got the wrong door. I gave them to Moulay Brahim. The amin put them on without looking, and he settled the port's quarrels all day long in lady's babouches! Nobody told him. Karim laughed for a week.
textes.Une fois, je l'ai croisé au marché ! J'a: Once, I bumped into him at the market! I wanted to say “your rhythm is amazing”! I said “hello, lovely weather”! IT WAS RAINING!
textes.Une fois, je lui ai posé une devinette :: Once, I asked her a riddle: “I'm red, I can smell tarts a hundred paces away, I pick herbs in my sleep, and I'd like to marry you. Who am I?” She answered: “No, you silly.” Laughing. I hadn't even finished smiling. The answer was “me”. It was a joke, obviously. Obviously.
textes.Une fois, je lui ai rapporté un pot de s: Once I brought her back a jar of sauce with a ribbon. She cried. I didn't know what to do. I said: “It needs a bit more salt.” She laughed.
textes.Une fois, je me suis endormi dans une ba: Once, I fell asleep in an empty cask, at the bottom of the hold. In the morning, the captain counted one too many. Apparently he nearly sold me to Isaac! Hic! I say it's not true: he'd have sold me for much more. The Silent One pulled me out by the feet. It was daytime. I don't like daytime, in the morning.
textes.Une fois, je me suis trompée de nom en a: Once, I got the name wrong when announcing the alert results. I shouted “BABETTE” instead of “GERMAINE”. Germaine crossed the Great Square so fast her net whistled. She didn't say a thing. She just looked at me. I corrected it, very loudly. I added that Babette hadn't caught anything at all. It was true. Germaine gave me a golden turnip.
textes.Une fois, je me suis écorché le genou en: Once, I grazed my knee following Sire Tancrède. Sister Pétronille closed her eyes, she prayed, and my knee healed. But she also healed the doll I was holding, whose arm had come unstitched. The arm stitched itself back on! I told Colombe. Colombe was jealous.
textes.Une fois, je suis allé tout seul au Céno: Once, I went to the Cenote all alone at night to watch the bats come out. There were hundreds! They flew around me, and I thought Camazotz was going to take my head, like Hunahpu's. I ran and ran! Peek' was barking. It was Balam who found me, under a tree. He didn't say anything. He carried me home.
textes.Une fois, je suis tombé exprès devant Pa: Once, I fell on purpose in front of Pastille to get the smiling-skull plaster. I didn't have a scratch. She saw. She put the plaster on anyway, on my perfectly clean knee. I kept it for a week. Everyone thought I'd had a massive fall. I didn't say a thing.
textes.Une fois, l'automate a fait match nul co: Once, the automaton drew a game against itself. It sulked and didn't speak for a week.
textes.Une fois, l'horloge a pris une seconde d: Once, the clock fell one second behind. Gaspard and I noticed at the same moment, a hundred metres apart. We ran. We arrived together. On time.
textes.Une fois, la cabine s'est arrêtée au mil: Once, the cabin stopped halfway. With the mayor of Port-Azur inside. He stayed there an hour. He wrote a poem. It was very bad.
textes.Une fois, la machine a sifflé pile quand: Once, the machine whistled just as I was drinking. I jumped so hard the chocolate shot up to the ceiling. Firmin said: “See, you know how to make things go up too.”
textes.Une fois, la reine est partie pour l'île: Once, the queen set off for the elves' island at the same time as me. Her, in the blink of an eye. Me, flying, like a proper flyer. When I arrived, she was sipping herbal tea with a smile. I said I'd taken a shortcut. She said: “Of course.” I hate it when she says “of course”.
textes.Une fois, mon bateau a coulé au large, à: Once, my boat sank out at sea, all because of a whale that was too curious. I made a raft out of planks and my shirt. I drifted for six days. On the seventh, I saw the Column shining in the distance. I rowed towards it. Ever since, when I look at it, I think: “There. Home.”
textes.Une fois, nous avons vu la même seconde: Once, we both saw the same second of delay on the departures clock, a hundred metres apart. We ran. Arrived together. We nodded. It was marvellous.
textes.Une fois, pendant son histoire de 1977,: Once, during his 1977 story, I said: “1978.” One word. He dropped his lemonade. Barricade was passing. She laughed so hard the seagulls flew off. Tapage didn't speak to me for an hour. It was very restful. Then he started again. Since then, I keep my words to myself.
textes.Une fois, pendant une course, l'Albatros: Once, during a race, the Albatross broke down over the sea. I turned back and towed her all the way to the Hautefond Mast. That day, nobody won. It was the finest race of our lives. We never talk about it.
textes.Une fois, pour faire la paix, elle m'a f: Once, to make peace, she had me taste one of her grogs. One sip. I coughed for an hour, on the terrace, in front of the caravan drivers. Rabia patted my back until evening. The next day, I brought her a mint tea. She sniffed it and said: “Smells like a garden.” She didn't drink it. We're even.
textes.Une fois, pour faire la paix, je lui ai: Once, to make peace, I had him taste a grog. The little one, the rainy-day one. One sip. He coughed for an hour on his terrace, red as a lantern. His wife was patting him on the back. He told me it was poison. Where I come from, that's a compliment.
textes.Une fois, pour rire, je lui ai demandé d: Once, for a laugh, I asked him to marry me. He stood frozen for eleven minutes, without a word, his clocks stopped all around him. I finished my tea. When he came back to himself, he said: “It is twelve minutes past two.” I've never loved him more.
textes.Une fois, terrible… Comme ma fille, alor: Once, and it was awful… Like my daughter, then! She was sick from the moment we left until we got back. Don't worry: the best merchants get seasick. So do the best sailors, in secret.
textes.Une fois, un aventurier est revenu du la: Once, an adventurer came back from the lake covered in slime and furious about his contract. He shouted for ten minutes. Églantine smiled, stamped his card, filled in a complaint form and gave him an herbal tea. He left thanking her. I've never understood how she does it. I think it's the stamp.
textes.Une fois, un caravanier très insistant l: Once, a very persistent caravan trader courted her for an hour. Halima listened to him, smiled, and dropped a tajine dish at his feet. On purpose. In a thousand pieces. The caravan trader ran off. She looked at me: “He didn't know how to carry a dish, khalti.” She's not wrong. That matters, here.
textes.Une fois, un dé est tombé de ma manche,: Once, a die fell out of my sleeve, onto the baize, in front of everyone. An accident, my friend: a hole in the lining. Sylvain picked it up with his fingertips, rolled it in his palm, listened to it, and handed it back to me, saying: “You've lost a tooth, sir.” The whole room laughed. I had all my sleeves sewn up.
textes.Une fois, une botte gauche est tombée de: Once, a left boot fell from the cliff while I was unloading the sparkling-apple boat. By the time I'd put the crate down, no more boot. The next day it was in the Bazaar window: “Boot fallen from the sky”. Bricolette says she “borrowed” it. Since then we've had a truce: on the first Monday of the month, we swap a left for a right.
textes.Une fois, une bourrasque m'a emporté jus: Once, a gust of wind carried me all the way up over the City of Clouds! I landed in a greenhouse, right among the giant strawberries. They had me stay for dinner. The dessert was bigger than I was.
textes.Une fois, une dame de la Haute-Ville a d: Once, a lady from the Upper Town said out loud that my jewellery was “scrap metal”. Rosalie burst out laughing so hard that the lady left. Then she came back and bought a ring. Rosalie told her: “Good choice, my cinnamon.”
textes.Une fois, une lettre de Tazira sentait t: Once, a letter from Tazira smelled so salty that Caramel sneezed seven times opening it. I waited politely. At the seventh, I said “Bless you” seven times in a row, to catch up. She went “Mrrr”. I think she smiled, on the inside.
textes.Une fois, une seule fois, j'ai voulu liv: Once, just once, I tried to deliver forty honey loaves up to the platforms. Halfway across the footbridge, a plank cracked. Taeron swears it didn't. Forty loaves fell on the square like golden rain, and the village had a party. As for me, I've never gone back up.
textes.Une fois, une seule fois, une prédiction: Once, just once, a prediction came true exactly. I'd said “Boulon will lift a house”. The next day, he set down the first container of the Boxes. I was so scared that I didn't predict anything for a month.
textes.Une fois, une seule, Gravier a parlé pen: Once, just once, Gravier spoke during my 1977 story. He said: “1978.” One word. I dropped my lemonade. Barricade, who was passing by, burst out laughing. Gravier picked up his fishing rod again as if nothing had happened. I didn't speak to him for an hour. That's a long time, for me.
textes.Une fois, une seule, j'ai acheté le safr: Once, just once, I bought saffron from a passing caravan trader. Cheaper. I put it in the tagine. Aïcha, at the far end of the souk, lifted her nose and said: “That's not mine.” She didn't speak to me for three days. Three days without saffron and without a good morning. I'll never do it again.
textes.Une fois, une seule, j'ai laissé Amine ê: Once, just once, I let Amine be captain. He shouted “Full speed ahead!” and charged straight into the fountain. The ship sank. Well, he did. After that, I made him first mate. He was so happy: he thought first mate was better than first. I didn't tell him. He was wet, but he was happy.
textes.Une fois, une seule, que toute la tavern: Just once, one single time, for the whole tavern to sing the old topmen's song in tune. All the voices together, not one wrong note. It'll never happen. That's what makes it a lovely dream.
textes.Une fois. … D'accord. Comme les voyageur: Once. … All right. Like travellers, then. You pass through, you look, you move on. That's good too. I think.
textes.Une fontaine qui soigne, sous terre ? On: A healing fountain, underground? We bottle it and make a fortune. … What, it's sacred? Everything's sacred, as long as it sells.
textes.Une forge. Une enclume neuve. Un feu qui: A forge. A new anvil. A fire that doesn't move with the waves. … Hm.
textes.Une forêt calme. Une maison au toit de p: A quiet forest. A house with a palm roof. Ix Sak weaving under the tree. Me coming home with a turkey. That's all. That's a lot.
textes.Une forêt… Oh, {surnom}. C'est la plus b: A forest… Oh, {surnom}. That's the most beautiful thing a human has ever said to me. The trees heard you, I promise. They hear everything.
textes.Une fraise de Flora ! Prends-en deux, va: One of Flora's strawberries! Go on, take two: they're as big as your fist, and as sweet as… as giant strawberries. That's the best I can do.
textes.Une fraise grosse comme le poing, mûrie: A strawberry as big as your fist, ripened day and night in the endless sunshine of the High-Altitude Greenhouses. Flora Verdine has surely given it a name. Restores two hearts.
textes.Une fraise, aujourd'hui ? Brigitte a une: A strawberry today? Brigitte has a sister.
textes.Une fumée âcre, des récifs noirs qui fum: Acrid smoke, black reefs smoking in the waves… No way to find a passage. Without a map, you'd better turn back.
textes.Une fée de la rosée ne boit pas, Majesté: A dew fairy doesn't drink, Your Majesty. She gives.
textes.Une galerie froide, des dalles noires co: A cold gallery, flagstones as black as holes in the night… Something is moving in them.
textes.Une galerie sous la mer, jusqu'à la jung: A tunnel under the sea, all the way to the jungle? I'd drawn it as a dotted line on my map. Dotted lines are for things I'm not sure of. I was right!
textes.Une galette de pain moelleuse, dorée au: A soft flatbread, baked golden in the Borgo oven, studded with rosemary and coarse salt, glistening with olive oil. Mamma Lasagna bakes three batches a day. Restores one and a half hearts.
textes.Une gargouille ! Quand elle bat des aile: A gargoyle! When it flaps its wings very fast and rears up, it's going to dive straight at you: step aside, then strike.
textes.Une gelée violette qui tremble toute seu: A purple jelly that wobbles all by itself and sparkles, Gloubi's speciality. It tickles your tongue. Restores two hearts.
textes.Une glace ? Vanille, fraise, coco, ou la: An ice cream? Vanilla, strawberry, coconut, or the Bruno special: all three at once!
textes.Une goutte d'eau, deux gouttes de couleu: One drop of water, two drops of colour.
textes.Une goutte de rosée de lune. Elle reste: A drop of moon dew. It stays round and cool in the hollow of your hand. (Brindille, in the Fairy Village, is looking for five.)
textes.Une goutte de rosée qui ne s'évapore jam: A dewdrop that never evaporates and shines like a little moon. Brindille the fairy is looking for five.
A drop. A tiny little drop.
textes.Une goélette ? Commence par le sloop, ma: A schooner? Start with the sloop, sailor: you don't learn to run before you walk… or to steer two masts before one.
textes.Une graine dorée ?… Attends. ATTENDS. Ga: A golden seed?… Wait. WAIT. Gaston, the treasure box! Here: I picked it up on the beach twenty years ago, it was shining in the sand. I always knew it was special. Take it, for your elf. And tell her Barnabé Coquillard sends his respects. Most humbly.
textes.Une graine dorée, grosse comme un œuf, v: A golden seed as big as an egg, veined with light: the first seed of the World Tree in a hundred years. The spirit of the tree entrusted it to you for the fairies. It is warm, and it seems to breathe.
textes.Une graine dorée, lourde et tiède. Barna: A golden seed, heavy and warm. Barnabé found it on a beach twenty years ago. It comes from the elves' Mother Tree.
textes.Une graine ronde et tiède qui luit comme: A round, warm seed that glows like a night-light. Photon says it grows into a flower that sings when the sun rises.
textes.Une grande assiette de spaghettis de Mam: A big plate of Mamma Lasagna's spaghetti, covered in volcano sauce, with three meatballs and a snowfall of parmesan. Blessed (a little) by the Noodles. Restores three hearts.
textes.Une grande boutique de potions ratées, a: A big shop of botched potions, with a flashing sign and vials up to the ceiling. People would come from all over the archipelago to get things wrong with me!
textes.Une grande dalle ronde gravée, entre les: A large round engraved slab, between the two shrines. “When the rain and the sun have received their offering, the path of the Five Suns will open.”
textes.Une grande feuille signée par Monsieur A: A large sheet signed by Mr Aldric Lisse (very small) and by all of Port-Boucan (very big, with drawings): "The old port belongs to those who live in it, bring it to life and share it. Forever."
textes.Une grande fresque, peinte il y a très l: A great fresco, painted long ago: a shepherd and his sheep at the foot of a grey mountain, a cave, and in the cave a bronze cogwheel. Above, the ridge of Stoneheart, seen from the north. An astronomer with a big telescope would surely know where that is…
textes.Une grande fête des chiens sur la Place: A big dog party on Pallet Square, with a patched bandana for every dog on the island, and a contest for the best tail wag. Tic-Tac would win. He wags so fast you can't even see his tail.
textes.Une grande fête des vents : tous les cer: A great festival of the winds: every kite in the archipelago in the sky over Arcanelle, all at once! Even Borée would hold one. He'd say the wind whistles. He'd sing.
textes.Une grande pierre ronde, gravée d'un cro: A big round stone, engraved with a silver crescent. Nothing on it… “Only the moon knows where it sleeps,” Mother Moon used to say. You will have to come back when the moon rises (night falls around 8 p.m.; you can sleep at the inn to wait for it).
textes.Une grande plume dorée. Utilise-la (ou G: A large golden feather. Use it (or G on PC, X button in VR) to call Ventaile: she arrives and lands near you. Then E (trigger) to climb onto her back.
textes.Une grande salle où les trois écritures: A big hall where the three scripts would sit side by side: the hieroglyphs of Per-Hâpy, the glyphs of Yaxché and our pictures. The children of the three peoples would learn there together. Pilli would sleep at the back.
textes.Une grande table au milieu du pont, avec: A big table in the middle of the deck, with Mange-Clous's stew, Mama's grog, and the whole crew around it. And nobody getting up before the pot's empty. Nobody!
textes.Une grande tablée sur toute la longueur: One long table along the whole length of the quays, from the Freighter to the dry dock, with all of Boucan and all the islands around. One soup, a hundred pots, and nobody pays. Or everybody does. Same thing.
textes.Une grenouille géante ! Elle bondit, fou: A giant frog! It leaps, lashes out with its tongue… and swallows whole whatever passes by. Keep your distance, parry (F) its jumps, and strike when it lands.
textes.Une grenouille géante a avalé mon chapel: A giant frog swallowed my sun rosary. My rosary! It was in my hand, and then… slurp. I'm praying very hard. But it won't give it back.
textes.Une grenouille m'a avalé, une fois. Sœur: A frog swallowed me once. Sister Pétronille saved me. I owe her my life. And a bath.
textes.Une grenouille à chapeau pointu, assise: A frog in a pointy hat, sitting very dignified on a chair. It looks at you sternly. “Ribbit.”
textes.Une grosse clé de fer noir, tiède, une f: A big key of black iron, warm, with a golden flame in the ring. Brother Cendrin, the keeper of the Ember Heart, guards it: it opens the gate of the Nine Circles, at the back of the Forge Cathedral.
textes.Une grosse clé de laiton, accrochée à un: A big brass key, tied to a cork (so it floats). It opens the captain's cabin of the Baleine Rouillée, the old freighter that houses Radio Boucan.
textes.Une grosse conque rose. Elle sent la mer: A big pink conch. It smells of the sea. It looks like it can make a lot, A LOT of noise.
textes.Une grosse galette dorée, cuite sur la p: A big golden galette, cooked on the griddle at La Marmite and cut into the shape of a cogwheel. The blacksmiths eat one every break. Brunehaut eats two. Restores two hearts.
textes.Une grosse marmite fume devant le feu. U: A big pot steams in front of the fire. An old dwarf tastes it and frowns: “Something's missing…”
textes.Une grosse miche ronde, cuite dans la mo: A big round loaf, baked in half of an old locomotive boiler (the other half is Brasero's bathtub). The crust is black as coal, the inside soft as an Assembly cushion. Restores one heart.
textes.Une grosse tomate de la Tomateraie de l': A big tomato from the Tomato Grove of Al Dente Island, heavy, ribbed, warm from the sun. Restores one heart.
textes.Une grotte cachée derrière la cascade !: A cave hidden behind the waterfall! Crystals glow in the half-light… and there, at the back, an old chest.
textes.Une guitare qui grince, une voix qui mur: A creaky guitar, a whispering voice, and rain recorded in the garage. Everyone in the yurt closes their eyes.
textes.Une harpe devant la baie, des carillons: A harp in front of the big window, chimes on the ceiling, and two old musicians whispering in the half-light: “The night wind plays with just its fingertips.”
textes.Une harpe éolienne ! Des cordes tendues: A wind harp! Strings stretched over a wooden frame: you don't pluck them, you open the big window, and the wind plays through them. It just needs a conductor, otherwise it does whatever it likes. Like a tenor.
textes.Une heure ?! Personne sait faire ça !: An hour?! Nobody can do that!
textes.Une histoire inventée, aujourd'hui ? J'e: A made-up story today? I've got a fresh one.
textes.Une histoire, c'est très nourrissant, tu: A story is very nourishing, you know.
A story, rather than an object.
textes.Une histoire… (Il pose sa tablette.) On: A story… (He puts down his tablet.) You can't display it. But you can tell it. Tell it to me, and I'll keep it in my head. That's my biggest room.
textes.Une housse cloutée ! Clou, tu es un amou: A studded cover! Clou, you're a sweetheart!
textes.Une idée, ça ne se vole pas. Ça se cuisi: You can't steal an idea. You just cook it better.
textes.Une image de la ville des humains, au bo: A picture of the humans' town, by the sea… How strange, and sweet. Thank the one who wrote it.
textes.Une image du monde d'en haut… le soleil,: A picture of the world above… the sun, the coloured houses… Tell Nadine that the queen of Atlantis thanks her. And that she exists.
textes.Une immense dalle de pierre ferme le ven: An immense stone slab seals the Great Moai's belly. In the middle, a circle of signs glows faintly, as if breathing. Far, far below, you hear flowing water… and something singing.
