textes.Une étiquette sur l'étagère : « Réserve: A label on the shelf: “Granny's stock. 412 jars. I counted them. Take one, go on.”
textes.Une étiquette sur le bocal : « Servez-vo: A label on the jar: “Help yourself (just ONE!)”. You take one. Just one. Promise.
textes.Une étoile de mer orange du fond de la b: An orange starfish from the bottom of Port-Azur bay. It tickles a little.
textes.Une étoile filante ! Elle file au-dessus: A shooting star! It streaks above the Spire… and falls somewhere on the island, softly. A fragment to pick up!
textes.Une étoile filante cette nuit ! J'ai fai: A shooting star last night! I made a wish. I won't tell you what it was: otherwise it'll fall through.
textes.Une étoile filante file juste au-dessus: A shooting star whizzes just over the Spire.
textes.Une étoile filante traverse le ciel… pui: A shooting star streaks across the sky… then two… then a hundred! A meteor shower is falling on Astralys!
textes.Une étoile… pour quelqu'un qui voyage la: A star… for someone who travels by night. I'll make it in silver thread.
textes.Une île avec des arbres. Et du vent. Je: An island with trees. And wind. I think.
textes.Une île entière ! Avec des palmiers ! Et: A whole island! With palm trees! And mosquitoes!
textes.Une œuvre de jeunesse : « La Sonate pour: An early work: “The Sonata for Socks Hung Out to Dry”! Allegro!
textes.Une, Khéty. UNE chèvre. Comme la dernièr: One, Khéty. ONE goat. Same as last time.
textes.Une, deux ! Une, deux ! Le tour de l'île: One, two! One, two! Round the island is six kilometres. I do one. But with conviction.
textes.Une, deux, trois ! Ohé, ohé, la Morue !: One, two, three! Heave-ho, heave-ho, the Cod!
textes.Une. Comme toujours. Et votre piano ?: Once. As always. And your piano?
One. And away from the coil.
textes.Un… câlin ? (Il rougit en doré.) C'est t: A… hug? (He blushes gold.) That's very… unprotocolary. But I authorise it. As an exception. Once a year only.
A… a very big slime, Titouan.
textes.Ursule ? Elle ne parle presque pas, et m: Ursule? She hardly talks, and I talk for two. Makes for the perfect conversation! I drop by the forge every evening at closing time. It's restful, at hers.
textes.Ursule ? Trois mots quand elle en dit di: Ursule? Two words where others use ten. And once, about my tea, she said: “Hot water.” Two words, exactly. I haven't forgotten them.
textes.Ursule chauffe ta lame au rouge, la plon: Ursule heats your blade red-hot and plunges it into a tub of cold mist: a hiss, a blue vapour. “It won't break any more.”
textes.Ursule forge les clous de tous mes ponts: Ursule forges the nails for all my bridges. The best nails on the island. But she sells axes! And she thinks my bridges dance too much. Too much? That's what they're for!
textes.Ursule m'a raconté que Grisou lui avait: Ursule told me Grisou had asked her for springs for his shoes, like in Cliquetis. I said: “Cheating.” Just one word. He sulked for a week, he walked past the start without looking at me, tail drooping. And then one morning: “You were right, Pépin. But still.” That's Grisou all over: but still.
textes.Ursule passe ta lame sur sa grande meule: Ursule runs your blade over her big sandstone wheel, for a long time, without a word. The edge sings.
textes.Ursule taille un plastron et des épauliè: Ursule cuts a breastplate and shoulder guards from thick leather, boiled in wax. “That stops claws. Not rocks.”
Useful! Ouch. Right in the heart. … Well. Here, I'll blow you a useful bubble. There. It's good for nothing. Sorry, I don't make any other kind.
textes.VICTOIRE ! Et sans brouillard ! Vous ête: VICTORY! And no fog! You're my witness, friend! You're my witness!
textes.VIEILLE-DENT ! Le roi des crocodiles du: VIEILLE-DENT! The king of the marsh crocodiles, as long as a rowboat. His jaws reach far: wait until he lunges at nothing, then strike.
textes.VOILÀ ! Gaston, note ça : une carte ne s: THERE! Gaston, write that down: a map is never wrong. It's the rocks that wander about. You're cartographer material, {surnom}.
textes.VRROUUM ! La soufflerie se déchaîne. Dan: VRROOOM! The wind tunnel goes wild. Inside the tunnel, the ribbons are partying; outside, so is your fringe.
textes.Va ! Et deviens plus fort. Je veux un ri: Go! And grow stronger. I want a rival worthy of me.
textes.Va ! Et lève le nez de temps en temps :: Off you go! And look up now and then: around here, everything happens above your head.
textes.Va ! Et si quelqu'un te demande ce qu'il: Go on! And if anyone asks you what's new at the bottom of the sea, tell them: “Ask Ernest.”
textes.Va ! Et si tu entends Marguerite, cours: Off you go! And if you hear Marguerite, run to the Southern Fields!
textes.Va ! Et si tu te perds, cherche la Grand: Go on! And if you get lost, look for the Great Pearl: all the walkways lead to it. Even the ones that pretend they don't.
textes.Va ! Et si tu te perds, lève la tête : l: Go on! And if you get lost, look up: the Brass Sun is always in the middle. Everything else turns around it.
Go in peace, child of the surface.
textes.Va en paix, et ne casse jamais tes spagh: Go in peace, and never break your spaghetti in half.
Go in peace, and come back to see us.
textes.Va en paix. Et bois de l'eau : le soleil: Go in peace. And drink water: the sun here is unforgiving.
Grog it is. Just a drop.
Go to bed. The stars will wait for you.
textes.Va voir la nuit, Gros-Louis. Plus loin q: Go and look at night, Gros-Louis. Further than the gate.
textes.Va, ami du vent. Et si tu trouves un mot: Off you go, friend of the wind. And if you find a word that's flown away, bring it back to me.
textes.Va, aventurier ! Et reviens entier. Ou a: Off you go, adventurer! And come back in one piece. Or at least with most of the pieces.
Off you go, and keep an eye on the sea.
textes.Va, et garde les cornes au chaud ! Enfin: Off you go, and keep your horns warm! Well… whatever you have instead of horns.
Go, and come back for tea.
textes.Va, mon petit. Et souviens-toi : ce qui: Off you go, little one. And remember: what's decided together holds better than what's decided alone. Even a bridge.
textes.Va, petit spore. Et ne mange jamais un c: Off you go, little spore. And never eat a mushroom that glows. Even if it winks at you.
textes.Va, petite branche. Une pomme par jour,: Off you go, little twig. An apple a day, and come back and see me.
textes.Va, petite graine. Et reviens avec un pa: Off you go, little seed. And come back with an empty basket: I'll fill it.
textes.Va, va. Et si quelqu'un te demande qui a: Off you go, off you go. And if anyone asks you who raised the island, say it was Séraphin. And that his grandson was there. Almost.
textes.Va, va. Je te réveille pour le grog du s: Off you go, off you go. I'll wake you for the evening cordial.
textes.Va, {surnom}. Le soleil te suit, même qu: Off you go, {surnom}. The sun follows you, even when it rains.
Clear off before I change my mind.
textes.Va-t'en. Tout de suite. Ou j'appelle Bru: Clear off. Right now. Or I call Brutus.
textes.Va. Et garde ta barbe au sec. … Ah, tu n: Go. And keep your beard dry. … Ah, you haven't got one. Pity.
Go on. And don't come back empty-handed.
textes.Va. Et ne traîne pas dans la jungle la n: Go on. And don't hang about in the jungle at night: the dead go walking there.
textes.Va. Et si tu prends un bateau, dis-lui b: Go on. And if you take a boat, say hello to it from me. It'll understand.
textes.Va. Et si tu vois un balai voler tout se: Off you go. And if you see a broom flying all by itself, don't follow it.
textes.Va. Et si une mouette te suit, c'est Fir: Go on. And if a gull follows you, it's Firmin. Keep one hand on your snack.
Go. The wind will bring you back.
textes.Vaincre Vieille-Dent, le crocodile géant: Defeat Vieille-Dent, the giant crocodile, deep in the Drowned Marsh (west of the island, under the dead mangroves)
textes.Vaincre la Naga des profondeurs: Defeat the Naga of the depths
textes.Vaincre le Titan de Givre au fond du Coc: Defeat the Frost Titan at the bottom of the Cocytus
textes.Vaincre le chef des gobelins dans son ca: Defeat the goblin chief in his camp, deep in the Goblin Wood (in the north-east of the island, past the East Gate)
textes.Vaincre le chef gobelin (encore lui ? ou: Defeat the goblin chief (him again? yes, him again)
textes.Vaincre les jaguars des pentes du Mont F: Defeat the jaguars on the slopes of the Smoking Mountain (west of the island, under the pines)
textes.Vanille ! Le parfum des gens sérieux. Le: Vanilla! The flavour of serious people. The sergeant's a vanilla man too. I'll put a scoop aside for you, in my mind. Nice and round.
textes.Vanille, fraise et coco : la spéciale Br: Vanilla, strawberry and coconut: Bruno's special. It melts faster than you can eat it. Restores one heart.
textes.Variable ! Il fera un temps. Je ne sais: Changeable! There'll be some kind of weather. I just don't know which kind yet.
textes.Variable. Le baromètre ne sait pas. Moi: Changeable. The barometer doesn't know. Neither do I. That's science for you.
textes.Vas-y ! Doucement, derrière les oreilles: Go on! Gently, behind the ears. He's all warm, isn't he? That's because he has no hair. He keeps all the warmth for himself. And a bit for you.
textes.Vas-y, mets le casque ! … (Il est beauco: Go on, put on the helmet! … (It's far too big. You can't see a thing. You hear the knight laughing.) HA HA! It suits you… very well! Well, your ears, anyway.
textes.Vas-y, mets-lui en une !: Go on, land one on him!
textes.Vas-y. C'est le pollen, il adore les pho: Go ahead. It's the pollen, it loves photos.
textes.Veille de nuit : je surveille les nuages: Night watch: I keep an eye on the clouds while they sleep. They snore a little, over in the west.
textes.Veille radio. Tout est calme. Même l'Alb: Radio watch. All quiet. Even the Albatross, down below, has gone silent.
textes.Velours ! Pneu a mangé son bandana. Enco: Velours! Pneu ate his bandana. Again.
textes.Velours a cousu mon premier patch. Elle: Velours sewed my first patch. She sews everything. Onto everything. She's got the eye. And needles everywhere.
textes.Velours a cousu un patch des Rats de Cal: Velours sewed a Bilge Rats patch on each of their bandanas. Since then, when they hear Clou's guitar, they all howl together. Rouille says they're the best backing singers on the island.
Velours sewed a Bilge Rats patch on the bandana of every one of my dogs. Now they're the most punk dogs in the archipelago. And they know it.
textes.Velours et moi avons cousu ma robe ensem: Velours and I sewed my dress together, with a piece of every garment donated in the first year. Twenty-two dresses. It took us three months and four hundred pins. When I put it on, Velours cried. She said: “You're wearing the whole of Boucan.” She was right.
textes.Velours m'a cousu une doublure secrète p: Velours sewed me a secret lining full of badges. She never asked a single question. I come by “to have a button sewn back on” every week. There's never any button.
textes.Velours prend mes vieux vêtements et les: Velours takes my old clothes and brings them back to life. She has the most patient hands on the island, and the most tightly sewn lips. She keeps every secret.
textes.Velours, j'ai reçu un manteau de capitai: Velours, I've been given a captain's coat!
textes.Venir au Festival du Larsen, le soir (à: Come to the Larsen Festival in the evening (from 8:30 p.m.) and join the crowd in front of the Main Stage
textes.Venir au Grand Boucan, le grand concert: Come to the Great Boucan, the Bilge Rats' big concert, in the evening (from 9 p.m.) at the Howling Hall, and dance in the pit
textes.Ventaile a repris des forces ! Elle dépl: Ventaile has regained her strength! She spreads her immense wings, then lowers her head to you… Fit her with King Thorgal's dwarven saddle.
textes.Ventaile a repris des forces ! Elle étir: Ventaile has regained her strength! She stretches her immense wings… She'd agree to carry you, but without a saddle, you can't hold on to her back at this altitude. King Thorgal, in Forgefer, might know more.
Ventaile is already here, a few steps away.
textes.Ventaile ne peut pas entrer ici : sors à: Ventaile can't come in here: step out into the open air to call her.
textes.Ventaile niche au bord du cratère, au-de: Ventaile nests on the edge of the crater, above the Golem Path. Break the rune on her chain, give her three fish, and the saddle will do the rest. After that… the sky, big one. The sky.
textes.Ventaile plonge comme une pierre et te r: Ventaile dives like a stone and catches you in mid-air! She sets you down on the Wind Perch.
textes.Ventaile se laisse caresser les plumes d: Ventaile lets you stroke the feathers on her neck… but you'd need a saddle to ride her. King Thorgal, in Forgefer, spoke of the saddles of the ancient eagle-riders.
textes.Ventaile te regarde avec ses yeux d'or,: Ventaile looks at you with her golden eyes, then at your empty hands. She needs fish: go fishing (with Barnabé's rod) and come back.
textes.Verrou n°3 — rebrancher l'antivirus: Lock no. 3 — plug the antivirus back in
textes.Vers cinq heures, avant de monter à l'ob: Around five, before going up to the observatory, Céleste hands me her night flask. A litre. I fill it to the brim, no sugar, and screw the cap on tight, because she has the observatory stairs to climb. She thanks me as if I were handing her a star. Nobody has ever thanked me like that for a coffee.
textes.Vers cinquante ans, mon oreille gauche s: Around fifty, my left ear started whistling. The right one followed, out of politeness. The copper sang further and further away. I was scared, for a whole season. Then I learned to listen to it with my fingers: it doesn't tremble the same way when it's ready. And Hnia, my wife, counts the blows for me. Deaf, but happy. Nearly always.
textes.Vers la mer ! Tu as raison : la ville ne: At the sea! You're right: the city doesn't move, but the sea changes on every trip down. A ray, a jellyfish, a shoal of lanternfish… You'd make a good driver.
textes.Vers la ville ! Comme moi, la première f: At the city! Like me, the first time. Three domes glowing in the blue… You never tire of it. I'll save you the front seat.
textes.Vers le haut ? Elle a peur de ma forge,: Upwards? It's scared of my forge, more like.
textes.Vers le soleil ! Ha ! Comme mon prénom !: Towards the sun! Ha! Just like my name! Don't worry, your wings won't melt. But wear a hat.
textes.Vers trois heures du matin, Lirael pose: Around three in the morning, Lirael sets a cup of tea on the harp bench as she does her rounds. She listens to one verse and moves on. Once she said: “The thirty-sixth is the best.” I've rewritten it ten times since, to make it even better.
textes.Vers trois heures, je pose une tasse de: Around three, I set a cup of tea on the harp bench, listen to one verse, and go back to my rounds. One night I told him the thirty-sixth was the best. He's rewritten it ten times since. It's not as good now. I won't tell him.
textes.Verser de haut, c'est tout un art : le b: Pouring from high up is an art: arm raised, a thin stream, and the foam rising in the glass. It took me ten years to learn. A hundred spilled teapots, all from my brother-in-law Abdellah's workshop. Rabia, my wife, kept count. She remembers every one. The eighty-seventh was on the amin's foot.
textes.Verser de haut, ça s'apprend. Il m'a fal: Pouring from up high takes practice. It took me ten years and a hundred spilled teapots. My wife counted.
textes.Verser le pot de brun dans son godet (le: Pour the pot of brown into its slot (no. 5): E in front of the Stone Palette, in the middle of the clearing
textes.Verser une première couleur dans la Pale: Pour a first colour into the Stone Palette
textes.Version deux point quatre : je faisais l: Version two point four: I gave the tour of Astralys in forty-seven stops. It lasted six hours. Visitors fell asleep at stop twelve. One gull stayed to the end. The Professor cut the tour down to fifteen stops. The gull never came back. Beep. Sad information.
textes.Versé de haut, mousseux, très sucré, à l: Poured from up high, frothy, very sweet, with fresh mint from the Fondouk garden. Restores one heart.
textes.Vert, comme lui ! Il va adorer !: Green, like him! He's going to love it!
textes.Verte ! Avec de l'écume ! Comme le lait: Green! With foam! Like Gustave's cloud milk, but green! Oh, I have to tell Ombeline, she'll have to change her paintings.
textes.Verts ? Tu es encore tombée dans la mous: Green? You fell in the fountain moss again.
textes.Vespérine ! Ton piment est prêt, dix pot: Vespérine! Your chili's ready, ten jars!
textes.Vespérine a analysé mon huile à cornes e: Vespérine analysed my horn oil in public: nine tenths perfume, one tenth vanity. She posted the figures on her stall. I replied by writing underneath: “And one hundred percent happiness”. My sales doubled. Hers didn't. She didn't speak to me for a month. Since then, she says hello with her eyebrows.
textes.Vespérine dit que mon huile à cornes ne: Vespérine says my horn oil cures nothing. She even posted the figures on her stall. Technically, she's right. But she forgets that beauty heals too. She's very gifted. Very, very serious.
textes.Vespérine m'achète du piment infernal po: Vespérine buys infernal chili from me for her courage potions. She's precise, serious and merciless about badly written labels. We argue over who invented fire-cinnamon tea.

Vespérine buys infernal chili from me for her “courage potions”. I asked her what was in them. She answered: “Infernal chili.” I asked her what else. She said: “Courage.” I never found out if she was joking. She never smiles enough for anyone to tell.
Vespérine buys infernal chili from me for her “courage potions”. I asked her for the recipe. She answered: “Infernal chili.” She didn't even smile.
textes.Vespérine, c'est ma fille. Ma petite rac: Vespérine is my daughter. My little root. She's as serious as a seed waiting for spring, and she labels everything, even my jams. She makes the best potions in the city with my herbs. I'm proud of her.
textes.Vespérine, c'est ma sœur jumelle. Elle e: Vespérine is my twin sister. She was born three minutes before me, and she reminds me every day. She's as serious as a label. I adore her. One day, I'll make her laugh out loud.
textes.Vespérine, ma petite racine ! Tu as mang: Vespérine, my little root! Have you eaten?
textes.Veuillez cesser d'aboyer. Merci de votre: Please stop barking. Thank you for your understanding. Please stop biting. Thank you for your understanding.
textes.Veuillez libérer les lieux. Merci de vot: Please vacate the premises. Thank you for your understanding.
Please vacate the premises. Thank you for your understanding. Have an optimised day.
textes.Veux-tu entendre l'histoire de la premiè: Would you like to hear the story of the first seed?
textes.Vibrante. J'ai joué dans le Jardin des A: Vibrant. I played in the Zero-Gravity Garden this morning. Up there, notes float for longer. One stayed in the air until noon. Photon says his flowers danced.
textes.Vibrato fait de la musique sans toucher: Vibrato makes music without touching his instrument. I make rhymes without touching the meaning. We understand each other. His antennae quiver when Prisme dances. I told him so. He said it was just for the rhyme.
textes.Vibrato joue comme le vent d'Ondelune, a: Vibrato plays like the wind of Ondelune, before it gets tuned. His antennae vibrate when I dance. I pretend not to see. I see it very well. That's why I dance so well.
Vibrato is playing better than ever tonight.
textes.Vibrato m'a donné une leçon de thérémine: Vibrato gave me a theremin lesson. I waved my hands really fast over the instrument. It made the sound of a falling saucer. All the glug-glugs in the Greenhouse answered at the same time. Nova came running. I said: “It's avant-garde music.” Vibrato gave me a second lesson.
textes.Vibrato, ô musicien, ton cœur bat-il bie: Vibrato, oh musician, is your heart in good condition?
textes.Victoire ! Encore un exploit pour ma lég: Victory! Another feat for my legend! And for you too, a little.
textes.Victoire ! Mon père serait fier ! Mon gr: Victory! My father would be proud! My grandfather too! The cat too!
textes.Victoire ! Personne n'est blessé ? Laiss: Victory! Nobody hurt? Let me check anyway.
textes.Victoire ! … Pardon. J'ai crié. Je ne cr: Victory! … Sorry. I shouted. I never shout. Shouting was nice.
textes.Victoire. Et je ne me suis foudroyée qu': Victory. And I only zapped myself once. That's very good.
textes.Victor ! Avez-vous la plus authentique,: Victor! Do you have the most authentic one this week?
textes.Victor ! T'as un coquillage pour moi ?: Victor! Have you got a shell for me?
textes.Victor dit qu'il triche pour m'entraîner: Victor says he cheats to train me. He hides cards in his straw hat. I saw him. He saw me see him. He said: “It's educational.” When he wins too much, he pays me back in painted shells. I've got a whole crate of them. I called it Victor.
textes.Victor est le plus grand artiste de l'ar: Victor is the greatest artist in the archipelago. He makes snow fall in a land where it never snows! If that isn't magic, my dear, I don't know what is. And he gives me friend prices.
textes.Victor m'a vendu mon cerf-volant à moiti: Victor sold me my kite for half price. He said: “For you, captain, half price.” Daddy said thank you three times. Now Victor says he should have sold it full price. But if it was full price, would it not have flown off? I don't get it. Grown-ups don't get it either, I think.
textes.Victor m'achète un timbre par jour, depu: Victor has bought one stamp a day from me for years, and he never sends a letter. One day, I asked him what he did with them. He pulled an album out of his pocket: three hundred stamps, sorted by colour, all brand new. He said: “It's a collection.” I said: “Of what?” He blushed. Victor blushing, that's rare.
textes.Victor peint ses coquillages et les appe: Victor paints his shells and calls them authentic. On one point, he's right: the paint is authentic. I don't buy fakes. Even pretty ones.
textes.Victor vendait des glaces avant moi. Ell: Victor sold ice creams before I did. They melted. He's got pride, the gift of the gab, and snow globes everywhere. I'm fond of him, my old competitor.
textes.Victor, aux souvenirs, vend des coquilla: Victor, at the souvenir shop, sells painted shells as “authentic”. Authentically painted, yes.
Victor is the souvenir man. He sold me my kite, and then it flew away. The kite, not Victor. But he gives me painted shells, so I like him anyway.
textes.Victor, mon concurrent. Il crie à la con: Victor, my competitor. He cries unfair competition every morning, then buys a stamp from me. Just one. To have a chat. I let him chat.
textes.Victor. Mon partenaire de cartes. Il gag: Victor. My card partner. He wins all the time. He says it's talent. It's because I'm looking somewhere else.
textes.Vide. Gâchette près d'un objet pour le r: Empty. Trigger near an item to pick it up.
textes.Vieille-Dent dort au fond du marais, sou: Vieille-Dent sleeps at the bottom of the marsh, under the dead mangroves. Whoever kills him will have my gratitude. My gratitude is rare.
textes.Vieille-Dent ne bougera plus. Le marais: Vieille-Dent will never move again. The marsh holds its breath… Crochet will be pleased.
Vieille-Dent will eat no one ever again.
textes.Vieille-Dent, le crocodile géant du Mara: Vieille-Dent, the giant crocodile of the Drowned Marsh, took Crochet's hand years ago. Crochet wants someone to settle the score.
textes.Vieille-Dent… tu veux qu'on t'en débarra: Vieille-Dent… want us to get rid of him for you?
textes.Viens là, que je t'arrange le portrait,: Come here and let me rearrange your face, grouper-mug!
textes.Viens plonger. Tu me la raconteras en bu: Come diving. You can tell me in bubbles.
textes.Viens pêcher ce soir. Je te fais griller: Come fishing tonight. I'll grill you the other half.
Come and see the flowers in the second dome. Adèle's waiting for you.
Come on, I'll make it a bigger one.
textes.Viens, je t'en fais une plus grande !: Come here, I'll make you a bigger one!
textes.Viens, je te retourne vers la fenêtre !: Come, I'll turn you toward the window!
textes.Viens, {surnom}, mais tu ne dis rien. Au: Come, {surnom}, but don't say a word. At the back of my shed, under a tarp, there's a sailboat. I've been building it for six years, plank by plank, in the evenings, to sail round the archipelago. It's almost finished. Almost. Thing is, I've never gone past the harbour wall on my own. I'm scared to finish it, really. Because after that, I'll have to leave.
textes.Vieux Flint se souvient… Quand Vieux Fli: Old Flint remember… When Old Flint was little square, Old Flint's grandfather tell: one day come a SMOOTH thing, from other side of big water. It chase away big roar of north. And Clan will dance. Hmm. Old Flint think it you.
textes.Vieux. Mais content. Tant qu'il y a du r: Old. But happy. As long as there's rum and someone to listen, Silas is happy.
textes.Vigilant. Avec un galion pirate au quai,: Vigilant. With a pirate galleon at the quay, you sleep with one eye open.
textes.Vigilant. Toujours vigilant. Le Couvercl: Vigilant. Always vigilant. The Lid doesn't guard itself.
textes.Vigilant. Toujours vigilant. Même quand: Vigilant. Always vigilant. Even when nothing is happening. Especially when nothing is happening.
textes.Vigilant. Toujours vigilant. Quand on gu: Vigilant. Always vigilant. When you keep watch, you don't have moods: you have eyes.
textes.Vigilante. Il se passe des trucs bizarre: On alert. Weird stuff is going on in the Alleys. Machines suddenly going haywire.
textes.Vingt ? Tu vends vraiment autant de vent: Twenty? Do you really sell that much wind?
textes.Vingt ans de piraterie. On m'appelait Lo: Twenty years of piracy. They called me Lou the Terrible. I retired to Tazira, because nobody knew me here. Now everybody knows me. So much for that.
textes.Vingt ans que je dis à Berthe qu'elle sa: Twenty years I've been telling Berthe she uses too much salt. Twenty years she hasn't listened. Her heart is on her sleeve and her hand is on the salt cellar. We argue every day. I couldn't do without it.
textes.Vingt ans que je tiens ce port. Je conna: Twenty years I've run this harbour. I know every hull, every knot, every lie about the size of a fish.
textes.Vingt ans, cette graine dorée a dormi da: For twenty years, that golden seed slept in my treasure box, between a shark's tooth and a mother-of-pearl button. On sad evenings, I held it in the hollow of my hand: it was warm, like a little sun. I didn't know I was keeping it for someone.
textes.Vingt recettes de grenouille ! Il m'en m: Twenty frog recipes! I'm missing a twenty-first, to round things off. I'm trying honey frog. So far, it tastes like frog. With honey.
textes.Vingt-deux ans de service. Trois arresta: Twenty-two years of service. Three arrests: a chicken thief, a chicken thief, and the same chicken thief.
textes.Vingt-deux ans, et toujours pas d'excuse: Twenty-two years, and still no apology.
Twenty-thousand and a broken one. Noted.
textes.Vinyle a mis une chanson des Gouttières: Vinyle put a Gutters song in his shop window, right next to my mother's old record. I've walked past it a hundred times. I said nothing. Neither did he.
textes.Vinyle et moi, on a ouvert nos boutiques: Vinyle and I opened our shops the same year. He sells records, I sell chocolate. People buy a record, then come and listen to it at the café. We've got it well organised.
textes.Vinyle garde le disque de ma mère. Il sa: Vinyle keeps my mother's record. He knows I've never listened to it. He never offers it to me. That's kind, I think.
textes.Vinyle m'a offert un disque pour mon juk: Vinyle gave me a record for my jukebox. Just one song, which it's been playing on loop for twenty years. I've never changed it. I'm not sure how you change it, to be honest.
textes.Vinyle me laisse écouter le disque des d: Vinyle lets me listen to the two-village record once a year. He puts headphones on my ears and goes out to water his plants. He leaves me alone with the music.
textes.Vinyle, le disquaire, cache un disque tr: Vinyle, the record seller, hides a very rare record in his back room. A record where both villages sing together. He only plays it for people who are crying. I've heard it three times.
textes.Violet étoilé ! Comme le ciel juste avan: Starry purple! Like the sky just before nightfall. Noted.
textes.Violette ! On refait la charge foudroyan: Violette! Shall we do the lightning charge again?
textes.Violette ! Potion numéro douze. Elle est: Violette! Potion number twelve. It's ready.
textes.Violette ! Vous êtes la plus grande mage: Violette! You're the greatest mage on the island! Even when you zap me!
textes.Violette ? Ortie, qu'est-ce que tu as mi: Purple? Ortie, what did you put in it?
textes.Violette dit que c'est elle la plus mala: Violette says she's the clumsiest in the Guild. She zapped herself three times this week. I fell seven times. I don't know who's winning. Maybe it isn't a contest.
textes.Violette est la patiente la plus courage: Violette is the bravest and most lightning-struck patient on the island. My anti-lightning potions haven't worked yet. But we've discovered eleven new colours.
textes.Violette est la seule personne de la Gui: Violette is the only person in the Guild clumsier than me. Well, I think so. We each keep score on our own side, and we never agree on the result.
textes.Violette est mon plus grand défi : une m: Violette is my greatest challenge: a mage who zaps herself. Her outfits have to withstand everything. None of them do. But she wears them all with incredible grace.
textes.Violette est une grande mage. Si, si ! S: Violette is a great mage. Yes, she is! Her lightning bolts are the most powerful on the island. They just go a bit everywhere. Me included. But it's an honour to be struck by her.
textes.Violette m'a foudroyé par accident. Je n: Violette zapped me by accident. I felt nothing! I absorbed the bolt, thanks to a secret Tournevent technique. My hair took three days to come back down. But I felt nothing.
textes.Violette me fait penser à moi, quand tou: Violette reminds me of myself, back when all my spells ended up as bubbles. Hers end up as lightning. On herself. But one day, her butterfly will come. I know it.
textes.Violette, faisons la charge foudroyante: Violette, let's do the lightning charge! I run, you zap!
textes.Violette, la jeune mage de la Guilde, ne: Violette, the Guild's young mage, can only cast lightning bolts, and they often hit her instead. According to an old book, three storm crystals, which grow at the top of the Fangs, would channel her lightning "forwards".
textes.Violette, ne bouge pas, je prends ta tai: Violette, don't move, I'm taking your measurements.
textes.Violette, si l'éclair vous touche encore: Violette, if the lightning hits you again, I'm here. I'll heal your hair.
textes.Violette, si tu pouvais éviter de me fou: Violette, if you could avoid zapping me today, I'd appreciate it.
textes.Violette, vos cheveux se dressent encore: Violette, your hair is standing on end again. Would you like a flattening prayer?
textes.Violette, vos cheveux… ils se dressent t: Violette, your hair… it's standing up all by itself.
Aim well away from me too.
textes.Visez avec la main droite, gâchette pour: Aim with your right hand, trigger to click, stick to scroll
textes.Visez un objet et appuyez sur la gâchett: Aim at an item and press the trigger, then “Use” or “Drop”
textes.Vite et bien, c'est mon métier !: Fast and well, that's my job!
textes.Vite, vite ! Derrière le canapé ! … Bon,: Quick, quick! Behind the sofa! … Well, he may not come before tonight. Would you like a slice of cake in the meantime?
textes.Vivre le moment… sans photo ? (Il trembl: Living in the moment… with no photo? (He wobbles, puzzled.) That's a Heavy-Foot idea. I'll give it a try. … (Click.) Sorry. Reflex.
textes.Voici Germaine et l'ampli ! Et j'ai auss: Here are Germaine and the amp! And I've got the drumsticks too.
This is Gontran. He's a cumulus.
textes.Voici cinq navets dorés, Père Gaubert. D: Here are five golden turnips, Father Gaubert. Gently, I promise.
textes.Voici cinq objets des îles d'en bas, Orb: Here are five objects from the islands below, Orbe!
textes.Voici la bannière du chef gobelin, Sire: Here is the goblin chief's banner, Sir Tancrède.
Here is the seed of Yggdrasil, Your Majesty.
textes.Voici la puce holographique et la carte: Here are the hologram chip and the star chart!
Here is the Royal jelly heart, Master.
Here's what the weather will be. In theory.
Here are the logs and the stones.
textes.Voici les cinq champignons féeriques, Mè: Here are the five fairy mushrooms, Mother Morel.
textes.Voici les matériaux pour le Glisseur, Io: Here are the materials for the Glider, Ionie.
Here are the plans for the Lisse-Center, Mamie.
Here are the three pieces of the map.
Here are the three moon shards.
textes.Voici les trois éclats du Cœur, et trois: Here are the Heart's three shards, and three astral crystals.
textes.Voici mes dix pièces. Je pose la main su: Here are my ten coins. Do I put my hand on the ball?
Here are your three sulfur crystals.
Here are three blocks of iron ore.
Here are three logs of twisted wood.
Here are three hundred coins. I'll buy it.
Here are three mushrooms from the Twisted Wood.
Here are three storm crystals, Violette.
Here are three flakes of eternal frost.
textes.Voici trois fragments de météorite, Zéni: Here are three meteorite fragments, Zenith.
textes.Voici trois lots de pièces de vélo, Rust: Here are three lots of bike parts, Rustine!
textes.Voici trois paniers de légumes, Lentille: Here are three baskets of vegetables, Lentille!
Here are three feathers of the wind.
Here are three tufts of fever grass.
textes.Voici un cristal de soufre : c'est là qu: Here is a sulfur crystal: this is where fire is born.
Here are your five moon mushrooms.
Here are your five ember flowers.
Here are your four flown-away books.
textes.Voici vos trois graines lumineuses, Phot: Here are your three glowing seeds, Photon.
Here are your three pages, Madame Olga.
textes.Voici votre chapeau à plume, Monsieur le: Here is your feathered hat, Baron.
Here is your sun rosary, sister. The Duchess gave it back.
textes.Voilà ! Avec de la mousse en forme de nu: Here you go! With cloud-shaped foam. If you drink it fast, you get a cloud moustache. It's tradition.
textes.Voilà ! Héroïque ! Bon, je t'ai fait un: There! Heroic! Well, I made you a bit taller. And with a cape. You didn't have a cape? Now you do.
textes.Voilà ! Le quinzième toit sera le bon. T: There! The fifteenth roof will be the right one. Here, these glasses: kaleidoscopes. The whole world turns into a rose window. It's useless, it's marvellous, and it doesn't explode. Well, I think.
textes.Voilà ! Un objet de plus qui retrouve qu: There! One more item that's found its someone. It's the best day of my life. Like yesterday. Like tomorrow.
textes.Voilà ! Voilà la bonne réponse ! C'est t: There! That's the right answer! It's always both, youngster, always. Gwenola! A mug for this sailor! It's on me… well, it's on him.
textes.Voilà : {objet}, contre {prix} rondelles: Here you go: {objet}, for {prix} discs. Is that what you call them? “Coins”. Coins. What a pretty, useless word.
textes.Voilà la marchandise. Tout est forgé ici: Here's the merchandise. Everything's forged here, in the tree. You have {pieces} coins: choose wisely.
textes.Voilà qui me plaît. Cinq minutes d'avanc: Now that I like. Five minutes early is politeness. Ten is worry. I won't ask which are yours.
textes.Voilà un connaisseur ! Mes pommes rouges: Now there's a connoisseur! My red apples are the best on the island. Germaine says they're too red. An apple is never too red!
textes.Voilà un patient raisonnable ! Ça devien: Now there's a sensible patient! That's getting rare. You know my door, the front one. The back one is for people who don't want to be seen coming in.
textes.Voilà, Grand-père ! … C'est un nœud de l: There you go, Grandpa! … It's a shoelace knot.
textes.Voilà, c'est guéri. Vous voyez ? Je ne s: There, all healed. See? I'm not just a stumbler!
There. That's exactly what I'm talking about.
textes.Voilà. C'est presque ça. Rentre chez toi: There. That's nearly it. Go home.
textes.Voilà. Le thé, ça se mérite. Tu ferais u: There you go. Tea must be earned. You'd make a very good old lady.
textes.Voir Caelan et Ilyria se marier. J'ai pa: To see Caelan and Ilyria married. I bet on after the millennium, but I'd be delighted to lose. I'm counting the springs, and I have a few left.
textes.Voir Clara danser sur une vraie scène, s: To see Clara dance on a real stage, on the mainland, with a red curtain and well-dressed people. I'll be in the front row, smelling of fish, and I won't care one bit.
To see Clara dance on a real stage, on the mainland. Me in the front row, in flip-flops, cheering louder than everyone. Even louder than Mum.
textes.Voir Croc ouvrir ce coffre. Le voir comp: To see Croc open that chest. To see him finally understand what his grandfather left here. That day, I'll stand him a rum. The good one, from the back.
textes.Voir Vénus se lever exactement la nuit q: To see Venus rise exactly on the night my tables predict. Not a night before, not a night after. Exactly. Just once, and I'll sleep in peace.
textes.Voir de mes yeux les abeilles d'en haut,: To see with my own eyes the bees up top, the ones that forage the Mother Tree. Thalion offered to carry me up. I'd rather eat a beehive. Well… I'd rather think about it.
textes.Voir de mes yeux, une seule fois, une cô: To see with my own eyes, just once, a coastline I've drawn. To check I put the bay in the right place. And to cry a little, if I did.
textes.Voir des feux d'artifice ! Des vrais ! B: To see fireworks! Real ones! Bourrasque says there were some at the old festival. And skate on the Great Stage. And play with Bouton-d'Or in broad daylight. In that order. Or the other way round.
textes.Voir encore une fois le Feu Nouveau. Le: To see the New Fire one more time. The next one will be in seven years. I'll be seventy-two. I fully intend to carry a torch. Walking, this time.
textes.Voir entrer un grand navire dans la baie: To see a great ship sail into the bay at sunrise. A real one, three masts, all sails set. I'll count it. It'll be the finest number in my journal.
textes.Voir germer la graine d'Yggdrasil, la to: To see the Yggdrasil seed sprout, the very first shoot, with its two little leaves! And then to find my very own tree, my hazelnut's tree. I'd tell it: “Hello, it's me. Did you lose me?”
textes.Voir germer un nouvel Yggdrasil, et l'en: To see a new Yggdrasil sprout, and hear it whisper for the first time. And then, one evening, to go back down into the roots, sit beside Églantine, and talk about everything except the brambles.
textes.Voir l'automate joueur d'échecs d'Ambroi: See Ambroise Échec's chess-playing automaton (Fair stand, to the south)
textes.Voir l'avenir pour de vrai, une deuxième: To see the future for real, a second time. Just once. To know whether the first time wasn't a fluke, or one of Paulo's bouillabaisses with too much spice. A fortune-teller who doubts, traveller, is a lighthouse that blinks.
textes.Voir l'avenir, c'est facile. Le dire gen: Seeing the future is easy. Saying it kindly is an art. You don't want to know what we saw in Pyra's tea. Neither does she, for that matter.
textes.Voir la Cascade Arrabbiata tomber dans l: See the Arrabbiata Falls pour into the sea
textes.Voir la Cascade d'Encre tomber de la fal: See the Ink Waterfall tumble from the cliff
textes.Voir la baleine. Une fois. Je ne quitter: To see the whale. Once. I won't leave my post, mind you! But if it could pass right over the Gate, that would be very kind of it.
textes.Voir la mer de l'autre côté du monde. Mo: To see the sea on the other side of the world. My uncle says there's nothing out there. My uncle has never left his island.
textes.Voir la mer. Une fois. De loin d'abord,: See the sea. Once. From afar first, from the treetop, in Bourru's basket. With a skewer, for courage.
textes.Voir le Grand Cristal de mes propres yeu: To see the Great Crystal with my own eyes. Even through a porthole, even from afar, even for a second. I don't need to touch it. Just to know I didn't make it up.
textes.Voir le Roi des mares avant papy ! Et lu: See the Pond King before Grandpa! And ask him to bring Papa back. Or at least a letter. Grandpa says fish can go anywhere under the ground. So the King can go all the way to the sea, right?
textes.Voir le Sans-Pitié glisser de la grève j: To see the Merciless slide from the shore into the water, one spring-tide morning, with the whole port pushing and singing. And to hear the hull creak just right. The creak of a happy ship.
textes.Voir le volcan cracher sa sauce: See the volcano spit out its sauce
textes.Voir les gonds de la Porte aux Quatre Sc: To see the hinges of the Gate of the Four Seals. To touch that metal nobody knows, to hear it sing. And forge one blade from it, just one. Or a crêpe pan for Gwenola. We'll see which it prefers.
textes.Voir les pierres peintes du désert : les: To see the painted stones of the desert: the hunters, the animals, and the great round door. To paint them before the sand covers them. Painting a painting, can you imagine? Someone, a thousand years ago, had the same urge as me.
textes.Voir les quatre géants du village en cou: To see the four giants of the village in colour, on my birthday, with paper lanterns on every walkway and the whole village dancing all the way up to the Lookout.
textes.Voir les trois soleils réunis sur l'aute: To see the three suns united on the altar of the highlands, as the ancients used to say. I don't know who will do it. But I'd like to be there, with my sistrum, and sing.
textes.Voir ma voile se gonfler. La mienne. Sor: To see my sail fill. Mine. Sail out of the bay, round the point, and see Carène as nothing more than a little brown smudge on the coast. And then come back. I think I'll come back. I think.
textes.Voir nager les carpes de la Place des Ho: Watch the carp swim in the Hologram Square
textes.Voir neiger. Une fois. Une vraie neige,: To see it snow. Once. Real snow, falling from the sky and not from a globe I shake. Fifteen years I've been selling snow, and I don't even know if it's cold. I imagine it cold. Like Bruno's ice creams.
textes.Voir revenir les vraies lumières du Bois: To see the Wood's true lights come back, the ones that left the night I was born. They say they're coming back. If it's true, I'd like to see them dance above my lanterns. All together.
textes.Voir s'ouvrir une fleur de lune, une seu: To see a moonflower open, just one, one night, on my hill. They say it only opens by moonlight and smells of sugar and rain. I'd spend the whole night watching it, sitting in the grass.
textes.Voir un concert en entier. Un seul. Assi: To see a whole concert. Just one. Sitting in the grass, in the middle of the crowd, in front of the stage I repaired. Without carrying a single crate.
textes.Voir un jour le Serpent à Plumes voler a: To see the Feathered Serpent fly over Yaxché one day, just once, with all its green feathers. I wouldn't ask for anything. I'd watch.
textes.Voir un jour toutes les îles de l'archip: To see, one day, every island of the archipelago sitting at the same table, one huge Great Table from shore to shore, with a single checked tablecloth, and the Great Spaghetti serving everyone with its noodles.
textes.Voir un jour un Pied-Lourd et un Lumen d: To see, one day, a Heavy-Foot and a Lumen dance together on the Agora, under the auroras, without anyone finding it strange. And to win one game of chess against Tempo without cheating. Just one. To see how it feels.
textes.Voir un jour un apprenti réussir un sort: To see an apprentice one day pull off a spell I never managed to cast. My money's on Oscar: with all his getting everything wrong in such odd ways, he's bound to invent something eventually.
textes.Voir un vrai batteur derrière les Rats d: To see a real drummer behind the Bilge Rats. A real one, a brilliant one. And finally get to sit in the pit, with a lemonade, and say: “In 1977, I played just like him.” And have nobody contradict me.
textes.Voir une fois, une seule, quelque chose: To see, once, just once, something real to report. Climb up to Mère-Lune's and tell her: “Reported.” She'd be pleased.
textes.Voir une vraie perle de lumière. Bleue,: To see a real pearl of light. Blue, shining all by itself, with no paint and no lies. I'd have it set in a mount forged by Hector, he has the finest hand on the island. And I'd never sell it. Not even for its weight in gold. Especially not for its weight in gold.
textes.Voir, un soir, toute la ville éteindre s: To see, one evening, the whole city switch off its screens at the same time, just for one minute, to look at the stars above the towers.
textes.Voler ! Zéphyrine dirait que t'as pas be: Flying! Zéphyrine would say you don't need a potion. I say it's more fun with one. I'll give it a go. It might make your socks float.
textes.Voler ? Mais c'est le plus facile ! Il s: Fly? But that's the easiest thing! All you need is wings. Ah. You haven't got any. Right, I'll note it in my book: spell number three hundred and five.
textes.Voler ? Presque ! Léviter. C'est mieux :: Fly? Almost! Levitate. It's better: you don't bump into seagulls. To learn, you must first feel the wind in your hand. The wind loses feathers when it turns too fast: bring me three. They land where it blows the hardest: on the western hill, at the edge of the northern cliffs, and on the eastern cliff, above the sea.
textes.Voler, une fois, au-dessus du cratère, e: To fly, once, over the crater, and see the mountain from above, the way my crows see it. Croâ says he'll carry me. Croâ says a lot of things.
textes.Volontiers ! Les potins à gauche, les fa: Gladly! Gossip on the left, bills on the right, love notes between clocks in the middle… Thank you! Here, the capsule marked “To the visitor” that was waiting at the bottom of the basket: it's for you.
textes.Volontiers. Avec mes dés à moi, monsieur: Gladly. With my own dice, Monsieur Malaterre.
textes.Volontiers. Elle ne guérit rien, mais el: Gladly. It doesn't cure anything, but it smells so nice.
textes.Volt ! C'est déjà le début du mois ?: Volt! Is it the start of the month already?
textes.Volt ! Mon expérience a besoin d'un cris: Volt! My experiment needs a crystal.
textes.Volt dit que je lui dois un cristal depu: Volt says I've owed him a crystal for forty years. That's not true, it's thirty-nine and a half. I'll give it back tomorrow. Theoretically. Meanwhile, it makes an excellent paperweight.
textes.Volt dit toujours que ce n'est rien. Il: Volt always says it's nothing. He's been saying it for six hundred years, with the same face. I bring him tea at the foot of the Spire. He grumbles. He drinks it to the last drop.
textes.Volt fait semblant de ne pas m'aimer. Il: Volt pretends he doesn't like me. He brings me coffee every morning “because he made too much”. He's been making too much for four hundred years.
Volt brings me coffee every morning. He says he “made too much”. He's been making too much for four hundred years. He pretends not to like me. He's very bad at it. He's my best friend.
textes.Volt prétend que je lui ai emprunté un c: Volt claims I borrowed a crystal from him forty years ago. That's not true. It was thirty-nine and a half years ago. I'm giving it back tomorrow. Theoretically.
textes.Volt vient me voir tous les mois pour «: Volt comes to see me every month for “a little ache in the antennae”. It's never anything. I think he comes for a chat. I make him a tea, he grumbles, he leaves happy.
textes.Volt vient une fois par mois pour « une: Volt comes once a month for “a little ache in the antennae”. There's never anything wrong with them. I pour him a tea. He grumbles. He leaves happy. I think he mostly comes for a little chat.
textes.Volé ? Le mot est fort. Disons que tout: Stolen? That's a strong word. Let's say everything I sell has… travelled a lot. And its former owners aren't looking for it any more. They have other worries. Like swimming.
textes.Vos balayeurs m'ont encore écrit !: Your sweepers have written to me again!
textes.Vos bougainvilliers, Rose ! Encore plus: Your bougainvillea, Rose! Even lovelier than yesterday.
textes.Vos chaussures ! Qui ont marché sur tout: Your shoes! That have walked on every island! (He trembles.) No, no, keep them, you need them. But the thought… Fascinating.
textes.Vos livres envolés… je peux aider ?: Your runaway books… can I help?
textes.Vos navets… ils bougent, Père Gaubert ?: Your turnips… are they moving, Père Gaubert?
textes.Vos vingt boîtes du mois, madame Bricole: Your twenty boxes for the month, Madame Bricolette.
Your stars only come out at night.
Your stars have moved since yesterday.
textes.Votre atelier n'a plus de toit ?: Your workshop has lost its roof?
textes.Votre automate a bien dormi, Ambroise ?: Did your automaton sleep well, Ambroise?
textes.Votre automate saura partager. Il est tr: Your automaton will learn to share. It's very intelligent.
textes.Votre baguette, bien croustillante, comm: Your baguette, nice and crusty, just how Raymond likes them. You're his favourite customer without knowing it.
textes.Votre bouture grandit, Léa. Elle a déjà: Your cutting is growing, Léa. It's already eaten its stake.
Your coffee, then. On the house.
textes.Votre caillou est devenu une clochette d: Your pebble has become a little silver bell!
Your map is coming along, captain.
textes.Votre chaussette, non. Le cristal, si !: Your sock, no. The crystal, yes!
textes.Votre coup, Ambroise. Il vous reste huit: Your move, Ambroise. You have eight seconds left.
textes.Votre croissant est prêt, bien doré, com: Your croissant is ready, nice and golden, just how you like them. I put it aside before the Lord came by.
textes.Votre galette, Majesté ! Toute chaude !: Your cracker, Majesty! Nice and warm!
textes.Votre grand-père a reçu mon pot ?: Did your grandfather get my jar?
textes.Votre logement va être optimisé. Le bonh: Your home is about to be optimised. Happiness is not included in the offer.
textes.Votre machine à remonter le temps… J'y r: Your time machine… I think about it sometimes. In the evening, on the bench.
textes.Votre minute sans écrans… j'y pense enco: Your minute without screens… I still think about it, you know.
textes.Votre monnaie. Comptez-la, je sais que v: Your change. Count it, I know you like that. … Is it right? Of course it is.
textes.Votre monnaie. Je sais, vous faites conf: Your change. I know, you trust. Count it anyway. To please me.
textes.Votre petite explosion vous attend toujo: Your little explosion is still waiting for you, nice and warm. I've stored it far from Gaston's coffee.
textes.Votre phare a un problème ?: Is something wrong with your lighthouse?
textes.Votre piano tousse toujours, Prudence ?: Is your piano still coughing, Prudence?
textes.Votre pion a bougé tout seul, Moulay Bra: Your piece moved all by itself, Moulay Brahim.
Your secret is safe with me.
textes.Votre secret est toujours à l'abri ? Mon: Is your secret still safe? My pencil is put away. But it's twitching, I warn you.
textes.Votre serré, {surnom}. Je vous ai vu arr: Your short black, {surnom}. I saw you coming from a mile off: it was already in the cup.
Your tea, Moulay Brahim. And your piece.
textes.Votre tisane, Sauge. Froide, s'il vous p: Your herbal tea, Sauge. Cold, please.
textes.Voulez-vous savoir un secret, {surnom} ?: Would you like to know a secret, {surnom}? There's one phrase of the Singer's that I've never translated. A single note, very low, that goes on and on, and ends very softly. I think I know what it means. But I don't write it down. If I understood everything, I'd have no reason left to wait for her in the evening. So I keep that phrase aside. It's my rendezvous.
textes.Voulez-vous savoir une chose, {surnom} ?: Shall I tell you something, {surnom}? I don't want to understand everything she sings. If I understood it all, I'd have no reason left to wait for her in the evenings. So I always leave one phrase aside, untranslated. For next time. It's my way of always having a rendezvous.
Wanting to is already halfway there. The other half is a mushroom. Ask me when your heart is ready.
textes.Vous ! Combien de nouilles voyez-vous, l: You! How many noodles do you see, up there? Count carefully!
textes.Vous ! Ne croyez pas que je ne sais pas: You! Don't think I don't know what you did.
textes.Vous ! Oui, vous ! Une maison au Lisse-C: You! Yes, you! A home at the Lisse-Center? Launch price!
textes.Vous ! Oui, vous ! Vous avez l'air d'un: You! Yes, you! You look like an unregistered adventurer!
textes.Vous ! Oui, vous ! Vous avez une tête de: You! Yes, you! You look like a passenger!
You! Yes, you. Nothing. Have a nice day.
textes.Vous ! Un sujet d'étude ! Euh… bonjour !: You! A test subject! Er… hello!
textes.Vous ! Vous passez au-dessus de mon balc: You! You're flying over my balcony!
textes.Vous ! Vous êtes dans la Gazette de ce m: You! You're in this morning's Gazette. Page four. “A mysterious visitor”.
textes.Vous ! Vous êtes un ange. Hugo et moi, n: You! You're an angel. Hugo and I owe you everything.
textes.Vous aimez les jardins ? Le Lisse-Center: Do you like gardens? The Lisse-Center will have a garden! A plastic one! It needs no water, no sun, and it doesn't talk to tomatoes.
textes.Vous allez finir par ne rien posséder du: You'll end up owning nothing at all.
textes.Vous allez me rembourser, j'espère !: You're going to pay me back, I hope!
textes.Vous allez noter quelque chose. Voilà. E: You're going to write something down. There. It's come true.
textes.Vous aussi ! Margot vous a parlé, n'est-: You too! Margot's been talking to you, hasn't she? … Well. Perhaps. But then why does she wink when the Lighthouse is off? Eh? Eh?
textes.Vous avez aidé {qn} ! {Il} me l'a racont: You helped {qn}! {Il} told me all about it. I won't forget it, {surnom}.
textes.Vous avez assez bu pour aujourd'hui. Un: You've had enough to drink for today. A glass of water, and off to bed!
textes.Vous avez combien de chats ?: How many cats do you have?
textes.Vous avez commencé un livre ? Même un pe: Have you started a book? Even a little one? I've put one aside for you. With pictures, and a sturdy cover.
You said that two winters ago.
textes.Vous avez encore demandé de l'aide, aujo: Did you ask for help again today? Good.
textes.Vous avez encore des pièces en trop dans: Have you still got leftover pieces in your pockets? Bring them. I'll find where they go.
textes.Vous avez encore votre toit, professeur: Do you still have your roof, Professor?
textes.Vous avez essayé de dire bonjour à la ro: Have you tried saying hello to the rock?
textes.Vous avez eu l'occasion de lui parler, d: Have you had a chance to talk to them since?
textes.Vous avez fait la connaissance de {qn},: You've made the acquaintance of {qn}, I hear. What do you think?
textes.Vous avez frappé {qn} ? Ça ne se fait pa: You hit {qn}? That's just not done. Everyone's talking about it.
textes.Vous avez frappé {qn} ?! On m'a tout rac: You hit {qn}?! I've heard everything. You've got some nerve coming to talk to me.
textes.Vous avez frappé {qn}, à ce qu'on dit. J: You hit {qn}, so they say. I'm not saying it was deserved. I'm not saying it wasn't.
Word is you spoiled {qn}. Anyone who's kind to my folks is welcome at my place.
You look rushed off your feet.
textes.Vous avez laissé monter la marée, aujour: Have you let the tide rise today, {surnom}?
textes.Vous avez offert des fleurs à votre ami,: Have you given flowers to your friend since? No? The lavender is waiting. It's patient, but not eternal.
textes.Vous avez offert {objet} à {qn} ? Tout l: You gave {objet} to {qn}? Everyone knows {il} can't stand that. I'm still laughing.
textes.Vous avez pris le Funiculaire d'Azur, to: Have you taken the Azure Funicular, right down at the bottom? Then you know Marius Trident. For the reopening, I rode down with him. I tapped the glass of his cabin with my fingertips, listened, and said: “She's been well brought up.” He blushed. At the controls! Most irregular. I didn't make a note of it.
textes.Vous avez raison de ne pas juger trop vi: You're right not to judge too quickly.
textes.Vous avez rencontré la Présidente Ondine: Have you met President Ondine, at the bottom of the sea? For the reopening of their line, the four of us cut the ribbon: the Burgomaster, Dean Agathe, Ondine and I. Seven and a half centimetres each. She keeps my clouds in jars on a shelf. They all arrive empty. She says they contain the thought. Widespread sunny spells over my mood.
textes.Vous avez rencontré le Bourgmestre Hecto: Have you met Burgomaster Hector, down below? He sent me a forty-page speech of congratulations for the reopening. I read every word. Overcast, with long bright spells.
textes.Vous avez rencontré le Professeur Bentho: Have you met Professor Benthos, at the Azure Dome? My dear fellow “oceanographer”! He counts his lanternfish, I count my stars, and neither of us has finished. The line has reopened: at last I'm going down to see him. We'll start counting again together. Three thousand four hundred… drat.

Have you met Professor Benthos, at the Azure Dome? My oldest pen friend! He studies what's below, I study what's above. He names his jellyfish, I name my clouds. We agree on one point: a jellyfish is a cloud that chose the sea. The line has reopened: I'm going down to shake his hand on Thursday, at twelve minutes past three. Give or take a minute.
textes.Vous avez rencontré une petite Ondine, s: You've met a little Ondine, under another bubble? An Atlantean? (She smiles.) Then I'm no longer the only one. I hope she's less stubborn than I was at her age. And I hope that one day she'll come and have tea here. Or that we'll go to her.
textes.Vous avez toujours le marque-page que je: Do you still have the bookmark I gave you? Show me. … Good. I'm keeping an eye on you.
textes.Vous avez toujours votre souvenir ? Bien: Do you still have your keepsake? Good. I shan't buy it from you. I did think about it, I confess, but no.
textes.Vous avez tous la même tête…: You all have the same face…
textes.Vous avez trouvé mon discours magnifique: You found my speech magnificent. I added the word. It's in the third minute. Listen carefully next time.
textes.Vous avez une petite mine, vous. Vous av: You look a bit peaky. Did you sleep badly?
textes.Vous avez vu ? J'ai crié mon nom en enti: Did you see? I shouted my whole name, and it got scared! It works!
textes.Vous avez vu Anatole, à la Gare des Stra: Have you seen Anatole, at Strata Station? He told you about pulley twelve, I bet. (She puts her glasses back on.) It is very well greased, pulley twelve. I know it. I can hear it from here. I only hear what is regulation, and that is regulation.
textes.Vous avez vu le jet, là-bas ?: Did you see the spout, over there?
textes.Vous avez vu le voleur de croissants ?: Did you see the croissant thief?
textes.Vous avez vu passer le voleur ?: Did you see the thief go by?
textes.Vous avez été magnifique ! Moi, j'ai pri: You were magnificent! Me, I prayed very hard. It was teamwork.
textes.Vous aviez parlé d'une cabane en palette: You mentioned a pallet hut. I haven't forgotten. I shouldn't remember it. I do.
textes.Vous chantez tous les trois : « ♪ Tourne: You all three sing: “♪ Sunflower, sunflower, the moon watches you sleep… ♪”. It's a bit off-key, but very pretty.
textes.Vous chaussez les lunettes. Tout devient: You put on the glasses. Everything turns into coloured stars. You bump into a tree. You take them off.
You'd be looking under the throne, Majesty.
You'd be looking for your cane.
textes.Vous connaissez Mademoiselle Philippine,: Do you know Miss Philippine, from the Library of Maps? We write to each other. She sent me a copy of her map of the Fronde, drawn from Ysaé's descriptions. It's wrong in four places, and it's the most beautiful map I've ever seen. I won't correct a thing.
textes.Vous connaissez le Bourgmestre Hector ?: Do you know Burgomaster Hector? We reopened the Line together. He wanted a thirty-metre ribbon. I suggested thirty centimetres, as for the Clouds. He sighed, then he cut it with me. Afterwards, he gave a forty-minute speech. I replied in two sentences. People applauded the two sentences.
textes.Vous connaissez le Professeur Lunette, l: Do you know Professor Lunette, the astronomer up top? He wrote that he wanted to see “the stars down below”. My crystals. I'll show him round the Grotto, lamps off. But with a helmet. Even astronomers have heads.
textes.Vous connaissez le Professeur Lunette, à: Do you know Professor Lunette, at the Hautefond Observatory? He says my cloud Gontran hides his star Clémentine. We've signed an agreement: Gontran passes by in the day, Clémentine shines at night. Everyone's happy.
textes.Vous connaissez mon secret. Vous ne l'av: You know my secret. You haven't told anyone. Thank you. At the back of the pit, tonight?
textes.Vous croyez ? Alors surtout, ne vérifiez: You think so? Then whatever you do, don't check. Keep it just like that, nice and warm, without looking. An idea you believe is new is almost as good as a new idea. Believe me.
You were dancing with me. I saw.
textes.Vous demandez de l'aide. C'est la répons: You ask for help. That's the smartest answer I've heard all week. Nobody keeps engines running on their own. Not even me. Especially not me.
textes.Vous dites ça depuis cent ans. Je ne vou: You've been saying that for a hundred years. I still don't believe you.
textes.Vous dites ça maintenant. Attendez qu'el: You say that now. Wait until it finds your letterbox.
textes.Vous dormez debout, vous aussi. Je l'ai: You sleep standing up too. I told the Captain. He sighed. Twice.
textes.Vous dormez huit heures. Moi, cette nuit: You sleep eight hours. Me, last night, I did ten. Standing up. I'm improving.
textes.Vous défendiez la gravité. Vous aviez ra: You stood up for gravity. You were right. Yesterday I did an experiment without it. My glasses are on the roof.
textes.Vous entendez ce bruit ? … C'est un hibo: Do you hear that noise? … It's an owl. I think. I hope. It's an owl.
textes.Vous et votre Zéphyr… Voler avec un plan: You and your Zéphyr… Flying with a floor is cheating. But it's cheating I'd quite like to try.
textes.Vous et votre goût de l'aventure ! La fi: You and your taste for adventure! The blue vial made my kettle grow a moustache. Shall I keep it for you?
textes.Vous faites des choses qui font peur tou: You do scary things every day. I did a small one: I tapped on the wall of the Hall a bit louder. Does that count?
textes.Vous faites votre lit quand on vous rega: You make your bed when someone's watching? Well, I'm watching you. Just kidding. Or am I?
textes.Vous feriez ça ? Hugo a perdu son allian: You'd do that? Hugo lost his wedding ring playing in the waves, near the beach hut. It must be buried in the wet sand. You'd need a shovel… and a lot of luck.
textes.Vous gardez votre secret, et moi le mien: You keep your secret, and I keep mine. You're still at the top of the “Trustworthy People” file.
You taste after me. Yesterday I tasted. I stayed orange for an hour. Your turn?
textes.Vous improvisez… Je note. Je note aussi: You improvise… I'm noting it down. I'm also noting to always keep a potion aside for you. As a precaution. As a big precaution.
textes.Vous jetez ? Bon. Alors rendez-moi un se: You throw things away? Fine. Then do me a favour: throw them off the top of the cliff. Crane side. I'll take care of the rest.
textes.Vous l'avez fait exprès ?: Did you do that on purpose?
textes.Vous l'avez fini, ce roman, Colette ?: Did you finish that novel, Colette?
textes.Vous l'avez toujours, votre caillou ? Ga: Do you still have your pebble? Take good care of it. It's good for nothing, and that's what makes it irreplaceable.
textes.Vous levez la coupe bien haut. On croit: You raise the cup high. You almost hear, far away, the whole Games Clearing applauding.
textes.Vous lisez toujours les petites lignes,: You always read the small print, don't you? Of course. Ahem.
textes.Vous m'avez acheté %d objet, pour %d piè: You've bought %d item from me, for %d coins.
textes.Vous m'avez acheté %d objets, pour %d pi: You've bought %d items from me, for %d coins.
textes.Vous m'avez avoué avoir peur du noir. Je: You admitted to me you're afraid of the dark. I haven't told anyone. Tonight, I'll light up a little earlier.
textes.Vous m'avez crue, pour l'île. Je m'en so: You believed me, about the island. I remember it every time I look west.
textes.Vous m'avez dit qu'on ne peut pas tout p: You told me you can't forgive everything. I made a list of what I forgive Hugo for. It's long. It's tiny, actually.
textes.Vous m'avez dit que le Zéphyr vous faisa: You told me the Zéphyr scared you a little. Me too, sometimes. That makes two of us. That's already a crew.
textes.Vous m'avez dit que vous jouiez « un peu: You told me you play “a little”. I still haven't decided whether that was modesty or a trick.
textes.Vous m'avez dit que vous trouviez %s trè: You told me you found %s very nice.
textes.Vous m'avez dit que vous trouviez %s un: You told me you found %s a bit weird.
You told me that last week.
textes.Vous m'avez fait %d cadeau, le dernier :: You've given me %d gift, the last one: %s.
textes.Vous m'avez fait %d cadeaux, le dernier: You've given me %d gifts, the last one: %s.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit : un endroit où on m'at: You told me: a place where someone waits for me. I haven't forgotten. I won't forget.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit : une amitié. J'y repen: You told me: a friendship. I often think about it. It has no gears. And it keeps turning all the same.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit : « Ça dépend. » J'y pe: You told me: “It depends.” I think about it every evening, on the balcony. It depends… on me, mostly.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit que votre plus grand ex: You told me your greatest deed was yet to come. Mine too. We march on together, friend.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit que vous aviez fait une: You told me you'd done something that scared you, and that you were proud. I think about it every evening. In front of the door to the Hall.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit que vous fuyez. Je vous: You told me you run away. I saw you running towards the turnips the other day. I didn't say anything.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit que vous improvisiez. J: You told me you improvise. So I've planned for two: you, and your improvisation.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit que vous ne portiez jam: You told me you never wear a hat. Colombe is working on it. It's a surprise. Oops.
You told me you lose everything. If you're looking for something, ask me. It's my job.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit que vous vous essuyez l: You told me you wipe your feet when you remember. I have put down three more doormats. Do remember.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit que ça dépendait de quo: You told me it depended on what. I thought about it for a whole winter. You were right.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit « les deux ». Margot a: You told me “both”. Margot worked out that it was the best answer. She wrote down your name.
textes.Vous m'aviez dit « ça dépend ». Alors je: You told me “it depends”. So I'm keeping a colourful surprise for you. Only colourful.
textes.Vous m'aviez offert vos chaussures, en p: You offered me your shoes, in spirit. I made a label: “Traveller's shoes (lent, not given)”. The case is empty. It's very moving.
textes.Vous m'aviez promis une histoire. Je l'a: You promised me a story. I've filed it in my head, room three. It's the only room with no labels.
textes.Vous m'aviez répondu « la vie ». J'y ai: You answered “life”. I've thought about it again. It's still not a selling point. I think about it anyway.
textes.Vous me garderez une bouture ?: Will you save me a cutting?
textes.Vous mettez les oreilles de renard. Vous: You put on the fox ears. You feel like you can hear a little better. Somewhere, a rabbit is laughing.
textes.Vous méditiez très fort. Avec un ronflem: You were meditating very hard. With a snore.
textes.Vous n'allez pas me ressortir ça chaque: You're not going to bring that up every evening, are you?
textes.Vous n'avez pas de Carte d'aventurier ?: You don't have an Adventurer's card? Then I can't. Go and see Églantine. She stamps fast.
textes.Vous n'avez pas encore votre Carte d'ave: You don't have your Adventurer's card yet? O Dawn… Go to the Guild first. The crystal ball hardly bites at all.
textes.Vous n'avez pas vérifié votre idée, j'es: You haven't checked your idea, I hope? Keep it warm. I'm keeping one too. Tightly shut.
You don't have a mailbag any more.
textes.Vous n'avez rien tapé aujourd'hui, j'esp: You haven't whacked anything today, I hope?
You'd never thought about gravity. I think about it all the time. It makes me fall over three times a day.
textes.Vous n'aviez pas encore fait la chose qu: You hadn't done the thing that scared you yet. Neither had I. Are we still trying at the same time?
textes.Vous n'aviez pas encore goûté mes galett: You hadn't tried my crackers yet. Still not? Keep your innocence. But buy one anyway, as a decoration.
textes.Vous n'aviez pas tout écouté, la premièr: You didn't listen to all of it, the first time. I've saved the ending for you. It's about the mother-of-pearl paving. It's waiting for you.
textes.Vous n'êtes pas inscrit ? Hélas ! La règ: You're not registered? Alas! Rules are rules, even for Sir Tancrède de Tournevent. Go and see Églantine, at the counter!
textes.Vous ne dormez pas ? … Je connais. Je n': You don't sleep? … I know the feeling. I'll say no more. A cup of moon tea, perhaps. The management offers it to insomniacs.
textes.Vous ne dormez pas assez. Je vous ai gar: You don't sleep enough. I've saved you a spot against the gate wall. It's very comfortable.
textes.Vous ne goûtez jamais les potions inconn: You never taste unknown potions. I respect that. But I'll still show you some, just for fun.
textes.Vous ne lisez pas. … Je vais m'asseoir u: You don't read. … I'm going to sit down for a moment. Well. It doesn't matter. It's never too late. Start with a short book. With pictures.
textes.Vous ne me croyez toujours pas, pour l'î: You still don't believe me, about the island? Next clear night, the telescope is yours. Ten minutes.
textes.Vous ne passerez pas ! On a voté contre,: You shall not pass! We voted against it, unanimously!
textes.Vous ne rêvez jamais de voler, vous. Res: You never dream of flying. Stay that way. We need sensible people on this bench.
textes.Vous ne savez pas ? C'est honnête. C'est: You don't know? That's honest. It's nine. Repeat after me: one, blue; two, green…
textes.Vous ne… tu ne joues pas ? Alors pourquo: You don't… you don't play? Then why come into the Shark's Tooth? For the music? There isn't any. For me? … How flattering.
textes.Vous offrez des fleurs, parfois ? Et à q: Do you ever give flowers? And to whom, if it's not prying?
textes.Vous ouvrez la boîte. Il n'y a rien deda: You open the box. There is nothing inside. The maker kept his word.
textes.Vous ouvrez le parapluie. Il tire doucem: You open the umbrella. It tugs gently towards the sky… your heels lift off… You close it very quickly. You've come back down three centimetres. Phew.
textes.Vous ouvrez le parapluie. L'hélice se me: You open the umbrella. The propeller starts to spin, your hair flies away… and you don't.
You mentioned a pebble from your island. I'm still waiting for it. Well, I'm not rushing you. I'm waiting very patiently. Fascinating.
textes.Vous perdre ! (Il pose son crayon.) Je n: Getting lost! (He puts down his pencil.) I'd never thought of that. Maybe that's how you find the places that aren't on the maps.
You could at least read them.
textes.Vous pourriez m'apprendre à soigner ?: Could you teach me to heal?
textes.Vous prenez encore la capsule, aujourd'h: Taking the capsule again today? So am I.
textes.Vous préférez l'action. Alors je lirai p: You prefer action. Then I'll read for two, and you'll charge ahead for two. It's balanced.
textes.Vous qui adorez les surprises, regardez: You who love surprises, look behind you… No, nothing. Not yet. In twenty seconds, maybe.
textes.Vous qui aimez les cartes postales : j'e: You who love postcards: I've got a new one, with the lighthouse at sunset. Victor doesn't have that one. Ha!
textes.Vous qui aimez les choses jolies, revene: You who love pretty things, come back when the wind's from the south. It rains bubbles over the harbour.
textes.Vous qui aimez les orages, regardez le c: You who love storms, look at the sky tonight. There's electricity in the air. And in my coils.
textes.Vous qui aimez les perles, venez voir ma: You like pearls, so come and see my window. I have a new one. Round, honest. It looks like you.
textes.Vous qui aimez vous perdre, si vous trou: You who love getting lost, if you find a place that isn't on my map, come and tell me. I won't draw it. I'll keep it for you.
textes.Vous qui avez eu une idée nouvelle… elle: You who had a new idea… is it still yours? Nobody had it in the meantime? I was worried.
textes.Vous qui avez le vertige… vous avez appr: You with your vertigo… have you tamed a few steps since? I'm working on it too. Gently.
textes.Vous qui avez peur souvent, comme moi, s: You're often scared, like me, so know that I pray for both of us. Very loudly.
textes.Vous qui avez sauvé un chat, comme mon p: You saved a cat, like my father, so know that in my family, that's a title of nobility.
textes.Vous qui avez vaincu un grand monstre, B: You defeated a great monster, and Bertrand has made a song of it. I embellished it a little. Barely.
textes.Vous qui chantez devant les gens… un jou: You who sing in front of people… will you show me how it's done one day? Just the first note.
textes.Vous qui chantez seulement seul… j'ai pe: You who only sing alone… I thought of you last night. Windows shut.
textes.Vous qui cochez vos listes, je vous ai p: You tick off your lists, so I've prepared a special dungeon template for you. With a box for “come back”.
textes.Vous qui courez vers le danger, vous ête: You run towards danger, so you're on my reinforcements list. Second, after Sire Tancrède.
textes.Vous qui croyez aux légendes, écoutez ce: You who believe in legends, listen to this: a fisherman told me about a blue light last night. Another one! They're multiplying!
textes.Vous qui croyez aux signes : une mouette: You believe in signs: a pure white seagull landed on our balcony this morning. That's a good sign, isn't it? Say yes.
textes.Vous qui croyez à « certaines » légendes: You who believe in “some” legends: I found a new one this morning. Help me sort it out.
textes.Vous qui demandez votre chemin… Ici, dem: You who ask for directions… Here, ask Halo. But allow four minutes. He always starts with welcome.
textes.Vous qui goûtez sans hésiter, ma potion: You taste without hesitation, so my spotted potion is waiting for you. It's almost safe.
textes.Vous qui jetez tout : vous avez pensé à: You who throw everything away: have you thought about the cliff, crane side? I'll be waiting at the bottom.
textes.Vous qui lisez beaucoup, j'ai mis un liv: Since you read a lot, I've set a book aside for you. A little singed, but readable.
textes.Vous qui lisez des recettes, n'en essaye: Since you read recipes, never try one with me near the oven. It ends in lightning.
textes.Vous qui n'avez jamais peur, je reste pr: You're never scared, so I'm staying close to you. I hope it's catching.
textes.Vous qui n'avez pas de porte, sachez qu': You who have no door: know that at the palace, there are a hundred and twelve. I could lend you one.
textes.Vous qui n'avez pas le vertige, vous ave: You with no vertigo, did you look out of the cable car window? Tell me about the view. Nobody ever tells me enough about it.
textes.Vous qui n'avez pas peur du noir… la nui: You who aren't afraid of the dark… night is falling. Make the most of it. It's the finest hour.
textes.Vous qui n'offrez de fleurs à personne…: You who give flowers to nobody… take this one. If nobody gives you any, I'll start.
textes.Vous qui ne croyez pas au toujours… je n: You who don't believe in forever… I don't hold it against you. Not much. Neither does the engine.
textes.Vous qui ne croyez pas aux signes, dites: You don't believe in signs, so tell me the seagull on our balcony this morning didn't mean anything. Say it, please.
textes.Vous qui ne faites pas confiance aux mac: You who don't trust machines… You're still right. Hm. Unfortunately.
textes.Vous qui ne jouez pas aux échecs… toujou: You who don't play chess… still as wise as ever? Stay that way. It's rare, in Cliquetis.
textes.Vous qui ne perdez jamais rien, je vous: You never lose anything, and I admire you in silence. The Baron has lost his cane again.
textes.Vous qui pardonnez tout, je pense à vous: You forgive everything, so I think of you when I look at the sea from the balcony. I'm trying to do as you do.
textes.Vous qui pensez que tout existe déjà : P: You who think everything's been invented: Philibert has filed another patent. A button. It already existed. You'd agree.
textes.Vous qui perdez vos listes, sachez que j: You lose your lists, so know that I always keep a copy at the counter. Filed under your name.
textes.Vous qui perdez votre chemin, retenez ce: You who lose your way, remember this: in Montjoie, you always go up by going round. Always.
textes.Vous qui portez toujours un chapeau, j'a: You always wear a hat, so I thought of you this morning: I put on the one with the green feather.
textes.Vous qui portez un chapeau sous la pluie: You wear a hat in the rain, and it rained yesterday. I thought of you. I put on the drizzle one.
textes.Vous qui préférez les chats… Boulon a fa: You who prefer cats… Boulon pretended not to see you this morning. He's sulking. It'll pass.
textes.Vous qui préférez les chiens : Boulon vo: You who prefer dogs: Boulon saved you a nut. It's a bit chewed. It's a present.
textes.Vous qui préférez les pierres : j'ai reç: You prefer stones: I received a garnet this morning. Not perfect. Real. Come and look at it in the light.
textes.Vous qui préférez les robots : Boulon a: You who prefer robots: Boulon has learned a new trick. He gives his left paw. He'd never done that before.
textes.Vous qui regardez les cartes quand vous: You who look at maps when you're lost… I made you a little copy of Astralys. North is at the top. Normally.
textes.Vous qui rêvez d'une cheminée et d'un bo: You dream of a fireplace and a good bed: the Cottage awaits you. The bed is made. Has been for ten years.
textes.Vous qui rêvez souvent de voler… si Achi: You who often dream of flying… if Achille ever comes down, I'm warning you. You'll go after me.
textes.Vous qui savez attendre : le lac vous a: You who know how to wait: the lake saw you go by this morning. It said nothing. That's a good sign.
textes.Vous qui trouvez mes galettes délicieuse: You who find my crackers delicious… I've got a batch fresh and hot. I'll watch you eat one, it makes me happy.
textes.Vous qui vous essuyez toujours les pieds: You who always wipe your feet: know that the doormat in the hall awaits you. I had it brushed for you.
textes.Vous qui vous soignez tout seul… montrez: You who patch yourself up… show me that knee anyway. I won't tell a soul.
textes.Vous qui êtes du matin : comment était l: You, the morning person: how was the dawn today? Pink? I missed it, as always. Tell me.
