textes.Écliptique, mon discours a un nouveau mo: Écliptique, my speech has a new word.
textes.Écliptique, ta toge est encore de traver: Écliptique, your toga is crooked again.
Écliptique, one step to the left.
textes.Écliptique, vous avez dépassé de quatre: Écliptique, you've run four minutes over.
textes.Écliptique, ô grand chef, un discours br: Écliptique, oh great chief, will your speech be brief?
textes.Écliptique, ô grand orateur, ton discour: Écliptique, great speaker of the day, your speech goes on… all day.
textes.Écoute : chaque arbre a sa note. L'Arbre: Listen: every tree has its own note. The Mother Tree hums a C so low you can only hear it with your feet.
textes.Écoute aussi, petite. Pas seulement avec: Listen too, little one. Not just with your nose.
Listen too. Not just with your nose.
textes.Écoute bien, {surnom}. Ma mère disait qu: Listen carefully, {surnom}. My mother said she heard Kukulkan speak to her, in the wind at the summit. I've seen the serpent's shadow come down eighty times. I've never heard his voice. Not once. I've told no one. Maybe he speaks very softly. Or maybe he trusts me, and has nothing to tell me.
textes.Écoute bien. Il y a deux cents ans, le L: Listen closely. Two hundred years ago, the Léviathan came from beyond the horizon. The biggest ship ever built. Its masters were looking for an island that was said to have a heart. One stormy night, they found it. A little too quickly.
textes.Écoute la musique des lieux : la mer, le: Listen to the music of a place: the sea, the wind, the birds. They tell you where you are.
Listen to the wind: it's singing.
textes.Écoute, chose lisse. Au nord, dans le Ci: Listen, smooth thing. North, in the Bone Hollow, lives Grosse-Dent. Big lizard. Big teeth. Very big roar. At night Grosse-Dent come, Grosse-Dent break drying racks, Grosse-Dent eat all Clan's meat. Clan scared. You… you not same. Maybe you hunt Grosse-Dent?
textes.Écoute, voyageur. Quel est l'être qui ma: Listen, traveller. What being walks on four legs in the morning, on two legs at noon, and on three legs in the evening?
textes.Écoute, {surnom}, et que ça reste entre: Listen, {surnom}, and keep this between us. I can't swim. A Kerhervé, admiral of Carène, who sinks like an anvil. The morning I went to parley with Croc-de-Sel, under my coat I had a belt of corks, sewn the night before. My hands were shaking. He thought it was anger.
textes.Écoute, {surnom}, et tu ne le répètes pa: Listen, {surnom}, and don't repeat this. The day after the bath, I went to apologise. Borée was sitting by the lake, talking to it very softly, like to a sick friend. I didn't dare. Since then, every winter, I leave a bundle of twisted wood at his door, before dawn. He thinks it's Mathurin. The master of frost gets cold feet at night. I know it.
textes.Écoute, {surnom}, ça reste entre nous. L: Listen, {surnom}, this stays between us. The jungle boat that doesn't stop at Toni's any more? It's my cousin Mano's. He drops all his coconuts off at the beach hut, because we're family. I didn't have the heart to say no to him. And I don't dare tell Toni. Every evening, he tells me about his coconuts that never arrive, and I drink my glass without a word.
textes.Écoute, {surnom}. Dans mon coffre, il y: Listen, {surnom}. In my chest, there's an all-white huipil. The most beautiful I've ever woven. Not one colour. It's for my wedding, if a certain jaguar ever makes up his mind to send someone to talk to my mother. He's slow, Balam. A jaguar waits for hours before pouncing. Me, I finished the huipil two moons ago.
textes.Écoute, {surnom}. Depuis la nuit du four: Listen, {surnom}. Since the night of the kiln, two fingers on my right hand can't feel the clay any more. Nothing. So I work by ear: I tap the jar, I listen whether it rings true. Nobody knows. Especially not Mérit. She'd think it was her fault. It isn't. The kiln was well worth two fingers. And she bakes good bread in it.
textes.Écoute-le : il chante. Les anciens disen: Listen to it: it's singing. The old ones say you can hear it all the way to the surface on calm nights. The whales answer it.
textes.Écoute-moi bien, {surnom}, et oublie aus: Listen carefully, {surnom}, and forget it right away. The night before he died, my grandfather took my hand and said: “It isn't gold, lad.” Nothing else. I don't know what's in that chest. And what if it's nothing? A whole crew, a galleon, weeks of searching… for nothing. I've never repeated that sentence. If you repeat it, I'll salt you. For real.
textes.Écoute. Avant Tazira, avant Carène, avan: Listen. Before Tazira, before Carène, before everything, the island was a single mountain, and the mountain had a heart. Four peoples guarded four gates. Then the gates closed, and only one remains.
textes.Écouter Rachid, le marchand de tapis du: Listen to Rachid, the carpet seller of the Tazira souk, talk about the carpet of stars
textes.Écouter le Vieux Corentin, le conteur de: Listen to Old Corentin, the storyteller of Carène (on the deck of the Léviathan, or at La Dernière Bordée in the evening)
textes.Écouter le piano mécanique de Prudence T: Listen to Prudence Touche's mechanical piano (Fair stand, west side)
textes.Écoutez ! Elle sonne ! Ma vieille horlog: Listen! It's chiming! My old clock is chiming!
textes.Écoutez, écoutez. Celle-là chuchote en a: Listen, listen. This one whispers in English.
textes.Écoute… Ce petit « plop », là ? Non ? Mo: Listen… That little “plop”, there? No? Me neither. But I believe in it with all my heart, and they know it.
textes.Écrase-le comme un cafard de cale !: Squash him like a bilge cockroach!
textes.Écrasé par un piston ! Compte : il frapp: Crushed by a piston! Count: it strikes, it rises… go while it is up.
textes.Écrire ? … Oui. C'est bien, écrire. On p: Writing? … Yes. Writing is good. You can cross things out, start again, pick your words. And you don't have to see the other person's face. … Why are you looking at me like that?
textes.Écrire la grande chronique de Forgefer,: To write the great chronicle of Forgefer, from the forty-two kings down to today. With a chapter about you, if you stay long enough for me to learn to spell your name properly.
textes.Écrire le Grand Livre de l'Île : les his: To write the Great Book of the Island: the stories of the three peoples, in hieroglyphs, in Yaxché glyphs and in Aztlán pictures, side by side. Citlali will draw. I'll do the talking. We'll need a lot of papyrus.
textes.Écrire le grand traité de médecine pirat: Write the great treatise of pirate medicine: how to treat a brawl bump, a lookout's sunburn, a sunfish indigestion and a heart broken in Tortuga. With drawings.
textes.Écrire un livre, un seul, et ne pas le g: To write a book, just one, and not rub it out. I haven't found what to write yet. Perhaps the story of the island that lost its colours and the traveller who found them again.
textes.Écrire un roman qui se passe ici, à Port: To write a novel set here, in Port-Azur. A widowed grocer, an English lord who wants to buy a jar of jam from her, a fortune-teller who'd predicted it… I'm not making anything up, mind you. I'm taking notes.
To write a happy song. Just one. A short one, even: three verses. And to play it one morning, not under a window, but in the same room as her.
textes.Écrou est la meilleure mécanicienne du p: Écrou is the best mechanic in the harbour, and the granddaughter of a very, very angry shepherd. She's right to be angry too. I'd like her to be a little less so.
textes.Écrou, c'est ma nièce, ma fierté et mon: Écrou is my niece, my pride and joy and my little screwdriver. She saved my cable car at fifteen, she fixes the whole harbour, and she forgets to eat. It runs in the family.
textes.Églantine ! Tu as vu ma lettre ? Une vie: Églantine! Have you seen my letter? An old letter, in a drawer…
textes.Églantine est l'amie la plus fidèle, la: Églantine is the most loyal, most organised and, before she met me, worst-dressed friend in Montjoie. Now she's just loyal and organised.
textes.Églantine est la seule personne qui m'ai: Églantine is the only person who has always smiled at me, even covered in jelly. Especially covered in jelly. She says it's professional. I know it's affection.
textes.Églantine est ma meilleure amie. Le dima: Églantine is my best friend. On Sundays, we have tea, and she sorts my buttons by colour without realising. I don't stop her. It relaxes her.
textes.Églantine est redevenue notre reine ! Le: Églantine is our queen again! The kingdom is blooming once more, thanks to you.
textes.Églantine refuse toutes mes réclamations: Églantine turns down all my complaints with a smile of steel. I respect her. She's the only person in Montjoie I've never managed to change the mind of. Along with my rival.
textes.Églantine écrit mes annonces avec une éc: Églantine writes my announcements in perfect handwriting. I shout them a bit my own way. She sighs. But she smiles while she sighs. She's a friend.
textes.Églantine, c'est la Guilde. Moi, je suis: Églantine is the Guild. I'm the beard. Without her, Montjoie would be a heap of papers, bumps and lost contracts. With her, it's a tidy heap.
textes.Églantine, tiens-toi droite. Ton col…: Églantine, stand up straight. Your collar…
textes.Électre a été ma meilleure élève, et de: Électre was my best student, by far. She has brilliant ideas and a storm kite. I worry about both.
textes.Électre est la seule personne de Cliquet: Électre is the only person in Cliquetis who makes more sparks than I do! She thinks I'm dangerous. It's the nicest thing anyone's said to me this year.
textes.Électre est la seule, à l'Académie, qui: Électre is the only one at the Academy who doesn't laugh at my nights. She measures with me, she asks the right questions, and she makes lamps for people who live in the dark.
textes.Électre est une femme brillante, au sens: Électre is a brilliant woman, literally. We weren't made to live together: two currents that just didn't connect. But for Sunday lunch together, we're perfect.
textes.Électre m'a fabriqué une petite lampe ro: Électre made me a little red battery lamp, so I can read my notes without dazzling myself. White light blinds the eye for twenty minutes; red doesn't. She gave it to me saying: “So you're never in complete darkness.” Very seriously, like a prescription. I wear it around my neck every night.
textes.Électre. Léonce t'a parlé de sa fusée ve: Électre. Did Léonce tell you about his green rocket?
textes.Électrique ! J'ai branché la fontaine-ba: Electric! I wired the bathtub fountain on the square to Boulon's crane. When he lifts a container, the fountain lights up. It's completely useless. It's magnificent.
textes.Électrique ! J'ai trente diablotins qui: Electric! I've got thirty imps who can finally light a candle without lighting the candle next to it. That's huge progress.
textes.Émerveillé. Vous êtes vraiment monté sur: Amazed. You really went up to the floating island? You'll have to draw me the Citadel.
textes.Émue. Depuis la réouverture, des famille: Moved. Since the reopening, families from up top have been visiting the school. A child from up top asks a child from down here: “What's the sea like, from inside?” And the other one answers: “And the sky, from underneath?” And they tell each other. I've nothing left to do. It's the best lesson of the year.
textes.Énergie à fond ! Tu es devenu un vrai po: Full energy! You've become a true Boucan mosher!
textes.Énervé. Quelqu'un a mis du soda sur le b: Annoyed. Someone spilled soda on the B button. It's sticky. How am I supposed to do combos with a sticky button?
textes.Énigme gratuite : « Au fond du royaume,: Free riddle: “Deep in the kingdom, beneath the brambles, sleeps what was forgotten.” You might find it, one day.
textes.Énigmes, gardiens, portes, quêtes, coffr: Riddles, guardians, doors, quests, hidden chests: the hero grows by overcoming them.
textes.Épaisses ! Des nouilles qui tiennent au: Thick! Noodles that stick to your ribs. You know how to live.
textes.Épanoui. Le grand nénuphar du bassin a o: Blooming. The big water lily in the pond opened a flower last night. It opens one every hundred years. I watched it all night. It smelled of mint and thunderstorms.
textes.Épanouie ! Mes tournesols ont encore gra: In full bloom! My sunflowers have grown again. They're taller than me. They look down on me, but kindly.
textes.Épanouie. J'ai vendu tous mes bouquets d: Blooming. I sold all my lavender bouquets before noon.
textes.Épatante ! Ma grenouille en croûte a fai: Splendid! My frog in pastry made a traveller weep with joy. Well, maybe it was the pepper. But I decided it was joy.
textes.Épicé ! Ah, un aventurier ! Tiens, goûte: Spicy! Ah, an adventurer! Here, taste this pepper. … Are you crying? That's normal. It means it likes you.
textes.Épluchées ! Il en manque deux, comme vos: Peeled! Two are missing, like your fingers!
textes.Épées, haches, pelles ! Forgées à la vap: Swords, axes, shovels! Forged with steam and tempered with laughter! Feel the weight, go right ahead. You have {pieces} coins.
textes.Équilibre : parfait. Température du cœur: Balance: perfect. Heart temperature: lukewarm. Heart mood: purring. (This last reading was added by Engineer Nova.)
textes.Équilibre de l'île : parfait. Bon, à un: Island balance: perfect. Well, give or take a millimetre. That's Théo bouncing around in his capsule.
textes.Établir un record au parcours d'anneaux: Set a record on the ring course in the Zero-Gravity Garden
textes.Étape cinq : à l'ouest, le Café Nébuleus: Stop five: to the west, the Nebula Café. The cook, Gloubi, has four arms. If someone shakes your hand three times, that is normal. If it is four times, that is affection.
textes.Étape deux : la Flèche de Cristal. Cent: Stop two: the Crystal Spire. A hundred and ten metres of pure crystal. At the very top beats the Spire's Heart, which keeps the island afloat. Do not knock on the Heart's door. It is busy.
textes.Étape dix : à l'est, le Spatioport. Troi: Stop ten: to the east, the Spaceport. Three landing pads, a hangar, a control tower. The red saucers belong to Comète. Please keep clear of the red saucers.
textes.Étape douze : à l'ouest, les Jardins sus: Stop twelve: to the west, the Hanging Gardens, and at the end of the bridge of light, the Zero-Gravity Garden. You jump three times higher there. Please come back down. Everyone comes back down. Gently.
textes.Étape huit : en face, l'Académie des Sci: Stop eight: opposite, the Academy of Sciences. If you hear an explosion, that is Professor Quasar. If you hear nothing at all, that is Murmure, the librarian.
textes.Étape neuf : au nord, l'Observatoire, su: Stop nine: to the north, the Observatory, on its islet, linked by a bridge of light. The bridge lights up when you approach. It goes out when you are scared. No. That is a joke. Beep. Error: unauthorised joke.
Stop number one: the Crystal Spire. Stop number two: the Agora. Stop number three… Would you like the full tour? It has fifteen stops. You can also just follow me. I do it all day long.
Stop eleven: the holographic fountain. Every minute, a new planet spins in the jet of water. Ondelune, Saturn, Earth… Look closely. Oooh. … Beep. The guide's favourite stop. Pleasant error.
textes.Étape quatorze : au sud-est, le Portail: Stop fourteen: to the south-east, the Welcome Gate and its beam, which links the island to the sea. Halo the guardian will give you a four-minute speech there. Allow four minutes. Allow five.
textes.Étape quatre : l'Agora des Étoiles, la g: Stop four: the Agora of Stars, the main square. Its benches float forty centimetres above the ground. Please sit down gently. The benches are sensitive.
textes.Étape quinze : la Nuit des Aurores, chaq: Stop fifteen: the Night of the Auroras, every night from ten p.m. to two a.m. Prisme dances, Vibrato plays, the sky lights up. End of the tour. Thank you for your attention. Start of the tour. Beep.
textes.Étape sept : le Musée des Mondes. L'Arch: Stop seven: the Museum of Worlds. Orbe the Archivist displays objects from all the islands down below. The centrepiece is an old boot. Please admire it. Orbe is watching you.
textes.Étape six : à l'est, le Bazar galactique: Stop six: to the east, Nébula's Galactic Bazaar. It sells everything that exists in the galaxy. And a mechanical duck. Beep.
textes.Étape treize : au nord-ouest et au nord-: Stop thirteen: to the north-west and north-east, the Bubble District, where the Lumens live. And further north-east, the Greenhouse of Species: sky jellyfish, gurgles. Do not tap on the glass. The gurgles answer.
textes.Étape trois : la Salle du Conseil, au pi: Stop three: the Council Hall, at the foot of the Spire. Elder Astrée has presided here for a thousand years. She is one thousand and forty-three years old. Do not tell her. She knows.
textes.Étrangement… calme. J'ai signé le Bail c: Strangely… calm. I signed the shared lease. I thought it would hurt. It felt… good? It's a non-optimised sensation. I shall study it.
Stranger! The sun has led you here.
textes.Éveillé ! Les étoiles se lèvent, moi aus: Wide awake! The stars are rising, and so am I.
textes.Évidemment ! Enfin quelqu'un d'honnête !: Obviously! Finally, an honest person! I'll write to Héloïse. By pigeon. With your name in big letters.
textes.Évidemment ! Enfin quelqu'un de sensé su: Obviously! Finally someone sensible on this island.
textes.Évidemment ! Ici, on a un volcan entier: Obviously! We've got a whole volcano of tomato sauce here, it would be rude to have anything else.
textes.Évidemment ! Tu as du goût, toi ! Je vai: Obviously! You've got taste! I'm writing to Firmin about it. He'll whistle with rage. That'll keep him in steam for the week.
textes.Évidemment, c'est moi qui les ai faits !: Of course they are, I made them! Arm wrestling, tonight?
textes.Évidemment, que c'était moi. (Elle relèv: Of course it was me. (She lifts her visor, very proud.) Do you know what was inside the “Turbo-Adventure 3000”? A virus that opens windows everywhere to sell… other programs by Fil. It's not even a nasty virus. It's a commercial virus. Go and tell him. Me, when he sees me, he runs off.
textes.Évidemment. Elle a encore soif, cette en: Of course. Still thirsty, that sign.
textes.Évidemment. Je n'ai pas tant de visiteur: Obviously. I don't get that many visitors. In fact, I only get one. You.
textes.Évidemment. Je tiens les comptes, {surno: Of course. I keep the accounts, {surnom}.
textes.Évidemment. Personne n'y pense. Elles ti: Of course. Nobody thinks about it. They hold everything up, and nobody thinks about it. Go on. Walk. They're used to it.
textes.Être Grande Liftière, avec la casquette: To be Grand Liftkeeper, with the gold-braided cap, and take everyone up, even people who are scared of heights. Especially them. And to have a bolt from every floor of the Column.
textes.Être capitaine d'un vrai navire, avec un: To be captain of a real ship, with a feathered hat. Go and fetch dad from the south, bring him back with his whole crew, and throw an enormous party on the square. Even the pirates can come. If they behave.
textes.Être capitaine de mon propre bateau ! Un: Being captain of my own ship! A little one, with a green sail, and Gros-Louis as first mate. And a parrot that says “Hello, Captain Pierre!”.
textes.Être coureuse ET boulangère ! Je livrera: To be a runner AND a baker! I'll deliver bread at a run, faster than Uncle Bondi, and it'll still be piping hot when it gets right to the top of the Lookout, to Croc-Gris!
textes.Être le marchand le plus riche des Trois: To be the richest merchant of the Three Suns, with a stall in every village. And one day, to sell something to a god. Directly. Without the high priest in the middle.
textes.Être pêcheur de trésors ! Avec un bateau: To be a treasure fisher! With a black ship with a blue sail, Tibo as my second, and Yasmine captain of another ship, so we can race!
textes.Île de Braise, l'Arène des Cornes: Ember Island, the Arena of Horns
textes.Île de Braise, la poste du port: Ember Island, the harbour post office
textes.Île de Montjoie, le Donjon des Mille Mar: Montjoie Island, the Dungeon of a Thousand Steps
textes.Île du Boucan, l'imprimerie de la Filatu: Boucan Island, the Spinning Mill print shop
textes.Ô Aube bienveillante, protège-nous, prot: O kindly Dawn, protect us, protect me, especially me, well, all of us!
textes.Ô Aube, donne-lui la force d'un taureau: O Dawn, give him the strength of a bull and the gentleness of a lamb! Well, mostly the strength, right now.
textes.Ô Aube, faites qu'il soit gentil. Il n'a: O Dawn, let it be nice. It doesn't look nice. Let it be small. It doesn't look small.
textes.Ô Aube, gardez-nous ! … Voilà, c'est fai: O Dawn, watch over us! … There, done. We can go.
textes.Ô Aube, referme cette bosse ! … Et celle: O Dawn, close up this bump! … And that one too. And… there!
textes.Ô ciel qui danse et qui scintille… euh…: O sky that dances and that sparkles… er… that glows… like a… Oh well. It's pretty.
textes.Ô passant ! Viens par ici ! … Ça ne rime: O passer-by! Come over here! … That doesn't rhyme. Come anyway!
textes.Ô toi qui passes ! Écoute ce vers !: O thou who passest by! Hear this line!
textes.Ô visiteur venu d'en bas, bienvenue sous: O visitor from down below, welcome to our skies! My name is Lyre, and I speak… in verse… when I try. (She counts on her fingers.) That last rhyme was a flop. Let me start again: I am Lyre, the poet so fine, and tenderness rhymes in every line.
textes.Ô visiteur, réponds-moi vite : que préfè: O visitor, answer me quick: in a poem, what's your pick?
textes.Ô voyageur venu des mers lointaines, en: O traveller come from distant seas, in vivid hues and shoes that squeeze… (He stops.) That squeeze out sand, I meant. Achille Buvard, poet. I'm writing the epic of the Great Downpour. I'm up to the first drop.
textes.Ô voyageur, réponds à ma question : préf: O traveller, answer my question: do you prefer poems that rhyme, or ones that don't?
textes.Ô {surnom}, te revoilà, comme la lune au: O {surnom}, you're back with me, like the moon at dusk, you see! Sit right here by Lyre's knee: I've a poem for you to see. … Hear. For you to hear. “See” rhymed better.
textes.à qui étaient vraiment les ailes: who the wings really belonged to
textes.ça vient d'Astralys, l'île qui flotte da: it comes from Astralys, the island floating in the sky
textes.écolière de l'École des Abysses (10 ans): schoolgirl at the School of the Deep (10), who has never seen the sky
textes.épouser un homme qui ne parle pas: marrying a man who doesn't talk
textes.… (Gaspard baisse la tête, l'air coupabl: … (Gaspard hangs his head, looking guilty, and points at the parrot. The parrot: “KHADIJA! CROSS! A BIT! THE ADMIRAL TALKED TOO MUCH!”)
textes.… (Gaspard compte sur ses doigts. La vig: … (Gaspard counts on his fingers. The lookout, in the morning. The jetty, in the afternoon, with a rod and Si Larbi. A whale drawn for Youssef. A drum for Omar. A sleeping camel, for Zineb. Then he points at a roof near the Fondouk and shrugs. The parrot: “HE SAW! FROM UP THERE, HE SAW WHERE! THE ADMIRAL SHOUTS IT! NOBODY LISTENS TO A PARROT! SQUAWK!”)
textes.… (Gaspard dessine sur son ardoise une p: … (On his slate, Gaspard draws a little island, a tower and a beam of light. He points at himself, very small, at the top of the tower. The parrot: “THE NORTHERN LIGHTHOUSE! PAPA KEEPER! GASPARD TALKED IN BITS! THE OTHERS LAUGHED! SO GASPARD WENT QUIET! HE WATCHED THE SEA! SQUAWK!”)
textes.… (Gaspard fait des gestes : Amine montr: … (Gaspard gestures: Amine points at the rooftops, opens his hands, as if asking. Gaspard points at a roof near the Fondouk. Amine points at the same roof. They look at each other, and Gaspard laughs silently, holding his belly. The parrot: “THEY KNEW! BOTH OF THEM! SHH!”)
textes.… (Gaspard fait le geste de dormir, les: … (Gaspard mimes sleeping, hands under his cheek, then points at the Fondouk and smiles. The parrot: “ZINEB! THE ROOM! NOT TOO STEADY! THANK YOU!”)
textes.… (Gaspard fait le geste de lancer une l: … (Gaspard mimes casting a line, then sits down, very calm, eyes half-closed. The parrot: “SI LARBI! NOTHING BITES! VERY RELAXING!”)
textes.… (Gaspard hausse les épaules, l'air com: … (Gaspard shrugs knowingly and gives you a little nudge with his elbow. The parrot: “DEPENDS! DEPENDS! CLEVER!”)
textes.… (Gaspard imite un chameau qui ronfle,: … (Gaspard imitates a camel snoring, very loudly, then the waves with his hand: it's the same. He smiles, reassured. Then he mimes a date placed on a pillow, and eats it with his eyes closed. The parrot: “A DATE! ALWAYS A DATE! ZINEB IS KIND!”)
textes.… (Gaspard lève dix doigts, puis cinq :: … (Gaspard holds up ten fingers, then five: fifteen years old. With two fingers, he climbs up his arm to his shoulder: the lookout. Then he makes a bird with his hands, which comes and lands on him. The parrot, very proud: “SOUTHERN PORT! THE ADMIRAL FALLS FROM THE SKY! THE ADMIRAL CHOOSES GASPARD! AT NIGHT, THE ADMIRAL LISTENS TO THE DECK! HE LEARNS ALL THE WORDS! EVEN THE RUDE ONES!”)
textes.… (Gaspard met sa main en visière et reg: … (Gaspard shades his eyes with his hand and looks very far away. He shows ten fingers. Then he makes big swimming movements, more and more tired, and throws an imaginary rope with all his strength. He pulls, pulls, pulls. The parrot: “A RED HEAD IN THE WATER! THE ROPE! HEAVE! HEAVE! ROSA ON BOARD!” Gaspard puts two fingers side by side, like a brother and a sister.)
textes.… (Gaspard mime : la vigie, la main en v: … (Gaspard mimes: the lookout, hand shading his eyes, a little red head far off in the waves. He throws the rope, pulls, pulls. He shows you his palms, as if they were still burning. The parrot: “TEN YEARS OLD! TEN YEARS OLD! THE REDHEAD SWAM LIKE A SEAL! SQUAWK!”)
textes.… (Gaspard mime : lui à la vigie, Yousse: … (Gaspard mimes: him on the lookout, Youssef on the jetty, both pointing at the same spot, in front of the Skala. He makes a spout of water burst from his fingers. Then he draws a whale on his slate, a really big one, and points it downwards, towards the jetty. The parrot: “THE SAME SPOUT! THE SAME MORNING! NOBODY BELIEVES IT!”)
textes.… (Gaspard mime Amine qui le suit sur le: … (Gaspard mimes Amine following him along the quay, on tiptoe, to see the bird. The parrot turns its head, one eye, then the other: “GROUPER-FACE!” Gaspard mimes Amine jumping for joy and running to repeat it to the whole port. He shrugs: it's not even a rude word.)
textes.… (Gaspard mime la criée, la foule, Saïd: … (Gaspard mimes the fish auction, the crowd, Saïd on his platform. Then the parrot perched on a barrel, puffing up its feathers. The parrot, without warning: “DRISS TALKS TO HIS BOAT! DRISS SNORES!” Gaspard hides his face in his hands. He shows the whole auction laughing, and Khadija, bright red, behind her nets.)
textes.… (Gaspard mime la nuit sur la Murène :: … (Gaspard mimes the night on the Murène: the pump creaking, creaking, and him blocking his ears. Then he walks to the Fondouk. The parrot, in its most polite voice: “A ROOM THAT'S NOT TOO STEADY!” Gaspard mimes Zineb thinking, then pointing at the camel stable. Above it, he sleeps like a baby.)
textes.… (Gaspard mime la place, la fête, les l: … (Gaspard mimes the square, the festival, the lanterns. Then the parrot whistling, and the crowd stopping their dancing to listen. The parrot, very proud: “BOOM TA-KA BOOM! RIGHT ON THE BEAT! THE SQUARE APPLAUDS THE ADMIRAL!” Gaspard pretends to bow, then shows you that nobody ever applauded him.)
textes.… (Gaspard montre Youssef, puis lui-même: … (Gaspard points at Youssef, then at himself, then makes a big circle with his arms. The parrot: “THE CLUB! THE CLUB OF PEOPLE NOBODY BELIEVES! TWO MEMBERS! THREE WITH THE ADMIRAL!”)
textes.… (Gaspard montre des matelots qui rient: … (Gaspard shows sailors laughing and pointing at him, and him, lips sealed. Then he shows Rosa arriving, fists on her hips, and the sailors all falling silent at once. The parrot: “WHO'S MAKING FUN OF GASPARD? WHO? BERTHA! FIRE!” Gaspard laughs without a sound.)
textes.… (Gaspard montre le haut du mât, puis t: … (Gaspard points at the top of the mast, then taps very softly on an imaginary rail, with his fingertips, eyes closed. Boom, ta-ka. He puts a finger to his lips. The parrot, very quietly: “GASPARD PLAYS TOO. IN SECRET. UP THERE.”)
textes.… (Gaspard montre le mât, puis pose la m: … (Gaspard points at the mast, then holds his hand at the height of the first rung. No higher. He wags his finger at the second. The parrot: “FIRST RUNG! NO MORE! THE FIRST MATE IS WATCHING!”)
textes.… (Gaspard montre le perroquet. Le perro: … (Gaspard points at the parrot. The parrot: “THE ADMIRAL! I'M THE ADMIRAL! GASPARD DOESN'T TALK, THE ADMIRAL TALKS FOR TWO!”)
textes.… (Gaspard montre ses yeux, puis l'horiz: … (Gaspard points at his eyes, then at the horizon. The parrot: “HE SEES EVERYTHING! HE SEES THE WHALE!”)
textes.… (Gaspard montre un enfant haut comme s: … (Gaspard shows a child no taller than his belt, trotting after him everywhere. He smiles. The parrot: “THE KID! GROUPER-FACE! GROUPER-FACE!”)
textes.… (Gaspard montre une mouette qui passe,: … (Gaspard points at a passing seagull, then at the parrot opening its beak. The parrot: “A BITE! A BITE!” Gaspard mimes Si Larbi pulling in his line, empty, and giving the bird a sideways look. He does it ten times, twenty times. Then he mimes two men not moving at all, and smiles.)
textes.… (Gaspard pointe du doigt la falaise de: … (Gaspard points at the cliff behind the Skala. The parrot: “THE CAVES! THE CAVES! SHH! SHH! SQUAWK!”)
textes.… (Gaspard pose la main sur son cœur, pu: … (Gaspard puts his hand on his heart, then points at a lock of hair and makes the sign for red. The parrot: “ROSA! SISTER ABOARD! THE BEST!”)
textes.… (Gaspard regarde autour de lui, puis é: … (Gaspard looks around, then writes in chalk, slowly: “I HAVE A VOICE. I HARDLY STUTTER ANY MORE. I'M KEEPING IT FOR SOMETHING IMPORTANT. ONLY ROSA HAS HEARD IT: A LULLABY FROM MY ISLAND, ONE STORMY NIGHT.” He lets you read it. Then he wipes it all off with his sleeve. The parrot, very softly, for once: “Shh.”)
textes.… (Gaspard sort de sa poche une bobine d: … (Gaspard takes an imaginary spool of blue thread out of his pocket and holds it out, head down. Then he takes his handkerchief and drops it over the parrot, like a lid. He shows you: now, whenever Khadija speaks, he does that. From under the handkerchief comes: “… SQUAWK.”)
textes.… (Gaspard sort son ardoise et te montre: … (Gaspard takes out his slate and shows you a chalk drawing: the whole coast, seen from the lookout, with the caves and the reefs. Under every rock, a name written very small. He points at Si Larbi, then at his mouth, then at the slate. The parrot: “LARBI SAYS THE NAMES! GASPARD WRITES!”)
… (Gaspard sighs and wipes the slate. The parrot, delighted: “BLABBERMOUTH! BLABBERMOUTH! SQUAWK!” Gaspard flicks it on the beak.)
textes.… (Gaspard sourit. Le perroquet : « TOUT: … (Gaspard smiles. The parrot: “ALL GOOD! ALL GOOD! RUM!”)
textes.… (Gaspard tapote un rythme sur sa cuiss: … (Gaspard taps a rhythm on his thigh, boom ta-ka boom, then points at the parrot, rolling his eyes. The parrot: “OMAR! THE ADMIRAL IS A MUSICIAN! HIRED!”)
textes.… (Gaspard te fait un clin d'œil et lève: … (Gaspard winks at you and tilts his chin towards the roof near the Fondouk. The parrot: “SHH!”)
… (Gaspard waves at you. On his shoulder, the red and blue parrot squawks: “GASPARD SAYS HELLO! GASPARD SAYS HELLO! SQUAWK!”)
textes.… (Gaspard te refait son haussement d'ép: … (Gaspard gives you his knowing shrug again. The parrot: “DEPENDS! SQUAWK!”)
textes.… (Gaspard te regarde longtemps. Puis il: … (Gaspard looks at you for a long time. Then he points, discreetly, at a roof near the Fondouk, and puts a finger to his lips. The parrot: “SHH! SHH!”)
textes.… (Gaspard écrit sur son ardoise et te l: … (Gaspard writes on his slate and hands it to you. The parrot reads: “CAN YOU KEEP A SECRET?”)
textes.… (Il hoche la tête un peu plus fort.) B: … (He nods a little harder.) Good. You've got the ear.
textes.… (Il hoche la tête, puis tend l'oreille: … (He nods, then tilts his ear towards the Chasm.) It says goodbye too. Three times.
textes.… (Il lève deux doigts.) {surnom}. Ça va: … (He raises two fingers.) {surnom}. All good. Germaine too.
textes.… (Il ne dit rien pendant un moment, et: … (He says nothing for a while, and his moustache trembles.) That's what my grandmother used to say. You're the right buyer. I can feel it.
textes.… (Il pose ta main à plat sur le sable.): … (He lays your hand flat on the sand.) That. Boom. The heart of the track. Now you know.
textes.… (Il sourit presque.) Comme Tapage. Ça: … (He almost smiles.) Like Tapage. It can be learned. Sit down. Be quiet. There. You're learning.
textes.… (Il sourit.) C'est la meilleure répons: … (He smiles.) That's the best answer. Come back in ten years.
… (He points to Germaine, then to the Hall.) Noise. Tonight.
textes.… (Il te regarde longtemps.) Gravier. (I: … (He looks at you for a long time.) Gravier. (He looks at the sea.) Fisherman. (He looks at the sea again.) Sit down. Or don't. The sea doesn't mind.
textes.… (Il te regarde.) Tu préfères le bruit: … (He looks at you.) Do you prefer noise or silence?
textes.… (Il te regarde.) Tu sais écouter, toi: … (He looks at you.) Do you know how to listen?
textes.… (Il écrit sur l'ardoise : « CE JOUR-LÀ: … (He writes on the slate: “THAT DAY, ONE WORD. OUT LOUD. THE FIRST IN TWENTY YEARS.” He hesitates, then underlines “OUT LOUD”.)
textes.… (Le perroquet : « LA BALEINE ! DE TOUT: … (The parrot: “THE WHALE! UP CLOSE! WITH YOUSSEF!” Gaspard spreads his arms as wide as he can, then brings his hands together: really close.)
textes.… (Le perroquet : « LE CHAT ! LE CHAT RO: … (The parrot: “THE CAT! THE GINGER CAT! ON THE ROOF! THE CRATES! THE CRATES!”)
textes.… (Le perroquet, d'un coup : « BALEINE !: … (The parrot, all of a sudden: “WHALE! WHALE!” Gaspard points at Youssef and mimes someone shouting, hands cupped round his mouth. He shrugs: that's who the Admiral learned it from. Since then, the bird shouts it at every slightly grey cloud.)
textes.… (Le perroquet, dès qu'il te voit : « B: … (The parrot, as soon as it sees you: “BLABBERMOUTH! SQUAWK!” Gaspard shrugs, sorry.)
textes.… (Tchoum hoche la tête en rythme sans s: … (Tchoum nods his head to the beat without stopping.) … Hi.
textes.… Ah, et si un jour tu pêches une vieill: … Oh, and if you ever fish up an old boot, bring it to me: I'll buy it.
textes.… Ah. Alors tu sais. Ça reste coincé là,: … Ah. Then you know. It stays stuck right here, like a cannonball in the barrel. Go and tell them, if you can. Listen to me saying that, when I haven't done it.
textes.… Ah. C'est toi. Je t'ai reconnu au pas,: … Ah. It's you. I recognised your step, from the far end of the bridge. (A small smile.) That only happens with people I like.
textes.… Ah. Toi aussi. Ne le dis pas trop fort: … Ah. You too. Don't say it too loudly. People laugh, or else they get scared. Both are tiresome.
… So the moon spoke to you, too. Listen carefully. When the elders brought back the Seal of Mists, they laid it at the bottom of the big pond, on a round stone, and closed the old sluice gate so the water would keep it. The sluice gate is a bronze mechanism on the west edge of the pond, and no one knows how to turn it anymore. If the Bronze Seal obeys you, it will turn it. When the water is low, wait for the moon: the seal shows itself only to her.
textes.… Après ? Après, c'est le travail des na: … After that? After that, it's dwarf work. Borin Barbe-de-Fer, at Forgefer, under the Fire Mountain. He knows how to engrave runes. Tell him Ursule sent you. He'll grumble. That's a good sign.
textes.… Attends. (Il ramasse un de tes dés, le: … Wait. (He picks up one of your dice and weighs it.) This die's heavy. It's LOADED! CHEAT!
textes.… Attends. Tu gagnes trop. Beaucoup trop: … Wait. You're winning too much. Way too much. CHEAT!
textes.… Avec moi ? Personne n'a jamais choisi: … With me? No one has ever chosen the ground floor for me. Noting: “visitor, very kind”.
… FINE. I'M LOOKING AT YOU TOO.
textes.… Bien. Ceux qui n'ont pas peur de l'eau: … Good. Those who aren't afraid of water, the water eats them. Stay careful.
textes.… Bien. Moi aussi. Le virage des racines: … Good. Me too. The root bend. Take the left foothold.
textes.… Bienvenue au jardin. (Il ratisse une l: … Welcome to the garden. (He rakes a long straight line, then a wave.) Here, we speak little. The cherry trees speak for us. And the bamboo fountain counts the time.
… All right, just a little one.
… Fine. I'll write down: directed fall.
… Fine. A little bit me. A teeny bit.
… Good morning, Mother Brasille. Thank you.
textes.… Bonjour. (Il pose un doigt sur ses lèv: … Hello. (He puts a finger to his lips.) Listen. … Hear that? It's the Chasm. It says hello too. I'm Écho. I play bass. And I listen. Mostly, I listen.
textes.… Bonne réponse. La mer, ça va. L'eau qu: … Good answer. The sea is fine. Still water, no. You've understood something. Don't tell anyone.
textes.… Bonne réponse. Le jour, le silence. Le: … Good answer. Silence by day. Noise by night. Like me.
… Good evening. I… thank you. For the candle.
textes.… Bonsoir. Ou bonjour. Les heures se res: … Good evening. Or good morning. The hours all look alike when you keep a lighthouse.
textes.… Bourrasque. … Elle tape fort. … Elle p: … Bourrasque. … She hits hard. … She talks loud. … She wakes me up. … That's useful.
textes.… Brume. On ne parle pas. C'est bien. …: … Brume. We don't talk. It's good. … She knows everything. She says nothing. That's better.
… It was the best one anyway.
textes.… Caramel. Elle m'a élevée. À moitié. Su: … Caramel. She raised me. Half raised. On the jetty. … She saves me the biggest skewer. She talks too much about Grisou.
textes.… Change-le. Tout de suite. Je ne plaisa: … Change it. Right now. I'm not joking. Even Turbo has a better password, and his is “dragon”.
textes.… Chut. Moi non plus. Ne le dis à person: … Shh. Me neither. Don't tell anyone. It's our secret, okay? Cross my heart and swear on my ears.
textes.… Crochet. Maître d'équipage de la Morue: … Crochet. Bosun of the Cod. I don't like questions. Got a question?
textes.… D'accord, je te le dis. C'est un petit: … Fine, I'll tell you. It's a little white dog! He hides them near the crates, at the end of the quay, by the lighthouse. But you won't scold him, will you?
… A giant who reads under a lantern.
textes.… De la brume. Bien. On trempe l'argent: … Mist. Right. You temper silver in it: it sings clearer. Here. A little silver bell. I made it for nothing. Now it's for you.
textes.… Des tournesols. De SON jardin. (Elle l: … Sunflowers. From HER garden. (She looks at them for a long time. A drop falls on a petal; it isn't the rain.) That old goat… She remembers I loved them, then. Wait. On the porch of my yurt, there's an umbrella. The most beautiful one I ever made, with sunflowers painted underneath. I made it for her fifty years ago, and I never gave it to her. Take it to her.
textes.… Dis. Tu préfères le jour, ou la nuit ?: … Say. Do you prefer day, or night?
textes.… Elle a ronronné. Elle n'a jamais ronro: … She purred. She has never purred for anyone! Not even the high priest! Maybe you're… blessed?
textes.… Elle est meilleure que les miennes. Je: … It's better than mine. I quit. (Just kidding.)
textes.… Elle est passée, ce matin, la Chanteus: … Did the Singer go by this morning?
textes.… En secret… je vais écouter les djembés: … In secret… I go and listen to the camp djembes. … Behind the hill. … They play well. … I put chords over them, in my head. … It works. … Don't tell.
textes.… Et ce qu'il y a dans ma poche, je ne v: … And whatever's in my pocket, I don't want to know.
textes.… Et une au monsieur. Et une à moi, alor: … And one for the gentleman. And one for me, then.
… To make feedback… on the Great Stage. … So loud… they'd hear it on both sides of the island. … And everyone would look up at the same time.
textes.… Fort. (Il regarde Bastien, au loin, tr: … Loud. (He looks over at Bastien, in the distance, for a very long time.) He gave you earplugs, didn't he. Right.
textes.… Galet. Je fais des cordes. (Il tire su: … Galet. I make ropes. (He tugs on a rope.) That's a good rope. It would hold a boat. Or a whale. Or a whale in a boat.
textes.… Grisou croit que je le regarde comme u: … Grisou thinks I look at him like a skewer. No. The day of the root, he was the only one who asked “you OK?”. The only one. … He talks. He loses. He laughs. He starts again. … I like him. More than like. I won't say anything. As usual. Neither will you, {surnom}.
… Grisou. He talks. A lot. He runs. Less. … But he tries again. Always.
textes.… Ha. Ha. Très drôle. Tu as passé trop d: … Ha. Ha. Very funny. You've spent too much time with Caelan. Go away. … No, stay. That was funny. A bit.
textes.… Hm. C'est mieux, peut-être. Tu cours l: … Hm. Maybe that's better. Do you run at night? … Come. I won't tell.
textes.… Hm. … Moi aussi. Depuis longtemps. Ce: … Hm. … Me too. For a long time now. That isn't good news. Not for you. Not for me.
textes.… Hmpf. C'est vrai, mais ne le répète pa: … Hmph. True, but don't repeat it.
textes.… Hum. C'est très juste. Pour Dame Ysold: … Hmm. That's very true. For Lady Ysolde, I can talk for hours. For people, perhaps a little less. You are a sage, my dear.
… He said that? No. He didn't say that. He never says that. … Did he really say that?
textes.… Il a dit ça ? Vingt-deux ans… Bon. On: … He said that? Twenty-two years… Well. We'll see. Maybe. Someday. Not today.
textes.… Il a sauté. Par-dessus moi. Sans regar: … He jumped. Over me. Without looking. … One day, at the root bend, I'm the one who passes. In front.
… It does shine a little, though.
textes.… Il n'y a pas de honte. Le noir, je le: … There's no shame in it. I keep watch over the dark for those who fear it. That's my job. You'll sleep soundly.
textes.… Il s'appelle Amiral. … DEHORS, J'AI DI: … His name is Admiral. … OUT, I SAID!
textes.… Il y a deux ans. Je mène. Le virage de: … Two years ago. I'm leading. The root bend. The root is wet. I slip. Bondi comes. He jumps. Over. Like over a puddle. … He didn't look back. Not one ear. He won. … I haven't forgotten. I won't forget.
textes.… Ils se sont endormis. C'est la troisiè: … They've fallen asleep. That's the third time this week.
textes.… J'ai joué « Les Deux Côtés ». … Ma cha: … I played “Both Sides”. … My song from the notebook. … Nobody was asleep. … Not even me.
textes.… J'ai médité six heures avec lui. … Il: … I meditated six hours with him. … He says I snored. … I think it was a mantra.
textes.… J'ai trouvé ma première guitare… dans: … I found my first guitar… in a bin. … It was missing three strings. … I learned to play with three strings. … When I had six… it was too easy.
… I'm going back. Just in case.
… I'm going. But this is a one-off.
textes.… Je comprends mieux pourquoi tu as cett: … That explains the face you're pulling.
textes.… Je l'ai laissé à l'Observatoire. Mais: … I left it at the Observatory. But I thought about it!
… I'll note it in the report.
… I'll have a word with him.
… I fall asleep easily. … Meditating. … Eating. … Playing. … Once, I played a solo while asleep. … It was my best. … I don't remember it.
textes.… Je parle lentement. … Mais je joue vit: … I talk slowly. … But I play fast. … Really fast. … It balances out.
textes.… Je pourrais repartir. Chaque fois. Les: … I could leave. Every time. The camels wait, the caravan waits. I say: “tomorrow”. And I stay one more night. For years now. Because of Zineb. I've never said anything to her. In the desert, you don't talk about what's precious, {surnom}. You keep it. Like water. … You won't say anything either.
textes.… Je préfère ça. Mais je te tiens à l'œi: … That's more like it. But I've got my eye on you.
… I'm preparing a prayer, just in case.
textes.… Je suis né sous une tente, à l'oasis,: … I was born in a tent at the oasis, between two palm trees. My father led caravans. In the evening, he showed me the sky. That star is the north. That one is the well. That one is the salt road. I learnt the stars before my letters. My letters, I know badly. The stars, I never get wrong.
textes.… Je suis née à la pêcherie. La dernière: … I was born at the fishery. The last one. Fifteen years after Caramel. Dad said: “Watch the float.” I watched. Two seconds. Then I ran along the jetty. The fish fled. All of them. Dad sighed into his whiskers. Caramel laughed. … I couldn't keep still. I still can't.
textes.… Je vais faire semblant de ne pas avoir: … I'll pretend I didn't hear that.
textes.… Je vais te dire. … J'ai un carnet. … D: … I'll tell you. … I've got a notebook. … Inside… the chords for the camp djembes. … Every evening, I write them down. … I made a song with them. … It's called “Both Sides.” … I haven't played it to anyone. … Not even Flanelle.
textes.… La racine. Je suis par terre. Bondi pa: … The root. I'm on the ground. Bondi goes over. Nothing. Grisou arrives. He doesn't stop. That's racing. But he turns his head. “You OK?” … Two words. Nobody else. He doesn't remember. I do.
… Saying it is already a lot. You see. I said it.
textes.… Le gravier. Tu le vois en vagues, ou e: … The gravel. Do you see it in waves, or in lines?
textes.… Le héron. Douze ans. Il prend la perch: … The heron. Twelve years old. It takes Dad's perch. From the basket. I run. All the way round the pond. It drops the perch. I bring it back. Proud. … Dad says: “A cat waits.” … That's all he said. I think I disappointed him.
textes.… Le kick. Tu l'entends ? Il est propre: … The kick. Hear it? Is it clean?
textes.… Le larsen. … Le sifflement de l'ampli,: … Feedback. … The squeal of the amp, when the guitar's too close. … Everybody hates it. … Me, I love it. … It's the island's song.

… Feedback. … The squeal of the amp, when you bring the guitar close. … Everyone hates it. … I love it. … It's the island's song. … The island's called Larsen for a reason — that's what we call feedback.
… The mast went through the cork. The cork went through the window. Well. Let's say it's a submarine.
… In the evening, the guitar talks for me. … It's chattier than I am.
textes.… Les deux. (Elle te regarde longtemps.): … Both. (She looks at you for a long time.) I like you.
textes.… Les vagues sont là. Tu les vois encore: … The waves are there. Do you still see them?
… My waltz? Oh… If you like.
textes.… Mantra. … Il médite. … Moi aussi. … En: … Mantra. … He meditates. … Me too. … Well. … I sleep. … Shh.
… Mantra. … He meditates. … Me too. … Well… I sleep. … He doesn't say anything. … He's a good master.
textes.… Merci. C'est ma grand-mère qui l'a tri: … Thanks. My grandmother knitted it. … OUT!
textes.… Merci. Vraiment. Bon. Tu chantes, main: … Thank you. Really. Right. You sing now.
textes.… Moi ? (Ses yeux clignotent très vite.): … Me? (His eyes blink very fast.) I… I didn't have that option on my list. I'm adding it. At the top.
… Well, I'd quite like to sleep.
textes.… Mon père faisait traverser les gens su: … My father ferried people across a river. All day long, questions: “Is it deep?”, “Is it far?”, “When do we get there?”. My father answered everything. Me, I rowed. I didn't answer a single question for ten years. It gave me a taste for silence. There. Next.
… Come up tonight. With the coffee.
textes.… Montre. … Hm. Pas mal. Tu as navigué,: … Show me. … Hm. Not bad. You've sailed, you have.
textes.… Mrrr. Viens plus près. Moi aussi. Beau: … Mrrr. Come closer. Me too. Very. I've never told anyone. Don't repeat it, all right?
… Myrtille. She wants to run like me. … She climbs too high. She can't count. She's perfect.
textes.… Oh. Bonjour. Lin. Apprentie. Excuse-mo: … Oh. Hello. Lin. Apprentice. Sorry, I was on chapter twelve. The light spell is described in four hundred pages. It's fascinating.
